name: Zombie Rollerz: Pinball Heroes
detailed_description: Zombie Rollerz: Pinball Heroes is the ultimate mashup of classic pinball and zombie defense with rogue-like elements to ensure no two playthroughs are ever the same! Shoot, slam and smash your way through hordes of adorkable zombies in this fusion of pinball, point defense and zombie horde gameplay. Select from 10 different heroes , each with their own special ability to shoot zombies in hilarious ways. Discover and unlock hundreds of helpful powers and items to boost your hero. 11 epic boss fights await , requiring pinballing precision and careful ability management to be taken down! Rogue-like elements: 4 worlds wait to be explored by you via the overworld map. Random generation ensures that no playthrough is the same. You must adapt at each and every turn if you want to rid all worlds of the rampaging zombie plague – pinball-style! Better than ever! Zombie Rollerz: Pinball Heroes is the new and improved continuation of the famous original game that fascinated millions on mobile devices already! Fight 50 different types of adorkable zombies by pinballing through a cartoony world Addicting mashup of classic pinball and zombie defense Epic zombie boss fights that will test your skills Random generation of 4 different worlds ensures that no playthrough is the same More than 300 trinkets and skills for you to unlock, including legendaries!

_childDocuments_.review: Bringing classic gameplay mechanics into modern games is a trend that has seen a wide range of successes and failures. Pinball may be one of the oldest mechanics used for this purpose and one that has had some innovative implementations. Zombie Rollerz: Pinball Heroes isn’t the most direct manifestation of that classic game, but it does expand on the addictive qualities of bouncing balls and flashing lights to make something that’s pretty easy to get sucked into.Abbreviated Review: At its core, the pinball mechanics of Zombie Rollerz are pretty enjoyable. While you’re not (necessarily) going for high scores or following an elaborate unlocking progression of point accumulation, you’re still paddling a ball around for the bulk of the gameplay. The distinction is that now you just happen to be smashing zombies to death with that ball – which is a very enjoyable experience.Isolating just this, the pinball aspects are some of the best parts of the game. You can use the expected nature of the ball just hitting the zombies to do damage, but you can also trigger environmental effects like explosive boxes, whirling axes, and wells that blast water out onto certain areas of each arena. This design is rewarding in that it promotes the same sort of practiced aiming you’d get in a more traditional pinball game, but with a wide variety of effects. This alone would provide a unique enough platform to build out the game, but then the ball, support, and ultimate effects add a layer on top of it that gives it some of the depth it needs.The numerous effects that unlock allow you to have a fairly unique loadout for each playthrough. The ball effects are skills that give your ball certain abilities or damage types such as fire, ice, and even launching little swords. These effects charge a meter that, once full, can be triggered for additional powers like launching daggers or giving your ball an AOE of flames. Similarly, support and ultimate skills you accumulate can be triggered for their own effects – though they don’t necessarily happen on the ball. For instance, one ultimate turns your paddles into literal machine guns to blast away at the zombie infestation. Support skills can vary between simply buffing up your pinball’s damage or shooting lightning bolts at enemies and everything in between.All of this functions to create a dynamic and addictive experience when it comes to what you’ll be doing for most of the gameplay. However, it is still just a part of the overall progression within the game.The rest of Zombie Rollerz’s gameplay orbits around a roguelike mechanic that has you venturing through four hex-grid maps. On this journey, you’ll be collecting and upgrading gear and picking up tools that make battling zombies and moving around the map easier. Making it through the various obstacles, random discoveries, and zombie encounters will level you up - giving you a chance to unlock more skills and upgrade the ones you currently have. It’s advantageous to explore every nook and cranny and fight every battle, but you’re going to risk potentially losing too much health and ending your run early.As you move forward, you’ll have to defeat a boss at the end of each map before teleporting to the next. These are more elaborate battles than you normally face with other zombies and there is a significantly smaller focus on engaging with arena features. While they add some spice to the overall experience, they can feel a bit unfair if you happened to have a build of abilities that help you do direct damage. However, their difficulty isn’t so high that it makes it impossible to finish a run. Once you’ve made it through the static cycle of only four maps, you’ll have one final boss to defeat to hit the end screen.I didn’t really expect Zombie Rollerz to have a strong story, but I kind of expected to be able to find my way to an actual ending. After the 16 or so hours I’ve played as of writing this, I still have no idea what or where the ending is. I’ve unlocked all of the 11 characters and progressed through hundreds of levels on the “road” unlocking more abilities and trinkets, yet I’ve only seen a handful of the “endings” according to the collection pages. Each time you reach the end and defeat the final boss, a black screen of text describes a strange scenario with somewhat poor grammatical structure, and after a quick “The End” you’re back at the menu. With a story that’s already pretty difficult to follow given how broken up it is, this was pretty disappointing. I don’t really feel the motivation to play more without characters to unlock or any idea what is necessary to reach the ending.While it is nice to have a variety of characters with different starting stats to try out, they don’t bring much to the table outside of tiny broken tidbits of information as to what the story is trying to convey. Each one is looking to accomplish something, but much of it seems unrelated despite always culminating in a rendezvous with a portal. The only part you can reference afterward is those same couple of sentences that scrawled across the end screen of each successful battle.With this issue of an ending I can’t find and the repetition of the maps and arenas, it really takes away from what is a fun pinball-based adventure. If I could give a more middling score than “recommended” or “not recommended,” I definitely would. Yet, Zombie Rollerz: Pinball Heroes does present an otherwise well-crafted and mostly bug-free experience I enjoyed most of the way through, so I will have to lean toward recommended. It’s just frustrating to play a game without any idea of what it’s trying to convey to you or if you’re making any progress toward an eventual goal.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm rating this as a Yes for the gameplay in the stages, because the actual pinball levels are a lot of fun, but if it was a rating for all the stuff around the pinball levels it would be a massive thumbs down. I'm not a huge fan of roguelite at the best of times but here its a real drag, if you want to complete the game with all the characters at all you're going to be going through the first world a good few times even if you manage it on a single run each time, and you won't manage it on a single run. By the time you get to the end that first world is just a slog. What's worse is that since the upgrades and map are randomly generated a bad set of options can make a run more or less pointless but you still have to slog through to your inevitable demise since if you tap out early you don't get the legacy rewards. I'm uninstalling it now since I really can't face that first world again, I'm sure I'll go back to it one day, but I'd rather I just had a non-roguelike option to mean I didn't feel like leaving in the first place. Oh and incidentally, the process of going from one day to another really doesn't need to take two unskippable full screen pieces of constantly repeated dialogue.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fairly enjoyable.  At 15 hours into the game, I have unlocked each character and beat the game with each.  The first two characters unlock Hard difficulty, then you beat Hard to unlock Hell.  I stuck to Hard to beat the game with each character once, but I will probably jump up to Hell now.  The score, which gets a significant multiplier as you go up in difficulty, is what unlocks the different skills and items you will encounter randomly in each play through, and there are a LOT, maybe too many.  The items coupled with the map between levels, which is also random, are your rougelite elements.  The pinball mechanic is fairly minor in the game, which might be good or bad depending on what you are wanting.  Each level you complete causes the zombie plague to spread on the map behind you, so you can't just complete everything on later maps, which might annoy some people, unless you have enough hp to move through (each map tile will subtract some HP based on the difficulty and can easily kill you).There are a bunch of characters, which initially adds some variety to the game.  They each feel unique and get some unique dialogue, which is very minor, as you go through the levels.  Unfortunately, as you progress, the unique skills of those characters can be random skills you obtain, so eventually each character feels identical.The rougelite elements can also really screw you up, too.  I mentioned there are a LOT of skills and items you can come across as you unlock them.  Some skills are pretty worthless, some are amazing, and some I think the developers didn't realize were amazing because they are super cheap to upgrade.  There is a fatal shot skill that makes your next bullseye (directly hitting an enemy from a flipper, no bouncing) increase in damage by like 5000% when upgraded, and it's super cheap to upgrade.  I went from killing the last boss in one shot one play through to not even being able to beat the first map in the next play through.  Some mind enjoy this, some might get annoyed.  I always enjoy finding that ultimate combination of items/skills in roguelites that make you into an immortal murder machine and love when the stars align to give you that perfect build.  That can happen here, but sometimes it's just a single skill you can get that makes the run a joke, which is somewhat disappointing to me.All in all a fun little game.  The install is very small, so at this point it will be one of those games that I don't uninstall and play whenever I want something to do for a little bit before bed or while watching TV if I'm not too engrossed with what's on the TV.  It's a relatively inexpensive game, so it was definitely worth what I am getting out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish I could give game this a positive review. I love the mechanics of the game, the goofy self awareness of some of the characters, the progression path to unlock things, the music and sound effects are good and satisfying, the game balancing is relatively fair for the assumed younger target audience. It has a lot of things I really do enjoy, but it is simply not to necessary quality which a game should have on release at the current time (4/26/22)Some things can be excused (choppy sound effect loops continuing past boss deaths, visual glitches which appear if you alt tab while playing at certain times- which i attribute to user conditions for me personally, and a few others) That said, there's many things which are borderline unacceptable for me:I have been soft locked a total of 3 distinct occasions. When loading out of a level leaving only a black screen, when loading into a level (also black screen), and when inside a level with an enemy somewehere offscreen and completely unkillable (this has happened twice to date and the state in which I am currently which drove me to write all of this out this moment). Other things like a snow ball simply clipping through the ground after being summoned, balls being pushed out by physics of the zombies causing loss of life and once an entire run while in the last world, weather effects always being present on specific levels which have none active on the map, the map itself and its very poor optimization for mouse and keyboard (I cannot say for sure  with controller as I can't really play with a controller at the current moment). Other things which I want to comment on but are not particularly good or bad actively: potentially confusing wording on some items, for example the "takes no damage during the day" effects which I have had take effect even if i have taken damage on many occasions. Mouse aiming of the ballista can be started before the screen has properly transitioned down to the right place allowing for misfires. And a few other things which arn't coming to mind right now.It breaks my heart to have to write a review as harsh as this because I do not at all regret the time I have spent with this game. It was actively fun almost the entire time whenever the game is functioning properly. This all would be totally fine in an early access release or even a beta patch, heck i would gladly do bug reports for either of these situations. But as far as i see I can't find places to do so. If all this changes and the game gets some updates to fix the buggy and broken bits of it I would gladly come back to this game, because I adore so much of it, but cannot say to anybody in confidence "yeah buy this game" with the state it is right now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a neat blend of the classic pinball and zombie defense gameplay, but with a surprising amount of well-developed rougelite mechanics. It sounds like a weird mix on paper, but it just works. There are a lot of items, abilities, and 10 different playable characters, so every run feels unique. The game at first can seem a little easy, as you can get by pretty easily without much thought about your build and pathing across the overworld. However, if you put in the time to unlock the higher difficulties the game can definitely start to become challenging. In conclusion, I highly recommend to rougelite fans who want to try something unique, and maybe a little more casual.

_childDocuments_.review: Soft recommend from me here. I like goofy roguelikes and this game was quite enjoyable for the first few hours, but there's just not enough change for gameplay not to be repetitive. The runs are already long (about 30-40 minutes) so when you don't get anything new for the next run it can be quite discouraging to keep going. Other than that, gameplay is suprisingly fun and fluid for just being pinball and the art style is pretty funny, so still check it out if you're interested, the price is pretty cheap!

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review: Steam Curator: TBH, I expected exactly nothing from Zombie Rollerz: Pinball Heroes—a mobile port with a silly name and even sillier-looking gameplay. But I'll be darned if this little title didn’t turn out to be the most fun I’ve had with a game since... well, late January, but I play way too many games it’s... it’s bad, y’all. And, like me, you’ve probably got a packed gaming calendar ahead, what with Forbidden West, Elden Ring, and, dare I say it, Cyberpunk is hype-able again?  Anyway, the long-winded point I’m trying make here is that if you end up getting burned out by these massive, complex, punishing RPGs in the coming weeks or months and need a straight-forward and keyword easy change of pace, I think Zombie Rollerz could be that game for you, because it was for me. So, in keeping with the theme of nobody having any time for anything, let me hit you with just a quick thought or three about this game’s Gameplay, Content, Story and Style, after which I hope you’ll have a better idea of whether Zombie Rollerz is the right change of pace for you. GAMEPLAY – Combat (4/5) | Non-Combat (3/5) | U.I. (4/5) | Playability (2/5) The core gameplay loop in Zombie Rollerz is as follows: first, you’ll choose from one of the game’s 10 colorful champions, all of whom you'll gradually unlock as you accrue experience points in the game world; second, you'll use magical pinballs—and yes, you heard that correctly—to fight as far forward as possible through the game's handful of zombie-infested zones, at the end of each awaits one of ten randomly selected bosses; and finally, third you will do what you’ve done in Hades, Risk of Rain, and every other roguelite worth its salt—you'll repeat! But only after you’ve died a grisly death, right?  ... No, really, I’m asking... can you actually die in this game? I’m not sure. I’ve played Zombie Rollerz on every difficulty now, including HELL MODE, and have yet to not win a run. This isn’t some weak, #MLG brag, mind you, just me pointing out what I believe to be this game’s biggest flaw: it’s too easy. Really, I once finished the final boss fight with more health than I started with. Lucky for Zombie Rollerz, poor balancing doesn’t make the chaotic combat experience here any less glee-inducing—really, who knew launching little cartoon zombies into orbit would be my new therapy of choice. Meanwhile, the game’s user interface does a great job of cutting through all this visual bombardment to telegraph what's most important to the player—where your ball is, when your skills are ready, and when the boss is about to one-shot you. CONTENT – World (4/5) | Objectives (3/5) | Bosses (3/5) | Puzzles (3/5) | Value (3/5) As for content, the level-designs in Zombie Rollerz are varied and interesting and left me impressed, which is a small miracle considering that you’re never not playing zombie f**king pinball here. I suppose a light puzzle here and a treasure hunt mini-game there further break up this game’s otherwise conceptually repetitive objectives. But, speaking of repetitive, over time your playthroughs will probably begin to blend together—you see, each hero starts out unique, but loses their respective flavor as you accrue the same skills and items. I mean, for example, should Penny the penguin princess really get to use a napalm ballista? She complained about being too hot for the entire third zone, after all. STORY – Plot (3/5) | Characters (3/5) | Dialogue (2/5) On the subject of Characters, let's talk Story, and don’t worry, I’ll spend about as much time on this subject as did the devs. The plot in Zombie Rollerz is fast and loose, surface-level “rescue the princess” kinda stuff. Each hero sports a different motivation for reaching the end of the run, and will talk about it relentlessly to Professor Omnipedia, your quirky know-it-all companion. The dialogue here reads on an 8th grade level and is riddled with typos, but it’s got some charm and is occasionally funny—not funny enough to save it from a two, though. STYLE – Art (4/5) | Music (3/5) | Sound (4/5) Let’s wrap up with a few words on style. Zombie Rollerz is a bright, even vibrant blast of color and sound that all adds up to an audio-visual treat that kept me glued to the screen for far longer than I care to admit. Really, are all mobile games this addicting? Because Zombie Rollerz feels like drugs. Meanwhile the game’s soundtrack is equally fun but a little too repetitive to escape neutral three purgatory. Conclusion In the end, I recommend Zombie Rollerz as a fun and easy change-of-pace experience for when you get tired of Margit the Fell Omen beating you into a pulp and want to feel like a competent adult again. After averaging up our micrometrics, Zombie Rollerz: Pinball Heroes earns an aggregate MEGA score of 3.2/5. Until next time, this is Scope, and thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: zombies, pinball, rpg elements, and rogue-lite so what's not to like? you'll start with one of the characters with 4 states Stam/HP, STR/phys attacks (ball, flappers, some spells), INT/magic attacks, and Luck/Crit. as you play you'll get upgrades and special moves to help you fight undead hoards. you'll start on a randomly generated level that you need to get to the end of before the level is covered in hazards. these will spawn behind you after every fight and will take some hp from you for every step you take in it. you'll do a few levels with a mini boss at the end of each and finally a big boss at the end. fights are like a small pinball board but zombies will spawn and attack your flippers. you can attack with your ball and spells but also your flippers that will knock enemies back. besides this there are things to hit on the level that will damage an area of the level.i'm not sure if a hardcore pinballer would like this game as it feels slow. this is done so you can better line up your shots and the ball gets really slow on the flappers. i'm not sure if you can speed it up but even if there is i don't see it getting to the level of a fast paced pinball game. that said this is a great game for people who like pinball but are not that great at most machines and people between the two extremes.how could killing zombies with your balls not be fun.7/10p.s. if you like this game try Rollers of the Realm

_childDocuments_.review: When I originally got this, it was locking upon the menu screen and I couldn't play it.  Fortunately something changed and I was able to give it a try.If you're looking for a pinball game, keep looking.  This is not really a pinball game.  I'm frankly not sure how to describe it.  It reminded me of several things, including Final Fantasy and Pokemon.  You walk around various zones looking for treasure and ... power-ups.  Occasionally you have to do battle, and that's where the "pinball" part of the equation comes up.  It's kinda, sorta, like pinball.  It's nothing like what most  people would think of as pinball, but it's close enough that you can forgive them calling it that.I'm still  not sure if  I like this game or not, but I am withdrawing my negative review... for now.
_childDocuments_.name: Zombie Rollerz: Pinball Heroes

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to recommend this game. I am an old school pinball enthusiast.  I still remember the Pinball Arcades and how I would scour the town for cans and bottles to recycle so I could grind a few dollars to play... So when video pinball games became a thing, you can bet I was all over it. I really loved the old Pinball RPG for NES way back in the day... All that aside, this game has a lot of great things going for it outside of actual pinball play, but mostly feels like proof of concept stuff. The problem is the pinball. And that is a big problem for a game with pinball right in the title.  They dumbed it down so toddlers can play I guess...the ball physics are very odd and sometimes unpredictable outside of the track line that is provided when it comes in contact with your paddles.  But the ball sticks to the paddles I presume so you can better aim your next shot, but it kills immersion because the illusion of inertia for the ball is destroyed, as are your reflex expectations as a pinball enthusiast.  This game is not for pinball enthusiasts.  It is for someone else, not sure who, toddlers mostly I assume.  Aside from that the art style is terrible, lazy and ugly.  There is no ambient occlusion though there could be as the environments are rendered in 3D polygons with garish overlays.  Most of the action on the "table" is too frenetic to follow but you don't need to because the balls stick to your paddles so just wait till it comes around and then wait some more as it sticky rolls down your paddle like your scrotum peels off your thigh on a hot humid summer day after marathon sex with your best friends mom while you wait for him to come home from summer school....STICKY is the point.  Not for me.  But I will play some more just to explore a few more of the mechanics and game content.
_childDocuments_.name: Zombie Rollerz: Pinball Heroes

_childDocuments_.review: Its not pinball, its not a dungeon crawl, its not an A-RPG.. but it seems to combine the worst of all those genres. Combined with atrocious grammatical and spelling issues, terribly twee J-RPG style graphics and no explanation of how the 'overworld' map is supposed to work, if I was still within my timeframe to refund, I absolutely would, even for the super low sale price I paid. Feels kind of like a weird bullet-hell... but with a pinball? In a fiery helmet?? Trying to be a samurai warrior maybe???If you are after a fun pinball game, don't bother, its not.If you're after a satisfying roguelike/roguelite, don't bother, its not.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite pinball game on pc, it's a bit of a grind but a fun one!This is setup like a battle, with multiple heroes and biomes to unlock. Each hero and biome has unique abilities and skills. The farther you go, the more you can mix and match. The hero is the character that shoots the pinball. Each bad guy is another pinball level. Plus, there are bonus levels and puzzle levels. Map events occur as you work your way across the land, fighting villains and getting chased by the zombie plague. Your skills level as you go, making it easy to become too sure of yourself! I have no idea how many bosses are in this game but at 13 hours, I'm still defeating new ones. The game saving ability is kind. The game autosaves after every round, making it an easy choice for those times you just want to play a quick round of something. tl;dr, Pinball go pow, yay!

_childDocuments_.review: Zombie Rollerz is a game that is easy to pick up and play whenever you start craving for pinball. Let's explore the ups and downs of the game (+, +/-, -, ?):+The graphics are simple and pleasing. Everything pops out nicely.+The controls are pretty much perfect for a game like this.+Pinball and RPG together? Yes! Beware, you might get hooked!+Many cool playable characters.*+A sweet selection of balls, skills and items.**+An easy way to spend an hour or so every time you feel like playing pinball.+/-There's some story here, but it's not important at all. Does there need to be a story to begin with? I wonder...+/-*After your first playthrough with a character, there's no dialogue, nothing. It makes everything faster, sure, but...the story...+/-There's some balancing issues when it comes to skills. Some skills are clearly overpowered while some are practically useless.-The RNG determines your fate too often. Impossible situations thanks to having poor luck? Oh yes!-On harder difficulties, it can be impossible to defend your character from zombies because you got no reload ready or your skills are useless when fighting zombies near the flippers.-The hardest difficulty is an angel dust blitzkrieg of killing it against mobs, but some bosses become impossible to beat.-There's a glitch that makes you shoot and take damage on repeat, killing you. Cool.?I know, I know, this is a roguelite... but I wanted to save and retry so often...?Everything repeats a lot. Map layout, the "tables", everything.?In a way, this is better than Senran Kagura: Peach Ball... but is it really?Zombie Rollerz: Is a great pinball RPG when you just want to spend an hour having a good, chill time. However, it's a bit faulty and even infuriating at times on harder difficulties. But, I'd love to see a sequel to this. This might be the best pinball game on Steam...after Peach Ball...Maybe... 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I. F'ING. HATE. THIS. GAME. but i also like it, it's just i hate it more than i like it. i have not been so frustrated with a game in such a long time it was aggravating. be it my crappy skills, bad luck, bugs/glitches or whatever else....i raged and cussed that'd put an old sailor to shame. now don't get me wrong, the game is very fun to play...when it all goes your way that is. you can say it's all about skill, precision, timing. but i say luck is the biggest factor here. if you don't get the right 'tools', you will have a harder time beating it. that is why it is easier in some sessions and harder in others. still, it is very addictive and i enjoyed the game overall. it is very cute and charming, with nice art/graphics. but repetitively grindy too. i unlocked all cheevs but did not 100% the game. there are 2 endings for each hero, but that is just a paragraph or 2 of script. i do not know if 100%'ing will unlock anything new. you might have an easier time than i did, so ymmv as they say.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't really looking for this game, but since it had an interesting price and I could get it for a sweet price, I decided to give it a try. To be quite honest, I'm not quite the big fan of the roguelike genre, especially because that often translates to lots of grinding and frustration. Nonetheless, at least in this case, I don't think that it's so bad, especially because you can actually rely on your skills, rather than just dumb luckNow, is there a story? Who cares, it's not like the developers put that much effort into it, but I don't think there's anything wrong about that. You start with this warrior class type, and the more you advance, the more characters, accessories and skills you get to unlock. Each character has their own pros and cons, but in the end, I think it's fair to assume that depending on your luck concerning the items that you get to collect along the way, each individual playthrough could either be heaven or hellConcerning the gameplay, it's a combination of pinball, tower defense and RPG, I suppose. Each run is unique, so the maps are always randomly generated, except maybe for the "tables" (or playing fields), which all seem to follow some kind of standard pattern. There're three difficulty levels for each character, and if you're feeling like getting all the achievements, take a deep breath and good luckThe graphics are nice, the music gets old really quickly (considering that there's no diversity, which is a major problem in a game where you have to constantly grind) and although the sound effects aren't bad, they get annoying after a while (bell, I'm talking about you)Overall, it's an alright title to kill some time and I wish there were some other innovative types like that in the market

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game from a bundle, so I went in with no real expectation. Ended up playing it for almost 4 hours straight before starting to get a bit bored. All in all it was a fun experience, mashing digital pinball with some light rpg/roguelite elements. Instead of hitting bumpers and other targets for points, you're trying to kill a bunch of zombies before they reach your flippers and damage you. Can't say I've seen this format before, so props for originality.utSadly, the game doesn't offer a ton of replayability (yes, you can unlock items and characters, but it doesn't change a lot gameplay-wise). However, if you enjoy the concept of pinball and/or are looking for a fun, simple indie game to kill an afternoon or two with, you can't go too wrong with buying this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Zombie Rollerz was a pleasantly surprising pinball / RPG hybrid, with waaaay more depth than expected. Each level seems to be uniquely crafted, although of course the enemies and gameplay mechanics are shared.Whilst I only completed the first 2 chapters, there is definitely a lot of "brain off" fun to be had here. The levels were very easy, mostly due to the overwhelming amount of *stuff* happening at any time. You have 4 "powerups" activated by the XYAB buttons, a ball action activated by LB, and various effects happening on the dynamic board. This causes every level I played to be beatable by just firing the ball randomly and spamming powerups when available.However, there seems to be a pretty deep loadout system, with each ball powerup having multiple levels, and overworld with loot and puzzle levels, as well as enough variety to easily come back to the game over and over again.

_childDocuments_.review: Zombie Rollerz is a pinball roguelite. What sounds like an odd combination is actually a really fun game.In Zombie Rollerz you play as one of ten different characters and try to escape a zombie plague. The game is divided into two sections, the tile-based overworld map and the actual pinball tables.On the map you find different objects to interact with, gold, chests, shops but also zombies. Zombies block your way and touching them takes you to one of several randomly generated pinball tables of the game. Your goal in those is always the same, kill all zombies. Your pinball is your weapon, if it hits a zombie it will inflict damage. Direct hits directly from the flipper will do much more damage and may also activate additional effects depending on your ball type.You can have many different types of balls which are called ball modifiers. You always start with one that fits your character but you can get more if you collect four pinball fragments during your run, including balls from other characters. You can equip up to three different ball modifiers and the first one equipped also can use a special ability on a cooldown.Besides your pinball you also can equip an ultimate ability and three support abilites. These can do all kinds of stuff, they might launch fireballs, freeze enemies or give you another ball. Every modifier and every ability has up to five levels and on specific interactables on the map you can enhance your abilities. Additionally you can also find passive items that support you further and help you flesh out your build. Your character also levels over time, getting better stats and and new items for each level. There are four stats in the game that define your character, constitution gives you simply more HP, strength imrpoves phyiscal damage including direct hits with your pinball, intelligence enhances magical damage, generally used in abilites and luck improves chances for effects and the loot you get.The zombies in this game are your enemies, they come in many different forms but generally they try to reach your flippers to hurt you. You can push them back with the flippers but will take damage in return. You can also lose health if your pinball leaves the table but that only happens if you make a major mistake and even then it will do only a tiny bit of damage.It is important for the player to manage his helath during his run, luckily there are many ways to regain health. Potions can be found as loot ont he map or from battles, each enemy killed has also a tiny chance to drop a heart which heals exactly 1 HP. Having good crowd control abilites that slow or stun enemies can also help a lot.There are four chapters in the game, each chapter has a boss and the last one has a super strong final boss. Bosses require special strategies to beat and is a welcome change from the usual pinball hitting. The game also has a very straight forward unlock system. After each run you get points based on your performance, these points will automatically unlock the next items on your list. That way you can unlock new items, characters and abilites. There are also two special characters that you only unlock if you beat the game with two other specific characters.What I really like about this game is how different each of the characters is. While everyone uses the pinball to kill enemies, each one does in a special way. Your starting character, Burnjamin, does fire damage that burns enemies over time when they touch the ball. Rusty on the other hand goes for full physical assaults, smacking enemies wildy around or hitting them woith a sword. I find No 8 especially interesting, he has the passive ability to damage enemies while they move, so he has a crapton of displacement abilities.Whiel each character has access to all the items, some items are better on specific characters because of their passive abilites. Overall I find this game very entertaining, runs don't take very long which makes it a great casual game. The game offers three difficulties and the last one is really hard to beat, so you also can have a good challenge if you want. The tables might feel a little small compared to regular pinball games but this makes it easier for the roguelite formular to play many different tables without feeling fatigue.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely pleasant surprise this game was! The start is a bit rough, but progression gives you access to objectively better items, and playing becomes smoother. Very recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, it is such a great combination of genres that in my wildest dreams didn't expected to happen. But it did happened! That "shoot em up" and "zombie defence" tags are just a layer to the core game mechanics, and that is that this game is rogue like pinball. You got a map where there are random events, different paths to take (but only one is right way to the bosses), trinkets, items and spells to take, different balls and attacks for balls to chose, many buffs and curses, and random enemies that you can "fight". At that point, game changes to pinball. It have nice graphics and physics, lovely artstyle, happy music, cute characters and dialogs, many unlockables and RNG moments, and most important thing - it is really fun to play. You can play it in small sessions and in short loop, as any rogue-like should play. So, if you like pinball and also love rogue-like games, this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: My first impressions video: Zombie Rollerz is unlike any roguelite you've played and also any pinball game. It fuses these two genres in a way that's really cool and really fun, but also really grindy. You'll pick one of several different character classes, all of which have their own traits and unique personalities. Each level is the game is a pinball table of sorts, but with their own designs, obstacles and waves of enemies. The battles can be pretty intense and fast-paced, as you juggle the flippers and your various abilities. The first couple of worlds won't be too tricky, but it ramps up fast.Like most roguelites, there's a lot of things to unlock, which will gradually improve your characters and make subsequent runs a bit easier. There are several additional characters to unlock as well. Unfortunately, the grind is massive and that's my one real complaint with this game. It feels like a title that was originally designed to be a free-to-play mobile release with microtransactions, but was then turned into a full price game and removed the microtransactions, but not the grind. Given that this launched on Apple TV, I think that's a safe bet. To unlock everything, you'll be playing a lot of runs and spending a lot of hours. I feel like this could have been pared back and still allowed for a game you could spend a lot of time with, without a grind so long that it feels like you're going to get a prompt with "Best Value!" at some point.I'm a huge fan of both roguelites and pinball and Zombie Rollerz does a great job of mixing both in a really fun way. You just might have to spend more time with it than needed in order to see everything.

name: Saturnalia
detailed_description: A third-person horror adventure where you play as four characters, experiencing an intergenerational storyline tied to the haunting traditions of an ancient village in Sardinia, Italy, a region rich with unique folklore… The village itself is an elaborate maze with no two iterations being precisely the same—you will have to explore and solve the mysteries of the game largely unguided. Die, and watch the village reconfigure itself into a new form. Solve puzzles and open shortcuts to new areas with tools and items you find along the way, unlocking every piece of the story with different characters, each with its own power and suited for another aspect of exploration and investigation. Game Features The village structure changes each time all your characters die Discover characters' special abilities, use tools and consumables to open shortcuts Keep narrative and puzzle progress across game-overs (roguelite) Manage your supply of matches to help your sight and solve puzzles Non-linear progression, dynamic and adaptive narrative Investigate the ritual at the heart of the game and use what you find to stop it Puzzles deeply integrated with the game world and narrative (not abstract) Artwork and animations inspired by stop-motion and rotoscoping film techniques Info A playthrough takes approximately 10 hours, leading to one of several potential endings.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a horror game that is not just about "shoot the evil guys" or "find the red key to open the red door".Saturnalia leaves you hopeless in a surreal maze, surrounded by the mystery that unravel before you. Don't be fooled by the non-AAA graphic style, the game will get you and the soundtrack will shake you.
_childDocuments_.name: Saturnalia

_childDocuments_.review: There's a good game here, but its being held back by very rough movement and camera. Character gets stuck on nothing frequently, and while I appreciate the dark atmosphere, not being able to see three feet in front of me, even with matches lit is a bit excessive. Judging from these other reviews, I think there is an audience for this kind of game. _childDocuments_.name: Saturnalia

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fresh take on the survival horror genre, that creates its thrilling surreal atmosphere by mixing industrialized rural area in Sardinia, where yet the spirit of ancient paganism dwells. From the very start everything signals that we are very much on our own here, with only one non playable character that is not trying to hurt us in some way. The gameplay loop is relatively simple, but given the game length it doesn't get too frustrating. You're looking for clues, which in turn open up new leads to the new ones and bring you closer to unravelling this cursed place's mystery (La creatura doesn't let you do it in peace, though). The game lets you test your deduction skills and rid yourself of explicit goals, which help a lot in progressing through the game, but I played on the standard difficulty and can only imagine that this option would be more frustrating, albeit much more engaging immersively. The procedural generation of the map gives you a feeling that the village itself is a living breathing organism (don't put your ear too close to the walls) that paves and twists its narrow streets specifically to make you get lost in it, some "impossible" dead ends and rooms kinda add to this feeling.I wouldn't say that individual character's stories are top notch, if you consider them separately, but it starts to make more sense and engage with you, as a player more, as you start unravelling the tangles: they've gathered here to rid themselves of their trauma (and survive, hopefully) which leads to uncovering the wicked side of a seemingly calm village and its denizens.I hate and am bad at writing my opinions on anything, but Saturnalia stands as an exception, because I think it deserves more attention for not being a blatant copy of some classics of the genre, having charming visuals and uncanny atmosphere.E quando che menoti pensi, nel senoti vien a finire,bisogna morire.
_childDocuments_.name: Saturnalia

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful Horror Game with great Atmosphere and Soundtrack. Even though the controls were a bit clunky at first i got used to them really quick and the game is a blast after that (still geting lost in the village nonetheless...). Im also really loving the Story and its Mysteries so far. Can't wait to figure out the rest of the Story and hopefully not get cought by the Monster.
_childDocuments_.name: Saturnalia

_childDocuments_.review: The best horror game I've played this year. The game is quite ambitious and despite some minor jank it manages to come together masterfully. Unlike a lot of other slasher horror games (where you get chased around by a single enemy), getting caught is not the end, as you have 4 characters you can play as and at least early on there are opportunities to rescue the others. But that's not all, even if all your characters get caught, the town simply gets reshuffled and you lose some vital items from your inventory - a big enough setback to build tension into getting caught, without having to replay the exact same sequence as before, keeping that tension going.Come for that, stay for the great Italian giallo story with some of the most interesting characters. The devs also knew where to focus their polish - lots of minor details make the town feel uninviting and isolating. Would highly recommend playing in Detective mode - outside of one of two sequences that kind of require you to stumble on the right info with the right characters, the game gives you enough clues to actually investigate the town freely.OST rocks, too.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like it. This is a fun horror game with a really cool setting and time-period (Sardinian-Italian Catholic 1980's). The gameplay is similar to many horror games (e.g., a door is locked, find a tool to open it), with the twist that, if your characters die, you keep the progress made on your objectives, but lose the tools, and the city map procedurally regenerates. A big part of the game is feeling/being lost in crowded, Italian alleys, looking for an objective while being hunted by the antagonist. The characters each have a story mystery to discover, and a valid plot reason for being in the situation they are in.I've had a few stuck-in-the-wall bugs, that required clicking the "kill my characters and start the next loop in the city" button. (You can't switch between the 4 characters unless you meet one face-to-face in a safe zone) It's a little frustrating but not fatal, because the game loop is designed around you losing your characters and re-building the city fairly often. It does mean the hardcore option to play with one set of lives is probably a no-go.Overall, a very enjoyable, beautiful, and tense horror game about 10-15 hours long. I've been waiting the long year for it to come to Steam, and I'm glad I played it.

The controls and camera can be somewhat janky, and there were a few bugs. But despite these issues, the game managed to keep me hooked.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Saturnalia while on sale and started it on a whim not expecting much, but I quickly became engrossed in the experience. It is easily one of the most fascinating games I've ever played, but it will only appeal to a certain audience. This isn't a game for everyone, which makes it tough to give it a broad recommendation.You control four different characters, each with their own backstories, goals, and special abilities. You'll spend most of your time exploring the small town of Sardinia, collecting clues and piecing together the mystery of the village. Despite the town's small size, it is deceptively difficult to navigate (by design), and I found myself constantly getting lost in its labyrinthine streets and wondering how to get back to certain locations.You will also have to contend with the 'beast' of the village. Roaming the streets is a masked figure that will pursue you if spotted. There is no combat in the game, so you will have no choice but to run and/or hide from the beast. If caught, it will take the apprehended character and confine them to a certain location until another character can free them. If all four playable characters are caught and killed, then the game resets with all clues and shortcuts still unlocked, but all consumable items and tools reset to their original locations, and even the layout of the village itself is shifted.The presentation for me was a mixed bag. I didn't exactly love the art style of the game, but I adjusted to it and give the developers credit for having a unique looking game. The sound design was good for the most part, with the standout highlight being the creepy sound effect that plays whenever the beast is getting close. One thing to note though, is that this game is extremely dark. Even with the in-game brightness settings cranked up to max, sometimes I could barely see even a few feet in front of my character. I believe this is by design however to keep the tension high and keep the player disoriented while exploring, but it can be frustrating at times.All that being said, even after nearly 10 hours with this game and completing it at 100% with an S rank, I still feel like I don't know exactly what makes this game tick. This can be seen as both a positive and negative, but I think it's the main reason why I was so intrigued by it and still continue to think about it after completing it. Not a whole lot is explained to the player, and even after I felt like I had much of it figured out, it seemed like it changed the rules on me. I think there is a point in the game (either based on time passed or progression) where it just simply gets more difficult. The beast will pursue you more persistently, my characters were instantly dying when caught instead of being captured, the sound cues seemed to change (and were possibly messing with me?), and I could have sworn there was more than one beast roaming the streets (perhaps my 'killed' characters were now pursuing me?). This is all just speculation on my part and I could be completely wrong, but there's so little information out there about this game and there is no resource explaining these mechanics. I'm not even sure that these were intentional game design decisions and not just glitches! But, although it can be frustrating at times, it gives this game such a mystique that is rarely found in video games where the rules of the game are so often made abundantly clear.So would I recommend this game? It really depends. If you appreciate more of a 'slow burn' horror game that is light on action, then there is definitely something to enjoy here. The game can be completed in less than 10 hours, and I don't feel like there is much replay value once you've unlocked everything, although I suppose a case could be made with the procedurally generated village and multiple endings. I am certainly glad I played it though and would definitely like to revisit it sometime in the future once I've forgotten the bulk of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Saturnalia

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended to rogue-lite and horror enjoyers. Personally not a big fan of games where you're chased by somenthing, but I really appreciated the music, the graphics and the general atmosphere. The map isn't huge, but the sharp graphics (especially palaces), the narrow passages and the contrasting colors generate a unique labirinthic sensation, very important in this kind of games. There's a good balance between the chasing moments and the exploration/investigation phases as well. At some point I got lost, but I was still able to find important things and continue the varius tasks, thanks to a good level design and a very helpful "conceptual map" about all the clues, objects and points of interest I found and how they connect to each other. The only little flaws are the controls not always immediate and a few bugs, usually involving a little compenetration that leads to getting stuck (fortunately you can free yourself in a short time). Last but not least well done to all the Santa Ragione team for the attention paid to details, a praiseworthy job.
_childDocuments_.name: Saturnalia

_childDocuments_.review: You have never played any game like this.While most or all of the pieces are known and recognizable (e.g. running and hiding from a monster you can't hurt like in Alien Isolation and the Amnesia games before), the mix of all the mechanics, the story and the aesthetics is fully unique, and far more uncomfortable to play than 99% of the games classified as "horror".
_childDocuments_.name: Saturnalia

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best survival horror experiences I've ever had. I don't know how they made a game so kind difficulty-wise while also making it feel like an impossible feat to beat at times. The stress-pacing this game offers is absolutely incredible.I think horror games require a level of difficulty that feels unfair in order to push the anxieties that the characters would be feeling through to the player--but that usually makes the game not fun to play (think Silent Hill 4 [aka the best silent hill]).Saturnalia has done something special. Something about the game feels unfair, while at the same time being incredibly kind to the player. I was stressed out about my character's safety, even though the game has systems in place to make sure you don't get caught in an almost impossible loop of frustrating inventory management and health items. Anyone can beat this game, and it only takes 10 hours. The game ends before it lets you get tired of any of its mechanics.It's also a detective game with a difficulty slider that controls how much the game will spell out hints to the player. I'd recommend the default setting for most, but if you're someone who already has a lot of patience for solving puzzles, feel free to turn it up. You might miss out on some of the emotional pacing of the game if you lower the difficulty below the standard.You're missing out if you don't try this game.Take a deep breath. You're supposed to get lost. It's supposed to be dark. You're supposed to die. You can do it. The game respects your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Saturnalia

_childDocuments_.review: I hated how this game makes me feel. There was tension but the gameplay and visibility are so handicapping on a meta level that the frustration outweighs any intrigue or desire to climb over the wall of initially learning the game. Even a brightness adjustment on an accessibility menu would probably have been enough to make this game playable.I'm not new to the horror genre and even love a lot 90s horror games, so I can forgive the terrible graphics to an extent (although in this case it feels more a stylistic choice to make the game look like a late 90s computer remake of Aha's Take on Me Video), but the graphics shouldn't be the most significant challenge in the game. There may be an audience for this game. It could have a compelling story. And honestly it feels like it could work well with either better graphics or even older graphics (like say an SNES game). But as it stands it's cumbersome, punishing and not worth the learning curve.
_childDocuments_.name: Saturnalia

_childDocuments_.review: this game would maybe make sense if it took place before electricity and flashlights existed, let alone maps and smartphones. however, it somehow relies entirely on the premise that your only light source is a tiny amount of matches and that you would not even have so much as a paper map, which is absurd and completely ruins any sense of realism. practically everyone has a flashlight built into their smartphone, which also has a GPS map. i personally never travel anywhere without both a paper map and a small powerful flashlight, in addition to my smartphone. i hate media like this where the entire premise relies on completely idiotic and unrealistic conditions to create a horror atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Saturnalia

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game through in first person instead of 3rd which is a great touch that they added that. Absolutely fantastic little horror game. The sound design and environmental sounds are great! The story is provocative and keeps you guessing as to what comes with the next clue. I really enjoyed the different characters abilities and ways to play. Only con: the light radius is quite small, for me it was fine and I got used to it however some may feel slightly claustrophobic at times. Maybe a 10% increase would help this feeling but I understand the atmosphere building and horror of the dark.TLDR: Buy this game if you have any interest in horror games. If you struggle with maps or directions be ready to stop at the in game maps a lot XD

_childDocuments_.review: A hesitant recommendation. There were some incredibly frustrating parts, but overall this was a unique horror game that I'm glad I played.I think one of the keys to a good horror game is a lack of information, and Saturnalia excels at that, both intentionally and unintentionally. A lot of the game mechanic feel inexact, and I never fully understood how some things behaved. The procedurally-generated town you explore, despite being quite small, manages to feel very confusing and disorienting to navigate. There is a certain terror of its own to wandering similar-looking hallways and getting hopelessly turned around in the dark.Most of the issues I had with the game resolve around its sole obstacle, the Creature that stalks you everywhere. How it's supposed to work is that randomly as you're exploring, you hear the sound cue that it's close, and you must either run away or find somewhere to hide until it passes. Already this concept is annoying at best, but the AI of the Creature makes it so much worse. More than once it suddenly appeared out of thin air right next to me and caught me before I had the chance to react. Frequently it would get stuck in the wall and not despawn, or block doorways and refuse to move. And the sound cue never seemed to work correctly, as it wouldn't be associated with its proximity - I would be clear on the other side of town and not being chased at all yet it would still get louder and louder like it was right behind me. I wish I could've relied on the sound cue more, since when I'm in a dark maze and can only see a few feet in front of myself, I really need to know which direction the Creature is coming from so I don't run right into it while attempting to flee.Other than everything involving the Creature, though, I really enjoyed this game. The Sardinian town you explore is a super unique setting for a game, and I loved how it felt like one giant puzzlebox. You pull away at clues and work towards your mission objective, uncovering more and more in what at first seems like a small and empty area. The story and lore aren't super deep, but they're interesting enough that I wanted to see it through to the end. The reshuffling of the town touted in the description isn't as big a factor as it seems, but I liked that there are interesting consequences for death other than just reloading a save. Even before getting a game over, if a character is caught, you take control of another character and have the chance to track them down and rescue them. It's simple but a neat idea.All in all a mixed bag of a game, but certainly a unique experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Saturnalia

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game, love the story behind it and that it's not only some run and hide simulator! The characters really grew on me, and the artstyle is truely unique and beautiful. Sound design also mega nice :)Had some problems here and there with maneuvering or getting progress, but their discord contains a lot of helpful spoilers and advice!
_childDocuments_.name: Saturnalia

_childDocuments_.review: The town's spooky vibe, which keeps getting creepier with each secret uncovered, is undoubtedly a standout feature in Saturnalia. I wish we could spend more time exploring during the day to connect better with the main characters and get to feel the day-night contrast. While I enjoyed the different character perspectives, a deeper dive into their backgrounds would definitely add more depth. Reading their thoughts and feelings as we progress was the most intriguing part for me – too bad it was so scarce. This game has a lot of potential, and with some more work, it could truly become a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: I am probably going to write something elsewhere on Saturnalia, so I have little to say here without spoiling what I may write elsewhere. I will say, however, that this game is a little masterpiece, both in the genre of survival horror and more generally. It is both gorgeous and terrifying, though it may not meet everyone's expectations. Buy it, play it, tell your friends about it.

_childDocuments_.review:
A game inspired and heavily influenced by the folklore of Sardinia, Italy (a region rich with unique traditions and culture) where you play as four characters, experiencing a deeply connected storyline that ties back to the haunting traditions of an ancient village.

Die, and watch the village reconfigure itself into a new form. Solve puzzles and open shortcuts to new areas with tools and items you find along the way, unlocking every piece of the story with different characters, each with its own power and suited for another aspect of exploration and investigation.

With a limited supply of matches to light your way and darkness encroaching, can you find your way through the fog to reveal the truth? Or will you be engulfed by the secrets this town doesn't want you to know?

name: The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners
detailed_description: Tourist Edition Tourist Edition Get the Tourist Edition of The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners and you'll receive three unique weapon recipes, collectible voodoo dolls, the game's soundtrack, and The Supernatural Skeptic's Guide to New Orleans companion piece. Aftershocks Update Aftershocks Update You’ve decided the fate of the Reserve, but the story is far from over. Throughout New Orleans, supply caches once thought destroyed by the Tourist’s actions are washing up across the flooded city, and Tower and Reclaimed alike will do everything they can to secure them. If you wish to get your hands on the remnants of the Reserve, supplies and secrets alike, you must return to old stomping grounds revived with more dangers, more activity, and plenty more walkers. You’ve shaken New Orleans throughout your journey, but can you survive the aftershocks that follow? Take on new post-campaign missions that will put your survival skills to the limit. New and unexpected challenges await in the most unlikely places. A new expansion of the Tourist’s story; experience the chaos that is post-Reserve New Orleans and show its residents that you’re here to stay. Face all the dangers of both the Tower and Reclaimed to find the supply caches that await you. High risk, higher reward! Meatgrinder Update Meatgrinder Update The bells have tolled. The dead are swarming. And you’re the only living thing in sight. It’s time for you to face The Meatgrinder. In this new update to The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners, you’ll be able to battle the undead in ways you never have before. Face relentless waves of walkers in The Trial, a special mode with all game weapons unlockable, stamina and health boosts and where your wits, skills, and whatever you can craft in the midst of the chaos will be your staunchest allies. Choose your arena, score big points through creative kills, and see how long you can survive. Do you want a more casual tour of New Orleans? Try out the new Story Mode difficulty option for the campaign for a new take on your undead adventure. Finally, prove yourself as an apocalyptic samurai with the new katana weapon aspect: ‘Absolution’. If you are going to slice and dice those who dare challenge you, you might as well do it in style, and forgive their sins. All this and more await you in The Meatgrinder. About the Game LIVE The Walking Dead Saints & Sinners is a game unlike any other in The Walking Dead universe. Every challenge you face and decision you make is driven by YOU. Fight the undead, scavenge through the flooded ruins of New Orleans, and face gut-wrenching choices for you and the other survivors. Live The Walking Dead's dark drama in your own skin.​ Survive YOUR Way A new way to live survival horror. With the living, dead, disease and famine as constant threats, you have countless ways to tackle these dangers. Face the undead guns blazing or learn all the ways to sneak and hide among them. Take on missions from different factions and survivors to earn valuable resources. Risk life and limb to protect those in need or brutally murder anyone who stands in your way. See how your choices affect the people of New Orleans, and learn to live with the consequences. A New, Brutal Story New Orleans is at war. The living are not just fighting the dead, but also inflicting pain and brutality upon each other. As bodies pile up between warring factions, whispers spread of a long-lost mystery in the city that could turn the tide of the war. Will you be able to survive while caught in the middle of this conflict? Can you unravel the mystery that is behind it all? The fate of the city and its survivors rests in your hands.​ A Vast World To Explore in VR Crafting, exploration, freedom of choice and visceral combat make this a deep, 15+ hour game built for VR. Cut down both the dead and the living with an arsenal of melee, ranged and makeshift weapons, all physics-based objects you can realistically wield. Knock walker heads clear off and rip out weapons impaled in their skulls. Creep through ruined streets and creole mansions to scavenge for supplies and secrets. Scale the sides of buildings, cars, and walls to ambush enemies from above or make a quick escape.

name: Wintermoor Tactics Club
detailed_description: Wintermoor Tactics Club is a story about surviving high school, with gameplay inspired by tactics RPGs and visual novels. It was hard enough for Alicia at the famed Wintermoor Academy before it erupted into a snowball war! Now her club's only hope is to transform from nerdy nobodies into fantasy heroes. Unravel a reality-bending mystery. Test your strategic mettle against an avalanche of colorful characters. And don't forget to make friends! Features Unlock your Potential : Discover the power of 7 playable characters and dozens of unlockable upgrades across more than 40 battles. Explore the School : Get to know Wintermoor in visual novel-inspired gameplay. Break down the walls between high school cliques such as the Psychic Detectives and Young Monarchists. Make New Friends : Write tabletop campaigns to help students overcome their personal problems, and discover their fantasy selves as your club grows.
