_childDocuments_.review: Wintermoor, at it's core, is a strategy-lite RPG with a "Dungeons and Dragons in college" setting.  There are no levels to grind, but you can complete both side-quests as well as "challenge levels" to unlock additional gear for your players, tuning their abilities to be more in line with what strategies you employ.  You'll only field three team members at a time, but which three you use can change how you confront any particular challenge.  The challenges are simple enough that you probably won't find yourself banging your head on them, and since combat follows set rules you can more easily tailor your strats.  For example, there is no random change of someone hitting or missing...you'll always hit (and so will they).  Some monsters will always target the closest person, or the person with the lowest HP, or the person that last attacked them.  All of this information can be viewed in combat as well, and since there is no time limit to the turns you can really take your time.  That being said, don't worry about having to have the PERFECT strategy to progress.  Although there are "scores" you can obtain from various levels, you can always replay a level later for a higher score.  And there is a LOT of wiggle room for success...you can make a less-than-optimal decision and still succeed with no problems.This game has a LOT of heart and I really enjoyed it.  It isn't too deep, but can touch on issues such as isolation, pressure to succeed, and the need to find acceptance.  I enjoyed it, and got about 15 hours out of it while doing subquests but not aiming for perfect scores.  Even not on sale, this meets my "dollar per hour" budget factor, so this game really checked all the boxes for me.Give this game a try if you are looking for something casual, tactical, wholesome, or enjoy Dungeons and Dragons references.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable game set in a New England boarding school about how  C&C and friendship can save the world.At its core, Wintermoor Tactics Club is actually a puzzle game wearing a tactical RPG skin. There are some light "side-quests" which involve fleshing out the backgrounds of the different characters to gain equipment, but for the most part the main focus of the gameplay is the tactical RPG combat. It's fairly simple stuff, although the game does add more challenge in the form of medals you earn for having certain statistics under par or up to a minimum amount for the map. These medals don't have to be earned in one go, but it can feel pretty rewarding for some maps when you manage to meet the requirements.The game is just long enough to not wear out its welcome, which is a plus for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This game thinks outside of the box in a lot of ways, with the visual novel, top-down rpg, and tactics-based combat each contributing to the story in a unique way. The writing and sense of humor are excellent--I was as compelled by the eccentric characters and the jokes as I was by the combat. Though the side quests can be too many all at once some times (if you're the kind of person who has to have all the abilities), at least they are interesting, and overall the game is paced well into nice hour-long chapter chunks.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: There are very few games where I read all of the text the characters speak, but this is one of them. The characters are just so much fun! There are serious moments and deeply sincere moments, but for the most part, the story of this game is just fun! The gameplay is pretty standard turn-based-tactics, and not that difficult, but the enemies are fun and the settings are interesting. If you want a _very_ well made game, that had a lot of love put into it, that you can beat in a weekend, and that isn't overly difficult, this is your game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Pros-Nice art-style-Good controls (can be played completely with mouse)-Solid Performance-Nice balance of game-play. The core is a turn based, grid based combat system with a range of different characters and moves. Outside of battle there is also some basic point and click style quests in order to unlock new moves and progress the story. Not too much dept but all very enjoyable and keeps things interesting.-A decent amount of characters and skills.-You can't really get stuck or bogged down since after 3 failed attempts on a battle you can choose to play in no fail mode which means your characters can't die. Some of the battles can be quite tricky so this was really appreciated.Cons- The difficultly seemed kind of up and down and not linear. The final boss fights were considerably easier than some of the early ones in my opinion. Maybe some people will find this a pro,- No voice acting unfortunately (I think for a game like this it could have really brought some extra immersion.)-Occasionally after starting the game the saves won't load. Clicking the continue button or selecting an individual save and clicking load does nothing, not even an error. Usually just restarting the game resolves the problem but there is a discussion in the forums where some people had to jump through a few extra hoops.-While there is a wide range of character and skills, arguably there is only a few realistic choices since some characters do considerably more AOE damage than others. Granted there can be some balancing in terms of the characters hit-points but at the end of the day you will likely pick characters that can inflict the most damage to the most enemies at once.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: As a tactics game, it's really good. It's open to all sorts of ideas for how to tackle different situations, and allows you to make really good choices to best suit the situation.The story, world, characters, and all around flavor of the game are Heaven Sent. This is one of the funniest, most interesting, most heartfelt games I have EVER played.If tactical battles aren't you're thing, at least play it for the story. But I really do like the battle system.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know what to expect from this game, but looking at the scores it got, I gave it a go.As a fan of TRPGs, I really enjoyed the gameplay, and the story was really nice! I would say it is a great point of entry for players to get into the genre.If there is one weakness to this game, is that it has little replay value, since the battles are always the same. But it makes up with lots of heart and soul in the story and characters!I greatly recommend this game to anyone who is into TRpGs or Table Top RPGs like D&D!
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Charming game. Well put together. The gameplay is reminiscent of Final Fantasy Tactics, but the game is mainly a vehicle for telling a story (not a bad thing).I did feel frustrated some times because there seemed to be so much more than expected. Me, being the type of player that likes to explore everything, found myself wishing things would just get on with it. On the flip side, it does mean that if you explore, you get "rewarded". Lots of non-critical conversations, for example.Strategy-wise, it wasn't very difficult, save for a few places (let's say, "Fruit Bat Mastery"). Although I do tend to play strategic and tactical games, I don't think the game was designed to be overly strategic. It even comes with a "cannot lose" mode, which I assume was for people who wanted to enjoy the story more. And, as I said, it was a vehicle to tell a story. It also seems quite polished. And the soundtrack was pretty good, even though it was limited in scope.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Actually i would only recommend if you do not want to stress yourselves over complicated strategy and story. There is story and strategy in this game but on a lighter tone.  On the other hand there isnt much different types of enemies and towards the end, the final character did not get much screen time compared to earlier characters but you do know how to use that character for sure.  Is developed by a small group so i guess is alright game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful little game. I think it might have been better served if it were in the 8 hour range instead of 10-12 because I did find it dragged a little in the second act, but I loved the art and story. The combat isn't revolutionary, but I liked how intuitive it was. The game also adds characters and abilities at a steady clip, which added complexity after the standard paladin/mage/rogue start. The combat isn't especially hard (with the notable exception of one of the final challenge missions), but getting max rating on each encounter is a legitimately tough task for those who are looking for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: A charming game that may pull at your heart strings, but probably won't require as many tactics as the name implies.Wintermoor Tactics Club is a combination of the combat style of Into the Breach with the narrative style of Final Fantasy Tactics Advanced. It is very whimsical, and addressed a wide array of coming-to-age stories woven into a moderately interesting plot line. The combat is similar to Into the Breach where your actions have fully predictable outcomes, and you always know what you opponents will be doing. Unfortunately, where Into the Breach turns this into a deep challenge with tough decisions, Wintermoor Tactics Club puts you into pretty easy encounters where the hardest part is making sure you max out your rating for the battle.That being said, I still think that this game is worth playing. The story arcs for each character is short enough to make the game move along briskly, but just long enough that their stories don't feel incredibly reductive or stereotypical. I think this is a great game for younger kids as there really isn't adult content, and each chapter has a fairly strong moral to take away from it. Best of all, it does so in a way that does not feel entirely forced.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this. The mechanics are fairly simple, but there's a lot of opportunity for experimentation and creativity in your tactical choices. The par grading system is a cool way to allow battles to remain manageable while also rewarding effective strategies. I had hopes the story would sweep a little wider, but it's a sweet narrative and does take a few fun twists.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: A feel good story, great script, and gameplay that felt like a breath of fresh air. In terms of gameplay, the things that I loved were:- Characters that had very distinctly unique traits and upgrades- Stage rankings- the stages themselves- revert featureEach character had their own set of equipable upgrades that made a lot of sense and complemented their traits really well. One could also think of many ways the different characters with their personal upgrades could complement each other in different situations, and winning a stage easily because you found a good combination, was very satisfying.This is the first tactics game I played that ranked the way you played each stage. I felt that this incentivized the careful planning of each stage -- which characters to use, which upgrades, where to place them in the battlefield, how to make use of the battlefield landscape, etc. I think the fun thing about tactics games is seeing how your preparations and planning turn out, and this game made it very fulfilling.Each stage felt very well thought out. The combination of enemies and their traits, their placements, and the landscape just seem to "make a lot of sense" in that there often seems to be a certain character or a certain upgrade, or combination of characters and upgrades that would make clearing each stage a piece of cake. However, finding that best way is up to the player.Another plus for me is that you can easily revert a turn or restart a battle if your initial plan doesn't turn out well. This makes it easier to learn the best strategy to clear a stage.All in all a very satisfying tactics experience. Stage rankings really stood out to me, and I'm not sure why not more tactics games employ the same feature. Other tactics games can learn a lot from Wintermoor Tactics Club, in my opinion. In terms of story, script, art, and music, I can tell you that this game left a mark on me. If your into "feel-good" stuff, I think it will be the same for you. It was my "picker-upper" for the last few weeks, and it's a bit sad that I finished it already. I'll definitely play it again--I have some locked achievements left as an "excuse" to continue playing--but my real reason is that I just want to experience it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: A good story and some decent combat within a very simple system. I like that it runs smoothly on my low end device and that I can do back (after 22 hours of play and completion of the storyline) and play again to unlock additional achievements. Story adds some fun 80s nostalgia and sends a message of inclusion. The protagonist finds a way to reach out to others despite differences in the student population. It's a positive message that doesn't come across as a back-to-school special but as a genuine, straightforward acknowledgement about how to interact like a decent human being.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I would recommend this game, but mostly for the cute point and click adventure.I bought the game hoping for some really good tactical battles (I really liked Into the Breach and keep trying to find a new FFT) but was never really drawn into them. They are not terrible but a bit shallow.I did finish the game though, which I rarely do, and the story made me feel good. I like friendship!
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Wintermoor Tactics Club is a delightful and charming surprise.  I enjoyed the tactical/puzzle gameplay well enough but the real star of the game was smart and witty writing, wrapped in a warm blanket of quirky yet human characters.  This game had me biting my nails in suspense during the final battle, laughing out loud at the absurd 'where are they now' sequence', then had me tearing up when the story closed, having come full circle.  All within 5 minutes.  I also appreciate that the developers created a hooking mystery, inclusive and diverse characters, and engaging gameplay without resorting to blood, violence, sex, cursing, crude humor, etc.  I am fans of those things but it was a nice break to settle in with a game that had no issue being wholesome and thoroughly entertaining at the same time.  This is an easy recommend to anyone who enjoys tactics games or a good story.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: I had quite a bit of fun playing this game. It's been a while since I could just play through a game and enjoy it and still be challenged. I loved the story and lore in this game it was not what I was expecting and that made it that much more fun. If you are looking for a tactics game please try this out. Its not the same as most of the genre out there but its definitely worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: The tactical parts are genuinely interesting, but good lord there is a *lot* of busywork between them clicking from room to room fetching things to progress the frankly unengaging plot. The main gang of characters are all fairly fun to spend time with, but everything about the main conflict they're involved in is extremely thin soup. Not for the impatient, but the good parts are good. Recommended, with caveats.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: A cute Visual Novel/Tactics homage to 80's D&D nerds. The art and writing is fantastic, and while the tactics elements are a little simplistic, the game is short enough that it does not overstay its welcome. Most of the characters are likable and bounce off the protagonist well, which makes for funny and kinetic dialogue.If you are looking for a FF Tactics style game, you are going to rather disappointed. But Wintermoor stands well when taken on it's own merits.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy turn-based tactical RPGs and feel like playing something a little more lighthearted for a little under 20 hours, this game is definitely for you. It is a true love letter to tabletop RPG fans, and the story, although not as complex as some classic RPGs, has a pretty unique setting and is so well-put together that you'll end up knowing every NPC by name and understanding why they are so important for the plot, which delivers a message about empathy and belonging in a sweet and heartwarming fashion.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: More of a tabletop puzzle game than a traditional tactics RPG. You probably spend more time reading than fighting (which is good if you want a lite visual novel). It's a little slow to start and I'm not sure how useful all the different upgrades are, but you battles will give you a good think. The writing is endearing and ending wraps everything up nicely.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Visual novel with some turn-based tactical battle elements. I love the theme, casual high school club tactics battle.Very well-written story, good writing. All likeable and somewhat complex characters with their own personalities and styles. Tactical battle can be challenging especially during the mastery missions, but everything can be nulled by choosing the option to add more HP, or to engage visual novel mode. The upgrades are interesting; you sometimes need to choose your characters and upgrades to suit your next battle.I like how quickly you can restart a battle and have 2 turn resets. Highly recommended, especially if you like casual style tactics
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the games that makes you go "I wish there are more games like this!" The gameplay is simple but provide enough challenge to keep one engaged with a good story that go along with it. The diversity of the characters and their play styles are worth noting too, it's fun getting to know them. Overall, a really chill tactical game, suitable for just kicking back, relax and enjoy some story telling.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely game! It's an interesting take on a Tactical RPG. The game is about 12-17 hours and worth a look if you like TRPGs, TTRPGs, or early 80's nostalgia.The game is a management light system like Fae Tactics. No healing, only 2-4 actions per character. The combat can get a little dull after a certain point, but once you get to mid game, you get a bit more customization and characters.As the character list grows, each character gets more interesting. The game has the best use of D&D as a central plot device I've seen. Through the main character you get the chance to build a custom campaign for new party members to help them overcome their own personal issues. It's very sweet.The pacing can sometimes drag, especially as it relates to side quests, but some of NPCs are quite fun.The main character, Alicia, is a black girl and one of the main conflicts is her wrestling with that identity. These parts of the story are written well and tie into the greater theme of identity that colors the rest of the game.Overall, this game is highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed playing this game.  A relaxing turn based strategy that isn't very hard but has enough hero and enemy variety to keep things interesting and make you think some especially if you are trying to get max rank.  Didn't need it but it was nice that it was forgiving and story continues without max rank.  A quirky and interesting story and you can see the developers spent some time polishing everything which made it a smooth playthrough.  As others have noted, you do have to walk back and forth for several quests to advance the story along but it's always clear what to do next.  Some of the achievements you'd never know how to get without spoilers and do require a second playthrough but it was not hard to speed run a second time to get the missing ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly one of the most surprising games I have ever played. I honestly didn't think much about it, I went into it thinking that the story was going to be somewhat silly but pretty throwaway but I could enjoy some tactics gameplay and I was fine with that. BOY was I wrong. The tactics part was right, one of the most enjoyable tactics games I've ever played, but the story and characters just knocked it out of the park - well-written and likeable characters and a wonderfully enjoyable story. If you're on the fence about this - get it, even if you're not on the fence about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most feel-good wholesome games that I've played in a long time.  I find it unbelievable that this game is not more popular, I would definitely call it a hidden gem. Gameplay wise, it's a perfect blend of visual novel, point-and-click adventure, and tactical rpg all rolled up into one.  As a visual novel and adventure game the game is oozing with charm and wit and is guaranteed to make you feel nostalgic for tabletop gaming, or high school, or probably both. The tactical combat has a really good ramp-up in difficulty so that if you're new to the genre you couldn't ask for a better introduction. It starts off nice and simple, so if you play a chapter or two of the game and are feeling "bored" then fear not, it gets more interesting the more you progress. Some of the optional encounters can be tricky and will take some time to to puzzle out the best way to approach them.To play through all of the content and obtain 86% of the steam achievements I ended up spending 20 hours on it.  If you just want to do the main content then it will probably run you closer to 10-12 hours.  Either way, I cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This is an awesome casual strategy game with a lot of plot, characters to interact with, bonus quests, etc. Lots of party composition options and equipment. The story is very enjoyable, especially to table-top gamers. (but anyone will enjoy) Don't worry about getting stuck and unable to progress because there are various ways to customize difficulty so you can always move on, so the game respects your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews but this game absolutely captured me. It's really not very often I just play a game start to finish as soon as I find the time but I played this in like 2 days no issue. If you're looking for a charming set of characters (which expands as you play, my favourite turned up just a chapter before the end), some really solid parodying of D&D or just interesting tactical combat, Wintermoor has it all.Visual Novel is definitely a great descriptor, you do spend most of your time chatting with people and doing mini fetch quest style things for them (although some story elements like creating the campaigns you play through are particularly interesting) but it does such a good job of making everyone feel real. If you are in it for the tactical gameplay explicitly there's plenty of challenge in the achievement hunting as well.Definitely worth playing, short but very sweet.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished the game. It was great. Premise: you're in a pseudo DnD club at a private school when the principal announces that all clubs must face each other in a snowball tournament. The fights are presented as the DnD tactics battles. The story is very cute, I love the character designs and writing. The gameplay is quick and snappy and doesn't make you wait around. The sidequests usually involve helping students become friends or work together and it's great and are also worth doing. I laughed, I shipped, I loved it. The battles themselves seem a bit simple at first but there are some curveballs and challenges and with the level challenge goals the ability to revisit battles you could definitely have some fun there. Definite recommend if you want a tactics game that's fun and cute and about making friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Really, really good. The tactics gameplay is very solid, with a wide variety of characters you can use who all play pretty differently but have their individual strengths-- Baphomet's is clearly the best, though, and I don't want to hear any arguments to the contrary. The non tactics gameplay is unobtrusive, which I feel is totally acceptable for a tactics game. The side quests tend to just revolve you visiting a few locations to talk to different people, but talking to all of the different students in the school is a reward in and of itself, which brings me to the writing: it's great.The story is interesting and well told, but just generally Wintermoor is a very well-written game. I tend to be preeeeettty picky when it comes to that kind of thing, so this is saying something.  Is my opinion being influenced by the fact that I own a cologne called Book (it's made by Commodity and it smells excellent, btw) and felt seen by the jokes about a book perfume? Probably. But seriously, the ending is smartly executed, and wraps everything up neatly in a way that's both funny and touching. The only nitpick I would have with the game is that the controls feel a little finicky sometimes in the tactics segments, sometimes resulting in me attacking a square that I meant to just move a character to. Thankfully, the game lets you undo any character movement for free, and lets you re-do an entire turn twice per battle if you screw things up, so these infrequent problems didn't do anything to sour me on the experience. All in all, this game is great, and well worth checking out.as a last aside, I'd just comment on some of the reviews I saw where stupid chuds were talking about how they were scared the game was going to force inclusivity down their throats-- what a sad, pathetic life they must live, being afraid that they might encounter a fictional character who prefers to be referred to as "they/them". grow the ♥♥♥♥ up, you losers.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Wintermoor Tactics Club is a beautifully written game. It revolves around a group of friends playing a tactical tabletop roleplaying game and the happenings at their school which become more and more mysterious. Taking into account the themes that are involved I would recommend it for people age 12+. The tactical battles aren't to hard to beat if you just want to win them. But if you want to ace them, they become puzzles that need to be carefully solved. In the end it was a heartfelt experience, that despite me being in my 30s, being a ropleplayer myself I wouldn't want to have missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game and it was incredibly fun. The mechanics offer just enough challenge with easily adjustable difficulty to be really interesting while sporting a story that hit a lot of feelings. I love the diverse cast of characters, especially seeing a black woman who is able to be vulnerable throughout the story as the main protagonist. All the characters were very likeable and interesting, even the one I had begun to get annoyed with near the end - there was a good pay off for it!
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: A tight game, real good writing, plus a depiction of mental illness I can appreciate. Ending was a good heartwarming wrap. Combat is interesting and intuitive enough as well as quick such that things stay fresh. Not too much grind plus art while lacking much in the way of animation, is still pretty and has heart. Good mix of goofy and serious topics. Questing is somewhere between engaging flair and nagging annoyance, leaning slightly on the flair side for me. Most characters are written pretty aight. Even a lil development occurs.Difficulty isn't too much and loading can be a nuisance which leads to longer run time. Music was hit or miss, but ending fight music was an easy fave. Not a ton of replay value except to try to get medals or upgrades/trophies perhaps.Gotta say after finishing it, I kinda miss the club a lil bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute game that knows what it's players want and delivers. Good tactics, with some plot, fun characterization. Could easily be completely cleared if wanted, but without that it's a less than 10 hour game, and would be ok at the normal price point. (And I think it's the right price point, since I wouldn't pay more than that.)
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: A little more point & click adventure and a little less "tactics" than I was hoping for.  It also holds your hand so much, you really don't have any challenge, even if you forego the "no fail" modes.  I would imagine this would be ideal for kids (up to 12, maybe) looking to get into this type of game, but is that even a thing?Having said that, it is well written (it's legitimately clever) and good-spirited.  It's a really cute game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent fusion of tactics and visual novel only slightly marred by the difficulty being on the easy side for tactics lovers.  While the maps are set up somewhat like puzzles, many combinations of characters are viable to clear them, especially as you get more and more of the potential upgrades that can change how they work.It's relatively short and sweet, not overstaying its welcome, and was good fun for the entire running length.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This is everything you've wanted from a tactics / strategy game that doesn't feel overbearing but has challenges there if you're into it (with accessibility options for difficulty if you're just here for the other stuff).The story, characters, and humour never feel laboured or out of place and D&D fans will love seeing their favourite archetypes of both players and classes represented here.For £12, I think you're getting much more than the asking price would suggest and it'd be a disservice to the developers to think on waiting for a sale; you're getting more than enough enjoyment, fun, and game from that with Wintermoor Tactics Club.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very charming game.  I really appreciate the writing in it.  Despite the exaggeration in personalities for comedic effect, the interactions (especially between the tactics club members) feel really natural.  And although it strongly pushes its core themes of empathy and friendship, I never felt like the authors were beating a dead horse at any point, either.  There are also frequent nods to inclusion and acceptance, without hammering you with token social media buzzwords or jaded counter-stereotypes.  It's nice, much like a tabletop home game should feel.On the flip-side, the tactical play was never particularly challenging, even the optional character mastery battles, but that actually felt pretty fitting for the tone of the game and the age group it seemed to be designed for.  It has a small, diverse cast with moderate customization for each member, and together they cover most of the class archetypes you'd expect to see, with the exception of any sort of healer.  The battles are short and snappy, and certain offensive strategies tend to dominate the majority of encounters.  All-in-all, this probably won't scratch the itch of the hardcore tactics veteran, looking for something to put their skills to the test, but that said, most varieties of players will be able to find something that they enjoy.Lastly, taking into account idle time where I left the game running, I spent ~20 hours to complete everything the game had to offer, making it both accessible for working-class gamers who don't have time for a hundred-hour romp and perfect for a weekend's worth of entertainment for the more dedicated gamer.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Wintermoor Tactics Club is a charming stroll through boarding school, where friendship, self-doubt, a mystery come together to make a heck of a time. For me, playing felt like... Pulling up a good book, one that upon completion, I heartily recommend to others to enjoy!Gameplay-Following a simple to learn strategy system, you'll control members of the Tactics club in a typical DnD or SRPG fight screen. Battles are short, with some puzzle aspects for those who wish to get every medal for each one, but open enough for a number of different strategies to shine. -Each character has a number of customizable options. While I do find some were just absurdly better for most fights, almost every single one had use at one time or another.-Fights let you reset turns twice per encounter, and you also can always take a movement back if you haven't done anything else yet.Story-Mystery, magic and friendship all in one package! You follow the story of the Tactics Club through Alicia, a young girl with some personal doubts that still wears a smile and cares for her friends and fellow classmates. I found her to be an fun protagonist, and found her struggles really relatable. -If there's one thing I'd fault the story for, it's that I wish there was more! But perhaps that's a sign of how much I liked the personality of all the characters that I just want more time with them all.Other-UI and menus are nice quality, giving everything the paper and pencil feel of many a tabletop game. -Music was charming and fit right in for every scene. I found myself humming along to the battle themes as I debated moves.-I found myself laughing at many of the jokes and references throughout this game - it had a charming feel.Overall, I highly recommend Wintermoor Tactics Club to anyone looking for a nice story with some good strategy/puzzle parts to break things up.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly well-written game with fantastic, inclusive themes and interesting, compelling characters.  The game mechanics were simple, but enjoyable - nothing breaking the turn-based tactical genre, but solid.  Highly recommend.  Took about 17 hours for a playthrough - I could have spent a little more time replaying battels to get perfect scores, but I felt like I otherwise got all the content.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Such an enjoyable little game, a true work of love. A beautiful story of friendship and finding your place in the world wrapped into very simple but fun D&D style tactics. The narration is impeccable and will not leave you indifferent. The fighting is not very difficult but adds new options with a very good pace so you should never feel bored with it. Highly recommend if you like good storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: 8 full hours of glory. Imagine if Dungeons and Dragons had a Yu-Gi-Oh-esque show in the vein of GX. The combat is more like a puzzle, but they're all well-done and the character development and such running alongside it is phenomenal. You'll greatly enjoy the whole package, especially if you can get it on sale but still if not, and, if you're human, you'll even cry a little at the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Works really well through Proton, for any Linux users who were wondering! This game was more "visual novel" than I was expecting (really, mostly a visual novel but with the occasional simple tactics battle to advance the plot), but it was so charming that I didn't mind, with a neat story and dialogue that cracked me up IRL a few times. The soundtrack was pretty good too, especially when it switched to the "80s new wave" track. If anything, the weakest component was probably the battles, which felt more like puzzles stylised as battles because of how limited your choices are within them (if that makes sense - you get to choose your player characters, where they move, and which of their 2-3 skills you want to use each turn). In my eight hours of playtime I completed the main story and all the sidequests, but I didn't do any of the optional challenge battles or redo the compulsory ones to improve my score, so you could get more playtime if you want 100% achievements. (Of course if you DO want 100% achievements then check a guide before you start, because at least one of them becomes unachievable if you don't know about it from the beginning.) Overall I'd recommend this on sale, but it  certainly an endearing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a delight.  The story made me laugh and smile throughout, the game's got a good amount of depth without ever making you stop to grind to pad out the length.  Main story isn't overly difficult but trying to max out your rank in each battle gives a good challenge.  Accessible enough for someone brand new to tactical RPGs, genre-savvy enough to satisfy experienced players.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Wintermoor Tactics Club is a fun, laid back tactical game with a cute hand drawn aesthetic. The story and dialogue are well written if not sometimes cheesy, with the best moments being the funny interactions that you make outside the story. I would say the weakest part of Wintermoore would be the combat. The combat feels more like solving a puzzle then it does playing a tactical game, with the exception of skills and such. However, it was still fun to see what was the best way to finish the battle the fastest and still get an above S ranking. For 15$, this game is definitely worth it, with me being totally invested through the almost 10 hour campaign. (I did all the side quests and main campaign, only thing i didn't do was all of the bonus upgrade missions and missed a few people to talk to during the last half of the game).
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid - easy early on, more challenging later, but fundamentally simple to grasp - tactics game marking the main beats of a genuinely engaging, twisty and warm-hearted story with plenty of flashes of humour and the delightfully bizarre. It doesn't waste your time at all while you zip around - animations are fast, moving around the map is quick, and dialogue is snappy. And it’s the writing where it really shines - the main story is genuinely worth following along with and builds up as a good narrative should. Above all else, Wintermoor is a relentlessly positive experience, both in terms of its story and in terms of the game aspects. It’s very, very *nice*, in the same way that Stardew Valley, say, feels like it just wants to pick you up, give you a pat on the back, share a hot chocolate. As a game, it’s everything 2020 isn’t.Really good stuff, would absolutely fire a cybernetic horse into a black hole again.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of another such "Tactics" game franchise...Wintermoor Tactics Club is a good spiritual successor to such games. Although somewhat short for my liking, every part of the game was filled with a great setting, fun characters, soft but energetic music, and interesting gameplay mechanics. Definitely worth your money.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Take amazingly cute art, a little slice of high school social life, and pour it all into a tactical strategy game that is full of variety, complexity, and no small amount of humor. This is DnD (not their ruleset or the roleplaying, but the allusions are vital to the game's story) in the 80s as a high school club, and it works on every level. 9/10, only lowered due to low replayability (you can repeat prior battles with different units or abilities, but there is no reason to do so if you've already gotten the achievements). Hoping for some DLC or expansion that gives more story (or perhaps lets us fight the other teams in the bracket that we never faced?).
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: A bit grindy in having to go from place to place every chapter to make sure you didn't miss anything, but that may be the completionist in me. The story is fun, the combat is sometimes a bit too easy but overall fun, and they really put it all together. Note, I am 9 hours in and I would guess about 2h from finishing, so its not  a long game, but its still a  fun one.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute blast, I've been hammered with work and in the mood for some light hearted fun. As a massive fan of TTRPGs this game was a lot of fun, if not a little bit easier on the strategy side, which isn't necessarily a bad thing. I would definitely recommend picking this game up if you're on the fence!
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: A great strategy game, but kinda short tbh. The combat system is great and the characters are awesome. Sometimes you need to click on something behind another thing in combat and it tries to make you click the thing in front, and the maps are really small, but overall a game I think would be great for someone new to strategy games would like.To show I know what I'm talking about, I put 18 hours in over three days and 100%'d it first go, so I've seen every bit of the game. Or at least most of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Wintermoor Tactics Club is a solid game which I can easily recommend.The tactics battles are mostly interesting because the diverse characters you get and the possibilities of customizing them slightly with items (which unlock passive perks or additional consumable actions). Its also quite fun to play around with party compositions, as you will only find yourself able to pick a team of 3 for most battles in the game, but you will get some more characters to choose from after a while.If you have a lot of experience with tactical combats you will probably not find those battles all too challenging, even when aiming for the SSS-Ranks. They are still enjoyable as small "puzzle snacks" though, which live largely by the characters and the narrative.There the game really shines. The characters are quite diverse and likeable. The story is somewhat exaggerated, but in all the good ways, offering interesting "Clubs" to fight and having quite a nice conclusion. With all its unique characters it still has an enjoyable moral narrative about friendship, prejudice and figuring out other people, which I enjoyed a lot.One of the recurring events in the game is a "minigame" where you have to think about how to best create a pen and paper adventure fitting to those new people which will join you club over the course of the story. I found that to be one of the most entertaining aspects of the game, as it was always interesting to think about the story itself and see how the other clubmembers will react to it. This games story really has a heart of gold.So, yeah, get it. Its somewhat short (I finished with all battles on SSS in 11 hours), but if you can enjoy a nice story and like the occasional tactical combat, I doubt you will be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Wintermoor Tactics club follows the adventures of Alicia, a young girl attending the prestigious Wintermoor Academy.  While she's had some trouble getting to know people, she finds solace in the friendships she forms with the fellow members of Wintermoor's Tactics Club, who frequently gather to play their favorite RPG, Curses and Catacombs.  These bonds are threatened when the Principal of the Academy declares a snow ball fight tournament to find 'The Ultimate Club' with each club that loses one of its battles being forced to disband until only one club is left!While this is a deeply unpopular idea, the kids feel like they have no choice but to comply or lose their beloved club, and so begins a string of battles against the other clubs interspersed with Alicia and her fellow clubmates doing their best to get to the bottom of their Principal's strange behavior, a mystery far darker than it first appears.The game play is essentially a hybridization of a tactical rpg; representing both encounters on the gaming table and the snow ball fights between clubs, and a strong element of social interaction, perhaps most similar to the Persona series.  You get to know quite a diverse cast of characters, both on and off the battle field, and the game's themes of community and acceptance shine brightly through at all times, though particularly towards the ending.The developers noted that they wanted to make a tactical RPG that was accessible to everyone, and I believe they have succeeded in that goal.  Difficulty is generally low, except for some optional missions to grant your characters enhanced powers, though there is an abrupt difficulty spike at the very end.  Even the final missions, though, are not to difficult to overcome with some careful play and experimentation, and the developers thoughtfully included an 'auto win' option for any battle that you fail to overcome after three attempts.A game of this sort lives or dies by its writing, which I am happy to say is stellar.  While not up to the standards of William Shakespeare or Victor Hugo, the plotting, and particularly the characterization are all top notch, and I found myself caring a great deal about all of the characters.  This is the first game since the original Grandia that moved me to tears of happiness with its ending.If you have any interest in tactical or slice of life roleplaying, please buy and play this game.  Games like this deserve our support, and I am eagerly anticipating the next project from developer EVC.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just adorable.It's a one part visual novel, one part "Into the Breach" tactical game, just in the right mixture.I loved the story, the characters, the graphics, the music (although, it become quite repetitive after a while).It was a bit easy, and I felt there is something missing about how each battle ends: you can get "tokens" in different categories (like, win the battle within x turns), but at the end, these don't give you anything, other then a better final rating for the fight, so there is no real point doing it as best as you can.But overall, it's still a wholesome game, with awesome final battles and ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Wintermoor Tactics Club is a game that hits me very hard, for both reasons both personal, and universal. On a universal level, the gameplay is similar to that of Final Fantasy Tactics. Whilst, yes, this comes off a much more simpler version of that game, Tactics Club gives you a variety of tools to customize your characters, giving you a limitless amount of approaches to each level. One gripe I have with this gameplay is that you're rewarded for using more of the resource for your stronger moves, rather than less. In a way, this means being more efficient, won't get you as many shiny gold stars for completing a level.On a personal level, Wintermoor Tactics Club is a huge reference to Dungeons and Dragons, and tabletop games in general (the VtM reference slays me). If you've ever been a fan of these games, or even groups that play them like Critical Role, then play Tactics Club. Even if you've never played one before, the writing alone is a lot of fun, and can even be seen as a good way to build interest in TTRPGs. Overall, a solid 3/5 game, 4/5 if you're a TTRPG fan or appreciate fun characters and writing.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Gosh, this is great.  The premise is absurd but the writing and characters make it work.  The mechanics of the game are fairly simple and there game isn't especially challenging, so don't come to this expecting a hard-core RPG experience.  But they do what they need to do to support the narrative perfectly, and I'm pleased to say I enjoyed every moment with this.  Thanks EVC :)
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute story-driven game about a school D&D...I mean, "Cats & Catacombs" club. It intermixes easy-to-navigate story elements with short, tactical strategy matches held using the C&C system. It has a lovely amount of depth that touches on things like having emotional intelligence, paying attention to cues from other people, empathy, understanding, and helping others become better versions of themselves. All while playing a storytelling game with miniatures within the video game itself! Play! The best way to learn anything.It's been an enjoyable experience as an adult, but I would also very highly recommend this game for kids/teens, as I think they'll get exposed to a lot of good ideas while they're playing. Not only will this enhance the very important life skills I listed above, but it will also have them working on strategic planning and forethought at the same time in a very forgiving environment. Make a lot of poor choices and lose the battle? No problem! You can play it over and over again until you win with no penalty to you. A delightful learning environment. I bought a copy for my young teenage nephew, and I can't wait for him to get to play it!
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy turn based strategy games such as Fire Emblem then you are bound to find something to love in this game. I really enjoyed the art style and the music whilst playing it. After I was finished making the video I continued playing some more and I am still able to easily recommend this game.You assume the role of a student that is part of a school club called Tactics Club. After the possible termination of your club, you must battle other clubs in order to avoid closure. As you progress through the story you uncover more and more about how thick the plot is beneath the surface.You can recruit more people to your club in order to assume successThe difficulty of the game is totally up to you. You can double the health your characters have, you can decrease the enemy health to 10%, you can enable or disable battle loss where you cannot lose any battle. If you want to simply enjoy the campaign and uncover the story, then you can simply do so. I commend the developers for thinking this through and letting the player decide how they want to tune the difficulty of the game.This game is published by a publisher that has an eye for good games according to their track record. I would certainly give this game a try.GMG provided me with a key for the game but that did not affect my opinion by any means.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely worth the money for a lightweight mixture of visual novel and turn based tactics game.  I see why many reviews compare it to In The Breach, but another good comparison is to Black Closet.  The visual novel is well written and has interesting takes on many high school situations, maybe with more emphasis on inclusiveness and less on dating.  There are side quests and many points on the main quest where a tactical battle is required. The battles are much simpler than other games such as XCOM or Battle Brothers; that is not what they are aiming for.  The hover help and popups give much more information about the exact enemy actions, so you can plan more carefully.  That is where the comparison to Into The Breach comes from; but these battles have much less going on in a single turn, and they are more spread out.  So figuring out a good set of moves is much less intense than Into The Breach. I did appreciate the "par" ratings for each battle.  To get a maximum score, you should be sure to complete the battle in the recommended number of turns, while taking less than the recommended amount of total damage.  I guess I play a little conservatively compared to "par"; I wound up taking much less damage in one or two more turns.  I also succeeded without using the powerful special abilities, which oddly counts against your total score.  To get maximum score, you must use these abilities twice, and I usually only used one or zero of them.I don't buy visual novels much, but I found the writing very good and the main characters well developed.  Even the minor characters like the two jocks by the stadium get one enjoyable side plot.  Some dating aspects are hinted (one "crush" is especially poignant) but never in the foreground.  I mentioned the game reminds me of Black Closet, mostly for mixing a visual novel with another game type.  Black Closet has a mystery solving aspect and no tactical battles; it's also possible to get more into "dating at an all girls school".Overall this was definitely worth the $15 for about 15 hours of play.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: The world is a pretty awful place, and this game was exactly what I needed. The art is beautiful, the story is fantastic and has more turns than I thought it would going in, and every character is endearing. As tactics RPGs go, this one is super puzzley - it kind of makes me think of a much more accessible "Into the Breach."I love this game, I'll be buying it again when it hits the Switch, and really hope that this team puts a new game together in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: A thoroughly enjoyable tactics game, with good writing and likeable characters. The story is engaging, touches on some serious topics without losing its sense of fun and makes a nice change from the overblown fantasy of many RPGs. The tactics gameplay is solid, is supported by a clear UI and is pitched at a good level for players who are new to the genre. There's a lot of variety in the way you can set up your party, and you can rejig the composition of the party and their equipment every battle, so you are never stuck with a poor choice. For experienced players, the fun comes from getting the max rank on every battle, experimenting with the  many different party combinations and getting all the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very pleasant experience. The dialogue, the story, the combat, the music, just the overall interaction is a great time. A lot of love and effort went into the details, and it shows. Although the combat has not been especially challenging so far, I appreciate the clarity that it gives you. It's always clear what your actions will do, and it shows the reason that each monster has for taking the move that they take. For instance some monsters will attack the closest enemy, and this is shown as the reason that the move while it is their turn. This is a great addition to this kind of turn-based combat that I would love to see in other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Could not have recommended this game more! I bought it on release and it gave me 12 hours worth of gameplay for the price of 15 bucks! The story isn't generic and it really feels like my choices are properly incorporated into the game, especially the C&C writing portions. The enemies seem easy for now but they do start to get challenging late game, so I would advise against being eagered to crank up the difficulty if you feel midgame that it's getting easy. I also loved how the characters were built! It's rare to see games that can incorporate characters so well with other characters and the main plot! Overall, great game, great combat, and great story! I honestly didn't expect the ending of the characters, especially our main 3 characters! It felt really liberating to get to know how everyone did after the events of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: As a tactics game, the maps are significantly confined which leads to a more puzzle-like play experience. The limited character development options and the frequent control the narrative takes over who you can play makes each scenario feel very directed in comparison to other games in the genre. Still, feels like D&D encounters.While definitely a focus for the game, these tactics scenarios are probably the least interesting part and the thrill of them largely comes through the context by which they are played. True to the reality of roleplaying, the dice and figures are there to facilitate the resolution of some emotional or social trouble that the players are working through. This is something Wintermoor absolutely nails with its narrative.If you want to play a tactics game, this will scratch the itch in the most minimal fashion and force you through a lot of narrative between missions. However, if you wanted a game that encapsulates the wonderful complexities of the social order as it pertains to a roleplaying group, then Wintermoor Tactics Club will delight you with its quiet truth and realism.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This first point of this review is that I would not have purchased this game without the coverage of NorthernLion!This game is good as a tactics game. It is not the hardest game in the world to beat by any stretch of the imagination, however some of the harder challenges seem hard to perfect without getting very precise. The main campaign missions were not all that tough, but I think they were very fun and in a game that matters more. I did like how there were some very clear and powerful synergies you could use to decimate opposing forces. There were elements of the narrative that I really liked! The story grew on me as I wen't along, I believe I recall that chapter 4 really hooked me when I was unconvinced before.I will say that part of me wishes there were more types of playable characters to experiment with. Particularly those of the physical damage persuasion. I think that is a good problem to have, it means I enjoyed the game.Some minor gripes that I suspect are caused by early launch bugs or something I did:1. My achievements didn't record and haven't yet synced. I haven't gotten credit for some of the earlier chapters I completed.2. I felt like I mis-clicked a lot while units were bunched up. I would often attack with a ranged attack when I meant to move to a tile just behind the unit I accidentally assailed.In summary I wouldn't come here for XCom but with kids, I would come here for a fun and funny narrative that is told through the lens of grid based combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: A mix of an interactive story and a light tactical game. As a long time fan of role-playing games and a child of the 80's probably one of the most enjoyable games of 2020 for me. Started playing and couldn't stop until I had seen the whole story. Dialog is funny without going too silly. Highly can highly recommend for people who want a pretty quick (9 hrs, ALL the side quests) game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Quaint story with a lot of heart.  The tactical portion was was engaging and fun enough to support the storytelling, but don't expect a super challenge if you play many tactics games.  All the characters had lots of charm and each one felt like they had a story to tell that I really enjoyed finding throughout the playthrough.  Make sure you talk to everyone whenever you can, or you're really missing out.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly short game, but fairly priced as well.  The story and gameplay are both engaging and fairly weak.  There are a few characters and themes that are hamfisted and irritating, but seeing as how the genre is fantasy it's forgivable.The only real con is that for a unity game, it's lacking polish and finesse.  Apparently the achievements don't work, so I guess that's a con for the millennials and younger they're made for.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great visual novel / tactics game! The writing is extremely entertaining, I found myself laughing out loud at parts... which doesn't happen to me very often while reading. The tactics battles are engaging, not so difficult as to be frustrating. However, getting a really good score requires some decent brainpower. I would highly recommend! 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Take the heart and soul that makes games like Earthbound and Undertale so meaningful, mix it with solid FFT-esque mechanics and splash in a bit of Persona influence with the social aspects of the game... and viola: you get something like Wintermoor!This is a true gem, and hopefully one that won't remain hidden and obscure.  Even at full price, this game is an absolute steal. On sale, it's a no-brainer!
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the perfect antidote to any busy, stressful day. I don't know if it will ever raise your heart rate past 100 BPM, but that's pretty much the point: if you need a good excuse to lay in a beanbag chair and smile, then this game is right for you. The story is fun, the writing is witty, and the battles are cleverly done. For novices in the tactics genre (like myself), please know that Wintermoor Tactics Club is also an excellent overall introduction to the genre. The game nailed the cadence of escalating the level of difficulty for its players, giving them a chance to walk for a few levels, before asking them to sprint. If you're trying to teach a newbie how to play a tactics game (e.g., your parents, a significant other, the neighborhood cat), there ain't a better place to start them than here.I wholeheartedly recommend this game, and now that I'm done writing this review, its about time to start another round of Curses & Catacombs.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Wintermoor is a delightful, cozy combination of visual novels and light tactics gameplay. The characters are all charming and getting to know as the game progresses is one of its great treats. The tactics gameplay is streamlined and approachable, but still has plenty of opportunities to experiment with different strategies and builds, especially as you unlock more options in the late game.Full disclosure: I helped beta test Wintermoor a couple of times.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: I demoed this game at PAX East, which convinced me to buy it as soon as it came out.  I just finished the game (after ~14 leisurely hours), and I can heartily recommend it.I worried in the first couple of chapters that the combat would stay relatively easy and never pose much of a challenge, but after the first few chapters, the difficulty ramps up nicely.  That is to say, you're rarely going to lose a mission, but if you want to get the best score on every mission (which involves meeting conditions involving damage taken, turns taken, party members KOed, and special abilities used), you'll probably need to replay some a few times.  There are also special 'Mastery' battles, so which had me changing my tactics a few times before I found a setup that worked.  The final sequence of battles is also amazingly well done and brought a nice level of challenge.The combat itself is pretty simple and feels more like a puzzle at times than traditional tactics game.  There's no rng - every attack will hit, and you can see each enemy's intent for their turn.  The game gives you more abilities/characters at a decent rate, which helps keep it from feeling stale, and each fight rarely lasts more than 10 minutes.Outside of combat, it's a fairly straightforward exploration/visual novel: there are side quests you can do, that typically just involve talking to different people and traveling to different locations.  These often reward you with new items to aid in combat.The best thing about the game for me, though, is the writing.  The game is consistently funny and endearing.  The absurdity of the different characters, and learning about them as the game progresses, is wonderful.  From the Equestrian Club who continues to function long after their horses were taken away, to the Young Monarchists, who will explain to you the benefits of monarchy, the world feels quirky and fun, and the humor never feels forced.  The overarching plot is good - nothing revolutionary, but it works with what the game is trying to do.I have a few minor complaints (the angle of the tactics board sometimes makes it hard to click on spaces that are partially obscured), but overall, the game was a joy to play.  If you're looking for a hardcore tactics game, and aren't so much interested in reading a lot of story, you may want to look elsewhere.  For everyone else, though, I can't recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Wintermoor Tactics Club is a very chill game. Part strategic combat and part visual novel. On the fence about picking it up? Check out my full gameplay review video for Wintermoor Tactics Club. I go into great depth about the Story, Graphics, Audio, Gameplay, and other noteworthy things I feel needs to be mentioned: Disclaimer: I received this game for free. I was not paid to promote or write a review. All thoughts are solely my own. Thanks!
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Great art and music, amazing story, lots of fun jokes, planning your battles on the go. This game has it all!This game had me sitting back, clicking, and enjoying it all the way through. Characters you can relate to, love and see in your friends and family. It's cute, intriguing, awesome, and made me want to pick up DnD. And it has all the small things. The voice lines, sound effects... You even get to show off your artistic skills!Definitely recommend this to anyone wanting something new to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Wintermoor Tactics Club

_childDocuments_.review: Wintermoor Tactics Club is a story about surviving high school, with gameplay inspired by tactics RPGs and visual novels. It was hard enough for Alicia at the famed Wintermoor Academy before it erupted into a snowball war! Now her club's only hope is to transform from nerdy nobodies into fantasy heroes. Unravel a reality-bending mystery. Test your strategic mettle against an avalanche of colorful characters. And don't forget to make friends.

name: Century: Age of Ashes
detailed_description: SEASON 3 - LIVE NOW! Prepare to chill and thrill with a new character class and a heap of new content in Season 3: Path of the Beast, OUT NOW! Content included in Season 3: New rider class 'Rimeblood' Dragon Pass: 70+ customisations, including dragons, weapons, armour, celebrations and more New map: SnaerFell Rift New Ranked PvP season A rich Story unfolding in 8 lore tomes Split of Rider & Dragon ... and more! JOIN US ON DISCORD Join us on Discord and stay updated on all our announcements and most recent content! About the Game Century: Age of Ashes , the multiplayer dragon battle game is now available for free! Customize your dragon, dive into the arena and compete to become a legendary Dragoneer. Burn your enemies and rule the skies! Compete in intense online games ranging and discover the fast-paced gameplay of Century : Age of Ashes ! Dive into the arena alone or with friends and fight for your survival in exciting game modes: Outbreak (PvE): team up and protect the towers of Hel’s Breach against waves of horrific enemies. Carnage (PvP): A killing spree with special power ups. It’s Team Deathmatch, Dragon riders style! Gates of Fire (PvP): Two teams clash over possession of the flag. Gain points by flying through gates while holding the flag! Spoils of War (PvP): Steal gold from carriers & the enemy while protecting your own nest, and adapt to unexpected situations! Survival (PvP): It's every dragoneer for themselves! Pit against other players in a ferocious and unforgiving free-for-all clash. Experience different play styles with unique classes, each with their own abilities! Shield and disorient as the Windguard, track and destroy as the Marauder, stealth and trap as the Phantom, rush and thunder-shock your opponents as the Stormraiser or vine-trap them as the Thornweaver! How will you choose your path to victory? Your dragon, your style! Century: Age of Ashes offers carefully designed cosmetic items to stand out in the arena. Gain experience as you play and unlock awesome skins to customize your dragon and its rider! Don't worry, these items are purely cosmetic and offer no advantage in battle. Century: Age of Ashes is completely free-to-play. In order to keep the experience fair and equitable, in-game purchases are purely cosmetic. Battles are won by skill and teamwork alone.

_childDocuments_.review: A TON OF CHEATERS. Matchmaking is very hit and miss. There is no real format to it seems completely random. matching level 5 players and up against level 20 to even 60 is a complete joke. I love the premise and would love to suggest this game but it is completely lacking of any balance. There are only 5 game types including ranked. Speaking of ranked that is where i ran into the most cheats of course right. Flying is good controls are very intuitive but NO BALANCE. The classes lack any real sort of connection to the player. Their new game modes spoils of war is the ONLY ranked game so if you dont like it pretty much tough. In ranked EVERYONE is thrown together and you can play it as low as level 10 so the skill gap can vary wildly. No pay to win that is a plush and it is very polished and fleshed out in terms of mechanics. But no i would not suggest this game to anyone to wants to have fun with friends unless you all have a very firm grasp of how to play. Beware this free to play game. I will continue to play despite this as i do find it somewhat enjoyable in very short bursts. But downloader beware of this HOT MESS.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, micro-transactions. It's ALL micro-transactions. And it's not just a few cents or a couple dollars here and there, they want up to $60 for some things. Absolutely disgusting. Just set a price for the base game and let players earn the rest of their cosmetics by playing the game.Second, the game definitely needs to fix its matchmaking. _childDocuments_.review: This game started out fan-f*cking-tastically and has since lost steam. Matchmaking is awful and very discouraging. Even if you are good you have very little hope of winning in the ranked play style unless you are in a squad of people with extreme skill or straight up hackers. But this will never happen because they all play together. Basing player rank on Win/Loss systems don't reward the individual for their skill. The winter events were enjoyable and gratifying because you could EARN all of the rewards realistically because they were based on individual score... That is NOT the case anymore, since the community who plays is mostly toxic good luck inviting anyone into a squad. If you are lucky and snag a teammate, hope you don't start losing a match or they will likely leave the match to save their Kill/Death ratio.... I'm over it and won't play the ranked matches anymore, doesn't matter now anyways since there are only 300-600 players I'll get a reward when this event is over no matter what.I have ideas and possible solutions to fix things a little if the devs care about people enjoying this game again like we all did over winter. The Christmas of 2021 Age of Ashes kept my soul warm, it was all I could talk about to friends, family, and one random customer service man from the bank who definitely downloaded it after our chat. So PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE work on the real game-killing problems.-DO NOT NERF the dragons (wyverns grammar sticklers... we all know) If one class is overpowered do not weaken it. INSTEAD: boost the weaker classes. EX: Phantom goes invisible, can't be hit, and the first shot is extra strong. OK that's unbalanced for sure. Everyone plays as Phantom, people who are salty about it complain.... result is Devs nerf the phantom. DNN do not nerf. INSTEAD try to leave the Phantom as intact as possible and only fix the part that is like cheating... STEP 1: Let the Phantom go invisible and the first shot can still be strong but let other players hit him while invisible, just make it to where they need pinpoint accuracy and skill. ALSO only make minor changes one at a time, scientific method, this way you can find out what players actually need or want AND you can determine what actually fixes the issue instead of taking a shot in the dark and hoping for the best. At this point if the Phantom is balanced problem solved. If not... STEP 2: Boost the weaker characters. For the Windguard, let the smokescreen buff do extra damage to the Phantom while he is invisible. For the Marauder, let them get a new hunter's mark buff if the Phantom goes invisible within a certain range, or while directly in front of the Marauder.Overall my point is there are other solutions. I think boosting the dragons instead of grounding them will increase the chaotic-fun aspect of the game. Its fun to learn new ways to evade enemies as everyone adjusts, but the people who genuinely love phantom don't get punished and everyone who hated the class can now feel good too.-LISTEN to your players. AND COMMUNICATE MORE.EX: look at facts, player base was high in December. But now there are less than 1000 players and it is easy to find complaints that all start sounding the same. Here is what I have seen in less than 1 hour of looking at reviews....STEP 1: Let players choose their game. You can still have three different styles of gaming. I propose the FIRST be a Players Choice of all game modes. Allow players to select Gates of Fire, Spoils of War, Carnage, 4v4v4, Skirmish, Free For All, WHATEVER, like when the game first released but better. It was a beautifully simple checkbox style layout and was easy to understand, the rules would pop up as you hovered over each option. This will fix an additional problem as well (bonus round) players can complete their daily tasks easier which boosts moral and makes the ridiculous prices of the shop a little easier to obtain. SECOND game mode can be ranked. THIRD can be experimental. That's not a huge change. At first there might need to be fewer options until the player base goes back up, but once people love the game again it'll be easy to get a match in any style.STEP 2: Crack down on cheaters. If players can auto heal and devs can't fix it, ban the cheater. Nothing else makes sense. It is the ethically correct choice. DO BETTER. And quickly.STEP 3: Perform as advertised. The eggs you get by leveling aren't random. The skins are hard enough to earn or expensive enough that you can actually provide a unique random dragon. STEP 4: Balance the ranking system. The weighting system for wins vs. losses is very harsh. Losses are worth too many points. When players have to struggle for a win loss ratio of 1:4 soften the blow of the loss. It is extremely disheartening.I'm sticking it out and hoping it gets better. But if you're new its like that South Park ski instructor says...You're gonna have a bad time.

_childDocuments_.review: I deliberated on the recommendation and went back and forth on the "yes" or "no" for a good 5 minutes and unfortunately I just can't recommend it yet. There's the obvious growing pains of a new game, servers being forced to wipe the dust off and accommodate all of the people trying to rush into the game they've been eagerly waiting for for months. I can't fault that! If Playwing wanted to do P2P connections then that's all well and good, but they would have done well to do a third round of beta testing closer to the games launch to iron out the kinks because as the connection stands now, it's damn near unplayable. Trying to change an arbitrary cosmetic on my profile? Disconnect. Trying to queue? Disconnect. Win (or lose, but 100% of my wins thus far) Disconnect. Everything you do is a coin flip (or a 100% guarantee) of a disconnect. Not entirely unexpected, but still frustrating, and not what my review is about.1. The reason I can't recommend the game right now is because of the customer service (or lack thereof). If you have an issue with the game, you can forget about getting it resolved. The way to get it fixed is to clamor over the other 100s of people in the Discord server trying to get the Devs attention and get your problem fixed. Didn't receive the daily key for the quests you completed and are screwed out of the weekly chest? Tough luck, about 50 other people will have encountered the same problem and you'll be lucky if even one of you gets noticed, never mind gets it fixed. The game desperately needs a ticket system for people to submit their bugs/problems so that they can be adequately dealt with.2. In the same vein, this is a team PVP game. Without a report button. Teammate is very clearly intentionally throwing the game? Can't report. Enemy (or teammate, be a good sport) has already found ways to cheat? Can't report. That is... unless you want to report them in the Discord and face the same challenge as number 1 and probably never be acknowledged. I thoroughly enjoyed my time in the beta, I lost sleep over this game and made some really great friends while playing it! It's an extraordinary game, a very cool concept, and I had a lot of fun with it. But until Playwing starts to care about helping the community that cares about their game, I can't recommend it.I will absolutely change my status once they have those two things I mentioned.
