_childDocuments_.review: *First impressions, will update once i get more playtime*First impressions: For a free to play and most importantly NOT a pay 2 win game, i'm pretty impressed. I will say this game is very action heavy so it may not be for everyone. Luckily it is not too complicated to learn, but it certainly is hard to master. This is generally good game design.Starting with graphics/UI: The graphics look very good. Landscapes look exceptional as well as the fire. The characters themselves look detailed as well as the dragons. I hope to see lots more customization and it certainly looks like there is some planned (lots of slots for the character and dragon). The UI is a lot to take in at first but it makes sense after playing with it for a bit. I think they've tried making it as clean looking as possible, and i agree with that approach. I find the indicators for fireballs coming too small, but that's my only gripe. Music/Sound design: Its fairly average. It's not bad but i wouldn't say its worth raving about. If anything there might not be enough tracks. I'd say a game based on pvp and no story this wouldn't be a big priority anyways. I can say the same for sound it's pretty average. To nitpick the sound could have better hit sounds with the fireballs. Gameplay: They really nailed this. You really feel like the dragon is mobile yet has enough weight to it to not feel cheap. Flying through tunnels and mountains feels really epic. As for attacking: every dragon has a base fireball attack (2 charges) and a firebreath for close range. The game also has 3 classes (with more planned) that have a passive skill, one of two abilities to choose from, a power and a rage skill each. They all feel very unique and serve a role. Marauder's your brute warrior with the most hp, strong offense skills but fairly limited defense skills. Phantom is your rogue type dragon. It can stealth briefly and put down a mine, but has the lowest hp. Windguard is your support class. They can quickly aid another teammate to shield you both as well as strong defensive poison smoke. This make them and their teammates untargetable inside. So far they all feel balanced but windguard feels a bit obnoxious with all the smoke they can put out. Just note I have limited playtime so i can't accurately gauge class balance yet. Hopefully the devs put out decent balance patches in the future. Replayability: For a pvp game it will have good replay value for that fact alone. To add on to that, there are a decent amount of game modes to choose from and the devs plan on adding more game modes and classes. Cons: No chat/voice option (but there is pinging), the matchmaking seems non-existant and once a player leaves your team there's no player fill or option to surrender currently.Overall i'd recommend it if you're looking for a unique pvp experience that isn't a moba or battle royale, or if you simply like dragons. It's a free game too so really nothing to lose to try it.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun for a free game. You get to ride a dragon and shoot people. What more could you ask for?The skins and customization options feel very diverse. There haven't been that many yet due to the game being new to the public, but almost each one has been tempting to buy. I appreciate that the game is free to play and funded entirely by cosmetics, and they go absolutely ham on those cosmetics.Matchmaking is very clean; you can choose what gamemodes you want or don't want. Each of the 3 game modes feel unique.The controls aren't perfect and are somewhat disorientating, but were easy to get ahold of and I feel like I quickly learned all of the game's features without confusion.My only real issue is that the game has a long ways to go in regards to improving pickup registration and notifying players of item pickup. Picking up items is very laggy and delicate; there are many times where I or someone else fly right through the middle of an item, and then get notified that it's actually now held by someone 60 meters away. There is also little to no indication that you are holding an item which can easily cost a match. I think the best example is the Spoils of War gamemode which has an item called the Vault Breacher, which you pick up and fly into the enemy vault while holding to blow it up and cause the enemy team to risk losing most of their points. This alone can make or break a match, and there is almost no indication when you pick up the item or what you're supposed to do with it. It's very hard to tell when you are holding an item and the notification that pops up on top of the screen is delayed and unreliable for all team mates (often saying someone has the item when they've already dropped it--you basically can't rely on the HUD update messages and have to look around yourself to see who has it). I've had team mates fly around blissfully unaware that they are holding a nuke and single handedly lose us the match when they accidentally die with it in our own vault, handing it to the enemy team to explode us easily. Many situations are just a cess pool of "what's going on? Who has the item? Why didn't that team mate pick it up when I watched them fly right through it?" I consider this issue pretty severe and worthwhile of a refund if the game cost anything, but it's acceptable for a free game that only recently became public.Other than this the game only has a few other minor problems that I have faith will be solved with time, such as a few weekly missions being bugged and uncompletable.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this game and now, actively, advise staying away from it.After disabling ranked for 8 entire weeks - two whole months - because of matchmaking failures that caused no end of issues in all modes including ranked, Playwing turned ranked back on.For one hour.7PM-8PM UTC. They then said that top 500 get an "exclusive" player icon (despite being told numerous times that player icons are not good rewards that are worth playing for) while the top 50 get the fourth class . The problem with all of this?1. It's numerically  to reach rank 50 if you aren't already close to the top 50, due to the one hour a day to play restriction (even if you  play the game that hour every day.) 2. If you didn't get placed back in December when the game launched, you are statistically incredibly unlikely to place highly enough to be able to compete for the top 50. Ranked is, basically, rigged. And Playwing are the ones to have rigged it.3. The one hour time slot is fixed at 7-8PM UTC, which means if you're in America and attend school or go to work, you can't play because you're at work or school. If you're in Asia or Australia, it's extremely early hours of the morning. Even if you're in Europe you might have family obligations, but it's safe to say Europeans got the best end of this bad deal.When Playwing was told that they're very clearly ignoring player feedback, and that the latest update almost feels  towards casual players, the response was a disgusting backpedal using evasive language like "player feelings" rather than admitting any kind of fault, nor acknowledging the factual maths that proved the reward system was broken, rigged and unfair. The game's updates have almost constantly, excepting a couple, been negative and taken the game backwards. With the latest update of ranked, being time limited to one hour in a terrible time slot and the rewards  it very clearly smacks of a company who don't care, and even worse, don't  how to develop their game.It's such a shame. The game is so fun. It has so much promise. But in the hands of Playwing, it's going nowhere except the grave. _childDocuments_.review: So... Before playing, I've heard absolutely nothing about this game. I saw some gameplay online after researching for dragon games and decided to go for it. Little did I know, how absolutely AMAZING the gameplay FELT when you played it. Watching and experiencing are two different things, especially when it comes with the joy of having a dragon to battle with! This combined with the easy and awesome controls created a really enjoyable game that I saw myself playing for years...So why don't I recommend it?Well after playing the game, all of a sudden I heard a LOT about it. I heard about season 0 and how prosperous it was, how enjoyable leveling up could be. Guys, face it. Everything is behind a paywall nowadays, but even FORTNITE did a better job of keeping new players afloat with the amount of rewards they gave. This had it all before season 1. And now season 3 is desolate. The main goal of the game is to have a dragon, battle, hatch new dragons, get armor to make you look cool, customize little aspects of your character, and have fun demolishing the other team. Now, all you get to do is have maybe 6 dragons, battle, and maybe demolish the other team. For having to hatch more dragons as a key component of the game, why is it trapped in the in-game store? When I did a little more digging around, I found out that everyone else knows this. The developers know we're pissed. But they aren't doing anything about, they refuse to listen to real tips-- to what we as players want from this amazing game.Leveling up feels like a lost cause, because it is. At most, you get stars to unlock items in the season pass, but lo and behold, dragons, new riders, USEFUL currency, all of that's stuck behind the paywall of the premium pass. Oh but don't worry, every 10 levels you get to keep grinding the free rewards until you have enough coins to buy a dragon egg, in which you already know what's going to come out of it.I don't know what happened. Maybe they ran out of money and felt like this was the only way out of it? Anyone I've asked says the developers got greedy. Such a shame, seriously... It sounds like it was so much fun. It can be, if we were rewarded for our efforts. This game does not do justice for new players, that's why most of the ones still playing are veterans, who were there for season 0. Listen to your fans, guys... We're really rooting for this game, but right now it just feels so empty.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game. Controls are simple enough to learn how to play with only a quick tutorial, but still propose a lot of possibilities. Typical easy to learn but hard to master gameplay.Game modes are interesting because they all bring an objective to give more importance to teamplay and tactics.Though I have a cautious opinion about certain points.Firstly, Phantom's invisibility isn't fun at all. I'm not talking here about balance, but only about frustration. Dealing damage to enemies only to see them disappear with 2 hit points is just frustrating, and they have this ability quite often. I think it would be better to increase cooldown duration, especially as they have their invicibility rage.Secondly, Windguard's smoke gas isn't good either, it's blocking too mush line of sight. When there are several Windguards in a game, the battleground is just a huge poison smoke where nobody can see anything. Furthermore, it also blocks aim for allies preventing from dashing to an ally through one of your teammates' smoke. With the update, you got the Windguard weaker (less hp) meaning 2 things : you force peope to use the smoke gas just to survive (then worsening the issue of overuse of this skill) and you can't deal as much damage with this class making it too useless according to me. The best thing to do would be to change entirely the ability. To make it a smoke cloud that appear only where you're standing upon activation of the skill. People going through it would have a lasting effect of poison and wouldn't be able to aim during this effect. Like this, you would be able to see across the field, even when multiple windguards would use their ability.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the combat in this game. Its like Panzer Dragoon from back in the day. I hope to someday maybe see a further installment of this game because of its Potential. Id say if it had a campaign it would be even more enjoyable. Maybe some expandable story line could help. The gameplay is smooth and I really feel like Im the Dragon Rider chasing the enemy team trying to destroy them with fire and other spells haha. If you have a thought and think maybe I should give it a chance, do it! You wont regret it and if you do oh well! This game doesnt force you to play. They have Gems you can purchase for cosmetic purposes but Ive noticed that you can level up and to collect better differnt dragons at some point. As you progress through the game and play matches you will level and recieve items and differnt cosmetics that will change how your dragon looks. Imo the best content is when you recieve a dragon egg. This is when the game is expansive and could recieve a lot of support if maybe a known streamer or company could display Century: Age of Ashes on Twitch. So far though Id give this game a 8.5/10 I say this because its the most fun Ive had being able to just jump in even with a learning curve the dragon is fast but once you learn the controls of the game and you are able to start flying past certain parts of the game you will realize your opponents are only half the battle. Its you as the Dragon Rider to get win for you and your team. Also before I end this review, the free for all event is fun but its somewhat unbalanced. I only say this because when you have two people against one or 4 against one its not quite as fun. I think a map with a huge arena for each player to rise up in the ranks would be better then just one open map where everyone is trying to survive. Those are just my thoughts on the game. I hope it doesnt hinder you to play as this is a multiplayer based game Id say if your into Dragons fighting against other Dragons and flying, go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, this game controls great. The tutorial is a great way to get into the action fast and it's not too long. Each of the three classes (looks like they'll be adding a fourth) play differently and have a place on any team. The gamemodes are all fun to play and scratch a different itch. Hatching the dragons is fun and outfitting the dragon riders is a nice addition that adds a little flair to your character in the intro and pre-game. You don't have to spend any money to play at the same level as other, the only things you can buy are cosmetics, dragon skins, and booster (all of which you can unlock, besides certain dragon skins). Overall, the game is free and a fun time to play, each game is relatively short and there's a lot of fun to be had. Try it out!

_childDocuments_.review: I will recommend Century: Age of Ashes with some caution. Overall, it's a very fun, fast paced game with some of the fiercest and best looking dragons I've seen. The PvP fights are intense and exciting, flying around the map is extremely fun and it's a great game if you're just here to have fun and ride cool dragons. I've been waiting for a game like this a long time, and it's free to play to boot. Not to mention, it is one of the more... "completed" dragon-centric games out on Steam and actually seems to receive regular content updates. There's really no other game that quite scratches my itch of flying a big, powerful dragon (or giant eagle) to date.My main issues with this game, as many other people have analyzed, is the unbalanced matchmaking, numerous noticeable bugs and absolutely predatory prices for what is essentially just cosmetic items. The new battle pass system is abysmal, good luck getting any decent items without spending money. The devs have also pulled back on a few promises, such as promising a permanent PvE mode, adding it, then promptly removing it after a few months.I wish the devs would bring back getting decent rewards without having to need a second life to grind or fork out money to do so. It would retain the interest of more players, including myself, if we knew we could have feasible goals to grind towards. Hell, I'll go as far as saying players might feel more inclined to spend money on this game if they feel like their time and effort is better respected. A few well-known MMOs come to mind as examples.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up in a time where you could spend money on a game and it be single player AND multiplayer. I have played enough multiplayer to know that I'm average at best and MUCH prefer to sit in my own bubble and massacre fodder bots and AI. So imagine my joy when I noticed a PvE mode was added to this game, this game that has an amazing concept. Seriously, the graphics, controls, lore are all really good, and the promise of a PvE mode almost made me wish there was a price tag to this game. Almost. Imagine my chagrin when not only is it a timed event, but you HAVE to play the PvP to unlock it. It's not like this is a case of "go play something else". There's really not much like this. As cool a concept this is, it's not for me. If it tickles your fancy, by all means play it. The brief moment I had with the tutorial was really fun.

_childDocuments_.review: While I believe that the mechanics are very fluid and straightforward, I cannot beg enough that something be done about the consistent match-making problems. I have sat lifelessly for three games in a row because I, a level 13, was put against groups that were level 50 and above. In large PVP arenas where item drops and space are a factor this might not be a problem, but in a game where the arena is tight and it solely requires skill and mechanic understanding, why the hell would you not have something that keeps similar levels together.Until I see improvements when it comes to team-mate matching, making sure its ACTUALLY 6v6 when the game starts, and not putting newbies against pro levels, I am not recommending this to anyone.

There is almost no progress system outside of the battle pass (you need to pay).Very few classes, that even seem a little indifferent. As of this review there are 4 classes. Considering the very few abilities per class there could be more. Some classes even share secondary abilities which seems very dull.I don't understand people saying its pay to win. It's pay for skins but since it's not a grind game and it's free to play what's so bad about that??? _childDocuments_.review: At its core, this game is a flight simulator on dragons. It's a fiery reptilian blast, especially if you have some friends who you can play with. The pros:The game has simple, useful mechanics and is easy to get in to. The first few matches you play you'll spend confused as to how in the world you're moving so dang slowly and then eventually you'll realize how the stamina and fireball mechanics work and you'll be semi competitive. It's gorgeous. The characters and dragons are excellently done. Even if I don't love every class (and I don't) I think they all look gorgeous. The maps are great and show the dark fantasy vibe the makers were going for.Very few things are truly behind a paywall. You can collect dragons, classes, accessories for your classes, titles, icons etc. all just by farming the in game currencies. While it takes a while to achieve the money necessary to make a purchase, it's also not a hard thing to spend your money, as there's always something worth buying in the store rotations. Also, things that show up in the store will rotate out on a 1/3/5 day basis, so some things you'll not see more than once in a while, but you'll have chances to pick up your "perfect" set over and over again. Co-op in this game is really excellent. If you can get a squad together (easy) you'll find it a simple thing to blast the heck out of enemies with friends and the necessary improvement in your scores by being able to call audibles on the poor guys who don't have friends. It's really satisfying to watch your team descend on the foe like a pack of fiery raptors. The Cons:The amount of time necessary to grind the in game currencies is a little long. While it's not prohibitive for playing and enjoying the game, it can be irritating when you're trying to get your choice dragon and it takes about 8 hours of work to get enough in game coin to buy him.... and hope he's not gone because the store is rotating.The matchmaking could certainly be better for ranked play. Ranked matches are a BRUTAL experience for most. I'm fairly good at the game and usually score in the top 1 or 2 players in any unranked matches. I also average less than two deaths per match. In ranked matches I sit solidly in the middle and usually have half a dozen deaths or more. Watching me play in ranked matches is like watching an epileptic control a scaly golf cart. Or it feels like that. Overall:The game is a great experience and thankfully gives you plenty of tactics to mess with, plenty of dragons to see and a great art direction with intuitive controls. It's easy to link up with friends, it's easy to learn the mechanics and it's worth picking up.... because it's free!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game but it does have a few issues. For example, some of the issues that I have had are being disconnected mid-game through no fault of your own WiFi. The controls sometimes decide they want to go into controller mode even when you have never connected a controller to your PC. You do get a few cheating players who you are unable to defeat no matter how many fireballs you spit at them. But it's a very unique dragon vs dragon aerial combat game that given some time could become a perfect game, in my opinion. You have three current classes each with their varying abilities which give you three ways you can play the game (and a new one on the way) You have some very interesting game modes, classic survival which is a favourite of many but with the addition of dragons. And what is it that dragons covet? Gold, the unique Spoils of War game mode where you have to collect gold while attacking and defending your hoard from other dragons is a very fun game mode in my opinion. As well as survival and Spoils of War there is Carnage, a 6v6 Deathmatch, need I say more?There's a very unique capture the flag style game called Gates of Fire where two teams fight for over the flag and have to fly through gates to earn points. As well as other modes in the arena that rotate on a schedule throughout the week.And did I mention customisation? You have a wide range of customisation for your character and your dragon, to chose from that you can get through levelling or in game purchases in the shop with earned or bought in game currency. And best thing about it, IT'S ONLY COSMETIC. NO PAY TO WIN.There's items that change daily and then there's a weekly shop rotation so there's always going to be something to catch your eye.So despite the bugs which do make it hard to play sometimes the game is overall very fun and promising.

_childDocuments_.review: A good bud of mine and I have been waiting for this game to come out in MONTHS. We've hit the lull where we've cycled through the same few games and needed something new. This game greatly exceeded our expectations. It's just the game we needed and stoked that it's more than we hoped it would be.The aerodynamic physics of this game feels great. I've played a lot of Star Fox, my buddies played a lot of War Thunder and Elite Dangerous, and other flight-based games---and felt right at home with the controls. It was quick for us to pick up and the classes were interesting and all felt fun in their own ways. I'm sure as I play more I'll notice some gripes, but 4 hours in so far and it's the squad's next go-to timesink.So far, I don't notice any pay-to-win aspects and its super neat how customizable your profile, character, and dragon can be. I especially enjoy the mechanic where we can raise our own dragons, and are incentives to complete certain challenges in order to 'hatch/grow' the dragon---and so on. There will be new classes to explore and (presumably) new modes down the road. I'm cautiously optimistic to see where this goes.Overall though It's very impressive especially on Day 1. My friend group and I all decided to support the devs in hopes that they can really make this into something big and great. We will definitely be binging this all weekend

I had a lot of hope for this game, so i stuck it out each season and joined the insider program, but ranked is still broken, where you either never find a match, or if you do you are a 2 stack v 4 stack. This game essentially punishes you for just playing it and they REFUSE to nerf the marauder class which is easily the most cheesiest brain dead class to play in the game. _childDocuments_.review: So first off, I'm writing a review right now because the matchmaking system is currently broken. That being said, it is safe to assume that it will get fixed. I like the game so far. It's fun, the rewards are rewarding, and the game modes are creative so that it's not just dragon battle royal. The whole dragon aspect of the game is exciting, the flight feels decent, the combat is fast paced and it's satisfying to get kills and wins. There are some aspects of the game that really go well but there are some major issues that should be addressed, as well as some minor things that I would like to see.So first of all, it's a PvP arena game primarily focused on combat. There are 3 classes of dragons/dragon riders to choose from, i.e. a warrior, a support, and assassin. They each have different abilities that the game explains fairly well before going into your first match. Each class has 3 abilities (you have to give up one), a passive and a "rage" ability (an empowered version of one of your active abilities). Something to note, the different classes also have different health pools, and maneuverability that the game does not tell you about. granted, you find out quickly, after playing, but it begs the question, what else are they not telling? It is important that in a pvp game where you have a ranked system, that more detailed information about each class is made available. Cool, so the game has classes and a very minimal customization of each. How about the actual combat? It's fun, it's exciting, but it's chaotic and lacking skill based aspects. There is one skill shot in the game, and that is the optional ability "blast" and the aoe from it is huge; Everything else is homing, auto lock, or placement. So from what I see, the "skill" of the game is in your ability to fly, not shoot. So, since your ability to fly, and control your dragon is actually where the skill lies, let's talk about flight controls and aspects. Moving your dragon is easy, though I found that I had to crank the sensitivity way up to actually make sharp turns. You can speed up and slow down quickly, this is your bread and butter for sharp turns to avoid incoming attacks. When someone is on you, your best bet is to get distance to avoid fire breath as it does massive damage and is as hard to hit as just holding down right click, also to perform sharp turns around terrain to avoid the homing fireballs. When locked onto a target, It is near impossible to see which way your target is actually facing, all you can see is how they move across your screen. This means that you can’t tell if an opponent is coming towards you or away from you, and most importantly, you can’t see which way they face when they have slowed down right before they are about to burst into a new direction. This makes it very hard to react and move so that you can stay behind your target, forcing you to guess which way they will turn, which is hardly a skill.So it comes down to how quickly you can make those unpredictable turns. Well, the phantom (assassin) class has the sharpest turns and therefore will almost always win the 1v1. Some people may think that is over simplified, but understand that there are no other skill aspects of the game, it's just your ability to make these turns, which the phantom does the best. Now, the devs make up for this by making the support class extra tanky, or the warrior class do lots of damage. They also have well designed maps, put buffs and game objectives in all so that the game is not just a 1v1 in the air. Because if it was, the phantoms would win every time. All these extra elements do add to the game, but also detract from the actual skill matchup. I don't really count map memorization, or playing a character that "counters" another as skill. It's more your knowledge and tenacity."But the game is more about your ability to work as a team, get objectives, positioning and timing!" That is super true. The game rewards all of that and you will win more games and climb in rank by doing so. But there is not a single way to communicate with your team in game, so que up with friends and use discord or let fate decide by queuing solo. As for the primary game mode, which is gathering gold, and returning it to your base, there are lots of things happening that took a few plays to figure out. A simple explanation of what is happening in the game or in any game mode for that matter, (I think the gate one is the most fun), would go a long way for players that get frustrated at not knowing what is happening in the game. You will lose players like that. It really just comes down to what kind of game you want to play. I have not had a super negative experience by queuing solo. Though, I have seen the games literally start with 6v5, and have had players that just head hunt and end up at the bottom of the scorecard cuz they are not actually playing for the win.I would say that 95% of the games that I have played have been good, meaning that players actually played the game. The game is young, so things like the matchmaking being broken, only a few classes/abilities are to be expected. But I think they opened ranked play too soon. It's a game that rewards team play, knowledge, using the maps and focusing objectives to win. All things that the game makes hard to do, by not providing all the information, lack of in game communication and forcing you to guess when actually dog fighting. I think the game is a lot of fun. It's like ace combat on dragons. But it's skill aspect is definitely tailored to the majority of people with no real incentive for skilled based play allowing you to get kills just because of the chaos of the game. Even after all that, I like the game, I want to see it grow. The game is actually balanced with the classes, maps, and objectives. though I think the wing guard (support class) is the strongest right now, as she takes the least amount of skill to play and is able to hard focus objectives while denying the enemy team their objectives. Yes the phantom will win a 1v1 in the air, but there are enough options that the map provides as well as the fact that they are squishy to overcome them in the actual game. Also, the game is not pay to win in the least. Everything is cosmetic, and you earn the in game currency by playing. So if you love dragons, chaotic game play, excellent maps, dog fighting, and want to play out your dragon rider fantasy, give it a go. Would love to see this game grow.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game. It has dragons. And dragons are awesome. It plays incredibly well, the animations are fantastic and the flying just feels right. These beasts have a weight to them, yet can turn on a dime if you know your controls. It runs silky smooth, and while it currently lacks advanced graphic options and widescreen support, the game's potential is definitely there.It's the first title from an indie studio, and it shows. Some implementations aren't that refined. Matchmaking is basically non-existent, you'll queue with people 20 ranks above you from the other side of the planet. The game is still fun. And while Ranked is a thing, it yields no rewards you couldn't unlock otherwise, other than bragging rights. On top of that, the game is truly Free to Play. There is nothing locked behind paywalls, no microtransactions, no lootboxes or pay-to-win mechanics. Everything you can buy in the store you can unlock at one point or another, and all the items are purely cosmetic, too. Plus, they throw a bunch of gems your way every 5 levels, so you'll earn those even without paying for them.Overall, this game is a fantastic experience and a very welcome breath of fresh air in today's gaming scene. It's a new, awesome concept, executed well-enough to spend hours (or minutes) playing it. While matches only last around 10 minutes, I find myself binging this game for 12 hours a day, match after match, just because of how much fun it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Century Age of Ashes was the dragon game i was hoping for. It has fast paced PvP, beautiful dragons and environments and now in full release it also has a new game mode, lore for all the items and dragons and improved progression (its still slow but definitely not as slow as the beta was). I was really excited to get back into this game after waiting so long...but unfortunately my full release experience has not been a very good one. After a week of fairly stable play, i ran into a problem that plagued me in the beta - Disconnects. But not bad internet disconnects.Every time i win a match (or even just finish a match) before the XP starts piling in i get disconnected. You might think - "hey i still finished the match and got past the podium shot so my XP will just sync when i load in right?" WRONG. ALL of your XP, your progress to your weekly, daily and now event missions are all gone, like they never even happened. I would not be so mad if this happened occasionally as it can happen...but one session i had 12 matches and only 2 of those matches made it through (and to add insult to injury those 2 were my only losses that day). Worse still,  because of all the disconnects i received a time penalty! I've done all i can to ensure its not a "me" problem, like checking in with my ISP and rebooting the router and testing the connection. It seems server side. I'm not sure who provides their game servers but they definitely might want to look for other options.This issue has completely broken the positive time i did have with this game and it seems like its not being addressed or given priority at the current time. I am trying to be patient since it is still so new and i am sure there's a lot going on that i am unaware of behind the scenes. But i really hope they will take this issue seriously. I want to play and enjoy this game. I want to progress and participate in events and hang out with friends but its literally impossible for me to do so. As it stands, i cannot recommend this game in good faith. If you are one of the lucky ones with no issues, you will enjoy it very much! But if you have the same issues i do then be prepared to waste hours and hours just to get nowhere.

_childDocuments_.review: The first big issue I have with this game is the auto aim. Flame breath, fireballs, specials... it doesnt matter. Its all auto aim. If I can see my opponnent, I just need to keep them somewhat near the middle of my screen and press the button. Theres no skill required in that department. Maybe for fireballs sure, but flame breaths? If my enemy is on my rear, its inescapable.The flight controls follow the mouse. I managed to get them setup to wasd, but I needed the mouse for firing.  It felt wrong switching away from the mouse for all controls, but thats what I had to do, because the wasd movement is better. You get sharper turns, and better control then the mouse allows for some reason. However you cannot turn off the mouse for movement, and so while firing, any little bump of the mouse caused my dragon to ignore my wasd movement. And again, the mouse even on 5 sensitivity is not as sharp of a turn as wasd is. So...Its frustrating to say the least.If I had recommendations for the dev, fix your flight to be responsive. Take auto aim out of the equation so it can be truly skill based. Or at least take it out for flame breath and abilities. Fireball is somewhat understandable in this high speed game. And if your going to allow wasd movement such as you allow now...please let us toggle off mouse movement.I personally won't be playing until this game until things smooth out a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: For a free to play, it's unexpectedly beautiful and engaging. The lack of chat makes it easy to play without having to deal with toxic players, and the fast respawn timers enable you to shrug off deaths and continue enjoying yourself. Even when you lose, you wind up having fun. And I say this as someone who normally despises PVP.On that note, it's definitely not as fun to play solo. This is a game to play in a voice call with friends, because that's what everybody else is doing, and going in alone against a coordinated team is a good way to take a very hard loss.I also really wish there was a lobby system, so I could vs my own friends. At the very least, the team assigning needs to be less random, because if you wind up in a team of level 2-15 players against a team of level 25-50 players? You may as well throw the match, because you're not going to win. Instead, teams should be matched based on the total level of their group.Even with all of that, I'm still going to uprate Century for the single fact that they did a REALLY good job with not making this a ragequit game. It's still fun, even when you're biting the dust. And for something that you're not having to pay any money to try out? Fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Century: Age of Ashes

_childDocuments_.review: It's dynamic and exciting with multiple game modes to bounce between. The controls feel good while flying - not too complex, but not too easy either. Fast-paced game play and re-spawns make for less time waiting, even when you're not doing so hot and keep getting shot down so you can get back into the fight and try again. The skins look great, many of which you can unlock/purchase with in-game points if you're down to grind, or you can speed up the processes and fork over some cash - whichever is your preference.

Game is quite basic as there are only 3 characters and only a couple of extra abilities each. So it can be played casually from time to time. Ranked system contains only 1 game mode and it's the gold carrying mode.Worst part of ranked is that there are either bots or people afk farming the game. I had a player named sy151892591 in my game, which didn't do anything for 4 matches back to back. 0 gold collected, only walking towards a wall to avoid afk detection OR actually a bot that went wrong.Crashing your player against wall is horrible, you can't properly move and your sense of direction is gone because of absurt rotations.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Dragon Ace Combat.Wanna see a game succeed because I want some alive Dogfighting PVP. (Dragon/Wyvern is a bonus)Would recommend this game or delete this review, but right now there are major jarring issues. (No one gonna read this but I leave it anyway)"Can't see a thing" is the best way to describe the game right now. Where to start...First, on the offense side, why is the Missile Cooldown being so small (like 10x4 pixel horizontal bar on screen), so is the flamethrower bar, and the cooldown on the right-down corner is hard to see without moving your eye down.Not to mention the "Lock-on" target, it used the Green enemy HP bar and a gold circle in flamethrower range instead of dedicated UI (either a separate circle or square) and no distance measure. I know there's a Main Target icon for 2x2 pixel arrow each, a direction arrow that disappears and blended together, see below.And the defensive side, the incoming missile indicator blended into the game background too much and it is reversed (Why the missile indicator when being close is smaller while the one farther is bigger?), worse if you happen to get ganged you will see the red arrow (and a red !) EVERYWHERE on your screen. debuff icon also misplaced and bad colored, it is really hard to see if you get hit by a Frostbite or a Mark because the icon is on the middle down instead of a text, sound cue, or model effect on character middle screen where you focused most. (unless I missed it, I can't find a different instead of noticed I'm slowed down from the game effect and UI icon everywhere on the screen) Stamina color should be changed to be more green and black, not light green and grey too. (or just remove the icon when used)Make it much more cleaner, take Project Wingman or Ace Combat for a sample, it only shows the Big arrow when there's a missile coming at you plus the sound cue and flashing red UI, and a louder or more intense warning when it is about to hit you. When you lock the target (one target at a time) it has a different targeting icon and shows where the target is off-screen, and when you get locked on it show "Warning" and some sound cue instead of the red Arrow.Plus Ace Combat/Project Wingman has a radar map, while it might not be appropriate in this game due to a close-quarter dogfight nature, but it is easier to track what things are and where the missile coming from, and a tool for powerups location or your base.Bonus point, play as a Windguard now you have the useless Blue arrow on your screen and you may be targeting an ally instead of an enemy without a proper way to tab-cycling.Currently, matchmaking is to put you in the game ASAP and it will either put you in unbalanced team inexperience (low level vs high level or solo vs premade) Not to mention no backfilling when there's a leaver, worse at the start of the match that you cannot leave without getting a good punishment from the outdated MOBA system.It should work more like Team Fortress 2 (or even the recent Halo Infinite) where players can come and go in casual, but no filling in ranked.There's no official info on whether this game is Peer to Peer or dedicated server, but by looking at Resource Monitor the given IP address is not static during gameplay (The player progression server is amazonaws)The Desync issue is super annoying as well, you can see a person lagging and doing a Z shape movement or a barrel roll in the unnatural way, which is kinda funny, but the problem is your missile will miss from a target being randomly sped up/slowed down, worse when you dodged the fireball (sharp turn or behind a pillar) but still take the damage because it hit on their side or even used flare (Marauder's Gust) where you get both Stamina and damage. Or the objective pickup, you may fly through the object, but won't pick up because of the desync.Not sure if this pricing is to intentionally want to help limit purchase for the low-income countries, which is kinda nice? or being greedy.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally my dreams of a game since I was a kid playing Drakengard became real. Short answer: Recommend.Piloting the dragon is hard, and I love it. Gives a lot of realism, since flying is about the momentum and inertia.So have a the pros and cons:-Pros:-You ride a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ dragon, you can do anything in midair, even fly in place, they have amazing animations that feels real and fluid.-You get full access to all 3 characters/dragons, no need for pointless grinding early, you can choose what you want at anytime.-It's not p2w, you pay to look good sir.-Tutorials are really well made and you have a free practice area to try different things.-Many game modes and events that gives nice free stuff by just playing and completing missions/milestones.-No lag or ping issues so far, but will test it out with ping booster once it gets added to it.-You get better the more you play, you learn what will or not kill you or you can do many strategies.-Queue times are decent. Less than a minute every time.-Lots of customization/cosmetics, for the rider and dragon skins (most paid, but events gives nice ones).-It feels fun to play, not clunky. Cheers to the mechanics. Even when you die the crash cam is amazing, showing you dieing miserably on the ground xD-Cons:-Motion Blur can be immersive, but it's really hard to play with it on.-You need a hell lot of concentration to deal with everything going on your screen.-If you don't master the ways of flying, maneuvering, breaking, you will get yourself kill A LOT and it can be frustrating since you feel like you can't do anything. But it's really up to being patient and learning how to fly and use your skills. -There's no minimap, and that will get yourself lost a lot, or you will struggle to find your teammates and stick to them.-Get ready to chase the lock on circle and not see whats happening through all the fire going on (Wish there was FOV options)-Lack of more graphical settings ( it seems like they will add more later on so will be looking forward to that)-No mic on team game modes.Overall, it's amazing considering how new this is, no glitches, no bugs, no connection issues, I'm really impressed. I'm having fun like a little kid with a new toy. If you into medieval things, LOTR, GOT, Skyrim, you will love this. Try it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Right. Where to start. I had been DYING for a dragon game for a long time, they are so few and far between that it is lamentable. When this popped up on the radar I like many were super excited, with it free to play also a nice +1. When it first released it had issues, as do most games, but it was a fun experience.After a while though I noticed number of glaring issues beginning to stand out, first of all was game balance, there is a ranking system which the more you play, you gain experience and level up, much like COD. The game however has no real matchmaking, pitting you in a team of 6 lvl 3-5 up againt 10-20+lvl, to some this may mean nothing, but this denotes the level of experience between players. And it is a CRUSHING experience to be bested so hard, so fast, with no chance to learn if you had made any mistakes, which is likely not, because you had no chance to begin with.While this had been shouted out loud by the community, the devs had instead hidden the levels of players to other players, meaning instead of addressing and fixing the issue, they are covering it up, which immediately ring alarms as to the type of developer of this game.Another significant issue regarding matchmaking is the abilities to form squads, these are your immediate friends who can join on discord and play together, communicating during play. These teams can be as minimum as three up to the full six team. If you are up against one of them, its over before you have begun, matchmaking does not consider this setup, therefore if you are pitted up against this you will find yourself pursuing one player just to get killed by two on your tail. Communication is key, but there are no means of communicating to the team unless you are in a squad, and (again), if you happen to find yourself against one, game over.As well as the soul-destroying match making, the game balance (or lack thereof), is another glaring issue which experienced players will exploit to a merciless degree. There are three classes each with their own aesthetic and play style. The Marauder is a hard hitting and aggressive player dealing massive damage, swiftly killing players and moving onto the next target. Windguard are protectors, defenders of other players and of themselves, though slightly more squishy than the Marauder. Phantoms rely on stealth, ambush and very tactical play to make the most of.Of these three classes, the Windguard is by far the weakest and least played, it struggles to take a hit, and its protective abilities are lacking where determined players can still punch through. Marauders can almost instantly kill players in the hands of skilled players, giving the victim barely any chance to react, and even if they survive the first barrage, the next is already on the way while you have been shook up (literally) and unable to respond. Phantoms are the class that really grind my gears, they are the most played by the most experienced and (In my view) ruin the fun of the game. They have a stealth cloak that when you are pursuing they go invisible, that's your chase over, they can lay mines in the most frustrating areas which you will have no warning of where they are. These are but the main issues regarding class balance, there are more which further diminish the fun.Instead of the developer however addressing these issues, they instead work on cosmetics which can be bought for a hefty price. You "can" earn the money in game without buying them with cash. But it is impossible because the store will have been rotated multiple times BEFORE you will have earned enough, if you are still playing by that point that is.It is deeply saddening to see a game which would have filled a nice niche being treated so poorly, by accounts a significant chunk of the player base has left swiftly after launch because of said and unsaid issues, partly rendering the match making as it is. New players will be deterred from returning, old players will leave because teams are barely getting filled. Players quit mid-game or are disconnected due to server issues, it can take me over a few minutes to get into a game.The devs have recently released a road map, though I cannot see that they will fix the classes, even though they are introducing a new one this spring, we'll see. I'll keep on playing a few games a day, not many, keeping my eye on, hoping. Rare it is for a game where you can soar on the back of a beast of myth and legend, I hope they turn this around soon, or else this games wings will be clipped as it barely left the ground...

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen some comments mention it's pay to win, but it isn't. Other than the newest class, everyone starts with the same 3 classes. You can jazz them up with cosmetics, but changing gear doesn't alter your stats. So anyone can download the game and play with most of the classes other people have. It's no different than say, playing Valorant, where some agents are locked, and others aren't. I did try it awhile ago when you could get eggs every so many levels, and I admit that would be super cool to come back to. instead they've implemented a dragon pass (similar to a battle pass for valorant, or tomes for DBD). You can get 4 items on each page without paying for it. Once you complete it, you DO have to wait to hit a certain level to pass it (example: you need to hit level 10 to upgrade to tier 2 after the 4 items you get). There are some dragon skins in there, so you're not completely devoid of something. So none of my complaints are there. It's a free game. They make money off the cosmetics and battle pass (also you get gems and coins from it without paying as well, so if you save for awhile, you can also buy items in the shop that are for sale with those currencies). My beef... is with the matchmaking. I had a Spoils of War round with 5 on my side, and 1 on the other because it couldn't find players. That's not fun at all. Don't start a match if all people haven't locked in. I also got stuck on a spawn screen, where I had to wait to spawn for 1 second (but it was like 6 more after the initial) which is def not fun at all. So my issue is really with the servers, and how they continue with a match. I still think it's a fun game, and as another stated, very addictive. There are comms, but I haven't used them. It's too chaotic for that, imo. And there's no chat to flame someone else before or after the game, so if you want to play something competitive, and not worry about some incel on the internet, you're going to be OK.  As for cheating? No idea. I can't say I've seen it or haven't seen it. But that's always something a company can be working on improving.

They now have the advantage as you're facing away from them, meaning you can either attempt to maneuver the difficult turning (which I actually liked, btw, this isn't a negative point), or you can also run into a wall to turn around. There's almost zero penalty to just crashing into a wall at full speed to make a sudden stop. It's frustrating and looks incredibly silly as everyone is just crashing into walls over and over to try to flip a 180 or get the advantage on their pursuer. I can't recommend this game because of that.

_childDocuments_.review: Century: Age of Ashes is designed, in every respect, to be a mobile game - from the boost/power up centric flight model, to the fact that every single attack you have at your disposal is "lock on" based.  The skill ceiling is as low as they come, with win or loss based largely on blind luck rather than any sort of tactical reasoning or player ability.  You've also got your usual suspects when it comes to player base - with certain parts of the world absolutely swarming these types of games.The one thing I will say to its credit (though it doesn't lend it much), is that the game limits its micro-transactions to purely cosmetic skins at the moment - with nothing in the store that impacts players odds of success.In summary, Playwing LTD ought to stick to what it was founded doing - mobile games.  They aren't fooling anyone with this ill conceived mobile spinoff that they threw onto Steam instead.  Fix the flight model. Nix the powerups.  Make combat skill based rather than auto-aim, then we'll talk.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game but with some hesitations.I have played since launch - great model design, fun fast paced gameplay and flying around on dragons is awesome.There is new content added consistently - new dragons, classes, cosmetics, maps and modes.That said, they have made some changes which unfortunately seem to be heading in the wrong direction.First and foremost, they have clearly gotten greedy. The battle-pass has be reworked to give you essentially nothing unless you pay. Cosmetic packs are outrageously expensive for what they offer. You used to be able to earn in game currency, gems, just by playing. Collecting new dragons by hatching eggs used to be a core part of the game but I haven't seen an opportunity to get an egg for free since several updates ago. They changed it so any class can equip any dragon. Dragons are cosmetic so this is not game-breaking but it was entirely unnecessary and really takes away from the immersion. When there were three classes and three kinds of dragons each was matched to another and the abilities of each class made a lot more sense.Cheaters. I suppose any game enough people play will attract cheaters after enough time but it really hurts this game. They are not in every match but when they are you might as well quit. You will be consistently one-shot out of nowhere and the game will not show you who killed you as it usually does. Overall flying on dragons is a blast and definitely worth trying out for free. Honestly, the mode where you just fly around a map by yourself is a highlight of this game. I still have high hopes for this game, they just need to better address the cheaters and pull way the fk back on the over-monetization.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:• Interesting gameplay• Stunning look• Awesome atmosphere• Several game modes and mapsCons:• Nothing keeps you in the gameSummary: The game is pretty awesome, experience is fascinating. The look of the dragons and the game itself is totally worth playing. Personally not finding any reason to play longer that each of the game modes for several times I would say that it should be remade or added something. The game worth playing long hours and grinding, but there is nothing for. Taking into consideration that I was released 2 days before my play, I must say that the start is spectacular, but the ground is not stable.6.5/10Personal opinion:I could not remember any game that made it possible to ride dragons. Here it is. The dragons are awesome, the work done to make them look live is tremendous. Each of them is so detailed from the models to animations that they really look incredibly realistic. Flying in a stylized locations, fighting with others creates a wonderful atmosphere that really awaken a desire not to leave this world at all, as it is so awesome. The wonders of Unreal Engine are used to its limits. The gameplay is pretty straightforward, though surprisingly interesting. You fly, engage in fights with opponents, kill them, collect gold or whatever the game mode provides you to do. This will make you stay for several hours to try everything possible and compete with other players and teams. Providing there are several maps (more maps than game modes), each map makes adjust to its design and create strategies with your teammates based on it. The major disadvantage of the game that I didn’t find the reason to play it longer. The atmosphere is awesome, graphics are spectacular, encounters are engaging, but why should I play more and earn the currency. There is a store, but with only a little of items and mostly dragon skins that change only the color of the dragon. There is a possibility to customize characters but there is no store to buy those customization items. There are plenty of good examples, where you have lots of characters and each one has its own customization store where you can spend a lot to customize him/her. Here there is none. The difference between such games is not that significant, to play only for the sake of gameplay. In addition, from my experience I would say that the free-to-play game has to cover its costs. Make to choose either grinding or buying. Personally, I would gladly grind on some skin available in the store, but I should know about it at first and want it. It is not enough to get an offer of something like 5 items that gets updated about every week. As I said, to play I want to know what for. Here I have no idea why should I spend more.

_childDocuments_.review: So my review will be mixed. I wish there a way to give a notation, it could have been 8/10, but currently it is a 5/10Pros: very addictive combat, which requires skill. No dragons nor raider have stats gear which would give an advantage, the player needs to understand the class and be more efficient in skills. The best of world between plane combat, fantasy and competitive game. I really love that aspect. So the gameplay pushes the player to be smarts, fly efficiently, and try to improve oneself. The game is visually nice, and the modes are well done and thought between pure pvp, capture the flag and raiding money.Cons: The games really suffer from a common sickness of small companies, a total lack in economy gestion. The bad old gems systems is here, and skins are expensive. That's exactly what doesn't work. You buy gems, you will always get a boit too few or bit more, to they expect us to buy not to have unused gems or push people to buy some small xp boost so that they lack the few gems for a skin in the next promo wave. And that doesn't work. First people will buy more, if skins are cheap, people will have a tendency to by several 5-7 euros skins, several times a months, rather than spend 20-39 for a pack or a single skin. The result is once you have spend your initial discount gems to buy the season pass, you end up for a lot of player, paying for nothing.Second: it seems to make the company lacking in money, and they lack in communication too. The season is now over, the pve, so it's back to full pvp and nothing to replace it. The season pass is still there. And... nothing more. So we can see a dip in players connected, even in cross play, we end up knowing each others name etc. And several group of friends, just log in to check promos buyable with game money (some rare skins), then log out. Which according to some website, make the max players peak below 475 and average 200 .And that is something than also shows something unadressed bugs. PVE, no matter how many game we did, some way more than others, we got stuck at 80916 points, whereas a single day made me earn 12000 more. So I ended up in the leaderboard, with a third of the score I should have had, some friends, half etc... It was unadressed, and we ended up at 769 th place in the leaderboard, all at 769! Whereas there were not even 500 players, we should all, all player have been in the 500. Which either make it a bug, or a will to make believe we are more than shown to play.Combined with hack on the pvp leaderboard very often talk, moreover, with players bars refilling out of nowhere, stamina refilled when almost of out the map alone etc... Most people don't play the leaderboard because when you do nothing to a dragon with less than 10% life suddenly recovering, and one shoting players it's really annoying. There are veru veru good players, knowing maps well, and keeping themselves up, they are real genuine good players. But some just refill in "empty" area. Well, there is no option to report, to contact and try to speak. Than made also several players quit.So either something is change soon, either the game will coillapse, because, it looks quite abandonned to be honest. And it pains me to say so because there is a lot of potential in it, and I got addicted fast.

_childDocuments_.review: - Refreshing game, F2P. I love the aesthetics. There isn't a lot of graphical options in game right now but soon.- Quests are easy and the grind isn't too difficult so far (there is a free battle pass with 100 levels and a "prestige system", I guess a little bit like Titanfall 2 or Hunt: Showdown), it will get harder later I guess.You'll earn money and gems (the premium currency) quite easily : quests + when you'll level up.- There are 3 classes for the moment (new ones will arrive soon): A kind of balanced warrior, a support-ish one and an assassin.You ride a dragon but its purely cosmetics. There are dozen of dragons with really nice skins. Every 10 levels, you will receive an egg and you'll have really small quests (4 or 5) to complete in order for it to hatch (kill 1 opponent, use your special alility twice... really easy)Matchmaking is fast (less than a minute in order to find a game) but it can be difficult for beginners because you can fight against level 10/20 who already know how to play. I guess it will be better as the population grow.Game is (seems) easy to play, hard to master.

You're sure you didn't want to release this in 2015 or something?If this was a mobile game, I'd say it's ok, since 99% of all mobile games are trash. But for a PC game...nope. This ain't it. It's really just akin to some janky point and click MOBA'ish game you think you'd see in ad banners. You don't even aim in this game, fireballs etc. just magically home on the target when you point somewhat at them (which also is janky af).Like, it's free, so while it's trash, it's still free trash.But this isn't worth spending money on and you likely won't play it for long either. _childDocuments_.review: Review Edited 12/25/2021Graphics: The game looks spectacular. It's easily one of the better looking free to play games out there.Sound: Sound is on point. Dragons roar like you'd expect large reptiles to do, but they do it quite often. Very little variation in sound effects. Combat sounds are a bit hit or miss, being either loud and unfitting or quiet and almost not even there. Music is great though.Controls:You can tell when someone hasn't done the tutorial. Playing the tutorial will help you pretty much master the controls right away. You may need to do some tweaks in the settings, but overall, the controls are plenty fine. Bonus points for having inverted controls by default since that's more realistic for flying.Marauder Class:The black sheep of the classes. Has the best design, fitting a knight riding a beast into battle, but can't really compete on a higher level with the other two classes. Very easy to play, somewhat difficult to master. A great Marauder player is significantly more impressive than a great player on the other classes. He's a tank class, being beefy and hard to kill, but he does significantly less damage as a result.Windguard Class:A female knight riding a slender, almost majestic dragon. She has a lot of utility, mainly in the form of healing and shielding an ally, but she also has the most wildly useful attack in that she releases a poisonous gas cloud that obscures targeting. Given flak by the community for how easy this is to abuse, but it's not an "I win" button like some seem to assume it is.Phantom Class: A shrouded man riding a fish dragon. It's the most popular class, either due to his childish edginess or due to being the only class that can go invisible and deal a massive burst of damage with the least amount of effort. He's as fragile as a glass rod in a room full of falling hammers, but that's just how he's balanced out.Balance:Phantom > Windguard > Marauder. Phantom and Windguard are both pretty much even, but Phantom does more damage. Marauder is sadly undertuned, being unable to do any real damage without using all of his cooldowns when available. Tanks have no place in this kind of game, sadly.Dragons:Yes, they're wyverns. Yes, wyverns are dragons. Deal with it. There are NPC dragons in the worst game mode you can kill that have six limbs, but they're not playable sadly. They look like green rhinos with tiny wings, and that's kind of endearing. Please add that as a dragon for any class at some point, devs! Preferably bought with coins and not paid currency!Flaws:First and foremost is the dev team's questionable pricing on cosmetics. These prices are absolutely horrible. For $20 USD, you can buy one skin that isn't just a recolor. For $20 USD, you can buy like 15 games on Steam for hours of enjoyment. I will be absolutely negative towards this predatory pricing, because it's just greedy. Second is their odd love of pushing bundles back to back with little pause. The game hasn't been out for long, but there's been so many expensive bundles pushed in that short time. I get it; free games need to give the devs some form of pay. This kind of predatory pricing however? It's over the top.Now on to gameplay flaws; there's barely anything to mention. Sure, the balance of classes is a bit unfair towards Marauder, and the other two classes have gimmicks that are fairly overwhelming, but for the most part, the game's in an absolutely fine playable state. The lack of game modes is a bit underwhelming, especially in Ranked where you can only play the worst game mode. One issue that I've found is that the weekly chest for actively doing quests has HORRIBLE rewards. You will not feel rewarded from doing seven consecutive days of putting effort into the game. If you're not dishing out money for cosmetics, you'll rarely get cosmetics. If you don't have any interest at all for cosmetics, then this won't apply to you.Overall:My initial review lavished praise upon the game. As the game is almost a month old, and the new year is around the corner, I find myself enjoying it less and less. Hell, I barely play more than one match a day. The unfortunate timing of the game's release means there's not many players, and the lack of any publicity and advertising hurts the game's chances of even being seen. I only found out about this game from a random low-view youtube video that showed up in a recommendation for an entirely unrelated video. The extremely wild pricing of cosmetics hurts since I do want to support the devs for making a good game, yet I can't justify anything that high for a single cosmetic. I don't want to say the game is bad, because it isn't by any stretch, but there's no incentive to do anything. The game's biggest flaw is a lack of incentive. It doesn't make me want to play at all, which sucks. I want to play, but the game isn't giving me a reason to do so.I will still recommend this game since it's a rare gem, being a good game involving dragons. I will continue to hope that the devs make some drastic changes to everything, as the game does feel half-baked and out of the oven way too soon. I don't want this game to die in obscurity, but it's hard to really support it.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT, Dec. 19, 2021: My 8/10 still stands, and I'll add that it seems they've added a feature where every 10 levels you get a free random egg to hatch. I think a single-player story mode could be neat for expanding lore. I also like how when you encounter dragons enough in gameplay you unlock their models to view, it's neat. I'm excited to see what new classes they release (I predict some kind of aquatic dragon, or maybe a "magic" based dragon).Got it for free - if you're a dragon lover give it a try! One thing I think they REALLY need is some way to get eggs outside of random drops from chests or from buying them in the store. This could be solved by something like a single-player mode where you fight AI enemies and complete certain missions; you could have a set of missions for each class and at the end of each mission set you'd get an egg from that class (and rarer eggs would require harder difficulty missions). You could even use the map that's there now as a menu. This could also be a way to add more lore to the classes and dragons. But as it stands now I think it's a solid start. Good graphics, good gameplay, a fair bit of variety in game modes, I just wish there was a way to get cosmetics (like eggs/dragon skins) outside of paying or getting lucky on chests. Really solid start, just need to keep adding content - I'm looking forward to seeing more! 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow I've missed the development of this game and only discovered it recently when it was released. I was skeptical about it as  "dragonrider" games have been disappointing (for me personally) in the past. What I've seen in the couple hours I've played is a quite fun game with some GLARING problems.While the core game play feels fairly solid, the visuals, especially the UI is scaled all wrong. The flame breath, smoke/poison trails, etc are all quite large and bright on screen meaning that quick 180's leave you struggling to spot the enemy markers. Understandable against the effects I mentioned but even against the terrain they are irritatingly hard to see. I am playing on a smaller screen personally but the small, fine scale of markers, cooldown meters, etc is extreme. Outline highlights or something a little extra is needed.Usually I prefer M&K controls when they are available, as do most PC gamers. After my first couple matches had me wildly swerving back and forth, climbing and diving like a drunken fruit bat, I connected the trusty 360 controller and I've been claw scraping cliff faces and barnstorming castle ruins like a Nazgul with 2 rings. That's not really a problem, just a bit odd to me. Makes it a better candidate for console porting (later, after we get some of the wrinkles ironed).Last gripe I'll bring up is the characters. While I see the potential for plenty of unlocks in the way of armors, weapons, dragons (which you hatch and raise BTW) and other cosmetics, right now there is only one character for each class. The selection will most assuredly expand as new classes are released but come on devs. Can't we at least get one of each sex (not gender) for each class?All that said, I can't help but like this game. It controls surprisingly well and I seem to be at least half-way decent at it. I'm not having the ping disparity some others seem to be having, even with the Chinese kids. The matchmaking does tend to put them all on the same team about 90% of the time. Is this a region lock deal or something? Regardless, I've gotta recommend you try it out. It is free to play and not a very big download (for now). And I would be remiss not to mention that they actually reward you with some of their in-game currency as you level up so you can patronize the store without spending a dime. It's not Pern. It's not Berk. It's not Middle-Earth. But it's a dang good start for any aspiring dragonrider.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start this off by saying; I really wanted to like this game. Unfortunately, it's just not well executed. TLDR;Issues: Navigation is a nightmare, leveling is nigh impossible, matches are not fun due to collision death and aforementioned control issues, player base 100% targets. Good things: designs look very nice, and the cut-scene animations are well done.Full review:This game had a great concept, and I've been tracking it since it was in beta. Unfortunately, it seems another one that really falls short of being what it was intended to be. Built like smite but on dragons, CAOA tries its best to make match-style combat a unique, aerial experience. Regrettably, unlike smite, maneuver on this game is godawful. You move incredibly quickly, which presents as almost inoperable when you add speed bonuses. This of course would imply skill is the issue with navigating the boosts, but in reality it's the turn radius and steering which hinder any and all movement. Dodging is pretty much a joke in this game with a targeting system that locks on fireballs (which must be evaded at the EXACT right moment). Instead of relying on player accuracy, it turns into a game of who can spit the most fire first since you know it's almost guaranteed to hit. When in combat you default to flying, which I think actually makes it more difficult to steer in the long term. The only way to slow to a stop is by pressing S, which must be held to maintain that hover. When your entire game-play is based on functional combat and maneuvering, these faults really don't make the game enjoyable.I know this is a newer game, which is why the next part is not included in my shorthand. There are simply not enough elements yet released to make the game engaging. You have the option of 3 combat types, unranked/ranked and daily rotation. Between these three there isn't a lot of variety, and playing stagnates after a comparably short amount of time. I acknowledge games like dota, smite, etc, have been around long enough to better establish different game modes, but this is still quite boring. Pay to win elements are heavily present. It appears that most if not all of the 'better' dragons and more sought after things are behind a paywall. I understand the need to profit off a 'free' game to continue to pay developers, but as a new player it felt impossible to succeed without pouring cash into it to begin with. Overall, disappointed with the game. I wish it had been more playable, but I'll give it another year before reviewing it again and updating my commentary accordingly. High hopes that things can be better put together and/or updated.

Once??? Stupid. I'd be happy with a plain ol' tdm game. You kill someone, you get a point. The end. The game does a lot of extra things and it feels a bit too congested. A great game but the gamemodes are just so questionable. The capture the gate game? Let me make this short. If you die, in that time span someone can hop in about 3-5 gates while you are trying to spawn back in. The gates feel too linear and easy to drone into. What I like about the game: Combat feels nice, flying is 80% good. Few collision changes I would want fix but no gamebreaking. Dragon and player customization is nice. Some of the dragon skins and armors look absolutely great. I actually kind of like hatching your egg/dragon phase by completing quests. The quests are not overbearing and not difficult. They just want you to play matches to progress it essentially. I get it. The dailies and weekly quests are all not too bad and not entirely difficult either so that is a plus and chest progression system isn't too bad either when you upgrade your keys.Overall I like the grounding of the game and baseline it is pretty fun, progression for leveling is not that slow unlike Halo infinite so I cannot complain. Out of the gates, It is indeed a good game as for now though I cannot say it is balanced. It is very badly out of tuned.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games i wish steam had a "eh" button for. Yes, its fun, the combat loop is funish. Its free and you get all the actual gameplay for free so there really isnt a reason to NOT play it if you think youll like dragon rider arena combat sim 2021. This review is based on playing in early February of 2022, I dont know nor do I care if this game has improved since launch because I wasnt there. If this game does improve past this point, which the devs are saying that it will, then ill change my review accordingly. All this being said, frankly I cant recommend spending any money on this game. The progression and store is worse than halo infinite and I mean that with my whole chest. There needs to be a MASSIVE overhaul of the progression system and it needs to happen soon. If they want to give in game coins that you can purchase cosmetics with in game then fine, but make it like a reach system where you can purchase any item that meets your level at will and not have it randomly dictated by the store. Also the coins need to be increased about 2x or 3x if they commit to that route. They could go a season pass route and have you pay like 10 bucks and unlock content, that would be understandable as well. But right now its really sucky because you can see all of the things you can customize and its great, but then you have no ability to actually customize those things. Playing for 4 hours I unlocked about 4 things and all of them were random drops essentially. No way to choose a cosmetic for say, the class I actually like playing. I have not unlocked a single class specific item for the class I have played most with for 4 hours of gameplay (3 1/2 most likely in match), and I have no way of doing so without spending money. The day I began playing there was nothing even able for me to purchase for said class with the in game silver coins.One thing I do like is the egg system and I wish it could be expanded on a little bit because its actually unique. If you get a dragon egg you need to progress in combat to actually have that dragon grow. I like it, its better than just buying a dragon skin and plopping it onto your mount like its the horse armor DLC. It actually gives you some modicum of connection with your dragon and it probably singlehandedly kept me coming back because I was just so interested in growing it and getting it to adulthood. Not even really paying attention to the lack of progression going on around me. But then the egg you get runs out and from about level 4-10 its just a grind till the next egg. This is the stretch where I realized the problems going on around me with the customization system. I have seen some discussion of community dying and matchmaking taking long, Im in NA and I cant really say ive had that problem. Its about 30 seconds to a minute to find a match. So thats a plus. Basically, I like the game and combat, the store seems overpriced and the progression is slow as balls. I want to like the game, I do, and if any serious improvements are made ill change the review and probably spend some money because I like putting my wallet where my mouth is, and I dont expect game devs to work for free. I have gone back and forth between giving it a thumbs up or down and im going to go with down, but If the game keeps me coming back for upwards of 10 hours and i didnt spend a dime ill probably change it to a thumbs up. Hope the game gets better, really want to route for em. Dont recommend spending money until you see it happen though. Also please for the love of god let me skip the tutorial in the beginning. I cant recommend it to my friends and have their first impression be 15 minutes of forced tutorial. Review is over but this is essentially a breakdown of my time.hour 1, okay this is cool learning the combat, getting into matches.hour 2 ♥♥♥♥ yeah dragon egg lets level it up lets gooohour 3 okay, nothing is happening. hour 4 aight imma head out.
