The limited amount of dragon models are beautifully textured and fly intuitively. The controls could certainly use a little more polish, but they're easy enough to figure out. Mastering controls is another story and can be frustrating especially when playing tougher competition. The matchmaking isn't the best. I have a lot of matches where I'm either destroying everyone or I can' even get off of the platform. Getting into ranked reveals the weakens of the anti-cheat system. Ranked is PLAGUED with all sorts of tomfoolery. I watched a player fly around the map with such unrelenting  hyper speed that I immediately went to YouTube to find out how to replicate it, only to find that is a cheat that was being used. The cheaters in this game are unabashed about it. In summary, the game is fun. Stay away from ranked until they figure out anti-cheat. Enjoy the beautiful visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is that kind of a review that I wish I had a So-So button. I hope the devs can take a look and maybe do something because this game can turn into a real gem with some fixes (not necessarily easy fixes, but it needs more meat).The Good:- The game is free! Like, seriously! Great quality for a free game and certainly made me wonder why it is free to play until about three hours or so in (will cover in the "bad" section".- Quality, yes, I said it above - sound, music, graphics, dragons - there was a lot of love and attention put into this game.- Can get your attention for a while, has training, easy to pick up and play, has ranked match system, cross platform system, reward system, level system, doesn't make you choose a mode over the other unless you need it for daily/weekly (yes, there are new quests every day).- Achievements? Yes!- Three Dimensional battles with up and down, dives, precision flight through obstacles or around them? You got it!- Did I say dragons?- Has a fun element to it.- Doesn't crash.- Gameplay is fluid, mouse and keyboard a bit taxing on those hand muscles (don't have a controller, so can't say much about that).The game is very fun to play, can be intense, can have moments that you sit with your fingers on your pulse and its about to pop.With all that, yes, unfortunately the Bad:-- The dodging system is umm... yeah, whatever, it is basically trying to hide behind something to break line of sight. That is not dodging; thats hide and seek. I wish you could use double-tap a key or anything like that, even a 180 turn or some evasive maneuvers? Anything? No. Too bad. It has lots of potential, but unfortunately, it is too simple and not working well, especially when sitting on you with fire breath.-- There are only three characters. Your rider is linked to the Dragon, making the dragon and the rider one character. Yes you can customize their looks, but that is it. Rewards are for looks only, so it doesnt matter if you are level 1 or level 100, if you have the same gear, it is not going to matter because the stats stay the same. -- Each character has only two special attacks, and you have to choose one from them for a battle. Also only one **Ultimate**. Getting eggs for new dragons gives you only a new skin. You dont get a new dragon with new abilities, different stats, etc. It doesnt matter if you have a rare dragon or not, it is just a skin. So after a few hours when you went through all three characters you realize that thats it. There is not new experience with lets say new different dragons that can do different things or new characters, or items are not doing anything, skins are just skins, and the game is becoming somewhat stale at that point.-- Balance... As my grandma used to say "Oi Vei". The game is really not balanced. The characters, while all are great and a lot of fun, are clearly not at the same "power level". There is also no I choose to play this to counter that, and while its fun, it can get very brutal once you get one shot by a Marauder, or one shot by the Phantom, but the Windguard has a cloud of poison that unless your enemy is really stupid, everyone runs out of it. It can be nice, but not the same as the others. The Windguard saving grace is its ability to protect others, but you have to see others and aim at them, which is a bit hard because the game is really fast.-- Movement can be better and a bit smoother. It is the least problematic, but even with the mouse senstivity turned all the way up, it is somewhat slow.-- No reason to play Ranked. I really see no reason to do it. Ranked games dont trigger quest or achievements, they dont give a lot of anything, there is not sense of reward from ranked game. So why playing ranked? You level the same way, even slower because there is only one map for ranked, and it is resources based map and the more complicated one.-- Maps, only four all together, one is the tutorial map.-- PVP map, Spoils of War is too random for ranked PvP, with too many elements going on - coffer lock/jewel/bomb. It feels like a messy Harry Potter Quidich game that can be fun, but not as a ranked option.-- Map triggers like special events are not balanced and can ruin an entire game. One of the maps will have you hoarding gold, and while thats a cool idea, this map has the most annoying mechanics. The enemy can lock your coffers so you cant hoard gold until you get the key. Then there is a bomb that if the enemy brings it to your tower it blows up and you lose 50% or so of your gold that floats around your tower and the enemy can take it. That by itself can either tip the game or snowball it of you have a lead. There is also a jewel, but that part is alright - one player has to carry it and gives a sum of points, but even then, the points are just to much.-- Fire Breath... Short range but super OP! Hard to get away from because it autolocks on a target and has quiet a range to it. So while you can outsmart the homing shots, the firebreath is the bane of everyone's existance. In my opinion it is working great and how it should be, but this should bring us back to the dodge mechanic I have brought up earlier - use some sort of stamina resource to let you dodge. You you use it all or your opponent is more skilled than you? Too bad. But right now, without it, the opponent can tail you and burn you down good.-- It feels like a beautiful and fun person that you meet, then you go out on a date, take home and have lots of fun, but then by the morning you realize that that is it and that person is somewhat shallow and there will be nothing more exciting than the night before, which is sad, because the game can be absolutely awesome. But this is also why it is free to play - because while the skeleton is strong, there is not much past that. Unfortunate.-- PVP Ranking system is weird. The matchmaking is off. You can get your entire group to be low level and the enemy group can be high levels which shows a difference in experience. Also you get about 4-10 points when you win a match, but lose 25 when you lose. I have been winning two or three fights just to lose another and lose that entire progression and more. It's very taxing. Looking at some rankings, there are some people with 400 wins to 3 losses... like, really? I can understand a 4 to 1 K/d ratio, but 99% to win ratio? How?Again, altogether I think its a great game and its a free game, and I think it has lots of potential, but it is not there yet. I hope the devs will listen and change things, because honestly, a game about dragons that only has three dragons is... Think of playing League of Legends, but there are only three characters with one ability each? It gets boring, fast. Think of playing Call of Duty, Ghost Recon, or any PvP game, but with three playable characters that can only do very basic and limited things, and unlocks adds nothing but looks.More dragons, maybe different parts give some different stats here and there, more abilities? Different types of dragons? Not all fire. What about Ice that slows enemies? Or lightning that drains stamina? Poison that can cause daze? More creative approach would be amazing and interesting.But until then, the game feels stale and I have only played it for about 9 hours? It is not that it is not fun, obviously, I wouldn't spend that much time if it was not. The issue is that after the 3 hours mark you realize that this is it. There is nothing new to see or to do, no new or better experience, unless you are only here for the visuals.Currently, the game feels like a slight waste of time, and it makes me sad to even write this, but at the moment it is a hard miss of great potential. I did get a starter pack for $5 to show support for this game (which I don't usually do) because I believe it can go very far and hope the devs take all of the issues to heart on work them out.

_childDocuments_.review: I felt the need to update this review now years into the game's lifespan with no sign of improvement. As you might guess from over 1k hours of gameplay, I gave this game more than a fair go, I was actually a partner with them for some time, able to stream on their steam page and beyond. I took part in the betas before release, as well as a pre-release event before the game was actually finally released in the wild. TL;DR: I would not recommend getting into this game to... anybody. There's several reasons, I'll bring them down as follows for those that actually want to read a review: The good: - Beautiful graphics and gorgeous artwork. (Seriously the art team knocks it out of the park.)- Fun PvP concept. - Dragons! (We don't have enough cool dragon-riding games) - Decent customization. The bad: - All of the gameplay.  - Exorbitantly expensive premium shop.- P2W abilities (that can be earned in game only after an eternity of grinding)- Prohibitive battlepass system- Disorganized development team with an us vs them mentality towards their playerbase and frequent turnover.My Personal History: - Former moderator of their discord. (Left due to terrible community management and lack of care to improve from both Playwing and moderators at the time.) - Former Top 10 Player in the game (doesn't matter much anymore, didn't matter back then either.)- 1k Hours of Gameplay spanning from release in 2021 to fall 2023. - Former partner of their game streaming team. This game has made some heavy missteps in its development, frankly a case study on how not to manage a game. At the time of release, things were chaotic, people were optimistic, and the crowds were hungry. 12k Concurrent playercount was by all means a big success for an "indie" dev. While decline was expected, had they managed it well, they should have been able to maintain good momentum with their player base but: - The team released the game, then left for THREE WEEKS during the peak of the holidays while the game was still non-functional. Stating that a team was on standby to handle any critical issues (except they apparently weren't). The Store was stocked with pure premium currency items, and games were practically unplayable. - The community management team s eemed at times muzzled and at times simply unable to provide answers for no good reason other than an apparent lack of desire or ability to communicate. This contributed to previous community managers departing out of frustration. - The moderator team dealt with the community with a heavy hand, silencing criticism and often resorting to bans for first time and minor infractions. (leading to the great Bell War of 2021) By the time a month rolled around 12k Players had dropped down to 1.2k as a combination of network issues, lack of communication, and terrible balancing took their toll. One class dominated early meta: Phantom. Make no mistake, gameplay heavily favored the phantom's untargetable invisibility, extremely long rage power, and buggy mines. Instead of gradual balancing changes done in tweaks at the suggestions of the playerbase, this was largely ignored with the initial reasoning given often coming down to "We've been developing games for a combined 20 years, you've only been playing for a few hours we know better." There was essentially no quality management as far as feedback went. It was either all or nothing with the developers and then what was implemented was usually counter intuitive to what most people were requesting. As a result we saw the implementation of additional cosmetics/cosmetic features (like hatching eggs and raising baby wyverns) over the balancing of  PvP in general which needs more rapid iteration. The number of players continued to decline dramatically. Don't just take my word for it, you can likewise check the charts of this game's history. It has never recovered from these dramatic initial mistakes. The majority of the active playerbase warned:- Rage system would destroy balance. (it did.)- Premium store was too expensive. (It continues to be, and remains unobtainable due to lack of regional pricing adjustments.) - Founder Packs were misadvertised. (They were, offered after release and later on iterations on the models/patterns found within the pack released.) - Premium packs were too frequent and too expensive. (After Founder Packs were removed, Arisen Packs went up for the same price differences, and a very short lived 'Lone Roar Pack' featured for 80 USD until it was removed due to backlash.) All this and more was continually ignored, other very unpopular issues included: Lack of reward for playing, removal of gem rewards post Season 0 for leveling, the introduction of battle passes with Season 1 closely mimicking the model of a much more popular game (Rhymes with Fortnight if you know what I mean), events that only favored players that knew how to abuse already badly balanced classes, exploits, and game time with little rewards for those that at least played the event. There was also a focus on adding more game modes before class balance was sorted, while maps were slow to be updated or otherwise ignored. "Lore" was introduced with the battlepasses that was hastily written and poorly translated. The leaderboard was often dominated by groups early on but they tried everything else before introducing a solo/duo queue and by then the game had essentially already been limping on two broken legs. Balances were often wide ranging and overtuned, playing into one another in a negative feedback loop of granting major dominance from one class to another. The UI was updated into something much harder to read for a majority of the playerbase. The in-game match UI was also made unnecessarily difficult to read. Going from clear reticles with visible (albeit at times buggy) HP bars to awkward floating bars and a hazy generalized reticle. Accessibility is abysmal. Advanced video options were never added. The developer (Playwing) saw a slash in funding basically two months in and a huge turnover of staff including one of the original game designers and product leads. The community itself also became very cruel, not to mention dangerous for some individuals. The moderators were known (at the time that I was active) for being petty and vindictive, fighting amongst themselves and dealing heavy punishment to anyone who didn't sing Playwing's graces or just didn't sit right with them. As a moderator I had to fight numerous times to adjust punishment scales so that people weren't being thrown out for the most petty things. I also had to stop individuals from exercising personal vendettas against individuals otherwise unaware of issues. The community manager that came in during the tumultuous first year after the best one was fired also fed the flames. Patch notes were often very basic and uninformative, with more details added only after people begged and even then often missing the details that people later discovered in the game itself like balance tweaks, map adjustments and even movement effects/UI elements. Customer support was abysmal at best, with people waiting months for a resolution that could potentially never come. I myself had tickets that never were answered or effectively solved. Events continued to be pushed out, favored in frequency over working on the issues in the base game, some bugs which continue to persist today. There's too much history and too many issues for me to go through, but it all comes down to bad feedback weighting and implementation.My recommendation? Find another game. I know that sucks to say but this game does not deserve your time or your money. Take it from someone who played it damn near obsessively for close to a year. It breaks my heart, but I don't see it surviving for much longer, or gaining much more than 100 concurrent players for the forseeable, necrotic future.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is very good, well optimized of course with some bugs but its overall fun! I love the mechanics and its not a pay to win game! There is a few problems so I'll list the pros and consPros:Cool designs for each dragonBeautiful backgroundsThere is no invisible walls meaning areas that you think you can slip through YOU CANCool abilitiesFun gamemodesMostly chill communityAnd active DevsPlayable for MOST computers and consoleNot pay to win. The only thing you have to pay for is rare items or skins and they dont change any aspect of the gameplay, its just customizing your character and dragon.ConsSmall playerbase and ALOT of players are beta testers or top 500 meaning youll be thrown into high ranking games most of the time and youll keep seeing the same players over an over, and it gets worse if its six stacks. Sadly the playerbase isnt high enough for the Devs to properly fix matchmaking.Lags when there are multiple effects going on at once. When abilities activate, the effects can lag your entire game which can get you killed pretty easily. (Using beserk, rage, or smoke trail)This game is STILL new. There isnt alot of diverse classes, we got the support Damage dealer, and tanky hard hitter, but each one of them dosent work the way you would think they would. If you want more diverse characters wait a bit! Theres only 3 dragons available so I suggest just waiting a bit! This isnt really a con just more so a warning.No one really uses VC: This is a huge team game so it can very much hinder you when your teammates are wayy below the skill level youre at and rarley people communicate, your best bet is discord.Thats about it though, the Devs sometimes will change things no one asked to be changed or wanted but oh well. Overall its a very good game and I hope the playerbase expands because it deserves it.

_childDocuments_.review: Century is exactly what it says. A dragon dog-fighting game. At the time of this review, it has only been out for a few days, and there are definitely some issues, but most of them are minor and will probably be fixed very soon. The gameplay itself is really fun. It can take a little bit to get used to the controls, but once you do it feels like you're actually controlling a dragon. There's a lot of skill involved in order to maximize the potential of each class, and you'll definitely need to learn all the tricks in order to perform at a high level.There's also a surprising amount of customization, you can change each armor piece your dragon wears, as well as the armor and weapons of the rider. These don't affect the gameplay at all so its purely about making your dragon look as cool as you want.Overall I'd recommend this game if you like dog-fighting games or you just want to ride around on a dragon. I'm very much enjoying my time with it and I'm excited to see where it goes in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: In all honesty I cannot recommend this game to anybody who likes to have fun in competitive games.Anyway:-You will not have fun as a new player. You will be curb stomped by a handful of vets coordinating their actions through discord 9 games out of 10. Maybe more. Because there's no matchmaking based on skill or time played.-The sheer incompetence of current managment of this game is baffling. You may think that all the tricks for f2p games to keep people playing are well known for a long time, but CEOs (or whoever is responsible for this game) seem to steer clear from them and instead keep adding overpriced cosmetics.-All the rewards are laughable. You get a little bit of in-game-currency coins for a match and that's it. Very little things in the shop are bought with coins. You can win a chest with random rewards once a week, but the percentage of good reward drops is minuscule even in the best chest. Dragon pass is a bit better, but you need to buy access to it with real money, and with each season rewards are getting worse.-Devs promised (and actually made) a permanent PVE game mod, but alas! it was taking players away from the PVP mods, so it was shut down.-The game is very repetitive, new maps are very rarely released (and some of them are just recolors of existing ones) so it gets boring pretty fast.-After reduction of player number in matches from 6vs6 to 4vs4 game became even more unfair to solo players.Ok now the good parts:-Graphics are pretty nice! Designs and animations of the dragons are also very cool. Existing maps are full of fun nooks and details. Baby dragons are adorable! And there is a cool little quest system to make them grow. Too bad you likely won't see them because dragon eggs are barely in the game now.-Matches are short, dynamic and fast paced. Flying feels nice.-Easy controls.-It is not pay-to-win. There are classes and abilities you can purchase in game for in-game currency, but those are pretty balanced- they might add some new playstyles but won’t make anybody more OP.-I don’t think there are cheaters there. Probably. Maybe because I cannot fathom why anybody would want to cheat in an almost dead game with almost no rewards¯\_(ツ)_/¯

_childDocuments_.review: Set in a Dark Fantasy world, Century: Age of Ashes is a third person multiplayer arena battle video game in which the player can mount dragons and fight with them. In the game, players have to choose between three classes before each game, each with its unique design, abilities and customisation: Marauder, Windguard and Phantom. The Marauder is a skilled hunter that can mark its prey. The Windguard is a supporting class that can shield its allies and the Phantom is a stealthy assassin that can cloak itself. Each class is bound to a specific kind of dragon.The game currently includes three 6 versus 6 game modes: Gates of Fire, a “capture the flag” like game mode, Carnage, a team deathmatch game mode, and Spoils of War. Spoils of War is a new game mode that was announced in November 2021. A 3 versus 3 game mode is also available.During a game, players can fly across the maps, shoot the enemy team using Fireball, Dragonbreath or different skills unique to each class, and dodge enemy attacks.Century: Age of Ashes has been developed by Playwing Bordeaux since 2017. Pascal Barret, art director, and Emmanuel Nouaille, creative director of the game came up with the idea in 2014. Their goal was to create an aerial dragon fighting game with a competitive aspect. They started working on the game on the Unreal Engine 3 with a small team and resources, before being approached by Playwing in 2017. The game has since shifted to a development on the Unreal Engine .Century: Age of Ashes was announced during the 2020 Game Awards ceremony.[4] The game was originally scheduled to release via Early Access in February 2021, but was delayed to April 2021. After their second closed beta,[5] the developers decided to postpone the release of the game following beta feedback.A new trailer for the game was featured during the 2021 Gamescom, announcing a release date of December 2, 2021, and introducing the addition of baby dragons, as well as a new game mode.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to anyone who is into PVP. There is ranked, unranked and arena. Many different game modes to play and experience. Some of the things being uneven teams when someone decides to disconnect. Ranked has unbalanced skill levels matched up against each other. There was also a point in time where you could choose the game modes you wanted to play. Now that is no longer an option and your favourite game mode might only come up once a week. The game also has a Beastiary where you can obtain dragons via events, shop, or season pass. They used to have an old leveling system where you were able to obtain dragon eggs, gems, etc. but that doesn't seem to exist anymore. Instead its been replaced by a season pass which has very little free items to unlock and most of it behind a paywall. The majority of the dragons in the shop are for gems which requires real currency to purchase. It becomes an issue when one dragon seems to cost about fifteen or more dollars just to purchase. You may also grind for silver coins to purchase dragons as well that allow you to use this in-game currency. However, that being said it is not required to purchase dragons to enjoy the game. Really more a matter of collection purposes if you're into collecting all the skins.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I've already written a review, and it was a little too soon for me to completely judge the game. But now, I think I can,The gameplay is not as bad as I thought it was in the beginning, although sometimes when I try to drift, my dragon wont boost, but that's just a minor nuisance. What I still don't like is the Keyboard controls that remain, in my mind, to be rather clunky and unpredictable. Either too sensitive or very slow which makes movement a little finicky. I had to watch guides on movement to even stand a chance out there. And don't get me started on matchmaking, one of my most recent games, I, level 12, was pit up against two level 26 players, who completely smashed us even when they were a man short. My irritation grows with each passing hour i force myself to play through this torture game, constantly being pitted against skilled opponents and coordinated teams and with rookie teammates. What's my level 2 marauder teammate going to do?  On the same topic of matchmaking I want to add that the punishments for leaving a current game is way too lax. I checked and got around 15-30 seconds of time-out when leaving a match for the first time, how is that going to prevent me from not leaving again. (And not to mention that it seems to reset back to the lowest amount after a while as i assume the timer slowly scales up with every time you consecutively ditch matches. Unless you only get 30 seconds of waiting each time which is-.. pretty meek to say the least) And then again there is an actual option for us to leave the match. And the people who do are removed from the match board so you can't take note of the name of the person who left, but there's also no way to report them, so again, no punishment for handicapping you team. I dare not even think about when hackers manage to slip their way in somehow, and there's no way to report them. I would not recommend this game to anyone who is solo, or casual, or anyone but the hardcore rank climbers with a full team of good players, because there's only a slim chance you can win on your own with rando teammates and a lack of communication. What could help this game would be adding some PvE activities for the more casual players. Like big raids against mega bosses, wild dragon taming, breeding for rarer dragon skins, personalizing the Dragoneers more. Give us something other than being assridden by lvl 20+ players over and over, on repeat.  Or, they could just fix the games matchmaking in general. The merged regions was a terrible idea because some people are seriously teleporting around. This game has a solid amount of players, so splitting them up wouldn't hurt, maybe longer wait times but I'd rather wait than play with a tping enemy team.. I am willing to bet most of the new players will play through the tutorial, only to be completely owned in rookie matches, and leaving once they realize the matchmaking is the way it is. It'll only hurt the game's growth in the future and I do want it to succeed and show the world dragon games can work. But what I have experienced has been pretty bad overall so far, which is a great shame. This game has such good potential to be up there with the greats.

_childDocuments_.review: The meta has already been defined, and the main reason that the "Killer" achievement is so rare is due to it being so easy to pick up and immediately put down. With TL:DR ||VAs to define the meta, its best to lay it out as it is. There are three maps to my knowledge of the game: Desert (CQB & Traps), MOBA-like thing (Long range & Traps), and a snowy mountain (A general rounded arena for the three). Now, you would think that in an aerial combat game, traps would not be as useful or required to play. But before delving into that subject, the classes. The Marauder (Coloured Red) sounds like your average damage dealer, with a marking ability and the option of flares (Gust) or fox 3 "special" stuns (Frostbolts, pretty obvious). With the prevalence of a modern-ish armament, this seems like the modest choice to win most fights, but it isn't. Its short "guns" (Firebreath) counters its DPS potential to being the main or offensive tank within "Gamer" terms or whatnot. The Windguard (coloured Green) doesn't sound too special, sounding more like a tank than the Marauder, but is the games support. Having a Shielding dash for when you are in the position to be a wingman tends to help turn teamfights around, when either you or your support stops becoming Maveric and realize they are more helpful as Goose. It also comes equiped with Chaffs (Smokescreen, you wont need it for "zoning" ever) and a Concussive Blast (conveniently, named Blast. Does what it says, and is barely used.) It has mid of the line "gun" range with mid damage, so some gun solutions if you want to approach them. A typical offensive support, no strong "true" or defensive capabilities except for Chaffs but tbh dont trust it.The reason that the Main Damage Dealer hasn't made an appearance yet is because it is the Phantom as of now and Thor: Love and Thunder is only given to the top 100 at the end of the season for free. Someday. I'm not joking, its basically someday. We don't know. Back to talking about this annoyance of a goth stage, this dude has the furthest "gun" and the weakest damage. Already off to a bad start, surprisingly that's just about it. Comes equipped with a visual/lock-on radar jammer as standard. A jammer. Compared to a dash, and a mark. Anyways, the main issue I have with it is its mine (yes, a mine. CQB & Trap/Zone capable. You should see where im going) and a Concussive blast (dont want to give him too much now.) and thats about it for the meta, he can strafe you as you barely put a dent on his map control. Feels weird saying it without any stack tactics to be seen.Now the reason people cant seem to rack up a 50 on the board. The easy way in and out is to say it is hard. It is not, completely. It can be difficult at times, and can be exceptionally easy at others, its just a roll of the dice to what the matchmaking systems do with 500 players. Flying can use a few tune ups, specifically the use of viffing (V/STOL use to achieve incredibly sharp turns, binded to brake or S) close quarters slalom (so you dont become a pancake every so often) climb speed and energy/momentum usage. I dont want the game to suddenly become DCS if that is what you have read, its that the need for an auto aim system so sharp, it turns ninety degrees on a regular basis is absurd.TL:DR: Phantom or you could be considered throwing, gaming trinity half or even quarter baked due to map capabilities alone, not even ability based. No free content past the desert stripes camo and a few bits and bobs. Fully realized storefront, albeit almost all storefronts tend to be fully realized off the bat. Horizontal aerial gameplay. And thats all you need to know.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much better than many online multiplayer games. The game modes are styled in such a way that losing players get a boost (Going Berserk), people who leave matches early get a penalty (First strike is a five minute ban, second is thirty minutes), and it is incredibly easy to grind and level up due to the many XP boosters. Its also not pay-to-win. See those packs? They only provide skins and armor, none of which affect gameplay. Plus, getting gems is as easy as leveling up, as levels that end in 5 gain 250 gems each time they are reached (15,25,65, etc.). You also get to raise dragons instead of just equiping them as skins, which gives a sense of achivement when you final get to ride it. There is also little to no learning curve, so getting into Century is as easy as installing it! Overall, I would give this game an 11/10!

In fact if they expanded upon this, I wouldn't mind fronting cash here and there for more extensive customisation options, its just for what its offering theirs so damn little for such a hefty price it isnt worth it in my eyes.The next issue is how limited this game is. You have solo mode, 4v4 in treasure hunting, carnage (which is basically trying to eliminate as many players as possible), and relic hunting (which is a version of capture the flag.) All in all their really isnt much to do or grind for in this game, and addicting as the matches are, eventually you WILL get bored.For the devs: What you have is a solid idea for a game, but id seriously consider expanding. I know for a fact if you added full customisation options you would have more players interested in playing. Id suggest adding Race, hair, armour, dragon, ect, options. Another idea could be adding customised nesting area you can decorate for dragons and your character, you can add a free flight option in this solo type mode where you can design a small flight area for you and your dragon to practice in. there can be a small variety of chosen landscapes for the flight area you can pay or grind for.Another suggestion if you insist on a a pay wall, is adding three modes of dungeon hunting. Having two teams try and defeat a dungeon filled with enemies and rare loot. Each mode has a higher chance for rare loot and legendary items, which you could add as a pay option (ie: dungeon one: free , dungeon 2: 500 coins, dungeon 3: 2,000 coins or 100 blood, ect..) it would make matches more exciting.

_childDocuments_.review: Played around 13.9 hours in the beta, as well as 31.7+ hours as of present.May update this review as more comes out; but for now...Century is a dog-fighting game where instead of aeroplanes you are fighting on dragonback.This game as of 2021-13-15 (Time of review written) has 3 classes. - A DPS-centric class focused on dishing out damage in quick succession. - A 'stealth' class focused on trap-setting and dealing bursts of high damage. - A support class focused on buffing allies and area-control rather than damage.Marauder and Phantom are both fairly balanced, and of the three have the most options for avoiding taking damage from other players.Windguard could use some work on its defence tactics, but as of right now it is top tier when it comes to supporting the rest of the team.These are the gameplay pros / cons I've noted so far. - Controls smoothly, and controls are very reactive making it easy to react quickly in combat situations.- Graphics are incredibly gorgeous, especially for a F2P game.- As of right now, not P2W. Only thing you'll really be spending money on are optional cosmetics and XP boosters if you're looking to level up faster. (Said XP boosters also provide boosts to players not using one.)- Decent variety of skins, though expect to see the same legendary skins a lot as there are very few currently.- Targeting is simplistic and easy to grasp.- Learning curve is fairly low, with controls being easy to get a handle on.- Matchmaking times are fairly quick.- Very easy to get in game and play matches with friends.- Your in-game stats are easy to locate and look at on your in-game profile.- Levelling is easy to accomplish, you can easily make 2000+ XP per 5 minute match.- Matchmaking is quite random and you'll often end up with unbalanced teams.- Few options for dealing with opponent's close quarters firebreath.- Currently no way of earning skins for free aside from levelling.- Early-leaving penalty is a bit broken, and can penalize you for crashing mid-game.- Currently no way of rejoining a match if your game has crashed / your connection was lost.- When equipping cosmetics, previews/icons are only visible within the menus and not when you're viewing your rider / dragon as a whole.As a whole I've thoroughly enjoyed Century from beta to its current release, and look forwards to what the developers do with the game in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game since the 2nd beta in early 2021. I can optimistically say that this is by far the worst state the game has ever seen. Upon release the developers released "Founder packs" made exclusive for those who played the game since the beginning, rewarding the OG's. Just last week, they spit in our faces and released a reskin of the flagship founder pack dragon, Aelion.This is nothing compared to what the recent announcement entails. The skill ceiling in this game revolved around map knowledge, and player movement given auto-aim fireballs, auto-lock flamebreath, and generally easy to use abilities. Now they've introduced new abilities that you have to BUY ($5 for ONE). The developers used to take pride in how they created a game where everyone started on equal footing, and skins/items were purely cosmetic (similar to Rocket League). They ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ruined that.Then, they also announced that they will be switching the premier gamemodes (Carnage, Spoils of War, Gates of Fire) from 6v6 to 4v4. This entails that we will have COMICALLY large maps for far less players.Worst of all for me personally, is the announcement of a "Dodge" Mechanic. I would consider myself a pretty good player, I've been playing since beta, have 800 hours in the game, peaked top ten on two seperate event leaderboards, and in the Solo/Duo ranked leaderboard I currently sit at #3 (peaked #1). As I stated before, the skill in the game primarily came from map/locational awareness, and player movement. The Dodge that they are adding completely spits on this, previously you had to know how to time your boost and brake, notice a projectile tracking you, and use your own creativity to avoid the ensuing player. Now all of that comes at the push of one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ button. This is devastating, the true uniqueness of this game was the beauty in it's movement, and now the developers have broken it.Do not play this game if you value your time. Do not financially support these money hungry devs and fall into their pay2win model.

_childDocuments_.review: Love it!  I usually get motion sick with a lot of games; this one I have zero problem with.  Very fast paced; always something to do. _childDocuments_.review: It's the Jessica Simpson of video games: Beautiful, but completely lacking in substance.On the positive side, it's free, the dragons and maps look amazing, and you  feel like you're Daenarys Targaryen ruining the last season of Game of Thrones. It's the closest you will ever come to feeling like you're riding a fire-breathing monster of destruction riding to the defense - or destruction - of your kingdom.Unfortunately, as a pure PvP sandbox it has attracted a hardcore playerbase unrelenting to incoming newbies (like my daughter), and completely toxic community. _childDocuments_.review: To put it simply, I have 2 criteria when it comes to deciding whether a game is good or not. I find that things like story and music are different things to critisize and require different skillsets to do so. What makes a game good to me is whether or not it works (as intended or otherwise), and if it's fun, cause I'll be f***ed if Im gonna spend hours of boredom just to get some arbitray accomplishment.So is Century these things? Yeah I would say so, if you like a fast paced competetive action game that is. Its gameplay is definitely fun and the reward programs (nesting dragon eggs for new skins and earning rewards through level up and randomly rather than just buying a lootbox) are well, rewarding. So if you like this kind of gameplay, yeah it's a good time. If you find trouble keeping track of fast moving targets, or you want to play something more akin to brain chess against your opponents, maybe not so much.So the game is fun, and it works on a fundamental basis. So what's wrong with it and why is it getting so many negative reviews? Well that would be the effect of its matchmaking system. To be completely honest, the matchmaking system is not particularly good as it is at launch. There's no support for your team if a team member (or god forbid your entire team) leaves, as in no bots or anything. And there yet to be any in gane communication tools. To play devils advocate on that note, I don't think this is a game that would necessarily support the typical communication tools you see in other games. The gameplay is too fast to effectively type something out and the mouse based controls don't align well with an emote wheel or anything of that nature. Im sure there are options, but it's important to take into account that we're not dealing with an cod style fps or a war thunder esc battle sim. This is a very different beast to handle when it comes to game design and we as players and reviewers should recognize that.So basically, if you need a tl;dr, the game is good. But I would probably get a group of buddies to play over discord with if you want a consistently good time. It is free to play, and it doesn't even take up a lot of hard drive space, so it should be a pretty easy sell to anyone else you might want to play with.One thumb up for a fun gameOne thumb held cautiously at center for online features, let's hope they improve it soon.

Every match has people from the other ends of the world, leavers, and people a bazillion ranks higher than you.- The gameplay is unbelievably basic. An arcade, low time-to-kill dogfighter with absolutely NOTHING youve not seen a hundred times before.   - The maps, game modes, classes, attacks and skills are all bland as hell and theres zero innovation.   - The dragons dont fly like living, wing-flapping beings but like spacecraft-fighterjets. Theres no momentum, no weight, no collisions, you dont even go faster in a dive. The basic fireball is heat-seeking on lock-on. A huge missed opportunity - its not a dragon-game but a space-game with a dragon skin.Hugely disappointing. The amazing customization progression is fatally let down by the pedestrian game that carries it.

_childDocuments_.review: I heard about this game about a year ago during one of the showcase conferences. Completely forgot about it until now, so figured I'd try the cool dragon flying game. With Draconia and DGP both in development, it looks like a great year for dragon focused games.So right off the bat the gameplay is REALLY solid. The movement is the most important aspect and it does an incredible job with it. Te aerial manoeuvres feel amazing to play with, there's nothing like being chased by an enemy, rounding a corner and hard breaking then finishing off their sorry behind with some flame breath. Partner this with some high BPM tunes and it'll really have your heart pumping. The three classes are pretty solid with the only differences being secondary skills (focusing on stealth, healing and pure damage styles respectfully). Hopefully for the next class they add something tank-focused with melee skill, that'd feel super cool.There only seems to be 3 maps at the moment (desert, alpine and snow) but I understand that it's still pretty new, and this is how most free-to-play games operate. Only complaint is that it's not really an even spread and you go streaks where you get one map a LOT.The downsides come when you step away from the gameplay. If you care at all about cosmetics, expect to spend money. You very rarely get anything in level ups that isn't just a tagline, icon or a pre-match banner, and let's face it we only care about how our dragons look because that's all you're seeing in game (your rider can be customised but they're not at all noticeable during matches). You also get a standard currency, but what do you even spend it on? Almost everything in there is bought using flat out cash (and it ain't cheap) or the premium gem currency- which you get a small amount of every 5 levels, naturally you'd have to spend many many hours to level up enough to actually buy anything with them, and even longer to buy anything significant with the purely earned currency. I'm not even sure how you get dragon body customisation parts other than the cash shop bundles, because they aren't in the level up or weekly mission rewards.I give this game a thumbs up only because the core gameplay is really, really damn fun (but it's on thin ice). I'll never get tired of swooping around, flying through broken walls and diving down into narrow canyons. If you can find a few friends to team up with on voice chat it'd be pleasantly chaotic.If Century had an optional buy-to-play version that drastically increased drops of cosmetic items for those of us that want to support development and see where this game goes without the godawful cash shop, i'd welcome it.TLDR: It's free, might as well try it. If you don't care about skins and just wanna shoot fireballs, you'll love this.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited eagerly for this game and while it has a lot of potential and was fun to play at launch, it's gone down the drain. The graphics are fantastic, the gameplay mechanics can be really fun with a few bugs to work out, and the dragons are perfect. There are only 3 classes to play as and a handful of maps to play on, so if you like variety this won't be for you. Unless you want to spend hours a day grinding away at the game it's not worth it. You can spend hours and days grinding to earn very little XP and complete daily and weekly missions to earn pitiful rewards that do not make up for all the time you've put into the game. The rewards you get when leveling up, if you can earn enough XP, are mediocre and there is no randomization, everyone gets the same rewards and too bad for you if your reward happens to be for a class you don't play as. And while you've been playing the game and grinding away, you've spent the entire time being slaughtered by gangs of high ranking players because the matchmaking still hasn't been fixed or improved. The only changes the devs made to the matchmaking is to make levels invisible so you no longer know who you're playing against. If you point out you're not having fun being beaten down constantly or ask for help in learning to play, a resounding "get good" is the only reply you get from the community now that almost everyone else has left. If you actually like competitive PVP, too bad for you because the ranked mode is only open for about 4 hours a day instead of 24/7 the way it was when the game launched. Overall, just a lot of wasted potential in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, hear me out. This game is beautiful, a great concept and free. Several different game modes and up to 6 players per team which means 6 friends having a great time. Mechanics of the game are extensive but easy to understand for a seasoned gamer and controls can be customized. They only have a few maps so it can feel repetitive but with the alternating game modes in quick play each game regardless of the map is a new experience. My issue falls within the matchmaking experience. I'm a casual gamer. I like to have fun and go against other people that are equally matched against me. I don't like completely destroying another team. I also don't find getting completely destroyed constantly being fun either. There are a lot of players who have created factions, you can find them in discord. They play as a team and when together you can't do anything but spawn in and die over and over. These players are teamed against new people who have no idea what to do. While one team will be randoms with players from lvl 30 to lvl 2 the faction team will all be 50+ lvl. This isn't fair for the newcomer or the casual players. In conclusion, the matchmaking really needs to be addressed. I've already seen several people uninstall, delete their yt vids and stop playing it on twitch. Meanwhile the discord community is screaming "We need more people" while also being the reason people are leaving. The discord community is very toxic. You can't ask a simple question without being told to get good. Tumbs down....I had such high hopes. :(

_childDocuments_.review: Its so nice to have a release that has a bit of polish to it. In my experience, other than some infrequent network and minor frame issues, I havent seen major bugs or glitches. The progression system is solid and all 3 of the games classes are a blast to play. If there was a negative, it would be those network issues above. Peer to peer can be tempramental at the best of times, and though I havent done in depth testing, Im sure going up against EU players in NA will have some hiccups. In addition, I had to play with my settings a bit to get a smooth mouse and keyboard experience. I cant speak for controller but fully expect to go into settings and play around a bit because by default your mount is extremely clumsy. Its a free to play game with 4 fun modes with a ton of good progression and customization. While I would like a few other things, those are nitpicks and I would say give it a try and see how it feels.

_childDocuments_.review: So far its been a truly phenomenal experience for me. Infrequently will the enemy team leave the game and you will not get your XP. Although this might be frustrating, it does not effect the gameplay much and is a bug I am sure they will easily fix in the future with a small patch. This game is difficult at first. Set your sensitivity HIGH, DPI way up. This will help with the learning curve when learning to maneuver your dragon. There is not much to catch on with the abilities and the game modes are classic easily to play categories, notwithstanding the gold capture gamemode which is very unique and will take a few matches to understand. This game, in my opinion, is what the gaming world needs. Stuff like this takes brilliance to make and to do so effectively. This is a game YOU MUST TRY. I sunk almost three hours into it without and then suddenly woke up. I will easily put a hundred hours into this game, maybe more, especially if they keep working on it. The dragon egg system is cute and funny; a solid incentivization to complete challenges to get more unique and interesting dragons. So far there are only three archetypes, all with varying abilities and play styles, and there are soon to be more. DO IT.

_childDocuments_.review: 360 Degrees of freedom at its best. Think Overwatch + PanzerDragon. Simple to learn difficult to master. One of those games that consistently rewards player skill. Every Match getting better through experience and knowledge. Also as a dragon Fan when xbox's Dragon IP was canned a few years back I was heart broken. This game though not single player has filled that void. Graphics and Style - 10/10 Looks gorgeous Flight mechanics though difficult to master are very realistic and fair. I never felt cheated. Though there are power ups such as berserk for each dragon that can be very OP, these are more one off ultimates that change the tides of the fight if timed and used correctly. Thus adding more to skill gap. All three classes are very close to a good balance. I image we will see some sort of nerf on mines, and some of the abilities, but minus a few launch balances the current classess sit pretty well. Every match you see a variaty of classes so currently theres no held to meta flooding the lobbys with a single type.Plenty of unique and fun game modes, looking forward to seeing what other ideas for modes they will come up with that fits the theme. Its free, highly reviewed, and popular so jump in. But Bare in mind you will have to learn and for probably the first 5 - 10 hours you will be behind the most experienced players as far as dog fighting. Push past it and you will be rewarded, learn from each death and lost match.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, look... I am going to start with some often offered cons, offer counter-cons to consider and let you decide. I personally give it an 7.75/10, deduct some points for the problems but acknowledge that it could easily be a perfect game and maybe it will be if more time is going to be invested on side of the developers. They should increase their communication with the community too!1. "The prices for cosmetic items in the shop are high." They indeed are but nothing needed to play the game or compete can be bought there. In fact, everything that is unlockable is cosmetic only. In that sense it is a shop as players prefer it. On top of that, the devs seem to listen to this criticism and have already doubled down on some of the more pricey offerings.1.5 "Progress is only cosmetic." If it were not, players would be upset that in a competitive game you gain an advantage by being higher-level. So let's be real, which one do you prefer?2. "The matchmaking groups you against pre-made teams." It indeed does but Call of Duty does too. The matchmaking here is both based on MMR and player level. Seperating the queues for more ease (more ease than CoD has) shouldn't be a problem and I would honestly expect it in the near future.3. "There's bugs preventing progression." That's true and it's quite annoying... However, all things considered, this game is honestly a much more polished experience overall than can be said about AAA titles releasing these days... I haven't experienced any major bugs in a while now. Let's see whether the devs do their part and give them a chance to get things right.4+. There's more issues like the anti-cheating being weak but those are not things this smaller studio does wrong that for example a AAA title like Battlefield always got right in comparison... I want to see this game improved upon and give them a chance to do so.But let me really explain to you why I actually like this game a lot and anticipated its release. If this is a kind of game you like (one that offers quick and accessible PvP and competitive modes in atmospheric worlds) consider whether this is for you, despite the things that still require smoothing out.There are not too many PvP Arena games out there (except lame Vehicle Shooters, BR, MOBA and classic 2D/2.5D Fighting Games), this one is clearly polished and well thought through and here you can fight on the backs of dragons which is just as good of a concept as it sounds. All the dragons are cosmetic, no tier-list needed. You can tell it was playtested, the classes make sense, even though they should be further balanced in the future, and the maps are fun & detailed, very atmospheric (former Ubisoft developers as one can tell) and even provide the thickest weather effects... Flying feels good and getting the gist of it is rewarding. I cannot imagine how much time they must've spent on putting everything together as it is, because to me it's just a round experience, apart from the issues. The gameplay, graphics, atmosphere and level of thought that seems to have went into it are very nice. I'm concerned that if this game isn't successful, we'll lose just another Arena PvP game that's not a MOBA and doesn't offer driving tanks... So hop on, support a polished exemplar of that genre (help making them smoothing the experience out worth it!) and make riding dragons an e-sport maybe?! Love.

_childDocuments_.review: Alrighty, I'm updating my review and leaving a full breakdown of the pros and cons. First off, I have a love hate relationship with this game. I have about 30 hours actually in the game and I am very invested in the gameplay. However, the cons make it hard to enjoy. PROS- Gorgeous graphics - Unique concept for gameplay/movement- Great sound effects- Good cosmetics - Decent queue timesCONS- Certain abilities either suck or fail to work entirely. (Phantom Mystic Shroud, Windguard Salvation surge, etc.)- Some abilities are entirely broken compared to other classes. (Phantom Rage ability can't be countered at all and is incredibly broken in certain gamemodes)- Matchmaking is awful. Not kidding, it's atrocious. You'll have 4 level 3s in the same lobby as level 40+s. They don't even stand a chance. - The servers have serious issues with connecting sometimes.- Sometimes games will start even if it's only 6v2. - A lot of people end up leaving ranked games making it hard to play without a full stack.- Sometimes missions fail to work.- Devs try to money grab where they shouldn't. (Ex. Extending the deadline for the founders packs for weeks AFTER the game released, making all legendary event skins only obtainable with money, etc.)

I like how the paid content and microtransactions aren’t forced on you, but it absolutely preys on fear-of-missing-out.Visually, it looks about as fine as UE4 could. The models are nicely detailed but the texture quality could be better. Even on epic, the bellies of the dragons look like soup.My main issue with the game at the moment is consistently finding a server with players on the same side of the globe as you. It's very frustrating to lock onto someone and watch them rubberband away from your attacks just as they're about to hit. The "press any key to continue" screen when the game launches could have more than just a small loading wheel in the bottom-right corner to let you know that it registered the input.The reason why I can't recommend this game now is that there has been ZERO serious effort to keep this game alive. No addition in content, no addition in basic gameplay features - only minor events that only change number values... every two months...

_childDocuments_.review: If you like this game, good for you. You should move on now, and not get worked up over my contrary opinions.Ok, rant time.I think its extremely important that PC games don't go the same route as Mobile Games. Phone games have abysmal 'free to play' design that is focused on milking money from its little piggy consumers. Let's be better than that, people. Don't support this kind of game. This is a mobile game made for PC and consoles, and if anyone tells you otherwise they are fooling themselves. From UI to progression, this is, straight-up, a mobile-styled game.That being said, this game isn't all bad. Its got cool visuals, relatively smooth flying (its not amazing, regardless of what the fans are saying) and a great premise. Dragons are awesome. Art design is on point, graphics, etc. And clearly some degree of love went into it. At the end of the day, its shiny and hollow. It's a golden out-house: its pretty on the surface but its still full of crap.I played through several matches, tried the three different classes, finished some 'quests' (mobile game style: they are just random checklists, like 'play in three matches' and 'fly faster 4 times in one match'), hatched a dragon egg (didn't find it, just got it as a reward for playing a match), and was constantly reminded of the store-page by the pop-ups and home page. Matchmaking took anywhere from 2-10 minutes of queue time, and then the matches...Look, maybe there's a lot of tactics here that only show up for long-time players, but the speed and coordination available with this game makes me think that its mostly just a matter of grinding out matches and shilling out your money to unlock the best dragons so you can stomp on new players. Each match is three rounds, each round is 2 minutes. So 2-10 minutes of queue time for 6 minutes of actual game-play.This game was somewhat headache inducing. There's a lot of light/magical effects while you're flying around super quick. Its a lot of beauty you miss out on in the map, animations, model-design, and skybox, because you're really just looking at your HUD and the opponents zipping past you.Control-wise, its simple, but maneuverability is shoddy. You can't turn very quickly at all, there's no useful dodge, even though your dragon can go super fast in a straight line, and you can't attack backwards from what I could see. Can't roll, can't bank sharply, can't really turn around unless you make a wide loop or slow completely down.So the only real tactic in this game is carrying a bigger stick than the other guy and getting lucky enough to sneak up behind him, since people are pretty much screwed if you approach them from behind. If someone comes up behind you, you have almost no chance of responding because there isn't any way for you to turn on them to fight back. Hence, the PVP boils down to picking your moment and zooming in to gank the poor sucker ahead of you, then circling away whilst hoping nobody was lucky enough to spot you before you spotted them.This mechanic makes the game feel like it was almost designed for battle races instead of arena dog-fights. Dragons who turn very slowly, riders who have weapons they don't use. Then again, I don't play a metric ton of dog-fighting games, so maybe I'm just out of my element. There are people who talk about how fun this game is, but I just can't take them seriously. It's a gimmick based on a cool idea, and I honestly just feel bad for the developers who made it only to have it shipped with a mobile platform structure. Anyone who enjoys this for more than a quick match or two either LOVES dragons, or is so used to phone games that they don't know there are better options out there. I got bored after the first couple of matches. Not frustrated, just bored. There's no campaign, no PVE, its all just PVP, and not GOOD PVP. The different 'modes' are all the same thing; they just change up the team sizes. So do you want to experience this with 3 people on your team, or 6? Big choices.I honestly believe this dragon-riding concept would have been better suited to a co-operative campaign experience than this PVP-only mobile game model, but what's done is done. Based off of their approach to monetization it is highly unlikely the devs would move in that direction.Its ultimately not one I'm coming back to. I am genuinely disappointed, because the mechanics of this game have a lot of potential and the art design, premise, and visuals are very enjoyable. But they decided to turn it into just another empty PVP Arena with mobile monetization, and that just kills it for me.Rant over.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I've played Lair (if you don't remember that game, well I can't say I blame you) I've always wanted to play a fun dogfighting-like dragon game. Well, after waiting at least 10 years, we finally got that type of game and it's free! The controls are great (at least for controllers. I've heard kb&m is a mixed bag), I haven't encountered any bugs, and the connection issues were fixed in a few hours. That being said though, the ui is way too cluttered. You got indicators telling where incoming fireballs are coming from, where enemy players are and if they are close enough to hit you with firebreath, where dragon npcs carrying gold are, and both ally and enemy player health all in the same area of the screen, which is overwhelming. I think having the ability to switch targets on the fly and have the camera follow your current target like in Ace Combat, simply adding a FOV slider would make it easier for players to comprehend what is going on around them.In short despite one area where this game could improve, this game is a blast.Edit: While I still think the ui needs some improvement, it's not as bad as I originally thought it was. I guess it takes some time to get used to it. Although there are two things that this game needs: a way to communicate to your team (the current pinging system is lacking. All it is is "group up here" and "attack this target"), and a way for players to join matches in progress because I constantly find players on both sides dropping out which constantly leaves matches becoming one-sided.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm approaching on rank 30 now so I can probably talk about this game. I didn't plan any of this, so apologies in advance. It's just my raw thoughts. It's been a really long and frustrating road. Century is crazily fast-paced and skilful, and for somebody like me with no experience with games of this type (I'd never played a PvP game prior to this - no I'm serious!) and also with high anxiety, I had to crawl out of the gutter and sweat, scream and "gamer rage" to the point I'm at now, frequently coming top 3 in a match. I think the point I'm making is that if you're considering trying this game but are hesitant due to how the game looks/plays, if you have experience with other PvP games, you're already doing better than me, and you'll hopefully have a less rocky time than I did at the start, and this game will hopefully hook you in a less painful way it did with me. (I was literally a masochist for my first 15 levels, joining matches although I knew I would lose.) Although the game has a very steep learning curve that stems from its unique concepts/controls, unless you're a prodigy/god/highly experienced pvper you're probably going to lose a lot at first. Losing is one of the keys to learning in this game. The way I see it, you physically can't improve without it. According to my more pvp-savvy friends this game is quite unique in its execution and there's only a couple games that are similar. A game they tell me it's kinda like is War Thunder - an aerial dogfight simulator, if you will, except with living, breathing mounts instead of planes, so make of that what you want.The game had - and is currently having - a really shaky release due to Playwing (the developer) releasing the game and then promptly taking everyone out of the office for Christmas, meaning that nobody was around to resolve post-launch issues, some of which are still persisting. However, Playwing have since announced they're working on fixing the most glaring of these, so time will tell. The player count has dropped considerably because of these issues, which has made matchmaking a bit of a problem. Unfortunately whether or not you win a game tends to be decided by the ranks of those you're up against and the ranks of those you're playing with - for example, at level 26 I ended up in a party of all under level 10's, and we were against people actually my rank. We tried our best but we got demolished. For somebody who's been playing since release the matchmaking can be less of an issue, I just try my best and carry the team if I have the skill, but for new players trying to enter the game this is presenting a huge problem, many will likely be put off first match. Some newbies have even reported ending up against those at the top of the ranked leaderboards, which obviously should not even have a percentage chance of happening, but unfortunately it is for the moment. I have to stress, if you're a new player, PLEASE don't give up on this game. There's an entire community built around Century already and 99% of its members are friendly, I've learned so much from them and they've been quite patient with me. There's lots of people to play with and many are just a message in the LFG channel away. If you'd rather play solo, those same people would still be willing to give you tips, tricks and advice on playing the class you want to try. Upon downloading the game and getting stomped for your first few matches, I highly recommend joining the Century Discord and getting in contact with some of the people in there. Heck, you might even see me trying to help you/offering to play with you as well. I'm basically trying to say the matchmaking is only an all-consuming problem if you let it be one - yes it's a problem, but admittedly, some of my best and most fun matches have been with crazy matchmaking. It could end up being the same for you. Plus, you should try not to let it stop you from having fun with the game regardless, getting kills, doing objectives, playing with friends/clans or even just enjoying the sensation of flying around and clashing with other dragon riders - it did mess with me at first but now i'm mostly just along for the ride. If I end up against somebody who's been playing more than me, with a higher level, I meet them if the battle takes me there and see how I get on. Sometimes I get lucky, lol. Things like that is how you learn.Some other points: The graphics - especially the dragons themselves - are gorgeous and sometimes I sign on just to fly around in Free Flight with them. There is an in-game shop but you can get plenty of beauties for free via levelling/events/the ingame currency, Silver. The premium currency, Gems, are quite pricey in my opinion but they do discounts on them and you also get gem discounts as level up rewards, so this isn't always too painful. - Some people are having issues with memory leaks/fps drops/disconnects, I personally only experience the fps drops, but again, I think Playwing are planning to work on these, so hopefully they won't be a problem forever.I think those are my thoughts. Might edit this later.

name: WARBORN
detailed_description: Rise up and deploy for battle in the Variable Armour, a technologically advanced suit of war. As the political climate between factions is thrown out of balance and the solar system is engulfed in conflict, lead your strike force of deadly mecha towards victory in turn-based tactical combat. Choose from four commanders, each representing a different faction and bringing with them their own unique power, traits and play style. Think tactically as you move your units, clash with rival mecha, and watch the outcome in dramatic battle sequences inspired by 90s Japanese animation. Call in reinforcements from orbit by picking from a range of mass-produced units with differing combat roles. Assemble a force to lead into battle and strike fear into the enemy with imposing second-generation Variable Armours, piloted exclusively by your commander. Push forward and secure your supremacy on a battlefield of hexagonal area tiles. Use a variety of terrain types to take cover or undermine the enemy, and capture structures to gain additional resources or deployment sites. Inflict status effects, plant traps, support allies. Each type of Variable Armour is armed with its own specialist equipment and unique skills, allowing you to engage the enemy with a variety of tactical options. CAMPAIGN WARBORN takes place in the Auros System, during a time of war and political uncertainty. While inter-faction disputes erupt, see the war unfold from the eyes of four different commanders across a story-driven campaign featuring over 40 missions. SKIRMISH & MULTIPLAYER Configure your own match parameters and develop new tactics by competing against AI in Skirmish mode, or take the battle online to outwit rival commanders across the world in tense one-on-one matches. MAP EDITOR Feeling creative? Make your own custom maps using the built-in Map Editor. Take your custom maps into Skirmish mode to try against the computer, or play them online with friends.
