_childDocuments_.review: Summary: Encased offers a fascinating world with an intriguing and gripping plot, filled with a vast cast of characters full of colour and personality with an astonishingly deep dialogue system. However, enthusiasts of open-world exploration and turn-based Fallout style combat may feel disappointed with the small amount of both there currently is to do.A full detailed preview video of the game can be viewed here:Plot:As a whole, the writing, general story and world-building together bring a fascinating place full of mystery none of which I want to spoil. Based on what I have experienced I get the impression there is going to be tones of secrets to be discovered and mysteries to solve. I feel that somewhere along the way the player is going to get tangled up between factions and leaders and having to decide who they want to side with. There are plenty of factions each with their own beliefs and agendas. Though what those agendas are, are not very deeply explained at the moment.There is no denying, everything with Encased’s world, plot and the likes is very early. There is lots of information missing, lots of questions still to be answered and lots of locations still to be developed. But as far as first impressions go and giving the player a taste of what is to come with its story and world, it certainly succeeds in leaving you wanting more.Gameplay:As a whole, the gameplay to Encased consists of more disappointments than anything else. Indeed the current build showcases the many ways of getting around obstacles well along with having a very deep character creation and development. The real show stopper, however, is definitely the dialogue and the vast amount of options that are available and how those options change in accordance to the wing you are playing.Aside from those positives, however, Encased’s gameplay quickly goes downhill with underwhelming combat, a largely empty open world, uninformative descriptions and barebone mechanics that simply don’t give you enough to play around with to get excited. There are a few bugs too, one which is a major annoyance where the interface becomes disabled and you can’t click on or interact with anything. It forces you to either reload your previous save or sometimes even exit the game completely and reload to fix it.Unless plot, world-building and a ton of dialogue are what you are looking for from such a game, right now, it is best left on your wishlist and to see how development progresses. If you are into turn-based combat and open-world exploration, Encased will without a doubt leave you underwhelmed.Atmosphere:The atmosphere of Encased is reasonably well done. There is always that sense of desolation about The Dome even in the populated and futuristic areas. Never do you ever feel that you are in a place that could be considered normal or everyday life. The world of the Dome is alien and has many hostilities, and every nook and cranny of it gives that sense of danger.There is an equally fitting soundtrack to the game too which combines sci-fi and horror themes very well which together get across the sci-fi setting of the game along with the post-apocalyptic nature too.With that said however, it isn’t the easiest of games to get immersed into at the moment. Despite the atmosphere be relatively good, there is still a lot of work to do with ambience and there are times where the atmosphere just gets pushed to the background and forgotten about. The atmosphere does the job, but currently isn’t anything that would make it stand out.Conclusion:Encased is a game that should tick all the boxes for me, but it just doesn’t right now leaving me very much sitting on the fence, unsure of which side to jump to. Dark Crystal Games hope to have the game finished and fully released within an estimate of 6 months from now and honestly from what I’ve seen from the game, that just isn’t going to happen. There is just too much still to be done.Encased has a fantastic world full of colourful and unique characters and a dialogue system with a depth that is unmatched with this game style along with a character development system that is fantastic for the most part. But right now everything else is lacking. Mechanics that are expected to be there are either not there at all or are so early in development that it is impossible to get much enjoyment out of them.If complex dialogue, plot and world-building are what you are looking for, there is plenty of it to revel in right now. But if you were looking for a relatively polished beta that gives a good showcase of all its mechanics including combat and open-world exploration, you are going to be greatly disappointed.At the end of the day, I didn’t enjoy my time with Encased. It is a game attempting to do so much and nothing has really come together properly yet. It feels like a mish-mash of mechanics and ideas that haven’t been thought out or implemented well.It is at a stage where I can’t even call it promising. Hopeful would be the best word I could use to describe it right now. Is it possible for this game to become something worthwhile? Yes, it is but I am not convinced that it will offer anything that will make it stand out.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short, Encased obviously had extremely passionate people behind it. The question is, what happened to them after the initial early access release? The game feel like it's about half done. It's front loaded, with prologue and act 1 feeling amazing, while the rest of the game is more of a whimper. Not to mention the ending... Last 2(3) cells are a joke, and feel like they were cobbled together on the weekend before release. Now, I mentioned that it feels like the devs had a lot of passion, and I stand by that. There are plenty of cool ideas, nice writing and attention to detail, at least initially. But none of these mechanics and ideas were finished, just left there, making you sad about the missed potential. You have a vehicle system, obviously inspired by FO2, but it's just that, a movement speed buff on the map and a storage access. You can get an upgrade, but it kind of comes late and is less useful than you would initially think. Inventory is a mess, it obviously wanted to be a Tetris system, but gave up half way through. So now it both looks bad and is annoying and is not very functional. About 10 hours in your inventory will be filled with keys and notes you cannot get rid of, so look forward to that. Overall UI is not great. Some parts of it work, but generally you would expect better. I understand that unity has limitations and will leave a mark, but this is just shoddy work. Story is ok. Some writing is very enjoyable, especially for some side characters and stories. Not the story itself, but characters. Random NPCs have more humanity and look like more real and believable humans than major characters in most AAA games. I've always had issues with FO games in regards to believability. Not that such events can happen or something, but that if they did, this is how people would act and behave. Encased does not suffer from this problem, most people have defined and realistic believes, wants and ambitions. Too bad most quests feel unfinished and just end abruptly, never having follow-up or real consequences. And lastly combat. Oh boy. Imagine Divinity combat, but really bad. Like, if skills were made by someone who heard about what skills DOS2 has, and tried to recreate them from memory. While heavily drinking. Long story short, half the skills are just the same attack, but for different weapons. The other half are badly scripted basic abilities. There obviously was almost no testing, balancing or though that went in to combat. AP economy is a joke, damage scaling is out of whack, enemies are bullet sponges early on, and overall combat is the weakest part of the game. I would mention stealth separately. Normally I'm not a fan of stealth, but I would recommend it here. Not that it's well made or fun, but it allows you to avoid turn-based combat, making the game much more enjoyable to play. Get a quiet weapon and stack some detection threshold (think of it as your "AP" outside of combat). I like syringers for their shroom laced dart, or cryo laser so you can root people in place. They can't detect you if they can't reach you. And then just go wild, killing all enemies one by one without starting the combat. So overall, the game is not worth 30 euro. Get it on sale for a fiver, and have some fun. Don't expect a finished game, just a passion project that ran out of passion long time ago.

_childDocuments_.review: So you're probably thinking "he played it for 73 hours and is not recommending it? how does that work?"Let me explain whyFirst, bugs. There are still a great many bugs in the game - some small, some potentially progression-halting.The quest objectives and descriptions are, at times, woefully inadequate - bordering on broken.Some weapon types seem to not be spawning at all during certain play-throughs of the game.A couple of the major features of the game seem to be tacked on, last-minute and have no instructions on how they work or what to do or even tell you that they exist. Some of us just happened to find them randomly and told everyone else on the forums how. Also, one of those features doesn't seem to be working at all and may in fact be bugged but it is difficult to tell because there is nothing in the game which explains how it is supposed to work and no one else has figured it out yet.Without spoiling too much, I didn't like any of the endings (I tried them all) and they were all dissatisfying IMO.Enemies scale with your level, but player weapons and abilities don't scale well (or at all) passed a certain level so you can end up fighting hordes of unbeatable enemies if you level too much.The out of combat movement follows the same grid pattern that in-combat movement does. This does not work well for out of combat because sometimes you just want to go diagonally from point A to point B but the game forces the character to run in a square grid pattern so you end up running through obstacles you otherwise could have avoided.Some of the combat animations are unnecessarily long and slow, making it a chore to fight as certain character archetypes (especially when facing many enemies).Some story lines seem to end abruptly and without any real resolution. It feels like it was cut content.Vendors have extremely limited funds to buy your stuff so you will be traveling back and forth across the world just to try to sell a few high-value items to get some money. It is so limited that it might as well just be a barter or direct-trade system instead of an economy.So why did I spend 73 hours on this game? I do like crpg's in general and I like the theme of this one. It was a unique story, if a bit difficult to follow at times. I kept thinking that the game is going to get better as I went along and it did improve some from start to finish but never reached a point where I could say I really enjoyed myself. At first I had planned to try some other character builds later on, but by the end of my first play-through (and after seeing how it ends) I just didn't have any desire to continue playing the game anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Encased is a solid, Fallout-inspired CRPG with strong exploration but weak combat. As with Fallout, there's a ton of player agency.  You can align with different factions and most quests have multiple solutions. The environments are littered with interactive objects but this can cause some tedium if you have OCD and feel the need to open every container. Exploration is easily the game's biggest strength, as the world is packed with interesting POIs and random encounters. The writing is decent, with interesting companions and lore, though it feels like some of the dialogue was awkwardly translated. There's a good amount of loot variety and a large number of viable builds to get through the game with.Combat is the weakest part of the game, largely due to the stupid AI and highly exploitable stealth system. You can enter stealth mode at any time if you aren't near an enemy, which then creates a visible detection radius around every NPC. Stay in the red radius for too long and your stealth is canceled. However, with enough points in the Criminal stat, you can stay in the radius for a lengthy amount of time. The big problem here is that attacking doesn't cancel stealth. As a result, the optimal strategy is to enter stealth, snipe an enemy with a ranged weapon, repeatedly shoot it while it approaches you to investigate, then if it somehow survives long enough to detect you, just finish it off in the first combat turn before it can retaliate. Rinse and repeat until all enemies are dead. You can do this in almost every encounter and it completely trivializes combat. I don't know why the designers decided to let you maintain stealth while attacking but it just breaks their encounters entirely.If you don't use stealth, the combat is more interesting but still pretty shallow compared to games like Wasteland 3. There's a nice variety of active abilities based on your equipped weapons and you can use some fun tactics like swapping places with a distant target so your bruiser companion can start punching them without wasting AP on movement. There are various debuffs too, which can be important as some enemies have high resistances to various damage types. However, the AI is still pretty dumb so you won't find many interesting tactical challenges. In that respect, the combat is pretty similar to the original Fallout games so if you enjoyed those, the combat in Encased shouldn't bother you too much.All-in-all, Encased is worth a try if you enjoy CRPGs, particularly those of the Fallout variety. The world is a ton of fun to explore and the quests are generally well-designed. However, if combat is your top priority, you might find Encased a bit underwhelming.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews but after giving this game a chance in early access what feels like ages ago. I honestly can't recommend this game at full price. It's not a bad game but as many others have said it is very mediocre.The game has huge potential and that's why I kept forgiving its shortcomings and bugs. But here are a few things that I've noticed through my adventures under the dome.• Combat is interesting! Until you realize that there won't be much variation or variety to the encounters.• The locations are beautiful and populated. Unfortunately, the NPCs are generally lackluster.• NPCs can be broken down into 3 main groups:     - Quest related (may be voiced) with actual branching dialogues and sometimes unique interactions based on Wing.     - Filler (random townies) all NPCs are named but these guys say like 2 lines of dialogue and that's it. Unfortunately, most NPCs seem to fall under this category in my experience.     - Enemies (Combat Filler) These guys exist to be fought and or killed. There are some variety to these guys and can be interesting but just like the filler NPCs they just aren't fleshed out enough to really immerse you.  • Quests are janky and quest log does not help really. For instance there is a main quest which requires you to get a reactor working again. In this reactor you have to do a little puzzle to manage power (to my knowledge there are no hints for it aside for looking it up on forums) and replace a fuse in a fuse box. Now in this reactor there are only 2 other areas, the elevators and an access path where you meet some orange wing members who were sent to replace a fuse. Going through this area there is nowhere to replace the fuse and no indication you should go elsewhere aside from stumbling around through all the areas of the reactor to find it. The reason for this is because in previous versions of the game that same area WAS used to replace the fuse but was changed with no indication of having been changed. Experiences aside it was interesting to a point. The power armor was cool but it usually felt like it was just used to get me through tough areas. Enemies WILL kill you if you're unprepared, and hell even sometimes when you are as the weapons are usually underwhelming.All in all the game has potential it's had potential since it was first released on Early Access. But will it actually manage to achieve that potential? From what I've seen so far I'm doubtful. This game won't be the next Fallout CRPG but could it given the time and effort? I'd say yes. Pick this up on sale if you're interested in CRPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not convinced there is potential here for something compelling. You can definitely tell the developers have played games in this beloved genre and theme - I needed strategic foresight in setting up my character to be successful in my very first monster encounter - but what is available so far leads me to believe this will end up being in a bargain bin bundle when it's complete. Right off the bat: the writing is terrible. Cringy, even. The developers could learn a lot from Pillars of Eternity in that games ability to craft a scene through excellent use of language. They could also learn from games done by XSEED (Trails in the Sky series) for how to employ a distinct vernacular for characters representing different socio-economic classes/cultures/nationalities. The game tries to do both, and it does it terribly. Between the grammatical issues, grade-school level dialogue/scene setting,  and the awful attempt to make some characters stereotypically Italian for some reason, there might be a story worth telling. Encased has most of the basics down in terms of combat and exploration. However, for a game that is attempting to meet or exceed the quality accomplished by Wasteland 2 or Divinity: Original Sin... come on now, really? Interactive environmental elements are limited (aka, just a barrel) and you cannot interact with them meaningfully outside of combat (you can't electrify or explode toxic gas clouds, for example). Crafting is rudimentary. Combat is also very basic. The inventory system is standard, but it is chaotic and hard to organize or prioritize items (a lot of what you find is  garbage, with a note insinuating it might be useful somehow). None of the weapons I found particularly stand out... Importantly, there is nothing new here for me to be interested in. All the abilities, items, and weapons I have at my disposal have been done in other games. Fortunately, there are glimpses of what might actually be compelling. The use of vehicles, the use of mechanical armour, and using different ammo types. None of these are explored fully as of the first content expansion, but I can see potential uniqueness if they double down on those elements. There are a lot of enclosed spaces, blind/stupid enemies, and frustrating-to-unimaginative level designs. Character movement and stances look awkward and stilted, environmental elements are repeated over and over, and basic functionality like interactive element highlighting is not present.I had a few game crashes after Steam chat notifications and using the Steam overlay.This was a very critical review of Encased, I wish the best for the developers. There was one small scene where the game really opened up - when you find the survivors of the cataclysm you are sent to investigate, all staring vacantly at an ancient relic of a forgotten civilization - the freedom of movement, the eerie scene, and the creepy music, all combined to make that particular segment very enjoyable.+ Post-apocalyptic turn-based tactics rpg+ Challenging- Terrible writing/dialogue- Uninspired level/environment design- Re-hashed weapons/abilities- No killer-feature

_childDocuments_.review: Would you rather watch than read? Me too. Check out the highlights of the gameplay here:Let's be ultra, crystal, super clear on this one: This game has problems and bugs. It's a super early access version and you are going to run into skills and abilities that don't work, skills missing, chunks of the game that bug out... the list goes on. That's what you're GETTING with Early Access and you need to know that. It's what you're signing up for. Knowing that, as long as that's okay then read on.Encased is doing a ton of cool stuff that I haven't seen before. It takes the standard "Kit out your character" with stats and abilities, but then it has each ability have sub abilities that you have to activate. Let me explain. In a game like Fallout of Atom RPG you just put the points into thievery and you use the skills, but in Encased you put points into Criminal, in this case, and then you get access to sub abilities in that tree. One of them is lock picking and one is stealing. Neat right? I think this actually does a lot for the game because it removes the dependency on gear to give you the abilities and it puts it on how you're building your character instead. The game has a ton of dialogue, stuff to explore, quests to do and cool stuff to interact with and it's glorious. You want to touch everything around you and just the intro area can take you a few hours to get through. If you're thorough then you will be here for ages. That's not a bad thing! The game has a ton of character and detail in the world. Quests and objectives will have a lot of different ways to tackle them like any good tactical RPG. It just depends on how deep you want to get into it.I played some 100 episodes of Atom RPG and thousands of hours in various Fallout games. I LIKE this type of game and this game shows that it can absolutely contend with those big titles, but maybe just not quite yet. One of the big problems I ran into was after taking off my Power Ar--- I mean my exo suit, I just died instantly. It was a bad bug with the way the game calculates your health but a bug nonetheless. Stuff like that is going to happen and you just have to roll with it.tl;dr - Game is really deep and great if you can get into it knowing that it also will have a ton of bugs. It's Early Access, know what you're buying.Join the Curator group for more reviews like this:

There are a wide variety of weapons and equipment to choose from, each with its own strengths and weaknesses, so you'll need to experiment to find the perfect loadout for your playstyle.Overall, Encased is an absolute must-play for any fan of sci-fi or post-apocalyptic games. _childDocuments_.review: This game is okay. That is pretty much all I can say about it. Exploration is not really great, there are not many intersting spot worth visiting and the loot is most of the time bad. (Not even talking about all the locked containers with no keys anywhere to be found, so the game forces you to have a character who is good with picking locks, if you want the good loot). Combat is kind of boring and repetitive or complete unfair towards the player. There is no in between unfortunately. I even chose a psionic character, since I fought that it would be more fun with magic, but not really.The stealth system in this game is too easy, since you will only be spotted if you are right next to the enemy in their red zone, which is 3 meters.The voice-acting is good for the main story parts, but since it is only present there, it is only a slight positiv. The writing is good, everything is described in great detail.Pathfinding in this game is also not great. Your character often stops moving if an NPC moves infront of you, so you need to select the point where you want to go multiple times sometimes, especially in cities. It is also not very precise, leading to your character walking into traps and anomalies even though there would have been enough space to avoid them. The puzzles in this game are sometimes made in such a way, that it doesn't make sense in the world itself. (For example: a sign, nearly completly covered with rubbel, hast for numbers on it in differnt colors. You need them in order to close a gas leak, which is blocking your way. Does it make any sense in the world itself? No. Is it just another unnecessary riddle thrown into the game without any real conection to the surrounding area to make it more "challenging"?  YesDon't get me wrong. I like riddles and puzzles, it makes stuff more intersting. A good puzzle, which makes sense in the world itself and is directed to the character not the player is fun. But not when it is just there to be there, with no real reason to exist besides being an obstacle.Another problem I have with the game is, that the resources are not distributed well. "You need a medpack and don't have the rare componets to make one? Well, you either sleep for about a week somewhere to heal naturally, or you travel all the way back to Magellan to buy Medpacks for expensive prices. And all of that, because you fought against 6 cockroaches with acid-spit." After a fight, you need about two medpacks for everyone in your group, and having to spend nearly all your money on medpacks is not fun. And don't even get me started on Ursula's Medbay where you have to pay your own Medbay money in order to get healed.The game could be good, if it didn't have all these small annoyances. The grafics are good enough for a game like this, the voice-acting is great when it is present, the visuals are nice to look at, the UI is simple to understand and the writing so far has been very good (at times it feels like an audiobook)I will continue to play the game, since I hope that the game will get better then this in mid- to late-game, but for now my review for this game is only a 6/10, so just enough to be positive.

_childDocuments_.review: i think this is my first review, so it's not really well worded.  more like a flow of consciousness I'm a bit surprised at how many people are recommending the game.  I don't think it's a horrible game, but it feels quite incomplete and a bit milktoast.  I think the reason it has so many recommendations is because the reviewers have only played about 15 hours or so and haven't hit that wall of "what the f am i doing", "where am i supposed to be going", "what's supposed to happen next", oh god, "not another encounter" etc.The objective tracking feature is non existent.  and before you say this is in the style of other crps or a throw back to the crps of old, let me say that this isn't the case.  There isn't enough information about the objective, where other crpgs add more context and details to the current objectives.  you talk to a person and they say, "I already gave you the coordinates."  you check your journal and it says, "go to the coordinates", but you'll have no idea what on your map or where in your journal those "coordinates" are what they are referring to.   you'll  get a quest that says, retrieve this thing at this place, but i have pulled out a magnifying glass trying to find it with no success.  there is woefully little context to go off of.  compared to other crpgs, the combat is milktoast.  My character happens to have contraptions maxxed, so my character has A SINGLE advanced movement option - jetpack.  but none of my companions can use that nor do they have any form of advanced movement outside of walk.  Enemies just walk up into a firing line and you just take turns shotting at each other.  there is no cover mechanic outside of getting out of line of sight completely.  This makes kiting extremely easy, but extremely painfully slow.  Contraptions are really really useful, but not having them kinda sucks and it requires you to pick up an absurd amount of parts, so you have to empty every single container, and this is just a bore.I could overlook the hologram bug that breaks the game.  I could overlook having to loot everything in sight to build a contraption, i could overlook the shallow combat.  What i can't overlook is me spending 30 hours and not making progress because I have no idea what or where i need to go to complete a quest.  I've barely made a dent in the game's content and story, and if my time/per objective stays at the same rate, I don't feel like i'd want to continue.I like the concept and i like the world.  I really just wish the objective tracking was more fleshed out and detailed.  I'll probably revisit the game if they ever enhance that part.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version - not finished enough to enjoy, but has great potential.Haven't played it long enough, but here is what i got from 6 hours of playing it:The intro part was good writing/engagement-wise, but as soon as you are free to explore you will notice a moderate drop in quality of writing, the game is clearly not finished and there is a lot of missing dialogue for a certain event and your character basically has acces to a lot of information they shouldn't know in the first place.My point being a lot of dialogue needs to be fixed.You can't expect player's character to go exactly where you want them to go for some crucial plot information first when you toss them onto the world map.There are actually locations which assume you've been at some other location first because there isn't any option to even ask for pointers (citizenship etc).The settings is interesting and the whole wing system is great for role-playing.Judging from the supposedly finished part, the amount of dialogue checks is pretty decent, and the low intelligence dialogue is there too.(even some perks for low-ints, damn.)Tutorials are plenty and will explain thoroughly _childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game but there's so many little things holding it back. I hate to say it but it genuinely feels like "We have Fallout at home". For the most part this works well: A lot of the style and game play is reminiscent of the first two Fallout games and if that's your thing that works out great! The problems come in the deeper you get.Some of my main issues:- Combat Chatter: Characters will not shut up. Ever. Every turn almost every individual involved in combat, excepting your own, will say some line of dialogue. Great at first for a bit of flavor, but when combat drags on  and you hear the same two or three lines recycled again and again it's severely grating. You can turn the voice over down or off but that doesn't truly  the problem.- Suspecting Something: Characters will become suspicious if you do something sneaky, this is a good thing! Until it happens every time to every character when you enter combat. Attacked by a giant roach? It gets suspicious of you after you shoot it the first time. It's clearly tied to whatever system they use for handling crimes and such but it shouldn't be happening .- Difficulty Curve: Truly reminiscent of Fallout (Fallout 2 specifically) you can build your character however you want, but if you don't start out good at some form of combat you're in for a terrible time. The prologue requires you either fight several enemies (in groups of 1 v 3 with you being the 1) or you sneak past/avoid them and also neglect some objectives. If you're a good little adventurer and do a lot of talking and exploration you'll have an advantage in levels to help you through the prologue. Then the game starts. The majority of enemies I've encountered after the prologue have been at least 5 or 6 levels above me and even if I'm able to survive these encounters they drag for far too long. They don't even provide equipment or resources to help bridge the gap. It's almost as if the game punishes you for not relying on a melee knockout strategy.I haven't gotten especially far and, as of writing this, I still intend to keep going but I cannot recommend this game. If I hadn't gotten it for free I'd be seriously considering a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: I advise you to read this before purchase. My impression of this game is that it is a good RPG that nevertheless has some serious problems. That's why it should not be viewed as outright positive review, but more of a cautious recommendation with warnings to new players.I have played it for many hours over the years back when Encased was still in various stages of Early Access. Over time the game has progressed a lot and is in much better shape now. Still, the release version has a lot of room for improvement.The game's main positive is not that it aims high, but that it sincerely tries to get there. There is a huge map with many locations, no less than 6 main factions, over-the-top plot events, at least 6 companions, many skills and abilities, Fallout 2's vehicle system, original five wing population system, relic system, many unique random events, eight attributes, tons of specific damage types and resistances, specific low IQ and pacifist systems that radically change the gameplay. These mechanics are implemented in full release, however...The game's main negative is not that it aims high, but that it clearly aimed way too high. Throughout the game, starting from very beginning, it gets more and more clear that there is just not enough content to justify all the mechanics. Yes, there are decisions that affect the story, but there are not many of these decisions. Yes, there is a huge map, but there is not much of things to do outside combat. There are six distinct factions, but there are about 2 straight-forward quests related to each. Some attributes are useful in rare circumstances. It goes on and on. While mechanics themselves have their own problems, generally game plays alright, it is just a severe lack of accompanying content that may be off-putting.This problem gets really noticeable as the story progresses from a middle game into a late game. As you get to the story's final part and unlock the second half of the map, things go downhill. It gets less and less fun to play.Personally, I would not replay it until more content is added. As of now, in its current state it is a game for people willing to tolerate the problems. The situation may change, so I will keep this review positive as an encouragement for people to continue working and improving the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not without flaws, but Encased is a fairly solid game. Worth the price for the 25-ish hours of main game gameplay. I think it's a game worth one full try, but it drags on a little too long to do another playthrough. If you're looking for a game that's got the mechanics of Divinity 2 put into a Fallout setting, then it's definitely worth giving a shot.Positives were that it has a wonderfully fascinating setting, the characters were all unique and I found myself remembering even minor NPCs, the voice acting was a great and pleasant surprise. The companions I chose, I really loved. The battle mechanics are reminiscent of Divinity Original Sin 2, which is to say they were excellent. I played on the normal mode, so battle encounters were challenging enough without being a walk in the park. Inventory management wasn't too annoying. The variety of choices that made an impact on your story was overall impressive. Character customization and building is great, what you can pour your stats into is pretty varied, having perks further helps to optimize your character in the way you really want to play (I played a medic/melee character, so that was fun). I liked how Encased started, and I liked how it ends.As other reviews said, however, the Second Act is lacking. It feels like this huge extended fetch quest with other side fetch quests if you wanted to do those. I also really didn't give much of a damn about most of the factions; they were all pretty sucky in their own ways, and I was so exasperated by the Second Act's main fetch quests that I ended up choosing a neutral ending. Random encounters stop being threatening or interesting, especially after you get the train. As mentioned, I loved the companions I chose, but I was upset that getting high Reputation with them essentially meant nothing. I was hoping for a romance option, but this game doesn't have one. Also there were no other companion quests after the initial recruiting one, which was a bit disappointing too; I wanted to know more about them.I'm keen to see what the developers make next :)

_childDocuments_.review: Only a couple of hours in but my first impressions are very positive. The character creation is very like the original Fallout games, but even more detailed. There are loads of options here to tailor the character to your play style.The art style is great- it has that same 1950's vibe as Fallout but "shinier"- more Flash Gordon than Fallout if you know what I mean.There are reputations to earn and ruin with the different groups within the game- helping one will almost certainly upset another. You are constantly making little choices like this which gives even the the most basic of side quests a larger significance. The overall premise and plot is intriguing and the world is interesting and packed with incidental details. Combat is turn based, very like Fallout, with a choice of basic and certain special attacks, depending upon your character's skills and what weapon you are using.There is crafting to learn, puzzles to solve and secrets to find.All in all, although the total amount of content is currently limited, what is available is polished, detailed and packed with things to find and do. If you are a fan of Fallout, or fancy something akin to Pillars of Eternity or Divinity Original Sin in a Sci-Fi setting, its worth some consideration.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game - and there is a lot to like about it. The writing is good, the world quite reactive... But unfortunately playing through the game feels too much like a chore for me to see the end of it.Exploration is extremely tedious. Movement speed could have been increased, but the fundamental problem comes from the inability to fast travel between maps. If you need to go speak to an NPC in act 1's central hub to complete a quest, be ready to have to walk through 3-4 maps to go back to the world screen and move on with your game. While this initially encourages exploration, after a while it just feels like a huge waste of time. To make matters worse, as the game goes, there appears to be less and less content to stumble upon anyway so exploration isn't really rewarded anymore anyway.The map itself would have benefited from serious improvements, like displaying the orientation of the camera (without which it is impossible to figure out where to go) or better, the ability to set a destination for the squad from that screen.Finally, while the decision to flood the map with searchable containers may appeal to the more loot-oriented players, I personally found myself ignoring them all after a few hours of play because I just wasn't getting anywhere. All in all, the game makes it extremely hard on you to go from point A to point B, to the point of throwing the towel.The beginning of the game is strong enough that you may overlook the poor quality-of-life, but as the novelty of the universe fades away, as the later zones become less polished for probable budget reasons, as the quests turn into mindless fetch missions, it becomes harder and harder to keep enjoying the game. I really hope the devs can try again with a less ambitious but more mature project.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend this game? Possibly, right now I am very excited from the little bit I played - however it's still young in it's Open Testing (Early Access) phase, and it shows rather drastically. However, I have hopes for things like the Hunger / Thirst to be an option - not forced on you, as well as having clearer UI pointing to those resources (a simple meter would be perfectly fine with %'s on it). Simple quality of life things are what hurt the game most in my opinion right now, not what most people complain about in "half the games not here!" It's Early Access FFS, what did you expect? Other than the abundance of god-awful writing and overacting, this game is bare-bones in every respect. World map looks terrible. Sounds sucks. Combat is dull as it gets. Combat sound and action has zero punch or emphasis. They could not even make an animation for going up and down ladders, so your guy simply teleports up or down. They did not bother to put exclamation points (or any other indicator) for all the people you have to visit before you can leave the intro base and venture out, so you have to search all over for them and then listen to them run their mouths FOREVER about stuff like how armor can protect against more than bullets blah-blah-f-ing blah like nobody has ever played a game before with armor stats for fire/acid/radiation etc. They have to describe every dumb-assed NPC you meet from the armory or gun-range like they were major characters in a novel instead of just letting them serve their stupid little utilitarian role at the base without a bunch of text description of their every feature and foible. They even have the narrator describe special effects rather than making a simple graphic or animation to SHOW the special effects. As with too many other games, the devs think stuffing a zillion pounds of zany into every character creates a cast that people will find charming and interesting. I just find all the mild-mannered wackiness to be tiresome...like accidentally walking into some hipster bar where every single man has a handlebar mustache and every single woman is walking around with a giant snake over her shoulders. They offer nothing memorable, like that absolutely insane sociopath Tiny Tina from Borderlands. She was not zany, she was ruthless and mad and extremely dangerous...and that's what made her lovable.I got the game during a major sale, so it is no big loss. I took a gamble, like I often do with sale games. Crapped out majorly on this one. Even on sale for $5, which is what I paid, this game is not worth the effort. _childDocuments_.review: : At time of writing, game is unfinished but still fun, and looks like it will be amazing when it is done. Solid update schedule, transparent roadmap, reputable team working on the game, and highly recommended purchase for RPG fans.The combat is very reminiscent of Shadowrun, if you've played the Shadowrun games on PC or mobile. You have Action Points you spend in turn based combat to either move or attack with whatever weapons you have equipped, or use skills or equipment. It works well enough and provides a tactical challenge. The weapons are all unique and have different pros and cons, seldom was one simply a flat upgrade of another, which I thought was great.Crafting has some way to go, perhaps in determining the difference between crafting materials and junk, but for the most part it works well. Simply find a workbench of the right type and you can craft relevant items from a list there. Items you can craft are all shown, the ones you're missing ingredients for tinted red. You can invest ability points into crafting skills to unlock more craftables or become better at breaking stuff down into crafting materials.Those of you familiar with the Fallout series will remember being given different dialogue options when talking to characters, with the relevant ability related to certain options listed on the option itself, sometimes greyed out if you lacked the necessary abilities or background to select it. This game does that, but takes it a step further in letting you know there would be an option if you had a certain skill, item, or background, but doesn't spoil the outcome. Characters are lively and have their own personalities, and similarly to Divinity: The Original Sin 2 where you can barter with most individuals by clicking the button while speaking to them, the same is true here. Worth noting, you choose which caste of society you come from when you make your character, each one called a "wing" and representing a different sector, white for science, silver for political, orange for criminal, and blue for engineering. These vastly affect the way that people treat you, where you're allowed to go, and what dialogue options are open to you. Super impressed by this.I was pleasantly surprised with the amount of options in dialogue, however I would have liked to see an option to drop my current course of action and attempt to walk away in at least a couple more conversations.To elaborate: At one point I listened to two criminals planning to rob a storeroom. After I told them I had heard them, my only dialogue options were to join them in this. Now don't get me wrong, after I told them that I opened up dialogue options to tell the guard what they were planning, or I could've simply ignored their requests and screwed over their robbery by telling them I'd done what they'd asked. Or I could simply ignore them after this. So the player choice is there, I simply wasn't 100% aware of it during the dialogue is all. Conclusion on the roleplay side at leas is that things are looking very good.Not much to say here, but the environments are solid! There are plenty of secret areas and alternate tunnels and many ways to go about getting somewhere or reaching your objective. The environments look good too and really give you the feel of the place. PLENTY to loot as well, perhaps a bit too much, and best I can tell there is no punishment for "stealing" at present, but I do not believe a law and punishment system has been implemented at time of writing. More on that in a bit.The story for this game is rather impressive. It is transparent in what it advertises, a post-apocalyptic wasteland adventure that reminds one of the Stalker series, the early Fallout titles, and indeed many a classic RPG. Yet somehow the game has a fresh take on this concept and uses it to tell a new story without being stale. We see the same tropes from those aforementioned series used in new and interesting ways. Remember anomalies from stalker? They're here too but serve new purpose to the story and increase intrigue. Remember the vaults from Fallout and all the madness they contained? The relics of Encased provide similar shenanigans. Encased is a game that I found able to capture the charm of these things we loved in other titles and present them to us in a way that is fresh and interesting through the story of the Dome, and that's a story I'll not spoil as I loved exploring and learning more and more about it.At the time of writing, I've just finished this game in the sense that I've reached the end of existing content so far. That took me, excluding time spent AFK, a total of about 16 to 18 hours. This was exploring every room, looting EVERY container I could, and trying to find every secret I could (though I didn't find them all). This was done on one character build. If I made another character with a different background, I'd end up with a somewhat different story-line and new ways to approach problems, as well as a lot of characters treating me differently. It would be a fresh experience and the game has replayability in that sense.This heading is all caps because it's the elephant in the room. We all know the usual fate of unfinished early access titles with big dreams and ambitions and we know how many of them end well. At the time of writing, the game has barely been on Steam for 12 days and is an Early Access title come from Kickstarter. On opening the game you are presented a roadmap screen indicating that this is the first stage of Early Access, and that we can expect 3 large content updates before a final large full release update. We do not know what this schedule is but I am hopeful.Why am I hopeful? because in the 12 days this game has been on Steam, it has already received (at least since I purchased it) two rather large updates solving a plethora of bugs and simply adding quality of life features to improve gameplay. In my mind a dev team that cares that much about fixing bugs and adding nice features INBETWEEN their large advertised updates and in such a swift manner is a team worth supporting.Now, as for bugs, I didn't find very many. In all the combats I found myself in, only one enemy went a little janky and ran into a wall instead of attacking me, and this was a random encounter. At one point I was able to receive a refund of 20 currency for a gambling ticket I never paid for (but it's a one time event). Only twice in all the dialogue, did I speak to an NPC and have the camera wildly teleport all over the map. Conversation still went fine but was a tad distracting. These were all the bugs I recall encountering.As for the missing content, my understanding is that the devs intend to release the actual content of the game (story + world + quests) in large patches rather than bit by bit. Thus it can be discouraging to finish the prologue and realize that after such an enticing and immersive prologue, there's nothing else out there, however I am confident in the proof of concept that Dark Crystal Games are showing us with this prologue and I trust the story and world released in coming large content patches will do the prologue justice and make the game something truly special. You can see hints of what's to come in character customization alone.Honestly? I loved the experience. The Devs making this game helped out on Divinity: The Original Sin 2, and it shows, you can see the inspiration in it. Larian Studios also endorsed this game, which is what initially gave me the faith to purchase it even in early access. I do not regret this decision, and I highly recommend this game as an investment into what it will become. Let's help the devs get there together!

_childDocuments_.review: Encased is a CRPG that unfolds in a unique alternate history, blending elements of dystopia and sci-fi within a 1970s setting. Drawing inspiration from renowned titles like Fallout 1 and 2, S.T.A.L.K.E.R., Wasteland, and the tabletop RPG Paranoia, the game immerses players in a rich narrative. With striking artwork and visuals contributing to the atmospheric ambiance, it captures the essence of the genres it draws inspiration.In the early stages of my gameplay, I found the main story to be both interesting and engaging. The game's appeal is further heightened by its potential for replay ability; the world and its NPCs dynamically respond based on your chosen "Wing" or class during character creation. This ingenious design choice introduces diverse play styles and varying dialogue choices, offering a fresh experience with each playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; You control a single character fallout-style and spend your time exploring a sort of corporate owned planet. If you like a cool setting and a lot of NPC's with interesting things to say you will thoroughly enjoy the role play aspect. The interplay between the "wings" (basically job groups) is very interesting and apparent. However, gameplay is terrible. Combat is EXTREMELY basic and dull to the point of tedium. The Good: The Story: The story is Interesting enough. There's Nothing terribly unique about it but it's shown effectively through interaction with NPCs and the environments you visit. You get a good sense of your identity and position as a cog in the machine of what is essentially a corporation owned planet. Each "Wing" (group that denotes your job and status) is unique and has a fair amount of specific interactions you can only do based on which wing you choose. There's a lot of quests to be had but keeping track can be confusing (see "The dec). I'd say if you are only interested in the story and walking around talking to people there is a good amount of gameplay to be had. If you don't like reading this is probably not the game for you as there is A LOT of dialogue everywhere you go and skipping through it without reading can have big consequences.The Decent:Abilities (Mechanic): Pretty fallout-esque you need a certain amount of skill in certain abilities to pull off specific tasks. For example you need a certain rank in criminal to lock-pick certain doors. The ability system is layered and pretty similar to those found in fallout games. At the beginning of the game you spend your points on deciding what your persons characteristics are (muscle, charisma, brains, etc.). What you choose as your characteristics will affect the starting values of abilities as well as things like HP and AP. You then select 3 fields to specialize in which will increase your skill in them by 20 each. Layered on top of this is a perk system which allows you to unlock specific actions within an ability. For example in the hand-to-hand tree you might unlock the kick ability allowing you to use it in combat. The ability to do other things like hacking or pick-pocketing also require a perk point to be spent in them before you are able to use the ability. Very fallout-esque but feels very janky in its execution. Some skills are far more important than others. The (very very) Bad:Combat: You ONLY control yourself and the combat is outright terrible. The "cover system" is not a cover system of any kind. When you end your turn you can decide to spend your remaining action points on "cover" which raises your defences to make you harder to hit. This being said there is no skill required for this as you can get the same defence buff regardless of where you are. There is nothing you can crouch behind for cover to get an increased chance of not being hit by ranged fire. Due to there being no cover system every fight devolves into just spamming attacks and medkits (if you can find some) and hoping you survive. It's a joke, a bad joke with no punchline, just utterly abysmal.

I did not care for this game so I will place here a recipe for huckleberry pancakes instead.Huckleberry pancakes.1 3/4 cups all purpose white flour4 tablespoons sugar1 tablespoon baking powder1/4 teaspoon salt1 1/2 cups of buttermilk5 tablespoon butter, melted2 large eggs1/2 cup HuckleberriesIn medium bowl combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt, set aside. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR:Yes it is an isometric futuristic shooter that you can easily confuse with Wasteland or the old Fallout games. But it lacks immersion. The developers wanted to create some sort of SF Dungeons & Dragons and made the game needlessly complex with totally unneeded obstacles (like sleep, hunger, thirst) thrown your way. Also I spend the first 3 hours opening containers and talking, with no combat at all. That kinda remained so.- The Good:- Finished, bug free with reasonable content- Good talents, perks, skills and gear- You can use different approaches like ranged or melee fight, criminal path, stealth, non violence- It looks reasonable okay- The Bad:- You spend at least half your time opening containers of which there must be 10.000, most of which have very little and un exciting content- Most NPC's have nothing to say and are just there for flavor. You cannot tell in advance which ones have quests.- This game is 1/4 combat, the rest is talking, doing fetching quests, puzzles, traveling all over, and.....opening containers- Without Google you will need hours extra to figure out how to proceed with quests and puzzles- The story and lore is pretty mediocre- Combat is slow and static, and not very exciting- All side quests are neglegible for reward and XP (you are better off doing random encounters for XP)- The ambient sounds are very repetitive with a truelly annoying laughing bird, laughing at you ploughing on- The developers wanted a true nerdy D&D system with lots of stats, statuses, afflictions, buffs, debuffs, but by doing so you are wasting your time doing useless things like sleeping, making food and drinking, which also helps to kill immersion and adding grindIf you like these type of isometric games I would suggest The Wasteland series or Atom RPG. This does not have the *one more turn* feel. I even skipped everything at 3/4 of the content just to finish it. Getting new level, new gear, new perks did not bother me anymore. And that says a lot about this type of game.Gameplay tip (SPOILER):- Instead of opening hundreds of containers, develop the criminal skill and rob all merchants (very easy w good skill). That way you can buy everything you need from those same merchants (they forget your crimes soon). You get ten times as much money that way and ten times faster.

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off great and gets increasingly worse.Progression is basically non-existent. I've worn the some armor for 10+ hours. Different armor is just different. I've swapped weapons ONCE in my entire game time, but I realized the weapon gave different skills, most of which were useless (I'm using Psionics, so the diff. is huge), and I just switched back to my first weapon. Upgrading my weapon gave me...2 damage. I have collected 20k in cash and have nothing to spend it on. Absolutely nothing to do.Skills are also mostly useless. The varied abilities I get are stretched across a variety of playstyles: sometimes I lack a stat to use an ability in the skill tree I invested 80 points in, sometimes its for a build I'm not. I haven't even noticed upgrading psionics affecting combat, so I have no idea what the point is.Scanning is a great idea... but all it does is give points that can be redeemed for healing items. XP scaling is also so egregious that the XP you get from doing anything but major quests and killing major enemies is completely useless. At the beginning of the game I managed to cheese and kill a very hard enemy and got 9000xp, jumping up one level. The average scan gives me... 32xp.The different between the factions also falls apart, and your role doesn't really matter at all (blue, black, etc.). The diversity of the prologue was exciting and awesome, but it quickly petered out. The first major city you get to, Magellan, is full of characters, dialogue, and quests. The biggest town in the game in Act 2 is... empty. And I mean empty. There's two major buildings in it and then... nothing. Just HUGE areas with nothing in them, taking forever to get anywhere. Generic NPC dialogue, empty buildings. Nothing. Whereas Magellan was full of items and things to loot and quests, almost every single container I opened was empty. It was like the team ran out of energy and decided to stop putting anything in the game.There's just nothing to keep me excited or interested. Companions don't matter much, and the story becomes mostly fetch quests without much logic or intrigue behind them. Also, what the hell is the point of a vehicle? You click it and it takes you to a random place on the map NOT of your choosing? And I can put points into this as a skill tree? Jesus.

_childDocuments_.review: 1976. In an alternate timeline, the Cold War comes to an end prematurely after The Dome is discovered; a monumental, indestructible structure in the middle of the desert. The world joins efforts to explore this area, where anomalous events and otherworldly artifacts are plentiful - the CRONUS corporation is born. As one of their employees, you'll start a new life in the Dome, ready to undertake assignments related to your specialization. Encased does a good job in offering a variety of interactions where your career and skill choices truly make the difference, with both characters and the environment, other than text-based roleplay panels. The writing is of high quality in most cases, with voiced narration and important characters creating a solid immersion feeling, effects / music are used wisely in most instances. This all proves true in the first parts of the game, however it progressively diminishes and falters as the story evolves. Later on, it feels like most NPCs are just standing there saying their piece, companions don't evolve or progress their agendas; terminals, documents and similar items become scarce or underwhelming compared to earlier on... it just becomes an unfinished, hasty mess story and lore wise.Venturing around the Dome is no joke: bandits, mutants, anomalies and more dangers await all explorers: moving through the desert will take a toll on body and mind, requiring sustenance and rest at regular intervals, otherwise heavy penalties and even death may incur. Random encounters - positive and negative alike - will also be a regular occurrence; later on vehicles also become available, considerably speeding up the exploration process with less effort.The world is divided into locations scattered through the Dome, some small, some sprawling multi-floor bases with dozens of NPCs and quests. Exploring each place thoroughly will reveal many secrets, and allow you to rack up a ton of loot to sell or use, but watch the weight limit. You can have your own way of exploring: stealthily lockpick doors and steal everything, pickpocket merchants, brute force your way through, or use diplomacy to become a friend of everyone. On a side note the stealth component is too good, allowing to pickpocket monstrous amounts of stolen loot from early on very easily, thus breaking game balance big time.The AP-based turn combat system is not the most complex, but works fairly well and is fun to play around with. Up to three people can compose a party, pitted against enemies that have diverse skill sets, resistances, weaknesses and unique proprieties depending on their type. Environmental elements like barrels, mines or other hazards can play an important part in fights, as they can be used to lure enemies into danger to your advantage - this mechanic is rather limited though, and never a main feat of gameplay. Weapon types, from pistols to clubs and heavy weapons, have specific skills related to your character's proficiency with them: the better your skill, the more abilities will be available to use - the same goes for utility skills like Science or Technology, Medicine and so on. Weapons use a 1-10 tier system, can be upgraded to improve damage, but lack any unique variants in their respective classes, with some being just better without downsides.While the challenge is solid in early and mid game phases (on hard, anyway), the party will feel overpowered in late game, especially if one does everything and acquires some serious gear. Hell, there isn't even a proper final boss or anything, just a spam of high-level mobs you fought many times before, in the endgame phases. Stealth once again screws combat, as with some good positioning you'll be able to pick off single enemies before they call for help, effectively reducing any fight to an easy 1v3, I didn't even have a stealth focused character, and this was really easy to pull off if I wanted to. Companions are useful, however they have one locked weapon you can never change (and a free slot), only upgrade via crafting using the materials found with looting. Also, they can't be leveled to your liking, as they follow a pre-determined progression... this really sucks.I cannot understate how bad Act 2 (second half of the game) is. Most quests, even main ones, will boil down to boring fetch tasks or boring dialogues with NPCs you'll have to travel the dome back and forth, like a ping-pong ball, to get a hold of. Quests start to become same-y, and sometimes with dubious descriptions of what to actually do, if any hint is given at all. Many logical interactions, like "what is that in your basement I just saw" simply do not exist, as they apparently never were accounted for. The roleplaying and interaction components become streamlined, only a shadow of what seen in the brilliant Act 1. The ending is a mess, in my case not even accounting for my actions in multiple cases and not elaborating on the destiny of many NPCs or companions.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really on the fence with this one.  There are plenty of things to like and dislike about it, but no game is "perfect" since everyone has different likes and dislikes.  I will say that chapter 1 is a lot more fun and the rest of the game kind of declines after that from a story standpoint.  There is plenty of story around if you choose to find it, but also plenty of ways to skip the story as well based on choices you make.  However, the story you find isn't very coherent after a certain point and really, after a while none of the factions are very appealing and I kinda feel like letting the dome die.  But overall it's a fun game with some mechanics that hearken back to the days of fallout.I am perplexed about some of the negative reviews complaining about the fatigue system, combat, and experience.  Well, perhaps if you're solo combat is difficult?  But combat and combat abilities are based on your skill level as well as damage level of the weapon of choice, then damage mitigated by the protections that enemies have.  It's a pretty cool system and encourages you to either have a variety of weapons on hand or variety of companions or at least think a little.  Paired with certain perks, though, combat gets downright easy later in the game... so I suppose eventually it's a bit disappointing.  As for the fatigue system... It's a pretty cool element to keep you from doing too many actions with impunity.  Besides, take some Energon or find a sleepng bag... they're all over the place.  And level 1 fatigue penalty is a joke so you can really perform a ton of actions before you have to sleep.  Not sure why it's such a stumbling block for people.  As for experience, you don't HAVE to fight... I'm pretty sure ever... so how is a character who is built for non-combat supposed to be able to level up other than searching through boxes and exploring?  Again, kind of an elegant solution so just about any play style can enjoy the game.The story that is there is kinda cool.  Locked under the dome, exploring alien technology, which is also exploring you.  It does get a bit bogged down in the middle and late game, though and would have been cooler if the alien tech angle could have been explored a bit more.  Lots of cool encounters traveling in the desert.  Be careful, though, your curiosity can easily get you killed... which is also cool, in my opinion.  You can choose to fight or sneak and it seems like it is possible to not fight at all if you build your character the right way.  I don't know because... I'm a terrible thief, always get caught and don't like confined spaces.But there are some bad things about the game.  Companions are not that helpful... almost bordering on being nothing more than mules.  Sure they might have some skills that are useful for a bit, but they seem to level up and get all their points allotted to combat so the reality is if you want tech, science, medicine or criminal skills... you've got to level them on the PC  because you have no control over companion level up and their point allotments seem to concentrate more on combat.  The only useful one seems to be Crump because I can use his freak strength to break into most things that my criminal skill can't yet open.  As the mid game and end game approach the story gets slower and things are bogged down by fetch quests to disparate parts of the dome.  Everything takes too long and it can be a struggle.  As I said before , I don't particularly want to help any of the factions.  The all pretty much suck in their own way... except maybe Picnic... but I think that might be by design.  Anyway, I think it's a fun game despite having a bit of a slog in the middle.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite only just getting into in early access, this game already has a lot of love and effort put into it. Black for guards, orange for menial labour and so forth. This is one of the most refreshing ideas for a character background I've seen in a long time and I greatly enjoy how it changes which info you can get, how some quests play out and how others interact with you. I really hope this system will carry on through the full game and not lose importance along the way, because it really makes your choice matter and you'll want to replay the game several times over just to try the other "career paths".With very nice and detailed scenery, good music and genuinely interesting writing this is one of the games I cannot wait to follow as the developers continue to work on it, and I am happy to be able to support it as they do. I am certain it will grow into one of the all-time RPG greats if they continue on this path. With the first massive content patch around the corner, things are definitely looking good.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to most post-apocalyptic games, Ecnased offers a very different world, which is a plus if you're tired of the old nuclear wars and zombies. The main story is interesting enough, but I think the game doesn't give you much reasons to join available factions aside from the "default" one - the logic of the world really forces you to side with scientists and administrators, not with warlords and crazy fanatics.I also liked that most characters in this game are named - including corpses left over from The Incident, which makes it a bit more personal, and should in theorhy push the player toward a more pacifistic path (but it didn't quite work for me, to be honest).What I didn't like was combat. Compared to Wasteland 3, or even Underrail it's boring. Available abilities are uninspired, enemies are not very varied, there is no covers sytem, and basically the only thing you can do to gain advantage is to use the rudimentary stealth system. It would be OK if the whole game was designed around this concept, like Mutant Year Zero, but it is not. And so most combats are plain boring.At the time of this review, the last quarter of the game feels a bit unfinished, especially compared to the first few hours, which set a very high bar. Hopefully, this will be remedied in time to some degree with patches, and maybe an enchanced edition, but for now, you have to be prepared for somewhat lackluster locations farther away from the starting point, and somewhat confusing finale (hint: you need to exit the location to trigger epilogue).Character development is comparable to other Fallout-like games (and make no mistake, this IS a Fallout-like), which is to say it's interesting and provides several paths through most encounters.There are a few named companions, but I'm not sure if they have quests - I never discovered one. At least, you can control them in combat, unlike in ATOM RPG or the original Fallout.

_childDocuments_.review: Very uneven game. Interesting world, cool companions, wild stakes and starts off very strong with lots to do but then falls apart hard once the 1st act is finished.Like others have said: You get massive cities which are barren with very few things to interact with. I'll add this, too: even the english translation gets much worse after Act 1, with typos becoming way more common and a very ambiguous meaning to what is said and the consequences of your actions. I had trouble understanding the implications of some of the final decisions and endings (of which there are like 10) because the meaning in their description seems like it got mildly lost in translation from Russian to English. I honestly didn't care much about what happened to the world and its people and that's pretty bad in a cRPG.Combat aims to be Divinity: Original Sin in a post-apocalyptic setting but doesn't quite get there. Most of the time you're better off just doing basic attacks and all the extra skills and effects are mostly fluff save for a few. The fatigue system is also a major pain in the butt. It just forces you to always have stacks of a certain item that you down like tic-tacs to counteract it.It's extremely easy even on the highest difficulty. The game awards too much XP, which in turn means that skill-checks are also too forgiving, in my experience. After a certain point I actively avoided getting XP because even with 90 skill points unspent I was able to pass every single skill check the game threw at me barring the ones for basic stats like Deftness.Economy is completely messed up. I had no issues but someone who doesn't pickpocket or lockpick and has no Tech skill is in for a rough time. There is also a shortage of traders and you'll more often than not have to rely on random encounters if you want to buy gear.Faction system feels like a forgotten afterthought. The game tries to pass this idea of "complete freedom" but the systems aren't robust enough to let you do that. If you try to antagonize a faction too hard you might easily break the game or at the very least make it miserable for yourself with the constant hit squads that are sent out to kill you. On this topic, the game seems to offer some options for silent assassination of certain key characters but for some reason it doesn't work out.Bugs aren't as bad as Wasteland 3 but they are there. I found one cool bug near the end when I tried to kill the 2 key leaders of a certain faction and one was unkillable because of certain circumstances, forcing me to stay in combat indefinitely with no chance to end it.In the end, although I got a lot of hours out of the game because I love the setting, it did leave a sour taste. It's still an early access title that they just decided to brand as "1.0" and launch. Heck, they added the voice lines for companions a week after launch. The game also does a lot of "tell" rather than "show" and while I'm not averse to reading it does feel like you have to use your imagination more often than you'd like."Atom RPG" is a more interesting, deeper and all-around better Fallout clone than "Encased" is. To be fair, they also built a lot of it after launch, so maybe "Encased" will grow into a much better title over time.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I've changed this to a conditional like. I'll leave the original review intact for comparison. See the edits that follow the initial review.Like many have said for other games, I REALLY wanted to like this game. Story-wise, the game is great. I loved the set up, and the conversations I engaged in. The graphics were good, and immersive. However, what killed this game for me is the combat system. It's extremely one dimensional. You have no options to use cover and movement is not a factor in making you harder to hit. You generally get hit about 80 percent of the time with both ranged and melee, so what combat devolves to is your character standing still, firing off an attack, and then hitting the v key in hope that the boosted defence class will carry you through to the next round. Sadly, in more difficult encounters, this is not the case. Even turning down the difficulty only mitigates this somewhat. So stand, shoot, defend...rinse, repeat. Ultimately boring as hell. Granted, I'm prejudiced by games such as Phoenix Point. Starfall, which does not focus solely on turn-based combat utilizes a move and cover system that makes their tactical combats fun and engaging to play. Proper use of terrain can give you a huge edge in a combat engagement. Even Shadowrun had a basic cover system, which again made combats fun. It should be a key component in this game, but sadly is not. So, with regret, I submitted my refund request. I would've like to have seen the story play out, but the combat system just annoyed me way too much.Edit: So no refund, as I had played too many hours as per Steam refund policy. So I'll reduce the game to story difficulty and plough my way through it just to see the story unfold. Hopefully at least that will live up to expectations.Second Edit: Playing on Story difficulty. Getting used to the combat system, and having companions definitely helps. But I'm still not impressed by it. However, the other game mechanics, and the story itself are great. The reputation system is well done, as is the skill and barter system. Also, you can pretty much interact with everybody, which can yield quite a few side quests as well as some surprising companions. So I can honestly say I'm enjoying the game now.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: Still raw, needs more salt, more time in the ovenI really wanted to like this game, but I couldn't finish it. Time will tell if the developers come back to this game because parts of it look rushed or unfinished.Story: The game has lot of influences like Fallout 1/2, Roadside picnic, stalker and reminds me a bit of Stargate and Atlantis because of the scientific archaeological corporation that your character works for. The intro to the game serves as a strong hook, after that the rest of the game struggles to live up the expectations set by the introduction and you find yourself losing interest once you enter the "rest of the game" stage which leaves me wanting what could have been.Gameplay: Pretty much your standard turn based rpg like Fallout 1/2 and Wasteland 2 where you have a semi-classless system. When making your character, you chose which branch of the corporation your character comes from and that gives them bonuses towards certain character skills and interactions with the other factions. I think it adds a nice flavor to game in terms of player choice and adding something to the game's setting.Unfortunately after the game's introduction is over, you will find yourself with a number of unskippable combats like town raids where hostile npcs will randomly spawn and attack whatever settlement you happen to be visiting. Settlements don't repopulate and once the guards are finally killed off, you will find yourself having to defend the town yourself. This is also annoying during the beginning parts of the game because you will find your starting gear more and more obsolete and you will find yourself facing off against harder enemies which eat away at ammo/healing enemies in your inventory and many of the rewards not worth the risk. There is a crafting system to offset your logistical burden, however the burden remains and many main quests will require some form of combat to be completed.Overall: I think its still worth checking out if you are GM and you looking for ideas for your next campaign at the table. Just don't be deceived by the game's introduction.
