_childDocuments_.review: Encased is a pretty interesting and engaging game. It has good Story Line and multitude of side quests and small tasks typical of a RPG Game. It has some cool concepts and mechanics of its own like the dome, the relics, the scanning system and Knowledge Points. There are some bugs as the game is in EA stage. After 5/6 months and with some work it may become a great Post-Apocalyptic Game. PROS:1) Good Story (At least the starting part which is accessible 2) Plenty of Small Side quests and tasks 3) Good Character Customisation Options 4) Interesting Mechanics like Scanning and Knowledge Points 5) Exploration is very much awarding on the World Map and Location Maps.6) Fighting skills and social skills are plentiful and varied. There are also many types of weapons can be found even at this Early Access stage. 7) Interesting Caste / Profile Concepts and Unique Dialogue and action choices CONS (May be changed at later stages of EA):1) Combat Animations specially for Psi abilities and Hand to hand combat are poor and not varied 2) Quest Logs (Specially for side quests) are sometimes confusing and You have to do plenty of reading and needed some guesswork to resolve the quests3) Major Translation and Language Issues. 4) Companion movement and controlling the companion character out of combat5) Inventory Management 6) Tiresome and complex weapon creation and upgradation mechanics. 7) Releasing small asethic components and customizations like gears and clothing as DLC and extra paid content is not cool thing at all. It's a very bad thing for an EA Release. These should be available for free for at least EA buyers. I am overall happy with the game at the price I bought it. Its being developed steadily and there has been regular Dev Blogs, Lore Snippets and Hotfixes. I am very much hopeful that it will turn out to be a great game after 4/5 months.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the funniest games I have played in a long time. I would wholeheartedly recommend anyone to play a "as a bag of hammers" play through with max 2 in brains. I had many belly laughs.Story wise this game is absolutely fantastic.Gameplay it does a lot of things well, hide information in the environment, all the skills work the way they are supposed too, that kind of thing. I would advise to look at the "Condition" of to use items, and to read recipe's you find to learn them. The game is not very clear about these aspects.Combat is ok, it could be better. I'm personally not a big fan of the fatique system, and a big part of that is simply not having a bar on screen to accurately keep track of it at all times.The game is huge, it took me about 70 hours to play through it fully reading all the lore and doing everything there is to do.I would add there are 2 places in the game that feel unfinished, but with the upcoming content patches I feel this is something that may get improved upon in the future.Stealth, lockpicking and the like is something that could be improved, especially how it ties into the fatique system, but also that it's a bit overpowered compared to the rest of the skills. Also the pickpocket lockouts are unnecessary - lots of way to circumvent anyway, and the feel of some weapons and psychics could be improved.The level design is gorgeous, even though there's a little too much loot lying around, and you get encumbered pretty quickly, as a hoarder,... bit sad to leave loot lying around. This coupled with an inventory system that could do with a small update in terms of sorting and stacking, and a clearness of learned/used items. But this is offset with how much there is too craft, and I should've started sooner with that because resources are plenty.There's multiple ways to play though quests, and if you want to have a blast - murder everyone in the church and come back a week later :pAll in all I would recommend this game. Big + for the story, the quirkiness and the love that most obviously went into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I only just barely recommend this and only if you absolutely love isometric RPG's like Fallout 1 / 2, Wasteland 2 or the like.WARNING: Make sure you read through what your stats do before finalizing your character. There are next to no primary stat upgrades in the game, so make sure you understand how you've shaped your character!This game is extremely poorly designed and obviously is missing a manager or has an inexperienced and/or incompetent lead developer. It lacks vision, a lot of the content is pointless, the story is barely functional, the progression is garbage and you will spend most of your time fruitlessly clicking on containers to find absolute tons of trash that you might feel compelled to hoard for crafting purposes.Enemies don't drop their weapons, which is infuriating. Getting gear is a test of extreme patience and there's nothing you can do to accelerate the process. The game seems to scale most things according to your level, which continues to be a terrible way to design games. Some enemies, for no logical reason, are scaled too high for an area. Crafting is barely functional and overloaded with components. The skill system is convoluted, hacking is almost entirely pointless and lockpicking is tiered weirdly. You want lockpicks? You need scissors to break. Why? Apparently bobby pins are an overused trope and it had to be something you can make with crafting, I don't know...The pacing is god awful. It's always been bad in CRPG's what with you running around in towns and talking to everyone, but here it's even worse with there being micro hubs with next to no content and then a couple of massive hubs where you run around forever with next to no combat to break it up. Outside you just go from one combat encounter to the next and a lot of it is meaningless filler content with no story or logic behind it. There are giant cockroaches. Why? Because Fallout had giant radiated creeps, but radscorps are probably trademarked so let's make a creature known for surviving radiation be giant. The setting loves to tell you every five minutes that this is supposed to be in the 70's, but there's nothing besides some retro futuristic design to actually prove that.The game follows the trope of every competent leader being a woman and every man is incompetent/evil/naive/stupid.There's a non-binary person, because those were all over the place in the 70's and you can't even question it.Every second or third security guard/soldier and nearly every mechanic you can talk to is a woman, because that's totally what the 70's were like. There's one guy who sort of matches the setting and that's a slick black dude with an afro, who also happens to be an alcoholic. Apparently that's the only appropriate time specific representation they were comfortable with. There are interesting ideas, but they rarely go anywhere.Most of the dialogue is somewhere between "full of tropes" and "infantile". This may have been a good practice experience for the writers but if they haven't learned anything, fire and blacklist them from the industry.Review was longer, but steam complained about the length. Avoid if you don't have time to waste on a rushed indie title.

The development team also seems to quite active if you take the time to read their community responses, so I am hopeful for continued support and additions to the game. I hope this turns into another ATOM RPG, as the first game took some time to get better (both as the team learned new tools, added new content, and improved their writing) which is reflects in their latest game of trudograd with all that they have learned. _childDocuments_.review: A friend purchased this for me, and turned me on to this game that's coming out Sept 7th. A sci-fi isometric action rpg called Encased. It's like a combination of Fallout 1&2 meets Shadowrun, with heavy influences from Outer Worlds. It's currently in a BG3 style Early Access - the first Act is available, and the rest will come out at release. The devs gave a technical explanation for why more content can't be added to the EA version. It is understandable.Interesting concept. Based in the early 70's, just after the Cold War. A giant, semi-invisible Dome is discovered over a great expanse of remote desert. Scientists, Soldiers, Laborers (Criminals looking for a new start - they seem to need to earn this freedom, as they have special handcuff bracelets that allow them freedom to roam, but shock them if they pick up a weapon), Explorers, and Administration. These are the class types, divided by color-coded "Wings". I chose a custom made scientist. White Wing. A corporation, "CRONUS", hires these people to enter, live, and work in the Dome, uncovering strange "Forefather" relics to send back to the outside world, which must be entered via a long elevator from the top, miles above the earth. Any living creature who tries to leave, disintegrates. Once you enter, you can never leave the Dome. They hope to solve this mystery.I've not gotten far in (In fact someone in the discord informed me I'm almost better off waiting for the full game to be released because save files won't transfer over). But I'm just enjoying it so much. The writing is phenomenal. No voice actors - this is an old-fashioned isometric - with one major difference. The camera angle can be turned a full 360 degrees! Refreshing!I look forward to playing the full version, and will update my review if necessary.

_childDocuments_.review: After some thought, I have decided to recommend the game after all. My original points remain unchanged, but the promise of additional content and the fact that this game is really cheap for the amount of content it does have, has swayed my recommendation. First the good:(1) 99% bug free. - I explored the entire map, such as it is, and the game was pretty much bug free. Nothing stopped you from progressing on any quests, and there truly are multiple ways to complete each quests. Go ham and kill every quest giving NPC and you can still progress. Steal everything from the NPC that needs to give you the quest item and you can still progress. The development team did a really good job with their programming, which is rare for newly released games (I'm looking at you kingmaker) Now the bad.(1) The game content is unfinished. While there is plenty to do in the first 1/3 of the game and the areas feel fleshed out, the later half of the game is extremely disappointing. Many of the main faction locations have nothing other than the main quests and the NPCs are sparsely sprinkled. While it did make it easy to give all the quest givers - you can literally talk to everyone since there weren't a lot of people. You do spend most of your time just running around. (2) Nothing really matters. Your choices doesn't really matter, your reputations doesn't really matter, the factions doesn't really matter. In a word, the your impact on the story is pretty much Nil. While indiscriminately killing everyone will not stop your progress, it also doesn't really affect anything in game or the ending. Build up your reputation with a faction to over 100? No affect on the game. Build up your reputation with a companion to over 100? same thing. When you finish the game, it feels like you just wasted your time running around, hoarding stuff, and for me, be OCD and open every item on every item at every location in the world map. Take away.The game could have been great, but it suffered from too much ambition. It had some pretty funny jokes, great mechanics, but the actual story itself needs to be fleshed out more. There were too many factions, too many companions but not enough content for each wing, companion, or location. The game would have been much better served cutting the number of factions in half and giving a greater depth to each faction. Rather than standing with the greats like Wasteland 2 and 3 or divinity, this feels more like a half-assed attempt of Trudogrod.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start by saying I am a fan of lore-heavy, character-build fest RPGs, and Encased DELIVERS solidly on both scores. The graphics aren't insane by any imagination, but the mix of static artwork and a rotateable 3d  field of play meshes very well with the turn-based combat. There are a million little ways to game the system, and it feels very much like the designers built it that way. Got a Criminal skill rating of 150? You can steal (almost) anything in the game! Should you? Maybe not! The outcome of events in the plot, whether this is true or not, *feels* very choice-heavy. The constant reminder of what choices WOULD have been available to you in various encounters, had you picked a different class, certainly aids this feeling. The explicitness of stats being tied to battle conditions, being tied to combat effectiveness is great - if you pay even a little attention to how the stats all interact you can start to pick apart enemy weaknesses - as long as you have the right skills and tools in your party! And not all of the NPC companions are super easy to find, which I find kind of great. Multiple endings give you the chance to either savescum all of them, or try new playthroughs with different classes. I've just started a second playthrough and I'm not sure about replayability, but it's got potential. All in all a solid-a** game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, until suddenly it isn't.The first 25 or so hours are fantastic, and all I want from an RPG: original setting, choices that matter, quests with different outcomes, different ways to handle situations depending on your build, fights that are difficult but mostly avoidable, no 'filler' fights... I don't like how scarce ammunition/health/healing kits/money are, which often makes getting into fighting a bad choice, but that is a defendable design choice.And then, after powering the Emulator, all that changes: the new maps are still huge, but will have only one or two persons of actual interest on them, side quests all but disappear, leaving only the main quest, NPC don't have interesting backstories/dialog any more but just the lines needed for the quest, and your have to travel more which leads to random fights which you don't want (see above).Judging from the Steam achievements, less than 1 in 5 players get to this point, so I can't blame the developers too much for focusing on the beginning of the game. I still recommend the game based on that first 25 hours, but how I wish it could have maintained that level of content... As it is, I don't think I will finish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, great experience. Suffers from the same curse a lot of other CRPGs suffer from: the conceptual scope being far beyond what material reality could allow for. There are a lot of things in the game that felt half implemented or as if there was meant to be more but there wasn't. That being said, the story is great, setting is actually quite unique, writing is good, endings are satisfying if you take the effort to complete side quests, and you get to kill yourself in a million different very fun ways.
_childDocuments_.name: Encased: A Sci-Fi Post-Apocalyptic RPG

_childDocuments_.review: Encased gave me a nostalgia of my younger years playing Fallout2. While the game is fun, I have found many things to be quite tedious. When I first started, I could not find any guides describing the character builds and play styles. I ended up restarting the game probably about 4 times and playing all the way through until fast-forwarded through time. After finally making a decent build (and quite burnt out on redoing everything) I found myself getting irritated with the amount of lootables in any given area. Like you can have 6 plants, 4 ammo boxes, 3 crates, 4 lockers and so on only in one area. I found myself wasting SO much time trying to loot everything to make sure I didn't miss out on anything important. As the game progressed, it became so excessive that by pressing ALT, my screen would just be flooded by dialogue boxes. That being said the game is sort of cheesy because collecting loot from places just doesn't seem all that exciting and I was never low or feeling in need of supplies.The game is also a bit predictable. There is a work around to everything so I just don't feel very challenged progressing through the maps except for when I encounter an exceptionally tough baddy. The perks/ inventory system doesn't always do what its supposed to do.  For example, you have 8 strength and you need 9 to bust open a locker. You take a perk giving you one additional strength and you still wont be able to open that locker. Same thing applies to stats given from equip-able items.Encased has a lot of potential and is still pretty fun despite a few drawbacks. Hopefully in the future some of these things get addressed.
_childDocuments_.name: Encased: A Sci-Fi Post-Apocalyptic RPG

_childDocuments_.review: I just started playing this, it definitely has an old school isometric feel that echos back to fallout and fallout 2. I like the general feel of the play, although I am not a fan of the inventory system, the system could be better then what it is now.  I also wish the overall map system had more of a glossary to it. I found myself wandering around for a good 10-15 minutes trying to figure out where I was supposed to go. I have high hopes for this game, I am sure it will be even better when it is fully completed.
_childDocuments_.name: Encased: A Sci-Fi Post-Apocalyptic RPG

_childDocuments_.review: Strong (pre directors cut) wasteland 2 vibes: solid RPG mechanics with an interesting setting but clunky, ugly, unpolished game with awkward combat and writing and voice acting that varies wildly in quality. Plus points to the design and writing of (some) of the companions because I wanted to know more about them. Wasteland 3 was much better though and I hope the devs get the chance to deliver a sequel to this which hopefully will also be better. 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Encased: A Sci-Fi Post-Apocalyptic RPG

_childDocuments_.review: For an early access game it's pretty good. Some missing textures and a lot of bugs (buying houses, no bed in the Magellan apartment, etc...) still but that is to be expected. Quest system needs location information, also a problem with picking up and completing quests before they are given but this will come with better scripting in the final release. Some lessons to be learned still from Fallout 2 but I am very optimistic about this game. It deserves to be supported and is worth playing.=========Feb 2021 update. I am changing my recommendation for from yes to no because of the lack of development with all these content patches. For an early release this game had some potential but I am not seeing much in the way of progress. Will revisit this as updates come in

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge Fallout 1 & 2 fan. When Wasteland 3 came out, I thought it scratched my itch pretty well, although it's quite combat heavy. This one manages to recreate the overall feeling of the good old FO's even better. I haven't played that much yet but I already love it. I'm glad I waited for it to leave early access so that I could dive into the whole thing for my first play through.More games like this pls.
_childDocuments_.name: Encased: A Sci-Fi Post-Apocalyptic RPG

_childDocuments_.review: It's the Fallout 1/2 homage you've been waiting for for some time. The world building is fascinating, there's multiple playstyles and it's actually pretty hard to screw up your build, you won't find that halfway through the game you have to start over because you skimped out on a stat. Combat is not difficult as some reviews state, you just have to specialize and invest your first few skill points in it, the game throws experience at you for EVERYTHING so leveling is not an issue. They've promised a completely different style of playthrough if you give your character low intelligence, I'm looking forward to trying that.The game's not without issues, Act I is very busy and polished (as it was the playable portion in Early Access for two years); after that the world opens up yet it feels like there's nothing to do but the main quest. Companion pathfinding is bizarre. The economy is kind of wack in terms of getting money. You'll spend 90% of the game with your starting gear. There's a reputation system that feels like it doesn't matter, neither do most of the choices you make during the game except at the very, very end. All that said, I still think it's worth playing if you loved the original Fallout games.I've been watching the game improve over it's time in EA and was excited for its release. Encased definitely scratched the itch more than ATOM (a game I'd also recommend) but there's a lot of missed potential that I hope the dev team continues to work on for to balance the pacing of the mid-late game.
_childDocuments_.name: Encased: A Sci-Fi Post-Apocalyptic RPG

_childDocuments_.review: A big fan of cRPGs reporting in. I can't recommend this game because it lacks of everything. I keep pushing myself to like this game, expecting it to become better, but it fails to entertain me in every aspect.1. The quality of DIALOGUES is just poor. They are extremely straight and dull. The narrator reads them ridiculously slow and sometimes I had to turn off the volume in order to read it faster and just get over them. Most of quests (maybe 90%) are straight forward and nothing interesting come out from them.2. SOUND and MUSIC are horrendous! Music is barely noticeable and it sounds like someone very untalented composed it. Sounds and FXes are also very simple and uninspired.3. Not much I can say about COMBAT. It exists and lack of Tactics or any of "fun" elements itself. You just use skills and simply shoot enemies and et al.4. STORY is not catchy and it didn't resonate in me at all. I completed story missions to see the plot development, but when I look back at them now, I see them as chores, more than entertainment.

_childDocuments_.review: Its like fallout and Xcom in that the handling, targeting and even how the mobs almost never miss but your guys always do. If you consider buying it beware that if you leave the main compound where the game is boring you to death with faction quests and move out into the real world you won't have long to play. Make sure while your in the compound to stock up on all things trash, eventually you'll get to work benches and can make lockpicks, and essentials you'll need later. I sold the majority of that stuff on the first run. I hope they keep their promise and keep adding on to the game. Its not bad and not great and what I expected. I will recommend this game at this time however I'm a bit skeptical in this day and age of Betas, and Alphas requesting money then not fulfilling their obligations. BEWARE!I lost interest in the game after the latest patch. I had already pushed the content, new content came out and rehashed the game that I didn't really care for doing the first time. I started over and just quit when i couldn't open doors in the beginning.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this on kickstarter some years ago, and I have played every stage of the beta builds/Early Access they uploaded here. The amount of progress and changes was great to see, and the assets/areas they have shown off for the final build look solid. I definitely recommend this to any Fallout fans, or old school RPG fans in general. It is a unique world, that has familiar feelings and themes. One bit of advice, don't be afraid to try other zones if you're having trouble in one. Go get more ammo, better gear, or a few levels under your belt, then come back and try it again. The game has difficult combat at early levels, so you have to be mindful of how much you are tackling.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy the game. Ok, let's start with the cons:- there are patches coming and bugs, too. Devs are working on it, but it is still pretty much enjoyable. The community shares solutions for serious bugs, so no problem there.- when you kill an enemy, he doesn't drop his weapon. Reason: the higher the level of a weapon, bigger the damage, and bigger the cost, so the game' economy is built over this concept. If enemies dropped their weapons, you would be millionaire in seconds;- few enemy types with different (odd) subtypes. For example, there is the hyena monster type. Then we have the cannon-mounted hyena, the psychic hyena, the tanker hyena, you got the drill;- I would not recommend playing like a lone wolf. Some things are odd about a solo build. For example, the Action Movie Perk, which gives you +40% damage if travelling alone, is only available if you have Charisma 10, which is a skill focused on giving bonuses to companions. - Influence with factions or companions doesn't do much right now, which is a shame. I love to have access to different quests or ways of ending the game based on my actions and who I support or hate;- Contraptions skills require items PER USE. Explaining further, Contraptions is a weapon skill that have the "toys" of the game on it: teleporters, jetpacks, cloacking devices, etc. BUT you consume the items when you use the skills, forcing you to keep crafting or buying it in order to have access to these skills;- Pilot, when related to vehicles, doesn't do much, and that doesn't make sense at all. You may have the skill Pilot, you may find a car with a working battery, and you may be carrying fuel, BUT YOU CAN'T DRIVE the car out in the world map. I just have no idea why... Devs must have a reason for this, probably restraints in what they code program or not.Now let's talk about the pros:- RPG game with an open character creation approach. You can master any skill, create any kind of build. Right now I am playing a charismatic psionic with expertise in high-technology weapons like blasters and flamethrowers. But I want to try a survival and explorer Lara Croft build, a Powersuit (called Servosheel) Machine Gun Soldier build, and others. This game allows many different approaches;- Although not having a deep story, companions can be gathered to cover your weak points. Example, my char has Muscle 1, but I have a follower with Muscle 10 that does Muscle tasks for me. - You can bypass main quests. As an example, you need to get an item that a church character holds. My character that respects people's free will was asked by the representative of the "Church" to attract more people to them and then he would give me the item. I said "Not doing that", went to his office, opened his safe, took the device, and got out before they realized I commited a crime (they can notice crimes and follow clues until they reach you, which is a nice concept on itself).  THIS CONCEPT IS AMAZING! It doesn't obligate you all the time to follow a predetermined path. You can try to make your own path as your character' roleplay sees fit;- VENDORS DROP ALL THEIR INVENTORY! This is something we don't see all the time in games! I chose to be enemy of a faction (the crazy faction, the Fops, at the moment) and I attack all their caravans and get all the items the vendor had. - (For players that like to explore) There are maps on the Internet but I suggest you to go blindly looking for unkown locations to explore. It is really nice to find a new area, reveal its secrets, kill the monsters, get the loot and go to where the wind is going to take you next. Just be aware that many missions are hidden in some of these maps, including parts of the main mision;- And talking about exploring, everything changes when you find URSULA, that metal huge bear! When the mission appears to you, do it. When I found it and got it, it can be an incredible asset to your playthrough or game style. Some "old school" explorers may prefer not use it, but it is amazing anyway.- Crafting system is meaningful. Something seems useless until you realize where it is used to craft something. Take a look at some crafting guides if you are too much lost as I was in the beginning. Anyway, of course this game is not for everyone. It tries to be a turn-based (check) post-apocalypse themed (check) RPG (check) with an open character development approach (check) focused on exploration rather than linear main story development (check). If you don't want to explore the map, the game will be way quicker and boring, that is for sure. But all things considered, this is a game so well done that made me stop playing PIllars of Eternity (not saying Pillars is worse, it is not, it is just different) and come to play this every day since. I hope you have fun, too! And kill all the FOPS!

_childDocuments_.review: Encased is a great attempt to revive the gameplay of the classic Fallout games, with a few notable changes and more than enough Larian Studios DNA to change things up a bit.This is a diverting and fun game with the caveat that currently it requires significant patching as I have run into multiple game breaking bugs, not to mention the multiple game logic bugs such as perks not working, park descriptions being confusing and occasionally AI thats too stupid to defend itself.Overall, very good classic-Fallout-style gameplay but it needs a little more time to take the rough edges off.
_childDocuments_.name: Encased: A Sci-Fi Post-Apocalyptic RPG

_childDocuments_.review: Great theme and good worldbuilding, but undercooked gameplay and poor writing make it a mediocre game, a significant number of bugs and crashes turn it into a thumbs down at launch.As a huge fan of the original Fallout games this follows in their footsteps in many ways while adding some neat diversity in terms of what "Wing" you start with that has actual repercussions in the game. Lots of skills, perks, etc. make making a character fun but there are extreme balance issues. Don't worry though because even the hardest "Tactical" difficulty is very easy for anyone who has played a game like this before.The diversity of skills are great, and tasks often have a couple of valid solutions, though not every quest can be solved with any given method, as is good and proper. Combat is hilariously unbalanced with certain builds ripping through the hardest difficulty trivially. Crafting is a hot mess, you can build some neat things but you need to gather up every bit and bob just in case some recipe might need something, you end up with an inventory full of generic crafting stuff, and using your supplies has little in the way of interesting decision making.The UI and UX are severely undercooked, you'd think the game came out 15 years ago with how many modern UI conveniences it is missing and antiquated design choices like have 10 different boxes you need to loot one by one in a given room of an area. Most of the time the loot is worthless, but occasionally you find amazing things like a book worth a whole level's worth of skill points, so the smart way to play is to tediously loot every single container, corpse, etc. you can find.The writing is poor, it's a little better than the original English release of ATOM RPG, but not by much. Quest instructions, both from characters and the quest log are mostly worthless,With some more time spent polishing and a significant writing pass the game could be great, but it is under-cooked at launch, wait to see if they make an effort to patch things up before buying at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Encased: A Sci-Fi Post-Apocalyptic RPG

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little weird science Fallout-esque RPG. The early combat especially reminds me of Fallout because trying to kill anything with weak ass guns is a lesson in futility - hand to hand and bladed weapons are much, much better than shooting someone with a 9mm early on. So unless you want to go melee you should plan on a lot of sneaking (Criminal skill) early on, though you can combine the two later with a throat slit from stealth attack so thats cool. My main complaint is that even with a nice powerful silenced assault rifle, using anything other than aimed shot is pointless because of absolutely absurd accuracy penalties for all the other attacks in the light arms skill tree (and I assume this will apply to any other ranged weapon that fires quickly). I'm already at level 10 and the accuracy penalties (which are on the skills themselves - there are no "accurate" weapons, just how accurate the skill is) are still pretty silly against anything my own level or higher, so I just stick to aimed shot with the perk to remove its cooldown and this is fine I guess. Pop a few aimed shots, throw down a smoke from the criminal skill tree and fade. Repeat.  Maybe they'll do more combat balance passes in the future to make being a brass spewing madman worthwhile. Still good, 89/100, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Encased: A Sci-Fi Post-Apocalyptic RPG

_childDocuments_.review: It's a top down isometric CRPG with crafting mechanics.  It's fun right up until the moment that you realize that the game forces you in to combat, and makes combat something you want to avoid.  There are enemies who will jump from several meters away, and instantly knock your character out.  There are swarms of bugs all of whom have WAY more HP than is necessary.  There are enemies with tranquilizer weapons that can and will render you unconscious, which if there are enemies around; is game over.  There are hordes of enemies and so far, no allies.  The weapon upgrade system has you sinking time, energy (literally, fatigue is something you have to manage in this game), and often money to allow you to do enough damage to actually kill enemies before they light you on fire, knock you out and toast marshmallows on your corpse.  Just to hand you a better weapon in a random drop.  How the game determines hit chance seems to be based entirely on the target's dodge.  Which means some enemies will just avoid the majority of what you throw at them including grenades because being in the explosion radius isn't enough; there's actually a roll against the targets defense which often results in your grenade not accomplishing anything.  I could go on with all the frustrations that have made me about throw up my hands, but what's the point?  Don't buy this game.  One more thing.  They call this a "tactical" RPG.  "Tactics" implies group combat, but near as I can tell; there's only gangs of enemies and maybe two allies (if you can find any).  It's not "tactical", it's obnoxious.UPDATE:  Having played a bit more; I have discovered that your character's base accuracy is ENTIRELY based off of the appropriate stat.  Upping the weapon skill does NOTHING to increase hit chance.  On top of that; enemies can have dodges/armor defence that means that even if you hit, they may just negate the entire attack.  This is quite possibly the worst combat system I have seen in a CRPG.
_childDocuments_.name: Encased: A Sci-Fi Post-Apocalyptic RPG

_childDocuments_.review: Magnificent. Brilliant  world-building and writing."Encased" just  oozes atmosphere.  With it's fantastic 70's influenced art style, memorable characters and situations, great faction system, extensive and deep systems of interaction, it is absorbing, immersive and compelling.Possessed of a level of density almost  approaching "Disco Elysium" as far as sheer amount of things, people and opportunities to interact with and sometimes in it's sheer weirdness. Evocative of the great Russian "stalker" genre sci-fi novels like "Roadside picnic", "Metro" etc but with it's own angle, spot-on existential horror and humour sometimes reminiscent of the pen and paper rpg "Paranoia", Encased reminds me of so many cool things whilst being pretty original and very cool  in it's own right.The combination of these factors coupled with a robust character creation system, some excellent music, surprising curve-balls and masterful storytelling make this a must buy for fans of RPGS. For me personally the game is actually better than "Fallout" 1 or 2 whilst reminding me why those games were so great and reminding me that other modern games that aspire to this end  have lacked a certain something for me, a certain presence that "Encased" displays in everything it does.Now of course, as many of you will know, this game is not yet a full release, in fact is reportedly the first third of the main story. Having said that there is still a lot of content here and what is here is very well executed in my opinion. Even at this stage you'll get your money's worth and the finished work should be amazing judging by the 14 hrs I've played the game for with the same character whilst still not at the end of the content currently playable. I'm seriously impressed.  9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Encased: A Sci-Fi Post-Apocalyptic RPG

_childDocuments_.review: (My) Reasons to play this game:- you like (C)RPGs- you like retro scifi and post-apocalyptic games- you like Strugazki novels and especially Roadside PicnicReasons you might want to skip this game:- you dislike dialog with no voiceover- you like sophisticated stealth, crafting and combat systems (they are all fine but noting exciting)- you expect a masterpiece like Divinity or similar games.All in all I hat quite some fun with this game and I'm pretty sure I will go for another playthrough sometime in the future. The gameplay and story are above average and its filled with reverences (especaially to roadside picnic) that make you smile everytime you find one.

_childDocuments_.review: As of July 15th.This game is great, especially since you can play a super powerful psychic idiot. The reason I don't recommend, however is one glaring flaw in the combat. To hit chances are just horrifyingly bad. Not XCom miss at 99 levels, but being at melee range you have an 89% chance to hit with a gun and a 67% chance to hit with any melee weapon. At any range that isn't point blank you're lucky to have anything above 29% chance to hit. There are no cover mechanics and quite frankly with these two problems, it makes the game almost a chore to get through. I know it's in early access so I hope they fix these issues, otherwise it's just not worth it.As of November 14th.A lot of the issues I had with this game are improved but not exactly fixed. The difficulty settings definitely allow for a better experience if you're looking to tone down some of the difficulty. Although, I've found myself save scumming a lot in combat still. I'd like to see them add improving your attributes to the game now as I've noticed there's no real way to and when you gain perks could be explained a bit better. Otherwise, it's a pretty alright game now. But still not as great as it can be yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Encased: A Sci-Fi Post-Apocalyptic RPG

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim because it was on sale and I can't say I was disappointed. First of all it very reminiscent of the classic fallout games with a action point based combat system. I was a little disappointed to see that while they have their own action/skill system that makes it unique from the original Fallouts it does little else to improve on combat and fells primitive compared to other grid based strategy shooting games, like X-Com. -The Really Good PartsAll that aside I want to now get to why I stuck around with this game till the end, its the story. It while burrowing from other sci-fi ideas does its own unique spin on it builds one of the most intriguing worlds I've seen in years. The characters and factions all feel unique enough to have their own identities and goals that I felt compelled to learn more. The crafting system is simple enough to be understood easily but compelling enough to want to keep doing. I often would go around the world hunting for and shopping for rare crafting material to upgrade my guns. The fact they change appearance at certain levels as you upgrade them is a nice touch.  Also as quick aside when you upgrade the AK its gets a underbarrel grenade launcher but you can't use it, why must you taunt me with a decorative noob tuber. The combat while sometimes feeling really unbalanced and simplistic was still fun. Each weapon type has its own unique set of moves tied to it so gives a different gameplay strategys for each weapon. While I didn't try it I could see the game giving me tons of options for a pacifist run so there is that if you want to play that game.-The Really Bad PartsNow I feel I have to talk about why I wanted to write this review in the first place and its going to sound like I hate this game but I don't. I just see how much potential it and this company has and that is why its all the more frustrating with what I have to talk about next. First the quests direction, journals,  tutorials and general explanation of some even basic details is absolutely atrocious. This is pervasive throughout the entire game I often spent long times just wandering around looking for quest NPC locations and items. There are no quest markers and NPCs rarely if ever are marked on the map so I hope you can memorize where everyone you need to talk to is. Often NPC will tell you to go to a place but give no indication of where that place is and speak as if you already know where it is. Near the end of the game every quest was like this every little thing became an exercise in madness as you look for something. I'll give you an example in on quest you have to fix a water supply. The NPC literally tells you to just go “fiddle” with the valves till it works, 20 minutes later of doing that it just says I did it with no indication of me having done anything, pure madness. Maybe that was a bug so one more example. A quest tells you go get a receipt from a terminal the npc during the quest just points to the door that is all the direction you are given. Which terminal? Does it have a different name or color? What room is it in? Why can't you just give it me now instead of me having to do it? The answer to these questions is none of these things its not on the terminal its a piece of paper sitting next to it that looks completely identical to all the other random pieces of paper in the room. So not only was not given specific information I needed I was also given misinformation or at least a confused answer. Now I want to talk about some of the dialogue in this game with a particular focus on your companions and just how shallow and devoid of content  this part of the game is, I'll give you another example. In a lot of RPGs you can ask the NPC giving a quest for more details about a quest like location history, people involved or what your doing stuff like that. In this game there is none of that you walk to the NPC they give you like a 2 second intro you either take the quest or you walk away and that's its in most cases. Its frustrating because I want to learn more about the world but the game just doesn't have anything for me. Now the companions while I like them but you have basically no interaction with them. Which is even more baffling because you can gain rep with your followers and each chapter it unlocks ONE additional dialogue tree and the first 2 are just asking your companions what they think about the factions or people in them. Why have the reputation system with your followers if you use it I kid you not all of 3 times in the entire game per character. I know there are some things you can get special actions during events if your high enough but I saw this only once and the choice to go with it was so unappealing as to be seen as downright the cruel option to go with (Left it vague so it wouldn't be to spoilerish). You know how in like Mass Effect you would have over the course of the game have a few interactions to get to know your crew better, yeah this game has ONE of those kinds of conversation per character per the entire game and it last less then 2 minutes. Your companions entire character development is a 2 minute conversation and a handful of random things they spout out when your walking by certain people or places. I know I'm a real stand up guy for constantly comparing this to games with far more money behind it. Overall I do like this game even with its glaring flaws. I really don't think they can fix most of their issues in this game but hey who knows. If this does well enough, and I hope does, to get a sequel they can some more money and address some of these issues and be able to put some more time into polishing it. If you have some free time and are looking for a sci-fi fallout inspired story I highly recommended it. If you don't have a lot of free time and can only pick from a handful of RPGs to spend your time with, then I wouldn't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a Fallout 1 or 2 fan or a fan of CRPGs then this is really a no brainer. The devs are very active on their Discord and it is clear this was a work of passion. Despite toxic elements here on the forums demanding the game be released and smearing their name they stayed the course and delivered a great game which is what matters when you get down to the brass tacts right?Pop on their Discord and you will see a passionate team engaging everyone and I mean from their Team Lead down, I hope they reap their well deserved rewards via big sales and that we can see more from them.

_childDocuments_.review: I am 15 hours in, and for now the game is mostly watching the world map and waiting for your character to get somewhere, so that you can perform ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chores for people to convince them to graciously give you what they are obliged to give you, so that you can save their lives. And those travels take ages, and you have to stop in a camp to rest every minute or so. If you don't, your character will pass out, and good luck waiting for him to get up. After several minutes I decided to load.Also, game offered me a pre-build character Isaac Crowley, a loner engineer who just wants to be left alone, then does not give me the option to show everyone the middle finger and tell them to leave me alone. Also, every single problem with the game is solved with a gun (which I don't do), or being a criminal (which I am not), or convincing people with your charm (of which I have none). Literally nothing my character can is useful anywhere.I wanted to love it, but I am really, really disappointed.Maybe I will give it another go after several months, and I'll pick a trigger happy gun-slinging psychopath, that character will probably have something to do

_childDocuments_.review: After almost 50 hours in this game I can't help but write a review for it. It was certainly a unique experience, the kind of which are rarely seen in modern games. Starting from the pros:- many elements insipired by old isometric rpgs are modernised, adjusted and refined to better suit modern gaming- elegant and coherent graphical style, above what could be expected from a small, unexperienced indie studio- huge variety of playstyles, boosted by even bigger amount of weapon and armour types, damage types, grenades and other contraptions, skills and abilities - interesting and often thought-provoking side quests, encounters and locations- various and unique companions with their own agendas, preferences and skills- dynamic combat, enemies in many variants and varied enviroments provide a very interesting and modern combat experience- the plot is interesting and heavily inspired by Strugatsky's "Roadside pikcnick" and STALKER games, which is a strong side on its ownAnd now to the cons:- those inspirations drawn from "Picknick" and STALKER are a bit too visible and predictable, when you know thier plot you can basically predict the plot of the game- the soundtrack and ambience is lackluster, the game feels devoid of life and very silent - comapnions are... weird? They feel a bit strange and quirky, often even edgy, a bit teen-like- some locations are shallow, uninteresting- the plot is centered around being other people's courier and workhorses and not about your personal feats- the game is often very indirect about what actions can have what consequences, especially in case of companionsAaand that's basically it - overall a great game, solid 8/10 but not without some flaws, but nevertheless not important or big enough to impact the overall positive impression of the game. A strong recommendation for someone looking for a more classical aproach to RPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some very quirky mechanics. Such as fully randomized loot.Searching a plant pot? You might find  dirt, nothing or an artifact worth hundreds of coins.This is also newly generated on reloading a save pre-searching. So I felt incredibly insentivised to reload to get better loot, because the variance is ridiculous. The random loot seems mostly a coverup for horrendous loot tables and little to no handplaced loot. This RPG also feels the need to stat out everything. Wanna know how much hp that table has? Now you know. It doesn't matter of course, because it can't actually take damage but hey, it has an hp value.Getting into spoilers(for the first idk 3% of the game) and what  made me quit: The first mission sees you going to a base recently gone dark. You find out most people went insane from some evil whatever. Ok, so I try to avoid killing the insane people right? Because maybe we can like break the spell or evacuate them, which seems to help. So I use the tazer, seemingly made for this exact reason.  But no the tazer stuns for exactly one round and does nothing else. Arguably one of the most pointless weapons in the game.In general the controls are okay if a bit weird, the HUD is bad, but tolerable. The location design was good on the places I got to, with very pretty enviroments, though thoroughly gameified layouts, which is ehh but makes sense. An overall 6/10 experience, where it not for  the inclusion of the absolutuely baffling loot system.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so this game was made by ex-Larian devs and that can be seen. The quests, writing, characters, narrative are really well done, on the par with AAA tittles. I got no complains about that factor, the game just draws you in, it knows how to build up atmosphere and knows how to tell a story.But it does have big downside, the gameplay.I am gonna start with the inventory management, that was a pet peeve for me. In the game you can have up to 3 team members, 4 is special occasions. So, the frustration beginnings when you try to compare equipped items with the ones in inventory, for some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason the position of the items keep randomizing every time you switch characters…Then you got the shops, good luck trying to compare items for companions, because the shop NPCs keep saying they want to talk to the MC and you cannot change characters while shopping, you have to open up the dialogue with a member and hit the Barter button on the NPCs portrait instead of normal dialogue choices.Yeah so much fun…Another point is the pathfinding of the AI of the team members, they sometimes run right into the enemies, or even more annoying and common, they trigger mines by running on them. Keep an eye on them when you getting close to enemies or hazards.That gets into the combat factor. It aint that good. It’s a tactics based combat style, but not to the degree of something like X-Com, your characters cannot take cover properly, you can waste action points to do that, but going behind a wall will not count as cover.It does offer plenty of different guns each with its own abilities (depending on the weapon’s group), so I do like that. However, companions will have their specific weapons which cannot be changed, you could upgrade them, but if you reach far in the game,  those become redundant, especially due to the fact that I could not get enough mats to fully upgrade them. Let’s get to the stealth system, I dunno what is up with that, without even investing much points into it, I could sneak up and stare the enemies right in the eyes without them reacting for a couple of seconds. Is OP, that is clear, but there aint many talents to optimize a stealth build, so at best I used it to get in the middle of enemies and spam grenades, heck sometimes they do not even react to that.Regarding the reputation system, without much spoils, at the end you are aided by the faction/s which you helped the most before, well I build up almost max rep with some factions, however at the end they were very hostile, ofc I did not do all the chores they asked me too but still managed to build up rep. close to max even. It should have been made to properly reduce the rep when I do critical choices, but instead the rep hit you get is too insignificant, and can be easily recovered, but you still end up getting utterly hated… but because of this rep system you will have no idea until the end.It falls after Act 1. By this I mean that Act 1 is the best thing about the game, it is very strong with enough side quests, character growth, the most interesting locations, and builds up the main story in the best way. Afterwards its just falls, the main quest is just the same as Act 1 with extra steps, the others just feel like an expansion to Act 1, more of the map does get uncovered but that is all, it is not very interesting.Overall, this game does beautiful work with the narrative but and ugly job with the gameplay. I grabbed it for a few bucks and for 60+ hours it sure as hell worth it. Really wished Steam would have a neutral button, I would place this game as a 6.5/10, nice writing but it is being dragged down by mediocre gameplay and other bad design choices.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This is a definite recommend for anyone that loves apocalyptic settings and RPGs. Encased is a well written and immersive game that deserves a place up there with the great classic Isometric RPGs of old. It does have a few things that I felt it could have done better, but it did not hamper my overall enjoyment of the game and for the near 44 hours it took to complete a single playthrough, it was definitely worth buying! I'd even go so far as to call it a great entry-point for someone looking to play an Isometric RPG for the first time.    Encased is the first venture by indie company Dark Crystal Games and is an isometric styled RPG in the same vein as Fallout 1 and 2, and  Arcanum: Of Steamworks and Magick Obscura. This game is an absolute hidden gem. While it does have its small share of flaws, I found it to be very well put together and on a quality bar equal to (and greater than, depending on the companies in question) many AAA games.Encased offers a variety of ways to earn experience for leveling up: you earn it from combat, completing quests, exploring maps, crafting, and opening loot containers/corpses with items inside of them. I found this to be one of the game's greatest strengths as it encourages the player to play how they want without punishing them for their preferred play style. Speaking of combat, combat is turn based and done through the use of Action Points which determines what specific and how many actions you can take within a round (as with most old school RPGs). The number of Action Points granted to each character is awarded based on their build/stats. I played on easy and didn't find the combat difficult (which was a problem I used to run into on some of the older RPGs).  I'm of the opinion that the character creator did a concise and excellent job explaining stats and how things were calculated, something that often struggles to keep my attention. However, if one is unsure of how builds work or doesn't feel like cobbling one together, there are a wide range of premade characters (I think it was around 20?) with interesting backstories to choose from.     On the note of backstories, you get to choose from a small list of factions - “Wings”- to be a part of at the start of the game which will open up some potential dialogue choices for you on down the line. That said, you are free to pursue your own interests and don't have to act in your factions interests at all. The factions are both one of the strongest and one of the most disappointing aspects of Encased. The factions all have really great aesthetics, motives, and writing – they just feel right in the world – but I wish more was done with them. Granted, they are involved in the overall story, but it would have been neat if they'd had their own quests instead of just those that intersected with the main story and if you could have joined them. Not being able to join some of the factions is a huge missed opportunity, especially considering that all factions have a reputation bar that you can build up. This leads me to my biggest gripe about the game; toward the end of the game you meet with each faction (assuming you didn't choose to wipe them out, you can do that to any of your choosing) and their representatives are gathered to ask you to do a certain thing for their specific factions. However, some of them won't actually ask you/tell you their plan unless you have specific stats. The faction I was trying to help had a requirement of 8 Charisma (among one other high one that I forgot) for them to tell me their plan which would have led to unlocking a new potential ending for me. This decision baffles me, because the only time you can set your Charisma is during character creation, and it makes the reputation bar kind of pointless? I had a few of the factions do this, actually. This is something that I strongly feel should have been tied to the reputation bar. That having been said, I thought the writing was great, and that both the main quests and side quests were engaging and varied. One of the side quests involved going to a family dinner, that was fun. I think that's one of the things that made Encased so endearing to me, that it wasn't always about combat or going somewhere to kill/collect things, but that you got to sit down, talk to people, and have some brief normal moments in a not so normal world.The companions are great fun. All of them were unique, felt like a part of the world, and had some interesting things to say about themselves. That said, I wish they had more dialogue options and passive dialogue, it felt like I went through all they had to say rather quickly. And yet... I wanted to have all of them in my party, but could only have two at a time so I ended up spending the entire game with the first two I met – so overall I'm of the belief that the companions were done well since I had a hard time choosing who to take with me.As far as I know, companions aren't romanceable (the two I had certainly weren't). There aren't really romances, but there are rare opportunities for brief encounters here and there with certain NPCs.There's also a crafting system. It was straightforward enough. I liked being able to make my own ammo, grenades, med-kits, and drugs.  My second and last gripe about the game has to do with the maps. I've seen a lot of people say that they felt the maps are empty, but I don't feel that's the case. I'm in the camp that believes the maps are too big. There's a lot of resources on each map and if the maps had been condensed a bit, then that feeling of emptiness wouldn't be there. It's a minor annoyance but since the combat is turn based and the maps are tiled, it costs AP to close the gap between allies and enemies so you might have enemies aggro'd on your playable character and your companions might be a ways off, so then you have to waste a round or two because you are using your AP to get in attack range; that would have been less of an annoyance if the maps were shorter. While the maps have a few different biomes (desert/swamp), I would have liked to have seen a couple more: snow, forest (of all dead trees), ash, salt, any of those would have been a welcome addition.  Now that I think about it, this could probably count as its own complaint, but the companion AI pathing is a mess, so every once in a while your companions will try to take the most complicated route to get somewhere on the map (when out of combat) when the maps being smaller could have circumvented this. There is a lot of content. I did every quest and fully explored every map I came across, while dreading that the game was almost over, and it took me nearly 44 hours to complete it. I've no doubt that the game could be finished in half, maybe even a fourth the time if one were so inclined to do so, which makes the prospect of going back through it again appealing for me. In closing: Yes, Encased does have a few things I feel it could have done better, but I found it a very memorable and enjoyable experience. I realize I went into a lot of detail with my complaints, but that's because I really love Encased, and I hope that Dark Crystal Games sees my review and takes my feedback into consideration because I'm looking forward to seeing them improve and what they might put out next!

_childDocuments_.review: READ FIRST, NOT A FULL ENDORSEMENTEncased is an RPG where you run alone or with up to two companions. You find yourself under a massive dome that is threatened by a Psi-Storm and have to save the day. The story and overall design reminds of RPGs like Fallout, with elements (artifacts, anomalies, bolts used to determine where the anomalies are) of S.T.A.L.K.E.R. / the novel "Wayside Picknick".  There are no character classes in Encased, but different wings of the Cronus Corporation, of which you have to choose one. Each wing provides you with a different set of advantages and disadvantages, factually creating an alternative form of character classes. The problem with that is that if you actually create your own character, some of the most valuable perks later in the game may be completely out of range for the rest of the game. Which is the reason I started over completely. So check the perks list beforehand and adjust your character accordingly. Yeah, I know that is not it is supposed to work, but this is how the game works here.   Encased is a prime example why I prefer to play without companions. Companion behaviour most of the time is really ruining the fun - companions run back and forth b/c someone/something is obstructing their path, alering enemies, setting of mines/anomalies, ruining stealth approaches, standing in the way of the main character. You cannot modify you companions´ skills, just equip them - although they too seem to level up. Stealth and detection are also a huge problem. B/c companion behaviour was so bad, I parked my two morons somewhere else on the map and went alone exploring and pillaging. Nobody had seen me, but my reappropriation of stuff alerted some NPCs. Suddenly one of my companions was arrested for something I did half a map away. Quest tracking is also a very frustrating problem, as you have to pierce together from the description in the quest log what to do next. That would not be so much of a problem, if the description was complete, which it isn´t at times. For example: You find quest item in soandso´s office. It does not state where the office is. And in Encased you have very, very large maps and places with multiple levels of large maps. And you have a fog of war type of mechanism that prevents you to check the extra large map wheter your questgiver is here or not. So... happy searching your ass off... Inventory is another mess. Like in Diablo you have a box that appears in some of the maps and allows you to stash stuff. So far, so good. You cannot just look into your box with your companion and pick equipment. You have to transfer stuff from the box into inventory, then you can choose equipment for your companion. Very clumsy and time consuming. Another issue in the category is that you cannot properly organize your stuff. Any DIY organization is deleted once you close the box again. Also, too many item classes are in the same category - especially clothing and artifacts. Having more categories would really help.   Weapons - Encased has a lot of them - with different damage types to battle different enemies. Using the wrong type on an enemy may not only inflict no damage (not a little bit, we´re talking absolute 0) or even heal the target. All weapons have a malfuction rate of 1% or so - which is quite misleading, as pistols and rifles malfuction all the time. Very, very frustrating.  Weapon upgrades are costly in materials, so you have to pick a set and stick to it. Testing the various weapons at higher level is not really an option. What really pissed me off, however, is that I upgraded an assault rifle to lvl 10, was delighted to see that an underbarrel grenade launcher appeared on the model (and in the description) and then found out there was no way to fire said grenade launcher. Great. As you can see, Encased has a number of really frustrating problems. Which is why I give it a 6/10 - barely recommendable (get on special sale) Please note: If this was not in Early Access and produced by a AAA Studio etc., this game would absolutely not be recommendable. Encased is, apart from the problems mentioned, a solid RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate isometric games. There is no situation in which an isometric game is better than a first or even third person game. If you need an overview for a battle, scroll out and upward. But for exploration, first is best and third is ok.So, I almost never play isometric games. I played disco elysium because it was disco elysium and therefore entertaining in its own way. I played Encased because graphically, contemporaneously, and somewhat tonally it resembled disco elysium, so I thought I'd check it out. And also because of the Roadside Picnic/STALKER theme connection.Exploration was tedious because it always is in isometric games, and also there was no compass so it was harder to figure out which way to go. Combat was tedious but still somewhat entertaining in some hard to define, isometric turn-based sort of way. Companions were annoying and weak and it was too easy to accidentally click them in combat and shoot them. You had to steal to get all the best items, which is ok with me in a game but there's no way to RP a good guy without crippling yourself even further. The story was meandering, the quests were interconnected in unnecessarily confusing ways and I had to consult guides many times for things that should have been clear.Ultimately, Encased was different enough from other games that I put 100 hours into it, so despite most aspects being problematic, it's a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat in this game is acceptable, though most other things are severely lacking.- misspellings EVERYWHERE. In the game dialogue, in the flavor text of things, on descriptions of things - it's like they didn't consider having someone proof-read stuff!- the quest log is utterly useless. You can pin quests, but you can't pin anything of actual value like a different aspect of the quest, so you're just meant to constantly scroll up and down through your quest log looking for that one part of a quest you were on.- the puzzles in this game are horribly designed, and represent the largest issue the game has next to the basically-nonexistent story. I finally decided I was done while trying to unhitch a vehicle that you can find in Act 2. The puzzle itself was so incredibly convoluted that even using online guides, and following specific instructions, it wouldn't work and made absolutely no sense. - the skills and perks in this game and their corresponding numbers don't seem to match up AT ALL. I kept looking for what skills would increase my base stats and it doesn't seem to tell you *anywhere*. - the weapon jamming is a fine feature by itself, but if you're going to tell me I have a 2% chance of the weapon jamming, only for it to jam AT LEAST once in EVERY. SINGLE. ENCOUNTER then at least give me the courtesy of making the percentage accurate, because I'm pretty sure that Sparrow's jam chances are somewhere in the area of 10-15 percent. I could probably think of more if I spent additional time trying, but I've already invested more time in this game than I should have.I really am disappointed; I absolutely adore RPGs such as these and I was hoping this one would scratch that itch.

_childDocuments_.review: Encased is a CRPG that definitely shows its inspiration from the classic Fallout games, Roadside Picnic, and other Sci-Fi fiction of the like. If you are a person who prioritizes story and writing over core gameplay like myself, this games main story can decently deliver but unfortunately struggles to hold its story together much later in the game. With very vaguely written objectives, strange oversights in how major characters react to certain actions, and the majority of quests for characters diluted into a simple premise of fetch questing.The World Building and the many side characters within the dome, however, are phenomenal. Absolutely beautiful world made by such a small team deserves a lot of praise. Many side characters such as Fox, Cheerful Jack, Kingsley, Aaron Melville Etc. bring this world to life. There is so much attention to detail in the small parts of this game which kept drawing me back to it. I would actually recommend this game simply for the small bits here and there along that make up the world, it made the main story that felt unfortunately rushed worth it in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: I completed the game twice and enjoyed it. If you are looking for something like Fallout 1&2 or Wasteland, this game is for you. However, it is far from perfect. What I liked: * Story. The story is rich and entertaining. Characters are diverse and well written with a lot of details. * Abilities and combat system. There are a lot of skills, the skill tree is not linear, interesting perks. * Sound. The voice acting is stunning. It's really on AAA level.* Music. Some themes are great, some are just ok. But overall I liked it. * References to sci-fi books, movies and games. * The fact that you can complete most or all quests in several different ways.What I did not like:* Setting. It seems there is no single theme in the setting. It's just a bit too much. You can encounter mystical things, mutants, zombies, robots, cyborgs, computers, VR reality, etc. It's just does not feel like a complete piece and feels overwhelming at times. That's probably just a matter of personal preferences though.* Atmosphere. In my opinion what brings good and distinctive atmosphere to a game is details. In Encased a lot of thing that could have made the great atmosphere are not there. E.g. architecture. The game is set in late 197x but the architecture of most buildings does not look like 1970. Same applies to computers. It's too many of them for 1970. There are people from different countries, but that does not affect the story in any way. Etc. * Skills balance. Some skills are just too versatile in different game situations. E.g. you can complete literally all the main quests just by maxing on criminal. You can easily avoid battles by sneaking, you can sneak in, unlock, and steal quest items, you can pickpocket all the items and money you may want, etc. * Food and water. It just feels annoying and doesn't really help the immersion.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is full of buts.- This is a great Fallout clone... but it lacks the integrity. The game is a collection of different ideas not really playing well together.- The premise is rich... but not exactly strong. A lot of plot lines die off quickly, most of the main story quests end up in a dull way.- Dozens of skills and methods of combat... but there's not enough challenge, as well as motivation to explore them. Once you figure out your style of combat you can easily carry it throughout the whole game. You can pick 2-3 types of damage and weapons and it will be enough to win almost every battle. - Hundreds of inventory items... but many of them are useless. Especially contraptions. Inventory management is quite subpar too.- Character progression is lateral... but level up system is rudimentary. Closer to 3/4 of the game you will max out all of the most useful attributes.- Writing and dialogues are mostly fun and engaging... but there's a lot of empty talk eating time unnecessarily. Not all the NPC need to be talking, especially given their huge numbers.- Graphics and UI is rather beautiful, with great lighting, dynamic shadows and well designed locations... but some parts can look makeshift (such as - weapon shooting effects, skill effects, character design, etc.)- Level design is smart, with not too large or too small areas... but exploration can be overwhelming with so many 'containers' and interactive elements to deal with. Almost constant object highlighting is the only way to cut through the locations.- Music is amazing and voice overs are great... but audio editing can be disappointing, especially combat sounds.Overall, I enjoyed the game. If you like to munchkin - this is a great opportunity to do so in a very relaxed pace, nowhere to hurry. Sometimes the game does reward you with cool finds, and the random encounters are rather interesting or funny. In fact, the game is funny - a lot of satire every now and then.My biggest fun was actually discovering new places and upgrading unique weapons (but as I wrote above - this is not really needed). That's why I spent nearly 70 hrs.The biggest disappointment is that the whole this was kinda in vain. There's not much of a challenge after the mid-game, and I only continued because I got used to this comfortable chore.For the next part (if it comes) I'd recommend to seriously revise combat system and challenge, and make the whole world more engaging.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm hoping to swap this to the much coveted thumbs up very soon.short answer: a good basic game with great potential that shows its shallowness as the game progresses. Could be amazing but needs a lot of work to flesh it out.Long answer: It was very hard to rate encased as it seems like the basic are in place for a very good game but its just not near complete enough to be enjoyable. I appreciate that its a WIP but unless you want to contribute and provide feedback I don't think its worth buying yet. To their credit the developers provided a very handy feedback icon that is always available on screen so its super easy to flag issues as you find them. The whole thing reminds me of being a play tester in the 90s/00s which I guess has a certain unintended nostalgic charm to it.The engine does work well and the character creation/wing idea is great with a lot of breadth. Right away I was able to create a character that was so weak he could not use a basic weapon yet he could run away from danger better than anyone. I even enjoyed the very first challenge of trying to figure out all the different ways of escaping the elevator. It felt like there were multiple ways to accomplish goals but unfortunately it ran a bit more linear as the game progressed. The starting area felt alive and well designed but once the game progressed to other areas they felt like quite barren sections of map that were made for an particular purpose or set piece. It just didn't have that same organic open feel that fallout 1/2 had. I was hoping (perhaps unfairly) that encased could capture this open feel but it just didn't translate.I like the idea of the story and it makes for quite a unique and interesting world but it just still feels empty and a bit flat with the current dialogue and options available to the payer. This is something I'm hoping will improve as the game develops.I encountered 2 separate bugs where I could not leave a previously visited areas after the prologue section was complete. It seemed like the areas were left in by mistake but on my second play through it was fixed but the maps still had missing items that were not appearing. These basic issues keep popping up and combined with the set piece feeling of each map area it just kept reminding me that I was playing a game. It feels like a basic board game the way you move between these areas with specific tasks to accomplish. Some of the story was also a bit hard to follow. In the prologue section you are stuck in certain areas with a very clear objective you need to do accomplish but unclear instruction on how to do it. Unclear instruction is fine when its open world like the old fallout games but when you are stuck in a set piece map it gets quite frustrating. I really do hope to change this to a thumbs up because I can really see the potential. If the developers can work on bringing these map spaces alive a bit more it will really make for a better game. The closes thing to a well fleshed out map was the starting base and even at that I had covered every point within about a hour or so. Add more content to these already well built places and you could have something magic. At the risk of raising a controversial opinion I would rather a rich scaled back story than a bigger emptier game.
