_childDocuments_.review: Received as a gift thru Humble so I don't feel too bad slamming the game.Half baked Unity project that is clearly unfinished. For instance, what I take to be native Unity terminology persists in the game (click 'TRANSITION: Door to next level'; when your character is knocked out, 'PROPONENT UNAVAILABLE: asleep or knocked out' or words to that effect). This indicates a lack of polish that unfortunately, permeates the basic mechanics of the game rendering it unplayable in my view.The plot, dialogue & NPC interactions are generally interesting and good. I persisted through to some post-Junkyard quests for this reason. I like the setting, I like the attitude, I like the branching possibilities. I want to like the game & I want to see it through, but I can't and won't.Props for including very easy portrait customisation.The game mechanics are woefully unbalanced. Having focused the early game on a) stealing, pawning, and accumulating credits while b) focusing skill points and c) upgrading the appropriate gear, I'm now in a situation where I can enter a cockroach fight with two companions, 13 medkits and a range of decent weaponry and, due to continually missed point blank punches / shotgun blasts, erm, die having barely dented enemy HP. Yes I have tried flamethrowering to equally little effect. Ordinarily I might accept this is a git gud issue, but COME ON. The game gives you NOTHING, for round after round. It's just not plausible for the setting.If you are lucky enough to connect your blows & down some foes, what you will loot from them is exactly what you'll get from any 'Pile of Documents' or 'Cardboard Box', i.e. a handful of trash items. You will NOT get their weapons or armour. This is so profoundly UNLIKE Fallout, where half the joy is hunting NPCs knowing you're about to play dress-ups. Again, an indicator that random generation, once established, does not appear to have been checked for any kind of balance or sense of reward.Another issue is that your survival stats (eg Fatigue, which accumulates very quickly) are buried in the inventory, which means you have to constantly flick between screens just to monitor your condition. This might be a minor issue if survival wasn't so weird. Picked a lock and cleared a room of enemies? Congrats, you are now critically fatigued. Your character (sorry, PROPONENT) collapses to the ground and recovers 2 fatigue (of something like 1500) PER GAME HOUR, during which... you can't do anything. Can't sleep, can't wait, can't skip. The game just sits and runs while U wait.I'm willing to be mocked for not realising how you're meant to deal with this... but that's not my fault. If there is a solution, I'll be damned if I can find it.FOV is pretty yuck, camera controls are janky AF & your movement tiles all too easily disappear under scenery overhangs that are meant to dissolve, but basically don't unless you've dragged the cam to just the right angle.It's a Unity project.To charge $40 (aussie) for what is clearly a work in progress would be pretty steep for EA, but this is presented as finished. It isn't. I'd say ATOM is better, but for your money you could as easily pick up Exp:ROME, which is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ excellent.tldr: plot is interesting, game sucks, read a book instead

_childDocuments_.review: After waiting for more than a year, I gave in today and bought the game.  It is a brutal reminder of how badly the newer Fallout games missed the mark and didn't live up to the originals.  The new Fallout games are good, but they are huge departures, and Encased exists as a tremendous modern spiritual successor.I thought it was a little funny that they had a $5 DLC that included shoes, as it reminded me of Wasteland 2's Red Boots DLC parody.  I bought it anyway, not because it's a good value, but because I wanted to support the development of this excellent game.The dialogue is especially well done for an RPG, with responses being in *second person* rather than direct quotes.  This lends a lot of creative agency to the player, and I liked it a lot.  There are lots of skill and background checks that either limit or open up your choices in dialogue, and there appear to be a lot of ways to get through challenging puzzles.Combat escalates quickly.  If you're going through a combat build character, you are going to get your ass kicked in early game until you can develop better gear.  The difficulty curve is steep, especially with stealth options seemingly non-functional for the most part.  I hope this is addressed in further patches.According to the dev road map, there are two more major releases before the game is content complete.  Hopefully those big patches are released soon, because the game being in an unfinished state limits its depth.  The developers respond in steam discussions regularly, so I'm hopeful we'll see things progress by the end of the year.Overall, great game, I'm really impressed, even with things being in an unfinished state.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is 3 weeks after release. At it's current state, this game is not worth the price of admission. I am 92 hours into the game and I keep wishing that certain features were added to this game. It desperately needs a cover system. The way defense is handled in this game is not very tactical or fun. I was expecting XCOM style combat but without a cover system  the game suffers. There is very little tactics involved overall and sneaking is the way to defeat any enemy in this game easily. There is a weapon upgrade system that plays well for a while... until you realize all you need to do is level up and buy from a local vendor to get a leveled up version of whatever weapon you are using. Looting isn't fun, infact it's a hassle. You will spend way too much time looting new locations and not enough time doing fun things like combat and crafting. Armor isn't diverse so your character looks like any other NPC. I would rate this game a 3 out of 10. Wait to see if the game evolves into something good or buy at a 60-70% discount.

_childDocuments_.review: A cautious recommendation. Was especially surprised at the variety of ending slides after checking all endings on youtube.Honorable mention of having an option to play a complete idiot character, that changes all the dialogues and interactions. I don't know how well its done for the entire game, as I only tried for the early game for fun.I didn't encounter game breaking bugs or crashes. There were couple logic bugs, some quests thinking you both had & hadn't done something at the same time, but just pick the dialogue option of what you actually did. You can end up skipping a lot of quests by hacking, lockpicking, looting and stealing everything, which might also cause the logic issues I had.The companions bugged out and stopped gaining any more skills, making them weaker.The fatigue system is annoying and does nothing to improve the game. Constantly having to drink coffee, use stimulants or sleep, after picking a few locks, hacking etc. Hunger and thirst system felt pointless as well, easily get more than enough drinks and foods, especially with the broken criminal skill. Just busy work, inventory clutter and carry weight.Voice acting and visuals are fine. Not a lot of music or much variety in it.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid TRPG! Dark Crystal Games nailed it... Encased is quite fun for all its short comings... they all make sense by the end of the game...Positives:- 6 Unique companions from the vigilant who only sees the world in black and white, to the kawaii Sniper...- All unique NPC are Voice attack, the narrator has great Voiceover- Replay-ability through 5 starting Backgrounds and 14 endings 12 of which are locked behind actual choices the player makes in act 2... (there are a lot of major and minor choices that have an effect on the ending dialogue)- NO Fetch quest or filler missions- Great TRPG gun and ability balance (no multi-layered ability bars unless you choose a melee build)- Even Medium is challenging but fair- Each Companion is similar but by end game they each are unique in the way they complement the main character- Companions can be perma killed before being recruited- Work arounds to skip past MAJOR Story quests to finish ACT 2 faster- All in one experience, no Expansion... for the price you get everything... for $30 or less looking at 30+hours of entertainmentNegitives:- Limited Party Size... the story states parties are usually 5 or more as expeditions under the dome... but you are left with choosing 2 companions... (this can be edited with mods, but it makes the game very clunky in places)- Limited companion customization (outside of armor and secondary weapon)- Unclear quest markers... well no quest markers... - A min- max build makes Companions basically useless after lvl 15 minus an extra target in combat...- Companions can Perma die before being recruited- Companion relationships are there but shallow at best... no real interaction or words except at the occasional junction- No New Game plus or long term end game, could use with 14 possible endings- Ending combat section is a massive increase in difficulty and ends rather anti-climatic - All major characters and Factions are introduced at the end of Prologue- No censor settings that I could find...(at least 4 instances of Adult content)In conclusion, Encased is a worthwhile investment for any TRPG fan, Offers multiple endings, satisfying Companions and moral choices, a challenging difficulty curve even on medium if your not familiar with mechanics, It ends rather abruptly...3.5-4/5 Is my Rating.

_childDocuments_.review: This is Fallout/Wasteland game with interesting original lore. Only 3 hours in, but if you like Wasteland and Fallout, you'll like this too.--Edit-- Having played game throughI still recommend this to FO/Wasteland fans because the world is interesting and different than many others. But after playthrough, some issues came about.First, the game is much more finalized and packed with content on the first third of the game. In later game, big areas are really empty and vast maps have only few meaningful NPCs and a trader or two. It seems that at first there was ambition and time and perhaps money, but later on the game they just did what was necessary for the walkthrough.The game has few really annoying fetch quests that make no sense, they just seem to drag things out unnecessarily. In many places you feel like there was idea to do more based on some lore bit or context, but they just didn't have time or money to create the vision.To put it simply, contentwise it feels like 1/3 of the game is retail ready, 1/3 is beta or alpha and 1/3 is early access barebones.There is fatigue system in game that makes you get fatigued doing certain things, i think it's OK system, it's just needs balancing. Some things create way too much fatigue compared to others. Like picking 10 locks means that you are ready for 12h sleep or so.All in all, it's OK game for 20 euros and while i wouldn't recommend it to anyone playing first game like this, friends of the genre who don't mind it still has early access feeling are going to be just fine with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Even with at 15 hours in I still feel like this is going to be more of a "first impressions" review...there's just that much going on with this game. With CRPGs like this I always try to play myself as closely as possible in terms of both character build and moral choices. Since I'm kinda weird, that first playthrough usually gives me a good idea of how much the game lets you really enjoy playing your own character; oftentimes I find myself forced to pick from a small number of min/maxed builds unless I feel like suffering a bit - oh sorry, unless I feel like being "challenged".So far Encased has yet to let me down when it comes to being able to find some goofy trick that lets me get out of a pickle; when it comes to these kinds of RPGs that's the critical metric - am I allowed to find my own creative solutions to problems, or am I going to have to google the "right" answer? So far I've only been frustrated enough to turn to The Google one time, and I was REALLY inebriated there so I'm not sure it counts.I do have a couple gripes of course, but they're all minor - things like more keybinds to minimize hunting for icons with the mouse or more clarity about where a particular object is when holding ALT to display its name - and it seems like the devs are very open to player feedback and hopefully if I just keep being annoying they'll fix those things :) For the most part the UI is pretty intuitive and the quest texts provide just enough hints about what I'm supposed to be doing that I've never felt lost or like I'm missing something that everyone else thinks is obvious.Dunno what else to say really; my bar for recommending a game in this genre is "will I feel the urge to play it again with some kind of weird character build just to see if I can get through it?" So far, the answer here is yes; if you see this review and it turns out I've only played this game for 30-50 hours then either I've been too busy to dedicate enough time to it or something changed my mind and made me say "ehhh I'll just finish the first playthrough and be done with it." If I'm past that much playtime then it probably means I've beaten the game at least once and everything I've said already still holds true.

_childDocuments_.review: A short description of this game will make you think it's derivative. And in a way it is. It's clearly an attempt to do a Fallout game. Just like every other indie RPG, yeah. The thing is, this one does it in a different way.I've seen a lot of Fallout-inspired games. More often than not they try to copy aesthetics of the game and concepts like post-apocalyptic sci-fi setting. They often even have a similar character progression system - no classes, basic attributes, traits, skills, perks. The thing is, devs in those games probably played not the Fallout I know, or they liked the least interesting parts of the original Fallout. That game was interesting because of a combination of systemic approach with storytelling not based on fights. Fallout 2 and especially New Vegas less so. But the core interesting part of Fallout was combat being not the main pillar of the game, but just one of the tools at your disposal. Many RPGs have non-violent solutions to the quests, great reactivity, interesting ways to differentiate between player characters outside of combat. But when you play Dragon Age, Pillars of Eternity, Divinity Original Sin, Witcher, and other deep varied RPGs you always play a character who fights, period. Maybe you can get through some of those games without killing anyone but this would be a gimmick challenge run.Don't think that I want all RPGs to be Disco Elysium, it's not about that. It's about interacting with the world itself being a gameplay system. To many of those great games is extremely simplistic outside of combat. If you're in dialog chose a [skill] option, it will probably skip a fight. If you're making a choice it's usually about some moral issue or asking for a bigger reward you don't usually need. Fallout is famous for giving you a way to "talk down" the villain of the game, and too many games just copied this specific feature instead of seeing it as a statement of game philosophy. Encased embraces the idea that you can play the way you want. Sure, the easiest way to get through the game would be to specialize in one of the weapon types and several "peaceful" skills. It's probably hard to navigate through the game without fighting at all. However being peaceful would not just save you from several bossfights by clicking persuasion. You don't really have to fight much at all. Very few sidequests directly require to dispose of somebody. You can certainly fix most problems with violence, but it's almost always not the most obvious choice. It's not like you can apply some skill to "skip" gameplay, looking for ways to solve problems using your specific character build *is* gameplay.That's really all you have to know about this game. It's junky, but not too much. The writing is fine, sometimes good. Character progression is great. One thing I'd want to warn you about is that it doesn't have boring default obvious builds. As in every type of weapon or support skill has some synergy with others. Even if you try to be a dumb fighter with a rifle you'll have to use special rifle attacks that depend on some other skills and apply some interesting effects. So the game is quite involved and replayable.So, the most interesting RPG mechanics since Fallout & Arcanum. Surprised this game doesn't get much more attention.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, let me get this clear. Encased is NOT a bad game. But it has not yet fulfill what it takes to be a good game. I give the bad review so the developer will notice what I have to say. If not to make this game better, then probably for the next game.-- Good --1. The UI is good. It addresses some small quality of life issues such as right clicking to interact and double clicking to move item in inventories (I played some games that don't). 2. I like the sneaking system, it's not too realistic, but it is appropriate for this kind of game though I love the sneaking system in DOS 2 a lot more (you can do some team works to do sneaking tricks).3. The fatigue system in combat. Man, this one is so good. It gives an enormous strategy possibilities to take down strong enemies while it threatens to your characters as well. Being high level in this game does not mean a battle with low level enemies will be a walk in the park.--Complains--1. THE MAP. Man, this is frustrating. You cannot move your camera to a specific point in the map. You have to move it after closing the map. You also cannot command the chars to move into specific point in the map. Some of the areas are huge, so some fixes will be desirable.2. The loot. You don't get a weapon\armor loot after killing weaponized enemies. Even after goes into a long battles, you don't get a lot of things to sell. 40 hours of playing and pickpocket is still my go to money collecting.3. The selling system. Well, let's say you meet a battle that needs specific skill from specific weapon. Since the items in the store are mostly randomized, it is quite difficult to create some specific builds. Especially in early gameplay. 4. Companion level up. The companions level up by themselves. Making you wonder why the system spend the skill points on some unused skills. Creating some customized party strategy is limited because of this aspect. Moreover, you can only add 2 companions without any summons.5. The companion itself. Besides the unavailability of companion skill customization, you also cannot change their main weapon, forcing you to often spend AP just to change companion secondary weapon. The companion itself is  so passive and lifeless. Only a little bit joined conversation and no small talks (if there is any, I did not notice it) outside of the one that they says when you ask them to join the adventure. There are also not much story involving the companions.6. The enemy skills. In this game, low level enemies get the access to the highest level skill. First, this makes the battle feels so unfair. Second, this makes fighting the higher level enemies feels like fighting the same enemies with longer health bar and higher damage output. Creating unbalances in a game is important at some points but this one, it breaks the balance.7. The story and side quests. Well, this should be the strongest point of CRPGs. Bad gameplay can be fixed with mods. Bad stories? It needs a whole new game to be perfectly fixed. Most of the quests involved a lot of travelling without some interesting things to discover and just so you know, the travelling in this game does take a lot of time, real time.I think there are still some more complains that I have not yet found. But no worries, I always try to send in game feedbacks as much as possible. I know the devs give their best to this game and put a lot love into it. These feedbacks are my way to give my utmost respect to them. Hopefully, this game (or the next one) will become a really great game both for the developers and the players.

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing first half.What a terrible slog of a second half.I have never played a product that screamed "We are out of time" as much as this one. I would even wager that this is even more half baked than Knights of the Old Republic two. The worst part is that the edges of this, that is to say the parts that got focus before release. The writing that was examined by an editor, the locations actually filled with content, the weapon and skill trees that got attention are all compelling. Yet that's only half of the experience with the other half feeling as if it was thrown through google translator, empty maps that waste time simply traversing it, random events that run out before repeating the same 3 events over and over, weapons and skills that clearly should have been cut or massively expanded upon and just...it's frustrating.It's frustrating because this world is very interesting. It's frustrating because at times this feels like the isometric crpg fallout sequel we never got. It's frustrating because there's so much potential in this system to craft interesting builds. It's frustrating because for every interesting thing you do you have to waste hours getting to it through a slog. 80 hours of playtime I can safely say that only about 30 hours of it felt finished. In the end Encased feels as barren and lifeless as the apocalyptic wastelands this game draws from.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll update this later, but want to say, at 37 hours, this is one of my favorite games of all time. Great writing and dialog, numerous paths to quest resolution, extreme attention to detail, a near overwhelming number of quests/side-quests, a truly unique and interesting story, piles of RPG stats/perks/skills/gear, huge exploration opportunities with a variety or terrain and settings, crafting. Great stuff!Update after finishing: Excellent game. I was worried the quality would wane towards the end. While there were fewer voiced characters and sparser narration as well as a more grammatical errors than earlier, the quality of the game remained astounding until the end. I was reluctant to be done so reloaded the ending scene 6 times, finding very different outcomes to the game based on my final action. While I don't intend to replay the game, even those 6 endings don't appear to be the only ones. There are insinuations in each ending that refer to various choices I made during the game. Also with regard to the endings, I think it is/was necessary to explore the various endings to get a "real" view of how things *really* end. Individually, they offer a more realistic ending, offering information that your character would or could know. Exploring multiple endings offered a third-person/narrator view of how the story ended. That is one I am more satisfied in having. I was a bit disappointed after the first ending.The two things I would have asked to be improved in this game, which are minor in view of all the fantastic things, are;1) More tactical options in combat (e.g. the usual cover and overwatch that have become synonymous with XCom combat) would have been welcome.2) Quick travel *out* of location. Quick travel *into* locations is an option. Once a location has been visited numerous times, the trip out to the larger map becomes tedious.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very clearly inspired by classic Fallout (1 and 2), Wasteland 2, and perhaps a little of the Outer Worlds - with a hint of STALKER of all things. This is of course a good thing. What is not good is that all of those games have a very enticing start - but this one doesn't.It's hard to make legitimate criticism here; I just was constantly bored. Looking for the plot. NPCs were annoying rather than charming. There was some background dialogue, but that also wasn't very enticing. The worldbuilding is at least somewhat interesting, but I wouldn't call it great - maybe it gets better later.When I was told to go on a mission to an interesting place and I ended up at some run-down redneck roadside cafe with drugged hippies, I lost my patience. It failed to grab me, and now I can't even make a proper critique; it's the uninteresting kind of bad. Two good things in spite of all that: the UI is nice and clean, if a little unwieldy. And The skill point system is nice, it grants you additional skills/perks every 30 points. A very nice evolution.As a closing statement, a bit of statistics. 73% of players leave the tutorial area, but only 7% beat the game. Source: Achievements. Have a lovely day, internet stranger!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game so far. It has a great story, so despite not doing much other than talking to people, walking around and gathering supplies for the first few hours it's been very immersive. Once I left the main area and headed out into the world it just got better. Everything has just made sense up to this point. I haven't struggled to figure out where to go or what to do for very long. Some other games like this I've bailed after a while (ATOM, Stellar Tactics) because I can't figure out what to do next and I'm stuck in a loop and walkthroughs just ruin the game for me, even more so than being stuck.The voice acting is superb and there's a lot of it and for me personally that really helps because I don't like reading a bunch of text while playing games. There's still some reading, but there's also enough voice acting to break the monotony and it's so well done that it adds so much to the game and really draws you in.I wasn't really expecting so much voice dialogue going in and it's really a pleasant surprise after watching this game develop over a long time and reading reviews. After a few months I took this out of my wishlist thinking it just wasn't going to have much content or wasn't going to fun to play due to some reviews, but I'm glad I saw it on some isometric game lists tonight and checked out it's progress again.Encased is the most enjoyable game I've played since Project Zomboid and Wasteland (2,3) when it comes to getting immersed into the game-world, but the story in Encased has been better IMHO than Wasteland up to this point (about 5 hours in). Wasteland was just nuts (but funny), but Encased has a cool sci-fi storyline and pace that's more my style.I highly recommend Encased if you're into this genre!

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game after around 70 very entertaining hours.With the current patch status I encountered no bugs or anything impacting my enjoyment of the game.This really is a worthy successor of Fallout 1&2. The look and feel of the graphics and interface have a strong resemblance.The RPG system behind it is solid - but not perfect.The combat is fun and tactical - but if you play it in easy there is no big challenge - if you prefer following the story (like I did).Some minor aspects that would have improved the experience from my point of view:- the quest log is sometimes not clear. In a few cases it's hard to understand what you need to do next to finish a quest.- there are some quests where you need to find people in a larger area, but the map doesn't help you here, you really have to search every possible corner and click on every NPC before you find the one you need.- the movement speed is a bit to slow, it's pretty annoying to run for a minute or more over the map just to get to the next exit.- the fast travel option exists only when you enter a big location with several sub-areas, but not when you want to leave it.So you have to run through long corridors just to get from one area to the next.- the strange artifacts you find all have a positive and a negative modifier. For me the negative modifiers were a bit to tough, so many of the cool artifacts seemed useless to me.- the perks you can gain every few levels are a bit blank and underwhelming. Helping you only in very selective circumstances. Why aren't there more generic perks that just have a nice little impact. Like needs to consume less food and water, has one additional relic slot, direct improvements for your attributes... - why is there no place all the companions are gathering at if they are not in the party? It's hard to find them again once you tried out another companion?But all together this is a great game with a satisfying story, cool sub-quests and good mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Encased (2021) represents a turn-based role-playing game (RPG), developed by the company Dark Crystal Games and published by the company Prime Matter.++ Explore the mysterious wasteland within the Dome with up to two charismatic companions that will comment on your every action. Or, do a pacifist run with ≤ 2 intelligence and relish how every character reacts to you in a unique way, while the universe bends to your will in order to protect your spotless mind. One scientist even gave me bonbons for each finished experiment, she was very nice to me. + Solid character progression with badass endgame abilities. Fascinating locations encourage exploration, curiosity is rewarded, and the perception attribute defines the chance to discover secrets. Good balance between loot found and items purchased. Tactics difficulty satisfies the needs of hardcore players.o The story has its high and lows, but I disagree with the advertised emphasis on storybuilding, where the player’s decisions affect the rest of the gameplay. Instead, your influence and fate of the various factions are summarized in form a slide show during the epilogue. Somehow, I miss the classic showdown.- Inventory management can be frustrating due to incorrect stacking of items and lack of automatic alignment features.Despite being the first game of the developer Dark Crystal they have surprised me with their level of quality, especially in regards to a playthrough with a low intelligence character. I consider it a hidden gem.Recommended for connoisseurs of a low INT run.Estimated time for 100% completion: +50 hoursSingleplayer achievements: 47Multiplayer achievements: none

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty great game if you enjoy the gameplay of Fallout 2/Divinity: Original Sin/ATOM RPG/etc. It has a setting strongly inspired by Soviet sci-fi (chiefly including the primary inspiration for STALKER), so in a sense I could describe this game as "Fallout 2 meets STALKER". It has a pretty large freedom of choice - you can completely exterminate any faction you dislike or even all of them, no NPC's have Bethesda-style protected flags, so the game doesn't stop you from making itself unwinnable if you choose to do so by killing a key NPC. It also has 14 different major endings, not counting things like "you died in an unusual way".The main gripes I have with the game are that psionic gear is very rare and very annoying to get as a psionic build unless you cheat and that non-lethal combat is just much worse and less enjoyable than lethal combat. But they don't detract from the game enough to ruin it.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on release, but I never played it, It took me a little bit of time to get into it, decided a couple of weeks ago to just sit down and play it out whether I liked it or not. This time around, almost immediately I got into it, the interface/engine (unity) is common, it reminded me so much the point/click style play like Baldur's Gate back in the day, it's just set in a different time/scenario etc. The quirkiness of the character reminded me instantly of the RPG golden days where humour was always thrown into the game, it was so refreshing to have this thrown in. The story line is great, its not one of those typical save the world or rescue the damsel in distress scenarios, the options and paths you can take seem endless, you can test a scenario and reload a save if you change your mind on the outcome, there's 14 different endings apparently, I only got 3 and they weren't that great but I decided to finish it as I just wanted this game off my list, but to be honest.. I have an itch to play it again and go for the other endings.There is plenty and plenty of content, the side quests are great and there is allot of them, factions are welcoming and so good to work on, (apparently it helps with the ending if you try and get in everyone's good books).Encased is enjoyable, you can sit down and play hours on end and not realise the time go by, you can build your character anyway you want, but for me, been a avid RPG fan, I've always loved the hack/slash builds with tons of HP and strength to just get up in the action and tough it out but no matter which way you choose to play it, this game is enjoyable and it just keeps giving.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: A modern, polished and well-thought out spiritual successor of the original Fallout series. The beginning is rather slow and some mechanics seem confusing at first but put in an hour or two and you will experience an exceptional rpg.Long version:CONS: - Wonky movement animation, the characters move like mechanical dolls rather than humans.- Confusing quest log and quest descriptions (hint: there is a personal craft menu, press J to bring it up.    You're welcome.)PROS:- The list would be just too long. Everything else in this game is great or amazing even. The story and the setting (the Strugatski brothers would have liked to play this game imho), the quest design, the leveling and the combat, the companions and so on. One last thing: I have encountered 0 bugs, 0 freezes and 0 glitches. This is what a full release is supposed to look like. Exceptional job by the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved Fallout 1 and 2 you'll probably love this game, too. It's isometric but modern and you can rotate your viewpoint so you can actually see everything quite well. It has a stat and skill system similar to the Fallout one yet different enough to feel new. I definitely recommend to invest some time into reading up on all the skills and stats and maybe look up a build or two online so as not to mess up your first play-through. As with Fallout, some perks are OP and others are meh and the best combos are not immediately apparent. The story is quite nice, set in alternate 70's, again borrowing from Fallout. The universe is full with esoteric concepts, alien tech and old tech and all sorts of strange things to keep you entertained. Where I feel underwhelmed is the weapons. I feel they could have done a better job with diversifying them and upgrading them and also with their skills. But they do the job quite nicely so far so I can't really complain. Overall I would give it a 4 out of 5. Not great but good entertainment value for your money. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very immersive SCI FI RPG. For me it was the first CRPG ive played in a few years since Divinity Original Sin 2. Largely I wanted something short and contained to around 50 hours to prep for something a little more meaty in the CRPG world and this game fit that bill. I played out 4 endings and over all thought the games first 2 acts were very strong. The third act could have just been roped into act 2 since its largely one last small battle before reaching the conclusion and seeing you ending. The Pros:Very good story telling with nice choice and consequence elementsEngaging combat due to weapon varietyDecent size tech tree for the size of the game on offer. Good level design in each zone. Cons:The third act leaves a lot to be desiredThe psi abilities could have been a little more fleshed outThe companions are pretty much 1 quest and thats it as far as their story.Overall 6.5/10 Glad I played it for sure but would recommend waiting for another sale to pick it up if you miss the winter sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The almost 18 hours that I played were very rough. Combat is very unpolished, many dialogue trees are nowhere near complete, calling the story weak is a bit like referring to the ocean as "damp", and the overall feel of the game is substandard. Yes, it's an early access title but it's one that hasn't had any substantial updates in quite some time now. There have been vague promises of a release date that have been pushed back for over a year, and the updates that have been seen in the last year are for very minor cosmetic changes and cheevos. It may end up being a great game but, as far as EA titles go, it is looking like a dicey thing to invest in. Best at this point to not take any chances and wait for a full release. A heavily delayed game, with minimal developer communication, and no roadmap is a poor place to park your hard earned cash.

_childDocuments_.review: [Updates after completing the game] I have to say, after going through it all the game feels ... thin. Or maybe incomplete. It's still a yes, but maybe a 5 or 6 out of 10. The main story line is good, even though I don't agree with the message behind it. But the side quests largely feel tacked on after Act 1 and offer minimal rewards. Same for companions: other than another gun, they bring nothing to the story or world enrichment, and the perks of being a loner arguably outweigh the benefits of bringing them along. Honestly, if you are looking for a game like this and haven't played them already, look to the ATOM games. They are much more complete and still actively supported.Strange but interesting Isometric RPG. Slow start with some interesting (and some awful) mechanics. AI pathfinding is abysmal to the point where your companions teeter on the edge of killing themselves much of the time. The inventory management is downright horrible, odd like getting even basic things like money to stack. The story is good so far though. Overall the game lacks polish and its a shame it will never be patched as the studio went under as a result of the war in Ukraine.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't bad. It is competent, looks decent enough, and shows the developer cared. This being said, the layout, gameplay, and campaign failed miserably to pull me in. For the layout, specifically with character-building and progression, uses a unique and off-label mapping. The traditional Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, etc. modifiers are switched up in a manner I don't believe was necessary. A new IP isn't defined by the uniquity of stat names and feats. It isn't something I feel is necessary and encroaches on the flow of the game more than it should.The gameplay is fine, but not terribly inspired. There is little-to-no impact behind combat maneuvers and actions that one can feel through play. The dialogue and story are not affected by this criticism.As far as the campaign failing to pull me in, this is a unique case where my dislike of the flow and hook of the campaign elements doesn't lead me to conclude this game is a bad one. Just because I did not like this specific title, I would not say it was a bad one. While I would personally give this game a thumbs down, I wouldn't say it is a bad investment. They priced it exactly where they should have it as a solid "maybe."

_childDocuments_.review: Game seems to be good and promising as an RPG with numerous interesting mechanics and in active development.The only reason I can't recommend it is it's sluggishness. The game is slow. Slow as a turtle riding a snail. Slow to the point you may start hating it despite all the good features it has.And when I say slow I don't mean progression - I mean animations and combat. Every animation is lazy and takes it's time to complete. Every combat move has some weird pauses (small but irritating) and in result a simple melee fight against 3-4 rats can take like 5 minutes. Maybe 10 if you are not lucky.Right now there's no way to increase the speed of the game either by ingame means or by outside stuff like speedhack.Developers have been requested to add some animation speed options but they merrily ignore it. I don't know if it's a dev limitation or simply a way to artificially increase gameplay hours but right now it gives you more irritation than fun.Game would be good for you if you are super-patient but otherwise be ready to test out your patience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the closest game "feel" to Fallout 2 I've played since Wasteland 2, which is commendable, but the actual gameplay (quest solving, combat, map exploration) just feels like a slog with no payoff. The world is interesting on paper but stale & lifeless past the tutorial area. Combat has plenty of abilities that look or sound cool, but ultimately are inferior to just shooting an enemy 90% of the time. Itemization looks promising but turns out to be a bunch of inventory management for impercievable gains. Player interaction via stat checks are everywhere, which is great, except often there's like 7 solutions for every obstacle so you don't ever feel challenged or punished for building your character or team a certain way.Things I genuinely enjoyed: the voice acting, the concept of the Dome, and the ideas behind all the ways combat could happen. Encased feels like it'd be a much stronger game if they had cut some of the features and focused on others vs just having it be a collection of ho-hum mechanics and ideas. If you really like tactical RPGs and this is on sale, maybe, but there are so many other games to try before this one.

_childDocuments_.review: “A very decent clone of Fallout.” That’s at the same time the biggest compliment, as well as the strongest criticism for . It is a labour of love that is almost as fun as the one it passionately pays homage to, and is thus easy to forgive its lack of fine-tuning. Unfortunately, it also lacks what made Interplay’s gem the legend it is, which is, of course, the writing. You see, the key word in the phrase “a very decent clone of Fallout,” is the word ‘decent.’ This otherwise entertaining piece of software is definitely that, but decent just won’t do for most people.

_childDocuments_.review: Well... Where to start. This scratches an itch I didn't even know existed for me. A classic CRPG with a modern twist, heavy influences from Fallout 1,2 and what I feel is a tiny bit of dead space. I'll premise this by saying I got this game on release and prior to it releasing I had never heard anything about it. In like a week and a half I've put in 55 hours. During that time I cannot put this game down. The game feels full and alive. I haven't even looked at the developer - Or anything else about it. I highly recommend this for anyone who just wants to get embraced by something you might have not seen before - I've yet to complete the game but I will say I like how it doesn't hold your hand. Quests are just written word and sometimes you just have to find a hidden passage behind a wood pallet into a crumbled sewer to reach a higher parking lot to drop a beacon. All without being seen or you get run over by Dead, Brain fried humans who want to eat you. I found a ... war truck? in the desert and it literally took me 45 minutes to figure out how to get it dis-lodged from a sandpit. It feels like a throw back to when games were games and you had to figure something out, without quest markers and auto questing like, run here get this, return, quest down. Now I will say about half way through the game if I didn't find that vehicle I'd be pulling my hair out travelling up and down the dome but they do make mention of grabbing a vehicle from a certain faction after what I assume is half way through the story. I might have just lucked out and found the guy who warned me about the truck. Can't wait to finish the game! Start it over with a new wing! I started white-wing and the medic abilities are paying off hands down! The only thing I could say is I wish your companions would put some of their skill points into anything other than weapons. I find the main character has to do much of everything else where companions are basically made for fighting. Reminds me of fallout 1, where companions weren't really companions more like hired mercs.I'd recommend this to anyone who loves a traditional CRPG and wants to sit down and get enveloped in a new Universe. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a little bit of a tough game to review, if Steam had a "meh" option then this would be pretty accurate. Genuinely, the game starts out with a very interesting premise, but unfortunately by the end of the prologue, they don't do much with it. To have a sci-fi RPG with competing factions within a massive multicorp attempt to seize power, that is interesting. To then get rid of most of it and replace it with the most generic post-apocalypse, it is a waste of a good idea. Still, I wanted to give the game a good shot, and I will admit that I had fun with it some of the time. I think the nuance of their leveling system was entertaining and I was having the most fun when I was leveling up.However, the game has a lot of issues. It isn't very good with explaining itself, it lets you figure out a lot on your own or look it up, which is fine as long as the mechanics make sense which I don't believe they do most of the time. The combat is meaty and with very little ways to heal yourself reliably, it bogs down the entire experience. Additionally, the writing is dated for even coming from 2021, if I have to hear, "It came from the outside, like some kind of...outsider" one more time, I will lose my mind. Additionally, like most TRPGs, all of the good content is in the first or second act (in this case, only the first act as 75% of the second act is literally slowly going from one map to the next to do simple fetch quests), and by the third act it is the most barebones experience you can imagine. By the end, I didn't really care about any of the factions and the ending slides are almost all, "well, you made your choice, and things still ended badly eventually" which is just simply disappointing.Credit where credit is due, they made a solid game. All of the foundations are there and that is why I am going to still recommend this game, but ONLY ON A STEEP STEEP DISCOUNT. I got it for like $2 and I can say with certainty that I got my moneys worth. However, do not purchase this game for $30, it is genuinely not worth that. The game could've been better and as the studio has shut down and there will be no more updates or future content, you're paying for an okay game that you wished took a different turn during production. I hope the people who made the game go on to learn from it and make even better stuff in the future, there is a lot of potential here, but that is what it stays at, potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent experience that takes may queues from the early Fallout 2D games.  Rich story, crazy encounters, and plentiful voice acting.  Stealth is a bit obnoxious, but combat, and exploring is where this game shines. They can't alert anyone if they're dead, right? I did kinda feel the game cut short and the ending was a bit "meh," but the ending result slideshow was certainly fun. I would seriously love to help kickstart another 2D game by these folks. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game because of its similarity to Wasteland 2 and ATOM. There are two significant problems: the story and combat.With the story, I just couldn't get hooked into it. And it's not without a slew of dialogue and information that the game throws at you, but here's the thing with good writing: less is more, particularly in dialogue. The backstory can unfold, so there's no need to throw it all out there immediately. Way, way too much information too soon. Additionally, the linear nature of the story made it less interesting to me, too. It really didn't seem like I could deviate from the main storyline because of the possibility of death. If this is Earth in the 1970s, it has been mapped out already, so there shouldn't be this much confusion about which direction cities are in.The combat is problematic, too. I tried multiple different builds -- I think all of them -- and just couldn't find one that wouldn't make it either too easy or too difficult. And the way combat progresses, I'm left ignoring the probable hit numbers because they don't seem to relate to reality and cover and action points don't seem logical. In fact, cover seems completely useless. I think the main issue with combat is the UI is just so awkward. Why is my character's portrait scrolling by on the top of the screen with the enemies? Why is it just not updated once in one place?And I guess there are things that just seem broken still. I just don't get stealth or how that works at all. It took me half an hour to figure out how to take off the servoshell -- why is this just not on the main toolbar? There's also a lot that's still in Russian language that doesn't seem vital, but it does make it un-immersive to an English reader like me. I was also not thrilled with character creation and customization, but if I go down that road, I'm just nit-picking and nobody wants to read anymore of this.This game just left me disappointed and I'm uninstalling it now. Sigh.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's setting and concept looks good so far, a sci-fi with mysterious elements. It has a decent combat system, various ways to interact with the world like repairing stuff, lockpicking, (probably) driving vehicles, so various ways to deal with certain situations and to solve quests. Has crafting and reputation systems, which may potentially affect gameplay alot. Game looks like it was inspired by Fallout 2, Wasteland 2, Stalker and other games. It's not outright "western post-apocalypse" or "soviet" one, as we see in ATOM or Fallout series, but a sci-fi, which is not seen often, but it still manages to fuel player's desire to explore the world, and gives you a feel of adventure even in this limited EA build.As for the game's downsides - it's not clear about stat's purposes - It could use some bug hunting, but most of the bugs that I've encountered can be easily fixed, so those are not to be concerned about. Active abilities don't bring much depth into the combat, as seen in the EA the game misses items like traps, grenades and such, player is not well informed about crafting and other systems right away, so it short - it needs some tooltips. And it's kind annoying how player character starts to slowly move tile-by-tile when you need to interact with any object.Overall, I'd give this game 8 blue duct tapes out of 10 and a happy banana sticker on top.

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with this game can be summed up with one word: "Meh". Everything about it is just meh.Conversations with most NPC's involve slogging through walls of text about stuff you shouldn't be expected to care about, and I just found myself skipping through a lot of it.The conversations with voice-overs are even worse than the text only ones, since they all sound like people reading off of scripts (which, duh, but it doesn't feel like any real effort has been put into them). The narrator especially is really annoying, since he sounds completely disinterested in what he's saying, and talks in a really meandering, drawn-out cadence.Meh.The crafting system is completely unsatisfying, as it just involves using preexisting recipes to cobble the random junk you find lying around into consumables. And everything you craft  a consumable, including all tools and gadgets, so any benefit you get from managing to craft something from all the crap you've been lugging around is only ever fleeting.You can also use specific items to increase the tier of one of your weapons. What does that do? Marginally increase its damage. .Scopes? Silencers? Extended magazines? Anything like that? Nope. Brand new weapons or pieces of armor? Ha; you wish.Meh.Combat isn't fun at all, as it's an absolute bare-bones turn-based combat system with zero tactical depth. There's no cover system, flanking system, maneuvering, terrain exploitation, overwatch; nothing. You and the enemy just take turns plinking at each other.Also, due to the abovementioned lack of tactical flexibility, there's pretty much jack-all you can do to gain an advantage in combat, and since you start out on your own, with a max of two additional companions, you'll find yourself outnumbered in almost every encounter, and the action economy is gonna be kicking your ass. God help you if the enemy decides to focus one of your guys down (since there's nothing you can do about it, with everyone just standing out in the open like morons), because then you're really boned.Basically, most encounters end up feeling like a complete crapshoot.Meh.The most disappointing part is probably the progression system. I don't recall ever being so underwhelmed by leveling up. Most of the skills and perks you get are really situational and not impactful, and unless I've missed something, the only stat that increases between levels is HP.The only real impact to a character's performance comes from weapons and gear, with levels and skills barely contributing, so the only real difference between a level 1 character and a level 10 character is that the latter can take more hits.MEH.If you want to play a TRPG that's actually fun and has some depth, get Wasteland 2, since it's better than this game in pretty much every way.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "maybe" option, because by absolutely no stretch of the imagination do I think this is a BAD game. The fanboys are going to tear me to shreds in the comments, I'm sure, but... Everything about this game is just . The combat, the story, the quests... It's all kind of just slapped together - after the first section, that is, which is mind-blowingly good and very, very obviously what they worked on for the EA content. I'm really not a fan of what they did to separate the EA and v1.0 content, and I think that's a major, glaring problem with a lot of the story that comes afterwards.The maps are huge... And enormously empty. The NPCs are vast and varied... With nothing really much to say. The skill system is dense... And you'll be using 2 of them at any given time. The combat is serviceable... But so slow with such horrible payoffs that you'll want to avoid it constantly. The story is bog-standard, with very, very obvious homages being paid to other games/genres and very little payoff - routinely you'll talk to someone you think is very cool or important, only to never speak with them again. Props to the devs for allowing for players to have such a freedom of choice and the like, but this is absolutely a case as "wide as an ocean, deep as a puddle." Hopefully I'm wrong - hopefully the game sorts itself out after the Maelstrom content - but seeing as how (at writing this review) only 4.5% of people have even completed the first act, I don't think I'm being unfair in suggesting that the game has serious potential, but is often overwhelmed by it's mediocrity.

_childDocuments_.review: Did you like Fallout 1&2? You're going to like this.UPDATE: After having finished the game, I am sorry to say this game has, for me, quite unsatisfying story. My main problem with probably is that even though the whole story is only happening because of this mysterious dome and equally mysterious maelstrom inside it, this game seems to be completely uninterested in exploring these phenomena in any way. You could argue they drive the story forward, sure, but the story isn't about the dome or the maelstrom, it's not about their secrets or nature, the story is purely about how the people trapped inside the dome react to them. Don't get me wrong, you would expect to be an element of the story, perhaps even the main element, but not the ONLY element. At the end of the game, you know absolutely nothing more about the dome, the maelstrom or the forefathers than you do after prologue. Nothing. They are essentially deus ex machinas.I personally find this very frustrating. See, it's not like the game doesn't focus on them, it kind of does. It keeps showing you thing and telling you "Look at this! Look at how wierd all these anomalies are! Look at them! Aren't they mysterious? Do you want to know more about what they are or where they come from or what their purpose is? Tough luck. We'll just keep showing them to you like magic tricks, but we'll never ever actually reveal anything about them."It's like you're in Plato's cave, but all you get to see are the shadows. Not even hint of considering of maybe leaving the cave one distant day.On top of that, none of the endings really tell you or even hint at what the future consequences of that ending to the dome and it's inhabitants are (like Fallouts did). Maybe this was some kind of bug, but after each ending, the game just kind of unceremoniously plopped me back in front of Nashville and that was it. Most main NPCs didn't really have any interesting reaction to my final decision other than maybe Nakamura, who was mad at me no matter which of the options I've chosen.I'm still recommending this game for Fallout 1/2 fans, because this game absolutely is spiritual successor to them both mechanically and aesthetically (and it doesn't just emulate these aspects, but improve upon them). However, the story left me quite disappointed after finishing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: New Review:Game is functional, if still not quite ready imo due to design decisions and changing some things up at a stage that was too late to truly fix (it feels like a lot of planned functionality ended up cut). They are in a good spot to continue on with Encased 2, while refining the remaining issues. Storyline: Feels like more of a prolonged introduction to the world under the dome imo, than a complete comprehensive story.Wings: Don't really feel like a true rendition of each wing. One Example: Whites should honestly start at somewhere between -20 to -50 rep with oranges, simply due to the 'fluff' of having free reign to kill them with experiments. There would be at least one who took advantage of that to put oranges into line that didn't do anything he wanted. Computers: Feels incomplete, with way too many 'system down' messages even after hacking the hack-able ones with that message. Relics: I like the variety introduced, but it should still be remembered that for-1) Employees via 'fluff' are afraid of relics. We should have been shown why.2) Relics are effectively magic items. That means more than permanent grade magic items. It includes the Encased equivalents of potions/scrolls/oils/etc. of fantasy. (This is really what I focused on for the lack of relics available in concord)Old review below:The game is flatly not ready or even at the 50% complete stage and the developers still seem to be too focused on little things and not major things from my perspective. According to their progress chart we are on the second of the three major content patches before game release. Despite being on engine version 0.17 something, having several functions still completely disabled (like sneaking and driving), no ability to make guns despite having a literal gunsmithing skill, and a bunch of other things. Quite frankly, they need to tone back on the efforts to create the little 'unique' stuff, and buckle down on all this crap that they're missing from the complete game. Among other things, for Content Patch 3 they need to make all benches the same so that all crafting possibilities can be seen and discerned right away.Enemies, need a cutback on general power option for those who don't understand how to, or want to, power-game. That or remove the charisma requirement on companions so that those stat points can be redistributed into places that increase survivability for non-talkers.The horrendous loading times NEED to be fixed. It took me some four hours to get to nashville, at least a third of which were load times. That is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.And flat out stupid decisions like implementing weapon deterioration before implementing repair options, needs to be stopped.

_childDocuments_.review: So it's 343 hours spent on this game and i guess i am ready to write my review.If there exisited "Strong but medicore" score i would put it on this game. Encased is game between two contrasts - at first it seems like your classic Fallout adventure with strong elements of Roadside Picnic or STALKEr but in depth there bit...different picture. Story and Quests - Some quests sounds really cool! Some secondary quests have nice vibe and feel but in end they feel like unrewarding enough. I mean - my PC just passed some death-row labyrinth, witnessed horrors and rewarded with some medicore artifact. Feel bit unfair but well reward is reward and this is just one spoilerless example. Main story feel nice but yet not very branching and somehow cut on edges. Factions ain't feel so alive cause they have one or two side quests and no unique rewards. But still story feel good and somehow complete. Companions and Items-weapons-armors-relics-crafts -  Companions are very nice edge between "Weird" and "Unique" - there just few people who will follow you in Dome and barren-lands - They are typical archetype of "Ranger", "Melee" and "mage" but in some mixes and matches. They look cool, they feel unique yet somehow they are dull and lack of "personal quests" yet they feel like they SHOULD have some but been cut that idea on release. There lot of things that can Player use - from drinks, foods, stims to some cool gadgets and weapons but some of weapons and relics feel somehow useless or too repetive to use. I haven't find my "favorite" type of weapon or item in Encased yet i feel most of them have potential that haven't been released. Psionics feel very situational and mostly awesome but impractical at some moments (Like onehit kill but only when your opponent is tired enough), some guns and melee feel like "magikarp power" - they start to be useful after good dedication of upgrades and resources on them. Relics are bit dull - they sound like their artifact analogues from STALKER - giving some benfits with some negative effects , and some unique quest rewards give benefits only but...I didn't found anything cool and most of relics been sold or salvaged except some few for my psionic-melee build. Yet they  still feel like something - i wish there could be more relics, maybe some should be "weaponized" more, or give more abilities but well we have what we have now.World and Gameplay - World feel unique. There some nice feel between Gothic's 1 Prison dome and strong sense of "Roadside Picnic" in a world of "Atompunk" of Fallout 2 vibe. Shame that only few unqiue random-encouters and after 1/4 of game random encouters became very repetive and lose  their vibe between "Horror" and "Science wonder of exploration". Also as small cherry on top there craft system - it's nice. I reallt like it. but some objects feel very "uncrfaty" - for example you can craft pistol, rifle and machinegun bullets but shotgun shots are buy-only and can't be crafted from same polymetal ore. There few items that seem to be must be useful but ended up in my endless stash and never came out. But on 90% craft system is niceAtmosphere and Gameplay - Yes we came to moment WHAT saves it all and why i played 300+ hours in Encased :D. It's awesome and unique world and atmosphere build-up. I am finishing my 2nd playthrough and beside all dull and questionable moments i still like this game. Verdict? - It's a solid good rpg that have lot of potential in form of DLC OR...Sequel. Yes. Sequel with all reworks and mistakes fixing would be great. Cheers!

Everyone is just like, "oh it's you". The time travel moment lacks impact. And after this I have no motivation to progress the story. Really, I have no idea why I should do anything in this world. In fallout you are trying to find the chip, then you learn about the master and you want to stop him. Wasteland 2, you try to stop massive robot hordes from killing everyone. Here, your guy wants to find a dude, then you meet him and now you are just a guy wandering around in the wasteland doing errands for people. Cool.Also in the beginning you get to choose a profession, prisoner scientist, administrator etc. and while this seems like a rather pointless decision for stat boost this actually is a massive decision that will impact almost all interactions from here on out. You are your job, you are not a character in an of itself. Not good.You also have companions but again they all quite forgettable. Unique personalities means that one guy likes science, one guy likes punching everything etc. The turn based combat can be at times cool, but I played for almost 8 hours and I had combat encounters maybe 3 times? Other than that I was just running around trying to get XP by doing side quests, and I didnt get a lot done frankly. The UI is clean, moving around feels great, Interacting with the world feels nice and smooth. From a technical point of view the game is fantastic that much is for sure. But the main story is so nonexistent that I don't have any motivation to keep exploring or leveling myself up, I mean what for? The world itself just doesnt feel that interesting either, sure you have magic objects and mutants but everyone is just chilling around in these massive facilities and nobody cares about the world outside their own little bubbles. And you dont even get to impact anything either. In fallout 1 you have these locations you explore and meet people, then in the end you decide basically how the place ends up. Leave gizmo alive, kill gizmo you decide, and it will impact the location and endings. Here you just run around talk to people and do or dont do their side quests. You just end up feeling like an errand boy instead of an actual character.And while in the game description it says you get to make decisions that impact lives I have a hard time remembering a single one. One time two people tried to escape and I convinced them to be imprisoned instead. This wasn't a moral quandry more of a confusing little decision. Two people that live in a safe location with food and water want to "escape" into the barren wasteland so that they can be "free". It just does not make any sense. So I just convinced them to give up and get imprisoned. The choices are not interesting in the slightest, and once you make them nobody cares. Your reputation with a faction goes up by 10 points. Two morons that stood around in the hallway now stand around in jail. Ok? Who cares? Did I impact the world? Did I make a moral decision that had an impact on my character? Nah. Side quests are not interesting, no moral quandries, main questline is non-existent, companions are boring, no romance(oof), locations are just places for NPCs to stand around and dispense pointless missions, your decisions change nothing, your character is defined by the profession you pick at the start of the game and that is it. I just don't see the point to any of it.Maybe it gets better after 10, or 20hrs but it is simply not that interesting to make you want to play it to that point.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I would say that I liked playing Encased. And if you like CRPGs, it is worth playing. However the game is not without flaws, and my overall opinion actually leans more in the middle. I would mostly recommend it on sale, and assuming you have the patience to play it through, as it can be tedious. First lets go with the pros:- I enjoyed the setting and overall concept of the game quite a bit. Frankly I would like to lift a lot of the setting concepts for a TTRPG campaign of my own.- The game has some really strong rpg mechanics, with a fairly fun progression system, and a lot of autonomy given to the player in what kind of character you want to play as. If you really wanted to, you could be a murder psycho and kill anyone, including the leaders of the major factions, or entire settlements. Or you can be a smooth talker and convince everyone to be your friend (well, not everyone, but you get what I mean).- There is an impressive variety of game endings to take into account your decisions. Though most of them are rather depressing or somber, and are given to you in an end of game slide show, I still enjoyed the variety. For example, one of the settlements in the game lets you choose a mayor, possibly yourself, and just that quest has an impressive number of end game variations.Let's get into the mixed bag- Other reviews have complained about the very large number of containers with random loot drops in the game. Yes there are many flower pots to open, and each container can give you xp based on the loot inside. As a hoarder I enjoyed opening everything. But I understand how this can grow tiresome quickly.- Although the core of the main quest was interesting, much of it revolves around meeting the 6 main factions in the game. These factions will assign you tasks in exchange for supporting your efforts in the main story, but a lot of these quests boil down to fetch quests or quests to talk to npcs, npcs which you will likely have a hard time finding, because there are a lot of npcs and these quests don't always tell you where to find them. - The companions in the game (I only ran around with two of them) had some interesting character details, however, they are very underdeveloped, with only a few lines of dialog you unlock by raising their reputation high enough. Once you ask those lines of dialog, there is no reason to talk to them again. The reason to have them along is to carry things and help you in combat.- The combat system is a mixed bag. Although mechanically it seems to have a lot to it, in practice it is bland, and the game rarely forces you to change your tactics.Now for the cons- The quest log for the main missions are very cumbersome to read. Because rather than a clean concise checklist, the main story quests are actually a log of events, which means if you do them out of order, it can become difficult to remember what tasks you still need to do. This is a problem because the main quest for each act branches out for each main faction, but the logs of events are contained within one central quest. At one point I was about to quite because I forgot to pick up an item from a safe after completing a quest, because the faction quest had been completed, but I forgot to pick up my reward, but the mess of a quest log made it unusable to determine I missed it. - There is a reputation system in the game, with all the factions in the game, as well as your companions. However aside from a number, the reputation system really does not have that large of an effect on the game world. NPCs don't seem to have special dialog or deals if you are friendly with their factions, and aside from some variations at the end of the game for the main 6 factions, this system really doesn't serve any meaningful purpose. After royally pissing off a faction, such as by killing their leader, you are not attacked on site, and can still trade with their vendors.- The crafting system is kinda pointless. Although you will find lots of junk which you can use to craft all kinds of things, and you can find upgrade manuals to upgrade your weapons, it is often smarter to simply hope the RNG gods will grant you something better, rather than waste your limited resources on item upgrades. The upgrade manuals are especially a problem. The whole game I kept finding upgrade manuals for melee and high tech weapons, weapons I do not use in my party. But because companions have a locked unique weapon (out of two), if you want them to be effective with their unique item, you must hope you find enough manuals and resources to upgrade those unique weapons. It is important to have two weapons, as having a variety of damage types is important in combat, as some enemies have high resistances to certain damage types. - The game can be quite tedious. Although I didn't mind opening every chest, it can be annoying hoping for anything decent if you don't have high luck. However, traversal is the most tedious aspect. The major settlements are way larger than they need to be with things spread far apart, making completing quests in these larger settlements a slog, as you wait for your character to run across the map. For some reason you can "fast travel" into these settlements, but not inside of them. Making leaving these settlements also quite time consuming. The game tells you that you will eventually get a car, which requires a driving skill of at least 30. Being able to drive makes word traversal much less of a slough, so it is worth getting your driving skill there fairly early.

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to write a review after finishing the main campaign of the game, I played on tactical difficulty, but I would say choosing between the second and third difficulty would probably be my recommendation for people looking into playing the game.Politics, Conflicts and decision making, these are the core of Encased, you generally can't please everyone, I went for mostly a combat build using a servoshell that is somewhat similar to what power armor  was in Fallout 1 and 2, it has it's downsides of course and heavy guns, mostly machine guns and tactical rifles.I think despite the combat being a little slow at times and enemies feeling somewhat bullet spongey when they are scaled to your level in random encounters, you are generally able to deal with them as long as you have your companions with you, I will probably do another run and get a different set of companions so I can experience the game with a new perspective.There are comparisons that can be made between this game and fallout, I would say the game might suffer a little bit from having to run back and forth like fallout 2 in some quests, I believe some locations should allow you to exit to the world map when you are on the exit similar to how fallout 2 does it, that would reduce some of the tedious walking around when moving around big locations.Combat feels solid if a little slow at times, I feel when I was using psychic abilities or some other weapons there was a little bit of delay between attacks that could be reduced so the combat felt a little faster and snappy, I also think the enemy scaling should go down a bit in random encounters.Random encounters with enemies scale with your level which is fine until you can't keep up with gear upgrades, then the enemies might be too much for you to handle, I think the world map should be divided into sections and enemies should have different levels on random encounters depending on the sector you are in, if there are higher level enemies in certain locations in lower level sectors that is fine, those are meant to persuade you not to fight, although I suppose sneak does allow you avoid combat if you wish.Quests overall can be somewhat confusing when you first start, there are plenty of items in the game, from equipment, to gadgets, resources, food and quest items, I was a little stuck before in one of the quests because I didn't know how a certain item needed to be placed, I was not even aware that you had to use said item from the inventory or the belt bar, I think these things should be a bit more clear.You will feel overwhelmed when venturing out the first time, that was the fallout 1/2 experience for me, you are going to get killed if you don't know what you are doing.Overall, I think the game is solid, definitely worth it's asking price, devs have already fixed a number of issues and I only expect the game to become better over time.

_childDocuments_.review: cRPG's are among my favourite game genres, especially combined in a science fiction and/or post apocalyptic setting. It probably does not come as a surprise that I'm a huge fan of the original Fallout games as do the developers of Encased. Obviously it instantly peaked my interested to play Encased but a lot of the negative reviews held me back at first until now.Right from the get-go, it's obvious Encased could be a combination of Fallout 1/2, Wasteland 2 and Shadowrun. In terms of graphics and gameplay it would be closest to Wasteland 2. The feeling of the game next to the music would be more like Shadowrun. Basically this game should have everything to potentially be one of the best cRPG's in my opinion.At the start of the game I could not understand what people were complaining about; there's a lot of dialogue, voice acting, loot, a lot of eye for detail, pretty good story/writing. I was genuinly having a really good time. It was only after many hours I started to understand the negative reviews. Many of the good things in the beginning fade over time or become annoying.The voice acting pretty much stops after the prologue except for a few characters. A lot of the areas you visit are quite dull and there's not much to do or see which make the game feel rushed at some point.Some quests are interesting but often make you walk (or drive) a lot back and forth between locations, also often you are not sure what to do next.Looting in games like this is fun but it often seemed like that is all you were doing. It felt like every location has like hundreds of crates, boxes etc. to loot. Looting should be fun, not a chore. The survival aspect is also nice at first; you have to drink, eat and sleep but after many hours just gets annoying.Encased is just a very plain game; not good, not bad. The combat is fun but rarely epic. The areas mostly pretty dull. Long boring conversations with npc's but companions with almost no real story. Final mission was rushed. I could go on like this.Overall I did have fun with Encased and I would like to see more of this developer but I doubt I will replay this game.
