_childDocuments_.review: Encased is an interesting beast. It's one of those games that has a great foundation and a pretty solid first act, but then takes a sharp turn downwards... It goes so wrong so quick and it's sad because it could have been great. It starts out so strong too with:- An interesting skill system which lets you build into nearly anything you want and it feels really good. - Inspiration from quite a few sources (Roadside Picnic, Classic Fallout, etc) but with it's own spin on things and does it well. - Several interesting companions. - an interesting first act that shows a good chunk of the factions. - Some interesting locations with a fair bit of depth to it.- Great use of references and easter eggs. - Some great bits of voice acting (I adore Foxs VO)- A great use of narrator.- Servoshells that are a nice take on Power Armour.But where it starts off so well... Act 2 really lets it down apart from like 1 thing. The big bus tank you can get that you can cruise around the dome in. I kinda wish you got it earlier. My gripes with Act 2 is that takes all the good things that Act 1 builds on with story and characters and just... takes it back several steps and then drops off a cliff.- The main story falls apart, like it's unfinished.- Game devolves into just a majority of fetch quests, and not even interesting ones.  - Exploring feels like a chore, infact there is no reason to explore in Act 2.*- NPC Dialogue is so dull following into Act 2, almost rushed. - Very little challenge if you're just playing normally.- Quite an alarming amount of typos. - Factions you're introduced to in Act 2 feel really bland.*What I mean by this is, there is literally no reason to explore ANY of the locations outside of the main story, even for XP. You're so flushed with XP/levels so early on, it really puts you off from exploring. It's such a shame, If you do get this game however I'd highly recommend the first act and stop, or steel yourself for a boring slog. It's unlikely we'll have another Encased again, which is a shame as the idea is brilliant. But if there is, I hope it's cooked more than this was. Edit: Aside from fixing some typos, I wanted to touch on a feature that was a stretch goal for their kickstarter, that wasn't reached sadly but kinda gutted the Tech tree a little. Upon reaching 135,000 in their goals... they would have added in "Drones" Little robot allies. which would have complimented the Tech tree really well as they have the ability to buff robotic allies. Since you only get one robot companion and frankly I don't think she's that good... You're kind of left with some dead skills if you don't end up taking her. It's not damning but it's for sure annoying. I would have liked Drones!Edit 2: I decided to try Encased again, thinking that maybe I judged it too harshly, and after dumping a good load of hours into it again... I wish I could thumb down this game even more. I couldn't even finish it! Everything in act 2 to act 3 feels awful, like it leaves a really horrible taste in my mouth. I got to the point I was just rushing through to try and finish it and I couldn't. It's really bad and I got better things to do with my time. It's a shame, I still think this could have been a solid game that could have stood with the big titles of it's genre, but it was let down so much. :( I'll probably never touch this again.

_childDocuments_.review: Encased might not be the most polished and high-budget game, but it does certains things right, thing that are scarce nowdays. Mostly it's quests. Forget about markers on the map and exclamation marks over NPCs heads. Journal with vague directions is all you have, figure it out on your own. If you feel nostalgic about old school quests (Fallout 1-2, Morrowind, etc), Encased is a must-buy. It features lots of memorable characters and pretty much quest is hand tailored.One other thing worth mentioning is setting. Devs cite Fallout 1-2 and Roadside Picnic (novel that also inspired STALKER videogame) as a source of inspiration, but there are also strong SCP Foundation vibes. All of it is packed in a unique retrofuturistic setting (think 70s brutalism where ruthless capitalism meets overwhelming bureaucracy). So here are the main reasons to buy; what about reasons NOT to buy?There aren't any, to be honest, it's just that other aspects of the game aren't as good as quests and setting. Turn-based combat system is solid, but gets nowhere near Divinity: Original Sin, for example. UI clearly needs to be worked on (the game won't tell you why the heck you cannot throw a grenade - you have to figure out that you need to have a greande-throwing passive skill, and there are lots of thing like that). Those few lackings, however, do not change the bottom line: the game delivers genuine old school turn-based RPG experience without carbon copying it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have nearly 60 hours played and I feel I can give an informed opinion now.The game starts out great with a very fun and interactive introduction. The conversations and your role in them are entertaining. Your first mission is engaging, entertaining, and mysterious. You want to play on and find out more. You'll care about the characters you meet.The next few locations your quests steer you towards are also very well developed and engaging. However, without giving location names and quest spoilers. You will notice an incredible and sudden shift in the locations you go to after the first few. They feel absolutely lifeless and very empty. I can also tell you, this trend continues throughout the game without letting up. An incredible let down from the first part of the game.No, I have not finished the game. Encased got to the point where I was simply overwhelmed with the amount of looting you do with negligible results. 75% of the loot you gather is food, water, crafting materials you will never use. The other 25% you will somewhat use. I love looting. However, the looting became absolutely cumbersome, literally as well, for nearly no results but a huge time sink.The game is still pretty good. I simply lost interest with the shift in quality of the game in the later stages. The developers tried to do a little too much here and the project perhaps became a little too grand with the size of the team and lack of funds.Even with that said, if the game is on sale, I would recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: Finally finished one play-through, from beginning to end. What is it about the endings feeling so rushed/phoned in? Maybe it's just me. All this buildup, to just read some text. Honestly, though; how would you end a game? There has to be an end to the quests, etc; maybe there isn't any better way to say, "hey, you're done; start over, if you want."That being said, I still loved the aesthetic. And the music. All in all, it is a relaxing game. Does that mean it is boring, or slow? No. I think the turn-based combat, and not having time limits to quests keeps things mellow and stress-free. As with every game out there (pretty much), I wish that I had unlimited carrying capacity, LOL. I hate having to constantly wrestle with how much I am carrying, etc. I think the only part of the game mechanics that annoyed me was the "quantity selection" tool, when you were splitting multiples, or when you were in the Trade screen, and trying to apply a specific quantity to something. It's a highly imprecise slider, that gets frustrating, really fast - no way to input a specific amount, either. But, if that is the only real "issue" I had with the game, I think that is a good sign. I think, were a player to invest the time into playing all types of characters, and all various factions, there would be slight conversation/storyline differences. But, overall, I don't think that there would be enough to difference to convince ME to play through all over again; it's quite a long game.

name: DOOMBLADE
detailed_description: Lured out of her solitude, Gloom Girl discovers a chamber containing DOOMBLADE: a sentient weapon, trapped and bound for eons. “Doom and Gloom” join forces and begin a quest to regain the blade’s powers and exact vengeance on its captors. Wielding DOOMBLADE, Gloom Girl can ride through the air to attack enemies. Target monsters to attack them directly, and slay them with DOOMBLADE’s wrath! The blade hungers for vengeance on the Dread Lords, who bound it in chains and stripped it of its powers. But first, it must regain its strength. Search for demonic shrines, where DOOMBLADE’s powers were hidden and stored by the long dead Gloomfolk, awaiting its return. Then use Doom Drop, Wicked Wind, and the Nightmare Onion to teach your enemies fear. From the abandoned halls of Gloomhaunt, into the New Wilderwood forest full of untrusting tribesmen, through the Molded Mines with their hedonistic shroom people, and into a technological hellscape known as the Power Sector. Gloom Girl must fight her way through these interconnecting worlds and destroy the monsters within as she hunts down the Dread Lords who imprisoned DOOMBLADE.

_childDocuments_.review: I can tell you right now - there will be people mad about the controls, this is because despite being a metroidvania, it controls more like a twin-stick shooter, and as such, I found it orders of magnitude more fun with keyboard and mouse (and would rank it as just "playable" on controller due to personal preference)Game length if you just rush through will be just a few hours, if you're going for 100% (ignoring speedrunning achievements) - would put it closer to 10-15 hours. It's a satisfying length without being too long or too short.As usual though pros and cons -Pros: - Excellent music, it doesn't get in the way, but still does an excellent job of setting the mood with solid metal vibes at times, and enjoyable ambience at others.- Once you get used to the controls, they are fluid and enjoyable to use in more than 90% of the game, and I never felt hobbled by them- There's some cheesy puns, but it strikes a nice balance between story and action for a metroidvania (with bits and pieces here and there that give you more than enough to know what's going on, while the primary focus is on the gameplay itself)- While it doesn't explicitly tell you where to go, it's still very easy to navigate due to how it staggers the progression zones and skills, I am terrible at pathfinding and I only got lost once the entire time.- Boss design is really solid, only one irked me (you'll encounter him later on guarding an elevator, but that's all I'll say) - nice mix of easy and difficult bosses that use your movement skills in fun ways.Cons:- Red, so much red - in some areas it's hard to keep track of what's going on since your aiming marker is red too - this is only a problem in some zones though.- The swarm encounters are just a little too long for my taste (taking longer than any of the bosses usually) - and require a lot of clicking, thankfully, I can count on one hand how many of these there were (not to be confused with boss fights that have additional units - since in those cases, the additional units are useful for navigation)- If you want to see gameplay in action - you can find the video review here: Or you can view uncommentated gameplay of the first 53 minutes here:

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the better metroidvanias out there.Doomblades unconventional movement is refreshing, though takes a tiny bit of getting used too.  (One thing you will learn from boss fights is that if you slow down a bit and don't just kill everything on the screen mindlessly, you'll do better).I enjoyed the map and exploration.  In places, traversing reminded me of Ori & the Will of the Wisps.Nitpick (more an expression of my preferences): 100% Steam Achievements isn't possible in your first run (And i typically only play a game once), because there are a couple of speedrun achievements.  At the end of the game, missing objects aren't marked on your map, which i'd prefer that they were.  I like to fully finish a game and do it in one play through when it is both reasonable and possible.  You get enough power-ups and abilities for your character that backtracking and exploring is fun and rewarding.The music and graphics were very good.  The overall production reaches the slickness of Aeterna Noctis.The music can get a bit repetitive in places though which i would put down to the game needing more tracks (But then where do you put them without more areas..) _childDocuments_.review: Finally, the countless hours of training my right hand will pay off!It’s as if Ori and Doom had a child together, which is both terrifying and unnecessarily badass.Think of it as Hollow Knight, but on crack.This is the first Metroidvania I played this year that fully lived up to my hype. It is of a similar quality to Ori, but has a unique twin-stick DOOM melee gameplay and a really cool story. It is very polished and the world is dense, and is absolutely one of my GOTYs. I remember casually browsing the Steam Store, seeing this game and just being drawn to the dark, crimson elements like Cult of the Lamb with the metroidvania feel of Hollow Knight. It’s an amazingly quirky, but extremely well crafted, metroidvania where you play a non-human creature in a non-human world. The storytelling, music and atmosphere are absolutely exquisite.If you're expecting an uplifting story, this is not it. This is a tale of devastation and revenge. While the protagonist is silent, you'll get details about what happened through other speaking characters, 'monuments' and scrolls detailing various parts of the world. As you get more details, you'll likely share the protagonist's indignation and want revenge. The game does a good job at making you sorry for what happened to her world and there is definitely a social commentary buried under the game.The game is beautiful, with each biome being very distinctive and gorgeous. The player movement is very addicting and as each ability unlocks it has a similar speed and fluidity as late game Ori. The exploration is basically perfect, with a final game cleanup being the highlight of the whole experience. Great boss fights, great combat, interesting story and atmosphere.By far the best part is the middle of it though, where you get a chance to explore a ton and unlock some crazy and unique abilities. I found the difficulty of the game well balanced. The game was not easy and I died my fair share, especially during boss fights, but even on the fights that I had to retry 5-10 times, I always felt I was not too far from winning and the next try would be the one.  For me, it was really difficult from the beginning, but then again I'm not a pro at gaming by far. I also really liked the weird character designs and the constant borderline chaos of the action. I was intrigued by the melodrama of the game moment when I picked up the sword.There are various environments with unique terrain to navigate and a lot of creatures to tackles, each with a unique feel that are a natural fit for their environment. Everything is very organic in this game and flows very well together.  Like any well crafted metroidvania, there is some backtracking to do as new abilities will unlock new areas of the map to explore. The protagonist's ability to attack and move by flying/ramming into select objects and opponents is rather unique and interesting which, combined with the alien organic feel of the world, contributes to give the game a very distinct feel. I started playing this game with a controller, then tried a mouse and I'll say that this is one of the very few games in this genre that will give you a superior experience with a keyboard and mouse I found. Clicking on things you want to ram into in quick succession works far better.  Doomblade is clearly meant to be played with keyboard and mouse. Unlike most, if not all, other platformers this game is NOT enjoyable with a controller.Doomblade is awesome. Rarely do gameplay, level design and art design blend together this seamlessly. Truly a joy from start to finish. Exploring the world always felt meaningful. Speed running the game felt like a fresh challenge as well. Together with Elden ring, Doomblade is my favorite game from the last ten years and my second favorite 2D metrovania after Super metroid. Assuming you can appreciate the "doom and gloom" theme of the game, I heavily recommend it. It’s memorable and likely to leave a lasting impression.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give  a neutral recommendaction, instead of a negative one as I think this game had some really good sides, and I really wanted to like this game.Positive points:- The art and animation in this game is amazing. I love the colours, character designs, walking and attacking animation, all of it- The story is pretty solid as well. You could kinda predict where it was going, but it was really good in the end.- I really enjoyed the mechanics of flying around the screen to attack, made the game quite dynamicThat being said, here are the negative points:- This game is unplayable on a controller. I tried playing this with a controller for the first 1h since this is tagged as metroidvania and almost ended up asking for a refund, but decided to try keyboard before that, and the experience is completely different- The game can be really buggy. I ended up having to restart the game after 4h playing cause an NPC was supposed to give me a key to continue, but they never did and I just got stuck. 1 of those 4h was me going everywhere on the map trying to figure out what to do until I decided to find a walkthrough online only to realize there was no way for me to continue. Another time I dashed into a whole and just got stuck. Had to restart the game and go back to my last save.- Some bosses mechanics are quite bad. Some of them you basically depend on luck and no hability and it's just too frustrating- You can't go down on platforms/edges by pressing jump and down, so you have to manually go around them, which I haven't seen in a metroidvania in forever. This really makes some boss fights terrible.- heart magnet mechanics SUCKS. Like really. The bones magnet make sense as they just fly straight to your character, but the heart one was done with a gravity like effect that made you miss the heart even though you went straight over it. There were a couple of boss fights that I'd lose 1-3 hearts just trying to get one cause of this.- When you die, you go back to your last save, so you end up losing a lot of time going back and forth between save spots. If you forget you end up losing all the progress. I think the experience would have been much better if it was like hollow knight, where you lose some bones. I don't mind if you just lose them or if you have a way of getting them back, but I just have that you lose all progress.I think this game has a lot of potential, and if they deal with some of these points, it could be a more enjoyable experience.Also, regarding the 4h save that got stuck, I did contact the developers about it, they had no idea how that happened, but manually added the item to my save so I could finish it, so just a shout out to them for that!

_childDocuments_.review: Not going to lie, the biggest barrier for enjoyment at the start of "Doomblade" is getting used to the somewhat unorthodox controls. I highly recommend (and I cannot believe I am saying this) playing the game with Keyboard&Mouse over controller. It feels much better.After you start getting some upgrades (specifically by the time you grab Shadow Form and Grim Ripper), things start to come together and moving around becomes much more enjoyable, though jump&dash being on the same button still tripped me up with some regularity.Music is great, the story has a certain kind of dry acerbicness that I appreciate, and the exploration is generally good — though the game lacks custom map markers which caused me some problems and stretched the cleanup phase a little too thin for my liking. I would have turned to a guide if I'd had opportunity to do so, as finding the gloomsouls near the end was just a little long-winded for my tastes.Definitely worth the price, in my opinion! (For the soundtrack alone, which reminded me of Doom meets Portal).

_childDocuments_.review: After getting past the fact that my toaster PC refuses to let the game run smoothly, I realized that Doomblade is a great metroidvania.For the past month or two I've been hunting down metroidvanias like Ori (if you can call it that) and Axiom Verge. I watched a video from a Hollow Knight content creator who played the game, and it sure looked like fun.When I bought it and tried it out, my computer was unable to accept this new game and instead transformed it into a PowerPoint presentation. I was annoyed and started to regret my decision. However, after turning the quality down a bit, my desktop seemed to ease away from the nightmarish frame rate.Before I delve into the good parts of the game, I'll get the bad stuff out of the way. So for me at least, when I died in a certain area, on the loading screen a repeating, monotone thrumming noise plays until the game loads. I have no idea what this is, but this happened with the final boss and the sound played even during the end cutscene and the credits. If anyone knows what the sound is or is experiencing a similar glitch, please let me know.The only other bad thing about Doomblade is the somewhat annoying combat. I felt like the devout enemies were very difficult to dispatch without taking much damage.Although there were bad things about the game, I still really loved it. The art was good(not Ori level, of course), but what I REALLY loved was the soundtrack, especially since I'm a huge fan of heavy metal and doom-themed music.It's also pretty obvious that the movement in this game is brilliant. Launching yourself at enemies feels SO good as a key mechanic.The theme of Doomblade is pretty cool and unique, and unlike other games *cough*ORI*cough* it lets you explore without shoving a quest marker in your face. The midgame is the best part, because it lets you explore and opens up the world.Overall, I was really impressed with this metroidvania and would definitely recommend it. I am very surprised that Doomblade is this underrated and not heard of.

_childDocuments_.review: This marks my first Steam review, which I felt compelled to do because I loved this game and hope this game gains more traction. I came here to say that this game is AWESOME. Seriously, I cannot believe more people are not talking about this game. I love Metroidvanias and have played through a long list of them. This game is top notch. The combat is mixed with a travel mechanic that lets you traverse the map in an engaging way, unlike anything I have ever seen before. The story is dark with humor scattered throughout in a way that leaves much of the dialog and motifs up to interpretation. I can see where people say the music can get a bit repetitive; however the music is moody and unique to each area in a way that fits perfectly. The game play can require a bit of precision which can be difficult with a controller, and it does say on the main screen that it is recommended to be done with a keyboard and mouse. I did about 90% of the game with a controller and only needed a keyboard / mouse for a few boss fights, and I think both have their pros and cons. Either way, it is still do-able and incredibly engaging to play with either control scheme. I experienced a total of zero glitches playing this game as well. This game is polished, unique, and a true joy to play.

_childDocuments_.review: First, let me say that I love the core mechanic of this game and I think flying across the screen with one simple attack is extremely fun. Also this is the best walking animation I have ever seen.Sadly, all the secondary mechanics of the game are implemented in weird and frustrating ways, making the experience more tedious than fun. Most of these things are basic and are done well by almost every other platformer so I don't know why you guys felt the need to reinvent the wheel. Here's what I mean:1. When on a thin platform, you can't drop down from it by pressing jump while holding the down button. Seriously, this is basic platforming 101 and it may not seem like much, but it's frustrating in a game like this. Some platformers don't really need it but this one really does because you constantly have to reposition yourself before attacking, so that you don't eat a projectile mid air.2. Speaking of repositioning, this part is very important. You can't dash on the ground. You can only dash mid air and the dash button is the same as the jump button. A dedicated dash button and the ability to dash on the ground are a no-brainer and highly necessary. Almost every game in the genre has this and the ones that don't, are usually more chill and don't need it but Doomblade is a game where everything is about movement and yet it imposes so many limits on it for no good reason.3. Going over ledges tends to be inconsistent because sometimes, the thing that you have to attack in order to climb over the corner, be it an enemy or an onion, is just a tad bit too low and instead of going on the platform you will hit the wall. If the dash wasn't tied to the jump button this could easily be solved with a double jump since the jump itself is very low and and I'm pretty sure it wouldn't make you reach certain areas earlier than you should. I'm convinced that, because of the way the attack works and how central it is to the game, having a double jump from the get go would make the experience a lot more fluid and fun.4. I completed the Onion gauntlet and I found it annoying to do, mainly because, unlike the electricity projectile, the onion doesn't fly straight but in lobbed way. The last thing I want when I'm stranded mid air is to fall from my course because the freaking onion didn't go where I aimed it. I don't know why you made it like this. Maybe it's because the onion is a physical object that the Gloomling throws but really, no body cares about that. Realistic physics don't matter that much and should be secondary to the feel of the gameplay, especially in a cartoony game like this one. Seriously, make it fly straight and bounce from the walls just like the electric one does. The onion should be precise first and foremost, because you depend on it a lot for movement.5. When you die you lose all the pick ups and all the map progress you've made after the last save. I know the original metroidvanias used to do things this way but the classic saving system has been replaced for a good reason: it is out dated as hell. Having to re-explore everything  you've just explored and pick up again all the items that you already found is tedious and boring. Instead you could have made it so that the character would lose some of her bones that she would have to recollect by backtracking to the place of her death if she wanted to or not lose anything at all just like every other self-respecting, modern metroidvania does.6. Don't get me started on the fast travel system.All in all I am sad that this game is not better because I didn't want to like it. I wanted to love it! The main idea is amazing and it could have made Doomblade a ground-breaking masterpiece if it didn't fumble on so many basic aspects of the metroidvania genre.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: Can I recommend this game? I want to, but consider this...First off, the game is a piece of beauty. I can spend my whole day just sitting in front of it, enjoying the visuals and the music. It's so good that I can't stop playing.Being a rather purist metroidvania, the game doesn't hold your hand regarding story, quests and game progression. You have to completely figure out by yourself, what is going on, where to go and what to do. The map reveals itself only as you find new areas. Which isn't a bad thing in itself, because this can keep you busy for quite some time depending on how much completion you want. There's also a fast travel system. It's not as simple as just clicking on the map and be teleported there. All the movement is done in the game. So be prepared to spend extra time for going to the next location, travel somewhere else, going to yet another location and then travel to your final destination where you hope to find something new. The player character is a lovely little creature and I like that they left it silent so that I can fully enjoy the surroundings.Gameplay. Well, let's put it this way: This is not your typical 2D platformer/metroidvania where you walk/run/dash/fly with the established control schemes. The philosophy is: In order to move, you have to kill/attack an enemy. And they are serious about it. The whole game is designed around that philosophy. While progressing, you gain additional abilities that have to be combined with this core mechanic in order to reach some spot or defeat certain enemies. And that's where the control scheme comes into play. Since you have to attack/kill all the time, you are aiming and pressing attack while doing additional horizontal movement and jump/dash at the same time. On controller this means you have to use both sticks all the time. Which also means that your right thumb is occupied and jump/dash has to be performed with some other finger (left trigger by default). It looks like the game was originally designed with keyboard/mouse in mind and controller support added as an afterthought. But there is more. You can't dash on the ground, only in the air. Wanna dash out of the way real quick? Nope, you just forgot to jump beforehand. You can't simply drop down through a platform. You can get there directly by aiming/attacking, if there's an enemy. Otherwise you have to go around. This also applies to boss fights that have platforms in the arena. Overall it feels like the character is a sitting duck on the ground and comes to life when airborne. To be fair, after some hours in the game and with a few abilities unlocked, the "can't move!" feel fades away.Combat in the field is practically nonexistent, as you abuse most enemies for traversal. Which leaves the boss/miniboss fights. Most of them evolve around the general pattern of having a big guy or two that can't be attacked directly plus a bunch of small enemies that respawn frequently. The small enemies are vital for you to move around, but they also give plenty of opportunities to collide with them, bounce off of them and getting attacked by them from multiple angles. So you spend most of your time zapping around in the air while dodging enemy attacks and projectiles and getting in the occasional attack at the big guy. It can get hectic and a bit chaotic. There are also a few welcome deviations from this pattern. The fights are more on the difficult side (you will probably die a lot) and require you to learn the attack/movement patterns and find your way to counter that. It helps that save points are never too far away from the boss arenas. Although they can sometimes feel a bit scarcely placed across the map, especially when you just barely managed to get past a challenging platforming puzzle.So, is this game worth playing? Presentation wise yes, absolutely! Gameplay wise also, if you are willing to adapt to playing a 2D platformer/metroidvania in a new and different way.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is good, but like, not amazing imo. please for the love of god play this game with mouse and keyboard. i know its a metroidvania and like 99% of metroidvanias should be played with a controller, but not this one. _childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty great metroidvania.  When I first started I was worried when I saw how the character controls.  It's very different than other MVs.  Fortunately, it works really well and the design of the game around this movement feels great with each new upgrade you unlock.  Another thing that jumped out on this one is the music is really well done, my hat is off to whoever handled this.Map is fairly decent sized, not massive, but big enough that you can get around it really fast if you use the movement well.  I do wish you could mark the map, but it's not a deal breaker. There is a weird fast travel system, which at first concerned me, but like the movement its unique and it works thanks to good design especially later in the game.  There are multiple endings for people who really make a point to explore enough, but there are achievements you probably will not get on a first play, so trying to 100% will take more than a single playthrough as they require speed running.Definitely recommend this one though if you are a fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: If hollow knight and doom had a baby this would be it!It's a great game with unique fun combat and traversal that works really well. Only downside for me was the lack of navigation assistance which had me going around in circles lost at times. Needs ability to mark the map or track objectives. Also beware the bosses in this game can be very hard at times.Overall I really like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: Good looking visuals, pleasant decently varied biomes, fitting music. Devs made some strange decisions regarding how saves work - you'll have to redo all the actions since the last time you saved, including all the collection, kills, purchases, etc. which is a big bummer, as i barely remember what i did a minute ago. Got a big green warning on the main screen that mouse + keyboard is preferred, but i played through with controller and had no problems. Backtracking became super tedious at the end, as i realized too late i should manually mark things i find on the map for later, biggest problem being the shrines that i could not read at first. Some kind of (expensive? hard to find?) upgrade to show leftover collectibles on the map would have been great, even if it's as vague as the one pointing at gloomsouls. Final boss made me mad, the stage with lasers was far enough from the start of the fight that dying and replaying was annoying, and fast enough for me to not understand how to do it. Nearly dropped right there near the end, but accidentally figured it out by chaotically mashing buttons. Movement felt fun most of the time, especially satisfying was navigating using the void once i received up/down charge upgrades. A side/diagonal/omnidirectional charge and more void exits would have done wonders for collectible cleanup. Oh, and there's a fetch quest i diligently followed over the whole map (kinda like talking mushroom in Hollow Knight and spores in Roku's Island), only to find out it's for the worst ending. Dev mentioned it's kind of a bonus and is separate from the real endings, but i remember feeling quite bummed by it.Edit: Forgot to say that my gaming laptop took off every time i ran Doomblade, full fan speed blasting heat every which way, huffin, puffin, struggling to breathe. The game does not look demanding but apparently is.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts strong, but is just rough around the edges in a lot of different aspects.The twin stick shooter style of movement is interesting and starts quite fun, but especially the last 50% of the enemies are just kamakaze enemies, which are quite boring.  Just general movement is -extremely- floaty and slow, leading to lots of tedium and frustration when navigating the map and going to previous areas.Exploration is quite tedious, as you tend to get small amounts of progression in various areas, but no real indication on where to go.  Since the movement is quite slow and floaty, it takes forever to get from place to place, as the fast travel doesnt always bring you to where you need to go.Overall, 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: The boss encounters are interesting but the game in general just doesn't have biomes and areas that I find interesting to explore. The combat mechanics can be a bit finicky and dashing at the right target  with something else in line is really really difficult. I really tried giving this a fair shot but it just didn't hold my attention.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: Doomblade is a fast-paced Metroidvania with things I have never seen before. At first the controls may seem weird before you get used to them, since there can be multiple things happening at the screen at the same time, but the challenge is part of the fun. I didn't know if I should focus on the character or the crosshair, then panicked and died multiple times on the first boss. You unlock areas of the map as you play, and you realize quite early that if there is a platform you can't reach yet, you will have to come back later after you have got some new powers. The first few hours have been addictive and challenging just the right way. It is a must-have especially for Metroidvania fans, but the intelligent design makes it desirable and interesting even if you're not familiar with the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: I simply have no desire to finish this game, but I did at least try. The art and soundtrack are pretty great. Some songs go really hard and it's awesome. The movement feels pretty fun throughout the whole experience, although it can be tiresome to find things to target. The story and lore are there for you to find, though it's mostly through 'atlas' entries about an area. Maybe I missed some things, but I had no idea until just recently (in the ~7 hours I've played) why the main character was doing what they were doing. That said, once I had a reason, I was more motivated to play until I hit (what I presume was) the final boss.: I was worried about this game after the first boss fight but was optimistic. It turns out most (if not all) boss fights have the exact same formula: the boss is invulnerable or is doing damage around them, so you just have to avoid them and then get a few hits before repeating. There are about 2  bosses off the top of my head that were interesting to fight for me personally. Neither of them uses the formula as before or if they do there's an interesting gimmick involved so you can actually do something besides dodging. No spoilers for the final boss, but it was the straw that broke my back. Probably the biggest offender of this strategy and there are a few one-shot kill things to really make it fun.: There are many sections that require you to remember where you can use a new ability (pretty similar to how other metroidvanias play). This is where someone will say "Just take notes", which is fair, but still frustrating. On top of that, near the very end of the game, there are 8 (I think) things scattered on the map, with seemingly no rhyme or reason as to where they are or hints as to where they could be. It's implied that finding them will be very good for you, but I simply can't be bothered to survey the entire map, the movement isn't  fun.: Platforming is not fun, it's especially difficult to do some of the more challenging sections because three of your abilities are on your scroll wheel, and are often required to switch between them midair.I don't know, maybe if you enjoy boss-rush-like games, this might be more up your alley, but personally, the bosses and fights were hardly interesting and weren't challenging in a fun way, but an irritating way.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunatly, it is hard to recomend this game. despite being called Doomblade, the combat in this game is incredibly simple: left click the enemy. there are no combos or really any abilities you can use in combat. just left click alot to win. this makes the few bosses this game have incredibly bad, because most of the time you can't just spam left click. you have to do other stuff first, and most of the time it simply doesn't work, or is tied to RNG. spamming your ranged "attack" (that doesn't do any damage) so that maybe one shot will bounce off the wall in an angle to hit the weakpoint of the boss, so you can continue spamming left click the boss to win. terrible boss desing all around. or how about those bosses tho you can only damage by flying throught them when you attack an enemy behind them. to this 20 times and the boss is dead. and if there is no enemy behind the boss? then ♥♥♥♥ you, the boss gets to hit you because there are also no dodge skills or anything related to mobility in fights in this game. this is probably the only metroidvania I know where you hardly get any stronger  the longer you play.the only good part of this game is the platforming, because it is apparent that this is the only part the developers put any thought behind. some part are quite difficult and fun to get through....other on the other hand are quite bad.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: Doomblade is a well executed Metroidvania platformer with a unique moving/fighting mechanic. The world is interesting to explore and there is nice variation in the kind of challenges the game throws at you. The game is also polished both visually and from an audio perspective. The difficult has a few spikes, but most of the time there has been steady progress. I'm now closer to the end of the game and at this point it would be nice to have some sort of chance to make notes on the map, as it starts to be hard to know which areas to explore to get onwards. But all in all, a positive and unique experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game surprised me immensely! Shakes up the metroidvania formula in some very interesting ways. The movement and combat are extremely satisfying. The art and music are top tier. Highly recommended. I wouldn't even try this game on a controller honestly. Coming from someone that has played every single other metroidvania on a controller.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: This game was great! The core gameplay design was really unconventional but the devs made it work really well. The world and story were compelling and made me want to keep going, to see everything and help the residents of this broken world.Then I got to a point where the only remaining accessible and incomplete part of the map was an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gauntlet of seemingly endlessly spawning bullet hell enemies in the absolute worst tower defense arena I've ever seen in any video game. It's  not an arena that plays to any of this game's strengths, that much I can tell you. This isn't the first time you fight these enemies, but it  the first time you fight more than three at once, and in this arena that's just the  wave out of at least three.The enemies all have directional shields and fairly random movement, the arena is covered with platforms that theoretically are what make dodging projectiles possible at all but in practice just make it harder to avoid damage, and the collision of every object in the arena plays out in whichever manner is most inconvenient to the player. Enemy projectiles hit you during your attacks and interrupt them, your own projectiles you have to use to activate the turrets bounce off their shields yet can't damage them, platforms inhibit your movement more than theirs so you can't weave out of their direction of fire or avoid getting surrounded by them...you get the idea.I was already tired of these enemies by the end of the first arena that featured them, and this was, like, the  one. I didn't get any meaningful combat-related upgrades between the first arena and this one, either. I actively scoured the map hoping for some kind of projectile defense or improved sideways dash,  that would make this arena more bearable, but found absolutely nothing.I guess those cultists are getting their hands on the sword after all, because I don't feel like wielding it anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: I love fast paced games like this you are never stuck because of the map providing you ideas of where to go next and the Bosses can maybe be slightly to bland (relies on using summons for the gimmick of the game to work I feel like) but still fun if you are able to beat them in a reasonable amount of attempts. It has it unique game mechanics and fun power-ups which all feels good to get and doesn't take too long. Overall I like it and would strongly recommend.

When going back to fight a boss get rid of some of the animation to start the boss fight. 3. Add more labels to the map for everything.4. Make traveling easier even just by speeding up animations.

_childDocuments_.review: a game whose central mechanic of chasing down enemies and slicing them fails horribly when it comes to combat. Your dodge is not capable of actually dodging all attacks, and all defensive moves can only be done while you're in the air, which means you are constantly in motion trying to dodge attacks from angles. The game desperately needs an actual way of avoiding damage that doesn't involve rapidly moving in a cardinal direction. The boss fights and arena battles become frustrating and demand more than the combat system allows. You will get hit by attacks that there is literally no way to avoid, even getting hit while you're attacking something else that is just close enough to your hitbox to strike you, but not close enough to get hit by your attack.World design is interesting, but there is no sense of pacing or structure, it's a game where there is no rhyme or reason given to the player as to where to go next or what you should be doing, made worse by a limited fast travel.  The premise starting out well, but the combat and issues are too frustrating to ignore.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a masterpiece at work since there are some points that could be optimized.The difficulty is set correctly to serve a normal gamer with a small experience.Very good devs since they are willing to help in their discord with hints where to find items or how to progress if stuck.Story wise and music wise it doesnt need anything else but when it comes to controls there are some flaws.In the map ,that is that big, having the ability to mark locations in order to visit later since it needs an ability you dont have is crucial.Seems an easy fix for later though.The bosses are simple yet use various mechanics to make it fun but i would love the ability to replay some gauntlets.Once you are done with the main game and you are missing a few collectables you should have the ability to pick an item thta reveals hidden areas/items to manage all achievements or hearts/whatever to make it easierThe movement is unique and it takes a while to learn but once you get used to it you start to shread.But I dont understand why you have to jump first in order to dash???Some bosses or even travelling would be much easier and faster to complete.The game is worth buying and hopefully they fix those minor inconveniences.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start off by saying I don't have an issue with the controls, and I played on controller with no issue since that's my preference, it's very possible if you take a bit of time to get used to the controls since they are different from other metroidvanias. Now going on to the review: I wish there was a neutral option to let people know I feel pretty medium about the game but if I'm being honest, there are a few good things but in my opinion more bad things in this game as a whole. For starters the game play is unique from other games like it with a different attack mechanic and a couple new abilities that help differentiate it from others without it feeling like a copy of those games. The art and music are also really stellar, the color palette and different boss musics are good throughout the game which is always a plus. This game can be very fun if you have the patience to get through some parts of it. Some things I feel neutral about; people in their reviews complained about not being able to drop through a small platform like in other games, this doesn't bother me really as it's just part of the game, it is very easy to work around. The story is also just okay, it's not stellar writing but I wasn't really looking for a story in this game so it was nice that it had it at least. Now for the bad parts of this game. The game play has fun aspects but the main issue I have with the combat is there is no neutral attack to attack right in front of you, this makes certain enemies that shouldn't be an issue tedious to fight as the only option is to go through them with an attack, but there isn't always an option to do it without taking damage. This is an issue you'll face more and more as you go towards the end of the game, especially the tentacle leg monsters, I am not talking about the shield enemies. Speaking more on the game play, the enemies and fights, while they look great, are extremely repetitive, you'll see the same boss fight and game play loop throughout the entire game which can get very monotonous after a while. More on the boss fights and going back to my first issue, there are too many fights in which the ability to attack them without taking damage is not possible, while it's not a game ending issue it does make it less fun in my opinion not being able to work around many attacks. The map and "notes" are extremely useless in most cases, having the fast travel and save points are great, but there are many many many things you basically need to look at a tutorial for to find due to the lack of markers on the map, making it tedious if you want to 100% the game. This issue is also further pressed by the fact that the game gives you essentially NO direction, leaving you to aimlessly wander through the map until you find a place you can go forward. My last and biggest gripe with the game is how incredibly slow it feels due to how immobile you are. The only way to move quickly at all is through attacking, otherwise it feels like you are crawling through the game at a snail's pace, which pulls away from the game a lot for me. The inability to jump as well is frustrating as it causes you to not be able to get around certain attacks and other things in the game, making it tedious to even go from place to place in the game without the end game abilities. These issues stacked with the lack of direction make this game more of a chore to play than it is necessarily fun. Some of these issues can be fixed by devs, but with my main issues being with the mobility and basic game play things, I personally would not get this game at full price (which I did not thankfully) There are many other metroidvanias out there that you can play that have an overall better experience, but I will note that the game has a unique game play style that does still make it fun in its own regard. TLDR: The game is okay, but there are better games on the market. Only buy it on sale if you can help it.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game with a lot of fun unique mechanics. If you like metroidvanias, definitely give it a try. Character movement feels slow and clunky in the beginning but you obtain movement abilities quite quickly and then it feels very satisfying and dynamic. Missed a more detailed map with a legend (mostly for gloomstones). That would save a lot of backtracking and speaking of backtracking squids teleporting you to any unlocked void point would have been appreciated. Custom markers are a great help, though sometimes you forget what have you marked there. Was it an HP upgrade, a gloomstone or just some point of interest? Dont know, I forgot lol. In terms of difficulty a game is quite tough but fair, punishes carelessness and leaves some wiggle room in execution if you actually come up with a proper approach to specific situation
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: A nice metroidvania with an interesting pair of characters you play as. The gameplay is fun and the writing in this game is great. If you want a more in depth look at this game I did make a 1st thoughts video.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: - Horrible tedious bossfights.- Movement feels slow, you are dependent on enemies to traverse quickly, but a lot of them either throw a lot of ♥♥♥♥ at you really quickly, or have some kind of shield/painfield, and because you travel towards enemies in a straight line you are often really limited to dodge.- Inconsistent save point distance, be ready to lose 15 minutes of progress at any time.- Hard to judge where to go, be ready to stare at the map a lot. At one time, i unlocked a teleport from the left side to the map, to the right side. So, take the teleporter right? why else would i unlock it? Nope, i had to go smackdap in the middle of the map, where i overlooked a room ( which is really easy to do, because there are a lot of ways you cant go which basically look like open hallways on the map. Wanna know if you need to take a hallway to proceed? gotta move over there. I got stuck, i had to try out 6 different locations. And you can move through walls, so i had to move through a wall, but i didnt move close enough to the wall, so only a sliver of the room was visible on the map )- Insane fights in general, often its smooth sailing, but then you get dropped in 4 waves of bullsh*t.- Stingy rewards, you spend a lot of time doing some hard gauntlet, bouncing on moving platforms while avoiding spikes, just to get 1/4th of a heart container.- No temporary invulnability from enemy hit, you can instantly lose all your health.- No way to heal. Youre often dependent on enemy health drops or save points to heal, but thats really inconsistent. Sometimes, heaps of health spawns, and sometimes nothing. i'm often running around with just 1 heart health, and then die and have to do some large area over again. Its the back to the previous save point, the stuff you've explored does not stay in the map.I'm also not that fond of the world so far, frankly im not having a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game, and it's SO CLOSE to being great in my eyes. But there are a few quality of life touches that are missing that would send it over the edge.Right now I'd put it at maybe a 6 out of 10, still recommend playing it, but it can be frustrating.The game does not hold your hand and sometimes doesn't even really *hint* at where to go next.. which would be fine.. IF they let you place map markers.A metroidvania with backtracking and progression abilities that does NOT let you place map markers is.. well.. Rough. There are things that will be important later that are not marked by default and you simply have to just.. remember.The story, the art & aesthetic, and the general vibe are all wonderful. I love all of it. The gamepad controls confuse me a little bit, but weren't a gamebreaker, and I was able to get used to them with time. (I've never seen Left Trigger be the default jump button with A/X is not used for anything except dialogue.)I'm hoping they take some feedback on quality of life updates, but the game is quite lovely and worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: Doomblade has a lot to like. It is worth getting on discount. The game is fun and a unique. The most frustrating part of the game is how the game handles saves. If you die in between a save, all progress is lost. Instead of just making it that you loose experience or bones, you have to redo everything you did since the last save. The game is relatively easy so not a train smash. You will sometimes miss relevant mission critical parts in the game. As you might not see a button or something that can be interacted with in some way. I ended up trying to search the internet for clues where to go next as traversing the map endlessly looking for the next step is painful. I am almost at the last boss but I am probably going to give up searching for him as I already have a 9/5 not looking for another one. I suspect 7 hours would be fair to get here and another 7 to get to the end boss searching through the map or online for tips.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a narrow recommendation for a metroidvania that really brings back the glory days of mouse & keyboard platforming that existed before the xbox 360 and its hugely popular controller came out. Movement is done via WASD and space while attacks are done via the mouse. attacking is often combined with movement in order to traverse. Perhaps the biggest mistake this game did was to make dash require a second tao of space, essentially making space the key used for both jump and dash which is VERY awkward and takes a long time to get used to. Another issue with the game is the insane amount of backtracking needed because of how poorly the warp points are placed, I think about 2/3rds of the time spent in this game was just me purely backtracking to some ability gate that is now unlocked. Indeed, I did feel this game wear out its welcome as a result and I was really glad to be done with it. A third problem is that the sound mixing is just not very good. Still, it is well designed, polished, and unique. I recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Very neat and polished metroidvania with a sick soundtrack. Boss battles have Doom djent sounding tracks that are head bang worthy. The fast travel system was an interesting take on the system.My only gripes are having a maximum of 20 markers that are confined to 1 icon so you can;t distinguish them, and being unable to read glyphs for the whole game, maybe I missed something but there seemed to be glyphs and shiny spots I should've been able to interact with but couldn'tOverall a solid title and surprisingly not as well-known despite being an overall great game.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still early into this game, but I can definitely recommend it.I've been on a hunt for a metroidvania that would give me the movement vibes that Ori and the Will of the Wisps gave me: that jump->jump->jump->throw on enemy->throw yourself->hit enemby->resume throwing that makes it one of the most aerial combat ever seen.This game, while different, captures the aerial combat idea and goes all in on it. Most of the time is spent in the air, for some really innovative movement mechanics.So far I gained 3 new skills (plus the ability to look at the map), one of them is a classic (but great) one for movement, one of them is the classic area-unlocker skill, the third one completely shocked me. A movement skill that makes level design probably the hardest.Between the basic skill (that already trigger insane movement) and that new skill, I have no idea how the level designer managed to keep designing this game, KUDOS.Boss fights are interesting, platforming is way more pleasant (probably due to my addiction to aerial combat), graphics is great, the plot is also intriguing.I'm not sure about the complaints for the lack of fast travel, I found a fast travel mechanism within 2 hours of playthrough?! Maybe it was added later.I'm very careful with anything below 90% positive all time, but for some reason the trailer of this game was showing me everything I was expecting.Within 10 minutes, the game did exactly what I wanted from it and I was hooked.Highly recommend so far (2 hours of playtime), if you like how ori flies, this game is for you.EDIT: I finished the game in about 20 hours at 94% completion (Steam doesn't register the hours when offline on my Steam Deck).I can say it's an amazing game, I already miss it. There are a couple of new skills that makes traversing levels even more incredible and the level design manages to hold up. One of the fastest moving metroidvanias out there.I played the game with a controller and was very happy with my choice, no regrets for mouse and keyboard.Some boss design are really creative, at points I felt demotivated by how hard they looked like, but then with some thinking, I was able to solve the challenges.Might not be Hollow Knight (which I score as a 10) but it's an 8 or a 9. My only complaints are: - longevity, I loved all of it and 20 hours felt "short", I wish it was longer! Some areas could have been expanded in terms of lore, would have been great- There were one or two boss fights (thinking the ninjas right now) that were frustrating more than fun- Some of the "platforming" sections were incredibly fun, but there were only a few of the major ones which played on the whole movement idea, I wish there was moreOverall I suspect this it's only a matter of content, this game could easily be a 10 with more budget, the development team did an amazing work.HIGHLY recommend, you should play this game if you like metroidvanias, it's incredibly innovative
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hit-or-miss. Either you manage to master its unique movement controls and it will be fun or you don't and it will be frustrating.To explain, in Doomblade, your character can jump and air dash but your main way of moving around will be by attacking. To attack, you need to target an enemy with the right stick or your mouse and press a button to make your character fly to the enemy and hit it. Then you can attack another enemy, and another, and yet another, flying around at high speed and reaching high and faraway places. Later in the game, you will even gain the abitly to attack through walls.The whole gameplay is designed around this feature.Besides that, here are a few good and bad points.GOOD- Great level design and map- Good art- Good music- Responsive controlsBAD- Difficulty, especially during arena fights and some bosses (the final boss is especially insanely hard)- Not completionist-friendly at all. There's no in-game way to track your progress and many collectibles are impossible to find without a detailed map- There are 3 mains endings (plus an unlockable post-credits scene) but they are mutually excusives so, if you don't want to play the game three times, you need to know beforehand what their conditions are

_childDocuments_.review: I tried really hard to like this and complete it but I've given up after getting the Nightmare Key. In the very few sections where the game gets fast-paced and relies on quick responses, it's really fun and engaging because it leans into the point-and-click piloted movement.But it just keeps getting bogged down in slow platforming bits and I'm not sure why because the whole gimmick is you using a Keyboard & Mouse (good luck with a controller, it feels bad) to rapidly click to points with lightning precision. Paradise Wells, for example, is a completely tedious area that brings movement to a crawl to navigate around and you have all these abilities and upgrades for movement unlocked. Is the area designed for you to be able to use all of these stacked-up movement options you've just spent hours collecting? Nope. But then in saying that some of the upgrades didn't feel great to use anyway, like the onion-flower thing, the projectile is a slow arc (almost as painful as the walk speed) and it keeps interrupting the rhythm of the click-dash's high speed. And I think this is what my main problem is: the movement has great potential to have this great rhythm to it but the majority of the game just won't let you do it.Also I really wasn't a fan of the the majority of the bosses. Void Dragon felt good because it embraced the frantic, fast pace needed to keep pivoting around the boss and then rapid-fire damage when it's vulnerable but I think Cybersentinel is a perfect mascot for the levels of tedious the game feels sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOMBLADE is one of the most unique games in the metroidvania category, which is already a unique genre itself. Unfortunately being unique isn't enough to make a game enjoyable, especially when you forgo many of the standards established by the genre. Specifically speaking for doomblade, it's a game with an innovative movement system that's really great when it works, but suffers when it doesn't. This is because in doomblade your movement is tied to enemies, flying from one to the other as you slaughter your foes. This opens op a lot of level design opportunities but also limits it in a lot of ways especially in regards to backtracking. This movement system doesn't actually allow for that much freedom, as you can only fly from one enemy to another. This makes  everything between and around them accesible this way. Anything further away from those enemies is for the most part inaccesible. This is frustrating because you want to see what's behind that ledge but can't because there's no enemies nearby. Ofcourse this is a metroidvania, so this is sorta like ability gating but not quite. Even later in the game when you've found most movement abilities this feels restrictive. Because these additional ways of movement are still inferior to the main method of traversal. This makes exploring the map a slog, because anything that isn't on the main path feels like a chore to reach.What also feels like a chore is the ridiculous amount of backtracking in this game. A good metroidvania imo should allow you to pick up most things along the way on your first pass through an area, but have a few ability gated collectibles or side routes inaccesible until you later backtrack here with the necesary upgrades. In doomblade you constantly have to go back & forth through whole areas for the main upgrades. There's areas i had to go through more than a dozen times just following the main path to the next main upgrade. What makes this worse is that due to moving to enemies, the area plays out the same each time you pass through. And it's not that the movement feels clunky, flying from enemy to enemy is fun, but only for the first few times. These backtracking issues are further compounded due to a complete lack of guidance or direction. Unless you're playing with a guide, which hampers exploration, you'll be left aimlessly wandering a lot of the time. Looking for that one path you missed is way more frustrating in doomblade than other MV's. Because those little paths forward are sometimes very small on the map, making it so you can easily glance past them. There's also a complete lack of markers on the map for anything other than the ones you place down yourself. And even those are limited to only 20 markers, not nearly enough to keep track of all the collectibles/paths. The final mayor annoyance related to backtracking is the absolutely terrible fast travel. Unlike most MV's with instant fast travel, doomblade has you ride void squids. This is cool in practice until you realize that to fast travel you first have to make your way to the nearest void gate, enter it with a lengty animation, then attack the void squid and ride it for an even lenghtier animation to a nearby point. What makes this even worse is that you can't directly travel to any point. It's like a subway traveling from station to station and making a stop at each one. So if you are in the bottom left of the map and want to go to the top right you first have to go to the void gate. Then ride EACH squid from the bottom all the way to the top. There you have to exit the void gate, again with a long animation. Do you see the issue with this? Getting anywhere takes you so long with this system & having to do it so many times makes the game last way longer than it has to. There's also just not enough of them, especially at the outer edges of the map. Ofcourse more travel points would also mean more stops, but if they solve that problem by allowing you to directly pick a destination then that also solves a lot of the backtracking issues.The level design on a whole is pretty mediocre. As cool as the levels can be sometimes, you don't have much time to appreciate them. Because you're busy flinging from enemy to enemy. You'll also have to do the same section many times not only due to backtracking but also due to an archaic save system which reverts your progress to the last save point when you die. You know, like those brutally unforgiving games of old? This has no place in a modern metroidvania, as all your exploration can be lost by accidentally bumping into damage too often. This happens a lot more than you think because the game is so fast paced it's easy to make mistakes. You start of with only 5 health and no way to heal. Some enemies drop health but this is very inconsistent, often not worth the risk of taking more damage. With save points being your only consistent way of healing, you often have to backtrack to the latest point to save your incremental bits of progress. This adds yet another amount of backtracking in this already backtracking heavy game. I really just wanted the game to be over but it kept going.What also kept going (up) was the difficulty. Later sections became tremendously hard & finnicky with more ways to take chip damage but still requiring you to keep a pace to avoid as much damage. Maybe if your brain goes 300 fps this game is easy to you, but i assume most normal people will sometimes struggle dodging all damage with such fast movement. This happens during gauntlets which push you to your limits, but due to a large amount of enemies to zip between these are actually quite fun. However for bosses it's quite different as this game has some of the most finnicky & annoying ones i've ever beaten. Early bosses are fun but the later ones, especially the cyber sentinel, slime cubes and final boss really had me gritting my teeth. Some were too hard to take on at that time so what did i have to do to even the odds? That's right backtrack for some upgrades, AGAIN. For example there's a boss that takes place in a room with poisonous gas, and you can miss the immunity upgrade before stumbling into their cave. Even with the upgrades i still had a hard time with some of them. Even when you understand their mechanics they are quite chaotic so you will fail often before you get them down.If and when you die, you have to sit through a lenghty death animation and an even lenghtier loading screen. In fact the whole game is plagued with them. Initial loading times are long, and it uses the same art every time. No flavor text or hints at all. Just a screen you'll soon grow tired off. The issues with this game are more fundamental than they are technical, but there's also many performance issues. Especially in the larger rooms with many enemies the game can drop as much as 20 fps trying to simulate all of it. I had no crashes though, and no major bugs. Then there's story, writing and characters, which are all stereotypical & one dimensional. The NPC's are either cruel bad guys, innocent bystanders or outright idiots that do a poor attempt at comedy. The overal writing is very poor, and the translation is rough. The visuals then range from beautiful to ugly. The background assets are placed without thought, especially the mechanical level. These levels feels cluttered, only the forest levels looked good because of this, like a dense jungle. There's also just too much red in the game, it really hurts the eyes after a while and is monotenous. Luckily the amazing soundtrack isn't. If there's anything the game deserves praise for it's the kickass music. Dashing acros the screen slicing demons with chuggy riffs is quite cathartic and the game is actually tons of fun at the start before all the backtracking & difficulty spikes. If you don't plan on completing doomblade it's a fair recommendation, but if you're a completionist like me then the game will wear out its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the metroidvania formula, this game is a slam dunk. Just enough tweaks to make it different and interesting, while delivering on all the things you want/expect. TL;DR - if you like Hollow Knight, Ori, Grime, Ender Lilies, get in here and have a great time.Awesomeness:- Combat - really enjoyed the combat, fast paced chaining mechanic. at first i thought it might be a bit button mashy, but it turned out to be really skill intensive the further you go into the game. some really nice boss and enemy designs too. - Upgrades & Abilities - a good consistent flow of new abilities that unlock new areas. the abilities themselves aren't all totally novel, but they are done nicely within the world that the game sets up- Secrets & Exploration - a great balance of providing enough breadcrumbs to get you to the right place, but not holding your hand too much. a big map that is fun to traverse especially with some of the mechanics they introduce.- Difficulty - thought it was a really good scaling all the way through. a few boss battles that were real tests and made me much better at the rest of the game once i figured out how to get through- Lore - weaved into the world nicely to give you that story element while not interrupting gameplay with long cut scenes- Music - rocks. - Art Style - great.Areas for Improvement:- Played with a controller - as has been mentioned, this could be frustrating at times but was able to make it work, definitely needed to be a little more thoughtful with some things than i imagine you'd need to be on mouse and keyboard.- Map - there have already been some improvements with marking things on the map, i would have appreciated something marks collectibles on the map (or even general vicinity / area of where to find items) at the end once the game is beaten so i could more easily 100% things. don't think i'm going to slog through without this.- General quality of life -  i did find it a little frustrating that if you discover areas on the map and die before saving, it resets everything. felt it was unnecessarily harsh in a way that was more frustrating and led to me saving more often.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOMBLADE

_childDocuments_.review: Great metroidvania, with a really unique movement/combat mechanic that feels fresh and satisfying to use. Had a really good time fighting all the bosses, each one with a unique combat style and an epic OST, and exploring all of the map that has biomes with a lot of variation, from a lush underground to a mechanical facility. My main complaints about the game are more on the quality of life side, as I think the game would benefit from having more map markers, for completionists that wish to 100% the game (I reached 96% completion and it´s taking me some time to get the other 4%) , faster loading screens, with maybe a phrase with tips or lore, just to make the waiting when you die a bit more tolerable and an auto-save mechanic whenever you defeat a boss or gain a new ability. Apart from these the game doesn´t really do anything wrong, though I wish it was longer, although it tells it´s story perfectly in the span of the game. Hopefully more people pick up this game, really great hidden gem in the metroidvania genre, defininely one of my new favourites games.
