_childDocuments_.review: This review is going to be contradictory. I liked it, but it's not a good game.Harold Halibut (HH) puts you in the role of Harold, a docile man who does what everyone tells him to. He lives on the Fedora, a crashed spaceship in an alien ocean, and his life is turned upside down when he meets and befriends an alien.Presentation-wise, Harold Halibut is spectacular. The art style is exactly like stop-motion clay figures, and the detail of each area and person runs deep. There's some beautiful scenes that had me in awe. There's also a lot of worldbuilding in the story and environment that captivates, despite the dreary and isolating world they live in.Audio is relatively decent. Lots of good music choices, the voice acting is solid, and the sound design has that feeling of deep.The story was alright, lots of highs and lows (will get into this in a sec).Yes, if HH was a TV show or movie, it would be lauded as amazing.As a game? Meh.Any time I had to take control, I got annoyed. Whether it's the incredibly simple puzzles, the constant busywork, or the long swathes of slow walking through nothing, HH takes the most boring parts of any game and adds them to terrible effect. It took me 8 hours to beat the game, and I reckon more than half of that was walking/running from one place to the next. There's only so many times I can run through the lab corridors before I get sick of it!Potential story spoilers here!Whilst the story was mostly good, I was a bit bummed by some of it. Overall, if I close my eyes and ignore the game part of this, HH is a great story presented well. But, be prepared for some tedious gameplay!
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY wanted to like this game. I'm a sucker for stop-motion and strange storytelling, but this was just tedious. Beautiful art design and music, but totally uninteresting dialogue, characters and plot. Characters are unique and eccentric to be sure, like any good stop-motion thing should be, but they're just not likable or interesting.I hate to leave a negative review and feel about about a potential negative impact on developers...but be warned: I couldn't care enough to finish the game. Very bummed.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, for the most part that is. I wish there was a yes button, with caveats. Firstly, this is very much a visual novel type game. If you're not interested in a game where you're mainly walking around and talking to people, it's not your kind of game! And that's totally okay. I really loved most of the conversations. There's interactions between characters that are so wonderful and charming, and really helped me the past few days. I've been very sick, so it was nice for me. I honestly feel like the ending....kind of ruined it for me? I wish we had the ability to make a choice for Harold. ((Don't read below this if you haven't yet played/finished the game))The ending didn't really align with how I was playing Harold- reading all the messages about how much people were concerned about him, meeting everyone before the launch, it made me excited for Harold to really step into his own. Even the walking sequence- it felt beautiful and bittersweet, but nice. The ending on the other hand....was so sad. Like not in a good way, in a 'why did I ever connect to all these people and make such meaningful relationships if the game was going to make the decision for me' bad. I get it, as a fellow artist, you have a vision. But I still would have liked to have stayed with my human community. So! Play the game, and like me....pretend the last ten minutes of the game doesn't exist. Still would recommend for a good weekend/dreary day game. But just be aware of that ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very well made. You can tell they put a lot of time and energy into it. I truly enjoyed every minute of it.However, I feel that the developers may have cut some corners and I would have liked to see more of some things. There were not enough interactive puzzle-like elements. I realized that since the developers put so much effort and time into the handmade props and scenes, they may have neglected more of the interactive elements. Further, some parts of the ship were un-explorable. We did not see the Restricted VIP area, which made me a bit sad. The candle-like tube system could have been made into a sanctuary or church instead of left blank. I also felt that I spent so much time in the same areas that they started to feel bored and repetitive after a while. I think that the developers could have added more in the social area of the ship. I did notice that some of the buttons in the tube system did not have anything on them, which I feel could have been utilized as other areas to explore.Overall, the game has a rich story, and the characters are really fun to get to know. However, the developers could have added more puzzles, inventory-type tasks, and other areas to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, hand-crafted slow burn. This game is definitely not for everyone; unlike other point-and-click adventures, there isn't anything to 'solve' or 'figure out,' it's more of an interactive slice-of-life abroad a fantastical setting. But if you love thoughtful, meditative games where every moment, big and small, is meant to be savored, then Harold Halibut is just a lovely experience. I will miss my time on the Fedora.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: It's like playing an arthouse movie with clay-motion! I have a lot of love for this game. It's slow-paced, dialogue-heavy and immersive in the best way. The story, the quirky characters and the art style of the game are amazing. Plus, the soundtrack includes a song by Hildegard Knef. Iconic.Also, a contribution to the dark forest hypothesis! Maybe aliens are just too relaxed, distracted by reading jelly and anti-materialistic to bother with the human species.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: The passion of the creators shines through in many aspects of Harold Halibut. The visuals are beautiful, the music well chosen, the characters are well drawn and you are encouraged to care about them. The story has a nice arc and you see the changes in the main character and their relationships.However, this is not really a game. At best it could be described as a walking simulator. Harold is given a task, which is usually walk to a location and talk to someone. The dialogue is really just cut scenes, with some very minor and non-impactful choices. There are a few mini-games (e.g. a tetris room packing mini-game), but they are not well designed and don't provide any challenge.The game this most makes me think about is The Artful Escape, but in that game you do have some level of control over your character and the musical game sequences are more involved and interesting to play. Furthermore this is far too long, with too many long sequences of walking. It took me 3x longer to play through this than The Artful Escape, which is too long for a purely narrative experience.I would recommend people who are interested in an emotional narrative experience play Harold Halibut. But if you need gameplay - I would avoid.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It is very slow paced, but that is what makes it so enjoyable. The characters and bits of dialogue are quite funny, Chris especially. Make sure you learn how to run. I finished the first half without realizing Harold could run and it took me ages because the ship is very big and you will be going back and forth frequently.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game is a work of art; it looks so good. Even the camera movements are wonderful, along with the details, textures, and materials. It's so lovely and unique. I especially liked the little TV ads.I'm used to games with minimal gameplay, but I just felt like there was a pacing issue. The first few hours turn out to be very slow and repetitive, almost to the point of wanting to ditch the game. Then the middle of the story picks up, but the ending is a bunch of cutscenes and exposition with unnecessary technical explanations from characters.Also, the writing felt a little dumbed down and aimed at kids, though I understand the desire to appeal to a broad audience.Still, it's mesmerizing to be in this universe and enjoy such creation, beautiful original music. Very worth it, and I hope more creations like these will happen.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: For me this is simply the most decelerating game, i've ever played. If you're looking for a relaxing and refreshing kind of game, with a lovely art of course, then this might be worth a try. The stop motion technology is lovely in every way. The "world" and characters are so well made, it's just fun to watch them.Forget the time, sit back and take a deep dive into this...Performance Update:On PC (7900xtx / 7800x3d) absolutely flawless.On Steam Deck, i've tried a few different configurations. Funny thing, it works way better without any upscaling technology active. On medium settings you're getting about 40-60 fps most of the time. It's okay for this kind of game, but i'm sure a few patches later, it will run maybe a bit better...
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: God, this game is like a warm hug. The theming, the message, the music, the visuals, it all feels so healthy to experience.Some people don’t like this game because they think the main character is boring, but that is quite literally the point. He’s just a regular Joe like us that gets his life turned upside down and makes very important realizations throughout the story. He grows more into himself and I think that’s something we all worry about at one point or another. Harold is so sweet and so relatable.This game is a slow-burner, but man it’s so worth it. 100% Achievement Completion Perspective:The game creates a save file for each section, so all achievements are easily obtainable and all worth getting since most achievements revolve around delving into conversation with those around Harold, learning more about everyone’s lives.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much. I played 13 hours in two days because I was just hooked. I refuse to talk about it because everyone should just experience it. Go into it blind, you'll be glad you did. I mainly bought this because I loved the way it looked. The stop motion look is always great. The artwork is beautiful, the story is great, overall 10/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully-made art-house movie in the form of a visual novel/walking simulator. (But not nearly as pretentious as that makes it sound.) The graphics and music speak for themselves in the trailer, but also the gameplay mechanics shift in cinematic ways at various points, changing perspective or control scheme to communicate Harold's state of mind in similar ways that a film might use camera angles and editing techniques.Every character you meet manages to be likeable and relatable, and the mundane tasks and situations you navigate through manage to add up to philosophical pondering on topics like friendship and loneliness, boredom and ambition, community and belonging, all presented with warmth and humour and often surprising twists.Recommended for any gamer who likes gently-whimsical cerebral cinema. Just don't come expecting puzzles to solve or challenges to beat.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: After spending too much time on this game, I have come to the conclusion that I very much dislike it. As much as I really want to like it. I came in with high expectation with the trailers and the wonderful art style that is actually really good.Harold Halibut manages to make me frustrated with the writing at every single turn, and the worst part is that a lot of the story arcs were really REALLY close to being good but they either face plant the landing, or it's executed so poorly that it turns into a half hour of going back and forth for a quest and the reveal of the conclusion to be actually not a big deal and we didn't need to spend the last half hour running all over the Fedora.Another thing that makes me frustrated is that Harold is treated like a doormat for over half the game. I understand that near the end of the game,  But this comes wayyy too late to matter because the end of the game happens and it actually just doesn't matter because we do not see the outcome of this. I also just hate the ending. What a way to ruin a perfectly good bittersweet moment.And finally, I cant believe journal doodles are not stored between chapter select when there's literally an achievement for completing the journal and there are missable doodles. Meaning if you miss even one doodle, you need to start the game again from that point. Even if you miss one in chapter 1.This is was made especially frustrating when you take into consideration that this was acknowledged on April of 2024(year of review) several months ago and then completely ignored thereafter. Here is the steam discussion page in question: All in all, this game was made with the 3D models first, and the actual game itself is an afterthought. I saw another review saying it should have just been a movie, and I think I completely agree with that sentiment.I don't want this game to be bad either. I wanted it to be good and a pleasant story with good characters and colorful writing.It just makes me feel sad, honestly.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Well it is quite nice game to play but unfortunately it wasn't that thrilling to do i kinda felt sleepy in many parts of the game the game is very slow based and kinda boring ngl i enjoyed buddy's part enjoyed the scenery enjoyed the music and enjoyed the art however overall this game deserve 5.5/10 for me
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know exactly what I was expecting with this game, but one thing is for sure, the stop-motion styled animations, hand-crafted props, and overall design was very enticing. It felt like I was experiencing the combination of Laika Studios and Wes Anderson come to life in the unfolding story of Harold and his mundane life. The game itself was more about going from location to location, talking to other crew-members and delivering information, and completing simple tasks for anyone that requested it, but the level of design, quirky conversations, and funny hand-drawn pictures are some of the real charming qualities to admire here. Don't even get me started on the outstanding soundtrack too!The story gets very interesting in chapter 3 (Ch 5 was one hell of a ride), and especially from there starts to take unexpected turns. With every major event that happened and unfolded, I was always eager to see what might happen next.Aside from carrying around a tool-belt, there's actually no inventory or anything to collect, and unfortunately a lack of objects to interact with, that is besides quest markers and NPC dialogues of course. It was unfortunate since everything looked so intriguing and I just wanted to fiddle with everything I saw. I don't think any of that hindered my enjoyment though and still enjoyed all that was offered to me in this game (although having stuff to interact with would have still been nice).Along the journey, I found a few wonky animations  here and there, but this game looked so incredible and so much effort was put into it, and truly was a blast to experience. I do hope to see more indie titles like Harold Halibut make a rise to the top.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Looking at the screenshots and trailer for this game you would never guess how deeply disappointing it is. The premise is interesting, the art style is beautiful, but the story and characters have no dimension.Every single time things are about to get interesting (Harold having to walk home drunk or Harold having an "experience" from the drink Weewoo gives him or Harold asking about the alien technology) the player is treated either to a black fade away, the scene is quickly abandoned, or you get a "well that's too complicated to explain" cop-out from the writers. All the characters in this game hate you, Harold. You are constantly being yelled at for being a "dumb delinquent" when there are no actions by Harold to substantiate this. I have a theory that maybe Harold is supposed to be autistic, or neurodivergent in some way, and this is why you are abused and manipulated the entire game. Not exactly feel good or cozy. Cyrus tricking you into shocking yourself for entertainment was the point where I began hate-playing this game cause it was too late to get a refund.The characters are so mean and dull and inconsistent it was maddening. Buddy the mailman goes on and on about being a rule follower but then finds a loophole in the bureaucracy to read peoples private letters instead of finding a way to deliver them, but then just gives them to Harold to deliver after he suddenly, and without any foreshadowing, kicks the bucket. What was the point of any of it? That's what you'll find with many of the “tasks” given to Harold. You need to check on someone? They just tell you to go away in so many words. Need to teach the alien our language? Well the professor is just going to whip out a translation device right after you waste your time on the fetch quest for the book to teach with.Harold has a musical scene where he wishes for “more to this life” and then laments before bed that he hopes things get calm and boring again. Wtf? Weewoo is presented as an adventurous member of their species yet never shows curiosity for anything other than what is required by the ramshackle plot. No one ever has an interior moment where we get to empathize or understand how they feel about anything other than surface level gobbledegook you'd expect from a friends first time on shrooms. None of it made any connections to past plot points or character development. Just surface level snake oil.I am so mad at this game for not taking the time to make me care about anything or anyone in it after obviously spending so much time on its looks.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: This is a difficult entry to downvote.  It was clearly made with a lot of love and it nails what it seems to be going for.  Unfortunately, what it’s going for is not a game.  It’s a 2D walking simulator with slow walking and a lot of backtracking.  I’ve been known to enjoy a walking simulator but they tended to be first person.  Side scrollers are just not immersive and one has to make up for it by engaging the player with the likes of puzzles and just any kind of challenge.  This title has none of that.  It also features very slow walking thru rather few (admittedly handcrafted) environments.  Decent writing and acting only takes one so far.  There’s a reason movies are rarely longer than 2 hours.  Once I had my fill of atmosphere, which did not take long, I came back once more hoping against hope that the game would pick up.  It did not.  I then read a few reviews and found that it’s not going to.  I doubt I’m coming back.  It’s a bummer because there is a lot of talent here.  Just no game.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it.Upfront: One should go in with the fitting expectations. If one goes in expecting in depth point and click adventure gameplay, or focus on gameplay at all, one could be disappointed.That’s because this does not focus on gameplay at all, the gameplay aspect is mostly like a walking sim or most simple fetch quests mostly.This focuses on a lot of other things. The graphics are amazing. But not (just) amazing in terms of, oh, see, this is all the latest graphics api features using terms(though it has excellent lighting and is also sorta state of the art in combining claymation with realtime 3D in very well done way i’d say), but rather beautiful art direction on a level of attention to detail very few games or any media achieves or even attempts to strive for.There is world and story building right from the first second and it moves one to a strangely calm, comfy and yet in a way sad almost melancholic world of a small civilization stranded under water on an alien planet.I feel like it is a metaphor for our times where people (try to) live a normal daily mundane routines fullfilling life despite many things around us are meanwhile totally insane in more than one way.Spoilers, but since that’s unveiled pretty early on: Mankind on Earth was thought to be close to an extinction level event and so a small group was sent outerspace to have a new civilization of mankind somewhere else. Sadly the place they ended up in seemed un inhibitable on the surface and/or their spaceship sunk and now they have their underwater colony.One should not expect (fast paced) action and one should be in the mood to engulf oneself in a strangely fascinating world, mostly experienced by talking to a bunch of characters in dialogs while walking forth and back a bunch.The experience totally takes it’s time, some dialogs can feel (almost) overly longwinded sometimes.But then once in a while there i some really thought provoking or really touching stuff that to me made it all quite worth it.That may sound and actually be boring to some, to me it is something refreshing and amazing.I played so many games over the years and many are focused on a tight gameplay loop which balances dopamin and punishment kicks as addictive way to pass time.(which can be totally cool, too)In Harold Halibut i felt like instead i’m really accepting to experience that unique scenario of that group which lives there under water on an alien planet outpost and spend a few hours a day there, seemingly do mundane tasks which lead to strange plot aspects over time.it’s slow in buildup but also moving to some interesting unexpected places in story over time.Overall i’m rating this more as an outstanding artistic achievment than a regular game.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Harold Halibut is a delightful game with its unique stop-motion art style and captivating soundtrack. The visuals and character designs are meticulously crafted, creating an immersive world. However, the long walking sequences for minor tasks with NPCs can be a bit tiring. Additionally, I found the ending disappointing and felt it could have been better executed. Overall, it's a charming experience, with a few drawbacks.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Harold Halibut is a masterpiece.If you have the slightest interest in character driven story telling then you have to chek out this game.Okay, there´s not a lot of gameplay here, except talking to characters and running from location to location. But over the course of the game i grew so attached to Harold, I wanted to see him succeed. I just finished the game and it´s such a beautiful story, I cried like a baby. This game made me happy.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this game, it is great looking at first glance, stop-motion like technique is well made, but ; the game features a main character which is dumb as a brick. Whenever an interesting conversation occurs - which is very rare in this game - Harold says he is bored and skips the conversation. Otherwise most of the dialogues feels like written by chatgpt or some ai. Endless and pointless conversations all-over the game.   Also the game design is unfortunately garbage , during the game you will always have to make rounds for poorly written quest lines. I.e. you should deliver some letters to the npcs in one quest, but you have to go back every time you deliver one single little letter because our dumb harold doesn't think he can carry more than one letter.   And while doing these reroutes there is a stupid tube system, which is necessary to change areas, while using these tubes you have to wait around 1 min. every time you use that tubes which you have to use excessively. The game could have been so much better, it had the potential , the idea is fine but they served it poorly in all possible ways, it could be fun if it was a 1h long stop-motion movie , but as a game for 15+ hours it is just boring and repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: A simple, vvvvv slow-paced game, with some puzzles and dialogue choices to choose from. Fair warning to all, the game is really slow, and I almost gave up in the first chapter BUT stick it out - I found getting myself comfy, and cozy to help in combating the slowness of the game, placed me in a mindset of chill. The dialogue choices do not affect the outcome of the game or scene, so no alternative endings - game is linear. At times, I honestly hated some of the characters due to the way they spoke to Harold, soooo RUDE just because Harold is "just a handyman", wish that I could choose to say something snarky back but I admit, Harold can be quite oblivious @.@ Visuals: I love love love anything stop-motion and that was the main reason why I bought this game. Unfortunately, I do find that the 3D elements of stop-motion is lost in certain aspects of game and wonder if it is a worthy style to pursue in the context of a game. For eg, the characters appear flattened sometimes, which defeats the purpose of using stop-motions. HOWEVER, I was enthralled by the sets. They were so beautiful (like Agora Arcades and Utility District) and I wish it was bigger so that I can explore more (was desperately hoping to see the Art and (a functioning) Agriculture district, that would have been so neat!), but alas, the limits of stop-motion sets.Achievements: If you are a completionist (like me), it will be good to spend some time looking through guides - wish I found out sooner to do this. Also, be sure to refer to a few to cross check reliability. One of the hardest achievements requires a complete notebook, so you will need to talk to the characters often to obtain these notes. The only achievement I did not manage to obtain is "Busybody", annoys the heck out of me T^T. It requires Harold to carry out certain activities across several chapters which made it difficult to go back to game saves at the specific chapters after finishing the game. I found out the achievements that are to be carried out all in one chapter were obtainable after finishing the game - so those are not as tricky.Overall, I still love the game, but would try to get everything in one try as the pacing is sooo slow - HOLD the (square) button on your controller to sprint!! It is not for everyone, but give it a shot - you may like it!
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Harold Halibut is an amazing wholesome game with an impressive art-style and story. The dedication to making this game by hand (modeled and recorded in stop motion I believe) is admirable, and the developers did a fantastic job.As some others have said, the game is quite tedious with a lot of running back and forth to complete tasks or talk to people, of which can be pretty lengthy if you add it all up. That being said, at time of this review I have 25.7hrs on record and have just finished the game - however I did go through this game at quite a slow pace as I wanted to get all of the dialogues (and I probably had it paused occasionally for over 30 minutes).On other positive notes, everyone you encounter in the game is authentic and it really sells the world as being lived-in, and the music is unique and matches the ambience the game gives off.Having finished the story, it honestly reminds me a tiny bit of the 'uniqueness' that Hideo Kojima's games have (Death Stranding in this case), in that one of the focuses of the game for me was around the aspect of connecting with people. Harold himself is a lonely man with no real hopes or dreams, and his personality is just quite bland overall - but throughout the game he really grows on you, and you do start to see him developing and growing more as a person. While I can't directly relate to Harold, I still definitely felt some connection between myself and him.There's two main negatives I have regarding the game, of which the last is a bit of a spoiler (no specifics):All in all, I would highly recommend the game to anyone who enjoys an immersive story-telling experience and doesn't mind the slow pace of the game. I certainly enjoyed my time with the game and it was especially nice to play while I've been ill for the last week.

Those that say this is just a movie....  yeah, it essentially is.  I didn't think that I'd so enjoy a "game" with no inventory and no decision making. _childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Harold Halibut is an incredible experience both visually and in narrative, the first chapter is amazing and truly establishes the charm of the Fedora and its inhabitants, and I really wish we had more tender moments with them like with Buddy the ships courier and mailman.But despite this the game does an amazing job at making the characters feel like people.Harold especially and his woes and feelings of social isolation and unhappiness with his monotonous life were some I deeply identified with.While the first chapter of the game is great, but the further chapters is when the game slowly but surely becomes noticeably rushed.and especially with the Fumylm, we are introduced to their culture briefly and don't engage with them in the same manner as the inhabitants of the Fedora.further negatives is how much walking has to be done from place to place, while I accepted at the start, it began to wear on me by the 10 hour mark.The puzzles I can't exactly call puzzles either, they're more so just chores and while charming at first with how straight they're played I often wished for one that were more engaging.And finally how quickly and anti-climactically the main conflict of the Fedora is resolved really left me wishing for something more.But in all honesty despite all this the game was an incredible experience for me that I can recommend if you've got time to burn.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: If your looking for a game to sit back and take it easy with and  just enjoy some story. This game is for you. With its slow pace and mix of linear and exploratory game-play Harold Halibut is a heart-filled and emotional journey. This story make me think and ponder and sometimes in today's gaming landscape it seems speed and a desire to hold attention is what is valued more than actual story telling. This game let me unwind and just enjoy the adventure and life of Harold. I cried, laughed and was angry in all aspects and story beats of this game. I really love that these type of games are still being made and allow people to reflect on themselves whilst also enjoying a fantastical story that explores many themes of life. Keep it up Slow bros. Excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals and art direction of this game are astounding and maintain a very high standard all throughout, not unlike many stop motion animation movies. The humour and tone are found in every little detail and fit perfectly with the writing and characters, which are are quirky and endearing in their very own way.Sadly, it is difficult to overlook the lack of imagination driving most of the gameplay. Even keeping in mind that we are taking the role of a bored underachiever, the repetitive nature of the fetch quests often felt like a mean to put some distance and context between the numerous, and sometimes lengthy dialog cutscenes.Although I can appreciate a game that favors being inclusive of as many players as possible - rather than introducing pointless difficulty - I could not help but find a ton of missed opportunities that could have better leveraged the beautifully crafted environments and made players look around and make sense of their surrounding, like finding leaks or faulty air ducts in X area, look for evidences of [some event]. It felt, generally, a little too scripted.Despite all that, this is still an amazing game and I would recommend for the story, writing, art direction, and visuals. If you can take the many A to B back and forths.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Chicken Run and Wallace and Gromit growing up, so naturally as an adult I also love Harold Halibut which takes similar styles of animation and makes it into a video game. Turns out? It's quite good! Excellent voice acting across the board, superb writing, and a lovely story. I enjoyed this game muchly and my only real nitpick is wishing Harold would speed it up sometimes or there were quicker ways to get certain missions done, but these are real nitpicks. Lovely game, go and buy it or play it on Gamepass!
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: This is such an evocative and wholesome game with a great narrative. Lots of "if Wes Anderson made a video game" comments, but this game stands on its own. It's incredibly unique and a breath of fresh air.   (Gameplay) It's really an engrossing game with lots of stunning visuals. The lack of any typical gameplay elements didn't throw me, it definitely doesn't feel like a point and click. The decisions you make in the game probably aren't making much of a difference, but it always feels important. You assume the role of the protagonist, Harold. The control that you have by walking around the Fedora I, learning about the Fedorans and completing missions is quite fun and serves the narrative.   (Themes) If there is one theme that stuck out to me here;   There is this innate desire to leave something behind and consistently learn and grow as a species, yet we struggle with meaning and finding happiness. There is always something not yet attained (An absurd tide in which we seldom ask, 'to what end?').   These existential/ introspective themes are explored here in Harold Halibut. Not directly telling the audience to think a certain way, but it explores the idea that maybe we don't need to be in a rush to find happiness, nor do we have to have a clear-cut meaning.     Also, really enjoy the tunes: Hildegard Knef - Im achtzigsten Stockwerk, Mehmet Celal - Bella Çav, BADBADNOTGOOD - Time Moves Slow   I think this game is a triumph. It's got lots of bluglglgl

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not good at writing reviews, but I felt I needed to write one for this. I had the same experience with this game as with Unravel. While I was playing, I felt that this game was made by a small but passionate team with unique ideas and a lot of effort. I just need to mention the fact that everything in the game was created in real life (characters, objects, even the places), and they 3D scanned it afterward. This gives the whole game a unique look. I'm sure that not everyone will like the gameplay, though, because it mostly includes walking and talking, but I don't mind it at all. I think the walking part is needed to understand Harold better and see his point of view, but that's just my opinion.In conclusion, I would 100% recommend this game if you are looking for a relaxing, story-telling game where you can explore at your own pace.

The writing is incredible and I feel the way it explores characters and the two cultures of the people living on the ship and the flumylym in the cave, both strange and almost insular in their own rights, went over a lot of players heads. _childDocuments_.review: Had to write within the refund window. I'm about an hour in and nothing engaging, interesting, fun, funny, or really anything has happened at all.. I'm just walking back and forth helping a few people with menial tasks, there hasn't even been a clear advancement of an overarching story...all of the dialogue is short, quick answers with nothing really interesting being mentioned, it's like talking to a stranger at the gas station for a few moments, you forget about it within momentsThe art is great, you'll have to get over some totally goofy animations (like using stairs) but that's part of the charm I guess?There are frame drops, fairly regularly, it always seems to be during transition cutscenes so it doesn't really hinder gameplay, it does take you out of the zone though. My machine is way above what it takes to run "high", or it should be.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: 15 hours or more 2/10 1 Yes, I used  and  No Unsure yet No No No even the opposite, to play the game in a relaxing way because there is an achievement for playing the game for 15 hours (in-game time)  No No No difficulty setting Yes, 1 or 2 achievements are broken atm, the developers are aware of those and are working on them. Woah this game blew me away. 15+ hours watching the artwork and I'm still in awe because of how wonderful it looks, and how much effort was put into the details. How the lights are done, and how the people on the ship live their lives. They don't stand still when they are in the background. For example, in the coffee shop, you see people talking, even when just passing by the window. Or when you pass by the classroom where a boy is sitting alone, he will interact with you through the window and show you a sign if you give it a few seconds to stand still. Shops that are indeed closed if their owner is somewhere else at that moment. So many small details but they make the world not just a normal game world but lively and a joy to explore. You will get to know the people and their lives and struggles. Furthermore, there was not only so much detail in the artwork but also in the music and the voice acting. So many times it just felt right! And while that may seem normal, it is also such a wonderful thing that makes this game come to life. The story was exciting, you get enough background in the beginning to understand enough of how the world you just got dropped into as a player works. You instantly have questions on how things are done and why.  What I also enjoyed was that some chapters were quite open, with lots of tasks to do, and people to meet, which was followed by a more linear chapter, and the world would open up again in the next. How you go through different chapter structures felt just right and would make you appreciate the other style just as much. The only thing I struggle with is the walking speed. You will walk a lot from one place to the other and while the walking speed allows you to see all the details at first, for me it became a bit boring and gave my mind room to wander of. However, I'm well aware that this is a "me problem" and the reason I normally play a bit more action kinda games is because I know my mind will wander off otherwise. At this moment 1 (or maybe 2) achievements are broken. The one for filling up the sketchbook and the one about playing for 15 hours seems a bit off. The developers are aware of the sketchbook achievement and are working on a fix. I'm unsure if any of them will end up missable. There is a system in place that you can reload a subparagraph, but at this moment when you do that, you will lose sketchbook entries. I'm not sure if that is part of the bug. 3 achievements have actions continuing throughout the story, the sketchbook has many many actions, but the storyline with Buddy is a daily task and there is also the one where you listen to all the different dialog of the 2 people in the coffee shop. I'm unsure if you could still unlock those by going back to the section you missed and playing that one again. Most of the achievements will be unlocked by just playing through the game or by going back to a specific section and unlocking it that way if you missed it in your first playthrough. I give Harold Halibut 4.5 out of 5 stars.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: While the art and story seemed amazing, at the end of the day it's still a walking simulator... and justifying paying $35.00 for such game is a bit of stretch. It's still quite buggy, and lots of times where I had to reload the game. I enjoyed it yes, but for the game-play and content, its simply not worth $35 in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is stunning, it's breathtaking and I have been so excited for its release. I think the devs have done such an amazing job and it's refreshing to see a game on release run this smoothly. However, the dialogue leaves a lot to be desired. The joy of adventure games is how much humour they manage to achieve within character interactions but I find Harold just uninterested and it makes me uninterested. When the dialogue is aiming for humorous the delivery doesn't match it and it's a real shame. I wish there were more fun little interactions to be had, I wanted to chew up the scenery but there were very few opportunities to do so, and maybe there is later in the game but I personally couldn't see myself playing it any further. I wanted to like it and I'm so happy this game exists, but it's not for me sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: The most quirky game I’ve played in years. It is also very warm and calm. There are no explosions, no big drama, it seems like the authors deliberately make their world as cosy as it can be so that the characters with all their uncountable eccentricities have some safe space to live. This feeling is very unique and I love when games or movies present to me something which cannot be replicated.That being said, it is certainly not for anyone. It can easily become weary. I found it best to play in smaller portions so that it made me relaxed after a whole day.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Couldn't get past the 1st hour - I really wanted to like this game, love the art style and the world building - but Harold starts out bored of his life, and as a player I have a hard time feeling invested in a game when the main character (whos supposed to be my eyes in the world) seems bored of all the interesting things I'm seeing.Plus, literally all the other characters are constantly passive aggressive towards him, and I kept thinking "just walk away, Harold! Say goodbye!" When im trapped in more and more abusive dialogue.Hopefully its setup for Harold's character arc, but I turned off the game after an hour of playing. The city Harold Halibut was set in was sooo cool and I just wanted to explore, but I felt like the game's narrative fought me trying to get me to sympathize with a character who hated his surroundings.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Very much way more story than game but an excellent and extremely fun story. Very British comedy, the craftsmanship behind the story, the sets and the characters is wonderful.Harold, a bit of a head in the clouds maintenance man, is your MC. Explore his growing connections across the ship, his own existential coming to terms with his own desires versus what others expect of him coupled with a incredible ending and adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: That's the vibe this game oozes. It is a charming, cozy, funny, and visually stunning experience.While some may not like it for the lack of gameplay elements and being narrative forward this kind of game tickles me in exactly the right spot. The gameplay is like many other reviews state, mostly walking from point A > B with the occasional small minigame. _childDocuments_.review: Positives:~ The visuals are STUNNING~ The story line is very thought-provoking at times, it discusses a more deeper, almost anthology like view into life, meaning and purpose.~ There are some twists and you think 'ohhhh' at times.~ The need to go everyday and check in with people to ensure you haven't missed a side quest or a hint of a job that might need doing is good.~ Its a slow burn, AND THAT'S OK!!!!~ The music score is also just as stunning and fits so well for a cosy gameKey points: ~ If you don't like slow burns - this isn't for you ~ Its designed to make you think, question and look at different opinions on how people see the world, their circumstance and what is important to them ~ If you want something guns blazing, mad adventure, always on the go - again, this isn't for you. ~ Its a beautiful game, that lightly touches on topics anyone with a thoughtful and curious mind would enjoy. ~ I played the full game in approx near 16hrs and i don't regret it one bit.I hope this helps someone out there who would like a slow, cosy game which have just the best amazing visuals using stock motion animation
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED this game the repeat schedule at the start does last a little too long but that's probably because i only did main quests and no side quests, but that feeling of seeing a weird alien thing come down the filter is just utterly shocking, after that the game gets even better the quests become a lot more interesting, then you go down the "crack" the best way to explain this is a cocaine happy land, you chase a FREAKING DRAGON. after that cocaine happy land. you have to relaunch and go back to space, but instead of leaving your alien friend you stay and see your family and everyone else disappear into space. the ending actually made me want to cry, I always knew we had to make the decision to leave the alien or stay with the alien, but actually having to leave your friends and family behind was extremely difficult to do. 10/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished HH yet, but I do love it so far. It's an endearing story about people. There's a subtle humor that probably escapes me most of the time (I take things too literally). The music is often very serene and well suited to the scenes.In many RPGs "fetch quests" feel demeaning and tedious. In this game the tasks are more than a MacGuffin. It feels like the main character is making a difference and developing a purpose. It's hard to say more without spoiling anything.Some events in the game seem strange canonically. I doubt that most people will notice them. Some words seem to be mispronounced; but that doesn't bother me, because people trip on their words in normal speech. What really gets me is that there are occasional typographical errors in the English closed captions. A diamond with smudges on it is no less a diamond.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great. Features a lot of dialogue and atmosphere. The voice acting is very good. It brings all of the characters to life. Graphically the game looks great as well. It ran smoothly for the most part. I haven't gotten too far in the story but I am intrigued enough to do so. _childDocuments_.review: Please, give this game a chance. This is one of the most beautiful, deep and artistic videogame adventures ever made. Its plot is naive and meaningful at the same time. Its artistic style is one of the best examples of stop-motion in the whole history of videogames, inspirational and pure. There might take place some speculations regards gameplay and monotony - I agree with that, but this exact moment when you feel like quitting - give this game a chance and it will pay off twice in the end. When people tell you "Watch it on YT" - give it a chance and buy it. It wil gift you experience you'll never get anywhere else. For developers I'd advise to add more mini-games in the middle of the game to dilute the routine (mini-games are quite tactile and make this world more palpable). Add more context to flumylym's everyday life, they seem like just standing there, not living. But all that is just a nit-picking. Score is fantastic! Give this game a chance and if you are disappointed - blame me because I'm repeating all those words of satisfaction and telling you again: please, give this game a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: The game is visually stunning and has a few just incredibly jaw dropping moments that left me in awe. If you like very dry humor and a more narrative story than game, this might be for you. It had some great lines, but I do wish there was a bit more of that humor. It has a pinch of Monkey Island and Wes Anderson, but don't let that over sell the game. The middle of the game did drag a bit, and definitely got fatigued by the back tracking back and forth fetch quests. Thankfully I stuck through it for some amazing almost movie like cinematic moments. There's a chapter before the end of the game that was great to experience. That's all I can say with no spoilers. Pacing would have been better if it was maybe a 6-7 hour game. Overall a visually stunning and cinematic composition masterpiece, with not much actual "game" to it, kinda dull story, but at times thought provoking. Not for everyone, but man it's pretty.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this! It's a very slow start, but it continued to grow on me as the game went on. Sad that it's over.Beautifully made, just a laid back relaxing stroll through an alternate universe. Very few decisions to make here aside from guiding the character to his next task and taking in the scenery as you do so.I think the story has a very satisfying ending, and I can appreciate all of the hard work that went into crafting the aesthetics!I do wish there were more interactive parts to make it feel more like a game, but nevertheless, it's a very impressive work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: A nice-looking game is a fine thing, and this game looks fantastic. That's really all I can say to its credit, because I played this thing for an hour and I did not encounter one single narrative hook, one single cool or interesting or lovable character, nor one single joke. What I got was stock dystopian world-building, a couple of fetch quests, weak dialogue, and a bunch of voice actors giving real *cold-reading lines with no context or meaning* energy.I believe that as long as you have good story and characters, your adventure game can look like dog vomit and still be great. I don't think it works the other way around.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game just because I always liked claymation and stop motion style films. Thumbs up for the developers. Very creative and refreshing to see in a game. Unfortunately, the game play seems like it was made for 10 year old kid. For the first 3+ hours, you just walking and backtracking. Doing the most mundane and repetitive tasks for different characters in the game.  Just when I thought something new finally happened, more backtracking and walking. There is a run button but more like a brisk walk than running. Certain part won't allow running at all. Don't get me wrong and I am not criticising the game developers here. It is a gorgeously detailed looking game. I have played similar linear style games such as Bramble, Little Nightmares,Inside and Trek to Yomi... All of which I truly enjoyed. Harold Halibut has such painfully repetitive,  slooow pace story telling game play that make it difficult to me stay interested in. I am already 10+ hours in. I will endure and see what happens at the end.....

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw the trailer for Harold Halibut, I knew it was going to be something special.  When I got to play first the demo and then the early chapters of the game, I thought that maybe the special-ness would be constrained to just the visuals, the vibe and its unique construction.  That would be fine though, not a lot of games reach the level of "something special" in any way.  Having finished the game now, I can definitely say, that is not the case.The back half of this game is so full of beautiful, emotionally impacting and surreally affecting moments it has become an instant classic for me.  As things change in and around the Fedora, and you meet more folks in the Fedora and beyond... I just really can't express how wonderful this game becomes.I've seen some middling takes on the game and I can understand the criticisms of the actual gameplay, which boils down to mostly fetch quests and wandering back and forth through the halls of the Fedora (especially in the first half or so of the game), there's little challenge, and the game takes its time, but when it gets where it's going it's so beautiful that the good outweighs the negatives so sharply it doesn't matter in the end.Thank you for giving us all this game Slow Bros.

_childDocuments_.review: Harold Halibut has an excellent story,  visual, and audio design. The strength and uniqueness of these aspects are enough for me to recommend it. This was a great experience to gradually play through.That said, this is more of an interactive movie than a game. That is perfectly fine, but you should know that is what you're getting into. It is a lot of long cutscenes with a mostly linear sequence of tasks in between. There is no strategy, risk/reward, or typical game mechanics as dictated by conventional game design wisdom. Through that lens, it would be said that the development effort was invested more on art and story design than gameplay design. Nevertheless, I think that the developers did an excellent job with what they were trying to do, and I would recommend giving it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: Should have just been a movie.I'm very disappointed that that is my major takeaway for this game knowing it took them something like 7 years to make, but ultimately that's what it feels like. I know it's is a narrative based game, but the amount of incredibly slow walking you have to do to get from one dialogue tree to another is unbearable in my opinion, and just ruins the whole experience of the game. Yes, the graphics are very well executed as that is what took 7 years to finish, however the voice acting is a little stunted and mid level. _childDocuments_.review: Good, It's a nice change from all  the killing and explosions and bright lights of a lot of games. So far the game is slow, (slow bros hah), BUT i think of it more as playing a book instead of a game. You get plenty of time to think about the world and its mysteries and possibilities. The art is REALLY interesting, it looks exactly like a stop motion show from TV in the 1900s (except at 200 HZ on a monitor not a CRT). I've only encountered one bug so far and i was able to solve it myself without reloading, but the game seems to autosave every time you change zones which is frequent so it's no problem to quit any time you need to. _childDocuments_.review: I'd reckon I'm about halfway through so I'm making this review. This game is cool, it's a good idea and I like the claymation everywhere.However, this game is S L O W. Not talking about the storyline, which is well paced, fun, and twisty and turny to keep it exciting while still singularly focused, but the actual playing of the game is like waiting for maple syrup to come out of a tree with your mouth open.The walking is traumatically slow, and they give you a run option which is a reasonable speed, but many "kind-of-cutscenes" have you follow an NPC manually with run turned off. They move faster than you.The run option speed is fine but you keep hitting into everything, turning around is molasses, and interacting with anything requires a 5-15 second waiting period before the person talks, or samples come down, or whatever.This reminds of me the abyssmalness of starfield where every time you took off or landed you lost some 10–30 seconds of your life; just wasted time that you can't control, and it makes the game feel like it's out of your control and you're barely even playing.It makes it exceptionally easy to get distracted, if every 100 seconds of playtime there's 10 seconds of downtime, it's hard to stay focused during those 10 seconds.That's compounded with the fact that you have to use tubes to get around between floors, each floor only having a few interactables (meaning you're taking that tube a LOT), and that tube has a long cutscene too.Anyway, I can tell a lot of work went into this game and it's pretty well scripted, especially the characters and character personalities. [Although, I am editing this to a "Would not recommend" after finishing it.] Please, though, devs, make the player go faster and the cutscenes/interactables happen quicker. There are other ways to slow down a game so the feeling of time can pass, but this is DEFINITELY top on the list for worst ways to do it..

_childDocuments_.review: A point & click adventure with a very unique, hand-crafted style about a man and his fish. In space (or rather, in an alien ocean).It took me about 12 hours to finish, a lot of that due to how slow the walking is and how long it takes to get between places.+ Bizarre characters and story.+ Decent voice acting.+ Gorgeous environments and visual/audio design.+ A lot of it feels highly detailed hand-crafted with excellent materials.- Performance is terrible on a lot of devices (especially Nvidia).- No mouse support... Which is just weird. Several puzzles would benefit from it.- No real challenge.- While gorgeously designed, it's very rough around the edges. Plenty of clipping, weird leg positions, animation glitches, skip dialogue getting stuck, etc.- It's very telling that 55% of people left the game before completing chapter 1, only 17% of people completed the game.- Pacing is kind of awkward and inconsistent. The routine into deviation is fine, but when things are exciting/time critical, we suddenly slow down and when things are irrelevant we speed up. It makes little sense.I don't want to hate on this. It's a work of art and a lot of love has gone into this.It would make for a great video series.As a game, however, I feel it is lacking and I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Visuals: 10/10Audio: 10/10Dialogue: 1/10 (Unless it's Buddy, Buddy's dialogue is 8/10.)Story: 2/10Gameplay: It's a walking sim, except it's the same handful of environments with little variety bar one. 2/10(as compared to other walking sims.)From a visual and an audio standpoint this game is exceptional, any time these parts of the game were accentuated were phenomenal. However, the game is extremely shallow. The dialogue is boring, the gameplay is boring, and the story is boring. Walking sims can be described as tedious, but as a fan of most walking sims I've played, this game is incredibly tedious. 99% of your time will be spent getting a mundane objective(i.e. "Harold, go talk to this person."), walking the exact same path you've walked 20 times prior, if not more, and then walking back. And your reward? Cheesy millennial writing that contributes nothing to the story. That is this game in a nutshell, stretched far too long for what it really is. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is one of my favorite movies that it is trying it's hardest, and unfortunately failing, to be a video game. This game has a wonderful, in-depth, and though-provoking story, yet it is told in such an unfortunate way. There are three main issues I got with the game - the aesthetics, the environments, and the gameplay. First, for the most part the aesthetics are simply breathtaking. The scene where Harold first discovers the alien hiding in the filtration tank is something I will never forget; I truly felt as though I was in that moment with him. The music is beautiful, the animation is jaw-dropping, and for the most part it truly feels as though you are in the Fedora alongside Harold. Yet, despite all the beauty, some parts of the game feel so overlooked! The entire text that the subtitles and HUD (when it is present) is in is so elementary and uninspired in comparison to the rest of the game. They even already have better font with the listing of days that is present everytime you sleep, so why didn't they just use that?? It just feels so little, but I had to stop playing with subtitles as it just felt so immersion breaking. There are also just little things that make the game feel unfinished and strange. In the central station, if you zoom in by pressing E on any people sleeping on the bench, their eyes are a soulless white. This was funny at first, but like cmon man for real? You put so much effort into making this game so beautiful and then the slip ups are so tiny but so numerous and constant. Its like if you made an amazing apple pie and then you just like put vegemite all over it - what are you doing????The environments feel so underdeveloped in a way that makes this game feel unengaging and puzzling. This game takes place on a ship with a nominal chunk of the human race, it was on a massive ship with its own power plant, and yet in the Agora Arcades (the main entertainment area of the Fedora) there are like 10 people MAX at one time. There is not enough people to warrant the immersion that the game is striving for, and it just makes things feel very disconnected. Even when the AllWater CEO is speaking to a large crowd, they are never shown and we are just meant to imagine them. In a stop-motion game this makes total sense, there is no feasible way to make like a thousand figures to create engagement, but then scale down the story or something of the sort. When you tell one thing and show the other it feels so confusing and false, and it made me feel less and less motivated to see the end of the story. There is also not enough variation between the environments to warrant the massive amounts of backtrackingThe gameplay is so so unfortuante. The entire game is just backtracking and running around. Harold is supposed to be a handyman, but like don't make the player immersed in the handyman life of walking around all day its a video game, man. There is no inventory, barely any important mini games, and it just using WASD and Space the entire game. There is no engaging gameplay at all, and after a while you just wonder why this was made into a video game in the first place. If you strive for high intensity, or just any amount of engaging gameplay at all, I would be really wary of buying this game. Again, I really do love the story of this game, but just why was it made into a video game if there is nothing engaging about the gameplay? If this was made into a longer movie it would have DESTROYED box offices, but I fear that this game will now just be remembered as something that could have been more than it actually is. I really really liked this game, but I have no motivation to pursue it further and finish it. It is slow paced, drawn out in a way that doesn't feel like it will be rewarding, and has no substantial gameplay to it. Sorry for the strong language, but I'm just confused as to why this game was made into a game in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this one for a long time!I haven't played Harold Halibut long, but I've loved what I have so far. The claymation art style and graphical fidelity combine for a really unique and awesome looking game, the writing and voice acting are great, and the setting is interesting and different! From what I've played so far, it really takes some of the best of 90's adventure games and adds a few more modern touches (walking around with a controller instead of click to move feels great) for an experience that leaves me feeling, somehow, both the nostalgia itch scratched, yet like I'm experiencing something fresh too!Kudos to the developers for working on this game for 14 years, yet still being on top of things enough that HDR, DLSS, and *lots* of graphical options have made their way to the release! There's a lot to offer here and I feel the ~$30 (got it on launch sale) price point is a good deal for this.

This was literally me steering a character to a point where i hit X and animation played out with early 2010 graphics, abominable dialog, a story that started nowhere and ended nowhere, characters that could be ranked by how much you dislike them and drag it out for as long as possible. How did this game get these raving reviews? It had one existential moment where the main character completely breaks from his personality the whole game and spits out some lines that were probably slight variations on a classic philosophers quote, utterly a different tone than the rest of the schlog that this game is, so much so it is in a dream/hallucination/psychadelic sequence. I seriously want my money back.    I don't usually write bad reviews. It takes more than a passive dislike of a game for me to rip into it. I realize that everyone has different perspectives and that some that dont appeal to me, do to others. But this was a piece of crap. I'll go through the different things that make a game individually, I'm not just talking out my ass. I also know that several people spent a lot of time and effort on this and part of themselves, so I hope me pointing out this stuff helps them and I apologize to them all, now, because I am going to be harsh.       First, gameplay... you know, the part that makes it a game? The part where you interact with the game?  This has ZERO. It shouldnt be called a game. it should be called an animated novel that needs a thumb to press a button to advance. There is NO mechanics AT ALL. I dont even mean its linear, it is way worse than that. The little 'PDA' that tells you what tasks need doing.. literally TELL you how to do it. Most are just go to this character and initiate more dialog. I cant emphasize this enough, the only 'gameplay' in this is the simulated arcade games you can do in the arcade.     Now, I've seen some walking simulators ( this is worse!! ) that manage to pull it off with some redemption because of the incredible writing, characters you connect with like friends, daunting suspense or jaw dropping visuals.... This failed miserably on all counts. The graphics and tech level was pretty clunky polygonal but really failed at the cartoony style everything was in. I think that they were trying to go for a 'heartfelt story' or some ♥♥♥♥ but couldnt make up their mind between that and funny cartoon. The story they had needed a more realistic style and the style they chose needed a fast paced goofy-lighthearted story.. The color palette chosen was almost as if 15 different people all did whatever they wanted and no one communicated. Visually it was awful. The player character was ugly and unlikable, the alien was a 3rd graders badly scribbled drawing with computer texture mapping. You could tell that absolutely zero thought was put into the creature as a viable species that had developed its shape and form by way of evolution adapted to its environment... it was a stickman with a fish as its head. The other members of the species have NO continuity and basically looked like a person putting weird shapes as heads on stickmen and is running out of ideas. The language was the most baby talk generic goo goo gaa gaa blurble poop crap I was actually shaking my head for the lack of effort put into it.     The story? It starts as a stranded colony. So, no hope. One guy, the stupidest, lowliest guy, practically a drooling idiot (and the other characters treat him as such) somehow encounters an alien. An alien that is wounded, taken inside another entity's area, Fed chemicals and drugs through an IV when they dont even know its physiology, and yet doesn't feel threatened, isolated and weak and uncomprehending. Not only that, but is so uncaring, unassuming and naive that it immediately brings these creatures to the center of its kind, a group of about 10 aliens that live in a cave and never leave it, yet treat the foreign species as if it is an irritating and simple minded member of its own brood. fast forward through stupid and half assed attempts at social commentary, corporate greed, self-absorbed individuals (who, by the way, are almost all horrible examples of people, that treat each other like they are all bratty elementary school children, including the 'genius level' and super intelligent trope characters) fast forward to the idiot main character decideds to stay with the aliens, as the only human amongst the 10-15 isolationist aliens. I don't care who you are, in a story, that represents suicide. When someone rejects the rest of humanity and chooses to seperate from the rest of the humans and remain with non humans, that symbolizes suicide! Its someone that feels like humanity as a whole has rejected them, they find comfort in the non-human group, symbolizes delusions and imaginary, comfort personas, even more so that they are complete alien and not a real creature at all. So the PLAYER CHARACTER chooses suicide and the rest blast themselves unrealistically into space to continue on a human ark type journey, a generation ship, where whjole generations are born live and die while the ship crosses space, an already dark and bleak prospect....   and that is the BEST CASE SCENARIO the rest of the group heads off into. It is a story that starts nowhere, goes nowhere and ends  NOWHERE.       The dialog is so utterly horrible that instances where a character says something like... ' Hey, there's something i need to tell you...' another character answers, ' Oh yeah? What is that?' and the first character says. 'oh, uh... nevermind'  ..  <--------- THAT kind of crap? happens at LEAST three times THAT I noticed! The main character is the STUPIDEST idiot, I know that because every other character treats him like that  and ALSO because he speaks his rudimentary thoughts aloud during the whole thing and doesnt grasp simple concepts long after the player understands, the NPC's are Yelling at him/ us/ the player?! in the game??! Theres a point where a librarian is telling him over and over to shhhhhhhhhhhh! repeatedly, but the character is trying to figure out what shhhush means, and we know each step in his thought process because he SPEAKS IT OUT LOUD... even AFTER he realizes that they are telling him to shut the F$%^& UP!        The other characters are all the worst type of people. The corporate greed and exploitation message is undercut by the fact that it is the player character that exposes the victim culture to the predatorial  corporation, the invasion and exploitation is allowed, normalized and is the means for the group to escape. This ♥♥♥♥♥♥ behavior is not punished in the course of events and even sometimes rewarded. at one point, an old postman that everyone liked dies and at the funeral ceremony, there is a video eulogy that he did for himself preemptively. He makes an observation that is about seeing the importance in other individuals....  just before turning it into a excersize and workout video...   The humour and seriousness cant get their ♥♥♥♥ straight. the humour is not funny, the subjects and themes attempted are far over a kids head, yet the atmosphere and dialog is kids cartoon like. And even though this is probably a foreign made game and some of this can be chalked up to interpretation or cultural, its so inept at all of it that it doesnt cover how fundamrentally incongrous and cobbled together it is. and all on the frame work of a steer and press X animated story...  it is GOD AWFUL. i dont know if that is grounds for a refund, as it is my fault for buying a piece of ♥♥♥♥... but i feel swindled.      Thats my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: A truly gorgeous game and I loved almost everything about it but unfortunately I have had to refund it as it's simply just walk from point a to point b.you'll really love this one if you're into those types of games but sadly I was sort of expecting puzzle elements, inventory stuff or choice making (again I don't blame the devs as this was clearly an issue on my part) which unfortunately are not in the game and as some have also pointed out the game doesn't really do anything to hold your attention and while I really love the art-style unfortunately besides that the game doesn't really offer anything else and instead i'd rather get my money back.Overall I really do think if you enjoy slow pased games or want something with incredible visuals and a relaxing story this one is a definite recommend but just from my perspective the walking alone sadly didn't do it for me which I do feel bad about as you can definitely see the love poured into this.It's also left me questioning as to who exactly this game was made for or what exactly the target audience is as the game while having a Wallace and gromit style with the stop motion and clay work the game features no real dialogue that kids would understand But I just felt like this would have worked better as a movie rather than a game as simply walking from point a to point b isn't really the most entertaining as some cut scenes can go on for over 4 minutes with nothing really interesting happening leading to wonder does this even technically count as a game?
