_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; A unique, slow-paced, story based game set in an aesthetic world. If you are looking for game play over story, either pick it up on sale or skip.I could go on and on about the amazing art style and the work put into it, but it speaks for itself, so I won't. Basically, if you like Wes Anderson, you will like this.I really enjoyed the characters and their backstories, and I liked how there wasn't too many people to focus on. The choice to limit the number of interact-able characters on board really lets you focus on building a relationship with them and caring about the story, and it's impressive how quickly you do care. It helps keep the world small for what is overall a shorter game.The story is very slow paced with a lot of cut scenes and that will kill the game for some people. It didn't for me, but that doesn't mean that I loved every turn the story takes. Certain acts of the game will drag on and that was hard considering how much I loved other parts. It was frustrating when the story didn't take the turns I was expecting, and I wish they dug deeper into the larger themes, such as what it would usually mean to have a large corporation on board who doesn't seem to have the residents best interest in mind. I wish that they cut down on making certain ideas so large only for them to burn out quick. The story is good for what it is, but it's not going to be elaborated on like it starts to make you believe at certain points. If you can deal with taking the story at face value and enjoy this as a "cozy" game, you will still enjoy it.There is also some monotony with the travel system and quests, which can make you want to put the game down for a bit... and so I did. And that's partially why I still recommend this game even though it can make you feel like that sometimes. Yet again, if you look at this game as a "cozy" game to unwind with, you will enjoy it. I am excited to see what Slow Bros does next, especially if they pick up where this game ends and take some of what the reviews say into consideration. If you are having doubts from reading these reviews like I did, pick the game up on sale. It's worth a play through, just understand it will be slow going.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Visuals are absolutely stunning and the music is extremely well done. I wish the story ended around Chapter 5 (with some epilogue afterward, potentially), as Chapter 6 felt extremely sluggish with little payoff (for me). This is a game that requires some patience to get through some of the extremely long/repetitive portions (i.e., walking back and forth to see if -this- NPC has anything new to say / spending minutes on a submarine drive that can be done by just walking away from the computer)Overall: beautiful in both sight and sound, story and gameplay could've been tightened up/vastly improved on in some areas
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it!The game is exceptionally slow and is more of a fetch quest simulator. There isn't a lot of action for you the player to do but is more like an interactable movie. BUT! If you enjoy narrative game play, charming visuals and fun characters, please do check it out. It is a sweet story about discovering one's self.I felt bummed when it was over as I could no longer meander about as the titular Harold!
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I will address the bad things right away: - The running around became annoying. I couldn't always find the person I was looking for meaning I was running around for what felt like forever. I guess they used this to prolong the game but I just felt like I was playing Skyrim and getting sidemissions the whole time.- Before I played it I read about some rude characters and man there was some rude characters! I felt so bad for Harold, just a nice young man, and people were talking to him like he was a total dumbass! He was trying to do something and the person talking to him was so mean to him! He came to Mareaux more than one time just talking normally and she was addressing him like he was a pain in the ass. I got so annoyed from time to time, behaviour like that can make people feel really really bad about themselves over time and they will start question themselves if they're even worth anything. Mareaux and that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the game store was the absolute worst, overall people could from time to time also be rude. I wonder what sadist came up with this.Please people out there, this is not a normal behaviour, nobody deserves to be treated like this. Nobody deserves to one time being cradled into safety and then the next time being told off like you're a waste of space. If you have someone like this in your social groups please find other friends and stop talking to them. You do not deserve to be treated like that, nobody does. - The game was really beautiful and unique. It really felt like people had put a lot of effort to make this game and the stop-motion effect really came through. If this was a movie I'd totally watch it and I'd enjoy it just as much.- The characters felt unique and funny, no character was the same. Really well done!- It was nice hearing some familiar voices from The NoSleep Podcast. The voice acting overall was really good.- Story was also very cool and unique, I liked the design of the creatures and the developers even made those unique. Would I recommend this game? Absolutely! It's a slow paced game and you should totally go for it if you have the time and patience for that type of game. It's not as much as exploring as I would like but it still has something to find and see. As I said, except from the rude characters the game was good.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Some games are about choices, some make you feel smart with puzzles, this one is purely story. A walking simulator, if you will. There are no puzzles that you need to solve, there is always a list of your current tasks, and the rare dialog choice has really no impact.The game is aware of this and *almost literally* turns to camera to say, that an adventure can be getting to know people. So, don't expect anything more than that.The world building is pretty good, you'll get a little bit hit over the head with it in the beginning, but it doesn't feel too forced. The corporate overlord / water punk portion of the setting is ridiculous - it's saved by not being questioned at all for the obvious problems a capitalist mini-society would have.I think it's mostly meant to be very differently to the alien commune we will get to know...So, it's walking, using the tube-system, walking (again) and talking with lots of bigger and smaller cutscenes in between. The English narrators do a great job and the writing is solid throughout. It tries to be funny at times, but doesn't push too hard - it's more situational comedy, not slapstick.Where does it fail? Well, the first thing I noticed is climbing stairs with Harold: He places his feet precisely in the wrong spots, slips around wildly and yet somehow doesn't fall... On the topic of looks: While wool and fabric looks very nice, the shiny, plastic-y hair of the characters neither looks real nor like something puppets would wear - it's really odd.The tube system isn't something our protagonist likes for the price structure - I was getting annoyed at the constant announcements when leaving and arriving. I'm sure it's intentionally.On the technical side, there were also little problems: There are slight stutters now an then when a room is loaded, I think. After a cutscene, the loading stalled forever - trying again on the another day helped... Not too bad, at least the autosave works.Overall, I liked my time with the game, even when there was nothing really to stimulate my brain with. If you like a story-focused game about a guy slowly connecting with the people around him, this might be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Such an interesting story line with insane visuals and an atmospheric soundtrack. Although the gameplay does feel slow at times, especially while travelling from place to place (I wish there was a sprint option lol), I think being able to look around at the intricate and detailed corridors and posters make up for the inefficient travel.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: If you love narrative games, and don't mind a slower pace in exchange for a really beautiful payoff... you'll love this game. I played Harold Halibut as a way to wind down before bed over the course of a few months and it did not disappoint. It's not overly complex, and it doesn't to be. The story, characters, and dialogue are what shine. It almost reminded me of the small town I grew up in, and felt so cozy to return to every night.Oh, and the graphics! 14 years was worth the wait for something as gorgeous as this.Haven't been this moved by a game in a while. Sad the experience is over, but very glad I had it.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I have ever played anything quite like this game. It's a narrative experience which haunts me - in a good way. A lot of moments made me pause and think - they were usually something Weeoo or Harold said. The visuals/artwork are amazing and the amazing music perfectly supports the great writing. My only gripes are as follows: : There are instances where the controls feel laggy or ill-timed, like when you get off the elevator which leads to Capt. Zoya's. The player has to wait until the entire animation of the elevator doors closing before they can get control of Harold again. Perhaps it's something that can be fixed with a patch.  (SPOILERS): I saw plenty of opportunities where player choice could have added a lot more to the game in a meaningful manner - and without affecting the game's narrative message, atleast not in any drastic manner. (That includes a second ending, but alas!) Further, after all the time we spent with the colourful cast of characters, I think we deserved to see all the emotional goodbyes Harold could've had with them besides Mareaux. It would've added a lot more emotional weight to the single ending we got.Nevertheless, you've spent 7+ years creating this gem of a game which which will stay with me for a long time. Thank you for this.I hope to see more such games from you folk in the future! My score: 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: This game connected with me at such a deep level.Offering insight to aspects of my life I've been frustrated with and haven't realized.You play as Harold, a handyman, handling the busywork of a society of space colonists.The vibe of the game is essentially like a Wes Anderson flick, but maybe not with as many of the monotone quirks that comes with as far as dialogue.Every day Harold completes monotonous work, never truly satisfied.Always wishing for a connection with someone or something. Over the course of the game Harold will meet people and realize things about himself and life The art direction is phenomenal, the entire game is handcrafted to a meticulous detail using claymation. All locations of the game feel alive and lived in This game is a true masterpiece that I hope receives all the attention it deserves. Thank you Slow Bros, you guys know what's up. Thank y'all for reminding me I'm enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. 10/10 The games concept is very interesting, new and excellently exactitude, the animation is funky but the art style more then makes up for it. The only problem I had is that the PDA doesn't always tell you where the different people are. Sometimes they're in entirely different areas or I forget who the name relates to and I end up looking all over the ship to find they were in the same place I started at. Other then that Its a wonderful game. Ewoo, Harold, and Buddy are gems; GEMS.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: It is more of a visual novel than a game to be fair, Given that, it is quite special and worth experiencing, I found the story to be really meaningful and relatable. A lot of really important questions are asked in this game and I was left with a lot of food for thought. I loved the art, music and philosophy incorporated through out the story, it is all so well crafted and beautiful. I totally recommend it,  but it is for a really chill time when one needs to be inspired or reflective. And you do play as a handyman of sorts so expect to be running errands all game. I found transitions and actions to be a bit janky and the pacing possibly a bit boring at times, maybe performance issues will be fixed eventually.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is special, however I would not go into it thinking of it as a game. A better way to think of it is an interactive 12 hour movie. The story was amazing and I really connected with the characters, make sure you talk to everyone aboard the ship anytime you get the chance as it greatly enriches the story! 10/10 I would definitely recommend, this is the only game that has ever gave me the feels and left me melancholy.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game and I recommend it. I thought the art design was very original (my wife loved how the fabrics looked). We thought the dialogue and story was wonderful and unique as well. Harold Halibut is more of a slow-burn, focusing heavily on the characters and the day-to-day life of a handyman, Harold, aboard a crashed star-ship. The majority of the game play is a 'walking simulator', and involves Harold completing tasks for various people aboard the Fedora and walking through different parts of the ship. Other than minor visual anomalies, I did not experience any bugs. The most succinct summary I could think of the actual story: Harold is a depressed handyman, having resigned himself to his current role as Mareaux's lackey, until a fantastical experience alters his entire life.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute beauty.Everything is intriguing! The story is well-designed and the conversations have a weird sense of humour, and the choice of music is perfect (I love Harold's song), I even cried a little at the ending!My favourite part was I bought this game because of the art, as I first saw the making of the puppets and props (I made stop motion animation too!), I'd been eager to see how 3D-scanned puppets work out in game since then. From what I feel, although the modeling has kept most of the textures and styles, they still feel quite 3D and not too puppet-y. Not that it affects my playing experience anyway, the art itself is still very unique, the light and the atmosphere are really eye catching too! I can see the team's effort and love throughout the gameplay. 😊10/10 will play it again!!
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Huge Caveat - you have to go into the game with the correct expectations. It's very noble and impressive of the devs to dedicate so much effort into crafting the truly breathtaking environments you'll see in the game, which makes navigation the best part of the game. The story is nice, and the characters are serviceable and likable enough if a little simplistic. That being said, there are a lot of problems. The performance (especially if you don't have a controller or a very good PC) is not the best, and this game is pretty much a movie with some optional side storylines, meaning there is very little gameplay/reward for playing. The protagonist also moves fairly slowly and that can make parts of this game a bit of a slog to get through. I would love to see a movie based on the game instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with a nice story and amazing art. I enjoyed learning about all the characters and the unique environments they are in. _childDocuments_.review: A beautiful narrative game with themes of finding happiness and self worth. A bit of a slow burn, but worth running around and getting to know other characters, and primarily living life as the main character, Harold. Chapter 5 was the most breath-taking part and was absolutely an artistic feast for the eyes and heart. I love and care about Harold and our fishy friend, .
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a joy to play. I wish I'd known that every character, item, and set in the game was made by hand.  I would have felt even more amazed as I went at what this tiny team has created. The story was extremely charming, and continually gained momentum throughout the game. The interplay of the characters was consistently sweet and funny, all while having a cynical edge regarding bureaucracy's hold over people.I couldn't have anticipated where it all went, I'm excited for those yet to play it. I imagine people will call this game a"walking sim," given the sparse and simple gameplay mechanics. Those who are into getting swept up exploring a cozy sci-fi world and experiencing a unique story are in for a good time.I tried to play at a pace that was leisurely enough to get the achievement for playing for 15+ hours, but it seems that doesn't count track time spent in menus and perhaps also dialogue? I'm currently chilling in the Arcade vibing to the sound track, which I could have spent four paragraphs raving about. 10/10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: slow pace and relaxing , if you love the old claymation style animations then you will love this , it's an interesting and quirky game that some might find a bit tedious but i personally find it is an excellent way to relax and wind down , no stress , no need to rush a nice break away from shooters and simulations
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely, relaxed and artsy game. _childDocuments_.review: The story's a bit long and wanders a little here and there, but so does Harold. It's very normal on the surface, but deep inside it's mytstical and full of wonder, kind of like Harold.It's got it's flaws, but stick by it long enough and it will make you feel something whimsical and wholesome.Just like Harold.A work of art, the attention to detail is incredible, and while that doesn't make it a 10/10 game, it's still worth experiencing, like a great novel.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: It's really pretty to look at, if you enjoy the experience of looking at things and taking in the details.  buy the game knowing what you're going to get, it's not really a "game" - you have no agency, your actions are singular and advance the story, no more, it's just a nice warm friendly, it's innocent in lots of ways.There are no puzzles to solve in this "adventure" game, it may need a genre all of it's own.I could go for minutes without pressing a key, some sequences were like that, using submarines through the ocean, you're being guided by rails even though you can move you submarine a little bit.Some character relationships felt really forced, Buddy for example, was boring and not enjoyable.I would still recommend, it's nice, it's unique, it's cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a really nice game. The story is interesting and also someting to think about. I really much like the Graphic style. You can also check out how they did it on their page. Awesome work! I played the whole game on Gamepass, but seeing how well it was done I decided even to buy it to support the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Harold Halibut is a pretty unique experience. I say experience and not game because there isn't really much gameplay to speak of, but I enjoyed my time on the FEDORA, getting to know Harold and all the characters in his life.The game is beautiful, and it has some really cool, weird and charming moments. It feels like what you'd get if Wes Anderson made a video game.It won't be for everyone, but if you're at all intrigued by the trailer I'd say give it a shot
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Finished in just under 17 hours.  I liked the artwork, the voice acting, the creativity, and the mood.  But it is a misnomer to call this a game.  It is an interactive story.  That's not necessarily a bad thing, but keep that in mind if considering purchase.  I'd say the only thing that I did not like is all of the walking.  If the walking were to be removed from this game, I could have completed it in 4-6 hours, it's that dramatic.  Now, to be fair, I am not one for 'games' such as this.  I mean, I do like all the things mentioned above, but I want more of a game in my game.  And with that context, I must admit hat if someone suggested a game and said that it was a lot like Harold Halibut, I'd pass.  I want story, artwork, good voice acting, creativity, and mood, but I also want to be more than a voyeur of a story.  So yes, for someone interested in 'games' of this nature, I think this is a great example.  I just prefer games of a different nature.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly entertaining and looks amazing.  No puzzles but the world building/lore and creative graphical presentation more than makes up for challenge.  Reminiscent of Truberbrook in level of detail and how gorgeous it is.  Best played with a game pad/controller.  Disable Steam controller override, the game supports all.  Voice acting is nicely done, definitely would recommend.  Again, it is not a challenging game - no puzzles, light fare, fetchy oriented but so nicely done.  If you're looking for an easy peasy romp through a pandorum adjacent plot with delightful visuals - give this a whirl.  Haven't finished the game so there may be some surprises - if so, I'll drop info on any changes in mechanics.  Speaking of which there's variety with mechanics that aids in breaking up any task monotony.  I played full screen at 3840x2160 @60, vertical locked with the majority of options bumped to high with motion blur off.  Slight stuters/frame drops on occasion but nothing that deterred or detracted from the game at all.  So far, no bugs or game breaking sitches.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game! Extremely charming and unique. The story was actually much longer than anticipated! _childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I personally love this game! The graphics are amazing, the music is fantastic and the atmosphere is so immersive imo. I should say that there isn't much game play (beside a few mini games) other then walking around and talking to people, but I knew what I was getting into when I bought this. There are also quite a few stunning sequences (particularly in chapter 5) and the ending is sad but also very heartwarming at the same time.I will say the game isn't perfect however. For starters this game is LONG... I'm all for a slow burner but when it takes 8 hour to finish your game when going at a break neck pace, your story might need a bit of fat trimming off of it (and believe me there are some sections that are soon slow even for a slow burner.)Speaking of the story, it feels a bit over stuffed. The story constantly keeps flipping between 3 major plot points that don't rly fit well together and kind of take away from each other. There's also a twist villain reveal at the end which just felt really random, and alot of the game's twist reveals are rather predictable. The story is also full of time skips that can make things a little difficult to follow along.I will say the world building is extremely immersive, with there being tones of back story and history to be learned about the ship and some of the characters, but it can feel overwhelming at times. Like you're just bombarded with names and new characters at the beginning of the game which can be quite off putting and confusing at first.One thing I would like to also mention is the price, I think charging £30 to play this is a little bit steep especially given the fact that most other walking sims are like half that price with there being nothing much more to differentiate this from the rest appart from the visuals, and the story (while engaging) definitely isn't worth the £30 price of admission.Over all I'd say this game is definitely for an acquired taste, but I'd definitely recommend picking it up if it goes on sale for dirt cheap, or watching a walk through on YouTube.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: is a charming little game. Like  mixed with a Wes Anderson movie, it is slow-paced, silly, and utterly heart-warming. There is no action, no drama (okay, maybe a little drama), no blood-pumping chase sequences -- and it's better off for it.  is the type of game that you play on a rainy Sunday, indoors with a warm drink, while you let yourself slip away into another world.Harold is not your typical protagonist, he's not a go-getter, or particularly good at anything. And yet, he feels real...grounded, in a way that other protagonists aren't. Some won't resonate with him, and that's okay. But those of you who do, will find yourself in a similar position as me: where your adventure with Harold becomes something greater and this experience leaves a lasting impact.If you enjoy narrative-based experiences, or games that are more "art" than "game", give this one a go. It's a slow one, but I promise it'll be worth it. Definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute delight. I just completed my playthrough and I'm left with that feeling you get after a once-in-a-blue-moon experience. A beautifully, soulfully crafted story that feels like it carries heart in its every stitch. I grew attached to all of the characters, fell in love with the setpieces, and found myself grateful to have spent a little bit of my own time with the citizens of Fedora. Highly recommend for anyone looking to escape into a tremendously beautiful and weird microcosm of its own.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often write reviews so please excuse my first attempt at this but I felt obligated to share my thoughts on this game. Harold Halibut is one of those games that comes around only once in a while. A game that will catch you off guard multiple times with the feeling that you are experiencing something truly special.That's not to say this is everyone's cup of tea because it challenges the concept of what a game is. I often forgot I was playing a game as it is very much like watching a quirky indie movie.This is a SLOW BURN that crescendos at the end which has left an imprint on me that many games fail to accomplish these days.Harold Halibut rewards the kind of player that likes to take their time exploring, talking to NPCs, and listening to the ambient sounds and music. Playing this game in a dark room late at night with a pair of headphones and zero distractions is a MUST to fully appreciate it. The devs and artists at Slow Bros truly hit the nail on the head with the world building and character development that instantly made me a fan of the studio.At this point I'm rambling but if you are in the mood for something unique I highly recommend giving this one a go. Hopefully, you will enjoy it as much as I did. :-) And for anyone at Slow Bros reading this, I'm looking forward to your next one, you all are simply amazing! Bravo and brava!
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: This was an interesting experience. I wasn't sure it would be with the slow, repetitive nature of much of the game, but the flashes of brilliance build to an intriguing boil in the latter third that I found made it worthwhile. The writing can't quite decide if it wants to be a run-of-the-mill adventure game story or a thoughtful pondering on life, home, motivation, and meaning, but when those deeper themes pop up it really elevates the experience beyond being a cute little adventure game. As gratingly mild as Harold mostly is as a character, he and a few other characters occasionally knock you off your feet with some real galaxy-brain-type relatable wisdom, which I loved. The experience is carried by these little surprises-visually beautiful dramatic moments, interesting music choices, the characters having heart-to-heart that isn't just about the main plotline/side story, and that is what makes the game and shows what a labor of love it is. That said, the gameplay is standard narrative/walking sim stuff with a few minigames, so don't expect innovative mechanics. A few gripes:- Even as a narrative game fan I found it more sluggish than I'd like both in gamefeel and pacing, the errand-boy loop takes up far too much of the total game time.- The mocap work is great but it detracts from the stop-motion aesthetic they were going for, and besides some of the character faces it's hard to see how it's different from regular stylized 3D models- It would have been nice if there was more to see or at least more to interact with in the small area you are in- More weird visual bugs than I would expect but thankfully nothing affecting gameplayCome in with the right expectations and patience and you'll be rewarded. Huge congrats to the devs for pulling it off after such a long project!
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: If you have eyes you already know this game is something truly special visually. Its also one of the most unique stories I've experienced in gaming, anywhere really. _childDocuments_.review: An interesting story. A big setting but a relatively small plot. Most of the time you're a lowly schlub janitor/handyman spending his time having social anxiety and doing menial odd jobs. As soon as the game starts feeling bored and getting that "is that all there is" feeling not only does the character echo but then the game starts throwing wrenches into the routines.A classic story arc: establish a pattern, then break it. The setting reminds me of Bioshock's Rapture just without the super powers and with more of a Outer Worlds "incompetent corporatocracy" thrown on top. The characters you meet are pretty memorable with decent writing and voice acting. All in all if you like the idea of being a plumber on a sinking intergalactic space ship, then this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: From the start, to set out where I am, I liked Edith Finch, Dear Esther and other walking sim/story led games. So Harold Halibut is naturally in my wheelhouse.This is genuinely the intersection of art and gaming - a beautiful story, gently told. The richness of the environment along with the beautiful soundscapes and character design that is reminiscent of 60's Eastern European animation art houses make this a delight to play.This is not to say it is for everyone. The pacing is *very* slow. A speed-run will be at minimum 8h. The puzzles are just story vehicles and will not challenge at all - but they are not there for that. They are there to expose more character and story. This is a novel, a sc-fi novel that is a bit Harlan Ellison and a bit le Guin, that happens to use a game-pad.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing art style. I felt immersed in this strange underwater world. This is an experience that I can't stop thinking about. Yes, it's a little slow starting out, but the slow burn is sometimes that best. BUY this. EDIT: Just finished the game. It's an absolute masterpiece, I didn't want it to end. This game has more heart than anything I've played in years. You owe it to yourself to experience it.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not really sure what Harold Halibut accomplishes. It's a nice little story, with very stylish visuals, and a sort of theatrical energy to it. The gameplay is hard to classify. There are very few meaningful choices, most of the interaction is done through walking around and dialogue. It feels like going to watch a community theatre marionette show, in a good way. My main nitpicks are to do with language - it's a game made by German developers, and it's clear that whoever was doing the voice direction was not a native english speaker, even though all the voice acting is in english. There are some inconsistent mispronunciations and inflection mistakes that really stick out and make the listening a little bumpy, and that could have been ironed out with the right voice director.Also, the game's humour is hit or miss, with some jokes making me chuckle, and others that just feel strange.There are a couple times the game crashed on loading screens, but the autosave is frequent enough that it wasn't a huge issue. It's a good length, and it's a sweet little production. There are times when it feels like it's trying a little bit too hard to be deep, but mostly it has a nice vibe. It's worth the time, if you want a relaxed, whimsical little adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most beautiful Story Games in a long time!You can tell hour by hour how many Years of hard work and Heart have flowed into this Project. I'm very proud to have bought this Game 2 hours after its release, because it is truly worth every penny. I played it with the Keyboard and had a lot of fun with it, because you can easily play it with only one hand. I played the Demo Version with Dual Shock and it was just as relaxed to play. The voice Actors are uniquely good & all fit to their Characters. The Atmosphere is easy to enjoy and has a touch reminiscent of Bioshock. The Story has a leisurely flow and it was mixed very well, so that special events and music have a particularly good and strong effect.It took me comfortable 17.4 hours for the first run and I will play through this Game again.I just love everything about this game! ❤❤❤❤
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Harold is professor Mareaux's lab assistant investigating the energy crisis on Fedora I, the last bastion of mankind in an alien ocean, after 250 years in space. However, he's destined to do more than just insubstantial repairs.Narrative game of retro-futuristic aesthetics and sci-fi theme, with gameplay similar to a point & click game (with much less puzzles), whose scenarios and characters are hand-crafted and animated by stop-motion. A charming journey that has taken its creators 14 years of work. Think that practically everything that appears in the game (it lasts about 12 hours to complete it) is made with real materials and animated frame by frame 🤯As I mentioned, the title takes place in an underwater base on a planet 200 years away from Earth. Here, all the space is organized in modules (recreational area, school, laboratories...), and the transport (a "gift" from All Water Corp.) consists of a tubular payment system.Here, Harold is the go-to guy for everything. Maintenance, errands, cleaning... He's always willing to pitch in, although he doesn't always feel as valued as he would like to be. Besides, every day at Fedora I is too much like the last. Fortunately, in addition to the incredible plot twists of an exquisitely narrated plot and masterfully written characters (they're feel alive), the entire title exudes a very fine humor. To the point that its optional tasks are a compendium of hilarious and crazy requests.With a satisfying gameplay loop that reminds me to Night in the Woods, in its final stretch it feels somewhat artificially elongated, with heavy errand "missions" and endless travel between characters. However, I'd argue that this is deliberately so in order to bring us closer to the protagonist's feelings.Personally, and as a lover of stop-motion animation, I felt I was playing something magical and, despite its occasional small flaws in rhythm, I was moved by its story and characters as few games manage to convey.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I was originally going to expand on the same bullet points that other reviewers have mentioned:  the art style is fantastic and the VAs are great; but the game overstays its welcome and the gameplay is a little too simple.However, I think that would go contrary to one of the game's central themes.  Sometimes, we have to stop pursuing the perfect life (or game, in this case), stop regretting what we don't have, and come to terms with the cards life has dealt us.Harold Halibut is a game with heart and a story that's told warmly; and that rare feat graduates it from a game I would recommend on sale to a game I'd legitimately recommend at the current price.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning and captivating from beginning to end, I was completely invested in this game before its release and even more so while playing it! Kudos to the team - it's one thing to make a game but to make a stop motion one - a job well done! A gripping story, beautiful scenery, an array of individual characters and plenty of laughs - 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Wishlisted this game when I saw the trailer and bought it upon release. It is 100% a passion project and the love that the developers/creators had for it really shines through. I thoroughly enjoyed the experience. Lovable characters, interesting and funny dialog, a cohesive story with twists all around. I just finished the game 5 minutes ago and although I wished it ended differently, I cannot say I am dissatisfied. It is a cinematic game, and if you aren't prepared to be watching as much as you are playing, you are barking up the wrong tree. 11.9 hours was my finishing time, although I did not get all the achievements and explore every possible avenue. I would imagine that one could get up to 15 hours by the end if they completed everything. To summarize: This was a worthwhile purchase. My friends and I loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it, but you have to say that this might not be for everyone. This is more of an art project in the form of a game, but there really isn't much gameplay. So if you are looking for a fun game, this is not it. If you are looking for something in the line of a story or a painting, then you will have a great time. I think the correct word to describe it would be an art piece walking simulator. If that doesn't interest you, don't bother. If it does, then this is a really great experience. I can see why it took 10 years of work to make Harold Halibut.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: the music is good, the characters are great aside from a couple moments where they were a little grating to me. The visuals are superb, and the game doesnt overstay its welcome as long as you trudge through a couple lulls. Discovering the alien "world" was a little underwhelming, but i love weeoo so its ok. My only wish for this game is that its story was a tad more adult, and a bit more meat on its bones thematically. however, the character writing is very fun and a joy to experience. I took no issue with its limited setting and retracing steps, because of the handcrafted assets with a lot of love poured into them and the story gives just enough progression with the characters to keep it fresh. If you want to relax and enjoy an innocent, beautiful stop motion film with some (a little) interactivity then i do wholly recommend this game. If you prefer vampire survivors type games over firewatch type games, maybe wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: This is a story game. Don't expect to be running, gunning, or anything else like that. You're going to explore, talk to people and experience a story. This is 100% like playing a Wes Anderson movie. The animation/art is amazing, the voice acting is very well done and overall it is fantastic. If you like story games (Night in the Woods, Firewatch, Fall of Porcupine) this is a must.Edit after finishing: I can't recommend this game enough. The story is compelling and beautiful. Every set piece was masterfully crafted. The voice acting could be a little iffy at times but overall very well done.11/10
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: Unique, very nice world building, goofy and silly characters that are far from what is usually seen these days.Very nice sceneries, graphics suited the mood perfectly. At times almost bizarre visuals that caught me off guard, whomever came up with them deserves a raise. Had a few uncanny valley moments that were very enjoyable.The story was enjoyable as well, well balanced and i would easily recommend this to myself if i was a kid.Synopsis and the whole storyline felt unique. Suitably goofy as a whole that it made it feel like a adventure movie, back when adventure movies were fun.Also the fact that a few obscure oddities and plot holes manglings left in gave the impression that one does not quite know the whole story as of yet, nice touch.A few bugs with the first released build, just player character locking up or walking endlessly in a loop while engaging convo, nothing big, and was solved with exit to main menu and then reloading.Would have loved a even more detailed texture on characters, was a bit washed out, might be a game engine limitation(?).Maybe a bit too much fetch quest at some points, but not to a displeasing degree. Puzzles involving direct character actions (as 3D printer puzzle) would have been very fun.All in all, very enjoyable, will play again at some point and hope that this game or series gets a sequel.Recommend it to pretty much anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

The game is basically a narrated story with very few and light puzzles.But it is a very interesting and cute story who will surely bring a smile on your face.Even Harold Halibut isn't really the type of game that I usually play, I had a really good time onboard "the fedora"..  7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: If you like narrative-heavy games, walking simulators etc., or if you simply watch the trailer and think "hey this looks pretty good", then you'll almost certainly enjoy Harold Halibut. The visual style is, of course, its big standout, but it's remarkable in pretty much all other aspects as well - voice acting; writing; story; music; sound design; animation; character design; etc. It isn't an especially "gamey" game, and (AFAIK) your experience won't be much different from the experience of others, so if any of this bothers you then you might want to avoid it, but that's the only warning I'd provide. Thus far my biggest complaint is simply that subtitles can't be disabled, which seems to negatively impact immersion of the stop-motion style just a bit, but obviously this is a very minor complaint. I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Harold Halibut

_childDocuments_.review: I completed the game after 22 hours, and I have to say it's one of those special gems that resonates with you for a long time. It's not really a game...It's an interactive movie. It's an experience. This won't be for everyone, but if you enjoy games like Pentiment, and you want to relax and go on a ride that has a nice slow burn with emotional payoffs... this is for you. I highly recommend it, but again, it's not for everyone. Don't go into this expecting something like... Disco Elysium or any such game. It's a very very chill experience. _childDocuments_.review:
Harold Halibut is a handmade narrative game about friendship, and life on a city-sized spaceship submerged in an alien ocean. 

It's been 250 years since your home - an ark-like spaceship - fled an Earth on the verge of cold war to find a habitable planet on which to preserve the human race. 
You are Harold, a young lab assistant for the ship's lead scientist, Jeanne Mareaux. While most of the ship's inhabitants have reconciled themselves to a life lived aboard the sunken ship, Mareaux still works tirelessly to find a way for the ship to leave the planet and find a new, dryer home. 

But of course the weird, wonderful and diverse people of the Fedora keep Harold busy too. Until one fateful encounter plunges Harold into a new world that nobody could have guessed existed - and one that may hold the key to Mareaux's re-launch plans. 

Join Harold as he explores a vibrant retro-future world, talks (with full voice acting) to its inhabitants, and occasionally goes hands on by sticking screwdrivers in things, operating complex machinery, and more in his quest to find the true meaning of 'home'.

detailed_description: Back 4 Blood: Deluxe Edition Buy Back 4 Blood: Deluxe Edition and get: Base Game Annual Pass: Three upcoming downloadable content drops with New Story, Playable Characters, Special Mutated Ridden, and more Back 4 Blood: Ultimate Edition Buy Back 4 Blood: Ultimate Edition and get: Base Game Annual Pass: Three upcoming downloadable content drops with New Story, Playable Characters, Special Mutated Ridden, and more 4 Character Battle Hardened Skin Pack Additional digital in-game items: Rare Banner, Emblem, Spray, Title About the Game Back 4 Blood is a thrilling cooperative first-person shooter from the creators of the critically acclaimed Left 4 Dead franchise. You are at the center of a war against the Ridden. These once-human hosts of a deadly parasite have turned into terrifying creatures bent on devouring what remains of civilization. With humanity's extinction on the line, it's up to you and your friends to take the fight to the enemy, eradicate the Ridden, and reclaim the world. Cooperative Campaign Fight your way through a dynamic, perilous world in a 4-player co-op story campaign where you must work together to survive increasingly challenging missions. Play with up to 3 of your friends online or go solo and lead your team in battle. Choose from 8 customizable Cleaners, one of the immune survivors, and a range of lethal weapons and items. Strategise against an ever-evolving enemy bent on your total destruction. Competitive Multiplayer Play with or against friends in PVP. Switch between playing as a Cleaner with special perks and the horrific Ridden. Both sides come with unique weapons, abilities, and specialties. Extreme Replayability A new 'rogue-lite' Card System creates different experiences each and every time, putting you in control to craft custom decks, roll different builds and undertake more demanding fights. The Game Director is constantly adjusting to player actions, ensuring exciting fights, extreme gameplay diversity, and tougher legions of Ridden - including mutated boss types up to 20 feet tall.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so this is a pretty fun game. It comes in with a solid, working system and takes you for a ride.- Deck system is a lot of fun and adds a lot of longevity to runs.- Gun/mod system is very approachable and overall makes sense.- Visuals are very well-done. The scene is really set well for the grim zombie apocalypse.- Character interactions are really detailed and fill in a lot of lore!- Bots are kind of...not great. Like, you're at a severe disadvantage with bot players.- It takes a little bit to learn the distinct sound cues of the special ridden. Some of them are very obvious, others are far more subtle. It would help if there was an additional music cue of some sort.- The only place I see the special ridden system explained is when you practice or play as the ridden. I think this could be corrected just by adding loading screen tips, or additional materials at Fort Hope/in the menu.- Flashlight management is automatic (very minor, but still - it's my flashlight!)- In PvE modes, I would really love to see a game mode where instead of having the special ridden mutation tree (E.G. Tallboys have three sub-mutations, etc.) that you have as many base special ridden as you want (leaving room for DLC) with each mutation having the same base percent to spawn. Then add in episode and/or chapter-long mutation cards that modify the chance of certain mutations happening. For instance, you might draw a mutation card that increases the chance of the Crusher mutation spawning for a single episode. I think this would further engage the deck system that is really at the core of B4B, plus it would both simplify the mutation tree in PvE, but build in a lot more flexibility for future content.Note: For PvP, I think the current system works just fine, though it might be neat to have an experimental PvPgame mode with this deck mutations?Overall, a very fun game to play with friends. Definitely not worth the $60 price point, but if you can get it on sale for $35 or less, it's worth it!I think there are some things the developers can play with to improve the overall quality of life, but they are minor.

_childDocuments_.review: Had a decent amount of fun playing this with friends. We played all throughout the game's lifespan so we were there for the good, the bad, and the ugly. Some patch cycles were definitely painful to get through but Back4Blood has definitely come a long way since its admittedly rocky launch.The core gameplay here is satisfying; gunplay feels solid and the card deck system allows for a good amount of playstyle customization. The player decks are especially important on the harder difficulties, where it's necessary to plan as a group since you need to cover things from ammo diversity, economy, and group buffs while also having basic roles like "horde clearer" and "anti-specialist" filled or else you're gonna have a bad time. Some of the finales were seemingly impossible but with a bit of thinking and deck tweaking, we were able to tackle them by approaching them differently. Each "role" has a variety of ways to be covered so I never felt like I was forced into a playstyle I didn't like to pick up where our group was lacking.Our group is pretty stubborn so we were able to forgive and overlook a lot of the more frustrating aspects of B4B and write them off as a challenge to be overcome. I think your enjoyment of B4B really comes down to if you have a group of regular friends to play it with and if you have enough patience to forgive how ruthless the game can get on its harder difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game is pretty fun, doesn't deserve *all* the hate.I am writing this review currently with 26h played in B4B and I feel that I am informed enough to share my experience.I am an old Left 4 Dead and Left 4 Dead 2 fan. years ago I clocked 765 and 1457 hours respectively, and played both PvE and PvP extensively. I don't know how impressive or unimpressive these amount of hours are these days, but I did play the ♥♥♥♥ out of those games back when they were released. Safe to say, I enjoyed them thoroughly.So, let's get down to brass tacks, the major complains of Back 4 Blood are:#1 - Too expensive for what you get, and#2 - Doesn't feel like Left 4 Dead.#3 - The PvP Sucks.OK, fine, those are valid criticisms, and contain truth, but miss the mark of what the game is. So, when I picked it up, honestly I enjoyed what I played. I took those three pieces of feedback and framed my expectations accordingly.So back to #1 - Too Expensive for what you get. I got mine apart of the Stand with Ukraine Humble Bundle, of which I wanted other things, and it was for charity I think it was valued over $2500 USD and I payed about $50 USD, so I got my value's worth. But what about those who miss out on that, well as of writing, it's 60% off, bought a copy for a friend and he's been enjoying it.Now on to #2 - It doesn't feel like Left 4 Dead.See here's the sticking point. Players were expecting this game to be the spiritual successor to the Left 4 Dead series, and why wouldn't they? Same Dev's, same genre, same expectations.Well if you wanted a yearly Call of Duty copy/paste job, then go play that. If they simply just copied Left 4 Dead, swapped/expanded characters, added some more maps. Critics would complain that it's just more of the same, and GASP doesn't deserve the amount of asking price, which of course probably would be at the typical AAA starting price. But let's be honest, there aren't really any AAA games that are worth their price.I for one have switched to waiting for sales for all games (even those I really wanted) for two reasons. Launch Issues (bugs) and Price which is all too frequent. If you want to be smart with your money, you'll do the same. You ultimately get a more complete product, for cheaper, and all you have to do is wait 6-12 months. Big deal, go play your other favorite games or your massive steam library backlog which I know you have. These days, you cannot trust that games will be good out of the gate, far too many titles that could be named that ended up being trash.Back 4 Blood IS NOT Left 4 Dead, and it wasn't supposed to be, so if you can look at the game of what it is you'll see why. Keep reading.#3 - PvP Sucks.Look, I'll be honest, I don't care about PvP. I stopped caring around when I stopped playing Overwatch Competitive and it's toxic community. If you're like me and want something fun to play without the member-measuring contest, keep reading. But hey, if you get your jimmies off by besting other players in skilled sportsmanship, talking trash or engaging in coitus with your opponent's moms, then yeah, I bet the PvP isn't that strong, and as I will explain later, the game isn't PvP Focused and never was.PvP in B4B has one team has to survive as long as possible in an arena-like map, where the other team takes control of the special zombies and tried to take them out, then they swap positions. The team that survived the longest wins. This differs from L4D's versus mode where the survivors traversed each map to the next safehouse with the opposition trying to stop them.Now with the way B4B campaign is designed, I can understand why the Dev's decided not to replicate L4D's Versus mode. First, getting 8 players to commit to several-hours long session is asking far to much, the ego of players, especially teams of randoms, are far too fragile and people would leave as soon as one team any significant advantage. This happened a lot in L4D, late joiners are often on the losing team, not fun.***Regardless if you're a L4D fan or not, what should you expect from Back 4 Blood? Is it fun? Is it worth your time? I say yes, especially if you enjoy shooting zombies with friends, of which there are many many games in this genre.At it's core, it's a action coop first person shooter game. It has light rogue-like, and RPG elements. You can play with up to 3 other players in your party and you can play solo offline with 3 AI players if you don't have people to play with, but it's a real treat to play with some of your friends, who I am sure will lead to goofy shenanigans. I used to play a lot RPG games such as Borderlands, Destiny, Warframe, Diablo, etc. There are clear inspirations from those titles, and fans of them will have their loot itch scratched a bit, just know that this game isn't a full fledged RPG, but there's enough "collecting" that feels impactful, and a light grind to get what you are looking for.So let's highlight what works in Back 4 Blood.It's PvE Focused. Converse to what I said about PvP, I love this. I am much older now compared to back when I played Left 4 Dead, and while I hate the toxic nature PvP carries, I do still like action games. So the fact that most of the game's content caters to longer, replayable PvE content, is an absolute dream.Back 4 Blood is way more random, but in a good way. It keeps game play fresh by introducing random effects, such as explosive enemies, fog, evolving multiple types of enemies, boss encounters, and the Card System. This is what some people would describe as "rogue-lite". You play through, random things happen, you adapt to the changes and hopefully overcome them. Generally speaking, the player has a lot of power, but harder difficulties will test you.Look, you don't need to know how TGC games work to understand the card system, basically, each card is a power up (or power down) that can affect you, the monsters, the levels, and even objectives. But as the player, you can collect cards and build a deck of them to gradually crate a refined game play style you enjoy, so while things can get chaotic, you can bring order to it.So far, I've built a deck that is focused on being the healer of the team to keep them in tip top shape, because lord knows what will be thrown at your team, or what your teammates will do to get them all banged up. I also made one focused on melee, and my god, it's a lot of fun cleaving through crowds of angry undead, bonking the heads of tougher foes, and yes, even getting shot by teammates, because I deserve it, but ultimately might will outlive them :)At the time of writing, the game presently has 5 acts. These acts are broken up into smaller sections that range from 2-5 maps that are linked together to create some consistency in narrative. You can play a whole act from beginning to the end, and understand the efforts your team had gone through to fight back the hordes of undead, and regain a foothold for the living.Each act are pretty lengthy, probably requiring you to spent 2-3 evenings to get through them, but you can stop at any time, and your progress will be saved up to the last safe house you passed which is at the beginning of every map. Each map doesn't take too long, I'd say about 10-20 minutes. There are some consequences to failure however, because if your whole team dies, you'll have to use a CONTINUE to try again at the last safehouse you passed. Different difficulty levels will give you a certain number of CONTINUES.As you play through an act, you'll find random weapons scattered throughout the levels, ammo and medication to keep you battle ready, currency to purchase upgrades and SUPPLIES, a currency used outside of an act, to unlock other content, such as cards for your decks and cosmetics for your weapons and character.The game does NOT have premium currency, or microtransactions, just the DLCs or if you wish the Annual Pass which bundles them together. So far they've been pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: Back4Blood is a good fun game, if you like Left4Dead you'll love it, it looks good, runs good and the AI are pretty good at handling themselves.However the settings have an annoying issue, there is no "Exclusive Fullscreen" mode at all, there is only "Borderless Windowed Fullscreen" (Borderless Fullscreen) and it locks the resolution to your monitors maximum resolution so if your running on an older system you cannot change your resolution to increase fps, its a pain but there are work arounds on forums, the other setting is "Windowed Mode" this setting you can change resolution but it might only occupy up to half of your monitors screen depending on the resolution you choose.In terms of starting gear, it is set up much like Left4Dead whereby you have default starting gear that you cannot change, but when in a mission you can use other weapons to carry out the mission via pick ups, the similar to Left4Dead, so you cannot change any gear in the hub area but you can customise unlocked skins n cosmetics in the hub area.Price wise the game is a bit much, so I would suggest getting it on some form of a Sale period, its not that its not worth full price, its more that without "Exclusive Fullscreen" it kinda limits what spec systems can really play the game especially with restricted resolution settings.All in all, if you love Left4Dead its great, it looks good and runs good when you get the video settings in a happy place.

_childDocuments_.review: If it's £20 sure go for it, but that's if it includes the dlcI love Back 4 Blood, but I really don't like what the developers are doing with every update, it's like you get one good thing and then several things that made the game worse.The game currently is lacking variety with a PvP that feels abandoned and a campaign mode with 4 acts and a single boss level with no real variety to the level design, when they boasted about the director originally in the trailers I was hoping for something a little more in depth than "hey today on this level you're going to get a corruption card that makes you need food or sometimes we'll set the level at night"I enjoy replaying the game on nightmare and no hope as I enjoyed the challenge, but you can only do the same 4 acts so many times and with turtle rocks latest idea of keeping player retention by forcing to replay a single act over and over for cards (see my review of dlc for context), it's certainly soured my experience.Back 4 blood should've been a fun time waster with a simplistic formula to keep players coming back for more, but over the last year all we've got was poorly thought out new mechanics (legendary weapons being a prime example, over half are useless and are base epic stat weapons with no means of upgrading them and legendary accessories are poorly utilised because of how scarce they are)a now rather bloated card system that I fear will get needlessly complicated as time goes onand easily the worst vote to kick system I have ever seen, I primarily play solo but the fact you can hold a game hostage if someone doesn't want to go in a hive and it's easy to avoid being kickable really sums up how little turtle rock are listening to feedback.There's fixes on the trello we've been waiting for since launch, some are simple things like seeing the name of a player instead of a bot when they need to be rescued, or the ability to see other players buildsside note, in the latest update, the little taste of mod support we had is currently broken so I can't even use client side mods like the Alpha Hud icons anymore, not sure if it's accidental of not, knowing turtle rock I wouldn't be surprised if this was deliberate

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the pros and cons have been covered in previous reviews but i'll add my 2 cents. One of the biggest complaints from other reviews is "it's not as fun as Left4Dead" which is... debateable. It has some different aspects from Left4Dead, like the deck building and lack of campaign versus. But I would say the biggest difference is that it's not a new/genre-defining game like Left4Dead. If you were a big fan of Left4Dead or played it when you were young and have fond memories of it, this game will not recreate a similar feeling, but honestly neither will any other game. Can't really fault B4B for that.When it comes to difficulty/poor gameplay, the critiques are mostly fair. People seem to think that veteran is where you should start if you aren't a complete newbie to the genre/gaming so you run into way to many randoms with no decent cards/custom decks and you can't really succeed in vet for long without them (for better or worse). Crossplay also doesn't help this as console players do not seem to play as well as other pc players. My biggest issue personally is that this game relies way too much on the "spam mutations" to increase difficulty and yeah, it's very frustrating and not fun to lose over and over because the game spawned 3-4 tall boys at once and your teammates can't hit weakpoints if their life depended on it. I have yet to try nightmare so I can only assume these issues are 10x worse, so keep that in mind.The other thing constantly mentioned is "not worth the price". I disagree completely. There are more missions in this than the base Left4Dead 2 which was $60, if you feel that you wasted money because you don't like the game personally that doesn't mean there is not enough content. If you are comparing it to huge, open-world RPGs or to competitive multiplayer games that you put 100s of hours into then sure you may not get as many hours out of it as other $60 games, but that is more an issue of the video game industry refusing to change the price of a new game from $60 for decades at this point. I won't go on a tangent but really, stop complaining about optional season passes/cosmetics/dlc, unless you want companies to charge you $100 for the base version of new AAA games then they need to make money somehow, games cost way more to make than they did 20 years ago but they still cost the same.Overall, I enjoy the game and would recommend it to fans of the genre, but there are issues. If you do not enjoy grinding/horde-style games then you will not enjoy this one. It is not the Left4Dead sequel some people wanted, but it wasn't supposed to be and it certainly doesn't have to be. It is a fun, mostly mindless, zombie horde shooter, and that is good enough for me.

_childDocuments_.review: PS5 | 765+ Hours, 1 Year. PC version tried, no real differences if not for the smoother controls.[Just my experience.]I was waiting for a game like this for years, a old school genre pioneered by the same parts of the team with Left 4 Dead but with improvements like deeper gameplay, narrative and more in 2021, the cards system really adds to the replay ability and its fun to mess around like a melee deck, healing deck or many more. ❤️‍🔥The gunplay feels pretty damn good, especially with the PS5's Dualsense Adaptive Triggers, not exaggerated but a nice comfortable level of pressure, only negative here is the aiming/camera movement that is not smooth like other FPSs like CoD (on controller ofc), but its easy to get used to it and with the settings you can find your tune! 🔫 Levels have good variation for launch, the level based story is the classic Left 4 Dead style, makes sense, its simple to understand BUT the fact that character dialogues change based on who's in the team for the game its really interesting and just makes you question how much backstory and maybe hints at future plans there are! Nice options for more challenging difficulties too! 🏞️🏚️🏘️There’s many characters (already 8 at launch, more now) that they pulled off having thier own style, moods and looks! There's one for everyone, fun, serious, crazy and weird (looking at Hoffman and his shenanigans), all to love!  👥👥👥👥Swarm i haven't played much at first, but now that i got decks and somewhat strategy is pretty fun, but only thing about it not really right for me is the matchmaking which 90% of the times a team as a WAY larger skill gap than the other, this makes often to see people quitting early or just not fun games (too hard or too easy), when you finally get a game in the between or playing with friends in private match its where its fun! 🆚Only MTX are the Expansions which content its also shareable with friends by beign in the same lobby, work in random/public/quickplay matches too! 💲🚫Expectations met, i just love it and cant get enough of it! ✅Back to slaying ridden i go! 🩸 My Multiplayer GOTY for 2021. 🎮--<Expansion/Updates overall review section>—————————-<YEAR 1>—————————The first major updates and first Expansion really made the game even better than ever, with now way more balanced and enjoyable matches, always fixing bugs, new content like the new 7 levels/hives that can appear in the launch levels new legendary weapons and items, 2 new characters, new burn cards, the change that now at the start of a match you draw your whole deck instead of the more “pick in this level” kind of thing and more… the support from devs is really good, also lovely to talk to in thier Discord. 🕳️🦠Expansion 2 is the biggest yet, adding 6 new levels making the new Act 5, new weapons, items, a new character, cosmetics and the new extreme difficulty called No Hope.This Expansion takes the world and story into a deeper plot with its Cultists called the Children of the Worm, a mix between Ridden and Humans. The creativity of level design in this act is really great, from objectives to do to plot moments/set pieces. Great new character Dan with his insane god-like attitude which really makes him apart from the group. Very cool new cards that now add abilities that you pay with ammo to activate making decks even more varied. And like the previous (and future) expansions, friends can play the new stuff by playing with at least 1 person who has it! Best expansion yet. Though this act in No Hope difficulty is BRUTAL kinda too much. 👹Nice smaller yet interesting Halloween/October update, few skins, Heng revamp, new legendary items etc.. 🎃Expansion 3, wow, this one is a banger. 5 beautiful new levels that this time really varies in different aesthetics, from a resort filled with nature to a strictly urban area with a huge broadcasting building to a museum that goes from science to the prehistoric and finishing off in a giant arena. All with intense moments and set pieces to create your path forward, all made with beautiful designs and colors. The best levels in the game for me. The new Cleaner Tala is a good addition for players that like to do damage (bleeding damage on enemies) but also defending because of her tall friend Jeff, a mutated ally that will smash your way through hordes if called by a cleaner with its whistle, awesome addition. All this with the new melee attachments, cards, cosmetics, a flamethrower and a special (and powerful) single use pocket rocket launcher to create an even more powerful (and stylish) arsenal to kill the ridden, like the new Sentinel a new multi attack monstrosity that will need to be taken care of sooner than later and a new final boss. Also the story got a good direction here with more great cutscenes! Trial of the Worm is a great new PvE mode where you, you and your friends or with randoms can collaborate to create your own custom 4 levels adventure by voting to add statistics that will challenge you and voting one level map at a time (with different corruption cards themselves) all this for one goal… getting to the top of the new leaderboards, the bigger the challenge the more points you get! If you still haven’t joined Back 4 Blood but still having doubts, i can absolutely say that with a sale (since they are common) + annual pass you’ll now get the best experience of this game! (Even better with friends!) Looking forward to what’s next (hopefully) for Back 4 Blood.

_childDocuments_.review: This how you shoot for Left For Dead 3 and miss. This isn't inherently a bad game but it's not exactly good either.The good parts,: The maps are nicely designed and interesting with a variety of close quarters and ranged combat.It looks good, the character and weapon models are nice. The textures and lighting are well used.It didn't freeze, crash or stop taking mouse and keyboard inputs often.The flame are nice and I like the explosive effects.The corruption cards are at least an interesting way to vary game play, I don't really care about their effects nor do I modify my game tactics to compensate for them but they are an attempt to keep game play fresh i suppose.The bad: Everything else.The gun play is average at best, every weapon in each class feels almost exactly like every other weapon in it.Gun sounds, firearms are loud, painfully so at times. If you fire a shotgun or rifle, you know about it and so does everyone around you. The weapon sounds are so muted and lacking in distinctiveness in this game  that it strips immersion out of the game.The tedious in game character chatter, nothing more needs to be said on this, it stands for itself. The in game economy, This allows you to purchase items to help you with your play through. It is pretty much pointless. I don't know if there is a Micro transaction system in this game as I'm never going to use it if there is one, so I didn't look for it.Choose any character, it makes no real difference who you choose, they are all so generic.The enemy types,  No real imagination spent on these, some could be considered a lift and re-skin from Left For Dead 2. They are either annoying or simple bullet sponges. The choice to add dead space type weak points to enemies is in my opinion a bad one, that mechanic is so over used and played out. The balance: They simply could not get the game play balance to feel thought through. You find ammunition everywhere for some reason and your comrades seem to be able to drop it all the time to assist you. The horde are no longer a real threat, they are there to distract you so that the endless repeated appearances of the mutated zombies feels less obvious. This should be called, "Special infected the game". Oh look, a Crusher, oh look a Tallboy followed by  a bloater......sorry an exploader. The horde used to be a danger to the player, the special infected were there to make the horde harder to fight. Now it is the opposite and it simply does not work.The atmosphere: This feels like the division or any tripe dropped by Ubisoft. The horror feel and suspense has been lost, replaced by better visuals certainly but the feeling that you are some of the last human beings left alive fighting to survive just isn't there. This game lacks character, it feels like a Left for Dead knock off, not a successor.This might seem harsh and I don't want you to think this is a bad game, its not but its not great either. While I don't think its terrible, I would not recommend this to a friend. It feels like it is a grind to play it. 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up playing the L4D games back on the Xbox with friends, this game feels like a breath of fresh air. TL;DR - The card system, gunplay, level design, and characters are all great, and add to a very successful replayability factor.[[Pros and Cons]]Pros:- The card system is extremely fun to play around with, allowing completely different gameplay styles and overall gameplay experiences. - The games level design and art style are captivating and immersive, specifically the design of "The Clog" area.- The difficulty of the game, while quite challenging at times, is enjoyable. The difficulty and the card system combined gives this game a lot replayability, as it gives you something to work towards; building a better deck to take on the harder difficulty. - The characters are all well designed, and while some of the voice lines are cheesy, I kinda find it charming. I laugh at how cheesy they are, it always puts a smile on my face. - The gunplay also feels very well crafted. It's snappy, the animations are smooth, and I like diversifying how my weapons are used with attachments.- The game devs are extremely invested in the community. From a public Discord server ran by devs, to a trello board that posts lists on what they're currently working on, what they have done, and what they plan on doing, they truly do care about what changes the community wants to the game, and these points show it.- The Bar Room Blitz level. It's self-explanatory.- The boss ridden of the game (The Ogre, The Breaker and The Hag) are all very fun to fight. The Ogre is this giant behemoth of a ridden that's fun to gang up against with your team, The Breaker requires focus and coordination from you and your team to take down due to having tough armour plating therefore requiring you and your team to all target different or the same weak points, and The Hag has horrifying music, a very unique but scary design, and a terrifying way of killing you. Honestly the best Mutation of the Ridden, and some of the best monster design I've seen in awhile.Cons:- The price is a little high. I'd say knock 20$ off of it, and that'd be perfect. Though this point can change based on the content they add after release.- The lack of enemy variety (visually) is a little disappointing. Instead of the Exploders, Crushers and Bruisers all being a part of a Reeker or Tallboy family, each one should have had a more distinctive, characterised design. There are plenty of enemy variation, but they all feel the same due to very similar visual appearances and not any unique weak point variation.- I'd love to see more lore building. How exactly the Devil Worms function (regarding nests and how it mutates other ridden) should be explained more in game. Another topic that should be explored is with what kind of parasite the Devil Dorms are, why/how are certain survivors immune? Another lore topic that would be interesting would be more backstory for the cleaners (why the way they are, who they were before the collapse etc.).- For the love of god please let alarmed doors take a few bullets before setting off an alarm. I can't tell you how many times I've set off an alarm for a door I didn't even see due to a stray bullet hitting it. Sometimes they don't even give you enough time to notice they're there to avoid them.I would give this game an overall:[[8/10]]I highly recommend you pick this game up. It's an absolute blast with friends, and has great replayability!Note: I did not include "No Solo Progression" as a Con, as Turtle Rock has already stated they are currently working on changing that.
