_childDocuments_.review: Let me state at the very beginning - the game is not worth the price they ask. If you plan on getting this game for the original price then I am giving it a negative recommendation.I bought the game at heavy discount (70% off) and I am glad I did cause it was totaly worth the money I paid. However I wouldnt be satisfied with paying 60$ for it. At least half of that price is what the game should cost.With that out of the way let me explain to you what the game is in its current - FINAL - state.It is a game that is based on the L4D formula but it is NOT the "L4D3" that many wished it to be. The game only uses the base concept of L4D and then takes it into its own direction.Major difference from L4D is that B4B puts a much heavier emphasis on special enemies rather then hoards of regular zombies - they are much more frequent and pose a much more significant threat. There are still buttload of zombies but they are not the main and biggest threat in this game.The game has sth called the card system and while at the launch of the game it turned out to be pretty horrendous - developers made a major change that actually turned it into a really great concept that allows you to basicly create your own unique class as opposed to typical way it works aka certain class has certain skills. In here you have no class - you just have cards which in essence act as "skill" and you select 15 cards to act as your "class" and they are all active the moment you start the map (before it worked like you were starting with few cards being active and activated more with each map you completed in the campaing). It works and it is great. Especialy since you can add even more cards as you play the maps further boosting your skillset.There is also a much more expanded gun mechanics in B4B where you can find attachments for guns that further expand their stats. At first when the game launched, you couldnt detach those attachments in any way except by installing an attachment that would replace the one you have. It was horrendous system and it didnt work. Many people were angry and rightfuly so cause when you found a better gun you couldnt transfer your attachments to it. Well now that changed and you can detach attachments in Safe Rooms or even outside of them if you equip yourself with a card that grants you this ability and now it works nicely and just how it should've in the beginning.What is also different in B4B when compared to L4D is that here choosing what character you play does indeed matter as they have their own unique perk that applies to them and also a unique team perk that boosts the entire team. So it is a nice touch.Maps are great and I really like the environment that the game is placed in. You can find many people crying and shouting "They are reusing the SAME MAPS" when in reality some maps have indeed SMALL PARTS that are shared with other maps but that is totaly natural cause in most campaings you will start at this FORT that is outside a city that has become survivors stronghold and it is being invaded at the very start of the game. So you start at the fort and enter the city through the main gate and you have same street there BUT you almost immidately take a DIFFERENT DIRECTION there and move to a totaly new area and from there it is nothing that you will see in other maps... so yeah... that main street that is shared in like 3 maps throughout the game that had people screaming and shouting "REUSED MAPS".As far as the actual gameplay is involved - it is pretty solid stuff. Teamwork is essential to succeed and with the card system that was mentioned before you can have people play a very specific role in the group - melee specialist, medic, heavy gun expert or even try to be a bit of jack of all trades. The possibilites are almost endless in that regard since you choose each card aka skill yourself and nothing is being forced on you. Shooting feels satisfactory. Guns feel just right and there is quite a nice variety to them. Each time you play there are mutators that can make the same map play quite differently by having different mutations of specials on it (each special has couple of different variants that makes them do different things). Throughout the maps you collect coins that are used as currency for many things in the game - buying stuff, using extra medical care, detaching gun attachments and all sorts of other stuff. After completing maps you also get points that allow you to buy new cards or cosmetic stuff which is nice cause it gives you the incentive to replay the game to unlock more.Missions are varied, there are boss fights that are more threating then Tanks from L4D. And there is even an Uber Boss fight in the game's finale where the entire map is about fighting this gigantic creature. There are some voices that scream that the game is full of bugs but I personaly in the time I played didnt experience anything gamebreaking. Some small glitches or some minor bugs happen from time to time but nothing that forced me to restart the game.After the game launched people rightfuly so complained about the game having insane difficulty level even on normal and I am glad that in the current version it has been quite nicely ironed out and now game feels much more accessible even on higher ones.The last thing I will say is a HUGE PRAISE to developers for a certain feature that they introduced to the game regarding bots and in my opinion this is sth that SHOULD BECOME A GOLDEN STANDARD IN ALL L4D-like games. So the feature that I am talking about is "possesing bots" after you die. Normaly in other games like that, for example WWZ Aftermath or Vermintide 2 when you play with bots and you die, the game ends if there is no human players left or you need to wait for respawn. In B4B when you die and bots are still alive - you can jump into one of them and play as them until you find your original character once it respawns and rescue it. Then the game automaticly transfers you back into your original survivor. Simple yet brilliant - I honestly have hard time now when playing games that dont have this feature to accept that they didnt come up with it in their games.Overall - the game is good and you will like it if you dont expect it to be L4D3 and you just let it be its own thing... and also if you buy it on significant sale cause the initial price that they ask is simply ridicolousIf you like coop games and are looking for a place to learn about interesting games with this feature I recommend checking out my Steam curator

_childDocuments_.review: B4B is a good game but it gets stale really fast and isn't memorable, TurtleRock decided to go with quantity over quality, there are a ton of levels but most of them use the same areas for them and are very short, the entire time you are nonstop killing because every area is just filled with zombies, even areas that are meant to serve as downtime.  The amount of special infected is just too many, there's multiple types of the same specials that just do slightly different things, and there's nothing actually special about them, no special noises or music, just a bigger zombie with a glowing weak spot, and there are way to many of them at one time, you can easily kill around 50 in a level, the levels are also really short so every five feet you have to kill 3 more of them. The game just devolves into shooting, just keep shooting, it doesn't matter what it is or what it does just shoot it.  They added special commons that have things like spikes or explode, but it doesn't matter since you still just shoot them.  They tried to add a lot of customizability with different skins for the cleaners, weapon skins and attachments, but there's no really good skins for guns or cleaners that make an actual difference, and attachments don't transfer from gun to gun so whenever you find a better version of the gun you'r using you have to restart in getting good attachments.  The deck system is kinda cool but some of the builds are just completely invalidated.  In short the game is just shoot zombies constantly, never stopping, no downtime, the customizablity is bad, the special infected are boring and not memorable, the amount of zombies is just too much, and the game gets extremely boring very fast.  L4d2 came out almost 15 years ago but still manages to be more fun and memorable than this game, and for a 1/6th of the price.

_childDocuments_.review: This has all of the fantastic co-op mayhem of L4D and it's sequel and also offers a fantastic array of new features and abilities:*Graphically I like the aesthetic and appreciate some of the more modern Dx12 techniques.*Gunplay is tight and crisp. The attachment upgrades give a real positive and tangible boost to the active weapon. You can also upgrade secondary weapons.*There is a fine assortment of different weapon types and plenty of them (At least 30), which is quite a treat.  *Control is responsive and easy to adjust on both Keyboard\Mouse but also Controllers*The money\resource system promotes exploration and the shareable cash you find as you traverse an area reduces competition thus promoting the spirit of teamwork and cohesion. *I find the maps are very attractive, art assets are spot on, routing makes sense and I only get lost for short amounts of time, relieving a lot of frustration :) *The AI is more than competent and I find the later Acts appropriately challenging.*PVP mode can be very fun in-between running missions*The community has been mostly embracing of new players, working together, formulating strats and sharing tips and techniques.  (There are exceptions of course, but the vast majority of pubbers I have played with have been pretty damned cool). *The card System adds replay ability, depth and granularity towards shaping your play style. It took a moment to wrap my head around, but once I caught on, I was building decks specific to Shotgun Mayhem- (Quick Reload and additional damage, for instance)- Stealth Builds and Teamboosting decks, the list goes on. It really adds an extra dimension to how I play each mission and when working with others we can play decks that compliment each other.  It makes more sense when you see it in action :)All in all a well rounded game and a worthy successor.  I would easily recommend to anyone.I am hopeful they will add in a survival mode eventually :)

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, an honest, short review.Graphics are great and really well optimized, I have a 2070 TI and run epic settings, getting 175+ fps CONSISTENTLY. Characters are fun and well animated.Game play like left for dead but with more "customization" (you actually need strategy, hence the card system)NOW THE BIG MOAN: The 60$ Price tag, look, I haven't played a game that costed 60$ and had the game be playable and not a buggy mess for, well not since me playing Mario Galaxy. So, 60$ for me, is worth the game being this polished (minus the team bot AI, and I'll get to that).Overall, in terms of price, its a good game and extremely enjoyable with friends, so at least for me, it warrants the price.Though, if you think you can get it on sale for 40$, do it. Anyhow, Bot Ai sucks, it needs to be better. Is it difficult: Yes, I'd say veteran mode is the equivalent of Expert mode on L4D2. Nightmare mode is just, an actual nightmare, and this is where creating a deck is absolutely essential. In sum, this isn't L4D2 with bells and whistles, nor is it a third game, its a seperate zombie shooter with new story, characters, and game play. If you see people say "it's easy" they are just a person who plays COD zombies, they are retarded and don't even take time to appreciate the game. Play the game with buddies, have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Normal mode is too easy, barely a challenge. Veteran mode, the "mid-tier" difficulty is too punishing. Even when playing with more cards unlocked and with a well composed team the game has no difficulty curve. When starting an act with only a couple of cards the game has the same level of difficulty as the end of the same act, there is no buildup whatsoever, only either disappointment or punishment depending on the setting you choose. The AI director is also too punishing, it will often spawn enemies directly behind you (ie in the same room with no windows that you just cleared) as soon as your team looks away. This leads to some very un-fun moments that spoil an otherwise mechanically sound game. The weapons feel good, the perks feel good, and the level design is great. The aggressive AI and lack of flexibility on difficulty make most of these good design elements feel wasted and frustrating far too often. Hopefully Turtle Rock fine tunes these additional gameplay elements, until then I would recommend a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Back 4 Blood feels like 2 steps forward, but 8 steps back. It's nice to have a new zombie horde shooter in high quality graphics, and a good engine to support it on. There is high paced action fun to be had with friends here. But there's quite a few teeth grindingly frustrating aspects of this game that just lets me down. I want this to be the success story of Turtle Rock bringing their old franchise that practically defined the 4 player co-op experience into the modern day graphics we have now but unfortunately it falls flat of its predecessor. If I had to give you advice on how to properly enjoy it. Get some friends, and complete the story campaign on recruit difficulty a handful of times. Do not progress to veteran difficulty. Do not attempt to play it singleplayer. And God help you with competent teammates if you solo queue.The card system is not the revolution this game thinks it is, nor is it very good. It hypes it up as being able to play game winning cards, but aside from a few they just don't help much in a pinch. They don't let you counter the cards the Director plays against you very well, particularly since your deck is always pre-made going into a run. Besides, who loads up a zombie shooter to sort through a hundred cards and picking out a deck? Most of the cards don't even provide straight benefits either. A lot of them help in a certain area, but hinder others.Game balance for the special infected is a huge issue. You might have heard it before, and probably know of the infamous Retch and Hocker by now. If not the Retch is massively irritating because it just took the Left 4 Dead 2 spitter, made it ultra beefy, and able to just sprint off after dealing massive damage to you from range. Often without you even realising it is there until you get bile on you. The Hocker is the annoying combination of the Smoker and Hunter. It bounces around like the Hunter, but can pin you from a distance like the Smoker. It's hard to detect, annoying to get stuck by, and the source of your problem has likely already leapt away to safety before your teammates even realise your predicament. In Left 4 Dead, you could free your teammates pretty easily and quickly by either shooting the Hunter or the Smoker itself, shoving it off, or shooting the tongue. You had a few snap decision ways to free your teammate and eliminate the problem. In Back 4 Blood, all you can hope is someone already pinged the Hocker, and you can shoot it before it leaps 5 times away into cover. You can only shove your teammates to free them. And the Retch you're almost guaranteed to take massive damage from it unless you're lucky and spot it in the distance. The Tallboys have their weak spot on the arm always behind their back, and thus facing away from you. I guess the idea here is to figure out which person it is targeting, and letting the team flank it. Unfortunately, you're almost always in a cramped indoor environment and usually grouped close together. It can cover distance pretty fast when it wants to, and slam the ground for an area of effect that does decent damage. Or a mutation just flat out grabs you and deals massive damage until you get freed by your teammates. This time, your only option is to shoot it, and hope you spam enough damage in to kill it quickly. Mind you any number, and combinations of these things can spawn in at once. The Director can and will just throw 3 Retches, 2 Hockers, and 6 Tallboys at your team at once, and it becomes an inevitable mess of just being forced to take massive damage. It does not feel like there is much you can do to prevent the specials from attacking, and you will always be taking damage. Unlike Left 4 Dead where you could defeat the specials before they got to you by being aware, and having good aim.Trauma. Trauma can absolutely be thrown into the bin. In Back 4 Blood you will never not be taking damage. Some of that damage is permanent, and cannot be removed by normal healing items unless you sink several thousand in game currency to purchase it. There are fixed spawn locations around maps that have first aid cabinets where you can heal some trauma, and you can find more if you remember to bring tool kits to open stashes. On Recruit, trauma isn't usually a huge issue. At least, not if you understand how to manage it. The cabinets let your team heal 4 times for free, so presumably one use per player. If you were to bump it up to Veteran only ONE player can use it for free. Others must pay 400 in game coins to use it. Keep in mind, this difficulty you're taking even more damage, and trauma ramps up quickly unlike in recruit. Compare that to Left 4 Dead where you get one first aid kit that restored you to almost full health and reset your downs. More importantly, your maximum health was never ticking down constantly in Left 4 Dead. I am not sure why this mechanic is introduced, but I can definitely say it is unpleasant and we could really do without it especially when it is much harder to avoid taking damage. God help you if any of them are given the "armoured" mutation which provides a shield you have to take down first before you can even start damaging the weak point. I miss being able to click on the head, which is above the shoulders, and the thing dies mentality of Left 4 Dead.Veteran difficulty, which presumably is the normal mode, is such an awkward lurch from recruit. If you read the descriptions that differ recruit from veteran some noticeable things pop up, and are even more glaring once you load into the game. Recruit lowers the amount of HP infected have, as well as how much damage they deal to you. It increases how much ammo you can carry in reserve. It lowers the rate at which you accrue trauma. It also allows you to heal at medicine cabinets 4 times for free to help restore each player to maximum health. However, when you jump to veteran things change drastically. The infected no longer have toned down HP and damage. You no longer have the same carrying capacity for ammo. So not only does it take two more shots to deal with infected, but your carrying load is halved. The infected deal significantly more damage, and your ability to recover from said damage is hindered. You take more trauma, and have less opportunity to deal with it. Furthermore, bosses show up far more often. It becomes a difficulty overhang instead of a naturally progressing curve to ease players up to more of a challenge. Common infected are also annoying as you progress. Unlike Left 4 Dead where the common infected were all just ordinary, Back 4 Blood infected get progressively more difficult. Act 3 infected will take stronger weapons to put down, and deal more damage. They also get added effects to them like flames, explosive heads, or acid. Acid ones should be canned from the game entirely. Especially when you have to run through tight corridors during an endless horde to the safe room. It becomes impossible to make any progress without sacrificing health just by trying to walk forward. Also anyone who wanted to run a melee build, hope you are ok with taking unavoidable damage (and thus trauma) or abandoning your zombie chopping fun for a firearm.There are a lot of grievances that need to be addressed for Back 4 Blood to become the endlessly replayable and fun game its predecessor has. Turtle Rock needs to listen to feedback, and tweak their game. More importantly, I think their attitude towards the shaping of this game needs to change. It does not feel like it is designed with players to overcome challenges in mind. It feels like it was designed to counter any strategy the players could conceive of, and thus create frustration. Back 4 Blood is missing the elegant and balanced design of its predecessor. The game needs to focus on letting the players adapt and have fun naturally, not just constantly oppressing them in every conceivable way.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty apparent that the developer's can't really make a well-rounded game even after only a couple hours of play. And by the time you've completed the campaign, you're left with a feeling of, "is that it?" because the only thing this game has on offer is decent gunplay. The characters suck, and repeatedly fail at making witty remarks. The campaign levels are incredibly one-note with no atmosphere whatsoever; so much so that I can barely recall a single level. And the card system is pretty unwelcome in this kind of game. I want my shooters to be a test of my skill at shooting, not deck-building, and that's coming from someone who loves deck-building games more than just about any other kind of game. But without the deck-building, then the game would have to rely on a good gameplay foundation, which this game does not have. The zombies are just not that fun to kill, and the special zombies are so uninteresting it's painful. Charging $60 for a game this unrefined should be criminal.

In its short run, they released a number of DLC packs that I believe added value to the game. I will say that this game will not have the longevity that L4D has, and that can be attributed to workshop contributions. I do believe that this game is fun for the meantime, but it inevitably will completely die down. Ultimately, I think this game is enjoyable and I would recommend it. However, I think people would be better off buying this game during a sale. This game's player base has definitely dwindled since the release, and certain times of the day it might take a little time to find a match. If you are able to overlook all the hate this game receives and some problems here and there, I think there is still fun to be had on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's disheartening to witness the considerable amount of criticism directed towards this game, despite its actual quality and the consistent effort put into its development and subsequent updates. While it faced a somewhat rocky launch, such occurrences are not uncommon nowadays, and I've maintained regular play since its initial release.There appears to be a faction of hardcore Left 4 Dead 2 enthusiasts asserting its superiority, but this claim doesn't hold up. Let me debunk this by addressing the unique features that make this game outstanding. First, the card system, often disliked by some due to biased reasons tied to its name rather than its actual functionality. In reality, it's a modifier system that introduces diverse challenges in each level/run. The game selects a set of cards (modifiers) based on difficulty and other factors, allowing you and your team the opportunity to choose your own counter modifiers, enhancing the gameplay significantly.The variety of classes adds another layer of depth. Each character, and there are more than four, comes with distinct starting weapons, perks, and voice dialogue, providing an entertaining and dynamic experience. The incorporation of weapon upgrades, attachments, and item upgrades is self-explanatory and crucial for creating customizable loadouts/builds that will be required through the playthrough, especially on higher difficulty levels. it also helps ensure sustained replayability. The addition of skins as rewards adds an extra layer of enjoyment, Supply points, duffel bags, and skull totems are all currencies that contribute to a unique mechanic, allowing players to collect them through levels/runs and each being spent towards different rewards. The game would likely be widely praised and beloved if it hadn't been perceived as Left 4 Dead 3. While it serves as a spiritual successor, it is a very well-executed tribute to Left 4 Dead. Those expecting and adamant about it being Left 4 Dead 3 were left disappointed, resulting in an initial negative perception. Reading through the comments, one quickly encounters Left 4 Dead elitists claiming it's not L4D. They are correct; it's not. In fact, it surpasses Left 4 Dead in various aspects. Aside from perhaps story and character depth, which it still does fairly well.  It's essential to assess a game for what it is rather than what it isn't, or better yet, avoid projecting expectations onto it.  However, it's worth noting that the current price tag of $79.99 might be a bit steep for many potential players. While the game is undoubtedly worth its price, a more budget-friendly approach could be to wait for a sale or check other vendors. It's currently available for $5 in my area from another vendor. (I can even use the product key to add it to my steam account) This way, enthusiasts can enjoy the game without straining their wallets.

A pinned survivor literally does a 🧍‍♂️, and a pounced survivor freed goes straight from "on the ground" to "🧍‍♂️" in less than 0.5 seconds. It also is very frustrating that there is no reactive counterplay available to these other than strafing and getting lucky. _childDocuments_.review: A little over a year and I have to say I am very disappointed despite the effort these developers put in. The game, it's play, the story, the community, just EVERYTHING is and will forever be a subpar effort to reboot L4D. Er... I mean... a subpar attempt at creating a new and unique zombie shooter experience. And because this community is utter garbage, playing with randoms is about as fun as lighting yourself on fire or playing Call of Duty. From the start this seemed fun and promising but as you advance in the campaign you are just let down run after run after run with things like the high level of repetition, weird laughable in game character dialogue and just a plethora of other things to suggest these developers have zero imagination. It's just easier to rinse and repeat it seems.Virtually no story line just your typical "Zed Apocalypse is happening" story which I am not upset about, but this new update, "Children of the Worm", tried to implement some sort of narrative as if the developers said, "Welp, we are already heading toward an aimless route, so might as well try this." It was a halfway decent 4 player co-op zombie shooter, but now I don't even know. Take this description taken verbatim from their website,"...These once-human hosts of a deadly parasite have turned into terrifying creatures bent on devouring what remains of civilization. With humanity’s extinction on the line, it’s up to you and your friends to take the fight to the enemy, eradicate the Ridden, and reclaim the world." Okay, so why is it we now face off against people? This really showcases the developers lack of direction as now during the game-play you battle snipers, people throwing jars of green garbage at you, bear people (literally charging at you with bear claws) and archers firing flame tips. If it looks like a human, acts like a human, talks like a human and shoots back at you like a human, then it's a human. So instead of "eradicating the Ridden" with your pals, you are now additionally fighting against a cult of survivors... where is this going? And if that's not bad enough now as you run through these maps there are bear traps interspersed along the way. To this I ask, Why?I'm beginning to wonder if at every Update meeting they spin a wheel of sorts with a set of developers name on it to decide who will be the creative head for the update. Maybe you'll get to battle cyborgs in the next update. I say "you'll" because I wont be.This game should've stayed in it's BETA phase, at least they could have an excuse for all the bugs and claim they are testing things out in order to give us a polished game. Can't believe I pre-ordered the 100 dollar package, and sadly I convinced at least one other to do the same. Never again Turtle Rock.

_childDocuments_.review: The Positives:- Kept the core gameplay of L4D with short levels tied into an overall larger "Act" (the B4B version of L4D's Campaigns) which provide fun gameplay without having to dedicate too much time to a single session.- I actually enjoyed the "build as you go" component with grabbing better, stronger weapons and finding/buying attachments along the way.- Tony Todd- The card system is great. I was skeptical it wouldn't be anything more than a gimmick and an excuse for microtransactions but they actually add a very fun component to the game. You can build decks that are essentially like building character abilities and stats in an RPG and each deck can focus on whatever you want (sniping, healing, melee, etc).- The team play component is very well done with a lot of focus on planning strategies based on character abilities. Having to strategize who takes what guns to conserve ammo and being able to drop ammo and money allows you to plan your run and you can buy team upgrades and play team-based cards in your deck.- In that same vein, a large variety of items add to that strategy component, like a healer carrying med packs and having a dedicated toolkit person to open locked and alarmed doors.- Guns are pretty well balanced for the most part. They feel nice and the customization adds some complexity to the game.The Negatives:- The Cleaner (Player) AI is... bad. Like... very bad.- The difficulty scaling is horribly unbalanced. Recruit is a cakewalk (at least for the first two Acts), Veteran is quite difficult, and I haven't even attempted Nightmare yet. It's like the difficulties are easy, hard, and hardest. There's no nice middle ground to build you up for the harder difficulties. Even on Recruit the later campaigns get oddly tough for a low difficulty setting. There doesn't seem to be a good entry level for new players and the game scales too quickly for it to have a middle ground for casual players who want a little challenge.- Mutated have a tendency to spawn ridiculously fast at times and can get overwhelming when you're let go from a Tallboy's grab only to get frozen by a Hocker while your teammate gets grabbed by a Stalker all at once.- The campaign is oddly linear. With L4D2 there was a general structure on level direction but there was a bit of random changes that altered how you got there - different barricades, open doors, pathways, stuff like that. B4B has a couple instances where a room or two is boarded off differently, some bosses will spawn in different points and that's about it. I guess I was expecting a bit more of a dynamic level design for a 2021 game to keep the gameplay fresh.- Once you beat the campaign there's not a whole lot to do. Somehow L4D was able to keep me entertained for hours and hours despite the same few levels but for some reason I can't get that same enjoyment out of this one. It might be my own fault, but still a negative for me anyway. At least a horde mode or other goals wouldn't go amiss.- The customization is kinda lacking. You get 2-4 different skin choices for each gun and player which sounds like a lot until you realize you want to have a couple different camo options for your M1911 and all you have is a light green and a 'Murica skin.The Nitpicks:- I really, really wish I could remove attachments. If I get a Barrett with a red dot sight and pick up a SCAR with a long scope I would love to be able to swap them but you have to live with it until you find or buy a different attachment.- None of the characters really stuck with me. I appreciate that they all have their different perks to make them unique but none of them really have any worthwhile personality, at least compared to characters we grew to appreciate in L4D. That also might just be my tastes so not a huge deal. The dialogue is rather off at times and interactions feel very robotic.- Really nitpicking here but some guns have two reload animations depending on whether you use all of the magazine or part of it. This is great and I appreciate it... except it doesn't do it on all of them. Consistency is important to me, dangit!Overall, the game is a lot of fun most of the time. It's got the core aspect of what made its predecessors repeatedly enjoyable while trying some new things. It needs a bit of work, and I am not 100% sure if the price point justifies the content but it still scratches that L4D itch that we've been having for years and I look forward to seeing what the DLC brings to the table. Thank you for all your work on this, Turtle Rock!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Review: Game is fun, give it a chance, buy it on sale, have fun with the homies. Game has improved a lot since launch including the netcoding and balancing. DLC is accessible to everyone in lobby as long as one person owns it.Rambling Room Temp IQ Review:This game is similar to Left 4 Dead in the sense that, there is safe rooms, explosive canisters, special mutations and hordes where you run a gauntlet from A to B with some stops in between. That's about it though, the game isn't meant to be played the same, game requires coordination (which people drop a dislike about in a team based game???) so its great for co op with people. The way I describe this game is it's a FPS Gauntlet with rougelite elements and MTG commander built in. Starting off you choose your cleaner(commander) which has their on two sets of perks and one passive perk, and you make a deck built around that player (if you're trying to be optimal, not necessarily required if you can coordinate with a team). Then you build a singleton 15 card deck, these cards have a variety of mechanics for healing, ammo, damage, buffs, debuffs, damage resistant, trigger on specific actions etc. You progressively get stronger as you continue through the games act which is divided into several chapters/levels. You progressively gain strength choosing a card every level but so does the enemy, at the beginning of every level, the AI director chooses cards/modifiers (varies with difficulty). When you first start playing you don't have all the cards unlocked but you gain supply points for beating levels (supply points vary with difficulty, and team members that made it to the end alive). You spend supply points in the ingame hub area for things such as cards, emblems, cosmetics, and burn cards. Burns cards are cards that are single use and can be used at the beginning of every level by each member of the team. They mainly are used for economy and recovery. This game has a lot going on and I think that's why people are really struggling (that and people lacking coordination, comes with any team based game). Visuals are alright, music is eh, dont really notice it usually because youre busy trying to survive. Gunplay is excellent and the game is very well optimized especially when using FSR, practically anything can play it (running a 1070 and getting well above 100 fps). Content wise they reused a lot of areas for the acts but DLC is dropping and the great part about that is only one person in the lobby needs to have access to the dlc for everyone else to have it. LOTS of issues have been fixed since release and the game plays a lot better than it used to. Crossplay in the game is seamless with the social id system for adding players so that's a plus. Netcoding is surprisingly good now, been playing with people from EU sometimes without much problems. There's tons to talk about mechanics-wise. Players are usually willing to explain lots of the mechanics if you talk them on the back 4 blood server or just watch videos on it (shout out to Swingpoynt).Conclusion: Overall the game is fun and has really improved a lot since launch, devs have constantly updated mechanics, cards etc.Recommend buying this game on sale with the dlc pass (got it for $52). Hyped for the new content drop.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge Left 4 Dead 2 fan and used to play it a LOT with certain friends but eventually it did get boring with the lack of variety and some outdated things. This is basically the perfect replacement for me and my friends and really fun.It has the things that are good about Left 4 Dead 2 and improves on them. Actual character progression and the deck-building system are fun and the variety when it comes to weapons is nice. There is a decent amount of attachments for weapons as well and things go up in quality as you progress which means you don't end up with the same weapon for your entire run. The characters are diverse both in general and when it comes to skills. Could do with more variety in cosmetics though, I assume that's something that will be added to over time.Enemy variety is VERY nice and though I'm not personally a fan of PvP the playable Ridden seem fun to play with solid controls. They are definitely fun to fight against. Boss Fights are tense and fun!I appreciate the accessibility options and the fact that the game starts with text-to-speech on and then gives you the option to turn it off since I imagine that makes it easier for people who rely on that. Options in general are nice and comprehensive enough.My performance is very good even at high settings, I didn't have any stutters even with masses of enemies and effects on screen at the same time. The audio options are nice too, especially the Night mode. One gripe I do have is that unlike Left 4 Dead 2, this game doesn't give you an option to go AFK and let a bot take over but doesn't allow the game to be paused for all players either. It's terribly inconvenient when someone needs to take a phone call or run to do something for a moment. Some sort of vote to pause feature would be useful. I imagine the lack of a bot taking over is due to the fact that you actually get experience points in this game which is pretty understandable.The guns feel and look really nice. I find especially the weapon sounds really satisfying personally though I can't vouch for realism or accuracy. All weapons feel very distinct as well. I wouldn't mind some more fancy attachments but the amount that's there isn't lacking or anything. Something like temporary attachments or rounds that degrade with use would be nice but since we've only completed Act 1 so far it's possible that those are available later.Graphics-wise the game is pretty nice especially considering how smoothly it runs (for me at least) and I like the different designs of the Ridden. The effects arent bad either Decent quality all around.Basically, I like pretty much everything about the game. I'd only add a pause feature, more unlockable cosmetics and maybe some more out there attachments.10/10 game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember L4D? Yeah, no.The comparison could be unfair, but it is what it is.MAIN CONS:◉ Zombies design and special infected. Being a concept artist I'll admit I might come off as picky about this, but the undead (all, special infected included) are extremely bland and look way too similar. You barely can differentiate them, apart from their obvious main shapes (big guy, tall guy ... that's it). They don't have distinctive sound cues either, which definitely doesn't help the issue at all.◉ Special infected spawn rate IS ♥♥♥*ING INSANE and the most annoying thing you can find in this game. You NEVER have a second of silence, NEVER. It's special zombies going at you all the time along with the standard ones, and it makes it very difficult to actually explore a little bit. It makes you want to finish the task as soon as possible just to avoid those boring arses running at you constantly. L4D was very chaotic but at least you had those little moments of silence in which you could gather your thoughts and decide what to do next. It's a problem the developers know since release date, with many people lamenting about it, and they didn't do anything about it.◉ 98% of the weapons are pretty shi*ty no matter the cards you use. Yes. And the zombies do lots of damage too, so it comes off unbalanced as hell. Had no problem playing it, so it's not a matter of "GIT GUD", more like "you should have hired more game testers" to assure a balanced and satisfying combat experience.◉ Maps. Again, might come off as picky, but they have no distinctive trait whatsoever (both aesthetically and technically). Remember that map in L4D in which there was an invisible countdown to a rainy whirlwind that brought hell on earth every 4-5 minutes? Hordes, special infected, maybe you'd get so unlucky you'd meet the Tank while you were in it. Nothing of that nature is included in this game, so the maps look very bland, boring, and there's no satisfaction whatsoever when you escape said map.◉ AI Team intelligence. It's the worst I've ever seen. I had Hoffman RUN FROM BATTLE while we were getting screw*d by 3 bullet-sponge special infected at once (see: problematic spawn rate).◉ Plot. What plot. Dialogue is honestly (and personally) boring as well. L4D kept you smiling from time to time with the witty responses.PROS:◉ You can change skin to your character, there's a very limited number of these though. I guess it's a good cosmetic addition. Character design is very good too - they all have their own "vibe".◉ I don't   h a t e    the card system even though it's totally unnecessary, kinda underwhelming and no one really asked for it. But it's the devs choice, still.◉ If you have a friend, you might be able to finish the campaign and have mindless fun for a few hours. Then you completely abandon it and go back to L4D.The game had so many good premises, but it fails to deliver in all the MOST important aspects of a zombie game (even for a mindless-type shooting one), and as spiritual successor to L4D.Might edit if something comes to mind.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who spent hundreds of hours on Left 4 Dead, this is a very refreshing and modern take of the genre.  The card deck system is surprisingly deep to experiment and play around with, and makes a big difference on the effectiveness of the gameplay.  The roguelite progression really helps keeps the replay value of the levels fresh every time. This game really shines with 4 friends. If you are playing first time, HIGHLY suggest playing through all the Acts in Recruit mode first to earn some cards.  When you optimize your card deck, it will be overkill and make Recruit mode easy at first. But will have a big impact on how far you can go on Veteran and Nightmare difficulty.Will I like B4B if I love Left 4 Dead?It depends. The card deck system and roguelite approach may not appeal to everyone. If it appeals to you and craving a fresh modern take of the genre, yes give it a try. If you simply want a modern Left 4 Dead, then this game may not be for you.Will this replace Left 4 Dead 2?No. Left 4 Dead 2's 10+ years of modding support really kept the game fresh and going today, I highly doubt it will be going to be overtaken by this game. There are still things I missed about Left 4 Dead 2 that makes we want to go back to it at times.tdlrIf you want a fresh take of Left 4 Dead, enjoy roguelite (even just a little), the card system, and have 3-4 buddies, it's worth getting. There's some replay value to be had with the corruption card system. If you want simply a modern Left 4 Dead, prepare to be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: The devs have been making changes for the better over time, but the AI is still beyond abysmal. It's actually embarrassing how bad the AI is. Game is fun, especially if you liked the Left 4 Dead franchise in the past. Get it on sale.EDIT: Not deleting my original review. At this point, I think the best way to enjoy this game is just to take it for what it is. It isn't perfect, the bots are helpful in some ways (dropping ammo when you run low, healing you every so often, etc.), but are extremely hindering at other times (getting stuck, watching you lose over half your hp to a special, and the classic running in front of you while you're shooting). If you accept the game for its flaws, you will enjoy the game. If you go in expecting it to be a genre-defining game, you will be heavily disappointed. I remain by original claim: get it on sale and use that time to see if you enjoy the game. If you do, consider getting the DLC. Tunnels of Terror is okay and simply adds a few new map tilesets. Children of the Worm adds a new Act V (6 levels, 1 checkpoint in the middle) with cool new enemies and atmosphere. Tinker with different decks instead of only subscribing to "what's best". Above all else, just have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I would absolutely recommend this game. The similarities to  Left 4 dead 2 are apparent however the game is its own thing. It takes a lot of the ideas from the left 4 dead series and expands on them while adding a level of customization many of us wished for in those games. Namely the card system. That customization expands the replay ability of the game massively,  There have been some difficulty issues but this game is still very much alive and the Devs are listening, tweaking and adjusting things with frequent updates.  The game has a few more maps than Left 4 dead 1 or 2 did at their launches and with the first DLC even more. Overall The game is amazing and while I have no doubt i will play more left 4 dead 2 in the future Back 4 blood has eaten up far more of my time  and, when i'm not suffering bad luck with randos its an amazing experience. With the latest update (june 2022) the game feels smoother than ever and not having to deal with constant card draw makes you feel your customization sooner allowing you to feel distinct faster, again something many of us wanted with the left 4 dead series.In conclusion  Its basically Left 4 dead with more customization. Frequent updates and difficulty adjustments. Rating: Pre june 2022 7/10. Rating: Post june 2022 9/10Edit: The thing I find ridiculous is people arguing Back 4 Blood is "bad" just because left for dead (specifically 2) is so good. So I want to put this as plainly as humanly possible; yes L4D2 is God tier, debatably one of the greatest games of all time but that fact does not in any way shape or form stop B4B from being good nor should it.Edit2: Sadly development and updates have stopped for now. I still fully recommend the game and think it is amazing. Better than L4D2 if you're looking for a customizable shooter with a ton of unlockables to customize your character. but if you want something to jump in and jump out of without any long term work to unlock stuff it is as always L4D2. Hopefully the devs come back to this game like they implied in a year or 2 but we never know. But even with the announcement that they were stepping back from active development I still play on occasion, and as i said before, still fully recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy playing this game, but it does have some issues.  If you liked Left 4 Dead or Left 4 Dead 2, then you will probably like this game.  They are similar, but this game has cards and updated graphics.  The cards add another layer of strategy to the game.There are still some improvements needed:- Reduce wait time from 3 minutes to 1 minute for players to select their next card between rounds.  3 minutes is a long time to sit there waiting.- I wish that the weapons and attachments were more available.  You can have all the copper you want, but still not be able to buy the weapon and/or attachments you want.  You're at the mercy of the game to randomly make them available to buy or give them to you, if your teammates don't take them first.  Then once you have the weapon you want, you lose the attachments you had on the previous weapon. You can go through an entire run and never get the weapon you want with the attachments you want.- Some of the levels are very difficult, even on the lowest difficulty level.  For example, "The Body Dump" in Act 3. You have useful grenades spread throughout, but you have to open each case of 4 in order to use them.  The action never stops in this level, so opening the case makes it more difficult.- The ammo availability seems to fluctuate.  Sometimes there is more ammo than you can pick up.  Other times the ammo runs dry and there is none available.  Especially after fighting larger ridden like the Ogre and Breaker, that can take a lot of ammo to defeat, and when you've just joined a quick match, where you have no ability to choose cards, buy more ammo, etc.- There are still some bugs that need to be worked out.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally making this review post 500+ hours of gameplay on my favorite cleaner, getting all the weapon skins, cards, unlocking all the supply lines and killing thousands of ridden with exhilirating ravenous brutality. This game has enormous potential in all honesty but the $60 price tag for entry/base game is not worth it in my opinion as writing this review. Great gameplay despite all its numerous flaws in-game even after a hundreds of hours playing with random squadmates.|Gameplay: A hybrid mix of Zombie killing, RPG elements, L4D2 and Apex. Absolutely great for squad play and team cooperation (Which is rare these days). In-game: Solo/Coop + Deck/Cards + Cosmetics + Playing with random squadmates to make any progress + Difficulty. Price: For $60 on the base game. Not worth it. Yet.Solo: Great for practice and deck experimenting. All effort in this mode does not affect your achievements or earn you any supply points. Coop with random squadmates in quickplay or hosting is the only way to make any progress and get supply points. Unless you have a good squad/friends assembled to play well together with Deck/Cards: The honest saving grace of this game. Allows you the mix and make your cleaner as powerful or ridiculously the best among your squad. Cards ranging from making your rich in copper per squad or make your weapons deal unholy amounts of damage to the ridden. Melee is overpowered but might get nerfed by devs soon.Cosmetics: Skins for weapons seem limited. Skins for cleaners good enough. Hopefully fixed with the road map the devs revealed. Total Apocalypse is more of my style for cleaner skins tbh. Difficulty: Recruit to Veteran is playable with random squadmates as long as you have a good deck of cards. Nightmare is an actual nightmare regardless of any attempt. Even with some good squadmates I met in-game. Still an actual nigthmare to even play. I can live without ever unlocking the ZWAT skins for the cleaners.|After writing this review. I shall return to the game with another random squad and commit mass genocide against these ridden until their extinction. _childDocuments_.review: This game is bare bones and is lacking a lot of common sense, its great if you're nostalgic to L4D franchise and wanted something a little spicier but ultimately its heavily flawed.A list of things: - When playing Single player you cannot work towards and supply crates or get points toward unlocking new cards, only the multiplayer/coop helps you grind toward getting better decks.- When playing this game in Swarm, if someone leaves/rage quits it will boot out random players or shut down the lobby, wasting players time.- When looking at the achievements for collecting the golden skulls or unlocking the 4 extra in game characters, you MUST play it online/coop, you cannot earn anything on your own in single player.-  When hitting Quick play, if you join a player on the same level as you, none of the progress from that lobby goes toward your own campaign, just wasting your time and forcing you host the lobby that everyone joins.- Very punishing to players with no friends.- The bots literally stand still and watch you do everything if you play it on single player or have someone disconnect, its like baby sitting 3 children who occasionally heal you while you're already healing yourself or throw a grenade at a single zombie.- Game objectives are very repetitive, not a lot of change as you progress in the game; go to point A, horde. Go to point B horde. Defend location/jukebox. Boarding up windows and fighting against horde to create safe house. Its just the same like 3 things the whole game over and over again.- The bots have some sort of immunity to Snitches, so if you're able to get your bots to attack it they can kill it without alerting a horde.- Bots are also do the voice line of being hurt while standing in bile, but take no dmg.- Nightmare mode is literally impossible unless you have a group of 4, hence making this game very reliant on the coop/multiplayer option and punishing single player.- The way some cards are worded is debatable, some just do not work together, example there's a card to have two primary weapons, and another card for infinite ammo on your secondary but no ads or something along those lines. These cards don't work together, there is more combos but too many to list.- You can get this game for $1 on Microsoft game pass, LITERALLY why would you ever buy it on steam...- If you fail a run in the game you are rewarded 0 supply points which is really punishing and wastes your time because you're not working towards building new decks.I would not recommend people getting this game unless you intend to buy it on the Microsoft store for a $1, there's no reason you should be wasting your time and money on it to start. This is just a cheap rip off to get you to buy DLC once they make 8 since the campaign is so short and they will most likely turn to cosmetics to keep people sucked in and make a quick penny, I'm calling it now. 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Back4Blood is an excellent zombie co-op shooter in the veins of L4D. It is not perfect but i doubt you find a much better experience (after L4D2) in this genre. It's made for co-op so if you want to go for single player you better leave it aside. Also there is no versus mode in campaign which is (for me) no issue because my 700/1800 hour in L4D/L4D2 are mainly done in 4player campaign co-op which i loved most.- enormous fun factor in many different co-op missions for up to 4 players- each round can be different through a card deck building which is more effective in higher difficulties- very liquid game and gunplay, fantastic controls- great variety of customizable weapons with nice sound effects- clear option and menu- ingame text chat- nice skins, no pay2win- a good selection of characters with different abilities- crossplay (can be good or not :)- quickplay- very cool and overall good graphics - high replayability- sometimes long waiting in lobbys but mostly it´s ok.- not made for singleplayer, like the L4D franchise.Well i think and think of more issues but it´s hard to find some. Of course you can pick around in the game and try to find things you don´t like but if you focus on gameplay, replayability and fun you don´t have to look further.In short, if you like a modern great looking co-op shooter with amazing zombie slaying and a hell of a good time ... then Back 4 Blood is a must have!UPDATE: After 144 hours playtime i can safely say - for me GOTY 2021!UPDATE 2: April 2022. New DLC Tunnel of Terror released and gives us lots of new content. The game is improving more and more. The fun is insane. All playable content included in this expansion will be available to all, provided that at least one player in a party has purchased the new content. Great news!

_childDocuments_.review: Well well well, more zombie killing run and gun fun is it?  Sign me up.  Well, I signed myself up and I experienced a mix of genuine delight and surprisingly enough - boredom.  This review is based on gameplay I enjoyed closer to the release of the game.  I understand a number of patches have been released that might directly address some of my critiques.First off, let's get the basics out of the way:  Guns feel good and powerful on medium and higher difficulties.  Yes you will be one-shotting most of the easier to kill zombies in the game.  Run speed and movement feel fairly fluid, maybe a bit stiff if you've been playing Apex Legends for 800 hours, but it's pretty standard FPS fare.  FPS controls are exactly what you'd expect.  Following that, here are the THINGS I LOVED: THE CARD SYSTEM:   It's a really novel way to provide some variability to your games and allow people to class themselves quite specifically to whatever role they enjoy playing.  It's also a great way to completely hamstring a team of really decent FPS players at higher difficulties, I'll get into that later.ENGINE, VISUALS, SOUND:  This game looks beautiful and plays just as nicely.  Great optimisation means that I never ever gave performance a second thought.  My 2070 super desktop ate this game for breakfast and the geforce 2070 mobile laptop I have performed fine.  The game also sounds great and I didn't have a lot of situations where zombies were right behind me because they failed to produce sounds.Conversely, here are the things I DIDN'T LIKE:THE DIFFICULTIES:Easy too damn easy and hard too damn hard.  I don't have a crew of 3 people to work together with, so it's always randoms on the internet.  Early leavers that have decided you're not good enough will doom you because at higher difficulties the bots are completely useless.  Coupled with a community of impatient and somewhat hostile gamers, this is the perfect frustration storm if you're honestly just trying to work your way through the story.   You can play solo, but only on the most basic difficulties.  THE CARD SYSTEM:Mis-choosing cards in the earlier difficulties has veritably no penalty because these difficulties are so easy you can leave mid game to go piss and come back and you'll be fine.  In the later difficulties, making the wrong choices can completely hamstring your team.  More annoyingly, some characters require specific card combinations to be viable (Like the medic) which is cool, but also forces you occasionally to build a deck you rarely use when all of the other characters are taken and you need to have a medic on your team.  When I played Back 4 Blood, Melee characters were too strong, too important, and had builds so powerful they were relegated to melee gameplay.  STRONGER ENEMIES:If you really enjoy chucking ALL of your ammo into veritable bullet sponges, this game is for you.  Not a lot of indicators to show that an enemy is close to death means you'll be wondering how much progress you're making until the jerk finally dies.  Special infected at higher difficulties also take a lot more damage and it's not that fun.  I'm curious as to which gamers actually like this tired old gameplay trope.  The end boss is kind of cool because it has a bunch of glowing weak points you need to work together to smash, but a lot of situations require you to stand in a line and dump hundreds of rounds into larger more menacing enemies.SAME OL', SAME OL'Other than the card system, Back 4 Blood brought back a lot of what I loved from the L4D games.  The feeling of just making it out by the skin of your teeth doesn't feel as prevelant as the AI director that I experienced simply spawned crowds and crowds of special infected to wear you down.  It seemed broken, but it was still playable, so wasn't addressed (As far as I know).  The critisism I have here, however, is more about there being less innovation in terms of technology in the game.  You're still on rails, you're still playing with 3 other people, and it's still bullets and melee weapons and your wits.  Maybe there will always be room for games like this, but I actually think turtle rock will see a lot less interest if there is ever a fifth iteration.  Destructible environments, more interesting and unique AIs, fire, water, ice physics systems, maybe open world segments where the players need to make it across wider expanses while searching for and collecting important items.  I'm not sure, but I think after 10 years and countless iterations of processors and video cards and related technology, an excellent studio like Turtle Rock could give us something more compelling than Left 4 Dead 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Back 4 Blood at release, like a lot of multiplayer games these days, is plagued with bugs and issues. The main difference is the developers were not ready to patch these day 1, and with a month gone by and a major patch dropped, not much has changed.Just some of the issues which slowly pile up and become incredibly frustrating:- You can purchase a season pass, but no indication when it will become relevant- RNG will make or break most games (even with scavenger perks)- You can't take parts off guns without finding another part to swap it with- Gunplay isn't as tight as games like Killing Floor 2 or Call of Duty (zombies)- Netcode is actual garbage. Zombies can skip around, things can die well after you hit them, etc- Joining random people at random points with random amounts of knowledge isn't fun- Bots only carry grey starter guns and a starter deck which make them dead weight, and ruin people joining the game- Falloff points in levels are nearly indistinguishable from what would be a walk-able place in other levels- Pick all your cards for Act 4 and pray the class of gun you picked appears on the ground- Grind the same levels over and over for supply points so you can actually get the correct cards to player higher difficulties!- A large amount of the game mechanics are unintuitive to new players, - Game maps are often recyled- Story is less compelling than zombieland, even though it targets the same buddy road trip vibesStraight up bugs:- Weapons and items being bugged and unable to be picked up- Retches can puke through walls, buildings, whatever they want- All supply lines purchased showing up and not allowing more purchases even if you know you had other supply lines- Breakout perk can get bugged so it's unusable for the whole game- There's an issue with joining games where if you join a character that already existed, you have to play with their cards, don't get your starter cards even though it shows you that, and have to pick your cards from the beginning of the deck (thanks November update!)Expanding more on the RNG:Everything from the weapons you acquire, the parts you find, the tier of weapon, the hazards you have to deal with in a level, secondary objectives, what kind of offensive/support/quick items you find, upgrades in the safe room, literally everything is random. This can make for some really fun experiences, and some really straight awful experiences. The problem is since you have very little control over it and you have to pick your cards before/through your run, you have literally no idea what to expect. Snitches, birds, in fog, with a silence is golden challenge? well not only will you not complete the secondary, good luck surviving.Now lets compound the RNG with joining random games. A single new player got all these modifiers and is halfway through an Act with 3 bots. You join and they are getting murdered. You can take over a bot and have Grey starter guns, with a starter cards. How do you make it through the level alive?The answer is you run to the end and hope for the best, so you can pick the character you want to play and get your card draws. Oh wait, you still don't have proper guns for your build, and they are still grey!Don't worry though, the devs "nerfed" melee, because balancing the game is more important than fixing bugs. Mean drunk disabling sprint was such a huge drawback to begin with, nerfing it feels like they are targeting an edge of the community playstyles/efficiency rather than actually caring about the game itself.Somehow this all feels like it's still in beta, but also like some of the core pieces of the game are untenable. The network layer needs a massive overhaul, and mid-game joining does not feel well thought out. At the rate they are fixing bugs and addressing issues I guess check back sometime late next year to see if they actually made any progress.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel that this game should cost $40 at base without the discount, but as it's priced as a AAA title, wait until it's 50% off or more. Also, if you don't have friends that you can play this with, don't buy it; joining random public lobbies is a nightmare.This game is fun overall (when played with friends), but is seething with basic inconveniences, bugs, and glaring design failures. The devs have extremely poor prioritisation when it comes to tackling issues and bugs, so they don't treat basic ones with any degree of importance or respect.Here's an example of an extremely simple quality of life feature that should've existed since day 1 but still doesn't exist to this day: Removing attachments from your guns.TLDR: Finding weapons and attachments is all RNG based - you can find the same weapon in a better quality later in the run. When you find a new weapon, you can't transfer your currently attached mods to the new weapon (there's an annoying workaround that makes you a clown). The players have been asking the devs for the ability to remove attachments from their guns since day 1. The devs answered saying that it's on their to-do list, but they have other pressing priorities right now. Ok, understandable, so what are those higher priorities? Let's list a few:- Twitch integration to allow twitch viewers to spend points to name zombies that spawn to attack the streamer. (prioritising this is such a brain-dead decision that it HAS to have been an executive order).- Nerf most of the relevant cards for melee builds to make melee impossible to use at higher difficulties.- They said that they fixed the zombie spawning mechanics (excellent!), but they feel more broken than they already were. Now special zombies can spawn literally under your feet, and some of them are fatal. - Since the last update I saw more bugs, such as the drop-bridge on the first level not being properly clipped, so you fall through it as you try to run across. There's also the janky movement, more rubber banding than before, etc.By comparison, attachment swapping or removal feature would take  a junior dev 2-4 hours to implement, everyone wants it, and should've been in the game from the start. The whole dev cycle consists of massive time investments with zero (or less) positive effect on the playing experience of 99% of the player base. The only people that benefitted from the above stuff are twitch streamers, and even that's debatable. To expand a bit on the above a bit: - By nerfing the melee builds, they removed an entire weapon archetype from being used in the game. It's just worthless now. Agreed, it was a bit too powerful before, but they crippled it. The result is that they herded the community into searching for alternative ways to deal with Nightmare difficulties, and settling for glitches rather than playing the game. At first it was speed running (a deck that lets you run so fast that you just do a mad-dash from safe-room to safe-room, and not have to kill anything), now it's grenade glitching (infinite grenade exploit), tomorrow it'll be something else. In fact, if you go into their discord, you'll find that most of the people are looking for groups that have someone doing grenade-glitching or some other dumb cheese. Nobody is trying to play this game properly, because what's the point when it's not properly working?- Zombie spawning mechanics may have improved, but it's very hard to tell. The devs did come out and walk back their statement that the zombie spawning was fixed, and clarified that they made improvements to it and that they'd continue to work on it. However, I didn't notice any issues prior to the update, and I'm noticing them now. Maybe my personal experience isn't reflective of overall state of the game, and it's actually improved, but it's hard to tell.- As per the other bugs, again, it may be personal experience, and they were as likely to happen before the latest update as they are now, but it's hard to tell because for me they didn't. More qualms:- Unlike L4D, all games are hosted on B4B's servers - it's not client-hosted. The initial lobby is client-hosted, but the game sessions are not for some reason. Even if the net code wasn't bad, you will see rubber-banding. Also, because all games are server-hosted, this game doesn't have community-created content (custom skins, maps, and mods).- Your "lobby" is a camp where you can walk around and talk to NPCs, and one of the sections of the camp is a dedicated shooting range where you can shoot at dummies with any weapon and see the damage that you can do. However, you can't change that weapon's quality or apply cards while in the shooting range, so it's pretty much worthless for testing 95% of the game's damage mechanics.- Because when the game starts nobody is technically the "host", you can't kick people from your play session. So when you have a screeching PS4 player that can't set up a PTT join your game, or a grifer that runs in and shoots all alarm doors and birds that he sees, you are forced to play with them.- The game's "report player" functionality doesn't work most of the time. It complains that you aren't connected to the internet, despite the fact that you can't play the game without being connected to the server.Now, I know that the devs are very active in their reddit community, they just don't reply often. That being said, devs, if you're reading this, here's my advice:1) Please start listening to your community. You want to nerf stuff? Fine. You want to waste time on pointless garbage like twitch integration that most of your players don't use? Sure, but please, PLEASE, add the ability to remove attachments from weapons. 2) Give us progression meters for mission completion stats on a per-character basis. We want to know which missions we have completed on nightmare with which characters. You already have the stats being tracked - just make them visible to us.3) Please fire your god-awful writers. The banter between the characters is stuff of nightmares and most of them are repulsive. In fact, the only character that I don't hate is Evangelo, and that's mainly because I can't recall him partaking in any dialogue with the other characters. The two final scenes after the abomination mission were the worst. What was the point of that conversation between Mom and Doc? Is that how you think human beings talk? Have you ever talked to another person? Nightmare! Saying that I wouldn't feel anything if these characters got killed off in the story would be a be an understatement- I'd feel a great sense of relief and satisfaction.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes when I read B4B reviews it feels like the people didn't even bothered to play the game and compare it to L4D2. Devs made a big mistake to market B4B as a successor to L4D. It's way too different. Doesn't mean it's bad.Special zombies. "There are more specials in L4D". So many people mention that there are less special zombies and L4D had a witch. In B4B are 4 basic types of special zombies. Each type have three mutations. That's 12 specials with different attack patterns. Plus there's a Snitch. Two new specials are coming in the next update. And all are also modified by corruption cards. Yes, specials in L4D were more distinct. But B4B have more specials in the end.Bosses. There are three bosses - Ogre, Hag and Breaker. All very distinct and epic. I'm sorry but L4D Tank (with main tactics to burn it with molotov and run) can't even compare to Ogre. Had behaves similarly to Witch. If you don't startle Hag, you don't have to fight it. And Breaker is just pure havoc. Maps. "There are more maps in L4D." No. L4D originally had maybe 20 maps. And same for L4D2. More maps were added later. There are 33 maps in B4B. I don't see any problem here. Many are very disctinct and unique. And with unique tasks. Also there is no point to cry about lack of maps since it's known from the beginning that more maps will be added in DLCs. Weapons. There are 32 weapons. All possible to upgrade with 3-4 mods which all result in a very different play style. "The game is too hard." Nope. You are supposed to play on normal difficulty until you get familiar with maps, weapons, corruptions, bosses strategy and unlock cards for basic builds. Then you can continue to Veteran difficulty. With good teammates and cards you can go through all maps without any serious issues. Honestly Veteran is often easier than Normal since you'll usually meet more experienced players with better builds here. (I'm slowly moving towards Nightmare.)Crossplay. Do not crossplay. People on PS/Xbox can't shoot and aim very well. Usually have not so good and stable internet connection (maybe it's the consoles issue). And generally console players are slower and bigger dumbasses. Speed and relfexes are important in B4B. Versus mode is ♥♥♥♥. That's the only one I agree. Nobody is playing versus, it's almost impossible to find any games to get the achievement. The mode itself is terrible. I wouldn't recommend it to anybody. The only good thing is you'll play as Specials and it will help you understand better how they move and attack.---B4B is a 4 player co-op FPS with zombies. That's it. That's the similarity to L4D series. Forget the rest and try to enjoy the game. Of course B4B isn't perfect. Far from it. Instead of trying to cover all the bugs and lazy programming just watch this video: . It explains a lot and shows how L4D was polished and fine tuned. And of course the overall feeling from the B4B is somewhat weaker. The co-op part is good and I can enjoy the game without breakable item and top notch zombie animations. Bugs are not happening very often. Shooting zombies is fun and action is intense. The only really bad thing is the bots AI and it's absolutely terrible. I love that they throw grenades, share ammo and supplies. But in general they behave like lobotomized morons. Several times I've been hit by a Hocker and three bots were just standing in front of me watching me to die. Card mechanic is good. I like it. But it's a reason why the community of this game is dying slowly. In games you need to get better and train your skills. In B4B you need to get better cards. And farming points to buy cards is less fun then practicing to get better. Maybe that's why people feel the game doesn't have anything to offer after certain time.And finally. The most stupid and not understandable at all decision. No community mods and maps. Why? I know why. TR are not so good devs and community mods/maps would probably break the game in some way. Prohibiting community to participate feels like a backwards thinking nowadays. And that's the main reason why in 1-2 years, after all DLCs will be out, there will be no players. So just buy the game now. Later there will be nobody to play it with. Sorry, the review is probably a bit messy. I just wrote some random thoughts.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really, really enjoying Back 4 Blood. It's not L4D3, if that's what you were looking for, but who knows if we will ever get that game. B4B takes the L4D formula and adds many sweet innovations, including some made by other entries into the genre, like Vermintide, for example. The card and deck building system is a really fun way to create classes and builds, and I like that the Cleaners bring different stats to the table, leading to creative mixing and matching to balance out the team to complete challenges. Adding attachments and weapon and item levels is definitely a huge plus in my book, as it presents the player far more interesting decisions than what the weapon selection provided in L4D2. And, generally, the roguelite elements and corruption cards add good twists between the levels and challenges.There are some changes I hope to see - allowing flashlight control and fixing how quick play queue players replace bots are two major ones for me, personally. But all in all, if you already like games in this genre, then I think you are incredibly likely to enjoy this game. It is probably not the best game for someone new to this genre, though, as there are definitely some complex mechanics layered on top of the base game, and L4D is probably the better entry point.
