_childDocuments_.review: First off, long time left 4 dead 1 and 2 player here. To begin, I don't even know what the devs were thinking when they implemented some features. I want to love this game, I really do. For the most part this game is actually extremely fun. However there are several moments that completely outweigh the good and make me forget all of that and absolutely hate it. I enjoy a difficult game, too easy is too boring. Back 4 Blood is just something else... They leave you with three choices: Recruit, Veteran, and Nightmare. Or what I like to call (respectively): "Where are the zombies?", "Is this the same game I was just playing?", and "Mega tallboy fist up your *** slumber party galore".Recruit is basically a walk in the park, you may see 10 zombies at one time and they might even come up to you and spare you ammo. Veteran is essentially a **** fest of brawler zombies constantly "sneaking" up behind you, (but actually they spawn 2 feet behind you after you cleared a room and just turned around thinking the coast is clear because the devs were too lazy to create proper pathing). Some levels will make it near impossible to clear because your success is almost certainly determined by the horrible RNG system in this game. Mission requires you to rush through an infinite hoard of zombies, including specials? Well good luck with acid exploding zombies that will chunk your health by 10 every time you kill one, even with maxed out damage reduction cards active. Forget using combat knife with healing in this case. Oh yeah and don't forget the infinite bile pools that spawn all around you and the dead zombie that will ultimately kill you if you somehow managed to survive the 80 damage you took from shooting a few zombies. Even manage to cheat death 1000 times? Fret no more, 5 to 7 crusher and bruiser mutations will be sure to finish the job by teleporting on top of your team and grabbing everyone in synchronization so clean that the US Navy SEALs shake in their boots. Nightmare is just that, a nightmare. The devs probably were afraid that the player base would shrink drastically after putting up with the horrible teleporting zombies, connection issues (90+ ping to one state over), bad RNG, and much more. So instead they made some achievements for completing the game on this difficulty to give most players the illusion that it's possible to beat without losing their job spending 20 hours a day honing their zombie slaying skills. You probably won't make it 20 feet outside of the safe house on this mode.Bots are the epitome of this game, great at times but mostly just an awful experience when the dust settles. They constantly moonwalk, shoot snitches, alert zombies, and occasionally they will turn around and try shooting you in the head for no reason. Often times you will see them walking up to a tallboy and get smashed into the Earth's core without putting up a fight. Other times, they will give you some ammo or might even heal you when you're at 98% health. But you can forget it if you're limping with one leg smashed into a piece of paper, no heals for you. I honestly wonder if the devs made some bots, who made bots, who made other bots, who made the AI in this game.Why play with bots, just play with other human players? Well if you enjoy never being able to fire your weapon because players don't want to share ammo they aren't using, then sure play online! Hope you sharpened your machete before popping that queue button. Bots will at least not set off every single alarm in the entire level while having the audacity to ping the alerts for you.Anyways, overall a great game! 11/10 from me. I look forward to purchasing the 40 dollar DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Back 4 Blood feels like a mix between Left 4 Dead and Killing Floor. The pace is slower and the fights longer. Play on Veteran only with your friends and it'll be really hard. Loving the deck building and the specialization balances, plus a variety of guns and attachments add a lot of replayability and excitement as you put together an awesome gun over the course of a run. Healing/trauma/stamina/ammo/accessory management are all well balanced and fun and make specialization important and satisfying.I'm disappointed the PvP isn't supported for campaign levels and hopefully they'll change that eventually, but for now the campaign has been a lot of fun on its own and veteran has proven extremely difficult to finish which is satisifying. EDIT: After putting some more time into Swarm I've discovered it's also super fun in its own right. I still hope they extend PvP to campaign levels but for now this has plenty of replayability and in many ways its an improvement on L4D's PvP.

_childDocuments_.review: Read other reviews before writing this - wanted to know what the complaints were. I'll admit my review sounds like I shouldn't be recommending it, but it IS a really fun game. I don't think it needs any flowery language or analysis on that part - it's just a zombie shoot 'em up [with a *groan* card deck system]. Not much to it. Here's just a list of stuff to be aware of I guess.*ABsolutely get it on sale if you can. But I don't regret buying it full price. *Is it L4D? No, it's a different game. You're on the wrong store page. Use the search bar. *Bots do suck, I'll give everyone that. I've been playing with friends and I'm going to credit them with my having a good time. The bots are completely useless. They'll throw grenades at nothing, trigger a trap if you were shooting vaguely nearby, and get stuck on everything. *You do NOT need to look through every single card before you build. You don't even have every card to begin with - if you play more than one round it's incredibly easy to pick up what does what. Learning a new mechanic can be annoying, yes, and the card system here is unnecessary, but it's really not that complicated in B4B. If it were, this would probably be the thing to switch me from "do" to "don't" recommend. Luckily for me it's unintrusive, and I can't put into words how much I hate card systems in games like this where it's completely unnecessary. Just stop putting deck-building in non-card games please. *You're not gonna like this game if you feel the need to speed through. The game rewards you for taking your time and being strategic. If that's not your thing, fine, but it's not the game's fault if that's not your playstyle.*I really enjoy the crossplay. My friend has it on PS4, but I prefer PC. Very nice that I don't have to be beholden to my friend's console choices. I've had no problems with the crossplay so far, other than the people we get matched with don't seem to want to be playing this video game. It runs just fine, and the one time one of us got disconnected it was super easy to load back in to the same lobby.*Totally leave reviews since they're for other people, but remember that Steam does allow you to return games as long as you've played them for less than a certain amount of time. It's a very short amount of time, but in my personal experience it takes less than an hour to figure out if I want to keep playing. *Would LOVE local co-op.

_childDocuments_.review: Back 4 Blood:~~~~~~~~~~ Humankind is on the verge of extinction due to a deadly parasite that mutates humans into dangerous creatures. They have been named the Ridden by a small group of survivors who have the tiny task of finding a way to destroy them and save humanity. While most of the Ridden look like normal human beings (slightly decomposed), others have mutated several times into giant and powerful beasts. They all have one thing in common . . . if they see you, they will come at you like flies to a fresh cow pat, and it will not be pretty! So, are you ready to face the Ridden onslaught? Because it’s going to be tough, gruesome and full of Zombies in Back 4 Blood!Back 4 Blood is a first-person Zombie action game developed by Turtle Rocks Studios and published by Warner Bros. Games on the 13th of October 2021 on the Steam platform. The game is also available on PS4, PS5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S and Microsoft Windows.The game consists of two modes of play, which are the Campaign and the Swarm modes. The Campaign mode can be played solo or online via an individual platform such as PC, Xbox or PlayStation, and can also be set as Crossplay if you don’t mind playing with people who use another platform. My review is mainly based on a solo campaign and several online co-op games on PC and Crossplay. After launching the game and signing in, you’ll arrive at the Survivor’s Camp. There, you’ll be able to try every single weapon in the shooting range, and go to the armoury to see the skins you have (or will unlock) for each of the weapons. Two tables, one where you can create your next deck of cards and the other where you can purchase new cards. You’ll also have two tents, one where you can customise your character and the other where you can set or continue a run (game).In terms of difficulty, there are three: Recruit, Veteran and Nightmare. I find the Recruit difficulty extremely easy, while Veteran is more like hardcore, and Nightmare is truly difficult. Interestingly, in my few Crossplay games with Xbox gamers, everyone (console gamers) was amazed at the difficulty when they joined my game set on the Veteran difficulty. I didn’t like playing Back 4 Blood in Crossplay at all, as it was laggy most of the time and probably too difficult for console gamers on the level of difficulty I set! I didn’t enjoy playing with other PC gamers either, as it was clear to me that these players knew most of the levels and were more interested in speed running each level rather than keeping up with a newcomer, and this is probably one of the negative points of the game. Not only does it take at least 10 minutes to find an online game, but when you find one, you’ll be playing with people who have more experience than you.  On the flip side, it would be extremely fun to play this game with your mates!So, playing a solo campaign was actually much better than playing with other people online. There are some issues here, too, such as the bots AI is dumb, to say the least. One or two bots might get stuck in an area for a while, or when you are down, and while waiting to be healed back, the bot stays in front of you doing nothing and therefore you and your party fail to reach the saferoom because you all die.However, I did enjoy the game for many reasons. The first one is that you have a total of 32 missions divided into 4 Acts. As I write this review, I am currently playing the third act, and I am having a lot of fun. So far, a larger number of the missions have been long, while a few were quite short but intense in terms of fighting. I also like that you receive an additional difficulty or rewards from the corruption cards at the start of each mission. For example, you might have 5 corruption cards at the start of each mission, but only one will be chosen as you start the run. To give you an idea, if you were to play the entire act 1, which has 13 missions, it would mean that 13 corruption cards would be added to your run and it would become really difficult, especially on the Veteran and Nightmare difficulties. You’ll also have active cards which are relevant to your deck card (s). So, as you start the next mission, you’ll be given a few cards to choose from, which will hopefully help you through whatever follows.After choosing 1 of 4 characters available to you at first, there are another 4 characters to unlock. Right from the start, you’ll be thrown into the thick of it. You’ll start the run in the safehouse. There, you’ll be able to purchase all sorts of items, from weapons to extra inventory slots for you and your party. When you are ready to rock and roll, you just have to open the safehouse door to face the music. As soon as Ridden sees your group, they will start coming at you super-fast. You’ll need to be very careful not to activate car alarms and security doors, or to scare the birds, as it will make noise and therefore attract another wave of Ridden.  The next wave of Ridden is usually more aggressive and will also have bigger Ridden, such as the tallboy, which has a huge, strong arm and can do heavy damage to your health if you are on the receiving end of it.  There are a few other big and powerful Ridden in this game, and I particularly like the mini-boss that runs after you and tries to gobble down its oesophagus. It’s inevitable that you’ll find yourself down on many occasions, but hopefully one of the other players or bots will heal you before you die.  But let’s suppose that you do die while playing on the solo campaign; in that case, you’ll automatically become one of the other three characters until you free your initial character ,who will be trapped in a sort of cocoon somewhere further down the track. Then you are able to play again with the character you had chosen before starting the run.  As you go through each mission, you’ll find cases on the floor that hold many essential goodies such as bandages, health kits, weapons, weapons attachments and ammunition. You’ll also have a mini-gun case, but you’ll need a tool kit to open it. The other collectable you’ll find around is money which you need in order to purchase additional items in the safehouse. Intel are cards, of which some are free, and others will cost money to activate into your current run. It is a lot of fun.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Fabulous graphics+	32 missions in total and three levels of difficulty+	Online (crossplay available) and solo campaign+	Swarm mode+	Good arsenal+	8 different characters+	Hectic fighting+	Steam achievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~-	Few graphic glitches-	Laggy while playing Crossplay-	Difficulty levels needs to be adjusted-	Quite a long wait to find an online game-	No trading cardsGet ready for hectic fighting in Back 4 Blood! The Ridden will make it difficult for you. . . for sure!7/10

_childDocuments_.review: If I could, I'd give this a middle thumb but due to the lack of variety and actual fun I will give this game a thumbs down. I feel like the game could be way better in nearly every aspect, but they decided to roll with whatever they had because they knew this would sell cause it’s the “spiritual successor” to the iconic Left 4 Dead franchise. Promoting the game like it was pretty much L4D3 was one of the biggest mistakes they possibly could have done. You go into the game with the expectation that this would be like left 4 dead and on the surface, it is. 4 player co-op shooter with zombies. They didn’t try to improve upon the now generic and boring formula, they decided to make another forgettable boring game. Oh, and before I forget to mention; They are recording the ingame chat. Just letting you know incase you didn't know.The entire community gave them plenty of critique and as far as I am aware they listened to no one. They didn’t balance the infected, didn’t change the maps, didn’t add weapons or fix hitboxes. They pretty much changed NOTHING from the alpha or the beta as far as I remember except the horrendous performance. They didn’t even change the goofy stun animation when a reeker dies next to you. You fly away like a cartoon character and they haven’t changed it since the alpha. The performance in the beta and the full game is way better than in the alpha, but there are still quite a few hiccups with the performance, especially during Act 2’s and 4’s finale. The game is also a buggy mess. I cannot stress enough how many times we had to kill ourselves on purpose cause the final boss was glitched and wouldn’t let us hurt him. The hitboxes are also incredibly broken especially when it comes to the bruisers. It also really bothers me that you cannot play alone with your friends. I know you can, but the game is buggy and it just doesn't work so we always get randoms that got their mic volume at 500% and destroy my ears. The game has been out for 4 days by the time I publish this review and they still have not fixed it. The gunplay is fun, but kinda feels hollow sometimes. You sadly cannot remove attachments on your guns which is also really annoying especially when you pick up a 4x zoom scope for an AK by accident lmao. Stamina is also a pain in the ass in the game. You can level it up if you pick cards that give you +10% stamina but stamina is still a problem. Speaking of the cards system. It’s unique and sort of cool. At first I was against it, but now that I’ve seen it with my own eyes I kinda like it. It adds to the replay value but most of the time you get some annoying cards that add a fog that is so thick you can’t see a metre in front of you. The map design for the most part is bad. They look nice, but they are really bad when it comes to gameplay not to mention do they constantly reuse maps and the only thing they change Is the time of day. At least Hard Rain in L4D2 added some heavy rain to the backtracking but Back 4 Blood doesn’t. The atmosphere in general in the game is just average. Left 4 Dead somehow managed to be creepy and incredibly fun all at once when you played it, but Back 4 Blood instantly gives off a cheap and unfinished vibes. You open the game and the second you load into Fort Hope you can just feel how cheap the game is. The characters are all right I guess. Nothing really outstanding outside of maybe Holly, Doc and Jim. They definitely do not have the charm and chemistry that Bill, Zoey, Francis or Louis had. The melee still feels weightless and it seems like they only have one animation for it. Left 4 Dead 2, a game that released in 2009 unironically got better melee animations than Back 4 Blood that released in 2021. That ♥♥♥♥ blows my mind. It is not fun to use melee weapons at all so I avoid them at all costs. The Infected are incredibly underwhelming when it comes to design and variety. Overall there are only 3 different categories of infected. Stingers, Tallboys and Reekers. Tallboys are pretty much a mix of Chargers and Tanks, Stingers a mix of Hunter and Spitter, Reekers pretty much only (suicide) boomers. In each of those categories you got 3 new infected and they look pretty much alike so you can never see the difference in-game. Some infected are still ridiculously overpowered or underpowered. There is no actual balance. Stalkers are basically hunters which you cannot prevent from pouncing you except when you somehow dodge them, but that is not proper counterplay because they are faster than you can react. Brousers are incredibly overpowered and frustrating to play as / against. They can rush ahead with their power several metres catching up to the survivor so they make barely any distance and then hit 5m infront of them LITERALLY taking 1/4 of the cleaners health. They can take down an entire team if you're not careful and overrun by ridden or stuck in a small space. They take more than 2-3 mags to take down which is just bad and unfun. But on the other hand, cleaners can throw stun grenades which stun you for 10 seconds and then just throw molotovs and kill you without you having a chance to react. Hockers are alright but annoying to go against aswell ESPECIALLY when they hide on a roof or behind a wall cause there is realistically nothing you can really do against them. The entire tallboy category is just a huge problem. They do too much damage and got too much health. Then there is the Ogre, which is pretty much a huge tank but he is overall ironically the weakest enemy in the game. If you hide in a house and shoot from inside there is nothing he can do about it. However, if you are close to him he is quite strong duh. He sounds quite cool right? Well I thought so too until I realised that every time he appears it is always scripted. He can’t appear randomly and that just ruins it at times because you can just run past him if you know what is about to happen.The swarm mode is also incredibly stupid. Maps are horribly designed and 9/10 times open where all the infected struggle to do anything and cleaners can just camp in the corner of the map where they can oversee 50% of the map and shoot anything that moves. But on the other hand, sometimes infected can take the high ground by camping on a roof, behind a wall or some other spot where you physically cannot reach them or react fast enough to counter their attack.I've also noticed that there is no system like in L4D2. Back in L4D2 you couldn't get 4 hunters or 1 jockey, 1 hunter, 1 charger and 1 smoker that could kill you all in one move because that is quite unfair but here? If there's a horde you get run over by dozens of zombies countless of hockers, stingers, walmart boomers and brousers all at once which is just frustrating.Also allow us more customization. I wanna change my crosshair to my liking and not either some dot or some ugly cross. They are also way too big which looks really off. The servers are also quite laggy currently which is a bummer.I bought the 100€ version and hope they improve upon everything but due to them not really changing anything from the Beta or Alpha I won't expect too much. You also HARDLY get anything from the 90 or 100€ version lmao. Like all you get is a few sprays, 3 ugly and 1 good skin and a useless title and emblem alongside one of the worst pre-order weapon skins I have ever seen in my entire life. The only good thing about these versions is that you get to play 4 days earlier but that is still a ridiculous price for that pitiful content.Overall I’d give this game a 6/10. It is fun but NOT a worthy successor to the Left 4 Dead franchise and it is NOT worth 70-100€.Edit: 40 hours later and everything still remains true.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed playing Left 4 Dead, you'll enjoy this game. Keep in mind that this isn't exactly like the Left 4 Dead franchise though.A couple new features include:- Card Decks, which are vital to gameplay. You can customize your deck at the menu and with each mission you complete, you unlock a card in your deck to activate. You can collect cards by unlocking Supply Lines, which cost Supply Points that you receive at the end of each match.- 3 separate difficulties (Recruit, Veteran, and Nightmere). Be aware though, that on Veteran and Nightmere difficulties, friendly fire is enabled and each requires a good amount of teamwork and planning to beat.- Bosses/Mutations, each of which have their own weakspots and abilities. As a general guide, there are 3 different types of Tallboys, Reekers, and Stingers, along with the 2 current bosses, the Ogre and the Breaker.- Corruption Cards, which are added at the start of each mission. These cards make the experience more difficult, add new events, or add a new challenge for a reward.- 4 separate Acts, each of each has it's own checkpoints and maps.- A final boss at Act 4, which thankfully will give you your full deck for the mission.Some Tips:- Don't rush in guns blazing. Often times you will either screw your team over or get yourself killed by a horde of incoming Ridden.- Share your resources with teammates. If you notice someone on your team is out of ammo, spare them a little but of ammo until they can find some more.- Diversify your gun types between your teammates. If you all run guns that take rifle ammo, it will be very hard to find any ammo to use. Try changing things up by using shotguns, smgs, pistols, snipers, lmgs, or even melee.- Bots are actually very helpful, as they drop ammo and will occasionally heal you.- Health does not regenerate naturally, so be mindful of this. Meds and certain cards will help keep your health up.- There are 2 different types of damage Normal (red) and Trauma (black with red stripes). Trauma damage can't be healed from any handheld meds, and can only be healed using med stations on some walls.- Your extra lives appear next to your character picture in the corner, keep an eye on those. If you run out and get incapacitated, you will permanently die until someone either finds your body later in the level, or heals you with a defibrillator.- Carry a toolbox with you to unlock locked rooms with loot in them. They will appear as dark blue doors with a target on them and usually have weapons, ammo, and meds.General ratings:Gameplay: 9/10Playerbase: 7/10Act 1: 9/10Act 2: 8/10Act 3: 6/10Act 4: "Where's my ammo?"Ridden: PainMutants: Have mercyBosses: "Hey man how's your face? Oh it's completely off your body, that's cool, ♥♥♥♥ off"

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an utter disappointment. I came in knowing this obviously isn't going to be l4d3, but even as a standalone game it is horrible.This game believes difficulty is spamming special ridden constantly and ruining the players plans instantly. Of course this game is an attempt at a l4d style game that TurtleRock was trying to skirt off of so pretty much every complaint can be compared to l4d without trying to say the game is meant to be l4d.I'd also like to preface these complaints by saying I'm playing this with one other person and am playing casually on recruit. I'm by no means a god gamer but I'm good enough to play l4d on it's hardest difficulties.Special Ridden - This game loves special ridden in the worst ways. When you aren't having enough of a tough time or the map has been designed to put you in a tough spot the game will throw unending amounts of special ridden at you to make your day even worse. This can be and exploder to throw you into a group of crows to ruin your silent run, 5 tallboys to smash you in a building, or a snitch will hide under a bridge and cause a horde when you walk over it because you didn't know it was there. This game will constantly try it's best to screw over the player and in unfair ways.Alert System - Causing hordes is far too easy. This game gives little to no leniency in alerts. Crows will be alerted by getting to close or shooting at them which seems fine but the area for alerting them by distance is too far out. If there are multiple patches of crows then it's near impossible to get past them all without hugging walls, and if you get spammed with special ridden good luck. Occasionally the game will even go out of it's way to place crows behind a wall so when you walk around it you'll run right into it without a chance to back out because it's already so close to you. Snitches are another story, being that they work fine until they're placed in a horrid spot that you can't see them and you won't know they're there until it's too late. The worst part is that the snitch doesn't have a gradual build up. If you get close to them they go off near instantly, at least the witch in l4d gives you time and space to not alert it.Player A.I. - The bots in this game are worthless. They kill some ridden here and there, give the player ammo, and heal them occasionally but that's all they're good for. They will constantly walk in front of you be it shooting your gun or a mounted minigun and eat your bullets. These poor excuses for bots won't even try and help kill a boss when they appear as far as I can tell. They are more a burden than anything, more-so when playing with a corruption card that for a bonus your team can't be incapacitated so many times since they'll do all the falling over for you by standing in front of a tallboy and letting it kill them because they're so dumb.Corruption Cards - These are mostly fine. I have little to no gripes with this system, it's a great way to increase difficulty in a unique way. It becomes an issue when you have so many stacked against you that it's near impossible to happily play the game. Sometimes the game will throw so many cards into a mission with huge negatives to your team that it makes the game go from a challenging and fun time to outright frustrating and angering. There needs to be some serious rebalancing of the corruption cards at the recruit difficulty for sure, the game shouldn't become frustrating to anyone at such a low difficulty. Not to a horrible gamer or an experienced gamer.Direction - Oh boy, this is the worst part. This game has no direction for new players. Safehouse doors are never highlighted and most objectives aren't either. Very seldom do I find the game pointing out to me where to go and even when it does I'm typically getting destroyed by an entire army of ridden so I can't even see it. Most of the time in missions I spend it aimlessly wandering hoping I'm going the right way while shooting the ridden that are scattered around. For a player that's new to these missions it's disorienting to be given no clear direction. Nothing is ever marked so unless you already know where you're going you're gonna have a fun time wandering in a circle till you stumble across where you're meant to go.Even this wouldn't be so bad if it also wasn't coupled with the game never telling you or even telegraphing to you what is about to happen, often times being suddenly attacked by a horde after an in game cutscene that doesn't warn you beforehand like many interactables do. Sometimes the game will give you objectives to you and bring you to them, but suddenly after completing the last one you're pulled out of the mission without warning, assuming that you were meant to go somewhere else before the game pulled you meaning that anything you were saving to grab till after the objective is lost because you hadn't known the game would pull you from the mission after.This game is just a frustrating mess. I don't recommend anyone bother with this game unless you're a real god gamer and/or enjoy frustrating gameplay. Even the souls series isn't as frustrating as this game is.

_childDocuments_.review: It has been years in the making, Back 4 Blood is a 4 player co-op game by the maker of Left 4 Dead. Except it's slower, grittier and has a bit more of everything.The game did launch with some drama about it not being a true sequel to Left 4 Dead. Some complaints are because of the premium price of the game, slower action and limited versus mode. But this is a co-operative experience first and foremost.There are a huge variety of weapons with different quality levels, lots of playable characters, tons of weapon mods and cards, all of which can give bonus stats like affecting the damage you deal. Deck building is a nice touch for customizing your style of play.Each level portraits a realistic world overrun by ruin and chaos. Enemies consist of common zombies to mutated creatures with special abilities. Replayability is very strong as enemies placement is different for every game. It can be quite challenging to finish a campaign and there are also lots of difficulty options so you won't get bored easily.Starting up a game is easy and matchmaking works up with players within 30 seconds of wait. When matching with other players, teams are hit or miss. Your experience will be just as good as the player you partner up with. Personally I found removing cross-play with console players did help me find better teammates.Finishing a whole campaign can be long and does suffer with fatigue but there is drop-in drop-out co-op. In summary Back 4 Blood stands on its own as a very good co-op action shooter..

_childDocuments_.review: I quite liked the old left4dead games but unfortunately back4blood is a complete and utter failure. I wanted to like this game but it is just annoying. The game does have nicer graphics but the gameplay just sucks: Unfortunately the developers chose to just add useless gimmicks (e.g. annoying "card decks" for "upgrades" and an "immitation  FarCry" 3D lobby that I could not care less about, but that just slow down the game flow, wasting startup time by searching for online players to join upfront is another annoyance - rather than just letting them join later: which had worked just fine in left4dead, and which is also still available anyway). The same game levels are then repeatedly reused in "different" missions and the whole thing just feels as if the goal was to stretch the available content by the cheapest means possible.. the player is forced to complete the levels in sequence and unlike left4dead it is not possible to just have some fun with your friends by directly starting a specific map. The additional players that later join a game (i.e. everyone but the "fiends" that had been specifically invited at the start) then get automatically thrown out whenever a "run" ends: The game does not allow to just keep playing with the same team - and you'd have to add all those players to your friend list to then explicitly invite them to the next run. The game then still seems to be quite buggy: It managed to crash on the initial "quit to desktop" functionality and I repeatedly got disconnected in the middle of a game.More often than in the old left4dead you get jumped by combos of uber-zombies that just kill you without giving the player any chance to defend or to get back into the game.. I wonder why the developers thought that it might be fun or motivating to just getting killed by an occasional "random asteroid". To me it just feels like an additional pathetic attempt to stretch the game's overall play through time.I regret having spent 27€ for this POS and I'd recommend to wait for a future "Back 4 Blood 2" (hoping that the flaws might get fixed at some point) or to at least wait until the price drops below the 10 US$ mark.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really want to recommend this game, but when you advertise yourself as "from the creators of the critically acclaimed Left 4 Dead franchise" when the only thing in common with the two is its a 4 player zombie shooter that has special zombie types and bosses, it gives expectations that aren't met. This game lacks the same level of replay ability as the Left 4 Dead franchise, now a lot of this is just my opinion and others may disagree, due a couple of big things like special Ridden that were way too similar, the lack of support for mods, the start where supply points could only be earned via online sessions meaning single-player mode reaped no rewards/character unlocks, and repetitive map usage. Whereas L4D 1 & 2's special Infected are unique in ability and design, has access to the workshop for mods, game was purely shoot zombies and have a blast, and each campaign felt unique (ignoring the fact Hard Rain has you get gas then go back the same path except with a flood). Sure I can't expect Turtle Rock to limit themselves to the Source Engine and I love all the new things they did do with B4B like the gun play was fun and building a weapon to use through a run was fun(despite losing it the very next run for no reason), the idea that the Ridden will always comeback as long as there's bodies/nest, Hoffman being voiced by Rigby from Regular Show's VA William Salyers while not changing the game is just something I really enjoy hearing in the game, and the designs of the Hag and Ogre are cool even if the which and tank are cooler. But yeah, TL;DR Good game just builds hype for itself that I don't think it lives up to so imagine you're about to play COD zombies instead of thinking you're gonna play Left 4 Dead 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Update Dec 9 2022I can finally say the game has corrected most of my problems. The new dlc has better maps than we have seen before, good mechanics, fun new items, and added new gamemodes. I would now recommend this game as a complete experience with good gameplay and solid base so longs as they dont go trigger happy in the nerf department like they have done many times before.Update Nov 8 2022Running out of text space so quick tldr. Game is better but they need to add card picking when you join in progress and quick play bonus should not be removed after 2 matches cause people just leave once its gone. Too many runs ended because the lobby you joined is screwed and you cant save it. Update June 9While the idea of changing the game to get full deck on game start is the first thing to add fun to the game since launch, they could not help themselves and gutted melee perk cards further limiting your diversity in builds. Now that speed builds and melee is dead the only true viable builds are ranged, and medic. I dont really understand why they continue to take the few things for the 2000-4000 concurrent players who still drag themselves through the game and ruin those few things with each update. I imagine within this next year they will declare this game a flop because they dont understand why they can get back or retain players. Update Feb 10While they have begun to make more things viable they ended up destroying many of the things the community has taken a liking too including speed builds and major adjustments to melee. They added a card that allows you to remove attachments which should just be part of the main game. With how the community has been reduced to either the small amount of die hard fans and people picking up the game for the first time doing anything in quickplay is near impossible. Low team coordination and lack of people acting on the objective. Unfortunately due to the slow response time of fixes for the game what is left is hard to enjoy with the current player base. With the 24hr peak being just under 5000 its no mystery why left 4 dead 2 has literally 5 times the 24hr peak players than back 4 blood. The team has trouble balancing things in a way the the players find fun and the numbers reflect that. Big problem is also the fact that joining quickplay and being loaded into game actively being played is that when you load in you dont get to pick your cards or anything, so if you are on the second to last mission and you dont have cards, gear, items and most likely based on the fact that it was a back filled lobby no revives meaning you waste all of your time being loaded into a quick play. Either let players pick their cards or just let the run lose, no need for other people to share the same fate. Update Nov 11They have not addressed the majority of the problems in the latest update and even more so made the balancing even worse with all the nerfs to various cards and buffs to special ridden.I am changing my review to negative in light of their inability to read consumer feedback. The rest of my review is left unedited.Its a great game with some major balancing issues.For example as time of writing 4.4% of players have beaten the middle difficulty, and .2% of players have beaten nightmare. For reference dark souls 3 alternate ending that requires you to do order sensitive steps to achieve has a 14.someting% completion rate. Being as realistic as possible your middle difficulty should have some where around a 40-50% completion rate and nightmare should have somewhere between 10-25%. Btw the lowest difficulty has about a 26.5% completion rate. I have beaten veteran difficulty (middle difficulty) and completed the first 4 missions on nightmare. The level of cheesing, manipulation, gliching, and extended game knowledge about what you can get away with in order to beat that difficulty is ridiculous. I see many players have a hard time with recruit and have absolutely no chance on veteran. Finding competent like minded players skilled enough to play nightmare come few and far between. As someone who enjoys the challenge i have no idea how they will continue to make playable DLC acts without making them unplayable. Gameplay related gripes i have are-inability to drop attachments (they plan to make this a perk card but that is beyond dumb)-nightmare difficulty not enabling you to collect all your cards ( the difficulty is hard enough without that limitation)-unresponsive AI that will not break you out of grabs-lack of build options for secondary,sniper,and smg (meaning more cards that make using them a more unique experience)-making adding a unreasonable amount of specials their idea of difficulty-over half the specials ability is a grab-excessive range, Dot, and use of acid spit-making mutated sniches always alert horde even when coordinated with your team-team damage on veteran and nightmare difficulty being ridiculous (not uncommon to one shot teammates killing them instantly)-trauma damage values are insane on higher difficulties forcing you to have a medic build without virtually any exceptions-shotgun card that gives back temp health barely functioningPositives of the game-The characters seem unique from each other and offer unique build decisions when running different decks-The card deck system is fantastic and offers dozens of ways to play the game through various positives and negatives. -The gun play feels very fluid, and there are 1 or 2 guns that don't feel great to use-The gun parts system offers you to change your guns feel and have a impact on your build-melee is a perfectly viable deck build and feels good to play-shotguns have good power and feel devastating at close range-assault rifles feel good at most all ranges and handle very well-smgs allow you to truly play run and gun and complement movement speed build very well-the secondaries feel viable and useful despite not having any cards for them (but i would really like some build variety there)-weapon and character skin unlocks are fun to use-the acts in the game (despite reusing some areas) feel unique in each encounter and offer a variety of ways to play- the ping and loot sharing/dropping system make it easy to coordinate with randoms and keep other players engaged-the unique enemies are engaging to play against (despite sometimes being oversaturated by the quantity of them)-story is not super in depth but has vastly more depth than left 4 deadi love the game, but want to see it do better so others may enjoy it as well. For the time being there is some skill required here to play this especially if you want to unlock skins from defeating higher difficulties. The amount of potential here is great and i can see that DLC can expand this game and its ways to play for potentially years to come. If you are on the fence about the game wait for a sale but i can assure you if you played left 4 dead and were left wanting more this is a solid game but in some areas rough around the edges.

No one wants to support a studio that puts very little content and ends a game's life so quickly.Cons-not a lot of different guns, each types of guns such as snipers, smg, shotgun, assault rifles have around 3-5 different types-you cant remove old accessories on to your new gun-some toxic players who blame you for everything (when all you're doing is watching them trigger every alarm in the world)-spawn rates of special zombies may as well be as many as commons on nightmare mode. its too much.-somewhat of a short game, i wish they added more maps-only 2 game mode (i do not count solo since its just singleplayer story)if you are looking for a game like l4d, but with a updated version, this is it. killing zombies feel more solid and getting those head shots is more enjoyable. the guns never felt better. _childDocuments_.review: Back 4 Blood is a strange one.Its not bad, but it is also realy easly forgettable.Its decent fun to play on a low dificulty with some friends, but beond that there is not much replayability at all right now.The community exist of players who mostly stopped caring about the game, and that is never a good thing for any game.The card system that lets you gain buffs towards weapons and specific playstyles, adds some customisation for the player. The negative cards that buff the enemy, dont add anything to the game other than make runs harder the further you get. And dont add replayability.The gameplay is like any horde shooter, you shoot zombies with some stronger ones mixed in between and try to scavage weapons and the like to survive. It keeps the same map progression from the L4D series in that you go towards a saveroom, and then start in that saveroom and run through the next map.The gunplay is somewhat fast, and the guns feel good to use.The zombies are uninteresting and run at you one at a time mainly, and dont work together in any way. The special infected is where the L4D series seperated itself in how to add character to that game. However in B4B special infected are mostly just bigger zombies that have more hitpoints and hit harder and dont stand out in any way as being ''special''. They dont stand out from the crowd much visualy, until an enemy with a big arm starts smashing the ground around it like a little kid trowing a fit and your hitpoints start draining if you stand somewhat close. Your maximum hitpoints are reduced to a sliver that cant be regained easly and thats about it. Special infected also spawn a lot, and in large amounts. Making them not feel special at all.It does not feel like specialy infected are there with any specific role, and they are mostly just annoying stronger zombies that look a bit different up close. Special infected have so called weakspots that glow and make them stand out slighty, but they are badly placed obscurring them on the special infected where it matters, and with how many hitpoints some have dont actualy serve a point. Since you wont kill them all that much faster by shooting the weakspots, than normaly shooting them in the head or anywhere els.Bosses are interesting, but having only 1 boss and 2 minibosses with bad pathfinding for the main boss, means it does not make them stand out enough especialy after you combat them the first time. Attacks or animations/sounds dont change throughout fighting them.The maps in this game look realy well done, and detailed to a point where it tells a story most of the time. Aside from the guns being good, the map design is the main thing this game does well. Places look lived in, or recently abandoned. Or in some cases reclaimed or fought over, and that adds to the atmosphere of the game a lot.However a missed opportunity is the maps not giving multiple paths or changing between runs to create replayability. Maps stay the exact same every time you play.The game already lacking replayability, this would have added to the game, and seeing how good the map design is, would have been easy enough to do. It would probably not have been enough on its own, but would have helped a lot.There is one issue with the map design compared to a lot of other horde shooters, and that is that most of the world cant be interacted with. You cant destroy most things, tables and chairs are glued to the ground, and the things you can damage or destroy are extremely limited.There is not a lot to say here, its not great nor bad.Some sound cues on danger are done well, like with the Hag a special enemy. Creating an earie music and adding to the game. But most other sounds playing dont add at all to the urgency of a situation, feel like there isnt any danger, nor add much atmosphere.The music that plays in the game is pretty decent, and there is not a lot more to say about that honnestly. Without ingame sound cues standing out and creating atmosphere, the sounds and music is mostly forgetable and does not add enough to make it stand out.This is where a lot of people complain about, and for good reason. Turtle Rock Studios (TRS) and Warner Bros. Games (WB) did not release the game in a stable state or even playable for most people, and players keep running into bugs and problems.TRS still seem to struggle to address the most basic of bugfixes and issues the game has, but they have done a lot to fix things after the huge backlash from the playerbase. The amount of hate and backlash they have to get to get to a point where they adress issues, is somewhat concerning however. They do take some feedback, and things I have suggested have been added to the game or adressed. However giving feedback is not something most players will be doing through forms on websites, and something that takes a lot of time and effort. Most bugs, issues, and critique that is said in videos, reviews, and the forums, get ignored. And thats where most people share things. And in the end the playerbase is not getting paid to develop the game, so TRS being this reliant on the players to point out obvious bugs and issues, is somewhat of a problem.The first month the developers went radio silent, only reposting positive statements game journalist said. Then after the huge backlash started communicating, and halfway December went mostly radio silent again. They mainly use sources outside of Steam to share things, but communicate very poorly for a company this reliant on the players.The game is suppose to get paid DLC content, and the developers have stated no lootboxes will be added. The DLC have yet to come out, and microtransactions like lootboxes have to be proven in the future. But this might be positive for the future of B4B.This game has had a lot of bugs and problems, some things got fixed, others remained. And ofcourse new ones have popped up. All in all the game is mostly playable, but right now (January) there are bugs that impact gameplay;- Connection issues with servers and problems joining friends lobbies.- Stutters in cutscenes and lag ingame.- Guns dont always fire projectiles and wont do damage.- Enemies can teleport at times.- Lots of lag in Fort Hope, that is the starting hub and ''menu''.- Still issues with the Matchmaking in this game, where you might not find players to play with at all.Other than that, special enemies are not balanced properly. Or just not that well made in general, and could use improvement.This game is only realy worth playing if you have friends to play with. With the lack of replayability, you are reliant on friends to make the game more fun in the long run. Maps and runs dont change, and it has fairly little content for its price point.The game is worth 30 Euros at most in its current state, for someone who loves horde/zombie shooters.Less so when you just like shooters or coop games in general and are less invested in the genre.The 100 euros when you include the DLC pass, is a huge price point that has yet to see if it actualy delivers anything at all.I recommend getting this game on a huge discount if you have friends, or skipping it for something better or more reasonably priced. Buying the DLC content is not recommended, until you know for sure it delivers in the future.I cant recommend it at this pricepoint however considering the issues, so I wont.

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a good solid 30+ hours to finish the game on lowest difficulty;   To summarize my experience, this was a challenging zombie horde killing game to play and worth the money.   This was seven days to die zombie horde and world war z aftermath combined into one.  Every multiplayer i joined, experience is different as players have different cards and different style of play.  Of course you could watch other youtubers or watch twitch stream for hints but that spoils the fun in my opinion.   Try to play through it, then watch and learn more about the game :-) you'll be surprised with a lot of hidden features that you can find out later to make the experience unique. For new players,       -  always play multiplayer as it is cross function platform (xbox/pc/ps4) and connect with players      - continue to spend points on cards, its meaningless to save up on points      - card system gives you boosts to your character,   higher on the list the earlier it will be available to select so play ACT1 like a dozen times and get as much cards as you can before going to ACT2 and beyond.      - its about working as a team, solo will just kill you and makes your team waste bandages and revive on you. so please don't.Difficulty i had was to understand the card system in general;  This game isn't about leveling up by experience.  This is about your ability to make a deck towards the level which you are playing on. Therefore you die a lot and play over and over the same level   (i.e. I could not figure out how to finish ACT3 and 4 until I modified my cards).  Players may not feel this as a reward because if you really have a bad selection of cards (i.e. increased all armor but not stamina...  or all in on ammo damage but no healing ability... etc. etc.  ) it kills the fun because you lose often... but again you have to look at how this game is setup so  try to make some balance to your card selection.  Trial and Error or you can't learn or improve.The only wish they had a default card selection already prepared for all the characters and from their you could modify so that average players didn't struggle in this area.  Otherwise,  awsome!   I hope they come up with more ACTs in the future or I would be somewhat disappointed

_childDocuments_.review: The longer I played this game, the faster the nuance and honeymoon phase lifted and I found myself just wanting to load up Left 4 Dead. As I said, at first this game has a ton of potential, new guns, attachments, items, mechanics, cards, infected types, the works. They took the initial idea of Left 4 Dead and decided to not necessarily re-invent the wheel, but to add to it. What they added, however, were chains while there isn't snow, spikes, while you're driving on a highway, and painted the wheel a pretty color to make it look new while taking off the two front tires. Effectively, they tried to get complex with a simple formula, and flew too close to the sun.1. Weapons - I LOVED the weapon variety, but why the hell would I bother with 99% of them when they're usually outclassed by the M4 or the Scar? In L4D, you can use whatever you want. The Uzi will carry you through any map, if you try that in this game, even with cards that change damage types it will only make the guns that naturally are better, even better.TLDR - more weapons doesn't change anything when one is naturally the best one. Also, melee with health regen is so op, you're more likely to have a melee weapon in your hand if you want even a shot at Veteran. I'll get to difficulty later. 2. Special infected - Jesus, where do I begin. It's bad enough that they effectively copy pasted the specials from L4D, fair enough, they're the old devs, but to make them so much worse and in some cases put two in one that leaves no real weaknesses. Tallboys- the bane of the existence of any player, they're so strong they can take a full mag of any gun, including a high damage scar. Good luck hitting the sweet spot until after they hit you, which isn't even baitable, you just get hit. Retches- these things are a lose/lose, they can either damage you from afar and run, or they can be the kind to trigger hordes on explosion. Unlike however, the boomer which you could push away, and move, they just charge you and you have zero recourse. Snitches- Honestly, probably the fairest when not an auto-trigger. The Hag- a ♥♥♥♥ you to the player. Imagine a witch that comes twice and can't be dodged. Ogre- a snoozefest boss. No real threat, nothing besides a spectacle, usually just ran past. Stinger- These can either lock you in place with aimbot efficiency, or they can beat the hell out of you. Honestly the least of your problems but just ad onto it. You might hear these complaints and not really think twice about it, but the real issue is that these things are insanely strong in numbers, and it's not like L4D where you kill a few and see them rarely. These NEVER slow their spawning, they never stop coming, and usually overspawn. To ad to that, they can spawn the same one, for instance 2 Tallboys can wipe a crew in a rough spot, this happens often and after barely surviving that, another can come in seconds later. These things also don't have audio cues to let you know they're coming besides their footsteps which by the time that is audible, they're on you. 3. Cleaners and Cards To minimize this review, I'll combine these as they're pretty fundamentally boring.I at first glance was so excited for the cards, I thought ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, all the customization! In fact, if you EVER want to win against Veteran, you'll be locked to meta builds which will be an incredible grind to ever unlock the cards.You unlock cards by earning currency by beating campaigns, campaigns that without unique cards and builds can be boring after multiple runs. On top of this, failing tasks, and having people die, despite winning SEVERELY limits your currency.Most cards and cleaner abilities RARELY work as advertised. One card that says you gain health per shotgun pellet that hits? Well it only takes a few shots to kill, so if 2 or 3 out of 6 pellets hit and it dies, well you only get that much health. In fact, despite that, I'm convinced the card just doesn't work right. Temporary health which at one point was INCREDIBLY important to avoid Trauma (Trauma will be an entirely separate number), temp health only goes up to a max and disappears all at once.4. Trauma. ♥♥♥♥ me. Trauma. This mechanic is another needless ♥♥♥♥ you, if you are at 90-100 health, you will take Trauma damage, lowering you max health from 100 to maybe 96.So in chaos instances where you're scraping by and you are down to 20 health and barely survived, you finally find that medkit, but you got beat so bad, now you only have 50 health total. Fun! Don't worry though, we can be smart and avoid this mechanic, you can use pills, temporary health to avoid this when low!ERROR - BUG DETECTED - PATCHED - FUN COMMENCE NOWYes. They saw that as a bug. Now your only way to avoid trauma is to not play the game. 5. Difficulty levels. Ok, a background, I played a few hardcore games, I have over 3k hours on Dayz mod and standalone together, I am a vet of Tarkov since alpha, I know what difficulty is. I know fair, and I know ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Veteran, the 2nd tier of difficulty is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. In fact, the best way to even play their nightmare difficulty, is speedrun car builds to outrun everything. I have beaten Veteran, but only by cheesing it by having me and my friend play without players as the bots are nearly indestructible. Playing with people, unless they're very capable and on coms, it's nearly impossible. If you think this is a fun chill kill zombies game, it's not. My wife is very casual and new to games, and the easy version kicked her ass. We've breezed through L4D together on normal, but there is no normal for this game. Theres - Rough, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and Don't even bother. I hope my book of a review helped you avoid this dumpster fire.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't perfect, but it's very very good. The beta was a little rocky with some of the issues, but it looks like they're taking player feedback seriously and making lots of good design choices. While some of the decisions such as not being able to drop weapon mods once it's placed on a weapon don't make sense for realism, it makes sense in regards to game balance. Some people may find that too many special infected spawn, while me and my friends find it to be very well balanced on veteran difficulty setting. The game has some very memorable sections that I can't describe without spoiling, but it had me laughing and praising how enjoyable it was during the debriefing screen immediately following them. It's definitely worth the price tag of a AAA game, and I look forward to what the game delivers in the future. If a dev reads this, please realize that there are only a handful of things you need to change to make this a masterpiece, but as of now, there are very low hanging fruit and easy fix issues that is holding this game back from a 10/10.EDIT: Changing my review to negative since I have progressed further in the game. There are just some design choices that completely ruin the game. I can't see this game surviving the next year in the state it's in. I hate to leave a bad review because the game gets so much right, but it's just ruined over poor design choices that literally any amount of play testing could have resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the antidote to that left 4 dead itch I've had since l4d2. It fixes the slow feel of L4D's movement, and gives gunplay that feels just far enough past arcade shooter to be able to relax and unwind to. The card system is an innovative way to make a typical zombie co-op game have near infinite replayability if you don't mind RNG for the cards against you. It also invites even the weirdest builds to keep your adventures fresh. Genuinely the first 10/10 game I've played in years, even with 1k hours between both l4d games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets a fair amount of hate, and I think I understand why. Going into this expecting Left 4 Dead 3 is something a lot of people did, and it doesn't help that gaming news sites and even the devs at time, pushed this thought. This is not Left 4 Dead 3. I originally played this on PS4, and was involved in the pre release trial runs they did, and the game was in a far more rough state then than now. The AI didn't have the I part, and weapons felt weak. The second complain still stands,But now it's 2023, and the development is finished, and the game is...fairly good, It still has flaws, level design is weak at points, with some being too long or too short, the characters don't carry a ton of charm, the AI still has issues. Yet regardless of these issues, there's still quite a bit of fun to be had. Shootings things is fun, customizing weapons with attachments is enjoyable, the money system is a neat addition to the genre, and cards are a lot better now that you start with a full deck.  AI is improved from the open beta as well, even if still not great. It's a more positive experience since the Beta, but one that probably could've used some more work to smoothen out. It's a shame Turtle Rock seems to have such issues getting their games into a good stateBack 4 Blood is a tough recommendations, but it may be advisable to get the game at a discount, $60 is a bit pricey for what you're getting, but the game is still an enjoyable experience if you can get some friends to play it with you. If playing Solo, your experience will, similarly to left 4 dead, be less satisfactory and not as enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not Left 4 Dead, but it certainly carries the same ideas and feeling as those games did. The gun play is crisp and responsive, attachments give versatility to your build along with range of each weapon type. Melee combat isn't left to the wayside either, attachments for melee as well as different types of weapons for that slot gives you the choice of play style I personally love from a zombie shooter.The card system is unique and I love the variety and different types of play that these allow. If you like snipers, you can make yourself a viable sniper load-out, if you love melee like myself, you can kit out to heal when you kill a Ridden, or if you're a quick in and out lots of bullets kinda guy there's a build for you. The cards also apply in some sense to the Ridden, and that offers different mutations, threats, and additions that keep the basic loop from feeling too repetitive. _childDocuments_.review: The game isn't bad, but to be honest, it's not great. It's startlingly meh. The game is very close to being good, it has a solid foundation, but next to no polish. You can play with less, but a lot less enjoyable.It has interesting set pieces it doesn't capitalize on, it has sections that feel really well paced and fun, surrounded by incredibly forgettable sections.The story is a bit of a mess, not because it's strictly bad, but because I was  to know what was going on, but everything got lost in the noise. It feels like the devs had crystal clear images of lines and scenes that they wanted, but never bothered connecting them together. The game's characters are hollow, but the cutscenes consistently act like we've been endeared to them for the entire game. As the game goes on, more and more interesting set pieces get used, and wasted entirely because they lack follow-through and buildup. _childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10 Despite people and bots this is a Fantastic Game. The problem With this game is not the stat leveling, not the glitches, not the patch equalization, not the Difficulty... its the players. That is the same with people in general and players online in general. I like The fact that XBL has Reputation, but not how it does not hing to prevent matching you up with a trash Human player in  matchmaking, nor Crossplatform. PC doesn't have this, but I hope that the TRS system does; if not why am I rating matches and reporting griefers? Its a pity that at the time of writing this the player load dropped by 75% from launch on PC(steam stats); in less than a month. The Game is Great otherwise. Licensed songs, great levels, decent story, alright characters; This is L4D3. Aside from it being Good gameplay there are a few things that might distract players. The repetitive dialogue gets old fast(even the Poor dialogue written for Phillips, Mom, and Evangelo), Matchmaking takes forever even when there is no one to match against(almost like it tries to put you into every server instead of looking for an open slot), The BOT AI is terrible(making it almost impossible to play solo), and the quick progression of most everything to the last 5%(I have an abundance of Supply points and barely scratched Nightmare) . The Dialogue is just bad. L4D had nice random Dialogue, not every time did Francis Say he hated Stairs on stairs, but he did often enough, not every time did Louis Shout PIllz HeRe! but He did. Every time I play the Diner mission in Act 1 with Holly you have to listen to her drone on about shooting fish in a barrel, or every second mission with Evangelo you have to hear about him watching cartoons and now living a depressing life  that will surely end in death with a rebuttal of "that got dark quick" instead of look on the bright side you are alive, or suck it up buttercup, such is life now. Everytime I play Bad seeds we have to hear about hoffman's Father, Is there nothing else interesting about this region? Maybe Mom has fond memories of dating a local or childhood local Fairs. The bots, well the AI budget was put into the Special or mutated Ridden, this is clear. The AI pathing is horrible on the bots, they get stuck on corners, they just stand there doing nothing sometimes, and sometimes will teleport to one player over another only to run back to another player. They Often times walk in front of you while you are aiming, and Rarely save you from being incapacitated when you are arrested right next to them.  They shoot great, but throw their offensives wildly like someone who's cat jumped on their keyboard. I remember this stuff being an issue 10 years ago, with a bot standing over you while you waited for them to resurrect you or while they did the other bots would stand watching that bot while a horde of common pummeled both of them, seldom would they throw a pipebomb that they picked up because you pinged it. Thats another thing, Bots don't pick up or use anything other than their stock inventory, you can't ping a Defib for them to pick up, in fact when you die, they stand in a circle waiting for you to respawn. They don't carry tool kits or use their tasers. They do however Attack Relentlessly to their doom when fighting most Specials and bosses. But they take their Ques from the player, if you are stealth and quiet they are too, meaning if you try to avoid the HAG they will not shoot it, BUT! it takes them far too long to engage when you do. I still Like the game alot. This is why I recommend it. It is L4D for anyone looking for such a game. It Feels like  3 times what  L4D is now. Everything about from the glitchy bots to the grand levels are 3x more. I felt the Same about Brink and ET, it is Gone now. I hope Turtle rock studios can keep this going.

_childDocuments_.review: You can't not compare this to Left 4 Dead as it is so blatantly trying it's hardest to be the next step to a modern L4D. Problem is it fails to take what worked in L4D and take it a step further.The level design is so basic, it ignores the vertical level design used in multiple maps in L4D 1&2 which is like forgetting to texture a model, just having a grey character running around. Think of the hospital levels and scaling floors to exit at the top. Another thing Valve did was seeing the end point of where you're going at the start. Good design. Here we have bad and simple design. Not enough thought into the development.There's huge problems with AI; bots being useless, no playerbase remaining, and enemy spawning the same special infected multiple times within seconds of where you are, that still remain months after release it's ridiculous. Bots won't shoot at the Evolve-like giant monsters at all nor will they shoot at the final boss. That's a huge problem on multiple maps as you really are solo. Now it's not impossible, but on harder difficulties it nearly will be. I constantly have bots go in front of me when shooting, how is that a thing with bots? Seriously. You're wondering why not play with people? Like I mentioned, playerbase has entirely vanished. L4D has more current players than this. Crossplay became a quick hell no with how toxic I found Xbox players to be in this game. So that was an instant switch off.I will say some positives in that the card system and upgrading weapons does keep things somewhat fresh for each playthrough. I don't hate it like some may. I think having a monetary system in a zombie apocalypse makes little sense though. Why would anyone give a F about using money when humanity is near extinction? It'd be better if the game let you pick your loadout and you just found upgrades in the map/ new and better weapons while playing. Coin system is an F for me as some maps like the "Bar Room Brawl" map don't have that many coins to begin with. It can also completely slow you down and distract you and due to it being "needed" to upgrade/resupply; it comes off poorly in execution.With all that said, mostly not so great things, it's still an okay game. It's fine. Doesn't do better than its' spiritual predecessor, but isn't unplayable. I find it somewhat entertaining for a quick 30 mins or so as the maps don't feel like they require you to play through as long as L4D did, turning easily into an hour or longer playthough. So if that seems more appealing to you, then this might be up your alley. This is like fast food. It's fine, does its job, won't be that memorable, may inflict severe stomach pain to you or may not. This is not a fine dining experience, but it doesn't have to be.Mediocre, mid, a "C". It's sort of fun. It ain't broke (much) but leaves a lot to be desired. So when are we getting L4D3?.... :)

_childDocuments_.review: I can't in good consciousness recommend this game.  While its not fair to compare it to L4D2, that's what happens a good majority of the time playing the game.  There are a lot of very basic problems with the game that just ruin it.  The bad-The characters aren't really that interesting and feel like they have no life to them.  I get that its supposed to show a more serious tone to the zombie apocalypse and what not, but it becomes very boring very fast.  -The game is admittedly very linear with few rooms to explore on my own, half of which are locked behind toolbox requiring doors.  -Its very difficult to distinguish between the different types of special zombies.  Theres 3 dudes with a big arm, with the only difference being which glowing spot to shoot.  Same with the 3 dudes that resemble the hunter/jockey from L4D.  And 3 more dudes resembling the boomer/spitter.  Personally they all sound very similar to each other so I never know if Im about to be pounced by a....hunter, or by a big arm dude. -The card system doesn't really add much besides a reason to grind out levels in the game.  It adds difficulty towards the end acts with a bunch of negative cards being stacked on.-Each of the 4 acts take about as long as a L4D game used to which I don't really have a problem with.  The problem with the acts though are that acts 1 and 2 are excruciatingly boring to go through.  Act 3 is when it gets good, but then act 4 becomes a bullet dump of "hit the glowing red spot to win".-The gun attachments mechanics are........counter-intuitive.  That's me being nice about it too.The good-PVP is somewhat fun with friends.  I need to stress the friends part. (but as far as i know you cant have 4v4 lobbies of your friends?)-Sometimes cards make things a little more fun with all of the attributes you can stack on top of yourself.  The only problem is it takes so much of the act to get to the fun part of the card system.There isn't much I can recommend about the game because simply L4D is just overall the better game.  I can only imagine in short time, this will die out while L4D2 continues to hold their fan base like they have over all the years already.  Idk, you tried Turtle Rock, that's more than I can say.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to be clear that this game isn't bad or awful, but more that it's victories aren't very big and are outweighed by it's flaws and overall "meh"ness.The visuals are pretty decent and showed effort and passion, the environmental design actually was good, the alien parasite (I assume that's what they are) are neat and less common in the near-zombie games for me and are more digestible in terms of the massive monsters and obstacles, the shooting itself is pretty decent.That being said, the game just overall tends to feel bloated and spends most of its time dancing around 'passable'. The characters and attempt to tell a story aren't great and frankly are dragging the game down and I'd be glad if they got cut or even just made more character designs (or even just added character creation). The variants of monsters and even the roles of weapons feel pretty generic honestly and could be trimmed down with little to no difference in the gameplay loop.The mechanics of this game (missions, card decks, supply routes, etc.) added on after games like L4D are obnoxious and I scarcely have any appreciation for them: really just padding or maybe trying to make this game more marketable, but the borderline MMO elements are just cumbersome. Though if the decks were more limited to just variables of the mission to make the campaigns more replayable, I could see that working.TL;DR: some good design outweighed by a lot bland of filler and very clunky mechanics

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game (I enjoy PvE zombie shooters more than their PvP equivalents, so keep this in mind when reading this review),8/10 from meYou can tell it's rushed, but it feels complete, everything I would expect out of a zombie co-op game.The only thing new player should be aware of is higher difficulties are REALLY hard if you don't know what you're doing. It takes awhile to understand the card system, how to deal with special infected (much less tell them apart), but it becomes really fun when you get used to the game.After playing nightmare mode a lot, veteran mode is really easy.Game loop is essentially the same as L4D1. Safe room2. Travel the map • much lengthier3. Shoot infected • few different variations than in L4D4. Shoot special infected • different variations than in L4D5. Activate map hazard that causes hordes to show up6. Get into next safe room7. RepeatI think a lot of the negativity towards this game is a bit unfair.Things I like about the game:1 of 6. The difficultyEach difficulty changes the way you play. I used to be infuriated not knowing how the cards work, deciphering which special infected was which, figuring out how to avoid sleepers, getting used to sprint stamina. The learning curve for a PvE in is surprisingly hard and it's really satisfying knowing how everything works and mastering it.2 of 6. The card systemI thought I'd have a terrible time figuring out the card system. Turns out I'm getting along just fine and have found decks I prefer even to the 'highly recommended' ones players create in their B4B guides. I have 8 different decks of cards I selected to decide how I want to play a campaign which I think is pretty neat. Sometimes I wish I had the option to switch decks based on the players that go in and out of the game.3 of 6. Characters and LoreI hate how the characters use 'gamer-speak' (holly is the biggest offender) to try to sound badass but come off sounded really cringey. I don't like hating this, but some of the characters I do like (Hoffman, Jim, Doc) and the story backing up the environment you're fighting through really improves the experience for me. I wish L4D did this.4 of 6. Weapon and upgradesUpgrades and items you buy in the saferoom store can change how you play the rest of the levels (if you get enough copper to stack upgrades per level).5 of 6. Lack of player management systemI haven't seen any griefers in this game. Maybe some uncooperative / bad players, but these were manageable and certainly don't ruin a game as badly as a griefer could. This game currently has no vote kick, though sadly is planned to have it. No one Things that annoy me:1 of 4. No modsThis would really extend the life of the game and be free content for the players and relieve pressure from the developers to release new content.2 of 4. Buggy interactive objects/animations (doors, items/weapons)Special infected projectiles freeze in the air, make it difficult to see where it's going. Laggy infected make it 3 of 4. Annoying special infectedSome of the special infected could use some nerfing, Too short is the cooldown of a hocker (spitter + hunter) constantly pinning teammates (plus the buggy projectile makes it sometimes impossible to see where it came from). Chargers that grab you move too fast and are difficult to dodge if you don't have high speed/stamina cards.4 of 4. Corruption Card RNG (cards you pick give you buffs, corruption cards the game picks do the opposite)Too often do I get unforgiving corruption cards that will put a boss right outside the safe room, or riddle the map with horde-calling traps. These make nightmare mode especially difficult. I know it's supposed to be a ridiculously hard mode, but it should be hard because your timing needs to be better, positioning better, resource usage better. If the only way the players are beating nightmare is by breaking the game (or being stupid fast), then there's likely something wrong with the nightmare mode. Nightmare mode is beatable, but devs can you ease off the hockers/crushers please :c? (and fog while you're at it)

Fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: I only recommend this game if you have friends that you can play with. Preferably 3 friends for a full group.Overall this is a worse Left 4 Dead. The gameplay feels tight and accurate, and the action keeps up a consistent pace on the lower difficulties.The game does have many large misgivings however. Players are unable to make any tangible progress in the game when playing in a singleplayer environment. This extends to achievements as well. Another issue is the difficulty. The hardest difficulty, nightmare, demands near perfect play from all players. Even normal difficulty can be too much when relying on matchmaking. Finally, the largest issue in my eyes is the AI. The bots in this game are beyond abysmal. At times they feel like they are in a pre-alpha state. I would often have bots running up to me and standing right in my line of fire whilst doing nothing. This is exacerbated by the inclusion of friendly fire on normal and nightmare. In the end, I did have a lot of fun with this game, but I cannot fully forgive its faults. I suspect I will return to this game at some point in the future, and I can only hope that they fix some of the issues plaguing the experience.
