This system encourages experimentation and adds a layer of strategic depth, as players can tailor their decks to suit their playstyle and the specific challenges they face.ReplayabilityThe combination of different guns and the card system significantly boosts the game's replayability. Each playthrough can feel unique, thanks to the numerous combinations of weapons and cards. _childDocuments_.review: This game overall is a ton of fun with a group of friends. It gives a fun mix of L4D2 and WWZ vibes along with a lot of its own personality. One thing that I don’t see mentioned much in reviews is the game’s acceptability options. It provides many ways to change your setting to help with sight, color blindness, audio, and conditions worsened by repetitive clicking. I personally struggle with tendinitis, but the game has a full auto mode for all guns which allows you to repeatedly fire your gun without having to continually click your mouse with all weapons. Ex. Hold down the left mouse button to continually fire your sniper or shotgun. This is a great tool for me personally and wanted to highlight that for everyone.In terms of the gameplay, the gun handling is very smooth, and the attachment system gives all the guns a lot more variety in your playstyle. The card system allows you to play a ton of different roles and change up how you play the game as opposed to being stagnant repetitive gameplay as some other games can be. One point people seem to dislike is 'reusing' maps or part of maps in some levels. Personally, I enjoy seeing how each area changes over time as you progress through all 32 levels and the areas that are 'reused' are generally only at the start of a level before you head off to explore a different part of the game. As of Nov 29th when I'm writing this, it has its bugs that need to be ironed out but I'm sure will be in the coming months. A lot of people are bashing the game for the November update changing the melee build, honestly, it's nowhere as bad as people have made it out to be. As with any game that has a large amount of gameplay-changing options with the card system, balancing is ongoing and to be expected. So far I've found most of the card changes very reasonable and have only been in favor of making more play styles viable. The difficulty scaling is the only real negative for me, however, it has given me a lot of hours of playtime from trying to overcome the challenge (142 at the time of writing, and another 42 from alpha/beta testing). Overall I very much enjoy the game, have played it probably too much for my own good, and am excited to see where it goes from here. Sadly, as with basically every game released at this point, a new release comes with its bugs and needs for fixing. This game will be amazing in probably 3 or 4 months when TRS gets more patches in but is still a ton of fun on recruit and vet difficulty as we speak. I’d give it a 7.5 out of 10, with the potential for an 8 or 9 out of 10 in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be fantastic IF the devs actually cared about the game, the setting is there, the story isn't so bad and the dlc is pretty interesting as far as story goes. The perk system is, despite people complaining that its not an exact L4D clone, is pretty solid and you can make some pretty fun builds with weapons both ranged and melee. and the characters are plentiful and somewhat unique HOWEVER... the game, since launch, Is still a broken mess. before and even still there are too many mutants no matter the act or difficulty, the game relies on constant mutant spawns to make the game a "challange" when instead It makes it near Impossible since they all soak damage even on weakspots and the game spawns around 5 or 6 every minute or so on top of hordes of ridden that do about 4 to 5 damage per hit on higher difficulties. And now on top of this the server latency is the worst I've seen from a modern game. enemies not dying when they visibly get killed only to revive and still attack, bullets not landing, throwables reappearing by your feet or disappearing all together. teleporting enemies. In other words the game is a hot mess right now. So, Is the game worth Its full price? No, this game shouldn't even be out, It needed far more time to be polished and tweaked before it landed in consumer hands and instead of fixing these issues that plague this game with negative reviews, they insist on for some reason adding more content which only adds to the existing problems. I'm not saying the game is entirely bad, It has its fun moments especially with friends but overall Back 4 Blood Is in my opinion a failed title that had so much potential but received so little love.Edit: In case no one has noticed, this game is abandonware with no more updates to come, the devs refused to listen to the community to rake in as much cash as possible then ditched what could have been an insanely good L4D successor. DO NOT BUY

_childDocuments_.review: --------EDIT---------------------------------------------------------------------------EDIT----------------------------Dang 2 years later, the game is a husk of it's self, ADVISING AGAINST IT IF YOU ARE BUYING IT SOLO... Idk how long the servers would be up? but for longevity, just go ahead and just play the old school L4D.  -------------EDIT------------------------------------------------------------EDIT-----------------------------------So B4B, a $60 USD re-texture of L4D....But It is more than that, it's introduced so much to the hoard survival game play, a card system that can put you in the seat of the hero, or if poorly utilized, possibly the underdog... Unique character perks to fit a players preference, and a neat* weapon modification system.Now I don't want to seem like a bandwagon hater or lover of the game. so I want to give you a decent idea of what you'll run into... (listed i the priority list of things that'll ruin this game for you.)---- FATAL ERRORS!  So, I've "upgraded" my PC, 3 times between the original beta, to release, to today's review. During the beta, I never lost my crew of 4, there where some buggy aspects thought the beta campaign, but nothing that would flat out crash my game. During the Beta i was running a 6600k, 16gb @2666, and a 1070. 0 Fatal errors and pretty good settings etc etc, great time absolutely zooted by the experience... A little wary of the coming $60 price tag tbh, bc how often can you get 4 friends to commit to the same thing at the same time. and the $/hr ratio seemed bleak at best in those aspects. Beta cross-play was interesting but fun bc nobody had a clue what was going on.  At release I had upgraded CPU 3700x, 16gb @3000, 1070, Game looks great, ready to play with the crew I built during beta. Playing through the first Act on the week of release, collectively 5 fatal errors (IN ONE NIGHT) amongst my crew leading to having one of my peers to call it an evening at the climax of the Diner Mission. The week before this review, 3700x 16gb @3000, 3060 ti, there was a small patched released a few days before I played with this build. Current play-through fatal error count 0. (But in my crew 2, which we believe is tied to a single users hardware issue more so, than a fault of the game.) So I am under the assumption they plugging away at the bugs as they arise. But said issues need to be known about. So kudos Turtle Rock to your work so far, keep it up. ----Single Player, Multi Player, and Cross-play (?)So solo game play, Throw the idea out the window if you're trying to earn supply points to unlock the cool stuff... BUT! If you wanna see a deck build first hand, sure... You can build a deck around a run, got a new card but don't wanna blow a current run to try it out? Solo is there for your guinea pig plans.    Multiplayer, Friends, STEAM friends and B4B Friends, was a good attempt to integrate the cross-play functionality to the friends list, Idk why they didn't just to a filtered list  vs the tabs they used, but that is more so a UI design than a game play mechanic, but I think a better implementation would have been creating a (#1234) code like discord uses to just staple to the end of a user name vs splitting them all up the way they did, (But I am not a programmer and I may have 100% understanding of the logistics in that process. )Accessing the cross play toggle is a little annoying, But at least they put it somewhere you can find using context clues. (PREFERENCES for those who have't figured it out yet, bc it took me a second when my Gamepass peers found out I had B4B.)--- That little * from before, Weapon RNG, Weapon Modifier system. It actually makes you have to make decisions! OH NO A CHOICE! Do I wish I could have all gold attachments, yes, I think anybody would love that... I Collected quite a few cool builds of guns. _childDocuments_.review: 60 hours in, and I'm already getting bored of the game.There is no public lobby system, where you can wait for people to join your lobby. Instead, you click a queue button and a mysterious algorithm matches you with other players at random. Unfortunately the matchmaking in this game is very atrocious, and seems to prioritize starting as many games as possible instead of making full games. So, very often, you will  have one other human with you in campaign. As well in Swarm, there are a few issues with the matchmaking literally making lopsided teams (3 versus 1) and now they have a . Thankfully, I discovered a work-around to bypass the leaver penalty right now, but man that is a disaster.The guns feel like noodles, and the mutations (special zombies) feel like sponges. I would imagine, even at the lowest difficulty, the game constantly reminds you how weak you are as a single individual. There are some serious balance/mechanic concerns that need to be addressed in both swarm (PvP) and campaign (PvE).The game feels incredibly rushed and you can see a serious lack of QA in many parts of the game, such as sleepers (traps) spawning out of bounds. As always though, Turtle Rock Studios never disappoints in the graphics department, but that's generally never been an issue for them.

_childDocuments_.review: Wait for a sale, then don't buy it anyways. Boring game with difficulty only meaning fight LESS somehow and ignore everything. Devs don't know how to balance at all. Cards add literally nothing to the game and are either required for higher difficulties, or do super lame "+5% damage while you're exhaling" and never change gameplayThe devs actively discourage you from fighting zombies in higher difficulties and change the game to make fighting harder and speeding through easier.It feels like almost every 'change' in this game from L4D is a bad one. The rougelite elements don't enhance play. They just discourage many forms of it.And I guarantee you you'll stay on the fence over the 2 hours required for refunding, because this game has A LOT of new knowledge checks to keep you guessing "am I the problem?" at first. You are not.Edit: When I wrote this review I realized it was a little brief and I mention changes being bad. It's not just the roguelite. Specials: Several new zombies are just old zombies split into two. Ogre and crusher both are steps down in threat level and AI capabilities from tanks. Basically the new specials are a huge mixed bag. It's like the game already needs a Back 4 Blood 2 to revamp that aspect, and more one-dimensional specials isn't going to fix it later.Survivors: They just don't have the charm. They aren't as sassy and don't comment too much. This leaves the story lackluster, and I couldn't care less if every one of them went the way of Bill.Level design: Yeah you get like 30 levels or whatever in this game, but honestly it feels like less overall. Many of the levels are straight up re-uses of previous levels, and several more are short single-room locations where you do the single objective then win. More money, less content.Progression: In L4D the only real progression is weapons getting slightly better in terms of models that could do more, but in this game since cards and upgrades are stacked towards later chapters, that just means you should pick up and play on later levels always. I like the idea of weapon mods you can pick up as you play, I don't like the idea of of 2-1-1 being harder than 2-2-3 because I don't have enough cards to actually heal myself or force heals to spawn or whatever, or weapons strong enough to actually fight what's in front of me because gray rarity and blue rarity are identical, except one poops damage and one can't kill a tall boy without reloading 3 times.Weapons: I won't lie. The gun play feels ok, except the then they go and gimp normal gunplay features like reload speed and weapon swap speed unless you get cards to reduce them. I guess I'm just incentivized to play with one weapon? To uhhh not reload? So my question is this: If you like gun play in your FPS, what would you sacrifice for faster aim down sights speed and weapon swap, etc. to make it feel better? Would you sacrifice move speed? Would you forego the ability to melee? Give up some damage? That's what the card system is doing, and it doesn't feel good.

_childDocuments_.review: While I was on the fence when playing the betas due to the wonky spawning and rather worrying trends I can honestly say that I would absolutely recommend this.   The game hits the same pleasure that L4D did upon its own launch and yes people fault in so many ways and saying how it can't live up to the masterpiece of L4D2.     The thing is.. with living up to master pieces of the past is that people never seem to be able to remember that left 4 dead had a rough start as well.  But multiple updates,  nostalgia and a passionate community is why left 4 dead is remembered fondly.There are still a few things I want to go deeper into.Weapon rarities and attachments provide opportunities and incentive to mix things up,   With 3 rarities on the weapon for their main stats which then get further enhanced by what attachments they have.While I would like a way to move attachments around better or at least carry one attachment for later use I cannot say that I felt this in any way hindered my enjoyment of the game.  But then again I love my roguelites and roguelikes so sacrificing the total stats for a weapon with better base stats is one of those gambits you will encounter.    Attachments also provide a healthy source of being able to reduce the weaknesses of certain weapons,   Faster aim down sights or faster movement speed,   Reload speed or increased damage.   very much a refreshing take that I have wanted in the genre for a long while.It is true... i'm not particularly a fan of the current way the deck functions.   in the beta you would frequently see similar decks with the much well known cards be run time and time again.   And some cards like Combat Knife was just to good to pass up.   The rebalance to make some cards more interesting is a nice thing like buckshot bruiser now giving temp health for each pellet hit similar to vermintide's mechanics has turned from something I kinda like to something I pretty much use for every shotgun build.My biggest gripe with the deck system also involves the corruptions.   As I feel like the intention of needing to adapt your deck to what corruptions appear does not happen as some cards just are so much more impactful than others,   And some of the corruptions feeling much to generic and not having enough impact.The challenge cards also have a few issues in the way they are implemented as there are seemingly nothing stopping birds from spawning on the one path to the safehouse.  Usually leading to a perfect completion being ruined due to larmed doors or birds in the very last sectionAnd to end this I would like to say that I know why people feel like this game is missing something and I do feel it to.   I miss the visceral glory of L4D's dismembered zombies and the explosions of pipebombs and propane tanks sending things flying,   I still feel the force behind B4Bs weapons as they visibly are pushed back and staggered from shotgun rounds of 50cal,  But other than that there is no real visual reaction.I love the game and fully reccomend it even if quickplay with randoms can be a bit frustrating with people still not being used to the game yet.   if you are on the fence then wait until a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Times I've killed an ogre: 22Times I've killed Evangelo for standing in front of me: 200$20 game with $60 graphicsSpoiler alert: I compare this game to L4D2 more times than I've misheard walker saying "stinger"Keep in mind the whole time I only played as a group of 2 with 2 bots.My main complaints might not effect you if you always have a group of 4 and don't have to deal with the WORST AI I'VE EVER EXPERIENCED IN A GAME. I've never complained about AI in a game until now. Even call of duty campaign enemies have more brains than Evangelo the teleporting houdini who has a buckshot fetish and prefers to run in place for 5 minutes instead of reviving you. I don't get how they can program your ally bots far worse than L4D2, a 12 year old game made by THE SAME DEVS? (I'm sure the dev team changed talent a lot, I know)On top of that even in a full multiplayer group of 4 everyone is stuttering around at 2fps like they're using grandma's pacemaker for an internet connection. Being physically blocked and pushed around by AI or friends that stutter around like this is infuriating, especially when you are on a higher difficulty with friendly fire. Expect to get into arguments about who stepped in front of who and why it's your fault that Walker has a hole in his left lung. On recruit, playing as a duo with my buddy (you can't turn off the 2 additional AI allies) was ridiculously easy, sort of as expected, didn't die once until we got pushed off the map one time. More of a difficulty for playing twice over to figure out different builds and characters and early farming those supply points for deck building. My first experience on veteran however...<<Friendly fire: Enabled>>Not a fun experience, at least with AI teammates that take "sticking together" far too literally. On top of that, the amount of special ridden spawns seemed to triple in one difficulty increase from recruit to veteran, and all the specials seemed to be made of diamond coated kevlar from how many bullets it takes to take one down if you don't hit the weakspot (which is usually armored or hidden behind stuff). I found that the best way to beat veteran with 2 people is to just use a broken melee build with a fire axe to one shot the specials and hope you don't get 90% of your health trauma'd.The deck system seems...okay. They definitely needed something like it to make it different from L4D2 and to keep people coming back and playing. I think they did it pretty well, but would definitely like to see more cards added over time.The story was generic. The characters are generic (I can't stand Holly's voice, she gives me Borderlands 3 Ada PTSD). Didn't expect much on that front so I can't say i'm disappointed. A whole playthrough is actually pretty long, much longer than standard L4D2 i think.  For whatever reason they decided to make the main menu into a far cry style home base where u wander around and interact with the NPCs except you don't interact with the NPCs at all because individually walking to each vendor NPC is pointless since all the menus are connected if you just click tab. Oh deck builder guy over there? Too bad. Why should I walk over to him when clicking tab gets me to it. The base ends up being a "what can I parkour on while I wait for my friend to finish his deck" simulator. Feels like they wanted to do something with it and just didn't.Swarm mode was a mistake, just don't play that, ever. It's like everything you hated about L4D2 versus mode except there's no objective. You just survive the longest in a fortnite bubble that constantly shrinks, against 4 VERY FAST SPAWNING player controlled exploders and crushers, and then swap sides. L4D2 did it better by far.Gunplay is decent, would've liked a bit more unique guns rather than 4 different variations of the same rifle, and then the standards from L4D2. But at least they added attachment pickups! -which you can't remove... or swap onto a different gun... or drop for a friend...Graphics and optimization, yeah its good. First game i've seen running DX12 that doesn't make my pc explode. Solid 120+ fps on a GTX 1070 on medium-high ish. Definitely looks more visually appealing than L4D2 (the 12 year old game that's still better even without workshop support)Despite having 9 different* (3 variations of 3) special zombies, I feel like they are far less memorable and clear as to what they are, compared to L4D2, as well as less scary, harder to differentiate, and bullet spongey on higher diffs. There are the bosses that show up once in a while, kinda cool except when they summon a horde of 20 crushers alongside them so you have to ignore the boss for 5 minutes while u beg Evangelo to take the hits for you.The game COULD improve on a lot and end up being amazing, but for right now, it's not, or at least without 4 players, and I heard matchmaking is abysmal.A lot of people got B4B from the xbox gamepass, which is what you should do and don't spend $60 like I did. Or wait for a sale, a big sale, $20 at most really.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the systems in the game feel like they exist mostly to pad game time instead of having a more complex take on the level design and enemies. The biggest offender i feel is the trauma damage system and armored enemies. The levels themselves are noticeably short and straight forward, so to compensate for this enemies are dumped on you in droves, while this itself isnt an issue, problems arise when friendly fire is so punishing. You have these two systems playing tug of war with each other where you want this fast paced gameplay killing all the zombies but are punished for doing so if you accidently shoot your teammates where they lose a good chunk of health. So its either let them get hit by zombies and lose hp while they clear it out themselves or kill the zombies around them and shoot your team making them lose the same amount of hp. This might not be a big issue if the trauma system didnt exist. What the trauma system does is make it so your total hp is reduced when you take a certain amount of damage, which eventually will result in your hp reaching as low as 40. Aside from these systems the armored zombies just in general arent fun and dont make much sense, spongey enemies that arent bosses are more of a chore then interesting game design. Why not just make a separate enemy that is tankier and an enemy that is a glass cannon instead. If you're going into this game expecting it to feel like left 4 dead you might be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy spiritual successor to LFD2. It's not a perfect game, but it's definitely a lot of fun. It can really be summarized like this: -It has all the same features as the old LFD2 game. Only with a ♥♥♥♥-ton of progression, unlocks, and features added. Oh and btw, 2021 graphics. -The problems with the game really come from matchmaking, worthless bots, and really other players.... There's a lot of players that are really just ♥♥♥♥ at the game, and don't really try to learn to play properly. And many just turn out to be trolls and griefers. You'll definitely have a better time with friends, or a dependable gaming community than you will risking running into console players that shoot every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ alarm they come into contact with. Overall, it's an outstanding game hindered by a lack of quality-of-life features that many other games in the genre have had for years.  Those problems listed below. But, overall  grade is 8/10. The games downfalls come from a lack of quality-of-life features. -Bots are absolutely worthless. Devs reallllly need to take notes from Vermintide 2 on how to correctly program and use Bots. they aren't overpowered, but they are at least worthy teammates. -Players seemingly can't hot-drop into games once it's started. If they're able to, it certainly doesn't happen. Algorithms need to be adjusted to fill empty games. -Difficulty levels are absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Rookie at times is completely insane. Veterans and higher difficulties are just absolute chaos. Either difficulty needs to be adjusted, or more levels need to be added, on a varying scale. -The whole weapons information/attachments system can be vague, and frustrating at times. Seeing what you have, and trying to quickly compare something new. -A votekick needs to be added. There are some players that just want to grief the lobby, purposely hitting every alarm, triggering every trap, bringing Mutated to the party without trying to kill them, -A timer needs to be set on the saferoom when exiting. Because other griefers will sit in the room, trying to halt progress, or trying to handicap the team. Once the majority of the team leaves the saferoom, a timer should start, and once it expires, those left in it should be kicked from the game and replaced by a bot, or another player. Other minor nitpicks:Again, this is me admittedly nitpicking. -Not all weapon attachments show visual modifications. Suppressors, laser-sights, and sights do. but not all barrel attachments, and extended mags. -It would be cool to be able to shoot at random roaming zombies out front of Fort Hope while in the safe zone. Extend the shooting range capabilities. The dummies are okay for gauging damage and all, but they aren't moving targets. -More guns would be cool. Yeah there's a good selection now, but more is always better. More attachments too.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy this game at full price.It is overpriced and I bought this game on a sale expecting a somewhat bad-to-mid experience and that's what I got. I had a fun experience over all, but I feel like certain parts of the game mudify it entirely and over all this is kind of a miss. It's a fun little thing that can keep you entertained for a while but you'll be left salty that this isn't better.Story sucks, character sucks, gameplay is fun for a while, especially with friends. Solo experience is miserable for me.1. The corruption cards can make this game really interesting, or really not fun by putting some really annoying modifiers. Getting armored bruisers or powered up enemies that oneshot you from 80 hp is just not fun. Additionally it makes it so that when you plan and make a deck that seems solid, a corrupt modifier can just run it into the ground anyway.2. The deck experience has a fantastic UI but honestly it's a pain in the neck to build a deck because of the amount of possibilities you can gather. This is my subjective opinion - if you like that kinda thing where you plan builds and stuff, it's pretty cool. I as a casual player who isn't really sold on it (I just wanted to kill zambies ), it's fine as at surface level and it seems like you can get by with just slotting whatever you feel like.3. Trauma HP is really punishing for no reason, and while it encourages you to make builds that go against it, you don't have the cards at the start. I don't mind it later on, when you can pick your cards better, but early on its a pain in the neck.4. Continues and acts are more frustrating and time wasting. Considering people can farm the extra continues cards, this should've went away.5. Easy anti cheat and mod prevention. This game was brought to you by from the makers of L4D. Most of what we got in L4D2 was permitted by valve, yes, like workshop. But the addition of EAC and different engine means that we can not server mod the game, nor easily host locally as we want to. This severely for me hits the replayability of the game as I had a lot most of my fun in modded campaigns, workshop, and modded servers that I can host. This to me severely, drastically makes the game so much worse.6. Can't choose, pick your bots, etc.EDIT: After some playtime I think it gets better at the end game with decks and stuff, so I updated my review to reflect it. I still don't think it's worth its current price but will upvote it instead.

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the Left 4 Dead series, then you will most likely enjoy this game. However, it's a game worth playing with your friends because it takes a fair bit of teamwork to get through the campaign as well as the pvp mode (swarm). The replay value is pretty high especially if you have friends who just buy the game so you end up running through the missions again and getting supplies to unlock new cards, outfits, and skins. Be warned, the difficulty level jumps pretty high from recruit to veteran to nightmare. There is no in between and you might find yourself getting frustrated, but that's why it's fun to replay the missions with some challenges (similar to running a COD campaign from recruit to veteran). Another reason the replayability is so high, are the corruption cards that always change the threats you face each time you start a new campaign run. You have to be very flexible in your card deck for buffs as well as the type of weapons you decide to use or the tactics you employ with your friends.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, don't get me wrong, but I struggle to find incentive to keep with it. Upon completing campaign on Veteran, I attempted Nightmare a few times, but eventually found it to be more frustrating than in was worth.The first big blow is the characters. If you're coming from Left 4 Dead and hoping for anything remotely close, you wont find it here. You have characters like Karlee who seem like the most cookie-cutter "daddy issues" girl; characters like Jim who cant stop reassuring everyone that he's a country boy hunter; characters like Holly who have such forced dialogue at times, particularly the diner, to "drive home" (heh) how much of a quirky tomboy she is; characters like... you get the picture. With that laid out, how about the story mode with characters like these?How about the gameplay? Well, it's interesting. I would say that it does feel solid, the weapons design is great, and the sound work is phenomenal; however, I feel that Back 4 Blood falls short of its goal of being a tactical horde shooter due to some seemingly great ideas, and some genuine oversights. First of all, this game being on Game Pass seems great, but when you have NO ranking system and NO barrier to Veteran and Nightmare, it becomes a nightmare. To put it simply, your team needs to be incredibly communicative, organized, varied, and persistent. This becomes a fleeting result when casual players using the Game Pass will join high difficulty lobbies and, to put it lightly, ruin the entire experience.This doesn't even touch on cards too much, but its well designed, and is genuinely quite enjoyable; however, I think that it also adds to how sweaty the game ends up being and how necessary it is to have good teammates.Side note: I personally hate the change from Source-like hipfire accuracy. I'm a source game and Halo game fan, so going to ADS and low-accuracy hipfire hurts my soul. Feels too much like COD.Narrative: Eh.Without spoiling (not spoiling much, trust me) the story follows a varied crew of flat characters. No development happens of note. These characters, who often don't have the interesting dialogue you could have with a set cast, fight through four acts of, sadly, often reused assets. You know, taking a map that appeared earlier in the campaign and slightly altering it. This happens an unacceptable amount of times. I can see possible "world building" surrounding Fort Hope, patrolling nearby areas, but I never got that sense of defending the fortress whatsoever. It just felt lazy.The turning of the tide toward the end is pretty damn predictable, in all honesty. Smart science man make big discovery, ooo we may win! whats this? they're more powerful than we thought? oh, how compellingly original.PVP: Can't hold you.I got into Swarm for a while. Its essentially a survival VS mode, teams switching sides playing as ridden or cleaners; however, it's on set maps with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fortnite circle. Ther's no interesting gimmick like going point A to point B, filling something, etc... It's a set experience that essentially has a hard time limit due to the shrinking of the map.What you end up with is a super competitive mode with no ranks, minimal supply points, and all the problems listed at the top.I've just vomited all this out in about 15 minutes, so I hope it helps you decide whether or not you purchase the game. As someone who spent 80 USD, I can tell you that it is likely not worth your money. There are INFINITEly better games to play, some quite ICONIC as compared to this, I'd say....it's halo. im talking about halo infinite.hell, just got play L4D2 if you want this experience.

Also the fact that a special spawns every 30 seconds to a minute even while doing absolutely nothing completely ruins most cards that require you to kill things from range that are near your group because you know for a fact that something is going to try to spawn on you which is more annoying than fun, also the concept of when you clear an area it doesn't stay cleared gets old fast. _childDocuments_.review: Putting more time into the game I decided to update my review.There is also a lot of hate surrounding this game, so I will try to make this as objective as possible.+Card system is very fun, it can be quite tedious to grind it out, but once you do, it feels very rewarding and opens you up to plenty of ways to possibly play the game.+Post December patch makes Nightmare and Veteran easier. While you can have moments where you die to BS, a lot of the time it is reliant on your team composition and how you are performing. This game is not as hard as it seems once you put time into it. Players need to realize you get punished HARD for mistakes on harder difficulties. -+ Unfair at times due to its roguelite elements, but IMO, keeps the game fresh and interesting.- AI is dumb.- Dialogue is poorly written at times except for a select few character: Mom, Hoffman in particular. I do hope TRS works on improving this in future content.-No Vote to kick makes the you have to tolerate or leave a match due to trolls or players who are sabotaging a run. I haven't run into this much though, and there are tools to counter some of these things.+Gunplay is solid and feels good.+Challenging.-Swarm/Versus sucks ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ plans of a campaign versus has also been deconfirmed.-+While the dialogue sucks at times, the cast does actually have some depth and synergy. The problem here though is that it's not all equal. Certain characters feel more relevant than others and certain characters have no synergy at all. Anybody who tells you they have no personalities or no depth is either lying to you or hasn't played the game.++++Hoffman.Buy it on sale. It's a fun and enjoyable game and I feel I have gotten my moneys worth thus far, but I can see the price being too steep for others who many not get the same enjoyment as I. It's good but not mindblowing, the card system allows many different methods of play to keep the game entertaining or cater to your playstyle.Anyway, Hoffman/10.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off I will have to justify my hours. I liked this game, I used it as escapism and as an aim trainer. B4B has many problems which can be relatively ignored by casual players, but their problems are building up and the bad just outweigh the good at this point. Their greedy DLC also introduced many complications.It was quite a forgettable story but my main point: nothing in this game makes sense. I am aware it’s a game, but when you follow the story you are forced to do dumb actions that would get you killed or would make no sense in real life. Due to the character limit I cannot provide examples.Gunplay is great to an extend but tries too much to be like other shooters with upgradable weapons. Alarmed doors changed as they are now unbreakable by any enemy unless you either trigger the door or have the card Stealthy Passage in your deck. This was an unwelcome change and most players don't bother anyway so if you have Silence is Golden you lose a lot of money. Endless hordes are also a thing, but are ridiculous at Bad Seeds Act 1 and Cabins by the Lake Act 3 when using the moving platform.Here are some points that killed the fun largely in the game for me:The developers want you to play the slow and steady approach with lots of hordes. They nerf cards that are over-used even tho that is precisely what this game is about: find the optimal deck for your play-style. They are against speedrunners to the point they have nerfed all the move speed cards and move mechanics where the (offline speedrunner) community just left the game. Not all changes are reported in their patch notes and some changes have not been implemented as indicated (chaos card gave -75% healing efficiency instead if the indicated -50%, On Your Mark gave players only 5% ammo instead of the 10% (used to be 15%). Mistakes can be made but it’s starting to feel unprofessional having to rely on players reporting these issues. Melee was also nerfed a lot but is ultimately redundant, as shooting will always be more effective.The game introduced a great mechanic to enhance your runs by using an extra card that would be consumed and activate for the current level. The devs, however, did not like how users obtained and used these cards. They raised the cap from 99 to 999 burn cards, made it harder to pay for burn cards you actually want, as you have to go through a section of “common” useless burn cards in each supply line, making you waste supply points essentially. They nerfed hired gun massively by two ways and made it selfish. From 500c copper (1c per kill) to each player to 750c to only one player, which costed 80 SP but now you have to spend 3 skull points (was 4), an absurd price tag and only accessible if you have the DLC or play with people who own it. To beat the burn card Windfall now you would have to kill at least 600 ridden.. I get it was overused since it made money cards slightly redundant, but I would argue that using burn cards was always an optional way to play the game.This game has too many bugs. Bugs happen in any game I understand, but there are some game breaking bugs that will never get fixed since not all bug reports are looked at unless they have a sufficient amount of upvotes, invalidating some valid bug reports. Some bugs can really frustrate you since some don’t have a work around and players will have to wait 2 to 3 months for the developers to possibly fix. Most annoying bug was the increased special spawnrate, where at times we had to deal with more specials than ridden and could not catch a break. I also find it laughable how they prioritise "fixing" a fence now blocking you from picking up items through it at The Diner instead of fixing game-breaking bugs.Their servers are not always great to play on, often times ping is elevated, making it hard to either shoot the ridden accurately or punch them away in time, making you miss your shot, take damage or even have the game trick you into killing the ridden on your screen, but not on their server, which will reset their HP but not refund your shot. A way to fix this is to host a local server, but that is not an option right now.Bots have great aim, too great at times, as they are very good at clearing hordes, but very bad at dealing with specials and bosses at times. They rarely heal you when you need it, they run in your way A LOT, they stay behind sometimes or just literally go into the middle of the horde while your team is hugging a wall.Most players you will face are casual players, new players or if you’re playing at night stoned/brainless players. It’s rare to find good players so if you find them, try to befriend them to enhance your experience. The overal quickplay experience is terrible. Almost everyone is selfish, takes the free first aid cabinet heals all by themselves and yoinks attachments/items. It’s a first come first serve kind of deal. Healers are not appreciated and/or forgotten as players just heal themselves, even when there is a doc in the team or you stated you are a healer. People rarely listen and do their own thing. The side objective “Silence is golden.” is almost never met and you will almost always lose the money as hordes are so easily triggered. Team Upgrades are hardly ever bought unless someone takes the initiative to ask for money to pay for an upgrade, most players just buy items for themselves and not think of the team and often forget to buy a toolkit for the stash room. Also, cross-players seem to be the most braindead players you’ll ever meet.I can’t judge swarm too much since I have barely played it. And that is just the issue, it’s highly unpopular, it’s hard to find a game and whenever you do find a game, theres a 75% chance of players leaving after or even during the first round, leaving your chances of winning to 0.I got it gifted, but I would not have spent the amount of money they ask for this game. The game looks great and has amazing cgi animations, but it relies too much on team play from the player base, fails to make much sense when it comes to the lore, has too many bugs to count that we have to deal with for long periods of time, has iffy servers, force you to play how the developers want you to play and has questionable balancing. They also have now split the playerbase in this online game as Act 5 is part of the overpriced DLC. Non-DLC players were left with nothing with the new act 5 release until they put cosmetics unlocks in the Supply Lines due to the Duffel Bags being bugged ...

_childDocuments_.review: The game's major good point is the card system. It gives the game just enough variety to make it feel different from the old L4D series, and is fun to craft and build strategies, but it doesn't take away from the classic zombie co-op feel. Furthermore, the unique characters also make the game interesting, along with fun voice acting that changes depending on who is in the team. However, I must tell new buyers to stay away for many reasons. However, most of the reasons can be boiled down to one: the continue system.1. The continue system on the Veteran and Nightmare difficulties is a huge pain. Essentially, instead of having a save point every round, you get a save point every 2 or 3 rounds. Compound this with the fact that you only get 1 continue (retry), if you lose both attempts, you have to restart potentially 2 or 3 rounds. This is a huge pain, especially on longer levels. I am currently stuck on reaching The Clog in Act 2 (I have been stuck on these two levels for 8 hours now, and have tried with three different teams of all competent players), where the sheer length of the two levels makes keeping health and ammo up very very difficult, even on Veteran. Essentially, the developers want you to grind in the game. But here is the second problem. 2. Losing rounds doesn't even give you fractional supply points. That means you can grind for hours on one level and not get any points. Essentially, you are forced to play on recruit or play Swarm multiplayer to get points, in order to play the actual game, which is the Veteran/Nightmare campaign. But I don't want to play some super easy recruit mode and ruin the story just to get points. 3. The single player mode is a joke. I don't even need to go over the points here. 4. The enemy spawns are ridiculous and totally random. Even though you can theoretically learn the maps by doing recruit, every match there are minor differences in placements or spawns of items or enemies. Although this randominzation is supposed to make the game replayable, it just makes the game impossible. For example, once, we went through the sewer pipes and met like 2 mutated enemies. That was it. And then in the next level to reach The Clog, we were attacked by an Ogre + 4 retches and 3 tall boys at the same time in the middle of a field of crows and we died. The next time we tried again on sewers, we were all killed by back to back sleepers who spawned in places they didnt spawn last time. And so on. 5. They record voice chat. Need I say more? 6. The quick play system is a joke, I'm not sure how it even works with the campaign. There are either two options: first is you create your own run and hope people join you in a reasonable time, which doesn't happen, because everyone wants to start where they last left off. My average wait time is about 10 minutes, but if you include the matches that dont get a full lobby (usually I just get one other human teammate), the real wait time is about 30 minutes. The Second option is to join another team and hope they are at the same place you are, otherwise, you may be grinding through the entire act again, just to be with a full team. 7. There is no option to stick with the same team after a section is completed or after you lose, unless you are in a party. TLDR: All in all, the game is fun and nice, the core card concept is good. But the continue system and the mindless grinding makes it not worth it. Also the cost is too much, 60$ and no DLC even. Don't buy this game. Wait for the price to come down and then buy. And when you do buy it, make sure you have a dedicated team of friends with discord to play it. Because currently it's impossible.

_childDocuments_.review: Back 4 Blood is a game that has the potential to be great, but falls short in some areas. On one hand, the game has excellent graphics and a fantastic soundtrack that immerses you in the zombie apocalypse world. The gunplay is also satisfying and offers a variety of weapons to choose from, making it a thrilling experience. Additionally, the game offers a unique card system that adds a layer of strategy and customization to the gameplay.On the other hand, the game is let down by its lack of content and repetitive missions, which can become dull after a few hours of gameplay. The AI-controlled teammates are also not very intelligent, often making foolish decisions that can be frustrating for players. Additionally, the game's difficulty level is inconsistent, with some levels being too easy and others being too difficult, making it hard to find a good balance.In conclusion, while Back 4 Blood has its strengths, it falls short in some areas. However, it's still a fun game that offers a unique experience for zombie apocalypse fans, and with some improvements, it has the potential to be even better.

_childDocuments_.review: As it stands now, it is the edgelord cousin to Left 4 Dead. It wants to be "cool" and "edgy" but fails to be either.The major issue is the AI. The NPC bots are dumber than a bag of bricks (a bag of bricks would be more useful). If you're not strolling with four human players then good luck, you'll need a lot of it. The AI that controls hordes, the ridden, and specials is also broken. The way it handles hordes and specials worked before the November 2021 updates. After these updates the manageable, but difficult, horde and special structure worked. It was challenging at all levels and scaled up as difficulty scaled up. Now the easiest difficulty is harder than what was once considered moderate. Pump the brakes on your breaking the game devs. I get balancing the gameplay and cards, but breaking it makes it annoying.The other big issue is the "continues" system. By making their game the edgy, Dark Souls wannabe of zombie shooters the game ensures you will die a lot. But the continues system makes that impossible to manage. You're always being dumped back at Fort Hope because you ran out of continues while exploring, experimenting, or playing with the new horde AI. It's stupid and discourages exploration, experimentation, and attempting harder difficulties. Instead of growing and mastering the game, I just want to get my achievements and go home. Little to no replay value because of the stupid "continues" system. The cards do not add anything there.The buggy and glitchy achievements have been worked on, so that's a plus. I haven't has as many disconnect issues either. Framerate problems still plague my friends' computers as the forced locked framerate in settings causes a lot of screen tearing.Overall, the gameplay is rather good and it is challenging. With completely broken and terrible AI systems and an awful "continues" system the game is nearly unplayable though. Hard to appreciate the characters, the lore, the gameplay, the multiple gun combos, the card combos, and more when the AI simply breaks everything and you're punished for trying new things.4/10. I hope the devs get their act together and fix what they continue to break.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I don't really do Quick Play, so I have no clue how the matchmaking is. _childDocuments_.review: This game has one of the most replayability values I think I've seen ever. The "content cycle" (I guess?) is extremely replayable and hella fun. (I can run with with a 3060 and so can my friend with a 1650)The character system is fun to change each game and how it plays.There are great cosmetics in the game, and ZERO MICROTRANSACTIONS!There are multiple different modes, whether it be PvP or PvE for you to experiment with.The training range is very fun with ranges to mess around in, and I've spent over 10 hours combined with the beta and now playing there with friends.Cons:The game is definitely not worth $60, I got it on sale for $6 and the DLCS for $4, so that's why I'm more happy with the game compared to others.There is not enough content, and the devs game up on the game too early due to the hate from the game not being L4D3. (which is quite a shame, I could see this game being in my top 5 if it got more content.)All of the DLCs suck. After buying them, I cannot see much change in the game besides the new characters & the warped chests. There is no new acts added or even maps, just little coves and gambling + overpowered characters. Of course, I got these with $4, so I'm still happy, but they're normally $15+.There aren't enough weapons in the game.Overall, still a great game. This game has sparked a feeling of fun in me that I haven't gotten since I was a kid. Don't get me wrong, this game is no where near worth $60, or $45, or even $30, but it's definitely worth $6. I am so in love with it, and can see myself booting it up in the future whenever I'm bored to just have some mindless fun. (Kinda like older Call of Duty games with good zombies?)8.75/10. _childDocuments_.review: As a diehard Left4Dead fan, I didn't buy this game on release, but 2 years later. The reviews kind of deterred me away from it as I'm sure it did for other people, but it went on sale so I said screw it, I'm gonna get it. I'm REALLY happy I did. I even decided to get the annual pass as well after the first day because I can see myself playing this game a lot.Back4Blood is packed full of action, it can get intense. I've been playing it with friends and my husband, and we've been enjoying the hell out of the game. Basically played it all night the first night. It feels somewhat familiar like Left4Dead, but it plays like a more polished and modern game. The FEEL is L4D as is the core premise, but the mechanics are a different game all together. The class system is really fun to mess around with, as are the cards and cosmetics. You can modify weapons, modify perks. There's more depth to this game than just logging in, hopping into a match and just going. There's a feeling of progression and there's definitely a higher sense of achievement for completing missions. The graphics are beautiful, and there are lots of things to admire about the game looks. The zombies are creepy and badass looking, the characters are awesome. I really like the custom weapon skins and changing up my characters appearance.I like that there are hives you can jump into during a campaign. So it's not just the same old campaign over and over and just switching difficulties. You can choose to take on a bunch of difficult modifiers and hop into a hive. The feeling of communication and teamwork is really important in B4B too.I will certainly get my monies worth out of this game. I really like where they went with it and it makes me sad it got the hate that it did. It's actually really fun and well done game. The only negative I have to say so far, is it would be awesome if there was mod support or at least player made campaigns, but maybe some day.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, the story is something that you’ll most certainly ignore in this game. It's the same old plot setup, where the majority of individuals transform into zombies and the survivors must now struggle to survive. Back 4 Blood's storyline would be the same if the survivors were renamed Cleaners and the zombies Riddens. Most of you have probably played or heard about Left 4 Dead 2. This game is essentially an improved version of that one. The majority of B4B's negative reviews are comparisons to L4D2. Let's get into more detail about the mechanics of the game and how they differ from the well-known zombie shooter.To say that Back 4 Blood's gunplay is enjoyable would be an understatement. Zombies have never been slain with such enjoyment. You'll discover a diverse armament ranging from melee weapons that can one-shot zombies to assault guns that can be fully modified. Personally, I like utilising melee weapons because I wanted to experience the exhilarating feeling of slicing through the zombies. But when the difficulty rose, I was forced to swap out my melee weapons for handguns. I definitely wasn't let down! You can always try something new because nearly every weapon has a different recoil, handling, and attachment. The gunplay was a solid 10/10 all around.Without a question, the champion in this regard is Left 4 Dead 2. Unlike B4B, where the whole campaign takes place in and around Fort Hope, L4D2's campaigns were all situated in distinct places with unique settings. To make the game even more immersive, the game creators could have worked on this. The environments get incredibly uninteresting and start to seem repetitive as you progress through the levels.This is essentially the part that sets it apart from other zombie shooters. There are 11 different Cleaners that you may choose from and play as; each one has unique skills that affect gameplay. However, the Cleaners themselves are not the only ones with skills! Using game Cards, B4B has developed a unique method of introducing diversity to each replay. These cards may be obtained by just playing the game, and you can create a Deck by using these cards. You can alter your deck according to your playstyle before each run begins. You may create overpowered decks by using cards that fit your Cleaner's capabilities. The card mechanism guarantees that each playthrough is distinct, greatly enhancing re-playability. Additionally, certain Corruption cards make things more difficult by imposing restrictions, such as the restriction that taking up any discovered currency will slow down your movement. It’s a perfect blend of abilities and limitations! (When you obtain the necessary cards, please create a custom deck rather than using the default one because the default one prevents you from fully enjoying the game.)As you advance through the game, even on the easier settings, the difficulty will increase significantly. Custom decks are the only thing that can balance the experience. So, to collect cards and build a deck, just choose the Recruit difficulty when you first start the game. Once you have a strong deck, you may try your luck on the harder levels, but I can assure you that it will be quite challenging.The variety of zombies that appeared in the levels was fantastic! As you might have guessed, the game is designed such that you can go through the same campaign several times. As you advance, you'll encounter many zombie varieties that also include Zombie bosses that only die when you've penetrated their body with the majority of your ammo. Each level includes a different sort of zombie waiting for you, ranging from zombies who summon a large army of other zombies, to zombies that charge through the crowd at you.Co-op mode allows up to three friends to experience the whole campaign together. When playing co-op, friendly fire is incredibly frustrating because you are unable to distinguish your friends from the zombies when there is blood all around, including on your friends. In spite of this, I still think playing co-op is a lot of fun.There is just one multiplayer option available, which is PvP, despite the enormous potential for new multiplayer modes. I was not shocked to discover the same mode here because it is already available in L4D2. As Cleaners and Riddens, players take turns trying to live as long as possible. In the end, the team with the most points—which you acquire by surviving—wins. Honestly, it isn't really enjoyable unless you are playing with a large group of friends. Even if you want to play with friends, there are more better co-op games available than Back 4 Blood's PvP mode.The terms I would use to describe the game's graphics are 'simple' and 'beautiful'. The game looks stunning despite having textures that aren't particularly realistic because of the inclusion of little details. The player will have an eye-pleasing and enthralling experience thanks to the fluid animations, an environment filled with blood, and zombie explosions. The body structures of several riddens are the only aspect of the visuals that I would modify. It's difficult to distinguish between them because so many of them share the same appearance.I only saw a very limited number of visual bugs and was able to play the game without experiencing any performance problems or crashes. Therefore, the developers did a fantastic job with the visuals and optimization!How does Back 4 Blood compare to Left 4 Dead 2 then? B4B, in my opinion, offers all the ingredients for a satisfying gaming experience that lasts for at least ten hours. However, the cost does not correspond to the amount of content that is being provided. Therefore, I would only advise purchasing it during a sale. Also, keep in mind that playing the campaign in cooperative mode will greatly enhance your experience.Rating: 7/10Zombies stink!

_childDocuments_.review: As much as it is the spiritual successor, it has also changed up the mechanics enough to not really be the game you go to after you have played Left 4 Dead or Left 4 Dead 2. It is still mostly a zombie shooter with some story and objectives, but it makes the characters give you benefits, and you need to use cards to get stat boosts to improve your chances.  Not really bad, but it's shortsighted and leaves you limited if you don't learn the mechanics that make most of the game work. There is also an amount of dispute over the difficulty gap between rookie (super easy) and the next difficulty veteran (Don't expect to play this within your first week). The first time you play you can select any of the difficulties but it is strongly advised you play rookie first.  The problem is that on rookie, every shot is good.  They give you so much healing that you should never be at risk.  They keep the enemies weak and doing minimal damage. Then after you get really bored with playing rookie, when you try veteran, you find out that the enemies were crippled, and your guns were overpowered in rookie mode.  They fix all that and suddenly if it isn't a weak point shot, it just doesn't really count.  The enemies also hit like a truck thrown by a behemoth riding a train.  And the healing is cut back drastically.  The heal boxes are still roughly found in the same places but instead of four heals, you get one for the whole team. Veteran is doable, but the difficulty gap is very large and throws off a lot of players.  They aren't used to being focused and many players are so bent on speed running and finishing before anything catches up to them that they just run into trouble and ruin the attempt for everyone. The game is worth it, but you don't get much challenge out of it if you play on Rookie, and you get squashed for quite some time on veteran if you aren't talented or focused on the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: There is one campaign, but split into 4 acts, with several levels in between. Loading into que for online takes an outrageous amount of time, and you only get one continue if the entire team wipes. If you can get past this, you are welcome to one of the most toxic communities that encourages people to be hostile towards one another to get the attachments they want for the gun they're using. Bosses are broken, they are either thrown at you before you have enough gear to reliably take them down, or show up toward the end of an act and they're a joke because your character can become too overpowered. The Card system is clever, but broken, which can be great or bad on how balanced you want the game to be. Although the combat is fun, the rules are unclear, there are some sections that say the horde will be chasing you, but what they actually mean to say is that they will infinitely spawn unless you proceed to the next area. The game discourages you from playing offline to unlock cards, and has issues with server connectivity like lag. The AI in general is atrocious, I have seen plenty of reviews making fun of the Bot AI but none about the Boss enemies that will shuffle in place and vibrate trying to pathfind to the person they are focusing. The enemy variety is also wanting. For example there's a ranged enemy, that can stick you in place if you aren't actively dodging him, but his sound que happens when hes attacking, so you only have enough time to get slowed rather than completely immobilized. Not to mention an enemy called a tall boy, whos weak spot is directly behind him if he is walking toward you, meaning even if you strafe out of the way, he will still be facing you so you cannot deal damage unless you take the hit of his attack. There's also an enemy that can alert a zombie  horde if you don't stealthily kill them, but the game has a card that modifies it so they call a horde regardless, so you are not rewarded for skillful play.Lastly, the difficulty is just broken, the starting difficulty is far too easy, but when you get to higher levels like veteran or nightmare the usual rule of thumb is to just run past the big enemies, which seems like a missed opportunity because I bought the game to fight zombies not to ignore them and run through the mission. in the second act, you can potentially have to fight a boss with just the cards you have starting, so, if you do want to fight the boss, it is just a war of attrition as you widdle down his health bar, with weak weapons while you hid inside a parking garage because his AI can't enter. I have a fair amount of time played with the game, and can safely say this game will be dead sooner rather than later if they dont address the glaring issues of the AI and pacing of the missions for future content. But There previous work should be an indication, Evolve was just as janky and unbalanced as this mess, and they never ended up resolving any of that either.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is bad, really bad. The "bosses" are not scary, they just look dumb with their size and pathing/animations. Also why do all the ranged enemies have such a high hit chance. Retches have a highly accurate AOE attack that covers way too large of an area. While Hockers are way too accurate and tanky.Sound design is extremely lacking in the game. Common ridden barely make any noise when they are up behind you. Special ridden lack unique charm that the left 4 dead special infected had in the sound department. Card mechanics. Listen I get it, you want content to last longer, but you really don't need it. Left 4 Dead never had these systems and the game HAS MORE PLAYERS PLAYING CURRENTLY THAN BACK 4 BLOOD. Your card system doesn't make the game better, it doesn't make it unique. It makes it ♥♥♥♥. A pile of unbalanced garbage. When players finally wade through the trash to find a decent build to play on veteran and nightmare modes what do you do? Nerf the cards. You nerf them right into the ground while buffing the enemies and making the spawning issue WORSE. The card system only gives the illusion of skill. Hope you have a good enough deck to dps down the 20 tallboys that spawn.The difficulty in this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and difficult for the sake of being difficult. It is not rewarding when I push through the campaign on nightmare and die to two tallboys, a retch, and a hocker. That spawn all at the same time. _childDocuments_.review: This game is very poorly made and balanced.  It is clearly intended for streamer reaction videos, as the game will reshuffle special infected and spawn them on top of you. _childDocuments_.review: B4B took a little while to get under my skin, but then it did, and it has come to reign supreme for the time being in my apparently inexhaustible addiction to zombie killing.My story with B4B goes like this: the demo didn't hook me--I couldn't see the sense in the game play. The map the demo played is one of the more difficult and one of the few recursive maps--you have to go back and forth to finish the objectives--a little like Hard Rain in L4D2. And of course, you have in the demo no experience of B4B's innovative perking process for the distinct characters, which is actually built around a large deck of cards that players get access to only pieces at a time. As Mr. Horse would say on Ren and Stempy, "No, I didn't like it."Then my son, veteran steamer mistersneak, and I took it on. We started at the beginning, Act 1 Scene 1. For 3 scenes, that is 3 maps, I didn't like it and just floundered forward, not making sense of the play. Then, it hit me--I was able to make sense of the frenzy. I begin to enjoy the heck out of it. The ancestry of L4D 1 & 2 becomes evident although there are so many more kinds of weapons, and attachments that go with them, all progressing in a color scheme like Diablo: white, green, blue, purple and gold. There are offensive, support and quick accessories. Each new map, the team starts next to a level box and can buy their HP and ammo back up, and purchase the standard equipment items, as well as randomly selected weapons with accessories. All these are purchased with coppers that are scattered about each map, and at the end of each map, the players are awarded points which they can spend on... CARDS! The cards cover an enormous range of play styles and philosophies. Some have modest bonuses. Cards you pay more for may have larger bonuses, or big bonuses with trade-offs. Most affect just you but some can affect the whole team. Some cards are called Burn Cards and they are used once but can provide some nice bonus or piece of equipment for that Act or that level (=map). In terms of zombies, there are, of course, the standard fast-running "28 Days Later" "I'm going to eat your face" fare. But there are many more special zombies than in L4D 1-2, and then there are the behemoth creatures which can put a little holy fear into you when they appear. But the big ones also have "weak points" that if you concentrate your fire on these bulbous, unarmored areas, you can drop them much more quickly.The DLC is excellent, adding two more characters and a whole new dimension to game play, a multilevel underground series of "Tunnels of Terror". Most of the levels are soupy and goopy, and the standard zombie fare is enhanced with ones that go boom or turn into goop. The "Tunnels" right now have a standardized approach with levels that descend toward an inner sanctum which holds the "Nursery". The Tunnels add a new currency and so, all told, the DLC contains a lot. So, B4B is a new addictive hit for me in the zombie killing zone. I'm lovin' it and it took me a while to get there. Right now, it and the DLC are premium priced so I am holding off purchasing it for my other son until--I don't know--some Halloween or Christmas special hits. But it looks like the developers are going to continue to add content, and that's just fine with me.I have finally come to the conclusion that B4B is a very worthy successor to the L4D and L4D2 mantles. The only thing missing is the chance to kill zombies with en electric guitar or skillet. I miss those sound effects. They were the best!In the "town" (=lobby), a player can select his character, and go to the different stations. Either at the deck building or supply lines stations, he can purchase the cards that have come up randomly in different stacks--which the game calls factions, with a picture of some unvisitable location occupied by unknowable persons. But the purchasing of the cards allows immense variety in character perks and design, which add to and can dramatically supercede the permanent character perks. The game currently is divided into 3 very large Acts with each Act being made of around 4 episodes, and each episode being made of 3-5 maps--I may be using the wrong terms for these components game-wise but I hope my terminology is clear. The maps vary significantly in length and difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun with Back 4 Blood, but it has issues. The fact I keep having fun is why I give this game a thumbs up. It's obvious the developers wanted to create the new Left 4 Dead in their own way, and I think they did (and yes, I know Turtle Rock made the OG).My issues revolve ammunition and stamina. You never seem to really run out of ammo except in the finale. Stamina for sprint AND melee makes me use melee less because I'm constantly sprinting everywhere. I do like the card system. I find it intriguing to play around with. There are also supply lines you can buy with points you earn that give you cosmetics and a few new cards.One major criticism I have is not being able to continue or start a run without needing a party first. This NEEDS to change.Overall, I do have fun with this game. I find myself enjoying it a lot despite its criticisms and issues I have. If you want a fun, zombie shooter that feels like L4D (although not really a L4D3), then I say get it.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. Left 4 Dead and Left 4 Dead were some of my favorite games back in the day and this game really feels like the next iteration on the genre. This game has a progression system and a lot of weapon variety. It even has character builds that have a very large impact on your runs! This provides a lot of the replayability that L4D lacked.The card system is awesome. I love making new builds and tweaking existing ones. Want to be a sniper? You can make a deck so you completely trivialize special zombies even in the Nightmare difficulty. Want to mow down hordes of zombies with a melee weapon? You can make a deck that cuts through zombies while healing you with each kill. Want to do both? Well, you *could*, but you'd end up with a mediocre sniper and a mediocre melee build. That's one of the best things about this game. Build choice. You can make a deck to suit just about any playstyle (I run a healer/grenadier build that focuses on healing and killing bosses and rely on teammates for everything else).One of the mistakes I often see players make in pubs is jumping in on a harder difficulty with the starter deck or very few cards unlocked. You should be playing on recruit for a bit to unlock cards and get used to the game. B4B is not Left 4 Dead. You're going to have a bad time running around rushing through things. You're not playing as survivors trying to get to safety. In Back 4 Blood, your characters are cleaners. It's your job to blast through an area to either "clean" it of zombies or get to far away places for resources. You need to have a deck that has an actual build to handle the higher difficulties.This game does have its issues though. Sometimes the starting level of the later acts can feel almost impossible if you get a bad combination of modifiers on higher difficulties. This has been greatly improved since the December patch, but it does still sometimes happen.A lot of complaints have been about the number of special zombies and the frequency. This was definitely an issue before the December Patch when you'd get swarmed by multiple tall boys during a horde. It's been mostly fixed since then and it feels close to being balanced. Specials are definitely harder than in L4D, but that's because you can more easily handle them by building your character to deal with them on higher difficulties. It's not just about unloading as much damage as possible, if you can stumble a special even once, they become significantly easier to deal with and that's where your choice in weapon mods and builds comes into play. That said, they really need to take another look at stingers because even though they don't disable you per se, they have very high dps at range and that means they can apply the hardest crowd control: death.All in all, B4B definitely has its flaws, but I feel that those flaws are out weighed by the sheer number of things to enjoy about it.

_childDocuments_.review: The spawn rate of the special infected makes Back 4 Blood unplayable - on all difficulty levels. Hey, I don't mind a challenge, but what Back 4 Blood throws at you is just ridiculous. You start a game, leave the shelter - and you're swarmed by special infected. Once you've killed them all, you walk 50 meters further - and get flooded by special infected again and it takes forever to kill them.It seems like the developers could only create a challenge by throwing special infected at the players. _childDocuments_.review: Hey devs, here's a word of advice: make a new difficulty called normal and make it an actual middle ground between veteran and easy. I would still advise balancing nightmare and veteran because mutation cards and how mutations spawn in this game are currently terrible, but at least this would substantially improve the quality of your game. Because in it's current state you're required to have 4 human players that have a semblance of what they're doing and good decks to just complete the game on veteran. This game has lots of potential to be good, but you need to listen to your community and really put the pedal to the metal with these rebalances so your game doesn't end up dead (cough cough Dead by Daylight). Other things like making the bots brighter than they currently are and balancing the some of the mutated zombies (the ones that immobilize the player in particular need to be investigated, the rate at which they can immobilize and their effectiveness is insane) would also go a long way in balancing this game and making it less difficult. Just remember Turtle Rock Studios, you can still turn this game around and bump the reviews up, the game is still relatively young and fresh so you're still within the ability to do this, but let me reiterate you need to listen to your community.

_childDocuments_.review: After getting to play it for 50+ hours, I can say that it is a fun game to play. Recruit (as of right now Oct 10th 2021) anything higher than that in difficulty is brutal to unfair, unless you have 4 good co-op non bot players. The amount of special infected that spawn is excessive, and will seem to spawn perfectly when 1 person goes down, to suddenly you'll notice your whole team got killed. And it will happen when you least expect it. So do keep that in mind. Randoms can ruin your game play too, due to lack of exp yet,or bots being buggy by staring at the infected and not doing anything.  I've had countless times of that happening. Recruit (easy difficulty) can be REALLY easy once you played through the levels a few times knowing what to do, because special infected don't spawn as much. At this point, only randoms could really screw you over. So with that in mind you'll notice that there needs to be a difficulty between easy and normal. (Recruit and Vet)I haven't touched nightmare, except to join on other's games to see how it is, and every game I've joined has been when the team has died or seconds from doing so. I've tried (And yes I kept count for this review) 30 random game joins. I've seen honestly only 4 different game sessions on nightmare that the team wasn't already dead, but it was very grim for the team. Now, I'm not saying the game's bad in any respect. It's fun if you know that as of right now the challenge rating for the game is unbalanced. This may change in the future of course, which I do hope for.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: As to look back upon B4B it is sad that it was starting to show potential. I came back to it a bit after they finally said "all support is done" for the game. When I first reviewed, it was still getting patches. This, right now, is the FINISHED product. Unless WB comes back to revive B4B, it is done. It still is alright. They seriously did not need to nerf everything as they did. Instead of forcing everyone into the 4 things of: Damage, Support, Tank, Healer. They should have made this into a quasi puzzle game, funnily enough. I think they maybe had that in mind.with how a lot of the cards were made, a lot of them were almost like puzzle pieces rather than builder cards. Solutions to potential problems you might have. And with their addition of the tunnels, i think that they could have had fun with it. Add roadblocks that could be destroyed by specific means that would be easier to do via cards. Thats just me backseat deving for a game. Which we can all only say "I wish they did this" because it is what it is now. Gone. It died as it lived, trying. I got back 4 blood back when it first released, didnt pre-order. I just simply thought "It can't really be as bad as everyone is saying it is.Even now I think that holds. B4B isn't as bad as you think it is. It's just an OK game, back then and right now.B4B suffers from not really knowing what it wants to do, and not doing much of anything extremely well. It wants to be a zombie shooter, it does that alright. It wants to be a deck builder. It wants to be a linear level game. Again, all of these are done ok. Most of my fun was spent speedrunning and seeing how absurdly stupid you can make certain card builds. When you can get like +400% move speed and 300% use speed, its fun to see how far you go before you die. Or how much money you can accrue. But ultimately if you tried using the deck building system to play "as intended", it wasn't really that cool or fun or interesting. The DLC's added some cool levels and weapons and stuff, but ultimately B4B still isn't worth it. Turtle Rock was trying for a bit, tooth and nail, to provide updates and content to make B4B noticed in the scene. But because it's launch and reception was lukewarm, it suffered a similar fate. To be kinda forgotten. As far as we know, this is the final product. All DLC's are out and all updates are out. I cannot recommend this game.
