_childDocuments_.review: I know that nobody will actually read this, but that is fine, I just want to share my thoughts.This game is very flawed, it started with a lot of hype due to it being "from the creators of L4D and L4D2" despite only like, three people working on that worked on the L4D franchise, that is its first downfallNext, let me talk about the card system, it started as a system where you could make a deck of cards to help you in the game, pulling three cards in the order you placed them in your deck meaning that placement had a lot of meaning, and once you pulled all of your cards you were able to pull basic cards that gave you things such as extra health, stamina, ammo, and money. This changed however, as now if you play the game the drawing system of the cards is completely gone and you start with every card in your deck to begin with, which comes with the upside of you don't have to wait to have you actually be able to play a build of your game, but comes with the downside of you can't get the extra basic cards, what you have is what you have. (As a side note, another flaw is that in the tutorial it still has it as "You draw your cards in the order of which you put them" and not the new way, they couldn't bother getting the guy to re-voice a few lines or just cut it out of the tutorial )Now the "randomization" aspect of the game: It sucks. To elaborate, the pool of "corruption" cards you get depend on your difficulty, with the harder the difficulty the more card pool you have, though the problem comes from the fact that the pool really doesn't matter unless you are playing on Nightmare (Hard difficulty) or No Hope (Impossible Difficulty), as the game has scripted events (not talking about the finale cards, which are played on finales, which is fine), from scripted bosses, to cards consistently being played on the same map (not when dying, I mean an entire different "run" as they call it). This really throws the "rougelike" elements they brag about (this is a rougelite, not a like) into the ground, though I can't contest anything above Veteran (Normal) difficulty, as I can barely get past the unfair onslaught that is this game.I want to touch upon the difficulties for a bit, I will talk more in depth about recruit and veteran and a bit about nightmare, I will also voice complaints about no hope but this is only going off both the wiki and word of mouth. To start with the easy difficulty, Recruit, you get increased health, damage, and ammo capacity, it is in fact an easier mode, as even the corruption cards you get are drastically limited. It also disables friendly fire and is a nice starting point for if you are just coming into the game as you won't have any cards to put into your deck, though you do get less supply points than you would playing on harder difficulties. For Veteran, you still get an increase to health, damage, and ammo capacity, but it is a lot less, there are the normal amount of corruption cards and friendly fire is now enabled, you also get 75% more supply points, by now you either are confident or have built a deck that you will use with just one character as each character has their own meta build. For Nightmare you take increased "trauma", which is this game's permanent damage that can only be healed by specific means or specific cards, and you have one less down, meaning that you have one less life when being swarmed by enemies, and you start at having three downs with the third being death. Enemies have more health, damage, and appear in a greater variety, there are more corruption cards and friendly fire is more dangerous, though you get 150% more supply points instead of just 75% extra from Veteran, fewer resources also appear when using a continue. In No Hope you have the ridden dealing a lot of damage, you take a lot of trauma, your corruption pool is at its max, friendly fire is horrid, you recover nothing from the safe room, and you only get 200% extra supply points instead of the 150% from Nightmare, now this sucks to begin with but this difficulty also has zero continues, you don't get your downs back at the start of the level, the bosses roam, and once a player dies, they are dead until the start of the next map (with still one down and they are dead) or maybe not even that (I don't know) as there are no respawn points in the map, I also heard that something they don't tell you is that basically zero extra supplies (health items, quick slot item, throwables) actually spawn in the map itself, which is a problem when you are playing "It is what it is" simulator.For the supply points since they came up, the supply points are used to buy cards for your decks, except they are random when they appear and you have to buy everything before the card in the section it appears before you can actually get the card you want, and then there are burner cards which give a negligible boost to the current map you are in, I don't even think it carries over after using a continue. Supply points are nothing to go into about, they are the average currency you have to buy the rougelite element cards to boost your next run. That is about everything with the base game, I have a complaint with the DLC though. The characters you get can be fun, but aren't anywhere as good as the base game characters, the hives you get are unfair at times as you can easily just be launched off the map by an enemy, and the rewards aren't even worth it metagame wise, as most of the cards you get from the new currency (skulls) are burner cards, that still will never make or break a run. The maps that come with the other dlc I haven't even played yet, I don't know much about them besides characters, the leaderboard thing they have is fun, you make the game harder for points and also supply points.Now I will talk about the good: The gun play is about what you would expect from an FPS game, it is decent. The maps are very nice except for the few times where there is a ledge that you shouldn't have fallen off of that puts you in the "HELP ME I'M FALLING" state (not to mention the insta-death I launch you off the ledge lmao instances in maps) and they also reuse maps. That is it, that is the only good I can find, the gun play is functional and the maps (while still being pretty flawed at times) are nice, that's it.All in all, the reason I keep coming back to this game isn't because of fun, it is because I want to beat this crappy game and get my money's worth, do not buy this game, even if you are a hardcore fan of this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: As it stands, I'd give this game a D. Playing with friends, in voice chat, after unlocking a lot of cards and coordinating your decks, and the AI Director isn't doing his best to make sure you aren't having fun, it can feel like a C.It's almost Left 4 Dead 3 but... falls short.To be clear, I bought the Ultimate Edition. I don't regret it. I'm gonna keep playing it, but I haven't recommended it to anybody, and have talked a couple friends into at least waiting for a sale.The game is either going too easy, or it's too punishing. The AI Director either leaves you alone, or gives you 5 of each special infected at once. Recruit is too easy, Veteran spikes the difficulty way too hard, and Nightmare is simply masochistic.The grind doesn't feel worth it. The cosmetics are uninteresting. Unlocking the cards was... tedious. I'd get it if I felt like I was picking up skills along the way, but strategy seems totally out the window. It's a frenzied mess. Zombies spawn from everywhere. I wish it felt more like clearing areas out, but... they just spawn in from wherever. The deck building is almost good. Some of the cards are poorly worded - vague, confusing. Some cards don't seem to trigger, or have conditions that almost never happen.A LOT of cards have downsides to them, and they often feel disproportionate to the bonus you get.A lot of cards have the same downside, so you cumulatively end up with a huge penalty like -60% stamina or -30% damage resistanceHow come the mutation cards don't have downsides? We have a card that gives us +25% damage but -30% health; the mutations just get +50% damage, +50% health, also heals when it does damage to you, also is armored, also does 100% trauma damage instead of regular damage, and, like fighting a hydra, you kill 1 and 2 more are coming around the corner.I have lots of complaints. I could keep going, honestly. I will say a couple nice things.This game has some of the best-looking fog I have ever seen in a video game, ever.I like the safe room notes, and the stuffed turtles. And looking for the secret golden skulls. I'm still looking for a couple!Some sections are pretty good. Like I said, I'm gonna keep playing it. I'm just not going to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game had potential but the creators were lazy in execution. Turtle Rock may have created the idea of Left 4 Dead but Valve made it the great game it is. That's apparent in Back 4 Blood. The characters are lifeless and the dialogue is dull and uninspired. Infected animations are generic and the environment interaction with inanimate objects is limited. The music in Left 4 Dead helped set a convincing horror ambiance which Back 4 Blood lacks. You're allowed limited replays in a single play through which is ridiculous (like 1 or 2). The damage weapons to infected is considerably different than what they're capable of in real life, even with the idea of balancing the damage in mind it still falls short and Turtle Rock should be embarrassed. There is no support for the modding community. However, the idea of character perks and weapon mods are cool. It's a shame Turtle Rock shilled this garbage as a "Left 4 Dead 3". I wish I got a refund. I'll never buy another turtle rock game.

_childDocuments_.review: From the creators of Left 4 Dead, Turtle Rock Studios has come back to try and claim the throne of the zombie shooter genre. Featuring a familiar formula of gameplay loop starring four playable characters in one match, hordes of Ridden clawing to eat your brains and Mutations that offer mini-bossfights in order to prepare you for the colossal Boss-Ridden.The devs had a decade between games to review, revise and reinvent a beloved zombie game to create a worthy successor to L4D2.And they kinda screwed it up.Back 4 Blood critics tend to get a lot of flak when they compare B4B too much to it's predecessor Left 4 Dead; that they are different games and should be treated as such. I humbly disagree; the devs knew their target audience; they did everything from the naming sense and the marketing to inform their fans that this would be the long awaited spiritual sequel to their favorite Valve zombie shooter. Instead we get a ok-ish looter shooter which endlessly frustrates players with unreasonable, artificial difficulty.- Familiar 4-player cooperative gameplay for L4D veterans- Card System gives player opportunities to choose builds that suits their playstyle and allows for specialization metas.- Mutation Cards changes things up before the stage begins, so every match plays out differently- Wide range of weapons and attachments alongside a rarity system that give players choices and options to balance their team's capabilities as you and your team progress through each Act.- Each Act is long and requires quite a bit of commitment to play through the entire thing in order to get the full experience of a B4B session.- Difficulty spike from Recruit to Veteran is  and misleading. Nightmare mode is -levels of total human suffering and grinding for so little reward.- The AI Director . It is a blatantly cheating, artificial, unfair mess of a difficulty system that enjoys sending disproportionate amounts of Mutations that not even experienced teams of veterans can humanly handle.- Ridden Mutations are uninspired. There are different variants, each having sub-variants that are difficult to identify and therefore counter, especially in the heat of battle.- Bosses, including Mutations are unintelligently designed damage sponges with hard-to-hit weakpoints (looking at you Tallboys/Crushers). Players also cannot use any inherent skill or reflexes to counter them; either needing equipment to break free, teammates or dependent on Card Skills/being Evangelo.- The random difficulty of the game forces a high coop standard from pubs. One random mistake on Veteran/Nightmare will bring endless hordes that will turn any decent game into a complete clusterf**k.- VS absolutely sucks. The matchmaking is horrible due to the lack of votekick or autobalance systems that incentivize staying in a match; too many people just leave when they see any lack of balance.With the current amount of content and the inherent issues since launch, I  recommend this game at the full price, but if you have XBOX Game Pass or found a discounted copy, go ahead and give it a try. The game can produce some fun moments with a close-knit group of friends, but be prepared for some moments that can convince you that B4B just simply hates you for trying to have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: + Really Great card system. Caught myself spending large amounts of time changing things and tweaking my builds.+ Runs amazingly smooth.+ Maps are fun and great. The areas feel great and creepy to explore. Even more so former human controlled areas.+ Character Designs standout and look great.+ Weapon selection has me( who primarily just uses ARs )wanting to use everything. The customization is great. Yeah, I wish you could remove attachments but at the same time I like how the game pushes me to think before I do something.+  Difficulty is pretty good & keeps me on my toes.+ Special infected are tricky and tough. Special infected variants are a bit hard to differentiate at first. But I got around to figuring them out.- Spawns are a bit weird for specials, more so Tallboys & the variants. Needs a tweak here and there.- Characters are a bit flat.- Not crazy about it having to always be online.- Solo play is fun to go into and test builds. But the choice to disable progression is irksome without a doubt. I don't normally solo run a game like this and many others also. But there are people who do and it sucks that they can't progress through achievements or the supply line. I hope this is reversed for the Lone Wolf runners so they can enjoy the game to their delight as well.- We need a kick function. I haven't had any horror stories cause I'm running with friends all the time but I've seen other peoples horror stories.- I rarely play PVP for games like these. But I do know of the small issues or big issues that are over there. Or lack of modes for them too. I do hope the studio hears them also. Tweaking and adding things to make it better.A few random points I've noticed constantly come up. Just wanted to give my two cents:One side of the player base is still learning how to play. They haven't touched the beta. Help them learn. The other side are just the toxic players coming from the toxic side of l4d2.Steam workshop. Come on guys, this game is barely a month old. I understand and I hope it comes. But you need to chill.The map argument I can't entirely get on board with. Despite some of the maps being reused, it VERY obvious that a new area of that map has been unlocked. More so, our community is a stationary community. We aren't trying to escape the city to some refuge. We are the refuge. So it makes sense to tread old ground. And I like that the story shows this. These arguments of the maps being reused just feel extremely nitpicking for the sake of it.Lastly the l4d2 comparisons. B4B and l4d2 are completely two different games. Yes, the promotional material felt like this was going to be I guess very similar to l4d. Yes I thought it too. But the moment I played it, I didn't get any form of blinding rage that it wasn't. I am actually glad its not. l4d2 holds a special place in my heart like it does everyone else and I hope that game continues( it will )to thrive. But I also wish the same for B4B. If I wanted to play l4d2, I can just go play it right now.Do I recommend the game at its standard price point? Yes, to people who are able to afford it and love it way I am or other people are. Xbox Game pass has it and I recommend that anyone who can't afford it, not sure if they fully want it or just plain want to save money.

_childDocuments_.review: Back4Blood isn’t a bad game but, unfortunately, it was missing something to hook me in. I really like co-op games but I couldn’t drag myself into the game enough to finish a single entire run. Maybe it gets better later on but, after 5 hours of playing the game I was just… bored.What B4B has going for it is a lot of things to do, collect and experience. It's not a small game and, if you have a couple friends to play with you, it can be fun.What it has going against it, however, is a lot of convoluted systems, a general lack of introducing players to those systems and little reason not to just blow through a level as fast as possible. Maybe it’s the whole leaning on its Left4Dead roots that hurts it so much but the game feels bloated around the edges with its decks and collectables while missing a solid, fun core game to encourage players to  play the game.The weapon system  be really good but it felt fussy and cumbersome, taking the time to figure out what weapons were good or better than my current took an unnecessary amount of time, checking stats, swapping attachments. Ammo was unnecessarily divided; maybe this is a bigger thing in harder difficulties but it felt dumb to force the team to diversify weapons so there was enough ammo for everyone to use the weapons they wanted. I dunno. If you get the game, you very well may have a blast with it but I can't give it an up vote with how lackluster the content felt. A game I have to struggle to like isn’t worth the money IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite enjoyable and has even more replayability than Left 4 Dead 2 had with the card system. All of my playtime has been solo or with randoms with mixed results (mostly unsuccessful). Unfortunately, you have to go out of your way to say what build you are running, or make a guess what others are running based on character. This makes strategy more complicated instead of just showing the name/cards of your deck to the other players in character select.With the most recent patch (Dec 16th), the game's difficulty has been curbed to fit a more casual playstyle versus the competitive mess it was before. Nightmare still stands to be a very tough challenge, but more forgiving than previously, and without the BS of old nightmare.I found veteran to be too easy for a middle difficulty now though, and would like to see a fourth difficulty to fill the gaps. There's also still a few minor-moderate bugs in the game that can be annoying, but I'm sure will be patched in the next few weeks.One last thing that doesn't get nearly enough attention is that nearly all of the current customization is a reward for your playtime and achievements. The only monetization right now is the annual pass that contains future DLCs, and a few weapon skins that were given to people that pre-ordered the game. Skins are obtained with SP (supply points) that you earn for playing the game and you get more for each person that clears the level to the end. The more prestigious skins are earned by playtime and effort, not bought with money. I haven't found a game in a long time where I saw someone's cool skin and thought "Wow, he must be good at this game." Here's hoping that most of the future content continues to be obtained through playtime instead of money.It has its fair share of shortcomings, but it has so much potential for when new content and patches come out. I look forward to when there are multiple campaigns out and the story gets more meat to its bones.

_childDocuments_.review: So there's people complaining about lack of progression in campaign. These people don't tell you that it's because Campaign has every card unlocked for you to build and test with before playing with friends online. Besides; If you want a solo experience then play online and select to make a private server. Or make like a real human and be social. These games will always be better with friends.There are a few bugs here and there, but nothing overly game breaking or frequent enough to affect my enjoyment of the game, itself. It has solid gunplay, the card system for deck-building is fun and the characters are all interesting in their own way. The Ridden, or zombies, each have variants with subtle differences while others are more unique in model. These become more easily distinguishable by the way they act and tracking their weak points- Experience, overall, in playing the game will allow you to quickly recognize which type of big guy's running at you.The chapters called 'ACTS' are super long, broken up into small segments from safe house to safe house. You can drop out at any safe house and start up with all your progress/upgrades/gear if you want a break mid-campaign instead of restarting completely. There is a very uncommon bug that I've encountered where it will disconnect you and the party, use up a continue. Super bad, but very rare. Only encountered this once, thus far.The guns are all solid with their highs and lows, not much else that I can say about it. Good thumbs up from me. My bud loves melee, so I assume that it's also a solid yes in the books. Bosses are tanky, but that's what explosives are for and the armored mechanics are interesting- Make sure to pack some silver bullets when you get that card.Overall, I can say that we enjoyed this game. If you've got friends and enjoyed Left 4 Dead, you'll enjoy this game. I give it a thumbs-up if only because I have at least 1 friend to play with!

_childDocuments_.review: It's worth giving a play through if you enjoyed Left 4 Dead, but this game becomes frustrating once you've really played it. It's buggy and laggy, often leading to team wipes.I have not played any of this game's vanilla campaigns straight through since Tunnels of Terror came out. Tunnels of Terror has undercut the vanilla game to the extent that it is no longer playable unless you want to solo run by yourself, and if I wanted to play a single player zombie game I'd play Resident Evil.Tunnels of Terror are not fun. I want an option to disable them so I can just play the story mode with like-minded players without getting into a standoff with randoms in quick play about whether to take the tunnel or end the level normally. I don't care about the skull totems and skin unlocks. I would like the option to play the regular game straight through. I liked the vanilla levels. They are fun. The tunnels are not fun. They are repetitive, not interesting to look at, and often demand a level of team cohesion you're not going to find in online quick pay matchups.Create an option for QP matches to have tunnels or not. Or create a separate game mode so players can just play tunnels to farm skulls. I don't care what you do, Turtle Rock. But stop forcing me to play these lame tunnels.Second, this game has been laggy and buggy from the start. Matches implode half the time when a new player joins in. The Breaker *always* causes a huge lag spike and I come out of it with half health most of the time. I was willing to tolerate this during vanilla because I enjoyed the base game. But now that I'm constantly in the frigging tunnels, I have a lot less patience for the lag and bugs.I'm tired of the tunnels and I'd like my matches not to implode from lag and bugs 51% of the time.I paid $100 for this product, Turtle Rock. If you don't fix this game's FUNDAMENTAL issues, I won't buy from your company again. I will keep my eye on B4B's future updates (I did pay for them, after all) but I'm pretty frustrated at this game's messy, harebrained state.

_childDocuments_.review: Back 4 Blood is a pretty weird game. Is it good? Kinda, its decent. Half of it is great, it is one of the more engaging horde shooter experiences. The other half is a janky game with weird design choices that really hamper the enjoyment of this title. +Very good gunplay. The guns are snappy and sound great, headshots pop zombies quick and it feels satisfying to snipe. Shotguns feel powerful as is, and generally all guns are pretty decent at their role. You can modify the guns to behave slightly differently and with the cards system it changes more as well.-Weapon attachments cannot be pulled out of guns, and the game uses a RPG style colored loot tier that does not gel very well imo.+The card system is pretty good. I like building different decks which completely change up your playstyle. You can build a sniper deck which focuses on damage, crits, and get cards that reload your rifle while you switch to your sidearm. You can build a melee deck / shotgun hybrid with good move speed and healing effects. Quite a fair bit of choices, with some meta cards on higher difficulties.-Because cards are all locked behind a progression tier called supply lines, you have to grind out unlocking these cards by advancing the tiers. They are like battle passes, and you cannot selectively choose what you want in each "pass". At the start of the game, your cards are pretty bad, so if you want to play on higher difficulties, you have to grind quite a bit. This is good for some looking for farming experience to prolong shelf life though.+Map atmosphere and sound design, visuals are great. Very atmospheric. Distant gunfire, screams, growls, the world feels very alive and you feel like you are part of the war. The voice acting is decent, and the characters have some interaction with each other.  I do like the whole angle of how you are part of the 'remaining military' carrying out operations and strikes against the zombies vs the usual survivors merely living theme. Levels are pretty well done, with set pieces that are fun to navigate and look at.-The entire game is set in one general region, with a lot of reused areas. The same map can be reused 3 times, once each campaign, except with some changes in pathing and the time of day.  This isn't that big of an issue, but it does feel a little stale after a while of grinding.+-Basic mobs are great to fight, and specials, while pretty engaging to tackle, do have a big issue of spawning in massive amounts. The game likes to do the l4d equivalent of spawning 4 spitters, 4 boomers, 3 chargers, 1 witch and a tank all at the same time, from spawn points literally a few meters from your team. The result is a coin toss where some runs are very easy due to far spawns and sometimes you just wipe because the game thinks its funny to spawn 3 of the smasher types around a small bend and then 2 exploding specials behind you so you have nowhere to retreat to, all the while having another 2 specials that can range grab you. You end up with a wide range from smooth easy runs on higher difficulties when everything falls into place nicely or some badly spawned combinations just wipe your team.For content value Im not sure i can recommend it at this price. It feels like a 45$ game, and this sentiment I had before and now, 28 hours after launch early access, I share the same view. More free content needs to happen, but looking at Evolve my hopes aren't high. The game can feel a little stale unless you're okay with grinding for supply points to unlock cards in the same environment for hours on end. A recommend, but take caution.

_childDocuments_.review: Spiritual successor to L4D, unique characters with different abilities and passives, and pretty good personality. Good amount of special infected, though on every difficulty feels like they spawn TOO many. Very fun card system so that you can get creative and design different builds based off characters and roles. The gunplay is really tight and solid, the weapons just feel right. You need to earn supply which you get by completing levels and the amount you get is based off certain variables, one is difficulty. You spend supply to unlock cards and cosmetics (there are no microtransactions), I feel like they should change how you can earn supply because if you play a level for a half an hour and fail you earn nothing. The matchmaking is terrible if you're hosting, it can take up to 20-30 minutes (with 41k players playing) to find one game on veteran which, in my opinion, is the optimal difficulty if you're not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at FPS games (try recruit first and if it's too easy go veteran). If you're just searching for a game that's being hosted it's usually pretty fast. The melee system is okay, could use a rework or a touch-up, the melee card builds are broken but melee in general doesn't work unless you're going with a melee build. The amount levels you play far exceed L4D I was actually surprised with the large amount of levels this game contained after the beta, so there's plenty to play. PVP in my opinion isn't that great, very small maps and little to move around, no campaign PVP which is the most requested feature to be added.I actually really love this game, I feel like it can only get better with more content added, I think that's when it will really shine, the potential for more levels, special infected/common infected, characters, weapons, cards/corruption cards, there's a lot that can be done. But for now the game as a base is good, just needs a lot of tweaking in patches to make the game more balanced. The performance is great, the game runs like butter, no problems there.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I'd start off by debunking that Crowbcat's popular video.-While death animations are lacking in favor of standard ragdolls, it does look great when there's large hordes of zeds, not pictured in their easy mode photos. The zeds are disgustingly rendered, and tend to move very fast, especially with the "Fast ridden" cards. The damage looks fine enough, especially because shooting guns and bashing brains feels so incredible and tactile, a detail l4d2 never got quite right.-Bots are dumb. They're stupid and broken, and tend to stand directly in front of turrets. While they're being worked on, a lot of the bugs presented are actually work-arounds. Bots don't trigger snowflake zombies like the Snitches or Hags or Alarmed doors so their pathing doesn't screw over real players. So, that at least explains a lot of the clips.-Versus. It's.... uhh, bad, honestly. That video got that right. If I had to guess, there's no full campaign versus due to their card progression and somewhat linear structure, so holdouts are the best way. They've dropped a ton of role-defining cards in survival, making it a more samey experience as opposed to the campaign.-Themes. The game's theming is perfect: good bits of comedy, camp, gore, horror, and tension (and if you're a Karlee stan, plenty of "relatable" millennial "humour"). They got on this game's case for the campy comedy. But then at the end, they showed some clips of wacky, zany, mood-destroying mods and the chocolate heli scene. So, in a sense, they've offered a contradictory statement, which invalidates their argument. They did everything they could to show b4b's worst moments to make it look like a Cyberpunk launch.-Mods: On a similar note, I think we lost mod support in favor of crossplay. So, get mad at Sony or whatnot. Crossplay is tight.If they wanted to attack b4b, they could have argued on some current issues with the game, like:-Dumb bots, though that's alleviated by not actually needing them to enter saferooms before closing the doors-The game seems to encourage individualism with "breakout" card, speedrun solo-ers leaving hordes to the other three, no benefits for healing others unless you're a dedicated doc (i.e. systems that encourage charitable acts aside from snares and pins), and the excruciatingly long stumble time when a survivor is grabbed or knocked close to you-Character-intrinsic abilities, essentially making a very clear tier list of "required" picks-Punches and stumbling is a hidden value and many times has no effect on specials and commons-Commons can scratch you at a longer range than your punch when retreating-You can't tell what roles/guns your friends are taking unless you are chatting with them, which makes the initial deck pick rough with tons of costly overlap (using ammo your friends desperately need)-Aim Down Sights is a great addition but most the best DPS cards disable it, so like, what's the point-Joining in-progress missions, or continuing runs, is a buggy confusing mess that often resets your deck, changes your deck/characters/loadout entirely, or leaves you with less cards than playing through normally.-Retches are still OP, and Crushers often have too much HP guaranteeing a down or tons of trauma damage-No clear tutorials for medicine cabinets, the most important and ONLY way (aside from a Doc or fully upgraded f-aids) to heal trauma. Newbies often use the entire kit for themselves, or just bypass the kit altogether.-Muting players also mutes pings-Also a clear tier list for weaponry - for example the tec-9 is the best pistol sidearm, Vector best smg, M1A best general sniper, the Tac best shotgun (modded up, due to its high damage, stumble chance, and doesn't eat through ammo like everything else). There's tons of other weapons, and some definitely perform great (the Barret is a tank-killer sniper), but they tend to be less popular or less useful in all situations throughout the match.Aside from that, B4B is a ton of fun. The strategy of the cards makes the game less infuriating to lose - when we lost matches, we'd dive straight back to our deck, considering top-decking different cards, changing things in and out, and more. The strategy allowed us to get a huge leg up, on top of prepping items and shooting better. If you're looking for a game to surpass L4d2, just play l4d2. This game is vastly different game of the similar 4-player co-op formula. It's fun, the missions are varied, and the similar zones/streets you walk through are vastly different. In Nightmare mode was the first time I actually had to play cards against the randomization, as opposed to just picking my top-decked items according to the pre-scripted level events, so there's tons of opportunity for repeat play thanks to that and your builds. As a die-hard l4d2 and Payday fan, no game can ever surpass them. Instead, this game is just a unique twist on that genre that has the benefit of a decade of FPS design since their launches.

name: Trials of Mana
detailed_description: Trials of Mana Free Demo Available Now! Play the Trials of Mana Demo today and transfer your save data to the full version of the game. Reviews & Accolades 'absolutely charming' - IGN 'pure gaming comfort food' - GameXplain 'a lovingly crafted remake.' - Hollywood Reporter Note: Reviewers quoted on this page may have been reviewing different platform versions of Trials of Mana. About the Game This daring tale of overcoming the tests of fate has been given new life! Experience the beloved adventure fully modernized with graphic improvements, character voiceover support, a remastered soundtrack and a new episode which you can experience after the ending, in addition to an ability system and a new class that reconstructs the character levelling system plus more active battles! This overlapping story of interwoven destinies changes depending on who you choose as your main character and companions! Will these young adventurers be able to use the power of mana to save the world from the brink of destruction? When the world was shrouded in darkness, the Goddess of Mana drew forth the Sword of Mana to smite the eight Benevodons, monsters of destruction. She sealed the horrors inside the eight Mana Stones, bringing the realm back from the brink. Weakened from rebuilding the world, the Goddess changed herself into a tree and fell into a deep sleep for many years. However, the forces of evil soon sought to free the Benevodons to gain control of the world. They started a terrible war to further their plot and destabilize the kingdoms. Peace was at an end. Mana itself began to disappear from the world and the Mana Tree started to wither... KEY FEATURES Revamped 3D Graphics Trials of Mana is a full 3D remake of the third game in the Mana series, originally released in Japan as Seiken Densetsu 3. The entire game has been fully rebuilt from the ground up with modern 3D graphics. Pick your Party Players can choose their favorite protagonist and two companions from six different characters. The story will play out in different ways depending on the combination of the protagonist and companions in the party. Battles and Character Growth Will you go for light or darkness? Create different character types with the class change system! Character growth has been re-worked, adding in a new “abilities” mechanic and a fourth class for each character, to expand the breadth of customization. Build the party you want to enjoy a thrilling battle system with expanded action gameplay. Music New arrangements for a total of 60 music tracks, overseen by composer Kikuta Hiroki. It is also possible to switch between the original and arranged soundtracks freely.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun game. Great for an escape, with enough combat to keep you engaged, but not frustrated (unless you want to be). The range of difficulty options really caters to different moods, the graphics are great and fluid, the combat is smooth. And with tremendous replay value... being able to select characters at the start means different storylines happen, different interactions with characters happen... really, I can't praise it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Trials of Mana is a lot of fun! If you ever played Secret of Mana or Seiken Densetsu 3, you will feel right at home with this game. They actually did a remake correctly. Amazing for 2020!One thing you will want to do first is change the voices to either OFF or Japanese. The English ones sound annoying but the Japanese ones sound okay because you don't really know what they're saying. That's really the only thing you need to do. The game itself is fun and easy to get the hang of as far as controls and getting around.They recently added some new difficulty levels, which is good for replay value and some added challenge since the normal and hard difficulties aren't really too hard (I think there is also an Easy mode too just so Kotaku was able to review the game). You'll also want to play around with different character combinations and classes as you play through again (If you're trying to unlock all the achievements, it's at least 3 playthroughs).
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: A mediocre game overall. The skill system is nice but doesn't matter much for most of the game. The best part of the game was the last section before the final boss. Some fights actually required some effort and skill choices mattered to some degree.  Comparing it to the original, this is definitely an improvement. I tried to finish the original many times and never could because I lost interest. I wouldn’t recommend the game to anyone except for those who want to have some mana series nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: No future mode makes the game a lot more fun. I spent 300+ hours on the game just because of this mode. It's not too hard once you are familiar with it, and it forces you to utilize many abilities and strategies to beat bosses. My favorite duo is Kevin Fatal Fist and Duran Edelfrei. They can trash all the bosses easily. The third one in the party could be anyone, doesn't matter much.

_childDocuments_.review: - Concept: 4/5The idea of being able to pick your party and seeing their stories interacting is cool.- Story: 2/5Each one of the characters specific story bits is super cliche and boring.- OST: 3/5The quality of the music is pretty high, there are some bangers, but there are so many moments where the song playing doesn't fit the scene at all. And the same songs play in multiple areas, making it pretty repetitive at times.- Gameplay: 2/5Combat is basic button mashing with some rolls. Extremely easy even on the Hard difficulty, and switching characters is so laggy that you'll definitely get hit for doing it.- Voice Acting: 1/5My god there's some awful voice acting in this one.- Total: 2.5/5I had fun at some points, but wasn't interested by either the story or the combat most of the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute treasure of a loving tribute for a forgotten 1995 classic.I played the original (via fan translated Romhack, sue me, it was literally impossible to play otherwise outside of Japan) and I can say this new version improves upon the original in every conceivable way possible.Short version: 8/10, a must have for anybody who can overlook some of the dated elements.Long version:I'll start with the major cons.-Voice Acting is a mixed bag. There's some real bad performances in both English and Japanese, so you won't easily get around jarring voice work.-Script is a little too faithful to the original. A lot of lines worked well enough in writing but not spoken. I suspect the fan translation was actually better in places. They could have tried to write less awkward lines to read for the voice actors.-Plot is very basic RPG fare. There's a few minor twists and turns, some cute character moments but overall, the main plot when its not focused on smaller more intimate parts of the narrative is very weak. Thankfully there's at least barely any mention of a prophecy. There is one, and it still adds nothing to the story, but it's brought up 2 or 3 times at most.-Animation, especially in cutscenes character animation is extremely awkward at times, though there are a few gems for at least special attacks. (Dark Tier 4 Angela's final special attack is cute and funny for example.)-Difficulty is a bit on the low side I'd say, even on Hard, I never struggled until post-game content and I have yet to finish that but some first impressions are better there. (Again shout out to Angela for having a particularly hard post-game boss fight associated with her.) ((For reference, I do not consider myself a particularly skilled player of action games. I did after much pain and hardship beat Dark Souls 3, but only by summoning help on some of the trickier bosses and on WoW I generally capped out at Heroic or early Mythic bosses of current content. I consider myself a medium quality player when it comes to action games.))The major pros-Gorgeous and faithful translation of the classic 16bit graphics into a breathtaking 3d world. This is why I always say aesthetic is more important than graphics because despite some lower-res textures in places you're used to from modern releases, the art design is top-notch, charming and unforgettable.-The music is some of the best RPG music ever, but that's not unusual for the often overlooked mana series.-Quality of life improvements over the original are numerous, from the way inventory management works, character select at the start of the game, the ability to watch flashbacks of your other party members so you don't have to restart 6 times to see everybody's introduction segments and more.-Combat is an absolute blast. The original had normal attacks, special attacks (now called class strikes) and magic. That was it. The new version has light and heavy attacks, jumping, dodging, area of effect attacks, swing arcs, combos, passive abilities, greatly expanded boss mechanics... actually...-Boss fights are really cool, and as soon as you hit the first time you're likely to change classes there is a notable spike in boss complexity which is very welcome. You cannot just wail on enemies while ignoring their special abilities.-The game now has a post-game content with 12 new character classes, (2 for each of the protagonists) and a new mega-dungeon.-The optional super boss is a joy to fight. As added bonus this boss is now in all 3 plot branches. It used to be only accessible in the Duran/Angela protagonist storyline. -The new more complex character class system and training system have reset/respec options so do not worry too much about your choices being final. Though you can only reset classes a limited amount of times and not until end-game and post-game.-The new class system with numerous passives give you a lot of customisation with how to kit out your characters in combination with each other as well as from fight to fight. Special mention are the new Chain Abilities that are characters can unlock through their classes that are thrown into a communal pool, making different party combinations more interesting than they first seem.-Chain abilities are also unlocked by plot progression and by talking to various NPCs. Be sure to talk to many minor characters, virtually anybody with a distinct part to play in any of the protagonist's stories will yield a passive, giving you an actual reward for exploring the world's NPCs.-New Game +... I've not finished my first playthrough yet after 30 hours (bear in mind I'm exhaustively exploring and sometimes do a little grinding for specific items) so I cannot comment much yet but it does exist, which is always welcome, especially in an RPG that requires 3 playthroughs for the 100% experience.May update in future.

_childDocuments_.review: Trials of Mana is a great re-imagining of a game we in the West have barely had access to prior to 2019's Collection of Mana. Remaking the world in full 3D and completely reworking the combat system, as well as adding new classes for each character in a post-game chapter, this is a lot of quality content on offer, even if it has its flaws.If you enjoy action RPG's that aren't intensely challenging and don't mind fairly archaic storytelling, the gameplay of Trials of Mana, as well as some character moments, are enough to offer plenty for a fan of the genre. Though this doesn't have the level of polish that Square Enix poured into FF7 Remake, there is a lot of love and hard work put into this and it has plenty of content to offer. I'm only partially through my second playthrough at the time of this review and it's fun to have a new party makeup from the start, with cutscene skipping making repeated scenes non-intrusive while allowing me to still view the new characters' scenes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be summed up very easily as "Poor Writing" and "Baby's First RPG". Aside from the litany of contrivances the writer(s) just jammed into a boring story to make it work, leaving some monumental plot holes, the glaringly obvious fact that Angela's character is, in it's entirety "Bimbo", the bad guy's motivations are "Generic evil plot #1" and don't even get me started on Charlotte. The game is just an incarnation of the term "Meh."  The combat is bland and uninteresting, I just run from most fights tbh, quicker and less of a waste of time. Boss battles are mildly more interesting with some mechanics behind them to actually pay attention to.All in, should you play this game?Well it depends:A. Have you had a lobotomy recently and just need lights and colours to draw your attention to something for a while?B. Are under 13 years old and want an intro into RPGs?C. Have you played every good game in your library an just want something mediocre to increase the longing for a good game?If any of them are no then no. Then no, no you should not. I'm going to complete it begrudgingly because I paid what can only be described as a "rip off" amount because while this is technically a game, I don't think it's a good one.Lastly, art is subjective, just because I don't like it doesn't mean you won't. Don't take me as gospel, always remember Steam has a 2 hour return period not that you'll get a good feel for the game in 2 hours, but you'll definitely see some of the "Writing".Also Square seem to be trending to making worse games faster and for higher prices and... Well fúck Square Enix. They ruined FF7 with that demake and now they're pumping shít out because they think you're an idiot who'll buy anything. Which in most cases is true, look at me and this hot pile of garbage.Aside from the vitriol I feel toward Square, even if this wasn't a Square game, it's still bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Trials of Mana is surprisingly a very refreshing and simple game. It's not really hard at all save for a couple instances (even on hard mode), and it isn't super long either, but honestly that didn't bother me. It was fun to just explore a very charming world with characters I really grew to like by the end. The story isn't too complicated mostly due to it being a remake of a game from the 90s, but again, I see it as an upside as it just makes the game all the more comfortable and easy to enjoy the ride.Trials of Mana is a game with a lot of heart put into it. Everything from the visuals to the gameplay, from the stories to the characters, has this simple but likeable sense of genuineness to it that creates a pleasant, almost nostalgic, ride from start to finish. It's an easy recommend to anyone if you ask me.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically, the combat was upgraded (I never played the original so I dunno for sure), but the plot and character builds are still really outdated.What I hate most about the game is that the class descriptions are not only vague and unclear, but they also outright lie sometimes. And this is compounded with the fact that you can't reset your class without either starting the game over, or using a consumable item that only exists once in the final dungeon and 4 times in the post-game dungeon. I imagine most builds will inevitably devolve into stupid, overpowered strategies like having unlimited mana to cast spells that oneshot entire encounters, tear up bosses, and rapidly fill the class strike (read: limit break) meter. It's really hard to experiment with different team compositions, and there isn't much reason to experiment with them because of how easy it is to beat the game. My first run of the game was Warlock Charlotte, Fenrir Knight Riesz, and Fatal Fist Kevin.Aside from that, your AI teammates are completely useless when you need them the most (DPS checks; killing adds), and the plot is also boring, so replaying it is a drag. The notoriously bad voice direction makes the plot itself worse. My original plan was to run it three times, once for each possible main villain, but I might burn out on this game before I finish my 2nd run.

_childDocuments_.review: Rate this game solid 3.5 of 5. Overall a great JRPG and would recommend the game.Rating given based on the following metrics.1. Story - The story has a great overall arching them saving the world from this ominous threat however there are parts within that do not tie together towards the end, I guess that what you get when you have to make the story from multiple perspectives and still have varying outcomes.2. Combat - Combat becomes a bit repetitive towards late game as the move pool is very small and the pause action spells leaves little excitement when you have to cycle the wheel to find the right move.3. Characters - Characters do not really develop much over the game and the dialogue at points contradicts the characters personality.4. Length - Without the post game material and little exploration the game can be completed in about 24 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything in this game is...well...nice. There is absolutely nothing oustandingly special about it and it just doesn't need much explanation. The grafics are nice. The artstyle is nice. The voice acting is nice. The music is...very nice. And so on.There are only a few minor aspects of the game that i find...well...not so nice. First, there is the strict linearity. Trials of Mana doesn't have any sidequests and the different areas are visually varied, but very straight forward and rather small. Since their structure is so similar to each other (Town, area with enemies, another town, another area with enemies, dungeon, rinse and repeat) the game gets somewhat repetitive after a few hours. At least the different options who shall be in your party and who's supposed to be the main character provide some small story variations and replay value. Secret of Mana is rather linear, too but the general design of it's world and story progression make it feel a lot more non-linear and open-ended than Trials of Mana.Compared to the original Secret of Mana (and it's remake), the combat- and gameplay mechanics in Trials of Mana are almost radically different and don't have that rather tactical "strike at the right moment-wait to charge-strike again"-combat flow. In fact, on the lower difficulty settings, Trials of Mana's combat is nothing more than simple monotonous button mashing.The stories of Secret and Trials are completely unrelated, too. Only some returning enemy types and plot elements (Mana Tree and -sword, cannon travel, eight elementals, etc) provide some consistency.Regardless of those few points of criticism, Trials of Mana is good enough to stand on it's own. I haven't played the original Seiken Densetsu 3 (since it was never released on the SNES in Europe), so I have absolutely zero nostalgia and no idea how faithful the remake is to the original, but if you like rather casual and lighthearted RPGs that are not too epic and not too hard, Trials of Mana is...uhm...nice._________________________________________________________________________________TRIALS OF MANA (Remake)Genre: RPGRelease: Q2 2020( ) 0/8 Simply one of the worst games ever made. It plays pretty different since its a full remake, unlike what the SOMR did, but it has all the core features that the SNES version had and improved on pretty much everything.Some of the English voices are strange, but they don't bother me to much.  New post game is pretty meh, but its something.  Balancing in a normal run on Hard for the first time is fine, but with all the knowledge you have, it becomes pretty easy unless you speed run.  AI is pretty dumb, so they can make things more annoying than it should be.

_childDocuments_.review: The most enjoyable experience iv'e had with a jrpgish game in a long time.It's simple, short on dialogue, and heavy on wacking things. Mana games have always been pretty straight forward with lots of goofy sights/sounds to keep the gameplay entertaining. This is a faithful, just about 1 to 1, with some annoyances removed, recreation of the very hard to remember japanese title 3 we all emulated and played through a fan's translation back in college. Given that there are somethings that don't translate well into 3d, and a lot that does, it's a bit experimental in that regard. So far it's been a mostly easy ride, i won't take points of for a game actually being not a pain to complete, with steady progress and a lack of a grind. All in all i would put it at overpriced at 50 bucks, but i have been thirsty for something like this, and it really hit the mark. A sit down cutesy brawler, no side questing, no super complicated systems or dark souls difficulty, just, pure enjoyment, so pick it up, i say.p.s. the guy complaining about denuvo can go eff himself.

_childDocuments_.review: This game brings back a lot of nostalgia for me. I always liked the creatures, characters, elementals and lore of the mana games series. It's a classic JRPG, the story is a bit railroaded in one direction for some people these days, but the combat is fun, it's neat to be able to build a party of 3 out of a a possible 6 heroes, that's 9 unique combinations with dozens of different iterations of the various dialogues depending on who's the main hero, who's the first comrade and who's the second. Not to mention there are 3 different final dungeons and villains depending on who's the main character. All in all, it's fun, but it might not be for everyone. I get it if you like a more open world adventure game, but sometimes a railroaded story can still be a good story and game.

_childDocuments_.review: Had a blast with this game.  Outside of missing the old multi-player mode, the remake beats the original clean.  The game keeps its simple and fun action RPG adventure gameplay and returns with gorgeous art that captures the spirit of the original.  I know the biggest issue with the game was difficulty when I demoed it before it originally came out, but for PC players there was a difficulty rebalance mod that made things so much better.  Square Enix definitely saw the complaints about difficulty so we got new modes to address that but I don't know how good they are as I've stuck with my difficulty mod from Nexus).There have been updates to free post game/new game+ content, difficulties and such since I've last played and it is all good stuff with nice replay value since you have 6 characters, 3 main stories, 3 person teams for every playthrough, and a truck ton of classes with brand new ones added in this remake.  The combat is nothing crazy like Ys or Tales of games, but it is simple yet fun with even a couple of spikes and challenges with the new modes.  Lastly, the modding community has some good stuff out there for gameplay stuff and aesthetics so check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game though I would definitely recommend playing it on the Harder difficulty. My only real complaint about Trials of Mana is the blatant amount of hand holding that takes place during the first half of the game, it treats you like those parents who put a leash on their kids when they go to Walmart. Dont worry though cause eventually the game breaks open beautifully, giving you full freedom and thats when it really shines.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a faithful remake that don't change the things too much to the point it is unrecognized like many remakes out there. The battle is fun and fluid. The new post-game contents are great additional for this game because unlike in the original version, there is nothing for you to do once you beat the final boss.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played the original version of Seiken Densetsu 3 now rebranded as Trials of Mana, not because I disliked it or never had an interest but because I never got around to it. As someone who grew up with Secret of Mana on SNES it was one of my favorite games growing up. I had always heard about SD3's legacy and how excellent it was. Through this remake, I too became a believer!I finished my first playthrough today and the party I cleared the game with consisted of Duran, Angela and Charlotte. It was an excellent experience, full of fun and responsive gameplay and one of the best soundtracks I've heard in a game! I'm wrapping up the post game content now and plan to start my next playthrough immediately after. I'm going to play through as Hawkeye, Riesz and Kevin next.If you're a fan of games that do not have an overly complicated story, great music, great classic character art then it's a home run! _childDocuments_.review: • great soundtrack • looks just like on the images in the manual of the original game • everything looks so darn cute – and sexy for some reason (even the wasps) • superior fighting and skill system (similar to the Tales of Series) • all the additions, changes and updates to the remake are great • good entry-level action RPG  • low-res textures (on almost everything but the main characters) • polygon meshes in the environment are updating too late and keep popping up while walking around • stupid AI companions • way too easy and very basic (the hardest thing in the game is keeping your suicidal allies alive) • you receive too many items and money • some unskippable cutscenes• Charlotte is vewwy vewwy annoying• some odd voice acting decisions (is it campy and fun or bad?) This is a way better remake than Secret of Mana and I'm glad they put more effort in this one. I hope other games would get this treatment as well (even remaking the remakes of Sword of Mana (Final Fantasy Adventure / Mystic Quest) and Secret of Mana). I would love to see an updated version of Legend of Mana. Unfortunately Dawn of Mana is irredeemable. Or make a new game in the series!  7,5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Someone else has probably already written a more in depth review, and one better suited to new players who have no idea what the Seiken Densetsu series is, or what random cluster of names Square has released them as over the years. My review is to the fans of the SNES version of SD3.They nailed it.It's new yet classic, familiar yet refreshing. It's the game as it would have been made today... or maybe five years ago. It's not exactly cutting edge, but considering the strides it's making to be faithful to a 25 year old game, it's more than good enough.The biggest changes are that the game is entirely real-time now. The ATB queue is completely gone, and you can reflex your way out of most all attacks if you know they're coming. However, so can the enemy. You can also be knocked out of spell casting (but so can the enemy). The old attack delays have been replaced with a basic combo system and the ability to jump, with various enemies requiring you to vary your moves a bit to fight them effectively. It works quite well, and while the early bosses are almost trivial with all of your new moves (Full Metal Hagger won't know what hit it), the game only gives you until the second stone before it starts giving the bosses all new patterns designed to test your understanding of the new mechanics.The other major change is character development. The somewhat vague stat increases have been replaced with points that you can spend as you like, or just hoard. Magic and abilities are also no longer automatically granted when the spirits are collected, you have to have specific minimum scores in your governing attributes to unlock them. This means that you can play each of the characters fairly differently. You can for instance forgo buff/debuff completely on Riesz and just make her a physical bruiser by ignoring her Spirit stat in favor of Might. Hawkeye's ninjitsu is curiously enough governed by Luck.The English text is actually quite close in tone to the translation Corlett's team produced all those years ago. The deviations are mostly irrelevant, Dragon Emperor -> Dragon Lord; Demon Prince -> His Dark Majesty. Apparently Bil spells his name with one el, and it's Navarl, not Navarre. (Which is utterly indistinguishable in Japanese anyway) The only one that gets me is God-Beast -> Benevodon. It just strikes too close to benevolent as a root, which those things absolutely are not. Also the Death Jester is the Goremand now, but I kinda like that.Voice acting is okay. You can use the Japanese voices, but the combat/exploration banter has no subtitles, so you're missing a lot of little touches if you don't comprehend the language. (Nice stuff, like if your party contains Riesz and Hawkeye, during the Laurent section she will bemoan the state of her kingdom as you pass through the halls of the citadel, and Hawkeye will repeatedly apologize for his people having anything to do with it.) (And as an aside to an aside, why is it a kingdom? There's like two men in the entire country, Riesz's mother must have married her father out of love, but why did he end up king when she died over Riesz inheriting? And why don't they consider it a queendom or something else?)Music is fantastic. It's a mix of symphonic stuff, and just higher quality synth arrangements which works well. The drumlines are almost all synthisized and retain that crunchy sound that stood out on the SNES. You also have the option of the SNES soundtrack itself.The only negatives I have are that some stuff just isn't as impressive in 3D. The Full Metal Hagger doesn't fill a screen like it did on the SNES due to the lack of a fixed perspective, and the path to the heavens, when rendered for real, looks, well, kinda realistic, and not super stylized like the backgrounds for the SNES version. You never get that final scene where it looks like you're ten miles up. Small price to pay for actual class change character models and visible weapons and everything just being brought to life.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better remakes that ever came to be since it's very very faithful to the original (aside from the obvious). Combat is simple and fun and melee characters have more depth than the original (not so much, but still enough).Pros of the remake : - Faithful to the original (at least 90%, 10% was changed/added)- Added more depth to the skill tree, it's not just raw stats, there are abilities now.- Added some new content with the 4th class tier and post-game content- Remade soundtrack is amazing (if you don't like it, there's also the option to switch to original)- The game runs very smooth on highest FPS (120), feels great.- Very good controls, making the exploration and combat feel very good.Cons of the remake (a few nitpicking as well) : - The game holds your hand the entire time, there's a mod to turn it off but what's the point since you probably won't be using a mod on your first playthrough and after that you already know the game.- Voice acting (English) is sometimes cringy and overall bad, but the game was made mostly for the Japanese audience (lip syncing on models is for Japanese audio). So switch to Japanese with English subtitles for a better experience.- I understand that it's a console port, but having limit to 4 quickcast moves is kind of annoying (thankfully you can switch them in combat as well)- Hard mode is easy, I love the game but it's very easy, there are mods in the work to increase difficulty so there's hope. The AI is slow, they more often than not have a waiting period after an attack which makes them boring and less fun to interact with. Bosses are very easy, they go down way too fast and their mechanics are not really transferred that great from the original (with a few exceptions of course). - Party AI is a little neither here nor there, you have to understand exactly what you're doing with them. I suggest that you set the target as "Same target" when fighting bosses or spawned monsters will distract them from the boss and will just die to random stuff (looking at you Zehnoa)- Loading screens... If you never experienced the game before, I highly suggest playing the original as well.Overall, very nice remake.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Stunning visuals for a remake.- Love the combat system and easy to navigate UI.- Feels good to play as these characters after all these years without the story being released episodically or something of that nature. Essentially, staying true to being a single game.- Actually has a post game that you don't have to pay for.- Remastered soundtrack sounds beautiful. Cons:- Exceptionally easy, even on the hardest difficulty. I would hope that they consider patching in some changes to hard to make the game mechanics a little harder to react to or something that adds that extra spice. - Do yourself a favor and play the game with Japanese voice and English subtitles. English voice acting is... special. Overall:This game is a true nostalgia remake that keeps to it's values and adds the necessary changes needed to make it even better. Don't be surprised if you blow through the main game quickly because things are a bit too easy.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game and one i bought off of pure nostalgia.  Despite my reason for buying it i was greeted by a wonderfully constructed game that modernizes a SNES game very well and is honestly a lot more fun then expected.  GameplayThe game play at least on hard if punishing if you fail mechanics but not so punishing you can't recover from a mistake or two, however repeated mistakes can run you out of healing especially if you do not have a team with a healer.  The base gameplay is simple yet fun, melee boils down to using light attacks to combo into heavy attacks which do different things based on where in the combo you put them.  1 light 1 heavy is a knockback attack to enemies which is good to interrupt them, while 2 light 1 heavy is a stronger attack with more area covered.  You will get longer combos during class change but they will be similarly simple.  Your only ranged attacks are spells and items.  This admittedly basic system stays fun by making you dodge attacks and giving you spells on all characters once you've started to master the basics.  While during the demo the game is almost painfully simple and easy even on hard this is done so even if you choose the team with 2 casters and no melee as your first two you will not have a bad time before you get spells.  How you acquire spells is simple you progress the story to get elementals who grant spells and put your training points into the areas that unlock those spells.  Only 2 characters can cast spells in their base class those are the mage Angela and the priest Charlotte.  StoryThe story is very faithful to the SNES game it comes from.  This means the story is also very basic.  This will not be an amazing story that you've never seen before.  It will be a story that you've seen every part of done multiple times before just maybe not put together in exactly this format.  The characters are likable, however the voice acting is inconsistent in quality.  Some is done very well, but at other times you will be getting Big Gay Al flashbacks from South Park when the spirit of light is talking.  Thankfully most major characters are done decently, though some times with the voice not sounding as say angry as the body language would make you think it should.  Also some people hate Charlotte the healer due to her having a lisp that is for some reason put even into her text (why).  She basically talks like Elmer Fud and replaces R with W in her speech.  This makes text hard to parse some times but her voice actress does a wonderful job on making it easily understandable.  Replayability / DepthThere are 3 different endings to this game.  Which ending you get is determined based on who you choose as your first character.  the paths are split by Duran and Angela, Kevin and Charlotte, and Hawkeye, and Rieze.  A lot of both replayablity and depth comes from the same place and that is team composition.  This is good as a team of say Kevin, Duran, and Rieze can and will give a very different experience then a team of Angela, Charlotte, and Hawkeye.  The bad part is the game gives very little indication of how people mesh together.  All the game tells you at the start are here is a mage, a priest, and 4 flavors of hits stuff.  At no point do you get any indication that Rieze for example specializes in buffing in the light class path and debuffing in the dark class path.  The game also doesn't tell you there are in fact 3 people with healing spells in the game light side Kevin, light side Duran, and any Charlotte.  The good news is this version did put in items to reclass your characters, however they are limited in quantity so you can't reclass at will.  You will never get stuck in this game due to choosing the "wrong class" every class is good and most spells also have an item form letting you use items instead of a certain class comp. All in all this is a fun game great for everyone even if you've never played a mana game in your life.  Its has depth where team comp will help, but gives you easy ways to make it so you won't be overwhelmed if you choose a team that meshes poorly.

So then they added a beginners mode and trust me, no beginner would manage this either. So if you fail in beginners mode, you get a continue. _childDocuments_.review: Trials of Mana is a rare example of a remake where the script and art direction remain true to the original, but the technology has been updated for modern audiences.  Whereas many other remakes (/"re-imaginings") have a pension for rewriting dialogue and redesigning characters -- often swapping out old-school cliches for modern-day cliches, and changing the personality and tone of the game to suit whatever modern ideology or trope is being pushed by the company -- Trials of Mana remains largely faithful to its SNES counterpart.  As far as I can tell, the script, plot, art and characterization are largely and lovingly carried over from Seiken Densetsu 3, but given a modern tech facelift.  What little has been added in the post-game is inoffensive (perhaps a bit sillier in tone?) but arguably fits.  PROS: -The rare faithful remake!  Tech/graphics are updated, writing/art/music is preserved.-The world and characters are bright and colorful.  The art direction is as great as ever.-The characters have a nice anime-style look that seems like a fitting progression from the SNES sprites.-Special moves are flashy and fun, and there is a large number spread out amongst the many classes.-A skill system was added for a little extra customization.-Mana music is amazing, and you are given the choice of hearing the updated tracks or the original ones.-Voicework is overall good, though I've addressed it further below in "Pros/Cons".-Modding is possible.CONS: -Denuvo.-Difficulty balance is a bit off.  --Expect an easy time, even on Hard, until you suddenly and unexpectedly hit a rare unrelenting boss.--NG+ only makes things easier.  You may want to consider only sticking to New Game instead, though you'll miss out on a few skills.-Repetition regarding bosses.  --Most bosses have a phase you'll encounter multiple times per fight where they go invulnerable, charge up a super (possibly insta-kill) attack, and leave you hoping your allies will help you destroy multiple new targets to interrupt it.  You can deal with it, but it gets annoying and dull after a few times.--You will have to many bosses again towards the end of the game (this may or may not bother you).PRO/CON-Voicework is a very subjective topic, and your personal preferences will likely determine whether you like it.--Charlotte has a speech impediment which I personally find interesting due to its rarity in game acting.--Many NPCs share the same flamboyant voice probably better-suited to a main character.-Few extras added other than a short, mostly inconsequential postgame story.Trials of Mana is a personal favorite example of a remake done right, and I highly recommend it.  You don't need knowledge of the series or the original to enjoy it, as it is a self-contained story.  There's also a substantial demo available if you still aren't sure, where you can try out each of the main character's intro.

_childDocuments_.review: Cannot recommend this game enough to RPG fans of all kinds. I 100% it the first few weeks it came out on my Switch and decided to get it on Steam when it went on sale. An incredibly faithful remake to the original game and has a solid/fun story. Music is some of the best in the genre and really pulls you into the experience. The gameplay is solid and the ai settings on your companions is good enough to get you through the entire game feeling like they aren't totally useless. It also has tons of replayability due to the three different main stories you can experience depending on whose in your party. Plus getting to experience different character parties brings about fun unique conversations. I really do love this game and while it has several quirky issues l feel as though they all play into the game's charm.

_childDocuments_.review: Held off on this game for years.  I didn't like the Secret of Mana remake and felt like the original did it better.  Finally gave in after watching a friend play for a while.  Credit where credit's due.  They did amazing with this one.The combat system is very simple, but they managed to make it engaging with some lite combos, charge attacks, heavy attacks, quick mapping items and spells and moves.  Goes so well with the class system, which also got upgraded.  The charm of the original has been maintained despite all these improvements, which I feel is impressive.  Not easy to remake a game from the ground up and keep the good parts and rework the bad parts.  Sounds easy, but it isn't.  Otherwise all the companies doing remakes would be pulling it off more often, in my eyes anyway.  I'd recommend this to anyone who enjoyed the original, which is rare for me to say.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 31.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game too many times, or play nearly as long as some of you. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you
