_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  It's great.  You know that feeling when you haven't been to one of your favourite ice cream places in years, then you finally get a chance to go back and the ice cream you already loved is somehow even BETTER than you remember?That's basically how I feel playing this game.  It's the same Super Nintendo classic I enjoyed, only now without most the old game's busted issues (like missing half your attacks, etc)I was kind of dreading the Bucca Island segment, as it's the part of the original game that I felt dragged the most...But even that nadir of the game is actually fantastic here.  All in all, I'm quite happy with this remake.Despite the game being somewhat easy for the first few hours of Hard Mode, once you get your first class change, the game will start to bare its fangs and you'll actually NEED to upgrade your gear reasonably often.If you enjoyed the original, you will most likely *love* this nostalgia trip.  It really is the same old classic, but vastly improved upon.If you haven't enjoyed the original, as long as you adjust your narrative expectations to "oldschool game" level, you will probably have a good time with it.Squeenix, if you made a new mana game with this exact same engine, I would buy it in a heartbeat, it's really solid.

_childDocuments_.review: For me it's a HUGE yes for several reasons. Indeed the game is far from being perfect and in many regards could be better BUT in my opinion, all in all, the good parts are far more than lessening the bad ones.Let me tell you what are IMO the great parts of this game :First of all THE MUSIC !! OMG this music .... some few decades back, when i played the SNES version on an emulator (yeah it never made it through in Europe), i already LOVED those musics but the remastered one .... Geez it's really UNCOMON to have such these days but the remastered musics are even more enticing to my ears WHILE staying TRUE to the original. That is some SERIOUS feat to take in judgment !Then the game story/plot, just as the original game it hasn't changed at all as far as i can see, making some real tiny adjustments here and there (something that came to mind to me as of now, in the Angela prologue, when talking about Victor and earing his complaint, she did a funny face then looking at her feet in sadness, now in this remade version, the funy face is gone, she just looks lost in her thoughts ... it's a tiny adjustment but it's still there).But it is not a bad thing since the original story/plot are all really GREAT and for a game of that time, very well thought !The gameplay mechanics, while in the original version, it was cool and doing its job ... the new version IMPROVED it greatly, now it's less of a mess, you can jump, evade hits, charge hits, etc. Nah, really it feels polished up and way much enjoyable to be able to finish a fight, see how well you've performed with doing a fight under 20s, not being hit, etc.The graphics, while not being TOP NOTCH of what we could see in other genre games, it is still really much enjoyable and once again, stayed TRUE to the original game and for that, i just ENJOY that !So far it's a really GREAT game, staying TRUE to the original game and IMPROVING it in many way, so why shoudl'nt you not like it ? For the fans it's a MUST HAVE while for the newcomers to ARPG, it's an interesting game bringing FRESHLY new mechanics not found in any other games that much.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Great game.  Very true to the original.- An updated battle system from the original to fit the 3D third person view, which turned out to be very fun and addicting.- Character (re)designs are great as well.- Great art direction provides vivid characters and environments.- Newly added passive abilities adds another layer to customizing your characters.- Remake music is well done.  However the original music is included for anyone who would like to try that as well, which is also one of the best.- Extra post game content and class 04 provide something new to the players who are already familiar with the original.- Responsive controls makes fluid movement and combat.Cons:- Definitely too easy even on Hard mode.  Bosses need more HP.- Lower budget title so the cutscene animations and voice acting are a bit weird.  Japanese voice remedies some of that.Seiken densetsu 3 is my favorite game of all time so I'm definitely on the nostalgia hype train here.  However overall I'd say it's a solid A or AA title as a remake.  You can't expect AAA quality since it wasn't designed to have such budget to begin with.  And since it's true to the original, some of the story content is over simplified due to the original was a 25 year old game. _childDocuments_.review: !!!WARNING!!!The following review may contain potential spoilers, you have been warned!.PSA: I suck at formatting, so what?Let's address something important first, I will be reviewing the game based on when it was first released back in the 90s.I am a big fan of Square-Enix, which is why I even decided to buy the game. I have completed the game with all the achievement after roughly 50 hours of game play.Let's get right into it.First off, will I recommend getting the game? Well, Yes and No.The story is a pretty generic and basic, found mostly in AJRPGs. However, it has it's own twist which is kind of cool. Based on the character you chose, the story changes. This includes the interactions with NPC, bosses, the characters, and even some monsters. Yes, you heard it right, there's different interaction with some monsters based on which character you chose.Now, I've never played the original Trials of Mana, but from what I gathered on things that confuses me in the game seems to have some impact on what you chose to do on some certain parts, which makes it very interesting. The negative side of this review is, even though the story changes based on what character you chose to play, the dialogue is more or less the same, it's not a big difference that makes it obvious enough to know it's different which is saddening. There's a lot of potential with the dialogues even for a games in the 90sNow, we have 6 characters, all of them have different play-style. Going through all of those will make this review longer than it already is. So I'm not going into full detail with this, but the general idea is, we have a thieve, a dragoon, a black mage, a white mage, a monk, and a warrior. They all can pan out to two types of classes, Light & Dark. Some gives insane damage, some gives insane supportive power, some gives insane abilities to help with the post-game content. The skill-tree system is pretty interesting as you can mix-match with Light & Dark class to get the abilities you want.You could reset the class too, but it's only doable after you reach certain parts later in the game. Changing class is a pain if you don't know what you're doing. This is kind of a bad pickle in the game.You'd need to find some items with a random chance of getting the certain item you need to change to a class you need in the later stage of the game, and it can't be re-rolled. "So, why bother?" I ask myself every time. That said, the RNG in this isn't that bad to be honest as you have 1/3 chance of getting it since you'll be playing with 3 characters instead of the aforementioned 6 chars. The game isn't very "grindy" at all, you could get all the items required for changing class and getting what you need by re-selling things you picked up along the way.However, the pacing of the game is pretty slow, and sometimes notoriously slow.Playing through the first time or loading into a New Game+ with new characters on your second run would probably tear your hair out. Once reaching a certain point, there's tutorial on showing you how to change into advanced class, but you won't be able to get any of the class changing materials until a little bit further into the game. If you're doing this on New Game+, you could do it immediately since you probably have the materials to do so, but if you're doing it on a different roster of character from the previous run, you won't be able to do it at all since, you didn't pick up any from your previous run.This in my opinion, heavily slows the game down.The game is released in the 90s, yes, there's a remake version of the music, but it's still not good enough for me to give it a big praise. Square-Enix is known for making great graphics and good music to go with their game, but this to me seems a little bit off and pretty "meh". Though, the graphic is pretty good for a remake. It's has elements from Dragon Quests, which isn't all that bad. The only music that caught my ear the most is probably going to be [The Sanctuary of Mana], this is definitely entering one of my favourite song list.So, should you get the game?If you've played the original game and want some nostalgia, why not?If you're bored off because of COVID-19, it's a great time killer. If you like hack-and-slash, give it a go.It's a overall Yes to me, but if you don't like Action-Hack-and-Slash type of game with generic plot-line from a JRPG, I'd suggest to stay far away from the game.In my honest opinion, it's not worth RM200 for this game (Approx. 45USD), but it's a great time killer.I give the game a rating of 6.8 out of 10!Happy gaming! :D

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game. I have played the original several times, yet this game has somehow made several things worse:1.) It's incredibly kitschy and childish - characters make everthing seem funny and stupid, drama is made fun of, one character has a terrible speech impediment to sound like a toddler.2.) The story is confusing, even more than the original, due to a weird pacing in the game (and I've played the original)3.) the fighting system is horribly dumb (and you gonna fight a lot here). It mostly comes down to repeating the same button sequences like attack-attack-attack-heavy attack to do a "finisher" and that's all you do with the fighting characters. In the late game when you finally have abilities, you use them to buff and debusff, then hit the attack combo over and over again.4.) The leveling system is just bad and bears no impact - it's almost negligible to select any stat - the benefits are minor.5.) Post game... Oh boi.. is also boring. One major dungeon which is just more button mashing, has basically no impact or meaning in the game's context, but you can repeat it to get more abilities. But since the game is over, you don't need them anyway.Also, "Hey we get the super upgrade...lets call it "class4". How boring is that? Ever thought of any RPG where they just said, "we get class 4" - not master class or any unique name, just "class4". and it has no canonical meaning either.6.) the ???? seeds. Hey, you thought you could play as a cool ninja class? Nope, need the right item, which you might not get, so you take the other class and can't switch until MUCH later in the game.Sadly, this game has ruined an SNES classic by DEACREASING the value gameplay and story-wise. _childDocuments_.review: First off, i'm something of a fan of the mana series.  so right off the bat, i'm biased in the game's favor.I feel that trials of mana is a good way to remake and modernize an action RPG.  unlike the secret of mana remake, they rebuilt many of the game systems from the ground up, while leaving as much as possible just as it was.to be honest, i feel the game only has 2 main weak points.  1st, it's very easy.  the mana series has always been easy games, though, so that's not a huge issue to me.  2nd, the voice acting.  it's not that it's all bad, there are many really good parts.... it's just really inconsistent.  the sound engineer also made a few questionable decisions.there's also the minor issue of this translation not being the same as the fan translation of the original, if that matters to you.  it's also single player only, which may offend some mana multiplayer diehards.

_childDocuments_.review: My first introduction to the game was the demo that was released on the Switch. After looking around and doing some research I found out about Seiken Densetsu 3 which was never released in the west due to the N64 being release the same year making it hard to still invest in a game for the SNES. A translated ROM made the rounds for emulators in the late 90s and in 2019 an official english version made its way into the Collection of Mana last year. At the same time the 3D remake was announced. I never played the ROM but the demo convinced me to give the game a try and as a someone growing up in that era the remake is well appreciated.Visually the game looks decent. It won't win any awards but it has a charm to it and a design to it that makes everything fit. The story is the basic chosen one to defeat evil thing and there is no real in depth character progression. Everything is fast and straight forward even though you will get bits of the characters backgrounds and motivations. Dialogs are straight forward as well with little or no run arounds.The design is worn on the sleeves. You can make it they tried sticking close to the original game. The game soundtrack is redone but you can hear its 16-bit origins and switching to the original soundtrack you can clearly hear the similarities.Sadly there is no multiplayer which really is a shame as I can imagine the game being much more fun with other players. I've only started post game now with another chapter that was never in the original. There is also a new game plus bringing over much of your previous games progress. There is little grinding in the game with it only becoming a thing once you start looking for class items otherwise you can easily play and finish the game without ever needing to grind for levels.A note on class selection, you are stuck in your class that you have selected until the last chapter of the game so decide before hand what you want to class up to. You can reset your stats about 1/3 during the game so just spend points on what you feel will work for you the best as you level.

_childDocuments_.review: This is something you really don't see very often: a very faithful remake of a classic SNES game. Well, Super Famicom, it was never released outside of Japan until last year.The combat is really fun, the world is gorgeous and fun to explore, it's just a joy to play through. I am looking forward to playing through at least three times to see the different variations in the story, including completely different final bosses.The original was already a great game, but this improves it in myriad ways. You can now use items and special attacks and cast magic in battle without everything screeching to a halt while the animations play out. As a result, your AI partners can now actually use their abilities without you having to constantly switch around and manually activate them! They've changed the level-up system so it's no longer just boring point assignment, now you're unlocking abilities and can actually see when you'll get a new move.The only problem is the cutscenes and voice acting, which are downright amateurish. Honestly, the kind of thing you'd see in like a really early PS1 game, or a modern indie developer's very first prototype. It's downright bizarre, but easy enough to ignore.Highly recommended, especially for old fans of Seiken Densetsu 3!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has brought me so much joy. Over the last decade, I have strayed further and further from single player games. They just don't hit me like they did when I had no friends, so now with all games having multiplayer platforms, it has taken my attention to say the least. However, this game brings back fond memories twenty years ago when I nabbed and emulator for SNES, playing it with each character and different stories. The replay value adds so much in that light, wanting to know how different evils will interfere with our heroes' journeys. Everything they have added to game has been helpful, from the 3d rendering, to added combat mechanics, and fun easter egg (Lil Cactuses to find throughout the world.) Exciting to see the original story being turned into a new story! It's like if you wanted Pokemon Red/Blue revamped into a 3d world without destroying the integrity of the original content itself. SPOILERS...Furthermore, I was happy to find out after beating the game that there was a continuation post-endgame. I'm excited to found out what new plot has taken place, because I was ready to just start over with the other 3 heroes and play on hard mode. I guess that will have to wait! Thank you Square Enix. The only con(s) I have for this game is that normal mode was far too easy (I may have an OP comp, but still,) and that the game isn't multiplayer like the original. Maybe SE can develop a way for friends to take control of the other party members? That would be the cherry on top!

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, basic staple RPG without the gimmicks and fluff.Graphics:Good for the genre. Soundtrack:Excellent all the way throughStory:Decent basic apocalypse story. Serious dialogue that gets to the point. Characters backstories are done well, and dialogue is not hammy or cheesy. No gimmicks here.Combat:You are limited in what you can really do in combat for a large swathe of the game. Once it starts to open up in the midgame, it is better. AI will never be as good as the player , but they are passable.Cons:Very linear point to point game.Lots of walking back and forth between objectivesNot much variety in enemy type. The same enemies get reused over and over again. There are probably only about 15 in the entire game -- they simply get palette swapped, or become higher leveled.The dialogue and cutscenes become overwhelming when playing NG+ since you will just be rushing through the game. No way to quickly end dialogue or skip cutscenes.Far too many load screens for such a simple game in 2020. The load screens are only a few seconds each, but there is just no reason for most of them. Becomes more apparent in NG+The seed pot system for obtaining characters ultimate equipment is too reliant on RNGPros:Simple but fleshed out story that's easy to get into and understand. _childDocuments_.review: Well, first it’s important to know how Seiken Densetsu 3 (I keep calling it that way anyway, even though Trials of Mana was a precisely chosen title. And please, no fuss about Secret of Mana 2) is important in my gamer life, more specifically of JRPGs in general. Back in my distant 13 years, I met the SNES game, and I didn't even know that that game had only been released in Japan. It was passion at first sight, Seiken Densetsu 3 was a wonderful game in all aspects. Graphics that are certainly among the Top 5 best SNES visuals. Sublime songs, composed by master Hiroki Kikuta, I consider his best work. Simple combat, but that hooked me and provided me with a lot of fun. The story, events, wonderful characters, even above what was common for the time. But something that impressed (and is still impressive today) are the 6 characters that can be chosen, you choose 3, and depending on the formation, events change, dungeons change and final bosses change (and thus, the endings too). It is something that for me is only astutely equated to the various endings (and also some events) of Chrono Trigger. Seiken Densetsu 3 was developed at the end of the SNES' life, and also with a large budget for the time. Those were other times when the series was still very strong. And then we're back to Nintendo's E3 2019. Yes, I will not deny it. When I saw that that beautiful game was the Remake of Seiken 3 (I just saw Duran's hair) I let out a few screams. Even happier was when I saw that we would have the complete collection of the first three Mana on the Switch. And even more incredible is that they were launching digitally at that moment. I bought it right away. And I bought a physical copy later. By the way, there are few games that I buy on more than one platform when they are not exclusive. Mana, Final Fantasy, etc. It would also be like that with Nintendo if it weren't a First Party. But was it a successful endeavor to turn a 2D classic into a fully 3D game? It is now that my analysis begins. I chose Angela, Duran, and Riesz (I prefer the fan-made translation, Lize, or Lise). First thing, to succeed in a transition from a 2D game to 3D. The world has to be interesting because the 3D perspective allows for more exploration (just see a Metroid Prime type case). And Trials of Mana Remake does this with mastery. First, something simple, it's really cool to explore every corner of fields, dungeons, and villages after items. I thought that was very nice. These chests (which are shown how many are missing in each area in the first update of Li'l Cactus), finding Li'l Cactus itself, jars, and the bright spots are a great incentive to explore each corner. It was very good. And these explorations extend from cities to Fields and Dungeons. And it was balanced, you will find many Cup of Whishes, for example, that comes at the right time, since they are expensive items for the beginning of the adventure. Still talking about scenarios. They became organic, the developers excelled in larger areas, without several mini areas as in the original. And it was just a natural thing to explore. They endeavored to improve exploration, to be faithful, and at the same time to improve the design of the scenarios, I saw a certain location that reminded me of Trine at the time (whoever played the original must suspect which one it is). Another thing that I thought was cool is to look for the other two companions when you arrive in a new village. This did not happen in the original game. And it is a small detail, but it gives even more polish to the new exploration. The dialogues with voice acting between the characters, when the events change, also give a great spice. I am very sorry, but I MUCH miss JRPGs like that, reminiscent of the SNES, PS1, and PS2 times. Every time I progressed I felt that today's JRPGs no longer do this homework. A somewhat corny story, but much more charismatic. You can walk there in various locations without hindrance, use a World Map of various types (how absurd to think that we would be celebrating entering homes and a game having a traditional World Map in the middle of 2020!). Trials of Mana Remake is charming. And something that improved the exploration, was the update on the first day, leaving the dash on without having to press the analog stick every time. Total QoL, which made and makes a huge difference. Regarding the combat system, it changed from ordinary wine to a 1992 Screaming Eagle Cabernet. The combat just got a lot better. Mainly due to the increase in its complexity. You can jump, and attack in the air, send air enemies to the ground, and slaughter them. Hit and run. Use dodge. Knock out enemies in a variety of ways. Having to break your protective defense. And the best: according to how you change classes, there is the unlocking of new combos, very fun. Not to mention spells and abilities, which do not interrupt the action as in the original. And the bosses... They are delicious! And those who think that the game continues with difficulty drool like in the demo are mistaken. The battle against Genova (that wall that looks like a fireplace) became much more difficult in the Remake. For the first time, I had to change Angela and Riesz's strategy to attack what I was attacking: the boss. The mini-enemies are not worth, and you can't, to finish them off as in SNES. I also realized that you can only carry 9 items in the fight, even though you can stock a lot. The AI ​​is problematic, especially with the spikes coming out of the ground, boss pushing everyone, and attacking with magic and enemies to get in the way. I had 5 Game Over, 1 in Genova, and the other 4 in Benevodons, and it seems that the AI ​​gets a little crazy when there are several attacks or elements to be defeated on the screen. If the game was overly difficult it would be a problem, but as it is not, you can forgive. The fights against the Benevodons shine. Many said that it was a problem in the original, successive battles that add little to the story, but here: it's time to beat the best way possible! The OST must be the best remix I've heard for a remake (or, at least, is easily among the best). It doesn’t try to look super complex and developed, it’s just the same OST but vastly improved by Kikuta and his team. Keeping exactly the same tone as the original. He didn't go crazy on them, either for good (inevitably wanting to orchestrate everything) or for bad (Secret of Mana Remake). They did their homework with praise. All laurels for the composers. So, Trials of Mana is approved or disapproved? Very approved, both as Remake and as an individual game. It is not always that a game, in this case, Remakes, outperforms the original. I know, Seiken Densetsu 3 from SNES still has more charm with its 2D Pixels, but the 2D of the original still seduces me more. Rejoice! Fans of Mana! The series has returned. May Trials of Mana open the door to Seiken Densetsu 5. We know they have the talent. Congratulations to Naoki Matsue, Masaru Oyamada, Shinichi Tatsuke, and the entire team that worked on the game. You made my favorite Action-RPG to be surpassed by your Remake, 25 years later.

_childDocuments_.review: Playtime is +9 hours as I've started my save on another accountA must have for any fan of the Mana series. A safe purchase for any JRPG lover.This is probably one of the best, if not the best, remake of older games that exists.It's completely faithful to the original story (which is a good story)Pros:- Can build a group of 3 out of 6 characters that all have their own background story. Every 6 characters get incorperated into the story, regardless of who you pick, each one plays their own part in some way. Each character has a completely different playstyle and different abilities. Character design is top-notch. Animations are fine. Dialogs etc. change fully based on the characters you picked.- Very solid and fluid fighting system with combos, items, skills, power moves, dodging, jumping, air attacks etc. Leaves nothing to be desired except for some camera related stuff maybe (which most JRPGs with a real-time fighting system suffer from)- Very good story. Not the best there ever was, but it's a typical nice JRPG story with many villains and many things to solve and master- Very nice graphics. Surely not AAA graphics, but typical nice JRPG graphics. A bit cel-shading, it reminds of Zelda BotW and is on the same quality level, maybe a little bit below- Very nice music. I've seen negative reviews about the music, personally I love the music. You can even activate the original 8-bit music.- Many bosses, quite a lot different monsters, many towns, many dungeons, many areas- Constant progress. You're always leveling up. You're always improving stats. You're always gaining new skills. You're always equipping new stuff.- The class system is nice and has a high replay value. There are several different classes you can reach on each character with a ton of skills and build styles to choose from- Post End-Game- Quite polished. I didn't notice a single bug or clipping error or anything. There are probably some here and there based on what I've read, I didn't encounter a single one and I'm through the main part of the game- Know that feeling when you search every single inch of a map and there's simply nothing to loot? Well, you don't have that here. Collectibles everywhere. It's wise to search every single corner of a map.- For every character in your team you can configure how it will act in a fight. Dedicated heal & buff slaves are no problem, as an example- Mouse and keyboard controls are native and work well, this game is still best played with a controller which is also supported. I used an Xbox One controller and it was very fluent and nice to play with a very good control setup- Unreal EngineCons:- The voice acting and translations are quite broken for some languages. I suggest you switch to Japanese audio and english subtitles, that's probably how it was supposed to be and that way nothing is broken anymore- It's easy. Some early game bosses felt stronger than most late-game bosses (Zehnoa, Dolan and that light benevelon were the hardest imo). Played on normal, didn't die a single time and I'm everything but a pro-gamer. No grind was needed. If you are looking for a challenge, directly play on hard (but even then it's not as much of a challenge as some other JRPGs out there) A friend of mine, who is playing her first JRPG with this one, _did_ have a hard time with some bosses and mob groups- Some boss mechanics are very confusing, hit-boxes for some skills suck (e.g. some cleaves of monsters hit you even if you're standing behind them etc.)- Denuvo. It's a problem for some (e.g. if you don't have a constant internet connection), for most people it isn't.- The AI is not the best. It's not completely bad either, sometimes they dodge properly, but sometimes they don't and in boss-fights that can cost some items or MP to heal/res etc. Some moves are ignored, e.g. Charlotte won't automatically imbue weapons with elements for whatever reason (it's no problem doing that via the radial menu at the start of a fight, though)- Charlottes baby speak is a bit....too much...They really tried too hard and it's annoying most of the time. But it's nothing that reduces the gameplay fun.Is it worth its money?It is not worth 50€, but you can buy the game for 30€ if you know what I mean. It is worth 30€. For the nostalgia factor and to support these remakes (maybe Chrono Trigger soon?), 50€ is okay, too. For the first full play-through you need approximately 30 hours. If you look at the negative reviews, most of them have these 30 hours. You get 1h playtime for every buck you spend. If you play again with the other 3 chars you get 2h for every buck. To get all achievements you need at least 2 playthroughs, probably 3. If you want to play all classes in every possible combinations you have a new way to live through the quarantine, it will take a long time.Most negative reviews contain a lot of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥."I can't save" - Yes, you can save. Like every 2 minutes at mana statues and there's auto-save, too"Game doesn't start" - Well, fix your ♥♥♥♥ PC, thousands of people can start it well"People only like it for nostalgia hurr durr" - It's a good game regardless if you played the original game or not. Many well rated JRPGs have a lot more flaws and still count as some of the best RPGs out there. eg. from a technical standpoint it is better done and more fluid than any of the Tales of * Games"Game is too short" - The game is long enough and has a lot of content. Obviously if you rush through it and just skip all cutscenes, deactivate audio etc. you're basically playing a hack-and-slash fest for a few hours. If you go and enjoy the story you'll have enough playtime and content to get everything out of your bucks spent."Music is 30 second loops" - It is simply not. If you don't like the music, turn it off, but don't just go and lieThere is some valid criticism, especially regarding boss-mechanics, localization and AI, but the ones above are not. They are lies or exist because of sheer incompetence.You won't regret buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've done three runs of this game. My personal opinion on the various facets of the game:The meat of the game. Action RPG fans will get a fair amount of enjoyment out of this game. Combat is simple and straight-forward, but that's not a bad thing. Every playable character brings something different to the table, and the class system allows for some freedom in how the heroes progress, which also adds to the replay value. Challenge is a bit lacking, although the AI for your allies can be a bit wonky and result in wasted resources in boss battles. Outside of battle, it's a standard RPG layout. Game starts off linear, and eventually opens up, although if you're looking for an RPG with heavy exploration focus, this game won't scratch that itch. Overall, combat is good if a little easy, and exploration is average.The story is nothing groundbreaking, but it's good enough that you will likely remain interested. The story changes up slightly depending on who you choose as the main protagonist, and if you want see all there is to offer in that regard, you will have to do three runs minimum. The six heroes all have defining traits and personalities, and depending on your party combination, they can have some funny interactions as well. I found myself enjoying all of them by the end of my three runs, even Charlotte.Great, and the art style in general is very eye-catching. Everything from the locations to the characters are vibrant and colorful. Some may think the character designs are tacky, but I actually think they did a great job, especially with the class outfits.Very solid soundtrack. I won't say it's a favorite of mine, but the music goes well with the game. Boss fight themes are probably the highlights in the soundtrack, but there are some great overworld songs as well.The game is rather short by modern standards, though that might not surprise considering it is a remake of a Super Famicom game. At regular pace, the game will take 20-25 hours to complete. As I said earlier, however, in order to get the full experience, you have to complete the game at least three times, so total playtime can end up being around the general playtime for a modern RPG.I got more enjoyment out of the game than I expected, and only had a few gripes with it as a whole. If you're seeking a game that puts you to the test, this game won't provide much, but if you're more of a casual ARPG fan, this is definitely a worthwhile game to play. Even paying full price, I don't regret my purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Remade graphics in 3D.-All classes and stats have depth in them, unlike the dated original.-Secrets sprinkled in the game; even an unlockable 3rd class if u beat the game and fulfill certain late-game side quests.-Soundtrack remade into awesomeness.  Even the option to play the original soundtrack if u liked it instead (its still a banger to this day).-Progression is much faster and the gameplay isn't a push-pull system between u and ur enemies when using skills.Cons:-Can't rename the main characters.  That's how the original Secrets of Mana 3 was special; it made the characters ur building so special to you and you only.-No two-player option.  Wanted to see a way to incorporate a 2nd player or even a 3rd, just like the original did with co-op.9/10.  A close representation of what a Remake should do.  Would have liked it if they had multiplayer or name customization.

_childDocuments_.review: Seiken Densetsu 3 was not my favorite game, but I struggled through it all the same. It took me until this was announced to finally pick it up (on the Switch) and play through it. Man, was that a struggle - the dated systems, the horrific grind, the original was an absolute mess.Which brings me to this game, which somehow kept the charm of the original, the aesthetic was nearly identical (although clearly remastered), and yet, they updated all the right parts of the game to make it fun to play in 2020. The new systems for progression were much more forgiving of weird situations than SD3, and honestly much more enjoyable.The worst part was that they kept the dialogue. Exactly. The. Same. But, I was here for the gameplay, and considering that, I'd say the game was exceptional.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It's a faithful remake that stays very true to the original while using its 3D upgrade to make the gameplay more engaging. I was really impressed how they managed to preserve the fun, lighthearted spirit of the original sprites and music so well. Dungeon areas are usually very modestly sized with frequent save points throughout, making this a great game to consume in about 20 minute chunks. Lastly, some small upgrades to customize character progression mechanics were fun and welcome additions.In the negatives column, the difficulty of the game is almost entirely owed by AI party members being too dumb to avoid attacks, which isn't at all enjoyable. I killed more than one boss with only one character alive just to save healing resources. Also, the story doesn't hold up to modern standards at all, and yet still receives a lot of screen time compared to other story-light ARPGs of the current era. This issue is exacerbated by VA that is often spoken very slowly for reasons I can't understand.In summary, a fun, light game that does a good job of finally bringing a SNES classic to the English language, but it's hardly best in class for its genre. Buy it on sale if you want some 90s JRPG nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: My first foray into the series so I'll be commenting on this game in a vacuum.What I liked:- Visuals. For the most part, visuals look pretty clean and colors are very vibrant. Nothing ground-breaking but it doesn't have to be.- Gameplay. Can be chaotic but it's still very fun in battles. It's a lot quicker than in turn based combat which also has a place of its own but I also really liked what they did here.On-the-fence:- Voice acting. I played it in Japanese and allow me to possibly discredit myself: I don't understand Japanese but it's definitely aimed towards a younger crowd. The voice acting sometimes seem a bit exaggerated or maybe even a bit whiny?- Music. Some tracks are fine, but other music loops can get a bit infuriating. - Level design. Some locations make me want to rip my hair out like the one with the poisonous pools and then you're suddenly playing in a 2D sidescroller. Platforming is already not great. Some dungeons are sorta monotonous.- Controls. Platforming is not the most accurate so it's not fun when you have to do it. In combat, it's fine.What I didn't like:- Characters. Well, just some. Some characters are a bit annoying. Possibly aided by the occasional whiny voice acting, but again it seems to cater to a younger audience and I'm just being an a-hole.- Story. Nothing to write home about. Plays into story troupes heavily so it's forgettable or just not very interesting.- Some boss battles. Some bosses have insta-kill when low HP. Das whack.- Team AI. They're dumb. Almost always, they're just standing there while you're doing most of the work. Like DON'T JUST STAND THERE. BUFF OR HEAL ME PLEASE.Overall, it's an ok game. I enjoyed it more than I didn't. Combat is surprisingly engaging if not infuriating at times. Just don't expect a deep or interesting story, or multi-layered characters. Get it on sale, not at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played the original or any of the other Mana games or remake(s) but this was a great time. If I had to cite one positive above all it would be the pacing, which is fantastic, never really slows down much and doesn't waste your time or overstay it's welcome. You are drip fed progression at a reasonable rate that never starts to drag in a way a lot of RPGs tend to as you move towards the late game and that alone makes it an easy recommend for me.  Game felt most similarly to me to Tales of Berseria of RPGs I've played, but I enjoyed this more due to it's shorter length, less button mash-y combat and general pacing (story is nonsense but doesn't try to be anything other than a vehicle to drive the game forward. Also worth noting this is a lovingly crafted remake - a lot of work and polish went in to this and it shows. Feels like it's built on the DQ11 engine, so that should give you a feel for how traversal/handling works if you've tried that game. Gameplay is action RPG style. You pick 3 of 6 possible characters, one of whom is the "main" character for your playthrough and from who's perspective the story is mostly told. Game seems designed around any combo working - I didnt have a dedicated healer and still managed to beat the game on Hard with little trouble, and I wouldn't describe myself as particularly good at games. Progression system is pretty fun - there are two branching class trees with a couple of options that allow for some customization and/or party optimization.The game also has replay value - there are 3 "final" bosses and only one will be available in a given playthrough depending on your chosen main character. You also only use 3 of the 6 characters in one go so a minimum second playthrough will hopefully still feel fresh.No regrets whatsoever purchasing this at full price, hopefully square makes more of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I did love this game, it has great soundtracks to keep in memory, a lovely art style, beautiful world design, and pretty charismatic characters with a nice background story for each one of them, adding to the three different endings available. If you search to play with a bit of a challenge, I would recommend everyone to play with Difficult settings from the first playthrough, because “Normal” did seem to be quite easy in my opinion, to have a better game experience i had to change it to the maximum difficulty available before unlocking New Game+.

But sadly the story doesn't seem to have been reworked to a more epic setting; it is still quite a happy "fairy" tail settings, it's 1:1 on that side.Very happy to have bought that game, could have used more Manzai/tTsukkomi comedy in between characters; they missed the chance to develop them stronger, they come off as well offkey a bit.In anycase, i'm happy to play this game again, the 3D is enjoyable ^^

_childDocuments_.review: Old classic from SNES era JRPGs.Pros- Soundtracks have been redone, can be switched back to old ones.- Story remains unchanged, characters have more abilities to play around with.- Less xp grind than in original release- Easy controls (even with keyboard&mouse)- Dodge and jump mechanics- New game+, cactus, items, gear, money and character/levels abilities transfer over.- Post game boss + challenges + 4th class- Revamped battle mechanics, AI Companions could use little sharpening though.Cons- Destination/Quest tracker mechanic, made feel like my hand was held thorough the game.- Game is easy even on Hard difficulty, enemies no longer have guaranteed hit abilities.- Translation is decent, but those knowing japanese notice the mismatches right away.- Charlotte's voice acting, cute at first, super annoying after 10 mins.- New game+, no increase in monster/boss levels to compensate player's levels- Needing to run again to laurent to switch classes in NG+- Item box is broken, grants error items, aka wasting seeds that are already hard to come by.- Monsters do not spawn fast enough, imo could be two times faster than it is now.- Local Co-Op not present, as it was in originalIn overall the game is enjoyable and brings back memories from long gone era of gaming,but the price tag of 50€ feels bit iffy, but I guess I can accept it since known voice actors aren't cheap to hire.

One of my favorite side portions of the game was finding lil' cactus. The class system  was a nice way of choosing my play style as I progressed. The costumes with each class also helped by visually showing that my character was stronger than before rather than stats only. Overall this game covered most bases for me as a player.

It feeds well on my nostalgia.It's pretty on rails, with objective markers where to go, don't remember that from before. So the whole RPG feeling is gone, as you just talk to the people and go where you're told to. The combat was pretty statisfying though and your computer controlled companions do well enough, even if they're sometimes still dumb as ♥♥♥♥.Worst part, I went with Kevin, the wolf man with a speech impediment and learning disability. He's had a bad youth so don't take it out on him, it's just pretty annoying hearing him talk. But, even worse is Charlotte. Didn't like her in the SNES version, and sure as hell don't like her now. With a voice over on top of her/him/it now it's bloody annoying!Not sure if I'd rate if that good if it wasn't for nostalgia, it does well, but what it a great game? Don't know. The story is pretty corny with voice overs. So, yea. Decide for yourself, it's still a solid JRPG.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it's a nice SNES RPG with modern graphics. Music is pretty good, art style is really nice. The new combat perspective is great, all the stats now mean something (DEX and Luck from the original didnt do much).Always make sure to have plenty of medicinal herbs on hand for when you get status effects. Gameplay loop is essentially cutscene -> grinding -> cutscene -> boss -> cutscene -> exploration -> repeat. Level ups don't feel very powerful one-by-one, takes several to notice a difference, which makes it difficult to overpower the game (good or bad thing depending on your take). The three different stories add a layer of replay value, and there are some endgame challenges for when you've beaten the main campaign's final boss.GREAT.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This is what remakes should aspire to be.-All of the problems of the original SD3 are fixed while preserving or enhancing the best parts of the original.-All characters are equally viable, and the customization options allow for a decent amount of variety for how you want to play.-Visually, the world is alive, vibrant, exciting, and encourages exploration simply to see what the devs did. Do yourself a favor and wander around and just look at the scenery. The additional platforming elements add some spice to exploration, too.-The soundtrack is gorgeous. Nothing else really needs to be said. The soundtrack was probably the best part of the original game, and the remake improves on it.-The quality of the voice acting is above average, although there are some directorial decisions that I think undermined the skill and talent of Angela's, Riesz's, and Hawkeye's VAs. Still perfectly fine to listen to. Because I do not speak/understand Japanese, I don't feel qualified to judge the quality of the Japanese voice acting quality, but it generally sounds fine to me.There are some problems, though. Without intentionally spoiling anything:-The target locking system is frustrating to use because of how it messes with the camera, so try to avoid using it. -Party AI is suicidal, so some fights have added frustration because the AI doesn't really try hard to avoid/dodge attacks. -There are some bugs and glitches that can result in softlock situations for some boss fights. Fortunately, between the prevalence of save points and autosave, it's not going to kill all that progress you made, but it is annoying. -The post-game writing is pretty uninspired, and almost feels tacked on just to have a post-game. -The mechanics behind the item seeds, particularly the ??? Seeds, could have used some additional attention. -Some default controls felt wonky, especially with the ring menu. Maybe I'm just too used to how the ring menu works in other Mana games, but it felt weird.-Lastly, and this is a personal issue rather than a gameplay issue, the sheer volume of fan service borders on this game being somewhat cringe-inducing to play. Some things make sense (aurora sisters dance), but some things are... bad (a few class outfits for Angela and Riesz; camera angles in cutscenes that seem to only be chosen to show off cleavage or upskirt shots).Despite these issues, this game is something that fans of RPGs will adore. Get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Trials of Mana is a full 3D remake of the original 1995 SNES classic and it is truly remarkable as it contains all of the original game. Boss battles are extremely fun, but if you are looking for something difficult this is not the game for that. The graphics aren't as heavy as most of the modern games, but they still look great with the art direction used. I'm actually surprised how good the screen space reflections are in some of the areas. I think the developers did an incredible job on the remake and deserve full support for their hard work. I highly recommend this title!Features:・Performance is perfection 4K with well over 60fps at all times on my PC.・Graphics are both colorful and beautiful with some highly detailed effects.・Every track has been faithfully recreated and we also get the SNES music.・Voice Acting in Japanese better captures the feel of characters in my opinion.My Specs:・HP Omen 15 (dc0030nr)・Intel Core i7-8750H 3.91GHz・GTX 1060 6GB Dedicated GPU・Samsung 32GB RAM 2667MHz・Samsung 970 Evo 1TB M.2 NVMe・Samsung 860 Evo 1TB SATA SSDMy eGPU Specs:・Razor Core X Graphics Enclosure・RTX 2060 Super Founder's Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original version of this game a long, long time ago, and I'd argue that this is an almost point for point remake of the original, down to remakes of the soundtrack and the sound effects for all sorts of minute things. It was clearly made with love and care. However, the fact that this is a hit for hit remake means that there's no sidequests apart from a small one to find li'l cactus all over the map, and additionally, the voice acting is _terrible_. I'm playing with english voices, and Hawkeye and Angelica are honestly ok; Hawkeye is just straight up good, and Angelica's voice is very much appropriate for her character. Charlotte is in a weird position where the execution of the voice acting is definitely accurate to her script, but can and will be grating. Duran and kevin are bleh, but Riesz.... Riesz's voice acting in english is a mess. I've heard that the english localization team didn't have a huge budget (which is understandable, because the original Seiken Denetsu 3 didn't have a formal english release until this year), and I guess this is where the budget cuts happened. Still, if you can look past the voice acting, and you don't need sidequests to keep you busy, Trials of Mana is perfect for you. Bonus points if you've played the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is really short and simple.Difficulty can swing wildly from: yawn this fight is so boring as you whittle away 1% of the boss health every 5 seconds to WTF is happening why did I just lose all my health.Combat doesn't change throughout the entire game. Those first few fights you have will match how EVERY fight will go for the rest of the game with just more dodging. There's nothing interesting the the combat mechanics and the numbers are balanced so that no attack/defense upgrades change anything until you're at the end of the game where you can just start insta killing things.AI is terrible with no real way to customize them other than a few very simple options with one making no sense how it works. The hardest difficulty makes the AI companions unable to die because of how bad it is.I played the hardest difficulty from the beginning that was available to me. Going up in difficutly after that only makes fights more boring and tedius as one hit kills you and the dodging/attacking mechanics make it so you just need to wait things out and attack at the right time.

_childDocuments_.review: I had huge nostalgia glasses on while playing this game. I played this game WAY back in 98-2000 when I had a DOS SNES emulator. Ah, good old ZSNES. Anyways. I was super positively impressed the work they put in this game after I read the review from Secret Of Mana remake and it failing so completely. I read that this game was very close to the original gameplay even if it had many new mechanics and revamped fighting system. I was very eager to play this. I meant for waiting for a sale but I couldn't resist buying it full price.So. What this game gets right:Let's start with the graphics. They are just awesome. The workmanship animating all the enemies and characters are top notch and very close what you wanted from the original game with very chibi-style expressions and colorful environments. I think I prefer this from the original because you really get to see how the characters were supposed to look. I have no memory seeing any bad textures. Very nice.The sounds and music. The remastered soundtrack is very close to the original (which you can switch to if you liked it) and it sounds awesome. Some of the more meatier tracks I preferred the SNES drums but otherwise super good OST overall with full of ear worms that haunt you for DAYS. I changed to Japanese voices straight from the start because I really hate dubbed stuff. And I heard the dubbing was done with very poor voice actors so I really didn't choose it. The Japanese voice actors were very good and I didn't notice any complaints about that. The sound effect were good too and actually quite close to the originals. I would have liked to change my sound effects to SNES version if possible but there wasn't any option for that :(.The gameplay itself was actually better than SNES version. The combat felt way better. And the biggest reason was the enemy counter attack nerf. I really hated that you really couldn't use your techs in SNES version at all because if you used a full screen special ALL the enemies on the screen that had a counter attack tech used it. That was so awful and it was so broken late game. For example if you used a whirlwind sword from Duran on ..let's see... THREE WEREWOLFS?!, all the damn wolfs would counter with full screen tech that did around 300-400 damage wiping the party. So you were stuck with only level 1 techs and autoattacks. In this version all the techs were ACTUALLY PLAYABLE! The combat itself was solid and liked it quite a bit. The enemy AI tho was kinda passive and predictable. It was quick too and I liked the new dodge mechanic and changes how you could dodge spells and attacks. Only complaint was in some of the bosses they used a full area attack that you countered with attacking some "stuff" you really only damaged with heavy attacks. That meant only your controlled character could destroy the ..."stuff" while your other party members just roamed around doing nothing to them. If you couldn't destroy the...*sigh*..."stuff".. the boss usually did a AOE attack that usually killed your party. Or you were just lucky and somebody happened to survive. This next portion is a double-edged sword..the story. Okay. It's very simple. Like NES Final Fantasy-simple. There is a generic bad guy who wants to take over the world, you need crystals(mana spirits), kill the baddies(mana beasts this time) and you got a final battle. That's pretty much it. Really. This isn't really a Oscar-worthy storytelling but here's the thing: if you are actually looking for a good, simple, SNES-era RPG there's nothing wrong with the story. It's a relic from the ERA that didn't really need the story to sell games. So you really have to decide if you really need a story to play this game. I didn't. I liked the original from the start.The things that were somewhat bad. Okay. The story is ..very barebones and it gets kinda boring after a while. So you really play this game for fun gameplay and experiencing a SNES-era action game from a SNES-era perspective. So it could be a strong factor to not buy this game.The soundwork was too busy from time to time. The characters talked too much and sometimes between battles they would say something but it would blend into the music, the battle jingles and not having subtitles I could't make what they sometimes were saying. I understand japanese enough to understand but even I couldn't read polygon lips. The party AI was oh, so stupid. You could change a lot of party AI but I really didn't notice any difference at all. If you didn't have casters in your party they were kinda useless most of the time. Angela was always useful because you could change her AI to spam magic that usually hit the opponents.The new ability "tree" that you could equip to your character was nice addition, but it made the game WAY TOO EASY. Even on hard difficulty. You really could break the game early with few of the abilities and late game was super easy. Even if I didn't grind at all. I would have preferred the game without the abilities, actually. I think I'll play next time without using any, see if that makes a difference. Overall the game was a breeze. I think I died few times only to the boss AOE attack oneshots that I couldn't avoid because the party was not killing the "stuff" that countered the attack. I would have liked more Spikey Tiger roadblocks in the game.There is some post game content as well but if felt a bit short and not engaging. The true final boss tho was epic and fun fight.In the end this game is a must buy in my opinion ONLY if you are looking for a simpler SNES-era style action game. And even if you are not used to play these kind of games bump the difficulty up because it makes more fun. I'm on my second playthrough to get the other characters endings on New Game + and It's a nice addition to get the full experience. And there is so much replayability with multiple classes for each character so every playthrough should feel different.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing to keep in mind about this game: It is not an RPG. It as a beat-em-up with the trappings of an RPG. 90% of gameplay will be bashing your controller buttons to kill enemies, and the other 10% will be the time running to the next fight.Now, as far as the game itself goes, I greatly enjoyed it. You'll pick a party of three characters from the available six, all with different abilities that will change your strategies. Pick the wizard and the summoner and you've got a couple walking atomic bombs that just need a meat shield to keep enemies off them. Or pick all three warrior types for a more brawler style play.And the best part is that two characters are each tied to one of three different endings. Depending on who you pick as your main character, the story will branch off at a specific point, with the three sets of villains all going to war and those tied most closely to your main character will come out on top and set up which final dungeon, as well as which final boss, you will fight.You'll also change your characters' classes as you progress, upgraded their abilities on a tree of upgrades with four possible final classes. Usually it's straightforward with one branch focusing more on support/healing and the others focusing on offense, but then the wizard for example picks between a class that gets area-of-effect spells while another give more potent single-target spells.Story is very predictable and average hero-versus-villain, but it's a product of its time. The voice acting of this version is clearly low-budget, but nothing that made me hate it. There's also quite a bit of added dialogues over the course of the game to flesh out the characters more than the original SNES version gave.All in all, a very enjoyable game if you go into it expecting it for what it is. Don't be expecting it to be some spectacular masterpiece because it's not and never was. Just a good old beat-em-up with a very endearing cast.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're worried due to how bad the Secret of Mana remake was then stop worrying!  This is a very faithful remake and the music sounds like it should rather than completely different, and then again even if you don't like it, you can switch to the snes soundtrack on the fly!  I played the ever living hell out of the snes port and this one hit almost all the right notes.  My only complaint, literally the only one is the voice acting.  It's very clear that it was a lot of the voice actors and actresses first times.  I only wish they'd done a few more takes of just about each and every line before calling it good.  The game is fun, enjoyable, and addicting as any Mana game should be, but I find myself skipping cutscenes on repeated playthroughs just because I don't want to hear them talk again.  Overall, I'd give this game a solid 9 out of 10.  Just falls short of a perfect score due to amateurish voice acting.

_childDocuments_.review: Two years ago I wrote a review for the Secret of Mana remake that ended with a mention that I would be ‘so damn lit’ if we also got a remake of its sequel that would get released globally. Not only did we get a release of the original Trials of Mana via the Nintendo Switch, but also an announcement for its modernized remake of it in the works. What a time to be alive.I told myself I would wait to beat the main game before writing this review. I had forgotten what it feels like to be a little sad as the end credits of a game roll, and your characters say their farewells, go on their own adventures, and your left sitting alone in a dark room, remembering that you have work on Monday. I haven’t really enjoyed jrpg’s in a long time, and it took reviving a stellar 90’s jrpg to remind me why I use to enjoy them so much. I was cautiously optimistic walking into this, but the crew at Square-Enix who put this game together deserve recognition. The Trials of Mana remake succeeded in every way that the Secret of Mana remake did not; while Secret of Mana stayed true to it’s early 90’s combat game play and forsook its inspired soundtrack, Trials of Mana updated its combat to be much more engaging while staying faithful to the original soundtrack. I get the sense the developers listened to the reviews.The class design that the original was so well known for has been well updated to fit with the more fast paced and engaging combat system used in the remake. Tailoring your characters’ builds, passives, and spell lists requires some thought to make efficient, but even if you choose not to give a damn you can still balance out your party’s frailties through items at the night market, just as the original. It’s complicated enough that it can give a more in-depth player something to think about, however this is where my first criticism will come in; character scaling is very high, and some characters and classes get so powerful they can melt just about any opposition. Angela became the bonafide boss stomper of my group, especially. I went Nomad for Hawkeye thinking he’d play support, but I’m not sure he really supplied much compared to her- though I did have more fun playing him.Class balance is better than the original, however it still needs some fine-tuning. It’s difficult to talk about without bringing up the more important shortcoming of the party AI. Your allies will be stupid and downright suicidal unless you put them on a more defensive option, and even then they’re vulnerable to stun-and-done boss combos. In light of this, overpowered classes are actually a blessing. I don’t know how difficult programming competent AI is, but I could see erring on the side of making classes too strong as a suitable compromise when constrained by time and budgets.Personally, I don’t really care that much about class mechanics being too strong for single player or co-op games. I think that really matters in player vs player games, however I do prefer classes to be reasonably balanced in terms of power and utility between each other. Buffing Nomad’s utility power is more interesting to me than nerfing Magus’ damage.My gripes are mostly mechanical in nature, but the English voice acting deserves a mention. It didn’t really bother me that much, I grew up playing games with silent protagonists, so voice acting in games generally isn’t a huge deal to me to begin with. However, I did play the game with English voice acting and I can say it starts a little rough, but seems to get better as the game goes on. Maybe it was my imagination idk, but the talent in the voice acting is not equal. Some characters are much better than others, but the most consistent problem was pacing in character dialogue. There were unusual pauses in how the sentences were spoken at times, perhaps staying too close to the original Japanese cadence than adapting it more naturally in English. It’s a problem I have noticed before in other instances of Japanese to English translations, such as in anime.I did not have Charlotte in my first play through, so take that for what you will. :PI have to say that I really enjoyed this game a lot. It’s the best remake of a game that I’ve personally played, the dev crew here really pulled a miracle I did not expect. From what I’ve read, they’re interested in seeing what Mana fans have to say about it, and there’s potential for more games to be made for the series. As excited as I am for the Mana series to receive an update, I have to admit I’m a little concerned. I played Legends of Mana and Sword of Mana when they first came out years ago, and I felt both of those games lost the spirit that the original Secret of Mana had, and I eventually figured it was just gone for good. Somehow, the Trials of Mana remake revived that too, and I didn’t expect it. I don’t want to go into my gripes about Legends and Sword of Mana here, but what I can say is that Secret of Mana completely captivated me as a child for its lush graphics, beautiful, choral music, and sense of exploration and wonder. I remember loving that game so much that I wanted to live in it.The Trials of Mana remake brought back something that I thought was dead. These developers have shown that they can distill that original essence and create a solid product with it. It’s not clear to me how possible that is going forward, though. Modern jrpg’s sport characters with an excess of belt buckles, zippers, and just flat weird character designs, and feature plots that are excessively dour and emo. Maybe my preferences are niche, and maybe I don’t know what makes a ‘good jrpg’ anymore, but I can say I lean more towards Studio Ghibli in preferred aesthetics. That, I think, is closer to where the heart of the Mana series lies. Contemporary trends might only sully it. :( 9.5/10! Solid remake, minor gripes, double kudos to the devs behind it. Also, ask Sakurai if he’ll put Riesz in Smash Bros. I know it’s unlikely, but a Mana rep in Smash would be fantastic.And I, for one, would be so damn lit.

I'm saying first because to prevent repeating myself later in this review, there's so much more to be had. Needless to say, this 'review' might come across slanted due to influence of some heavy nostalgia. So strap in cause this may be a long write.Well actually, I just realized after typing it all out that my review won't possibly fit the generous character limit of Steam reviews. So I saved all that I already wrote and may finish writing it out and post it somewhere should anyone show interest in a full review for whatever reason. That in itself though should be a good tell on how much I enjoy the game and can rave about it. But for the sake of steam reviews and clear overview, I'll try summing it up as short as I possibly can.Whatever I write here won't do it justice for what I wrote in my original review. But with all respect towards the English voice actors and actresses, I think it's mostly a matter of the direction they were charged for the game. It is at least a commonly shared perspective that I see being echoed all around. But bear in mind this may very well be subjective of course and for me it's coming from someone that strongly favors subs over dubs in things like anime. But to name one example, English 'Chawwotte' sounds more like a Boston accent trying to speak 'uwu' (weeb for cute/babyish) rather than just having a cutesy speech impediment. Take it as you will, but I would press anyone to check both out and get to their own conclusion. is an enjoyable one that captivates and captures the grief of each character and their respective kingdom(s). There's 3 main story lines depending on your chosen main character and each differs greatly in how they play out with having a different antagonist and final bosses. They all converge somewhat eventually but out of the 6 characters only 2 of them tie in more closely in that they follow the same story and enemy. Having these sets of two in any run to me attributes to more enjoyable interactions/relationships but it's not a necessity. Technically you could multiply whatever playtime for your first run by three if you want to see it all and if you don't, there is newly added post-game content and story that provides even more without me spoiling anything about it. is a welcome and refreshing change over it's top down 2D predecessor. It comes with an entire overhaul and re-balanced system for stat allocations, skills and classes as one may expect and is much needed to supplement the drastic change. Combat in itself is an action-packed management of combos, moves, spells and timing in a fluid perpetual motion with how smooth it transitions in and out of combat. A definite treat to players both new and old. are pure ASMR to someone with nostalgic ties to the classic and I would think a very pleasant mix of tunes and melodies to newcomers as well. You can switch it from remake version to original in the options menu and I would say both sound absolutely stellar with me only preferring one or the other for certain specific tracks. Regardless, having the choice is nice if anyone wants to switch between them at any given moment. from visible changes on equipping weapons, an actual difference in appearance for class changes in the form of changeable skins to having quality of life additions like class and stat resets or new systems and mechanics for people like me who take the time to fully explore everything and talk around. It's easily missed but the game does hint you at rewards for going out of your way from the main objective markers as you can find hidden items or acquire chain abilities from talking to almost seemingly random NPCs. In any case, having most of the main story objectives marked now is a nice means for those wanting to just get on with the story and as a deterrent for those with explorative mindsets. There are so many more things I could mention like the addition of flashback chapters but I think this is a good short glimpse and wrap-up for it all, and I'm quite sure that players of old will easily recognize all the pleasant changes and improvements themselves throughout the game.So in conclusion with all that I have managed to shorten down to in this review, bearing in mind there's much more I wanted to share; you can easily make out what kind of rating I would give this game. Even without the nostalgia glasses, I would think it's a more than enjoyable JRPG in how it's based on a classic that doesn't suffer from certain modern ones that utilize reused assets for mobs and dungeons that dull the immersive experience. There is more than plenty of replay value to be had in seeing all the story lines and/or doing the post-game content but it may very well depend on how much one gets into it. For me judging by my first main story run without post-game content, it will easily reach over a 100 hours to 100% it and see and experience everything there is to it. So to me, it's definitely worth it's weight in gold at the price they're asking for it.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS is the Secret of Mana remake I've wanted since before the Secret of Mana remake was being discussed or likely even in development.  Sadly, what we got instead was pretty lackluster, but we did eventually get this absolute treat of a game.  I was cautiously optimistic since the early gameplay footage, but Squenix usually blows it when it comes to action.  I played the free demo, and I was convinced; this is excellent.  This franchise isn't nearly as popular as the likes of Final Fantasy, so it's great to see it getting any kind of attention, but this was clearly made by people who truly love it.The combat is what you typically see in 3D Action: light and heavy attacks that can be used in conjunction with each other to make combos; this one follows the example of Castlevania: Curse of Darkness, just using the heavy attacks for combo finishers.  You've also got air combos and a dodge roll that works both on the ground and on the air.  Magic no longer BREAKS THE FABRIC OF TIME with each casting, so you have a chance to dodge.  The class system is mostly the same, but now, the stat bonuses that you apply with each level up are separate from your base stats, so waiting a few levels before changing no longer screws you over, like it did in the original.  New are the passive skills that you can equip, and while they don't seem like much in the beginning, certain combinations can absolutely BREAK the game; I basically had infinite MP for my entire party at one point.  What's interesting about these is that they make previously less useful classes into something you might now want to consider.  My only real gripe is the item seed system, and how some of the best equipment is locked behind it; that was in the original, too, but I really wouldn't have missed praying to RNG-zus every time I picked one up.  At least they drop fairly frequently, if you play your cards right.Okay, so I expected good gameplay, and it delivered, even if there were a few additional surprises, but what I never could have expected was how beautiful this game was.  The original had some wild environments that went beyond the usual green grass and leaves you always see, but this...  I found myself watching every sunrise and sunset, staring in wonder at the scenery as I traversed it, and even prison rodeod myself over a fence and off a cliff to walk on the pretty beach alongside Golden Road.  Locations that had been just nice in the original were absolutely gorgeous here.  It wasn't even just the lovely colors and outstanding lighting effects, either; everything was even constructed in a way that fit together beautifully.  I was walking up a winding path in the mountains, and looked down to see another path winding up a peak you'd never get to traverse; it didn't even have to be there, but there was so much detail.  Really, this world was like something right out of my dreams; I couldn't have asked for something more wonderful to explore, and it was clear that the team who made this loves the original game SO MUCH.The story isn't really any different from the original, but if you haven't played that, the story isn't all that deep, and probably isn't going to change your life, but there is an interesting dynamic going on between the 6 kingdoms from which your playable characters hail.  Beyond that, whoever you pick as the main character will put you on one of 3 different story paths; you'll see and do a lot of the same, but there are areas exclusive to each path, and it's definitely worth exploring them all.  The characters aren't bad, either, even if not terribly complex; there's someone here for a wide variety of tastes.  There's also a surprising amount of interaction between them in cutscenes; they all have things that they'll say to each of the other 5 characters at different points in the story, and that level of detail is unusual and impressive.  The overall feel is fairly lighthearted, but not quite as much as its predecessor.The soundtrack is pretty much what I expected: an orchestrated version of the original that's not bad, but not as good as the source material.  Some tracks sound pretty good, like Evening Star and Religion Thunder, and a lot of the time, I didn't even notice that I was listening to the new audio.  Then, you have some where the theory was "electric guitar = better", and it really doesn't, and Weird Counterpoint has this flute that's just... wrong.  Luckily, there isn't much to  complain about, because you can sub in the original soundtrack whenever you want.  Lots of audio options, really, which is good, because the English voice acting is just...  Listen, I don't usually flip games to the Japanese audio, because I'm not  person, but it's clear that a lot more effort went into that; blame the fact that I played this not long after a Yakuza marathon, if you must, but the English voice acting just rides that line of bad, but not bad enough that it'll get enough laughs to make it worth playing the whole game like that.  The Japanese audio also reveals that a lot of weird changes were made to the names of places and characters; it's not the sort of thing that really bothers me, but I couldn't help but notice it.If you're like me and your biggest draws to a game are solid action and a beautiful world, you owe it to yourself to pick this up; it's more than I ever could've dreamt it'd be.

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite fun, to be fair I have limited experiences with the mana series. This game is very fun, I have close to 2 hours logged on my character with a lot of exploration.The combat feels fluid, characters are "interesting" and have some unique styles to their moves, which I do enjoy. I love Hawkeye and Kevin, I think Chawwotte (Charlotte) needs to be quiet... Replacing L's and R's with W's is incredibly obnoxious, and with her high pitched voice, it makes me want to mute character voices... all though I do like the cat puns from Niccolo... My biggest complaint is the lack of normal mapping. The texture work is amazing and if I didn't look closely, I might not have realized it... but a lot of the design could have been optimized with the use of normal maps. The biggest examples are the trees and the archways. These include extra tri's (triangle polygons), with amazing texture work to make it look like it has more depth. This increases the tri count, which can put a load on very old systems; a normal map can make it look like it has indentations and pops out a bit more without the need of extra tri's. As a graphics designer/3d modeler with a decade of industry experience, I can clearly say this is very sloppy by design.
