_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful 3D remake of the amazing old school game. Very nicely done and well transferred to 3D. Beautiful drawn characters, places, monsters. Very addictive game. Play time depending of your play style, could be quick and easy for few hours, could be longer if u want to do most of the achievements in one go, or even more if you are completionist. If you love Mana series, old school jrpgs, this game is must have for you. You will love it.If you are interested in achievements, I can give you few advice.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Man, if you've been lucky enough to play the original SNES version of Seiken Densetsu 3 (Trials of Mana) then you'll realize that a good game, NEVER stops being good, just because of age. Everything is here that made the original game great; jokes, references, interactions and even legit costume changes when class changing. It's all here, plus MORE. WAY MORE. Everything got expounded upon. Combat, the entire game is practically fully voice acted, the maps are literal 3D renditions of the original 16-Bit terrains although, I'm not a big fan of changing some of the names of spirits (Wisp/Lumina Djinn/Sylphid, etc) but that little change doesn't stop this game from bringing back GREAT memories of a truly solid video game. Hell, even the 'SQUARE ENIX' opening is a call back to the original  'SquareSoft' intro that you'd get back on SNES.If you want to do a legit remake of a classic video game? THIS is how it's done. HIGHLY reccommended. Even if you're just a fan of action RPGs. America never got the original copy, so if this is your first time playing it, saddle up, cause it's fun, challenging and VERY addictive, lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Trials of Mana is a simple, fun RPG with deep party-building mechanics, tons of potential for build diversity, some replayability, and fun hack and slash gameplay.I chose Duran, Charlotte, and Riesz as my 3 characters. Duran as the main character and attacker, Riesz as support, and Charlotte as healing. This worked really well, especially later in the game as healing skills piled up and started stacking with each other. Playing around with the different ability combos was a highlight.The graphics are nothing special, but the art style is nice enough. Same for the music. The voice acting is famously cheesy, but in most cases loops around to being decent. The story is as cookie-cutter as it gets too, but sometimes that's a breath of fresh air.All in all a pretty good action RPG that's not going to blow you away. Simple good fun that'll keep you entertained for the 15-20 hours a main story playthrough takes. Solid 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I'll just drop a short version of my thoughts right here. The game isn't worth the full price. As an RPG, the game is very barebones. The demo had me thinking that the full game would offer a whole lot more. If you played the demo, you've pretty much have seen all that the game has to offer, in terms of gameplay. Each character has multiple classes that you can unlock as you level them. However, no matter what class you change to, the game feels the same - spam attack button, use abilities here and there, and on to the next fight. The combat itself is pretty bland and repetitive. The animations for attacks and abilities aren't all that great either. While the game isn't exactly difficult, you'll often find yourself searching for a balance of difficulty between just about every common enemy and some of the larger boss fights. Simply put, the fights are either brain dead easy or designed poorly as an attempt to simulate difficulty. There is a lack of challenge to be found, outside of boss fights with cheap mechanics. The story and voice acting (at least in English) don't help this game's cause either. I put nearly 8 hours into this game and wanted to like it more. However, I couldn't bring myself to push through a game that isn't fun or engaging. Unless the game is at a steep discount, I'd stay away.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: If Square Enix added coop and a harder level of difficulty as DLC, my pants would be filled with glorious and juicy white goo. Not only this is a faithful remake of the original SNES game, there is new end game content increasing the longevity greatly.The soundtrack is one of the best, if not the best.It's rare to see a product filled with so much soul.Angela's sumptuous body is worth the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this was a fun game. While the combat is simplistic and the story is not revolutionizing anything, there is just a charm to these old school games. It's just fun to play. The neat art style and colours and especially the fantastic soundtrack throughout the journey set the tone for a great adventure. It’s also helped by not having tons of side quests with barely any purpose other than time padding. You can try to find all Lil’ Cactus for neat rewards but they’re all in areas you pass through anyway. Some people dislike linear games, I personally enjoy a streamlined story without any boring and distracting nonsense on the sides. It’s also fun to build your characters and you really do feel like you’re getting stronger as the game progresses, giving you more options. The characters are also very likable albeit cliched.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Completed my first play through and I have to say... wow! Total revamp of the original game done RIGHT. I've been very disappointed with some of Square's recent forays into remaking some of their classic games, but this one here was done so well I honestly don't have any disappointment here. I know the original incorporated multiplayer but honestly I feel like it literally would detract from the play style and fast paced combat. Switching and spells have never been more fluid in battle. The addition of the extra content at the end of the game is amazing. Leveling doesn't feel like a complete grind. The voice acting is actually not half bad! The new stat system is done very well. I just don't think I could come up with a bad thing to say about this game. Those who complain about how "easy" it is, just get to the end game content. The game just has a gentle ramp up to the harder enemies and bosses. I found myself dodging around like crazy trying to make sure I didn't get KO'd too often. If you're a fan of the original game or even of the Mana series in general, I really feel like this one is a must have!
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I have no previous experience with this series other than Sword of Mana for the GBA. So far I love most of the game I've experienced so far. The combat and class upgrade is a nice treat. Being able to swap between party members on the fly is great. I love the art style. I do have a few negatives though. The AI is a little braindead. Some fights you'll spend most of your time healing your party members who will just stand right in front of one shot enemy moves. The story progresses a little too fast at some points and makes things feel a little insignificant at times.My biggest gripe though is the English voice option. Who did they get to do the English voices in this game? It's so terrible and feels like they pulled in strangers off the street and told them to read a script not knowing the context of what they were reading. It's so awkward to listen to and you can tell there's no effort put into it. I really can't stand Charlotte's English voice. I'm glad I kept leaving her behind. Her baby voice is like nails on a chalk board.

_childDocuments_.review: Very well done remake(remaster?) of original Trials Of Mana multiple playthroughs depending which characters you chose as a main pair (third is a support character mostly) story being told from said pairs perspective I have one playthrough left to experience but so far have enjoyed this JRPG gem quite a lot hope you will aswell
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I've played around 100+ hours on Switch and i liked this game so much that i bought on Steam too. One of if not the best remake of an old school game i've ever played, it leaves what's good on the original untouched and upgrade everything else masterfully. My only critiscism is that it should have had some triple A treatment from Square Enix instead of being like a side project, the graphics even if very enjoyable and colorful isn't the Square Enix standart but that doesn't impairs the game in any way. _childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Played Sword of Mana on GBA when I was a kid and had never heard of Seiken Densetsu 3 until the Collection of Mana was released for the switch. I immediately pre-ordered the Trials of Mana remake and was not disappointed.The soundtrack on the title screen sets you up for a phenomenal score of remastered tracks that can be set back to the original at any point for nostalgia.Combat is fluid and playstyle customization is rewarded. With so many combinations of characters, playstyles and abilities, multiple playthroughs are encouraged, with a New Game+ feature allowing for a scenic, completionist route should you desire. Downsides would be the English VA. Stick to Japanese voices and subtitles for optimal story experience, The difficulty is also a factor. Whilst it can be set to Hard at any point, it isn't overly challenging if you have the combat system nailed. If you are looking for a Dark Souls experience, this isn't for you.If you are looking for a compelling story, reimagining of the original soundtrack with the nostalgia that comes with it and a fluid combat system this is the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: The game is just superb. This is how remakes should be, solid, that's it. It begs the question why do we suffer through such crap remakes if this is the quality we could get? _childDocuments_.review: Very faithful 3D remake of the original Seken Densetsu 3 (Secret of Mana 2, Trials of Mana) for the Super Famicom/SNES.The good:The music is extremely respectful and beautifully done. Rumor has it, it was supervised by the original composer and it shows. The gameplay. The action combat has been brought to the modern era with fun, quick skill animations and adjustments that keep the game fun. I love how items are scattered around (oh! A piece of Candy!)The OK:The visuals are great, but may seem dated for 2020. For the budget the game no doubt ran on, they did a good job.The Bad:What the hell is up with Square Enix using the same button for Interact as Jump? The English Voice overs are horrible. The actors have a lot of talent but the direction is just so god awful and weird at times. It borders from laughable to just cringy. Thankfully you can switch to the Japanese voice overs, so as long as you don’t mind subtitles you’re good to go.Overall a great game. _childDocuments_.review: I didn't play the original game and would never even try it after playing this one.This game is bad and those who say it's good are looking through nostalgia glasses. I'm not sure what is even good about the game? Music is mostly bad, limited, and then reused often. Graphics are basic 3D models with no details. Clipping is common in every character's costumes. Facial expressions of any cutscene is less than a Mii in Wii Sports. Voice acting is awful in English and below average in Japanese. Combat is limited to the same 3-4 combos with a class attack mixed in for "flair." Party AI is atrocious as they constantly die to bosses therefore forcing you to 1v1 them. I would have chose the healer, but I'm not a fan of pedophillic uwu lolis. The only other characters that can heal are locked behind class skills which you can't access until haflway through the game. Gear upgrades adhere to the age-old idea of increasing of passive stats only equals fun (maybe this changes in the later part of the game?). The overworld has less viewing distance than minecraft at the lowest block setting. The story and antagonists are laughable. I really don't see what there is to love about this game! I'll try to continue to play it based on the sunk-cost fallacy, but don't think I'm going to like it!

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard for me to say what this game would be like as a first experience in the current day. I can highly recommend it for anyone who enjoyed the original though. This keeps very faithful to the original in just about every way with the exception of it being 3D(obviously).The original game was pretty ahead of it's time with many aspects like the class system (at least by JRPG standards). This made the game really pop, however nowadays these things may not be seen as very unique. If it is your first time jumping into any version of this game it might seem a bit "generic", but either way it's still very well done.The game looks, feels, and plays very well. The soundtrack was even better than i remember it (with every track being redone). However if you loved the old snes/fam sound, then there is an option to use the old OST... very happy to see that as an option.Even though it's tough for me to make a call on people who are new to Trials of Mana(Seiken Densetsu 3), I still think most people would have an enjoyable time with it. _childDocuments_.review: Rom's were downloaded and translation patches were applied but it was a disservice and injustice to fans of this franchise to deprave us of this game for this long. Here it is in all of it's 3D glory and it's incredible.Unfortunately I only ever finished this game through once back in the 90's on an emulator and I don't remember much of it, only that it had insane amounts of customization and you could finish the game with a number of different groups which would change the final boss / ending depending on who was in your party.If it sounds up your alley, then continue reading.As of typing this review, I've just completed Chapter I of the game, and I'm having a blast with it. If you're on the fence about how the 2D mechanics have translated in to 3D, do not worry, they're 100% better than they were back in the day. I remember the original feeling much clunkier and slower compared to Secret of Mana on the SNES but they've smoothed out all of the combat, everything is very free flowing and feels incredibly natural for an action RPG title like this.There's plenty of new customization like allocating stat points, and equipping passive skills which I don't think was in the original game, but I could be wrong... regardless, it feels good. You can respec your characters for a fee at a fortune teller a bit later in Chapter I and throughout the rest of the game so it's fairly casual in that regard. I don't believe anything is missible either, there are these tiny cactus guys you have to find, 50 of them total, but guides are up for them and they're all fairly obvious and out in the open if you just do some looking around. The game is structured fairly linear at first but eventually you'll get a dragon to ride on so you can explore past areas again at the end game.There's new content added on the game as well as a final 4th character class to upgrade to for post game content. The game has a new seed system where you can upgrade a flower pot in the Inn to level 5 and it will increase the drop rates of seeds. You can find these seeds just grinding enemies and planting them, they instantly flourish and give you a random item. Later on you need to find ??? Seeds to find class change items to get your 3rd class change.It's very much RPGish... so if you're looking to grind XP, Item Drops and Money then this is the game for you, it's very old school in that regard and it's a literal 1:1 remake with some added features that only enhance the game, nothing has been taken away from the original, only added.I love Secret of Mana and I'm ashamed with what Square Enix did to it with the crappy ios looking remake they made a little while ago. They've done a complete 180 with the sequel and gave us fans what we expected from a Secret of Mana remake with Trials of Mana. Even with what little time I've spent with it, I can tell I'm going to enjoy this ride all the way through, it feels fresh, fun and it was money well spent... this game has hundreds of hours of content and replayability. There's even a NG+ mode where you can keep ALL of your items, so anything you've grinded in previous playthroughs, you won't have to grind again! Just equip end game gear on fresh level 1 characters to experience the game all over again with different party configurations until you have all the best possible gear for every character.I give this game a solid 9 / 10. It's not perfect by any means, nothing is, the English voice acting for some of the characters is pretty terrible but it's something to be expected when a Japanese game is localized to Westerners but the game play and mechanics are solid. THIS IS HOW YOU DO A REMAKE!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros - Great flow, smooth combat, excellent soundtrack.Cons - English voice acting is mostly terrible. Camera during combat can be janky. Quite easy.This game is proof that Square Enix actually DOES know how to properly, faithfully remake a game, when the right people are in charge.I did play through the original version of this game using a fansub patch many years ago, and I have to say that nearly everything about this remake impressed me. Voice ActingI can't really speak to the quality of the Japanese voice acting, but the English voice acting is really quite bad. Most of it is just mediocre, but characters speak in stilted sentences with cardboard inflections. Kevin has a weird, broken sentence structure that makes him sound like he has social anxiety issues, Reisz has no personality, Charlotte is hunting wascally wabbits, and the others are overacted. One of the villains has weird volume issues where she's alternately screaming into the mic and impossible to hear, and the light spirit Lumina sounds like somebody put a quarter into a slot they found on tumblr and just used whatever fell out the bottom.Ultimately I decided to stick it out and play through in English, but if this bothers you, at least you can switch the voice work to Japanese and put the subtitles in English. CombatThe combat really feels very good, with a weak/strong combo attack system, with jumping and dodging. The combat isn't nearly as in-depth as something like Bayonetta, for example, but the flow of the combat felt similar, and my hours spent fighting in that game very neatly translated to me just crushing the combat here. At least that's what I like to think. The other very real possibility is that the difficulty of the game is overstated. I played on the hardest difficulty right out of the gate, and at no point did I break a sweat or game over, until I tried fighting an optional superboss near the end of the game. I always had tons of healing items, even without ever buying any, and even without access to healing magic for most of the game. (I played the all boys party which is very light on magic access)Boss fights are just the right length, forcing you to learn to deal with the boss's moves, but not to the point where you start getting tired of it. Audio / VisualThe game looks exactly the way you would expect a Seiken Densetsu title to look. Iconic designs are all present and easily recognisable. The new outfits for the characters are all style-consistent and feel like they fit. Sound effects get the job done without being really noticed, but again, classic sounds for menus, item acquisitions, and level ups are all there and super nostalgic. Music is all remastered and excellent, but the original music is still available in the options menu. Overall I feel like my gripes with the game are minor. I had a blast playing it, and I'm well into my second playthrough. If only all their other remakes were this faithful.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Trials of Mana (2020) is one of my favorite RPGs of all time. It's incredibly underrated. I love everything about it. Visually it's one of the most artistically beautiful looking games I've ever played. It's just so good to look at. I cannot count the number of times I've taken screenshots while playing it. Characters look awesome, bosses look awesome, the backdrops look awesome. I love the OST. I listen to tracks even when I'm not playing the game. The gameplay is also amazing. I generally don't like games with real-time combat that has AI controlled companions, but, they're fine here. On a first time playthrough you're never going to lose a fight because of something they did. On new game+, on hardest difficulty, they're next to useless because they literally get one-shot. But that mode, like a Dark Souls game, is all about proper timing, avoiding boss attacks, and attacking when the time is right. It was a challenge but super fun and rewarding. What I really love about ToM's combat is how rewarding it is for proper play. If you end a fight without taking any damage, or defeat all the enemies in a short amount of time, you're given extra experience points. So it constantly encourages you to perfect your play. Another thing I love is the strategy outside of combat. Depending on how you level up a character determines what magic, abilities, and passive they get. So a lot of thought goes into what's best for each character. Something else to talk about is the story. On my first playthrough the characters I chose were Angela, Riesz, and Charlotte. Each one of them have incredible backstories. At the very start of the game before you've even really gotten to know these characters, if their backstories don't make you cry you don't have a soul. Each one of them will wrench your heart. And it's not just the start either, there are many high points like that throughout the story. The only negative thing I have to say about ToM is that I wish on the hardest, new game+ difficultly, that there were added end-game shopkeepers who sold expensive rare items. Because you will get to a point where you have tons of gold and nothing to spend it on. And it's a bit of a grind if you want to min-max your characters. To conclude ToM is excellent. There is lots of replayability between the different game modes, starting characters, and achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: A really good remake of a SNES RPG that I remember playing the fan-translated ROM of a long time ago.Has six protagonists each with their own reason for setting out on a journey to save the world, and three villains that must be stopped. Depending on who you select as your primary protagonist (whoever you pick first when starting a new game basically) will depend on which plot threads are focused on the most, and ultimately who the main villain will be.This means that you need to play the game at least three times to see all the main villains, but if you want the full story experience you'll have to play through with each of the six characters as your primary protagonist.Good hack-and-slash combat, lots of cool abilities/spells unique to each character, and a unique class system that allows you to prestige characters down the path of "Light" and "Dark" to build them for either defense or offense respectively. Or you can do a mix of both, as Ninja Master for Hawkeye is probably my favorite class.My only real complaint is I think some parts of the game are too easy, even on Hard mode, but I think they've patched in another difficulty mode since then so I might be due for another playthrough to test it out!Highly recommend to RPG fans new and old.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review with tears in my eyes.Don't get me wrong, the game's story and voice acting and anything that's not the core combat loop sucks, and you NEED to download the difficulty mod.But I thought that being a mid-30s adult, cynical and jaded now that I understand how the world works, and constantly burdened with real life problems, had completely managed to rob me of that childlike wonderment I had towards RPGs. For years I tried to just 'lose myself' for hours on end like I did as a wide-eyed kid in pajamas playing Final Fantasy for the first time - and nothing ever worked.This game brings me right back there. Today, I get to be ten years old again.

_childDocuments_.review: Read Full Review Here: For those of you who are unfamiliar with Seiken Densetsu 3, it is a somewhat unique JRPG for its time as it allows you to choose your own path through the story by selecting a protagonist of your choosing from 6 different characters. Because of this, Trials Of Mana’s story feels rather shallow a lot of the time due to the fact that it has so many possible character combinations that telling a complex narrative would be difficult. Instead you are given an introduction to your character of choice and are sent on a mission to hunt down a bunch of plot devices to, I don’t know… save the world? Put simply, you’ve seen it all before, in a way you could argue that Trials Of Mana is the Dragon Quest XI of the Action RPG side of things in the sense that it is a modern adaptation of a classic style RPG so if you’re looking for something fresh in the narrative department, Trials Of Mana may disappoint you.While it may not be as polished as the modern YS games, Trials Of Mana’s combat feels strikingly similar to modern YS but with a little bit of Star Ocean Integrity And Faithlessness sprinkled in there. If you’re familiar with any of those games then you will feel right at home with this combat system. Each character comes with both strong and fast attacks that can be used together to form a combo, much like in the Dynasty Warriors games. Unfortunately however, the combos can only be unlocked via class change and initially you are stuck with only a single combo attack which can make the combat feel a little too simplistic at first but if you managed to stomach the original game’s combat then this shouldn’t be too much of an issue for you. On top of all this you can do pretty much everything you can do in YS VIII aside from the flash maneuvers and the extra skill. What this means is that you can jump, dodge and perform special attacks by holding down a button and pressing the corresponding face button, these attacks consume the CS gauge which can only be filled up by collecting crystals left by the enemy upon being hit or defeated so in a way it’s similar to the way SP acquisition works in YS VIII. There is also a charged attack that you can perform which is useful for breaking the enemy’s guard as some enemies are shielded, decreasing damage dealt to them by fast attacks. Put simply, the combat isn’t particularly groundbreaking but it’s definitely a lot of fun if you are into simplistic action.While it’s difficult to find many faults in the combat, there’s one thing in particular that I believe could be improved upon and that would be the game’s AI. Now don’t get me wrong, the AI aren’t the worst out there as they do seem to dodge attacks every now and again but there have been many times where AI controlled characters end up walking into enemy attacks or just stand in them. While this does make sense considering the fact that healing magic is involved in the game, it still feels like you’re babysitting the AI at times, throwing heals at them constantly each time they screw up. Now of course Trials Of Mana isn’t the only action RPG that suffers from this issue, it’s been an issue with the genre entirely but since YS SEVEN managed to circumvent this issue, I don’t see why other games can’t follow in its footsteps. There were many times playing Trails Of Mana where I thought I was playing YS VIII and I was shocked by how often my AI companions were receiving tons of damage and dying. Perhaps I’ve just been spoiled by the modern YS games I don’t know but I still think that this should become a standard that all action RPG’s need to follow as babysitting idiotic AI companions is never fun.What I did find fun however is the game’s character management which completely blows YS out of the water by comparison. I found that the biggest appeal of this game lies in the class system, though I’d argue the class system is a double edged sword mainly due to the way the game handles the class change system. What I can say however is that most of the classes feel really well balanced and they each come with unique skills which can be handy for fine tuning each of the character’s traits to suit the player’s play style. Each character has a light and dark path which dictates which classes they get at class 4. Once on either the light or dark path, players lose access to classes on the opposite path so the first class change is really important. Fortunately changing your class for the first time is a simple task as you merely have to be level 18 and interact with a mana stone to change your class. The issues with the class system become more apparrent when you are going for the more advanced classes later on as you will have to acquire unique items to learn each class. Now while there are treasure chests that do give you these items, by the time you have gotten all of them, you’ll have just about reached the end game, therefore if you want to experience those classes early you will have to grind… a lot and pray to the RNG gods that you get an item which gives you the class you want because the class items are all randomly generated by a seed. If you receive a class item from a seed for a class you don’t want then too bad, you have to find another. While farming these seeds may be easy enough later on in the game, farming them early can be a real pain in the ass, especially if you didn’t pick Hawkeye for his drop chance bonus skill since the drop chance for these items isn’t particularly high. This is without a doubt the most agonizing part of the class system and honestly I wish they made the class system more straightforward. I get not wanting players to gain access to powerful classes too early but relying on RNG to delay the player’s class progression is not the best approach if you ask me, especially when it’s the game’s most distinguishable feature.On top of the class system, with each level up you acquire training points which can be used to learn new abilities and increase stats. Each ability and stat increase is separated between attributes, though these are not the attributes tied directly to the character’s base stats so if you’re playing as a melee fighter, don’t think that stats like intelligence are useless as it may come with some handy abilities. I found this system to be executed a lot better than the game’s class system as it is not only well balanced but it makes leveling up feel a lot more rewarding. In a way it kind of gives me Star Ocean vibes and that’s never a bad thing. I’d argue that out of all the features, this is the one that stands out to me the most and while it might not be as involving as Star Ocean’s systems, it still has the same appeal that made those systems so engaging to begin with. The only downside to this is that each attribute is capped by the character’s class level and the ability slots required to equip the skills are also capped depending on the class. So the class system governs all of the character growth and this means that there will be times where you may have to stockpile skill points until you reach a new class just so you can develop a character’s stats further if you don’t want to learn certain abilities. On the plus side however, upon reaching max level, you will have enough training points to max out all attributes but depending on your class will depend on what abilities will be available to you in each attribute, so you won’t be able to learn everything in one playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge Secret of Mana fan, I was very excited for this. I did play Seiken Densetsu 3 back in the day with a fan translated rom and I loved it. Personally, this is a nice sequel to Secret of Mana (story unrelated) and I think it's better as well. The graphics have been updated and are pretty good quality although they do lack the charm of the original sprites.I think for any Secret of Mana fan, this is a must have. Absolute wonderful JRPG from back in the day which I never understood why they didn't release it here.Criticisms:- the game is not challenging, even on hard. That may or may not be a problem for you, I still enjoyed it, I have finished it 3 times, but don't expect it to be hard.- new game+ doesn't scale. This is a mix, because it is kind of fun to just smash a Benevodon in 10 seconds. But at the same time, it also means any second or third play through will be even easier.- I appreciate the addition of Anise, but the endless dungeon grind that it turns into is kind of where I think a lot of these games fell flat in later sequels. The towns and story provide much needed break up of the monotony of a dungeon grind. However, Anise is a slight challenge the first time you face her, I guess unless you are a much higher level than when I got to her. I also wish she gave you exp for killing her.- You can't get every costume for a character. I really wish that you could reset class and keep any costumes you had gained. I know it's a little thing, but I would have wanted to do that.Overall:This is a fantastic game and a great remake. I enjoyed playing it and will likely play through it one last time before uninstalling it. Maybe I'll play it again some day, who knows. But definitely a classic and worth it for Mana fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I did not play the original.I have finished one run through the story and postgame I can safely say that this is a good mid-quality action JRPG at a mid-budget price.Took me 22 hours to complete the main story with another 5 hours spent cleaning up some collectibles and finishing post-game.tl;dr: If you're on the fence then wait for a sale. It's a solid enough game. If you like this kind of action JRPG then check out the Ys series especially Ys VIII which now has a good Steam port after the latest massive update.Good: - PC port is barebones but solid. You can edit UE4 config files but you need to re-pak them with a tool. A bit annoying, but it works. Highly recommend searching the forums to just grab a preexisting config to increase draw distance. - Action combat and class system offers gameplay diversity and some fun build optimization. By the end of the game I was very overpowered. Maybe the game balance is just way off! - Simple, classic JRPG with a fairly thin and simple story and some overworld traversal. Overall a good time. - Japanese voice acting is fine and what I would classify as "standard anime." - Lots of replayability since you only use 3 out of 6 possible characters in one run and your main character determines one of 3 ending paths.Not good: - English voice acting is bad. I couldn't stand it for more than a few minutes. - Charlotte is very annoying. I don't think I'll ever finish all the achievements because I can't deal with her being in my party - Game is really easy overall with some difficulty spikes with some bosses, mainly because I found the camera to be really bad in some arenas for flying and highly mobile enemies - Contrasting what I said in the "Good" section: the story is bland and rather boring. Some characters have better motivations than others, but don't play this game looking for a complex plot with twists and turns. It's really basic "defeat the darkness" stuff from beginning to end. There was potential for interesting interactions between the factions competing to take over the world but it never really went anywhere.Other: - Endgame is pretty barebones even with the extra postgame content that they added. Once you reach mid level 70 it's very easy without much left to do. Not really any reason to try to get maxed and farm all the best equipment. I beat the "super boss" handily at level 75 with a half decently geared party.

_childDocuments_.review: A great soundtrack is necessary in any tolerable JRPG, Trials does that and more. Sometimes I would grind certain areas just to breakdown whatever I'd been hearing onto guitar, other times just because it was that relaxing, top notch compositions here. The switchable party system allows for grinding to become much more enjoyable than most grind heavy RPG's, also boss fights of which there are PLENTY can become very interesting and useful thanks to the party/battle system. Trials leans more on the side of a linear open world if that makes any sense, everything will open up further into the game as you unlock ocean and then air travel. There are multiple class systems to unlock with plenty of spells and physical abilities to boot, there are also a number of endings to be had determined by the composition of your party. I cant say much about the voice acting other than it was great subbed, even though the least tolerable character of the games speech impediment carried over to the subs >>. I really wish there were mini games throughout, maybe scattered among some villages but whatever ^^ It was overall fun. Finally got to let loose as a caster for a change.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, but the extras added make the characters OP.First, the pros:1. The feel of the game is a lot like the original.  The class changes, the skills added, and the different characters give this game a high replay value. The environment is pretty well done.  It's nice how they changed a 2d world and made it 3d, and yet still managed to make it feel like the old.If you want nostalgia, this is the game for you.  But even if you are curious, this is a game worth playing through at least once.That's all I can think of, actually.The cons:1. When you learn the skills, the characters are too OP save a couple of boss fights. This makes the game too easy, even on Hard mode. Perhaps being unable to predict the enemies' attacks would make it more challenging and enjoyable for some. Maybe that should be an option for ultra Hard mode?2.  The voice acting can get annoying. The English version is a little lackluster. As many have complained, Charlotte's voice is not pleasant. The Japanese voice acting is better IMO, but as you defeat enemies, there is always a dialogue that the characters say.  Repeating that dialogue over and over can get annoying.  Also, in cutscenes, I find myself skipping their dialogues as well. Perhaps it's because I already know the storyline.3.  Dashing/runningMaybe it's my computer, but the speed for dashing is no faster than regular running.  Granted, my device clocks this game around 58 FPS.  Dashing while riding the beasts, however, is more noticable. Over all, it's better than the Secret of Mana remake.  If you are into casual gaming, then this game is probably for you.  It might be worth waiting to see if it's on sale. Despite my cons being more than the pros, I still recommend this title because of the classic that SD3 was in the 90's, and most people in the States could not play it unless they got their hands on a translated rom.

_childDocuments_.review: --I'm a big fan of Secret of Mana (SNES). Played it to death when I was 13-14 years old. I played the fan translation of Seiken Densetsu 3 many, many years ago.----If you have money to burn, go ahead and buy this game. If you're saving your money, wait for a sale.--Gameplay - ExcellentArt - GoodMusic - GoodStory - OkayCharacters - PoorVoice acting - BadGameplay - The best thing I can say about the game. The action is smooth and the game largely stays out of your way and doesn't make you wait on it. Battle isn't really complex or nuanced though.Art - There's nothing here that makes me say, "WOW", but there's nothing bad enough to take me out of the experience. Some model clipping, but that's it.Music - A straightforward reproduction of the original score. Not, "meh", but good.Story - A straight copy-paste of the original, which is not a surprise. I think the story suffers from trying to do too much at once. I played the original years ago and I couldn't remember what happened in it if you paid me. The plot - "Mana is fading from the world. Load up with your party and save it." It's pretty basic.Characters - The reason why I think the plot suffers. The characters are more vessels for their abilities. Each character has an origin story and a resolution, but there's no significant development in-between. Like a bread sandwich. The idea that any of them can be "The Hero/Heroine" and the modularity of the plot didn't leave much room for the characters to really be themselves.Voice acting - My party was Duran, Reise and Charlotte. I don't have an issue with Duran and Reise, they're not great but not bad. Charlotte is written with a very uncomfortable lisp, it's painful to listen to. Various other side and supporting character range from bland to goofy-bad. If you manged to read this far, thanks, and do yourself a favor and switch the game to Japanese voice acting with English subtitles.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much has everything you could ask for from a SNES remake. Usually remakes fall flat in some aspect like its too different or not different enough. They often butcher things people loved about the original like the music being completely different or new graphics ripping the SOUL right out of it. Sometimes they change story elements and character interactions that made the original so memorable. With Trials of Mana you don't have to worry about any of that. There is so much that is different about the remake but everything that is different is either additional content or MUCH needed improvements to the original. Despite all these differences the game retains so much from the original like overall pacing, memorable character interactions, and NPC placements/dialogue. The music is very similar to the original but different enough to give it that modern feel. Pretty much every track has been perfect and I'm really looking forward to some later tracks. The game play is just better. I played all 3 routes of the original right before jumping into the remake and let me tell you the original is a broken mess. Its still enjoyable of course but I'll say there is nothing that I miss about the original in terms of game play.My only real complaint is with the localization. There's some minor questionable name changes and then there's Charlotte. Her dialogue is borderline unreadable. I don't even want to think about what she sounds like with the dub. There's no way her speech is supposed to be that difficult to understand. I get wanting to add a little flavor to the text but cmon its clearly overboard. I'm thankful for dual audio at least.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid remake of the SNES classic Seiken Densetsu 3 that was never officially released in the west.  Trials of Mana is a fun but fairly short action RPG with a few problems that keep it from being great.  This game gets my recommendation BUT I would say it's only worth its current full retail price of $50 if you played and enjoyed Seiken Densetsu 3 and have some nostalgia for it.  If not it would probably be best to wait for a sale.  I feel that I should also mention that this remake is far superior to the Secret of Mana remake we got in 2018.- Fun (but repetitive) combat.  There are simple combos that you slowly unlock more of as you progress, as well as a dodge roll.  The aoe of enemy spells and major attacks are highlighted on the ground giving you time to properly react and avoid them, rewarding you for paying attention and not just button mashing.  The combat has much more of an fast paced action feel to it compared to Seiken Densetsu 3.  Casting spells no longer pauses everything else while the animation plays out.- A lot of party customization. You choose between of 3 of the 6 available characters at the start of a playthrough, and develop them by allocating training points between different stats to unlock different spells and abilities.  Eventually you upgrade classes twice, plus a bonus third class change in the post game, choosing between a light and dark path for each character which can vastly change their role in combat.- 3 different possible final dungeons and final bosses depending on who you picked as your main character to give incentive for multiple playthroughs.  The overarching story does remain largely the same however.- Minimal puzzle solving and platforming.  Progressing forward or exploring different areas for hidden treasures is rarely slowed down by annoying and pointless puzzles.  The few locations that do have puzzles are very simple.- Grinding.  You don't really need to do it at all unless you want an edge meaning that you can keep moving forward and making progress instead of getting stuck in one area fighting the same enemies over and over.- You can choose between the original SNES sound track as well as the remaster.- Story and character development.  It's overall generic and mostly forgettable but it does well enough to get the job done.- Character and class balance.  Although all characters and classes are viable there is most certainly a meta and certain characters/classes and combinations of them are far superior to others.- Difficulty.  It's pretty easy to get OP near the end of the adventure if you know how to the point where even the hard difficulty setting is a breeze.- Graphics.  The art style is neat and colorful but this is no AAA title so don't expect highly detailed textures.- Game length.  I clocked in around 25 hours for one playthrough including the post game stuff.  - PC specific graphical settings.  There's not much.  Resolution, display mode, and max frame rate are the only things you can adjust.- Texture and object pop in.  You will notice this from time to time as this game was clearly optimized for consoles and there is no setting to adjust draw distance.- Voice acting.  Depending on the character the English voices range from passable to horrible.  I haven't tried the Japanese voices but they may be better.- Post game content.  The new post game content added to this remake could have been so much better.  The 3rd class change for our party is neat but the bonus dungeon that we get to use it for is just one big slog through re-skinned areas from the main game with some higher level enemies.  There aren't even any higher level boss re-fights, just regular mobs until the new boss at the end.  New game plus also should have had an additional "hard mode" or something of the sort with high level enemies that you could choose if you were bringing characters from a prior playthrough that were already leveled and geared up.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I can't judge how this game will feel to someone playing it without the nostalgia of the original, or games from that era, but for those who did play the original this game is an easy recommendation. For those who haven't played games from its era, it still seems well done enough to be worth your time.In terms of the layout of the game, it's an almost exact copy of the original game, which I don't necessarily think was the greatest approach. But for what it is (probably a labour of love of someone who really wanted to get it made, and wouldn't be given a giant budget), it's as good as you can reasonably expect/well done.Some highlights:- Updated/improved combat, stat system, etc.- Options to choose between the original music and updated (SNES was limited) versions though the original sounds wrong to me, and seems focused on one channel.- Additional/new content not in the original game, including a new final class change.- Denuvo was removed eventually. Anyone who says it didn't negatively affect performance is flat out wrong. A common symptom is worse frame pacing.Some lowlights:- No multiplayer. This is a major bummer, even the original had multiplayer (local obviously). This is a game that, despite being great single player, is even better with friends.- Voice acting which will make your ears bleed. It's unreal how bad it is, just a random player reading the lines would sound more believable/realistic, and less like a broken robot struggling to read a piece of paper.- Follows the Japanese tradition of putting arbitrary and extremely infuriating limits on setting options... of course including frame rate. In this case it's less frustrating 120, which is always derpy to see as 144 & 165Hz became standard half a decade ago for high refresh panels. As for the rest of the options, there are very few things you can adjust, and unlike other UE4 games, you can't just adjust the settings through the ini files. This game has the UE4 settings files locked away in archived/packed files, so you have to essentially mod the game/those files to fully be able to customize the settings as you want.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I've done it, game complete.The final boss was... well, I didn't think it WAS a final boss.He died as fast as all other bosses and didn't do much different either. That's a minus for sure.Kevin's ending also sucked with the line-up of team members I had.Now, after finishing the first playthrough, all I can say is.... I'd rate it a 9/10. I can't blame the Remake for the story, that's something the original ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up.I was 99% sure that Unreal Engine would fail me and that I would end up going out of bounds through some glitch, but the game consistently kept me away and safe from any glitches apart from a minor model issue.I haven't fled from a single battle, which is a huge accomplishment for the game devs because I ALWAYS start fleeing battles 50% into the game, whether for laziness or boredom or whatever, but I never was once bored by the battles. It could be entirely because of how much fun it was to play Kevin, maybe it's gonna suck next playthrough when I don't have him on my team anymore, who knows - for this playthrough though in particular, I'm rating the game a clean 9/10. Were I to take all the nonsense story elements into account, I would drop it to a 7/10 clean.If I was being more fair I'd probably even say I'd rate the game 8/10 as it is now. The AI in this game has driven me mad multiple times because the Strategy tab is really simplistic and useless in boss battles. Bosses have AoE attacks that deal a ludicrous amount of damage and you can't avoid your teammates tanking damage because there is no strategy or in-battle command to make them take distance and prioritize defense.Note to self and others at that point: Never make a Caster the main character of your playthrough.Angela was so full of flaws and errors that the game could've handled better.Her gameplay builds up on three types of attacks: Melee Attacks, Magic Attacks, Class Strike Attacks. Because of how Angela is coded to work, her magic doesn't generate even a tenth of the Class Strike Gauge other characters generate. Due to this, if you actively use Angela you'll find that your team is actively performing worse. As a caster, her melee attacks are generally very weak and early into the game you'll run out of Magic very, VERY fast. Her only advantage is that later into the game she'll turn into an actual maniac that can just spam magic and go out of all fights with zero damage received. Looking back on this game, that's the best advice I can give to you: Do not use Charlotte or Angela as your lead character. They're generally the weakest links of your team and better off serving as your sidekick because they can heal and cast while you're playing a character like Kevin, Duran, Hawk, etc who can generate Class Strike Gauge more reliably.

_childDocuments_.review: Trials of Mana is a remake of Super Famicoms Seiken Densetsu 3 released in 1995. This version of the game would never truly be realized until The Collection of Mana which was released exclusively on the Nintendo Switch in 2019 (If you're into retro games it's kind of a banger). In a surprising turn of events, Trials of Mana was rebuilt from the ground up in all of its 3D glory, and honestly, the game doesn't disappoint. At first, I didn't care much for ToM and just wanted to see how it withstood the test of time mechanically. What I ended up finding though, was something a lot more fun in the long run.    At its core, ToM is a very simple neatly wrapped Hack and Slash RPG with a nice UI to pull everything together. All six characters reprise their roles each with their own class evolution achieved through leveling and allocating stats. Being able to re-allocate stat points by visiting a certain town gives you a lot of ways to build and experiment with group composition. After a bit of a slow start, It's fun, it flows very well, and experimenting with chain abilities and class combos can be super rewarding. Some of them fall off hard, but it doesn't mean they aren't useful in other comps and that you can't have fun with them. Ideally, you're stuck with the three characters you chose following their specific storylines until the game is over. During the play-through, there are differences in interaction and story depending on who you have chosen as well as a few surprises here and there.    As someone who loves the grind, I found a lot of joy especially after completing the game. After playing on hard (I would say about 20 hours at most minus grinding, maybe?) and after finishing the side stuff, you can NG+ and pump up the difficulty. So not only do you have a new cast, but you keep all of your items and chain abilities while fighting harder mobs. Then, once you have done all six you can take on No Future mode and enhance them even further provided you enjoyed the gameplay. With beautiful design, awesome music, and a wealth of options you can truly dive into the world! ToM gives you plenty of reason to stay in the world and soak it in and for that, I love what they did with the remake and highly recommend it.The Voice acting is kind of poor at least to me, but switching it to Japanese fixes the mood. It's not for everybody, but it definitely has all of the tools that it needs in order to be a complete gaming experience which is more than I can say for a lot of developers. The biggest downside is some might find it too simplistic, but there is definitely depth there if you're willing to give it a shot.As someone who loved and adored Secret of Mana growing up, it's great to see its unseen sequel take the spotlight with such nice replay value.Thank you for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure people who played the original SNES game were blown away by how faithful this remake is, and there's certainly a lot to love in here as an old-school rpg.  However, the system of choosing 3 characters for your party out of a possible 6 is a real double-edged sword.  Does it add replayability?  Yes.  Does it also mean that half of the cast and their story content is locked behind New Game+?  Yes, which is annoying.  Maybe I'll come back and see what the other two stories are like someday, but for now, I don't want to replay 90% of the game for the 10% that's different this time.But what really matters is that this will be remembered as the game with the character who talks entirely in UwU-speak.

_childDocuments_.review: Story and character development are nonexsistent, dialogues are cringy. Well it's a 25+ year old game, can't expect much.Other than that, there's a lot of good things about this remake as an action RPG.Actions are quick and responsive, the dodging mechanic allows me to take on higher level boss without problems. The indicator of enemy attacking path is a well thought design, because when you're going 1 on 5, you're not going to react to all 5 attack from different directions. And having the enemy attack path showing gives you time to dodge and react to them.  This is a well paced game, I was playing on hard difficulty and rarely needed to grind for levels. Enemy levels are always within 2 levels of me as I advance the story. The game just makes you keep on moving.The main game took me about 27 hours and post game in 4 hours. But this is me going over every corner of the maps hunting for chests and cactus. So for casual players, this could be a 25 hours or less game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The game is good, but i really wish it had multiplayer. if you havent ever played trials of mana (Seikendensetsu 3) 8/10 amazing story its a literal crime this game was never officially ported to the US, If you are a returning Seikendensetsu 3 fan (6/10) shiny new graphics, better normal systems, some things you probably really want are missing for sure though.Square really did a better job on this than any other of the recent remakes, the new system is much more optimized and plays much smoother than the original, im still not so sure on how i feel about the changes to the level up and class system but its not the worst. The Art is beautiful and well upgraded .... still tells the same amazing story and it still has that chrono trigger feel where you want to beat it from each characters perspective ..... new bigger inventory is fantastic .... it is so long into the game before you get a healing spell that being able to hold more healing items really prevents the game from bogging down, and allows you to really push yourself for low leveling content without having to save scum to get it done. You never feel compelled to have to stop and level grind anywhere near as much as the old school titles.Cons: The game by default is kinda easy outside your own ally AI being derpy as hell .... like standing in 3 second charge up moves that a single press of dodge will avoid derpy. The sliders to adjust their AI doesn't work at all in most cases i could never get the AI to use Angela's CA, i frequently had to toggle to her to cast magic on bosses despite her being at full MP and only supposed to hold MP at 25% and she is the closest thing the game has to a blasty wizard.The new level up and class system is ... not my favorite, a lot of the point buy equipable passives seem nearly useless leading to a lot of illusion of choice, and pushing for raw stats is almost always better.My biggest gripe : NO MULTIPLAYER ..... Its a mana game guys ..... WTF, No local co-op, no ethernet, no online, nothing ... nada ... the SNES version had multiplayer ... its 2020, the tales series is dumping all over you with fun game features wake up SQEENIX remember how to game dev before you become a fossil.

_childDocuments_.review: I did have some nostalgia for the game and its characters. Many felt like seeing old friends again. The overall story lacks a lot of emotional depth that could be found in other contemporary SNES RPGs, but it was enough to keep me going. What really won me over were the simple to learn battle mechanics that are used in some pretty tight-knit fights. The Normal and Hard difficulty aren't very difficult, so I'd recommend starting w/ Hard. I found Expert to be tedious, as bosses just become damage sponges. On the other hard, No Future run was the most fun. Bosses aren't spongy, but mistakes are more costly.The character you choose to control will largely determine how the game feels.  From my experience, the game really only has a few different gameplay flows: 1) long animation, multihit melee ie. Kevin, Hawkeye. Useful for triggering effects2) short animation melee ex. Duran, Riesz. Easier to find windows of opportunity3) spellcaster ie. Angela, Rogue Hawkeye. Easy to position4) focus on building up and abusing invincibility frames ex. Divine Fist Kevin, Ninja Master Hawkeye. I found this playstyle to be somewhat unsatisfactory, as the characters go into long animations, which take away from the moment to moment decisions in the game.Normally you want to control the character you are dealing the most damage with. However, No Future has an additional gameplay style available: focus on dodging while commanding a spellcaster to deal with the enemies.I would definitely recommend looking up and planning your runs beforehand. I ended up doing 2 Hard runs, 1 Expert Run, and 1 No Future Run, but I think it's possible to limit it to 3 if you want to experience each difficulty with smart decisions beforehand. I'll write some notes on how to do it below, so you can avoid spoilers.=== SPOILERS (in the form of game tips) ===Things I wish I'd known before I started:- This is mostly an easy game. If you want difficult boss fights, choose Angela, Duran, and Kevin. I intentionally picked these 3 for my No Future run. My favorite fight of the whole game was Duran's class 4.- Cacti sightings persist through runs, so if you get all 50 in your first run, you don't have to worry about it in later runs- Advanced weapons are important on later runs. Pedda offers the best Class 1 and 2 weapons, so it's important to get these for subsequent runs. However keep in but these only matter for the characters you intend to do lots of damage with either attacks or magic.- Rogue Hawkeye is the exception as the only way to increase his damage is by increasing luck or reducing enemy defense.- Advance armor is only useful for Expert.- Most runs after your first one will probably look more like boss rushes, so abilities that deal with regular enemies don't matter as much other than for farming items or leveling up to hit the thresholds for class changes.- You can fight Anise four times total for more rewards. It's worth doing it your first playthrough to get it done with.- To fight all bosses and see all stories in the game, you need to do 3 playthroughs.- Characters have chain abilities, which they can share with other characters. Chain abilities that have been unlocked by a character from a previous playthrough can be used, as long as you didn't select that character for your current playthrough.- It is easy to use Goddess Scales to reset a character before your next playthrough, so just choose what you want to play for this playthrough and change them right before you select New Game+.- You will have your first two characters (and also Charlotte if she's your third) before your first boss fight.- Any end game chain abilities (abilities after defeating Zable Fahr) will be blocked in No Future- Class change items provide some pretty sweet battle effects. They are worth using alongside the Mana Miracle chain ability gained by defeating Anise.- Get the Mana Bracelet and Mana Ring from Anise's dungeons each playthrough. They are the best accessory in the game.--- Doing Hard -> Expert -> No Future ---This covers a possible way to do all three storylines and experience all difficulties (other than Normal). Feel free to pick either of the story's pair as your main character. I do recommend you make sure that you have starting weapons for one of the first two characters in your Expert or No Future run. It's easiest to explain my party selection reasoning backwards:As mentioned, I aimed for a No Future run of Angela, Duran, and Kevin for the boss fights. I recommend either (Archmage, Edelfrei, Divine Fist) or (Archmage, Liege, Fatal Fist) depending on whether you like how Duran or Kevin feels. Or feel free to not use a Divine Fist or Liege if you're good enough at avoiding damage to not need healing. This covers Angela and Duran's story.For the Expert run, select Hawkeye, Riesz, Duran. The community consensus is that the strongest character is Rogue Hawkeye. After playing it, is was pretty smooth sailing. This relies on a few powerful New Game+ Chain abilities from your previous run to make it palatable. Enemies do a lot of damage here, and unlike No Future, your allies will die. I'd recommend using Fenrir Knight Riesz, as she can debuff enemies permanently. Finally you need a tank. Though optimally it would be Warlock Charlotte, you won't have the chain abilities necessary for her if you follow my 3 playthrough suggestions, so instead I'd recommend Liege Duran. You will rely on the Mana Miracle Chain Ability from Anise to be able to use Cup of Wishes, Kevin's Death Auth, Hawkeye's Wicked Dice (your main source of damage early), and Charlotte's Holy Bottle and Salt Bottle often in fights. This will also get you starting weapons for Duran in No Future. This covers Hawkeye and Riesz's story.Thus this leaves the first playthrough to set up everything. I recommend using Kevin, Charlotte, and Hawkeye. If you choose Kevin as your main, select Charlotte as your third, so you can have all three party members available for the first boss. Completing the game with Hawkeye and Charlotte will give you the ability to boost the Rogue's damage in the Expert playthrough and pass on a magic defense boost to Duran. Make sure to beat Anise 4 times, defeat the Black Rabite and get the Converter chain ability from the monsters on the volcano island for Angela in your No Future run. No class suggestions, as Hard mode should be easy enough. Make sure to switch Charlotte to her Light Class 4 for Miracle II, which can optionally make your more difficult runs a little easier. This covers Kevin and Charlotte's story.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game overall, a must-play if you like the Mana series. Game runs fantastically, never crashed once and it runs at 60FPS solidly even when my laptop is on silent mode, something which most other games can't claim. Be aware that the game only has resolution options for 720p, 1080p, and 4K and framerate options for 30, 60 and 120Hz. Gameplay is simple and honestly pretty repetitive, but not trivial to the point of feeling like a grind. There is enough variation in enemies that you need to change up how you deal with them fairly often, preventing the game from feeling stale. There are a LOT of gameplay styles and builds available so if you are the kind of person who likes character building this is a great game for it. When the game starts you choose 3 of 6 characters to use, and each character has 4 possible class configurations (but you can't easily switch classes to be careful), along with a lot of room for customization within each class. All 6 characters fill their roles well and I don't think you could go wrong with any team combination.The music is very good overall, with a few overly repetitive tracks here and there. There is an option to switch between the original SNES soundtrack and the remastered one at any time, which is really cool. IMO the original is better, it has more punch and conveys the mood of the game a little better, but the remade tracks have a little more going on. Both soundtracks feel natural for the game, so don't worry about the SNES tracks feeling out of place. If you are new to the series or if you aren't familiar with japanese games, this game is VERY anime. The plot is very straight forward and predictable, but still fun to experience. The story of the game changes slightly, as well as the final boss, depending on the characters you choose, allowing for 3 different stories/bosses. I will definitely laud the game for its replayability as you are guaranteed at least 2 unique playthroughs of the game, assuming you choose a totally different team of characters each time. There is also optional post-game content which met my expectations beautifully. I was hoping for a really long dungeon and some cool bosses and I got exactly that. There is also a NG+ option after you complete the post-game, allowing for a much quicker second playthrough.My main complaints with the game are that it is too easy and the AI is pretty awful. Definitely play the game on hard mode, and I'm not just saying that to be cool. Enemies can barely touch you on Normal mode or below, and can be dispatched with basically no effort. On Hard mode enemies and especially bosses hit much harder and force you to be at least a little bit careful. Even so, the game gives you SO MANY consumable items that it's virtually possible to run out, so you can save yourself even if you mess up. Some of the bosses can be a bit tough, so don't think that every part of the game is a cakewalk. I got a game over 3 times in my playthrough, and 2 of those times were from the optional super bosses. As for the AI, the player can only control one out of the three chosen characters, leaving the other two to be controlled by the AI. The AI is pretty decent at some things, especially at using magic because they know all the weaknesses, but is complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at other things like avoiding damage and actually attacking enemies. There are options to adjust how the AI behaves but they are too limited to make a big difference. Most of the time your AI allies will get absolutely trounced by bosses and you will have to resurrect them multiple times. This is a mixed bag, as they will take a lot of hits for you, but they will also force you to use a ton of consumable items to save them, meaning you might run out of items for youreself. Overall the bad AI isn't a deabreaker, I was able to complete the game just fine and it never felt like I was being worked against, it just felt like I was playing with two 6 year old kids who didn't really know what was going on. I really enjoyed this game and went back to play it again as soon as I finished my first playthrough. The character diversity is great and the number of build possibilities and team compositions is a theorycrafter's dream. When I was a kid, Seiken Densetsu 3 was this legendary game that never got a worldwide release and everyone who played a patched copy via emulation would sing it's praises and they were absolutely right. If you're not sure about this game, PLAY THE DEMO. This game has the most expansive demo I have ever seen. It's about 2 solid hours of gameplay and allows you to try out all 6 characters. There's no reason not to try it and it definitely sold me on this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Trials of Mana is a modern revival, a remake/remaster of the old Seiken Densetsu 3, only released in the Eastern lands in the era of the Super Nintendo. I was expecting it to happen for decades, and I'm so happy it's here now!tl;dr: That game is one of the best RPG's I ever played back then, and stays true to its roots in this new version, with a few extras.This new release changes many things starting from the old 2D sprite graphics going to 3D, and combat system stays relatively true to the original. It also features many improvements and additions which weren't possible in the SNES era.For the oldschool players this release will feel VERY easy, depending on how often you would play old ARPG's at the time. If you already know the story from the first release, you can expect a few added things in newgame+ like unlocked chain abilities, retained character levels and you get to try another story with another group, with the possibility to bring characters used before with their retained level to this new playthrough. It will make the game easier though, it's your choice.Once you understand the game system, it's all pretty simple, and all you have to do is choose the right moves and/or spells and spam the enemy. At certain points, your characters will evolve and change class from a pool of choices you make through the game. Also, I recommend you play it in the "No future" mode for an extra challenge. The rolling mechanic is an entirely new addition that further facilitates the game for new players.One important aspect of the game was left out, which was the multiplayer, I used to play with friends using the multitap adapter on the SNES console. It was incredibly fun and SquareEnix is not probably bringing it back for this release. Maybe things will change down the line, but don't hope for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I sit here and wonder why didn't the other Mana games get the same remake treatment as this one? It's fresh, it's fun, it's never boring or grindy, it's relaxing, isn't overcomplicated and convoluted, has a good straightforward story without plotholes and it looks stunning. Overall it's a beautiful game with a pleasant atmosphere (the world has that Ni No Kuni feel) and with pretty good replay value, almost feels too good to be a game made by Square Enix considering the disastruous ports they used us with in the last few years

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: definitely not worth full price, better pick it up on sale for 20 bucks (which is still a little too much imo). good game to give to a 8-10yo. if youre looking for a simple and lighthearted game then go ahead.story is mostly generic. introducing any kind of depth for a game from 15 years ago that has to accomodate a coherent story for 6 characters at the same time is just not possible. there isnt even a story around midgame, you just go into 7 different areas in any particular order and fight the boss in each one. i finished the story on hard difficulty in 21 hours while collecting most chests and all cactuses, and finished the postgame in an additional 3 hours. you can probably get 35 hours of playtime out of this game if you do a NG+ run with the other 3 characters you didnt pick.the combat feels fluid and nice. nothing complex but its a nicely executed and pretty solid system. the item usage has a good balance. the combat isnt easy enough to do completely without items and it is encouraged to use a lot of them since youll get a good number of them from chests. the only issue is that it feels unfair at times when the AI makes unreasonable decisions that hinder your ability to fight or straight up just dies.exploring the areas is mostly linear, most of the time its just a matter of seeing where you have to go and going the exact other direction to pick up a chest thats basically not hidden at all. the exploration aspect is taken out of the game once you unlock the ability to .skill progression is very spike heavy, all characters feel the same to play at the beginning of the game and you dont really feel like you improve your character at all until you unlock the class system about 8-10 hours into the game. the progression between classes is basically non-existant compared to the power spikes that classes give you. you do feel op at the end though once you unlock unlock class 3.the class system is interesting and allows for a lot of different playstyles, youll be happy with your characters no matter which one you pick. its just a shame that locking the second class behind a rng mechanic kinda ruins the midgame since you might struggle with a few bosses if you dont unlock the class you want for the character you need in time.the equipment system is very barebones. you basically dont pick up equipment on the field and instead have to rely on shops to buy the latest equipment (which is very affordable assuming you dont skip fights and collect everything on the way), or from good item seeds later on. equipment does not have any additional traits or effects (except for rings, which only have small effects like sleep immunity) and instead rely on stats only. the equipment system feels as spike heavy as the class system during the endgame, because your stats are going to increase by 50% at the point you can get equipment from good item seeds.there are some numbers about the game that are kind of hidden. knowing how much an attack buff/debuff affects you or the enemy is pretty important, yet is not explained anywhere (the value is 20% in case youre wondering). these 20% are pretty important to know, since it will decide whether you want to run additional abilities to boost that value on your buff/debuffers or even decide at the beginning of the game if you want to run a buff/debuffer after all. i understand the incentive of simplifying the game for a more comfortable experience, but it does hinder the decision making at times.the game feels very polished. menuing and combat feels fluid, everything looks pretty, tutorials explain the mechanics of the game pretty well and cutscenes are mostly motion tracked.soundtrack is meh. dont get me wrong, the tracks that you hear are very enjoyable (at first), though nothing memorable. what makes it meh is the very very limited selection of tracks, its going to feel like youre listening to the same 6 tracks over and over for the rest of the game.
