_childDocuments_.review: TL,DR: Very fun game and a nice update to a classicPro:- Updated for the current age without sacrificing the core experience (New Game+, voice over, seeing what one will gain from certain stat increases)- Updated 3D graphics that still stick to the original design- High replayability with three different end bosses and several possible parties- Action oriented combat that doesn't outstay its welcome- Removing some "where the hell am I supposed to go" moments with the help of map markers and a journalCon:- The camera can be a bit fiddly during the boss battles- I loathed the squeaking sound Angela made when dodging or jumping- Some of the Voice acting of minor characters (and Charlotte, though that seems to be intended) can get a bit gratingReally loved this game back in the day and am glad I was able to play it in this updated version, especially since some of the things that were improved would have just been grating these days (not knowing where to go and so on).While it may not be for everyone, I do recommend this game to anyone who enjoys old school action rpgs.The addition of a new optional boss and the chain abilities is nice and helps keep the game fresh for those who have already beaten the original.Still, despite my nostalgia goggles, I have to admit, that this game is probably not for everyone since it can get a bit grindy and neither the story nor the overall voice acting is that great. Still, both are serviceable and don't really diminish the overall fun factor of the game (at least for me).All in all, I would definitely recommend this game
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Trials Of Mana is a classic JRPG where our heroes try to save a medieval fantasy world in which the power of mana/magic is withering and evil forces try to sow chaos while trying to claim the power of the Goddess for themselves.At the time of its first release, the game stood out for the multiple playable characters, which were quite innovative at the time, as well as its memorable music, which had a Latin America feel to it. The battle gameplay was in real time, as opposed to similar, party based rpgs of the time that were mostly turn based. This was not such a surprise, since the game came out in the snes, where action rpgs such as The Legend of Zelda were the norm.The game uses standard tropes with abundant silliness and hero stereotypes in its storytelling. It's not supposed to be deep, but nevertheless it works very well as the fairy tale that it is. If you are looking for an elaborate plot this game might not be what you want.Like many, I played the hacked English translation of the original Seiken Densetsu 3 on snes. Square not only recreated the original vibe of the game, they also added a lot of gameplay elements that make the remake a very enjoyable and fresh experience. The battle is more elaborate than the original with some rudimentary combos that characters can perform, as well as dodging. You can now see exactly what kind of abilities you get by leveling up and can try different combinations of abilities to get the most out of situations. It does get a bit repetitive, but it is more involved, action-like and immediate than attacking and waiting for the weapon cooldown, which is what players did in the original.Plus you can jump now, and this has been integrated to both combat and exploration. There are even some platforming elements, walls to break and small environmental puzzles to solve and the world feels much more interactive than in the original.The graphics are vibrant and colorful. On the technical side, you won't see elaborate PBR shaders here, but there is HDR, depth of field, ambient occlusion and the kind of cartoony look that makes this feel like a Nintendo game. Seeing the world in 3D is amazing, and they did a great job in adapting the original 2D levels into captivating 3D scenes. There is always a lake, forest, mountain or other pieces of pretty scenery in the horizon. The free camera was disorienting for me at first, having played the original game in 2D, but you are getting used to it very quickly and now it just feels like this is the way it was always meant to be. I know I'm going to miss the scenery next time I play this in 2D.There are some great quality of life improvements in item management. Quest markers help players move on quickly without getting lost, such as in the original. The game has some extra elements outside combat, such as a collectible mini-game where players can search the world for a cactus plant. Seed planting also has its own system, with players getting progressively stronger items as they level up.Generally the UI is simple, straightforward and understandable. Exactly as it should be.I can't tell if it's nostalgia that makes me like this game, but I believe its "Nintendo" vibe and simplicity is very appealing to me. It does get a bit repetitive, just like the original, but the beautiful world and the amount of new abilities makes up for it. Sometimes you just need a fun to play game, and this remake delivers very well in this regard.Overall, I think they did a great job modernizing it.Well done Square!So final verdict: If you've played the original, should you get this? Absolutely YES, this is the definitive version of Secret Of Mana 3. For those who haven't played it, it might feel a bit simple compared to modern RPGs but but I believe the game stands on its own as a modern, enjoyable game, even for those who haven't played the original.  Go play it and have fun!

If it weren't during the COVID crisis I'd maybe hold off for a little cheaper, but still worth playing for any jrpg fan.-Fluid, fun combat system-Varied characters and play styles-Great art style-Lots of content-The writing...is not good.-The voice acting. Some might say that's due to the script and this is redundant but it's also just very monotone and broken up very strangely at times. I don't know if the individual lines had pauses added to them to match the dub or something but it's pretty janky throughout the entire game. I think Hawkeye is the only character that actually speaks like a human and that's only on occasion. For this reason I'd say play in Japanese with subs on, at least for me, I stop noticing issues with cadence. And also because Charlotte's English voice is insufferable.-A little too easy. I'd say all my deaths are more due to carelessness than actual difficulty but the combat is weirdly satisfying even if it isn't challenging. Hard difficulty just makes you spam items more but you end up with like 100 spare healing items just wandering and fighting.-Not enough information on classes. So this one is probably my biggest frustration with this game honestly. If you come with knowledge of the original Trials of Mana, you might know what each class does and specializes in but I felt completely lost on making class decisions. On top of just kind of guessing at your class upgrade, you can't revert your class until the very end of the game, so all decisions are pretty final. The information they provide is just vague and every class upgrade provides different skills and options so not knowing what decision you're making in game is frustrating. Since the game is so easy, there's no real risk of screwing yourself over by just classing up randomly but it just felt like the game should have provided more information internally. For instance I picked Riesz specifically because at the start of the game it mentioned she had summons. Awesome I want that. Only one path mentioned anything about having summons, so I went in that direction. But actually, every one of her tier 3 classes has a unique summon. _childDocuments_.review: I liked this game, but let me explain why I wouldn't recommend it. I would also note that I never played the original game, so I have no idea what was and wasn't added/changed from the original.It's a JRPG. If you don't like JRPGs then you won't like this. This game is full of annoyances that are common to JRPGs. Bad dialog, bad (obnoxious) voice acting, hyperactive characters, and the typical JRPG inconveniences that we all know and loath. Why does an ancient elemental spirit sound like a vapid Californian? Why does switching classes take so long? (I mean going through the UI menus, not getting to the correct level or finding the right items.) Why does Duran keep moving in cut scenes as if he'll literally die if he stands still? Why is Angela's final class item locked behind the most difficult fight in the game because she decides she needs to fight it alone? There's no reason to use a weaker piece of equipment. (Except for the elemental amulets you get at the end of the game.) So, why not just have an "optimize" button that equips the best equipment? That's a very common convenience in a lot of JRPGs. Calling the dragon (I forgot the name of the drum and dragon) is inconsistent. Most of the time you can call him whenever you're outside, but for some reason you cannot in a few places. So you have to walk outside the area to call him. Why is the sand area and the ice area so annoying? The moving sand and slippery ice add nothing to the game but annoyances. Several times when I was in combat I would be slid down a hill away from the enemies who are not effected by the terrain and I would miss attacks. The platforming is particularly bad in the ice area. Platforming in the game is not difficult. The platforming is really only in the game for some variety and hiding items. In the ice area though you slip on the ice and when you jump you lose all momentum for some reason. Making it weirdly difficult to get some of items that are hidden in that area.If you can get past all that, the combat is pretty fun on hard difficulty. On lower difficulties it's way too easy. That's really what made me complete the game. The story is fine. Bog standard JRPG story where you have to collect elemental stones (in this case spirits) to prevent the end of the world.I really hope that Visions irons out a lot of the annoyances. If that game ends us being more of the same then I don't think I'll be picking it up.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where to start, so I'm just gonna jump into this. I want to recommend this game because of its charm, but I can't bring myself to do so. The ones you pick up along the way. As long as you just grab money, the "rare" items you get are so cheap in the shop there's no point. I like the vibe of the game, it's nostalgic. However, the voice acting completely ruins it. It ranges from ok to absolutely ridiculous. Some of it is straight up suggestive in the worst way possible. Don't know why they felt the need to make a faerie moan into my ears, but I guess they did.Let's get into one more thing: the story is boring and cliché. Their stories are so rushed, cliché and stiff its laughable. They aim for dramatic moments after knowing a character for a few seconds. One second, they're up, and the next they just fall to the ground with their stiff animation like a log. There's nothing emotional about it.The music and monsters are both good and cute. _childDocuments_.review: What NOT to expect:-Dark Souls/Sekiro difficulty - Even on hard, this is easy.-Nudity (I've seen some screenshots...) - The best you're going to get is bare legs and pantie shots. Since this IS a team comprised six 15 year old heroes, don't expect Witcher.-Non-linear plot - You have 6 heroes, of them you can choose 2 companions, and the ultimate goal (as well as things you have to do in order to get there) will ALWAYS be the same, with notable differences in bosses and levels being the beginning, and the end levels (depending on pairings you choose). There are ONLY DIFFERENT POSITIVE ENDINGS, depending on whom you play. The only bad ending you can get is GAME OVER.  For players that do not get into the positive aspects of the game, this can be too linear and repetitive.-Character progression - If you jump into this straight from Dragon Age:Origins, you will find inability for your characters to get to know each other better during the night rest at the inn a bit lacking. Once you choose the 2 companions in the beginning of the game, once you ACTUALLY MEET THEM in the game, you IMMEDIATELY become B.F.F.-s and are ready to die for each other... The only difference is when you get the adequate pairings of the characters, that you get extra cut scenes and comments between those 2 characters, cut scenes that happen during the story, which can also change a bit, and random comments during the game play. And the pairings, as everyone already knows, are:-Hawkeye/Riesz-Duran/Angela-Kevin/Charlotte- Romance - Only a kiss in the cheek.-Simplistic combat - You can do fast/power attacks, special moves, spells, and you can dodge roll. It is very easy to get into it, and might get a bit repetitive and tedious if you don't get into the good aspects of it, and get bored of killing monsters. This is not challenging as DS or Sekiro, neither it is versatile as Devil May Cry, but it is fantastic in it's own way, and I personally can't get bored of it unless it really gets EXTENSIVE by having to clear every single chest in the area, even if it means forgetting a chest, then going all the way back. ^^-English V.A. - It is a painful spot for everyone, having hard time getting used on it for Kevin, but I didn't have THAT much of a problem... Didn't try Japanese one yet.If you can endure all of the above, then you're in for one hell of a remake. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge Seiken Densetsu 3 fan, having played the Dejap Translation for well over a dozen times, my expectations for this remake were teetering in the border between massive hype and serious apprehension, especially after the botched Secret of Mana remake in 2018. Thankfully, Square-Enix listened to the complaints and feeback and delivered what is hands down one of the best remakes from the 16-bit era.Trials of Mana fully captures and expands on all of the highlights that the SNES game had achieved in the past. The gameplay & combat system has been extremely overhauled thanks to its venture into the 3D realm, gaining a lot of fluidity and consistency that further improves as you unlock classes, abilities and spells, becoming a very competent action RPG on the later stages of the game when bosses start throwing their own mechanics into the mix. The story is pretty much intact, hitting all of the high notes that the original game hit with it's three separate story-lines, giving it that much more value and replayability. The remastered orchestral arrangements are as good as the original 16-bit ones but for those of us feeling nostalgic, the game does offer you the option to switch to the original BGM. While there's a lot (A LOT) of good things with this remake, there's also an assortment of small negative things that, while not marring the overall experience, do cause some small annoyances, such as the companion AI being a bit too suicidal in some Boss Battles, the english VA being severely underwhelming in some characters (Charlotte...) and some small bugs here and there. All in all, this is the right direction that all companies, not only S-E, should take in any future attempts of remaking a classic. Improve on what was already delivered and keep the spirit of the original game alive.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game all around. It's almost entirely story-driven, but with three separate story paths (and some differences depending on which characters you chose and the path you play), gives Trials of Mana a good amount of replayability. It's faithful remake of the old SNES Game (Seiken Densetsu 3). The gameplay style is that of your typical hack-n-slash (J)RPG from that time period, so the gameplay is about what you'd expect.Now, the game isn't hard by anyone's standards, although that said, becoming complacent WILL end up biting you in the rear, so although the game isn't majorly challenging in of itself, there are certain times the difficulty will ramp up to provide a bit of challenge. Most noticeably, boss fights. There are also certain fights that use mechanics that you have to approach in a specific way, or you will not have a good time.The remake is most certainly faithful to the original, including the outfits of the characters. So for those who are 'purists' and like their remakes to be as close to the originals as possible, this should suit you fine. Of course, the majority of the artificial lengthening was removed, so if you're a 'purist', you'll have to be the judge on whether or not this remake is 'pure' enough for you.Although this game doesn't have too much grinding bar the end-game and post-game, when you do have to grind, it is an absolute SLOG. Trust me. If you're feeling burnt out, go and do something else for a while, other it becomes yet another game that will sit in your library never played (to finish) because of near-end-game grind.Another fault with the game is the controls (no I'm not going to go on about the camera, because literally every 3D action game suffers from this problem). The controls are weird and janky, With keys such as J, K, and L being used to navigate menus, and Q and Ctrl opening up the quick menus. You get used to them, but for the first few hours of the game, you'll be cursing the devs for why they set up the control scheme this way.Arguably the worst flaw however, aside from lack of post-game content (excluding the quest that feels shoehorned-in), is the lack of a modern save system. The game uses checkpoints. CHECKPOINTS.  What game uses checkpoints these days? It makes it really irritating to save the game, as you can't just save whenever you want. This makes it really painful if you have to redo a dungeon just because you missed a checkpoint or the game crashed (totally not speaking from experience here...)---In Conclusion, Trials of Mana is an excellent remake that is very faithful to the Original. It uses a tried-and-tested formula that guarantees hours of fun, just as long as you can look past the game's few faults. If you can, then you'll most likely enjoy Trials of Mana, whether you're a casual player, a hard-core gamer, an achievement hunter, or literally anyone else.

_childDocuments_.review: After some back and forth, I have to say that all in all I really enjoyed Trials of Mana. The main story only takes around 20 hours to beat which at first may seem like a con, but I honestly liked how the game didn't lag on unnecessarily and really got to the point. The combat, while not overtly complex, was actually really enjoyable, particularly when you get to the third class (). Also, the game is not very hard. I only died twice, and I'm not the greatest at combat games. If you are a big JRPG fan, you'll want to play on hard mode. Then again, there are some things I didn't enjoy about the game. The fact that you get to pick your party is really cool, however, don't expect much in terms of interaction between party members. This game suffers the same problems that Octopath Traveler has where there isn't really any development between characters. Instead, it is more like three people acting to achieve the same goal with limited dialogue between. I didn't play the original game so going in I didn't know what to expect, but I was hoping for some character development. The plot isn't anything to write home about either, but despite not being very unique, it was still enough to keep me entertained throughout the whole game. A unique feature of the game is that it's meant to be replayed so that you can experience the three different story routes based on your main character. I've only played Hawkeye's route so I'm not sure how variant these stories are. I'd recommend getting this game on sale. The combat was fun, the story was basic but still relatively compelling, and the world was fun to explore. Just a classic JRPG!Final thing! A lot of people say the English dub is unbearable. I thought it was absolutely hilarious and definitely added value to my experience. It is so bad at times that it completely ruins your immersion, but it's not like the story is deep enough to immerse into anyways. The dub almost feels like it was a joke, like Ghost Stories. Briliant.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Trials of Mana is a very faithful recreation of the original game from the SNES with great improvements where needed to update the game for the modern age. The changes to the battle system keeps combat fun and complex and the whole stat allocation and abilities thing means that there are a ton of fun ways to build characters.Graphics are extremely faithful, too, and you can see that care was taken to translate the original sprites into 3D. Everything is colorful and vibrant, and all of the characters look just how they did way back when.Honestly, the only real complaints I have with this game are that there's not any kind of multiplayer aspect at all, and that English voices sound really really rough and awkward. However that second one doesn't really matter too much considering that there's the option of just using Japanese voices, so no biggie, there. Though I do wish that there was subtitles for the dialogue between characters when you win battles.Seriously great game, pick it up if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: The best remake I ever played, and for a well deserving game.The first time I've played Seiken Densetsu 3 was on a SNES emulator, through an unofficially translated ROM. For a long time, I've been thinking that the game deserved at least an english version launch, for modern platforms. Fortunately, not only did Square Enix launch the official western version, but also decided to make a beautifully crafted remake for one of the best action RPGs of all time.The remake stays true to the original, "story-wise" and "gameplay-wise", but also made some improvements (specially when it comes to graphics, sounds and design). It also added some extra features to keep you playing it a lot more than the SNES version did.The game has:- Amazing graphics, truthful to the original's JRPG style;- Beautiful soundtracks, with the option to play both the remake and the original versions;- English and Japanese dubbing (the Japanese voices adds to the "oldschool anime-like" vibe);- Good and challenging combat mechanics (played it with keyboard and mouse, but might work better with a controller/gamepad);- Many possible combinations of characters (you can form a party of 3 from the 6 available), which will define the party's combat style, some bits of the story flow and what happens at some cutscenes;- Each character has their own set of classes and skills, allowing you to make different "builds" and combat strategies;- Three possible final dungeons and final bosses, which will be defined by the main character you chose;- An awesome world with a good variety of dungeons, monsters, bosses, villages and many different areas that can be explored;- Some content that are exclusive to the remake.Even after playing through the game three times, with three different character combinations and 80h+ of gameplay, I still feel like playing it more. If you liked the original, or simply like action RPGs, this game will definitely be worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal remake of what continues to be my favorite RPG on the SNES/SFC, improving upon the original's shortcomings and limitations, all while retaining its best qualities, though I do miss the lush pixel art, much as I enjoy this at least equally cozy, PS2-esque presentation.The music and sound effects? It's all there. Characters, monsters, and bosses have been wonderfully interpreted from the original sprites in their transition to 3D, with class outfits being a notable highlight. The script remains more or less the same, for better or worse, pointless English name changes in typical Square fashion being the main detraction now that every major character is voiced.Adding modern combat touches to the original battle system is perhaps the most notable change. While  was revolutionary for its time, it also pushed the SNES/SFC hardware to its absolute limits (it's the only game I know of on the console, at least off the top of my head, that consistently causes visual glitches courtesy PPU desync); battles were a slow, clunky affair, boss fights in particular suffering from massive performance issues when shuffling through the circular menus mid-fight. , however, is the exact opposite: fast and fluent, maintaining all the character without any of the sluggishness.A brand new post-game chapter is absolutely a welcome addition, as is a new game+ mode. Pacing-wise, I always felt like the original comes to a close much too soon, more or less ending shortly after the plot begins to  take off. That said, while I enjoy this chapter (along with its included 4th class change), its timeline is somewhat confusing, and can't seem to make up its mind rather it takes place before or after the final boss, never mind all the lore implications that come with that very indecisiveness.But then again, that's indicative of my overall complaints here: surmised, they're all nitpicky ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that most people would never care about, and easily ignored by hardcore fans like me. Outside of the port itself, there's very little to mention, as the game contained within has nothing noteworthy at fault.An absolute masterpiece like its 16-bit counterpart, though I recommend playing the original in some form first, to truly appreciate all this remake does to bolster that experience.  wishes it were even half as good.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the Mana series, I would definitely recommend this remake. It improved on a lot of things, however few, from the original game. One thing I don't like is the terrible English voice acting and the way point system. In my first run I wanted to turn it off but there was no way to do so; but in subsequent play-throughs it did help in getting through the game quicker and not wasting any time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is some simple, classic action RPG fun. If you're here for an incredibly long game with a complicated combat system that requires strategy guides, you're in the wrong place.If you're here for an action RPG with a colorful world, charming characters and a combat system with a deceptive amount of depth despite its simple surface, then you're in the right place!Trials of Mana remake is an excellent game and I adore it. It's the kind of game that is very simple, maybe even to the point of off putting for some people really early on, but it just rapidly expands in ways that will surprise you and make you want to play it over and over again, and the New Game+ makes replaying it an absolute blast, trying different 3 party combinations of the 6 different heroes to choose between.I'm not that good at reviews so let me try to summarize...This is a good, simple RPG with a lot of charm, a lot of replay value and accessibility. It's a bright and colorful game that despite being pretty new (coming out in 2020) manages to have this sort of Playstation 2 era RPG nostalgia about it (even more fascinating when you consider it's a remake of an SNES game) and I can't recommend it enough if you're into that kind of thing.(I love this game so much I double dipped on the Switch and PC version during a 50% off sale and have beaten the game on both platforms! _childDocuments_.review: After having played the remake of the original Secret of Mana from Feb. 2018, I was a little skeptical when I heard about Seiken Densetsu 3 getting a remake too since I didn't enjoy the one from the first game that much. It felt more like a mobile game to me. However, I don't want to digress now, it's a review about Trials of Mana after all.I've played the original Seiken Densetsu / Secret of Mana games back then sometime in the 90's, and I've always been a huge fan of the franchise!This 3D remake of Seiken Densetsu 3 aka. Secret of Mana 2 is really splendid, beautiful characters and well done, detailed locations - my childhood dream come true. I don't know for HOW LONG I dreamed about this game getting a remake or reboot, I always wished that to happen, and now it's truly here, finally.If you played the original from the 90's and fell in love with it, well, then you should absolutely try this 3D remake! I don't think you'll be disappointed. It's really amazing seeing all these characters coming back to "life", and they are exactly how I always imagined them to be, especially my all-time favorite Kevin. I do still have some drawings from my childhood, and teen years that show the main characters together, and they're quite similar to these from the remake, especially Kevin. And the Rabites are so cute!Developers left some stuff just as it was in the original game; in this case it's positive actually as it was already near to perfect. They didn't remove any characters nor places, and - most important for me - the main plot is the very same, so I think you'll recognize everything pretty fast if you played the original Seiken Densetsu 3. That can be perceived as both, positive and negative since the story feels a tad "old fashioned" for today. It's also a matter of taste ofc, for me it's good the way it is. I got all nostalgic.The only thing that makes me sad is the missing multiplayer. My friend and I wanted to play this together, he was fairly new to the Mana franchise, and I wanted to show him my favorite childhood's video game, but I couldn't. So we were "forced" to play each for themselves which is simply not the same...For my first playthrough I've used my favorites Kevin, Charlotte and Angela, starting with Kevin's plot. He went with Angela as main, followed by Duran and Riesz. As for the memorable soundtrack, you can choose whether to use the original music or the new remastered version. I've used the new musics for my first playthrough, and I can tell you it's totally worth it! The combat system is well done, and really fun! I love the new fighting animations a lot. The fights feel smooth, there isn't anything that I find negative. You learn pretty fast what to do, and how the combos work as these are quite simple.I don't want this to get too long, so I'll slowly come to the end. Even if you're totally new to the Mana franchise, but you still like colorful fantasy worlds, action oriented realtime combat and of course JRPGs, then you'll love Trials of Mana. Just give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't aware people knew of this game and were asking to remake it. Goes to show how popular SNES emulation has become since the early 2000s. That said, a 3D remake doesn't make a lot of sense for this game's visuals: a lot of what made Seiken Densetsu 3 'special' were the layered 2D effects and the limited sprites. The 3D visuals in this remake are about what you'd expect from a 360 / PS3 game. The gameplay is grindy-but-unchallenging, there's not a whole lot of extra stuff to explore or neat tricks to figure out. The 'post-game' dungeon and 'New Game Plus' options give you more time with the game, but Trials of Mana is exactly as straight forward as its original version. The highlight of the gameplay is figuring out boss attack patterns, that's about it. Story-wise, it's mostly a knights and princess type deal. The actual plot beats were never important: the main highlight of the SNES version was having six different stories to play through. We take that multi-character approach in stories for granted now. I guess you could enjoy the story with a retrospective type approach: "this was one of the first game to have multiple entangled storylines". Nostalgia only goes so far though... There's also an arrogant naiveté about the game's voice acting that removes any nostalgia for this game I had as a kid; you probably should not hire a grown adult to voice a toddler character for hours on end of dialogue. At least they kept the original soundtrack; the soundtrack is quite good as far as video-game music goes and is what glues this remake together, in all honesty. If you have the urge to play through a JRPG, I don't think you'll go wrong with this. The average person is better off finding something else to do with their time.

You run into weird issues where the environment will block what you see and a lot of times you end of fighting blind. - The AI on the characters is not the greatest. I have them set for the most aggressive and they still seem a bit timid. All in all I am having a blast and I am looking forward to multiple play throughs on different characters / party make ups. _childDocuments_.review: So I'll get this out of the way first: yes, the English voice direction is a little iffy. This game had a very limited localization budget and it does show in places.That being said, if you played the original Seiken Densetsu 3 fan translation then you absolutely owe it to yourself to get this remake, as long as you don't mind the removal of the original's multiplayer mode. The characters, enemies, music, and locations are faithfully re-created in 3D and the remake perfectly captures the mid-90s charm of the original game. The basics of the original's real-time-with-pause combat are still there, but characters can now dodge, jump, and combo light attacks with strong attacks. Frequently-used spells and items can be bound to shortcut keys. Passive abilities have been added; they can be obtained by levelling and talking to various NPCs, then equipped to enhance your party's performance in battle. There's also a new post-game chapter with a fourth tier of classes and a big new dungeon to try them out in.If you've never played the original Super Famicom game then give the demo a try and load your demo save into the full game if you want to continue. It's not a particularly difficult or lengthy game, but the world, music, and visuals have a lot of charm to them, and the game is designed for multiple playthroughs with different party compositions and class choices; the story plays out slightly differently depending on which of the six potentially playable characters you pick as the protagonist and their two companions.

Do give a Google to the 1995 version if you haven't played it before, it looks amazing for its date, way ahead of its time.PD: You know your first choice was Angela and why.

_childDocuments_.review: i don't think this is a bad game by any means, but its not a game i could recommend easily. I'll try and keep this brief. - story sucks. the original did a better job of masking its generic plot, because of its pixel art charm, but with fairly modern, 3D graphics, it comes off as cheap and cheesy.- Faerie is one of the worst companion characters ever. mostly because of how boring the plot is, and how none of the other characters seem to give a ♥♥♥♥ except her. I also didn't give a ♥♥♥♥ about the plot, and her constant badgering started to piss me off. - Doesn't look great. not bad, but there is a lot of blocky geometry and low quality textures. very few graphics options as well. - tons of invisible walls and sometimes questionable collision detection doesn't help.- Wack hitboxes on some enemies, namely Dangaard and the Dragon Lord.- Fighting regular enemies gets boring quick. very little variety. enemies are quite bulky but are never fun to fight, so they just take a long time without being enjoyable. i found that i just ran past most enemies towards the end. - absolutely awful friendly AI. often run into attacks, and rarely fight back. Angela pretty much never used magic, even after changing tactics. Kevin died during literally every boss fight.- Zehnoa was an awful boss. AI pretty much ran into his traps, which turned into an absolute cluster♥♥♥♥ near the end. was not fun. felt like i had to cheese my way through it. also the shape-shifters, which are constantly spammed at you, heal every time the shift their shape. so they are pretty much unkillable. - Dangaard was probably the worst boss in the game. you have barely any room to move in the fight. also the game likes to repeatedly use a gimmick where a boss charges up an attack, and you need to damage it enough to prevent it from unleashing it. here though, the absolutely awful hit box means that you literally cannot hit it, if it's the orange head charging up. maybe i was doing something wrong but none of my attacks connected. friendly AI also got overwhelmed by the fact that they had very little room to move, and just ended up being useless until they died.- Voice acting is not great. A lot of the characters sound really stiff, and Charlotte has probably the most irritating voice in any game ever. Overall not the worst acting in the world. but that doesn't mean it's good.- sound track is good. not like sonic level or anything but still a groove. although a lot of tracks repeat often, which gets stale quick.- lots of questionable character designs. Belladonna, Spellbinder Angela, and Fenrir Knight Riesz come to mind. - very replayable, since there are a lot of party combinations you can have, and 6 different possible main characters, each with a fairly distinct story. That being said though there are only 3 main stories, as some characters share antagonists. Your party barely acknowledges each others existence, which is a let down. And pretty much all the main characters are really boring and not interesting at all. the tiny bits of character development they get feel incredibly forced. - class system is cool. The game gives a lot of freedom with how you build a character, however it can seem overwhelming at first. Also not a whole lot of information is given in game, so if you want to make an informed decision about what classes to pick and what stats to invest in, you generally have to resort to the internet. - Bosses, aside from the few i mentioned above, are  definitely the highlight of this game. Generally really fun, juggling dodging, attacking and healing. the game is at its best around Chapter 3 and 5, where it starts to open up and its pretty much back to back bosses in what ever order you want. Only minor issue with them is that they drag on a lot. I think their healthpool needs to be lowered, as it often gets to the point where they start to go through the same attack patterns in a loop until they die. - I believe there is some good post game content, but i genuinely cannot be bothered to carry on playing this game rn. overall im left with fairly mixed opinions about this game. definitely better stuff out there, but its not bad by any means. its a good remake and is faithful to the original game, whilst also changing a lot of stuff that needs changing. but at the same time it seems like for everything good about this game there is something bad to counteract that. (i.e bosses are fun, but regular enemies are boring. sound track is good but repeating tracks gets annoying, they made angela thicc, but she's kinda irritating. the idea of the story changing with your party selection is cool, but the story sucks anyway.)its hard to recommend over other games, but if you have the time, give it a go if you want. 6.5/10oh and there is a very  modding community.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little bit more than half way through the story at the time of writing this. The game is good, I can't deny that. Great visuals, cool atmosphere, nice tunes... I feel like combat system is a substantial improvement over other similar games in the genre that stick to the turn based pattern. Movement during battle is not only useful, but fundamental to dodge enemy attacks and re-position yourself to have a better use of your skills.Now, enemy variety is really not that good. You'll be fighting the same 20 (or maybe less) types of enemies with different colors most of the times, but at least there are some visually beautiful bosses to compensate. The game is really not difficult at all (playing at normal difficulty), and you can overcome any fight even by yourself. Your allies, when controlled by the CPU, will do an awful job at dodging enemy attacks, and will die almost instantly in any boss fight. But then again, the game really doesn't punish you for that.I love the visual changes for characters class changes, really appreciated. So far, the only major negative element of this game is the narrative itself. The story has made no improvement from the original version of the game. There are no extra details in the dialogues or in the environments. Cities and towns feel pointless, and most citizens will deliver some of the most basic one-liners that you'll ever see in a video game. Entering people's houses will prove useless 80-90% of the times, and there are very few rewards scattered inside them. Talking about rewards... man: I honestly can't remember when, if ever, I got any item from a chest that was not a healing item. There are too many candies and chocolate bars scattered around the world. The thrill of seeing a chest disappears after you open the 10th one, and you find out that you still got candies out of it. No weapons, no gear... nothing.Aside from these issues that persist from the original game, I'd say that this version of Trials of Mana is a significant improvement over the original, and over other competitors in the genre. Again, this is mostly because of the dynamic combat system. Visual quality like this (or better) has already been seen in other titles, like the latest Dragon Quest.I'll be jumping back into the game now, but I want to end this review by saying that I could easily see this being a new "reboot point" for the "Mana" series, of course with the necessary improvements.Recommended if you're a fan of the series or the genre, and you don't really care about in-depth storytelling.Peace!EDIT: I'm approching the end of my second playthrough now. All that I said above stands true, but the game grew on me a little bit more, so I'd say I have more positivity towards the title than I had when I first wrote this review.

_childDocuments_.review: This remake was designed with fans of the original game clearly in mind. It preserves the flow of the story and art aesthetic of the original game, even going so far as to use the original layouts of areas in several parts of the game. You can even switch to the original soundtrack in the Options menu. The new content added to the game takes care to respect the original's form...even preserving some of the more 'awkward' dialogue style the original script contained. Mostly what you get here is a new combat system and character development system that takes the original into account such as branched class trees and attribute allocation to unlock new skills. I will say the game is considerably easier than the original game, mostly due to the greater range of combat capabilities and the ability to dodge most attacks or given a chance to cancel major boss attacks. All in all I would say this is a solid remake.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the Mana series, especially the original Seiken Densetsu 3 this is based on, it's a very nice touch-up on the original that mixes up some of the mechanics but keeps the storyline and feel intact. If you're not, it's still a fun low-effort-required action RPG with multiple storyline variations based on which characters you choose. Good casual adventuring and hack'n'slashing.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Trials of Mana is an excellent example of how to do remakes . It is clear as water that the dev team learned a lot from the remake of Secret of Mana, because this sequel improves nearly everything that game did wrong. Gameplay is smooth and character models look great.However, the game has some issues. The story is pretty simple and straightforward, as one would expect from older JRPGs; unfortunately the devs didn't improve the plot from the original 1995 game, which shows. Villains are extremelly one-dimensional and can be described with few words. The main characters lack any form of development, and just kinda go with the flow. Also, the game is relatively short and not so difficult.But my biggest gripe with this game is arguably the battle A.I. for the non-controlled party members. Characters will often stand in front of telegraphed enemy skills and get killed over and over; other times they'll be just doing nothing even if you set the strategies to be aggressive. This alone makes the game actually hard in some boss battles because you'll find yourself having to resurrect A.I. characters every few seconds, which is very frustrating.Even with all those problems, the game still is amazing, and they even added extra classes, post-game content and a New Game+, which adds a lot of replay value.Below a short Pros/Cons that sums a bit what I said above:+ Gorgeous graphics and a cute artstyle.+ Very well designed dungeons in terms of variety.+ Responsive combat that is easy to grasp.+ Diverse cast of characters, each with their distinct gameplay.+ Characters can unlock additional classes which further improve their abilities.+ Interesting skill system with points the player spends on specific stats to unlock new passives and abilities.+ Post-game content and New Game+, greatly improving the replay value.+ New Game+ allows you to keep nearly everything, ranging from Lucre and items to levels and abilities.- Relatively short game.- Over simplistic story with little character development.- Most dungeons are a bit straightforward; some feature interesting puzzles, but those are unfortunately very sporadic.- Not very challenging, even on Hard Mode, although some bosses are a bit "cheap".- Terrible A.I. for the characters the player is not controlling.- Some animations for characters during cutscenes are a bit weird; you can see that there is a bit of "over-acting" in the mocap.Overall, this game is really good, and it is nice to see the Mana series getting some well deserved love. If you enjoy a simple, yet engaging action adventure and/or love the Mana series, this game is definitely for you.I wish Legend of Mana was the next to get a remake, but it seems we'll be just left with the HD port, a shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Trials of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Trials of Mana is a long awaited official 3D remake of Seiken Densetsu 3, which came out in 95 but was never officially released in the west. I remember playing the fan translation, and for a SNES game I was impressed how the team had topped what they had previously done in Secret of Mana and included new elements to the mana series (and to RPG’s). Though the game is very linear, combat is simplistic and the plot shows its age, the positives still vastly outweigh these negatives. As far as ports or remakes go Square-Enix seems to have listened to fans after the 3D release of Secret of Mana, Trials is jam packed full of extras, options and some new content. If you’re looking for a simplistic RPG to play with great music and I highly recommend picking this up (or at least playing the demo so you can make an informed decision).Most of the Mana games follow a theme and aren’t connected to each other (with the one game that does preceded this not released on steam) so you aren’t punished for not having played other entries. The story unfolds slightly differently in Trails of Mana – you pick a “main” protagonist from 6, and then pick 2 companions to join the party (each with their own prologue on how they were forced into this quest). This setup allows for fairly unique party setups, and changes the dialogue between characters in each play through depending on who is in the party. The party is hindered by 3 separate groups of antagonists, each which pairs to 2 of the characters and are seeking the mana sword for their own nefarious reasons. This leads to a fairly large amount of unique dialogue between the matched pairs, and 3 separate end areas and end bosses you can end up fighting. As a bonus a new area and additional story line has also been added post game which loosely ties the end boss from a different game in the series, as well as making a previously hidden boss available to all characters to now face off against. Gameplay and combat has been significantly altered with minor quality of life improvements. I feel it makes the game a fair bit easier to play and really reduces the difficulty in some fights, though the difficulty settings can be changed at any time. The characters can now dodge, and need to jump to attack flying enemies. Each character now has multiple light and dark paths they can change to, each which affects their stat growth, spells and combat rolls. While they do have set roles (pure DPS, tanker, support ect) you can vastly change how each character plays depending on which path they take. The game has added a 4th class tier, which lets you do some stupidly high damaged attacks. Objectives are displayed on screen by default, which has the feelings of leaving the game feeling fairly linear (no more unneeded exploration), though you do still have the ability of tackling bosses in any order once you get to chapter 6. Abilities are a new addition which give minor boosts to stats or attacks, some of which can be shared across players or games, which can result in really OP combinations (some of the end game ones are OP by themselves).Combat is a mixture of performing light and heavy attacks, with a chargeable heavy attack being used to break shields and different combos that increase as you change classes (instead of holding the attack button to charge the top tier move). I thought this over simplified the combat from Secret of Mana, where you were punished for button mashing. All the enemy attacks now are easily telegraphed and show the attack path for you to evade, though the computer AI isn’t particularly smart and seems to run headlong into them (even if you set them to play defensively). The CS gauge which allows you to perform class specific super attacks now let’s you select from all the attacks you know rather than the last one, and enemies no longer counter. These moves are fairly spectacular and are great for clearing out mobs and taking large chunks of life from bosses. The spells cast quickly and look good (you no longer have to constantly use them to upgrade their levels), and are now affected by the day and week cycle (so fire magic is stronger on the fire day), and dark magic is stronger at night ect. Many of the previous games instant death attacks have been removed as well. I found the changes to boss fights where super attacks have a slow charging period that let you interrupt make the fights a lot easier and take a lot of the challenge away. On normal the game isn’t difficult, with deaths more being a bad luck (like having the whole party petrified in rapid secession), and new game+ modes can either make the game stupidly difficult or total pushover depending on how you want to play. You now have the option to reset levels back to one for a challenge, as well as a one life mode if you’re seeking a challenge.Graphically everything has changed. The character models, enemies and environment are now all 3D (same as Secret of Mana), though lots of the special character animations now seem to have been replaced. New weapons are visible on each of the characters, and you have the options of changing the visual clothes the characters are wearing once you class up. Each of the environments looks great and are quite varied and detailed, and have been rebuilt for the jumping mechanic. While the environments look great, lots of the lesser character assets are reused, with beastmen townsfolk being the best example and looking silly when there are more of 2 of them together. Every old person in the game has eyebrows that cover a large portion of their faces.  Most enemies are re-used with different skins (they do have different attack patterns), as are some bosses which was fine in 95 but looks lazy now. Like its predecessor, Seiken Densetsu 3 had an amazing soundtrack for what the SNES could put out. While I enjoyed the remastered soundtrack from Secret of Mana, I think it butchered my favourite song for listening to out of game. I was worried that it would happen this time around for Trials, but the remastered tracks seem to have played it safe and all are quite well done and very close to the originals. As before you have the option to either play the original or the remastered tracks. The voice work of the characters was well done (and I had concerns for Charlottes considering she rhotacizes the R as W’s). Kevin’s speech pauses (as if unsure), which was a good take rather than just portray him as always using simple speech. The shopkeeper was the only NPC I had an issue with, and its only because its reused in every city. The spirits now have throwaway personalities and lines, after hearing them once there aren’t really heard from again.It’s a crime that Square-Enix don’t have soundtrack available as DLC.If you are chasing 100% achievements then it’s easy to do though it requires at least 3 playthroughs and has a few items that need collecting along the way.For more reviews please visit

_childDocuments_.review: When I heard they were doing a full remake for Trials of Mana I was really excited. I spent dozens of hours playing an emulated version of this game back in the day. In fact even though this game was (at least at the time) never released in the states, I liked it more than Secrets.So when I saw that the remake had dropped on steam, much to my surprise I snapped it right up. And I was not disappointed. This game is nearly perfect when it comes to what I look for in a remake of a game:-Improved Gameplay.-A remastered score that captures the heart of the original. (Remember when the music of a game was so catchy it would stick in your heads for days afterwards?)-Updated Graphics (Don't get me wrong sprites are great and there's a few touches I still miss from the orginal)This game is really good. It does have its problems mind you. I'm sure you've heard a lot of people talk about how bad the voice acting is, that's pretty consistent. This game ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed with it's voice acting, at least in english. I think Angela, Duran, and Faery were the only members of the main cast that I didn't have some problems with. You might hear people mention Charlotte, and yeah she's bad if you can't handle uwu speak. I for one am not bothered by it so much, I actually think the voice actor did alright for the material she was given. I'm not going to go into it too much, just change it to Japanese if you can't deal with it.Second this game is easy, really easy. Like I started the game on hard and I beat literally everything without having my party wiped once easy. Maybe that's just me. On the plus side I will say that if you're skilled enough you can do very well in this game and the game rewards you for doing so. I'd very much recommend setting the difficult to hard and then forgetting about it.I'll just leave with this statement, any game that I finish playing and I immediatly hop on steam looking for more like it or I start again with new characters is good in my books. And that's exactly the feeling I had after over thirty hours of playing Trials of Mana. I can definitely see myself picking this game back up in the future and putting another 37 hours into it.

_childDocuments_.review: Game overall is good. General flow of the story is good (though that's more towards the original game than this remake I believe). It has some pacing issues here and there with how quickly you go from having to face one major threat, and then tells you to just jump on over to the next one without any real setup or discussions as to what it is or why exactly we need to fight it.Combat itself is good for the most part, as you can change up your attacks and there are enough enemy types and attack types for those enemies that it keeps you on your feet in the middle of battle. There are some issues when the game forces you to use less than the 3 normal party members as the combat itself is centered around the 3 characters, and not less than that (other than starting areas). Combat can also be a bit frustrating at times though as well, as the CPU for your party members can be a bit braindead at times and stand in a very obvious AoE circle that will go off for the longest time, or just run to the edge of the arena and seemingly be doing nothing but waiting extended periods of time in-between its casting of spells.The voice acting in the game is where there are the most issues however. Voice-actors themselves are good, though the cleric can get quite annoying to listen to quickly, but that's how she was meant to be portrayed and not just a fault of the voice actor. In general, nothing seems like it was meant to be put together and actually discussed like a proper conversation, everything is so disjointed and has so many pauses and bad timings that it just seems there was no effort put into making these actual conversations, rather than the voice actors just reading random lines and someone was trying to put them together somehow. There are also plenty of times that I would get out of a cutscene before a boss fight or something major, and the characters would just start talking about how the next enemy or room I was going to encounter was difficult and give specifics on that enemy/room, which just spoiled the next encounter or event for me. There's also quite a few parts that honestly just seem like someone too the original Japanese, plugged it into Google, and had the voice actors read off whatever was in there, as the English didn't really make sense or just seemed broken.Overall, it's a 7/10. The major parts of the game are good, it can give for a decent multi-playthrough with the differences that can show up between character stories, but there are some issues with the game that aren't likely to just get patched out like a bug would be. This is on the good side of JRPGs. (Though probably not a full-purchase buy for most people.)

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't know what to make of this game. While it has so many flaws, it was still fun to play... somehow.That's an honest review of a guy that doesn't have any nostalgic feelings towards the title. Never played the original.Everything seen in Trials of Mana i saw better made in other games. Story, characters, gameplay and gameworld wise. Ys 8: Lacrimosa of Dana, Tales of Berseria, Ni No Kuni 2. Just to name a few available on Steam.If Trials of Mana has one problem, then it's the feeling of a budget title. It feels very very cheaply made. Let me list some of the flaws i've witnessed.- No graphical options at all. Change the screen resolution to 720p, 1080p, 1440p and 4k. That's the graphic "options" you get. It doesn't even offer Vsync. I'm used to very bad console ports by Square Enix, but that's some next level sh1t. If you want to change graphical options you have to rely on community made tools. Pop ins are the biggest flaw of the game. No joke, the textures load IN the actual cutscenes, not in the loading screen before, which make cutscenes look horrible. Luckily you can reduce that time a bit by adjusting Streaming.FullyLoadUsedTextures and Streaming.HLODStrategy values. Search for the "Modify Visuals and Tweaking Settings" guide by Anna_Maniac. Download the tool and change graphical setting however you like.- Another big flaw is how cheap the game feels. There are literally 5 different npc models ingame, in 3 different color variants each. Same goes for trash mobs. 10 different trash mobs with multiple color variants. Besides some vases, there are no destructible background elements in the game. House interiors look all 98% identical. Much content recycling. This game might be much, but surely not worth full price. It's a 30 bucks game(while being generous), for 20 bucks in the first major sale. Whatever you do, DON'T buy it full price!- The story... feels so generic. It's mind numbing. I'm playing games for over 30 years across many many console generations. But i never saw such a generic story.- Same goes for the main characters. So generic. At least they were somehow likeable.- The voice acting is HORRIBLE, especially the english one. I really don't know how the devs decided about which voice actors to contact. But judging by the quality probably by drawing lots. Do yourself a favor and change to japanese voices right after starting.- The game is WAY too easy. The hardest difficulty feels like Normal. That's it. Plus, you can have nearly unlimited healing items ingame what makes it even easier.Now onto some positive stuff about the game:+ The battle system is really solid. Enough skills so it won't become boring quick.+ Judging by gameplay i saw, this game seems to live up to the original(besides the camera perpective and missing coop mode). That's probably the biggest selling point.+ The soundtrack is good. Plus it lets you choose between the original soundtrack and a remade one. + If you can't get enough of the game, you can play through the game at least 2 times. There are 6 characters, each one has it's own story. Plus, there are some minor challenges after beating the story.This game isn't especially good, nor especially bad. If you're into action rpgs, there are better game choices out there. Dozens of them. If you have any nostalgic feelings toward the game, you might wanna give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend Trials of Mana for fans of the genre, and am still in disbelief that this game exists.This game, originally know as Seiken Densetsu 3, was the holy grail of lost  jRPGs from the 16 bit era. Though it never took the crown from FF6 or Chrono Trigger, SD3 offered a really cool take on story and combat. A very young me saw it covered in GAMEFAN magazine and was quite sad I would never get to play it. Prior to the 2D release last year (Switch exclusive, 24 years later), there was no *official* way to play this game in English. I was baffled why SE never saw fit to port a major sequel with so many concepts new and different to that era- - Branching storylines for each main character, which are augmented further if you pick a party member from their rival kingdom (including one possible romance). There are 6 possible starts and 3 possible story arcs based on the binary conflicts between these kingdoms.- A fluid take on action combat, including day/night and elemental weekday cycles that have a palpable effect on gameplay. (One of the heroes transforms into a werewolf at night.)To me it was the highest evolution of the 16bit jrpg systems.. and was totally left on the shelf for us.Finally, and much to my surprise, this game has received the type of release it deserves.  This is an incredible remake of a forgotten epic, its more true to the original that I could hope for. Its no exaggeration to say my mind is blown by how they captured that old school magic in a 1080p 120hz bottle.I would recommend Trials of Mana to anyone who wants to relieve classic Square nostalgia in a sleek 3D package that is almost surreal in its authenticity and quality.

Overall, if action JRPGs are your thing, this game will definitely scratch that itch.

_childDocuments_.review: Really like this remake, it's doesn't have the exact same feel as the original, and the voice actors were generally given bad direction but it doesn't bother me enough to affect my opinion on the game. The music was remixed really well, the visuals look much better than the Secret of Mana remake, character's lips actually move when they speak. And I still love the class system, I think there should be more games that use a similar system and expand some of it's ideas even further, rather than the completely linear progression many of them do now.The story of the characters will seem much less interesting to people now because of when the original game was made, of course it keeps the same story as the orginal. Most elements in the story have been done to death by now, but you shouldn't hold that against it, it's not making a new story it's reusing one that wasn't even close to as overused when it was first thought up as it is in 2020. When the original was made only a few games used the story elements it did, now there are hundreds of medieval fantasy games that have used the exact same ideas.     People say this game is super easy, but not really there is challenge, maybe not as much as they expected in hard mode, but it's not like the enemies just sit there and die. You have to dodge attacks and keep an eye out for your allies (which are stupid so die a lot). There are much easier action rpgs where you just stand still and sip potions as the boss dies. It's not Dark Souls and that's ok, it's not supposed to be.     Yes it could use some changes to make hard mode harder but it's not like there's absolutely no challenge like people make it sound. If they would just make the enemies do more attacks (and more often) it would make it the difficulty people who play hard mode want. I don't think they should do the same thing as the original and return all the attacks that used to have a map wide AOE back to that. That's kind of just artificial difficulty, of course if you can't dodge any attacks at all it will take you much more tries to kill bosses, but it's unfair too.

_childDocuments_.review: Very recommended. It is a welcome addition to the mana series that we all though was dead. Instead of trying to mimic the top down perspective it instead remakes levels to be big 3D areas with some verticality added and a lot of tresure chests and stuff to look around forAlthough it is impossible to replicate the 2D scenarios and sprites of the original (unfair, considering its considered the best looking SNES game ever) the remake remains charming thanks to very competent modelers. Not a single thing was touched from the original story, something apreciated, except that it now has better cutscenes and voice acting. As usual, original japanese voices are nice, can't really say for the english voices (but I bet they suck, as usual)Gameplay wise imagine its the original kingdom hearts except this time you can trust donald to heal youProgression is smoother, you get to do a class upgrade much sooner, and you are encounraged to build your characters in different stats instead of just putting everything into strenght for fighters and int for the mages.Very recommended

Despite the lack of difficulty, the pace never lets up and you're constantly getting new things to fight and spells/moves to play about with, so thankfully it doesn't get boring being borderline omnipotent.Graphics are gorgeous, runs at a solid 120FPS at 4K on a 2080Ti, nothing more to say.Soundtrack and sound effects are faithful modern recreations of the original, voice acting I can't really judge since I played in Japanese cos I'm a huge weeb or w/e.AI is the biggest problem really, I found in a lot of fights it'd be mostly spent trying to steer the AI out of danger or telling them to heal themselves/reviving them constantly.Takes about 20~ish hours taking your time to get through the whole game, maybe 23 if you get every treasure chest/collectable in the game, very linear and there's never any mystery as to where to go next due to all the waypoints everywhere.Cool fun game, worthy remake that only adds on the original.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely magnificent remake of an already magnificent classic jRPG :) They took everything that made Seiken Densetsu 3 so good, and amped it up with a modern 3D twist, all without sacrificing the heart and soul of the original.This is how you do a remake!Gorgeous visuals, excellent VA, breathtaking remade soundtrack, and tweaks to the combat system that made it much more of a joy to play; case in point, the original game stops action when you cast spells which makes mages all but useless due to how arduous it becomes just to play the game. Here the action continues during spell casting animations and attacks, it's a small change but an utterly crucial one! The ability to attack and run without consuming a stamina gauge is another greatly-appreciated tweak. Yeah, this was excellent, truly excellent and I wholeheartedly recommend it to Mana series fans or action-based jRPG fans in general!

_childDocuments_.review: Can't say I'd recommend this game without mods. Mods do help a bit.Running slow? There is a mod for that (just be careful not to make it too fast)Don't like the zoom depth? There is a mod for that (Just be aware that cave sections are horrible unless you like your zoom extra close).There is a glitch that makes your items disappear when you class change? Well, there is actually a mod for that too. It doesn't fix the items disappearing, but you have options to rebuy the lost items or to find extras in a chest later on.Attacking just doesn't feel very smooth? There is a mod for that.You can't continue the game because a glitch hardlocked you? Well, there is a mod to fix that as well.You messed up your characters' classes and want to change or want to experiment? _childDocuments_.review: Little back story about me.  I loved Seiken Densetsu 3 as a kid and played the heck out of it alongside other classics like Chrono Trigger and Bahamut Lagoon.  Day Night and Week Cycles that affect combat?  Multiple story paths based on party composition?  Branching class levels?  This game was really way ahead of its time for 1995.  In around 2003, Tales of Symphonia came out and I thought to myself, it'd be nice if Seiken Densetsu 3 got a remake with these kind of graphics.  17 years from then and it is now 2020 and I finally got the remake I wanted in 2003.  I might just be a little bit biased, but here goes my review.This is a very splendid remake of the original that follows the original extremely accurately.  Every NPC you meet are located in very much the same place with very much the same dialogue.  This can be a good or bad thing.  Mind you this is a game from 1995 and the story hasn't changed from a game of that time.  NPC will repeat the same dialogue over and over, you pretty much buy equipment in one town use them and sell them in the next town to get newer shinier weapons.  The story is linear with only a little bit of slack in the 2nd half when you can tackle the 8 bosses in any order.  Trials of Mana's remake does little to change all these things from the original.  There seems to be a bit more flavor dialogue between your party members and each of them are given more time to shine.  I think the voice acting helps.  I will have to warn you, while the Japanese voice acting is great, the English voice acting is quite a mixed bag.  Some voices are serviceable while others seem bizarre, or stilted.  The combat is where this remake truly shines.  In the original, there are full screen attacks from enemies that are just unavoidable and your characters slowly waddled around trying to attack.  The clunkiness is now gone, you have a dodge roll for most enemy attacks and the full screen attacks can now be stopped on most bosses by destroying certain objects before a timer runs out.  The combat is simple, fun, and fast.  Your combo involves hitting the light attack several times and ending with the heavy attack for different combos and effects.  So LH, LLH, LLLH, LLLLH.  You also have jump attacks, and can charge your heavy attacks to break an enemy's guard.  The soundtrack is another highlight, everything is recomposed to be more modern, but they still capture the spirit of the original perfectly.  This is a lot better than the soundtrack of The Secret of Mana Remake.  The rebalanced exp gain is a lot better in this game.  You'll definitely be level 18 or higher once you reach the first mana stone and can class change as soon as you get there.  The ??? seeds can be found in chests and as enemy drops in the game making acquiring them easier than the original.  The new passive abilities allow a great deal of customization to the characters and stat distribution makes it very clear what skills and abilities you get for them.  You no longer have to build a character blind.I'll list a bunch of pros and cons!Pros: -Smooth and improved combat-Soundtrack is modern but captures original spirit-Graphics are cute and vibrant-Sticks very closely to the original-Grinding for EXP and farming for items not as bad as original-Character stat distribution more comprehensive than original-Post-game content is a nice addition even if it's not muchCons:-Mixed bag voice acting for the English dub-Game is very faithful to the original (I consider it a pro and con, don't fix something when it isn't broken but sometimes you can't help but wonder what more they could have done)-Animations are not as expressive as the original.  I know only I would care about this, but the pixel art of the original had more expressive animations.  Even if the graphics were basic, Kevin stomped around when he walked and always landed on his feet in pain after a cannon ride, Hawkeye did a Michael Jackson dance flair when he casts spells or opens chests and had his guard up when he fought.  Angela had her sexy butt wiggle in one of her moves.  Those sprite animations told you a lot about the character's personality and it is an absolute shame they weren't recreated for this remake.-Kevin no longer has his throw techs.  I was really looking forward to suplexing every enemy in my path with these new graphics.  It's a pity really.  In summary, if you were to choose a way to play the game, I definitely recommend this over the original as you have to be rather forgiving of the limitations of the time when the original was released.  It's a very strange thing this remake is.  You have to be forgiving of the original because of how much of a product of its time the game was.  However you kind of have to be somewhat forgiving of this remake for trying to stick very closely to a product of a different time while making many quality of life and gameplay changes to cater as a crossbreed of modern and old.I am biased though so 10/10.  I waited 17 years for this bloody remake!
