_childDocuments_.review: I don’t usually play turn-based strategy games but found Broken Lines to be a fun experience. You get to command a team of soldiers dropped into Nazi occupied territory during WWII. Its sort of like Commandos but turn-based like X-COM and its surprisingly satisfying. You must utilize covering fire, flanking maneuvers, and whatever limited tools/weapons at your disposal to complete mission objectives. You also need to pay attention to team morale and how friendly the members are to each other. These aspects may be determined by dialog options in between missions, availability of food and the choice of missions themselves. Team members will regularly argue over which mission should take priority, whether to risk their lives to take civilians to safety, whether to risk failing a primary objective to gather resources, and of course, how to handle the enemy. Their moods will shift and affect their battlefield efficiency.  Your choice of mission matters since it will directly affect your story outcome and who survives. There are multiple story branches and endings which will provide some replay value if you like that sort of thing. Also fans of alternate history/secret Nazi experiments will no doubt find this interesting!! 😁  #BrokenLines #TurnBasedStrategy #SupportIndieGames

_childDocuments_.review: In the past year there's been a variety of Strategy RPG games out:Road to Eden, the "new" XCOM, Fire Emblem, and Broken Lines looked unique enough to try out.I beat the campaign on normal with limited trouble. Once you get a loadout you like (sniper rifles for me; range is king), you press forward.I won't bore you with all the details so:1) The gameplay is fun enough. There's not a ton of variety. You fight a tank and an AA gun as a boss, which was welcome, but it was very seldom. The primary gameplay is a rock-paper-scissors style affair: rifles for long range, assault for mid, and shotgun for short.I was surprised how little skills and sub-weapons factored in. They probably would make the game easier.The real novelty is the 7sec per turn system. You position all your units and within a span of time they act on your plan, for better or worse. There's some hiccups with it. Hiding behind cover can be problematic if another character occupies the space in the planning phase, even if they are moving-- I think that's an easy fix.Your characters aim at what I assume is the highest percentage, so sometimes they don't always act as you'd like, but it's manageable.2) Story and ToneThis is where the game lost me a bit. I find the developers were conflicted about what sort of game this should be. Should be be arcade-like fun with stylized characters? Should it be a gritty war game?It seems this game wants both and doesn't quite get either.The characters are sort of distinct, but nothing memorable.The narrator goes on and on about some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ every level that I usually ignored. Some fake-profound nonsense about "are we making the right choice?" Whatever.3) In Conclusion...None of the negatives distract from a decent experience. I played it through to the end.There are enough systems in place to keep you on your toes enough (panic, composure, relationship). None of them as affecting as say Darkest Dungeons sanity effects, but they do influence gameplay.All in all, I'm glad to support titles like Road to Eden and this. Different enough experiences that scratch that strategy itch.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game that makes you think carefully.The gameplay itself is a lot of fun. A solid amount of options to choose from each turn. The way you sort of explore the map and reveal enemies is interesting and can wind you up in either a very advantageous or disadvantageous position. The way you have to manage your characters and swap between them coupled with individual relationships gives some depth to the story and way you play. The style of 8 second long turns is neat and I enjoy it. The maps are cool and well designed.The story itself is alright. Nothing too crazy. You get to make decisions in dialogue and in which mission the squad decides on, which is cool and makes you feel like your choices matter. There's multiple endings and I just beat the game after almost 12 hours. The ending was very lackluster and disappointing. I will definitely play through at least once more to try the missions I didn't chose but I'm assuming the other endings will probably be just as unexciting. One of my biggest gripes is not being able to move all your characters at once. There are plenty of times where you need to move everyone to a specific location, usually at the end of a mission, and you need to path out movement for each character. Feels like a minor waste of time. For the price of the game it's worth it. Short but with solid replayablity.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed it very much. Tactical game with enough time to make decisions. I like that the story has options. In terms of team composition, I never found much use for shotgun. 1 rifle and the rest sub-machine guns suits me well for any situation. Becomes a bit repetitive. I wish LMG was available, but...Runs smoothly, has an immersive atmosphere.Reminds a bit of Blades of the Shogun in terms of simultaneous execution, but it lacks stealth and character functionality diversity. _childDocuments_.review: More Reviews @ A World War II turn-based, tactical RPG? Sign me up! I love the era and I love the genre. It’s more of an alterverse version, but the weapons and aesthetic really do a great job recreating the feel of some of the older FPS’s I played as a kid in a different setting. Kind of like MoHAA, but isometric, or maybe a more modern version of Commandos without the sneaking. Maybe you could sneak… well the option is there, but I just ran everywhere. Let me just break it down for you before I ruin the review in the opening paragraph.As I mentioned above, Broken Lines is  turn-based Tactical RPG, but it’s not the norm. This game is more gridless similar to The Bureau: XCOM Declassified. This is my preferred version of the genre. The freedom to put my “heroes” wherever I want makes a ton more sense spatially for my brain. I know that they design the levels for grid based combat when the game utilizes that method, but it feels more natural to run amuck. This is where the game shows its first real issue though. There are certain spots in the game where the path-finding will go awry. Sometimes it’s more obvious, but other times it’s so subtle that you don’t notice that you’ve used up all of your time doing a simple task. (You can adjust before going into the action phase, if you catch it.) Below you’ll see that Wood simply can’t go around boxes without making a wasteful detour.There are ways around the random path-finding errors sometimes by giving your soldiers shorter, more specific paths. The “shorter paths” method will let you do more with your allotted eight seconds too. Yes, every turn is exactly eight seconds long. When the eight seconds are up or you encounter an enemy, your action phase will abruptly end and you’ll be able to plan your next eight seconds accordingly from there. This is SUPER nice since that means you can react instantly and not be stuck running right into a death-trap like other games where your soldiers will finish up the pre-planned action. As I just mentioned, if you break down how far your squadmates run into different sprints or walks, for some reason you’ll be able to go farther than if you ran in a straight line in one single action. This will help you get an extra sniper shot off, heal a bud, or start letting the bullets fly by laying down suppressing fire on the current turn instead of the next. One mission I had to have my people wait a few seconds while one of my guys finished up using suppressing fire. It’s a pretty flexible system.This is where the second issue comes in though. This one is both major and minor at the same time, but it deals with Veteran Hailey. Veteran Hailey gets “stuck” at times. Not just when she panics (which would obviously make sense not to move when you’re panicking depending on the situation), but on invisible walls and can’t go anywhere. It happened three times on my play through and it was rather frustrating. I’d click on her and tell her to move and the game would accept what I told it to do, but when the action phase started she’d just wiggle in place and not shoot or do anything. On one level I had to finish with three of the four soldiers because Hailey found a nice rock to cuddle and just wouldn’t let go. (I didn’t think the rock looked that attractive…) On another stage, canceling all of her actions and telling her to go to a different location worked thankfully. It’s only been her, but on the bright side, you can still finish the missions by getting one person to the exit point (most of the time from what I remember). That’s why it’s not a major issue, but the level of difficulty definitely goes up when you’re down a man. Woman! I meant down a woman. (Phew, close one!) (To note: a recent patch makes it sound like they may have fixed this in some areas: “Characters would sometimes get stuck in/behind cover.” I haven’t noticed it since, but I did say it was rare.)With the few hours I’ve spent in the game, I’m still not quite sure what the pacing of Broken Lines is supposed to be. You start the game with a plane crash behind enemy lines and there’s some weird crap going on with this nasty yellow fog. You kind of want to get out of there right? But there’s an option to sneak during the missions… and none of my people have a knife with a one-stab-kill ability. I spent the whole game running from one place to the next and let the game stop me when I needed to clear out some baddies. (What your people don’t stop to do is shoot if/when an enemy runs through the middle of your lines. Your people will continue to shoot even at each other to get a bullet in the enemy. This only happened once and it was bad positioning on my part, but I still blame AI.) As of the writing of this review, haven’t “lost” anyone officially. (I may or may not have scum-saved, but you’ll never get that information from me!) At the end of each level you’ll be rewarded depending on how fast you made it through, how many baddies you’ve killed and if you lost anyone or not. This “Missions summary” screen gives me the impression that faster is better, but I’m not really sure.Another thing to worry about in-game is that everyone in your group needs to eat. Yes, that makes sense. However, after every mission you’ll consume supplies based on the number of people that are in your party. With a full group, the supplies go down rather quickly. Am I supposed to have people die off to make it easier? You can only buy so many supplies from Izkor and you can’t eat the bandages or guns he sells. If you were to take your time, there are supply crates in most levels that I’ve noticed. However, the minute you hit that exit, you leave. There’s no extra exploring. I don’t see much benefit from getting medals for a faster completion at that cost since you can’t eat the medals. Maybe I should be taking it slower…Score: Gewd/TastyI want to like Broken Lines more. The game mechanics alone are fantastic and the “stop your action phase when an enemy is spotted” feels so right I wonder why it wasn’t implemented in more games in the genre. However, there were a few hiccups along the way that don’t really ruin the experience, but don’t help it either. In the end, while I’m not expecting kittens and unicorns, Broken Lines has a very interesting storyline, but tends to come off as a “horrors of war” game with hope dwindling throughout the game. There’s a place for this, no doubt, but it creates a really heavy atmosphere that wears on me with play. The levity and humor in the beginning help, but as the situation gets worse, well… so does the mood. If you can get into all of that, the ride is rather fantastic, but I think I need to play something with a bit more levity like Animal Crossing in between every other level.

_childDocuments_.review: A short-but-brilliant game.  A little bit Jagged Alliance, a little bit Frozen Synapse.  Tense and challenging without resorting to computer cheats or rigged scenarios.  The no-going-back nature of it may turn some off, but it gives the minimalist story depth and stakes, and the ability to retry missions (and retry from checkpoints no less) at a slight morale penalty strikes the perfect blend of rewarding smart play but not unduly punishing trying something brave but foolish.  It's probably a little easy on the default level; I wished I'd amped it up a bit, and will in some future replay.   Those looking for an XCOM-like campaign will be disappointed in its terseness, but those who enjoy retrying missions over and over at increasing difficulty will love it.

_childDocuments_.review: After 7 hours just completed the campaign.... and what a journey.It may seem a bit short, but while playing you are offered to choose beteween 2 or 3 missions in some points, so it has a high replay value. Also it offers 5 alterative endings.In fact i find the duration is fair, because making it longer it will became boring, because the gampley is simple, so extending it to reach the endings will be a bad thing for most of the people.To sum up the experience, you will find here  an interesting plot, that it goes "in crescendo", with a dark atmosphere, a tense ambient, all put in together with an awesom OST that makes you feel the troubles your soldiers are facing.There's just a little of voiceover with a female narrator just to give ambience, but the main dialogues are without dubing. Its the only down i can find for this game. Because if they had a voice for each character, they would had more personality, because a couple of them feel a little bit simmilar.Anyway, this game is a must have for anywone who likes TurnBased Strategy, it has a fresh (but simple) approach to the genre. And anyone who likes IIWW with a bit of Sci Fi will enjoy the experience. 25 bucks is a fair price for this.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed completing my first playthrough today. I took my time and the campaign took about 11 hours. I will probably do a second playthough to see if I can get a different ending. It seemed like I there were a handful of other missions that I could have found by making different decisions. _childDocuments_.review: After finishing the campaign what I've got to say is that this could be a great game; the only thing that I don't like about this game is the story. They try to make this weird, nazi, cthulhu cross over thing happen and it just subtracts from the experience. The game mechanics are really fun and the pause and play is exceptional. My wish list on the next iteration of a game like this would be: -Stick to a standard historical or even scifi war storyline instead of some Lovecraftian Strange one.-Gear looting; including depletion of bullets and so more survival feeling given limited resources and weapons.-More clarity around penalties and bonuses including reloading from checkpoint being a retry penalty. -More specialization for characters rather than every character being potentially good at assault. -More emphasis on squad dynamics where putting certain fire teams together perform better in various ways.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves more attention. I didn't finish it yet, but once I do I will update my review. So far the game is really good, is a slow starter tho. But after day 4 things get really good. Enemy variety isn't the best there is, but the tactical approach to it makes up for the lack of them.Another thing I like is the soldier management. You have to manage resources and the morale of your guys, also decide on events that will give you some perks, etc. The game has some replayability on it, for example you choose paths so that leads you to experiment  playthroughs in a different way. For example you can decide to go and infiltrate at night or go blasting the front door and delivering mayhem. You can play it slow stealth or be rambo style and rape everything.Of course is not AAA, but what they do with Art, graphics, music I think is really well presented for a indie game. It does feel like a finished product, so far I didn't encounter any bugs at all. AI is decent, i'm playing on hard difficulty and even tho I didn't find it super difficult, I had to reset some encounters once or twice.If you like tactical simultaneous turns, and are appreciative of flanking tactics or luring enemies, this game will be a blast. WEGO for me is the best kind of tactical turn based system, and this game is awesome. For the price, is well worth it.

name: Airplane Mode
detailed_description: This is a game where you play as a window seat passenger for the real-time duration of a long-haul commercial flight across the Atlantic. Airplane Mode's gameplay explores the airline travel experience down to every last detail—from the design of your seat and the seatback in front of you, to the contents of your carry-on bag and smartphone hard drive, to the behaviors of cabin crew and other passengers. The circumstances of your flight will change every time you play. Simply put, Airplane Mode is the most realistic flight simulation ever created. Sit back, relax, and enjoy. Featuring: Taxi, take-off, and landing. Fairly accurate satellite imagery of your flight path. Snacks, premium beverages, and meal service (incl. fish option). Carry-on bag with a book, headphones, pen, and charging cable. Overhead reading light and complimentary aircraft information card. Inflight safety video produced by IFC's in-house team of expert air hosts. Randomized events on every playthrough, such as turbulence, bad wifi, and delays. Authentic ambient noise—whose baby is that???* Inflight entertainment system featuring a flight tracker and hit movies of the 1930s. Our award-winning magazine, Stratospheres, filled with articles, crosswords, and Sudoku. From AMC Games, IFC, Bacronym, and the NYU Game Center Incubator. *Crying baby not guaranteed on every flight.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the idea - interactive experience with some small random elements making each "flight" a little different. Still it is more like a concept demo rather than a real deal. There are only two routes (2h and 5h flights), no airplane to choose from (and the only one is fictional), animations are clunky, world behind your window looks terrible, engine sound during taxiing is some short loop (throttle going up and down with no sense). Your avatar have mobile phone, but there are some bugs with its interface making me unable to quit the game from the menu (I had to use Alt+F4). From time to time "game" also freezes. There are few more bugs and glitches - for such a small project it should be more polished for the release. Additional customization options like choosing your seat, time of day etc. could be a nice addition. For now I would not recommend this experience (it is not a game) for this price. Refunded.

_childDocuments_.review: As a frequent flyer, a pilot and a major avgeek I think I am more than qualified to review this game.  I rarely make game reviews but I really want to see improvements to this game with so much potential.  I will separate this review in Pros and Cons and give an overall conclusion.Pros: - The attention to Detail in the game is pretty good.  I was impressed by the in-flight magazine which had legible articles and the fact that you could read a book from your carryon bag and watch some old movies on the seatback IFE  was very impressive.   It just shows that the developpers put  a lot of effort into the product and the content isn't superficial its not just smoke and mirrors.  If you can click on it there is depth to it.  I hope they keep this up for any addition- The Sound.  The sound isn't perfect but I never expect it to be, It's not possible to fully replicate the sound onboard. I think overall the sound was pretty good it did cut out shortly after takeoff and that was really annoying and killed the experience for a few minutes.  But after that the sound came back and it was okay.  -Interactivity: The game is very interactive for what it is.  I could manipulate the contents of the Seatback Pocket, the contents of my bag, the window, the seatbelt, the the functions on the Inflight Entertainement System, the remote control, the air vents. I was very pleased. -VisualsThe visuals in the cabin are pretty good Outside was okay but I will get to that later.  The In flight magazine was great, the IFE was really good, the people were a little Yikes... but overall I was happy with the visuals inside the cabinBonus: I love Pan Atlantica.  I have created made up airlines myself and I love the creation of new airlines. The more details about it the better.CONS: So as much as i enjoyed this game there were many things that made my Avgeek self want to quit the game and burn my computer.1. For the love of Aviation FIX THE AIRPLANE TAKEOFF FOR Airplanes that takeoff before our flight!  I was watching the plane ahead of us takeoff and i saw it go down the runway slowly, then basically go vertical without rotating.... I wanted to commit No Breathing.  I was fuming after that takeoff by the "Fly American" Jet that took off before us.  That was pretty bad animation. Please fix this in a future update.2.  Fixing outside animation.  I mentioned the Airplane thing because that's a problem of its own. But there are a bunch of smaller things that should be fixed.  -When the flaps go down.  They don't go down during the takeoff roll, they usually go down before you start taxiing after pushback.  If they don't go down then they go down while taxiing to the runway.  - There could be more variety when it comes to outside scenery.  Maybe some more aircraft variety or more accurate terrain for after takeoff or during landing.  -The Wing doesn't seem very real.  I think a better job could be done with it especially for the JFK-Halifax route.  Also I never saw any strobes or position lights or any other lights that would be on the wing during takeoff and landing. -Timing of things.  Things go really fast at the beginning of the flight.  The plane pushes back and starts taxiing really quickly. I barely looked around the cabin, the boarding door was closed and the plane started taxiing and I was like WOAH! That was quick!- The fake airplane....Come on... an E320-300....?  Is it not possible to get an actual aircraft type in there. I mean at the same time it makes sense with the wing but it kind of rubbed on me the wrong way.- Other glitches: The sound cut out at one point the music on my phone wouldn't (in game) wouldn't play.- Also. The Pan Atlantica route map does not show Halifax as a destination but we are flying to Halifax.... A bit of a mixup there.Recommendations: It would be cool if there was more modern music to listen toBetter Scenery during cruise (doesn't have to be detailed just not always clouds but that's not necessary)IT WOULD BE REALLY COOL if you could walk around the cabin or choose your seat before departure! That way there could be multiple views and more things to do to make it more realistic.  Adding more routes would be pretty cool too Conclusion:I am honestly very happy about the game even though I was critical about certain aspects.  That is just because I am a stickler about airplane stuff. (I am the type of person watching a movie with airplanes in it and I go "that makes no sense! WTF" But overall I am happy with it but I do hope changes will be made to make the game more realistic!Hope this helps! Happy Flying!

_childDocuments_.review: Very niche game. You either get it or you dont! I miss air travel (thanks, 2020), and i like niche, novelty immersive simulators that emulate mundane processes. I did the 2 hour flight, and enjoyed messing with all the stuff!  Despite being a bit rough around the edges, there's a lot of detail and things to do and i feel like there's more ive not discovered yet, looking at the achievements list.It would be nice if there were a choice of books to read, or more things to watch - or better still, the ability to input your own entertainment, or maybe even youtube URLs! It was a fun novelty experience that made me smile anyway! _childDocuments_.review: . There’s a lot of problems that take away from the enjoyment of the experience, with the most glaring one being that it crashes constantly, even when it’s not suffering from memory leaks or overconsumption of resources. There are some minor points that also take away from enjoyment that immersive experiences like this game rely on for value.In Airplane Mode, you play as an avatar on a commercial flight of either two hours in length where you fly from New York to Nova Scotia, or six hours where you fly from New York to Iceland. On this flight you essentially try to keep yourself occupied as if you were  on the flight. Something that’s minorly notable is that this is AMC Games’ first published title, and I thought that was interesting that they chose to go with this.You’re given some tools such as a phone (that you have to charge!) that has some music tracks, podcasts, and photos to look at. In a bag that rests under the chair in front of you, you can access a book (Against the Grain by J.K. Huysmans), a sketchbook, some sleeping aids, wireless headphones, a pen for writing, and the aforementioned phone charger. The plane provides you a flight monitor where you can see your progress on the flight, watch some copyright-free movies, and order food and drink. If you’ve been on a flight before, the game doesn’t skip out on the in-seat features. There’s also a magazine that you can read through that contains a crossword puzzle, a sudoku puzzle, and a kakuro puzzle in addition to some light articles.Even though this is a simulator, you don’t get to skip the instructional flight video and you better fasten your seatbelt, or else the flight attendant is going to stand and stare at you. There’s also some random events that take place on the flight, but the only ones I was able to experience are being seated next to different models or being placed in a different line in the taxi-queue before takeoff.That covers the basics of the game, so let’s talk about what I enjoyed.I do enjoy the randomized elements on flights, even though I only really got to experience a couple. If the game played for longer, I would have liked to experience more, but I guess I’ll say I’m happy with what I experienced so far.Secondly, I think the voice acting is appropriate. There’s a tone of apathy in the pilot’s voice that captures the experiences I’ve had on airplanes, but enough compassion to convince me that he won’t be diving the plane head-first into the Atlantic. Flight attendants are also convincing enough for me to confuse their concern with affection.Sadly, that’s about all I enjoyed during my playtime, so let’s move onto what I didn’t like.I’ll start with minor inconveniences and lead up to the most critical shortcomings, so I’ll start with  Since you’re using a pen, you’re not able to erase what you write, so if you make a mistake on your puzzles you better look for a coping mechanism because you’re not undoing your mistakes.Next up is that there is some very obnoxious bugs in the phone UI. I was never able to successfully pair my headphones to my phone because I would get stuck in two different parts of the phone’s UI where I couldn’t go . So… unfortunately, I did not get to experience the pre-provided music tracks or podcasts. This happened consistently on the two times I used the phone before I decided it was a waste of time to try and work around it.Thirdly, I found some either graphical bugs or oversights, mostly originating from the provided magazine. One was that there’s this workout ad that has text that goes outside of the provided text boxes. I guess this  be on purpose, but it doesn’t look good. Another one was that on the sudoku puzzle, there’s a small cornerstone that talks about the answers to , but it doesn’t show all 81 squares as it skims the outer layer all around. Finally, there’s a map of the provided routes for the flight provider, but there’s no shown route provided to Nova Scotia which at the time, I was on.Another thing that bothers me is that this game hides all 31 achievements in the Steam library. However, Steam and its infinite wisdom, shows you all the achievements on the store page, just without the descriptions on how to achieve them. So, if you go through the list, you’ll see some achievements that should be easily achievable, however, during my five attempts at playing the game I had gotten zero achievements. This leads me to believe that either you get achievements at the end of a flight, which doesn’t make that much sense, or achievements are broken outright. But also, why are  31 achievements hidden anyway? They spoil nothing except the gameplay element they depend on. There’s no story to lose.Lastly, the game crashes . While I did experience the dev-acknowledged memory leak once, the game did crash four other times without the memory leak bug appearing or other system resources being maxed out. It crashed at random intervals so I don’t believe it’s anything in specific that I’m doing. The first time was during the memory leak and the game crashed after five minutes in the two hour flight; next was the game crashing after eight minutes on the six hour flight. Third happened 13 minutes into going through the phone in the two hour flight, fourth was about an hour into my two hour flight while I was working on the sudoku puzzle, and fifth and final was 20 minutes into the two hour flight while I was working on the sudoku puzzle again.All in all, I gave the game a lot of different chances, but it’s just broken and nigh-impossible to enjoy.Well, that’s about everything we’ve got character-count for today. The dev acknowledged the memory leak problem which is a start, but is just a small step in the long line of fixes I’d hope for before I would recommend this game. It’s a shame, because I think the experience has a lot of charm to it and appeals to me, but it’s poorly executed in the current state of things.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted to sit and do nothing for several hours while watching old movies from the 1930's? Well, you can either watch them for free online (since they are so old that they are no longer copyright protected) or you can pay money to watch them in this game while pretending to sit in an airplane... while doing... nothing.Just to be clear, the trailers you watch on the store page are far more entertaining than the actual game itself. This is a game about sitting in a seat for 6 hours while watching a small TV or playing solitaire.I bought this knowing it was likely going to suck, but hopeful that maybe it had some hidden, deeper meaning or maybe some comedy elements, maybe it was a satire or a parody or an experiment of some kind. You can't even interact with other passengers, you just sit there isolated while listening to a planes engines and nothing happens. The audio of the engines isn't even accurate, you want to treat this like a sim game? You can't even be properly immersed, it's the same couple seconds of looped audio of the throttle going up and down, no one throttles up and down… up and down…up and down, it's a total lack of attention to detail.If you have the ability to sit down at home while doing nothing, you already own this game, it's called being bored at home while doing nothing. And the options you have in game to alleviate that boredom are the same as you have at home: watch TV, listen to music or play games. The difference is what's "in this game" is very likely far more limited than what's already available to you through any other venue of TV, music or games. Old black and white movies, a few stale music tracks and a couple of solitaire card games. That's what you are paying for.it's also technically flawed. For as simple a game as it is; they didn't even manage a quality release. When the flight attendants give their lecture about how to buckle your seat belt the animations don't even sync with the audio. Moving your phone, remote or books around can glitch or leave things stuck inside of each other.And it's functionally incomplete. There's no way to save the game, you have to complete an entire session at once if you want to get to the end. And you can't idle the game while playing multiple games, there's no windowed mode and alt-tab pauses the game. So in order to actually see the entire thing you'll need to dedicate the entire block of time in one sitting. I hope you have a second computer / tablet / phone / TV or something to do IRL while your computer sits and does nothing for a while.There's not much else to say, because there really just isn't anything here.--------------------EDIT 1: And all of those positive reviews with less than 2 hours of play time, might as well have nothing to say: They didn't even bother to finish the game. They turned it on, watched one old movie from the 1930's and turned it off. If you think that has value, there's plenty of them on YouTube for free. Or go do the crossword puzzle in your local newspaper, at least those have a new one daily.And the forums are overrun with people claiming that to enjoy the game "you just need some imagination and you can entertain yourself" well freaking duh, but I can do that for free without needing this game!Maybe we've come to a point in history where I should just make a game called "Boredom for narcissists" and it will just turn on your computers camera and let you stare at yourself, you'll have all the fun of looking in a mirror and making funny faces, for just a small fee. That's the kind of people that will truly love this game.--------------------EDIT 2: They "updated" the game, but all they seem to have done is introduce more bugs and glitches. Sometimes the in game buttons don't even work now and even the quit game button was not functional (alt+F4 to the rescue). This abomination of a trash game is getting worse instead of better. For such a small nothing of a game (where you mostly just sit and do nothing) they still managed to make it a terrible and buggy experience instead of a relaxing environment. I can't even enjoy it "on the side" while playing other idle games because it just pauses if it's not the main focus and thus you can't multitask the game if you want the achievements. You actively have to bore yourself to death to even finish the achievements.I can't wait to uninstall this garbage.---EDIT 3: If you find yourself owning this game for whatever reason, you might as well go ahead and try to get the achievements I guess. For me it was a 30 hour slog of turning the game on and mostly walking away to do other things, I even wrote a guide for it:I had more fun writing the guide than "playing" the game, and now I can happily uninstall this and forget it exists.---EDIT 4: Just to set the record straight for anyone that reads my (positive) review for  Here's the contrast:1. Desert Bus is intentionally boring, this isn't supposed to be, but it is anyway.2. Desert Bus lets you alt-tab and multitask while the game is still running, letting you play it like an idle game in tandem with other games. This doesn't.3. Desert Bus has at least a 20 minute interview that is interesting on the radio, this doesn't..4. Desert Bus is less buggy than this.5. Desert Bus you can sit as a passenger for as long as you want or as the driver. Desert Bus you could coop with your friends and at least have people to talk with (separate voice program like Discord required, but still you're doing something together), Airplane Mode has no coop.6. Desert Bus is free, this isn't. My thoughts on a game aren't just about quality or entertainment, but also value in relation to cost. Airplane Mode has a price tag, I expect more from it than Desert Bus and yet it doesn't deliver.Neither game is "good" in the traditional sense, but Desert Bus you can download free, get the point and then either soak it up while simultaneously watching TV, listening to podcasts or alt-tabbing through other idle games. Or just know it exists as satire and not play it. This on the other hand is asking for money for what is effectively "sitting simulator" since you aren't even flying the plane.So, when I tell you that I hope Desert bus is the worst game you ever play, yea that's because there are worse games: like Airplane Mode, that will charge you money to have a boring time.---

_childDocuments_.review: As a self-proclaimed frequent flyer who's logged more miles than I can count, I was initially skeptical when I heard about "Airplane Mode." After all, how could a game possibly capture the magic and chaos of air travel? Well, consider me pleasantly surprised, because "Airplane Mode" not only met my expectations but soared right past them.From the moment I fired up the game, I felt like I was stepping into an airport terminal. The attention to detail is absolutely astounding. From the bustling crowds to the familiar sounds of boarding announcements, every aspect of the air travel experience is faithfully recreated.But what truly impressed me was the level of immersion. As someone who spends more time in airports than I'd care to admit, I can attest that "Airplane Mode" nails the feeling of being in the air. From the gentle rumble of the engines to the subtle shifts in cabin pressure, every sensation is meticulously recreated.As someone who's spent countless hours staring out airplane windows, I was blown away by the realism of the scenery below. Whether I was flying over snow-capped mountains or bustling cities, the views were breathtakingly lifelike.But "Airplane Mode" isn't just about realism—it's also about fun. The game offers a variety of in-flight activities to keep you entertained, from browsing the in-flight entertainment system to striking up conversations with fellow passengers. There's even a selection of airline-themed mini-games to keep you occupied during those long flights.In conclusion, "Airplane Mode" is a true gem of a game. Whether you're a seasoned traveler like myself or someone who's never set foot in an airport, there's something here for everyone. So buckle up, stow your tray tables, and get ready for the flight of a lifetime. Trust me, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: First, let me say that I appreciate the concept of this game. As someone who has grown up flying all her life, I miss it more than I thought I would in the wake of this pandemic. The idea of sitting with this in the background (but also interacting with the in-flight simulation) seems like a fun, wholesome idea. The problem is in its execution. The phone sometimes bricks when you hit the drop down, usually toward the beginning of the flight since that's the way you're supposed to connect your bluetooth headphones. The game itself has crashed on me twice, and the second time I made it through a full flight without crashing there was no way to quit the game because the phone had bricked sometime earlier, which meant I couldn't hit the "Quit" button. It takes up a TON of memory during play, which would be understandable if the graphics were great and/or there were lots of things to interact with and do. Unfortunately, the game feels like a bare-bones beta at the moment with mediocre if sometimes creepy graphics (watch the fight attendants help the other "passengers" who also look like creepy AI--I dare you) and very little in the way of in-flight entertainment. There's also no customization whatsoever. You don't have an avatar, and you can't customize anything from the clothing you're wearing to what's on your phone to the phone itself to the bag and its contents. I sincerely hope that the devs build up this game to its fullest potential. Given that it's sponsored by AMC, you'd think they have the money and resources for a much more fleshed out experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Once the performance and crashing bugs were fixed, this has become the sim game I always wanted, ever since I fell in love with the concept of Desert Bus (Penn & Teller's simulator).  The graphics could be improved, but they're fine for now. You can pretty much do anything you do on an actual flight except walk around a bit.  You can get to the bathroom, however, to break up the monotony.  There are also things like books, podcasts, games, and of course the in-flight status screen on the seatback.Lots of people say, "but y doe" or "I hate this game for existing", but I really love it.  I've flown quite a lot over the years, and it's awesome that they included all the details.  Like all the announcements, the animation for take-off, and even the flight instructions on the seat display.  Heck, on the shorter flight you get a snack and drink, and the longer one you get a full meal.  The guy actually comes around with the cart and hands you your food, and you click away until it's gone.  Then they even come back and pick up the refuse.  And if you want, there's a packet of sleeping pills to help speed the flight along (approx 30% each time I did it on the 6 hour flight).I like to sit and read (a real book) while it's going on in the background on my monitor, listening to the engine noise, and watching the clouds out the window.  It's just a fun little game and neat experience.  I echo those folks who say they'd love more routes, maybe the ability to walk up and down the aircraft.  Maybe even the ability to eventually play your own MP3s/4s or whatever, into it.Anyway, if you're looking for the flight experience, or heck, maybe you even know somebody whose never flown yet, go ahead and give this a try.  It's not silly, they're actually being pretty serious about your "experience"!

I have four quality of life improvement suggestions, however: (1) fix the bugs--the sound cuts out and becomes some weird low volume garble with high frequency ringing on top too often, (2) add static arms to the avatar--it currently looks creepy, (3) dim the cabin lights before takeoff, (4) add an option to invert the mouse y-axis for players who've been playing that way their entire lives (like me), and the bonus (5) it's not a dealbreaker however improve the 3d models external to the plane. name: Age of Empires III: Definitive Edition
detailed_description: Knights of the Mediterranean DLC Available Now! About the Game Age of Empires III: Definitive Edition offers players a trial of this historical single & multiplayer RTS experience. Enjoy diverse civilizations, co-op historical battles, stunning 4K Ultra HD graphics and modernized gameplay. For more ongoing fun, content unlocks will rotate monthly, which includes rotating civilizations, Hero Cosmetics and events - so come play often! Jump into the robust community – and invite a friend to play today! *Note: To unlock all features of the game please see the “Base Game” product. Age of Empires III: Definitive Edition completes the celebration of one of the most beloved real-time strategy franchises in definitive form with enhanced features and modernized gameplay. Command mighty civilizations from across Europe and the Americas or jump to the battlefields of Asia in stunning 4K Ultra HD graphics and with a fully remastered soundtrack. The trial version provides access to a rotating roster of the full game's 16 civilizations to play freely in both single player and multiplayer games, a first look at the 'Blood' Story Mode campaign, the Algiers Historical Battle, along with the tutorial and The Art of War challenge missions to learn and master the game. Jump online to play with your friends or to battle your way through a select group of random maps in skirmish games against the AI. Whichever way you choose to play, you will enjoy the stunning graphics, the fully remastered soundtrack, and modernized RTS gameplay in this third installment of the award-winning Age of Empires franchise.

The original will still be under a line of dashes.So because I like Age of Empires 3, I reached their "awesome" support team, saying that I did all of the basic "fixes" in my first mail. They asked for some files, I sent them those, did a few tests. They tell me to update my game completely ignoring all the issues I stated.So, about the updates, by the way. The updates range from 50-250 MB for now, but they will BREAK your computer. Installing these update patches takes many hours for some reason (8gb ram), and while it is installing, it will completely slow down your PC, you'll likely need a hard restart after installing whatever the hell that file was supposed to be.There have been three updates. _childDocuments_.review: Simply an improved version of the old version, which was already great to begin with.You get loads of new content for free, including a few new civilizations, the Arts of War coaching scenarios, which teach you basic but super important concepts about the game so you can have a smoother transition into the multiplayer atmosphere, and the Historical Battles, which depict important moments in history and allow you to play as one of the sides.Otherwise, the experience is just streamlined and cleaned up, the menus are easy to navigate and are intuitive, you have a bunch of new accessibility options and a reworked multiplayer UI which is much simpler and easier to use.The gameplay itself is basically unchanged, it is just as you remember it, with a few updates to modernize and update it, such as a wider camera angle, and a cleaned up ingame UI to maximize usable screen space.Notably, the multiplayer experience is much improved stability wise, going from unstable with a lot of delay to a mostly smooth and responsive experience in the Definitive Edition - competitive players will have a much smoother experience here.There is a built in mod manager in the game, allowing you to install and activate mods and custom scenarios with a click of a button in the menus. This is a welcome feature for community created content.Unfortunately, the Definitive Edition is not a direct port of old content, meaning old mods or scenarios aren't guaranteed to work flawlessly, meaning some of the fun custom gamemodes aren't as visible in the multiplayer lobbies, even though some do pop up.Finally, graphically and sonically, the game is much improved, sporting updated textures and lighting, redesigned unit and building models, and redesigned sounds and ambient effects that make the game feel current and super enjoyable to hear and look at.Overall, super enjoyable experience for new and especially old players, there's a lot to both discover and rediscover.

_childDocuments_.review: Trashy M$ "definitive" product.The whole angle they approached this remastering from speaks for some completely braindead decision making happening somewhere in the higher ranks and I hope that group/person has no influence on the upcoming AOE 4 in any form.------------------------I directly compare it to AOE 3, since that game is still playable, available and visually pleasing... involving north american indigenous factions as well as naming related to colonialism. This directly impacts gameplay by reducing usability of some buildings. The game increases polygons on all models, uses higher resolution textures and increases model count due to eye candy foliage and clutter items. Stuff that seems quite scalable by adjusting the game options, but somehow the game tanks the CPU and never reaches smooth FPS (on my mid tier system). like crashes in certain missions (e.g. "Bolivar's Revolt") or jumps to wrong missions after finishing the previous one. Cannons destroying buildings and ships exchanging broadsides flinging pieces of debris everywhere was always a standout feature of AOE 3... In this they decided to reduce the spectacle to more explosions, fire and smoke puffs. The destruction animations of buildings and ships were also downgraded. Due to Anti Aliasing techniques used and the added clutter, texture fidelity and polygon counts, units are harder to read than ever. There were always plenty of redundant units of the same class in AOE 3, but now its even harder to clearly distinguish parts of a force as anti-cav, anti-heavy-infantry, anti-light-infantry, etc. for troops (e.g. getting stuck on trees, in buildings or on top of cliffs) and villagers (e.g. stopping to gather wood although a new tree to chop is right next to them).  Movement of mixed armies still feels like crippling mobility since the troops constantly slow down and shift position to adhere to some weird formation balancing algorithm. The best bet seems to not mix units by walking speed but by knowledge of their turn-speeds and size requirements within the formation. I played through the campaigns on medium and switched to hard after 1/3 since the AI just was not doing much on maps which don't heavily rely on triggers to spawn and send waves into your base. Many Missions I remember as a struggle turned out to be so easy that I managed to casually destroy the enemy bases which the mission instructions explained me to be "too heavily defended to attack". Resembling the problems of AOE 2 DE's skirmish AI, playing against anything under hard feels like beating someone in a wheelchair. Even on the highest settings, the attack patterns and movement decisions feel odd. Total army sizes stay relatively low. Villagers often decide to gather stuff on the opposite side of the map, preferably in LOS of my forts, outposts or defending army : | While the unit stats are now easier to get to (all in one unit description element, like in AOE 2), groups are still horrible to use. To be able to utilize a units context menu, the unit has to be chosen from a list of all units of the group. There is no way to give the same action to all units of the same family (e.g. tell all cannons of different types to switch from transport to firing mode). This was a major negative in the original game and stays basically unchanged.- Nice graphics. Detailed units, pretty buildings, idyllic flora and fauna. Sexy water.- New menu UI- UI fixed for modern resolutions and can be scaled from down to 80% size.- Two new civilisations (Inkas and IKEAs)- Balance. I never played the game extensively in MP back then or now. All I remember is the meta involving early rushes, making only a handful of civs viable.- Progression of individual civs card decks is gone. Every card is now available from the beginning, and many cards have been removed to streamline the card pool. - Menu structure. Its should, on paper, reduce clicks needed to get to certain things, but it seems to trade clicks for extensive scrolling when it comes to tech trees and deck building. Not a fan. I preferred the old system.---> There are many more issues (some bugs, some technical issues, some questionable design decisions) which can be found in the forums (if one can be bothered to wade through the scummy fanboys).----------------------------As someone who didn't enjoy the classic AOE 3 gameplay much (compared to AOE 2) this product gives me nothing. It adds some eye candy while taking some away (physics destruction). While trying to play historical revisionist games with me it is still sporting the same cheesy, uninspired campaigns which neither speak to the amateur-historian in me, nor the gamer looking for some RTS challenge. The game does not use the setting in any pleasing way:-> Concerning military: Pike&Shot and later musket line-fire are awesome military concepts utilized better in other game series like Total War, Cossacks or American Conquest where they hand the player tactical tools to tinker with instead of just reskinning the same melee and ranged units seen in classical/medieval AOEs.-> Concerning Map size, design and general gameloop: Exploration and tactical/strategic decisions about building/troop positioning are much more prevalent in AOE 2, where hills, plateaus, forests and bodies of water all play a role, while AOE 3's small, balanced maps feel more like flat 2D playing fields where the better composed blob of units defeats the opposite blob while fighting over "flags" (trading posts). This could have been huge looking at the ways the new world was explored and conquered in real life.So even if you just play the game for its setting, civs and quick gameplay loop. I still recommend sticking to the original since it runs better, comes with a a bit more spectacle with its use of havoc physics and offers a surprisingly loyal fan base (which now will be split in half with the new release and maybe murdered by shutting down support... thanks, daddy M$).

_childDocuments_.review: The somewhat maligned successor to Age of Empires II (AoEII), Age of Empires III brings several innovations and challenges over its well-regard predecessor. The main innovations/challenges are (i) the fast pace of the game and (ii) the highly-differentiated nature of the factions. This makes makes the learning curve steeper for beginners especially compared to AoEII.Fortunately, in the Definitive Edition, there are now learning scenarios ("the Art of War") geared to helping newcomers master basics for single-player as well as multiplayer. There is also a plethora of good-quality videos created by aficionados on YouTube. These tutorial videos are also helpful in understanding the roles and strengths and weaknesses of the different units (e.g. musketeer vs skirmisher, culverin vs falconnet)Moreover, the strong differences between factions makes for a very unique playing experience each time, not only between the major faction "families" (African, Indigenous American, Revolutionary American, Asian and European), but also within these families (e.g. Dutch vs French, Ethiopian vs Hausa, Mexico vs United States).This game is very much alive, with many free comprehensive updates/balance changes released by the developers, a strong multiplayer scene and high-quality DLCs (especially the Knights of the Mediterranean, but the African Kingdoms was also innovative). Personally, I would like more historical scenarios to allow me to get to grips with the factions in the same way that AoEII did. However, I can only commend that time that the developers are devoting to develop new fully fleshed-out factions (e,g. Ethiopia, Italy, Hausa, Malta, Mexico) and new maps/game modes (e.g. Tycoon). Besides, there is already so much content in the game that one can acquire the DLCs (or not) when one is ready to try out new factions: no need to buy them all at the start to enjoy the "complete" experience.All in all a thoroughly enjoyable experience if you are willing to invest the time to understand the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Instead of calling them by their preferred name, Europeans insisted on using wrong or insulting words to describe the natives of the new world. This is a wrong that has been corrected, and while I can't pronounce one of the names, I prefer it to calling an entire group of people by an 18th century insult that has gone on for a couple hundred years. Two things. 1) I'd say about half of the people represented in this game have never actually colonized anything, so it's not representative of the factions used. 2) The game reflects the very lengthy colonial period as a whole, so it didn't honestly make much sense to call a 15 minute phase the colonial age. I mean, are they done being colonial once you upgrade? And weren't they already colonizing before you went up the tech tree?Similar to the previous points, the word plantation bears a very slaver-y vibe to it that may not apply to all the factions involved. The broader term "Estate" implies a wealthy landowner who has servants, and that sort of concept is absolutely ageless and universal around humanity.The original Age of Empires III was never truly accurate in its application of history. Even the well-loved AoE II has huge inaccuracies (China doesn't get gunpowder..). It isn't about what they get wrong, it's about what they try to get right.Much of the story was always fictional. Much like Civilization 5, you're able to win as a team/country that never won in real life. If they opted not to represent a real life slaver by name in their video game, then that's fine by me. Historically authentic > Historically accurate. Even the best movies are wrong, and ultimately this is a video game where game balance influences the overall expression of every civilization that was represented.The colonization of the Americas was always political. Changing the game to be more historically authentic builds upon the same politics that created the original game. The further back in time you go, the more disconnected we seem to become to the controversy, but Age of Empires III does not have that luxury, so we must remember not to freak out when little touch-ups occur over time. Think of it as the second edition to an encyclopedia.So please, focus on the fact that this game runs like crap on most machines, because that's the outrage that matters! Hopefully this review has been educational to some of you who were confused.It does. I mean, honestly, there's no real excuse. The original doesn't work out of the box for me anymore, so an updated game with improved story and extra factions is an appealing sell, especially since it's not that expensive a game. Sadly it just doesn't deliver, and there are many reviews out there that will tell you in better detail what's wrong with it.Age of Empires 2 Definitive Edition exists, and it's overall a much better game. Smoother, much more of a visual upgrade, a larger community, more factions, and (in my view) a less problematic time in history because I don't actually like colonialism even in video game settings.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate that I have to write a review like this because this game is near and dear to my heart. After playing it for almost 12 years now, I can safely say this is a poor remaster of an otherwise excellent game.The Good:Graphical improvements are top-notch, especially when it comes to the foliage, scenery, and units.New Civs that look really fun, haven't touched them just yet.Balance changes that have been needed since 2005-07.Free cards that encourage more people to play in multiplayer.The Meh:Half-assed Native American rewrite. The voice actors sound incredibly disinterested for the Iroquois and Sioux. Only made worse by the fact they outright hack up the voice overs in the campaigns to fit the new changes. It feels rushed and tacky, and that's not what we should be seeing from a company with more than enough backing behind it that hired a broader variety of voice actors to do the voice-overs for the campaigns in AOE2 DE.Discovery and Colonial Age being renamed to Exploration and Commerce age. Plantation being renamed to Estate. I can forgive the former, but the last two just feel like unnecessary changes. Not that it impacted my enjoyment of the game that much.No new orchestration of the old soundtrack compared to the rest of the definitive editions. (Some would argue the soundtrack wouldn't need it, but new renditions are always appreciated in my book.)The Bad:The audio quality in certain sections of the game ranges from minor quality loss, to sounding like they got it off of a 144p Youtube video. This is made very apparent in the cutscenes throughout the second campaign of the game.Cutscenes just don't plain work. There are some cutscenes in the game that just remain paused and never play Ex. Reunion and headed west in Act II: Ice. Uncanny valley models. Up close, many of the updated versions of the models look rather jarring up close, especially when it comes to close-ups in the Blood, Ice and Steel campaigns.Graphical issues on launch. Sure, the new textures look pretty but good luck actually getting to enjoy them with water textures bugging out.Bugs. Not just new ones, old ones from the original game that should've been ironed out by now.AI is more A than I. No water map functionality is one of the main complaints, will update as I play more.Performance Issues. I have a 1060 and can run AOE2 DE with the enhanced textures on with zero lag. Even after the recent hotfix and toning down some of the settings, it just feels choppy.UI. The UI in the original was a joke. Nobody could unironically use the massive HUD that took up most of the screen. At least it looked presentable with some interesting textures. this version is just half-assed in many regards.There are more gripes I have with this, but I don't want this review to be an entire essay. I would've been happy knowing that this game was going to release somewhere near December if it meant they could iron out some of the bugs. But, releasing it now has made it feel more like it just came out of early access.I'll update this review once a majority of the bad has been fixed here, otherwise, avoid this game and play the original version. Still works on modern computers and there are some great mods out there for it.Edit: 25 Hours later and I've played a couple of skirmish games and completed every campaign.Pros:Performance issues have been fixed somewhat. The game runs smoother on my card, but be careful not to alt tab out for too long.New Campaign Rewrite + Voice Acting: Act 2: Shadow in the Warchiefs now has completely new voice acting and a new take on the entire scenario and its context. I'm disappointed that they didn't get new Voice actors for just about every campaign.Cons:Audio Skipping: Sometimes while playing the game, the audio will loop over, almost like I'm playing the game off of a scratched disc

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Age of Empires franchise and have hundreds of hours of play time in legacy Age of Empires 3. I really want to love this version of the game but I cannot recommend it currently until it is patched. It is not "definitive" or polished in any way. To start with the positive: PROS:- The music is epic and new introduction chords add a lot of flair to each civilization.- Two new civilizations have been added (Swedes and Inca); although some balancing is needed.- New UI options and hotkey functions allow for plenty of customization.-The revolt system has been completely overhauled to allow for many new interesting options.-All home city cards are unlocked - this means no pointless grinding to unlock powerful civilization abilities.-New maps that are more balanced for online play.- The game uses the AoE3 ESOC community patch with really helps to balance the game in general.-"Art of War" feature allows new players to learn the game and "Historical Battle Mode" adds twists and challenges for the player.CONS:-Unit pathing is absolutely horrendous (even worse than the old version of game).- The AI is laughable (sometimes the AI will not even attack you or forget to build villagers).-Units can sometimes clip into cliffs, trade-posts and other objects permanently preventing movement.-Lag and de-sync errors  in online play (although not as bad as original AoE3-Political-correctness has changed many aspects of native civilizations. Two specific changes are lazy and are poorly implemented. The "fire-pit" has been re-named to "community plaza" and units using it look idle and frozen. A new 25 wood building (much like a gold camp from AoE2) was added for gold mines and looks like your villagers are lazily gathering berries for some reason. These changes do not add any value to the game.-The new voice lines for the Native civilizations are too quiet and do not sound high quality like other voice lines of the game. -Sound effects have been changed and cannons sound terrible (compared to the old game). These are my thoughts on the definitive edition of Age of Empires Three. I have faith that the devs will fix many of the issues and give the game a solid 5/10 in it's current state. If the game goes on sale I would suggest it.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played an HD version if there was one before like for AOE2, so I'm just going off of what I remember but while it's definitely a different beast all together than AOE2, I think AOE3: DE can stand on it's own two feet. I love the amount of zoom allowed, I like being able to be super picky with graphics settings, I like the little nice touches added, like a cannon ball having physics programmed for it, allowing it to smoothly roll down an incline and make a large splash into the water. It's also fun when corpses of your enemy fly 20 feet in the air and then splash into the water, but don't tell anyone that.My only real complaint is I very much dislike the health bars for units. I liked the previous AOEs where I could clearly see an HP bar above their heads, clearly, from any zoom, and do "intense" micro like walking a wounded soldier away. Still, I'd like to save more units please, I would like those HP bars to at least bigger.Also, I've not done any of the story, I've only done skirmishes so far, playing the United States challenge. And let me say something about that. I love how this DLC was released. You can buy it right away if you wish. But if you need a few grand in the bank just so you can say that you're broke, being able to earn it for free with challenges is cause for high marks indeed.I know some people are unhappy with the United States being OP right now, but I hope they will chill and enjoy the game again when they realize that the US is blatantly OP for now, to draw attention and players into the game, and for them, money from wallets. Once the hype is gone, they're going to rebalance the US to make sure the people they brought in, stay with the game and aren't getting steamrolled all the time.Also, the graphics for ship combat and building destruction in nice and meaty, which is weird since it's all wood, but when you broadside or have 6 heavy cannons open up on a town hall, the impact feels very nice. The explosions are bright, and seeing chunks of wood and debris fly through the air and splash into the water is very, very satisfying. Good weight and impact.If I start to come across some real issues or my opinion changes for some reason, I'll update the review, but for now, I can give a pretty confident thumbs up.*Update* Really, my only complaint is that the game lacks any real structure. The campaigns are headache inducing levels of boring. The multiplayer isn't that great either, a lot of instances of less then three minutes into the game and Imperial Age cannons are rolling towards you.The game is really good when there are structured challenges, such as the United States event, but dull campaigns, MP that really could use a few pass overs with better anti-cheat software, and "smarter" AI would be nice. I doubt there will be much effort other than balance and server maintenance with AOE IV already announced. Hopefully it's AI will be better.I hope that we don't get the levels of disappointment that Humankind was to Civilization with poor balance and somehow even worse AI.

_childDocuments_.review: First i must start with an apology i gave this game an unfair write up upon first playing as a bug riddled mess not knowing at the time one of my ram cards had failed which was causing me to crash.The game still in my opinion needs a bit more re balancing and tweaking but for the most part it is a sold if somewhat modernised RTS.If you are coming to this game from older age of empires game know that resource gathering has been streamlined stone has been removed and you know longer need to build storage pits ect to gather and gathering is automated upon being assigned wood gold or wood. this makes this age of empires far more combat involved.its mainly to be enjoyed in a 4v4 style though FFA can be enabled as well the maps were designed to play into the 4v4 setting.Combat is the main focus here so expect to be thrown into it much faster than previous age games all round its an enjoyable faster paced game. with each game lasting 30-50mins a piece a much faster game than previous Age.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Age of Empires III on Steam for almost 350 hours and I've played the CD version for many hundreds of hours more than that. I love the original game and I was elated to hear that AOE III was getting the same Definitive Edition treatment that AOE I and II received. I really enjoy AOE II DE and it's my current go-to game to play when I have a few hours free. I purchased AOE I DE on the Microsoft store and it was a buggy mess, so I purchased it on Steam so the multiplayer would be easier to set up. Honestly, I found the entire AOE I DE experience to be a mess until I purchased it on Steam - I should have learned :(I didn't pick up AOE II DE until almost a year after it was released and I was very pleased with the remaster. The graphics are beautiful and the AI seems intelligent and well-rounded. I do think there are too many campaigns now and I find it more rewarding to just play standard games instead of replaying campaigns I already finished when I was a kid.This brings us to AOE III DE. Like I said at the beginning, I was so excited to see what they changed. I thought a new campaign series could be in order - something to rival the previous campaigns from the original game or its two expansions. I played the original campaigns more than once and I loved the storytelling and the rich history that unfolded.I am very frustrated about the actual mechanics and underlying coding that went into this game. I have a really good setup and this game crashes my computer every 40 minutes (I'm talking a mid-tier dedicated GPU, the best i7 processor money could buy at the time, an SSD, 16 GB ram, and a PC mark score of over 3500. I understand this is slightly below the "recommended" levels, but HOW do the changes that were made take up this much processing power? You got rid of ship physics. The general movements of the units and functionality of the AI remains the same. That means that all of the processing power is going to the visuals (I like pretty leaves as much as the next guy, but I really like playing games more than seeing leaves flutter in the wind). I set everything to low and ran the game at the lowest resolution and THEN I could play without it crashing - but it looks like a marshmallow....I love the Age of Empires franchise. AOE I was the first game I poured hours into as a child and AOE III felt like the AOE game I always wanted. I was thoroughly disappointed with the lackluster work the developers did on this Definitive Edition.To make the Age of Empires III community happy you would need to:1. Add a full-length campaign that is full of rich history, interesting characters, and quality voice and video work.2. Make the game run on mid-tier systems without issue.3. Fix the multiplayer issues that so many people have already complained about (I tried to play a game with my long-time AOE III friends and it crashed on us all after 40 minutes).4. Put the card system back so we have to unlock stuff. The cards are organized so poorly now and it's no fun anymore to build decks.5. Bring back our ship physics!If these changes are made, I could give this game a good rating. I hope that Age of Empires IV has nothing to do with any of the thinking, planning, and execution that went into this Definitive Edition.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok.  I read all the reviews from everyone but still decided to give this game a try.  Now I'm a 55 year old leukemia patient who has played every strategy game there is going back to the days of stronghold, AOG, Rise of Nations, etc.(does anyone remember KKND2 which was awesome!)  For a while, I gave up on PC games and went to XBOX games but none of the xbox games distracted me enough from my leukemia symptoms (I needed more strategy).  I'm also a big history buff (see Patrons which is awesome if you're a COH/Xcom fan).  I've only played this game so far for 4 hours at the Revolutionary selection where you start out as indians and work your way up to Washington's revolutionary war.  Are there a few flaws in the game (yes) I mean in regards to sometimes your military might get confused on where to go and walk around trees.  Could that be because I'm just getting back into PC games and re-playing games like CC, Red Alert and so on...., maybe.  But I gotta tell ya, as a fan of distraction and playing games to help you, this game plays out the single-player campaigns like you were there (for instance:  George Washingtons revolutionary war was a game of chance to win.  Follow the right path, you succeed (save often - my only complaint is that you must remember your last save filename otherwise it gets buried in a scheme I still can't understand.)  Anyway, it makes you feel like you're there.  And as a developer myself, you can really see the attention to detail the developers made in making this game.  All the other reviews are probably from the new age that can critique the game-play at the advance level.  When I set a game to "Easy", it means I want to play to enjoy the game at a simple pace (I want to play a lot of other strategy games so I'm not interested in conquering this game at it's max level).  Am I dumb to play it at easy, well, I helped revamp the WI Lottery code so I guess I know a little bit about coding. I'm not going to criticize the game for giving me what I want (an easy quick game to enjoy and pass time.  I won't ever get stuck and put the game on the shelf like other games (cough, cough - you know - the ones where you get to level 20 and suddenly it becomes impossible to play even at easy level because the game thinks you should have "learned").  I give the developers 5 stars for their effort in this fantastic game.  Everything from the birds that fly over to the bears, fish and other attention to details so many other games lack in developing.  As a big Stronghold fan, I'm hoping to enjoy the rest of the campaigns on this game.  If you're like me and looking for something to distract 10+ hours in a day (for some reason or other), this will easily do it.  If you like easy level, expect easy level to be easy and for those who aren't an expert in single-player war-fare tactics (at least what I've played so far), you'll enjoy the pace.  I can't speak for the multi-player since I'm not a multi-player fan or good enough to play against the new age of players but this game... for me.... is a thumbs up!
