_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Recommended with the caveat that you either lower your expectations or wait 2-3 months before buying.Even though I'm giving this a recommended, many of the negative reviews have fair points and its current review score is, for the most part, deserved. I'm pretty much only playing competitive multiplayer (haven't even touched the campaign or art of war missions yet), and so my review will mostly be based on that.I'll just briefly summarize the cons because there are plenty of other reviews that go into detail on them.- The game would have benefited a lot if they had waited 2 months before releasing and took some time to fix some of the issues. Lag, crashes, lobby system that won't let you scroll, etc.- I'm not talking about the name changes for the native civs, or the flag changes, or the firepit -> community plaza. Those are at least attempting to fix historical accuracies. I'm talking about removing the word colonial from a game that is based around colonialism and takes place in the era where colonialism was taking place. Normally I wouldn't mind, for the most part these changes don't effect gameplay too much, but when combined with the state that this game was released in it kind of feels like an extra slap in the face. How much time and effort went into determining what might be offensive and what needs to be changed, that could have been spent making the game more functional? I believe that if this were the biggest/only issue with Aoe3DE, it would be infinitely more well received, and the majority of reviews would be positive.- In its current state, the game has not earned the title "definitive edition". You cannot message friends, you cannot invite people to lobbies unless you have them added on steam, you cannot look at other lobbies while you are hosting one. Playability is also worse, the graphics look amazing when zoomed in but if you zoom out a bit (like, enough to play the game) it looks blurry and it's difficult to differentiate units. The age up screen blocks your resource count. You need to download user created mods in order to solve these problems. There are a lot more little annoying things that were not a thing on legacy Aoe3.- I only play multiplayer, so I haven't experienced this for myself. However, for a large portion of the community, the campaign is a big selling point, and if it's not functional then that's a huge problem, so I'll still mention it.I've been playing Aoe3 for 10 years, and seeing these issues and the negative reviews that resulted from them was disappointing to say the least. How many people are going to be understandably turned off the game because of this?So, why the positive review?- There was already one hotfix between the game's release and now, and I'm expecting more. Aoe2DE (which I have 250 hours on) also released in a pretty bad state and is still going strong now, in no small part due to efforts from the devs. Maybe I have too much faith in the devs, Aoe2DE was both a bigger game and not released in as bad a state as Aoe3 DE, but I am expecting the same for Aoe3 DE.- The game is far more active than before, and it's easier to find games. Viewers on twitch have gone up as well, with some relatively big streamers giving it a try. It's just amazing to see.- Legacy Aoe3 was peer to peer. If someone had a bad computer or connection, everyone playing with them suffered. The switch to server based multiplayer in Aoe3 for me is a godsend, even though it's far from perfect atm.- Legacy Aoe3 was left in a horribly imbalanced state. Maps would sometimes spawn without a start hunt, or with your second hunt not in herdable distance. Civs like Iro and Otto were pretty much unbeatable. Eventually, we started playing on a community made patch, which implemented both community made maps and changes made with input from top players. Matchmaking on the community made patch was unfortunately dead; to get games, you had to host or join games.  Changes from that community made patch have been made official with Aoe3 DE, and for the first time ever, I am able to do matchmaking with fair maps and far superior balance. I know some people prefer the lobby system of hosting and joining games, but to me, this is also a godsend.- For single-player, you can make arguments either way, some people have good arguments for wanting home city leveling to have been retained for single-player. But for multiplayer, trust me, this is a good thing. It's ridiculous to force people to grind for levels in order to play on an even footing with their opponents in an RTS game. For multiplayer, I am glad they have done away with this idea entirely.- Some of the problems I described above can be solved by downloading user-created mods (the blurryness, for example). Aoe3 has a passionate community and giving them a way to easily push out quality of life mods is a big saving grace.- Incas are cool, Sweden is cool. Some things are annoying to deal with when vsing these civs (Inca strongholds, Sweden musk in melee), but with some tweaks they'll be fine.- Aoe3 is a fun and unique RTS game.I wouldn't blame or disagree with anyone choosing to leave this game a negative review or asking for a refund. The reason I'm leaving a positive review is because I have faith the devs will work hard to fix these issues, and because for me personally, the game has enough going for it that I am still able to have fun playing it. I saw some people leaving negative reviews saying they'll change it to postitive if something changes, so I'll do the opposite here. I'll leave a positive review and change it to negative if the game is in a similar state in 2-3 months. I said in the cons section that in its current state, the game does not deserve the title "definitive edition", but I believe that if the issues are worked on and fixed, and I am confident that they will be, Aoe3DE can be a competent remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: Age of Empires III DE is a worthy conclusion to the remastered trilogy and as such offers no surprises. It is questionable whether such a game has something to offer today's modern gamer, but Microsoft doesn't have to think much about that. It's enough that they think of us, the veterans who played Age of Empires at the time of its release.If you want to play a classic RTS, this trilogy is one of the best options. A huge amount of content, sensitive and well-thought-out changes and, on top of that, nicely polished graphics – all of this also applies to the current trio, even if it is the black sheep of the whole family. And even if I prefer to recommend you the practically perfect definitive edition of Age of Empires II, it does not change the fact that the definitive edition of the third part is a fun historical strategy with sophisticated systems and a decent portion of content.In the end, this is a solid remaster and update of a good strategy, whose biggest problem is that it will forever remain in the shadow of its legendary predecessor.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Age of Empires III gameplay, you'll like this. Fair warning, you are basically paying for a slightly better looking AoE3 with two new civs. Now mind you, if this was any other game you'd probably be ok paying $15 for two new factions, or rather you wouldn't be ok with it but you would do it anyway. Consider that, and consider that you also get a discount on this if you own Age III.A note on Historical Revisionism:As someone with a BA in History, and who understands the current political climate, I understand and support why you changed the names of the Sioux and Iroquois to their preferred name. That doesn't bother me in the slightest, and it really has only positives for people of those backgrounds and cultures to support their representation. However, I find it problematic that you are attempting to erase the word Colony/Colonial from a game that is about the whole colonial system. You guys felt the need to apologize for creating this game in a climate that generally had no issue with these words, and you changed them to appeal to changing political climates. What you fail to understand, is that at least your campaign does a good job of explaining the brutal and unjust nature of imperialism and colonialism. The whole India campaign is an amazing scorch of British imperialism, as the Warchief section is a scathing and honest representation of US imperialism.By changing terms and pretending this game is something it's not, all you're doing is attempting to conceal history. Terminology matters when discussing history, changing terms makes no sense. In the academic community, we don't alter colonialism from our terminology, rather, we acknowledge it for what it is/was and write or study it. Also, be mindful this game greatly exaggerates all societies and communities, and while some portrayals can be considered unsavory in our 2020 world, just note that the European communities represented are also stereotypes. Why is this important? Because it's a VIDEO GAME!

_childDocuments_.review: There's definitely bugs to iron out, but at $20 dollars it's easy to rationalize as DLC for owners of AoE 3 Complete. If you own AoE 2 DE, you probably get a discount. If you are coming into this as an AoE noob, this is the most forgiving AoE title of the bunch.tldr why you'd like the game:1. Lots of variety in civilizations and the playstyles they can do.2. Many systems are focused around team multiplayer, as well as 1v1.3. Less micro intensive, more focused on macro and strategic considerations.4. Pacing is focused around combat and gaining the advantage.5. Always want to feel like your strategy is godlike, but so is your opponents.---AoE 3 is a more beginner friendly title than AoE 2 in a few ways, and more complex in others.Pros:- Macro > Micro, secure resource gatherers, developing production, and stat increases matter more than saving a single unit. That's not to say rushing and exploiting early vulnerabilities isn't important.- Less micro-intensive, no dodging arrows, or stutter stepping.- Civilization offerings are more unique than AoE 2. Each civilization has units and buildings that change the dynamics of combat, forcing you to do exploit and adapt to the unique strength of the civilization.- Home City system allows for customization of playstyle beyond what you build.- New Politicians that open up new game play options of civilizations, further increasing players ability to tailor game play.Addressing major criticisms to the game:1. Home City cards are all unlocked rather than earned by leveling up.2. Politicians (age up bonuses) are all available without unlocking.These however come at cost to higher learning curve of opponent's civilizations and the metagame. Also there's still a lot of cheese, and all civilizations seem OP right now with this new balance.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really hoping to enhoy this, but I don't see how it can call itself a "definitive edition" when it is buggier than the original game. It just updated, I got twenty minutes into a game and it crashed on me. Even if I had saved there is still the old problem of not gaining XP for your home city, not that it really matters since there's no motivation for leveling up your home city anymore unless you're one of the 8 original civs and can change your city's appearance.As for the other changes, the new civs and maps are nice, and the new revolution system is an improvement, but I'm not a fan of most of the other changes. I get why the changed the names for the Iroquois and Sioux, and even some of the characters, I can even understand changing the discovery to exploration age, but colonial to commerce age is really arbitrary, especially since they left the imperial age as is. Was colonialism somehow worse than imperialism? There's plenty of examples of stuff like that too, in one part of the campaign Morgan Black and Sahin the Falcon engage in some banter. In the original version Morgan say's "I'm Scottish, you Turkish dog," but they cut off the "Turkish dog" part. At this point I was thinking "Whoa did they just remove anything even remotely offensive?" However, Sahin follows it up with his usual response of "all you Europeans are Frenk to me." The cherry on top is that later in the campaign Morgan refers to the "Spanish dogs" and they left it in.If they can fix the bugs and crashes, I will pick this game up again. Even then though, I'm glad I still have my original copy of the game so I don't have to listen to a badly censored version of the campaign. I'm also annoyed that steam would not acknowledge my disc copies of the game so I couldn't get a discount even though I own tha game and all the expansiions.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing the AOE series since it first came out when I was a teenager and have been playing AOE III consistently for the past 12 years. While many additions were welcomed and I was very excited for this revival, it has been a huge let down. I was happy to see some balance changes and some cards made more attractive that were seldom used. I liked that I could request to join a clan, However too much was changed that was going good and didn't need to be changed. First off the graphics, they can look impressive, but on any low settings is very blurry and the units are hard to distinguish. The original game had perfect balance of realism and recognition. The UI was greatly changed and is more distracting that everything is nearly invisible or being camoflauged with the background. The zoom is far too wide you can barely distinguish unit types. The game lobby is very chaotic. Once your in a game you cannot check on other hosted games or visit your clan room. And then there is this question, as to why do they even have a friends list? you can not see who is online and cannot chat or invite them to games. This was a huge flaw and really the main reason why I could not recommend this game over the complete edition.  How does a game with this many failures build upon a solid foundation fall apart so quickly? I feel like I could go on and on with so many poor choices for the direction the game has gone. Sad to say I want my money back and play regular old game full of cheaters and soon devoid of players.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending this game but it comes with a big caveat: this game shouldn't be treated as a sequel to AoE2. It feels, looks and plays very differently, feeling much slower and generally more forgiving on the player. However, these features that can feel like they make the game too easy (the home town shipments system) can also be very enjoyable and help speed the game up. The campaigns are also very different to AoE2, with a much stronger focus on the narrative that makes the individual missions feels much smaller and shorter when compared to AoE2's large maps that felt like a brand new quick game each time you started one.In short: I'm enjoying my time with it. I wouldn't say it is better that previous AoEs but it is nice to play something different, knowing that I can go back to the others whenever I like

_childDocuments_.review: I can still remember an interview or article, about the Warchiefs. One of the programmers or designers, cannot remember completely talked about the new civilizations. Here is mentioned that initially they were planning on adding four new civilizations. Inca’s were among them, but he explained they had to cut one civilization, because of time restrains. They ended up cutting Inca’s from the game, leaving us with the civilizations we got in the Warchiefs. This was because they felt they would be too similar to the Aztecs. I think this sums it up for the new Inca civilization.The Incas have a very similar unit selection as the Aztecs. Two good examples are the priestess and priest, maceman and skull knight. Both were pretty unique and cool units for Aztecs, but now the Incas have basically the same, but even worse the Inca ones are better. The priestess can convert units and the maceman is trainable, whereas the skull knight can only be gained from the fire pit.Not only are the units similar, the idea behind Inca is similar. Good defence, like wall upgrades, which were also a thing for the Aztecs, but now also for the Incas. The strategy of what I see is also very similar to the Aztecs.All in all this doesn’t only make for an unoriginal new civilization (not to mention the houses just being a combination of the longhouse and shrine, yet better) it also makes a whole other civilization (Aztecs) useless. Why pick Aztecs, when Incas do the same, but better?The Incas however weren’t the only new additions to the natives. There were some new changes to the existing ones, primarily the Sioux (Lakota now) and Iroqouis (also name changed).Both of the previous civilizations now have to build a special building to gather coin. This was done, because those civilizations never really mined coin in real life. This in itself could have actually made for a cool new mechanic, which could have set the natives apart from the existing ones, and maybe give them some wellneeding buffs. Needless to say, it did quite the opposite.The point of the building was to remove coin mining, yet the building is bound to a coin mine, not only that, villagers are still tasked to it, making it a barriere in coin mining, both unnecessary and actually nerfing the natives. It’s a change that didn’t benefit the game and I think a quote from the original developers fits in here. It wouldn’t be any fun to have slaves. Now what has that to do with the fur trading? Slavery was unfortunatly part of the colonial history, yet it’s not in the game, because it wouldn’t be any fun. This building might be more realistic, which is also debatable, but doesn’t add value to the gameplay and actually hurts it.Then a small thing about the minor civilizations, when the Warchiefs came out, they replaced the Sioux, Iroqouis and Aztecs with new ones, because they were now playable, yet DE, has not replaced the Inca minor civilization, which is just odd really and I would like to see it happen.In general I would have liked the developers to have put less time into the Native changes and some more in the new civilizations. They both, Swedes and Incas, have a house bonus, which we have already seen four times in the originals (Chinese, Japanese, British, Iroqouis). It would have been nice to see something new, more creative then the same old. The Swedes also feel pretty underwhelming, but that might just be me. Their unique units just feel weak/odd as their Musketeer and Dragoon counterpart have more melee attack then range, making me wonder why they even have range.Also the games performance is pretty bad, lag spikes when anyone ages up and lag spikes in general.Well to end on a positive note the new revolutions are pretty cool and some new cards are fun.

_childDocuments_.review: There is no real reason for this game to exist. It is a COMPLETE DOWNGRADE with respect to the original. I only see the following 2 improvements:- The graphics and sounds, which are basically to be expected for a remake anyways. The only downside I could say about this is that some of the lighting is too white, not allowing yo to see models correctly.- The historical battles, which are a nice refreshing addition to the game and really enjoyable.That said, both things could've simply been added as addons/dlc of the original! So, you may ask what is worse here than in the original?- Stability: I have NEVER crashed in the original, in this game I have crashed multiple times.- Glitches/bugs: people getting stuck into buildings, units getting stuck behind trees all of the sudden, ships with infinite range, units in limbo between a state of in range and not in range, having them infinitely switch between the two (and never shooting).- Pathfinding: your units will derp out when moving together, much worse than the original. Boats movement is also horrible in their default movement way.- AI: The bots bots in skirmishes and missions are TERRIBLE. Barely anything they do makes any sense, they will send you all of their settlers (even more than in the original), they will have enemy units right next to you without them attacking you (unless you attack first).- Progression: This one may be more subjective, but they removed the leveling progression in multiplayer and have everything unlocked from the start, which is unfortunate.- UI: Also subjective, but I found the UI of the original to generally be better with some exceptions.- Cutscenes: All kinds of little details present in the original are omitted.If I thought about it more I could probably remember more downgrades but I think you get the point. Maybe they should've spent more time on the game instead of making sure they accurately represent indigenous people.

_childDocuments_.review: "Dead Island 2" aims to continue the franchise's legacy with its unique blend of horror, humor, and action-packed gameplay set in a zombie-infested world. Despite high expectations, the game struggles significantly across several fronts, leading to an overwhelmingly negative experience. Here’s a detailed breakdown of the aspects that contribute to its disappointing performance.Technical Problems: A critical issue with "Dead Island 2" is its plethora of technical problems. Players have reported numerous bugs and glitches that range from minor visual oddities to game-breaking errors that can cause crashes or loss of progress. Such frequent technical interruptions severely detract from the gaming experience, making it frustrating and often unplayable.Poor Gameplay Mechanics: The core gameplay mechanics, which should be the foundation of any action game, are lackluster and poorly executed in "Dead Island 2." Combat feels clunky and unsatisfying, lacking the visceral impact and fluidity that modern zombie games strive to achieve. The movement and combat systems are cumbersome, making encounters with zombies feel more tedious than thrilling.Uninspired Story and Dialogue: The narrative and dialogue in "Dead Island 2" fall flat, lacking depth and failing to engage players. The attempts at humor and quirky characters do not resonate well, often feeling forced and out of place. This failure to deliver a compelling story or relatable characters makes the game's world feel hollow and uninspiring.Repetitive and Boring Mission Design: The missions in "Dead Island 2" are repetitively structured and quickly become monotonous. The lack of variety and creativity in mission design means that players are often tasked with similar objectives that involve little more than fetching items or clearing areas of zombies. This repetitiveness saps the enjoyment out of what should be an exciting survival horror experience.Outdated Graphics and Audio: Visually and auditorily, "Dead Island 2" does not meet the standards expected from current-gen titles. The graphics appear outdated, with poor textures and lackluster environmental designs that do not leverage modern gaming hardware capabilities. Similarly, the audio design is underwhelming, with lackluster sound effects and a forgettable soundtrack that fail to enhance the atmosphere of the game.Poor Value for Money: Considering the game's numerous issues and the overall lack of polish, "Dead Island 2" does not offer good value for its price. Players expecting a high-quality, engaging zombie survival game will likely feel that their investment is not justified given the subpar quality of the experience provided.ConclusionIn conclusion, "Dead Island 2" is a major disappointment that fails to deliver on almost every aspect that fans of the genre might expect. From its flawed mechanics and repetitive gameplay to its uninspiring narrative and technical issues, the game struggles to provide an enjoyable or memorable experience. It stands as a stark example of how not to execute a sequel in a beloved franchise, and it serves as a cautionary tale about the importance of quality control and player-centric development. I think this review is completely sufficient as I do not wish to continue playing such a bad game. However, perhaps I might keep playing to get my money's worth.NOTE: A friend from Turkey was unable to pre-order Dead Island 2 from the Steam store before the game was released, so he pre-ordered from a different store. Despite the game key being worldwide, it apparently does not work in Turkey.Review Update: My opinion on this crappy game remains the same...

_childDocuments_.review: So I had problems as many people with Epic Online Services. What I did to make it work is to uninstall Epic Games and Epic Online Services. Then I went to SteamLibrary>steamapps>common>Dead Island 2. Then here, open the configuration file (DeadIsland.ini) with the Notepad and change NoOperation=0 to NoOperation=1. Save and open the game. Then I opened the game and finally it went through. _childDocuments_.review: So lets start off with the bad:So far this game is objectively worse than the previous installment in a lot of ways. The combat feels clunky and slow, so does the movement. The dodging feels like you're wearing heavy armor in a souls like game. It feels like they just sprinkled whatever was 'in' in terms of game design over their old design, copy paste a few things and call it a day. The elemental effects are less reliable, interactions between water, electricity, fire, ect. seem to be poorly programmed and don't always behave in the same ways. The enemy spawn logic is really horrible too, with zombie popping in in predetermined 'interaction spots' withing 30-60 seconds if you walk more than a few feet from them, this combined with a lack of 'clear' mechanic that lets you exhaust the zombies in an area for a while feels like they stack up enemies to make it a slog so you don't notice how sparse and tiny all the environments are. You will notice how sparse and tiny they are because you'll be backtracking through them over and over and over again. Killing the same zombies in the same places with slightly higher numbers attached to them until it all runs together like a taco bell meal the day after. The game design gets worse with the level curve, expecting you to willing go out into the world and grind a significant amount of time before each new story mission or else face the wrath of neigh invincible skull level zombies. The content is being milked so hard it it's emaciated by the end of a couple of hours of play. On top of this you don't even get to enjoy more than a few corners of any of the areas you start play in because of artificial walls created by high level zombies that will 1 hit you, leaving the entire game feeling claustrophobic. The skill card swapping RPG elements is novel, but just not as deep or rewarding as the RPG system from the first game, everything just being tied to passively increasing stats makes each 'slayer' feel unique, but they never really feel 'fun'.The end result is bland and frustrating, even little things that are fun like the puzzles and loot rooms aren't enough to save it, and the lack of any real openness makes this feel like it just falls flat even as just an 'open world' zombie game. What's better?The graphics engine is better than last iteration, but the actual models, environments and attention to detail are barely even an incremental upgrade, the level design and levels themselves are a downgrade. The graphics it's hard to even give credit to because it's had a year to cook and the shader caching still takes longer than any other game I've played.I'm glad they released it on epic store first so that I could at least pick it up on the cheap, this piece of crap was not worth $60, it's hard to justify $30. I've played steam Greenlight games that felt more polished.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the game. I have 46 hours played but I must have spent about 10 hours afk.This is probably the first game in a long time where I just stopped playing after doing the main mission and had no regrets not doing the left over side missions. Yeah, I'm the kind of player who does all side quests before continuing with the main story in order to get as much content done as possible. By the end of this game you unlock a few side quests but I had zero desire to continue once I beat the game.The only positive about this game is the ending not being dragged out. Thank god it wasn't dragged out. The boss fight is fairly easy, very straight forward and then the last bit toward the end isn't forcing you through a massive hours long slog to get through. Only saving grace.The combat feels worse than the originals. Much slower, more clunky, less reason to smash a zombies head when it's on the ground which is something you seldom have the opportunity to do because you first have to deal a certain amount of damage to the zombie in order to smash their heads even if they're on the ground for 10 seconds unable to move. Very poorly done.Spawning zombies - Yeah, this sucks. They spawn zombies out of the ground. Literally, they come out of the ground on front of you, behind you, to the side of you, on top of you. The further you get into the game they just stop caring about trying to somewhat make the zombies spawning on top of you make sense and just flat out have them materialize right on front of you to the point you can literally run straight and run into a zombie not just spawning but materializing on front of you. Very, very bad.The perks system/level system is crap. Your max level is level 30. Guess what? Zombies level up with you so you never get a feeling of getting better. You start at 200 health and go down in 2-3 hits? You honestly think having 2-3k health at L30 is going to result in it taking more hits to down you? Nah. Doesn't matter. What does levelling do? Bigger numbers that mean absolutely nothing. You also unlock perk cards and perk slots.The card system sucks. When you level up 80% of the time you don't both to do much of anything. You don't invest in your character you don't unlock amazing skills. You unlock a card. That's it. You can pick and choose which cards to pick but by L10 to L15 you'll likely have the cards you care about(For me it was the power kick that I wasn't even using midway through the game). The cards aren't really game changers. They're just lazy passives like drop kicking deals damage and makes zombies vulnerable(yet you can mod any weapon to do the exact same thing per swing) or healing when you successfully dodge an attack or main a zombie... Rubbish stuff really, not exciting at all.The writing was really bad and the side quests were boring. Every side quest consists of "Go to X and kill these zombies". Yes, that's every side quest. The "Lost and Found" quests are pretty much the same thing except you follow a slightly longer trailer, kill a special zombie at the end of it and loot a chest for an incredibly underwhelming drop. Yeah, very bad and not worthwhile. Does it add anything to the story? Nope! Not at all. Can't even remember any of the side quests except Curtis who was completely forgotten about straight after you save him.The story is just... It's bad. I don't think anyone will care about the story after the first few hours.  It gets so convoluted and never really elaborated on in regards to Konstandt and the threeo of what looks to be cat people - yes, they basically look like they've got cat make-up on. The character and story design in this game is so bad that one of the main antagonists(Are they an antagonist? Hell if I know!) is wearing headphones... Yes, one of those "stories". Because during a zombie outbreak you'd have a try hard "mysterious" (Imagine someone saying "ooOoOoOo" as you read "mysterious) person wearing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ headphones and then talks about "the beat"... Ugh. It's just bad and the DLC, Sola, that ties into this "The Beat" arc does not help at all.Bit of a rant but honestly, this game wasn't great. I finished it, yeah... but only because it was a mindless go from A to B to C type game I got for 50% off. The DLCs aren't worth it so save your money if you're buying this on sale.The originals are actually better in gameplay, setting and mechanics. This one is smaller, more linear and far more boring.The characters: What did they do to my boy Sam B... He sounds NOTHING like the original character. It's jarring. I get it's been a few years and they couldn't get the original voice actor but holy crap is this something bad and out of place. Speaking of; why is he even in this game? He shows up out of nowhere with an incredibly loose reason to be there.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun zombie slasher! I got a little burned out on the zombie games over the years, but I'm having a lot of fun with this one! _childDocuments_.review: This is a REALLY good zombie game! But its not a Dead Island game. It has collectible skill CARDS instead of a actual skill tree (you get most of them as you level tho). Utility items like bait or molotovs are called "curveballs" and are infinite with a cool down eliminating a huge part of the crafting from the other 2 games. You can also only have 2 equipped at a time. Zombie's are a little too gimmicky this time, example: Zombies carry water tanks, flame tanks, acid tanks, I feel there are way to many. They also took the (lazy in my opinion) borderlands route with enemy variety. A "crusher" can have fire fists and send out a fire wave by hitting the ground Bloaters can be fire bloaters spewing flame like busted gas pipe. For electricity you've got zombie electricians or zombie sound guys that have some short circuiting device that will occasionally explode in a big AOE of bad. Of course this also some how makes the zombie immune to electric damage. They even made a zombie for the element "bleed". Spiky zombies. That are either filled with glass shards or wrapped in barbed wire. I think this is the dumbest thing, oh they are also immune to blood damage which yeah sure I don;t really think bleeding a zombie dry should work in the first place but whatever. To many times you have to back track to get quests done forcing you to reclear an area multiple times, sometimes in the same go. I have had plenty of zombies reverse Thanos snap materialize infront of me or just pop into exsistance as soon as I turn my back which is the most annoying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing in the world.Above ALL ELSE. the biggest sin the game commits? Doors. You cannot. Close. Doors. You cannot close ANY doors behind you. Say you accidently set off an alarm, you run into a side room to try and prevent getting swarmed but... oh no. Now that the door is open you have no idea how to close it! It simply isnt possible! It even loses ALL collision once you open it. Oversight or extremely lazy developers?With all that I AM having FUN with the game. It is a pretty good zombie killing game. Just NOT a Dead Island game. The only thing that tells me im playing a dead island game is knowing Sam B is in the game. Good things in this game: I love Ryan. He's amazing. You can use cash to make a weapon you like the same level as you so if you find a really good weapon early on you can keep it with you for the rest of the game. It feels good to bash zombie heads in with Sledge hammers. Actually this reminded me of another thing I don't like. Curb Stomp ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks. They treat it like its an execute move you can only use on zombies that are below a health threshold. Again, in the other two games I saw the curb stomp as a tool to save weapon durability on small groups or easy zombies. Just the old jump and kick. Can't do that in this one. I guess thats really what all this boils down too. There is absolutely NOTHING in this game that plays like Dead Island 1 and Riptide.  They could have just called the game "Hell-A: guest starring Sam B" Feels like one of those times that a dev studio had a game almost ready for release but last minute they get the licenses for some popular property and just shove a couple references in to be all like "see guys its the same game you all loved"!The sum of the good and bad in this could probs be summed up as "Idea Vomit"

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy games with a consistent tone in their writing, especially when it aligns seamlessly with the gameplay. Dead Island 2 is a prime example of this. While the first game felt like pure trash, this sequel embodies the kind of "good trash" that you can't help but embrace for all its quirky charm. It carries a distinct B-movie flair, and in the best possible way.I really appreciate the sarcastic and exaggerated undertone in every conversation, as it hit the perfect sweet spot for me in terms of humor. At times, it even came close to the sharp, intense tone of a GTA game. Although the main story is entirely forgettable and I didn't expect much from it going in, every other aspect of the game pleasantly surprised me.The first time I smashed a zombie's head with a giant hammer and saw it explode like a ripe melon, I knew I was in for a wild ride. The level of detail in the gore was unmatched and highly entertaining. The variety of ways to take down zombies is impressive, with every weapon feeling viable in its own way. I picked Dani, an Irish badass you’d recognize from any hardcore or punk rock concert crowd. She’s the kind who’s always the first to dive into the mosh pit. Naturally, I gravitated toward heavy weapons like hammers and even a claymore, which seemed fitting given Dani's enthusiastic commentary about them. Yes, you can actually slay zombies with a claymore! My Dark Souls fanboy heart practically screamed with joy when I discovered that, haha.There is also this nice addition of elemental damage, and some zombie types are more vulnerable to certain damage types or methods of killing. I've never felt I really needed to change my way of playing that much, except when they were straight-up immune to a certain element. This is obviously not a challenging game, but it encourages you to pick your favorite weapons and get slaying, which is very fitting in terms of tonality.The sound design is highly polished and exceptionally crisp, with some songs during key story moments being thematically spot on. That main menu song is definitely going to make its way into my usual rotation. The level design is solid and occasionally reminds me of Dishonored. While it may not achieve the same verticality or complexity, It also features some well-hidden secrets and occasional short stories conveyed through text snippets.This could very well be my surprise game of the year. I rarely enter a game with such low expectations, only to have them completely exceeded in such a positive way. The change in studios has definitely benefited the franchise, especially considering the game faced development hell at one point, which makes the consistently high quality in it's key aspects even more baffling.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mainly reviewing this as NOT RECOMMENDED for 2 things. First off, this game was an Epic Exclusive for a year and now that it's on Steam a word of warning that this game forces you to have Epic Online Service (EOS). No you don't need the Epic Games launcher, but this is far worse than that as the game will just close on you if you don't have it installed into your system. There is a workaround to bypass the EOS, but you may not be able to play Coop without it. I'm going to say that any publisher/developer that takes an Epic Exclusive deal their game should remain on Epic Games Store permanently as we don't want any of Epic Game's garbage into Steam. I'll give the PC Building Simulator 2 devs credit for doing just that. Second, to add insult to injury with the requirement of EOS for a singleplayer game they also have Denuvo enabled on this game as well. So far the game did run fine most of the time, but there were some random performance drops due to Denuvo in the background. If you were planning to buy this game I'd wait until Denuvo is completely removed from the game and if you don't want to deal with Epic Game's garbage EOS...then pirate the game. You be you.With that said, Dead Island 2 is a game that went through development hell for nearly a decade. Gone through 3 studios to develop this game as the dev team to finish it are the same ones who made Homefront: The Revolution...yeah that hardly marketed failed mediocre at best game from 2016. I find it odd that the game takes place in Los Angeles, California. Like the 3 dev teams who played GTAV thought that LA was an island, but I guess it has beaches and palm tress so technically it's island theme...question mark? Anyway, to cut it short it's long overdue sequel to 2011's Dead Island that is...mediocre at best.The Pros:- Smooth performance (most of the time)- Beautiful graphics from the UE4- Best gore details since L4D2's gore- Weapon crafting- Killing lots and lots of zambosThe Cons:- Epic Online Service REQUIRED or you don't play- Denuvo- Predictable story with a ♥♥♥♥ ending- Horribly written characters- Jank melee combat- Guns not holding enough ammo- Effects in the game that tanks performance hard during a slaughter fest- Maps are not very bigSo yeah not a bad game, but definitely mediocre at best. Ngl, after hours of playing it made me want to play Dying Light 1 and Dying Light 2 again.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 9/10Prepare to Laugh, Scream, and Bash Some Zombie Skulls!Imagine this: you're on a sunny Californian beach, the waves are crashing, the palm trees are swaying, and...wait, is that a zombie?! Welcome to Dead Island 2, where your dream vacation turns into a hilarious and blood-soaked survival adventure. If you thought you were just here for the sun and surf, think again. This game is a wild ride from start to finish, and I'm here to tell you why it’s an absolute must-play!Gameplay: A Gory Good TimeDead Island 2 is the perfect mix of adrenaline-pumping combat, strategic crafting, and open-world exploration. The game takes you through a beautifully rendered California that's now crawling with the undead. Combat is as satisfying as it gets, with melee and ranged weapons providing a brutal ballet of gore and giggles. And the crafting system? Want to add an electric shock to your machete? Go for it. The possibilities are as endless as they are ridiculous.Visuals and Sound: A Feast for the SensesThe graphics are spectacular, with vibrant, sun-soaked environments contrasting the gruesome zombie carnage. Every blood splatter and decaying corpse is rendered in grotesque detail. The sound design is top-notch, from the guttural growls of the zombies to the satisfying crunch of their bones breaking. Just make sure you don't play with the volume too high if you have neighbors—they might think you're running a horror movie marathon.Story and Characters: Surprisingly EngagingThe story and characters add an extra layer of enjoyment. You’ll meet a cast of quirky and memorable survivors, each with their own backstory and personality. The dialogue is witty, often hilarious, and helps to keep the mood light even when you're knee-deep in zombie guts.Multiplayer MayhemTeaming up with friends in multiplayer mode is an absolute blast. Coordination and strategy come into play as you tackle tougher hordes and boss fights. The chaos and fun are multiplied when you have your buddies by your side, sharing in the triumphs and hilarious failures.Conclusion: A Must-Play for Zombie FansDead Island 2 is a rollicking good time that combines intense action, dark humor, and beautiful yet horrifying environments into one unforgettable package. Whether you’re a hardcore zombie fan or just looking for a fun game to play with friends, Dead Island 2 delivers on all fronts. So grab your weapon of choice, slap on some sunscreen, and get ready for the zombie vacation of a lifetime. Trust me, you won't want to miss this.Pros:Satisfying and varied combatStunning visuals and immersive sound designHilarious and engaging storyFun and chaotic multiplayerCons:Occasional bugs and glitchesSome repetitive missionsGet ready to laugh, scream, and have the time of your (after)life. Dead Island 2 is calling, and it’s a vacation you won't soon forget!

_childDocuments_.review: After years of development hell, here finally comes the awaited sequel to DEAD ISLAND!How is it?A pretty fun game to be honest. Very similar to the original game but with improved gameplay mechanics and of course, visuals... while the first Dead Island game was a feast for the eyes back in 2012, DI2 is a looker for sure! Best way to describe it would be to mix a couple of existing game mixed into this one. Visceral melee combat like the first Dead Island and of course, the unavoidable DYING LIGHT and the horror from the "CONDEMNED" series, add some "LEFT4DEAD" adrenaline infused action and combine the whole thing with some "BORDERLANDS" for hub-like open world aspect, story telling and levelling up by doing quests. A very "Borderlands" way is the 4-way Co-Op gameplay DI series offer. I played DI and DI2 solo but co-op should be interesting.DI and DI2 doesn't have day/night cycles and contrary to DI, DI2 has a night time for certain zones. While I preferred the DYING LIGHT aspect of "real time" day/night cycles since it added a lot of tension, DI series is more of a comedic approach compared to DYING LIGHT.DEAD ISLAND 2 gives you a lot of content for its whole package. Just the game alone should take you a good 30 hours to finish. Add the two great story DLC's which would add another 10-15 hours of playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: The main appeal of this game is the gore system. The graphics are amazing and the violence is gruesome! If that's enough to keep you entertained, than you'll probably enjoy this game... but is it fun? Yes, I'd say so. It's pretty repetitive from the start, but you should know what to expect before you buy it: you beat zombies to a pulp (or slice them... or burn/electrocute/melt them) and go from A to B. Wash, rinse, repeat. It's monotonous, but fun enough. I play solo, because I like the horror factor. I tried to join an online game but didn't find a game after waiting a few minutes. Apparently it's laggy.Anyways, I just played 5 hours and so far, my only real complaint about the gameplay is that the enemies could be very spongy and even worse, they respawn way too fast - and in groups too! All you gotta do is walk 10 feet or spin in a circle and they'll pop up right behind you. It can be more annoying than tension building. This, along with weapon durability being an issue, can be problematic. You might find yourself backtracking to a repair bench just to stand a chance, only for all the enemies you cleared to spawn back. This can be very annoying. It probably won't be an issue if you play on normal, but I was playing on hard (by using a skill-card that increases the difficulty). Get used to dying. You'll be doing that a lot on if you choose to make the game hard.Lastly, as others have griped, I don't like Epic Games and I really don't like Denuvo - especially when they don't announce that it's included until literally the moment that the game is released. That's just scummy! And frankly, I really don't get why it's even a thing: we need to purchase directly through Steam or acquire a brand new key another way; isn't that enough security?TLDR: 7/10 - it's okay; not bad, not great.Graphics/gore = absolutely insane!Gameplay = fun enough/meh.Epic Games/Denuvo = garbage.Get it on sale (I got Gold Edition for ~$32) if it still interests you.

_childDocuments_.review: So much more enjoyable than the first and Dying Light 2. If you can bare the fact it has Epic Game Store integration, its a must-pick up on sale. Combat is what you're here for, not the story. The weapons are satisfying, the heavy two-handers have a degree of weight and impact that is just so satisfying. The sharp weapons feel devastating and the upgrades actually have some interesting and fun effects outside of the stat increases. The reveals of each special infected are pretty obvious and you've seen most of them before, but they've added some unique spins with new variations of the typical formulaic mutated zombies. The best part aside from the combat is the environments. So interesting going through the upper LA area, especially in context of the zombie apocalypse. _childDocuments_.review: Essentially, the developers decided to create a game that's fun to play and visually stunning. They also didn't stress over zones having different times of day, which sometimes results in rapid changes from day to night and back again.The game has some bizarre elements, but I'm genuinely enjoying it. _childDocuments_.review: Got the game and both story DLCs on sale for 40 bucks total and got 42 hours out of a single play through. It's a first person, open world, RPG in a similar vein to Borderlands. Like Borderlands, this game is all about killing hordes of enemies for loot. Unlike borderlands, this game is about gear customization not finding the perfect weapon rolls. The reward for exploration and quests is unique weapons that you can use as a base, blueprints for mods or perks that can be put onto weapons, or cards that you can use to create your build.While every enemy is a zombie, there are A LOT of variations. The amount of different kinds of enemies encourages you to have different damage types, and keeps the moment to moment gameplay loop from getting stale. I was enjoying myself enough to do all of the side content available before beating the game. More content makes itself available after beating the game, and I'm planning on doing it.The story is fun, nothing crazy, but it held my attention and was good enough when paired with the actual combat gameplay. Everyone says it ends on a cliff hanger, I think it more ends like they're planning on making a Dead Island 3. Reminding you that Reed is just the beginning, not the end of this story.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. The gore system is very detailedand satisfying. The voice acting is very good and interactive. Even doing the smallest of things like looking over a cliff your character will respond and say something. I really loved the music and it's sound design.The atmosphere is creepy and scary. They really nailed the look of Los Angeles. The story was good and humorous. You can hear screams from distances and footsteps that are nearby. The sound effects had me looking around corners being cautious all the time. I actually jumped more than a few times as a zombie can hide and jump out of all kinds of things. The guns and melee weapons all feel different which makes them more fun to use. So you don't feel bored like you are using the same weapon with a different skin. You can upgrade and modify any weapon. Even if it's completely broken you can fix it and keep it forever.You can also add fire, electricity, zombie parts, acid effects and more to take them a step further. Guns never need to be fixed but melee ones need to be only if you are using them. The game even lets you match any of your weapons to your current characters level if you don't want to part with them. You also get throwable weapons called curveballs like pipebombs, stars, molotovs, grenades and more. You can use themas many times as you want but they do have cooldowns. You unlock them by finding them in the world or simply by completing quests. I should note that your main meleeweapons can be thrown as well and you can recover them wherever they land.I liked how you can use the environment to your advantage.Take a battery from a car and throw it in a pool to electrocute the water or take a gasoline can and make a puddle out of it and light it on fire. Kick a zombie into a pool of acid and watch them melt. Lure them into power lines and more.Leveling up your character uses a card system which you can mix and match to what you like. I kind of wished they stuck with a skill tree instead but it works. I didn't feel like my character was tough enough until I got cards that had certain abilities tied to them later in the game. You can also find cards if you explore the world but I felt theyare not as good as the ones you get by leveling up. Exploring is fun and going into places gives you a sense of what happened to the people that were there at the time.I really loved searching for the unknown. The atmosphere is so well done you have to at least play it one time in single player instead of co-op and take your time exploring. The only minor thing I was disappointed in was I couldn't drive anything. You can in the first game. Regardless I love it to gory bits.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Rating: ★★★★☆Dead Island 2, developed by Dambuster Studios and published by Deep Silver, revitalizes the zombie-slaying genre with its sunny Californian setting and intense action. This long-awaited sequel brings new life to the franchise, offering players a thrilling and gory adventure.Graphics: ★★★★★The game’s visuals are impressive, with detailed environments that capture the sunny, yet apocalyptic feel of California. The character models and zombie designs are grotesquely detailed, adding to the immersive horror experience.Gameplay: ★★★★★Dead Island 2 excels in its gameplay, providing a satisfying mix of melee combat, exploration, and crafting. The combat system is visceral and intense, making every encounter with zombies feel impactful. The variety of weapons and the crafting system keep the gameplay fresh and engaging.Sound: ★★★★☆The sound design effectively complements the game’s atmosphere. The ambient sounds and music heighten the tension, while the grotesque sounds of combat add to the visceral experience. Voice acting is solid, bringing the characters to life in this chaotic world.Story: ★★★☆☆While the story is serviceable, it’s not the primary focus of Dead Island 2. The narrative provides a decent backdrop for the zombie-slaying action but lacks depth and complexity. The characters are interesting, but the plot may not leave a lasting impression.Replayability: ★★★★☆With its open-world design and numerous side quests, Dead Island 2 offers plenty of content to keep players engaged. The co-op multiplayer mode adds significant replay value, allowing players to team up and tackle the zombie apocalypse together.Conclusion:Dead Island 2 is a solid entry in the zombie genre, offering intense action, detailed graphics, and engaging gameplay. While its story might not be its strongest aspect, the game excels in providing a thrilling and enjoyable zombie-slaying experience. Fans of the genre and newcomers alike will find plenty to enjoy in this apocalyptic adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: "As I write this review, I've just wrapped up an 8-hour gaming session with this captivating title. Throughout the entire session, I found myself repeatedly reminding that a break was necessary:"After this mission...""Maybe just one more mission...""Ugh, I'm too thrilled to leave the game at this point; let's finish this story arc first, then I'll get up...""Just a quick check of the challenges tab, then I'll log off," I said to myself, only to find myself completing the entire combat challenges section.This game is truly remarkable, a testament to the dedication and love poured into it by the developers. With its myriad of activities, from exploration to challenging encounters, amusing interactions with NPCs, and engaging mini-missions like riddles and treasure hunts for valuable gear, it's easy to get lost in its world.The attention to detail is commendable, especially evident in elements like journals, voice recordings, and character dialogues. And let's not forget the visual splendor - the graphics are stunning, the gore effects are incredibly satisfying, and the soundtrack perfectly complements the game's atmosphere.I would be remiss not to express my gratitude. I vividly remember the anticipation I felt after watching the first trailer nine years ago, only to be disappointed by delays and uncertainties. But now, in the capable hands of Dambuster Studios, the game has truly found its home. Thank you, Dambuster Studios, for delivering this phenomenal experience. Indeed, good things take time to come to fruition!"

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Island 2. A game that on release was getting the most mediocre, bland, and just meh reviews was still a game that I was very much excited to play. As someone who thinks that the original Dead Island is a 50/50 game, in terms of enjoyment, etc, etc, I was still looking forward to the sequel because despite being under new management, from everything that I'd seen looked really good.Positives. The environmental mechanics, and more importantly the gore mechanics are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brilliant. It's clear to me that the developers put a lot of time and effort into the mechanics because I didn't see a single flaw in them. The weapon modding and overall combat, I think was really solid. Visually, I think this was very impressive and the level of detail they put into this game was really nice from the locations to the zombies themselves, I think it looked really nice throughout. Small things like the soundtrack, sound design, and pacing were all pretty nice. I also had and am still having fun with a lot of the side missions this game has, too and as someone who doesn't typically do side quests in games, that says a lot to how much I enjoyed them.Negatives. The biggest flaw I think Dead Island 2 has is it's narrative. I think for all the time they put into the mechanics took away from this game's story because I think it really struggled. In addition to that, the dialogue was pretty rough throughout and at point was bordering on ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful. I understand this game and this franchise is silly but it's like the humour is 10 years too late because so many of the jokes fell completely flat and were just insufferable at times. A lack of enemy types, bosses, and good side-characters were noticeable, too. When it came to the standard enemies, they either got boring after a while or they just got annoying to deal with and not because they were hard, they were just annoying. And if none of those issues were bad enough, the ending might be one of the worst endings I've ever experienced. It didn't even feel like a fully fleshed out finale, instead it felt like the game just ends after you've had a fight that you already had several times before hand. Straight up, the ending sucks.With all the good and with all the rest included, it may be a hot take when I say that I actually prefer this game to the original. I think it flows a lot better, I think looks ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ superb, and my enjoyment level was just miles ahead. However, this is nowhere close to a perfect game or even that amazing but I do think this is a very good and bordering on great game. Flaws and all, I'm giving Dead Island 2 a 7.3/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A ton of fun so far. Graphics are absolutely gorgeous, performance is stellar, controls are smooth and responsive, and the gore system is sublime.Tons of weapon variety, with blunt, knives, axes, swords, scythes, staffs, daggers, handguns, rifles, crossbows, pickaxes....and tons more. On top of that, every weapon is customizable with elements, so they can emit electricity, fire, acid, or you can simply improve stats like damage and durability. There's so much variety in how you take on enemies.The gore system is wild. Kicking zombies into a pool of acid and watching their flesh and muscle melt off the bones as they slump to the floor is...an experience. All enemies have a full 'layer' system, with flesh, muscle, bone, etc, which can be cut and stripped away by different types of damage. Smashing a zombies face in and seeing the jaw swinging around and the eyes flopping out of the sockets is gnarly.The game also makes a lot of really cool use of environmental elements, like cans of water, fuel or acid. Each of which can be picked up, shot and thrown. So you can create an oil spill to set ablaze. Or pour out a trail of water and then electrify it to kill enemies or power up a locked door or something. It makes for some really dynamic encounters.Playing on a 4080 and i7 13700K with everything cranked to the max, it runs at 240fps (300fps uncapped) and looks insanely good. FOV controls and plenty of accessibility options for UI elements, etc, is nice too.Story is fairly standard fair, with overly exaggerated L.A characters, some cringey Youtube + A-List movie star type characters, etc. Lots of caricatures dialled up to 11. That said, all the performances are solid and keep things interesting. The player character (of which you can choose from 5) each have fully voiced dialogue and are pretty entertaining too.The world design consists of lots of open 'hub' areas, like Beverly Hills, where you can fully explore a lot of streets, homes, shops, etc. Lots of cool environments and details to find, with hidden loot and collectables. Along the way there are optional side missions for characters.If you enjoyed Dead Island 1, or the Dying Light games, there's plenty to like here.

Game's difficulty, it can go from really easy to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ difficult. 3. _childDocuments_.review: DO NOT SPEND MORE THAN $30 ON THIS GAME!!I got the game optimistic that maybe it got better with time but I was wrong.The game play consists of going from Point A to Point B, turning on power, and killing zombies (and that's pretty much it, no joke). Now this wouldn't be so bad if the zombies didn't have entirely too much health, and that's not even starting on the special zombies. This is made worse by the fact that every time you turn around, the game spawns more zombies behind you, and you can only take a few hits before you die (even at higher levels). The zombies sort of have power armor, meaning when they lunge at you hitting them won't stagger them all the time and they will get a free hit unless you dodge (again, this is the REGULAR zombies). For reference, I'm entering end game and I was hitting a regular zombie (a walker) with fully charged heavy attacks using an upgraded rare weapon that hit for over 1,000 damage each time. The zombie had to be hit five times before it died. The guns are a joke too, even upgraded. Regular zombies take multiple head shots, and special zombies barely even feel a full magazine.I would be able to overlook this if it weren't for the fact that every mission is "kill all the zombies in the area" and then every time you're almost done the game spawns in between 30 and 100 more zombies (depending on how important to the story the mission is) that you have to kill to progress.The story is not great, the writing is bad and it feels like the game didn't know if it wanted to be Dead Island, Dying Light, or a parody of L.A. Every character is one dimensional yet trying too hard to be quirky.The dismemberment is cool, that's about all the good I have to say. Don't buy this game unless it is heavily discounted. You would be better off getting Dying Light 1 and/or 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't play due to "Connecting to Epic Online Services"Update: While there is a workaround for this, due to frequent disconnects and gaming over multiple sessions, I've had to unlink and relink my Steam account to an EGS account over ten times in order to play this game with an EGS friend.You will be stuck at a "Connecting to Epic Online Services" loading screen if your accounts are linked, so if you re-launch the game or disconnect and experience the issue I've been having, you'll need to go sign into EGS, unlink your accounts, launch the game, then from the main menu (once you pass the normal loading screen with issues), you can successfully link your accounts (which means reauthenticating with username, password, and MFA multiple times each session) and then load in with a friend.Doing this once is painful, since I don't even want an EGS account. Doing it each time I launch the game is worse, but to top it off, the frequent disconnects we experience that don't allow me to re-join without relaunching the game compounds the issue to the point I'll have to unlink and relink my account several times in a night just to keep playing.  Not to mention how annoying it is to disconnect in the middle of this game in general.The good news is, this game is fun. I'm liking it a whole lot more than I thought I would, and I'd love to have this be a positive review, but I do not recommend this experience until this issue gets resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: To be frank, it's the original Dead Island with a fresh coat of paint, worse balancing, less to do, and located within a series of small maps. Worse balancing: leveling, damage types, loot, and respawning (enemies and you)Leveling:I shouldn't be able to find overleveled zombies that will one hit kill me from level 2 because I took a LEFT. On top of that, I CONTINUE to find overleveled zombies that one hit kill me no matter where I seem to go in the story, despite doing all the side missions. It's not hard to SCALE YOUR ENEMIES TO PLAYER LEVEL. If you don't want players to go to an area, there are plenty of other soft and hard methods of keeping them from doing so.Enemy:They experimented with different enemies but in a way that's rather annoying. There are two different types of standard zombies, and one is weak to blunt damage and the other is weak to cut damage. The problem is, this is rather annoying to deal with in fight when you're fighting more than one and you have to scroll through your weapon wheel based off a "walker" or "shambler". Other than that, you have the standard zombie enemies. The exploders, the tanks, the runners, the two types of walkers, and walkers of each element type (fire, electricity, and acid). Nothing special, but that's somewhat to be expected out of a zombie game.Loot: Traders or rather A TRADER (as there has only been one so far) is the ONLY source of fuses, which are required to open loot caches. The problem is that the trader is only available from your hub, and the fuses cost 1500, whereas repairing a good weapon costs 900. Zombies sometimes drop 15-20 bucks, so this means that you often have an ok amount of money, or just enough to keep your weapon repaired and/or level matched so that it won't start lagging behind in damage as you progress in levels. Unless you buy fuses from the trader, you cannot open loot caches.Respawning:The enemies may be temporarily cleared from an area, but they respawn fairly quickly, appearing seemingly out of nowhere. While this keeps me on my toes, this is also rather annoying to have enemies respawn in a place I JUST CLEARED. Speaking of respawns, there isn't any actual consequence for death in game, as you (and enemies) respawn close by when you die. I assume this is done for the benefit of co-op, but it just doesn't feel right.Fresh coat of paint:The gameplay is near identical to the first Dead Islands, they just look nicer, and the zombies have more bits that fly off them. This isn't to say the gameplay is bad inherently, but somewhat stale. The skill cards aren't exactly an intriguing way of doing so, though the "wildcards" or side abilities that you find like a rechargeable pipe bomb ability do make things slightly more interesting and allow you to use the environment more creatively.Less to do:I have 8 out of 24 missions done. nearly a THIRD the way through the story, and I have done 4 side missions. This is because there were 5 side missions over the course of the 5.6 hours and * story missions I played. I bypassed one because of the previous overleveled enemies problem.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10If mixed reviews were still a thing, that is what I would give this game. It does some things fine, some not so fine. Ultimately, what makes this game a bit dissapointing for me is the fact that so little has changed from Dead Island 1 and Dead Island: Riptide. We're not even on an island anymore, we're in L.A!If you somehow stumbled into this without playing any of the previous titles, Dead Island 2 is a first-person zombie-slaying game with a lot of focus on loot-n-hack-n-slash. Yes, you mainly use melee-weapons. The game plays somewhat closely to the Borderlands-series, where you grind for gear, walk around big maps with respawning enemies, do some sidequests and mess around with a few friends in multiplayer.I'm not going to get into the story that much. You are a survivor of a zombie-apocalypse that is happening all around you and you are tasked with getting out of L.A (or Hell-A, as they cringeingly keep calling it). Along the way you meet some questgifers who help you out and you are a big action hero who clears the way for some people to be able to escape. That's all you need to know. It is set after the first two games and although the story is not that important, there are some connections and characters that makes the game more enjoyable if you have played the previous ones.The action is alright, I think the combat is okay and that (although not for me) the gameplay-loop is fine. It looks great and I like the fact that the damage you inflict on the zombies is VERY detailed, accurate and visable. The writing and story is god-awful, almost worse than Dead Island: Riptide. Your character is quirky and cracks jokes all throughout the story and it is just terrible. No character has any depth and the interactions feel so stale, most of the time. But you are here for the action and not for the story, I am sure.The thing is that although this game is new and fancy, it just does not present enough new things to catch my interest. It has been 13 yeas since Dead Island 1 and this game feels almost exactly the same. It feels old, it feels stale and they just pumped out a new game for the money. I just feel as this game is not made out of passion for anything, it does not fill a certain purpose that has not already been filled by the previous entries. It makes me sad, as I used to enjoy the first game back in 2011. But without anything new to present, I cannot properly recommend it. It is FINE, it just is not necessary to play or buy at all. Especially not at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: There's not much to talk about here. The combat system, which should be a thrilling part of any zombie game, feels clunky and repetitive. Graphically it looks good most of the time. The storyline also leaves much to be desired. The characters you meet are shallow, and their quests often boil down to repetitive fetch missions. The narrative attempts to engage, but with lackluster voice acting and poor dialogue, it’s hard to care about what happens next. Level Designs are constantly doing the same thing for 10 hours, which is so frustrating. The game gets very hard after some point because you get under-leveled if you don't grind. In Dead Island 2, grinding is mandatory. If you don't grind in boring side quests, you'll get one shot later in the story, horrible game design.Performance starts well with 80-90 FPS, then becomes 20-40 FPS with constant stutters after a few hours into the game. They optimized the first 2 hours so that you won't be able to refund it. Load times are frustratingly long. Being an Epic exclusive is also a huge negative. _childDocuments_.review: P.S.A. Don't bother with COOP (too much) or the Neighborhood Watch mode. The netcode and hit detection are very low quality. DI2 is just a single player game with some multiplayer bling.---------------------------------------------- So i finished the game the third time on Steam (after two times on Epic) and here are my opinions on the current state of the game:+ beautiful visuals, very attractive locations with awesome ambiental sound and even music.+ one of the best combat in a action game since the 2015-2016 years with Shadow Warrior 2, Doom and Dying Light 1. Watch zombies melt, explode, burn, bleed and be ripped in small pieces with the best physics and effects in a game !+ the cinematics and main quests are very nicely made, side quests and collectibles are also quite entertaining and there is a LOT of lore in notes and audio recordings to be found.+ the base game is very well optimized (100 FOV, fps limit, only FSR so far) also Haus dlc.+ each slayer has own dialogues with npcs (and even the npcs have LOTS of dialogues between them). The whole world is VERY IMMERSIVE ! After you unlock fast travel with the maps you can choose to play the level in day or night !- the story is not finished, even if every piece of information is collected in game we still don't have a closure, we get to settle the score with only one of the four main antagonists and they said the expansion pass contains only the current two dlcs.. some people hope for extra dlc or content added post launch on Steam, others hope for a Dead Island 3 soon.. haha, right...- the game comes with mandatory "epic online services" even if you only play single player solo by your own.- also denuvo (so far) but i did not felt a single performance problem on my 12700k with a 4080s at 1440p with ingame 120 fps max.- SoLA is not optimized (in the Steam launch period) and quite unbalanced combat and number wise.This game is a must buy for a zombie genre fan !For other people.. maybe on 50% sale.P.S. You can try to finish (and you should) Haus dlc as soon as its available but not after you leave Blue Crab Grill on Venice Beach if you don't want to deal with a very annoying zombie type that you will encounter later and will automatically populate Haus areas. If you play Haus before unlocking Fury you will see a very cool cinematic when you're turned back to progress the main story before you can progress and finish Haus ;-)P.P.S. You can play SoLA as soon as its available if you don't want to deal with the same annoying zombie but you will need to have a higher level (27+) and a solid made slayer (with weapons and skillset) if you want to finish the SoLA unbalanced and three-stage-boss at the end of the dlc. The whipper new zombie type is alright but the clotter type is out-of-place and very CRINGE. You should unlock the Bodycount AK weapon (after finishing the main/base story) and then use that and other end-game weapons at the final SoLA boss.P.P.P.S. Start with Clara (she is a tank with more damage around more zombies) and after you finish the game with her you should experiment with others like Dani (good fast damage dealer) and Jacob (damage dealer tank). Ryan is a tank for the ladies, Amy is a squishy gal and Bruno is a backstabber that has no real place in a game with very little stealth (same for Amy).

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Island 2 is a fantastic game but people have passed on it. A lot of this was due to the game being exclusive to epic for so long, and that's on them. Regardless of that Dead island 2 is very polished, plays well and looks beautiful.When drawing comparisons to other games like Dying Light, Dead Island 2 sets itself apart by a slower and more realistic approach with impressively real zombie design. Every slice, whack, stab or shot is reflected in zombies you're fighting. Be that, lacerations, broken arms and holes blown clean through, to name a few.The atmosphere of Los Angeles setting is great, it is wonderfully recreated with beautiful lighting and eerie atmosphere. The campaign is split up into various map locations that you load in and out of, with some areas barred due to progression, level requirements or with keys and other items.The game is tons of fun with it made all the better by loading up coop and running wild with 3 other playable characters. Each character has their own strengths and weaknesses, and can be customised with skill cards that are earned through mission rewards, level ups or found through looting. Again, Dead Island 2 is a fantastic game and expands on what made the original so beloved weather that's the zombie design, expansive world or improved gameplay, zombie slaying has never felt so good.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really disappointing to see that another game has been snagged up by Epic's awful business deals and I do hope that Deep Silver will take note of the feedback on here going forward and will stop accepting the bribe that Epic provides to have anti-consumer exclusivity rights over a game. Treat your customers with the respect they deserve and let them choose where and how they play your games!That being said, the game itself is not at fault for this and the developers have done an outstanding job. The environments are beautiful and it's fun being able to use a large variety of weapons to shred zombies into pieces. At the heart of the game is the gore system which in itself is unique and is a piece of technology that other game developers should really take note of. The game really does have that Dead Island feel that the original game offered and I am personally a fan of the more simplified skill system being based around cards that you can unlock and swap out whenever you feel like switching up your play style. The story may not be the most engaging for me personally, but Dead Island 2 certainly makes up for it in fun gameplay and an overall very polished experience all around.So overall, while I am disappointed that Deep Silver decided to hold this game hostage on Epic for a year and that even now it still requires use of Epic's online services to allow for crossplay between the 2 launchers, since the game itself is great it would be disservice to say that I do not recommend it. We're here to review the game and not the publisher's business practices after all. Well worth a try if you can look aside the 'Epic' side of things!
