_childDocuments_.review: After years of anticipation and a lengthy development process, Dead Island 2 has finally arrived, and the wait has been worth it. As someone who held out for its release due to a dislike for Epic Games' exclusivity, I can say that this game has exceeded my expectations in numerous ways.One of the most striking aspects of Dead Island 2 is its approach to level design. Unlike other open-world games that focus on vast, sprawling landscapes, this game chooses a more refined, detailed approach. The environments are smaller in scale but brimming with intricate details that make each location feel lived-in. I find myself taking my time to explore, not just to loot or complete objectives, but to appreciate the incredible amount of care the developers put into crafting these areas.The game's new gore system is nothing short of amazing. You can feel the impact of every swing, every shot, and every explosion as you take on hordes of zombies. The visceral feedback and the realistic damage mechanics add a level of immersion that's rare in zombie games. It's both gruesome and fascinating to see how the zombies react to your attacks, making combat feel intense and satisfying.Dead Island 2 also shines in its co-op mode. Playing with friends amplifies the fun, turning an already enjoyable game into a fantastic multiplayer experience. The mechanics and progression systems work seamlessly in co-op, allowing you and your friends to tackle the zombie apocalypse together. It's a blast to strategize and team up to clear out zombie-infested areas, and the game's light-hearted tone keeps the experience from becoming too grim.While there are some minor technical hiccups and occasional glitches, they don't detract from the overall experience. The game's focus on smaller, highly detailed locations rather than massive open worlds is a refreshing change, proving that sometimes less can be more. This approach makes the game more manageable and enjoyable without feeling overwhelming.Overall, Dead Island 2 is a fun, engaging, and immersive experience that's well worth the wait. Whether you're playing solo or with friends, the game offers a thrilling zombie-filled adventure that's hard to put down. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a game that combines detailed environments, satisfying combat, and cooperative multiplayer. It's a welcome addition to the zombie genre and sets a high bar for other developers to follow.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say this game barely makes the grade, as a 'recommended' title.It's a fun game, it looks good. If you're a fan of the first game and it's expansion, Riptide, you should be able to enjoy this game for it's combat and sandbox elements such as using the environment against the zombies, be it pouring water on the ground and electrifying it to set a trap or dropkicking zombies off of ledges or into hazards or even into more zombies to knock them down like a bunch of bowling pins.The melee combat feels a alot more fluid compared to the original Dead Island & Riptide and the overall feel of the game is less jank than the original Dead Island & it's Riptide expansion pack. Not to mention the gore system has been massively improved and it looks absolutely horrifying in a good way of course, it definitely boosts up the feedback and impact of smashing and hacking zombies to bits as you get to work.Guns also feel better in this game compared to the original game's own, even if they aren't a significant leap forward in quality if one ended up making comparisons to other games. They actually get the job done now, unlike the original Dead Island 1's janky and stiff firearms!I haven't tried out the DLCs yet, but I am hoping that since now it's on Steam, which I've been waiting for it for a while now. That the game gets a DLC to finish up the story and adds a New Game Plus mode. Or at the very least, lets us skip that absolutely tedious airplane tutorial segment on new playthroughs, seeing it just the once is enough, for me at least anyway.It does have some performance issues in certain areas on some of the larger maps but most of the time I'm able to keep well over 120FPS on maxed out settings with the DLSS3 mod during fights with large groups of enemies, so take that as you will. I'd say buy this on sale if you enjoyed the first game and you are aware of what you're getting into by tempering your expectations with this sequel if you decide to pick it up. If you got friends to play it with, that's an added bonus that should make it more fun.Anyway! The first Dead Island and Riptide games both have NG+, this not being in Dead Island 2 hampers replayability. Moreover, due to how levels are designed in DI2, along with the limited amount of quests and areas, with most areas being much smaller than the open world areas in comparison to the original Dead Island, there isn't as much to explore. There's also the issue of how the game phases in new enemy types and features, which also makes additional playthroughs due to the enforced plane tutorial sequence, very tedious and repetitive, so once when you've done it the first time on one slayer, that's about it. Unlike the first game in which you'd get into the actual game and it's world way sooner, DI2 takes a lot longer to spin up to it's fullest, which is also bad for replayability. Some of the Slayers' innate skills are worthless due to their design, or just straight-up awful unless you're playing in Co-Op mode, if we were to compare this to how the original DI and Riptide balanced the heroes available, you'll see how the sequel handles their lineup as inferior in the case of balance. A good example is Bruno having the 'Backstab' innate skill, but the game lacks a proper stealth system, so unless you're playing in Co-op, chances are, you'll never get the full value of this skill off, outside of maybe stunning larger zeds and forcing them to kneel. If you were to just rush through all the main story quests and focus on finishing the game, you'll realise that there isn't much on offer in terms of main story content. Unlike the original Dead Island, DI2 feels a lot more linear and quite short in comparison. The ending is the biggest offender, as there's a lot of elements and questions introduced with DI2, which are genuinely good additions and help flesh things out a bit more for the series. But, overall, you'll get the impression that the developers ran out of both time and budget to finish things off properly, so you're left with a cliffhanger ending, with certain characters just being completely forgotten and their stories not being given any sort of indication of a future or additional lead, with Tisha for example becoming the new Yerema, who was also never wrapped properly up in Riptide, simply being forgotten about as soon as she was sent off-screen. Maybe she'll come back in a DLC or the sequel, who knows at this point. The first game allowed you to specialise and maximise the potential of certain playstyles, depending on what hero you picked or what weapons you were using, this was carried over into Riptide, alongside a new hero being added. With the sequel, Dead Island 2, they've lowered the max level to 30, as well as how skills are handled between characters. Whilst it's arguably more flexible and freeform than the original game and it's expansion, the skill cards feel more like augments to existing abilities (Jump kicks or heavy attacks and such) and don't let you specialise into specific weapon types or mods, along with most additional types of skillcards (e.g. Numen Skills) being locked behind the story mode, so by the time you get to all the fun stuff, since there's no new game plus, you've pretty much stuck as is until you run out of things to do like side-quests.: I'm not sure why the devs decided to make this game only support 3 players instead of 4 like how the originals did. Especially with it's larger line-up of six playable characters, you'd think they'd try to support more players in Co-Op mode and it's not like they're working on an engine that isn't capable, given it's on the Unreal Engine 5. The other thing, it's 2024. Crossplay with every platform that a game is available on, if it's multiplayer, is pretty much standard. I'm not sure why this isn't a thing outside of 'Ran out of dev time + budget'.If any of these negative points are a big take-away for you, or the flaws present in the game are too glaring to ignore or perhaps you wanted more of the first game and the changes to the sequel are too drastic for your personal tastes. Then yeah, avoid giving this game a go to avoid any disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all. Great PC port! A rare sight these days. So kudos for that!Specs: 13700K/6950XT/32GB DDR5 6000MHz/970 EVO PlusI ran it @ 1440P on High settings. Native resolution. It runs smooth as butter @ 120FPS for me. Rarely dipped below that in the 70 hours or so i put into the game. The game looks gorgeous too. Very quick load times as well. Nice to see a shader caching process that actually works and doesn't take forever to complete.As for the gameplay? It's a nice middle ground between Dead Island and Dying Light. The combat is definitely faster and more kinetic than it was in Dead Island and Riptide. Good. I hate slog fests. By the way. Every FPS should have a drop kick imo. I will never tire of it. Be it this game or Dying Light. It just feels so damn gratifying whenever you use it to launch a zombie into the stratosphere. The melee combat is definitely deeper and more refined in this. There's plenty of guns too! The game's damage/FLESH system adds an additional layer of disposing the walking dead in all kinds of new and gruesome ways. Some of the level design is definitely smaller but more focused and i actually prefer that. There's some zones that are more confined (I am looking at you, Metro fans) but there's plenty of more open world places in the game as well. Traversing the game world didn't feel like a chore to me and i had fun exploring it as well since it features more defined places instead of vast copy and paste environments.Story? Eh. They've expanded the mythology, i guess. It's definitely more on the fantastical side. No spoilers. The latest DLC goes much further into that. I'll just say, it's very meaty. Some people may not like that kind of thing. Personally? I couldn't care less. If the gameplay benefits from it? Go right ahead and add more of it.All in all, tis a very fun romp.

_childDocuments_.review: Underwhelming! If you played Dying Light, you will be disappointed with this one. Movement is not fluid - climbing is set animation and not part of movement, so climbing a fence is not you running, jumping right in front of it and climbing it. No. You smash face first into the fence and than you can kindly press a spacebar to start the climbing animation. Fighting is just aweful - reminded me of dead island 1 (not remastered). You swing next to zombie and it almost feels like playing Xcom, because invisible dice just rolls, if you hit or not, even if you are in kissing range. For zombies though, you can dodge back 10 feet and still, the force of wind of their powerfull slash will still hit you. Spawning is also a problem. When you trigger alarm, lets say car alarm, zombies start spawning around you, and not just from the hole or such, I caught multiple zombies just appearing right behind, when I turned around faster. And way to turn of alarm is to remove car battery, which makes sense, if the prompt to do so would actually work half a time. Zombies spawn without alarms too, so you can never actually clear small area before looting it, because before you done, someone will spawn behind you.Exploration is fun, but so many elements make it irritating. Level based enemies ruin every explorers fun. With how aweful the fighting system is, and zombies above your level just one slash you, exploring without getting gated by them is impossible. Also there is so many locked boxes around the map for which you need to find specific zombie, that drops the key. When you actually finally find it, you no longer know, where the box was.Story - I didn't get far, but I do not think writers for this one ever left their friend group. All the "non-important" characters are caricatures of stereotypes only tumblr user could think of. Main characters make choices, that in real life would end in catastrophe. Only likeable player character to choose seems to be Jacob. I chose Amy for her skill set, but after while I turn down speech audio, because her one-liners where obnoxious. Most characters we are supposed to like are clearly writen for young Americans. For some reason side-quest one-off characters are actually fun and interesting. It's almost like coming into different, actually fun game, and when I saw another side quest, I dropped everything and run there. Whoever wrote those should have writen the main story.What I enjoyed was weapon and overall damage system. If the combat would be well made, this could actually rival Dying Light. Weapon variety, animations, upgrades and blending in to world system with elemental damage was reminiscent of Dying Light 1, but world gives you more occasions to use them. It is almost on the way to be Dead Rising level of fun. But again, it can be overpowered for zombies your level and do nothing to higher level ones. Overall, only thing I got from this game is shame, that I was too hard on Dying Light 2, and urge to go play that instead. I was hoping this game would bring more of the movement and fight of Dying Light 1, with fun of Dead Island. How can this game be outmatched in most ways by almost ten year old game?

_childDocuments_.review: After completing Dead Island 2 and its accompanying DLC's, I have several problems to note for anyone looking to purchase this game. The dialogue can get annoying and cringey, at times, and the story is pretty middling, especially since it ends on a cliff-hanger when everything starts picking up, much like the Medal of Honor game that was put out many years ago now. Furthermore, enemies will spawn directly behind you, or materialize right in front of you. However, the sound effects, music, combat, weapon variety, and gameplay mechanics are all up-to-par, mostly the combat and dismembering of zombies, its fan-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥-tastic. Also, the graphics are quite good when compared to the original, but nothing to write home about when comparing it to other games released in the past couple of years, yet still good to look at. When compared to other games in the genre, though, this can fall a little flat, especially if one has played Dying Light 1. Overall, I had a great time with Dead Island 2 and the absolute carnage I unleashed on the undead, but its middling story and side quests, along with cringey dialogue and enemies that appear right in front of you out of nowhere, makes this game a solid 7/10. So, pick up on-sale for tens of hours of entertainment and zombie slaying; highly recommended just for the dismemberment system itself, but make sure to get it on-sale since it is not worth purchasing at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to the first Dead Island, this game just pales completely. For starters, the locations feel a lot more bland a recycled compared to the variety of the first game. The same white suburban house over and over and over with barely anything in it. The only real danger are running zombies or more than 5 weak zombies because the melee combat sucks, but I'll get into that later. The characters don't have gimmicks as much as they used to, and it's more of a "Whose voice do you want to hear" type selection. While they have different perks that they have access too, multiple characters have access to some of the same perks, so it's still not unique. I like the personalities, love the voicelines and dialogue, but the gameplay of the characters just feels shallow and paperthin.My biggest issue was the melee combat, and combat in general. Zombies will often respawn in areas you've already cleared literal seconds after you've cleared it. The only places this doesn't happen is story areas. While one or two zombies isn't a problem to deal with, it's still annoying to deal with them in the first place because the combat sucks. It looks great, sure, but you can be beaten to death by like two zombies if they decide to swing at the same time. There's no stunning them mid-attack because they seem to just ignore the fact that you hit them in the face with a giant metal poles. Damage for almost anything is sub-par even with modified weapons, because the health pool is ridiculous. Your character will have like 1200 health and get killed in 3 swings from a rotting corpse, but the rotting corpse you can stab in the head with a literal cavalry sword 12 times and they'll be completely fine. This game also suffers from the same loot problem that Days Gone suffers from. If you die in an area and it re-loads a save, you've still lost all your stuff. Did you break a weapon mid fight and swap to another one, getting it's durability to half before you died? Well when you go back, all the zombies and items are back, but you're still down a weapon and a half. Your medkits, resources, and weapons do not save through death or checkpoints but the zombies sure do. And a lot of areas don't give you weapons, so eventually you'll be down to using your fists. Which, much like normal weapons, do practically nothing. At least it's satisfying to punch zombies like in the trailer, right? For the first 10 minutes maybe. It's the same animation over and over for everything. It gets old, fast.I played 5 and a half hours, the first hour was getting through dialogue, cutscenes, and tutorial stuff. The other 4 were spent practically running in circles. If there's anything I'll give this game, it's that the missions feel more alive rather than the first Dead Island; in which every single task was a "Run to place, kill zombies, grab item, come back, rinse repeat until you beat the game" type thing. There's more character to the characters, so to speak.Basically, I wouldn't recommend the game, but I'm a random person on the internet so if you're dead-set on playing it, go ahead. Wait for a sale, though, because even if the game was more fleshed out, $60 is not worth it

_childDocuments_.review: If this is max $25 its worth it if you can look past the sorta mediocre story with the repetitive (depending on how you play) combat and the surprisingly custom power/skill system in this game. There are "End Game" skills you get about halfway through that can drastically change how you play. Depending on the character you choose the game can be different due to same as before stat system that the old games had. Many factors to change how you play and I will most likely do another new game on a different character as their play styles and stats drastically change how you maneuver and play through the game. Its a 7/10, if the gore and maiming were any less than they are the review would be a negative but the combat alone is cool enough to keep everything interesting. Just don't use the same stuff and try different mods in crafting otherwise its the same animations over and over.1st play through is done at about 15 Hours in. Played as Carla, a heavy hitter that can stay in the fight with healing combat stats and abilities. Once I got a combo going it was pretty cool taking hits and stuff but just healing over it in the middle of a group just SWANGIN was where the character really shined. Who you choose as your character really does change how you play and can determine the exact play style you want so pay attention to each characters little excerpt and you'll understand. As the story goes on, you continue through L.A (I refuse to name it HELL.A like it does ALL over in the game) going through the same locations as you would in the real world, all of it lines up with whats nearby and practically matches how it looks in the real world, like the Pier and Carnival area, all the fast food places and beaches. The environment itself is actually quite stunning. Graphically wise, albeit with correct AA settings, the game looks amazing. With each new location you get new sets of zombies in different clothes, different mutations. Keeps it interesting. Runners, Big guys, Fat Guys, Honk Honk, you get the jist. Your typical line-up for a Zombie FPS really. As far as environment, Enemy types, just general things you see and interact with for the most part of the game is solid. My biggest gripe, is FOV. Anything above 75 just means you really gotta time/get used to swinging what feels like farther away, standing wise, at higher FOVs. Not a huge issue, just a console thing. The story, while being fully voiced, including all side missions, is lacking? I don't know where to put it really. The story makes sense, I understood all that was going on and the characters were remember-able but something about them just didn't click with me. For a zombie apocalypse, everyone was just chill. No one seemed to care that the entire world is on the brink of total destruction by flesh eating monsters, most of which are mutated beyond comprehension of our real world views. Everyone has the pippy, kids of the day tone around them. It just didn't really let me connect with them, it just became a "Tell me what to do" and then understanding whats going on by just doing the quest itself. Maybe its just the cut scenes. Don't get me wrong the story that they are driving the series towards is actually really interesting and a cool take on human evolution, so I really am looking forward to the next one as I want to see how they put everything together.Weapons, Items, Crafting. All still here and for the most part how it was in the previous titles. The mods you find during the story both organically and as RNG drops from certain Elites keep what you can do with your weapons fresh and some of them can change the way you go about your fights. Some weapons are meant for maiming and limb dismemberment, some weapons are good for blunt headshots, they all are meant to be played a certain way and as long as you change it up and keep your inventory in check damage wise you can coast through most of the stuff in a fun and different pace. The environment has plenty of gas tanks, electric wires, anything classified as elemental is apparent and plentiful as a way to spice up your fight. Drop kicking zombies and having them fly 10 feet back moaning is always funny. A new thing they introduced are "Curveballs" items that auto generate like grenades, spike pipe bombs, mollies. You can get abilities to make getting curveballs faster, build your character around them. Its all there.All in all, the game is actually quite good. The Epic Games drought for a year let the game cook and now that its on Steam I hope Deep Silver will put its player base over money for the next title and skip any exclusivity. In the end your here on Steam, keep it that way and stop giving a private company the rights to all the work you all put in.

_childDocuments_.review: it feels like.... coming homeAs a long-time fan of zombie games, Dead Island 2 has quickly become one of my favourites (also Dead Island). Right from the get-go, the game's setting in a zombie-infested Los Angeles—hellishly dubbed HELL-A—grabs you with its mix of familiar landmarks and apocalyptic decay. The developers, Dambuster Studios, have truly outdone themselves in creating an environment that feels both hauntingly real and thrillingly dangerous.Immersive Setting and NarrativeThe narrative thrusts you into the roles of six diverse survivors, each with their own quirks and backstories. My personal favourite has to be Dani, whose spunky personality and unique abilities add a refreshing twist to the otherwise grim atmosphere. The story is engaging enough to keep you hooked, with plenty of twists and turns as you navigate through iconic locations like Beverly Hills and Venice Beach. The addition of the Skill Cards system lets you customize your character's abilities, adding a layer of strategy that I found immensely satisfying.Combat and GameplayBut what truly sets Dead Island 2 apart is its combat. The F.L.E.S.H. system, which allows for detailed dismemberment of zombies, is nothing short of revolutionary. It's gruesome, it's visceral, and it's incredibly fun. I can't count the number of times I've gleefully hacked my way through hordes of the undead, each encounter leaving a trail of carnage that felt deeply rewarding. Whether you’re crafting makeshift melee weapons or wielding powerful firearms, the combat never gets old.AtmosphereVisually, the game is a feast for the eyes. The stark contrast between the sunny, glamorous LA and its current state of decay creates an atmosphere that's both beautiful and eerie. The attention to detail in the environments and character designs is impressive, making every moment spent exploring feel immersive. The sound design complements this perfectly, with ambient noises and zombie growls keeping you constantly on edge.Co-op Mode or as I call it One of the highlights for me has been the co-op mode. Teaming up with friends to tackle the zombie apocalypse adds a whole new dimension to the game. The cooperative gameplay encourages strategic planning and teamwork, making each session unpredictable and exciting. It's an absolute blast to coordinate attacks and share the horror (and fun) of surviving in HELL-A.Post-Launch ContentThe post-launch support has also been stellar. With expansions like Haus and SoLA, there's always new content to dive into. These expansions have not only added more hours of gameplay but have also enriched the overall story, keeping the experience fresh and engaging long after the initial playthrough.ConclusionDead Island 2 is a standout title in the zombie genre. Its blend of immersive storytelling, visceral combat, and cooperative gameplay makes it a thrilling ride from start to finish. If you're a fan of zombie games, this one is not to be missed. It's a game that I keep coming back to, and with its recent release on Steam, it's more accessible than ever for a broader audience to experience the gory joy of surviving in HELL-A.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 4.5/5Dead Island 2 is a thrilling and engaging zombie survival game that truly shines in its simplicity and immersive gameplay. Set in the sun-soaked, post-apocalyptic streets of 'Hell-A', this game offers a similar take on the zombie genre as the previous games but with its vibrant environments and over-the-top action.Gameplay: The gameplay is where Dead Island 2 truly excels. The controls are intuitive, making it easy for players to jump right into the action. The combat system is satisfying, with a variety of weapons and creative ways to dismember the undead. Whether you’re using a baseball bat, a machete, or a makeshift weapon, each encounter feels visceral and rewarding. The game’s simplicity is one of its greatest strengths, allowing players to focus on the fun of zombie-slaying without getting bogged down by overly complex mechanics.Soundtrack: The soundtrack is another standout feature. It perfectly complements the game’s atmosphere, with a mix of intense, adrenaline-pumping tracks and more ambient, eerie tunes. The music enhances the overall experience, making each moment feel more immersive and exciting.Graphics and Design: Visually, Dead Island 2 is stunning. The detailed environments and character models bring the world to life, and the vibrant colors add a unique flair to the apocalyptic setting. The game’s design is both beautiful and grotesque, capturing the chaotic essence of a zombie-infested Los Angeles.Story and Characters: While the story may not be the most original, it is filled with humor and memorable characters. The dialogue is witty, and the interactions with various NPCs add a layer of charm to the game. The narrative may not be groundbreaking, but it serves its purpose in driving the action forward.Overall: Dead Island 2 is a fantastic addition to the zombie genre. Its straightforward gameplay, amazing soundtrack, and stunning visuals make it a must-play for fans of action-packed survival games. Whether you’re playing solo or with friends, this game offers hours of gruesome, zombie-slaying fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Game Review: Dead Island 2As a long-time fan of Dead Island and Dead Island: Riptide, I couldn’t wait to dive into Dead Island 2. My anticipation was high, and somehow, the game managed to surpass even my most optimistic expectations. Dead Island 2 is a fresh yet faithful follow-up, successfully keeping the elements that made the original games so compelling while introducing enough new features to feel exciting and immersive. For fans of the series, this is a must-play—and for newcomers, there’s no better time to join the chaos.Gameplay and Mechanics: Familiar and RefinedOne of the highlights of Dead Island 2 is how it nails the fundamentals of the franchise, even refining them to be smoother and more immersive. The combat is as visceral and engaging as ever, but with far better animations and mechanics. Killing zombies feels satisfyingly intense, and the animations bring a new level of detail and realism. The card-based system for special attacks and buffs is a brilliant addition that adds strategic depth without complicating the fun. Jakob and Dani’s hilarious voice lines and banter lend a great layer of personality, keeping things entertaining even during the most intense moments.Challenging and Exciting DLC: SOLAThe SOLA DLC was another fantastic experience! The new map, fresh zombie types, and additional weapon options made it a challenging thrill ride that I couldn’t put down. I loved how the DLC seamlessly added to the game’s universe, keeping the excitement alive while adding complexity and challenge to the game. Each encounter felt new and engaging, thanks to the expanded zombie roster and unique map environments, making SOLA a high point in my time with Dead Island 2.New Features and AmbianceFrom the moment you start, it’s clear that Dead Island 2 has poured effort into ambiance and detail, from gritty textures to the epic intro music that perfectly sets the tone. The soundtrack goes hard, bringing the kind of energy that sticks with you long after you log out. The addition of "curveballs"—a variety of throwable bombs from flashbangs to beehives—adds a new layer of strategy that kept combat fresh and unpredictable. While they removed the option to drive cars, I honestly didn’t miss it; the game offers so many other ways to navigate and interact with the world that the lack of vehicles felt like a non-issue.Multiplayer Fun and Weapon CustomizationPlaying with a friend elevated the experience even further. The co-op is seamless and makes for a fantastic team experience. Weapon customization is top-notch, with countless ways to upgrade and modify your arsenal. It’s a thrill to experiment with new combinations, making each weapon feel like a unique creation tailored to my play style. Whether you're setting zombies on fire, freezing them, or delivering electrifying blows, the options feel endless and are satisfying to execute.Hope for a Future ReleaseDespite some of the tough criticism the game has faced, Dead Island 2 feels like a true evolution for the franchise, and I hope the feedback doesn’t dissuade the developers from moving forward with Dead Island 3 (especially after that tantalizing endgame tease!). It’s clear they’re passionate about their work, and this title shows how much they’ve honed their craft since the first installment. Living in a time when I can experience this level of quality from a series I’ve loved for years is something I truly appreciate.Final ThoughtsDead Island 2 is a beautifully crafted game that any fan of the series will enjoy. From its compelling ambiance and upgraded combat to the humor, voice acting, and fantastic multiplayer features, this game is worth every minute. For both newcomers and veteran zombie-slaying enthusiasts, Dead Island 2 delivers a highly entertaining, memorable, and thrilling experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel this is a more modern version of the Dead Island games and I feel like ♥♥♥♥ saying that. I think they've aged horribly coming back to em, they feel stiff and janky a lot of the time. And it sucks, like me going back to Force Unleashed 1, just stiff and hard to feel satisfying. Dead Island 1 and Riptide felt that way and I hate that, games were fun when I was a kid. Loved Dead Island and I think Dying Light just ruined my expectations going back. Dying Light just felt so smooth while Riptide felt like driving a truck. This game feels like a modern truck. Slow and weird but very smooth and fun. Enemies react to hits so well and the weapons ♥♥♥♥ them up. No joke, the gore in this game is next level. You can beat the jaw off a zombie and even have it dangling from their skull. I remember I was testing out how far the gore goes and bashed a dead zombie in the back of the skull until the brain was just caved in and jiggling with each bash. Broke a dude's ankle and it was just swinging in his meat suit. It's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥ detailed and amazingly good. I don't suggest this game for the faint of heart. Story is Borderlands-y but in a better way. Everything is a caricature of millenial and zoomer stereotypes, just streamers and dumb kids. I don't hate it at all, find some characters annoying and others just funny. Story was never the best part nor was it taken seriously. Felt like a Romero film for chirst's sake. Matter of fact, they have an Oscar-Like award called a Romero for zombie films. So it's really just trying to be a cheesy and campy zombie film like Romero's films past Dawn. It's LA stereotypes as well so just smarmy asshats or surfer bros. I live in Cali so it's just all the places with the worst people: Santa Monica Pier, Venice Beach, Belair, Beverly Hills, all the places that have the worst kinda people. Well, worst stereotypes. Weapons are fun, the weapon crafting is fun but taxing as you get further in rarity. I think it follows the same as Borderlands which is at level 15 you start seeing purples everywhere. Barely Level 23 so let's see if the Guaranteed Legendary drops in two levels. Gonna be a pain to repair it but eh, I will manage. The higher the rarity, the more expensive it is to repair. You don't use parts (thank Romero in the sky) but you need a lot of cash. I'm paying 5K to repair my blues and almost 10k for my purples. Been trying to keep a few low end items for cheap repairs and high end items for larger ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but that hurts. Only really taxing thing about the game, managing that with mini-bosses roaming around makes dealing with anything a pain. The perk system is a bit thought out. You have a loadout card system and have a limited amount of space to use them, so you gotta think about the ones you want to use the most, which speak to you and all that jazz. Not like the skill tree from the previous games where you can become an untouchable monster to the zombies depending on the character. And the cards aren't character specific, you can randomly find cards for different characters that you can use without being them. You can turn a slow classed dude into a speed freak with a knife that kills and break bones in minutes. Or you can be a lil tiny woman that can wield a 40lb sledge that breaks through Crushers with ease. Can take time to do that but it's fun. I like this system more. Weird it took them this long to get the game, I was still in High School when that I'm the Bomb trailer came out. Even playing the E3 2015 build that got leaked - think you can still download and play it - glad we got the game in the state. I ain't gonna say Dying Light is better or worse, they're both great at doing the same thing for different audiences. Don't like the parkour? Play this game, it's dumb fun with hardly anything to think about while playing. tl;dr: Game's great, amazing gore, stupid plot, and I'm happy it came out.

_childDocuments_.review: While some graphical elements are very impressive, at its core, this is an extremely mediocre game.This game likes to wrangle the player with contrived limitations. At the starting areas this is not so noticable, even though some character decisions and being unable to climb certain walls feels frustrating. But this has nothing on the later parts of the game, where you face straight up invisible walls and extremely hare-brained cutscene out-of-control decisions your character takes so just the plot can happen. Dialogue, log and quest writing become tired, line delivery botched, and the pacing and game tone are all over the place. The last two locations are no joke corridors with barely any exploration or side passages. And then the game just ends, dropping plotlines, disregarding characters and pretending to deliver a mystifying cliffhanger. In other words, feels a lot like Dead Island 1, except much more expensive in production.All in all, this game is better than DI1, though it is hands down inferior to Dying Light.It is an OK game to play in coop, though once again, I will recommend Dying Light over this. Surprisingly, I will even recommend DI1 higher, since it has a benefit of being a jankfest you can play in coop.

_childDocuments_.review: [PLAYED AND FINISHED IN SINGLEPLAYER, NOT A CO-OP REVIEW]GAMEPLAY: 7/10, Phenomenal, a bit finnicky at times but the impact of melee weapons and the gun-play are just AMAZING. The Maimed System makes it feel like you're really doing damage to the zombies with their body taking physical, visual damage from your weapons, caustic x, fire, lightning, etc.There's a lot of components that could've used work, the card-system feels out of place, the particles and pop-ups sort of overwhelm the senses a lot, and screamers have way too much health. It also doesn't feel like you become stronger in terms of defense, zombies level with you so they take the same amount of health as your health-bar just gets bigger to compensate.WEAPONS: 10/10 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ THE WEAPONS ARE SO FUN AND THE MODDING MAKES THEM HIT LIKE A TRUCK I LOVE IT I LOVE IT I LOVE ITSTORY: Main story is a 6.5/10. I was enjoying it a lot but the ending cut-off just feels so underwhelming and leaves a lot of questions unanswered (maybe they're answered in the DLC, idk). Side quests are a blast as well, Curtis is the GOAT.However the actual objective diversity is very...lackluster. Every mission is some combination of these 6 options:-Kill all the zombies in an area-Pressure balance puzzle-Find a key-card/key-Investigate the contents of a room for an idea of where the thing you're looking for is.-Grab a thing-Find a way through a path covered in fire, caustic x, or electrified waterCHARACTERS: 7/10, The characters are fun all around, even if they're a bit flat. Patton and Rikky were my MVP's and I wish we got more of Michael. Amanda was fun, even if her side quests were annoying as ♥♥♥♥. Captain Vixen and Sebastian were also a neat duo, and the VCLA students were fun. ___The thing that kills this game for me is the length. I finished 60% of the game in 16 hours, and got halfway through the story in my first livestream session of the game. 60$ for a game that could be 100%'d in a day. It is such a shame that over a decade of development for less than a day of playtime to finish it, but what's there is an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blast.A fun game, co-op is probably a lot of fun, but wait 'till it's on sale to get it.6.5/10 game overall.

_childDocuments_.review: The game works perfectly so far (6 hours in). Having a blast in co-op from the get go. Melee feels weighty and satisfying, the gameplay loop is much like the first Dead Island with less jank and more tastefully written characters with a sense of humor. The world they've created with Hell-A is nothing short of beautiful, albeit restrictive in the sense of loading from zone to zone. The game has introduced a unique change to the character progression system through inter-changeable skill cards. This allows full autonomy for the player to make and enjoy a substantial amount of builds for their Slayer. Skill trees can be rather daunting, and I view this as a welcome change that promotes ease of accessibility while maintaining creative freedom, absent of long descriptions and interlinked paragraphs of text that simply tell you that your character now does 2% more damage with a hypothetical skill.I've viewed a lot of individuals stating the game requires you to go through EGS as a requirement to play online. I haven't noticed this at all. It has certainly asked for permission to which I denied it's request. My time played online has been very stable, no disconnects or desyncs and no drops in performance, though I understand this will also differ between hardware. In summary, the game performs exceedingly well, it's been a very enjoyable experience so far in both singleplayer and co-operative play. I haven't experienced any gamebreaking issues and my entire online experience has been enjoyed without the requirement of a connection to the EGS. Hope this helps!

_childDocuments_.review: Best in the series so far! If only they didn't sell out their fans for profit from Epic. But putting that aside, let's dive into the guts of it. All the characters are likeable, the gore system is disgustingly brutal—there's nothing like smacking a zombie with a concrete block staff and seeing their jaw hang off or their scalp flinging around!I'm genuinely impressed. Yes, loading screens exist, but I never had to wait more than 2 seconds to traverse. LA is absolutely stunning with bright, vibrant palm trees and vivid colors all around. Even playing on less-than-recommended specs, I had no stutter or FPS drop, which left me shocked, to say the least.The sound design is a solid 10. Walking over corpses and hearing that grotesque squelching never gets old. And as usual, they've killed it with the soundtrack. Heavy melodic guitar riffs while bashing zombies' brains in? Brilliant.Slight spoiler warning: I'm so glad to see Sam B make a return. It truly floods back those memories of 'Who do you voodoo?' while running around in the swamps of Banoi, and he's just as badass as in the previous titles.Overall, as a huge fan, the wait was definitely worth it. My only complaints are the fact that they sold it off as a timed exclusive to a terrible launcher in exchange for profit (despite Epic being an awful platform) and the fact that Deep Silver is already a AAA company. Also, the game feels rather short compared to its predecessors.But hey, if you're looking for a brutal, gory, and vibrant zombie slasher game, as of this review, the game is on a 50% sale, so I would highly recommend it!   TLDR;The Good:- New Gore system is disgustingly Brutal- Music is brilliant - Bright and Vibrant- Characters are charming and funny while also Badass- Sound design is amazing- Plenty of Easter eggs to find across LA- Short loading screens- Steam Deck approved and tested by the devs without issues The Bad:- Sold out the fans for times exclusivity to a less superior platform- Epic requirement to play online- 8 hours in and almost half way to beating the game

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. Ignore the people claiming it needs the Epic game store, it only needs a service to connect to online play that runs when the game runs, not the full-blown store, and it installs when you boot the game up and doesn't linger.I originally played this on the Epic store, and bought it again because I enjoyed it enough to want to have a copy on Steam and play on my Steam Deck.The game is a ♥♥♥♥ ton of fun, with a simple but solid story-line, a ton of different weapons, skills and perks to find. Side quests are fun, give varied rewards and the game never feels like a grind and weapon customization is diverse and it's impressive how many viable builds I've managed to make with different skill combinations and weapons and customization. The game also has a really fun cast of characters that I really enjoyed a lot more than I was expecting to from this type of game. I was expecting borderlands-like cringe and was pleasantly surprised. There are a few cringy/nutty side characters, but those feel more like something from Dead Rising than anything else.The combat is rock solid; every weapon feels a joy to use thanks to an incredible dynamic gore system and fantastic sound and game design. The different elements have fun effects that you can expand using perk combinations, and guns feel powerful and ammo distribution feels balanced; you never are starving for it, nor swimming in it. Durability feels like it's in a great place; weapons degrade with use, with different types and perks quickening or slowing the durability drain. However, every weapon can be repaired for a little bit of money, so if you have a favorite weapon, you can keep repairing it indefinitely without hassle. The durability and enemy resistances does promote the player switching weapons without punishing them for having a favorite. Getting money is fairly easy and you can simply sell weapons you don't like to maintain the weapons you love.Speaking of favorite weapons; there's no limit on leveling up a weapon, up-to the level cap. Weapons drop at your level, and once you out level them, you can simply upgrade them to keep them relevant through the entire game, and enhance them new perks you find.They updated the stash so you have plenty of space to hoard all those cool weapons you find, and there are a ton of them. Weapon and material drops are relatively generous, and you can get unique legendary weapons from quests and hidden caches.I definitely, absolutely, recommend this game. I play a lot of "zombie themed" games and this is one is definitely one of my favorites because the combat is just so satisfying.One big caveat: Just don't connect your Steam account to Epic when prompted; its not needed for online play. If you get stuck "Connecting to Epic Online Services" this is why; it's currently bugged. Just unlink the accounts from each other from Epic's Account management website.

_childDocuments_.review: An mediocre zombie apocalypse story, a good zombie hack-and-slash sandbox, and a great Dead Island game. Overall a good game. If you really crave the Hell-in-paradise setting that the original game had, this game has it, and it's definitely worth $60. While $60 is a fair price for the content for most other people as well, I would recommend waiting for the game to go on sale; it goes on sale for 50% off so often that I swear I see the game selling for $30 more than I see it selling for $60. That's the TL:DR, I go more in depth on the game below.The execution of the zombie apocalypse story is serviceable. The story didn't really sway me. It's the typical "scientists are saying the ends justify the means again" type of story, and it works fine. But if you're looking for the game to pull your heart strings around like how the first Dying Light did, or even how the first Dead Island game could at times, I wouldn't get your hopes up with this game. This game has a lot of character (I'll talk about that later) but that character is not about drama or deep feelings. It has fun, if slightly mundane characters, good (somewhat dated) written comedy, and some interesting side stories.The zombie sandbox as designed in this game is alright: There is a good variety of zombies to slash and smash, but it's just that- just about every zombie, with exception of the butcher, amounts to a larger zombie with more health, a problem that is easily solved by just hitting it really hard in the head with your choice of big stick (pointy bits optional). There are very few zombie encounters that push you to get creative in how you turn that walking corpse into a pile of blood and guts. But that process is rendered in incredible, gory detail. The gore system in this game is fantastic; from exploding in a burst of red mist to hacking off limbs and literally slicing zombies in two, it holds up wonderfully. The character customization options are limited compared to Dead Island and Dead Island: Riptide though. The skill cards were an interesting twist on the typical RPG system, but it lacked a lot of depth. The same could be said of the weapon sandboxing; the vast quantities of weapons and blueprints in Dead Island and DI: Riptide make way for a somewhat smaller, more concise selection of implements and modifications. There is still a good variety but, again, it's lacking compared to previous titles. The exception is in firearms: guns shine in Dead Island 2, with their own selection of mods and a few very fun unique legendaries. Overall, the sandboxxing was significantly simplified; player choice on their character building and choice of weapons matters less than previous games. The map is also much more linear, unfortunately. In an industry full of open world games, an RPG with a focus on exploration and discovery with a severely limited, almost linear world feels downright wrong.But the most important part? Some may disagree but, to me, dead island has never been defined by being the best at zombies -the horror of infection, the pain of loss and watching those you cared about shamble around like lifeless caricatures of the person you once knew. Even at it's peak moments in the first Dead Island, other titles and series have always done this better. What this game nails is its setting. Dead Island 2 practically breathes, sweats, and bleeds "hell in paradise." This was what really made Dead Island stand out in the first place, and it's what makes it stand out now. The (virtual) physical comedy and shock humor, as well as this contrast between the sunny and lavish California environment and the zombies and gore inhabiting it, all are executed extremely well, and much of the game makes great use of it to enhance the player's experience. Most of the time I spent playing this game wasn't spent wishing it had the weapon selection of Dead Island or the character building of Dying Light and DI: Riptide. It was spent clawing through crowds of zombies with flaming claws, splattering blood and guts everywhere, taking a calming stroll down the beach in Santa Monica while my friend sends zombified surfer bros flying with explosives like they're makeshift fireworks flying into the sunset.

_childDocuments_.review: "I keep dying to my own fire is this a bug" -rev3 or something, memes.This game is great fun but it's missing a *lot* the original had going for it. I got a list, here's the order of my list that it's in:Legendary weapons are non-existent, basically. I think two are available before the end of the game, maybe 8 in total, including from the DLC, all from side-quests, all the rest gotten at the end of the game. That's crap, and not the point of games like these. Random legendary drops that change the way you play completely are kind of required in looter-shooters. You can't even use them! IT'S THE END OF THE GAME! You can't give it to a new roll, it's level locked! WHAT'S THE POINT?! How'd you eff that up? Are you serious?The Rage system: Another thing they boned for this game. Aside from a last resort, I never used this that much because it wasn't actually that powerful. I also highly doubt they gave each and every playable character their own version of rage, so I doubt this changes between characters.The card system: Let's be honest with ourselves. There are near useless cards, and there are broken cards. It's not until you reach the endgame of the DLCs that you get anything that will change your cards up. You will never bother using spit during rage, it's useless, in both forms. You will never use the high kick, the dropkick you get from the start is too useful. You *will* forget you have a special move, and never use it. You will slot everything to "if it maims it does a thing" and keep it that way so they proc all the time and go about your day. This system needed several overhauls before going forward. It's bad.There's no way to change the difficulty, but also, there's no penalty for dying,  Stupid but I'll take it.Playing offline isn't possible because they can't just check my steamID to see if I own the DLC, so it gets stuck trying to auth when you don't have internet. *Crap like this makes people more likely to pirate, stop it.*The first line is a joke at the expense of a very old review from a now dead yt channel, but seriously, it's way too easy, ESPECIALLY late-game, to own yourself with your own attacks. The hazards don't go away for a good two or so minutes either, so you're kind of stuck...waiting for it to go away. Or you just eat the damage and heal. Again, stupid.Dodging and blocking, they don't really work all that much? A *lot* of zombies don't get tripped up by the dodge, and a *lot* of my brain cells die when I think of using block. Ok maybe I'm not the guy to ask for the block stuff, sue me.The limit on parts gets annoying very fast. It got to the point I *pined* for the old dead island and the ability to just edit an ini file to make it so I could hold 999 of anything, including the energy drinks, which you weren't supposed to be able to hold. Limiting me to five healing items at a time is fine and all but you're also *regularly* put into positions where you have to spam heals.The haus DLC. In general. It's not good, the one weapon type you get is honestly crap and I stopped using it after leaving the DLC area.The story. I skipped most of it after the mid point. It's not good. Then again, it's never been good. Story wasn't the point of this series.So why do I recommend this game, then? Because it's fun. It's not as good as the original, but it's better than Riptide. The only things I would demand change if it got another entry is ACTUALLY PUT PROPER LEGENDARY DROPS  IN THE GAME.Oh, and I never got the problems all these other people did with the EGS crap, literally never bothered me. Screw the haters.Also Eff the SoLA end boss all my homies hate that prick.

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay. The gameplay is pretty good and the gore is much more gnarly than the previous games. I just wish I could say the same for the story and characters. A lot of them are just annoying or unlikeable, although to be fair this does take place in California so they got that part right. The plot isn't terrible but it has a lot of strange decisions. The base game's ending is so bad that the devs said screw it and added a bunch of sci-fi elements with the DLCs. Not gonna spoil it of course, you'll know when you get there. The comedy is just awful. A few times it was funny but most of the time the joke either doesn't land or it just makes me physically cringe. When the game attempts horror it's usually really good but then they immediately ruin it when the PC or another character makes a dumb quip out of the blue. If this game focused more on horror elements instead of trying to be hip and cool with the kids this game would've been amazing even if the dialogue wasn't all that good. Also would have made this game a lot more faithful to the previous games.There's a lot of weapons to use which is great. There might be less than Riptide though but I'm not sure. Guns, unlike in the first Dead Island, are usually pretty good against zombies. Shotguns might be kinda bad at least in my experience. I might just be crazy though.The workshop is exactly what it is. You repair weapons and add mods, but unlike the previous games you can also scale your weapons to your current level at the cost of money. It's a good or bad change depending on how you felt about grinding for weapons from before. For me, I don't mind the change. I also don't mind the fact that you can get the strongest weapons through quests rather than grinding, which is good because trying to get a good weapon like the Defender of the Motherland in DI1 was almost impossible without exploits or just being really lucky.The zombie designs are much more detailed than before. The gore like I said before is amazing. The killmations are pretty cool although some are a little awkward and some are a bit over the top. They change based on where you're hitting them from which is neat. They might get a little repetitive though. The enemy variety in this game is definitely a step up too, although I wish you could still damage them instead of the zombies just being immune to it completely. I can't say much about co-op as I haven't tried it. If they let you do co-op without having to install software you don't want I might give it a shot, although I'm not typically a fun of playing with others anyway so I don't really care.I can't say much about most of the characters as I haven't played all of them but I did play Ryan and despite the unfunny stuff and the constant reminders that he's a stripper he's got some pretty real moments.TLDR; If Steam reviews had a mixed option I'd probably pick that. It's similar to Borderlands 3 where the story is bad but the gameplay is good. However unlike THAT game, you can sit through the bad and enjoy the good parts of the game. You'd be better off waiting for a major sale rather than paying full price anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game was an awesome addition to the franchise and definitely stands on it's own as a super fun experience. The weapon mods and skill cards kept combat feeling pretty varied throughout the game and you really felt more powerful as you progressed. The gore and details with maiming and melting zombies was super fun with some wacky rag-dolls adding to that as well. The story felt a little goofy at times and I wish the game let you spend more time with some characters before they died, but it wasn't ever to egregious. Found myself craving more hordes of zombies often as they could feel a little sparse and sometimes they would spawn back in areas you just cleared unnaturally quickly. There were some moments that were surprisingly creepy and unsettling as well, which was nice. But overall it was just a fun lighthearted zombie slaying playground with a simple narrative to give you more reasons to kill more zombies and have more fun.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: 🎵  🎵🎵  🎵🎵  🎵🎵  🎵🎵  🎵🎵  🎵The right middle ground between big-scale extravagant ideal depictions of a paradise gone awry, and a staggering amount of attention to the finer details. DI2 didn't try to go big as all other competitors in the same genre, but it lingered in my mind simply thanks to how it turned its straightforwardness into a comfortable yet rarely formulaic rhythm. Would I have preferred a true open world or at least a seamless one? Of course. Would I have preferred fewer sewer levels? Sure. Would I have loved some more creative weapon designs? Definitely. But I am completely satisfied with the current DI2 we have, a love letter to the cult B horror movies that have just the right amount of campiness and body horror, a delightfully punchy combat system that has just the right amount of variety for the game's length, a card-based character building system that's just the right amount of complex for this type of game, and some shockingly decent voice acting and out of the left field writing choices that impressed me with how ambitious the developers are willing to go. As someone who adored the janky original 2011 Dead Island, one of my first purchases on Steam and a pretty significant part of my teenager years, I couldn't have asked for a better comeback.

_childDocuments_.review:
Dead Island 2 is stylish, vibrant and flooded with zombie infection. Explore iconic, gore-drenched Los Angeles. Meet larger-than-life characters. Slay countless foes in exquisitely bloody detail. And evolve to become the ultimate Zombie Slayer!

A deadly virus is spreading across Los Angeles, turning inhabitants into zombies. Bitten, infected, but more than just immune, uncover the truth behind the outbreak and discover who -or what- you are. Los Angeles is in quarantine and the military have retreated. Only you, and the handful of others who happen to be resistant to the pathogen, hold the future of the city (and humanity) in the balance.

Features:

    Explore HELL-A – Dead Island 2 takes players across the most iconic locations of the City of Angels, now stained with horror, in an exciting pulp journey from the verdant suburbia of Beverly Hills to the quirky promenade of Venice Beach.

    Brutal Melee Sandbox – Combat delivers the most intense, visceral and gory first person experience possible, with plenty of weapons and tactical (and brutal) options to chew your way through the zombie horde. Whether you’re slicing, smashing, burning or ripping, we want you to truly feel it.

    Be the Ultimate Zombie Slayer – There are six characters to choose from, each with their own unique personality and dialogues. You can fully customize the abilities of each Slayer, with our brand-new skill system allowing you to re-spec instantly and try out the craziest builds.

    Zombie Infestation – Ready to experience the most advanced dismemberment system in games? Our LA is crawling with zombies that look and react realistically. These mutated wretches are the reanimated, rotten heart of Dead Island 2 with dozens of distinct zombie types, each with their own mutations, attacks and hundreds of visual LA-themed variants. Our monsters are relentless, challenging, and true Los Angelinos. Will you be able to survive?

    A Cinematic Co-op Adventure – As a proper RPG experience, Dead Island 2 offers plenty of exciting quests, a crazy cast of characters, and a thrilling pulp story, to truly immerse you in its twisted universe. Re-playability is guaranteed. Add an over-the-top co-op mode for up to three players, and you’ll stay in LA for a very long (and gory) trip.

name: Ary and the Secret of Seasons
detailed_description: Journey across the magnificent world of Valdi! Ary and the Secret of Seasons is an award-winning adventure game following a young girl named Aryelle, or Ary, as she journeys across the great world of Valdi. By becoming the Guardian of Winter, Ary gains the ability to manipulate the seasons around her. Ary will learn to control the seasons and use them to defeat enemies, overcome obstacles, and solve complex puzzles on her adventure across Valdi. Long ago, the world of Valdi was threatened by an evil mage. After a great struggle, he was defeated by the Legendary Warrior and sealed inside the Vault, imprisoned for all eternity. To ensure the mage's imprisonment, four great sages swore to keep watch and protect the Vault. They formed the original Guardians of Seasons, a secretive organization now steeped in history and legend. After a mysterious force throws the seasons of Valdi into disarray, Ary decides to assist the Guardians of Seasons and sets out to find the source of the mayhem. Using her wits and courage, Ary will have to overcome monstrous enemies, secret plots, and stuffy traditions to save Valdi and bring balance to the world once more. Rewarding exploration. Harnessing the power of the seasons, Ary can traverse sweeping landscapes in search of new destinations, solving amazing environmental puzzles to progress. Captivating storytelling. Ary is recruited to help the Guardians of Seasons, an old organization caught up by rigid traditions. As she ventures through uncharted locations across Valdi, Ary will discover secrets and hidden meanings behind the Guardian of Seasons. Dynamic environments. Manipulate the world around Ary with her environmental powers. Leap between ecosystems to bend the world and seasons to her needs. Fluid combat. Ary’s skills will be put to the test as she encounters foes looking to thwart her progress – from local inhabitants to hulking behemoths, she will use all the tools at her disposal to overcome monumental obstacles. about_the_game: Journey across the magnificent world of Valdi! Ary and the Secret of Seasons is an award-winning adventure game following a young girl named Aryelle, or Ary, as she journeys across the great world of Valdi. By becoming the Guardian of Winter, Ary gains the ability to manipulate the seasons around her. Ary will learn to control the seasons and use them to defeat enemies, overcome obstacles, and solve complex puzzles on her adventure across Valdi. Long ago, the world of Valdi was threatened by an evil mage. After a great struggle, he was defeated by the Legendary Warrior and sealed inside the Vault, imprisoned for all eternity. To ensure the mage's imprisonment, four great sages swore to keep watch and protect the Vault. They formed the original Guardians of Seasons, a secretive organization now steeped in history and legend. After a mysterious force throws the seasons of Valdi into disarray, Ary decides to assist the Guardians of Seasons and sets out to find the source of the mayhem. Using her wits and courage, Ary will have to overcome monstrous enemies, secret plots, and stuffy traditions to save Valdi and bring balance to the world once more. Rewarding exploration. Harnessing the power of the seasons, Ary can traverse sweeping landscapes in search of new destinations, solving amazing environmental puzzles to progress. Captivating storytelling. _childDocuments_.review: I was eagerly awaiting this game well before its release. On release, so many people were complaining about issues I figured I'd give it more time and wait for patches or a discount. I finally bought it last sale for €10, or a 75% discount from the €40 list price. I played through the whole game bar a few sidequest endings. And oh, god. So much wasted potential. Why, devs? Why would you release something so clearly unfinished?I have to make clear that this game, in its current state, is absolutely not worth €40 to me. If I had paid €40 for it, I would have been very angry. For €10, it was a good deal. This is the main reason I can't recommend the game at this time, but as I played my opinion changed several times on whether I'd recommend it or not. Ary and the Secret of Seasons is a template for an excellent game. The aesthetic is great. Ary's world is cartoonish, but looks good, especially on a macro scale. There are many beautiful vistas that will make amazing poster screenshots for your desktop wallpaper. The cities, in particular, and the large spaces in the dungeons/temples. Ary herself is cute, well animated and has a plethora of outfits you can dress her in. Crocus is silly and distinct, as are the guardians. Their personalities shine through their visual design and through their voice acting, which is good but scarce.The puzzles are also great. Most of the puzzle solving in the game is concentrated in the four temples and a couple dungeons. Those temples are top notch--wouldn't be out of place in any AAA game. I had fun solving each temple--there was some challenge, but they never got frustrating.A lot of the platforming and puzzle solving in the game make use of the cool season change mechanic. I imagine the developers had to work hard on this part of the game, and that paid off. In fact, there is nothing wrong with the premise in general. The combination between the asthetic and past of Ary's world, as well as what little visual storytelling there is, are intriguing and leave you wanting more.The boss fights in the winter and spring temples were fun and memorable. The final boss was also OK. I would have liked more fights like these. The combat mechanics in general were... fine. I didn't have a lot of use for the slingshot or the solstice powers.One of the things that pissed me off most was the dialogue. Most of it is conveyed through writing, which is stiff and feels off. In their written dialogue, all characters have the same vaguely mocking voice. There is also storytelling through infodumps, which are boring and hard to care about. The dialogue system is terrible--just rectangles with Arial text, which makes the unnecessarily long paragraphs even harder to read. By the end I was just skipping most of it. This might be related to the equally mediocre menu and inventory system.If you look at Ary's beautiful world more closely, it feels... Empty. NPCs are either immobile statues or have very simple animation loops. The ones who talk all say the same two or three things, usually random stuff. The few NPC quests are incredibly boring go-here-then-go-there garbage. NPC lines never change, even when the story has moved on and they no longer make sense. In fact, nothing ever changes. When Yule's weather was fixed and back to winter, the waterwheels were still spinning happily (clipping through the frozen water) and the farmers were hoeing their fields, ignoring the fact that they were now frozen solid. The exact same three shopkeepers (other than the wig seller) exist everywhere at the same time, selling the same things for the same price. If you buy everything, that's it.There are many chests that you can collect, and that's a good thing, but... Usually they just contain a small amount of money. After the 30th time you get 20 or 30 coins from a chest, about the same as the loot from 2 weak mobs, you're going to feel kind of robbed. A few chests contain more money, but outside the dungeons and one quest that I can think of, no chests contain anything else. Consider that each outfit costs in the neighborhood of 1000 coins. Combat upgrades are also expensive. It's a lot of chest-opening grind for very little. The whole thing feels like a waste of time.There are only two "weak" template enemies everywhere, whether it makes sense or not, humanoid hyenas and some kind of weird exploding aquatic mushrooms (there are a few others but only in very specific locations).The game crashed to desktop several times, particularly in the Ostara region (multiple locations).There is a dialogue option from Dagdann in the dome, near the end, that locks the game until you alt+f4.The largest hyena's collision capsule (the one that dashes and kicks) always remains upright after it dies, preventing the coins it drops from being collected.Switching to winter inside a piece of ice will kick you into the underground void.It takes about an hour to climb anything, because for some reason Ary climbs at a snail's pace. Often, she will not climb over the top ledge but stop near the top, so you have to hop away and then double jump back onto the ledge, which is quite difficult and means some platforming is absolutely miserable and janky. It also doesn't help that sometimes the camera wants to be inside a tree or a wall of ice while you're doing this.Others have mentioned how you can't run uphill. This applies to every little bump and slope, meaning you're slowed down all the time.It's impossible to finish the guardians' sidequests before defeating the final villain.It seems to be impossible to do certain things after the seasons are fixed, such as in the big cathedral in the summer region or climbing the huge vine wall in the autumn desert.I collected all three legendary keys but only two showed up in my inventory. I was unable to unlock the sword. Not that it would have been very useful, as this can only be collected near the end, when you barely need to fight anyone anymore. Weapons in this game are weird. There are a few alternatives, but most are useless due to pacing, such as when you get a weapon in the mines only to lose it almost immediately. You spend nearly all of the game with the mechanical sword.It's the same with the platforming challenges in the outside world, which are made frustrating by the janky mechanics, and require you to unlock additional platforming mechanics in the four temples before they can be solved, and the overly expensive outfits. All of those things would have made being in Ary's world more fun  the game, but out of some misguided sense of "this has to be longer" are essentially endgame content only.This game needed another year of development. It felt like the developers didn't properly play through it in order to test and debug it. Like, not even once. If that wasn't practical, they could have asked for beta testers. And if they couldn't afford to continue development, then they shouldn't be selling the game for full price. I did have plenty of puzzle-solving, platforming fun in this game. There is an entertaining experience here. There is value. But the frustration and issues and disappointment mean it's not worth the current full price. Sorry.An experienced lead developer might have seen the writing on the wall and limited the scope of the game. The terrible writing, sidequests, NPCs, etc. are unnecessary and make the game look worse than it is. The dungeons are so good, I wish they had just said screw it, gotten rid of the unfinished stuff and focused on debugging and improving their platforming mechanics and adding more equipment and monsters. Or get rid of the equipment/shops too. I would have traded 80% of the non-aesthetic content of the outside world for another cool dungeon with a cool giant boss fight.

_childDocuments_.review: A 40€ unpolished, unfinished, basic and empty, almost asset flip that should be an early access game, trying to evoke some Zelda and old school platforming vibes. The price is inexcusable for a game in this state and this short.It's going for a kind of low poly cartoonish look, but it looks very rough and unfinished, showing noticeable graphical glitches and bland textures, some of them breaking with visible seams and lines and even different colors at certain places. The character models for everyone except for a few main NPC's Ary interacts with look very basic, almost like design placeholders and are poorly animated and voiced. All the menu screens and in-game prompts look very cheap, like something from a trashy mobile game, and there's an issue with interaction triggers. I've noticed them sometimes placed totally to the side of the NPC you're trying to interact with. There are also serious issues with colissions in every way, especially noticeable in platforming. The animations in general are glitchy and full of clipping, even for Ary, whose model is prone to breaking. I've had her stuck in animations with arms outstretched, like a chicken running and clucking around or stuck inside scenery. I've even managed to clip under the game world by just using season powers trying to do a puzzle. And when swinging a weapon, the animation would sometimes get stuck for a few seconds at the end of the swing. Some of the animations and sounds during conversations and cut scenes are comically out of touch with what is going on in the game world, like they're being played at the incorrect time. Or is the game maybe going for some comic relief? If it is, it's embarrassing and very, very cringe worthy. The environments you go through are really empty, giving the entire game world an unfinished look.Combat is simple, done well with minor lock on problems and includes dodges, parries, extra season powers and even a slingshot, but is boring and pointless, except for a few boss fights with some nice puzzle mechanics for them. Regular enemies drop coins since the latest patch, but there's no experience and it's better just ignoring them and running past, unless there's a chest near them you can't open until you take care of all the enemies. And there's no healing in combat. Healing is weirdly affected by a skill you can purchase for out of combat healing and some orbs/apples that you occasionally find in pots or on trees. There are chests scattered around the world, but you only get gold coins from them, in varying quantities. No items, no upgrades. There's a lot of sidequests in the game, but they are at odds with the story, dull and feel tacked on just for the sake of having them.The only good thing about gameplay are the dungeons and the platforming in them and even that has issues with clipping and weird collisions. I'm pretty sure I wasn't supposed to solve some things the way I did. This, let's call it fun part of the game, starts when you get well around 40% into it (there's a counter on your save game file), when you are sent into the Dungeons of the Seasons. Before that you're just meandering through those already mentioned empty spaces. Dungeons are well made, fully using the season power mechanics and puzzles to make the dungeons interesting. They even skipped enemies here, there's very little of them, if at all. And when you collect all the accessories and can backtrack for all the stuff you couldn't access, the game does drop an inkling of what it was supposed to be from the start. But, it takes ages to get there and it still manages to just do it in a passable manner.There aren't many collectibles. Besides the mentioned chests, there's a kind of a letter collectible that gives out lore about the world and as you progress the story you get the ability to break giant crystals around the world which increases your hearts. There's a decent amount of cosmetic items, from clothes to helmets and wigs and a few weapons which Ary can equip. When you break the crystals, it's a cutscene, the game switches the weapon you're wielding and doesn't return to the weapon you were wielding before it, making you go through rather awkward and poor menus and equipping of items.Story goes by the wayside here, with all the issues the game has. It's ok, very oriented towards the younger audiences, and nothing spectacular. You play as the titular Ary, looking for her lost brother and trying to restore the seasons in the world of Valdi that is split into 4 different parts. The game does seem to not take itself too seriously, even breaking the 4th wall, but doesn't particularly succeed at melding together all the different things it wants to be. It just comes out as an average children's fairy tale that you can find a dime a dozen.This is a very ambitious project that falls far short of what the developers envisioned. I'm hoping it gets at least fully fixed because it has the potential to be a charming game for a certain audience. But in this state, it would be a mess even if the game was in Early Access and it's not. It's a an unfinished, unpolished, empty mess of a game they had the audacity to charge 40€ for. Until, and if ever this is fixed, .Take a peek inside the  if you like to walk off the beaten path and only sometimes return to the main roads. You might find something worth exploring. And if you do, thank you for the visit.: , 35/38 now, only the 3 annoying ones remaining.38 achievements, most are easy to get, even with the game being bugged as it is. I've earned 32 of them by the end of the game. There's a speedrun (why this is here really boggles my mind), finishing the game without dying and finishing the game without doing any sidequests. Because of the poor state of the game, not dying might be very annoying, wrong collisions, or platforming glitches will drop you to a black screen easily. Speedrun also comes under the annoying part because of the same issues. The game stays playable after the Epilogue.
