_childDocuments_.review: Honestly? Not bad. So far, there are a couple of things that irk me a little, but they don't get in the way too much. If you like these kinds of games, by all means: this is more of what you love. If you maybe played a little bit of the first Life is Strange and weren't a fan of it, or you liked what Telltale was doing but didn't play LiS, this might be worth looking into but you might want to wait for a sale just in case it isn't your thing. It's also worth mentioning that if you hate the lite-adventure style of games where playing it is more akin to watching a movie or television show, this won't change your mind and it's likely not worth considering for you.As is typical for these games, the game will proudly claim that your choices matter. So far, I've replayed a few sections out of curiosity and it's kind of inconsistent. Some choices do change the mood of a scene while others are pretty much what you'd expect (i.e., the only thing that changes in the moment is what line of dialog the main character says). This can be frustrating, but I'm used to it and maybe these choices will add up? I don't know, I'll have to see.Something that I'm more on the fence about is this new feature where, by pressing a certain button, you can pull up your phone and look through texts that other characters are sending you and what's being posted on their social media accounts. This is a great idea on paper, but functionality-wise, it's more akin to the many letters and posters you'll find all throughout Haven. While this does add some interesting backstory and is neat for a second, its novelty wears off quickly when you realize that you have no input in any of it. I guess that might be something you should expect given what this game is, but because the main loop of these types of games is making choices that may or may not come to bite you in the ass, it feels like a bit of wasted potential.Three things that have stuck out to me so far, though: one, the characters are strong and the story has made a strong impression on me. I definitely want to stick this one out to the end. Two, this game is absolutely beautiful. I honestly wasn't expecting this, I'm not as impressed with visuals as I used to be, but the art direction in this--mixed with the technology they're using--consistently has my jaw on the floor. The original game already had great art direction, but this blows it out of the water. Three, the vocal performances are superb. There's a bit of a test I have with games going forward which I'll dub 'the Welles test': if a scene early in the game that would have no impact due to the pacing of the story is made effective solely based on the vocal performances of the main cast, it's a strong indicator of the quality of the voice-over. True Colors passes this test.Overall I'd say my impressions of this are strong so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Life is Strange: True Colors is a captivating and emotionally charged gaming experience that I wholeheartedly recommend. The game follows the story of Alex Chen, a young woman with the ability to sense and manipulate emotions, as she unravels the secrets of her brother's death in the picturesque town of Haven Springs. The game's narrative is its strongest asset, tackling themes of grief, identity, and the power of empathy with exceptional depth and nuance. The characters are expertly crafted, and their relationships feel authentic and relatable. The addition of Alex's empathic powers adds a unique gameplay element, allowing players to delve into the emotional lives of the characters and make choices that have meaningful consequences. The stunning visuals and atmospheric soundtrack further enhance the immersive experience, making Life is Strange: True Colors a must-play for fans of narrative-driven games and anyone looking for a deeply engaging and thought-provoking adventure. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing is you'll want to go in as blind as possible to get the best experience. I'd say this is the best Life Is Strange game to date, I couldn't be happier that Deck Nine took over the franchise, since they did wonders with Before The Storm, and made the most of some tough times.This is largely a stand alone story, Steph from Before The Storm has a much bigger role here, but even if you never played it, you wouldn't be missing anything, she never talks about life before Haven Springs, but her DLC prequel will probably cover that. No one talks about the events of the other games. It's a small tight knit mining down community.The game play is like previous games, but everything feels more polished here, especially being one whole game made in 4 years, no episodic releases. Deck Nine have also made the most mature and human story yet. The game is about emotion, plenty of sadness, fear, anger, and some joy. Sensing emotions isn't something you're constantly doing, Alex does give people privacy unless it's really important to the story. It's a great adventure that makes you feel at home in this town, growing friendships, and learning how much one person can do to change the lives of everyone around her.

_childDocuments_.review: Improves on all shortcomings of previous entries in the series. If you're new to LiS and are hesitant to buy after hearing about the faults of the previous games (cringy dialogue, flat/uncanny animations, poor writing), don't worry as True Colors does away with it all. It has natural dialogue, realistic animation, and beautiful camera-direction all tethered to a solid story. Keep in mind that this story will not be as cataclysmic the first. But it is good for what it is! TC feels very grounded to reality and imo captures the concept of an **everyday hero** far better than the first did. I like the direction TC takes the series and I believe this is where LiS was meant to go since the beginning. It's done well relating the idea that any everyday person could have their own little personal power. And with it, be able to be a kind of "hero" to someone, even if it mostly means themselves. If were going to be sold on the idea that all these games are in the same universe, we can't always have outlandish stories with protags who have extremely destructive powers.This is the definition of "Life is Strange".

_childDocuments_.review: I have to admit I wasn't even a little bit excited about this one, until the day before it was actually released and suddenly I couldn't wait to play it. I don't know why it took me so long to get hyped about it, but I suppose it's better than anxiously waiting forever. The game? Absolutely stunning. They have done it again, given us an absolutely gorgeous game with characters to fall in love with, just have them crush you in the most beautiful way, leaving you with a broken heart and the desperate need for more. At least this time, we didn't have to wait for months for the next chapter. Instead I could sit and play for almost 12 hours straight before realising that "huh, food is a thing," and "jesus my back hurts."In the end? Totally worth it. I loved every second of it and I'm already excited to play it all over again. In the Life is Strange forums people are right now wondering why we would want a remastered collection, because who would want to play the games one more time when you already know how it will end? Well. I do. I've played the first one five times, and I bet I will play it five more when the new collection comes out, and I know for sure I will do the same thing with this one. There's something comforting about it, returning to this universe, even though you know it will leave you heartbroken in the end. Thank you for yet another beautiful game. I already can't wait for whatever heartbreak you'll bring us next.

_childDocuments_.review: Time to Completion: 9.5 hours- LiS #1 was my game of the year. It was an amazing concept and story that pulled on your emotional heartstrings at every turn in creative ways. I consider it one of my favorite games of all time.- LiS #2 was my disappointment of the year.  It made no logical sense and failed to land any emotional impact due to the heavy-handed message and the imbecilic way it was delivered. It's a pile of crap that should be avoided by anyone with a modicum of self-respect. That gives you the extremes I've experienced in this series. If you don't want to read on, let me give you the lowdown right now - LiS: True Colors is more like the first than the second but isn't nearly the great ride.You play as Alex, an empathic young lady newly arrived to the mountain town of Haven Springs. Haven is a seemingly perfect mountain town and for the most part it is. But something bad happens and you spend the rest of the game trying to unravel the conspiracy behind the bad thing.There are a lot of good things about this game. The graphics are attractive and make the town of Haven Springs looks beautiful, the characters are well drawn and it's a very pretty game to play. Most scenes look like they could be paintings and I wish I could move the camera back to get some overhead shots as Windows backgrounds. The animations are fine if nothing to write home about. The voice acting is quite well done with nary a bad performance in the bunch. The music doesn't quite land the way it did in #1 but it's acceptable. However, the devs probably want to try something else besides that soft acoustical guitar as a way of trying to evoke emotions as it's gotten quite stale.Where True Colors shines is in the small moments. Rather than making the mistake that #2 made of a constantly shifting cast and trying for illogical big set-pieces in every other scene, True Colors makes its best impact when you're surrounded by the NPCs you've come to know in a location you're familiar with and somewhat care about. There's a long sequence in the 3rd episode that really has nothing to do with the story but it shines as the best part of the game simply because it's wholesome, takes its time to develop and you get to interact with a number of NPCs. It's in the moments when you're tending tables, or playing foosball with a potential love interest or just spending time with your family where True Colors is at its best.The main story is okay but after an emotional moment fairly early in the game it never really hits that high again. It kind of progresses in a fairly predictable way.  In fact, the game telegraphed most of its punches. I guessed the real villain just an hour or two into the story and the whole story of corporate greed is overplayed. A more personal enemy is usually better for these stories and the predictable way in which one character turned heel didn't provide any real emotional punch. Nor did the climax move the ole' emotional meter. As such, it fell a bit flat.  The same goes for some of the emotional choices - most of them really weren't any choice at all. In fact, I wasn't conflicted about any real choice until perhaps the very last one which takes place after the game is over.  But unlike #2, at least the situations weren't so convoluted as to make a mockery of itself. The NPCs were entertaining but none of them had the kind of growth that LiS #1 had. Characters like Victoria or David Madsen were nuanced and subtle. Not only could you see both the good and bad of what they did, you could influence their actions/reactions. In #2 there were no NPCs who weren't temporary cardboard cutouts. In this game, the NPCs feel more fleshed out but they really don't grow in any appreciable direction. Things may happen to them but they don't tend to make any real progress or changes. So yeah, it's not the best story-driven adventure game out there. Games like the original TWD, LiS #1 and The Wolf Among Us are far better narrative tales, with more developed NPCs and far more interesting choices. True Colors is simply a much more tepid affair. Again, it really shines in the small moments as it flounders a bit in the big ones. The NPCs seem like real and reasonable people but never develop. The graphics are really pretty and the voices are well done but the music doesn't hit home. And the emotional punch is simply lacking throughout. At 9.5 hours to play thorough all 5 episodes, it's nowhere near worth the value of it's absurd $60 price tag. I got it at 60% off ($24) and still think it's probably overpriced at that number. But if I decide to fire it up again I will probably get enough value out of it to not regret buying it. I'll give this one a tepid thumbs up but only buy it on sale.

I played all previous LIS games and i have to say i wasn't impressed with the previous game LIS2 with the two brothers, i felt the decisions didn't have too much meaning and it was more of a movie i was barely a part of. True Colours in comparison is amazing, the visuals are really stunning as well as the lip syncing of the characters to their voices, it really seems a lot more alive! _childDocuments_.review: I can safely say that I'm a fan of the LIS series; I've played all of the games, and loved every one of them. When the announcement for True Colors went up in March, I was immediatly excited. I couldn't wait to jump into another story. I can safely say I was immediately sucked in by the story. The town of Haven Springs is strikingly beautiful, and immediately inviting. The inhabitants of Haven are all believable and distinct, with realistic motives, and emotional reasoning behind their actions, many of which can be directly influenced by Alex's decisions. The story starts off slow, with the early hours serving mostly as an introduction to all of the characters. After the inevitable happens, the story picks up quite quickly; a pace it doesn't drop for the rest of the game. While most of the game, you'll be chasing the mystery of your late brother, thankfully there's some time on the side for other events in the story, which keep things fresh. While the ending was surprising to me, I think it could've been written a bit better, with a couple of questions left unanswered. But don't let those couple of missteps spoil a great story, with a satisfying conclusion. The gameplay is very similar to the rest of the LIS games, with which I mean that the gameplay is mostly based on conversation, with some puzzle aspects. This entry introduces Alex's power; the ability to feel anyone's emotions in an aura, if they are strong enough. This adds a bit of variety to the game, with Alex being able to basically read peoples' minds. Furthermore, she can recall other people's memories from objects strewn around the locations, from which you can learn more about the characters around you.The ability to read emotions was a great choice for this game, as the Life is Strange series already focuses so heavily on characters and interaction. However, the focus remains on conversation. And this is of course done well, with impactful choices, and dialogue options that are usually spot-on with what you'd want to say. The visual fidelity of True Colors is leaps and bounds ahead of all of the past installments of the series, with some of the most beautiful landscapes ever put on a screen. The game does an excellent job of upgrading the visuals without losing the trademark art style of the series. The watercolor-esque textures are brought to light very well with modern rendering techniques such as sub-surface scattering, which is very noticeable on foliage and skin. Raytracing is also a feature, however I've not had the pleasure of experiencing it. It's the blending of technologically advanced techniques with the matte, almost clay-like look of the textures, which gives the game it's soft look and aesthetic. The animation of the characters is an enormous focus in a game as character-driven as this one, and it's safe to say you won't be left disappointed. With facial motion capture as well as body motion capture, all of the characters move and emote in an amazingly natural way. The upgraded animation enables the characters to more easily convey and express emotion, immersing the player even further.The town of Haven Springs is full of interesting characters for Alex to interact with, all of which feel real and are played amazingly by the very talented cast. Some standout characters include Steph and Ryan, the former an eccentric local radio host and record store sensei, and the latter being a charming park ranger. Both are great characters, with memorable lines, and some great scenes. Another great character is Gabe, and while we don't get to spend a lot of time with him, he's almost the secondary protagonist of the story, with him being the person who connects Alex to Haven, and Haven to Alex.Other townsfolk include Jed, Ryan's father and owner of the local bar, Eleanor, the owner of a local flower shop, Duckie, an eccentric retiree, Charlotte, Gabe's girlfriend and dispensary owner/artist, Ethan, her son, along with many others. All of the townsfolk are profoundly realistic and likeable.The game features an amazing soundtrack, comprised of songs by Angus & Julia Stone, mxmtoon, Novo Amor and Kings of Leon, to name a few. The soundtrack is one of the qualities of the series, and True Colors continues that with an amazing score, with dreamy indie/folk tunes, but also some other songs to mix things up a bit. The music really helps with the atmosphere of Haven, and somehow makes everything even more beautiful.I really enjoyed Life is Strange: True Colors. I was really sad when it ended. One of the things I enjoy most about this franchise is how it motivates me personally to make choices. It somehow makes me feel like I can choose my own destiny, just by making one small choice at a time. Also, ever since I've played True Colors, I've been looking at random objects around my house, and just thinking about the memories I have associated with that object, and it's interesting how playing this game made me do that. I love how this game makes you think differently about stuff. I felt like I could relate to the characters, I felt like I could empathize with them. There's a lot of feeling stuff, just in general. Would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a Life is Strange fan since the second game, as I started really following the series after the fourth episode was released. When this game was first announced, I was super excited to see what was in store, and ecstatic that there was yet another Life is Strange game. I will post a warning though, for a long review and spoilers ahead.I'll be going through this review and putting my thoughts about different categories or aspects of the game, and then my summed up thoughts at the very end. Let us begin.First off: the characters.I really liked all of the characters in this game, and I really liked all of their character designs and overall character idea. the only thing that did change throughout gameplay was my feelings towards the characters of the game. You can not like a character due to their personality or motives (for an example), but like their overall character, right? Jed and Mac were the only characters that I didn't really like, but I really liked their overall character idea and how both of them played into the plot (especially with the decision about calming Mac down during his panic attack, I think that's a really interesting decision that plays into his character). Besides that, I quickly fell in love with all of the new characters (especially Gabe, since we get so little time with him), and was thrilled to see that Steph would have a major role. One final thought I will add is that this is the first Life is Strange game where I've actually really liked both potential love interests. Ryan was just a good character in general, and the biggest thing turning me away from choosing him as a love interest the first time was that he was basically Alex's older brother's best friend. Despite this though, I'll probably choose him as the love interest for my second playthrough.Next: the plot.Wow, I really like the big, overarching plot of the game. There wasn't a moment where I wasn't sucked into the plot, and I really wanted to figure out the truth behind Gabe's death. Each twist introduced to the plot was something that I wasn't expecting, and with each episode and each twist sparked more interest in me, especially when everyone found out that Gabe's death wasn't exactly an accident. I don't ever remember there being a time where I thought the plot was too slow or dragging (or if I did feel like that, it was probably due to me not understanding directions because I wasn't fully listening to what was going on).Third on our list: the graphics.I was blown away by the graphics of this game. I will admit though, that also may be because I haven't played a game with graphics as good as this before, and I ended up getting an actual gaming laptop pretty much just so I could play this game (and because I'd been wanting a better laptop for awhile). The graphics of the mountains were absolutely stunning, and I really felt like I lived in Haven Springs with everyone in the game. I couldn't help but sit down at the dock for a little bit each time Alex sat down there, and the environment was just so nice and calming, and the background music or noises helped add to the experience.The second to the last thing on my list: the choices.This is the only real thing that I had trouble with throughout the playthrough. So, I'm just going to get right to it. I didn't like the big choices, and felt like they had no real addition to the story. With that being said, I chose certain decisions because I thought they would have a bigger impact on the story or ploy, only for them to pretty much not matter at the end. Or, more specifically, this is what happened to me with Pike's big decision for whether or not to sign the affadavit. I only said to sign it and not take his fear away because I figured that if I had taken his fear, something would happen to Alex and that would cause future problems within the plot. However, like I said before, that decision wouldn't really affect the end of the plot at all. In fact, thinking about it now, I'm not sure if I even like the final big choice of whether or not you stay in Haven Springs or travel. The only impact the other bigger choices have are who is with you at the bus stop if you choose to leave Haven Springs, or basically who likes you in the game. None of the decisions throughout the game really build up to that final decision, and I was actually a little disappointed by that.Now, the final thing: the rating.And no, I don't mean my rating of the game on a scale of stars, though I will put that at the very end. Instead, I mean the rating that this game has received on the scale from Everyone through NC-17. I understand that this game got rated Mature (or M) due to specific criteria within the game, but I don't think that it should be only playable for ages 18 and up. Instead, I think that an appropriate rating for this game could be ages 16 and up. The quote on quote "worst" thing to happen this game in my opinion is violence or gore, mainly when Jed shoots at Alex and she falls down the mine shaft near the end of the game. Language isn't too much of a problem (especially since the language used in the games are closer to the language that me and my friends use as brand-new 18 and 19 year olds), and the alcohol representation in this game is something that anyone could encounter in their every day life.With everything that I've wanted to say being said due to this super long review, I'll give the TL;DR or shortened version for anyone who didn't read this. So, long story short, I give this game a 4/5 stars. Definitely my favorite Life is Strange game so far, though I have a few complaints about the game, but they don't take away from the overall game. So, thanks for listening, and I hope that you enjoy the game as well!

_childDocuments_.review: This is my least favorite Life is Strange full length game, but it still gets a recommendation, which should tell you that I think highly of the series overall. That being said, it is my least favorite. While Life is Strange 1 and 2 were a complete 180 from each other in terms of storytelling and dynamic, they still had a sort of glue that bonded them together. The music, the mood, and the atmosphere of the first two were very cohesive despite being very different in terms of plot. This game, while being very musically rich, took a departure from the vibe that the first two games had. I'm not saying that the music here was bad, but perhaps it was not as memorable or iconic as in the first two, including Before the Storm. I've downloaded all the songs from Life is Strange, several songs from Life is Strange 2, and quite a few from Before the Storm. Here, I don't know if there's anything that stood out to me enough for me to find a place for it in my playlist. Another factor for why I likely feel that this game is less cohesive to the rest of the series is because of the first two being done by DONTNOD and True Colors being done by Deck Nine. They're two separate companies, and if I'm honest, I vastly prefer DONTNOD's Life is Strange games to Deck Nine's. Deck Nine did do Before the Storm, which I enjoyed, but I feel as though this wasn't quite on the same emotional level as Before the Storm or the previous Life is Strange games were. Given what we know about how Life is Strange played out, the entire game essentially forced the stage to be set for Before the Storm in a tragic, dramatic, and intense way, given the characters and plot lines involved. However, seeing as this was a stand alone game that wasn't a direct prequel or sequel to a previous game, I do feel as though DONTNOD brought more imagination and creativity to the characters and writing vs Deck Nine, as far as original games are concerned. That being said, I know that Deck Nine is in charge of making future Life is Strange titles, so I try to be optimistic about them taking over and building onto DONTNOD's masterpieces. The relationship progressions also didn't feel very cohesive. In the case of Max and Chloe, Chloe and Rachel (in Before the Storm), or Daniel and Sean, you had the whole game's length to essentially focus on and build bonds. Here, the bonds felt very much like an afterthought. The romantic connections in this game rely heavily on superficial factors rather than heavy ones such as deep and meaningful conversations. Here, romancing someone feels like going from point A, to point B, to point C, and then skipping the rest of the points and toppling straight into a very deep and meaningful love connection. If you tell someone that they look cute, give them a gift, and stop yourself from misbehaving in front of them, then they will love you in the end. It didn't feel as raw and organic as it did in other LiS games, where two characters could have an absolutely chaotic, imperfect, and dysfunctional dynamic, while still growing and bonding over the course of the game. I admit that LiS 2's romantic dynamic also fell a bit flat, but in their defense, the romance aspects were always meant to be far more of an afterthought there than it was in True Colors. Plus, the brotherly bonds of Daniel and Sean more than made up for there being a lack of romantic connections. Here, I feel as though the friendship and romantic bonds suffer with progression and lack of proper development. The exploration aspect of the game also initially feels promising until you realize that your locations are essentially limited to one strip of the town center and a very small park. You no longer have the luxury of hanging out in multiple places and are essentially stuck in one small area of town. I found myself running into invisible walls a lot by going outside the bounds far too many times. Places that might look like they'd be accessible actually aren't. There are a few small shops in town (such as the flower shop and tavern) but these environments mostly exist for the sake of running errands, so they don't feel very fleshed out either. The graphics are a solid improvement over the other Life is Strange games, however, and I love the usage of vibrant colors here. My final main critique is that for a game that is centered around a protagonist with an empathy superpower, the main character often seemed very stoic and devoid of emotions, as did some of the side characters. The game did touch on the protagonist, Alex, having had trauma in the past, so this likely played into why her character was the way she was. Nonetheless, some scenes that were supposed to hit really hard and feel very emotional actually ended up having a very monochrome mood to the scene, as if people were just going through acting out the emotions rather than feeling them. Throughout the game, I couldn't help but miss Chloe's emotional outbursts and Sean and Daniel's painfully raw scenes, which made me sob more than once. Here, I didn't really find myself getting teary eyed like I did in Life is Strange 1, Life is Strange 2, and Before the Storm. I'm a total sap who will cry at everything, so, I definitely feel as though I wished that the emotional impact was stronger. Still, despite all of my criticisms, it is still a good game. It's not the best Life is Strange game, in my opinion, but I found it to be about on par with the game Tell Me Why, which is a stand alone game made by DONTNOD, the creators of Life is Strange 1 and 2. My suggestion would be to get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated after finishing: Definitely a great game! I think the choice to release it all at once is slightly less my thing, but since I can (and did) still choose to space out the episodes a little, it doesn't really detract from the experience. I suggest taking a day to sit with the results of each episode before moving on.I strongly recommend this story. That said, to temper my positivity with some criticism that might help you decide if you want it, I think it holds up very strongly compared to the others in the franchise over all, but I would like to have had perhaps one more filler episode, or even a filler scene, to really anchor the core relationships between Alex, Steph, and Ryan--they clearly bond off-screen, according to their texts, but those scenes would have slowed the pace down in a way that I would prefer, giving me a better sense of how they all feel about each other, rather than just serving to justify the trust that the game assumes we will have in them. Though, I suppose, it is much better a game leave you wanting more than wishing you had your time back.Original Review:I'm a diehard fan of the LiS franchise, so let's note that bias from the beginning.That said, True Colors starts off strong, doing a great job of introducing the town and characters you'll be interacting with. The facial expressions are continuing to improve, and now do a much better job of complementing the voice acting and music to create strong emotional connections. I will update this review with my final thoughts once I've completed the game!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a harder game to for me to recommend mostly because of the £49.99 price tag. If you're a fan of the series and you're looking for more LiS content then pick this up.Compared to other LiS entries however, I think the story is lacking here, it starts and ends strong but it has a big chunk of what feels like filler content in the middle. Deck Nine did a great job with the characters but a mediocre plot ties it all together. I still enjoyed my time with the play-through but less so than LiS1 (which has one of my favourite stories in any video game). Alex's power was subjectively less cool than Max's power as well, it's hard to get excited about the power to read peoples emotions when you've had the power to rewind time already.Being able to customise Alex's outfits each episode was a nice touch and Haven Springs is a beautiful little town to explore but the high price tag did leave me a little bit disappointed that there wasn't more areas and set pieces in the game. You're pretty much in the same areas each episode usually with the decor changed slightly, and although you can walk about Haven Springs and enter different shops as you please only a handful of shops are playable areas with most locked off.The Wavelengths DLC where you get to play as Steph was really great but I may be biased as Steph was one of my favourite characters and I'm glad she was brought over to have a tie-in with the Arcadia Bay story. _childDocuments_.review: I tried to play this game. Having played LiS and LiS 2, i did expect more from it, but let's take things from the beginning. The first thing wrong about the game, is not even the game but the summary posted for it: "Alex Chen hides her 'curse': the psychic power of Empathy, the ability to absorb the emotions of others. When her brother dies in a so-called accident, Alex must embrace her power to find the truth." Whoever wrote this must and should feel ashamed, because it is not a summary to use and sell the game. It is a nice way to ruin one of the important parts of the story, if not the most important one. The result of it? I wasted the entire first episode trying to figure out how and when he dies, instead of paying attention to the actual story which would enable me to connect with my main character! That's a total failure on how to promote a game! Moving forward i'd say the game is well designed, the characters, the animations, Alex looks very pretty and i dig her whole nerdy/geeky style. But that's about it. Even though the characters seem to have their own history, the way it's presented, feels shallow. I wasn't able to connect with ANY character from Haven's community so far. The power of empathy is really cool and unique but from all its uses in the first episode, only one of them was really impressive. That's a let down to be honest. Trying to explore your power, should make the first attempts more intense, more real, more uncontrollable. Only had 1 random crash so far but can't be sure it is was something on my end or from the game's end, so i won't add this into the list of "bad things". Anyway, for me, LiS True Colors does have potential, if it get's reworked. The current game may share the "Life is Strange" title, but it is not the usual Life is Strange experience. I barely finished the first episode, started the second and i don't feel neither the need nor the desire to progress through it. My only regret is that i bought the steam key from an off site at 50% the game's original price, which mean's i can't refund the game. Trust me when i say this, the game's true price for what it presents is 10 euros, maybe 15 at its current state. It is not worth the 30 i paid, much less 60 on the steam platform. _childDocuments_.review: If you played all the other LIS games (LIS, LIS: Before the Storm, LIS 2, and even The Awesome Adventures of Captain Spirit), you will definitely like this game. Great plot twist and awesome song choices. Compared to the previous LIS, this one is definitely abit different.The visuals and colours are breathtaking. Call me cliche, but when I first saw the scenery around the town, I felt relieved with a slight tinge of nostalgia. In the first chapter, I spent a lot of time walking around and just soaking up all the visuals and colour.Mxmtoon is an  choice for the singing voice of Alex. The Indie Pop approach to this game definitely hit my nerd-dar hard. The songs just flowed so well with the visuals to create such mellow and nostalgic game. The collectibles are definitely easier to notice and collect because it has a different indicator. LIS 2 has the most difficult collectibles for me as it is very subtle. It feels a bit more "Open World" as you get to walk around the town and go to the various shops. There are some scenes that allows you to go in and out of various shops without any limit. It also allows you to venture the whole town without making you feel like you're caged within a small setting. For someone who likes playing Open World games, at first, I hesitated about buying this because it's quite straightforward without the need to venture. But after playing, this definitely feels more Open World compared to the other LIS. Characters are so well written in the story. You started as Gabe's sister in Haven, and ended up as your own person - Alex. The interaction in this game is refreshing in the sense that you started not knowing all these townsfolk. But because you can pick up their emotions, listen to their memories, and help them cope with their difficulties and emotions, it provided a lot of platforms to build a "relationship" with them.  Building these relationships is definitely why the plot twist in this game is so much more jaw-dropping.Another part I absolutely love about LIS series is that they have these reflective scenes where the character just sits by the dock or on the bench and they have these reflective thoughts about what is going on and their feelings about it. And these scenes are of course made more MV-ish because of the fantastic songs that were inserted. One of the many reasons I love LIS is because of these scenes. It kinda give a humanity to the character that we are playing. Also, it gives a lot of opportunity to get really breathtaking screenshots. No matter how good I think this game is, there will always be a downside to it. After the plot twist, the story just isn't as strong. I felt it was rushed, and it quite spiraled down very quickly. Because of this, the last chapter felt especially short and unsatisfying. I played an average of 2 to 3 hours each episode, but I was surprised that the total of hours I played was only 13.4 hours. Romance plotline wise is a little disappointing to me. There was 2 options given. Of course to promote and support the LGBT community, there are both a female and male romantic plotlines. But I feel that the story is more inclined for Alex to go with Steph because of the "signals" that she gave while Ryan gave no signal at all until the end. Also, the plot just swallowed up Steph when Alex choses Ryan, which felt imbalanced to me. But overall, i still think this game is  good  because of all the other factors. It will never beat the first ever LIS because i still think that is . But it .

_childDocuments_.review: Life is Strange: True Colors brought everything we loved about the franchise and made it better. The game made me fall back in love with the universe thanks to its beautiful soundtrack, interesting story, and amazing set of characters. Alex is easily the best protagonist in the series. She's just so human, so relatable, and very believable. Steph is also probably the highlight of the show, right next to Alex. She was so well expanded on since Before the Storm and the game makes the lovable geek even more lovable. The rest of the cast and acting/voice acting were night and day compared to the previous entries. Visuals are unmatched in comparison to the older games, the game is truly stunning to look at. The power itself is back in our hands and it actually compliments the theme and story of the game very well. It challenges you to make huge moral decisions throughout and makes you question the consequence in many key plot points. I was waiting for Wavelengths to release so I can post this entire review. The DLC was very fun, at least for me, who was very interested in Steph's story. It's a very relaxing experience where we get to learn how, what, and when things happened in her life, all the way back from the Arcadia Bay days and we get to relive memories with returning characters we all love while also learning the truth of the decisions and consequences during our stay in Oregon. Overall, this game should really reignite the spark we all had since the very first entry. Simply put, if you love Life is Strange, you'll love True Colors.

_childDocuments_.review: Life is Strange is one of my favorite games of all time, it took me on a real emotional rollercoasted and left me emotionally drained yet satisfied at the end. Sadly, none of the other Life Is Strange games that came after it have managed to even come close to affecting me the same way. I was just about to lose my faith in this series, and didn't even bother watching the trailer for True Colors because I just wasn't excited, but now that I've played it...They did it. They really, finally, did it. We have a true successor, a game that is just as good as the original (if not better). A 5-episode long emotional journey that brilliantly tells a wonderful story about great characters. What an absolute joy.Here are some things I think are worth mentioning:+ First and foremost, Alex Chen is such a great character. Well written, extrememly likable, fully three-dimensional character that won me over before I even finished the first hour of gameplay.+ It's not just her though. The entire cast is filled with such great, diverse characters that really make the town of Haven feel alive.+ Voice acting throughout is very good, but the protagonist is especially great (and according to IMDB this is Erika Mori's first and only acting credit, which is really incredible considering she did such a great job I actually bothered to look her up).+ One of the things that was missing in the other Life is Strange sequels/prequels, imo, was a good mystery, so getting to play superpowered-detective again made me very happy.+ Some genuinely difficult choices to make that had me compeltely stumped for a good few minutes.+ Alex's power fits really well into the gameplay, and does a great job of blurring the line between helping people and manipulating them, making you question yourself whenever you use it.+ This is the first LiS game that is  about teens (So much for calling this series Angsty Teen Simulator), which gives it the ability to deal with more adult situations, which it tackles beautifully.+ The graphics are beautiful (easily the best the series has ever looked), and the animation is perfect. Especially noteworthy are the facial expressions that seem extremely realistic and precise, and the fact that they actually animated Alex's hands to finger the chords correctly when she plays guitar.+ Truly great soundtrack, especially the covers played by Alex herself at different points in the game.+ There are lots of random stuff to interact with around Haven and some smaller side-stories happening in the background, so you can take the story as slowly as you want.+ It's a small thing, but I really like how everyone keeps changing their outfits every day. Makes it much more believable.- I've had a few technical issues - one sudden frame rate drop for no apparent reason (nothing special was happening on screen), a few odd visual glitches, and one crash that cost me about 10 minutes of gameplay that I had to redo. It was smooth for the most part, I'm mostly upset about the crash.- While having a mystery was great, I found it a little too predictable.- I've only done one playthrough, so it's hard to know how much your choices matter - but there are certainly a few that felt completely pointless, as they became irrelevant when the circumstances changed shortly after.This game restored my hope in the series. Deck Nine have not only outdone themselves, but they've outdone DONTNOD and managed to make a game that is just as good as, if not better than, the original. I'm gonna have to give this a few more playthroughs before I can truly decide which game I like better, but the fact that it's even in the running is praise enough (and also, I need to take some time before I can play this again). If you're a fan of the series, and even if you've been disappointed in every game but the first, this game is easily worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: I guess the first thing to say about this game is, if you're looking for the classic, self-reflective, 'Life Is Strange Feeling' that you get from the previous Life Is Strange games, I can say for sure that you will find it here. However, it is worth noting that the first Life Is Strange game is pretty much impossible to beat or match and the difference in development styles between DontNod and Deck Nine shows when you compare the two games. Neither is better or worse, they are just different - just don't expect this game to feel exactly like the first.True Colours does a great job in getting you to invest in the characters and care about them, it also does a great job in creating that sense of small town community spirit like in the original game, which is key to the story and gamer experience. Alex is a relatable character, with real-world insecurities triggered by real-world-type experiences and this is how the game succeeds in making the player reflect on their own lives in true Life is Strange fashion.Deck Nine has made a solid story that takes place in what feels like a rather confined space; even though you're in a town, the story spans only a handful of shops and locations, with only a handful of characters playing a key role in Alex's story. This can give a sense that the rest of the town and it's residences only exist in the background at times and risks destroying the players immersion in the world - but you care about Alex and her journey enough not to let this get in the way.All in all, I have nothing really bad to say. It's a compact story, in a compact location, and as such, by the time you finish, you get a sense of satisfaction relative to the size and scope of the game. Don't expect your mind to be blown, but you will have been on a nice little journey with a nice little pool of characters that allow you to reflect on who you are as a person and how you treat others. So: new Life Is Strange game = mission accomplished by Deck Nine! The soundtrack is lovely as always btw. It's also worth mentioning that there is a 'Woke' element to this game: whether you welcome the woke factor or not is up to you, but for those of you who might dislike games that aim to be socially right on, don't let it put you off because it isn't at the forefront of the story. Deck Nine have wisely made it so you can be as woke as you want (or not) with your in game choices, and personally I think that is the best way to do things. These games are all about choice after all! Highly recommend. Enjoy!Addendum: I'm half way through the Wavelengths DLC which is very different to the base game. Wavelengths follows Steph, who is a lesbian, and so needless to say this part of the game handles many issues related to being a lesbian in today's world, as well as the current 'Pride' movement. If you're not into that stuff or don't care about it or whatever, I'd say the DLC won't be for you. Peace.

_childDocuments_.review: Godd@mn, Deck Nine knocked this out of the PARK. My favorite installment is still probably BTS, but True Colors comes very, very close. The story is well-written and well-executed. Alex is exactly the right blend of nerdy and snarky and genuine, and the rest of the cast is strong as well, showcasing the wide array of personalities that might enjoy calling a small town home. Every voice actor brought their A-game, making me CARE about these nonexistent people during a terrible time in their nonexistent lives. The fear and anger and sorrow and hints of PTSD left me afraid and furious and heartbroken right along with them, and the culmination of the mystery was incredibly emotional. Haven contains a surprising amount of lore if you take the time to look, and every character's backstory is fleshed out through dialogue and items and auras. As of the time of writing, I'm nearly done my second playthrough, but could have finished the first in much less time had I not trawled through town inspecting EVERYTHING, but I'm a sucker for that kind of thing.I like that I didn't have to wait between episodes. I like that this new town had ties to the original game via Steph (and I LOVE that she's getting her own DLC because Steph is a GREAT character!). I like that you can choose your romance options, and that your early decisions don't screw over your attempt to woo your lover of choice. I like that Deck Nine included more than a few token POC. I like just... so much.For longtime fans of the series, I highly, HIGHLY recommend, even if you wait for a sale. I grabbed it brand new because I want to maximize my support, but f you haven't dipped your toes into the Life Is Strange universe yet, maybe wait for the price to drop. And go pick up the original and Before the Storm in the meantime.Edit: Wavelengths made me cry. After being able to explore Haven all through the main game it was a little weird to be stuck in the record store for Steph's entire story, but that was still fitting, in a weird sort of way. DEFINITELY worth the extra cash!

_childDocuments_.review: Life is Strange: True Colors is undoubtedly the best audiovisual work throughout the whole franchise. The graphics are stunning and the sound effects and mixing are way above the past Life is Strange games. The characters in this game are pretty much well acted and there is not a big gap regarding development between the main and support characters. Musically, this game also sets up high standards.How the new superpower is used to tell the story is pretty much interesting. I'm usually skeptic about superpowers, but thankfully they always get them on the right spot.My favorite chapter is the third one, which contains the experience of playing a LARP with costumed residents of a decorated town. The game try to give you the impression that the character who worked on the decoration is a hard and good worker, but the dedication is 100% of the deserving art team. It's beautiful.The series is well known by its player choice driven gameplay and story, but I think that this game lacks of depth on that matter. On the first game, what you were choosing really mattered, because you could fail, go back and time and try something else again. On Life is Strange: Before the Storm, what you were choosing really mattered, because you could fail to persuade someone and . On Life is Strange 2, what you were choosing really mattered, because it the questions regarded matters of right and wrong and good and bad, and those choices would define which of the vast selection of endings you were going to get. On Life is Strange: True Colors, almost none of that seems to matter. Most of the time, you're not choosing  to do, but rather  to do. And most of the time everything will happen exactly the same way, regardless of what you chose. Because only a few selection of choices really matters, this installment of the series feel rather linear, comparing to the past games.The amount of endings also felt like a regression from the last game. The first game and its prequel both had two endings for each installment; Life is Strange 2 had five endings (or seven, depending of how you count them) and they depend both on your last decision and the accumulate of decisions you've made throughout the whole game. Life is Strange: True Colors only has two endings. And just like the first two releases, the endings pretty much depends only on your last decision to make. They also come in pretty quickly, this being the shortest game of the franchise.If you're looking for a single first Life is Strange game to try, play the first game. Try the remaster, if it's already available for you.If you're a Life is Strange fan looking for another adventure, this is actually a good one, but don't expect it to be any better than what you already experienced. Wait for a sale, though, as this game is overpriced.I also don't recommend watching any teasers or trailers of this game, since it spoils important things way ahead on the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Only finished the first Chapter so far, will likely finish the game tomorrow but wanted to give my first impressions. Firstly I love the setting, I instantly felt at home in a weird kind of way, when I think of Arcadia Bay i'm instantly hit with nostalgia, like it was a real place that I had actually been to, I can't really explain it. I didn't think they could make another location like that again but it appears as though they have, i'm sure i'll be looking back at Haven Springs and get the same feeling I do when I think about Arcadia. The characters are great, it definitely helps being set in a small town again, with a bunch of local characters. Life Is Strange 2 really missed the mark for me, a large part of it was the constant change in characters every episode, i'm really happy the same characters will be consistent throughout the entire story again, and i'm very happy they're all likeable and believable as real people. The story is only just really starting so I can't comment much on it, I'm not sure how I feel about Chapters instead of Episodes. I always liked the ending of each episode being this big moment, and then teasing a little bit of the next, this one sort of just ends suddenly, which I get but I think I would still have preferred an episodic type ending. Overall so far so good, I think this is definitely going to be up there with the original. If I finish the game and decide I don't like it i'll edit this review, otherwise just assume I loved it.EDIT: After finishing the game I am sad to say it wasn't great, not bad either, I do prefer it to LiS 2 but it definitely didn't reach my expectations. The story was okay but I felt it was too slow for a game series like this. I mean in the 3rd episode you spend most of it on a glorified side quest which could be looked at as "character building", but by episode 3 you should be well into the story at that point. It just felt like everything was moving in slow motion regarding the main story until the 2nd half of episode 4, and even then the ending really fell flat. The "climax" to the story just felt really uninspired and anti-climatic, it really left a sour taste in my mouth. Adding on to this i'd like to take a second to talk about the structure of the story, so it felt weirdly slow paced with a lot of filler in-between episodes but here's the thing. I WOULDN'T HAVE EVEN MINDED THAT IF THEY HAD GOOD FILLER! Look, each episode starts out usually a week after the previous, so at the start of each episode you can read your texts and find out that Alex, Steph and Ryan have been hanging out and doing a ton of fun stuff I WOULD HAVE LOVED TO HAVE SEEN but instead they give me an episode of playing a LARP with a kid I don't really care for. If you're going to have episodes that are "connection building" episodes that's fine, and this slow story format would have worked for me if they had focused on the two characters they were pushing the most, Ryan and Steph. They're your love interest options, the ones you're going to want to spend the most time with yet you spend hardly any with them. If they would have cut the LARP crap and instead had all of those moments with Steph and Ryan you read about that entire episode would be considered much better in my mind, and the entire story along with it. Also I think the choices in this game were the weakest in the entire franchise, I read reviews before it came out where the choices were being praised highly as incredibly impactful choices, but that just isn't the case. When I play these games I don't expect my choices to completely alter the story or anything like that but I do expect them to change my relationships with people in meaningful ways. With this game they all pretty much lead to the same outcome, I think the only meaningful choice you have is "which person do you want to date", everything else is pretty pointless. A fitting example here is Kate from the first game, not only do your choices affect her life in *that* moment, but depending on how much you actually listened to her and genuinely cared about her determines if you can save her or not. This game has none of that, none of your relationships come back to bite you in the ass later on whatsoever, not even in the ending. Now i've highlighted the things I disliked because they're pretty big, but it wasn't all bad, here are some of things I liked: Voice acting was incredible.Believable and likeable characters all around (it's just a shame the story didn't hold up to what they were capable of).Amazing visuals and animations, really brought the game to life in a new way.Incredible setting, as mentioned previously I think Haven Springs is up there with Arcadia Bay. StephhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhSo yeah, it wasn't great but I do prefer it to LiS 2, and although I have a few complaints overall I did have a good time playing it in the moment and for that reason alone I am still recommending it. I don't think it lived up to it's potential but it's still a fun time. I can't tell you if it's worth the AAA price or not, that depends completely on your values, only you are capable of making that choice, all I can say is you'll probably get 10-13 hours out of the game having a pretty decent time throughout, but there isn't really any reason to replay.To me, these games are about the journey not the ending, so although after finishing it I have problems with it, while playing it I was genuinely having a good time, so do with this information what you will. Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly designed game, mediocre ending, but worth a play nonetheless**Does not include major spoilers**The creativity and love that went into development of this game is clear; the atmosphere, beauty and 'geeking out' about certain topics are what makes this game. The town is charming and immersive, and walking around town talking to the inhabitants is amazing. The UI as a whole is beautiful, from the color highlighting to the social media pages. There are multiple replayable arcade games within the game, with highscores to beat if that's your thing. At one point the entire game even briefly turns into a 2D Pokemon-Esque RPG seamlessly; even as someone who doesn't enjoy that kind of format, couldn't help but chuckle how well it was integrated within a story-driven game.I'm a huge fan of the original LiS and also played through BtS. Couldn't get into LiS2, mostly since the premise seemed to be caring for the little brother who I thought was annoying and unlovable. Through the first 4 episodes, both from a story and overall experience perspective, this game outclasses the original. Nearly everything is well polished, and much of the cringe lines from the original are gone. Similar to the original LiS, the atmosphere builds up from a lighter, carefree vibe into a progressively darker and gritty later stages. Without spoiling anything, I think episode 5 was a big let down from a writing perspective, and failed to tie the game to a satisfying ending like the first LiS did so beautifully. Some common-sense concepts stopped making sense, comparable to later seasons of Westworld or Game of Thrones. Nonetheless, the overall experience was positive, and if you can afford the fairly steep price tag for a game that will take ~10 hours if you play at my pace, would certainly reccomend.
_childDocuments_.name: Life is Strange: True Colors

_childDocuments_.review: Remember the semi-real super freak-out in part five of the first life is strange? Well, in this game, those sequences are central to the narrative. On the one hand, these scenes are a good time to show off animation and explore characters and their emotions. On the other, since these sequences happen around once an episode, they don't feel that special.  The realty break in the first life is strange is a stand out moment, and I struggle to think of a single part of this game that stands out quite as much. I also have a much looser sense of who these characters are, and what they want. Maybe it's because despite being a similar length, this game has so many more characters to spend time on, while in the first game it was just Max and Chloe. As a result, all the characters feel... impersonal, I suppose is the right word.Especially the two romance options, by the middle of episode three I barely had an idea of who these two were. They were likable sure, but liking a character is different from knowing a character.Ironically the only character who was spared this treatment, and felt both knowable and likable, was the older brother. But... ah... That doesn't really go anywhere. To top it all off, the empathy power feels gimmicy. It acts like a separate use button, and unlike the extremely flexible rewind power, it often leads to extremely linear solutions to puzzles. In total, yeah, I enjoyed it. And no, I don't regret paying full price for it.  But it probably won't stay in my mind the way the first one has.Edit~Upon playing the wavelengths DLC, I have to say, it cleanly solved my only objection with the story, and I love Steph. MY issues with the gameplay still stand though. It has become one of my comfort games, and I HEARTILY recommend it!!

_childDocuments_.review: To my great surprise this season of Life is Strange is by far my favorite of them all!While the somewhat cringy memeworthy lines are still there (and im a sucker for it) the dialogue and writing is vastly improved imo, with the right blend of seriousness and comedy. I did feel like Season 2 was way too much misery porn sometimes, and Season 1 while pretty good could take you out of the immersion with some bonkers dialogue and plot points.Being able to see other people's emotions didn't sound too exciting, compared to Max's time manipulation or Daniels "Eleven" shtick. But thankfully it got pretty interesting towards the last chapters, with the choices that were presented to you.The graphics and facial animation were top notch and with RT on some scenes looked downright gorgeous. Had some minor stuttering and two crashes, but thats mostly due to Directx12 being a bit wonky as other people reported.The only issue is that i felt most of the choices didn't have much of a consequence as i expected. But thats something that most if not all games of this genre have.Very recommended if you are a fan of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Years later, I finally finished LiS True Colors, my second favorite after the original game. It was a bit of a journey, had its ups and downs. Started it a year or two after it came out, but life got busy, so I put it on hold. Picked it up again before my dad passed, but I couldn't bring myself to finish it until recently. Now, after his passing, completing it hits differently. It's not just about loss, but about all the stuff the game touches on that hits close to home. It's about accepting your feelings, forgiving if you can, being there for others, finding where you fit in, and just moving forward, you know? Despite the tears I was trying very hard to suppress, I think it's a really beautiful game. Those LiS writers sure know how to get you thinking and pull at your heartstrings. Well done.

_childDocuments_.review: if they can keep going in this direction, they might salvage the franchise. And if this had been the immediate sequel to LiS, I think I would have like this more. But it's just so... slow and bland. The poor pacing on this one just absolutely kills it. It's one of the only games I've ever played all the way through just because I was absolutely certain it was going to get better in the next 5 minutes, and then it never did. It's a thriller that is always just about to take off and never does, or at the very least it never really finds a consistent pace.I could spend several pages breaking down what does and doesn't work, and there definitely are moments that work, but the best way I can think to explain this game is with this stupid simile:. If LiS is like lasagna, and BtS is like spaghetti, and LiS2 is like Cup O' Noodles dumped onto an expensive plate with ketchup... TC is is like throwing all of the lasagna ingredients into a stock pot full of water. Sure, it has all the same ingredients as lasagna. But it's not lasagna. It's never going to  lasagna. And it's not good.TLDR: The LiS elements are all here. But they clearly don't understand why they worked there, and why they do/don't work here.Edit: My played time is incorrect. It was about 9 hours to complete.P.S.:Next time you want to have a bi character in your game, maybe say it outright in the dialogue. Allowing people to pretend that a character isn't bi is participating in the same bi erasure that your characters would definitely hate. That, and bi people don't generally appreciate being treated like a secret society that you can only recognize if you know the signs and handshakes.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Life is Strange. But after playing some of Life is Strange 2, let's just say I didn't have a very charitable view of it or any faith in Dontnod's ability to do a good follow up. While Beyond the Storm lacked powers, I felt Deck Nine understood most of what people liked about Life is Strange more than Dontnod did. So I was pleasantly surprised when they were lined up to make the third major entry in the series, and boy has it turned out good.In short, True Colors shows Dontnod up. I've not played a game that has fully captured the magic of the original until I played this game. And it takes it so much further in so many ways.For a game about feelings, I'm so glad they invested in the acting and the animation of people's faces. It is so expressive in a charming, game-ish, animation-ish way. Little glances, body language, a wry smile betrays so much from the characters in this game, and it's specacular. After this, I will be holding other story games to a very, very high standard.The writing is excellent, from moment-to-moment dialogue to the bigger overarching plot, everything is well paced, considered and written.Gameplay is, well, Life is Strange. Deck Nine nailed that. I love Alex's power and my only disappointment is that it wasn't used so much for puzzles, but then I struggle to feel how it would be used for puzzles in the same way that Max's or Daniel's was.About my only major criticism is the performance. The game runs pretty badly, to put it bluntly. I had to disable VRR and enable Vsync because the framerate was so buck wild I was getting pretty unpleasant freesync flicker as the game wildly jumped from 30-odd fps to 90 fps or more in a matter of seconds.But I'm willing to forgive technical issues that will hopefully iron themselves out as patches are released and PCs get faster in the future, because what Deck Nine have done here is take what was looking increasingly like captured lightning in bottle with Life is Strange 1, and reproduce it in a faithful and wholly original way.Step aside Dontnod, this is Deck Nine's series now.

_childDocuments_.review: I think it would be interesting if I listed off the negatives and positives of the game. Overall though;The game is great, it really depends on the person playing if you'd like it or not. Game is too expensive. But overall everything felt right and well made.Negatives- Yes, its too expensive for what its worth; there are alot of improvements the game could have to make it possibly worth  €60  but unfortunately with the other points I have listed its just not.- Gameplay is short (12 hours taking my time checking everything out), it's basically a movie but thats speaks for itself (for it being a story game). Although, I feel like theres   less interactive gameplay compared to other games.- The story progresses at a really slow phase compared to the other games. So if you dont get easily immersed or would play for a good story, you might be let down, just dont expect too much thats what I would recommend.- The storyline feels really short.- The story doesnt have much variety, random line choices dont really matter, just the 'highlighted' choices do..- The super power is underwelming, but it suits the main character. Some people say that empathy isnt a super power, but its kinda more than that. A lot of the time you feel like you're reading someone else's mind to benefit your gameplay.Positives- Compared to the other games, the animations and facial expressions are what made me fall in love with this game- The environment looks very nice- Character writing and designs are, in my opinion, great. I just wish there were more moments with all the characters, down again with the game being too short.- Plot is good- Choices you have to make are subjectively hard.- Voice acting is great, the lip syncing is on point.- The game has it's charms, if you play it, you'll know what I mean.- Steph. That being said, I love the game, I would even say that it's my favorite LiS game to this date. Just because of the main character, I can relate to her and she is very likeable. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely LOVED this game - another exceptional instalment in the Life is Strange game series. [Skip to end for TL;DR][A No-Spoiler Review]I honestly don't get the criticism about this game, I thought it was a wonderful story, and there are several great endings based on the player's choices. Speaking of, the choices in the game feel like they really do make an effect on the story. There are a few weak points in the consistency of some choices as they happen, but the developers, in my opinion, have ensured that these choices make a real emotional difference in the ending, and that the choices really do matter, as opposed to the choices being empty or pointless.As for value, which is a common subject for reviewers to highlight: some users report that the game is too highly priced for what it is and that the game is too short to be considered good value-for-money. Disputing this, I think that the game is well worth the money. I got this game on sale, so I spent approximately £30. The game took me around 15 hours to complete, as I aim for full story completion, and I tend to take my time exploring and utilising the "Moments of Calm" where the character sits and discusses story elements through internal dialogue. This being said, the value of the game is great and is well worth the price for the emotional and moving experience that the game gives you.If you enjoyed the previous Life is Strange games and their stories, you'll love this game too.A truly moving story full of emotion and moral turmoil. Not just a spectacular game, but also an absolutely amazing experience. For sure a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only review I've wrote where I feel comments are actually necessary. No spoilers, no worries.There is SO much to love about this game so I have trouble saying the things I'm going to but because this is part of a series it needs to be said.Things I loved:You can clearly see the amount of talent that was put into this game by the artists, map designers, voice actors & writers. They continued with the formula of the series and clearly know their target audience but with upgrades to the visuals to take it out of a niche genre. They continued with an episodic formula that made it really easy to tell when you should take breaks for playing and continues to leave each chapter in a cliffhanger. So many characters to love. One's you'll hate tend to have really good redemption moments and one you love may fall off the track. Even nameless NPCs are revisited on multiple occasions and gives them some life beyond just a line of text you'd expect from them.  Included awesome polling options for live streamers to interact with their chat with hard decisions. I didn't get to enjoy the full soundtrack but the songs I heard were fantastic. The game features a DMCA free mode where problematic songs are muted for streaming. Couple Arcade mini games made for great little time wasters and one actually helps with world building.Things I absolutely hated:I understand the work on this title seemed to be cranked up to 100 compared to the previous titles, but its hard to justify a 100% price increase compared to previous entries (this dollar value includes the dlc which I'll write a review separate on its info page). For example, an average play time for a chapter in one of the previous entries were between 2.5-4 hours on all chapters (from rushing to actually indulging in everything) but the two final chapters in this game were a total of 3 hours during my play through. Those 3 hours were filled to the brim with A+ story telling but I couldn't find anything in the chapters in order to increase the play time. Talked to everyone, walked into every building it would let me, checked for easter eggs in every corner of every area (I'm sure I still missed a few, but I still took the time to try to find them) and I couldn't get more than about 80-100 minutes. I streamed the entire game on twitch and after playing chapter 4 for about 80 minutes and it being about 1145 at night I was cautious about starting another chapter and being up until early morning trying to complete it. As mentioned before though I could've easily fit the final chapter in because of how short it ended up being also. There was a major feature left out of the game that the previous one utilised that gave it a bit of style and reminded us that this is a season based series (ala walking dead and others). When starting Life is Strange 2 it asks if you played the first game of the series and reads your save data if it finds it and alters the game based on the outcome of said first game or, I believe, the game uses a method of asking how you wanted the game to turn out based on your own optioning (in case you played it another system or whatever). True [Colours] doesn't try to make it part of the series other than the lovable Steph and the recurring unexplained ability of main cast member. The DLC opens it up a little bit and you do make a choice during the start of that game to branch Steph's story between the two games but she is a supporting character and her story does not influence the main characters motives so you feel that your previous choice influences someone else in the story and not yourself. Next, the episodes were all dropped at one time. The previous entries gave us a month or so between an episode and we paid for individual pieces. I personally feel this previous model is a double edged sword. On one side it keeps fans at a common pace and drives discussion between fans of the series between each part. The players also had a choice that if they are not enjoying the game after a chapter or two they don't need to continue to invest in the title. So if it wasn't the right game for you and you were outside the refund time you could just stop investing in it. It's a good option for those to tell the devs when they stopped having interest and could help with the writing process in future titles. Because this was over $100 (Canadian) up front this was an ALL-IN purchase. At 18 hours I got more story in this game than my only other AAA title purchase this year (RE Village) but in taht case I got newgame+ or harder difficulties to argue which one I'll put more time into unless I completely want to rewatch it again with just slightly different outcomes. Would you rewatch the 4hour Zack Snyder cut of Justice League again within a week if you found out they popped in 3 slightly changed 2 minute scenes? Replaying an action game with higher difficulty has more replay value because of the challenge. Its not about story at that point, but just the action. A glorified visual novel only has replay-ability to enjoy the story again with a small percentage change if answers have been altered and that's difficult to justify another 10-12 hours of playtime to see the small changes. But without these replays the value isn't it there argh. l want to be angry at the game because of the cost but this game is a work of art in every aspect a game can be, but it will be no more remember-able than the previous entries to the series. The fact it sold well will tell their marketing team that this format and pricing will be permanent for future titles also.The quick summary.. This game is worth experiencing. If this is your first one in the series, the DLC may not have value to you (unless you absolutely love Steph, but you should invest in LiS1 and Before the Storm first). The main game has a lot to take in and does a fantastic job of world building. Every character is deep and its very easy to get attached and relate to them. Don't rush the game or you may feel like its not worth the money. It's already sold well, but if you haven't experienced it now, get it during the first major sale on this title.Gameplay: B Graphics: B+ Story: A+Music: A+ Difficulty: N/A Value: CMay make small additions to this. This was a rant the minute I finished it and may have left out a detail or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Looks like I'm back to where I belong!I am a huge fan of Life is Strange Season 1 and Before the Storm, these games truly touched a lot of strings in my heart and joined a short list of my most favorite games of all time. Chloe, Max and Rachel - in a short list of my most favorite game characters of all time. But then season 2 came out. The expectations were high, the preview episode "Adventures of Captain Spirit" was great, but the game was a flop for me. The characters seemed artificial and didn't change much along the story, the road movie format destroyed the storytelling, the political problems were so obvious and one sided...And now we got True Colors. Maybe some would prefer a Chloe/Max aka Pricefield aka BAE sequel, and I would be delighted to play a game like this, but this story of Alex Chen and Haven Springs, CO truly lives up to the spirit and atmosphere of the original. Eternal problems, likable living characters, small American town atmosphere - it's all there. Maybe it wasn't as emotional for me as Season 1 or "Farewell" episode of BtS, but I loved every second of this game and didn't see flaws in it. Brilliant job, ladies and gentlemen of Deck Nine (Square Enix, you're Ok), can't wait to play more games from you, inside and outside of Life is Strange universe. And I won't forget to replay this too quite soon!P.S. Extra special thanks for Steph!
