_childDocuments_.review: This game left me stunned. I sat through the credits thinking about my memories with Life is Strange, all the conversations I had and the friends I made through the game. And how much I talk about the game with friends who just sit and listen who're are yet to play these masterpieces. This game heavily reminded me of Life is Strange 1, but with less stakes. And I don't care. I know people may view this game as boring, or dull because Alex Chen doesn't have a power capable of punching a hole through the fabric of time and space - and I don't really understand. This game is, in my opinion, a lovely tribute to how Life is Strange started, and I can't fault it. (The story - I'll get to the price in a minute)...what T-pose glitch?Anyway, as I was saying...True Colours is fan service, but that doesn't necessarily mean it's bad. The LiS franchise thrives from these sorts of stories. "Stories about regular people living normal lives, with a supernatural twist". I can't describe the feeling I felt while watching the credits pass by slowly, as this song started playing:  It brought tears to my eyes. Even bringing back these artists that had a vital role in the music for Life is Strange 1 makes it seem so warm and close to home, which translates well to the town of Haven Springs; it being a small remote town, covered in pretty lakes and beautiful mountains.Also, this game is really funny! Intentionally! And that's always a good sign. There was often a reason to be happy in this game, ignoring the usual Life is Strange trauma and focusing on the scenes that truly make this game what it is.  I hope many people are drawn to this game, I saw a rise of content creators on Twitch get to this game as quick as I did, which made me happy. The price is at fault, 60 quid is a lot...I understand it took 5 years to make, but damn, we're not made of money...I don't even think all of LiS 1 costs that much, and we're getting chapters here compared to the episodic format in the other entries in the franchise. (Not that that makes much of a difference, I just prefer episodes) That's the only main critic I have of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been in love with the Life is Strange games! They have been full of powerful characters with unique and deep stories. The games have a roller-coaster of emotions and ultimate tell some of the most meaning stories with heartfelt messages to the players.I have said many times over that Life is Strange and Life is Strange: Before the Storm are my all time favourite games, simply for what they delivered and the experience I got to have playing them. I personally wasn't a fan of Life is Strange 2 but not because I thought it was terrible but more because for me personally I couldn't gel with the main characters unfortunately which does make me sad truly, as ultimately I think that game looks great and I wish I could've played it through.Now Life is Strange: True Colours is a game I love as much as I love Life is Strange and Life is Strange: Before the Storm! And for people who know me that is an impressive feet for a game to pull off.For me this game had some of the most amazing characters, Alex Chen as the protagonist is this broken but caring young women who is trying to find a meaning to everything that she has been through and everything she is going through. But she isn't the only person that makes this story great. Every character in this game is powerful with their own unique personas and wonderfully thoughtful stories, and I really mean each character: Steph, Ryan, Duckie, Jed, Charlotte, Diane, Eleanor, Riley, Ethan, Pike, Mac and of course Gabe! They all were amazing and each one played a big role in making this entire story feel so heartful, emotional and just absolutely wonderful.The game also didn't push any agendas or tried to push any political angle on the player. The game rested on its characters to create a story that gave the player an amazing and emotional experience. That delivered very meaningful messages throughout that really leaves a lasting impression.The visual art style of the game is reminiscent of past Life is Strange games but just every so slightly modernised to make it feel fresh and unique in the design of Haven Spring. The soundtrack is stellar! Such a well thought out OST that adds so much to the experience and the story as everything unfolds. I absolutely love it! I will be listening to each song over for a long time now.This game did exactly what I wanted Deck Nine to do, which is to take the magic that I got to experience in Life is Strange & Life is Strange: Before the Storm and bring it back to life in Life is Strange: True Colours. The Life is Strange games all have this magic that gives you this emotional and heart pounding and heartful wonderful experience that you never forget!Simply put: I love this game! Very few games give me tears, in fact the following are the only ones: Life is Strange, Life is Strange: Before the Storm, GRIS, The Suicide of Rachel Foster and Paradise Lost. Now I can add Life is Strange: True Colours to that list.I know for some people this might not be what they expected or wanted but for me this is all I wanted from this game and it delivered plus it delivered so much more than what I expected.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so I'm 7 hours in and have finished Chapter 1. I'm rather enjoying this game and don't usually leave detailed reviews but I think this one deserves it. I will continue to update it as I progress through the game. This is my first Life is Strange game. TL;DR: so far I give this game a 9/10EDIT: I've now beat the game and watched a few Twitch streamers beat it as well.Accessibility: Objectively a good thing here and very in your face about it as soon as you launch the game. There are font options that help Dyslexic people, colorblind options (I don't know if I'm learning that I'm colorblind or not, but the tritanopia filter is really, really nice. I prefer it over no filter at all.), and the ability to turn on content warnings in the game and skip segments that would be distressing to you. Which, this is a heavy game and I have not turned that feature on so I don't know exactly how much it allows you to skip by but I'm sure you're gonna be feeling feels anyway. EDIT: I still haven't played with this on and probably won't but having played through it I can imagine where this is used and I think that there could come a point in time where I would want to use it because the themes especially near the end of the game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ heavy as ♥♥♥♥ and I can see how it would be majorly distressing for some players.Choices: I honestly am not sure yet if choices actually matter or if the game is giving the illusion of choice like so many other Choices Matter games, but it definitely feels like they do. Your decisions on what to do/say feel like they have actual weight to them. It feels a lot more impactful than TellTale games ever did. You are making peoples lives better, and in some cases worse, through your words and actions and it *seems* to have a meaningful impact on everything that is going on. There is a segment at the end of the chapter like in TellTale that shows what percentage of players made the same choice as you.EDIT: Your choices do matter in so far as getting people on your side at the end. There are apparently 6 endings, the 4 main ones and the "Good Ending" and "Bad Ending." I'm not sure what the good and bad endings consist of but I'll either youtube it or try to do a perfect/perfectly bad playthrough.Silence: Silence carries a LOT of weight in this game. It's so incredibly heavy and you can feel it weighing down on you as well as the main protagonist. All the conversations are very genuine. The voice acting and script writing for this game is phenomenal. There will be points where you literally just sit in a chair and listen to music for 20 minutes because you want to, because it FEELS right. And I think that's a difficult thing to pull off, but they've done it incredibly well.Edit: I don't have anything else to say about Silence really. This is a crucial part of the game and what I said at 7 hours still counts near the end of the game. Running: This is the only thing currently keeping me from giving the game a 10/10 on my personal review score. The "Running" is really just a fast walk, and it's not much faster than the normal move speed. To the point that I don't even pay attention to whether I'm walking or "running." This is meant to be a slow game with lots of silence and intentionally drawn out moments though, so I'm sure this is intentional. They should have just been more upfront and called the mechanic "fast walking" instead of "running"EDIT: Okay so apparently I had only tried running indoors which is what caused the fast walking mechanic. Still, running outdoors is not really quick either it's more of a paced jog.If you like story driven games, this is a solid buy and the $60 is well worth it in my opinion.EDIT: I still think this game is worth $60, hell probably worth $80 for all the work the developers did on this.

_childDocuments_.review: I may have given this game a thumbs down, but I do actually suggest playing this game if you're a fan of the franchise. The reasoning for my thumbs down, as others have expressed, is mainly out of disappointment.As a LiS fan who very much adored Life is Strange, Life is Strange: Before the Storm, and Life is Strange 2, this game unfortunately does not live up to the standards set by the previous three titles. This game had all the elements to make this a successful addition, and yet I feel there were many missed opportunities.The narrative in Life is Strange: True Colors is fundamentally weaker than all of the previous titles combined. To put this in perspective, Life is Strange: Before the Storm, a prequel which consisted of only three major chapters (in comparison to this game's 5), was more engaging, emotional, and (at least in my opinion), offered longer game-play overall than Life is Strange: True Colors.Alex Chen, a strong character, with on paper, an intriguing gift and backstory that was let down by her own ability. I felt that her peculiarity of empathy was simply not used enough in meaningful, unique or clever ways which effected the narrative. This, I felt, was the single most disappointing and flawed aspect of game. Perhaps the choice of empathy as a power for the protagonist was self-limiting as to what could be used for, or perhaps the writers simply did not get creative enough...whatever it was, the character of Alex Chen was let down by it. The game was also rather short. Alarm bells started ringing in my head when Chapter 1 ended. I turned round to myself and went 'seriously? that's chapter 1?" It just felt far too short in comparison to the other games. I at first thought they may have shortened each chapter, compensating by having more overall, but, that's not the case. After completing the game, there was only five chapters. This I believe also stems from the weak narrative.As others have also made reference to, there was entire segments (even 75% of a chapter) devoted to scenes and shenanigans which had absolutely no bearing on the story. While you could argue it was great to interact with other characters it just felt...pointless. Remove the plot-fillers and the game would probably last two hours at most if you cut through the exploration and unnecessary world interaction. This really does speak wonders for how weak the narrative is.While I admit that towards the end of the game there were definitely scenes which had me engaged and feeling emotional, I felt that the narrative enigmas which drove the game forward (that being the mystery surrounding Gabe's death) was just completely underwhelming. Even the climax, where you finally learn what happened was just...bad. And I hate to say that, especially since I love the franchise. But...there's no other way to describe it. I just wasn't as emotional, nor impressed, as the last three games made me.In short. The payoff at the end just...wasn't that great.Despite my negative review and disappointment, there are aspects of this game which I genuinely adore. First of all, the setting of Haven Spring. The town, the scenery, the community, is beautiful and true to Life is Strange. Alex Chen and the characters and faces which make up this games cast, in my opinion at least, are well written and enjoyable to interact with. They add to making the games setting really feel like a tight knit community. It's a shame the over-arching narrative drags these characters down. Steph and Ryan. The two supporting characters and love interests in the game were also great. It was great to see Steph again and her character development since Before the Storm. She was hands down one of my favourite parts of the game. Though, I felt a little betrayed when no references at all were made to LiS Before the Storm, or Arcadia Bay. I went into the game pretty set that Steph would be my love interest (and she was), but Ryan definitely had me questioning that. Again, great characters overall...but, well, I don't need to repeat myself by now.The graphics were also nice. Visually, it is much stronger than the previous titles at the expense of the art style, but, despite that it still felt visually like a Life is Strange title, and I honestly cannot knock that.If you are like me, and enjoy the franchise of Life is Strange, then at the very least it is worth a play-through, Unfortunately this game just slips in narrative quality. Which is a shame, because every other game in the franchise delivers in this area. I hope Deck Nine genuinely take the negative reviews into account for future LiS projects. I think I speak for many others when I say I love this franchise and do not want to see it fall from grace.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings. I personally really enjoyed this game, but I also feel it could've been so much more. Alex Chen is charming and likable, and you can’t help but want her to succeed. The character writing is great for the most part; they did a good job introducing people who you like and feel connected to in a short time. The setting and graphics are beautiful, the chapter subplots are a lot of fun, and there are plenty of the poignant interpersonal moments that make Life is Strange great.However, the main story is very short, formulaic, and predictable. There are very few meaningful choices, just little sweet nothings here and there that have no impact in subsequent chapters and only seem to serve as collectibles. Most of the relationship building with Steph and Ryan happens off screen and is only seen in phone messages. The “dark secret” you uncover is very implausible the way that it’s written (without giving too much away: how was this kept a secret in such a small town when there were clearly multiple witnesses?) Some relatively simple tweaking would’ve made it a lot more believable. There’s also a tedious dream sequence that was inserted just to fill time - sorry, “build tension”. It’s meaningful content, but it would’ve made more sense if it was broken up among each of the chapters to gradually reveal more about Alex’s background while also highlighting her current grief and inner conflict. Instead you have to sit through this long exposition that’s clearly a “plot speed bump” simply because the writers ran out of steam and were trying to draw out the otherwise woefully short climax. I also wish Alex’s power could’ve been shown evolving a bit more, instead of staying more or less the same.Despite its flaws, this game definitely deserves at least one play through. The heartwarming character interactions and Alex’s charming sarcasm are worth it all by themselves. I would recommend waiting for a sale, though, unless you’re really a fan of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this might even top LiS 1? I can't explain why but I believed this story, it's characters and everything that happened so much more compared to any other LiS title I've played. Whenever I play LiS I have to prepare myself, as for me, the feelings and emotions come on so strong that I need to take long breaks, otherwise it becomes too much. Possibly because of my own mental health difficulties? But this just speaks to the strength of the stories and the amazing work done by the artists, musicians, voice actors and everyone else involved. For some reason I connected with Alex so much more than Max, Sean or Chloe. Possibly because I've felt similar feelings throughout my life and share the same fears about belonging and being alone.I can't sing this games praises enough but that's mostly because of how much it affected me personally. The same may not be true for you. My only criticism is that it was unexpectedly short, which left me feeling like some of the characters felt unexplored, with their true potential not being fulfilled. Easily could have been six or seven chapters long as a lot of the plot progression is just dumped on you at the end of each chapter rather than being evenly spread out over the whole thing. I really hope we see more of Alex, Steph and Ryan in the future, as they are such amazing characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I fell like this game threw emotional stuff at the wall to see what sticks to make you feel something. I did feel somethings. The game had it's moments. It made me happy cry and sad cry.  For a brief part of it. The rest of the game felt boring and tedious. The powers are utilized very poorly except for a few edge cases. Most of the time I figure out someones emotion before I even saw their aura because they were so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ obvious. Even when there are major emotional outbursts you tend to figure out everything before you even investigate any objects then you have to wait for the character to get it too. I loved chapter 3 and I hated chapter 5. The ending didn't feel satisfying, very few of my choices had weight and those that did had very random outcomes. The game is contantly telling you what is morally right or wrong and it felt very preachy and in one particular case you have the option to do something to someone and it is presented as morally wrong while later on when you are presented with the same option but for someone else and it is presented as morally right. When I talk about the plot of life is strange 1 I have to articulate so much, navigate through so many hoops, because I need to mention different stuff to give the story justice, It would take way too long. And the plot of this game can be summed up in a sentece or two. I feel like I wasted my time. I will give credit where credit is due. Although the plot was bad the characters were not. In fact most of the cast was amazing, and I felt a deep connection with them. I just wish I saw that connection more especially at the end. Another aspect this game nails was the atmosphere. The zen moments were wonderful and the game felt like ASMR at times.I also want to praise Alex's character design. I absolutely loved her face, her hair, her outfits, her headphones and glasses.I had very high expectations for this game and although it was good on some parts and I enjoyed some bits overall it left a funny taste in my mouth.Taking all of what I said together I think this game is a beautiful screensaver/music video or a roleplaying ASMR video. It does not have enough susbtance to be a movie and certainly not a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. What an amazing game. Emotional, gripping - I teared up several times while playing it. And I rarely tear up from games. It really has to be very well done to do so. The characters, Alex, Ryan, Steph (and others) - are all so well done. They all feel unique, interesting and you want to learn and know more about them. I already miss them and I'm sad it's already over. I want to see more of them. The graphics also look very nice and the scenery is stunning - I took so many screenshots. I also quite liked the moments were you could just enjoy the moment and it would change the scenes and play a beautiful tune to it and you could just relax for a moment. It was a rollercoaster ride, but I enjoyed every bit of it! The devs didn't spare any details in creating the world. It looks beautiful, something you'd love to call your own home. The music accompanies the story and situations very well, and they fit incredibly! They help tickle every inch of emotion you have, out of you. From the start of the game to the end, it was interesting and cool to explore little small town of Haven, to meet the characters and help them, and make friends and flirt. I'm glad I got to play and experience it. I hope I will see either more of these characters or similar stories. But I think I connected so much with Alex, Steph and Ryan that I or we NEED to see more of them. I'd really hate it if we'll never see more of Alex, Steph and Haven. I already miss them like friends. Especially Alex, she's just a loveable character. Having finished the game, I'm feeling that kinda emptiness I haven't felt in a looong time after playing a Singleplayer Game. Beautiful experience, worth every dollar! Thank you to the devs!

_childDocuments_.review: As a begin my replay of the Life is Strange franchise, it felt right to look back on the latest installment and, after over two years of reflection, explain why I think this game was such a big disappointment for myself and my friends. Before I begin I just want to say that Life is Strange: True Colors is, by far, the most visually stunning Life is Strange to date, and although I still feel like this game as a whole fails in a big way, there were some story elements I thoroughly enjoyed. I liked Alex as a protagonist, Steph continues to be my favorite love interest in the entire series, the achievements were creative, and I found the LARPing episode to be charming despite its detriment to the overall plot. That being said, Life is Strange: True Colors fails because it refuses to take risks with its story, and since making choices is the heart of the game-play, if you don't have a strong story you don't have a good game. I understand Life is Strange 2 was controversial for a number of reasons (though it is personally my favorite in the franchise). Because of this, I believe the developers of this game attempted to backtrack by incorporating similar story elements from the first game: a small town where you get to know the characters, a murder mystery subplot to solve, a protagonist that has powers, and a plot that doesn't lean towards any stark political views. This would have been fine if it offered a new and engaging story within that framework. However, unlike the original Life is Strange games, the narrative is weak. The plot and pacing feels disjointed and meandering. Your choices never feel like they create any profound impact and the stakes are low, which I feel is most evident in the story's final choice. In Life is Strange and Life is Strange 2, the final choice is an intense climatic moment with dire consequences, whereas in True Colors the final choice is a resolution that doesn't effect the ending in any meaningful way, and I think that says a lot about the story overall. I believe the plot of Life is Strange: True Colors relies heavily on nostalgia while offering very little intrigue, creating a game that ultimately feels hollow. In place of an exciting plot, this game chooses to focus more on the relationships between the characters of this small town and using your empathy powers to decipher their stories. Again, this would have been fine if it worked. However, unlike the previous games, I found it very hard to connect with any of the characters. Most Life is Strange games have a strong secondary character that you spend a lot of time bonding with and that relationship is the emotional core of the story, but we don't get that here. Most of the characters are forgettable and lack depth. I didn't feel betrayed when the murderer was revealed and I cared very little when the characters' loyalties were tested at the end. I missed the sometimes annoying but flawed and multifaceted characters of the previous games. And, because her powers are so dependent on these characters being interesting, Alex's powers are, as a result, disengaging. It's a shame that what I expected to be the backbone of this game wound up being one of it's most disappointing aspects. So, overall, this game was a huge let down for me and the two friends I was playing it with. While trying to play it safe and recreate the success of the first game, they made a boring and forgettable story while sadly missing the parts of what made Life is Strange so compelling in the first place. I don't plan on replaying this one anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure if I am allowed to say this, but I picked it up the steam download code for like $6 on a website that sells KEYS of CDs (do some lite googling). Not worth the full $60 that the vanilla steam store is selling it at (only due to length -- I finished in about 8.5 hours), but if I would have been happy if I spent the ~$35 I have seen this go for on steam sales. Anyway, enough money talk***Maybe some lite spoilers but TBH nothing you won't learn from a trailer or the first 5 minutes of any of the LiS games. Any real spoilers marked out by the spoiler filter.***I have really enjoyed the other entries in the LiS series but I admittedly was not as excited about this one. The premise of "emotion powers" just did not seem as appealing of a story mechanic as telekinesis or time control. I was dead wrong though.I fell in love with Alex and she is my favorite of the main characters so far. The game beautifully uses her emotion powers; you see flashes of anger after certain dialogue choices or feel the sadness of passerby in the beautiful town of Haven Springs. At a high level, it is what you would expect from a LiS title if you have played any before. Extremely cinematic and ambient, heavily story driven and full of dialogue choices that will have lasting consequences. You roam around areas interacting with people and also can discover items or clues throughout the world that can offer new perspectives or dialogue choices. A great cast of characters. A few quicktime-esque button pushes to influence events. But as I said, if you have played any of the LiS titles before, you will feel at home from the start.A few encounters are extremely thought provoking. To the point that they make me examine my own life and how I interact with others. It's the same "wow" feeling I have only felt from some really deep and heavy novels before. I am particularly struck by my encounter with There is also a wonderful gearshift All in all, a wonderful thought provoking adventure. I regret waiting so long to play it. If you think the concept of emotions is lame -- you're wrong. If you don't enjoy the hokey dialogue and sometimes-awkward encounters -- you're wrong. If you don't play this game -- you're wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not Bae vs Bay and honestly it's not even close.LiS is back but the magic is mostly gone. If you don't compare True Colors to the Masterpieces that are Before the Storm and LiS1 the game is perfectly fine. The three main characters are well written, particularly Alex and Steph. Steph and Alex are worthy of the Life is Strange title. Their romance is worthy of Max/Chloe or Rachel/Chloe status. The character animations put LiS1 to shame and make the LiS1 remaster all the more disappointing knowing what this team is capable of. Graphics are as phenomenal as ever.Some serious issues though. One is that there's no compelling story hook in the first episode. LiS1 sets the tone right off the bat. True Colors E1 is all character/world building. The story starts to take form in E2 but still just nothing compared to LiS1s setup. Next weakness we all already knew before launch: The power. There's just... not anything to it. The rewind powers were so cool in 1 and I have no idea why the devs refuse to go back to that. We really don't get any significant control over it either. Its more like in LiS2 where there are a few predetermined spots where you can use the power. It's basically just mind reading that you can only use when people are feeling powerful emotion.The town of Haven is also a major weakness. By making it a highly concentrated open world it makes it so a focused story can't be told properly. Each episode has story elements that have to be written so they can be done in whatever order. This makes it so the story feels very choppy. LiS one didn't give you any control over where you were going next. This made the story progression very fluid. Also there's just nowhere interesting to go in Haven. You've seen everything all in the first episode.The side characters are mediocre and under developed. They're SUPER well acted and animated but because of disjointed story telling due to the open world and lack of screen time I just didn't care about anybody beyond the main characters (who are freaking awesome). This IS a fine game, but only fine. And next to the absolute masterpiece that is the first game it falls completely short.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game.  It is not a great game.  LiS2 is an attempt to trade on the fandom's love of the original using a similar plot of a superpowered young person being thrown into an emotional rollercoaster.There are a lot of things I hate about the game.  I hated the fact you can't save so you can easier replay the storyline using different decisions.  I hated that the game doesn't protect the player from accidentally advancing the plot and missing out on decisions (Chapter 4 is the worst in this regard).  I understand their decision to reuse the same game assets in every chapter to save on development costs but when you do this the game needs to make pathing decisions clearer so players needed to go next.  As the game only pushes players to finish the major plot lines it is easy to miss the small ones.I expected LiS2 to be emotionally manipulative.  LiS1 and BtS both do this to a degree but LiS2 takes this notion and turns the dial to 11.  The emotional rollercoaster wouldn't be so bad if the game had better character motivations and so of decisions didn't feel so unbelievable.  The game also using several coincidences well beyond believably with plot holes they don't bother to fill.All in all this feels like a game where the developers weren't given enough money to develop it fully and the cracks show.  Having said that, the base concept of LiS is still good and worth play if you get the game on sale.  Where LiS is an 9/10, I'd put this game at around a 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: When people think about the Life is Strange series, what comes to mind is often the writing, the characters, the emotions the games can make players feel.Life is Strange True Colors is no stranger to any of that. The story of this game is way up with the first game, meaning, it's really good. The cast is minimalistic, there aren't a lot of people but they all have these defining parts that makes them believable. The voice actors and their mocap performances are STELLAR, especially in the heartfelt moments where emotion very much needs to be papable. The game's story is told just as much through events than the character's facial expressions and eyes. All of that becomes even more apparent when taking into account that Empathy is the big theme here. Whether it's helping people realize their feelings, or keeping secrets for the sake of not embarassing someone. That, and it's the main protagonist' superpower.And talking about the protagonist, I feel like Alex Chen was made in such a convincing way that I was very close to feeling like I'm watching an actual human. Her facial expressions, her reactions, her ways to convey and process emotions, in relation to her past, is all so coherent and realistic, it's hard to believe it's a character in a game.Also, the little town in which this game takes place feels very cozy, there's a warmth to it that instantly puts the player in a state of comfort. I'd compare it to Pelican Town in Stardew Valley.All of this is empowered by a great indie soundtrack that really hammers down the small town feeling. This game isn't a perfect picture though. The thing I noted that I was not a fan of, is the price. The game is too expensive relative to its length. 60 bucks for about 12 hours of gameplay (if you don't miss anything on your first playthrough) is a bit steep in my opinion. I'd have justified a 40$ price with the graphical leap of the game, but as I said, 60$ is expensive for what it is so I'd recommend picking it up while it's on sale. Overall a great experience, and Deck Nine showed they were trustworthy of being handed control of the LiS franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Im not so sure with everyone else who played this game, but this game was such a nightmare and a roller coaster to play at the same time. Everything just happened to quickly and stuff that happens to Alex Chen (the protagonist) is so relatable. I really enjoyed this game just as much as the other Life Is Strange games. This one sort of had a lot more interaction with the community than with any other of their previous titles. This also had a much larger area to roam around compared to their past titles and their DLC is like a full game, but also somewhat teases their next title. DLC SPOILERThe DLC is almost like a full game. Not to spoil anything, but it does ask if you have played the first one with Max and if you saved or destroyed Arcadia Bay. Then sometime after the first few seasons pass, Steph makes a reference to Arcadia Bay and Amber. I've tried to look into the back story and i dont ever recall a "Steph" in the previous titles other than a connection to Blackwell Academy.. and that well.. Steph somewhat also has a connection with Seattle in some way shape or form... Couple of things that stands out:Why do you have to reach your hand out someone to read their emotions?I think pauses in conversation can be powerful, but its too long sometimes for a normal interaction.I hate Ethan.Yay for Asian representation.Overall, I enjoyed the game, the LARP was kind of a curve ball and the mini games did help break up the pace and tension. It could be something you can play for a second time for a different outcome and if youre the type to hunt for achievements, just like the previous titles, you can easily go back into their chapters and get what youre missing to get 100% in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so visually stunning, I wish I could attach links and pictures. The beauty and design of it is so intricate and detailed; at one point of the story (chapter 2), the game is Semi-Open world and you can look around the town (barriers to stop you going somewhere, are so well made that they don't seem strange or weird). The aesthetic, design and characters (townies) are so well done, that nothing feels out of place! Out of all the games I have played, I have never seen such a pretty one, as this. It is remarkable. (Also, I am not on a modern, day, fast pc, that costs 1000s. This game has given me no issues on displaying these AMAZING graphics, on something that struggles with Dead by Daylight graphics, so it is clearly well done and made). The soundtrack also helps build atmosphere and sway your mood; definite listen to, even away from playing it. It's well chosen and sung, with the songs playing at the exact right times.Story wise, it just gets better. You have a main plot and things you can do at the side (you can ignore them, if you want, but they can help certain interactions or moments throughout the game). It definitely adds time to the storyline and allows you to find things you would have never noticed, otherwise. After checking over the town and certain areas, you'll still find that you missed something (the replayability is always there, as you will want to see what you missed)! I might just be slow, but it has taken me 5 hours to reach chapter 2. I am unsure of how many chapters there are, right now.So far, each character has come to life; they all distinguish themselves in that you know the difference and enjoy interacting with each one, for a different reason. It's strange to say, but you genuinely feel apart of the Haven community (they have done so well with character design for a small-town community, that it actually feels inclusive of you being there). The fact they look so graphically expressive (tears, smiles, frowns), they treat and interact with you like they would in real life and they are given thoughts and feelings, causes them to have so many dimensions. They all have different personalities and you get connected to each one; 'evil' characters you end up sympathising with, as they are more than just 'grrr, I am a bad guy!' The game is amazing and I would recommend buying it, 100%.

_childDocuments_.review: DISAPPOINTEDSPOILER ALERT? I have finished Life is Strange - True Colors, and I must say I am disappointed. I am not going to keep this a long review, but I am going to keep it short, address the major issues, and straight to the point.An average player will get to finish this game around 7-8 hours as it did for me. The gameplay is pretty short compared to Life is Strange 2; even that is priced around $50-$60 and lasts for about 14-15 hours long. I did not went along with the full side quests, but I know which ones are. I could have squeezed in probably another 1-2 hours of the game, but it still didn't give me overall a good impression. The fact that this game is priced around CDN $79.99 is not worth it, and I already regretted it. I bought this game out of pure faith over at Deck Nine's studio, as they continue on with the Life is Strange Series. This is the same feeling that I had with Life is Strange - Before the Storm. The story was pretty average, as there isn't exactly a super huge threat going on Alex's journey. The first Life is Strange offered an intriguing narrative; knowing what the player is about to expect with the story. It offered shocking twists at the end of some episodes, and the mysteries and interests are what pulled me into the first game. The story is pretty much a simple, typical drama with a supernatural twist in it, and I wish that Deck Nine could have been more innovative with the narrative. The devs could have made a story that focuses more about the power and making it a huge impact to others. I felt the narrative here was weak in my opinion. The characters were pretty memorable, especially my favourite Life is Strange character - Steph. She is amazing in this game, and I was glad to see her being a dorky/nerdy radio host girl. The power plays a huge part in the first Life is Strange; unlike Life is Strange 2, it is the same for Life is Strange - True Colors. Alex can feel and absorb other people's feeling as she has the power of an empath. The mechanics of this power during gameplay is rather intriguing, as I can tinker with how I can use it when making decisions. However; it doesn't fully explore the full potential of having the power of empathy. There were moments when a player can take away emotions from others, and it only happened 2 times in major moments. I hoped I could explore more of this concept when talking to random residents, but I haven't encounter those moments. The consequences of the decisions I made didn't made a huge impact to the story, and is a similar experience to the other Life is Strange series. There's very little variations to the ending of this game, and I feel like this is the weakest of the series in terms of an impact from the ending. It doesn't matter what I do, as the decisions made only impact the people Alex cares about the most. Life is Strange has a binary ending where you choose who you want to save - the life of your best friend or the many residents of Arcadia Bay. It was still tough to choose, and that was an important aspect to how a player chooses the outcome of the ending. Life is Strange 2 had multiple endings, but showed little variances between them. The choices did somewhat matter based of the relationship with Daniel Diaz, and the choice you make at the end of Episode 5. It did offer multiple endings, but it is not perfect. Life is Strange - True Colors has the weakest ending of the series, as the choices you make only influences the ones Alex loves the most and a final choice that just felt dull at the end. Graphics were ok? I felt Life is Strange 2 had a much better animation/art design, as it captured sense of the world that DONTNOD build that is similar to the first Life is Strange. Life is Strange is known for their good choice of soundtrack, and I was surprised that I did not find a single thing that was memorable. The soundtrack choice for this game is a miss for the most part. True Colors has a cartoony design, but this is a matter of personal preference. The environment of Haven Springs was neat though.The facial mocap is much better than the awful lip sync issues present in the first game; although, that could change with the upcoming remaster. This is MY OPINION. As a fan of Life is Strange; I am disappointed.Pros:- Decent graphics- Improved facial expressions- Beautiful set location- Good voice actingCons- Weak story (could have innovated with the story much better)- Weak ending- Unexplored potential with the power- Short game for an $80 game without tax- Unmemorable soundtrack- Hardly noticeable impact with the decisionsIn conclusion, I am just interested with the Remastered Collection when it comes out. I just hate that this is how it turns out, and I wanted this game to surpass the original. It didn't turn out that way, and I am disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Life is Strange 3, a game I was incredibly excited for upon it's announcement. Upon receiving time to actually sit down and play it, I was excited to be taken on a journey, I point to the other previous Life is Strange games as an example. Those two followed a cohesive, interactive, and engaging story. While going through this entry, I found the best aspects to be the graphics and some of the characters.However, I don't believe my care for the characters was placed correctly. I believe the writing on the side-characters, Duckie, Eleanor, and Jed were incredible. However, not enough care was placed into the protagonist's two "sidekicks". To me, Steph felt like bootleg Chloe, and I hate that. I really wanted to like both of Alex's friends, but the story didn't really focus too much on them. They felt like cookie-cutter obligatory protagonist friends. That all being said, more focus should have been placed on Steph and Ryan (I had to google his name to even remember it... that should be self-explanatory within itself.)Chapter One has a great setup. Chapter Five has a great ending. These two chapters are dedicated to the plot. But the game did not earn it's payoff, instead focusing on filler. I personally feel more could have been done in chapters two through four to correct this. Additionally, chapter four is egregiously short, the shortest chapter in the Life is Strange series to date. Life is Strange has the "story rich" tag on Steam for a reason and this game fails to deliver. Do yourself a favor and watch a play-through on Youtube instead.

_childDocuments_.review: As a LiS franchise enjoyer, I gotta say I am little disappointed with this one.Character development, voice acting and unexpected plot twists are great as well as other LiS games. Howewer the disappointing point is the story feeling short and rushed, I know "Sh*t just went from 0 to 100 real quick" moments have always been a part of LiS stories (which can be easily seen in the prologue of LiS 2) but in True Colors it these moments feel too frequent..Talking about characters, our new protagonist is Alex Chan who is reuinting with his brother after being apart for 8 years, visiting where he lives and constructed his new life and we have a comeback character Steph Gingrich featured in LiS 1 and Before the Storm and events take place much time after the events of LiS 1 Overall even it is not better than previous LiS titles in terms of story depth and lenght, I'd still recommend to everyone who enjoyed LiS games so far. But obviously not with that price, no f*cking way, I was lucky to get this as gift.WAVELENGHTS DLCThis DLC contains Steph's story and only obtainable by purchasing/upgrading to Deluxe Edition for now. Events take place months before the main game story, tells how Steph started her career in the record store. It is like a Radio DJ Simulator, mostly you do record station chores like reading ads, answering calls and attending the record store plus some optional objectives.

_childDocuments_.review: The storytelling and character development are top-notch. Most of the negative reviews fall flat once you actually play it. The overall narrative is  well-crafted. You've got those classic Life is Strange mind-bending twists, and Chapter 5's abstract storytelling is brilliantThe game builds on Life Is Strange's supernatural foundation, scratching that itch for superhuman abilities while making you really think about the consequences of your choices. Unlike Max's rewind power in the first game, the empathy ability doesn't let you try out different options and see what will happen. Instead, it's more "Okay, this is what they're showing on the outside, but this what's happening in the inside" This pivots the key of decision-making into details observation and you instinct,The two-sided reactions to True Color (and maybe the whole Life is Strange series) come down to how they handle endings and player choice. If you're on the fence about buying it, I'd say it absolutely lives up to the Life is Strange legacy. You've got a gripping story, cool powers, a script that makes you delve deeply, and characters that's feels like one of your friend. If narrative games are your jam, definitely give it a shot!And if it's not your type of game? No worries. Gaming's subjective – one player's masterpiece is another's snoozefest. What clicks for you in a game is totally personal

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start with a controversial line:  I absolutely loved the game, but I don't feel it was worth $60.  If you can, wait for it to go on sale.Pros:-The story was much better than the first two games with less plot holes-There are various endings and three romance routes (two characters + solo)-The protagonist (Alex) is relatable, and those who have "broken" family situations will probably empathize with her-Unlike the second game, players are back in the "driver's seat" in regards to the powers Alex has-Very character driven-The visuals are amazing-Excellent soundtrack-LARP in chapter 3; 'nuff saidCons:-Again, not enough content to justify a $60 pricetag; I completed the game in about 10 hours (and that was with a lot of exploring) and managed to get one of the top two endings on my first playthrough (with no walkthrough)-There were times when the options provided in dialogue felt either too similar, or it was difficult to tell what the intent was due to the wording-It's very easy to miss a couple optional events for some of the characters (and those events are needed to get the best ending)-Players might experience one of the couple visual glitches (I spent the first twenty minutes or so of the game trying to fix an unlisted visual glitch of a black horizontal bar which sometimes went across the screen, plus choppy transitions.  I had to turn down the settings, even though my computer is no slouch and can play games like FFXIV just fine, and make a few other adjustments...plus restarting the game...until it finally worked properly)-The core game isn't the only thing overpriced about it:The DLC of Steph's story, a 3-chapter backstory, is sitting at around $12; if you want to unlock some additional outfits for Alex (though you still have an in-game choice of four outfits per chances to change clothes), it's another $4 or so.  I know, from experience, how much work goes into a video game; still, I can absolutely see the game being worth closer to $40 (with Steph's story maybe bumping it up to close to $60).  I'd recommend this game, but wait for a sale if you can.

What happened to Alex's dad, how Alex's powers were used, and her life before coming to Haven. The only problem that I have with it is just that the ending is so underwhelming. _childDocuments_.review: Life is Strange: True Colors sucks. It's the first game in the Life is Strange series (including Tell Me Why) that I really didn't enjoy at all. All of the main characters - including the lead - are utterly insufferable hipsters that make me cringe any time they open their mouths. You get stuck in this dead-end town and after an event that closes episode one you remain there to solve the mystery of what happened... But it's not really a mystery because it's clear pretty much from the first episode what happened and who is to blame.The game railroads you into taking part in stupid activities, most egregiously a boss fight that features completely different controls from the rest of the game. I must have spent twenty minutes clicking all over the screen until I found that you can't actually use the mouse in the boss fight and have to use the keyboard. Real amateur hour stuff in a game that tries to emphasize how inclusive and accessible it is. And then cherry on the top of the ♥♥♥♥ sundae, you are forced into a romance that you never asked for. The creeper broke into my house and professed his unrequited love for me, and then when I turned him down, he decided to ignore that and come after me in the closing scene of the game! It's so gross, I can't imagine how the developers thought it would be a good idea to have the last moments you share with Alex make explicit that she is now being stalked by an obsessive nutjob.All in all, this game has really soured me on Deck Nine, whose Before the Storm game was one of my favorites in the series. These guys have the rights to The Expanse too, so I really hope they don't screw it up as badly as they screwed up True Colors. Not recommended. There are much cheaper ways to play Arkanoid again.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler-free review!I've played this series on Xbox since the first LiS, and I gotta say this is easily one of the best ones so far.The characters are written super well, with depth, they are believable and have stories that really hit home, and were sometimes personally relatable. Visually, they've really upped their game, facial animations and character models are fantastic, and the emotion really comes through on them without feeling uncanny valley. The attention to detail to environments are great, as always, the blended style of realism but a sort of comic book look works very well. There's attention to detail in all the little extra things like talking to people, reading your journal, texts, social media, looking at things in the environment, though these have always been strengths of the series, so its not surprising to see them return.Alex, the protagonist, is very likeable, and the game spends plenty of time diving into her mindset, who she is, her strengths and weaknesses. Sometimes you are presented with difficult choices that may have no clear right or wrong answer, and though I've only experienced the outcomes of my own first playthrough so far, the way she made them was always made sense and felt like a solid, believable continuation of how you are choosing to develop her character as the story unfolds.Not really much to say negative about the game, and I won't really count this as a true negative as this was my personal experience. With the decision for all the chapters to be released together this time, it made the pace of the game a lot faster, and the passing of time within the game can be a little disorienting if you're not looking closely at dates and times in text messages and the social media tab. There's some emotional moments that you might need a little longer to process before jumping into the next chapter. Of course, one can pace themselves between chapters, and this is really just how I chose to go about the game. But I guess the good side of it is that I was really enjoying it overall and I just wanted to keep playing. Its certainly possible the game could have some general or fundamental pacing issues, but having all the chapters laid out in front of me, for me, has sort of clouded my feelings on it to really say much more about it.The only other negative would be the romance options. Not so much because the two are bad or boring characters necessarily, but there just wasn't enough time spent with them one on one to really feel like there was a genuine connection building between the characters and Alex. And I'll just leave that at that!Didn't encounter any bugs in my playthrough as far as I can tell or remember, and game performance was solid.If you're a fan of the series this is for sure a worthy installment, and if you're into story driven, choice making adventure type games, there's a lot to like here as well!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying that I liked the previous LiS games and that even in True Colors there are moments that were enjoyable with characters that are generally likeable. Buying True Colors is ultimately not some "catastrophic waste of money" but I also cannot recommend it in good faith. I have NOT played the DLC "Wavelengths" and cannot comment on that.I haven't played the other games in a while so maybe this was a thing in the previous ones as well, however my first issue is the game's style which I feel is at least a bit weaker than the first game, where the objects that adorned the spaces used to be neatly stylized they are often now not-quite-right looking 3D objects. This was especially jarring to me at one of the endings where we see photos of Alex and someone else, which looked as if made in a Sims game, a pretty background juxtaposed with mediocre looking 3D models. The facial animation in this game, especially the mouths, also often times don't look right. This wouldn't be as much of an issue in other games, but in one where emotion and thus, facial expression, matters so much thematically you would expect better. Otherwise it's a pretty game with a decent soundtrack.My biggest complaint comes in the writing, now Life is Strange was never a masterpiece of literature but here I felt annoyed at all the social media lingo, the characterization of people as well as Haven Springs. All of this is not badly acted or directed, I simply think this game was overly tailored towards a certain demographic, I'm sure people outside of that demographic were in fact less annoyed by it than me, someone in that "18-25 left leaning social media user" group who can relate to this lingo, but it gets tired and overbearing fast. Yaas bestie. When I say the characterization is badly executed I mean that everyone is too damn nice, essentially. With the exception of one character even the "villain" of the story is simply a nice guy who turns on you predictably yet randomly at the end. But let me take a step back, the following part may contain spoilers:You play as Alex arriving in Haven Springs, a picturesque mining town in Colorado. Alex had a rough childhood and was considered unstable and essentially treated like a petty criminal (a thing that will only be relevant in flashbacks because everyone in this town is really nice, you included) partially because of her 'superpower', she can read people's emotions and manipulate them to some extent. In that town an accident happened in which a person is killed that you investigate, the local mining company becomes your antagonist, represented by two characters you will meet. Alex' character arc is basically, getting to grips with her emotions and power, finding a place to call home and solving the mystery. But this arc disappoints because the "villains" of the story not compelling *as villains* for the aforementioned reason, the anonymous company is not enough of a villain so Ubi has to throw some otherwise nice guy under the bus for a twist ending. Furthermore Alex apparently starts "feeling like home" after a day and the town immediately accepts her because she saves a child and does some chores. It's not unreasonable for people to like her after that but after only a month of diagetic time it seems like Alex' own emotions (is this "really" home?) should be more of a point of tension. What I do think is satisfyingly dealt with is her power, which she learns to control but isn't treated by the end as some mastered skill but a journey for her to begin. Here I would also like to talk about the game's politics for a moment. The reason, I think why Alex' arc is dealt with such an unsatisfactory way is due to the bad handling of politics. Alex is (at least potentially) an asian queer character, while I don't want to imly that every small town is bigoted the game does seem to imply that it's hard for queer characters to live in such small places while not exploring this at all. Izzie, a trans character who mind you only appears off screen in a memory (great representation on this one guys, you did it) literally says that she doesn't want to be the only trans person in a place like Haven Springs. But again, everyone in this town is actually so incredibly nice that such statements, if left alone, basically don't make sense. My suspicion is that,  trying to market the game to young alienated urbanites that wish they could live a calmer, pastoral life in the country as well as making an attempt not to be unfair to small towns resulted in a totally sanitized setting that doesn't contain the conflict needed to carry this story.Oh and Steph is totally just an attempt to recapture the spark they think they had with Chloe right? Oh whatever who am I kidding I'll buy the DLC anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished Chapter 3 at 7.5 hours in and so far I'm in love. With Steph, but also this game which had me bawling at the end of chapter 1. It's a wonderful return to form for the series after the swing and a miss that was LiS 2 and as a bonus, it features a far more complex and interesting decision tree than LiS 1. Deck Nine definitely knocked it out of the park and I am so glad the game was turned over to them, as they appear to have a much better understanding of what elements made the original Life is Strange so popular.Additionally, the graphics are fantastic and give me hope for the remastered collection featuring LiS 1 and its prequel coming out next year. I'm so excited to actually be able to make use of raytracing on my RTX series GPU.Other pluses: good soundtrack, quality voice acting, accessibility options out the wazoo, for a narrative game this is everything I could ask for.Cons: Denuvo DRM is crap and comes with an often significant performance hit, even on my Ryzen 7 5800x. Squeenix should seriously evaluate what they're actually getting from including that garbage, as it seems like it exists solely to be a hassle for legitimate purchasers like myself. People who pirate the game (and denuvo is notorious for being cracked within a week or two) don't have to put up with that, so why should we?Update: Finished the game at a bit over 11 hours in. I suspect people saying it's an 8 hour game are speedrunning the main story, which means they're missing out on a lot of the flavor and side story. (As well as the best ending.) Still love the game!Update 2: It appears Square Enix has removed that denuvo crap already, that's possibly a record for fastest backpedal.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely would recommend this to those that love the Life is Strange games or anyone that enjoys narrative games but not for the price. I don't regret playing the game only paying $60 for such a short game. First game was my favorite and I bought it after all the episodes were out, so there wasn't the anticipation of waiting on a new episode to release. The length and depth to the first game makes it better than this one imo. I disagree with those that say the characters are meh except the main character. I took my time and interacted with everyone every chance I got so I will say some of them you get more tender moments with and some not. What interaction I had with them I could see how that persona would develop if they had fleshed out more time to make the game longer we could've gotten to see their personality develop more creating a deeper attachment to some of the characters. In the end when you are betrayed I wasn't even that wounded by it because there wasn't any real relationship developing interactions with them for me to feel my character was betrayed. Didn't have as much of a "mind-blown" ending at the first but still kind of surprising. In the first LiS I felt desperate at the end to make it out alive, and all throughout I felt I needed to take care with my decisions because there were real consequences. There are some consequences in True Colors but maybe because the story line is darker in the first you worry about your choices more. You do really get into the story; I laughed so much and even teared up a little at one point. The whole game is beautiful and they REALLY did so well putting emotions into every face. The story is there it just needed more time to fill out some more so things didn't feel so rushed. I do wish there were more moments with the romance options to have that buildup before you're both saying or showing that you like each other. For that "I really like you" moment to feel like you both REALLY do like each other. Wish the game was longer. 27 hours in and about to play my second playthrough.**Side-note: Eleanor's conversation with the random young man at the spring festival had me taken aback. Like where did that come from? lol

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Life is Strange series, I couldn't wait to play this - and I was not disappointed. I absolutely loved it - the visualization of Alex' powers was beautifully creative, the town of Haven and its inhabitants interesting to explore. I especially enjoyed Chapter 3 - I'll let you discover for yourself what your character gets up to there. The story was beautiful, I felt like exploring the world really mattered, and I really appreciated the LGBT+ representation. They also dropped the episode format, which I think was a good improvement.I'd deduct points for two things:  compared to the other games, this one felt a bit more predictable - I guessed all the important plot points and there were no surprises. It was also much shorter than the other entries The latter in itself isn't necessarily a bad thing, however I feel the price asked was too high for the amount of content. Overall, I'd give it 4/5 stars and definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original LiS when it was first released, it was one of my favorite games. Since then, I've played them all. Lis 2, Before the Storm, Captain Spirit, etc. I absolutely loved this game. It takes about 12 hours to beat so, the one downside that comes to mind is if 12 hours of gameplay is worth 60 dollars.  However, that's my only bad remark for the game. To me, this felt like the best spiritual successor to LiS 1. I loved the characters, conversations felt very organic, the town was beautiful. Alex is a fantastic main character and I felt that the two love interests were way more balanced than LiS 1. Without going into spoilers, this game does have similar faults that LiS 1 did, though I feel like people unfairly don't criticize LiS 1 for the same flaws. That being the severe weight of choices, or lack thereof, and the ending. To me, I feel like this games only faults and the same faults the other games have had. If you like LiS 1, you'll like this. If you loved LiS 1, then I think you'll be in the same boat as me and love this as well.

_childDocuments_.review: My only Gripe with True Colours is that alot of the seemingly important choices do not influence the overall outcome of the story.The Story itself was full of emotion, and from multiple playthroughs I noticed how the small dialogue choices throughout change how Alex responds in later situations, from small bouts of confidence to different emotional connections to the games surroundings. Made replayability more fun.The music/soundtrack was amazing, multiple songs made into my personal playlist, enjoy the musical vibes, they SLAP!🎶Overall I think that the experience you have with LoS True Colours revolves around your level of interaction, the game isn’t particularly long, but I still highly recommend giving it a chance.Summer Sale is coming up too! Good time to get it for a more reasonable price. (80 dollars is a little high for the level of time output it gives).

_childDocuments_.review: My overall feelings are that I really enjoyed it and that it was a fantastic game. That doesn't mean I don't have criticisms of it, but overall it was great.So, on the positives, the characters are really standout for me. I suppose the nature of Alex's power requires the characters be fleshed out, but they were great. Eleanor's whole sequence in the flower shop was just heartbreaking. My grandpa had dementia, so that whole sequence hit close to home.Damn it, it's right in the description of the game that they were going to kill Gabe, but they still managed to make you feel attached to him before he died. I like how they handled his death. You could see the different ways that people handled their grief.I liked the LARP. I understand if some people don't like it, and it would have been better as side content, but I enjoyed it, and wow, they really foreshadowed Jed by making him the villain in the LARP.I like that unlike 2, they settled us down in one place so that we could get to know all these characters rather than just having the central characters keep moving.On the not so good things. They really followed the flow of the first game way too closely. Really, did they need to do the "Guy everyone likes is the bad guy" reveal followed by a nightmare sequence? They were both well done, and the nightmare sequence was better incorporated in than it was in LiS1, but really? Those were boxes on a checklist, weren't they? I didn't particularly enjoy 2, but at least it tried to do something new. This was, at the end of the day, pretty formulaic.The game was short. Like, really short. This is a five episode game that is the same length as the three episode Before the Storm. Like, these games aren't the longest things ever, but that's short.The ending was... alright. Just alright. It wasn't amazing or horrible. Just alright. I get it. Your decisions through the game influence who stands with you at the town council, and then the ultimate decision after about whether to stay or leave is a personal one for Alex. It's no Bae or Bay, but it was fine.

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime fan of Life is Strange, I was very excited for a new game, especially since it's made by Deck Nine. Personally, I was not disappointed. The characters and graphics/setting were BEAUTIFULLY done! I loved the power of reading auras/minds. I also really enjoyed the story, but I understand why some people thought it was weak - it's hard to live up to a game people loved so much. I can also agree that the ending wasn't very strong, and there weren't many "big" choices either. But overall, I thought it was a beautiful and emotionally-charged installment in the series! As for the price tag, I do think it's time to stop equating playtime to price tag. There is so much more to a game than how long the story is. In the first chapter alone, I could tell how much went into this game, and I was impressed by it. Also, I clocked in 12 hours total and that was from doing side quests, and I still missed stuff! So, in my opinion, there is plenty to do. Generally, if you like the LIS series and other story-driven, choices matter games, I think you'll love this. And if you're turned off by the price, wait for it to go on sale. I can't speak for everyone, but for me personally, *I* think it was worth every $1. (Also, if we get another LIS game, please do a full-game-at-release again! This was so much better. I do NOT miss waiting months in between episodes)

_childDocuments_.review: Life is Strange: True Colors is a nice addition to the Life is Strange series, and I enjoyed my time with it. I'll say it again, but if you're at all familiar with Life is Strange, you already know if you will enjoy this game or not, given the stigma surrounding the style and subject matters presented here,This game felt far more concise and digestible than the other Life is Strange games, and I really enjoyed that every chapter was available immediately. I really enjoyed the plot and characters through the story, and the special gameplay gimmicks and powers available felt quite a bit easier to utilize this time around, and it made for a more relaxing experience for me. I was never unsure of my choices this time around. This is also the best looking game in the series by far with much better facial animations, and a consistent setting that admittedly looks very nice.I enjoyed the experience that this game gave me, and I definitely recommend it to anyone that enjoys decision-based story games. If you like the other Life is Strange games, you'll most likely enjoy this one too. If you aren't a fan of these games, you might have a better time staying away.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: I loved the game, characters, the world, everything. If you are into games like this, that aren't action packed, I would recommend it. If you're looking to getting into this kind of game, I would recommend. Even if you never played or considered a game like this before. I would not recommend this game to anyone who does not want to take their time and experience this game truly. Too long version: 3-4 years ago I would have never considered a game like this. I didn't care as much about my choices mattering in games. That slowly changed, I would say due to the witcher 3. Then many other games came out similar to how choices mattered in that game. That lead me to games like detroit become human. Heavily focused on player choices. I just kept wanting more games that really focused on my decisions. I watched PewDiePie play the first life is strange, and before the storm. That was before I was more interested in this game. But all that lead me to getting this game and absolutely loving it! The characters in life is strange true colors are amazing. I really enjoyed building a relationship with everyone, moslty ryan and steph, but especially steph. The character models look amazing, and the voice actors did an amazing job. I liked their voices too! I feel that is something not mentioned often is the sound of the characters voices. All fantastic and pleasant to hear. Ryan's voice especially. The story is really good and captivating. It throws some twists and turns at just the right time to keep me on the edge of my seat. I want more, but the game feels like the perfect length. I really just want more of Alex, Steph, and Ryan. They're a great trio, just great. The choices we the player can make do feel really impactful and really keeps you thinking about what you feel is the best option. No option is so clear and cut dry. You are given choices that all make sense, and it's up to you truly to shape your Alex's story. Choose wisely. I had only graphical issues and only in chapter 1. Crazy flickering graphics that no amount of tweaking could fix, and Eleanor's plant watering still happening when hugging Alex. Otherwise, I couldn't recommend this game enough. Buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, but definitely the weakest in the franchise after Before The Storm imo. The game has such a good premise, the mystery is so interesting and the power is incredibly done! However, the whole mystery felt like a mini sub-plot in this game? Everything else in this game took more time than the murder mystery. It felt rushed and I found the ending to be extremely unsatisfying. There wasn't a "big major" choice at the end either that had much impact. The game ended and I just thought "that's it?"I'm still giving it a positive score as there are very golden moments in the game and generally it's good and enjoyable. It just lacks many things the previous games had (the story progress of LiS1 or the choice mechanics of LiS2 for example). The game's script was very witty and probably the most realistic out of all games. The graphics and animations are stunning as well. It had the most potential out of all LiS games, but it really just lacked a good pace and buildup.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is probably extremely biased, so better take it with a grain of salt. After playing through this game I asked myself, if there was any game that I liked more for it's characters and general mood. No there isn't.I fell in love with Alex and got deeply invested in her friendship with some of the people living in the small village.The plot is pretty straight forward and I could smell the "plot twist" from 2 miles away. But honestly, I didn't care.The plot is only a byproduct to the Characters in it. I know some of them might vary in comlexity and yes, the developers could have put more time in developing the relationships with some of those characters even more and tying them into the story. But at the same time, I think that most of the interactions that don't effect the plot are enjoyable because they don't effect it. Imagine a young woman coming into a new town and everything she does serves a greater good or a big plotline. That's just not realistic isn't it?I loved that there where no "collect all 5 bottles" quests and I loved the small (or big) minigames like the Foosball game in the second chapter.And about Alex. I found her believable. I loved the subtle eyemovement, the nervouse blinking and I loved, that she doesn't look... well... perfect... it makes her seem like a normal person that just so happens to be a SuperHero.All in all this is just a great game with great characters.But I also understand if someone has a different taste in charakters and lays more focus on plot and gameplay. Then this game might not be for this person. Atleast not for this price.Nevertheless, I give this game a 10/10.
