_childDocuments_.review: ♦♦♦♦♦ATTENTION SPOILERS ♦♦♦♦♦Life is Strange TC will give you around 12 hours of gameplay if you do the side quest stuff or you want to look at very  inanimate objects in the game  and talk to yourself about them. Otherwise it hits the 9-10 hour mark for only the story so the 60 euro price tag is absolutely ridiculous. It's worth 30 max 40 but let's dive into this a bit more. ..... ..Story/ending:Now the story how do i put this its good but not Lis 1 or BTS good  its is certainely better the the political driven trainwreck that LiS 2 was. However it falls kinda of flat after the first episode when as the "mystery" of foul play is uncovered pretty quick and so is the conclusion to who is behind it all. In chapter 3 we play though  this LARP thing which is fun but in my opinion it goes on for too long and it really isn't that challenging nor does it ad anything significant to the plot except just you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around town we could have focused on the so called mystery and Typhon or the main supporting characters like Steph and Ryan. The game only really picks up at the end of the 4th chapter and then then end of the 5th because the start of the 5th is just one long flashback which again would have been fine if it wasn't that long. What am  getting at is that there really isn't a mystery or a suspense to keep you wondering what happened or what is going on or who can I trust.  Typhon is the bad guy and is supposed to be untouchable as well as resorting to extreme measures to keeping their secrets  but we take the whole company down with a usb stick 2 days of research and a council meeting wtf. Also lets us explore the mine in chapter 5 lets us find the bodies see them uncover it by ourselves or at least piece it together with our powers here it's just served to us on a silver platter by focusing on a amulet we get the whole story.The endings oh god the ending just flat uninspired fade to black bs if you stay in haven, you get a  little more content if you leave  but still fade to black bs.It because the games plot is no enough to deliver an interesting yet satisfying nor sad ending it just isn't enough bad guys lose good guys win we don't even get to see what happens with the rest of the characters like Ethan or Eleanor etc we get to see one moment of empathy with your romance character as the curtain closes but it's not enough imo as everything happens so fast and ends even faster nor do you care once you are done.    CharactersWell most of them do a good job like Eleanor with her struggle, Riley with her fear of the unknown, Ethan is for once not an annoying kid he actually has opinions and feelings that are relevant to what is happening to him, and Charlotte who is just yeah idk what she is a deranged artist maybe, Diana who is this Typhon rep who we find out doesn't want anything to do with typhon and their shady dealings but in the end she is just a another corporate drone so i don't understand why she was depicted as someone who wasn't. But let's focus with the main supporting cast Steph and Ryan.Steph is really well made but maybe it's because she already had some spotlight time in BTS so when we see her we say “o yeah that's steph from before the storm“ with her D&D fascination and her passion for music and then you have Ryan who feels shoehorned in as he disappears in the background of the story from every standpoint may that be his backstory or his active participation in it which isn't much by the end. As a result you end up not caring what he does except maybe if you romanced him but that's exactly the point you don't feel he has that much to offer for the plot as he is a bland character so you kinda avoid him in general.PowerOmfg the power it's so overpowered and underutilized with no repercussions except maybe the taking the anger away from Charlotte that leaves her a shell of former self. It just makes the story so easy to breeze through just click a button gj now you know what everyone feels. For a game that is based on your decisions this power really just bulldozes the whole feeling of thinking before you speak just clicks a button now he is sad, oh she is scared etc let me focus on inanimate objects and get all the answers from there. In Lis 1 you couldn't use your power with the Kate Marsh situation you felt you had to think of what to say next,do some research beforehand in her room to find out things about her to save her life. All this is lost here just like it has been in last couple of Lis games. World/GraphicsI dont what to say open world neither semi open its just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ road and no i dont want the map size of fallout or the witcher. The town is small as it is so why not open it all up you know since this game is 60 bucks or maybe some more maps like the mines or Typhons HQ where you do some detective work idk am not a dev to have to come up with these things but Haven is pretty i guess. The engine is a fresh look for Lis it looks great also seems they are really happy with there teeth technology since its feels like a main showcase point. Nothing else to say about the world nor the graphics in my opinion.MusicMusic has always been a focus point for LIS games there are some good tracks and a lot of meh ones here but it feels that a lot of time went into leasing or buying licences for the music then focusing on delivering a well tailored story. Don't get me wrong I like the effort but it has to be placed in the right place first and then focus on miscellaneous stuff like adding 20 different music tracks. Closing remarks:Its a good game but the asking price is just to much for what you are getting a mediocre short story with some good moments with good to meh characters and a plain unsatisfyiying endings wait for a SALE because 60 euros is just to much for this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Pre-reading note:Before you begin to read my review and either like it and remember it for ages, or bore of it and forget it a moment later, I want to say - yes, it's THAT kind of review. The kind that takes half a hour to write and, like, ten minutes to read.Now, let's begin.I want to start by saying that this, by far, has been the game I have been most comfortable with. Somehow, the developers made me not want to turn away from the screen at times, and not be easily bored or frustrated by it. I honestly enjoyed every moment of my playthough. And, just so you understand, I have been playing the perfectionist (collecting every memory and performing every possible action that is available.)Never before have I played a Life is Strange game that is actually an open map; free-travel game. Some people might dislike that idea and claim that it does not fit the genre, but I tell thee - HELLA YES. I take it that a game of this kind is supposed to be extremely plot-focused and a relatively big map is just improper, but I see it as a great addition. The open map gave me the opportunity to do what I wasn't able to in the previous games, which is to actually have time to enjoy the game.The first, original Life is Strange pressed me against the wall a lot of the times and made me feel stressed because in each chapter, we were either threatened, chased, or would have to be saving our girlfriend, Chloe, from imminent and repeating death. The action and drama induced Life is Strange 2 didn't leave you a moment to breathe, obviously, because the whole game is about running from the police; Meeting new people and having to leave them in the same episode, thus, not getting the chance to connect with them too much, and, of course, having our little brother act like a brat. The closest this series has gotten to providing me that comfort (before the release of True Colors) was in Life is Strange: Before the Storm. Something about Chloe dropping out of Blackwell gave me that thought that I can finally sit down and relax and have one less thing to worry about. Then we had Rachel Amber join our adventure and we started dropping bombs on Arcadia Bay and watching the world burn together.It's just my opinion, but Deck Nine have managed to create two of the BETTER games of the series.DON'T GET ME WRONGI adored the original Life is Strange and it will forever have a place in my mind and heart. The game was so new, full of feelings and breathtaking, and I will always think the same of it - WHAT A MASTERPIECE.BUTThe atmosphere in Before the Storm and True Colors is just better.It's like saying "I know this person is good for me and they are doing their best, but... i like this person better." Sorry, can't help it.Now, more about True Colors - we play as Alex Chen, who is the newest member of the Life is Strange family, but has no relations with the previous characters. She has a power to see what people are feeling, and, at times, FEEL what they feel. Alex is embarrassed about her ability because of the trouble it has caused her in the past, and she find it difficult to be around people because of that. The game, of course, forces you to talk to people and have Alex face her fear.She comes to Have Springs, a small town in Colorado, in search for a new life; a new beginning - a better one with her older  brother Gabe. At first, everything is fantastic and the town is welcoming and has an actual feeling of HOME (what Alex has been seeking for many years). After her brother was taking to jail, she was alone and had to face all of the world's flaws by herself.Alex arrives at Haven, and a day or two later, her brother dies. At his wake, she hears everyone say good things about her brother and she starts to see them as family. Together with Ryan Lucan and Steph Gingrich; yes, THAT STEPH GINGRICH, they start to uncover the truth behind Gabe's death.As they do that, they discover some nasty and ugly truths that no one likes but everyone has to hear, and the further they proceed into the investigation, the worse the truth gets.As we play, we (that is, I) begin to develop some serious trust issues towards some of the characters and it just makes it the more interesting. It is only in the end of the game that we are really betrayed and get stabbed in the back by a person we (that is, again, I) really trusted.The game teaches you that not everything is colorful and full of flowers and butterflies and that some things in life are just gruesome. The game also teaches us that no matter how low you fall, and even if your legs, ribs, hands and many more parts of your body are utterly broken, you can still climb up to the top, Proceeding her brother's death was a dark era, but an opportune one as well. You basically get to choose whether you mourn over Gabe's death and do nothing, or mourn over Gabe's death and act. I chose to take it positively and to get to know that part of Haven better.One thing that caught me, and, I believe many more players in the game was the almost consistent, and repeating presence and appearance of Steph. As some of us know, Steph studied in Blackwell at the time Chloe was and back in Before the Storm, she was a side character that not many people paid attention to. In this game, the developers really integrated Steph and made her an inseparable part of the ongoing adventure. I really like Steph's personality and, generally, her whole character is amazing. We knew Steph as the D&D and nerd queen in Blackwell. Well, now she is the D&D and nerd queen of Haven. She is a great addition to the game and I really love seeing the interactions between her and Alex. Also, there is a romance option with Steph, which I, undoubtedly choose.The most important aspect of the game, which is also the thing that made me love this gamea as much as I do is the open map (as mentioned earlier). The whole exploration of Haven gave me enough time to connect to the town, the people, and each part of the story separately and that is the missing puzzle piece in the previous games.TO CONCLUDEThe game teaches you that being different is absolutely normal and that you can climb out of any hole, even the deepest. Also, the game teaches you that when life gives you lemons, make lemonade (which is an analogy to Alex using her "curse" as she called it to actually make a power out of it and make something useful out of it).I recommend the game to everyone, and give it its own10/10.Welcome to the Life is Strange family, Alex Chen.P.S and perhaps spoilers:I didn't ever hate Mac,and neither do I hate Jed after finishing the game.They are fantastic characters, and they obviously made mistakes, like all of us, but they aren't villians.the end.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a good change for the LiS franchise.  While it has been a good formula for all of the previous entries, that caused them to have underlying similarities, which become obvious if you play the games in a row.  True Colors gives more sympathetic and likeable characters, moral choices that you aren't herded into, and a more relaxing setting.  There were various complaints about the first game that this one has successfully corrected, in terms of sexuality, small town life, and gender (anything more would be a spoiler).  It also does a great job of exploring how empathy can be a double-edged sword, and learning how to harness your differences for the better.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game more than I thought I would. The story was fairly engaging and I really connected with a lot of the characters. The (now standardized) Life is Strange structure of 'young adult with mysterious powers goes on a journey of self-discovery while simultaneously changing the world around them' is as present here as it is in the other games, and it works just as well. While Alex's super-empathy is not as earth-shattering a power as something like controlling time, the story utilizes it well and the game mechanics surrounding it are fairly well done, if a bit simplistic. Alex herself is a fairly good protagonist, defined well as a character while also open to some amount of shaping through the player's choices. A lot of the side characters are fleshed out well also, specifically the two potential romantic choices presented to the player (Steph and Ryan). Being a character brought over from Deck Nine's first Life is Strange game (Before the Storm), Steph gets a bit more focus than the other romanceable character Ryan, but that isn't to say that she hogs the spotlight. Her role in the plot is integrated well, and her characterization is solid. If you have played Before the Storm in the past (and liked it), I'm sure you'll appreciate her continuation here. I would still say that the first Life is Strange game is the best, no other game in the series since has been able to connect me to its plot and characters quite as well, but that is not to say that this game (nor the others in the franchise) are bad. True Colors is a solid narrative experience that (while on sale) is worth a purchase in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a must-play for anyone who is a fan of the original LiS and BtS. However, I caution that perhaps it's best to wait for a sale rather than paying full price for it. When they announced that this would be a full game rather than an episodic release, I'd assumed that meant the story would be longer (this game comprises 5 chapters, the same as the original game), and when they advertised you'd have a town to explore, I imagined being able to explore more than a single street with a couple of buildings. Also assumed that meant the story would be less linear, more open-ended. But the truth is, this game is no different than if they'd simply released all episodes of the past LiS games at once. It's basically just an episodic release, released all at once rather than broken into chunks. Which makes the game much less ambitious than I personally feel they advertised in trailers and pre-release information. Was it because they simply didn't have the budget to make a larger game, as LiS is a niche series? Is it just due to developer Deck Nine's inexperience? This game is indeed larger and more ambitious than their last project, LiS: Before the Storm. But I feel like, when compared to Dontnod's games in the franchise, it doesn't quite live up to what one would expect.But overall, if that doesn't matter to you, then I definitely recommend this game. The graphics are wonderful, the soundtrack is superb, the story made me feel deep emotions in a way only LiS is capable of making me feel, and the game didn't crash once when I played, nor did I notice any glitches. It's a well-polished experience.Oh, and Steph is the best character in the franchise, and it's not even close.

_childDocuments_.review: Welp, another LiS game, now finished in 24.4 hours total playtime.Alex's (the protagonist) story is okay, although the story could probably have been completed in less time if I dedicated more time to play. It felt like one of those games I didn't want to play, because I think it'd be over before I'd like, And it kinda, was. This intuition led me to play it only when I desperately want to play more LiS game, but the ever becoming of the end made it hard to appreciate the game and go with the flow. Plus Alex is someone that is difficult to sense her personality, so that made it difficult to make good choices during dialogue. You don't know what to expect her say or what would happen, given the low amount of blind choices you make, And I think that is kinda the point with Alex as a character.The interactivity is better imo than Tell Me Why, this time around. Lots of things to click on and ponder about to draw you into the world. This time the RPG "game within a game" was executed a hell of a lot better than Tell Me Why. In Tell Me Why the DnD RPG game was too fantastical like "fairies and flowers" Where is in this game the DnD inspiration is more comic related and "Turned Based Battles" which in this case was an excellent side lining to the game. A more accessible plot.I recommend this game as a fair continuation with the Life is Strange Series, and the side story Stephs Wavelengths story is not bad as well, it has a subtle but nice ending too.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this story in one sitting. The Devs of the Life is Strange franchise put their best work into True Colors. The writing was superb, the graphics are gorgeous. _childDocuments_.review: True Colors is the appropriately named 2021 release in the wonderful Life Is Strange series. It is the most visually beautiful of all of the LIS games and the details are exquisite as Alex, the protagonist, negotiates the charming Rocky Mountain town of Haven Springs, Colorado and the residents therein. This time, you have the power to read people's auras and know what they think and feel. But, as always, you must make some difficult decisions and those choices will have consequences. In fact, some of the most agonizing decisions in the Life Is Strange series are here. Choose wisely!In addition, there are not just one, but two 1980s style video cabinet games to distract you when things get a little too difficult and plenty of opportunities to enjoy another brilliant collection of music throughout each chapter. If you enjoyed the previous games in this series, you will absolutely want this one! And there are a number of cute references to all of the earlier games embedded here, making this game an additional Easter egg hunt! Even if you have never tried an LIS game before, this is a great way to start, as the original two games are getting remastered and will be re-released in early 2022. So, spring for the bundle and get them all!

_childDocuments_.review: When I play games like this, I don't tend to try and determine the extent to which my choices matter. Instead I just take the story as it comes to me without playing the "what if" game. From that perspective I found this to be a very enjoyable experience for me -- I think more so than the previous Life is Strange games (which I liked too).However, in retrospect, I do question if the choices would have had any significant impact to how the story unfolds, so if that is important to you, this might not live up to your standards. But take this with a grain of salt because I've not tried exploring this; it's just a gut feeling.

_childDocuments_.review: Fans of Life is Strange will also like this installment. People who already had problems with the previous games will have the same with this one. All in all, the third installment of the series is an entertaining game, but for me it is the weakest game of the series so far. The atmosphere is once again great and the characters are once again likeable. In these areas, the game is in no way inferior to its predecessors. Unfortunately, the same can't be said about its story. Its story is clearly weaker than that of the second game and not nearly as captivating as that of the first. Unfortunately, it also continues a weakness that was already getting more apparent in the second game: the production team obviously lacks social (and perhaps political) diversity. I'm sure I must count myself among the offshoots of this culture, but Life is Strange 3 is a game that was obviously created in a hipster bubble. Some of it is close to persiflage. Haven springs is a remote rural mining town, but its stores and town culture are a hipster's dream. The Chen's spacious loft-like apartment is like a museum of hipster culture. As I said, I don't have anything against hipster culture in principle, but in this setting it just seems ridiculous. It just makes the game lose touch with reality and the only explanation for me is that there are too many people from the same social class and culture at work here.If I write so much about this now, it's because it worries me for the future of this game series. I consider this point to be a real weakness of this series, which will probably continue unless the producers also recognize it as a weakness at some point. All in all, however, I enjoyed the game despite this fact, and I would also buy a fourth installment, although no longer with unclouded anticipation.

"Well" with herself.Con: I bit expensive for 20hrs of gameplay. I usually consider about $1 per hour to be Ideal, some games I pay $15 and play for 500hrs tho... so you be the judge. is $3 an hour worth? then play this, it is a well crafted jem.Review:In a rare return to form the Life is Strange franchise is heading back to it's roots of compelling story without the unbearable political garbage preaching to the player. Overall an on the scale of "No/Yes/Wait" This title lands in between yes and wait. Both good enough for the price if you love these kinds of games and totally worth a $30-$40 price on a sale if you can stomach the wait. With a casual playthrough taking about 20hrs the game is an atmospheric and immersive delve back into the LiS universe.While this story takes place far from Oregon it's DLC respects the choices of the past and will include them in the story. With the "Bae" ending an chloe's survival the "LiS Comics" readers will recognise the "Home Time line" is in effect like in LiS2. But it has little to do with the main story of True Colors. Players who are fresh to the series will lose nothing by playing through this game first, just know that "Steph" is a returning character and we all love her.TL;DRLiS: True Colors is a 8/10 and only damage comes from low play time to cost ratio. on the scale of "No/Yes/Wait" This lands between Yes and Wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for February 2024, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before March 5th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.True colors shining through.Life is Strange can be a bit of a roller coaster and while each title is an independent story, they all revolve around a few things.  They are “choices matter game” where the choices affect the journey more than the destination.  One of the main characters has special powers, in this case, a form of empathy, where our main character can read minds, oh and licensed mostly indie music which, yeah I’m going to try to avoid here. But that’s just what the game is. True Colors though is extremely good at what this series does.  Creating interesting and somehow relatable characters, a good universe, and a drama that will pull the player into the story with minimal effort.  You start to care for every character in the game, and the world is well-built so that it flows naturally.  It’s well-written and has a unique style to its dialog which feels refreshing. At the same time, admittedly True Colors does little to stand out on its own.  It falls back on a romance triangle that feels a bit like a trope at times.   There’s great writing, but the entire fifth chapter feels rushed, and the big twists in this game just don’t feel like they make the impact the team was hoping for. Pick this up if you like narrative stories or if you enjoyed any of Life is Strange.  Yes, I sound like I have issues with this game, but I still enjoyed my time with it and would consider playing through this again.  Just because it wasn’t remarkably different from the franchise, doesn’t make it bad, and the writing works extremely well when it is supposed to. _childDocuments_.review: Life is Strange games keep getting better and better. I was blown away going into this adventure and I always love seeing how much developers have learned from the games they've worked on before. You can really see the love they've put into this game from the:- Characters (backstories, attitudes, much better and less cringey voice acting, FACIAL EXPRESSIONS AND MOVEMENTS!) - Environments (being a 3D environment artist, I have fallen in love with the scenery of the game. Everywhere is full of life with the mass amount of foliage, as well as all of the assets/prop dressing to populate the environments inside and out. Everywhere is so lively and beautiful.)- The main and side stories and all the little details in between.The only two things I was upset with during this whole thing were:1. The fact that the game is a lot shorter than the previous games. Life is Strange 1 and 2 I feel like I was able to spend a lot more time in game, doing little side things and a longer story. After finishing the game to 100% with all collectables, I ended it at 147 hours.  2. That the game came out all at once. LiS 1 (can't remember if 2 did it as well) forced you to wait a little bit before the next episodes were released. This gave you time to build anticipation and also NOT PLAY THE GAME ALL IN ONE GO - and maybe gave the devs more time to expand on each episode more than they were able to here (could explain the shorter game length here.)

_childDocuments_.review: firstly, if there was a way to give a meh-review, i'd give this one a meh. since there is only thumbs up or down votes, this one leans more towards thumbs down. this game had more technical issues (crashing, graphical issues, weird flickering, frame drops) than it definitely should have. it got frustrating especially since the game only has auto saves and they seemed to be far and few between. i had to replay so many things because the game kept crashing. after  of googling i figured the issue was with dx12 so i recommend staying away from that.replaying things wouldn't have been that big of an issue if it wasn't for the game's  sluggish pace. everything seemed to happen so frustratingly slowly and the transitions between scenes seemed to just happen without any thought put in them. many times music didn't fade, it just came to a halt. things just sort of happened and many times i was left sitting here like "".the story itself was just ok. i wouldn't purchase this game full price because it definitely doesn't have enough in it to be worth it. characters were kind of one dimensional and the choices you made didn't seem to make much of an impact. i mean.... the few choices you even got to make since most of the game felt like cinematic after cinematic.i'd give this game a solid 6/10, it's not all bad but it definitely wasn't all good either.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an improvement from the second game by making the choices at least matter at the end. And have you done things from your choices in some of the stories but not all? That being said, it's still mediocre for your standard choice-based game. What at least the first game accomplished is by having a decent introduction to the main protagonist finding out more of this supernatural world where you interact with time travelling and character developments with a long-lost bestie. (executed poorly or not) It still got people curious and wanting more about what happens next and discover the mysteries in the school and find out what happened to the missing gals. In this, this protagonist has some kind of emotional disorder powers to see through, use it, and take emotions away from others. (in some ways creepy and terrifying since they never got in to see what it's like feeling that) The conflict is generic and whatever since the twist is as worse as the first game did by revealing who was the culprit behind it all behind the scenes. The relationships are ok at best. From the gen Z crackhead being over the top and cringy to being quirky which gave me down syndrome and Mr. southern man that'll chop your wood for you just loves talking about smoking trees from your land, and just love nature like it is his Jesus Christ. All three of these breakfast club gangsters are going to take down the evil corporation (that is Mr. capitalism) that lied to them about killing her brother from a mountain because some kid that has batman syndrome got scared of the dark. in conclusion, the story is slow and rushed the backstory too quick at the end, characters either be fine or they just watched a full season of MLP and need their purple pony to cure their negatives. Choices are eh, and the development is too quick and cliche for the protagonist to go through just from losing her bro and nothing from her struggles in life or her powers. it's just sad, moving on, that's it. Also, by the way, the "big battle debate between you and Santa Claus" in the last episode literally gave me aids of how pointless all of this is...

_childDocuments_.review: The LiS series has and always will be amongst my top favourite games, and True Colours is a welcomed addition to the series. The facial animations honestly wowed me the most - there are scenes where you can read their lips and understand what they're saying when they're not even speaking at all. The overall graphics are wonderful and only add to the immersion, and I didn't even have them set to max. As in the others, there are moments of peace where you can just sit and listen to a song as a little 'break' from the story, and in this they fit in so well with the theme of musicality. The steep price may deter one from buying this game (especially if you're in Aus), so maybe wait for sale - a single playthrough + the DLC took me 14hrs (you might play faster). The Wavelengths DLC does kinda just feel like DJ booth simulator, with Steph's backstory sprinkled in (since she is also in Before the Storm), so expect to be doing some chores with the music in the background. I wouldn't mind a DLC featuring Ryan, as he is a completely new character. But overall, it's a lovely game with emotional scenes, and it seems very well put-together. You can miss out on little scenes that just add to the world, so be sure to explore all you can.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is Incredible. Every issue of the original has been fixed, and the things the original did right have been wonderfully magnified. I absolutely adore this game and cannot recommend it enough to anyone who loves point and click adventures, tons of feels, and small town murder mysteries with a dash of adorable romance.

_childDocuments_.review: Although emotion-wise this game didn't hit me as the first one did, Life is Strange: True Colors was more enjoyable to play and with a better story (in my honest opinion), with a good message behind it. Undoubtedly a large step up from Life is Strange 2, for sure.There are many important choices, as well as choices and interactions that change details, whether big or small. The soundtrack has always been good in the whole franchise, and this game was no exception. I loved the power, it's like a "Super Empathy" thing, that can easily affect Alex's relationship with the people around her. As always, like with every Life is Strange, you have two romance options, a guy and a girl, - Ryan and Steph, in this case - but we all know that Steph is the superior choice! The visuals were enhanced without taking out the essence of the Life is Strange style, and the colors felt more vivid compared to the previous game. The LARP part was really fun, with those turn-based RPG-style fights, it made me want to be there participating!I love that Steph made a return on the franchise, it caught me by surprise. Another thing that caught me by surprise was the song "Thank You", by Dido. Nice touch, Deck Nine!Special thanks to my girlfriend who gifted me this game <3

_childDocuments_.review: For context: I loved the first Life is Strange, I enjoyed Before the Storm (it's the weakest IMO, but I think that's the fault of it being a prequel and not really the story's fault),  and Life is Strange 2 is my favorite (I have zero understanding for the negativity that one gets). I enjoyed LiS True Colors. The series once again creates a great cast of characters and great emotional moments. The atmosphere is wonderful. There are so many small things in the game that made me smile. It was absolutely a great game. I am not sure it's a $60 game. Especially because it feels shorter than 1 and 2. I don't think it actually is, but at twice the price of games past I was hoping for a bit of a reason for it. The price is easily the biggest negative of the game, so if you get it on a sale or you don't really care then you're golden. The emotions mechanic of the game works well I think. There's a lot of moments and conversations that feel very real - too real even. My heart was broken several times. So it's also a bit odd for me to say that I felt like the choices were no where near as impactful as installments past. There were only a handful of choices where I had to stop and think about it before clicking. Where it wasn't uncommon to sit and weigh my options for minutes and minutes before. I can't say more without spoilers, or even showing the hand of the ending.... but really I don't think there was as much of a best of bad options that I am used to. Maybe that's a pro for you. If you found the other games more stressful and you want to enjoy the world without everything on your shoulders this might be a better experience. Also, again I don't want to say too much, but a lot of the end hinges on a particular plot point and IMO I don't think the plot point was earned. Overall I think it's a great addition to the Life is Strange family. If you've never played one before you can very easily start with this one. The puzzles and game play were a lot of fun and I love the friends we got to meet. The romance choices were both great for their own reasons but the game is also fine to play without romancing either. There are some things I just don't think landed as well as they could, especially for the price. But one person's meh is another's magic! It's definitely an emotional ride.

_childDocuments_.review: Is the game worth 60 dollars? Based on play time...not exactly. Even looking at everything I could it only took me 15-18 hours - the rest of the playtime is from playing the DLC, which I had to pay for separately. You can replay it to try date different characters or fix mistakes, get different endings, etc, but in that realm the game is also pretty limited so it's kind of a neutral point.Is the game worth 60 dollars based on quality?Well, yes. It is a high quality game. When I played it was free of glitches, and all the graphics are very pleasing and well polished-especially compared to the other games in the Life is Strange series. Specifically with how much richer the colors are. Besides that the characters are very good and the story, I found, was very, VERY good, particularly in what I guess you would define as payoff for the main part of the plot that I'm not revealing here. They improved a lot of the side characters and gave smaller, better defined arcs within the main story. Basically I think it's one of the best put together games in the series and objectively is a very well put together game. So for that reason, if you want to support the developers or are impatient, I don't think it would be regrettable to purchase the game for full price. BUT based on the playtime of the main game being so short, I think it comes out to like 10 hours if you're not very thorough (then again if you're not very thorough you probably don't play games like this a lot) I do advise waiting for a sale. A more reasonable price on how much time you get out of the game is probably 40-45 dollars, I think I got it for 30 on a half off sale. Overall though great game, and having been there since the start I hope for more in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of Life is Strange since the very first game. I played every game from this franchise since then and I can confidently say - none of them ever managed to recapture the magic the very first 2 games had. Life is Strange: True Colors is a prime example of trying too hard. Not just by bringing up an old character (Steph) but by trying to make a character which resembled the very first protagonist in this franchise - Max Caufield. LiS: TC is just...not it. The twist at the end came out of nowhere and was completely unnecessary, the charcaters were very bland and the dialogue was quite clunky. I really tried to give this game a chance and I did. The end almost got me crying, but it still didn't. No scene in this game could come even close to the moment Kate Marsh attempted suicide, or Nathan's voice message as he begged for forgiveness through tears. I am very disappointed.Now, after explaining how I feel about this game, I want to say that I can see the effort. The soundtrack was alright, nothing special though. Her powers were interesting but ended up being unexplored and not as useful as Max's rewind powers were. Her relationships with people were fun to develop and entertaining to see them blossom. The animation was gorgeous and the voice acting was okay.I will always say that the first two games were the best Square Enix could ever make, and with this game they just proved me right. Then again, give this game a chance. But wait for a discount as the full price just doesn't reflect the quality of the game in my opinion.Have a nice day.

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely enjoyed the game, and I would recommend it to people who have played and liked the past LiS games. It's not flawless, but I will try to summarize what I feel are the strengths and weaknesses as fairly as I can. Strengths: I thought the graphics were beautiful, I wanted to step into the town of Haven and walk the streets myself. The same went for the character animations, they felt very lifelike. I thought the characters were mostly well written and likable, especially our protagonist Alex. In some ways I felt I got to know her better than Max of the original LiS though that still remains my favourite game in the franchise.  I cared about Alex and wanted the best for her. Minor characters obviously weren't given as much depths, but I still thought they felt lifelike and not like the caricatures of LiS2 (My least favourite game in the franchise and the only one I truly disliked.) There are two romance options, one male, one female. I've so far only played the male one, but I like the female option as well so suspect that will also be enjoyable. The focus of the story isn't romance though, and you can skip out on it entirely if you so choose. Weaknesses: Mostly I think the game could have done with being a little longer. There was a lot of buildup, and the sense of a deep plot, but once I learned the truth of past events it all felt a little anticlimactic to me and I didn't think the antagonists motivations felt entirely plausible.

You can use your power and alter the story - but here is what I actually am not too happy with.I only played the game twice but it feels like the story doesn't branch like the previous games. It all comes down to the very last scene. It felt like my decisions hardly did anything at all. Mostly it was just for the aesthetics. I wanted to actually make an impact. Make characters fall apart or not - and I guess it's the case for very few characters but the changes aren't too grand. The last chapter stitched the story together but it felt forced to me. Like, what are the odds? It was emotionally breathtaking, done incredibly well with the graphics and the soundtrack. But the story didn't really convince me. The end of chapter 4 was amazing and gave me chills. But chapter 5 was more like a sorry explanation and wrap-up. The backstory was nice and emotional but stitching it together... gives me mixed feelings.I still like the game a lot, I would recommend it to other fans of the series for sure. I just would have expected more. More possibilities and more risk. It was too much of a "safe" playthrough all the time. Can the ending even be bad? Maybe if you really try. _childDocuments_.review: The game feels, in a way, like a return to form from LIS2 to LIS1, with a story way more focused around one location, a clear choice of romance through most of the game, and fewer political commentaries (it remains political at times, but more in a topical, safe manner). For many, this will be welcome. For some (including me), it will seem like a bit more risks could have been taken to try new things.Globally, the story is very compelling, with a set of eminently interesting characters, a beautiful location, and strong drama. Both the overarching narrative and the interpersonal relationships are well developed and frankly believable; you know, disregarding the supernatural stuff. About the latter, the superpower of being able to feel what others feel (like a super-empath), appears original and absolutely well implemented, with even the welcome, occasional uncertainty about whether those powers should be employed at all times or not. I'd say the pacing could need more work. To me, the game truly peaked between chapter 2 and 3, while chapter 1 and 5 seemed otherwise way too slow. Be prepared to be amazed, but also possibly bored at times. The game is definitely a visual treat: that includes the town and environments themselves as much as the numerous special effects. However, I did experience visual glitches, from flickering shadows to textures often loading late. Also, I tried but failed to find any difference between ray tracing being enabled or disabled. Looking online, it seems I wasn't the only one...The choice of music is a positive aspect, with both many licensed and original tracks. As is expected from the series, music takes an important role throughout the story and for sure, this area of development seemed well respected. [Slight spoilers ahead!]When it comes to choices, they seem clear and felt usually sensible to me (). Choices tend not to matter too much in the long run though. It's been the case in the previous games that most events would remain the same regardless of choices, but here, the difference between endings are quite accessory. I don't personally mind, considering the length of the game (I wouldn't want to go through it again to get, say, a "good" ending instead of a "bad" one), but this will leave some disappointed. To be fair, choices do have multiple smaller consequences when it comes to interactions with the town's inhabitants, and in the end, that was totally enough for me.[Very slight spoilers here too...]I tend not to be a big fan of romance in video games, and while I'm happy this game seemed to treat such romance with a minimum of respect (like, I didn't feel I was manipulating anyone to win their interest), I still feel it didn't need to be there. Or if the developers absolutely wanted to include romance, an occasion was totally missed to not force a couple: it absolutely feels like all three characters involved could have easily ended up together, thus rejecting tired tropes.Overall, I very much enjoyed the game. There were frankly breathtaking moments, although the pacing was often (too) slow, story wise, and also in terms of movements. I don't remember the game telling me this, so here: you may usually walk (or jog) faster by pressing the right trigger. In any case, the game's a yes from me.7/10

But as someone who loves lis 1&2, I don't find true colors as emotionally gratifying as the previous two. The plot at times feels like a rehash of some aspects of LIS 1 and the can feel pretty stagnant at times. Episode 3 is by far the best as it truly fills the player with a real feeling of joy and once again the moments of calm that are put in the game are a major highlight of the game. The soundtrack is once again a massive plus in this game as it is in all the games, with both a great licensed soundtrack and original score. Overall It's different in many ways from Life is Strange 1, but in its own special and beautiful ways and tells a great story with well written and voiced actors.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I love the Life Is Strange series, but I won't let my love for it cloud my judgement. I love the game but this is my opinion;I rate the story a solid 7/10, not great, not bad, but good. I loved everything from chapters 1-4 but the end is a bit anticlimactic. I enjoyed the twist but the end feels a little off and a bit bland. It feels rushed, its like they took the time to make the first four chapters good but somehow missed the target at the end. There wasn't even a bit of closure with the characters you met (except maybe for who you romanced). I seriously loved the first four chapters but the ending kinda ruined it for me, the ending was very obvious from the start, the only thing that was good was the twist and the moments with your romance partner but that was it.I rate the graphics/lipsync/animations a solid 10/10. Everything looks great and polished, some glitches but its to be expected and its not really gamebreaking, and there's no such thing as a perfect game. You can really feel the emotions and now I'm much more excited with the remastered games.I rate the music a 9/10. Don't get me wrong, every music in this game is perfect like the other games but the only thing keeping me from rating this a 10/10 is that the music wasn't placed well. _childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS AHEADSo I can definitely see where other people are coming from when they say that this game is no where on par to the first game but here's the thing. This isn't the first game.The story and setting make sense for the backstory we are given for the protagonist, it's not as fun as running around Arcadia Bay, no, but it can still be fun.I went into this game prepared for disappointment, especially since I played it right after playing the remastered of the first game and its prequel, but I was pleasantly surprised. I liked Alex's power, I felt like it was done really well, and I enjoyed her as a character for the most part. (She's a bit hard to deal with at times but given her whole empathy power thing it makes a LOT of sense.)I love the subtle foreshadowing we get in chapter 3 with the LARP session we do, even if I didn't pick up on it the first time. The biggest thing with this game is that it doesn't really focus on Alex, but the entire town. In the first one and its prequel, it was more focused on the MC and whoever they were closest with. Max and Chloe, then Chloe and Rachel, it focuses on whoever is making the biggest impact in that persons life. It doesn't do that here as it focuses on EVERYONE. As Alex, you get to help the entire town with their own problems, such as Eleanor with her dementia (a really heartbreaking scene to play honestly), Mac with his relationship with Riley/what he's dealing with in the aftermath of Gabe's death because he was forced to ignore the call and lie. Riley wanting to leave town but not wanting to leave Eleanor. I think that's part of why a lot of people didn't think that Alex was an interesting character, which I think is fair, but I still really enjoyed this game.The only real thing I disliked about this game was the ending. It felt really weak to be honest, it was kind of annoying to just suddenly have all of Alex's backstory thrown at you in the beginning of the final chapter. It would've made more sense and been better if it was sprinkled in throughout the game instead of just thrown at you all at once. And the final confrontation feels a bit meh IMO. I also wasn't really a fan of Ryan, it isn't that I hate him (though I did on my first playthrough, really enjoyed him more during my second) it's more that he's just kinda.... Boring. He's a golden retriever boyfriend and that's awesome but that's kind of ALL he is, I dunno he just felt a little plain to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Life Is Strange True Colors is a third person narrative adventure containing slice of life content. In this installment we are introduced to a new protagonist, a young woman and musician called Alex Chen, and are reintroduced to Steph Gingrich who played a cameo role in LIS Before the Storm.Alex Chen is a patient at Helping Hands, a counselling and boarding facility in Portland, Oregon.After years of moving around between various foster homes and orphanages she is finally ready to be responsible for her own life. Her older brother, Gabe Chen, has invited her to live with him in the small town of Haven in Colorado, but he is unaware that she harbors a deep secret. Alex has special abilities, and is able to sense and connect with people’s emotions.Arriving in the close-knit community where Gabe has planted roots is daunting for Alex at first;Everyone is welcoming and it is not long before she bonds with the townsfolk; For the first time in her life, she realizes what a home may feel like. Alex is finally happy and content, until a tragic event has a devastating affect on Alex and the community.LIS True Colors is an excellent addition to the franchise and one which I thoroughly enjoyed.There were some noticeable differences in the graphical quality of facial expressions, which enhanced the emotional content of the story. Emotion is central to the mechanics and story of the game, and True Colors pushes the boundaries in this respect. It was a turbulent journey with some amazing highs and incredible lows.Alex Chen’s “superpower” is the ability to sense and even manipulate emotions of the characters around her. This puts you firmly in place to experience more than ever in regard to connecting with the characters. I felt closer to them in this story than I probably have in any other LIS story. I can see there are a lot of similarities between this one and Before the Storm in regards to emotional content but True Colors manages to pack in more drama and excitement too. There are a few scenes that have you on the edge of your seat and it is a wonderful mixture of sentimentality, humor and tension.The characters are very memorable; even the fringe characters have a decent amount of development and fit into the story very well. Our new protagonist, Alex Chan, makes a superb debut, as well as her brother Gabe. They have a brilliant bond and their connection feels very real and believable. We see some masterful story telling with various different ways of presenting their relationship making everything that happens to them feel raw and engaging.I only remember a little about Steph from Before the Storm. She’s turned into a fascinating character and my highlight of the game. It was a pleasure to watch her feisty antics and well worth playing the optional DLC Wavelengths, telling us how she got the job as resident DJ and record store manager, and filling in some background of her past in Seattle. Wavelengths is fun to play, playing the records and reading out the ads, with a lot of nerdy Steph humor to entertain. The music is cool, although I wish they could find a way of not having to disturb the track every time you leave the booth with a lengthy save icon. We get to hear her thoughts of event in Arcadia Bay and have to perform a few tasks as manager of the record store. If you enjoyed Steph’s character in the game, then Wavelengths is an enjoyable and meaningful addition.As usual, visuals are stunning and voice acting is superb. I wasn’t as impressed with the town and setting of Haven. There is only one street and a handful of venues to visit. For example, go inside the record store and it seems cool, but go outside and come back ten minutes later and the exact same songs and announcements are repeated; That felt annoying and ruined immersion a little. There are a few people sitting outside on benches and in the park but they look planted and plastic. I wasn’t even aware I could interact with these characters until after the game had finished. There are other venues outside Haven that we visit, and also travel back in time to see parts of Alex’s upbringing with her father and Gabe, and her time spent in orphanages. The story is always interesting and imaginatively presented.  Gameplay follows the usual third person mechanics we are used to; Branching narratives whilst speaking to characters and those tormenting decisions that need to be made, that affect the story later. All the choices made are displayed after the chapter and you can compare them with others. Alex can sense emotions by the color of their aura. A blue aura detects sadness and anguish, a red aura detects anger and a purple aura detects fear. When Alex wants to delve deeper into their psyche she can concentrate and amplify the feeling. She can then see and hear what they are thinking and why they are feeling that emotion. Sometimes, this plays out in cut scenes and may offer new branching dialogue. If an emotion is particularly strong it can have an affect on Alex and make her feel and act the same. It is also used on a humorous level with peripheral characters who you can read and then talk to, and even solve puzzles once you know their dilemma. The ability can also be used on objects to look into its significance and bring about memories of past events. The objects are extremely easy to miss as there is no way of knowing they are memories unless you activate your ability to see them.The journal records Alex’s thoughts each time she reads somebody and this can often reveal more in-depth knowledge.Throughout the game Alex will get text messages from her friends mostly pertaining to trivial matters about events attended or situations occurring. You cannot input any text. It is purely to read and digest. The social media feeds are the same. They are just extra ways of building lore within the game and getting to know characters better. The visuals were very nice. The environment made you feel like you were in a remote wilderness somewhere in the mountains and was very picturesque. The zen moments were nice to watch.I thought the town could have contained some more shops to visit and more things to do perhaps.I was particularly impressed with the facial expressions and the amount of emotion they portrayed in scenes.The voice acting is once again superb, and the story has a heavy musical influence with both main characters being musicians, and Steph working in the record store.There are some great soundtracks throughout the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap, where to begin.  First and foremost, questions of pricing aside, if you enjoy Life is Strange titles or narration-based games in general, True colors is worth a buy.  A lot of people are saying they beat the game around 9 - 10 hours, and that's feasible, but I spent 17 hours on it from start to finish and loved every moment.  In my opinion, it is WELL worth the price of admission.  From a technical standpoint, the game runs great.  I've seen a few graphical hiccups encountered online, but personally I had zero save one brief frame-skip at the very end of the game.  Movement through Haven is fluid, navigating the various locations and interacting with the cast, even the load times while moving from one scene to the next ( entering establishments, changing zones, ect ) are fast and natural.  Fidelity-wise, the advanced mo-cap and animations are clearly evident, and characters move and emote and speak with a level of realism I'm not used to.  You don't just read or hear these characters, you SEE them move and evolve and express, and it did wonders for the experience as a whole.  Of course the rest of the game is positively gorgeous as well.  A lot of fans lament the lack of the foggy, 'painterly' style of art that the first Life is Strange had, but I think so few realize that was a decision made to cover for the various infidelities of the engine and not so much an expression itself.  Nevertheless True Colors ( TC ) seamlessly blends that sleepy, indie vibe the series is known for with a bright and vibrant Colorado mining town filled with animals, characters and memorable locations, and tons of 'Zen moments' pop up to give Alex and the player a chance to relax, chill, and appreciate both the scenery and some calming music.  In the first game the town of Arcadia Bay was almost a character in itself, and this absense of a central location was very noticable in the second Life is Strange title, so it's refreshing to see Deck Nine acknowledge and return to one of the core strengths the series was built off of: familiarity.  Speaking of characters, I would put any of the main cast of TC against any others in the series.  They are all so perfectly crafted to be Human, flaws and all, and all of them have a back story for Alex to uncover apart from the main story itself, much like reading lore pickups in RPGs.  Duckie and Eleanor, to me, were the two stand-out characters that I loved exploring, mostly due to their interactive 'scenes' that make use of Alex's unique power to really delve into their emotions and help them in ways that only she can.  I won't spoil anything, but Eleanor's in particular was almost too painful to take, and from that point on I made it my goal to speak with her at every opportunity to see how she was getting along.  The personalities in this game are just so beautiful and unique, and every one interesting...that, to me, is what makes this series AND the genre itself so entertaining.  When the credits roll, you actually FEEL like you are leaving friends behind...I can't think of any outcome for a game that can speak any higher of it's efforts.  And the story....from the very beginning, the main protagonist Alex Chen is both extremely likable and also extremely pityable.  Life has not been easy for her, and as the story progresses you unlock more and more about what she had to go through, and very little of it is good.  This serves, I think, to help outline why exactly Haven Springs is such an important and meaningful stop for her.  It's the first actual solid ground she's had, and reconnecting with her older brother helps her figure out that the 'home' she was looking for isn't any specific place.  This is how they make you empathize both with Alex and her plight, and when the story takes a sudden, dark turn you're already invested like an angler hooking that prize catch and you're just along for the ride. Hook, line and sinker.Deck Nine has managed to make their first original entry into the LiS franchise feel true to the form in every way that matters.  Characterization, music, diversity ( without that annoying forcefulness that LiS2 had with it's politics and messages ), all done tactfully and tastefully and always organically to the player themselves.  Each episode, while short, serves mostly to break up the pacing with time skips, allowing the progressing story to play out as your choices dictate, and all of them carry over into the final episode and confrontation even better, I think, than all of the other LiS titles.  Some are paced slowly and more exploration-based while others are packed with heady, dramatic character bulding...and Chapter 3, in particular, might be the actual BEST moment I have had in the Life is Strange franchise, maybe even in story-based games entirely.  I can't remember the last time I had so much bald, effortless FUN playing a game, all with a big goofy smile on my face.  And while I'm not quite ready to place TC above the original LiS, and nobody is going to be dethroning Chloe as my favorite gaming character anytime soon, both the game and Alex herself are IMMENSELY successful in leaving me feeling emotionally invested, drained, and heartbroken when 'The End' shows up on the screen.  I would absolutely recommend this game, with all the fervor of the original and Before the Storm.  I feel this is the natural sequel to the first story with Max, Chloe and Rachel and I already know I'm going to miss Alex, Gabe, Ryan and Steph in my downtime between play sessions.  Because there's no way in hell I'm not playing this again.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be saying some small things about the story but no big spoilers. So far LiS3 isn't really doing it for me. I've seen it all before in better games from Dontnod (mainly Tell me why). In their previous game I also felt Deck Nine were copying Dontnod but since that was a direct prequel that was normal. Rationally I can see a lot of good stuff here. (Voice)acting, believable characters, story and script, audiovisually really good... But there's too many things that bother me that take me out of the story. That make me not believe in this universe. For instance, Gabe gives Alex a large appartement with foosballtable, arcade machine, big terras and a gitar. Is he trying to buy her love? Apparently it's working. How is he able to afford that kind of gift? She doesn't pay for it, we hear that later in the story. Nor can she. Apparently a grown man is much heavier than an adult women and a child as well when they walk over a tree over a ravine. Then there's the superpower. What exactly is it? First she can feel other people's emotions, or see them in colors (hence the title). Not long after suddenly she can read thoughts as well. Not long after that she can even look in the past of other people. Sometimes she can't walk through the "barrier" this superpower creates and somtimes she can.It's never really defined and it's only bounderies are defined by what the developers think the story needs at the time. It's not like she can read everyone either. When walking through the town she can only read a select number of people. I doubt this "super power" is even necessary for the story. So far it seems like a gimmick for gameplay purposes and because that's what previous LiS games did.Some things that bother me I can see as a design choice though. All the conversations feel awkward but that might be intentional, it fits the story. There's nothing in terms of comic release from the heaviness though. In contrast to the whole game is bright and colourful to the point where it can be too much and it's full of people who look beautiful all the time even when grieving. The gameplay loop got to me as well: Talk to person, can't get them to open up, read their mind, find something to put them at ease that makes them talk, rince and repeat. It just became predictable and tiresome real quick. Because of the whole "read minds and feelings" thing the conversations also become less and less meaningful imo. She could have found all that stuff out the old fashioned way, by building a connection (or not find out at all because people don't drop their defenses) making it a true to life experience. The fact that Alex can so easily read people though makes that I can't connect any of these real life issues to actual real life. Because life will never work like this. I fully realise everything I've summed up is completely subjective. But every review is subjective and a review about a game that is all story is bound to be even more. It didn't connect with me personally and that's okay. I hope it does for other people.Lastly, technically. So the game looks and sounds great. Even small things like facial expressions are quite good. I also haven't come across any bugs. It's not well optimised however. I understand they work with different budgets but this game is still just as expensive as let's say Call of Duty. Call of Duty has more detailed graphics and is an action game. I can play that on 4K Ultra settings 60fps. LiS3 is an adventure game with zero action and I have to downgrade it to 1K 1080p for the framerate. It's a beautiful game on any setting but how many people that are into these type of games are going to be able to play this on the highest settings I wonder.

name: INMOST
detailed_description: Something is lurking in the shadows... INMOST, by Lithuania-based indie studio Hidden Layer Games , is an emotional and deeply atmospheric narrative-driven puzzle platformer. Uncover the story of an adventurous young girl, a stoic knight and a man in search of answers. Explore a crumbling, nightmarish landscape, slice through enemies, and spring deadly traps in order to escape the evil that awaits… **INMOST is an intimate story of loss and hope that some may find upsetting. Player discretion is advised.** Features Venture through a hauntingly atmospheric pixel art world 3 main characters, each with their own unique gameplay styles A knight adventures into the depths of a deteriorating castle. A child uncovers the past of an eerie house. A wanderer searches for answers. Lure enemies into lethal traps, solve environmental puzzles and utilise your scythe, hookshot and pickaxe to avoid a gruesome end! Discover a 3-5 hour emotional story, intended to be played in a single-sitting on a dark, stormy night Explore every nook and cranny to find secret passages and collectibles Featuring the vocal talents of Andrew Dennis and Cassandra Lee Morris Playable in 14 languages, including English, French, German, Russian, Spanish, Italian, Arabic, Dutch, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Turkish, Simplified and Traditional Chinese Each pixel is placed with love! Features CORSAIR iCUE RGB dynamic lighting functionality for PC

_childDocuments_.review: INMOST is a video game that I believe deserves a category of its own, namely 'visual poetry'. The whole game just did not feel like a video game, even though it is one. It feels more like a literary work rich with metaphors and other figures of speech in visualized forms. The simple and somewhat crude aspect of pixel graphics feels more like a rhetoric device employed by a skillful poet than a budget-friendly choice of a lazy developer; The heavy and gloomy music sounds like a carefully calculated trap to capture our souls rather than a half-baked attempt to scare our ears; The mysterious and secretive writing reads more like a masterful strategist's deliberate plan to disrupt our mental defense line than a chaotic mess of a wannabe writer. The whole game purposefully creates chaos so that you can appreciate the order within it more later on.I am honestly mind-blown by this game. This is my first time seeing a game studio testing and expanding the limitations of video games as an art form. There are many games out there that have more visually pleasing graphics and amazing stories, but in terms of artistic merit, I think INMOST is one of the few, if not only, games that reach out to the bottom of artistic potential of video games. I strongly recommend this game to those who want to experience video games not as a simple entertainment but as a serious art form.

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous game about very heavy topics!(SPOILERS AHEAD!)I had never before played a game that dealt this masterfully with such heavy subjects such as dysfunctional families, inter-generational trauma and grief. The visuals, albeit always dark and cold, match the tone perfectly, same as the soundtrack. The gameplay feels great, and even if you fail, you are immediately brought back to where you were, so you can focus on the story being told without having to do the same parts over and over.This really is the main event here: the story. The puzzles and the platforming are never too challenging and I never got stuck to the point of frustration, it all just comes naturally and lets you enjoy the narrative. If you are not into story-driven games and are looking for something like Celeste, with lots of platforming and challenges, this isn't the game for you. Inmost is a heart-wrenching story about pain, grief and trauma that uses gameplay to convey its message and manages to turn a bleak narrative into a spark of hope.Honestly, one of the greatest games I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game in one sitting on a rainy Saturday, took a little break to eat so my time in game is probably slightly longer than actual playtime. It’s a short but bittersweet game, and I recommend it. You play as three different characters in three different timelines of the same story, a bit confusing and odd at first but I’ll touch more on that later. It’s much more puzzle-platformer than metroidvania, but it certainly has a “you need this item to open this door, come back later” aspect that scratches that Hollow Knight itch. There is very little combat, only one of the three protagonists has fightable enemies, though what combat there is hits a decent bar. Not great, but it’s mainly there for story reasons so it works just fine. Of the 4ish hours of gameplay, 3 of those hours are played in a typical metroidvania map with puzzle-platforming gameplay. Not platforming like Celeste or even Ori, mainly avoiding enemies and using the environment to progress. The 2nd character is the combat-focused one mentioned above, and the 3rd is the story of a young girl living with her parents. The story doesn’t make a ton of sense while you’re playing; how does a knight, a wandering old man, and a random 6 year old girl all exist in the same narrative? As you progress, and mainly as you rush towards the finish, you begin to understand just how tragic and disheartening this tale is. If anyone out there is struggling with the loss of a loved one or mental illness, this game may hit close to home. It’s beautiful and cathartic, but could be a gut punch to some. This was an enjoyable and relaxing game, that touches on some really difficult themes at times. It’s a far cry from Hollow Knight or Ori and the Blind Forest in terms of gameplay or story, but I don’t think it was trying to emulate those games. Think more like Gris, it’s art using the medium of a video game to tell a beautifully tragic story. For that alone I recommend this to anyone looking to experience a somber but poignant tale in only a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Maudlin, but mostly inoffensive depiction of some standard fare family trauma nonsense. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful game. The art is awesome, the atmosphere is incredible, and the music is just perfect. This isn't a scary game...not in the sense of making you jump out of your seat anyways. It is scary in how candidly it confronts the truly terrifying aspects of living as a human being.Love. Loss. Pain. These are all addressed in an incredibly intimate and raw way. This is a story game more than anything. The puzzles are pretty simple, its not mechanically difficult at all, and theres no leveling up, inventory management, or anything like that. Really, its pretty relaxing. When you die, you just instantly respawn and retry whatever it is you were doing.At first the story is a bit confusing. The game really demands that you think, and piece together the intricately woven metaphors throughout the game into a cohesive mural within your own mind. There was something so surreal about playing this game. I found it hard to put down, so it was a good thing it wasn't super long.If you like pixel art, or story driven games with strong emotional content, this one is for you. Even though the game can feel just a tad clunky at times, it is a beautiful experience that warrants more than one playthrough!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright I played this game and I felt like it was more of a visual novel with some platforming elements and super brain-dead simple puzzle solving.  The story was pretty confusing but checking YouTube for the story explanation helped me grok what was going on.  Except ... I was left super annoyed by the whole experience.  I got the same vibes as Gris, where a whole lot of nothing happened and it took pointless platforming to get the story across.All of the annoying, stupid, slow, pointless parts of the little girl's platform segments didn't coalesce with the other two characters gaming experience.  Her segments focused on the storytelling and, at times, I felt like I was stuck in a JRPG drama.  The designers probably felt like they hit a creative brick wall around the 3-4 hour mark, and after spending so much time pointlessly platforming, the game goes into autopilot.  The most interesting part of the game, when the knight does his final battle, is completely automatic and unplayable.  You're just left watching the end of the game play out for what felt like a half hour.I never really felt like I accomplished anything.  There's probably a secret ending, I dunno.  I'm not motivated to replay the game.If you want to feel really sentimental about a game, play Spiritfarer.If you want to play a really stunning, platforming, story telling game maybe try Hollow Knight.If you're really more into the WTF moments of story telling and puzzle solving, try Inside.

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost is an incredibly beautiful and atmospheric experience, but I think it fails in the narrative department. It makes you spend the last 20 minutes of a rather short game (4-6 hours for a playthrough) taking in a confusing exposition dump. The narrative is already scattered across three different perspectives, (which I actually enjoyed), so it really doesn't help having such a rushed ending where the game throws all of its plot at you. Even then, I found the ending kind of unclear and had to do my own research to figure out what all of this information actually meant. It sucks to see how well the game does everything and have it be bogged down by a story I can't understand.In short, I still recommend the game for its overall feel (and breathtaking art), but not for those expecting an effective or moving story. Just get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is about going through the motions while being fed a story about pain before it's revealed at the end that, surprise surprise, it's actually about something super deep, and what better way to do it than with a very long cutscene? I guess this can move you if it's the first game that touches on similar themes you've ever played, but many games did this much better before (To The Moon) and do so even now (Spiritfarer.)The art is pretty, the music and sound design have their moments, but that's about it.Also, please note that a chunky portion of the game is spent slow walking, and whatever platforming or combat there is, it's very simple and clunky. _childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying that this game is a technically competent cinematic plat former with a dark psychological story. It has plenty of moments which are fun like the chases with monsters but it also makes numerous missteps.1. The multiple characters: The game brags about having multiple playable characters when really this is one main character and 3 side characters who you control for scripted set piece. The little girl and old man are both very slow and can't jump meaning most of their segments are slow tedious walking or slowly moving chairs into place to climb one. The knight is an action combat focused character which sounds cool but his segments get very repetitive very fast as the combat is not very deep and kind of jank. For instance when enemies are close together it can cause issues where you target one you don't want or a sword strike will hit two enemies but only damage one.2. Cinematic immersion: one frequent trope of cinematic platformers is giving the game an unbroken continuity where the player plays everything in real time with minimal influence from cutscenes , world maps, or other gamey level transitions. This genre varies game by game in how strict this is but inmost has a very high cut scene count and the character switching means continuity is frequently broken. It doesnt help that there are quite a few cutscenes which easily could have been gameplay.3. Story: inmost has 3 separate stories which it switches between and which are thematically connected. The big issue here is the ending which is a massive cutscene that explains the entire literal plot and all of symbolism making the other 2 stories seem pointless in comparison. Having the climax of a game be entirely out of a players hand is just a bad move especially as the last bits of gameplay leading up to it don't feel like they should lead to a climax. Really the main gameplay and its story seem more the game just spinning its wheels in the mud to buy enough time before the literal story is arbitrarily revealed. The actual story itself the symbolism of the gameplay I really didn't find that compelling either.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend to anyone who enjoys good story telling. _childDocuments_.review: ***The story deals with traumatic issues around domestic abuse within families. This is focal to the plot, so player discretion is advised.***I personally love short games. I think succinct themes are some of the best ways of getting ideas across.Inmost is a 3.5 hour long game that’s $15, and every negative steam review just loves to bash that price tag.I personally waited for a small deduction to the price to pick it up because of how wary the negative reviews made me, but starting the game and seeing how painstakingly detailed the visuals are made me realize this game holds its value. The animation and artstyle are so fluid and expressive. These are some of my favorite visuals I have ever seen in a game. Think Octopath Traveler, but 2D and a little bit of Hollow Knight's dark aesthetic. I sat down and played this game from start to finish in one sitting because I was so immersed.  The opening cutscene had me initially skeptical: "Alright that was a pretty intro, but what does the actual game look like?" The entire game looks that good. The dazzling artstyle followed through every puzzle, every action sequence, and cutscene. If you are the puzzle platformer guy, the high octane action Knight, or the small can’t jump baby, this art follows.The story is good. But the plot’s presentation is disjointed and convoluted. It’s a lot to take in and you will not understand it unless you are really paying attention. But taking its themes and each story at face value still works. It’s a brilliant little game that I could not recommend enough.
