_childDocuments_.review: +Atmosphere was good; solid visuals & great music. -Unfollowable, functionally meaningless story. -Dull, uninspired, gameplay.I've looked online to try and get some clarity; so many people don't understand what's goes on in this game, (including me), and not in a good "it's up to your interpretation" kind of way. The story simply doesn't work as it's currently told.It's pacing is so inconsistent; as other reviews have said, I found myself completely un-engaged at moments; it seems they've tied drama solely to walking slowly. It's a bad sign when I chuckle at supposedly emotional moments (mostly because I had no reason to care).The game ends with a long-winded exposition dump of the core concept that they failed to communicate cleanly through the rest of the story-- "show don't tell" at its finest.There were some good fragments, here and there, but overall, I really didn't enjoy the narrative- seems like the devs hadn't fully realised what they were trying to convey, both with the moment-to-moment story and the overarching concepts. I've dealt with issues that the game explores, but due to the muddled structure, they failed to resonate with me. The gameplay sections are split into 3 parts, which the game jumps around in as is convenient story wise. They are all INCREDIBLY linear; I bet there's virtually zero room for differences between different people's playthroughs. For most story games, that wouldn't be a problem, but it feels like this game deliberately harps on design tropes of other game types, and fails to replicate them in a fun, meaningful way.The "main" portion of the game features some serious padding, largely containing bottom-of-the-barrel keycard-esque / back-and-forth puzzles, with some dodging thrown in here and there. There are a couple chase sections, with one that actually worked quite well, and helped to pay off the atmosphere, though it contains various instant deaths for choosing certain routes, to force the player down a chosen path. The a second section follows a knight, who goes round killing goo. These "Combat" sections also didn't really have anything that was particularly engaging; mostly devolving to button mashing. There's a hookshot mechanic that I thought might be used to make some semi-engaging puzzles, but ultimately went nowhere. It felt like a cutscene I was barely interacting with; into which it devolved completely towards at the end.The third section, the "real" sections of the game, you play as the child, and these bits are probably the tightest part of the game- I think I was more forgiving though, because this was the part of the story I (initially) managed to engage with.I understand the intention behind a lot of the decisions made by the devs- the three characters, the ideas, the concepts- but they ultimately fail to achieve what they were (I think) trying to accomplish. I think they bit off more than they could chew. The look and vibe of this game were great, and demonstrate real passion - but it would probably have been better had there only been one, more focused story, rather than trying to tell 3 at once, hazily at best.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing hundreds of pixel games like this I can honestly say that I really love this game. There are few things that I want to make note of before I get into my review. First of all, the character movement can be a bit buggy and wonky at times; mainly with using and scaling the terrain, however it is not that big of a deal. I also ran into a few weird bugs but nothing game breaking. I want to start with by saying the music of this game is incredible. It gets you scared, mystified, happy, sad, and all sorts of emotions that are hard for me to describe with words(which is why I recommend the game). Its enchanting and has you at every turn and never misses a beat. The music really drives this story. The pixel art is AMAZING. I love the style and adore the character design to death. The backgrounds are interesting and the enemies are scary. Each character has a very unique feel and their own mechanics that are intuitive and give a sense that you have indeed switched characters. Each character has their own unique movement mechanics as well,  just to reinforce the fact that each character is independent of one another. This really gives them their own real identity in the world. The story makes you think about the realities of each character and how they play into the whole message that the game is trying to tell. The story is not repetitive and is told in a way that makes you think in a larger picture. However, the only issue that I have with the story is the end. I don't want to spoil it to much but I feel that the writers kind of just tell you what happened rather then letting the "mind" wonder so to speak. The ending, however, is still very cute and makes you really reflect and makes you think about events in reality. I know that this story really hit home for me and really made me think. I love this game and would highly recommend it if you are interested in a narrative and beautiful told story.

_childDocuments_.review: A stunning overall experience. From the opening cinematic, you could tell it was going to be something special that a lot of love, care, and attention had gone into. It's amongst the most beautiful pixel art games I've ever played and is dripping with atmosphere, helped greatly by fantastic sound design and emotional soundtrack.Aside from the narrative having me gripped, the gameplay is, by in large, excellent. The detail of how differently the various characters feel to control based on their physicality is something that I wouldn't have thought about if it wasn't there but adds a lot, and is another example of going above and beyond with polish. Some of the sections are reminiscent of Another World or Heart of Darkness (in the best way) with you facing puzzle/platform challenges to deal with a lethal foe you can't fight directly.I neither rushed nor particularly took my time and it took around 3.5 hours to beat (though with a good number of achievements left to chase). With all of that time being enjoyable and nothing feeling like "filler", for me, the quality of the experience made it absolutely worth the cost of admission, but it's worth bearing this estimated duration in mind if longevity is especially important to you.So, expect to wrap it up in a day or two (or even a single session if it grips you like it did me!) but it's an easy recommend from me.

_childDocuments_.review: So let's start with the good. Inmost does an absolutely fantastic job of establishing the mood. You feel extremely helpless when playing as any character other than the knight, which feels amazing from an immersion standpoint. While many of the major plot points occur in non-interactive story segments, there are a few masterfully executed callbacks that have you pounding the buttons on your controller anyways, feeling just as frantic as the characters. Even the knight comes with its own emotional gut punches as you come to realize how proficiently you dispatch violence. I'm not ashamed to admit that this game made me cry.Now on to the less good. The game is extremely heavy handed in its use of symbolism. The meaning behind various elements is alluded to, hinted at, illustrated, then painfully explained in the epilogue. I understand that in an atmospheric game like this, you don't want the player to miss the message, but the number of "yeah, I get it" moments just piles up and is distracting. This alone would be forgivable, but having the uncertainty stripped away so bluntly also undermines the story itself. By showing us the explicit meaning, we see that of the three stories, one is based on a central conceit that isn't applicable to the overarching narrative and another is just dumb. These weren't a problem when it was just metaphor and symbolism, but making them literal detracts so much from the finished product.Games like this are supposed to invite you reflect on everything that occurred in the hopes that you'll learn and grow. Inmost, on the other hand, begins to unravel like a cheap sweater as you look back on it. It's emotional and heart wrenching in the moment, but will ultimately leave you unsatisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost is a lovely looking pixel game with a grim world setting. It is one of those stories that is not told in a linear order, but in a way to tell you things in the order that tries to keep you guessing and wondering which way the story is going and for what reason why the events that are happening happen. In the game you play 3 characters in different settings, With the little girl you explore a singular property, with the man you complete puzzles, run from enemies and explore a large map unlocking different areas as you progress by collecting items and meeting npcs. While the knight allows you to get some combat in albeit very simple combat. The game breaks it up so it doesn't get stale in either setting although I personally wasn't big on the little girl parts due to how slow she moves and the controls for her seem to work worse than the other two.  You, for what seems like most of the game play the man which is what I enjoyed the most as I couldn't really understand the situation with the little girl and the knight. At first I honestly thought the little girl story was a child predator who would abduct little girls and the older one was getting jealous of the little one because the child predator wasn't paying attention to her. Luckily I was wrong.I don't see the game having much replayability and it isn't particularly long. While I do recommend the game I would say that it is a game you buy when on sale, but that is me.

_childDocuments_.review: I have found the story of this game to be incredibly enjoyable, it feels like a long time since I've been able to play a genuinely good short game, I find this game very similar in theme to LIMBO or INSIDE in this regard. I'm looking to play through more of the game again as there is more story that can be gained on subsequent playthroughs if you're not incredibly diligent to searching the first time playing through.I would only really say that initially figuring out the combat mechanics was difficult and I got stuck and unable to get down off a table right at the beginning of the game, but a quick restart fixed that and I had little to no issues aside from some slightly annoying climbing not working on occasion while using a controller, I found that more has to do with you needing to completely stop using the analog stick for a moment after getting on a ladder to presumably reset the input, which could be a bit annoying in certain chase segments in the game, I was fortunate enough to not have this issue during those.

_childDocuments_.review: The intent behind the game was good. The gameplay, story, and delivery were lacking . I don't regret playing this game. But I also wouldn't recommend it.The game is about depression, child abuse, and eventually suicide. It's not a light, happy game. The end of the game does tell players that they aren't alone in their struggles. However, the hopeful message appears in the last two minutes of the game. Waiting an entire game to tell someone "you're not alone" is IMO a bad choice when there are several potentially triggering scenes of abuse, bullying, and suicide. The eventual good message might not reach people who are struggling since they might give up on the game before they get to the end.I give the developers HUGE props for trying to tackle something as heavy as depression and suicide. But the story is played out in a really confusing way that made me wonder what was going on most of the time. The three characters you play as are supposedly related but it isn't clear how the knight is related to the child or the old man.It seems like the developers wanted to create a mystery and didn't include enough clues for it to feel like I knew what was happening until the very end.Pros: - Sends a good message eventually- The pixel graphics are gorgeous- It's shortCons:- The story is obfuscated too much until it hits you over the head- The gameplay isn't really all that fun or compelling-  The puzzles feel either very generic or  genuinely unintuitive. There's no good middle ground between "this is a common video game puzzle" and "what do they even want me to do here"- Waiting to the end to be supportive for people struggling with depression instead of sprinkling it through the game is the wrong choice.

Sure, you lure one or two enemies on a tile and then make something fall on it. Solving puzzle ? yeah, put a wheel in a wheel shaped hole. Utilise scythe hookshot and pickaxe ? yes, the scythe is required only ONCE to advance in the game, the pickaxe destroys like 2-3 boulders, and the hookshot is because your knight can't even JUMP.Seriously, I thought this game would have a fun gameplay, but it's basically a few puzzles with super slow characters, that's how it expands to a 5h game. That was seriously one of the most boring game I've played, and understanding the story doesnt justify that the game is BAD. And trust me, I love indie games and helping young studios, but this ? _childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME IS GREAT! It is much shorter than I had expected (about 3-4 hours for a blind run) but great nonetheless. After playing through the game and getting all of the achievements I can say with utmost certainty that if you're into games like Celeste, Hollow Knight- Actually, just any platformer game or puzzle game, you WILL enjoy this game! The art is truly incredible (honestly, some of the best I have seen) which makes you wanna explore and take in your surroundings, the map is designed amazingly so that you can easily navigate to older areas via checkpoints or simply on foot and this adds to how nicely the collectibles are placed which are nicely hidden so that you can kinda guess where they are after finding a few while still remaining a fun side-quest. The story/lore is very intriguing and the gameplay is just awesome! I won't go into detail as there are minor spoilers but there are plenty of cool little mechanics that give this game such a nice, fluid feel. In conclusion, when you put all that together, you have yourself an excellent game! However, I have read other reviews and there was a common complaint of there being a 'huge lore dump at the end'. While I agree with this, it really was a long sequence of cutscenes, I don't particularly think this is a bad thing? The game is short and while yes we usually play games for the gameplay - We would just watch films otherwise - I think the developers' intentions were to tell a story rather than make an awesome platformer. They just wanted to tell the story in this format. In short, It's a short game so in my opinion, it doesn't matter too much where you have cutscenes and where you have gameplay. I think the game is paced well and I recommend it to all platformer enjoyers. It is a shame that I am writing this review now as I believe the game is coming off sale soon. Anyways, have a great day and seriously consider getting this game! <3

_childDocuments_.review: I once said that Wandersong is my favorite game, and one that just exudes joy and positivity. But we're here to talk about Inmost- a dreary yet beautiful game that demonstrates A. how beautiful stylized pixel art can be, and B. how profound the medium of games can be. After finishing the game, I really needed to take a minute. Like, it's the kind of game that addresses many ideas, both dark and deep, about pain and our impact on the lives of others. Without getting too far into it and spoiling everything, I can safely say this is one of the most depressing yet satisfying gaming experiences I've had since, like, Silent Hill 2. I will highly recommend this title- whether you want to get real sad and broken, or whether you just wanna see what video games can really do with regard to storytelling. Oh, also, the Music is STELLAR.

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost is a beautiful pixel platformer that owes some of its genetic material to cinematic platformers but due to how it is structured feels pretty unique in how it approaches those genre conventions. It's also a game of three-thirds that is constantly at war with itself. One-third is the story of an older guy exploring a depilated castle, slowly opening gateways to connect sections and make shortcuts, solving little puzzle-like things along the way. It's basically the core game of the game, so to speak. One of the main limitations in that part is that your character can't attack and has to bait monsters to jump to their own doom. On the other hand, he's the only character with the ability to jump like in a typical platformer, which makes this part of the game feel the most conventional.One-third is the story of a knight. It's supposed to be a solemn rumination on the cost of violence and seeing everything in the world as just something to be cut down. You play a character who can't jump but can attack quite vigorously and who even upon death respawns close by to go at it again. It's the most action-y and agile part of the game and in some sense the most fun.The last third of the game is the story of a young girl exploring a house in a contemporary setting with hints of lots of drama lurking beneath the surface. Your character is short and slow, and can't jump or do much of anything else. Later she picks up a stuffed bunny that talks with her in her mind. If the third about the older guy exploring and puzzling himself through a castle is the core pillar of the gameplay, this third about the young girl is the core pillar of the story.But those two parts work against each other. Whenever you reach an important milestone puzzling through the castle the story about the young girl kills the pacing and momentum and her slow movements make it really hard not to just hit escape and do something else. This is the part of the game that makes you question whether this should have even been a game and not just done as a movie or as prose fiction or some other medium that is less interactive.In the end, what remains is a story that allows multiple layers of interpretation but whose narrative stands in the way of the game being really much of a game. When you reach the end of the gameplay section you don't even have to do something specific, you just reach a part where the story takes over fully and unloads 20 minutes of story on you with a dramatic fight where you can only watch and not do anything. And then eventually the credits roll.Inmost has nice enough visuals, and the few gameplay parts that are there are solid but overall it doesn't really feel enough like a game to matter. This is a story pretending to be a game only to wrest control from you, in the end, to tell its story irrespective of whether you care how the story unfolds or whether you care at all for its narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: I should've paid more attention to the description of the game. It says right there: cinematic. Which means the game's main focus is the look, the aesthetic, the ambience, and the storytelling; the gameplay is an afterthought. I only played for 17 minutes, but even then I noticed that it's more of a game that you watch and feel, rather than play. This can be a plus; there are games that do this well. But here, just during those 17 minutes, I got my fair share of cheap deaths, backtracking for seemingly no reason, slow movement... and a story that is too disconnected for me to appreciate.It's a little like GRIS. The game seems to mostly be an excuse to look at pretty pictures. Admittedly, the pictures are very pretty; but that's not enough to get me invested. This seems to be one of those projects which would've worked better as a short film, in my personal opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: While Inmost is short and the overall theme is depressing, the exploration of the areas and slowly discovering the game is satisfying. Mostly due to the level design which is very well done, it's completely logically planned out. The game doesn't have a map but because of the level design you don't need it at all. This game isn't hard to complete at all. The enemies can easily be dealt with and if you were to die, chances are you aren't far from where you failed. You get items to interact with the world as well as unlock new areas. There's little glimmering pieces of light which you can collect throughout your playthrough.The story is OK, it required a long (10 minute) exposition at the end in order for the player to understand the characters and how they fit into the world. Once you finish the game, I think you'll come to your own conclusions to what is going on.You shouldn't play this game for the story, but for a good lite-platformer with a little bit of combat in-between which is set in a dark fantasy world full of misery and hopelessness. It's a good price if you want something like that. Took me 3 hours to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so I am gonna down vote this one, and maybe I am just in a bit of shock but this game is NOT what I thought it was. It was at first. A nice puzzle platformer. It jumps between a few characters in a way that keeps gameplay fresh. The art is wonderful, the sound is wonderful, the music is wonderful. All in all a creative game. Most of the negative reviews will probably say it's not worth the price unless on sale, it's about a 4 hour game. My only gripe with the gameplay is I couldn't always tell what I was supposed to interact with or sometimes would break the puzzle and would have to reload the stage. But all of that would have been totally fine for how well crafted the game was as a whole. The problem is the ending. A lot of people say is it sad and beautiful. It's just plain downright depressing. And heavy. In a game that goes on and on about hope and belief and claims to be about love ... it had a soul crushing ending that completely misunderstands its own point in a superficial attempt to be deep. It goes from a fantasy platformer tagged as an adventure game and hard turns into to talking (poorly) about mental illness and throws a disclaimer up AFTER it plot twists you into potentially triggering content. Yes there is a nice, italicized, yet easily miss-able warning on the game description in the store. After you scroll down quite a bit.Without the ending I would have gladly recommended the game. But the end isn't moving. It *is* woven together in a creative way. But what it's weaving is so serious and dark it feels out of left field. More so because it seems as though the game actually thinks it's an hopeful and profound ending... when it's shock value.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game in my '' list for quite a while. I regret not playing it earlier- The game won me over with it's charm from the very first scene.Throughout the game you play as three different characters, each having their own story to tell. Their stories are all connected, though you most likely will not link them at first. Finding enough  might give you more insight in whats happening. In some of the storylines weird living goo starts corrupting the world around you. Blob creatures with vicious fangs, spiderlike crawlies, nasty tentacle spike thingies. I think an important part of the experience is finding out for yourself what's going on exactly, so I'll leave it at that!🍬 If you're looking for your next game to play, and you enjoy puzzling, platformers, think games with themes like LIMBO and INSIDE, theeeen give INMOST a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: I always hate to give a negative review, especially on indie projects that you can tell a lot of effort and heart went into it.Unfortunately, the game opens up with incredibly slow and painful gameplay. I almost soft-locked myself at the very start and called it quits right there. But I wanted to be fair, give it a real attempt. You play three different characters throughout the game, each with their own playstyle. The girl is a painful walking simulator where you never know where to go so it's even worse than walking in a straight line. The "main" character has platformer puzzles, which are totally fine. Has it's own issues, but has it's own strengths. And the final knight character has below par combat.All of this gets in the way of a story that never really makes sense or matters until the last cutscene.It's only a 3 hour game, but when 2 hours are boring and frustrating, it makes the 1 hour of underrated indie darling not worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: A logical platformer with a strong emphasis on narrative. The game is mainly focused on puzzles. I really like the pseudo-metroidvania style, where you explore the castle and its surroundings and gradually unlock abilities to get to places you couldn't get to before. There is combat in the game, but they are limited to a few side quests. With the main character, you have to evade enemies, which thankfully isn't difficult.Like I said, the focus on story is strong. But the narrative is very abstract, metaphorical, cryptic... So while I was impressed by some of the scenes, overall I can't tell what the game was about. But maybe that was just me... and the language barrier.

_childDocuments_.review: *Spoilers*INMOST is a maddening display of wasted potential. The gorgeous visuals alone almost single-handedly earn a candidacy to the pantheon of all-time pixel-graphic greats. With decent mechanics and a serviceable story, we'd be talking about the best 2D-title since Hollow Knight. However, over the four hours of watching the game continually trip over itself -- eventually settling for 'quite good' -- the question that stands out is: why could no one save INMOST from itself? After setting the expectations sky high, why could no one make sure the creators lived up to their own aspirations?---The advantage of a three-headed game is that each section can whet the appetite for what's next while keeping boredom at bay. Or, in INMOST's case, each section can leave you wishing it hadn't been left half-developed, for Pete's sake. The exploration section might want to reward explorers with more than goofy dialog ssssnippetsss. The combat section might want to offer more combat depth than mashing E and ctrl-dodging behind enemies. The narrative section might want to not principally consist of glacially re-arranging furniture. If this were a novel, there would have been an editor to say: "all three sections should be good enough to stand by themselves, and right now, we are zero for three."Clunky and shallow mechanics could have been saved by the telling of an excellent story. The themes are certainly potent: multi-generational trauma cycles, suicide, managing grief. There is immense depth to work with here, and to the creators' credit, the sprites are incredibly emotive. However, the written and verbal plot delivery is a tiresome blend of opaque and trite. Too little was invested in anchoring the three story arcs to the master-narrative, the nuances of trauma weren't explored beyond repeating the word 'pain' to the point of semantic satiation, and the 15-minute 'tie-everything-up-exposition-dump' coda would be an insta-flunk in any script-writing 101 class. A story isn't automatically compelling just because it deals with trauma. It demands care and craftsmanship to tell it right.---None of these failings would matter so much if they didn't stand in such harsh contrast to its successes. Visually and acoustically, INMOST can keep up with the very best in the industry. But if you talk a big game and don't deliver ... game design students will spend the rest of your days lamenting what *could* have been. Ultimately, I hope that the awards INMOST garnered will propel the creators to even greater heights. I hope that we will be able to look back on it as the promising but flawed first chapter in an amazing game-design legacy. Until then, I will take the game's advice on how to emotionally overcome two suicides and a murder in your immediate family, and summarize INMOST thus: "It is what it is."

_childDocuments_.review: I saw the "Chucklefish" screen and that finally sold me on the game somehow, knowing that Chucklefish was involved with Stardew Valley. However, I knew going in that where Stardew Valley has captivated me for over 200 hours via Steam PC and Android, this title will only last for a few hours, plus a few extra hunting down secrets. I was and I am fine with that.This game is beautiful and haunting. It didn't take much for me to get the game once I saw the mood and art style and realized it wasn't an impossible "roguelike," which fascinate but also tend to annoy me with their difficulties.I have played only 20 minutes, and I love it, and I am glad I bought it. It intrigues me in the way that "Darkwood" intrigued me, just a simple beautiful game at once strange and singular and not to be missed.This is more of an experience than a game. This is like Liam Neeson reading a dark fairy tale/bedtime story to me while inside a blanket fort at night, in a dream world where the rain beats at the windows outside, and words are tangible thought balloons that fade into an emotional morass.My only gripes are the controls, which are a bit quirky using a controller. Methinks this game may be best experienced as a touch control game, and if you have to have it right away like I did, fine, but I would guess that the best version is yet to come, an Android version. (As far as Stardew Valley goes, I also prefer that game on Android. SV's Android touch controls are superb, and I wish Graveyard Keeper would take a lesson from Stardew Valley on how to do controls right on a touch screen.Anyway, recap: love it, too short, but worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;drThis game is very short and doesn't have much replay value. With its $15 price tag, it hardly returns its value. Just buy something else.I'm a fan of platformer games and dark stories, so watching Inmost's trailer certainly left me intrigued, particularly with the implication that it was a horror/platformer. I bought it with high hopes...and lost most of them in the process of playing it.Gameplay:The gameplay itself is a two-edged blade: a lot of interactions are theatrically pleasing and have splendid visuals, but it comes at the cost of the efficiency and action of an actual game. You could see it as more of a "interactive story" type of thing. For example, when playing as the old man (the main-ish character), you will do a number of platforming stunts and challenges. Rather than the usual platforming-style free movement of your character, however, you simply jump while moving towards the desired goal (a higher-up platform, for example); if that goal is reachable, your character leaps to it automatically. This isn't too much of a bother at first, but as the environment becomes more complicated or intense, it can be really annoying when the game "decides" where you move. Also, falling a certain distance means instant death. This is fair enough, but after accidentally tumbling off another platform for the dozenth time, you would wish the game's controls were a bit more refined.In scenes involving the little girl, gameplay changes from being a platformer to more of a puzzle-solver. Instead of jumping challenges, you climb around and use objects in the area to reach your goals. It's an interesting change of pace, but her scenes can be very slow and tedious for those who wanted more action from the game.Scenes involving the knight are the opposite; the game becomes a full action-platformer, kind of like Zelda II. You hack through roaming monsters as you march dutifully towards your goal. The combat suffers some similar issues to the old man's platforming, however, in that it's more visually pleasing than functional. You mostly mash the attack buttons until you either kill a foe epicly or you die. Not the most sophisticated fighting, but at least it looks cool.Story:Inmost's main draw is its story. In hindsight, it really is an impressive and dark tale. New players will unfortunately get little explanation as to what is going on, other than some scattered hints. Since the game tells various parts of the story by cycling between each of the three main characters and their current environments, it can be a difficult puzzle to solve on your own. The game offers extra lore insights as you progress and collect hidden "pain crystals"; however, it is far more likely that you will finish the game before you actually get enough crystals for a full explanation, and at that point it doesn't really matter since the final scenes basically explain the whole thing.Music:The soundtrack is quite well done. Considering how theatrical much of the game is, it really sets the mood. In my opinion, this the best quality of the game, and it's a really good one.Replay Value:This is unfortunately where the game falls flat. Without any walkthroughs or other insights on this game, I was able to finish it in under 4 hours. The entire game. Sure, there are a couple collectible things and achievements to get for the adventurous and dedicated, but besides that there is no compelling reason to play the whole thing over. It's like a movie: you might watch it again after the first time for memories' sake, but you'll know basically everything to expect. Due to the game's theatrical style of story and play, there is little variation to be had in any replays.Considering this length and lack of replay value alone, Inmost's price seems extremely high. When you toss in the various other annoyances from the gameplay, any remaining value simply diminishes. It's much like a Funko Pop collectible: pricey, doesn't do all that much for what you pay, still desirable to those who collect/enjoy such items but not really worth the time for anyone else.I might return to the game for the sole purpose of dogmatically farming the remaining achievements; my review should still show that I only played 4 hours before seeing basically everything the game has to offer, though.In conclusion, you should only get this game if you REALLY want the brief experience and are fine with the price. If you don't think that description fits you, hold onto your money and look for a different game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game description is totally incorrect.You think you are going to play a platform game with 3 characters; which is not what you are getting. You think you are going to play a horror game, which is partially what you get, but it is more an unsettling game with very good moments, that goes beyond the horror or jumpscare, and really put you in a mood where you don't feel scared, but you feel very uneasy.Long story short, it is a narrative experience that jump between 3 protagonists; it all revolve around the main story about pain and a knight and a flower; you will figure that out as you play the game; as it is worth to experience the events as they unfold and the story is few hours long in the end (I think some people finished it in 4-5 hours). The gameplay is kinda like Limbo and similar puzzle games, where you solve puzzle and proceed; although when you control the knight you can actually attack. That is the only time you damage enemies. The other 2 characters cannot cause any damage.Also you do not switch at will between characters; the story goes on rails, and at certain points the story swap, narration goes on and you experience the transition between the characters. So while technically you have 3 characters; you don't play the whole game with 3 different characters, only sections of the game.Another thing to keep in mind is that you don't use tools; you find puzzle on the way that require a tool; so a wall need a pickaxe, you find a pickaxe, you can break the wall... A rope has to be cut, you need the knife, you find the knife, you can cut the rope; all happens only as action when you find the tool, so there is no player action basically, everything is very linear.The platforming is OK; not too difficult except few very precise encounters where you need to be very specific in how you perform the puzzle solution, but nothing that will make you lose your sleep. At times it comes to a stop, I think to stretch the story overall, but it is part of how the game has been designed so I don't see a problem with it. It is not a metroidvania type of game, and there is no map, although you have to trace back your steps at times.I found the experience enjoyable; maybe not worth the full price but as I got it as part of a bundle, it was totally worth it; so if you find it at a discounted price or in a bundle, it is suggested as it is very entertaining for few hours, especially if you have a Steam Deck

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game; it's description and image gallery gave me widely different expectations of what the game really was, but I am unsure whose fault is.First, I must say it's art, cinematics, effects, sound design and music are all great. It's control's felt unpolished, but it's not a big deal.That aside, it's story, story telling, and gameplay is what conflicts me; by themselves -in a vacuum- they are great, but they don't feel like they get along well. I don't feel the gameplay helps the story, and viceversa.So, I kinda recommend it? But not too much. I wish steam had a neutral recommendation option.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost has been a fine addition to my library. Not quite what I expected, not at all disappointed nevertheless. Filled with emotions and plot twists, it was worth every penny.More than a game, it's a story. There are no bosses to defeat, no challenges to accomplish, it's you trying to figure out what happened. The good narrative, accompanied by a beautiful soundtrack and pixel art style, will get you hooked enough to finish it in a few hours and even drool sometimes out of sheer focus.Overall easy, the puzzles proved no difficulty. Controls may be a little treacherous if you are playing with a joystick.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: When I bought Inmost, I had only watched the first trailer and thought that it would be like Dead Cells or something in that vein. I don't think I've ever been more wrong.Firstly, the game is a masterpiece. The sound design is top notch and the music is incredible.I don't think the pixelated artstyle takes anything away from the game, it only adds to it. I haven't played too many pixelated games, but to me Inmost's style is my favourite. It's incredible how much emotion the art team managed to squeeze into so little space.Then there is the story. There are probably many things I didn't completely understand, but it was really well written and I liked the pacing: going between the different characters with their own stories that are somehow all connected.Overall, I really enjoyed the game and I'll probably play through it a couple more times in the future just to see everything there is to see. I highly recommend Inmost if you are a fan of good storytelling, great pixelated art and incredible sound design.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: I guess I'm not the target audience for this game but I've heard a lot of positive things about it so decided to try it out (although I've not played any platformers since the 16bit era). It was remotely interesting and intriguing. I've had to check a few youtube playthroughs (one around the bell puzzles and one near the end when I had to climb up the kitchen drawer but I think there's an issue with the bounding box of the trigger preventing me from going up and I had to load one of the available saved games so I had no issue climbing up). Overall I've only made an effort to finish the game cause I was expecting it would make me cry in the end (I did cry a bit at the end of "To the Moon"!). The ending was a bit disappointing. I guess anyone can relate when talking about pain but it didn't touch me. I also felt the ending was trying too hard to be too dramatic adding extreme story twists that felt out of place. I haven't enjoyed the visuals too much as the combination of 8 bit graphics (pixel art resolution was below 320x200 and massive pixels looked ugly on my 27'' screen) and high quality particle effects at a much higher resolution were always creating a dissonance for me.Music and sound design were outstanding, which kept highlighting the dissonance with the reduced palette low-res graphics.Respect for finishing this with a tiny team and better luck with the next game!
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know what to fully say about this game or where to start. other than that this was the first game on Steam to make me cry. Mild trigger warning below (self-harm, depression).The music of this game was AMAZING, my only complaint being the occasional freezes or stuttering I'd get but I'm going to assume that was from my hardware. The chase scene with the first Hunter was probably by far the most "scary" aspect if you're approaching this as a horror game, however it's mostly a puzzle-platformer. The artsyle is really good for as pixel art goes, however it being Chucklefish they always have had good quality with their pixel-art designs. Achievements are a bit buggy and won't load for some from what I've read on the forums and through my experience as well. A surprising amount of people worked on this game, and while the 15 dollar price tag may look daunting for a game that may only have about 3-4 hours of gameplay, buy it if you are truly interested. If not, definitely buy this game when it comes on sale. I've never played a game that tugged on my emotions this much before, let alone personally enjoyed something like this.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the aesthetic of the game, the music and sound design. Some of the narrative elements like the voice over were pretty nice too. Those are the things that drew me in initially...BUTYou must understand that this is a game HEAVILY reliant on narrative and visual appeal. In other words, it LOOKS COOL, but for me I spent most of the time being confused with the cryptic-ness of the story. The characters are pixel deep and it felt like a story and gameplay slapped onto some sick artwork.The bulk of the narrative comes at the end of the game, so at least you have that to look forward to. Otherwise, you're left guessing for most of the 3 hours, and without much of a satisfying resolution in my opinion.A game I'd like to compare this to which has a similar visual style and has great atmosphere is KATANA ZERO. The gameplay of that game is very strong, its storytelling is linear and engaging. Inmost's story is all over the place and the majority of gameplay is walking around and clicking the X button.This is a puzzle platformer, so most of your time will be spent trying to open a new area; due to the slow walking speed it can get pretty tedious. Note that there is a combat aspect of the game, but it's very basic and gets old fast. I'm not so sure if it belongs here.I know this is a pretty critical review but if you value the artwork and atmosphere please support the game, as it's got that going for it. If you're much more patient with this type of game this could be for you. Otherwise, I cannot recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where I wish I could give it a mixed rating. The story is alright, but it struggles in delivering it in the context of the video game. There are many points which serve as very long cut scenes, even when I think there could've been a component of game play added for interactivity. There is basically no loss component to this game, where you will very easily be reset to nearby checkpoints if you somehow die. Most of the puzzles are so straight forward, they serve only to delay your completion of the game. You bounce around between stories in this game, which I think is an interesting concept; however, one of these story lines is rather monotonous and has you slowly walking around a house, and dragging objects just to climb on them.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely dark and psychologically challenging pixel art puzzler. The style of gameplay is comparable to that of 1991's "Another World" and involves switch puzzles, careful timing and jumping locations, along with a few hidden object and simple sword combat segments. To say anymore would be to ruin the game. For me a play through was four hours, but an enjoyable four hours with the beautiful pixel art graphics to be expected from a Chucklefish published game. If you're short on cash then wait for a sale, but for the intricate pixel art and the memorable story line I think the price is fair. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and sad, with an atmosphere to match, this game is a masterpiece of storytelling. If you let yourself dive into the story, and play through this in one 3-5 hour sitting, you will be rewarded with an incredible tale of suffering, loss, and love. A big congratulations to the developers, you did a fantastic job!

_childDocuments_.review: Frankly not impressed. tl;dr At best, INMOST has you explore an interconnected map, using the environment to defeat monsters or create a path forwards. At worst, the game forces you through long segments of bare-bones combat, walking around and cutscenes for the sake of its plot.Unfortunately, the story is all at once obnoxiously cryptic, unsubtly metaphorical, and eager to dump all the "truth" on you at the very end. Underneath the metaphor is a confusing, melodramatic, mundane tale that didn't grab me. Overall, I wish the game explained .More under the cut:The game has touches of genuinely funny humor, and the world's atmosphere is absolutely fantastic, with excellent pixel art and lighting. But big chunky pixels don't convey bloody knives or sorrowful facial expressions well, which contributed to the gut-wrenching moments falling flat for me.From the constant mentions of metaphorical "Pain Crystals", "The Keeper" and "Soul Flowers", to its long final cutscenes of confusing, so-dark-it's-comical reveals, to the final screen's "seek help if you're in crisis" text, INMOST hits with the subtlety of a gorgeous, fairy-tale-themed anvil.Does the exploration gameplay save the experience? Not sure. You're often just moving or slowly carrying an object from A to B, and rarely feel clever for it. You never revisit old areas in different circumstances: at best you'll bring a new key to open an old lock. The map's interconnectedness feels unexploited.Some final gameplay-related annoyances: The "roll" action button is only used 2-3 times in the entire game. INMOST's control scheme is generally awkward, worse still if you're on a non-QWERTY keyboard like I am, and keys cannot be remapped! For a 2020 game, this is unacceptable.In the end, this is a heartfelt story with a message and I can feel the passion and love shining through every pixel, but I still come away feeling like Limbo did "problem solving side-scroller set in a gloomy metaphorical world" with better gameplay and fewer cutscenes ten years earlier. Ah well.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this. You play as a knight/assassin, a young girl and a lone man each with their own unique goal.I found myself rooting for each of them, as the game switches you between the three of them every so often. The gameplay is simple platforming and mid difficulty puzzles with interwoven enemies, which at times can feel pretty sluggish and repetitive. But this games strengths far outweigh the weak areas. The gloomy atmosphere and pixel art are done so well. As for the story, which is easy to lose track of sometimes, is very thorough with an emotional crescendo as a reward at the end.8.5/10Pick it up if you like simple indies with good stories you can bang out in less than 6 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could give a mixed review but here we are. Gameplay is the weakest aspect, it's pretty dull and is often padded out with unnecessary bits. The Pacing is dreadfully slow and the story is an odd mix of predictable and confusing. It's a shame because the art is top notch and the ideas are certainly interesting but it just kinda feels half cooked and made overly complicated to help stretch the story out. I think if they simplified it a bit this would be a much stronger game. As it is there's a lot left unexplained and while I can normally appreciate that in a story it doesn't feel like there's enough there to make you want or really able to speculate. I will give it credit for its art and having its heart in the right place but the gameplay and pacing make the whole experience kinda tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: There's a decent puzzle-platformer buried in this, but I can't really recommend it.The biggest problem is everything takes 5-10 times too long. It becomes tedious. You're just sitting around waiting for animations or cut-scenes while nothing much happens. That's despite the game only being 4 hours long (unless you subject yourself to getting all the achievements, but I can't imagine why anyone would want to go through that again).The story is incoherent and utter misery from start to finish, with characters it's hard to like or have sympathy for. It tries to be deep but felt pretentious to me. And you're forced to sit through it.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: I put this as a thumbs down, but only barely.  It has some good things going for it, and some not so good things.The graphics are one of the good things.  Pixel graphics with a muted color palette but they look quite good.  The animations are great.  The environments are good.  No complaints here.The gameplay is also on the positive side.  Most of the time you're playing as Puzzle Solver Man making your way through a castle-like environment.  You push, you pull, flip switches, climb and drop, collect items that open new paths, and so on.  There's black blob like enemies that must be avoided or evaded, since Puzzle Solver Man has no offensive capabilities (occasionally you can kill enemies with use of the environment).  Sometimes you play as Puzzle Solving Girl and solve smaller scale puzzles in a house.  Gameplay is engaging most of the way through.The story is where things start going south.  It becomes very clear within minutes of the game starting that this is one of those "guilt driven illusion" kind of games.  I feel like this sort of ruins the proceedings, especially since the game tips its hand so very early on in the game.  None of the interesting environments then hold any real intrigue from then on since you know they're all some kind of delusion.  You can't ever see things for what they are, you have to constantly try to parse everything in terms of a metanarrative you don't even understand yet.  I feel like the best of these type of games have the game play out in a believable self contained world and only at the end start implying that things aren't what they seem, so if you played it a second time you could start recognizing signs of what things really were.  It's just not the case here.The pacing of the story is another issue.  Your puzzle solving is very, very often broken up by flashbacks and cutaways to either Puzzle Solving Man's past, a series of intermission scenes with Puzzle Solving Girl, or a series of gameplay bits where you play as The Knight.  I feel like this breaks up the flow a lot.  The sequences with The Knight, a character with a sword who can actually attack the blob like enemies has brief snippets of combat.  These scenes are actually engaging, but they are even more vague storywise.  They're like an allegory told by a character inside of an allegory and barely make sense most of the time.The story itself is kept extremely vague and confusing until the end where it just dumps on you all at once the "truth."  I was left wondering "Ok, but then why does Puzzle Solving Man even feel guilty about these events at all?  What was the point of all this."  It's not good.There's a "secret" collectable currency you obtain by finding shiny bits scattered around the map.  These unlock optional pointless story bits from a shop character.  My problem here is many of the bits are located in secret passages or chest-like objects you open using your various item unlocks, but many are also simply invisible until you touch the spot where they are and they appear.  This kind of secret is just online guide bait - unless you jump around every square inch of air you won't find them all.  More baffling, some aren't invisible!  It's much better design to see them and then have to plan how to get to them, or be able to notice the subtle signs of a secret passage, which the game is actually quite good at with its environmental design!  It's a shame.The final flaw is the game is insanely short.  A mere three hours.  Like the dev juuuust made sure it would take long enough to complete the game so it couldn't be refunded.  Look, I'm fine with short games, but this is just too short for the cost.  Half price or more on sale is mandatory here.The experience was enjoyable overall, but there's just enough issues to tip this towards the negative end.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost is a Depressfest 2d platformer about a girl, a knight, and a guy roaming their own worlds of hurt.  Beat it using a controller in roughly 3.5 hours.  Difficulty is easy with some scarce parts being vaguely medium.  A good game to play with headphones on.  Recommend PG-13+ for angsty content. Most of Inmost is a manageable bunch of basic puzzles to solve, baddies to flee/fight, and a few jumpscares with an interspersing of key items to help you get further.  The menu keeps track of where you are and lets you know how close you are to finishing.  The areas the three characters traverse are large enough to have plenty of secret spaces and small enough to never get lost without a map.  There are also collectible gems of paaaain (no rhyme or reason how to keep track of what gems you do and don't have that I found), a few pieces of mood paper, and a handful of replayable achievements to attain.  The plot is there, and sad.  Nowhere will you find this game happy.  Prepare to writhe in the throes of pain and woe.   Actually, you would probably get lost in all of the heavy-handed surrealism and connect your own dots on what happened if you stopped at any time.  Thankfully you wont be put in that position if you play through the whole thing.If you're looking through reviews for flaws, then Jumping is the worst of the bunch.  One of the characters has the jumping skills of a wet rag.  I have died so many times because he will willingly throw himself off ledges and to his doom if you don't keep him under wraps.  Getting Gud fixes this to a degree, but by the time you get there the game will be more than half way over.  Slow walking/limping/sulking here to there is second worst, but it works.  In summary, I got Inmost from the Ukraine humble bundle and played it start to finish.  It's got a dreary look and feeeeeels to it, is short, and I can see why it was nominated for Best Narrative and other awards.  If you're into games with sad plots, there's no reason you shouldn't play this one.  If you're overly depressed and aching on the inside from your own deep-seeded turmoil, please take a break from Inmost and seek professional help.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my heart! _childDocuments_.review: 11/10 -- A story-telling masterpiece.INMOST has you play as characters and experience their current strife, both actual and metaphorical. Then the finale hits you with their connections & backstories, shifting your point of view on them so that you understand that everyone's pain is individual and unless you know their whole story don't judge someone.It initially tells stories about pain, but becomes a story about love.Animations are excellent, full of details to convey motion and emotion. Pixel art but not stiff at all. Each character feels distinct.Color and music set the tone exactly like Hollow Knight.  If you have colored lighting in your room that you can sync to your monitor, do it!Exploration and puzzles are smart, never frustrating. Whenever you die, you'll respawn very close with nothing lost.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to begin with... I loved the story and how it is told. The pain concept and the design of the game complement each other delightfully. _childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: The screenshots were intriguing so I gave this a try.Inmost is very basic yet-another-indie-platformer that does  to stand out among fifty million others. While the  is rather nice to look at, and minimalist animations are really well done, decision to go full grayscale and color just via some sort shaders or lighting solution hurts more than helps the game; it all feels like a dream or memory sequence in a colorful, much nicer game. Except here, it all there is. Feels like developers screwed themselves over with this. And as modern curse that'll never be lifted,  this game also mixes high resolution screen effects into pixels. Luckily, it's less visible than in other similar modern titles and in some cases, actually looks good.The  reminds me of old Dizzy games on Amiga. You basically solve very simple puzzles, which consist mostly of picking something up and taking somewhere else. Except that movement is odd mix of typical Mario-like platforming and those precise grabby-pointy games like Prince of Persia or Flashback, somehow taking worst of both worlds. It feels slow, constricted and cramped, you don't feel the joy of going fast or high. Few sequences where you can actually fight the enemy show how weak the design is. Also, if you die, you respawn in the same screen, so there's no true challenge. I'd say the gameplay target audience should be 6-10 year olds, it feels weird to spend time on something so simple and pointless otherwise.The  are decent, I'd say even pretty good for an indie game - the music and rare bits of voiceover here and there. But like everything else, lacks any design, sound effects don't add much to atmosphere or player enjoyment, no meaty slaps or swings or anything remotely as memorable - say - shooting your shotgun in original Doom.The  is one of those cases where you're not sure if developers went ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane with metaphors in desperate attempt to appear deep while being just pretentious, used Google Translate to translate game from Vietnamese, or just got really high on mushrooms. No matter which, in a game that in every other way is suitable for 10 year olds, I don't really see the point. I think it's quite dumb to slap the story of Witcher 3: Wild Hunt to Tetris. Yet, that's what it looks like. To me, it just came off as weird, drug-induced nightmare.So while the game looks and sounds decent, and provides few (short) hours of very basic puzzle platforming, I feel like it's mismarketed and thus cannot really recommend it. It's a game for kids. Get it on sale, if you must.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game insofar as the atmosphere is fascinating, the puzzles are interesting (if a bit easy), and there's an ongoing mystery to sort of uncover (though it isn't really explained or even well-hinted-at until the final 10 minutes).The female voiceover is excellent. The male VO at the end is subpar, and the script kind of smacks of a 16-year-old trying to be deep. It's very on the nose and sort of just barfed out in an expository way at the end. Tl;dr: Come for the great pixel art and spooky aesthetic, but don't expect to be moved.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic sounddesign and atmosphere in this little gem of a game. Each have their own brand of gameplay, but the majority is light puzzle solving to advance the story further. It's quite a linear experience with minimal exploration unless you're achivement hunting.However the thing that sold me on the game was the hauntingly beautiful soundtrack and aesthetic, evolves as the story progresses. _childDocuments_.review: To the devs, you really did some stellar work, and there's a lot of things I like. If you read this review, but if you do don't let it get you down. If you put in the time to make something, you're instantly super cool in my book.this game costs money though, so here's my review:I'm 1/3 of the way in and I don't think I'm going to play anymore. The world, frankly, feels like an uninspired souls like type of vibe. I was skeptical of hallow knight for this, but they really made it their own. This game is like if a 10th grader played dark souls and wrote a book about it. "there was a... uh... light? and the light was.... uh... pain? there was a monster that hunted and fed its offspring? I guess? and there's a ghost girl that lost her key. And a super bad knight guy that kills to feel pain cuz thats his deal. etc." Maybe this was because it was too much too soon, maybe it's because I've been spoiled by other games, but it really does feel like that to me. I found myself skipping through the optional dialogue from the guy that looks like the scream, which is the whole point of these types of games, and that's when I decided to quit less than an hour in.The art is pretty freaking good; the animations are really impressive, the visual art is good, and I was genuinely really impressed with the music. All that said, the game kind of feels like crap. There's no real consequence to death so it's just kind of annoying, the game lacks polish in certain regards (I got soft-locked after being chased by the creation of Adam monster) which makes the unclear nature of the game frustrating, and movement is booty. The enemies are kind of interesting (I really liked the rat), but you can't really interact with them in any meaningful way.All in all, this game feels like some talented animators and a musician played dark souls and decided to make a game, and thought about the actual game and storytelling components as secondary and tertiary. As someone who likes almost any artsy game I get my hands on, I honestly do not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I was not expecting this game to be as intriguing it was, While I had no idea what was going on story wise right up until the end, I was still very interested in the story the whole way through.In terms of gameplay, it's mostly a puzzle platformer with bits of horror and combat sprinkled throughout, it never took me too long to figure out any of the puzzles or where to go next except for in one spot which took some backtracking to find but the map is very well connected so getting around doesn't take long at allThis was very much a pleasant surprise of a game I was expecting to drop pretty quickly, as I do with most games I get from humble bundle that I didn't buy the bundle specifically for but I do feel the games price as a standalone is a little high, maybe wait for a sale unless you are just very in to games like this7.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: INMOST is a heart-wrenching story of unspeakable loss, suffering, hope and love. We learn that there is hope in finding purpose even after death has taken everything away. It’s an emotional story and one that we can all relate to. We have all suffered, and we have all lost, and we have all had a small spark of hope to get us through the darkness.The graphics, the colors, the music, the characters — everything works to bring us this story and leave us reflecting on our own lives. I was immersed in this story the whole time , and it was amazing from start to finish. It may seem too short a time to spend on a game like this, but it is exactly how long it needs to be to tell this story, and I am all right with that.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost is a video game as art.  This is an emotional story driven masterpiece.  I know that kind of accolade gets thrown around a lot, and to be honest "story driven narrative games about depression" are showing up with boring regularity on Steam, but Inmost is one of the few that have truly gotten under my skin.  Mechanically it plays like a puzzle platform but controls like a survival horror... as in you never feel safe or nimble (even as the warrior), but none of that matters.  It's the story and relationships that develop in between the puzzles that matter.  There are layers to the story, and I dont want to spoil any of them for you, so I'll stop there.  If you enjoy a relatively short., slow burn of a game with, bit of metaphor (and a bit of wiggle room to work your own baggage into a story) Inmost is absolutely worth your time.  It is a beautiful way to spend some time with a great story.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: "Inmost" is a game that deserves a spot in your gaming library. While the story may initially seem unclear, the pieces gradually come together, weaving a beautiful tale of pain and redemption. The game's simple yet striking visuals may lead you to underestimate its depth, but that's part of its charm. The pixelated design gives it a retro vibe, but don't be fooled—the interplay of shadows and lights creates a visually stunning experience, complemented by an exceptional soundtrack.You'll follow the journeys of three characters—a young girl, a troubled knight, and a mysterious wanderer—as they navigate a world veiled in darkness and mystery. While "Inmost" may not be a lengthy adventure, clocking in at around 6 hours for completion, every moment is well worth it. I wholeheartedly recommend diving into this captivating and emotionally resonant game.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: This game plays with some sensitive heartstrings and isn't the easiest story to decipher along the way. The gameplay can be a little clunky feeling (okay a moderate amount when dealing with the knight), but it is still quite playable.It was very worth the time spent on it.  The strings it played with have caused bottled up pain to bubble forth and leave me.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up the demo of this in June and then spent the next two and a half months waiting for this to come out in full. I was very excited to be able to play through it.This game is a very nice experience. The music is lovely; it was probably my favorite part of the whole game. The main storyline isn't very long but it is compelling enough that I wanted to keep going. I personally feel the metaphor is a little obvious, but the story uses it well and the bits that are revealed down the line add in well. I don't have a lot of cons for this. My only real complaint about this game is that it doesn't have much replay value. It's not something you play over and over for a different experience -- the story is the experience. Even so, it was a delight and I can see myself loading it back up to go through the story again, even if it remains unchanged.

_childDocuments_.review: This beautifully atmospheric pixelgraphic game straddles the line fantastically between puzzle and platforming, an intriguing narrative and just enough chronological shenanigans to make it even more appealing to find out what the mystery is. _childDocuments_.review: I think this is a short but sweet game, left me feeling emotional with a new perspective on things or at least a new way to put things to words.The gameplay took a moment to get used to but once figured out worked great to give some interesting puzzles and conflicts between the narrative moments.Voice acting is well done and the overall sound design does a great job at setting the tone.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: This game is alright, although I don't recommend it. Firstly, I didn't have any issues with the Game-play in this Puzzle Platformer. I played with a keyboard and mouse, and it controlled fine. Most puzzles were basic, barricading me only by the unexplained direction you're supposed to be moving towards. It's worth mentioning that for some achievements, you'll likely have to collect those Soul Crystals, Pain Crystals, or Gems, which look strangely familiar to what I also believe to be soul flowers, you'll have to play through most if not all of the game in one sitting. Speaking of those Soul Crystals, the story is confusing. This game wanted to be mysterious, and yes, it is mysterious, so mysterious in fact that I don't understand it. It's obvious that each segment isn't in chronological order, and that makes the story harder to follow. Maybe the story is intentionally meant this way. Maybe some things were left intentionally unexplained to be put up to player interpretation, however, for some things in this game, I couldn't interpret ♥♥♥♥, at least for my first playthrough. For seven bucks, the amount I payed for this game, it's value is alright, but fifteen dollars? Really? Would not pay that much. So yeah, this is my review.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Some Ideas are just better done for movies than games. This is one of them. The art style is nice, the story is not too deep but fun to ponder. Is it worth 15$? Not in a long shot. If you can snag it for a little less than 9 I would say try it out.For gameplay, it's kinda lacking. There are 3 different sections you play being the old grandpa, chad knight, and this confused little girl. The best parts in my opinion were the little girl sections because it has a nice mix of story and puzzle, and luckily for the player, it does take about half of the game. You're wondering what in the world is going on with her family, you get the perspective of a cynical little girl talking to her toys, and solve puzzles where your size, strength, and creativity all come into play. If the game had more or just the girl sections then maybe it would be worth a solid 12$. The Grandpa sections are meant to be more puzzle solving but it feels more like a goalless Mario level from how often I used the jump button to get everywhere. There are some interesting ideas but you could completely miss all of them if you’re not searching the world like it’s Wolfenstein 3D. It’s alright for what it is just get ready for some cheap horror tricks. The dumbest section of the game would be the chad knight. Does the trailer make this look cool? Does the parkour running from the snake look like the coolest thing? Well, guess what bucko. No. Just no. The trailer just over hyped it because the movement is like moving a brick. These parts feel like they should be the hardcore action sections but it falls right on its face. The fighting is clunky and frustrating sometimes. The only part I thought was the most fun playing as this character was the first level and it’s just boring and a chore you have to do in order to get to the next character. The story parts in my opinion are far better. I liked the writing and symbology of the story but the gameplay just does nothing. When the gameplay seems to start getting good again (Spoiler alert) it jumps right into a cutscene. Again I feel like this should just be an episode or short film because the art is pretty, and symbology is heart-touching, and the story is interesting. And it almost turns into a short film at the end of the game right after another frustrating knight section. But his is certainly not worth 15 bucks. I completed the game in about an hour and that’s with me getting lost, stuck, or having to take a dump. This feels more like a 5$ game. You would get more just by saving your money and looking up a play-through. It’s a shame too. I was really hyped for the game because I liked Chuckle Fishes games but this definitely wasn’t worth the hype. Again save yourself money and look up a playthrough. If they made an update adding at least another hour and a half of the girl section or make the knight or grandpa section better then I would give it a better rating.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: I've always liked to play cute puzzle platform games but since I saw Inmost there was something ion it that wanted me to have it. It spent some time in my wish list as it looked dark to me. But in the end, I just let curiosity bite me... Long story short i got in love with this game since minute one not only for it pixel graphics but the music, sound effects and story all together. This is one of those games that you don't actually care for its length as the story is really involving and you don't realize how much time you spend on it. To be honest I'm one of those who looks for the game length to give me an idea how long I will spend on it but definitely not Inmost. It was hard to me to understand the story but it has just the right flow for you to unravel the mystery throughout the game play. Sensitive topics indeed, but despite how difficult they are to talk about Inmost leaves you with a learning. Loved this game. I truly did.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game sitting in my Wishlist for a while. Then a good friend had bought it for me for Christmas.I never bothered to buy it myself, because at first glance it didn't really seem like my cup of tea. My thought process was, "Oh, it looks good, seems interesting enough but I'm not sure if I *really* want it." So, it remained in my Wishlist for.. 1 or 2 years. I can't really remember, just that it was collecting dust.I spent a good chunk of time on this game. So, here I am at 3:30 in the morning and writing this review.The music was spectacular for me. It'll either set you on edge, fit the environment that you're in, or in a few cases.. Set the mood for one of the scenes. Never a dull moment. The puzzles were intriguing and creative. Overall, they weren't too difficult to solve.Other than the puzzles, sometimes I was unnerved in some areas. This game did well in catching me off guard and go into a slight panic a couple times.Also appreciate that it wasn't punishing at all when you die. The setback is so small that you spend 5-10 seconds getting back to where you were.I was really captivated by the lighting. It was well done in this game for pixel graphics. I also really enjoyed the SFX with whatever you were doing with said character in whichever scene (I.E. The Wanderer or the Child). It made the game feel more alive, like I was playing a human being inside the game. I must admit that, at first, the story can be a little confusing. Once I had reached the end, it all began to make sense and it really punched me in the feels. I had cried.This game is well worth the time I've spent on it. If you're apprehensive, don't be. This is a nice little gem.And if you're one of those that's up for something different, then give this a try.It'll definitely keep you entertained for 3-5hrs. I know it did for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has beautiful visuals and a very emotional story behind it, with a few simple, but important life lessons. For that reason alone I can recommend it.However, I can't say I love it, and there are several reasons to that:- The game is very short, you can finish it in about 3 hours- The gameplay is very simplistic. Puzzles are obvious, and the combat is as basic as it gets. It's enough to tell the story (which is the goal of this game) - Storytelling is made in a way that the gamer can't possible understand what is going on until the very last 10 minutes of the game, and this is my main grievance with it. Once the plot is explained at the end, a lot of things are clicking, but before that, you can only make endless theories, because 2/3 of the game is a fantasy metaphor.However, if that doesn't sounds like something that you won't like, this game is definitely for you.

_childDocuments_.review: What to say about INMOST, I find it a hard thing to do really without it sounding shallow or spoiling the story and thus cheapening  its impact, but I will still try my best.    INMOST in a world where the developers of Hidden Layer Games were less talented would of been the equivalent to a "walking simulator" and by that I mean an impact-full story but with little gameplay to speak of but instead they did the hard thing and made this small Metrovania and meshed the story into it in a way that without the gameplay just wouldn't of felt as meaningful and I'm truly glad for the experience. and I would definitely recommend this gem to anyone who like a emotional story .   But that game does have its problem even if small the biggest one is the lighting most game where it's as important as it is here would of prompted me to adjust it before the game started and unfortunately INMOST did not so I played through the game without being able to see a lot of their very well made backgrounds and that's a real shame, for most this wont be a problem they would of looked at the store pages pictures and realised that it needed an adjustment and fixed it but for some like me that avoided them cause they've  been recommended the game it's as I said a real shame.
