_childDocuments_.review: Honestly i was pretty disappointed by this game in most aspects.First of all I'm gonna say that the presentation was good and it's a very beautiful game with a nice soundtrack.. But...That doesn't excuse the horribly slow and dull gameplay and the way the story was told. Okay so the gameplay is split into 3 parts: A puzzle platformer, a walking simulator and a combat part where you just walk forward and mash buttons to attack. All of these are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in their own way.First of all, all the walking is terrible slow and you get so impatient with the game and just want to quit, Especially in the girl scenes and the old man sequence where you take like... 5 min to walk down some stairs and listen to some 5 year old narrate over it. The knight sequences with the combat was dull and uninteresting, they were just the same thing 5 times with a bit more difficulty and a new coat of paint. Lastly the puzzle platforming was the most enjoyable out of all of them, but it was still frustrating in certain parts. There was just too little guidance on what to do and some parts of the background was so obscure you had to just button mash and hope for the best to progress. Also a lot of the action prompts just wouldn't show up when you were at the right item so i had no idea i was actually supposed to use that... Also i really dislike the whole minimalistic menu system they went for. There is 0 text in the actual game that tells you what the different icons means so i accidentally lost some of my gameplay because i clicked the button that immediately takes you to the menu without saving and not asking you to confirm what you are doing...Also also i had to turn the game down multiple times and ended up on the lowest settings for audio. Jeez it's sooooo loud. The voice acting was acceptable i guess but i couldn't really take anything the girl said seriously when she sounded like a 7 year old. Which yeah i get it's the girl narrating but still it didn't work for me. Not much to say about the story, it was confusing and boring at the start but at least i was hoping it was getting somewhere and then the last like 20-30 min of the game is just a cutscene where they are just exposing the crap out of the entire story and themes and you just have to sit there and watch. Like wtf let me play the game.. The knight sequences ends with him fighting a giant snake/dragon thing .. IN A CUTSCENE... ffs let me play the game this was so aggrivating and anti-climatic i just quit the game as soon as the credits rolled. So if you like a slow boring game with a confusing story and no endgame then yeah buy it. It took me like 4 hours to complete and i went back over, and over again through the same area trying to find all the collectables, so if you aren't into that it's probably like 2 hours to complete the game. Which in my opinion makes the price ridiculous. I bought it on sale and i don't even feel like i got my moneys worth...

_childDocuments_.review: Every once in a while a game comes that delivers its story either as premature information dump, before one had a chance to familiarize with the world, or as metaphor heavy delivery that requires utmost attention until the end. I'm not a fan of either but latter is the lesser evil and one which Inmost heavily exploits to unravel its pretty convoluted narrative right from the beginning.In all previous cases I have always lost interest long before reaching the conclusion, simply because I lost faith that my attention will be followed by a worthy rewarded in form of appreciation and satisfaction of what laid behind. Big titles rarely have this problem as they avoid the trap or employ professional writing team that can pull it off without risk for either side. Indies don't have the luxury of relying on repetitive gameplay so they attempt to gain attention by mixing stuff around, even if it's not the best choice.Inmost delivers in almost every aspect except for the actual story, although it has to be said - presentation is pretty darn good. Just a small heads up: pay close attention to whenever "flower" is mentioned. It will help in understanding the whole thing, which by the way is largely revealed (but not all) in one on the longest animated ending sequence I ever saw - over 20 minutes long!Most is just good old fluff and melancholic drama but sufficient for those who paid enough attention. I wasn't that lucky so my reward was partial at best and unfortunately didn't left me craving for more besides mindlessly collecting missed stuff for achievements.Game is primarily meant for those who suffer, to let them know they are not alone and to seek help or whatnot. If you ask me I'd say rather try few rounds of Counter Strike, or watch some Kay & Pelee skits, or pet a cat. All far better alternatives.As for actual gameplay, it's pretty good. Small in size and short in length (RIP if that's you) but visually and audibly rich light metroidvania. The way sound effects and music tie the gameplay together is one of the best I can remember being part of.Main character is an old Wanderer and it is he who pushes the story, explores world map by finding items to progress past various obstacles, and picks up collectibles. Some people complained about controls but I can atest to no such issues. Pretty standard stuff as far as they go. At several stages of progress, control switch back and forth between another two characters: young girl and a knight in shining armor.The girl's story unfolds in a separate large house area where you get to explore more of it each time, where she lives with her estranged parents. Puzzles are of simple type of using a single object in the right place.Knight is solely combat oriented, in another separate contained area and his story unfolds automatically as you complete his fighting mini-arenas.All 3 characters and their stories are deeply connected through heavy metaphor usage so don't feel bad if you miss out on majority of it on your first go. As I said presentation is so well done you'll cling to that without a problem. Sadly there is one major issue that destroys much of any enjoyment on consequent playthroughs.* * *And that is inability to skip animated sequences. Only intro skip is permitted... How in the hell was this allowed is beyond me. Roughly 33% of the game are long forced cinematic sequences from which there is no escape. Maybe it was too much work to align music and other scripts to numerous sequential skips player would undoubtedly perform. Whatever the reason it's unacceptable and I expect it to get addressed.I'd even consider creating Wanderer-only mode or just allow skipping entire Girl/Knight sections, since his metroidvania section is rather enjoyable and best experienced without interruptions.One other thing that could use improvement is UI clarity. Buttons do not have text, and icons aren't good at demonstrating what the buttons will do. Their arrangement isn't optimal and focus when you wish to 'Continue' isn't focused on chapter select.Oh yeah, how could I forget. Knight's sword swing only affects 1 enemy in damage hitbox, allowing for others to freely wind up their attacks (usually goes unnoticed). Coupled with 'no damage' achievements it yielded some pretty deep self-reflections about life and the universe. Just give us a proper sword, ffs.* * *Another cautionary recommend which you'll likely complete once and never again. Weather you'll like it depends on much you enjoy putting effort in unraveling intricately woven storyline. At least I hope it is, it may very well be a simple one masked behind plain word switches. From my searches I couldn't find a definite answer or I'd tell you.Whatever it may be, it's definitely not worth the risk of paying full asking price. Get it in a bundle or something or wait for sale. Strengths are very well done gloomy atmosphere, solid exploration and puzzles, and perfect usage of sounds/music to amplify many dramatic elements. In dev's own words "it's a mix of To the Moon and Limbo" and I'm inclined to agree. If that's enough I leave up to you.Also, before even buying, I'd seek a guide for wtf these words mean: flower, Keeper, Spark. At minimum those 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Loss, pain and depression as the main theme for a game isn't for everyone. If you play games only for maximum playtime for the cheapest price, this won't be your game. If you like games for their art and exploration of these topics, this might be for you.The color palette isn't static, but mostly cool and reminds me of the gameboy. Music and sound ties in nicely. Different characters give varied angles to explore the story. The different play styles mean none of them is especially deep - also serviceable, I don't think the game excels at the fighting parts. It's not surprising to have a cutscene rather than a real boss fight. The adventure-platforming - the biggest part of the game - is pretty good. Not hard but pleasant.I don't think i have grasped completely the metaphors used here, but the story gets quite clear (and emotional) in the end cutcenes, so I'm not totally lost. Not a masterpiece, but all and all a nice experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A story about pain, a story about love.... also a story about how much I hate steam review system lolThis is one of the most beautiful platformer I have ever played. The graphics and the score gives this game an extremely rich ambiance, able to move me without using any words.... mostly (more on that in a bit)The gameplay isn't anything great, by anything, it's actually a major pain... ironically. It feels clunky and unresponsive. At some point during a segment I was supposed to move a box down, but the game wouldn't let me because the chair was one pixel off, even though it was pretty obvious visually that I should've been able to.Every animation is slooooooooooooooow... unbearably so. It's kind of a good thing the game is short in a way, so you don't have to suffer long... ironically again.When it comes to the story, it's where the game really shines. It isn't perfect by any mean, and gets pretty on the nose near the end, but it sends a pretty powerful message.I kinda wish, weirdly, that there were less voice overs and even less text. As stated above, the game works best when it doesn't need to say words to convey a story. It doesn't get *bad*, far from it, but, again, too on the nose for my liking. When I started the game I was really hoping for a good word-*less* story 30 mins in, but sadly it gets word-*ful* at the end. Kind of a shame, but the experience was still incredible.Honestly if this game was any longer my review might've been negative, but hey, Steam's binary review system is still complete garbage

_childDocuments_.review: This one is super hard to review/judge. I love the three characters with the very different skillsets. I love that they have three parallel stories, in individualized worlds. I love the art. The soundtrack may be a little overhyped, but it's sufficient and appropriate (heavy on the simple, repetitive piano melodies). It had that hard-to-pin-down something that made me want to keep playing, and which is not so easy to come by.BUT (but, but) the way the game ends is a terrible let-down, on more than one front:1) The controls are wrested from you, without warning, when you still feel like there's plenty more to do, and you must watch all of the end action (including the final boss battle!) WITHOUT PARTICIPATING. 2) The story becomes an impossible jumble at the end. I could barely make sense of it. What... happened to the Witch? And the Keeper? The girl was who--and the man was who? The mother, and the rabbit, and the little rabbitlike creatures, and the father is actually sympathetic after seeming villainous? They weren't child abductors... or were they? What's with all the toys in the basement? If you collect all of the pain, do you get a better ending?  Left with nothing but questions--in a bad way. 3) Well, that's really enough.My impression (* as a guy who has a hard time finishing things *) is that the developers ran out of time, money, interest, or all three. It is, as far as I'm concerned, an unfinished game. A GREAT unfinished game, but impossible to recommend in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: System Played: Steam DeckYear Released: 2020Year Reviewed: 2024Inmost is an “indie” 2D puzzle/platformer, the only release (that I could see) from Lithuanian developer, Hidden Layer Games.It’s a typical example of one of those (literally hundreds at this point) games that are sat in my Steam library which I have no particular memory of buying, or even strong intention of ever playing!The main hook is probably the art-style, combining an almost monochrome palette with pixelated sprites, reminiscent of Game Boy but much higher resolution and with HD lighting effects on top.It’s going for “dark”, both in the presentation and subject matter, with some mature, even sinister, themes. At the same time, it isn’t upfront about what’s going on, storywise.First you’re a young girl trying to escape a locked room, then it switches to some bearded bloke. It’s constantly thunder-and-lightning’ing and there’s ghost or something about…!?Control switches between 3 characters, each with a different style of play.The girl is more environment-puzzle based, the bloke is more platforming (being the only one able to jump) and a swordsman is able to perform basic combat against enemies.It seemed like most of the 3.5 hour runtime was spent as the beard guy, working his way through some derelict castle-type place, then it will occasionally switch to one of the other two for a bit, like it’s telling some kind of connected story, except you have no clue what’s even going on…The swordsman is also in a similar environment, while the little girl is in and around a comparatively normal house, with apparently abusive parents? Her’s is kind of the most interesting of the 3 storywise, if also the least engaging from a gameplay point of view.The mechanics are all very simple, probably because it was developed for mobile originally.With the bloke, there’s a fair amount of back and forth, as you can’t progress until you obtain an item but you just got some other item so can now go back to that bit from earlier, and probably that item you needed is there. Etc.Enemies are these shadow-blob-things which (mostly) kill you instantly on contact. Fortunately, the game just restarts you right before, with no limitations. It’s trial and error stuff.I guess it grew on me a little bit while playing. Did the story make much sense by the end? Not massively. Is it a “must play”? No. It was short but that’s fine. The presentation is probably the best part of the game, with lots of nice little details in the sprite work.Inmost is a very typical indie game, the sort of thing that used to be a dime a dozen on the Humble Bundle of old (before IGN commercialised it). You probably already own it.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I feel comfortable saying this is a really great story wrapped in a solid game.The only negative thing I have to say about it is that sometimes the gameplay can be tedious in places in a way that really disrupts the flow of the storytelling which was frustrating for me.But there are maybe 3-4 times where this is super obvious.There are three different gameplay styles, but ultimately they are all platformers. But when the gameplay is about charactersand their 'power' the differences are more apparent.I don't want to divulge too much of the story because I think it's genuinely great, but I think the one thing worth noting is how amazing it is to cover 'pain' and by proxy grief and trauma through this lens. It was incredibly moving and rewarding playing INMOST. Time will tell since I have only freshly beaten it, but I enjoy playing story-centered games and this one hit me a little harder than some of the others in recent memory.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful. The pixel art is so well done, the music is great, and the atmosphere is quite dark. The story went much deeper than I imagined, and I was not expecting the amount of symbolism. It takes a while for the story to be woven together and become clear, but when it did, I was impressed.I understand why some were irritated at the way this game is presented. The gameplay is slow and methodical, but that wasn't what had me hooked. The story and the world that was created, the atmosphere, the smoothness of an animation, all of this created a very pleasant experience for me.When I first booted it up, my corsair keyboard went dark and I thought something was wrong. But then I noticed the rain pattern and realized the dev had integrated keyboard lighting into the game. A nice touch.I did one pass through and it took about 3.5 hours. The achievements were mostly about not taking damage, and I didn't feel like going back and doing that. So I decided it would be once and done for me with this game. Given that, the asking price might be a bit steep, but it's a high quality product, so I'd say it's worth it. It's not a must have at this price though. I'd wishlist it and wait for a small sale. Great game though!

_childDocuments_.review: 12+(depending on maturity)Graphics: GorgeousI have never played a pixel game with graphics this breathtaking. The colour scheme is spot on, and it perfectly matches the theme of the game.Audio: MagnificentPerfects the mood and completes the immersion. Sometimes you forget you are living being and not a part of the game itself. It matches everything else seamlessly.Plot: BeautifulThe story is both simple and intricate, dark and touching. It is deeply entangled in all aspects of pain, and conveyed flawlessly. It doesn't require (though one certainly can) contemplation, it simply is, and it is beautiful.Gameplay: EnjoyableInmost is an action, adventure, exploration and puzzle platformer. It also includes combat. It is not a difficult game, which is part of it's beauty. As it is, the gameplay is fun, satisfying and merges well with the rest game. Inmost is a single-player game and has minimal replay value.Themes: DarkThe game includes mature, dark and painful subjects such as . Takes on horror (including psychological horror) and thriller themes, though only mildly. It is dismal but hopeful, touched with pain, selflessness and beauty.Skills & Benefits: ConsiderableProvides a hopeful but fairly accurate message to depressed and suicidal people as well as assisting in realising, releasing and recognising internal suffering. However, it could also be distressing and rekindle pain for some viewers.I'm not sure if it is physically possible to play this game and not cry, or at least enter a kind of grieving state.10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The pros:-really nice visuals, as youve probably gathered. the animation and presentation is done quite well-good music, no complaints, and does a lot of heavy lifting emotionally-decent world structure, its intricate enough, with backtracking that fleshes out the space without turning tedious-mercifully short (3-4h)The cons:-the controls are Quite Bad. I assume by 'cinematic platformer', this meant that the distance of your jump (and occasionally the direction) is decided by the current context. the game is bad at deciding at both. interacting with items is also a fairly clunky experience. 90% of this game is jumping and moving stuff, so thats a shame -guidance in the game is rather inconsistent. no text telling you what that sprite made of 10 pixels was supposed to be that you just picked up. a third of the time the prompt to interact just didnt pop up. some object like the boxes dont tell you that you need an item to use them, so you just kinda jump around them, hoping to get some prompt to come up, only to give up and come back later -while the fidelity of the pixel art is nice, it does come at a cost of being noisy. trying to find secrets with cracks in walls in a game where damn near every wall is cracked is a bit of a crapshoot. also half of the collectables are just in mid air from jumps, with no visual indicator as to their location, so if youre trying to find all of them, guess youll either be looking at a guide or jumping around like a mad man -most egregious of all was the story. this has a comically cruel story told in a very obtuse way. It really felt like the developers were playing depression bingo with the amount of stuff they throw at you. suicide, suicide of children, domestic abuse, mental illness, child abuse, murder of loved ones, etc etc etc. It is utterly crass. and whats more is through the dialogue, the game seems to forgive all of this as just 'people dealing with their own pain, it is what it is'. it all comes off as deeply apathetic to the topics it brings up.from the presentation of it all, it really felt like the developers were really trying to say something deep and tug at the heart strings of the people who played it, but i really wish they tried less. i got this game through the humble bundle, but if someone were to ask if the game was worth it to buy outright for 20 aussie bucks, that answer would have to be no. if you have the bundle already, may as well try it for the visuals and the soundtrack. who knows, maybe youll end up being part of the 91% of people who like it

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this by saying I didn't complete it, and from a quick check of the forums, completing it would not have answered questions - so to take my review with a grain of salt from the get go.This game says a lot without actually saying anything of meaning - if you like the idea of everything is up for interpretation, and could mean any number of things depending on what you personally think, then ignore this review and get this game, it'll be right up your alley.If you'd like some semblance of coherence and answer, this game is probably not for you.I ended up refunding it after the second (or third?) time of playing as The Knight, I continuously glitched out of boundaries, came across an enemy that was stuck in a wall, or just generally wasn't able to progress because the intended grapple mechanics wouldn't work properly, and my streaming partner commented "So.. what exactly is this game about?" and I was unable to give an answer.

_childDocuments_.review: "Inmost" is a shockingly beautiful and atmospheric game. The sound design, the music, the story, the little details; all top notch. It didn't take me long to switch from speakers to headphones after I got a taste of how well-done the soundscapes are, with each little footstep, creak and impact sounding so textured and weighty. Honestly, the rain effect is worth the price of admission alone.I set out thinking it'd be yet another indie game with a simplistic grief metaphor but thankfully it's more specific and meaningful. The ending is unfortunately much less subtle than the rest of the game and decides to directly tell you the message and what each metaphor means, but it didn't harm the experience too much for me; the emotional impact had already occurred by then.Basically, if you liked the film "The Fountain" you're almost certainly going to like this.

_childDocuments_.review: The world of Inmost presents a beautifully dark atmosphere. Sound design and soundtrack are intrinsically woven together to bring its pixel artwork to life vibrantly. Even if it is short, it is packed with great platforming moments and I've gotten more out of it than a lot of recent AAA title. My biggest gripe with the game is the ending. For the most part the story does a good job, the characters are separate and distinct with each giving you a piece of a bigger puzzle. Though Inmost does like spinning a bleak web, the ending bursts the floodgates wide open and gets far too preachy and heavy for my liking. A misstep, for sure, but one in an engrossing journey which leaves you wanting more.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a conflicted no for me. The story seems to be completely convinced of its own profoundness but it really just boils down to a needlessly cruel and angsty narrative with heavy-handed symbolism that ends up being so confusing I had to go online to understand who was related to who in which way and how many kids there were etc. The gameplay is clunky, I died a lot because of that and at times there are game elements that just send you in the wrong direction (e.g. a door you can open at the end of a small puzzle section but you actually have to be on the other side of the room and I basically ran around confused until I came to the right conclusion by eliminating others).That being said, I do believe there's talent here and I will be on the lookout for their next title.

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous story driven puzzle game, which causes a huge impact in the player almost at the very first steps of the story. The gameplay consists in solving little puzzles that are not very hard to solve, obtaining different tools that open new paths in the map, and learning about the story of three different characters: A Man, a Knight, and a Girl, being the Man's part the one that covers most of the story.INMOST is a difficult game, but not mecanically speaking, but because of its story. As the developers warn, this is a tragic story, but where we can also find hope in it. I totally recommend it if you believe that you are perfectly fine to play a game with a story that will hurt you for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost presents its story as an allegorical fairy tale involving a witch, a knight and the pain that ravages the kingdom. It tries to convey emotion at every turn, be it with the storytelling, the music, or art direction. This is NOT a horror game, if you are looking for something like that, look elsewhere. Moreover, it lasts about 4 hours for a single (not a completionist) playthrough.The gameplay is of the puzzling platforming genre, as you play several scenes with interchangeable characters -the knight, the little girl and the wandering man. However, be prepared for clunky and slow controls, with the little girl being the worst, while the man being the best and least clunky of the three -thankfully also the one that you play the most with. The puzzles are very easy to solve, solidifying the impression that this game is more about telling a story than it is about its gameplay mechanics. Overall, I wouldn't go as far as to discourage people from getting this game, as it does have great music, atmosphere and art direction and I am certain there is an audience for it out there. Were I younger and more impressionable, I would perhaps be fascinated, but it seems to create an unnecessarily convoluted story and consequently misses on the emotional impact it could have otherwise had for me. I would therefore, recommend to read a couple more reviews and perhaps watch some gameplay footage before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost is a strange game and not at all what I was expecting based on the description and trailer. I would call it more of a light horror story game with mild puzzles and collectable aspects. It a neat experience no doubt but it's only a 'platformer' in so much as there technically are platforms and you do need to jump between them some times.Also, there aren’t really 'three playable characters' so much as there are three (technically four) separate blocked out parts you control individually as each character progresses through their little piece of the story. While they all have a different moveset, only the 'main' character has any real reason to be a playable character- the rest could have done just as well as a cutscene.Combat technically exists but not really. There's an achievement for doing the combat sections without taking a hit but, unless you want that achievement, it's just mash A to win. This wouldn’t be so big a deal except became a regular interruption of the 'main' game for, again, what I felt would have been just as well served by a quick cutscene. It just pads the game time unnecessarily.Or maybe necessarily as the game is only 4-5 hours, tops and a lot of this was stretched out by slower moving characters and lengthy exposition. I am all for world building and creating tension but there's only so much you can get out of dragging a chair around for the 3rd time.Sound design was fairly well done overall, no complaints there. Controls didn’t feel great, not terrible but certainly a bit mashy and less consistent than I would have liked. The collection aspect wasn’t bad but a lot of them are invisible out in the open and you just have to jump, duck or fall into them to make them appear. Made it way more tedious to find rubbing my face against every corner and falling off every platform to see if one was there.Story still strung me along for the ride, I enjoyed it even though I was so thoroughly lost by the end that it took the final exposition dump to give me any semblance of clue to what was going on. Of which, since the game made you play out all the other 'cutscenes', based on the almost 10 minute scene at the where you have no control over anything and it just vomits out all the answers, it makes me unsure if the game was just rushed out.Its still a finished game though and an interesting journey. You definitely need a  discount for me to really recommend it. At half off or more and a couple hours to kill for what amounts to a neat graphic novel isn’t too bad.

_childDocuments_.review: A good, very dark metroidvania-esc game. This is one of those games that's just there to tell a story, and not so much for you to replay. There's a lot that I like and some things I dislike (of course I'll try to be spoiler free).Things I like:- Deep emotional experience.- Amazing music and sounds.- The voice acting is epic.- Awesome VFX.Things I dislike:- Story is too convoluted.- Too little action. Cutscenes mostly play for themselves.- There's no boss-fight (Sorry! Don't get your hopes up).- Despite the low price and quality of the game, it's still too short to be worth 13€ (and the sales rarely get below 10€). Despite all the bad things, this is one that I strongly recommend for those who likes being emotionally invested.

_childDocuments_.review: HOO boy this is gonna be a tough review to write. And it will garner some hate of that you can be sure. So here goes.StoryThis is by far, one of the most touching games I have ever played in my life, heart strings tugged, cards on the table, I was moved. Such a deep story concept, and great imagery are once in a million years material neatly packed into this little gem.  I was confused, heartbroken, sad, tearful, suprised, joyous, angry, confused again(this one happens a few times) all the way to the end of it. The take-away being a very deep and moving subject not alot of people touch upon, at least not well in video games, and this game does it well. GameplayAt first the game will feel sluggish and slow, but the more you play the more deliberate you, and the game become. Very few of the platforming sections prove more than a quick think and you'll figure it out. Only one section of the game proved difficult(moreso annoying) what with blind pitfalls into certain death and backtracking due to lack of fore-knowledge of actions that should have been taken, so a plus in that regard.The Good:Great storyBeautiful sceneryWonderful character animations Overall just a fun experienceThe Bad:A few bugs, and glitches here and thereA few very very slow sections that almost made me take a break from yawning1 area I found where you are guaranteed to die if you've not done it or seen it done beforeOnce you find all the pain fragments, zero replay valueThe Ugly:This hurts me to type this, but I feel at least for myself it must be done. This game I am fairly sure can be beaten in about 3 hours, under 4 hours for sure. I beat it just over 4 hours, and I took a break to do some laundry while the game was left open and unpaused, along with a few bathroom breaks. This wouldn't cause me concern, except the Price Tag.14.99 is absolutely far too much for a game this incredibly short, and zero replay value. It is beaten, I got almost all the pain fragments and considering how slow the game plays and how much of a chore it can be getting around, I have no intention searching blindly for the last few when they can literally be anywhere, invisible waiting for you to jump in the right spot.The price tag alone is why I cannot recommend this game, and if I had know it would be that short with no replay to it, I certainly would have waited for its eventual sale price around Christmas. I certainly urge anyone reading my review to do the same.Being published by chucklefish, I am very disappointed in the final cost to play value, no matter how wonderful the story may have been.

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost a walking simulator/Metroidvania which fails to deliver for me on just about every level.The game is split into 3 parts: a walking simulator where you play as a little girl named Lizzie (the main story), a weak Metroidvania where you play as the Wanderer (the main game), and a few very short action segments where you play as the Knight (intermission segments).  The game advertises itself as if you're going to be spending all of your time playing the Metroidvania sections as the Wanderer, but the reality is that you're going to be constantly pulled out of the Metroidvania sections into walking simulator sections with Lizzie (which ended up being a majority of the game) or an occasional short action segment as the Knight (which serves no real purpose other than to drive the narrative and shoehorn combat into the game).  The overall gameplay is weak, the combat is basically non-existent (outside of the Knight sections - there is no combat in the Metroidvania sections and you're constantly running away from the enemies), there are numerous bugs, and the collectibles are unnecessarily hard to find.  The whole gameplay experience is so barebones that feels like it was probably originally developed for mobile devices. It's also a very short game.  I really, really took my time and 100%'d it in 4.5 hours.  The graphics are OK but a very muddy in many places.  The music is generally good.Story-wise, I did not like the presentation at all.  A lot of the characters and environments shown in the advertising artwork are not even central to the game and only make very brief appearances.  The story is really bizarre, but it is completely buried in lots of unnecessary allegory.  Despite that, it's fairly easy to figure out the general direction that the story is going early on even if you don't understand the allegory.  In the end, the story is heavy-handed melodrama filled with cliche.    However, just to put a fine point on the narrative, the storytelling suddenly stops being subtle at the very end of the game and bluntly dumps the entire story on you in a truckload of exposition.  So game's ending is 30-45 minutes of animation and exposition, and the "final boss" fight that the game builds up to is just part of this animation.So overall this game was just underwhelming, and I honestly didn't have a lot of fun with it.  It does have a few merits, it fell far short of my expectations based on the advertising so I cannot recommend it.

The game play is basic but fits the design well.  The story is a little confusing but it comes together.  If you're looking for a short game this is certainly worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost was a surprise!A must play, for story driven games lovers. True... It's a short game. But the story compensates for that. Especially for people who struggled with loss and depression. Is it the best game visually? NODoes it have the best gameplay? NODoes it worth its price? Yes, If you love story driven games. If you don't care about the story, this is not a game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost simply oozes style. The game looks absolutely amazing and establishes an atmosphere of strageness and dread from its first scene. The graphics, the ambience, the sound/music, the gameplay - every piece of the game comes together to build the atmosphere and story. The story is also something else. It starts off feeling like a run of the mill flashback/lifespan tragedy but evolves into something much more personal than you'd expect from a videogame. I was really shocked by how the game pulled the rug from under my feet near the end, wasn't at all ready for the emotional and personal impact the author delivers with this.It's truly a work of art to be consumed, all the rewards it got are well deserved.There are some things to keep in mind before diving in though and I think it is super important to come into this with the right expectaions because otherwise you might be disappointed.- It's a short game, it takes around 3-4h to complete the whole thing- Easily half of that time is spent in cutscenes or areas that basically constitute as cutscenes (You move around but it's really just storybuilding setpieces for you to interact with)- The game is super forgiving in difficulty, you respawn right where you died barely losing any progress.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Playing through this game is like finding pieces of a puzzle that make up a great big emotional hole.  When I got to the end in my normal way, which is a full on sprint with no sleep so that I can see where everything was going, I find that I missed a whole lot.  This is a game that I can play again, even though I find myself unable to do so with other games from bigger, more well known companies.  10/10 Story, 8/10 Gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Oh this was such a good surprise! I walked in knowing basically nothing, the artstyle drew me in, I loved the "monochrome but not really" pixel art but that was it. This was very fun! Very fun puzzles, incredible story-telling imo, a good amount of foreshadowing but that still keeps you guessing, the story is very moving (I will warn you it is on the heavy side). , I liked how throughout the game, the gameplay felt organic but didn't get in the way of the story and wasn't punishing so as to get a more streamlined experience, the cutscenes were beautiful and the music was great! This is a very solid − albeit very short − game, I'm happy I got to experience it.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Just finished the game, and I can easily say the game is about something that should be talked about more. Very few games tackle the concept of pain, happiness, depression, and how serious of a problem it is if left alone. It grows, amplifies, becomes overbearing. INMOST is every bit as amazing as the rest of my review makes it sound, albeit a bit niche.If there is only ONE thing I do recommend this game for, it would be the sound and ambience design. The colours though limited, get the current emotion across beautifully and the sound design is truly the superstar of this short, thoughtful game. I enjoyed every second of this game. It is not a fairly simple game to be honest, and I was a bit annoyed by the initial difficulty suddenly plateauing, but the narrative and sound design more than makes up for it in my opinion. This game is NOT for you if you are looking for a challenge, or something short.The colours are creepy, the sound design is great, and you can see the love and effort put into animating and overall game design. It's fluid, you can feel the characters get sluggish after a big jump, run when there's danger. There are 3 characters you play as, and each play very differently. I am hoping at some point it becomes clearer how the 3 are linked. The world is scary, creepy, and I felt unnerved and nervous plenty of times. Highly recommend this to anyone looking for a narrative game that focuses on a different concept than most games (UPDATE: I originally wrote clever puzzles, but I was wrong as they simplify quite quickly and focus more on the narrative exclusively)
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever, in my entire life of playing games, had one that elicited such a deep emotional reaction as this one. Sadness, fear, some good laughs, some things to make you think, this game has them all. This isn't a game, this isn't just entertainment, this is a work of art in the highest of forms. I followed this game for quite a bit before the release because the moment I saw it I knew it would be something special but nothing prepared me for what this is. It didn't just exceed my expectations, it made them look like Fallout 76. The pixel art, the voice acting, the writing, every animation, every puzzle, it was the best it possibly could have been. Even the combat sections were really great and I was fully expecting them to be just something thrown in there, but no they had just as much love put into them as everything else and helped with the pacing of the game to an extent I can't even describe... I just... AHHH WHY IS THIS ONLY $15??? Every platform, every line of dialogue, every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pixel was perfect to a degree I've never experienced before. Just buy it. Buy it or buy it those are your only 2 options when it comes to something this good. Hollow Knight, Celeste, Undertale, whatever indie games are your favorite right now this is something either on par or better and you will enjoy it I guarantee you. Congratulations Hidden Layer Games, you are now in my top game development teams of all time, and I can't wait to see what other masterpieces you create in your journey.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: “Cornflakes…milk…bourbon — breakfast of champions.”Inmost is a beautiful puzzle platformer about loss, neglect, and other disturbing topics.  I was initially drawn in by the beautiful artstyle & flashy-yet-smooth srpite-based animations, but the story has a way of slowly sinking its hooks into you.  The three characters play in vastly different ways, to the point where it feels like playing an entirely different game, but this adds to the experience as the variety keeps gameplay from growing stale.  Exploration reminds me of a Souls game in the sense that the entire castle is one giant maze, in which pathways are constantly opened up to minimize backtracking.  Also appreciated how forgiving the respawn system is — there’s nothing worse than making progress, dying, then having to remake said progress.All in all, 10/10 — beautiful project.  The fact that this was produced by only two individuals is absolutely astounding & I’m very excited to see what they create next.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of the gazillion games I got in a bundle I purchased months ago, and I decided to play it based on the pixel art on the thumbnail. I didn't know anything about it, and I was completely blind. Inmost is one of the best games I have played, period. Beautiful art, interesting puzzles, and the movement feels great. Above all, though, is the story. You feel lost at first, and it's not clear how the different characters are relevant to one another. I promise it's worth the wait. I was not prepared for this game, but I am so glad I played it. I just finished moments ago, and I had to come write a review. It's left me in tears. Fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: One would think that such a super-pixelated game would be, well, boring. After all, we have all of these high-end graphics cards to show off! Not so, my dear friend. In this age of hyper-realistic gaming, we have somehow forgotten about the Story. Put away your plasma rifle.  is all about story. You play three characters. How the devs managed to put so much emotion into these pixel people is truly amazing. It's neither a long game nor a complicated one. It's your basic 2D side-scroller. Find the key, chop through the barrier, find the crystals. Been there. Done that. But not with so much creativity.  really is, beyond all else, a story of loss, pain, and love.

_childDocuments_.review: INMOST is a story-game about love and pain. The story will revolve around 3 storylines; a little blonde girl, a knight and the Keeper and an old man. The objective is to collect pain and complete the story. Gameplay-wise, keyboard mostly but a controller is recommended. The game is mostly an abstract overlap with confusing storytelling devices. But don't worry, they'll explain it all in the end.The story telling is pretty bad. If you pay attention, you will find logical contradictions e.g. the old man and the suicide story makes no sense, since the old man isn't supposed to know about it. Likely that the writer tried to overlap multiple potential storylines to confuse the player but didn't notice logical mistakes.Conclusion, INMOST is an okay game. Nothing special. The story telling is horrendous but at least there's a game and puzzles to solve. You will keep guessing the story until the end when you realise there are actually 5 characters in the story, not 4. The toy is not a legit character. 1. Some GameplayHelps me get through the bad storytelling.1. Bad storytellingPretty confused storyteller. There are a lot of strange contradictions like the suicide, the old man. According to the story, they should not know about each other.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent experience despite a few annoying flaws.First, the graphics are very nice. Very good use of pixel art. Lots of atmosphere, beatiful art and animations. Second, the music perfectly sets the mood and adds to the emotional journey, never taking over.Third, the gameplay is smooth, though never really challenging. Some platforming, some basic puzzle solving, a little bit of "combat", lots of walking and very little metroidvania elements, where things locked or not available in the level at first, will become so, once certain item is obtained or puzzle is solved, backtracking pending. Overall, none of those overstay its welcome, and the game switches between activities at a very good pace, keeping the gameplay flow nicely.Now to the flaws:First, the story is bashingly confusing at first. It's all atmosphere and mystery, but lots of confusing nonsencial narration that basically means nothing and has very little effect on the eventual resolution. The meaning behind all the alegories and metaphors got so lost, I barely remembered anything while playing. Only towards the end, things begin somewhat to make sense and then the ending bashes you on the head with an "aha-a-a!" moment that really feels quite disconnected, though starting to fit the narrative in retrospect. But not before that. So, the narration gives very little motivation to play. Thankfully, everything else compensates nicely.Second, the knight sections are frustratingly simple and repetative. These are the only sections where you're barely engaged in anything but button smashing in extremely simplistic combat, except the enemy doesn't really fights back. I understand that narratively it works, but gameplay-wise it is simply boring and annoying.Same with the old man's sections. You just walk. Very slowly. It halts the game and tests your patience. Fits the narrative, but works against the gameplay.Third, the controls can be wonky sometimes. It doesn't bother most of the time, but occasionally it would really hurt the experience.So in the end, the game left me with a very pleasant after-taste. The story was good and packed the emotional punch needed after the confusing beginning, the gameplay was fun and easy and the graphics along with the music contributed a lot to the short but very good experience.

Well-designed puzzles.3. Varied gameplay.Cons:1. The narrative is too fragmented and cryptic,  I was still confused after finishing it. I had to go searching for a detailed interpretation.2. Overly preachy. The logic of the story does not flow well, and the behavior of a certain character () does not make sense, as if it is forced to serve the purpose of teaching a lesson. 3.The characters are stereotypical. The women are hysterical or childish, the men are the guardians, the givers.

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost is a linear pixel-art platform puzzle adventure that seeks to enthrall its audience with an emotionally poignant narrative that unflinchingly wrestles with the profundity of loss, suffering, hope, and love. While this daring exploration of universal themes is undoubtedly well-intentioned, it eclipses the gameplay, rendering it seemingly shallow by comparison. Moreover, the game's deliberate monochromatic aesthetic, while appropriately reflecting the somber undertones of its story, contributes to a visual ambiguity that ultimately hinders the overall gameplay experience.Furthermore, the keyboard controls fall somewhat short of expectations, hampering one's ability to fully engage with the platforming elements of the game. The omission of keybinding options is a source of frustration, as it limits players' capacity to tailor their experience to their preferences. Consequently, it would be prudent to employ a gamepad as the primary means of traversing Inmost's linear, narrative-driven journey, as doing so is likely to augment the enjoyment derived from the game as a whole.I must note that a number of crucial junctures within the game, designed to prompt advancement to subsequent stages, did not invariably activate as anticipated. This state of affairs regrettably compelled me to revisit and replay segments in order to successfully transition to the next level.The overall tone of the game, imbued with a palpable sense of melancholy, proved to be too oppressively grim and joyless for my personal taste. However, it is quite conceivable that another player, drawn to the game's introspective nature and unapologetic exploration of weighty themes, might find it to be an exceptional and deeply moving experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Im a lover of all things Chucklefish, I originally bought it just to support as it looked like a beautiful game, however. I had no idea how deep the storyline would be, I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a deeper storyline that keeps you guessing, endings such as this one are the ones I love most. <3

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game was going to be a platformer. It calls itself an "exploration adventure game." It is none of those things. At best, it's a slightly-more-interactive visual novel, but even that is kind of generous. The game is frustratingly linear, and although 2 of the 3 POV narratives you play through are rather enjoyable, only one of them involves any deeper engagement than simple routine interactions laid out for you by the devs. All three narratives come together quite suddenly, which leads to an extremely long cut-scene that ends the game. I didn't time it since I never imagined it would be remotely this long, but the final scene must have been a good 20 minutes without any ability to pause, save, or exit. 20 minutes sounds like an exaggeration but I swear it's not.I clocked in a cool 4 hours playing this game, but probably a full 45 minutes of that was straight cut scenes, and I did a lot of backtracking along the way to see if I could explore new areas once I had gained new equipment. You know, since it's supposed to be an exploration game. Unfortunately, a lot of the backtracking was either a futile exercise or offered a new shortcut to get from one area of the map to the other. All in all, straight game play probably amounts to around 2 hours for a $15 game.On top of all that, the controls aren't incredibly obvious and kind of inconsistent between the 3 playable characters. There were just a lot of really weak aspects to this game that made it unfulfilling to complete. I did it all in one sitting, and once it became clear that the really long cut scene was the end of the game, I was just impatient to get to the end. I do want to repeat that the story told here is actually really good; however, the interactive vehicles chosen by the creators to tell their story are just consistently subpar.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully told, but very bleak and sad small story about pain and suffering. The artwork is very nice and the depressing atmosphere is following you all the time. The music is supporting the tone of the game even more. The three sub stories connect in the end and everything what happened makes sense, although you could guess a bit earlier in which direction the story is going. The ending is on one hand awefully heart-breaking, but on the other hand satisfying and enjoyable and even a bit encouraging.I recommend this 4-5 h journey to veryone, who enjoys well told stories and is not afraid of some heart-breaking and dark stories.

_childDocuments_.review: It can not be emphasized enough how short this game is.Even then much of the time is spent with long cutscenes, sections where the character moves slowly and a repetitive combat section.The focus of this game is not the supernatural aspect nor horror. It seems like the fantasy aspects are just meant to be metaphorical. The most impressive setpieces are only shown in cutscenes loosely connected by the main narrative.Something to note is that there is a lot of interesting visual storytelling going on. But then there is also narration which sometimes differs in tone and the most story comes in chapters where you only walk around while the others quickly stop doing anything interesting.The puzzles are well integrated into the environment but finding out what objects can be interacted with is about all the challenge they offer.Then there are the secrets. Half of which require you to pay attention to the level design. The other half is invisible and requires you to blindly guess. There might be content locked behind them because during my playthrough I haven't seen things shown in the promotional material.

_childDocuments_.review: Well....it's an interesting game. And I use the term game loosely. To be fair, I've only been playing it a few hours. If I play some more, I'll edit this review. I don't think I'll make it much further, and I usually don't give up on games.The game is slow. And I mean slooooooow. Even my grandfather got bored. He's been dead for over 5 years.The all-star cast:Would you like to play half the time as a little girl who has a penchant for moving furniture around and having tea parties with her stuffed animal all while moving at a snails pace? Look no further!You get to briefly play an old man who moves even somehow SLOWER than the little girl, and you do nothing of note. At least you get to briefly pet a cat.You also get to play the largest portion as a middle aged man who is so inept he can't even muster a punch, and has an  Abraham Lincolin-esque beard. You do light puzzles, backtrack a lot, and find exciting items like levers for machines.You also get to very briefly play as a knight, who has a sword and a kick ass grappling hook. While this knight would die instantly in any normal game, the company he keeps is so awful he comes off looking like a demi-god.The "story" is very vague, and seems to be some avant garde BS about mental health and abuse. Or it could just be about an evil knight, a crazy step-Mom, and flowers. I'm not sure.In any case, usually games start out pretty fun, and maybe start to drag on after a couple of hours. This was about as fun as clubbing a baby seal from the get go. I'd advise against it unless you are a first year Art Major who is angry at your parents.The pixel graphics are pretty nice.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: This is hardly a game. It's basically a bunch of pixel graphic cut scenes with sappy music. For a game that is mainly about the story, the story isn't interesting at all. It feels really preachy and sounds like it was written by a very young person (specifically a young person trying to sound wiser than their years).The gameplay elements are not open ended. The game essentially prompts you to do something and then you figure out how to do it. Then you wait for some excruciatingly slow paced animations and cut scenes to happen. Wait several minutes for some sad, but quite obtuse story to happen, rinse and repeat. Only one of the characters' gameplay is remotely fun. The knight and the girl are tedious and it feels like you're just pressing the button for a cartoon to proceed. Everything is painfully slow, which I could perhaps appreciate if it didn't feel like it was clearly just to prolong a very short game (and probably to make it feel more artsy.)The puzzles are either far too easy, or just plain confusing because of poor game design. I'm not sure who this game is for. The puzzles feel like they're for children, but the story is certainly not.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: INMOST is basically a PhD level thesis on the pain of living. Do not play INMOST if you wish to laugh, or just waste a few hours. If you don’t game to think, learn and find answers, it may be best you pass INMOST by. I mean that in all seriousness, since I doubt you would enjoy playing.By all means do play INMOST if you wish to grow emotionally and to understand what a lifetime of pain has taken from you, and what it has given you. INMOST wants players to know that no matter the cause or result, you can be larger than your pain.I’ve never played a game quite like this, but I have absolutely lived a life just like this.Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really see why people like this game so much. It looks pretty good most of the time, though I do think the characters look pretty awful. From the screenshots you'll be able to tell if you'll like the style. I liked it for the most part, but the game is incredibly short and it doesn't really go through a bunch of areas or anything. Most of the game happens in one place. Calling it a game, though, is very generous. The combat is awful. You tap the attack button a few times. Death doesn't matter. If you get hit, you can just move away for a second. It's actually more interesting to fight with the non combat character, though most of it involves tricking your enemy into suicide or moving in the right way (it's never done in a clever way, though). There's only two really cool enemy designs and you don't even get to fight them. The puzzles and movement are even worse. It's like if Hollow Knight was made in a day. You have some backtracking, but it's annoying and unrewarding. You can open certain passages, but you'll never use those passages. The movement is slow. Moving things around to progress doesn't really feel right either. The puzzle aspect of the game is just as bad. It's so shallow. I was "stuck" for a second because it's sometimes hard to see what you can interact with. But none of the puzzles require thought. Just get whatever item you need and then use that item. Or move a box to access a place that you couldn't reach. The puzzles don't go beyond that. The story, though, man I had no idea what was going on really. It didn't help that the husband and the character you play look pretty much the exact same way. It would have been nice if it was a little clearer and didn't try to be so vague. That might have helped the story. It's also very dense at the end when you're still kind of trying to figure out who is who. It's a decent story all things considered, but I had to read some analysis on Reddit to fully understand it. There being a thread where multiple people get the story wrong should say enough really. The story isn't that unique to begin with, though it's the best part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: This game was impossible to put down once I started playing, completing the game in ~4 hours. It's unfortunately short, so I'm glad I picked it up on sale. The story is quite robust but a little complicated; I was able to follow it just fine, but others might be a bit confused as the narrative progresses. My only other complaint is that the control scheme for each character is different. While that's usually not an issue, you might have a problem playing with a keyboard+mouse, so use a controller if you have one. Overall, though, the gameplay was varied and engaging, the puzzles were simple enough that even someone as notoriously bad with puzzles as I am could solve them (but, the answers aren't always obvious, and you often get the answer to a problem before you get to the problem itself, which is a lot of fun), and the game itself is quite forgiving when it comes to deaths. The game also rewards exploration and backtracking, so be sure you take advantage of that.I'd rate it a 9/10, closer to an 8 than a 10.

Inmost is filled with love, you can feel it in every aspect of the game.I will follow closely hidden layer games from now on!Do i recommend this game... ABSOLUTELY!

_childDocuments_.review: It surprised me by having a decent variety in it's gameplay. I assumed it basically be a 2D walking sim or just a limbo type game, but it has action and puzzles.It has some really beautiful music and artwork with a very emotional story. But it also has a sense of humor (some of it pretty dark) with some things that legit made me chuckle.It's kind of a metroidvania but really light so the backtracking is usually kept in a small area.My only issues is the controls can be a bit clunky and while I get why they did this some parts are slow bc some of the characters are very slow.Overall if you like dark stories that use the medium of gaming (i.e gameplay, environment, atmosphere) to tell the narrative and want some decent gameplay then I'd definitely suggest it

_childDocuments_.review: I will try to avoid spoilers for this review, note that it took nearly four hours to complete the game for me, and I got stuck at multiple points of progression (I got lost and didn't know how to continue for a fair bit), so if you're afraid of a massively long game this shouldn't be a concern.This game has very nice visuals yes, but that alone would not get me writing a review after completion of the game; The story of this game is truly beautiful, I'm not someone who normally cries at movies or other games but this had me tearing up at multiple points in the story and I'm not ashamed to say that at the ending I was fully crying my eyes out. All this isn't to say that visuals and story are all this game has to offer though, game-play and puzzles are very intuitive and the level design is masterfully directed, if I had to pick something to criticise it would be that at certain points there was a hidden wall I missed and I did two full loops of the map before realising my mistake, though this could just be a me thing so it's not even really the game's fault.Overall I HIGHLY recommend this game to everyone, I don't believe it is too difficult for someone who considers themselves 'bad' at gaming, there can be a couple slightly tedious bits but with sufficient recognition of game mechanics I believe anyone can do it.Thanks for reading my review of INMOST,Crowan out.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game. It is confusing for a while but not too much, player takes turns to control 3 characters: an ordinary man, a little girl, and a knight who can fight. As the game progresses there are hints between those characters, but the player will have to beat the game to see the big picture, to understand the relationship and know what has happened in the past because the gameplay is the consequence.INMOST is an adventure game that features action, puzzle solving and platformer. It includes battles with enemies but focus on game telling, and I constantly surprised by how a pixel style game has wonderful graphics, much goes to the delicate movement like when control the little girl, she crawl onto the floor just to silently bypass  , and the movement she drags Mr. Rabbit feels so rich and smooth it is unbelievable.Most of the time I can sense the slight of bitterness, as the man escapes the chase of monsters, seeing a lady take her life by jumping off a balcony. However, there are humorous, like the old man stuck at the broken bridge talking about tea pots, the "many" maps he made, and that super long instruction on how to fix the bridge made me laugh out loud. There are also dialogue made me thinking, like controlling the little girl, take Mr. Rabbit to the house entrance he shall mark: "There are monsters in the woods. I wanted to invite them in." and the little girl replies "I think they are already in." The dark fairytale about the knight takes flowers from others and has a darkened heart is fascinating. At a moment I thought it was part of a Grimms' Fairy Tales with me controlling both good and bad guys, at the end I see how things are going and there's no good or bad people, just people hanging on to survive because they love their family. What I also love is the good use of the limited map - you travel between places, unlocking higher floors you see earlier but unable to reach, it gives me more pleasure than exploring a brand new area. I like the dark setting and the bright ending - The creative aspect is, INMOST features both a knight in a fantasy world to fight monsters, and man in the real world solving puzzles and a little girl's daily life. They mix well and give them a metaphor. I sorta feel like the monsters might just be the difficulties in real life, and the knight as the father himself trying to give a better life to the kid. There are still things left unclear but I get the point (mostly). It is not about a sad story, rather, a story about a once broken family trying their best to survive and love each other and to be loved.

_childDocuments_.review: I would have given this game a mixed rating if steam offered that option but had to settle for Not Recommended because I feel like the negatives ultimately outweigh the positives.The developers clearly spent a lot of time and effort to make this game look and feel really nice, and they absolutely succeeded at that. The pixelart style is gorgeous and the controls feel nice and snappy. This game falls short on the storytelling and overall composition however.You're playing from the perspective of several characters that tell parts of the story in different ways. Three of them are puzzle-based characters. You move around objects to progress, and those characters go well together in terms of atmosphere and storytelling. Then there is one combat-based character that absolutely doesn't fit in in my opinion. For all the other characters the gameplay and atmosphere is calm, but for the combat based character there is this really unnerving music and narrator voice during gameplay which consists of nothing but boring combat against shadow creatures that are easy to beat. That character doesn't appear to be directly connected to the other characters, it's more a metaphor of the cruel story and it just negatively stands out so much that I feel like the game would actually be better if the devs straight up removed it from the game altogether. Speaking of the story, I like the style and pacing in which it's told, but I dislike the structure and conclusion. It's needlessly dark and the conclusion is just stupid. Without getting into specifics, imagine watching a story about the murder of an entire family due to serious mental health problems of some of its members and in the end, after the whole scope of cruelty is revealed, you're just told that it was actually not a story about pain, but about love. As someone who has dealt with mental health issues myself, that just felt like a complete punch in the guts, like the developers realized how cruel and depressing the entire story was and then made a halfhearted attempt to put rose-tinted glasses on it during the ending as an afterthought. The combat character aside, gameplay, atmosphere and visuals are really nice and could have made for an amazing game if it wasn't for the horrendous story. For about 4 hours of content it's very pricey, even if what I'm writing here sounds appealing to you I heavily suggest waiting for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was beautiful, it was well thought out, but most of all... it was emotionally evoking. i was scared, startled, tense, worried, sad and confused, ever so confused. But as i went through the game, I knew it was trying to tell me something. there was allegory, there was symbolism. There was tragedy and I knew it meant something more... And at the end... At the very end, it was all tied together. the three stories, the three main characters that you have a hard time trying to piece together... and when it is all tied together... it breaks your heart. even when you think its going to end well it doesn't, and when you think it's going to end horribly it ends well. the suspension it holds you in is just enough for the moment when they lift the curtains and everything falls into place.More than just a game, its a story, it's a warning, and it's a promise. because its so parallel to life that you can't just have joy or sorrow. everything is mixed together, and that's what makes it feel real in it's own way, that's what makes it compelling. and that is what draws out your emotions. its not just something to play. it's something you experience.and at the end... despite the joys and sorrows, the catharsis of an ending was so nice when i had felt dragged to the edge of an abyss with each different character. all wrapped up at the end, maybe not with a neat little bow, but with a bow handled with love and a bit of exuberance.tldr: it was sad, it was sweet, and it was complete, and the story was powerful and the puzzles were just taunting enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost is a masterpiece indie creation. It uses game play, art, story telling, pacing, and music to create a work of art. It doesn't play like some thrown together AAA game. What it does it does well, and what it doesn't do it doesn't do on purpose. I never felt "daytime tv emotions," the game was designed so that I was encouraged to pause and reflect on what I was doing. It had all the advantages of reading a good book, and playing a great game. It is 100% worth the price point, and a worthwhile experience.

_childDocuments_.review: INMOST is a captivating puzzle-platformer that immerses players in a melancholic journey. As you navigate a young girl, an old man, and a knight through three interconnected worlds, the narrative delicately unfolds, shrouded in tragedy and exploring the themes of mental trauma and healing. The minimalistic yet impactful gameplay features sparse but punchy action, logical puzzles, and a trio of characters that provide a diverse and engaging three-to-five hour experience.Following the store page's recommendation, playing INMOST on a dark and stormy night with lights off and headphones on enhances the atmospheric experience. The charming pixel art visually communicates movement and emotion, while the haunting audio adds an extra layer of intensity, sending chills down your spine.I received this game as a gift. If the dollars per hour metric is a consideration, it might be prudent to wait for a sale. However, the concise and focused experience that INMOST delivers makes it worth considering, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Make sure you know what you're getting. The game is very short, and gameplay is more of a narrative device than an actual gameplay. The subject of the narrative may not be for everyone. Instead I got an "emotional journey", which, I'm terribly sorry, is way too overdone to work for me — personally I felt it's trying to squeeze emotions from the player a little too desperately. As for the gameplay, the puzzles felt nice, but knight's gameplay is a very shallow button mashing, and girl's part is simply too drawn out — intended as emotional, it is so painfully slow that all feeling can turn into frustration and boredom.This is a matter of personal taste, of course; what's not a matter of a personal taste is a very vague game description which mislead me. Had I known what kind of game and story this is, I simply would not have bought it — this kind of entertainment and especially the game's subject is simply not my cup of tea. Unfortunately, the nature of the game fully unfolded after the 2 hour mark — if not for that, I would have refunded. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with this game, and the ending left me feeling emotions I was unable to comprehend (autism and stuff, hooray). _childDocuments_.review: I was expecting something like Hollow Knight, but easier and more chill, and maybe more puzzles. But that wasn't even close. I have barely played three hours, so maybe I have more to experience. But according to the progress bar in the game, it looks like I'm closing in on the end of the game already.First, the pixelated style. I don't get it. It's not even consistently pixelated. Many things actually have a higher resolution than the characters, and the characters themselves have such a poor resolution that it becomes impossible to see anything other than a pile of colored blocks. It could be as simple as a bad pixel artist behind the job. But I don't think it's pixel art at all. I think it's a result of shaders that scales down high res images to low res. For no reason whatsoever. Just look at Hollow Knight.Second, the story. It don't get that one either. It's something about pain and evil. Black hearts, flowers. So, way too abstract in my opinion. On top of that you have the three characters. One knight, one hipster with a beard, and a little girl. What's the connection? I have no idea. maybe the answers will come later. Maybe not.Platforming? Tight controls? Well... No. The platforming is more of a setting than a game mechanic. The little girl cannot jump more than one pixel in height, and has to rely on objects to climb in order to move vertically. The knight cannot jump either, but has some budget version of dashing and grappling. The hipster? He can jump, but nothing like Super Mario or Hollow Knight.This game is more about story, which I don't understand anyway. And puzzles. But the puzzles are simple and pretty straight forward. So what is there to be had in this game? I have no idea. And that's why I give it a thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost never bother with Steam reviews, even if I really love or really hate something.  But this game made me so mad I just had to get it out of my system.Inmost does so many things right.  Graphics, sound, music, and story combine for a rich and gloomy atmosphere that pervades the entire game.  The three-part structure, once you get used to it, is well put together and there's a clever ludonarrative consonance between the characters' stories and the way they play.  The game is polished and plays well and the achievements are challenging but doable.  The writing is sometimes a bit clunky but mostly does what you'd want it to, telling three intertwined stories that thematically and metaphorically parallel each other.  Inmost shapes up to be a real gem.And then it throws it all away and sets itself on fire.The ending of this game is unforgiveable.  Half an hour of cutscenes.  The little girl's story goes from sad but fairly normal broken-family stuff to tabloid-level lurid and grotesque.  The knight's story wraps up in a way that makes sense, and then we go back to the little girl so that everything the knight and wanderer's stories implied can be made absolutely, ludicrously explicit.  Were you confused by any of the metaphor of the fairy tale stories?  Not anymore!  Let's hammer home over the course of the next half hour exactly what each part of the metaphor meant!How much of any given story to leave ambiguous or metaphorical is up to the writer, of course.  I prefer more ambiguity to less, but understand when a writer wants to help the reader/player along.  This isn't that.  This is the writer deciding that the player is stupid.  This is them deciding that there's an exact sequence of events in the story that they want the player to precisely understand without the tiniest chance of confusion or ambiguity, and they don't trust us to get it from either interpreting what people did and said in the main story, or from the heavy-handed metaphor in the fairy tale.  This is the writer telling us the story, and then stopping us before we leave to say "HEY! LISTEN! THIS IS WHAT HAPPENED IN THE STORY I JUST TOLD YOU!"  Yes, I know!  You just told it to me!  Chill!(Side-note:  the ending actually really does ruin the rest of the game.  I did a second playthrough to clean up achievements and the story feels so cheap and stupid the second time through after all the details of the metaphor have been slammed into your skull with a two by four.  Whyyyyyy)I wouldn't be so mad about this if the rest of the game weren't so well-done.  Maybe you should play it anyway.  Maybe you'll like it and won't be bothered by the ending.  Whatever, I've got my rant out.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely lovely atmospheric adventure-platformer. Visually superb, fantastic sound design, and an engrossing, emotional story that sucked me in and kept me hooked. I wouldn't go so far as to say that I was blown away by anything Inmost did, but it accomplished all of its creative goals very, very well. It's short, tightly designed, and strikes a good balance between clarity and ambiguity in its unsettling narrative.This is one of those games that I think I could recommend to just about anyone, provided you're on board with the premise of a relatively slow-paced atmospheric adventure. There is action in Inmost, but it's simple, minimal, and failure is not punished hard. Most of the game focuses on exploration, basic puzzle solving, and narrative sequences. If I had to compare Inmost to anything else it would probably be games like Limbo and Inside. If you enjoyed those, you'll probably like this one. Alongside the eerie, unsettling tone there are many gameplay sequences that focus on the idea of escaping or outwitting threats rather than combating them. Unlike Limbo or Inside, though, Inmost has an almost metroidvania-esque structure, with lots of shortcuts, secrets, and optional unlockables you can backtrack to as the game progresses. This gives it a bit more longevity, and a satisfying collect-a-thon sense of progression if you get bitten by the optional content bug.Really though, the main appeal of Inmost is the delightfully dark atmosphere and emotionally heavy story. It's a little narrative you can get sucked into over the course of a weekend that left me with a lump in my throat by the end. For fans of short, unique, story-focused experiences, this one is absolutely worth a look.
