_childDocuments_.review: It's interesting how film and even novels these days seem to become simpler and simpler and to have to spell everything out, while independent games seem to be where the bounds of storytelling is being pushed.  I'm thinking of things like The Cat Lady and Talos Principal (and even moreso its expansion) that leave with things to chew over.  This game provides you with three stories that seem unconnected at first and its only through the symbolism that you begin to see connections that become more plain at the end.  That is all good and it's also good that it's a pretty dark story in the end, if a little more complicated than it needs to be.What doesn't work so well is the gameplay itself.  You'll be working your gray matter way more on figuring out the story than on any of the puzzles in this puzzle platformer.  Additionally its irksome how slow all the characters move, and the knight's sections are just the worst of all.  I think the idea was that the girl's game is an adventure game, the adventurer's a platformer, and the knight's an action game, but there is zero skill involved in the knight's combat moves.  You just push the joystick right or sometimes left and mash the attack button.  And there are so many sections with him.  Every time the screen fades away from the adventurer portions, you dread how long you'll have to spend with the knight.  And it's not like the adventurer is all that inspired either, as I say it's all too easy.  The girl's portions are the best because they are the most focused on uncovering the narrative, but she moves the slowest of all, and that adds its own frustrations.So, yeah, compelling story, but poor gameplay.  I guess its up to you if you can put up with the one for the other.

_childDocuments_.review: An example of storytelling accomplished via the medium of video game. Definitely a dark story with jumpscares and traumatic events. While it is not overly gory in a visual sense, it certainly conveys brutality and death in a clear way. I'm not one for a bunch of blood and guts in my multimedia, and I am not much of a horror fan, either. This was "horror lite" in my opinion, which is about as much as I ever am interested in. If you're looking for something really extreme, this isn't it.In terms of gameplay, it's basic. There are three playable characters throughout the story, and while each has their own set of abilities, they each are very limited in their actions. Very, very light platforming. A lot of dragging or moving objects around to create a path forward. I am reluctant to say "puzzle-solving" because it really was basic to the point that "puzzle" may be overstating it. One character uses a sword for extremely basic combat. The game is, as stated initially, an example of storytelling accomplished via the medium of video game. It basically is an interactive book or movie. If you can pick up a controller and memorize 2-3 button functions, you can complete this game.So, it's a story game. Well? How is the story? It's a good, dark tale, albeit a bit hard to follow. Perhaps that issue was exacerbated by me playing more than half of the game in one sitting, taking a couple of months off, then coming back to it and finishing the rest in another sitting. I would recommend just spending an evening with the game and getting it all done in one go. You can definitely complete the story (not 100%) in less than 4 hours. I will admit that I searched "Inmost game explained" after the credits rolled because I was sure I didn't connect many of the dots, and sure enough, that was true. Thankfully, there is a really good write-up of the story among the top search results. I had understood the general gist of the story, but there were definitely neat connections and nuances that went over my head during my playthrough that I'm glad someone made me aware of, because it definitely enhanced the story.Overall, I paid $5.99 for this game and while it isn't my favorite game ever and didn't blow me away, if you are interested in a dark storytelling experience with entry-level "gaming" difficulty, this is worth a try.Certainly don't spoil yourself on the plot though, because truly, that's the whole point of the game. If you've already heard the plot, there isn't really a reason to buy the game, because you're not paying money for gameplay IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know where to start.This game is at the same time beautiful, horrifing, touching, devastating and uplifting, a true emotional rollercoaster without any breaks. For the first hour of the game I was thinking "Ah yes, the same family story I've seen in many other dark story-based games" but oh boy I was wrong - there are some twists and turns I would never expect.The visuals suprised me as well, it's probably the best pixelart I've seen in a while, greatly composed with the soundtrack. The environment is filled with details to the maximum and every area has it's own atmosphere related to current story events.What I totally didn't expect is how fantastic the whole gameplay is - every character has it's own abilities and flaws, giving you different feeling of the world - Child is small and vulnerable, having difficulties even with climbing onto objects, Knight is powerful and full of rage and allows you to move through areas without fear of monsters, which you have to outsmart as an agile, but fragile Wanderer. Each interactive object has it's proper weight, giving great feeling of how difficult it is for the characters to interact with it.An absolute must-play if you love story rich games. It is short, but the quality is worth it and the plot stays in your mind like after reading a good book. Instant nominee for story-rich award, but if I could I would also nominate it to best visuals and soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost is a beautiful puzzle / story game with an amazing atmosphere, plenty of frightful moments, and a cryptic story that is heartwrenching once you start figuring out what's actually going on. The atmosphere is good, but it can get in the way sometimes because since all items in a setting have a similar hue, so its hard to tell what is part of the background and what is an interactive object of the scene. Overall I think the art, animations, and music carried the experience.The story is...there? _childDocuments_.review: A rich man asked a Zen master to write something down that could encourage the prosperity of his family for years to come. It would be something that the family could cherish for generations. On a large piece of paper, the master wrote, "Father dies, son dies, grandson dies."The rich man became angry when he saw the master's work. "I asked you to write something down that could bring happiness and prosperity to my family. Why do you give me something depressing like this?""If your son should die before you," the master answered, "this would bring unbearable grief to your family. If your grandson should die before your son, this also would bring great sorrow. If your family, generation after generation, disappears in the order I have described, it will be the natural course of life. This is true happiness and prosperity."Well this is a story about grief, pain and family. Just for the story and the art it is well worth playing. I don't want to spoil anymore. Play it.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't love it. Steam says i have 3.7 hours into Inmost, and I've beaten it. the story was alright. I think it tried to be deeper than what it is. There is a sad twist at the end that was well told. The mechanics aren't always smooth, but it's playable. You switch between several characters to tell the story, and they all have different limitations, the knight can't jump, the man can't fight, the girl can't really do anything, and the old man can barely move. I think that's supposed to be an element of the story, but it wasn't for me. There are a couple points where you are chased by 'hunters.' I'm trying not to spoil anything, but i have to say at least the first instance of this is very abrupt and there is no guidance as to what you're supposed to do, I think I personally could have really liked this part of the game if it weren't so frustrating to me.There is a charming little 'evil' stuffed bunny that made me chuckle a couple times.The worst part for me was the final battle, you aren't a part of it at all, it's all a drawn out un-skippable cinematic scene. I think, had the developers added in even a few directional buttons or something, that would have gone a long way.The best part for me was, in the beginning of the game the enemies seem so strong, and you will die a few times very suddenly, it did have my heart racing at certain points. my final verdict is, it isn't a bad game, but it isn't for me. I believe I got it in a humble bundle or on sale a while ago, but for a game that was released in 2020 and currently retails for $14.99 I would be upset if I had paid full price for the quality and time it took me to beat itEdit: I forgot to mention the soundtrack! that was my favorite part of the game, it was actually so very good! I also saw another reviewer mention 'not for me, but there's talent there.' and i could not agree more. I do look forward to seeing what the devs come out with next. This wasn't my flavor, but they seem like a very competent budding chef.

But I still treat the thumbs system as "good/bad", like I'm sure plenty others do.Anyway, I draft my reviews as I play and I was going to give this a thumbs down.  Then I beat it and didn't feel right giving it a thumbs down.  So let's go over the pros and cons.Pros- Interesting story.  The journey is decent, the destination is great.- Game rewards exploration and attempting weird jumps (certain rewards are given for just doing sorta offbeat jumps you normally wouldn't think otherwise were relevant).- Quick resets on death. - Touching, even profound, narrative ending.Cons- Platforming controls could be improved.  If you press down+jump, "jump" still takes priority and if you have a ladder that goes up on a platform, but you want to drop down the platform, you'll climb up the ladder, rather than drop down the platform even if you press down+jump.  Also, game has ledge autograbs, which is fine.  But some ledges to autograb are placed in chase sequences or platforming challenges that they shouldn't be placed in.  Part of this problem is that you sometimes ledge grab in the middle of a platform, not even on a ledge.  Also, jump projections seem inconsistent.- Melee character can't hit multiple stacked targets.- Some puzzles are, like...too intuitive?  To the point where, as a gamer, you don't think to do certain practical things.  But in this game, you do them.  Sometimes.  Other puzzles are just a tad abstruse.- Drops are invincible to pickup for the first couple seconds they are dropped.- The little girl, who can barely jump, suddenly is able to .- A save didn't work apparently towards the end, making me have to re-do a level when I started back up.- Apparently has bugged achievements (per forums and even my own experience)Game doesn't hand hold, which is both nice and frustrating.  Whether it's figuring out where to go or realizing you can interact w/ environmental objects after you weren't able to previously...some things are both neat to discover and also like "wtf, why didn't the game make that more apparent?"But yeah...the ending saved this game for me.  There are obviously a lot of Cons on my list.  The game was unenjoyable at times, and I'm not a fan of environmental puzzles.  But the payoff was worth it, imo.  Plus, it's $15 and takes a half day to beat, so it's like, even if YMMV, why not take the risk?

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD:-music and sound effects.-art style and animation.-runs perfectly fine with Proton.-I appreciate the Steam page being upfront about the expected playtime; it was accurate.THE BAD:-Periods of pure tedium. Playing as the little girl and having to slowly move chairs and boxes around the house to find stuff. Playing as the wanderer and just walking down a never-ending corridor without nothing to see or do.-The puzzles are ok, except for the bells. One of the bells is hidden until you happen to walk over a particular spot, which is actually located above the area that the game has you drawn to. Why!? I spent 20+ minutes on that, when it should have taken 3 minutes tops.-Foreground scenery often blocks sight of enemies when playing as the knight. Especially the rats, which for some reason do more damage and are more tanky than any other enemy.-Only one of the three characters can jump. It makes sense that the little girl can't really jump, but then she manages to move a grandfather clock, an oven, and finally uses a crowbar to destroy a chimney! The knight, who can dodge and rapid attack with his sword, and zip about with a grappling hook, also can't jump...-Clunky controls and platforming, and slow movement. These are more than just frustrating, it's often infuriating.-Pretentious and confusing story. It was a convoluted mess of metaphor on top of metaphor. It wants to be somewhat of a dark fairytale, but it doesn't pull it off. It ends with a 10 minute cutscene that tells 90% of the story! I just couldn't care about any of the characters because we didn't learn anything about them until that final cutscene.-Strange placement of checkpoints. Sometimes they were so close as to be pointless, at other times way too far apart.-Playing as the knight is simply tedious. The combat is just dodge then attack, over and over again. Enemies spawn in around you all the time. You drop down or climb up a level and repeat. At one point I dropped down a level and was immediately swarmed by 8+ enemies. They killed me instantly, and the game kept respawning me at the exact same spot. It took about 15 deaths to get enough hits in to kill enough of them to break the cycle.-Almost nothing will be explained to you, so throughout the game I found myself confused as to what to do. The checkpoint system means that there's usually no penalty to trying and dying, but it can be frustrating. I don't enjoy it when games hand-hold you too much, but this game goes slightly too far the other way. A gentler introduction to the mechanics at the start would have been appreciated.-I think the Steam store page is misleading. The quoted review by EDGE featured on the page describes it as a horror game. I don't consider this anywhere near scary nor confronting enough to be horror. It states that you will "lure enemies into lethal traps". Hmmm kinda, but it's almost always just jumping over them as they leap to attack you, so that they fall over an edge. It also says "utilise your scythe, hookshot and pickaxe to avoid a gruesome end!". Your scythe is only to cut grass to reveal gems that let you buy more of the backstory from an NPC. The hookshot is just there because the knight can't jump, and so that's how he navigates the levels. And the pickaxe just gets you more gems and opens shortcuts back to the rest of the map you've already explored. Nothing interesting in any of these, they're just there to move things along. Finally, the store page recommends playing this on a "dark, stormy night". I took this advice literally, especially given the promise of "horror". But don't play this with the lights off like I did, because there's numerous times in the game where it unexpectedly cuts to a pure white transition/loading screen, and it was like being flash-banged!I played this in chunks. I kept getting so bored and frustrated that I had to take breaks. And this is not a long game at all. I forced myself to keep going back to it, because the reviews were so positive. I figured that it must get better, as people were raving about the story. I think people are over-hyping this one. It's just not that fun to play. Watch a playthrough instead. I really don't like to dump on indie games that have obviously had a lot of work put into them, but I think a lot of these reviews are unjustifiably positive. If they could have just taken a bit of mechanical inspiration from the likes of Trine and Cave Story, and upped the horror/thriller elements a bit, it could certainly have struck the right chord. Unfortunately, I think a lot of people will get sucked in by the art style and animation, and the promise of an amazing story, only to be disappointed. Consider yourself warned.[edited for spelling and grammar. no changes to the content or tone]

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be completely blunt. I did not like Inmost at all. It's not worth 20 dollars AUD at all and i would only recommend it if it was around 75% off AND you know what you're getting into. This is NOT a horror game. It is a narrative game with puzzles and horror elements. The first 20 minutes might make you think otherwise with an honestly awesome chase sequence but the game just goes downhill from there.What potential Inmost had in the first 20 minutes quickly dissolved into tedious, slow and often repetitious puzzle design as well as a pretentious and confusingly told story that tries to be emotional but comes off as overly sappy. Combat as the Knight is a chore and overly simple. Platforming as the Wanderer is fun but backtracking is constant and it gets boring. The girl has the most interesting side of the story but the most slow, tedious and boring puzzle design i've seen in a game in years. You know the types of puzzles that have an obvious solution and you just have to move some things around to do it? So there's no actual thought involved? Yeah, almost all of Inmost's puzzles are like that and i hate itInmost also controls fairly poorly for all characters in different ways, especially with ladders. It feels stiff but slippery at the same time if that makes any sense. The Wander controls the best but still gets stuck on ladders and has a annoying short forward jump for some of the platforming involved.The only reason you should play this is if the story interests you but it has it's own problems and I thought it has been done before and far better than here. It is so jumbled up and confusingly told at times that the ending literally just explains it to you through narration. So yeah i didn't like that much either.What DID i like? The sound design is brilliant and the music is well done. It really sets the atmosphere and the game is very good at immersing you. Playing with a good set of headphones is an absolute must. Soundtrack might be worth a buy if you're into that as well.Look i don't write reviews let alone NEGATIVE ones often, i only do when a game impacts me in some way. Inmost absolutely did by making me feel like i wasted my time. The game was so tedious overall that the almost 3 hours i played to beat it felt like 6 hours, and a game should NEVER make a player feel like this especially for 20 bloody bucks.Only buy if you desperately want a narrative focused game (have already gone through the GOOD ones on steam already) and ONLY at heavy discount.*EDIT*I did want to clarify on my completion time. Since a couple of others simply don't believe Inmost was that short.I completed the WHOLE story in that time, 2.9 hours, and have not gone back since. There is content left over in terms of finding the little hidden "pain shards" that you can use to get more lore on the world and you could get another 30 minutes to an hour of playtime just hunting these things down. I simply did not find most of them as they are not needed for main progress and in my opinion are too tiresome to collect with very little reward.Now no spoilers here either  however anyone who knows the ending to the game, and how it's explained by the narrator tells you, it's essentially pointless to find out more about the world. Now even if you DID want to know more i don't think going out of your way to complete MORE tedious puzzles/ scouring every corner of the game for little snippets of lore-dumps is at ALL worth anyone's time.I'll say it again. The STORY and MAIN GAME is less than 3 hours long. Unless you feel like hunting nearly worthless collectables for 100% completion. Which as you can tell by my main review i was very much unmotivated to do so. *

_childDocuments_.review: ((edit)) I've now completed the game, or at least, reached the end of the narrative, to give an idea of game length.I don't think it's possible to see this game and not become captivated by it's art style.  Even among the deluge of pixel-art games that we see these days, Inmost stands out from the crowd thanks to it's simplistic fidelity and exquisite use of lighting and animation.  It's attraction is immediate and no-doubt will form the primary appeal for many towards this game, but there is more to it than just a pretty facade.Inmost is linear in it's narrative and seems to exist as a device to tell you a story, rather than an environment in which to experience your own story.  You will progress, through puzzles and light combat, and through progression you will unfold the story.  There's very little punishment for failure, and persistence is the only tool required for narrative advancement.  Controls are simple but never less than they need to be, and never less than feels right for the situation.Whilst following the plot is a straightforwards event, there are collectables along the way, some more hidden than others, which can serve to unlock more of the background to the world - a dark fairy tale of pain and despair.Sound is minimalistic but always appropriate, and follows the game's excellent design.  It's immersive without ever becoming overwhelming or distracting.  There is some well-done voice acting, but it's limited, and mostly the story is revealed visually rather than audibly.Overall, whilst this is unlikely to be a game you will sink dozens of hours into, nor one that will constantly challenge you to improve your reflexes or your cognitive processing skills, it is nevertheless a worthwhile experience, beautiful and haunting, and I doubt anyone would regret spending their time and money upon it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna split this into 2 parts: storytelling and Game playStorytelling: I don't think this game did storytelling all that well. It makes NO sense until right at the end, where it gives you a 2 minute long cut scene explaining everything. You then have to go back through, pick up all of the previously obscure story references and THEN do you understand everything. The story doesn't feel like you learn it and are rather told it and then sent to find where it was.Game play: Slow. Clunky. Lots of the animations are slow, puzzle solutions are often hidden instead of you trying to figure out what each piece does, and most segments have little movement options (knight segments are mashy, the little girl segments are all in the same repetitive spot and are extremely dialogue driven, and wanderer segments are just you looking for off screen solutions). Also, since this is a puzzle game, most of the time spent playing wasnt playing, it was watching cutscenes.Don't trust the trailers. Most knight segments aren't even in the game and the description paints this out to be less metaphorical than it actually is.I will admit that this game has wonderful graphics and sound design, but i didn't enjoy the game as much as others.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game. The story is fantastic, the graphics are beautiful (even is everything looks likes its been crushed to bits), and the game play is also... pretty good... I'm one to focus more on the story and the art.Because this game is pretty short and made for one long sitting, hence the review at 3 hours, the game play was never a huge issue but definitely didn't stand up to the story and art. While I do enjoy how tight the movement is, when playing as one of the three playable characters, it feels cumbersome for the girl and for the man, it feels pretty good, but bland. As for the third character, they have their own set of actions that feel REALLY good. I wish there was a whole game where you got to play as the knight. i think that there is a healthy balance of time where you solve puzzles as the girl and man and fight monsters as the man and knight. Overall, the game play experience is good, just lacking in some departments. But what isn't their to say about the story? No spoilers, it's just really good. It'll tug at your heart strings, maybe even make you cry. You get invested in the characters pretty quickly, even though they aren't given names or much personality, and I think that this has to do with the art. The movement and motion of the character and the world around them looks so appealing -- and the scenery? Breathtaking. There is so much to say about this game, but to sum it all up; If you like story rich games that don't just give up the whole plot, gorgeous graphics, and a more cinematic game experience, I urge you to give this Inmost a shot. Sit down for an afternoon and just enjoy the game for a couple hours. You (hopefully) won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying I do recommend inmost.  Someone took a lot of time and effort into creating a beautiful little gem of a game and it deserves recognition.  This isn't the longest game or the most immersive but it's a decent little 5 hour one-and-done story.I also want to mention that I almost didn't recommend this game because it gets a little bogged down in its own theme.  There's a lot of metaphors here for bigger ideas and frankly, the game gets a little lost in those metaphors occasionally.  If it was intentional to confuse the player, that's fine but you risk losing some of your audience to frustration.  “What the hell is going on?” is a good question to ask, and can drive the player to discover more but when “what the hell is going on” turns into “ i'm too confused to care” you lose your audience.  I hope the developer continues to make games because they are a talented storyteller and I look forward to their next tale.

_childDocuments_.review: This Lithuanian adventure game made a well-defined start on my 2021. INMOST plays on the theme of loss, regret and hope in stunningly crafted, pixelated style. The story is split between 3 different characters at each environment, ranging between adventure platformer and 2D action gameplay.Pros:-    Exquisitely designed, pixel-based graphics.-    Well contrasted atmosphere for the story, which themes range between innocence, tragedy and bits of horror.-    The emotive yet powerful soundtrack brings up the pivotal story moments to a touching level.Neutral:-    Fragmented story and background, which makes more sense when it all comes together at the end.-    Metaphorical narrative may appear enigmatic or whimsical at times.Cons:-    Some parts require trials-and-errors in the 1st playthrough, like a certain chase sequence.-    Controls can get clunky more than often when navigating and getting over obstacles.Summary: INMOST is a narrative-driven, introspective adventure game with 2D platformer and a bit of action in the mix. I perceive the overall vibe of the game as melancholic and delightfully dark. Recommend for gamers that play more for the story than the puzzle challenges it provides.Song for the mood: Mesarthim - Absence, Pt. 2 (Atmospheric black metal)

_childDocuments_.review: Is it weird that I feel like this game could've been a bit shorter? I'm aware it's already pretty short, but some of the cutaway segments are just shallow metaphors that waste your time and could just be removed. Here's looking at you, knight. Still, with the visuals, music and overall decent story, it's quite an enjoyable experience, even if it's one that I wouldn't personally play through again, let alone get all of the achievements for. _childDocuments_.review: Inmost is a short and sweet game presented as a glimpse into how people take action in tough places. Great sound design and visuals carry the game all the way through, and the story gives you just enough to bite on for you to want to know what happens next. A great game to be played while relaxed in one or two sessions to take everything in. Recommended for those who want a solid game with a good story to unravel with it. More detailed thoughts on specific aspects of the game below.Sound Design;Sound design and music are the game's strongest components. Music is used appropriately and is both beautiful and impactful, complimenting and boosting the visuals accordingly. Map Design & Puzzles;The world that is fleshed out through the game serves its purpose well and adds to the mystery and intrigue of the story well. Finding and exploring new areas, and gaining information and a better view of the world is the strong-suit of the core gameplay. Puzzles and tasks very from acceptable to smart and rewarding. There is nothing that requires a supercomputer to figure out, but there's nothing dull and overly long weighing the game down either. Puzzles and tasks don't overstay their welcome and reward the player enough to stay engaging and feel accomplished upon making progress.Story;The story of Inmost is well crafted but somewhat understated. The underlying themes, dialogue, and message are nothing new or ground-breaking for any medium, and that's not a bad thing. The attachment formed with the protagonists, the pacing of critical information being revealed, the mystery of the real meaning behind it all, and the strong character moments sell themselves to the player well. That being said — The game does make the player ask "But what does it actually mean/have to do with everything?" and players who are not fond of that method of slow storytelling may not be as invested. However, the game gives you enough to piece together everything you need to know, and the tense segments of the game keep you wanting to play and see more.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: It could be a blast in other circumstances. 3 characters, with different playstyles, separate stories leading to one by the end. But hear me out - gameplay is dull as ♥♥♥♥.I wonder why this game has so many positive reviews. Yeah, the story is touching, full of symbolism and blah-blah-blah, but it is so tedious to progress in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: My main take away from INMOST is pain; but it is lovely that the story can evoke such response.Overall INMOST is a fairly simple game. Puzzles and combat are rudimentary, and though some of the control bindings are weird it is usually more that the characters aren't capable of much that makes things awkward. The knight segments are even more out of place. Despite this the game manages to remain engaging enough to tell its tale. It doesn't feel like you're just watching a movie while having to keep the play button pressed.The background art is wonderful throughout, while the foreground loses some of the beauty the visual distinction is important for gameplay clarity. Invisible collectables are very silly, and I can see the game being a bit of a struggle to play through again if achievements are your driving purpose.Comparisons to Braid are valid, the two do feel quite similar, and though Braid is a much more solid game I still appreciated my time with INMOST.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay was easy to understand and fun to play, with multiple achievements and characters that keep you in the game longer. The story was deep and it kept you guessing without making you confused. My sister and I actually cried while playing this. The art direction and music were brilliant. And the overall vibe of the game was spot on! In summary, this game is a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: This a very short narrative focused game, with simple gameplay, that can be finished in one sitting. It has some very beautiful pixel art, and a nice sound design.The story connects 3 characters with their own styles of gameplay, and probably won't end how you think it would, but that can still be picked up on pretty early on.go buy it i guess
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from the story, i actually enjoyed the gameplay part quite a bit. You have the contrast of the 3 characters each with different abilities. I enjoyed the 1st hunter chase scene, wish there were more parts like that.When it comes to story, no game so far left me with such an emotional impact, 10/10 on that part.Music and pixel art is gorgeous.All and all this isn't a very long game, if you care only about gameplay don't buy this, but if you want to enjoy a good story told in an interesting way give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: INMOST is a pixel art platformer. It is also tagged as a metroidvania game and while it does have some mechanics that could be considered metroidvania, I would like to note that it is first and foremost a story-driven game that’s still mostly linear. There’s no character upgrades, and combat is scarce and very simplistic. Nonetheless I enjoyed the gameplay quite a bit. The art style is beautiful and the overall atmosphere is well done.For the most part I liked the game. It was easy to get into, and it was easy to finish it in a day. That’s because it kept me interested in both the story and the gameplay, it wasn’t very challenging and because playtime isn’t that long. Even though it’s a new release I didn’t encounter any bugs other than some achievements not unlocking. As for the story, I liked the three different characters and settings. However, the ending soured my experience a bit. It felt a bit sudden and the final cutscene is quite long and there’s a lot happening, some of which I would have prefered to play myself rather than just watch it. Also, but that’s probably just me as most people seem to like the story, the game left me a bit dissatisfied storywise. It’s not a bad story but to me it's very similar to how other games tackle themes like depression, loss and pain, and in a way that just doesn’t seem to appeal to me. Leaving that aside I still recommend the game as I enjoyed playing it, it is beautiful and even though I ended up a bit disappointed yesterday, I found myself waking up wishing I could play some more of it today.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterclass in storytelling, a short but compelling game that really grabs the soul. It takes topics that you don't want to ever talk about and makes it so gripping that it makes it impossible to stop.The sound is fantastic, the story and themes are fantastic, the world is fantastic. If these things are important to you in a game then I cannot see any regrets picking this up.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Even though the game is only a few hours long and sports little replay value, INMOST delivered exactly what I expected from it. I played the demo a few weeks before the release of the full game, and I had high expectations for it. Nonetheless, I am happy to say that it delivered. It has incredible sound design, gorgeous artwork in the pixelated style that I among many other players adore, and above all else, a beautifully crafted and emotional story with dark twists at every turn. While I feel that $15 USD is somewhat steep for a game that only lasts about 3-4 hours per playthrough and has little replay value, I still recommend purchasing purchasing a copy if you enjoy this kind of game. The somber atmosphere combined with the beautifully crafted story made this an extremely enjoyable game and one I would recommend to players who want a more laid-back experience where you can calmly solve puzzles in a dark and mysterious world as the land's tale unfolds around you.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Had no idea what to expect, this was interesting and deserves some attention. Still confused with some aspects of the story after finishing the game, though the general plot comes together clearly towards the end. Inmost seems to have a positive message for a game with disturbing subject matter. Three play styles come up in this game (the core puzzle one being its strongest, with good controls and interesting movement). Characters are interesting (), and this game features some of the most expressive sprite work I have seen. Speaking to aesthetics, I don't think I have seen many games do pixel art mixed with more modern looking texture and particle effects, it looks good. Music is good but there are not many tracks, so it sometimes gets repetitive. The only key issue I came across with the game was a soft-lock (sort of, but not really, since you can reset a chapter), where . Otherwise, there were just things I didn't personally like much, such as the random invisible collectables that you must happen to jump into to collect. While these "pain" collectables (what a fitting pun) are not essential, it would be nice if the game primarily stuck to hiding items in chests and hidden passages instead. This is not a game I would try to 100% for fun. As stated previously, I didn't totally get the story, because it jumps between all these narrations with analogies/metaphors that sometimes seem to take away from what is being visually told by scenes and text (that part conveys the most emotion and meaning honestly, other than some concluding text towards the end). I didn't have a problem with the vocals themselves, but they did feel somewhat out of place (so did the knight). I kind of despised sitting through the , but at the same time, I believe that was done this way with purpose . Some tedious gameplay comes from the child character segments, given limited mobility and slow furniture pushing (though clearly the developer(s) thought ahead to avoid some exceptionally tedious furniture pushing with a fadeout animation, and that is much appreciated). This game is not totally flawless, I understand the negative critiques this game gets. However, it does offer a unique story-driven experience with a point to it. If you like puzzle platformers, this is probably worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Platforming, puzzles, combat, storytelling: Inmost attempts all of these... and does a mediocre job with all of them. The end result makes you wish you spent that time either playing a game with better combat, a more exciting platformer, a more interesting puzzle, or reading a better written story. Some games manage to fuse all these elements in a well designed package--not Inmost.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost is a story first, then a game. That being said, the level of interaction as a player is perfect, no more no less. You will feel how each pixel react to your actions (great animations btw).The pixel-art in this game is absolutely beautiful, the atmosphere is brilliant, that alone is enough for me to recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Lets make this clear. If you buy this game you do it for the atmosphere and the experience. For me it compensated for everything else so I recommend. But:Gameplay: After the part of the game we know from the gameplay trailer (ends with the first chase) it never gets that engaging again gameplay wise. It has its moments and is not bad but repetitive and because you will discover how you can die with zero consequenzes lose its thrill quickly. I even managed to temporarily skip challenges by jumping into my death ahead of the challenge and respawning on the spot speak behind it. I have to admit tough I love the dynamic of the movment even if someone could say the controls of it can be a bit sluggish.Story: The story is greatly symbolised and purposly withholds key pieces you will only get at the end of the game making it very exhausting remembering a lot unrelated and unfitting information until you can finally tie them together. The end comes in a long cutszene with even something like a boss battle you cant participate in any way. Not even a quick time even or so. Even though I enjoyed the cutszene I had wished for more. With all of that the game tried to convey a message about emotional suffering and actually is in need of a second playthrough so you can finally put everything into context while playing but for that it hardly was fun enough.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: I write this review with teary eyes, still grasping what just unfolded in front of me. Yes, I recommend it, very much so. But do know that this is not really a platformer or an action game or even a metroidvania. It plays mostly as the classic Out of This World and therefore is much more of a puzzle game. Gameplay-wise, it's a good game. But where it really shines is in its story and ambience. As the story slowly reveals itself, it's hard to avoid all the feelings that it brings. Specially if you're a mother or a father.Do you like games that make you feel? That might make you cry? That make you remember that we always seem to forget how to truly love those that are most important to us? Well, this is one of those games. Enjoy the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: The way this game conveys the story is through a atmospheric castlevanian like design that proceeds you through a bland and gothic reality. I can't believe how incredibly well narrated this game put through the abusive and complete depressing journey. This game is quite short and doing this the whole day will help uncover every piece you need...When I finished the game and did some more stuff to uncover the truth behind all of these events happening. A touching and sorrowful path I couldn't handle in every scenario put in front of me. When I reached the ending and concluded what needed to be done; Both my mind and my heart lost to probably one of the saddest stories I've come across in the past five years. I can't believe what I witness turned fantasy, into the reality of pain and loss. This entire game is completely relateable to my life and some aspects, especially the loss scene got me too badly. Chucklefish is one my favorite indie development studio's that continue to impress with the games I've purchased from them. Inmost became one of my most favorite metrodvania's of all time. I will come back every once or so to play this and continue reminding myself how I got this far, and how I can tell the same tale to the people I love once I've found my peace as well.I will give Inmost perfect scores on a personal occasion because this game needs to show exactly how narrative story driven games are suppose to be. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game; the art style, the music, the story - all of it is just so good. It keeps you in suspense and I love playing as different characters - each with its own respective feel, and mechanics. It kind of walks you through the puzzles, but overall I liked them a lot, and they felt very fitting with the overall game. I liked getting the little pieces of lore from each character and finally being able to put it all together at the end. I loved playing this and will play it again in a few months. 9.5/10 I very much recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part I really enjoyed this game. Nice to cuddle up with for a few hours.I died countless times because the whole ladder issue is clunky as heck. Thankfully, the game is very forgiving. You can't really *die*, you just get to try again and usually from a spot on the map that is really close so you don't have to slog through the same largish  chunk just to die at the same place. That's nice.I guess there is a story there but to me it seemed disjointed so I pretty quickly stopped paying much attention.For a few dollars (USD) I found it worth my time.Sometimes you just want to chill and stop frantically shooting things for hours on end.What I don't understand are so many reviews from people who cried, got sad, were moved by emotion. I don't mean to say the reviewers were not moved. I guess at my age I've lived though real life gunk so like I've resoled these themes over a few decades. But that's just me. 40 years ago I would likely have a different take.Whatever you do, at end game go make a sandwich or fry up a steak. Mow the lawn. Wash your car. Do laundry. You have plenty of time. Like super oodles of time. I think it was the longest wrap up I've ever witnessed. I mean thousands (yes, really) came no where even close. That said, there is a nice message there and I can understand why people have an emotional response. That's a good thing. If you have half an hour to spare.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie, not the best game out there, but the visuals, music and sound effects are really something. They complement each other as an orchestra that pulls you in for a couple of hours and tells a story of pain and a story of overcoming pain and living on. You don't keep playing for gameplay, but for the atmosphere and the narrative, which is hidden in the world around you. Everything you experience is just a shard of broken mirror which you pick up to build the real story which is hidden but in the end revealed. The synchronicity of events, switching of the tempo is thought out symphony slowing when you need to process emotions and escalating when the moment is right. Bit of calm before the storm, a bit of power, when you feel weak. Bit of joy in a world of pain.There are not many games or stories that pulled me in their atmosphere as Imnost. I could not stop but to finish it, even though there were moments I felt sad and it felt that it will be just too much if I'll continue. But in the most depressing moments the artistic brilliance comes in. There are pure moments of excellence when the game prefers to tell its narrative purely with music and animation, without reliance on words or text, these moments combined with amazing art I consider unique and immersive and adored how each strong moment was followed by very well though our moment of stillness so I could gather my thoughts before venturing on. In the end, I was surprised how such a depressing natural story can escalate into a hopeful spark showing something beautiful. Revealing the other side of the story and instead of leaving you with a heavy heart, elevates you instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Man this game is awful. I was so excited to play it. Not once during the entire playthrough do we ever learn any one of the characters' motivations or goals or why we're even playing this thing. It's so short, and many times during the game they just slow down the character's movement to drag out the play time. The art is really great and that is really the only thing going for this game. All the tool discoveries are inconsequential and contrived. The entire last twenty minutes is nothing but the game playing for you in an overly long cinematic that I eventually just quit (so I don't really know how long it actually is) since it didn't really explain anything anyway, and I hadn't played in so long I was bored out of my mind. Seriously, the end just makes the game more confusing and disappointing. It is so contrived, patronizing, dull, and underdeveloped I am actually angry at having played it.

_childDocuments_.review: Very sad and thoughtful game. I admit I had to google it to piece together the full story after finishing the game, but for me at least that didn't detract too much from the emotional experience. Overall I thought the game could have helped itself out a lot by making it more clear that various characters are distinct. _childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this sitting in my wishlist for a couple of years now and finally decided to grab it (and play it immediately, which doesn't usually happen lol). I managed to beat it in <7 hours while also working and taking breaks, so it isn't long or hard (TWSS) at all.That said, I only regret not getting/playing INMOST sooner! I was originally interested because it's absolute eye candy, especially for pixel art enthusiasts, but the story is the real focus - the gameplay, while perfectly enjoyable, is just a means to an end. There were only a couple of parts where I got even briefly hung up with the platforming/puzzles, but I had a great time exploring the (extremely well-designed) map trying to find all the little bits of lore tucked away behind hidden walls and floors (and managed to miss quite a few - might go back for them, maybe). The story, though - it's extremely well-told and well-crafted - a worthy star of the show, and well-accentuated by a suitably atmospheric score.One thing is that the game is pretty dark, as implied. You can piece together what's going on by paying attention and being thorough with your explorations, but the end caps it off in a very emotional way that I wasn't really expecting, and that was what got me, lol. No tears, but I came close! If you play this (which you should), be prepared for some feels. In my opinion, INMOST was definitely time and money well-spent! I only wish I had played it on a dark and stormy night as recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game but for me the story was kind of vaguely explained, leading me to not quite get what actually happened. Covers some really dark topics and a generally dark story, through indirect storytelling, using fantasy elements. A decent journey of 3-4 hours. The exploring and puzzles are pretty clever, and relatively straight forward. However, it is almost entirely uncorrelated to the actual plot, you're mostly just kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around in this fantasy world, then you're suddenly reminded that there's actually a story, you're supposed to follow. The post-game completion had me sort of look back at different things I did in the game, and just wondering "and why did I have to do that?" There's just a very clear divide between the storytelling and the gameplay, which often feel like they're in two seperate worlds and share little in common.For me the storytelling was hard to understand due to how it's executed, but at the end it helped clear up most but I still had to look online to find out what I missed. It's so vaguely explained and from looking through other reviews, I wasn't the only one who genuinely went through the game not quite knowing what was actually going on. Naturally since the story is quite dark and important I don't want to spoil anything, but I can say for example that I didn't entirely know how many characters there were, and how correlated they were. In fact, there was a character I mixed in with another, not knowing they were two seperate people! So don't blame yourself if you don't quite get what's going on, you're not alone!Now the graphics are easily the best element. This game is suuuuper pretty, so pretty I pretty much forgave it for it's odd style of storytelling, and playthrough of a world I didn't even understand how worked. It's definitely one of the better looking pixel-graphics games I've played in recent times, alongside Celeste (which I'd say this is prettier than) and Octopath (which I think is prettier than this though)6.5-7/10 would kinda recommend
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. What a story. Been looking for a dark story that makes me think, and a story that is not too obvious from the start. This is not some sort of Hollywood story where you can guess your way through all the acts. I had no clue what to expect next throughout the story, which is both good and bad. The bad part was that it felt a bit messy in the start, but the longer I progressed the more sense it made. Give it time, and keep progressing and it will all make sense.The controllers were a bit wonky while climbing objects when i used my PS4 controller. I wouldn't call it game breaking but a bit annoying sometimes.I would really recommend this game even though it's a shorter one. I finished it in 3.5hrs.Don't expect many hours of story progression if you buy this game. Expect puzzles and a great story.
_childDocuments_.name: INMOST

_childDocuments_.review: I sincerely enjoy stories like this one, tragic, yet has a hopeful twist. They do an excellent job with the atmosphere and music which does its part in enhancing the feeling that the various moments in the game are meant to provide. It's a short game, but honestly if you enjoy a metroidvania style gameplay and are looking for a good story then I 100% recommend. No spoilers, but i will say this is a rather grim tale and may not be enjoyable to those who dislike such things.All in all 10/10, worth the purchase.

It especially suffers near the end, where the story takes over entirely. But the payoff is very good, so I didn't mind.If you're OK with artsy narrative platformers, highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only spent an hour in this game, so my review may change.  Given that apparently the game is ~3 hours, I doubt it will.I'm not a fan of the story so far, but that's subjective and I haven't completed it anyway.  I don't know if I will, however, because the controls are .  The movement is floaty and clunky and feels overall unresponsive.  I regularly get stuck in ladders and have to jump off.  Every platform I jump to seems to be just a little bit too high so instead of jumping  platforms I'm constantly grabbing onto ledges and slowly pushing myself up.  I'm sure this is intentional as a lot of things in this game are slow.  There are "cutscenes" where you take control of another character, the first of whom is an old man who moves at a snail's pace.  This isn't inherently bad.  I don't mind it when games limit my abilities for the purpose of telling the story.  There is just this overall sluggish vibe to the whole game which is just not at all suited for a platformer.So far, the puzzles haven't been interesting or challenging either.  I'd say that if you're reasonably certain that you'll like the story and don't mind some mediocre (and sometimes bad) gameplay, get it on sale.  At full price it's definitely not something I'd recommend, even for the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game, and my heart is fairly wrecked. This is a deeply depressing game, but I'd say it was well worth the play. For a pixel art game, the developers went WAYYYY above and beyond editing the heck out of every last sprite, background, and character. It is beautiful how much detail there is, and it's beautiful in the most sad way. I do not want to spoil the story. As a trigger warning, this game depicts some brutal things. I'm a full grown man, and I wept at one of the scenes. There are several worth weeping for. This game depicts severe trauma in some of the deepest ways I have seen in a long time. It is smart, sensitive, yet doesn't pull back from how horrible some of the situations are that get depicted. There are moments of terror, horror, and suspense that all blend together incredibly. It almost feels healing to experience in a way. They managed to depict some things that are awful, terrifying, and horrendous, without feeling like it crossed a line. It doesn't ever feel like they did things strictly for the shock value like a lot of horror/suspense games and movies do. A lot of those things show equally awful stuff (or worse), but it is done so with such grotesque imagery that any intended message is lost. The purpose is to shock, and draw people in with the horror and fear. This game has shocking moments, but it depicts everything with deep tact and purpose to every action and experience. Having survived some awful trauma, I found that this game was not so much triggering as it was an acknowledgement of my own pain - I felt heard, if you will. I felt in some ways that this story was reflective of my own. I can't adequately describe it - experiencing the sorrow in this game allowed me to connect with my own. This game has touched me in a way - I am touched by the bravery of the authors, in that they were brave and bold enough to put something this sad, this painful, together. There is no way they could have done this without some brutally sad and painful experiences of their own. I love it. I love seeing art, and this is art. This is art at its finest, and it helps me to feel like its okay (helpful, even) to make brutally sad, painful art. Someone else made something so hard and painful to experience, and it has helped me to feel validated about the severity of my own experiences as a result.I am not sure I can give higher praise than this: thank you. I can connect with the experience you intended.I highly recommend this experience. It's not strictly a game, but an experience. Again, be warned that it addresses material that may be deeply upsetting for many. But for me, I feel moved and valued after playing this. Someone communicated their own pain, and I could connect with not only theirs, but mine. They get it. My sorrows are not without hope in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost is a pixelated platformer that weaves you through a series of tales slowly and does not disappoint on telling it. Although relatively short, if the player is involved in understanding the world of Inmost then they will surely agree by the end that it is a tale worth playing again to absorb all the details. Although I do not think of myself as one who likes storyline games, I found Inmost to deliver more than my expectations and evoke some of my own personal life through empathy (even if they are pixelated). Would recommend this game to really anyone who likes a rich atmospheric game with puzzles of all sorts.

_childDocuments_.review: This i by far one of the best story telling games i have ever played. Now, I'm not going to spoil anything in this review so I'll say as much as i can without spoiling it. This game is... well a masterpiece, ChuckleFish has been good at storytelling (look at starbound) in the past but this blows everything I've ever played out of the water. And I know I keep saying "the game is spectacular" and not explaining why and I have a reason for that. remember when i said i didn't want to spoil anything, this game is almost all lore and storytelling, most of the negative reviews say that they focused to much on telling the story that the gameplay feels like a cutscene and you're more or less along for the ride, i disagree (shocker i know). I admit, the game does focus a lot on the story telling aspect more then gameplay but I don't think that's a bad thing personally. One of the reasons I haven't been able to say much other then play this game is because of the fact that it's as story based as it is. one way or the other though as far as gameplay goes it's pretty straight forward. i didn't have to ask myself "what now" a lot of the time because at it's heart this is a story told through a game. I will admit, the story is a little hard to understand but after you look at it for a while and start to understand what's been going on you can see the true beauty the game holds.tldr, I can't say much because the game is story based and it's told better then anything I've ever played

_childDocuments_.review: Yeh for 13 quid i just expected more of a game. This could've been an interactive movie and I'd actually have been fine with that.The artwork is at some points very good but will flip flop back and forth, if you compare it alongside Blasphemous it's pretty apparent that the game engine lighting is holding it up. Animations and characters are very simple and basic while control over the character is very stiff which just gets tedious after a while.There is a bizarre mechanic where you have to pay for more story in the game currency. It's an interesting idea but in practice is very tedious. Nothing really drew me in during the first hour and for the most part the puzzles are very simple. There's nothing mechanically here that requires a lot of brainpower. Progress doesn't really entail much. Combat is ho hum, nothing very dynamic or really necessary honestly. _childDocuments_.review: Doesn't remember how much I actually paid for it, but 4 hours for game like this is actually a good length.This is a game about pain, and I really feel it, that's why after 4 hours, I had enough. The character takes fall damage, dies to most enemies in one hit, moves slow, and at times, forced to crawl slowly through some intense hostile environment.The weakness and vulnerability is fully evident. He can't attack, double jump, ground pound, he is just some old guy that stumble after doing one forward jump to narrowly avoid some shadowy monsters hunting him. He gets progression items that just feel like keys to unlock doors to new area, and helps him hunt for collectibles, he remain weak and slow from start to finish. So, this game kind of qualifies as a metroivania even if I feel it is more of a platform puzzle game.The map is small and interconnected, but divided into each section that require you to do some platforming and solve some environmental puzzle, such as moving things and breaking walls. It is nothing too fancy, but it isn't boring either. It is kind of satisfying how after unlocking door, everything will loop together and connect. But almost the entire map feel monotonous with similar type of aesthetic and enemies, not really have the wonder of exploring, and really get the message of endless pain across.The lore is messed up, Omori-level of messed up.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best pixel art adventure since Heart of Darkness (1998) and Another World (1991), Inmost is a love poem to the games of early ninties, such as Ecstatica, Alone in the Dark, Dizzy, Kyrandia and many, many others. However, Inmost gets all the best elements of those, such as thoroughly though-out, hand-crafted gameplay process, and mixes those with the comfort of a modern game shell.Again, praise to the animator and the artists! Every scene and animation is hand-crafted, pixel-by-pixel, frame-by-frame. Despite the theme of the game being bleak, the looks of the game world leave a cozy feeling, and such a visual treat, that you'll want to replay the game, just to enjoy the scenery (and some easter eggs left by the authors).p.s.Speaking of easter eggs, there are so many, I've lost count. Though, those are subtle and not noticable, unless you know the imagery. We're talking things like Banner Saga or Little Prince here ;-)

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna be honest, I was pretty disappointed. I think the game didn't really utilize the fact that it's a video game if that makes sense. There were far to many moments for me where I was upset I was watching a cutscene when I feel like I should have been playing or getting to interact with what I was seeing in some way. There were also so many times where I feel like everything grinded to a halt due to movement being kind of slow or even kind of clunky. Now all of that being said, I don't think that really matters a whole lot, because I don't think Inmost was setting out to be an amazing action platforming adventure. Instead, the game tells a sad yet very real story while having the player traverse through beautiful and haunting environments (that's probably why both of those adjectives are in the game description). _childDocuments_.review: An incredibly tedious game that has flashes of fun, and at the end of three hours I just found myself annoyed. Characters exist as vehicles for metaphor, providing nothing of interest or an urge to learn more about them.  I found myself referring to characters as "Oh No The Girl Again", "Old Man" and "The Knight" because nothing else interesting arose for them.  The Girl's storyline involved a "twist" that wouldn't have even been interesting had I been invested in her, but fell flat even harder because it was telegraphed from a mile away. The Old Man is the Metroidvania portion full of collectibles in nondescript locations, yet is still the most compelling portion of the game. The Knight is the combat demo.  It works but after the first two chapters or so it feels like you've fought every enemy you'll see through the entire game.  Even at 3 hours this game is utterly skippable.

_childDocuments_.review: "Puzzle platformer" is both a fitting description for this game's genre and, at the same time, barely scratches the surface of the experience Inmost provides. At first it might seem confusing and possibly a little pretentious, but the more I could make sense out of the background story, relayed in bits and pieces of information by multiple narrators (and not entirely reliable at that), the more I felt invested in the characters' ultimate fates, to the point that nearing the end I found myself begging for a happy ending......Well, to know if I ultimately got my little wish granted, you'll have to play the game. I really think it'll be worth your while.From a technical standpoint, graphics are lovely, as long as you can palate the old-fashioned, pixelly style (I sure do). Backgrounds and lighting effects are especially egregious. Gameplay-wise, the game might suffer a little for lack of direction, but it's nothing impossible especially if one had a little experience in adventure games and the like; if anything, it adds to the challenge and allows for a little longer playtime (game is a bit on the short side). Apart for that, I enjoyed the mechanic of having three different characters with wildly different skillsets (or lack thereof), allowing for a little extra variety. Not to mention that in a platformer based on puzzles and exploration, being allowed to play an unstoppable juggernaut such as the Knight repays for the patience and caution required when you're playing a little girl and an agile but mostly harmless man.All in all a pleasant gaming experience, with a story that gets really moving the more you get entangled in it. Thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: INMOST is a beautiful piece of art. I bought this game a day after it released and boy did it blow my expectations away.But, for the sake of not overthinking, I'll keep this quick.For myself, this game was a big thrill-ride. Full of intrigue and wonder, it had me coming back to it over and over again like reading a good book until completion.The game-play I found was very simple and engaging. It integrated with the cutscenes so smoothly that it felt as though I was playing the cutscenes themselves.I only ever found myself confused once when introduced to the wanderer's first puzzle only to quickly figure out the solution. So the puzzles I'd have to say that the puzzles excellently presented themselves in a fun-to-solve manner.Now the only con that I found in this game was the confusing save files, such as an undescriptive save menu and collective items not being saved across different points of the game. (P.S. there was an update after the game's release, so I'm not sure wether or not this was fixed)The story is one of the best aspects of the game in my mind. It's excellently carried along with absolutely amazing voice-acting, powerfully written dialog, engaging animation, a compelling music track, and well laid out pacing for the story.Now I am aware of some of the criticisms people have on this game and those criticisms are perfectly fine by me. This game IS slow-paced and emotional. It's full of slow burning mystery. The game is one big metaphor, a metaphor that requires YOU to think deeply to fully understand the main story and the game's message. And I personally enjoy this game FOR that REASON.If what you're looking for isn't this but something fast paced, long-to-play, or a horror game. This isn't for you then. The reason that I like this game so much and highly recommend this game, is that it tells a message that I wish more story-told media shared.Keeping these in mind, if you like slow-burning, highly emotional, heavily metaphorical stories, then this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: A very confusing game. The meta-plot is poorly told through the three separate interwoven game segments which all fail to properly hint at what the concept is meant to be. Even with that, there is little actually tying all the segments together in any sensible way, leaving the narrative fragmented and hard to reconcile. Up until the ending segment, I was confused. While the gameplay is solid enough and somewhat interesting, and the art satisfactory to excellent, the overall length of the game and its inability to cogently present its theme makes it very difficult to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding example of 'games as interactive art.'"Inmost" has some things to say about pain, trauma, suffering, compassion, connection, and ultimately, love. It could have been a walking simulator, but the decision to make it a platformer with puzzle and combat elements was brave and absolutely spot on. In a walking simulator, you're really just witnessing events; you're a passenger along for the ride. By requiring the player to provide the inputs, you're an active part of the story; not just an observer, but a participant. It's wonderful and makes the emotional response to situations and developments all the more powerful.The messages have more impact when you're in the driver's seat. Whether that's guiding the girl to confront her fear. Or directing the knight to 'attack' his 'enemies'. Or, as the middle aged man, wandering through the hybrid fantasy/real world (an amalgam of the girl's world and the knight's world), only to realize what kind of morass you're helping that character navigate. When they fail, you fail. When they're hurt, you're hurt. For games in general, this is standard presentation/projection. It's not even new that this kind of experience is offered in a pixelized format. What is a bit on the newer side is not only how accessible this sort of delivery is, but the fact that there is such a market for this kind of immersive, interactive art. That's... incredible. And quite welcome. For all the darkness on offer in this game, all it's blunt sadness and inescapable hurt, it's wonderful to consider how therapeutic it was. Not only from a production standpoint (i.e., for the developers to work through their own burdens or suffering), but to know that the end result had an intended audience, and that those players might also achieve a semblance of cartharsis by way of this shared journey. As corny as it may sound, "Inmost" and what it stands for is actually... inspiring.Pro tip: In the second half of the game, when the girl is having her tea party, and the game fades back into her room with no one sitting at the table, your game isn't bugged. The little girl is hiding under a table on the left edge of the screen and thus not readily visible. Because the controls aren't always as responsive as they should be, it might take a few seconds for her to appear once you begin to move her toward the table. If I can save anyone the heartache and time spent searching for prospective solutions to a bug that wasn't there, I mos def want to do so. ;-)Two thumbs up, 8/10. Recommended for: those who enjoy quick, pixel-based platformers; games with a message (and a heart); players looking for an emotional experience. Addendum: two points of unsolicited advice. Point 1) consider not hunting for achievements on your first play through. If you're an achievement hunter, the game is short enough (~4 hours) that it's unlikely to prove a huge timesink in order to 100%. Point 2): try to make your play through (especially your first!) in one sitting. Again, the game is pretty short, so this is unlikely to be a (haha) tall order.edit: clarity. or more precisely, the desire for clarity. delivery of clarity?  as always, that is in the eye of the beholder.

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite game of the year without a doubt. I was really hoping as the game was nearing its finale - that it would stick its landing - and it did. I love that rare feeling when an experience really fulfills you - and this game 100% did this for me. I am so elated I had to write a review straight after finishing it. I really enjoyed the story. Just beware as it deals with some dark themes - but does it it a way that is really uplifting. Despite the metaphoric language - the context was clear to me from approximately the half of the game - which opened the story for me and made the approach towards conclusion really intriguing. The music was haunting - absolutely stellar actually - and befitting the story beautifully. I would like to especially highlight game direction - I really felt like I am in a exceptionally capable hands throughout my whole experience. Kudos to all involved and I look forward to their next experience.I would suggest not looking anything up about the game - just to keep the experience spoiler free.I would say this game is mainly for players who enjoy great/emotive storytelling - as that is the strongest part of the game. There are also puzzles, combat and platforming in the game - but it is all secondary to the narrative. While I did not find most of the puzzles difficult - there were few which put a smile on my face and made me feel clever for figuring them out. Definitely don't go to this game for combat or platforming as while those are serviceable - those are not the main focus of this game. At around 6h - this has been a fantastic bite sized experience - and exactly what I needed. As many games these days do not respect players time and stretch over 30, 50, 100+ hours. Congratulations to the creators - big pat on the shoulder and hats off.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface with this: THE GAME IS AN ENJOYABLE EXPERIENCE AND WAS FUN, BUT THERE ARE REASONS WHY I CANNOT RECOMMEND IT WHOLLY. THIS GAME IS NO HOLLOW KNIGHT, NO ORI, NO BLASPHEMOUS, so do NOT go in with those expectations. Inmost is...a strange thing. It's not so much a game as it is an experience/interactive story. The gameplay itself is not very interesting with the exception of the Wanderer, but that gameplay is still a far cry from being anything incredible. The story is interesting. It is very intricately woven and drowned in symbolism to the max. I don't typically enjoy these kinds of stories, but the fact that there was a 'game' to play along with it probably made Inmost an enjoyable experience for me. It's a very nice tale that takes a lot of brain whirring to understand.However, the game is too short. Far too short. I beat it in basically 4 hours if you don't count my time spent AFK. Personally I don't really think this is worth $15. I bought it at $12 and while I don't feel ripped off a la Halo 3: ODST (which is still a masterpiece btw, just not remotely worth $60), I do feel I overpaid for this experience. A saving grace to this, however, is that you could think of it as paying $15 for an IMAX movie; maybe then you won't feel like you overpaid for Inmost.Overall I would recommend Inmost to people. It's a fun and enjoyable experience. It is very unique and interesting to the point that, again, I wouldn't really call it a game. However I do not think it is $15 or even $12, but instead something closer to $5 to $8. If money is not an issue, however, then I would 100% recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Inmost is a fairly enjoyable game, that I would recommend to anyone interested by the trailers they've seen. It mostly delivers on its promise of a moody, atmospheric, and somewhat emotional allegorical journey through trauma. Sadly, it is let down in some ways that prevent it being as memorable or impactful as it could have been.The gameplay consists of three characters with different mechanical sets; a point n' click, a puzzle platformer, and a power fantasy leaning combat focused character. Each has ties to the others, and each feels completely distinct as characters and in action. It is certainly interesting seeing these representations and discovering their backgrounds. However, where the game falls down is that it never ties these representations back to the actual 'real' people the story is about in any cohesive way. They're too distant, and true story and message seem slapped in to try and make everything make sense. It doesn't work well. Still, can't fault them for trying, and it doesn't stop the game from being worth a play. You'll likely just be left feeling like you almost played something very special.

The map was easy to navigate and I didn't find backtracking to be much of a pain. Some people blasted through this game and complained about the challenge, but that's not why I gave this a thumbs down. I found the puzzles to be easy, but the puzzles were not the main attraction imo.This game really suffers from the story.  It was like running on the beach, fun for a short time but holy hell does it get exhausting after a while.  Please guys, LESS IS MORE.Edit: Steam says I don't have the achievement for completing the final scene. Oh, believe you me, I watched the entire thing which felt like an hour and I even sat through the credits, so unless there's ANOTHER scene after the credits, I'm not sure why I didn't get that achievement. And I am NOT sitting through that again.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game--the description and promised mood was right up my alley, the pixel animations are dripping with love, it played well on the Deck--but, for me, it wasn't a fun game to play. I DNF'd it and I almost never do that with a short game (though I felt this was longer than a "long evening" length game.)I got stuck two hours in on a late-game scene with an aggressive tar critter, some lampposts, and insta-death. I know I could post in the Discussions or look up a video guide (though YouTube won't run on my deck currently) but I realized...no. I'm not having fun. I don't want to spend any more time on it. Doesn't help that two of the three characters you play as are quite slow and not maneuverable. I liked the way the Knight played and probably would have enjoyed a completely different game (and genre--like a Metroidvania, or straight 2D platformer basically) based around his movements...but yeah. The majority of the time, you're slow, you're defenseless, and the story was too oblique for me. And I'm a fan of, like, RUSTY LAKE games and other thoughtfully-paced spooky games, so that's saying something, I think.
