_childDocuments_.review: Meh.Got this mainly cause the art style looked pretty unique and distinctly creepy, and while that mostly holds up, I was mostly just bored throughout the game. It's very story-focused with platform-puzzling - makes me think of a cinematic Limbo - but the story didn't engage me because it very much falls into the realm of the stereotypical 'arty indie game" field, i.e. the real story is layered in loads of metaphor.But the total lack of actual surface level and hyper-focus on what everything represents made the framing as a creepy trek through a grim, winding castle feel more and more like a slog as the game went on. The gameplay and story just don't feel very tightly interconnected at all - they're each an interruption to the other.There's some merit in the puzzle platforming, but I never particularly struggled except for on one puzzle, whose nature made it more frustrating and unclear than brain-teasing. The one exception which does tend to be challenging are the monster encounters, which do have some satisfying ways of resolving them, but too often descend into annoying trial-and-error.Also notable was that there was one puzzle where I had to reload a save, because I pushed an object farther than the game expected, couldn't pull it back from the ledge, and therefore broke it, so they're not exactly tightly designed.But even were the gameplay perfectly done, Inmost is so story-centric that I wouldn't be able to recommend it on that alone. And I *adore* story-centric games when it's actually done-well, but the story feels so utterly lacking in involvement on the player's part - as most clearly emphasized in the ending, which is a several-minute ridiculously long-winded cutscene in which the game basically just resolves itself with no input on your part. Even the art style started wearing down on me after a while, because literally everything is blue. Blue, blue, blue. It's visually tiring, so to that point the shorter length is probably in the game's benefit, because it might've put me to sleep.I don't hate the game - far from it, it's very competently made and has the odd really effective moment - but I was so utterly unengaged for most of it that, for all the game tries to be deep and meaningful, I can't see it sticking in my memory for long as much more than a loose disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: is an example of how important honesty can be for a game concept. Because despite being deeply allegorical,  doesn't feel concieved - instead it's fully genuine and humane. It feels like the developer is weaving the elements of his creation out of the fibers of his own painful experience. Every half an hour of the game I though that in my review I would condemn its fantasy-ness, its grimness, its abundance of drama, its lack of measure when dealing with painful themes - and I just couldn't bring myself up to do it.  won me over. All of the things I mentioned still stand, but it doesn't matter - because the game is honest. is not a platformer so much as a miniature metroidvania. It's a very story-centered handcrafted game - and that defines its design. There is no emergent gameplay, every mechanic is one or two-use only, the locations are small, the combat sections are no more than serviceable - and no more than serviceable they need to be. At the same time the game world is insanely detailed, almost all encounters - including the enemies - are unique, the animations - especially for the protagonist - are fantastic, and there's so much responsiveness in the movement of the character. You can interact with almost anything in the world - and for every interaction there is a specific animation. If you're a pixel-art conoisseur,  is a must-play.A great achievement, especially for a two-man team.

name: Relicta
detailed_description: Relicta is a first-person physics-based puzzle game where you need to creatively combine magnetism and gravity in order to unravel the secrets of Chandra Base. Alone in the treacherous depths of the Moon, your scientific mind is the only thing that can keep your daughter alive… Play as a top physicist stranded on an eerie, derelict Moon base. Find your way around the enigmatic, terraformed craters by bending gravity and magnetism to your will in order to solve physical puzzles. Will you rush straight ahead and try to reach safety - or will you take your time to gather clues and unravel the intrigues of 22nd century orbital politics? Buried in the eternal darkness of the lunar craters lies a secret that might claim your daughter’s life - or change the fate of humanity forever. Are you ready to face the ultimate consequences of your research? Features: Mind-bending mechanics - alter gravity and magnetism at will. Complex physical puzzles - combine your abilities in innovative ways to solve these physical riddles. Lovingly detailed environments - each corner tells a story, each new step is a challenge. Deep and enigmatic background story - Find clues and piece together the details about the investigation of the Relicta's anomaly. Immersive original soundtrack - slip into the soundscapes of an sci-fi psychological thriller.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Relicta is an enjoyable, if not occasionally frustrating first person physics puzzler that I would recommend if you are a fan of the genre or you like pretending you are Magneto by surfing flying boxes using the power of magnets and levitation. As a disclaimer: I would recommend anybody who plays to cap their framerates at 60 fps to avoid issues with boxes not flying in the correct trajectories, as 60fps seems to be what the physics were tuned for. This will probably save you hours of frustration, softlocks and restarting if my experience is anything to go by. There are also DX11 and DX12 versions of the game, but I'm unsure if there is a difference to gameplay.The puzzles are a mixed bag, where the good largely outweighs the bad. There are a lot of clever puzzles in this game that require experimentation and cumulative understanding of the game's physics. Only a few puzzles felt like a breeze to complete first try. The bonus puzzles added after release are even more challenging. This is partly owing to the design but also to the annoying length of some puzzles in the game, especially the last two levels of the main game. The lack of checkpoints in the middle of lengthy, multi-staged puzzles, combined with the occasional instances of softlocking do bring down the enjoyment of otherwise nicely designed sequences. They are still fun to play.The story is quite prevelent in comparison to other puzzlers in the genre and I found it to be a nice backdrop to the puzzles, the player receiving an update after every puzzle or so. During the second act, the story starts to drag and the characters started to feel less realistic, but it picks up again towards the end and reaches a nice conclusion, depending on your choice. The VA is well done and makes the dialogue feel believable. Some jokes made me chuckle while others made me wince a bit. If you're not into the story, the game wont force you to listen as most of the dialogue and cutscenes are skippable and your enjoyment of the puzzles wont be diminished.There's a lot of content here to keep your brain ticking and its worth the price, especially if on sale, considering how much time can be sunk into launching boxes and standing on switches. I think this game stands up on its own merits, that being said, there are plenty of other, better, FPP games to whet your apatite if this is your first foray into the genre.Regardless, I would recommend trying out the demo if you're unsure about picking this up.TL,DR: Nice puzzles, the narrative is nice and fun, just make sure to cap framrate at 60fps.

Also after a while maps just became all about clustering a lot of things into a single zone or making a single puzzle consist of multiple zones. So again, the difficulty wasn't really solving an interesting puzzle, but trying to see through the mess of options you have in your face.I's a real shame.

_childDocuments_.review: pfffiuuu, just finished the game and man... so many things in mind. First of all great game, so many ideas of puzzle rooms. Might not be recommended for those who are reluctant to mid to hardcore puzzle games. Now, concerning the mass of puzzle rooms, a certain number are very good and well thought. Others are made complex to look like they are complex just by hiding some perspectives or making some objects not noticeable. To give an example, there is a puzzle room in the jungle where I spent hours either because an object was blocked and I had to reset, or because I did not see an element hidden in the field and I progressed without having this element activated.Also, the physics of the objects made me solve puzzles in a way that would not, I guess, have been expected by the developers. Usually, I do not really care, but when you accomplish a puzzle that took you quite some time, you are satisfied, but the reward from the game is just a discussion between the protagonist mostly based on swear words... you are just in a hurry that they stop talking. _childDocuments_.review: Seemed fine, but gets increasingly more annoying as the game progresses.This is a puzzle game, there are several principles that you DO NOT break:1. Dont hide parts of the puzzle. So many times I've found out that HEY THERE WAS A PANEL BEHIND THAT BUT I CANT SEE IT.2. Dont put mechanics that only serve to screw the player. "Look, there's a corner here with a green screen. Why? To trap your box and force to reset your progress."3. Make sure your mechanics WORK ALWAYS, not just sometimes.This game breaks all of them, much to the frustration of the player.The story is bad, and only serves to make the game longer. The lobby sequences are unnecessarily big and confusing. Something should only serve to take you to the next puzzle is a maze itself, with many long corridors and unnecessary travel sequences.AVOID

_childDocuments_.review: is a linear, first-person puzzle game similar to  and .  Both its puzzles and its story are decent, though there is a sense of disconnect between the two. The puzzles are numerous and grow to be quite difficult, which dramatically slows the feeling of progression, and the existence of the puzzles themselves holds a somewhat flimsy connection to the story, making the gameplay feel disconnected from the narrative.  Taking AFK time out of the equation, completion took me 15-16 hours — 6-8 hours longer than I would expect from this type of game. Relicta's gameplay will likely feel familiar to those who have played the aforementioned similar titles; it features a first-person perspective, device for manipulating the environment and objects, and an ever-present A.I. to talk to between puzzles.  Players cannot die or suffer ill effects.Aiming and moving feel smooth and precise, if a little restricted.  On occasion, a puzzle segment could be solved or bypassed if the player character were able to simply crouch or climb, which is potentially a bit immersion-breaking.The core mechanics are the ability to change the polarity of certain objects to repel or attract each other, and to remove the affect of gravity on cubes, allowing them to fly through the air —  sometimes with you riding them.  It's a system that often requires players to think several steps in advance, in order to get the cubes and themselves past the myriad of obstacles present.  Various new environmental mechanics such as barriers and mobile platforms continue to be introduced right up to the end of the game.In the latter half of the game, puzzles quickly grow more complex, to the point of being a convoluted mess at first glance.  On occasion I found it easiest to find the end goal and work backwards to discover just where I was supposed to start.  These puzzles take some time to complete, and often the reward for doing so is a three second walk to another, equally complex cluster of cables, buttons and barriers.  This is where my biggest issue with the game begins. Though I don't mind a challenging puzzle, doing several complex yet very similar ones in a row with little in between begins to feel repetitive and tiring, and made me want to play the game in short burts.  Now, that's fine when the game is just a casual puzzle game, but  is a linear story game, and I feel the density of gameplay content halts story progression significantly, as the puzzles contain little relevance to the narrative.  For this reason, as well as the complexity of many of the later puzzles, I think the game's pacing and accessibility would be improved greatly by relegating many of the levels (harder ones, especially) to optional content, making the story experience smoother and less repetitive. Set in a near-future sci-fi moon base featuring several distinct biomes,  offers great visual variety.  Working in various craters near the base, scientists have created small natural biomes on the moon, including lush jungle, tropical beach, arid desert and more.  Though these areas are beautiful and distinct, their differences don't really translate to gameplay.  The base itself, which players travel though between puzzle sections, is a great piece of design, with extensive decorative objects and equipment, beautiful natural features blended with the architecture, and a very high level of detail overall.  I wish I'd got to spend more time there, interacting with the environment. story is told through the eyes of Doctor Angelica Patel, one of a small team of scientists occupying a base on Earth's moon.  The base was established by a previous group, and contains a strange alien artefact known as the .  Using scientific knowledge gleaned from this artefact, the past and present scientists have created technology far beyond humanity's current level.  An example of this is the gloves that allow Patel to manipulate her environment in the ways described above. The existence of the gloves and puzzle tracks designed to test them is briefly explained, but has rather an odd fit with the rest of the story.  Every one of the biomes connected to the base features a puzzle track, which is apparently the only way to navigate them, even when there's a vital piece of base infrastructure — such as a generator — at the other end.  Invisible barriers also prevent any deviation from the path.  Things go very wrong for the protagonist throughout the story, and she constantly needs to be at the other end of a puzzle track.  Conveniently, the tracks are all unable to be switched off for some reason or other, forcing her to complete every one in its entirety.Besides Doctor Patel,  features a few other voiced characters, and I found the voice acting, story telling and characters to be of pretty high quality, barring the protagonist having some dumb moments occasionally. The humour is good, and I enjoyed many of the exchanges later in the game.   manages its time well by focusing its efforts on a small number of characters and relationships.  Unfortunately, dialogue would sometimes be cut off by moving into the next area too soon, causing me to stand still and wait to make sure I heard everything, rather than getting started on the next puzzle. Some of the biomes feature decorative structures or features that cannot be reached due to the invisible walls, but would be ideal places to find collectables.  This would also offer a short break and some variety between large puzzles.  A missed opportunity, I feel. As pretty as the natural environments are, it's the interior of the base I loved the most.  The combination of clean, neutral surfaces, vibrant lighting and themed displays such as planters and animated equipment sets a great scene. The game's loading screens feature nice art, too. Using the specs listed above, the game ran at a steady 60fps on max settings.  It would occasionally hang for a brief moment, but this was rare enough that it didn't bother me. features a nice, high quality soundtrack, with quite peaceful, if slightly sombre music.  Sound effects are crisp and of high quality, though the lack of footsteps is a little odd.  My only real complaint is that the intro movies when starting the game are not affected by the volume sliders, and cannot be skipped to avoid the problem.I did not encounter any issues worth mentioning; the game is well polished. is a game with a good story and challenging puzzles, but the two don't interact very well, and it can get quite repetitive.  Those who typically have trouble with puzzle games will want to think carefully about this one, or use a guide.

_childDocuments_.review: how can this game have such review scores?+ nice graphics- wasting your time walking and moving back and forth in bland soulless corridors- has some bugs like glitching cubes that wont react anymore to your input- non elegant puzzles that instead of making you feel clever are just easy but long and make you walk a lot with no meaning to it other than to pad gameplay time- copying other puzzle games elements with no reason without understanding why those elements worked in them- janky puzzles + sometimes not putting save points that makes you restart the level because of some janky puzzle that gets stuck- bad choices in telegraphing interactivity and inconsistent meaning for colors - if you're going to put a story to a puzzle game , at least try harder to  give some plausible excuse for why your character keeps solving those puzzles this is one of the worst puzzle games of that type that I've played , before you waste you're time on ityou should first play games that actually have a soul like:- portal 1 & 2- The Talos Principle- The Witness- Antichamber

_childDocuments_.review: This game suffers from several issues that would require massive overhauls to fix. As it is, I definitely don't recommend the game for puzzle fans nor for people looking for a good story. There's none of that here.Puzzles in Relicta are very repetitive. The progression feels incredibly slow due to the fact you're doing the exact same thing for multiple test chambers straight, only in different biomes.Everything boils down to manipulating cubes to push a distant button that opens a door. It's all you do in the game: grab a cube and gravitize it red/blue/yellow, so it moves where you want it to move. In the latter half of the game a new mechanic appears every 10 levels, but it also involves transporting cubes, just in a different way. Cubes, cubes, cubes. Everything is cubes.The more you play, the longer the levels become. They're not getting any more difficult, just more tedious due to increased length and complexity. Instead of using the mechanics in a inventive way, the puzzles require more cubes to press more buttons, and the test chambers are visibly split into multiple independent sections. You don't need to think harder, just need to repeat the actions you've already done a dozen times or find out the order by walking around the huge areas over and over.To further increase the artificial difficulty, the cubes you need to solve the puzzle are sometimes hidden around the test location, so you need to scout the area before attempting to solve it. This is a learned skill in Relicta. If you don't look around first, you'll repeat my mistake of flying on a single cube, wondering what the hell to do, until you notice there's another cube on the other side of a tall structure. Since getting these cubes is trivial, they could just as well be provided from the start without making it so difficult to spot them. What a terrible puzzle design choice.Finally, the worst thing related to puzzles: You aren't really sure if what you did was correct. You could even be doing the right thing, but due to physics engine tied to framerate, it might not work the first two times and only pass if you try again. You could be surfing a cube across the map and get stuck, because the developers didn't think of this approach. You never know for sure.The voice acting is equally poor. I don't mind hearing non-native speakers communicate in English, but their dialogues aren't believable; no cutscene evokes any emotion other than pity for the poor actor that had to use an expletive again.What's more, the characters constantly "interrupt" each other. I'm putting "interrupt" in quotation marks, because what's happening is a character stopping mid-thought, , and another character saying something. This is happening Every. Single. Time.This feels fake, and since all dialogues are littered with these "interruptions", every cutscene becomes a pathetic exchange of detached sentences instead of a genuine conversation. It breaks all the immersion that the content of the dialogue could have built.Every location is either an enormous hub, a long tunnel that's roughly 16 washing machines wide, or an "open" area.Oh, look, quotation marks again. Why "open" and not open? Because there are  surrounding most places, and they're placed in such bizzarre spots that it's the funniest part of the game. In one place the character could literally jump down six feet and they could exit the level. But, ha ha! The developers are smart! There's an invisible wall preventing you from doing that. This joins the list of things that prevent Relicta from being believable.An inviting house on the beach? Can't get there, there's an invisible wall. A fork on the road? Can't go left, there's an invisible wall. A literal wall made of rocks? Yeah, there's an  invisible wall in front of it, just in case. It's hilarious.Absolutely don't waste your time playing Relicta like I did. It doesn't respect your time, doesn't test your wit, and doesn't reward your efforts with a good plot.Avoid.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this. It's very close to be excellent but they just didn't quite nail the very nebulous "good puzzle design" issue. I think the main problem I had is that the designer(s) treated every new level as building on all previous levels, not just conceptually but also mechanically. Almost every new puzzle mechanic, once introduced, is used in all future puzzles. And the game is long, easily twice as long as it needed to be. As the number of elements in a puzzle space rises, the available interactions go up exponentially. So by the end puzzles are these sprawling spaces with dozens of potential next steps to prune through which makes it feel more like random fumbling a lot of the time, as opposed to the sought after "a ha moment". Add to this that the mechanics are very "fiddly", you're often going to need to launch one cube off another an angle but there nothing in the game which snap it to the right place, you just have to eyeball it. It's very common to have the solution in your head but spend 20 minutes just wrangling the pieces into the right alignment. If they had made each segment about half the length and focused things to build reasoning skills about the game's world rather than just laying mechanics forever I think this could have been a real winner.All the above is really a shame because the 3D art, lighting effects, sound, etc all completely gorgeous. I see in other reviews that some found the characters annoying and while I can see how they would rub some the wrong way, I really liked them. It felt like a very "real" set of people, more rough edges than sci-fi usually shows (swearing, being sarcastic, having an unpleasant phone call with an ex). The ending is a bit "and then it was over" but it does the job nicely in the context of a Portal-a-like lightweight story.If you get frustrated part way through (I made it almost exactly halfway and then rage quit on one extra fiddly puzzle I had to completely restart 3 times), there's some excellent YouTube videos of the whole thing you can just blitz through to see the mechanics that get added and watch the ending, it was a much better way for me to experience the game and it might be for you too.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is a puzzle game and actually the best one I have played since Talos Principle.My reviews always represent my own opinion. I am not a reviewer / curator who plays/idle each game for 30mins then writes some crap about the game. As you can see from my playtime (and achievements) I finished the game, created videos, guides about the game so I experienced the whole content. Additionally, feel free to check my reviews, I have negatives on “games received for free” if that is what reflects my opinion on that game..As usually, I don’t want to reveal too much of the story. You play as a female scientist on a moon base who is trying to find the secrets of an alien object. That object, the Relicta is actually a living entity and slowly infiltrating your mind.Game includes 9 different puzzle areas + the 2 tutorial areas. That means about 50 different puzzle locations without the tutorial levels. Each area includes new mechanics so the game never gets boring, it stays refreshing, interesting and keeps offering new challenges. You also need to be creative, you need to think about all you could do while you use magnetism effect and anti gravitational effect on the cubes. The new tricks are not shown to you in every single area.Update April/May 2021: Game has now 2 extra story, each with 12, hard levels. These levels very challenging, complex and long, literally doubling the playtime Relicta offers.The perfect game is not existing. Every single one, even good ones has some minor issues or something we dislike in it. For me these were:-between puzzle areas you can explore the moonbase. However, these areas feel empty. Yes, there are collectibles for some lore, but still, these areas are a bit boring.-physics puzzle games will never be perfect. My cube levitates to one direction while it has a zero gravity effect on it, then hits a wall. Shouldn’t it start to levitate to the other direction because of the force it had by the collision to the wall? Well, I believe that would make a game extremely difficult and more random and this is why more logical puzzles, like Talos Principle will stay better, even if just slightly.Relicta is great. It will train your brain. One of the best puzzle game of 2020 for sure, definitely worth its price. If you love puzzle games then this is a MUST TO PLAY. You probably won't remember the solution of all puzzles, so perhaps replayable once, but such games usually are not good for replaying. Perhaps after a few years...  Characters look cute, enemies have some nice graphics too, it is a visually pleasant game. The best part of the game. Physics based puzzle games always have some minor problems, RNG in executing this, this is not an exception but it is close to perfection.  Some say accents on characters are bad. I quite love it actually. It is totally understandable, clear, but also gives some charm to the characters. English became a global language but I believe 80% of humanity, or more speaking it with accent, me included, so negative reviews just because of this is just another clear sign of the anglo-american imperialist suppression. Some puzzles hard to figure out, but if you like puzzle games then you should be able to figure out each of them. Still stuck somewhere? Then check out my walkthrough where I also explain what I'm doing during puzzles so you can solve it easily. You can find timestamps for the playlist in my steam guide:Perfection time: 40-50h+. ~20h first playthrough on main story (without guide, hints, walkthroughs), then +X hours you need to finish the 6h speedrun achievement. It is not that hard actually if you skip cutscenes and you go to the menu at each puzzle start and refresh your memories on that puzzle by checking my walkthrough video. About ~20h more for the 2 extra stroies added to the game during April 2021, less if you follow a video (my guide has vids for these levels too).There are also collectibles in the game and you need to get them in a single playthrough, all listed with screenshots in my steam guide: Only the main game has missable achievements, the extra missions has only storyline related achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, the puzzles have been nice but fiddly and somewhat clunky. They may devolve when physics and timing become more of an issue in later puzzles - even in these first couple of hours, I've often had to perform the exact same maneuver several times to get a cube in the right spot due to the fiddly physics. It's been a good challenge nonetheless and I can see the appeal of all the puzzle mechanics. The things that really broke the game for me were the story, characters, and save system. The main characters are supposed to be mature, high functioning scientists, and yet it seems what they do all day is bicker at each other. The story itself doesn't fit the puzzles at all. You have to undergo urgent rescue missions and whatnot, but you get stuck behind these puzzles for hours at a time and the story essentially has no acknowledgement of the time spent. In terms of the saves - the game only autosaves between puzzles. Sometimes puzzles can take a long time to finish and are essentially segmented into multiple small sections. Due to the physics, sometimes you can accidentally push a cube back into a previous section and have to redo everything. I think the game really needs manual save slots.I also didn't see the point in all the collectables lying around in the zones in between the puzzle areas - it seems like they were just added because other games have collectables. One of my other complaints is the large size of these in-between zones.  If not for the collectables, they could have been shrunk by probably 90% or more. If you're just looking for a game to scratch that first person puzzler itch, Relicta will probably be a good choice albeit a bit more clunky compared to other titles. For me, at least, the overall cohesion between the puzzles and the story just wasn't there, so I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended with caveats. Relicta is in the same class of physics-puzzlers as Portal, Talos Principal, Antichamber, etc. If you liked any of them, Relicta definitely belongs on your wishlist... but not at the top.Relicta has a huge number of fun puzzles - it's really good value for money if you're in the mood for them. The problem is that Relicta is really not as polished as the others. The story's sufficiently interesting, but almost all characters are impatient and snarky, making them quite unpleasant to listen to. The hub map is a completely unnecessary sprawling maze full of easy-to-miss collectables that only add frustration to the experience. Many of the puzzles (especially in the DLC) are excessively long, meaning you have to replay a lot every time you ragequit/softlock and have to reset. If I wasn't already hooked on the puzzles, there were many moments where I would have just stopped playing.So basically, Relicta isn't the game that will get you hooked on this genre, but it's a good hit to feed the addiction. Play the other major physics-puzzler games first.

_childDocuments_.review: I had to think about this rating a lot, and in the end I have to say I don't recommend it by a hair's width. Relicta is a pretty good 3D puzzle game. The obvious comparison is PORTAL, but instead of portals, you have the powers of magnetism & turning gravity on or off. And instead of damaging obstacles, you have like 8 types of barriers. It's not a bad game, but it has two massive, and I mean MASSIVE problems. There's no clear exit marker or special color for the final barrier you need to deactivate, and the beautiful nature environments actually make this worse because there's a lot of visual clutter. The visual clutter gets progressively worse each area, as a new color of holographic light is added for the new mechanic. And finally, because some of these puzzles have verticality / multiple floors, you literally can't see half the map until you solve half the puzzle, and then go "oh" and have to restart and do something different.  First off, they appear to be locked to framerate (bad), and second, the margin of error allowed in most of these puzzles is super low, way too low: you can do everything right but somehow fall off a box, or get bounced slightly in the wrong direction, bump a ceiling, walk too close to a ledge, etc. and bam! Retry it all! Go set everything up for the solution for another 4 minutes :) There are several puzzles that I've basically completed, only to bump a ceiling somehow, or otherwise get knocked back to the start, repeatedly, for no discernable reason. I think another issue is that, because of the gravity-type repulsive forces, objects tend to move very quickly which seems to make some puzzles much harder than they should be. I don't really know how to explain that the physics of the game just don't feel right. They're too realistic for a puzzle game but not realistic enough for a hyper-realistic sim game. To conclude, while the puzzles are fun and quite difficult, most of the difficulty actually comes from the game's puzzle setups being annoying and convoluted, as well as the practice of knowing what hitbox jank to avoid. It's a beautiful game, and the mechanics are cool, but I just can't recommend it because it feels like half the game isn't solving puzzles at all, it's just fighting with the game engine or confusedly running through buildings. Story wise, it's quite good, with the exception that there's zero reason to solve all the puzzles. I don't care if it's a "computer glitch" there's no way literally every inch of this planet has been filled with energy walls and high powered magnets and boxes with no shutoff.  Nobody besides the player character even has the ability to do the magnetism thing! This is a futuristic space station and they have -2 contingency plans, so when things go wrong our very intelligent scientist friends just decide to solve the puzzles anyways while people are actively freezing to death.

_childDocuments_.review: I went through about a half of the game and will probably not continue.It had started like a 1st person puzzle game, something more complex than Portals, but less complex than Talos.The puzzles are nice while you think about the solution. But then you have to do implement it, and it requires precise jumping,  running, falling from the same platform over and over - and the further into the game the more of such exercises, to the point when implementing started to take more time than thinking. It was nice in Prince of Persia, but why one would want something like this in 1st person puzzler is beyond me. Talos had SOME amount of that (which I can forgive this otherwise perfect game), but Relicta has too much and is too unforgiving for my taste.When I want to master complex movements in 3D space I go to dance classes or play Tomb Rider. So if you prefer stress-free brain-stretching games like Myst, Quern and such - you might not like Relicta.If you want a parkour game with additional challenge for the brain - you can give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: "It's so dense. Every single [puzzle] has so many things going on." - Rick McCallumThe story is phenomenal (so far). The voice acting is great. The writing is pretty funny, I'm very happy that a puzzle game let the scientists say "♥♥♥♥". The environments are beautiful. The puzzles start out pretty neato. Then they stop being pretty neato.The puzzles at the beginning of the game are fairly simple and do a good job of conveying puzzle mechanics. Then as puzzle games do, the complexity ramps up. What usually happens is that later puzzles combine concepts in new and interesting ways, and every so often add a new mechanic to permute with all the other things that the player has seen so far. The design of Relicta makes this ramping complexity extremely tedious. I got so fed up with the puzzles that I looked up a complete play-through on YouTube to see how long the game takes. The play-through was 16 hours. Time-wise, I'm only a quarter done with this game, and I'm rapidly approaching the point where I don't want to keep playing.In the later levels that happen about one-third of the way through the game, I go to a new room and am overwhelmed by the number of moving parts. I stare at it for 5 minutes, then make one move and get some progress. Then I stare at it for another 10 minutes, and make a second move that gets even more progress. Then I stare at it for 15 more minutes until I solve it. I'm looking at 15-20 different features of the puzzle map and trying to figure out how they can all relate together, or whether they're even related to each other.The complexity of all these puzzles would be fine if the process weren't so draining. There's a visual overload that saps my energy as I stare at a physics puzzle and try to figure out how on Terra (to reiterate: story good!) I'm supposed to proceed. Then when I figure it out, I don't get a sense of euphoria at finding a new mechanic. I feel like a third grader learning how to open dial locks for the first time, helplessly toying with the lock on my locker, and feeling a sense of relief when it opens that I don't need to deal with the lock anymore. Rarely in this game do I look back at a puzzle I just did and say "Wow, that was cool!" Instead I remember that the play-through is 16 whole hours and I need to get a move-on if I want to finish the game and spend my time on other things.I think if the game were somehow shorter, then I would be more amenable to playing through the whole thing. The plot points should absolutely stay the way they are, but maybe the number of puzzles within each region could be cut down. A lot of energy is required to progress the game to the next major plot point, and I'm busy enough otherwise that I don't have that energy.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, interesting world and setting (the story is simple, but it's good enough to carry the main story thread that gets told through dialogue and data collectibles), lots of puzzles to dig into. Dialogue could sometimes be written a bit better but the voice delivery is good. Production values are great, the world is really well done and each biome feels unique and interesting. The art style is nice and fits the game well, the execution is great. The game also runs really well for how good it looks.The puzzles are based on interesting fun concepts but start out way too easy (which is fine as an intro/tutorial, but it stays that way for quite a while). Later instead of increasing the trickiness and difficulty of the solutions and making you think harder the game makes the puzzle areas convoluted and less intuitive instead, which is a shame because the underlying concepts are great.It shifts the focus from logically thinking about the solution based on what you can see to wandering around in a big messy puzzle area trying (sometimes unpredictable) things until you find the right steps.   Which would be fine if you could just repeatedly try things, but it can get your cube stuck and unretrievable and make you restart the entire puzzle area, including big chunks of the old steps you have already solved, which is quite annoying.In some cases you can't even try to save it by playing with gravity and polarization (which would actually be fun) because the cube will be stuck behind barriers. On the bright side the physics are usually quite predictable and you can really focus on what you want to achieve instead of worrying about it glitching out. Thumbs up for that. In short, the puzzles could (and should) be harder and trickier but more readable and logic focussed which would add more challenge and take away frustration and randomness. It's not too bad and it's still fun to progress and find solutions, but it could be even better.In all other aspects the game is absolutely great.

_childDocuments_.review: Main Story took me near 17 hours to finish. Unsure if it has also counted the times i had left the game running in the background(Probably). Personally thinking at least several stages took me a while to finish and a few to redo.Its a First Person Puzzle, the likes of the Witness, Portal and Turing Test. Although it uses some boxes like Talos Principle. I can assure you that it uses different mechanic from all the other games i have played and mentioned. I am also glad it has a story like Turing test.Most of the puzzles are more like gradual progression per stage. Not like The Witness where you solve one puzzle with nore lation to the next one.  When reaching the halfway of the story, there will be longer puzzles per stage and you will take time to understand some puzzles starting point first before proceeding. There is usually just one way to finish a stage but there are some instances where i solved it skipping a step. Not ideal since i was only making it harder for myself lol. Also leads to a tendency to get stuck resolving it via other waysPos- Decent Story and some lore kinda like Turing Test- Good use of puzzle mechanics- Has some VA (but...)Needs improvement- There are a lot of F words for some reason. And this is not really normal(or i would think not normal) for scientists

_childDocuments_.review: Play this only if you want a lot of puzzles and don't need a story. Pretty graphics though!The story segments are way too sparse and too uninteresting to keep playing for them, but if you want to witness the possibly worst death lamentation scene I've ever seen, be my guest.Put on a podcast or a video instead of listening to the dialogue written with a constant sass level so high that it makes you think you're reading a political twitter thread. Though that feeling suddenly likes to flip-flop, becoming dramatic at times and then venturing into (intended) comedy, which is pretty strange.The puzzles play well and while they're complex, they're actually pretty straightforward - I didn't have to use a walkthrough a single time which is very uncommon (yeah I'm bad at vidya). And again - there are a lot of puzzles, and there are even more after you finish the game. Probably the best puzzle/price ratio out there.If you're interested in more story focus (and frankly, a better story) and fewer puzzles, get The Turing Test or The Spectrum Retreat instead. Maybe even QUBE 1 & 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give this game a good go. Even though the characters were irritating. For being mature (at least middle age) scientists/professionals, they sure were catty and hostile toward each other. Very tiresome. The story seemed rather generic but I was curious how it was going to play out.The world between the puzzles is just too big. Big for the sake of being big. Everything looking alike and very little to indicate what direction you should be going. All so that some collectibles can be scattered around. The lore pieces you pick up could have been interesting. But I found the text in the PDA to be difficult to read and stopped bothering.But I finally had to stop due to the puzzle game play. Even when performing the puzzles correctly (confirming with YouTube videos), I would run into occasional issues of a box not flying correctly or not being able to jump from the box to the intended landing. Causing me to have to repeat the steps multiple times before I could proceed. The final straw was the end of the Cliff Track. A box kept getting blocked by a green screen. The type of screen the boxes are intended to pass through. Leaving me completely unable to complete the puzzle and proceed.

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is a first person puzzle game which, for me, really scratches the Portal itch. You are constantly thinking about where you need to place your boxes and how to traverse the environment. Aside from this the visuals are very enjoyable and the game runs great. The story to this game is a nice addition but nothing special. Overall the game is enjoyable to play because the puzzels are well thought out and are placed in awesome environments. I reccomend playing this game very much if you like portal and/or the talos principle.

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles themselves were ok, it was sometimes ultra easy and sometimes you didn't realize there was a mag plate somewhere or a box was up on a cliff and when you finally see it you're like ohhhhhhhh there is a pad/box in that spot that i didn't even know existed.  Then once you realize there was this item you didn't see you realize the puzzle wasn't hard it just took you forever to see the one item was there.  But i would have just not given an upvote or downvote cause it was a decent puzzle if it was just the gameplay.But the story was so so so bad.  It's like in the distant future the dumbest scientists ever are on the moon working haphazardly, recklessly, and arrogantly with the most advanced freaky alien relic ever.  Like imagine the team that developed the nuke but instead they all talked and acted like love island characters.  Literally every time the main character talked i got more upset, it just kept building until i was furious and was hoping either the main character actually had no child ever or the child had been dead the whole time.    So after the final cut-scene i was like omg this story is so unbelievably bad i have to go write a negative review just to ♥♥♥♥♥ about this story writing.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like Relicta. I truly did. I kept playing a little more, thinking "It'll hook me eventually." And it never did, I'm afraid.  I went in expecting something similar to Portal... that's what I was hoping for anyways, but I didn't get that. The story didn't intrigue me. There was nothing really piquing my curiosity to push me forward or motivate me to solve the next puzzle. I didn't really feel invested in this character or the world that they were presenting. The "invisible walls" made it feel artificial.  The story was not engaging and the puzzles didn't require any sort of creativity. After about the 10 hour mark, I went ahead to and turned it off. That's not to say that this game is all bad. It has a few positives in its favor. The setting was cool. If you like immersing yourself in science fiction, Relicta certainly delivers that. The gameplay is fair.. there's nothing wrong with it mechanically speaking. The visuals are nice.  It just left me wanting something a little more.... engaging.It wasn't for me, but that's just one guy's opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I find Relicta to be an extremely fine first person puzzle game. It definitely draws from games such as Portal 2, The Talos Principle or Q.U.B.E but has unique puzzle mechanics.Basically you have to move cubes around and place them on 'buttons' in order to proceed and finish each test. That is done to a great part by using your gloves which can apply a positive or a negative polarity to cubes. Although that sounds very simple there is a vast array of using these manipulations for a certain outcome. What makes Relicta stand out among the multitude of FPP games is that puzzle areas are vast and require a particular understanding of which intermediate goal can be, and has to be, achieved in what order. I thoroughly enjoyed "reading" the environment and making my conclusions as to what I should do next.As to the visuals, Relicta certainly is a beautiful game but save for regular radio communication you are alone and the lunar station the game plays in feels sort of empty but that is a minor gripe. The voice acting is good but be cautioned that there is a lot of strong language if you are sensitive to that sort of thing.Lately, two bonus campaigns have been added for free which almost doubles the content of Relicta so it is a definitve recommentation from me. Expecially considering that it is on sale for another two days and costs only 10 €. Go and get it!
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: While I do liked the game in the beginning, some time afterwards the riddles start to become very tedious. The just get bigger and bigger. Then you just run around trying things just to find out where you are going.In the last part, I thought that the puzzles started to deviate sometimes from the logic of the game so far.The story is not that great, but not a let down. You can give it a go but do not expect a Portal or a The Turing test. As another suggested, it become a chore near the end, and I as well started to play the puzzles in breaks. A way point would be also appreciated. If you are at the 3rd part of the puzzle and you leave, you go back to the beginning.

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to give this a thumbs up but can not. I wish Steam would bring back the 5 star system they used to have for games like this. This game fails, but only just and if no one reads this review all they are going to see is a thumbs down. This game runs beautifully, and the visuals are quite good. The puzzles are challenging without being overly so. The story was decent even if the voice acting was not all that good. Not terrible, but not good either. Where this game fails is the cludgey game play. It's a poorly done platformer, with invisible walls all over the place, the inability to crouch, and jumping not always being allowed. There were many times where I figured out the puzzle almost immediately, but because of the weak controls, simply could not execute. Especially any time were were required to ride a cube. This was extremely annoying. As such I can't  give it a thumbs up. This is fixable with a bit tweaking to the jump and your players ability to stay on a cube they are riding. A bit more traction is needed.  I may revisit this title if they update it.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy puzzle game so I made it to the end of Relicta but I have nothing good to say about this game, which is disappointing because it looked like it had so much potential. Relicta has so much timing and platforming it is borderline a puzzle platformer which did not play well when it should have just been a puzzle game. By the halfway point the puzzles just get more convoluted and bloated with interference instead of intellectually satisfying to play and beat; after finishing a level I frequently let out a groan for how frustrating it was instead of feeling accomplished. Relicta would have been good if they just made a puzzle game instead of trying to imitate Portal so much, especially when it comes to making "funny" dialogue.The loud raven caw as the very first sound when opening the game is a rookie mistake... we are about 20 years past when that should have been fixed.Some say the story is functionable but in my opinion is it actively bad and detracts from the game. The dialogue between all characters bounces between tense+dramatic to flirty+playful even between the main character and the main antagonist. Personal qualm about the story teaser at the start, I hate when media starts off showing an exciting hook and then you play through the exact same sequence later in the game like I've already seen this five minute you showed me earlier, don't make me play it again, just don't do the cheesy *record scratch* "You're probably wondering how I got into this situation, lets start from the beginning"The interstitials between puzzle zones definitely need a map or waypoint indicators because each time you are dropped in a large facility with no way of knowing where to go and several dead ends, and what you are looking for is a small panel that is not lit up on a console that looks like several others. There is even a PDA that has your current goal that would the the perfect place for a map, but it only has emails and lore documents.... It's so bad that I had to look up a video walkthrough JUST to get to the next area because I was so lost.A big issue for me personally is the lack of colorblind mode, which is a problem when they have overlapping laser grid walls whose color is supposed to tell you what can and can't pass through, and a switch changes a far away gate from green(?) to red(?) when a colorblind mode could easily put a pattern up to replace the dot pattern on each gate.... The game is full of oversights like this.My biggest issue overall is that the main challenge of each puzzle is the intentional obfuscation of puzzle elements. The goal to each puzzle does not have any wires or indicator of what button to press to solve it, so all you know is a wall is blocking what could be the exit and something somewhere lets you go past it. On more than half the puzzles in the first zone I did not notice a box in a corner or behind a wall, and there is nothing pointing to it. The puzzles themselves are not that great which might be why they have to pad with the annoying additions of finding the pieces or platforming fillers. In the final zone you have to spot a key part of a puzzle through literal cracks in the floorboards. In that same puzzle trajectory puzzle was done correctly but got stuck on visual shrubbery and makes it seem like the wrong path because of the colored walls. All the stages have too many visual barriers and separated chambers so you can't get a good idea of what there is, leading to much running around just to get a feel of where you are each and every stage. This puzzle design just chains multiple separate puzzles together that could have easily been separate stages but they are mixed together just for the sake of confusion, like having 4 sudoku grids adjacent to each other just to make it seem like a bigger puzzle.Even early in the game a mechanic has to be used in a non-intuitive way. Several times they introduce a mechanic in one puzzle and the very next puzzle you use it differently. That pacing is just too frantic, at least think of a second puzzle using the mechanics the first way you introduced before forcing a creative and obscured solution. There is just way too much platforming and timing in this game that is intentionally designed for your to fail the first time. The second real puzzle of the whole game relies on timing, by moving your character over pressure plates you aren't looking at and don't snap to, and then grabbing the box in mid air as it flies by or else you have to repeat the process.There are several more timing ones and even others where you intentionally have to not lock the cube into the pressure plate and leave it floating to line up a shot that might go where you think it should and might not. When new puzzle elements are added there are zero prompts or tutorials on how to use them, which would be fine if the learn-as-you-play style of Baba is You starts you off slow but Relicta just keeps the same cluster of random puzzles and throws in a new one and says have fun figure it out.The visuals are nice enough I guess, but for a 26GB game it really should look a lot better.. even the moisture pattern on the screen (the character is wearing a helmet?) does not change and there is a big streak slightly above the crosshairs that catches the light and is annoying for the whole game once you notice it.The cherry on top is how each time you get an achievement you get a second one right after the cutscene. Why doubled up achievements? Really lame and makes no sense.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game. It has its weak spots for sure, but overall I think it's a good first-person puzzler that's worth your time if you enjoy games such as The Talos Principle, Portal, Qube 2, etc.If I had to describe it all in one word, it'd be... sprawling. The puzzle areas are very large and cover a lot of ground. It can be a little overwhelming at first. I often needed to do a little recon/exploration before I even started solving anything. The puzzles mainly involve manipulating magnetic blocks, hitting switches, moving platforms around, wrangling forcefields, and taking advantage of various gravity and momentum tricks. You'll need to pay attention to how things are connected via their power cables, as this will outline your prerequisites for toggling stuff. I thought the level designs were well-suited for the types of mechanics involved, and nothing felt unfair or overly awkward. You can reason your way through most sections by working backwards, so trial-and-error does not play an overly large role unless you're choosing to wing it.That being said, your FPS setting may impact physics. Like others have suggested, switching to 60 FPS is a good idea. Sometimes things don't behave correctly otherwise, even at 144 FPS.Visually, I thought the game was very colorful and pleasing to look at. I liked that the biomes all had different climates, which helped add a lot of variety and visual distinction to the puzzle environments. The two DLC chapters are harder than the main campaign, and they're included for free. However, based on the Steam achievement stats, maybe <= 4% of players even start the DLC - which is unfortunate, as I think those puzzles are a lot stronger in their design. It's a bummer they don't get more visibility. At the same time, it's understandable. The main campaign is very fatiguing as it is. The glacier stage midway through the game is particularly long and exhausting. I was running on fumes after that one, and yet there were three whole biomes to tackle afterwards. I think the VAs do a good job with what they are given, but the dialogue itself is often awkward, immature, and cringey. And everyone curses... a lot. The story is neat conceptually, but it seems to have a hard time deciding whether it wants to be serious or silly. It's also supposed to take place in the year 2120... anachronistic internet humor as "new phone who this" doesn't really fit. It would be like developing a game in the year 2000 that takes place in the year 2100 where people are still cracking Whassup jokes or something.There are in-game collectibles - but none of them are actually found within the puzzle areas, which is a missed opportunity, in my opinion. Instead, the collectibles are often in plain sight, scattered throughout the base station that you return to between biomes. Each collectible gives you some lore that you can read in your PDA, but most of it is pretty meh. In general, the base station is too large - it's mostly window dressing with lots of cloned assets and nothing to do. It takes a while to navigate, and it becomes tedious with all the maglev schlepping. Most of the Steam achievements come naturally by completing puzzles and picking up collectibles. Past that, there's a speedrun achievement for the main campaign, which is very generous (6 hours) if you've already played the game once and know what to expect. I went at a leisurely pace, and my second playthrough came in around 3 hours and 40 minutes with plenty of mistakes and a few resets. There's no visible timer in-game as far as I can tell, but you can safely pause or quit if you need to take a break.In the end, I thought this game was decent -- not bad, not amazing, but somewhere in between. Still quite fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle gameplay and graphics are the highlight, though gameplay stops evolving and becomes repetitive around the mid-point. Plot and conversations are embarrassing. Buy maybe if you're a puzzle fanatic and on heavy sale only.As far as qube-puzzle-games are concerned, this one quickly becomes challenging, even if you're quite familiar with said games (though not as hardcore as DLC for QUBE2).The only thing that feels off is that you can't throw qubes or drop them while jumping, which is a strange limitation. This first impression lasts a couple hours before stagnating, which makes the game really worth around 2-3 bucks.Visuals look great and it runs well even on my potato PC with graphics settings: highest-mid-low-highest-highest-mid-highest (then resolution scale adjustment to get max fps)gfx settings are bugged and don't always apply, or sometimes reset. Changing them should be done in the start menu of the game and not while playing.Plot is meh. There's some illogical nonsense to make it seem like solving these puzzles is sth important and heavy suspense of disbelief is required, but usually it's not too distracting. The most annoying thing is the voice acting. It's obviously a small budget game. But then it just should be less of it. It seems like one single voice actress recorded the lines for almost all characters, with slightly varying pitch and accents. Overuses "f.uck", to seem cool or edgy, but most of the time it's out of place. The humor is corny and unimaginative.There's a ideological propaganda red-flag with them calling themselves "women of science" instead of "scientists". There's enough SJ-filth in games as it is...All of these characters don't sound like scientists in space. Too much swag, too cool, too unrestrained, too confident, too extraverted. They seem more like at a college party than on the moon.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Portal, except instead of portals, you push blocks.It's like The Talos Principle, except instead of philosophical commentary, it's pointless melodramatic dialogue where the "writers" think the height of humor is saying ♥♥♥♥.Puzzles start out okay, although not particularly well designed, as you figure out all the gimmicks of the main mechanic. As you can imagine, there are only so many ways to push and pull "magnetic" boxes, and it quickly devolves into long, convoluted puzzles that feel like busy work. Honestly I probably would have just uninstalled and not a left a review, but the dialogue made me want to blow my brains out.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for May 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before June 1st, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.This is a first-person physics-based puzzler, which means it’s like Portal or Talos Principle, though this time around, the big gimmick is the ability to enable or disable gravity for the blocks as well as magnetize them.There’s also a story that Relicta keeps trying to make the player care about.  The concept is fine, but I found myself tuning out after the first hour, I didn’t care about any of the characters, and a few of them felt like they were having vicious mood swings in between each line.  Relicta could have been better off just focusing on the levels which were well designed. The puzzles in Relicta are rather solid, and after the first couple of sets, they started to introduce interesting and unique concepts that kept me having to understand the rules for the world.Pick this up if you enjoy block puzzle games, though I would say this isn’t as well done as either Talos Principle or Portal.  If you don’t like puzzle games, there’s not much here for you. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion a very enjoyable, challenging and atmospheric puzzle game with nice story integration.All in all the main game (without DLCs) took me about 33 hours to play through without walkthrough, where I enjoyed almost every minute of it. The game also has it's not so good sides indeed, but 90% of the game I really found joyful.So on the good side:+ Great graphics+ Challenging puzzles, but fair and always able to find a way out with logic or "creative" thinking+ Well I would say "nice" story integration, while not perfect and not always logic, it still gives you a part of the game's atmosphere+ Great atmosphere+ The chance for a "dead-lock" situation is very low+ nice sound effectsThe neutral side:o There is some music, but I would not really call it music. But it's okayo Indeed there is much profanity in this game, but that's part of the protagonist's personality, so for me it's okay :)The negative side:- There are some few situations where, with bad luck, you really can stuck and have to restart the level- Checkpoint saving ... I personally really did not like that, because it means you have to complete a puzzle before you can save the game .. which in later levels can take more than an hour.. Most time it's not a big loss, as, if you already know how to solve the puzzles, you can usually redo the steps in about 5 minutes, but there are also some puzzle elements which needs accurate moving and/or timing, where it's really annoying if you can not save and have to redo it, if you need to quit the game..But all in all I would buy this game again and I even rebought this game for the full price to support the, in my opinion, developer's great work. Thanks for given us that game. Perfect for people seeking out for more after Talos Principle or Portal :) It's not the same .. sure! .. it's not that perfect .. also sure! .. but it's still totally worth buying and playing :)

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game and I made it pretty damn far (only had two more sections of the game to complete) but this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game is just way too much of a slog. It has some great satisfying puzzles coupled with some stupid boring puzzles. The puzzles in this game also suffer from “Did I do that right?” almost 40-50 percent of the puzzles I completed without using the tools that were obviously put in place to use. On more then one occasion I skipped entire sections of a puzzle segment because I had a “lucky” spin or toss on a block or solved it a different way. It completely feels like you (the player) are breaking the rules of the puzzles but NOT in a good way because you then take those techniques, that you should not be doing, and try to use them in another puzzle segment and it completely throws the flow of the game off. Not only that I had multiple instances of the blocks getting STUCK in the level and there being no way out without resetting the segment, while this may not seem like a big deal the later segments in the game are much longer so a block may get stuck in an unrecoverable area and you are forced to reset THE ENTIRE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SEGMENT, this is what put me over the edge in the Forest River area and caused me to quit. The story is also very meh…Pass on this one, even for free.Go play Talos, Qube series or the Portal series instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I will not be comparing this game to Portal. It has not only been years since I've played that game, but many other reviews have already gone into depth with their comparisons between Relicta and Portal. I also believe it's better to judge a game focusing more on its individual qualities.I have also  this game for reasons I will specify in this review.tldr: Buy it only for the gameplay. The first 10 hours are excellent. If you get any more mileage out this game, I commend you.You control a scientist who loves spouting witty dialogue, whether it be to her daughter, her ex-husband, her colleagues, or the AI controlling the station. The voice acting is pretty good and it was interesting to hear english-speaking Indian voice actors. The plot itself is alright, but there's a pretty weak justification for the player to be doing all of these puzzles. You wouldn't want to play this game for the story. Solving puzzles with gravitation and magnetic powers sounded daunting at first, but the first few hours did a really good job teaching the player how to use both of these mechanics. Over the course of the game, you are also introduced to new obstacles that you must learn to circumvent. These range from color-coded barriers that prevent the player and/or blocks from passing through, switches that are powered from manual activation or pressure plates, and platforms with their own magnetism or movement properties. One irritating note is that the game tries really hard to make sure that the puzzles are done in the most linear way possible. On every level, there are invisible ceilings and invisible walls. If you jump while sprinting, your jump will only go a fraction as high. You can only pick up blocks while you are on the ground. Ironically, I found completing the puzzles in unintended ways to be a much more fun approach, especially in mid-late game levels where numerous obstacles are stacked on top of each other and can take quite a long time to complete in the intended way. It was at this point in the game that I stopped having fun and I felt like I was doing work to complete each level. I no longer felt joy from thinking about what was coming next and instead every level was just one step closer to finishing the game. As such, I have yet to finish the game and I do not feel any motivation to continue. Relicta takes place over many different locations but absolutely none of them have any discernible effect on the puzzles. You also cannot interact with the environments in any way. The game runs at high graphics settings on my GTX 1650 at a solid 60 fps, but my GPU reaches temperatures around 75-78 Fahrenheit. This is surprising, considering that I am able to run games I would expect to be more graphically intensive at similar frame rate but much lower temperatures. I believe this game is not particularly well-optimized, but it's not a huge issue if you settle for medium/low graphics.Because I can tell that the developers put a lot of work into the quality of this game. It has several shortcomings, but I am not in the slightest disappointed with the first 10 hours of my experience with the game. I believe if you get this on sale or in a bundle, it's worth playing to see if you might enjoy playing this game after the 10 hour mark.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was gifted to me! The concept is great. It reminded me of Portal, but it should NOT be compared to it.It just didn't quite hit the spot and the story did get a little confusing in some parts, especially when it would get you worked up for a story arc end or turn and then.... it was just more puzzles. There's bugs that need to be worked out, load times were long, and it just didn't run very smoothing no matter how I adjusted the settings. Puzzle difficulties were inconsistent. Sometimes I got threw in under ten minutes, other times it took me longer. With and without tutorials.Don't really recommend this game overall.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine. The main puzzle elements are shooting blocks from one magnetic plate to another and navigating colored gates that are only permissible to certain things (purple you can cross, green blocks can cross, gold nothing can). The first two areas are really nice, I loved some of the momentum puzzles in the second location. In fact, I thought the game was going to end in the ice caves, the last few puzzles were by far the best in the whole game.Sadly, it's just fine, not great. The game runs out of ideas fast. Later levels are just full of tedious steps. Blocks are hidden on the ceiling, elevators are hidden around corners, switches are wired in confusing ways (this is obviously intentional, and funny at first, but after a while you just want the wires to be clearly placed), etc. Later puzzles are full of extra little steps, just padding to slow you down. If the game was 3 hours long I would have loved every minute.There is a story, in the technical sense that they included one. It's boring, is not integrated with the game at all, and the dialogue is... strange. Lots of swearing, like a 14 year old boy with something to prove, but coming out of the mouths of 40 year old women. There is some political intrigue stuff which is interesting, but since it's all just spoken into your ear via radio it's more like you are playing a puzzle game while a strange radio drama full of way, way too many F-bombs.It's a fine puzzle game, and there aren't many of those, so I'm recommending it on that basis alone. But this isn't spectacular.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: IF you like solving puzzles...Get this game!You can immediately tell that The Developers have spend a lot of time and work to get this game to this level of perfection.The environment and graphics look great, play is smooth without any glitches or bugs, and the puzzles are wonderful (Some are very hard and some are very easy and the rest fall somewhere in-between)...BUT they are all fair and logical.   My Main Gripe with the game is the SAVE Game Feature.<<<The Game Saves Itself When It Wants To. You have No Control on when to save your progress.  Example: You may have worked on a puzzle for over an hour, made great progress on getting through it but you have to quit the game for whatever reason. The next time that you start, you will be BACK at the beginning of the puzzle and not where you left off when you quit and that is VERY Frustrating.{But don't let that stop you from experiencing this game.    My only little nit-pic is: Between the puzzles, you have to go through this needless array of rooms, trams, etc. that, to me, was just a confusing waste of time and it felt disjointed from the puzzles. (Would have worked Much Better if that part of the game flowed more easily. It felt like you were playing two games at once...one puzzle and one adventure)And that would be great IF the connection between the two would have been smoother.  Overall - I think that it is a Fantastic value for the price and I'd say buy it immediately. BUT...The Wonderful thing that The Developers have done is given you a DEMO to check out...Do This NOW!That way you can form your own opinion before purchasing.I've read people saying things like This is No Portal or Talos Principle and PERHAPS it isn't BUT I'd say that this game is 'right-up-there'.UPTATE: I'm 40 hours into this game (40 HOURS!) and it's still going....LOVE IT !!!

_childDocuments_.review: Nice puzzler akin to talos principle or gravitas. Other than some other reviewers, I enjoyed the story. And I really adore the design of the Labs.It makes a bit too much usage of invisible walls, and the domes from the inside don't look like domes, which was a bit sad. Also, I got softlocked twice, which sucked, as there are no in-puzzle-save-points and some puzzles can get big.Didn't quite understand the background lore tho.
