_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle games are my favorite genre and I've played all of the major ones.  The puzzle design in this game is fantastic starting with easy stuff at first.  But it soon gets serious though, eventually branching into huge multi-tiered puzzle arenas that soak up hours of your time.  By mid game expect novel tricks and red herring solutions that make you feel clever until you discover they don't work!  The skill of these puzzles is way better than the simple Portal games or even the Talos: Road to Gehena stuff.There is a trivial story about some of the cattiest, most potty-mouthed scientists who hid a haunted rock from the Corporation or something.  The script is good for comedic relief if nothing else but you can skip the dialog scenes if they start to wear thin.The puzzles are truly great and should be savored.  If you love the genre I'd suggest refraining from the use of a solutions guide.  Better to save and return after resting overnight.  Challenging puzzle games don't come around often because they are too frustrating for most leading to rage quits and negative reviews.  If you enjoy this game you might try Qbeh-1.  It's also challenging with similar puzzles to Relicta.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: + Nice visuals+ Pretty good atmosphere/setting/lore- Puzzles don't get more complex, just longer- Puzzles are extremely repetitive and tedious- The game is insanely long and dragged out (16 hrs first completion)- Annoying protagonist with annoying voice acting- Many puzzles can be broken or partially skipped- Invisible walls absolutely everywhere around youGosh, this was such an insane drag. I really, really wanted to quit Relicta since about halfway through and the only reason I didn't is because I'm just so dead-set on 100%'ing every half-playable game I come across. Honestly, this was borderline masochistic.The game throws a couple unique puzzle mechanics at you in the beginning and then proceeds to reuse them literal hundreds of times over. The puzzles grow larger and larger later on; they  complicated at first, but they really aren't. At any given moment you can only do one particular thing to advance the puzzle. Basically you're solving a dozen tiny, isolated, already-done-before, and mostly trivial sub-puzzles to proceed.The puzzles sucked so much man, it's all just busywork. I constantly wished I could just noclip to the next area and be done with it. The only times you get to actually think creatively is when you break the puzzles and skip entire sections of them. This normally would be pretty cool actually, except the method to break a particular puzzle comes to mind first, and how to solve it the intended way comes to mind much later. Or never at all. That is not good. That's just poor testing.The game tries so hard to be "like Talos Principle" except the writing is nowhere near as good and there's bloody zero exploration involved. In Talos, you could climb almost everything you see, or bring an item from one puzzle to another via clever tricks. But in Relicta absolutely everything is smeared with invisible walls everywhere, so no exploring for you whatsoever, sir.Finally, can I have less of this "strong independent Indian woman VS oppressive manipulative men" crap in my videogames please? It's not exactly in-your-face but it was hard to pretend like it's not there. The very thick Indian accent of the protagonist (and several other characters) made it difficult for me to get invested in the story. Call me politically incorrect all you want but English isn't even my native language and the accents still made me chuckle instead of being empathic whenever drama happens. I just couldn't take it too seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks nice, puzzle elements are fun and challenging, and overworld is well designed.The story is atrocious, as if written by a neglected toddler. Just bizarre how poorly it was done. Bizarre how a publisher let this go out. The story was all just passive, remote dialogue - no animations or interactions, just pure voice acting. It would have taken such little funding to change it. They could have even made it a silent game without any dialogue and it would actually improve the game. Such a stark contrast with the attractive design of the world/puzzles......At least until you get about 10 hours in to the game, then the puzzles start to reflect more closely to the story. Almost as if there were quotas for every puzzle to have more and more steps  - but no additional challenge. They devolve from fun exploration of gravity/magnetism/ordering, to pure busy work, running extended strings of movement without error. Almost like it changed from a puzzle game to a programming game. There is zero room for creativity in any solution, you have to do it exactly as they intended. They even went back and added a bunch of walls to prevent creative solutions. The programming aspects are tedious - having to go back through a 2 minute sequence because a box clipped a tiny edge is not fun. The puzzles also become much larger towards the end, to the point you have to complete 3-5 full puzzles worth of content before you can get a save point.They even added a huge number of free DLC maps, almost doubling the game. And those reflect perfectly to the base game. Terrible dialogue that makes me want to play silently, and puzzles that are more of a chore than challenge.All in all, I'd say there are 5 up-front hours of fun game. Then 10-15 hours of unpleasant, tedious work.Maybe get it on a deep sale and play til it stops being fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Upon loading the game you’ll be given the choice of playing the game in either DirectX 11 or DirectX 12. I never tried playing in DirectX 11 only in DirectX 12 and the game played fine. The game starts with Systems (AI) declaring a “Security Breach. This is not a drill. Initiating containment sequences...” The containment field in the Relicta chamber is collapsing, Doctor Laia Alami screams at Doctor Angelica Patel (you) not to approach the Relicta chamber! Ignoring her. Doctor Patel goes for a manual shutdown of the systems while Doctor Alami tries to override you and lock down the sector with Systems.  While this is happening, there’s a critical containment failure, in the Relicta chamber. Systems identifies an Unidentified Malicious Vector, Emergency Lockdown is initiated, Core Systems have been compromised. Shutdown is in progress, as Doctor Alami politely screams for the override to prevent Doctor Patel from shutting down the system. It then goes dark and the story continues from an earlier point in time, 2118, two years earlier in the De Gerlache dome. The Der Gerlache dome is one of several terraformed biomes at the Chandra Base on the moon.  You enter the dome it looks just like it would on Earth, multicoloured leaves adorn the trees, green grass and blue skies. You are testing the Gravitonic Wearable Interface (gloves) which you will use to move and manipulate cubes so that they can be placed on pressure pads. Upon placing the cubes on the pressure pads they will open forcefield gates. Sometimes you’ll have to place cubes on multiple pressure pads before a gate is opened. You can walk through some gates but not with carrying a cube. Each cube has Positive and Negative Magnetism which are controlled by your left and right mouse button. So, that when you have two cubes that are the same colour they will have negative magnetism and will push away from each other, while two different colours will attract to each other. Turning the gravity on and off with the middle mouse button will then allow the cubes to float. Using the positive and negative magnetism will allow you to send your cubes further distances, pull them closer to where they are required or send them higher above the ground.  You will also come across plates on the floor and walls and you’ll be able to change the magnetism to the same or opposite of the cubes. This will then allow you to send your cubes along a pathway to where they need to be. There are also some stations where you can place certain cubes and teleport it to another station. There are different types of stations each have a symbol to distinguish which cubes go where. You can then teleport the cubes to other areas that have a station behind a forcefield.  There are multiple puzzle areas for each biome region you visit and after completing an area you’ll head back to Chandra Base. Upon returning to base the story will reveal its self some more and giving you some information on what is happening and what your next move will be. Also scattered around are collectable items to find and documents which will give you some information on what is going on at the Chandra Base. In the Options there’s settings for Graphics (Resolution, Window Mode, Show FPS, FPS Limit, Render Scale, General Quality, Vegetation, Post Processing, Shadow Quality, Texture Quality, View Distance, Visual Effects, Antialiasing and V-Sync). Audio (Master, Music, Sound Effects and Voice Volume Sliders). Controls/Accessibility (Mouse Sensitivity X + Y, Controller Sensitivity X + Y, Invert Y Axis, View Bobbing, Motion Blur Crosshair Type). Languages (English, Spanish, French, Italian, German, Russian, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese and Chinese), Gamma, Key Binding and Tobi Eye Tracking. Relicta is a great looking first-person physics-based puzzle game that takes place in terraformed biomes on the moon. The puzzles can be challenging but with a bit of thought you’ll figure them out. There is some “French” language in the game which doesn’t bother me at all but it may offend some folks. I’ve had one problem while playing and I got stuck between a cube station and a wall after jumping around. However, a quick reboot and it was back to normal and haven’t had any other problems so far. Positives + Looks great + Challenging puzzles + Decent story + Has achievements Negatives - Can be frustrating at times - No cards currently Combine magnetism and gravity to complete puzzles in biomes on the moon in this first-person physics-based game.  7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I completed this game on a different platform.There are 3 different intros each time you open the game and one of them is a loud raven. Unskippable too. Totally not needed.Awful dialogue and storytelling, almost makes me not wanna recommend the game. I wish I didn't have to listen to it whatsoever.Transitioning between levels through the base can leave you often lost in a huge maze as the game only tells you where to go once and provides no additional indicators, so you can end up wasting even up to 5 minutes just to get to the next puzzle tracks set. I just wanna play the game, I don't care about the base especially when there's nothing meaningful on it. The long embarking and lift animations don't add anything good to it either.Also, you can get stuck. Literally. The game has some ways to prevent it but it's inevitable to eventually occur and then you have to restart. It comes from the player's error but it should not be possible, especially when the game is already so restrictive on what you can do with all the plaster-like blockages such as the invisible barriers and inability to interact with cubes while jumping.However, the game-play is wonderful if you're just a puzzle enthusiast and this is what makes me recommend this game. The levels get progressively more difficult, challenging and complex, introducing some additional mechanics that sometimes have to be used in unique ways. It's always logical what you have to do when you take it step by step. Doing random things until it works is not an option so it requires you to analyze the levels and think of your options.The graphics are incredibly wonderful with stunning views, landscapes and a beautiful detailed environment. I was left jaw dropped when I witnessed just how gorgeous this game can look. A screenshot from afar can look like a picture taken in real-life on an expedition. It's very eye-pleasing. But you don't get to see the best of it until a bit later in the game. Each set of puzzles has its own thematic: forest, jungle, canyon, glaciar, etc. so the game doesn't feel repetitive visuals wise.The sounds effects are satisfying and the environmental noises are really good, especially in the tropical beach levels. Don't know what to say about the soundtrack as I don't have a good musical ear but I wasn't bothered nor dissatisfied by it.It has a lot of negatives but I just wanted to complete puzzles and this is what I got. If you think the same as me, this is a good game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Thumbs up/down is really insufficient sometimes and here is such a ~meh~ case.I am one of the few people that actually kinda liked Magrunner Dark Pulse and this game is basically the exact same mechanics. Yet here the puzzles feel somehow even more fiddly. Whenever I finish a puzzle I look up what was the intended solution as the way I did it felt like exploiting some kind of bug or unintended solution. And it is not a good sign when most of the time I was correct in that assessment. Examples: In a cave I skipped half the puzzle because I rode the cube through a small gap in a green field rather than using the spot on the other side of the cave which then afterwards made feel stuck since I couldn't figure out what this part of the level was for. Or I would just jump and drop a cube on a ledge you were supposed to ride a cube to. Let's talk aesthetics. I feel like the idea to set this game on the moon was an after thought as most enviroments are just forests or caves with not a hint of the moon in sight. Problem is: with all that useless nature surrounding you it makes the puzzles harder to parse. Obvious comparison is Talos Principle but that game had a) cross puzzle secrets and b) was much more visually clear than this game. Worse are the "hands off" puzzles where you have to guide a cube through a maze by changing magnetism. Except you can't see the entire track most of the time and have to do it without seeing where the cube got stuck this time. That the walls are made out wood instead of just something transparent adds to the problem. There is a sort of Hub in game that let's you go back to old areas but you can't actually enter the puzzles and only go to the entrance if you missed a collectible, thus rendering it useless. It's weird having a completely linear game have a useless hub.Speaking of the story: You start with an intro cutscene where you don't know what is happening. Then you play everything up to that point but nothing that was important was explained in the mean time. Afterwards you are also on your own again with the other characters basically not mattering anymore, which would be more an issue if all the characters didn't have the same personality anyway. They are all Woman who swears alot which is basically a worse version of Lishari Peghast.As said the game is not great. But the visuals are nice and some of the puzzles are kinda fun. So if you some one that can put up with a lot of jank then you can try the game for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is an interesting first person puzzle game. I personally really liked it. In different domes (themed areas), you have to solve puzzles by using the power of magnets. Same color repels, different color attracts. This simple mechanic never changes and you will have to manipulate cubes and plates to activate switches and open up paths.The game slowly introduces some additional obstacles over the course of its rather lengthy campaign, though the base mechanics won't change. Including the two content packs that come with the game, it took me 25 hours to beat it which is more than generous for the price. The game looks good, the different areas are varied and the mechanic and the physics attached to it work very well.There are a few negatives though. Let's address the elephant in the room first: the dialogue is absolutely horrendous. At first, I thought that the characters acting more human by showing weaknesses and swearing a lot would add some spice to the game, but it gets tiring very, very quickly. I am assuming that the dialogue is meant to be funny and lighthearted, but it is completely misplaced and only rarely humorous. The voice actors are top notch though and they did a great job delivering even the most cringeworthy lines. The story is nothing to write home about - it's okay, really - but hearing a demonic alien voice unironically say "new phone, who this?" made me walk away from my computer and contemplate life for a few minutes. If only I would smoke, I could have completed that dramatic moment as I made my way towards the balcony and gazed into the distance. My wife was like "did I just hear this right"? If I would get a penny for every time a character would say "f***" or "s***" for no reason in this game, I would have enough to fill a pretty big swear jar. Seriously, though, the dialogue is a goldmine for cringe - a word I only use when it is absolutely warranted, so trust me on this. It is honestly oddly endearing, but also really annoying. A weird mix.The puzzles themselves also have some weaknesses - the biggest one is that they never change and are overall rather easy. New obstacles mix it up here and there, but every single puzzle in this game can be solved by finding the one thing you can do and going from there. They get really big and complex eventually, but even that doesn't matter. It's always: find the start point, go from there. This completely eliminates trial & error - which is a  - but the base mechanics are sadly not varied enough to ever really make the puzzles challenging or elevate them above "mildly difficult at times", and often that is just due to the inherent complexity of some of the levels. I love puzzle games without trial & error, but I almost think Relicta went to far in the opposite direction at times.Still, though, I definitely recommend Relicta. You can tell that the developers and everyone who contributed put a lot of effort into this. An orchestrated soundtrack, a ton of puzzles - maybe a few too many - and great voice actors make the game worth playing, even if it stretches a bit thin in the last few hours. Just try to take breaks to calm down your annoyance levels at some of the dialogue.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's weakest point is pacing, in both story and gameplay. The beginning of the story starts out bland, and the beginning puzzles spend a bit too long teaching you core mechanics. If you get far enough through, however, believe me when I say it pays off. The story gets far more interesting, and new mechanics get added over time, slowly making the puzzles more and more complex, to the point where only about 11% of people who have played this game have actually beaten it. The core concepts of magnetism and gravity are very compelling, and they're used in very interesting and unexpected ways in later levels. One common complaint I see in negative reviews of this game is that there's too much profanity. Now, this next question, I genuinely, truly mean from the bottom of my heart: Who gives a ♥♥♥♥? Seriously. If the presence of profanity somehow detracts from the value of the puzzles and mechanics presented...that's just a very shallow assessment, to be honest. That being said, this is a puzzle game, first and foremost. The story exists, but you only really hear dialogue in between puzzle areas, so it could be a good while between hearing one part of the story and hearing the next. Admittedly, the puzzles aren't tied into the story as well as they are into a game like Portal or The Entropy Centre, but the puzzles and story themselves are still good enough on their own to be enjoyable. If you aren't looking for a puzzle game, though, then you aren't looking for Relicta.

_childDocuments_.review: REVISED - Thumbs up after 100 hours of play after rating Thumbs down only a dozen hours in.  Stick with it - it gets better.  Especially the bonus level Ice Queen - very Portal 2-esque.Great concept.  Combine a Portal or Talos Principle type cube & button puzzle adventure game with magnetism and anti-gravity and weave a story into the reason for having to pass various testing chambers.  The early chambers are fairly easy, then applying logic becomes more important, but unfortunately near the end the puzzles start depending on very quick timing, which is very challenging for mobility impaired players and have nothing whatsoever to do with puzzle solving capability.  Unfortunate.  That said, if you stick with it, you will be rewarded with more challenging puzzles.I  recommend it because I love the genre and applaud efforts by developers to build such games, but be cautioned that the UI is a bit glitchy and the fact that in some of the long puzzles near the end there is no intermediate save functionality (meaning you have to completely restart a long level if you have to quit before completing the whole level - which compounds the whole dexterity/speed issue).

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is another superb entry in the first person puzzle genre.  It follows a format reminiscent of Portal 2, mixing puzzle areas and narrative storytelling, though with a hub area layout more similar to The Talos Principle.  I personally enjoyed the sci-fi story and and appreciated the really solid voicework that goes along with it.Gameplay mostly revolves around manipulating blocks and pressing switches using magnetic charges and being able to toggle gravity on said blocks.  Various types of forcefields also need to be worked around, and a few other mechanics are added later.  I found the vast majority of the puzzles to be intuitive, even the later puzzles which get rather long.  There were a few instances in the final chapters of the game however where I found some puzzle steps overly fiddly since they rely too much on free form physics simulation.Relicta is a very good-looking game with beautifully-designed environments and utilizing the high quality presentation of Unreal Engine.  It runs very well too, staying locked at 120 fps the vast majority of the time on my GTX 1070 and scales down really well to even older mid-range hardware.  The only fault I can find is the "dirt" overlay on the camera that can really get in the way of appreciating the game's visuals in certain lighting conditions.  I'm sure it's supposed to simulate the character's helmet, but I can't imagine anyone would wear such a dirty visor without cleaning it.So overall, I highly recommend this game.  I can't get enough of good first person puzzle games and it's nice to play a higher quality production again since they don't come around very often.Edit: Two free DLCs were released for the game (accessed from Extras on the main menu,) containing about 12 lengthy and difficult puzzles each along with new story dialogue.  I was very impressed with the quantity and quality of this content, particularly since it's free.  But while the puzzles are good, there are some issues.  It's very easy to block progress in many of the puzzles and force you to reset - which can be a large setback due to how long many of them are.  I also ran into some issues with overly complicated physics movements not being reliable.  Overall though, a very satisfying addition to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle game that gets ruined by hidden mechanics and terrible writing...The game itself isn't too bad if you just think about the puzzles itself. The characters act weird ALL the time. The boss is always screaming at everyone, but then 2 minutes later can have a "normal" conversation with the same person she screamed at..The main character for some reason sings a line about "going to the moon" which the the AI called Sys(short for System...) interrupts her to say "but we're already on the moon". Such a usefull conversation, not at all forcefully written to say "AI are robots who doesn't understand human behavior"...2/10 - Couldn't even finish the game because of the terrible writing and annoying puzzle mechanics that are for luck only.

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is a Portal Clone. I love Portal Clones. But not like this...Firstly I don't know why but whenever an indie or even AA studio gets their hands on the Unreal engine they manage to make it hog way more performance than it's worth. This is another example of that, just bad frames over heating my computer for no reason. The assets and voice lines are super high quality. The story is a drag for the first 3 hours but the intrigue hits after shoemaker which makes you want to continue. The gameplay.... it's nothing we haven't seen before. I've played every Portal Clone under the sun and this is just the least fun I've had solving puzzles in a test chamber. The game just removes all the usual toys from you. The Y rotation of every cube is permanently locked, there's invisible walls everywhere, you can't let go of boxes in midair, the physics is just tame, quickly picking up up boxes while running is just not a thing, and this game features one of the most unsatisfying jump arcs ever. It's more of a *Huughh!* than a jump.There's also so many fudgable solutions that sometimes make me wonder if I just cheesed something... which I prbly did at least twice...I do plan on completing the game but I can only take a little of it at a time.

_childDocuments_.review: The attempt towards making a portal-esque puzzle game is respectable, but the game is very flawed. For starters, some of the puzzles(even at the later stages) make no sense at all from a logical standpoint. The puzzles revolve around gravitational mechanisms but maintain no consistency in how the cubes move or function. Secondly, the story and the dialogues are pretty boring and lame in my opinion, and I can't seem to enjoy any of the characters or their dialogues. I have no interest in finishing the game with such mediocre and inconsistent puzzles and a boring story who's only positive attribute can be the space and sci-fi setting, which can at least be said to be respectable. But the part that really made me dislike this game are the jumping mechanics. It is EXTREMELY frustrating to jump in this game as the player jumps way too low and requires multiple attempts just to get over a ledge. Parts where you're elevated from the ground and have to jump over a tiny ledge can be frustrating when you keep falling off and pretty much have to repeat the puzzle over again. This one tiny flaw really put the nail in the coffin for this game, and makes it borderline unplayable. Decent graphics and atmosphere mean nothing when the mechanics are so poorly made. I love puzzle games such as The Talos Principle, The Witness and Portal and each have their own amazing traits that make them unique amongst each other which elevates them into the pantheon of great puzzle games. But this game is far far inferior to even the average ones such as The Turing Test. I would not recommend this game unless you've played every other puzzle game out there and are obsessed with the genre like I am. But even I couldn't really get into this game. 4/10 at best.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to give it a hard "Meh." It has interesting puzzle gameplay, but the plot is boring and dull. The environments look pretty, but they're too complex for the gameplay; and make it hard to know what you're supposed to be doing. I spent about 10 minutes trying to solve a puzzle incorrectly because the admittedly very pretty level design made me think there was a completely different answer.Also, the soundtrack is uninspired. This is a game where you're supposed to stand around, think, and solve logic puzzles. You don't want an overpowering or distracting soundtrack, but you want something to help you not stress about the puzzles so much.If you enjoy puzzle games like the Witness, or Myst, with very little active plot and just puzzles presented to the player, I recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is a flawed masterpiece. The puzzles are challenging and clever and had me hooked all the way through. The game should appeal to anyone who likes the "test chamber" genre (Portal, Talos Principle, Turing Test, Q.U.B.E.). A fairly simple cube mechanic is steadily built upon incrementally and there never seemed like there was an unfair learning curve. Huge congratulations to the puzzle designers as the game is also quite long and each puzzle area has a unique take on the mechanics.The graphics and environments are also stunning, even running on 4-5 year old PC on low graphics.The storyline is pretty silly as a loose way of linking test chambers but is at least a partial driving force to hold the whole thing together. One thing that baffled me is the dialogue has a huge amount of swearing. It doesn't bother me so much, but I feel the developers could easily have removed this (or had some way to censor it - there isn't) to make the game fun for all age groups.Enjoyed from start to finish, and look forward to more from the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a hard time warming up to this game. I took me way into the second half of the game to realize how the game works, and I don't speak of the magnetic abilities. But once it clicked, I couldn't stop playing. What I learned:When you enter a new room, you'll find ten switches, twenty walls of different colours, thirty cables connecting them and one little cube hidden somewhere. And you don't know where to start. Eventually, I learned to "follow the cube", and take the smaller parts of the whole step by step. This made it way easier to play and enjoy the game. The big rooms have no checkpoints, which can be annoying if you solved half a room and run out of time. It explains the basic abilities in the beginning. But after that you have to find out all the shenanigans you can do with your magnetic gloves yourself. This can lead to a lot of "How the F are you supposed to solve this?!?" moments.Some solutions feel "not right" and you often start to think if that  was the correct solution. You check a video guide, and yes indeed, you were supposed to manipulate the flying cube with your magnetic plate through the wall so it magically hits the button. Having played other games like Portal before, it caused me quite some headache to turn my thinking around. It doesn't help that some riddles, especially in the extra levels, have a few softlocks causing you to restart the level. So if you don't see the correct "cheaty-feeling" solution, you might have to reset the whole 10-minute level. With these tips in mind, the game is really good and will hook you in. But prepare for a headache. A lot of headache. The story is okayish, you can usually smell the plot twists some miles ahead, but the dialogue is fun and the voice actors do a very good job. The environment looks absolutely gorgeous. But unfortunately all you ever do is look at it, the nature itself does hold no secrets at all. One minor negative for the record: The riddles are great, but they do not fit the narrative. Your friends are freezing to death, but you just have to solve all these rooms in your way "for science". Test chambers like these fit way better in a laboratory setting like in portal, not in the awesome nature they built on the moon. TLDR: Good game, good riddles once you get the hang on them.

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is a darn good game. It is one of the best first person puzzle games that I’ve played.The main puzzle mechanic of Relicta shows great similarities to the puzzle mechanic of another game called Magrunner: Dark Pulse, which I also recommend playing. Still, in my opinion the puzzle mechanic in Relicta is better implemented.What strikes me most about this game is its length. It took me a whopping 46 hours to finish the game. If you look at the Steam Achievements then you’ll see that only 11,1% of players got the achievement to finish the game. I suspect this is so low because the game is so long. _childDocuments_.review: This is by far the longest puzzle game I've seen and it even has two DLCs included which I didn't have the patience any more to complete. But it's also a prime example of how more content isn't always better value.First off, the environments are littered with translucent walls as a gameplay element, which is really ugly, and not-quite-invisible walls above every wall, edge or elevated surface you are not supposed to be able to get across because it would invalidate the puzzles, which is just poor design. Even so, apart from the simplest levels in the very first chapter, there is not a single level where there aren't very obvious ways to circumvent at least half the steps/set pieces you are supposed to take/utilize. Most of the time this wasn't faster than the 'correct' path, because it always took me several attempts to get the angle/direction/velocity just right and while in the beginning it was kind of fun to solve the courses in obviously unintended ways it got really tedious later on when the levels become really large and require several dozen needlessly convoluted and often redundant steps to complete, especially once you need to place specific cubes on each pressure plate rather than just any one of them. Somewhat contradictorily, the very techniques that allow you to skip things in earlier levels (mainly jumping over energy walls without deactivating them, which you are generally not supposed to be able to do), are required in some of the later levels.On the whole, I would argue the level-design is at the very least inelegant and even borderline incompetent. I rate the game only on the merits of its gameplay elements, but it might bear mentioning that the purpose of the puzzles in-universe was also completely ridiculous and the story itself was cheesy and uninspired, but kind of funny near the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite my recommendation, I want to start on a positive note. This game clearly has had a lot of work put into it and I respect that. The environment looks really good and is really well developed, much like the Talos Principle as others say. While the environment design was phenomenal, I can't say the same as much for the puzzles though. Most of them are fun, but there are some that left an overwhelmingly negative impression in my mind. Now, I enjoy finding the solution that the developers intend. There are a lot of games that you can either abuse mechanics or come up with a different way to solve the same problem, but I just like finding that clean, methodical solution. Early game, there were some puzzles though that it seemed the intended solution was to abuse mechanics. As another reviewer mentioned, in the late game, individual "chambers" - thinking of Portal's idea of testing chambers - were MASSIVE with lots of moving parts. Some may like that, but I'm not a fan. There are two reasons why. First, it becomes very difficult to find the button, cube or whatever you need to either get started to continue working the puzzle. Second, it is VERY easy to soft lock yourself. Yes, you can reset yourself to the beginning of the chamber, but you lose a lot of progress and it takes time to work through a massive puzzle all over again. I'm no stranger to first person puzzle games and if I go back to those same puzzles later I very well may facepalm and realize the solution was right in front of me but I was just being slow. However, the frustration I felt on account of these previously mentioned reasons is why I cannot recommend this game to others.Now I have some additional criticism, but it's very minor compared to everything above. The story. Moves. Very. Slowly. Late game especially, since at that point I generally only heard dialog every other "chamber." Keep in mind, each "chamber" gets larger and larger, taking more and more time to complete, so it can be a while before you hear even just a single sentence from the character you're playing as. Story isn't that important to me - Rethink didn't have a story at all and I still really enjoyed it - but story progression at slightly faster pace would improve it, in my opinion.I want to end this review the same way I started - on a positive note. Once again, I appreciate the effort the devs put into this game. The amount of content this game offers is absolutely worth the 20$. I really wish I could recommend it to others because of that. Please do comment if you disagreed with me at any point. A discussion would probably better capture what I really wanted to include in this review anyway.This review is somewhat a work in progress - I'll be updating it occasionally as I think of better ways to describe what I'm thinking.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a breath of fresh air. It's very much in the style of puzzle games, and it hits it out of the park on that front. I've had a lot of experience with these types of games, having played Portal, Portal 2, The Talos Principle, The Witness, The Turing Test, Steamroll, Lightmatter, Q.U.B.E,  The Swapper, Chromagun, The Spectrum Retreat, MIND: Path to Thalmos, Etherborn, Polarity, and Magrunner: Dark Pulse so I feel like I can speak with some leverage in the this particular niche (which happens to be my favorite!)You play as a female scientist on a base on the moon. You are trying to get everyone in your crew together but things just don't seem to be going the way you want them to and in order to press forward you have to complete various puzzles. These puzzles typically involve cubes, pressure plates, switches, gravity, anti-gravity and magnetism and you have to use all of them to your advantage to move forward. Early on as the game introduces concepts through puzzles, they easier and quicker to move through. As you progress the puzzles in Relicta become challenging almost, at times, to the point of frustration, but very satisfying to solve and totally reasonable when you realize what you are supposed to do. The breadth of some of the levels makes them take quite a bit of time to both analyze, set up a plan, and implement it. Occasionally the implementation of your ideas does not function right and you have to try repeatedly to accomplish what you want to do (or give up on that method), but the game does a good job of allowing easy ways to get your cubes back as well as an easy way to restart a particular puzzle if you need to. I was particularly impressed with some of the really unique ways that Relicta has you solve parts of puzzles. When I made the discovery of how to do these particular things, it felt so incredible. You have to really think outside the box! Since I would describe this game as a puzzler, I wanted this to be the first thing I discussed.The graphics of the game are good. Each area of puzzles has it's own beautiful biome style and they are impressive. I was a bit disappointed that I couldn't explore as much as I'd like due to the invisible walls. I particularly liked the jungle biome and I liked the sounds for it too.The game runs smooth at about 80-100 fps with my GTX 980. I have not had any bugs and the game seems well polished.The voice acting is good, but I wouldn't call it outstanding.I was not too happy about all the crude language in this game so, fair warning, you're not going to want to play it around kids at least during the times you are travelling because that's when the dialogue happens. Every game I've played in this style has managed to do it with little to no cussing from what I remember, but this game excessively uses it in my opinion.The one other gripe I have is with the travelling. Travelling from place to place through the main area and the other world areas was really kind of difficult. Half the time I didn't seem to know exactly where to go and had to just stumble around. It would be nice to have some sort of arrow to direct you where it wants you to go so you can get there - there are just so many ways to go. That said, the game does have hidden PDA notes and some collectibles hidden throughout the worlds, which is nice.I forget where I made the discovery of Relicta initially, but I am glad I decided to pick it up. Typically I don't buy a game at full price, but I did with this one knowing the style of game it was and I have to say it had totally been worth that amount of money. Based on what I know about the game, I'm guessing I am a little over halfway through it at the time of this review and have put in 12 hours. The story has kept me interested in what is yet to come, and I can't wait to know what the ending is going to be. For very few people working on this game, I am very impressed with the quality of it. It's hard to find a good game in this vein, but this is definitely one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is a first person puzzle game that really wants to be Portal.Like all such games, it falls well short.But unfortunately, it doesn’t even manage to stand out particularly as its own thing. Despite its high graphical fidelity and production quality, it starts out promising but ends up falling apart about halfway through, both in terms of gameplay and story.Like all such games, it has a “core mechanic”. The core mechanic here is the ability to give blocks (and some pads that can hold charges) either a red charge or a blue charge. Opposite colored charges attract, same-colored charges repel.In addition, you can make blocks weightless, allowing them to fly through the air after having been given a push from a charge, or continuing on their momentum from a moving platform.That’s it. That’s all there is.The game is entirely centered around grabbing blocks and putting them on buttons to get rid of various force fields blocking your way, and sometimes toggling the odd switch. The force fields can either block everything, or only one thing – you, blocks, or drones.There are some platforms that you can move, along with some drones that remove all special effects on all nearby blocks and charge pads, and which can carry blocks.And… that’s all the mechanics there is.The problem is, this is a 15 hour long game, but it has fewer, and less interesting, mechanics than something like Portal 2.So how does it make the game last 15 hours?Unfortunately, the answer to that is by just making increasingly long puzzles in the back half of the game. Frequently, puzzles would either be multi-stage things, where you go through a series of mini-puzzles, or a puzzle where there was some sort of “hub” that you kept on having to solve mini-puzzles to unlock a central door. Only rarely were there big puzzles that actually felt like they integrated all the pieces.As a result, the entire second half of the game starts to end up feeling tedious rather than interesting. Some of the later game puzzles were okay, but never was there a puzzle in the game where I felt like it was particularly amazing to solve. A lot of the “harder” puzzles were harder because you couldn’t find a particular “puzzle piece”, so to speak; once you actually had the pieces in hand, what you were actually supposed to do was often fairly straightforward, if sometimes fiddly later in the game, as you had to line things up rather awkwardly to make some puzzles work, as the “snap-to” portions didn’t work in some areas due to them not sending you in quite the right direction or being aligned in the right way.The game ends up just kind of dragging on by the end, and I just wanted it to be over.Which brings up the other problem – the story.It starts out promisingly enough – there’s some sort of inciting incident with a weird purple crystal, you have a set of coworkers around and a daughter who is coming to the space station, ect.The problem is, this all ends up falling apart about halfway through the game. The central plot twist of the game isn’t very good and results in almost all of the characters you spent the first half of the game talking with never talking to you again throughout the rest of the game. As a result, the game's supporting cast dynamics end up being totally tossed out the window and not mattering at all for the rest of the game, as you end up interacting with a second, and less interesting, set of characters for the second half of the game.Indeed, if you spend any time thinking about the plot twist, it both feels unnecessarily convoluted and makes no physical sense, nor sense with the other characters in the story, who act like no time has passed at all. The loss of contact with their former colleagues gets short shrift and the story itself seems to forget about what happened to them, as the characters don’t seem to care despite supposedly being emotionally invested. Only at the very end of one of the game’s two multiple endings (which are chosen at the last minute for… some reason? I don’t even know why it has multiple endings…) does the game remember “Oh, these people existed” and actually follow up on it at all, and then only in a stinger thing that is not very satisfying (though there’s more from a title update I have yet to play).Overall, then, the game fails to deliver in terms of story, character, or gameplay. The story doesn’t even make a ton of sense in terms of characterization, and the gameplay is too simple for a game as long as Relicta is. Despite a potentially promising start, it just doesn’t hold up, and it never really does anything particularly good, let alone great.

_childDocuments_.review: I made it to the last section of the game (Jungle) and I have to say, I can't finish it. I am just not interested anymore. I was soldiering on, doing the same kind of puzzle over and over for 15 hours or so and it's just not fun. Compared to Magrunner, I can't often tell if I solved the puzzle right or if I "cheated".The puzzle mostly is not "figure out how to do X" but "figure where we hid all the pieces.The envinroments are good, the story I didn't care about, the section where you have to go back and forth through endless corridors to reach the next area is an absolute chore. Problem with the environments being scenic is that it obstructs the puzzle. I like that the game tries to steer away from the clean design a'la Portal or Turing Test but I feel like it is to detriment of the gameplay here. It is always disappointing to hit an invisible wall when you feel like you have the right solution.It's not a bad game, but it's not very good either - as far as FPS puzzlers go, you can do better and you can do worse.

_childDocuments_.review: Is a decent puzzle game. But not great.Graphics are just ok. Music is rare, but fits the game. Story is serviceable. But dialogs are poorly written. Puzzles offer a decent challenge. But a several are dependent on physics and sometimes don't work at the first try, nor the second, nor the third. So you have to keep repeating, until the physics engine does what it's supposed to do.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal first-person puzzle game. There was some jank flying on boxes, but not enough to deter me from finishing or recommending this game. For what it's worth, the game ran pretty well on my old toaster of a desktop but turned my PC into a space heater, raising the temperature of my office a few degrees in the process.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent 1st person puzzle game with some enjoyable spins on mechanic without really breaking any new ground if you have played any of the pillars of the genre. Nice, if shallow, premise that meshes reasonably well with the central conceit that all of these games have to ignore/confront: Why am I doing this set of self-contained puzzles? Interesting characters with good voice acting even if that side is also not explored much. Idea of locations are clever although in execution bit generic space station/forest/desert and a bit too much trudging without anything of note happening. Most of the puzzles are grokkable with a handful of tedious ones that overstay the point where you know what to do but have to wait for timings to align.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: I typically like puzzle games, but this one doesn't work for me.The riddles are just tedious. You need to move boxes from A to B pressing buttons to unlock your way or you ride on the boxes to your next riddle. Pretty early on, the levels get too big to have a good overview. You run around a few minutes to figure out the layout, where to get the boxes and where to move them. This just feels completely unnecessary.Then the riddles themselves involve just simple push pull mechanics, sometimes with kind of a dexterity check because you need to change polarity on the fly.Solving the riddles feels really unrewarding. You don't feel any sense of accomplishment, just another tedious section done.And then there is the voice acting. The indian accent gets pretty annoying after just minutes.If you're looking for a cool innovative puzzle game, I'd recommend "Lightmatter" or "the Touring Test" but not this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is a truncated version based on the upper character limit for Steam reviews. For the full version, watch the video.In essence, Relicta fits the term “first-person physics puzzler” about as well as you could imagine: It’s mostly about moving blocks through levels in order to hold down buttons or transport you around. Both things are achieved by what the game calls magnetism, because apparently the cubes and plates you can operate are made of magnetic materials, but honestly, it seems more like you’re able to just manipulate gravity itself even beyond mere magnetism. I say this mostly because the main attraction/repulsion mechanic is actually expanded with a third option that allows you to cancel out downward gravity altogether in order to fling these cubes around without them falling to the ground, so both types of manipulation do similar things.The game is overall structured in a handful of zones spanning a couple of biomes on a moon base, where each zone introduces a new obstacle in a handful of enclosed “test chambers” that you must overcome with the use of your basic powers, which stay the same over the entire length of the game. So while at first you only have to figure out ways to traverse these levels with the aforementioned cubes and mounted plates by giving them a polarity to either attract or repel each other, later challenges introduce switch puzzles, moving platforms, shifting scenery and flying drones that cancel out any polarity you’ve set, so there is a variety of interactions the game gets out of its simple mechanic.And to the game’s credit, it never overcomplicates these additional mechanics. A trap I’ve seen very often in these types of puzzle games that build up in complexity while maintaining a simple basic core of mechanics is that some think throwing in every conceivable obstacle at the player in a single level is a good idea. So it’s usually a sign of quality and that the developer really thought about the challenge curve of their game if they manage to avoid this pitfall.However, the game falls into another pitfall that ended up frustrating me at certain parts. As the term “physics-puzzler” implies, the game relies on physics interactions. And one of the most important aspects of a game that relies on physics interactions as part of its core mechanics is that the physics must be predictable and repeatable. And unfortunately, that isn’t always the case. So while you can set up your blocks and plates in a way that make you think whatever you’re attempting is going to succeed, if the physics system decides to not play ball, you can sometimes lose all progress of any given test chamber through no fault of your own and you have to reset it.While resetting is not that big of a deal in the beginning, because the challenges are all short and snappy, it can cause you to tear your hair out in later stages. Later test chambers are actually multi-stage puzzles, where in order to gather the cubes to move on to the next chamber, you’ll first have to figure out how to get these cubes to the main area of the chamber in the first place. And if the physics system craps itself just before that final hurdle, you’ll have to do the entire thing from the top again, which just isn’t fun. Because at that point, you’re not solving a puzzle, you’re just executing a solution. A proper save-system that saves this kind of progress would’ve been very welcome during some of the later levels.You might have noticed that I mostly focused on the gameplay aspect and haven’t mentioned the story in the slightest here. And that’s because I don’t really think there’s much to say about the story. It’s a fairly generic little tale about a moon colony getting taken over by the titular alien artifact that’s also responsible for giving you the ability to control magnetism and gravity. Most of the narrative happens over the phone because modelling, rigging and animating people is hard, so don’t expect to interact with people face to face. The story is also mostly told at you through not that great voice-acting and your character is either ordered to go somewhere to do something or decides on their own to go somewhere and do something. As it happens, “going somewhere and doing something” always means passing through one of the test tracks littered with the test chambers. So in essence, the whole puzzle aspect, even though it’s initially caused by the MacGuffin du jour, has absolutely no overlap with the narrative. It even goes so far that the main character points out that everything they have to do is always on the far side of one of the test tracks that can’t be circumvented for some convenient reason, so the gameplay actively interferes with the narrative instead of complementing it.I didn’t particularly enjoy these kinds of fourth wall breaks where the game highlights the tedium of trying to move on with whatever you’re attempting to do while constantly being roadblocked by what should be the main attraction of the game. It highlights a certain disconnect in what the game thinks people show up for, because if you include a narrative that makes fun of the gameplay it forces the player to endure and makes it seem like the most tedious aspect of the game, you might end up causing players to ask themselves why they’re even playing a game that makes fun of what players who like puzzle games show up for. And in fact it did cause me to resent the later sections of the game, because the new mechanics they introduce aren’t used in varied and novel ways, you’re just expected to solve five or six challenges that involve the same mechanics, but they almost never ask you to apply the principles you’ve just learned in the first level of any given section in alternate ways in later puzzles, so they literally turn out to be roadblocks I wished I didn’t have to endure on my way to wrap up the narrative.Between the puzzle sections, you have to walk through empty parts of the moon base that are built out of endlessly copypasted segments that all look the same. You can explore a few of the crew quarters, communal areas and laboratories, but there’s no real visual storytelling going on anywhere, it’s just a stereotypical sterile sci-fi environment. The only background lore you can pick up on is communicated through collectibles that you have to go out of your way and find. It sets up this needlessly complex backstory of how these various non-Terran colonies went through revolutions, fights for independence and how they’re currently under a not too favorable administration, which is why the team working at your base must conceal any knowledge about the Relicta seeping out from the colony. Honestly, the game just couldn’t manage to make me give a shit about either the setting or the story it tried to tell and the story actively made me not really look forward to doing the later puzzles because my payoff would just be more badly voice-acted narrative steeped in this terribly overwrought and yet still ill-defined setting. Unfortunately, I can’t really recommend Relicta, not even to fans of physics-puzzlers. The basic gameplay is interesting and while I certainly had fun with some of the puzzles, its overall execution leaves to be desired and the narrative lives in this entirely separate world from the gameplay and it’s just not an interesting tale worth telling. I think a good indicator whether the game was worth playing is provided with the fact that the game contains two additional campaigns, one of which takes place after the narrative of the main game and I didn’t even bother playing either of the two, because I honestly had more than enough after finishing the main game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if I'm seeing things, but I swear every time I go though the main hub, it's just *slightly* different. Like a potted plant has changed to a different, similar plant or some similar change. And considering certain events that I won't spoil, that fits PERFECTLY!I don't care if it's not actually happening and I'm just not noticing certain details until a later trip through, This game is perfectly playing my paranoia, without making me feel threatened! Just puzzles, no real danger. Just keep doing those tests. It's fine. Keep testing. Everything is fine. We can wait for you to finish the tests. We can wait for you to join us...

_childDocuments_.review: In Relicta, you play a woman who's a scientist on the moon. In the biospheres there (ice, desert, jungle ...) she has to test her gravitational gloves which are bades on an artifact.And that's the first minus: The tests that you play are not about the gloves, they are about your ability to solve puzzles. So that story premise makes no sense.Next thing: something happens, she has to get from A to B. Too bad, that there are more test hindering her on the way. So the tests are presented as a nuisance to the player ...And why the hell would you build the test in the way where you have to move from A to B without any possible way around? This makes not a single bit of sense as other characters have moved to the place I need to go, but I'm the only one with the gravitational gloves.That's basically the whole story. OK, there is a bit more to it. The story is only told in uninteractive dialogue after completed tests. Only at a handful of points there are short wannabe-ingame-cinematics.Between the tests you often have to take the maglev-train. And that's where you have to walk through empty train stations. (well there are some emails & logs left to find, but that's all you can do in the train stations.Where in portal you have the e´levator, walk 5 meters and are in the next puzzle room, here you have 3 loading screens, 2 to ~5 doors to walk through, an 'enter the train' animation that has potential to annoy as a time-waster and you always have go to a table with a holographic map to set your destination.Sometimes it feels like 50% walking to the next level and 50% playing that level.That being said about the story - the gameplay of the puzzles is fun.You've got the typical cubes and switches to put them on. You've got the gloves that can magnetize the cubes and certain surfaces. You've got walls for you or the cube. Sometimes you can mark a cube and then teleport it to a teleport exit. Mash all that together and you can generate many maps from that.There is a "story walkthrough" video that is shorter than 5 hours, but that's only when you know the solutions already. I needed 20+ hours for my first playthrough.Finding the solutions is fair. It's mostly 'see what you CAN do and do it'. New puzzle elements and their function are easily recognizable.TL;DR: Gameplay is fun, but prepare for tedious walking between the puzzles. Forget the story.Quality level: Magrunner. Portal and Talos Principle are out of reach for this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Felt no desire to finish the game. Despite a compelling sci fi idea and environment the characters and writing of the game are very poor. The characters are repulsive people despite the good work of the voice actors. It is unrealistic that any of these people could function or hold a job in any professional or team work environment.The puzzles are not difficult in a puzzle solving sense but the difficulty is artificially enhanced where you have to try your same solution over and over until you get the physics and timing right. A lot of the puzzles are very easy to cheese.Even for the $3 on special I paid for it I feel there are better games for the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Cube-n-Button based physics based puzzle platformer, decent story and a large amount of puzzles that will leave you head scratching, even for someone as experienced as me. I've logged 11 hours as of this review and will continue to log many more after this review. Has a very nice difficult curve that doesn't get too difficult to quickly, but also doesn't waste your time teaching you all the super beginner puzzles. Not reccomended for starting out, see Portal / Portal 2 if you want the creme da la creme.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who only just recently realized the PDA serves as a quest tracker and is notoriously unwilling to pay attention to any given storyline, finding my way to the respective puzzle next in line appeared to pose the biggest, as well as most tedious, challenge yet. Until I, to my own astonishment, found myself absorbed in the ongoings of Chandra, which also significantly relieved my directional confusion. Legit one of the most entertaining ingame dialogue styles I’ve come across in years...can't help but love the latest addition to the crew.+ Diversified and generally great level design+ Original approach to the 3D puzzle theme+ Progressive complexity+ Amusing and captivating StoryGo get it, pronto
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Other reviews are already better than what I could write, so I'll just keep it short.  Overall, if you like Portal or other Portal-likes, it's a reasonably fun and challenging game.  It seems to run on a bit long and is a bit repetitive at times.  Also, you'll find yourself solving levels without using all the magnets and stuff that were laid out, so either there are intentionally a bunch of red herrings placed throughout the game, or a lot of ways to cut corners and dodge stuff.  The game usually avoids letting you get yourself trapped, but it's still possible occasionally, meaning you have to hold down R and reset all progress to redo the level up to that point.  Luckily that's pretty rare.I guess that's enough rambling.  I wish some of the other Portal-likes I played were as decent as this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: I have played, but not completed the game and don't think I will reach the end, but still I recommend it.The reason for not finishing this game is that I personally have found that I do not enjoy first person puzzle games that much, however I will not put that as a slight against the game as from what I have played (half way through) the puzzles are good and get increasingly more complex and hard as the game goes on. I found not noticeable hikes in difficulty, but rather a steady increase in difficulty. I would also say this game is harder then Portal 1, but seems to be heading towards the difficulty of some of the later areas of Portal 2.The story was the most enjoyable aspect of the game for me and I liked the world building and lore, it did not just exist as a backdrop or justification for the puzzles.The Characters where enjoyable. The environments are good enough for the story and puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: IMO this is one of the better puzzlers out there. It has a surprisingly engaging plot and probably a higher quantity of puzzles than any other game I've played. The mechanics allow for a surprisingly large amount of diversity in challenges, but still some of the puzzles were repetitive and others felt like I solved them incorrectly.I also appreciate the protagonist being an Indian female, an incredibly under-represented group (I'm pretty sure this is the only game I know of that this is the case). The scenery and environment was also absolutely beautiful.Overall, I definitely recommend. You get a lot of game for the price, and the puzzles and plot were definitely well made and engaging. I don't consider it the best puzzle game I've ever played, but it's among the greats.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta doesn't make the best of first impressions but quickly makes up for that with satisfying game play mechanics and well crafted physics.Voice acting ranges from adequate to good and the dialogue strikes a neat balance between serious and funny.The story/game play balance is also good, delivering portions of the story at the end of each puzzling session.Overall, Relicta is a well made experience more than worthy of it's price tag.
