_childDocuments_.review: Relicta has filled the void in my heart that The Talos Principle left me with after i have finished the game. Finally a truely awesome Puzzlegame, mixed with an interesting setting, beautiful looks and fitting soundtracks! But before i just overwhelm this review with praise lets look at the details and let me explain, why i like this game so much.  You play this game as a scientist who is altering gravitiy with some new future technology and uses it to overcome puzzle levels to study the limits of this technology. You are playing this on Habitats that were created on the moon itself! And if you are woundering, why a scientist should basicly play puzzlelevels...on moonhabitats, that look like Forests, Icefields or Sand Deserts...well there is a very good explanation to it! But i dont want to spoiler it for you so only a few words: The lore in this game is really interesting. Over my lifetime i have played i guess over a thousends of games and i have to say i never saw an sci-fi universe like this before! The storys of what is going on, how the world outside of the game looks, and why there are habitats like this on the moon is really interesting and refreshingly new! I personally was just a bit sad, because since the world is so interesting i would love to learn more about it, that what you learn from the data-logs you collect on the way. Now let us come to the main element of this game: The puzzles!  There are in my opinion two type of puzzle games. There are those like Myst, where you have no idea what is possible and what not and you have to find the solutions in the world while not knowing what you are even supposed to do. These type of puzzle games always turned me off, since after a while i get stuck at some place and i dont have the slieghtest idea what i am supposed to do, if i should be even be here and so on. And then there are games like Portal, or The Talos Principle where you get thought very early the basic mechanic of the game and how it functions...but then the level you encounter are warping this easy concept more and more into a complex monster, where you really need all your brainpower to solve it. But even when the games can become really hard it always feels fair, since you know how the mechanics work, you just have to apply them to this new situation you are confrontet with. Relicta thanksfully fits into the 2nd kind of puzzlegame that i love so much. Your main game mechanic is that you can charge a cube and certain fields positiv or negativ and thus make the Cube beeing pulled towards or pushed from certain object. Also you can remove the gravity from the cubes, so that if they have a certain acceleration into a direction, they can go towards it, until they hit a wall or source that pushes them into a different direction - and thats it! What sounds like a cool concept but that got figured out after a short while let me say you: No! Even after i played this game for 15 hours, the game still finds way to surprise me and force me to think of new ways how to use this mechanic to solve the later puzzles! Also i have to say: This game is hard! Especially in the later stages. But what i love about this kind of game that because you know of all the possible mechanics already early on, it is never unfair! There were points where i was to stubborn with a wrong idea how to solve a puzzle and was thinking "ohh man! This game is bugged! There is no solution" and called it a day...only to come back the next day, with a clear, fresh mind, and figured out a new method that worked this day! Moments like this really give me a great feeling of accomplishment and fun, and they make out  for all the frustration, when i am stuck on a certain puzzle longer then i would like :D Also i have to congratulate the developers for how much polishment must have went through this game! Because since its a physics game in where your cubes can basicly fly everywhere, and since it is a not to big developer studio, i was afraid that there will be many moments where i have to load a savefile because my cube got stuck on impossible locations where you cant reach it anymore, making the solution of this puzzle impossible. And ohh boy did i ♥♥♥♥ up my cube-locations many times. But there was always a clever way how i could still get my cube, or how it could never get stuck on some place where you cant reach it anymore. In general the whole game was totally free from any kind of buggs, and i was really positive surprised how well polished everything plays.  My only critique with this game are the "Angle" puzzles. As you know by now, this game is physic based, but with this cool idea sadly come certain problems. Because the physic of how, where and with which tempo the cubes move is calculated by a physic engine, the outcome can sadly greatly vary. Most of the puzzles are very methodical. If you know what to do, you will accomplish the puzzle in 100% of the times. But there are also a few puzzles where your cube has to move in  a very certain angle to reach his goal without clear sides that will guaranteely push him in this direction...and in this cases you have to pray to RNG'sus that the cube will behave in the way you want to. Sometimes the cube will hit a wall, because you have misplaced your cube by one pixel to much to the left, sometimes you cube dont move at all even though it should, sometimes you make everything exactly as you should but the cube still hits a Wall to fast, and jumping to a location it never supposed to go. There were a few moments where i figured out exactly what to do, but still had to try 2-3 (in the later case even around 20 (  ) of doing the same thing over and over and hopeing that the physic "RNG" will be kinder to me this time around...what as you can imagine is extremly frustrating. But thankfully this kind of puzzles where really rare, and in most cases the difficulty only came from figuring out how to solve a puzzle and not by executing it right in terms of angles. Between solving puzzles your character talks with various characters that are also on the moonbase. This conversations are either pushing the plot forward (because you realise more and more that something is not right) or are just a welcome distraction in between puzzle levels where your character banters with the other Persons of the Station. And even though you sadly never really interact with them, it was so interesting to see how  much you come to care for all the characters from their voices alone! I really have to salute all the voiceactors in this game, i found all of them spot on! There was not a single character where i didnt really had an opinion on, i either really really loved them, or found them very shady and untrustworthy. I also dont know languages enough to hear which accent most of them are talking, but it was so refreshing to hear them talk since its not the generic english that you hear in most other games. I dont know how to describe it: While most of the games i rather thing of "wow this Voiceacting sounds really really bad" or "yep thats good voiceacting, where the characters sound as i think they would sound" i cant think of a nother game where i was looking forward so much of hearing the characters talk again...just to hear their voice, and cute banter once more.All in all, i think that Relicta is a fantastic puzzle game, and a true hidden gem, that sadly dont seem to get the recognition it deserves. If you like the idea of puzzle games look no further, since this is without a doubt one of the best you will find. I wish the developers all the best and cant wait for their next projects, since they really got my attention after i saw how much work was put into every detail of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good puzzle game for the price! Especially with the dlc out, there is plenty of puzzle to do. The major thing to note about this game is that it is more or less a free-form puzzle game. Unlike something like portal placing portals in set areas, you can place the cubes (the primary puzzle manipulation object in the game) wherever you want. One of the outcomes of this system is that it is not always obvious exactly what you need to do. There are some puzzle areas in the game I'm pretty sure I did incorrectly. Even if you are not looking to take shortcuts, or solve things incorrectly, the techniques the game teaches you to use look no different being used right or wrong. I myself think this is fine. There was never any time I could just skip the entire map, just got to the end in an alternative way. The only major problem is when the gameplay is set to be fast. In a game like portal, speed is a big part in many puzzles. In this game you wont be throwing cubes and catching and throwing objects. Just standing in front of a cube to pick it up can sometimes be a problem, a bit finicky. So, when the game wants some "fast" action it isn't very smooth. Luckily it seems the devs understand this limit. The game never goes past its limits, but you can feel it on some puzzle sections. A smaller problem is since you are placing the cubes anywhere, you need to align them carefully or you might shoot it off into nowhere. IT IS possible to soft lock the current puzzle you are on. It only happened to me once, but its just one of the consequence of having a very open puzzle system.One other thing I want to mention. THE STORY, It has to be said. The story is insane, in the insane way. The voice acting is great, but the characters are also insane. Every time the story shows itself, I am being blasted with so much dramatics. The story is very consistent though, but it's like a soap opera turned up to 11, both in style and in volume. So much yelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for the setting. I like sci-fi. This game definitely delivers on this front. The puzzles are good. They are not too difficult even for an inexperienced player. The graphics are good enough. The world is a bit less interactive than I expected. But it is tolerable. In general, it is a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: If you like challenging puzzle games, give Relicta a try. It will wrinkle your brain.BUTIf you like to relax while playing puzzle games, skip Relicta. It's too complex to be relaxing.I'm in the second category. I made it through the Tower level, then - blocked. The difficulty escalated quickly after that point. I don't know if I'm dumb or my brain just isn't wired right to complete magnet-and-gravity puzzles, but it was impossible for me to progress past the Tower without major help from guides & walkthroughs. That's not how I like to play puzzle games, so after 11 hours, quitting for now. Up to that point I enjoyed it - good graphics, good soundtrack, a surprisingly interesting story, and the puzzles were fun too. But those advanced puzzles... Some problems that made the puzzles frustrating:- frequently can't see where to go - ie the objective of the puzzle. - it's not always clear what a switch or pressure pad does.6/10 because I liked it right up to the part where it got too complicated.Linux users: played perfectly using Proton 7.0-5 #Arch #Radeon
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Finished another 1st person view puzzle from my backlog... Wee!Rather than saying this is yet another portal spawn... this one looks more like "The Turing Test" wannabe... as my review on The Turing Test said before, the game is pretty weak for a Square Enix game... so i am not sure why someone will want to follow its footsteps anyway other than the brand power of Square Enix. Anyway, this game is very similar to The Turing Test in most of the way especially in stage design and story telling part.The puzzles of this game is no where near hard, but this turned out to be a pretty hard game. So what's making this game hard? The total randomness of some of its physic is causing a lot of trouble in the puzzle solving, and sometimes we can even solve the puzzle outside the intended solution just because the box floated and slide into a flavorable position. Yes, the box slides and floats with a momentum that's not fit for puzzle building imo... so this game ended up having more than one solution on most puzzles and we can simply cheat our way using those sliding malfuction of the puzzle design. In short, this is not a perfect puzzle design at all, pretty much a fail. And due to the sliding and floating flaws, even when we are doing the intended solution, we will find the box doesn't land on the switches in alignment most of the time. So there's no 100% fool proof solution to any of the puzzle and yeah, some even require "luck".The story, started out pretty great and dramatic, eventhough it gives out a heavy feel of The Turing Test, which is very very linear and no side tracking, they actually pulled it off in telling a story better than The Turing Test imo... but about half way down the story, things started to change, a lot of the story seemed forced on and not very logically placed, more like just adding a detour to the story so they can link it to the puzzle solving part of the game... and pretty rough in the edges joining up the story pieces making some part of the game story feels awkward and out of place. And even though one of the ending turns out pretty nice (with the other being a predictable bad end), we don't get to meet a single living soul in this game, eventhough the protagonist (an old lady that seemingly able to survive high jumps from the puzzles) is talking to several people throughout the whole game, we don't get to meet any of them , we don't even get to see how the protagonist looks like in 3D, only her "profile picture" during her phone calls. Probably the devs are too lazy to make any character models...Well... If this game only have those problems and none else, then i wouldn't have given this review a thumbs down. But what makes things worst is, this game physic engine is actually effected by our graphic settings. When we are playing a game with physical puzzle that require us to control gravity, this type of set off simply is unacceptable. For example, we can jump onto the box easier putting the setting on High, but will have difficulty jumping on the box in Highest setting. The box sliding problem varies with the settings too, when setting the graphic to low, everything seems light weighted. Not only that, the higher the setting, the more difficult to grab the box up, which is super frustrating when the box slide off our grab everytime we try to grab it, and have to repeat a few times or have to grab and turn in slow motion to avoid the box sliding off our hands. That adds to the stress in playing this game. And to top that up, this game has a very weird save system, it doesn't really save at the mini check points, and often require us to replay the game from the beginning of each stage after a continue from last play. Yeah, another fail design imo, and this can adds to the frustration if the game loads before some frustrating puzzle that you've already cleared.And lastly, the physic coding they use in the game is very outdated.. kinda like those clumsy physic in games 20 years ago... almost can't believe this is a game released in 2020 with that type of physic. Well yeah, technically, we are supposed to be on the "Moon", but with the "terraformed" view only and the gravity is like on earth? Well, might as well "pretend" we are on the Moon then, it doesn't matter much since all we see is "Earth" in the game. If you notice the clouds (atmosphere) and water body in the game, then you might just noticed the dev never really did any research prio to their design, they just use the word terraformed to justify everything. Then why the moon anyway? Might as well just said it's on Earth. Oh yeah right... the buggy physic setting, blame it on bad terraforming! Brilliant! (roll eyes)The only stuffs I like about this game is probably the rather beautifully made Terrarium placed all around the place in the game. The graphic is pretty since it's on the Unreal Engine afterall. But that's just it. Other than the graphic, the game is just on the average level, maybe even slightly below average. Can't recommend getting this on its full price, maybe on a large discount then you won't feel so frustrated with those lousy physics they use in game. And don't expect any mind blowing puzzles either, these are pretty easy and not very challenging at all. Those contraption puzzle games for kids probably do a way better job than this game in physic and "fun" imo. So yeah, don't give a high expectation if you wish to give this game a try. The graphic may makes it looks like a great game, but in the end, the graphic is all you've got to enjoy, the rest isn't on par. Story ain't bad, but if it's the story you are after, then my advise is, just youtube a play through and save your money and frustration.Oh, and a little add-on here, this game isn't suitable for for kids either due to it's packed full of the F-words.And... Nauseating alert! This game is by default set to maximum blurring and light effects which can easily cause one to feel dizzy in less than a minute's game play. There are settings in the game that allow us to turn off the effects and blurring as well as camera blobbing and other lighting stuffs but bear in mind that will cost you to end up with a slightly different physic result due to the game's physic somehow rely on graphic settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked The Talos Principle, Portal, or The Witness, this will be right up your alley.  Much like The Talos Principle, Relicta offers individual puzzles in different worlds that grow in complexity as you go.  The anti-gravity and magnetism mechanics, among other features, provide plenty of novel puzzles with interesting solutions.  The game also looks great, and the physics feel real, too.  There is a little more plot here than is required, which I largely ignored, but it does add some flavor on top of the pure puzzles.If you are into puzzle games like those mentions, you'll enjoy Relicta.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is an enjoyable puzzle platformer with some interesting mechanics and a fun story-line. The collectibles help to flesh out the world a bit, making it so you want to find them to learn that much more about this future world. The characters you interact with have unique personalities and desires, some of which are less obvious than others.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: A very strange puzzle game. Not for its puzzles, which are fairly rote magnetic block pushing whose occasional flashes of brilliance are marred by loose controls and inconsistent physics. The game is strange because it's half puzzle game and half walking simulator, and honestly I think it would be more fun without the puzzles. The writing is authentic and well-delivered, the worldbuilding is cliche but reasonable, and you grow to care about these characters and their interactions on this moon base. But to get more of the story, you have to go through yet another cavalcade of blocks and magnets.Overall if you liked Portal and liked The Martian, and are down for a piece of media that's worse than either of them but is trying to be both, it's at least worth a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is a super linear puzzle game. It's simply going from Point A to B, from puzzle to puzzle, the corridors are just fillers. There's absolutely nothing to interact with outside of the puzzles and there are invisible walls everywhere to prevent you from exploring anywhere outside. Soon it becomes a chore rather than being fun. The earlier half of the game genuinely had good puzzles, it made me think and plan, almost made me feel clever but the other half just increases the number of hoops you have to go through just to get the cubes at the right place. For me, it went from 'This new area looks fun' to 'Let's get this over with and move on.'I honestly can't continue playing Relicta anymore. I'm halfway through it but now I'm tired. It's not that the puzzles are hard, but it's a just complete slog to drag around cubes and it started to feel way more tedious than it needs to. I just couldn't see the point of playing the game anymore because I felt I was "working" to get the damn puzzles right. Once you reach the Tropical islands, you'll understand what I'm talking about. The Story and Puzzles are totally disconnected, the sci-fi plot is interesting honestly but it doesn't work with puzzles: Oh a giant alien ate me? Oh I'm getting hallucinations and hearing voices? The AI has gone sentient? My daughter might be in danger? All you can do about it is solving damn puzzles that's it. See where I'm getting at? The only reason I'm leaving a positive review is because it's an indie game and yes I did have fun even though for the short while it lasted. I even smiled from the inside when I saw that the protagonist is Indian. The voice acting is good, even though the speaker is non-native, there is no bad stereotypical Indian accent like Hollywood portrays. Though the quality of dialogue really degrades and no. of F bombs drop more & more and it felt really unnecessary. (I didn't care much but if it is something that bothers you) Maybe I'll continue where I left someday, but for now, I almost feel like I am wasting my time behind it. If you like these type of problem solving puzzle games, the game provides huge amount of content for the price. The graphics are good as well thanks to unreal engine. Surely pick it in a sale if you are thinking about it!
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the few genuinely challenging puzzle games i have played in years. i was honestly expecting the game to be around the 6-8 hour mark but well, from what ive seen the game is gonna be a lot longer than that. the puzzle mechanics are super interesting, one thing i liked was how the game just tells you the basics and lets you figure the rest out. The graphics are next level! aswell as being really well optimised, the only time the game ever lags for me is during cutscenes and well, thats to be expected imo. the one thing i would ask of the devs is to add a fov slider as i find the game hard to play for extended periods with such a small one. it honestly wouldnt be hard with unreal engine but thats the only thing i would change! well done guys
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game I must say that I am looking forward to some DLC or even a second part.Relicta is a puzzle game in which physics-driven cubes play a very, very important role. It may remind you, especially at the beginning of games like Portal, but as the story progresses it becomes its own sub-genre.The premise is easy: Opposites attract each other while equal poles repel each other. What starts out as a simple move of this cube from point A to B in a linear fashion ends up being a challenge for your brain. Move the cube A from point A to point B but in the middle of the way you have to press a button that opens doors, put another polarized cube to attract the one that is traveling and thus make it turn or even prepare a path of polarized plates that in its path open doors to a robot that overrides the polarization and that is your key to the next puzzle.And although when we play this kind of games we want puzzles, puzzles and more puzzles we also find a minimally decent story. The game starts by introducing several characters but it doesn't go deep into any of them so that they end up being irrelevant. - Very varied and even difficult puzzles, with many different mechanics and dynamics.- Visually it has AAA quality.- Optimized and highly polished (no bugs)- The game is immersive, you can go for hours and hours without realizing it.- The story animates the journey between the different puzzles and maps- The developers have greatly improved the game, listening to the feedback of the players, since the first demo.- The story could be tremendously improved.- There are some mechanics that are introduced in the middle of the game that are not explained beforehand and can be frustrating
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: The core of Relicta is pushing and connecting cubes. Move them from area A to area B, attach to exit buttons and proceed to another chamber.Simples?No story whatsoever. Lots of swearing though! Right, there's Moon research stations with giant domes, inside which main characters play with cubes.What's the purpose of magnetic maps, origin of that purple mineral - who does even care. Just solve room by room and listen to another bunch of f-words. Puzzles on their own are great. Have to consider multiple elements:angled pole platforms, force fields (one for you, another for a cube), pole alternating fields, drones intercepting cubes, timed platforms and soft locks...Incorrectly calculate trajectory - you cube flies accros a map. Hesitate a bit and a drone carries your cube away.Nice game to play solely for solving puzzles (I get serotonin for that!)Horrible story with inadequate language for no reason. "F-you, f-them"... really?
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: This game is .... OK I guess. It looked good from the screenshots and it does look good in-game but that's 90% of the best thing about this game: how it looks. For the rest it's basically a very poor man's Portal but with annoying voice actors, a mediocre story and worse puzzles. Despite the game's good graphics, the game lacks a soul - the environment is far too clean and lacks detail to make it a believable world. In Portal you had the excuse that they were test tracks - here you have squeaky clean corridors & rooms with at most a cup of coffee here and there. OK, the game was made on a small budget but giving heart to your game to me is a very important element and it wouldn't take all that much effort to do. Just add some more personal notes, leave around personal effects, show the world has been lived in.The game also uses the lamest excuse for you to do puzzles. Crew trapped and freezing in an arctic biome? "Well you have to do the puzzles to reach them". Yeaaah right. Because the only route anywhere is through  a giant maze of puzzles using gloves only you are wearing. What nonsense.I have to give props to the devs for trying but a game is more than a "by the numbers" thing and I feel that it doesn't offer enough outside its basic scope. You have a "story" which is not all that interesting and it's clear the game comes up with excuses for you to do pretty lame box puzzles. Portal had a far better mechanic than this and also had GlaDOS to keep things interesting. This game only offers some annoying people with heavy Indian accents blabbing in your ear all the time.It's a 5/10 basically - at this point I'd rather they'd have cut all the story nonsense and just given you a bunch of puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Nice graphics. But story is poor and puzzles become boring.The density of puzzles is too high, after 20 minutes of the game you start to get tired.Big job were done, but in my opinion it was better to split this game on several small ones and rich the gameplay with cutscenes and plot. it's 6/10I gave up in the middle of the game and watched the rest walkthrough on youtubeP.S. I played Portal, The Stanley Parable, The Turing Test, Superliminal, The light matter, etc. They all are cool because plot events and puzzles are balanced there. Unfortunately, this is not the case of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Hidden gem of puzzle games. I really enjoyed beating it. The difficulty was balanced just right for me - not boringly easy when you can read the solution as soon as you enter the puzzle room, but not tediously hard so you could get really stuck. A few puzzles can be cheesed or at least feel like you solved them in an unintentional way. But this was actually also satisfying, because it felt more like you outsmarted the game, instead of it being just broken. The story is ok and the characters are likable. Great game, it deserves more attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: A bit more fleshed out lore than Portal, and a bit more puzzle difficulty as well.The game is decent, with a few minor hiccups here and there. IE. -Some puzzles requires pixel perfect placement-Some puzzles does not have enough checkpoints or method / ways to undo a mistake.Game time: About 7~10 hours of puzzle solving + 2 expansions.Relicta is a generally decent first person puzzle platform game. Basically Portal, but with Magnets and Gravity.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: You are a lunar scientist with some magic gloves that let you control gravity and magnetic polarity of magic cubes. You can ride the cubes and make interesting trick shots.This game is the other side of the coin of Portal games. Nice puzzles and definitely deserves a playthrough.It also works on Linux through Proton-GE
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: -Some puzzles were extremely tedious if you messed up even in the slightest. The difficulty never really ramps up, the puzzles just get longer with more and more opportunities to mess something up-Waiting for the drones to move around was painful.-Why is there a speed running achievement? I don't see how you could think it's a good idea to have that achievement in the game -Collisions are very bizarre, boxes getting stuck midair, yourself getting stuck midair, etc.it's painful looking at my stats and being one off of 100% for this game, but there's no way I'm playing through the game again. The overall story is good, but the dialogue is jam packed with vulgar language that really ruined it for me.I'd give this game a 5.5 I guess, I really liked the art style, but almost everything else is sub-par
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: I like puzzles but this first-person story is boring. I'd rather skip any lore or cutscenes. Just take me to the puzzles. Okay, I didn't think this was going to be puzzle game at all. I just like the nice scenery but I think that's what the game is trying to do. It shows nice scenery but only allows you to enjoy if you beat the puzzles. This game also reminds me of another first-person puzzle game that is much better than this game. I wouldn't waste your money on this game unless you love puzzles. If you like first-person puzzle games, then get this game while its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Very well made physics puzzle game with a lot of levels for the price - took around 40 hours to beat the whole game altogether.  Each new puzzle presents it's own challenges and there are sometimes multiple ways to solve the same puzzle if you look closely enough.  My only slight complaint is that the solutions to the puzzles feel cheap sometimes - like carrying a box sideways up a stair way that has purple box-blocking barriers, and then moving the mouse around until the box is in just the right position to be placed over the railing at the top.  My advice - not all solutions are elegant.  If you're stuck, try something that might seem stupid.  This is probably only about 5-10% of the puzzles in the game.The story was decent and kind of funny at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta will always be compared to games like Portal and The Talos Principle and out of those three it comes a strong third. The short version of this review is that yes, it's a good game, yes, you should give it a go if you like first person physics puzzlers, no it's not the best of its kind, and no it's not going to be your favourite.PUZZLESThe puzzles themselves are clever though it's worth saying that they aren't super taxing. I had to get a fair bit of help with later levels in Portal and Talos Principle whereas with Relicta I didn't have to check all that often and usually I was stuck because I'd not seen something, rather than I didn't get the solution. That'll be a pro or con depending on how much of a challenge you want.The magnetism and zero-gravity mechanics are solid and the puzzles well put together - levels are well designed so that most sections can be re-attempted without a length reset if you mess up - only in some parts of the Ice Queen update did I find some of the harder puzzles had really tedious resets if you missed something.The weakest part is that by half way through the base game you've been taught all the different tricks. The rest of the game is is still solid but you've had all of your "oh that's cool" moments. Ice Queen adds some new mechanics which were good fun though.The other downside is that some of the puzzle rooms got quite big and there's no mid-puzzle saving. The levels in the Aegir Gig update even warn you about this - those ones are pretty fun levels though.The visuals are very good for a game of this nature, and they developers put extra work in for the two free expansions (Aegir Gig and Ice Queen) that they could easily have avoided, just reusing old assets.The story is pretty average average, lacking the punch of Portal or the background intrigue of Talos Principle. I think the voice acting would have been helped if the script had less swearing in it - the bad language didn't add anything to the drama and the actors had to pour a lot of energy into the swearing which undermined their other efforts.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Truly beautiful visuals. Especially impressive how good it looks without that RTX nonsense.Challenging and demanding puzzles.Sometimes indecent, vulgar language.Annoying, childish dialogues and moody, noisy, not likable characters. Although I liked the idea of having some plot in a puzzle game but that was poorly written.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that boasts about how beautiful its environment is, it sure works its hardest to make sure you explore hardly any of it with invisible walls at every corner.Extremely restrictive movement (no crouch or even jumping in certain sections) makes completing puzzles you already know the solution to a challenge, and not much in the way of innovating to solve a puzzle in an unintended way (because of all the invisible walls).The attempt to put a story was ok but felt weak, am i really supposed to believe people use language that is outdated today over 100 years in the future?I wanted to like this game but solving the puzzles wasn't as fun as it is in other 3d puzzle games like Talos Principle etc. If you are desperate for a new 3d puzzle game buy it on sale but I would skip it at full price
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: As a copy of Portal and the Talos Principle, this falls short. the plot is not original and the gameplay is repetitive. Not to mention that the puzzles are boring and the graphics tend to be generic.I don't recommend this one unless you received it for free. Otherwise save a little and buy the originals. Portal 1 and 2, The Talos Principle, among similar ones that are far better than this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Portal done wrong, just replace portals with magnetism and gravity.The story is dragged out and boring. Luckily it can be skipped.There's a gazillion of pointless animations you have to wait out - PDA opening. Sliding cards into PDA. Touching to open the doors. Especially lovely when you have no idea where to go and so pointlessly wait to open doors you've already opened twice.There's no reason why a game of this concept should require a significant amount of computing power to not be laggy. But for whatever reason the authors decided it'd be a good idea to spam the game with foliage and stuff. The hands just flailing around in the air are kinda pointless too, especially since you can't see the rest of your body when you look down.All controls are made for two handed play - one hand on the keyboard, one on the mouse. So why in the world did they put the PDA key to I and not TAB?Essentially the only good element in this game is the puzzle element. With that the authors did a good job and since it's the main aim of the game, I am willing to recommend it for that. But the game as a whole is unimpressive, with rather mediocre design.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: An hour in, already scratched my head a few times learning the mechanics/possibilities!so, that's better than most other puzzle games i've tried recently!graphics are a solid 9/10audio is 8/10 (+1 for more interesting accent variety)gameplay so far 8/10 (1st section past tutorial done) oh also, Motion blur is under accessibility optionsand the game runs really well so bump the supersampling to 120% (GTX1070, i7 6700)
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Any experienced gamer will romp through this, the puzzles themselves are not difficult. In the same way Portal was just a 3D rendering of a classic puzzle game, so is this, the logic behind the puzzles is basic with a graphical wrapper. While that sounds harsh, it's no different to tons of other puzzle games out there.I mentioned Portal, this is nothing like Portal in the sense that the storyline is just cancer. If you can manage to listen to more than 3 lines of truly awful dialogue and take note of the overly sentimental nonsense storyline then well done you, I certainly never managed it.Is it a bad game? No, it's certainly not a bad game. Has there been considerable time and effort put into the title? Sure, you can see that. Is it "good"... em... well that really depends on your experience, imo. If you are new to puzzle games then this is as good as any other to get (if you can deal with the dialogue) but anyone who has played similar puzzle games will find that once you scratch the surface of this game all you find is more surface.It's a 'no' from me, if only because Steam doesn't have a 'meh' option.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game so far! Great graphics and storyline! Voice acting on point. The puzzles are interesting and not over the top.  From what I gather, you are a scientist experimenting with technology discovered by a shady lab that dissapeared, technology decades past what it should be. Sounds like a good idea, right? Things seem to go well for two or three years. But at the start of the game you find out something went wrong! Now, you will find out what happened. The main character is an indian woman with a daughter which was a nice change from the usual caucasian male. I love her spunky attitude and rebellious nature. She also comes off as responsible and wanting to make the world a genuine better place, not a crazy scientist who will explore new tech even if it destroys all humankind. I never realized how often the crazy mad scientist sterotype came up before this. The nature graphics and lab were really cool to see too. My favorite are the little flying robots.  Despite my short time playing the game so far, I am confident I will keep playing. Check it out!

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta : By Triple F"Relicta" by Mighty Polygon is a first-person puzzle game that combines physics-based mechanics with an atmospheric sci-fi setting to create a unique, cerebral experience. Set on a lunar research base, the game challenges players to solve a series of complex puzzles using gravity manipulation, magnetism, and creative thinking. Though it has drawn comparisons to games like Portal and The Talos Principle, "Relicta" stands out with its own unique mechanics and compelling narrative backdrop, inviting players to both explore and unravel the mysteries of the moon’s Chandra Base.The game’s story revolves around Dr. Angelica Patel, a physicist who uncovers a mystery surrounding the moon base she’s stationed on. There’s a clear focus on narrative here, with well-written dialogues and an engaging storyline that gradually reveals the protagonist’s motivations, her relationship with her daughter, and the dangers lurking in the isolated environment of Chandra Base. Through audio logs and in-game interactions, players gain insights into the backstory, and there’s a real sense of tension as the story unfolds. The combination of a sci-fi thriller plot with personal stakes adds a layer of depth that is often missing from puzzle games, and the game’s dedication to storytelling keeps players invested between puzzles.The core mechanics of "Relicta" center around the manipulation of gravity and magnetism. Players use these abilities to move colored cubes across platforms, through obstacles, and around increasingly elaborate puzzle rooms. Each cube can be manipulated to have different polarities and gravitational effects, which players must use strategically to reach each level’s exit. The mechanics are gradually introduced, allowing players to learn the nuances of each ability before more complex challenges emerge. The physics system feels both intuitive and rewarding; puzzles require precision and timing, but they also encourage experimentation, as players can often approach them in multiple ways. This open-endedness in puzzle-solving allows for creativity, making each solution feel satisfying.Visually, "Relicta" does an excellent job of creating a sense of place and isolation. The game alternates between stark, sterile laboratory environments and outdoor areas that showcase the moon’s desolate yet beautiful landscapes. The environments are filled with small details that reinforce the game’s sci-fi aesthetic, and lighting plays a key role in establishing mood. Each sector of Chandra Base has its own visual theme, from icy landscapes to red-hued caverns, which helps keep the visuals fresh as players progress. While the graphics may not be groundbreaking by today’s standards, the art design is cohesive and atmospheric, creating a sense of realism that complements the cerebral tone of the game.The audio design in "Relicta" is another strong point, using subtle ambient sounds and a haunting score to underscore the game’s tone. Dr. Patel’s voice acting is well-performed, conveying both her professionalism and vulnerability, and the audio logs she discovers provide additional context that enriches the story. Background noises like the hum of machinery or the faint rumbling of lunar landscapes, enhance the sense of isolation and danger. The soundtrack, while minimalistic, is used effectively to build suspense and focus players’ attention on the challenges ahead, without distracting from the puzzles or story.One of the main criticisms of "Relicta" lies in its pacing. The game’s puzzles can be mentally exhausting, especially as they grow more challenging, and the story segments that break up puzzle sequences sometimes feel too brief to offer proper relief. The balance between narrative and gameplay is sometimes skewed, leaving players with little respite during lengthy puzzle-solving sections. Additionally, some puzzles may feel overly difficult or unintuitive, which could lead to frustration for players not accustomed to extensive trial-and-error. The save points are well-placed, but certain sections require precise timing, which can lead to repeated attempts that break immersion for some.Considering all this, players seeking a mind-bending puzzle experience with a strong narrative, "Relicta" offers a rewarding and immersive journey. Its challenging puzzles, combined with an intriguing story and atmospheric design, make it a standout among physics-based puzzle games. While it may be less accessible to casual players due to its difficulty and pacing, it’s a game that rewards patience and creativity. Overall, "Relicta" carves out a niche for itself, offering a sci-fi puzzle adventure that is as thoughtful as it is challenging.

_childDocuments_.review: The main game wasn’t that bad but the DLC is quite a bit worse.  In the main game there were a lot of solutions where you could kinda abuse the physics to send a cube to a place at a weird angle or ride it somewhere unintended as a shortcut and it feels like to combat it in the DLC they made these physics jank solutions the intended pathway.  And maybe milk it a bit too much.  You can have a sensor on a wall and with two cubes you can do this trick where you stack them, make the top one levitate, move the bottom one and offset it, then make them repel to drive the cube into the sensor.  The first time it’s a puzzle, but when they reuse the -exact- same trick at the end of the next three puzzles it’s just tedious.  To make things harder they start hiding solutions by not using the easy to aim set-ups and instead rely on placing a cube the correct part of a 360 degree circle so it’s aimed correctly which involves a lot of repeating meaning you can solve a puzzle and get stuck on tedious repetition and split second timing trying to get the execution down.  Doesn’t help the physics is sometimes buggy and things get stuck on weird theoretically flat surfaces or edge geometry and if you don’t have a cube recovery device in the section you’ll sometimes have to restart the entire level.Story isn’t that great either.  Some of the elements in it are interesting to find out more about but I cannot think of a single likeable character in all of the game and in one DLC it feels like the writing and acting direction was think of the most annoying and condescending dialogue and tone you can take exaggerated to the limits of believability, and then double it.  There was a forum post that mentioned how all the swearing was a bit off-putting but I didn’t think that much of it at the time.  I was not expecting excessive use of expletives to be a major part of the characterization and development of the alien AI thing.But the one thing that really makes this game unpleasant to play is the lack of a feature, quicksaves.  Especially with all the physics jank solutions in the DLC.  You have to aim boxes via repulsion in situations where you have no alignment guidance and then when you fail you have to repeat entire sections.  You click the wrong button or stand in the wrong place and a cube becomes unrecoverable so you have to repeat the entire section.  A cube would get caught on flat surfaces or I’d miss the split second window to shift colors and would need to repeat both that section and the one right before it.  I missed a 2 second window to middle click on a cube as it flew by and had to wait 58 seconds for it to path back to try again.  All of this could have at least been mitigated with quicksaves.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Decent puzzler. Wait for a sale.If you like first person puzzlers, there is a good chance you'll enjoy this somewhat.The game feels little uneven. What I mean is some puzzles are great. Sometimes the puzzles are difficult and it takes me a while to figure out the solution and when I have the “aha” moment, it feels great and then I can solve the puzzle. But then there are the puzzles where I immediately see the intended solution right away, but is tedious and annoying to execute, requiring way too many retries just to execute the solution that I already understand but can’t quite get the timing of. I hate those puzzles.And then there are the puzzles that I have the aha moment and can see how it *should* work, but I can’t convince the floating cube to go to the precise direction that I needed to and it either gets stuck or falls into a place where I can’t reach it and I have to start the long puzzle over again from the beginning just to retry the part that doesn’t work consistently, and I just get frustrated. So then I look up the solution on YouTube to make sure that I am doing it right, and the person that provided “a” solution was also frustrated, but found a more advanced yet  *easier* way to bypass half the puzzle, so I never actually learned if I was doing it right. 🤣The PDA button is so easy to accidentally press on a gamepad, and takes so long to go through the animation before you can dismiss it. Thankfully, you can remap (or remove) the button that triggers the PDA.I didn't care for the music. What I mean is that music does a lot to create the atmosphere, and I felt like I didn't connect with the atmosphere, and when I thought more about it, I realized it was the music. It was too quiet, and is lacking something. It helped to turn up the music volume, and turn down all the other volumes.One of my biggest gripes is the inability to save in the middle of a puzzle, and no chapter select to easily replay specific levels.One thing I really appreciated was the inclusion of a "run" button, so I can move around faster.Some of the puzzles seem to have parts that have no reliable solution, and are based on luck.In a couple cases, I'm not even sure how I'm "supposed" to solve the puzzle, and when I found a solution, it feels like I broke the puzzle or solved it in an unintended way. I like that I was able to progress to the next level, but when I solve something because a box floats and bounces around randomly, and coincidentally *accidentally* ends up where I need it to go, that doesn’t feel right and it's not a satisfying solution.I didn’t like the writing. The voice acting is OK, I mean, there were some parts I didn't like, but the acting was not terrible. It irritates me when one character supposedly interrupts another character, so they stop talking mid sentence, but there is a pause/silence before the next line is played. But that's not really the fault of the voice actors. The story was OK. I didn't find the story terribly compelling. It was merely there to string together the puzzles to provide a reason for doing them. I stopped caring about the characters and just wanted to get through all the puzzles. I really liked the last set of puzzles.Overall, it was still an enjoyable game to play because I purchased it at a good sale price ($3), but does not compare to my favorite first person puzzlers: Portal, The Talos Principle, and The Entropy Centre.I will never get the speed run achievement because it would be too frustrating for me to redo all the puzzles with a time limit.I do wish there was a level select, or at least chapter select, or a way to replay specific puzzles, since there were some puzzles that I really liked, and some of the more frustrating ones could be considerably less frustrating if I could retry them… easily.

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is a mixed bag for me. Belongs squarely to same genre of games as Portal 1&2 and The Talos Principle (TTP), it isn't nearly as good as those.The good:- looks very nice, especially the jungle levels; some levels are really laid out in three dimensions- some "new" physics compared to the classics mentioned above: anti-gravity and magnetism- a good amount of play time- you probably never have to reset a puzzle because you're really stuck- keept me playing while waiting for TTP 2The bad:- the puzzles in the second half of the game just keep getting longer/bigger, way too long really, without really feeling more interesting or even harder- the constant verbal abuse in the first half of the game was really annoying to me- the story isn't bad, but really thin and formulaic- various usability issues: the game tries to make a number of actions easy (like grabbing or dropping a cube), but often fails to do so (gets your intent wrong and pulls you away), and this is mildly irritating- the hall areas are a real waste of time, even though they look okay- the areas LOOK open for exploration, and yet they are clearly notOverall, I don't think it's worth the full price, and not worth playing to the end (except for the sets). I think I'll skip the two DLCs, even though they were included.Recommended with caveats, only if you're a real fan of the genre, and in need of more 3D puzzles, whatever they are.

_childDocuments_.review: Some believe that puzzle games should be all about brain and not require dexterity or luck. I leave it up to you to decide for yourself. But in Relicta, you will need a little dexterity and a little luck. Sometimes you will struggle with one or the other and might be frustrated because 1) you know what needs to be done but you can't quite do it or 2) there is a subtly new way of interacting with the universe that you did not yet realize and the game did not do a good enough job of teaching you. I don't mean a new mechanism, but a known mechanism that you need to manage a little differently. You'll know what I mean when you encounter it. So listen, this game is not perfect, but there is delight along the way, there is satisfaction, and there is a LOT of content. A lot. An outlier in that respect. The puzzles are not easy. The setting is visually interesting and not just an afterthought as is too often the case with puzzle games. I wasn't too into the story aspect but there is that for those who like it (and the rest can skip it). Also, you should know there is abundant swearing. Despite its flaws, I am fond of this game and it is without doubt excellent value for the money. I will look forward to this studio's other games.

_childDocuments_.review: some "solutions" are so obscure, they ruin the puzzles for me. the physics sometimes makes no sense at all (same setup, different outcomes) and the game gives you absolutely zero feedback when you need it the most. especially for a game like this, the rules need to be absolutely clear, otherwise the player spends his time making random guesses because it's unclear whether something is supposed to work or not. you need to be able to solve these things in your head. it shouldn't be necessary to repeat the same thing many times to see if it's possible in game. if you had the correct idea, the game needs to show you that. if your idea is wrong, it must *clearly* not work. but in relicta, things often barely work (or don't), so the player is often lost in an ocean of maybes.not a single time i looked up a solution did i think "oh, I was so stupid". it was always "wait, *that* was an option?". the game simply fails to present the rules and sometimes hides relevant puzzle elements or how they are supposed to be used. sometimes  the rules change without any notification, like when you're suddenly required to micromanage a floating cube (until thast point you always only had to set things up correctly in advance)

_childDocuments_.review: As of now, I haven't finished Relicta, but I feel like I have a good grasp on what it is about. Hell, I think I've already seen pretty much everything the game has to offer. Let's start with the positives: graphics are truly gorgeous - beautiful landscapes, detailed environments with vibrant colors and artistic lighting. Levels create a calming mood further enhanced by nice atmospheric music. It's a shame that you can't really explore the world you traverse. Futuristic technology present throughout the game has a distinctive look (the cube design is especially cool), although a bit generic. Nevertheless, it contrasts really well with naturalistic biomes you encounter. I don't care about the story, didn't watch a single cutscene, so I have no opinion on it. The overall premise of manipulating magnetic fields and gravity is also cool and pretty unique - I love the inclusion of cube-riding, very satisfying way of moving around. I would say puzzle design is solid and creative at times, when they force you to think outside of the box, but..BUT... Relicta becomes very repetitive very quickly. You use the same mechanics over and over again ad nauseam, puzzles feel too similar to each other, barely introducing any new mechanics whatsoever. From what I've seen on YouTube, final levels aren't very different from the ones in the beginning. As the game progresses, puzzles become needlessly large, even maze-like, but more often than not you know exactly what to do after like 20 sec of exploring, but still need to run around doing tedious chores for about 5 mins before you're able to progress. Wonky physics and janky hitboxes are your bread and butter. Not to mention, at times all I can see is a visual cluster♥♥♥♥ of colorful magnetic fields, cubes and laser fields. And don't get me started on the hub area, it's totally pointless and legit annoying after a couple of hours.Overall, not a bad game, but don't expect anything amazing. It's just a mediocre experience. Another Portal wannabe.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: This was a good puzzle game, very much like "Q.U.B.E." but with beautiful (and less oppressive) environments.The puzzle aspects are almost all based on manipulation of gravity and magnetism. The physics (at least for me) worked well and were very intuitive (remember that magnetism can go through surfaces!), and only a few times I had to fudge around my solution to get it to work in ways which seemed unintended.... oh, probably my fault for trying strange solutions.Besides, the graphics are absolutely gorgeous to look at, and I found the story and dialogue well written (mind you, characters use the F-words frequently, so, if that bothers you, you might want to stay away; and the main character has "plot blindness" for a while, but that is oh-so-common in all media).Some flaws: the game severely limits your ability to go explore the environment, using many artificial walls; but that might be a good thing -- the "space station" environments, which do allow some exploration, are graphically pretty but very empty and lifeless (nearly non-interactable), which comes across as very boring. I would rather have limited but interesting exploration than lots of freedom to do boring stuff (looking at you, collectibles).But all in all, an enjoyable puzzle game, not as creative as Portal or The Talos Principle (in part because there are very few different puzzle mechanics), but still a nice romp, with an interesting story. Score: 82/100.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like cube and physics based problem solving games like Talos Principle, Portal and Quantum Conundrum, then you'll like this too.Big game with many hours of play - don't forget to play the 2 extras as well, as these also add additional game mechanics, and are quite long games in their own right.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is a pretty good physics puzzle game. It wouldn't have the broader appeal of the Portal games but for fans of these type of games it may be worthwhile.The puzzles are of pretty good quality. At it's heart it revolves around manipulating magnetism and gravity to move cubes around to the right switches. The puzzles are challenging but generally manageable. Some of the puzzles once you get further in to the game are quite convoluted and can be a bit overwhelming to take in once you first enter a puzzle area. But with looking around and a bit of trial and error it's usually possible to break the steps to complete it down. That said I did on occasion have to consult a video guide to figure some parts out. But it was usually a case where I was stuck on one specific part of a puzzle and could usually figure the rest once I'd seen how to do the part that was troubling me.The areas the test tracks are set in look really nice too. The game is set on the Moon but most of the puzzles take place in biome domes so rather than doing the test tracks in sterile lab rooms you'll find yourself in an icy biome or a jungle one and I thought this variation in scenery helps especially as it's a fairly long game.It's the parts in between the puzzles that are kind of dull. When moving from one biome to another you'll find yourself running around samey corridors to find the train in the next area. Even though there are collectable items and logs in these areas it just feels like padding. The story just isn't interesting enough to make those inbetween bits worthwhile. In fact at times the story feels hilariously disconnected from the actual gameplay. The story is basically about an alien lifeform taking over the moonbase and it feels more appropriate for a shlocky 00's sci fi first person shooter rather than a physics puzzle game. It often doesn't really make sense why your character is just going through the motions and solving puzzles when all that is going on in the background. Also all the human characters are quite annoying.But I dont want to be too harsh because even while I didn't like the story parts of the game, you can tell a lot of heart went into the game. The puzzles I enjoyed, even if the main campaign feels a bit long. If you are still itching for more puzzles there's also two short extra campaigns which are a free addition so thats a nice touch too. All in all it's not an amazing game but I liked it overall and would recommend if you fancy a some physics based puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles are quite good, but there are a few levels that could have used a bit more play testing - you can skip some mechanics or brick the level and you'll be forced to restart the puzzle. Most of the time they are short enough so this is not an issue, but it was especially painful when it happened for me on one of the last puzzles that is quite large and I had to replay it again. It can be infuriating.That being said, the game is ~17 hours long. Even if the puzzles are based around the same core mechanics, each new level presents a new variation that keeps you thinking. The last few levels can look complicated and even messy, but on further inspection they are just several puzzles stitched together that are solved one at a time. These can be daunting, but the difficulty is manageable.Story is OK. Sound and voice is good. The only thing to note is that there are no footsteps sound when you're running around the ship.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Medium to hard puzzles, sometimes requiring to think outside of introduced game mechanics. A bit of platforming or timing-based stuff, but mostly no rush. Mildly interesting storyline. Quality product for puzzle lowers, but might be too hard for those without puzzle games experience or creative mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Solid graphics and performance, an although cliche story of an alien entity found on the moon but there's a mystery to it and it it is presented by a solid voice cast. The dialog could use fewer edgy f bombs though and a less angsty protagonist. There are also datapads littered around the game in random places, with a wealth of background information that is just a poor and passé design and really something that should have been weaved in to the overall narrative more fluidly.The core of the game is ultimately the puzzle solving, but by the time I made it roughly half way through the game and hit the Glacier Test Track, I had had more than enough of them and was ready for the story to truly unfold at that point and not continue to have it served up piecemeal.Given the perhaps physics nature of the puzzles, or due largely to their design, too many of their solutions ends being affected by randomness or unpredictable cube behavior, or dexterity/timing check, leading to a repetition that adds to the tedium of the puzzle designs.The puzzles becomes more and more tedious as you progress through increasingly convoluted and confusing map designs, that just serves to drag out the game and ultimately overstay their welcome.Ultimately solving the puzzles doesn't feel rewarding in the end, more so they offer a sense of relief from the tedium of not having to go them again, until the game serves up another more tedious puzzle. And the satisfaction in solving the puzzles is really why you play a puzzle solver game in the first place, right?
