_childDocuments_.review: Played for 6 hours so far, probably 35, 40% of the way through. Some quite challenging puzzles, nothing too hard yet, a lot of new mechanics thrown at you with no hints however it does kind of make a tutorial out of each new mechanic in the sense that you will learn it yourself & then continue to use it. I've only been stumped on one level so far but because of the games' physics it allows you to experiment in a bunch of different ways to find the right solution. I'm sure I've completed some levels in non-intended ways which is actually fun. Would Recommend, 8/10(Received through a humble bundle subscription)
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is one of the better first person puzzle games, but still a far cry from Portal 2.The visuals are fine, the story is ok, and conversations are mostly nicely written, and sometimes have some great puns.However, the puzzles quickly turn from fun into chore (which is evident by the fact that 70% of the players completed the first area, only 40% completed the second area, and then less than 20% completed the next one, with only 10% of the people finishing the game).Even when you do everything correctly, sometimes a box fluctuates just a bit away, making you miss the button or a platform, and forcing you to redo part of the challenge (and that's not because of bad performance, I had stable 60 fps). Furthermore, the game has a lot of minor issues with collisions, which become more and more evident and infuriating as the puzzles become more complex and longer to finish.Finally, some puzzles are divided into clear stages, but those stages don't have checkpoints between them. Since some puzzles could easily take you half an hour to figure out (withot using a solution, of course), you then have to redo part of those if you have to go away from the game. In my case the game crashed once in the middle of a puzzle, just after a spot that could've easily been a checkpoint, so I had to spend 5-10 minutes to redo the first part of the puzzle. And again, it took 5-10 minutes only because I already knew how to complete that part optimally.So overall, while Relicta is certainly not a bad game, it has its flaws which make it far less enjoyable than it could be had the developers added more checkpoints and polished controls/physics more.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually very good and entertaining with puzzles even if it keeps falling between chapters due to repetitive tasks, so it's taking me long time to proceed. Admittedly it's wrapped in a beautiful graphic, both inside the base and outside in the various biomes. Even sounds and voice acting are great but... WHY that pointless tsunami of profanities tempesting all along the game? 65% of the words being spoken are profanities.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: The world is great, the story is alright. Most of the puzzles are fine, but they are physic based. That means that sometimes you got to fiddle with the magnet fields to make them go at, what it feels, not the correct way, but is. I don't like that there is not a clear and consistent way to solve some of those puzzles. It seems sloppy at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: I like puzzle games, but this one falls short. I keep having to repeat the same solution multiple times, not because what I'm doing is wrong, but because the games physics is too unpredictable. The story, which is usually the hook for me, was very lack luster and a lot of the world is presented in text documents. The story is also very strange. You're trying to save people's lives, but there's cube puzzles standing between you and your friends freezing to death. You ask the game to turn off the puzzles so you can save the lives of the people who work for the company, but the game tells you if you do that it's going to snitch on you and you'll get in trouble... for trying to save lives and not complete 50 cube puzzles when time is critical. O...K...Also, the lady who I think is your best friend, cusses you out every time you talk to her. She's a massive a*hole and the dialogue between them is not engaging or enjoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Positive: -nice graphics              -general mechanics are easy to understandNegative: -The physics puzzles are all based on moving magnetic boxes around                -The game is reaaaaaaaally slowly paced                -Puzzles become longer and longer which is frustrating when a puzzle bugs out and you have to restart everythingI got this game from Humble Choice. If you are planning to buy this, buy on sale. It's definetly not worth 20 bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: This game is enjoyable, but I don't find the puzzles as satisfying as a lot of similar FPS puzzle games. Often they seem to rely on quirks rather than logical deductions.I also don't particularly care about the narrative, but for this type of game it's definitely not make or break. For me its hard to be as engrossing as Portal 2 or even Lightmatter. Definitely worth the sale price though!Edit: Honestly the puzzles completely lost my interest like 1/3 or 1/2 through and I'm not even going to finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Nice puzzle game, even though quite unpolished. Graphics is great! Story is fine... but you can totally feel that this is another of those games that was made for console and then forced onto PC. Also for Physics-based puzzler this game has HORRIBLE arcade physics! Also a LOT of part of the game do not make any sense, it is a bit mess ...Still the game is not bad
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Story is bland and transparent. The language of the characters seems forced and jarring. The areas between the puzzles although pretty, are so similar I found myself getting lost. Puzzles are forgettable and tedious.  This might seem like nick picking, but I feel it's important. There is this one puzzle in portal, where there are a series of elevated platforms. You bounce up an down while making your way up. I always think of that puzzle when portal is brought up. It was fun, it was memorable, it's one of the many reasons I recommend that game.  The puzzles in this are like a game of Simon, you start off with a few steps to complete the puzzle. The next puzzle is the same as the previous, except there is a new step at the end. I wouldn't say it's a bad game, but I will not recommend it to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: I have a love-hate relationship with this game. On one side, I like how it really goes deep into the base mechanics of the puzzles by not adding almost any extra feature alongside the whole game, and just exploring how the different elements work together and how you can exploit some of the physics involved.Buuuuut then the puzzles are longer and more tedious the further into the campaign you are, reaching a point where, when you enter a new puzzle and see such quantity of elements all packed into a tiny space, knowing that if you decide to take on the challege you have to do it in one go because there are no checkpoints mid-puzzle or saving features, that your brain just says "please don't".But in the end I've liked the game and, with the free DLCs they released, this is one of the few puzzle games that has given me over 20 hours of handcrafted playtime, so I can't really not recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: got to give it a thumbs down. especially after trying my damnest to use the keyboard/mouse and even controller after reading the constant reviews. it shows some promise, but the lack of consistent physics with the boxes i can only imagine the buggy mess when given even more to interact with and control/manipulate.. and im not looking forward to that cluster f**k of a mess and would rather give myself a hard pass and some tylenol for the effort i put in so far.not worth the effort. by any means. boring interactive enviroments. seemed more like a physics puzzle test lab for throwing some ideas in with a lamented story thrown in afterwards for half a**ed good measure too. so theres 2 against it. and the third, every single area: devoid of life, other then the puzzle areas, which are aswell, if you dont count the blocks. lol. and the folks doing the voice overs.. half the time i would read subtitles and they were supposed to talk.. and nothing came out, then the game would skip forward in conversation and i would have missed a ton of "content and story" meh.i really wanted to like this game, but for real a game like this needs to invite you in, and have a bit more substance.. not run folks away with the at best child like interpretation of physics, and adapt the concept to 3 buttons and make the game fight with you at every turn to utilize the concept and button presets.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: The game has story and puzzles, sadly they are completely separated and mostly unrelated.1. The story plays a "graphic novel", and "walkie talkie" discussions. 2. Then you move around to empty maps that are pretty much copy and paste of the same asset. 3. Eventually you get to the puzzle level. Rinse and repeat. PosCons
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: I had this sitting in my library for a while, started it on whim, and boy am I glad I did.If you liked The Talos Principle, and to a certain degree the Portal series, then you're gonna love this first person puzzler.The presentation, as in, graphics and voicework are all top-notch, but the writing and story is pretty C-grade terrible (it gets better in the two free addons that comes with the game), but all that doesn't matter at all, because the quality and challenge of the puzzles were more than enough to keep me solidly hooked and playing nothing but Relicta until I completed all three missions, and got all achievements (except the speedrun one)In short, if you like 3D first-person puzzle solving, then this one is a guaranteed hit!
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this was a moderately good first person puzzle game. It may be worth playing if you like the genre and have already played Portal 1&2 and the Talos Principle (if not, go play those first). It has some strong aspects and some weak aspects, which probably reflects a relatively smaller team or lower budget.Strong aspects:The puzzles. The game's core mechanics of magnetism and gravity manipulation work pretty well and I never found the game either getting too unintuitive. The maps are pretty well designed. It's completely linear, but I never really got stuck, but also didn't feel like it was unchallenging.The graphics. It's a little bit generic looking, but it's pretty. The challenge and length. The game was hard enough to be worthwhile but not so hard it was obnoxious (which can easily happen with puzzle games) and it didn't outstay its welcome.Weaker aspects:The writing. Oh, god, the writing. The plot and setting is ok, I guess, not amazing or anything. But the DIALOGUE, dear lord. Every single character talks like a 20 year old techbro. And they swear constantly, even in internal communications and memos, which feels extremely out of character for a bunch of scientists in a corporate environment (maybe in their personal lives, sure, but not in workplaces communications!) Maybe it just got mangled when they were translating it to English?The voice acting. It's mostly just tolerable, but there is one character for which it is kind of laughable. You'll know it when you get to it.The collectibles and hub area. They're pretty perfunctory and just there to be there. Doesn't hurt anything but doesn't add much.So basically, play it for the puzzles and gameplay, not so much the plot.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Slightly uninspired puzzle platformer which feels a bit like a cross between Portal and The Witness.Pros: -Pretty long and many puzzles - You'll get quite a lot of game for your money. I think 12 hours of puzzles is quite possible even if you're a regular on this kind of games.-Looks beautiful - The open colorful levels are quite a relief compared to some other puzzle-platformers.Neutral: -Puzzles in the first half, didn't feel inspiring or challenging. They IMHO get better later on, but "later" means 6-7 hours, so you might need some perseverance to get to the better parts. And even then there's some levels that are just long, not good or challenging.Cons:  -Invisible Walls: looks beautiful, but thanks to a lot of invisible walls it often feels even more restricted than other some other puzzle-platformers. -Story. Not many characters and no story development for the first 2-3 hours and once something happens? The protagonist pretends nothing happened for the next 2-3 hours. And even after this, it felt like someone had a pretty cool idea for a story, but decided not to inject a sense of urgency or suspense in an otherwise relaxed puzzle game. So they toned it down. Undecided whether to give it a thumbs up or down. It's very medicore, but as I have to give either up or down...
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: I'm decently far in now and I just need to say Relicta is extremely underrated. Seriously, there's less than 100 positive reviews despite effectively being on par with other 3D puzzlers such as Talos—it does a couple things better, like the puzzles are crafted more fairly with the environment properly hinting towards intended actions, and the difficulty curve is close to perfect, forcing you to learn the right things at the right time or place. It's  lacking music . The story is very questionable, with shoddy English, incoherent gibberish and awkwardly forced F-bombs, but pretentious gibberish is honestly par for the course with its competition. A few more mechanics get introduced farther into the game.The graphics are beautiful, it runs well, puzzles are consistent and there's plenty of content.Early game has a few "hidden" cubes you should look out for that may confuse you.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying it so far. I don't mind the walking sim story stuff, though it does seem a bit disconnected from the puzzle stuff. The puzzles are good. It's kinda a bit too obvious to make comparisons to Portal, Turing Test, Talos Principle and Lightmatter; Relicta can stand proudly alongside them as a very worthwhile addition to the genre. There are a lot of criticism here saying it's just ripping off Portal and them complaining that it's not Portal. It's a bit like saying that a pizza is just a flat open sandwich and them complaining that it's not a good sandwhich.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: If you like puzzle games, I'd say this one is a must. First-person puzzle game which is clearly inspired by games such as Portal and The Talos Principle. It's not a good as those, but still worth your time no doubt. The puzzles are cleverly designed and work pretty well despite being mostly physics based, which will sometimes lead to an undesired outcome even if you did the right steps, but this happened very rarely to me. The story is interesting, even if the ending is a bit weak.Game also includes 2 extra chapters, which could perfectly be sold as DLC, but they are included in the game, points for the devs for that.Conclusion: if you're into puzzle games, stop reading reviews already and go play it !
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is a 3D physics based puzzle game with puzzles revolving around magnetism. You can switch the color objects from Red to Blue so that they attract/repel each other. The game is fairly good overall. The voice acting, plot, assets, physics, and game design are fairly high quality.The game follows a linear difficulty curve, but I think it would have been better to have a few difficult puzzles mixed in early on as long as they were optional. The odd thing about this game is that the first half feels like a different game than the second. Not only does the plot completely change, but the puzzles required more out of the box thinking. I liked the changes to the puzzles, but I'm not so sure about the story. The game also forces you to take breaks every 5 puzzles by making you walk around a facility to find the next zone. This is where you obtain collectibles and notes. I was fine with this at first but eventually felt like a pointless task since every transition felt the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: It's an okay puzzle game. Played the main story and now waiting for bonus content patch. Will not try speedrunning it.While playing, I did not feel excitement but tediom when going to the next puzzle set in each level. Puzzles get longer and a bit more convoluted, sometimes with obscure steps I could not figure out myself. There are a few puzzles requiring very accurate placement or timing of actions.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re looking for the next Portal game then this ain’t it, but Relicta might just scratch that itch for a clever physics-based puzzle adventure.  Best of all, Relicta makes you feel smart…if not immediately, eventually.  I enjoyed exploring the concepts of magnetism and gravity and the clever use of switch pads and teleporters to defeat some truly mind-melting puzzles, often in ways I’m sure the designers weren’t expecting.  If you’re even considering this game you likely have some experience with the genre and know what to expect, and those expectation will be fully realized and more when you explore the intriguing world of Relicta.Full review at Live gameplay video at

_childDocuments_.review: First I want to say I enjoyed this game, it was fun. But it was too long.Here is my review on youtube: I feel like the gratuitous use of invisible walls is too much. Let me jump off a cliff and die if I want to and then restart the puzzle.Late game puzzles feel drawn out. That being said once you understand the puzzles there really no reason to try again aside from maybe a speed run. Were it not for invisible walls there would be a HUGE opportunity for speed running in this game.I've done a video review of this game on my youtube, I was a bit critical, mostly because I was frustrated at the end of the game.I did REALLY enjoy the story, the jokes interspersed here and there were excellent (except the twitter one, srsly, I doubt if twitter will be around in 100 years)I 100% recommend this game if puzzle games are your thing, just maybe don't be like me and go ahead and look up the solutions if you start getting stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: I give a HUGE recommendation for Relicta. REALLY HUGE. It's one of those games where you bang at a puzzle for 45 minutes straight, solving challenges one by one until you see how everything fits together. I'd describe it as blending parts of Talos Principle with Magnetic: Cage Closed, then mixing in some similarities from Q.U.B.E. and Magrunner: Dark Pulse.Yup, my favorite cube-type 3rd generation Portal family all wrapped into one game. Cubes on pads, cubes on triggers, flinging cubes, flying on cubes, magnetizing cubes, moving platforms, different types of barriers, etc. Gameplay has a hint of training on each new concept, relying much more on your creative puzzle-solving abilities. i.e. - Sometimes you will have to do a simple task, learning a concept. Other times, you can be in the middle of a level and think "Hey, I wonder if I can do it this way  ... "  I counted 6 times when I wanted to peek at a walkthrough, but found that perseverance got me 100% through the difficult parts.The environments are varied, which is good. Audio is great, and background music is well produced. My GeForce 1080 handled the game fine at 2560x1440.Bad things? Not much. The game's opening has an intro with some chords that sound like my speakers are blowing out. I got stuck a few times (three times a glitch I couldn't get past, and twice because I thought I was stuck but actually just needed some more effort), but there's a level reset command which will put you back to the last savegame. That's a bit of a weakness: the savegame gets stretched out in the last half of the game. Levels can be 3 or 4 parts, but the save point reset will return you back a half-hour of progress (which you should be able to get through in 5, now). And there's an achievement for a speedrun. Ugh. Not going to happen.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. This game visually reminds me of the Talos Principle with its mix of beautiful natural environments and technology. The puzzles start simple and get progressively more and more complex, each set of levels introducing some new mechanic. It helps the game not to get stale and repetitive and shows that some thought has been put into the game design.The story is captivating and really pushed me through the puzzles as I was eager to get to next part and the one after that and another one after that. It even has some really funny moments and two endings that you can choose from.Visually, the game looks amazing and is really well optimized. I have a pretty old rig (7 years at this point) and could run it on max settings fairly comfortably most of the time.The game could use more music. There is some, but the game is mostly silent, sadly. It could also use some sort of a save feature when you don't have time to go through the whole level. It gets a bit tedious when you have to repeat what you've already solved, especially near the end where the levels are HUGE.Overall, the game is amazing and a must-have if you like to solve puzzles. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Very complicated / multi-faceted puzzles, the solution to which is almost never immediately obvious. Many times I was left wondering if I had solved a puzzle the intended way, or if I had cheesed it with clever use of mechanics... there is not always a way to tell (unless you straight up don't use some puzzle elements, which happened to me several times), which is a great feeling. This game will undoubtedly be compared to Portal, because there are many similarities, but it holds its own in spite of that.If I had to give it one con it would be that I felt like I was constantly on a wild goose chase running from place to place to solve these damn puzzles when my friends and family desperately needed me! But that is really just a testament to how likable and believable the characters are - they tell a great story despite having a clear low budget and no human models in the whole game. It would have been satisfying to pay an extra $5 to see some of these people I connected with, even if it was just some CGI or otherwise animated epilogue.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are quite fun and sometimes I feel stupid for missing something very obvious. Some of the puzzles incorporate items from a previous puzzle. The game really challenges the way to think and I'm quite enjoying it. The story is interesting as well and actually have me paying attention to it. Would recommend this to anyone that likes physics based puzzles for sure. There are a few small bugs here and there but nothing that can't be overcome!
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is a first person puzzle game that let's you manipulate boxes found in test environments strewn over the world. You can make the box weightless or magnetize them to either of two polarities. There are magnetic plates strewn over the test courses that also have a polarity and either repel or attract boxes based on their polarity. The same goes for the boxes, allowing you to manipulate two boxes by their placement and (change of) polarity. Also you can ride on the boxes. Later teleports for the boxes, fields impassible for the boxes, configurable magnetic plates and other contraptions up the ante.The gameplay is well realized and varied, with a not too easy difficulty I've enjoyed.Sound is nothing to write home about, but the story, told in cutscenes and dialogues between tests and set pieces, is livened up by a good performance of the voice actors.Graphics are nice, with a steady fps (that the game's physics engine also needs, so no suprise there). They are somewhat taxing on my a few years old high end graphics card, though.So far (I'm four hours in at the time of writing) I'm enjoying myself, due to a competent presentation, interesting story and a good difficulty for engaging puzzle mechanics.EDIT: I put the game on hold eventually because the designers commit one of the cardinal sins of (first person) puzzle design: relying on timed memorization of puzzle solutions far too much.What I mean by that: at a certain point the difficulty of the game lies not that much in figuring out HOW to beat the puzzle, but being able to execute the solution as a sequence of turns, jumps and mouse clicks. All timed, of course.
_childDocuments_.name: Relicta

_childDocuments_.review: Relicta is a first-person puzzle game whose main mechanics combine magnetism and gravity. The player is equipped with a pair of special gloves that allow them to change the magnetic and gravitational properties of experimental cubes scattered around each level. These cubes can be moved by the player, either carrying them bodily or using magnetism or gravity. They can also be placed on teleporting machines to warp them to another teleporter and help solve puzzles. Mechanics really come alive when combined in ingenious ways. For instance, magnetism can be used to repel or attract cubes, but repelling a cube that has previously “anti-gravitated” gives you a frictionless device that will retain inertia until it collides against something solid, like a wall (or your skull). It can even be used as a means of transport for the player to reach new places. Cubes can also be used to power up some devices, in order to operate doors and force fields. As the player progresses towards more complex puzzles, they will encounter other devices - magnetic plates, elevators, buttons or even drones capable of nullifying magnetic and gravitational fields as well as stealing cubes.

name: Pode
detailed_description: Pode is a co-op puzzle exploration game about a rock and a fallen star working together to solve ancient puzzles in a stunning environment inspired by Norwegian art and culture. Travelling through the insides of a mysterious and magical mountain, Bulder and Glo breathe life into an ancient sleeping world and explore the ruins of a long lost civilization with their unique talents and abilities. Only by helping each other can these unlikely adventure companions solve the ancient puzzles that open the secret passageways up the caverns of Mount Fjellheim. Key Features: Exploration. Discover a beautiful and ancient cave system and uncover its secrets to reach your goal. Puzzles. Solve puzzles, riddles and mysteries. Combine the two character's special abilities to overcome obstacles. Co-op or single player. Share the experience with a friend, or enjoy playing it by yourself. Unitque art style. Enjoy a world inspired by Norwegian art and nature. Music. The soundtrack is by the legendary Austin Wintory. For optimal experience, gamepad is recommended. For co-op, minimum 1 gamepad is required.

_childDocuments_.review: The world needs more games like Pode.It's the best game a couple in love can play together.I played it with my boyfriend and it was a lovely experience. Pode made us all emotional, we were really feeling the story of the 2 adorable little characters. It's impossible not to feel attached to them, so so adorable.What a beautiful experience for a couple.I'm so glad I found this game, thank you to the developers for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend this sweet little co-op puzzle game.In co-op mode, Pode demands teamwork the entire game to solve all of its puzzles. These puzzles are usually very easy. Same can be said for the few platforming parts. The visuals, animations and sounds are well made and super cute. All this together makes Pode perfect for some nice and relaxed co-op sessions, even with non-gamers or children.By the way, Pode runs perfectly on Linux, if you use a Proton version with MFPlat support. You need MFPlat for the pre-rendered videos. Right now I can recommend Proton-6.9-GE-1, which however must be installed manually.Played on Manjaro Linux (Kernel 5.11.6, Mesa 20.3.4) and this hardware: AMD Ryzen 1700 @ 4GHz, AMD 5700 XT and 16GB RAM.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game to play split screen co-op with my sister (me on keyboard, her on the controller). Unfortunately, the game suffers from a game-breaking bug that causes the controller to move Glo & Bulder at the same time. You get to connect with two of the characters throughout their journey, and I have to say it is wonderful having your loved ones experience all of the stories by your side. It felt like the game told you always to cherish those you hold dear.I played this game with my wife, and we have a very great memory

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! Great for couples.How I played:I hosted remote play with my ldr fiancee. It worked fine 99% of the time. Every once in awhile, we would have trouble connecting her controller, but I haven't done remote play much, so it's very possible it was some other problem.My Opinions:- The puzzles were very cooperative and not too stressful.- The ambience was calm and relaxing.- The aesthetic was gorgeous!- The map kinda "grows" as you move around it and it was satisfying to do so. Like popping bubble wrap.- The characters are cute.- I felt immersed, I was invested in the characters.- The game didn't feel too short. _childDocuments_.review: AVOID | LACKING | MAYBE | WORTHWHILE |  | UNMISSABLEPode is a casual co-op puzzle game. In a world where combat-based/MOBA co-op games reign supreme, this is a nice diversion from that. In this game, there are two players and each one has a unique ability that helps in solving puzzles via making changes in the environment in different ways. There is no combat in this game. In general, the puzzles aren't very difficult, but a few require some thought and playing around to figure out how to solve them. I'd say it's good both for experienced players who want a more laid-back experience, as well as new(er) players who think they'll enjoy a relaxing puzzle game. The music is very chill and the characters truly need to work together to solve the puzzles, so both feel equally important in implementing solutions. The end chapter artwork is super cute and there is a sweet and simple story said without any words. The art design is simple, but I think it works here, and is nice in context.Overall, I don't have many complaints about this title. The only real negatives are that sometimes the camera view gets funky and you can't quite see what you want. The camera also acts in a weird way if the players get too far away from each other, making it difficult to get back to your partner without just yeeting yourself off the edge. Sometimes the 2.5D perspective makes depth perception a bit frustrating as well. In general though, none of these points were a big deal in terms of affecting my enjoyment while playing.The game took exactly 6 hours to complete at a relaxed pace with all achievements. You can very quickly move between levels once you open them up to go back and get collectables if you missed them your first time through. Otherwise, achievements are linked to game/level completion. If playing co-op, only one person needs to own the game, though I feel like the price is just a bit too much, so I personally suggest waiting for a sale.In general, if you're looking for a relaxing and laid-back co-op experience that is focused on solving puzzles with your partner, this is a solid pick. If you're looking for a challenge or combat, then this title likely isn't for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game with my girlfriend and had a blast! Mechanics are solid and fun to use, and the puzzles (almost) never too difficult/frustrating. _childDocuments_.review: Cute game :) Pode had satisfying puzzles tied together with a cute story. The art was simple yet beautiful and puzzles are relaxing without feeling boring. The game had a nice progression with each level feeling unique in atmosphere. This is a relatively small frustration compared to the rest of the game:I had to look up how to progress because the "combined aura" mechanic required to grow the plant in the main lobby area, was never explained and not hinted at in any way. _childDocuments_.review: The best couch co-op game I have ever played ! Characters are so lovable ! We had lots of fun playing it with my wife.There is no time pressure, you have to discover what to do next and you do it at your own rhythm in a beautiful setting. We loved growing all plants and rocks everywhere even if it did not serve an end other than discovering how they grow.I hope the developers make more games like this or even a second Pode game.Finaly a game were we have fun collaborating and are not frustrated by the game mechanics.What could be improved: not much honestly, but we would have liked at the end to be able to select the chapter to go back to to find all the hidden features and know where we missed some.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of those adorable hidden gems in the endless library of steam. With the dwindling amount of games for couples being released and currently available, this is definitely one for every gaming couple to play, keep and play again. It isn't overly common to find a puzzle game that is driven by a narrative, but Pode has a short and sweet story line that effectively adds to the whimsy and purpose of the puzzles within the game. The characters (Glo and Bulder) both convey a personality through the short story and will win your hearts over by the end. The majority of the puzzles are easy enough to solve together with a sprinkling of more challenging obstacles that you may have to think outside of the box to overcome.  Overall, this beautiful yet short puzzle game will pose a fun challenge for couples whilst also bringing you closer by focusing on the loving story of the two characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game as a review copy from Plan of Attack / Henchman & Goon. Overall, before saying yes. I was shown some screenshots, the trailer, and a description. I did not hear about this game before they emailed me. I said yes, as soon as I saw the artwork. I wanted to stream this, as I tend to be more vocal about games that way. Got a bud of mine to play co-op with me through the Steam Play Together feature. The artwork, excellent. Music mixes right into it blending into the background but you still know it's there. The lighting was great which complements the environment and draws your attention to the scene and its details.The characters were super adorable, and you were able to tell what they were feeling just by facial expression; as they did not speak at all. Myself and my friend, both found ourselves attached to the characters, even up to the end. The puzzles made you think a little about both characters abilities and made you explore the map. But were easy enough to still be rewarding when you solve them. My few complaints, and it was only with one puzzle would be the star puzzle. Couldn’t seem to figure out the right and left rings and pillars, but figured out the center rings. Somehow we just brute forced it. Menu system: No volume control in game (you have to use Windows Volume mixer, and when game is not focused music is muted.No built in online co-op. You have to use Steam Play Together. My friend’s complaint was the dark/no light maps, but that could be my fault for not using my power as the star to be bright lol.I completely recommend this game as it makes you focus on the artwork and looking around the world, without being a hunt and collect game. Great way to pass 6 hours :DStreamed on:  /
_childDocuments_.name: Pode

_childDocuments_.review: Pode really shines with its presentation, featuring a wonderful art style with great lighting effects and some stunning growth animation, as all sorts of vegetation springs to life as Glo moves around barren earth radiating warm light, while Bulder can do the same, infusing energy into small chunks of crystal to create towering crystal spires.  You can even link the characters together for maximum regenerative effect.  Pode has modest system requirements and looks fantastic on the highest settings.  Oddly, your only graphical options are Small, Medium, and Large, so I can’t even tell you what resolution the game is running at but it looks great.  The simplistic yet stylish art design can be breathtaking at times with so much life and animation, both in the wildlife and level design as well as the adorable waddling of the two characters.  There is even this cute animation when one character gets to the exit and turns to the other, unable to exit without their partner.Even better than the graphics might just be the soundtrack composed by Austin Wintory.  I must have sat at the title screen for over ten minutes just listening to the soothing music, and it only gets better once you start playing the game.  Combined with the effervescent, sprouting environments, Pode is this mystical place of enchanting wonder that dazzles from start to finish.  Every visual effect, every tune, every sound effect is spot-on perfection.  If this is what Norwegian art and culture is about then I want to experience more.For only $20 I can’t recommend Pode highly enough.  Don’t even wait for a sale; especially if you are looking for a great co-op experience to share on the couch or using Steam’s remote play. The only fault with the game is the lack of support for the switch pro controller and the lack of key rebind options. _childDocuments_.review: I played entirely in 2 player coop. While the game was never BAD, there were a lot of places where I felt it also wasn't GOOD. The visuals are great, and many of the mechanics are very interesting, but the second half of the game does not feel like coop. The rock character tends to have sit around and wait while the star character does any number of the abilities it got over the course of the game. There were many puzzle rooms where I would just sit there, either as a stepping stool, or sometimes not at all, while my friend got to the end and then teleported me to the end too. The dark levels were even worse, as the rock character sheds no light, AND the star character can again do 90% of this puzzle without help. I literally put my controller down for 5 minutes while my friend solved this room without me.Playing alone and switching between the characters, this is probably a really good game, but as a pure coop experience, it's a bit of a miss.
_childDocuments_.name: Pode

_childDocuments_.review: is a very pleasant and colorful cooperative puzzle game. Both Glo and Bulder can project a sphere around themselves that "activates" the flora and stone formations around them, and this is probably the most enjoyable aspect of the experience. It's a delight to walk into a barren room and have both players activate their spheres, and then run to each corner of the room. The formerly featureless room will explode into lush plants and rocky spirals.Although it's fun to see, much (but not all) of this flora and stone don't play much of a function in the puzzles, but instead just beautify the space. On a couple of occasions I attempted to mount the stone formations to reach a platform, only to find that developers Henchman & Goon didn't design the game to support this possibility. has essentially no hand-holding, which is both a blessing and a curse. Obviously, it makes solving the puzzles on offer much more rewarding, but it can be frustrating to not even know what the puzzle is, much less how to go about solving it. Regardless, we powered our way through and ended up with a positive impression of the game, although it's not necessarily a game that I would prioritize playing.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cute and has very satisfying animation and sounds. In some sections one of the characters does almost nothing at all, while the other one does everything, for example. That doesn't make any sense to me, as it's a game that requires you to control 2 characters, one at a time, it had potential to be a very good indie local puzzle co-op game.In the end, it actually was a very nice and relaxing experience for me and my partner, very good specially if you are looking for a non-violent, cute and relaxed co-op game to play with a non-gamer friend.I hope they make a sequel that is bigger and made with co-op in mind from the ground up.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent little puzzle platformer. An absolute indie couch co-op gem - undeservedly overlooked. If the genre is at all interesting to you, definitely do get this, especially if you're looking for something to play with your s/o.The story is simple, and generally keeps out of the way, but still manages to tug at your heart strings. And it's told in a very well thought out way, pretty much completely via the gameplay and level design. Packs more charm than just about anything in the couch co-op space.Speaking of level design, this is probably just about one of the most beautifully designed things I've played of Steam's co-op offerings. Think artistically beautiful, not so much technically impressive. Tasteful to the max, an absolute visual delight.Gameplaywise the puzzles are really right in that sweetspot where you don't get hard stumped, but do get to scratch your head a bit.The platforming itself is sometimes a bit iffy, but that doesn't really get in the way of any of the charm and puzzles that this game packs, and there's no showstopping bugs. On the rare occasion that you do get stuck on geometry, it's handled very charmingly by the characters' hand-holding feature that helps you pull one another out of sticky situations.Overall the product is very well polished and thought out.If you're looking for a particularly long play, this won't really be it - we got through it in just over 7h time - but what's here is top notch.
_childDocuments_.name: Pode

_childDocuments_.review: With some quite lovely sights and sounds to behold, Pode deserves more attention than it has currently received on Steam, owing possibly to its earlier appearance on Switch. What Pode offers is a thoughtful, heartfelt co-op puzzle experience with some forgivable, if considerable, flaws. The cryptic puzzle hints, when coupled with sometimes too-wide camera angles and imperfect hit detection, can lead to failed attempts and frustration; that said, the strength and artfulness of the game design will carry you through. In the end, I didn't really want Pode to be over so soon. Be prepared for some unexpected feels.

_childDocuments_.review: Just Wow....We just finished this wonderful game. I usually don't give reviews but I feel like this game deserves one. Pode is a coop puzzle game. It's about a star wich falls from the sky and lands in a cave, where it meets the stone. The stone tries to help the star out of the cave, to the top of the mountain. On the way they become best friends.In the game you can clear different levels and each level consists of multiple rooms. Each Level has a different "theme" (e.g. Water or "Light"). You must use the special abilities of both characters to solve the puzzles. Only together they can reach the goal. Coop or alone?It's possible to play the game alone. The game does not require you to do multiple things at the same time, so you can easily you the build in mechanic to switch between the two characters. However, I would highly recommend to play the game together with a friend, because it's a lot more fun together. Furthermore the game is about friendship and love <3 :)Too hard or too easy?Obviously the game gets harder each level. The first few level are very easy. I wish they would be a little more challenging. Last levels are just the right amout of a challenge. Overall I think the game can easily be play by kids and adults. Art style, graphics and sound..The art style and the graphics are simple, yet wonderful. It's very mesmerizing to watch how a plain, dark and boring cave, turns into a wonderful canvas with shining crystals and vibrant colorful plants. I caught myself many times trying to find every single spot in a room where I can grow some plants.The music also is very wonderful and relaxing. It isn't to loud or anything and doesn't keep you away from thinking. I really enjoyed the combination of the music and the art style. I would also like to mention that the two characters are SUPER CUTE and that they fit perfectly with the story! Any downsides?Where light is, is also shadow, and this game is no exception. Fortunately, are there so few downsides, that I still can happily give a positiv review. The only downside are that we encountered some bugs, and some of them where even game breaking so we had to restart the game (Worst part was that restarting the game once, didn't helped all the time.  We had to restart multiple times to get it working again). For the dev: Is there any way to report a bug ? If not, feel free to send a direct message to this steam profile. I would like to get in touch with you to support the game :)Price and playtime:We finished the game in about 5 and a half hour. If you like you can search for all the collectables. I think we would need about 2-3 hours more. So if you play very relaxed and try to find everything the game has to offer, I would say that you are done with the game in about 10 hours. I think the price (16€ atm) is a bit high for this much content, but still acceptable, because the game is so good. Overall:If you are stuck at home at a rainy weekend, just grab a friend and this game and you surely wont regret it!

name: The Last Friend
detailed_description: In a world that has become yet another post-apocalyptic future where humanity is distracted by chaos, destruction, rampant mutants and a thing called surviving, something even more sinister is afoot... The World's doggos are disappearing! Now enters Alpha (you) who at an early age lost his man's best friend... While traveling the wastelands he comes across some mutants up to no good dognapping a lost puppy! During this battle he discovers has the ability to understand what the pup can say and his name is T. Juan! Now T. Juan joins Alpha on this grand adventure looking for answers about what truly has happened to all the doggos. It’s time to join them and put dem paws to the pavement! Woof! Got to Pet them All From the warm and fluffy Newfoundland who has a healing passive, the Tibetan Mastiff with a beast mode unlocked, and to the ever charismatic Beagle, it's up to you to rescue these fearless pups and then set them loose on the bad guys! Welcome to the World, Pup The world has changed and some could even say it’s gone to the dog house…WOOF!!! Get ready to explore deserted badlands, ruined cities, a military base or two and not to mention forgotten jungles teeming with challenges as you set out in an upgradable RV! Who let the ‘Brawl’ out It’s a dog eat dog world out there so best bring your best when it comes to going all paws with the various bad guys you’ll be sure to face! A Unique Bark on Tower Defense Your bite isn’t your only defense when dealing with overly tanned mutants, electrifying enemies, and one or two tofu aficionados! From super soakers, steel walls, and wire traps you’ll have your pick of the litter when it comes to offensive and defensive options to protect your yard!

_childDocuments_.review: I have officially completed the game, save a few arbitrary medals. TLDR It's a new look at Plants vs. Zombies with side scrolling brawler mechanics. All in all I had a good time with it, but it left me wanting a little more in the way of unique challenges forcing me to use the plethora of unique dogs (towers & abilities) at my disposal. I think it's worth it at the price point of $15 though, I feel like the content that is present is good and they let you pet the dog. So that's pretty neat.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Friend

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Friend is a brawler and tower defense game. You're a guy with a talking dog. Your goal is... To save other dogs. Every new, rescued dog will give you either a new tower or ability. Build turrets and fight your way through hordes of enemies on three different lanes. There are three different lanes. Scrap is your currency to build towers. You will need to get it by diggers (a tower) or beating enemies up. While managing your towers you can/need to fight enemies with normal attacks, heavy attacks, and special attacks. If your HP or your VANs reach 0, you lose. Survive wave after wave to win. Usually, there are three different conditions (No damage to your VAN, beating the level in under 5 minutes, etc.) to meet to get more rewards. Stars and dog treats are your rewards. You can take up to five different dogs into a battle, the choice is all yours. With rewards, you can upgrade your dogs or van. Stars allow you to upgrade your van (like you start a battle with more scrap, a shield for your VAN, more HP to walls, turrets, and more). With dog treats, you can upgrade dogs. This will end up in better towers. After upgrading towers, you will unlock the ability to upgrade the specific tower within a match for scrap. There are other missions aside from these battles described above. For example, there are story-specific events, boss fights without turrets, Beat 'em up-missions, and more. It brings enough variety into the game. I've played the "old" version of The last Friend and the "new" one. In the old version, I had plenty of negative points to talk about like the gameplay (almost no range for attacks, it feels like moving a tank, delays, etc.). All of them got improved a lot. It feels much smoother now to control your Character and it overall is a way better experience. They also changed how turrets work and that's a very good thing. What they also changed is the difficulty. While the old version was much harder, partly because of the sluggish gameplay, it is now way too easy. There is almost no strategy needed to win. It mostly now feels like a dull Beat 'em up. Some will enjoy it for sure but I am no fan of this. Why add tower defense into your game, if there is almost no strategy needed? Even in the second "world", I don't really need towers that much, and if, I have plenty of them already. I can't understand how and why they changed the difficulty that much (Enemies have much less health, you do much more damage, special attacks aren't needed anymore as well as counter-attacks).  The Last Friend could be a very fun and tactical brawler and tower defense game if it wasn't so damn easy. The art style is great as well as the idea. Combining these two genres is a perfect fit. It's not as grindy as many other TD games and also brings new things to the table every few levels. The variety in missions plus dozens of different turrets, dogs, attacks, and enemies add a lot to the game. That's also a reason why the following sucks even more: It's just so damn easy, especially if you played the old version of the game. It was tactical because you NEEDED towers, special attacks, grabs, and a strategy. Now it's so easy, you don't need any of that. You will easily win if you build even one turret and button smash your way to the end. If you want a strategy game or even just a challenge, The Last Friend isn't the game you're looking for. I just can't recommend it in its current state - sadly - because I very much liked it a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: After accepting a review copy of The Last Friend (LF), I kept forgetting where it was in my library because I couldn't remember the name. I associate the game with dogs, so a title like that, which sounds kind of somber to me, doesn't stick. If anything I'd have gone for The First Friend, with how long dogs and humans have shared that unique bond. Either way, the game footage made me interested enough to see if these friends are true blue or sadly undoglike.  LF is primarily a tower defense (TD) game, but instead of playing an inactive role after placing towers, you can go out into the front lines and beat up the foes directly. This tends to be a good idea, as your towers are both vulnerable and not high damage dealers, but they come into their own after an upgrade or two. However, since you have a base to guard and enemies will move forward relentlessly, having backup to pester and slow them down is helpful. It requires you to juggle moving forward to fend off approaching enemies, while running back to build up your towers, but I found it a good way to maintain my engagement and always kept my full attention since I couldn't just sit back and watch. That can be a downside to TDs, as you otherwise wait with nothing else to do until you have enough money to upgrade or build a new tower. Most of the stages will involve this style of gameplay as you rescue captured dogs, but sometimes you'll also have another objective, such as clearing burning obstructions or sneaking past a laser grid. There's also different stage types, such as the trial stages, which act as a tutorial to introduce new moves and mechanics. Another recurring stage type were boss battles, where you can't use any turrets, but many of them were pretty easy. These different stage types made for nice diversions from what could otherwise have been overly repetitive gameplay.  Due to handling two completely different functions, managing towers and engaging in melee combat, the controls are more complicated than you might first think. However, the game introduces them at a good pace so not everything is dropped on your head at once. For the most part I thought everything worked well, though managing the towers could sometimes be annoying as you're busy dealing with bad guys. It can feel clumsy changing lanes quickly to try and deal with a small swarm of enemies approaching all at once. Moments like that really make you appreciate the turret back-up, as you'd be all on your own otherwise. Ay chihuahua.  You play as Alpha, a human with the normal propensity for loving dogs, and his tech-savvy chihuahua, T. Juan. Their RV serves as both the means for how they travel around, and is the base you have to protect, which is pretty clever theming and game design. Kudos. It's not strange that they work together to rescue other dogs, but more the people they're rescuing them from: a bunch of dimwits following the orders of a pyromaniac. At least he's not setting the dogs on fire, or the tone of this game would be much different. As you topple the main boss of an area you'll open up new locations, though it takes a while to finally find out what's up with the dog-nappings. LF doesn't take itself too seriously, with plenty of meta humor and silliness about a demure human with a talkative chihuahua.  I'd say the game looks decent. Compared to other indie games, the backgrounds and settings are more simplified, but it still conveys the general look of the locations they were striving for, such as a high-tech factory and desert. The art for man and dog alike has a cartoony style to it, and doesn't involve much detail. Admittedly the guy's fighting moves are animated well enough, but I find the visual design passable instead of impressive.  As you open up new areas, the music will change to suit the atmosphere. However, no matter how much I tried paying attention to it, it never made an impression on me. I don't think it was bad, just unremarkable. When defeating bad guys, they have an enjoyable, “Oof,” sound effect, and there thankfully isn't nearly as much random barking as I might have expected from a game like this.  🌟 The pacing of the game is pretty good. Tutorials are spread out enough that you don't get overwhelmed with too many mechanics at once, and the variety of stages and rewards prevents the gameplay from getting stale or feeling unrewarding. 🌟 Your starting units are useful, and you might use some of them through most of the game.  ❌ I thought the dog units could have had more interesting default names. When getting the German shepherd that provides a defensive shield, it's just called German shepherd. I named it the Barkin Wall, and hope somebody gets the joke. ❌ If you don't start off an attack with a few light hits, the combat can feel kind of stiff. Even how you approach certain enemies can make a big difference on whether you shut them out or vice versa. 🔍 When fighting the tank boss near the end, build walls across all five rows. The strongest will need to be in the center three rows. Save enough to build a chihuahua turret and place it on the top or bottom row. Stay in the middle three rows and beat down the grenade launchers (they drop a lot of scrap). The tank will start shooting a laser cannon; counter with the space dog cannon. Build a new turret in the same place, maybe one in the middle. Then rush back and fight the goons. Rebuild your walls, upgrading the center to be very strong. Repeat until the tank is defeated.🔍 Since upgrading the turrets requires you to spend more scrap, I invested into Pumi early on because an upgraded row of them right next to the RV produces enough scrap to build up other upgraded turrets. Otherwise, I think you'd go most of the stage without having the materials needed to make it worthwhile. 🔍 It's surprising how effective basic combos are at defeating weaker enemies. For instance, the two light, one heavy combo one shots the weakest enemy every time. It can be useful to do the three light, one heavy combo if there's a few bunched together as it'll wipe out all of them at once.  Having beaten LF, it started off really easy, but later on certain enemies were rather annoying and made me approach them differently. For instance, the guys throwing grenades makes it worthwhile to have a front wall to absorb attacks and protect turrets. The first minute or so of each stage is usually the toughest because your forces are the most basic and weak, but if you can fend off that first wave you can upgrade and replenish those turrets. Additionally, there's the option to play the game coop, and I'm not sure if the game increases enemy HP or how many spawn for the second player. If not, I could see it being too easy, though that may make for a good parent/child game. Regardless, I had fun, and think others who want a casual TD kind of game would enjoy themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: A hybrid of tower defense and brawler where the dogs you rescue become your weapons!A very colourful and charming hybrid of tower defense/brawler developed by the collaboration of The Stonebot Studio and Ludus Games.In a post apocalyptic setting, the main character, Alpha (the brawler), has discovered that someone is kidnapping all the doggos in the world. Alpha sets off on a mission in his RV (which you must defend) to rescue all the doggos and being grateful for their release, become Alpha's weapons in his journey.The tower defense works as a lane system, similar to Plants vs Zombies while Alpha jumps around lanes brawling and picking up scrap/bones.  If you succeed in the level, you will be able to release a new doggo of varying breeds and abilities. The doggos can even be renamed.Towers are built with the scrap you collect from killing the gangs who kidnap doggos. Sometimes they will drop bones, which will be used to enable your doggos to be upgraded within the battle field.Each level has 3 stars and the stars can be used for upgrades to both your RV and overall weapon effectiveness. The upgrades for this take place at a camp which is featured mid level and the doggie weapon upgrade is available a little further on, marked by a bowl on the map.There is a little story which accompanies the game and seen cutscenes can be skipped.Pros:* Lots of different dog breeds that you can rename* Doggos become your weapons* You can pet your dogs* Very colourful and charming* Local and remote play Co-Op* AchievementsCons: * Console port with no instructions for keyboard controlsUnder the proviso that you are comfortable using a controller to play, it is certainly recommended.7/10 (keyboard and mouse instructions need to be added)

_childDocuments_.review: ☑️A fun beat'em'up.☑️Beautiful art and designs.☑️Great music.☑️Cute doggos that you can rename.☑️Different usable synergies.☑️Good character designs and story.❌There isn't any cats.❌It's a casual game, not a challenging game.A challenge mode would be really nice, like "Don't take damage." instead of the same "Complete the stage." and other prerequisites for a 3 star. I won't go into too much detail, as there isn't much to really say. Imagine if Plants vs Zombies (was good) and also imagine if Street Fighter both came together to make a new game. But with cute doggos that you have to rescue. That's the game. You move left -> right using different dogs that you rescue to use their powers. Each dog is different, and each stage plays differently.It's not very challenging at all if you are adept at tower defense type games or simply know that using a full combo on a heavy punk will simply keep him down forever. But besides this it's fun!You might have to punch your way through a lane, or use water to take down walls of fire, while being bombarded by enemy after enemy while also having to manage your turrets so that they assist you from behind. Some missions are defense. Some missions are offense. Most missions are just fun with no challenge. Give it a try. It's worth your monies.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Friend~~~~~~~~~~~~~Ever wished you could play Plant vs Zombies but with dogs? I know I sure did, and my wish has finally been fulfilled with The Last Friend, A dog-themed Tower defense/beat ‘em up with all the barks and no bits!You play as Alpha, as a pack alpha along with your trusty sidekick/ best bud doggo T. Juan, who are on a daring journey to battle all the baddies and rescue all the captured doggos. Not only have you fought off all the baddies in order to save the doggos, but you also get to use them in your fights against all the baddies.  Each doggo comes with its own set of abilities, defenses, and skill set.During each battle, you need to earn enough scrape (currency) to drop a doggo defense, in order to collect more scrape to drop more doggos! In the end, you get to rescue a doggo in distress. Not only do you get to play with doggos and rescue them, but you also get to pet them; it’s an absolute win-win!Plot: Another post-apocalyptic future where humanity descends into chaos, destruction, rampant mutants, and a thing called surviving, something even more sinister is afoot...A sad sad world where doggos are hard to come by and are disappearing in worrying numbers. You play as Alpha.  While traveling the wastelands he comes across some mutants up to no good, dognapping a lost puppy!Upon fighting off this nasty filth, you find a scared little pup, and you discover you have the ability to understand what the pup can say, and his name is T. Juan!As T. Juan becomes you, trusty wingman, you two set off on a daring journey in order to uncover the mystery behind the missing doggos and recover them in the process. Gameplay: Okay! First things first . . . do you get to pet the doggos? Yes, you can and that’s an easy + one point for the game. After a brief intro setting up the plotline, you are thrown in as Alpha, with whom you get to play the beat ‘em up part of the game, and your first dog/defense, T. Juan, who shoots a scrape-based projectile.Your main goal in The Last Friend is to complete each mission, while defending your RV, with the added bonus of rescuing new and unique doggos with unique abilities of their own. This game would’ve been your average tower defense if it weren’t for its simple yet effective beat ‘em up gameplay and story-based doggo rescue mission. Now let’s back it down, shall we!Beat ‘em up: You get to get your hands dirty as Alpha. You are the first line of defence against the baddies as you charge headfirst into each fight with your bare hands, and all you’re might.And along the way you pick up some neat hand-to-hand combat tricks. As you move further you will encounter bigger, meaner, and stronger foes in large numbers. Keeping up with them will be a challenge, but luckily you are not alone; you will be picking up doggos with special skills who will boost your abilities or combat effectiveness. Each of these doggos will require a tower defence slot and you only have a limited number of them, so choose wisely. Tower defense: At each starting round you get a limited starting amount of scrape and you have to collect, earn and build your way up from that. Each defense will cost a different amount to place and upgrading will cost more. Nothing we haven’t seen before, other than the fact we are using dogs as defenses!Something I absolutely hate here is the fact these defenses are so slow-firing! They seriously need to bump these fire rates up! I get it, this is a beat ‘em up as well, but you should have a decent fire rate.And remember I mentioned doggos with skills? They come into play here as well, as some supplement the turret doggos during battle. You just have to place them and upgrade them; it’s a small arena so there’s nothing much to manage. And so much more: The Last Friend at first glance seems like a typical Tower Defense, but it features so much more! Mini-games, a lot of unique breeds of doggos, multi tier/type upgradability and so much more. A word of advice for the devs: 1. Bumping up the fire rate of your turret damage output is perfectly okay.2. Put the lady who makes soup (to upgrade the doggos) permanently in your camp for easy access.3. Slightly bump up the scrape output. Due to the fact that the scrape drop rate is so slow, I felt actively discouraged to stop trying to upgrade my turrets and play as Alpha mainly. World design: The Last Friend’s world setting was supposed to be a post-apocalyptic future! Ya about that, I don’t think that worked out well; I felt it more as a rough urban arena type scenario. This is fine by me, because the game looks and runs great. And I absolutely love the visuals, it’s just that the post-apocalyptic future setting didn’t work out. Music and sound effects: The theme music and background music in this game sounds super generic and oddly familiar! And it might be a controversial statement, but the music doesn’t really go well with the theme of the game. Don’t get me wrong, it sounds good, but in my opinion it doesn’t go well with the theme. Sound effects on the other hand I’m perfectly fine with. Although it’s nothing special, I think it suits this odd theme of using doggos as turrets nicely. Positive: + Fun story + Simple yet super fun mixture of Tower defense and beat ‘em up+ Rescue a lot of unique breeds of doggo + Doggo turrets and doggos with unique and fun abilities + Get to pet all the doggos at your camp + A lot of missions to go through + Mini-games+ Supposed to be post-apocalyptic, but looks like a rough urban setting Negative: - Some aspects of the turret defense gameplay need a second thought - Fire rates need to be improved- Lane Changing of Alpha’s gameplay needs to be smoother- Felt discouraged about upgrading by turrets Join forces with some furry four-legged friends and fight off the mean mutant baddies to rescue all the doggos! Anyone who loves dogs will get a kick out of this one. 8/10 Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: 12h 4/10 1 I wrote  No No No No No No No No "Lost" can be hard to get because the shrine level has difficulties with the cameraI have a hard time writing this review, and I'll start by explaining why. I got the amazing chance to play this fantastic game a few days before the release. I found some bugs and had contact with one of the developers. First by e-mail, later through discord to make talking about what I found out easier. Everything was fine, they quickly fixed the bugs and it was just nice to be able to help out. The last bug I found was that the camera stopped following the character in the Shrine level, and with that 3 achievements were impossible to get. At first, everything was still fine, they tried to fix the bug, but it didn't help.. at one point (3 weeks after the release) the communication completely stopped. No response in private discord messages, no response on the discord server in general, no response to e-mail... nothing. I tried multiple times and after 2 months I made a topic here on steam about it and wrote a negative review. The response on that steam topic was that they would look into it, but then it went silent again. This still hurts today, as I adore this game, I think it is awesome and the developers strike me as lovely people who care so much for their game. So I have no idea where it went wrong that I got the silent treatment and that it took 7 months to be able to finish the Shrine level with minimal bugs, but I still lost the camera at some point. So much for a bit of the backstory where I come from when writing this review. and keep in mind that it is 7 months ago that I played the game, but here is my review from what I remember of it: The Last Friend is an awesome tower defense/ beat 'm up type of game. Most of the levels are a bit like "Plant Vs zombies' that you put towers in lanes and they kill the enemies. The twist is that you are quite strong yourself also, so you'll help beat the enemies by going up close to them and beat them to death. Each level has their own sub objectives which ask you to play a different way/ use a specific power or complete it in a certain way to make it more challenging. To unlock all the achievements you have to complete every sub-objective as well. It also has a lot of "do this X amount of times" and "try out this awesome combo you wouldn't have done otherwise" kind of achievements. It has the kind of challenges and achievements I love and that in combination with being such an awesome game is great. If we forget the history I have with the developers and just look at the game and its achievements itself, I would have ranked it in my top 5 indie games in 2021.

_childDocuments_.review: SHORT VERSION:The Last Friend is a lane-based tower defense game in which you balance tower placement with runnin' around smackin' fools. It's a pretty good one of these, with a good variety of towers and personal abilites that you can combine as you wish. Things can get a little stale at points though, as certain late-game strategies are extremely solid once they're built, and a good brawler won't have much trouble collecting the scrap to build them. Overall, I had a pretty good time, and even the overpowered builds were pretty fun to unleash upon the enemy during my final push.LONG VERSION:MY PROGRESS:I've completed every mission in the game and earned every achievement. Took me just a touch over 10 hours.STRENGTHS:- VARIETY:The game does a pretty good job of taking simple building blocks and building them into a wide variety of scenarios if you choose to engage with them. By the end of this game, you'll have 12 towers, 24 passive skills for yourself, and 6 supers, and your RV will fill in 6 upgrade tracks. There are also elemental field effects, some of which can combine, or just explode. The enemies are fairly simple, but there's enough going on that through most of the game you can vary your strategy and bring in new pieces as you go. Also, the brawling has a fair amount of options to it, though bosses don't do as much to mix it up as they could.WEAKNESSES:- SEVERAL OVERPOWERED STRATEGIES:Things get a bit stale late-game, as there are some build strategies that are darn near unbreakable once they're up. Level 3 sniper in particular is incredibly broken, allowing you to stunlock most units in defense missions.OTHER POINTS OF INTEREST:- I'M OLD:All of you referencing PvZ in the reviews here clearly never played The Last Stand. The name has to be a reference, right?OVERALL:I had a pretty good time with this game. Though I did find it easy, it was an enjoyably active sort of easy.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm on the fence with The Last Friend.This is kind of a Plants vs Zombies clone with lanes for a tower defense game but it's also a beat em up. You control a character who runs around the level and can fight enemies while turrets also do their thing. All of the mechanics are rather basic between tower defense and beat em up. It certainly works pretty well for what it is.Now I don't know if maybe the game isn't for me, even if I got it to relive some PvZ nostalgia, but after about 2 hours, I don't really have any desire to go on. The first turret you get is very strong and you can level it up to cover three lanes. After about an hour and a half, you'll enter levels with 5 lanes so it prevents you from just building those turrets down the middle but I still just found myself building those in lanes 2 & 4 over and over. As a result, every level started feeling rather repetitive.Fortunately, there are some levels that are strictly beat em up to break up the pacing a bit. I did enjoy the first hour and a half or so but it starts to drag from there. I got the game cheap as part of a bundle so I'm happy with my purchase with my limited experience with it but your miles may vary. I'd say it's worth picking up on the cheap if you can find it at the right price.

_childDocuments_.review: I was not expecting this game to be so good! The writing's very meh in the beginning and gets marginally better later but it is a great experience. This is like 's cat befriending mechanics but with dogs, and as a beat-'em-up/tower defence hybrid instead of an open world action RPG.If I had any criticisms other than the writing, it's that there's not much reason to diversify your turret lineup. Unlike , the terrain and enemies aren't particularly diverse no matter what biome you're in so having the typical shooter-miner-shield-buffer-healer combo will get you far no matter what you're up against and there's little reason to mix things up.Also, it's cool that there are dogs for turrets and dogs for self-buffs, allowing you to play both with the tower defence and beat-'em-up elements. It's just a shame that you only have so many slots in your loadout so it's a pair of scales you have to weigh. I think games like this and  would benefit heavily from having two separate loadouts; one for towers, one for personal items and abilities. This would allow players to enjoy both sides of the gameplay to their full extent without sacrificing one for the other due to limited inventory.I also suffered from weird graphical stuff with effects not having transparency so a lot of people were covered by squares whenever they had some kind of aura or status ailment for some reason or another. The Golden Retriever's Charge and the final boss' second phase were notorious offenders. But that didn't stop the game from being fun to play so I toughed it out and had a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: Long review:So far the Game is easy, simple & and doesn't offer that much of a challenge in general, but is comfy asf, maybe you don't play it for the amazing and immersive story that it has, but just because the game is cute as heck.I don't play many games as I used to, everything feels empty, and I don't know if it's because I'm getting older and I can see the pattern of how videogames are being made,  or is truly just more of the same and finding innovation is extremely difficult because we are reaching to the point of " this has been made " ( Oh sh*t, another Call of Duty shoting wanna be game damn ! ).But you know, sometimes things don't have to be innovative or be the GOTY, sometimes I wanna play something comfy, something that doesn't require a huge development, or with realistic graphics ( and a huge pc to run them of course ).I don't need a mindblowing story or relatable characters.Sometimes there's beauty in simplicity, and this game has that, is simple, colorful, cool, and I enjoy that rather than your typical FPS of the year.And the most important: it has a chihuaha as main character.Game is short, but you know, I enjoyed it it a lot.Short review:9/10 not enough dogs

_childDocuments_.review: A game that I can't think of anything negative to say about. It contains doggos, grid based tower defense (a la PVZ), the ability to woop the crap out of enemies in a Streets of Rage kinda way, and a campy story that doesn't take itself too seriously.  The game introduces the dogs as a slotable upgrade that you get to pick before the actual mission begins. There are 3 variants and all are useful in some way. By the end of the game you will have found your own groove to how you want to handle things. For example if you only wanted to kick 7 hells out of the enemies you could literally just set up a crap ton of shield turrets and go to town on the enemies mono a mono. If that doesn't suit you you could pop on a healing doggo and set up several rows of good bois to wail on the baddies coming your way. The games not really all that difficult so it really just lets anything fly and I like it for that. It's not overly long at around 10-12ish hours to do everything but I did enjoy my time with it. If there was to be something I would suggest maybe a new game plus with everything unlocked but the campaign is much harder the second time around. At $15 I would definitely say it's worth it but at $10 you should jump on it and enjoy the cuteness!

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Friend is a easy Plants Vs. Zombies-like with 2-player coop, three lane tower defense, and brawling gameplay. Unfortunately, it's nothing stellar, but with the right mindset, or budding gamer it can be good decent fun.The levels are short, the unlocks let's you work for something, the story has you going around rescuing dogs and is written well.However only player 1 can build, P2 can only do supplemental actions like drill for scrap (currency for player 1 to build turrets- both players can brawl). Which is fine for what they're going for. The biggest negative is (my personal bias) the game's too simple, too easy. You do get more complex strategies a short bit into the game but with only three lanes to defend and 5 Doggies to choose from, more seasoned gamers may not enjoy the gameplay loop.
