_childDocuments_.review: Early access means that you are the guinea pigs to discover the bugs withing, and there are plenty of them.Now, finding bugs can be an exhausting experience, and I do not see why we should pay to be stressed.  We play games to amuse ourselves and to relax.  This is not amusing.  This is not relaxing.  This is WORK.  And work should be paid.  Instead we pay for the privilege of being stressed or irritated.Let me know when the cleaned up version comes up, and I will buy it.  But I refuse to work for free
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful interaction and gameplay. Great characters and character development. Storyline reveals itself with flourish. Villains and enemies are interesting and the fights are challenging. I never thought of typing as a weapon - I thought I was just improving my typing skills - nice to play a game that is interesting but still teaches you things. Fantasy element is beautifully expressed. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Way over a year ago, I reported multiple bugs on the forum. The game won't run on ultrawide screen. Your keyboard configuration may not always be the right one (I'm using Bépo). The missing words are invisible and cannot be guessed. The first game cinematic is a black screen with only subtitles on top. All of these issues, game-breakers. Not even one of these issues has even been solved. All in all, Nanotale doesn't hold a candle to Epistory, it's just the sad reality.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: is an awesome typing game that is at the apex of the typing genre. It's actually pretty awesome to play a game with keyboard only, especially a well made game such as Nanotale. Expect about 6 hours of game play (game can be played offline so my hours show as less). The typing is forgiving and pace of enemies isn't too difficult. Coordinating attacks > typing speed.Awesome game! Picked this up after playing their older typing chronicle game (epistory). This is game is super well done. The fights are fun and the typing doesn't feel like the focus of the game, despite all the controls and fights requiring typing. I really like the combination of spells and the reactions that can be made by typing words. Comparing it to Epistory, this game is more polished and the movement and fighting is better. They are unrelated story wise though, but you get to ride a fox around and type words to uncover the lore of the world in both. However I would recommend Nanotale prior/over Epistory. Epistory had a higher typing speed requirement to complete the story line  (awesome but too hard for beginners). In Nanotale, you can get away with a much slower typing speed, and the world feels a lot more alive and cute (there are NPCs you can talk to and side quests to complete.) However there are a few bugs (character gets stuck) but you can respawn using the menu (not an issue with Epistory).
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes what worked well in Epistory and improves every system, from the depth of the story, to the control you have over your spells, to how much freedom you have during combat... and the result is that doing so exposes all it's flaws. A deeper story reveals how boring the story is. Having more control over spells reveals how terrible typing is as an interface for spell casting. Freedom in combat changes the strategy in combat enough that it becomes less about typing speed and more about positioning, which isn't great for a game about typing.But even with all that, it still manages to scratch the 'typing rpg' itch in a way like no other game save Epistory. So, if you've played that and want more, this game delivers on that. If you haven't played that, go play that first. It's a simpler game, and is better because of it.Edit: The last half / third (not sure, haven't finished yet) feels rushed. The collision bugs that have been present throughout are worse, the game does a worse job at balance, the story progression feels barely connected and the boss fights feel like more of a drag. On the other hand, the puzzle design starts having actually half decent puzzles that make good use of the spell mechanics. Still an overall recommend - just be aware that the experience gets worse in many ways as the game goes on.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I much preferred Epistory to this game, but it's still quite good. The are different maps, about 4 I believe that you'll have to go through to move on with the story which is fine.There are a few bugs in the Desert area, which I found online occurred to a number of people, don't know if it will eventually get fixed but that was quite irritating...
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty half-baked. There's enough substance that, with a bit more polish, it could have been a solid typing game (which, admittedly, I consider a lower standard), but Nanotale falls short of this mark.I'll add that my copy of this game was neither free, nor outright paid for - it's part of the package when you buy a ZSA "Voyager" keyboard. My experience with the game was while learning this new (and exotic) keyboard format. I mention this as an aside, and isn't influencing this review.* I was stuck on terrain multiple times, requiring a self-kill/respawn.* Several of the spells that modify the terrain have invisible gaps where the player cannot cross where expected, and break immersion repeatedly.* Pre-rendered video (loading-screen background, all end-story cinematics) seem to be in the wrong color-space, and are saturated with reds and yellows.* Nearly all environments/maps needed gamma-correction, and were either washed out, dim, or both.* Nearly all voice-acting was missing post-processing effects (or maybe it was just that bad?).* QA (if there was QA) missed obvious things like the voice actor mispronouncing words (said "gracious" instead of "graceful").* UI appearing off-screen and unreadable because of it.* Puzzles that made me look back and squint, wondering how I was  to solve it.* Plot points that I can only describe as laziness on the part of the writer.I also have a strong suspicion that much of the game's assets came straight from the Unity store, but I haven't gone to confirm that one.All of this is sad because it's clear that at least some of the team put a lot of care and thought into this game. I want to like this game, I do - but if I had deliberately spent money for the purpose of getting this game, I would have sought a refund long before I reached completion.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: => Improves upon Epistory in a lot of ways but like Epistory, it still feels unfinished even if there's fun to be had with what is there. Can walk into out of bounds areas. Forgets hotkeys. Character can get stuck but there's fortunately a "unstuck" setting. Can be hard to move along the ice paths so sort of have to run at the path from all sorts of angles until you finally path onto it. Given the option to choose between abilities when levelling up but there's pretty much only ever one option to choose from. Base attack is a bit too weak versus most enemies so end up running around until there's enough mana and then using the spells for everything and I think this makes combat worse than what it could be. No longer have enemies that are weaker and stronger vs. different damage types, which is a downgrade from Epistory. Felt like in every battle, there's always a best spell to cast instead of there being multiple viable spell options. The voice acting was quite bad at times. Final trigger for me was a problem at end of game that stopped me from finding any more Starlet plants. Think it was bugged but had 99% so used Steam Achievement Manager for that last achievement
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: A little clunky, but fairly unique and well worth the price.It's an upgraded Epistory in most regards.There's a world to explore. The game is mostly a collectathon, but because the world isn't bland and doesn't handhold you, it feels like a exploration, rather than ticking boxes. The clunk comes from weird default controls and collision detection. I've already fallen off a map, got stuck on various tiny obstacles (for some time, as character gets stuck in a slide) . The world is top down with no jumping so it's really weird for them to have such complex collision detection.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Game is ass compared to the first title, they literally made every aspect worse.The story is boring and dragged out, talking to NPCs feels like a chore, as do the puzzles. The mechanics in the first game were easy to understand, this game just makes it more complex for no reason, and sometimes doesn't work as intended. Finally, optimization is very poorly done, some parts have fps drops worse than Dragon's Dogma 2.In conclusion: ass, play the first one instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing Epistory and would consider it one of the best typing games out there. This feels like a rushed afterthought, the gameplay isnt nearly as good and the game isnt as cohesive. At the end of the game you have a ton of spells which the game doesnt force you to cycle through. Game was far too easy, I had adaptive difficulty on which worked really well in the first game but in this did not make the game hard enough. Would recommend you stick to Epistory.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy testing my typing speed and I enjoy fantasy rpgs. This is a nice short combination of both, and a puzzle game to boot, as you have to use a combination of powers to keep advancing, (ex. you must type "ray" + "fire" to shoot a beam of fire, perhaps to burn away obstacle thorns). The voice acting is not great, except for the main character who is decent, but I didn't find it too distracting. I enjoyed their previous game epistory, and I found this one to be a step forward in terms of story and gameplay. I would love to see a new game that has advanced even further!
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy typing games and epistory but I avoided this game until now due to the reports of bugs.  I just grabbed it as I wanted to work on my йцукейн layout typing and get some language practice.  Just finished the game with only one side quest that was blocked form being completed by a bug.  I did get several bugs where the game would get stuck in slow down mode and I would have to exit an restart to clear it.  I also had a few lockups.  Annoyingly twice at the end of boss fights (had to redo them).  However, all in all, I enjoyed the game and did find it helpful for practicing my typing with alternate keyboard layout as well as with the language I am studying.  I had to screenshot some of the text (a few places where it disappears on it's own) to give me time to puzzle out the sentences but that was no problem.  So, yes there are bugs, but at least I managed to complete the game with nothing game breaking.  Would buy it again.  I also recommend it for the purpose of language study if it's localized to the language you are working on.  Especially if it contains a different keyboard layout.  Only for reading, as the voice acting isn't localized.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: The game wasn't so bad, until when it got a bug in the final boss battle and I was stuck without changing to next stage, me and fox and boss were awkward.So I reload the state to play the boss battle again, and the end credit was cringe that it had no BGM but just ambient sound, me and fox and boss were awkward again.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: It's been 2 years since the launch of this game, and it's still incredibly buggy. BUGS: It is playable, but incredibly buggy. I finished the game in 8 hours, got all the lore, and died about 4 times to bugs, and had to restart the game at various points, like at the beginning of the desert where you're supposed to use the push spell to get rid of the brambles, or when I tried to leave the caves too early and my character died, but I wasn't able to do anything but force shut down the game to try again. I had to use the debug movement in the menu twice. Another bug is that I skipped the part where the queen went mad, and was thoroughly confused when the wood people were freaked out by her. And I was not able to sprint during almost any fight. The help icon was incredible, thank you for adding that because you can't follow the story otherwise most times. ANNOYING DESIGN: The most annoying two things on the top of my mind are that when you make a spell pathway, whether ice or brambles, it's incredibly janky and it takes a few attempts just to walk on it most times. And during the final boss fight you're encouraged to just skip dialogue because you're literally being attacked during it, it is a feature, you're able to fight back, but it's hard to do so when 5+ left-over enemies from the wave come at you from behind with less than a second's warning before they hit. And one other game design flaw is that you can go back to your previous areas after completing them, but the rest of your adventure has zero impact on anything else to my knowledge. It's like they made a linear pathway and didn't expect you to go back and talk to the queen after completing the caves. STORY(spoilers): The storyline was interesting, but they never explained anything about spirits other than that foxes only show themselves in times of great need, they never flesh out the teacher, but throw her in at the last second before the boss fight because they have to make sure you know that she's proud of you. Then you get the reveal and you can't even emotionally invest into the main story because you barely know the fox, and all he does is plea with his father and tries to explain that everything was different, and that he had to stop, which immediately translated into the guy apparently dying? Maybe? They flew away as spirits leaving everyone else who believed in the Baron to kinda just figure it out themselves?ART: Absolutely fabulous, but my computer is pretending to be an air plane engine on the lowest graphics settings, and I can't see any faces or emotion on faces, which makes it incredibly difficult to connect to different characters, but it's a very pretty game.DIFFICULTY AND CONCLUSION: I have a typing speed of about 55 to 60, and the difficulty is challenging, but the game lowers accuracy if you're not focused on it because it focuses a lot on speed. The end game abilities makes it almost laughably easy if you take too much time to warm up on the initial test. It's a very pretty game, but because of the bugs and lack of thought put into the story, I don't recommend it, even 2 years later.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun exploration game where puzzles and combat are solved with typing words and proper positioning.But it is not without issues. One crash at a guardian battle. Camera locking when I changed areas and no longer fallowing the character. The player getting stuck in the terrain or in sheep.The game play somewhat improved compared to the first game by adding positioning and selective buffs to your word attacks. But it felt too easy and I was not very engaged with the story.I was expecting the game to improve my tipping, with entire sentences, not random words related to the scenery. But was also happy with what I got.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Nanotale is a good game but not a great one. The new spell system is pretty intriguing, and i it gives the gameplay and traversal another great dimension. There is also an openness to the game that feels pretty novel for the epistory game.However I find that the other parts of the game lacks polish. There are some stutters and bugs around the game, the animations arent that smooth, and the different visual elements of the game don't interact well with eachother in my opinion. I also found the story a bit harder to follow and figure out.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone who loved Epistory and it's gorgeous unfolding origami world, this is a total disappointment. I just don't know what the devs were trying to do with this game; the scenery is very very PURPLE and AQUA. I put that in caps because the colors are very much in your face. It is still a hand drawn world but still feels flat to me. There are characters to interact with in this game that are all a bunch of jerks that I have no desire to help whatsoever. There is some mystery about a Tree of life and a sort-of evil queen but I just can't bring myself to care. I'm uninstalling after a disappointing couple of hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited because I finally got to play this game after Epistory. If you liked that one, keep playing that one. The art is beautiful and I kinda want to keep playing, but the fact that I encountered a bug by the time I was starting the prologe and that the tutorials for some spells are really, really bad deter me from it. A pity really, becaue I truly wanted to play and like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Love their typing games, this one was great as well. But... very buggy. Some of it is understandable, it's because your spells are directional and you can walk on them. Other bugs are game crashing. The hands in the desert had the most for more, the game was somewhat fine before. The hand part is also very unclear how to progress before you do the first one, the game stops telling you what to do just "find your own path".This game has a reverse difficulty curve lol, it's hardest at the beginning and easiest at the end.Good points - the art is gorgeous, the collectible system great. You have many ways to solve the different challenges. The puzzles are thought invoking, and there are secret quests around.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice looking game.For me it seems that the game is most bug fixed in the beginning of the game and then the further you play more bugs occur. Once at around 30% of the game my character was glitched into a mission animation and i couldnt get out of it. Also with the respawn function it glitched into the same position. Closing the game and restarting it fixed the problem. Besides that i found that the 'ice spell' creates a lot of dynamic bugs. And many in game movies hang and it then takes about 30 to 60 seconds of nothingness and then the game continues. And the amount of typing sometimes makes my hands feel dead.Judging the game as a whole I believe this is a great game. I have not yet completed it, but I experience this game like FEZ which means to me a complete new way of gaming and that innovation makes gaming fun and attractive again.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, really nicely executed. Challenging, without being frustrating, which is always appreciated. Whilst I found Epistory frustratingly hard in places, Nanotale seems to have gotten the right balance. Took me about eight hours to 100%, so good for achievement hunters too. It's a little janky in places, but it's a very gorgeous game, so I'd definitely recommend picking up in a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Game has degraded since the original.On top of not improving on the glaring problems of the original game, the game makes even more mistakes then before.- The Controls are still poor, having the player switch in and out of typing mode is irritating and now they want the player to do it mid battle to avoid getting hit. They have also moved the default mapped keys for movement to be esdf? It would be so much easier to map movement to just be on the mouse and arrow keys and stop the player from having to switch into typing mode.- There is still no incentive for you to spell words correctly, you can type half of a word then press every other key on the keyboard other then the next letter and still finish the word without any consequence.- Typing games are generally more suited towards younger and elder audiences, meaning complex puzzles and confusing pathways are often overlooked, definitely something this game didn't need to implement, and yet it does.That being said, I did like the notebook drawings, which was not in the original.5.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game with an interesting story. The concept of typing to play is relatively well executed and enjoyable. The achievements feel satisfying without being too difficult. The graphics are pretty even with the graphics at their lowest setting, and it runs fairly smoothly even on a meh laptop. There are, however, some notable bugs and flaws. Some of them are minor and can easily be fixed by respawning or don't affect game play. Others are fairly significant. The scoreboards in the arena don't appear to function properly. Player-created "platforms" (such as ice) are finicky and often have to be redone several times to allow the player to walk on top of them. One of the areas where the player can get a spell fragment remained grey even after collecting that fragment. It's possible to open the menu right as a cut scene starts (which is not unlikely to happen since the cut scenes take a moment to begin), which soft locks the game and prevents the menu from being accessed. You can change the key-bindings, but they reset to the default each time the game is closed. This in particular was very frustrating to me since I would prefer to use wasd for movement, but the default is esdf, so I had to change it every time.All in all it's a good game, and I really enjoyed playing it through. I do recommend it, but it does seem like it needs some fixes.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Nanotable - Typing Chronicles is a decent typing game that unfortunately doesn't live up to its predecessor. While it's still enjoyable, the game can be frustrating at times, especially when it comes to navigating the map. The story also falls short compared to the previous installment, failing to captivate and engage players in the same way.That being said, Nanotable - Typing Chronicles is still a fun game for those who enjoy typing games. The game mechanics are solid and the typing challenges are engaging, providing a good level of difficulty without being too frustrating.However, given its shortcomings, I would only recommend this game to those who are able to purchase it on sale. While it's not a bad game, it doesn't quite measure up to the excellence of its predecessor.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: The typing part is very fun. Typing out the spells you want is really interesting. Combat is not bad either, although you'll usually find one favorite spell to spam when you have the mana.The art looks good. I like seeing how something looks in the overworld compared to its drawing in the field journal/notebook. Sound and voice acting is good enough for this game, it's not like someone reading off a teleprompter.Ending feels a little short and sudden, but that's because the antagonist isn't a salty scrub who values their pride over what's right. In another game the antagonist may have a fit and refuse to come around to the protagonist's side, but it's nice to see here that the antagonist hears out the protags and changes their own way.The main downside of this game is the bugs. There's innocuous bugs, like if you sprint away after talking to someone your animation is frozen for a second while you're moving. There's distracting bugs, like if you trigger a cutscene while your tab minimap is open, the minimap may get stuck open and block a lot of your vision. And there's disruptive bugs, like certain areas in the map which may cause you to drop through the floor and die instantly. Luckily, there's enough autosaves so I've never felt like I lost any progress, and if you ever get stuck you can try respawning, or if that fails, go to main menu and continue game.I got all but 3 achievements going through the main story, and the rest of the achievements took less than 20 minutes while following a steam guide.Overall, I recommend this game if you like typing games - for example, if you've played their previous game Epistory - Typing Chronicles and liked the typing part, there's more typing here. Everything else is average. I like the easter egg though, that was fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Prettier than Epistory, but I liked the atmosphere in Epistory more, though this didn't have such a dissappointing ending. The controls are an evolved version of Epistory and not in a bad way. There are more bugs, and some of them affect gameplay. Also, in the last third there are some unclear parts in the story; I was stuck for ages until I accidentally triggered a boss I should've been looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I found Nanotale to be a relaxing game overall.  There is a certain magic to typing in words and having them turn into spells on your screen.  I found it rewarding to find things to archive and appreciated the poetic descriptions they would unlock.  If you are looking for something more challenging with a more rewarding story go check out Epistory... but if you want a light magical adventure while brushing up on your typing Nanotale will be a very pleasant time.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second game in the Typing Chronicles series. They've made several improvements to the combat, including some more specific spells such as "RAY" and "SPREAD" that allow you to move elements across the battlefield. The story is just as good as the first one, and it actually features some nice voice acting. Exploration here is a little tedious because many places require backtracking and rely on your ability to understand how to use spells. Many of the puzzles I had to look up for help online and the game will show you "where" you need to go but not how you need to get here. It could do with some more hints from the characters in the game. They have a lot to say but not much to help you gameplay-wise. One thing I miss from the last game is the ability to teleport between regions of the map. Especially later on in places like the Underground and the Desert, this would have been very useful.Sometimes you can do a lot of quests out of sequence unintentionally, which may spoil some of the story. There were a fair number of times I also got stuck due to falling off an unintended edge or running into a corner of the map that wasn't meant to be traversed. Thankfully, there is a "RESPAWN" spell from the pause menu, but it can be frustrating to have to navigate back to where you were. Is it worth the trouble? I did enjoy myself, but it did come with some headaches. If you get stuck too, try looking in the discussions. I left some bread crumbs in there to help. With a little more polish this game could go from good to great! The combat is interesting and they have some interesting mechanics. It's overall an improvement over the first game, so I'm excited to see what they do for their next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Nanotale is a good solid build typing game and one worth giving a go if looking for more after finishing Epistory (recommend playing first).However, found I enjoyed the story, exploration, combat and art style of the first game (Episotry) better than Nanotale. Epistory just felt and bit more charming to play and I also preferred being able to focus on just typing rather than needing to also consider type activating spells like in Nanotale.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

being that sadly this game is very buggy. initially, i didnt experience or notice any during my first time trying the story, in fact i was so hooked that i spent well over 7 hours first day i tried the story mode. loved the typing it makes you feel like a powerful mage. and when you finally get that right combination of words together quickly it can have devstating affects. addittionally. this games isnt just combat but a little bit of puzzle.  i will be honest, and say that there needed to be a little more guidance in the beginning but once, i got past that the puzzles became much more fun and intresting. however this is where i must go with the flaws of the game. 1. game does not save your progess correctly or at all.   i understand that this game uses an autosave system however, it doesnt save shard placement or lore items. this conflicts with the fact that i continued to have one of the spell modifers that required  a shard. once, i ended my seven hour session and went to bed.  it didnt save the lore, i got stuck somewhere fighting an arena battle i couldnt win, then died where i was, i attempted to reload the game. but still couldnt get back where i was. before i realized that respawn was there, i decide that i would play story mode again just for the heck of it becuase i enjoyed it however, i attempted to stop after thirty minutes and work on something else planning _childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Nanotale is beautiful graphically and I had a blast exploring and completing the journey.  You can choose to either set the difficulty to a set wpm amount or let the game determine what is best based on your typing skill.  Ultimately I had fun playing through it, so I will rate it as a thumbs up despite all the bugs.There is arena (endless) mode where you can continue playing even after beating the story.  I encountered quite a few bugs along the way.  A lot of markers remained lit on the map (as if an objective seemingly wasn't completed).  The "Fairest in the Kingdom" objective never showed as completed on the map, but I did complete it in game and was able to progress.I was also never able to complete the Soraya quest.  After healing the dragon and examining all the Tamarai lore I returned to Soraya.  The objective wouldn't complete; she only kept giving the same 2 dialogue boxes over and over.If you care about achievements and 100% completion:  It's seemingly impossible to get 100% achievements done in this game.  I have no lore left on the map and it's showing as I'm missing 1 Stray Starlet from the log of plant life.  I tried running all around the forest area (where the Stray Starlet is located), thinking possibly it was unmarked, but was able to find nothing.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Story is pretty short and not really that special, but the fighting mechanic is really fun. Fighting aspect is a huge upgrade compared to Epistory. Spells can interact with each other. For example, you can throw water at enemies then poison or zap them for AoE dmg.Unfortunately, fun spells (self apply, water, poison) only available at near end game so I didn't get to enjoy them more often.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: For some, the game can be tough, for others relaxing - it depends if you are a fast typer and if you can write in English (for foreigners).You can play the game in 10 hours, including achievements, for some challengers you can finish it in less than 4 hours.It was worth it, a lot of imagination, the storyline was beautiful - you will learn not only about botany, but also words from everyday life - both simple and difficult ones.One point down for me because I couldn't get my bearings on the map at times. And I'm a bit dumber, so it took me a while to figure out what to do with ... certain things ... :)I recommend the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Unless you can get it on sale, I wouldn't really recommend it.The story is quite uninteresting and feels wholly unfinished, gameplay outside of boss fights is exactly what you get - type a word to either damage an enemy, gather a resource (health/ mana) or traverse the obstacles, puzzles can be quite janky at times and act 3 can get bug prone due to either bosses not working correctly or just getting stuck in places from sprinting. The map is also godawful. And difficuly also seems to be all over the place. There "is" an option to turn on adaptive difficulty, but thoughout the whole game, even at the start, it would just excessively long words to type even for the weakest enemies and then straight aftrer just a three letter word.Honestly, I dunno if I'm misremembering something, but Epistory did this type of game way better while being very similar.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Loved Epistory and loving Nanotale! Both helped me discover how much I love and excel at typing :D Even though Nanotale still has many bugs, its gameplay is like no other, the balance of retrieving spells is excellent, and it has a great flow. And as for the bugs, at least the game has a respawn function, so whenever I get stuck in an invisible barrier, or there are some problems with the game, I can just press that, and it's done. I couldn't put Nanotale down, and I hope they make a similar yet different game again, just like how this one followed Epistory :)
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to enjoy this game and I love the concept behind it, but ultimately it just felt like it was missing something. I can't recommend it.✅ I did like the exploration aspect and various puzzles and the way the game makes you think about how to use your spells. The battles were interesting and there isn't any severe consequence if you mistype. The voice acting wasn't stellar but I didn't mind, I thought the way the characters spoke fit with the game's atmosphere.❌Controls can be awkward at times. You easily get stuck and trapped on ordinary rocks and plants, to the point where they had to put in a respawn button in the pause menu. If you want/need to backtrack it's very tedious. The plot meandared and the ending felt rushed to say the least. And the biggest crime of all is that the poison sound effect won't. ever. stop. You literally have to reboot the game for it to go away... tssssss.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't think I could enjoy a typing game as much as I do this game. The art is beautiful, the music is great, the combat is fun, and the exploration is interesting. It hooked me in pretty quick. I've played a few hours now and it's hard for me to stop, plus my typing has already improved. It feels good to be able to enjoy a game guilt-free because the time I spend isn't just a waste of time it's actually improving an ability I use for everyday life.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game, it's fun to play, the visuals an music are nice. Apart from interspersed "arena" sequences when enemies come from all sides and you have to type like mad it's also relaxing, often you can just walk and look around while exploring a huge map. It never really gets scary, even the monsters look kinda cute really.My only criticism is that the game is buggy sometimes. Nothing that kept me from finishing the game, but it can be distracting. The most common bug is getting stuck in some place without being able to move. Luckily there's a respawn button to get out of this.Anyhow. I liked the game and recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Nanotale is a really creative typing game. It takes us through multiple regions to uncover the mysteries and quests of the people who inhabit these lands. There are puzzles, enemies and bosses to conquer! Our ability to type spells helps us solve puzzles while our speed helps us stay alive during mob fights. I found the storytelling to be lacking in quality a little bit, but all things considered, Nanotale was a very good game. I definitely recommend! And if you're not sure about it, give the demo a try👍🏽
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: is an excellent typing genre adventure game, has a interesting story and it was overall fun to play out. Typing itself has made better from previous series so accidentally starting two words or your power words won't get mixed up while playing.As a bug hunter master, encountered few of those but game own respawn system got me out of those.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Great development of the mechanics of Epistory, graphics and art design are really nice, challenge is appreciated -- this is a game that requires you to be a highly competent touch typist from the start; if you come here expecting Mavis Beacon you'll be frustrated early and often.Cons: Story, music, and voice acting are pretty optional; lots of backtracking on a map that isn't always super easy to navigate; certain puzzles require precision aiming that doesn't feel great; keyboard controls can get frantic during boss bottles.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun and beautiful typing game! Totally cheesed the last achievement where you need 4805 words typed. When I finished the game I had just gotten the achievement for 3450 words. So after standing between 3 crystals typing the full words for 15 minutes, I realized I could just type "Ice" about 800 times for the rest. Needless to say my WPM went from 44 to 160 and VOILA last achievement about 6 minutes later! XDDefinitely recommend this game! Looking forward to trying out it's predecessor!
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: The second Typing Chronicles game is a completely different story from the first, Epistory. The gameplay is much the same, with typing words to affect the environment. Unlike the first game, where the magic was elemental, here the magic imparts modifiers to the words so that they have larger or more focused effects was well as the effects they wish to impart, pushing, pulling, or healing, and so forth. They work well to make various combat options interesting and allow for a much greater degree of crowd control than was possible in the previous game.Conversation is also possible by typing keywords as they appear in the conversation (oh, yes, there's other entities in this game to talk to!) on those subjects as you encounter them.There's also a fishing cactus, just like in the last game, too.If you like games with story and where you can control destiny with your keyboard, or you are a fan of Epistory, you'll like this game. Butt if you come in expecting more of the same that you got in Epistory, you're going to be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard for me to decide whether I'd really recommend Nanotale or not... More yes than no, I guess. But it just feels too long and too big. Epistory had perfect length. Plus the story in Nanotale was kinda disjointed, with lore being given out of order. The writing also kinda off at times. Like when the tree guy keeps saying "dude", just takes me out of it. A few annoying bugs. Like in the caverns when i got past a serpent statue surrounded by poison and could go back. Had to find a long way back, which was annoying. And the final fight glitched, with one of the waves just kept coming,But... i did have fun with it for a while. The art style was nice, as well as the voice acting. I liked messing around with spells. I just wish it was shorter, i guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: ACHIEVEMENT REVIEW--How difficult is 100% all achievements?--☑ Easy☐ Average☐ Challenging☐ Impossible/Excruciatingly Difficult, Tedious or Long.---I completed the game and obtained all achievements in about 11-12hours. One thing to keep in mind, is that you can only see Lore markers in the same region as yourself. And typing just the spell (i.e. FIRE/ICE) will still count towards your word count achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: haven't beaten it yet, however it is way better than the first game and feels more like an actual game. not that the last one wasn't a game, but the addition of npc's and quests and everything really make this a more enjoyable experience and even less of chore. Ran into a game breaking glitch that has a current fix, unfortunately it requires the devs to manually fix my save file and the response time is a little slow as you can imagine. coming up on 2 weeks and i have lost all momentum with my typing practice.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game, but I just can't. There are just too many bugs and poor design choices for me to get into it. Rather than being able to get lost in the world like one can get lost in a good book, it comes across as getting lost in the world in the sense of needing to ask for directions.The deal-breaker for me was when I tried to continue my saved game, only for the character to be dead as soon as I loaded. The "respawn" option in the menu didn't help either. That they needed to put a respawn option in the menu to try compensate for bugs - and for it to still not work - really should tell you a lot about how much more bugfixing this game needed before it was published.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: It seemed much easier than Epistory which was a shame, but the adjectives addition really add some fun strategy to the combat. The ability to play around with different elements made for some great traversal/puzzles, but they felt a little unpolished and buggy(ice in particular).I would rate Epistory a little higher than this one, but it's still worth a purchase and a good addition to the Typing Chronicles franchise, I look forward to more.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I played all the way through Epistory, and now I'm hooked on Nanotale. It had a slow start for me, but it picked up as I went and I really enjoy it. I think it would be more frustrating if I was a beginner typist but I feel confident enough that I can nail the challenges, so it isn't a stressful experience. I find the game pretty relaxing and a way to stretch my vocab.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I played Epistory a few years back and absolutely loved it, so when I heard that this game was coming, I was extremely excited. Life stuff kept me from getting it during beta, but when I finally had a break and was able to pick it up, I wasn't disappointed! At the time of writing, I've only experienced getting stuck once or twice, and no other bugs. The only reason I haven't finished the game is that the desert can be hard to navigate when you're tired and it's 2am!Both the story and the game mechanics are a *huge* step up from Epistory, so even though I've played through that game twice and spent many hours in the arena, Nanotale was still a fresh game that brought fresh challenges. I plan to spend many more hours playing to complete all of the achievements. The soundtrack is also a gem that works well with the story and on its own, and really helps round the game out.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Nanotale on Mac is beautifully designed and generally a joy to play. instead of pointing a gun at enemies, you type words to strike blows. This mechanism engages the rest of the brain, and challenge me physically and mentally, making for a more engaging experience than with typical games. I'd love to see more story based games using this mechanic, or other mechanics that take advantage of our input devices. Both this, and the Cactus' other venture, Epistory, are beautiful worlds, with perfect soundtracks. I've played both games on the Mac, and I can say that while it is basically functional, glitches abound. I think that's the price of playing a game by a younger studio, who is focused on story, art, and this awesome typing mechanic. Highly recommend Nanotale & Epistory.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: If you're here after playing Epistory because you want more; I hate to say it but this ain't it, chief. It's bright and colorful and has an interesting magic/problem solving system. It is otherwise not as interesting as Epistory and feels very unfinished. It's very buggy, the dialogue volume is really inconsistent, my character constantly got stuck, bosses did too, one of the skills (possession) straight up doesn't work for me, and it's really easy. Boringly easy. I'm giving this a thumbs up because it looks like a huge amount of work went into it. And the foundation is there. I didn't have a terrible time; but I didn't have a great time. If the two major things here got better or fixed, bugs and characters getting stuck, this would be an easier recommend for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely spiritual successor to Epistory. As with its predecessor, the art and world are both enchanting and enjoyable to discover as you progress. The different biomes and additional spells you learn add a nice complexity to the game's puzzle-reliant exploration without ever being too difficult. Combat also feels more varied and improved over Epistory's original design, with more options and modifiers to your magic.There's only a few minor critiques I can give to Nanotale. One is that I encountered a few bugs throughout in which I fell through the map or otherwise got stuck, though the game does include a forced respawn option for these cases. The frame rates on the beginning and ending cutscenes also feel significantly choppier than the rest of the game. Story-wise, the end of the game feels rather abrupt, though the rest of the story is nice in its simplicity and charm.Overall, a game I would recommend for a short, pleasant experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Wonderful story and world, it's challenging but not too difficult and still fun (I say this as someone who gives up very easily, but this game made me wanna keep trying)About the story (Spoiler free) Personally I loved the ending and it gave the whole game the feeling that everything that happened along the way was important.I can only recommend it.Note: There are some minor bugs that need fixing but there's a simple "respawn" option in the escape menu to get out of the stuck positions.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games that require you to do a lot of typing and that has a decent storyline, Nanotale is a great game for you. If you don't like typing, this game would not be for you. The game is, nonetheless, enjoyable. My wife enjoys watching me play Nanotale and I like games involving typing so this was a no-brainer for me, after the developers' previous game Epistory: Typing Chronicles, which I enjoyed very much. This one plays a little differently, involving a lot of puzzles you really have to think your way through involving casting magic in a push or pull direction, whether you want it to spread or be refined with sharp. Due to all of these maneuvers and can take some time messing around with stuff to find out what actually works. But it wouldn't be much fun if you could just blow right through the whole thing, right? I definitely recommend this to anybody who likes typing games.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

There were some points where I didn't pick up some details for much longer than I'd like to admit, but there was only one point where I had to turn externally for help, and that was either a bug or a mistake on my part because I thought I'd tried the solution, but when I tried it a second time, it worked perfectly.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: An improvement on Epistory in every way. This game places an emphasis on typing bursts of short, repeated words quickly, which lets you get a good feel for the keyboard and makes you more familiar with the keyboard. This is a much better approach than something like Textomancer where you have to type out long sentences and are penalized for mistakes. While I don't know that this game taught me good typing habits neccesarily it definitely improved my typing speed and I find myself being able to touch type more and more after playing it. Its shorter (5-6 hours) but definitely worth the full price. I felt very engaged while playing it and pushed myself to type as fast as possible and kind of speedrun through it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start by saying this game is really cute! The creatures and sounds in it are all very pleasing, as well as the art style. The developer did a great job of creating a relatable yet fantastical world setting. The gameplay style is unique and can be challenging at times. A couple of things that could use improvement: movement and vocabulary. I know that the developer was keeping in theme with the words used throughout the game, but by the end of the game I was thinking "Well, now I know all of the synonyms for evil." My only real issue with this game was the story line- up until the last third the game was fairly well fleshed out, but then the game kind of splutters and then SUDDENLY THE GAME IS OVER. There is no real "boss fight", just some waves of baddies, then a cutscene, and roll credits. No real resolution, just a big "HEY ITS OVER NOW THANKS FOR PLAYING" and that was reaaaaaaaaal disappointing. I wouldn't say to not purchase or play this game- but be warned that you will be sorely disappointed at the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I played in the Early Access, the game was great.I played after the release, and I'm not disappointed.The world really feels real, I loved to read all the little stories about each plant, or about the different people. I'm however a bit sad that there is nothing more to do with all this knowledge. I don't know what, but having something to do with them (apart from leveling up) would have been really great.BuuuutThe game is coherent, in any points:- All the visuals go well with each other- The different zones have their own feeling- The level design is great, and sometimes got me into thinking longer than I thoughtThe voice acting is great even though it feels sometimes a bit off, not conveying the right emotions, but that only occurred a handful of times.However, the game felt too easy, even with the adaptive difficulty setting. _childDocuments_.review: Nanotale is a unique typing/puzzle/exploration game hybrid in which all of the elements work very well in tandem. Who'd have thunk? Well, the developers, for one, since this is a loose sequel to Epistory, which laid out some of the ground rules and is a great game in its own right. Very loose sequel, I should say - there are some shared elements, but the story is completely separate. You play as Rosalind, an apprentice archivist who during the prologue gets lost in a forest, finds a magic talking giant spirit fox whom she conscripts as a mount, and then sets off on a series of adventures to investigate and fight against a mysterious corrupting force that threatens the land. The story is standard fantasy fare, decently told. I really liked the how Rosalind's occupation ties into the game; you gain experience by cataloguing flora, fauna and cultural artifacts, which she writes down on her beautifully illustrated journal. The game is divided into three biomes, each with a large open map of interconnected nodes which hold things to catalogue, enemies to fight, and puzzles to solve. Combat is simple - different types of enemies spawn and make their way to you at different speeds, and each one of them is assigned a different word. You move around with the cursor keys to position yourself away from them, and enter typing mode by pressing space - every time you complete an enemy's word, it suffers damage. You also get some verbs to cast spells (Like Ice or Fire) and modifiers to change their area of effect (like Large or Ray) which adds some variety to the proceeds - this costs mana, though, which takes some time to replenish. There are some bosses too, some of which are a little frustrating (multi-stage bosses... ugh,) but nothing too bad. The environmental puzzles were my favorite part of the game. The different elements you can command (you can cast them on the landscape by targetting nodes by, you got it, typing out their keywords) react differently to different types of terrain. Early on, for example, you can use shrubbery to sneak upon opponents - this shrubbery can be burned down, or grown with water. You can create bridges with Ice, energize machines with lighting... when you factor in that you can change the shape of your spells, it gives you a pretty sturdy toolkit with which to face the game's puzzles. I felt the systems weren't quite put through their paces as they could have, and I can't wait to see how everything is refined and developed for the next game if and when that comes. There's a simple RPG progression system that rewards you some abilities when you level, too, and a (very simple) keyword dialog system (like in Ultima or ye olden RPGs!). Lovely stuff. The music is good and the levels look great - the 2D art, in particular, is really something. I feel like I need to mention the fox's tail, which looks beautiful while he runs. Lots of love, craft, and attention to detail shine through almost everything. The bad? Well, this is a game made by a very small indie team, so expect some jank. There's been some problems which have been duly patched away since release. I've had to quit to the menu and restart a small section due to getting stuck and some other random minor issues. I also had some (again, minor) issues with the pacing of the story, and the abruptness with which the end credits come up actually made me laugh. But all in all this is an extremely fun, well made and original game. If typing games appeal at all to you, it's well worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: You know when you're waiting for a bus to take you home for /hours/ before someone shows up to tell you that the bus doesn't run on weekends so you might as well call someone to drive you home? Yeah the desert level is like that. (You wouldn't think that it would be possible to softlock yourself in the first area of the level, until you softlock yourself into the first area of the level.) The art of this game is gorgeous and I adore it, but that doesn't take away from the fact that the game just doesn't become fun to play the more you get into it. The forest and the cave environment might be really pretty, but being really pretty doesn't take away from the frustration of being lost in an area or not knowing where to go because the game lacks two crucial UI/UX elements on its HUD that make adventure games less of a hassle - a minimap and a quest log. (There's not even a 'hint' - 'why don't you try checking this area out?' system in the main game.) The only UI elements in your HUD are your HP and mana bars, and your spell list when you're in typing mode.Seeing where you are requires you to open up the main map which is zoomed in to just where you are. There are quest markers with quest objectives - but the only way to 'toggle' between active quests is to navigate between each individual quest marker on the map. (There also seems to be a glitch of some sort where you can complete quests that you haven't even gotten or get a notification you completed an objective when you re-enter/re-explore an designated area for a quest you've already completed.)If you were hoping that you could find your way out of a location using the main map alone - tough luck because the main map doesn't clearly mark spaces that are blocked off due to cliffs, rivers, topography (why I can't cross this shallow ditch I couldn't tell you either), or a literal wall that the game won't allow you to pass through because you haven't gotten a quest objective. Also since quest objectives are marked with literal quest icons or blue 'area of interest' circles on the main map, determining where to go next if you're lost can be ... tricky and not very intuitive. It's very likely that you will need to backtrack quite often to get to where the game expects you to be.As for finding lore objectives - the unlockable lore markers on the map seem to remain lit up as long as you haven't "completed" the entry for that particular thing. This makes finding actual missed (or unfound) lore objectives very annoying.Tldr: The game is pretty but it's lacking crucial elements, and suffers from some pretty bad design, which end up making the game more frustrating than fun. Hopefully in the future, these concerns get addressed so it's not as frustrating to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Very pleasant gameplay, even though it is early access, only once I had to load last checkpoint due to the bug (less than in Cyberpunk :)).Graphic are nice, the spells mechanics are more complex than in any other typing game, so we also have to think and solve some environmental riddles on the go (big + for this, thanks to this it is not boring).Looking forward to the next chapters becoming available.
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved Epistory, so I immediately got Nanotale when it became available and I definitely don't regret it. The art style is really beautiful and especially the environments look great, the story is very interesting as well. The gameplay is a lot of fun with all the different spells you can unlock and the puzzles pose good challenges. _childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the early access content. Wow! What a ride.Pros:- I really like typing, so this game was pretty great (loved Epistory too!)- Puzzles were fun and intuitive; I was never frustratingly stumped- Exploring the world was pretty great, kept me wanting more- Has some influence of the Divinity series with how different materials and elements interact- Overall aesthetics were pretty great!Cons:- Few bugs  - One of the characters appears out of thin air, without any sort of effect which is kinda jarring  - I somehow moved into a pool of water, clipped through the floor and eventually died after floating a while- You'll wind up typing a lot of the same things over and over to prep abilities- Some combat zones seemed a bit buggy with random win conditions appearing mid-way through the battle- Some of the NPC animations seemed a bit buggy or choppy on my machine Improvements I'd suggest (take or leave as you need):- Alias/Macro menu similar to how you can alias commands in, say, VIM or Emacs- Quest menu would be golden- Percentage of area completion for Lore- Support for ultra-wide monitors would be a big plus- Specify clear win conditions upon entering a combat zone whether it be wave clear, enemy takedowns, or survival- Area-specific fast-travel (e.g. from forest into caves)- Damage stats during combat (e.g. remaining hp as a number placed into the hp bar kinda thing)Overall, I can't wait to see what the rest of the game will be and the continued polish that the developers are adding.  I'm not normally an Early Access kind of purchaser, but Epistory is pure gold, so I'm holding out hope that the developers keep up the truly excellent work and see Nanotale through to the finish line!
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game!  I had played the first in the Typing Chronicles, Epistory, and I was ecstatic when another game was being made that was similar.  I will say that even though this game is in Early Access, it has been an absolute wonderful game so far.  The storyline is amazing and it has diverse characters.  I really like the monsters you see so far, especially the big burly monsters I want to say remind me of Clydesdales.  They are very interesting, and I love how there are so many different ways you can apply the powers.  There is a ton of different quests you can take and information you can gather, and frankly I love all of it.  It also gives me a chance to sharpen up on my typing and get back into the hang of typing more while making it super fun.  I am super excited for when the full game finally releases, but thank you so much devs for putting out what you have already!!

_childDocuments_.review: lovely game that is very simple to play and intuitive, simple premise and beautiful design, and has a good story with a good message. But just because it is simplistic doesn't mean that it's not challenging, it took me about 5 attempts to finally heal the serpent.there is lots of interesting lore and the green jaspers and garnies are very cute. and i like the fact that the main objective is documentation not fighting. the movement controls are slightly jarring and could be smoother, and it could do with slightly more instructions for using the magics, for example explaining that any word is an anchor for the spell rather than just the crystals i.e. plants and enemies. an in-game mini-map might prove useful as i struggled at times to know where i was supposed to be going, but that might jut be me. all in all a very good game and i will be eagerly awaiting updates
_childDocuments_.name: Nanotale - Typing Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to the previous one, encounters are more boring... you don't get the same sense of accomplishment. Being able to move, as is, makes fights devoid of tension. Getting the words right feels like doing homework, walking around the map collecting trivia feels like a chore, the enemies are either super easy or unfair, sometimes you have 5 minutes to write a word, but if you pass 3 meters from the enemy they hit you anyway.The mechanics feel clunky, I don't like having to position the character just right behind an object to do what I want, this is not what should be the focus of the game...While the other game had fast, reflexive, precise decision-making to be done in few seconds, this one is about sluggishly dragging yourself around the area. Getting complex words feels like an hindrance to your gameplay, rather than being what's fun about it.I still think this kind of gameplay is very fun and something different compared to the average game, I wish more developers changed the way in which you input your commands.I think being able to move could have potential, but as is, it was more fun being still.It's not a great sequel, but as a stand-alone I think other users will enjoy it, and people who finished the previous game looking for more will make this do.Maybe the mechanics of the game will get more complex and will start to make sense in the next chapters. I did not enjoy the boss fights.The story is also bland and predictable, and nobody cares about these 20-page descriptions of a tree, I doubt anyone reads them...(a "no errors allowed" mode could be useful, since when you stop playing this game and go back to reality, you get this bad habit of making tons of mistakes that make typing faster useless, and it might make the game more challenging for the people who finished the other one)

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because there are few PC typing games and I want to support this type of game. Currently, I own Steelseries Apex M500, lubed with Krytox 205g0 so I like typing on my keyboard very much.That said, I have to complain several things:1. First bug, the first survival battle after you find a spirit fox, the enemies don't spawn. The game said you needed to survive for 90 seconds. I killed all the enemies in 30 seconds, so there were still 60 seconds left, but there were no enemies again to fight me, so I waited for a solid one minute and did nothing. This was surprisingly underwhelming and bad.2. The main quest is not updated after the first main quest, so it means the main quest would still show "Follow the blue ball" even after I followed it and there was no more blue ball to follow, so I had to explore the map myself, which is an unnecessary hindrance.3. The linear map, damn it! I think one would prefer one while other prefers another, but it almost made me suffocated. I expected a more spacious map.4. Related to number (2), so because there was no more blue balls, there was nothing to guide me to the next objective, which is daunting for me. I felt lost, honestly. And to exacerbate it, there was no hint or help. Furthermore, sometimes the way to open a path was obscure; the first way to open a path was to start a fire, but there was no plant near the blockade to burn it.5. The upgrade system is worse than the last. The only way to upgrade your character is to explore the lore in forms of plants, which is shown on the map if you buy the "Lore on Map" upgrade, but then the game doesn't tell you how many plants which names you have to type, and you don't know how many upgrades are on the game, so you don't know how many you should expect for this game. It could feel like I was blind.6. The words only varies little. I saw several words surfacing again ephemerally after I finished typing it, so in large scale this could bore me too quickly.7. No way of backtracking after first time riding the spirit fox, which is unfortunate.8. Wish there were any spoken dialogues, though. They should hire several voice actors, it would be great.I really wanted this game to be great, because I had this amazing keyboard and I love so much typing on it and this game helps me greatly to do it. But in this current state, I think I had to refund this game.Insyaa Allaah, if there was any discount, I would buy this game, and only hope that this game would improve.

_childDocuments_.review: Before hopping straight into Nanotale, I suggest to try 'Epistory - Typing Chronicles' first. The games do not share the same nor related story to each other, but they share the same people behind it. Very likely the experience from Epistory can give a player better understanding, and clear and concise reason to support the development of Nanotale during EA.As of today, Nanotale is very far from finished and I guess it will need at least another year to do so. I do not recommend the game during EA for fellow gamers, who are looking for polished product because currently the provided quality does not match the price. However I strongly recommend it for fellow gamers, who would like to be support and be part of community the devs have created.PROS:+ beautiful graphics, which is being improved with every patch+ amazing environment sounds and battle soundtracks+ support for multiple languages+ unique battle mechanics+ the support of devs in case of occured issuesCONS:- a lot of bugs (in current version)- performance (optimization) issues- only 4 hours of gameplay- missing or incomplete features

_childDocuments_.review: If you know Epistory and love it, Nanotale is the same fox spirit, Learn powers, type word and free new zone. At the same point it is not just a new skin on the same engine. The powers works differently and the graphics are not the same kind.It's still in Early Access, but the updates are frequent, and the playability improves each times. At the time I am writing this review, there is two biomes and largely 5 or 6 hours of play without rushing. Everything is done by typing. Using powers, herding sheep, killing big bad bluish wolfies,, every action you have to do in a classic rpg will be done by combining the layout and some powers you activated by typing. If you think you are blocked, look around, try to move and have another perspective. This island seems unreacheable? Could pushing/pulling this large leaf open a passage? I hugely recommand this game, especially if you liked Epistory (and if you don't know Epistory, check it out ^^)

name: Here Be Dragons
detailed_description: Here Be Dragons is a satirical turn-based strategy game featuring unique 'living map' graphics, where you lead a group of crazed captains and eradicate legendary monsters in order to allow Christopher Columbus the discovery of the New World. STORY Christopher Columbus discovered the Americas in 1492. In 10 weeks. With 100 men. With 3 ships. This is a LIE ! Firstly, someone had to defeat kraken and tritons. Someone had to vanquish the Leviathan. Someone had to banish all the ghost ships. The information about these deeds is missing from the archives, and you can’t find it in any great statesmen’s memoir. The knowledge of the “Avant Armada” was completely erased by some bloody officials. The people who took part in the expeditions were not sane people. Maniacs, psychos and common crackpots were forced by royal orders to eradicate Evil in the uncharted seas. “Here Be Dragons” describes these events. GAMEPLAY Use original Dice Activation System to attack enemies, heal your crew, and upgrade the fleet. Collect Ink and use Errata to turn the tide of the encounter. Cross the seas with an ancient, living map , full of terrible creatures that want to devour you! Confront the most fierce beasts that ever lived: leviathans and krakens, predatory whales and lustful mermaids. Decimate tritons, awake Dagon, and then erase them from human memory. SATIRE Meet an extraordinary company of weirdos, madmen and oddballs . Their vices and virtues fuel the journey. Experience clashes with bureaucratic machine. Don’t lose your mind when confronted by absurdities spewed by authorities and royal advisors. Sniff at pirates. Ignore the settlers. You are above them. You are a monster hunter traversing through the aqua incognita. Who cares if you are insane?

_childDocuments_.review: First let me say that the game's concept is good.  The idea of assigning dice to actions and to improve attributes is a good one, and initially the game is a lot of fun.  That fun quickly turns to frustration for a few reasons:1) There is no progression.  Ships can improve within a chapter but then reset at the end of the chapter meaning none of the improvements carry over to the next one.2) Each chapter introduces a new enemy with one or more annoying attacks (poison, bleeding, seduction), as well as an environmental effect that works against the player.  Coupled with the lack of progression above leads to battles quickly becoming frustrating rather than fun.  It really feels like all of the game's systems are working against the player and it often feels unfair and I restarted battles many times until the RNG worked in my favour.There isn't much of a story, and what little there is is nonsensical at best.  The various characters spout gibberish most of the time and there is no coherent narrative.  It wouldn't have taken much to weave things together to make a somewhat cohesive plot.  Sadly, that wasn't done.The games art style gets a thumbs up.  It's pretty and fits the theme.  Unfortunately, the sounds leave a lot to be desired, in particular the cherub which sounds like tires squealing.Finally, the game is short.  I finished it around the 6 hour mark and have no desire to go back and revisit it.Ultimately, if the concept is appealing it might be worth picking up in a deep sale but be ready for a frustrating experience.  I think the best way to sum this up is the comment I made to wife when she asked how it was going.  I said, "It's a lot of fun when it's not frustrating the heck out of me."

_childDocuments_.review: Phew! After binge-playing for over 6h ours...✔️Graphics ✔️Music ✔️Audio ✔️Humor ✔️Innovative and unique combat ✔️VERY tactical gameplay ✔️AAA level of polishing and care for details ✔️This Early Access game is higher quality and more 'complete' than most of 'fully released' games I know ✔️Quite elastic in terms of engagement, you can play for 5 minutes or 3h non-stop - you will always get a valid portion of entertainment ✔️Huge variation of enemies, bonuses, skills, ships and unique external factors/events, no two battles are the same ✔️Boardgame/Tabletop vibe all over the place ✔️'Cozy' overall atmosphere (this music and paper-like art style REALLY stimulates imagination and roleplaying)One of the most enjoyable tactical-strategy games I've played in past year. Took me totally by surprise. And seeing as this is the FIRST game of this developer - I am simply in state of awe. Makes me remember Steam from before Greenlight... Can't believe its labeled as 'Early Access'(maybe by mistake?).And the game is actually damn hard at times! But in a challenging and rewarding way. So be ready to see your ships sink and w/o b1tch1ng - just go back there and fight! >:DMoney well spent. 😊UPDATE 13.01.2020I edited the review as the developer has fixed everything I was complaining about :)Kudos!

_childDocuments_.review: We all know that Christopher Columbus is credited for discovering the Americas on October 12th, 1942. Once Columbus managed to receive funding, after years of trying, he left with 3 boats and 100 men. The trip took way longer than Columbus estimated as the trip turned out to last for 10 weeks before land was spotted. However, what if I told you there was more that was redacted from our history books?Here Be Dragons brings in a satirical alternate history story that takes place before Christopher Columbus began his voyage. Yeah, the sea was calm when he set sail, but it wasn’t always like that. In fact, there were monsters lurking just beneath the water. How did they get eradicated though? Surely the accounts would have been archived! Well yes but no. Due to the expeditions, known as the Avant Armada, was erased and the only reason you know of it now is an innkeeper that was kind enough to retell the tale.As of writing, there are currently eight campaigns with 25 scenarios (or battles). Each one puts you in the shoes of the Captain and switches once their voyage is finished. Between each campaign, you’ll check back in with the Innkeeper so you know what was happening during that time.Here Be Dragons’ battles are an interesting beast. At first the combat is simple enough, but once you progress further into the tutorial, more is added on top. Every turn will have a cherub spit out some dice for you and your enemy to assign. You can only assign one dice to each ship and it can be assigned to an action or used to buff that ship’s defense or attack.To help you out a bit, you also have Errata. At the start of each turn and after each enemy death, ink bottles will appear in the water for you to pick up. You can use these ink bottles to activate Errata once you have enough. At first you only have the Reroll Errata, but you’ll get more options later on. In addition, if a 1 is assigned that ship (or enemy) will heal while an assigned 6 will increase attack for that turn.You’ll then go into Salvos, or the attack phase. Damage is based on your attack minus your enemy’s defense. Thankfully, you can have each ship attack the same target so you can do more damage (or actually do damage if attack and shield were equal). This also goes for the enemy as they always team up against the weakest ship.Lastly, you have the Action phase. If an action has the needed dice they will go off here. Actions can be a heal, let you have an extra Salvos, or do damage to your enemy (which also ignores defense!).While you will have first picks at dice at the start of each battle, that won’t last. Here Be Dragons implements an initiative system to determine who goes first each phase. Initiative is determined by the sum of your assigned dice values. Whoever has the lowest will go first, unless it’s a tie then it simply switches over. Having initiative can be extremely important as not only will you not have first picks at dice, but you can’t heal a ship before the killing blow if your enemy has an action queued up. To keep track of who will get initiative, it’s visualized with a scale. This makes you decide if the risk of losing initiative is worth it or should you not assign any and take the damage. It also goes the other way as you can leave dice that your enemy can’t assign so they take damage, but they’d get initiative.After winning each battle, your ships will be repaired and you’ll be able to choose an upgrade per ship in most campaigns.The look of Here Be Dragons is based on maps that are seemingly resting on tables while text boxes look like they were transcribed on scrolls. The town map shows where all the major players are and where they’re going with the campaign map mapping out the Captain’s route so you know how long it will be. When going into locations, a second scroll is pulled out showing what the building looks like inside in all its glory. Though, the Captains (or any other character that moves around) won’t be depicted. Even the loading screen when loading into a scenario follows the style. However, the best part is during battles. It keeps up with the map style, but brings everything to life as you see your ships and the monsters bobbing up and down, clouds and birds traveling around the map, and each action is animated. The only companion you have out at sea are the sounds of the waves and seagulls.While Here Be Dragons brings in a unique art style and an interesting combat system that will have you hooked, I wouldn’t necessarily say this is for everyone. You not only have to like turn-based games, but also not mind the dice system. I’m someone that’s more lenient on games that utilize dice (considering that most of them are board games), but I can’t say that I didn’t get a little annoyed sometimes. Nonetheless, Here Be Dragons is a wonderful title that doesn’t really feel like an early access game apart from missing the rest of the story. If you decide to pick this one up, get ready for some difficult battles.
