_childDocuments_.review: Really love this game. As a fan of Tower of time I wanted to try the next game from the Event Horizon team. Bought it in a bundle for 10 euros and  immediately played it until 4 am.  Not sure if I would buy it for full price, but at this discount it is no-brainer. World building in this game is just awesome, I love the whole magic/technology vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: So far I really like the game. Pros: It is in the same theme as Tower of Time, it is great to see that Event Horizon are creating their own style. The same style combat, challenges,  same type of gear. Characters are very nice so far, I'm only in Act II at the moment but I do like playing with all of them.  The world looks well themed and I think it was going for more of a steam-punk look to the world. I like it.  Fights are generally engaging but the difficulty is off, you have areas that you clean out fast even on hard but then fights that are hard even on easy.  This is more of a nitpick to be honest.  Cons:   Has some bugs, nothing major: some tooltips missing on monsters, stealth mechanics just means it takes some time in agro zone before the enemy engages - this sometimes means they are standing next to you and you are about to hit them but you are still stealth somehow seems strange and probably needs to get fixed by having the stealth timer go faster the closer you are to the enemy.   Story is good but not as interesting as Tower of Time, I love that game.   Levels are replaced with dungeons so no more inter-area puzzles, they also have little in form of puzzles.   Voice acting is not that bad but it needs some work, eg. some time after Act1 I expect the main characters to not be very cheerful but they act normal, is fine but it needs some work.    No dwarf companion?!? At least so far.    Overall:     The game is great, immersive and fun but I think Tower of Time is better.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. Ran the first play through in ~50 hours. The class flexibility, especially for companions was really appreciated. The voice acting is great, and the story pulls you in.The synergy between skills and status effects was really well done, inviting you to be more tactical with your combat skills, but that doesn't take away from the builds that just want to ham fist their way through with as much burst DPS as possible.I started with an Adept, and an Engineer, and didn't regret anything about it. Massed summons with the Constructor specialty and the adept went full elemental caster and topped the DPS chart every combat encounter.  *however, the mage required a lot of micromanaging for skills and keeping them away from enemies, so your other classes should be more self sufficient if you go this route.The addition of Challenges was really awesome, it was a great way to test out new builds in a safe environment.-One of the only negative things I can say is that the ending felt a little rushed, with too much happening too fast until you hit the end. -The only other thing i didn't like is that once you have the skills you want for your build, the other skill points you gain are basically useless.**So let's pretend your build is 'complete' by level ~5 lets say.   Then leveling up the rest of the game is only for stat points, because you already have the skills you want/need.And you can only hold 4 passive skills. so you can buy all the other skills, or never learn them, and it doesn't matter. **See Edit belowStarting another run to see the other outcomes to the story ^_^***Edit: 6/26/24There was an update recently that unlocked the skill trees outside of your original Archetype after a certain point. So, Warriors could chose Engineer skills and so on. This is a neat fix that allows for a good deal of customization. I really like this change :)
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: pro:-100% voice acting of all characters-u play as a sibling pair (male/female)-4 base classes (each has 3 evolutioni at lvl 7 and u can get a few skills of the other 2 paths at lvl 14)-at any point u can completely reskills any skill or attribute points (only thing u cant reskill are class choiced/evolutions)-battles are fought in real time with pause (like dao) but u can also freely (one button) switch to slowed time and the amount of slow can even be adjusted in the option ranging from 0.01 to 2.0(yeah speed up xd)what should be added/changed:-hovering over a skill/spell that adds a specific debuff should open another window that explains what exactely the debuff does-mission reward ep lowered and enemy kill ep increased to make killing enemies and especially doing side missions feel more rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: The game is similar to the studio's previous title, but the graphics are certainly at a higher level now.For me it's an expended tower defense game, but with the variety of situations, tactical strategy and the ability to customize your skill set. I like combat system it's a real-time action with the space and I don't have to wait for each move as in turn-based games.Small flaws in this game definitely don't take away from the fun and it's definitely worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Tower of Time and was more than willing to give this one a shot, based on the fact that it came from the same developer. The game itself is pretty good. I enjoy the atmosphere and the story (don't want to spoil anything but I was surprised).For the hardcore gamers, insane difficulty is not that insane. Once you figure out the broken skills, anything other than insane will be a bit boring as you mow down everything in your path. Still feels satisfying at least. The combat is cool. I tried to make things a bit harder for myself by not allowing full on pausing. You can control the % of slow-down in the settings. The only downside is the horrible fps in certain areas of the game. With maxed out settings and pc load at around 50%, I struggled to maintain a stable 40 fps in certain locations, never reaching 60. Perhaps this can be addressed in the future.7.5/10I will come back later on to collect all the achievements. For what it's priced, was worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: So far very good.  Nice amount of Difficulty and Nice Pacing.  The combat is really fun.  infinitely better since Patch 4, they seem to be going in a good direction.  I love the characters, character interaction and the RPG Mechanics.  So far the story is interesting and teased the things to come well.  Highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to play this because Tower of Time is a very good game but this.... this is very janky. You will be strugling to control your party because everything is so snap on. Someone attacks you in melee? well, focus on them, move a little bit? need to reselecting the target. Want to move and use a skill? Well good luck because there are barricades, aoe damage from enemies and many ranged enemiesI am refunding this. There are also times where the commands don't respond to your inputs like giving a character the order to use a skill and it doesnt work or pathing issues when trying to move someone out of the way.When reloading it actually switches back to the difficulty you had when you savedGraphic and art style seems to be made by different studios and don't take into account how cluttered the combat can become.There are also problems in seeing the cast range so sometimes a character will simply walk through attacks to cast a spellThe difficulty is all over the place, the first area is very hard to win even on Hard because how fast the enemies lock on your party and start following your weakest member.And the funny part is that you are supposed to control 4 characters that have different skills and cooldowns in a screen wide arena where you have to beat a reinforcements meter. The hp bars are very misleding as well and with 4 part members and the 5-6 enemies everything becomes a colorful mess.The dialogue is also more silly modern dialogue with silly jokes made for very simple people wich ruins the immersion.The AI of companions is the worst since it makes controlling them a gambleThe rest of the game is great...Buy this game in one year, i am done playing janky games at release. And when i say janky i mean unplayable and not fun, not charming jankyAlso, how did all the reviewers who got a key 1 month early did not notice these problems? I am refuding this, i just have no patience for jankyness.This is not fun janky, this is barely playable jankyness and not fun
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Envly is a tactical party based PG.The story is okey. Can't say it was anything exceptional, but it wasn't bad either. It was good enough to move the game forward. I count that as a positive.Crafting was done pretty well. The loot is random so there is a good chance if you want something specific you will need to craft it. That being said I pretty much ignored it 2/3 of the game, but it was for a more practical reason. I didn't feel i was to weak to waste my resources on gear that wasn't High tear (Tier 3) gear, because the resources for crafting are limited. At the later stages of the game when i was making my endgame gear i was looking forward to getting more upgrade materials to finish my endgame sets of armor.The combat is real time with pause, but it has a nice gimic where instead of normal time you can make it play slower so you have more time to react and move characters in combat without having to pause all the time. You can change how much you want time slowed. By default it is set to 12%, because i played the whole co-op with one other person and each had to only control 2 character we played it at 30% speed in combat. Overal i think it is a pretty good system.As for the co-op, it is currently buggy as hell, but we still managed to beat the whole hame on hard. The bugs are mostly on the side of the one joining. Some of the bugs encountered were he can't see my combat animations and sometimes anemy attacks and aoe. When reviving or using any interact action his characters would just cancel the action and autoattack if there is enely in range, so he can't revive my characters 90% of the time. Bosses just don't spawn for him, for third of the fight he just can't see them or attack them untill they teleport for a phase change or use a specific skill or something.Overall i recomend the game, but if you are planning on playing it co-op wait for the bugs to be patched.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game. I wanted to enjoy it as much as I did Tower of Time. I recommend Tower of Time to people all the time. I've uninstalled this game after 90 mins spent in the tutorial dealing with random keybinding/unbinding issues. I've reported the issue and posted a thread on their forums, but I can't play the game like this, and for such a simple technical issue to even be a thing in this era of gaming is beyond shocking. I have no faith in the quality of the rest of the game. If only I'd started playing it soon after I bought it...then I could get a refund, because I would ask for one.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: A flawed but fun RTWP RPG. Story is middling, and there are definitely some bugs still lingering (a few requiring reloading a save so save frequently, and an annoying one where the game freezes when you exit game and you have to kill it in task manager), IMO the thing that pulls it out though is the combat. The satisfaction of playing a well balanced party with multiple summoner classes (looking at you constructor) and setting up all your summons/buffs in slow time then returning to normal speed to watch the entire screen melt is hard to beat. Dual wield sword/dagger berserker is also a great boss melter.Overall 7/10 game.(Note that I have not tried co-op so cannot provide an opinion on those issues)
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: I truly am enjoying my experience with Dark Envoy. The learning curve is low, and being able to teak and re-develop your characters on the fly (with no cost) is refreshing. I resisted this idea at first, as I consider it mandatory for rpgs, but now I've come to enjoy it and spend time each session mixing and mashing.My only "real" negative comment is the story. It's fun, predictable and interesting enough to keep you entertained. However, I "live" for the minor details, and for the commentary in side quest and books to help enhance my experience. DE doesn't offer this yet, they do offer notes in each level; however the counter arguments or enlightening comments in this notes are not sufficient for me in the world building process. Overall. I enjoy this game. I have no regrets. thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little strategic rpg as a follow up after Tower of Time. The micromanagement (babysitting) in combat can get messy, and fighting with only one character can be easier than with a group. But the quest writing is terrible, every quest has a twist, the simplest twist you can think of, just to "subvert your expectations", it gets boring real fast.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: I will recommend this - ON SPECIAL. At full price there is a lot better out there, which offers more RPG, and doesn't feel like a really dumb'd down console version of a game.-----------------------------------------------While the game has some good elements to it, overall, I am not overly impressed with some of the "design" decisions they made. And the Developer continue to use the excuse of "When we had testers/play-testers looking at it, it was decided to...."Example - you can only have 5 Max active skills at any time - so if you want to spread out your skills.... forget it. Also Passives have the same issues. These are game decisions which are really stupid for a RPG!!I have no major issue with the Real Time Tactics with this game, because you can pause, give controls, and even play at slowed down. Not turned based, but good enough to allow you to control the battlefield where you want.The RPG in it however is very light however from what I have experienced so far. You do get some "decisions" but they are just one of two options. Overall, I would rate this as a mediocre role-playing game - it has some fun elements, and the story isn't too bad (though at 8 hours I feel bored already....). The "design decisions" that have been made make it very frustrating and you probably would be better to "re-spec" a lot after you have decided on a skill you want - and max that out.

_childDocuments_.review: Three hours in on Hard difficulty, and the game is enjoyably challenging. Environmental effects, synergies between skills all good stuff. A little bit of jank when using the inventory and swapping items, but nothing particularly annoying. Nice graphics and effects, good music. Combat is a little floaty, sometimes your characters or enemies will seem to skid across the ground for example. However I've been enjoying the game so far and will update the review with more detail as I play more. So far my first impressions are positive and I felt the game deserved a thumbs up even without having a full playthrough as yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid party based real time with pause RPG, if you have played the devs previous game, Tower of Time you'll feel right at home.  The game is primarily focused around combat, loot gathering/crafting and adjusting your builds.  There is a story and it is pretty interesting but is not the primary focus of the game.  You do have some choices you can make and they will have minor effects on the game (choosing to help rescue someone can have them help you later on for example) but the main narrative is mainly set in stone.  The combat is fun, you can have your party members act atonomously (they'll automatically use their abilities and engage the enemy) or you can control them all, on normal difficulty it's fine to leave some of your team mates to fend for themselves, but on the higher difficulties you'll want to micro everything.  There is fun loot to collect and a solid crafting system.  There are some minor pathfinding issues, people will navigate around obstacles but will get stuck on NPCs or other party members sometimes.  It took my 30 hours to beat one playthrough and I skipped quite a bit of side content in case I do another run in the future.  All in all its a solid game and frequently on sale so if you enjoy this style of play I recommend picking it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has loved DIvinity OS (1 & 2) this is a really fun game to me. It has some glitches, and some of the cutscenes and voice acting is a little cheesy but it's nothing that takes away from the game as a whole. They've thrown together alot of elements (like steampunk with elves and robots and... etc) which sometimes makes the plot a little difficult to follow. Overall it feels a little like a genuine 'passion project', as in you can tell the creators have so many ideas that they want to put into the same game, but I think that is what makes it so endearing and enjoyable to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: It is not one of those atmospheric games that provides unigue experience. It is very random title, that provides truly engaging gameplay. Fight mechanic, skills and character cutomization is really well done. So despite all its flaws I had a lot of fun playing it. Fights are dynamic, fluent, diversed and really satisfying. Quite good game, worth checking if you are into that type of things.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this by saying that generally I really dislike RTwP. I always felt that it was inferior to both TBS and Action games. However Dark Envoy I think utilizes RTwP very well. The combat has enough depth that you NEED to pause on higher difficulties and for players who aren't exactly speedy you also get a slow-motion mode, which is very nice for more challenging fights, where you never feel like you can play at full speed.Overall I am charmed, pleasantly surprised and generally hopeful about this game studio. Always a pleasure to support indie devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot of rough edges currently (shortly after launch), but the devs are putting out patches pretty quickly and I'm confident they'll fix the bugs.  The core game is great, and the real-time-with-pause combat is quite challenging and makes many fights feel like a puzzle (playing on hardest difficulty).  And RTwP co-op games are very few and far between.  I'm giving it a thumbs up assuming that a lot of the jank will continue to be patched out :)
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

The Host is the only one that can play the full game, the one that creates both characters, use crafting, use research, make dialog options etc. etc. etc.. If you play as the client... you have payed full price for a 1/6th of a game... wait until they have a "friend pass" because this game is not even close to be worth the money for the client side...Another couple of MAJOR issues...Bugs, bugs, bugs and more bugs. _childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately a good game got bad. When I first played the game, it worked well and was an enjoyable experience. Every few months I come back to it to find it more broken than before. Somehow it's release in November 2023 was better than now.It's basically unplayable in it's current state, with massive lag spikes, inability to revive fallen allies, poor balance, crashes, and UI issues that prevent coop companions from being able to even see enemies or see damage they deal when they do see enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: I can most definitely see why someone would like the game with all it has to offer.Unfortunately, it is not for me.I got really frustrated with the combat, the unfairness of it such as an enemy can hit you as long as it started the animation, you can be far away from him, even after a dodge (ranger) and you'll still get damaged. Same goes for ranged attacks since they follow you. I get it " MAGIC ", but I reckon a scorpion won't have a seeking head acid launcher in his stinger, so agree to disagree.I'm sure it just goes beyond me and this play style is not suited to me, that's fine.Although, the game feels pretty janky at times, unpolished on certain things I'm sure, but I can't tell from so little time. You can see straight away that it's a very linear, story driven game, sadly I like my RPGs open, just like the peeps going at that bar that only opens at night and you're never quite sure what's inside but the lights are pink, looks fun.Apart from that, the setting, atmosphere, story, graphics all seems really good and enjoyable, as such I will still recommend the game, because it's most definitely not for me but someone out there will have loads more fun than I.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: The combat, story and gameplay are simple. No hardcore mechanics, no need for hundreds of hours to complete or for mindless grind. it's a simple CRPG which hit the spot if you want a casual simple game for fun but not for hardcore players. It was easy even at insane difficulty.The combat was becoming a bit repetitive with few strategy even at insane difficulty but since the game was quickly finished it did not bothered me that much. It also had very few bug which is nice. For a 30$ game compare to common price tag of today RPG's it was decent., just don't expect the next GOTY.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: A fun action RPG with good combat, probably the main draw as the story itself is quite linear. Playing feels like trying to control 4 heroes in LoL or dota at the same time with a slow time/pause option. I've just passed act 1 and got the 4th character slot unlocked. It really upped the difficulty and required playing it more like Pillars of Eternity where you need to pause or slow time much more frequently to manage the combat. I'm playing on the hardest diff(Insane) as after the first hour or so and getting a bit of gear everything below that felt a bit too easy. Now I actually have to try hard and still fail quite a bit on first attempts for some fights, so I think it's a good and balanced challenge. The character stat pages could use some work as there's no tooltips on mouseover, you have to go to the codex to lookup what things are. THe camera controls also took a bit of getting used to, coming from BG3 and using AWSD to here playing more like a traditional RTS with screen-edge panning with the mouse and using alt to rotate the camera, but it's not really necessary during most fights so it's not a huge issue.The things I think are done well aside from the combat are the free respecs and how plentiful crafting materials are. I've focused on crafting with a bit in the enchantments and combat trees fro my research tech and it's paid off. I've been able to craft gear to keep up with slots on my characters that are falling behind and the ability to re-roll the mod rolls is really nice as well, not to mention the base stat boost crafting can have over found gear! Overall, I think this a good game with a few flaws holding it back from being great and would consider it well worth the price and support for a small indie company.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game trying to give it an open mind in hopes that I'd like it.  The real time battle turned me off, but I have played RPGs that do it well.  This game, well doesn't.  Combined with the other issues I cannot recommend this game.  I'll go down things I thought were bad.1) The cinema scenes are janky, as in outright laughable.  I don't even typically care about this feature, but it's so bad I had to skip some of them.  It's irritating because they are able to do some emotional bits, but those are still, artistic scenes.  The ones with the 3d models are horrible in all the worst ways.2) You have 4 classes, with 3 specializations.  That doesn't matter much.  Depending on your build you can do like 1-2 skills / spells every few seconds.  A spellcaster is better there but not by much.  You can only equip limited spells by the way, so it's spam cooldowns that deal damage. 3) There's a cross between too much information and too little.  The real time part means that you have to pause to read info, and when you do there's an entire list.  If you want to try to use the status effect combos then you'll have to memorize or look things up.  None of this information is visible on the character model by the way, or if it is I couldn't see it, so you need to select things.  Hence too  little information.  This gets really irritating for various reasons.4) Adds, adds, reinforcements.  Range is borderline useless because when you fight you're in an arena with limited space and adds that come in from all sides.  It is tremendously irritating, especially because you can have something lined up for what passes as a combo and end up getting people pinned down by an add out of nowhere.5) Why bother with real time when to play it correctly, you have to pause enough to make it seem like a turn based game?  Why is it so hard to see which units are selected and what their orders are?  There's a bunch of little niggling issues like that in the main part of the game (Combat) that makes it unpleasant to play.  There are little terrain effects that don't really matter.6) Last bit, since this is turning into a rant rather than a review.  Combat skills are DPS or occasional shields.  A game like this hinges on positioning and smart usage of skills to arrange appropriate effects.  There's very few ways to pin down or force an enemy to move, and the ones that exist aren't strong.  So if you end up doing a janky kiting that's really unsatisfying.  I personally stopped at a boss that had endless adds and a dash that happened every few seconds.  I could have pushed through, but I wasn't having fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Envoy is a solid cRPG, the magic and technology somehow remind me of Arcanum, but with modern graphics and more enjoyable combat.The characters look great, especially the main characters.For someone who likes to play Pillars of Eternity or BG2 - it's similar and completely different.Active pause, but with the addition of slow time, adds a more modern feel, especially with in-game slow time sound effects.The story looks promising, but there are no dialogue options, fortunately we can still decide about major plot events.I look forward to enjoy more of it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: The devs lied. They said Director's cut fixed a lot of stuff. It did not. There's still crashes, softlocks, poor netcode, the co-op experience is one of frustration as you desync from your partner and don't see NPCs, or hear some dialogue because the NPC didn't load in. The attempts to fix desync by juttering around from one end of the map to another, because it acts like you're connecting to another person, whose connecting to their servers, so there's additional latency. Its ridiculous. Nearly unplayable tbh. Save your money, avoid, and avoid the company in general if this is how they treat their consumers.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Envoy feels like a hidden gem that I wish more people knew about. Combat is satisfying and every encounter feels engaging.  You can slow down time to issue orders for your characters to execute (think V.A.T.S. system from Fallout series) but you're also highly incentivized to dodge AoE's and position your units to make use of the environment. It's one of the best combat systems I've experienced lately and recommend it to anyone who's ready to be challenged.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: I do not often leave reviews. I also do not know what has drawn me to review this game. It is not Baldurs Gate no matter how hard it tries to be.Yet for some reason I am having more fun with Dark Envoy then I did with BG.Why you may ask....... I do not know, but I am.As long as you keep and open mind and enjoy games just off the beaten path....Then I strongly suggest you try this secret love child of Diablo and BG.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: It's an absolutely incredible game. It clearly bears its inspiration but still manages to be a completely unique experience. Despite the steep difficulty curve from start to finish, I still managed to enjoy my time by overcoming those challenges. Highly recommended to anyone looking for something incredibly solid and who doesn't mind the difficulty.

_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent RTT game with a solid if non-complicated story. My favorite part of the game is the combat so thats what I'll focus on. Comabt is quick and flexible, its nice to have the options to pause time for more granular spell casting and the spell animations are all really well done. Classes feel good and strong though I do believe Adept is stronger that the others by a fair margin with their large assortment of spells. Aiming spells feels good and impactful, really cant ask for anything else in a real time game than what they do here. Choices can feel a little less impact in the early game than you likely expect but they do stack up later and provide some replay-ability. Story wise the game is fairly simple on the surface but at least each choice feels useful for the smaller parts of the story building up.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: Just 4 hours in this seem like a pretty linear game , sort of like a cross between jrpg and crpg . Feels a bit janky but expected as much from an indie developer . Game play combat mechanics are different from others but overall im enjoying it .... if it starts disappointing me i will change my review .
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: I played tower of time, on and off, but never finished it.  I may go back after playing this.  I am 14 hours in and I am having a blast.  The graphics are extremely good, and while maybe not AAA level, they are perfect for the game.  The voice acting is mostly good, with a few flubbed words here and there. I appreciate the effort that went in to adding this to the game.  I greatly prefer voice acted games.   Each character gets a set number of skill slots, so you have to pick which to equip from a fairly large amount of options.  Class alone can fill up your bar, then you have the entire specializtion class (3 per main class).  This allows for quite a number of diverse setups, and could allow for completely different builds on subsequent play thoughs.There are enchanting and crafting systems that actually matter.  Crafting actually allows you to make good items that arent completely eclipsed by every random drop.  There is also a global buff system that you can make your way through to grant permanent increases to many stats.  The Companions are varied and interesting.  You get to chose their specialization, but their classes are locked.  Considering there are only 4 main classes this works out well.  You can always have each of the 4 main classes in your party if you so desire, or mix and match as you like.General fighting takes place in dungeons in real time with slowdown or pause (you can flip between all 3)  The combat system is engaging and fun.  I do wish you could adjust the slow down speed.  I would prefer to set it to 25%, but at 12% it certainly allows you to dodge targeted strikes, and manage your 4 team members.   The story so far is interesting and somewhat mysterious.  I haven played multiplayer at all, but from the patch notes, it has been drastically improved since launch.   At the end of the day I recommend this game to people who like CRPG's, or even light strategy.  It does have its rough edges but feels better than a lot of AAA games I have played.  Will probably be a game I come back and play every year or 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun title, and has an engaging story line, with some really good voice acting, and enough depth to the rpg mechanics and class system to keep the combat plenty interesting over the entire story arc. While it's not Baldur's Gate 3 levels of depth and quality, it's not trying to be, and it excels at what it sets out to do, and is absolutely worth your time for anyone that's a fan of the genre and a great value even at full retail price.It's also worth noting the most recent patch added some great QOL features, such as being able to set the scale on the slow motion time effects, so you can have the combat move as quickly (or slowly) as you find enjoyable. (The devs are still very involved in the game post launch, and are continuing to improve things and make an already wonderful game even better.)
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: If you are familiar with and enjoyed Dragon Age's combat system, you will enjoy this. The combat and game can feel a bit slow, but that is probably due to the side maps/quests. If you want things to go faster you can ignore the side maps. Overall this is a fairly fun game but may suffer from bouts of repetition.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: This CRPG is really fun, with highly satisfying gameplay. The combat mechanics remind me of Dungeon Siege, featuring quite a lot of spells and projectiles flying around. I really wish the developers would go fully on this path with larger parties and bigger battles. Oh well, hoping for the 3rd game to finish the trilogy.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually share my first impressions after only 2.5 hours of gameplay, but I felt the need to express how much I appreciate Dark Envoy's opening moment to moment gameplay. This is the first  RTwP sci-fi tactical RPG I've played, and I have to admit that the flow of combat is very intense and involved after you get the hang of it. From a gameplay standpoint I think the game's opening hours are strong. Another aspect I appreciate are the cutscenes and dialogue camera. I wish more CRPGs had this framework to help with immersion, atmosphere, and tone IMO The only cons I've experienced so far are a couple of minor bugs or glitches. The first one was the black screen of I think where the cinematic opening was supposed to be. I had to jump on YouTube to view the opening because there was no opening cutscene in my new game. The opening cutscenes that I did watch on YouTube seems completely different from what I think I would have gotten because I had control of both characters as opposed to the one character that was on the other video. Maybe this has to do with the updated Director's Cut of the game?The only other gripe I have is that I'm playing on a PC handheld (the Lenovo Legion Go), and the controller UI seems a little undercooked. It's a little difficult to see what I'm clicking on in the inventory screen for example. Luckily, I can just use the touch screen to go around this issue. I know it's a small issue, but it's there nonetheless. Also, whenever your controlled character collides with any static assets in the level the character model kind of twitches all over the place. Again, not a big issue at all, just wish it was fixed.I'm looking forward to playing more of Dark Envoy and will update this post accordingly if the game changes my overall opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game so far.Writing: The world-building is fun and whilst it does feel a little generic to me, this is probably because of the number of fantasy works I engaged with in the past. The dialog does not feel forced and characters are likeable and well written and behave in a natural way. The story so far manages to keep my interest easily.Combat: It can be a little chaotic at times, but the 'tactical combat' system is well designed and helped with this a lot once I got used to using it. There is a variety of different skills, which make it fun to learn how to master them.Aesthetics: The game is quite pretty even on a lower setting. Fun looking arms and armour, alien-yet-human-like elves, etc. There is a reasonable variety of environments in which dungeons can take place, with a fair variety of different enemies. Other: I wish there was more of a difference in effect between some of the weapons, mainly guns/crossbows, and I encountered a couple of minor bugs, such as missing voice lines and being stuck in combat for a little while without any enemies around, but those didn't lessen my enjoyment. Maybe 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: Buy it, it's a fun game.I enjoyed Tower of Time and this game makes substantial improvements, especially to the combat. Story is decent, and I think it get's more interesting later on. Characters are decent as well; bit too dramatic and long-windowed though. Dialogue can drag on for an unnecessary amount of time. Choices are cool, and they do seem to modify the play through in a meaningful way.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10This is a very good RPGPros:The story is good, the graphics are great , detailed talent tree, and lots of equipment to try outThere are meaningful decisions that do change the outcome of the ending and lead to multiple play throughs to see everythingCons:There are a serious difficulty spikes and no real way to grind above them if you didn't set up right or have the wrong gearCampaign is short ~15 hours, but you will need to do two runs to see both main faction completion endingsLimited enemy variety Well worth $30 and even better if you can get it on sale
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: Game will be updated as progress has been made but has very detailed character customization and if Tower of Time is any indicator of what to expect from this game and the development team this certainly will be a game that will not disappoint. I standby that this feels like a natural evolution of tower of time and expect the game to get progressively more strategically challenging as you move further in the story as indicated by the reset skill tree. I assume you may need to re-plan your skills out as you approach tougher battles. I have no issue with this just adds more depth and complexity to the gameHappy to see a game launch when it says it will and does not launch into "Early Access" and remain in early access for multiple months or years.Game also reminds me a little of dragon age and weird west.Playing it on easy mode right now just to get an overall feel for the game.Good: + Controller support is intuitive and easy to learn         You can hit the L3 and R3 buttons to change the speed of the game from normal to tactical and game really feels like an ARPG which is really cool but you can slow the game or pause it for big battles+Not experiencing the Janky controls other have mentioned, granted playing with controller and I could understand if people do not like the play style of having a game that is semi strategic. The combat is fluid at normal speed but you have to understand even with that there are skill time delays that could make the game feel clunky.Neutral: +Voice acting does not exactly match character's expression but for a non AAA game and price point very happy with what I am getting+There is an easy fix to the mumble mouth and that is when the characters get full face helmets you do not have to watch their mouths anymore :)Negative:-Not a huge fan of the long asset load on startup but if it makes game play smooth with no loading then I'll deal with it.Nitpicky:-I do not like the walk speed outside combat makes the game feel slow. I get there are teleporters in place to alleviate this issue but would have rather had faster walk run.-Also find it a little irritating at times not being able to get in an out of item menu by pressing the button i did to get into it i.e. what would be the select button on a PC controller gets you in menu but you have to move the cursor to the X to leave rather than pressing select again.Final thoughts: This dev team is on solid pace to be the next Larian studios. they know their strengths, build upon that, and continue to try to incorporate something more with each iteration.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I reverse my judgement.It's actually a fun game with an interesting world and surprisingly good cutscenes for such a small developer.The developers are continuously improving on the game and moreover they are actually listening to feedback from players, which is not a thing to be taken for granted.I do really value their personal dedication to this game and its continuous improvement.If anything, the difficulty seems a bit overdone in certain boss fights, whereas in others it seems ok.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Envoy

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game, really enjoyed it!  Really like the adjustable speed of combat and being able to toggle in and out of slow mode.  The story was pretty cool, though pretty linear in nature, but didn't deter from the experience.  The art/graphics in the game world were just gorgeous.  A number of characters to build your team from with enough classes, specifications, and skills to tailor your team to your needs.  Plenty of loot to find but even into the late parts of the game seeing tier 1 normal drops seemed a little out of place.  Didn't matter as by then you'll craft most everything you wear/use. _childDocuments_.review: I really like combat, its fun and engaging. Setting is very promising (magic vs technology), but in reality doesn't differentiate enough between both sides of conflict. _childDocuments_.review: I bought this game today and dumped 5 hours into it without a break. The last few days i searched steam for another game to play because i was starved of a bit more "different" games. This one is good to go if you don't want to learn all the stuff BG3 or Pathfinder has to offer. It has a smooth gameplay curve with a tutorial that progresses through the first act. Everything is voiced and i didn't run into bugs so far - even the framerate is stable at high settings (RTX 3060 laptop). Seems to me that the developer is one of the good ones that drops polished games. For the 26 bucks i paid it really is worth it! Give it a try if you like topdown games.They pushed out a hotfix which made the gameplay a tick smoother for me because it worked fine before. The story is nothing that you can compare to a BG3 but it wraps up some mature topics mixed with a bit of sarcasm (and hey the first mission hooked me where the bad guy gets  made me laugh so hard that i nearly fell of my chair)I keep an eye on the discussions from time to time and the developers try to answer a lot of the constructive ones. I for example had an immersion break when they implemented an orange border around the HP/Mana bar (nothing too terrible - i still play). 6 hours later it was commented by a developer that said, that they think about an on and off switch for that thing.I really hope the game and the developers are successful!

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review:The teambuilding is great with the new patch and almost all bugs have been removed. Some things have been rebalanced, which is good, with the devs saying an even greater rebalance coming in the future.The difficulty feels fair, with the easiest difficulty being very approachable for new gamers in this genre, and the hardest difficulty providing a good challenge for most people. If you try to break the game with OP builds, you can. Devs have noted there will be a large rebalance in the future and I'm definitely interested how combat will go then.Story is decent, nothing to write home about, but engaging enough to want to know how it ends.Overall, a very good game for its price, and be sure to check out their previous game, Tower of Time, if you enjoy this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Wouldn't recommend this. Story, characters and cutscenes are poorly made and uninteresting. Progression feels odd and bloated - you get more skill points than you need, once you get to around level 10, and you can straight up buy progression from vendor. It was fun for a few hours, but at this point I have no desire to keep playing, as the combat is extremely repetitive and irritating. Your units get cc'ed so often, and if you try to select them when they are cc'ed, you just can't select them and you still have your previous character selected, which can make you press skills by accident as you thought you had selected the next character, but they were cc'ed, so you couldn't... and there's no clear indicator of them being cc'ed btw. Classes are also unbalanced, and inventory/character management is poorly made, with many stats and attributes hidden or unexplained. Crafting is okay, but simplified, and as you progress through the game you are just farming for and crafting the same gear over and over, but with higher values. Enchanting is an annoying part of crafting because you cannot see an item's stats when in the enchanting screen, so if a character is wearing two identical rings there is no way for you to know which ring you are enchanting, which can be important to know. I frequently have to swap between inventory and enchanting menus to check which piece of gear I am actually enchanting. Side missions are extremely generic, but main missions are often not much different than a side mission with some dialogue, and almost every combat encounter is exactly the same. Voice acting is poor and doesn't fit, characters seem to care as little about the story as the player undoubtedly will, so much boob armor, graphics make it look like a ps2 game, non-existent help index. And the price - This game is not a 30 dollar game - that's 50% of a triple A title. This game is an indie B-game, and it seems likely to me that, just as I was bored playing it, the developers were bored developing it, and wanted to release it and be done with it. If you'd still like to check it out wait until it's on sale, as I regret spending this much money on a title that looked deceptively fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into dark envoy knowing nothing and I haven't played tower of time. My experience started off with the game launching on my third display with no way of changing it. I had to turn off two of my monitors to be able to play the game, and then when I tried to change my refresh rate the game would tab out, and I couldn’t go back to it. Great.  About the game? The dialogue is badly written. The voice actors aren’t very good. The cutscenes look terrible. And worst of all, the characters are “zany and wacky”, I don’t want unfunny, immersion breaking humor in a game about war. I want the tone to take itself seriously.  From what I’ve played, combat is the best part of the experience. However, it is a frustrating affair. Controlling these characters is a challenge, you can’t rotate the camera, clicking on an ability does not select the characters and pathfinding is frankly terrible. For example, when I’ve obviously selected a path to avoid a trap and my character just walks straight into it. There’s plenty of other small things that I feel need more refinement.  Honestly, I think the game could’ve avoided having voice acted dialogue and cutscenes. Instead, it should have opted for dialogue boxes. I’m Interested in seeing what happens later in the game, I’ll probably keep playing, But Dark Envoy desperately needs quality of life updates and well it certainly isn’t for everyone. If I could give a mixed recommendation, I would.

_childDocuments_.review: I can certainly see others having fun with this game, as it does have some good elements. The character customization is pretty solid and the combat is interesting and engaging. Aside from that though, this game really feels like it needed more time in the oven. The voice-acting and animations can be really jank at times, especially during the cutscenes. And while the moral decisions the game presents are a nice touch, the story also feels sub-par. Not only does it feel like you're being thrust into the middle of an already on-going story, with several prior connections and plot points already set up, but it also takes a while to get going. Even when it does get going, the characters are going to be far more invested in the stakes then you likely ever will, with some pretty intense melodrama at the start of Act 2 that is really hard to sympathize with. If you have a friend and just wanna sit down with the multiplayer mode, enjoy some engaging combat and make fun of the jank, go for it, but there are far better options out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Misses the mark for me.  - main draw in Tower of Time, and yet the main problem here, is combat.  It can be very chaotic and doesn't feel as smooth and tactical as Tower of Time.  Maybe because the environments are very cluttered and it's difficult to keep track of your companions.  - music is basic and repetitive, as it was in Tower of Time.  At some point, I just turned it off because hearing the same few notes looped over and over was exhausting.  - there isn't much exploration.  Maps are relatively small and easy to traverse, lacking the complexity of Tower of Time.  You move from one enemy encounter to the next, items/chests are clearly marked on the map, no hidden loot.- given how little experience you get from combat, optional dungeons are pointless.  Most of the experience is gained by progressing the story.- voice acting is amateurish.  Don't expect BG3 quality here.While it's not a bad game, it feels like a step backwards, rather than an improvement over Tower of Time.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming here from tower of time ( the previous and first? event horizon title) feels like somewhat of a let down. This could have easily been an arena or hub based arena type combat sim and sold as dlc for tower of time. The game itself is slightly above average as a general package , but let down by technical issues, UI and ux implementation and a rather weak excuse for story telling and quest design. What you get here is generally just a combat sim, The combat itself its pretty cool with slow mo and real time pauses. However unless you're playing on the highest difficulty it quickly turns into an auto-battler and/or CD Whack-a-mole. Where all semblance of tactics are choices are made before battle with gear choice and skills. The skill system is at first a breath of fresh air but quickly becomes limiting during the mid game because of forced balanced by the devs forcing you to use only 4 passives and 5 abilities. This means that you only get marginally more powerful after around the mid game point and then don't really look forward to levelling up. The game is a 5.5/10 for me, worth picking up on sale if you're looking to kill some time, but i would recommend tower of time over this, any day of the year.

Not sure if I'll finish the game, this is too gd annoying.Controlling units is nearly impossible, the feedback is inconsistent and sloppy feeling. Units cannot be given absolute orders, without you microing in this terrible control scheme and when you let them act autonomously they do consistently stupid sh-t like blowing their mana on immune units and doing wasteful stuff.The voice acting made me take off my headset. _childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty damn good game, got 40ish hours of content, It's a CRPG mixed with a lot of ARPG aspects game play wise, it has a very fun combat that you can slowmo or pause to read the fights better and plan out your abilities, you'll struggle in the begining if you're playing on insane but once you get the right gear and stats, you melt bosses in 2 seconds and everything is trivial. Story is fun and easy to follow along and get into, it's enough to keep you going and wanting to figure out how it ends, as there are choices to make, most of them minor, the few big ones make you wonder if you chose right. Overall for a double A or indie studio, they did an excelent job and you can tell they put a lot of work into it but were cut short by either time or resource, that being said all of the game is voice acted, and they're decent enough, again, budget issues, but they did what they could and overall created a very enjoyable experience. I wish companions were more impactful and you can build relations with them and approval but other than the ONE companion quest they give you, there isn't really much you can do for them. Only real complaint I would have. The music is great and pretty intense at times of combat, the OST keeps a simular dark theme and it just sounds so good. 100% recommend picking up this hidden gem, 20$ is well worth.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game several months ago and played it for appx. 45 minutes, then had to put it down because of the struggle I had with the controller support.  I recently picked it up again after noticing a few patches had gone through, and although it's improved, there are still instances where the pad is unresponsive as well as several actions that have required the use of a mouse to accomplish.  I have to say, though, I am really glad I persevered, as the game is very fun to play and the graphics/artwork are absolutely fantastic (especially for a Unity game).  I'm also really enjoying the story, which is made even better by the banter between the two main characters.  Lastly, the optimization is fantastic and I haven't had a single issue since I started playing.  I have a 4070 with 32 gigs of RAM and a 7800x3D processor, so while my system is above average, it's still rare to play an indie game like this in 4k/60 with all the settings on high or ultra and have zero issues.  Lastly, and probably the most impressive part, is how involved the developer has been with fixing issues and overall just making the game more enjoyable to play.  If you go through the discussion section and look at the last 30-40+ posts, almost every one that needs developer input has resulted in them getting involved.  I play a lot of games on Steam and this is a very rare (but very welcome) occurrence.  To sum up (TLDR), this is a really fun game to play with what I consider to be excellent artwork/graphics and an interesting story to boot.  If you don't have to play with a gamepad and you enjoy this genre of games, you have absolutely no reason not to pick this up and give it a try.  Even if you need to use a gamepad for some reason (it's hand issues for me), it's still worth persevering through the relatively minor struggles involved.  It's also on sale right now for just over 20 bucks during the Steam Spring sale.  Have fun playing!Cheers,H

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not normally one to buy a game the day it is released but the price was good and I really liked the company's previous game.  I also don't normally write a review until I have played the story all the way through but today the game decided that I couldn't load any of my previous saves.  Rather than start over now, I intend to wait a while so they can hopefully fix more issues with the game.  This game should really not have been released in its current state without it being marked as early access.  It is riddled with bugs and general design issues.First of all, the interface is just poorly designed.  It doesn't work well with mouse or the gamepad.  Part of it is by design and more of it is just bugs.  Simple things like scrolling on a merchants inventory just don't work sometimes.  There have been lots of cases where the text doesn't fit in the box.  Buttons appear on the screen overlapping other buttons.  The designers have been somewhat responsive and fixed some of it already but really they should have tested these obvious things before release.The graphic style, sound, and voice acting are all fine but the cutscenes are just weird with the characters flailing their arms around while they talk and the mouth movement is mostly not synced up.  There have been many cases of the text not matching the sound.    The AI needs a lot of work.   Most of the levels are played with up to 4 characters but you have no control of their formation and while you are moving around they autopath over traps a lot.  During combat the AI mostly takes over but you can pause and try to direct as much as you want.  The AI doesn't seem to care that there is AOE where they are standing and not only will they not move out of it on their own, after you redirect them they will often move right back into it.  They AI just consists of puking out their abilities toward the nearest enemy with little regard for what each ability does, sometimes using up abilities nearby that should be used at range.  They will also keep moving farther and farther apart chasing new enemies and won't maintain any formation.   There is also a bug that randomly sends them running off on a long path across the map in the wrong direction.  While you can pause at anytime and give them all direction, unless it is something that happens immediately they can and will just decide to do something else. While I haven't had any actual game crashes yet, there is some kind of serious memory leak.  The longer you play the game, the longer it takes to load in each time you zone somewhere.  It also takes a very long time to close after you end the game.  During this time windows reports 100% disk usage but I have no idea what it is doing.Overall, I cannot recommend this game in its current state.  Unless you enjoy paying to beta test a game, I would skip this one for a while.UPDATE:  I was able to load one of my saves that only lost about an hour of play.  I managed to finish the storyline which was fine but not particularly inspired or any surprises  The game has many places where it forces you to make binary decisions between things but the choices didn't seem to affect the gameplay.  Its also not clear how they affected the ending because the game crashed while it was showing me the end cutscenes!

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of Tower of Time, was very excited for this game's release.  I really think the mechanics in place are full of potential, but I was just hoping for something a bit more polished from a game that underwent the early access process.  So many cool concepts, combat skills, and customization wasted on a game rife with technical errors and an overall janky, clumsy feel.  The minor nuisances I could maybe look past - broken tooltips, inventory glitches, loot disappearing, major UI pieces disappearing, and somewhat frequent crashes, (especially when using tactical time, a very important game mechanic).   However, the combat is a mess.  Pathing is awful with characters constantly running into each other, especially if using the terribly unreliable behavioral sets.  So combat in normal mode requires minimal effort.  Like, run in your characters and watch them do battle.  Maybe you have to move them a couple times during the infrequent boss fights.  Now, if you actually want a game to play and scale the difficulty up to hard, the game becomes ridiculous.  Not due to strategy or skill level mind you, the awful pathing/AI just turns combat into a micromanaging nightmare.  Constantly in slow motion, managing 4 characters.  Again, I strongly believe there is a game here somewhere, an excellent one, but I'm going to wait and hope somebody does it right.  Everything I've mentioned coupled with one dimensional, cliche characters, and an overall lack of story substance has me left me disappointented.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. The little I've played of the game indicates that there is a fun time to be had with Dark Envoy. I thought the kind of auto battling with slow down to adjust attacks, positioning, and such; and the aggro rings. Were very cool and the world looked nice.Unfortunately, using the developer's recommended Steam Deck settings for the game, it hard crashes my Deck repeatedly. It did so several times, so I then waited for this big patch that released yesterday (as of the time of this writing) to try playing again. What happened immediately after opening the game again? Yep. Hard crashed my Deck before even loading my save.This is the point where, had I actually paid for the game, I would request a refund and probably move on, outside of following the game to see if people having this same issue had it resolved at some point.I realize that the hard crashing isn't being universally experienced by people playing Dark Envoy and that the game isn't currently Steam Deck verified (although any Steam Deck owner can confirm the the verified status isn't a true indication of a game's playability), but enough players in general and on various rigs are having the issue for it to be taken seriously; and given the Steam Deck's streamlined specs, should be an easier fix for people playing on said handheld. It is worth noting that the in game reporting tool is broken on the Steam Deck as well.In reading through the game's forum, it does appear as though this is far from the only issue with bugs in the game, but I wasn't far enough into my own playthrough to get to those.If the devs would like to detail how to pull the game logs from the Steam Deck (i.e. where they can be found on the Steam Deck and how to access them on the Steam Deck), and also note if they will also show hard crashes that happen while simply opening the game, I'd be happy to send said logs to them.Anyway, since I received a curated copy of the game, I'll simply follow the post release patching and forum entries, and perhaps revisit the game in the future, but for now, it hardly seems worth potentially risking my hardware over it. Would I like to play through this game? Definitely. Am I going to take a wait and see approach at this point? Definitely. Do I hold out hope that this issue will be resolved? Not necessarily.For now, I will be offering a negative review, potentially subject to change in the future. Via curation, this will be listed as informational instead for now

_childDocuments_.review: It's janky, it's buggy, but the main problems are it is linear as hell (despite having a world map?), all the levels are incredibly similar and combat comes down to being locked in arenas while enemies spawn out of thin air.But all of that can be forgiven for the price tag if it wasn't for the leveling issue. You gain a level every mission. You can assign some stat and skill points. There are a lot of classes, many active skills and even a bunch of passive skills...you'll learn dozens of skills to make your build.No wait, I lied. You can only equip 5 active skills and 4 passive skills. This is absolutely crazy. Halfway through the game you'll be sitting on dozens of skills and you're only able to use a fraction of them, so leveling up becomes almost useless. Wanna play an rpg where leveling doesn't do anything? It completely removes any fun from the character progression so fighting just becomes a chore and advancing the story becomes a job.Terrible, terrible design decisions.Update: Dev says the limits are intentional. I understand that, but I disagree that they're necessary. I would gradually expand the number of passives you can have equipped as the game progresses, for example.

_childDocuments_.review: I think many of the negative reviews are cRPG players thinking that this is one and it's not. It's more of a combat-focused isometric real-time with pause (or slow) RPG with *some* cRPG elements. There's a difference.That said, it does have severe issues right now. It feels like an Early Access, with most elements hastily thrown together with no real thought or cohesiveness. It's still fun, but almost every element of the game needs to be improved to justify the price.Pros:- Visually appealing- Combat is fun- Good character customization where every stat matters- Magic shield system gives you leeway in taking damage- Challenge is mostly good - random optional dungeons go fast/easy, story dungeons have a few fights that will really test you, as they should- Fights involve using objects, terrain, hacked turrets etc to your advantage... but you probably don't *have* to unless playing on a higher difficulty- Gameplay changes dramatically as you get more gear, enchants, etc, so late game your build really comes together and it's great to seeCons:- No respec- Dodging red stuff is a little too much like a MMO/MOBA/whatever- VA is a bit weak, it's often rushed, making it sound very unnatural- Some annoying minor bugs- General lack of information and no combat log- Healing is nearly useless yet a huge part of gearing/skills/specs revolve around it- Balance issues in some specs like Combat Medic and in some specific boss fights- Pets scale poorly in the late game because they don't get any attack speed. Meanwhile your group (including the summoners) attack so fast everything is dead before the pets can get a hit in- You can screw yourself with crafting as there are finite mats. Some enchants are *far* better than others, too, so if you make a bad choice it can really hurt.5.5/10, will be 6.5/10 with some bug fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game for several years already with several beta tests, played the first game of those developers (Tower of Time) and now spent a solid amount of time in the release version of Dark Envoy and want to share my impressions. Here is my short video review with the main points but a detailed text review goes below as well.Game is surprisingly good in the part of story and role-playing - all the time you have some choices that really affect events in this world, you can see the results of it. That is not so deep stuff like in games like Divinity 2, but as for an indie game that is really impressive level of RPG element.RPG element is also enhanced by a system with 4 classes and 3 subclasses for each of them, tons of active and passive skills. We also have attributes that give not only small bonuses with each point but also some substantial boost upon getting each 5 points in the respective attribute. That is nice. What is not good here - is that we are limited to 5 active skills and 4 passive skills to use at the same time for each hero - with game pacing that is just not really enough for some mastermind tactical games and in most events you will adapt to some playstyle and most fights will look really similar.While the game from its cover looks like a classical RPG with a focus on tactical combat, in my opinion, it is much closer to an Action RPG from the point of fights and dynamics in general. We have a crazy amount of enemies, in most fights we have enemy reinforcements that attack you from all sides, you have cover system but with all that crazy amount of AOE and long-range attacks from enemies - practically there is almost no place for positioning and in most events game gets into crazy action on the battlefield.We have in this game real-time fights with the possibility to use pause or use 12% game speed to properly react to attacks and situations, and everything works nice, but after several fights with ~same skills with 12% speed you will most likely get slightly bored. How I handled it - I changed difficulty, on max (5 out of 5) difficulty - you need to be extra careful about everything and in most fights slow speed is recommended. On normal difficulty (3 out of 5) - the game is like Path of Exile where you grind enemies in crazy amounts. So by changing this difficulty every hour or so - you can improve your experience. You can also always reset skills and attributes, but for your preferred playstyle there normally will be optimal skills so I don't expect someone to completely change their build all the time.Extra two details worth mentioning. First, we get experience from enemies but in most events level up we get when we finish the story mission. Second - while we get some gold and sometimes loot from enemies, in most events everything valuable is locked in chests on levels. Unfortunately, those two moments together make fights less engaging as you don't receive instant dopamine at the end of the fight by getting a level or good drop. I hope that at least in part of the drop they will slightly fix it, as collecting gold from the ground is more like routine and not pleasure.Apart from everything mentioned - we have crafting, enchanting, research to get permanent upgrades, side and companion missions - everything works well. And we even have 2-people coop mode (I haven't tried it).There were several bugs (non-working healing fountain, lost items from inventory after trading) - so better to save game from time to time. From the technical side - game is not greatly optimized and with my RTX 4070TI, 16gb RAM and i7 8700 - the experience was not really smooth. So I hope for some extra optimization from devs and will recommend to play the game with at least 32gb RAM - I felt my 16gb was not able to handle everything on the screen and I had to reboot game/PC from time to time. I feel that this game is worth your attention if you are interested in a good indie RPG experience with not-so-deep but pretty fun and flexible action combat. I really hope devs will work on optimization and bug fixing because currently I expect many players with medium PC builds will have not a perfect experience in the game. But the concept itself here is really good and in the same way as in their previous title Tower of Time - I can confirm that developers did a great job by creating an RPG where you feel the passion and soul that was inserted by developers into the final product.If you enjoyed the review, I will also be happy to see you on my  to make sure you will not miss new interesting indie games :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, although I will not be recommending it now or ever in the future.But if you hesitate to buy it — do it: unlike Starfield it DOES get better the longer you play it, and it will NOT set your butt on fire like most modern games tend to do.For this feedback to be most relevant both to developers and players I'll go an extra mile and do my absolute best, since I intend to finish my first playthrough. Yeah, I don't need one to have an opinion.-= What is? =---10, Marvelous? The bullet-time.For a sophisticated player like me with half a century of gaming experience this is the first case of real-time slow-mo isometric view party combat done right. First time ever.Projectiles vary and differ, look cool with all the AOEs effects, and do not overload your senses, serving it's visual purpose. You can pause at will. Bravo!There is plenty of room for improvement since there are no aim/dodge/block/parry/clash/sustain damage/hunker down/assess environment animations, but with all the possible maneuvers and skills it still looks pretty awesome.Sometimes a barrage gets busted after issuing a command and you get shooting animation with no shooting, or character stays frozen in slow-mo and you wonder if the attack animation on cool-down or what? The above-mentioned animations would have solved that.Rigging and merging need better artists, period.Also it totally doesn't make any sense when an unencumbered character walks in battle. Unless it's a stance, comprende?--9, Impressive? The game mechanics.Despite certain overpowered skills and features like an on-attack mana gain the mechanics is very solid not just number-wise, but gameplay-wise too.The counter-effect concept is brilliant, and you can squeeze just enough synergy from your party to make any encounter unpredictable.Here you are catching up your enemy pantless, just to be overwhelmed in a moment from all sides, just to come back from it with your skills, just to get a small break, just to be overwhelmed again, just to have one last berserk enemy chasing you around. Done.I casually play on insane difficulty and have only one problem. With hitpoints. Why do they double themselves? Bullet-sponges are not a big deal. It's just... confusing? I can't one-shot anyone anyways on this difficulty, so.Regardless, combat feels right. You either dominate the battlefield, or you get owned.--8. Good (aka Enemy of the Better). The environment details.The amount of effort put into the background is a bit contradicting with how it is perceived.The cardboard map level restricts your camera, but there's oh so much when you zoom in. Textures, polygons, bump-mapping, lightning...On a cardboard box. A print, not a drawing, and definitely not a masterpiece.Also arena-like encounters and rail-map exploration are dumb. They break all immersion, and can't fill the gap a smart and eloquent DM can.With a little more effort you could have easily multiplied and hid the spawn points all over the place to achieve the same goal, but with a much more believable result of ringing a bell for waves of enemies.The way it's implemented is... controlable. But not authentic.--7. Okay? The loot.It looks better than it is useful, at least on characters. Has style.Total disregard for ammunition is a strained design choice, but OK.Below this one topples the other.--6. Meh? The economy.Craft? It just works with a pretention to be complex.Since what is dead cannot die and 99% of the time you parade the thropies, waddayaneededfor?Enchantments. Just for the sake of having these?--5. Poor? The quests.And the journal. And the "exploration". Railway-maps. Poor execution altogether.Oh, and the bear-trap too. That's an icon, not a visualization.Heck, ranger's traps look better! Hello!!--4. Bad? The cutscenes.They are so lame that I don't even have time to waste explaining.You knew you could get away without them entirely, right?Their mere existence makes it all worse.--3. Awful? The characters.The voice-acting is actually OK, just not the choice of personalities.They are either too bland, or out of place.Particularly not cool when a cocky teenager defines your playthrough.--2. Sucks hard? The exposition.*Wha? Wo? Who? Ha?* Those are my first impressions.Who are these people which, as it turns out when you hear them out for the third time, make a lot of sense?Fade to black, aaaaand... fade to black. Dialogue! Ugh.Hang the screen-writer!--1. Abysmal? Nothing.And that is really a good thing!Although there's plenty of poorly implemented features, there's nothing actually too bad in this game.Yes, the negative review is to draw attention. To this.Not a big achievement you say? Well, more than one other title would disagree.Once again, if you hesitate to buy it — do it.Okay, maybe the lore pieces are abysmal. Those "pieces of the story" you find around?It's abysmal you don't bother about those. And who's fault is that?--P.S. Yeah, I'm not yet done.Listen here, all the devs. Don't strain yourselves.Don't do the unimportant. Like you don't need the map or the journal AT ALL if your game is a railway train with a few loops.Wrap'em into a 5 sec dialogue instead, even text will do. Silly-stupid effective way to make your storytelling better. Stub features look like innards. You're better of without'em.Hire smart people. Who will tell you stuff like I do. Let'em speak.Oh, and please DO tell effective managers they are not actually effective if they do not allocate budget to do re-work. To cull what is built. To trim it.To have a say in what you DON'T need in YOUR game. Especially if it turns out that way DURING the development.--P.P.S.Demo is always a wise choice.

_childDocuments_.review: main issuesThe progression of each character feels good until the final act where you end up with too many points that you could possibly use to complete a character so you are sitting on complete skills trees worth of skill points and not being able to use them due to the character building. Then there are enemies that aren't balanced around the slowdown time feature where there is a 1-2 frame windup onto an attack that will do all the damage on contact with a move which if your characters aren't spec d into hp will do 70-100% of your health (this is on the hardest difficulties), for the normal difficulties they 1/8 of a ranged damaged dealers health bar.crafting does feel good at the end game but only if there isn't a unique item that makes a build work better and since the gear works on a tier system your gear becomes obsolete so if you can't find that unique weapon that is a large portion of your damage at a higher tier you will have to keep resetting the merchant to hopefully sell you a new one but there is also a chance of it not increasing the stats of the item with that tier upgrade which doesn't make sense since the item will be a tier higher that the other copy of it but will have the same stats.crackhead autonomous AI that will cause your characters to run away from the fight or walk into enemy skill and just die positivesthe choices in the story feel like they make a difference in the world you are in, so giving the game some solid replayability. decent art and skill effects in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I do really enjoy this game! The combat is fun, the skills are satisfying and the crafting and enchanting systems are great! The first one I was able to inch through (took me a good two hours), but the second I haven't been able to get past.As for the progression, it feels a bit unrewarding, as once you have the "good" abilities unlocked, you either have unspent talent points laying around or you end up with builds which should fit in one or two more skills. My guardian warrior for example has two filler skills which really isn't used and there are no viable alternatives. All in all, a great game, but I'd recommend that you give the devs some time to iron out the kinks and iterate in the skill trees and progressionEdit: The last patch fixed my second issue.
