_childDocuments_.review: I was introduced to Wizardry with Wizardry 8, which led me to liking dungeon crawlers in the vein of this game. Unfortunately, this game doesn't quite scratch the itch that I have due to a handful of issues that, were there only one or two of them, I'd be fine with.My first issue with the game is character creation. Five races, not a bad selection even if they're all effectively Humans With Different Names + Actual Humans. (Human, Dwarf, Elf, Gnome, and Porklu. No, I do not know what a Porklu is.) What stood out to me with prior Wizardry games was the inclusion of races like the Rawulf, the Dracon, and the Lizardmen, a lack of similar option is less fun for me. This, plus the random nature of your bonus attributes on character generation means you're effectively refreshing until you get a high bonus, which can be time consuming and boring.Another issue I have is that the UI is not particularly intuitive, and there were a few moments of a lack of feedback for me to know if something I did actually worked. (Like using a torch to light up a dark area, only for literally nothing to happen.)This isn't even going into the 'Growth Seeds' that are basically a bandaid for the aforementioned random bonus attributes that started out as a microtransaction and got retooled into something that just doesn't really fit.I personally don't recommend the game, but if you do, all the more power to you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an exact port of the Playstation 3 game and it is great! A game where you need to take your time to build a good party and that means re-rolling the dices to get better stats (the option is there). Don't expect to get a Lord, Bishop or Ninja right from the start; the game expect that these will be available as your stats goes up by levelling your characters (they can class change). Only one save spot (one better then rogue games and you can use it anywhere) and a lot of grinding (fun). Don't go far while you are building your characters, make sure you bought the floor 1 and 2 map for 20 gold at the item shop and whenever you get a better piece of equipment, exit the dungeon and have it identified as it might make your life much better! Early on, you can sleep for free at the in; it won't get your health back but your spell points does. So use your Cleric to heal your characters before you sleep! Just like the first 3 Wizardry games from Sir-Tech, this game can surprise you with a hard group of monsters at anytime; this is what I like from this game! There are 2 huge dungeons I will have fun exploring. If you like this type of dungeon crawling, get this one!

_childDocuments_.review: This game really deserves a thumbs up. I love Wizardry AND Japanese DRPGs, so obviously am a fan of them both mashed together! _childDocuments_.review: Excellent old school, party turn-based, dungeon crawling RPG. I have the five ordeals as well, but I've started on this one because I think it's a remake to the first Wizardy with enhanced anime graphics. Creating decent characters is important, the re-rolling of stats until you get that bonus 20-30 attribute points can be tedious, but once you have a party going, it's a great experience. While the game offers a pre-selection of heroes, I recommend making an entire party of your own with as many bonus stat points as possible. *Edit* If you like this game type, I highly recommend Labyrinth of Refrain. There's tuns of quality-of-life improvements, higher risk/reward mechanics, more items, an intriguing plot that doesn't spam too many visual novel cut-scenes, a second game after you beat the first, contemporary graphics/art, etc. I got it on sale for 15$, but they're 50$ a piece on averedge, and you'll see why. One of the top blobber RPGs, easily.Note: As you're "registering" new characters, the likelihood of high stat heroes goes down. After consistently making 6-10 stat points, save the game and back out to main menu. This resets the % chance counter. Then continue spamming "Register" and the back button until you get a good roll :)

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the worst major Wizardry-like on Steam. RNG-overladen battles against random numbers of opponents who use random skills for random (like, 1-200 random) amounts of damage (a problem which the permadeath mechanic only aggravates, though the game mercifully allows you to savescum freely); incoherent dungeon design on a level never seen before—Wizardry 1, the game that started the subgenre, was less ugly and baffling; flag-maze quests that force you to blindly wander either previously-cleared floors or the hallowed halls of Gamefaqs. It's a testament to the quality of the Wizardry formula that the game remains mostly playable until the endgame, which throws nasty enough monsters at you that you'll probably have to spend a few hours walking back and forth in a hallway killing the same monsters and reloading whenever a demon drains three levels from your cleric again. No real strong points to speak of, though the art is solid.To reiterate: there are at least five good-to-decent Wizardry-likes on Steam alone, to say nothing of other platforms. There's no reason to play this one unless you just want to check out the carnage.

And that makes the whole paid inn mechanic an atavism. There’s literally no reason there’s no auto-heal when leaving the dungeon. Not in the mechanics, not in the lore — it’s magic.Leveling is not exciting since you have no involvement in it. You just randomly get some stats. So randomly, that on a level-up they all can go down. Of course there are also enemies that level you down. All the magic is predetermined, there are very few spells and you get all of them anyway. There’s no mana to upgrade, you just can cast 9 times a spell out of four, inside a category. You can get into an epic fight, get a lootbox of the best quality, and pull a 10$ torch out of it, if you even survive. But then again, the shop doesn’t re-stock, so the gold = exp with additional steps. You just spend everything in the temple. The run-away button is near the class-skill button and it has no confirmation. The game has fake mouse controls so it’s super easy to run from a giant fight that you’ve almost won.And the controls are absolutely insane. It’s a combination of an archaic design paradigm, with archaic GUI, and archaic gamepad button limit. It’s hard to describe with words just how sucky it is to navigate all these archaic nested one-dimensional menus with these fake controls.♥♥♥♥ these controls; ♥♥♥♥ these dungeons; ♥♥♥♥ these graphics; ♥♥♥♥ this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Wizardry: Labyrinth of Lost Souls. It's a straight-up dungeon crawling game based on the famous classic RPG series. Wizardry, Ultima, Might and Magic. And this Steam PC version is a remastered version of the PS3, and it's a complete edition that includes all DLC. This allows players to fully enjoy the game.Directly bringing a classic RPG experience is hard to quantify its appeal. This game has an old-school challenge featuring the time honored formula about the original dungeon crawler series. Looking at it in today's games may mean that it is interesting but not convenient. This game is faithful to the restoration of the classic game experience. Simple, but random elements exist, strategic, interesting and addictive. But except for those classic features, every other amenity of the modern RPG we have played so far is lacking. This game has stuck so closely to the classic RPG form that you might love.This game keeps the basics of the dungeon crawler well. If you have experienced this kind of game before, you can start playing it easily. But hard to master. Sometimes your party can be wiped out by ridiculous events. The gameplay is addictive and challenging. You can explore the dungeon with six party members. Different classes, various weapons and items are available. You may have to lead party members, make carefully choices, and sometimes do bold moves as well. There is no automatic mapping function in this game. Players can buy maps and handle it in various other ways. Most times, you need to graph paper for mapping or depend on the uncanny sense of direction. If the convenience part can be improved, it will definitely be a better game.Wizardry: Labyrinth of Lost Souls. This game is a simple but addictive dungeon crawling based on the classic RPG game. You can choose from 8 classes and 5 races to build a 6 person team with various skill sets. There are a variety of side quests, items, and vast dungeons available, offering high replay value for long play. The game is rough overall, but it has its own charm. Your preference for this game can vary depending on your taste. If you have a good nostalgia for classic RPGs or are interested in these games, you may want to give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly playable and addictive. The UI is very functional for a gamepad though still could see a few farther improvements. Gameplay could be refined and improved also, the enemies are generally pretty dumb, the “1 hp hits” are strange (I guess these are hits deflected or absorbed by armor, and could be indicated as such), and save scumming is mandatory, though could be totally avoided, due to how the stats have a tendency to decrease at random when advancing a level, which is a totally unnecessary mechanic. _childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much the top-tier RPG formula. 1st-person grid maze dungeons are so much more imersive than any top-down view dungeon crawler could ever be, and the crude visuals of the long samey corridors in each maze floor makes you feel lost like in no other kind of game. Simple portraits for characters and enemies is all you need to understand what is in front of you and let your imagination fill in the gaps. A menu-like town where you quickly manage your resting, questing, items, and party members is all you need. The combat is punishing and grindy - but the interface is swift enough and simple enough that you can swiftly and efficiently hit buttons to make your party members do their jobs and get through it all smoothly - some of these games are a pain to grind because of the way you have to navigate the interface or due to jarring scene transitions - but this game is thankfully frictionlessly smooth in these regards. The art style is just fine, too - I like my party member portraits and I enjoy the enemies. I wish more games were exactly like this one. Exploring the labyrinth as my characters' spell slots and resources dwindle away from battles of attrition, wondering what i'll confront next, and above all a blissful ignorance of how the game mechanics all work, some actual mystery and going with my gut because the game just lets you learn by doing and has minimal explanation for itself - what an absolute joy. And just think, what is even the budget of a game like this? how expensive would it be really, to take this framework and add in a few hundred more monsters or items or mazes? I now totally understand why this genre of wizardry games took off as popularly as it did back in the day. I just hope it all comes back because I am so ready for more of this.

_childDocuments_.review: As a veteran of Wizardry series, this game essentially a modern reskin of the popular dungeon crawler games.  The same questionable early design choices that plague the old games are still present in this version (e.g. stat rolls, paying money at inns, character instant death if surprised by strong enemy parties, quests systems that are vague, and  etc.), and the lack of explanation for other game design features (e.g. stat requirements for classes, reclass issues, and race choices) still plague the modern take.  If you have never played any of the classic wizardry games, I won't recommend this, but if you have, this game offers exactly what you might be looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: The artwork is wonderful and the music is great!  Whereas, the game-play is rather straightforward, or is it?  The game allows for the player to seek their own solutions.  Hence, the map is obtainable but not available until your mage reaches level 5 or 6 (this isn't explained to you in the game and only does it make sense to you once you've diligently leveled up your characters by powering through that first dungeon alike a lost puppy); and the fourth floor, in the first dungeon, is a lot harder than the first three floors, so you're forced to explore the second dungeon out of curiosity, just to find out that the first few floors, there, are a lot easier than that notorious fourth floor in the first dungeon (then it becomes apparent to you that the fourth floor, in the first dungeon, is only beatable once you've cleared the first few floors in the second dungeon--so on and so forth).  Challenging as it is, this makes for a rewarding adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: As a seasoned player and fan of the classic Wizardry series, I can confidently say that this installment is a worthy successor to the original games. The graphics have been nicely updated, while still staying true to the original aesthetic, and many of the mechanics remain unchanged. The dungeons, while still challenging and lethal, have been toned down slightly, making them more accessible to a wider range of players. While the absence of Murphy's Ghost may be missed by some, it doesn't detract from the overall gameplay experience.The Quests and Heroes feature is a mixed blessing, allowing players to take on the game's challenges with a pre-made party or by creating their own characters from scratch, similar to the original game. The three full dungeons, including the DLC, provide ample content and a satisfying level of replayability.Overall, this game is a nostalgic and enjoyable trip through the old-school dungeon crawler genre. It may be a bit of a time sink, but for fans of the original Wizardry series, it is well worth the investment. I would give it a 9 for nostalgia value, but for players new to the series, it may be a bit of an endurance test to master.

_childDocuments_.review: If you played Wizardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord on the NES, this game has a lot of callbacks to it.  Slay some bubbly slimes and let the good times roll. I enjoyed this game a lot in spite of itself.  We've come a long way since 1981, and while this game has some improvements over the game it reminds me of, it also has plenty of old-timey ideas we've moved past, from status spells that hardly ever work (and are basically there to be used on you), to classes who sit there like bumps on a log most of the time, to exciting treasure chests that drop - trapped! - and are empty. And many more, but there's no need to harp on it... it is what it is.And that is a relatively straightforward dungeon crawler that doesn't try to be anything else. Cut down the enemies in droves (where do they all come from?!), level up as much as you can, brave absurdly low drop rates (but sometimes find epic loot off a pointless fight) and just have at it, my friend.What I think I like about it the most, aside from the old-school vibe, is that when I finally caved and looked up the quest and gear FAQ, there's maybe a dozen quests and it doesn't much matter if you do 80% of them, and as for gear, there just isn't that much of it to obsess over (a pro and a con, I guess). You can just run around and have a good time (I mean, if grinding and mapping floors is a good time) without having to stress too much about all the stuff you're missing, not doing, etc.  And even if you do want that one drop, good luck, pal! I ground ninjas for *days* until I finally got that sword... and when I did, it didn't really change my life.Best 15 bucks I've spent on steam in a while, and I hope we see more of these (with improvements, especially QOL).

_childDocuments_.review: Following in the grand tradition of the Wizardry series is the very first version available for todayâ€™s Next-Gen gamers; Wizardry: Labyrinth of Lost Souls features a deceptively simple game system complementing deep and involving dungeon designs. name: Cities: Skylines II
detailed_description: Ultimate Edition Cities: Skylines II - Ultimate Edition gives you access to the Base Game , the Waterfronts Expansion Pass , and an additional 3 Creator Packs and 3 Radio Stations . Included in the Waterfronts Expansion Pass is the San Francisco Set, the Creator Packs Modern Architecture and Urban Promenades, the Bridges & Ports Expansion and the radio packs Deluxe Relax Station, Soft Rock Radio and Cold Wave Channel. San Francisco Set Bring some sunny vibes to your city with this San Francisco themed set. A Muscle Car Garage building, 5 different Muscle car models and a police vehicle will spruce up your bustling beach city. Included in the set is also the iconic Golden Gate Bridge and of course - a San Francisco map. Exclusive when buying the Expansion Pass Content Creator Packs x 2 (Urban Promenades/Modern Architecture) Introducing more than 30 assets each, these packs will infuse your city with some extra personality. Crafted by two of the Cities: Skylines community’s favorite creators, these packs truly highlight the talent and artistry of our modders. Bridges & Ports Expansion Livelier coasts are now available with this new expansion, Bridges & Ports! With a new set of tools you are now able to create a bustling port to your city, and add beautiful new details like draw bridges and lighthouses. With over 100 new assets as well as the new addition of Marine Industries you can expand your waterfront landscape and connect your city in exciting new ways. Radio Stations x 3 (Deluxe Relax Station/Soft Rock Radio/Cold Wave Channel) Set the tone in your city! Introducing a new host and 60 min of music, each Radio pack will give your city building experience a new vibe. The Radio stations are paired with each release. About the Game Raise a city from the ground up and transform it into the thriving metropolis only you can imagine. You've never experienced building on this scale. With deep simulation and a living economy, Cities: Skylines II delivers world-building without limits. Lay the foundations for your city to begin. Create the roads, infrastructure, and systems that make life possible day to day. It's up to you – all of it. How your city grows is your call too, but plan strategically. Every decision has an impact. Can you energize local industries while also using trade to boost the economy? What will make residential districts flourish without killing the buzz downtown? How will you meet the needs and desires of citizens while balancing the city's budget? Your city never rests. Like any living, breathing world, it changes over time. Some changes will be slow and gradual, while others will be sudden and unexpected. So while seasons turn and night follows day, be ready to act when life doesn't go to plan. The most realistic and detailed city builder ever, Cities: Skylines II pushes your creativity and problem-solving to another level. With beautifully rendered high-resolution graphics, it also inspires you to build the city of your dreams. AI and intricate economics mean your choices ripple through the fabric of the city. Remember that as you strategize, problem-solve, and react to change, challenges, and opportunities. Cities: Skylines II lets you create without compromise. Now you can build sky-high and sprawl across the map like never before. Why not? Your city is you. Your decisions shape each citizen's life path, a chain of events that defines who they are. From love and loss to wealth and wellbeing, follow their life's ups and downs. Pick a map to set the climate of your city. These are the natural forces you'll negotiate to expand your city amid rising pollution, changeable weather, and seasonal challenges.

I feel like I can place them around without destroying the entire look of the city.Negatives: There isn't park life, and it didn't look like park life was on the roadmap either?I can deal with there being no bikes, for now. _childDocuments_.review: (Original review: Optimization patches will come in time, yes it is not the best in performance, but I am thrilled they came out with CS2. This game is much less cartoonish and was my biggest gripe to CS1.)EDIT: 6 months later, optimizations have come, sort of, still a former shell of itself. CS2 has just launched Paradox mods and a beach asset pack. The asset pack itself is very lackluster and introduces a new low residential building type, signature buildings with a radio station. Paradox mods are aimed at providing a better modding experience compared to its steam workshop predecessor in CS1. Ultimate edition suckers like myself were scammed at launch because I wanted to support a company that threw out a game half-baked and call it good to record profits from one of their biggest titles returning to the scene. All the gripes about traffic doing the dumbest things imaginable have reared its ugly head back into Cities Skylines 2. Traffic simulation does not use all available avenues to transport CIMS from point A to point B, it will instead, overload one junction one day and overload another the next. You can never predict what the game is going to simulate, so the simulation aspect of the game that was shown in its release trailers is in shambles as well, even in smaller cities.SimCity: 2013 was such a grand disaster that EA discontinued another title to the gates of history and CS1 set out to fill that grand void in 2015. Paradox had released hundreds of dollars worth of DLC as they normally do to patch/update the game from the developers side up to the debut of Cities Skylines 2. CS1 was a hit from release priced at 30USD, garnering support from fans everywhere and had the steam workshop to give us something fresh to play with user created content.It is unfortunate to say, but the game is a slightly more polished turd than its initial release back in October 2023. The developers themselves are truly not to blame, just like every other big corp in the gaming industry. These companies milk the game IPs to the fullest extent to keep their shareholders happy and not allow a game to be completed on release anymore. It is the new normal and hopefully this game gets better as time passes, but there is ZERO reason to give Paradox any more of your cash until CS2 devs fix basic core mechanics of the game and deliver on the promises of the release trailers.These issues that have arisen have also raised a different question overall, how hard was this game carried by Steam workshop created content? Die hard fans know that answer.

Now I understand that a 1070 Ti is old hardware and should be replaced, but this game doesn't actually show anything for all the GPU power it requires. It's just some basic scenery and a single road. CS1 actually looks better at this point! How will this performance look like when there's a bunch of buildings everywhere? Apparently it gets to 25 FPS on a RTX 4080 so... very very bad. I've been told that a top of the line GPU on a fully built city gets to sub 10 FPS areas from time to time - how is that a thing?This is not even close to being ready. And also - there's this distinct smell already... The smell of future DLCs that will fill the obvious gaps in the game. New styles? Sure, coming soon. Some non-boring-green maps? Sure, we have that in the pipeline. It's Paradox DLC hell in 5 years or so and an empty game on start. Steam workshop? Can't have that - it's too much effort, just like the optimization. Nope, no thanks guys! Work on it for a year or so and get it to a decent state and I'll consider changing my mind. For now I would rather give Highrise City a go.

_childDocuments_.review: (My Impression of the game after one week and 35h of play)With all the controversy about performance at launch, I was worried about the way the game would run on my Laptop with a RTX 3060. Right from the beginning, I turned down the graphics settings as they were recommended by some content creators pre-launch. All the time I played the game, I had consistently around 30 FPS (but mostly above) and all-tough I'm on low graphical settings, I still think the game looks beautiful, so much so, that I never really thought about the game being no low settings. Once uppon a time, you notice the small trees vanishing, when you get far away, but that isn't a problem for me at all. But by far the biggest thing for me are the tools, the game comes with. The Network tools, which pretty much apply equally to all network types, work extremely well and are super easy to use. In CS1 I always played with mods to enhance the network building experience, but it always got annoying and I quickly got bored with perfecting my cities, because it was quite a hassle to do anything. In CS2 on the other Hand, it just feels natural to build complex networks and it's really fun too. When being close, building stuff, the FPS also averages around 40FPS for me. Last I would like to mention the "realistic factor". Everything in the game looks so much more realistic, and even more important, it also feels that way too. The way all the things interact with each other is pretty much like in real life, and therefore the solutions are also quite realistic, reducing the number of times, you get annoyed by things, not behaving as you expect them to and loosing the will to play, which was a big problem for me in it's predecessor. I know there are a bunch of kinks with the game as of now, one week after launch, but following the open communication from the developers, I think it's pretty clear that it's only a matter of time, until those are evened out. And of course, I can't forget the modding community. Once mods come to the game, it can only get way better. So I would definitely recommend the game, if one is into these types of games. Due to the DLC-Business-Model of Cities Skylines, we can expect a long supported and feature-rich future, meaning, even if things aren't great right now, there is still a lot of time for them to become so.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good - it's an improvement on the Cities: Skylines vanilla base game experience. It's rough around the edges and needs optimisation and balancing, and desperately needs more content, but it is an improvement. Cities look more realistic. Service buildings have more sensible footprints, and the progression system helps prevent providing services from getting overwhelming. The new economic system is certainly interesting and adds something to think about. The new road tools are so simple to use and allow for great looking interchanges. Terrain tools are so much better and don't require "soil" like in CS1. But it is really buggy - it performs horribly, crashes randomly, and the agents do incredibly random things. I have gridlock in a city because people perform 50 point turns in the middle of a 6 lane main road congesting traffic, or wait until the last moment to change lane so they can make a turnoff. Traffic lights and pedestrian crosswalks clearly do nothing because people will walk across roads without a care in the world. It's common to see a hoard of people at the base of large apartment towers, doing nothing. Trees turn into green circles after about an hour of play. I'm sure these will all be fixed in time but it is a frustration that makes the game seem worse than it is. Not to mention the game has no map creation tool or modding - this is really the best sign that this game launched unfinished. It's a solid core game and will absolutely become the definitive city building game. Just not this year. Not even next year. Come back to this game in about 3-5 years and it'll be worth playing over CS1.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's face it, it wasn't going to release with content to rival a decade of development on Cities: Skylines.But what I DID hope for was for core gameplay components and loops to be working right out of the gate. This is sadly not the case. These are all personal things but; Building at night is just out of the question.Zoning for specific industries will sometimes just either not work or make the industry disconnected from an attached road for no specific reason at all, forcing you to rebuild it.Building a subway underground is an exercise in futility sometimes.Upkeep early-on outstrips any ability to make a profit meaning you have to make massive urban sprawls to even come close to making a dent in a deficit.Performance is shambolic.Couple these few things with the lack of modding support and gating it behind Paradox's own mod support is just another reason why everything seems so unsatisfying. Come back in 4 years time or just stick with CS1 because CS2 is a shell without anything inside of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely cannot recommend the game in its current state, and I'm incredibly disappointed to have to admit that, as this was something that I've been looking forward to for most of the year. Horrendous performance issues aside, the fact remains that the "simulation" does not exist as advertised. There is virtually no challenge; you can have garbage overflowing in the streets, high crime, low healthcare, bad traffic, and you will STILL make money and see a city that is clean, happy, and flourishing. After a mere 10 hours I became demotivated to play as I felt that there was no point, especially combined with how poorly the game ran in the first place. Blows my mind that we had better animations and player feedback in a city builder which was released 20 years ago. In C:S II you can paint a nice looking city, with cool interchanges... but no real detailing tools, no assets to plop aside from trees, so even if you prefer city painting over city simulation, you'll eventually be left feeling pretty bored. I hope that these things along with the performance issues are addressed. I really do. But even if they are, and C:S II eventually becomes the product that CO / Paradox told us it was, it will likely be at the very least a year or two until that happens. Do not buy, do not support these shady business practices.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I go into further detail, this is my first sim-style game, I have only played FPS shooters and the likes before, so I cannot compare CSII to CSI or other sim builders. However I do enjoy this game and was pleasantly surprised at the depth and freedom of the game in regards to so many aspects and for me personally, the highlights are building public transport and tinkering with the economy (taxes, import fees, subsidies, so much to play with). All in all, a very fun, chill game. I see lots of people here complain about things like performance and in-game problems, but most seem like a skill issue on their side. I have a MSI 1060 6GB that I bought 5 years ago from someone (so god knows how old it is) and on my near 400,000 (!) population city the game is running ok, which is odd since people claim theirs lags out at 30k population or something similarly low. Others claim the economy is hard and weird, which in my opinion adds to the fun of the game. The entire economic system is tied together with essentially every aspect of your city and its part of the beauty of the game to diagnose such problems.There are however a few issues, some greater than others. A pet peeve is the education system capacity. Once your city starts to grow around 150k+, it is very, very hard to keep up with the education demand, schools/high schools, colleges etc seem to have a unrealistically low capacity. This is an issue because poor education leads to many issues in game, both economical and social. The only workaround (aside of building a metric ton of schools i guess) is to download school capacity mods. Second issue is gameplay motivation. I've only built 1 city in my 60 hrs gameplay and I start to feel a lack of motivation in playing the game, especially on that city. My current motivation is to unlock all unique buildings, but there aren't many and what do I do after? Unless you absolutely love the game concept, after the novelty of the game runs out you might start to feel a bit bored. Last issue is price. Its just expensive and not worth the full price. At least imo. Wait for a sale. Other than that, solid game. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Cities Skylines 2 is a disappointment. _childDocuments_.review: There are good and bad things about this game, and I genuinely thought about this for a little bit while playing. At the end of the day, it's a very mixed bag for me. The Bad:  - I've read a lot of these comments, and I guess I'm one of the lucky ones, as frame rate hasn't been a big issue for me. However, a common issue brought up that I have encountered is the graphics quality not changing anything. I have a pretty hefty computer, having a 3070 and can play all games at max graphics with smooth game play. The game, while the frame rate is fine, sitting around 50-60, doesn't make up for some of the assets looking straight out of a PS2 game. The roads never load properly for me, they look like hazy gray squares that have refined text on them.  - Shadowing is either great or *really* bad. The bad shadows mostly show up on roads that are particularly rounded or on weird terrain, and it ruins immersion instantly.  - There's been multiple points in which the ground will become transparent and you can see through the map with certain roads on terrain. While that was present in the original game, it mostly came from all the mods that I had that could lead to the map losing textures.  - The landscape is *not* complete at all. They kept the concept of buying tiles from the first game, which was fine, but the fact that you can see the rest of the map that isn't tiled, it becomes an issue of ground textures stretching out and not rendering. It'd be forgivable if it were far away, but it's not, it's *right* there and very distracting. I don't really understand why they got rid of the fog lining the outside of the tiles. I understand why they could have done it, but if you want to make it so you can see the rest of the map, make it look nice for gods sake.  - This ties in with the textures I mentioned earlier, but man, the aliasing is not polished whatsoever. Every time I move my camera around, it's like I'm tearing the fragments from each road, tree, building, car, etc. It also ties in with the graphics issue, where no matter how much you turn up your graphics, it'll look and act the same.  - This game feels very incomplete. It feels like the devs were about 70-80% done with the game by release date, and just pushed it out to keep promises to the audience. I may be in the minority with this, but DELAY YOUR GAME IF IT IS NECESSARY. You have a loyal fan base with the first game, it's not like the first game was poorly received. At the end of the day, this game needed to be delayed, badly. The Good: - I am happy to say that there are good things about this game. The camera, for instance, is *fantastic*. It was something I always loathed about the first game was the inability to move your camera around to see your city in different angles. The camera in this game was something they really put a lot of effort into, which is great.  - I know this might be a hot take, but the inclusion of radio and radio hosts talking about city events and problems is kinda fun. Sure, it'll get annoying over time, but having it there is really fun, it adds charm to the game. - The additions of upgrading buildings themselves is a cool concept, and I honestly like it. I can't say for certain if it's worthwhile, but it's definitely a nice touch.  - The zoning, in my personal opinion, is a lot better. The fact that buildings are larger makes your city feel large. It's satisfying to see the commercial/residential hybrid buildings (I *LOVE* these buildings, I craved them in the first game) tower, as well as see all the new businesses they added.  - Not all of the landscape looks bad, the water looks pretty cool in my opinion, just needs a touch up on what it looks like from a distance, as it just becomes a blob of color. To sum this up, I sadly can't recommend it at this point in time. This game needed to be delayed to be fully polished. I'm tired of companies doing this, where they push out incomplete slop with big promises, especially when the previous title was really good. I *sincerely* hope the devs fix this soon, as I really want to like this game and recommend it to others, but I can't. The pros outweigh the cons here, and it's sad to see. Paradox, please fix your game.

While the performance is still unacceptable, if you drop down to 1080p and follow their guide or ones on YouTube to tweak performance, it doesn’t look awful and can hit 60-70fps. Still unfortunately cooking my room for so little frames, but the games fun and I thoroughly enjoy all of the new features and improvements. Only recommending it to players really itching to play that are ok with ~30fps. Initial review:awful performance. get like 65fps max, usually around 30fps though with 1440p and settings massively lowered. _childDocuments_.review: "City Skylines 2" has been a highly anticipated sequel in the world of city-building simulation games, developed by Colossal Order and published by Paradox Interactive. The game builds upon the success of its predecessor with a variety of enhancements and new features. It includes a range of gameplay features from day one, such as a night and day cycle, seasons, broad public transport options, and natural disasters. The base game feels like a complete, well-rounded experience with plenty of room for expansion and refinement.Significant improvements include a revamped progression system that combines population growth with an experience system tied to citizens' happiness and city infrastructure improvement. This system provides a more nuanced and engaging progression experience for players.Economic aspects have also been smoothed out, offering a more balanced and realistic experience. Players can now engage more deeply with the broader economy, selling surplus utilities to neighboring cities and specializing their industry to utilize natural resources. This, combined with upgrades and expansions to service buildings, adds depth and customization to the gameplay.The road-laying options have been overhauled, providing detailed overlay information for precision engineering of roads, tracks, and paths. The game also introduces new road types and upgrade options, adding to the overall realism and player control.The visual and architectural aspects of the game are particularly noteworthy. "City Skylines 2" offers two sets of building themes – North American and European – with a new addition of combined commercial and residential buildings, which greatly enhances the visual appeal and style of the cities players create.However, the game has faced some performance issues. Despite being developed for modern hardware, players have reported frequent game crashes and performance problems, even on high-end gaming PCs. Issues include low frame rates, typically around 20-30 frames per second, and subpar graphical quality, with blurry and grainy visuals. These issues persist even after the release of patches meant to address them, causing frustration among the player base.To address these performance issues, some players have found success by re-enabling their Windows pagefile, which helps manage the game's memory usage. Additionally, adjusting in-game graphics settings to medium or low and turning off resource-intensive settings like Depth of Field, Motion Blur, and Vsync can improve frame rates and graphic clarity.In conclusion, "City Skylines 2" is an impressive sequel that builds on the strengths of its predecessor with significant improvements in gameplay, economics, and visual aspects. However, the game still requires optimization work, as evidenced by the performance issues experienced by players. Despite these challenges, for those with the right hardware and settings adjustments, "City Skylines 2" can offer a highly engaging and enjoyable city-building experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Great bones, but C:S1 is the better game right now simply due to the wider amount of content the game has after years of development and DLC.  C:S2 will get there too, I'm confident in that, but that will come with time.  Enjoy it if you want, but waiting will probably be a good choice too.3 minor issues that I'll leave here:  - Elementary schools are massive, and as a result, once my city was a mature size, I was never able to meet demand.  I found that very frustrating. High schools also likely had the same issue, but I never really experienced it since my bottleneck was always at elementary.- The second problem is low density residential, in that there was never demand for it.  I've seen different results for people online, so I don't know what I'm doing wrong, but I was never able to build any LDR due to lack of demand.  I tinkered with taxes, proximity to city centre, car-dependency, surrounding amenities, job availability, nothing worked.   There was a brief window at the very beginning of the game where I had demand for it, but that's completely gone now.- The third problem is that my zoning seems to preferentially grow on alleys rather than full streets. Very frustrating.  Made me sorely miss the zoning cell toggle in C:S1.Finally, a wishlist for the future would include:- Mixed use office/commercial zoning, mixed industry/office, mixed industry/commercial and even mixed use residential/office but I'm aware that's somewhat unrealistic.  - A light/heavy industrial distinction.  All industry right now is heavy, and I would love a light-industry option.- Better industry zones overall.  Everyone's talking about how ugly the specialised industry is so no need to repeat it here.  I will say though, the new system of defining flexible boundaries for resource extraction is wonderful mechanically; very intuitive, just needs some refining.

_childDocuments_.review: A hollow sequel with the potential to growThe positives - Graphically the game is a good step up from vanilla CS1, the sense of scale is much improved, and there is significant potential to build on the improvements made here to make CS2 better than its predecessorThe negatives - The game feels unfinished, especially considering it cost €90 for the Ultimate Edition. It really lacks a lot of the depth that its predecessor had, and I share the fears of many that it will be incredibly costly to get CS2 to the point where it offers the same level of fun and depth as its precedessor - given Paradox's love of paid DLC.There is a real lack of content here at launch. Just a few maps (most of which require significant terraforming to make them truly playable), and even when you do get to play, there's really no sense of achievement or fun.The lack of design tools (Prop Line Tool, Move It, etc) is a massive omission, and one that is deeply concerning given the large community that played cities skylines for realism.I'm sure that this will be a great game with time (and more expenditure on pricey DLC) but at the time of launch and review, it just isn't where it should be.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I've been having a blast with the game on a rig with a 1070Ti, 16GB of RAM and a 3600 CPU running at a bit over 30fps with some stuttering. The tip is to follow the dev guidance on settings and disable anything volumetric, turn off depth of field and motion blur, turn Vsync off, and go for 1080p for the resolution. I've seen a lot of people complaining about the performance of the game at 4K but flat-out refusing to even try 1080p "because it's 2023" which gains a massive number of frames. Though I will admit to being used to playing at 1080p for the last eight years as I've never had the money for a 4K monitor and I'm also used to playing CS1 and Transport Fever 2 with hundreds of mods. However, besides the optimisation being rather bad, the game is perfectly alright. It's feature complete (apart from the mod manager coming soon) and it has massive improvements over CS1. For one thing road building is actually nice to do and has a lot of possibilities, the traffic simulation actually works now, several CS1 DLCs are now in the base game (as to be expected), mixed-use zoning is here along with a reworked demand system, the economy and supply system is massively overhauled, and overall management aspects of the game have been deepened significantly. Overall, even in this state, if you want the much deeper management aspects and you have a mid-ranged rig it is worth the try.

_childDocuments_.review: CS2 has significantly more features for the release compared to the release of the first part. Many things that were only possible with tons of mods in the predecessor are now integrated into the game and work intuitively. (e.g. road construction, traffic control, electricity and water supply, ...)Innovations like industry types, upgrades for buildings, different needs for housing types, seasons and air pollution give a breath of fresh air, which was not possible in the first part even with mods.Performance is not optimal, there is still a lot of room for improvement, but the graphics settings in the advanced mode are incredibly customizable, as I have hardly seen in any other game.With 1-2 adjustments, like deactivating VSync, DoF and Motion Blur, you can get a lot more FPS out of it.Even on older hardware (Ryzen 1600x, 1070ti 8GB, 32GB) you get sufficient 40-50 FPS on medium/high settings. From 50k population onwards, it was still at least 30-40 FPS. Small stuttering/1% low dips are present, but they disturb relatively little in a build-up simulation.For PCs with less than 16GB RAM, however, I would advise against it. For people who have played the first CS with all DLCs and some mods, this should not be a problem.Also runs well under Proton Experimental on Linux, which was very important for me. (runs even better than on WIndows)So far still a recommendation from me, even with the performance problems. The modding support is missing, because the map selection is ok, but expandable.

_childDocuments_.review: 9ish hour review: I recommend this despite everything I'm about to complain about, mostly because I just wanted a new one of these kinds of games to play. There's a skill tree now and you can upgrade buildings.Performance is bad, yes (with more research MAYBE I could make it better). With a 2060 on Medium graphics with dynamic resolution on auto, vsync(60), at 1440p, and DoF off the game is, at times, more unreadable than wearing the wrong glasses prescription with petroleum jelly smeared on the screen. I've never thought "Wow, this looks good." (My settings are supposed to prioritize FPS). The developers already commented on this, it's not really worth talking about further.I don't know how to play this game. There are tutorials, and I read them, but I'm not a city planner. There is so much stuff this game doesn't prepare you for after it says "hey the guided tutorial is now finished." I constantly feel like I'm about to drown and I can never get ahead. I've never made money because the budget is balanced, only because my city has grown enough that I got a huge bonus.Pipes and electrical lines are super annoying to connect despite being very important; with all the UI assists turned on I can only tell if it's properly aligned because small mouse movements don't move the endpoints. And even then it's sometimes wrong. I can't tell the difference between power lines that aren't properly connected and power lines that are properly connected but the city doesn't need the power yet so the UI hasn't changed (wind turbines).All roads at 90 degrees all the time. Grid city. It's easiest and I've constantly felt pressured to develop my city so quickly that using curves is just not an option.Sometimes the info overlays such as wind pollution or district type displays inside trees are literally unreadable. Between the graphics toys and what the display is actually supposed to show you it just doesn't work. I can't imagine what playing this as a colorblind person is like.I have no idea how to defeat suburban sprawl. People want houses. All the time. Despite single family homes being 70%+ of my total city area. Commentary on real life or a bug? You decide.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, yes - the game's performance needs help. If you have a higher-end system it is certainly playable, but Colossal Order has quite a bit of work to do to optimize the game and fix the graphical glitches/errors that I've seen over the course of my 10 hours playing (so far). I think Cities Skylines 2 does make some notable improvements from the original. It's familiar enough to feel comfortable jumping in, and different enough to not feel stale. Some of the highlights include the new progression system, the new road/building tools, seasons, overhauled industries, and plenty more. Of course, you may remember the dozens of DLC that Cities Skylines 1 had and be wondering if the game feels empty in comparison. With the new mechanics introduced (as well as ideas from some of the most popular CS1 mods), I never felt like the game was hugely lacking compared to the original with all of its DLC. The  exception to that was the absence of the ParkLife DLC, which was painfully noticeable. The parks in the base game, much like in CS1, leave little to the imagination and kind of suck. Hopefully we get a new ParkLife DLC to flesh out parks more.I haven't encountered many bugs while playing, its mostly been graphical errors or performance issues. However, I have noticed a few things that I personally believe should be changed (or quite frankly don't make a lot of sense):- There should be a toggle to place trees at 'maximum' age, instead of the current system of placing them as saplings- It is  too dark to build/see at night- The sun never rose in a North American 4 seasons map during winter... which makes no sense. I'm not sure who is building a city on the Arctic circle in North America.- Winter is just completely dark/grey the entire time, and if you're in a colder map you get snow, otherwise rain. Why can't the sun be out during winter?- North American low-density suburban households do not match their real life counterparts very well.- Boat cargo lanes are incredibly picky about roads/train tracks going over them. This makes building on water/island maps very frustrating, because it blocks rail lines from going over the designated cargo lane.- There should be a better explanation on how to make money, because the entirety of my time playing I have had a negative profit- The 'Rent too high' pop-up is also confusing and there is not a clear way to resolve it- Mods really need to be supported ASAP, because I need the 'Move-It' tool immediatelyOverall, I think that Cities Skylines 2 is definitely worth playing, but I would recommend waiting to pick it up until a few months after they have worked more on the game's performance (unless you have a higher-end rig)

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly,I don't even give a flying toss about how many issues the game still has. Them locking their mod platform behind a superflous third-party account is enough grounds to give this game a negative review.To some extend, I get why they elected to make their own UGC distribution platform, but the audacity to have people create an account even just for simply downloading mods in a game of a genre that traditionally relies heavily on UGC is almost like making it mandatory and simply too much. At the very least they should flag the game with "requires third-party account for all features" in the store.Nobody needs yet another account for something that can be done without.Take Giant's Modhub for the Farming Simulator games as an example. Same reasoning and principle, but no extra account needed.I'm not even talking about official user repo APIs anymore. I'm simply talking about doing something others have done successfully for over a decade now.Everything is enshittening. We gotta create our own free and open-source alternatives or we are done.UPDATE: Just on the day I wanted to revisit the game, and try out a bunch of new and cool mods, it was announced one of the most essential mods on Paradox' proprietary mod platform quite possibly delivered malware. Great it was announced just in time (for me anyway, big F to everyone affected), but apparently it took them almost a week to discover this. How can this stuff find its way onto there in the first place? With such high dependency on mods and apparently lax and slow op-sec on the side of PDX and CO, this game has turned from a bugfest quasi-mandating a third-party account over a superflous mod platform into a security risk.

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this review because I am genuinely baffled by the 53% as of writing negative reviews (at time of writing.) I enjoy this game wholeheartedly and think the prices is justified, at least on a sale of at least 25%. Will the game have a lot of DLC with a high price tag? Yes. But it's all optional, took time and money to produce, and provides the means and will for further patches. Is it as bad as the Sims 4 (currently at 87% on Steam) charging you $5 for digital vacuum cleaners? No. Was its launch rough? Yes. It was poorly optimized and lacking in feutrues. But everyone was warned it would be, not just in the hardware requirements, but in the press releases. And it's a whole new game, features will be added with time. Was it as glitchy, feature poor, and poorly optimized as Fallout 76 (currently at 75% on Steam) upon its release? No.Yes, Paradox is not perfect, and their are legitimate criticisms of them. However, EVERY game the release/publish is lacking in features upon release to be filled out over time, and EVERY game will have DLC produced for that is at a high price point. Despite the fact I agree with many of your complaints, at least partially, and despite the fact I agree with many of your complaints both about this game and the company as a whole. However, I agree with Paradox that this community is incredibly toxic for little reason. I have seen discussions on forums about this, where anyone who says that we may be acting to harshly is condemned out of the room for not seeing things the right way. It feels like a fan-base or community that is regressing into increasingly high-control-type behavior.Almost inevitably, people will tell me I am a massive Paradox stan for saying all this. What I hope to gain from this review is not brownie points or money from the devs, but just one person who agrees to help restore my faith in this community, to confirm I am not insane. This game is flawed, but still enjoyable to me, and I think It's ok to think that. Thank you for your time.

_childDocuments_.review: C:S2 might have a potential in future... but in current state, it's simply a bad game which is not worth of your money.As a fan of old C:S, I was quite optimistic about sequel and I did have quite high expectations. They got bit lowered when I saw videos of beta version but I thought - well, it's beta version, they'll fix some stuff till release. But then the release came... and the game looked same as that beta version. They tried tried to put out the fire with several fast updates - so the game runs little bit better but there are still a lot of bugs and issues with simulation, graphics, performance that it actually takes all fun from the game.Graphics is quite underwhelming but also quite demanding. AA seems not to work at all - only TAA looks little bit decent but then there are a lot of artifacts and ghosting effects. Textures are meh. For example, I think that Transport Fever 2 looks much better than C:S2. Seasons could be cool - but they are unfinished (as apparently everything in this game). Day/Night cycle could be cool - but there is no cursor light, so you can't do anything during night. Also - shadows shivers as hell (probably due crap AA). There are no animation - you'll never see firefights to put out the fire, policemen to arrest criminals, medics to pick up patients. There are no people hanging in parks or playing in on stadiums. What a step back from C:S1.There might be a "deep" simulation - but you won't know about it. The game UI does not give much useful info, there is no manual or so - only vague description in dev diaries. So player actually doesn't know what is happening in the city. But it doesn't matter at the end ... because there is so many fail-safe systems that your actions doesn't matter. It looks like simulation preserve itself. And you can't do anything to affect it. Money doesn't matter - game just throw them at you. Landscaping is free and unrestricted in any way. So one could say that map doesn't matter neither. There is actually "Unlimited money" game option but you don't need it because you'll have endless money on normal game. All this is cause that there is no fun and no challenge in the game. You are just a spectator of the simulation - and you just build some roads and buildings and some zones. There are only some simulation bugs which can break your city (e.g. land value bug).Traffic management - which I would see as quite a fundamental part of this game (based on predecessor) is almost non-existing. Handing a traffic is just annoying because you don't have much tools to do that. You can't even set priority roads. Though road building tool is quite cool - but zoning grid functionality is just frustrating.Assets look quite nice and I like more realistic sizes ... but there are so few - so at the end, everything looks same. Doesn't matter if you use American or European assets.It is sad that only way how to make this game a bit enjoyable, is to use "unofficial" mods (there is still no official support for mods).It is also worth to mention the terrible way of communication from CO/Paradox - e.g. famous "If you dislike the simulation, this game just might not be for you". I would say that players don't like broken game which they paid 50€/90€ for. There were few quick paced patches to make the game at least somewhat "playable" but it seems that last decision is to release patches a long new DLCs only! That is something totally unacceptable! There are tons of game breaking bugs - not to be left there for months.So really - do not buy this game now... it is a s*itshow... come back in a year or so - then it might be fixed and actually a good game worth to buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Cities Skylines 2 is a highly anticipated sequel to the popular city-building simulation game, but it fails to live up to the expectations. The game is a letdown in many aspects, especially in the road design and water physics.The road system is barely an upgrade from the original game, and it does not incorporate any of the features or improvements from the community-made mods, such as TM:PE and other road manipulation tools. The game does not allow for much flexibility or creativity in creating and controlling roads, and it limits the options for road surface type, direction, colour, vehicle type, transport lines, pavement and embankment.The water physics are also worse than the previous game, for example you can't cut off a river and watch it drain, it travels through the damn like it's on a pre-determined path.One of the most baffling decisions in the game is the roundabout system, which only offers a few fixed sizes for roundabouts, instead of allowing the player to adjust the size and shape of the roundabout as they wish. This makes the roundabouts inefficient and unrealistic, and it contrasts with the superior roundabout creation in the community traffic mods for the first game.It seems that the developers have not paid attention to the efforts from the community modders, having not learned from the most popular and successful mods for the original game. The game feels like a downgrade rather than an upgrade in some aspects, it is likely that the game has been watered down for the console market.The only hope for this game is that the modding community can salvage it and enhance it with the quality and detail that the official developers have failed to deliver.

_childDocuments_.review: Just over 50 hours in and first city is at 50,000Without doing a Fukushima to my RTX 3060 Graphics card nor has the game crashed once on the journey to 50,000.Knowing it took 8 years to make CS1 perfect and knowing what CS1 was like in 2015 when it first came out - bare bones, to expect anything major beyond bare bones might be setting oneself up for failure in expectations right off the bat. Knowing CS2  is bare bones right now:Positives: It has blended some aspects of CS1 right off the bat including industry, upgrading roads and so on and with a bit of gumption from your CS1 days it shouldnt take long to get the hang of the basics and get your first 5,000 cimsMixed Use. OMG this was a big let down in CS1 after it could be done in SC13 but to see it in even its most basic form in CS2 brings a smile and my residents do certainly love mixed useUpzoning leading to intensification. No more dezoning and rezoning, just place new zone and done!Road Tolls. If you are familiar with Road Anarchy etc from CS1 then the road tools in CS2 should come along fine. Just remember upgrading roads is now split and done two different ways (upgrade tool for bus lanes etc, click and drag for bigger roads or changing one way systems)Seasons and clouds. Yeah a nice touch for winter. Pre-made roundabouts work but major catch. NegativesRoundabouts and intersections get overwhelmed very fast and with no TM:PE yet to optimise you start getting snarl ups at the 50,000 Cim markCargo: we know that is pokedCims having a whinge. I suppose it is like real life whinging about nothing but come on team lets fine tune this up a bitRoad upgrades and bus lanes not quite intuitive as CS1 High Density Residential and Public Housing zones are poked which becomes a problem in larger citiesI think the nuker station might be a bit OP but I am not complaining - muchGround and water pollution does not disappear if you remove a sewerage treatment plantTrees should minimise noise from roads and absorb air pollution from industryWould I recommend it. If you are a die hard CS1 fan - maybe not yetCasual City Sim Builder player or coming to this type of game for the first time, then yes but just watch a few How To vids on YT first.

_childDocuments_.review: The review below after a line was written when the game was just released. I actually stopped playing it after couple of days, and came back to it now, almost after a year. Also, the usage of the Unitiy's burst compiler and parallelization features really shows in the # of sims that are possible on the same hardware compared to CS1. Overall, now I definitely recommend to switch to CS2 as it will only become better!--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I am an active CS1 user and a modder, author of the very popular 5-star "Demographics" mod. Overall, the game is somewhat of a disappointment. The only thing that's better than CS1 - is road tools, but then again, with TMPE CS1 was arguably better. Season change is new, but it's mostly visual and doesn't add much to the gameplay.There are lots of NO BRAINER things that should have been included from CS1 mods into CS2, at the very minimum:- custom "real world" maps import- TMPEQuestionable features / chnages from CS1:- Separate demand for specific zone density makes no sense and feels forced- Industries are way too simplified, takes away all the fun- In the game code, they have added lots of separate goods categories (electronics, groceries etc) - but there's NO visible influence on the gameplay of this deep simulation change (and I know what I''m talking about, I've dug through the code when modding)All of it could be redeemable if only THEY GAVE US MOD TOOLS!! _childDocuments_.review: Cities Skylines 2 is like a rough diamond. It just needs some more work to shine.Lots of things in this game are half-baked: The imports-exports game mechanics, the natural disasters (p.x. tornadoes are popping in and out and there is no sound cue), some infographic panels, even the radio station announcements. The performance is bad, not because of the complex game mechanics, but of the bad graphics optimization.It's like an early access game (an impressive early access game, but in early access nevertheless), but there are some things that they look finished, even if they need some more polishing.The road tools and the agents (cars/citizens) ai are impressive. The new zoning demand game mechanic is quite realistic. High rise buildings are awesome. The modular service buildings are a great addition. The XP system is very good. The low/high voltage electric cables are adding just a touch of realism.I'm just curious why they released this game as a final version, and not as an early access version.I was very conflicted if i can recommend CS2 to other players. Don't buy this game now, if you' re expecting a final product. Wait for it. If you are ok (like me) with an unfinished product that needs more work, you can buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cities Skylines 1 was a mess at release, too, but CO has learned a lot from their last title and built Cities Skylines 2 to be something that will, in time, be a massively improved iteration to the series. After putting in 110 hours since release, I've gotten to the point where I will probably come back in several months to try it again. The list of bugs is long right now, some of which have ruined entire segments of the game. I think once the kinks are ironed out here, the game will go right back to occupying a lot of my free time. Even with all the bugs, I'd still recommend the game right now.1. Parking lots are a nice addition but broken at the moment once you start zoning some high density residential areas. Your Cims will clog up all your roads with traffic just to drive in and out of full parking lots. Underground lots aren't as bad at first, but once you reach 50K+ population, even those lots will start causing traffic to back up with Cims driving in and out of full lots.2. Enormous ploppables will consume entire sections of your city in very disproportionate ways. You can place the National Gallery as a special building, but it is as large as 3 city blocks, at least. All the high level service buildings will take up at least a block and more than likely require you to delete roads and pedestrian paths. Don't even mention the size of the international aiport.3. Exports are completely broken at the moment. Cargo buildings (air, land, and sea) all act as little more than giant storage buildings at the moment for your industrial zones. There are other bugs associated with cargo buildings, too, such as every building in your city becoming flooded with mail when you build a cargo train terminal.4. Commercial buildings catering to tourism is broken at the moment, because they won't get built in your city unless you lower your taxes so far that you're actually subsidizing those buildings (lodging, entertainment, etc).5. Garbage management is broken at the moment, causing your city to generate far more trash than you can possibly manage. Things got so out of hand in one city I would've had to place something like 20-30 garbage buildings to service all the trash my city was accumulating for a population around 50K.6. Some service buildings are completely broken at the moment, such as the mail sorting facility.7. The radio and Chirper notifications don't reflect anything actually happening in your game and quickly become annoying. Thankfully you can turn them off.8. Lots of building LOD bugs, which will take a considerable amount of work from the dev team to fix (from my understanding).9. Since the latest hotfix, the number of Cims who will perform "dangerous" driving maneuvers such as making U-turns, illegal lefts/rights, taking bus lanes, etc, is far higher than expected, which is currently breaking the traffic management for all the cities I've built so far.    9a. Other confirmed driving bugs: Cims will drive on pedestrian-only streets; Cims will drive through grass and sidewalks to get to parking lots; inversely, Cims will use parking lots as roads.10. Some of the configuration settings for the landscaping tools aren't completely working. Some settings will only be effective until a certain percentage and then drop off completely, others do nothing unless all the way on or all the way off. I assume this is a bug.11. Silly bugs like snow not appearing on roads, or Cims not removing snow from their cars before driving them. Water/sewage raining from the sky in a giant column, flooding the entire map. Missing animations. Building land over water but not being able to build stuff on that land because the game thinks the water is still there. Majority of radio content just doesn't play. Graphics flickering for trees, roads, various things. Paths can't link up with paths in ploppable parks. Can't delete some roads at intersections unless you delete the entire intersection (sometimes you even have to delete entire highways, roads, etc). 12. Cims do not use your parks or attractions at the moment, which is presumably affecting tourism, too.13. Known performance issues related to rendering water and LODs.

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest thing about this game is the performance. If your pc can run it, I HIGHLY recommend purchasing it. That said, I have a 4070 and still get 30fps on high detail 1440x3440 (city population 116k). Lowering settings and resolution to 1080 would help but ultimately the advances in detail from CS 1 will make this game much harder to run. If you have a 2060 or above, and find urban planning interesting, then I’d say give the game a chance. The Dev team and the Modding community are making this game better by the day and it is already a ton better than it was at the launch. I feel extremely optimistic for the future of City Skylines 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Performance caveats apply. Just get yourself a save game from a bigger city and test things out prior to the refund window closing.That being said, I run this game on hardware that is neither top tier nor curret gen and  it generally runs somewhat close to well enough. The game appears to do heavy backgrounds things after loading into a map, so waiting a few minutes improves performance dramatically. This is true even after waiting for the texturte backing in main menu to finish. Also, for whatever reasons, turning off clouds fixed the stutters for me.Oh, and for the stuttering main menu, lower settings first. It will become much more responsive as well.--------------------------------------That aside, below all of this, gameplay wise Skylines 2 feels like a really solid basis for a continuously expanding game. It is ßretty much exactly what it should be, a sandbox ready to be filled with more and more content over the next years and with more and more mods. Having played it a bit more now, the basic concepts and mechanics feel really solid. What is missing is the 'bling' atop of it, little things like park and stadion animations. There is nothing in this basis that doesn't either feel right or feel like it can be fixed, if said fix isn't available as optional anyway. Paradox has enough long standing titles and has historically not shied away from reworking major parts of a game again and again, as such it is no leap to trust that the bits and pieces that need balance and polishing will be delivered.

_childDocuments_.review: Cannot recommend as a "fully released" game at this time. It's fair to remember that CS1, base game, sucks. But it has been just under a decade since its release. That's a long time for updates, patches, DLC, mods, etc we all took for granted. I've spent a solid amount of time playing this game, relative to its release date, so far. I can tolerate the performance issues and the "bare bones" base game limitations given that this is the initial launch. That being said, this cannot be recommended for purchase in its current state. This should be an "early access" game at this point. Visual glitches (flickering), misaligned road decals, glitched buildings (farm/mine hub buildings glitching through ground), general balance issues with demand and cost, and crashes. The worst for last; Paradox has cast aside the primary reason CS1 was successful - the Steam workshop. Paradox's very small workshop, in membership and participation, will destroy CS2 if it is the sole source for mods. CS2 has potential with great graphics and things like smoother zoning densities. An attempt was made at creating automatically adaptable intersection markings, like a popular CS1 mod offers. But there is so, so, so much left to be desired. And if Paradox will knowingly anger its customer base, and essentially handicap its own development, by cutting the Steam workshop then all there is to say is "save your money, for now."

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased this game when it first launched. It had many bug issues and needed some patching so I have waited a few months to let them sort out the launch issues. Unfortunately the game is still not what I expected. The bug issues have been resolved and if you set the settings as they recommend, everything looks great too. If you are having trouble with this there are a ton of youtube videos walking you through it. The actual game play is the issue for me. The economy system is broken and although players have been complaining since the launch, they have done nothing to fix it. You can not successfully manage the needs of a growing city and stay on budget (not even close to budget). This makes what should be a fun challenge of balancing, unrewarding and frustrating. You can do everything right, limit happiness to bare minimum and still not have a positive cash flow. Money management is the game so if you can't slowly build a city through small increased budgets, the game does not work. I even tried to play with unlimited services and money to get a hang of the game. I tried several cities from scratch and still was unable to manage the economy successfully. The closest I got was to have extremely unhappy citizens with no services until the city grew into 3000 plus population. Then I could slowly add services that are necessary to keep people moving into the city. This still did not allow a positive budget. It's really sad because the first game is so much fun and everything we were hoping for in this game is present. It is just not playable right now. I really hope the economy system is patched so that we can enjoy all the new features this game as to offer.

No exaggeration right now the economy simply does not function, it is not linked to income, it is not linked to supply or demand, it does not tie in to anything to do with your commercial or industrial buildings.  So unless you are playing this game to be a pretty city painter then do not bother as right now all you are getting is a pretty city painter, quite simply NONE of the fundamentals which make up the entirety of the game, NONE OF THEM WORK...I like the city creation element of it but I take as much if not more enjoyment from making a working city whereas right now that is simply not possible, the developers have put a great big (hidden and unmentioned) invisible plaster to make the game work, but it fundamentally removes EVERYTHING that the makers said this game will be.So you like a pretty city builder? Get it. You want a city management game, stick with CS1 or wait for this to be fixed. I'm not one to over react to these things but if I could I would get a refund right now, the fact that they have lied about the fundamentals of the game working is horribly deceitful and a despicable attitude from the developers.---This is a good game.Everyone is entitled to their opinion but the complaints are pretty hyperbolic and extreme. A lot of people had a lot invested in this being the "perfect" game from day one, it isn't, but the reactions to this are over reactions.My machine isn't a potato but it isn't far from that, but still it plays the game on medium settings well, no lag, no FPS problems and in medium it looks massively better than CS1 (unless you modded it to the high heavens) in fact I would go as far as to say it is beautiful. In particular base level assets (industry, residential etc) look so nice and so thematically better that with little issues a City can look good from the start. The soundtrack is nice and the building variance is so cool, cities can really have some character and look great. In addition the building upgrade option is great, such a cool little addition which helps a lot and allows a good degree of customisation.As I said though it isn't perfect. For a game that is much better graphically there are odd quirky little interactions with ground height variances which look a little silly and look worse than they did in CS1 because the game looks, otherwise, so well. It may be a personal one with my machine but I have a weird light flicker effect on all buildings, cars and pretty much everything during dusk and dawn times. The new road snapping tool is good but equally not great, they've put a lot of effort into making the roads better for non grid layouts but I find with it being more fluid it makes a more standard grid build more awkward and it is easy for it all to look off set and a bit weird. I also expected a lot more of the new base level traffic management system, it is better than base level CS1 but so far behind modded CS1 I'm a little disappointed, it isn't game breaking but it is irritating and makes me want/need mods from the start. Finally the panels and getting the info you need from them could be better, it is OK, but needs tweaked and made a little more logical.All in all, is it perfect? Nope. Is it very good and does it improve on a lot of, even heavily modded, base level CS1 features? Absolutely it does. Performance wise don't believe the doom mongers, it needs optimised but it is 100% playable with no issues.
