_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I recommend but not now.After almost getting every achievement and reaching the final milestone in a couple of cities i would consider this to be my final review of the base game. (will update when new content releases)First of all the gameplay is really good and you can understand it even if you're a beginner or an advanced cities player. The milestone system based on XP is easier to achieve than the last game's population based milestones and can be very exploited (yes i've done it before). The map tiles system seems to be very good but i do have a pet peeve that i can only unlock so much before i get limited by the permits i have. And the signature buildings is a feature i hope get's used more as expansions release.And also the maps we have in the base game are fine. my personal recommendations are:Archipelago HavenRiver DeltaMountain VillageAnd i pre-ordered the game so i also have the Tampere map which is really great for starter players.And then we have the simulation. Colossal Order is known to making simulation focused games in the past and with cities 2 i think it's better than the last game however, some parts of the simulation seem off like when i put the game on 3x speed, it doesn't even run on 3x speed more like 1.5x. And then there's the traffic AI. It is better than cities 1 but, there are some thins that don't make sense in my opinion like: cars suddenly turning to the next lane on the last second. that dosen't seem realistic to me. Up next we have the tools! First of all i used the *unreleased* editor early and it seems really good and promising! (i even created a map). Then we have the road tools which i think is simply complex and simple at the same time. The grid tool definitely saved a few brain cells of mine, the curve road tools is so satisfying sometimes and the upgrade tool is simple. that's it.And finally we have the services and the service upgrades. The basic city services are there like water, power, healthcare, education, and police but we also have communications, garbage, and we also have new sub categories of services like administration, disaster control, and research. And the service upgrades are basic but it can definitely be expanded.We're almost done I promise! But We need to address the elephant in the room, the performance and optimization. I don't have the best PC (2060 Super, 11700K) but i was able to run it at medium settings at just over 30FPS (Colossal Order's Benchmark for the game)But i know other people who had a bad experience with the game simply because of FPS (and a few people who got BSOD) and Colossal is doing a good job fixing the gameplay and optimizing the game.And that's it. It's a game that can be a great game but it's not there yet. give it a few updates and i think it will be there. overall id recommend this game but not now maybe in a few months and a couple of updatesthanks for readingnum

_childDocuments_.review: After spending a considerable amount of time with the game, I feel compelled to share my experiences, which have been a mix of fascination and frustration.Starting with the positives, the scaling of service buildings is a noticeable improvement, offering more flexibility in urban planning. The graphics, with less of a cartoonish feel compared to its predecessor, are also praiseworthy, although a wider variety of assets would be welcome. The improved traffic AI seems to promise a more realistic flow, and the addition of seasons and street-building tools are steps in the right direction, bringing a fresh look and strategic depth to the game.However, these enhancements are marred by persistent bugs and a lack of content that makes for a lackluster experience. From exporting glitches that cripple trade to a hoarding problem in goods depots, the simulation falls short of expectations. Issues with waste management, post services, and a general economy that seems to function independently of player actions undercut the supposed simulation depth. The traffic glitches and unrealistic behavior of zones further sour the gameplay.Furthermore, the introduction of 'failsafe mechanisms' seems to contradict the challenge expected in a city-building simulator. These mechanisms protect players from the consequences of their actions to such an extent that failure becomes almost impossible, detracting from the game's challenge and ultimately its replayability.The handling of natural disasters and protective measures also lacks refinement, as do the achievements and announcements, both of which have bugs. The water physics defy logic at times, and the terraforming tools are rendered nearly unusable due to inexplicable water sources that can unexpectedly flood your city.The lack of animations in places such as parks and for emergency services like the fire department strips away layers of immersion. Complaints of businesses about the lack of customers, the absence of mod support, and the inability to create custom maps are significant drawbacks, which make the game feel incomplete. It's as if the whole economic simulation is an optional extra rather than a core feature, despite the promises of a 'deep simulation' that impacts the city based on your decisions.In conclusion, while the foundational elements of the game show promise, the prevalence of game-breaking bugs and the lack of real challenge present significant obstacles to enjoyment. I hope future updates will address these issues and that the game's economic system will be made more robust and integrated with the consequences of failure. Removing the failsafe mechanisms might instill the stakes and challenges currently missing, turning what now feels like a playable beta into the deeply engaging simulator it aims to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I know others' mileage may vary, but I'm honestly having a blast with this game. On the balance of probabilities, I would recommend buying this game if you're a big fan of SC4. If you're worried about a lack of features compared with CS1, or play CS1 with a lot of mods at present, consider waiting for more DLC. But I would say it is a perfectly serviceable city builder, and with some fine tuning and bug fixes it will probably surpass Simcity 4 as the best game of the genre of all time.An honest review: PROS: - Better simulation and challenge than the first game, at least for those without most of the DLCs. I never really found CS1 very challenging and towards the late game I just tended to spam high density, which immediately developed. I found the first game lacked character. CS2 meanwhile goes some way to injecting a bit of life. There's peak hours where your traffic and PT ridership swells, and then it ebbs away as the hours tick by. - It scratches that Simcity 4 itch. - You can really sprawl. My first and only city so far is on a map with a river straddled by mountains, and even then I've not even filled out the buildable area entirely yet. It feels like you can really build for ages in this game, to a much larger extent than CS1 or Simcity 2013.- Despite sprawl, you can still build a really fun little downtown.- Art direction is heaps better than the first game. Way more character, plus the European and American themed zones mean you can switch it up in different suburbs to give each one some uniqueness. You can zone row houses to add flavour to the areas surrounding your downtown, or go full LA and make a sprawling sea of low density detached houses.- No matter how bad you are at building a city, it's hard to make this game look bad. The day-night cycle is gorgeous, especially with the camera feature. - Highway and road building tools are insanely good. Better than the first game by a fair way and really allow for some interesting and innovative ways to build out your road network.- Modular buildings are really nifty. Mayors can really build out sprawling university campuses or upgrade inner city hospitals to boost the health of residents. NEUTRAL- Performance for me has been fine, with some small stutters here and there. My city is now 80k people and I'm still running fine, but I have a decent gaming laptop. Your mileage may vary. Look up guides for how to improve performance.CONS- Some modular buildings need rebalancing and more additions by CO. For instance, elementary schools aren't balanced. Way too much capacity for smaller towns but then woefully inadequate to cope with surging demand in inner-city areas. I have five schools in my  relatively small downtown that are overcrowded despite being fully upgraded. The devs either need to add an upgrade for these schools that really boost capacity (I'm talking doubling, tripling, quadrupling the number of students), or release special inner-city vertical schools.- Some features are broken. Garbage collection seems a bit strange. And the postal service doesn't seem to work properly.- Rent stress seems to occur without there really being a reason? Right now it doesn't matter how much medium or high density I zone, any low density households seem to scream that they are suffering through too much rent. But then I build public housing, and they get abandoned because residents hate the small apartments. Go figure.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve given up.I’ve mostly ignored all the comments at first so that I can give an impartial view of this game.Foremost, Cities Skylines 2 is broken. It is riddled with many serious algorithmic and performance bugs that affect core functions of the game. Widely reported bugs such as frequent crashes and taxation glitch, which causes unexpected income and deficit spikes that breaks the gameplay — and this is just one of many serious ones out thereWhile it is understandable for bugs to be present in games and software, Colossal Order’s lack of urgency and genuine interest in tackling bug reports makes it unacceptable.It’s been 3 months since launch, yet recent statements from the company were deliberate in evading questions on roadmaps for bug fixes, and attempt to obfuscate users by saying that something is being worked on for the near future.Hard to believe that this is the same company that made Cities Skylines 1 — a realisation of what the company once was. For now, stay away until more is done.—(Quick update — 29 Jan)I’ve given this game another shot with a fresh install and a new city — issues remain and let me summarize my experience- At first glance, Cities Skylines 2 provides many quality-of-life improvements compared to Cities Skylines 1, such as better road building and modern assets.- You’ll find that it is now a breeze to build roads, highways and intersections, tools are intuitive and easy to use. Want an intersection? Just drag across an existing road and you’ll have an intersection. Want a roundabout? Just plop it down.- Assets are refreshed as compared Cities Skylines 1, gone are the cartoonish buildings and vehicles.However, most of the gamebreaking issues start occurring as you progress into the game.Game stability and optimization- As your population increases, game simulation will slow to a crawl — despite my setup being well above the recommended specs- Occurs on my two different cities and save files. Service Mechanics- Garbage management and healthcare vehicles will regularly depart from their facility and return almost immediately (alerts will popup frequently that healthcare and garbage management is inadequate despite well within their capacity)- Buses, trams and trains will frequently and randomly despawn or stop working completely.Economy and industry- Taxation for industries will become highly erratic due to an algorithmic bug, taxation income will fluctuate randomly by the millions for a town of 10k citizens. Completely breaks the budgeting and financial system.- Local industries will not export goods, cargo terminals (both air and train) will hoard all mail and breaking the mailing system (also impacts citizen happiness)- As confirmed by many others, due to a land value bug, prices will increase to astronomical levels, which makes residential suitability zero for most parts of your city and its outer suburbs.- This the most critical bug since it completely stops the progress of your city and game, as residential demand will be zero, and no new citizens can move in. These are just some of the numerous bugs I came across while playing this game — you do find yourself having to look up online for any workarounds whenever you come across one.While I’m almost certain that these issues will be addressed eventually in the future.. but is this what it is expected of a published game that cost $50? Was this game ready to be published in the first place?After two gameplays and two cities, one thing is certain for me — Cities Skylines 2 would not have passed QA and should not have been published in the state it is in. This game is in beta.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright after investing around ~6 hours into the game at this point, I can flesh out some of a review.So where to begin...While I will acknowledge that it is incredibly difficult to balance a governmental budget in real life, at 14k population I have only nearly achieved a balanced budget for about 6 seconds. And that wasn't even balanced, I was still in the red. What this does is make the player reliant on the bonuses from reaching milestones, and playing the game of trying to balance the budget or take out loans to maintain operation until you get enough exp to reach the next milestone. I've had to do this multiple times. Several hours spent just balancing a budget just to get several chirper notifications about how my services aren't good enough. Oh yeah, speaking of which..In theory, as you gain population, you should expand city services like fire, police, and medical. These come with massive costs, and the medical clinic especially costs 105k per month while only costing ~60k to initially build. These upkeep costs add up, and fast. Especially when your population is still relatively small, it can become incredibly difficult to keep up with the costs when your tax revenues are next to nothing. Alongside that, there's a new system of .What is efficiency, you might ask. Efficiency is a boost or loss of performance of employees of every business, industry, and city service. These can be based on the health of employees, the budget, the amount of natural resources, and 'employee happiness'. These factors sounds great when you have maxed out budgets and a well running city, but at the start, they can cripple city services with ease. Every 2% I lowered the budget of a service, because you can't pull it for just 1% for some reason, meant each city service took a massive 3-5% hit in efficiency. Trying to save money to survive to your next milestone? Too bad, everyone is dying and nothing is functional.This issue is as the title states: from around 1500 population till now, at 14000, all my commercial businesses state that there are not enough customers to sustain their business. Even as commercial demand increases. Even as population skyrockets. What causes those factors to not affect that issue is beyond me, but it's extremely frustrating to have half the screen be covered in issue bubbles I can't solve.Public transit in this version is extremely limited, and if you just want to improve your population's happiness then just place down bus and taxi stops. No need to make a route this time, the star increase comes from plopping down the stop, not having a bus route run to it or even having a route running. While I will acknowledge that this feels extremely prototypical for using the American buildings pack instead of the European, it makes it feel as though public transit is more for improving citizen happiness than traffic.Onto highways, alongside most other roadways in this game. I will admit to having playing Cities: Skylines 1 with a multitude of workshop mods to improve my experience, however I don't think that excuses drivers turning left onto the opposing lanes of a freeway from an on-ramp. This is something, in my travels between Europe and America, that I have NEVER ONCE SEEN. It makes building highways without a median or road separation near impossible, as every spot will form a traffic jam as drivers cross whole halves of a highway to reach the other side. At least there's a roundabout generator, right? Even though it's extremely limited and doesn't form that large a roundabout and will only place if it can destroy some of the zoned buildings and won't place if it can't and there's no telling if it will or won't until you try!Listen, I was really excited for this game, pre-ordered and everything. But between the widely known about performance issues, which at this point are causing my game to stutter, and the limited ability to actually build a functional city, I'm just going to put this on the shelf for now. Do I recommend the game?Currently? No, absolutely not. Play the first one and enjoy it. With mods, you can achieve roughly the same game play as 2 with far better industry, far more to work with, and far better performance.Do I think C:S 2 can improve?Yes. I've seen and played hundreds of hours of C:S 1, and if updates can bring some stabilization, and mods can be allowed, this game can flourish for the future. But the future is not now, and if future proofing your game means it struggles now, then it may not survive to the future you built it to endure. And that would be quite a shame.

They have listened to the community and have retracted the beach property DLC and incorparated them into the main vanilla game instead. They have reworked the economy which is a welcome change and actually makes the game a challenge and fun to play. The newly released assets are fantastic additions that now allow me to build smaller communities, and cul-de-sacs!!The game still has more promise. _childDocuments_.review: I remember how excited I was when the first Cities Skylines was announced. I did not hesitate to pre-order that game and do not regret doing so. It more than exceeded my expectations and just got better and better with age, especially thanks to the modding community. I personally feel like it is the best City Builder to date, and because of that I assumed I would be having a similar experience with Cities Skylines 2.Unfortunately that is not the case. I'm sure we have all been burned before with game pre-orders. Normally my rule is to wait until a game is released and reviews are out before I spend my hard earned dollars.  But because my experience with Cities 1 was so good I made an exception. I was so hyped I even forked up the extra dough for the deluxe addition, making this the most expensive game I have ever purchased! Once the embargo for CS content creators dropped and initial reviews posted I wondered if I made a mistake and was considering a refund. I ultimately decided to commit to the game and try it out for myself.I've now played about 30 hours and the verdict is out. In my opinion, Cities Skylines 2 should have been delayed. As other reviewers have stated, it feels like and Early Access or Beta, and its not hard to find someone highlighting all of the performance issues, missing features, and bugs the game is currently plagued with. I just can't enjoy playing it right now knowing that it will take 6 months to a year, maybe longer before it actually feels like a true 1.0 release. This game is the final nail in the pre-orders coffin for me, regardless of how excited I am or how trustworthy a developer may seem. I am truly disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: DEFINITELY WORTH A BUY(I had over 70 hours of playtime on Xbox Game Pass before buying it on Steam)This is the ultimate city-builder sandbox. You can dream—and build—many unique cities that all differ depending on the map. There’s no one-size-fits-all approach: you can "finish" the game with a futuristic, densely populated gem of a town between the mountains, or a sprawling metropolis by the sea. You can have a zero-emission utopia where everyone uses public transportation, or a car-maxxed motorist's dream.The new economy update finally makes progression interesting. You can't advance milestones without managing transportation. Again, you can produce locally or import goods—everything works as long as you adapt to the challenges and overcome them.The road construction tool is tricky to master, but you essentially have full control of traffic flow, pedestrian crossings, and traffic lights with the vanilla version. I recommend watching some YouTube tutorials to get up to speed.WHAT I WOULD LIKE MORE:-Further optimization. Boy, this game is THIRSTY and CHUGS resources. Understandable given the magnitude of the simulation, from aerial view to single-person zoom in real-time with just a scroll of the mousewheel. The developers have made great improvements since launch, and I encourage them to keep going.- More unique buildings. The more, the better :) - RADIO MODS that don’t disable achievements. The radio music is great, but it can get repetitive during long sessions. Sure, you could play your playlist in the background, but radio mods are better for immersion.FINAL THOUGHTSWhile still imperfect, this is the state-of-the-art city-building simulator. Eventually, some other title might arrive to supersede Cities II, but for now, if you like building and optimizing cities, this is the game to buy. Totally worth it at its current price.

_childDocuments_.review: I disagree with a great deal of the negative reviews. I think this game has the bones, the spine, and a great deal of the flesh to make a good game. Simple as that. Having played the first release, I watched the earnest effort of a developer caught between the publisher and the shareholders, deal with the fallout of a very poor release. They have now come to the point where the latest patch does deliver on the promise of a gamified city builder with the option of a free sandbox, sating the demands of many of the players.I know many, like myself, felt that the game lacked the challenge of a game, of CS1. They fixed that. They were called out for poor marketing with a bad DLC, its now free. Is the game optimized? I see so many "this game dosen't work on my XYZ". I'm sitting on a 1080x and a 5ish year old computer. It running very well. CS1 by late game in the last DLC... just too big for anyone's rig less you mining cyrpto and actually destroying your cities power grid.I find the game play enjoyable, and relaxing. The challenge satisfying, and i am happy to know I can go Simcity 4 anytime I want. Is the paradox mod store a bit silly as a concept, and still under construction... yes. I trust the moding community however to make due until they get on top of it. So hey, take all reviews with a grain of salt, but I can say that after almost a year, the game is now definatly worth checking out in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: After much deliberation and time spent awaiting fixes, I think it's safe to say we have entered a good time in the game. The devs reversed some seriously concerning paid content so that it is now free and included with the game, and there have been substantial improvements to the core gameplay as well as performance. I can now safely recommend purchasing this game to new players, and with that is the promise that whether you're a novice city builder or an enthusiast, you will find real enjoyment here. Cheers!I am incredibly sad to see even CS:2 fall into the "modern game release" nonsense of selling consumers unfinished products so we can be glorified beta testers. Just recently at the time of this review, the developers are talking about how they are working on over 100 "gameplay bugs". So you're telling me you had no idea the game ran this poorly? I was so excited for this game after the 600+ hours of CS:1 but they have really missed the mark with this one. Please do not waste your money. Wait for this game to be good, if it ever becomes good enough.Edit 3/25/24: The developers and publisher have completely lost touch with reality and are absolutely out of their minds regarding the state of the game and the recent launch of paid content including landscaping tools (palm trees). What a miserable experience this game has been so far. What little hope I had they would dig this game out of the grave they put it in on launch day is quickly dwindling. How sad.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game is really great right now,  but it has a lot of room for improvement and despite the good looks on a surface level, it has a lot of underlying bugs and balancing issues.1. Major aspects of the game need serious re-balancing / bug fixing such as garbage accumulation, neighbor imports / exports, education demand, abandoned buildings occurrences vs. RCI demand, population count vs. residential demand, natural disasters, traffic flow, traffic rules, pedestrian rules, and much more.2. There are minor visual bugs that should get fixed like water inside of tunnels, pedestrians walking along highway bridges / tram bridges, cars clipping through pedestrians and other cars, tunnel entrances getting decimated on certain terrain slopes, simulation lag, random crashes, autosave getting disabled after loading the game, and many others.3. There are a lot of missing QoL things that would make the game better such as a demolish button to demolish all abandoned buildings (or just re-haul how abandoned buildings work - right now it really makes no sense), more details about specific imports / exports and options to disable them (like neighboring cities dumping garbage in your facilities when there is an active road connection - currently no way to disable this), and more insight to specific needs of RCI demand (currently it is very vague), there are missing animations for a lot of things like soccer fields, car accidents, fire trucks, police incidents etc.4. Minor game play bugs such as Collider building using immense resources and monthly price of emergency shelters being astronomical. Other game play bugs include many achievements that won't activate when complete and hearse / ambulance popups show up way too quickly (they should only show up if the vehicle is taking a long time to get there but they show up after about 10 seconds), my map seems to always be raining (it would be cool if weather had an effect on driving - more car accidents / slower highway driving)5. Features I would like to see added - More city buildings that have better purpose than some included. Town hall and central bank are two examples of buildings that do almost nothing significant despite costing a lot per month. More recreational buildings like a marina, or other types of parks / rec items. Would be good to be able to delete additions to buildings as well as have some that you can really customize like a large park area with many additions. It would be good if abandoned buildings could get fixed up again after going abandoned so they wouldn't always collapse. It seems a bit weird that shortly after going abandoned it collapses. It would also be good to see new types of water transportation on a smaller scale. In addition to all this, there needs to be smaller versions of all buildings. For example, the elementary school is gigantic. Lets have a small school that holds 250 students and have it be 1/4th the floor size of the current one. Same with police and fire, they are just really massive and don't fit well in a downtown area. Also, the policies and district policies sections are extremely lacking, they need at least 20 more in each category to be sufficient.Despite all these bugs and issues, the game is still playable and still fun. I had a lot of fun with it but I will definitely give it a break until these major issues are resolved and new content added. 6/10. The most frustrating issues are the issues with garbage being imported into the city with no way to disable it and abandoned buildings not having any correlation to job demand, employment or RCI demand. Please fix those at the very least.EDIT:Removed my favorite radio ad

_childDocuments_.review: Cities:Skylines made me fall in love with a completely new genre of games. I was so excited to hear about it's continuation I eagerly bought an Ultimate edition of the next game. I kind of expected a launch full of bugs and performance issues. Treating players as free testers is the hallmark of modern game development. However, a few months went by since launch and even though it pains me a lot, I still can't recommend this game.1. Broken economy does leave you constantly wondering why game is not working as intended.2. Clunky roadbulding. Forget about perfectly horizontal roads sticking to desired elevation level, easy-to-integrate highway interchanges or connecting pedestrian paths to the ones included in a building.3. CS2 took some inspiration from community applauded mods, like TM:PE. However, their rendition pales in comparison with the original by offering very limited tools to control traffic. With mod support constatnly postponed, I expect this to be an issue for a long, long time...4. The game locks you in a certain type of gameplay. No bicycle lanes and only one option for pedestrian-only road, constant demand for low-residential and limited options for upscaling your buildings at certain points in game progression mean you're still going to end up with car-centric, highway-centric, rapidly sprawling city. You can kiss modern urbanism ideas goodbye.5. Region (USA/EU currently, hopefully more soon) is just a visual reskin. No building, intersection or road types are added, which is a bummer. EU cities don't feel EU-like.6. Missing features: quays (possibly added in DLC), bicycles, freely drawn parks, props, terrain painting and moreTL;DR This game does not bring joy despite it's huge potential. Be mindful of ongoing situation with bugs, delayed DLCs and mod support before deciding if you will trust this game producer with your money.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 2: (8/7/2024) The game is so bug ridden that at this point mods don't even help. Homeless people will swarm your city with no way to get rid of them, causing crime to increase and people to leave no matter what you do.Medical facilities will bug out and say that 10/10 ambulances are dispatched, but none of them leave the parking lot.Mail sorting facility still does absolutely nothing, it just sits there while cims complain about poor mail service.Cims still just make random U-Turns on the thruways and other illegal areas, with no way to prevent it, causing total gridlock as your traffic will stop completely to wait for that cim to make its illegal turn.Performance is still atrocious. For context, I have a Ryzen 7900X, 64 GB of RAM, a 4070ti, and the game is installed on a nvme SSD (990 EVO) and at 100k cims my game drops to less than 20fps. This is at 1080 resolution, when i can handle much more graphically intense games on 4k Ultra with 60+ fps (more commonly 130+) This is also with DLSS turned off because DLSS is horribly implemented in this game, DLSS will cause horrible ghosting literally everywhere in the game. Cars leave trails, the building overlay randomly renders, its all ass. This game is CPU intensive, so how come when i upgraded to a stronger CPU(5600x to a 7900x), my performance remained the same? Because optimization is horrible and they refuse to do anything about it so they can focus on a "console release"Beyond all of that, this game STILL has less than 1/10 of the content that CS1 has. Some basic QOL features, like the ability to control traffic signals, is still absent from the game. Oh and the promised free DLCs have been delayed, again. Theres like 30 assets for buildings in this game making literally every single street look the exact same. We were promised asset packs that just keep getting delayed over and over, like they aren't even trying.Thank god we have Cims with rendered teeth though. Cuz that was super important.Update: Still missing content. Traffic AI still completely sucks. Game crashes on almost a consistent manner. Playtime is only going up due to stubborness.After 67 hours and 12 cities started, tweeked, lost to game breaking bugs, I can not recommend the game in its current state. Traffic is hell again, and with no mod support there is no way to adequately address the traffic issues.Traffic will also just stop, causing bottlenecks that ruin your city. 1 car bugs out and stays in the middle of the road and traffic in both directions just stop. The only way to fix it is to find the bugged car, delete the road, rebuild the road. Good luck if the road has a lot of public transport lines on it.If you have 2 left turning lanes, 1 of the 2 of them will not move if the other one does, even if both lanes go to entirely different areas.Having a 5 lane one way highway, all the AI decides to use the left most 2 lanes only, causing massive traffic jams when there are 3 wide open lanes.Performance also is atrocious once you get more than 75k people. the sim speed on 3x with a population of 150k takes 10-15mins to build 1 building. thats real world time. Some people have reported populations of 250k+ taking as much as 45 mins per building.At the end of the day, just play CS1 until, i would bet, june of next year.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I have waited a long time and hoped that the game would be finished almost 10 months after its release. Unfortunately, I was proven wrong.The game frequently crashes back to the desktop, and unfortunately, auto-save is not pre-activated. Does this have something to do with performance?The performance itself is indeed dreadful once the city grows larger. And this with a 7950X3D, 64 GB RAM, and an RTX4090. That’s really bitter.What bothers me the most, however, are the strange menus and the awkward usability. I don’t feel that the developers have ever consulted with external users. For example, the routing of tracks on different levels was better implemented in other games 10-15 years ago. Buildings cannot be copied, and road traffic does not follow any dynamic logic.The game is basically fun until the next crash happens and a complex structure has to be rebuilt. At these moments, I just lose all enjoyment, and it turns into a negative experience.Here, the problem is the clunky usability combined with the fundamental system weaknesses.And given that we are in the year 2024, I miss many things in the game. For example, wind turbines in the water, building entire wind farms (placing each wind turbine individually is just a joke), upgrading residential buildings with photovoltaics, designing photovoltaic parks individually with significantly larger areas, much simpler routing of the entire infrastructure, or really the most basic like upgrading multiple buildings at once as in Anno. It is just so ridiculous that I have to click everything individually, and it feels like meaningless side quests in RPGs.The fact that this game is a so-called "full-price title" is bold. And the fact that it still has many essential problems almost 10 months later is simply outrageous.For the past 3 years, I have gotten used to not buying any game directly after release, and this once again confirms my approach. Probably, one should rather wait 1-2 years to make sure the developer doesn’t just abandon the game.Now, a bit of a "rant." Dear gaming industry, please start listening to the developers and the players again. Stop this marketing madness. YOU have created the situation in the gaming market YOURSELVES. Trust is simply almost nonexistent anymore, and therefore gamers prefer to play other games that are short-term and just "there." Why should I invest hours in a game like Cities: Skylines II or Starfield when I only have to deal with problems and FRUSTRATION? I’d rather play something that gives me a bit of fun for a short time and doesn’t make me angry in the end. I know that you earn a lot of money with the "quickly produce a lot" tactic. But that’s only short-term, and now we are seeing how it backfires.I hope that one day we can look forward to great big games again, where a lot of passion has been put into them, and it’s not about making shareholders rich.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is actually really solid. I can pull about 30 frames with a 1660 and for a city builder that's fine. Naturally I would like 60, and I'd be amiss to say the performance currently will be a deal breaker for a lot of people, but the gameplay makes up for it for me.It's quite a bit harder than CS1, as you actually have to think about things like supply/demand and imports/exports and other logistic problems. These mechanics ultimately existed in Cs1, but you didn't really need to pay attention to them as money past early game was super easy to come by. All you had to do was manage the traffic, water/sewage, power and RICO and the city would kinda just take care of the rest. Not the case in Cs2, as importing is not only more complex but also much more costly. Not producing certain good domestically results in manufacturers and stores having to import goods, which inturn hurts their profits, which in turn generates less money for you. Through these mechanics the city really manages to feel a lot more alive and dynamic than the previous entry, and I'm left optimistic for future updates and expansions.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really disappointed to have to write a negative review because like many others I really wanted to like this game. However, its so broken and frustrating that I have to leave this review. I can't believe how wrong they went with this. I would have preferred they continue to delay this game than to sell it at this state. I would plead to get a refund if this wasn't a gift.The economy is broken;-Ports, Airports and Cargo Rail fail to export goods properly under any conditions.-Randomly, after building a good economy industry taxation will start generating negative revenue at any positive tax rate and net you money while subsidising the industries at a negative tax rate. Then eventually it will flip back to the proper tax rate and they cycle will continue unless you place the industry taxation rate to 0%. Once you change it to 0% that entire industry will disappear from your city.-Industry zoning for wheat products will become so demanding that you could zone an entire city to farm wheat (as if you would even have enough fertile ground) and there will still be a massive amount of deficit no matter what you do.Building is crippling;-Additions built to city building, such as expanding a school with a sports field are impossible to move or alter without demolishing. This applies to all additions to all buildings.-There is so much demand for elementary schools that you could never possibly keep up, you whole city will become overwhelmed with elementary schools.-CONSTANTLY you have to demolish entire roadways, buildings and transit lines to accommodate a "overlapping items" error which often stems well beyond the node you're trying to alter or demolish. Often times it means ruining entire transit systems and moving or destroying existing infrastructure just to rebuild it in the exact same locations for things that make zero contact with the node your working on. Essentially you can't delete things without deleting everything around it as well. Sometimes you can't even demolish stuff and its just stuck there because it just moves the error node down the line until your left with a segment of road you can't connect anything to because of the error, and you can't delete either.-Building pedestrian pathways is neigh impossible based on the distance it takes to raise them to an elevation to cross a road. Pedestrian pathways can not span across all types of roads and you can't build supports in the centre of traffic circles making it even more impossible to make walk-able cities.Other bugs and issues-The Radio station is supposed to play "relevant" ads and reports based on issues in your city. In reality they just play random "traffic reports" "health care crisis" and "housing crisis" ads which bears no factual resemblance to your city. ITS CONSTANT. -The demand for commercial and low density residential are endless, however, building more than 1 commercial zone at a time leads to constant "not enough customers" conflicts because it'll only ever zone one type commercial build at a time and never randomise the industry that those commercial building align to. Zoning low density residential will ALWAYS eventually lead to "rent too high" conflicts which is sometimes as stupid as toddlers living on their own.With those smaller bugs STILL not addressed after being repeatedly reported by the community there is still no modding support! They totally pulled the rug out on us for the steam workshop with nothing in place to substitute!There are still performance issues with the game that go unresolved which are well documented and STILL not addressed.They are still trying to release DLC without addressing issues or adding mod support. Obviously they are trying to milk their cash cow before they deliver modding support which was promised upon release. Clearly they don't want to give you access to free community mods before they sell you more content.They promised massive game changing updates before the new year. Its Jan 27th, draw your own conclusions with that.I am very disappointed in their response and lack of action to remedying ANY issues to date. This game has strong beta vibes without being able to blame it on growing pains. Avoid this game until they do a massive overhaul. Not recommended, stick to cities skylines 1.

_childDocuments_.review: Bland, lifeless, and without soul. Those are the 3 words I'd use to describe this game.Which is interesting because Cities: Skylines I is such a widely regarded success, and I wonder where it went wrong for its sequel?Functionally the game is ridden with frame-rate issues and bugs on release, while it is getting better it cannot hold a flame to its predecessor. Gameplay-wise, its your goal to increase your population and city-size... That's it. In Cities Skyline there were challenges you could do to unlock buildings that significantly increased tourism, electricity output, etc., that were fun to attempt and do but this, you just tirelessly increase your city for seemingly no reason.Regardless, I'd suggest buying Cities: Skylines for a more refined experience where the DLCs add new gameplay features as oppsoed to whatever this is.
_childDocuments_.name: Cities: Skylines II

_childDocuments_.review: An under cooked glitchy version of what could have been an incredible game. Although the introduction of new zoned areas is incredible, the removal of taxes dependent on zoned area is absolutely stupid. The game only allows you to set taxes by education not district, wealth, or zoned area. You should be able to tax by all 3. Additionally it does not seem unreasonable by any means that bike lanes should be includes in the base game. A pivotal part of all cities is its bike infrastructure. Finally the bugs surrounding the economy are horrendous. Upon 20 hours into my first play through my city had a budget of roughly 10 million dollars monthly and expenses of roughly 9.75 million monthly. Then the economy glitched. Despite running a deficit on our beverages and pharmaceuticals (meaning we are importing more then we export) I raked in over 106 million monthly from these two industries. This game needs some serious fixing before it can be considered playable. Do not buy, yet.

Performance issues. the list of bugs goes on. CO and Paradox, I hope you have your devs working 24/7 right now just 6 days after launch. Patches should be being released daily to fix these enormous bugs.

Does not run well on minimum graphics on a mid-high end pc, and various stimulative systems in the game remain and are still currently broken. DO NOT BUY.
_childDocuments_.name: Cities: Skylines II

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime fan of the original Cities Skylines, I was eagerly anticipating the sequel, hoping for an enhanced experience with more features and smoother game-play. Unfortunately, Cities Skylines II has left me deeply disappointed and frustrated.The biggest issue I encountered is the overwhelming difficulty right from the start. In previous versions, building a city was a relaxing and enjoyable experience. In this sequel, however, I found myself struggling just to keep my city afloat financially. Within six hours and three attempts, I faced the same recurring problem: my city services cost more than I can possibly afford early on. This forces me to implement services before I'm financially prepared, pushing my city into a downward spiral of debt and inefficiency.Gone are the days of casually expanding my city and experimenting with various layouts. Instead, I'm forced into a constant battle with the budget, trying desperately to balance income and expenses from the very beginning. It feels less like a creative simulation game and more like a stressful accounting exercise. Every decision carries the weight of potential bankruptcy, leaving little room for creativity or experimentation.One of the joys of the original game was its accessibility and the ability to gradually unlock more advanced features as my city grew. In Cities Skylines II, it seems like every advanced feature is front-loaded, forcing players to grapple with complex systems and economic challenges right from the start. I found myself longing for the simplicity and gradual progression of the first game, where I could enjoy the process of city-building without constantly worrying about my city collapsing due to financial mismanagement.The introduction of new features that were previously only available through mods is appreciated, but I don't want to resort to "Unlimited Money" mode just to have a functional city that doesn't teeter on the brink of bankruptcy within a few minutes.Overall, my experience with Cities Skylines II was frustrating and disheartening. Instead of feeling like a master urban planner, I felt overwhelmed and defeated. If you're looking for a game that respects your time and allows for relaxed, creative city-building, I would recommend sticking with the original Cities Skylines or exploring other simulation games that strike a better balance between challenge and enjoyment. Cities Skylines II, unfortunately, missed the mark for me and left me questioning whether the sequel was a step forward or a misstep in the series' evolution.I really hope they can find a better balance, because I paid a lot of money for game I hate playing, and want to love it so badly.

name: I Am Dead
detailed_description: I Am Dead is a charming puzzle adventure game from the creators of Hohokum and Wilmot’s Warehouse about exploring the afterlife. Morris Lupton is the recently-deceased museum curator of the tiny island of Shelmerston who is reunited with the ghost of his dog Sparky, only to discover that a disaster is about to destroy his beloved island. Together, they must uncover Shelmerston’s ancient mysteries, prevent the island’s volcano from erupting, and save the place they call home. Morris and Sparky must unearth a number of Shelmerston's lost and scattered ghosts. To find them, the duo must visit the places they spent time in, dive inside the memories of the people who knew them best, and learn the stories of their lives. To help with their mission, Morris uses his newfound power that allows him to peer inside objects and people to reveal their contents and memories, like a supernatural X-Ray! Along the way you will discover many stories about the history and folklore of Shelmerston, and its cast of curious inhabitants and visitors: tourist finches, the fishfolk, morlos, and the Legend of Aggi - the one who originally silenced the volcano...

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 3(2020) is a remake of the Resident Evil 3(1999), and just like remakes of the RE1 and 2 tries to recreate the old survival-horror classics with new graphics, mechanics and small changes to overall structure. I have to preface this review with the statement that I never played the original Resident Evil 3, and probably never will, since I have no0 way or desire to try and launch without original harware. Unfortunately, compared to the incredible RE2make, R3make is kind of let-down. I guess it was released too early after RE2make, but this game just feels underwhelming in a lot of ways.The story of the game follows Jill Valentine, one of the protagonists of the original Resident Evil. Unlike most of the members of the S.T.A.R.S team, Jill got stuck in Raccoon City during the outbreak of the T-Virus, which turned most of the population into zombies. Making things worse, Jill becomes a target of the unstoppable monster, known as Nemesis, that was created to hunt down and eliminate all of the remaining S.T.A.R.S. members. Thee main objective is simple, get out of the Raccoon City and save as many survivors as possible. With the help of the small squad of the Umbrella Biohazard Countermeasure Service, and in particular Carlos Oliviera, Jill has to leave Raccoon City before it will get wiped out by the epidemic and following missile strike that will destroy all of the living things in the city.The story by itself is fine. The voice acting is great and characters don't do anything stupid. Nicholai is a wondertful scun of a villain, and Carlos is a great sidekick to Jill. it may lack some slower, somber moments of the RE2make, but considering that this is a different type of story where the main characters race against the clock it's fine.The graphics are incredible. The first time going through the dying Raccoon City you really get the feel that the world as we know it is ending. The glowing storefronts and dark streets lit with streetlights and police car signals just look great. Zombies roam around trying to eat something on it's path. Later portions of the game feature abandoned hospital and generic secret laboratory, that also look great and full details. Considering the visuals of the game, I have no complaints.The main roblems with the game are it's direction in gamedesign and levels. Firstly, the game doesn't follow traditional RE formula of searching for keys in an open environment for exploration. The game is mostly linear and broken up into small segments with minimal puzzles and exploration and can be completed in an hour for the first time playthrough and maybe ten minutes if you speedrunning. The exploration that this game offers boils down to tedious backtracking through the same level. There is no interconncted design with shortcuts multiple paths that you can take to avoid danger, only tight corridors and rooms where you have to fight enemies since you can't avoid most of them. The only segment that can remind you of classic Resident Evil is extremely short hospital section as Carlos, where you have to find key items, but it culminates in absolutely stupid defense section where you just shoot down hordes of zombies and couple of hunters.The game is also very easy and offers no real challenge. i played the game on the hardcore difficulty for the first time, and if RE2make kicked my ass multiple times with it's scarce resources and agressive enemies, R3make is just turns into very boring action game with spongy enemies. I will say that I don't have anything against action in Resident Evil or horror games in general. My favourite horror games are RE4 and Dead Space 2. But the fact that the game is built on the foundation of the RE2makewhere you ahd to ration every little thing and be very careful with your resources and inventory space, and just gives everything to you to plow through every situation just kills all tension. There was never a situation where I was actually starved of ammo or recovery items and had to adapt to the current situation. Most of the enemies just rely on gimmicky weak points, that you can exploit to get rid of them. Also one of the most hilarious new features of this game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dodge move. In short Jill can quickly avoid any attack by stepping out of the enemy's way and it givesyou a brief invincibility window to avoid an attack. By itself in vacuum I don't think it was a bad idea to add this feature, since the game is focused more on action, but where it get's stupid is when you realise, that perfectly timed dodge gives you Bayonetta-style slow motion effect, and with a knife gives you a powerful counter attack. I haven't played the game for a long enough time, but when I realised how this feature works, the only thought I had was "oh no". Main issue is, this opens up so many opportunities for exploites and easy ways out, that a survival-horror game should never have. Second playable character Carlos, has a shoulder tackle instead of a dodge move, which has more of an offensive option instead of defensive one, but timed perfectly with enemies attack it can be used as counter since Carlos punches enemy and knocks them down, opening them up for an attack.But the main dissapointment I had with this game is front and canter, proudly presented in the first minutes of the game and prominently featured in all of the promo materials of the game. I'm sorry, but Nemesis is a little b*tch in this game. Before playing this game, I thought he was more of a dynamic threat, appearing randomly in different parts of the game to ramp up tension, but in reality he is just a scripted jumpscare that annoys you a little bit and looks kind of intimidating for the first time. On the hardest available difficulty this idiot goes down to a single hand-grenade, drops you a lootcrate and disappears until the next scripted section.The bossfights are disappointing as well. They boil down to "shoot it until it dies" approach. It's not something you want to see from such a hyped up enemy. He's not scary or intimidating, he's just annoying. The third boss-fight is particularly bad, because it looks like designers realised that this section was too easy and just decided too add zombies that constantly spawn in on the edges of the arena and distract you from bullying Nemesis, that tries to hide from you behind electrically charged containers or something.the last problem I have with this game is the fact that it lacks in content compared to the other remake. There is no alternative character campaign with a different storyline, no challenging modes like The 4th Survivor or Mercenaries. The only thing this game offers is just higher difficulty levels and some bonuses that can make the game easier if you complete certain challenges. So the game by itslef is pretty short, you have no real motivation to go through unles you really loved the experience for the first time and want it all over again, but harder. i can understand that, but this is really not worth the price it asking for. This is a AAA release asking full price, but giving like half of the content a similar game offers. R3make is not the worst game in the series, but it is by far should have been more. i think the game was rushed in development, maybe that's why it feels so underwhelming, but in any case, get it only for a BIG discount and only if you are a die-hard fan of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Playtime- 6 hours (probably a bit less though)It's times like this that i wish that Steam had a mixed review button. On one hand this is a visually stunning game with fun gameplay that runs amazingly well. On the other it's a boring, 4-6 hour long story that they try to sell to you for 40 dollars. It tries to be a horror game and yet it's so unintentionally funny with how stupid it's enemies are, especially the main big bad Nemesis. Nemesis is always just spawned in for a scripted sequence that usually ends in a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ boss battle that shouldn't present any problem to you because you're constantly showered in ammo and resources anyways. Despite that, i do think this is kind of a good place to get into Resident Evil as a series as all the other games are so much better so you'll definitely appreciate them more after playing this.Not worth it for the base price but for the discounted price of 10 bucks (or if you can find a key for less) i say go for it.Final Rating - 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost; Yes, this RE game is quite short and yes, RE2 is far better, but that isn't to say RE3 is bad in any aspect.While it's short, it's action packed without a time to catch your breath (only in save zones like in RE2).The graphics are just as good, if not a tiny better than RE2's, with an inventory upgrade that looks cleaner.Difficulty is a bit higher than RE2's in its "Standard" difficulty, mainly because Nemesis is a tough mf.I never found myself running out of resources, which is good but also bad at the same time, so much so that I'd run out of inventory space often.I do wish it the game had more variety, like an extra bit of the story, extra modes or something, but no, you only get a shop to get 1 Jill costume and other utilities/weapons, which is sad to see.All in all, RE3 isn't as bad as people made it to be, but I'd recommend you buy it if it's on sale, it's not worth full price,

_childDocuments_.review: I'll just address the elephant in the room here by saying yes the game is short. Yes I would have preferred if it was DLC for Remake 2. All around it took me about 5 hours (in game timer) to beat. First play thru was on Hardcore mode so it actually took me about 10 hours to beat with re loading saves on death and whatnot. Length of the game aside I enjoyed this remake and it honestly was exactly what I was expecting in terms of quality. I do wish Nemesis was around more (specifically stalking in his 1st form). Other than those nitpicks I enjoyed this game and will probably 100% it in the next coming days and put it down for a couple years lol

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending this game is a little hard due to its high price and short game play. At the hardest difficulty unlocked during first playthrough, its a short four hour story. This can be compressed into 1.5 hours during your second playthrough now that you know all the paths and tricks. I loved the game, but wouldn't spend more than $20 on it. _childDocuments_.review: Capcom delivers Resident Evil 3 remake and makes it pure Eye Candy. Right from the start this game brings it. Your enemy The Nemesis has one goal in mind... your destruction. While he hunts you down you got to solve puzzles like the subway puzzle. Boss fights are against The Nemesis too and you are armed to the teeth so battles are fun. I rate this game 9/10. It loses a point because of the final fight with nemesis is hard to believe considering what happens to him in the previous battle. He should be dead. The final fight is epic though. Regardless of this I still recommend this game to Resident Evil fans. A must have in your library. :D
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: I'm on the fence about this one, wish I could give it a neutral review.It IS a good game, the graphics look great, there's plenty of production value and the gameplay is solid.The main drawback is that it is a HUGE downgrade from the Resident Evil 2 remaster. Short. Action Oriented and a LOT of missed opportunities.Don't get me wrong. RE 3 remastered IS a good game, if a bit short, but to me, it falls very short of the expectations set by its predecessor. If you're deciding on which one to buy, do yourself a favour and buy RE2. If you're still hankering for more, check this one out.Also, no Mercenaries mode? What the hell Capcom?
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, but at the same time a disappointing remake, it feels like its a shortened version of the original and Nemesis, which is the most iconic villain in the series for many people, was misused.The classic Resident Evil games were focused on puzzles and horror, Capcom kept those details for the RE2 Remake where we had Mr. X wandering around the map chasing after us for almost the entire game, but now on RE3 Remake it's quite different, most encounters with Nemesis are scripted and when he shows up everything we need to do is run forward through a linear path full of pyrotechnics and jumps that happen like cutscenes from the rebooted Tomb Raider franchise. I remember only two moments where Nemesis was really wandering freely around the map to chase me, and both moments were extremely short, those were also the only moments i felt frightened by him.In the end it feels like Mr. X was a more intimidating villain than Nemesis, the puzzles that were so characteristic of the classic Resident Evil games are almost nonexistent, some parts of the classic game were completely removed from this remake which is not good for various reasons, but mainly because the campaign only lasts from 5 to 6 hours, to close the negative details section about this game i wanna talk about the replay factor which is close to zero, because all the choices and alternative endings were removed.Now on the other hand, this Remake is not just disappointments, the gameplay remains incredible being basically the same from RE2 Remake, with the additional possibility to dodge enemy attacks, audio is still amazing and the graphics got even better.All the characters are better developed throughout the story, they all have more dialogues and amazing voice acting. Carlos has a bigger role on the story and both him and Jill are very likeable, strong and interesting characters, Nicholai is boring as hell and everytime he shows up you'll feel like you want to kill him.Overall its a decent game, it has a lot of wasted potential but i had fun playing it. From 1 to 10 i would rate it a 7 and i recommend it to everyone that is a fan of the series, and to those who liked RE2 Remake since their gameplay style is basically the same. If you want to play it because you love the classic RE3, well... just lower your expectations and maybe you won't be so disappointed by all the stuff that got removed.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: If you're the kind of gamer who plays a game through once and has no interest replaying for collectables or achievements, then the length of Resident Evil 3 Remake is going to disappoint. If you like to replay and collect everything and unlock all achievements... it's still short, but you'll like it a little more than the former group.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played the original, this game might disappoint you. But if you are like me and have never played the original, this is the game for you. A perfect follow up to resident evil 2 remake, fast paced and less scary. Don't expect too many scares, but expect the game to move from area to area at a faster pace. After all the point of the game is to get out of Racoon City before things go from bad to worse. I liked the game overall, the pacing and the structure and design of each areas. The only disappointing thing is the length, but i highly recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: This is a phenomenal game but a pretty mediocre remake. There really is no justifiable excuse for what Capcom keeps doing with these remakes they should far surpass the ps1 originals in more than just graphics technology is much better now. I actually love all of these remakes but it's just a shame they can't do better on a remake of 90s ps1 games and include all the necessary content from the originals something good always seems to be missing that was in the originals. I can understand cutting certain things to make a game better in a remake but in this it's clear they rushed it and cut a ton of good content to get it out faster. Entire sections and mechanics are missing like the choices and the clock tower section as well as other areas.With that out of the way it's still one hell of a game Capcom doesn't miss. The pacing and story are pretty much perfect imo even if Jills character is kind of inferior to the original as far as growth goes. She's a bad ♥♥♥♥♥ from the beginning she doesn't grow into one. But maybe it makes more sense considering she's already been through ♥♥♥♥ in re1 that was pretty bad. Carlos was fine. The story kept me interested I could see the plot twists from a mile away though blind.Now let's talk about the elephant in the room Nemesis. I think he was actually great and well made when not scripted. The scripted parts where cool but obviously being dynamic and free more would of been better and scarier he's only really set loose on you like one or two brief times. He was terrifying though in that encounter though he was way under utilized.The gameplay felt really good and smooth. I liked the dodging mechanic it felt really good when you got used to it. All the weapons felt really nice. The puzzles felt super simplistic for the most part. Weather that's a good or bad thing is up to you. The graphics are great like any other re engine game this game is pure eye candy.Honestly games like this are rare these days it's extremely short under 10 hours and pretty linear but in a world of open world games this is a breath of fresh air and a joy to play. It can often be picked up for cheap on a steam sale and it well worth it for the heavily discounted price. I'd much rather play this short game than some bloated open world filled with boring filler content. This is definitely worth the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: The game was way too short and Nemesis was a serious let-down, RE2's Mr. X was way more of an threat then nemesis, yeah, he has more mobility but so does Jill. Nemesis just never made me feel like I'd better run then fight. _childDocuments_.review: In a vacuum, this is perfectly functional Resident Evil game that would feel right at home during the earlier part of the last decade - where RE wasn't sure if it wanted to be action or horror. However, the reality of the situation is that Capcom had to not only live up to the legacy of Resident Evil 3, but the mirror-shine-polish that was the RE2 Remake. I'm just glad I read pre-release reviews before I played (and have not played the original), because otherwise the disappointment would be crushing. The reviews mentioned that there was very little of the clever open-ended level design found in 2, outright cut areas and concepts from the original game, and – most distressingly – Nemesis having the double-downgrade of not being as intimidating as both OG Nemesis and Mr. X. All of these ended up being true.This last point is mindbogglingly terrible on so many levels – remember Mr. X patrolling the area, making navigation instantaneously more nerve-wracking when you heard his footsteps? Remember how dynamic his appearances were? How you ended up dreading him? All that is gone. Replaced with utterly scripted sequences (save for one where he actually chases you around the area early in the game), sometimes employing the dreaded quick-time event that I thought Capcom – let alone every other game developer on the planet – got over around 2015. It’s honestly a travesty. It’s especially insane given how heavily Capcom marketed the game around Nemesis being a terrifying threat in the same vain as Mr. X – it’s flagrant false advertising. Evidently, Capcom had so little confidence in RE3 as a product that they bundled some asymmetrical multiplayer garbage, microtransactions included. At the time of writing, I have no interest in even touching it. I’m sure the community will last all of two months before dying out. Mercenaries would have been , Capcom. As a side note I think some of the horror aspects could have been saved with less music during gameplay – with the corny “tense” music playing in the background, it really does begin to feel like one of the lesser Resident Evils. However, at the end of the day, this is still a sequel to the most mechanically polished games in the series, and it inherits the basic mechanics that make it so appealing. Inventory management, weapon upgrades, a precision-centric aiming system – they’ve all managed to make it to 3 mostly unsullied. The guns are still fun to shoot and feel immaculately detailed. The game itself looks gorgeous, so good in fact that it almost feels like parody using these near photorealistic characters for a game that originally had faces comprised of four polygons and 50 pixels.Honestly, the structure of the game and the few new mechanics it adds are an interesting change of pace – if only they could have been expanded upon further. I like the idea of a more aggressive RE that doesn’t entirely buck the horror trend, with way more ammo and health given out per area. The dodge move is a neat way to encourage both defensive and aggressive play – dodge an attack at just the right time and you’ll be given a bit of bullet time to finish off your bewildered attacker. Carlos even gets the ability to clock enemies in the face with this ability, making it a ridiculously fun move to pull off.From what I understand, this was developed by Capcom’s B-team, instead of the A-team that brought us RE2. First off – I can only imagine how insulting this would be to RE3’s original fans. Secondly – I can only hope that their A-team is working on a Resident Evil that will knock our socks off.  EDIT: Huh, looks like they are.You know how RE2 is now going for 20 dollars? Wait until RE3 hits that. For 20 bucks, I’d dare say RE3 is an above-average game, but 60 dollars is a ridiculous price for a cut-down sequel with an average first playtime of 6 hours and a bargain-bin multiplayer mode. I do recommend this game – 6 months from now.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 3 (2020), despite being a remake of one of RE's titles from the 90s, feels more like a spin-off of Resident Evil 2 (2019), it's remake predecessor, than an outright narrative deserving of its own entry. Despite its lineage in the same horror and puzzle stylings of its predecessor, the tone of Resident Evil 3 is, from the get-go, an action oriented affair.That's certainly not a bad thing. In fact, there's a lot of moments in RE3 where you're reminded, quite wistfully, of Capcom's capacity to present a dynamic, dramatic narrative, more mindful of its villains and heroes than the creeping dread of RE and its sequel (finding a great balance, in my view, in RE4). But the result produced in Resident Evil 3 is the tone and pace go hand-in-hand and you quickly find yourself flying through environments in Raccoon City. There's a lot that I like about that though and having a greater diversity of environments (and spending less time in the drab corridors of underground Umbrella bases) is always a plus. Coupled with the relentless pursuit of Nemesis (not quite as meaningfully relentless or memorable as Mr X though) is a great, cinematic struggle between Jill and the villain.I'd certainly say that the length of the game is a bit of an issue, depending on how much you're willing to pay for Resident Evil 3. While the game does provide incentives to fall into additional playthroughs, it doesn't quite have the spread of base content that Resident Evil 2 arrived with. Emphasising this is the uneven split between Jill Valentine and Carlos Oliveira. The writing has the purposeful charm to turn its cheesy 90s progenitor into a sincere but still fun narrative, but this is a much more singular story all together, passing back and forth between the two characters a handful of times, without the benefit of another run of RE2 as Claire/Leon, giving you 6-8 hours of playtime depending on your speed. I finished my first playthrough of RE3 in a little over three and a half hours.So my recommendation here is largely conditional. If you liked Resident Evil 2, you're likely going to enjoy this too. For its regular price of £49.99, it's an absolute no-go. For the present discount (with the showcase of RE8), £16.49 is reasonable enough, but I wouldn't pay £20 for this.I really enjoyed it, partly because the RE Engine is absolutely beautiful, there's some great performances from the voice actors across the board and the narrative, while a bit begrudgingly straightforward, is still fun and moves along well enough to fit its pacing and tone. No one can doubt the earnest efforts of Capcom to try and reinvent these games and shape them into experiences for a new generation, that's something to be celebrated over everything else, as it's not something we've ever been fortunate enough to see done so well, so consistently.

Nemesis redesign is so bad it almost makes Jill's redesign look inspired by comparison. 5. Nemesis is VERY poorly utilized in this iteration. Went from Mr. X on steroids to a glorified set piece instigator some 20 years later. 6. An hour shorter than the original version, with only a fraction of the content to boot. 7. Many areas from original have been cut from the game, making this 60 dollar purchase seem like overpriced DLC to RE 2: Remake. 8. Nightmare mode and Inferno mode are gimmicks at best9. Very little replay value, especially compared to the original titles (one unlockable outfit! In the words of Jill herself:  "Are you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ kidding me?")Let me be clear before I get into the nit and gritty: I enjoyed the three hour ride. I enjoyed perforating zombies with shotgun shells and dodging Nemesis like Jill was a DragonBall Z character. But this was unequivocally not worth 60 dollars. Classic locations from the original are outright gone, characters are butchered beyond all recognition upon the altar of censorship, and the game overall just feels like a husk of what Resident Evil 3 used to mean to me. Like a zombie, if you will. I mean, the thing is clearly moving on two legs and seems sentient. But it's just a walking corpse. It is undeniably bereft of anything that could be considered a soul. Jill now curses more than a sailor on shore leave, and her new personality is abrasive to say the least. I don't mind a few F bombs myself, but Jill Valentine has always been classier than this, and that goes for both REmake and the original Resident Evil 3. The opening section is very interesting though in what it supposedly foreshadows or tries to set up. But like the remake itself, it feels incomplete, like a question half-pondered. I could write a 20 page thesis paper on everything so incredibly wrong about this new Jill, along with the story beats and her subsequent character interactions. But I know the internet doesn't have that kind of attention span, so I'm going to end my criticism of this Jill impostor here.  I will say though, that Jill now feels like every other run-of-the-mill female protagonist/co-star in video-games nowadays. And her VA can't act. Moving on. As far as gameplay goes, I don't have any particular qualms. It's RE 2 Remake but with added mobility, which is welcome.  But certain bosses on Nightmare or Inferno mode feel like they weren't balanced at all. Let me explain using a simple term: stun-lock. When Jill gets hit on the higher difficulties the first time, you feel fine because you know you ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. But it's when enemies suddenly have the power to hit Jill repeatedly while leaving her UNABLE to dodge or counterattack, the frustration is instantaneous and gets exponentially worse with each passing death.  There is barely any exploration in this game. During the second half of the game, I felt like I was playing Resident Evil 6 again, only with slightly more polish and budget. RE 3 OG was certainly more action-oriented compared to its predecessors, but the developers of this remake took to that approach a bit too emphatically.  The Raccoon City segment feels like it should have been at least an hour longer, and with so many of the other classic locations removed, the game will more than likely end before you realize it. Oddly enough, it is during the Carlos sections that you get the most opportunity to explore. This is great and all, but I was hoping to do the same thing as Jill. Don't get me started on the replay value, because compared to the many other titles RE 3: Remake has less substance than a single-celled organism. Only one unlockable outfit, and it looks like a cheap cosplay attempt at the classic Jill Valentine from the mansion days. Game can be finished 100% in the span of a weekend.  Even if you discount the unlockables and weapons with infinite ammo, there is still very little to call the player back for repeat play-throughs. Gone are the branching paths, the exhilaration of Nemesis constantly being on your heels, and the sense of exploration and nuanced puzzle-solving.  Again, I enjoyed the ride, but in hindsight, I shouldn't have paid more than 20 dollars for this. It is as clear as a Resident Evil epilogue daybreak that this game was given nowhere near the same amount of care and love as RE 2: Remake, and it shows in almost every facet of the game.  Like going on a ride at a Disney theme park you enjoyed the time for what it was, but still end up feeling hollow and fleeced by the end of it.  If this game was  20 dollars, you would see a thumbs up instead of a thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 2 remake was a brilliant modernization of an old classic. Nemesis was a random encounter but in this remake he serves more as a set piece which is weird considering we had the tyrant walking around in RE2 remake. To focus on the positives along with what the original was, the game is more action focused with ammo more readily available. It takes a more linear route with less backtracking or rather it blocks you from going back at certain points. Puzzles are dramatically absent with the game always pushing you forward. The sad reality is I went in with bloated expectations given the quality of both RE2 and its remake. RE3 just is the lesser of the two games and can be considered a swan song for the series before it moved away from the survival horror genre.
