_childDocuments_.review: I know I might catch some flack for saying this, but I like the Original RE3 just a little more than the original RE2. With that said, I feel that the RE2 remake is better than RE3 remake but not by much. I'll deliver my spoiler free review and include spoilers at the end for people to read.Resident Evil 3 is a third-person over the shoulder shooter survival horror. You play as RE1's returning character Jill Valentine, the game starts and you are immediately  attacked by a hulking super zombie-mutant named Nemesis, however this attack is very scripted and acts simply as a rough introduction to the game. The opening of the game right after meeting some soldiers you get access to a somewhat open (and small) area of Raccoon City (a fictional mid-western town).The game-play is almost similar to RE2 remake except for the knife/grenade defense weapons just becoming regular weapons and the introduction of a dodge system that when executed perfectly gives you a pseudo bullet time auto lock on the attacking zombie/monster. Puzzles are completely absent from the game (except for maybe one near the end but it was pretty simple to solve, at least for me). Nemesis behaves somewhat like Mr. X for the first section of the game, after his first actual encounter he will stalk you from area to area and unlike Mr. X, he does not follow sound clues and moves much faster being able to jump from behind you to in front of you at a moments notice. Nemesis only stalks you for a little bit though so it is not too overbearing or overwhelming.  The game does have 3 levels of difficulty at the start and two locked difficulties that I ended up really enjoying more than I thought.The story is alright, most of the story is found through all the files you find scattered throughout the game with some exposition given from dialogue exchanges between characters in and out of cut-scenes, almost all of which can be skipped.  The original RE3 I do not recall having a really deep story but I do remember a somewhat forced romance at one point (from one the play-throughs) between the two main character which is almost completely absent from the remake, I feel this was for the best as now instead of being lovers they feel more like people working together to survive. Very earlier on and at the halfway point it does become apparent that Jill does seem to suffer from PTSD from the events of RE1 which i do feel adds a sprinkle depth to her character.To sum it up, its a good game. I really liked it and if you are reading this and still on the fence about getting it, then just wait for a sale.***SPOILERS***

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 3 ReviewOverview:Resident Evil 3 is Jill Valentines story and she has never looked or signed it better. Jill is the stone cold professional rolling her eyes at the direction of UBCS whenever she getsyet going out of her way to protect the vulnerable whenever she can one scence towards the end of the story wil have you punching in the air as she steps up to destroy everyoneany everything standing in her way all while cursing and being sarcastic. Every character performed their all regardless of how much screen time they had.The real show-maker is definetly Nemesis he has numerous transformations and brings a different weapon or form to the party at different parts of the story. However it is the earlyparts of the game showing up on the streets and chasing Jill Valentine through Racoon city with his tentacles, his fists and showing up right in front of Jillthat makes him terrifying. It is kind of a shame that Nemesis dosen't feel as terrifying as Mr X in Resident Evil 2 most probably because you don't spent a lot of time with himwhile he is chasing Jill, Nemesis abillity to track and hunt down Jill definetly needs some improving: mostly the amount of time he spents chasing Jill and the speed of how fast he can catch up to Jill, maybe even the abillity to break into places you don't expect such as every single safe room and the walls of the shops in Raccoon City where you would normally expect him to walk in polietly through the front door.Atmosphere:Unlike Resident Evil 2, Resident Evil 3 replaces the rooms of the police station with the streets of downtown in Raccoon city, the time you spent in Racoon City is prob the most funin the game, not only you start in Jills apartment but the streets of Racoon city are packed with the undead, most of the citizens are most probabaly going to wind up dead, correction undeadStory:Resident Evil 3 takes place either side of its predecessor Resident Evil 2 in the former stars agent Jill Valentine suspended after the Spencer mansion incident that is in the events of the 1st Resident Evil is active in a rapidy unraveling Raccoon City before Claire Redfield and Leon Kennedy. But due to a bit of a time jump in the middle of the game, leaves the city after those twohave long vacated the area, Jill is not working alone however, early on she is rescued from a potientally dangerous situation by UBCS aka Umbrella Bio-Hazard counter measure service squadmember Carlos Olivier and after a rocky introduction (Umbrella is the company that cause the virus outbreak) the two worked together to get out of the city in two pieces.Gameplay: Exploring every inch of Racoon city that is not on fire is fun as Jill does what she can to survive and take whatever loot that is left and get everyone away to safety the pace never lets up as you go up toe to toe against each enemy you encounter. Most enemies that is not your regular city zombie has only a few weakness that you have to take note of in order to take them out without wasting bullets.Jill's new dodge abillity and her larger arsenal of weapons makes perfect sense for a story that is taking place in a city that is being overrun. Zombie are far greather in numbers and things can go wrong if you get cornered or if you are not paying attention to your surroundings. Pros:-Jill Valentine-Good Story and Gameplay-fantastic atmosphere that suits the setting of the story-In game Characters-After game content: Unlockables, and two new difficultiesCons:-Game and time spent with Jill Valentine feels too short-Definetly could have mutiple endings to epand more on the gameplay-Nemesis dosen't feel as strong and scary as expectedOverall:Resident Evil 3 is Jill Valentines story and she has never looked or signed it better however, considering what Capcom has managed to achieved with Resident Evil 2, things such astime spent in the story feels very short and it could have been better if mutiple endings were included in the game. Nemesis does not feel as powerful as Mr X in Resident Evil 2 and definetly needs some improvement to his abillities mostly chasing Jill in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a missed opportunity...I have never played the original RE3 so there is no question of petty nostalgia getting in the way of my playthrough but boy after the pleasant surprise that was RE2 I was expecting so much more from this one.Simply put:Storythe story is serviceable if not a bit generic but I never play an RE game for the story (except 7). The characters though are a bunch of hollow husks with very little personality or anything to get me invested in them. Kendo (the gun shop owner) has more character in the 1-minute cut-scene he appears than any of the other characters.GameplayThe controls are tight and responsive, and the moment to moment gameplay feels good. The zombies are amazingly well rendered and killing them is a blast.GraphicsThe graphics are great, each monster feels appropriately juicy when you shoot into them and the general appearance is quite stellar with plenty of environmental detailsSoundThe sound is good, special mention to the ambiance in the hospital that kept me on edge throughout.Game DesignHere is where it all comes tumbling down, the game design is horrendous. Here is a list of my largest gripes:I regularly found myself just missing important items and notes throughout the game.Regularly, new enemies would show up, with no clear explanation or introduction, creating a lack of tension and build-up, and no clear path to defending myself (after wasting nearly all my pistol ammo on those white zombies I had to shelve my pistol for the rest of the game due to lack of ammo, right after getting an upgrade)Some monsters would do a special cut scene move and one-shot me even if I was at full health, and with no clear windup animationNemesis is a joke, gone is the tension of hearing the enemy coming or making tough decisions to keep from attracting their attention, this guy runs after you for 5 minutes and then you fight him during set-piece arena battles.....awesome...Exploration becomes redundant (and useless) because Capcom reimplemented the cleared room color system they introduced in the RE2 remake - which tells the player if they have cleared the room of items directly in the map menu. Usually, in RE games, the environment loops on itself and grows as the player unlocks doors and explores the area. New enemies spawn in places you have visited previously to keep you on the edge of your seat. Instead, here you have 2 very small areas that can be explored and the most interesting one was in the free demo, everything else is a linear playthrough.Verdict: Don't buy it!Get the free demo, play it, imagine how the rest of the game could be based on the demo's design.Congratulations! You have probably imagined a better version of the game than crapcom was capable of putting together.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let my play time fool you, i tried to pace myself with this game. But not only did i complete the game, but got over half the game's achievements, all in 5 hours. This game should be called RE 3: The Director's Cut, with 'cut' being the operative word here. Yes cut-content and an embarrassingly short campaign is the item of the day here, coupled with a shallow and incredibly sub par multiplayer mode in an attempt to save face. At its core, RE 3 is unquestionably a fun third person shooter. Shooting zombies and hitting Nemesis in the face with a bazooka has never been more satisfying. Jill and Carlos feel good to control, especially given how third person camera angles can sometimes be hit or miss with mouse and keyboard (I go back and forth on it personally, but this game feels good to control no matter what you're using.) Plus in comparison to the playstation, the controls here are a godsend. I had almost zero technical issues to speak of, which is good seeing as how this game barely had a 2 year development cycle. But there is no way i can justify anyone buying this game for $60, i feel cheated and i spent $40 on this game! Replayability for this game is low to average at best, with that replayability being present solely due to higher difficulties and its short length, not due to any desire or feeling like you could explore the game further. Compared to the far superior RE 2 remake, my experience felt like i was zooming through a tunnel in a car at 100 mph, with barely any time to take in the gorgeous environments and characters that i see fading in my rear view mirror. The next thing i knew, the game was over. I'm not gonna go into how much content this game cut, there are plenty of other reviews on Steam alone that have covered that. To keep it short, the cut content is A LOT. For context, the original game had 8-13 hours worth of content, this game has only 5. So, faced with a deadline and a lack of content, Capcom decided to make a foolish mistake that a lot developers do: pack in a "free" multiplayer mode that is more shallow than a kiddy pool. Overall, the multiplayer feels superfluous within a series that is almost solely single player, serving only as extra padding and a justification for its 60 dollar price tag. If it was a choice between the cut content and the multiplayer mode, i would pick the cut-content every single time.Like what did you expect me to use this multiplayer for Capcom, to wipe my butt with it? I would but I'm afraid that my butt cheeks would chafe. If this had come out as a $30-$40 expansion to the RE 2 remake, I wouldn't be as harsh on this game. My main hope is that Resident Evil 8: Village follows more in the footsteps of RE 7 and RE 2 remake than this game.6/10- Don't get this for $60 unless you are die-hard RE fan and you HAVE to play it. Otherwise, just wait until its 20 or 30 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: I currently have 18 hours played, and I've beaten the assisted, standard, hardcore, nightmare & inferno difficulties. With that being said, I'm going to list my personal pros & cons with this game:Pros:- Amazing soundtrack- Fun boss battles- Graphics are good for the most part, besides the 30 fps zombies in the distance- Voice acting & character movements look great- Gameplay feels smooth, and the dodge mechanic is pretty fun once you master it- Multiple difficulties to try out - The game is short (I beat it in about 5 1/2 hours on my first run). The RE2 remake was pretty short too, but I think it's more noticeable in the RE3 remake because they cut out some locations from the original game. I list this as a pro because this game doesn't overstay its welcome. Even though I would have preferred a longer campaign, this short and sweet/fresh experience satisfied me still. Cons:- This is half pro/half con, but the fact that they cut a lot out of this remake that was in the original 1999 RE3 is a bummer, but in addition, they also reworked the whole game, so it's a fresh experience for new and old re3 fans.- It's 2020... I expected Nemesis to be a little more intelligent and stronger than the original RE3, but in this remake, he goes down with 1 grenade & mainly stalks you in the beginning of the game. After that, he just becomes scripted boss battles. (However, his boss battles are extremely cool). - Where are the puzzles? There are only like 5-6 puzzles max, and most of them aren't even actual puzzles that require thinking. It's mostly "Go pick up this item, and put it here". There was only one puzzle I did that actually took some time, but overall, the puzzle aspect of this game is little to non-existent. - The cutscenes are intense and good looking, but there are way too many scripted moments and cutscenes in this game. Resident Evil isn't known for that in my opinion. While I still enjoyed watching them, I prefer to have control over my character most of the time, rather than the game play it for me. VERDICT: 9/10- As a fan of resident evil for over 16 years, I ended up really enjoying this game. I'm a completionist, so I'll be getting all of the achievements and doing all of the in-game challenges. While 60 bucks is a little too much for a game this short, we also have resident evil resistance included. That game isn't everyone's cup of tea, but at least it's included to help kill time. If you don't plan on playing resistance, then you might want to wait for a sale on RE3. Not a perfect remake, but it's definitely one worth remembering.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as making a recreation of the original game; this fell a little short in terms of story as many parts from the original seem to have been cut. That being said it is still good and will provide you with some solid entertainment but retro fans of the originals may feel somewhat letdown.  This is a survival horror games in which you will need to complete objectives, solve puzzles and conserve limited recourses to fight the un-dead in Raccoon City. At the time of this review there is only a single player mode in which you play from a third person point of view with the options for many varying difficulties to challenge yourself with. It is easy to control with the same control schemes as previous RE:Makes and during the time I played I found no bugs. Visually this game is very dynamic and definitely hits the mark at impressing the audience. There are multiple options in which you can tweak your graphics so you can make sure that the settings are right for you. I personally hate motion blur and always appreciate a game that gives me the option to disable it. The soundtrack is solid with high pitched swells and chase music that will put you on the edge of your seat. Sound FX are clear and well thought out including with the occasional jumpscare accompanied with a terrifying burst of sound or two. I played this 4 times in just under 30 hours with my first play through lasting around 8 hours whilst fully exploring. Then my final play though was under 1.5 hours. Replay value is definitely there if you want to go for the achievements or unlock cheats from the shop which will be available upon your first completion of the game. This can add modifiers to the game including weapons with infinite ammo for very fun playthroughs.All in all I really enjoyed this even if the story was a little short compared to the original, the gameplay is fun and will definitely appeal if you are a fan or survival horror games or even just action/adventure games, the graphics and sounds are also good and work well together. Personally I DO recommend this game but if you want to get a little more value out of your money; I would wait and pick this up on sale.

I know some people wanted him to be more like the Alien from Alien Isolation but in my opinion that would have been awful, so I'm glad the devs didn't go that route.If you enjoyed RE2R you will love RE3R as it's better in every way.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I hate to say it, this wasn't what I'd hoped for out of Resident Evil.I love the series. It's my favorite of all time, and there was a lot of good things. But Nemesis was negligible, showed up way too fast, there was hardly any tension building, and after the first sequence and outside cutscenes characters' dialogue and movements are clunky and weird and kind of ruin the fear factor of it all. The fact that the character you're on more is starved for inventory space while the other gets all the hip pouches you could ask for is frustrating, especially since she gets more weapons. And cramming a room at the end of the game with invincible zombies that look completely different but aren't explained in the game and are I think explained somewhere back in the series, new people are confused and lost about this pretty annoying enemy, especially when five of them are crammed in a room you can barely fit one person through at a time and forcing players to go through it several times. The first encounter with Nemesis was a cake walk, the next two were cuts and pastes of each other, and the final wasn't very intense and also over too fast, with only two uses of the mechanic to kill him. The exposition was all over the place, clunky, and too convenient to be taken seriously, and there was hardly a story to speak of crammed into hardly 5 hours of a game.However, as a standalone, Resistance is very cool and a neat new concept and a breath of fresh air to the survival action series, and I wish- no, PLEAD for Capcom to release it as a standalone. Let people dodge the mediocre campaign and get to the honestly really cool and new stuff.I'm sorry, RE. I love it to death, but I'm very unfortunately disappointed. Wait for a sale, or pick up Resistance if it somehow gets detached from being sold along with RE3.

However, in the case for this game, it seems the formula was just butchered away. I played through this game three times, taking my time mind you, and my longest playtime was about 4 hours 30 minutes. If Capcom thinks tacking on a mediocre multiplayer makes up for an unfinished game, then I fear for future "remakes". That all being said, I do recommend this game--with extreme cautiousness. It's still a generally fine experience and it can be fun to play, but I would highly recommend purchasing it while it's on sale. It's good for a nice weekend, nothing more.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, if you liked the RE2 Remake, you'll probably find something to like about this game. But I can't in good conscience recommend that anyone buy it at full/launch price. In the RE2 remake, you got Leon's campaign, Claire's campaign, as well as some other bonus scenarios. But with this game, you get one very short, underwhelming campaign. I'm not amazing at RE games, but took me roughly 5 hours to complete on standard difficulty, including deaths. With how linear and predictable the campaign is, there's really not a whole lot of reason to replay it. Hopefully there's some sort of free DLC to make purchasing this feel worthwhile, but who knows. When I finished RE3, I thought it was decent. It had been a while since I finished RE2. But going back and playing through RE2 after finishing this, I'm reminded of just how amazing and atmospheric that game was, and how RE3 pales in comparison. I definitely understand that the original version of RE3 was more action and less horror, but this game feels like a mediocre action movie. RE3 feels like a cheap, rushed DLC campaign, a lazy cash-in on all of the love from the previous game, not a full game. With that, if you're thinking of buying RE3, buy RE2 instead. If you already own RE2, just play through that instead of buying this. I promise you'll have a way better time.If you're desperate for more Resi, then I guess this game will suffice, just wait for a sale. After how amazing RE2 was, this game is extremely disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mixed bag to me and its hard to judge becouse of that, in the end I will judge the whole game not just what I enjoyed about it.The game is short on content, and the content that it has feels unfinished in some respects.At some point I had to open a text file and write down some of the bad things that I encountered while playing, becouse there was so much of it.In short the game feels rushed and unfinished for the price they ask for it.+ World looks amazing+ Music and sound is great+ Voice acting is great+ Story telling is amazing both dialogue and text files- Has some bugs (not game breaking for me)- Loot locations and amounts make no sense- Fight mechanics have flaws, bossfights break immersion- Scripted dammage that you can't avoid & animations that you can't break- Some mistakes were made in the worldbuilding and cutscenes- Game slows you down to drag out content- Short 4-12 hours of gameplay (vast pace vs search everything)The game has a great feel to it, eerie yet enticing to enter and explore. The grafics are on point most of the time, and fit a game of this time. Comming from a franchise that is great in city design, this game draws from that and does not disapoint. Some areas will be familiar to those that played RE before, yet felt new and refreshing enough to me.The worldbuilding has some flaws where the developers have most likely used props from previous games, there isn't much of it, but it was immersion breaking to me at a few points. Where a sign or poster is such low resolution that you cant read it, while every other sign or poster arround it is newly made and high resolution. There is also a point where you pick up a picture frame commenting that Clair is in it, while the picture only shows a group of male soldiers.The Cutscenes are mostly well made and realy add to the game, however there are points where a weapon gets trown away and disapears in that same cutscene, and someone shoots with an empty gun without picking any ammo up.Loot is in the weirdest places, where a locked weapon save or crate got a single box with a few rounds of ammo. While a hospital treatment room has grenades and ammo on the food and treatment tables. Healing items aren't always spread arround logicaly, you might get tons of healing items at places where there is no combat, yet where there is combat you might struggle finding any. Some loot is randomized, this might be the issue.I have also noticed that some paper maps can be interacted with, and will update your digital map, while the exact same type of maps in other places can't be interacted with.Some areas are blocked in a stupid manner with small objects or ankle high plates of wood blocking large openings or passages. You can't jump over logical items/places.The sound and music in the game felt great, from the background music to the voiceacting, it realy pulled me into the game.The gameplay is realy a mixed bag for me, its challenging and engaging, yet at the same time flawed and annoying.Zombies heads have hitpoints, yet every zombie has a wildly different amount of hitpoints, some might take 2 shots, while the exact same type of zombie might stand up again after 12 shots. There is no animation nor model in place for a dead zombie only for critical hits, so the player gets no feedback what so ever.The combat finds place in a lot of confined places, sometimes as big as 3-4m2, yet you can't aim at your feet, this becomes a problem when you need to make sure a zombie stays down.Zombies dont react from getting shot in most cases, and attack animations can't be broken. A downed zombie that is not dead can be shot without reacting, while slashing a knife at that same zombie makes it stand back up, as if you hurt it.Zombies have attack animations that take arround 3 seconds and can't be interrupted, even longer if you get hit, yet the game tells you to click your left mouse button to ''break free'' when a zombie grabs you.Zombies will break through doors that you have to open with a handle or doorknob, while doors that you push open (like in hospitals) they can't get through and walk away from. Creating a wierd sight, when you stand in a doorway and move forward and backwards.Boss fights are just mini games of hit and run, loot scattered in the boss fight area breaks immersion. Becouse of attack animations, you can get stunlocked or blocked from moving.The dodge mechanics are terrible and for me immersion breaking, you run faster than you dodge out of the way of an attack and even stop walking or running for a while afterwards, just standing there casualy like nothing is going on, breaking down the speed of gameplay.The game throws a lot of items at you to open doors, passages and containers, and its inventory management I quite enjoyed, yet you have to sellect the items to use every time from the inventory, where a simple 2 second cutscene would have worked better.The game also stops when using those items, even if you are in combat.Those items have to be discarded manualy every 30+ of them, while you magicaly know you can't use them anymore for the rest of the game for some reason.The game feels like its made to slow you down, and with its limited amount of content that makes sense.The game has rendering bugs, that happen when you go through a doorway into a new room, showing a dark grey void before rendering the area again. This happens a few times and i have managed to reproduce it every time. The game also has some locations where the camera clips through walls, and the game glitches objects in the map sometimes.A finished AAA titel priced at 60 euros, with only 4-12 hours of gameplay, should not have bugs in it, especialy those that could have been fixed by playtesting.The game can be replayed at a different dificulty setting, with some starting items and/or to unlock achievements. No actual content will be added to the game, so this wont be for everyone.This game is a strange one, where some of the development team have delivered content well and truely beond expectations, other parts seem unfinished or rushed. The game also feels like it hasn't been properly playtested, or the dev team didnt have a gamer on board that looks at details.I cant recommend this game with a straight face, so i wont. Did i enjoy the game? Yes i did. Was it becouse i already love the franchise and gametype, absolutely.Do i recommend this game, to someone who wants to play RE for the first time at any price point? No.Do i recommend this game to someone who already likes the franchise, yes for 8-12 euros to someone who is mildly interested. And maybe 20-25 euros if you are a die-hard fan, but be warned that you might get disapointed.

_childDocuments_.review: When Capcom announced they'd be remaking Resident Evil 2, I was apprehensive. I doubted they'd be able to do the game justice. News of the radical departures Capcom was taking from the original just added fuel to my concerns. Yet, my concerns proved unfounded. Capcom produced an excellent Remake. Could they repeat that feat? I wondered when I heard about this remake. I'm afraid this time around, with the Resident Evil 3 remake, the answer is a bit more complex.Resident Evil 3 takes place before and after Resident Evil 2's story, during the T-virus outbreak that turned Raccoon City into Zombie Central. The original was the most actionized game in the classic trilogy, giving the signal for the direction the series would subsequently take. Still it was very much a classic Resident Evil game. The remake takes all that action up to eleven. It's not even trying to be a survival-horror game. The already rudimentary puzzles have been effectively taken out. Options and branching paths have also gone the way of the dodo. Nowhere throughout the game is there any real pressure or fear. Instead you get a completely linear and (relatively) bombastic action-shooter. Entertaining? Yes. Faithful to the vision of the original? Hardly. Good? Hm...The action focus permeates the game. Positively and negatively. The attitude of the protagonist is a good example of the tone of the game. Jill is for the most part confident, at times even assertive. She knows what she wants and won't be deterred. Narratively, this is justified. Jill isn't some greener than broccoli rook like Leon, or a rank-amateur like Claire. She is a battle-hardened veteran, a member of an elite police unit. Plus, she has earned her zombie apocalypse stripes during the Arklay mansion incident in the first game. Jill is overall a great character. Even so, the game does take it too far at times. The things Jill survives, during cutscenes, are simply impossible for a normal human. Cars crashing down several stories, rockets exploding right next to her. It's too much. Makes me wonder why Umbrella bothers with bioweapons when they could just clone Jill.Visually the game is a treat. Yes, it plays more like Resi5 rather than the game its based on, but it's still wearing the right clothes. Action-focused or not, this is still good ol'Raccoon city. With its RPD, slow lumbering zombies, enormous sewers and secret high-tech underground labs. Not some jungle filled with Rambo zombies wielding assault rifles that leads towards a rock punching duel inside a volcano. This is still the real original setting and style. Only prettier than ever. Jill and the other characters look and feel right. With the exception of a few strange facial animations here and there, I have no real complaints on the aesthetics front. In fact, some of the deviations from the original here were good. I enjoyed the new more distrusting dynamic between Jill and Mikhail for instance.On the other hand, the action focus hurts the titular Nemesis, making him one of the game's greater disappointments. When compared to Mr.X from the previous game, that much more so. Nemesis is the bioweapon that pursues Jill throughout the game. At least narratively. But gameplay-wise you don't see much of that. All encounters are scripted and much of Jill's interactions with her pursuer happens via cut-scenes. Frequently over-the-top and heavy on action ones, with explosions that would make Michael Bay turn green with envy. As a result the whole pursuer gimmick falls flat on its face. It doesn't really feel like an unpredictable danger, a looming threat, just another typical obstacle to overcome. In the previous game you had to constantly listen for Mr. X's loud, ominous footsteps, dreading the next time he catches up with you. Now  was a pursuer.The other great disappointment is length. The game simply doesn't have all that much content. The original Resident Evil 3 was also the shortest to that point, this is even shorter. Some areas have been left out and as mentioned above the story branches have been nipped, making the game completely linear. It also lacks any extra modes, like Mercenaries. When contrasted with the previous Remake this feels even more strange. That one had extras, along with the two scenarios of course. But no, this game is 6-7 hours to finish and that's it. The end. No more. Well except Resistance. I suppose realizing this shortage of content Capcom bundled a completely separate asymmetric online game called Resistance to the package. Does anyone care? Seriously who asked for this? People want to play Resident Evil 3, not another half-assed online façade for a casino.So, is it good? I had fun with this game while it lasted. Yes, it is primarily an action game, but despite some excesses, a mostly enjoyable one. It also takes place in a great, classic setting. But it's not really a classic Resident Evil experience nor does it last that long. For a €60 game, the amount of content is decisively lackluster. I am glad I didn't pay full price for this. I believe the game is worth a shot. But only on a good sale.

_childDocuments_.review: R3make.3/5 - Story4/5 - Atmosphere/Environment4/5 -  Gameplay4/5 -  Audio2/5 - ReplayabilityFor fans of old. You'll be disappointed but nostalgia is still there. For casual newcomers, the game is almost solid as it sounds. You'll be facing a threat known as Nemesis throughout the game just like the original abeit in a lesser capacity. R3make is a solid continuation from R2make. The experience is rightfully deserved for atleast one playthrough.Story-wise the game presents it's retelling of the original Re3/Biohazard 3 Nemesis and most of it is presented well. The focus of the game is clear. Escape (defeat) Nemesis and escape the City. Raccoon City is pretty much dead. Several support characters (and new ones) also return to help Jill and Carlos to find a way out of the chaos. There are no more option dialogues and thus, no multiple endings afaik. However, the story is also short but the focus is clear whereas R2make gave a sense of "what the hell is going on." Also, Nemesis doesn't really chase you down in every sequence of the game.Environment is rendered beautifully. Volumetric lighting and bloom used to it's fullest. Dark areas barely illuminated gives a sense of dread and eerie-esque vibes. Especially, around corners, alleys, sewers, and roads. The modernized Raccoon City feels like complete chaos and abandoned after the outbreak. Immersively impressive. Though the levels are highly linear and personally would like some variance (different routes to try in each playthrough). There are cut areas from original that didn't make it (clocktower/park/etc.) unfortunately. The new expanded areas such as hospital and underground labs replaced them in a way.Gameplay controls are tight and almost identical to R2make. Knife doesn't break anymore but you don't have a freebie anymore either. If you're attacked, you're definitely going to take the hit. The new dodge mechanic is clunky unless you're timing is just right. Keep in mind that Zombies will lunge 2-3 times at you. Also note that Carlos and Jill have different dodge mechanics. Jill = Dodge. Carlos = Tackle/Punch. Guns feel great and ammo is scarce. The impact of every bullet gives them enough justice and most Z's won't go down that easily. Character movements are solid but not as fluid as Re6. Boss fights are tedious and a chore; doesn't give room for variability. There are less complex puzzles and it focuses more on action. I'd say R2make still has better puzzles compared to this game. Inventory management returns just like in any RE/Biohazard game.Audio is well done. Every enemy has distinct sound and noise. Every room/area has it's own vibes. It either gives peace or a sense of dread. VA for Jill was exceptional and really portrayed her stress and sense of urgency. The rest of the cast followed suit and provided good support development for Jill. However, the guns sounds are almost identical, Nemesis doesn't shout "stars" unless you're upclose and the distance audio needs some work (hearing zombies 1m away when they're 5m away). Also, hearing "door-banging" when you're 10m away, but it sounds like 1m away is hilarious.Replayability. There is none...almost none. New Game Plus opens up a shop where you can spend your achievement points from previous playthrough to buy items that'll enhance your next experience. Items include special passives or weaponry. They need a larger selection of firearms and items to use if they plan to use this feature. Simply put, it is too boring and mundane to attempt multiple playthroughs unless you really love the series.R3make = C Grade- Recommended to buy on discounted sale -

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I’m glad Resident Evil 3 is a short game because it was really, really stressful to play. After six hours of it, I was thoroughly jangled, and just wanted a break from things trying to messily dismantle me. Before my nerves tattered and I evolved into a Strategy Dad, you see, I used to love a bit of survival horror. So I knew what boxes RE3 needed to tick - and it left great bloody claw marks through all of them.Let's start with something seemingly dull but crucial: the inventory system. It’s simple, easy to manage, and extremely satisfying in its limitations. Crafting items isn’t just busywork here; it's vital for freeing up limited item slots by combining things. You're constantly thinking about what to stash where to maximize space. The scarcity of items and ammunition keeps you counting bullets most of the game, making looting both rewarding and necessary.Shooting feels fantastic. Zombies' heads burst in a satisfying way, and each weapon feels suitably hefty. I played with aim assist on because I'm no sharpshooter, and it still posed a challenge. You might fare better, but I bet you won't find it a cakewalk.The level design is top-notch. Play areas are modestly open, enough for exploration and backtracking, and every corner serves a purpose. It's navigable, thanks to the handy map feature that marks uncollected loot locations.And I can't emphasize enough how great everything looks. The game is masterfully lit, with incredibly detailed textures. Even protagonist Jill Valentine looks almost real at times. But it's the details that truly shine, like weird in-universe film posters and adverts that make exploring a joy.Fearwise, RE3 is spot on. The horror comes not just from jump scares but from a sense of constant dread. The environmental sound and lighting are masterfully used, making you feel perpetually unsafe. The game establishes this right from the start, leaving you on edge even during routine moments.This is an action-heavy game with less skulking than traditional survival horror, but the dread carries through to the combat sections. The camera and controls are solid, but there's always a sense of unease. Even basic zombies are a constant threat, thanks to their erratic movements. Jill's running isn't a brisk sprint but the effort of a real human trying to escape, and it's refreshing.The true star is Nemesis, a bioweapon with an obsession for Jill. His constant pursuit is genuinely oppressive, and it took me a while to realize I could fight back. As he transforms into more grotesque forms, the game maintains its horror, though his basic, imposing presence is often scarier.Now, about the elephant in the room - the game's portrayal of violence against women. It's a theme, and it's presented with a hint of relish that might make some players uncomfortable. Jill's character design leans into sexiness, and she endures a lot of physical punishment. This aspect doesn't sit well in the current gaming climate.In conclusion, Resident Evil 3 is a relentless rollercoaster of a game. It's an intense experience, visually stunning, with thrilling gameplay. However, its portrayal of violence may not sit right with everyone. If you're in the mood for a linear, day-long series of setpieces, this is it. But whether it's worth the price depends on your appetite for action-packed horror.

My rating is a 6.5 / 10.( + Positive ) Great graphics and details, very action packed and cinematic game play.( + Positive ) Neat rewards for replaying the game and tons of challenges to give you additional things to do. ( + Positive ) The content here is great for what it is but makes you want more as it's really on the short side. I'd say average person's 1st play through might take maybe 3 hours. If you like to go slow and look around while admiring scenery and atmosphere like me then you might be looking at 5 hours.( + Positive ) Jill and Carols are playable characters with different play styles. Not sure if I find Jill's perfectly timed dodges into head shots more fun or Carlos's superman styled counter punches that send creatures flying. A little disappointed Jill never obtains an automatic weapon without playing easy mode or unlocking the infinite assault rifle. ( - Negative ) Nemesis is a Joke the entire game. Majority of his interactions with Jill are cut scenes which ultimately show him being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on. Sadly he did not spend much time in form 1, and did not actively pursue Jill as much as was implied. The original RE3 handled it much better. ( - Negative ) Zombies at a distance are locked to 30 fps, their exact copies of the ones used in RE2 Remake yet lack the fun features of limb dismemberment. For as much marketing was done as this game having a larger pool of creatures and being more action focused, the most you'll ever face is like 5 at a time. ( - Negative ) I feel like this version of Jill's dodge is far too easy and rewarding. Being granted slow motion and aim assist for timing a good dodge takes away a lot of the intensity of the game. Knowing at almost any moment I can dodge for a free head pop without aiming turns some encounters mediocre. I would of personally preferred the dodge just be a dodge. You positioned yourself badly, and here's a single chance to make up for it thanks to Jill being a trained veteran. Along with a longer cool down or a sprint penalty to showcase the stamina requirement for moving like that. ( - Negative ) The game is just way too short. You're actively encouraged to speed run the game and finish it in under an hour. It feels like I spent more time watching the cut scenes than I did playing the game, figuratively but not literally. Really would of been interesting to have had more area's to explore and more bosses like the giant worm. A lack of Mercenaries from the original also hurt the package to me, especially since if I recall this was the game that introduced it to the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely made it into my top 3 favorite Resident Evil games.Resident evil 3 -having not played the original 1999 title- for me was a brilliant game that with its length did not overstay its welcome.Cannot say how well the game did as a Remake, since many have complained about cut or changed content as well as there's no more multiple endings present in the game.However for me it did everything that RE2 (2019) did right, and enhanced those where (for me) RE2 preformed poorly(mostly talking about the combat and the breakable knives). RE3 was never sluggish or boring. All other previous titles I've played I had to put down after certain hours of gameplay in one sitting because it got stale, not this one however, it kept pulling me back, it was like experiencing a fast paced movie.The visuals were stunning the characters were interesting enough, excluding 1 that is your classical "evil guy doing everything for money" type of villain.It was fun how in 1 walkthrough you get to control 2 characters and no need to replay the game to experience both "campaings". Nor was it needed to switch between them, their story line intertwined but not so much that you had an all time companiong by your side which for me just enhanced the immersion.RE3 manages to keep a tense suspended atmosphere without turning into an action shooter like the more recent titles after RE4 (some might argue that they would include that one as well) and for me Nemesis following your every footstep was just as fun -in a terrifying way- as Mr X was in RE2.However that being said I did get annoyed and later on frustrated even how you had to beat him over and over again as a boss, and it seems like all resident evil bosses seem to work the same way (which I absolutely hated in Resident evil 7 as well) that it almost feels like bullets and weapons have no effect on them until you get a cutscene or they just die at some point.The last and most important downside of this game is its price tag. For a 6 hour game they charge 60 euros? Come on that's a robbery. Don't buy it unless it's on a discount.So quick summary:The Good:Really fun exciting fast paced game that didnt end up as a cover based action shooter luckilySome improvements compared to the second game, mostly it's not longer than it should be avoiding becoming boring this way.The game looks absolutely great.NemesisThe bad:Ridiciolous pricingFIghting bosses like you are armed with a nerf gun or somethingYet again a boring basic stereotypical villianLength?

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: the soundtrack in this game is absolutely amazing. You can feel tension, flow of the horror and action when it needs to be.Jill Valentine - I love how her PTSD from RE1 events is more visible here, showing up her mental health (pills everywhere and bottles of beer in apartment section at the beginning). I know she is not the same as in OG Resident Evil, but I do believe they made good improvements here on what already was good. She is badass female character, stubborn and dedicated to survive. Carlos - I love the change of his character, the visual appearance as well. I feel his connection to Jill, as "partners" now is even better. There is no way of not loving Carlos, although Capcom left us in "cold cruel Carlos-less world". I would like to see him coming back to games or movies.Overall: I do recommend this game. I know it's getting a lot of harsh words, but I did enjoy it.Besides Nightmare and Inferno last boss fight with Nemesis. It almost made me cry. Did I beat it? Yes. Did my mental health suffered? Absolutely. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: When RE2 remake was released I watched everyone play it till I had the courage to play it, bringing back my terror from playing the original (directors cut allowing me access to the infinite rocket launcher from the beginning- which was the only reason I completed it as a scared little kid).This time with RE3, I hadn't played the original (because I was a kid and to scared to) refused to watch other play until after I had played it myself.The remakes are both incredible games and RE3 accomplished what its original had also intended. To be a true survival horror with more action. Nemesis is a real pain when it shows up but when its not around the vast array of zombie variety will keep you busy.However, it falls short in comparison to RE2 remake but as a stand alone I highly recommend. It falls short on the puzzles and the fear factor as RE2 was a labyrinth and had Mr X listening out for you and stomping around constantly looking for you which brought the fear factor just hearing those steps. Whereas RE3 doesn't have this as it is much more linear in its approach with all you ever needing to do is open a door, pull a lever, etc; and when Nemesis shows up its just a race to get away or a clear boss battle. I really did enjoy this game and once you have completed the game the first time Capcom have given you plenty of stuff to do for replay value just not as much as RE2 in my opinion.Looking forward to hearing if they do a RE4 remake (another I was to scared to play as a kid).

_childDocuments_.review: Ayy, where can i start... My main problem with the game is that, I can feel that the demo purposefully deceived me as a player of the game's further content.- The game is absolutely linear after the demo content and the paying of the game was all over the place (I   was just stunned that in the sewers I had to play as the devs planned it by using flame rounds on that one   corridor of a map).- The items and the results of 'puzzles' were spoonfed to me all the way (Couldn't play the usual survival   gameplay, only the 'brainless bring everything and then all will be fine' type of play).- Half of the mechanics from RE2 literally were thrown out of the window in the name of 'action' gameplay   and the dodge mechanic was great at times, but was too clunky (Not even mentioning reversing the Carlos   dodge half way through).- Nemesis was a mumbling melting pizza-faced, Dark Souls Boss. _childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't know what went wrong here. I've completed one playthrough on standard so far and these are my impressions.Pros:-Looks great. Seriously phenomenal looking graphics (played on an RTX 2080).Cons:-Nemesis isn't nearly as present a threat as it should have been. In RE2 I spent probably the entire playthrough after Mr X was introduced wondering when he'd next pop up. Here it quickly became apparent that Nemesis was restricted to scripted encounters and I think only one segment where it actually followed you around the map like in the original game (which itself turned out to be extremely scripted, and not dynamic like RE2's Mr X was).-The action feels worse. Something about the weight and impact that weapons had in RE2 is gone. The knife is infinite, but has been rendered primarily a box opener by its newfound inability to damage limbs (or it seems like even stagger enemies).-No real backtracking. I remember an earlier article about this game that said there would be fast travel. What happened? (In general it seems like there was a LOT of misinformation spread about it, particularly by what should be reputable sources).-Where is the replayability? The choices from the original game are gone, and unlike RE2 there's only one playthrough. While you switch between Carlos and Jill on occasion, it's nowhere near the amount of variation RE2 had and presents almost no reason to touch this again after the first playthrough.-There's some frustrating difficulty spikes that really contrast with how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ easy the game is in general. The hunters in this game can one shot you from full life on normal difficulty, but only under some circumstances (I could not figure out what made it happen)? -A lot of the setpieces were just not great. The first fight with Berkin in RE2 was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ setpiece. He plows through the environment, pipes burst, you can lose track of him as he disappears behind machinery. The sound and feel of that fight was amazing. The first proper fight with Nemesis you're just in a place. There's like a couple stacks of boxes. Some fire.  It feels weird to give this a negative review because it's still a perfectly fun, playable game. It's just SO much worse than RE2 in basically every way. Resident Evil 3 gets a 6/10 from me, bumped to a 6.5/10 if you can get it for <= $20. It feels and plays like an expansion to RE2, not a standalone game, and I'm hoping that post launch support can fix at least some of the issues I have with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm... what to sayBack when i was a little girl not only was I utterly forced by my parents to focus on my studies, but we were also, not very rich. We had enough money for a decent house, for daily living and some more, but not enough for things of luxury, such as was video game consoles back then. Furthermore, being a girl, I was expected to like dolls not video games. Therefore you can expect their surprise when I asked for a Playstation One back then. It took awhile before I was granted my wish, it was as a reward for being 'top 1' in my class back then, I still remember my first 2 games, they were 'Tekken 3' and 'Resident Evil 2'. I enjoyed both games, but enjoyed Resident Evil 2 more because I didn't have anyone to play with on Tekken 3. I never got to finish Resident Evil 2 no matter how much I loved it because ironically, despite my love for horror games, I'm scaredy cat. After some years passed I heard Resident Evil 3 was released and immediately bought it.Resident Evil 3 for me was a step up from Resident Evil 2, and I loved Resident Evil 2! While Leon will always have a place in my heart, Jill Valentine, back then stole my admiration. Furthermore, because I was older, finishing the game was an easier ordeal for me than it was before. Sadly, despite my new found courage and fortitude, Nemesis made sure I'd run out of pants to pee in and eventually give up and leave another unfinished game, but I at least made it past the clock tower before letting my cousin finish it for me while I hide behind him.When I heard about Resident Evil 3 remake, it was a 'must buy' for me. I couldn't help it. I wanted to see the RE3 Jill properly remade for the new generation of gaming consoles and the PC. Furthermore I saw this as a challenge from my younger self. I wanted to see, if I could finally finish what 10 year old me couldn't! Have I grown enough metaphorical balls to finally beat my demons? Well.... yes but....You see, to compare this game to Resident Evil 3, is to compare shooting a gun, to shooting a bow. They're just too different. The original RE3, like its predecessor the original RE2, will choke you with its dreary atmosphere. Every time you open a door, you literally open a door into the unknown wherein you're not sure if you're going to be someone's dinner after the screen loads. There was a sense of foreboding, that maybe the saferoom you're currently in is the last saferoom you'll ever see before you load an older save file because you used your last ink ribbon. You don't feel any of these in the remake.RE3 remake commits the sin, of not being very scary. When I played this game the only thing that worried me was the jump scares. Giving Jill a very powerful dodge and perfect dodge mechanic removed much of the suspense which I loved from the original. I get that Jill is a badass, but she's not a super human who should be able to do 'bullet time'! Furthermore, the original, and its predecessor RE2 remake, were very dark, but this game apart from very select places, was instead very bright, maybe because everything's on fire! Lastly, where is the gore?! Sure you get pierced by tentacles sometimes, and get some salami bitten off from your neck by zombies, but is this really all the gore you're willing to put in a zombie game? Even when you explode the head of zombies they only burst into boring chunks of meat and strawberry jam! Resident Evil, I do believe your audience is mature enough to watch a hunter decapitate someone's head off!And then... there's nemesis. Call me crazy, but I always found Nemesis' original design to be incredibly intimidating. Mr. X from RE 2, the original not the remake, always scared the living daylights out of me. Imagine my surprise when Nemesis, something like Mr. X, but is able to move faster, use weapons, and make sinister voices especially "STAHHRS". The new Nemesis gave me that same feeling... until they turned him into a bloodborn boss. In the original, Nemesis transforms too, but that's only near the end. His transformation in this game feels too early and pushed the game even more towards the action shooter genre than survival horror. So the game wasn't very scary was it at least enjoyable? Mmm... yeah. I can't lie, as much as I didn't want the direction they pushed this game to, I still enjoyed playing it. Getting chased by Nemesis was a thrill until he became the Bloodstarved Beast at least and shooting felt fun, probably because of how accurate Jill's aim is. I know I complained about the dodge mechanic, but as soon as I accept that this wasn't 'survival horror' anymore, I began to appreciate it to the point that I became good at it.Overall I can still recommend this game even though I dislike how unfaithful it is to the original. As a survival horror game, it's borderline mediocre, but as a game itself it was pretty good. I mean Jill is still very pretty and Miguel from Tekken made a cameo I guess that's a plus but I didn't like playing as him because... reasons. It was also very nice to see how some people we saw in RE2 remake got into the situation they were in like Mr. Kendo and that police guy. Yes, I think I can say that despite some disappointing choices, this game still made me smile. I just hope the next entry would be more faithful to its survival horror roots than this one is.

Sure, there isn't a crazy story, but I feel they could have at least added two more chapters.My first was a blind play-through on standard difficulty. _childDocuments_.review: I was eager to play this remake and it was a huge let down for me. The game itself plays well and looks good, but, it just lacks  some serious content even in comparison to the the 32bit original which had bigger maps, puzzles and choices implemented.  Playing through seems so generic, you are basically on a track to the finish line. There are no puzzles to solve, everything is basically in front of you or in the next room, the progression is that linear. This is made worse by the total lack of atmosphere, the tiny map with limited game play and excessive cinematic scenes throughout. They have tried to rectify this by initially making the nemesis  appear intense but even this must of been too much like hard work for them as it becomes predictable after a short time and progressively easier as he evolves into a dumber, larger and less aggressive enemy following a very similar attack pattern. The only real difficulty in the game is the toughness of the enemies, if you manage to get caught a few times you die. This is also an anticlimax as it's usually down to the bulletproof zombie skulls and their gymnastic ability to grab you from questionable  angles while absorbing a constant stream of head shots.This is also becomes easy to avoid and worst case scenario you can continue from basically where you left off.I explored every aspect of the tiny map and completed the game in 5.13, it really  is that small. I have no desire to play it again, sadly, after one lap you have saw everything it has to offer.Other than the vague reference to the setting and the characters it does not resemble the 1999 game at all. In fact the part where you go into the police station seems like a copy and paste file from RE2, just without content again. Then suddenly, before you know it the games over, well done, here's a rank and an item shop to try and distract you from the fact this is another example of lazy developers milking a franchise for a quick buck.  There is nothing remotely nostalgic or unique I'm afraid.I would not say don't play it, but, take my advice and wait until its on sale, 5/10 at best.

_childDocuments_.review: If Resident Evil 2 was a yummy pizza with extra toppings then Resident Evil 3 is a calzone - still yummy, but a much smaller portion. This game is really short, like  short. You can finish a first playthough in under six hours, and second in less than half of that, easily.Despite its length, RE3 is excellent. It's action focused this time around, but it still retains the horror elements that defined RE2. This campaign takes place in the same locations as RE2, but in areas different enough that it doesn't feel like a copy and paste job. The creepy abandoned hospital was a great original location - I just wish there had been more to explore.The Nemesis encounters are mostly scripted Kool-Aid wall smashing sequences, which personally I preferred over Mr X constantly bursting into rooms mid-puzzle in RE2. They've also added a dodge and punch mechanic that gives you the mobility to avoid a Nemesis attack or zombie bite, and counter a Hunter swipe with a jab. If anyone from Capcom reads these reviews, please go back and add this into RE2. Zombies with a six foot magnetic grip are super annoying, this makes the situation fairer and the gameplay more fluid.There's also an in-game shop, which thankfully is only tied to challenges that can be completed throughout the campaign. It's a nice touch that you can reload a save game, mow down some zombies, die, and then reload your save and still unlock the challenges. The items for purchase include new weapons, infinite ammo, skins and various attack, defence and health improvements. You'll want these trinkets to blast your way through the hordes on a second playthrough.Basically RE3 is fantastic, just don't spend more than £15 if you don't want to feel ripped off.

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game multiple times and on the hardest difficulty, not worth 40$, barely worth 20$.Game took 4 hours on my first playthrough on normal to beat, getting almost every item besides about 2 weapon upgrades from knocking Nemesis down, and most playthroughs after averaged around 2:30 hours. This really doesn't feel finished, as it clearly uses a lot of assets from the previous game and and its very easy to rush through with minimal experience. On lower and medium difficulties you won't see much enemy variety, with each enemy type being used like two times throughout the whole experience. Higher difficultys don't solve the problem either, as they just change the encounters a bit to catch you off guard the first time with at most THREE of the rare ones showing up ever again. It doesnt feel playtested either, as a lot of deaths came from getting combo'd by multiple or even the same enemy, sometimes immediately after a perfect dodge. Also the main draw of the game being Nemesis doesn't work considering hes barely around during actual gameplay, and his sections are generally bad. During free roam sections i've had him teleport directly in front of me instead of actually chasing me through doors like Mr. X, and the close camera isn't conducive to trying to use Jill's dodge mechanic when he does decide to run after you. His chase scenes are very boring and easy, and his boss fights aren't fun after the first time. His final fight is especially bad, either being too easy or excruciatingly tedious due to getting easily combo'd by most of his attacks depending on the difficulty.The game has a point shop to add "replayability" but all it does is make the higher difficultys easier with straight stat boosts. Being able to replay the game a lot doesn't matter when the game is not good. *Also if you did not preorder the game there is only ONE unlockable costume for ONE of the characters. Costume mods exist but majority of them are either Jill naked or look terrible, and i could not find a way to unlock the preorder ones either.5/10 game. If you like the Resident Evil 2 remake, this is like an expansion thats not even close to being worth its current full price of 40$.

I got lost a bit and died 11 times. There isn't inherently bad with short games, there's some short games that are amazing, but this is a AAA $60 game. Short games tend to be smaller and cheaper than that. I'm not asking for a 60 to 100 hour long game. Unless it's A Persona game, games that length are draining as ♥♥♥♥. Me being insecure about my skill in games, I accepted. It proceeded to give me a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ assault rifle and 90 bullets for it for Jill. It's like RE wants to relapse into action.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed playing the game, but it did not meet my expectations. _childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: (Summary: an incredible remake of one of the lesser games in the franchise, however $60 is asking a lot for what feels like a $30 DLC for the Resi 2 Remake: Buy on sale and you've got more than your money's worth.) It's not as good as the Resi 2 remake for the obvious reason that the original RE3 wasn't as good as the original RE2 either. But still, the gameplay and overall story still match and at some points exceed the RE2 remake despite the super-linearity of the level design and shortness of the overall game. In short, they did as good as they could've done given the lesser material they had to work with, and while the Resi 2 remake gets a 9.5 or 10/10 for me, this game gets an 8.5 or 9/10, which is still a strong great to light amazing. HOWEVER, this is ignoring the $60 price tag, as keeping that in mind I would drop the game to a strong 7/10. My main complaint is that this could have totally been a $30 DLC pack for the RE2 remake since it uses the same exact engine and mechanics and even reuses a lot of assets and even entire AREAS (Granted the reused areas were done well and felt like a really enjoyable homage, these areas benefit the game and make it a more enjoyable experience, I won't spoil it) so it definitely does feel like I'm playing a $60 DLC. Still almost worth the money, and would definitely be much more worth it if it went on sale. (As I said, if it was $30 I would give it a strong 9/10.)

_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: RESIDENT EVIL 3 Remake is a fantastic action based resident evil experience that was an absolute blast to play through but it is currently hindered by it's price point.Before going any further I must say that the game is very short for the price tag and you should wait for the game to be about half the price before diving in. The game lasts about 5-6 hours and doesn't have any additional playthrough modes unlike it's predecessor Resident Evil 2. You get your standard run, your hardcore run and a point based unlock system after beating the game and that is it.Having said that RESIDENT EVIL 3 is a fantastic game and definitely should be played. It goes for a more linear action based approach than Resident Evil 2 and feels like a collection of the later sections of RE2 as opposed to the police station approach of having one large area to explore. It's a shame that approach wasn't taken here but the levels designs while small are still great and suit the action based approach very well. The action has been ramped up dramatically with the game giving you plenty of ammo and upgrades to take down zombies with and it makes you feel like an utter badass once you've kitted Jill out with a hefty amount of gear. With the higher emphasis on the combat there has been some work put into the boss fights which are improved compared to Resident Evil 2 mostly due to the addition of a combat roll which makes defence much easier alongside the addition of the captivating villain Nemesis.When it comes to Nemesis he ramps up the excitement and drives the narrative forward at a blasting pace. I found nemesis to be an interesting and intimidating villain and he kept me hooked the whole way through. I do think the portrayal of him in pre release footage was a bit misleading. He is portrayed to be a Mr. X style replacement. Whilst he is a bit like that in a few points in the game for short periods he doesn't keep it up and is mainly encountered through scripted segments and action set pieces.Seeing as I never played more than 20 minutes of the original resident evil 3 I never knew of any of the missing moments in the story that had been rewritten so from a fresh point of view I thought the story was great and nicely ties in with resident evil 2.The feeling of Resident Evil 2 remake is very much here with this remake but the lack of a large sprawling area to explore and the lack of any extra playthrough mixups leaves the game feeling rather sparse in comparisson to the previous entry in the series especially at this price.While falling short compared to Resident Evil 2 I wholeheartedly recommend this game if the price is not a problem as I truly think it stands with the better games in the series but the game is very hindered by it's lack of additional content for the price its being offered for at this time. I'm giving it a recommendation but don't buy it just yet and wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend the game...but only for a one time play or so. Resident Evil 3 Remake is an ok game, but considering how much content from the original 1999 game has been removed in the Remake, including a fun helicopter Boss battle in the original, I'd say this game should be marked as a major disappointment.  The original had multiple endings and various choices that dictated the course of the game. All of those choices have been removed and you now have just one ending. Additionally, though it uses assets and locations seen in Resident Evil 2 remake, there is a severe drop in quality. Even the dismemberment of enemies, the sensation where you can feel each hole, each piece of flesh blasted off which made Resident Evil 2 Remake so amazing, has been remarkably reduced in Resident Evil 3 Remake. Removal of several key locations like City Hall, Clock Tower....Overall this game is much shorter than Resident Evil 2 Remake, let alone the original 1999 Resident Evil 3.

Comparing this to RE2 remake, this would get a C grade at best from me. As soon as I heard this would be released this year, I thought "Oh no, It's going to be rushed," and by god, it was. It's a good game if you don't compare it to the old version, but they took a lot out of it.I can't in good conscious recommend buying this at a full $60 price tag. _childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who played the Original Re3 as his first Re game... this was a disappointing remake..I had read a lot of bad reviews about this and only just purchased it to see for myself. I don't hate this game but it definately isn't as good as the Re 2 remake and certain falls short of the original Re3  It is clear that the development team behind this were perhaps under pressure by Capcom to get this game out asap because you get the impression there are chunks taken out of this game and parts rushed.Look at the concept artwork it is obvious they did plan to have more locations of Downtown RC and this leads to the biggest let down of this game, unnecessary cut content. Downtown seems more or less complete but in the original it feels like a bigger environment, choices of where to go first which impact the story line, nope this Downtown was a linear experience. They drew the car park and clearly even designed it with exploration in mind, but you never get to explore it, same with the Stagla gas station. The Clock Tower section is completely missing which is a real disappointment. In the original game that was a great middle section of the game, with puzzles and randomising enemies to avoid; depending on what choices were made. In this remake they just seem to jump to the fight in the courtyard. Hang on what about the Clock Tower area, can I just play some re for a moment and explore a remade clock tower? Nope i've got another battle again already great.. And not even that was great..Oddly enough, the apartment you run through downtown to escape nemesis had clock tower esque doors and walls..It isn't just the clock tower though is it, it seems if there was an area around the tower and Hospital that was removed, which should be the Park and Dead Factory....Well they decided, no let's forget the variable looking environment and just go straight in to the Factory and Hospital. Boring! Nest 2 just comes across as well we can't be arsed to do anything more now let's re-use assets. Even the concept of Nest 2 shows more interesting areas and even ideas.. Come on Capcom, what happened to the different environments?!Another gripe I have is what happened to Nemesis? In the original game he practically wouldn't leave you alone for most of the game, in Re3 remake apart from one or two moments he stalks you, other than that he appears in scripted moments and even so, when he does appear in scripted moments the game protects you and holds your hand. You know that something is wrong as soon as the game starts, since he fails to get past the bookshelf...This is a huge step down from the original pursuer who would take several rooms to lose. He also mutates in to an Alien Queen early in the game; yes it seems like an Alien Queen. Gone is the humanoid pursuing monster and now it's just a blob that keeps turning up to taunt you. Personally I would of liked to of seen more of humanoid Nemesis, I rather liked the way he was re-designed and gradually became more mutated, his Stars cries reflected how angry he was getting at losing Jill constantly, like I said though sadly this is cut far too short. In fact when I think about it, this game is actually called Resident evil 3... Hmmmm I can see why they removed the Nemesis word!Puzzles? Well there aren't many if any. The original game had several and even Re2 remake had a lot more than this. Puzzles are good at varying the gameplay and one thing I liked about the original Re3. The only puzzles we get are, inserting jewels, setting a train route with the answer shown and a pointless vaccine puzzle with the solution being press random buttons until it lines up.... Yeah very inventive.Live events? Nope also gone are the choices and varying routes to take. Would it have taken much to of given us the chance to go to the Stagla gas station or Garage first, to change things up a bit? Nope. The Raccoon Press as well? Nope gone. I mean come on, maybe even change events so Jill goes to the Rpd instead of Carlos resulting in a nemesis encounter, or just Carlos and then the Nemesis breaks through the wall making a Nemesis sized hole... Oh yeah I forgot that is just c4.... Any music this time? Well the music oddly enough seemed better in this than the Re2 remake, they remixed some of the original music and re-used it in places and the game didn't seem as silent.Gameplay? The game plays out a lot like re 2 remake with a few additions. One being a dodge where you can dodge enemies, this was a welcome addition as it was also in the og re3. Imo this is also a vast improvement on the original dodge, it feels more like it works. It also mixes up the gameplay a bit more from re 2. However, the game also likes to hold your hand in a lot of places and you aren't really doing anything! Poison is also oddly removed from this game not sure why?Boss battles or lack of?The bosses in this game consists of the Nemesis and the Alien Queen. That's it... There isn't a Gravedigger or anything else. They give the Hunter Frogs gravedigger mouths but that doesn't count, that's just lazy enemy design.The Nemesis boss battles aren't very inventive either. There is little difference between the clock tower fight and the treatment vat fight, the final battle was a joke. In terms of replay valueI feel like you don't really get much for finishing the game or much of a reason to re-play it. The original had a mercenaries mode and alternate paths to take which added replay value, even Re 2 remake had several battle modes. Re 3 remake gives you a shop and some extra guns and accessories you can buy, This is nice but it doesn't make up for missing game sections and a lack of an extra scenario. There is also only one ending, you can't do anything differently or frankly do anything to change the game at any point, as there are no event selections. Pressing a button to do something doesn't count!The lack of event selections is annoying, anything to vary the gameplay experience? Nope just linear over and over again.As I said above I don't completely hate this game, there are one or two moments that I enjoyed like the Rpd visit, it neatly ties certain events on Re 2 to this game; although I wish it was Jill going there and having another Nemesis encounter.. If you are a fan of the original re 3 you should play this game to enjoy the brief good moments, but i'll warn you it is disappointing what could have been. If you are expecting the same standard as Re 2 remake, even a game as good as or better than the re 3 original you will feel slightly disappointed.   If you are a fan of the Re 2 remake you will probably find yourself wanting to play the Re 2 remake again.

_childDocuments_.review: After just finishing the game on Hardcore, I'd say it's about 7/10 easily. Without spoiling, it has some weird pacing issues where the player gets carried through certain areas too quickly without being able to soak in the environment and too many events that could be playable happen via cutscenes, some locations seemed to last only a few minutes and even on Hardcore felt very easily dealt with, while others were a slog and really difficult due to high concentrations of enemies and weird level design.Sounds like I'm dragging it, but honestly I thought it was a really good game which had a lot of moments which were great and some others which weren't the best.PROS: Amazing presentation (this game is beautiful), Fun combat with a high skill ceiling, pretty good voice acting, plenty of incentive for replayability, the story presentation itself is very well done.NEUTRAL: The game is more survival action than survival horrorCONS: Pacing issues (the game pushes you through areas and events too quickly), Combat IS fun, but skill ceiling may make even Hardcore difficulty feel fairly easy, boss fights are few and feel too scripted,

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write reviews, but as a long time fan of the series, this has been the most disappointing Resident Evil game since RE6. RE2make wasn't perfect; it had it's mistakes, as did the original RE3. I still was super hyped for this game as I did enjoy both of those games. This remake dropped almost everything unique and interesting about RE3 and altered what it kept in a way that left much to be desired. The first minutes of the game created an engaging atmosphere that showed promise, but that atmosphere got smothered by the barely interactive first encounter with Nemesis. For a game that already feels so lacking it is frustrating that some of the most intense moments of the game are cinematics of Jill get chased by Nemesis.It usually takes me at least 8 hours to finish a Resident Evil game the first time around. I always explore, take time to think about things, make mistakes. It took me about 5 hours to finish this game, and that includes all the above and me just leaving the game idling for a bit. There was just too much taken from the original that was not sufficiently replaced. Gone are several puzzles, brain suckers, the Grave digger, spiders, The Clocktower, Graveyard, Park, City Hall, freeze rounds (rip), Mercenaries mode, the live selections, Barry's appearance, multiple endings, and so on. Nemesis was intimidating for about 5 minutes during the first part but was ultimately less dynamic and terrifying than in the original or Mr. X in RE2make. Nemesis, THE Resident Evil pursuer, being less dynamic than Mr. X is such a let down. Additionally, I felt like there was more time with the U.B.C.S. in the original, and that Nicholai was more interesting as well. Perhaps this lack of content was to be expected. This game came out a year after RE2make, and was being bundled with the multiplayer game (which I have yet to try as it just reminds me that Capcom will never give Outbreak another chance). However, the original Resident Evil 3 offered more with a similar time frame. of development.
