_childDocuments_.review: Once again, Capcom brings another great game on the amazing RE Engine, this time in the form of Resident Evil 3.While the previous remake, RE 2, was more slow paced and conservative, RE 3 quickly switches gears from the start and it really feels more focused on letting the player be a bit more proactive towards the different enemies; we can dodge now, even in a “perfect dodge” way if properly timed, so that’s already a pretty good indicator of the intentions Capcom had with this remake.Just like in the original RE3, dodging can be an interesting way of dealing with some enemies, but also risky if we have yet to master it; fortunately this time around the mechanics behind it aren’t as obnoxious as in the original game.When it comes to PC exclusive settings and other stuff, any PC review should mention at least some of these, when it comes to performance, control settings and keybinds, etc. Very much like RE 2 Remake, the game offers a wide array of graphical settings and the controls are pretty customizable, even quite left handed friendly.On the performance side of things, the game runs flawlessly on my  and , even on max settings, but as it happened with the previous game, the  can be a bit taxing in certain scenes, but dropping it to Medium solves the issue while not losing much quality on such volumetric effects.As for the dreaded “short” duration of the game many people are afraid of, on my first run I spent, according to my save, around 7 and a half hours, and around 10 in total (as the save seems to only count time for essential stuff and no other time spent in menus or what not, I guess, not sure). Anyway, what this means is that if you finished the game on your first run in like 2 hours, you skipped a lot of the fun and exploration, so that’s on you. The game felt to me, on the first run, just as long as RE 2 remake, all things considered. RE2 Remake on the other hand, I felt it had a lot of wasted potential with the A/B and B/A scenarios, meaning that once you did let’s say Claire A and Leon B, there was no need to do the reverse…none, it was the same, with some plot inconsistencies even regarding some of the Birkin fights. In any case, that didn’t stop me from considering RE 2 Remake a very amazing game, and it is.For RE3 Remake I felt that this time the  seems even more  to me, and coherent. It may feel shorter for those who spent the same amount of time doing A/B back in RE 2, but no…it really isn’t any much shorter than RE 2 Remake, just like the originals, both could be completed in a similar time back then, especially when speed running. For this remake I also felt that  like Carlos have been vastly improved, to the point that now he feels like a very well written character and not the...whatever that was on the original game. Really good job there with Carlos, Capcom, his character development really made me enjoy the character a lot, in a very good way. The rest of the cast is also very well written, even those whose stay is more brief than others, so yeah, solid cast for this remake, most of the original game's characters are very well written and dubbed, at least in english.Sound design is very decent too in this game, and compared to RE2 Remake I felt that the music here in RE 3 is more varied and very cohesive with the rest of the action packed situations we find ourselves in. Great job in general with the soundtrack, something not many reviews seem to mention, really enjoyed it.All in all, I’m still face palming heavily myself after having read some of the most bizarre “professional” reviews for the game (like that pathetic 58 score PC Gamer review, if you can call that thing a PC game review, with no mention on performance or PC specific stuff, to be very honest with you here), but luckily from what I’ve seen on Metacritic, from like 90 professional critics reviews, not too many are that low, so they seem like pretty much outliers. In general the game is quite solid, and if you have any reason to believe it isn’t, well good for you, but I myself had a pretty amazing blast playing this game, and hopefully Capcom ignores those people fixated on bland nostalgia and they keep making remakes like these. That seems to be the intention here, they seem to be fixing some of the inconsistencies in the original stories for the main characters and all that, so hopefully they continue revamping these mainline games and we can see more remakes : ): this review stays positive as the game is not as bad as some so called "RE Fans" make it to be. Content was cut and not included in both RE 2 and 3 remakes, in fact RE 2 does have a pretty poor A/B - B/A scenario system compared to the original experience, yet that doesn't make it a bad remake at all.RE 3 has many expanded areas like the Hospital, or the Carlos sections, or characters that actually have more than one line of dialogue, compared to the original, and it's still a fun game to complete back to back with RE 2 Remake. It's also a very challenging game in Nightmare and Inferno difficulties which many of the "so called fans" haven't even completed yet, I'm sure.In conclusion, still a decent RE game, and fun to replay. Could have been bigger and with more areas? Yeah, but it is what it is, and it's not a bad game at all, and if you feel like staying within that dumb circlejerking process of hating on this game because "it's not like the original", well neither is RE 2 Remake, because they're remakes, the originals are still excellent games, and you can go and play them too, as I do sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR This is a good game in a vacuum. Mechanically it's pretty good. The music is good, the atmosphere is good, the monsters are memorable. But as a *remake*, and a sequel to the RE2 Remake, it is very, very disappointing. But only in that respect. So if you want a remake of an original, this performs poorly. If you just want an isolated sequel to RE2R, then it's pretty good. What follows will go in depth about this opinion.This game is conflicted in what it wants to be. It felt like it was being designed by two different teams at the same time; one that was committed to being a loving tribute to the original RE3, and one that didn't care.On the one hand, you have the music; modern, atmospheric, bringing back the original RE3 score and perfecting it in one of the most lovingly nostalgic tributes to an OST I can remember hearing in a game. You have the atmosphere; dark, oppressive, bleak. The city is dying, death and despair are consuming it, and it FEELS like it. The environments are grimy, bloody, smashed, burning and crumbling. It sells the setting perfectly. It feels like a wonderful modernisation of the sights of RE3. It absorbs you into it. It looks convincing.On the other hand, you have the plotline. It seems to rush through the story without letting any particular segment of it *breathe*. Like a tour guide leading you through a museum at a jog rather than walking through slowly, teling you the history and answering your questions.You have the removal of whole segments from the original. The Police Station which should have been Jill's first stop, is never visited by her, and instead is a short detour for Carlos. The park is completely missing. The Clock Tower has been turned into a distant background landmark you may miss entirely if you're focused on your immediate surroundings and the boss fight that takes up most of the time it's visible. In the original it was an entirely separate location you had to explore. There were plot points tied to it; an escape route. It was a refuge, and a character-switch point.Then you have the main antagonist, Nemesis. Arguably one of the most powerful and dangerous of Umbrella's various Tyrants. The original Pursuer of the franchise. He's been downgraded from a semi-persistent threat that pursues you from location to location to 3 brief encounters in the first 25% of the game and 3 setpiece boss fights for the rest of it. This is especially noticeable after RE2R's Mr. X and his stellar reimagining as a persistent pursuer; the role that should have been Nemesis's hallmark.There's also the removal of the branching decision and diverging plotline system; a feature that introduced a lot of replayability in the original. As a result the game can be experienced in its entirety in one playthrough. The lazy difficulty system offers none of that replayability, as it can basically be summarised as "everything is faster and hits harder".And then there's RE: Resistance, which is an online multiplayer subgame that was packaged alongside it, and which inherently has a low and dwindling playerbase which will eventually render it worthless. The development time for this would have been much better spent focusing on the main game itself and making sure it was as expansive and well polished as it really should have been.It all just feels discordant. Like Capcom considered this game an afterthought while they worked on RE8. And it's a shame. Because the RE-Engine and the formula they achieved with the RE2 Remake could have made this game timeless.I am giving this game a thumbs down because I imagine a lot of people coming to this game will be fans of the franchise itself, as opposed to new players coming to experience Resident Evil with no prior experience. On that basis, this game doesn't live up to its predecessors, neither RE2R, nor the original RE3. But if you just want to experience an RE game in the vein of RE2R and have no knowledge of the original, then this is a good game to play.

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: I bought this game for 45$ so my review will be based taking into account that pricetag. I do NOT recommend getting this game over 40$ unless you want to play Resistance.Actual Review.Cons: I really think steam should have a 'meh' rating system. The game is good. It's very good, it's honestly so good that it's the first game I've replayed like 5 times in a week. But is it a good remake? Not really. They cut a lot of stuff out, I personally don't really care for it but a lot of people do and if you're one of them then be warned. Nemesis is very toned down (Like Mr. X). He's scary at first but then it just becomes a chore to get through to him plus he's featured way less than he should be and also the second transformation is very weird and so not scary. The final boss fight is probably one of the worst enemy design I've ever seen, gameplay wise. On normal difficulties it's super easy but on higher difficulty it's like Dark Souls but very unfair. It's like the game automatically jumps fro a 0 to 100 and expects you to keep up.Pros: Because of the cut content, the story feels much more smooth. It captures the atmosphere of the original perfectly, in my opinion.The characterization of Jill & Carlos is very grounded and has much more depth than the Original, in my opinion. Also the Jill remodel is very pretty.Tons of replay value. A lot of people will disagree because it's the same campaign over and over again except with higher difficulties but isn't that what RE is?Final Thoughts: The game is very meh. If you wait for the price to drop to around 20 (Which it will) and buy it then it'll be a perfect DLC to RE2. Even at 40$ it'll be a good RE game but not at the current price. Also, I see a lot of people jumping on the bandwagon and hating it just because the game is 6 hours long. Don't listen to it. It has a lot of replay value and you can't quantify a game's value solely on it's length. If that were the case then Ubisoft's checklist formulaic games would be getting GOTYs every year.

_childDocuments_.review: So... The remake of Resident Evil 3, a classic a lot of people love and hold dear in their hearts because of the childhood memories... That may be the main reason of why it got so much hate, although some people say it goes beyond that. Does it really, though?Let me just take it off my chest: I had a blast playing Resident Evil 3 Remake. Was it was good as RE2 Remake? Hell no. Was it better than the classic game? In some aspects? Sure. For most of it? Absolutely not. But here's the thing, the hard to swallow pills: Not even the classic Resident Evil 3 was that great to begin with. Sure, it was fun, it felt much more complete than this remake. But storywise? That original version was as just as rushed as this one. While the puzzles and the act of coming and going and coming back again gives the sensation that the classic RE3 was longer, if you look at it for real, it really doesn't have a lot to it. If you know exactly what to do and how to avoid the enemies, you can finish it in 40 minutes.And what about the remake? I think what it really went and even goes against it it's the expectations. We came out of Resident Evil 2 Remake, which was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing and felt more complete (even if they make you redo a lot of repeated things in both campaigns, something that the classic RE2 didn't have) and our expectations for it were huge. In the end, it ended up being rather underwelming and different than what many people expected. Nemesis encounters were much more scripted than the classic, the plot beast went and came much quicker than the original, so a lot of moments that were supposed to be memorable, like they were in the classic, couldn't be properly digested and felt, because the story was going forward at full speed, and we also didn't have a lot to do or explore, the game doesn't make a lot of effort for you to invest on exploration. There was a lot of disappointment and hate.But now... 2 years later, what do I think of it? This was my first time playing this game, because I finally got a good computer. And I tried to play this game as it is, not accordingly to my expectations and to what I wanted it to be. If you are gonna judge something, judge for what's actually in it. And while yes, the story and the gameplay were super rushed, and some narrative aspects, and mostly gameplay aspects, were disappointing and left a lot to be desired I had a really good experience with Resident Evil 3 Remake. The game felt like those uncomprimised sequels that just wants to make you have fun and enjoy the experience with some big dumb bombastic and frenetic action while mixing a good amount of body horror and ugly monsters. In that aspect, this remake delivers it. It may not live longer in your memory, but I don't think it really needs to be more than that when not even the classic game was more than that. You may have a emotional bond with the original, but not even it was perfect or the most revolutionary game ever made.I don't mind what this game attempted or didn't attempted to make. Do I wish it was better? Yes. But am I happy with what I got? Yes. It was enough. It kept me enternained and engaged all the way through. Sometimes, that's all what games, movies and books need to do.

_childDocuments_.review: First, one cannot deny that the new engine (started from RE7) is absolutely a great system for the game. Almost everything looks gorgeous and it keeps the gameplay of RE2 Remake. But Capcom made several lapses in this one1. Distant zombies are locked to 30FPS or even lower, making them look jarring to everything else, this is probably a porting issue and thus will not be fixed officially2. The game is absurdly short. Way shorter than RE2. This is primarily because the game cut off too much content. RE2 and RE3 remake should have been one release if they did really planned this games to be this short. Alternatively it shouldn't be priced at a full 60$. Even the additional multiplayer mode isn't worth the full price.3. Nemesis is a push over, even at inferno. He doesnt pursue you as much as Tyrant did in RE2R, or game mechanics (barrels / grenades / dodge evade system) made him trivial. I personally liked his design aside from his "black garbage bag wraps like a mummy". They should've never added the nose though but that's a minor detail.4. The design change to the classic Jill attire is a bit of a disappointment too. This is the only game I've ever pre-ordered and I did so only because of the classic Jill attire. So meh.Capcom, you did great in RE7, good in RE2R, and poor in RE3R. You're slowly going back the path of RE5 and RE6. So much hope for this game but eh.Edit: more gripes5. Attires are uninspired and limited. Aside from the classic jill attire, Jill has the default and RE1 attire. Carlos has default shaggy hair and classic hair, will probably be addressed by future DLCs6. Aside from cutting off content, Capcom added some sections which are forgettable at best7. 8. Nemesis aside from being a pushover, is almost entirely scripted. Aside from his sprint and combo attacks, he is clearly a downgrade to Tyrant from RE2R. The only time I had problems with him is his last form in inferno where he attacks successively one hit attacks9. The MP game is too broken to be any good. Wish they just focused on the campaign and released the MP game separately as a paid DLC, now instead of one great campaign at 60$ we have one mediocre campaign and a mediocre MP for 60$10. There are only 2 puzzles in this game. Is this even RE3?Final conclusion: Game was definitely rushed and poorly done. A pale imitation of the OG game. This isn't even a horror game. This is an action game with a pinch of horror in it.Don't buy it unless it is on sale. Don't pre-order. Looks like Capcom needs a new lesson again.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very fun for what it is, it's the same story as the original so its fun and intriguing. Gameplay is an upgrade from original and is great. They also really cut down on how much Nemesis encounters you. He's more so limited to boss encounters, you don't really get chased by him a lot, only in the beginning which is a shame. _childDocuments_.review: I Recommend the Remake but I do so with a bit of hesitation------------------------The Resident Evil Remakes are Capcom going back to a series which has slowly lost itself throughout several iterations. A return to stories that aren't as easy to access due to their Console and time while, also, being able to offer a fresh perspective. In my review of 2 I noted that the biggest flaw was that it felt too short. Something boosted by the new controls, new camera, and new combat. It also lacked the effects of where the world doesn't reflect the passing of your characters. A point needed to make sure one play-through isn't as crippled as the other but one that is even more addressed in 3.One can see, easily, the effects of your characters passing between the rooms. The major difference is loot still spawns between the characters and/or disappears should it be left unless the object left behind was a Lock.  It shows how certain situations came into play within the Police Station but does nothing to explain why certain things are simply not there. Did someone move that box? Why is that door now Padlocked when the majority of the compound has already fallen. It isn't consistent but this also doesn't matter.Resident Evil 3 is worth getting on sale. It is worth the price for a chance to come back and it starts to further advance the gameplay from 2 to 3 which leads us into what the 4 Remake is but - key feature - get the game on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game, it did Jill and Carlos Justice, their personalities are great, and the chemistry between the two is very well made. However, Its a shame they axed one of the key features of RE3 on this remake. The alternate routes gave the game an extra layer of replayability, for a linear game that would help a lot.My second gripe with this game is that Nemesis sadly isn't as memorable as Mr. X is on RE2. I still haven't checked the other difficulties to see if his presence is felt more often. Other than that he barely had any chase sequences that werent scripted, and that really sucked. Mr. X would chase you for multiple times inside the RPD and not having nemesis be like that really hurt the overall experience really.The Dodge however is somewhat badly implemented. The Enemies have these bad telegraphs of when they're gonna attack, and do 180 on you every single time you walk close to them, making you have to dodge them 100% of the time. Which sincerely is not a good way to implement dodge systems in your game. The inplementations on the combat are great, and the changes on the Enemy AI that they did (which probably was one of the reasons they didn't have enough resources for everything else) were a welcome change to make you actually have to use the dodge more often. Zombies are way more grabby and faster. You can't just do the same RE2 strategies every time because on enclosed spaces you'll need those perfect dodges to avoid those grabs.I sure hope we get some post launch content like RE2 had, Raccoon City is just too beautiful in this game not to have some extra stuff to go with it. Unless if thats gonna be reserved for REsistance. In the end, if REsistance wasn't a thing and that meant that RE3 could have one extra area or something like that I would've preffered that. Still, the contents of this game are very solid. New Carlos is an amazing redesign that the old one just cant compete at all, and Jill is finally being a badass pro on her way out of a zombie filled city. I wouldn't be angry if Capcom did another game with these two. I'd play it.

_childDocuments_.review: might not be the strongest in any single category out, but hot damn if it's not one of the most consistent entries, too.A remake of 1999's , players step into the shoes of Raccoon City S.T.A.R.S. officer Jill Valentine as she attempts to escape a zombie outbreak threatening to destroy the city; along the way, she unwittingly becomes the partner of a well-meaning corporate mercenary named Carlos, who is unaware of how his employer is directly responsible for the outbreak of undead. In spite of a somewhat complex summary, the bulk of the game flows pretty naturally, with Jill and Carlos attempting to traverse the city and stay alive in the wake of chaos and destruction. Initially comprised of standard, classic  gameplay, the game leans further into action more and more as the stakes of each chapter grow higher and higher. Once again rendered in Capcom's internal Reach for the Moon Engine (or RE Engine for short), it's the most lavishly realized zombie apocalypse the game franchise has yet served up, complete even with ray-tracing, if your PC can handle that sort of thing.A lot of discussion about  centers around how action-centric the game is, and this is fair, on one level.  certainly asks more from the player in combat scenarios than either prior remake in the series, which can be daunting. What is missed in this conversation, though, is how the increased pacing actually helps the game. While most games in the Resident Evil series err towards either the slow survival-horror school of design or else the action-combat-flavored horror school,  finds a sweet-spot between the two. With  enough resources to make it through encounter to encounter, it never felt like the game was being easy on me. It's not necessarily strict "horror" per se, but that's fine; it's wonderfully crafted , and for the game's relatively short runtime, it's a perfect match. In fact, somewhat controversially, I think the game's pacing actually fares better than the more faithful remake of .If there are drawbacks, they fall into one of two camps, neither being a deal breaker. The first is the Nemesis, a super-powered monster that pursues you through out the course of your Zombie Misadventure. In the original release, it was a more systemic part of the game, organically pursuing your and forcing you to reconsider your approach in-game. Here, it's reduced to a cinematic set-piece, stripped of the same mechanical complexity we saw in the remake of . What's preserved, however, is a sense of pacing, and while the Nemesis's presence is less felt in the moment-to-moment of play, the times when you face off against the creature are . Similarly, some may find the game's playtime too short, and a $40 price tag, a 5-7 hour campaign is indeed short. However, not a moment of gameplay is wasted, and the campaign's pacing never feels contrived. In fact, I think  holds the distinction of being the only RE game I've ever played that well and truly lacks a disappointing third act,. isn't the strongest game in the series, with neither the adrenaline packed combat of  nor the tight, terrifying horror of . But that almost doesn't matter. It is almost the ideal version of the game that it , and that's a rip-roaring, tension-laden, zombie-shootin', survival horror romp through the dying gasp of the most '90s city you can imagine. It's great. Perhaps wait for a sale before picking it up, but rest assured, Jill's escape from Raccoon City remains a superb title.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a fan of the original game but was interested in trying the remake to see if it will improve or possibly let me see something I never saw in the OG. This is a very water down version of the original with a very clunky gameplay at points. The dodge works will with one enemy; however, once you get a lot of enemies that are very aggressive and fast (basically the high difficulties), the dodge will not be as good because they can either double lunge to grab you during the dodge or another enemy will do so while you have no chance to counter it (this includes the perfect dodge). This also includes the inability to dodge while you reload in addition to not having the chance to dodge due to Jill recovering from the hit (like getting up etc) since the enemies can move much faster on the higher difficulties. Thankfully, on lower difficulties this isnt as prominent but it is still there. Furthermore, a lot of the bosses are very bland in addition to just being bullet sponges for better or worse. Nemesis third and fourth boss is identical with two minor changes. Speaking of Nemesis, he is VERY downplayed and not as prominent compared to the original. They played another villain of the game more than Nemesis which I did not care for. I do like the fact you can kill Nemmy in certain sections to obtain upgrades or items but it isnt as much as the OG. Oh, and I must mention, the hospital level is so bad. The defend Jill section drags on too long and just seems like padding to the game. The rest of the areas besides Raccoon City seem very devoid of anything very interesting and just appear very generic compared to more iconic areas of the RPD or Spencer Mansion. The only area that stood out to OG RE3 that was original to it was Clocktower which was cut out along with several other areas and unique bosses of the game. The game has more "on rail" sections where you arent really doing much and just seeing some action or running from Nemmy etc. I found them personally annoying because of how often they appear in the game in order to relive Nemmy chasing you in the original. It is just done poorly in my opinion and should have been done to how the beginning of the game did it. I will say, Carlos' character got a major upgrade and thought they did him very well. Jill is a bit hit and miss and appears to be more like RE2R Claire with some minor differences while the other characters are just there. I do like the weapons you can get within the game and using them were fun. I just wish the fire rate of the grenade launcher was faster but otherwise it I enjoyed that. Personally, very disappointed in the game and was expecting more. They cut a lot of unique events, areas and bosses within the game which makes it a very watered down RE2. It feels like it should have been DLC for RE2R rather than its own title. If you are an RE fan and want to try it-wait for it to be cheaper.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a game that played like the RE2 Remake, then sad to say that this is not what you're looking for. If you are looking for a nostalgia hit with updated graphics, then this is still not what you're looking for.The RE3 Remake is an action-packed game, but most of the action you will be doing is dodging and dying; especially if you want to play on hardcore mod to unlock nightmare mode. The knife and grenade mechanic of stuffing these items into zombie mouths when you get grappled is no longer part of the game. The controls feel a little like trying to make a sharp turn with a big rig truck as you tend to swing wide no matter what your mouse settings are, and the aiming for your starting handgun in general does not feel good. I have tried with aim assist off and on - it makes no difference.The claustrophobia the game seems to be trying to create also does not mesh well with how much action is going on at any given moment. There IS an FoV slider, but at this time it remains grey'd out in my options regardless if I am in game or starting from the menu. This has to be a bug, but the way the tight quarters and cluttered space are, I doubt changing the FoV would do much aside from throw off your sense of perspective.And this last one is a bit nit-picky, but Carlos no longer has his Hispanic-American accent. Mikhail kept HIS accent, but Carlos now sounds like a Chad. I'm not certain why they thought to do that.I will say that the game is beautiful, and the story explains some of what the original RE3 did not, but I was personally hoping for another experience like the RE2 Remake provided. Bullet sponge zombies regardless of head-shot accuracy are not particularly fun.I could play on easy mode instead of normal or hard, but I feel like I would be babying myself. If you want tense action from start to finish, this game probably is what you are after - but be warned: the controls are not as precise as they should be.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, but it's very short.  $60 USD is too high even with RE: Resistance.  I enjoy the extra guns. I enjoy the voice acting and facial expressions of the characters. I enjoy the more action focused parts even though I've been playing RE since the first RE2 came out over 15 years ago.  What I do not enjoy is how short the game is.  I managed to stretch a play-through for about 8 hours.  That's with me searching every corner I could find and also restarting a zone if I thought I had missed something or if I was using too much meds. Even then it's apparent the game is very, VERY short.  It's also much more scripted than RE2 remake and possibly any of the RE's out there...except maybe RE6.  That one was very linear.   I've enjoyed this one more than RE6 by a mile.  I would even say I enjoy it more than RE2 remake because of the dodge mechanic.

_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: Playing immediately after the RE2 remake, RE3 is such a massive ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ disappointment.RE3 is on par with DS3. Ludicrously faster gameplay compared to its' predecessor (dodging, QTE, etc), and the game generally feels like it's just some flashy playable thriller movie, going so far as to start the entire game with the main antagonist of the game busting through a wall and kicking the piss and ♥♥♥♥ out of you.Oh, and they completely scrapped the ability to ward off zombies if you get grabbed. Stabbing them? Hah, ♥♥♥♥ no. Stuffing a grenade into their mouth? Aight, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Doing a poorly made QTE to... eh... take slightly less damage? You hit it on the head, brother.The enemies take SO much more ammunition to even stun as well, and even then, their animations are so poorly transmitted I put extra rounds into them to make sure they're stopped.RE3 also revolves HEAVILY around the dodge system they've added, so much so you might as well bind that ♥♥♥♥ to W cause you're gonna need it for every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ region of this game, and definitely crutch on it during the final fight.Larger enemies (specifically Nemesis) are especially horrific to fight, and can straight up stun lock you to death if you make even ONE misstep. Once they get a swing in on you, good luck mashing the dodge button, cause you're not gonna be moving for the next 3 seconds while they liquidate your skull into a bloody pulp.The game also STARVES you for healing (which normally wouldn't be a massive issue), but due to it's heavy leniency on combat, it doesn't make up for the damage you're GOING to be taking in healing items. Onto the plot, the story is sufferable. You're basically playing an action movie character, surviving deadly feats and letting everything break on your plot armour during cutscenes.Oh, and Nemesis is genuinely the worst ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ enemy I've ever encountered in a game. He's not scary, he's not particularly difficult, he's just really. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Annoying. His entire plot point is just "Big man hard to kill, here's generic DPS check number [insert digit]", and other than that, he serves to just follow you around occasionally and make you waste ammo and healing items.All in all, if I hadn't played prior Resident Evil games, I'd say RE3 is a good game. But, I have, so I can't recommend it on any level.

_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: As a Resident evil fan who has played most of the entries over the years, I will say that this game was quite enjoyable. HOWEVER, it is not worth a full $60, but I got it 50% off. Yes it is short (5 hours on my first run), but I find that it is for some people will be quite fun to play through multiple times. It is not as good as the original PS1 version, nor the RE2 Remake which also had its flaws, however this game is still worth a purchase when the price comes down. I am still not done with playing this game, I fully intend to put a few more playthroughs into this game.Did not bother with the multiplayer, will never bother with the multiplayer. It has no reason to exist and I believe this remake would have been better if all the resources that had gone to that garbage had gone to the main campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: A soft recommend, as it is dramatically weaker than the Resident Evil 2 remake.  Re-playability is also reduced.  The gore is toned down, the environments aren't as compelling, Nemesis isn't as ominous or as entertaining as Mr X, and the entire game has a disjointed flow.  The sewer section in Resident Evil 2 had the backtracking and inventory management that we'd come to love in the Police Station, whereas in RE3 it's just a corridor shooter.  The Gammas aren't a puzzle to be engaged with or avoided like the sewer mutants in RE3 were, they're just enemies in front of you to kill that aren't avoidable so there's no depth beyond see monster shoot monster.  Resource management is basically gone after the short city section, as pretty much everything has to be killed.  It's ok, whereas RE2 was amazing.  Very hard to fathom how the one that came out first was the more polished one

_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: Most of my review and comparisons are between this and RE2 Remake.- I would highly recommend this. Even at $40 I would feel this would be worth it.- RE Boomer fans are impossible to please because they don't know what they want and they all want different things.- I enjoyed this far more than RE2 Remake. This felt more like RE4's playstyle. Fairly linear, little backtracking, more story, less puzzles, more action.- I never played the OG on PSX. This game standing on it's own is fantastic. I would honestly replay this over RE2 Remake.- My playtime casually was 11 hours. The playtime on howlongtobeat between this remake and the RE3 OG on the PSX, is about the same. 6+ hours. But a 6 hour playthrough is not possible imo if you play casually. Unless you're rushing and skipping stuff 4 hours seems not possible at all on a first playthough. Yes, RE2 Remake is a longer game if you do leon + claire 2nd scenario. But RE3R's story is more interesting.Pros- Jill. She's is now my favorite RE character.- There wasn't constant pressure like RE2 Remake with Mr. X where you would run to the other side of the police station, only to have Mr. X appear right in front of you. In RE3R, if there is pressure, it is temporary and not constant.- Wielding the knife in RE3 remake made more sense than how RE2 remake did it.- There's no durability to the knife in RE3 remake, which i would prefer but you also can't use it deter a bite either.- Scripted animation sequences were well done, the graphics overall were also very good.- Characters were very high quality, and so were the animations. Mocap I'm guessing was used.- I saw very little reused assets from RE2 remake, other than the police headquarters which was less than 1/8th of the game, and even that wasn't exactly identical.- The story was far more interesting and action packed than RE2 Remake. But less horror survival.- The music was absolutely significantly better than RE2 Remake in every way. RE2 Remake music was either weak or non-existent/silent in areas it shouldn't have been.- I really enjoyed the boss battles. I died a few times, so they felt challenging, but not impossible and they weren't easy I felt.- I didn't feel the game was a walk through the park or overly difficult.- The dodge mechanic is handy.Cons- The laser sight could have been graphically improved other than just a red dot on the HUD...- There are a few bugs, but nothing I felt was a deal breaker, such as collision areas blocking my shots when they should have hit the zambies. Sometimes dialog only occurred if I died first and replayed the scene.- I still don't know what pressing A repeatedly during a zombie bite does... I always get bit and take damage.- There were a few textures (very few) that could have had an increase in res. Fire maybe, nade explosion particles, and a few environment textures I saw, but that's all.- The fire in some places looks somewhat poor and planar, and the animation rate for it felt a little too low to me.- The animation LOD budgeter kicks in at a distance that's a bit too close. This also occurs in RE2, but since you're always inside and you don't seem zambies at a distance usually, you don't notice it as much. So it looks like it's an RE3 only thing but it's not. Basically, when you view zambies from a distance, they animate at a low sampling rate so they look choppy, but I only noticed this in RE3R about 3 times total.- The fire hose sequence with the water spraying at the beginning of the game was quite poor imo, but it's a minor forgettable thing.- The biggest thing I felt could have been better in RE3R were the 1 shot kills/insta deaths. Several times there was nothing I could do to avoid it or I would get stun locked and get his 3 times in a row resulting in death. Mainly with nemesis a couple times, and definitely with the dudes in the 2nd half of the game. So I saved often. I died about 30 times for my first run though this game. Fortunately, there is usually a save point before the 1 shot kills seem to occur, so not much time was lost and it wasn't as annoying as it could have been.Note: Some of these things there are mods for to correct, so that might be something you could look at.Overall the things I noticed that are negative are also minor. The biggest thing being the 1 shot kills. But, despite this, I would definitely suggest playing it anyways, but just make sure you save liberally to avoid some frustration.

_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot of fun, and had some awesome over-the-top action moments I couldn't help but laugh along with. Initially I heard this was a very short game in terms of Triple-A releases and it was a big put off at first, but don't let that deceive you - the gameplay is polished, the new dodge mechanic is great and takes time to master, the UI is minimal, the diologue feels natural and the cutscene transitions are pretty seamless. I don't think you'll be disappointed by the end of the 6~ story, especially if you're already a fan of the series. If you wanted to play a game you can beat in a sitting or two (which is not always a bad thing!), this is what I'd recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: It feels lazy and uninspired but I enjoyed it for what it is.Dodging and sprinting removes any stress from enemy encounters; there is no horror. Ammo us abundant. Puzzles are non existent. Too many save points. The boss fights are repetitive. Some cool enemy designs but you just pepper them with bullets until they die. Also the gore and weapon sound effects are toned down massively, which is ironic since this game is more action focused.it's way too linear compared to the RE 2 police station which connects to every other part of the map. The police station was itself a big puzzle that you solved. In this game all you get are huge empty outdoor areas with a couple of places to explore.It's a more "casual" and digestible experience but offers nothing innovative or interesting while removing parts of gameplay that made RE 2 remake fun. It's essentially a Resident Evil game on rails. Kinda like an Uncharted game, heavily scripted and cinematic, while having mediocre gameplay. It's a pretty ♥♥♥♥ Resident Evil game but an ok action game with some nice cinematography.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the Resident evil 2 remake and played through that one multiple times.  I thought this remake would be on the same level but its simply awful. The original RE3 was weaker than the original 2 and yet I use to like that one on the old PS1.  The RE francisie has always been hit and miss with this being a miss.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: Playing RE3 for the first time I have to say I thoroughly enjoyed this game. I am not a big RE fan and only started with 7, also playing Village and RE2 Remake before this but I feel like this is a fantastic experience.I understand the reputation it has and the inherent shortcomings of remastering a game that was never officially meant to be a numbered-sequel, while also stripping content from it, but something about this experience feels very tight.RE2 has an incredible amount of depth, which is lacking here, this feels far more on rails and straight-forward. I rarely had moments where I found myself stuck for items or wondering where to go. The game is just set-piece after set-piece but oddly it works for me. I find the areas of central RC, the substation, the hospital, NEST 2, all to be visually more interesting than the sewers and police station of RE2. Nemesis isn't all that scary but he works to keep things moving and I enjoyed always being under pressure from him, moreso than Mr. X in RE2.My first playthrough took about 4.5 hours on standard difficulty and there aren't any alternative scenarios here so I can see why people who purchased this at launch weren't happy but for €10 I feel like I got my money's worth.

There aren't many great 3rd person games with this level of polish.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry but did it just take me like 5 hours to beat this game? You can scratch off a good hour and a half to my hours on record because I left the game paused to go to the market and another 20 mins of me messing with the graphics settings. I combed every area of this game as best as I could and read every page of every document because I love the RE atmosphere and it still took me 5 HOURS to beat it. But was it a good game with a good story? Definitely.I'm a newer Resident Evil fan (RE4 was my first) and I'm happy Capcom remade the older games and modernized them, but was the original RE3 this short?! It incentivizes you to do multiple playthroughs by giving you points to buy cool items and an OG Jill skin but it does not even change up the story a bit like RE2 Remake did after your first playthrough. It also feels more linear like my hand was being held throughout the game. For a price tag of $60 I certainly feel cheated, especially with how good RE2R was. If anyone manages to read this review, I suggest you wait until the price drops or there is a sale.EDIT:To address some of the comments: I do plan to play multiplayer, unlock everything, and replay the story on higher difficulties (I played on standard). Yes you can flame me for playing on Standard difficulty but I don’t find dying easily to be very fun, I wanted to enjoy the story and have a decent challenge. Higher difficulties might mean more hours to beat the game, but in my opinion it’s not a valid excuse for the game being as short as it is. To veteran Resident Evil fans I may sound like a moron, but I never played the original RE3 or RE2 so I don’t know what they’re like story and lengthwise, but my disappointment stems from how great RE2R is in comparison to this game.

_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: The best way I can describe this game is;It's the game adaptation of a decent enough film adaptation of the original game. Or...it's an interactive film adaptation of the original game, that's a bit easier to read.After the frankly incredible RE2 remake this IS a cracking let down. If you've played the original RE3 don't go into this with high expectations because it simply won't deliver. It is still a perfectly decent game in its own right but I am very glad that I waited until it was on a decent sale before buying it. Definitely not a £49 game.Overall I actually enjoyed it. Voice acting is spot on, Jill's attitude is amusing, most of the combat is fun aside from the Nemesis being about an eighth as intimidating as Mr X was. The areas are very compressed from the original and you won't likely find yourself running to youtube for help with any of the puzzles. But! A fun, short/sweet zombie shooter nonetheless.One thing that would have seriously given it a bit more ground to stand on would have been the inclusion of Mercenaries mode. Apparently there's a Nemesis Edition on the way so hopefully we'll see something like that when it comes around.

Would still recommend for $10 to $20. I enjoyed it, nice change of pace, good looking game, only wished it was longer. More fluid movement and aiming than what I am used to from RE. Go in knowing that the game is originally called RE3 Nemesis, and make no mistake about it Nemesis is the star of the game, don't let him catch ya!

_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of hate for this remake, most of which seems related to expectations for the remaster vs. reality. As newcomer to the series, I can only judge this game as a standalone item.I played the RE1 and RE2 remasters just before this. I loved that those games centered around a primary location. It felt like it created an icon of those places, opposed to the usual "on rails" feeling in many story driven titles. In other games, you often find yourself rushing from one bit of scenery to the next so quickly that there's little to retain or worth remembering. That was one of the only pieces that felt "missing" to me from the Resident Evil recipe I was getting used to.The graphics are stunning, although oddly demanding on the highest settings. Am RTX 2070 super really struggled to kick out 4k resolutions at decent settings, so I had to settle for 1080p. Not heartbreaking though.The story itself is a bit shallow, only providing you pieces of the puzzle. However, I think that actually gives the Resident Evil titles a reasonable cohesive feeling. Tiny bits of plot add up over the entire series, opposed to other games which build something new with common threads. This definitely works for me!In the end, I consider RE1 and RE2 better games overall but this was still money well spent at just about $1 per hour. There's plenty of replayability if you are into that kind of thing, with some cool features you unlock after your first playthrough. But there's too many games out there now to just grind one over and over in my opinion!

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game in the least.-No Live Selection System.-Minimal replay value with no real rewards for beating higher difficulties-Nemesis is BEYOND gutted, when it's to the point it's just better to throw a single grenade at him rather than running or having to dump an entire arsenal in him(like in OGRE3) something is terribly wrong. He had scripted parts in the original but they were fairly random and the game had far more RNG, this one has NONE.-Virtually no exploration, you play the demo? Cool that was LEGIT 90% of the explorable city. It's painfully linear.-No extra game modes, outside of a sadly rushed side title that was originally meant to be standalone.-Jill suffers from "Bad Sass"On the plus-Great presentation-Carlos is much better.What could have been maybe the best modern RE game is a baffling and shocking misstep on Capcom's part, the game is certainly rushed.Should point out some odd lack of responsiveness in dodging and reloading at times, this does just seem like a bug however.EDIT: On Nightmare and above it takes a whopping TWO grenades to down Nemesis.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 3 is a great reimagination of the original released back in 1999.It has great graphics, good soundtrack, no major bugs and the base story of Jill struggling to escape Raccoon City is very well told.It's important to play this game with a very open mind if you're a die-hard fan of the original.Many things have been removed from the 1999 version. No clock tower, no gravedigger, no cemetery amongst other thingsNemesis transformations are very different from the original too.Even so, it's a very nice game, it's more towards action than horror just like the original.It makes a very slight connection to RE4 and also makes connections to RE2 Remake events.Could've been better if more faithful to the original, but it's a good game nevertheless and Jill is hot

_childDocuments_.review: Like it's predecessor, the RE3 Remake looks gorgeous and plays sooo well. The only slight downside is the Nemesis himself...all of his chase sequences seemed to be scripted to the point where if you press forward or dodge a couple of times you will avoid him - this is a stark contrast to Mr X in the RE2 Remake, who was genuinely sh!t your pants scary, wandering the police station at random and organically appearing much like the Alien in Alien:Isolation. However, the fights against Nemesis are great big bombastic set pieces and Jill is a great character to spend the 10 or so hours this game lasts with. Didn't try the multiplayer - ain't interested - so can't comment, soz.

Rather than ever having to figure anything out, I just blasted my way through hordes of zombies until the game ended four to six hours later. Get this game if it is on sale! I would say $10 or so is a worthwhile price to pay. Downloading 4 now! Hopefully the puzzles will return :)

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say I didn't have fun with this game. It is enjoyable and all-round solid as a experience. That being said, it is a heavily abridged experience that has you fast tracking through one of the most interesting entries in the Resident Evil franchise. The story is cut, enemies are limited, threats are minimal, and even with a lot of exploration and blindly wandering around - the game is a measly 5 hours at best.What is worse, is that you can unlock items that fast-track the experience after you complete it. So you could possibly crunch that time down to something like two hours or maybe even less if you know exactly where to go. Don't worry, Nemesis doesn't chase you down like Mister X does in RE2: Remake - so you'll only really get a taste of his disappointing ass in the many scripted appearances. Basically, someone thought the best way to handle Nemesis was to hit you with as many boss battles involving him as possible. While those boss battles are good, they are ultimately incredibly easy once you find the obvious gimmick in each of them (shoot his back, trip him, etc).This game is overpriced, I'd say maybe $10 at most. You get the multiplayer thingy with it, but its just momentary fun and the population is low right now.

Nemesis comes off as more of an annoyance than anything.  Simply put, the game is far too short and is more action than suspense.  What a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me be clear: This game is fun, its satisfying, and I enjoyed it thoroughly, but IT IS NOT WORTH $60 WITH THE AMOUNT OF CONTENT IT HAS.**SPOILERS AHEAD**The start of the game is rather enjoyable, with Jill's nightmares, and Nemesis chasing you down, but it lacks a lot of the thrill that re2 had since you were going through areas with Mr X chasing you. Whereas with Nemesis, he's far too fast to ever lose sight of you, and you switch areas so often that his threat is hardly noticeable. The scenes where he is chasing you are far more action movie-esque then a game. For instance, I got hit with a rocket launcher three times in one segment, and I survived. Then I ran through the burning building after, and in hindsight, there was absolutely no threat to my life until I go on top of the building. And even then, I dispatched Nemesis without too much issue. I beat the game in 3.5 hours, and that got me a B rank, meaning that above average players will clear the game long before that. TLDR: This is a full price AAA $60 game, and I beat it in 3.5 hours. The scenes with Nemesis feel more like a telltale interaction then a game, and there are many time Im wondering to myself "why is Jill still alive even though Nemesis had so many opportunities to kill her."Wait for a sale.Edit: There aren't any additional single player modes either.

_childDocuments_.review: So I tried getting a refund for this 3 times already, now I'll just give a negative review.This is an abysmal downgrade compared to what the remake did for the second. What does that mean?Ok, granted, that the graphics are nice, it's something great that Capcom did to the series from the seventh entry to here. Graphics in the environment, when I played it I thought it was weird that the textures were not loading but in fact; other game review articles had the same problem. Visiting the STARS headquarters again in RPD with pixelated textures and weird tiled graphics (like the river water); it was disheartening to see the rushed quality on this game.The acting was varied from 7, RE2 and RE3. 7 was okay, RE2 was good, RE3 was somewhere between 7 and 2.Gameplay? I personally think it is great that they used the game and gunplay from RE2. I thought that was the best part. However the sounds from the pistols share the questionable authenticity as it more sounds like ball peen hammers hitting metal sheets covered in a cloth. Carlos's rifle loses a lot of accuracy after firing short bursts. One would think that he would have had some training in firing short bursts or something. It was a weird change of pace to have the space bar be the new dodge mechanic when I was used to it pulling out the secondary weapon like the knife.Nemesis? Oh boy. Let me put it this way, Mr. X was scary and remained scary after I played RE2 for the seventh time. Nemesis is nothing like Mr. X, he is more like Jason X; complete with a lack of scariness. The RE2 RPD demo's teaser with him screaming "STARS!" was pretty scary. I feel as if the people who greenlit the idea to make Nemesis a demon dog thing after the first boss fight was focusing on what is "cool" rather than what is scary. I'm fine with the hermetically sealed trash bag look and the elongated teeth, but it's a bad sign when there is a mod of the original Nemesis model for download (last time I checked).After all that, the biggest cherry on top for me is the lack of real thought provoking puzzles. The need of more action over puzzles has been a real drag when there's no fun for people who love puzzles like me. While RE2 did not have the most complex of puzzles, it was still rewarding when I solved them. I used mnemonic devices to remember the combination locks. I might make a small guide on RE2 to share them. RE3 just has lock picks (I know Jill is the master of unlocking blah blah blah) but it would have been nice to have Carlos figure out new combination locks that I don't already remember (hint, it's the same mnemonic devices I used in RE2.) Perhaps, they could have ACTUALLY put in whatever puzzles that Carlos had to solve from the original.The biggest deal breaker was the inclusion of loot boxes in their shoddily made multiplayer. Now I admit that I never played it and I only saw the gameplay videos (It looked boring). But having some gambling problems myself, so I need to avoid any game that has loot boxes. One could argue that I could never have to play the multiplayer and just focus on the campaign. They would be right. However, I just do not trust myself enough to have the will power to never play the multiplayer part. Even if there's no microtransactions, I just can not scratch that itch and I should just stay away from this game entirely.TL;DRGood on you for having funIt's exciting to shoot a gunBut the lack of puzzlesand the graphics quality muzzled.Sorry but I got to run.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a 9/10 rushed into a 4/10. To Capcom:- Tighten up boss hit stun moves (give me a chance to evade for a frame or two)- Add S+ rank for people who don't use infinite weapons and buff coins- WHERE ARE THE COSTUMES?- Add campaign content immediately. Even if it's ghost survivors out-of-context style, add the content that was cut from RE3.The game's released but it's not finished. Runs great, audio production is great, graphics are amazing. Story plays out fine, character remodels aren't cringe. Game isn't scary. Pretty much one puzzle in the entire game, and it doesn't change up at all between the difficulty modes. This is one of those 50%+ off picker uppers currently unless they add content.Edit:I should have taken a little more time to write this review since it's one of the top reviews on steam. The main issue with this game is that it feels incomplete in important ways. There is literally one in-game costume unlock besides the pre-order bonus. Jill basically walks by the iconic St. Michael Clocktower only to read a brochure about it. That combined with the campaign feeling short-ish gives a very bad impression. Other areas feel awkwardly empty of content, almost as if you're standing in a room that was supposed to have something in it. S+ is not a rank, and you can achieve S rank with infinite weapons, rendering ranks completely irrelevant as achievements. (Something that could be so easily updated.)Clearly they rushed this game out. Like I said, this feels like an incomplete good game, and at full price I can't recommend. One quick update and an announcement for additional campaign content would turn this review around completely.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: buy during a sale.  you can finish this game in under 3 hours if you skip all the cutscenes and linear qte pieces.Sidenote:  The fact that Resident Evil Resistance, the online only asymmetrical multiplayer game is bundled with this game, but is not available as a separate purchase is baffling, and will like mean that both RE3 and Resistance will fail as a result of a bad marketing decision.Mild spoilers***Things they got right:-Remake Nemesis is cool as hell, terrifying and when the game actually allows you to do it; he’s an excellent boss to fight.-Emergency dodge is a really great mechanic that is easy to understand and challenging to master.  It rewards skill while absolutely punishing you for failing to pull it off.-The city hub area also featured in the demo is fun.  -Jill and the other characters look great here, and for the most part they’re fully realized for what limited time you get to see them.-Hunter beta and gamma enemies are fun to fight.Things they fudged:-Most of your time spent fighting Nemesis is actually just a corridor set piece where the only way to progress is simply to run away.  Other than one or two instances where you can stun him, all of your battles against the big guy will be locked into certain boss fight parts of the game, unlike the original.-drain deimos enemies are kind of underwhelming but also tedious and cheap to have to deal with.-The Clocktower, Park, and City Hall hub areas are not in the game.-There seems to be an overall lack of hub areas to explore throughout the game.-The game is very short, even shorter if you skip cutscenes and quickly navigate through the very many set pieces that link the whole thing together.

_childDocuments_.review: So I played the game and I must say, it's a bit underwhelming. After coming from RE2 Remake I can say for certain that RE3 Remake is a massive downgrade, but before I explain why I will start with what the game did better compare to the original.1) Graphics: Ok, that was a given.2) Nemesis revamp: Ok, many people will hate me for it BUT, I love the NEMESIS redesign. He is so more imposing, threatening and WAY more aggressive. I like his second form even more showing the T-Virus mutagenic power. In the original was just a growth of tentacles but, here you have getting bigger and more aggressive. And his third form is even better, yeah he gets out like a b*tch but he goes out in style.3) No ink-ribbons: The were very annoying and I'm happy they got rid off them.4) Script/Characters: They made a tremendously good job in that department. Jill is dynamic, clever, throwing one-liners without sounding insecure. Mikhail has the biggest character remake and I love it, in the original he was just a throwaway character but here you hear his age and what he gone through. Carlos isn't a d*ck, stick shoved up his a** and has a better voice actor.5) Puzzle references: Throught the game you get the characters look at old puzzle references and look confound like the color gems for the time table in the park in order to open the door, or when Carlos founds on of the doors with the specific shaped key and makes fun of it. Now for the bad that keep the game from getting a better "score" for me.1)Nemesis: Unfortunately for his fearsome outlook, he is dump and gets boring fast. He doesn't change his tactics, he only appears in one level and after he gets his second form you BARELY see him. In the original you had random encounters with him in 80% of the game. What a waste opportunity but that gets me to the second problem.2)Short-a*s story: The game is EXTREMELY short! Yeah the original was short also, if you know all the puzzles. Also they removed the puzzles, which makes the game even shorter, and made it almost on rails with too much cutscenes. In 6-7 minutes I passed from the alleyway to the bar to the back alleyway to the warehouse abandon the old guy pass from the news office, the park, the restaurant (which is cut) and got to the metro (originally a tram) in ONE breath. That is a huge disappointment.3)Too many cutscenes: There isn't a moment you don't get cutscenes, even one after another. I beat the game under 3 hours with skipping cutscene and I believe I can shave more time if I skip some I didn't because I was bored.4)No puzzles: Come on guys!!! The game is already short and now without puzzles it's boring too and too much on rails.5)Way too much cut content. It's practicly missing half the game compared to the original. No park, news office, police station, church, water-park, gas station, restaurant, graveyard, hidden laboratory and way too much enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game, but far less faithful remake than Resident Evil 2 Remake was. The knife isn't as bad against normal enemies either, and you can actually kill a standing zombie facing you with it.Only issues I have with the game, beside not being able to see most old memories from RE3 remade, is that zombies are stuck in "rooms". If you walk back and forth a door or up some stairs, you lose aggro and can freely kill zombies. Another thing is that Nemesis, both as pursuer in levels and in some boss fights, can combo you from full health to zero on hardcore without letting the player attempt to dodge the 2nd hit, or even open inventory to heal.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, Massively disappointed and I only played like 35 minutes of the game. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ talk about dropping the ball. _childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 3 is not an unenjoyable game, but I can't in good conscience give it a thumbs up. It's more of a cash grab by Capcom than anything. Capcom rushed this game instead of giving it the proper time to be developed and fleshed out. RE3R has a lot of content that's missing from the original Resident Evil 3. In reality, the original RE3 was short, you could finish it in 5 hours or so, but it had actual replayability. You could redo the campaign and go through different areas that you didn't see in your first playthrough because of choices, and even have different endings for the game with different characters surviving or dying. The original also had Mercenary mode, which added even more replayability as well. Sadly, the current RE3R misses out on the replayability bit, and once you finish the game, there's almost no reason whatsoever to go through it again. It's a once and done kind of game. It's even shorter than the original RE3, and you can finish the game in 3-4 hours. If I had to compare it to Resident Evil 2 Remake, I would say it pales in comparison in many ways. Because at least with RE2R, you were able to feel that the game was well developed and that Capcom had put a lot of time and effort into the game to make it replayable and enjoyable with different branching paths. They took the original RE2 and remade it with care while also improving on the original game. RE3R doesn't do any of that, and Nemesis is a literal downgrade from the original RE3 game. He's scripted and barely shows up, in the OG RE3 he was randomized. He would show up at random times and attack you, and he was definitely more menacing and scarier in the original than he is in the remake. He's not really scary in the remake. He's more of an annoyance than anything else. I actually found Mr. X from RE2R to be a lot scarier than Nemesis was in the remake, which is just depressing. The gameplay is pretty similar to RE2R, but now you have an unbreakable knife and a dodge ability that makes you evade attacks from Nemesis and zombies alike. It's a nice addition, and it works well, but other than that, the gameplay is almost the same as RE2R. However, there is one big difference between the two games though, RE3R is mostly an action game and isn't horror focused like RE2R was, so you're going to be seeing a lot of action and less of the atmospheric horror feel that you got from RE2R. How about the graphics? I can tell you that the graphics are as good as RE2R because they obviously use the same engine, but sadly the game was downgraded when it comes to dismembering the zombies. You can no longer dismember zombies like you did in RE2R. I feel it was downgraded to allow the consoles to run the game smoother since the areas in RE3R are a lot bigger than RE2R, and they do throw more zombies at you to deal with, so they downgraded the game just so the consoles would be able to run it well. I'm also not a fan of how they redesigned Jill's model. I feel the new face doesn't look remotely similar to the original or previous games. I won't dwell much on this point because it might be subjective, but overall I was not a fan of the new redesign. The game also came packaged with Resident Evil Resistance, I personally feel it should have never been bundled with the RE3R, and it should have been a separate game that's f2p or has the same model as Dead by Daylight. It took development time away from RE3 to make this game, and I feel it wasn't needed. RER, as It's currently, is a mess, the game doesn't have dedicated servers, and It's solely reliant on p2p hosting, which comes with its own issues. The game has many game-breaking bugs and glitches that the devs are very slow to fix, and it also relies on a loot box system to unlock items and cosmetics, in 2020 I can't for the life of me understand why this mechanic still exists for progression. I haven't delved a lot into Resistance, but my early impressions are not good. Now, what are the good things about the game? Well, I can tell you that the action bits are enjoyable, and being in open areas feels a lot different than RE2R and gives you a different atmosphere than the previous game in a good way. Also, having to deal with hordes of zombies and other enemies all at once definitely puts you on the edge of your seat and can be challenging. Sadly, that never lasts long because the action setpieces are short, but are definitely the most memorable parts of the game. All in all, Resident Evil 3 Remake is a forgettable experience, and a missed opportunity by Capcom and the game isn't an improvement on the original like RE2R was. Capcom took the short route for this game, and it shows. It's such a shame, this game could have been so much better, but greed won out in the end with Capcom. My overall rating for the game is 6.5. I can only recommend buying this game if it's on a big sale. Otherwise, It's not worth the full price tag at all, and you would be wasting your money for a game that only lasts for 4-5 hours tops with almost no replayability whatsoever.

_childDocuments_.review: Really solid survival horror experience, but not a lot of content and replayability compared to other Resident Evil installments. RE3 steps away from the openness of RE0, RE1 and RE2 with more linear level design that doesn't involve much backtracking or puzzles. The game seems to expect you to fight enemies more than you would be expected to in the previous titles, but the game definitely gives you the firepower to handle anything thrown at you. You also have more capability to avoid enemies mid-combat, with a perfect dodge-roll for Jill and a perfect counter for Carlos. The enemy design and diversity is well done as with most RE games, forcing you to fight them differently and with different weapons in your arsenal. Nemesis provides amazing tension throughout the game. As you would expect, he appears at the most inopportune times to make your life miserable and make your objectives more difficult to carry out. The threat that Nemesis poses always looms over you in the beginning portion of the game, when he is in his first stage. The boss fights with Nemesis are engaging and a fun challenge, and they demonstrate what an interesting bioweapon he is. The character interactions provide corny one-liners and charming interactions, and the story rounds out the beginning three Resident Evil games well. Having played RE4 and RE5 before this game, it's easy for me to see that this is where RE games started to take a new direction, with more level-to-level based design rather than placing the player in an open setting like the mansion and having them explore their surroundings. Personally, I like both types of Resident Evil experiences, but regardless, this game should cater to fans on either side of the spectrum. However, I do think the game is lacking in content, since there is only one route in the game while most RE games have at least 2 routes. The game seems to attempt to make up for this by adding an additional difficulty, Nightmare, and of course the game comes with the multiplayer game RE: Resistance. Resistance is good additional content for sure, but Nightmare is not a good enough replacement for a route. I never played the original RE3, but as I understand it did not have a second route, so not adding a second route is probably more faithful to the original game. Nevertheless, I would hope that a remake would dedicate itself more to adding content that adds to the original content of the game it is reimagining. Regardless, RE3 is a great survival horror game, but it might not be worth 60 dollars.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall good game, but not as good as RE2 Remake.  As a matter of fact, I can copy/paste most of my review from that game, as little has changed gameplay-wise and aesthetically from that.  See below for that, as well as a “What’s New” section added to each category:GRAPHICS: Realistic facial expressions, environments loaded with personality (just like the original PS1), great detail in everything ranging from the monsters to the weapons. The game looks too sweet at 1440p, 144 fps.What’s New:  Nothing, really.  Everything is identical, even many of the zombie character models, background objects, weapons, items, etc.  There are a handful of newer monsters, including “yours truly” from the game’s cover art, but that’s it.  Still looks great, but don’t expect to be wowed again.`````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````SOUND: This to me is the key element of any horror game. The eerie sound of silence mashed up against a subtle air vent rustling, or was that a monster growling........? Uh oh, better approach that corner carefully in case something tries to eat me. The score kicks up in intensity when you engage in battle, which further fills the situation with dread. The only negative I can say about the sound is the voice acting (or should I say script) almost sounds like a teenager wrote it at times. The voice work itself is great, but there's waaaaay too much swearing to the point where it just feels overplayed. A good "F-you" can give a situation that needed punch, but it loses meaning when it gets thrown out every other sentence.What’s New:  Again, nothing much.  The sound continues to get the job done, but many of the same sounds from RE2 Remake are recycled, making for less of a fresh experience.  You’ve heard many of those groans and shrieks before, but there are still a few audible surprises that might get you.`````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````GAMEPLAY: The most important part of any game. This being a remake of the original RE2, comparisons will naturally be made here. Gone are the tank controls, in favor of the RE4 style over-the-shoulder view. Therefore, combat is more particular and aiming based, allowing the user to perform head shots, or slice off limbs, or come up with other creative ways to stop the undead. The overall environmental layout mirrors that of RE2, including some of the puzzles, though they do kind of hold your hand in some spots to guide you to the next objective. Controller and keyboard/mouse options both play wonderfully. Added is a much welcomed "Assist Mode" that can help players recover health automatically over time, aim assist in hitting critical areas on enemies, and generally easier difficulty. For those who enjoy punishment though, the Hardcore difficulty gives players just enough ammo, health items, save opportunities, and harder enemies to get through to claim victory. The end of each game is graded based on the difficulty, time, and number of times saved on a scale of C through S. Obviously getting that S will earn you better goodies if you're skilled enough to achieve it.What’s New:  Yep, you guessed it!  Nothing much is new here either.  You’re still solving puzzles as usual, though there seems to be even fewer compared to the RE2R.  Was there a time in crunch in finishing this game or something?  I wrote a guide for solving RE2R’s puzzles to help me speed run, and that thing took up almost 4 pages (including diagrams).  This game:  less than half a page!  The few puzzles that are in this game are pretty simple, and combat is just a continuation from RE2R.  You’ve seen this and played this before.  Of course, there is a different story behind this game which takes slightly different twists and turns compared to the PS1 original, so this aspect will be the main highlight for playing.```````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````REPLAY: As you can see by the number of hours I poured into this game, there's a lot to see and do! Being a master at it, I'm now able to get through the game on Hardcore difficulty in less than 2 hours, but my first playthrough was closer to 7 hours. There are 4 different scenarios in the main campaign to play through, so you can see where all that time goes. After the main campaign, there are additional Ghost Survivor challenges to complete, as well as weekly challenges issued by Capcom. To fully 100% the game, you're tasked with performing certain challenges to unlock all the artwork, character models, and infinite weapons. Some challenges are as easy as "Shoot a zombie in the head 10 times" or as hard as "Get S+ rank on Hardcore mode".What’s New:  Well, get ready for a big difference here.  I fully 100 percented this game in less than 40 hours at the time of this review.  There’s less content here compared to RE2R, so a good speed runner can finish this game in less than 1.5 hours easy.  After that, you unlock a few more difficulties and that’s it!  No extra scenarios or special gameplay modes, which is kind of a downer since the original RE3 was known for that fun Mercenaries Mode.  ```````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````So who is this game for? Anyone who likes the Resident Evil series, newbies who have no idea what Resident Evil is but lover horror, and even those folks who are terrible at third person shooters (thanks Assist Mode!). There's something for everyone here. Still a good game, but one that you shouldn’t pay full price for compared to the value that RE2R offers.  Maybe wait for a “LEGENDARY” Steam sale for less than $20 one of these years so you get your money’s worth.  Otherwise if you’re a diehard RE fan, you’re going to play this game either way.  This game is worth your time for the right price.

_childDocuments_.review: 4 Years later and 15 hours of play being able to do quite a few play through's and unlocking plenty of extra content, I can't really recommend, but at the same time I do... Hear me out..The nostalgia is just not really there. I'm torn because RE 3 Nemesis was one of my absolute favorites before OG 4 hit the market. I was beyond excited when RE 2 Remake happened. I was shocked at how amazing that game was as whole, and how true they kept it to the original with some creative changes (always having Tyrant around, not just in 2nd scenario, and some others).Then we got RE 3 Remake... I was expecting more after RE 2 remake and we got a shell of a remake... Like many others have stated, this remake cut out SO much content from the original for seemingly no reason at all! Why?! The restaurant sections, the train, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Clock Tower! All cut out. The city roaming portion was pretty meh too. With no extras, you can beat the game within 2 hours. With extras, under 2 hours. It is still fun to play, don't get me wrong, but if you're like me and looking for a nostalgia fix, it's not there imho. Get it on a sale, don't pay full price for this. You'll have a bit of fun going through and unlocking the extras to run through again like a boss. I haven't gone back to play after the 15 hours as I kinda did all I wanted to in that time sadly..
