_childDocuments_.review: If it isn't broken. Don't fix it. Cons: The devs were so faithful to the source material for RE 2 Remake. What happened? No clock tower. No park. No graveyard boss fight. No cinematic last minute 'choice system'. The once iconic-looking Nemesis now an eye-sore and looks like a Blue Meanie with lasagna on his face. No more strategic dismemberment (kinda douche-y because now you can't make sure enemies stay dead or crippled) - also, there are corpses lying around that you KNOW are gonna get you later that you can't do anything about. No ink ribbons. No blue herbs. No giant spiders. No more using to the knife to save your *** before getting chomped on. Countering with the knife does literally nothing and the dodge system feels awkward and ill-fitting. Very few puzzles (I think there are like two). The game is very linear and lost the charm and sense of dread of the original. They giveth and then they taketh away. Pros: The graphics are mind-blowing and some of the boss fights are amazing. Overall, this game feels like a tech demo in the form of an extended DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: With all due respect, i did enjoyed my time playing this game.As an RE fan, i love seeing RE3 being remade as it was one of the earliest games i still remembered my brother playing it on our PS1.I enjoyed the map, the weapons, the enemies and the mechanics of the game. However, i would not recommend this game solely for its price, replayability, and total play time.Compared to last year RE2, this game didnt achieved what RE2 did so spectacularly, which is what make an RE game good. To me, that is survival horror.Yes, RE3 back in the day was much more fast paced, and action orientated. However, that does not mean they should ignore what made RE2 remake a big success in the first place.1. Zombies : Compared to RE2, RE3 zombies are not as threatening. RE3 makes it possible for the player to kill each zombie without being paranoid on running out of ammo for the next area. This is because both the zombies became easier to kill, and the abundant ammo provided in the game. This takes the fun on what make Resident Evil a horror game.2. Nemesis : As cool as he is, he is scripted to appear in certain events. Compared to Mr. X in the previous game, Mr. X will chase the player almost everywhere in the RPD. Nemesis did not have that niche despite being the main cover of the game. Although the original RE3's Nemesis was also scripted to appear at certain time, that does not RE3 remake should do so.3. Options/Choices : In RE3 original, there were moments for the player to pick the route/options in specific events. This mechanic could have been used for RE3 Remake as it would shine out differently from RE2 remake. My last complain would be the price. As the game comes together with Resident Evil : Resistance, i did not enjoyed my time or even looked forward on playing the online platform of RE. As some other players such as myself agreed, that the reason we bought this game is primarily for RE3 remake, not the online version of it. If there was an option for me to buy only RE3Remake without the multiplayer option thus making my purchase total cheaper, i would have done so.All and all, i still love the game, but i wouldnt recommend for newcomers to purchase this as the price is too expensive for its flaws, RE2Remake is a better option for newcomers.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of the RE series, so this was a must-play. A very solid and fun game, but honestly not the best "remake." If you're familiar with the original RE3, you'll be a bit disappointed and let down by some of the changes, or more specifically, how much of the old game they didn't include (certain enemies, bosses, and locations were cut completely}. Nemesis is terrifying, but we don't quite get as much of him as in the original. As a standalone game, this is a solid 9/10 for sure. Very fun, scary, and action packed.As an RE3 remake though.. pretty tepid, maybe a 5/10, just because of how much was deliberately changed or left out. Also a pretty short game (I beat it in 6 hours on my first run, and less than 2 on each of my consecutive runs).Worth a play for sure for any RE fan or Survival horror fan, but may be worth waiting on a price cut if you're not

_childDocuments_.review: This was quite dull, so short and disappointing.  Very few weapons, no legit new game+ so scripted and predictable. The world was 99.7% unreactive.  Very very few items could be shot or used, play enough to get the shop unlockables n you can finish the game in under 1hr 30 mins.  Some of the landing n jumping of the characters felt like I was playing a 70 yr old senior citizen not highly trained paramilitary types.  Which technically could describe Jill to.  RE4 was much much more fun.  Even the "puzzles" in 3 remake were bad.  Some of which took me much longer than they should since I just played RE1 remake n thought they would be harder...just to find out no they were actually as easy as they seemed, and I overestimated them.  Also was full of G.F.YS. barriers....which is what I call a obstacle that a literal toddler could get thru / around with little to no effort. Yet it somehow totally impedes the path of a supposedly highly trained fully grown non handicapped operative. Those blocks just make me feel like the game is in effect saying "Go ♥♥♥♥ Yourself".  Due to the blockage being so insanely easy to circumvent but magically impossible.  Didnt like not being able to break doors down either despite Carlos senpai doing so frequently.  Which Jill had similar moments of what I would regard as "selective competency" where the char is able to do something that is clearly obvious to do, but perplexingly only in very specific situations.  Example, Jill squeezeing thru the shelving units in the underground....but not being able to just climb up the boxes n moving over the fallen cage box thing to get one of the fuses.   If a game is going to prevent pathing, fine...all I ask is that it provide a good logical reason as to why I cant go a certain way.  Near the start of RE3 remake, having to put out the fire to proceed is a fine example of a logical obstruction.  Or if an object is electrified...makes a good reason why you couldnt climb on it.  In RE1 remake, while not being able to do something very possible and extremely easy irl like usin the shotgun to breach locked doors.....it would have been a nice touch imo if when interacted with, info text would say something about the door being specially reinforced, thus giving you a lore / in-universe reason breaching it wouldnt work.While the weapon customization ability was certainly a neat feature....the weapon mods were quite limited still.  When you also dont have many weapons to obtain in the 1st place though, it just makes the situation worse.  So ultimately, If you want this just as a novelty or part of a RE series collection Id say only buy it on sale like I did (70% off at the time)  Cause it certainly doesnt feel worth the 40 ish dollars it costs when not on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I also love seeing the reviews hating on it for being short. As if the original RE:3 wasn't pretty short itself. Some areas are cut out I will agree, but the areas that are in get much more attention, you spend a lot more time at the hospital for example. Expect your first playthrough to last about 6 hours on a standard pace, if you take the time to look at read all the notes and view all the cutscenes of course. To get S ranking expect to complete the game at 1:45 for hardcore. They did a good job at encouraging following playthroughs, minor rewards you can pick up over time making each run easier, and earning your way to the infinite weapons. The soundtrack is an actual soundtrack, which has a good amount of remastered RE:3 soundtrack, which is amazing. Compared to RE:2 remake where I used the original audio versus the remastered audio, I would pick the remastered tracks over original for RE:3. Guns are sastifying to shoot and while you can get yourself quite a bit of ammo if your frugal, you will lose a lot of time in the process. So you have to determine which ammo is vital to get to progress if you want to get a good time. My only complaint is how quickly the game picks up, the beginning feels much like a action movie, and while it does settle down I do prefer how the original was over this remake. I see how people see this beginning and complain, however I like how they handled Nemesis. He is much more linear then how Mr. X was handled, but they managed to retain some mechanics that you see from the original game that wouldn’t really have meshed well with a free-roaming boss. I will agree with other reviews that not having the live selections that the original had is disappointing, and does slightly hinder replayability. But I personally can overlook it.Second-ish complaint, although I’m hoping a mod will fix it soon is the fps issue for zombies farther out, as RE:2 remake had. TL:DR; Get the game, don’t spoil yourself of that magical first playthrough. I ignored all media until I played it and I do not regret a single moment. Just be open to a little reworking of how Jill escapes Racoon City compared to the original and you will have a great time.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: There's not enough to justify $60, or even $40 when I bought it. I felt more annoyed throughout the game rather than immersed like RE2 remake. I beat it casually on normal in 5.5 hours total.Pros:It's a visually awesome game with a good amount of graphic customization which was appreciated. I didn't run into any glitches like most big titles nowadays.Cons:The Little to no item space was a burden more than a feature of a "choose your items wisely" mechanic. During the item collection periods of the story I was actually running back to a safe room just to make some space. The camera movement alongside the way the game promotes the dodge mechanic is also frustrating. I felt like I'd have to choose between seeing the enemy or my positioning. Then getting the dodge off wasn't rewarding most the time. The game was too short. Period. Did anyone think Zombies were just bullet sponges? I just moved around them most the game and took a hit every once in a while and healed it up due to all the healing items around.

I took my time and explored. I own every Resident Evil game and canon movie that has been made, I don't count the Milla Jovovich movies as canon. Maybe I'm biased because I love the series. This, in my opinion, is a solid remake. That's the key word here though. It's a REMAKE, not a REMASTER. That being said, this may not be for some people. Some people may not like it. If you don't, that's OK. What i will say is this.... if you enjoy the RE series, give it a shot. Buy it at full price or at a discount and enjoy it for what it is, not what it used to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I wish I didn't buy this. It is nowhere near as masterfully crafted as the original resident evil 3. Some of, if not, all of the Nemesis encounters are scripted and quite boring. Nemesis is nowhere near the same level of threatening as he was in the original, as by dropping a grenade he just dies. That's it. And the rewards you get from "killing" him are not even that good. You'd probably get a couple grenade launcher rounds and thats it. And even then, I never really found myself using the grenade launcher all that much since majority of the threats were zombies that could be taken down in maybe 2 shots from the starter pistol. The amount of gunpowder you find doesn't really help either. For the most part, the game was a cutscene. It's more like a movie than an actual game. Its also really short as this is the fastest I have ever finished a resident evil game. The map is about two streets, a sewer, a smaller version of the police station, and a lab with a couple rooms. Thats about it. Jill isn't really as likeable as she was in the original either, as majority of her lines were just cursing and insulting the very guy who helped her during her first encounters with Nemesis. It was funner playing as Carlos than it was playing the actual main character, Jill. For a game that's the same cost of RE2:R this really sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could have been so much better if they followed down the same path of quality RE:2 had. Much easier game even on higher difficulties, less back tracking, less replay value and a little more action than puzzle solving and exploring.Too many short cuts taken by the devs in my opinion, nemesis is so scripted that he spider man's out of area's when you pass into an area that he isn't programmed to enter rather the roam and patrol to add intensity. _childDocuments_.review: Where do I start... sigh...Let's just say, it was not what I expected - both in a good and a bad way.I started of hating this remake, as Capcom removed a lot of the content from the original and changed the way Nemesis behave and transforms. This 2 ton monster now slings himself around like spiderman, and leeps like he was a ballet dancer. He even looks wrong if you compare him to the original and the movies! I know this is a remake, and what that means - but still.Capcom had enough respect for the old RE2, to make a decent remake that still keeps a lot of stuff from the original.This however makes for a whole new RE3: Nemesis, that only gives a few pointers of its origin. Such as Nemesis drops crates when downed, explosive barrels in the streets, use of a firehose to extinguish a fire, Jill getting infected, mixing the vaccine, a dodge mechanic, characters, and a couple of other stuff. But more or less the whole game is changed. The story unfolds somewhat different, though with a few sequences remaining from the original and the map layout has been changed a lot!On the positive side however, it gets very fun the moment you unlock the "infinite rocket launcher" and are able to take revenge on all the stuff that annoyed you during the first playthrough.The shop where you buy the rocket launcher, is open as soon as you complete the game once.In short: If you expect to get a "remaster" of the good old RE3: Nemesis, you will be dissapointed.They put this up for 59,99€ at the time of writing this review, and that in my opinion is way to much for what you get here.-I would recommend this game, if you find it on sale for ~50% off. Otherwise I would recommend RE2 remake over this.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly am surprised at how accurate some of the early reviews have been about this game. It really is not worth paying £50 for this game, this truly could have been a DLC for 3. Before you think *Oh well the original was not much either* I know that. But for this game to get a remake and actually have good reason to be remade, doesn't do much. To get the quick review out of the way:  This game doesn't expand on the nemesis, actually in comparison to the original and RE2 remake, Nemesis in this is so scripted that he is barely a threat. The game is short, very short, as in even if you take your time to admire anything you will finish it within 5 to maybe 6 hours. Speaking of admire, there's not much to look at other than what you have already seen in RE2 Remake. Yeah there are some new buildings and the layout looks different. But the amount of re-used assets in this game from RE2 is mind blowing, and funny enough if you look at the end credits you may see that not a lot of people worked on this game, probably more worked on sound design alone than anything else.Graphics, yeah graphics are good, stunning even, the RE engine is a beauty. not much else to say there.In detail, I am really let down by this game, the biggest thing is the absolute lack of content. the puzzles are dead easy, there is barely any backtracking in this game compared to others and some are just there to get gun accessories and more ammo. The sections with Carlos are really just filler to get the game over with, they don't try to add anything to his character other than he has a mission. Some of the things to build this game excitement are a joke, like saying you will get to find out how some areas in RE2 became the way they did, maybe you may meet old characters. _childDocuments_.review: Before I go into my review, I really need to make this clear. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME AT FULL PRICE. MAKE SURE IT'S AT LEAST 50% OFF IF YOU'RE INTERESTED IN BUYING THIS GAME.RE3 Remake is a good game. Unfortunately, it's VERY lackluster compared to it's older sibling (RE2 Remake). The game is shorter than RE2, it lacks puzzles, and to top it all off, Nemesis was wasted potential.If you've played the RE3 demo that came out a while before the full game, you may remember Nemesis behaving like Mr. X, which was really cool. Only difference was that he was even more relentless and he could even RUN. That sold me back when I played it. However, upon playing the full game, imagine my disappointment when I learned that these instances of Nemesis chasing you like that only covered A FIFTH of the game. A short game, even. After that part, every Nemesis encounter ends up just being a fight around an arena. As he NEVER chases you like Mr. X did in 2, which really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks.RE2 had plenty of post-game content you could play like "4th Survivor" and "Ghost Survivors". And even then, you could always play the main game again because it has so much replayability. This game however, has ZERO post-game content outside of it's main game and unlockable difficulties. And even so, the replayability of RE3 is significantly weaker than RE2. Granted, this game does have a shop menu where you can get secret weapons, stat coins, infinite weapons and so on, but honestly, that's about it.Despite all of this, why did I still enjoy this game? Because the gameplay was fun! Having access to an evasive roll for Jill and a counter for Carlos was sick, which also made sense since those two are VERY experienced in combat compared to Leon and Claire in 2, who are just rookies. The story wasn't bad, which doesn't really say much since the story in RE games are not so consistently good (Except RE8 which is the best RE game story wise). And despite me criticizing the replayability of this game, it was still there. But what was most important for me was the atmosphere. The design of Racoon City being thrown amidst chaos was a sight to behold, since in RE2 you were mostly in RPD and at the NEST. There certainly were moments where I enjoyed the view whenever the opportunity was there.This game had a lot of swings which hit and missed. Fortunately for Capcom, there were enough hits for me to enjoy the game despite its many flaws. But again, I can't in good conscience recommend anyone to buy this game at 60 bucks. It's just not worth it. If this game had post-game content like "Mercenaries" mode, then MAYBE I'd recommend it at full price.Verdict: Good game, but buy it when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a helluva lot better than the original RE3.  Unfortunately, RE3 wasn't a great game to begin with.  And this is just a prettier version of the shortest Resident Evil. And if you want to unlock everything and get all the achievements, you will be playing that same story over and over again.  By the time you've got it mastered, it will barely take you over an hour from start to finish.  Capcom did take the worst of the series (except 6 of course) and make it a fun experience. _childDocuments_.review: The Pros:Great visuals.solid gameplay (tho the camera can be a little funky at times).The story is great.The atmosphere is just as Tense as REmake 2, especially in later areas of the game.Nemesis is absolutely fantastic in this game and i would say is the best incarnation of him outside of the original RE3.The boss fights are top notch and all look amazing.The game has quite a few collectibles to increase that replay value, along with additional difficulties.The Cons:So many areas from the original game do not make an appearance in this game.Which is weird, because Capcom have said they've been developing this game for three years.A lot of the gore have been removed from the Zombies.You can shoot off their limbs and the headshot is still there, but it's lacking that punch from REmake 2.The story, while not bad by any means, has been atered so much and is missing a lot of scenes from the original game that i was hoping would be in.They removed the Grave digger boss fight, which i was looking so fawrd to,The lack of Mercenaries in order for them to work in Resistence is a huge dissapointment to me.As amazing as Nemesis is in this game, i really wish that he had more of a presence in this game like he did in the original RE3, or like how Mr X was in REmake 2.Overall, i really did enjoy REmake 3 and for what the game strives out to be, it really did succeed in so many areas, but let me down in so many other areas.I would recommend that if you're going to buy this game, try and get it on a CD key website with a price tag that makes more sense than the full AAA price tag, because while i love the game for it is, i would not buy it at full price.Again, it;s not a terrible game and i absolutely do recommend it i just don;t recommend it at the price it's at right now on here.

_childDocuments_.review: While it does not stay true to the original, it is a pretty good reimagining of the original. The story flows a lot better in this game than the original. However, I don't feel the same sense of urgency in running away from Nemesis as I did in the original. That could be because it was legitimately more difficult or just that I was much younger when I played the original. In all, I think the game was fun, but it lacked the replay value of the RE2 remake. This game can absolutely be finished in less than an hour and a half. My fastest clear was just over an hour, but that's if you skip a bunch of ♥♥♥♥ and do a lot of ammo conservation (save all of your grenade launcher ammo. Craft mostly explosive ammo). The harder difficulties do not feel difficult or imposing at all. If anything the most annoying thing about the harder difficulties is the very last fight with Nemesis and that's only because he attacks pretty fast and can catch you off guard if you aren't that great at dodging. In all, I would give RE3 a solid 7.5/10. If you never played the original, this is definitely worth picking up though honestly unless you absolutely have to have it, I'd wait until it goes on sale as the campaign (even if not speed running) is quite short for a full price game (though I'm not surprised by this as the original was intended to be finished in 3 hours or less)
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: - Let me just start by giving my  on how long the game is. Yes, roughly five hours. Now look up any longplay, or average playtime for the original game, and you'll find out that they're surprisingly similar. Resident Evil games have always been rather short and intended for speedruns. The only thing that might have made the classics longer were the more in-depth puzzles, which I'll come back to, and the fact that games back then were generally more difficult. Again, this is my , and you're free to disagree, especially if speedrunning isn't your cup of tea.- The game still tries to encourage replayability, with two unlockable difficulties, and unlockable items for New Game+.- While it follows the same story as the original for the most part, the game is far from being a 1:1 remake, and reimagines a lot of things. If you're looking for an experience similar to the original game, then you will not find that here. If you're open to a new experience though, or haven't played the original, then I'd say you'll have fun!- Dodging is reintroduced from the original and expanded upon, and completely replaces defense items from RE2 Remake, which feels much more rewarding to me than simply pressing your Get Out of Jail Free Card™ button when you get grabbed.- There are a few tributes to the original Resident Evil, such as the full motion opening cutscene and .- The new character designs look absolutely fantastic, and Jill's not running through Raccoon City while wearing an inconvenient tube top and short skirt anymore. With that being said, Jill and Carlos' original appearances were available as preorder bonuses. Also Carlos isn't a recolor of Leon anymore.  - No original game OST option this time around, but the new soundtrack offers a few pleasant surprises.- With the game reimagining a lot of things, a lot of iconic moments from the original RE3 are nowhere to be seen. The Clock Tower's here alright, just don't expect to be exploring it.- Back on puzzles from the first paragraph, they are almost completely absent in this reimagining. The only proper puzzle appears moments before the end of the game, and can just be easily bruteforced.- Encountering Nemesis is much more scripted and predictable, which feels like a big downgrade from the original game.- Mercenaries mode is, as of now, absent from the game, and technically replaced with Resistance. While not that much of an issue to me personally, I get why people would complain about that one, and I hope to see it come back as a (free?) DLC.- It's Resident Evil Mercenaries meets Dead by Daylight meets Tower Defense. And it's a fun concept. Survivor mostly plays like normal Resident Evil/Mercenaries gameplay, killing enemies and completing objectives to get extra time to escape the map. On the other hand, Mastermind plays like a Tower Defense strategy game, where inflicting damage on the survivors will take time away from them until you run out the clock and win. You can also take control of most of the creatures to deal out damage personally. Did someone say playable G-Birkin and Mr. X?- At the time of writing this review, you get 6 Survivors, with Jill being added as part of a free content update on April 17th, and 4 Masterminds, all of them having unique abilities and counters, and they are fairly customizable, from alternative skills to passive equipment, as well as custom card decks and map layouts for Masterminds. There's also plenty of cosmetics available, ranging from alternative skins for Survivors, weapons and each type of creature, as well as Mastermind voice lines you can play whenever you want, and emotes for Survivors and zombies.- Four maps as of now, with each one having its own theme. As said above, the items and enemies layout can be customized by the Mastermind, so you'll often get a different experience each time depending on the kind of player you're up against.- Similarly to Resident Evil 3, the OST offers a few surprises, with remixes of G-Birkin and Mr.x's themes. The music that plays when time is running out is also one of my personal favorites.- The game, while bundled exclusively with RE3 as of now, is completely standalone, which means you can uninstall one once you're done with it, and still be able to play the other. - As it is a concept similar to Dead by Daylight, do not expect this game to ever be balanced properly if you want to have fun. Looking at you, January and Becca mains at the time of writing this review.- Matchmaking times can be highly inconsistent for both sides, sometimes spending 10 minutes in a queue before even finding players. It also relies on your Steam download region, so feel free to try changing that up if you're having issues finding matches.- It's a peer-to-peer game, and all it takes is a Mastermind having bad internet for the game to become unplayable.- Really needs a report button, if only for the lagswitching MMs.I personally like the fact that the Resident Evil 3 Remake tries to be different from its original counterpart, and I've been getting multiple runs in for personal giggles. Resistance is a fun alternative to Dead by Daylight if you can do your best to ignore the minor issues with it, though I understand why some people have bigger issues with that game.

_childDocuments_.review: After reading many reviews of RE3, my expectations were exceptionally low for this remake. I am a huge fan of the series, however, so I decided to buy it while it was on sale.I do get surprised by some reviews. There are things I disagree on. Here is what you can expect:: expect 4-5 hours of gameplay your first run. The campaign omits many areas and puzzles from the original RE3 game. : Very good! : as much as some areas could be made more difficult, others WILL offer you a bit of challenge. You WILL die. Several times. : there is abundance of ammo and you probably won't experience the lingering stress of scarcity that we know and love from RE. : the game is relatively linear for being a RE game, correct. But there IS definitely some optional backpedaling to acquire some upgrades.: you can play the campaign 2-3 times to try to beat your initial game time and complete some achievements. That was fun for me.: encounters with Nemmy are short lived, yet I would argue that they can be intense sometimes. There is little randomness to his patterns of attack. I can see why this is disappointing for some. But he is still powerful, and will definitely be the reason for some frustration as he will kill you. I have now played through the campaign twice, and I think the game has recieved way too much negative critique. As long as you accept that the game is 4-5 hours of gameplay your first run, you will enjoy it. Again, I bought it on sale, so maybe that's why it doesn't bother me as much. Try to view it as a DLC campaign for RE2 and you are good to go. If you want to make it harder, play it on Hardcore.

_childDocuments_.review: What does it do better than RE:2 Remake? - Introduced New Shop System which makes getting the points achieved from Rewards fun. - New Dodge mechanic spices up the gameplay - Running from Nemesis is scary as hell (I dare say more intense than the Mr X) - Introduces Nightmare and Inferno Mode (Though I haven't played them yet, but it allows for multiple play-throughs. - Small thing, but I enjoyed RE:3's save room music more. (But that's just my opinion)What does it lack in comparision? - Zombie placement doesn't feel right to me. In RE:2 you had more opportunities to just pass by the zombies, but in RE:3 it seems like they want you to do more killing. - While the dodge mechanic is cool, it is a bit finicky and probably needs some work. (More like definitely.) - RE:2's beginning setting felt like there was a lot more to explore rather than the beginning for RE:3 - Jill and Carlos's story are merged into one. There are no A or B scenarios. So it's just one story unlike RE:2, which had four in total. But to be fair, the multiple scenarios did just reuse most environments from each other. I was actually hoping for Jill and Carlos to have their own stories, but once I started playing as Carlos I knew otherwise... - The ending song from RE:2 was wayyyyy better than RE:3. Not to say RE:3's credit song is terrible, but it definitely doesn't compare. When I finished RE:2 remake for the first time, I was crying. That ♥♥♥♥ was good, and still is.Now I'm definitely not an Resident Evil Veteran. In fact, the RE:2 remake is what got me interested in the series. So this review might mean nothing to all the Veterans who expected much more from this game. From what I hear, the RE:3 remake just straight removed entire bits from RE:3. Which might seem a bit odd, but keep in mind that it is a remake, not a remaster.Anyways, both of these games still keep their amazing sound design and visuals. Had no issues running RE:3, but that just depends on what you're rocking. Now is $60 worth it? If you're a fan of the series and have a little bit of money burning in your pocket, of course. But if you're some random Joe, who is looking into buying this game, I would recommend to save your money. Wait for it to go on sale, because it will go on sale. If I remember correctly the RE:2 Remake went on sale pretty quick for how long it was out. But, I can't stop ya if you want to go ahead and make the purchase. Just don't want ya to have buyer remorse. Ya know?

_childDocuments_.review: I was a little worried going into this Remake. I grew up with Resident Evil 3 as my first experience with the franchise, so I cherish it fondly. Unfortunately, this just isn't a faithful remake for the original. There was alot cut from the original. RE1 and RE2 remakes both took the original content and re-imagined it in a modern setting while remaining faithful to the source material. This remake for RE3 just cut content completely. Arguably some of the better locations and moments just removed. Seems like more time spent on the single player experience would have beneficial. I can not comment on the asymmetrical multiplayer, but that may be the culprit for the lackluster campaign. If you're a die hard RE fan, maybe pick this up during a sale? If you're a big fan of the original RE3, taper your expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, but not worth full price for most casual players. It's just too short, coming in around 4.5 hours on my first play-through. Modders create RE2R costumes all the time. They could have taken a few days to make a few extras given the lack of content.I don't consider Project Resistance to be extra content. It's a separate game that I didn't want. I'd have much preferred they spent those hours improving RE3 to justify the purchase price.I still recommend the game because it is fun and RE fans in particular should enjoy it, but for the content they've provided it's only worth 2/3 of the current purchase price at most. Get this one on sale. I'll get my money's worth in speedrunning the game, but I think most will be disappointed by the short campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: Staaaaaaars!!Jill Valentine returns to the blood soaked streets of Raccoon City. As a Veteran S.T.A.R.S. member her combat training gives the player the upper edge in combat making for a more action oriented experience much like the 1999 original. The game for the most part walks its own path and just treads some of the beats of the original while streamlining it's story and game play into a short but oh so sweet blood dripped roller coaster ride that never slows down. The puzzles are overly simplified compared to REmake 2 and there's almost no backtracking with the exception of the early part of the game. That being said I don't take that as a downfall because playing through the game in a single sitting is actually one of my favorite aspects of REmake 3. The game has an amazing game play loop that encourages you to play through the game multiple times to unlock points that you use to unlock Infinite Weapons, Gameplay modifiers, and more. I Highly Recommend checking out Inferno Difficulty in particular the remix of enemies and harder difficulty make it a much more frantic horror thrill ride. Overall I've had a blast playing through the game multiple times throughout the past few months and can easily see myself playing it for years to come. Bring on REmake 4!

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game at its current price and definitely on sale but with some hesitation. It just barely gets the thumbs up. At launch for 60 dollars this game was definitely lacking in content and if you're not looking too get all the achievements than the game will give you about 5-6 hours total. The core shooting and movement mechanics feel very smooth and fluid and its always a blast to kill zombies in this game There's a dodge mechanic that is very satisfying to pull off. The story is not too deep but its entertaining. The game play of the game is certainly a letdown in comparison to the original Resident Evil 3: Nemesis and RE2 remake. The game has a city environment that is completely unrealized and linear. I was hoping for something very expansive and explorable like the police station in RE 2 but as a city. Unfortunately that's not the case and much of the game is actually indoors with very few outdoor urban environments. This to me was the most dissapointing thing about this game. The original RE3 accomplished this better. As a remake this game falls flat. the game is missing levels and enemies and alternate choices that effect the story that were in the 1999 original. It feels more like a re-imagining that's even smaller in scope. Moving on the visuals The graphics are excellent especially with the recent ray-tracing update. I think RE3 actually has the best ray-tracing of all the Resident evil games if you're interested in ray-tracing. There isn't much to complain about in regards to visuals and sounds. The RE Engine truly is a masterwork. Overall I would rate this game a 6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: In a remake of the finale to the classic Resident Evil trilogy (before Resident Evil 4 started down a new path), Raccoon City returns torn up between a deadly virus, its own citizens and the mysterious and powerful Umbrella corporation. Similar to the 1999 original, half of the events of Resident Evil 3 (RE3) occur before those of the 2019 Resident Evil 2 remake, and the other half after. The overlap between the two timelines is particularly evident around the police station (where we finally learn how Marvin was bit), and at Kendo's place (another homage). On the upside:-The new RE3 features stunning visuals and rich, beautifully detailed environments that feel ominous and immersive. Devour all the stunning visuals RC has to offer! The return of a number of familiar enemies and villains is welcomed, although the collection is by no means expanded.-The inclusion of a new quick-step dodge system is an excellent addition and the controls feel connected, involved and agile.-Jill Valentine is a much more rounded, engaging and likeable character than either Leon or Claire from RE2. This iteration of Jill may be my new favourite Resident Evil character (having played the entire canonical series).-Carlos has undergone some massive improvements since his last appearance in the series, and it's about time (goodbye corny 1999 Carlos).-Nemesis is a noteworthy, well... nemesis. His pursuit is not as ever-present and creeping as Mr X in RE2 (who felt like he was constantly on your tail), but he is larger, faster, more aggressive and more intimidating when he does jump into the action. His evolution through boss fights into menacing final monster is impressive and well-executed. For a boss fight worth frustration and a racing heart, try the final boss fight on Inferno difficulty.On the downside:-The campaign is short. Really short. Across 6 runs, my originally chilled 4h50min was reduced to under an hour (albeit with the help of some helpful additions acquired with achievement points).-While the action is good, there is a serious lack of puzzles that formed a large part of the foundation of early RE games. Where are the cool puzzles, Capcom?!-The original RE3 featured story choices that altered the game and the endings. Here, there is really only one ending (arguably two if you REALLY refuse the no-brainer choice the game forces you into). This is a serious under-delivery of an otherwise excellent game and seriously cuts replay value.-Past the early phases of the game, this is really a very linear experience, often underscored by cinematic click scenes that really have neither alternative nor challenge.-There are some weapon modifications and the usual arsenal, but I miss some of the bizarre customisation options that really allowed one to decide how you want your weapon to behave (I want my lever-action Western Custom M37). Shotties should be fun to fire. Period.-As many others have pointed out, the trade of Mercenaries mode for 4v1 Resistance is just not acceptable. Surely the addition of both could have been possible? It feels like the 2019 RE2 had a little more body to it.RE3 is both a worthy sequel to the 2019 remake of RE2, and a worthy remake of the original. For a reality check of how far gaming has come in 21 years, check out comparisons between the 1999 and 2020 RE3s, particularly the final boss fight. With that said, RE3 is a good addition to RE2, rather than an evolution of it. It's very good, but it could have been so much better, especially at the premium price. Still very much worth a rainy weekend, and then some.

I think it lacks replayability, and some areas in the game feel frustrating or cheap, where the main difficulty is to throw many enemies at the player. The exploration factor is greatly reduced compared the RE2 Remake or the original RE3 Nemesis. On the plus side, graphics are great in this game. If taken in a vacuum, the game is good, although 5 hours of good gameplay are not worth $60 price tag.I'd recommend playing it at a lower price tag. Wait for a sale of 50% or more unless you really need to play it now.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the best survival/horror games I have ever played. the only other resident evil game I have played is resident 4 vr, which is really good, but this one tops that heavily. The advanced graphics are amazing and the story is great. I haven't played the original Resident Evil: Nemesis, so I can't base this review off of that. The only problems I had was the camera control sometimes bugging out. I also found it hard to know where I was going if I missed one little speech bubble or cut scene. Overall 9/10, has some bugs but great game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying I don't believe the game is necessarily bad. The Game is good but in my honest opinion it is not worth the full money. This game feels empty. The game lacks so much content and playability compared to the RE2 Remake that its pathetic. This feels more like a glorified DLC for the RE2 remake. Its so short and so small comparitively that you could beat the game rather quickly. I spent hours upon hours just in RPD on RE2 just searching and looking around for hidden things and notes etc. There just isn't much exploration or "tidbits" of investigation. It feels so rushed that it lacks serious content. I really think they messed this game up especially since there are things not even included which were in the original. I just hope if they plan on doing another remake of another game (RE4 possibly) that they do not do what they did with RE3. CAPCOM take your time and spend resources making a good game with lots of content. Even the old versions of the RE games have more content than this and they had a small fraction of the storage space to do so. This is starting to happen with all game development. Big price tag for so little content. It's sad but this is what games are coming to.TLDR: Lacks content and replayability. Not worth $60 find it on ♥♥♥ for cheap if you want to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 3

_childDocuments_.review: I "somehow" recommend this game. For the ones who didn't expect too much, nothing more than just a cinematic adventure within the Biohazard Lore, it is worth the buy (maybe not full price, maybe look somewhere else first). It has it's great moments and I can't deny I enjoyed it at some moments. But here's my review for the '99 RE: Nemesis Fans: It disappointed me more often. The way every scene from the beginning was so scripted you couldn't really take Nemesis serious, it really left me feeling angry, just like the fact that characters were finished off in the blink of an eye. The spirit wasn't there. I really tried to hype this game because  RE2 Remake was such a great masterpiece, they really did sooo good.  And no, I'm not trying to hate on RE3 Remake, just in case you misunderstand. I kept telling everybody: let them show you how great RE3 can be re-made, then cry later if you aren't satisfied. But yeah. Now I am one of those persons who cry a little about how many opportunities they didn't take. I am disappointed for many reasons. So are the others. They maybe released RE3 Remake, but if we are honest: Its just a reinterpretation. It's entertaining. Somehow.But as a fan, I can only say that these moments I just watched scripted scenes when I should've been running away from Nemesis as Jill, or the Bossfight with Nemesis a lá "Resident Evil: 6 - Nemesis Doggo", they made this game a devastating disappointment. It really was frustrating.For waiting for this too long, I am really sad about the outcome :/ (and yea, just let me "cry" a little about it). My thoughts to "Resistance":Now the amount I payed doesn't hurt so much. I really like assymetrical horror multiplayers, and this one has a lot of potential. Keep working on it, sell it without the need to buy RE3 and it could get even better. Fix the matchmaking, make Push to talk possible and more people would play it. Yea, it's not The Mercenaries, but I won't cry about that. I somehow really enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have an extremely mixed feeling about the current state of the game and may update this review pending further game updates (or DLCs... given modern game development practice).TL;DR summary at the bottom.(SPOILERS AHEAD)As a remake, RE3 is visually outstanding but also streamlined much of the story and characters (for better or worse).1. The opening and introduction: a. In the original, Jill talks about her last escape and a cut-scene follows with the RPD making their last stand in the streets.b. In the remake, Jill is confined to her apartment and placed under watch by chief Irons... then is surprised by a visit from Nemesis. When she breaks out of the apartment, she is completely shocked by the events in the streets.There is a lot of potential here to explore. In the hours before Jill's breakout, Carlos's survival and how the UBCS was deployed and ambushed (hinted at by Mikhail) can be added to the game.2. Carlos and Jill split journeys.Rather than going out and assisting Jill in the first hour of the game, Carlos stays behind doubling as security and radio man in the subway station. (Strange, because Tyrell in the remake is appears to be a tech specialist and likely could have worked the radio).Carlos ends up  investigating RPD with Tyrell without Jill ever going to RPD.3. Carlos investigates the RPD.- Carlos and Tyrell arrives to find Marvin being attacked by a zombie Brad Vickers.The potential additions leading up to this scene is actually the most interesting to me. Based on RE2Make and outbreak (if its still canon), some survivors LIKELY did escape RPD and the city itself. Marvin and Elliot ended up dead and zombified in RE2, but other officers (Rita and Kevin) and their whereabouts remains unknown. Also, given the concurrent event of the RPD making their last stand in the streets, the ideas don't seem too far fetched for me.Either way, I think the potential here is great for further exploration. Perhaps (free?) multiple DLCs or new scenarios titled "Their Finest Hour, "The Last Escape"... or even "The Outbreak" is suitable? Assuming Capcom is working on DLCs/Scenarios for this game.- I am not including HUNK and/or Ada because they had their moments in RE2Make.4. Treatment for Jill after her infection by Nemesis.- Not too much to say, Carlos plays hero but Tyrell supports him in the RE3Make storyline.5. Final chapter, underground lab- The final fight against Nemesis; kind of over-the-top sci-fi and no Delta Force.Summary:I am CURRENTLY not inclined to recommend the game at full price in its current state.- I am fine with the story changes, but the streamlined story also leaves me very wanting because of what I have played and experienced in the past.- The "wanting" is basically me not getting what I am expecting, hence my mixed feelings.- The game being "too short" isn't an issue for me, but I am assuming RE3Make will also get a similar RE2Make treatment; in which additional scenarios will added.- Again, this review will be updated depending on how well Capcom going to is meet the expectations I have in the next year or 2 for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of noise around this game being way too short. For the most part, I agree. It's really short and should be longer for the price tag, but I think there's something else to consider. It's a damn fun 4 hours. It's also really fun to learn the game for higher difficulties. When you beat the game on nightmare and inferno it feels like you have accomplished something. I think that the difficulties do actually make replaying the game super fun for different reasons than speedrunning Resident Evil 2 Remake (I do it very casually compared to the pros, but my Leon A time was around 1 hour 7 minutes so I'm no slouch). I don't even think I can go back to playing RE2make without the dodge mechanic, and I loved that game dearly before RE3make came out.There is one big stinker in all of this though. There are no stipulations for achieving S rank (S rank is now the highest achievable rank in all difficulties) on inferno mode. In RE2make you weren't allowed to use the infinite ammo weapons to achieve S+ mode. Now in RE3make you can use the infinite ammo weapons along with any of the other 'shop' items, that can quickly turn the difficulty of your campaign down several notches, to achieve S rank. This really hurts because you could do a 'no shop item' run, which is super impressive, and if it's slower than your meme-y rocket launcher run it won't find a spot on your results screen. There's no reward for that level of challenging yourself either. This is a very disappointing change in my opinion. They streamlined puzzles too. The RPD section with Carlos has the west office safe and the 2 lockers on the second and third floors respectively. These have the exact same codes as they did in RE2make so I clearly have some bias here as I knew the codes without ever having to try and figure them out organically although from what I can tell it might be even more simple than it was in RE2make. Other than the RPD section there are 2 safes in the game. 1 with Jill and 1 with Carlos. Jill's is '9 3 7' and Carlos's is '9 3'. I'm terrible at remembering codes so when I used to speedrun RE2make I would always have a cheat sheet pulled up on my separate monitor. I would never have to do something like that for RE3make because the codes are the same minus 1 number. Also, the RPD west office safe code is '9 15 7'. Jill's safe and the west office safe being so similar really rubs me the wrong way. I don't even know if I really consider the lab puzzle 'm h l' to even be a puzzle either.Those were the things I thought the game did poorly, but this doesn't reflect my opinion of the game as a whole. Overall, I still think the game is worth playing despite the change to the ranking and puzzle systems from RE2make. The core gameplay is much more fun due to the heavy action theme they took. It will feel like there is never a dull moment.

_childDocuments_.review: while the game does seem short is is fun to play and rewarding to complete, while i did not 100% the game at the time of writing this review, i definitly will at some point. one of the pros of the game was that the dodge was handy to have and was a good combination with the knife, allowing for the early stages to be passed using very little ammunition, making the late game easier than what i would've expected, it did seem a little harder to pull off if you simply dodged the wrong way. while Carlos did have a "dodge" mechanic, his was more useful as it felt as if he had more of a forgiving dodge in comparison to Jill as i was able to pull of the "perfect dodge" 5-6 times in a row with Carlos instead of 2-3 times in a row with Jill. Another great thing about this game that I found better in this one instead of the re2 remake was the fact that the knife did not have a durability bar, making it so that if i wanted I could use my knife more than the ammunition that I found throughout the game, once again, for late game or simply because I wanted to instead of having the thought "my knife is about to break, time to back off" and finishing the think i was killing with my precious ammo. overall I found this to be a 8/10, great story, witty banter between Carlos and Jill, simple but fun puzzles, just not quite worth the $60 price tag. buy it when it is on sale as it seems to be often. good luck and may you survive the Nemesis

_childDocuments_.review: In short: REmake 3 is unfaithful and a downgrade to the original game and due to the lack of a severe amount of in game content. it's simply not worth the justification of a full priced AAA game. If you still haven't gotten to play RE3, you're better off playing the 1999 version instead. If you still wish to buy this game however, I recommend when it's on sale.Longer version: After playing this, I wanted to try out the original Resident Evil 3 Nemesis to see how it compares to the REmake, I heard the criticisms and the backlash it first received so I thought it'll be a good try to give it a shot. I realize now, REmake 3 is nothing more than just a cashgrab of the original. To put it short, there is lots of cut content that didn't make it from the original game, Most notably are the mercenaries and civilians are randomly seen throughout the game, an entire explorable location removed and only use as a quick boss fight segment, some crafting elements have been cut, etc. The playtime due to this is way too short, I've only beaten the game in just about 6 hours, and I usually would take my time playing the game without having to rush it. The game feels completely linear and too easy, puzzles aren't exactly has challenging and the all the "threats" in the game aren't not as intense compare to the other RE games. Speaking of threats, I wanted to talk about Nemesis himself and oh man, he got shafted hard. I hadn't played the 1999 yet, so I never go the chance to see what it's like to against Nemesis, considering the RE community really hyped him in the original due how terrifying he was. However, after REmake 3, it's definitely not the case. The main issue for me was, unlike Mr. X from REmake 2, Nemesis felt and was completely scripted in events you would most likely expect, the chase sequences are not has terrifying compare Mr. X and I even found myself laughing at times where Nemesis felt like a complete pushover and just overall silly play against. Although, after playing RE3 1999, Nemesis' presence is very different, while it some occasions it was scripted, he still gets me off guard and overall was actually quite scary. Quite good actually, I love REmake 2 and this game still uses the game mechanics and functions making it a solid gameplay experience. If I would rate based on gameplay and graphics, it would be a 9/10 game. Especially the improvement of no fixed camera angles and tank controls. But this does come back as I said earlier about the playtime duration, because this game is very short, you'll won't be able to engage as much it has to offer, even the replayability of it is lacking. In this case, just get REmake 2.I still like this game even though of its issues, it still have some decent things to offer, I love the mod support it has and its community, but I can't for the life of me recommend to people who never got to play RE3, if you don't mind dated looking graphics I heavily recommend getting the original and if you do have the original on PC or plan to get it, you can get the Resident Evil 3 Nemesis: Restoration Project where the game quality is improved and some QOL are added, it works on Modern PCs very well too. Other than that, just for a sale on REmake 3 if you do still want this, while the game is short, it's not bad by any means just not as good as the original. Score: 5/10

Fight your way to freedom from the brink of despair. A series of strange disappearances have been occurring in the American Midwest within a place called Racoon City. A specialist squad of the police force known as S.T.A.R.S. has been investigating the case, and have determined that the pharmaceutical company Umbrella and their biological weapon, the T-Virus, are behind the incidents though they've lost several members in the process. Jill Valentine and the other surviving S.T.A.R.S. members try to make this truth known, but find that the police department itself is under Umbrella's sway and their reports are rejected out of hand.

However, soon reports of a grisly "cannibal virus" begin to surface, and vicious dogs begin roaming the streets. With the viral plague spreading through the town and to her very doorstep, Jill is determined to survive.
However, unbeknownst to Jill, an extremely powerful pursuer has already been dispatched to eliminate her.

name: CARRION
detailed_description: CARRION is a reverse horror game in which you assume the role of an amorphous creature of unknown origin. Stalk and consume those that imprisoned you to spread fear and panic throughout the facility. Grow and evolve as you tear down this prison and acquire more and more devastating abilities on the path to retribution.

short_description: CARRION is a reverse horror game in which you assume the role of an amorphous creature of unknown origins, stalking and consuming those that imprisoned you.

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion is a short but fun game about being a writhing mass of tentacles with HUNGER.Your core movement is keeping the mouse pressed and aiming where you want to go and it works really well, you are extremely mobile and can swoosh into ventilationshafts with ease.Other than that you get an increasing arsenal of tools to deal with enemies that also get stronger, but there isnt really a lot of variety when it comes to the enemies. Its enough for the duration that the game has though, which is probably around 3-4 hours.The concept is as follows: all cool Sci-Fi games get fleshwalls permeating an infested something, deadspace gets em, Warframe gets em, Halo etc. and you are in charge of building that infested fleshstation. You break out of a glass container and from then on go on a rampage with naught a line of dialogue.The last time i had fun being a thing consuming humanity from the shadows was probably that weird Venom game from the gameboy advance and this hits just that note. We just dont get enough eat people games so im glad this exists.The game also throws in plenty of fodder scientists to scream run away and die in a bloodbath to balance out getting decked by flamethrowers with electric riot shields. The main gameplay loop is overcoming combat challenges that mainly consist of you snatching someone into the unseen darkness one by one and unlocking new abilities, since these are used for both combat and unlocking new areas.While the "levels" are all connected as one big area the game somewhat guides you from place to place by way of leveldesign and this mostly works really well.This games biggest weakness is when it doesnt. If you miss the obvious hint where you need to go next well then you are stuck in an interconnected megalevel of every place you ever visited with no idea what is next.And this can lead to unfun backtracking and speeding through many empty rooms.There is also hidden collectibles so a completionists approach will be constantly going back to everything anyway.Well all in all i guess its a devolver digital game, fun while it lasts with a quirky and violent idea but way too short.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, if you expect a really good metroidvania game, don't. This is a very linear game (at least on the level flow), there's no substantial level up, and there's very little back tracking.Yes you can use some of your new skills to find the other additional upgrades, but that's it. If you want to call this game is a metroidvania, you can call Megaman X4 is one too.I think you will love this game if you love John Carpenter's The Thing or The Blob. This game feels like a tribute to thise kind of horror movies. The soundtrack is your typical brooding monster movie and it's a quite fitting.There are 2 cons that kinda annoyed me:- The biggest size of the monster is hard to control, you will make unnecessary mistakes just because you can't make head or tail, literally.- I wish the power upgrade is a little bit more useful and not too trivial when you can obtain them. A simple map can help the player to navigate the stages and know where are the upgrades.I'm glad that this game doesn't overstay it's welcome, 5 hours is a sweet spot for this kind of this game. The puzzle is unique and not too hard, the stage is not too big (albeit a little bit confusing, too many corridors and samey design), and it's very satisfying watching the creature scrawling around your screen.And that simple ending is very fitting and I can't think any better ending.Highly recommended game 👍

_childDocuments_.review: I of course got this game for the thrill of being the bad guy in the story, but the concept of being a, not brainless, but a weird amorphic bloody organism was so appealing as well--eating the scientists and trying to escape the facility. The "powers" learned are cool and original, helping you navigate the facility, certain tough enemies take some thought as to how to defeat them, but there are multiple ways to do it--it just depends on your personal fighting style. I don't want to give anything away here, just in case you've yet to play, but the ending is...predictable? But to me that didn't matter because I was playing for the creature, not for a ending that would blow my mind. I still was very satisfied with the ending anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite unusual experience. Play as a "glass cannon" flesh monster mixing smörgåsbord mode (when there are no military equipment around and you consume everything on your path) and stealth mode (use tentacles while hiding in vents, or else you will be killed in 0.5 seconds). If you gonna play it, after ~1 week of break from the game it's hard to remember how to use skills and where to go. Also, one of the puzzles with a collectible requires you to use a certain skill (Arachnoptysis) you usually use to activate switches, but instead to recharge your energy bar. Also, bookshelves and other throwables go through thermal shield of military.

_childDocuments_.review: Reverse horror, not directed by Ridley Scott. Fresh, gory and sweet just like all the humans that got devoured in my playthroughs. I wanted more but unfortunately good things end quick. Nitpicking, the mouse controls sometimes are irritating and the background music is very monotonous. Carrion is the perfect example why the indie scene is so strong as it constantly innovates and takes risks.

_childDocuments_.review: The untapped potential of the gameplay combined with level design and levels themselves, kill this game dead.There is no map, locations look alike and there is no fast way to return to previous areas. This makes the game extremely frustrating and makes the player wander around until they come across the correct path. Once you exit the game and return, you have problems remembering which path is which so you once again roam aimlessly until you find your way.The problems doesn't end there, there is no feeling of power and progression. You don't get gradually bigger depending how many people you consume, so once you're on full health, there is no reason to cause mayhem and eat people. The only way to permanently increase mass is to find areas that contain certain abilities. Speaking of abilities, you can't use every ability you unlock at any time, you have to find pools of liquid to shrink yourself and then use them. You can't even shrink yourself at will, you have to backtrack, find a pool, shrink and get back, it's pointless.In my opinion the idea is great, the creature is great, but the game needed completely different gameplay. Let the creature start in a lab that created it, sterile corridors and white rooms all over that can be covered in blood instead of the current industrial / factory setting. Let the creature grow with EVERY people it consumes, let the player use every single ability they unlock whenever they want instead of the current limited system and really make them feel like they are gradually getting powerful, one body at a time.I really wanted to like this game but sadly it's not very fun and commonly a chore to progress through.

So I had to use youtube walkthroughs near the end, just to find out where to go. Other than that. Good good good.

_childDocuments_.review: (Ignore the playtime; I tend to leave games on and that greatly inflates the time) Fantastic pixel based graphics, good pacing of enemy types and power ups, all in a world that doesn't overstay its welcome. There are moments where you truly do get to feel like the monster, even in retreat, and that alone is wonderful. Very linear, and sometimes difficult to control, and often difficult to know which direction to go, the shortcomings do not overshadow the value. Feel free to skip this section. I think it's important to have context about the reviewer, allowing you to gauge your own interests, tastes, etc, against their's and thus hopefully know whether or not the review fits your with your own likes. I come at these reviews as a Software Developer at a FAANG company. A place of high stress, high demands, and intense annual crunch. On top of that, I have four children, five pit bulls, and a house that constantly threatens to implode on itself like the one at the end of Poltergeist. I am a busy person who only gets weird moments in the corners to get out there and play games. And I love games. I'm a fan of both short and long games, but lose the thread if they go on too long. I have little patience for convoluted stories that aren't so much complex as they are internally confused (think Hideo Kojima or Final Fantasy). Seeing my way through to the end of anything is rare these days. Prior to this game, the last games to really absorb my time were (in order) Call of Cthulhu (completed), Hades (one pass through complete), Dragon Quest VII on the 3DS (50 hours in), Paper Mario Origami (played until, I dunno, the fourth area? Then I fell off).* It really does look great. Pixel art fits the game.* Tons of fun manipulating your tenticular appendages all about, tearing apart the "enemies." (I particularly enjoyed slamming the soldiers against walls and each other as vengeance for them daring to hurt me)* Good special effects sound, especially the monster growl.* Dolls out monster upgrades and new enemies at just the right pace. Always feels fresh.* * The controls work until they don't. They especially fall off at your greatest mass. At one point I just wanted to pass through a door and it took me maybe a full 30 seconds of coaxing my little creature along. Controlling while in the water really slows things down. When the controls do work, though, man is it a joy.* Backtracking and knowing where to go is rough unless you happen to be one of those people that can keep a map like this together in your head. While each "world" is distinct, the color palette is limited and the overall structure of each area is basically the same. It's pretty easy to just roam in circles.* It's length is a big deal for a lot of people. I like a short game. Not everything has to be a 200 hour Dragon Quest marathon. That being said, you'll need to do your own math to know if the length justifies the price. For me, the length was good. Unless they had new, radical ideas as the game progressed, it would have become tedious. They knew where to cut it off so that finishing it didn't start to feel like a slog.* Story. I mean, I guess there's one. Heck if I know what was supposedly going on.

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion is a horrendous game in the exactly right way, no I'm not saying the game is bad, it actually looks horrifying. It looks and sounds just like a horror, but with none of the scares, because... you are the one who is scary. The flipping of roles of the usual "run away from the monster" to "you are the monster" theme is one that is slowly becoming more and more trendy, and I believe Carrion is one of the pioneers of doing this correctly, empowering the player enough to feel like you represent an all powerful monstrous organism that ravages everyone in its way, but that is still challenging enough to feel satisfying. Overall a great show altogether, but 8/10 mainly because the map can be a bit infuriating to naviagte, as there are no maps and the indications of where to go aren't always the clearest. That asides, still very great game that is fun for a good 6-7 hours, well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute gem of a game. Basically you play as an alien creature more or less reminiscent of the Thing and have to bust your way out of an underground research facility, along the way you absorb genes from biological samples stored around the place usually locked behind puzzles, these give you more abilities which turn you into even more of a freakish biological terror, the game markets itself as a reverse-horror and it definitely pulls that off. The creature itself is really well animated and is just plain disturbing to look at as it crams itself into vents and propels itself all over the place with it's tentacles. It's what an indie hit should be, focuses on the gameplay but subtly tells a compelling little story through environmental clues and a few short flashback sequences. There's no dialogue or cutscenes whatsoever, it's all fed to you through intuitive means and overall it's excellently paced. I loved the fact that you could control so many of the enemies in the game and actually use each of their unique abilities, everything makes logical sense and the attention to detail put on the AI behavior and how they interact and respond to their surroundings is great to see in action. The levels themselves are very well crafted and do a great job of guiding you to wherever you need to go to progress, I only got lost a couple times but those were due to not paying attention to the environment. They did an equally impressive job on creating and maintaining an atmosphere like that of classic sci fi horror movies, the levels all have that oppressive sterile look to them in the same vein as the sets of the original Alien film, but there's still a good variety of areas and each feels suitably distinct from the others so you don't get completely lost when backtracking for things you missed. The music is ominous and understated, mostly consisting of ambient stuff with some more energetic tracks when the action is amped up. Really the sound design is just perfect overall, the creature sounds like it should and the screams that the Human and synthetic enemies make as you savagely murder them are bone chilling. I didn't experience any bugs or optimization issues throughout the entire thing and I got a good 10 hours out of it. It really reminds me of the pure creativity and focus on fun that Flash games had, while still being much more refined and larger than those games could have been. There's also apparently workshop support but I can't speak on it as I haven't tried any mods yet, even then there's a lot of fun to be had with what's already here and I'd happily pay full price for the level of quality and addictive gameplay this has.

Overall, its pretty intuitive to play, and the only gripe I have is that it's a pretty short game, although that's probably just a bittersweet acceptance that we have to take for games like this. That being said, being able to re-enact horror concepts, like picking off parts of a group that are too far separated is still quite entertaining, and the brevity does allow the game to be fun without becoming much of a chore. _childDocuments_.review: Every so often you want a game thats simple yet compelling.  Carrion is best described as a puzzle/exploration game. _childDocuments_.review: A game that I was really looking forward to playing but couldn't find time for. Finally played it last month and it was all that I was expecting and more. In Carrion, you play the role of a large fleshy amorphous creature that is trying to escape a research facility (presumably) where it has been contained. Even armed with guns, flamethrowers and armored robots, you are too powerful to be stopped by the human beings in the facility and it is just a matter before you find your way out back to the surface. What makes Carrion special of course is that the horror is reversed. It is the horror of devouring vulnerable bodies instead of being one. Granted that it might be fun to toss around the human beings like rag dolls but there is a foreboding as you come closer to finishing the game. Through flashbacks that reveal how things came to be like this, the horrific possibility that you do escape to the surface and that no one will even know that you are out, are some of the ideas that are always looming in the background while playing this game. The developers have a great and original cinematic sense, only showing that much to arouse your imagination regarding what all is in store, after you have already finished the game. Carrion has amazing visuals and animations. It manages to convey a loneliness and terror throughout, as you try to evolve, get bigger and slither menacingly through the facility, stalking, hunting and ripping the humans limb from limb, making your way out to the surface. Carrion is a great example of a game that can produce an amazing visual atmosphere and immense life (and death) in all of its characters, without requiring an expensive graphics card. I find that truly inspiring and it makes me happy that I can play such a brilliant game on my potato computer.  There is not much to say about the music though it is good and complements the visual atmosphere of the game very well. As others have said, it might have been a good idea to have a map. There were a few places where I got very confused as to where I was supposed to go. However, not having a map does also play a part in maintaining the atmosphere of the game and gives your journey through the facility a real sense of desperation and rampage. Maybe the developers could add a map and players could have the option to play with or without it.    Other than that, I cannot think of anything else that game might need. I hope there is a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun, straightforward but clever game that delivers exactly what was promised, doesn't outstay it's welcome, and challenges without ever being frustrating. You're a horrible monster, you eat people, and you want to get out of the base that is studying/containing you.  That's it, and it does it well.  The puzzles are simple and relatively straightforward, it's very rare that you can't quickly figure out what is expected of you.  Like all Metroidvanias, the only real frustration is sometimes you're not entirely sure if there is a puzzle you haven't figured out or if you're just supposed to come back later when you pick up new powers.The design of the creature and the way it moves, the power it has, the different functions it has at various levels of biomass etc are all put together in a highly satisfying way.  There isn't much variety in enemy types but what is there is used effectively.  The graphics aren't fancy but the aesthetic works, and each section of the base does a good job of presenting variety while still feeling like it all fits together.This is a very fun game, well worth the price, and you'll get 6-10 hours at least of a good time out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is short but sweet. I have played it for 37 hours, replaying the campaign multiple time. The game also has workshop support with multiple custom-made campaigns. The controls are good on controller and on keyboard. The keyboard controls are hard to get used to, but are sometimes a nice change. The map is crafted very well, but is confusing to navigate. An important piece of advice to remember is, if you can't reach something you're probably coming back there. There are optional upgrades like resistances and more tentacles in the game too. Overall the game is very good. It is short, but it is very good.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)Carrion, a unique and unsettling reverse-horror game, is a captivating experience that had me immersed in its nightmarish world for 3.5 hours. It's a game that takes the traditional concept of being the hero and flips it on its head, allowing you to become the lurking monstrosity.Carrion casts you in the role of an amorphous, tentacled creature that escapes from a containment facility. Your primary objective is to wreak havoc, consume everything in your path, and navigate the maze-like environment to unveil the secrets behind your existence.One of Carrion's most intriguing aspects is its gameplay. As the nameless monster, you are a force of destruction and chaos. Your abilities include slashing through obstacles, latching onto humans to devour them, and regenerating health by consuming biomass. This unique approach to gameplay provides a refreshing change of perspective from traditional horror games, where you are usually the prey.The level design in Carrion is praiseworthy. Each area offers a series of puzzles, challenges, and enemies, making it feel like a living and breathing ecosystem that you, as the monster, must adapt to. Progressing through the game involves using your evolving abilities strategically to bypass obstacles and defeat adversaries.Carrion's atmospheric design also deserves recognition. The pixel-art visuals are both gruesome and beautiful, capturing the grotesque nature of the creature and the dark, eerie environment in which it thrives. The sound design further amplifies the tension, with eerie noises and cries of terrified humans, adding to the sense of horror and immersion.However, the game's brevity is one of its main downsides. At 3.5 hours of gameplay, Carrion is a relatively short experience, leaving you craving more of its unique and terrifying world. The narrative is minimal, with the story mostly conveyed through environmental storytelling and notes found throughout the game, which can leave you wanting more depth in the plot.Carrion is undoubtedly an unconventional and memorable horror experience that flips the genre's conventions on their head. As the player, you get to embrace the role of the predator and become the embodiment of terror. Although it's a bit on the shorter side, the game's gripping gameplay, atmospheric design, and inventive premise make it a must-play for horror enthusiasts looking for something refreshingly different.
