_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted a video game adaptation of John Carpenter’s  where you played as the monster rather than the humans?  is basically that.It’s a pseudo-Metroidvania where you play as an amorphous body horror rampaging through a large laboratory complex, with your ultimate goal being to escape into the outside world.The monster controls very smoothly (though it does become more cumbersome to move around tight corners and passages when you reach maximum size) and the special abilities you pick up along the way are satisfying to use and feel like they have a lot of weight and power behind them. Luckily from a “fun” perspective, you never end up feeling  overpowered, as the humans still have plenty of weapons and robots capable of obliterating you in a matter of seconds if you aren’t playing at least somewhat carefully.If you’re the type of player who values playtime over all other aspects, then be warned:  is a relatively short game which can easily be 100% completed in a single sitting, and outside of collecting all of the upgrades and Achievements, it offers nothing in terms of replayability. If you think this will be an issue for you, then I would advise waiting for a sale so you have a better chance of feeling like you got your money's worth.My only complaints:1. It's often easy to get lost as the game lacks an in-game map, though the game generally does a good job at giving you a sense of direction.2. The monster can be somewhat difficult to maneuver through passages and around corners when it has reached maximum size.3. Controlling your tentacles can be a bit finicky if you’re playing with a gamepad, especially when you grow in size and therefore gain more surface area for tentacles to protrude from.Overall,  is a unique, satisfying, and enjoyable experience, and I highly recommend it to fans of horror and exploratory games. We need more villain protagonist games!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like 2D Metroid-esque games and always wanted to play as a flesh eating parasitic monster, this might be worth a look. The Xenomorph looks like a cute little puppy compared to the ever-growing pile of worms, tentacles, jaws and eyes that you play in Carrion, The controls are unique, but fluid and intuitive and the abilities you aquire are pretty... interesting...However, the way you switch between those abilities isn't fun and confusing at first. Imagine Super Metroid where you can only use morph ball at a certain health level. The way it works in Carrion is that you have your health pool divided in 3 segments, each segment representing a differnt stage of mutation. Each stage of mutation has 2 different abilities tied to it, one offensive and one defensive. In the weakest form, you have a cloak as defensive ability and a whip-like attack as offensive. You need both to solve certain puzzles, like not being detected by security cameras or pulling switches from a great distance. Now, if your health bar exceeds a certain threshold, you reach the next level of mutation and get your abilities replaced by something different, like a ram attack for destroying certain barriers or blast resistant skin. Same if you lose too much health, you will also lose the abilities that you may have needed for the puzzle ahead. In order to manage your health level, apart from taking damage, visiting save points and eating humans, there are these biomass pools where you can store chunks of your health bar in the form of biomass blobs. You can return to those pools and pick up the blobs later to restore your health and swap the abilities. Some puzzles require switching between mutations multiple times, so you have to go back to these pools constantly (which can be a puzzle by itself). I guess you could design it that way, but there are good reasons why no other game does it. It's just annoying as hell! It would be much more fun if you could transform on the fly and switch between abilities whenever you like and have your game designed around that. That would also make combat much more interesting.The second big flaw this game has is the backtracking and lack of a map. I've never seen a game like this where the backtracking is done so badly. With all the one-way pipes, holes in the background (which function as connectors between sectors), lack of distinct visual landmarks and complete absence of a much needed hub system, chances are high you will take the wrong turn at some point and find yourself in a location that you've already visited hours ago, but without the ability to go back quickly. As soon as I realized this, I pretty much skipped all the optional backtracking and only focused on what's ahead. Lots of wasted potential there!I'm not going to say much about the graphics. It is what it is: Pixel art. Love it or hate it. Seen worse, seen better. Sound is also pretty unspectacular, Not bad, but not very memorable either.  Overall, the game is pretty short. I completed it in about 6h. There was no Boss fight or anything, it just ended kinda apruptly and the credits started rolling in. Not sure if there's a better ending if you do all the backtracking and complete it 100%, but I doubt it and don't care enough to play again. It's ok if you like those kind of games and find it on sale, but for the full price of ~25€, you can definately get something better (e.g. Blasphemous). 6.5/10 happy tubular worms up my bowels.

_childDocuments_.review: There isn't anything WRONG with Carrion. It's a fine game. Very reminiscent of the arcade style web games that one would play back in their childhood, except much better polish. The mechanics are not very well described in the game but with enough fidgeting and experimentation you can figure out most of them. The controls are... fine. A bit janky once you get to max size. But that's just the issue I have with Carrion. It didn't do anything wrong-- in fact, it was  very fun! There were issues here and there but nothing particularly damning. A fine flash game on newgrounds. Except it's not. It's a $20 game. A $20 game that I 100%'d and got all 21 achievements including the full collectables... in 4.5 hours. Even getting it on sale for $8, I was left with a sour taste in my mouth. Less than 5 hours of gameplay? And that includes backtracking, upgrade-collecting, full completion, and even having a bit of fun stacking soldiers' bodies on top of each other then ripping them all around? It was FINE. A FINE free-flash game, one that I would even suggest $3 or even $5 for. $19.99 for a game that is just... over way too fast, is unacceptable. I loved playing it, but even as I beat it I was left with a bitter disappointment, thinking "... is that it? Are we moving on to a new facility? Or perhaps there are city-levels now?" Nope. Roll credits. 300 minutes of playtime for $10. Dave & Busters Arcade-level pricing.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever played classic platform games such as  or perhaps ? This game is very similar to the base premise of such games, in the sense that you play a character stranded somewhere and trying to get ahead. To succeed with that and actually get somewhere, you need to figure out where to go, as well as get past obstacles in your path.Of course, in this particular instance, you do not play a human trying to get home again, but a monster trying to escape its confines.It's a wonderfully wicked idea. I mean, you get to devour humans along the way so that you can grow, spraying gore everywhere as you do so. When you meet drones, your tentacles smash them against the walls until they break! You look like a deformed cousin of John Carpenter's classic , so no wonder these poor humans flee in terror.It's no use, though. You smash your way through barricades and slither through tunnels in order to get past obstacles, all so that you can devour them all. Poor, poor little humans.The only issue I have with this game is that I wish there had been a minimap of some kind, since it's quite easy to get lost when trying to figure out where to go next. This is especially true if you're trying to figure out if there's a problem-solving step you might have missed somewhere along the way.Otherwise, I can thoroughly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: While it's a very entertaining idea that clearly has a lot of thought put into the upgrades, story and general idea of the game, the levels constantly alternating between a metroidvania-like, exploration-driven game where you're encouraged to go back and redo things with the new upgrades and figure out your own path to an arbitrarily-handholdy experience where you're forced forward with no way back at all- not to mention the inconsistency where the save spots that unlock something and spit you right back out are visually identical to the ones that force you to a new area immediately, and the former becoming the latter once used once so they're not even usable for quick travel later.Whoever did the design for the creature's gameplay itself did fantastically, as did whoever drafted the upgrades and where they are / the difficulty of getting them, but whoever actually did the level design should be ashamed of themselves for very clearly having talent yet being willing to throw it away completely every other level. This is also compounded by the two-forms system being theoretically a great idea yet not a single point in the game actually allows you to take advantage of it. There's just a few points where you need to downshift to solve a very obvious puzzle then go and get your mass back to continue, rather than having any exploration with alternate takes on how to handle situations. Sucks if you like the webbing upgrade because the need to break wood to be able to actually make it through the game means you're only allowed to use it when the game says okay.I'd also argue the store description is a lie. It's not a game where you really do much stalking, you just have AI that's dumb as bricks so they act like they've no idea what's going on despite also very clearly being able to know exactly where you are at all times and respond to sounds more than two rooms away. That's not a bad thing, but not describing it as a puzzle game first and foremost is misleading- and the lack of transparency about it being a puzzle game plus how utterly short it is, for £17? Get it on sale or don't get it at all,As to the DLCs - the OST is great, don't get me wrong but also incredibly samey and nondistinct. I couldn't possibly tell you where any part of the game the music is from, nor in a month or two could I even go "oh yes that's Carrion music" if not for the fleshy sounds included throughout. Not worth the £8.50.Deluxe edition art book is neat, but also not worth a separate £9 either, and we're several years past a desktop wallpaper being something that's worth any monetary value at all so I'm opting to consider it a free bonus included with the art book, with the art book itself being the thing they're asking £9 for.For me? Summer sale dropped it to £6.70, and that's a price that's fair, as is the deluxe edition bundle dropping to £7.60 (price not including base game). If the soundtrack were rolled into deluxe edition outright rather than having them be two DLCs, I'd feel happier with the pricing but the core game is just asking altogether too much. It's short, frustrating and feels half-baked and almost 100% of that is attributed to the shoddy level design, because the potential present with literally everything else can very much be felt. Steam also stopped picking up the game entirely a little over an hour into playing, my total playtime beating the game was slightly shy of two hours, in part due to giving up searching for the secrets when entering the gardens level.

Controlling your tentacle beast can be a little bit awkward at times, but in general, things work well. The only other negative I would point out is that the lack of a map makes getting around sort of difficult, especially if you need to backtrack to an area for a collectible. After getting lost for a good while, I finally gave up and looked at some maps online to help me finish things off. Overall, though, this was a great experience, especially for the sale price. A nice little slice of creepy-crawly action.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: A somewhat unique metroidvania in my experience, really fun to rampage through the map breaking stuff and eating people, and I really like the mutation system with 3 forms with different abilities. Biggest downside is there's no map, which can get really annoying when you don't know where to go next but all in all, it's a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Such a good game! All you need to know is that's extremely satisfying to control the creature and wreak havoc on objects and poor humans. I had plenty of fun manipulating objects and humans (heh) to make my way through. If you stop and think, you can always find an elegant, albeit gory, way to escape a room full of enemies without risking yourself.The game is rather easy, but I think this was a deliberate choice to make you feel like an overpowered beast. And it works! You really feel unstoppable, in an exciting - and terrifying - way. There are some tough rooms, though, and you can tackle them by brute force (which requires skill) or by using the environment and objects to your advantage (which requires some thinking); either way, it feels very rewarding when you clear it. That said, I do wish there were a few tougher battles (maybe some boss fights?). I'd also love more difficult environmental puzzles. Most of the really good ones are optional: you clear them to get containment units. It'd be great to have more of those in every level.Carrion exceeded my expectations. I'll play the (free!) DLC now, but I can't wait for a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: CARRION was developed by Phobia Game Studio, a team of 4. Sometimes, the smallest teams will put the most love into a game. It's clear that a lot of love was put into CARRION.-Getting this game on sale is a steal. You'll definitely get your money's worth.-The graphics are very well done. Beautiful pixel art.-The movement alone is entertaining.-Goreand, of course, the gameplay is so much fun. It's a fairly fast paced puzzle game with just the right amount of difficulty. Lots of dying and no map to help you.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding indie journey from start to finish, this game immerses you as the scientific entity initially studied, now cast as the  antagonist. Breaking free from your restraints, your goal is to evade captivity, grow, and feed on biological matter, ultimately spreading throughout an expansive research facility.  This game is a metroidvania experience, crawling at immense speeds throughout a massive facility, you are not tasked with jumping over boxes or slashing with a sword to fight a set of boss villains at various corners of the sprawling metroidvania map, rather, you are the boss, a monstrosity moving at break neck speeds, using your tentacles to grab and shred anything in your path. As you advance through the facility, you develop parasite mind control abilities, the ability to grow shells for protection from bombs, and the ability to shoot our your tentacles like needles, among many others. Carrion also has a fantastic soundtrack by Cris Velasco that evokes the cosmic horror of film soundtracks like Alien and The Thing. It also runs and looks great on the Steam Deck. It's really a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun! The upgrades are gradual so youre never overwhelmed, each room and area is well designed with different ways of solving it, and at some point you just start to feel like an absolute bad ass.the only downside is that later on it can be a little difficult to figure out where to go next. The game is very linear, which works well, but its not a straight line path and you'll often revist areas (which i like! I enjoy criss cross map design) but it does mean that if you happen to miss the hallway youre supposed to go in you can wander around for while. Still, its a minor annoyance at best.If the one downside i mentioned seems like it matters to you, id buy it on sale. If you read that and think 'pft whats this clown on about?' then you should buy it at full price, as it is well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly unique, tons of fun and ridiculously well made. It takes the premise of being an amorphous tentacle monster and executes it to absolute perfection! From the smooth and satisfying movement system to the brilliant level design, great combat encounters and amazing visuals/soundtrack, this game is a must play for every fan of the sidescroller genre!The main campaign is relatively short (3-5 hours) but there's enough to do afterwards. From the free DLC (about 30 minutes) to great workshop mods ('The hive' and 'chaos theory' in particular) that can easily double your playtime. Even then it's still a short but sweet experience that does not outstay it's welcome (like this review hopefully). A game of this quality at this pricepoint is a bargain, trust me, you won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty good. Took me about 4.5 hours, steam's saying 2.8 now and I'm not sure why but I checked before and commented about it so someone so it used to be 4.5You're playing a tentacle-y murder monster that eats people and tries very hard to eat robots. Controls are straight-forward - click to move in direction, right click to grab people and pull them in (or throw them around), various other abilities are unlocked as you play.A unique aspect of the game is that your size and health bar are one and the same, and your current size determines the abilities you have available. Puzzle solving often revolves around working how to get yourself to a different size in the right part of the level, so that you can use that size's abilities. The rate at which you're introduced to new abilities is well-paced, with the application of the ability becoming apparent a short while before actually getting access to it, so you get this new thing and immediately know what to do with it. The puzzle solving clearly takes into account what abilities you'll have access to, and sets you up to employ them all in a fashion that makes you feel clever. Main issues I had: - You move so quickly through some parts of the map that I had a hard time building up a mental image of my surroundings for the first hour or 2.  - In your larger forms, in tight spaces, pieces of your body can get kinda stuck around a corner. Easily resolved by backing up, just a bit annoying.I haven't looked at them, but there are modded levels to play on.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, Carrion! A masterful dive into the squelchy world of tentacles, writhing movement, and intricate engagements. As a connoisseur of fine art, I found this game surprisingly... familiar?From the moment I began, the detailed rendering of the tentacle protagonist instantly piqued my interest. Its seductive motions, the way it reached out and ensnared its surroundings, and the fluidity with which it moved through tight passages was nothing short of mesmerizing. It was almost as if the developers had peered deep into my internet search history.As I progressed, I awaited the game's narrative turn, anticipating the moment when our tentacled protagonist would encounter the inevitable schoolgirl or hapless adventurer. But hours passed and... nothing? The military resistance and screams of digital victims were all in good fun, but where was the spicy content I was promised? Where were the shy glances, the blushing faces, and the intricately detailed scenarios that I, erm, 'research' in depth?Curiously, I noted the lack of dialogue choices, romantic subplots, and well, any hint of the 'intimate engagements' I was so familiar with. Instead, there were labs, puzzles, and ever-growing tentacle mechanics that seemed more about destruction and escape than any form of entwined romance.It was then, dear readers, that I was hit with the cold splash of reality. This wasn’t the tantalizing tale of tentacle trysts I had inadvertently been expecting, influenced by my, ahem, extracurricular viewing habits. No, this was a genuine horror-themed indie gem where YOU are the monster.In conclusion, if you're seeking a game where you can terrorize unsuspecting humans as an ever-growing amorphous blob, Carrion is your perfect match. And if you're looking for... other forms of tentacle engagements, well, I might have a few browser tabs to recommend. But for now, I can confidently say that Carrion is a delightful monster of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a shame that we don't get more games in the style of Carrion, it is a shining example of less is more. _childDocuments_.review: This review contains some mildly implied spoilers but nothing explicit. Short list of bullet points:* Fun game, too high price.* Too much backtracking without map.* Game ending lackluster.* Some stupid design choices. Has tell tale signs of being rushed out.I loved the demo. I mostly liked the final game.So why won't I recommend this game? I think it's mostly the price. It's clearly more expensive to supplement the large amount of marketing this game had.Game is fun, the mechanics complement each other and all abilities are used even in late puzzles. Problem is, that for a metroidvania style game with lot of opportunities in backtracking the game lacks map. I found all but the final game ending 'ability' because finding my way required massive amount of backtracking without map. It didn't help that a lot of the time I circled back accidentally forward(?).Biggest kick in the teeth was when you get the last ability directly related to progress... you are also forced to end the game. No chance to look for those secret locations and challenges they give. Not only that but the 'final' ability had so much potential to be used in puzzles... but no... you are forced to lackluster ending.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: + cool concept & art style+ fun monster gameplay+ interesting special skills & upgrades- really short- no map- somewhat useless passive unlocksSurprisingly, the game is mostly a puzzle platformer and all the puzzles (which are based on your modes/abilities) is what you will spend the majority of time on. Well ... that and wandering around aimlessly because there is no map. This is probably due to the short campaign but feels like artificial game time padding. I also played it in four sessions which added time too as you are lost when you hop out and then back into the game. I dare say that with a map my game time would be around three hours. Apart from the puzzles there are fights, sometimes even extended/boss fights. These are often pure chaos and your success mostly depends on how you go about it. Sometimes it is unclear whether it should to be stealth or direct combat. It seems like it wants you to choose which style YOU want but some enemies cannot be taken down by the low HP stealth mode and often times they can spot you from afar. While I tried to stealth too I got FAR more wins by tackling everything as the big blob of death that I was. And really this is where the game is most fun and I wish they had expanded on it. There is also the option to mind control enemies later which was really cool as well. For unlocks you can find a containment unit in each level. These add passive bonuses to energy or life ... but are sort of useless because you need extra abilities to unlock them. You see, these abilities are acquired mid to late game so by the time you can unlock them you basically already completed the campaign and don't need them. So that is somewhat of a design flaw. It is really difficult to make a stand on this game. On one side it is super short and makes you wander around the same areas. On the other, it is a great fun to control the monster, gradually upgrade it and fight your way out. Tentatively, I do recommend this game for the fun inside ... but on a good sale (like a quarter or half off). I realize it took work to make this but it sort of feels like a teaser demo, you start to have fun with the monster abilities and the game ends. Here is hoping they add content and/or work on a more meatier sequel... (pun intended)------------------------------------------------------------------

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:A perfect pitch; you are the shapeless horror from any one of a dozen classic 80s horror films, escaped (or set loose?) from a secret underground laboratory. Slither through air ducts, along metal grated corridors, and through concrete bunkers devouring all in your path. Adapt and overcome enemies, puzzles, and environmental hazards. Delightful, charming, and gruesome gore courtesy of excellent art direction and stellar sound design help sell the fantasy.The Ugly:The game follows the metroidvania design that has you backtracking to previously explored areas as you unlock new powers. This in and of itself is not a negative but the game lacks a map function and the warren-like maze of caves, corridors, and pipes can become more than a little disorienting. The controls can be a little haphazard when you're trying to grab onto a specific thing, be that a lever, enemy, or access grate in a crowded environment while under fire from enemies. On that note there are four enemy types in the entire game, not exactly a wide diversity, although I suppose enough for the games runtime.And here is the true shortcoming of this game, it's short. Expect to 100% it in roughly 5 hours.The Verdict:A gore slicked romp through a fun pixel art world. Short game length, a lack of enemy variety, and no real story or challenge modes hold back what could be an intriguing premise of a more fully fleshed out experience. A true 7/10 game, pretty good, not bad. Wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvanias are hard for me to enjoy, but Carrion gets me there. It's short, fairly linear, and does a good job of directing you to the next section. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion is a Metroidvania/puzzle game where you play as a shapeless blob of teeth, eyes, blood, and gore, and you explore a military/science/military science complex while murdering and/or eating every human in sight. The graphics are pixely and retro, but very clearly modern in the lighting and effects. The game looks really good for what it is.The gameplay is smooth, and the movement feels wonderful as you whip around tight tunnels and more expansive caverns with uncountable tentacles. The game is relatively short, but enjoyable all the same; after a while the puzzles start getting repetitive, but the game introduces new mechanics every so often to keep things fresh. The combat is quite interesting--despite being a monstrous abomination, you start the game rather weak, and have to rely on ambush tactics to not get shot to death. Later on, as you get more abilities, the power level of the enemies ramps up as well, so the combat stays feeling fresh the whole game.The story is...somewhat anemic, but for what the game is, I think it works really well. You get bits of lore in flashback sequences where you control a human, and quite a bit remains unclear at the end of the game, but I didn't mind that--story wasn't what I was here for. And while what story there is is quite interesting, it doesn't make me feel like I missed out.All in all, probably my third favorite game of all time. 10/10, wish there were more games where you get to play as a hungry shapeless blob of meat and terrorize the military and civilians alike.

_childDocuments_.review: I won this game in a giveaway and I'm glad I finally gave it chance after so long. I wasn't sure if I would like a reverse horror game, but I may've had too much fun playing it... +1 perfect games!I've enjoyed some 2D games here and there, but I've never gone out of my way to seek one. After playing this though, I might be swayed... I don't know if it was the reverse horror sub-genre or the satisfaction of swinging people around so fluidly, but it was kind of a vibe!It seems Carrion was more of an introduction to the "amorphous creature of unknown origin" as any remnants of a story reside in the various flashbacks you encounter along your path of carnage. In the end, not much information is given on the creature other than it being hungry. I haven't looked much into it, but it seems there're hints of a sequel. I hope so! I could see writers taking what was given to us already and spinning quite a story out of it for the next game.I found the controls pretty clunky. It defaults to controller, but it made more sense to play on MKB for me. Even near the end, I found myself getting a bit jumbled here and there. I really wish they would've allowed for WASD movement instead of just the mouse. On a similar note... No map. Period. I get why though! I say more later, but it would make the game far too easy.This is where the game really shines. Grabbing and munching down on people, grabbing and throwing people, throwing objects at people... There're just so many ways to get the job done. That doesn't even take into consideration the best part of this game...There are quite a few. I won't say how much, but I'll say that the creature ends up with 3 varying sizes. These sizes grant the option of using certain abilities, if unlocked. This added a bit of a puzzle aspect to the game, which was unexpected, but I absolutely loved it. The biggest obstacle is the map. Or rather... the lack thereof. I urge you to try your best before using this, but you do you! Below is a link to the maps from the official wiki. I ended up using them after failing to navigate the world for probably an hour... on Carrion Wiki

_childDocuments_.review: Obvious answer is that the game is overpriced for 4-7 hours with almost no replay value, not only that but there are not many chances that you get to use your abilities to actually fight stuff, as most enemies die as soon as you grab them. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, I do want to say that I do enjoy this game and would recommend to anyone who likes to inhumanely kill random people in games. Half the time you do not even need to kill them because the only real reason why you need to do so is if they have a weapon or you need health. So there are times when you are in full health and all the humans do not have any weapons, more than likely you will still kill them anyways because its funny to ragdoll them around with your tentacles and cover the room in their blood. But enough about the fun game play that is actually rather tactical (at least until you get the 3rd transformation attack command, then it just becomes a hide in the corner and spam e to defeat most enemies game), let us talk about the actual problem of the game.As many people have pointed out there is no in game map of the world and while it is true that the game is rather linear and only really has like a 5 hour game time, there was still moments where I was legit lost and kept running around in circles trying to find where to go. This makes it even more frustrating when if you want to collect all the containment samples, you have to explore the map. There is not even a fast travel option between areas either which makes the experience even more annoying as you are literally travelling through empty areas to get where you need to go (because you probably already killed everyone for teh lolz). I get that might not match the lore of the game to match a biological super organism with fast travel and map awareness but the easy fix would have been to tie it to the save points as they all seem to be connected throughout the entire facility and the creature does use them to travel between different areas. It would make this game so much less of a headache if I could select where I go from those save points and know what I have left remaining. Other than that, I love this game and hope this indie project is able to make a worthy sequel that fixes this issue from an otherwise solid, albeit short game.

_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Finished this game 100% with all achievements unlocked. Game is very fun and a change from the usual Human vs Alien/Monster trope, where you are the monster hunting humans in a secret underground base under Seattle (The city is never stated, but the space needle tower gives it away). While playing as Carrion i felt a mix of being The Thing monster from the classic movie and the Xenomorphs from the Alien franchise. Not much lore in the game apart from the different areas of the base you visit and the brief few times you play as a human in flashbacks. From what i gathered they found an ancient ruin under Seattle which they then built a base on top and around of. They found the Carrion creature in this ruin and started studying it and some how it woke up and escaped and that's where the game begins. It roughly took me 3-4 hours to finish the game too 100% Only cons are its a bit too easy and a bit too expensive for how short the game is. Also when you are at maximum size (3 health bars) it can be a bit glitchy trying to make the monster go where you want it too, especially down narrow passages. Apart from that a fun game that will keep you occupied over a weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewed after 100% completion. A surprisingly fun puzzler, wrapped in an atmospheric package. The atmosphere in this game is really great. You feel like a menacing "THING" like entity that can devour anything in it's patch. It feels really great to naturally gain new abilities over the course of the story that also unlock new areas. this is nothing new for metroid-vania style games, but it was well done here. Movement and combat are physics based, and rather fun to experiment with. Bursting through a vent and hurling enemies at each other never got old. The game is fairly short, which some may see as a negative. However, with all the 80+ hour games in recent memory, I found it rather refreshing to have a self contained playable experience that is short but doesn't compromise on content. I did find a few instances where I needed to reload in order to "unstick" myself from certain puzzles. I'm not sure if this was required, or if I just could not think of any other solutions. Thankfully these instances were really rare. A standout entry in the slew of recent metroid-vania style games. This one offers a fresh take on the player character, and the puzzles felt very satisfying. This game felt like a refined package, and is highly recommended if you are into this genre or monsters.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: You wouldn't think that a platformer without jumping would work, but this game is a slithery, destructive delight. My one criticism is that the lack of a map makes navigation tricky at times, but the way the character movement, level traversal, and puzzle-solving work really add a new fun factor to a game that feels both classic and fresh.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhat of a katamari of gore, with some smart puzzles that demand you to think, but not too much. Tons of action. Very short, and that's after getting lost tons of times because the game has NO MAP. Nice atmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: If you like a side scrolling puzzle game, this game delivers satisfying gory content. But if you want to immerse yourself in the role of the monster as the game suggests, you may find the immersion broken up with seemingly silly mechanics and abilities. Not to mention you switch to the humans sometimes, the purpose I don't know as I refunded the game after I couldn't take anymore.Love the blood tendrils, the feel is smoothStealth elements are left to be desired, i want to hunt and stalk and kill, the short rechargeable stealth to just move past lasers isnt exciting to me.less logic more alien based ways to solve puzzles would be nice. I want to feel like im invading the humans research facility, I was so lost i had no idea where I was going half the time.i dont feel powerful when i have to shrink to use abilities, going back and forth to dump biomoass, then oh wait i need it to bust thru wood, let me go grab it, oh wait i have to dump it again to shoot thru these blocks, ok i need it again to move on... the guys with the laser shields and machine guns that you cant eat? really? I feel like this could seriously be an awesome game of cat and mouse, but in its current form its not my cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: If you like John Carpenter's The Thing or similar movies and wanted to experience the other side as the lethal and unknown creature then this is as close to the perfect game as it gets. It is very Cinematic in the ways the enviroments are set up, often times you will be in a position to ambush the unsuspecting victims in one decicive strike, one after the other while people run and drop unconscious from the mere sight of you. The music and sound design really add to the atmosphere.The way the Monster moves around is also very different from humanoid characters and gives alot of freedom while also feeling completely alien and adaptive to any enviroment. Truly an amazing although short experience worth getting if ur have any Interest in it.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: It doesn't really do all that much with its own concept, leaving it as an incredibly plain experience. It's supposed to be gory but the most you can do is bifurcate people. You're supposed to be an ever-changing monster but the abilities for each tier are really not exciting. Get it on sale or you'll probably feel cheated; There's nothing innovative here.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved it. The presentation, the mechanics, everything. Not going to read all this? Just know it's everything it advertises and then some. Takes about 5 hours to 100% the main game and an hour to run the extra map.  The feel of being this predatory mass of flesh scuttling around at 100mph is amazing and unsettling, You are quick and very agile. The bigger you get it can get a bit clumsy trying to squeeze through but it just adds to the feeling of being this freight train of death. Don't let it go to your amorphous head though, you can get torn to pieces pretty quickly if you aren't careful.   Puzzles are light, nothing too taxing or complex. The pacing is spot on for the most part, backtracking for extras flowed it a bit but even those are fairly quick. Maps have enough thought put in that you aren't rerunning entire maps to 100% the game. Overall the game feels more linear than most search action titles, but there is a hub world and all. For the most part you won't be backtracking much, this isn't a collect-a-thon and there aren't many unnecessary collectables to find (9).   I know people gripe about the lack of a map and I get it, but the game isn't a massive map sprawling out everywhere, so the few times I wasn't sure of where I was going were brief and all of them involved backtracking for 100%. If I had any other small issues it would be the occasional hiccup with aiming. When you get massive sometimes it's hard to tell where things are going to erupt from and it caused a few bad situations. I could see people complaining about the length versus the cost, but at five hours I feel like it's just right and doesn't overstay it's welcome. There's a decent presence in the workshop of new maps and levels if you want to squeeze more time out of it.If you're a horror fan and/or a gore hound you'll love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: well the base game is incredible its has an unique atmosphere from the get go, and it makes you feel like an unstoppable beast tearing through everything in your path. If anyone enjoys high paced action, with a strong resilience to blood and gore I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that a 2D game about playing a deadly mass of flesh and sinew can feel WAY MORE immersive than 80% of the stuff out there shows HOW MUCH this game's design is incredible. This is a DEFINITIVE PICK.In order to spoil as little as possible, first a few notes that don't go in-depth but distill what the presentation doesn't tell you.Sound design, level design, mechanics and environmental story-telling mixed so well in Carrion that despite being a 2D game, it's immersive and challenging (also, it's not just gore, there are some puzzles!). It's a short game (less than 6 hours for me to fully complete), but it's the best buck you'll spend, provided you get into it.Devs risked not putting an in-game map, but I only call it "risk" because the average player expects a map. But that makes Carrion better for it. Trust me. And if you don't......then here's the in-depth part. No story spoilers, but some gameplay aspects will be spoiled.Controls are minimal and easy to get, but the gameplay excels through the level design. A lot is taught to you on how to play the game without a single word or button prompt, by just doing things like adding a vent above a room. At the start, you only move though ducts as you hear scientists and personnel screaming, selling you the feel of how it goes being a amorphous life-form who just escaped containment and now wants to escape/hunt. As you see more rooms with multiple paths, like ducts and such, you might ignore them, but as powerful enemies appear, you get more reasons to use them. Ambushing, using environment, and other emergent gameplay choices are never taught to you in a tutorial, and the discovery of them imparts in you this feel of learning, as if you actually are that murderous mass of flesh. This aspect is the textbook example of how "less tutorial" is better. Or actually, make a tutorial that doesn't use words, and doesn't look like a tutorial.As you move, the movement goes from clunky and strange, until the point you're darting through the map at high speed like it's the natural thing to do. And the biomass grows, it gets less nimble and harder to move, giving a perfect sense of what it feels to move all that flesh and sinew. And since you don't have an in-game map, you'll be exploring a lot. This again helps imparts the feeling of not only controlling, but actually being in the Carrion's place. You squirm, swim, and move about, until you stumble in a new place. Then, a grin appears on your face, as you go about hunting your objectives (and whatever stands in your way). Exploration in this game is SO satisfying, even if a bit frustrating. But at least the length of the game and the maps aren't great enough to the point getting lost doesn't become a problem.And all these gameplay techniques that impart immersion are backed up by great sound design. The minimal sounds that you hear every time, like the tendrils reaching for spots or grates being destroyed. Everything sounds crisp and representative. Then, the guttural sounds the Carrion makes bring home the feel of being an abomination. Music is mostly background, with great care to not force its way into attention, but spiking in tension on the right moments.I think the last game that I played which felt this immersive was Elite Dangerous, and that is a first-person spaceship flight simulator. Carrion is the best thing I've played in the last year or so.

_childDocuments_.review: For such a simple game this is definitely one of the most fun I've ever played! _childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: There is a kernel of a good game to Carrion. If nothing else, Carrion delivers on its core premise very well. Every animation, from the way your tentacles extend to move you around, to the satisfying feeling of ripping a door or a grate off its hinges, down to the screams of your enemies as you streak by with vicious hit and run tactics, it all comes together to truly make you feel like a terrifying killing machine.What kills it is the size-changing mechanic and the backtracking. You see, the actual core gameplay mechanic of the game is that you have different abilities available when you are different sizes. Kill enemies to grow bigger,  and get stronger, deadlier abilities, though at the cost of mobility. However, all puzzles use this mechanic, and often boil down to "you must be this size to solve this puzzle!" Nothing kills the momentum so fast as when you realise you have to go back and find a pool to dump some of your biomass in before continuing, then backtracking to open a single door, then backtracking to pick up your biomass, then returning to the door... and you do this over and over and over. I dreaded every time I cleared a room, feeling like a badass, only to see a lever behind a grate, realising the monotony of what was coming.It's not a good puzzle if it takes 5% of my time to solve it, and 95% of my time just going back and forth doing busy work.But not content to waste your time on just a small scale, the game also wants to be a metroidvania, and of course, with that comes more backtracking. Now don't get me wrong, I enjoy returning to old areas to explore previously unreachable areas, but Carrion does everything it can to make the experience as tedious as possible. Firstly, enemies don't respawn, so when you do go back, you'll find nothing but empty room upon empty room to greet you. Then you have to contend with the lack of a map, which, considering samey corridors and a maze-like overworld, seems unforgivable. Then, when you finally do find the ONE room (yes, only one per level) you were looking for, it contains nothing but a disappointing fire resist or energy upgrade.In summary, a good game, wrapped in a very lazy metroidvania. It really feels like they just wanted to make a linear action game, and it would have been better for it.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect length, great polish and execution and pacing. Playing The Thing from The Thing is great fun. All it was missing was a real victory lap gorefest at the end but all in all, an excellent game. Played the whole of it on the Steam Deck and had a great time of it, though mousing is plainly a lot more precise, I think for veteran fps players it would trivialize the difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited for the game, and did indeed enjoy myself.People who are quick to learn new things AND have spatial memory will probably plough through this game as fast as I did (4 hours).The game was not at all difficult, the only deaths I incurred were at my own hand when i forgot something or was exposed to something new for the first time. Having no fog of war and a lack of any real resistance to being grabbed means enemies are just waiting to be slaughtered. Do not go into this expecting a challenging experience combat wise.The map is well crafted, however it would appear to have no random elements which means replaying is a dull experience unless there is some rogue-like mode added in the future. All in all, I recommend the game, it's a fun experience and definitely one of the fastest games i picked up on. I never really felt stuck.While I don't mind the amount i paid, If I knew all the details I know now going in, i'd have waited until the game was 10-15 dollars.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of the game is very interesting. _childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game ALOT! The main campaign is maybe 5 hours? And it's super fun on its own. _childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly enjoyable with a menacing twist in the horror monster genre. Your movement and speed and game play options throughout the game really encourages you to deal with obstacles in your own unique way. Puzzles littered throughout the game are thought provoking yet don't bog down the experience and lore, while sometimes sudden in its introduction, is very welcome in a game which could very easily been devoid of any as a generic horror game. There is quite a bit of gore, so be warned, but what else can you expect from a reversed horror experience.I did however, find that knowing where to go and mini cutscenes where your camera was forced to watch the opening of a door could slow the gameplay.All in all, my biggest gripe was the fact that there wasn't more game to play. Though mods and the community help with that a bit.7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Refreshingly disgusting. So much fun. Just long enough. All my initial rubs related to navigation, but once you realize which area is the "overworld" and that everything from there is a "dungeon," the rest comes down to puzzling your way through the screens, and a true map would probably detract from the overall experience. You're a flailing—but intelligent—organism, not a drone with GPS. Feel your way through it—you certainly have enough tentacles.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent 2D game, not too short, not too long, metrovania light, but with the twist of you playing the monster rather than the hero. The controls are allot easier than it looks and the monster is fun to play, while the story is strait forward. A decent back catalogue game to get during a sale at around 10 EUR, in my view.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: What a unique and refreshing experience Carrion was! You can tell just how much love and enthusiasm the creators had for this title. Just wish there was more. Took less than 7 hours to 100% it but I would still say it's easily worth the $20. I wasn't expecting so many puzzle elements, but found that they balance the pace of the game out pretty well. There were several moments of where I'd find myself even more eager for action after spending a few minutes on a puzzle. While this was frustrating at times, the anticipation made it that much more exciting to discover a new room to rampage through.My biggest critique I have for the game is that without a hubworld map, I often found myself getting lost or just wandering (often in circles) until I stumbled upon my objective. Movement is so fluid and free that you can at least cover ground quickly... so you usually don't have to wander for TOO long.  It also became a little sad backtracking to complete the game, as any time you revisit an old area there's almost nothing left to destroy. Everything considered, Carrion is a small masterpiece. This game totally breaks the mold for the metroidvania genre with subtle storytelling and tons of unique mechanics that are introduced intuitively without ever holding the player's hand too much. If you've ever wondered what it's like to be a  hyper-intelligent Lovecraftian spaghetti-monster, definitely pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: It sounds fun and the idea is good, but it is a metroidvania type and real bad at it by not giving any help about where you could go back after unlocking new abilities coupled with a lot of one-way tunnels which prevents you to go back the same path you came in case you missed/forgot/now unlocked and in general hard to navigate on the map.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Ok let me be honest, this game is able to be beated quickly but is pretty fun I have so far completed it twice and honestly, I say buy a better game with the ability to play much longer like PPG, teardown or something like that but if you want a low spec game that brings fun for 2 - 4 hours then this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful pixel monster game, where you get to enjoy the unique pleasure of guiding the squirmous mass of tentacles and teeth around narrow passage ways and into small rooms to gorily rip and tear hapless humans to pieces. It's exactly what you would want from the game, but also with an understated humour and light-heartedness to it. Equal parts puzzle-exploration and action, this is good for a good few hours of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and epic game. I love games with blood and gore and this is a very good game. A bit challenging but not really. The soundtrack, the mechanics, the animation is just 10/10. However, I wish this game was a bit longer because this is my type of game and it took me a good day and a half to finish it. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: CARRION is first and foremost a fun game. You slither around chomping on any unarmed scientists you can find and grow stronger as you progress with some fun abilities. The game is mostly a stealthy puzzle solving game with great pixel art and organic movement that you can feel the weight of as you grow larger and more unwieldy. The enemies are absolutely lethal at times, but you can definitely overwhelm them quickly if you want to play that way.The puzzles are fun and I rarely found myself being frustrated with the difficulty of them, but I did find myself getting lost at times and having to roam around looking for the next objective since the game lacks hints or guidance. The game knows exactly how long it should last since playing as a bundle of flesh being fun can only last so long and I respect that. If you really enjoy the game, there's a modding community that has made more challenging levels if you're up for that. Overall a great game for some chaotic fun.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion has been the definition fun to play from start to finish.  Its general gameplay is fast and enjoyable. You get skill upgrades throughout the game, so it doesn’t get boring, and you can get additional powers by solving puzzles in each area, if you want to. The puzzles require you to think but aren't hard enough to get you stuck on anything, which makes for fun and engaging gameplay. In some scenarios, you have to think strategically but it won’t bog you down with anything actually, terribly difficult. The art style and settings are great. It’s charming pixel art makes your kills feel gory, but not actually horrifying and the gritty mechanical setting makes a nice backdrop to the gameplay. The story isn’t deep in any way, but it has a great concept. It puts you as the horrifying monster and sets you on a mission to escape from the lab you were created in. Carrion is mostly gameplay focused, so don’t expect the story or ending to leave you stunned. Overall, it’s a super fun and engaging game that stays it’s welcome but doesn’t drag. I’d recommend it to anyone who likes this type of game :)
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not that hard, pretty much plausible to play, but gameplay is the same for an entire game, puzzles and fights are lacking unqieness. _childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: 9.75/10, awesome game!Can't give it a 10 out of 10, because it is VERY short. Sadly, i've completed it by 100% in 6 hours. (And i enjoyed every second of it!)The only bad thing about this game is the lack of map. If you have problems with directions - you might have a bad time.I got so confused that i had to draw a map in paint for a couple of areas. So yeah, you can complete the game in 4 hours or less.Developers, CARRION (wheeze) with this amazing job!
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Become a monster and smash things. It really is quite satisfying to just smash random things and terrorize people. However, the puzzles get slightly repetitive after a few hours(yes I know I have to deposit bodymass to get through this part, just let me rampage please), and the gameplay is pretty short, plus there's basically not much replayability after getting all the achievements. Highly recommend using this  if you get lost. I would still recommend buying the game if you can get it on sale since overall the gameplay was enjoyable and the pixel art was pretty decent
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Carrion: A unique platformer where you play as a tentacle monster. Interesting and fun, but its short campaign makes it a better buy on sale.Gather 'round, fans of the twisted and unique! 'Carrion' invites you to step into the slimy shoes (or tentacles) of a monstrous blob. In a brief but engaging 6-hour playthrough, you'll puzzle-solve and people-absorb your way through a world filled with intrigue. While the graphics and sound design hit the mark, the story might leave you with a lingering hunger for more answers.Despite its fascinating concept and enjoyable gameplay, 'Carrion' might feel a bit too short for its full price tag. So, if you're eager to explore what it's like to be the nightmare creature in a horror flick, you might want to snag this game during a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion is an amazing game, it has a very unique idea done perfectly.It makes you feel like a real, movie-style monster, you won't be rushing into battle killing everyone instantly, you will have to plan your approach, picking them off one by one.The movement is fast and smooth, making it easy to quickly dart in and out of enemy sight.Navigation can, however, sometimes be a bit annoying, as you do not have a map to show charted/uncharted locations. Sometimes the lack of a map can make you stuck on a point, not knowing where to go next. I can see what they went for with this navigation style, they wanted it to feel like your a creature thrown into an unknown environment, but that doesn't mean that it can't be a bit annoying at times.It is a very short game. In 8 hours of gameplay I have finished the game twice, which is a shame but I understand why they did this, because if they had added anything more it would've felt like the game dragged on for too long and any less it would've felt unfinished.In conclusion: Should you get Carrion? Yes, it is so much damn fun and everything works so well.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion delivers on its premise (reverse horror game about a monster escaping a military lab bunker) very well but doesn't do much else.  This is one of many cases I wish Steam had a star or number rating system.  I'd give this game a solid 7/10.  Reason being, it's very easy to do everything the game has in one playthrough which you could complete in 4 hours if you didn't get lost and confused a bunch like I did.  Personally, I did it in 7.While very enjoyable for what it is, I wish there was more.  For instance, if you spare a bunch of humans that aren't directly threatening or blocking you, nothing different happens than if you slaughter them all mercilessly.  Also, most the optional upgrades are very boring and don't change the gameplay hardly at all.  More fire resistance.  More total energy.  Completely superfluous and only worth collecting for the puzzle solving and achievements.  I would really like more meaningful upgrades that allow you to use abilities in newer, cooler ways.  None of that here.There's also these...flashbacks I guess where you play as a human.  I thought these flashbacks would show us how the monster came to be in the humans' possession, and it sort of does but in an extremely vague way.  There's just not enough to "sink your teeth into" here.  Essentially it's a Metroidvania with limited puzzle solving, exploration, and combat that's over with leaving you wanting more but not in the awesome way a fully realized game leaves you wanting more.  You want more because...there wasn't quite enough.It's worth a buy, but I'd wait for a sale.  $10 maybe $15 is what this game is worth.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game with novel mechanics and beautiful design. The puzzles are interesting and stimulating but the combat, while satisfying at first, is not challenging enough. More often than not you can just blitz your way through enemies rather than using any form of strategy. Also, it is a pretty short game but I feel like this could be fixed by upping the difficulty and increasing the amount of enemies. If you're bored or have some extra pocket change this is definitely worth a picking up, especially if its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really like a lot of games, so the ones I do I tend to ration out as long as I can, but with Carrion I couldn't help but finish it immediately then start a second play through to play over the next few days. I can not resist coming back to the absorbing atmosphere, engaging combat, and pretty much everything else about the game. Even the movement controls are fun!  Also space monster go nom.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the old school Sega Saturn era graphics of this game. Despite the look, game play is smooth and seamless. The way the creature moves and attacks is incredibly aggressive and violent, yet almost graceful. This is a great sci-fi story that conjured memories of movies like The Thing and games like Half-Life. The reverse horror angle is great fun from annihilating screaming scientists to the challenge of later enemies. The maze like levels and increasingly difficult puzzles make this game both fun and engaging. I'd recommend it if the above description sounds interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion is unique game where you take control of the monster and slither your way in a mild Metroidvania-esque environment. _childDocuments_.review: This game seemed really cool but I'm just sick of it.  This is a soft "don't recommend".  It might be for you but I'm about 70% through the game and didn't like most of it.  Playing as the monster, especially one that's just a big fleshy nightmare, is a good pitch.  The problem is that the actual level design and gameplay aren't that fun.The best parts of this game happen when you break into a room of people and cause carnage.  It's as fun and gross as you'd imagine.  The issue is that a lot of things are put in your way that make it hard to do that.  For example, there are base human enemies that die quickly and also ones in armor with a shield.  These shielded enemies force you to play around them; you need to hide and wait until they've turned around then strike when the moment is right.I understand why these enemies are here.  It breaks up your normal playstyle by forcing you to hide.  This can create cool moments where you feel like you're stalking your prey.  It also ensures that not every combat encounter is the exact same which adds variety and prevents it from getting too repetitive.  It even makes you feel powerful when you're later given the tools to face them head-on.  But none of those reasons matter to me because it wasn't fun.  This disconnect between the design decision and its fun-factor was everywhere.  I could usually understand  a design decision was made but that didn't make it fun to play.One design decision I can't understand was the lack of any map or direction in the gameplay.  I know monsters don't keep meticulous maps but I'd really appreciate one.  It wouldn't be necessary if I could tell any of the environments apart.  So much of my time in the game was me just searching each path I could take until I found a dead-end.  Then I would double back and try the next path.  If I hit a switch, the game moved the camera in the direction of doors that are opening which gives a pretty clear guide of the direction you should go.  But it was still so easy to get lost if you got turned around a single time.  You can make your monster roar and it will tell you the general direction of checkpoints but that's about it.Hours into the game, you're introduced to a hazard that one-shot kills you if you walk through it.  I don't know why they would do this.  As far as I saw, it's the only instant-death mechanic in the entire game.  This one feels uniquely bad because of how I encountered them.  Most of my traversal time is me flying between rooms as fast as I can because I barely know where I am.  Then suddenly I enter a room and explode.  I'm only moving so quickly because the rooms all look the same and it's hard to keep track of their relation to each other.  This forces me to run around a lot trying to find where to go or whether I just missed something in a past room.  But halfway through the game, I'm suddenly punished for it by random trips back to a checkpoint.  That wouldn't be a big deal if the level design and traversal problems didn't exist.  But because they do, it's extremely frustrating to suddenly be forced to move more slowly through the worst section of the game.Once you get where you're going, there are two types of encounters: combat and puzzles.  We already talked combat so let's talk puzzles.  The puzzle rooms are usually not very challenging or interesting.  The usual experience is that you're running aimlessly around the world until you come across a pinkish pool of water.  You think to yourself, "hm, I bet theres a puzzle coming up," and continue on your way.  One or two rooms later you see a switch on the other side of a small gap.  You, being the smart player you are, go back to that pool of water and press A to change forms so you can hit that switch from a distance.  You then go back to that other room to hit the switch.  Half the time this will cut you off from that pool which forces you to move on in the other form.  The other half the time, you just go back to the pool yet again to change forms back to your original one then you can head back to the room with the switch to continue playing.  That means the most common puzzle experience is just running back and forth between a few rooms which barely counts as a puzzle.  There was exactly one puzzle that required me to put any thought into it and it's not like that felt satisfying to solve, either.I don't know what the deal was with me and this game.  I also don't know why I wrote this long of a review.  I really wanted to like this game.  I like metroidvanias, exploration, and unique movement and gamplay styles.  The core idea of this game is really good.  But, oh my god, why is it like this?

_childDocuments_.review: There's potential in Carrion, but as it stands it's mostly just a flash game. The graphic design is not very good, and the game isn't much fun to play. Just by the premise, it sounds like it would be really interesting, but there isn't any true reward to your time and money invested. It's an insanely short game with no real replayability. The controls and mechanics are obnoxious, trying to force in puzzles and power-ups in a way that feels entirely artificial. Though there's entertaining sounds and some vaguely challenging segments, it never becomes really amusing to play. You're at your weakest at the start and it's insanely disappointing, but by the end of the game it just feels tedious. There's only a few small parts where I felt it genuinely played on the amorphous tentacled monster trope, but I think there's just something that is not satisfying about how it's played. Get it on sale, or skip it entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the classic Metroid games from the NES/SNES era then this is the game for you. _childDocuments_.review: CARRION is kind of a Metroidvania in which you play a monster trying to break out of it's lab.The idea of CARRION certainly is fun and the atmosphere works well. Dashing through small corridors as a giant monster feels great, especially with the fitting visuals. The sometimes clunky controls partially diminish this feeling, though playing with a controller worked well most of the time. I can also imagine very well that the few issues that exist, like having to explicitly eat a human in two phases rather than just one, or the monster having trouble finding the vent you are going for when you are at junctions, could be fixed by future updates quite easily.The biggest weakness of the game is it's length and how you spend it. While you're cruising through the main quest line, it feels pretty fluid and like a continuous adventure. But any type of backtracking is horrible. There is no map of any kind and all corridors within an area look similar. Take a wrong turn by accident? Now you have to wander through empty corridors to find where you have to go. Even worse, the game deliberately forces you to backtrack if you are going for 100%, as many of the secret containment units require abilities only unlocked later in the game. I gave up on those in the end and looked up their location in an online guide after I finished everything else.All that considered, the game still only offers a few hours of gameplay. I cannot imagine requiring more than 7 hours for a 100% run even without any external guides. And then you're spending only maybe half of your time actually having fun.Would I recommend this game? For $5, definitely. For $10, maybe. For $20, no. If you can get this on an at least 50% sale, grab it.

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance, this is a stripped-down metroidvania with an excellent theme. Throughout the game, the simplified combat takes on new and challenging aspects, all within the theme, making it even stronger. The abilities you gain are fascinating and useful, things that either wouldn't work or wouldn't fit in a more traditional game in the genre, and they work in combat and in the environmental puzzles. The variety of powers, and their variety of uses, keep things fresh. None of them become outdated, either, thanks to the biomass mechanic.The idea of the powers available to you changing based on how much biomass you have--basically how much life--is genius. It keeps the toolbox manageable for general situations, since you only have immediate access to a subset of your powers, but some of the more complicated puzzles require you to manipulate this mechanic to switch sizes so that you can use different powers. It's not just the puzzles, either; there are enemies that are easiest to deal with using the webbing from the smallest (and weakest) form, some to which the midsize dash and defensive spikes are better suited, and big bads that you should only engage at your beefiest. The story is sparse within the action, but it's mostly told in details and in the environment. The red alert chyrons tell you something about what's going on. Near the end, it tells you where the last of the humans are hiding. The flashback segments are slightly annoying, but they lend a sense of dread to the rest of the game that I think you'd miss if they weren't present. I loved the ending, too.There's no map, which is kind of a cardinal sin in this genre. Getting around requires a pretty good memory, even with the environmental cues. If not for the control room idea that gives you an in-game way to figure out what you missed and where, it would basically require outside help. Honestly, even though the gamespace is so small, adding a kind of map that is formed by memories of where the hives are would be welcome. This game is short, which to me is a strength. It certainly makes the most of its core idea, and then it ends. There's no fluff or needless bulk to it. There's a level of collectionism to it, but it's not hard to get everything in a reasonable amount of time. There are challenging segments, too, but usually the problem is approach. It feels like if you take too much damage, you can't finish a fight, but there's always a way. Looking at a room and deciding how to attack is a lot of fun, and there are always options.All in all, this is a special game. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game,Ok so first to start with dislikes. I am not crazy about pixel art but I understand that is the craze and it "can" be easier to work with - to be honest I let it slide for this game because its clear they used those resources in better ways. Second I feel that its a bit short - I wish there had been more flash-backs to make it more clear what was the story (not going to spoil it).For good stuff. The controls feel natural; sometimes they are a pain in the ass (when you get big and are moving through small spaces). The controls respond well and quickly which leads to some wonderful horror movie moves like snatching foes into the vents or flooding into a room. On that that did a great job making the metroidvania style advancement. Someone should get a raise for such a great job mapping out the levels - they put in the puzzle progression AND put in quality of life short-cuts so you do not spend hours back tracking and trying to recall where you saw that puzzle mechanic you just got the tool to overcome. I realize had they done a worse job; they could have dragged out the game. I found it funny in the end credits the # of voice actors.I would say 8/10 - totally worth full price; but be mindful that after its over your going to want more of it. _childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion is terrific little metroidvania, with a great hook.  You are the monster!  You are in some sort of science facility, and you wake up and start exploring and eating people.  As you eat more people you gain mass and get larger and more powerful.  As you explore the facility and the areas nearby, you find mutations that give you various powers.  Each power only works at a particular monster size, so you need to be strategic with your mass to solve puzzles or to get through combat scenarios.   The movement and animation are first class.  You monster looks amazing, and as it moves it is sticking its tentacles out to all nearby surfaces and slithering all over the place, yet at the same time it is super responsive and goes exactly where you want it to, it is extremely cool.  The combat is great, you are fast and powerful, you pop out, wreck some ♥♥♥♥, and then slither back into a vent before anyone can respond.  You get very cool powers that are fun to use in combat as well.  The game has a lot of little touches that help with the atmosphere, some of the people in the facilities are unarmed civilians and when they see you they just cower and start crying or run away screaming, you can let them be, or slaughter them.  Everything looks great, the pixel work is fantastic.  Carrion probably has my favorite ending of any game I can remember.  I didn't see it coming and it is awesome.  It was a short ride, but I enjoyed every minute of it and would recommend the game to anyone.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Deep in an underground research facility, a study sample held in a glass container shakes and bursts apart, unleashing a new horror onto humankind. A living biohazard to anything made of meat, it rips apart and consumes flesh to add directly to its own biomass, becoming bigger and evolving into more aggressive abilities. Creep your way through vents or leave blood spatters in the hallways as you make your escape from below the surface.  6-8+ hours to complete, CARRION is a reverse-horror game with pixel graphics where you play as the monster hunting down humanity and those who imprisoned you. Be sneaky or loud! Changing your size changes your abilities allowing a solid amount of gameplay variation. Weirdly chill and relaxing, the character's movement is smooth and natural despite being a mass of flesh-eating tentacles. The level design is clever with engaging logic puzzles and steady game progression. Rare are the games that let you play as the Lovecraftian Monster, rarer that the game is made well, and I highly suggest you take the opportunity to play CARRION.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't reasonably say that CARRION is worth the full asking price. I haven't found everything there is to find or done every last little thing to be done, but I beat the core game in 5 hours, so half the asking price would be much more reasonable. Buy it if it's ever 50% off or better.CARRION encapsulates your journey from a small, squishy organic monster into a slightly larger, squishy organic monster. Gameplay is fun, especially if you enjoy shrieks of terror and the wailing of their women, and is challenging but beatable. CARRION is equal parts action-horror and puzzle-platformer, as your progress is checked by your ability to match the right combination of size & function to a series of locks in your way. At a few points, you cannot progress until you find the right function (I once had to look up a guide to find the right function, since there are no in-game maps or objectives).Controls are at times tiresome, but overall uncomplicated and suitable for a casual gamer. I don't think I ever encountered an actual bug or crash, and this makes sense because the game is built to mid-1990s aesthetics, so it should not put a strain on your system to run.I would overall give CARRION a meaty 6 or 6.5 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion breaks the mould for 2D side-scrollers in two ways! Be the anti-hero, with a clever, fun-to-play and incredibly unique story. You're a tendril-spitting **flesh mound** that loves the taste of human flesh, specifically the humans that caused your slimy meat-sac to exist. Mechanics in this game are so fun, watching all your little meat tentacles shoot off constantly to grab the walls and grow bigger. Consuming your 'diet' is endless entertainment and BURSTING through wood, doors and walls just... C'mon. Even if this game had no point other than domination as a D&D-style flesh mound, that'd be enough. 5/5, would partner up with Super Meat Boy.

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion is everything I ever wanted. If you are like me, kind of tired of being the hero. Always saving princesses in different castles. Always being that special agent that always does the job perfectly. Always building new settlements to make Preston happy..... This is it. Do you want to be the bad guy? Do you want to be the scary twins at the end of the hallway? Why not be the horrific amalgamation of flesh fiercely running wild in an underground facility slowly leaving your fleshy entrails, to take over the entire structure!Carrion first came to my attention a long time ago, I found a post on twitter with the concept of an awesome game. I´ve been steadily following the development and I could not be more pleased! This game delivers on every aspect of what was promised and more! I won't spoil anything, but I am pleased that there was more character development than I expected. I had a total of 7-9 hours of gameplay, although the game does indeed have replayability. There are many ways to play, mostly in the form of different routes to take and a ton of ways to annihilate anyone standing in your way.I do have one recommendation. If you are the type to go for secrets or achievements, get them along the way. I ended up going back after I finished getting everything I missed. The game is rather linear, though you won't notice it. But trying to go backward is so ungodly confusing. That is not a bad thing about the game, im just an idiot. So overall on the Dove scale of awesomeness, Carrion gets a 10/10.
