_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: CARRION is a very fun reverse horror game in which you assume the role of an amorphous creature of unknown origins, stalking and consuming those that imprisoned you at a secret research facility. As you spread fear and panic throughout the facility, you'll solve puzzles to acquire containment units which will grant devastating abilities on the path to retribution. Slowly growing and evolving into a unrelenting monstrosity that only hungers for blood. The visuals look amazing, and the gameplay feels very unique, its incredibly fun to play as the monster causing torment throughout the facility. The soundtrack is also insanely good and helps add a sense of eeriness to the game. Pretty short but a very enjoyable experience nonetheless, I recommend getting it when its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really know how I feel about this to be honest. The reverse horror premise felt kinda unique. The movement feels fluid until the creature gets bigger with upgrades, then it's a nightmare if you want to navigate across tight corners, especially the one-way vents that suck you in and navigating back to the same place where you came from becomes a hassle. The atmosphere is really well-designed with great pixel art and the accompanying soundtrack that enhances the horror experience. That being said, the game was fun for the first hour and a half and then becomes a chore to finish. There's no map, or visual distinction between areas in the main frontier map. It's like I'm in Daedalus's labyrinth. Some passages are blocked behind upgrades which is fine as it adds to the puzzle element but backtracking after getting upgrades to the same area, with no sense of direction, can be quite frustrating and takes away from otherwise a great game. This also artificially inflates playtime for a game which could be completed within 2 hours. Thanks to maps compiled by , I was able to complete this game.tldr: apart from really frustrating level design with no map, it's a great game. Definitely worth getting on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Was really excited for this game when it was revealed. However, I was so disappointed that I didn't even care enough to play it until now. This game is mindless experience where you search for levers to pull to open a door which leads to more levers and so on. What breaks this game is the lack of variety, there is like 5 unique enemies and the rest are copy pasted throughout the game. On top of this, this game fails to mention it is literally only a puzzle game, who cares if you get to play as a cool monster when you are trapped in a facility filled with boring and un-fun puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: I waited for Carrion since the very early announcement, and wasn't disappointed. Reverse horror is quite interesting genre, and the game's music and visuals are perfect. Controlling inhuman being required some innovation too, and devs nailed it. The only downside is that it is easy to get lost on some levels, where you backtrack dozens of empty maps where everyone was already killed, searching for That One Proper Exit to proceed to the next level. Also some level elements become a bit boring (go there, deposit biomass, return back, do something, go back to gain some biomass, repeat), but it is probably hard to create real obstacles for unstoppable inhuman super-powered nightmare monster. Anyway, the game has delivered its promises, and also it has that rare quality that when you get bored, after a week it feels fresh again and you want to continue. So, I recommend it both for its rare perspective of anithuman protagonist and for pleasing visuals and sound. You can complete the game in several hours, and that's an upside too.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion is an interesting game, its sort of like Metroid, if you played as The Thing rather than a space bounty hunter killing Aliens. Like Metroid you are finding and collecting power-ups to progress forward, and dealing with adversaries and enemies along the way. Carrion often feels more like a puzzle game than a typical metroid or castlevania affair. Sometimes in similar games, the challenge comes more from getting through enemies and finding the right spots on the map, with Carrion you play the monster, so most of the combat encounters are actually not all to difficult, not that you can't or wont die in certain encounters, but it feels like the challenge comes more from finding out which power to use to progress forward or managing your biomass, or finding the powerup to bypass an obstacle.The story is quite sparse and only told through a handful of flashbacks, it leaves a sense of mystery that doesn't really tell you quite what happened or what the carrion creature is or what its motives is, or the motives of Relith the company the was containing the creature. This may bother some, but honestly if they tried to explain everything it probably would have lost mystery and intrigue and very may might hurt the experience.Overall it is a good game with an interesting premise, but feels like it could have done more at the same time, with the latter half slowing down a bit, I look forward to see what else this team will do.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: This is more a mixed review than a negative one but i find Carrion lackluster in a lot of ways.Simply put, the gameplay is boring and most of the time i felt like i was watching the game instead of playing it. Enemy encounters can get tougher later on, but overall you'll be breezing through most of the game.The game does have a few puzzles to mix things up, but they're rather easy and serve more as a distraction than a challenge.To an extent i think this is what the devs were going for, to indulge the player in a power fantasy where next to nothing can stop them, but in the end it doesn't make for a very interesting video game.I do think this game gets a few things right: the character progression is satisfying and constant throughout the experience and the fact that each form you can assume has unique powers means you won't always want to use the same one.Basically, if you're fine with the game being more about the spectacle than the gameplay, i'm sure you'll enjoy Carrion a lot. If you dig the style but want something that doesn't play itself, give BUTCHER a try. It shares Carrion's tone and ultra-violence but actually offers a challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Refreshing puzzle game! Love the concept of being the evil creature. Love the screaming of the people when you enter their sight. It is quite short, but I had heaps of fun and it kept me engaged.I had a slight issue playing on a 1920x1080 monitor. The game would hang on full screen (very weird). But playing windowed in a lower resolution would work. On my 4k monitor running the same resolution, no issue?!
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome and unique, Carrion is as enjoyable as the trailer implies. The puzzles are satisfying, the carnage is glorious. Only negative would be the lack of map in a metroidvania style world design, but you're eldritch abomination on a escape rampage, you don't use maps...I give it 8 delicious scientists out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: First time I played this game I ended up playing for 4 hours straight or so. Basically your getting to play as some kind of combination of the monster from The Thing and Blob, maybe mixed with some lovecraftian old one. Being this monster and finding random ways to kill people for me in endlessly fun. There are some light puzzle elements that I appreciate. A lot of people get hung up on the repetition of the puzzles or the random backtracking and lack of map. I think in some way this meant to get you more into the perspective of "the monster" who's sort of navigating this world blindly and only by aid of vague clues on alerts and messages on the laboratory walls. Whatever, if i got stuck i looked up a walkthrough just to get me to the next area where i could kill and eat more people, it never gets old, and this game is gorgeous. If you like beautifully rendered puzzle games and ubiquitous gore and are remotely interested in this game youll have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing idea, good execution, but some issues with this one. The atmosphere feels like something between Inside and Dead Space. Being a monster is fun, especially when slithering around like angry spaghetti, gobbling up poor researchers from toilet seats. The music is great, the "protagonist" is animated amazingly and I did not encounter any bugs. There are a few issues though:1) The environments looked a bit to samey to me, with their descriptions ("uranium mines" or "leviathan base") being more important than the design2) Being a scary monster is fun ... until you get stuck on a grate not being able to reach a lever on the other side. Yes, it's the puzzle aspect and main gameplay mechanic, but it's somewhat detrimental to the whole b-movie monster madness3) Metroidvania aspects are annoying - I am referring to the kind if gameplay where you see an obviously temporary obstacle early in the game, knowing that some time later you can come back to it and overcome it. Sometimes this can be a great part of the level design (Dark Souls being the prime example) but in this game, it's just annoying - everything looks rather similar and the new ways opening later do not really do anything for me besides feeling stress about having to remember everything.Nevertheless, it's a short, fun game with a unique setting and some very good ideas and most likely not a waste of time at all. :)
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Great aesthetic. Great art. Great animations. Great sound design. Good gameplay. Decent music.Very short. Can 100% in under 6 hours. Maybe has potential for speedrunning, if you're into that.Having to backtrack in order to deposit biomass so that you can use an ability of one of the smaller forms gets very annoying, very quickly.While I understand that it's not "immersive" for a game like this, having a map to help backtrack for containment jars would be nice.Overall: Letter grade B/B-. Buy for full price if you really like the concept, buy on sale if you're not entirely sure about it.

_childDocuments_.review: I followed the development of this game on Twitter quite awhile before it came out and I was really intrigued by the idea. _childDocuments_.review: It's a short but fun game about playing as a monster similar to the alien from The Thing; with morphing abilities, you can disguise to be a person to solve certain puzzles in your way. The physics system makes for a fun rag-doll effect for the humans as well as any objects. Evolution is pretty straightforward, snagging bio samples from people as well as any unique upgrades hiding in the facility. It is a short yet satisfying game, so I can't say it's worthy of the full price; if there was more length and depth to the story I might be able to say $20 is reasonable, but there's not much at the moment. I did think there might possibly be more content in the future, like a full release of a story through an update or at least through DLC; but nothing has come out.

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is beautiful, love it. the mystery/horror vibe, excellent!Gameplay is straight forward and fun. _childDocuments_.review: A bit expensive for the game duration ~4 hours but the experience was interesting.The controls and the way you control the beast is really satisfying and terrifying at the same time. You feel overpowered but also at the same time, some tricks deployed by the humans could do some serious harm, including the deadly fire.Basically, you go through well designed sets of levels and unlock ability by ability. Then you learn to combine them to finish a puzzle or sometimes a combat that I feel is also some sort of puzzle.Really well done, excellent sounds and very fun to play. I just regret the duration and the price but really good quality anyway !I also got a bit confused by the direction of things... couldn't figure out if there was a way forward of it was some metroîd like map where you keep going in every directions the more you unlock powers, it turns out it's an interesting mix of the two where you can go back and forth but often limited to a sub zone, so thta you don't get overwhelmed by the size of the map, good design I think.

_childDocuments_.review: If you watched the monster from John Carpenter's 'The Thing' wreck gory havoc upon the unfortunate human characters and thought "hot damn, that would make a fun videogame", then Carrion is for you. Overall, if you're looking for a short, fun, and exceedingly gory game, then play Carrion.

_childDocuments_.review: A bit short (you can finish it in one longer afternoon session), but on the other hand the game doesn't wear out its welcome. Controls are good (mouse & keyboard are much better than gamepad), graphics are pretty and detailed, music does the job.It feels a bit like a Metroidvania game, but only a few optional upgrades really require you to go back to previously visited areas. _childDocuments_.review: At the time of me writing this I have not completed the game. Even with that I would still recommend it to others. Thus far it's been a delightfully sloppy, body part flinging, parasitic chest popping good time. I mean who the heck doesn't want to play as 'The Thing' from the classic horror hit by J. Carpenter? Carrion lets to be the bloody freak of nature and within some limits you move between levels creating a body count with ever more challenging foes. 9/10 I do recommend, the -1 to score is only due to the music in the game. They could have done a bit more with that and the only time it's good is the 'danger music' when fighting the 'mechs. _childDocuments_.review: Fun Metroidvania-type game where you play an evil monster escaping confinement. The game itself is fun and I would say well-paced for the most part, mixing enemy encounters with puzzles. The whole thing can be completed in about 5 hours casually, which I don't mind personally, but it's certainly not as much content or replay value as you can get from other games at this price point.
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion is a story about a containment breach and the resulting mess thereof. The fun part about it is, that the player actually controls the horrifying creature that escaped the containment. You gain mass by consuming humans which serves not only as increased health but there is also a 3-tiered ability system that depends on your current mass.Gameplay-wise, Metroid comes to mind. You must figure out the way out of the lab facilities and this involves some backtracking as switches can manipulate doors on or off the current scene. Puzzles iteratively integrate new abilities that you can gain on your journey through the facility. So instead of always solving the same puzzles new abilities that you gained recently are absolutely needed for the more recent puzzles. Since your abilities are also tied to your mass, sometimes you need to shed some mass to solve a puzzle. Fortunately, whenever you need to do that, there are biomass pools, where you can deposit some of your mass, which you can later also reattach again.Abilities range from spider-silking opponents to spiking them with thrown projectiles as well as more defensive abilities like cloaking and short time invulnerability. Whenever you gain a new ability, a puzzle is guranteed to be nearby where the new ability is needed to solve it.The overall gameplay isn't too hard. There are occasionally "boss rooms" but they are normally not very hard and can either be brute forced or done by using the terrain and specific features in the scene. I like that there is not "one" solution for these rooms.The graphics are great; the gory mess is presented very nicely in a relatively clean pixel-art style that is pleasing to the eye. I expect nothing else from a game, that is distributed by Devolver and this game certainly delivers in that department.Overall play time for my first playthrough (without walkthrough or any hints) was around 4 hours for me. While 20$ may seem slightly too much, I do not regret my purchase since I was well entertained during these 4 hours. Replayability value seems however low to me; something that may be be omitted by new maps/campaigns via Steam Workshop.I absolutely recommend this to anyone looking for the Metroid feeling and who is not put off by the large amount of (beautiful) pixel gore. Two thumbs up!
_childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: First...this is not a long game, about 3.5 hours-ish. But, I have played through it twice. I love it.  The animation is so damn fluid when you move, its like you can feel being the creature.  Watching it evolve as you unlock upgrades, and feast on the fleshy meat sack hoomans, is very rewarding!If you think the price is too high for the play time, then wait until its on sale. But either way, if you ever wanted to be the creature instead of the humans, or, if like me, you are a fan of John Carpenter's The Thing, or, also like me, love H.P. Lovecraft...get this game.  The HPL part is you basically are a shoggoth...so damn cool!I hope that further levels or DLC's will be made for this, if so, I will snag them.Great game from the point of view from the creature...buy it!

So I didn't get to fetch all the collectables since I was afraid of not being able to find my way back. _childDocuments_.review: Everybody knows the monster movies and games where some scientific facility creates a monster they cannot control. This horrid creature then proceeds to rampage throughout the facility killing the staff one by one. At this point hiding from the monster is less scary, more boring. Except you're not hiding from the monster. You ARE the monster. You play as a rampaging blob of nightmares made of tendrils and teeth. Whether you're snatching unsuspecting prey into the ventilation ducts, creeping around the armed guards, or going ham on a swarm of drones, this game is fun on a bun with a fresh take on a tired type of horror.

_childDocuments_.review: So short, really listen to everyone saying it.I finished a 100% in 6 hours, although I did end up using a map someone had made towards the end since I kept getting lost.The map is huge, which is great and not so great. The art is amazing, and the soundtrack lives up to it as well.So why do I recommend it? simply put, the theme and flavour are perfect, you really feel like a horrid monster crawling through vents and turning people into meat, the story is great, the combat (while clunky at times) is great.If you're into the genre I can't recommend it enough, serious thing vibes all the way through.If exploring a beautiful world as a disgusting tentacle beast, leaving destruction in your path doesn't tickle your fancy then maybe don't buy it at full price, possibly even at all.I'm hopeful for future content to be released, either through the workshop or by the devs. Another 6 hours of gameplay (without a price increase) would make this an absolute gem.8/10, would love some more but enjoyed what I got, would burrow into a man's skull and make him murder his coworkers again.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't even beaten the game yet, but after <2hrs of play I am so impressed. The creature you play as moves so fluidly, and the controls are intuitive and easy to pick up which makes that movement even better. This game absolutely NAILS the "you are the monster" feeling and it's so damn fun while also piquing your curiosity about the story. There's something so satisfying about coming into a room of armed enemies and figuring out the best way to get rid of them, whether it be sneakily snatching them from a vent or barreling at them like an angry plate of spaghetti and meatballs.Progression is very smooth and well-paced. You unlock new powers over time which both open up more areas and improve your monster's killing toolkit. My only gripe is that occasionally I got a bit lost while trying to find my way around, but overall the game does a solid job of keeping you on track. The puzzles are straightforward so I found little frustration with them.Definitely a 9.5/10 if only because I'm stupid and kept getting lost. Absolutely a fantastic game, and it looks like there's even more to do after you beat the main story because this game has Workshop support. I got it on sale at ~$8 and it was worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion is a short game you can beat in 6 hours 100% it with all the achievements in one run. After beating the game there is no reason to return to the game. There is no new game+ or Harder Difficulty. At times the game is a bit confusing because there is no Overworld map and if there was the game would probably be a 3 hour game. At some points in the game you are given ways to handle enemies as you wish your various abilities but most the time your sticking to the same straight forward combat design. Combat at times can frankly feel like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Getting hit by things you can't really be expected to suddenly deal with and losing your Biomass so you have to go back to some area and refill your biomass. Its annoying to run back to areas to get rid of you biomass so you can use lower level abilities, to run back again to grab that Biomass so you can use your higher level abilities.I do think at 20 dollars for 4 to 6 hours of entertainment this game is just fine. That's really no different than going to a movie for 2 hours of entertainment. Sometimes a game doesn't need to be long to tell a simple story and that's what the story and gameplay of this game is. Simple.

_childDocuments_.review: The day shift is almost over. Just need to check over a few samples of tissue found on some distant planets, and it's home sweet home. A sound resonates in the lab. A few footsteps, a colleague must be opening the containment door soon. The night shift doesn't begin this early usually, but in this cursed facility, one can appreciate leaving early. Last sample has been thoroughly analyzed. A final, abrupt footstep. Only thing is, it comes from the vent right above the biochemist. Now you can decide what to do with the poor human you masterfully caught by surprise, as you leave the vent with a monstrous roar. Will you hurl him to the other side of the room with your herculean tentacles, or maybe take possession of his feeble mind to make him open the secured doors for you? It matters little, for in the end you will doubtlessly consume him and gain more biomass. Biomass is awesome. Sounds cool? Well this game is quite wonderful in that respect. You play the formless, mindless (or is it?) entity that devours and consumes its way through a secured facility full of fearful scientists, desperate guards and armed drones. You use the ventilation, the sewers and even your captors's technology against themselves. The Good:-The concept: You are the final boss, everybody else is fair game-The Gameplay: the monster moves very smoothly, the controls are great;-The combat: easily the best side of the game, it's just very satisfying to send soldiers flying in the air as you lay waste to an entire room of armed guards that are most certainly not paid well enough to mess with you. As you unlock many gruesome abilities, combats become playgrounds where you can decide how best to destroy everyone in your way: parasites, surprise attacks, projectiles, or just plain old brute force. I found myself purposefully failing puzzles that are meant to make some fights easier, just to have more with ennemies to utterly destroy. -The Art: great looking, with the monster in particular being as awesome as it is disgusting-Soundtrack: instantly makes you feel like the ultimate predator, or sometimes the prey when guards and armed drones are around. Reminds me a lot of the Zerg's theme in Starcraft 1. The Bad:-Scenario: error 404, not found. You are a creepy, awesome, all-devouring entity that tries to escape. Humans yummy. The end. Don't get me wrong, I love it, but...well, there it is. -Too easy: the combat can be challenging, but death in combat is *somewhat* rare, and end-game fights are not as hard as they ought to be, particularly considering the powerful abilities you get late game. The monster is powerful (which is great), but a difficult setting that adds many more enemies would have been welcome. -Can get tiresome: here I am especially thinking of the fact you are essentially creeping around a huge labyrinth: it can plain boring when you need to remember where to go (read: luck into going the right way eventually). Puzzles can be entertaining and satisfying to solve, but they are not the best side of the game. -The special bonuses you can unlock optionally by thoroughly exploring the map come very late, since you need all the late game abilities to unlock them, and therefore there is barely 1 or 2 fights left (if any) when you are at your full potential.-NO BOSS. NO BIG END FIGHT. Where is the fully armored and motorized infantry division that should be trying to keep us from leaving this bloody facility and maybe reaching civilization? Or the big exterminator mech? They're probably hanging out with the lore, somewhere. Overall, great game for its price, very original, I loved every second of the combat and the few lore pieces we got, and I really hope there will be a sequel. 4/5!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall amazing game. The graphics were wonderful, the level design was great, the combat was amazing, the progression felt balanced, the music created a great mood, and I absolutely loved the movement. The only thing I didn't like was the fact there was no map. Most of the time the directions you went were logical and liner, which worked well. _childDocuments_.name: CARRION

_childDocuments_.review: At first this game seemed like fun, I was enjoying running around and solving the puzzles and eating people with this weird tentacle monster but as the game went on it started to drag more and more. The puzzles became less enjoyable, the combat was less about ambushing your prey and more about just slapping them with your big, meaty, red body until they stopped squirming and don't get me started on trying to control the monster in the later stages of the game. You've accumulated so much bio-mass that it's a nightmare to try and pilot this meat sack through the narrow corners with how big you are. I'd recommend getting this on sale because it's not the $20 price tag for three hours of game time.

As you're finding your way through the lab, you encounter many enemies - a lot of them have guns and weapons that differ from one another - you fight them off or avoid them. Strategy is also important as you have to figure out where to go, remember different paths, strategies how you're gonna defeat the enemies, robots and survive deadly traps.To sum it up - i had a lot of fun playing it and would definitely recommend it to others!

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend, but definitely wait for it to go on sale. Watching the credits roll, though,  I couldn't help but feel like there was a lot missing. _childDocuments_.review: It's gross, it's violent, and it's reprehensibly vile.10/10, would absolutely recommend.Though i do have to say that even with fanmade workshop maps, my experience with this game was disappointingly short. _childDocuments_.review: CARRION made a lot of noise with its gameplay reveal. A “reverse horror-themed game” where you play as a monster sounded novel. Except for that Paradise Lost: First Contact game that has been Kickstarted years ago and hasn’t come out yet which had a very similar look and premise, if not the exact same gameplay. Either way, it looked curious, but not that exciting to me so I was planning to wait for the other people’s reactions before deciding on if I want to try it out myself. Now that it has come out and had lots of positive reviews, I decided to take the plunge. And yeah, my assumptions were spot on. It’s curious and fun, but not that exciting.The basic idea for this game is like this – you’re controlling a strange biomass of mouths and tentacles that has escaped containment in a research facility. It can eat, it can grow (with metroidvania-ish upgrades you find along the way), it can do object manipulation and it can move freely vertically and horizontally in all locations, as long as your way isn’t blocked by something you can’t move. As such, it works as somewhat of a metroidvania-ish mix of action, adventure/puzzle-solving but without any real “platforming”. The world is divided into levels connected by an overworld where you get from one location to the other. And each level, except for the first one, has a hidden collectible upgrade that provides you with some additional beneficial effect. Though they are usually hidden behind challenges that test your mastery of special abilities. And said special abilities are found in each level, so each time you get new obstacles and new ways to overcome them.And most of the way it works really well. It’s fun, if often simple, it’s disguising in an entertaining 80s horror way and it’s well paced for the most part. The last separate level of the game was at times infuriating with how badly thought out the camera and randomness of things could kill you, but up until that point the game was really solid, and after that it’s a smooth sailing until the ending. Few sections where you can control humans have surprisingly poor controls, especially when using ladders, controlling the mass at its biggest can sometimes be finicky. But other than that, the only big potential issue the game has is the lack of a map. Even if you don’t backtrack for unlockables, you can easily get lost in these levels. I know I did, and I’m usually very good of remembering level layouts in these exploration-focused games. But if you start exploring and backtracking, expect to constantly go wrong directions, which often are one-way as well.Is CARRION nice? Yeah. I enjoyed it as an overall nice experience. Did it excite me or made me want to ever play it again? Not really. I can recommend checking it out if what you see in the trailers and the demo is appealing to you, but don’t expect anything more out of the game. It’s just a nice game. And maybe that can be enough.

_childDocuments_.review: For every thousand games that you play as a regular humanoid character, there's one that lets you play as something different, and blessed are the devs who take that less traveled path. What we have here is a game that tests two questions:Can it be fun to play as an amorphous tentacle monster in a 2D side scrolling environment? Yes.Is it fun for the creature to spend most of its time wandering around a narrow twisty maze looking for levers and switches to open locked doors? NoPlayed through it on Gamepass, just fyi.Here's a comment that's not at all relevant to Carrion.The last non-humanoid game that I found, Maneater, taught us that it's fun to swim around as a shark, but it's not fun to do 50% of your "maneating" while flopping around fruitlessly on land. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR:It breaks my heart to give this game a negative review, because I love it.  I love everything about it...  Except the price point, length and lack of replayability.  If the pricepoint drops or they add more content, I will happily change this review to positive.IMO the concept and gameplay are fantastic, and you will have some epic reverse-horror moments.  But this game was $20, I only got 6 hours out of it, and I really took my time.   If I hadn't searched and explored every inch, it would've taken far less.  Once you reach 100%, that's it.  There is no harder difficulty.  There are no randomly generated levels or endless mode.  There's no reason to play it again, other than to relive the same experiences you had an hour ago.   Maybe asking for more is unreasonable  Games of this quality take a lot of resources to produce.  Maybe in the middle of a pandemic, when everyone's money is tight, I just expect more from luxury items like video games.  BOTTOM LINE:I like to get 1 hour of entertainment per dollar i spend on videogames.  Often times I think $2+/hour is reasonable if it's a unique concept.  For any gamer, CARRION will almost certainly miss that  mark.  If money isn't an issue and you want to have a blast for a few hours, then I recommend this game.  Otherwise, wait for it to go on sale or for the devs to release more content.TO THE DEVS:  You've proven you know how to make a great game.  Please make more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I was incredibly hyped for Carrion the moment I saw the first trailer, I had very high expectations for it, if you've never heard of it before you might have a better time with this game than me.This game does many things very well, the spritework is very enjoyable to look at, controlling the monster feels great and is exactly the kind of power-fantasy I was hoping for, the sound design is exceptional and helps tie the whole experience together, its main mechanics, although not revolutionary in any way, are extremely polished for an indie title.My main gripe with Carrion is that it is simply too short for its pricetag and has next to no replayability value, I was able to 100% the game in just 5 hours (and I'm a very slow player). Another problem I have with the game is that the gameplay doesn't really go anywhere (you do gain new abilities as you progress but they are rarely used to solve puzzles in interesting ways and mostly serve to unlock paths to new areas of the game) which is a shame. It also doesn't help that most side content leads to upgrades that just give you more health or energy and don't really change the gameplay whatsoever.TL;DR game lacks content and doesn't take its core concepts far enough, buy it on sale or don't buy it

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game, above all, so it's hard to not give it a passing grade, whatever else you think.Reverse horror is always such a power-trip, and they didn't disappoint in this front. The movement of the monster is almost hypnotizing, the pixel art is always appreciated when done properly, and the drops of blood that spread everywhere as you move stay there for a surprisingly long time.Story is unexpectedly deep, but you sort of have to read between the lines and find the extra material by yourself, do your due diligence, so to speak. I liked the open-ending all the same.What really sets this apart from other games is the incredible support for mod that is built into the game so others can actually add challenges and levels, elevating the game a tier or two just for the replay value and creative outlet it can become. _childDocuments_.review: "Carrion" is a reverse-horror game developed by Phobia Game Studio and released in 2020.Gameplay: The gameplay of "Carrion" puts the player in the role of a monstrous creature who must escape from a research facility and wreak havoc on the humans within. The game features a unique movement system that allows the player to slither, crawl, and squeeze through tight spaces, as well as a variety of abilities such as tentacle attacks and the ability to mimic objects. The game is fast-paced and action-packed, with satisfying combat and challenging puzzles. However, some players may find the game's lack of variety in gameplay and short length disappointing.Story: The game's story is minimalistic, with no dialogue or cutscenes, but the player can piece together the events of the story through the environment and encounters with NPCs. The game's atmosphere is eerie and unsettling, with a sense of isolation and desperation.Graphics and Sound: "Carrion" features impressive pixel art graphics, with detailed environments and gruesome creature designs. The sound design is also effective, with atmospheric sound effects and a haunting soundtrack that adds to the game's horror elements.Replayability: The game offers some replayability, with the ability to replay levels and unlock additional abilities. However, the lack of variety in gameplay and short length may limit replayability for some players.Criticism: "Carrion" has been criticized for its lack of variety in gameplay and short length, which may not provide enough content for some players. The game's minimalist storytelling may also be disappointing for some players who prefer a more narrative-driven experience.Overall, "Carrion" is an excellent game that offers a unique and engaging experience for fans of the horror and action genres. The game's impressive graphics, effective sound design, and fast-paced gameplay make it a must-play for those looking for a different take on the horror genre. While its lack of variety in gameplay and short length may be disappointing for some players, its satisfying combat and challenging puzzles make it worth checking out for anyone who enjoys a good horror game.

_childDocuments_.review: Be advised. This is not really a game where you cause horror and hunt humans. This is primarily a puzzle game where you use your various abilities to get through series of switches, levers, doors, and one-way paths.Eating humans is, well, optional. It awards you nothing (except for hit points but so does every checkpoint anyway). Wrecking chaos and killing humans is fun for like five minutes at the beginning (and each time you unlock a new offensive ability) but then it simply gets mundane. Eating a human requires consuming several bodyparts individually; it's slow, clunky, and ultimately useless. There's also combat in this game but honestly every time it happened I wish it didn't. It wastes your time, it robs away the feeling of being an unstoppable horror entity, and it's just not fun to engage in due to the funky controls.So what's left is a linear puzzle game. And the puzzles themselves are alright. However, for 100% achievements, towards the end of the game you need to do a ton of backtracking to collect some extra upgrades which are now entirely useless because every puzzle is already solved and every enemy is already defeated. The mind-blowing lack of an in-game map coupled with the fact that every area is indistinguishable from another makes this stupidly tedious. Not that there's any incentive to do it in the first place since you gain nothing from it anyway - no final form, no alternate ending, nothing. There is also zero replayability to be found; beat the game once and uninstall it.Finally, the game starts out fairly interesting and quickly sets up a backstory that keeps you hooked up. However, without any spoilers the backstory subsequently falls flat and the game ending is extremely disappointing. Just save your money and watch a walkthrough on youtube, it'll be the same experience but less annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: Carrion is genuinely one of my favorite games. You play as a mass of flesh and teeth, getting upgrades as you progress through the game.The movements are fluent and look good, the game is fun to maneuver around and you can grab people and bash them against the ceilings and floors just for fun.I enjoyed being able to either do sneak attacks or ambush people, or even both. The enemies began to get a bit harder to deal with each time. Going from people, to people with guns, to people with suits and guns, to drones, to people in suits with flamethrowers and then to mech-type suits. There were also a few other things that you had to go through, like turrets and things that stick bombs to you.I however had two problems with it:1. I had no idea what I was supposed to do next or where to go most of the time. There were multiple occasions where I finished a level or a room, and then just got lost. You either have to wander around aimlessly or memorize the map. I looked at playthroughs but I could never find where I was in the game. I would like something that tells you what to do, or just some sort of mini-map so you don't get lost.2. The puzzles are a bit annoying, as you often have to go back and deposit biomass, and then go back for it once the puzzle is over. My main problem is that normally you have to go a room or two back to find the biomass pool.Honestly, despite my problems, this is a great reverse horror game and I highly recommend it.The game is fun, the idea is cool, eating and destroying things is just fun in general, the art design looks good, its a bit difficult which is usually good, and I wish there were at least a few more rooms and/or another level in the game, or that there was another game similar to this.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent reverse horror game with puzzle elements! Worth it at full price if you like what you see. Relatively short but sweet and high quality.+Play a monster and eat people! Smash their bodies around for gore and fun!+I liked the puzzle elements. As your mass gets bigger, up to 3 levels, your abilities change. There are special pools to remove your biomass for access to earlier abilities to solve puzzles.+Variety of ways to kill your enemies. My favorite being Parasitism where you can control humans.+Containment units are a nice collectible that give you bonuses: fire resistance, more energy, and more prehensile tentacles.+Steady progression of abilities helps mask the repetitiveness.+Very well polished with no real bugs or glitches except some very minor physics based ones.-This game desperately needed a map. Players will stalk and consume those that have imprisoned it to spread fear and panic throughout the facility. name: Bright Memory
detailed_description: Bright Memory is a lightning-fast fusion of the FPS and action genres, created by one-man development studio FYQD using Unreal Engine. Combine a wide variety of skills and abilities to unleash dazzling combo attacks. SRO (Supernatural Science Research Organization) agent Shelia's adventure is about to begin. This game depicts the maiden adventure of a woman named Shelia in the year 2020. The 1000-year-old relic swords known as 'Kanshou and Bakuya', discovered through SRO research, have been found to comprise a unique multilayered structure, containing a mysterious substance in their cores. This substance, known as the 'Soul of Jiu Xuan', possesses the ability to reanimate the dead. In an attempt to take possession of the substance, the 'SAI' - a massive terrorist organization controlling its own army - has used a cutting-edge piece of technology known as a 'Quantum Transporter' to infiltrate the SRO research facility and steal top-secret and incredibly dangerous data. To make matters worse, while attempting to calibrate coordinates on the Quantum Transporter, Shelia mistakenly activates the device, immediately transporting everyone in the vicinity to the Floating Island - an airborne continent near the North Pole, undisturbed in its slumber for over 1000 years. It is soon discovered that the various beasts and corpses of those who once populated the island have been reanimated by the 'Soul of Jiu Xuan', and they're coming for Shelia... Game Features Rack up points and enhance your various skills to freely create your own original combinations Employing an FPS-style POV, discover and solve the various puzzles throughout each stage to advance A mesmerizingly beautiful world combining science fiction and Chinese culture and created using Unreal Engine 4 Main Characters Shelia: Hannah Grace The female main character. 21 years old. Her parents were in the military. After losing both parents in a sudden tragic accident at the age of six, she was raised by Professor Richard Carter, founder of the SRO. Having spent years undergoing various types of military training and shining among her peers in virtually every field, her near-superhuman abilities landed her a spot as a member of the ultra-elite 'SRO Emergency Inspection Team'. Carter: Jack Merluzzi Founder of the SAI. Male, 35 years old. Taking advantage of his influential status, he struck it rich by buying and selling vast numbers of ancient artifacts on the black market. After learning of the existence of the 'Soul of Jiu Xuan', he immediately infiltrated the SRO in an attempt to steal top-secret data.

_childDocuments_.review: In my infinite course to boredom today, I visited a imageboard as I do most days, with the most fierce intent to procrastinate, but something really did caught my eye. I saw this one webm clip on of an fast indie shooter game, by accident, wouldn’t have pressed play on a normal day. It had a couple of replies, and I decided to read along because it caught my interest.This looks like a decently budgeted game by Electronic Arts, it plays like Titanfall, DOOM and Revengeance with a style point system à la Devil May Cry. It’s the most impressive indie game I’ve played for the last months and it’s definitely a fun experience. The game was produced solo by someone, doing it part-time of all things, which tugged at my heart as a wannabe video game developer with severe autism, who immediately reached for my credit card to support the dude and buy it through Steam.The game looks good, like, really good, running on Unreal Engine and with good looking characters rocking some average facial expressions. As mentioned before, it’s a game that could put some renown studios to shame, simply before the fact that it was a professional production.The gameplay is VERY fun, your character deals damage with both a small range of firearms and some sort of energy blade, complemented with various unlockable abilities. Together you can combo all these to fill up your combat score meter like in the Devil May Cry franchise. Combat is always fluid, you dodge sideways and backwards to move during fights, and can even pull yourself to enemies, even freeze them in time or knock them up to unleash a flurry of slashes.The level design looks nice and has some platforming, that didn’t particularly feel the most brilliant aspect of my first run, the ‘grapple hook’ mechanic isn’t particularly well defined, only being available from specific spots, and not on specific spots. There’s some puzzle solving and collectibles, that don’t seem to be missing from ANY video game nowadays, overall the combat parts really shine through during the episode, starting with a decent premise for a shooter story that ends on a good cliffhanger that looks promising.In conclusion, this Early Access game is ‘the treat’ that I was expecting from Early Access games for quite a while - a great ambitious project that is pulling all the stops. I’d recommend this game to anyone who enjoys shooters. It’s a project worth supporting, in hopes that it becomes a great, full-game for more people to experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory is a very fun and short game. The game is definitely unfinished and is lacking in the variety department but when it comes down to gameplay, that's where it excels. The game is like a cross between the call of duty and devil may cry. The animations of the guns are amazing and the same with the gameplay overall. The one thing that I do have to say is the way the game doesn't give you the ability to change your controls but that can be passed by due to it being in early access. The game offers you about a 45-minute long story that isn't really all the compelling. It throws you into this world. You are given very little explanation of what's going on and what's happening. On top of that, some of the cutscenes aren't the greatest looking. One notable scene is when a grenade is thrown at our character towards the end of the game and the main character just kind rag dolls to the floor. But other than the very weak story this game is very good. Here are some pros and cons that need to be statedPros:-Beautiful game-Amazing gunplay-Very Smooth combat -Interesting Designs-Cheap-When the full game is released you get it for freeCons: -Very Short-Unskippable cut scenes -Wacky animations in cut scenesOverall, the price of the game and the enjoyment factor of it makes it worth buying.

_childDocuments_.review: Neat idea though you can tell its an indie game for sure. Combat is pretty fast paced, has all of your traditional mechanics like double jumping and air dashing. The abilities seemed unique for the most part and the game looks pretty. That being said There is little explanation as to what is going on story wise. From what I can gather the main character is basically lara croft but with powers. The voice acting is decent though the dialog itself kinda made me cringe, plus it didn't help in some cut scenes you could tell that it was dubbed over poorly. Also the cursor speed when using a gamepad is obnoxiously slow. The other two big gripes i have with the game is to ADS you don't hold the button like in traditional shooters, you click it once and you stay ADS until you either click it again or have to reload, some people might be ok with that but me personally it just felt wrong and kinda annoyed me when i would try to switch enemies after killing someone and id just kinda slowly pan over. The other thing is that there is a part towards the middle of the game(demo?) where you find a literal darksouls bonfire to light, it even uses the same font when the "Bonfire lit" message pops up. Not sure if this was meant to be some kind of easter egg or if bonfires play a part to the game but if I was the developer I'd change that up, not sure how stingy fromsoftware is but I would hate to get a letter from their lawyers telling me to shut down the game or something.Overall you're basically paying 10 bucks to play a demo with the hopes of a full game somewhere in the future. Its not going to win game of the year in its current state but its a cool little hour thing and damn impressive of someone who made the game on their own.

_childDocuments_.review: Littering the ground with bullet casings and the corpses of your enemies rarely feels this good. Bright Memory is one of those titles that does exactly what its name says and remains a bright memory not soon to be forgotten. As a first person shooter, this game wildly succeeds producing a fantastic gameplay experience that left me only wanting more and more.From guns to blades to energy, you have quite the arsenal of weapons and techniques to obliterate your foes in a very stylish manner with, which works out spectacularly with the combo system that's so wonderfully implemented. Rarely, do I ever see combo systems of the likes of character action titles built into first person shooters, but my goodness does it work here. Busting caps up to an SSS rank is so satisfying.Stylish outcome is not only the effect of a wonderful combat system, but the game is absolutely gorgeous. It really does help with getting sucked into the hectic chaos that is combat in Bright Memory when it looks this great. Sparks, water, blood and metal all come together in a mesh of fantastically rendered bliss that will woe any mayhem junky.I feel that this is a great title for just about anyone. The complexity of the combat is really something to with and enjoy, so despite this game not being super long, it is still something you could come back to time and time again and still enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure if I just got a completely different game to what most of the other reviews are saying, but the game I got was.... bad.This game is.... all over the place. It feels like walking through the fever dream of someone who's dreaming about Call of Duty, Dark Souls, Uncharted, and Halo all at once, while also tripping on acid. You're thrown into the game with no explanation, no story, and the character just starts making comments on things that happened that the player never saw or experienced. Gameplay wise, it's fun I guess, but story wise it did nothing but confuse and frustrate me with the total lack of answers, complete randomness, and just... really bad pacing.Pros:-Decent gameplay. Guns feel fun and satisfying, abilities are pretty good, movement is about what you'd get from a call of duty or battlefield game.-Decent graphics. The models are good quality, though animation can be rough sometimes.-Decent music/SFX. All of the sound design is pretty good, music goes well with the action and gameplay and feels energetic.-Voicing is okay, dialogue is clear and subtitles are on by default (love it when games do that). A little lacking in the emotions department, but otherwise not bad!Cons:-Pretty much everything else? It starts off like a typical action game might: you're a character who's trying to infiltrate a place for some purpose. You get almost to your purpose, before getting stopped by a bad guy. Things go wrong, you're placed in a new environment for the "real" beginning. But this is where the writing goes from basic to poor. You're dropped into a random place that the MC calls the "floating island in the arctic" even though you're surrounded by greenery and none of the terrain you're on floats. You shoot some wolves and get tossed into a cutscene of a dragon or something, before being attacked by zombies, while the character monologues about something some doctor (who goes unnamed and unexplained) said, and a tablet (also unexplained). You then solve a Lara Croft/Uncharted puzzle which leads you into a cave and get attacked by the special ops forces that were fighting you in the beginning, before you both get ambushed by more zombies and a random rat person who seems to be some kind of leader. You do some more Lara Croft puzzles, shoot a few more zombies, shoot a few more Spec Ops, then touch a weird light and get thrown into a boss fight in a weird pocket dimension where you fight a flame-sword night a la Dark Souls style (dodging attacks and whittling his health away whenever your skills recharge. During this fight, the MC talks about how this must be the lost forest the doctor mentioned (again, both doctor and forest are STILL UNEXPLAINED). You beat the boss and get teleported back into the real world where the cave you're in is now collapsing and exploding (it's rock with no bombs on it, not sure how or why it's suddenly exploding) you then get dumped into ANOTHER boss fight where you have to fight a large number of Spec Ops with little cover. The solve another Lara Croft puzzle and you open a black hole gate way that more zombies come out of, and this is where it got to be too much for me and I had to turn it off out of sheer confusion and frustration at the lack of any cohesion.Oh, I forgot to mention, there's random and awkwardly placed easter eggs, such as random Uncharted-esque treasures you can pick up (they don't appear to give you anything, money or experience) and a very obvious, very forced bonfire you can interact with to get a Dark Souls "Bonfire Lit" screen. All in all, this game is little more than a peek inside the mind of a person who's higher than cloud nine on acid, trying to design a game while watching six other games at the same time. Play at your own risk.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory is a mish mash of different genres. It starts with one and a few minutes later a different genre blends in and a few minutes later another one. This is happening almost continuously until the game’s climax, around 30 minutes in. But is it fun?Yes, it is. This could easily be a train wreck, but somehow most of these genres combined deliver a fun experience, no doubt thanks to the short length. Bright Memory is a first person shooter at heart, and during the game you’ll be shooting almost always, mixing it up with different techniques and skills.The game drops you right into the action, letting you take out a few human enemies. And quickly after that scene it becomes more supernatural, with monsters and animals all getting into the mix. Then comes the first puzzle, and the first collectibles and the game starts to feel a bit like Tomb Raider, but naturally shown in first person view. Eventually it tries a bit of horror, unsuccessfully though, and the game quickly and fortunately drops that aspect. And then it’s back to shooting, hacking and slashing, unleashing powers, finding collectibles, swinging around and puzzle solving. All in a matter of minutes. It’s fascinating and every time you think the whole thing is going to crash and burn, it switches up the gameplay to keep it just fresh enough for just a few minutes more. There’s even a Dark Souls reference in it, something I didn’t see coming at all. And then it ultimately ends, after around 30 minutes.Every now and then some physical obstacles have to be cleared, which can be done by using your skills. Your default skills are an EMP which blasts enemies into the air, in some form of stasis, a blade that has different moves, a grapple hook - for both environments and flinging yourself into enemies – and dodging. You’ll be using these skills a lot. Enemies aren’t dead with just a headshot; it sometimes takes a while before they are defeated. So switching up shooting with skills makes this easier and it stops you from being killed. And yes, you might die, even if it is short. Enemies drop both ammo and experience – not all though – and that experience can be used to level up your character Shelia. These unlockable skills consist of taking less damage, or using new skills like lightning, time freeze or a force field that deals area-of-effect (AOE) damage. It’s a way to keep things more fresh and varied and I appreciated that, especially during my second playthrough where you do the exact same things. It’s nice to be able to use some other skills then. During combat you’ll also be rated. Dealing damage increase the meter with SSS being the best rank. Yes, think Devil May Cry here, but more limited. The meter will decrease once you stop dealing damage and taking damage doesn’t seem to affect this meter at all. Except for showing off I don’t think it does much else or even adds anything to the game really.The world consists of nature, caves and some temple ruins and not much more than that. Despite that limited variety (or plenty, depending on how you look at it) it never gives off the feeling there isn’t enough. There are some open areas, but when you want to explore you’ll walk into invisible walls and fall/jump to your death. It’s a simple way to keep things linear, but it’s also confusing as you’re also supposed to search for collectibles. I fell to my death at least once thinking I could go there when in reality I couldn’t. That’s poor design. Either get rid of the invisible walls, or the collectibles, or just mention that collectibles can be found without going out of your way to find them.At the end of the episode (it’s called an episode) you’ll be rated by deaths, damage and time. It doesn’t add anything except for, again, showing off your skills. After the episode you can play through it again with New Game+. In case it isn’t clear; an episode is the entire game. I didn’t think the enemies were harder the second time, and nothing story-wise seemed to have changed either, but you can use your other skills since you’ll quickly have enough experience to unlock them all. You can even finish the game a third game, but after the second one I had my fill.Also because the second time the game seemed to have more issues, even though it plays out exactly the same. I had an area in the beginning where I couldn’t progress because the fire didn’t go out as it should’ve. Maybe it was a bug or an enemy didn’t spawn or get stuck in the environment, but reloading the checkpoint seemed to fix the issue. And near the end, after defeating the very last boss, the game froze on me for at least 30 seconds, making me thing it had crashed as the game didn’t respond to any of my button presses. Fortunately, it did continue, but I seemed to have been stuck in super slow motion.Graphically the game is pretty, but it looks like a game that was created with free assets. Highly detailed assets, mind you, but assets nevertheless. Despite coming across that way the game does manage to feel like one whole. There’s rarely anything that feels off. The lighting is pretty good, as are the models and textures. The interface is a bit crowded with UI elements circling around the crosshair and multiple icons in the lower left corner. And the menu also feels a bit simplistic, but it gets the job done.I also experienced some heavy framedrops during my two playthroughs. The game runs at a high framerate, but shifts in scenes together with the quick action caused multiple slowdowns. Unnecessary, but fortunately it’s still very, very playable.The voice acting is actually pretty good. I didn’t expect that. Same goes for the sound effects and the music which consists of several genres.Bright Memory is a game that should’ve been a train wreck, but ultimately - because of its short length – is actually quite fun, mixing different kinds of action and game elements together. I think most of us will have seen all the game has to offer after playing through it two times, so I’m not sure if one hour of gameplay is enough for the price you’re paying for it, but if you have the money to spare then yes, I would recommend it. Plus, buying this game also gives you the upcoming and bigger sized sequel, Bright Memory Infinite, for free. That should be a good incentive, at least; if this sounds like your jam.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I had more fun in that 31 min (I paused at one point to talk to family over-the-phone) then I have in a long while. What a cool start to what would make a really great full-game. I hope buying into EA helps them make the full-game I am sure they want to. I would at least say this, if you are the type of person that could play a "mission" over and over again as long as it was fun, then you would get your money's worth out of Bright Memory so far for $5. If you are not that type of person, I might wait for it to go on sale, just because $5 for 30 mins is pretty meh, at least here in the states. But again, wow. If you are neither of those people and just have $5 to spare and you like shooters, I do not believe you will be disappointed by Bright Memory for several reasons.The biggest reason is that it feels like Asian Doom with Dark Souls enemy design, and I say that in the best of ways. The soundtrack rocks, and kicks in just as combat does. The combat itself is basically neo Doom (adrenaline-fueled speed, crisp gunplay, blood splatter, etc.), but with added powers/skills that are just plain cool. In my short time I was able to get enough XP to test out the Lightning ability which was crisp and required charging (something that you will see requires a bit of timing and strategy because of how fast paced combat is), among a few others that were also very cool. To be honest, I am seeing some things in this game that I don't think I have ever seen before, which you will just have to experience to understand, but overall I would buy a game that was 30-40 hrs of just this, if that makes sense. It was just that fun, even considering:- The terrible subtitles work (which, I get it, it's not the native language of the development team, so no biggie); and- The pseudo-anime styled characters (not sure how to describe it, but I would have just went with realism instead).  The main character is the best example of this - she is gorgeously modeled, but the art-style just looks out of place.P.S. that Dark Souls nod was awesome. I wish the best for the developers of this game, whether the full version sees the light of day or not. This half-hour was definitely a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory is a neat FPS mixed with button-mapped abilities and light hack n slash. Think of a mix of Overwatch's hero abilities, Devil May Cry's hack n slash combo system, and top it off with solid shooting gameplay. You play as a cute Chinese waifu named Shelia and you start with a pistol, shotgun and assault rifle. You are also outfitted with some abilities such as the EMP blast which sends enemies into the air, and can obtain EXP to unlock new skills and abilities. Additionally, you have a sword which fires laser slashes with each swing.Negatives out of the way first. The major downside is that it feels like a demo. For the price, Bright Memory is also painfully short (finished a run in under an hour). HOWEVER you will be given Bright Memory Infinite once it releases which looks incredible. It also lacks any semblance of a story as you are immediately thrust into the action with next to no explanation or backstory. Presentation is very solid in both visual and sound aspects. You encounter futuristic soldiers and Chinese mythological creatures and monsters, and even engage in some neat (but spongy) boss battles. Gameplay and combat feels amazing as you dodge and weave, while firing off bullets and abilities at an unrelenting speed.Oh, and did I mention this was made by pretty much one chad?Overall, 6 skirt physics out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Bright Memory

_childDocuments_.review: It is kind of like a weird unholy matrimony of Bioshock, Tomb Raider, and Metal Gear Solid -- Metal Gear Solid for the sharp gunplay, Tomb Raider for the ancient scenery & light puzzling, and Bioshock for the immersive-sim-esque powers. As aforementioned, its a strange amalgamation of a game, but it surprisingly works. Unfortunately, Bright Memory is really just a tech-demo, regardless of what other reviews may have you inclined to believe. I beat this game in a little over thirty minutes. It was fun & got me interested in Bright Memory: Infinite (the sequel game). But, I am definitely going to refund it. Perhaps, I will buy Infinite to get a thorough experience. Leaving a positive review because my experiences were positive with the game. But, would definitely caution against purchasing this game in particular over its successor.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, good effort for a one-man job; I wouldn't recommend this game to my friends though, since it is still early and needs work. recommending this game at the current state would be irresponsible, in my opinion. Now, the game itself is not terrible, albeit with some weird and bad design decisions; I will point out a few that stands out to me. - The beginning sequence doesn't make a lot of sense to me; the line about the twin is vague, and without logic. In what circumstance would they need to sacrifice one of their own?  - The  in the middle of the game is very out of place. It is an obvious reference to the  , but without any meaning or utility. If this was meant to be an Easter egg, then I would say it is way too obvious; if it will be designed as a game mechanic further along the development, I would strongly suggest a different model and activation effect, because as of now it is presented as an obvious knock off. (I mean, the text and the sound effect is nearly identical) - The bosses have telegraphic moves that mirrors somewhat of a souls-like game, but the character weapons and skills are more fitting to a combo-action genre.  Overall, I would say that if this game is intended to be a souls-like game, then it is not working out so far. It works ok with a combo-action tag, though. - Character animation needs refining. (Expected for early access) - Character dialog is due to improvements. It feels to me that the developer is not a native English speaker, or at least the original script isn't written in English. Some sentences and name tags feels like harsh translation from a translator software.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game all the way through, and all I can say is...It's okay. For a game developed by one man, it's pretty polished.The animations are okay, but could use some work. The weight painting on the waist and torso creates a really noticeable crease that does not look very good. The rest of the body looks fine. The eyes could use a little bit of work as well, just a few little eye twitches could help a lot.Some of the spaces that you are given to fight in are a little bit too small, and the movement speed feels far too slow.The HUD looks great. I love how the HUD is located entirely in the center of the screen, aside from the things in the bottom left, which are less important. Native Ultra Widescreen support is very welcome.The music was kinda forgettable, but enjoyable to listen to. To be fair, though, I don't expect one man to be able to compose the absolute best music.This game is very promising. I'm looking forward to the full release. In this current state, I would probably recommend it if it were a much lower price, but with the full release promised for free with a purchase of this demo, I would definitely recommend purchasing this game if you have money to spare. Plus, there are plenty of "good" camera angles to go along with the female protagonist.

_childDocuments_.review: The main selling point of this demo is the fast paced, hack 'n slash combat. However, it's very janky and takes some getting used to before you can really accomplish something besides holding S and shooting whatever is in front of you.Once you finally get used to it, it starts to get fun, but you still can't shake the feeling of jank. It looks nice on video, but doesn't play as well as you'd think. I hope Bright Memory: Infinite is more polished, because this wouldn't be fun if it was a full length game.Story is there, it's confusing, and you don't need to care about it. Game design is nice overall, but some boss battles have unavoidable environmental hazards that damage you. Not anything too infuriating, but it's worth looking out for if that kind of thing squicks you.All in all, it's a solid, short, fast-paced experience for a cheap price. Worth getting if you're alright with janky-but-fun combat, although I'd recommend getting a game like Doom Eternal if you want something more polished.

_childDocuments_.review: You probably want to read up on the history of the Bright Memory games to really understand what they are and what happened with it. Ultimately, Bright Memory is an extremely short first person shooter crossed a bit with a spectacle brawler built near exclusively by a single Chinese developer. It feels like a demo for a longer game and only features a single episode, meaning follow up episodes were never released. Seeing the game was originally a dream come true to me, combining two of my favorite genres into a glorious spectacle of shooting with modern guns, slashing and causing explosions, dashing, and having your performance scored like a Devil May Cry or Bayonetta game. There's a few platforming segements, a single puzzle, miniboss fights, and boss fights, but a decent run can be finished in less than 25 minutes.Warning: Keys ARE NOT rebindable, so you will probably need a third party tool like JoyToKey to change your input. Hope you enjoy 'C" to crouch instead of Left Ctrl. Also, once in a reload animation, you can't change weapons which is a huge oversight for this kind of game in my opinion.Bright Memory at feels somewhat fitting due to it's low price of $3, but a shattering disappointment of what could have been. The "sequel" is a separate game with more to it, but also a very short game taking generally no more than two hours to complete and not really having any mode or content worthy of calling it Bright Memory Infinite, especially at $20.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory is a fast-paced action FPS game created and developed by just one man (yes you read it right, just one single man) yet it's quality is almost of a triple-A tittle. There are a few things that need/should improve: - skills tree: perhaps more varieties for different play-styles not just the basic ones. - bugs/glitches: just a few but not game-breaking at all. - combat: make it easier to jump and shoot/use skills mid-air. - bosses: 1st one you basically just run around and shoot it because you are in such a huge space where as the 2nd (also last) one is such a small one so you just literally tank it. and bosses are quite bullet sponges too.Over all it's a great demo, i definitely had a lot of fun playing through it 3 times and highly RECOMMENDED you to give it a shot. _childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet. As a proof of concept from a small team this game rules. It lacks polish here and there and the grapple mechanic is a little finicky but the gun play is solid, the abilities are satisfying to use and the fast movement, including a generous dodge, make combat a blast. With two and a half boss fights, around 10 regular enemy types and a hand full of collectibles spread over essentially one long level a run of this game will take you a little under an hour but if you want to unlock all the abilities you generally will need a second run and likely a third to really give them all a proper spin. (abilities carry over, sadly actual xp doesn't so remember to spend your xp after the final boss before ending the run)all in all you can see most of the games content in under 2 hours, and all of it in something around 3 although as of writing this that's just a guesstimation. I'd still argue the game is worth getting on it's own merit, add to that that buying the game nets you the currently under development sequel and it's a hell of a deal.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory is sort of a demo of Bright Memory: Infinite. This is not a full game, it's a short preview of around 30-40 minutes, to give the player an idea of what the full game is about, and how the game feels. And oh man, did that guy impress me. Because yeah, this game was made by a SINGLE person.I was actually blown away by this game. The graphics in the background of the main menu looked amazing and I thought: no way I'm getting decent FPS with this. I set every graphical option to the highest possible, and to my surprise, I got over 100 FPS with my GeForce 960, and I simply couldn't believe what I saw.The game starts off in a... strange way. It begins in an elevator with Shelia, the protagonist, running to cover as she is being shot. Not knowing why you're there or why bad guys are shooting you, you are able to shoot back with your pistol. Still a little overwhelmed by the graphics and the surprisingly smooth FPS I got, I satisfyingly defeated the bad guys. You enter a room and start hacking a computer when Carter shows up. I assume he is the main villain in the game, but I'm not sure though. He stops you and things get weird. Suddenly everyone in the room gets sucked up by something, and puts you outside. You see a beam of light in the distance that you need to investigate. Once again: you don't know why, or what, but you want to know.I had a blast with the 40 minutes I've played. What I just summed up are the first 2-3 minutes of this game. It seems like a pretty standard FPS game, but it's not. When I got outside, I was picking up collectibles, shooting up a lion/wolf-creature, fighting off demons that came out of nowhere, spotting a dragon in the sky, grappling over a cliff, and solving a puzzle which let me enter a largely detailed tomb.This game makes you want to know more about it's story, and that's great. It contains a nice mix of shooting up enemies, solving puzzles and giving the player a beautiful world to explore. The game sounds great too, weapons sound powerful and the music is really fitting.For me personally, it did have too many things just SUDDENLY happening. For example, you examine a certain thing, the screen goes white and you're in a whole different place having to fight a boss. On the other hand, it made me wonder how I got there, because it was still kind of interesting. It could have given me more information on the story though, things were a bit confusing at times. One last thing, the Lip-Sync is way off, but maybe that's because the game originally is Chinese? Not too sure on that one.Long story short; this game seems to have it all. I didn't even mention the superpowers Shelia has, like her EMP-Blast or her Light Blade, which is amazingly satisfying to use.It takes place on a floating island(s) above the Arctic, which is a very unique setting in my opinion.On top of all that, if you buy this game, you will get Bright Memory: Infinite for free when it launches, and I'm excited for that! Oh yeah, did I mention this game was made by 1 single person?!?! Oh I did? Sorry...8,7 / 10 would smash a boss through a wall again.

Framerate goes from 80+ to under 5 in specific areas (I assumed it was loading at first, but then I ran into a snake that, each time it bited me, the framerate would drop sharply for a few seconds, so I can only deduce that its poor optimization or spaghetti code or whatever). Empty the entire clip in a fraction of a second). One of the bosses just teleport next to you to attack, or has a pretty uneven hitbox scan where it can hit you with a sword from across the room. But anyway...This is an indie title, made by one person alone, and I respect that a lot. Unfortunately this still needs work in order to a stable experience.
