_childDocuments_.review: Ok, So here is my honest, unfiltered first impression/review.This game has something there. The action/fps fusion is a marriage made in heaven and is super fun to play. Yet this game left me extremely frustrated. Usually frustration is bad, but this frustration is good. I WANT MORE. I received about 35 minutes of gameplay, maybe less from this game. Maybe I missed something in the product description, but I was expecting a full game, considering it left early access. Instead, what I got was effectively a demo. That said, the graphical fidelity of this game is astounding. I play on a mid-range computer, rocking a Ryzen 5 2600x and a GTX 1060 6gb graphics card, and on all high settings, I was pulling a consistent 60 frames, all the while the visuals are stunning. The level of detail in the models and weapons truly impressed me, as I take modelling and texturing classes as a part of my Game Design program. On to criticisms. Game is super fast paced. In everything. You're sort of just thrown right into the action, no real time to sort of introduce yourself to the game, controls and mechanics. There's a tutorial, but its barebones. Aside from the combat encounters, which are your only times to really experiment and get a feel for the game, the rest of the game feels like you've been put on rails, which is fine if this game is to be a linear experience. The character rigging and animation needs work, specifically facial features. I noticed that characters that had a face didnt really emote well, and animations felt like shortcuts were taken in the interest of expedience. As this game develops, the animations could do well with either mo-cap or more detailed movement, both general and fine.Weapon handling was nice, if not a bit squirrelly. Same for the controls. During combat situations, or after a cutscene/QTE I noticed controls would act up a bit, causing skills I didnt want to activate just then to fire off. Voice acting is mediocre. I dont quite know how to describe my issue without insulting the voice actors and actresses, which isnt my intention, but it felt like they rushed their performances and were just line reading, though this might be an issue with how the pacing of this game or first level felt. The quality of the voices also sounded off, as if they were too loud in places they should be quiet, or too quiet in places they should be louder. Overall: I really enjoy this, and want to see more from this developer on this game and future projects, but there are some glaring problems with pacing, content, and some animation and voice things that need to be adjusted. Still recommend this for at least a couple playthroughs, as the gameplay and combat is rather fun, despite other setbacks.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright memory is one of the most promising game released in this year. I am really impressed by using shift plus direction for quick dodge. + Nice graphics. Heard it supports raytracing (not sure it is now or in the future since I don’t have a RTX video card)- Camera is too shaky.- Optimization is not good.- Glitches. When I fought the final boss, the rating system didn’t work, and it also happened a few times before. Also, freezing power could not freeze enemies sometimes.- The game is too short. This early access version is only about an hour and more like a demo. Little advice to the dev:UI looks a bit messy and font is a little odd in my opinion.Make a better tutorial. Even I beat the game once I still didn’t figure out how to use light blade properly.Work hard on the plot and story telling as well as the line. I really don’t understand what the story is beside the protagonist was sucked into another planet, and some lines are kind of strange.The biggest flaw is the game is too short, and I think the full game will only be five to six hours top. Yet I do recommend this game since it is such a good shooter and the dev promised owners will get the full version for free once it is released. Ps. _childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory (BM in short) developed FYQD-Studio and published by FYQD-Studio, PLAYISM. BM is released on 26 March 2020 for the PC version. As of this writing, there is no feedback on Metacritic (  ).The news of a lone developer who develop this gorgeous FPS was just absurd & mind blowing. Initial images and game footages looks impressive -  shaming AAA game studios. Just nearly? My first impression and my actual experience from the gameplay is totally different. Now that I have seen and felt BM...it's not as bright as many think it is.What is BM about?I have no idea. I launched the game and i put was put through hell and i have no idea what or why am i doing all this for. For me it feels like a big mess up FPS with so many ideas/inspiration taken from other game titles. err. Sticky situation.Controls, Audio, Visuals, Writing:Writing? Let's just leave it out for now. There is no way to confirm this yet.Visuals: Generally, It is visually appealing. One of it's marketing approach/selling point is in its visuals. There are certain things that just looks "fancy" that serves no purpose. or nearly useless. I for one have no idea where my HP bar was or my exp bar. That 6 button and all that numbers were annoyingly huge on my screen. I am not sure why the 6 buttons were designed so big - maybe its to cater to a certain audience. I rather have smaller buttons and have larger FOV and menus with more meaningful explanation and less fancy stuff that serves no purpose. -1Audio: Surprisingly, it is well made. The female voice is clear and sounds real with emotions. Reminds me lara croft@tomb raider. Music changes tempo, monsters noise/weapons & force sounds good. I've no complains on the audio dept. +1 Controls: Awww this is disappointing for me. It uses mouse and keyboard. Just like the fancy visuals, the controls of the combat suffers. Basic changing weapon option is non-existent. You are expected to run around + crowd control + use your force and using numbers 1,2,3 to switch your weapons. Actually in all combat situation, you are multi-tasking like a mindless lara croft who can spew out EMP force (f key) & flying blades (e key),  and super dodge (spam shift key)..its not fun!!! WTF is this?! Are you trying to entangle my fingers?! Nay. No. -1MechanicsThis is my personal impression from this release, i can see & feel inspiration taken from: Dark Souls, Tomb Raider, Dead Space, Devil May Cry (The combo nonsense), Doom/Half Life maybe? as well. Its not wrong to get inspirations from others but how you deliver the final product matters. I feel like i am eating a fragmented fried rice with a mix of spices from everywhere. I no longer know if its sweet/salty. It just doesn't taste well together  it sure looks good.My personal thoughts/My Summary:I really felt excited before launching the game.I really was in shocked during the game.I really am sad now after the game.I don't mean to stereotype <things> but most of the games that I play are developed from western game studios so i am accustomed to the way,controls,feel, the positive & negative from a product as well. I seldom play games developed by asian game studios. When I played BM, it reminded me of the Chinese MMORPG, Chinese RPG games that I onced played long long time ago. The story, the pacing, the clunky control feeling..omg you just brought back all the miserable memories. Yes, its here. It's so here that i know it was developed by a Chinese game studio 300% spot on. and that is why i am so, so sad right now. I don't even have the energy to rampage in hulk review mode. BM was a promising product but i guessed i expected too much from a lone developer. BM doesn't feel solid as compared to other FPS. The major turn off for me was the control and the pacing/story. Don't make me watch useless cutscene every 2 minutes man. it breaks the immersion abruptly. Normal Enemies are okay. From dumb skeletons to some animal wild life. Mini-bosses? and bosses are dull. uninteresting. Made for bullet sponge grade. it's either rounder, bigger, thinner or smaller but they are all sponge grade.My Summary:I no longer expect much of Bright Memory. All the hype. hope. dream. Crushed by dumb sponges, dull uninteresting whack out pacing/story that makes no sense whatever. It's a shallow, pretty but lame product. First time i am using the word LAME here. So no scoring system needed here.If BRIGHT MEMORY: INFINITE is an extension of this lame product, i'll be back with a hulk mode review. by then, nobody will ever live to remember this memory. Not even Sheila.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Bright Memory is a fun game that's a blast from start to end. My friend bought me this game, but if I had bought it myself I would have got a refund. While fun, this game can be completed in less than 1 hour.Bright Memory is a crazy ride where stuff is just happening with no context and no explanation. You're in a lab, you fight some soldiers, a portal opens and you're sucked into it, reappearing on an island floating above the north pole, characters acting like this is normal, talking about other characters you don't know. Then you're fighting wolves. Then you're fighting zombies from Dark Souls, then you see a dragon, then you fight some big monster, then there's a basic puzzle, then there's more soldiers to fight, then you do a Dark Souls boss fight against a knight. You're looking for an artifact. The place is falling down around you. You're teleported around. There's another boss fight against some headless demon called the god of war.All of this happens with no build up, reasoning or explanation for anything happening being given at any point. I assumed some explanation would be given later along the way once the cocaine fuelled first hour was over.And then it ends.At the time it just left Early Access, and at face value looking at the store page you could be fooled into thinking you're getting a complete game, but you're not. Once you finish the second boss you're told to look forward to Bright Memory: Infinite. This game ends with less than 1 hour of gameplay, so what is this game? A paid tech demo? If I had paid the asking price for less than 1 hour of content after being lead to believe I was getting a full game, I would have asked for a refund. There's just not enough here to make it worth it.I'm told that everyone who bought this game will get Bright Memory: Infinite for free, but even if that's true, it doesn't matter. I'm reviewing the game I played, not the game that I might be able to play in the future which I have not played. As it stands now, Bright Memory doesn't have enough content to justify the price.

So basically this is a ducttaped kickstarter in hiding.The gameplay can be described as "Bombastic" with lots of elements inspired by other fps and souls like games, and a literal bonfire lighting process...with the exact same animation and sounds as Dark Souls lol. FPS, Swordplay, its hard to describe, and definitely not worth $10 with the provided content. BUT, if you like what you see, the full version (or next game) is promising to be just that and even more. Do check out the sequel's steam page for more info. _childDocuments_.review: Impressive game for being made by a small team, but it does not appeal to me since there are way too many things going on at the same time. It's just a game of button mashing to dodge enemies from all angles, and then hope that you have some skill to stop time, throw them into the air and similar. Why are there even guns in this game? They feel useless.Pros:* Cool concept.* Impressive graphics.* Audio is quite good and fits the situation.Cons:* There are enemies _everywhere_. Your fingers will hurt from pressing crazy combinations of shift+WASD, Q, E, F, C, etc - _all the time_.* The FOV is quite strange. It feels like you see too little of the actual world.* Did I mention that there are enemies everywhere? Well, that in combination with the limited FOV means that a single enemy will be able to block your whole view - and that happens all the time. It's difficult to play when you can't see anything.* If you have to dodge enemies all the time, at least make it so that you can't fall down cliffs and such.Not recommended for casual players. This is for people who love to play over and over again until they learn the perfect combinations to finish off their enemies and progress further.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what can I say. I had a blast playing Bright Memory. This first person action shooter, developer by a single man, does a lot of things right and is a blast to play. Yes, it's short. You can finish the game in it's current state in less than an hour, but this hour is totally worth it. I played it twice (currently in third run) and am still enjoying every bit of this game.Bright Memory left early access four days ago. The game is still not complete, but every buyer will receive the additional content for free once it's released.Due to it's shortness, the game feels more like a demo than a game but I think once the additions are available we can call it a game.Bright Memory feels like a mixture of Doom and Dark Souls with a shot of Tomb Raider. Gun fights are mixed with sword play and the most outstanding achievement of this game is it's engaging combat. The different ways you can attack, use special attacks like EMP, sword blast or time freezing in combination with intensively fast dodging is huge fun. Bright Memory nails combat in a fantastic way.The games story is a mixture of Science Fiction and Fantasy but doesn't really matter, at least not in the games current state. You learn a hundred times more about the story by reading the Steam shop page, than you do in the game.Your hero is a teenage Japanese schoolgirl and the game adds the typical skirt and blouse combination as extra skin if you like.Graphics are decent, although could be better and the Unreal 4 engine does a good job. However, the game allows you to play in DX11 and DX12 more. While Bright Memory runs great in DX11 mode, DX12 produced a lot of graphical artefacts and caused lighting problems.The game seems a little buggy. Enemies get caught in the environment from time to time, but seldom. The game crashed once.Considering the fact that this game was developed by a single person, the result is fantastic and I personally believe this should be supported. Who knows, if we help this boy, maybe in a couple of years he'll surprise us with a game we've all been waiting for.Pros:- fantastic combat - great boss fights- great enemy design- good graphics (not outstanding but OK)- good music- inexpensiveCons:- short- a little buggy- simple level design- grappling handling needs to be improved

_childDocuments_.review: Since there's only one mission that'll take you an absolute max of 45min to finish, one can't say TOO much about this game yet. What I CAN say is this:F***ing gorgeous graphics, and it ran well even on my ol' potato PC that I just recently replaced.Guns are fun to shoot. Might not be quite DOOM levels of fun gunplay (I mean, all you get is a pistol, an assault rifle and an automatic shotgun) but it's up there.The writing and voice acting is... okay. Not Valkyria Chronicles or Mass Effect stuff exactly. Not sure how story-heavy the game will be, you seem to mostly run and gun in this game.Decent enemy variety. I can't say I enjoy fighting humans much since they all seem to hitscan and there's no cover system (aside from hiding but that obviously breaks your LOS too). The monsters are much more fun to fight as it becomes very relevant to use your spells to keep them at arm's length. The fact that you have to sprint to avoid them, because your regular run speed is slow af, does mean the pace of combat is a tad uneven as you can't kite and shoot at the same time.The one level you do have has replayability as you won't unlock all abilities in one run, you can do it again to improve score and keep unlocking spells which allow you to perform better. Overall I enjoyed it, but it will require some improvements. It'll only set you back a few dollars and I can recommend it for that price.

_childDocuments_.review: Not my usual type of game but I'm giving it a try. First of all, if you like to customize your controls, wait for a later version. So you have no choice but to stumble your way through until you get used to the default layout, which so far leads to instant death. The game tosses you right into the arena mode immediately where you step on a twig and then fall into a coincidentally round and inescapable area where enemies spawn around you and attack for several waves. A slower ramp up would have been nice especially if I can't edit my control layout. My first session was frustrating enough for me to wait until I can customize my controls. I might revise my review to something more favorable at a later time but for now, I can't recommend the game unless you are mostly a console player who never needs to customize settings.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory is a visually striking game that initially draws you in with its flashy combat mechanics and impressive graphics. However, beneath its polished exterior lies a game that ultimately falls short in delivering a satisfying experience. While the combat can be enjoyable and the graphics are undeniably nice, the confusing and meaningless story, coupled with an exceptionally short duration, leave players feeling unsatisfied and wanting more.Let's start with the positives. The combat in Bright Memory can be quite fun at times. The fast-paced gunfights and flashy swordplay offer a level of excitement and intensity that keeps you engaged throughout the game. The combination of ranged and melee combat, along with various special abilities, provides a decent amount of variety and allows for some satisfyingly stylish gameplay moments. Additionally, the game's visuals are undoubtedly impressive, with detailed environments and eye-catching effects that contribute to a visually appealing experience.However, the biggest downfall of Bright Memory lies in its story. Or rather, the lack thereof. The narrative is convoluted and confusing, making it difficult to understand the motivations and connections between characters and events. It feels as if the developers attempted to create a complex and intriguing storyline but failed to provide any meaningful explanations or resolutions. The lack of coherence leaves players bewildered and detached, ultimately making it challenging to invest in the game's world and its characters.Adding to the disappointment is the game's incredibly short duration. Bright Memory can be completed in just a few hours, leaving players craving more content. The brevity of the game not only leaves you feeling unsatisfied but also raises questions about the value of the overall experience. With such a short playtime, it's difficult to justify the price tag or feel like you've truly gotten your money's worth.While Bright Memory showcases potential with its enjoyable combat mechanics and stunning visuals, it ultimately fails to deliver a coherent and meaningful experience. The confusing story leaves players disconnected and craving clarity, while the disappointingly short duration leaves them longing for more substance. If you're solely looking for flashy combat and impressive graphics, Bright Memory might scratch that itch momentarily. However, if you seek a fulfilling and engaging gaming experience that offers a cohesive narrative and adequate length, you'll likely be left disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Not all it's cracked up to be. The visuals are stunning but the gameplay is borrowed and aggressively average.The game takes some clear inspiration from Dark Souls, Tomb Raider, and DMC, however each borrowed element is done in a very boring way. The boss fights play out somewhat like Dark Souls bossfights, but usually just come down to spamming one attack over and over. There are "puzzles" but they are really just dumbed-down parkour segments that are done worse than the dungeons in Tomb Raider. Finally there is aerial sword combat with freezing enemies in place somewhat like DMC, but it lacks finesse and isn't blended well with the shooter elements.This game is fine I guess. But that's about it. Just fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, so this is the best shooter I've played since DOOM (2016). Combat is a ton of fun and has a lot more to use than just guns. You have an emp blast which sends enemies flying into the air for a short while, a leash that will rocket you towards any enemy, and a light sword with three different attacks that each have a purpose. Combat is fast, frenetic, and fun. There's also a slew of interesting upgrades that can spice up your combat style like one that lets you hover in the air by damaging enemies while airborne. The game is a little jank, that's why it's in early access, but jank is just about it. It runs wonderfully on my five year old desktop with a slew of different graphics options to make the game as pretty or performance heavy as you want. The story is, well, it's fun. The price is absurdly cheap for how fun the game is. Can't recommend the game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend Bright Memory. The entire game feels like it's been designed by a teenager. Frequent and interrupting cutscenes with no breathing room sets an exhausting pace, and the inconsistent tone doesn't help. The marketing pictures on the storefront shows off environments not even included in the game...Bright Memory sets you in the shoes of one-woman-army Shelia, armed with an assault rifle, shotgun, handgun, sword, some sort of electrical grapple, and... EMP? The shooting experience is quite uninspired, with minimal kick, boring sound effects, and especially the complete lack of hit impact on enemies makes them feel like the developer had to include them as some sort of obligation to the genre. The sword is different in that is another shooting weapons with a couple of alt-fire options, all linked to completely asinine button mappings, it should really have been the main weapon, especially considering most of the enemies are melee-only. Most of the shooting is done at enemies charging straight at you, which means there's barely any challenge in aiming. The shooting arenas are basically coverless, meaning your only defense is shooting enemies and mashing the dash key.There is no explanation of what's actually happening, but at least you're not getting lost in the linear level design as the only way is forward. To break up the action, you get to do some platforming, this would be fine if the mechanics weren't so incredibly stiff. To grapple, you have to stop and press Q, completely removing any semblance of fluidity from the game. While the "EMP" will clear out most obstacles in your path you need to wait 3 seconds for the animation to play out. Most obstacles are also insta-death out-of-bounds zones, meaning that whenever you fail to do exactly as the developer wanted you have to reload back to the latest checkpoint. If there is a positive here, it has to be the fact that the developer made checkpoints for basically everything.While the game can show of some impressive graphical technologies with Nvidia RTX and DLSS support, some textures are quite lacking in detail. And there is some unfortunate camerawork in play, making you focus on the especially poor wall textures. There's also a general lack of polygons, making a lot of surfaces quite a bit less smooth than they could be.While I hope the developer has learned something about game development from this demo, I am worried if he's planning to create the entire game alone. As a lot of my gripes could have been fixed with a bit more polish and playtesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Bright Memory

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and engaging DOOM style gameplay with unique abilities, if that's your cup of tea and you have £5 to spare then definitely pick this up. If you're still undecided then keep reading.PROS: Shooting, movement and abilities (especially the sword) all feel extremely good, the dodge is a very welcome feature that more shooters need to include.The soundtracks used during firefights makes you feel like an absolute badass.Graphically stunning and very well optimised.CONS/POSSIBLE IMPROVEMENTS:Massive headbob combined with earthquakes in game shaking the screen made me feel almost dizzy at times. A headbob and FOV slider would be welcome to help with this.Had no idea what was going on story wise; the most info I got on the world I was in was sentences on the loading screen, I would love to be invested in this world but the demo does not make that happen.Sound effects were weak and bland in some areas, notably the guns that sounded more like air rifles.This game has a very exciting future ahead of it and will only improve with time. Being a one man developed game but looking this good already could turn it into the next undertale.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't tend to give a positive review if a game is not finished, but getting this now will grant you free access to the full game that's still in development. Very fast-paced and trying to get some good combos could be both challenging and fun. It's short, a speedrunning may take only 15-20 minutes to finish, skipping all the cutscenes. But it's super dense, your adrenaline won't stop any second during the gunfight.My words may be a little bit biased and exaggerated. _childDocuments_.review: Short, but great fun. I don't understand the story at all, since the voices are in Japanese and reading the subtitles during action sequences is pretty much impossible. There's talk about some artifact and a dead guy. Between the main character passing out every few minutes for story reasons, I was not able to follow.You're given a few ways of attacking from the start. Three guns. An assaul rifle, some kind of low spread shotgun and a pistol. You also have a sword, which attacks at a longer distance than expected. Your sword has three different kinds of attacks: Normal slash, an X-slash kinda thing, and a ground pound that knocks enemies into the air. There are other abilities to unlock as you progress too, but I didn't get them all in my first playthrough (Took roughly 50 minutes.)Overall the platforming sections are the weakest. I had to make use of an unlockable ability that let me float in the air while firing my assault rifle in order to get past a long jump. The combat is just SO much fun though. Dashing around, firing and slashing at waves of enemies was cathartic. I will absolutely be purchasing later episodes in this series. If the length is an issue for you, just know that you will want to do multiple playthroughs to try to beat your score, and stay as long as you can in SSS rank.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write a lot of video-game reviews, but this game seriously had me surprised. For the price of $9.00, Bright Memory is well worth the money. To get me started, I'd like to touch on the biggest and best aspect of the game, the combat. It is engaging, fast-paced, and incredibly satisfying. The game is like a big mix of Devil May Cry and Doom, while also maintaining it's own identity and unique world and characters. Another thing I would like to point out are the graphics. For such a small development team, the visuals of this game are absolutely stunning. It looks very nice and the environments are put together quite well (although, the graphics are probably not something you will be focused on while obliterating the monsters and enemies with kick-ass combos.) The story is not the best, and it definitely failed to get me intrigued, but the astonishing gameplay and visuals really kept me going and grew my love for this game.To sum my review up, if you're looking for a fast and action-packed fps game for a small price, you have come to the right place. Bright Memory may be a short experience, but for that small price, it is totally worth every last cent.

_childDocuments_.review: HOLY $#IT WTF DID I JUST PLAY?!?!?! I don't even know where to begin with this game other first stating I am totally blown away by this. This is one of the best EA titles I have tried/supported ever. Fast pace action like the newer doom series mixed with DMC, and amazing special abilities like an energy sword that has 3 different attacks, lightning, time stopping and more. Gun play is pretty smooth. Wouldn't mind seeing a more expansive skill and ability tree but this is a great start. The story is ok to start but seems to get me more interested right at the end lol go figure, but I would like to see that improve some in the story writing. 1st run through took an hour so you can expect about that amount from this demo. _childDocuments_.review: I am a 55 year old biker and trucker father, and probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 15 now. My son got this game for from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 12 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he let me borrow his controller. Me and my son then played in turns and I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: A mash up of games that the developer liked. Notably Call of Duty Advanced Warfare and the Shadow Warrior reboot due to the movement options, gun feel and focus on combat. There's even a Devil May Cry-style ranking system and an unlockable ability that lets you float mid-air as long as you're shooting. For the environments and enemies it's really obvious they like the Souls franchise - there's even an unmissable reference to it near the end. The plot isn't even worth mentioning since it's obviously unfinished and it starts so in media res that it plays out like a fever dream. Probably better that way since the main character's SOLDIER EXO-SUIT ARMOUR has such an absurd boob window that it's impossible to take seriously.The combat is fun but it's in between a bunch of boring glitchy platforming gimmicks and a lame Uncharted-esque match-three puzzle and really at the end of the day it's so short - clocking in at 40 minutes - that you're better off playing the games it's trying to copy until it's finished.Games like these make me wish Steam had a "mixed" button for recommending games. I didn't dislike it, but I didn't really like it either.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a lite first person shooter with a sci-fi Tomb Raider style about it.Tomb Raider (lite) in terms of environmental puzzles, platform jumping, etc, as well as the basic idea behind the story line.. sort of.Content is short... very short. It is a good demo style teaser of a first episode, but don't expect a deep level of content here. With 6 wreckless deaths, tweaking of controls, and minor time wasting on one of the platform jumping puzzles, my playthrough time came to about 30 or 40 minutes.And it is worth remembering the "lite" aspect of the shooter design. So there are aspects of the level design in this first episode that are a little repetitive (you literally double back over certain areas several times). But there is an upgrade system, and the game appears to be designed for multiple re-runs with more and more upgrades unlocked.Gun play feels generally very good, but it also feels a little like it is designed for gamepad controllers first, mouse and key second. I did encounter some odd bugs where the game decided not to respond to my left or right mouse clicks. This made ADS and firing a very noticeable problem more than a few times during boss battles. And I don't mean a split second loss of input... I mean not being able to go ADS for a dozen button mashes spanning at least 3 whole seconds... and suddenly not being able to fire when there are still 4 rounds in the shotgun... mash mash mash... nothing.. dodge.. mash mash mash... nothing... mash... firing again... frustrating, but it is a bug that should at some point be ironed out. It was unique to those two actions as well.The combat as a whole is actually quite good. You have abilities, like an EMP "force" blast from your hand, a melee blade weapon/ability that has projectile slashes, and an interesting use of rapid dodge/dash movements make engaging the enemy pretty cool.But even the dodging, dashing, and even non combat/platformer jumping... you are reminded a few times that a controller is the preferred method of input, not mouse and key. That is not say this is some blasphemously garbage port, but mouse and key definitely needs tweaking/refining.I only played in DX12 with Ray Tracing on because.. if you offer me the best, I will accept nothing less than the best!!!There are some interesting little glitches and anomalies with ray tracing, but they are very minor. This game does not have the Ray Traced visual polish of Cyberpunk 2077, but considering the solitary developer and not having a monster budget, it is pretty impressive the only glitches present are the inevitable ones that come with new tech being introduced into the Unreal Engine.Feels like the full "Infinite" game will have a lot of potential to become an enjoyable, casual action-adventure FPS. It's not perfect, but it is far more polished and "finished" then a lot of AAA titles the fanboy slaves rush out to spend stupid amounts of pre-order money on for fake/marketing "Beta Access" and are still delivered game breaking Day Zero bugs and glitches.Worth supporting this indie developer!!!

_childDocuments_.review: This is essentially a demo. That you *pay* for. Normally that's not a good look. But considering this project was put together by a one-man team, the results do speak for themselves, and while I didn't realize it was basically a demo when i bought it (I didn't read everything before buying, so that's on me), for the almost one-hours worth of playtime it took me to complete it once, I honestly wasn't too disappointed. The models were pretty good. The environments felt a little basic but at the same time had some decent detail to them for what they were. Combat felt good enough, though some of the more basic enemies felt a little bullet-spongey at times...kinda makes sense, they're Undead after all...and the bosses were fun enough to fight, you just have to find their weakpoints (its not hard) and keep hammering them. Make sure you master that dodge mechanic though, it's pretty vital to your survival at times. Can't wait to be able to alter key bindings though, play this on mouse and keyboard and assigning dodge to one of my mouse's side buttons will make it so much easier.All this said, I'm intrigued by what I've seen here, and can't wait to see where the developer goes for BM: Infinite. Normally I wouldn't recommend something like this, an incomplete product that you still have to pay for...again, it's apparently just one guy putting this whole thing together, and the results speak for themselves. And it's cheap enough that it's not going to put a dent in your wallet (unlike some companies that charge full-price for broken messes of unfinished content). Overall, I'd give this demo an 8/10. Decent in most regards, just a *little* lacking on some places, but all in all an incredible presentation for what it is and where it's coming from.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite enjoyed this one! Best way I can describe it is Call of Duty meets Devil May Cry and it works pretty well! Has some light puzzle and platforming segments too. Short but sweet, you'll be done in an hour, give or take. If you liked this, you'll get Bright Memory Infinite for free once that comes out. Looks gorgeous, the RPG mechanics work well to define your playstyle (They act kinda like COD perks). Gunplay, movement, and swordplay is tight and the enemies are interesting to fight for the most part. While the english localization is certainly not impressive, I was able to follow what was going on, I never felt misled and in fact reminded me of the janky but excellent E.Y.E Divine Cybermancy, was rather charming at times (though not as memetastic). Pacing was also excellent, It will not waste your time, but will slow things down after a heavy fight to help catch your breath with a light puzzle or platforming challenge. Graphics are also very good too, both artistically and technically.My main Issues are Technical. Whatever they are using to load and apply said loaded data doesn't work. I have the occasional load crash and my graphics settings while saved do not reapply on restart (I'm running on a relatively old machine and the Ultra settings slow it to a crawl, low settings are more than manageable so its kind of annoying to turn everything off on booting the game). I also once loaded with a couple magazines in my gun instead of the full compliment I walked in with.There are also some questionable Level geometry. A lot of the tether points feel too tight, I feel like I should at least be able to fire it off earlier, also in that one puzzle room, I find it easy to get caught in the dragon heads during the final fight or just getting trapped by a mob of enemies with melee attacks and the level geometry (The first fight with the undead swordsmen were particularly bad).That said my Complaints are minor and fixable, I didn't mind the hour length given the price (6.99 as of this writing, not on sale) and the quality of the hour I spent, even with the technical issues.

_childDocuments_.review: This has some good potential for being a AAA-style indie game for under $10. The combat mechanics are complex but very interesting as you can switch from gun fighting to sword fighting in an instant, which is something I haven't seen in other FPS games before. You are also able to add and upgrade perks, and buy more abilities with XP gained from fighting. Not only is it an FPS, but it also has some elements from the Souls games and Tomb Raider games. Keep in mind that this game can be beaten in under an hour since there is only one episode so far for it being early access at the moment, but you can continue to replay the episode with the perks and abilities you got from your first playthrough (like a New Game Plus). The game can be a bit buggy, but overall it could be a great game that can compete with the trash $60 AAA games we get nowadays from greedy publishers.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory is a fast-paced FPS where you play as a woman named Shelia, trying to stop a terrorist organization from gathering mystical artifacts. Aside from her shooting skills, her suit is also augmented with powers such as creating energy blasts. With more XP you can unlock more skills such as damage resistance and force field. It's a pretty unique take of a futuristic shooter as it combines fantasy elements, you don't just fight soldiers but mythical creatures as well.This game is really short and can be beaten in around an hour, and with the lack of explanation of the story in-game whatsoever makes it feel like a tech demo. But it probably is, since apparently it's only made by a single person, and creating a game like this is no easy job. It's also not meant to be played only once, since every time you finish you can play Continue+ more where you play a new game but keep your skills. Plus there's an achievement for finishing the game 2 more times this way.My problem with this game is the pacing and difficulty. I know what kind of game I'm getting into, but it's even more fast-paced than "one man army" games such as Shadow Warrior. And there is no difficulty setting, while it's not impossible its kinda harder than I'd like. Still, it's a pretty fun, albeit short experience, and if you like fast-paced shooters this game might just scratch that itch. The full version of the game, Bright Memory: Infinite, is already released, but the levels here aren't ported there so it's best to buy both.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is made by one person in his own time, and I am honestly nothing but impressed. Now, of course there's gonna be some awkward downsides which I'll list later, but the biggest thing I saw in this game was its speedrunning potential, and it is fun as all hell.Pros:-Actually mildly interesting story, I'd love to see it developed further-Gameplay is fast paced and somewhat difficult-Theres a fair amount of replayability to be had, even in early access-This game runs way better than I expected, almost no frame drops*Not really a pro, but you can kind of think of this game as a dark souls game with guns with more stamina/less health that had a child with tomb raider.Cons:-The movement system is weird, borderline uncomfortable, but exploitable to have some fun with     -Ex; Press a direction then shift and hold space at the same time to get a massive speed and directional boost-The translation is messy and innacurate at times, but it gets the point across and this is still the one person doing the translation for the game-The enemies feel out of place. I'm sure everything will work itself out in the future episodes, but it's just a little weird.Really, if you have a little bit of money to bust, go ahead and buy this game. It's hella fun, the dev needs the support, and the future potential of it is something a large portion of the community playing this game is looking forward to.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome so far - mechanics & gameplay feel really great.Looks amazing.Has quite a few skills & options, but keeps the controls nice & tight.Dense, engaging & thrilling.Definitely looking forward for more!ps. Sometimes are fun translations: The saving will loose when quit.It's bite-sized, so one play-through will take slightly more than an hour.Edit after my first play through:I hope they keep the episodic nature (it doesn't look like it, but still).This one might be short, but after all, it was probably an incredible proof of concept.It's designed like a challenge. You just reload after death, you don't die or save.That changes the nature of the challenge to quite a degree.I'd love to have bite-sized episodes of 1-2h hours every 3 months or so.It'd be coming back to something that steadily brings some new design, some new areas, some new bosses. That'd be bliss in my opinion. This was a well designed, action-packed bite of something tasty.One impression I got over the course of the story: it sort of is a better Tomb Raider.It's not a phenomenal story, but it keeps you engaged (specially since I definitely want to fight the fly snake at some point).It has some easy jump & lever puzzles (which are mostly done to make you acquainted to control the powers).It's an interestingly structured game.Each element has been here in some other game, but the sum is more than it's elements and I haven't seen it done in that fashion before.Shout outs as well to FYQD for patching and re-tuning the experience so steadily. That really left a good impression to me. I hope the optimizations will help make the upcoming content better from the get-go.I'll be back for a few more reruns over time and look forward for the next episode - or as it seems from the announcements - the full game.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing first, this is not a full game. It is a demo for the full game that is scheduled to be released sometime in 2021. I don't like how the game's page on Steam makes you think (unless you read the reviews, which for some reason with this game I just didn't) this is a full game. As for the actual in-game, it is quite enjoyable. The graphics are quite good on 1440, with everything set to high, especially for $10. RTX makes a big difference, so if you can turn it on. Combat definitely has a clunky feel to it at the moment. Nothing that can't be polished and smoothed out. For this being a game originally in Chinese, the English dub is not bad. Lip sync is a bit off when you actually see faces, but nothing atrocious. Skills are pretty cool in this as well. Just a matter of learning each key and what they do, since you cannot change the keybindings at this time. For a $10 demo, I am really looking forward to the full release. Depending on how much content is added and if certain annoying aspects are addressed, this could very easily be a $20 or even $30 game at full release. Worth the money to try out now and get the game at full release.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally intended to be the first episode in a game with multiple episodes, this tech demo was eventually abandoned in favour of the "full-length replacement" that is Bright Memory: Infinite. In reality, however, the two games only share some elements (cast, some enemies, and some of the gameplay elements).That development leaves this original Bright Memory as a short tech demo that explores visuals as well as gameplay elements that would eventually come to be more realized in Bright Memory: Infinite.Bright Memory is quite short, especially if you get the hang of its combat loop and abilities quickly, and can be finished at around 30 minutes for regular FPS players.If you want a short and quick experience, or want to see where its mostly one-man creator FYQD-Studio began, and what impressed the media and gaming industry at the time for them to support the creator to eventually created Bright Memory: Infinitie, then this is something for you. But if you don't care about either, then Bright Memory has nothing to really offer you other than a short but ultimately forgettable experience that you can experience in one sitting.

_childDocuments_.review: Even tho we only can play for like ~30 minutes I want to give this game a Review.So I start with the Story.You just get thrown into the middle of the game it seems, there are alot things you just don't understand.You just need to accept it, we probably will get all the Infos we need when the full game is released.Skillwise you have quiet a few  to use, all of them are really fun and feel really smooth to use, the feedback you get when you hit someone is really satisfying.  It kinda reminded me of Bulletstorm. You throw enemies into the air, where they are falling down with really low gravity. So you can use your sword to really f**k them up. And it feels AMAZING ! The gore factor is on point, you can slice the bodyparty of your enemies with your sword ! The other spells are useful, but not as fun to use.The weapons are really enjoyable, the pistol feels kinda useless compared to your Assault Rifle and your Auto Shotgun. The Shotgun just shreds everyone that comes near you. But because you only had these three weapons I cant tell you a lot about it. They feels nice and powerful.The UI around the game has some pros and cons. It mostly looks really clean, but there is like a weird cyberring around your weapons wich just confuses me, it is so unnecessary. But you don't really think of it when you are having lots of action.The graphic is ok. I have to say that I have a GTX 1080, so I can't use RTX. All i can say that everything besides the weapons and the enemies looks okay. The weapons are actually very detailed, wich I really like.The surrounding of the map and the Charactermodels was something I didn't like, especially the hair . The Audio were made for asian synchro and you can see that. Besides that, the music is really nice, you have this awesome rock guitar playing in the backround as soon as something happens. The Audio of the everything else is also quite good.The Movement is like every other shooter you know, so I don't really have to write that much about it. The usage of spells ( Q,F,E ) is a little bit weird at first, but after a couple of minutes you'll get comfortable with it.The difficulty is pretty easy. I'd like it a little bit harder or that you could change the difficulty of the game. The normal enemies were relativly easy if you know what you were doing. The bosses you fight are really cool. The first one was the hardest one in my opinion. He is fast, does a good amount of damage and there are a few enemies around him attacking you. Thw reason  could be that it is at the beginning of the game and I was still learning the controls at that point. The second time you have to fight a Knight, wich is really easy, because he is slow and you have such a huge amount of space to juke him. But he does a lot of dmg. If he hits you three times you are dead. Another boss is the Demon ( the last boss of the demo ), he was a little bit harder and has two stages but again he...is...slow.He needs like 5-10 seconds to attack once, wich probably won't hit you anyways. They should make them harder, like a lot harder.At one point of the game you had to lit a bonfire... That confused me. The game doesn't feel like a soulslike game at all. I don't know if it was a troll, because it was literally the same font as in Dark Souls. If you died you also didn't spawn at the bonfire, you respawned were you died. So would I recommend the game ??F**k yeah I would. It was a lot of fun, I know there isn't a lot of content, but if you get this game for 5 Bucks now, you'll the full game too. This for me is a nobrainer. Get it, you most likely will love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Several people told me that I should give  a try; for good reasons, I suppose. I mean, I love first-person shooters, so it seemed right up my alley. When I started playing it, I was honestly pleasantly surprised, as it visually looks stunningly for a project made by a lone developer. Not only graphics are staggering, but some of the animations, as well as cutscenes and effects, are of good quality, too. After a short beautiful cutscene, I finally got into the action, and I was amazed. Shooting at several soldiers, seeing how their protection glass on their masks breaks, and bits of blood squirt out of it looked great, making headshots satisfying. Then I got my hands on an EMP blast, which both pushes enemies in the air or even literally tuns them into a pool of blood. Sure, I have witnessed such an ability in other titles numerous times already, but it still feels thrilling when done right, especially when accompanied by a blood-pumping soundtrack. Thus, I thought I would love this from start to finish.However, my enthusiasm for it went down after these first five enjoyable minutes, as then the game turns into a weird mishmash. It throws you into a fantasy setting with mythological monsters, which would not be a problem per se, as there are several shooters like that; yet, fighting them is monotonous, and there is no challenge in it whatsoever. I am not saying that to pump up my ego, so let me elaborate on it. When you fight with the abovementioned soldiers, they have the same weaponry and eve abilities like dash, so they are pretty agile and dangerous, especially in ranged combat. That is not the case with monsters, though. For example, the most common enemies are undead soldiers with a sword. As you can use a double jump, dash or even time-freeze capsule along with your shotgun — they do not stand a chance against you at all. Sure, there are tries to spice up these encounters by adding stronger foes, like monstrous lions who spits fire, but you can still put them down quickly, and there is not enough of them. Simply put, adding more enemy types, even the already existing ones, in each fight would make it both more entertaining and challenging; I would love if they would counter some of my abilities, but that is something you will not find here.That is my main gripe with , and it is a shame because the gunplay and abilities themselves are both satisfying and fun to use. Shotgun happened to be my favourite gun, as its fire rate is influenced by how fast you are pressing the mouse buttons, which obliterates everyone in your way. Your sword, which you can only use for a few seconds, is deadly too, and its slashes go even through multiple enemies. Plus, you can use its strike down ability that uplifts and stucks your foes in the air. Again, all of that is enjoyable to use for a while, but it gets boring soon.Bosses are a mixed bag. The first one is just another knight, behaving similarly to the ones with swords. It just has an uninspiring moveset and enormous amount of health. . You can basically circle around it as with the other melee-based enemies without worrying much. To give credit where it is due, the second one was quite enjoyable; perhaps because of the arena, the fight takes in, as there are environmental traps, making it a bit harder.I hoped that the New Game + mode would offer what I was looking for, but it was just another disappointment. Honestly, apart from the fact that you keep your obtained abilities, unlockable by experience points you get from killing enemies, I have not noticed any difference in the difficulty or enemy placement. If there even is any…As expected, it is a strictly linear experience, so there are no possibilities in how to approach each encounter. I do not mind that; however, as it focuses on the action, I thought it would be much better, which is sadly not the case here. There are also a few primitive puzzles between the combat sections, and while I appreciate their presence, I would gladly omit their existence in exchange for more captivating combat.Where  suffers the most is with its narrative. It is a bland, chaotic mess, which absolutely fails at being a competent introduction to this universe. Hell, even this title’s Steam Store page says more about its story and lore than the game itself. Atrocious. I do not mind when story-telling is a bit vague, so it would let me find bits of it in its world, but this is not the case. The premise is fine: you are a member of the special unit, trying to get an ancient artefact before baddies do so. What I have a problem with, as I said, is the presentation. Also, so-called plot armour is present throughout the cutscenes, mainly in the second half of the game — it just looks incredibly dumb when the protagonist survives a grenade a few centimetres away from her. Oh, and what I truly despise is when you have special abilities during cutscenes, invisibility in this case, yet you cannot use it.At its current state, I cannot recommend getting . Yes, it is remarkable what this solo developer achieved; however, I had fun with it only for five minutes or so, fifteen if I count in New Game + playthroughs for achievements. Keep in mind that one run is about half an hour long. That is not enough for me for its price, though. Especially as this experience is not unique, so there are plenty of other titles to choose from. And no, the fact that I will get the “full” game, , because I own this “demo” is not relevant for me to change my mind and recommend it, as that would mean I would be promoting an unreleased product. A product of which we know next to nothing apart from marketing trailers. Well, if this mishmash of a prologue is supposed to show me how it will all look like in the end, then I am sceptical about how it will turn out. Nevertheless, I will gladly give it a chance.

It seems like there will be experience and an ability tree in the main game. The fighting is really fun and fluid with some cool combos that you can pull off. There are also some puzzles and platforming which I found to be less enjoyable than the rest of the game, but they weren't implemented poorly. The game visually looks incredible and has some very cool enemy design, particularly the boss. The voice acting is solid and the world looks interesting from what little I can see.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoilers (maybe? I don't talk about the plot but... IDK) just thought I’d put that warning there as I generally don’t care about spoilers, so I tend to be super careful about them around others so if you want to go into this game blind don’t read this just know I think the game is good.Really fun gameplay but very short, the game is only about 45 minutes long. However I can definitely seem myself playing it through multiple times to unlock all the upgrades and master the combat system. Hopefully future episodes are longer and this was just to see if people would be interested in the game.  Some of these might seem nit-picky but these are some of the issues/ criticisms I had with the game. Take them with a grain of salt, I know nothing about game design.1. Reloading your guns doesn’t really fit the style of the game, it would make more sense if your guns used energy and overheated so you didn’t need to actively reload it was more of a passive thing as to not break the action. This would allow you to switch between guns and not worry about switching to a gun that you forgot to reload and screwing yourself. Gun switching could also be an interesting mechanic to deepen the gameplay. Or you just don’t need to reload like in Doom, though I could see this breaking some of the abilities you unlock, such as...2. The ability that boosts you higher if you shoot while already being in the air only lifts you a set amount per shot rather than scaling depending on what gun you’re using. It’s fine on the assault rifle but almost useless on the shotgun and pistol. It would be way more interesting if the shotgun boosted you up really high and you had to time your shots as you went up and down to get the most damage out of the shotgun.3. Speaking of the shotgun, it just feels super weak, not just in damage but also the sound it makes.4. One of the boss arenas is too small (IMO)5. The human enemies are just not fun to fight, I’m not exactly sure what it is about them, maybe they have too much health or the arena you fight them in isn't really suited for fighting more traditional FPS enemies. Luckily you only briefly fight them in two parts of the game so it’s not that bad.6. You have a move that lets you swing on certain objects in the terrain to get over obstacles, however for it to work properly you have to stop moving, which doesn’t seem like that big of a deal but the gameplay and movement is so fast that it feels like you should be able to jump off the ledge and start the swing mid air but often the prompt goes away and you fall to your death. I just think that you should be able to do the exploration/ platforming at the same or similar speed as the combat.7. Enemy attacks that look like they miss, still hit8. Guns are pretty boring (Assault rifle, shotgun, pistol) hope to see some more variety in the future. Despite all that the game is really good and I don’t mind paying $8 for a 45 min experience if it means that it’ll help the developer make the full game. What’s here is really good and the gameplay has lots of potential which makes me very excited for whats to come, as long as the developer gets creative with the gameplay and doesn't just shove you in repeating arena’s with the same move set and enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: I paid $8 for a demo. Granted, it's a pretty nice demo, but I kind of expected more. For what it's worth, the game looks and feels like a Triple-A game. It takes the standard gameplay and gunplay of your average FPS and attempts to give it some depth with you being able to dash and jump 10 feet in the air, along with other mechanics, like giving you a grapple, using a force push to get breathing room, and being able to slow down time. While these are nice additions, the pace doesn't match the mechanics. Everything feels way too slow. (also the game has a style meter when it really doesn't need one. DMC or ULTRAKILL this is not.)I don't want to be overly mean to the 1 dev that this game has, but let's hope the "sequel" has more to it. I really wish steam had an inbetween button instead of Yes or No, cuz I don't really feel much of anything for this game. I guess that in and of itself warrants no recommendation.

But some action platform sequences have surprise floor collapses that dont have any prompts or ways to escape them besides godlike reflexes or knowledge ahead of time.Neutral- $10 for a 30-45 minute demo...ehh...I tend to be pretty forgivable for game pricing, but this...i dunno. _childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory is a really sweet demo that gives you a taste of author's upcoming full release title Bright Memory Infinite. And what a demo it is! It is incredible what this ONE person has accomplished - from graphic fidelity through gameplay mechanics - this is a solid game that if polished a bit more would be even suitable for AAA release. The only aspect that I felt had been neglected in favor of awesome combat, environmental design and general graphical coat is story - dont get me wrong I am happy there is a story and voice acting is fairly decent, however - story could use a bit more thought about it because as it stands right now in this demo - it is rather bland. We will see, how it is going to be in Infinite. All things considered - BM is absolutely worth the little money you can throw to that hard-working dev and will give you enough satisfaction for the price. The best of all however, is that he smuggled a bonfire from Dark Souls in there - instant 10/10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal! To sum it up, it's a fast paced FPS mixed with Darksouls learning curve by how hard enemies hit and DMC action.Though the early access content is short it's enough to peek interest in the story and characters. There is also the Continue+ which lets you keep running through it trying to beat your own score and explore the map more. This also allows you to keep adding to your skills and play around with the mechanics of the game. The sound quality is very well done with a nice balanced EQ. Voice acting is surprisingly well off as well.With that said there are some flaws I'll note in my con section but that has more to do with programming than the style or quality of the overall experience. I CAN NOT wait to see a full version of this game! Incredibly excited for it!Pros:Incredible fast paced actionRPG elements like XP and cool downs of skillsInnovative game play adding hack and slash speed with FPS shootingWell directed scenes to keep the interest in plotQuality sound, graphics, and voice actingReplay ability is high to improve and try new tacticsCons:Sometimes after a cut scene the character model disappears. Only able to see the crosshair on the screen. This is solved though just by switching to the next weapon.Even after fully loading a all guns before entering a room character still goes through a reload/weapon check animation randomly when switching guns in combat. This has lead to me getting smacked several times. I know this is just me being critical but it makes no sense that someone trained for combat would waste time doing this in combat if they already know all their weapons have fresh clips in full of ammo.Glitched into the corner just under a lip of rock at the spike pitfall while trying to escape the cave-in. Was able to eventually drop down into the spike area and run through them. With no way to get out I tried jumping which the walk way was too high then died falling back onto the spikes.Outside of those issues very solid game! LOVE IT!

_childDocuments_.review: First off: This is not a full game, it's a demo. Playtime is around 30-45 minutes. Which means you can finish this game TWICE, refund, and still be back in time for lunch.THE GAMEPLAY.What we have here is a simple and fun PvE shooter. You walk into an area and monsters pop up that you have to kill in cool ways with guns and special abilities. And every once in a while, you fight a boss or solve a puzzle. Games of this genre include shadow warrior, serious sam, etc. Except this game only has ONE LEVEL. So yeah.WHY THUMBS DOWN?Because it's overhyped. It's a good game for what it is, but you at least have the right to know what this is. A 30 minute demo. Technically you get the full game "Bright memory: infinite" on launch for free, but that game doesn't even have a release date and keep in mind this is one person developing the game, so red flags everywhere on that one. There's a good chance this is all we will ever get. So if you think it's worth the purchase, you can play this for an hour and uninstall. Otherwise don't bother.I will now proceed to talk about the production aspect of the game. Not to criticize, just an analysis regarding amateur game development.As I'm sure you know by now, this game was made by one guy.Many people have messed around in Unreal, Cryengine, or unity in their free time. This dude from china was messing around in unreal 4 and decided to get real and make a full game.All of these engines are best suited to make a simple, level based game. If you have an open world, the graphics performance will go to ♥♥♥♥, because the engine will try to render everything at once. So these games aren't possible without being a c++ or c# nerd, and modifying the engine like crazy to optimize the performance. Same with cpu intensive operations, like simulators etc. That's one of the reasons why big studios use in house engines.But this game keeps everything very simple. Small levels, basic shooter gameplay, few objects, few enemies, a little physics, some particle effects, done. UE4 handles the rest which is why performance is good and everything works fine.Now let's break down the work that needed to be done.Gameplay: shooter controls, movement, camera, level design, story (not much of a story but ok) The particle effects look good. Physics are provided by UE4 but need scripting for attacks and stuff including animations.Environment: 80% from quixel.Guns: I'm gonna guess bought from stores, there are a million gun models for sale.Characters: This is by far the trickiest one. The protagonist and bad guy are probably commisioned from artists. I don't think he used generic characters for the main characters. Although the main characters are quite generic with her being a schoolgirl and him being some military dude.The monsters and soldiers are most likely just bought from a store. ALSO he ripped assets from other games without permission. So there's that.Addional objects like levers etc.: store.All in all, 80% bought, 15% ripped, 5% commissioned/self made would be my guess.Animations: All animations are probably done by hand through ue4, which is tedious to say the least. I'm guessing the models come with skeleton rigs and then you animate them in ue4. The main character only has a torso, no legs visble. Guns are EZ, reload is a bit tricky, but it's only 3 guns. Face animations are barely a thing at all, and they suck. Most animations are enemy attacks and effects. Lipsync is only moving lips while audio is playing. It sucks.UI: probably selfmade. Looks really good tho. Graphics options are provided by UE4.Audio: effects and music: most likely open source. EZ. Voices: commissioned from voice over people. There's only like 5 lines so should be cheap.DISTRIBUTION: UE4 deploys on win and consoles. Anyone can make a steam account and sell games on PC, same probably for epic games store. With consoles I'm not sure but there are indie games on console.TIME: he did this as a hobby in his spare time, I think starting 2017, so 2-3 years. Couple hours a day?THE COST: I would guess $300-700, pretty much all 3d assets and voice-overs. UE4 is free and so is most of the other stuff. Don't remember the quixel prices from 2017 tbh. BUT he received an "unreal dev grant" from epic games, so I assume he pretty much had 0 cost after that or even made money lol.NOTE that quixel is now FREE for UE4, so the cost of this game would drop to like 100bucks nowadays.PROFIT: Complete guess here, but seeing as dev cost is like 0. Let's say he sold 100.000 copies, at 8$, that's 800k,steam takes 30%, others vary. so that leaves him with like 500k PROFIT. Pretty damn nice for a glorified asset flip.VERDICT:the good: UI, camera, gameplay, effects.the meh: audio. the voice over is decent. Effects and music ok. Just lacking more content.Levels. they are tiny and boring, the only saving grace is that there is enough variety with jumping, fights and a puzzle. Also way too short and bland.the bad: graphics. Texture quality on those quixel assets SUCKS. Seriously wtf. Those textures are supposed to be AAA, but these look 5 years old. The game should look waaaaay better. I'm guessing he downscaled it to run on consoles. Gay.lipsync, it sucks.So all in all, this game proves that you CAN make a game in UE4 by yourself, that looks and plays ok, and get hype and lots of money. Now obviously this is just a 45 minute gameplay demo, and 3 years dev time for that....? But hey, as long as the plebs hype it, buy it, and give you lots of money...So I would still say it's a clear win for indie devs, because it gives others a proof of concept for this sort of thing. The problem is, you will run out of quixel assets after one level, and then your game just stops. Ooops. Also, all games using these assets will look the same, yo the first guy to make a game from them will get all the cash and good reviews, and everyone else will look like a shmuck, just because they're slightly too late to the party. Even though they're all just asset flips.

_childDocuments_.review: I went in expecting a ~1 hour demo. Got exactly that, but hot damn was I impressed and excited for the full release. Imagine DOOM 2016, more jank, less red in the color scheme, fewer weapons, and more abilities to score up style points a la Devil May Cry.Major technical note: when I say jank, I mean JAAAAANK. No option to disable head bobble, no key remapping, double jump is HOLD space (??), E is bound to Use AND your main dps skill (??), and lots of weird bugs. The cool thing is, if one of these things is a deal-breaker for you, the demo is literally not long enough to go past the refund threshold, even if you beat the whole thing.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally (or ever) give reviews for games. However, Bright Memory is a definite exception! For anyone who hasn't bought the game yet, this IS a demo! The game kinda just ends after a certain boss fight and goes straight to the main menu. however there are 2 achievements related to replaying it 2 more times off of continue. Now the "GOOD" stuff. Enemies are enjoyably (and annoyingly in  a good way) difficult. The combat is satisfyingly meaty and fast-paced without being exaggerated. Boss fights are intense since every boss spawns smaller enemies and have field obstacles making it just a little more difficult. Despite a very scarce story, what it does give you is just enough to make you curious! The guns and sword you get are feel like they have their own weight to them in the sense of recoil, damage and knock back. The sword has a nice AOE attack that combos PERFECTLY with a few of the skills you can use in game. Now on to the "BAD" things about the game. I want to stress before continuing that these are more on the end of mechanic preferences over problems!While sprinting is a thing in the game it doesn't really help much when trying to make some distance, as I've had enemies be right up on me after running away for a while. Combat while really fun and enjoyable does have an issue with (and i can't believe I'm saying this) but too many ability buttons. to the point where you end up fumbling through powers accidentally trying to get the right one sometimes. There's no standard melee attack outside of the sword ability that has a bit of a recharge delay. One thing I will say about the boss fights, One in particular is a bit of an annoyance only because of the hazards added half way through because it seems like it only hurts you and not the enemies and I don't know if that is intentional (story wise) or not...TL;DR Game is super fun demo for a full release later on and the Dev should be proud! Can't recommend giving it a try and anyone who purchases the demo gets the full release free when it drops, which I assume might be more in price at launch.

_childDocuments_.review: This. Game. Yes.And for one man building??!?! Early Access or not, this game is phenomenal.The FIGHTING MECHANICS flow sooooo well and yet the COMBAT boasts great depth (so yes, dodging, shooting, swording, jumping, pulsing, blasting, pulling--them combos man<33 :)The GRAPHICS are gorgeous for the games pace and the fighting. The atmosphere is amazing in this game. It stands on its own, but for imagery sake: picture Hellblade, Wareframe, and Halo 3/Deus Ex thrown together. The title reminds me of Remember Me but I have yet to even scratch the surface of where he's going with this. <3To the developer: You are awesome. Keep this up. I am in love with the atmosphere and combat direction. It is, at times, a little too much going on, but we'll see once I get a better grip on mechanics.Only things I would note in lieu of Early Access development is that sometimes after reloading the weapon would decide to keep firing without me firing it xD could be stopped, but wastes a lot of the clip. And occassionally the actions would not register quick enough (specifically when running and jumping). Again, that may be a configuration on my side.If you like solo gameplay and enjoy the pace of Remember Me but the mechanics and flow of Hellblade with guns and electrical force-wielding awesomeness, GET THIS REGARDLESS.Cause it's awesome. :)BONUS TRAITS THIS GAME HAS GOING FOR IT:1. _childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty cool game. People are saying it lacks polish, and that's true. What they aren't saying is that it lacks basic functionality like rebinding keys.The game *is* fun, despite it's numerous and glaring flaws - but it's clearly an unfinished product.I know that I could probably go looking for a config file to edit - it was built in Unreal - but should I *have* to do that? If they let me rebind the keys this review will change.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly good game for a one man dev studio.  It's fast paced, has abilities, and even a sword.  For some reason everything is wet constantly though.  I think it uses that to hide some of the visual blemishes otherwise. The biggest problem, which allegedly will be fixed in the expanded game, is the lack editable key bindings.  The game is very fast paced and has a dodge mechanic, which is on the Shift key.  This is terrible because it makes it practically impossible to use properly.  I found myself only being able to dodge backwards.  This made a lot of the gun fights much harder than they should've been.  The game is also just one chapter.  The beginning of a larger game.  It's about 90 minutes long.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like what others have said before, the game is a demo for a cool gameplay concept. 45 mins long, however, the gameplay does seem fun: FPS with an assault rifle, shotgun, pistol, and a sword that are available to you, and you can also quick-dodge enemies (very useful, stay on the move) as well as float in the air to give yourself some breathing room. You have a couple of powers that can stun enemies or make you teleport to them, and that is your basic gameplay loop.I hear this is made by one guy, and it's all very impressive if so. I need to check out Bright Memory:Infinite to see if that game is longer and more polished, however, if you're thinking of trying out this one, remember it's 45 mins long and wait for a deep sale!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing fantasy hero shooter game! The gameplay is really fun so you have ton of replayability, it feels really satisfying to pull sick combos with your abilities and beat the living crap out of the enemies.There were couple of bugs which really frustrated me which was the cause of 90% of my deaths each run, it's where you jump and dodge into enemies but the collision physics can sometimes glitch out and knock you back way out of the map which results in environmental death. Another bug was when you're boost jumping and try to grapple but it does not register and you fall resulting in environmental death.Another issue is the game optimization, this game increases the temperature of my PC really high when compared to other heavy GPU demanding games which runs fine in normal temperature for even hours of playtime.It'd be really great if you can skip the cutscenes after completing the game once and if there was training mode where you can select the arena you want and enemies you want to summon so you can practice or just mess around to have more fun and would be great if there were more unique abilities like invisibility which is shown in the game cinematic but there's no gameplay mechanic related to it otherwise it would've been great to surprise attack enemies from stealth and have a playstyle with it.It'd also be nice if there was a toggle third person perspective option so you can appreciate the skins, I know the core gameplay is first person perspective but you could simply make it so it automatically changes to FPP if the player does any action outside of just movement.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is GLORIOUS.Between it's Devil May Cry mixed with FPS, it's incredible. The game looks great, plays great and there's even a spice of progression added to the mix.It's honestly ridiculous how good it is for only $9.95 AUD and a free full release copy when it comes out.Although, probably due my PC and sub-par optimization of the game, I tend to get stutter issues both audio and visually. (Tend to occur more with NVIDIA V-Sync On as I get screen tearing with basically every game, but in-game V-Sync made the issue even worse. Turning it off basically fixed the issue, but what I realised was that the stuttering often occurred with CPU at 100%, which is fairly normal with the CPU I currently have, it shouldn't necessarily cause issues. At least it doesn't with other games when, well the other games are fully utilising both my CPU & GPU.)Now, my PC isn't horrible. But I can run practically every game 'modern' game around High/Ultra 60 FPS. So, if you have a really good PC you probably won't have the issues I did.Otherwise, it's awesome. There's honestly not much I can say, just play it and see for yourself.
