_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, I love Amanita Design, have played all the games so far, but this is the weakest, yet. Indeed, the soundtrack and the graphics are phenomenal. But the gameplay not, seen it before a thousand times, pretty boring puzzles, not too repetitive (at the moment), not too hard, so you progress pretty smoothly. But for my taste, there is something missing. There is no interaction with your surroundings, no surprise inside the puzzles that would make them more interesting, they are just too clean, too logical, too stringent. I'm a little bit disappointed, not because I was expecting much of Creaks, in fact, I didn't, because I already thought, it would go that way. But now the experience for me at the moment is, I hope it will end soon. And that is the first time that happened with an Amanita Game, normally I'm sad, it ended too fast. _childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe I even hesitated to get this, another Amanita masterpiece. Every level is a beautiful artwork, the music and sound design are top notch, and the levels can be challenging, but not too difficult (even though I do like being stumped on a puzzle for a while - didn't get that so much with this game). Collectables in the form of paintings which sometimes act as minigames give you glimpses into the a strange "meta world", and are often of a very different style than the main game. An amazing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: There's something to be said for developers that become 'that dev' for any one genre--e.g. Arkane for immersive sims, Rocksteady for superhero brawlers, etc. I would have painted Amanita Design in the same light--from Samorost 1, to their commercial work with BBC, the Polyphonic Spree and Nike, all the way to their 2010's work like Machinarium and Samorost 3; point-n-clicky, with incredible art direction and wonderful soundtracks...but mostly point-n-click. I say "would have", because Creaks demonstrates that Amanita Design's abilities far surpass the bubble I think I relegated them to. A puzzler based on movement, timing and environment manipulation strays far from Amanita's bread and butter, yet it plays so insanely well that I felt like I should drop a review. Incredible art reminiscent of Machinarium works with a fully dynamic score by Hidden orchestra to breath life not only into Creak's world, but also your actions as a player--I particularly like how a level's soundtrack gradually builds as you piece together the proper solution. Visually, the most stand-out thing to me were the collectible paintings, as each is rendered in such a stupid amount of granular detail that the in-game paint actually looks like real acrylic paint on my screen. Control wise, your character feels really smooth to handle. Even though movement is based on tiles, everything is animated with such smoothness and character that it doesn't feel it. There's an arbitrary zoom button too--it adds nothing to the gameplay, but zooming in on the wonderful Burton-esque art is a vanity mechanic I can get behind. The puzzles and level design are really, really something. Never too mind-destroying, but paced deliberately enough to give you pieces one by one, only combining a few at a time (think Portal, instead of the Witness). I cannot stress enough how cool it is to have the level transitions be the space IN BETWEEN the puzzle rooms--one sequence at the end really hammers home how deliberately this whole underground space is connected. Amanita was really formative to my childhood years, so I might be a bit biased in saying their portfolio is nothing but straight masterpieces. To the devs--please bring BBC's Questionaut to Steam if you figure out licensing!note--I played the apple arcade version first, and that took around 5 hours. I got it again on steam to collect all the paintings. also, edited for spelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Man, how can you not love Amanita. Beautiful game, stunning hand-drawn animation, puzzles are not too easy, not too difficult, perfect balance. Their best puzzle game since Machinarium. I managed to finish the whole game without looking at YT (I did need some help on finding all the secret rooms though). Love all the little games that you can play with the playable paintings, they are basically a game within a game. The story is good as well, I just love how the whole map is basically a large nest where little bird-like creatures are struggling to cope with a cat-like monster. I need to get my hands on the Collector's Box edition of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: It's impossible not to adore Creaks. A silent story, their dreary visual style loaded at the same time with so much love, the way they understand the puzzles, the music of the game... and the mystery behind the story.What characterizes them the most is their powerful visual style. Their scenarios and characters are gloomy, that's why the mission of their heroes is usually to find hope, love or a glimpse of illusion in their dark worlds.Excellent game from the hand of "Amanita Design".
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This game was quite a surprise gem! Came across it by accident and it instantly intrigued me by its visual style and character. After completing the game in its entirety, I can confidently say this game is a must play for anyone who enjoys puzzles, unique story telling, eccentric art styles, and just a fantastic game to boot. I absolutely loved every second of it! The puzzles were well balanced, yet challenging even for veterans. The music was superb and really captured the atmosphere of their art style and theme. I was deeply saddened when this game came to an end... in a good way of course. There really wasn't a negative I could find in this title. Give it a try and I promise you will love it! If this developer ever makes a game of this caliber again, I will surely be checking it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Creaks can be enjoyed at two levels. Firstly, there are its clever puzzle designs and platforming; secondly, the game is a complex artwork. In the company of zither, piano and clarinets, the player is invited into an underground fantasy world. Its surreal, pareidolic nature and strange workings are underlined by charmingly odd characters and a simple, wordless narrative.Art lovers can enjoy an additional feature of the game. Creaks showcases a beautiful interactive gallery—its scattered figure paintings depict humans and avians in both ordinary and unusual situations, e.g. testing a rat-maze, listening to the sounds of water through brass pipes, or teaching fish how to jump through hoops. Whether there is symbolism within these paintings is unclear; they may well be simple fun diversions in between the conundrums.Regardless, Creaks is a calming and easy-going adventure which revolves around solving simple to moderately challenging brainteasers and appreciating arts. Its originality and attention to detail convey it is a game made with genuine passion.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend- 7.5/10The Good: The game’s biggest attraction is the hand drawn art style and atmosphere.  These features keep you immersed throughout the game.  The puzzle mechanics are introduced to you gradually and are intuitive, with none of the puzzles being overly complicated.  There are some other characters you encounter throughout the game and an over arching “simple” story that will drive you to the end.The Bad: The main negative thing I felt in this game was a lack in replay value.  There are some hidden rooms with collectible art to find for the completionist out there, but that’s it.  The other was the loss of potential of the strange art scattered about, which could have been used to tie more closely with the characters you meet in game.Overall: I would recommend this to anyone who likes puzzle and atmospheric games.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Creaks is a different beast than Amanita’s usual experience, but it is an extraordinary puzzle-platformer with great depth. Taking just under six hours to complete, each mechanic is carefully introduced and put to good use in challenges that have a perfect learning curve. Solutions are satisfying because the tricks are subtle. With intricate and twisted world design, and some fantastic music, the entire presentation is up there with the best from the developers. Creaks will please fans of Amanita’s previous games and anyone who enjoys a good twisted puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Essentially it boils down to expectations; if you come with a desire for puzzle and sketched eye candy then you are in for a treat. Anything else and you will regret your purchase... now onto the review:Everything underneath his room was either rusting, living or covered in thick layers of dust from the years of neglect. It is a peculiar world where I felt safer with the flashlight our humble protagonist clumsily left behind. He looks like the studious-type and therefore wholly unprepared to face any foe that could overpower him (such as mechanical dogs and flying jellyfishes) so it is best to avoid confrontation at all costs. Understanding that the devs are Amanita, you should already know what you are getting; a unique, colorful (or rather colorless!), beautiful world that focuses on its twisted, hand-drawn hallways rather than the gameplay. Yes, the gameplay can be rather dull if you seek non-stop action but if a simple puzzle game set in the darkest corners of a makeshift castle is what you’ve come to expect, then please step in into the world of Creaks and try to make it all make sense.Verdict upon completion; play it until the end, you won't regret it! The art only gets better with every step.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another masterpiece from Amanita. After Pilgrims, which was already drifting away from the point-and-click genre, Creaks offers a new experience with the puzzle genre. The story is simple and good, the characters are very likeable, the atmosphere, art and soundtrack are amazing (which goes without saying given Amanita past record in these regards). I was a bit skeptical about the puzzle genre at first, being a fan of point-and-click, but in the end this game is a real Amanita experience, once again, and I think they are getting better and better.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is entirely linear, not a point and click adventure like Machinarium. However, the makers did a good job of breaking the puzzles into isolated scenes, so you can reset a puzzle, or reload a scene and try to find a secret without backtracking over trodden ground. There's no "flip a switch on one side of the world, listen for a thing, walk through a bunch of empty familiar places to find an open door" or something Myst-ian like that.There's a good progression and variety of puzzle mechanics. The latter middle was the hardest, it seemed to get easier after that.Great puzzles, cute animation and characters. The ending was sweet, made me smile.  Controls are simple. Music was good.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Review: Creaks is not only the best game by Amanita so far but also one of the finest in its genre to date. It keeps surprising you through everything it does – be it the stunning artwork, the dynamic soundtrack, the heartwarming humor, the varied enemy types, or the innovative level design. With Creaks, Amanita pushes games as a form of media far enough to be compared to the masterpieces of Pixar or Ghibli. And boy, does it deliver!

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games and have this one in their backlog (minor spoilers ahead). Creaks is an indie adventure puzzle game where you also need to jump and activate switches, while evading monsters. The story is about a young man that finds a new underground world behind his wall after his room starts shaking. There isn’t spoken dialogue or narration, but you can understand the characters by their gestures and sounds.The scenarios and characters are hand drawn very well and look amazing, like most Amarita Studio games, with a lot of details and good coloring paired with good lighting effects that makes the game look even better.   The puzzles are logical and relatively easy. New mechanics are introduced without being really explained very well, but after a few tries you can figure them out. The level design and puzzles, while not reinventing the genre, are fun to solve and original, in particular the use of light and how it affects the monsters. There are also a few short and simple mini-games that are also fun to win and several paintings to collect.    28 Achievements. Around 5,5 hours, without a guide for the puzzles. Easy, the puzzles aren’t hard to figure out. Guides are available too. Easy. All the achievements are easy but some collectibles are well hidden and are hard to find without a guide so you’ll probably need the guide for them. Creaks is a great indie adventure puzzle game set in a fantasy world. It has an interesting story, beautiful hand drawn scenarios and characters and easy platforming and puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun puzzle game! It's challenging, and sometimes I hit a few puzzles where it felt impossible but it's definitely not. I loved it, the puzzles were so unique and different. The game itself is way longer than I expected! I kept thinking I was getting to the end but it just kept going. It's definitely worth the money, a lot of work went into this one! The story, art, and animation are adorable. Well done on this game! :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: For me, the best part about Amanita Design's games have always been beautiful worlds they create through their artwork and the music paired with it. And it's easy to want to compare Creaks to previous titles like Samorost or Machinarium when you first dive into it. Don't do that, though!Creaks has its own unique art style that evokes a feeling that everything is constantly moving and shifting-each set looking like they're an artist's doodle that's come alive on the page. It's paired with a soundtrack done by Hidden Orchestra that sometimes takes a back seat while you try to figure out a puzzle, but is still pleasant and funky when it finally kicks in. Amanita created a weird, upside-down, ever changing, bird-world complete with a cast of adorable bird creatures, and it's certainly worth playing through to experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game by the Amanita Team. I've been following their games for years and i've finally got to properly play one of them and it couldn't be better!!!This game features a very charming, very dark and very grotesque art style that it only gets better as you go along.It has a sort of "Kafka" vibe to it: The story of the game starts with our main character staying on his room, looking bored with life, until one sudden unexpected movement makes a crack on the wall, leaving some strange marks, upon inspection we found the entrance to an subterranean passage which leads into the origin of these tremors.... and a whole cast of strange beings which live in the earth below.... passage upon passage upon passage, its laberintical, babilon like, almost. The journey starts very slow and even monotone much... but soon you will find your way through different places, sometimes rooms, sometimes a cave.... the atmosphere starts to change, the colors follow suite and there will be plenty of variety (graphically speaking).The music also follows this extravagant secret world. The Hidden Orchestra made an incredible acoustic experience which makes as much for the game as the illustrations and animations. Saying that Music is a character here is an overstatement, i can't say enough how much this soundtrack contributed to transport me to this impossible place and making it real before my eyes (and in my mind). As much as the visual presentation is king, i've found myself thinking (and hearing) this soundtrack long after the game ended. Of course, i was very happy to be able to buy it and listen to after the game.The gameplay consists mainly in escaping the dangers lurking in the underground , manipulating levers and some mechanical devices, playing with light and darkness and the effects this has on what you find there. This mechanic is pretty straightforward and simple, specially at the beginning. It is a shame then, that for this same reason, for whats probably half of the game this turns out to be very repetitive (as a game mechanic) since the type of interaction doesn't change that much for a good part of the game. That is not to say its bad, but it becomes tiring somehow, and the game story (which it is there, from the beginning) somehow looses momentum and becomes perhaps, temporarily boring. This could be easily been avoided if there were just a little more editing, (as much as i love the game and its art, it would've been probably a more strong experience being a little shorter on those first levels).As said, the game world becomes compelling and you get inmersed in it and their characters the more you go in (and you get to understand what the hell is hapening with them!) The story starts revealing itself and suddenly you actually have a purpose there. You'll  even start to see a story on their paintings (which you will find there), you will also search for the secret rooms.... I finally loved this game to is core, it had a very strong and exciting ending too and after playing it i've just felt like giving my heart a full warm meal.

_childDocuments_.review: "Creaks" isn't the best puzzle game in the world but it is a very competent one. It knows it's weird and sticks to it. None of the puzzles are very difficult but at the same time, they aren't stupidly easy. They all take a little bit to figure out but it does always feel like you solved it rather than accidentally getting the solution.I would recommend it to anyone who wants a relatively light puzzle game that isn't too easy.

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a rank B+ (80-85%)Cool game - definitely worth a try!See my profile for more details about my reviews.Jakub Dvorský and his team Amanita strike again, with yet another beautifully hand drawn game. I have been a fan of Amanita since day 1 (Samorost as a freeware on internet 20 years ago), and I am very happy to see that they keep renewing their style and game concepts each time.Creaks is a bit like Amanita's take on the 2D puzzle platformer genre, with mechanisms reminiscent of original Oddworld games, some concepts and styles similar to Braid, and a bit of fantasy and story telling ala Limbo. If all of these titles are your jam, you will have a blast with this game. Admittedly it is not very long, if you are good at puzzles (which I am not) you will take less than 15 hours - and the story, while intriguing, does not end up being very satisfying or deep enough to ponder about. But the puzzles are very smart (while not obscure), the art is splendid and sumptuous, and like usual in Amanita the music is impeccable and mesmerizing - real, acoustic, analogic music! A very poetical, oneiric game - your typical Amanita!Easy controls, and many secrets in here, lots to search for a game that should keep you busy for a little week if you are a completist. At the end of the day, not a game you should remember in 10 years, so maybe get on sale (Amanita's games often are), but still a very good little game. is  on

What starts out as a boring little scene in a bedroom and some really pointless seeming actions turns into a wonderful puzzle game with a charming story and lovable characters from a slightly dystopian alternate world. _childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: While I was never a huge fan of Amanita Design, some of their titles have been and still remain among my favorite games. What I always admired about their projects is the playfulness and unpredictability, with the art and music coming close second. And pretty much every time they wanted to do something more puzzle oriented, I was far less interested with their critical darling Machinarium being my least favorite of the titles. Yet, I was curious about what Creaks would turn out to be – a puzzle platformer from the studio is a new direction after all. The results are not as fun as I hoped they would be.Since we are talking about an Amanita Design game, it’s not surprising that it looks and animates fantastically. It has a really cool style which looks great in motion and the soundtrack is as always great. This time, they’ve worked with Hidden Orchestra and the end result is something in-between of what that project does and what you usually get out of Floex’ work. Not among the very best works from the studio, but beautiful nonetheless. The story/mood is also somewhat familiar for the studio, mixing fairy tale, surreal and realistic elements into something that generally feels nice, but I can’t say that I cared about it this time around. Which isn’t helped by the fact, that this might be the most predictable narrative from the studio yet, with every sequence, every setup, every joke being obvious from the start.It wouldn’t be that important if the gameplay was great, but it isn’t. It’s not bad either, mind you, just surprisingly repetitive for an Amanita Design game. The puzzles are more or less designed around using light to your advantage, avoiding enemies and tricking them into becoming helpful. Which provides occasionally fun puzzles that genuinely feel exciting when they click, but a lot of the time they just work and you simply solve them and move on, without any joy from solving them. It would be fine if the genre of puzzle platforming wasn’t so full of varied interesting examples from older times and since its resurgence in 2010s. Creaks simply gets too samey and too tiresome, and none of the optional minigames help bring variety either. At least the game doesn’t last too long and never completely overstays its welcome.For a first attempt at a new genre, Creaks is a solid title for Amanita Design. It has some cool moments and it’s often cute, it’s music and visuals are great and it is at least somewhat novel with its core ideas. But it’s not great and can get a bit boring. If you’re absolutely in love with anything the studio does, give it a go some day, but if you were looking for a fantastic puzzle platformer, there are far more exciting examples.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite hard for an established developer to switch from their long-running genre, and even more rare for them to do it well. Amanita have successfully completed that shift with a great puzzle platform game.The previous two efforts, Chuchel and Pilgrims left fans (or at least me) wanting. Chuchel was more of an auto-clicker adventure than point-and-click adventure, and while Pilgrims was fun it was lacking the ambition of the classic Amanita works. Well, it seems their effort was channeled into Creaks- a delightful and entertaining puzzler with captivating music and Edward Gorey-influenced art. You will find yourself spending some extra time on each area taking in all the small details and interactions. While the puzzles provide a solid challenge, they never become overly difficult and the adventure is a decent length without overstaying its welcome. The story is told through visuals and mumbles in true Amanita fashion, and I won't spoil anything in this review.let's keep it short; I recommend this game at full price, and consider it an auto-buy on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed machinarium and I enjoyed this game.The puzzles well clever and fit well with the environment. To me, this was a nice well-crafted story that happened to have puzzles in it.The hand drawn scenes looked great and the character development via hand signs and noise worked really well for me.I wouldn't go in expecting mind breaking puzzles. I kept playing because I enjoyed how the story was being told.Well done
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by mentioning that I have enjoyed Amanita Design games for many years! I adore their blend of thoughtful puzzles, cute but dark storylines, and beautiful, relaxing music by Tomas Dvorak. Creaks is yet another example of their somewhat formulaic game type. I am thankful for this and look forward, as usual, to see what they put out in the future! C:
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful and lovely game! I got this game as a birthday gift and it was a delight to play. The art style is stunning and puzzles are very well thought. They start on the easy side, then new mechanics are introduced that require a bit more thinking without ever getting too difficult. Creaks is a puzzle sidescroller, and we have to figure out what actions to take to move forward. As we progress through the game, there are also paintings to find, some actually being a unique and peculiar optional minigame to complete. This is a really fun and well designed game. I recommend it if you like artful games with casual puzzle solving.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Creaks is yet another fantastic game by Amanita Design, were you have to guide an unnamed figure through a maze of beautifully drawn and animated riddles, full of a variety of characters, some more afraid of light than others. In this 2D puzzle-platform game you follow a story told without words trying to find your way out of the maze and help new friends.It's been extremely fun and I can only recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful adventure game with a lot of heart. The story is told without words, but it doesn't make it any less compelling. As you progress through the game you will find out more and more about who the inhabitants of this strange underworld are, are they friendly, what do they want, etc. And you progress by solving various puzzles spread throughout the game. The puzzles are pretty smart, but never impossibly hard. And they also vary every now and then, you might get a new character and new mechanics to play with, so it doesn't get boring. _childDocuments_.review: Another fantastic game from Amanita. This one departs from their usual point-and-click adventure format, and is instead a puzzle platformer, with monsters that move in set patterns and turn into inanimate objects when lights are shone on them.Has a wonderful "Haunted Mansion" sort of art style, where the backgrounds are crammed full of creepy knick-knacks and decorations, a huge number of which play some sort of spooky little ambient animation. _childDocuments_.review: Creaks is a a very simple puzzle oriented game. The simplicity is in its overall story arc, the puzzles themselves vary in difficulty but the mechanics are very easy to understand. The game progress is through one puzzle scene to another, building on mechanics previously learnt while introducing newer ones every once in a while. The simple story unfolds much more slowly and has a good conclusion. Overall a very well developed game, beautiful to look at, with an nice ambient sound track, but may feel a bit protracted. Recommend playing this game slowly, giving yourself some room to mull over the obstacles the game places along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I just completed this game and I loved it so much that I was a bit disappointed it didn't last longer. The challenges presented by the various puzzles and the difficulty progression are very well calibrated, in my opinion. Never too hard or too easy. Sure I was stuck more than once, thinking hard to solve some specific aspect of a scene, but this never made me enjoy the game any less or wish to quit it; on the contrary, I always felt stimulated to keep trying and, after I found a solution, I was already looking forward to the next puzzle. I only needed to search help for how one of the interactive paintings worked. Speaking of this, instructions along the game are always very essential, leaving the players to discover by themselves the exact mechanics of the various obstacles and mini games, like a puzzle in the puzzle; this can either be considered a virtue or a defect, depending on the player's attitude.I've read other reviews lamenting a lack of variety in the game, but I beg to disagree. I appreciated how each obstacle worked differently from the others, and how their different combinations have been used (if anything, I think they could have dared more and create more complex puzzles with more kinds of opponents at once). Also I loved the mechanic of the opponents being transformed into tools under the right conditions. Each puzzle is unique, and each of them taught me something that I could use in the following one while, at the same time, I had to find some new way to use the same simple rules to my advantage.In terms of variety, the interactive paintings also help a lot, because each of them is a different mini-game. One will hardly need to try them more than once to complete them, but they are a welcome break between puzzles. Along with the other paintings, they also provide more details to the game's setting. The "normal" paintings form narrations of some imaginative and mysterious stories, whose interpretation is left to the player.Visually speaking, the game is stunning. I really like the hand-drawn style and the animations, all the little animated details in the environment, the absurd architecture, and how the whole gigantic place where the action takes place seems a dream version of a Victorian museum (I love museums too). The environment has lots of personality.The story is far from mind-bending, in the end it's very linear; but this is actually good. The cutscenes are lovely and useful to gradually learn the plot without it being too obvious from the start. Without a single word needed, you get to understand each character's personality and role; and while you know them, you start to sympatize and actually wish to help them with their struggle to save their oniric world, providing a goal to the exploration and puzzle-solving.I didn't find any bug or performance problem. The whole game is structured in "scenes" that, once completed, can be selected and loaded to play them again, take screenshots, complete achievements etc.If you are looking for an action platformer; for a point-and-click adventure where you can interact with almost every element of the environment; for collecting items that you have to combine or, you know, finding keys that then you have to use with that door that is twenty rooms behind; for deep phylosophical themes and a complex plot: then this game is not what you are looking for. Otherwise, if what you see seems interesting enough, perhaps try it.

_childDocuments_.review: The hero through the night.The art loverThe soundtrack that was joyful tunes to my ears.The book that everyone's looking for.Another masterful banger by Amanita Designs. It's been so long since I enjoyed a puzzle game as much as I did this one. It's not the lame kind where puzzles are just puzzles for the sake of it. No, puzzles here matter because they are intertwined with the story which is the main focus. They are also logical, convenient, and make sense. I appreciate that so much in those kind of games. _childDocuments_.review: Creaks is a pretty good example of game as art. Like many games from Amanita’s catalog you’re going on a weird escapade in a strange new world. This one happens to take place inside and underneath the walls of a writer’s apartment. This adventure puzzle trip has that same unique drawing style and while descending the tower? building? dilapidated structure you’re going to meet some interesting characters while trying to progress and not die.Some of the puzzles do take a bit of thought to successfully traverse them and new elements are added as you progress it’s not overall too difficult to figure them out. I thought the story was simple but cute. While your character did seem a bit on the confused, not sure what to make of his situation, and a little bit scared I thought that added some charm to his overall dull personality. There were so many questions left unanswered or maybe I just wasn’t smart enough to intuit them. Either way by the end of the game I didn’t care and was just happy to finally exit this mysterious world. The music adds to the sometimes creepy atmosphere and there were times when it just stopped that made me feel uneasy but rest assured there’s no horror elements or anything to jump at. Overall I really enjoyed my experience in this strange and quirky area. The painting mini games were also a nice side touch. Showing past events of one of the bird characters.

_childDocuments_.review: What an fantastic little game! The game itself is beautifully drawn and soundtrack is awesome. A simple game, yet can be very tricky at times. _childDocuments_.review: A pleasant surprise, simple but interesting puzzle-platformer, looks and sounds amazing, not particularly challenging. [17/20⭐, 6h🏅, 2/5💡] Amanita is not exactly known for puzzle-platformers, so I didn’t know what to expect from this game. I was pleasantly surprised to find a pretty solid puzzle game, if not particularly innovative. You follow the unnamed PC as he explores a creak in his bedroom and finds a decrepit underground mansion. It doesn’t go into many details (and it doesn’t need to) and all story-telling is non-verbal. Eventually you find that the ridiculously ill-prepared bird-like inhabitants are trying to fight away a feline-like monster (although it seemed to me that the decrepit state of the mansion was not to blame on the latter). In a very nice touch, paintings scattered throughout the mansion tell the story of how the bird-like people ended up exploring the world. Visuals are beautifully hand-drawn as typical of Amanita, with detailed and unique backgrounds giving life to the different rooms of the castle. At first sight, everything looks bleak and decrepit, but as the game progresses there’s some beauty amid the desolation (again, typical Amanita). The soundtrack is one of the best I’ve heard in a game of this nature. The historical paintings are beautiful and creative. There is no voice acting as there are no dialogs. The game plays as a classic puzzle-platformer, you have to avoid some enemies while triggering levers and moving obstacles. The main mechanic is that enemies are afraid of the light, and if caught in a beam of light turn into… furniture that can be pushed around. In many ways it resembles , and also some touches of  and  due to the way you have to control some enemies. While simple, it provides for some interesting levels, but to be honest, it’s not as creative as those earlier entries in terms of gameplay. It’s also not particularly difficult, I don’t think I ever got stuck in a level. There are some timed puzzles, but nothing requiring much precision.Some of the historical paintings are interactive, and they provide a refreshing and amusing break from the main game.You can die, and you’ll just respawn in a previous checkpoint nearby. You can restart levels, and there are no gameovers. Progress is auto-saved in the checkpoints. It took me about 6h to beat the ~60 chapters. The game is completely linear, but you can always revisit previous chapters through the menu and there are multiple progress slots. Achievements are related to finding hidden rooms and completing the interactive paintings, nothing too difficult but force you to further explore the level (the gallery has hints about where to find missing paintings)s. These accumulate through playthroughs, so you can just revisit a chapter without having to restart the game. Replaying means repeating the same levels, but the game looks and sound great, so I can see this happening.

The difficulty is optimal - the puzzles require some brain cells to awaken but don't make you pull out your hair, but after a while they get a little repetitive. There isn't much of a story as well, so it's fitting that the game takes only about 5-6 hours to complete - otherwise it would get too tedious. Although I generally don't consider collectibles in reviews, in this game they felt quite forced and infantile, or in other words, like a filler that doesn't really add to the experience. Overall the game was pleasing enough for those 5-odd hours, but isn't worth dying for.

_childDocuments_.review: Creaks is something very different from these devs, but a nice change of pace. This is a strait up puzzle game, but with much of their usual charm in art and audio. I love how the soundtrack changes dynamically as you solve each step of a puzzle, even when those steps are more mental than mechanical. It gives a great feeling of anticipation as the final pieces click into place. It feels like there could a couple more mechanics or puzzles in the final act or even a rewarding final cinematic, but it's still satisfying seeing how everything is connected.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty fun little puzzle game.Knowing Amanita Design, their games are mostly very weird or abstract, and puzzle elements in most of their games are very funny but hardly make any sense. This title, however, consists of pure logic based puzzles. Of course, again in a totally unrealistic and weird setting as you'd expect.Art-style is cool as always. And, while the puzzles are quite logical, the environment and the objects you have to interact with are anything but. The first monster you encounter is a metallic robot dog than turns into a wooden desk drawer when shining light on it. So yeah, it's Amanita allright.In total there are four type of monsters, each having their own mechanics. Together with the usual bunch of levers, switches, lights, movable walls and floors, ladders and elevators, these make up about 60 puzzle areas. Most of them are simple enough to understand what has to be done although there were a few good head scratchers as well.Was really fun to play though and liked the challenge some of these puzzles were offering.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 7/10. It's more a puzzle game than an adventure. Beautiful artstyle topped with incredible soundtrack and sound design. The mechanics do alter a little bit after some time but before you reach that point you're already a bit bored from dealing with the same foes over and over, at least this was my case. _childDocuments_.review: Another whimsical game with gorgeous hand-drawn art from Amanita Design. Creaks does an excellent job of immersing you in an imaginative world hidden within the shadows. The game conveys its simple yet compelling story through detailed environments and expressive, unintelligible characters. The monsters perfectly embody the fear of the unknown lurking in the dark. The music is atmospheric and ominous but transforms to charming and upbeat when puzzles are completed. The puzzles themselves have a satisfying progression from simple to challenging without becoming frustrating. Lastly, a collection of endearing paintings are scattered throughout the rooms, and the interactable ones have silly minigames that never failed to make me smile.

_childDocuments_.review: Amanita design as usual at its best, if you like great puzzle games without huge difficulty but non-the-less challenging brain teasers this is up your alley. Amanita's unique fairy tail visual style, funny animations and interesting musical melodies will embark you on a fantasy journey to explore dream world behind your room's teared wall paper.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this!The protagonist feels relatable, despite not speaking at all. The other characters are also very likeable, because they are so "pure-hearted". Just like in Machinarium, which I also really enjoyed.The setting is a bit more mysterious compared to previous Amanita games. This makes the story evolve nicely, without being too predictable. The art style is fitting: Detailed and cute as you would expect from Amanita, but at the same time a bit more dark, feeding into the mysteriousness.I enjoyed the switch in control scheme (direct keyboard controls; previously Amanita did Point & Click).Sometime it is a bit finicky, especially when timing is involved. From key press to action there is a small delay (where an animation is played). This can make timing actions a bit tedious. Luckily this isn't needed that often, and dying is very tolerable due to very frequent checkpoints.As has been teased in the previous paragraph, Creaks is no point and click adventure. There is no inventory and almost no exploring. There is always just one way forward, but since it takes many turns, I wouldn't describe it as linear ;)I would describe it as Jump'n'Run puzzle game (though there is no dedicated Jump button). It doesn't really fit any genres I am aware of.The puzzle mechanics are introduced at a good pace without overwhelming the player. The puzzles themselves get a little bit challenging, but without being unfair or frustrating. I could solve all of them without help. Sometimes some extended staring at the screen or trying random things was required on my side. I would guess my longest solve time was like half an hour. Most of them I solved in half the time.In conclusion Creaks is a fresh new game by Amanita, building on their strengths but trying new things in a good way.Anyone who has enjoyed Machinarium will like this as well. If you haven't played any Amanita Games, but generally enjoy puzzle games or Point & Click adventures and the art style speaks to you, then you should also give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Breaking away from Amanita's previous point & click formula, Creaks delivers a challenging and beautiful logic game. With a grooving soundtrack and best-in-class art design, it really cannot be stressed enough how truly alive the environment feels. The scenery is the star here, and manages to communicate the utter strangeness of Creaks' world while still allowing the foreground characters to tell their own story. Some will be turned off by Amanita's new puzzle design--but if you're like me and appreciate the slow accumulation of mechanics onto a basic format, you will find your brain sufficiently teased.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased the game solely on the interesting art style, but got quickly captivated by the story. Quite a pleasant surprise! I finished the game in a couple of days.Concluding: Nice puzzle game with mesmerizing story and art style. Recommended!Score: 8/10Pro:+ nice visuals & art+ good mix of easy & difficult puzzlesContra:- nothing!
