_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended. Another brilliant game from Amanita Design, alongside Botanicula as a personal favourite. The integration of music within each puzzle is wonderfully done, with new themes appearing with each step towards the solution. The paintings, which range from fanciful inventions to pastiches of Gainsborough portraits, are very well done, and tell several stories in themselves, separate from the narrative of the main game. Sound design is great, once again illustrating that intonation and gesture are enough to tell a story. The puzzles are challenging but logical, often incorporating only a few elements and are almost never dependent on timing or control. Amanita games are wonderfully life-affirming, able to create tension without cruelty, long may they continue.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect to like this game because I never go for this art style, and I didn't totally love everything about some of the studio's earlier games. But I love this one!Gameplay consists of basically walking/climbing across a weird surreal landscape from puzzle room to puzzle room, with little bits of in-world cutscene every couple of rooms, wherein your character peeks through holes in walls as a story unfolds among other characters.As for the puzzles, they are really clever in their designs. They often appear very simple but have many steps to solve. Not super simple, but not too hard either. I'd probably say this is accessible to any age group and skill level. (If you really get stuck, most puzzles are brute forceable within maybe 10 minutes.) In terms of variety, all the puzzles are just the right length, and no mechanic overstays its welcome.There are a lot of really cute parts too with tons of personality. In particular some of the "interactive portrait" minigames were just so refreshing in their aesthetic creativity. Sound design is on point.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: what an enjoyable wee 2D adventure. the art style is truly something to be admired. i do enjoyed the torn down old steampunk vibes. like machinarium, despite the darker dreary aesthetic it is actually very lively in game. it also reminded me a bit of labyrinth. i like that you don't get thrown into the reality right away, it does build until it starts to get very interesting. it really made me feel like i was on a quest in another world. despite no voices you're sense of the storyline is not impaired. a lot is conveyed through the aesthetics, music, objects, architecture & the demeanour of the characters. what a compelling world to crawl into!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A very artistic puzzle platformer with an interesting story revealing itself as you play on. I found the puzzles to be pretty straightforward to begin with, and found myself a bit bored and in need of some more challenge. But as always, be careful what you wish for, I ran into some pretty mind boggling puzzles indeed - ow my poor brainy! Even though a lot of the puzzles require timing and step counting, and seem repetitive, there is somewhat great variation as you progress in the game. I thought this was a smaller game, but I spent a good 8 hours playing it through. I enjoyed it, and would recommend it if you are into these sorts of games. Will definitely check out some of the developers' other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I am so in love with what you guys do. The style, the locations, all the characters, music...  This fulfills my childish dreams and desire to explore - old houses like this one. Villains inspired by your grandparents' furniture. What a wonderful experience, thank you. Oh and all the puzzles were so creative and interesting to solve! I spent three good evenings in this world and will gladly come back...
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I love puzzle/problem solving games and this one has it all. The puzzles have a nice progression from easy to more difficult and the artwork is beautiful. The puzzles are very cleverly made and fun to solve with calm and relaxing music in the background. No killing, no button smashing time crunch obstacle courses. I recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: What a great puzzle game. Really nice puzzles and up to almost the end every now and then a different feature / mechanic is introduced and used. I also loved the art. It's a bit odd the first ~20 minutes, but when you got used to it, it's really great.The story / plot is rather simple, which is fine as the game clearly puts the focus on the gameplay (the puzzles). It's also told completly text and speech free just in little cutscenes, which (only) works for such a simple story.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really happy to see Amanita doing a game with consistent logical mechanics (as opposed to the "try everything with everything else" methodology that most adventure games tend to have). There's nothing groundbreaking here, but the puzzles are accessible yet clever, and the graphics and audio are kind of high quality work you'd expect from this studio. Definitely going to be one of the top puzzle games I recommend to my friends who don't seek these kinds of games out on their own.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another visually charming game. I am a massive fan of the sketchy art style and lends to the setting for the game very nicely.You follow a man who finds a hole in his wall that leads to another world, there he catches glimpses of these creates and flows them out of curiosity, before becoming entangled in their problem and you help to solve it. most of the puzzles come from trying to navigate your way though this underground world in search of the creatures yo catch glimpses of though floor boards and holes. The charming mini games with in he paintings I found to be very well done and enjoyable, adding something to the game play loop. even if they are simple I found them fun.The puzzles themselves can get confusion with trying to remember sequences, and revolves around trying to manipulate and control the enemy to position themselves in beneficial was for your self to pass. A neat gimmick is that the creatures, when exposed to light, become ordinary house objects. which make the enemy come across as cute and maybe innocent in their part, despite cause you harm if you do come across them out of the lights presence.Overall it a very enjoyable experience if you enjoy puzzles, this is one of the first 2d puzzlers I have played and thus cannot comment on he originality of the ideas and puzzles involved int he game, but to me they were unique and interesting and the style helps tie it all together.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Bro this game is legit one of the best puzzle games i've played till now. It took me 8 hours to complete because some of the puzzles were a bit harder to beat, but overall it's very cool. The art is very beautiful and i completely love the hero. too bad he doesn's have a name, i'll call him Robin. The paintings are so gorgeous and beautifully well  done that it makes the game 10x better. The moving paintings are incredible overall and the minigames from some of them are also very cool! keep going. would be cool to receive a sequel to this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Machinarium, but since then I haven't played an Amanita game that quite compare to it, untill now. They are very different in that Machinarium is a point and click game and Creaks is a puzzle platformer, but I still got the same vibes that Machinarium gave me with the art, the music, and the feeling of a world that I want to immerse myself in.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game overall. From the artstyle, puzzles amd the music, it was fun and entertaining experience. The game is worth it, especially so since I bought this game with a discount. However while the puzzles were interesting, that's all you basically do in this game - solve puzzles. The storyline is basically non existent and so if going from puzzle to puzzle sounds boring, this game might disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool puzzle game. I didn't get tired of the puzzles, the minigames are also well-timed and refreshing, finished the game in a single sitting. I didn't really liked the visuals in the screenshots/videos, and the controls felt clunky at first, but it really came together in the first 10 minutes. Best proof that the game is good is that all the negative reviews expected a story based adventure game instead of a puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Charming art and puzzles that are mostly intuitive. The only iffy puzzles are ones that are the instances of fiddly mechanics that have to be done one odd way to pass, but those are few and far between. If you want a puzzle game that isn't just clicking on patterns on a grid, this is a pretty good option.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: - The hand drawn + watercolor visuals are very charming. It's a great looking game- The music is alright. While not bad, it certainly isn't all that memorable- Counter to that is the sound design, which was actually quite good. The ominous titular creaking of the giant crumbling edifice you're exploring, the thunderous stomping of the creature that's stalking you, and even the subtle sounds of footsteps and light switches all contribute well to the game's gloomy tones- It's not all doom and gloom, though. Creaks does a good job of breaking the tension with occasional doses of humor. There's nothing laugh-out-loud funny going on, but the occasional chuckle is appreciated- There's not much of a story. You're just a guy living in a small apartment who climbs through a hole in the wall to discover a strange world full of monsters and puzzles. So basically Silent Hill 4- That isn't to say that Creaks lacks a narrative. You are trying to help the residents of the large building defend against the giant who keeps bashing up their house, but the whole story unfolds passively as you progress - The puzzles in Creaks are pretty good and just difficult enough during the later stages to be satisfying. Just take your time, pay attention to the  environment, and don't be afraid to experiment- In some of the longer puzzles where it's possible to die, the game does a good job of providing checkpoints. It was a nice little quality-of-life touch- Most of the puzzles revolve around positioning, sequencing, and timing. Nothing revolutionary, but still fun- Be sure to poke around for secrets if you're trying to 100% the game. None of them are too deviously hidden (I only missed a single one by the time I finished). Fortunately, there's a chapter select after you beat the game that allows you to go back for any you passed up- Amanita may only make one type of game (puzzle adventure games with amazing visuals, minimalist storytelling, and heaps of atmosphere), but they're damn good at it- Creaks is an ideal Steam Deck game. I played most of it while dealing with air travel. It did a good job distracting me from the cramped 737 seat- . If you're already into Amanita games, this will definitely appeal to you and is definitely worth playing. It's not quite as heartfelt or complex as Machinarium, but it's still a good time with some clever puzzles. Nice to look at, too
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely awesome.The artwork is great.The puzzles are just hard enough.  The mechanics are understandable, predictable, and the solutions are achievable.The bird civilization is weird.The painting minigames are whimsical, fun, and optional.The developers have done just such an amazing job.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are amazing. It would have been easy to softlock but some how the devs made it so you never have to reset a room. So keep trying! Loved the atmosphere of the game. Its got a certain charm to it. The hand-drawn backgrounds and characters give a cosy feeling to the player. This extends to the paintings which are the collectables in this game. The puzzles are also very interesting. Overall, it does what it does well. Another winner from Amanita.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine the wallpaper in your room starts peeling off and what you find behind it is a hatch that leads you to a deep underground tower inhabited by creatures of fantasy.  is a 2D puzzle game with gorgeous hand-drawn scenes. The story is completely driven by a non-dialogue narrative and takes around 8 hours to complete. The puzzles have just the right amount difficulty to them but can be quite repetitive. The game has a superb soundtrack along with fitting atmospheric background sounds and effects. The paintings are a work of art and the mini games are short and fun. All achievements can be earned in the first walk through, but the game gives you the option of revisiting any of the 61 scenes in case you missed anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: My first thoughts were: "Oh no, it's a platform puzzler. I hate them." But slowly, I developed a knack for this cute game. The puzzles are increasingly complex, it has mini-games in between, and the storyline is compelling. I like the eeriness and the feeling of disintegration they perfectly created. Friends of this software company recognize of course their signature style of steampunk and decrepit environments. Will buy also their next game, for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoyed Machinarium, Botanicula, Samorost and Chuchel, I had hopes for this game, and was not disappointed, love every moment of it.It is a puzzle platformer, however you do move in a grid, meaning you do not have to be pixel perfect to move around, which works very well for the puzzles. Speaking of the puzzles, they are quite simplistic, some of them requiring you to just move stuff around without other mechanics, of course, as you progress you unlock more mechanics and get more complex. Had no problem with them, even the one at the end, they stayed simple enough, and I don’t think I saw a puzzle using all mechanics at once, usually it keeps to 2-3-4 mechanics per puzzle (even after unlocking all mechanics). Some mini puzzles are also scattered throughout the game, serving a collectible purpose if you solve them, they are nice to have.Art style of course is another major focus, a beautifully hand drawn style like the previous Amanita games. Accompanied by good audio just makes it a charming game. The story however it can be summed up to: You reach an underground city (or better said village in the form of multiple buildings connected to each other), which is attacked by a monster, with the help of the avian inhabitants go and deal with the threat.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty sepia-tone / steampunk-like(?) aesthetic/style. Everything looks wooden, or like yellowed pages of an old book.Very enjoyable puzzles, with a timing-related element in many of them (thankfully the reflexes needed are not big).Silent protagonist, and the NPCs speak in gibberish, but everyone is very very expressive (even the enemies!) and communicates in a very expressive way, with facial and body language, despite there being no written text-dialogue.  Fun to learn motivations of the NPCs you encounter via the ways they behave.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I was surprised at how competently crafted this game was. It's not incredible, but it's a solid game. I was really intrigued by the last set of puzzles, but then the game just kind of ends abruptly. On the other hand, I didn't feel like anything was wearing out its welcome before moving on.The art is beautiful, scenery is memorable and characters are very expressive. Animations are fine. Puzzle designs are rock solid. Short and fun game from a small studio with a great soundtrack and unique style. I was hesitant at first but it grew on me pretty quickly. Definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Gorgeous aesthetics with fantastic hand drawn graphics and nice earthy chromatic palette.- Clever, creative puzzles that offer some challenge. Good difficulty balance. Not too easy, not too hard to solve them.- Well designed, unique characters.- Cool sound design. Characters' sounds are so funny.- Great music that accompanies you nicely without getting tiring.- Aside from the main path, it has some hidden things for you to discover.- Interactive paintings are awesome and offer a lot of fun.- Constant saves even at the middle of a puzzle save you of annoying time by doing again the same actions after a mistake.The bad- Although some new mechanics are added down the road, the core motif of lights, staircases and elevators remains unchanged and may feel a bit monotonous after a while.- All these small cut scenes don't really add anything, contrariwise I felt that they were often ruining the pace I was into by solving puzzles.- Most of these puzzle games don't even have a story so I'm not complaining, but a better plot could have given you extra motivation.- The sequence towards the end that you have to backtrack the whole game following that guy is one of the most boring things in gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Creaks is good puzzle game where you climb ladders, toggle on and off lights, avoid enemies, move trap doors, activate switches, play mini games, look at pretty art, and explore a mysterious world. The story is something you have to put together yourself as you play through. In Creaks you have to perform actions in the right order with the right timing to make progress forward. This game provides a unique experience considering if your patient enough for it. I personally had fun completing Creaks overcoming all the obstacles in my way. Here are some negative points in Creaks, I still like it despite its flaws.This game only has 5 enemies which might be a let down. Its how the enemies are used within a puzzle to make up for the lack of quantity.The art style might get boring after some time, so much busy work you can't tell what is what with the dim lighting.  Repetitive puzzles with gradual increasing difficulty with a few new things added here and there to mix things up.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: thought I might not enjoy it as much since it's mostly a puzzle game, but I really liked the art style so decided to give it a shot. the game's relatively short but charming, pretty interesting world which you explore through solving puzzles and occasional cutscenes and ladders, just ladders, gotta love the ladders; even without using my brain most of time I still beat the it, so that's great.so if you're not a big fan of puzzles you still might enjoy it, just don't expect exploring for longer than a minute or two without having to solve a puzzle with some exceptions.if you read it, hi, have a nice day :)
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Creaks is one of those games that make you wonder whether you are playing a game or watching a piece of art. You are taken on an unusual adventure in a weird and wacky world. Exploring the walls and underbelly of a writer's apartment building, encountering intriguing characters and solving puzzles along the way.While some of the puzzles require some careful thought, new elements are introduced gradually, and they are not overwhelmingly difficult. The story is charmingly simple, and your character's somewhat dull personality adds to the overall charm of the game. I did have some unanswered questions by the end, but it didn't detract from my enjoyment of the game.The music is haunting and eerie, which adds to the overall atmosphere of the game. There were moments when the music stopped, which made me feel uneasy, but there are no horror elements to jump at. Overall, I really enjoyed exploring this strange and quirky world, and the painting mini-games were a nice touch that added to the story of one of the bird characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this one for the most part. The puzzles were varied and pretty clever, requiring some good thought to solve (or maybe a few hints from a guide). There's nothing overly difficult or frustrating about the experience other than the fact that it drags on just a tad too long. I think had the game been an hour shorter i'd have enjoyed it a lot more. Still the environments, art and characters are charming enough to make you want to reach the ending, which was pretty cool. This isn't the best puzzle platformer by any means but it's one of the better ones. Not worth it at full price but it's an easy steal on a steep sale. I got it on sale in a bundle with machinarium for 10 bucks and it was well worth my time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: It's amazingly beautiful. I managed to solve almost all puzzles on my own although I didn't think I would when I first saw some of them, which made playing this a really satisfying experience.The types of puzzles are quite similar though, but that didn't made it boring luckily, as the beautiful art more than made up for it.I would recommend to get the game when it's on sale though.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A Beautiful, whimsical, hand-drawn Adventure.Creaks is a 2D-Puzzler with some very charming music and an equally charming hand-drawn art-style.The puzzles are of medium difficulty imo and get supplemented with the occacional, optional mini-game.Story wise this is just a whimsical little jaunt into a world below ours in need of some help, with some charming and quirky characters and creatures.I highly recommend this one, but perhaps in a Sale, as 20€ for a 5-6h game might not be worth for it for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: So unbelievably ‘meh’ you’d have to play it to understand. I… don’t really know what to say about Creaks… I played it through, found the secrets, and came to write this review... The most noteworthy thing about the game is just how  it is. You know how water tastes different when you’re not at home? Yeah, that’s the kind of flavour and personality Creaks  it had. If Creaks were a person, it would have worked in the same office for 14 years, and specifically spends its days off to get the same hair cut it’s had since school or buy shoes for work. Creaks would consider adding two drops of tabasco to its chilli con carne both spicy and adventurous. Creaks goes to bed at 7, and isn’t just monotone, its voice is so flat spirit levels are jealous of the accuracy, and flat earthers’ use it as evidence. I’d call the game dull, but that simply isn’t fair, , and assigning it any kind of personality is a disservice to mankind. As I write this, I’m genuinely dreading the rest of the review, finding things to say about this is going to be . I can’t give this the thumbs down… Being boring isn’t a crime, and Creaks did nothing wrong… It just didn’t do anything right either. I am absolutely positive there are people out there who would love this game… like shoe salesmen, or Tracey from logistics, or people who enjoy filling in tax forms.If you want to play a game merely for the sake of doing something while you do something else more important, this could be for you. This might pose a challenge to a child if you want to give them a puzzle game without much in the way of violence (though the death scenes aren’t pretty). If you want challenge, or stories, or mechanics to beat… then I’m afraid this has nothing for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A simple puzzler with what seems hand drawn graphics. Very much little details and tons of fun little things to notice that makes up for partly very simplified puzzles. Music in the game suits the atmosphere well, music on the collectible artwork within the game can be quite frustrating. Fun casual game to lose a few hours to. Suitable for children also. Could imagine playing this with or watching my niece play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Really great puzzle game with an awesome art style and music directions that makes you feel like you're exploring a completely different. The puzzles are challenging but never unreasonably difficult. The world map / scene selector was a great way to track my progress, and was really cool visually (tbh the whole game was great visually) - If this game is on discount get it now! (Make sure to explore for secrets while exploring the mini games are fun and add a lot of depth to the game)
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: 2-D platform puzzle (move the object) genre. Medium to hard difficulty. Expert level design, spooky character, and background level (in a cute way, not a horror way). The arts remind me of Roald Dahl's children's book. There is no text or conversation at all. However, it can transcribe what's happening in the game really well. Finish the game in 7.5 hours. Totally recommended for gamers who enjoy the puzzle 2D platform genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Graphically pleasing in a Braid kind of style. I liked the birds. The puzzles are not too complex and over time add new elements. I got knocked over by a goat! You will play this for the story, the athmosphere, the music, the all around feel, not for hardship or "most puzzle money can buy". Time well spend.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Halfway through and I just don't think this game deserves "OVERWHELMINGLY POSITIVE."  This game is fine and I'm not surprised that more people thumbs up it rather than thumbs down it.  Personally I wish the puzzles were more fun.  Even with this being a short game I found myself only able to play it in very short bursts before getting bored.  After about 2 hours of trying to stick with it it felt more like a chore than fun so I cast it aside for other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I love indie games, especially those that are made with as much heart and love like this one. It is especially lovingly and detailed created, with wonderful handrawn graphics and scenes. The game is a 2D platform puzzle scroller divided into scenes, there are obstacles you have to overcome to get to the next one. It's not always easy/obvious to redirect the biting dogs and flying jellyfish so that they don't get in the way and you can move on. You should not be afraid of trial-and-error. Makes already fun. A wonderfull game.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: While only being a few hours long, this game was definitely a treat. It's a fun and for the most part simplistic puzzle game that is more of a fun journey of art than anything else. An extremely relaxing experience and was wonderful to get through. If you like puzzle games that are sometimes a bit difficult, at least making you stop and think for a moment at times, but for the most part just relaxing with a bit of adventure (on a very linear, but fun path). I definitely recommend this to anyone wanting to just relax but be entertained at the same time.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent puzzle game with beautiful art.  Amanita is one of my favorite publishers, I look forward to more that they put out.  A story without words but subtle bits of humor, beautiful and unique (even trippy) creations and characters, and some degree of intellectual challenge.  Creaks is a bit different than their adventure games because it's a scene-by-scene set of puzzles, but everything is completely unique, and you get  a satisfied feeling when you complete each one.  Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another hit from Amanita games. The design is incredibly smart, with mechanics introduced gradually and in delightful ways. The art is charming, and the music completes the atmosphere. An entire story is told only through visuals, musical cues and beautifully animated characters and their expressions. The puzzles were at times challenging, but never frustrating, allowing for incredibly satisfying "ah ha" moments. I cannot recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Really amazing game so far!! I was hesitant about getting this at first but was convinced by the reviews on Steam to get it. Finally got it while on sale and the artwork in the game and concept are amazing.I didn't even realize that this game was Amanita design and their games never seem to disappoint. If you liked Machinarium, Pilgrims and the Samorost series, you'd be a fan of this game as well as the artwork and gameplay are on par with all of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as a Christmas present, and I am enjoying it a lot.It looks and feels a lot like Machinarium (by the same studio), but it is definitely more of a "puzzle platformer" than a "point-and-click adventure" (gameplay is fully keyboard/controller based).In some respects it feels a lot like Braid as well.  The puzzles are less mind-bending, but it has a similar atmosphere, with hand-drawn backgrounds, and a lush, responsive, background musical score.)The background music is responsive in a way I haven't experienced before.  Puzzles are "environmental", meaning you are controlling physical things in the environment like buttons and switches, and often trying to direct or avoid "bad guys". Yet the game subtly tracks how close you are to solving a puzzle, and the music gradually builds as you work out steps of the puzzle, often breaking out in full in a satisfying way when you fully solve a puzzle or make a discovery.The paintings throughout the game break up the environmental puzzles a bit.  Many contain mini games, others are simply interesting to turn the key and watch subtle animations and ponder about.Overall it's a great experience and comes across as labour of love by the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of Amanita games. The illustrations never cease to provide visual enjoyment and the illustrators provide such a richly designed world to explore.  Some of the in-game painting puzzles are anxiety causing but none-the-less super fun to play.  I love how they are constructed to look like little leavers and built of jaggedly constructed metal and paint. You'll finish the game missing half of the wall puzzles and end up wondering where they were hiding. (Honestly, I have no clue!) Lots of crevices to explore in the Creaks.  Easily completed in 10 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game. I'm not normally a puzzle game person, but this is great. The hand-drawn style is pleasant to look at even for long periods, and the puzzles are hard enough to make you think, but not so hard that you'll always be looking up solutions. The game took around 5 hours to complete one playthrough that was not a 100% playthrough.Pros:-visual style is cozy-music is pleasant-the setting is a little surreal, but only enough to get under your skin-enough variety in the puzzles and rooms that you don't feel like you're in the same place for the course of the game-story is interesting, if a little sparseCons:-sometimes the puzzle mechanics aren't as clear as they could be. Was only once or twice, though. -nothing else. Normally I can at least say "a little laggy" or "a bug or two," but this game is polished
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Really smart and creative puzzle platformer with beautiful sketch style hand drawn art and a unique interesting world to explore. Gameplay has some similarities to older puzzle platformers like oddword (navigating room puzzles based on enemy ai rules) but with more focus on methodical puzzles vs twitch timing/action. Some puzzle mechanics later on also remind me of The Swapper (aligning clone of yourself).Overall a great game with puzzles that are just the right challenge and make you feel smart when you solve the. Really enjoyed my time with it. Highly recommend for puzzle platform fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: The artwork in this puzzle game is really interesting to look at.  The sounds and music are subtle, and are also very interesting.  I'm really impressed at how much thought must have been put into these puzzles to make them challenging, but not too difficult.  Also, the puzzles are complex enough that it seems that one could accidentally trap oneself permanently, but the designers were careful not to allow it.  I've played for 17 hours so far, and I believe I'm about 3/4 of the way through.  I had to cheat with a "walkthrough" guide for 3 or 4 of the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly my favourite Amanita game to date. As always wonderful artwork, music, and puzzles that progressively becoming more and more challenging without ever veering too far into the frustrating side of things. Add to that an interesting world to explore and a charming cast of characters and the whole package becomes a very easy recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A weird reversal of the usual amanita design formula; this game more than a few puzzles that take some thinking, but it's all framed in an extraneous and uncompelling veneer. The art design is not only unnecessary for the puzzles or atmosphere, it feels excessive and kind of stuffy and unpleasant. That said, some of the puzzles are good, the difficulty is a little higher than normal for this studio. The game is ultimately somewhere between unremarkable and frustrating though (other than the soundtrack, which is fantastic). Goat mechanic sucks, by the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Just a really solid and creative puzzle game. The puzzles were the right difficulty, required some thinking but I wasn't stumped for long. I loved the music swells when you completed a puzzle. I enjoyed the story too, it felt warm and nostalgic like an old kid's book.Played Offline on the Steam Deck; took around 6 hours to complete
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: "Creaks" is a beautiful hand-drawn game that is able to tell a nice story without using any words.Very easy controls, and not too hard puzzles (if you are thinking too much, then it is not the right way to solve the puzzle).The intricate design is very impressive, because you can actually see the connection between all the rooms. Sometimes it is confusing to find out where to go to, since you are able to return to previous rooms and there are no indications of the right path, but in the end you are able to find your way.Another thing I must mention is the details put into the paintings that you find, some with a different game inside it, and others just nice to watch.But IMHO the golden prize goes to the fact that the enemies turn into furniture when the lights are on them. Pretty interesting, because our imagination makes us believe that when things are in the dark/shadows they look like alive, but in reality they are nothing more than our own regular stuff just standing there.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A charming puzzle game with beautiful visuals and a great soundtrack.I'd recommend this game to anyone looking for a /casual/ platformer puzzle game. The puzzles didn't feel redundant and the gradual difficulty wasn't discouraging. My only gripe is that the game is somewhat short, even with the time it takes to solve puzzles. I wish there was more to discover about the world and whatever lore there is , but there's only so much that can be told through squawking and pantomime.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant at first, for the artstyle and the gameplay of a claustrophobic maze thriller somewhat deviated from the studio's familiar trippy fun puzzles. However, I got quickly drawn in by the ambiance of mild suspence and highly creative riddles within an intriguing fairytale narrative. And by the end, it is once again a trully unique, one-of-a-kind cultural heritage from Amanita Design, bless their souls.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning work, as always. Can't really decide what was more beautiful, the art or the music.The puzzles were fairly easy but entertaining, there was no repetition by mixing already existing elements and the mini games kept me longing for more. As fast as I took a dive into this fantastic universe, the journey ended. I just wish there was more to explore in this world. another adventure (maybe hiding behind the next shelf.) 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It was great and frustrating and fun all in one! There were times where I wanted to uninstall it because I just couldn't solve a piece of the puzzle, but I made it through and was so happy at the end. I am going to have to play it one more time because I missed some of the achievements and couldn't beat the Picture games. Thank you for creating this fabulous piece of work! I enjoyed it thoroughly!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Nice puzzle game. The visuals are good, I like how each mechanic was used to make compelling puzzles, though I'd have liked if the last puzzle was slightly more interesting.Riding the elevator up the all levels at the end was a nice touch. Same with seeing one of the bird listening to music with a painting, just like the main character can.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: As  a big amanita fan , This Reminds me mostly of a mix between the gobliiins series and the lost vikings (both absolute gems of the past) . initially a bit unimpressed with the "much gruesome dying" ,  left it for a while, then started appreciating the dark central european humour because the drawings and animations are just so well done. it is still often disturbing , but the artwork is breathtaking, the scenery is amazing and the story gradually develops into a full on another unique Amanita universe design . but the puzzles are absolutely of the "i died one last go" type. 8.5/10 so far.  a lot to discover left.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun puzzle game!  The world is unique, the art is amazing, the music is engaging, and the story feels like an interactive graphic novel.  The whole tale is told through the visuals.  Some of the puzzles are tricky, but none felt impossible.  Finding the hidden rooms for the achievements gave me a fun second play through.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another great puzzle adventure from Amanita Design. Unlike other games I’ve played by the game developer (Samorost, Machinarium, Pilgrims) Creaks is not a point-and-click adventure, yet it’s no full-on platformer either. The player primarily moves their character left and right along floors and platforms in strides of predefined length (this is intentional for the purposes of certain puzzle mechanics), as well as up and down ladders — there is no free-form movement nor any real physics involved.As with games like Machinarium and Samorost, it’s not so much about the challenge of the puzzles but rather their ingenuity, how smoothly they guide the player from puzzlement to understanding; nearly every puzzle has that wonderful “ah-ha” moment where the key to the lock of the problem clicks so nicely into place.The game is also visually appealing with the similar cartoonish, hand-drawn style one finds in Machinarium and Pilgrims. There is also much to look at: the maze of ladders and platforms on and along which the main character travels are surrounded by a myriad of intriguing objects and architecture, much of which contains familiar impressions, recognizable shapes. And while most trinkets in the game’s background can’t be interacted with, if one looks carefully, and with a bit of patience, small and amusing movements of life, in what was assumed inanimate, can be glimpsed.In following the tradition of all games by Amanita Design, Creaks tells a story with no dialogue, but rather through select images it reveals to the player (should they be observant enough to discover them) and cutscenes where other characters gesture and speak animatedly in a garbled sort of nonsense language that is typically meant, above all else, to elicit a laugh or two.Creaks is an artful adventure with well-crafted puzzles, a great soundtrack, and lots of appealing visuals that are sure to please most indie-adventure enthusiasts.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: First i thought that the Creaks will be a lot like machinarium, eye-candy "escape room" kind of puzzle game (don't get me wrong machinarium is amazing). That was somewhat wrong. Creaks is beutiful game with very (very) good soundtrack and pretty well made standard puzzle game with somewhat good progression.but to say it was challenging? no. sadly there was little challenge (elementary school puzzles).otherwise it is great game. i wont say much more than that.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A truly enjoyable platform puzzle game, with beautiful art and a slowly unraveling form of storytelling. Starts off nice and easy, but will eventually make you scratch your brain on how to solve certain puzzle scenarios. If you are into games like Another World, Oddworld, Heart of Darkness and if you loved previous adventure games from Amanita Design (such as Machinarium), you should definitely play this. A good little trip, which can be finished in two or three solid days of gaming. After that you can feel inspired and carry on with your life. Top!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: At full price, $19.99, this game is over priced.  I'm not a very heavy gamer and it took me between 11 and 12 hours to complete.  Somebody who has more gaming experience would probably finish this game much faster.  The game was interesting and enjoyable.  But it was short and does not have replay value.   I am recommending it, but not for the price of $19.99.  The price point for the game should probably be more like $1.99.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Love Amanita Design's work, love Machinarium, but this one is... incredibly boring. It only took me 15 minutes before feeling the need to check from Youtube if the rest of the game was going to be like the beginning. Yup... exactly like the beginning, only very very slightly different and harder. Feel sorry for what I paid for this game. Hand-drawn graphics look amazing though I have to give them that. Too bad they couldn't come up with a more interesting idea for the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Great art and nice atmosphere.Puzzles were hard enough to take minute to solve with no game stopping brain busters.One minus for the end.There is no "final exam" so to speak. Ideally a (puzzle) game should test all you have learned for one last time. Here the last puzzle of the game is nothing noteworthy and It left me expecting that the "thing" you pick up after that would be used as a puzzle element for the last leg of the game, but after that you just walk to the end and use it once and that's it.I'm going to guess that time and/or money ran out since the last area was so short.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This might be my favorite Amanita game yet, which is high praise.  This is much more 'puzzle platformer' (emphasis on puzzle) and much less 'point and click adventure' than their previous titles.  The puzzles have a great sense of logic, and a well paced series of new mechanics being introduced.  They generally seem to stump me for just long enough to feel smart when I get it, but not long enough to get frustrated.As always, the audio design is incredible.  They do a wonderful thing where they play a satisfying jingle when you 'do the thing' that is the lynch pin in the puzzle, right at that moment where you feel smart, but before the whole solution actually plays out.  It feels like mind reading, it's great.  And of course the art is stellar.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a big fan of puzzle games but if you're in to it you shouldn't miss out on this one. It's not a very hard game. The artwork is, as we are used to from this developer, stunning.I do prefer Machinarium over this one though and since I'm not that in to puzzle games I'll give it a 6.5/10 but for puzzle fans it's probably a 9.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Wow!  This is one of the best; okay, the BEST puzzle game that I have played in the past ten years!!  I love the simplicity, the complexity, the graphics are so storybook!!  This is an amazing Game!  I recommend for anyone wanting to zone out and forget the world they are in for a while and enjoy Creaks!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short arthouse game - the music, the storybook-like art and the whole ambiance are supremely attractive; the puzzles get repetitive quickly however (just the dogs and the lights over and over again). A great curiosity to have in your collection for aesthetic value (the musical paintings alone are amazing), but the gameplay is a chore. Not the best game form Amanita, they set a very high bar for themselves with their previous entries.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and beautiful puzzle game, made with lots of love for the detail. The puzzle elements are not overly new or original, but quite clever and enjoyable nonetheless. I also liked the setting. Very creative, being a mix of cute and a bit creepy. A nice soundtrack added to the atmosphere. All in all a perfect game for some bedtime puzzling on my dearly beloved Steam Deck!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable game to spend some time and watch an interesting story and incredible arts.It is generally a puzzle game where you have to move from screen to screen by discovering your surroundings and using things (mostly ladders and switches) in clever and sometimes timely manner to avoid enemies and certain death, of course.The riddles are logical and in general quite fair.Still, a few of them were a brain teaser to me and fun to experiment.Also, hunting for paintings and secret rooms is a neat extra feature, but still not too difficult to solve.This game is made for using keyboards or gamepads rather than a computer mouse.Currently it seems like there is support for some sort of gamepads (via settings menu), but I can't tell which one, as mines do not work, unfortunately.Perhaps only some X-box controllers work or so.... I think it would be better to have a configurable settings menu here - or maybe my controllers are just broken.Nevertheless, fun game. I am looking forward to see more stuff from the developer studio in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it when it came out and immediately got a refund.I was very disappointed.It is nothing compared with Machinarium.In Machinarium every scene was unique and a piece of art.In Creaks every room looks the same.In Machinarium you have to solve different kind of puzzles.In Creaks every puzzle is the same.So I bought the game now in sale.Without comparing it to Machinarium it is ok, not good, but ok.The puzzles are quite easy. The story is not the best.The character is ok.Almost at the end of the game the surrounding is getting more divers and beautiful. They missed so much potential, why did they not do these wonderful things already during the beginning of the game, why not making the puzzles more interesting, why not different kind of puzzles, whyyy.Buy it in a sale (especially if you like ladders, elevators and dogs) and it is a nice little game to distract yourself.I hope that they will produce something as great as Machinarium, Creaks - unfortunately - is not it.:josef:
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. I really hope they make a 2nd game. My girlfriend and I played this game and she didn't comp[lain once so that says something. I noticed the puzzles got progressively harder for the first 15-20 scenes so then kinda plateaued a bit and maybe got a bit easier but still an amazing game. The artwork is off the chain. PLEASE MAKE A 2ND ONE GUYS!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I was surprised by how much I like this game. It has way more content and narrative than Amanita's other games. The art is creepy and fun, the story is silly and confusing but keeps you wanting to pick up bread crumb after bread crumb to see where things go, and the puzzles span a healthy range of difficulty, but were generally not frustrating. If you can't project the exact steps you need to take to solve a puzzle, you can just play around until you understand the mechanics and the level layout better. The game also does a good job changing up the types of puzzles so you get variation - and I really recommend getting to the very bottom of the house/island, just to check it out :)
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another masterpiece by the game developers. Attention to details, the imagination, the subtle emotions of the characters is truly award-worthy. The ending is so cathartic! If it were a movie, it would have been the first good movie I saw in a long time. The puzzles are increasingly but also enjoyably challenging. I needed the walkthrough a couple of times towards the last 1/3.  I am especially glad no insects were involved (as I have a phobia of them).You can count me in as the buyer of the next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable puzzle game, easy one to pick up if you have a few minutes or a few hours. The story is told simply through gestures and pictures. The pieces of each puzzle are introduced individually as clues to build upon the next puzzles. I really enjoyed the game and think anyone who enjoys logic puzzles will too.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: -Beautiful, imaginative hand-drawn environments (with a childlike imagination)-Dynamic music that syncs with the puzzle-Hidden, interactive art pieces in-between puzzles - a nice change of pace-Challenging, but not frustrating.  It is simple enough to problem-solve but not too simple to the point where it's obvious.  The puzzles are very well thought out and the mechanics are leveraged in creative ways.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely puzzler adventure in a similar vein of Inside, Limbo, and Little Nightmares. The amount of illustration is amazing--every nook and cranny has detail--and there is similar care in the rest of the game. Music, mechanics and above all the pacing of this game is top notch, though it's short enough to not wear out it's welcome. Understandable why it was the Czech game of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I love puzzle games. In this game, you need to figure out a sequence of reactions to get through the rooms as you follow the source of music. There is a mystery that begins to unfold as you progress. The best part was interactive paintings (mini games) and the sequences didn't get old, or boring. It was bitter sweet to finish this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: The art design is impressive, but the gameplay is tedious. Progressing requires solving abstract puzzles, but they felt repetitive and like a chore. The locations look interesting, but I didn't get to interact with them, instead I was stuck climbing ladders and flipping switches to avoid exactly two types of robot enemies, over and over. I didn't feel involved with the story either, because the cutscenes are just about these bird people doing random things, while the protagonist merely watches them from the other room.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Let us get the elephant out first: Creaks isn't a great game, not even a good one. Gameplay mostly entails solving simple puzzles. Puzzle solutions are evident instantly, as there are just few puzzle elements with limited interactions and the puzzles always play straight - you never need to think outside the box. Puzzle size peaks during mid-game, to the point where performing the steps for a trivial puzzle solution becomes tedious. Towards the end, puzzles get shorter again, there is no actual climax in difficulty and no final challenge. With just five hours of gameplay (including the backtracking for all achievements), Creaks is also rather short for its calling price - but were it any longer, the gameplay would seriously get on my nerves.Yet, I can't get myself to give Creaks a negative review. There is just so much love and polish in this game. There are the hand-drawn, tile-less, unique backgrounds full of oddities and easter eggs. The charming animations. The sound and music design, which subtly reacts to gameplay events. The surreal mood. Last but not least, I love the whimsical monsters, the goofy bird people and the klutzy main character. I can wholeheartedly recommend Creaks as a piece of interactive art - even though it is not much of a game.Short supplement after I have watched my significant other do a full playthrough: You won't probably recognize this if you have played them Zeldas and Monkey Islands and so on, but Creaks is a rather good introduction to puzzle games for novices. The - by my standards - simple puzzles are nevertheless expertly crafted to teach all necessary tools and strategies you need for solving them, one by one, without tedious experimentation or leaps of logic.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an extremely strong aesthetic, both in the visual and music department. The music is unique in that it is improvised on the spot, with various tracks added and subtracted as you complete each level. It's a rather complicated process, and there's a rather interesting documentary on youtube about how they created it.  First I will say what I did not like.   All of the puzzles in the game revolve around the titular Creaks (the creatures that become normal objects when light is shone on them). While they did do some creative puzzles with them (especially later on in the game), it does get somewhat stale after a while, especially since the use of each individual Creak is not evenly distributed at all (for example the Male coatrack is rarely used after the female coatrack is introduced, and the goat is only used in one area).  The game is very linear and had very little backtracking. This is a problem in that you don't really get to appretiate all the work that went into drawing each individual screen, especially the "transition" screens between puzzles. The only "secrets" are a few of the interactive paintings you can find that are hidden away, which are usually as easy to find as "go through this wall that looks solid in this transition room".   Additionally, some of the ambient details got rather grating after being stuck on a puzzle for a particularly long time. What I mean by this is often random background objects in a room will move as if they're alive (an early example is the garden shears you see once you enter the attic). Some of them make repetative noises that become somewhat annoying when trying to solve a particularly hard puzzle (the laughing skeleton in one of the attic puzzles is a good example, as well as the creepy moaning face that takes center stage in a late-game level). This next part contains spoilers for the end game. It is also the biggest flaw with the game.   Now for the good stuff. Creaks has a very imaginative world and I LOVE how everything looks. It's the kind of game where I wish I could see more of how everything works and learn the backstory to everything. I attempted to parse information on the backstory through the paintings and various background details but I couldn't parse much. The graphics are definitely my favorite part of the game. Additionally, the way that each Creak is introduced and the gimmicks associated with them are integrated incredibaly organically (for instance the Dogs waiting on whatever side of a ladder you last left from), and I was rarely confused how each Creak worked (except the Goats but I did eventually learn their gimmick). It's also a fair bit longer than Machinarium, which it looks the most similar to graphically.Overall I'd say Creaks is a fairly good game. It has interesting puzzles that while not as varietous as Machinarium or Samorost still manage to be engaging. The graphics are beautiful and every scene feels unique. The music is one-of-a-kind and will get stuck in your head in the best way possible. And it's fairly long as well. And while the paintings aren't the best form of replay value, it does actually have replay value, unlike some of Amanita's other games.  This is the type of game you play once, then play again a few years later when you can't quite recall all the details. I give it a solid B!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: that's a very interesting game. It has beautiful graphics, amazing soundtrack, fascinating storyline, creative puzzles and intruiging different creatures. It's a logical puzzles game but it aslo has a few minigames. I especially love the graphics: different rooms, humanoidal birds, monsters and collectible paintings. The story is understandable but u can make different theories about the whole place and history between humanoidal birds and human beings. What i also find very cool is that u can play any scene u want after finishing it and u can see where it is located in the building which contains the scenes. And off course puzzles are the best, they have interesting mechanics and they change/improve during the game so that u can never get bored with them. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: - Beautifully presented puzzle game.- The graphics are stellar with really charming hand-drawn characters and backgrounds. The characters are all really nicely animated and lively, lacking that uncanny paper-doll feel that some indie studios have. Good stuff!- There is sparse music and nice sound design - everything fit well within the game.- The puzzles were just on the right level of difficulty for me, some head scratchers where lots of mechanics are combined but nothing frustrating.- The game is fairly short, but neither feels too short nor outstays its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game during sales. A chill, whimsical, "short-ish" (about 9 hrs + maybe another 1 hr to look for and complete all the hidden achievements) puzzles/brain teasers kind of game. I love the art direction and the music score is great. There is a story and plot of sort to move the gameplay forward but there really isn't very much to it.For the puzzles/brain teasers themselves, there are about 50-60 "rooms", are not super hard but I do enjoy them and some are quite clever. However there are maybe only 5-6 "types" of puzzles and you are solving 50-60 variations of them, the game can feel a bit "limited" and repetitive at times. Besides the puzzles "rooms", there are also small interactive mini-games paintings (about 8-10 of them), nothing too complex, littered across the game that adds a bit more whimsical detail and variation.Ranking Creaks to other similar puzzles/brain teasers games I played, I would rate them as such:Top Tier - Inside, LimboMid Tier - Creaks, DARQ (excluding the dlcs. Those are a little too convoluted for me)Low Tier - Little Nightmares (too simple unless you are age 12 and under)Conclusion: If you enjoy puzzles/brain teasers sort of games and have already played Inside and Limbo, I can certainly recommend you get and try Creaks during good sales.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Like all Amanita Design games, it’s wonderfully weird in its setting with great animations full of character and odd little details.  It’s an intriguing concept and well executed with some good puzzles, but it’s quite slow and light on the game play front, although it did grow on me the more I played of it.  Their signature sounds / soundtrack and the interactive paintings are superb in their ingenuity and style, but it’s not as humorous or charming as their other titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Amanita Design never fails to impress, but even by their standards, Creaks is the best thing they've ever done. It's not a puzzle platformer, although there are sequences which need quick reflexes. Instead, it's like playing a lavishly designed comic book. Kind of like a Metroidvania without the combat and the map, but much more imaginative and fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: The game is an above-average puzzle game. Beautiful visuals, good soundtrack, a great concept, large space for your own fantasy. Judged as a stand-alone it is a great game, especially from an indie studio!Judged in the context of other Amanita Design games, however,  it is definitely one of the weaker games. Where is the interactive background? Where are all the other avians? the hints of their lives? Where is the point-and-click? The repairing? The growth of the young man you play as? The climax of the final moments? If you play Creaks, do not expect an AD game, you get a puzzle solver with light horror themes and that's it.The puzzles themselves are not overly difficult. The separate mechanics are introduced gradually, a lot of them is a logical continuation of some of the previous ones, such as the Drawerdog - Chairgoat parallel, the two Coathangers (What even was that kissing scene?), and my all-time favourite: sliding bookcases as stepping platforms. The puzzles can be solved by children even before they can read, as there are no text-based ones, but are solid enough to give a fairly clever adult, which I consider myself to be, a pause to sit and think "Alright, so if I light this one up..." (However, the electrician responsible for this whole mess ought to be sued. The architect of this birdhouse just as well).I would like to highlight my favourite bit in the game: The gym level, which is a Czech visual pun, given the falcon picture featured.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Had my eye on this game for a bit and I'm so glad that I finally got it. The art style and music sets the mood of the game so beautifully. The quirky sense of humor is will sneak up on you and make you smile as you wonder through this castle that I swear that Howl himself cast a spell or two to bring things to life. This game, in my opinion, is a playable masterpiece. I will be playing this over and over again.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: That's a really nice adventure game with perfect-balanced puzzle and breathtaking art work. I love the idea from the Pareidolia tendency. Don't expect from it too much, however, the way to tell the story is really boring, the number of character is too small and the puzzles' designing is iterated. It is not like Machinarium
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Amanita is back with another gem! Original visuals and puzzles with catchy music. Although Creaks is much more puzzle-wise then other Amanita games but puzzles are not that hard and game progression feels smooth. If you like Amanita games you should definitely consider Creaks and if you also like puzzles then it is a no-brainer.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Simple puzzle-platformer with emphasis on atmosphere (but very little story). The art has appeal but the puzzles are lacking, and the movement-timing requirements on many of them are annoying and work against the otherwise "mellow" atmosphere. The game is too long for what it offers as well. "Braid" is better all-around.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game by Amanita. I love all their stuff. This one has a bit different look to it but still had some fun, challenging puzzles. I was able to beat the game in about 9 hours. I got all the achievements accept for 2 in my first run through. Would definitely recommend, just wait for it to go on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Remember Machinarium? Differences:- Creaks is more of a classic puzzle game with rules based on characters, not a 'find an item and see where it fits' adventure like most of Machinarium- For that reason, Creaks has better replayability. I've beaten it more than 3 times already. Probably will again soon. - Josef in Machinarium was the perfect mascot/main character--very unforgettable. If you didn't know, they have a plushie of Josef in the Amanita store. Go buy one now. The main character in Creaks... well he doesn't have the same adorableness of Josef, but it doesn't take away from the gameplay at all. Although I will say, if Amanita releases merch with the Creaks drawer dog monster, I'm buying it immediately. Similarities: - Excellent art style. The detail in the Creaks world is incredible.  - Excellent music. Fits the feel of the game perfectly. If you are like me and ended up listening to the Machinarium soundtrack long after you beat the game, you would probably like Hidden Orchestra's arrangements on Creaks. Thank you Amanita for introducing me to artists I would probably never have been exposed to otherwise. Verdict: - If you liked Machinarium, buy Creaks right now, don't wait for a sale- If you have never heard of Machinarium, go over to that page, buy that. Come back in two weeks and buy Creaks. You're welcome
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, this game isn't on par with masterful gems like Machniarium, Samrost and Chuchel. Controls are wonky, and puzzles are repetitive. I may even say I don't like the artwork. That said, game somehow lost the saves and  I just can't make myself to start all over again, which would not be a problem for Machinarium or Samrost. I played those games over and over again.As a big fan of Amanita, and two 5y kids to whom Chuchel, Gnome and Little robot are big part of their lives in this pandemic, I deeply suggest not going into dark direction. Your artistic power is not there.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful way to challange your mind.It's basically puzzle game where you have to first realize the mechanics of your surrounding and then find out how to use these to progress. It's split into "levels"/scenes, plus mini-games in form of Interactive Paintings and the story in between that glues it all togheter is really magical.The game is at the same time kinda creepy, cute and funny and I really enjoyed it. If you love puzzles this is game to try. All "levels"/scenes through the game took me almost 7 hours and I feel now little sad it's over.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Nice complex puzzle game with an excellent and mysterious story-line. Next to that it also has a good art-stylethat fits the game really good. I strongly recommend this game and other games from the Amanita Design developers! You can get it for a really low price for a game this quality so waiting for a sale isn't necessary.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: If you like clever platformers with amazing graphics and some puzzles, this is a great game for you. I was very impressed by the beautiful scenes and music and charmed by the young man who makes his way through this enormous structure that looks like a really big house floating in space. I would have liked to have a bit more help at the beginning of games - some kind of guidance about what the object of the game is, and initial advice about navigating rooms. I find with games like this that I lose interest in them when moving forward involves talented mouse and keyboard work and excellent timing. I'm just not the kind of person that finds it rewarding to repeatedly die to learn a new pattern, only to have a completely new one to learn in the next scene. If the pattern is integral to the storyline, I can hang in there. But in my opinion this game didn't do enough of that. Still, I think for those who like this style of game, they will love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. I played it with my gf and we both found it to be quite fun and interesting. Nice puzzles. I found the details and ideas behind this game quite creative, I hadn't played one like this before and I really enjoyed it. The visuals and animation were very nice. I loved it, it's among my favorite ones of this genre I'd say, together with Inside.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Every single game that this company produces is gold. The animation style? Beautiful. The gameplay? Simple to understand, easy to use controls. The story? Charming as always, and you'll end up attached to every character. Creaks isn't a super challenging game by any means, but there are some puzzles/scenes that make you think for a while before finally figuring them out. It's not long, but it is a fantastic game to play if you want something pleasant and low-pressure. I bought this during a sale, but I'd be willing to pay full price. The art alone is worth it to me! Overall - GREAT GAME!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Created with unique hand-drawn art style,  is, to me, a refreshing delight to the puzzle platformer genre (with heavy emphasis on ). The player leads the protagonist into a subterranean labyrinth full of puzzle rooms, in which creativity and repeated experiments must be tried in order to proceed from one level to another. During your adventure you will come across a set of collectibles: the paintings, some of which offer you a mini-game--a well-deserved break from continuous brain usage. Oh, right. And our protagonist is all too adorable. Look at him scratching his head in confusion when he knows not of what to do. A Adorable and mortally fragile, yet so stupidly brave. I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This is one perfectly crafted gem of a game.From the superb artwork, the flawless original music and immersive, gorgeous sound design, to thebrilliantly conceived and quirky humour which made me smile throughout.I can't praise this enough and though I rarely write anything like a review, this is one that trulydeserves every accolade.I don't know whether it was by design or simply serendipity, but the way the ending is constructed, allowing the player to travel back while glimpsing the completed puzzles is a really wonderful touch to a very memorable experience. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: As an artist, this game is beautiful. This definitely got me back into an art mood, and I thank it for that. As a puzzle-solver, the puzzles were just right for me; challenging and quickly timed, but not difficult for me to get stuck. I had to think, and about 70% of the time I got stuck, I was just being dumb. I understand that this game's puzzles may be too easy, but I'm perfectly satisfied. That being said, I have two qualms; first, it ended too quickly. Before I knew it, it was done and that made me sad. Second, the end ended too abruptly. I honestly thought that there would a final battle/puzzle situation, but that didn't happen and I'm slightly disappointed. That would've been so cool; it's very rare to find final battle/puzzles in games. But those definitely shouldn't dissuade you to get this. The music's not entirely my style, but I appreciate it very much; I even bought the art book + soundtrack too. The art in the book is wonderful, and the music is nice to listen to when working.Also, I like the implications of the paintings. There must be a story to them; most of them involve a person and avian. Maybe they lived together at one point? Maybe they got sealed down here for some reason? It's nice to think about; that could just be me. Also, the characters don't talk but they have so much personality to them. The boy you play as has about one (1) braincell sometimes and can be a dork. The birds have their own personalities and it's great to see that unfold. The tuba man??? is probably my least favorite character, he doesn't really have any personality. I'm still upset that the big guy was a wasted opportunity, but I might have had high hopes :P.Overall, it's beautiful, just right in challenge, and the characters are very cute. Also please buy the art book if you can, it's so nice to see this game's roots.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyable.The artwork is incredible and the puzzles are well done.  They're just challenging to the point where you won't need a walkthrough at any stage, but you'll still feel satisfaction at having bested some of the trickier puzzles.The story unfortunately is quite mediocre.  They're tried going the wordless route and honestly it just comes across flat.  It's established very quickly that there's a monster terrorizing this band of bird people who live in a kingdom underneath your house, and it never progresses beyond that.  All focus is on the puzzles and art.  There's also a few optional secret rooms and painting minigames which are a nice distraction but ultimately fairly thin as well.But those gripes aside, this is another good output from Amanita, and I look forward to their next outing.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: So first of, this is a puzzle game. Amanita Design titles are usually point and click adventures. I love point and click games, and Amanita makes some of the best, so it was a bit disappointing when I realized that this was a puzzle game since I often find this genre to frustrating. But I continued to play and I'm very happy I did. I loved the puzzles, they were never to easy or to hard. The progression was good and they introduced new concept when the old ones were getting old. If you play a ton of puzzle games you might find it a bit to easy, but I still think you can enjoy it a lot. Beautiful art, great sound design and great puzzles. Just missed an even more compelling story then it would have been perfect. 4/5
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is easily one of the most lovely, charming and brilliant puzzle experiences I've ever played. As always, Amanita comes back with beautiful art and coupled with the superb music, some brilliant puzzle design and one of the cutest stories in video games, this game is simply the whole package. None of the puzzles are particularly "hard" and you could solve any of them simply with some thought but they definitely make you think at times. The mechanics are extremely inventive, asking you to play with lights and enemies that are in themselves pieces to the solution. I don't want to say more because finding out the mechanics is a joy in itself. The music adds so much to this and is as much a part of the brilliance of the puzzle design as everything else. As you unlock and move through the puzzle, the music steadily increases in complexity, adding drums, flutes and other instruments, cleverly leading you along and letting you know you're doing the right thing. This seems like such a minor detail but adds so much to the exhilarating feeling of solving them. Scattered throughout the levels are small paintings and toys, some of them obvious to find, some hidden and each is an adorable and zany and such a pleasure to experienceI could easily recommend this game to people of all ages and this is definitely one of the most memorable gaming experiences I've had
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I love the visuals. I love the sounds and music. I love the imagination used in the game. I love the minigames.This is just an impressive adventure game. I play it with my kids (4,6,8) and they constantly smile, laugh and cheer when we finish a puzzle. The main thing, the story, is giving us fuel for talks at bedtime.Just awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure about this game at first.  The graphics were odd and puzzle games are often tedious.  This was simply one of the best games I've played in a long time.  It grew on me... I love this game I'm so glad I got to play it.  I don't typically leave reviews but thought this game deserved it.  I finished with a smile on my face.  I feel happy.  Games don't always give me that... this one did.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another gem from Amanita Design. It totally has all the vibes that you'll love from their storied collection of puzzle romps, mixed in with some fun semi-platforming elements. The puzzles are not overwhelmingly complex like those from their Samorost games or Machinarium, though they are significantly more difficult than the likes of Chucell or Botanicula. I think the experience will be unique for each player, it depends on your deductive reasoning. All I can say is, there are numerous puzzles, particularly later in the game, that do not have very clear solutions, and you'll need to use the movement of the enemies and precise positioning to complete them. I did have to look up a number of solutions online, but that's mainly because I am impatient haha. Don't play while you are sleepy or not focused as you'll just get frustrated trying to find the solutions.Art style and music from Hidden Orchestra comes together to create that perfect golden combination that only Amanita can envision. Bravo guys, seriously, bravo.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: At its heart, Creaks is a simple puzzle game in a beautifully hand drawn world.  While the puzzles are relatively easy and overall you can complete the game in less than 4-5 hours it is none the less a very enjoyable journey into the depths of this world.  Along the way you will encounter four avian characters who are struggling to save their world from a creature that is destroying it bit by bit.  All of them add to the story and atmosphere in charming ways through their wordless interactions and mannerisms.  Overall, I would recommend this game.  Especially if you can get it on sale because it is so short and does not have a lot of replay to it other than making sure you found all the secrets which consist of interactive paintings, some out in the open and others hidden away.  But none are too difficult to find.  I played for around 8 hours before I considered my playtime to be done.  Well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: If you are attracted by the aesthetics of Creaks then I think you would enjoy it unless you hate puzzle games.If you are mainly attracted to the puzzle aspect then I think you would probably enjoy Creaks. I would classify the puzzle design as quite good, but maybe not great. There aren't any standout exceptional puzzles, but there also aren't any stinkers.
