I never got stuck, but I also never felt insulted because anything was too easy.The puzzles are a bit different from other Amanita Design games that I have played: Instead of inventory items and context-dependent actions Creaks has a small set of well-defined mechanics and presents a puzzle idea and then expands on it. Maybe think of something like Portal or Braid to give you an idea of the approach that Creaks takes to puzzle design. I thought it worked really well; there were a handful of times when I thought a specific idea was maybe explored a bit too much (i.e. I thought "oh no, not another one of these"), but in general I thought the pacing was good. There is an interesting unifying concept to all of the various ideas, and so in some sense every puzzle in the game is kind of a variation on a single conceptual idea, which I like.The music is great (as is the case with all Amanita Design games I've played), but it is also used in a cool way in many puzzles. As you progress in an individual puzzle the music often changes, and it's a really rewarding feedback loop to have an idea, do it, and hear the music change which mirrors your inner reaction of "ah ha it worked!".I thought the art and creativity was incredible. You can probably judge for yourself based on screenshots whether it appeals to you; if it does I can say that the game itself lived up to and even exceeded my expectations visually. There are so many little details that clearly show that this project was a labor of love. I also appreciated the setting, which has kind of a fairy tale logic feel (think maybe something kind of like Labyrinth).
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A charming  journey into an unusual underworld. Difficult enough to get me to watch a tutorial a few times, but not so much that it interfered with the storytelling. I'll play through again to try and find the paintings I missed. I've loved all the Amanita games I've purchased, they all have a similar feel to them - that the world may be strange and at times frightening, but there is beauty and courage to be found in it as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I had a wonderful time with this game! While puzzle games normally aren't my jam, I was so captivated by the beautiful artwork and the varied soundscape that it kept me engaged the whole way. The puzzles are remarkably coherent given the game's sparse text, and I was rarely ever lost on what I should be doing. The game also was a solid length, never outstaying it's welcome. If you're feeling a puzzle adventure with remarkable world building and loads of charm, check this one out!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice and creative puzzle game. The art style is really beautiful and interesting. Every puzzle looked really hard, but after looking at it for a while, I was able to complete each one without a guide. The secret rooms also were easy to find, but not to the point where finding them was trivial.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: As expected from Amanita, Creaks lives up to their creators' names and granted some lovely hours of pure poetry and awe. We were not expecting it to be so long (almost 7 hours in our case), which is a great plus! Of course, after the game, we had to check some interviews and background; it was lovely to end up watching The Pied Piper from Jiří Barta :)I don't think I'll ever get enough of Amanita's taste. Great job, guys!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing games from Amanita for 20 years since they were flash...  the illustrations, design and music are always beautiful and entertaining.   Creaks is such a pleasure to play, I've gone through it a few times, the score is wonderful chill and relaxing.I hope these guys keep making more, they're so talented!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game!  The puzzle difficulty is pleasant (not too hard, nor too easy) and the art and atmosphere are wonderful. I am looking forward to play it with my son some day. Games from Amanita were a signifacant reason why I decided to entrer the videogames industry. And Creaks togethere with Samorost 3 are the best ones from Amanita (in my opinion). Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is much different from past Amanita games. I was expecting a standard point and click experience but was rewarded with some simple puzzle platforming. The artwork of the game is very well done. The level design was interesting with the complex series of winding ladders leading you through puzzles that progress a simple yet entertaining story. The music is nice and ramps up as you progress through a puzzle. Sound effects were good and I always enjoy Amanita nonsensical verbalizations. I found the quirky paintings to be charming in a very weird sort of way, and the little mini games were a nice diversion.This game is not even remotely hard as far as puzzle games go, but I still found it enjoyable. Took me around 6 hours to complete all content. Regular price is a bit steep for the amount of content, but it's a quality game for sure so it may be worth full price to some. If it's on a decent sale though and you like Amanita, I'd pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs some more love in the reviews. It simply is beautiful.It took me a moment to get over its only negative point: this is (again) no new Machinarium. Amanita has for long been experimenting with different game styles, focusing more on atmosphere, sound, exploration and artwork than on creating a new challenging point and click. This time, with Creaks, they go full puzzle platformer (think Braid). The game has a few simple mechanics -light and door switches and a handful of shape shifting monsters- that slowly get more complicated along the way. While never very hard, the puzzles keep you engaged throughout the whole game. This all wrapped into the amazing artwork that is Amanita's trademark. With every scene, it is worth it to press the zoom button and just check out all the details in the background. Creaks easily became one of my favorites in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished Creaks. What a gem of a game!It has the same whimsical charm and attention to detail as their previous games (Samorost, Machinarium) but unlike them, the game and puzzle design in this one is elegantly systemic and deep. Technically it's a puzzle-platformer, but movement is grid-based rather than physics-driven, so it's always intentional and never fiddly. Puzzle mechanics are revealed gradually in often delightful ways and you learn bit by bit how to manipulate the world.Several puzzles had me stumped for a while as they seemed impossible at first, but in the end I never had to resort to looking up solutions. Each puzzle is also centered around an idea; none feel like random filler. This is best of class puzzle design. I loved how the game's dynamic soundtrack kicks in with percussion or similar just as you've revealed you've figured out how to solve a puzzle, even though many steps are still left to be done. It almost feels like it's reading your mind and telling you "you've got this!"The game takes place in a single big, interconnected world. Progression is strictly linear, but there's frequent foreshadowing of areas you'll be reaching later, which made it satisfy my "explore a world" craving despite the linearity. And it's a very imaginative world!Overall I was just really pleasantly surprised by this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are fun, not frustrating: You don't have to take notes, there's rarely a way to work yourself into a corner that forces restarting a level, you don't get pushed back several minutes if you get killed, there's no branching to map, the devices you get to tinker with are nifty, and the entire thing is beautiful beyond description. I am recommending this to lots of people.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: It's no Machinarium, i'll say that, but it's still got that Amanita charm. I think the reviews are rather critical as I think we were all hoping for another Machinarium adventure. I think as a stand alone gig, it does well, but I probably wouldn't have bought it at full price knowing what to expect from the game now i've played it. I got it in the sale, I think half price, which seems fair. If you're after variation in your puzzles, this won't be for you, but if you like the Amanita vibe, I think you'll enjoy this. Not too hard but does get you thinking!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art, engaging music, a clever and quirky story, a few fun Easter eggs and smart, sometimes quite challenging puzzles. Appropriate for kids and fun for adults; might be a little dry/difficult for a child younger than 7 or 8. Amanita makes great games, this one is a little different (a little more predictable than some of their other titles) but entertaining and well-made.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: The amount of creativity that went into this game is just insane. Sixty-ish scenes with hand-drawn backgrounds full of intricate details, beautiful character animations, great music that matches the flow of the game perfectly, a simple story that artfully mixes dark and whimsical elements. A real masterpiece. It's relatively easy and can be finished in a few hours, but the puzzles are challenging enough to never get boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Creaks is a fine addition to Amanita Design's games library, an at times challenging light-puzzle game with the Amanita standard incredible soundtrack and visuals. Although I would still classify Creaks as a 'point and click' I would say that it is at least different than Amanita's previous games. Throughout the game you will be faced with obstacles in the form of creatures that avoid the light and when they are trapped in a spotlight, for example, they turn into inanimate objects. Each puzzles involves overcoming and outwitting these creatures in order to progress. I admit that I was stumped on some of the later puzzles but the level of challenge remains pretty consistent throughout. I played with a controller for a more comfortable experience as there aren't many controls other than one or two interact buttons and movement, so I'd recommend a controller although it's just as fine with mouse and keyboard. As always, the hand drawn visuals and the soundtrack are exceptional. Hidden Orchestra does an amazing job of captruing the mechanical and surreal setting of Creaks; I need to get my hands on the vinyl for the soundtrack! The game took me around four and a half hours to beat with an additional half hour to find the rest of the collectables (thank you Steam guides). Another classic Amanita Design puzzle game, I recommend Creaks to any fans of the point-and-click or puzzle genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: as a huge fan of machinarium you get quickly familiar with the art and sounds and the puzzles are smart but repetitive but this is not about breaking records or collecting cash, its about enjoying your time... slowly and fully relaxed. be sure to walk into every corner if your a painting collector - ps: had to google solutions a couple of time, because it becomes harder and harder. thank you amanita, its what i expected!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This game thinks I've played it for 65 hours, when what I've actually been doing is playing it twice - once during the daytime with kiddo, and once at night. And letting it run in the background the whole time. So total playtime might have been ten hours with doubling some of the puzzles?I thought the puzzles were really good, well designed, although sometimes I thought the puzzle was harder than it was, and overshot the solution. This game utilizes objects that change states based upon user input (switches and plates.) The dog robot becomes a chest of drawers, for example, that you can climb on. The obstacles in the game are objects that you can use to solve the game, in either state. Very clever, imo. This type of clever puzzle building makes me feel very inadequate.I also want to mention that the art in this game is fabulous. It is a genuine pleasure to play a game that looks hand-drawn, instead of the usual obsessively rendered detail.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, the first 30 mins of gameplay are pretty slow, and the story makes no sense, but if you're willing to invest a couple of hours into this game, you'll find a well crafted puzzle game centered around manipulating the enemy's AI, and finding beautiful secrets. (Oh and the story gets much better as it goes along). They've also done a great job of allowing the player to revisit the game upon completion, so it's not tedious at all to 100%
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: You will love Creak, play it for once and be sure that this is one of those games which you will play more than once. The game-play is long and engaging, soon after starting the game you'll come to know why it is long. You will come to like the music which is an absolute treat, it matches the scene and the pace of the game and you will be compelled to find the individual music pieces, some of them are connected to the paintings.The main character(you) is strong-willed and action oriented. You will appreciate the details of the game overall and how the main character tries to find the way through the obstacles. The sheer scale of the game will make you feel awestruck. In some places you'll feel fear and then with the strong will of the character you will overcome that fear and I can tell you that it is an awesome feeling. You feel as if you're making those jumps yourself, and I am not talking about just the game controls. Use walk-through helps as a method of last recourse, try completing it by yourself.Lastly, the effort that Amanita Design has put in making this amazing game is just beautiful. The music, game-play, puzzles and the overall story-line is worthy of praise. I recommend this game to anyone who likes to play puzzle, story-based, tactical games. It offers value for your buck, although i believe it has been kept under-priced. I just hope that Creaks becomes available on Android and other platforms as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I usually do not review games, but this one deserve an exception. This game is a GEM for various reasons. 1) atmosphere &  design 2) well crafted, non-trivial puzzles 3) overall game experience.  I finished it without looking any online help and I suggest please all to do the same, don't rush.  If you get stuck on a puzzle that seems impossible to solve, just sleep on it, ask yourself the right questions and the beautiful logic of the solution will come to you !  Congratulations Amanita !
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. I love the hand drawn ink style of it, and like all good puzzle games, its difficult enough to make you feel super smart when you figure out a puzzle, but not unsolvable. Also, the setting and characters are super unique and refreshing, with each creature being afraid of light and becoming an interactive object when hit with it. You use this mechanic to get through rooms and descend deeper into this weird shanty town underneath your house, with the puzzles, environment, and monsters getting stranger and more complex as you go deeper.I just wish I could learn more about the lore. There are these strange mechanical wind up paintings you can find throughout the game, some of which are mini games, that depict bird people doing various things. They're super interesting, and have only left me more curious about the bird people. They're the only friendly monsters in the game, and I would really like to know more about them and the world they live in.All in all, Creaks has become one of my favorite puzzle games. It draws you in with its enchanting soundtrack and creepy but alluring world. I highly recommend it, and plan to 100% it at some point.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking for games that were on par with "The Room" trilogy, not just for the puzzles, but the ambiance, characters and story. And found that in Creaks.First off, the puzzles: not too easy, not too hard to the point of frustration. If you ever get stuck, all it takes is to sit back for a second, look at what you got on screen and think it through. I liked them.The story is actually simple, and that's what makes it good. It doesn't have plot twists, it doesn't have a huge backstory per se (although they tell you a bit about the underworld inhabitants through paintings), it's just an adventure into a mysterious and magical world.The characters are what surprised me. I was expecting for the underworld inhabitants to treat the main character as some sort of intruder and chase him off. Their reaction to seeing him surprised me greatly, and the moment the first one took notice of the MC, I was completely onboard with these characters. No unnecessary drama needed.And I'm listening to the soundtrack while writing this. I really liked the atmosphere it gives to the whole game, as well as the art. Mysterious, creepy, yet somewhat charming.I've enjoyed it through, and it's one of the few games I'll play again soon, just to experience it again with new eyes after the ending.One mystery remains though..... will the main character ever finish reading that book?
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This game exudes the usual Amanita charm but also offering a good deal of really well designed and challenging puzzles. I don't understand why this title has not been received better by the critics, it's probably my second favorite Amanita Design game only after Machinarium. Please keep these coming, Amanita!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Amanita Design never fails to impress! They did it with Machinarium and Botanicula and now they've done it again!! A perfect blend of challenging gameplay, whimsical setting and a surprisingly solid cast of characters despite the game not having a single line of dialogue.Some of the puzzles are pretty tricky, but there are guides online if you get stuck. 10/10 a must-play
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphic design. At the beginning little bit boring, but later it gets better and better. You have to use monsters and few objects  properties to solve each scene. There are very good puzzles. I wish there were more! There are also few 'hidden' mini games. I didn't like those too much though. Neither did I understand the purpose of  the paintings. Regardless I still highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: i half don't recommend this game and half do. some of the puzzles are too easy, and then some of them are too hard and i can't do them unless i look them up on youtube. i like the art style/characters/music, but the game also frustrates me a lot to the point where i just stop playing. glad i got this on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely amazing game. Words cannot describe the amount of creativity and love Amanita Design put into this one.The puzzles on display here are a bit different than their other point-and-click adventures, focusing mainly on tight 2D environmental manipulation puzzles. The enemies in this game are the very tools you use to solve the puzzles, with each one having a surprising amount of depth. The game really opens up when levels start combining enemies together, as manipulating the enemies to interact with each other adds even more room for interesting puzzles. I should also mention that the pacing is really well done, as puzzle ideas are hardly ever reused, and most of the time puzzles either have a small cutscene introducing us to the other characters in the game or sometimes even tiny minigames right afterwards.The world that they built is to die for, with so many tiny details that I doubt many people would even notice. The backgrounds are dense with detail, creating a palpable sense that this now-abandoned underground city was once filled with people. The story is portioned out very well throughout the game, as you get to know the other mysterious bird people still inhabiting the crumbling structure, while a mysterious and unknown creature stalks you from the outside.It’s no surprise that the music on display here is phenomenal, featuring work from the incredibly talented Hidden Orchestra. Each song is so lively, dynamically adding more instruments depending on how far you are in the puzzle, resulting in a satisfying swell when the puzzle is completed.The intricately detailed background, the surreal music, the unique puzzles — it's all so refreshing yet so familiar. I highly recommend playing this game, especially if you enjoyed any of Animta's other work.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Creaks is a rare, absolutely amazing mixture of art and puzzle. Puzzles are clever, fun to solve but never brain-wrecking; moreover, they implement original mechanics perfectly integrated in the stunning hand-drawn world. In my humble opinion, the best work from Amanita Design so far (and the bar was high already!), so much that I went for the beautiful collector's edition of the game. Totally worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Game is 4 hours long. Full of charm and clever puzzles. Puzzles are designed in such a way that you can't get in a state where it's unsolvable, this makes discovering the mechanics of each puzzle a lot less frustrating to figure out then other puzzle games. Cute little story and characters that add a lot of mystery and charm to the world. Interesting how they made the entire world fit in a way that made sense, logistically speaking. You'll see what I mean when you play it. Made me hungry for more. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Such an outstanding little world to explore and puzzle over. Beautiful, hand-drawn art, compelling (and sometimes tricky) puzzles, and a world that soaks into you as you play. I adore Amanita Design; they make games that are really my cuppa tea; full to the brim with whimsy and wonder, and Creaks is no exception. Amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly beautiful and weird - really great game all the way through! It didn't repeat puzzles that I noticed, and introduced new mechanics as you played through the story. The music creates a nice atmosphere and isn't too distracting if you're trying to solve a puzzle. Machinarium and the original Oddworld games are some of my absolute favourites, and I can now add Creaks to that list!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, and it gets better as it goes along. FYI Although the heart, style, and characters of this game are similar to other Amanita games, this one is a puzzle game, not a point and click.You get a lot of bang for your buck too - I expected the game to be much shorter than it was. Despite the length it always felt fresh - not once did I think "I've done this kind of puzzle already". It ramps up slowly, and each stage introduces something new. It also creates a great atmosphere. Granted the first 30 mins feels slow, but you realize later that it was setting up the mood for the later chapters, and it does it well. Finally, it runs smoothly, and the controls are flawless which is critical for this kind of game. All in all, I really feel like this was money well spent, it was satisfying from start to credits.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art, wonderful music, and the puzzles are quite enjoyable, with a fair variety of puzzle mechanics and designed smartly enough that you're unlikely to get stuck for very long. Wholeheartedly recommend. Highly recommend you also purchase the soundtrack and download the adaptive soundtrack generator, its honestly cool af.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the game for exactly 7 hours.I didn't get all the paintings, sadly. I'm missing ten.A friend bought this game for me because they thought I'd enjoy it.AND I DID~!It's got the right amount of puzzle solving, right amount of mechanics to solve said puzzles, bonus puzzles (aka some paintings) to get more time into the game. This game is amazing. It's a unique story, only told visually with some dialogue (in game language, no actual dialogue in the slightest.)There's plenty of brain-tingling moments, when solving a puzzle. And the satisfaction it brings, BRO, it's amazing.Music is also fantastic, amazing soundtrack.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Great storybook style artwork (as ever from Amanita Design) that reminds me of books when I was a kid, clever puzzles that aren't too frustrating, really good.The only thing that bothers me is the protagonists bed is way too small for him, maybe this is why he can't run and jump - his back and shoulders are knackered.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Going through the first few scenes of Creaks I started to worry that it was going to be a short and easy playthrough with boring mechanics. Despite loving all Amanita Design's other games, I thought that they might have fumbled with this one. As the game progressed, I realised that I was wrong! Creaks is a charming puzzler, with all the features you'd expect from an Amanita Design game; a unique art style, great soundtrack and excellent sound design. The puzzles get fairly complex, but never have convoluted solutions. The story, while barebones, is fun, and the level design is top notch. My enjoyment of the game increased exponentially as I got further down the map. 9/10 Creaks is easier than their other games, but still offers a challenge at times and gets you thinking creatively within the limits of the puzzles. I highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished. Loved it. Everything feels organic, and the soundtrack is amazing as it was in Machinarium, a jazz/electronic hybrid that fits perfectly. This is one of those games I was bummed to complete, because I didn't want it to end just yet even though the ending was perfect. Amanita hit another home run.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A short, but sweet puzzle game with a beautiful art style and wonderful soundtrack and puzzles that are just the right level of difficulty. The story is very simplistic and devoid of any dialogue, but I'm totally fine with that. I frankly think having a complex story with actual written lines in it would just detract from the pure simplicity of the game. This game is just a good relaxing time and definitely a great example of indie gaming as a whole.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous and magical experience with breathtaking graphic/art design and awesome music / sound design. Level design and overall world building is playful and it's working together without any dialog. No pixel perfect approach, no time pressure. Just really nice logical platformer. Best game by Amanita so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: So I figured out this game existed almost a year after release. I immediately buy it to find out it is a platform puzzler... I was so down and depressed after first being thrilled to 'discover' a new game by the machinarium folks. Then I decided to give it a go against better judgement.Turns out, it is pretty amazing after all. I really enjoyed the difficulty, diversity and pace of the puzzles. The story that was told between the 60+ puzzles has the same endearing feeling their stories always have, which applies to the art and ingenuity of the overall design as well.Compliments, a bona fide work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first playthrough and it was a delight.  I liked progressing through the game and seeing more of the story unfold.  The setting reminded me of some of my favorite illustrated childhood story books where there were things going on in the background just to add some flavor and fun to the setting.  Thanks again for a fun puzzle game with a charming cast, and satisfying ending. Love the music and sound effects too!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable and creative puzzle game, clearly made with tons of love. The amount of little details in every screen is amazing. Challenging, but not frustrating, with a simple but engaging story that kept me interested all the way through. Has a wonderful soundtrack, too, just like all of Amanita's games. If you enjoyed Machinarium and Samorost, you'll probably like this, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with a fantastic setting. The paintings are a nice touch to provoke the player to explore and breaks up the puzzles very well instead of doing puzzle after puzzle. You can do a nice 'minigame' in between. I never felt like the puzzles were impossible, though there were a couple where I had to step away for the night, but coming back I always found the solution.My only complaint is how short this game is. I completed it in under 6 hours, which I don't think is enough for $20, but I had a great time so worth the money for me
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: It's a wonderful puzzle game that lets you take things step by step at the start, but slowly ramps up and you get to use your noggin. The music is delightful and on a couple of occasions I found myself just standing and jamming to it.The artwork and story direction makes it feel a bit like a fever dream, the paintings especially, but it is all worth it in the end, you can easily find yourself pushing forward to see more of the story that plays around the puzzles and what is causing the trouble around.I loved the game and had fun to the end, worth getting, and if it's on sale, absolutely.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Very original, as good as Amanita's other games although this one is a puzzle rather than point-and-click.Excellent art, very good music, unique atmosphere. Slightly creepy but in a good way.Puzzles are easy to moderately challenging, with a few frustrating exceptions. All in all a great game, well worth the price and time spent playing it. Achievement hunters will be happy to know that even if you miss some (which is not very easy, actually) you can replay any scene after completing the game. Good stuff. Seriously, if you like Amanita and you like a bit of puzzle fun, get this game. A solid 8/10, maybe even 9.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another gem made by Amanita? Yep.Similar to previous stuff? Not quite.It's not lazy-drawn as Botanicula or Piligrims, prepare yourself to Samorost-like visually magnificent world.Puzzles are easier than in Machinarium, but still require 90% of your brain CPU usage to proceed to new location.And, the most important part: if you do pay attention to what you hear during gameplay, buy this game right now because it totally must belong to Bureau international des poids et mesures when it comes to sound design, you get it?
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the story and game play. The puzzles are tricky but not impossible and have fun mechanics that shift over the course of the story. It is suspenseful but not scary and has some really, really, really, weird paintings. Overall, really fun game, not super long but definitely worth a play through.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little puzzle adventure in hand  drawn world. I was captivated by weird / original style and funky play with enemies. There wasn't any really hard puzzle I would  get stuck for long time so game has nice flow. There could be more puzzles with combinations of different mechanics but I'm still satisfied anyway.I will  definitely try some older games from Amanita studio as I was impressed by what you can make with so small team of people.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR go and play Samorost.Sadly, Creaks is not on the level of previous Amanita works. Game basically have one puzzle repeated over and over again. And not the best one either. It gets very tedious and repetitive quickly, and feels like a chore. They could have just abolished it from the game and it would only made it better.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I have played Machinarium before, and I liked it very much. The art style and the main character and especially the music had alot of fun to give. I saw this game (Creaks) during a sale and was wondering if I should buy it, because of my earlier experience from Machinarium, but the sale went over and I still had not bought it.Creaks is really something else than what I have seen before. Beautiful art, fun and weird puzzles, and alot of diversity. The main character might not have so much personality, but I'll guess other characters and figures takes care of that.The game takes you around the city of some birds that live there, and to avoid spoilers, I will just say that they have a big problem they have to solve, to save their city from destruction. Our main character takes us around the city, and the way to get around, involves puzzles to solve. Sometimes you can find hidden rooms aswell.I think Creaks is alot different than Machinarium, but they have the same energy in the game, with funny characters and things that happen. The game has nice music, and thousands of things to explore and see, related to art and objects.I like to do achievements, but I didn't get them all. Now, replaying the entire game completly doesn't seem like something I wanna do. The game is really fun, that first time, because you have to figure things out and follow the story. There is a scene chooser, where you can get back to a certain place in the game, to replay it, instead of doing it all over again, but all in all I think this game has a great replay vaule, because it's a big game. It's worth going through the game without help, trying to find the secret rooms and finish achievements, because after you can go back and see if you can find those secret rooms you didn't find the first time. That is your best replay value. I did use a guide for the missing achievements and painting, but after have done that I feel I could have easily found them myself. Was most likely busy with the puzzles.Edit: Started on achievements, and at once I see I can skip that the exact scenes I need where I forgot to find a hidden portrait. I realised that I was too busy with the puzzle and forgot to check out the hidden space. That was kinda a nice surprise, to see where that missing room was!Speaking of value. Since I didn't make the sale for this game I had to pay 200 NOK for it, around 20 euro. After completing the game in 6 hours (7.4 hours 28/28 achievements) I would say it's alright, but I wouldn't have minded to have gotten it on sale, since the sale price seems a bit more logical to pay rather than the full price.I really recommend this game. Buy it and play it! Have fun! Getting it on sale will make you feel you didn't pay too much for it, but I am sure anyone that plays this game will enjoy it nevertheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: If you love elevators, lifts, chutes, and ladders then you're gonna love this game! This game is as charming as I've ever played. It's got some fun challenges, all while leading us through a tale of kinship... through hardship.Nice, quick game with a slew of quirks that endeared it to me. Simple and tight controls.  Would buy again.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Amanita branches out from their usual point-and-click to a puzzle-platformer, and they nailed it. They bring all their usual hand-drawn charm to create another immersive and welcoming fantasy world. The structure of the whole game and level-to-level is very cohesive -- story and gameplay and design all work beautifully together, I was saying "this is COOL!" at so many moments. A wonderful escape.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Creaks is a puzzle solving adventure platformer. If you have played their previous adventure game, called Machinarium, you will know what to expect. Appealing graphics and soundtrack, good puzzles and likeable story characters. It took them 10 years but the wait was worth it.Like in Machinarium the graphics are hand-drawn and are really stunning. The world of Creaks expresses sadness and eeriness. The protagonist of the game basically descends into a cave entering this huge structure which is divided into several zones each with a different art style. As the player descends deeper and deeper, the story is slowly revealed. The story isn't super rich but in those types of games it is a good thing. The main thing here is the puzzle solving. Some really innovative and creative puzzle mechanics were created for this game. The difference with other puzzle solving games that I have played is that in this game you really have to have a plan. The trial and error trick isn't going to help you with most of the puzzles here. Some of them are really challenging but most of them are balanced.Like most of these types of games, don't expect lots of replay-ability. However, I did an instant second playthrough because the first part of the game- before the puzzles get too hard- is a real joy to play. There are some mini games through the game that give you extra achievements. Some of those are really catchy and creative and deserve your attention. All in all this is a casual puzzle game with well crafted puzzles, beautiful graphics and a fitting soundtrack that doesn't overshadow the flow of the game. Hopefully their next game won't come out in 10 years like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another gem from Amanita. Delectable art style that I've yet to see incorporated into this type of game. Puzzles that are just challenging enough to get you thinking, but rarely frustrated. The storyline is delightful as always, sans dialog to drag you down (as you'd expect from Amanita). Also, a fantastic musical score by Hidden Orchestra with production from the wonderful Tomas Dvorak as well. I guess what I'm saying here is, buy this game. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Pros-I'm usually really terrible at puzzles, but I only needed to consult a walkthrough once!-Adaptive music that plays differently as you progress correctly through puzzles. Very nice!-Signature Amanita Design art (see Machinarium)-Actually scary monster that prowls around the whole game-Really clever mechanics that demand careful attention to detail-Neat enemy behavior that you need to exploit-Many secrets to find with cute slightly animated art & sound-Main character is really well animated and expressive (if silent)-Funny characters with different personalities that speak in gibberish-A couple puzzles will have you have eureka! moments-Game ended before it got tedious (7.5 hrs), as it seemingly did all it had to offer at that point-Objects in the background are alive, move and make sounds-Ending is nice-Perfect for the whole familyCons:-Definitely not as memorable as Machinarium. Also I prefer Floex's music.-You can count the enemy types on one hand-The world isn't really explained; things are just... there. No lore. Like a dream.-Puzzles can get a bit repetitive/tedious at times-Final confrontation has no challenge. It feels rushed.-The things on the paintings you find feel disconnected from the game's world.-Lantern is underutilizedStill, highly recommended!!Looking forward to Amanita Design's next game! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A short puzzler. It took me about 6 hours to get one from end to the other, but I didn't actively look for all the secrets. The puzzles are not too hard, sometimes it takes a few minutes to come to the solution, but I never was really stumped. The main selling point of the game is certainly the unique artstyle, which I found very intriguing. It reminded me of cartoons I saw as a child, so I had a bit of nostalgia going on. Overall very charming and recommendable!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A hand drawn masterpiece of a puzzle platformer game. Similar in visual style to Gorogoa but set in a massive dilapidated underground chamber constructed by a mysterious race of bird-like creatures. The puzzle mechanisms are not the most novel, but always well designed and a joy to view. The accompanying music is fun and funky similar to previous Amanita design games.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loved machinarium but wished the character/machine designs were a little less goofy, I found the characters in this game to be more likeable. I'm also a fan of the tighter grid-based puzzles, so it's not a victim of point-and-click era moon logic that can have you banging your head against a wall or walkthrough.Also, I really liked how the music reacts to the progress you make towards solving each puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really engaging and it presents a variety of different puzzles to solve to proceed. The plot has an  aura of mystery as when you start, you have no idea what is going on. The light bulb in your room was just buzzing! The artwork is great, all the drawings have a handmade feel. It is ideal to relax after one day's long work,
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game so much! Dark andgothic atmosphere and yet, with your progress it turn pretty optimistic. Really enjoy its pazzle most of them fair, fun and challenging and not breaking your spirit. Only one make me too watch YouTube. This game is more pazzle/point and click style  not for those who look for actons norarcade. So I dont think this is fair to put poor review only becuase you dont attach its genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Creaks is a fantastic casual game. The art style and atmosphere are extremely charming, while the gameplay is consistently rewarding. The difficulty even managed to hit this sweet spot where each of bite-sized puzzles got me thinking without being frustrating. The game is short, but I really appreciate that it didn't overstay its welcome. Definitely worth a buy if you like chill puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wondered what kind of subterranean  creature inhabits the sunless world. Bet you never thought the answer was birds. Ones capable of animating the inanimate. and even worse they hate you, the furniture not the birds, that would be just silly otherwise. Anyway one day you find a hole in your house that leads into the unknown, so what do you do? what any sane person that realizes they are the protagonist in their story, Explore the heck out of it and and never question any of it!This is a fun puzzle platformer with some truly awesome level design and some fun and interesting enemies. They are well thought out and the enemy interaction really sells this game. Art style is very interesting and fits well together. Only real downside is it is a tad on the short side about 5 hours. Pick it up on sale and kill an afternoon. It will give you something to chat about with your friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another immaculate experience from Amanita Design.At first, watching the trailer, I didn't expect much. After such great platformer puzzle games as braid, swapper or ministry of broadcast, it didn't seem to offer much innovation in terms of puzzle structure.Part of that was the design of the first enemy - mechanical dogs. I wasn't overly thrilled. But with the introduction of new enemies and game mecahnics the puzzles and level designs become increasingly more interesting and complex. The solutions usually don't get much harder, since every level offers little liberty of movement and action, so you can easily figure out the solution by just trying around.This makes for a fast progression and fluent pace. Everything is hand drawn and your surroundings keep changing all the time as you enter new areas, which makes the exploration of this underground fortress a real joy.It took me a bit under 10 hours to finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a real big fan of Amanita's design styling and honestly would recommend this game solely for the art.It's a please to look at. Looks like twisted, dark, Richard Scarry.The game-play is simple and straightforward: solve spatial puzzles with simple movement with more and more complexities.The game also gives audio clues when you're on the right track (that must've been fun to design).Pretty.Functional.Entertaining.Something of a plot though there's not much spoken word.It can potentially get repetitive if you try to grind through the game as fast as possible but if you take your time it's pretty relaxing.A good few hours spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Amanita does it again. Quirky, beautiful and engaging world, teased and fed piecemeal to you through environmental storytelling locked behind simple puzzle mechanics. Fun loveable characters which convey heaps of emotion with 0 dialogue!Most puzzles are sequential logic with only a few more complex ones involving close attention to spacing. One of the few good things to come out of 2020, give it a shot if you like puzzle games, beautiful art and non-spoken narrative experiences!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: As a child I had explored most of our house pretty quickly, but there were still some hidden and inaccessible spots, which in a strange mingling of dreams and imagination became places with extra rooms, corridors and staircases. Maybe because of this (and because of the soundtrack and overall immersiveness), Creaks holds a special place in my heart, with such an adventure awaiting right behind a peeling bit of wallpaper, waiting to be discovered.After having played Samorost 1-3, Machinarium and GRIS (a direction from which you might come to Creaks with certain expectations), I should say that this game is different in many ways, but not to compete, but to be its own thing entirely. I'm listening to the soundtrack as I'm writing this, and just like finishing a good book, I would give so much to be able to discover it all over again for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Amanita have done it again!  is another atmospheric masterpiece and in my opinion, their best game since . Unlike previous games it is a puzzle game rather than a point-and-click adventure. The puzzles are really well designed, never being easy but not getting frustratingly hard either. The difficulty curve is perfect and the different kinds of puzzle keep things consistently interesting.Beyond just having engaging gameplay, the world you explore in  is another huge selling point. The hand-drawn environments are gorgeous and I love just looking over all the little background details. There are plenty of hidden areas to discover, and paintings and minigames that bring the world to life in a very organic way. Like , the game's art style communicates so much sense of place and history, while still being mysterious as to how the world came to be. And as ever for Amanita, the music contributes immensely as well - I particularly liked the way the music changes, giving little sound cues and expanding, as you get further into solving a puzzle. A lot of work obviously went into making the whole experience a holistic one.My criticism of the last few Amanita games has always been that they were too short. Well even here  doesn't disappoint, being a perfect length so you really get your money's worth. Honestly, I can't really think of any criticism for this game - I got a couple of crashes, but they disappeared as soon as I closed my browser while playing, so I'm inclined to think it was just my PC not being able to handle multiple processes. This game was on my wishlist for a very long time, as "Coming Soon". I believe they even released multiple games in between it first showing up on Steam and the actual release. Well, the extra development time definitely paid off, and is visible in every nook and cranny of this enchanting world. The wait was worth it. Buy it now!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: such a beautiful game, with an awesome graphic, a lot of details and such a great soundtrack. i agree too a lot of other reviewers, that this game is different to the games before. it's different too botanicula or chuchel , because it's a "dark" game. if you love machinarium and the interactiv puzzle's inside of the game, than you won't be happy with creaks. the puzzle's in this game are all the time near the same, with some differences and different degrees of difficulty from very easy up to a real brain damager. i guees i needed 3 times some "cheats" by watching a youtube clip to get some help and i was missing two secret rooms, but at all it's a really nice game by amanita design. at the beginning i was thinking the price is a little bit too high, but the soundtrack is so nice and you have a lot of hours fun with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: The setting, the art, the animations, the music with masterfully placed sound-cues are all wonderful. The puzzles are inventive and fun to solve. None of the puzzles were difficult for me but this is not necessarily a bad thing. I do love more difficult puzzle games but not all games need to be complete headscratchers to be interesting. The simplicity of the mechanics, the combinations of the various creatures and lights, built into the lovingly drawn environment is ingenious. It has the effect of a beautiful piece of clockwork machinery that you slowly piece together.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed this game. It's a relaxng and meditative puzzle game, using platforms in the logic of solving puzzles rtather than for action platforming. I love how this game combines puzzles with navigating the gorgeous setting, including secret rooms and paintings as achievements. I got frustrated at times but I think that was because of pandemic fatigue and not the game. This game is not too difficult, but as someone who often plays puzzle games I found it was also not too easy. Am not really a platform gamer so can't comment on what platform gamers might think of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Unique puzzle elements combine in increasingly complex ways to continue upping the ante in difficulty, and game mechanics are revealed to the player in excellently designed ways. On top of this, a killer soundtrack and gorgeous environments full of interesting (and animated) objects make Creaks one of the best puzzle games I've played in a long time.
