_childDocuments_.review: What I especially love is that the whole game world has a wholesome integrity to it. It's practically a one big house? village? mountain? idk, but you can see the whole thing, the room structure, where is you current room exactly, where are you going, etc.I love Machinarium as much as the other guy, it's easily my favorite point-and-click adventure. Here the structure is different, you solve one room at a time. And I don't mind it, it gives the game a steady pace. Being stuck and visiting same locations over and over is tedious, and it can't happen here.Another nice touch: the achievement icons for finding secret rooms are small parts of a background near the place in the game where the secret room is, which serves as a small hint. And you can load any room in the game. Which makes trying to find the secret rooms which you didn't find during during first playthrough fun and easy.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Animata Design does an amazing job creating games that make an emotional imprint on my brain and forever link themselves with whatever my life is when I play them.  This game a masterpiece that advances their approach to puzzle design, their art style, and the soundscapes they create.  Unlike Machinarium the puzzles don't require any awareness of inventory or kind of obscure point and click game thinking.  This game is perfect and easily the most accessible and beautiful experience I've had in gaming for years.  It would feel wrong to say it's somehow better than their previous work but if you're a preexisting fan I think it showcases a devotion to elevating everything they excel at.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to Abe's Odyssey: puzzles are built around understanding creature's AI and manipulating the environment so that they do what you want. The main character controls very fluidly for a Prince of Persia style game and is well animated. The puzzles vary between easy and medium difficulty and most players won't need a guide. Game way about 7 hours long. The art is really good: every room/area is unique, and there's always something interesting going on in the background. The game builds atmosphere through lots of sound effects, good use of background music at appropriate times. The collectables, especially the interactive mini-games, are delightfully odd.The NPCs don't have any understandable dialogue but the animation and character design really works to differentiate them. The story is told through "in-engine" cut scenes as you progress. The cast is unique and lovable and by the end you're glad everyone is safe, even the "monsters" who acted as antagonists in the game.All in all a very charming and enjoyable puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another homerun for the team at Amanita. It's amazing how they always manage to find new and exciting ways to hone their craft while at the core being undeniably true to their quirky style. I've been following them since Samorost was only known as a Flash game, hiding in the deep chasms of the old web. They never fail to surprise me. I raise a glass to one of my favorite dev teams around! One slight ♥♥♥♥♥♥ with Creaks is maybe the repetitiveness of the puzzles, but mostly just when you start to get weary of one, a new element is introduced. Also, the Paintings are a fantastic little detour.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Solid puzzle game.  Only slight criticism is that some of the mechanisms look like they're janky, but that's because you are doing them wrong.  If you do the puzzle with the intended solution, then they're all solid puzzles.  5 hours is completion time without much effort spent in uncovering secrets.  The secrets are kinda weird minigames and some are just strange artsy video.  The minigames are pretty damn jank though.  Usually there's two awkward controls for each minigame.  They don't work all that well, but the game itself is lenient enough to let you make mistakes.  I kinda liked the plot, it's a self told plot that doesn't narrate anything to the player.  There isn't one single text screen or word spoken, you just kinda figure out the plot based on what you see.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game! The graphics are cool and the puzzles can be really hard and make you go crazy, but once you solve them, you feel smart. Also, the puzzles are all very different, so it does not get boring. Soundtrack from Hidden Orchestra is also sweet. Oh yeah, it is a bit on the expensive side though...
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the game. The atmosphere is the kind that i really like. It absolutely does deliver, like other Amanita Design's games. It's the first game from them (iirc) in which we have full control over the protagonist since the game is not a point and click one. The mechanics and obstacles are shown instead of being told, in a very clever way. The music is MAGNIFICENT. It really helps in creating the atmosphere of the game, it's never annoying and the fact that gets louder for a bit when we do the right thing with the puzzles is so great.The game answers the majority of the questions that arise and the questions that are not answered still have one answer: the game's world is like this. Why is there something beneath a house? It's like asking why are there robots in machinarium, or why are there planets and strange animals in Samorost. I will search for fan theories, albeit the game does not have much unexplored stuff to theorize about. Still, there is room for doing that a bit!Congratulations, really nice game.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: It's a lovingly and well made little game. The soundtrack + artstyle are beatiful and definitly outshine the rest of the game and while the puzzles were individually really good I think they should have reused and mixed the different puzzle mechanics with each other more. For instance the last 2 mechanics introduced sheep and water were only used with 2 other mechanics. It kinda felt rushed towards the end and I don't really understand whythe indie dev team did that.Nontheless a great little 4-6 hours game. And the small puzzle art boxes were really fun
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Amanita Design has created a number of beloved adventure games and Creaks is not lacking in this groups excellent signature style.  Although instead of being a traditional adventure game, this is a puzzle game where you go from to room to room with some secrets here and there. Learning each monsters rules and the way they move is important especially with what tools you're given in each puzzle.  You get introduced to them gradually as you get further into it and they aren't too complicated and there's only a handful of them in total so there's not too much to learn. They do find plenty of ways to work with what they have I will say. There's some little cutscenes every so often as well as paintings, including interactive ones which are mini games which help break things up a bit but they're only a small part of the game.Overall this is a great puzzle game. None of the puzzles are overwhelming hard but they aren't super easy; just nicely balanced I'd say. The art style, sound track and every else are on point. This game is different from what you might be used to from this group but it's just as worthy as the rest of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: It is a new leap for amanita, but I am still a fan of their point-and-click games. This game is playable on many devices, which is awesome. Great graphics and simple interface make it perfect for tablets. The soundtrack is a delight, and I loved the worn-out style and the secret underground world. I found the story itself quite boring compared to the overall quality of the game. There is a separate puzzle in each room, but rooms and puzzles an running up and down the ladder are boring, the story and progress are too linear for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to Chuchel and Samorost 3, this game’s design is utilitarian. It’s detailed and intricate but doesn’t have as much imagination and life.Rather than give you a world to explore, this is one of those stop every screen and solve a puzzle to reach the exit type of games, and the puzzles are contrived. They are not integrated into their environment or story the way Chuchel’s and Botanicula’s were. (Sorry. It’s impossible to talk about one of their games without referring to their other titles. Go play them!) That’s disappointing, but since my main complaint with Samorost 3 was not giving the player enough to do, I'm relieved this one swings to the opposite extreme in that there’s nothing but puzzles to solve.The puzzles don’t become truly clever until the “spies” show up nearly a third of the way through, and that’s when the game finally engaged me. Still contrived, but entertaining in their own right for how well they utilize the mechanics and now we’re not just running from mechanical dogs but meeting some interesting new creatures.There’s a monster wreaking havoc in this hidden world, and finding out what it is and why it’s loose made me smile. Amanita games always have a peculiar charm to them, and Creaks has it as well. Just a glimmer, but it’s there. Another glimmer of this charm is seeing what happens when the two spies meet. It only happens once, and it’s another delightful detail. I was hoping for more of that, but the puzzles are separate from the story and characters this time.The paintings you find between the puzzles are a nice break in the gameplay. Some are interactive and are mini-games on their own, which is a nice touch. I think Amanita missed an opportunity to use them to hint at the history of this underground city of bird-people. That would have given the paintings a greater purpose than just achievements. Still, they are adorable, and the lost cat painting is so memorable I’m still thinking about it.As much as I desire another Botanicula or Machinarium or Chuchel, with special creative puzzles tied to the environment and story, Creaks has lots of solid brain-teasers that stand on their own to make up for it, and the story you see as you descend is interesting enough to pull you forward. I solved every puzzle without taking a hint or looking at a walkthrough. Everything is fair, and everything makes sense if you pay attention. Creaks takes a while to become engaging, but once it did, I enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of Machinarium and of Amanita Design in general so picking this up with a similar art style and gameplay was a day one purchase for me. There is no Josef but it has all the Amanita charm and feels. If you enjoy solving puzzles with this art style and a good story Creaks won't let you down.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Highly enjoyable, worth it even if it has a higher price tag than previous Amanita games. Suitable if you like a game that is effectively a sequence of find-your-way-to-the exit puzzles, set in a delightfully surreal context. With some other games' puzzles I hit the feeling that life is too short to  spend hours working out a solution, For me, Creaks pitches the challenge really well. Several times I thought `that's not possible', but persisted and enjoyed working them out without resort to a walkthrough. I love the artwork as usual (apart from the weird paintings, hmm...) and really admire the creativity and care that has gone into Creaks.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Although the game seemed less story-driven and thus had a bit less emotional resonance than other Amanita games, I enjoyed the art, puzzles, and music. Game mechanics are pretty straightforward, but a couple of achievements are overly complex, as are some of the puzzles. I did use walk-throughs when I couldn't get through a scene or achievement after many, many tries. The paintings collected during gameplay are quite bizarre and even unsettling, which I rather enjoyed.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: The beautiful art and sounds of Machinarium but with robust spatial puzzles rather than adventure game silliness. I love "serious" puzzle games and I love the art style so it's a 9/10 for me (would be a 10/10 except the controls are a tad annoying--having to press 3 keys at once just to jump down from a platform, for example.)
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Amanita design doesn't stop to amaze me by their stylistic choices. My only slight complaint would be a bit of repetitive nature of puzzles, but man - I simply don't understand people who write negative reviews because of this aspect. I love everything about this game including its puzzles, I only wish they could be bit diverse and less strictly organised scene-by-scene.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: As always amanita studio never fails to produce great games, incredibly beautiful universe with heart warming drawings. The only thing that I can say is that the gameplay is not what I was expecting. It's not ap oint and click like samarost and machinarium but more like a puzzle game. Still a great adventure
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Creaks was a really enjoyable experience - about 6 hours of gameplay to finish the storyline. I'll definitely do repeat plays to admire the design and artistry. Story was a bit weak and no puzzle was particularly demanding, however this kept the story 'light' made the experience more pleasant and playful. The current price might feel steep to some, however I feel I got my moneys worth from it. Overall rating: 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: That creepy and cute adventure is my treasure!I have not been playing puzzle game enough in my life but I absolutely recommend this game called "Creaks".I am sure that you will be absorbed in beautiful graphics, strange and charming neighbors, and great ambient music. The main puzzles is not too difficult and you can feel so good when you cleared these.  Thank you so much Amanita Design for an amazing time!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game, chillin' and sometimes thrillin' atmosphere with good music. The puzzles are hard but not that hard to lost interest, I love it. Different from Botanicula (which is one of my fav games ever), but it also has a soul, clearly made by people who care and want to give something beautiful and extraordinary.I also loved the small stories told by pictures/character actions. Tha drawing and style is awesome!I recommend it to anyone who likes adventure games and not only want to play to avoid reality or solve puzzles, but to also get involved into a nice story.Thanks Amanita Design!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: (4 out of 5) Creaks is like a relationship. You didn't even know they existed, then you meet and it starts out great. Then you get use to it and it becomes predictable but not bad. Then, as soon as it starts getting better, it suddenly ends leaving you wanting more. After it’s over, you are grateful for the good experience but you wouldn't play it again. You would still recommend it to others tho.First without spoilers.Creaks is a very innovative an experimental puzzle game that is challenging, fun and relaxing. It definitely stands out for its art style and soundtrack. On the negative side, it is very short, repetitive, and has no depth in the story or characters. I mention this because it was a missed opportunity but I understand how difficult it is to develop a game. Definitely don't miss out on this one. I love all of Amanita Designs’ work.SPOILER REVIEWAfter you pass the first 4 or 5 scenes you basically get the idea and it can turn a little boring if you are used to a lot more action and depth in the story. The controls are very simple even after they add the light control. I wouldn't say it is easy, but it is not that hard for the average puzzle gamer, which is the main demo in the first place. It managed to keep me playing for 6 hours straight until I unlocked everything. So it is very short. I wanted to see more in this universe. There are some secret paintings and achievements which honestly, add nothing to the plot or the game and only slow you down. They are there just there to fill time. Also, there are many movies that are fun for a 5 yr old but still they are charming. If you were just to play the actual game, you would finish it in under 3 hours. Honestly, it has no replay value in my book. Unlike other Amanita Designs’ work like Machinarium. I remember I used to play that game over 6 times.If I had to give them score for some relevant features it would look like this:5/5 Art Style5/5 Soundtrack3/5 Story0/5 Unlockables0/5 ReplayabilityMy final score is 4 out of 5 for Creaks for being innovative and not terrible. Also, because I love Amanita Design.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: If you like puzzles, brain teasers, and other things that drive you stark raving mad, you'll love  There are no convoluted controls to master, just your own logic processes. Spread throughout the world are mechanical "paintings," if you will. Some require your input, others do not (at least from what I've seen). Some are mini games in themselves. Some of the paintings are fun to work out; others are annoying. Fortunately, solving them is not crucial to playing the game. The artwork in  is flat out amazing, full of detail and whimsy.Prepare to be challenged.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Creaks is Amanita design's stab at a puzzle/platformer, much like Playdead's games Limbo and Inside. It starts off very much like Silent Hill 4/Alice in Wonderland. You discover a hole in your wall that leads to this huge structure. As you descend, you come to meet a small crew of characters that need your help with a problem. Puzzles are presented in linear fashion, with every ten or so introducing a new enemy or puzzle mechanic. I was never truly stumped, but there were one or two puzzles that I had to take a break and come back to. It amazes me how well of a job Amanita does to develop its characters through animations and noises alone. If I had to levy one criticism against the game, it would be that there are a few puzzles that rely on player timing that can lead to some buggy results (not running back in time might cause a visual glitch, which may give some the false idea that their idea is wrong, but really they just need to execute it faster). Really though, I find it very hard to find much to complain about. The game has a great pace, introduces new ideas consistently, and is always a sheer joy to look at. Christ, I haven't even mentioned the sound. Impeccable sound work and a fantastic score that adapts to your progress in each puzzle.Final thoughts: Creaks has easily the best ending of any Amanita game I've played. It does so much through sheer animation to develop its characters that I was completely floored by the ending. It also features an absolute banger of a song to wrap things up, as is typical of their games. Final thoughts: it's incredible all the little details there is to each individual room. It's like you're slowly descending into this tapestry that's unfolding before you. It reminds me of Silent Hill The Room, Alice in Wonderland, Tom Waits. A truly wonderful experience with a perfect ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: The logic behind every puzzle is unique and extremely creative, which makes each puzzle feel different despite having similar elements. Each new element is introduced at the right time as you get familiar with the current ones. Goes without saying that the music and artwork is amazing, it's Amanita after all. I went in with mixed expectations after having read some bad reviews. But having just finished the game, I don't understand what all the complaining is about.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: The artwork, soundtrack and mechanics of this game are all equally fantastic. If you loved Machinarium, and wanted more, well this is it! The puzzles vary in difficulty from quite easy to really tricky. I personally marvelled at how enticing and complex some of the puzzles were, using only the simple game mechanics combined. The music is totally brilliant again, a true mastery of sounds and mixed use of reverb, with the added bonus that the music increases in complexity and dynamic as you get closer to solving a puzzle. The artwork is intricate, and you can spend a long time just absorbing each scene. Fabulous game, can't wait to play it again!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game again from Amanita Design. If you are a fan of Inside and Limbo, you will love this game. The puzzles aren't hard, but can sometimes get frustrating knowing that you are so close to solving it. A great game overall and totally value for money. Really beautiful art style, soothing background score that doesn't scream over the gameplay and compliments the game really well.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of Amanita, but even so I had my doubts about buying this game. It seemed quite different than Samorost and Machinarium, both visually and in gameplay, and I was afraid that it would be underwhelming in comparison. Eventually though I decided to go for it, and I'm really, really glad that I did. This is one of the most enjoyable and immersive games I've ever played.The idea of an intricate, subconscious underworld of hidden passages and secret backrooms is something I found very appealing and extremely well-executed. Facial expressions are found in every corner, the walls and hallways are imbued with a sense of life and of knowing something you don't. The wonderful music swells and reacts to your actions without interrupting the melody. One of the game's features is finding 'interactive paintings' (at times complex enough to be minigames in their own right), which is sort of how the game feels like to me as a whole - a breathing, interactive artpiece that has your imagination filling in all the negative space. There's a lot of symbolism. It's even emotional, if you let it be.One of the things I was unsure about at first was the gameplay, which some people here complain is 'the same puzzle repeated again and again'. That wasn't my experience at all, but I can see why it's not the type of puzzle you would expect from this studio. In Samorost and Machinarium, they often relied on random association and dream-like logic, which meant that if you got stuck you got STUCK. It was varied and entertaining, but it didn't make much sense and it could occasionally screw up the flow of the game. In contrast, Creaks has very well-defined game mechanics and the puzzles are hard to get really stuck on, because eventually you would exhaust all the possible moves. I found the gameplay to be very fun and engaging. The puzzles are really clever without being hard-for-the-sake-of-being-hard, and progressing towards a solution feels very rewarding. That the same rooms can sometimes have different functions depending on the context is just a lot of fun to see and contributes to the overarching theme of maze-like, interwoven passages.After all that, you get to climb to the round attic of the mini-building you just solved, look out at the frowning kites and windy cliffs in the distance and just sit there for a minute in meditative bliss.I loved Machinarium. This is even better.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Like all Amanita games Creaks was created with love. It has an incredibly beautiful artstile and you shouldn't rush through the game without spending some attention to the background details.The story is cute and the puzzles become challenging, but never too difficult. I just whished there would've been a bit more variation in the puzzle style. But apart from that I've nothing to criticize.In case you already loved Amanitas other games, you'll have a good time!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I completely love this game! I was drawn in by the art (no pun intended), but it's almost as though this game were made specifically for me. Artwork that I absolutely adore, great music, a series of logic puzzles with increasing difficulty, a cast of imaginative creatures, and I swear, as a kid, I used to imagine the furniture in my house coming to life in a very similar fashion. I even recognized the coat rack as a coat rack before I saw it in the light. If you are the sort of person that knows what an Amanita is, without having to Google it, I think it's a safe bet that you will enjoy this game. I give it all the stars!Love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Amanita design shows that they can put out one amazing game after another. The level design, art direction, atmosphere, and music are all top notch. Amanita has always been excellent at telling stories with minimal to no dialogue, and this game continues that trend. The puzzles weren't overly difficult, and the mechanics always made sense to me. I think on average it would take someone 4-6 hours to beat, and I got my money're worth! Looking forward to whatever this studio will make next!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I thought long and hard about whether to give this a thumbs up or not.  I played for almost 10 hours, I completed the game.  I knew this was not going to be Machinarium and to be honest I've had enough of point and click adventures what with Machinarium, Samarost (1,2 and 3), Botanicula and Chuchel.  All excellent games in their own right so I was pleased to see Amanata come with something a bit different.  Graphics and audio absolutely without fault in Creaks.  My issue was the pace and the puzzles.  A very overdone puzzle mechanic - lights on and off, the beam makes things go solid, some characters mirror your movement and so on.  You will have seen it all before.  If it wasn't for the superb graphics and audio that lend themselves to the amazing atmosphere of the game this would be a grade A stinker.  But all that said there is enough here visually and emotionally to render the game enjoyable if a little protracted.  For fans of Amanata definitely check this game out.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Amanita is one of those studios that just can't stop delivering good game after good game even if they wanted to. This time they decided to go for a more lineal puzzle game, being a long series of very short scenes. And they aced it as much as they aced their prior games. If I had to critique it I'd say it doesn't have as much replayability as something like Samorost and Chuchel, and the story is plenty predictable. But that's so minor it feels wrong to even note it. The game's damned good, the puzzles are interesting, the graphics have an incredible degree of attention put to them, the animations are full of little cute details, and the soundtrack is great. If you want a puzzle game, you'll find few more endearing.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the previous games of Amanita design especially Machinarium was a piece of art and the gameplay was awesome.I really can't give Creaks more than 7/10 and there might be one extra point because I really love Amanita design art and style. Best thing about Creaks was the soundtrack made by Hidden orchestra. The art in the game was also great and it was a pleasure for your eyes. The game itself wasn't good.  You only have two different abilities plus simple moving mechanics. Puzzles were abit boring and repetitive. You saw maybe 5 different style of opponents in the whole game and the playtime was 10h when played really slowly. The storyline didn't really make any sense neither did the sidequests. I guess I stopped playing the game like five times before actually finished it. It just wasn't interesting enough. SPOILER ALERT: Suddenly after 9.50h of repetitive puzzles you end up in a bossfight which requires you to make 1 ability to finish the game. The end could not feel more rushed and I just felt completly disapointed.I will buy Amanita design games in the future and really hope to see Machinarium 2 someday. But Creaks gamedesign wasn't on point.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: THE BEST GAME I'VE EVER PLAYED! Checkpoints all the time, Cute and awesome storyline, Creative and amazing game design, Not too easy but not extremely hard when it comes to puzzles, satisfying feeling after each puzzle, creative, not scary, and it contains suspense that'll keep you playing but won't make you want to die!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: 7 hours I needed to finish the plot with all achievements unlocked. At first it might feel a little bit boring but further on this game becomes more and more interesting. Fantastic animations and creativeness. That's what we all expected after Machinarium! So they made it right!Update: Waiting for another gem like this!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another whimsical and weird puzzle/adventure game from Amanita Design. Some of the puzzle mechanics can come off a bit too stereotypical, but for the majority of the puzzles, I enjoyed the designs.  The art is beautifully hand-drawn and incredibly detailed, which is always one of the most impressive aspects of an Amanita Design game, so no disappointment there. Also, the sound design fully embraces the title of Creaks. It's lovely. Check this game out if you like puzzles, amazing art, and whimsy.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Creaks. At first I was a bit annoyed by the dogs and the lack of story, but after the dogs disappeared it became more enjoyable and I realized that taking in the small details of each room is a story in itself. In the end I wished it would go on a bit longer :) (although I love it when a game is short)The only thing which was totally annoying for me was the speed of the animation of my character. I wish he walked more slowly so it does not appear as if I am running away from some danger.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it was an amazing game and pleasant experience.The music and art style were superb and the story narration executed perfectly. The mechanics of the game are presented via an easy puzzle and not through pictures or text. And the puzzles had just the right amount of difficulty. Not too easy so that you can go through the game in under an hour but also not so hard that you just give up on it. Amanita Design has yet to dissapoint!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Creaks is a movement puzzle game, and a more traditional game compared to some of Amanita Design's other games. That doesn't mean its bad, it just, in my opinion, doesn't reach the same heights as Machinarium, Botanicular or Chunchel. The puzzles are fine and of the 50+ puzzles I was only stuck on two of them. They can be gratifying to solve and there are lots of checkpoints so the game can be played in small chunks. The environment is detailed, but there isn't much of a story, so I would recommend it mainly to puzzle fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This has become one of my favorite puzzle games of all time. Some puzzles remind me of Braid and some of games like The Neverhood. Can't recommend it enough.If you're looking for well-designed puzzles and an intriguing and heart-warming story, this is it!Go buy it instead of reading this review, it will be worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another imaginative and beautifully artistic puzzle from Amanita Designs!  The landscape is intriguing, the puzzles are neither too difficult, nor too easy, but you'll need to piece things together to progress.  I've just begun, and can't say enough good things about the game.  It is one of the few games with true integrity in design.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I came to this expecting another Machinarium, but other than some style crossover, it's a very different game. The game mechanics are closer to a level based puzzle game, that slowly increases in complexity as you go. The difficulty was just enough to make it not too easy, but hard enough that it had my scratching my head at a couple of points and was pleased when I finally worked it out. It's beautifully made and I enjoyed every minute of playing it, including the little mini-games inbetween each level.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I went in expecting a point and click adventure game but I am by no means disappointed. It's more of a puzzle-platformer but it's executed extremely well. The game has a great art style and wonderful music as well as puzzles that are intuitive but will still make you think. If you are on the fence about this one definitely pick it up, its a work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful and gloomy. A wonderful change of pace from Amanita Designs. If you love their quirky characters, beautiful art and challenging puzzles you will love Creaks. It is more linear than other games making it less frustrating and more engaging. Though it is their first game where you control the character like a platformer, it plays extremely well and they integrate movement into the game wonderfully. Thanks for a great experience Amanita! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely brilliant coming together of imagination! Amanita once again go above and beyond to give my brain a little vacation to some magical place. After playing Samorost and Machinarium numerous times, I was a little worried about the first couple of minutes of the game. I thought it was going to be dull without the brighter colours and the click and explore game play. I have been well and truly turned full circle once I got into it and realised the true beauty of the game. The wonderful visuals, sounds, characters and mini paintings are all works of art.  The depth and planning gone into the puzzles is incredible, a few have had me well and truly stumped for some moments. A true pleasure to play, and I'm fairly certain my little brain is getting a mini decent workout.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another wonderful game from Amanita Design. Very much enjoyed the puzzle platformer aspect alongside their usual wonderful visual and audio design. The pacing was great, seeing different elements and skills converge during puzzles was fantastic, and nothing overstayed its welcome. All in all, another great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Throughout the beginning of this game I found the controls a bit clunky and the puzzles a little annoying. But getting deeper into it I got the hang of the controls and started to find the puzzles more interesting and fun. The story was nice and the look of the game  is impeccable like a lot of what Amanita Design produces. They're one of my favorite game developers and I found  to be a worthwhile and fun puzzle-platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Another masterpiece by Amanita Design. I just cannot describe how much I love the Samorost series, Machinarium, and now Creak. These games give me some kind of feeling. Just takes me to another world, leaves me wanting more. I wish I could get lost in this universe. Can't recommend enough!!buuuuuut still would love to see a Machinarium 2 ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: The challenging puzzles, the visual art, the music, the sound design, the storytelling and the overall atmosphere are all astonishing and add up to an amazing game! You very rarely encounter a game with such unique vibes and integrity! I'd like to say a huge thank you to everyone in the team who made this possible! Best of luck with making more amazing games in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: This one is different from their other games. The puzzles aren't "quest based" where you get an item to get another item to get another item. The puzzles are logic based and cleverly designed. You feel genuinely satisfied figuring them out. I kind of like this because you aren't randomly clicking objects praying something would work.  I get they were trying to make enemies into household objects, but I wish some enemies possessed unique properties. For an instance, an enemy could turn into a fan using wind as a mechanic. All the enemies became blocks you push buttons with. Art style is fantastic like always. Recommended for puzzle lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: My kind of Amantia Design game.. have been waiting for something a little more coherent from them since Machinarium. Not to say their others aren't all great, but some are more experimental point and click and arty, where as Creaks and Machinarium are more sequential puzzle based, building on simple ideas and pushing your brain further each time. Of course the art style is still amazing, detailed and lovingly crafted, and there is still the charm and quirk I love from all the games, but this one so far feels more refined which I am really enjoying. Yet to complete so can't comment on how hard it gets, but i'm in for the ride regardless as i know this team always know how to make me smile!
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Gives me Coraline vibes but with a charming steampunk-like appeal.For me personally the puzzles were a bit on the easier side but still challenging enough nontheless. You get introduced to new "monsters" which add a new puzzle dynamic as you progress through the story.Artwork is beautiful and the characters are charming. Definitely a must buy for any puzzle lover.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Reminded me of classics of my youth like Fish Fillets or even Quadrax but with very nice and fresh style that also fits today's larger monitors very nicely. I don't get the negative reviews based on the fact that this game is different from the other Amanita Design titles - yes, this one is more focused on puzzles, but it does not deserve this backlash at all. The graphics and soundtrack are brilliant as well as sounds of the monsters and other 'creaks', and although I haven't finished the game yet, I like the puzzles a lot! I Highly recommend this game for anyone looking for a great puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Classic Amanita game with great art and great music. Not point and click though, it is a puzzle platformer and I really liked it. Finished in 3 sessions 5 hours total. Puzzles are not too easy but they did not require hours to solve. I really enjoyed solving them. Story and other elements are perfect. I was waiting this game for about one year. I am definitely satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game. First of all if you like the game Braid, you'll like this too. Game mechanics were better than point and click. Puzzles and atmosphere are so much fun. (and hard) The only thing I didn't like was the story. Characters, monsters they are all so cute but I was expecting something more at the end.  Another thing I d like to say is while having progress in the game, when we go down and down, there was water. And I was like ''Yeah! There is an episode of sewer adventure or underwater adventure with sea creatures too.'' But then... The End. I recommend this game because there is no much artistic 2D game like this. But after the great Machinarium and 11 years, I guess I was expecting more from Amanita Design.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: So i don't play a ton of video games, and leave even less reviews. But i have to say this game is a real treat. Amazing puzzle game with some amazing art features and the music is awesome. I can't wait to play other games like this. If you need something to push you to get this game, let this comment be it.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Sweet experience. The story was simple but great. I like the characters and especially the atmosphere. Actually that's what about Creak mainly is, about atmosphere :-) The puzzles were great too, not as hard as in Machinarium, but sometimes quite challenging. The only thing I didn't like was that it ends eventually. The game is not thaat long, so play it carefully (don't play it at once). It's best at nights for an hour or two :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A little over an hour into the game and the puzzles are pretty much the same. In fact it feels like an Amanita game crossed with the old Another World or Flashback games. I was hoping for more puzzle variation like Machinarium or Samarost.I like the platformer aspect of the game, but so far it's just too simple. I'd still recommend if you're a fan of Amanita's design aesthetic in their games. If the puzzles get more interesting I'll update this review.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a fan of Amanita games, but Creaks is just excellent.The game reminds me of Talos Principle, being somewhere in between a puzzle game and a puzzle-platformer. The puzzles are all essentially in the same style but gradually introduce new mechanics. There are about 40 main puzzle screens. Precise timing or precise positioning is never required. There are the same wonderful baffling moments as in Talos Principle when it seems that there can't be a solution with what you're given. But after figuring out the solution, the puzzles can be completed in under a minute. Overall, the puzzle difficulty is average.The graphics are exceptionally beautiful, with lots of amusing details (the map, the family tree, the Egyptian elements, the small background animations). The paintings are something unique. The animations are probably even more impressive: the game tells a story with animated cutscenes which are very smooth and detailed and happen inside the game levels rather than being detached from the rest of the game. Animations are also used to provide hints for the puzzle mechanics.The setting and the story are perhaps less abstract than in other Amanita games, while still having the right amounts of cuteness, absurdity and humor.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed playing this game. Most similar to Machinarium in visual style which I liked, but missed the variety of landscape and quirky worlds seen in Samorost. The puzzles increased in difficulty but never to an impossible level. I played through the whole thing in 6.5 hours so only a short game - I would have expected a little more game play for the price, particularly as some puzzle adventure games can take at least 3 times as long for not much more money. The music was great, very similar in style to other Amanita Design games. The characters and their little voices were amusing. So overall a positive experience and it will have replay value - even now I've missed a few secret rooms so can go back and look for those.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully crafted game with delightful graphics and and superb soundtrack. Puzzles are pleasantly straightforward but get fiendishly more complex towards the end. You can certainly feel the passion the developers have put into this incredibly creative piece of art. A pure pleasure to play and puts many AAA games to shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

_childDocuments_.review: Just a few minutes into Creaks, you will bump into some strange barking creatures in the mansion’s dark corridors. But are they as dangerous as they seem? Try to get them trapped under a beam of light and take a closer look. You may find out that what felt dangerous is a simple night table. Turning these creatures into ordinary objects is the key gameplay mechanic, along with pulling levers, stepping on pressure plates, and manipulating the environment to outsmart your enemies. [Radim Jurda]
_childDocuments_.name: Creaks

name: The Waylanders
detailed_description: AN EPIC STORY INSPIRED BY CELTIC MYTHOLOGY The first meeting between the Celts and their gods, the Tuatha de Danaan, should have been a time of celebration and enlightenment, but when negotiations go catastrophically wrong, a battle against a god leaves you near death and untethered from time! Return to a land overtaken by magickal corruptions and a kingdom splintered into multiple factions warring for the throne. The Celtic society, a complex tapestry of different religions, human cultures, and mortal and immortal races such as the Mourians, Werewolves, Goblins, and monsters threaten to tear at every seam. Will you support the immature, yet rightful, heir, or the pragmatic general in their bid for the throne? What alliances will you forge, what friendships will you foster, what romances will you pursue, and... what will you do when you are suddenly thrust into Medieval Spain? EXPLORE TWO ERAS Things look pretty different in Galicia under Christianity than it did under Celtic rule. Magic is fading, religion is everywhere, and much has changed. Where are your immortal allies now, and what has become of the souls of your mortal friends? Discover changes made to the land over a thousand years of cultural change. Could the corrupt magicks that interfered during your meeting with the Tuatha have led to the destruction of all that the Celtic world held dear? GATHER YOUR PARTY The Waylanders draws inspiration from classic RPG, opening up a world of adventure for you and your companions to explore. Use real time with pause to strategically select party member combat spells and abilities to defeat roving bandits, rampaging beasts, monsters of legend, and more! Discover a treasure trove of weapons, armour, trinkets, and more to outfit your party through your journey. With gods standing in your way, you’ll need every edge you can get. COMPANION FORMATIONS MAKE THE DIFFERENCE The companions who set out alongside you on your journey make a massive difference in how you’ll overcome enemies. Different party class makeups grant a variety of Formation options, each with powerful offensive and defensive abilities. As you level up, unlock new classes, and explore, you’ll discover new Formations and formation abilities to add to your roster. MAIN FEATURES The Waylanders is an exciting fantasy RPG inspired by classics such as Dragon Age: Origins, Neverwinter Nights, and Baldur’s Gate. Travel Between Eras - Time travel between two distinct eras: Celtic and Medieval. Meet old allies and discover reborn friends as you step from past to the future A Story Like No Other - The Waylanders blends Celtic myth from the Spanish region of Galicia with exciting fantasy adventure Faithful Companions - Befriend nine mortal and immortal companions to join you on your journeys through Celtic and Medieval Galicia. Discover their past, bond through special missions, and romance your favorites Lands to Discover in Two Era - Explore more than 50 regions filled with quests, secrets, and enemies in both the Celtic and Medieval era Multiple endings - Choices made in one time period have dire future consequences. Players will feel the impact of their decisions in surprising and shocking ways Strategic tactical combat - Unique party formation abilities based on characters and classes open up deep, tactical combat options. Different party makeups unlock special offensive attacks and defensive abilities like Daggertip, Phalanx, Golem and Conclave. about_the_game: AN EPIC STORY INSPIRED BY CELTIC MYTHOLOGY The first meeting between the Celts and their gods, the Tuatha de Danaan, should have been a time of celebration and enlightenment, but when negotiations go catastrophically wrong, a battle against a god leaves you near death and untethered from time! Return to a land overtaken by magickal corruptions and a kingdom splintered into multiple factions warring for the throne. The Celtic society, a complex tapestry of different religions, human cultures, and mortal and immortal races such as the Mourians, Werewolves, Goblins, and monsters threaten to tear at every seam. Will you support the immature, yet rightful, heir, or the pragmatic general in their bid for the throne? What alliances will you forge, what friendships will you foster, what romances will you pursue, and... what will you do when you are suddenly thrust into Medieval Spain? EXPLORE TWO ERAS Things look pretty different in Galicia under Christianity than it did under Celtic rule. Magic is fading, religion is everywhere, and much has changed. Where are your immortal allies now, and what has become of the souls of your mortal friends? Discover changes made to the land over a thousand years of cultural change. Could the corrupt magicks that interfered during your meeting with the Tuatha have led to the destruction of all that the Celtic world held dear? GATHER YOUR PARTY The Waylanders draws inspiration from classic RPG, opening up a world of adventure for you and your companions to explore. Use real time with pause to strategically select party member combat spells and abilities to defeat roving bandits, rampaging beasts, monsters of legend, and more! Discover a treasure trove of weapons, armour, trinkets, and more to outfit your party through your journey. With gods standing in your way, you’ll need every edge you can get. COMPANION FORMATIONS MAKE THE DIFFERENCE The companions who set out alongside you on your journey make a massive difference in how you’ll overcome enemies. Different party class makeups grant a variety of Formation options, each with powerful offensive and defensive abilities. As you level up, unlock new classes, and explore, you’ll discover new Formations and formation abilities to add to your roster. MAIN FEATURES The Waylanders is an exciting fantasy RPG inspired by classics such as Dragon Age: Origins, Neverwinter Nights, and Baldur’s Gate. Travel Between Eras - Time travel between two distinct eras: Celtic and Medieval. Meet old allies and discover reborn friends as you step from past to the future A Story Like No Other - The Waylanders blends Celtic myth from the Spanish region of Galicia with exciting fantasy adventure Faithful Companions - Befriend nine mortal and immortal companions to join you on your journeys through Celtic and Medieval Galicia. Discover their past, bond through special missions, and romance your favorites Lands to Discover in Two Era - Explore more than 50 regions filled with quests, secrets, and enemies in both the Celtic and Medieval era Multiple endings - Choices made in one time period have dire future consequences. Players will feel the impact of their decisions in surprising and shocking ways Strategic tactical combat - Unique party formation abilities based on characters and classes open up deep, tactical combat options. _childDocuments_.review: So this is my launch-day experience so far:--)When I tried it in Early Access I was certain there were missing cutscenes in the very beginning since it goes from, and sorry but that is hardly a spoiler, calm dialogue on the ship instantly to:-The King is wounded, possibly dying-We are on the island-Apparently we met the gods, pissed them off and they attacked us-Everything is burning and where the earlier cutscenes told us nobody, not a single person is on the island according to scouts there suddenly are now hordes of... I dunno... wild savages or something, INCLUDING their very prominent and obvious tents and fireplaces....So I think you can imagine my surprise when that was STILL happening in the release version of the game.Just some short dialogue tidbits that summarize what could have been a 2-15 minute long, epic, cutscene.Which is funny because a bit later the game loves to do cutscenes for the tiniest things it feels like.--) Next point:The writing.It is ...er... how do I put it?Off.Like for every line that fits the mythical setting in the past, full of immortal beings, gods, magic and worldbuilding you have 2-5 F-Bombs, thousand-year-old leaders of immortal beings acting like some teenager or phrasing that reminds me more of Pulp Fiction (granted I love PF but it is a grating juxtaposition that just doesn't work).The Voice Actors are actually quite decent to outstanding in places but the dialogue script is constantly at odds with how the lore of the world and the background of the characters are described in the codex for instance.I am regularly torn between wanting to snerk at the humor and cringe in every 2nd or 3rd line most characters say.I think mostly the writing just feels... immature.Which is a total miss for a game starring people being alive for centuries if not millennia. Humans in their twenties manage to have more grace, gravitas or charm than those supposedly immortals."Plus I'm charming as ♥♥♥♥." is one of the very first lines you hear from a person not only thousands of years old, mastered a ton of magic, can see the past and future of people AND is the leader of an entire culture.I don't know about you but to me that just disqualified the entire moment and character.Most characters in the first hour of the game also seem to throw little hissy-fits here and there and generally behave like petulant children. Which would be fiiine if there was supposed to be MORE than one immature character in the story at that moment. But, and this is funnily ironic, the one character that is supposed to be immature according to the others talking about him has less childish, cringeworthy lines than most others.Again, I do not know what the team was going for. Maybe I just can't see it, but for me it was like getting served mc-curly fries within my Black Forest gateau.I love that cake. And when I want junk food I love curly fries.Doesn't mean I want them sharing space on my tongue at the same time.--) And last but not least... COMBAT:I knew from EA that I probably was doing something wrong back in EA when I dabbled with the first few areas of the game.Individually, and without obsessive handholding from YOUR side your party members will run into their deaths as if an eternity of booze, drugs, sex and whatever was the reward for dying.Seriously, it's like the AI has a death wish.In the first area you can turn the entire problem on it's head by using the FORMATION you get from one, and only one mind you, of your NPC party members. Since the formation just removes the party members and replaces them with the formation you essentially have a free health pool and, admittedly, really cool and useful abilities.So you can run the entire island at the start by just going in formation and facerolling over multiple waves of enemy reinforcements that kinda leave you battered, bruised and drained of class-resources otherwise.What I took from that is basically "Okay, formations good. I want formations."Skip forward a bit...First combat after exiting the otherworld:Party of 5, player character included, versus 3(!!) guys.First attempt - most of the party dead.Second attempt - managed to get through by babysitting the suicidal AI like a rabies-infested mother-hen... had to heal up my party to full health using spells though as most were below 30%.Most of my party has around 250-290 HP each.The Weak Archer guy had 300+ HP and the two melee guys had 650+ HP... so they were tough little nuts to crack.Now the NEXT encounter looks like this:Cutscene and dialogue straight into combat with no pre-combat prep chances. Okay. Don't love it but okay.Half a dozen guys rush my party. Two of which are ranged I believe. Rest are 600+HP beefcakes that like to eat healers for breakfast.Before even HALF of those people are downed already the next wave comes in, with casters and archers happily peppering my still engaged party with utter impunity because in the narrow path another 3 or 4 beefcake melee guys are already charging into the fray.Somehow, don't ask me how, I manage to get through that clusterf-...Only to see I am still engaged in combat, I am shot at by two sides from enemies half a football statium away, and the best thing?...:One archer sits BEHIND A TURTLE FORMATION of enemies with and behind THAT, leading up to the bridge a RANGED FORMATION is pelting me with arrows.That is not even including about another half-dozen enemies, some just teleporting in it seems, that want to murderf- my party.Now... I know what you are saying: "What about using the formation you mentioned earlier?"Well, that one died with the guy on that island apparently.You unlock your first formation at level 3 and ALL characters are level two at that point with no way of earning EXP before that. So there is that.Not only do they take away a core combat feature from you, they pit you against over a dozen enemies (each of which has at least as much or up to DOUBLE HP than your guys) AND two formations at the same time!--) Interface and general interaction with the world:Mouse look at Maximum sensitivity is still like you drag a camera with lead tied to it with one wrist.The way mouse look turns feels weird. Mouse smoothing or accelleration shennanigans would be my guess.Moving around is tedious. WASD sends your character into the cardinal directions depending on your camera's viewpoint.Q and E rotate the camera, which is arguably better than mouse look tbh, as bad as that may sound.You can right-click to move but it's clunky and not just in combat. Combat just makes it worse. Possible pathfinding issue?Oh and I got stuck in little blood "river" when I wanted to go to the Gate of Exile which you could walk over perfectly one moment and was an invisible barrier the next. So that happened.Whenever you want to go to the options, map, inventory or anything else but the main game screen the whole screen fades to black and fades back in over 1-2 seconds. When you just want to check the map, change settings or do quick inventory stuff this gets old really fast. I swear I probably spent less time in those screens than I do in the FadeToBlack transitions back and forth half the time I go into any menu.Right now I am just exhausted and have given up for the moment.I can dig the artstyle. I looove the setting, the races, the worldbuilding.I am a sucker for mythology and celtic myths get waaayyy too little attention anyway.I really want to like this game.But the constant jumble between the writings TONE and SETTING, the dialogues and the clunky combat... not to mention the encounter design that apparently thinks fighting around 2 dozen enemies that have more health than you do is somehow appropriate at LEVEL TWO after you just left the tutorial is a good idea and fine.I only hope the team manages to pull a "No Man's Sky" and turn this thing around after a few months and/or years.But right now I just can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an intriguing stetting and location that's not often explored in video games. I backed the game on kickstarter because it showed great promise. When I got to play it on early access I was not impressed but I decided to wait for a full release to see if things improved.The game still has some jank and I also had a bug that prevented me to continue the story after defeating the first boss. Bugs can be ironed out and I have to say that the game can be charming and look really good. What I can't get past unfortunately is the writing. I saw an interview with one of the writers with Gamespot mentioning the decision of writing the dialog in a more modern fashion but to me it just breaks my immersion. The constant use of modern English slang like a druid calling other character a "dipsh*t" or other character saying that they're "charming as f*ck" or that they "tick all the boxes", I don't know, it doesn't feel natural. It's not just that the dialog is modern, it's the specific choices they made - most of the time it comes out as edgy just for the sake of it. This makes the game really difficult to enjoy.Anyway, the devs mentioned plans to dub the game in Spanish and I will give it another try by then.

_childDocuments_.review: there's a good game somewhere beneath a pile of bugs, glitches and just bonkers game-designthe art-design is pretty impressive, heck even the general visual design and quality are pretty goodthere has been a lot of time and effort put into world building, backround lore (codex inclusive, item-describtions, etc.)and the corpse of a "good" tactical-realtime-with pause-crpg includedbut that's pretty much where the "good" endsthe writing...i mean it's not just that the whole game sounds like Gothic on steroids, the amount of cursing is legendary. it's also that it's often hillariously cringy. most characters are pretty much dad-jokes come to life, one of the writers wanted to be a comedian in real life...there's no other explanation that makes sense. it's something you gotta hear and see to believe it. one moment a critical character dies, the next moment someone crack's a joke about how "tiny" another party-member is...the VO sports some well known actors, which either phoned in their lines or hadn't had the first clue about what happened while their lines were playing. mix that with horrible sound-mixing and the VO leaves a lot to be desired.the character system is stuffed with a lot of things that you usualy don't find in games like this: aka "strength" ups "resiliance" (mitigation), which leads to very strange numerical values, that are pretty out there and end up beeing mildly confusing for no reason. the U.I. is just...i don't know how to describe it: if you hover over an item to compare it's stats to your equiped counterpart you get to see the (weird) stats of the item, but only % differences of the newly selcted item. the U.I. doesn't scale? even playing 1080p it's tiny. if you want to play this game like say a Baldur's Gate...good luck hitting a skill/item and an enemy mid combat....or reading text (unless you play with your nose on the screen)i mean i could go on and onbut the state of the game says it all:-place-holder-text right in the character creation menu and all over the place, heck even in the options menue (HDR)-settings not working properly (v-sync only works after turning it off and on actualy ingame), the difficulty settings pretty much don't do what they say-missing VO, specific skips of certain text-lines or just a complete missmatch-items without ingame models (in general helms are shown on character, but within an hour i found mutliple helms doing nothing visualy), items without stats, buggy items not behaving like their counterparts (unable to stack for example)-one of the worsed sound-design i've seen in an crpg. many sounds are not loud enough, other sounds are completely missing (many skills and spells, got practicaly no effect), in-combat sounds are just miserable and combat feels and sounds more like a silent movie, which extends to conversations and ingame cutscenes-no real haptic-feedback, the game feels incredible floaty. hitting an enemy leads pretty much to 0 reaction, many skills got so tiny an animation effect that it's nigh impossible to see if it actualy worked...especialy combined with the sound-design-jarring pacing, which leads back to the writing. especialy at the beginng of the game you will sit there asking yourself "what's going on?". as it seems this was a deliberate choice, which tells about everything you need to know about the writing. the brake in pacing and cohesion is so jarring that many believed (myself included) it to have been missing cut-scenes-quest-markers shown at the start of the game, and disappearing again right after the game "realy" starts-heck even the U.I. and thus the inventory/journal/codex, etc. completely missing any feedback, aka no sound effects, etc.-the ingame mouse-pointer design only kicks in after alt-tabbin out of the game and back in, otherwise you get the standart windows-mouse-pointer..which just doesn't fit at all-don't even try running the game none windowed, which probably coalesces with the technical state of the game...i mean just watch that RAM usagei mean i could go on...but you see the picturecalling this a gold-release is downright offensivethere's a decent game buried beneath here, but even when you lower your expectations you will be shocked just by the state this "gold-release" is in...a real shame.

_childDocuments_.review: I was SO excited for this game. I heard about it a couple years ago and, as a huge Dragon Age fan, could not wait until it was released... However. This game is not complete. Until such a time as it is complete, I just can't recommend it.First, as other reviews have noted, it lacks polish: there are weird visual glitches in the cut scenes;  plenty of bugs; TONS of typos in the English subtitles/flavor text; bits of raw code showing up where item names/descriptions should be; people showing up as interactable on the map with whom you can't actually interact (or whose interactions are just basic NPC barks instead of cutscenes/quest-giving); etc etc. But there are also some serious pacing issues. I like the story, love fantasy RPGs with romanceable companions, but holy moly it feels like giant chunks of the storylines and character development have been cut for time. For example, Tiana's story is confusing to me; her dad is a jerk, and he's trying to make her the leader against your theoretical candidate, the True Heir. But then he lets someone use magic once, and she says "you promised me NO MAGIC" and leaves. The reason for this is not clear until one of your friends makes a comment that magic is causing the corruption, so no one should be using magic. She uses magic, so she leaves your party, but you have Amergin still, and then the PC can potentially use magic, but as far as I've played, this massive-seeming plot hole is never mentioned again. No one seems concerned that one (or more) members of your party could be endangering themselves. Also, maybe I wasn't following the story closely enough, but the link between corruption and magic use wasn't something I had picked up on at ALL until that point, which seems like a huge plot point to leave unclear! Anyways, after that inexplicable "magic BAD" cutscene, Tiana suddenly sends word to your ship that she wants to meet up at a pub. If you go, she is suddenly talking about her soldiers, who are evidently fighting against her dad's soldiers, and she wants your help finding a lost regiment of hers...????? When did any of that happen? How was one of her dad's guards using a single spell ONE time enough to cause her to turn her back on him and literally engage in guerilla warfare against him? Also, at this point in the story: WHO IS THIS LADY? Why do I trust her enough to help her? Wasn't she JUST under her evil dad's thumb?Don't get me wrong: Tiana being uncomfortable with being used by her father for his xenophobic kingmaking bullsh*t, being worried about his use of magic spreading the corruption, and slowly breaking away from his influence to dramatically stand against him as one of three potential choices to take the crown is not a bad story! But it happened so fast it was legitimately confusing. That good-in-theory story is instead stilted and rushed.Similarly, another reviewer mentioned this already, but dang, Amergin, you move fast, bro. I did like ONE quest with him and he's like "I love you and I would throw everything I care about away to be with you." I like him as a character and would have been interested in pursuing that, but it happened so fast, and my only options were to turn him down or to tell him (paraphrasing), "omg I've been waiting for SO LONG for you!! I love you, too! Let's be together!" And like...eugh. Just another story element that obviously wasn't given enough room to develop. Ironically, though, Amergin is now on the ship doomed to repeat that cringey confession any time I interact with him, so I guess if I change my mind in the future, I'll always have the chance to take him up on it. Now, about cultural stuff (note: I am not Irish, just married to an Irish person, so I do not speak for Irish people and I apologize for any inaccuracies here): I find it really weird that they didn't source Irish voice actors for at least the characters who literally live in Ireland. Some of them have what sound to me like English accents, which is borderline offensive. Tiana, the girl whose dad tried to put her on the throne by proclaiming that she will be a full-blooded Celtic ruler for the Celtic people, seems to have an American voice actor. I'm not saying the voice acting is bad (though sometimes a little stilted, and there are some big pronunciation issues--see below), but this seems like a super obvious and easy thing to have done to make the game more immersive and feel like you're playing a game set in, you know, Ireland. With Irish characters and gods and beings. It also strikes me personally as ethically sketchy to borrow the stories/culture/language of an indigenous group and then hire no actors from that group to actually tell that story. Media companies get dinged for this sort of thing all the time, so I find it hard to believe the dev team had no awareness it might be an issue. I also find it hard to believe that it would be too difficult to find good Irish voice actors. But I digress...Finally, a thing that bothers me a lot but is probably least likely to bother most players: the voice actors and writing staff don't seem to have gotten consistent coaching on how to pronounce/spell words in Irish. Different characters will pronounce the same word two different ways, and on at least one occasion I believe the same character correctly pronounced and then later mispronounced a word (I speak some Irish thanks to my husband and mother-in-law, so it is very obvious to me when this happens). Some words are just never pronounced correctly, as far as I've played. It doesn't feel like the team had an Irish speaker coaching or reviewing the dialogue--or, at least not consistently. An example: "Fir Bolg" has been pronounced correctly (as far as I've seen), but "Inisfáil" has been mispronounced like "Inish-fayil." A few names that appear to be Irish names aren't pronounced correctly for Irish. "Inisfáil" is a good example for the related problem of the lack of proofreading (or ability to proofread) Irish words used in the story. To my count, it's spelled at least three different ways: the correct Inisfáil, "Inisfail," and "Inisfial." There are multiple Irish words that are spelled with and without their accent marks at different parts of the game. The dev team is Spanish, so surely they understand that a word missing an accent mark is a word misspelled. As previously mentioned, the game does have just a lot of typos generally, so perhaps this is just part of that larger problem. But again, for a game that's taking so heavily from Irish culture/history/mythology, it seems like the writing team should've taken care to compile a handbook of terms with a special section for Irish words and their correct spelling/pronunciations.  Further, having three different spellings for the name of the island *where the main story of the entire game kicks off* is just sloppy, and it's worse when it's getting a real (and very endangered) language wrong.WOW this has been a long review. I'm incredibly frustrated because I'm SO disappointed! Even ignoring my linguistic observations, the game is just not finished. It feels like a tiny studio tried to make nearly a AAA game and, in so doing, severely underestimated their limitations. If some of the extremely resource-intensive flair (e.g. cinematic 3D cut scenes) hadn't been prioritized, maybe we'd have a game with a cogent, well-paced story with meaningful romances, acceptable proofreading, and no game-killing bugs. But we don't. And it's a damn shame.

_childDocuments_.review: Full preview: The Waylanders has a lot of potential to be the next good party-based RPG but this Early Access build makes for a poor first impression. Even if you excuse all the usual Early Access tropes like missing assets,features and bugs the game is let down by its clunky combat, terrible performance and the unstable nature of it. _childDocuments_.review: Very, very rough. Let me guide you through my magical experience with this game's early access.Character creation was rather simplistic, and I don't mean comestically (though that is simple too) but role playing wise, basically the only thing you get to pick besides race/class are your character's starting atributes, which if their descriptions are to be believed affect very little. There were no perks or skills to choose from, and while none of these are mandatory, it did feel a bit barebones. Closer to Dragon Age Inquisition than Origins.Oh yeah there is also a background to choose from but it didn't affect anything besides my clothing as far as I got.Next we are taken to a cutscene, a king is speaking with an advisor on a ship and right away two problems are obvious, one easily fixable, anotehr not so much. First the characters voices aren't normalized, some sound loud and clear while others are very low to the point of being drowned by the music (also the subtitles rarely match the dialogue). The second, much bigger problem is the writing. One of the topics of the dialogue is the prince who has been assigned to the advisor for care. The king admonishes the advisor for letting him party through the night and the advisor's reply goes something like this "Ouch, very true, but ouch, sir". There is a sudden and completely jarring change of tone from formal and faux medieval to something that sounds like a teen drama. This tonal shift happens often and no, it doesn't get better. Some cutscenes go by with the same voice and tone problems and we're given control of our MC. The controls and camera are a bit clunky and so is the interface. For example when talking to npcs you can only see three topics at once; if there are more you need to scroll down, It's not that the font is particularly big, mind you, it's just that the text is down at the very bottom of the screen. But I guess this is the least of our problems and the kind of things devs fix on early access.Some more inconsistant dialogue later the game makes a time skip to an action scene and we're given control again. We come face to face with the combat: you click on enemies once and your character auto attacks it until it dies. I guess a lot of good wrpgs use this method but even in dragon age origins you had skills to choose from at the start. The point of making a retro game should be to learn from the past and improve on it with the lessons of the present, imo. Then we find the prince stuck below a tree, "a skill check", I thought. Nope, my minimum strength mage easily lifted the log all on his lonesome. The prince automatically joins our party (i think he says like one line) then we advance though the map clicking on stuff we want to die and collecting mute party members who don't know to use their skills unless we manually tell them to, until we make it to the king. New cutscene, more people join the party and we get a special notification for one of them and even get to chose one fo two classes for them...i guess he's a main characters?We're now controlling a small army of mutes, (baldur's gate 1 had more voice acting than this) and we keep walking and clicking on things until... oops! clicking doesn't work anymore. For some reason i can't pick up loot or order my main character to attack enemies. I save and load the game to see if that fixes the problem but now enemies have respawned on top of us and no one is attacking, they just sit there waiting to die.I've honestly played rpg maker demos with more polish than this. I don't recommend it at all, at least for now.Seriously thinking of asking for a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because I like to support independent RPG's.  I'm fairly forgiving in this aspect, I'll defend a studio if I think they have promise.There is no promise here, I am genuinely sorry to say.The dialogue is modern.  Weird, for a game specifically set in Celtic myth, but okay.  Forgivable, on its own.However, it's also not terribly well written.  Actually, that's an exaggeration. It's badly written, with moments of inspiration.The story could be, and has the potential to be, interesting, but the execution is awful.  It has the feeling of a game presented with 30% of the product that was intended.  And that 30% does not present well.  Every character feels "peculiar", or idiosyncratic, without any buildup to explain them or why they are the way they are.  "Oh, you're from a race of miserable subterranean cannibals, but you're a cheery lighthearted person?  How weird!"  No explanation necessary, or given.Saying all that, the game crashes regularly.  Quite regularly.Some of these aspects could be forgivable from a new developer, but altogether this just feels like a half-assed cash grab.  Or, more likely,  a group that set their ambitions far beyond their abilities and eventually gave up and just pushed a product out that they are undoubtedly ashamed of.  I'd tell you to judge which you think it is, but then you'd have to buy it, and I don't recommend that.I'll modify this review if the game gets updated and improved, but I don't have high hopes.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm all for backing a good game, but it feels  insulting to release a game in this state and get people to pay £27 for it. Also please stop telling me this is similar to dragon age origins!! I understand early access is meant to be buggy, but even without the crash to desktops and my pc having to be physically restarted there isn't the groundwork for a good game. Runescape classic has more character customisation options. The animations are super clunky. Even just walking, which is mainly what you do so far. The combat is literally just click to auto attack and watch your ai companion sprint off.  Looting is a 'fun' game where you have to click on a tiny object hidden in grass to pick it up, while watching your ai companion sprint off to the next npc to kill. There's no point picking a race as it doesn't impact anything so far.  There's no stat bonuses, none of the npcs react differently. One of the first npcs tells me what my own race is as if I'm 5 years old. There doesn't seem to be any cohesion between the main characters and the style of voice over. The audio for the voice over changes levels and is really jarring. The tone of the story is really hard to follow - its hard to tell if it's suppose to be tongue in cheek or serious. Some of the characters are very cartoonish, while others are super serious. The conversation options are like picking Wikipedia entries and super dry. Normally I love hearing dialogue but, honestly, it was a drag. I don't want to spoil it, but the story is so jarring too. At one moment you're on a boat and the next you're randomly fighting on an island, with no explanation of a blackout or anything.
