_childDocuments_.review: The Waylanders is not finished and it likely never will be. From the very beginning, you'll be seeing the phrase “missing string” with some regularity. Subtitles are a must as voice overs will just cut out at random. Vendors will show a full stock one moment, then completely empty inventories the next. And that's just the first half, the bit that stayed in Early Access long enough to get some measure of polish. After the promised time jump, that when things truly go of the rails. The main city hub, where you'll need to get and turn in many of your quests, will go black with shadows constantly and stutter every few minutes as the church bells go off. A handful of quests seem to be impossible to complete, either because an area is inaccessible or because it will never update. Every other cutscene at this point is missing some of its voice overs and most of the 'off-book' character classes don't have any description for their new abilities, not even a “missing string”. Unsurprisingly,  this is also the point where the fatal errors become more regular. But thankfully there seem to be an infinite amount of save slots. So even with that barrage of issues, as long as you're saving frequently and in new slots, as any older RPG would have trained you to do, you should be able to play through this game just fine. The state The Waylanders currently exists in is more of a proof of concept and it'd be so much easier to dismiss it as the buggy mess it is if that concept wasn't so damn good. You have to start with the historical/mythological connections, because the game clearly does. It even uses its deviation from those myths as one its main plot points. It may seem like an average fantasy setting with some ancient Celtic flair at first. But doing a quick search for some the characters or set pieces will bring up Wikipedia as often as it does fan sites. Íth, Míl Espáine, The Urco, Tower of Hercules, Master Mateo: all of these are real people and places or real to someone long before they showed up in this game. I was even taught a bit of trivia about the pilgrims of the latter time period from a random side quest.As intriguing as the real world connections were, I found the companions to be the stronger hook. A lot is implied through their design and their little bits of dialogue. Sadly, you'll have to fill the rest in yourself as few of the characters or concepts get enough screen time to fully develop. The same could be said of this game's big combat innovation: formations. Combining three to five characters into a single, powerful unit feels like forging your own mini-boss and opening up a whole new world of possibilities. Or it would feel that way if The Waylander's combat was more suited to them. Everything speeds by a little too quickly and enemies move a little too freely about the battlefield to get much use out of a chokepoint-closing dome of shields or a stationary platform of archers. But much like the rest of the game's issues, there's nothing fundamental wrong with it. It just needs more fine tuning and further fleshing out. With the game's poor launch, it's unlikely to ever get the time or money it would need to see the attention it so deserves. For those of us who have found a way to enjoy the promise it represents despite its current state, it seems The Waylanders will remain a tale of what could have been.

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is just incredibly bad, I'm sorry to say.I don't really care that the dialogue is modern, although I think it's the wrong choice in a time-travelling story.  My complaint is that the characters sound like a bunch of adolescents who take nothing seriously and think their awkward cursing makes them sound cool. The voice talent is top-notch, but good delivery couldn't save the absolutely cringey script. There is some other wonky stuff about the game, but if the writing weren't so off-putting I could easily overlook the other issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. I really wanted to like this game. There are a few things that stood out to me. This is a fantasy world, with fantasy characters. I don't mind obscenity, and it can actually be pretty funny when well done, but the dialogue was just jam packed with modern phrasing and cuss words. I think if they made up a series of swears that fit in with with the game world (ALA Dragonage: Makers Balls! and Andraste's Tits) it wouldn't be so jarring. It's poor writing for dialogue. The characters seem pretty shallow like there should be more and there just isn't. I am FULLY AWARE this is early access, however there is a piece about 3 hours in that culminates in a very unfair fight that instantly destroys my party. The battle system is confusing and the tutorial isn't very helpful. The text is very small and the battle system icons seem cluttered. It is not intuitive. It also crashed about 4 times in my short playthrough.  I would be ok with companies not reinventing the wheel. Before anyone just rolls their eyes and says something like "get gud" I've been playing computer  RPG's since Bard's Tale and that was on a Tandy. As a wizened crone, I know what I like and this isn't it. Please don't toot the Bioware horn if you are not bringing the whole orchestra.

_childDocuments_.review: The Waylanders compares itself to Dragon Age: Origins (also, Neverwinter Nights and Baldur's Gate), so I'll go ahead and compare it with Dragon Age: Origins.Pros:- Oddball humor (You'll like this if you liked DA:O humor)- Feeds your nostalgia- Music is great (Inon Zur)- Narrated introductions to important areas- Armour design incorporates the different regions- Formations as your "special ability" is pretty unique- Respeccing your character's and companions' abilities is available and free!Cons:- BUGS*> No companion quest rewards?> Missing cinematics and cutscenes> FPS drops during some magic spells> Can't attack after certain cutscenes (WHY?)> Inaccessible areas or invisible walls when there should not be any> The map pointer stays north even if you turn (it's not like we have a compass on-screen)- Underdeveloped main characters (one-dimensional) and story.- You don't really recruit companions, they recruit you, you have no say. (But at least they're likable?)- Plot gets established too quickly, there's no build up. Just go and do that, ye? 20 min.- Dialogue does 180s frequently. The whiplash you'll get is insane. Camera and tonal shifts.- Seems unfinished, dead environments and NPCs interactions. (It's way way less interactive than DA:O.) There are little to no side quests! (Like one in each big area.)- There's also no depth in the companion quests, they take like 5 minutes to do and it's usually always a battle.- Looks (UI, HUD) and plays (certain mechanics like quest completion) like a mobile game*> When you defeat a boss, it teleports you back to your ship (your base). Give us a say first!(OR TELEPORT US OUT OF THE DUNGEON OR JUST GIVE US AN EXIT DUNGEON DOOR???)THIS IS AWFUL. Usually the boss is connected to a main quest, and there will be at least one side quest to do in the area where the boss is found in. When you defeat the boss, the main quest is completed and you get the rewards on the ship. But the side quests will not be completed, you have to travel to whatever area it is found in and TURN THE QUEST IN. Sometimes the side quest is connected to the main quest. And since the main quest will be completed when you defeat the boss, the side quest MIGHT DISAPPEAR. You can still turn it in if you find the NPC that gave it to you, but this could be a LITTLE EASIER IF YOU WEREN'T JUST TELEPORTED OUT OF THE AREA AND ONTO YOUR SHIP!- Companions aren't there with you during non-combat!!! If you like how companions banter and react to each other and the environment in other games, The Waylanders DOES NOT HAVE THIS!!! Except for a small part at the beginning, which was...kinda terrible. Dialogue just kept happening and it felt dry and had no flow to it. The rare moments when your Waylander companions are with you in a non-combat situation, they won't even follow you, they'll just teleport to you when you reach the NPC you need to speak to. (They'll probably say something funny though.)Pet Peeves:- No campfire?- Biased animations*(Some characters are more expressive than others, the others are actual robots.)- Character customization sucks!!!- 30 fps-locked cut scenes in 2022 ? ? ?- Text is too small and the side hud is nearly invisible- Fast traveling could be quicker (why do I have to hover over the place then click on it twice?)- The mumbling of non-human (Mourian) characters is quite frightening. Like, I know y'all speak English. There's no need to fake a fake language if there's not gonna be any lore on it.- Companions don't talk to you on the ship base unless they have a quest for you. You can't ask them, "hey you like the ship?" or something like that. I don't know, add something here.If you're looking for a game that's EXACTLY like DA:O to sate your nostalgia, this is about as good as it gets. It's mildly fun, aside from the possibly game-breaking bugs and the boring loot* variations. Also, the codex is nowhere near as descriptive. It does have potential though. Something that might need two or three years to reach...I could see modding and DLCs in its future. But right now it's one of the emptiest RPGs I've ever played in my life.If you're okay with another combat system, there are way better modern RPG games to play. I can recommend several new ones with all the stuff you want, companions, party banter and romance:Divinity: Original Sin II (2017)Pillars of Eternity II: Deadfire (2018)Greedfall (2019)Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous (2021)Baldur's Gate 3 has more content than this game and it's not even out yet. Honestly, I think that game is much closer to DA:O, if you're looking for that kind of nostalgia. It's got campfires, lovable dogs, romance, and funny dialogue options you can choose. Your character in The Waylanders isn't much of a comedian but all your companions are, apparently.uh, 5/10. Preys on your nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game through Kickstarter. And because of that, I don't have a high hope to begin with.The game looks nice, but it is very very unpolished with a lot of game breaking bugs need to be fixed.Some observation:- Character customisation are lacking and buggy. Some hair is not selectable. There are no options to customise your body shape without changing class. There are no way to customise underlying facial structure.- Inventory system is a mess and buying/selling things is a nightmare.- Party inventory limit to 50 items sucks- Exact same item would sometimes not want to stack together... further wasting the 50 inventory space- Some weapons/armors are not animated fully. e.g. Crooked Rod has these dangly bits that is supposed to drop with gravity, but in reality it is very stiff and doesn't move at all... it looks weird!- Comparing weapons and items are hard. They only show the changes in the value... I would rather be given the full numbers as well- Incomplete items and skills that displays <Missing string value>- There are no easy way to "show helmet", there is a toggle in the options, but this affects the whole party. It should be an individual toggle in their respective character sheet- The story is intriguing, but needs more depth, and the characters was not explored deeply enough... They seem rushed.- Romance system is very lacklustre and seems to be put in there as an afterthought.- Some subtitles doesn't advance properly, or different from the spoken/voiced dialogue.- Some dialogue has no mouth animation in one line, then animated the next. Some NPC such as the trainer Nitya does not have mouth animation.- The voice acting is acceptable, but not the best... There seems to be a confusion/disconnect between the voice actors on how to pronounce some words, especially Irish words and names... You would have two characters in the conversation saying the same words two different ways... Irish names such as Ciara was pronounced as Kee-ya-ra instead of the correct Kee-ra, Taliesin was incorrectly pronounced Ta-lee-seen instead of Ta-lee-eh-sn- Every single non essential NPCs has dialogue if you click them, which is excessive and doesn't add much to the story. I would rather if there are less of them and they automatically trigger when you walk by them- Skipping dialogue is hard to do (you have to click multiple times before it registers).- Quick saving does not make a quicksave file, but creates a regular save forever (it keeps making a new one so you have to periodically delete your saves otherwise you end up with hundreds of save files). - Saving and loading needs you to hold to confirm... really??- Quest bug such as the invisible wall in Cave of Eternity- Quest generally ends abruptly after you kill the final boss, and immediately transports you back to your ship... So if yous till want to explore parts of the map, well tough luck!- There are no separation of the main and side quests, making it hard to see in journals- Quest is tracked, but there is no clear way to make the quest tracked (you have to sort of just double click in journal). Tracked quest barely has any quest pointers. No option to hide completed quests in journal- The Blacksmith fetch quest did not give you any indication where the item is beyond the initial dialogue. So if you missed the dialogue or forget where the NPC who has these items are, you will have to just visit every place and hope for the best. The quest journal only says the NPC name and not the place. There are also no quest marker for side quests so...- There are no options to highlight interactable object, so chests with tiny sparkles are hard to find- Formations are not very intuitive to do, you have to select party members first which are fiddly- There are no keyboard shortcuts to select party members 1-5- Great music made by Inon Zur of Dragon Age, but it gets repetitive really quick because it is short and looping all the time. Transition from place that has same music (such as in Brigantia and surrounds) makes the music repeats from beginning  - Environment and character models are nice though!- I'm sure there are many more observations I will make while playing itAnyway tl;dr... this would have been a good game if they polish. It is playable, but you just need to temper your expectations. I can't recommend it at the current state, but willing to change my review if it is improved

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game with high (ish) hopes but so far I am really struggling. I love the RPG fantasy genre but never before in over thirty years of playing have I been reduced to playing in short 10 to 15 minute bursts because the game just bores me so much. I accept that this is not a finished product and I really do hope it improves dramatically by February but in my eyes I am afraid this practically amounts to a complete rewrite. I am aware that this game has garnered quite a lot of praise from different players/reviewers but I honestly cannot see what the fuss is about. I will not abandon the game entirely and intend to check out the finished product next year which I think is only fair but I am afraid this experience has put me off pre full release products for life!

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting and unique CRPG that doesn’t have a lot in it currently. The story is the game’s best feature and uses Celtic legends as the races and creatures’ basis and focuses on the struggle between mortals and their spiritual or immortal counterparts.   This game does not currently have a lot of content in it. What is in the game is enjoyable and unique which is why I narrowly recommend it, but if it is a long RPG you want right away, then I advise you to wait a bit longer. Please only purchase if you want to support the developers and believe that the game will turn into something that you will enjoy.The world is divided into a multitude of hubs with smaller key locations that are easy to access offshoots. It was nice that there isn’t a lot of walking to get to each destination and the loading screens didn’t take very long. As for battle sections, these are long and seamless so they don’t interrupt the action. There are small side areas that often contain more loot, but they aren’t necessary to complete any objectives.Character Creation has quite a few unique races which are quite interesting which makes it difficult to pick between them. There are the typical humans, but there are also lycanthropes which don’t turn into werewolves but are instead found in forms in between full wolf and a typical human with some extra hair. The third option is a combination of a dwarven and elven society. They live in an otherworld where they specialize in crafting that they have built with their large magical powers that are only compounded with their extreme amounts of knowledge gained during their immortality. Another immortal race are the tall, lanky, and exiled giants who have since begun breeding with humans to create the largest race in the world who still keep the giant’s ferocious strength. A feature I found interesting was that the player’s character has a body type determined by their class and background. A human fighter will be quite muscular and a little taller than his mage peer. This may disappoint some players who like to customize every inch of a character, but I found it to be more immersive.There are six main stats, with each class relying on two particular ones the most. Strength and Constitution focus on physical damage and extra character health respectively. Strength is the main stat of the fighter class which relies strength to do lots of damage. Guardians focus a lot on constitution to be a tank. Rogues are quick damage dealers with great dodging skills and rangers are their ranged counterparts who use agility, for dodge and dexterity, and perception, for crit chance. Mages like intelligence due to increasing damage of spells and willpower is used by healers due to its cooldown reduction properties. These stats can be mixed and matched so min/maxing is not a necessity. Some story characters also have their own unique classes such as a Formorian, the giant equivalent of this world, who has a class based upon leaching life and being extremely tanky.The unique ability set for this game is the formation system. The three stat archetypes each have two formations that they have access to. These are battle changing abilities that are required to be used to defeat bosses and large groups of enemies. How they work is that the player selects the heroes that they want to be a part of the formation and then they activate it. Not every hero has to be a part of a formation and if a tanky formation is made, the team’s main dps can be left outside of it so that they can continue to deal damage. The first major boon for formations is that they have a separate health pool. This allows for tanking and allows low health units to be in the fight in a certain capacity. Be careful, because if a formation breaks because it has lost all of its health then it will stun every hero in the formation. The second positive point is that formations have unique abilities that deal quite a bit of damage if they contain a lot of heroes. Special story heroes can’t be put in a formation though, so while they are powerful, they don’t contribute to any formations.The equipment is the typical RPG fare. Stats are raised by equipment and each different equipment type provides a different stat boost. Later areas will have stronger loot which can either be bought or gained from a dead enemy.Combat is similar to other CRPGs besides the aforementioned formations system. The game is real-time with pause and abilities can be set to cast during the middle of the pause. Enemies can be a real challenge without proper ability use as the stronger ones can do quite a bit of damage. This means that characters can die, but they will simply stand up after combat has ended.The story and world building are so unique. The game’s story and world are built upon Celtic legends which have not been utilized very much. There are multiple races that all have unique cultures and are forced to intermingle thanks to the magical powers that they all wield. The antagonists are also quite unique and I can’t wait to see where the rest of the story goes.The voice acting is decent and go for a larger than life feeling because the characters are powerful heroes. The music is orchestral and pleasant to listen to and I liked the inclusion of bagpipes for the authentic music from the culture the game is based on.The graphics for The Waylanders uses three-dimensional art that has a cartoonish style. The graphics are a complex and odd mixture for this type of game, a CRPG. Usually they go for a more realistic styling, and this game’s graphics certainly looks that way, except for the exaggerated features and bright color pallete. I think that this is a good thing though as it gives the game a feeling that it is a legend being retold at a much later date. The different cultures also all have distinct looks, buildings, and clothing. It helps to create a world that is full of life and helps to flesh out the origins of these civilizations and how they have risen. : Since this is an early access game, it doesn’t run very well. I didn’t have too many problems with my specs as it seems to be mainly GPU reliant. It doesn’t work well currently on lower end GPUs, so be careful. 👍  👍Amazing world buildingUnique formation mechanic👎  👎Not a ton of content yetPoor performance

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Certainly not today. Today it is a very ambitious project in Early Access that might one day become a fantasy RPG classic alongside Neverwinter Nights and Dragon Age, which the devs name as their inspiration. The Spanish devs clearly aim for something big with this game. The story is written by professional writers and takes place in two time areas, Celtic Mythology and Medieval Spain, where your actions in one time might have consequences in the other area. Build your character from five playable mythical Celtic races, six basic (warrior, healer, sorcerer, ranger, rogue, guardian) and 30 advanced classes, and meet nine interesting companions with extensive backstories that can join your party. The game has large maps to explore with a multitude of quests and contains many conversations in multiple-choice. Your characters have six main attributes (strength, constitution, agility,...) that can be leveled up, each character has his own set of abilities that can be unlocked in a skill tree, the shared inventory is large. Each character has five slots to equip items. The game draws an automap, writes down your mission progress in a journal and fills a codex with all the information you obtain during your adventures. Quite a lot to read. Combat is in real-time but pausable, your party members attack foes when they see them as long as you do not give them different orders. With experience you learn tactical formations to use during combat. The game starts a bit unexpected. You join your king on a diplomatic mission to meet your gods, sail to the homelands of the gods... and suddenly your king is seriously wounded and you fight against agressive brutes for your survival. While everyone must know at least a part of what has happened, the player does not get any information about it. It is just your first mission to protect the king and bring him back on board of his royal ship. Returning home, your homeland is in chaos and a state of civil war, and you have to choose your side. And so your story begins.Currently the game is in Early Access and not very polished. I encountered various bugs, and while there is already a lot of content implemented, it is not polished at all. The game can become a masterpiece, but it needs some serious fixing first. That said, I enjoyed what I saw.Addition after the "full" release: It has not become a masterpiece and is actually... quite buggy, and with a lot of questionable design decisions. The devs obviously overestimated their ability to produce a RPG epic.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to get disappointed when you wasn't expecting much to begin with. To be precise, when you didn't expect anything at all. I got this game as a gift and patiently waited for it's full release. Which will never happen, I'm afraid, even if the tag says so.You see, this game is not just broken, it's broken beyond repair because one can't fix something that was never solid and whole. I can't even call it a game, as it's just some random pieces of code, clumsily put together, it's a mess of great ideas, sometimes beautiful visuals, random very modern jokes that feel out of place most of the time, absolutely unsatisfying if not outright terrible combat system and endless gamebreaking bugs. The second half of the game is riddled with them, everything seems to be broken, literally everything - every step, every dialogue, every quest and cutscene, every piece of music. It's broken to the point of being unplayable.There is obviously effort in this project, love even, but technical, programming and writing skills of it's creators leave a lot to be desired. Sadly, this precious and sincere effort doesn't worth a dime if the result is that poor. Sad, indeed.

_childDocuments_.review: Right now, given the state of the game, I cannot recommend this one.  The biggest issue, for me, is how disjointed the game feels.  Being an RPG most people will come to this game for the story, the narrative, and because of the strange way the game has been developed / put together, the story as it stands, even the bit in game, makes little sense.  Cutscenes are missing (including a major one within the first 20 minutes), fights are missing, some dialog is voiced and others are not within the same scenes, dialog spoken doesnt match the subtitles at times, animations during cutscenes will sometimes just cease or not be there when there was animation prior to that moment in the same scene, ect.Its like everything has been put together at random, strung together as the devs randomly decide what to build next.  Hell, as I write this, the last update....was a combat arena zone.  Why was that needed? You can check my video review here for more thoughts, and an example of the disjointed dialog / narrative

_childDocuments_.review: Supported this game in early access, been here from day one. The story felt compelling, something fresh and different which is why I originally supported it. I really wanted to love this game, I had high hopes for it to be at least similar to previous big name RPGS I've played (DA, Mass Effect, Divinity etc.). However The Waylanders missed the ball big time, like most reviews have said the writing is absolutely terrible, boarder line cringe at times. The characters felt dull and lifeless with only small glimpses of what they potentially could have been if they had better writing, this lack of consistency really killed it for me. I might have been able to make it further if the dialogue wasn't so terrible. This along with a number of glitches, black screens, etc. have made the game unplayable. Now to top it off, the game appears abandoned despite Gato releasing a "roadmap" back in Feb with plans to fix the game. Because I am past the 2 hr game play time, I can't even get a refund for a game that I absolutely hate and will never be fixed. For anyone who is heavy into dialogue, well written characters and heavily story driven, STEER CLEAR OF THIS GAME!! YOU WILL BE DISAPPOINTED.

_childDocuments_.review: The bad things first: The game is a little buggy, some cutscenes lack animations, and there are some gaps in the story. I miss more combat levels, too.Despite this issues, Waylanders shows that it's going to be a great game when it's finished. The parts that are finished look really great, the writing the artstyle is amazing (specially the landscapes) and the music is beautiful. Characters are interesting, the lore is original and gameplay is fun.Developers still have a lot of work ahead, but this game will be a must. I'm sure about it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time Bioware fan, a lover of ancient Celtic history (seriously, Amergin being in the game sold it for me, literally), and someone who has been severely disappointed by the most recent rpg offerings, I am very excited to be a part of early access and look forward to the game's development.What I love So Far:-Camera options. I don't do first person (motion sickness), and I love being able to close in for a more over the shoulder look while exploring.-Dialogue between characters. I was hoping for a more traditional/historical flow, but the vivid personalities of the characters are already evident and leave me wanting more.-Captions on being default, and automatically scripted side conversations--I have to play with captions on in order to understand what is being said. Otherwise I have to crank my volume (auditory processing challenges). Pace of dialogue was nice, so that in the spots where captions aren't finished yet, I could make out most of it still.-The story is original. Again, I'm a bit of a traditionalist when it comes to referencing history, but I can see the passion and appreciate the storytelling that has gone into the game and feel that it is respectful of the source material.-Detailed origins, classes, and races. Available origins change based on race and class selected. I really missed this in later Dragon Age games.-Origin, race, and class change the appearance of the character-My game did crash at one point. The autosaving or lack thereof brought back memories of an unexpected dragon fight in DAO that ended in erasing about an hour of gameplay :D. This was more nostalgic to me than frustrating. Save often.-Skill tree is interesting without being overwhelming-Ability to determine companion's class when they join the party-I usually prefer rts with a pause function, but the gameplay was intuitive enough that by the second set of battles it was becoming a lot more fluid (and fun) for me-Companions showing up early in-game. Not having to slog through hours of gameplay to get to the companion you were excited for.Where I could see improvement:-Some ability to edit facial appearance and body shape-I have a tendency to get lost in open world exploration and prefer a strong, detailed, clearly defined story vs vast expanses to traverse (ie DA2). The story is evident in Waylanders...I just need the quest markers and trackers to stay in the final version ;)-Hide helmet function in-gameI can't wait to be able to leave the Vengeance! Thank you so much for this game. Seriously, I have trouble finding books these days with this level of storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: I've never known an RPG with such bad writing. It's like you forgot it was a game, which really hurts the great voice acting. It's even laughably bad, where it's so bad you wonder how it even made it to the final version. A scene that's supposed to be somber "tell your mother I love her" will make you cringe because of how embarrassing it is. Whoever wrote this needs some more practice. Someone giving exposition is not the same as a well-told story.This would be ignorable if not for the controls. I feel like this was designed for a controller and then it was ported to PC even though it wasn't. It does not work well with mice and I wonder if the person who designed the controls ever played a keyboard and mouse game. It's like someone took Dragon Age: Origins and decided not to make it PC-friendly.There are so many things in this game that make you think "Who thought this was good?" It makes me think that no one outside of the development team tested this game because so much could have been caught and corrected.Do not buy this. It's a $14.99 bargain bin game and should be played with very, very low standards. Not even Indie quality. Do yourself a favor and let this one go.

_childDocuments_.review: is a party-based RPG with Real-Time-with-Pause combat system and class-based character development system. The avatar is customizable and silent, there are several classes, races, and backgrounds to choose from and the body type depends on the class chosen.The game runs stably and there is only one place (a companion quest) where the game crashes (). There are several other quests that are impossible to complete because of bugs.  Many character abilities and equipment pieces miss descriptions. There are very few meaningful story-related choices outside of dialogues with companions, who join automatically without any input from the player, except for the one who is bugged. The presentation of the story is uneven and it is hard to follow for the first part of the game. There are some plot holes, related to time-travelling. The game presents a unique formation system which allows several character to act as one and provides unique abilities. The controls are comfortable and rebindable and 5-button mice are supported. The writing is heavily stylised and leans towards modern language. The graphics are cartoon-like, but reasonably detailed and expressive. But in many cases there are no facial animations and the camera points at an empty space during dialogues. I completed the game in 22 hours. Recommended on sale, at 60%+ discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Seems like a good game. It has charme and seems quite unique. All the swearing seems a bit odd, but I'm the last to complain about bad language, heh. It's refreshing, to be honest.  There are some issues however that lead me to refund it;- The graphics are blurry. I tried everything to my knowledge, but it didn't help. It's very heavy on the eyes. Maybe blurry isn't 100% the right word, washed might fit too. I think a sharpening setting might help to recognize forms, terrain and outlines a bit better.- Despite scaling settings, the text is just too small and hard to read. This might be because I (have to) play on a TV. - Subtitles are often not in line with what is spoken. Not in a major fashion, but still.- There are things like missing strings in Item Descriptions and stuff. Pretty sure this will get fixed anyway. Can't imagine the devs not being aware of this.- The small dots marking interactive objects are hard to see. Something with more contrast would be favourable. All in all, it's the display issues that lead me to put it away but I do hope that this will get better upon release. Until then, I'll wait. It's hard to not recommend it, we're direly missing a neutral setting there, so despite the issues and due to the devs being pretty responsive, I'll still recommend and wish the devs best of luck.I will give this another shot when it's released and if I still have those issues, I'll be more in touch with the devs to find a solution. And if not, I'll still find a way to play it.Edit June 2022; Changed to negative due to the lack of communication and therefore seemingly inactive development. Changing it when it comes apparent that it's being worked on.

_childDocuments_.review: The Waylanders has very reminiscent systems and gameplay that anyone who’s played Dragon Age will find themselves familiar with. However, the game has proven itself to be original with its engaging story, intriguing characters and unique lore.  Of course, the game is in its early access alpha stages, and there are plenty of bugs and things that need further improvement. But I can see the heart and passion that has gone behind this game, and that’s what I’ve grown to like about it.I’d say to anyone who’s a huge fan of Dragon Age: Origins, why not go and give The Waylanders a shot. Support this game as it grows throughout development, and releases as an epic Dragon Age successor.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this game when I backed it on Kickstater, but it has been iout of Early Access for over a year now and it still feels like its in beta with many bugs that make the game unplayable sometimes and many more that are just annoying most of the time. _childDocuments_.review: For a game with such an interesting premise and a wonderful idea for a story, well. It falls flat. A lot of it falls flat.One bug is quite frequent. Merchants will sell me things the first time I arrive in town, but if I approach them again, or I leave the area and then come back, they aren't selling anything.The voice acting started off passable enough, but then you get beyond the prologue. Where emotions  matter, since things are so emotional and all, and these characters seem to lack a full set.The combat is alright, if a bit repetitive... set most characters to have an aggressive attitude, so they'll use their abilities, then on your character of choice, press buttons 1 through 6 until the fight is over, maybe use a formation, but unlikely, then spend like five minutes using your healer to bring everyone up to full health, and repeat.I haven't gotten very far into the story yet tbh, but so far I have not been impressed, either. Tiana, whose father is a xenophobic and murderous usurper that tried to kill me and mine, gives me an order to find her missing men, and then sends along her (friend? bodyguard? general?) to do it, and there seems to be no complaint. Mr Prince on the other hand has gone through a complete personality change - or maybe not - sitting in a dark cave looking all edgy, saying he'll be king now, and I'm supposed to believe he's a suitable candidate?The graphics are nice, the scenery is well-made. But nice graphics and impressive backgrounds don't make up for the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: Some good ideas but it is very buggy and many elements need to be improved a ton. Animations are terrible, the writing is very bland, the tone is all over the place, tons of bugs and the game handles very clunky and unresponsive. Hope they do well in the future, I have played many early access rpg games and nearly everyone was in better shape than this game. It could turn it around, but it needs ALOT of work. Hope things improve but so far its not looking good if you wanted a Dragon Age Origins type game, this is not it. I have loved MANY games that where in Alpha state and early on, I can forgive tons of things, but I have had zero fun playing this game for the hour I did and had tons of issues.It tries to be Kingdoms of Amalur and DAO together (Two games I enjoyed alot) and so far it doesn't go together very well. I hope the devs keep improving things, but unlike many other great EA rpgs (Divinity OS 1/2, Pillars 1/2, Wasteland 2,etc..) this one just doesn't have the basics down early on. Check out the game later to see how things have improved, for now stay away. The combat has some potential but mostly everything else is not in great shape.If it was just clunkyness or stuff not finished yet I wouldn't mind but the base of most elements in this game just don't work well and most importantly the game is not fun in anyway, especially compared to the games it is trying to be like. Hell, I play the Gothic and Risen games religiously, I don't mind clunky games or games with bad animations if the other stuff is well done :)

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly this is a game I REALLY REALLY wanted to like.-So I bought this game as soon as it was in early access (Dragon age origins is my favourite game, so this sounded right up my street!) Though it was so broken I couldn't even manage the first few minutes of game play. A fault I put down to bad release choices and not a reflection of it's potential. - I didn't then and still refuse to get a refund as despite my opinions on the game, I genuinely feel bad at how bad this game has turned out, because you can tell a lot of love and hard work has gone into it. However, I can't justify the price being asked for this game. Going back, even asking £20 would be a bit much.- After waiting for the full release and ignoring previous negative reviews I finally played through the first part of the game, really hoping for even semi-enjoyment. I didn't have large expectations, but I still feel let down.- Bad voice acting: Sometimes I blame it on the writing, but I honestly think it's more down to certain characters voice acting (I don't want to name them as I think it would be harsh :( ) but a certain character has such a bad voice actor behind it all the things they say are either inconsistent, hard to understand or just plain cringe. - Glitches: Characters got stuck in rocks or froze mid battle, unable to fight.- Story comprehension: (SPOILER) There was a scene that switched so dramatically with barley any context and it felt like I accidentally skipped a scene. I went back and nope, it was a writing decision.Overall, I will attempt to play some more at some point. I REALLY wanted a be a positive review in the wave of negative reviews they have been getting. The only issue is I feel there WAS so much potential, but a lot of bad decisions around the game have made it hard to fix for the future. I didn't enjoy what I had played of it, felt like a lot of effort, but I am so desperate to like it because of the potential I know so many can see. This is just one of those games that has sadly flopped for a collective of reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: 21June2020: This is one of the most broken, unfinished games I've ever played. Its got missing assets, missing VO, missing animations, missing weapons/armor, missing effects, missing characters.. it's so ridiculously broken that I honestly can't recommend that you spend $30+ on this game right now, and the second big problem is that this game will require at least 2-4years+ of development before it's even remotely acceptable as a game. I'll keep my eye on this game and check back in on it in a year, and if it has dramatically improved then I'll re-review the game and update my review. There's a clear difference between 'early access' and 'proof of concept', and this game is clearly in the 'proof of concept' stage of development, not in the 'early access' stage... they just released it way way too early and it'll probably hurt them in the long run since many of the negative review and articles about the game now will never be revised.Below is my video review:23June2020 EDIT: I'd just like to point out that I've been receiving comments on my channel from what seems to be a disgruntled employee from this game studio. This person called me a liar and said that I should keep my mouth shut, all the while defending the game and the studio like a zealot... All I can say is: You were stupid enough to comment with your real name on your personal youtube account buddy. Learn to take criticism, or you'll end up without a job in no time.6Feb2022: EDIT 2: The game is still trash... the voice acting is still bad, animations are dog water, I've encountered 4bugs the first 60minutes, and they've cut entire swathes of story from the game so now nothing makes sense. You can't set priorities for your party (ie. focus on healing, focus on ranged, etc.). Your objectives aren't displayed on your map, or minimap. The balancing of the game is dog water... I'm playing on normal, and I can't get past one of the fights... There's massive amounts of lag when certain spells are cast... The queue system doesn't work, you issue orders to party members and they simply don't follow them... Health doesn't regenerate after combat AND mana doesn't regenerate during combat which means classes that use mana are MASSIVELY disadvantaged when compared to melee classes... everything is just terrible. They really released this game out of early access way too soon and it could have still used another 2years of development. Still, not recommended. _childDocuments_.review: to put it shortly the game is an awkward shallow mess that feels like the most amateur imitation of the great game it was inspired by.the longer version: I got this game when it first went into early access because I stupidly bought into the omg its like a new dragon age origins hype which is a comparison we can't forget for a second because the devs themselves never stopped bringing it up. I didn't play much in early access because it was an unfun buggy disaster but I figured I'd wait until release and give the finished product a proper try. fast forward to now and sure it's not as buggy but it still feels like things are missing and don't work. the words awkward and amateur I used earlier are really the perfect descriptors for this game because every single aspect of the game feels so rough. the ai in combat is infuriating with how often they immediately forget what you just ordered them to do with things like a warrior ordered to attack the enemy standing next to him immediately running across the field to target someone else. the ui feels so clunky with clicks not registering properly and the general way you're constantly left and right clicking all over the screen to arrange anything. the classes are very shallow only having 6 skills each with another I assume 6 coming from the advanced class you pick later. In terms of visuals and story away from gameplay the voice acting ranges from fine to absolutely horrible, animations are generally crap but facial animations especially are horrible to look at. The story is messy as can be and from what I've heard only makes less sense the further you go. The dialogue is painfully bad a lot of the time and most characters are trying so hard to be quirky or funny so you'll like them they all end up annoying. I really can't stress how bad the writing feels it's just embarrassing. Unless the cartoony artsyle really does it for you there is just nothing here to actually like only things you'll at best feel neutral towards. It's just not good and no amount of hotfixes and patches the devs are talking about will fix it.

_childDocuments_.review: I supported this game on kickstarter because I'd heard that someone working on the original Dragon Age was in the team and tbh I was quite stoked to see where this was going. Unfortunately though, I can't recommend the game at this point. It feels not finished, not polished. The moving around feels stiff, the character models square, the characters themselves more like pawns than actual people.I see the similarity to Dragon Age but Waylanders is missing so much heart, story, and depth. I appreciate all the work they put into the menues, the lore, the "codex" and quest log - but they should've put more work into the character designs, story, flexibility in character customization and in-game visuals (especially lighting), if you ask me.I really hope they'll keep patching, updating and improving the game because there's so much great work already done and so much more potential.At this point, I'm getting a refund but I'm gonna keep having an eye on this game and hope that they don't give up on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Never have I been so excited by a description on steam so quickly, only to have some sort of VeggieTales esque tripe of a game be spewed onto my monitor. Running a decent system (RTX 2070S, i7-9900k) there were few moments through my short run that did not have stutter, this would not be an issue for an early access title with claims to being from "the top-talents who brought well-known titles within the genre like the Dragon Age, Mass Effect or Pillars of Eternity sagas" if it were not for the insufferably bad dialogue between characters. _childDocuments_.review: Playing this game at the moment feels like I'm playing the rough draft version of the game for sure. This game EASILY has the potential to be an outstanding RPG among the likes of Dragon Age/Mass Effect. However there are a few things that didn't feel great for me playing the game:1. Movement/Camera Angles - I felt like it was a lot of work just to angle the camera in a good spot while running from place to place. Also adjusting the sensitivity even to the max setting wasn't very helpful.2. Combat - I enjoyed the tactical feature being able to plan out my characters abilities, but I had to control every single character in order to get them to do more than just auto attack. It would be awesome to have a setting where I can control when my characters use certain abilities, ESPECIALLY healing abilities/items. I had to take a break because constantly pausing to issue each of my characters next moves got tedious and frustrating. I appreciate the challenge, but that type of gameplay isn't for me. 3. Cutscenes - These were jumping from place to place and skipping parts of the dialogue. I understood the premise of what was happening, and I enjoy the story, but there were jump cuts which made it confusing. 4. Environment - I feel like there just isn't enough STUFF in the game to interact with. Sure it's pretty but it isn't very immersive. For example in the first city we see, I could only interact with about two characters and the shop. Getting to know the city by exploring/doing mini quests could be exciting and really make us feel immersed in the world that we're playing in. ALL of that being said, the game IS enjoyable and it is a good time. I plan on putting more hours into this game and trying to work through the kinks until it is fully released. Again, this could truly be a phenomenal new RPG and can't wait to see the final product.

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: Game's incomplete and seems to be abandoned, unfortunately.My review used to be positive back when game was in EA, now that it's been months since release and after reaching the ending I'm forced to change it. _childDocuments_.review: I've been following Waylanders since its first steps because I'm really interested in the setting and the world it is attempting to portrait. Now that it is entering early access I see I am not going to be disappointed. There are not a lot of games out there which explore celtic settings, and that's a shame, because it is such a rich and powerful mythology. The graphics are *lovely*. I'm definitely biased here, because I am a graphic designer — but hey, the eyes need candy too!I'm definitely enjoying the way they have revisited some traditional galician myths like the lobishomes (lycans) or the «mouros» (the moure, in game speak). These, particularly, I think are quite cleverly portrated. I've seen them described as a mixture of dwarves and elves from other mythologies, and that's quite accurate. The idea of «Mouros», in galician folklore, arose when people would find dirt-covered ruins of ancient celtic villages («castros»), and sometimes buried artifacts or treasure. That mixed with the pre-celtic megalithic graves, which often did contain treasure, and with traditional legends of spirits protecting rivers and fountains. How they «stole» the name given to the muslim kingdoms to the south, I have no idea — possibly because for most galician folk, those kingdoms were distant and misterious... At any rate, this is a digression, but perhaps it can serve you to see there's a lot of background to inspire the Waylanders' world.Gameplay wise, I'm really interested in the formation system, and I really hope they iron out the bugs and develop it further. I've played many party-based RPGs where the characters act more or less as independent units — yes, often they'll support each other, as in healers and tanks and DPS, but... that's not how real combat works, you know? Real combat involving groups of people means the smart use of formations, to varying degrees. This allows weak and strong people to join in their efforts, effectively supporting and supplementing each other, and allowing *the group* to achieve things the individual could not. I'm really, really glad Waylanders is exploring that concept, and that they have made it into a necessary part of gameplay, more than just an optional throw-in.There's still a long way to go before this game is finished, and they have a lot of kinks to iron out, but I really have my hopes up and want to see where the dev team can get. This really has the chance to become an awesome experience!P.S.: And if any dev reads this, I'm really looking forwards to that promised linux port. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: In short, if you love lore, watching scenes and listening/reading more than actual battle, then this game is good for that. At least that's my takeaway after 12 hours in the game. Maybe that changes further in.I can't disagree with alot of the gripes so far, but it's still alpha so I don't get hung up on some things still missing, getting stuck and having to restart, etc. Sure, some dialog seems a bit forced and the cussing maybe unnecessary, and maybe for a game that is heavy on story that's a big deal. My main interest is gaming mechanics and strategy, which I'm not sure I like so far. It almost feels like it's either too easy where you basically let your party do whatever it wants, even just lie dead on the ground while they fight everything off, or it's so difficult you're spending a majority of the time paused clicking on each and every thing to queue your next moves. Or maybe it's just me and I'm playing all wrong, but then I might argue the game isn't the most intuitive.However, the ability to customize the makeup of your team is nice and opens up a variety of ways to play the game. I'm not sure if you can re-run instances without starting a whole new character, but that might be interesting.Completion of some quest lines seems to end abruptly and hopefully that changes. For something so story heavy, for it to all just end once a boss is defeated seems jarring and anticlimactic.From the little I've played with the weapon system, one thing I like is the ability to swap gems around. They're not consumed on equip like most other games.

_childDocuments_.review: BACK TO THE GAME!I've put the Waylanders on the shelf for a couple months, and can now say that the game has become much more lpayable and enjoyable.1) There's a coherent plot now - cutscenes, voices and quest lines are mostly where they should be.2) Graphics has become better too.3) Some nice quests have made the progress more alive.4) GOBLINS! Goblins are adorable.5) The party members now have more distinctive character traits and interesting quests.Now I can say that i'm really looking forward to seeing the final product.________Earlier impressions here.UPD: The developers really respond to feedback and do it quickly. F5 key is with us again! UPD2: After the update, all old saves have been deleted. OK, I'm kinda getting used to it. But there are more important questions.1) Does the choice of a race even effect anything? I'm playing a mourian character, but nobody seems to be aware of it, even his own kin. Moreover, if mourians are immortal, how does all this plot twist with "You've been technically dead" make even the slightest sense?..2) Isn't the idea of the protagonist who resurrects and becomes fateless a little... umh... borrowed from the Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning?3) WHY ON EARTH isnt's the main quest mentioned in the log and/or map?4) How is it possible to keep up with the story, while video, sound and subtitles of the cutscenes don't correspond?5) Is there a safe way of quitting the game without crashing now?**The earlier part of the review.Ok, let's say that I was really excited when I knew about the upcoming game. Today I've purchased it - aaaand... It's a big "AND".Firstly, the game is still hugely unstable. You haven't saved? - oops, have yourself a pretty little fatal lag. You've tried to save the game via f5 (AS USUAL)? - have yourself a crash report and start the game again. Frankly speaking, I haven't found any normal way of saving the game except for the saving via the main menu, which is a long and inconvenient way. I miss the f5 key.Secondly, the graphics leaves much to be desired, and it would have probably left much to be desired even in the early 2k10s. It's not good and simplistic enough to count as "old but good", it's just not good enough.Though the voice acting so far is really great and some initial jokes were also good, the game has failed to provide any real plot and challenge in these first 70 minutes (mostly due to the crashes and the necessity to start again).But there's still something that makes me want to play more, something that tells that it's not THAT bad, I probably just need some time to adjust to all the settings of the game. In this case The Waylanders really is like all those old but good games, that captivate you even though they're not perfect.And I would be really happy if I could take most of my words back.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: Revising my review.  Game has officially launched and so have the multitude of bugs.  I was really looking forward to this game, I've been following it for years, but the final product has left much to be desired.Cut scenes are missing and I'm not talking about minor ones that don't mean anything.  I'm talking about right out of the gate before you even get into your first fight.When it comes to side quests, there are problems here.  I did a quest to the Cave of eternity.  and there are two things to do.  Find stones for an altar and slay a dragon.  I killed the dragon and then boom, i'm right back on the boat.  I was not able to complete both because after killing the boss the quest was over i guess.  I still have it in my journey as a quest that needs to be done (the stones for the altar that is) but I can no longer go that that map location...A lot of reviews focus on the dialog and for good reason...it's kind of dopey, but I get that they were trying to keep it more modern but it is just out of place. However, I was called mortal and treated like a human (seemingly?).2.) _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, it had all the components of what I would typically like in a game: a companion driven real-time-with-pause fantasy RPG with a romance element. Some of the creative talent are names I recognize and admire, and the game really does have fantastic dialog and top-notch voice acting to bring it to life, the fun characters made me want to devour this story and this game.The problem is the actual gameplay: the combat is a grindy, tedious, unbalanced mess, and it is probably one of the worst examples of RtwP I have encountered. Rather than give you a sense of fighting your way out of  a desperate situation in the prologue and first act, the combat is uninteresting grind against trash mobs, in which your spellcasters will quickly burn through their fixed pool of mana reserves and be left pea-shooting against boilerplate badguys, with mana not regenerating until the end of combat. I attempted to overcome this obstacle by changing the game to "Cinematic" (Story) mode, only to find the combat became even _more_ grindy, with the mobs not reducing in difficulty, my mana/health pools not regenerating, the only difference is that the last character standing in a combat will now just "not die" and will continue to grind away for as long as it takes until the mob is now defeated--the opposite of "cinematic" I'm afraid. That, combined with numerous interface and level design bugs fatally cripples this game.A real shame, this game had so much promise.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this but the way the characters look is really off-putting, like clay people.  The controls are clunky and certain commands are baked in like the middle mouse button being used to zoom high above the character.  The camera movement is achingly slow and annoying.  The character creation is absolutely not deep like they advertise, it's one of the most bare bones that I've seen.  No face alteration whatsoever and your body selection is based on class, it's very poor.I feel like there was a lot of ambition and maybe the story goes somewhere but I just couldn't get past the lack of polish.  It felt like the devs came up with the 'formation' battle gimmick and then tried to build a fantasy based rpg around it but ended up paying too little attention to all the things that make the most memorable rpgs good.OH and also, I bought the game yesterday before full release thinking that they'd increase the price after, like they said they would in the FAQ.  Instead they REDUCED the price as a special offer on release.  Bonkers.

_childDocuments_.review: Thumbs up here. Going to echo a few others here, this has real potential and I'm looking forward to the final product! ..but, there are some areas that need some polish before moving to full release.Most glaring issues encountered so far;-Combat targeting-Melee: This is kind of a mess and is my biggest gripe so far. Targeting is difficult sometimes, even with the pause feature. After confirming your target to auto-attack, there seems to be a slight delay before the character will actually engage the target. Not cooldown related, just a delay in the command for the unit would be more accurate maybe? Ranged: Sometimes when I'm controlling a ranged character and trying to attack a target that is in the melee dogpile, a misclick can  accidentally order to the target to move into the melee. Abilities stick to targets and respond very quickly upon activation, but auto-attacks seem to stutter a bit. Love the  grapple skill! (the skill preview in my play through wasn't showing correctly, but it worked fine during gameplay)One of my favorites :)-Time period appropriate Language-Uses a lot of current language, mannerisms, and profanity. Kinda prevents you from an immersive Celtic fantasy experience when an NPC says something similar that you've said about a crappy roommate you had in college.-Skill Descriptions/additional info-Most skills/abilities/stats need a hover over box with additional notes about what they specifically do or affect. Character creation especially needs this information, as there isn't much to be understood about putting Strength into a character except that it affects their Resilience and Intimidation. During character creation, we would like to know more about what resilience even does in this game.  :)       There isn't a clear  indication that raising Strength directly improves actually Damage, or for what weapon(s) it affects. A Preview at least would be a plus ^_^Beyond these issues the game is looking fantastic, and has potential to be great. The Formations are unique, I love this feature, but I'm not quite sure how to use it as effectively as I should be. Hoping to see some collision detection for things like the spearhead stun charge, maybe the formation breaks if the target is too big, or formation members break ranks from the remaining formation if they get stunned or crowd controlled. Plenty of potential, I'd love to see this in it's final form! PLEASE don't rush this into an early launch. You have such a good foundation for this game so far, it just needs polish and a few tweaks and you've got a real gem here. Well done.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I like the art style, the world it is set in and the genre. But aside from that everything in the game falls apart the second you boot it up. The game is plagued with an actually surprising amount of bugs. It doesn't even feel like the game is in early access titles. I have played prototypes that had more polish than The Waylanders. I'm sorry but when you encounter a bug or a glaring lack of polish every 30 seconds of gameplay if not more it becomes just painful to go on.The audio mixing is bad, the subtitles are not accurate to the voice acting, there are many typos in the english version of the game, the AI is an absolute disaster (your units can get stuck in battle against others and they won't even try to circle around them, they just wait and pray for whatever is blocking them to move, great).The list goes on and on and on.I personally have no issue with the writing as a whole but the dialogs and the story is painful to follow for multiple reasons. The pacing is really off, the game feels like it's missing half of its cutscenes and explanations and is at the same really slow in dialogs. Dialogs are built in the worst way possible in terms of immersion. It goes as follow: NPC dumps a lot of exposition on you (sometimes there are several talking to each other) and then you proceed to an interview session where you can ask 3 to 6 questions which are answered by a line or two of dialogs and then you either have another exposition dump or a very abrupt "transition" to the next scene of the game.I have seen persons saying this game feels like it's still in early access but honestly in its current state it feels like a game that is not even ready to enter early access. I get that the developers most likely didn't have the choice and released the game because of monetary reasons but that won't make me appreciate the game more.Nothing works in this game, every single good aspect is ruined by a lack of polish. The voice acting is really good but the audio mixing, horrible pacing of dialogs (was it really necessary to have a full 2 seconds of silence between each voice line?) and weird transitions between scenes ruin it. I personally really like the art style and it's probably the one part that is the least ruined but the weird animations at times (the strafing in particular looks very weird) and the lack of diversity really doesn't help it.The combat seems fun on paper there are a really decent amount of classes and even if they each have a limited amount of skills the advanced classes and the formations could be fun ? Well no because the AI is really horrendous, the aggro management feels beyond wrong and a lot of really questionable decisions have been made (resouce management, no settings for the AI ...).Unless somehow the studio gets a fortune out of nowhere and spend a year or two constantly polishing the game I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone. I wanted to love this game but in the end it only made me frustrated at myself for giving it a chance despite the fair negative reviews it's receiving.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is disappointing to say the least. I've been looking for a game to scratch that Dragon Age itch that Origins provided over a decade ago. Just playing through the intro, I think I've seen all I needed to about what this game is. I have no desire or drive to play more to arbitrarily please people about time spent. The intro is awful, the dialogue and subtitles don't match each other or the setting it's describing, the gameplay is rough and the difficulty sliders didn't even seem to work when I was switching between them for testing it out in the combat.Maybe they uploaded the wrong build, but missing a very important cutscene in the beginning of your game already shows the lack of polish and care that went into this game, not to mention the poor optimization. My frames were tanking in the intro just looking around and trying to move. This game is not finished and them "launching" it in this state is all I need to know. I'll get a refund and hope that for those who stick through it get a better experience, but I highly doubt it will.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has its graphical glitches, its audio clipping, its bits of jankiness. It's a little weird to pick up if you go in assuming it's 100% like Dragon Age (it's different from all three of them, to be honest). There are mistranslated pieces of text, the word choice is a lot more modern than one would expect of a game set in an old time period, and sometimes it feels like some lines were only given one take to record. There are also some things here and there that feel like they're missing, or parts where it felt like they'd deal with it later but then forgot about it. You definitely won't find me arguing with people who didn't have the patience or just the free time to give it a chance over something more familiar. And even though I like it, I'd  recommend people who aren't already 100% committed to start with to wait for a hotfix or two to fix some of the aforementioned glitches.But...how to put it... It reminds me of KotOR or Jade Empire, with hints of DA:O. It feels like a quirky, fanciful game made in the 90s or 00s, but made today. And that's not necessarily a bad thing, honestly. In fact, I think it's a good thing; there was a reason games like that were popular. Not to mention the fact that not every company is a AAA one backed by wealthy publishers.  was made by a company funded by a modest Kickstarter. As much as they go hard in saying, "It's like Dragon Age!", it isn't, but that's okay! They're bringing a new take to fantasy CRPGs, and I really appreciate them for it. Even if it doesn't hit, I hope that it at least makes an impact on  because at least Gato Studios attempted to make something different.The gameplay's hard to grasp at first, and thanks to some glitches, it's hard to tell what you're doing sometimes. But if, like me, you stick with it for a bit, give it an honest chance, you might just come to like it. Or at least tolerate it enough to get to the more fun dialogue, choice making, and relationship building. It all seems a little bland to begin with, but once you make it to the first real explorable zone, it feels more fresh and alive.Again: give it some time, both in game and out of it with hotfixes, and I think people could really enjoy the Waylanders and it's funky fresh style. :^)
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: It should be obvious but the Game is in Early Access and right now you are not getting your money's worth in what you can currently play.Just to clarify: I backed this game at Kickstarter and planned on playing it fully released so i didn't get alpha access but as they gave it to all backers i have access to the regular ea version not the developer one.At the current state there is only a very small portion of the game available to play with content being added regularly (at least from what i can see with the updates news) and the further you go in game you will see more things missing. There are dialogues with no voice-overs or face animations, in some you can't even see the character you should be seeing, there is a weird party switch during one quest that will make you question what is happening as it makes no sense in the game at this point (it's just a bug that get 'fixed' later when you get more companions), incorrect pronouns in dialogues and more... you can clearly see that's something that's still in the making.buuuut that aside, i actually had fun playing what is available right now and i'm probably going to play more when there are updates to see what's new. It looks like it's going in the right direction and if it all goes well the final product will be a good game. However it does seem it is going to be a 'simpler' game than Dragon Age and other games it seems to be compared to (but again, it's ea, things can change).If you know you're buying a game that's still not done and want to see how the game grows - then i can recommend it to you. Otherwise just wait until more content is added or the full release.- - - - - - - - - -Now to the other part of my review: LinuxGame played on Linux with proton. It didn't work for me straight away, got a "Fatal Error!" before even getting to main menu.First thing that did something was adding Media Foundation support  - i was thinking it may be a startup video issue and it added a screen with developer logo at the very start so probably it is needed for videos in the game.Second thing is installing dotnet with winetricks.It actually didn't install properly ( i tried version 4.8 i think, after clicking through the whole installation thing it got stuck at something) and during my first launch of the game i got an error but after clicking it away the game launched with no other problems and now it starts with no errors. So it seems to be missing something from it.I'm probably going to try doing this again on a clear prefix when i have more time just to check if what i said is correct and/or add more info to it.I only played the game that way so i can't compare if it works the same or with worse/better performance as it would on windows.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access Review!It feels like GW2 living world mixed up with Dragon Age, but not Origins, Dragon Age 2.The locations are amazing, I'm loving it, but the game is at an early stage. I did not enjoy combat, I feel it's weird for now and the devs will change it a lot before the full release.The presented story is simple but charming and the characters are awesome. I don't ming the druid, the Greek guy is my favourite and that blue 'charming as f***' creature should burn with all of her kin. But yeah, the characters are very well made, maybe the king and general are blunt but *spoiler* they die quickly.I'm looking forward to it, the lore seems to be great for lore geeks, however, I find it very odd to see that this immortal ancient being is so weak in the gameplay. The first boss fight isn't anything new, especially if you have played some top MMORPG games but it was fun. So yeah, good early access game. Nothing crazy... well, the locations are crazy. I went mad when I got into the palace. The characters' models are the opposite. It's clear that someone put a lot of work into it to make the plot cast looking good, but the style isn't working best for animations either.I would rate it 7/10 in early access and I think it can swing one up or down on the full release depending on the story and optimization.Yeah, optimization is bad here. I played it on my laptop with GTX960 and it struggles. I find it funny that it's not the number of characters or VFX in a battle. No, the fps drops when there's fog somewhere near.I giggled a few times, the game doesn't treat itself too serious which is also nice, at least if there are not too many jokes around.So yeah... that's The Waylanders for now. If you have something better than GTX960 then feel free to play it, but I'm going to wait for better optimization before I return. Or I will upgrade my setup.
