_childDocuments_.review: As a early access play I thought the game had a lot of potential.  I have edited my review to show how I felt then and now.  GraphicsThen: Pretty decent. Detailed and colorful.Now:  no change.StoryThen:  Right now the plot is jarring and i cant truly give an opinion on it.  I will say what i have seen is interesting and i cant wait for the scenes left out to be added to pull it together.Now:  Those scenes never came and the intro area becomes very jarring because of it.  The dialog feels mismatched or like you missed part of the conversation.  Some subtitles have the cues for the voice actors showing and that make it really awkward. It reads like a script instead of a conversation in those moments.LengthThen: Its earlier access still more to come how much only time will tell.Now: Decent length but feels a bit sporadic.CombatThen: I wish the ai for allies used their abilities efficiently (tactic scripts or something?) Now:  You can set how you want the AI to handle the allies abilities so great change.  Enemies are very health heavy some battles drag on.Still the same:  You can easily die if you dont pay attention.  You definitely control the flow of battle.  Ignore what is happening to even one character and it could change for the worse.  Now that I love.Player Character DesignThen and Now: There isnt much to pick from just hair style/color, eye color.  I wish there were options for longer hair length and more hair style options but that xould still change so later since this is early access.Class controls body type (which i love) but I wish I could do more with the facial features.As far as the werewolf like race I dont like how they look at all.  It would look better if all of their skin was furry versus the patches that make them look like hairy humans besides the shoulders and face.  Then their fur colors could offer more variety.NPC Character DesignsThe looks definitely fit the characters personalities.  I do feel like some got more attention than others as fair as details.My take away back then:If you are looking for a full game you should definitely wait but other wise it has a solid base cant wait to see how the finished product turns out.Now:  I was really hppeful about this game and I am now saddened by the progress.  I thought there were missing cutscenes but it wasn't.   I was hoping it would get better.  Less bugs more choices in character creation, more fluid combat.  I'm really just so surprised.  I just don't understand what happened with this game.  It had so much potential.  Still the story is engaging just jarring.  I hope the team can turn it around.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: (To note, I did refund the game)Of course, like many I was very excited to see how this game was coming along. But the tonal shifts in dialogue and poor story-writing made it hard to feel engaged. It really takes you out of the moment when characters from hundreds (thousands?) of years ago are talking in modern slang. I get the intention was to be comedic, but it didn't really work for me. I imagine the narration and dialogue will be nigh impossible to overhaul, so big bummer for immersion.The combat right now is quite shallow and under-classed when compared to the majority of other games in its own genre.  I know its early access, but the combat lacked strategy and felt lacking in general.I'll check out the game much later on, but the game feels like it was launched a bit too soon for the lack of complexity, features, and game-breaking bugs. Supposedly, the game has an experienced development team, but everything seems so rushed to be pushed out to steam. I've been watching this game for months, but after playing it, this certainly isn't in the realm of DA Origins, in either writing/narration or gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: A too ambitious game that fails at the basicsI have played during the Early access so my hour counts is not representative. Pros: Lots of Content, lots of narration, dialogues, lore. beautiful music, sometime beautiful scenery. Multiple difficultiesCons: Combat is a mess, too many things to manage, tutorial should be incremental with more of it. You constantly have to micro manage to keep you team alive, and the camera control is pretty much another enemy. Fighting in hills or inside a tight area means you lose sight of your team. If your characters are set to aggressive stance they will often leave to go fight an enemy so far away they will die because you can't reach them. The bugs are constant, some mission will crash. I have a mission where I was suppose to go back to a cave and it's not on the map anymore it is impossible to finish that quest. Overall it's a boring game and you can't get over the terrible combat. Your main character is mute and does barely anything. the whole game seem to be centred around the druid. So you lose motivation there too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing content and a lot of things to discover. As an Alpha i  highly recommend it for all type of players.It is inmersive and funny, just only some few details,  and comparing others it is the best game alpha tested until now.Long term to add content, stories, improvements... and a huge world to create starting from this.Good choice, good game  and good starting for GATO STUDIO.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: The controls are kind of clunky and the writing is bland at this point. I can feel the disappointment of the KS backers in that this should have stayed un-published until final release.  I played for almost one hour before deciding to get a refund, and wait until it's done.  I'm really afraid this early access release will kneecap the actual release, since people will be done talking about it or it will have enough negative reviews to put it way down in the recommendation list. This has happened with a couple games that I KS backed, and it's always so disappointing. Devs get run down by the negativity, and ultimately burn out before they can complete the project. Or, it gets half-a**ed and published with a whimper. This one is just such a cool idea, with a mythology that isn't overdone, and boy I am thirsty for another Dragon Age/DoS-esque party-based fantasy game. I hate the pressure on pubs/devs to release early access. Just call it alpha/beta testing like we used to, and select a group of people for testing, either through random email selection or KS backers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because I am a huge fan of DAO, and I would like to have that feeling again.The Good:The camera system is fantastic. With one click, you can change from third-person camera to isometric. The third-person view is good for a more immersive exploring, even sometimes in battle, if the AI is automatic for the companion and you are managing one character.Scenarios: The art style is excellent. I love Aunes and Dunnios specially for the moment.Dialogues and Story are fresh new and with personality and comedy characters, like the Fomorian, Delba. I really want to know more about it.The combat system is dammed fast for a CRPG. If you use the tactical pause and reduce the AI, you can micromanage every character and take your time to make every move. I also loved the alternatives offered by the battle formations. Cinematics: the animation is excellent for an indie game like this. There are only a few finished, but I suppose that we should expect more in the next updates. The voices are also outstanding.  The Bad:There are several glitches and content not implemented (facial animations, voices, cinematics...). I guess that the pandemic had a negative influence on all this.I really liked the game, and it can only get better during the next weeks. Hopefully, the team will solve these problems and I will have a game with the DAO scent that I have been waiting for.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: This game is...well kinda ♥♥♥♥ tbh. My first 20 minutes or so were alright, until i went to wake up the prince and all of a sudden we were all on the deck of the ship with no explanation. Then we had a short conversation, i "walked" around abit (its so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slow its more like crawling with two broken legs, two broken arms, and hemoroids for measure) and all of a sudden we're fighting in a jungle, the king is...dying? i think? the prince is stuck under a log and im confused.The fighting is...okay. Its not the best, but its not bad. Having right click do everything will take some getting used to (not that I was able to before a bug prevented me from going further)after fighting our way to A herculies wannabe, a cutscene broke my game and i was no longer able to attack or pick items up, so I saved and reloaded and I could pick items up again! Yay!But I couldn't progress as Someone was yelling at me to return to the boats, so i thought "oh okay i have to go the other way"Then I went the otherway and the prince was yelling at me to help him from under the log, and I was stuck.I understand that this is early access, but having missing cutscenes not even an hour into your game? Does that really seem like a good idea? I could see some later cutscenes since you may not expect players to get that far, but important cutscenes explaining plot points need to be there. I think this may be my first refund for a game since i don't see myself playing this until it is A LOT farther along.

_childDocuments_.review: I just wanted to post a quick review for those who are on the fence about this game.  It's early access and it's rough.  That said, it is also gorgeous, has a gripping story, and brings back a similar vibe from the first time I played Dragon Age Origins.  I don't have any idea what the final product of this game is going to be like, but I picked this up in early access for about 30 bucks and I'm happy to have it as part of my library.  I will update this review as the game progresses or in the sad case that it becomes abandoned by the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: I'v played 1.2 hours and even though it didn't quite meet my expectations, I see how great the game's potential is. The character customization was a bit disappointing since humans have the most origins. I expected to be able to choose out of at least two origins for every set of gender and race, but as soon as I picked those, I was left with only one origin... I liked that the game allows you to pick the pronoun your character goes by though. The game is also too quiet, and it isn't possible to increase the voices volume particularly, which makes it very hard to play without subtitles. I had to put my computer volume on 35% to start to hear characters clearly while I usually use only 20% percent of the sound. I wasn't able to increase the volume from inside of the game, 9 seems to be the highest value.Mouse does too many functions, which slows down the gameplay. Keys "F", "E", and "R" aren't being used at all, and these are such a nice keys. I wish I could search bodies using one of these keys and that I would be able to take all using a key as well.I haven't noticed "Cancel orders" button either. I gave orders to my party and then wasn't able to cancel them, so that wasn't very nice. Maybe I just didn't find it, but if there isn't one, there definitely should be. My screen also became blurred in the tactical view because of all the mountains around. They fade away and then come right back and it is quite distracting.Next, Lugaid seemed to abandon his tactics once I ordered him to use an ability. He just stopped doing anything. He stood there, in the middle of nowhere, waiting for some type of miracle.The game also asked me to give it access though firewall and I'm really confused on why. Does it use internet for some purpose? I never had such a situation before.Looking forward to see the evolution of this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: - Was too frustrating to keep playing, got a refund, not worth it.- Too expensive for the price, feels like a $10-15 product at this quality level.- Feel like I'm following a story, not engaging with it. Everyone else is doing things, I'm just a spectator.- Story isn't compelling despite the cool location and potential myth hooks.- Parts of story appear to be missing, not even a "placeholderinfo". - Character art is not good, kept getting distracted by how goofy the character's eyes and faces look. - Interface/formations confusing and basic fighting has so many frustrating interface issues (companions running off, not attacking, unable to pathfind). - Minor typos/subtitles error (not a big deal, but sucks for hearing impaired).- Couldn't find a "run" button but some areas are so big it's a slog (especially when hunting to find someone and you have no idea where they are).- No reward for area exploration, despite huge sprawling areas - they're just empty except for occasional loot box or merchant.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: There are too many bugs. Shops senselessly become empty at weird points in the game, and some of their items cannot be purchased and lack tooltips. Enemies such as the ancient dragon just stand still and die -- epic boss battle that the game hints you should come back for later, which you just absolutely faceroll stomp because the bugs.The story practically doesn't exist -- at times, characters just have four or five word sentences, or are unnecessarily and uncommonly vulgar (does Amergin have Touret's? Are all of the other characters frat boys?). Absolutely braindead trivial and boring.Chests and puzzles don't work. Quests which should award a companion fail to award it on some playthroughs. The game is steeped in bugs, should not have been released in its current state, and I spent countless hours reloading and troubleshooting trying to get the game to work and progress properly. Of course steam refuses the refund requests, but now I am happy to give a horrible review because the game is simply unplayable and should not be considered "released" at all.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: Played the Early Access first and found the game massively incomplete (Subtitles were missing, spellings were wrong, speech was all over the place and just a buggy infestation in general). However, saw amazing potential with the ideas and waited for full release.Full release now and the game looks like it has barely improved. Voice acting and subtitles don't match, some cut scenes last longer than the words itself. Characters sound like teenagers and what they tried to achieve as 'banter' just sounds outright silly. Companion quests and their storylines have literally no link to the main story and you just do it for the sake of doing it. No show of any progression from strangers to best buds/lovers with the main character whatsoever.I intend on finishing this game but it is so hard to complete ): Can barely grasp half the time what was going on in the game. No quest marker either so you're stuck with trying to run around figuring out what to do next. This game obviously needed more time in development.Edit: Game is unable to be completed as certain quests are bugged. I am currently soft locked in one where quest is completed but I cannot exit the area. This is ridiculous.

_childDocuments_.review: while the concept is really cool, the way they apply it is just awful. its trying very hard to be a dragon age game, but without any of the things that makes dragon age fun/good. it runs like a slug with combat that feels like were back in 2000, while the story jumps around so much that its impossible to understand whats going on let alone feel even the slightest attachment to any character. literally the first major story plot is just skipped over for "you" to be told to grab the special item that didn't help the guy who had it and it somehow saves you?
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely needs some time to polish. Here are some of the problems I've encountered in the 3.5 hours I've played:subtitles sometimes don't always match up with what is spoken, typos occur in the subtitles (ie turist instead of tourist), voice acting sometimes starts at awkward moments (too slow or right away), voice acting volume is inconsistent and sometimes not even present so it sounds like a one-sided conversation. Also one of my pet peeves was the voice of King Ith. I like his voice, but sometimes it seemed like he was mumbling even with the volume on fairly high compared to the rest of the characters. Camera angles were also a little frustrating when playing with keyboard and mouse, but it was much more manageable when playing with an XBOX controller. I would have also liked more interaction with the environment, seeing how there is a lot of space to walk through most of the time.Other than that I see a lot of potential with this game: the soundtrack sounds amazing and really elevates the game experience, the dialogue is fairly entertaining and voice acted quite well, the animation and graphics do seem a little bit like a last gen game but I find it charming, and at this point in the story it seems like there will be a lot to look forward to (like romances). Also not sure if this is just a personal problem, but I found a lot of the battles to be kind of difficult. My companions and my character seem to lose HP fairly quickly. I admit I don't strategize a lot in battle, but I'm hoping that there will be a difficulty adjustment setting in the near future for casual players like myself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately for now it's a do not recommend.That being said, I am liking the game for what works.The gameplay has promise, the story has some promise (if I understood it correctly), and the things that have been polished do look real nice. Actually quite fittingly the reflections in the game are incredibly polished they look so nice.But really the state of this release is shambles. I understand it's early access but certain animations are missing, crucial cutscenes are missing so you just jump from plot point to plot point not understanding what in the world is happening. There's bugs sure, there's weirdness sure, but don't butcher the story line - it's early access not like some alpha build. I think the dev's heart is in the right place but take a page out of the Divnity 2 book. Release an early access game where a certain area of the game is reasonably flesh out. Even if it's just 2-10 hours or something let that one bit give us a tease of the overall game
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: I initially wrote a positive review when this game came out. Talking about how I  really enjoyed this it. In some sort of Idealism I was hoping the games rough edges would be ironed it if not for the sole purpose that it was one of the few games to have Irish Mythology play such an active and present role. I was honestly so happy to see Irish Myth and History represented and celebrated in what I thought what the good building bones of a game. But facts were, the Irish myth focus was all that was good. The game could have been something if they had worked on it but I put out a positive review initially because I was blinded by the subject matter and that's not how reviews should work. Waylanders could have been an incredibly unique game and I wish it had been worked on more, Irish Myth and Celtic myth in general [If you'd like to call it celtic myth] Is throughly underrepresented and hopefully one day that will change. This is a dead game, it is not worth buying, don't waste yer coin lads.

_childDocuments_.review: First opinions of the game were promising, the idea and concept were intriguing. Sadly that did not last through the initial first encounter map. First off the companions AI is garbage at best, they do not defend themselves in combat not do they support the lead character at all. The biggest problem is that for a tutorial map it's way to difficult to learn anything since there is no tutorial to be had, then you end up facing a literal god for your first boss fight!!! WTF!!! I mean sure a gods henchmen maybe or at least the powered down version of the god would be okay, but the actual manifestation of a god on the tutorial level. Not cool, not cool at all. To summarize, I've tried to play this game a few times since it released as an alpha build early access and I think the company screwed up releasing it in this hot garbage mess of a condition it's in. Maybe in a year or three I might come back and see if this has improved ...... at all. Then again maybe not, they have a lot of work ahead of them if they wish to save this game from an early grave. This is just my opinion, I don't review games for a living.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: Cool concept but I cannot for the life of me create a character I care about in the slightest.Humans are humans but the customization options are extremely limited--and body shape is tied to class, which is about the silliest idea I've seen in awhile. Yes, it makes some amount of sense but it limits character customization for no good reason. Separate the body shape from classes or do away with it entirely IMO. Can't play a warrior without looking like a walking barrel with chicken legs. No thanks.Werewolves are disappointing. Extremely disappointing. They talk about them being disparate in the lore--they vary dramatically from nearly human to basically an intelligent wolf. We're stuck with slightly hairy short folk. They need more customization to swing slightly more or less either way--and give the ladies an option NOT to have mutton chops. Them being able to have facial hair is cool but the style they have looks goofy.The Mourians are just big statues with goofy eyes.The giants are almost cool but need more customization options--such as piercings, jewelry, et cetera.Giving the game a good review because it SEEMS good but when you can't get past the character creation screen because you dislike literally every character option... it's really unfortunate.Please add more options. Tons of potential but goodness is it limited at the moment--limited to the point, in fact, that you ought to just make pre-gen characters unless it gets changed. lol
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: What little bit I've been able to play, the game seems like it's off to a good start.  But as is expected in an Alpha build, improvements are needed.  The Party AI / Management System is not user friendly.  Having to setup and execute Formations during combat isn't fun for me personally. I feel like I have to micro manage my party.  Also, sometimes party members don't attack the target.  The just stand there and take damage and die.Targeting is terrible.  At times, I've been unable to target an enemy.  The tutorial said to use Right Click to target.  However, Right Click is also used for Movement, Formation Creation and Camera movement.  So when I right click the enemy to target it, my character moves towards the target.  Of course, as a mage and a ranged DPS, this is not at all what I want.  Also during right click targeting, the camera may move as well depending on how steady my hand is on the mouse.  Right Click seems to be (over) used for many things.  I personally feel the usage of Right Click needs to be limited to one thing or another.  And most of all, not associated with both Targeting and Movement.I noticed several voice overs missing or in accurate.  Sometimes what the NPC says is not what's written on the screen.  Also, some of the voice overs are very soft and hard to hear/understand.It would be nice to have a Camera Sensitivity setting.  The current sensitivity is too low for my large screen monitor.Auto loot, auto loot, auto loot ... That's all I'll say about that.This was about all I notice during my limited play time.  Currently, I'm on the BACK TO LIFE quest and have the assignment to FIND AMERIGAN IN THE OTHERWORLD.  Unfortunately, Amerigan is no where to be found on any of the maps I have access to at Level 2.  And there are no other quest givers around.  Therefore, I'm unable to advance any further.Overall I feel it will be a good game.  The character personalities are good and I like the comic relief from time to time.  I'm certainly interested to see what direction the game takes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: Seeing a lot of negative comments on this game, but I honestly don't agree with them in large part.The combat begins relatively tedious, but is more interesting the further you progress and as you unlock more abilities for each of your companions. It certainly isn't ever "too hard" like some reviewers suggest, and I think some players might be saying that on the highest difficulty (designed to be punishing) or on normal and not wanting to lower difficulty for some reason? The game supports changing difficulty on the fly at any time, so there is literally never a case of having to throw yourself at the same fight over and over unless you explicitly want there to be.Some people have said the writing can be cringy, and it can, but it's also at least passable and often intriguing. The voice acting, like some have said, ranges from okay to phenomenal on some characters -- which is a huge plus when literally all dialogue is voice acted (as far as I can tell yet far).Is it my game of the year? Probably not. Is it a passable to great CRPG that I'm having fun with? Absolutely.EDIT: After getting a few more hours into act 2 I did unfortunately have to drop the game. It loses a lot of polish very quickly, and I am not currently able to look past that. Hopefully future updates will help a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Waylanders

_childDocuments_.review: There's just no satisfaction in playing this game.Tiny skill trees, gameplay is not not fun at all, every combat feels the same. Character creation is superficial at best; seems like you have options, but you really don't. Maps feel dead and half empty. Auto-loot doesn't display what you've picked up.And the controls,....so bad. So so bad.Just stay away, pick it up when it's for sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to give this a thumbs up despite it being very rough. It is in Alpha after all. That said, the fact remains that right now, there is not a lot of content, a clunky combat system that seems light on the abilities. Oh, and it is buggy, for sure. Your mileage may vary, myself, I am running a GTX 1070 ti, i7-8700k, with 16 GB Ram.On the plus side, it is a nice looking world, the setting and story has potential. Also, the party formations is interesting. Regarding the DA:O comparison comments that I have heard about, DA:O, it is not. However, I would want to play Waylanders, not DA:O.In the end, this game needs a lot of work. I hope that they do bring forth a clean and polished game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, my input on this game so far at 1 hours is i can tell there is story (probably) intentionally missing, there are big jumps here and there. Not much explanation. The game is in a very early stage. Id say pretty accurate for an "Early Access" game, overall I think it has a good idea and good basis so far, combat looks unique and fun and the story is pretty solid. Id recommend picking this up only if you are interested in seeing this game through till release. Right now though its very early stage and can put people off. Best thing id recommend doing is putting this on wishlist and coming back in a year, if the game is in a better place, pick it up, if not then no worries.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is honestly very simplistic. Character Creation is bland, hardly any customization, recurring problems with voices and graphics. I had initially got the game in June, and played it for a while to try it out and dealing with the bugs along the way. I then stopped playing from the many bugs it had during gameplay and how bland the customization is. I picked it up again just recently to see if it had gotten any better, and to be frank, it hadn't. Customization is still bland as ever, the bugs are still many, and from what I have seen through their community posts and updates, they are just focusing on content more than this kinda stuff. I get it that it is early access, but this experience has just left me feeling bitter, so I will likely never play this game again, even when it fully comes out. Wish I could just refund this, but feels bad that it is been in my library for a couple months now. _childDocuments_.review: Waylanders starts off... pretty abrupt...After the Character creation and meeting the first few party members, you are thrusted into a diplomatic mission gone horribly wrong, which was summed up, in game, as: "A couple hours later". There, you get to encounter your first enemies and really begin your adventure.Pros of the game:>Storywise, it's got potential. It's a pretty standard "Evil arises, corrupts the world, build an army to save the world" sort of game, but with a mixture of Celtic, Greek, and more cultural backgrounds. Characters can be pretty sassy at times, and some are easily likable. >The game mechanics are interesting as there are 2 ways to defeat your enemies: - swarm them as individual units (with AIs controlling their actions)- create a formation with multiple party members which gives a slightly better advantage in the field (by how much is all dependent on the players)With these options, players are able to experiment on what tactics fits the best with their gameplayNow, here comes the cons:>As this is still in early access, cutscenes and quests are sometimes broken. In one of the loyalty missions (Amergin), skipping the cutscenes will prevent you from continuing as the crystal barriers will not disappear as you didn't see the spirit dissolve it. Speaking of, after getting a certain companion, you can't access his ability and inventory screen until after you reach the next battle. Which can be frustrating as it's a survival battle. >Character dialogues are also... a bit off... I expected the dialogues to resemble a bit like Dragon Age, with a more "medieval style" accent, grammar, or vocab. This wasn't the case as words like "f**k" are casually thrown in a weird way (intonation or tone, maybe?)>New players will have difficulty on navigating the game as the only tutorial available in-game is if you talk to the Trainer on the ship. And that only covers the basics of battle. Other things like navigating the world map (after a certain episode), figuring out the controls are all up to the player's trial and error.>It felt like certain attributes doesn't show much impact in-game. All the skills in the game are mostly determined by the damage and utility of the weapon, so having a strong weapon is good, but putting all points in one attribute is not so great. (This was tested using a lvl 4 Sorcerer with all points put on "ability effectiveness". The damage on the skill doesn't seem to scale with it as well as equipping a better weapon)>AIs are dumb. And not having the ability to adjust when to use their skills (especially lifesaving ones) can be costly.Improvements in the game will happen overtime, but this early on, it's not something you'd play around with until it's more polished

_childDocuments_.review: The Waylanders is a classic party-based RPG (feels like oldschool classic) featuring some of the top-talents who brought well-known titles (yes, there are famous surnames in the credits, I checked) within the genre like the Dragon Age, Mass Effect or Pillars of Eternity sagas...... Yes and No. It feels some like a younger stepbrother of DA;O, but filled up with bugs (just like DA;O on the release) but I feel like this last sentence is the cause of a lot of bad reviews. You see, this is not any of those games, it is an RPG, based on the same principle, however nothing alike. As a 'successor' of any of those titles, it does a pretty mediocre job, but when you play it without those references in your head, then you get a solid RPG.Do You want DA;O / MassEffect / PoE clone? This is not one.Do You need a reference to another game? Greedfall.Is it a good game? Yes, but filled up with bugs.Will devs fix it? ... I hope.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this in early access and refunded immediately.  It had incredibly bad writing in the first few minutes, so I set a timer and delved as far as I could for a game that looked like it would never see full release.  A king disowns his heir, his son, in front of the kingdom because his son had... slept in?  All of this the night before their upcoming meeting with the gods.  Immediately after this melodrama, the king confides in the player character, a no-name soldier on the ship.  Then when there should have been a cutscene, or a picture, or some text, any explanation at all, we skip past the meeting to learn that there are monsters attacking us because the gods are unhappy, oh and the king is dying.  It never gets better than that.  It was also a buggy, janky mess.  The combat was dull.  Enemy and friendly AI was nonexistent.  I watched reviews and Let's Plays throughout development.  I watched a few people playing after "release".  From what I've seen and read the game didn't get much better than what I experienced a long time ago.  Good luck with this mess if you decide to play it in 2022 or beyond.  They never even added that missing cutscene.  It's just a hard cut to the future, kind of like this game's early access to release experience.

_childDocuments_.review: So I played & reviewed this on the first day it came out over a year ago.. Now I've decided to purchase again.. & Re-review. This time I recommend the game wholeheartedly. They've updated & fixed various issues I've had with the game & now it is a joy to play. The character design, the world & the lore/story are a unique welcoming change since lately the RPG market has just been swarmed with indie titles that are just boring.The combat is tough & requires a good tactic mind at the harder difficulties which I love. You get to choose exactly how your party works in terms of classes, skills, armour & weapon types. You can upgrade your weapons with 'Gems' that allow you to choose exactly how the stats work so everything is in your favor. HOWEVER.. Enemies in this game come in large numbers so expect to be swarmed! (Which I love!) The formation system is awesome & helps you here. Now for my dislikes.. Again it's mainly with the starting part of the game. It is extremely rushed in terms of storyline & some of the voice lines are for some reason spoken really fast in some sections making it seem like the characters have just extremely broken their own characteristics. The Seer is terrible for this, making it hard to understand her at times. The story is really rushed so it's hard to grasp what exactly is going on & there is a part in the start of the game that I'm guessing for Early Access reasons is told with *A few hours Later* and then suddenly your rushed into things without knowing what the ♥♥♥♥ just happened. This happens for a good few hours & then you end up on the Vengeance again feeling like the story has just been rushed. I would wish for it to have more context in the earlier stages of the game as the later portions are told at a good pace. My own personal nitpick over the game as well is the character creator. As someone with a slim build I always make my characters quite small/thin. This game does have different body types from Heavy build to slim build which is awesome. HOWEVER.. They are locked behind what class you choose. So if you want to play as a Warrior you need to be a massive hunk of a masculine or feminine build. I normally play as a sword & shield sort of player so the inability to change my body type was massively disappointing & almost makes me not want to play the game. I hope this changes in a future update.Other than that. Yes I highly recommend this game. It has changed massively since last year & I cannot wait to see the full game!

_childDocuments_.review: Kickstarted this game. Doesn't disappoint. This is what I expected. It is a story driven rpg with a fairly deep combat system. You do have to pay attention during the tutorial. Most of the people complaining about the clunky combat system just missed a few key aspects. It is true that the game can be simple at times, combat can be overly easy at times. However....Combat can be as deep as you want to go. Pause the game and fully micro manage the game and its top shelf. Stand around and let the AI just ramble on.... yawn. There are times that just simply letting the AI do its thing is fully acceptable but there are times that taking over every character is not only more fun.... but possibly how the game was meant to be played.... and why so many people have conflicting views. I always give the game a go on normal levels. This game appears to favor combat in the pause mode. Being a bit of a micro manager. This kind of game play sounds good.... well this is your game. It has moments of just plain blah combat, but not to an obscene level. Just a normal game level of light grinding. What prg has no grind... come on now. I can see myself having fun with this game.My play time right now is low.... but I am hooked. Looking forward to more!

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Im Skill Incarnate and Welcome to My Games Review Series.My reviews cover indie games that i have bought, had gifted to me and have been provided by developers for review. In This Episode I try the highly anticipated new party based action RPG The Waylanders. Waylanders takes place in an alternate version of Medieval Spanish society with multiple kingdoms, races and religions fighting for control of the free world. The Celtic Gods, the Tuatha walk amongst mortals and when and the adventure begins when the a diplomatic expedition to the Tuatha goes horribly wrong.  The Waylanders draws heavily from Celtic Myths and legends and weaves a story of a rising kingdom with fantasy elements and an alternate version of history. Players control a party of unique characters each with their own relationships and goals in a fantasy epic.================================================The Waylanders First Impressions Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Bitchute: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Twitch: Twitter: Facebook: Email Enquiries: The Waylanders on Steam: ================================================COMPANION FORMATIONS MAKE THE DIFFERENCEThe companions who set out alongside you on your journey make a massive difference in how you’ll overcome enemies. Different party class makeups grant a variety of Formation options, each with powerful offensive and defensive abilities. As you level up, unlock new classes, and explore, you’ll discover new Formations and formation abilities to add to your roster.MAIN FEATURESThe Waylanders is an exciting fantasy RPG inspired by classics such as Dragon Age: Origins, Neverwinter Nights, and Baldur’s Gate.Travel Between Eras - Time travel between two distinct eras: Celtic and Medieval. Meet old allies and discover reborn friends as you step from past to the futureA Story Like No Other - The Waylanders blends Celtic myth from the Spanish region of Galicia with exciting fantasy adventureFaithful Companions - Befriend nine mortal and immortal companions to join you on your journeys through Celtic and Medieval Galicia. Discover their past, bond through special missions, and romance your favoritesLands to Discover in Two Era - Explore more than 50 regions filled with quests, secrets, and enemies in both the Celtic and Medieval eraMultiple endings - Choices made in one time period have dire future consequences. Players will feel the impact of their decisions in surprising and shocking waysStrategic tactical combat - Unique party formation abilities based on characters and classes open up deep, tactical combat options. Different party makeups unlock special offensive attacks and defensive abilities like Daggertip, Phalanx, Golem and Conclave.Full Character Customization - Choose from six basic classes and further specialize into one of 30 advanced classes. Create your character from five playable races based on Celtic mythology, including unusual backgrounds such as Mourian, Semi-Fomorian, and Werewolf, each with a different originImmersive Soundtrack - The Waylanders features music composed by Emmy award-winner and three time BAFTA nominee, Inon ZurPhoto Mode - Capture the excitement and magic of the world of The Waylanders as you discover it with newly added photo features

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly conflicted about this game...First, The setting and lore are some of the strongest points of this game. Very few rpgs use celtic culture aas the core of their universe, so it's a nice touch. We also have new races, a divergence form the usual races and cultures observed in that kind of game.Regarding the dialogues: I genuinely like the clash between the formal/ historical setting and the very familiar dialogues. I've seen that it's a very debated point, but personnally I do not find it cringe at all; at times it even feels very natural thanks to the great voice acting. For the story, it takes all the traditional aspects of your typical rpg: You have to save the world from dark forces, which is nothing outstanding and a safe choice for a first rpg.I like the characters too, we find some archetypes and I'm looking forward to learning more about them.Character creator: I Really like that pronouns are different from body types, but I don't get why the body types are linked to backstories in one instance .. ? Also it would be really cool to be able to customise more- Skin colour for one ... but even hairstyle or face types could be a great addition.On the least positive aspects: The pacing of the  story is off imo. Partly because it feels like some dialogues/scenes are missing (even without the elipsis at the start of the game, I think some dialogues are skipped.)There is also a strange clash between the natural feel of some dialogues and cutscenes and other which feel artificial.I'm playing on the easiest difficulty so I can't really judge but I feel like combat is clunky because the IA is entirely unresponsive even on higher autonomy. Healing VS damage taken are totally unbalanced, to the point where magic healing feels useless to me. (again, might just be bcse of the way I  play)There is a baffling lack of TRANSITION. They're just inexistant which makes the game feel very choppy, going from one thing to the other with at best a black screen to separate events?BUGGED! My game crashes constantly because my computer doesn't have enough memory for textures, apparently- Which is nonsense. I can run much heavier games. Some dialogues appear to be missing, sometimes I get stuck. The mouse cursor is the default windows cursor, some items or stat descriptions and icons are missing, I can't for the life of me change the graphics settings? They have a life of their own which is really troublesome.Although if it's only bugs, the good thing is, it will be fixed eventually (I hope so!)Conclusion:So far it's a fun game, with some promising aspects, however I don't think it was ready to leave Early access.. It's really a shame. I honestly don't know if I can recommand it or not, I'm putting in a good recommandation bcse I think it can get better with much deserved bug fixes and updates, but as it is- It's basically still in Early Access. You can see the essence of the game, but it's not  quite manifested yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really REALLY wanted this game to work. It had so much promise, and anything that smells like Bioware RPGs immediately has my attention. As a queer person, it immediately caught my attention that you can have queer relationships and also be polyamorous. It's hard to underestimate how important it is to someone like me to have that representation, especially in a game that promised great character development and relationships.I tried early access just about as soon as it was released, and it was rough, but that was no big deal. It's early access. I figured I'd just come back when it had more polish. The problem is, while it's more developed since released, it has...not really improved. Now, I want to say that some of my issues may be because I haven't figured certain things out, but if that's so, the game hasn't helped me do that either, which it should.I'll start with the little red flags: the subtitles often didn't match the speech, there was weird punctuation, and there were misspellings in tooltips. These are things I would have expected to be caught and fixed in beta at least. It comes off as unprofessional. The audio balancing is pretty bad, and the audio quality of different voice lines even within the same conversation is variable. There were a couple of weird screen tears in cutscenes.That was just the tip of the iceberg, though, because the real problem for me is that the combat is garbage. It's super unresponsive, the AI is stupid and has no self preservation, healing barely seems to work, and casters can't stand up against melee enemies. If I'm attacking something at a distance and an enemy comes up to whack me in the face, I just have to sit there and take it or run away and try to target it, but since it's followed me, that's only so effective.  The attack speed is so SLOW that the enemy gets in free hits while I'm just slowly dying to enemies at the beginning of the game. I am not new to RPGs, so it's not a lack of competence. Now, I've only played about 90 minutes of the game in total, but after I failed the first mission and had to restart it over from the beginning, I quit in frustration. This is not my idea of fun. If it's challenging, fine. It's more interesting if it's challenging. But the first mission ought to be a relatively low-risk extended tutorial that allows you to get used to combat and figure out how things work. You shouldn't be outnumbered by enemies in terrain that makes things even more frustrating while trying to learn what your abilities are and how they work. On normal mode, should be hard to fail  even if you don't really know what you're doing. I can forgive a fair number of things for an indie game that has such promise in the plot and the story world, but I can't deal with the combat. The game needs MUCH more polish and some substantial improvements to combat before I'll consider coming back. I'm actually kind of devastated it sucked because I haven't been so excited for a single player video game maybe ever.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly really disappointed, when I first got this game in early access there were a lot of problems but everything seemed like they'd be things that would be fixed before launch but now on the release date pretty much all my problems still remain. First off and most broadly, the whole things doesn't quite flow or gel together, instead it feels like a bunch of sepereated thing glued togetherThe combat is clunky, there are no basic things like auto-attack and you need to actually see a good portion of the enemy so you can actually click on them, this becomes difficult in melee where the character can easily cover up the enemy which will leave you standing there doing nothing while the enemy wails on you. The animations are kind of stiff and more than a little awkward. The writing is okay but sometimes it feels kind of off. The worst part for me was the audio implementation which is just- bad, that's the only way to say it, the voice acting will sometimes cut off early or be covered up other audio in ways that make it seem messy, choppy, and amateurish. The background ost is pretty empty and just feels like this massive gap in the world that could easily be fixed by good audio or even a passable one, as it stands scenes that would have been massively helped by some background audio just feel empty and hollow. The voice acting for the most part is pretty bad with it not feeling natural and has this quality to it that doesn't blend well with the game the characters don't really sound like they're actually there, for the most part, they don't really seem like the characters no they seem like voice actors in the recording room who's character is just kind of plastered on. They don't sound real. _childDocuments_.review: Welp, the game is out and I wanted to like it, but there's just too many little things getting in the way of me continuing. The minor texture glitches and missing item descriptions. Subtitles are wrong compared to the voice acting (which isn't bad, I'll give them that). Frame rate drops at random times. Hearing the sound for an interaction, yet not being able to tell what's interactable. All this piles up over time.I could possibly look past that if the plot was good. Unfortunately, it's a mess. Many times events will happen and the characters will allude to them like you should know what happened, but at no time were you shown or told what was going on. The writing isn't awful, but it falls into the Joss Wheden trap where nearly every character is "the clever one", always ready with a quip, humorous, or snarky remark for the situation or what someone else said. As a result, the character's personalities start to blend together and I feel like I'm watching a group of modern day 20-something role players that got transported into another world and decided "♥♥♥♥ it, let's just have fun with this". It's not this way 100% of the time, but it happens often enough that it really takes me out of the experience.All together, it feels like this was a studio who's reach exceeded their grasp and by the time they realized it, it was too late. I think they could make a fine game in the future and I'd be willing to give them another chance, but The Waylanders isn't it.

_childDocuments_.review: The description, sold this to me. This is from the creator of  Dragon Age and Pillars of Eternity? Sign me up! But see, that is the problem. I play those two series for story. Story. That includes how the story is told to the player which brings me to my first problem with the game. I can overlook missing cutscenes, I can ignore clunky gameplay, IF, the story at the core is compelling. I'll use one word to describe the story; "Cliche." Even though every adventure in some way is based on the "Hero's Journey," in many ways they differ from each other through the use of writing.Thus, we arrive at the second problem; writing. I am in now way an expert, and wouldn't presume to tell professionals how to do their work. I am however an audience/player, and in my eyes; 1. The supporting characters are shallow, embodying traits instead of real personalities. 2. The dialogues lacks depth, everyone speaks in the same way, tone, and style. 3. The hero lacks origin. Unlike Dragon Age or Pillars of Eternity, where what the hero experience beforehand plays a huge role on how others interact with them, in Waylanders, the hero is the same, no matter what he/she was before the story.4. On a side note, I just can't understand this decision. The story is set in Ireland. IRELAND. Orlesian from Dragon Age sounds French. The Vailians in Pillars of Eternity sounds Spanish. Why are the Celts from IRELAND, speaks with an American accent? Why? Do you know how much depth and personality you can add to the game  by just adding the right accent?The above are the reasons why I ultimately refunded the game (besides the hard crashes and buggy gameplay). I must say, I feel like I am looking at another Mighty No. 9 scenario. My disappointment is immeasurable, and my faith in "the top-talents who brought well-known titles within the genre like the Dragon Age, Mass Effect or Pillars of Eternity sagas" is ruined.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not going to a full breakdown, a review or a first impressions, non of those count for a game not finished and in Alpha.What I am going to do is tell you what I feel about the game right now, what I thin it's potential is and somewhere in there whyI would first of all like to ask everyone go read this  as it will tell you what it means to be in early access, it seems to me very few people seem to get what it means.I will make it simple though and draw you attention to my main point;Early access, also known as early funding, alpha-access, alpha founding, or paid-alpha, is a funding model in the video game industry by which consumers can purchase and play a game in the various pre-release development cycles, such as pre-alpha, alpha, and/or beta, while the developer is able to use those funds to continue further development on the game. To The Game! (can someone play that little piece of music they played in Batman when they would go to the Batcave)The world in which The Waylanders is set is beautiful, buggy, not ready for full release, missing some assets and cut-scenes to explain the story full, some line and so, this is Early Access and something I fully expect and understand so we are taking that off the table here and now.It is simply a beautifully crafted world, one that, when completed, you can tell will draw you in and gobble up hours of your time, it has fun charismatic characters brought to life in a wonderfully crafted story and by some talented Voice Actors.The game draws from many sources, or rather takes inspiration from them, Dragon Age (Mike Laidlaw even consulted on the project), Fallout (Something that is not a surprise seeing as Chris Avellone was a writer on the project) and pulling on characters with heart who act as you would expect them to in the situations thanks to Emily Grace Bucks (Lead Writer) experience writing characters we connect with and care for, for Telltale Games.The game is steeped in respect for RPG’s everywhere and pulls together a wonderful story for us to experience in a beautiful world to explore.The controls currently feel OK but need some tweaking and shoring up to make it feel just right but there is time enough to get there.The graphics style is perfect for the game and is delivered well, it is a beautiful game to behold and while far from optimised does a good job of running well enough, bearing in mind it is essentially an Alpha; there are FPS dips, it will crash occasionally and as I already mentioned, it is missing assets etc but what is there gives a very promising sneak peak at what is to come.  The world is not a truly open one rather large and small zones connected by load points, speaking of loading, times are short enough not to worry about and will no doubt get better, although the larger the zone you are going into the longer the load, makes sense right.The Developer, Gato Studios, founded by two brothers and has grown from a small team to something much larger that now consists of experience from companies such as Telltale and Rockstar and new talent with youthful and wide eyed enthusiasm to create the epic RPG they want to, and they want to exceed expectations.I for one think they can deliver something that will set itself apart from other Indie titles and that will win the hearts of many RPG gamers, at this stage of development I would say by the game only if you are happy you are doing so to help fund the further development and if you are so inclined test features and report back any issues you may find, i.e. buying an Early Access game.

name: Inkulinati
detailed_description: Buzz JOIN OUR DISCORD About the Game Inkulinati is a turn-based strategy game inspired by medieval manuscripts. Draw your army of Beasts, and spill the ink of your enemy, defeat medieval superstars and collect perks to unleash hidden powers. Being a master of the quill isn’t easy, so make sure you’re focused and plan every move wisely. Embark on your journey and become the greatest Inkulinati of all time! Don’t let the looks fool you. Inkulinati is a game of nuance and brain-sizzling challenge that will test even the most hardened strategists. And as every hardened armchair general knows, it all starts with your units, which we call Beasts. There are multiple deadly (and bizarre) Beasts to unlock. They all have their special individual skills, as well as class-specific abilities causing different effects. And when these Beasts work in unison, a symphony of destruction, death, until the literal apocalypse will endure. It’s not just your Beasts that can cause havoc and damage. There are special, battle tide-turning actions performed by the Inkulinati Masters themselves - such as yourself! Use your unique Hand Actions to smash your opponent's units, draw obstacles to create barriers, relocate your units with a move of your finger, or explode your troops to create pure, pure chaos. Just remember - your opponent can do it too. And to keep it more interesting, each Inkulinati Master can have their own set of Talents too that can help win the battle. But wait, there’s more. You will need to adapt your tactics to every battle. Each Battlefield is its own domain, with its own particular dangers that you should watch out for, and opportunities that you can use. Look out for objects that are scattered all over the Battlefields , such as exploding Pots of Beans, travelling Hell’s Maws, Clouds of Blessings, and use them to your advantage. And just when you think you have a handle on the battle, an Apocalyptic event can come in and flip all of your plans upside down. We’re talking fires, plagues, and the Memento Mori itself. However, when all hope is lost and you’re on the ropes, an Apocalypse might be just what you need to turn the tide in your favour. There are different difficulty levels to choose from depending on your cunningand know-how, so even younglings will be Inkulinati-Masters in due time. And for those that want to know the ins and outs, you can learn how to master it all in our Academy mode , where we teach you step-by-step all the nuances to win every battle. Uncover the mystery and secrets of the Inkulinati and face such opponents as Hildegard, Dante Alighieri, and more. Go out into the world and start your adventure! Fight the biggest Inkulinati masters in the land, tame the untamed Beasts, build your ultimate army, try to bring back your Master from the clutches of death, and most importantly, finish your grand quest with the biggest party that the middle ages have ever seen! The best adventures are those of your own. In Journey mode you will create and develop your own character. As any aspiring Inkulinati Master, you will get to create your own Inkulinati character. During your journey you will learn the secret techniques of drawing new Beasts and Inkulinati Hand Actions, allowing you to choose the composition of your army. You can be a brave knight that has no fear or a nun who with the power of prayer can confuse her enemies and heal thy own servants. Those styles, and more, are waiting to be discovered and made your own. Express yourself! On your journey you won’t just battle against other Inkulinati Masters. You will face untamed Wild Beasts, go against Beast Lairs, meet interesting characters such Bards and talking Geese, visit shops, scriptoriums, and loads more. It is one heck of an adventure! Inkulinati will bring you back to the Golden Era of hot-seat mode. Face your friends, family, or foes, and decide who is the greatest Inkulinati Master in the house! Choose your Army, Talents, Inkulianti Master, the Battlefield, and other criteria and options, and face a battle that will be remembered for the ages. 700 years in the making, finally these bizarre art pieces can come alive in a video game and show that medieval people also had their “memes” and that they laughed from the same silly things that we do today. You’ll see sword-wielding rabbits, dogs with spears, trumpets lodged in bottoms, human-eating snails, and more. Much, much more…

short_description: Inkulinati is a turn-based strategy game straight from medieval manuscripts, where a rabbit’s bum can be deadlier than a dog's sword. Become a master of the Living Ink, build your own bestiary, defeat medieval superstars and collect perks to unleash hidden powers.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, Inkulinati is a goofy game with unpretentious absurdist humour. It was made for the aficionados of tightly designed head-scratchers, focusing on delivering entertaining challenges, taken the visual form of medieval manuscripts. To make sense of its screenshots, you'd need to have a passion for delving deep into its strategic intricacies. And it's a roguelite, believe it or not! Permeated by funny and welcoming tactical puzzles where positioning is king. Having such a great setting and little to no RNG during its battles, the game is a joy to learn. I didn't say you can learn it fast, though. There's one extensive tutorial, which could take you hours to complete. However, in case you're an impatient type, you can jump into the main campaign right away. The UI is clean and intuitive, comprehensive tooltips coupled with a built-in encyclopedia should cover your lapses in knowledge. Besides, almost all of the tutorial pop-ups repeat during the campaign.Tiny is what the game calls the avatar of your hero, an Inkulinati (ink + Illuminati), who looks at the manuscript with your eyes while playing as oneself on its pages, drawing beasts to help them fight for your intellectual superiority. You win fights by defeating all foes and, if present, an opponent's Tiny. Directly or through devious means like pushing them into the abyss, feeding them to a hazard, or the Fire of the Apocalypse. Epic. Combat is turn-based, but you can't play all units successively. It's like checkers - you move a unit, your enemy moves a unit. Unlike checkers, when all units on the field made their turns, the round ends, triggering certain traps and damaging effects like bleeding, while also replenishing ink that you harvest in a few ways. You need the ink to draw units, it's their blood. Like in a card game, allies come to the field unable to act immediately. When they do, they can move as a separate action, then do something cool or just attack. Attack damage is determined by a simple QTE. Attack from behind for more damage, higher accuracy slows the QTE down, and so on.It only sounds complicated on paper, I swear! And we barely scratched the surface, I'm so sorry. Okay, so, talents are passive power-ups that can grant your Tiny immunity to plague or let you buff a beast by pushing it with a Hand Action. Hand Actions are like magic, except the spells are on a cooldown. Squish foes with your finger or swipe them into the abyss, create a special obstacle or make someone dance and fall to their doom. Yes, we have the heights to abuse as well as a whole Pleiades of obstacles and environmental hazards. Hell's Maws can devour anyone but a hellspawn, pots of beans explode, lairs spawn foes until destroyed. Healing Clouds, Clouds of Divine Inspiration, altars, boulders, gates that only open for one side or none... you get the gist. Pushing foes and obstacles offensively and defensively is half the battle. Throw enemies into plague clouds and maws, crush them against the gates. Set things on fire, camp the holy spots, spill their blood and draw your army with it!And what an army it is! The roster is vast, making for an impressive number of approaches you can attempt. Paramount for a tactical game. To boot, all units are drawn and animated in a dashing manner. Take a slug with a hand holding an axe or a sling or a levitating head of a bear. Each combatant even has a name for flavour and, more importantly, comes with a couple of unique practical skills. The creatures are diverse, and not just visually. Sheep put others to sleep. Cats are anointed and everyone who hits it becomes a heretic, receiving double damage from anointed creatures. Rightfully so. Snails devour their prey whole. Hulking hares throw explosive pups. A donkey can fart through a bagpipe, stunning enemies. Foxes are generally good at stealing ink, rabbits are pious, monkeys are pungent, dogs are sturdy, demons and fish leave damaging fields. And merry skeleton troubadours provide jolly good company.But draw these guys with care, don't spam. Your Inkulinati gets bored of drawing the same beasts. The level of boredom gets raised by one with each drawing and a beast's ink cost goes up accordingly after every fight. If a beast skips a fight, its boredom lowers automatically. This feature forces you to switch things up every other battle. It's beneficial to have separate trash armies for specific occasions and treat each unit as a valuable commodity. You can also lower your boredom in a Chapel or through specific random events. Dedicated beast battles where your Inkulinati doesn't participate provide that service as well. You learn all these basic rules in the first few hours, then embark on a roguelite campaign to spend the rest of the time wallowing in hardcore cerebral pleasures for nerds. What's the goal? To kill Death, for starters.The goal may not seem so hard at first, but the going gets tough on later maps and using certain army types can pose quite a challenge. Some boss encounters are cruel, too. With all the difficulty options, I'm sure you could find the one that suits you. The game is pretty freeform in all aspects. And it makes you come back for more, having a bunch of unlockable armies, hand actions, and talents. So, after picking your starting army and abilities, you venture forth, getting pitted against a bunch of freakish things, sometimes led by no one, sometimes - by other Inkulinati, from Saint Francis of Assisi to an Ape Professor. It's that kind of game. There's even a meta-plot - an overarching conspiracy! It's played for the laughs, but it got me curious enough to get to the bottom of it. In the end, the story is a nothing burger, of course. It's the path that matters.Your initial army is but a drop in a sea of beasts you get to acquire during each campaign. The combinations are endless and you'd be surprised at how different every run feels because of it. For example, using skelly boys with alcoholic monkeys is efficient since bones are immune to their filth. The campaign facilitates several branching Slay the Spire maps filled with shops, events, and battles. The encounters are varied and you can normally pick between two or three going forward, depending on your priorities. There are several types or randomised battles, each procures a designated reward. Quills are probably the greatest of them since those are your lives, but your army is your lifeblood, so units are one of the main resources to obtain. Then comes the gold to buy armies and talents. Keeping your Tiny's ink and health caps high is also important. To abuse your fame, you need to garner Prestige, which gives you more options in non-combat encounters and unlocks more armies in meta-progression.Despite being rather hard on higher difficulties, it's a comfy game to play while sipping on tea. Just make sure not to bite the cup too hard after ruining another perfectly winnable battle with a stupid mistake. This game could use an undo. Once per battle is all I ask! But I wouldn't want to seem ungrateful, the game did more for me than I could ever hope for. It's a bundle of joy! The FMV cutscene at the start caught me off guard, and it wasn't the last thing to do that. That's how you use the local array of spells, too! By messing with the manuscript with your FMV hands. On bosses, the combat log gets scribed on the very page you play. Isn't it just so clever and elegant!? Inkulinati is overflowing with such cheeky shenanigans. Once, I thought I won, but then forgot to move and made it a draw by burning in the Apocalyptic Fire while Godfrey got devoured by a Hell's Maw. What an absurd combination of goofs and brilliance! Monty Python lives through works like Inkulinati. Truly, there's nothing like it.My curator

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to leave a negative review for Inkulinati, because it's a genuinely charming game and the tactical battles have much to recommend them - the importance of movement and positioning of units is critical to success, and it's very easy to set up quick wins or suffer unexpected defeats because of your skill as positioning, or lack thereof. However, the game suffers tremendously from a campaign structure that works at odds with its battle system.The point of a branching campaign structure is to force the player to make difficult and interesting decisions to increase the power of his build to be able to better fight increasingly difficult opponents, but this simply does not hold true in Inkulinati. You're offered upgrades to your avatar on the battlefield, and can swap out the units you choose to draw, but enough units are similar enough to one another that they don't feel like upgrades but rather different tools in your arsenal, so there's no sense of progression on the campaign map. Further, later combats aren't significantly more difficult than earlier ones because the emphasis on positioning makes it possible for players to win battles with inferior armies - and "superior" units cost significantly more ink to draw than "inferior" ones, meaning it's often better to just use cheaper, worse units anyways.This creates a sort of fatigue playing through a campaign, where it feels like you're just going through the motions of a campaign structure because the developers believe it to be obligatory to hold the game together, when it does not meaningfully improve the experience. And as the player, I'm forced to go through these campaigns multiple times because in order to unlock new units with different abilities, I have to beat the campaign repeatedly. My experience with the game has been "picking up the game, playing a few battles, realizing that none of the decisions made on the campaign map actually matter all that much, and putting it down."Inkulinati has the potential to be a fantastic tactical puzzle game, but until these issues with the campaign structure are resolved in some way I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: After beating death on normal I don't ever feel like playing this game until they both properly balance the game and also make the roguelite mode more fun since it's rather bland. Currently there's a lot of very unfair stuff like donkeys still existing with their insane range fart stun on enemies(on 2 CD) that's way too strong for this game since most of the maps are very small, if you manage to get two of these as enemies at the start it's GG unless its a bigger map. They should make the range smaller or make it apply to friendly targets as well. Some maps are also filled with things like spark fire causing 3 damage each turn, an instant lose if you do not have access to devils that are immune to fire. You can also be a victim of random BS like plague clouds spawning on your side close to your commander which you cannot remove and deals 3 damage each turn on the target. The infected target then spreads it on contact or at the end of the turn to adjacent targets, making it harder to deploy beasts if you cant move the commander out of the way to not get poisoned. The duel encounters in this game which is 5 v 5 with no commander, is very RNG based in the later areas as all the enemy gets to move on turn one after you compared to all or some of them napping. Depending on the random placement of your units it can be impossible to win. There's also this really bad system when the enemies or you (with no commander) getting free +5hp heals and random damage boost on collecting 12 ink (way too easy to get with the amount of ink on the floor). This just makes the game too snowbally as the HP of most units is around 10, allowing it to just waste the enemy's or your first round of damage.Ranged enemies are also very strong as they can easily destroy your commander since you need cover terrain to block(randomly spawns or acquired from shop/loot). But these cover terrain cant really block shots vertically, forcing you to take tons of damage on the map where you are spawned on a top platform with enemy archers on the bottom that you cannot easily one shot since they are far away. They could give an ability to the swordsman which have shields the ability to block arrows for the person behind him since they are kinda crappy compared to other units with their extremely situational cleave skill.On the balance of starter beasts you can start with, between the animals you get early on (rabbit,dog,fox) I feel that the dog is way better compared to everything else since they have higher damage to kill things quicker. The rabbits dont get a damaging skill and have lower damage in exchange for a situational stun, which can be good as a pick up during the course of the game but not at the start where you need to kill things. The foxes are immune to debuffs on hitting clerics but also lose access to prayer, a very big downside since you need to be unpushable to stop the enemies from insta killing with a push. They also get ink steal on their damaging skills which is good if you manage to hit two enemy targets to steal two ink.The bean monsters and devil monsters are balanced well, but the skeleton enemies are just insane with their debuffs guaranteeing 5 damage since removing it needs another attack from an enemy, a push action on the target or a halo. Most of the time it might not be worth it as all the skeletons will be able to easily reapply the debuff.During the course of the game, you don't feel like you are getting stronger or really making any meaningful choices on beast picks(just collect elites and also cheap minions to cycle for boredom). The talents all kinda feel anemic, some are really good but the rest are just crap. Actions are also kinda the same, but you are limited to 3 even though you can collect more than that and mix and match for each battle. The act again actions and healing is probably the best there, with others like damage causing or enemy sleeping skills situational as you dont want them to get too close or move your commander near the enemy. I think there needs to be an ability to upgrade the beasts you own into more powerful ones and/or borrow a page from autobattler games, give bonuses for having same type of beast/class.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkulinati

_childDocuments_.review: Inkulinati is good game, but kinda lacks the punch; it feels like a proof of concept and in some ways the concept doesnt carry an entire game. The visuals are great but the gameplay loop is repetitive without at times offering a fair challenge (at times youre just matched against enemies that are way too hard). I dont really know how to mitigate those flaws, perhaps they should add a levelling system for individual units. I know all of the monsters are lovingly crafted, but at the same time many are not so good, or very circumstantial. Also: dont punish players for using the same units, its very counter-intuitive to disrupt the gameplay flow by making the good units too expensive. I did play 10+ hours but I didnt feel like playing another 10, and I guess this is the biggest criticism I have.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the concept is pretty good. Turn-based combat, rouge-like maps and upgrades as you go along. These are the games I love. I think the balance is just... off. Mainly trying to articulate this for the devs because I love this game so far, but see some pretty clear things that would make myself a repeat player.Making the early troops more meaningful would go a long way. Once I unlock the hellion starters, there's no reason to use anything before it. They clearly outclass everything up to that point. I'm not really sure the solution here. Ink costs? Re-balance some of the effects? Maybe have a thing where we can level up beasts once at the shop as opposed to hellions or skeletons who wouldn't be able to. To follow up on that last point, the effects are crazy. Bleeding, infection, fire, and especially that dance macabre one. I believe the fire sparks are actually in a good spot. The idea of comboing with some of the hell minions is a fun idea. The dancing effect? That is actually just not fun at all. Every time I get to skeleton rounds, I get to a point of just wanting to not play. There was one round that 2 characters wiped my entire team in the opening round because one can walk up 2 spaces and effect an area of 12 spots with an 8 damage move that leaves everyone dancing for another 5 damage at the end. This kills any character except the big dog and if nothing else touches you, cerberus. This can't be intended, right? Am I supposed to just skip after dying every time I come across a skeleton battle in a small area? Even if they weren't to insta kill and entire team with two characters, that dancing effect is just absurd. You have to halo, push, or attack your own team to end this. Like, are you serious? So half my team has to restore the other half, when the next turn they'll just start dancing again from the next skeleton. I do not understand why this is as strong as it is and I really feel like it needs to be looked at. Last thing, and I know it isn't supposed to necessarily be on my side or anything, but what's with always being forced at the bottom of 3 tiered maps and they get archers who can hit your tiny from literally anywhere? There are so many places in this game where it just feels like punishment to be punishment. No counter play to some of the tactics it seems like. Besides balance, there's been one recurring bug that has tilted me. I'll try and give as much detail as possible...It seems to happen on boss battles, and specifically when I am using that floating head. It seems to happen specifically around attacking with, or being attacked on that troop. The opposing mini will go to their turn after I use this troop/this troop gets attacked, and the tiny will be permanently "drawing". I am sure it's been reported, but just had to get that out there. You have to go back to the map and reload and get completely different RNG on positioning and stuff. Overall I recommend because it is fun, there are just some tweaks that would keep me in the hundreds of hours gameplay loop similar to slay the spire, and it's just not quite there at the moment. I do think it will get there though :)
