_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a simcade racer that plays well on a controller, this is it.Controller handling is SUPERB in this game. Pushing different cars to the very limit is extremally satisfying here.Ignore the hate, most of the negative comments are useless anyway, criticizing unimportant things like menu graphics (who the hell cares?), or saying stuff like 'just play PC2'. PC2 was a buggy mess, compared to PC3, and it was barely playable on a controller. Most of the PC2 physics and car mechanics is still present here, in a streamlined, more usable form.Track and car selection is very good. Rivals mode (daily/weekly/monthly challenges) is alive and well, so you can compete against other drivers in hotlap or pacesetter challenges.Multiplayer is also not dead, you can easily find people to race with, at least in EU.I recommend to get this one on a sale, with all DLCs - extra cars and events are really nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: This is from the perspective of someone who enjoys sims like Assetto Corsa, iRacing etc, but also enjoys games such as Gran Turismo, Forza, GRID, NFS etc.This game is not a sim. If you're after a sim, this is not for you. If you're after a fun racer with very enjoyable "simcade" handling, try this out, you will enjoy it. It drives great with both a wheel and a controller, and for those who like to play with a controller in chase cam, this has one of the best chase cam's in recent memory, right up there with Forza.What's the handling like? It's a blend between Forza Horizon and DriverClub, which is not a bad thing. While not a simulator, the cars still behave like cars, you will understeer, oversteer etc. Unlike NFS Heat as an example, where the cars don't really behave like cars at all, or GRID where they feel very floaty. The car handling is very enjoyable, as an arcade style racer.To avoid making this review too long, the game is fun to play but rough around the edges and lacks polish. It's fun handling is packaged around a mediocre mobile game like career, with average visuals and average sound. With that said, some cars do sound really good in "hood" view, so sounds are a mixed bag.Is it worth full price right now? No. But when it's on sale, get it.Overall, it's a 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great racing game, but labeling it Project Cars 3 is completely misleading. It has shifted to a more sim-cade Racing Game rather than a balls to the wall Racing Sim like the previous 2 titles. If you're a casual person who enjoys playing racing games with an Xbox, Playstation or any gamepad/controller, this game will definitely work for you. It's directed and suited toward the casual Racing Gamers, rather than the hardcore Sim Racers. It's honestly a let down, but me being a casual who loves playing Racing Games with an Xbox Controller, I love it. I've played NFS SHIFT previously, and Project Cars 3 feels like a successor to NFS SHIFT and SHIFT 2 Unleashed. Except, Project Cars 3 is overall better than both NFS SHIFT Titles Combined.Overall, I would recommend playing Project Cars 3 with a gamepad and search for a cheap Steam Key or wait for a Steam Sale. It isn't worth paying full price.

_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this for a fair amount of time, I have felt like I can come to a clear conclusion.1 This is nothing like PCars 1 or 2 which honestly I am fine with as I have always had issues getting my wheel set up to work comfortably with the games and so having the accessibility to play with a game pad was great but that's like the only positive I can think of. The game feels wrong to be honest, breaking is never smooth and setting up the car is like taking part a active bomb without the manual. The AI is way to aggressive and/or doesn't even realize where you are and the objectives feel way to hard to beat. It's almost as if there was no QA or play testing done and I feel that with being bought by Codemasters, SMS has gone down hill. I can not recommend this game at full price, maybe heavily on sale. but realistically I had fun for 2 hours and then it became a chore to play.

_childDocuments_.review: There are many Sim racers out there, all of which i am extremely fond of. I am by no means an avid Sim racer, i just love the challenge these racers offer, subjective realism and handling that all claim to be better than the rest.My 60 or so hours in PC2 have mostly been hot lapping as i wasn't drawn to the career, to be frank it was crap. Every race same car, different weather, rinse and repeat.PC3 on the other hand has kept me fully engaged within the career mode for the 6 hours i've had so far, you can mix it up, different cars with different set ups and upgrades.One thing i feel this is doing well is forcing me to rethink my upgrades depending on what race or challenge i am doing, each race requires a certain class of vehicle so this is quite challenging, we all want full on speed but the handling really matters and this is completely apparent for many of the races i've done so far.Playing with my Thrustmaster wheel is an absolute blast.Call this what you will, ill call it fun and leave it at that :)

_childDocuments_.review: I never wrote a review but after playing this amazing game I had to. I had hope for this game as I liked the shift series and thought that it was great. So when I first heard the news about this game I was happy. My first impressions of the game were okay. But then I woke up, and realized how bad this game is. My first problem with this game was that track limits were all over the place. On certain tracks you would get a penalty for dipping 2 wheels on the curb. On the some tracks you cant cut a whole turn and get no penalty. There is no consistency with the penalty system. Also if you hit people off the track you get no penalty, so if someone punts you off the track too bad. Go catch them back up even though you cant cause you are 60 seconds behind them. This is a major problem but there is many more. Another problem with this game is the curbs. Some of them are okay but some of them spin your car as soon as u touch them. Again there is no consistency.  But I remembered this is SMS and they never fix ♥♥♥♥. Another problem with this game is the liveries. If you are in a championship your liveries just disappear and your car is just all red. So there goes your hours spent on a livery. But they come back once you go back to the garage so its not to bad. Another problem is the AI they are so bad. Just as bad as the AI is need for speed shift and shift 2 unleashed. There goes your next gen AI punting you off the track. This whole game is just bad. They are also lying about the 200 plus cars as there is a good amount of racing versions of already existing cars. Which are made up racing cars that are made to match the real racing cars in the game such as GT3 Cars, GTE Cars, TCR Cars, etc. Pretty much the works system from need for speed shift and shift 2 unleashed but used in a much worse way. And don't expect any of this to change or be fixed because the game is made by SMS. Another problem is force feedback which is pretty bad and feels almost the same as need for speed shift except that's a 11 year old while PC3 is a 2020 game. This game has a lot of problems which is to be expected from a game made by SMS. This game is a bad simcade game and is a really bad simulator. The physics are fine until you turn traction control off and your car feels like it has no grip. Which is made even worse which the bad force feedback in this game. Even the upgrade system is worse than the shift series. If you upgrade certain parts like brakes in the shift series you can see the rotors and calipers change, if you upgrade the tires you can see the tires change, if you upgrade the interior you can see the interior change. In PC3 none of this is there if you upgrade you car nothing looks different. It looks like you did nothing at all until you do a race conversion which was in the shift series but it was called a works conversion. This game does not even have real gt classes but has real p1, p2, p3 classes. Guess which game had this shift 2 unleashed a 9 year old game. Ever since they left EA they went completely downhill. Which is the first studio I have seen that has left EA and actually got worse. That just shows you how bad this dev team really is. This game is a complete downgrade to everything that lead up to it. I have spent over 20 hours on this game so I could give it a proper review.  Avoid this game at all costs and save your money. I had hope before this game now I have none. I also had 100 more dollars before this now I have 100 dollars less.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't care that this is an arcade racer, there are plenty of other sims and there aren't many arcade track racers left anymore. I also have a pretty high tolerance for bad racing games, I liked Flatout 4, Ridge Racer Unbounded, and DiRT 5.What I do care about is that the career mode is one of the most poorly designed things I've seen in the literal hundreds of racing games I've played. It's structured exactly like a mobile game, you gain money incredibly slowly, and only meaningfully gain money from leveling up. It honestly feels like the game was built with micro-transactions in mind, even though there are none.All events require specific cars that you have to constantly be buying, and if you buy the wrong car (like the C8 Corvette in the early game, you know, the cool new cover car), you've just wasted your money because that car tier's events require cars made in Europe between 1990-1995 on a Tuesday and start with the letter L. Selling cars gives pennies back.If you want to save up for the car you want to drive without wasting money on extra cars at lower tiers, you will also have to spend money to unlock higher tier events early. I cannot wrap my head around why *anyone* thought this was a good idea.The driving mechanics are honestly solid, it feels like the natural evolution from the NFS Shift series, but singleplayer is god awful and multiplayer is dead. Buy GRID Legends instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this as a gift because I never wanted to play it due to all the negative feed about it. I really regret listening to all the bad press this game got because it is a really good racing game. I may even say its my favorite. It is true that this should definitely not be called Project Cars 3, because it isnt. Ive played PC2 and other sim racers and this game cant be categorized with those offerings, but this is definitely a great racer. Its like Forza Motorsport or Gran Turismo but even better, IMO. Ive been looking for an alternative to these games because FM nor GT can keep my attention for long and sometimes I just dont want to commit to a full fledge sim. PC3 fits this niche perfectly for me. Cant stop playing it. Sure it has its flaws, but nothing major. Overall, it is FUN, and thats what matters. Just think of this as Driveclub 2 or NFS Shift 3 and you will see what I mean. Just dont make the mistake of thinking this is a true successor to PC2. This is a fantastic racing game and doesnt deserve all the negative slack. If only SMS would release a demo so more people can try it.

_childDocuments_.review: OK after more hours I'd have to reverse the review to negative. TLDR: If you just want another racing game no matter what, buy this at a deep sale (>60%). I don't recommend buying in any other circumstance. SMS effectively committed a suicide after their three descending tries in the racing game industry. This game, ladies and gentlemen, is worse than every big name in the market. Yes, including Need For Speed. SMS tried to do something vastly different from what they were known for, into a market where nobody knows their name. This game, however, is a godawful first impression for those players who have been long used to Forza and GT series. The driving is nothing close to realistic. The graphics is exactly the same as Project CARS 1, which was released a DECADE ago. The sound design is just that, also decade old. The career progression system is atrocious - you earn a few thousand to a few tens of thousand after 2-3 dreary long races. All this plus the fact that you have to BUY the DLC cars with in-game currency, which means you have to GRIND for the car you bought with real money. Honestly I've never seen such practice in any similar game. NEVER. Races are designed badly as well - time attack mode will have the AI flooring your car into the first corner before you take control, and have that "GO" word occupying the center of the screen, which accidentally is also where you'd look at while driving, for a full second or so. Oh also it won't tell you when you drive off the track and make the current lap time invalid, that this will make you lose the race, only after you've driven 3 laps and lose the race. If you accept such a mediocore game and just are fed up with Forza alike, this might work for you for the first 3-5 hours. Otherwise, it's a bad game made with no effort, no attention to detail, no care, and no love. SMS, shame on you for ruining the racing game industry once again, and make it appear as if there's no one playing racing games. This kind of games is the exact reason why we don't get good racing games in the recent decade.

_childDocuments_.review: They've ruined the best racing game ever!If you were a fan of Forza and felt a bit of your soul die when you played Forza Horizon, then save the rest of your soul some torture and also save your money - AVOID this game!I could tell from the font on the loading screen that it had gone all Need For Speed - and not Underground 2... we're talking Most Wanted here. There's more emphasis on choosing your driver's clothes than there is on cars in the first part of the game and the introduction of points for drifts, clean overtakes etc. has made the ultimate sim into a tacky arcade racer. You remember how the cars in front of you in NFS used to pull away, until you did some "nice driving" and instantly caught up with them? Yeah, that seems to happen a lot. The racing line has been replaced with markers for brake points, apexes and exits, which you get extra points and apparently performance for if you hit.Then we get onto wheel compatibility. Erm... there is none. In PC2 I just plugged in my wheel, selected the model in the controls menu and away we went, gear stick and all. Not so in this. It took about half a dozen loads to get the wheel working, and even then I had to use paddles as my stick was selecting gear 6 in 2nd position, 3 and 4 were bumped up into 4 and 5 and there was no reverse.Talking about loading... jeeeeeeeez. I haven't waited that long for a level to load since I played my grandad's Spectrum. And the graphics are comparable. I mean, seriously, why does it take twice as long to load something that looks inferior to the previous game? There's NFS style motion blur everywhere and even when stationary the scenery and car graphics are terrible (I had everything set to max).I did a race at Knockhill in an Evo on this and then PC2 and there is just no comparison. I really believe most people on a blind test would say PC3 was the earlier game and PC2 the newer one.I can't tell you how disappointed I am with this game. At least Forza did Horizon and the regular game... but they've absolutely ruined Project Cars :(

_childDocuments_.review: Unintuitive, poorly optimized, and frustrating.When you first startup the game, it drops you right into a race with high performance cars.  You are unable to change graphical settings, VR options, and several gameplay options until you finish this race, and the first career race afterwards.  Want to exit the game before that?  Too bad, you either have to finish your first two races or use task manager to force the program closed (even then, you'll be dropped right back into the career race if you reload the game).  I normally try to be pretty understanding of the difficulties and limitations of game development, but this decision to gate the options menu (including the exit option) behind two races was just idiotic.I attempted to play the game with an Oculus Rift.  I know the graphical output of the Rift is limited, but this game seriously felt like a graphical downgrade to Project Cars 2.  Its hard to see upcoming turns in the distance.  The UI when racing is rediculous; the mini-map for the tracks is so far off to the lower left, I literally have to turn my head 60 degrees to the left to see it clearly (why can't I customize my screen layout just like in Project Cars 2?).  Speaking of the minimap, its super zoomed in, and does little to help you anticipate upcoming turns.The driving itself feels like it can't decide if it wants to be a simulation or arcade racer.  I understand that the game was designed to be somewhere in-between, but it ends up playing like an arcade racer with hints of simulated loss of traction when you least expect it.  Perhaps if I had played for longer I could have gotten a better feel for it, but I see no reason to force myself to play a game I'm not enjoying.Almost forgot to mention the car customization.  The customization options themselves are pretty nice, but as far as I can tell (in VR), there is no way to rotate or change views on the vehicle you're customizing (besides some preset angles for applying decals).  I also had trouble saving my customization choices; the game kept reverting to the default paint job when I tried to save or exit the customization screen.Its also worth noting that the game crashed to desktop three times within the first two hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I too was thoroughly disappointed by the fact Project CARS 3 was not a sim, but this is actually one of the best sim-cade / arcade racers in the vein of Forza, GRiD and Driveclub in a while! Yes, it is unpolished and a bit buggy like every SMS game, but the handling is genuinely excellent on game-pad, unlike every previous SMS game. If this game had a bit more polish and was called something else, it'd have been almost universally praised as one of the best sim-cade track-racers ever made. If, like me, you really wanted to like the NFS Shift games and just wished they were actually playable, this game will make you very happy!

_childDocuments_.review: Project Cars 3 is confusing, poorly marketed, made by developers with a piss poor track record of late, and masked by an army of angry Sim Racing Elitists. Yet somehow. Project Cars 3 stands as one of the best racing games (and I said GAME, not SIM) I have played in years. Combining elements from of some of the best racing games of the last 20 years, Pcars 3 stands as a love letter to the giants in which it stands. However, before I dive into Project Cars 3, I need to explain tell you a little story…------Prologue------My Story with SMS starts at a middle school book fair, where I bought a copy of GT Legends. A sim racing game from around 2004 made by SMS for SimBin. Since then I’ve been a sim racing fan and have driven everything from Rfactor, to IRacing, to Live for Speed. After SMS got kicked off the Need for Speed bandwagon in the late 2000’s early 2010’s, they started making Project Cars 1. A ambitious game, funded by the community that lived up to absolutely none of its expectations. It was basically a tech demo, with horrifically implemented controls (both wheel and controller), a bare bones career mode, and a tire model only Iracing could have be proud of. Driving felt like you were attempting to use telepathy to drive the car, instead of the steering wheel and petals.Project cars 2 fixed many of these issues, and on PC at least, it eventually became a pretty decent simulator. Many of the wheel control issues where fixed, the tire model was much more realistic, multiclass racing was a thing, overall things looked pretty good… Until you saw the dumpster fires that where the console versions. The Xbox one version of the game especially was basically unplayable on the OG Xbox as the tire physics would freak out with more than 6 AI cars on the track. This led to a whole host of issues, constantly overheating tires, Suicidal AI in Open wheel races, the game dropping frames like no one’s business, Xbox’s crashing and in a couple reported cases actually bricking consoles, and more. We found out after the game released, by SMS itself, that they had outsourced the console version’s testing to a 3rd party, and they failed to notice any of issues, somehow. To SMS’ credit, they attempt to fix as many of these issues as they could, but they also banned a whole bunch of people from the forums for demanding refunds. Anyway, the long and the short of it was, the Xbox one, (and indeed the Xbox one S) just couldn’t play Pcars 2 correctly. The only way they seemed to be able to make the game work, was to nerf the physics. Drive the Audi R8 LMP car or a Group C Prototype back to back with the PC and Xbox version and you will see what I’m talking about. 	So as someone who played mostly on a console until recently, you could understand how someone like me would be disenfranchised by SMS and Project Cars. 2 strikes, one handled far worse than the other I was pissed off and done with SMS. Anyway, it didn’t matter, I and many others were convinced SMS would wait until the next generation consoles launched, that way they could tap into their extra power, and not have a potential repeat of Pcars 2. Well, instead they went another direction entirely, and I’m honestly glad they did…------Review------PROJECT CARS 3, IS, NOT, A, SIMULATOR…What it is, is a game along the same vain as Project Gotham Racing or DriveClub. It’s an easy to pick up and play, “authentic feeling” driving experience. Cars still drive differently from one another; they’re all realistically effected by the weather and changing track conditions, and upgrades make a MASSIVE difference to how they drive. Front wheel drive street cars have a safe, natural push, while a lightweight, while a rear wheel drive sports car like to stick the tail out. It feels natural and believable, even more so then the likes of its stablemate, GRID 2019. In fact, I feel the comparison to Grid 2019, isn’t really warranted driving wise. In Grid the car feels like it’s on a pendulum based upon wherever the engine is, and there is no connection with the road. In Project Cars 3 it feels like the tires actually determine where your heading still, so in that way it’s closer to the likes of DriveClub. Anyway, regardless of what the game feels like behind the wheel is where Pcars 3 shines. Driving is a joy, an absolute ear to ear grin of a joy. I legit played this game for 5 hours straight, because I has having so much fun. It is insanely fun and rewarding feeling once the AI is set to a competitive level. Nothing beat wheeling a classic touring car around a rain-soaked track, blasting through a tunnel on the French Riviera in your Aston Martin, or banging fenders fighting for the lead at interlagos. No matter what you’re doing, it’s fun and engaging. The best way I can describe it, it almost feels like you’re in a racing movie or anime, with the laws of physics bending just enough to let you pull off some sick moves (or murdering you in spectacular fashion.)The Career also feels like DriveClub, but in a Project Cars meets Gran Turismo 3 sort of universe. Car collecting and upgrading is the name of the game in Career as you plow through a laundry list of events. It’s far cheaper to build a car for a higher class, but some events require a car from a certain country or a certain kind of driveline, or some other sort of theme. So, it feels very Gran Turismo-isk in that way. Multiplayer is there, and it worked well enough. It tries to Copy Iracing’s or GT Sport’s system of signing up for a race and then getting filtered into the event based upon your driver rating. I cannot comment how well that worked just yet as the game is only released to Deluxe Edition players at the time of writing. There are also custom lobbies, and Quick Race which throws you into the next open event randomly sort of like GRID 2019. I do have one or two complaints about Project Cars 3, the first is the sounds. Having watch some gameplay from youtubers and streamers, I know the sounds themselves have been made more realistic and maybe a little more flat, but I wouldn’t be able to tell you because even with my volume cranked up on my laptop and in game, I still can barely hear anything. The game is WAY TOO quiet and can be easily toned out by my window air conditioner. It’s almost like the game is set up in some sort of headphone safety mode as standard. I’ll be fiddling with it later to see if it’s an issue on my end, but for now, out of the box I’m not massively happy on the sound front. The car classes for the race cars are also a bit of an annoyance and feels like someone may have made a few miss-clicks when putting them together. For some reason, GTA (Basically GT3, GTE, and whatever else fits in that lap time bracket) has a Lamborghini streetcar in it that would be much more at home in GT Open or the Hypercar category. GTB (GT4) has a NASCAR with no headlight or taillights. GTC (TCR and entry level GT cars) had a rally car, again missing headlights and taillights. I know these cars had to fit into the game somewhere, but, if they’re going to be racing at night in the main career mode, they need to at least have headlights or taillights, even if they have to go the GRID route of attaching stupid looking light bars. Before I end, I must commend SMS and Bandai Namco for doing something. Free tracks for everyone, and more importantly, No Micro Transactions, None, Zip, Nada at launch. Hopefully, that doesn’t change in the near future.Overall, I really like Project Cars 3. It’s a breath of fresh air a console generation marked by incomplete games that feel more like tech demos at launch, greedy microtransactions, and SMS’ own track record. It’s a fun, complete racing game, that seems to know exactly what it wants to be, even if the marketing team doesn’t. It’s not a sim, but a game that makes you feel like a race car driver, and isn't that what we all want? HIGHLY RECCOMENDED  8/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you're coming to this looking for something that's closer to the realistic side like the previous games, this ain't it. If you're looking for a solid arcade racer with satisfying physics and a career mode that's pretty good for a modern racing game, this is something to consider whenever it goes on sale. The progression feels like a good middle-ground between FH5 and Forza Motorsport. You won't just be handed hundreds of cars, you have to make a little effort to get what you want, and while it's easy to upgrade them, you do have to choose wisely *what* you want to improve to get an edge on harder difficulties. Also, best of all, it's not a live service game! The only FOMO you could feasibly worry about here are the Daily, Weekly, and Monthly time trial races (Rivals) what's here is here, and will always be here. It's very nice being able to just slowly chip away at this game and not have to worry about tracks going missing and things like that. If this ever goes on sale for $30 or below, I recommend this for a chill arcade racing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my review for NFS: Shift 3. I mean PCars 3. My bad.Wow. They somehow managed to get everything wrong with this one. It's almost like they tried. I came into this game expecting 3 to be an improvement over 2, but they somehow took a giant step backwards. It seems like most of the problems are related to them working more towards making it overly accessible to console players in order to boost sales instead of trying to make a good game. I'm also pretty sure this is the same game underneath with a tweaked handling model and a handful of new cars. This is PCars 2: The Reboot. Not PCars 3.Graphics are terrible. Flat, dull car surfaces with little to no reflections/shininess despite running everything on ultra. Aliasing everywhere. Your cockpit is mostly clear but the rest of the track quickly degrades to PS2 levels of blockiness.The handling model has gone all cartoonish. You can easily recover drifts and slides in almost any car without even trying. Almost like they were more concerned with players being able to use a controller than a wheel. I have to say there is a nice feeling of weight to the cars but that's where it ends. The FFB is just numb and lifeless when it works. For me personally the FFB would not work in half the races I joined. Which was always a nice surprise.They have taken away time attack and the ability to set hot laps against the ghosts of others. This was one of my favorite things to do when killing time in PCars 2 and a large disappointment.Speaking of taking things away; there is no longer the ability to set realistic handling aids such as factory TCS/ABS. It's just an off/low/high setting now that applies to all cars globally. This is a particular PITA when you race with TCS off but get in a 1400 hp Jesko. Breathing on the throttle and spinning the tyres through 6th gear is less than awesome. So you would have to switch the setting every time you change between high and low powered cars. This would be sufferable exept that the low setting is TCS on until a certain RPM at which point the tyres break loose again. And of course high is kindergarten levels that prevent you from putting any power down.The engine sounds are muffled and muddy compared to PCars 2. This is punctuated by the horrible, ear piercing, universal tyre squeal sound.The game menus feel rushed and some things such as selecting the all cars option in practice mode have been unfathomable for some players. Not a great design choice. They feel like they were lifted from NFS: Shift. Weird flying thingy effects and all.AI can be tolerable if set to the right level of difficulty/aggression but that seems to vary from race to race. So good luck finding that.The only thing I found redeeming about this game was the Rivals feature. That was kind of fun but really is just a reskinned set of community events and was marred by the random crashes and/or lack of FFB that would result in losing one of your limited attempts.It is my opinion that they stripped everything good away from the PCars franchise and reskinned it as a weak, half-assed attempt at making an overly accessible arcade game to cater to controller users and console owners. I have refunded my purchase and might pick it up again if it goes on sale for a deep discount.Thank you Slightly Mad for killing everything I liked about PCars 2 and ruining my hopes of a better sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked PC2 you won't like this. I honestly expected this to be more arcade however the other aspects of this are just bad. Even if you just take this as an arcade racer the graphics are subpar at best- lack of settings and options, even on higher settings it just doesn't look that great. I'm just confused on how they took a really good game graphically and 3 years later made it worse? The draw in is terrible - and I usually won't complain, I get trees and backgrounds at distance but the car details and wheels will pop in even close up. Replays are especially bad. My G29 wheel works randomly, it works fine with all my other games but this game decides not to recognize it at all at times. When it does work it isn't near as immersive, maybe this is something that will be more adjustable but honestly it has no where near the feeling of PC2 or any other game.  My car randomly has a new color at times... not a big deal but just another weird bug. Physics - the cars have none of the body roll or tire response -especially when you see a replay.. I get it, Arcade Racer but you can still use physics and make it somewhat submersive, they aren't pitching this game as ridge racer and it shouldn't look like it. Career mode, I actually like the premise and like grinding for cars... however you win money per level, not really winning races? It eeks out the money and then will require you to buy other cars in the same class to complete the events. It will basically put you in a situation of re-racing events just to level up and gain a little bit more money to buy a car you don't want to race, it seems poorly thought out. I'm not saying this is a bad game overall but I'm forewarning anyone that has longterm been into Project Cars this isn't any form of that. As I said I truly was ok as buying this as a non-sim racer but I expected good graphics and some resemblance of project cars in handling and right now I'm disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so there's a bug that is very annoying and I want to talk about that first - I play this on two different PC's - and the game doesn't move between them gracefully. On a regular basis, the game will lose all my campaign progress on one machine. When it does this, I have to disable cloud sync, delete the broken save and then load up the other PC to force a "good" save to sync up to steam. Then when I re-enable cloud, it's able to sync the good save onto my other PC. Now that I've complained about that, I quite like this game - it's a lot of fun, and although it's a departure from PCars 1&2, to me, this feels like one of the classic TOCA race drivers games from Codemasters (pre GRID era), and I was a fan of those back in the day. The additional challenges are fun wee milestones, and add to the challenge of getting your driver level to where it needs to be in order to unlock the late-game race series. I think that the career progression and credits could be a lot more generous. You really do feel like you're restricted to one car per series for the first few, and progress is slow. There are plenty of upgrade options however, and if you check out the requirements for races before you get to them, you can make some smart car purchases and maximise the value. But if I'm honest, I'd prefer generosity over tactical purchasing.If you're a fan of the past titles, this one isn't for you. It's too big of a departure. If you're a fan of the old TOCA games, you'll see something in this game, but it might be too "gamified" for it to be fun for you.I've been enjoying it though.

Main issues are-Game has a ton of cars, but you can't drive half of them due to the asinine career layout and stingency with money.-AI borders on Paint licking to Ayrton Senna at times. going from impossible to catch to unable to touch you. Keep in mind I was playing on legend difficulty with aggression to the highest. I sometimes had to tone it down because it was hard to do anything to catch up.-The "difficulty" is putting 30 cars on motorcycle tracks like cadwell and telling you to pass them in 2-3 laps. they also like to pretend you are not there and just smash into you. _childDocuments_.review: A lot of the negative reviews are from people who didn't read what SMS intended to do with this game.  PC3 is an evolution of what SMS did with NFS Shift, Yes it probably should of been named differently but the fact is it was never intended to be like PC1 or 2.There are currently a few bugs:Drafting then overtake not registeringAI is super fast in the wet and snow yet in the dry once over taken the generally stay behind.AI in lower spec cars can be very slow, they are only a bit more of a challenge from Road A+Custom livery's are sometimes not used during races.Traction controls seems to bug turning on some AWD cars at slow speeds.Career progression isn't bad, it's worth looking ahead at the races and requirements as some cars can be used for multiple types before the need to switch. Some don't like that it's not pick any class like previous titles but your still free to do this in a custom race and still earn xp/credits for doing so.Some of the standard cars are also the race spec cars so if your on early progression it might be worth upgrading to get it's worth than buying racing spec version outright.Controller support actually works properly and for those with a wheel they have added PC2 wheel support to it. Cars look really nice although Super Sampling takes a massive hit in the rain when racing with a high number of cars.All in all cars are fun to drive and if they can make the AI more competitive it would make it even better.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great game, as an arcade racer not a simulation, its feels like Codemasters Grid but better. I think the graphics are ok, supports ultra wide monitors and the default setting (on my setup) were spot on.Its designed for a gamepad and it works well, I will try with a wheel a some point but I dont think its that type of game, I have played in VR, it looks great but I prefer arcade racers in a behind the car camera and thats not a camera position I like in VR so will stick to non VR for this game, although in car in VR is OK (there are better VR sims available).Some bad bits, you have to complete a series of races before you can get to graphics setting (as has been mentioned in other posts), You can get to other settings though (strange) The cars love to slide on every corner, Pit crew advice...Good bits, its feels fast, short races, tick boxes for achievements (great for the perfect score), very easy on Novice so great for everyone, its fun.My advice buy it play for 2 hours and if not what you want request a refund, its a keeper for me...

_childDocuments_.review: Highly addictive, it takes the best from every big racing sim and simcade game and adds a personal touch made of an absolutely gigantic mass of content.Career mode is fun and challenging, very well made and satisfying.Multiplayer is fantastic, I'm talking about the scheduled events of course, the races are absolutely fun but they require focus and consistency, the penalties are spot on aka corner cutters and wall slammers have no place, they go to the shadow realm real quick by getting a 10 seconds ghost slowdown(the car becomes transparent and it slows down to a crawl). The netcode is solid, never saw someone lagging or teleporting, you get kicked out only if you have micky dee's wifi tier connection. The average online drivers are pretty good, they can drive and I never encountered rammers so far.Also I never encountered career mode bugs or anything some people found, it's a really clean release.I think this game does everything right, it's both accessible and challenging as your progress, the graphics are nice if we talk about the track, the cars and the particles, great lighting, palette color, and animations, also I love the feels the dynamic weather and time change give out.Just like I said above, it's hard to put this game down and the fact the online mode is free on Steam unlike on console games, it's a big, huge thing, probably the true game changer.This will be my daily drive for years to come, absolutely wholesome game on every single level.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, this game is a huge disappointment. I loved Project Cars and Project Cars 2 and those are the games that got me into Sim Racing. I am not a big Sim Racer, I have a Logitech G920 so nothing major. I was so excited when I saw Project Cars 3 Releasing, especially when they said there would be Customization and an in-depth career mode. However, as they are there, they are not good. I only played this game a little but there is just nothing that would make me want to continue to play this game. This game doesn't seem to be designed for a wheel, I used my wheel and my Xbox One controller and I was much more comfortable with the controller. There is almost no force feedback on the wheel and it basically feels like the steering wheel is loose as you take a corner. The controller was fine and it made it more enjoyable, but that's not how I want to play a series that's been trying to be a Sim Racing series for years now.Everything in this game seems like a downgrade from the previous. They put heavy focus on the Career mode without changing it much from the Career mode on PC2. Its still roughly the same format. In PC2 you could go into a Custom match and race any car in the game without worrying about the career mode if you wanted. Now you have to unlock cars in career mode before you are able to drive them in custom games. The graphics look weird at times, they aren't terrible, but you would think that a game that has touted itself as the best looking Sim Racers out there, the graphics would at least be amazing. At times, it looks like a mobile game and there are no moments where you jaw hits the floor on how good it looks, which is not what you would expect from a game of this sort in 2020. Overall, this game feels like its confused on whether it wants to be a Sim Racer or an Arcade game. It does everything ok. There is a racing game out there that do what you want better. In my opinion there is nothing about this game that I would recommend to anyone and nothing that would make me recommend this game over superior racing game. I would recommend it on sale or when it inevitably becomes available on Humble Bundle. This game is not terrible, just disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: Wow - I know ppl suck at driving in real life but you'd think they'd be better in a video game...and not blame it for their own lack of skill.  Anyway - I'm playing in VR (Index) with a G27 racing wheel/pedal/shifter plus seat and it's very satisfying.  There are definitely some graphical bugs, menu bugs, and random crashes now n then which I expect they will be working to address.  If patience isn't one of your better virtues I'd wait a few weeks.The races that you start with feel really short so you fumble through the menus quite a bit from the get/go, but if you run super M3 solid-state like me there's no such thing as load times.  I haven't had much trouble pulling first place unchallenged with no driving assists thus far, but I'm still in D & E class vehicles.  Driving the early mustang is like trying to wrestle a badger into a zip-lock bag but when you finally get it right you feel like a boss!If you're buying for the VR it's definitely a huge graphical improvement over PC2 (the environment especially).Also, sitting above the track watching your race replays in VR is super cool...its like being at the races lol!Force feedback is authentic and enables fine vehicle control.  It too is a little buggy, but seems to clear up after the first race.  I have not tried multiplayer yet - so no comment there.Is it worth 95$ in its current state? - hell noIs it fun and challenging to play? - hell yesif you like NFS The Run "style" of arcade racing sim I'd recommend it, especially after it gets more polish!

_childDocuments_.review: Its my first Project Cars game, I bought it for arcade racing, not for simulation. I don't have gaming pad, I don't have wheel, I'm not so much into racing games (played Wreckfest, NFS Heat, and some others years ago). And finally I like (maybe not love, but I do it) going upstream, buy difficult games to play them on my own. I don't feel any prejudice towards this title.So Slightly Mad Studios did a mad game. Everywhere you'll see words "madness", "mad" etc., AI opponents will have names of SMS workers, and generally some events will have "mad" feeling about them like difficulty seemingly impossible, or changing weather for worser of course. Whatever you'll hear about this game, don't think about it, its simply the greatest yet example of this team madness. But is it a good game?So to begin, there're 10 subclasses you can complete in career mode. Each subclass has 4 subcategories with 4 events each. Each subcategory has 3 events like "preliminaries", and one championship event with at least 2 races (rounds). That gives at least 200 races in career, on more than 100 different tracks, and you can't complete all of them with one car. Some events require certain car, even 20 cars might be too little for 100% completion.Some races are difficult, and to unlock new cars and races you need to complete objectives from different events. You can grind on one track, but for career progress you need completed objectives. I'm not a pro, as I said, but I played some games, and this game is not easy. So to complete whole career even 100 hours might be too little imho, that's how massive this game is. This game isn't funny, or lacking something, its a very serious arcade racer with unseen amount of content.If you played Wreckfest, cars behave similar here like in Wreckfest on asphalt. Penalties for missing turns are rather painful, and AI opponents are serious challenge, you don't have to win races, AI will make it impossible to perfect turns, or complete other objectives.This game is worth its price. It might be one of best games I have played ever, and I didn't even try multiplayer yet, which is really big in this game. But as I said, there's madness here and there, you won't know the truth about this game until you'll play it. I think, that some people will identify with this game, but not many. Its hard to say anything about this game community, to predict anything. But I don't regret

_childDocuments_.review: PLAY PROJECT CARS 2. Project Cars 3 has lost what the PC series is supposed to be. This game deviates more from simulation to an arcade style racer, Now, it does have an engaging upgrades menu and livery choices and the like, but that's about the highlight of the entire game. I have played 90 minutes at time of review and that was enough to know the amount of effort the devs put in. Also, YOU HAVE TO PAY TO DOWNGRADE YOUR CAR TO QUALIFY IN CERTAIN RACES. PAY TO DOWNGRADE? REALLY? In seemingly every other racing game, you can swap to lower parts on the fly with no issue and at no cost. I literally got stuck in the game. Meaning, I was 10 credits short to be able to downgrade my car to just be able to race at all. I couldn't progress. I uninstalled the game and am re-installing it. I'll give it another go. There are also no additional career slots that I can tell, which is typical in many racing games, but when the flawed credit system in game doesn't work, then you have no choice but to start over. I am disappointed in this release. The devs can do better and have done better. I'm debating asking for a refund and I've never felt that way about a game to think that, let alone write a public review on Steam. Like I said, stick to Project Cars 2. You're welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I keep playing this game and never review it, I'll just get to it now.I also want to note, I did not see any advertisements nor even know this game was coming out until I saw it today.  So I came into this without any expectations other than there being cars and tracks to race them on :).The short of this is - Yes, its a arcade'y sim more along the lines of a Gran Turismo.  You get to start with a nice new or older Japanese sports car and build it up as you progress through the ranks all the way up to a race car.It reminds me of the older Gran Turismos where you eventually can upgrade your car to the racing version (for those of you from that era).  You grow a bond to the cars you have and you can simply replace the ones you don't like that much or move on to others.I am kind of the exact opposite of those here giving it a thumbs down.  I'm not looking to invest in a racing rig and was disappointed with the previous PCars because controller support was ok and driving was just a pain.  This is exactly what gives me racing enjoyment, to sit down, pick up a controller, do a few races without going nuts getting a perfect setup, and admire the cars from the inside and out.I find the races short enough out of the gate to progress somewhat quickly without getting way too serious.  The AI is decent and very customizable. It does remind me of the previous games where there are a ton of cars in a race and you're somewhat stuck just plowing through them in certain cases until the pack thins out.I like the AI better than GT Sport and Forza.  In the races I've done I haven't found any where there's that one guy at the front growing an immense lead while you struggle to get there.  Forza does this so annoyingly.  Gran Turismo doesn't usually have that problem too often but, their AI just moves right into you as if you're not there.  On Legendary difficulty and Max aggression, some may be disappointed that it doesn't make the racing impossible.  Once you pass everyone, you'll hold the lead until you screw up.  A worthy note before I forget is, there is weather in the game.  I don't know if its random or planned but a race can go from dry to wet.  Rain affects are what you would expect and a nice twist when it happens.  The race I believe lets you know ahead of time of the forecast.The game isn't exactly perfect due to a few reason.The graphics are somewhat mixed.  The car detail is very good both interior and exterior.  Driving from the cockpit gives you the option to have your head turn automatically for turns which is neat however, sometimes the camera is staring at the pillar which is useless so I turn it off.  Watching the driver steer the car is almost humorous in heavy turning.  Not that its bad in any way but, it looks like a mother frantically trying to steer her mini van from crashing down a steep hill.  Its handled very well to the point where its almost distracting.Controller sensitivity I don't believe is currently adjustable.  Its slightly over sensitive where its easy to over correct from oversteer.  So back to the graphics. . .  I have a Ryzen 3600, 16GB Ram, SSD, and aan RTX 2060 Super. . . you would think that would yield good results running the highest settings at 1440p.  Yeah uh. . . NOPE. To start off,  while the cars and lighting is very good, the environment is almost that of PS2 Need for Speed. . just in a higher resolution.  The ground off the track in some areas are just flat textures.  There is a grass setting in the graphics and I'm not even sure what it does since it looks so bad.  Some cliffs are fine while others are blocky as if they missed the fact the camera will pan over off track areas.  The side of houses are also flat.  I can only assuming this is because the game runs so poorly at high settings that there's simply no way to improve on those areas without making the game unplayable.  Here's to hoping future patches help.Then just wait until it rains. . . it your particle settings are on high (assuming this is the issue), crank those baby's down to the lowest option.  Nothing like the 50 FPS you're lucky to get in a race, dropping to like 25 FPS.  Don't even think about 4k.  Its not even that great on low settings.To mitigate this, I would recommend just leaving textures on high, car detail on high, AA on medium (unless you dont care for jaggies), and put everything else off or on low.  The game is fine after that.  I can only hope a $700 Nvidia Ampere card can run 4k at 60 on low.To make some sort of a conclusion here I you require both things to find this game worth a buy:1: If you like a casual sim racer (like GT or Forza) and don't have time or want to spend much time fiddling with your car to catch the perfect line.2: If you have a decent gaming rig  i.e. GTX 1060 for 1080p and don't mind some compromises in the actual performance you get from the game or the quality of in-game objects other than cars, this fits the bill.Otherwise I think the game is solid even at $60.  Bunch of cars and races with a cool upgrade path that makes the car you pick out have actual value.  Difficulty isn't too hard and other racers behave more or less like other people (they do hold their line much better than you but, if you hit them ;) they lose control like you would).  I just hope there are future patches that iron out the performance.  I doubt visually they will upgrade the scenery and as I said, you'd need a serious GPU to handle any more out of this game.  This seems as a safe, hold me over until Gran Turismo arrives with PS5.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one underrated Simcade title, it reminds me alot to GRiD: Autosport (which was my favorite GRiD). The car roster is huge one of the better ones I've seen, for being a 2020 title it still managed to throw in newer cars that just recently launched. Also the track selection is awesome, many classic circuits, street, sprints and fictional. I was also pleasantly surprised how good the engines sound (Was kind of used to Forza Horizon). Another plus is the huge amount of different Classes so there's always a different race style to choose from. As for customization, I like it that it's rather simple, you can do alot to your livery but visual customization you only have wheel and tire selection.I do understand why the terrible reviews from the community though, if this game was called Project Cars: Autosport then it would probably be in the 80's%. While very entertaining, it doesn't come without some issues, the AI is very wack, sometimes they're insanely quick and sometimes they're just so slow (in the same setting). Also for some reason the track loading is very slow (There's a fix in the forums). But other than that I think this game deserves a second chance which can only happen with a very deep discount which seem to be rare, I was able to find it at a reasonable price at Humble but hopefully sales come back to Steam. Get it before it's gone like PC1 & PC2, the era of simple Simcades like PC3 seem to be a thing of the past.

_childDocuments_.review: Seriously, I have no idea where all the hate for this game is coming from. I am going to review it from the perspective of your average simcade enjoyer, all sim sweatlords - move along.I am playing Project Cars 3 using controller with all assists turned off and I find the driving to be very enjoyable. It offers enough challenge not to get boring and not too much to be frustrating, with some of options for customisation.Tracks are quite varied with changing weather conditions to spice up races. There is a multitude of locations to race on, from your typical racing circuit at Monza, through green hell of Nürburgring, to the beautiful Azure Coast.Career progression is quite well thought out, as it takes more than just winning every race to progress. You need to complete specific objectives and challenges for next stages to unlock. Some events require that you use specific vehicles, which is great way to force players to move out of their comfort zone and try new stuff.You can upgrade your car to affect the way it handles and/or move it up to another class. Its pretty standard upgrade system, but you never have too much money and have to save up to buy new cars or some major upgrades.Music and sound of PC3 are a bit underwhelming. Some cars sound kinda weak and muffled, its not jarring, but could be better. Music on the other hand is terrible, I recommend you just mute it in audio options, as the music during races is so bad it negatively affects my driving.One of the most frequent complaints about PC3 is the interface. I admit its rather poor, but I disable almost entire interface for all my racing games anyway. Why would you want to use minimap or have XP progress bar anyway?Another complaint I saw a lot was graphics. Anti aliasing and motion blur are poorly implemented and both cause the game to look blurry. However, you can customize your game to improve it. Blur can be disabled in game options and to improve image sharpness you can enable image Sharpening in Nvidia Control panel, just set Sharpen to 0.60 and use ignore film grain at 0.17. After that my game looks pretty good, however its still not as good as for example GRID 2019.I am having a blast with Project Cars 3, I love the cars and tracks selection and the driving model on controller feels spot on.  If you enjoyed Forza Motorsport 7 or GRID 2019, I can wholeheartedly recommend you Project Cars 3, as its in a very similiar vein. It might not be worth full price, but definitely get it on reasonable discount.

_childDocuments_.review: The Fast and the Flawedious. Fun 8/10 old school 'simcade'  and much better than many of the reviews here would have you believe.  I was hesitant to buy this game given the mixed reviews but I've enjoyed what I've played so far, despite the occasional flaws.  VR throughout the full game is a bonus.  Recommended for those who enjoy games like Forza Horizon & Motorsport, GT  and GRID.  For those who prefer a full on simulator with VR (as I often do too) AMS2 is already available so pick that up instead.   I can understand the frustration of those who thought this game would be a successor to PCARS 1&2 - that is AMS2 - this is very much a pick up and quick play simcade game. Where does PCARS3 fit in the current simcade list for me?1. Forza Horizon 42. F1 2020 'My Team'3. Wreckfest4. Forza Motorsport 75. GT Sport6. Project CARS 37. DIRT48. GRID 20199. GravelIf you haven't played 1-3 on the list pick them up first and enjoy.  If you've already played and enjoyed those games and want something similar but with its own personality pick this up.The good:+++ Gamepad controls are intuitive, instantly pick up and play quality which is a huge improvement for PCARS.++ Cars have individual personality and the handling model is unique and fun - it isn't trying to be realistic but it is at the same time fun. ++ Full single player career mode, if you enjoy working through a career to open up cars and tracks you'll enjoy this. ++ Plenty of adjustable assists and AI settings to set the game for the level of challenge you want.  The bad:-- Variable performance and framerate in night and wet races, especially in VR.-- £15 overpriced for the style of game and content available.-- Many bugs reported though I've yet to encounter these.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute travesty Project CARS 3 is. I really wanted to like this game, but its has some of the worst design choices I ever seen in a racing game. Its like these guys completely forget everything they did on Shift.Lets start off with the positives, because this game does some aspects really well.-There is a lot of vehicles and tracks, giving this game a good variety of content.-The driving feel of the cars are great. How they bounce over the uneven road surface is very natural feeling.-Many of the vehicle sounds are excellent. -The sense is speed is done well. It could be a lot better, like closer to Shift 2, but it gets the job done.-The road surface effects the car a lot. Driving on the snow was much more slidely than in the rain.-Online multiplayer is great fun. I had a blast playing with a group of friends, and its one of the more competitive and intense racing I've done.-The game is rather polished and is not that unstable or glitchy (Looking at you, Fast & Furious Crossroads)So, what does this game screw up so badly?-The graphics and optimization are terrible. How can this game look worse than the original Project CARS, and run like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on my machine?-The menu and HUD art style is super basic and uninspired.-You can only play either race or practice in the custom event. The other game modes are in career only.-Lower tier cars are very boring to drive. Due to lackluster handling and controls, they are complete slugs to use.-The overall car handling is just too oversteery and slidely. Even putting on traction control makes the cars slide less, but can make them also understeer considerably. I can't find a way to make the handling feel 'good'.-The AI is awful. They all clump together, making hard to pass, and clogging up the tighter tracks. There is also no AI in multiplayer events.-No mechanical damage. I understand that this is more arcady than a sim like the previous games, but even games like GRID 2 and Gravel have mechanical damage. Those games are even more arcady than PC3! There is frankly no excuse to cut that.-The racing music is just very... forgettable. I appreciate there is race music, but it ends up becoming background noise real quick.-Crashing is not fun. It seems your car is glued to the ground in wrecks. See this comparison video between PC2 and PC3 to see what I mean: Now, I had to make this its own section because PC3 has the  singleplayer career I have ever played.-Money is given out only when you advance in your level, not from winning events, meaning its super hard to get cash.-It takes so long to level up. I'm only on level 2 despite 800,000+ XP like WTF.-You constantly blow money on cars you don't want to buy because of stupid event requirements. This means you have to repeat events you already did to earn money to progress.-You can buy your way into the next career tiers, which shows how much even the developers knew their career was that ♥♥♥♥.Overall, what we are left with a game that had amazing potential, that turns into a very dull, uninspired experience.My advice is just to buy GRID Legends. It may not have the same amount of content or have that great driving feel with its vehicles, but its more worth your $60 than Project CARS 3 is.

_childDocuments_.review: Changing my review from a positive to a negative. Why?I was tolerant with the game on launch, as it was fun but in need of patching. These days we just have to accept that a AA or AAA game is 'early access' on launch day. I am pretty sure that if Slightly Mad were still independent, they would have continued work on this game and made it into the game it should have been. Now that they are part of Codemasters, they have clearly been assigned to other work, and there have been just a few minor updates (some of which just repeat the same patch notes). No patches to rectify the basic and glaring problems. Now, the whole lot are under EA - so we can kiss this game goodbye. But, what really pizzes me off, is that they have the barefaced cheek to put out DLC for an unfinished game. My thoughts below still stand *for a day one release* (early access) title. It is still a fun game - but all this time later, remains a buggy, unoptimised game. To this day PC2 is superior in every way. So :Game - 4 out of 10Business practices: 0 out of 10. ___________________________________________________[Day one, original Early Access Review]Well - I had fun anyway!It's kinda funny to analyse the negative reviews here. Some are put up after under an hours play, and just as odd - some people are giving it a thumbs down after 6+ hours play - in both cases - go figure. Some people just seem to *need* to have something to complain and moan about - most of the bad reviews on Youtube seem practically jubilant. As many have pointed out (including SMS), this is not a sim. Good, if I want to play a sim - I already have many options. I bought this for one reason, and for one reason only - this is the *only* competent Arcade racer in VR - and I am having a ton of fun with it. Is it perfect? - not by a long chalk. Is it as good as PC2, ACC, etc? - as a sim racer, no. - as an arcade racer, it is better (!)Does it look rushed and unpolished? Yup (thank codemasters for that one - the EA wannabies of racing. I am guessing codemasters told them to 'get this damn game done, so we can get on with 'rationalising' you!')Does it need work and optimisation? - Yes. (what is with those white outlines around the cars? What is with the idea of cars *driving through me* rather than overtaking - in VR, with the added realism - that can get you in the gut.)Is it the best VR Arcade racer in VR? - Absolutely! (er, not competition on the grid though). Is it fun in VR? - A bucketful.[Hot tips - switch all of the assists of and ramp up the difficulty to max - or it will be like racing your granny as she heads off for her weekly shop at Tesco. Also, in VR - spend some time tweaking the settings. It is *not good* 'out of the box'.]When I first booted the game, it looked and played like something from the PS3 era  - but rather than beating my fists and posting a bad review after a few minutes - I actually spent some time teasing the settings and actually *playing* (what a novel idea). So rather than weeping all over the pretend car you made in your den (it will rust), why not take a pass on something you *knew* was going to be an arcade-sim and carry on playing the really good sims there are already out there (both in and out of VR)? I fear this may be the game that killed the franchise. Time for a street party? I don't think so. Certainly in terms of VR racing, I will not be pulling the party-popper. As the enzymes in Codmasters' gut slowly dissolve SMS - I morn their passing.

_childDocuments_.review: Off the bat, PC3 is not a "quite" a sim racer, some things are realistic, others are not.Best way to describe it would be slapping an extra 0 onto all grip values and greatly simplifying airflow and weight distribution to just impact speed / acceleration over handling and dynamics. Onward!Bad:- Career is a bit clunky / ignore that you're racing hotted up cars vs stock- If you make poor buying choices, you can cause some extra grind in career because theres money instead of just unlocks- Achievements locked behind DLC- Paid DLC still requries you to grind currency to buy the ingame things you paid RL money for.- Crashes quite a bit when using VR / google advises this is an ongoing concern since launchGood:- Is one of the better executed casual racers on PC- Does not require a racing wheel / setup to excel on. Can genuinely be played on KBM/Joystick/Controller without much handicap.- AI difficulty scales quite well, and they get harder due to better driving / better pressure than simply teleporting / rubberbanding - VR Support is fantastic- Car Customisation is satisfactory but also somewhat lacking, ie cant layer decals or use smaller objects to build truly custom.Personal Opinion:Its good for an unwind if you want something between Assetto Corsa and Need for Speed.If you do buy this start on at least the "Experienced" settings / turn off all the assists, they're straight up damaging and not required for this style of racer.Dont buy it full price, skip the DLC.Verdict: If you want a racing sim iRacing & Assetto Corsa are still king.If you want a "casual" sim racer toss up over this and Forza 4 TBH.If you want an arcade racer Split/Second and Need For Speed are over that way

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm not gonna lie, VR has some issues. There's some graphical glitches, and yeah, the frame rate in VR isn't so great, but...For all the people complaining about the game being too arcadey, VR NEEDED a more approachable racing game. There's already tons of sim racing games available for VR, but there's nothing in VR that feels like a GAME and is accessible to people who HAVEN'T already spent hours and hours and hours learning how to drive properly.Project CARS 3 is certainly not free of flaws, but it fills a hole in the VR community that has been empty for far too long. I would definitely recommend this to anyone who wants a fun and approachable racing game in VR. Sims are great for people who want a super accurate simulation experience... but for people who want a Need for Speed or a Ridge Racer, this is as close to that as you can get right now in VR. It's not as arcadey as Ridge Racer by a long shot, but it has enough assists and enough game to it that those of us who like arcade racers, like me, can still get into it and enjoy it. And most importantly, it is fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Short Version: Singleplayer is a mess, playing with friends is fine.Long Version: I wish there was a mixed rating i could give, because honestly the game is not as bad as most people say it is. As long as you have people to play it with that is, because the singleplayer portion of this game, in its current state, is pretty bad. That will be the main focus of this review as most of the following points dont apply while playing multiplayer.First there is the AI, which is extremely inconsistent. On some tracks you will lead the field with a 3 second distance to the next driver on the hardest difficulty, on some tracks you wont even reach 5th place on medium difficulty. Weather and track conditions dont seem to affect them at all, rain or snow, it doesnt matter, while you struggle through corners the AI will just blow past you. Sometimes not even that, sometimes they just straight up ram you off track, because how dare you drive in their line. And then, after you readjust and enter the track again you get a penalty for shortcutting. Yeah, the penalty system is pretty wonky too. Sometimes you very obviously cut the track and nothing happens, sometimes the left side of your rear bumper is a centimeter over the track limit and you get penalized.Theres also numerous graphical bugs and glitches like lights being way brighter than they should and damage to the car remaining after restarting a race. All of this makes for an extremely frustrating experience, especially seeing what this game could be. I wasnt really bothered by the developers choice to make a more arcade-y game, in fact, its the reason i bought it in the first place, but as it is i find it hard to enjoy. I can only hope that more work will go into it to adress these issues. If this stuff is fixed it could potentially be a great singleplayer experience

_childDocuments_.review: For the record, I absolutely adore this game. It's a sheer guilty pleasure to be blasting through the sheer myriad of cars old and new in custom events for a few minutes after a hard day at work, with a compelling driving model and plenty of tracks to mess around in.But at the same time I wouldn't ever consider recommending this to any of my friends, or random strangers on the internet. Not for the usual reasons, mind you. It is truly "sim" enough to be genuinely engaging and truth be told racing sims don't need to waste your time running qualification laps around the track before you are even allowed to race proper.But then again it's quite unclear who exactly this game was meant to appeal to. It's an indecisive, inconsistent mixed bag that struggles to please a certain audience. The absence of features like qualification laps, pit stops, tire wear, and such would indicate a more casual and streamlined racing experience, yet the core racing is still, for lack of a better way to describe it, so  it might as well had those features in right from the get-go. It demands a lot of patience to master not just the handling and feel of the driving, but also to know which of the corners that are  to be cut since the game is particularly unforgiving with mistakes, and which ones to avoid like the plague. Driving even so slightly off the track, or even close to the guardrail in some particularly picky locations, will completely invalidate an entire pace settler lap. Understandable when attempting to cheese the map, not so much for the grievous sin of mistiming a corner. Absolutely infuriating if the former, since the time milestones one is expected to beat are exceptionally brutal and you  to complete them perfectly three laps in a row. There isn't even a slowdown penalty or anything for that unlike normal races, and the reward you get for completing them with a mistake committed will be so meager that the game really should have forced a restart upon mistake anyway.Now while such a thing wouldn't exactly be out of place for a hardcore racing game like its predecessors, it's rather peculiar for this, a game meant to be more accessible overall to be so demanding yet hardly gives any margin of error. Not so much better in same-said normal races, which although don't completely invalidate your entire run (but still invalidates your time) when running off course, but it is nonetheless painful to have your car be forced to a crawl and for a few seconds become intangible for your opponents to drive right through you while you are already struggling to pick up speed. Again, understandable if you really deserve it, not so much if you were shunted to the shoulder and are punished for the crime of being at the wrong place at the wrong time.Oh, last but definitely not least, hitting the wall will deplete the XP you earned in the middle of a race somewhat inconsistently. Sometimes it is kind enough to take only an understandably small amount or none at all, but the game also likes to just drop it to zero as if all the clean driving you did to earn it didn't actually matter.Who does this game want to be for? Really can't be sure. I for one am patient enough to withstand a little everyday suffering in the career mode to enjoy it for all the breadth of content it offers in custom events and such, but those who are looking for a logical extension to the Project Cars franchise will be found wanting. Casual racers who would feel lost and out of place in the "sandbox" feel of the game would likely grow frustrated in the rapid difficulty spike in the career mode past the tutorial races. The multiplayer mode, which I have no idea how it works, is technically alive yet fundamentally dead due to the severely lacking playerbase.But, hey, maybe it's just right for you. Show those AI opponent racers who's boss by setting their driving attributes to "easy" if you really want to. You'll need it on the oval tracks.
_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, Project Cars 3 is a great VR game for me! I would never play it in flat, as well as all other racing games no longer. I didn't get to know the game at release, but only with all the patches. I wouldn't have bought the deluxe edition at full price either. But for just under 30 EUR absolutely fine. What did I like most about the game compared to other well-known racing simulations?- easily accessible due to high fault tolerance for driving errors, easy game entry without many settings and bells and whistles, good VR implementation, fast and elegantly operable UI- brings just the right mix of arcade and simulation and plays very well with an Xbox controller (steering wheel I will still try)- the standard perspective behind car plays amazingly well, but also in the cockpit you quickly learn to handle the cars- have long wished for such a relatively quick to learn racer, which is nevertheless no Horzion Chase Turbo, and still has some simulation feeling- nice arcade elements, like the track markers, the nice in HUD in VR, fun challenges like score walls, average lap time, three achievements per track- a very low keyed commentator who talks at the right time- nice simulation of different weather conditions- many customizable cars and a large number of tracks- good performance despite large driver field- works very well with Virtual Desktop- is already challenging on standard difficuiltyIf you like more arcadey racing games with some ambition, I think Project Cars 3 is a good fit. It still has the necessary depth, though, because corners have to be braked and turned in properly, and you can save seconds again and again. The bad ratings are mainly from flat players and disappointed hardcore simulation fans. PC3 would probably have had better cards with a different name. If I look at it as a VR-only game, there's no way PC3 deserves the bad scores on Steam. The immersion on the tracks is great, whether in an outside perspective behind the car or in the cockpit. The entertaining challenges fit the concept. I would say at least a 80% for the fun.I could now list a whole bunch of negative things, but I don't want to, because that has been done many times by others and for me does not detract from the fun of the game. But maybe the following idea, which also in Steam discussions someone had already noted, although I think more from the arcade direction:- an over the top story mode would fit perfectly into the game, where a racing career with over the top characters is told, embedded in all the available challenges and cups. Because as it is, it's more or less a string of events without a personality or story behind it but still fun!I know that this would scare off simulation fans even more, but PC3 is no longer a pure simulation, but a quite varied Simcade with a great VR feeling!

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing Forza 6 on my Xbox and wanted a similar game to play on PC. Was PC3 the right choice? I was disappointed that it didn't have engine conversions. To me, that was one of the fun parts about playing Forza 6. I thought PC3 would have something similar. They do have race conversions though. Basically, you pay a lot of credits to transform your road car into a GT race car or similar. The only aesthetic mods you can do is car paint, tire brand, license plate, rims, rim paint, and vinyls. I may be forgetting some options too. This game has a lot more race tracks than Forza 6. My favorite is the Azure Coast. As for the driving, it felt similar to Forza 6 so it wasn't hard to adjust to it. The side challenges are glitched. Sometimes when I complete a side challenge, I don't receive any exp. Sometimes I'll even get rewarded exp for an uncompleted challenge. I took a photo for proof but I can't even upload it on here. I don't care about those challenges. But if you're a perfectionist, good luck. Also, I think the "draft for 0.08 seconds and overtake" is bugged. I can't complete it ever. There is a driver and car level up system. You only get credits by leveling up and its not much. You are expected to grind races if you want to buy a new car with enough money. You can reduce car modification costs by leveling up your car level. Every 5 levels adds a 5% discount to that specific car's mod costs. Each race has 3 challenges depending on the type of race it is. The hot laps and average time races are the most difficult for me since they have time challenges. Just remember that the ideal race line isn't always the fastest. An annoying thing about the AI cars, they somehow manage to find grip in a turn where my car can't. I've had AI cars behind me dive bomb a sharp turn, hit the apex, and still have enough grip to stay on the inside and pass me. If I was to do that in my A90, I would be over steering to stay on the inside or under steering into a wall. Another thing, AI cars are faster than what they're rated. I did a custom match with 5 stock Z06s. Two out of the five, GAPPED me on the straight away on Laguna Seca. Not surprisingly, they both were 4 seconds faster than the rest of us on the lap timer. That's just not fair. It reminds me of NFS and their rubber banding cheat system. When I got to race in Road C, I bought the Lotus as my first Class C car. This car made driving easier. You'll know what I mean if you play the game. Eventually, I saved up enough money to buy the 2020 NSX. That car made racing easier. It was my first time on the Azure Coast and I had the NSX. My adrenaline was up that entire race. Lastly, I'll write about the car sounds. Inside the cockpit, for some cars, the sounds are muffled and quite often don't sound accurately as it does in real life. Look up the GT3 RS on Youtube to hear what I mean. It has a transmission whine in PC3 that shouldn't even be there. However, in third person view, the car sounds actually are accurate and decent. I bought this game on sale. It was definitely worth the money even though it has minor annoyances and sound imperfections.
