_childDocuments_.review: This will be a little longer but I have to write this...  As I enjoy simulation racing games, my expectations after watching all the previews/reviews for PC3 before buying were quite low. Basically the reviews can be summed up as follows: arcade handling,  watered down version of PC2 worth playing only on gamepad. Fueled by all the reviews I watched, my first impressions after starting the game were certainly not good, to the point of me being just a few clics away from a refund... The only thing which stopped my to do it was that for some reason I was really having fun... So I gave this game another chance, with a clear mind and a new aproach and that was the best thing I could do!!!  The game is basically all I want, without me even knowing. Some people will find this funny but I find the physics model among the best if not the best I ever tried in any game (And I played them all, expect Iracing...) This counts road cars only ATM, as I did not get into race cars yet... The cars really do handle like I would expect a real car to behave. What I was always missing in all the sims was the sense of real connection with the road, and missing weight transfer. And these are aspects where PC3 really shines. After I got used to the physics model I really feel like driving a real car... Go watch some episodes of ToopGear, where they are doing all the drifting and other madness when testing the cars (Lancer, Vectra etc)... I never was able to replicate that kind of behaviour in any other sim to the extent I am able to do it in PC3. The cars feel alive, connected to the road, but at the same time are willing to go into slides if you press too much. And it is so fun to catch all the slides and it feels realy natural. I have just finished a race with a Porsche 911 GT3 RS on Sugo, and it was the best gaming moment in my history of gaming. I was never so connected with a car in any game after just a few laps. I really felt like driving on rubber tires, and everything was just so natural...  My real life driving experience is only with standard cars, so I do not know how a Porsche should handle, but it behaved exactly how I always expected it to do with the engine at the back...  As you can see I am now pretty excited about PC3 :-)  I really recommend reading the developer blogs on the offical PCRAS3 site to get and idea what this game is about egarding the physics.To sum up, if you like realistic driving/racing but you do not want/have time to practice a lot and twinkle with the setups just to be competitive, this is the game for you, but you have to approach it with an unbiased mindset and you will see the glory... The graphics could be better at times, especially during the night, but I can live with that.  I am in love :-)   Playing on G27 wheel + pedals.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, this is my first Steam review but I just had to share frustrations that I have with this game, which ultimately made me uninstall it. I'm one of those people who don't mind the simcade driving model in this game. I just wanted Project Cars game that can work with a gamepad and this one delivers. Driving model is fine, especially with all assists off. But the insane on-track rules, slow progress, a ton of hot lap events that have stupendous qualifying lap times killed it for me. Until the game receives an update or two that fix these issues (luckily, most issues can be fixed with a simple patch) avoid this game like plague. I'm fine with a simcade title not having a rewind feature but then don't punish players every time their third wheel goes off track by half a milimeter. Really, did anyone playtested this game? Seriously, even sim games I've played, such as GT Sport, aren't this punishing. These on-track rules combined with F1 driver-level qualifying lap times will make you restart each event dozens of time. Then you'll try to get a better car but even if you have money for one, the best cars in each class are locked until you reach a certain level. But the leveling system is so slow you won't be able to unlock these cars until much later in the game, when you won't bother replaying old hot lap events where you weren't able to get three stars because every car inside a class that's unlocked from the get go cannot reach those lap times, even fully upgraded. Also, you simply cannot buy lots of cars because you earn money extremely slow. I mean, I know that Slightly Mad Studios tried to emulate Forza campaigns but even there you can buy a fair amount of cars with race winnings. And yes, you don't get money for winning races here, only meager amounts of XP, with the majority of experience received from reaching certain achievements (win 10 times in the same car, master certain amount of corners, etc.), which progress very slow. I would skip hot lap events without even thinking about them, but you need to earn stars from events in order to unlock championship events and advance to higher racing tiers. Which makes playing every hot lap event a maddening experience and the main reason why I uninstalled the game. And yes, I've read that at higher road car tiers and GT tiers the experience gets much better but I don't want to suffer anymore while trying to reach higher tiers. Next, some events require certain car models. Locking events behind specific car models in a game where you earn money at snail's pace is so ironic that I just can't imagine Slightly Mad Studios spent more than half an hour playtesting this game. It's sad really. This game has great NFS Shift (they would probably called it Shift 3 but EA probably holds the rights to the name) vibes and so much potential but it's ruined by simple mistakes that can be fixed so easily. But developers stay in complete silence ever since the game released, without any news about a patch. Seriously, this game can be tons of fun if they just decide to patch issues mentioned here. On the flipside, too many hot lap events in the career cannot be patched. But at least these will be much more enjoyable to play without silly on-track rules and lap times that cannot be achieved by cars that are unlocked from the start. Also, the AI is as chaotic as possible. On some tracks you'll finish first on Pro difficulty (one level behind the highest difficulty option) and on other tracks AI drivers will destroy you even on Medium difficulty. They are also extremely aggressive, even when you set aggressiveness to low. Oh, and those on-track rules and slowdown penalties don't apply to them, yay. You can get pushed off track by AI driver with you getting a slowdown  penalty and the driver who pushed will just swoosh next to you without any consequence. Also, AI drivers are fast on any surface, even on grass, which is also frustrating at times. I don't mind AI-related issues much because races can be great fun most of the time, despite aforementioned issues. But I cannot play the game while it has so many small, patchable issues that make it an infuriating experience.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR : If you have VR and a decent machine, love racing games that sit somewhere in the middle between arcade and sim, this could be some of the most fun racing you can get. I won’t do PROS and CONS because that’s so subjective, but I’ve split it up into chunks for easy reading.LIFESTYLE CONTEXT I'm 40s, two kids, busy job etc. Never seem to find enough time to PLAY games, let alone review them but I felt compelled to write this in the face of all the negativity, in case it helps someone in a similar position who is on the fence about buying it.RACING GAME CONTEXTBeen playing racing games since Revs on a BBC B back in the 80s - and they’ve always been a staple genre for me ever since. I have always leaned toward the less perfectionist titles - MotorStorm, Gran Turismo, Forza (Horizon, not Motorsport), Wreckfest etc. So not quite Ridge Racer and Need For Speed but certainly not Assetto, rFactor etc. The latest F1 game for example was too strict for my tastes. You get the picture - Lewis Hamilton, I am not. I own both previous pCars and use with my first gen Rift.GAMEPLAYThere's been a lot of negativity around this for the reasons we all know so I won’t repeat. But for someone like me, with the previously mentioned time constraints, I'd say pCars3’s balance of sim and fun is spot on. No it's not a sim - you can get out of slides with some careful steering, you can run wide on corners and stay in contention etc. But it’s also not an arcade - you do need to drive well, take racing lines and obviously can ramp up or down the assists to your taste. For me, I want close, exciting racing. Racing that doesn't require me to qualify for everything, that doesn't necessarily need me to know the track inside out to stand any chance of being competitive, and racing that if i make a few mistakes, doesn't mean reaching for the restart. And that's what pCars3 delivers, in VR! Cars jammed in around you, bumping and fighting for places, the grip slipping just enough to require concentration, but not necessarily enough to leave you driving around solo with the pack half a lap ahead of you.WHEELI'm using an old Gran Turismo Logitech wheel and pedals and in pCars2, I assumed the crazy jumping and juddering was just to add excitement. Playing pCars3 I realise it was just not working properly! The cars now feel far more controllable and calm - I whacked up all the force feedback to really 'feel' the car and I think it works great. You still feel it slipping and sliding underneath you, it just feels more manageable now than before. UII know people have complained about the UI and in game menus etc but personally I think it all works well PLUS there's now photos of the tracks! TRACK GUIDE MARKERSOne thing I've not seen a lot of people discuss is the new guide system - brake at the first marker, aim for the second, accelerate through the third. I was dubious at first - felt like a change for change's sake - but actually, it works really well. With no indication of what speed you should be doing when you hit the markers, it's entirely possible to fly through the first one with no hope of pulling back to hit the second. They tell you the curve you should take but it's up to you how you achieve that. VR POSITIONINGThere’s less VR positioning options now - seat up/down, forwards/backwards etc aren't there, but binding ‘re-centre’ to Enter on the keypad is easily mashable while wearing a headset.OVERALLIf you’re after exciting, intense VR racing, without the desire to perfect every corner, change every tyre and qualify for every grid position, I would definitely recommend this. Would I have bought this game if I DIDN'T have VR? No, probably not. As mentioned, I'm more of a Horizon than a Motorsport, so endless, clean, track races on a flat screen just isn't my thing any more. But in VR, this is some of the best racing I've ever played, going all the way back to Revs in the 80s! Intense, exciting driving that sacrifices punishing perfection for a focus on the pure fun of racing.Hope this is helpful to someone, have fun racing!

_childDocuments_.review: This should have never been allowed to be released using the Project CARS franchise name. What people seem to forget is that “CARS” stands for Community. Assisted. Racing. Simulator.- They didn’t work with the community to make this game.- This definitely is NOT a Racing Simulator. PCARS3 is an arcade game and sadly it’s not even a very good one at that.Before I continue, I want to be clear and let you know that I personally enjoy racing titles in all forms, from simulators like Assetto Corsa Competizione and rFactor 2 to Arcade titles like Wreckfest, Redout, Forza Horizon 4, Need for Speed Underground, and Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed -they all provide deeply enjoyable, fun, and rewarding experiences. Unfortunately, I didn't find Project CARS 3 fun or rewarding. The AI doesn’t follow a racing line, they will ram into you every chance they get (with the force of an armored van), and they will intentionally slow down on the last lap in order to let you win. All of this would be fine if I was 12 years old and this was my very first racing game on a tablet. Unfortunately for them, this is not a tablet game, I am not 12 years old, and the adrenaline rush that comes with healthy competition has been completely removed from this game (you will often finish 15-20 seconds ahead of the AI).  What’s bothersome to most people here is that back in June, Ian Bell stated “Project CARS 3 is a game changer, all of the sim you could want with all of the fun you could want. Handling is massively improved”. Esports Manager Joseph Barron then said, "We've also taken huge strides to make the game more accessible than ever before, without compromising the core racing and the driving experience that millions of gamers have come to expect from our franchise." However, none of that is true, it was all a lie. The handling physics are laughable, and even though this title took longer to produce than PCARS2, it uses 90% of same art assets but for some reason everything else is worse:  The graphics are a downgrade over Project CARS 2.The AI is worse than Project CARS 2.The physics are worse than Project CARS 2.The car engine sounds are worse than Project CARS 2.The game somehow performs worse than Project CARS 2.The VR experience is buggy -it wasn't in Project CARS 2.It has less tracks than Project CARS 2.Now, if you have never played the previous Project CARS title, I truly cannot fault you for having nothing to compare it to but there is no apologizing for the following issues:The UI is heavily tablet inspired.All sorts of arcade track markers litter the interface.Pressing C to hide the interface still shows the arcade-like track markersPaying to unlock tuning slots feels like something that was intended for the mobile release.The AI doesn't have to shift like you do so if you drive manual, you will lose on every straight.The AI uses a different traction model in the rain than you do.The AI doesn't use a racing line and bumping/smashing into cars is required.The AI has unlimited grip on certain corners of certain tracks.The AI will use it's brakes on the last lap to let you pass. Winning feels unrewarding.To progress, you have to slow down enough so that you can pass the AI a second time.If you restart the race, the AI seems like it slows down to give you an ever greater lead.The track limits are completely arbitrary and will sometimes penalize you and sometimes won'tEven though SMS had 3 years to produce this title, it honestly feels like it was rushed to release without any proper internal QA testing. To help paint why this is, the following timeline paints an ugly picture for SMS and it's one of many reasons why PCARS3 comes off as a desperate cashgrab since it has been purchased by Codemasters. It’s clear that they stretched themselves way too thin by trying to develop three racing games and a game console at the same time.2018: Ian Bell took resources from the development of Project CARS 3 to try and create a next-gen game console dubbed the "Mad Box".  May 2018: SMS announced that they had started work on Project CARS GO alongside partners at Gamevil. A mobile focused racing game.  January 2019: Ian Bell officially announced the Max Box with an estimated release date of 2022 with the promise of 4K gaming and 120FPS VR support.  April 2019: Ian and his console development team withdrew their trademark filing after two major investors pulled out of the project completely.  May 2019: they released a trailer for Project Cars GO to a largely negative reception.    November 2019: Codemasters purchased Slightly Mad Studios for a palty sum of just $30 Million (by comparison EA purchased Respawn for $400 million)  December 2019: Slightly Mad Studios announced that a Fast & Furious game would be released in May 2020  May 2020: they announced that Fast & Furious Crossroads was delayed to AugustAugust 2020: Slightly Mad Studios releases Fast & Furious Crossroads for $59.99 to 30% review scores.August 2020: Slightly Mad Studios releases Project CARS 3.Project CARS 2 is still $59.99.Even as an arcade title, it's missing the element of fun so I cannot recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: I played in VR so that's the frame of reference Quest 2 by Air Link, about 100-300mbps bitrate:If you can get this as part of a bundle or for 20 AUD or less, it's worth it as a relatively casual racing game. It takes a bit of stuffing around to make it look nice, but my advice is use Steam's VR menu or OVR if you've got it and punch up the supersampling as much as you can without blowing up your PC. This makes the game's forced lack of anti-aliasing far less noticable, and much nicer to look at. In terms of gameplay, it's not sim gameplay as any review will tell you. This is some weird unholy child of a crackhead from an alternate dimension, and maybe a kart racer from the 90s. I found it relatively easy to get used to and subsequently enjoy, but it's anything but realistic. There's an alright variety of tracks. As an Australian I'm always happy to see Bathurst featured. It's got an upgrade system for cars, and if you drive a Toyota it will NEED a supercharger, because otherwise they can't keep up with a gosh darned thing. The more you upgrade a car, the higher the "tier" of races it's allowed to do, but that also locks it out of lower tiers. So don't go trying to make your favourite ride as smexy as possible early on, or you won't be able to actually race it, since the career makes you unlock higher tier races by doing lower tier ones, which I've found pretty fun. Wheel support is absolutely stuffed for this if you use up to date Logitech software. You need to be using the Ghub build from March 2021 or earlier, otherwise it'll either crash the game or not register inputs in it. Same story for a bunch of other games too (DIRT 2.0, Assetto Corsa and Competizione). When the wheel works, it works excellently. Gear shifting doesn't though if you have a Logitech shifter. The game only tracks like 4 of the 6 gears, and not in an intuitive "oh so pretend I have a Five-Speed" way so much as a "who needs a second gear?" one. And like most games, you can't use the shifter to go into reverse for some reason. Thanks Logitech.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing after PC2.  I guess based on the trailers and critic reviews I shouldn't have wasted my money, but I did and now it's too late to return.  This game is an enigma.  I don't really know who it's for.  It's definitely no longer a racing sim, all the complexity and depth of tire wear, pit stops and ultra realistic handling has gone away and been replaced with something "accessible", verging on arcade.  It drives more like a Grid or Forza game than PC2 or a real sim.  The AI is pretty broken, sometimes it just rolls over and you win by a mile, other times it seems to cheat, not playing by the same physics as the player making winning feel impossible (a similar complaint I had about PC2 on wet tracks).  It looks okay, even nice in some places, but almost like a mobile game in others.  Customization is basically pointless, especially visually short of changing color and rims.  It's more a successor to Shift than PC, and still does it worse than both.  The career is uninspiring.  Race. Buy new car. Race.  Races are short and mostly not that fun because of crappy AI.  Spend your money on another game that has a target audience in mind, whatever audience you may be in, and does it well; this game isn't it.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can't recommend this game because of the high pricing. I got it through Humble Bundle and I have to say if you like racing games and like a bit of simulation mixed with arcade (simcade) then I say it's worth it (at <20$). I got the base game which has a lot (a lot) of content, so much cars and tracks (and I own/play all the hardcore sim games, probably only AC has this many tracks, and that's with mods). But for example you only have access to your garage (owned) cars unless you're in a custom event and press "x" to show all cars. This is a bit hidden, I think all cars should be available and you should press the key to show only garage cars, this way people think you have to unlock all cars and that's not true. So content wise you're great. Gameplay wise, this is a bit of a mix between sim and arcade so it has some weird quirks like if you hit the walls or some undesired parts of tracks (for example not the banks in daytona), your car slows down a bunch and you fall behind. AI has a behaviour that always follows close and kind of waits for you when you fall behind. Sometimes can be a bit strange but overall I'd say it's fitting with the game. TLDR; Pros:-This is not a bad game, it's a Simcade so it's a mix between simulation and arcade. -Lots of content-Gameplay is not bad for the niche genreCons:-It's priced too high. -Some menus aren't intuitive.-Niche genre, those who like hardcore arcade won't like this, those who just like sim games won't like this. I fall a bit into this latter category but since I paid very few for this game I learned it can be fun for killing some time and just relaxing, not having your heart beat fast because you're constantly trying to make consistent laps behind your wheel sim racing. Ps. I haven't tried story/career mode, I haven't played this with the steering wheel. I might update this review later nonetheless I still think this is a negative cause of the pricing

_childDocuments_.review: I am not really picky about what is a sim, a simcade, or arcade. I just love the feel of driving and maneuvering a vehicle. I have Project 1 and Project 2 already, along with AC, ACC, AM2, Rfactor 2, GTR2 SimBin, RaceRoom (all cars unlocked), Midtown Madness, Forza (all versions) etc., all sorts of sim/simcades. After running Project Cars 3 for straight 4 hours, I do enjoy Project Cars 3. I read the reviews about people complaining about the car physics. Let me say this, sim/simcades will never never capture the true car physics. So whatever car physics people in the internet say about how accurate AC, ACC or any other, these are sim/simcade video car physics..video game physics. The tracks on P3 are excellent, though it is missing Le mans and Spa, overall, good set of tracks.  I will recommend using a wheel/pedal/shifter setup and then turning off all assists, yes turn off all assists; also turn off automatic gearbox, drive using cockpit or helmet view.  I tried playing it on a controller and I couldn't control the car. For those struggling to gain credits and experience. The best way to grind is to do Custom Events and not use the very first starter car you gain (Road E) for Custom Events. Yes, do not use the very first car you bought at the start of the game when you do Custom Events.  P3 has all the cars unlocked for you already. The only catch is that you can't upgrade them until you purchase them BUT you can use them to do Custom Events. Now, go to your "Owned Vehicles", pick a Supra and then select Daytona Oval. Select Legendary AI, with aggression set to Very High. Turn off all your assists, set number of laps to 20, total AI set to 20.  You'll be gaining credits and experience in huge amounts. Remember, do not use the very first car you bought at the start of the game for Custom Events. Use a Owned vehicle, specifically the Toyota Supra Road E class, for grinding during Custom Events. Just keep driving this Supra to get XP and credits in Custom Events. And DO NOT upgrade this Supra. If you try any other Owned Vehicle, you will get "smashed" by the AI on the Daytona Oval. Highly recommended game.

_childDocuments_.review: The amount of hate this game received delayed my purchase. Opted to pick this up on sale & see for myself. Based on my experience, this is a great arcade racer for car racing fanatics & casual gamers alike!1. Telemetry data is available & works flawless with "Sim Dashboard".  I have custom dashboards that light up on my tablet displaying speed, gear shifts and other telemetry data in real-time. Very cool feature! 2. PC3 works fine with both the XBOX 360 controller & my old Logitech Momo Force wheel. Although I don't recall feeling any vibration force feedback thus far. Could be compatibility or I may require the original drivers. However, I can steer, use my throttle & brake without a problem. The only other issue that I recall is not being able to map the buttons on my wheel but for a wheel that is over 15 years old I don't care. I feel resistance on the wheel just no vibration.  3. All tracks & vehicles are unlocked by default within the "Custom Events" mode! No need to grind it out if you're just a casual gamer whom wants to race around the tracks.4. It supports VR & works great with my HP Reverb G2 (V1) WMR headset.5. There are plenty of game modes & play styles to choose from. You won't be stuck grinding it out in career mode if you don't want to! You can play other event options, gain credit & use it to unlock classes or vehicles.6. You can adjust the difficulty level before each race to increase XP earnings & or to challenge yourself against the ai. 7. There is alot of content available for this game. I can't imagine getting bored with it any time soon. The various game modes allow you to avoid repetitive tasks & just enjoy racing.  8. I have no performance issues on my ALIENWARE AURORA R9 I7 3.0 Ghz 32 GB RAM system with an NVIDIA RTX 2070 & the game installed to an external NVMe drive.When in VR, I have the game in window mode & graphics settings switched from the default  "Trilinear" to "Arthroscopic 16x",  all other settings set to Ultra or High with the exception of shadows which I set to Low or Medium. Didn't notice any lag or game breaking bugs ect .. I've already unlocked the first 3 classes E, D & C which grants me access to plenty of career races & challenges to keep me busy when I find the time to play. The only negative experience I can speak to is not being able to get a race going in multiplayer mode under the "Quick Race" option. There doesn't seem to be many players online but with all the content the game offers I think it's still worth buying especially if you have a wheel and a VR headset.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not, what I have come to identify as, a conventional motorsports sim.I'd call Project CARS 3 a Driving Sim, because unlike its two more conventional "brothers", Project CARS 3 doesn't simulate the regulatory structure around any motorsports discipline.What Project CARS 3 does brilliantly, and the reason for why I still call it a "Sim" (more specifically, a Driving Sim), is it simulates the forces acting on the cars very accurately, and it still provides that intangible feeling of actually feeling the car around you.You can easily feel the pedigree of Project CARS 3 in the driving feel, and if that's what you fell in love with in the two prior games like me, then I can absolutely 100% recommend it.See you out there.

_childDocuments_.review: What is this nonsense?I'd put off til now, not wanting to part with any significant cash, due to the feedback I had seen, but thought "nah, it can't be that bad"...Oh, it really is - PC1 and PC2 are just completely different games to this!In all honesty, the use of the PC brand is just an embarrassment, and for all those saying "it's change, it's not so bad" bla bla bla...Consider - Project CARS (Community Assisted Racing Simulation)The clue is in the name, it's meant to be built upon community feedback, the desires of the people who have supported it thus far.PC3 is a stain on this franchise - I mean, example, how can a game released "recently" have worse graphics than a game release a number of years back?The menu structure and overall UI is like something you would expect to see in the NFS franchise - except in those it's always been that way - arcade.Summary - This game has been utterly ruined, and it's really sad to see, as PC2 had so much further potential!

_childDocuments_.review: Since Pcars3 is an arcade game, I will mainly compare it with recent arcade & sim-arcade games. A little introduction of myself in case of trolling comments. I am a sim-racer who mainly focus on iRacing and ACC, the most recent result of 6hrs iLms VLN Nordschleife (iRacing) is the 4th place GTE class, in the top split. So if you want you play with your meme and comment down below, I don't really care, this is a review for ppl who have intention to purchase this game and hope this review helps.Pros: Grip & FFB: I am using the TS-XW Racer Sparco P310, the game recognized the wheel after I started the game, so I didn’t tweak any FFB settings. Compare Pcars3 with Pcars2, the feeling of grip and FFB is quite similar, even though Pcars3 is an arcade game. In Pcars3, I can easily oversteer the car and catch it, it's quite an enjoyment while putting the car on edge. Compares to Grid(2019), where cars slide a lot in low speed corners, Pcars3 actually has a pretty decent grip through low speed corners.Kerbs/Curbs: The detail of the kerbs is good. Compare Pcars3 with F1 2020, Pcars3 has a wide variety of kerbs, and more importantly, they are not flat and simplified like the ones in F1 2020. For example, the kerbs on Barcelona-Catalunya Circuit, the sausage kerbs and the white-triangle like kerbs at the run-off area in the last corner, are nicely presented in Pcars3. What's more, in Pcars3 the kerbs are not that slippery compares to Pcars2.Track Elevation & Corner Precision: I know, the tracks in Pcars3 are not laser-scanned, but the presentation of the track elevation, corner camber, and the corner angle is pretty accurate. For example, Bathurst (Mount Panorama), Compare it with ACC and iRacing, the braking zone, the time to lift, and the degrees to turn is quite accurate consider Pcars3 is an arcade game. (Even the track mod in AC didn't make the elevation in Bathurst right...)AI: Well, Compare to Grid (2019) ... Yes, in Pcars3 you can squeeze the opponents off the track where in Grid the cars are more like fixed to the track. Opponent do give you space when side by side if you set the aggression below medium. More importantly, the AI doesn't slow down a lot when they are in congestion, even in circuits like Bathurst & Monaco. In addition, the AI actually will spin off the track.Cons: Career Mode Mission: The quests in career mode is a disaster, starting from the back of the grid but finish in 1st in 2 laps? Draft from an opponent for 5s then overtake where the opponents are pulling away from you on straight? The quests are insanely hard, and some quests feels buggy, they does not register your completion of the quests correctly. Sometimes you have to reduce the difficulties to complete the quest. The quest system definitely needs some refinement.(Here are the bug quests I have encountered so far: Road E Majors – Eifel Weather – Master 7 corners. The ideal line indicated by the game in Nurburgring GP is not quite right, but still, I enabled the ideal line indicators, follow the instructions, still couldn’t finish the quest, it stuck at 85%, seems like the game could not register my line and movement after it rains.Japanese Roots – Dark Desert – Draft opponent for 00:05 seconds then overtake, I did it several times, could not finish the quest) AI: The AI difficulty in this game is super inconsistent among these tracks, which makes it super hard to complete the quests. They are incredible fast on straight, even though I have upgraded my car mainly on acceleration and top speed, sometimes AI can carry incredible speed through a high speed corner, an example would be the 130R in Suzuka (the track called Sakkito in Pcars). If you set the aggression above medium, the AI will basically get close to you on straight with incredible amount of speed, then torpedo from inner line. What if you cover your inner line to defend you say? Nope, the AI will cut the corner and squeeze you out.Penalty: The AI doesn't get any penalty by cutting the corner, but you do. Even you are the one getting squeezed and cut the corner, or you cut the corner accidentally for safety reason, you will be penalized and slow down, it feels quite frustrating if you want to have a fair race.Graphic: Not quite sure about the Graphic, seems like it is not as good as the graphic in Pcars2, it is definitely not something that I expected since Pcars is supposed to be absolutely dominating in graphics.Customization: Not like Forza Horizon 4, you can only customize rim, livery, license plate and tyre manufacturers. There is no visual change after you upgrade the aero, unless you upgrade the car in to its race conversion.Missing Components: no pitstop and damage system, since it is an arcade...Temperature? maybe, but I did see the tyre temperature indicators in Corvette C8, so I am not quite sure if they kept temperature system in Pcars3. There is no Le Mans, which is an track in Pcars2. Feel like there is a lot of decent details in Pcars2 that can be kept in Pcars3, but they threw them away.In conclusion: Is the game worth to buy? For sim-racers, not quite. For ppl who are bored of FH4 and looking for some fun, and you have surplus money XD, yes. Otherwise I would say wait for the discount. Hope this review helps.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is pretty decent, but otherwise the game consistently manages to piss me off.The car selection immediately tipped me off that this was developed in the UK. Unless you buy DLC, the selection is pretty scarce, especially for american cars.Speaking of DLC, this game reminded me why I rarely buy AAA games anymore. The car showroom and event selection screens constantly remind you about the DLC you didn't buy. Funny how these games get big discounts or pop up in humble bundles...While racing, the game has little markers around each corner to help guide you through the right entry, apex, and exit points. You get extra points if you hit each marker... sometimes. It's very inconsistent. I've drifted 2 car lengths from the exit marker and still got those points. I've also run right through each marker perfectly and got nothing (some events require a certain number of "mastered" corners, which makes that extra irritating.)The most annoying part is the money and progression system. So far I haven't actually found a way to consistently earn cash in the game, you can only earn money by finishing/winning a race for the first time. Afterwards you earn nothing. This makes cash a very finite resource, and many events require specific types of cars, some even require ONE SPECIFIC CAR! This left me carefully rationing money and trying to predict which type of car would be most useful to me in upcoming events, rather than picking a car that I actually want. Not a great feature in a game with such a small selection of cars to begin with.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a full blown sim with tire wear, pits, etc, but the physics engine is great.  I'm seeing comparable lap times at Sonoma and Laguna Seca to my real world times (though the game clearly does not 100% accurately model those two tracks).   Overall, excellent game for practicing your lines; I find this games method of showing braking, apex, and track out points more interesting than a colored racing line as it feels more like you're being coached through the track in the real world. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Great simcade game if you ignore the name. Dont bother if you want everything from the startProject Cars 3 is an anomaly within the racing genre at the moment because it doesn't fit the usual arcade scene nor is it a full on simulator. Instead it harkens back to a bygone era akin to Project Gotham and Enthusia where games had somewhat sim like handling and proper racing while being accessible to the masses due to easier handling and less heavy aspects like pit stop strategy and keeping an eye on the tyres. The game really does focus on wanting you to drive clean and well. An aspect i personally find great is the inclusion of a progression system that takes its time to make you earn cars. Unlike every modern racing game now which hands you most of the best content from the get go. Instead you have to slowly build up your cash to buy and upgrade cars. Stay away if you cant commit to a game or generally complain about having to put any effort in to get anywhere. The car and track list is phenomenal with a more honed in, varied car list and a track list that puts most games to shame. There is everything from EV, Hypercars, Sports and a large mix of category racing cars such as NASCAR, Indycar, Formula E and even Trophy Trucks. Also the majority of these cars have upgrades and racing conversions that allow you to bring even the slowest car up to some of the highest echelons of performance matching top tier cars like the Koenigsegg Jesko, Rimac Concept 2 and more. As for tracks they vary from well known circuits to hand constructed road circuits with everything inbetween. The main downside this game suffers from is horrendous menu design. It is easily the worst aspect with its mobile like structure and clear oversights like making you have to manually back out of doing the same race again and making you jump from the career area to the main menu just to open the full dealership to see all cars available to you.Overall its a very competent game that blends simlike handling to a more accessible arcade setting to make for an older generation style game where mass amounts of content being handed to you was a cardinal sin. If you have the time to invest in progression and enjoy some more serious driving while still being casual enough to sit back and not worry about every little aspect of racing, you will find a lot of enjoyment within this game even if it still bares its simulator namesake.

_childDocuments_.review: Really disappointed in this game. Project cars 1 and 2 was designed to be simcades with the majority of the focus beeeing on simulation. They were really enjoyable. Project cars 3 turned out to be a generic racing game that had more in common with Driveclub/Need for speed shift series/Forza motorsport in order to reach out to a wider audience. It is sad to see the developers aim more towards moneymaking than making the already rather large community satisfied.ProsArcade - Almost everyone can pick this game and learn it in a couple hours.Wide array of cars, all from ordinary road cars to hypercars and GT-carsWide array of tracks and different combinationsDynamic day and weatherUpgrades - Mostly noncosmetic, but they have recovered the 'Works conversion' from the Need for speed Shift series (SMS developed that game) which upgrades your car to a GT-kind of monsterConsGraphics/style - Looks more like an mobile game with its dull graphics and bright colours, a downgrade from previous installmentsHandling - Dumbed down to make it easierCareer mode - Everyone has a different opinion but this career mode is like Forza or NFS Shift. You start in a road car and grind your way up with moneyRaces - Usually you don't even have to finish on podium, you have certain goals instead such as pass x number of cars during race or slipstream for x seconds. This is what gives you money and unlockes more racesDamage and tyre wear - There is none, you can't even access the pits to change your tires when it is rainingPenalties/Rules - For a game that has lost the majority of its realism it is stubborn enough to have the almost the same rules as before when you cut the track by one inch. It slows you down to about 50 km/h (30 mph). Feels rather misplaced in an silly arcade game as this has becomeSound - Downgrade from previous titlesA.I - As of now, the A.I sees the other racecars more like bumpercars, they don't have the same handling model as you and is sometimes unaffected by water. I.e, I was behind a racer in the rain when he ran through a puddle, I was easy on the gas and still spun out, altough he didn't. Since the devs even have claimed that a car in front of you will push the water away I call ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on thisNot interesting - It is not on the same level of detailed racing as the more advanced simcades nor is it as easy to love as Gran turismo or Forza motorsport. It falls in between those categories. I have played both GT and Forza for many hours without getting bored, in this game 3 hours was more than enoughVerdict Not neccessarily a bad game, its easy to pick up and will be familiar to the most of the players. It is not as realistic as Project cars 2 or Need for speed shift. This should have been a spun off or a succesor to Driveclub. The biggest flaw is its name since the game is so far from the previous 2Even if you are an arcade racer you should wait on at least 50 percent discount, there are better games for the amount of money this game cost. 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: READ THIS. HONEST REVIEW FROM AN ENTHUSIAST. First off, I suggest lowering your wheels degrees of rotation, I like 540 in PC3. Otherwise use a controller, PC3 is incredibly controller friendly. Now to the review...    Honestly, I'm a bit torn. On one hand I actually enjoy driving the cars in PC3 something about it is relaxing and simple to understand. I currently have 34 hours into the game and intend to put many more in but if I'm being honest, there are some serious downfalls... Let me explain.    The tracks and cars are enjoyable at a relaxing level. You will Not find yourself giving 100% of your attention like in ACC. You will however enjoy lap after lap kicking the rear end out a bit or sliding with all 4 through an apex and smashing a sector record. There is something that's purely enjoyable about driving in PC3 and that can't be denied, it's fun.But it's not serious.....Here's where we take a DARK TURN. That's it. It's JUST fun to drive, for fun. There is zero competitive potential in PC3 both online and single player. The online presence is dead and single player bots are potentially the worst in the industry. They are incredibly sketchy, one moment they are going significantly slower than expected to the point of a track hazzard, the other they are absolutely flying by you mid apex with seemingly unreal grip levels. It's impossible to feel rewarded in this game. You either pass literally everyone in a single corner or your stuck behind completely daft bots that go unreasonably fast in some sections and stupid slow in others catching you in the middle.    Beyond the bots, the career mode is on rails and doesn't offer any sort of customization. You're stuck with short lap sessions and pretty much blow through content even if you try to 3 star ace each objective, You essentially buy a car and immediately upgrade it to it's series maximum potential, race it for maybe 9-12 races, 1-3 sessions each and move on to the next car. If you want to rush, you can jump from your first car to a hyper car within  a night. GT86 FTW, probably the best starter car than can take you through every road class race into GT class.    All in all the game is fun to play but ultimately falls short in replayability beyond "i just want to drive and chill". The graphics are worse than PC2, the anti-aliasing is horrible with jagged lines everywhere. I bought it on sale I think 23 bucks or something like that so I'm content with that purchase. I do not suggest buying for $50 this is a cash steal. They copied PC2 and somehow made it worse and are asking more. PC3 doesn't even have spa, an amazing track which is in PC2 but not PC3? Yeah enough said at this point if anyone's still reading god bless you. You're diligent and deserve more than the industry has to offer you.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game and it's DLC on a discount knowing that I was buying a circuit based simcade. For what I paid and based on my expectations going in I say it was worth it. I wouldn't say the game is worth it full price or if you did want a serious simulation. I'm well aware this game is nothing like PC 1 or 2. While there are plenty of good arguments to why this game should have been called literally anything else to save on confusion and dissatisfaction; it does seem unfair to not try and review this game based on it's own merits. No it's not a sim by any means and even compared to horizon or grid this feels more arcadey. While it is possible for the back to slide out or to even spin the car this usually only happens on wet surfaces. Even RWD cars tend to instead understeer more than anything else. Even with all assists turned off. This tends to make the driving quite easy as you are never really in danger of the car getting away from you.If you can adjust to the somewhat stiff handling though the game is still good fun and the AI is decently challenging without the same issue some games have where the entire grid is on your rear but one AI vehicle is 7 seconds ahead of everyone else. AI drivers still use lead bricks instead of actual cars and are near impossible to displace from their racing line but the game does a decent job of making them appear to be bound to the same limitations as your own vehicle rather than having infinite grip at all times and conditions.In terms of cars and tracks there is a solid enough offering. It probably won't have your dad's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ but this isn't trying to boast a huge collection in that way. Instead the options are more race oriented and while there are a lot of road legal sports and supercars there is as many if not more professional race vehicles too as that is where the game's focus naturally lies.In terms of tracks there is also a nice selection of famous and fictional tracks with a good amount of variety. In both tracks and cars there are a few questionable omissions but overall it's good. Sound wise it's above average, every car sounds unique so that is leagues better than horizon where everything sounds the same. Visually however it is below par, the cars and tracks look decent enough however visual effects like tire smoke are jarringly bad. In terms of the bad, I personally have not encountered many bugs nor do I use VR mode however there are plenty who have had poor results here. The progression system however is a mess. Completing events does not give you any money, instead your earnings come from when you level up and the amount scales with your current level. This leads to a situation where the game feels very grindy early on and the best way to comfortably progress is to spend some time playing a 99 lap race on the shortest track possible just to farm level ups instead of just completing the campaign normally one event at a time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is frankly one of the most miserable racing games that I've ever played. On paper, it was meant to be a sequel to the NFS Shift games. In practice, it's a mix of questionable design choices and poor execution that result in a game that pleases nobody.- The AI is overly aggressive regardless of settings.- The load times before races are unreasonably long (two minutes in a SSD).- The economy feels like they balanced it around a premium currency that doesn't exist, so you're grinding forever to afford anything. You don't earn money by winning races, only when leveling up.- Career mode forces you to buy specific cars, so if you can't afford them because of the above issue you better get back to grinding.- Road car classes are unbalanced and the performance upgrade increases have no real rhyme or reason.- Pace Setter events require way too much precision for an arcade racer, since letting one tire go an inch out of the track voids your entire run and some events are over 8 minutes long, and your overall time is based on your average time, not your best lap. They are also pretty much mandatory in career mode and their goal times are fixed regardless of difficulty.Just about the only positive thing I can think of is that it has a few cars that haven't appeared anywhere else to date, but given that everything about the game is so poorly done (besides the arcade handling), you can live without them and without this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit surprised at how quickly my opinion of this game took a 180° turn. After my first couple of races, I was ready to stomp into the reviews and write some huge diatribe about what kind of internal drama at Slightly Mad Studios would cause such a bizarre and half-baked product to be released - even as a casual player.After doing a few more races though, getting a feel for the driving, getting a feel for the career mode, checking out the multiplayer, and dialing in the graphics settings, my attitude is much different. It's actually not a bad game at all. Dare I say the game is even... good?Let me be entirely clear: If you are a hardcore fan of racing sims, and you must have as much realism as possible, then PCARS 3 unfortunately isn't for you. I do think it's odd that SMS has decided to go the more arcade-y route with this 3rd entry in the series, but, oh well. This argument has already been beaten to death on online forums. I don't have anything new to add. (Fun fact: 10 years ago, when Project CARS was a crowdfunded venture, CARS literally stood for "Community Assisted Racing Simulator". That acronym really doesn't fit anymore, because it's no longer a simulator, and it's certainly not community-assisted.)On the other hand, if you're like me, and you're a fan of "simcade" style racing games - in other words, games that still have a pretense of realism, while also being toned down just enough to have mainstream accessibility and playability with a gamepad - then you're in luck, because I think Project Cars 3 nails this quadrant extremely well. It's basically a more fleshed-out version of GRID 2019.Another way I would describe it, is that this game feels like what a modern day "Need for Speed" game would be, if EA ditched the open-world nonsense and went back to making traditional circuit racers. (Need for Speed Shift, anyone?)The game plays great on a standard gamepad. No question about it. As cagey as SMS has been with some of the other features of the game, making a racer that is "the most gamepad-friendly experience ever" happened to be one of their more explicit marketing points, and they absolutely delivered on it. The driving feels meaty and fun even on an Xbox controller, and there's still a fully-modeled cockpit view so you can sit right in the driver's seat for maximum immersion.The career mode has a slow, but well-paced and deliberate sense of progression. Unlike Forza, where boatloads of cash are constantly being thrown at you, this game forces you to be a bit more economical and think about where you're spending your money. You start out by racing Class E road cars, and you can buy mechanical upgrades that give you a slight edge in races. Leveling up actually takes a little while to do, and once you unlock more advanced championships, you can either buy a nicer vehicle or simply upgrade the old junker that you started out with. Your choice. From what I can tell so far, the vehicle upgrades seem to have a real tangible benefit, and you can feel the boosts to speed + handling that they give you.One similarity to Forza that I  like: All vehicles belong on a performance spectrum, which makes it very easy for you to know how much you can upgrade your car before it becomes a different class entirely. For example: "Road E" cars are all in the 200-299 performance range. You can upgrade and tweak your car as much as you want, but as long as it stays below 300, you can still participate in Road E events (or events with the same pir range).The multiplayer mode is linked directly with your singleplayer profile, and all of your XP levels, cars, and money are shared between both modes. When joining an online game, you can choose "Quick Match" to join something as fast as possible; but there's also a custom server browser (thank god). When creating your own lobby, you can choose track, time of day, time progression, weather, and number of laps, among several other options. You can allow other players in the lobby to only pick cars of the same class, OR the same performance range, OR simply have everyone be the same identical model of car. Up to you.A couple of other multiplayer features I really like, but haven't really tested yet: There's a "Scheduled Event" section of the multiplayer mode, which I assume lets you schedule races for some point in the future, so people can have advanced notification of them and sign up if they want. I think this is a brilliant feature for a racing game, and more games should have it. Additionally, there's a "safety rating" aspect to your profile - not unlike the old GRID games - and I believe you can filter out people with low safety ratings so you don't have to deal with bad drivers.As for the game's graphics... this is a bit of a strange thing. On maximum settings, with downsampling enabled, I'd say the game looks decent. But it doesn't exactly look great. It looks like a late-gen PS3 title or maybe an early-gen PS4 title at best. This is especially odd when you consider that PCARS 1 and 2 were such visually stunning games, and yet PCARS 3 feels like a step backwards in comparison. What happened here? All of the same time-of-day and weather effects are still here as before, except it all looks slightly downgraded. This is a point where maybe I  have to call back into question exactly what is going on at SMS. Did they have a smaller number of artists working on the game?  Budget cuts? Strict deadlines from the publisher? I don't know. Fortunately it doesn't effect my enjoyment of the game too much.Here is a general list of  that I have with the game. Keep in mind that there is supposedly a huge Day-1 patch inbound, and I have only been playing the pre-release version of the game, so these could be fixed very quickly:Overall, this is an excellent racing game. There's enough of a sense of progression just to "hook" you into playing more, and the multiplayer component has a feeling of robustness that is sadly lacking in other games. As for whether it's worth full price? This depends on who you are, but if you like games like this, then you probably won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm generally getting bored pretty quickly with racing simulations. I like when the handling is realistic, but the weekend format with all the practice and qualification sessions is way too long and repetitive for me.Project Cars 3 has found that nice balance of realism and arcade racing, which in my opinion makes it very fun to play. It's a completely different game from its predecessors though, and I think naming it as a sequel was a mistake. It's really more like a spin-off than anything else.The game has tons of content, cars, tracks, customization items... it's easy at the beginning, but gets tougher as you try to get all the objectives in order to advance the career. I didn't like how certain events are reserved only for specific car countries/models/years. Although it means that you can explore this content later when you have enough money to buy the required cars.The graphics are pretty good, but nothing impressive. The sounds and music are excellent. The game plays perfectly with an Xbox One controller. Despite being more arcady, the car handling still feels realistic enough.If you ever liked playing games like Need For Speed, Grid, Forza, then you'll probably like this one. If you're looking a simulation like Project Cars 2 or Assetto Corsa, then it's not this kind of game at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I like it a lot, its a solid racing game BUT, this is NOT the Project Cars we have com to know. This is more of a hybrid of simcade and legit sim racer.Playing on a wheel feels just as fluid and precise as the first 2 games, but this feels more like forza since you have the old 2 laps to win setup, starting at the middle of the pack, having to fight like made to get to first.I'm a wheel novice but its teaching me faster than PC1 or PC2 because I have to be perfect every time instead of easing into a race. This was not what I expected but I do like it nonetheless, just don't go into this expecting a hardcore sim racer, cuz its not. its more forgiving, its beginner friendly, its tough, and it gives me a good workout.This feels more like what Shift 2: Unleashed would have been if EA wasn't involved, a fluid simcade racing sim hybrid that is done very well. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I have played a lot of racing games in my life and i think it's a damn fine game. Everything you read is true, it's more arcade, the visuals are worse (especially in VR). I personally never liked it's predecessors much as the physics felt bad compared to asseto games or dirt 2. The game is more like Forza Horizon 4 physics in Forza motorsport setting. Where this game shines is in the balance of things. There aren't too many well made games for a casual pop VR on your head, sit down in your fatboy with an xbox controller type of games out there and this is one of the few that nails it. You probably won't find the best steering wheel and pedals sim here but you will get a game that is enjoyable in VR and is great with a controller which puts it on the same level as Dirt 2.0 for me.

_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; If you like NFS Shift 1+2, you can buy this. It feels like a mixed bag because it probably is. Don't expect a simulation, but expect a game.Pros:- It plays like an actual game- VR Support (no notable problems for me)- Upgrade mechanics (including racing conversion mechanics from NFS Shift)- Tracks contain more sceneryCons: - Driving model from PC2 is no longer present- UI isn't great- 'Simplified' time/weather options- No practice or qualification roundsBought the deluxe version in a sale and I like it. It plays a bit like a mixed bag, but I believe that's due to the fact that it's called PC3. It looks like they took NFS Shift and pasted that into the Madness Engine. The driving model of PC2 was way tighter than this, but I believe this is also due to the fact that it's not an actual Project Cars game. However, this does feel like an actual game compared to previous versions.So with the right expectations you can really enjoy yourself. Having no notable problems in VR, it plays very well. They must've patched the problems out probably.
_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: It's completely different from PC1 & PC2 because they went for a more casual racing experience, so yea it's no longer a racing sim.That's probably why the game received lot of backlash as fans felt betrayed.IMO they should have branded it with a different name because it's not really Project Cars anymore.I'm playing with all assists off (except abs on at times) and it's still more arcade than sim.To give you an idea I'd say the game is something like 65% arcade and 35% sim (with all assist turned off).Still i really enjoy the game so far, the controls and physics feels like a mix between NFS Shift and Forza, so not bad at all.Project CARS 3 is already a lot more fun and playable on controller for me compared to PC 2 which was almost unplayable with a controller.The physics are better compared to PC2, same for the controls, more fun to play and faster than the previous game, at least for me.The graphics are pretty nice too, it runs really well on my pc with almost everything on ultra.Content wise there's tons of cars and many great tracks to drive on.Only thing i really dislike is how the upgrades system works during the career mode...Honestly it's a pain to manage and it's really annoying having to pay to upgrade or downgrade each times for the cars.Once bought you do not keep the parts forever, if the car is too powerful for some events, then you have to downgrade and pay again that's a joke and a terrible game design decision right there.All in all it's not perfect but i think it's a pretty decent and very enjoyable racing game if you know what your buying.I'd recommend it on sale though, probably not worth paying full price (i bought deluxe edition for 19,99€ fyi well worth it.)Trust me I've been playing racing games for 30+ years by now and this game is far from as bad as some people want you to believe.
_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun to play, however at it's current state would not recommend buying due to many glitches and graphical bugs. Certain parts of career mode can't be progressed because of either glitches or impossible objectives set (ex: master 10 corners on a track that only has 9 corners). AI is also pretty bad. Playing on Legendary difficulty it can range from being rather forgiving to just plain cheating, taking corners at impossible speeds. They also have no awareness of where you are on the track so most starts you end up playing bumper cars with them. Also on races with heavy weather the frame rate drops dramatically. Overall it feels like an unfinished game.
_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: Actually not the best simulator you can get here, but still, this game is fine. Reminds me of the old Gran Turismo 4, mixed with some of Need for Speed: Shift mechanics. Yeah, kind of sad there's no tyre wear and pitstop like Gran Turismo 4 but still, pretty fun for a casual like me. Played with a gamepad, and having blast with it.Car lists were pretty huge, ranging from road cars, hyper cars and race car. We also got a nice selection of tracks, from real circuits to fictional city tracks. You can buy cars, customize them, upgrade them, and even convert it to a race spec car. But, you don't need to play the whole career mode just to buy cars, you can always go to custom event and play using any cars you want on any tracks.Even though the game is casual enough for a noob like me to win races with all assists off, the game is still challenging in some ways. There is events like Pace Setters and Hot Laps for example. Rains can change the pace of the race and puddles can spin your car out if you're not careful.But this game has flaws, and I mean it. The graphic isn't that good for a game released in 2020, while optimization is kind of questionable (FPS went from 100 to 30 if there's suddenly raining, and night race can drop your FPS too). I mean, really? I got a pretty decent rigs, this game should run better on any conditions. I also don't know if this happen to others but for me, the sound's volume is is awfully low I barely hear anything.So, if you're looking for a casual racing game that is not a street-racing themed, buy this game on sale (). Otherwise, leave it. You want a better simulator game? Go get Project Cars 2 or Assetto Corsa instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Literally just change the name and this gets a Very Positive rating ez.Should it have been called Project Cars? No, absolutely not. At the very least it should've been titled like a spinoff.Is this actually a full on arcade racer? Also, no. You can't just fly at every corner going 150 mph, tap a single button to get into a drift, and be completely fine. There's definitely some pure sim people who overreacted on what "arcade" racing is.This is the most simcade of simcade games. It's Driveclub but it feels better with a great selection of cars and an absolute huge selection of tracks to choose from.They somehow did the whole "car level" system better 3 years before Forza Motorsport did it (by just making the levels give you discounts for upgrades, with all upgrades just Being Allowed at the start).It's a great game for the Steam Deck as well as it's a game where it doesn't feel like you are losing out on the experience by not using a wheel.Is it worth the whole $60? Unless you are just absolutely looking for a Forza sized game (hell this one atleast has the Nordschleife at this current time) thats more simcade than sim than sure maybe. _childDocuments_.review: It's not the sim racer the other games were, if you want a sim racing experience head for another title,this is not the right oneAs a standalone title however, I recommend this game, it's simcade-ish leaning more towards arcade, the car list imo is great although notable exclusions are:Honda s2000, Honda CIvic Type R 2018 or newer, Mazda Miata, Mazda rx8, Toyota gr yaris (unsure how licensing for that stands), Toyota gr86 (unsure how licensing for that stands) and the GR Supra heritage edition (again unsure how licensing for that stands)The ai can kick the bucket in terms of competence sometimes but overall it's better than the ai in forza horizon 4, they take faulty lines,not identical lines with different speed depending on difficultyMax difficulty bots are not that difficult,but difficulty varies depending on weather more so than anything elseUpgrades and the performance rating system are fairly brokenMoney is earned in a very weird way, per level up rather than per race completedI have not yet had experience with online so I have no opinions on thatI like the single player so the game is a justified buy to me

_childDocuments_.review: (08/2020) First review after 5h in the game.This is not about the removed features (tyre wear, fuel consumption, pit stops). I'm fine with that for the new direction the game has taken.I'm also a big Driveclub fan and had high hopes for something like Driveclub on PC as the game director was also the same.Unfortunately PC3 is a huge step back from PC2 in form of performance and graphics. E.g. there is no setting for AA so it flickers a lot on fences. Also PC3 has a very noticeable pop in of trees, track objects and shadows while the trees a way more blurry in comparison to PC2 or AMS 2.The career is at the beginning only 2 lap races (later there are 3 laps) where you have to win and this is only possible if you bump aggressively through the AI. This is also visible if you go online all people are bombing through the field. TBH this is not really racing it's more bumper car. The concept of gaining money in the career is very grindy (besides the bugs on console where you get 1 Mio trying out cars) so if you don't buy the correct car (e.g. you need a Mustang and a AWD car) you are stuck and have to grind the credits.VR: VR suffers most of the bad performance even with all on low and a 2080Ti it's not possible to hold 90 fps. With some AI or other weather than sunshine the  fps drops down to 45 (reprojection). If we look at PC2 or AMS 2 we can see that the engine has a good performance in VR but not in PC3 here all is worse.Also there are a lot of bugs and it depends if SMS will have a long term investment in this game or only a rushed cash grab.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game because I actually find it fun and I like the customization that is available for the cars. I also am a fan of the fact that your starting car can be taken all the way up into the GT classes for racing eventually and the car selection is pretty nice as well. I also like the fact that you can change rims and the brand of tires that your car is using.  So in short I do actually genuinely like the game.However I do have some issues with the game that I will also highlight here. Number one being that there seems to be some sound issues when watching replays or when the game shows the winners of the race. I have heard that this can be fixed through messing with the sound options or the quality of sound at which your output device is outputting the sound at but it's such a small issue for me that I haven't actually bothered with trying any of that yet. Another issue is how the AI cars tend to go much faster than the players car on some tracks even when you start to speed up at the same time as the AI and they also seem to grip better when racing in rainy conditions than players do.On the game play side of things you should not buy this game if you are going to be expecting it to be a simulation type of experience... at least not in a serious simulation aspect. This game is essentially need for speed shift 3 but under the project cars branding which no offence to slightly mad or Codemasters or whoever made that decision but it was a poor one. This should have started a new IP not continue a simulation one with a game that tips heavily toward arcade racing. That being said as long as you don't look at it like its one of the other project cars titles it is a very enjoyable racing game.The Rivals mode is a nice little addition to the game and so are the scheduled multiplayer events. However if the player counts tanked shortly after the release of the game and I think this is due to my above stated point about how I think this game would have been better off going with a new name. I have heard of glitches and bugs that I have yet to experience and as I haven't had issues with them I won't be speaking on those unless they pop up for me. In which case I will update this review. Again if your looking for something like the shift series of games then this game is one you should pick up.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game not expecting a sim racer at all, but something closer to a Forza game as many before me have said.  That is not why I am giving this p.o.s. the sod off thumb, no this game commits the greatest sin of all that can be committed by a game; it's not fun.  God forbid you use a logitech wheel with up to date software, then the game wont even give you the pleasure of booting up so that it can disappoint you, it just straight up crashes to the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ desktop.  If that didn't prompt you to get a refund already  then once you do get in game it begins to treat you like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idiot as if you never played a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ racing game before, thankfully you can skip this annoying sermons unlike some games that are even more simple than this(literally any Burnout game, or game made by Criterion for that matter).  With that all done, now you can race and have fun right?  WRONG! _childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: I'm actually going to say non recommended but this review is actually fairly positive, but probably not why you think.Taking out the sim roots, it's really an OK game. The driving model is actually largely fine. I think most people would probably like it if they're into simcade racers like Grid or Shift / Shift 2. But even then the progression leaves a lot to be desired, there's quite a bit that feels hamfisted or unfinished even so.The car list is good, the graphics are serviceable, but even then there's still bugs and issues, and the racing itself has problems where difficulty can just be all over the place.If you ever wanted Shift 3, this fits the bill. You'll probably like it in fact. That's why I got it, I like Shift 2: Unleashed, it's theatrical and fun, not realistic in the slightest, and totally ridiculous, and that, actually is why I like Shift 2 it's just OTT. And honestly, if I'm totally honest, Shift 2's still a better GAME. Obviously with mod support. Which I suspect this will get if it ever gets some sort of cult following, which will probably alleviate a lot of its shortcomings.The game is actually fairly fine on it's own, but it's billed incorrectly as any kind of Sim. It just isn't. But, if you buy it thinking it's Shift 3? It's honestly pretty much right there, and a totally fair buy on that premise.But SMS is never going to admit this is SimCade, they just won't. It's a fleeting romp with bombastic, flashy driving style that's nothing like real life. If you like that sort of thing, and I do admit its a dirty pleasure on occasion for me, go for it. If you wanted a good Sim, visit the grave of the recently deceased Project Cars franchise, have a weep, and buy Automobilista 2 or ACC. If you own them, you've managed to come out of this 60 bucks richer.I don't like the idea this game was marketed wrong, nor do I like the idea it's basically ripped the spine out of what was a promising Sim game if SMS could have just actually worked on the dang thing properly. I expect SMS to handle subsequent Grids, likely having a Sim Grid and a normal Grid like they've done with DiRT, and PC as a franchise to die here and basically get folded into the existing CM franchises. But, who knows. Whatever happens, go into this with the facts. Failrace, and Jimmy Broadbent have done great insightful looks into the game, and provide their opinions, and I watched both before concluding I wanted Shift 3 and I've been just fine with it. With appropriately tempered expectations, the game's fine.But marketing has other ideas. So I like it, but for your own sake, scroll up on this page, read the entire store blurb about the game, and immediately delete it from memory, and watch someone actually play it. _childDocuments_.review: sim·u·la·tion/ˌsimyəˈlāSH(ə)n/nounthe production of a computer model of something. (In this context, to model racing accuratley)Okay, So lets start off obvious here. It is by NO means a "sim" racer. Neither was Need for Speed Shift. As a person who loves a good sim racer, This is great. It's not the next assetto corsa (nor will it ever be) But if you're looking for a Need for Speed:Shift alternative and not resort to "legally questionable" methods, then this is it. It was not going to be a hardcore sim game, They said it would be a succsessor to SHIFT and they did that well. SHIFT was a simcade (go back and play SHIFT, SHIFT2, or (i can't belive i'm saying this) Ferarri Legends) It's not an arcade racer. I can feel the differences between a Evo and a Evo Race Car. The graphics (especially on steam deck, for it's size) is stunning. The game is small, and it can get infuriating, but the gameplay is fun, and that's what racing is about, right? Fun. This game is Fun. Therefore, it simulates racing well, Therefore it's a simulation racer. In the end who cares about how good your tyre model is, or how accurate your ai is. Who gives .492 seconds of a damn about how many celeberties you have on screen at once? Racing is meant to be fun, and i think that's overlooked nowadays. If i'm not feeling dopamine, it's not a simulation. It sounds stupid, but DRIVING is practically designed to be game-ified in concept. You're strapped to an alloy tub moving at speeds faster than God intended. That's why Pcars 3 is good. It captures the feeling of being strapped in a alloy tub moving at 382 Kp/h. People just need to know what "Racing" means. People need to understand fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a die-hard sim fan, but I like my racing games to be more than the mindless arcade pedal-to-the-metal type. So PC3 is right up my alley, as it offers a solid middleground between the two categories.It's biggest forte for me is the controls. I'm playing with an Xbox controller, and I must say this is hands down the best racing experience I've had so far. You can probably still run much better track times using a wheel, but playing with a controller makes the game feel fun, and ultimately that's what a game should do.On the visual side, the cars look great, but the tracks have varying quality. Some of them are well made, with nice lighting and modeling, but there are also quite a few sub-par ones that look kinda prev-gen.Audio is well made I think, the cars have nice unique sounds, and the music is fitting.Career mode has ample stuff to keep you playing for a long time, but difficulty feels all over the place. Racing events are fine, since you can easily tweak the AI difficulty. But there is no difficulty slider for timed events, and I'm really struggling with those. (And after some forum search it seems I'm not alone with this.) The biggest source of my frustration are the pace setter events, where you not only have to set a very low average lap time (out of 3), but if you go just a little bit off-track in any of the laps, the whole attempt gets invalidated. I've seen in the past patch notes that the devs keep adjusting event goals, so hopefully this will be ironed out with time.Overall I'm having a great time with the game, so I can wholeheartedly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember playing games for fun? When games use to play different from one another? I've read a LOT of reviews here how this game is bad, how it's not a sim, how it's not like previous Project: Cars games... First off, game's NOT bad. Maybe a little difficult, AI is definitely more aggressive than say Forza or Gran Turismo, but challenge doesn't make a game bad. If I do have any gripe it's that hitting a wall will drastically slow you down BUT the AI driver can simply drive THROUGH your car and take your spot... Then 3-4 others do the same. Give me the whiplash! My car should still be an obstacle for the other cars! BUT every game has it's down points and that's my personal own that I noticed."Not a sim." Anyone wanting to do this is real life should stop playing games and actually save money, build their car, take it to the track. This is a video game and meant for fun if you like racing VIDEO GAMES. Even saw some complaints when looking if I could put in custom music (like a mixtape) and hearing, "I wanna just hear the engines! No music!" That's their thing, let others have theirs' for crying out loud. Go get sunburned watching Nascar if music is really a complaint.Now no, this game doesn't have the same physics that feel believable like Gran Turismo 7 but it's close, somewhere between Forza Motrosport (4 was the last I played) and GT. The VR seems pretty good and I'm playing on a Oculus Quest 2... But I wouldn't say this is an ARCADE game either, that labeling/genre just makes me think of Cruis'n World or Ridge Racer."Not like previous Project Cars" If you're hung up on PC1 or PC2, play those! Let that be your jam. I never played Project Cars before. Got this one bc I looked into 2 and I gotta say; I'm confused as to what incentive I have. I read this from Google -  "Project CARS 2 has a different approach – there is no purchasing of cars. Instead, you can either use cars applicable to your current races or use any car in free play." So sounding more sandbox-like? IDK. But I always enjoyed winning races and earning enough in other racing games to BUY cars. It keeps me wanting to come back to play again.All in all; I enjoy the game. Maybe it's challenging and maybe a little expensive (prices will drop or get your coupon codes ready) but for a PC VR racing game, beautiful graphics, I'm gonna play more of it. No, it's not GT or Forza but if I really wanted to play those (if PS5 or Xbox 360 available), I could simply just play those. At least watch YT videos or something before you judge it, we all got different tastes.

The graphics are a step backwards from the previous game and the physics are terrible - you can't even turn on your windshield wipers when the horrendous rain effects come in and halve your framerate.It doesn't have tire wear, pitstops, mechanical wear, qualifying, practice laps, DRS, tracks like SPA Francorchamps and COTA, visual representation of vehicle upgrades and a lot more...
