_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as a gift from giveaway that was hosted on Reddit. I was very greatful and excited about this game, because I used to play Project Cars 2 on Xbox One a lot and I figured this would be an improvement over an already excellent game. What I got was anything but what I expected. This is not Project Cars. The gameplay is severly lacking, the controls are terrible and the visuals are downright awful. It's like as if Project Cars had an illegitimate child with one of those free-to-play racing games that you can get for mobile phones. Gameplaywise the game is like as if it had a midlife crisis during development and couldn't decide if it wanted to be a car racing simulator or an arcade game. It tries to be both at the same time and ends up being awful in both of them. The cars have weight as if it was a racing sim, but you can't go around a corner without going into a drift every single time. The car models and the environment look like something out of 2006. The textures are very smooth, they lack any detail that would make the game seem real. This is most noticable on the car brakelights which look like stickers stuck on the frame. I've seen more detailed cars in Asphalt 8 (a game which was released for android I might add), which is downright embarassing for a supposedly "AAA game" that still cost 60 Euros 2 years after it's release. I got into this game blindly, not reading anything about it, or looking up gameplay videos, expecting the same if not better quality than what I was give by Project Cars 2. Even though I didn't pay a single dime for it, I still can't help but feel bad for those who gave their hard earned cash for is sorry excuse of a racing sim. It achieved one thing though because now I'll actively look up deals on ♥♥♥ for a Project Cars 2 key, because it's no longer available anywhere else for purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Original: The game play seems OK for the moment. That's about it though, performance wise, for the graphical quality of a lot of other games do better for less. How this manages to look less clear than Forza 7 yet run at less frame rate, I don't know. I mainly purchased this because of the VR support, it's currently worse than GT Sport VR for frame rate and just a bit better graphical quality. Haptic / force feedback using a controller is below GT Sport, there's just no feel to it, even at 100% setting, you just don't feel connected to the car. It's like a weak, delayed afterthought, Forza 7 has far better controller feedback. Track loading time is ridiculous, I have 2x NVME in Raid 0 at over 6 Gbps read and this takes longer to load a track than to get in game in RDR2 from the menu, every other game I have doesn't do this, even though they aren't optimised for fast storage they still load faster than anything in this game.I really wanted this to be good, I wanted something better than Forza 7 on PC, this isn't it so far, this doesn't even come close to wreckfest for car feel and feedback (wreckfest is fantastic). I'll give it more time but it seems very poorly optimised compared to anything else and you just don't get the feel of the cars. It's not the Gran Turismo replacement I was looking for, it's not more realistic handling so you need more skill, I've driven cars in this game on standard road tyres and they feel nothing like the cars in game.I hope to change this to a more positive review, however at the moment I'd pick Forza 7 and that's from a Gran Turismo fan.EDIT: Changed to positive after a few more hours. Main gripes are:1) Controller feedback: completely under-utilising xbox one controller trigger feedback, this is where FM7 wins hands down over this and GT Sport. Please make more use of this, it's a game changer. Even normal feedback needs a boost, tried a DS4 with DS4Win with 200% feedback and it was better than using an xbox one controller. Trigger feedback, please use it.2) General car feeling: Still feels mostly disconnected, you learn what you can do through trail and error rather than feeling the cars limits, again, probably more due to number 1.3) Performance: 5700XT; I'm getting over 120 FPS near constantly, but yet it get more for pretty much the same looks in FM7, which runs higher framerate and without my PC turning in to a room heater (even on the menu). 4) Loading times: 3700X + 16GB Ram and 6+GB/s read speed NVME SSD and this still takes longer to load a level than GT Sport, what is going on?I have yet to try VR again, this is possibly the worst performing and looking game I have played in VR, except for GT Sport (a massive VR disappointment). Maybe a few more hours in and some controller mods will improve it again. At least I would recommend it now.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore all the negative reviews. Not because the game is bad but because it isn't what they thought the game to be. Die hard I have teh pedals and steering wheel & am an extreme sim player and I am crying because this game isn't hardcore realistic like the first two games.The game is fun to play and progress through. You get a nice not super grindy progression system paired with a parts/car upgrade system, a car customization system & many difficulty options to alter to make the game fit your skill.The progression system has passive goals it keeps track of like doing x amount of perfect corners will grant you XP & cash. And it also has active goals for each event/race like clean pass 5 cars within 2 minutes, that need to be done during that race and will get you XP & Cash as well but also a medal which is used to unlock other events after you've collected enough of them. The Medals are not really grindy however since you only need around half of them in a series to race all the events for that series (like GT Class E series, or SuperCar Series etc). If you want to skip around you can even bypass the medal system by paying some of your money to buy into that series.The car part upgrades center has a bunch of options like brakes, transmission, turbos, tires etc and each option has several options like sports, semi racing, racing etc. You have to pay for the car parts to upgrade and every part will add or remove a cars points. These point values determine what class a car can race in. So if you go to the showroom and buy a new right from the factory Toyota you'll likely only be allowed to Race it in E or C class events until you upgrade it some. The higher level parts will also allow a player to enter the garage and put in fine tuned settings that relate to that part if you want to.The car customization system lets you change the way your car looks. You can change the color of course and also the rims, tires, license plate, car #/name. Choosing from gloss, matte, metallic, color change and a combination of those like matte metallic. You can also make the car look all fancy and racer like by applying paint patterns and decals. If you want a racer look on the car but don't want to go through all the trouble you can save a style you made and apply it to any car you own or you can use one of the default designs you'll see the AI racing around with and of course you can just leave it painted a solid color like it comes from the factory if you wanted to.The game has several difficulty options to choose from so you can find one that fits you best. You can change the scale of the AI racing skill independent of their aggression, once you get the AI set how you like them you can than change the settings for yourself by turning on (and select low/high etc) or turn off various car system aids like brake or steering help, traction control etc. You can get a bonus applied to your earnings and rewards that will scale up with increasing difficulty settings.

_childDocuments_.review: After 84 hours of game time, with a Thrustmaster T-300 wheel: the whole racing community roasted this game, I won't brave enough to buy this. Then with -70% sale I give it a try. It's a mixed bag.It's arcade'ish and not a simulator, but it is much better than Forza Motorsport 7.The time of day / weather progression, is one of the strong points of the madness engine.Sounds improved, and still looks great.Force feedback is not too strong, but ok.But....The AI in this game is terrible!The AI driven oppenents have nothing to do with physics, they are in a totaly different universum, not the same as you. Inconsistent as hell, but not just from race to race... NO! Even in the same race, once you easely pass them, and after you gain 2-3 sec lead, they can explode from nowhere to your back, or even pass you, like they have a BOOST function or 100 more magic horsepower.Because of that, I give up. The AI is clearly designed for adrenalin pump, and wheel to wheel racing, but not realistic at all. You think you will win the race, becouse you have 5 sec lead time, and at the last lap the AI is magicaly in front of you...Or vica-versa: you are 3d, and they slow down noticable, and wait for you.So, for arcade fun it's not bad, but for real racing, and driving, is not recomended.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to first acknowledge that the hate is real for this game and I get it. I have PC2 and this game is vastly different. I get the disappointment of hardcore sim racers who looked forward to another hardcore sim racer and didn't get it. Reminds me of how much I loved Battlefront I and II on XBox 360 because it allowed me to have massive battles in single player and then getting Battlefront I on PS4 and seeing it geared solely to multiplayer. With that said, PC3 is the racer I've been waiting for. As I said, I have PC2 and like it but as a casual racing game fan, I found PC2 to be hard to love. While it was beautiful, It was virtually impossible to just turn on and dive right in. I also play in VR which made it even harder to jump right in. Luckily I had a thrustmaster wheel but I don't always want to play that was but didn't really have too much of an option. That kind of sucked because I loved playing Drive Club VR on PSVR and had been looking for an equivalent since Sony stopped supporting it. Since I only play single player, it's still playable but I wanted to see what a powerful PC experience would bring graphically. PC2 was kind of a tease to me because it looked visually great but was not my go to game on a Saturday even after I got decent at it.PC3 plays a lot like Drive Club which of course I love. Here are the pros:-Great variety of cars-Great variety of tracks (More open road tracks than I remember in PC2 but it still could use a few more)-Customization features from drivers to car parts to colors (a la Need for Speed)-VR handles Ultra well with 2080 super, i7 combination-Racing assists practically drive the car for you but can be eliminated for a more sim experience-AI fights back in races-Reviews didn't like the boxing and blocking that AI did but I like the challenge (lost a few races because of it but it forced me to outsmart the AI)-I love the indicators, after one or two races you get used to them and they no longer break immersion. They are great and make it fun to drive on tracks that you never drove on before.-First VR racer that I've been able to race in such large races with no significant performance issues.PC3 is not perfect and I hope they continue to optimize and update it, here are the cons:-VR menu garage is very "hoppy" which is disorienting. -No ability to replay a race directly after the race. You have to save it and go to your profile to replay.-Little nitpicking but I preferred it when you had the option to not have a racing helmet on like in Drive Club or Need for Speed.-The profile replay views are weird, no passenger seat view and if you switch views it cycles through them rather than stays on one view. Not sure if I did that or if it's just a bug-PC3 kept turning off my computer music every time I entered the game, I like to lower the in game music and play my own tunes. Finally got it to work but had to fiddle around with the audio settings to do so.-The controller was buggy as well, my wireless controller worked on all the menus but not after the start of the race, I was sitting there getting slammed into by all the cars behind me, they gotta fix that.-In both VR and 2D you can't move around the garage or the car, kind of a bummer.-Little things like in VR, I have to manually change the audio to headset every time I play, why isn't it automatic?-No Lexus cars (another bummer)-Very few BMW options (I'm pretty sure they will come in DLC)-Crashing into cars to get ahead in races is fun like bumper cars, but definitely not realistic (good thing I'm not looking for realistic :-)-I'm not 100% sure but I think PC2 in VR looked better visually. I cranked it up to max Ultra settings and didn't see a ton of difference, cars were still kind of blurry. (I'm using a Vive Cosmos so maybe when I get my HP Reverb 2, I'll see a bigger difference)-Career mode is nice but sometimes it feels like some events are impossible to succeed with certain cars due to the restrictions they set on the individual classes. For example, I suped up my E class Toyota up to 296 out of 300 meaning I can't go any further without it changing classes from E to D and consistently struggle with cars that have better acceleration. Now I have to go buy another car rather than upgrade my car to improve the acceleration. I guess it adds to the challenge and strategy, but that's hard when they only reward you with in game currency after you level up and not after every race, which makes it very "grindy".Overall, the game is only a week old, I have mixed feelings about companies that release games riddled with bugs and incomplete or seemingly untested features, but it also helps us get the games faster so i'm not too hard on games when they first launch. I fully expect they will improve on it in updates and DLC. Perhaps they could have just put it as Early Access. Anyway, I'm excited and far from disappointed with PC3, it's not the game 2D simmers wanted but the game VR needed!

_childDocuments_.review: Update (original review below): After six weeks of playing, I have to change this game to a negative review. There are just too many bugs, and only a single patch, almost a month ago. There aren't even any new test builds in steamdb. Approximately 1/3 of races start with no force feedback, ruining your first corner (you have to pause and unpause the game to restore force feedback). This is especially painful on Rivals events, when you may have only 10 attempts at the event. Frequently the computer will start your flying lap in the wrong gear -- imagine a hot lap attempt where you should be in 4th but the computer locks you into 2nd until you get control... again, that attempt is already going to be slower than you deserve. Another fun bug is when you improve your time on a Rivals event, but the game doesn't record your updated time... and won't until the event changes for the day. And cheating is rampant -- the same couple of people post times over a minute faster than anyone else, but SMS won't ban them.In fairness, even with those problems, you'll actually be grateful that the Daily Rivals is even working... yesterday, there was no daily event at all, and the devs in Discord just said "There should be one... keep trying, maybe it will start working later". Yes, seriously. That was the official response.What else can I list? Rain resets your car's livery. Multi-lap events reset your car's livery. Daily deals offer you cars that are 0% off! Hot Lap and Pace Setter events sometimes invalidate your lap as soon as you start a new lap, even though you're in the middle of the road... Restarting a race after a crash keeps your shattered windshield, unless you quit to the menu. And the devs in Discord mark bug reports as not accurate/not reproduceable. The whole thing is a farce. SMS is doing *just* enough to try to salvage their reputation because Codemasters signed them for a two-game deal. It's clear that no one is working on fixing the bugs. Again, last patch was Sept 17, and no new builds are in test, according to SteamDB (though there is an update showing the game going on sale... six weeks after release, lol. I guess they want more than 200 people online at once (globally)).STAY AWAY. The game is already dying, and it hasn't been out two months.Original review: Good arcade/sim-like with career progression, but without some basic features, like friends leaderboards. Honestly, 90% of Shift 2: Unleashed's replayability was competing with friends for each race's leaderboard. Now we get no friend competition, and instead, just random Rivals... with limited attempts (for Rivals mode, I agree with limited attempts.) But why can't my friends and I compete forever to better our times on each race???Good for what it is... sim racers should find other places to whine, because this is not a sim. It's an arcade/sim-like and meant for fun, not realism.

I dropped my chair height to fix the issue manually.  I wanted to calibrate my t300. Nope.  Can’t do it.  So finished the first race.  Car was sliding all over the track, understeer galore.  It was like driving on warm butter in a hot frying pan, I was slid9ng everywhere. I still managed first place on expert.  Bought my first car.  Started the second race, and then the game crashed.  Next, I clicked on the Steam Support button, and then submitted my refund request.  Stick with Assetto Corsa Competizione, Automobilista 2, or PR2.  I wouldn’t classify myself as a diehard sim racer, more like an intermediate sim racer.  More sim with a bit of arcade mixed in. PR3 is too much arcade.  Plus crashing in the first 10 minutes cemented my dislike for this current iteration.  I’ll pick it up again when it’s $9.99.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun despite the majority of complaints being centered around this title's departure from the past two games in the series. It plays like a lot of old-school racing games like Project Gotham, Outrun, Ridge Racer, Forza 4, NFS Shift, etc, with a splash of Driveclub for taste. This is very much an arcade racer and if you are okay with that I think you'll enjoy this game. I think people are just upset this isn't another cookie-cutter, tryhard sim racer, it's actually kind of refreshing to play something that's unique but familiar at the same time. I think the graphics look nice and the car selection is perfectly serviceable. Handling model could use a little work but the controls are very responsive. Gameplay is fun and engaging, I like that there is a "campaign" mode full of challenges and objectives for every race. The track list is big and full of variety, and this game has a lot of attention to detail. Anyway if you grew up playing racing games in the late 90s and early 2000s, you will more than likely enjoy this game. I sure do!

Multiplayer if you want it.If you are a casual GT player who plays on a controller and isnt that into racing real people, get it. My only complaint would be it takes a while for tracks to load (yes, its on a SSD). that wouldnt matter so much but if you try to repeat a race, as in TRY AGAIN --you have to go out and reload the race and it takes forever. this happens often bc the races arent just who is the fastest. There are mini achievements in each race that you must complete. Like -pass 10 cars in 1:00- so if you win the race, freaking kill it, but you didnt achieve that goal, you may want to immediately rerun the race before you move on. Nah. You gotta go way out and then wait minutes more to load and actually redo the race you just did. If you do the RESTART it offers, it wipes the xp and stuff you just got for a 1st run.  Gets realllly annoying even at only 80 hrs.Big thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: This plays a lot like Project Gotham Racing/Driveclub, if you enjoyed either of those two series, you will probably enjoy this game. Personally I feel they would of gotten better reception had they released this exact same game under literally ANY other name. I feel with Codemasters acquiring SMS, we will see them collaborate on a sim experience under a new name.So far I am enjoying this game as we have more than enough simulator racing games to fill that sim itch, so it is good to get a heavier feeling arcade circuit racer as opposed to GRID.If you turn all assists off, it really shines as an arcade racer imo. The graphics are not the greatest on some tracks but pretty decent on others, especially the rain. Graphics aren't a be all end all though, the game needs to be fun and succeeds at it.The sound design is pretty good, some cars sound so much better than other games attempts, like the Pagani Huayra. Some iconic cars and tracks are missing but may be included down the line, if not, there is still plenty of variety to enjoy.The career mode parallels heavily with Driveclub, short burst races with specific objectives within each one.Come to think of it, they should of called it Project Cars: ClubAll in all I enjoy this a lot more than I thought I would because I loved PGR/Shift/Driveclub series. I was worried for a an arcade racer, that they (CM/SMS) slap the GRID handling model which I do not enjoy. But again, turn all assists off and it is a tonne of fun to slide around in the wet.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the previous titles, don't waste your money here. You get nothing of what was offered in the last game. Tuning cars doesn't exist. There's probably less cars (less Evos, less Ferraris, and other manufacturers too that were in base PC2). You can't time trial on any track because, they said no. I don't get that. I've got 7 minute lap times on the Nurburgring in the 86, P1 GTR, and the Evo X (RIP for not even being in this game). Now all you do is drive around the track for practice. You're confined to do the time trials they want using the cars they chose on the tracks they chose. The lack of freedom is honestly embarrassing If you want to have fun and drive any car you can. But only in practice mode and you cant do any of those "upgrades" AFAIK, the UI isnt user friendly or intuitive. There's daily, weekly, and monthly "trials". Not even worth it because you can't compete on the tracks you want to with the car you want. Graphically this game is a step down from the second and somehow I didn't know it was possible for it to be worse than the first game. I had to calibrate my controller to use it. I had to manually input every button assignment. This game trilogy has 2 previous titles that have had flawless (almost flawless) day 1 support for gamepads/wheels/inputs. This game has no true to life car physics, anyone that's telling you it does is straight up lying. the first time trial they i tried had me in a Mustang with a drift setup for a time trial. If you care about a car's stats like top speed, handling, if it has ABS, TC, or anything you won't find it. Just an ambiguous bar on a scale of 0-100. At least I couldn't see anything that told me the top speed of the car i wanted to drive. Somehow the UI has devolved into some garage-software pirate's attempt to copy this game's interface with their own twist. It's really awful. Beyond awful actually. I hope steam can direct me to whoever I need to talk to, so I can give up my real driving license after touching this game. No time trials (weak), MP functionality (that's been this series' biggest downfall, a lack of a serious MP community/experience).
_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: After playing more of it, I can't say I like Project CARS 3 at all. Graphics and arcade physics are one thing, but when career structure is horrendous with barely any progression and no rewards after each career race (you can only get money by leveling up), it just feels like the worst kind of jRPG grind.Meaning that I'll be limited to 2-3 cars for a while while advancing on a career, and *paid* downgrades of parts I own are stupid, all on top of more grinding. That said, there's barely any incentive to get a new car from the same class series (Road, GT) since you can just upgrade your way through with a Mitsubishi Lancer. And individual cars have levels, but I don't see any point in them.The drivers themselves are either idiots or the next Hamilton who are ways ahead of you, and apparently can ignore alternate surfaces while you happily skid on gravel. And don't get me started at Hot Lap and Pace Setter events, the times are oftentimes frustrating if not impossible to get, and there's a lot of pure (if costly) guesswork on which car upgrade combo works best. Not to mention you're screwed once you make a single tire outside of the road. With the lack of flashbacks and having to wait at least 10 seconds to actually restart, it's mindnumbingly frustrating to fail the event when you're at your last corners of a long 3-lap pace setter event or even better, Nurburgring.So yea, I though GRID 2019 was the worst I've played by lacking any substance. PC3 low-key makes me angry, and I barely played 12 hours out of it since I bought it years ago during some sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR It's an okay arcade game in which its technical issues prevent me from even playing it further.If it isn't obvious from other reviews, this game is nothing like the previous Project Cars entries.  It doesn't even attempt any notion of simulator qualities.  It's an arcade racer through and through.  That said, I can appreciate an arcade racer every now and again.  Probably the most comparable title to PC3 is Grid, if you need a reference point for it.  It's not terribly difficult, but the handling doesn't really feel realistic at all or, at least, not incredibly consistent across different vehicle drivetrains.  Regardless, it's easy to pick up and get used to fairly quickly so the average player can probably drop in pretty easily.  Access to cars is locked behind a credit system and the credits are locked behind a leveling system so progression mostly entails "leveling up".  However, the game seems to be relatively stingy with the xp even when you've got the assists off and the difficulty turned up so there's an element of throttling at play here.  Either way, it's fairly fun and easy to get on when it works.  Except...I was enjoying my first several hours of this game, but somewhere along the end of the first division of cars (road D), I had an issue of an infinite load screen on a particular racing series which required me to terminate the program.  I reloaded the game, attempted to launch the series again, same result.  I decided to simply skip past that series and simply move on to road C.  A few series in, same issue.  There are several particular racing series in the game that simply never load at all.  After several troubleshooting and repair attempts, it still does not work and puts any progress in the game at a full stop.  I would just return it, but the issues appeared after the two hour return policy, but early enough in the game that I don't get to even play most of what it has to offer.  It's already spotty as it is when an arcade game is trying to appeal to a simulator crowd.  It's even worse when it's literally unplayable.  What really sucks is that if you're coming into this game with an open mind without expectations, it's actually pretty fun .  I cannot recommend this.  I'd have at least liked to get my money's worth out of it, but it appears that won't be happening.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review after over 100 hours of play...Had to change from a slightly positive thumbs up to a mostly negative thumbs down mainly because the balancing is buggered, the PIR system doesn't work at all,you can have 2 cars with the same PIR rating and be over 2 seconds a lap faster in 1 car and 2 seconds off in the other (yes i am taking in to account the right type of car for the circuit and taking in to account the car's stats shown in game).Online consists of 3 things:Quick play which is the best of the 3 dumping you in to 1 of a pool of track/car combinations but you're lucky to get more than 1 other player in a typical quick play sessionScheduled events which expose how broken the PIR system really is, the winner is always the person with the fastest car even though the PIR is supposed to provide balanced classes for racing but the PIR number 9/10 times means absolutely nothing, your 499PIR rated category A supercar in a 500 PIR limited race will likely lose to 499 PIR sh*tbox with upgrades from category C.Also has too many laps for too little reward (will talk more about the payout rate in a moment).Lastly you have Custom lobbies, at peak times you find up to a dozen lobbies to choose from and the majority of the time you are lucky to have 2 to choose from, i would say i get 1 decent race in these lobbies out of every 20.If you win a race, drive cleanly on an average online race (3x laps) you get 7k XP (without bonuses if you get any and at max with bonuses you are looking at 50k XP,) and even if you win a scheduled event which are the longest races which can last up to 30 minutes don't pay out much more, considering the money you earn is tied to the XP system (around 70k XP to fill the bar to get any payout takes from 15k to 30k depending on your driver level) it really leaves you feeling like you aren't being rewarded for your wins or the effort you put in to a race.Offline isn't much better either although at least you get bigger payouts after championships but they only payout once so no grinding a single event for cash which really annoys me.I don't think i've ever felt so torn about a racing game in my 20 years in the genre,i stand by my original statement in the 1st version of this review, it has a good foundation for a simcade but the balancing is nowhere near good enough to provide close racing without having to resort to forcing everyone in to identical cars with default setups, that may not sound shocking but that narrows the possibilities severely, resulting in online play that is either mixed racing were the fastest car will win by seconds per lap even thought it claims via the PIR system that the cars are balanced and competitive but aren't at all, or you have tryhards running lobbies with a specific car they own then forcing everyone else to use it except the owner's car is tuned for the circuit and/or has performance upgrades to provide an advantage over people using standard borrowed cars.Not even going to go in to the exploits being used on specific circuits which allow you to cut chicane sections without any penalties which can save 5 to 10 seconds per lap (found this out on a scheduled event when i was leading the race and 2nd and 3rd caught up then passed by using this exploit, had to do it myself to regain the win, yes i felt dirty afterwards :/).Also since the first/last patch the game keeps crashing when it was stable before that (bug filled but stable), now it is unstable and still has too many bugs.The physics are pretty good, decent for drifting fun in a solo lobby because you try to find anybody to drift with in this game, tis hard, even more so than PC2, and that was very hard indeed to find a tandem partner online.Overall, don't buy it, SMS, what is going on over there? What happened to you?Blink if you're being kept hostage.

_childDocuments_.review: I so much wanted to like this game because I thought it got a lot of bad reviews because the developers tried to make it appeal to more people which didn't seem to sit well with the sim racing community. I'm not a sim racer. My main gripes with the game are that the races themselves are fine and the developers will let you play on very easy if you want to so it's possible to win a few races. There are also other challenges which are timed or have set targets and this is where I feel the game falls down. You need to get points on these challenges to progress in the game but the times and the totals needed seem to be way beyond the capabilities of someone like myself so I keep ending up frustrated that I can't progress too well in the game. Another strange thing is that you can win races and events but don't seem to earn any money from them - I could be wrong on this. Surely in a game where you have to keep buying new cars to compete in the next level you would think you could earn money from the races you've won to pay for these cars (and a lot of them are not cheap). The money only seems to come from the XP you earn as you go along so no matter how many races you win the money only comes in in dribs and drabs. Add to this the ridiculous timed events and the breakout events with ridiculous scores to get, both always on the twistiest, winding courses in the game and it all adds up to a lot of frustration. I realise you are meant to buy upgrades but what with - the money doesn't seem to be there. This is a shame really because the actual racing is great fun. A potentially good game but ruined by the things I've mentioned. Makes you wonder why they've released 5(?) DLC's because some of us will never be able to afford these cars playing on the easier settings. Maybe it is targeted at the sim racers and the really good players and not the wider audience as they implied. I'm now at a standstill because I can't go any further in the game. Quite disappointing - another good idea ruined by thoughtless developers. No incentive to even try to play now. UPDATE - I've persevered with this game and have found out that it is possible to earn XP from custom events and this gives you money as your XP levels up. If only they'd told us this earlier. I'm now just doing custom events and the money is coming in - and I don't have to suffer the non-race events in the career mode. The game is a lot better now just doing the actual racing and trying to earn XP points within the races for skills used in the races such as mastering corners. Obviously you have to use the cars you have already bought but I find it much better and you get to try out all of the tracks. Much happier with the game now - I think I'll steer clear of career mode or just dip into it now and then. Now it makes a bit more sense I am happy to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: EDITED: After months of waiting for them to improve this game I'm changing my review from positive to negative. There has been a complete lack of transparency from SMS and they decided to release a terrible DLC as opposed to focusing on fixing bugs and improving the overall quality of their product. Even when asked, SMS said that they are focused on fixing bugs and not on future content. The next update was, you guessed it, the DLC and a few bug fixes. So I've played both PC1 and PC2 and I can say that this is nothing like those two games. It takes a completely different direction that isn't at all Simulator, and I believe it shouldn't be called Project CARS. But hey! Brand recognition, amirite?However, the game isn't at all bad.  and they have nailed that aspect of the game. This game is so much more accessible than PC1 and PC2 and it's much easier to just pick up and play. With that being said, it's not as easy as something like Need For Speed, but it's also not as unforgiving as other simcades like Forza. At the time of this review I've played about 12 hours of the game and have loved almost every second of it. The racing is fun and challenging and the different gamemodes included in the career are an absolute blast. There are gamemodes like Hotlap, Race, Pace Setter (3 consecutive hotlaps) and this one where you have to destroy blocks to get points. I haven't had a chance to play the multiplayer, but from videos I've seen it's also pretty decent.I've had a chance to play in a few different cars and they have all felt unique and fun. They handle corners and curbs differently and I often find myself struggling to do a lap with one car and acing the lap with another. The customisation is also very neat, although I would have liked to have seen more parts customisation. Currently, you can slap on some aero, but your car will look the same. It's a bit upsetting, but still not bad at all!The progression feels balanced and fair with races for everybody and some very fun car/era specific events that force me out of my comfort zone. I absolutely love this because it forces me to play cars I would never usually consider.You are probably wondering how this game actually plays, input wise. With a gamepad this game is amazing. Maybe not quite as refined as Forza or GT, but very nice and fun. With a wheel it's not bad, but there is definitely a lack of settings for wheel users. I had to recalibrate my wheel in order to limit the turn limit because otherwise I've found myself having to go to full lock in order to take a turn. The force feedback feels quite light in my opinion and it's difficult to find traction. This being said, the game allows you to correct skids and oversteer quite a lot so it's still a very fun experience at the end of the day. I would still like to feel curbs more, feel water puddles and feel the grip of the car. Overall, I do with the cars would grip more realistically though.The car selection is honestly really good and so is the track selection. There are a nice amount of fictional tracks that are super fun to race around and feel really good.The AI is really good at times, but other times it's not. Some tracks it's literally impossible to corner as fast as they do. They also have a weird issue where they don't have shifting times. They accelerate smoothly and constantly and always overtake me when I shift, even when I tried the automatic gearing. I believe Jimmy Broadbent also mentioned this in his video. At times I do feel like the AI is a little too bad and I have won most races I've entered. So a bit of tweaking is definitely needed here.Graphically the game seems like a step down from PC2 and the anti aliasing is absolute trash, but I assume (and hope) SMS will fix this in the future and optimise the game further. If you are having issues you should probably disable the super sampling because that is a good method of AA that just kills any GPU because it literally renders the image big, then scales it down to the resolution. TAA, SMAA or even FXAA should be added to the options because they are much more efficient methods of AA. Overall though the game honestly doesn't look bad. Is it ground breakingly good? No. Is it going to make everybody within a five mile radius gawk at your screen? Also no. Is it acceptable? I'd say yes, because the game's not about the hardcore immersion that PC1 and PC2 were about. This game is about fun.Actually yes! I really would! But  I believe this game has been marketed so poorly with SMS consistently saying that it was a sim and what not, but it really isn't at all. This game is arcade. I wish they had gone and done what they have with the controller feel and basically improved upon PC2, to give us an even better sim, but PC3 is still a welcome addition to the arcade genre in my opinion. The key part of this game is fun and I think they did a very good job and it will make more people interested in racing games and could expand the community. This is really good. It focuses on the "C" in Project CARS. It doesn't have much S (Simulation), but what it does have works well. There are still things like puddles, which I was happy about because I thought they'd removed.Why would you make an arcade game and then have such a garbage unfair track limits system that also punishes the player for being PUSHED OFF THE TRACK?!?! MAKE IT STOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOP!I'm going to allow comments on this review so we can discuss. If you have any questions about the game, feel free to ask. Opinions are like a******s, we've all got one, and this one is mine (not my a******s, but my opinion).

_childDocuments_.review: In this game you lose up to 25K XP if you touch the wall in Custom Event, 10/9! Now seriously, who was the idea to do that? And to put Time Trial events that have more aggressive rules than taking a license in Gran Turismo? Damn, this game would be perfect if it weren't for that! In the gameplay aspect it is the best simcade since Forza 4 and Gran Turismo 6, SMS achieved the feat of mixing the speed of Forza with the handling of Gran Turismo, simply magnificent! But then in the Time Trial events instead of punishing by adding more time on the clock when we make a mistake, as it did in Forza 1 and 2, they just punish you by canceling all your progress! If it is already frustrating in Hot Lap that is only one lap, imagine in Pace Setter that there are 3 complete laps where you lose all your progress in the 3 laps if you put a nail off the track in the last stretch or curve before the end of the event , frustration is just the tip of the iceberg in this case. For this problem and the one mentioned at the beginning in the form of a joke, I get 1 point for the loss of XP without reason, 1 point for the Hot Lap and 3 points for the Pace Setter, final score 5/10, in a game that I could give 10 / 10 if it weren't for those 3 problems that can be solved if SMS wants, but I doubt it. Another suggestion for Pace Setter and Hot Lap would be to place a maximum number of errors before canceling our effort, in addition to making it fairer, you would be encouraging pilots to take more risks to improve their lap times.

_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: A really bad attempt at being Forza.So the game is definitely better than the previous two entries, which were absolute trash with the worst physics I've seen in a racing game. The car handling in this one is a big step up and now it's actually possible to play with a controller and still stay on the road after the first corner.However, the visuals are mediocre at best, with plenty of low res ground textures, poor lighting implementation (especially during night) and cars that looks to be made out of plastic during certain lighting conditions.The worst part of the game is the event objectives that you have to complete to progress in the career. Some of these are bugged and don't register even though you do a perfect corner or a clean lap. Some of them also seem to have been balanced by a rookie trash designer with no sense of balancing whatsoever. The difference between scoring a gold or bronze time can be as little as 3 seconds and requires nano second precison. This would be fine for an achievement, but not a mandatory objective that gates you from progressing. Please patch this and fire whoever designed this. It's litterary game breaking.Another really annoying thing is the way you gain money. You get exp when completing races which makes you level up and get cash in return. However you get very little cash so you won't have enough cash to buy the cars you need (some events requries certain cars) which will force you to replay completed events just to rank up and get more cash. They could easily have doubled the amount of money you gain to reduce the grind.Yet another let down is the AI, which is completely unaffected by weather conditions like rain and snow. They drive like a train on rails while you slide around like crazy. Even on medium AI difficulty there is simply no way to match their speed without sliding of the track. Agan, fire the useless tool of a designer who designed this.I would stay away from this game, at least until the event objectives has been fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: I am really enjoying this game. Career mode is refreshing and challenging. Customisation of the cars is cool and a nice upgrade from previous PC's. Multiplayer is good but could do with some improvements on multiplayer comms in lobby and race. Cars feel and drive very nice and tracks are awesome. Not sure why its getting such bad reviews but give it a little time and grows on you. I will get the dlc's when on special tho.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game if you take it for what it is, and that is an accessible casual racing game.It is not a sim racer, but it is also not on rails arcade racing either.This is a Forza Motorsport/Gran Turismo competitor, nothing more nothing less. If you want easy to jump into racing with consequences for mistakes but free of some of the complications and things that make sim racing un-appealing, then this is a fantastic game for that.In my personal opinion, those giving negative feedback clearly didn't follow any of the promotions for the game in the lead up, as it was obvious this is how the game would turn out.The only mistake is calling this Project Cars 3, it should have been an aside to the series (like how Forza do Motorsport and Horizon as 2 different series because of their differences in content and play style).The game itself plays and runs very well. I am a little disappointed I don't have more options in terms of graphics settings (the option seem very similar to the limitations you'd see on a console without the extras you see on a PC). The cars aren't as punishing as in a sim racer, but with the assists on "experienced" (lowest traction control and ABS only) I feel like if I make a mistake I will at least be punished for it.The AI steps nicely and after a few races I started to find the sweet spot for my preference where races were challenging but I didn't feel like I would be swamped every race.The progression also seems perfectly balanced so far. The next nice car is always JUST in reach. Enough that its achieveable, but also not too close that you have access to everything too quickly and just burn through the content.
_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really disappointed what happend to Project CARS. But worse, this game got announced as a simulation or at least sim-arcade, as the predecessors have been. I had very much fun playing PC1 & PC2. I never missed the career mode as I prefered the more realistic gameplay and physics, even tho it wasnt too simulation-like. I bought this game expecting the same experience as PC1 & PC2 gave me and what SMS had announced for this game. And after I downloaded it and started it, I was so disappointed. I run at least 60 mins. through the settings, to find the options I was used to, to make this game more sim-like. But nothing, its just an arcade bumpercar racing game like NFS. I mean srsly.. what happend? Its not only about the physics, where is tyre wear? Fuel consumption? Pit stops? Why is there no Kart Racing? Thats where a career should start, work your way up from kart to GT or Formula Racing. Speaking of it, why kick Formula A? SMS, you have to make a big update to this game. This is not to recommend to any PC-Fan or Sim-Racing-Fan.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a bad game, but it isn't Project Cars. This game is somewhere between Forza and Forza Horizon. If you want to play something like Forza, just play Forza.Whenever I get motivated enough to install my steering wheel I still go to PC2. If you liked PC2, please don't waste your money on PC3.

_childDocuments_.review: No, no and once more - no. DO NOT BUY IT.Reason: even after a year since release it is still an unfinished product, that requires a lot of babysitting to make it run properly.-the framerate ranges anywhere from 30 to 200 FPS. And any program running in background or on a second monitor will run like ass because this game bottlenecks someting in a system. CPU and GPU can be loaded lower than 50%, yet programs on my second monitor and OBS run at 5 FPS.-there is a ♥♥♥♥ load of graphical glithes and the game looks ugly as sin. TAA is broken, some special effects look wrong, there is a lot of flickering in the shadows and lighting.-ALT+F4 doesn't work. This is a huge sin on its own.-If ingame resolution is different from the monitor resolution, then if you click outside the game's window it will switch permanently to windowed mode. And because ALT+Enter doesn't work you can only fix that by restarting the game.List of problems can be endless, but I have to be honest: underneath all of this there is a fun arcade racer with very cool and deep phisycs engine. It breakes my heart to see this project doomed to be forever unfinished.

_childDocuments_.review: Recently, I've become hooked on racing simulation games using a VR headset and steering wheel controller. With limited options for VR racing games, I knew the reputation of Project Cars 3 wasn't great, but I decided to give it a try, hoping that more than two years since its release might have brought some improvements. To be honest, I can't recommend this game.During the races, generic EDM music plays as background music, while noticeable notifications and strange sound effects ring out every time you pass through a checkpoint, ruining the immersion.It's puzzling that despite the game's poor reputation, the price hasn't been significantly reduced and it's still being sold at a high price.Originally, the Project Cars series was a racing simulation series, but with its shift to an arcade style, it has become an entirely different game. Fans who were interested in the simulation aspect were disappointed, and eventually, the series met its end.This experience serves as a lesson in game development - it's crucial to ensure that the product image and content do not diverge.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly this game will dissappoint you if you are a hardcore Project Cars fan.Project Cars 3 shouldn´t be called Project Cars it´s more like a Need for Speed Shift 3 (which was also made by Slightly Mad).So it´s a Simcade Racer like Grid, Forza or as mentioned NFS Shift. And as such I think it´s a pretty good one.It offers a large amount of different cars which are - apart from bodywork - fully customisable (even rims and tyres).The career is nothing special but it is, because of that, focussed completely on the driving. In the career you have different playmodes which make a good diversion.The track list is pretty decent and there are only a few tracks I miss personally (Le Mans, Spielberg, Spa). But SMS included some custom made tracks which are very great to drive.Also there is the possibilty to lend a car and drive a race with it and you even earn XP with it just little less than with your owned car.Ince I´ve never played Forza and the last Grid I played was Grid 2 I can`t really compare those games. But I can say that in my opinion Project Cars 3 is a good - not awsome but defenitly better than decent - Simcade which has  a large amount of cars and tracks to offer. I give it a 7/10.Btw. English is not my first language and I´m sorry for my bad spelling grammatics :)

_childDocuments_.review: Its a damned solid arcade racer. It reminds me so much of Grid 2 which for me is a good thing. The handling is definitely different from Forza but I would argue that it is better. There is a solid car selection and a nice mixture of fantasy and real life locations to race at. Personal favourites are California Highway and Azure Coast.I can understand why OG Project Car players are salty about this release, but for someone who is more into the arcadey side of racing, this is a solid entry since Grid (2019) was pretty terrible on launch and FM7 and FH4 have become very stale.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off this review i'd like to excuse me for my terrible english grammar...Ok, first impressions after 13 hours are good! If you make terrible mistakes or try to ram others you'll be ghosted and your power is taken away for a few seconds. The game does have some minor problems with performance but that is just a matter of optimization. Those minor bugs don't bother me at all and the racing is straight fun. I simply love everything in this game.Please know that a lot of negativity flows from people expecting a true simracer after Pc 1 and 2 and they didn't get it. I can understand that they feel down about this but leaving a negative review and saying that everything is a joke in this game doesn't make sense to me.If you love Arcade with a mix of sim, this game is certainly for you! _childDocuments_.review: TLDR before I start rambling if you want to know what I think:I think the game is great, one of the best all-rounded simcades out there, but I do see why people are upset about this game being called a "Project Cars" game.Pros -Once I upgraded my pc to make the game run over 60 fps (I have a GTX 1080 atm), the game did turn out to be a very solid game. The career gets you trying out cars you don't normally pick in free run sessions, helps you adapt to different speeds and driving styles. The slower cars do make it seem a bit off-putting to use since races take longer to complete but I assure you the slow progression is definitely worth it.Another point is the large plethora of cars ; since there are so many it makes sure that you aren't driving the exact same way every time you switch to a different class, I do enjoy driving on a track and switching between a downforce-heavy GT3 car to a modern road car to see how I fair.One more thing I want to mention is the carefree nature of this game, because it isn't a serious sim title, it's more for the casual gamer using a controller, who likes to see cars that normally can't maintain a drift, doing that very thing once pushed to a point. The various cars do let you try the game seriously with online leader board events as well as getting faster lap times (I've been trying out a Logitech G920 Steering Wheel with pedals, I prefer the controller currently but the wheel is a nice addition to extending my play time of the game).Cons - When it comes down to what is wrong with the game, I only have a small amount of playtime so what I say is mostly from my experience, as well as what I've heard from others.Running this game, as it is currently, is a bit demanding. I had a GTX 1660 before my current upgrade and it couldn't run the game at 60 on anything close to High settings. I'm sure optimisations may come down the line to help people enjoy the experience as much (Guessing the good thing from this is that the game was telling me to upgrade my PC for the better :D)As well as demanding system requirements, some of the tasks in this game do seem a bit difficult at first, mainly the time trials. I personally like how difficult it is because it helps motivate me to try and get round the course better, but I do hear how difficult it does get down the line. Guess we'll see when I get there.Overall, if slightly simplified driving mechanics and the wide range of cars appeal to you, this game is for you. I'm sure even with the negative stigma surrounding this game, there is something to enjoy for everyone, experienced or not. :)

_childDocuments_.review: While there are better racing games out there I enjoyed this game for a few hours. You can set up custom races and drive all the cars the game has to offer. The driving does not feel as good as it did in Project Cars 2, but after tweaking the settings a little it felt ok and I had some fun with my Thrustmaster T500RS wheel. Less realistic compared to Project Cars 2 or Assetto Corsa, but I wasn´t looking for maximum realism with this.Then I tried career mode, where you have to buy the cars before you can use them. Many of the better cars in career mode can only be bought once you reach a certain driver level. So I leveled up and found most of the cars that should have unlocked were still locked. I checked on the forums and found out this is a known bug that has been in the game since release. Sometimes cars don´t unlock when they should and there is nothing you can do about it, besides restarting career mode from scratch and hoping for a different outcome. This ruined the game for me. There have been several patches and this still has not been fixed. So this game does nothing better than other racing games that came out in the past couple of years and it has a game breaking bug in career mode that has not been fixed several months after release. If you are looking for a realistic driving simulation, get Assetto Corsa instead. Want a slightly less hardcore experience, get Project Cars 2. If you are looking for what this game appears to be going for, a semi-realistic yet accessible racing game, go get Forza Motorsport 7 instead. I cannot recommend Project Cars 3 to anyone.

I've been playing racing games since i was a kid ... i say it's a hard game } ... if you're really focused and want a real challenge it might be for you because it's cheaper than Forza Motorsport but i like a bit more fun than stress { i waste too much time if i don't pass } so i prefer Forza Motorsport 7 for that reason ... the graphics aren't super sharp in terms of resolution compared to other games { like Forza Motorsport 7 or Automobilista 2 }. I'll probably go back to Automobilista 2 because there is a couple interesting tracks you get with the base game that don't get with Forza Motorsport 7 and the handling is more difficult than FM7 but some tracks are too tight with the turns to be good with the steering sensitivity settings you need on an xbox one controller { tracks in career mode } so ya know ... also any cars that are more powerful than stock cars are too difficult to compete with the difficulty all the way down to 70 { the lowest setting for Automobilista 2 }. _childDocuments_.review: The only fundamentally wrong thing with this game is it's name. Compared to its predecessor, they got nothing in common except your race engineer's voice.If you like semi-Arcade racers such as Forza Motorsports, Gran Turismo and GRID, then PC3 is a very competent game with a smooth progression system and stands right up there amongst the others.However if you were looking for, you know, a game that felt like Project Cars... Well that ain't it. Even at the highest simulation settings, this game feels nothing like its PC1 and 2, especially in terms of handling and difficulty. Races are short few lap stints with side-objectives and there's no tweaking of parameters like race length or whatever. If they'd called this something like SideProject Cars or Project Cars Arcade, nobody would've complained, instead thousands of fans have been mislead into buying a game that wasn't what they wanted.EDIT: Since this review I discovered that a lot of the SMS crew were part of the team that developped the Need for Speed Shift sub-series back in the days. You will definitely feel that influence in PC3. In multiple ways this is, for all intent and purposes the spiritual successor of Shift.

Going to give the VR bit a try next...VR left much to be desired.  Reminded me of playing Gran Turismo on my PS1.  My machine is a fully loaded i9 system with an RTX 2080 Super, so the reduced image quality and choppiness was surprising.  I'll read up on it and see if I need to do anything to improve it.***UPDATE***VR support is still not worth mentioning, however I've grown to like how PC3 handles the corner markers.  It's quite easy to leave the dynamic racing line on in a game like Forza and just follow it.  Here it merely suggests the best place to start braking so I can hit the apex properly...  Which forces me to learn the corners more than I would in other titles.  Not sure I'll ever switch them off but it does add to the enjoyment and challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve played 3 hours so far and from the moment I played Project Cars 3 I knew it was the racing game for me. It cut out all the things that I do like in sims but don’t have time* for: qualifying, pitting and long races.Is it like a combination of Project Cars 2, Gotham, Forza and Gran Turismo? Yes it is. Is that a bad thing? Not really.Is it an arcade game? I guess that depends on your definition, I would think an arcade racing game is Ridge Racer, Burnout or Grid 1 and 2.It’s more like driving a car than those, is it more realistic than Gran Turismo, yeah I think so, those cars don’t have enough grip. I think it’s like the later Forza games except the cars have grip.It has the structure of Gran Turismo and Forza of old, it isn’t throwing money at you and you aren’t driving McLaren P1 in the first 10 minutes. I think it wants me to hang on to my GT86 given it has a race conversion available like GT 1 or Need for Speed Shift.Does it look good? I think so, I think it looks like Project Cars 2. Would I prefer if the cars were shaded like Assetto Corsa Competizione and Gran Turismo yes, probably, but it doesn’t look terrible.Does it sound good? Yeah it does.Does it control well? Yeah I think so. Often people think that cars should be hard to drive, they’re not, but they are hard to drive quickly. I’ve done track days, I’ve only crashed once.The cars have a lot of grip, but cars do have a lot of grip anyway, especially with good tyres like some R888s.There’s a race in Class E on Cadwell Park, I defy you to play that with the GT86 and think it isn’t fun.It finally works on a controller; it’s only taken 4 games if you count Shift 1 and 2.I’ve played with a wheel for a bit, if felt fine, I wouldn’t be the expert of this. I didn’t crash loads, I didn’t spin lots but I was driving a GT86 on a track I knew.*Here’s my context, I'm in my mid 40s as of release date, I have a full-time job and a toddler. I love cars, I’ve owned loads, I wish 20 years ago I’d bought an NSX or a R32, I had two kouki Silvia's, I crashed one at Silverstone, I went blind in one eye for a night.I love games, I love sims, but I often only have 30 minutes a night after putting a toddler to bed, eating dinner, and tidying up. It took me a year to finish the main story mode of Assassin’s Creed Odyssey.I spent days playing Live for speed and hours and hours playing Assetto Corsa, Project Cars and Project Cars 2. I’ve played Assetto Corsa Competizione a little, it was awesome, but I don’t have time.I love F1 games, but I always end up dropping them as I don’t have time for practice, qualification and a race in that 30 minutes. I love Gran Turismo Sport, when my toddler was a baby I'd play every night for hours with a baby asleep on me, I got into Class B, but that took too much effort, I couldn’t drop in, do a quali lap and then have a good race. I used to love Forza, but each release I’ve liked it less, to the point where I played the demo of 7 and it was the first I didn’t buy.So here we are; time. I can drop in, do some races, earn some medals and progress my GT86 on. I need to do a couple more races because I don’t have enough money to buy the Evo, do I mind this, not at the moment.It's OK if you don't like something and other people do. So, it's Ok if you disagree, I don't mind, we can't all like the same things all of the time.*updated bit*After 2 weeks and 6 hours of play I've completed Road E. I got all but one medal, I'm .8 seconds too slow on the fake Suzuka track doing the Pace Setter race.The difficulty is wonky, I'm now playing on Legendary and I'm not sure ifa) the AI is too slowor b) The R34 Skyline is too good, you can breeze races with no upgrades.I think weight reduction is too good as well, especially on the R34.I think it's a bit of both, the AI doesn't attack the kerbs really. Probably it's like GT and Forza where you have to make your own fun by not upgrading too much and be a bit under their SR.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm someone who bought Project Cars 1 and 2, but struggled with the handling on a control pad. I love racing in VR, but in terms of track racing, nothing on the PC has managed to beat the ancient Oculus DK2 version of Grid Autosport, which I loved. You can probably tell from the above that I'm more of a simcade person than a serious sim racer. I love the Gran Turismo and Forza series of games, but aside from some very limited (but good) VR features in GT Sport, they're not VR games.Having given this a try, it's a perfectly fine simcade racer. But in VR it's transformed as an experience. I've been using the Oculus version with the Rift S attached to a PC with an i7 3770 and an Nvidia 1070. The game turns everything down to low, and it looks a lot like a PSVR game, and has a few graphical glitches, but it runs well overall. And because of how transformative VR is, this turns into a really great experience (much better for me than Project Cars 1 and 2).I've read a lot of the criticism of this game, and much of it is somewhat deserved, but for me this is a VR racing toybox, with a great range of tracks and cars (I especially like the old racing cars like 60s F1 and CanAm). So to any of the dev team reading this, you're probably disappointed by the reaction, but you've made me at least very happy. And to anyone else, if you're OK with a simcade game, this is a good effort with lots of variety, and if you have VR (Oculus at least) and a reasonably powerful PC, this could well be a really fun experience for you.

_childDocuments_.review: As a racing sim fan, I really do enjoy Project Cars 3 (PC3). I know you read comments from hardcore racing sim fans, saying that this is more of arcade racing than a racing sim, it is worse than Project Cars 2 (PC2). I beg to differ. Don't listen to them (I would say to them, just keep playing Project Cars 2, Asserto Corsa or iRacing)This game is not as punishing as PC2 and I think Slightly Mad Studios want to make the game accessible to other gamers. PC3 feels more like NFS Shift and Shift 2 (which coincidentally, was develop by the same developers) and I enjoy the NFS Shift series. So, it's no brainer that I would enjoy PC3, especially since I am playing PC3 exclusively with my Thrustmaster Wheel and Shifter.PC3 is a game that I would keep playing as compared to PC2 (which I have to set a specific timing to play PC2, and it perhaps became boring after sometime, it's not a game that you can enjoy).My only problem with PC3 is when I play using VR. At one point, the game crashes in VR, even after restarting the game. But, the game just released recently, I'll wait patiently for the update to make the VR gameplay more stable.Bottom Line, If you want the ultimate racing sim game, stick to PC2, Asserto Corsa or iRacing. If you think those racing games are too difficult and you want something that give you that racing sim experience but is more accessible, go get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: i prefer arcade racing games instead of racing sims so it's to let you know im writing this review completely unbiased. i ignored the reviews and still bought it anyway because when i heard its more towards arcade, it genuinely made me interested. finally, i thought to myself that forza will have some competition. sadly.. not really. PROS: 1. really really wide variety of cars, not on forza's level but still good enough. i hope that the team will keep on adding cars though, its never enough 2. interesting mechanic on the XP modifier that i dont see it often in other games3. usually good graphics (keyword: usually, will explain more about this under the cons section) 4. it paired my steering wheel instantly and well (i'm grabbing at straws now on the positives) CONS:1. the biggest con no doubt is the handling. feels artificial, incredibly difficult to keep it on the straight line and car loves to spin out of control even with traction control on to the max. i have 0 issues with driving in forza and other racing sims but for some reason PC3 seems to be tailend happy 24/7. even apart from the handling, the overall driving experience on the wheel is not that fun and accurate even for an arcade. 2. why the heck am i not earning money after each race? why do i only earn money when i ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ level up? this is honestly so annoying, its like im barely rewarded and teased by the developers for completing each race. it doesnt feel rewarding after awhile.3. the graphics.. yes its good but once in awhile, my exterior of the car starts spasming out and there are some screen tears starting to show (my desktop has an RTX 2060 GPU so this shouldnt be an issue) 4. the AI.. are one of the craziest and bonkers  in any racing game. i have AI difficulty & aggression on medium but they drive as if they are in mad max and they can turn almost 90° to crash into me, preventing me from passing and in the end they spin and i got stuck banging into them like what? occassionally, they start spasming out too and self combust by suddenly making a sharp turn into the wall and me, an innocent bystander behind that guy smashes into the side of him. 5. dont get me started on the physics of the game. yes this is an arcade, but at this caliber of a game, developer and price, you would expect at least some form of physics right? yea.. not really. i can be crashing into walls, making my car look like it has just came out from the scrapyard but my car drives as good as new. i might have missed an option out on whether i can enable damage but not that i can easily see. FH4 reenacts the whole arcade racing game perfectly, having 70% arcade but at least 30% realism. i really want to enjoy this game. the amount of hate for this game just because it isnt an actual simulator frustrates me but even for an arcade, this game falls relatively flat compared to its competitions. i will still play this game but damn, it isnt great at all. i would strongly suggest people who wants to get a new racing game (be it arcade/sim) to only get this game when its on sale. its honestly a let down.

_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: Disregarding other comments made about the game, I will be reviewing it from an objective basis (not whether or not it follows the Project Cars basis). - Does it stand on it's own merit? Yes. The game is great for pickup-and-play arcade/simcade racing.- Does the game have bugs and visual glitches? Yes. Visual glitches seem to be quite common so far.- Does the game continue the Project Cars franchise? No, it has been totally revamped to appeal to a larger audience. It's up to you whether or not that backfired.- Is this game enjoyable? Yes. The physics feel great so far and if you like grinding for money, you will love this game. Money is hard to come by as I have just enough money to buy a single car for each new championship (and that's it without grinding).- How do you obtain money? Leveling up. Races don't give you money, instead you gain money from leveling up. You gain XP from the races. I'd say you gain money for every 2-3 races on average.- I've played around 4 hours on my first day and I can expect myself to be playing for at least 2 hours consistently. Coming from Arcade racers and heavily not liking PC2, I can say I enjoy this game quite a lot.Final Verdict: Buy if you like arcade-style games with great handling. Otherwise - Wait for on sale.Overall rating: 7.5-8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: Well what can I say. This game should not have been called Project Cars 3. It should have been called something else like Shift 3 or Project Shift. It's not a sim.It's a pretty fun and addictive Arcade racing game, which I did not like at first, but it's strangely addictive, and I actually really like it now, just to play casually and work through the single player campaign, which consists of different events which you have to work through, earning XP and credits to buy and upgrade your cars to unlock further events. it's got a vibe a bit like the Ride series or Grand Turismo, Shift games.I bought this dirt cheap, so I think it is definitely worth picking up in a sale or obtaining a cheap PC Key somewhere. CD Keys or Gamivo.It has some bugs, loading times can seem a bit longer than some racing games, but nothing too serious.So to sum up, the graphics, cars and tracks are really good. I think this is a game that falls into the category of it is so bad, it's actually good. There is a huge amount of wasted potential and it's a shame it hasn't been modded to add extra events or championships. I would not recommend buying the DLC or Deluxe versions.A solid 8/10 from me.Let's just hope Project Cars 4 returns to form and delivers us what we all want next time !!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite refunding, I played 110 minutes of mainly multiplayer with a friend and did enjoy the game. We both jumped in with a arcade mindset. I tried both game pad and my T150 wheel, both were playable although I do feel like the FFB on the wheel is weak. So what are the pros and cons in my opinion and why refund?Pros:- Good graphics (Similar if not exactly the same as PC2) However I did have lower frame rates- Decent physics, some cars felt a little light. It was very easy to throw the car around without any problems (all assists off)- Very inclusive, players of all skill should be able to play with no issues- Lots of vehicles and tracks to pick from although if you played PC2 its a lot of repeats- A structured career (Depends on the person)Cons:- Far as I could tell the only way to race cars other than the career vehicles you unlock was on multiplayer (Could be wrong)- Multiplayer lobbies lack many options, no fill in AI option that I could find- Downgraded weather system compared to last game, fewer options- The UI- Force Feed Back lacks a lot of feeling. I would rather play with a game padPC3 feels like a downgraded re-release of PC2. Disregarding the fact that its not designed to be a simulator, the amount of great features that existed in the last game are cut short in this game. I primarily refunded because of the lack of things to do in multiplayer. Sure we can race just like any other game but there's a lack of options, no AI (that I could find), and it just felt like it would quickly become boring. Had the career been co-op we might've kept it. Overall this game is a slightly scuffed Forza Motorsport. I would only recommend buying it on sale if a casual racing game is what you're looking for.

While those two "old" games can't compete in terms of visuals, they would for the AI, while they were really not top notch at their time, because the Project Cars  3 is almost a disaster at this point.As a short summary, i feel you could have more fun with the Need For Speed : Shift series than Project Cars 3 if you're looking for a "Arcade Oriented" game than this one. I highly recommend the "Full Sim" enthousiasts to stay away of this game, unless they're looking for a very different racing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Project Cars 3 is immense. Any game with a claimed 160 tracks 200 cars, is going to be immense. I found Project Cars and Project Cars 2 very hard to get into and very unforgiving. I find Project Cars 3 a totally different experience. You can alter the drive assists and braking assists to be on or off and thus customise your experience to be hardcore, or, alternatively, you can adjust it to be fun, like I did. This game now looks very, very much like Driveclub - which is no bad thing. With selectable, unlockable stages, right down to triple achievement targets in each race, and the experience progress bar increasing several driver assets when you do well. But it's not trying to *be* Driveclub - which is important to note.Pleasingly, since it was made in the UK, the English is all spelled correctly - which is a rare and precious thing in gaming (do you have any idea how jarring it is to see all these "Medieval setting" games and then seeing words like "civilization" popping up). All the voices are also without any accent which is also very refreshing.The game runs astonishingly smoothly at max settings even on 'just' my 6th Generation SkyLake Core i7 with a GeForce 1060 GTX. These settings can be finitely adjusted too, right down to camera shake. Another rare and very welcome thing is how the menu system works. A good few racing games these days appear to want to perpetually trap you in the game and include the most obscure keys and convoluted procedures before you can get back to the desktop (sometimes I've even had to look up on the internet how the hell to quit the race and/or game). With Project Cars 3, wherever you are in the game, you just keep on pressing Escape, until you're asked "do you want to quit to desktop" - it's as simple as that, and yes, it's GOOD to be as simple as that (other developers, would you PLEASE take note). The music is pretty dire, but I don't tend to notice it too much - it certainly does not wreck the experience for me. You really feel the achievement when you've finally mastered a track - which is a pretty tight aim because the early stages are just 2 laps long.  What Slightly Mad Studios have achieved here is to bring back FUN into a racing game - without making it a pushover. That to me, having played around 90% of all PC racing games since the 90's, yet still not being super expert driver here, is a really great achievement because it's a tough thing to pull off well.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is arcade style, not a true succesor to the earlier project cars sim-games. It is more of a new addition to the need for speed shift series. The game is fun to play.Pos: Lots of tracks and cars, considerable amount of content in singleplayer and career mode. UPDATE: Found out that custom races also generate xp and money that can be used in career mode, which gives the game a new dimension. Huge collection of tracks and cars in custom mode. Good music.Neutral: Graphics, car handling, grinding. You have to do races over and over again to collect enough money to buy new cars but that's no problem if you enjoy the game. Minus: Game's title is misleading, should have been called for instance Shift 3 or something. Vast loading times.  Recommend to buy this game on sale, including the dlc:s.  This review is for the deluxe edition, including all extra content.

_childDocuments_.review: Being a huge fan of Need for Speed Shift, hearing this described as feeling more like a Shift 3 than a Project CARS sequel from someone made me really excited to get this... and it's okay, mostly?Like, the driving and sound design are good () but the career progression is straight garbageSo, the way you unlock new events is by completing career objectives, and there are 3 for every event. A lot of the time winning the race isn't even an objective, so for a bunch of events it's actually better to let everyone pass so you can master all corners in peace...Winning does net you more exp though, which you're gonna want, because the way you earn money is... BY LEVELING UP!You don't get any money whatsoever for participating in a race, or completing objectives, or even winning the dang thing, unless it provides enough exp for you to level up ()AND... you're really gonna need that cash, because a lot of events require very specific cars"Oh, this event needs a Road D from between 1980-1989, and there are only 3 cars that fit that criteria " so you grind the same races you've already played to try to get any exp to level up to get credits to buy a new car, and as it turns out this car is only needed for this one event... so you sell it for HALF THE MONEY BACK, WHICH ISN'T EVEN ENOUGH TO BUY ANOTHER CAR FROM THE SAME CLASS, so you have to grind the same boring races to get another car that you're only gonna use in a single event ()Almost forgot, if you're like me and aren't a great driver, you might get stuck because you can't complete any remaining career objectives () but fret not! You can spend some of your slowly earned pennies on unlocking the other events ()I have lost where I was going with this, I am only ranting because I want to love this game but am unable to do so
