_childDocuments_.review: I am usually pretty light on most reviews being I know everyone is extremely harsh and rarely optimistic. In this case with Project Cars 3 it is honestly far worse than the mixed reviews are stating. That is even me understanding it was not designed to be the same as Project Cars 1 and 2. Despite that I made the mistake of just assuming in the physics, graphics, audio, and basic core of the game would remain either the same, or developed by brilliant people who designed the first 2. It absolutely fails in all of those catagories.  THis game literally marks the second time in 11 years I requested a refund.  Its handling is overly heavy without a real sensation that you could eventually get in line with how tires interact with the road and how vehicle weight shifts. ITs insanely inconsistent here.   The sounds are on par with something from the PS2 days and feel very manufactured. The graphics seem ok looking at reviews but when actually driving a car it is horrid. There are almost no realistic options to improve any of this through menus either. We basically got the console version on PC without any perks to boost resolution or any of that.  From an optimist who owns over 40 grand in PC titles trust me when i tell you to look elsewhere. IT is a let down in every important category required to make a game worth playing, let alone owning. 11 years of Steam and hundreds of titles, this is the second one I felt must be returned.....

People also claim that it’s an arcade racer - I don’t think that’s true. _childDocuments_.review: Take Forza 7 drop in Project Cars 2 mix with just a smidging of Need for Speed and you get Project Cars 3.I always loved Project Cars 1&2 but thought the messing around with settings for the force feedback wheels and actually setting my wheel up (I don't have it permanently fitted) was more trouble than it was worth half the time so it left me playing with my Xbox pad and my wireless dongle however playing with a pad the controls left a bit to be desired and usually had me then heading to Forza. With PC 3 tough it seems to me that the developers have spent time considering the controls for those who want to play on a pad and drop in for a quick race every now and again. Don't get me wrong it does play so much better with a wheel mine is the Logitech G920 but I now don't feel I have to look elsewhere if i'm going to play with my pad.Another thing is the VR I use a Oculus Go (not strictly designed for use with a PC but if you have a good graphics card and stable WiFi by using a cool little app called ALVR you can stream to it) PC1 was good and a novelty to play in VR, PC2 stepped it up a notch with the stability and graphics however PC3 has improved this once more.Basically if you want a racing game with a load of Tracks and Cars then look no further.However, and no I dont work for the developers, i would also recommend getting PC2 and Forza 7..CPB.
_childDocuments_.name: Project CARS 3

_childDocuments_.review: The mistake they made was not calling it something like "Project Cars: Simcade". This would have given them brand identity but not set unrealistic expectations. Then they would have been free to use Project Cars 3 for the next version of the Sim.As for the game we have here, I think it's fantastic and I'm really enjoying it for what it is. It's more like Forza Motorsport in design and ambition. In some ways better, in some ways not.I love the handling model which strikes a nice balance between arcade and sim. It still takes considerable skill to navigate some of these cars around the tracks at a swift pace, and the drifting is a lot of fun, if somewhat unrealistic. But I don't care. The reason we sit in front of a computer for hours pretending we are in a car, is to have fun right? A pretend steering wheel and pedals are still not the real thing!Don't get me wrong, I enjoy Assetto Corsa too but some people take simulations too seriously in my opinion.I'm only 6hrs in but I thoroughly recommend it for those that enjoy cars and driving.Forza needed some competition and now they have it.

_childDocuments_.review:
Project CARS 3 is the third instalment in the best-seller racing franchise that brings all the intense thrills, emotions and fun from the vibrant world of motor racing to vivid life as players undertake a whole new exciting career journey that sees them rise from weekend warrior to racing legend.

Also new to the franchise is a deeply engaging metagame that challenges players to race hard and earn in-game Credits with which to buy and own hundreds of cars from the world's most elite brands and race them all on dynamic and spectacular circuits around the globe featuring stunning all-weather, all-seasons conditions.

Race-won Credits and XP will also entice players to buy authentic performance upgrades and customisation options for their stable of exclusive cars, including wheels, tyres, body kits, rims, as well as personalisation options to create their own racing hero personas.

With a completely redesigned and unrivalled controller experience, an even more accurate and fun handling model, adjustable skill settings for every level of driver and every element of weather-affected races, Project CARS 3 is the biggest, most exciting and authentic evolution to the definitive racing franchise.

name: The Valiant
detailed_description: We are the brave, the Valiant, and the strength of our brotherhood will see us to victory in our quest. THE STORY Follow the story of Theoderich von Akenburg, a former crusader knight who, after becoming disillusioned with the cruelty of war, is called back into action by events set into motion 15 years ago when he and his former brother-in-arms, Ulrich von Grevel, stumble upon a fractured piece of an ancient artifact - the Rod of Aaron. A young monk named Malcom appears at Theoderich’s doorstep, bringing him news that the Rod contains power never meant for mortals, and Ulrich has become obsessed with finding the remaining pieces and unifying the rod, an event that could bring untold evil and suffering to the world. Theoderich takes on the quest of locating the remaining relics to keep them from Ulrich and begins a journey that will lead him across Europe and the Middle East. Throughout his journey, he’ll meet many other warriors that decide to rally to the cause, from the old, seasoned Reinhard von Kempten of the Teutonic Order to the ambitious young mercenary Grimhild Eidottr and her Raven Company, each joining for different reasons, but slowly forming bonds that will keep through the trials and tribulations to come. GAMEPLAY Squad-based RTS with a range of units, from tanky Swordsman to quick cavalry Select hero-squads and auxiliary squads across 15 exciting, hand-crafted Single Player missions, each with custom cinematics, narrated journals, difficulty levels, and more 5+ Hero Squads each with 3 different skill trees providing players with unique passive and active skills to choose from while leveling up their heroes Large array of weapons and armors to loot and equip throughout the campaign, each with their own stats and special skill options Combine hero skills and weapons/equipment for a huge selection of hero builds Play cooperative with friends in the 3-player “Last Man Standing” mode, where you face hordes of enemies and earn experience to level up your knights and unlock new skills and cosmetics Play competitively in multiple pvp game modes that support 1v1 and 2v2, with cosmetic meta-progression and special rewards for ranked play

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so you see that thumbs up? Well there are only two options here. Yes or no.So I hit thumbs up. But please read anyway.Overall the game is pretty good. NOT GREAT. _childDocuments_.review: After 4.1hrs, 4 campaign missions and a couple skirmishes for first impressions, I can say that The Valiant has a ton of things going for it, and I was enjoying myself and excited about the game while playing it. However, I think ultimately it lets down the player on some key elements to the point where I wouldn't recommend it over other RTS out there.First off, the good: story, narrative, voice acting, general style. This game's campaign is essential Dawn of War II except you play as a Knight Templar on a quest for Holy Relics, against your evil brother (sort of a Cain vs Abel situation). That, in my opinion, is pretty sick. I loved that. And the missions did well to bring that to life. Activated abilities on most units and heroes, as well as gear and leveling your heroes was awesome.Where the game struggles to compete with existing titles, is in the unit controls and strategy elements. Most units either sit back and shoot until they get charged at (archers) or charge into a mosh pit and you wait for them to finish clubbing (infantry). Cavalry feel good, but they don't seem as strong as infantry, which seems backwards.In principle, that sounds fine, but in practice I found myself waiting for a lot of fights to play out, knowing the conclusion. And I felt like I could put my units in general areas, but I could never be precise with where and how they moved, which is essential to me in an RTS, including squad based tactics RTS.Then there is army building and economy, which you spend very little of the game actually doing. I played a skirmish and the technology system feels very arbitrary (click square to allow you to do more of what you expect to do) and inorganic. Whereas, in a similar game like Ancestors Legacy that has very shallow base building, there is at least a visual and mechanical progression that makes the progress of the tech tree and production feel right. Also, I almost always felt like the army size was too small. This is perhaps fixed in late stages of the campaign, but skirmish can be won with like 5 squads against the AI. I want an army!I commend the developers for what they got right - and they got a lot right - but I think the missing parts are actually the ones that are critically important for putting hours into an RTS long term. I hope they do well with this game enough to give it another go and invest in those areas, because the concept is incredibly badass and the execution was *almost* there.Pros:-Great story-Great voice acting-Cool units, heroes-Great progression and gear system in the campaign-Excellent use of activated abilities on units-Fortitude/valour systems are great-Experienced no bugs (in 2022 this is a plus for new games, sadly)Cons:-Unit balancing seems off-Controls do not feel precise-Combat is unwieldy, often does not feel impactful-Little thought to the strategy element of composing an army, building up an army, map control, etc.-Main Menu UI looks ugly (just a pet peeve - in-game UI is excellent)I hope I worded this in a way that is both helpful to consumers and encouraging for the devs. I still have a lot I like about this and likely will play more, but I know most of my friends who still play RTS with me would be too disappointed with the mechanical issues to recommend this as a purchase.Thanks!

_childDocuments_.review: As there are not many noteworthy real-time strategy titles lately, I tend to jump onto any that look promising enough. For me,  seemed to be such a game, as its attempt to deliver more of a tactical, squad-based approach in a medieval setting caught my interest, reminding me of what  brilliantly brought thirteen years ago. Thirteen! And yet it was way better than this mess…That is a shame, especially since it has a solid premise, perhaps even decent foundations; however, none of that matters in the end, as it all falls flat. Its shortcomings, both big and small, undermine this experience tremendously, to the point it becomes tiresome to play—as if some of the aspects existed to frustrate the players on purpose. Any excitement I had at the beginning slowly faded away with each mission, either because the issues kept reoccurring or new ones hopped onto the scene.Let us start “mildly” with the narrative. Maybe strategies usually do not have enthralling stories, but they still make them enjoyable to follow, like in the abovementioned . Here, however, it tries to deliver an emotionally heavy plot about family disputes and comradery without making us care about the characters. Due to that, the spam of cutscenes or in-game dialogues feels forced down your throat, and skipping them would honestly not negatively influence your journey, perhaps the opposite.The plot focuses on the clash between two brothers over divine relics – ones that turn its wearers into the “dark side” – which is not imaginative, but it might work fine if it would make you bond with the characters. But that does not happen, and it relies on eye-roll-worthy medieval tropes that try to pretend that this is how people behaved during the thirteen-century crusades. You know, there is that honourable knight with pure intentions, the slightly mad yet reliable berserker or sassy warrioress, and their interactions happen the way you would imagine them. Sometimes, these are straight-up dumb, like your old guy getting excited about enemies fleeing away just so he would walk into their trap for the fifth time. And none of that is improved by the lack of facial animations, undermining those wanna-be emotional scenes.Nevertheless, let us move on to the gameplay, and oh boy, there are tons of stuff to scrutiny!At its core, it is a squad-based strategy focusing primarily on combat, so do not expect any base-building or anything else. Thus, the said squads are the pivotal point; there are heroic ones, based on the narrative’s characters, and regular soldiers. While all belong to some class – like swordsmen, spearmen, crossbowmen… you name it – only heroes can level up, gain active and passive skills, and equip gear. To provide an example, the old berserker can bond with other squads to increase their stats, or insult foes, making them ignore anyone but him.Now, that seems solid at first glance, right? Unfortunately, it all falls apart. While there is a fair amount of abilities, most of them serve as buffs or debuffs, making them feel the same in the long run. And that is not even the worst part! Since there are varied unit types that counter each other, it pretends that its rock-paper-scissor approach works; however, when you try to abide by its rules, it actually punishes rather than rewards you—at least on hard difficulty. How so? For instance, spearmen counter the cavalry as you would expect, but their performance against anyone else is underwhelming—due to that, they are not worthy of wasting a unit slot on them. Instead, you can use swordsmen’s knockdown ability to immobilise these annoying horseriders. The same applies to archers due to their pitifully low damage; it is better to recruit the swordsmen again to avoid being overwhelmed in melee encounters. Yet, when you switch to an easier difficulty, some of these classes start obliterating the others.Another problem would be artificial intelligence, which is just incredibly stupid, as it ignores the diversity of squads and happily throws anything at you, even if it means its imminent death. So, the game tries to make up for it by introducing elite units, which only have better stats. Moreover, the missions tend to end with a boss fight that has an enormous amount of health and fortitude, sometimes even separated into phases. Due to that, I often had to retreat and replenish my soldiers to be able to join the fray again, so each encounter like that might take me even fifteen minutes to complete. Dear developers, just because you meddle with stats like that does not make the game harder to play; you just unnecessarily prolong it, making a monotonous experience out of it. Simply put,  is horrendously unbalanced.And since the gameplay loop is always the same, I became more and more bored. There are no different, surprising situations that would change the pace. Instead, you go to an objective, kill a bunch of baddies… and that is it. For sure, one could simplify  loop like that, as well; yet, the varied weaponry made the squads diverse, the destructible environment allowed for exciting opportunities, and each mission tried to put you in a new situation, forcing you to adapt. Nothing like that works here. Most of the mechanics are just a fancy facade that makes it look good on the  but fails to deliver. One of those glaring examples would be sieges, in which you “encircle” the city with your six units and defend yourself from constant assaults until you build a trebuchet to make a hole in the walls to get inside. It looks unbelievably dumb, especially since it is not even possible to man walls and towers.Moreover, as if that would not be enough, there are numerous technical problems like weirdly placed checkpoints, so at times you have to replay over twenty minutes—there are no manual saves. Then, there is a pause prompt that, however, does not allow you to issue commands, so it is rather useless. And my “favourite” is when the number row keys stop working after cutscenes because the game sometimes tends to switch squads, so if your berserker suddenly went to no. 1 from no. 2, these two keys stop working until the next mission. Truly a pinnacle of design. I could name more atrocities like that, but I think you get me.Apart from the campaign, you can engage in skirmishes against the artificial intelligence or other players—if you manage to find some, as the player base is pretty much dead already. Then, there is also a wave defence mode, but I honestly only tried both for a bit because they do not offer anything else apart from more fighting, and I got tired of that from the campaign already…When I played  some years ago, I enjoyed both my solo playthrough, as well as the co-op one with my friend. Here, however, I feel exhausted just after my playthrough. Even if I slightly enjoyed it at times, the number of problems buried my enthusiasm to the ground quickly. Thus, I cannot recommend this title even during a sale in this current state.As I said before,  is just a fancy facade.

Where do I start?The game's premise and set up is good for anyone interested in the Crusades.The settings, the graphics, the clashing of small groups of fighters are all good.Unfortunately the developers have made some reaĺly ugly design decisions.The first two campaign missions are designed as tutorials and the difficulty cannot be changed until after them.Sadly those missions are terribly unbalanced with the difficulty feeling extreme at times.You only have two groups of fighters and groups of NPCs fighting along you that you can't control.There is no strategy involved here at all.All you have at your disposal is a buff that you spam every minute or so to keep your own two groups alive while countless enemies keep attacking you.It's completely random whether you will survive and finish the mission or die and have to retry 10 times.I don't know if the balance was ruined with the latest patch or not.I managed to finish the first mission after a lot of retrying and now I'm stuck at the second with the same exact issue.Unfortunately the game seems to be pretty much abandoned from the developers so one can not hope for fixes.I can't recommend this game at any price and it's shame as I really liked the setup.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm seriously torn on this one. So Ill list some factors and my thoughts on them. Upfront I should say I have a major passion for the medieval period, have spent most of my life involved with it through academia, work, and hobbies. And am a huge fan of RTS and RPG games, so should be really predisposed to love this game. Story: The story is quite nicely told. The characters are pretty well written, especially for an RTS. And it does a good job of walking the line between obvious fantastic elements, while still feeling grounded enough... at least initially. And when they get "silly" out there, i'm willing to just go with it as the storytelling for the most part manages to carry it. The contained "help the peasants" and "rescue the heir" type missions had a very cohesive atmosphere with the story and gameplay supporting each-other well. Overall big positive.  Sound;The voice acting is good, particularly the narration and leads. There are some ham accents here and there but it feels appropriate in this sort of story. Music is solid. And sound effects are functional and atmospheric. Positive. Visuals: Now I don't usually think graphics matter much in a good RTS or RPG as long as you can tell whats going on. I will say the units and levels are generally pretty nicely designed (though I have some issues with historical accuracy lol). Fighting animations are functional enough etc. On the other hand, the game has a lot of unit abilities. so the game often devolves into a mess of glowing circles and flashing lines, which I'll mention more later. So I'm split there. RPG mechanics: For the most part are fairly fun, with equipment choices and upgrade paths presenting some interesting decisions about how you want to use the characters. And it's genuinely fun to replay earlier missions you may have struggled with and totally dominate the enemy... until you try a harder difficulty. On the other hand there are a lot of very similar abilities so in a game without tactical pause, remembering exactly what each one does in the heat of the moment can be a REAL chore. And Im pretty confident the game is intended for you to do a bit of grinding here and there. I found myself stalling a few times where it just seemed like the difficulty suddenly jumped. That said: I'm sure a better player could go through without such cheese. More good than bad.Gameplay: Its VERY variable. Careful movement and unit placement are VERY important. As is the careful timing of unit abilities. But juggling all that, with the heroes many (often barely indistinguishable) abilities, is a ridiculous hassle without tactical pause. And the rock paper scissors mechanic is very strong. If you let your cavalry get charged by spear-men and you don't immediately extract them, they are dead. Now. When you are managing a small number of units/characters (such as the occasional more stealthy missions) that's a LOT of fun. You have the time to feel connected to the characters and carefully plan ability usage. And at the other end of the spectrum, the BIG battles where you can pour mercenaries into the field, you can get by more with traditional RTS style play and using your heroes more like regular units. The problem is the game often, particularly towards the end, wants you to micro 4+ heroes, and be dodging enemy boss AOE attacks, AND dealing with hoards of chaff with a small handful of troops that often cant be easily replaced. REALLY cant make up my mind tbh. Multiplayer: Frankly its been dead from the moment of release. I've not managed to get a single complete game. And from trying the skirmish with AI it just doesn't play very nicely in my opinion. I couldn't tell you what the problem is, it just feels janky. It might be because of the AI though, as it tends to favour a quite disorganised rush which while not difficult to defeat, does at times feel a bit mind numbing when they spam the unit to counter whatever unit you just used to defeat their previous spammed unit. Cosmetic unlocks: Not something the game needs but always a nice inclusion. And apparently the game has quite a WEALTH of cosmetic customisation options....  which you'll never get to see, because they are all locked behind multiplayer successes, and multiplayer is dead. And no skirmish doesn't count.  I'm not even sure if the cosmetic customisation effects single player. I'd assume it does as that options menu is available on the campaign map. But no way to unlock anything. :( Closing statement: If you enjoyed something like Ancestors Legacy, you'll probably find something to enjoy in the game but its a very different beast. In some ways it reminds me too much of Dawn of War 3, with its very MOBA-esque features. But that's a game I had to walk away in disgust, where I've actually had a lot of fun here... I'm just not sure if I should recommend it. The good stuff makes me desperately hope for a sequel. And I desperately hope a patch comes along or some passionate modder steps in, and makes some QOL tweaks. (I'm not generally one who favours it, but this game really does need either tactical pause, or a major overhaul of the character abilities). As the game is now, with no saviour patch or DLC in sight, its hard to recommend... but I do want to. In some ways its a real gem, but that MOBA frenetic but precise game-play just isn't fun here, and feels at odds with how fast units go down, and how much other RTS stuff you need to be focussing on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Valiant

_childDocuments_.review: The concept is really good, but at this stage it's extremely difficult to mange the sprawling amount of units and their multiple skills, across a map, without any option to slow or pause time (note: you can pause the game and move the camera but you can't issue orders or select skills). This type of game is much closer to Total War than it is to Total Annihilation, and as such, it absolutely needs more unit-management capabilities.   Without this, you end up with a sprawling mess of units and their skills. Keep in mind that the AI can make split second decisions around strategy for ALL their units, while you have to bumble through it the long way. There are missions which are extremely frustrating and just very messy because of this.  I have given up playing for the time being because I just can't enjoy it. If this is addressed then I might get back in to it.I don't think this game is worth the money they're asking for it - not in the current state - and after looking at what they're investing their time in on the patches, I am concerned that gameplay and replayability aren't prioritised. - which they should be for this $

_childDocuments_.review: Got a review copy as a Youtube Content Creator for this title before it came out, decided to try it. Regret wasting my time. Here's the pros and cons. There's a lot of cons but it does some things well.Pros:- Good Graphics and Music- Great Voice Acting, Really great job there to sell the story.- Solid story, until the last mission. I was engaged in it until that point where the entire game was ruined for me. The cinematics were well done too, granted low budget but you can see love and care taken.Cons:- Bad sound design. Can barely feel there's massive battles going on due to the lack of good weapon sounds.- Horrible ending twist, horrible gameplay too in the last mission.- Meaningless grindy missions and boss battles Feels like the developers decided to make as many things as frustrating as possible. So you get thrown against hordes upon hordes of enemies constantly, and bosses that have huge amounts of HP. The last boss is especially bad as your gear is removed. Dawn of War II had annoying bosses too but it also had a lot of tools for you to pulverize enemies.- Dead multiplayer from day one. As an RTS that seemed to have focused quite a bit on the MP barely having anyone to play against kills it.- Ridiculously overpriced. With a dead MP scene and dull campaign gameplay you might get around 15 hours so through the campaign, but then what? Go back through the awful grindy gameplay in challenge modes in campaign missions? No thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure: This was the first RTS-style game I ever played and I only played the single-player campaign, using the tactical pause from chapter 3 onwards.I bought this game on a whim, because I stumbled upon a cheap retail version (which included the soundtrack as a bonus) and it looked interesting. And personally I had quite a bit of fun with the game, so no regrets there at all.The story - while not being mind-blowing or anything -  is quite serviceable and nicely told. It ties together the overall 16 campaign chapters quite fittingly, leads you to various places and gives each mission a narrative background. The voice acting is really good, I was quite surprised by this. The voices fit their respective characters well and all actors really bring their roles to life. Speaking of characters: I liked those quite a bit. Of course I didn't expect to get to know all that much about them in a game like this, but at least they actually have some personality.The gameplay was enjoyable enough for me, though I can see how it might get boring if you're playing the game continuously (I finished 2 missions on a given day at most, sometimes with a break in-between, too). Also, admittedly the in-game tutorial didn't do the best job (for me) to teach me all the game mechanics. The tactical pause on the other hand was invaluable and also gave me the time I needed to figure things out on my own.Conclusion: To me The Valiant was a great 'introduction' to the RTS genre with a nice story, varied characters and pretty fun gameplay.Pros+ great voice acting+ good soundtrack+ interesting setting+ interesting characters+ varied environmentsNeutral| serviceable story (nothing you haven't seen, and it also gets a bit tacky)| gameplay was fun overall, but could have changed it up a bit more often, maybeCons- (none really, from my point of view)

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game thanks to a channel I regularly watch. It looked interesting. It appeared to me that this title took the concept of a "Hero" unit from Age of Empires 3 and really centered or focused on the "Hero unit development" and minimal focus on the Empire Development aspect of game play. It essentially looked like instead of worrying about building an empire you were more concerned with building up a bad ass military unit with your hero commander. It sounded hella fun.So I went and purchased the title and said alright let's give this a go.But this is where the title broke for me. I did multiple skirmish matches with 500 team influence. I tried out each of the commander units and set my opponents to beginner mode. I obviously made some skirmishes harder on myself because I set my opponent commander to someone that clearly had a "type" advantage. So obviously that was way harder. Even when I set my opponent to someone I should have a type advantage over I was clobbered.My most successful match was when I played as the cavalry unit leader. The user interface map looks similar to Age of Empires 3. A rounded map that takes no time to go to the other side. Little white dots to claim which end up being your gold and lumber mines the only 2 resources in the game. The matches ended up being a capture the flag type of deal of which there are 3 points to capture.The units earn experience but it seems like the level up is handed automatically there is really nothing to do here besides realize your unit is becoming stronger. Just how much stronger it became who knows, the UI doesn't really show clearly the differences. Researching tech or building upgrades to a building, is built into the UI in a minimally invasive way. While I can appreciate this, it sucked. It wasn't until about 35 minutes into my session that I even noticed little teeny buttons around the map circle are where you do your upgrades and that's because they have really no distinguishing features compared to the rest of the UI and who is really looking at the bottom right corner where the map circle is for a tiny button that doesn't stand out and only exists if you click on something that has some sort of upgrade.That same area is also where your units special abilities are as you guessed it tiny buttons that are indistinguishable from the rest of the UI.I never was good at Age of Empires Multiplayer because I get Zerg rushed 5 minutes by even the AI worse by human players. That why I used treaties for like 10 - 20 minutes of peace. Too hard, too confusing and you'll be zerg rushed quickly and for some reason the AI is really good at burning your influence but when you have all 3 bases it never seems to burn the ai influence all that quickly well not as quickly as the ai is able to burn away your influence.The game is a tug of war and unknowingly your opponent always seems to have tied the rope to a tree you can't see and exhausts you before you even realize it was tied to a tree.

_childDocuments_.review: The Valiant is a squad based Real-Time Strategy game set in medieval Central Europe and the Middle East by KITE Games, makers of Sudden Strike 4 . The story of Theoderich, a former crusader in his quest to stop his former brother-in-arms, Ulrich from acquiring all the pieces of the Rod of Aaron. An artifact that wields unspeakable powers that is not meant for mere mortals.At its core, The Valiant is an Action RTS that focuses on squad-based and management on the battlefield. There’s some base building elements but one that is very minor and not very in-depth. After the 2 prologue missions, you are given the choice to pick the squads that you will use in the following mission. The squads that are locked are the “Heroes” squad that are tied to the narrative of the mission. You can however choose the “Mercenary” squads to bring in (or not) starting off with Spearmen, Archers and Swordsmen with other units unlocked and available the more you progress. From the squad screen you can unlock skills for your Heroes which will aid in the battlefield. Here you are also able to equip them with items that you find in the mission areas that act as upgrades or a change in style and skills for your hero.Once you start a mission, there’s a set of objectives you have to do which will then feed you with more as you progress the mission. Apart from the first 2 missions which are very linear, subsequent missions give you more freedom for movement in which direction, or area you want to attack/progress to first. Around the maps, typically near areas of interest there will be some resources scattered for you to collect. Equipment that can be equipped to your heroes for subsequent missions can also be found on that map. The resources you pick up are used for building of defences which are limited to the distance from the “Workshop” that you’ll find/capture. The other resource you find (gold) can be used to make units when you capture/find “Replenishing Camps”, which also regenerates your squad’s Fortitude, Health and also the units that the squad may have lost. If you lost a whole squad (except heroes). You can spend the gold to buy another squad as a replacement.Visually The Valiant is a really good looking game, smoke billows when buildings crumble, embers fly/glow & fire slowly engulfs burning buildings. The audio is on par with high standard with the voice acting playing a major role delivering a predictable story (at times) but with such interest and meaningful way to make players care. Roughness does exist at certain parts, after when you use a squad’s ability on an enemy, your squad will stop attacking the enemy even though they are within arm’s reach. As pretty as the game is, when there’s a cutscene for dialogue within missions, up close the animations and models look iffy.For what it sets out to do, delivering an RTS focusing on Tactics and team abilities to turn the tide of the battle, without much emphasis on base building or the micromanaging that it requires, The Valiant does it respectably well. There’s indeed skill to the craft that is apparent here that is at the forefront, just don’t expect an in-depth RTS where a small mistake could crumble an empire as that’s not what it’s going for. The Valiant is a narrative driven RTS, requiring some skill and understanding in terms of managing tactics & abilities that doesn’t require prior understanding to experience and enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, so far, this is a "mixed" for me. - Rating as positive for reasons below.Review might change as I play it more. - If I play it more.This game is in its early release stage, so things may change since I put this review up.Pros: The story is pretty damn good, and honestly reminds me of Age of Empires II and how they told their campaign story with the storybook side of things. - Honestly, this pro alone seriously weighs against the cons listed below. Characters feel like characters, and not just vessels for a writers' political opinion, fantasy, or biased view as to how the setting was - Something that is VERY prevalent in many Medieval/Historical games these days.Combat is pretty easy to grasp, with a couple of "hon hon hon" moments when you nail enemies with a charge out of an ambush or decimate them with some sneaky tactic that actually comes together. It's very satisfying in many parts in the short-term.The whole Crusades area is criminally understaffed with good games. - And after this develops more, it has serious potential to go on to amazing things.CONS and IMPROVEMENTSBeyond the campaign setting and story style, there is not much that differentiates this from Ancestors Legacy or other Squad RTS's of a similar ilk. - If the Devs continue developing this and put further time into it, who knows what other quirks or mechanics they can come up with to spice things up.Animations for this are /okay/ - But the flaws in how they often fail to properly connect with one another. - The most obvious of this is the charging animations, watching how they collide with an enemy feels... Oddly unimpactful at times. It's either that the health/fortitude bars and icons are distracting me from properly seeing it all, or there is just not a lot of "OOMPH", which is more so seen when using abilities like Trample with horsemen.To add onto this, multi-unit fights feels like a bit fusterclucky - Frankly - You cannot brace your units against a charge, you must simply kite them, or use another activate ability to cancel it out, once the charging is done, it's a blob of active ability presses, and glitched out animations as they collide with one another. - If flanking is a thing, it's not particularly obvious if it has an effect beyond stacking your stats together.Overall diversity. - Again, this is an early game, but because this was released as a full game, I gotta judge it as a full game, which means that for a fully released game, Indie/AA or not, I cannot honestly foresee it's multiplayer holding up against similar games for long.The reason why I have stopped now, right before the 2 hour mark, is because I'm not particularly confident that once I complete the campaign, multiplayer will be as enjoyable, long lasting, and completely re-playable as I'm fantasising in my head. - Low budget games can have good charm and character to make up for other areas, but beyond the good story-line, I'm not sure there's a lot there.

_childDocuments_.review: The Valiant:~~~~~~~~~15 years have passed since Theoderich and his former crusader knight Ulrich stumbled across one of the three pieces of the Rod of Aaron artifact deep in the holy land. While Ulrich becomes consumed with finding the two other pieces of the Rod of Aaron, Theodorich decides to let down his weapons and step back from his soldier's life. That is until one night when he receives the visit of a monk explaining to him that the Rod of Aaron shouldn't be reassembled due to its incredible power and that Ulrich must be stopped before he acquires the other two pieces. So, Theoderich, with the help of a few trusted friends, will embark on a dangerous journey that will see them travelling across Medieval Europe to the Middle East in the Valiant!   The Valiant is a squat-based real-time strategy game developed by KITE Games and Published by THQ Nordic on the 20th of October 2022 on the Steam platform. The game consists of a superb campaign of 16 missions and two online game modes: PVP Battles with up to four players and The Last Man Standing, which is self-explanatory. After 20 hours of gameplay and falling just short of beating the game's last boss on the normal level of difficulty, let me tell you, this game is fabulous in all aspects. First, the story is well-structured, with excellent voice-over and cinematic book narration between the missions that will grab you from start to finish, making you feel part of the 13th-century atmosphere. The graphics are breathtaking, and the gameplay is challenging and highly addictive. As you start the campaign, you'll have a couple of heroes for selection, and of course, as you play Theoderic, he is always automatically selected. But as you make your way through the missions, you'll come across new characters who will join your party and will give you new units to select from before launching the next mission. In most missions, you'll control 5 or 6 units, including heroes, but on a few occasions, you'll be fighting your enemies with up to 10 units. Each mission will have tasks, such as taking over an enemy base, moving to a location or fending off an enemy attack. Early on in the campaign, you'll have a few tasks per mission, and the length of these missions will be around 30 to 45 minutes, but as you progress in the campaign, you'll get more tasks, and the length of the mission will grow to between 1 hour to 2 hours. You'll also have items to collect, which you can find around each map or when you defeat an enemy. Some enemies will drop an axe or a flask of Greek fire (fire bomb) that some of your units can pick up and use as an extra perk. At the end of each mission, your heroes will accumulate experience points and will be awarded a skill point each time they level up. And before the next mission, you can distribute these points on their respective skill trees, which are Defence, Offence And Utility. You can also equip your heroes with the new items that you found in the previous mission.As you know, the 13th Century warfare was somehow, shall we say, limited in terms of units. It was pretty much knights, swordsmen, spearmen, archers, crossbows and a couple of siege constructions such as trebuchets and catapults. Yes, you'll be using trebuchets and catapults during the campaign at some stage, but mostly it will be hand-to-hand fighting with archers or crossbows for support. Each unit, including heroes, will have three bars on its unit icon: fortitude, vigour and how many men for that specific unit. Fortitude is a unit's defensive strength and will be the first bar to decrease. The Vigour is the attack strength of a unit, and it will diminish fairly quickly if the unit is constantly in battle. It can be quite a struggle if you haven't acquired an enemy tent to regenerate your unit’s health or buy new units to compensate for the ones that have fallen in battle. The only unit you can revive is the heroes if they have fallen, but only another of your heroes can revive them. If all your heroes are down, it will be game over. It's a good game!In terms of replayability, you can definitely increase the difficulty to Hard in the campaign, and you'll feel the difference. But ultimately, the Multiplayer modes are probably your best bet. You can set your own game against the AI to get training before facing someone else online. I find the AI very decent and not easy to beat.Great graphics with a good soundtrack, voice-over and sound effects. I thoroughly enjoyed playing The Valiant, even though it was occasionally slow. Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Great graphics+	Singleplayer campaign with 16 missions to complete+	Great story with beautiful cinematic book narration and great voice over+	A couple of online modes which give great replayability+	Challenging and highly addictive gameplay+	Achievements and trading cardsNegatives:~~~~~~~~-	 The campaign is a bit slow here and there Help Theodorich to recover all three fragments of the Rod of Aaron artifact before his old brother-in-arms templar, Ulrich. The Valiant is an RTS not to miss.8/10 Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!
_childDocuments_.name: The Valiant

_childDocuments_.review: GOOD GAME THAT COULD HAVE BEEN A GREAT GAME !! The Valiant is a good squad-based RTS with a compelling campaign, superb graphics, and a wealth of modes to enjoy. However, it would have benefitted from a deeper base-building mechanic and a smoother difficulty curve at times. _childDocuments_.review: After all, I enjoyed the game and would rate it a 7 out of 10. However, from a gameplay perspective it's rather a 6 out of 10,  The addtional 1 you can add if you're into medieval stuff. For the gameplay, if you've ever played an RTS in your life, you will get along with the Valiant very well. It doesn't have base building, which I like very much and you can't build up a large army to just roll over your foes. All missions come with a unit limit and have limited resources to replenish units you've lost. For the hero units, they don't die unless you've at least one other hero unit to 'revive' them. The mission design however I see as the biggest downside. Though mission goals are always pretty clear, some missions tend to become unfair. Reason is, that before you start a mission, you are to choose your hero and army units. Depending on your choice, the mission can become hard or a piece of cake. That is because some unit types seem overpowered, such as bowmen/crossbowmen. So if you think your last cavalry unit can cut down a pest of 2 enemy crossbowmen units, you will be surprised. You need to balance your troops somewhat beforehand. In most of the missions you can heal your units in captured base camps. The biggest downside however is, that you can't save mission progress! Each mission does have some 'autosave' points but apart from that there is nothing. It happend that I had to replay some missions, because I couldn't save in between and my last hero unit died just short before the end/autosave trigger.  Apart from the mission design the game works well. Graphics are nice, sound as well, story also above average and I liked the different hero units you'll recruit as the game progresses. So, as above if you're into medieval times, like RTS and can oversee mission design flaws, your bucks are well spent, if on a sale. Next I will try Wartales.

_childDocuments_.review: storywise it is good but has some unnecessary or missing parts there are some pathfinding issues when you give attack order with more than 1 unit selected and if there is an obstacle between the target and them. in this case, if some of the units engage in combat, slow units left behind starts to go left and right or up and down around the obstacle like with their every move shortest route is changing so they cannot pick the right one. also sometimes units move slower than their normal speed. i mean while there is no combat. just moving from point A to point B.priests are PIA. they cannot fight but hard to kill and if there are multiple of them, you are doomed. especially during NG+ with their earlier appearance than normal gameplay. when you use them, they melt like but meet hot knife though.the game needs a gear counter during gameplay imo. as the missions get longer and the heat of combats rise, i forget how many gears can be collected and how many of them i collected.i agree with steam forums about not having a manual save function. i prefer to build up first before moving on. once i had progressed a lot in a mission and the game crashed and i had to start over from a checkpoint from 1 or 2 hours ago.i did not get the medal and xp system in general. units get xp for kills? or more medals mean more xp?it is also weird to see heroes speaking with their mouth not moving.even though everything i wrote are negative, i liked the game. i would give 6(maybe 7 if i push a little) out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review:
Follow the story of Theoderich von Akenburg, a former crusader knight who, after becoming disillusioned with the cruelty of war, is called back into action by events set into motion 15 years ago when he and his former brother-in-arms, Ulrich von Grevel, stumble upon a fractured piece of an ancient artifact - the Rod of Aaron.

A young monk named Malcom appears at Theoderich's doorstep, bringing him news that the Rod contains power never meant for mortals, and Ulrich has become obsessed with finding the remaining pieces and unifying the rod, an event that could bring untold evil and suffering to the world.

Embark on a journey of brotherhood and redemption in The Valiant, a squad-based RTS set in 13th Century Europe and the Middle East. Command and level-up your medieval knights as you fight through an epic SP campaign, then take your skills online in both cooperative and competitive MP modes.

Can you make it to Eden or will your destruction be imminent? Genre-Bending. Experience a blend of strategy and real-time action. Build your deck and fight through bullet hell as you make your way to Eden. Comprehensive Deckbuilding. Customize your deck and play style with 200+ spells and 100+ game-changing items. name: Heavy Rain
detailed_description: Winner of several awards, including 2011 BAFTA Game Awards for Best Story, Best Original Music and Technical Innovation, as well as multiple Interactive Achievement Awards and NAVGTR Awards, discover Heavy Rain, a game developed by Quantic Dream which brought new standards to narrative-driven games. HOW FAR WILL YOU GO TO SAVE SOMEONE YOU LOVE? Experience a gripping psychological thriller filled with innumerable twists and turns. Spanning four days of mystery and suspense, the hunt is on for a murderer known only as the Origami Killer - named after his macabre calling card of leaving behind folded paper shapes at crime scenes. Four characters, each following their own leads and with their own motives, must take part in a desperate attempt to prevent the killer from claiming a new victim. You need to think fast and act even faster, as every choice and move you make can result in dramatic, game-changing consequences – and even determine who lives… and who dies. How this story ends is entirely up to you. FOUR CHARACTERS, FOUR PERSPECTIVES The award-winning storyline puts you in control of four distinct characters who are each following their own leads in a desperate search for a missing person. ACCESSIBLE AND INTUITIVE CONTROLS Not limited by gaming conventions, the uncomplicated HUD keeps you deeply immersed in the storytelling and features controls for both gamepad and keyboard/mouse players. FULLY OPTIMIZED FOR PC The classic title is brought to PC with stunning visuals including 4K resolution and 60 fps framerate.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played this on the PS3 and really enjoyed it but after playing it again, I just enjoyed it but was reminded of it's faults though.First the story is great. You get to actually control the ending and if you play it straight as the game should the ending is really rewarding and exciting.Next the mehs, are the controls are can be janky with input being missed when you know 100% you got it right and some of the decisions are timed and can't see all the options in time due to the dumb rotating prompts.Now for the bad... but it's really for stupid people like me, achievement completionists...Cut scenes are unskippable! If you've played though the endings once or twice there is no way to play through the rest of the endings and skip the cut scenes you've seen already, including the credits, so you have to wait a couple minutes to 10+ to continue on with your next run to see all the endings.Overall the game is great and worth the time to play at least once but if you're wanting to get all the achievements prepare to be a bit frustrated with waiting to go through the same scenes you've seen many times before.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that I played Detroit: Become Human before playing Heavy Rain and I loved it but it was a bit strange going from a 2018 title to a 2010 title. Well then, just like Detroit: Become Human, this game is phenomenal. The music, the story, and the characters are all executed so well. Obviously, this game has worse graphics than Detroit and it reminds me a lot of GTA 4, but for 2010, it's pretty good. When it comes to the plot/story, man was it shocking on my first playthrough. It is A LOT DARKER than Detroit in my opinion, especially since its set in the current times (2010 back when the game was released) and everyone is human. Drugs, sex, prostitution, murder, torture, its all there. This does make the game more interesting and it really feels like a neo-noir movie that you can interact with and choose how the story goes. I'm not going to spoil anything so just go ahead and play this game because I had a lot of fun with it and it's damn near a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: [b1]Story[/b] Heavy Rain tells the Story Of Ethan Mars a man Who at one stage had it all. High paying job, loving family but after the unfortunate death of his son Jason Ethan get's sent down a path of depression. this is where the story of Heavy Rain starts two years after the accident that killed Ethan's son. The story of heavy Rain is great it has lot's of Twists and turns that keep you guessing up until the very end. You not only play as Ethan Mars but 3 Other interesting Protagonists that i won't give too much about. 10/10 Heavy rains visuals are abit of a mixed bag for me some of the environment look washed out where as the attention to detail on all of the face models are superb what must be taken into consideration is that this game originally a PS3 Exclusive before being ported to Ps4 in 2016 then was once again ported to PC in 2020 Most of the Graphics hold up in 2020 what doesn't are the pre rendered cut scenes that have not had a graphical overhaul since 2010. these cut scenes really take away from the otherwise awesome graphical experience.8/10If you buy heavy rain for the sole reason of gameplay then you are most definitely going to be disappointed as the majority of the gameplay revolves around Quick time events. Calling Heavy Rain a "Game" in the typical sense doesn't really play it justice this is more like an interactive Movie. 4/10Heavy rain is a must buy for fans of interactive dramas in the same vain as Telltales Games but for those looking solely for an interesting gameplay experience then you will be left feeling dissatisfied with the experience.8/10

And one might think "oH bAd GaMeR jUsT bLaMeS lAg wHeN sHoUld GiT gUd"- but this isn't that kind of situation. Lag literally killed me. _childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game, but it is not without its flaws. First thing to know: it is mostly an interactive movie consisting of QTEs and making choices. You play a father looking for his missing son, a private detective, a journalist / good samaritan, and an FBI agent.Secondly, this game is a console port and is actually an older game, so expect 10-year old graphics. Like other older games, it had trouble detecting my video card automatically and I had to manually select it (twice). This probably accounts for many of the performance complaints in other reviews, since this is a recurring problem mentioned on the forums. Remember to check that your video card is being used before giving up on the game!The good:- Engaging story, well-written and with good pacing- Voice acting is excellent (mostly)- Good graphics for its age, good audio and soundtrack- Choices make a difference, and can even result in the death of main charactersThe not so good:- A bit of lag and stutter, sometimes at the worst times, such as life and death QTEs (although I never lost a QTE due to lag)- Character movement is a bit janky and sluggish, which was annoying, and is made worse by changing camera angles that suddenly mean you are walking in the wrong direction; generally, the controls are not great in this gameOverall, this is a really strong game. My advice is to not think about it too deeply - if you look for holes, you are going to find them. This is a game where you should just go along for the ride and enjoy the thrill.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavy Rain

_childDocuments_.review: Memes aside, this game was very enjoyable, the story kept me very interested the whole time, the acting quality is all over the place (in an entertaining way) and the visuals are still shockingly good, and I wasn't even playing on the highest settings.As for the PC specifics, the system requirements are an overestimation, it ran very well for me, with only some light stutters, usually at the start of a scene, which stopped when pausing and letting the game load a bit more.I went in expecting the keyboard controls to be poor, but actually they're really fun to use and in tense moments using the mouse directions come very naturally. However, in scenes where you're controlling your character's movement, changing directions can be really unresponsive. But overall, keyboard and mouse is a very valid option for playing the game.Really great game, honestly ahead of its time in some aspects, definitely a game everyone should try at some point.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavy Rain

_childDocuments_.review: Great story game which manages to squeeze in all the lore cliches: -After losing a child, father becomes a broken man, separates from wife to life a downtrodden life in the slums, and suffers psychotic breaks. -An out of shape overweight (plus size) former cop, who is now a Private Eye, with health issues (asthma). -A young urban professional white FBI guy with an addiction problem-Big muscular black man, ex-con who hates cops, and has a few skeletons in his closet. (Not to mention he's got no issues killing cops) -A goatteed gruff detective who isn't afraid to cross the line, and does NOT play by the rules, and doesn't care about the truth. -A crazy old former doctor who lost his medical license but still likes to perform sick experiments -Sleazy latino with a thick accent, who owns a night club -Hot young journalist who isn't afraid to use her looks to her advantage, who has problems of her own-Elderly mother in hospital suffering from alzheimers, can't remember she had two kids not just one. The graphics in this game are pretty great. The music is emotionally engaging, and conveys a sense of urgency during the QTEs. The story is well written with the exception of a few plot holes. Characters are all believable and endearing, albeit, cliche (as previously mentioned). Not too crazy about the convoluted controls (a game that was ported over from / or designed for consoles, doesn't have a great control scheme - what a surprise!), and I'm not a big fan of QTEs, but they weren't TOO horrible.There were even a few scenes that almost made me tear up.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavy Rain

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that's supposedly all about choice and player interaction affecting the game's conclusion, this game falls apart real quick when you don't follow the one narrative path the game clearly has set out for you.Boring, uninteresting, HORRIBLY acted (the guy who voiced Scott Shelby deserves a Razzie for his abortion of a performance), and if a character's path concludes prematurely or winds up ending differently than the game's ideal ending, it's totally unsatisfying and the game all but forgets them. Characters can die prematurely and the game just acts like they never existed, the whole world just keeps rolling and no one seems to note their abscence.Avoid at all costs.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me get this out of the way. This game is not flawless. There are some plot holes, some weird out of place stuff that doesn't make much sense, and some of the characters are not nearly as fleshed out as others. These are the most notable issues.But DAMNIT. If this is not one of the most fun and exciting games I have ever played, then I truly do not know what is. The concept is really good and all the different settings they have you go through is so cool. The action is amazing and the combat is very fluid. The mystery part was great too. The big twist was something I did not see coming. The dark tone works really well and fits the setting and situation. This game is amazing if you just want a fun time and is also endlessly replayable. Just try it out and expect a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, interesting crime drama, loved it. Heavy Rain is an interactive choice based story game.  It looks better than 70% of the games that come out nowadays and it has a very good and interesting story. There are multiple endings and I think it's harder to get a good ending. People can die according to your choices and even the wrong people can be arrested for being the Origami killer... It's very important to pay attention to detail and choose wisely. This game is not for everyone, it requires patience, so I would 100%recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm going with a no for a number of reasons. Steam won't allow neutral, so here we areIt's a $30 price tag normally.  If it's $10 you might consider picking this up.  I got it in a Heavy Rain + Two souls +Beyond Human Bundle, and I'm yet to play the others.First the good: it's about a 10% LA Noire, with less intrigue and actual investigation.Music is good, feels like it was lifted right out of Silence of the Lambs.Writing is mostly good (bar the massive plot holes mentioned below)The bad:The entire game is one series of quicktime events. It feels like it's padded for one scene in particular -they didn't have enough story for Silence of the Lambs, but decided to copy every lazy trope possible, including the Niles Crane psychologist and the 'inexplicable a$$hole cop' from every bad tv showLoad times are terrible, yet each scene is tinyThe games play time depends mostly on bad controls clearly not optimised for PC.  Up is down, and down is also down.  The number of times my character walks the other way for no reason .... frustrating to say the leat.No way to escape the forced dirty camera.No ability to run at 120hzStruggles on high end PC, with unforgivable frame clipping (this is a game that relies on you being in the moment to enjoy...so it's destroyed)No way to escape cut scenes (or credits, while I'm writing this)Movement is like a robotInability to freelook is annoying as hellgraphics extremely dated and textures haven't been updateCutscenes weren't updated, and appear to be in 360p.  Not sure why natural graphics weren't used to replace this.Plot holes:Why the hell did a law-abiding citizen not turn in evidence to the police immediately?Claims that every choice matters - yet I'm pigeonholed into a linear story. There's no reason to interact with that loser on the balcony. Why force me to?"Please help me to my room"  - room is one metre away"oh no don't go to the hospital"  - no reason givenrandom drugs just stashed in a motel6 for plot purposes"My pants caught fire so i'm going to stop drop and roll into more fire."

_childDocuments_.review: This was the game I wanted to play for a very, very long time.I saw this game for the first time on youtube, it looked interesting, then I started doing some research about it. I learned that it was only playable on playstation 3, a fact which made me really sad, but the age of computers are here, and I can experience this game on my very own pc.Since I wanted to play this game so bad, I had extremely high expectations, as a result of years of waiting. Some of my expectations have been satisfied, but not all of them.First of all, the game:There are 4 main characters, but I really think that it's actually 3.5 (Maddison's Insomnia wasn't explained in the game thoroughly, that's why I didn't feel connected to her for the good part of the game.) They areScott Shelby, An Ex-Police officer now working as a private detective (Why he left wasn't explained in the game( or I wasn't able to understand)Ethan Mars who lost his son some years ago and lost his second son againNorman Jayden, who is a drug addict, but his addiction too wasn't explained in the gameand Madison Paige,who, as I said, was just too bland compared to the other characters.Ethan starts experiencing ptsd after losing his son, so much so that he starts losing his conscuisness and does *things* before regaining it. Losing your mind was so uninteresting and strange for him that he didn't even tell anything about it to his doctor. He divorces with his wife and starts to live alone. One day, while playing with his son at the park, he loses his mind again and goes *somewhere* with an origami in his hand, after running to park, he sees that his son isn't there. After this accident, he receives a package filled with origamis, a phone and a gun. The Origamı Killer orders him to do the things if he wants to save his only remaining son.As the game progresses, you eventually take control of Madison, who, is, unfortunately, a tomboy. She experiences a severe insomnia. About which, she only told (It seems that I can only sleep at motels.)After that, we never got another explanation about her problem. I wanted to talk about her because, as much as I wanted to know more about her, I never got anything. She is just a journalist with sleep disorder. That is all. Of course, she helps with the investigation and (if you choose ) starts a relationship with Etan. It was great to watch them hold hands but, who is she?  I wanted to know more.Scott Shelby. I unfortunately knew about the huge plot twist before finishing the game ( Read about it somewhere even before buying the game) so, I can't say that I was surprised. But, there were some holes about his actions. (trying to erase the fingerprints,killing the old guy with magic etc...) But I probably wouldn't understand it even if I hadn't knew about him.Norman Jayden is one of my favorite characters. His addiction too wasn't explained in the game (except for the game's ending I got, in which he was surrounded by digital tanks) He played the "Good Police" during the game. His relationship with his commander tho, was bad. There was no interesting dialogue taking place, and his commander was just a person full of ♥♥♥♥. He was the "Bad Police" for the sake of being the "Bad Police"Gameplay:It's garbage for my taste. Literally, mouse events are extremely clunky, there were many moments which I wasn't able to do something because I needed to move the mouse left or right. I did it, but %60 of the time, game didn't recognize it. I know I shouldn't have many expectations for an old ass ps3 game converted for pc gameplay but damn, it's pretty bad.About performance issues, I wasn't able to play the game longer than 10 minutes at first. I updated my drivers and launched the game with my main graphic driver "GTX 1050". If you play on a gaming laptop, you should launch the game with your strongest driver. Otherwise, it will freeze and be unplayable.Is it playable? Of course it is.Is it fun? Of course it is. I enjoyed this game so much. Wish I didn't recognize the Shelby guy tho. But it was fun and interesting anyway. You shouldn't have many expectations as this game isn't "Detroit: Become Human" the characters are not as deeply exlored and detailed as in Detroit. But they were okay. Story telling is pretty good for a game released in 2010.This was my review. My main language isn't english so if I have any errors, forgive them. TL:DRGood game, but characters aren't detailed enough.Bad Controls, Bad optimization, unplayable on laptop if you don't launch it with your strongest graphics card.Great storyteliing, and great atmosphere.8.5/10 Grandfather of Detroit.

_childDocuments_.review: The mouse controls are pretty unique, haven't played many games that have a system like it. Movement is a little on the buggy side and it can be a little frustrating trying to get your character to walk in a certain direction, especially if the camera changes whilst moving, it can be a bit of a hassle.I can't put into words how the story made me feel but I loved every second of this game and was constantly kept on my toes. I was fully immersed in the world and while a few things felt out of place here and there, I could definitely find myself replaying this for another ending without question.

_childDocuments_.review: Easy and engaging game. The people complaining about the controls and that it's unplayable on PC is 300,000% false. Due to the lack of players experiencing these types of games, that's why it receives negative reviews. It all depends on your quick reflexes to press the right button so you don't fail a stage. Unfortunately, many gamers expect to waste their money on skins or camos like Call of Duty, so that's why they complain. This game tests your reflexes, and it contains an incredible story. The cast, movement, and animation is something I'd consider unbelievable back in the early 2000's.I consider this game tremendously, and if you don't like it, it has nothing to do with the controls. I also recommend Detroit: Become human, which is made by the same developers. Nevertheless, this game is a massive 10/10, and if you say the controls are bad, then just like any fortnite player who never goes outside would say, GET GOOD LMAO!!!

_childDocuments_.review: True, this game is completely unplayable with default gamepad settings, but once you use gamepad community setting, it works perfectly.This port was released in 2019 and possibly received some graphics update because in 4K it looks just stunning. I wonder if it's using RTX because lighting, shading nad reflections are also great, although the game doesn't suppoort HDR. 5.1 sound let's you better immerse within the game, as the constant heavy rain sound is more palpable in 5.1.I started playing this game after completing Detroit and found the game controls very intuitive. Somebody here mentioned full blown QTE simulator and I agree (and love it) - plus all these environment interactions makes you fully immersed in this world.Great visuals and perfect music setting, tense atmosphere, full dimensional characters with their secrets, genius intriguing story line (and it's always raining, and it takes few chapters to figure out HUD's "mm" indication) and emotional load - all this attribute to the perfect game.Detroit was great, but this game is just so much much better. The mystery is not solved until the last chapters and the plot twis was shocking.When I completed the game I felt shaken to the core, took few minutes to recover. Then I heard inner voice saying "this is the best game I ever played in my life". Thank you David Cage.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavy Rain

_childDocuments_.review: Holy Cannoli. That was one of the best and most interesting games I've played. I'm still reeling. Just...wow.After some time to ruminate over this game, I have come to the conclusion that I will try and play it to completion. You can really see and feel the love that they put into this game with every second you play. The voice acting is great, the graphics are beautiful, the story is incredible, and the soundtrack is fantastic. A couple of notes, There are some things in this game I would fix or remove entirely. The first is the graphic nudity. Not only am I not a fan of nudity in general but it is so beyond out of nowhere that I am actually gobsmacked that it was in the game at all. The first time it happened I was so shocked I slammed my computer lid shut. There is no reason at all for this to be in the game, and I really wish that they would've put at least a warning or, even better, an option to toggle it off. On the same line of thought, though it wasn't graphic, I really wish they didn't decide to put in lengthy bathroom scenes in the game. I do not need to see characters pee in my video games. Luckily, these are avoidable. If you are also not a fan, avoid bathrooms and anything that might lead to a sexual interaction. Note 2: The story is great, but it is bloated with really stupid simple actions. Its ok to not have the player interact with everything. It didn't help that controller support was dodgy at best throughout my playthrough. You have to do more chores over the course of the game than you do in real life. Everything is an interaction, and while its unique and I enjoy some mundane tasks in the game, that shouldn't be half of the playthrough. Note 3: LET US RUN. PLEASE. The characters sometimes walk so slow its agonizing. Note 4: The loading screens were really uncomfortable. I never wanna look at someones face that close. Ever. I don't wanna count people's pores. Honestly though, that's really all that bothered me, and overall, they are really minuscule things. What a great game overall. I was sucked into the story and played it almost all at once. Only small control issues (I suspect those came from the port) which almost made me have a heart attack at some parts, and minor bugs were irritating on the technical side. It was a lot slower than it needed to be in some sections. Overall, I would give it a solid 7.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavy Rain

_childDocuments_.review: Heavy Rain is definitely not a game for everyone. In the end, Quantic Dreams started the era of Sony and Cinematic Walking Sims with their games on the PS3. You need patience, you need to be interested in a game that is more interactive movie than active gameplay, and you shouldn't be thirsty for action or positive reinforcement after every button press.At the end of the day, what you have here is a crime thriller as it is written in the book. You experience everything from the perspectives of the four protagonists and gradually build up an overall picture of the plot. Quantic Dreams proved with Heavy Rain and later Detroit: Become Human that they are still the grand masters of such games.So if you think that you'd like such an experience, this game is definitely worth the money. If you don't want to actively play such games as they bore you or just aren't your style, you should just watch a longplay on YouTube as the story is totally worth it, but unfortunately you can't make your own decisions as a viewer.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavy Rain

_childDocuments_.review: Heavy Rain This 2010 psychological thriller videogame contains a heavy narrative in which the atmosphere and the story play an important role. Decisions and results are a big part of the game because there are MULTIPLE endings. The last time I played this game was exactly a month ago, despite the short time that has elapsed, I'm already beginning to feel a little nostalgia for every outstanding aspect of this game. So I've decided to review it.ᴘʟᴀʏᴀʙɪʟɪᴛʏThis game doesn't stand out for its playability and even less on PC. The controls feel uncomfortable, especially the mouse when making a movement. Nevertheless, there are parts where you don't need incredible controls to feel the immersion at its best. Personally, the action / tension moments made me forget how bad the controls were.ᴡᴏʀʟᴅ ᴀɴᴅ ᴅᴇsɪɢɴThis game has a compelling atmosphere (sounds, landscape design, details). The only aspect that presents weak points is the voice acting and graphics as long as you compare it to new games. From my point of view, this game exceeded my expectations regarding the originality of the settings and character design. ʟᴏʀᴇ ᴀɴᴅ ʀᴇᴘʟᴀʏᴀʙɪʟɪᴛʏThe stories are very well connected and the characters come into contact at the right time. In addition, each character is very well developed, the story has an adequate length and produces an impact on the viewer over time. In terms of replayability, even though there are 17 endings available, the game is obviously straightforward and feels repetitive after the second game. In short, I would recommend this game to anyone who wants to enjoy an intriguing and very well told story. 82/100

_childDocuments_.review: The game is structured around a series of chapters, each of which focuses on a different character and advances the overall plot. The gameplay consists of a mix of exploration, puzzle-solving, and quick-time events, which require you to press buttons or move the mouse in time with on-screen prompts. ✔️What sets Heavy Rain apart from other games is its focus on story and character development. The game's plot is intricate and suspenseful, with plenty of twists and turns to keep you fully engaged. The characters are all well-written and compelling, and their struggles and motivations feel authentic and relatable. ✔️The game's visuals are impressive, with moody lighting and detailed environments that bring the rainy city to life. The sound design is also top-notch, with a haunting soundtrack and excellent voice acting that helps further immerse in the game's world. ✔️Overall, Heavy Rain is a must-play for fans of narrative-driven games. Its focus on story and character, combined with its atmospheric setting and engaging gameplay, make it a standout title that is well worth experiencing. While the game is not without its flaws, such as some clunky controls and pacing issues, its strengths far outweigh its weaknesses.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is fine and the graphic is still today good enough. But the game play mechanics is a disaster and the game offers way to little game play.The story is good as i said. The game maight even get a movie adaption with David Milch as writer. But thats pritty mutch it. To control your protagonist is like paying Alone in the dark from the 90s - when you are drunk! The speed is faster but the steering is not. And the camera angels also works like they did in the 90s. You can´t cirkle the view when you are walking like modern games.
