_childDocuments_.review: The character's directional controls made me feel nauseous, as if you were trying to move forward but the game would force you to turn around, even in missions where you would be forced to turn your head and miss interaction points. After resisting the game's directional system for 24 minutes,I surrendered - using the fastest possible way to complete the game: killing every character I controlled as much as possible. So, someone who really likes rain ended up completing the game "Heavy Rain" in the fastest possible time with the worst possible outcome - in the rain.I don't want the game's disgusting experience to make me hate rain.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavy Rain

_childDocuments_.review: Well I'm enjoying playing this after  Beyond: Two Souls which was great. My feelings on this are somewhat mixed. The graphics, storyline, immersiveness and sound are all awesome. There are a few things that let it down for me unfortunately. I'm playing on the easier setting (occasional adventure player) yet some of the key presses are so damn quick to come and, more importantly,. go. Some don't work at all or not very well - the key in the glove compartment scene after Ethan's drive down the motorway the wrong way for example but many others. Some of the key combinations are all done with the left hand and when you're on a PC playing with mouse and keyboard, it's really hard sometimes. Also if you don't succeed, there's no replay - it loads the next scene regardless. Without giving too much away for those who haven't yet played it, getting out of the ropes at the doctor's was excrutiatingly difficult. I've seen YouTube videos so I know what's *supposed* to happen but I couldn't even get off the table! My character got killed off! I managed to kill off the detective who was trying to help Ethan, got Ethan caputured and put in jail and the woman in the car, I couldn't release her or help her either so she died.Now whether or not any of those deaths were avoidable, I don't know. My guess is they all were and mostly as a result of ridiculously fast key presses for the easy setting! People don't all touch type or play on keyboards so much that they know where every key is without having to look and by then it's too late! Another frustrating thing about this game, as with Beyond: Two Souls and Detroit Become Human, is trying to move your character around in the direction you want him to go. Sometimes it's frustratingly and annoyingly difficult, at least for me but, having said all that, would I still recommend it? Too right, YES! Maybe you're a better player than me and you'll definitely love all the good things this game has to offer, including the bonuses at the end. There's a twist of plot at the end - well a couple actually - that you simply won't believe - I will say no more for fear of spoiling it. Just buy it and play it. :)But Devs, if you're reading this, PLEASE make the key presses slower for those playing on the easy game. It's really MUCH too difficult or if a key character dies, at least give a replay option, not from the start of the chapter because yes those are there but from the last checkpoint! Make the key presses easier for those playing with one hand (ie left hand) without expecting someone to hold down 2 keys with fingers and mash another key with another finger! SO damn difficult! OK guys, thank you for reading. Now go enjoy this game. I hope you will.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavy Rain

_childDocuments_.review: Finished first playthrough in around 9 hours, got to save shaun and all main characters alive.This game is like interactive movie where your decision will affect the story, many cutscene and expect to do plenty of QTE. You may find a little animation glitch, other than that there is no issue in performance.For best experience please do play in one sitting if possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavy Rain

_childDocuments_.review: The juxtaposition of a well realized bleak urban atmosphere with some stellar original music and well aged facial capture against this plot hole ridden mess, uncanny body movements and bananas QTE moments create this insanely enjoyable little mess. While the second half does pick up substantially, and it's definitely possible to enjoy the game earnestly, it will take a lot of endurance to not crack at the sheer number of silly things if you keep looking for them.I do think the game was very close to being something so much better than it ended up with some small changes to the script and pacing, which does make the shortcomings more frustrating. This, and the "non" gameplay makes this a middle to no recommendation if you can only take a game seriously.Now, if what you want is entertainment, do pick up Heavy Rain if you have never played it because boy this is a genuine clown show ride to remember. I understand that the developers might be disappointed that I laughed more than anything else, but at least know you kept me well entertained back in the PS3 days to platinum the game and get all endings, so that's worth something.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you feel like relieving yourself every time you hear sound of running water? Do you struggle to find bathroom every time it happens? Fear no more! _childDocuments_.review: Amazing game and story.I finished this game on PS3 a few years ago and I glad to have and play in it again.But I wold recommend to play using PS controller or better to use PS3, 'cause some actions, such as controller movements, are not enabled (xbox 360 controller doesn't support it) and play using mouse isn't convenient.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavy Rain

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I didn't feel invested in the story almost at all, it made little sense to me most of the time, especially when the acting and animations feel very disconnected from what should be happening (I understand that the game was originally released in 2010, but the acting is not connected with limitations of the technology and the animations could definitely be better, seeing games like Half-Life 2 with great facial animations had released 6 years prior to that). The game is an interactive drama, a movie that plays a little bit like a game. Unfortunately, it's not so good as a movie because of the problems mentioned, and it's not great as a game because there's little you can do to influence the story (your actions only influence 2-3 scenes and the ending, but not the story as a whole). There's one thing the game is good at, though, which is interactivity of the cutscenes and QTE, especially if you have a DS4 or a DualSense controller, the unusual combinations and positions + using sixaxis was fun and mostly the reason why I liked playing the game, but wouldn't recommend it to most people.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavy Rain

_childDocuments_.review: This is tough to recommend. Although the game is never boring, the story has so many plot holes. I do like my murder mysteries and this game has that along with a lot of tense adrenaline-fuelled moments. It's a shame that they had to change the direction of the story from what was originally intended.The control scheme is terrible where it felt like half the time it didn't recognise my right thumbstick inputs correctly. Also, the response doesn't feel right when the camera angle changes sharply whilst you move your character.The game has a lot of random freezes, sometimes crashing the game altogether. It's not unplayable but it seems silly the devs don't fix this sort of thing.If you can overlook these flaws then it's worth playing, but most won't have the patience for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is intriguing but the controls and the way they change with camera angles are AWFUL. I keep walking into weird things. _childDocuments_.review: Don't analyse this game's graphics, animation or voice acting. They're products of their time and when put into perspective actually kind of impressive. Some scenes can be quite ridiculous, even comical when you play them nowadays but when I played them it actually added to my liking of the game. It made me think it was very charming.What's more the game's story had me completely hooked up to the point where I was terrified to make bad choices or accidentally miss my buttons in the quick time events when it mattered. I was on the edge of my seat. This game is hard, guys, even on easy difficulty. I guess what would have made it a little easier to follow along would have been coloured indicators instead of white ones and arrows that show the direction more clearly. But I can't say I was annoyed by the added challenge. I always play games on easy because I underestimate my abilities but this time I considered maybe having made the wrong choice in the beginning ("...after all it's just quick time events..."). I couldn't have been more wrong. It all added to my being immersed in the game and sleeping and eating were secondary for the last two days. Don't worry. I survived ;)Highly recommend the game to people who don't mind playing older games or even love it. The characters and storyline are absolutely great and some scenes are outright funny. Since the story is very tragic (depending on how "well" you play), this proved to be quite refreshing at times.Thank you for this game. Can't wait for some new releases. Maybe next time I'll actually play your games once they release and not 13 years later or 5 years, like I did with DBH (though that game's truly timeless).Keep being awesome!Love,G

_childDocuments_.review: Still a good adventure game. It is mostly an interactive movie with action sequences (until my playing point at least). If you succed or not in the actions sequences the story seems to have turning points.  The story is quite solid, gripping like a good thriller. Character animations are stiil striking and emotional (on the downside, some characters like the protagonist, are a bit cliché but i suppose this doesn't affect much the narrative quality). The game can be played with keyboard + mouse but it's really thought to be played with a controller.   Be aware : the standard developer's controller mapping has bug : you won't be able to complete actions with the right stick. Make sure to download the community settings for the xbox controller. _childDocuments_.review: Reading a lot of the previous reviews about the game being a bad port and not working properly, I was a little hesitant to buy it on PC when I could just go back to my PS3 and play it. Let me tell you, it was so worth it to get it for PC instead. Personally, the game ran beautifully and I had no issues with crashes, white screens, or any other technical issues besides having to change some of the default official controller configuration settings for the game. If you happen to run into controller command issues as well, changing the right joystick dead zone shape in the controller config settings to "cross" instead of "circle" completely fixed the issue for me. Being able to re-experience one of my all-time favorite games at its full potential has been even better than I remember it being on my first playthrough. If you're on the fence of whether or not to get the PC version, go for it! It's well worth it, especially with a good sale!

_childDocuments_.review: Heavy Rain is one of the earlier installments of David Cage’s choose your own adventure/ interactive ‘movie’ like games. And it was a wild and thrilling ride especially taking off in the earlier chapters. While it may be more rough around the edges compared to his more recent work, it’s still an enjoyable ride and worth playing for anyone who is a fan of David Cage’s work.The story of Heavy Rain starts off slow introducing tragic events and exposition for the story and main cast. It manages to tell a tale that is both fresh and interesting, many games have tried to tell a similar tale but none have in this fashion. It’s full of twists and turns and dramatic reveals that will keep you on the edge of your seat. The main premise is explained early on, there is a killer on the loose known as the ‘Origami Killer’. Each character is involved in the journey to find and stop the Origami Killer, some more so than others. Since there are four playable characters all with a similar goal, naturally the story is split between four perspectives. This helps keep the story fresh and engaging as you see characters try to achieve the same goal but with different motives. I won’t say more about the details of the story as like any game it’s best to be experienced first handed and blind. Just be prepared for a thrilling ride that can leave you shocked from time to time. The characters Ethan, Scott, Jayden & Madison are all likeable and intertwined one way or another. These characters are enhanced by a surprisingly solid supporting cast. You will grow to love and hate certain characters that often change the way you approach a situation for better or worse. As a whole, the story and characters tell an exciting tale that I’ve never seen before: Heavy Rain is a unique experience that puts its own twists on the tale of catching a serial killer to make the story its own.While the story is treat, the hit to Heavy rains enjoyment factor lies here in the gameplay section. Like many other David Cage’s games the characters do almost every action starting with your input. In similar games like Telltale’s Walking Dead series or even Quantic Dreams very own Detroit: Become Human the gameplay keeps you engaged and is relatively unobtrusive. But in Heavy Rain, that is sadly not the case. Many times I have found myself ‘fighting’ with the game to complete an action. There is noticeably more ‘Swipe up to drink water’ than in similar games. It just seems overly tedious at times, and makes less dramatic moments a chore. The bright side of this control scheme is that more dramatic moments intensity is considerably enhanced with the control scheme. Instead of just normal QTEs it really feels like you’re controlling your character in the high intensity situations. So the interactivity of Heavy Rain has its ups and downs that help at times but bores you at others. Besides the interactive input for the game, the most horrible aspect has to be controlling the characters. This part has aged horribly, and basic things like walking without hitting objects that impede your movement is one of the hardest parts of Heavy Rain. Besides that, the gameplay consists of mostly watching the story which is thankfully entertaining to say the least. One last point in gameplay is the world you explore. There are many well crafted points of interest and objects to observe, it is fun to interact with various objects throughout.While the gameplay has not aged well, the visuals and sounds have mostly stood on their own surprisingly well. The visuals are not groundbreaking but they aren’t expected to be for a game released so long ago. The HD remaster has done Heavy Rain well in allowing it to create a believable and immersive world. There were certain scenes that looked stunning combined with good lighting and rain effects to create an amazing atmosphere. The soundtrack is also top notch, that helps bring out emotion to scenes, the songs perfectly complemented the theme shots were meant to give off. Tie the visuals and sound together and something magical happens with Heavy Rains presentation. I'm not entirely sure how to describe the feeling Heavy Rain gives off besides comparing it to a ‘Lifetime movie’ you might be able to catch on late night TV. As a show maybe it’s not the best standard to live up too, but as a game it manages to create a unique and wonderful feeling while playing. Despite its aged look, the atmosphere and cinematography come together to create the experience that is Heavy Rain. On the topic of aged, the voice acting is noticeably not...good. The delivery of lines were sometimes poor mixed with the sound quality of the voice actors, take back from the presentation of Heavy Rain.Heavy Rain tells a story that starts slow but quickly ignites, making you keep saying ‘one more chapter’ to see what is in store for you next. Despite its age it still manages to create a unique atmosphere paired with some really good looking set pieces. The only thing that will impact your enjoyment of Heavy Rain is its controls, some maybe deal with it better than others so be prepared. As a fan of the genre and previous David Cage games Heavy Rain is a no brainer to play and experience. Others with a similar view on these types of games should play past the ‘jank’ at times to experience this thrilling story.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "meh" rating because this game falls somewhere in between. It's not terrible, but it's not great either.The animations and facial expressions haven't aged well, though it's worth acknowledging their advanced nature at the time of the game's initial release. Unfortunately, the voice acting is subpar. Most characters lack emotion in their voices, and some American accents are genuinely terrible. Gameplay heavily relies on QTEs, which are generally fine but become overused, particularly in critical situations that can significantly alter the game's direction – a feature I didn't particularly enjoy.The overarching story, centered around hunting a serial killer, is intriguing, but it's marred by numerous plot holes and contradictions that detract from the overall experience. David Cage tends to overcomplicate things to create shock, but it only really creates frustration. While some moments in the game are genuinely exciting, they are often nullified, and as the game progresses, the plot becomes increasingly ridiculous. It feels like Cage had promising ideas initially but began cutting corners and content, resulting in a messy ending.Nevertheless, I found some enjoyment in the experience. At $8 for 8 hours of entertainment, it's a fair deal for a decent but flawed game. I would rate it a solid 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to admit, I am a bit of a sucker for Quantic Dream games. Ever since Fahrenheit I have fallen in love with their unique story-telling style and gameplay elements unique to their brand. After playing through this for the very first time, I am thrilled to report that Heavy Rain is every bit as good as Fahrenheit, in some aspects even better now packaged in a HD remastered coat which makes it look really good for a game that has quiet a few years beyond its belt now. The main aspect that I really liked about both Fahrenheit and Heavy Rain is how, unlike in some other, similar type of adventure videogames, the gameplay does very little in terms of impacting the story in a significant way (*cough* Telltale *cough*). Here, Quantic Dream once again makes you use your logical thinking as well as testing your reflexes and generally makes you do some mental work to actually obtain the best ending but then makes it worth it. Endings were always my personal gripe with many, otherwise decent, story-heavy games - some games have the perfect flow from the beginning all the way to the end but that is where it all goes downhill as if that is where the creativity of the writer(s) went right through the window. None of that is present in Heavy Rain - the game has its flaws, of course, but it will keep you glued to the edge of your seat until its conclusion where you'll see, whether the choices you made were for good or bad. Heavy Rain is a Quantic Dream must-play classic if you are even remotely interested in adventure choice-and-consequence games.+ Remastered graphics look really good, particularly the facial details in the loading screens+ Visual effects - the game is situated around the concept of rain that that is an aspect of the game that is done magnificently+ Masterful level design+ Dark, black-and-brown style, while disliked by many, actually fits the tone of the game perfectly and serves to amplify its somber atmosphere+ Story is written excellently, even if I wish that some parts were a bit more flashed out or some that out right do not make sense that should not unveil the way they do - like the  - more complaining about that part in the Negatives+ Very well fleshed out choice-and-consequence system that actually does impact the story and utilizes both dialogue-based decisions as well as gameplay actions in order to shape the direction of the story+ Voice acting is incredible - the voice actors really gave it their all, particularly the main cast. The motion capture also didn't age that poorly which only shows the quality of the work done+ Soundtrack, just like in Fahrenheit, perfectly enhances the experience- The PC control scheme, while mostly competent, can be problematic from time to time as it sometimes decides that it just won't react to what you are doing - I would probably recommend a controller, should you have one- The presentation of the  is fairly nonsensical  - Certain story inconsistencies and stupid tropes ( - these are luckily quite scarce- 60fps lock by default - that one is always annoying, particularly with the game being remastered and especially since removing the fps lock does not really break the game in any way (btw, if you want to do that just change the vsyncinterval and vsync values to zero and you should be good to go)

_childDocuments_.review: A compelling story line on first play through. Enjoyed the Film Noir vibes, and characters. Getting All Endings could be a bit tedious. Recommend a guide to limit over-exposure to some story beats.Selecting an adequate difficulty is important too. Having done some achievements on lowest difficulty for brevity, there is a notable difference from the hardest on my original play through. The difficulty can be changed at any time, so it is worth adjusting if you find it underwhelming from a challenge perspective.Movement controls, partnered with a camera angle that appears to be actively working against you at times show the game's age. Not a deal breaker though. But can be a detractor at times.I loved this game on PS3 during its original release, and found myself surprised by how much I could remember from it 10 years later. _childDocuments_.review: Video game stories are often seen as an accessory rather than a critical part of them. If you turn the dial back 30 years, video games didn’t even have a story. People will turn a blind eye when the tenth COD or Pokemon game has a frustratingly stupid or boring narrative. This indifference to bad writing is even present when it comes to games that make their main selling point their story. Heavy Rain has won numerous awards for its interactive narrative and “amazing” soundtrack whilst also receiving mass praise. And not only do I not understand the appeal, but this is possibly one of the worst games I’ve played this year.Let’s lead the discussion with that award-winning story. When you’ve played one David Cage game, you’ve somehow experienced the exact same story for all of them. I have only played 2 of his games so far and I’ve noticed way too many similarities with story beats. I know it’s the same writer, but it’s pretty rare for so many ideas to be recycled for different stories even to that. Because of this, so many minor points are so incredibly predictable. There were a few scenes that I guessed exactly what would happen next by assuming the most baffling outcome. The story follows four characters pursuing the same serial killer, the main one being the father of the current kidnapping victim. Somehow, a simple premise like this is flooded with plotholes, inconsistencies, and horrendous pacing. Numerous red herrings, like Ethan Mars’ countless origami creations, or a copycat killer getting away with it, get dropped. Combine that with the most incompetent police force that somehow treats a child serial killer with negligence petty theft wouldn’t receive. There were several times where I went “that’s not how x works”. Plus the fact that you can read the thoughts of all the player characters makes the major twist completely nonsensical, while also allowing for one character’s motivations to be 100% in conflict with their actions. Some of these are explained so poorly in cut content that it actually makes things worse. Ethan’s obsession with origami was originally meant to be explained by him having a psychic connection to the killer. Which is absurd for a game that is mostly grounded in real-world physics. Heavy Rain tells a good story if you never think about it. You will probably find your own examples of things that never get explained or baffling interpretations of the real world. Characters as a whole have peanut-sized brains with no logical deductions of their own. Not to mention how the narrative treats the singular female lead.That deserves its own paragraph. Madison Paige is one of the worst characters in fiction I’ve seen and I’m astounded that her portrayal isn’t met with more criticism with the portrayal of her. Every scene of her is overtly sexualized to an absurd degree. Her introductory scene opens with her taking a shower followed by a sexually charged breaking & entering nightmare that doesn’t even provide character-building. The writer’s barely disguised fetish is a very blatant trope present here. Another scene includes her stripping her clothes off and twerking to sexually gratify a drug dealer. Her character exists solely to please men and there is a very awkward forced romance between her and Ethan Mars. She decides to be with him after knowing him for less than 4 days. Her arc concludes with another example of quick-time-event sex, on the same day Ethan’s son is ABOUT TO DROWN. The gameplay, on the other hand, is barely worth criticizing because it’s clearly absent. Heavy Rain is one of those games that parade about how your choices matter when they don’t. You might’ve been under the false pretense like I was that there are 18 unique endings. The actuality is that each playable character has 3 or 5 endings tied to them with each ending having little to no impact on the other. Whether Norman lives to see the end doesn’t impact Ethan. Madison living only leaves you with a single cutscene showing that the forced romance came to fruition. The number of choices that determine these endings total to single digits. Meaning a whole lot of the choices you make will not matter in the slightest, even the ones you think would. And unless you consider quick-time events alone as gameplay, there’s nothing beyond that. Failing most of them also doesn’t matter, besides the predetermined few that do. The most interactive element is the few timed puzzles that have consequences for failing. But, I swear some of them were scripted with their time limits to be impossible to lose and a good portion of them you can just fail with no acknowledgment. For example, I failed to treat Ethan’s deadly burn wounds and broken rib only for the game to just fixed them for me off-screen. I also literally committed murder only to face no consequences. I find it very on the nose that Cage’s games start with “New Story” or “New Movie” instead of the traditional “New Game”. But of course, you shouldn’t play Heavy Rain again, it’s a one-time experience. Like how you never rewatch a show or movie or read a book again according to David Cage. Oh, and let’s not forget some of the most aggravating controls from the forced camera perspectives.For a “movie”, the presentation is terrible. While the graphics are certainly impressive for a 2010 game, I can’t say the same for every other facet of what makes a good presentation. Character models may look great, but the inhumane facial animation and monotone voice acting never make me believe these characters are real people. The main cast has pretty bad voice acting overall, but Scott Shelby’s is a very minor exception. Norman Jayden’s voice bothered me in particular because most of his speech is somewhat slurred. It’s very funny that half of the cast can’t decide on how to pronounce “origami”. The soundtrack is incredibly generic and I will not be listening to it outside of the game. It is very repetitive and I don’t remember any of the game’s tunes besides the main theme. Even if you want to play this game, you shouldn’t even buy this version. I’m unsure if this is the case with other versions, but the performance is absolutely god-awful as well. The load times would last for several minutes, the game would constantly stutter, and the game crashed a total of 3 times during my 10 hours of playtime. It was a frequent occurrence for background NPCs to just break by getting stuck on each other as well. Even if they someday patch all the bugs and performance issues away, which I very much doubt considering the port’s release date, the controls are still horrendous. Every Cage game seems to want to treat the mouse as a control stick, instead of transferring the inputs over to WASD or arrow keys. It feels incredibly awkward to perform basic actions at times because of how the game expects you to throttle your mouse around like a madman. Even if everything I’ve said about Heavy Rain hasn’t convinced you to not play it, at least do yourself a favor and play the game literally any other way. Heavy Rain doesn’t just tell a muddy story with plotholes galore, it’s also terribly optimized with barebones gameplay.  The only redeeming quality is that it ends and that your choices will sometimes matter. I have unfortunately made the promise to play the rest of David Cage’s games. And knowing how Omnikron and Beyond Two Souls are, it’s only downhill from here. Good god if there’s another shower scene or quick-time-event sex again. Heavy Rain doesn’t even redeem itself on the principle that it’s so bad that it’s good. It’s just boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 3.5/5Heavy Rain is a gripping narrative-driven experience that blurs the lines between video game and interactive movie. Set in a rain-soaked city, the game follows four characters intertwined by the hunt for a serial killer known as the Origami Killer. As players navigate through the story, their choices shape the outcome, leading to multiple endings and branching storylines.One of Heavy Rain's strongest suits is its storytelling. The plot is filled with twists and turns, keeping players engaged and eager to uncover the truth behind the Origami Killer. The characters are well-developed, each with their own motivations and flaws, adding depth to the narrative.Visually, Heavy Rain is stunning. The rain-soaked environments and moody atmosphere create a sense of tension and unease, perfectly complementing the game's dark themes. The motion capture technology used for character animations is impressive, adding a level of realism to the performances.However, Heavy Rain is not without its flaws. The gameplay can feel clunky at times, with awkward controls and quick-time events that occasionally disrupt the flow of the narrative. Some of the character interactions and dialogue choices also feel forced, pulling players out of the immersion.Additionally, while the multiple endings offer replay value, the choices leading to them can sometimes feel inconsequential, with certain plot points feeling predetermined regardless of the player's actions.In conclusion, Heavy Rain is a flawed yet compelling experience that offers a unique blend of storytelling and gameplay. Despite its shortcomings, it remains a memorable journey through a dark and rainy world, leaving players pondering the consequences of their choices long after the credits roll.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted to be a dad so badly that you would go to extreme lengths just to find your lost son? You can experience the next best thing with "Heavy Rain" - the ultimate finding son simulator!In this game, you will take on the role of a dad on a mission, and boy is it a doozy. You will have to search high and low, solving puzzles, making tough choices, and enduring some seriously awkward dialogue along the way. Hey, at least you will get to feel like a hero when you finally reunite with your offspring, right?Be warned, this game is not for the faint of heart. You will need to have nerves of steel and a stomach of iron to get through some of the more intense scenes.But all in all, the game is a gripping, emotional, and sometimes unintentionally hilarious ride that is well worth your time if you are in the market for a good finding son simulator. Grab your tissues, buckle up, and get ready for one wild ride!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh wow. I'm impressed. This is a game i really like. It's the third Quantic Dream game I played, starting with Fahrenheit which I ran through thrice, followed by Beyond Two Souls. They improved massively from Fahrenheit in terms of story, character depth, voice acting and quick time events (QTEs). They forgot to improve camera flow - sometimes the angle of the camera gets in the way so you can't see what kind of action can be performed. Well, you get used to it. QTEs in this game are done so incredibly right that I was sucked in immediately and my heart skipped some beats until the scene was back under control. But be warned - play it with a controller and know the buttons. If you can't recall all the buttons on your controller instantly and move the right stick at the same time, it's impossible to master the QTEs. You can adjust difficulty in the settings if it gets too hard. So, this game is definitely worth a second, even a third playthrough because "You decide who lives and who dies".

_childDocuments_.review: A gem, rough around the edges.Although I tried out Heavy Rain not long after it came out, I won't pull any punches since my expectations were equally crippled as how highly I thought of it.First off, the game has  different endings. Additionally, playing with multiple characters really stirs the twist of perma-death to a story driven game. You've got the unique feature that'll sell you on right here.Then, the story: unique and crafted to the quality of a must-experience. The characters are well written, and mostly involve a different type of experience when played. However, even though there are 18 different endings, the game sometimes left me with no choice to progress the story differently. It is understandable considering how much the game has to offer, but you may often question what you wanted to do vs what the game does for you.Now, the gameplay: as expected from a high budget narrative game, the game is filled with different types of interactions you can indulge in; more immersed when your controller supports motion controls. The game tries to capture the nature of the action as is, use multiple mechanics. I'd be lying if I didn't mention the "clunkiness" of old game controls, but even as someone highly annoyed by it - it was never anything that made me want to stop playing in my first playthrough.Lastly, the graphics: the game isn't much of a remaster, if at all, from the PS3 version. The character models look stunning in the loading screens, but lose their graphical luster in the gameplay and very much in the cutscenes - along with rest of the environment. There are some visual glitches, and some rough animations - but are scarce.If I didn't receive the best ending in my first playthrough, and the controls weren't so clunky, I'd would finish 1-2 more playthroughs. Regardless, a must play for the story; really reels up your emotions. Also, a steal for the port's pricetag.

_childDocuments_.review: Masterpiece, that's really the only word you need to describe it. Masterpiece. The visuals, the characters, the music, the story, the pacing.. and the twists. _childDocuments_.review: Playing this brought me back to my younger days on Playstation 3 when nearly everyone who played Heavy Rain thought it was the most amazing and graphically impressive game of its time. I was worried that being as old as it was, it would show but that isn't the case and I had a lot of fun and nostalgia playing it.The graphics, while already pretty good, have been enhanced for the port. Seemingly, it doesn't enhance everything because there are blatantly blurry textures in frequent places but it's easy to overlook it because of the game's atmosphere and stellar-looking character models.As for the story, it's rich and amazing and can change depending on many, many factors which also means it has multiple endings, which is no surprise coming from Quantic Dream. I won't talk about details though since it's definitely something you should experience on your own.Unfortunately, I did have a couple issues that I'd consider a big deal since it did interrupt my gameplay. Firstly, I had extreme lag during load screens which sometimes led to outright crashing. I fixed this by putting the game on my SSD (even though it still lagged at times, but stopped crashing). This is likely an issue with the game itself considering it was fine running from a crappy PS3 HDD back in the day. Despite the updated textures, nothing justifies it needing an SSD. Secondly, I had some QTEs that just would not register when it had to do with using the mouse. Thankfully this was rare and only happened twice and I managed to get through it, but it was frustrating. Another issue I had with QTEs was the one where you have to move the mouse slowly. I would do exactly that and yet still fail the many QTEs that required it so I think it was just implemented poorly or something. I'm sure all the QTE issues in general can be solved by using a controller, but the issues I had probably should've been fixed or tweaked and never were.

_childDocuments_.review: I am on my third play through of Heavy rain on different platforms since its launch years back and i still feel it's one of the best games ive ever played with it's superb story and decent acting from the cast, Playing heavy rain this time around using Reshade and the superdepth3D in vr using the quest 3.Playing Heavy rain is mind blowing in vr seeing the characters pop out of the screen.I do wish there were more games like this (Detroit etc are next on my list to be replayed in vr)Highly recommended if you like great story games!

_childDocuments_.review: Heavy Rain gets some flak for uncanny facial animations and awkward voice acting, which sure, it does suffer a little for, but it's a pretty incredible and innovative game. The game relies almost entirely on quick time events as the main gameplay, but does it in an intuitive way that almost feels natural, despite not having played QTE-heavy games before. I think this speaks to the thought that was put into this game from the developers and the level of care given to the game.The story starts fairly slow; there's an entirely-too-long sequence where you play as Ethan just schmoozing around his house, living it up, doing various mundane ♥♥♥♥♥. I will say that it illustrates the importance of exploring your surroundings and showing that not every action is going to be highlighted for you, but in my opinion, it drags on too long and this tutorial section could have easily been translated into another section.Once it picks up however, you're quickly put on an in-game timer of a handful of days to unmask the Origami Killer, and the stakes remain high for the rest of the game. You take control of four characters who are all tiptoeing around the same overarching storyline, and will occasionally cross paths in their pursuit of the truth. These sections were always interesting to see the thoughts and judgements from one character to another.There's plenty of choices to make here, and those choices will guide you down different paths leading to several different endings, so I think it's definitely a game you'll want to go through a couple of times and see what drastically different outcomes you can find.This game is definitely worth a visit, though I can see how the gameplay would not strike a chord with everyone who plays it, but in that case, I'd recommend watching a video of it, because the story is still a thrill and worth checking out. _childDocuments_.review: So, after playing Fahrenheit: Indigo Prophecy (again) I finally got around to playing Heavy Rain.The only thing I knew is, that the Game was a big deal on PS3, the Reviews were great and I wished I could play it myself (at the time). Oh, and also that it was an "Interactive Movie Type Game with Choices and QTE's".I was quite excited to play and even though the Game has some shortcomings it kept my attention.The Graphics hold up quite well, apart from some animations or facial expressions. It did enough to get me interested and in a mood for the Game.The Game with it's graphics, setpieces and story is reminiscent of the Movie Seven and maybe has a small sprinkle of Saw in there.In some parts the story didn't make too much sense but it was still enjoyable. Felt kind of gritty and if you don't know anything about the Game the hunt for a Serial Killer is quite intriguing. The Ending (which I won't spoil) was satisfying enough.In the beginning I had a few issues. So the controls are not really good. I'd say they are slightly better than in Fahrenheit, sometimes the movement feels really clunky.Also right at the start I had the issue that I couldn't sit on a couch (in the Game of course), so I had to research a little bit and change a tiny thing in the Steam Control Schemes for my XBox 1 Controller.After adjusting it read my Input(s) and I could move on. So don't let negative Reviews because of the controls deter you from playing this Game if you enjoy Interactive Movie Type QTE Games. There is a solution for almost everything if you take the time to look it up.What actually did kill my immersion sometimes was the Voice Acting. It ranged from cringeworthy to ok to good to bad to absolutely awful and funny in the wrong way.In my opinion especially the Main Character Ethan and the FBI Dude sounded pretty bad and amateurish for the most part. (Wonder why they got picked, because in Bonus Scenes, it said that they cast over 450 Actors.)If that doesn't bother you I'd say get it when it's on sale, you will have around 7-10 hours of enjoyment and you can probably replay it when a long time has passed after your first playthrough.Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: You always know a game is great when you finish it and you don't even know where you are.This is one of the greatest games ever made. It had me feeling a lot more things (mostly anxiety) than any other game that came out in 2020. I was on the edge of my seat most of the time and I was very determined to keep everyone alive as long as possible. This game is more than a game... it's an experience.It's not without it's faults though. The intro as Ethan Mars is slow paced and somewhat meme-like. The controls especially the camera ones were difficult to maneuver.  I couldn't even help my wife with the groceries. I felt like the biggest beta dad in the world. Even more than Caillou's dad. Anyways, after the tragic event happens and the game gets set into motion. Things quickly pick up and you're on your toes fighting for your life or doing mundane tasks. I found it really entertaining when I had to quick time a make-over, a sex scene and making scrambled eggs. Yeah know... it gets me thinking. Are there people controlling your every movements? When you fail, is it because they failed the quick-time action? Nah. Couldn't be. Still, the unsettling facial animations. The constant mini-stuttering during certain cutscenes. Audio issues, lapses in both sound and visual. Long awkward zoom in of faces as loading screens and some strange black screens that seems like the game crashed. It all can be a turn off for some. It's an older game and it shows. But, I powered through it and I don't hate it despite it's many flaws. I fully enjoyed this game. You're going to need patience as well as quick and active timing.Final Score: 7/10PS: I can't disinfect a wound for ♥♥♥♥. Don't ask me to do so.

_childDocuments_.review: is one of the Quantic Dream games which is an interactive multiple choice drama.The plot of the game tells the story of the Origami Master - the killer of boys, who has his own style. The main focus is on the story of a father who is trying to save his son from death. The father needs to pass 5 tests to get the address where his son is, because every day there is more and more precipitation due to which the boy can drown.There are 4 playable characters in the game - the boy's father, a private detective, a journalist and an FBI agent. Each of them tries to save the boy and find the killer. Each of them may die or not reach their destination. Most of the choices in the game affect some details of the plot. In this case, you need to think several times before making this or that choice.The gameplay in the game is not difficult. This is an interactive movie. We explore the location, which is linear, watch a lot of cutscenes and make choices or just answer or ask questions. At the same time, it is quite exciting and I want to see each new chapter of the game.Frankly, the graphics in the game are not very good. Although the game was released on PC in 2020, it is a port from the Playstation. The game looks dated, but that doesn't stop it from being great.The game takes approximately 8-10 hours for one playthrough. Since this is a game with many endings and various choices, it can take another 10-20 hours to complete.This is an amazing game with a very touching storyline. I advise everyone to pass it, even those who are not very fond of the genre of interactive cinema. Throughout the game, you will empathize with the heroes, learn all the new details of the crime and try to save the boy.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played a couple of Quantic Dream's other games and very much enjoyed those.  Their graphics quality has definitely gone up since Fahrenheit: Indigo Prophecy Remastered, but the story is definitely lacking compared to both Fahrenheit and Beyond Two Souls (their other games that I have played so far).Don't get me wrong - I thoroughly enjoyed playing this game about 80% of the time.  The story was enthralling and intense, the music behind each scene was perfect and really deepened the tension when it was supposed to.  Having spent half my life as a musician, I really pay attention to the score of a game or movie and it's great when it all flows together.  The graphics, again, great quality.  It has been so cool to me since I played Beyond Two Souls that the game characters can be made to look so life-like and using real people to base them off of.  The bonus features that showed how they did this were very interesting to watch.  The main problem I had with Heavy Rain was in the premise behind the story, when we get to the actual killer.  Without giving spoilers, I just want to accentuate the fact that the answer to the mystery just makes no sense whatsoever.  Even without being a big Crime TV/Game/Documentary fan like I am, one can see the lack of logic and reasoning going into their ending of this story.  It seems they just wanted to play out a huge twist without resolving a large amount of plot holes or explaining important events that were witnessed during the gameplay.  This game could have been filed under Masterpiece if they hadn't done such a poor job with the ending plot.On top of that, I did have lots of issues with controls at times - getting the character to go where I wanted.  But I personally have some medical issues with my hands/fingers and could probably attribute some of this to those issues.  Controls just seemed a bit clunky at certain times, specifically when thePOV changes while you are walking with a character, meaning you now have to switch the button for the direction you are trying to go if a turn comes.TL:DR As a whole game, it isn't bad at all and the experience was great. So, unless you have a problem with plot holes and an illogical/unreasonable ending, I definitely would recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bad game. Not a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game, not a terrible dumpster fire, just plain bad. The story is B-movie grade without the fun. The whodunit mystery is kinda fun but the details of the story and how we arrive at the conclusion often makes no sense. Why does Ethan keep leaving his hotel room unlocked? Who keeps restocking the hotel bathroom with prescription meds? Is Norman a rogue agent doing his own thing? Why are there sci-fi glasses? Why is Madison doing anything? It's a very strange collection of nonsensical details meant to move the plot forward without question. There are a few different conclusions to arrive at  based on story choices and performance, but they're mostly the same and the story is very on the rails. It's like a much more basic version of Supermassive Games' titles (Dark Pictures Anthology, Until Dawn, etc.) with more involved QTEs.The gameplay, while an interesting concept, is janky at times and unclear at others. Interacting with things using specific motions and button sequences is fun until you have 5 seconds to make a decision using a specific mouse movement and it doesn't read it correctly. My mouse shouldn't have to occasionally be moved off the desk just to make a downward movement - and oops, now a character has taken a hit to the head with a lead pipe. Another issue is that sometimes it's unclear what a QTE will do and with little time to make a decision, can lead to unintentional choices.The sound and graphics are fine. It's an older game so don't expect anything amazing, but it looks pretty good for its time and the music fits well. The voice acting however, is often stiff which can come off as comical at times.I don't recommend this game unless you're really curious like I was.

_childDocuments_.review: This has been on my radar for quite a while and never thought I’d ever play it with it seemingly being a PS exclusive, so I was rather surprised to see it pop up on Steam along with the other Quantic Dream games. This and all David Cage games seem to be rather divisive, but personally I lean more towards liking this title. I found Heavy Rain to be a really compelling experience the first time around with only a few questionable moments. The overarching theme of fatherhood and how far a father would go to save their children makes this rather unique thematically, and it left me with plenty of questions I hadn’t previously considered. Choices have a decent degree of impact and the game has plenty of different endings to explore, so it certainly has a good amount of replay value, taking me about 20 hours to see every ending and obtain every achievement. Replaying certain sequences after finding out who the killer was one of my favourite parts of the experience, making me have completely different feelings the second time around. The game also looks surprisingly solid despite being about ten years old, with the ARI sequences particularly holding up well, and the soundtrack has songs which are easily instant classics.The experience definitely isn’t perfect though:- The game starts off very questionably and very slow, with the entire Jason sequence setting up the plot honestly being laughable. While I empathized with the motivations and ideals of Ethan, significantly so as this did much to carry me through the experience, his writing was poor and his voice actor didn’t do a very good job unfortunately. - The side plot of Madison and Ethan’s relationship made very little sense to me, and resulted in quite possibly the most awkward sex scene I’ve ever seen in a video game, worse so since it requires quick time event interaction. - While I think the overall idea and personality of Madison is cool overall, I was made rather uncomfortable by how sexualized she was throughout the game. Apparently that feeling is what Cage intended, but it really added nothing to the experience and the character would have been better off if they reworked her to simply be a heroic non-sexualized character.- The movement controls can be kind of awkward. The QTE’s are really well done and I actually enjoyed doing them (Though a controller is certainly recommended here), but moving around felt like there was a short delay between moving the stick and the character’s movement which made it feel really sluggish. - The camera is irritating in a good few sequences, but I do think this is something you can get used to.Overall I definitely enjoyed my time with this game. I don’t think it’s as good as many people claim it to be, but I don’t think it’s nearly as terrible as others consider it to be. It’s a really solid narrative experience that, if you can look past its occasionally contrived and awkward moments, will likely leave a positive impression on you when the credits roll. 8/10.Beyond: Two Souls Review - Detroit: Become Human Review -

_childDocuments_.review: A fun story-based game where you play as four different characters. Their narratives intertwine as they investigate the mysterious Origami Killer, a serial killer who leaves origami figures at the scenes of his victims.The gameplay is all QTEs. I usually hate QTEs, but I found that it's not that bad here for some reason. Maybe it's because QTEs are usually immersion-breaking, but in this case the entire game is based around them, so it doesn't matter as much. Anyway, depending on how well you perform QTEs and choose dialogue options, you can get different outcomes, and if you really mess up, you can even get your characters killed off. The amount of endings and branching is really well done.Unfortunately, there are a few big negatives as well. For one, the story is not that good, and it has a lot of plot holes. I'm kind of used to bad stories from video games, but it's really jarring in this game due to the fact that the game is essentially an interactive story.Another big negative is that the voice acting is terrible, especially whatever voice actors they hired to voice the children. It really takes you out of the moment. The voice actor for Jayden sounds like a Swedish person trying to do a Boston accent.Criticism aside, the game is tense and fun. You really feel a sense of desperation as you scramble to push buttons on your controller, knowing that if you mess up, you might continue the story with one less character. In other games, you'd be greeted with a game over screen and have to start at your last checkpoint. But in Heavy Rain, actions have consequences.I guess in the end, there isn't much gameplay, and what gameplay there is isn't too hard. But it's an enjoyable game overall.

Not Quantic Dream's best in my opinion, but still one of the better narrative driven, choose your adventure, games I've played.

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest strength of Heavy Rain by far is its really tense, well-written story and atmosphere. It is heavily influenced by some of the darkest David Fincher movies like "Seven", as well as the "SAW" movies and Quantic Dream's own earlier work "Fahrenheit", which also had a quiet unsettling and gloomy atmosphere. In addition it was really pleasant to see some actually believable, convincing characters in  a video game, who on top were voiced excellently.Gameplaywise on the other hand, the game has very little to offer, but that is to be expected in this kind of game. The mechanics are narrowed down to simple QTEs for the most part, with only a few puzzles and simple investigation thrown in here and there. The game is practically holding your hand the whole time, but since it places its sole focus on the story anyway, that's perfectly fine.   Even though it is among the best titles in its respective genre, there are a few flaws that hold it back from being a truly great game. The biggest flaw, which in the end kind of ruined the whole experience for me is the stupid revelation of the killer at the end. Without spoiling anything, it comes of as really forced, illogical and confusing and there were a couple of critical plot holes that made the ending not fully comprehensible for both me and my wife, who played the game for the most part while i was watching and occasionally helping out. Helping her out from time to time was necessary, because not being a gamer, she really struggled with the controls sometimes and even I, who plays videogames practically on a daily basis, had some difficulties with the controls here or there because of some problematic camera angles and at times very poor feedback.  Another minor flaw of Heavy Rain is it's long-term motivation: Of course nobody expects hundreds of hours of playtime and dozens of playthroughs from an interactive movie/adventure game and surprisingly there is some limited replay value here due to the three different difficulty settings, multiple endings and manifold decisions and turns the story can take. Nevertheless, the killer stays the same and once you know who it is, the pay-off of multiple playthroughs withers away quickly. You may want to see how some decisions or scenes alter the ending, or try the game on a higher difficulty setting once more, but i wouldn't say that the story is so fascinating or multifaceted that you'd want to complete the game more than a second or maybe third time.The last gripe i had with this was the very poor quality of the pc-portation. The first few hours we experienced horrible framerates and so many crashes and freezes that we considered to stop playing the game. After looking up a fix online and some fiddeling around with the settings of my graphics card, any technical problem we had encountered was wiped away, but from a technical standpoint, this is a prime example of how not to port a console game to the pc and how lazy ports of even close to a decade old games can be. If it had one or two of the mentioned flaws less, Heavy Rain could have been a great game and maybe the best interactive movie ever made so far, but given its problems, it trips and stumbles right in front of the finish line. Nevertheless, if you are looking for a game that does not overwhelm you with complex and distracting gameplay mechanics and instead focuses on a well-written, tense story, gripping atmosphere and believable characters, I can recommend Heavy Rain without hesitation.__________________________________________________________________________HEAVY RAINGenre: Modern Adventure / Interactive MovieRelease: Q2 2019( ) 0/8 Simply one of the worst games ever made. _childDocuments_.review: Heavy Rain was somewhat of a groundbreaking interactive cinematic experience when it first came out on the PS3 back in 2010 and it still impresses today on PC. Although the genre has become saturated thanks to Telltale's range of games plus a few others from Quantic Dream; this is one where your choices can have a profound effect on the entire story. The game is a psychological thriller about a serial child murderer branded the 'Origami Killer' and there are 4 characters to play as you use these perspectives to unravel the mystery. With 17 endings on offer,  it really does impress in this regard and every choice you make could prove pivotal. Choices are certainly not an illusion here unlike in Telltale titles. This experience is about 8-9 hours long and is best played with a controller. Mechanics are satisfactory but can be a little frustrating at times with some cumbersome inputs, irritating QTE's and generally clunky movement. The story is the main star here and it should keep you intrigued right to the very end that you've crafted all by yourself.

I'm a girl boss and a cool girl! Not like the others" type of character. Do yourself a favor and get rid of her first possible chance if you decide to play this game. _childDocuments_.review: I have not even finished this game yet and I can say with absolute certainty that I will not recommend it.To begin with something good: The game has a very good story and soundtrack. And that's about it. The gameplay itself is a catastrophe. You cannot move the camera, controlling the characters is wonky as hell, QTEs are sometimes extremely difficult to even see (as are some dialoge/thought/action options), split screen is not only unnecessary, but also annoying and a lot of actions are even pointless and have no effect on the outcome of a specific storyline.I have nothing against strongly narrative driven and choice based games - quite the opposite. Detroit: Become Human, also developed by Quantic Dream, is my favorite game at this moment. And Heavy Rain could have been something I really enjoyed, but the gameplay is so bad that I actually thought about quitting it before reaching the end. A good story can't make up for bad gameplay and vice versa.Maybe Heavy Rain was something special when it first came out. But now, if you compare it to other Quantic Dream titles, or other games from this genre, all this game has to offer is a very good story. Without a good enough gameplay, this would do better as a movie than a game.Addendum:After now finishing the game I have to correct what I said about the story. The story is very good - up until the point the killer is revealed. This was such a let-down and so many plot holes suddenly appeared that I couldn't even enjoy the last chapters of the game. The identity of the killer is ridiculous, the motivation for his actions is superficial and cheap.I can't remember the last time I was so disappointed with a game, especially after playing Detroit and wanting to try other games by Quantic Dream. While Detroit is a masterpiece in its genre, Heavy Rain could not live up to the hype. But at least I'm very pleased with Quantic Dream and how much they have improved their gameplay over the years.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first hour or so of this game on a friend’s PS3 way back when it came out and I loved it, just not enough to buy a PS3 for one game. Of course when it came out on steam 10 years later I immediately jumped at the chance to add it to my wish list and wait for it to go on sale.So here we are 14 years after I started the game I have finally finally played it all the way through and I still love it.The game is all about the story, and the story is fantastic. I want to keep this review spoiler free as I think loses a lot on a second play through when you know what is coming. It excellently keeps you engaged through the twist and turns of the plot. There is a great sense of atmosphere. The choices you make really make you feel like part of the story, some decisions can have small changes but others have drastic effects of the end of the game. However when I said the game is fantastic, I mean it is fantastic if you don’t think about it too hard. If you just go with the flow of the story and see where it leads it is very entertaining but if you think about the ramifications of what is happening it is riddled with plot holes. Only the most incompetent police force would have failed to arrest this murderer and allow them to become a serial killer.The game looks good. The environments are detailed and the characters are mostly well animated. The voice acting is good and the music is not obtrusive but does its job. All of this helps you get drawn into the story.Most of the time the controls work really well and complement the tension of the story. However they are a bit janky on the PC which I think is almost inevitable when porting from gimmicky PlayStation Move controls. A couple of issues to note are the sections where you have to use A & D to look round to find things to interact with. It is really difficult to interact with items in the middle as the lightest press of A or D can send you looking off to the edges. The other notable problem is the lag between the camera changing and orientation of the direction controls to match. This frequently leads to getting stuck walking back and forth between 2 camera angles until you get used to waiting a moment when the camera changes.So all in all this was worth the wait and I can heartily recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Heavy Rain, the game that's all about finding Jason. Wait, sorry, I mean Heavy Rain, the game that's all about finding your missing son. But let's be real here, we're all just in it for the Jason memes and jokes. So get ready to dive into a world of rain, drama, and one very elusive kid.Heavy Rain's story follows four characters as they search for the Origami Killer, a serial murderer who targets young boys. One of these characters is Ethan Mars, a father whose son has gone missing. It's up to you to help Ethan navigate his way through the investigation and try to find his son before it's too late.The gameplay in Heavy Rain revolves around making choices and quick-time events. Your decisions can have a huge impact on the story and ultimately determine the fate of your characters. The quick-time events can be intense and nerve-wracking, but they also add to the overall tension and drama of the game.The graphics in Heavy Rain are stunning, with realistic character models and environments. The sound design is also top-notch, with a haunting soundtrack that adds to the game's overall atmosphere.In conclusion, Heavy Rain is a thrilling adventure game that will have you on the edge of your seat. And let's not forget, it's also a game that's filled with Jason memes and jokes. So if you're in the mood for some deadpan humor and a great story, be sure to give Heavy Rain a try. Just don't forget to keep an eye out for Jason!

The story is so damn BORING; it's slower than a damn dirge. It's not exciting, it's not involving, it's clunky as ♥♥♥♥, the characters look like they were just waxed or polished, they're so damn shiny - and overall, the game is about as interesting as a paint drying. I feel bad being mean, perhaps the game will pick up and become more enjoyable; but I just find it mind-boggling that it's such a slow and monotonous drag to play. My advise; if you're a die hard fan of the company that made it - get it on sale and then strap in for the longest opening sequence of your gaming history, otherwise? _childDocuments_.review: While it certainly deserves credit for its influence on narrative adventure games (paving the way for such milestones as The Walking Dead and Life is Strange), Heavy Rain’s own narrative is way too messy to warrant a recommendation. Quantic Dream catalog is said to be more inspired by movies rather than other games, and while Heavy Rain’s atmosphere and themes may remind high-brow moody thrillers, they are presented with all the logic and subtlety of a dumb, loud blockbuster.It really is the kind of story that falls apart the moment you start to think about it. There’s an important plotline with supernatural elements which is responsible for half of our hero’s predicament, but apparently they abandoned it during development, so it just stops halfway through, never to be addressed again. The big whodunnit reveal is bold in theory and can be quite unexpected for some, but it achieves such a feat by effectively "narrative cheating" (trying to insert an unreliable narrator into what all conventional logic dictates to be unfiltered and safe), so one might easily feel straight up lied to rather than properly misdirected.It also doesn’t seem like the story understands the basic narrative tool of contrast – as in, to make sad or dark stuff carry weight, you need to include some non-sad and non-dark stuff as well. The very first sequence, with its somber music and various camera angles, makes the scene of a man waking up in a sunlit bedroom look like the most melancholic thing in the world… except those are supposed to be the happy times; nothing bad has happened to him yet. And when, surely enough, bad things start to happen, you can be sure there’ll be no sunshine or reprieve until you get a good ending.Just like there’s no "happy" to highlight the "sad", there’s barely any "slow" to highlight the "fast". It’s interesting to compare it with the aforementioned TWD/LiS, because both of those games have an abundance of slow moments and use them to great effect, lowering your guard before the next round of drama hits the fan. Heavy Rain, in contrast, wants to run full speed ahead all the time, as if terrified that you might lose interest.A lot of the scenes, no matter how unassumingly they start, quickly turn into a chase sequence or an over-the-top fight to the death. The rare "breathers" also insist on keeping you on a timer, usually throwing in some interrupting plot development to remind that leisurely exploration of environments is not expected. Even the filler in this game is frenetic: there are set pieces (like the crazy doctor’s basement or the apartment assault dream) that add almost nothing to the story but are still choke-full of choreographed QTE bonanza.There’s a very telling scene where a character whispers the killer’s name to one of the mains, and she looks all shocked… but once we also learn the name a bit later, we realize she had no reason to, because she’d never even heard about that person before.  could’ve been shocked in her place, so the narrative just awkwardly mirrors this reaction, despite that for her personally it doesn’t make any sense. The rest of the story unfolds in a similar way, always concerned with immediate impressions without much regard for logic or consistency. Now, if you’re not bothered by such things, then Heavy Rain might be worth a shot, but for everyone else it's likely to become a rather unconvincing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Heavy Rain is a hilarious adventure game made by our era's greatest comedy writer, David Cage. The game tells the story of four random idiots who, for various reasons, find themselves on the trail of the Origami Killer, sometimes known as the "Arrigami Killer", and the "Origarmi Killer". I have to admit that it's a bit of a ballsy choice to make a comedic story surrounding a murderer who drowns small children in storm drains. But David Cage went there. Where is "there"? I don't know, but it's the place where David Cage went. Heavy Rain takes place in some nondescript American city that has been invaded by French-Canadians who have all adopted English names and have started pretending they're Americans. Why is this? Because you don't understand the comic genius of David Cage! The story of the game is primarily driven by Quick Time Events. However, I recommend failing all of them on purpose so you can see David Cage's true vision come to life.There are few words that can describe the comedic masterpiece that is Heavy Rain. I can only tell you that you need to experience it for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, Heavy Rain. Brought to you by your favorite French weirdo, it’s Quantic Dream’s third game and perhaps the most important of their output.Designed as a PS3 exclusive, it got an insane amount of hype back then. The character models and animation work were quite something for the time. This here PC version is a port of the PS4 remaster and it’s quite good. It runs at 4k, 60hz, textures were cleaned up and a couple of new graphical effects were added. A game-breaking bug related to controller input is still present, but a custom Steam Input config fixes it. That aside, it’s a pretty good remaster.As for the game itself – first, let me get one thing out of the way: this is an  as David Cage puts it. To me, there’s nothing wrong with that. It’s one of the many ways to use the video game medium to tell a story. It’s more or less a modern version of adventure games of old, with less puzzles and more cutscenes.The entire gameplay revolves around QTEs with a tiny bit of exploration and simple puzzle-solving here and there. Depending on which QTE you succeeded or failed and the choices you made, the story will branch out. It’s probably Heavy Rain’s strongest selling point.While I won’t spoil anything about the story, I’ll say this: it has a very strong setup, but the payoff falls flat. The writing is all over the place, characters motivations are inconsistent at best, the voice acting can be very weird at times and the list goes on. It’s a glorious mess that amounts to a game that wants to be serious and dramatic, yet ends up being hilarious instead. Hence the many, many memes that spawned from it.While Heavy Rain can certainly feel pretentious I think it’s still an interesting game that I do believe is worth experiencing for yourself. It’s basically a TV show where you get to choose what happens next. I’d say it’s worth a try, though not at full price – it’s relatively short, and not everybody will want to replay the game to see the different outcomes and endings it has to offer. One word of advice: don’t aim for a specific ending or outcome for your first playthrough and stick by your choices. It’ll make the story more impactful, and I believe it’s the intended experience. Consider this review as “neutral” - I can’t really recommend it, but I did enjoy replaying it in 2024 and perhaps you will too.

THE STORY, DUDE! No spoilers here, but it is thrilling, characters are kinda likeable and believable, they have their humanly faults. It's a dirty, depressing, immersive world and damn... THE RAIN, so much RAIN (Heavy RAIN). It's a world to get lost in. Well... if you can manage that in not really well aged GFXs ^^One big minus for me were the controls. I have a XBox One controller. It needed a little fix in the steam controller settings, before it worked accurate. What stayed tho were very shaky, very hectic, spinning overlays, which tell you what buttons to press and how. I get it: in some situations the player should feel stressed and pressured. All good! But sometimes these quicktime events were too sensitive. I lost some of them here and there and since failure will be punished by this masterpiece of a game, it can be frustrating. I even killed one character off, just because of bad controls. Because yes, dear fellow players... you CAN perma die in this! ;) But Heavy Rains flaws almost doesn't matter: the game comes out beeing awesome anyhow. Only a few movies reach this quality of a story. But this is a story you can even influence.I definitely will check out more from Quantic Dreams. Next will be Beyong Two Souls and Detroit: Become Human. Than with better graphics and maybe even improvements to the controls?Btw, I really took my time in this. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 7/10. It's not life changing, but it's fine.Full Review:At this point in time, I think everyone knows what they're getting into when they play a Quantic Dream game. And that is, essentially, a 10 hour visual novel peppered with quick time events. So keep these expectations in line if you decide to play it. It's very much a "Press X to continue the story," type of game. While I don't think it's amazing, I see charm in the flaws of the game. That is, some predictable cliches in the story as well as the often subpar voice acting. Certain flaws are less lovable; the controls can be absolutely atrocious, to the point I was certain a character was going to die because I was stuck in a corner. Luckily, you can change the fixed camera angle and I was able to escape the dreaded corner, but there were too many of these instances to not leave a sour taste in my mouth.To reiterate, you can only perform actions on objects when your character is standing directly in front of them. But the action of walking is ambiguously restricted at times. Time and again I would be frustratingly spinning around in circles just to line up with something. And yes, I played this on Mouse and Keyboard, perhaps not the best choice. But this is such a simple thing, I would think it could understand 90 degree rotations.As I've said, story felt a bit cliche, or otherwise campy at times. Just padding the time of the game for a bit too long without progressing. And then in the last couple hours, everything progresses and ends rather abruptly. If it wasn't for the game telling the amount of rain that's fallen, I might have been guessing as to when the end was actually going to come. And I'd be lying if I said the characters were complex. For the most part they are generally flat with little development or even choices to make them develop. But even if they did allow you these choices, I wouldn't have felt compelled to do so, because it doesn't often put you in a position where your personal morals or established beliefs are challenged (There are one or two instances, yes, I admit).Still, the story does just enough to keep you interested and make you want to finish it just to see how it ends. Heavy Rain is the equivalent of a good slasher film. Mostly predictable with maybe a couple surprise twists, but ultimately entertaining BECAUSE of the poor acting and tense action scenes, in spite of other numerous flaws. Only in the last hour or so was I beginning to tap my foot impatiently and wonder when it was going to end so I could move on to something else. So it barely left without overstaying its welcome.For these reasons, I give it a 7.0/10. A decently entertaining narrative held back by it's lack of boldness and poor controls. Maybe 12 years ago it was revolutionary, but it hasn't aged all too well. I wouldn't pay $20 for it, but if it's on sale, pick it up for a couple bucks and enjoy it over a weekend. It's not life changing, but it's fine.
