_childDocuments_.review: It’s been a while since I’ve first played Heavy Rain, then exclusive to Playstation 3. It has been a somewhat controversial game, with some praising what it attempted to do, some criticizing what it actually achieved, some doing both. I was mostly doing the latter, as it has been a valiant attempt from Quantic Dream to do what they wanted, but at the same time a pretty poor game most of the time. Now, years later, the game is available on PC and that is the version I’ve decided to play. It’s been… interesting.In case you are not familiar with Heavy Rain, or the types of games Quantic Dream have been making since Fahrenheit/Indigo Prophecy, this is an “interactive drama”, a story-driven adventure game leaning very heavily into “cinematic” events and QTEs. The game is divided into chapters and those can be viewed as completely separate scenes, connected by the overall narrative, but otherwise working mostly independently, unless the scene involves some sort of consequences for your past choices. Most of their games, this included, feature multiple playable protagonists, all of whom are somehow tied in the main story but approach it from different angles. And additionally the game has very few straight up “fail states”, continuing from a failure or even a death of one of the characters, instead of leading to a “game over”.The plot of this particular title is centered around the Origami Killer, who kidnaps and kills children with rainwater. The son of one of the main characters is kidnapped, setting off the plot, and several characters get involved in the investigation. And, as I felt with when I originally played the game, the beginning of this game is one of the worst parts to get through. It is so incredibly stupid that going through it again I felt shame for playing the game. The whole “Press X to Jason” has become a meme immediately after the game release, and for a good reason. And replaying that section only makes it look even more dumb.However, as the game continues, it often times becomes pretty solid. There are countless great moments, really good character scenes, tense scenarios to go through. They almost always follow up those with the game falling flat on its face, of course, but many chapters or at least parts of chapters in the game are very good. Sadly, even if they didn’t get mixed with silly parts, it wouldn’t prevent them from feeling completely disjointed. Because the game simply feels like a collection of “cool” (and silly) scenes, that do have this overarching story, but more often than not it feels tacked on. As if the story was written as a series of “wouldn’t it be cool if…” ideas that got glued together, rather than something cohesive.And in addition to that, the gameplay is just terrible. Even if you’re less annoyed at QTEs than I tend to be, the game is consistently bad with explaining what your motion or action might actually do. You just see the button prompt over some vague direction, press/hold/mash it and then something happens. Sometimes it’s something undesirable, that you didn’t even predict the game would do. Sometimes it’s just not obvious.I’m also surprised that even though the controls were switched from the original more tank-like concept where you “drove” the characters forward and steered them left and right to the more common 2D controls, where the camera angle defines the movement directions, it still feels horrible. There are numerous moments where the characters Yogi Bear around like idiots as you’re trying to make them get to the spot you need them to be at.Overall, it’s very hard to recommend Heavy Rain. It has some good moments, but those are not worth going through all the rest of the game to get to. Especially since it’s not a game that is fun to actually play. Even the most interesting investigative bits with agent Nahman Jayden EfBeeAi are pretty simple and linear and not worth the effort. As an additional oddity, the PC version of the game (and PS4 port, it seems) completely lack the only DLC the original title has ever received – the Taxidermist DLC, making it far less of a definitive release than it could’ve been. Not like I would’ve recommended it anyway, but it’s still a weird decision. So yeah, even 11 years later, Heavy Rain is… interesting. But not worth playing.

Out of all of the versions released this is by far the most superior. The old controller scheme of the PS3 has been updated significantly. Players no longer had to hold down a trigger to walk. This small, but significant change improved the games overall playability in a huge way. The game is a wonderfully crafted interactive drama. If you enjoy choices matter titles. This is one of the best. This game is a masterpiece and an experience I will never forget.

_childDocuments_.review: Heavy Rain is an interactive thriller following the characters of Ethan Mars, Madison Paige, Norman Jayden, and Scott Shelby as they get wrapped up in the search for the Origami Killer. It is a story-focused game with Quick-Time Events as the main focus of the gameplay.-  As an overall, the story is pretty good. It has a lot of intrigue surrounding trying to find out who the killer is, and the tension is maintained throughout as the characters race against the clock to prevent the Origami Killer from claiming another victim. The story is well-paced in my opinion, and each character does go through their own fairly interesting and compelling story (with maybe one exception). Overall was a gripping story that kept me interested from start to finish.-  The game has some amazingly intense scenarios, which play out through Quick-Time Events where your reactions can determine the outcome of the situation and the story. I played on what could be considered the Normal difficulty in the game, and found that the QTE's required quick reflexes but were fair. I personally found that the games controls felt very smooth and responsive during action sequences.-  The music is really good, genuinely adds to the mood of the game and the situations you are involved in.-  Given this is a port of a PS4 remaster, I was delighted to find that for the most part the keyboard and mouse controls work really well for this game. As I previously mentioned, they work very well during QTE's.-  Considering that this is a more or less a port of a PS4 remaster of a PS3 game, it looks pretty decent for the time it came out. It's not gonna wow you compared to what's out now of course, but overall it has visually aged well.-  Personally something I like just because of how goofy and over-the-top Norman's Brooklyn accent is. It is genuinely goofy at times, but I find it that it does really make Norman pretty endearing (and a tad meme-able).-  My personal biggest issue with this game was some of the voice acting. While most of it is fairly passable, there were a few characters (especially the kid characters) who have just horrible voice acting. It doesn't detract too much from the game, but it is something I noticed.-  As I mentioned before, there are a few plot-holes in the game, and there are some things that exist in the game just to fuel coincidence in the story, like Madison's insomnia only being in the story so she could meet up with Ethan, or a sub-plot about Ethan's mental health. Speaking of Madison, of the four playable characters she is in my opinion the weakest as a character, having little impact on the overall plot until roughly around the middle of the story, and largely feels like she's just a someone to serve as a love interest for Ethan, and tends to be a bit unnecessarily sexualised at times. She does become more involved later on, but her story generally feels the least impactful of the four main characters.-  While the game controls well during QTE's, the rest of the game they can be a tad unwieldy, especially when the camera angles change and you're trying to change directions. A few situations where you need to slowly move the mouse are also annoying on mouse and keyboard. It's not too big of an issue most of the time however.-  The original PS3 version of Heavy Rain featured a DLC staring Madison that was really interesting, creepy, and tense, and unfortunately it has been omitted from all subsequent versions of it, including this one.Overall it is an enjoyable experience and I would recommend if you like story-focused games.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! It is a very good balance of story, combat, casual stuff (like making eggs), and crime solving. It took me a couple of nights to finish cause I could only get a couple hours in at a time, but I was so hooked on the story there were times it was hard to log off for the night! They'd leave you on a bit of a cliffhanger for a character then switch you to another. So that aspect definitely helped build suspense. The decisions to make were definitely tough ones for me. They'd have me on the edge of my seat before and after making my choice. The music really helps build up that anxiety as well. I did like the camera work, but I personally found the controls along with the dynamic camera work to be confusing. I also don't game that much, so maybe it's just because I'm not that experienced (especially in choice based games) but I did have some frustrating moments trying to interact with triggers. I was satisfied with my first outcome, but I will definitely be playing again and making different choices just to see the different outcomes play out. It would be neat if they turned the story into a movie. There were times I would briefly forget I was playing a game I was so sucked into it :) I got this on sale for I think $5 or so, but I'd pay $10 or $15 if I knew what I knew now.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been wanting to play Heavy Rain for years, to such an extent at one point that I considered buying a PS2 just to play it. Thankfully, it's now available for PC for a decent price of $20, and while I really enjoyed it, I have mixed feelings towards it overall and it's not the masterpiece that I expected. Basically you alternate between four playable protagonists searching for a serial killer who has kidnapped a child and drowning him within a cage of rainwater. The graphics are great, the story is a bit slow to start, but if you stick with it, it's really compelling and goes to 11 (one scene where you have to drive backwards down the highway is unforgettably anxious and terrifying), and in terms of narrative, it's shocking - all of the playable characters can die, or all of them can survive, it takes Telltale's Walking Dead format to the next level. And while I was shocked by the revelation of the Origami Killer's identity, the game is full of plot holes, not to mention terrible voice acting ("JASON!"), and the QTEs (i.e, button-mashing) can be challenging and unforgiving at times. While I loved how interactive the environments are, much of the interaction doesn't actually seem to matter that much and ultimately felt redundant and pointless. Still, I was very happy that my favourite character Madison (who endures way too much in this game!) saved the day and made it all the way through, and apparently I also got the "second best ending." Heavy Rain is full of flaws (I can't even imagine an ending where Madison dies!), but I really think it really sets the bar for video game narratives and the player's choices, and at the end of the day, it is a solid and entertaining game if you can look past its shortcomings. This is my first Quantic Game, and I'm really excited to play Detroit: Become Human and Beyond: Two Souls next!!

_childDocuments_.review: Quite possibly the worst PC port I have ever played. I have heard this game raved about for years, and was excited to finally play through it, especially since I am a fan of narrative driven, story altering, choice based games. Unfortunately the game itself was a huge let down, both due to a bad port and messy story. The game features many QTE (quick time event) sequences, which like to throw curveballs at you and change up the sequence and button/keys on you. If you fail and decide to refresh your most recent save, the keys/buttons sometimes changes.The controller port is absolutely terrible, and rarely registers anything button and/or stick movement. I tried with 2 separate controllers, 1 being brand new. The M&K controls also have their issues, but not as often. I had a scene where I was sneaking, but are forced to knock a stack of boxes over, everytime I redid the chapter scene and pressed the correct key, and it still didn't register, multiple times. Luckily there was an alternate route.The story itself was ok at best, you meet 3 of the 4 playable characters within the first hour of the game, but the 4th appears 6 chapters later and 3 hours into the game, which seems kind of late to add another co-protagonist. We start with an overly happy man (protagonist 1) and his family living the American dream, but suddenly it is all taken away when his ignorant, oblivious, care-free 10 year old walks off multiple times in a busy mall (once walking away while you attempt to pay a clown for a balloon you bought for your son. This sequence takes time as your character doesn't carry a wallet like a normal human, and has to struggle to find loose cash in his pockets.) You have to chase after him, and then he finally decides to come back to you after calling for him for 10 minutes. The care-less child walks right out into busy traffic and is hit and killed by a car. During the sequence of searching for your son I found him multiple times, or atleast a copy of him not moving, which was a bug that confused me during that part. There is a later chapter in which the character uses a VHS player, in 2011.Protagonist 2 is a private investigator looking into the murders of children, and he himself seems to constantly get involved in fights during each of his chapters. All the QTEs during these fights makes it near impossible actually visualize and watch what is all going on.Protagonist 3 is an FBI agent who uses augmented reality sunglasses and a glove that scans surfaces for traces of evidence. The sunglasses can also alter reality and store information/evidence from cases. Seems a bit unrealistic in a society where we still use VHS'.Protagonist 4 is randomly introduced later on, and starts her story with 3 masked men sneaking around her apartment. Not sure how she didn't hear or see them until the last minute. She can also die in this chapter which then makes her character basically worthless and a waste of a chapter.The main plot is trying to figure out who the real murderer is, but it's not a real mystery, as I discovered it fairly early on. The games tries to force you be convinced that it is protagonist 1, but the shock and awe (sarcasm) when you discover they are innocent, and it is someone else.In addition the graphics are good for 2010, voice acting is ok, except Shaun who is awful, but it's ok, he isn't in the game for long. The story feels very forced and suggestive, which takes the enjoyment out of it. I CAN NOT recommend this game, even if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game, filled with likeable characters, a tense story and choices that really matter. It's more of an "interactive movie" powered by Quick-timed events, but don't let that stop you-- it really is worth a try. If you've played any of these Quantic Dreams games on the Playstation consoles then you know the shtick.Story:This game follows four main playable characters, a middle-aged dad, a private investigator, a cute biker-chic' journalist, and an FBI agent. Following the abduction of Ethan Mars (the Dad)'s son, suspected to have been kidnapped by a murderer known as the "Origami Killer", the quartet have stories that cross paths as they all solve the mystery of the killer, and find Ethan's son. Your choices matter, and you may not complete the game with all four characters, there are a LOT of choices and endings in this game and it's definitely good for replay value.Graphics:The game was only recently ported to PC, alongside Beyond: Two Souls, and Detroit: Become Human. The game was originally a PS3 exclusive that was released in 2009, so don't come in expecting something from the "next-gen". Nonetheless, it was a phenomenal technical feat back on the PS3, and was ported to PC with some upscaled textures and visual effects, the ability to play the game at higher resolutions and framerates, as well as fine control over the visual settings. It's definitely a good looking game from 2009, ahead of that time, but in 2021 you can't expect it to blow you away.Optimisation and the port:Not a bad port. You can max this game out and achieve 60fps on a mid-ranged rig from yesteryear. It supports keyboard input quite nice, and I hadn't experienced any noticeable technical issues.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're planning to play or have tried to play on Steam Deck and quit because of the controls then just sit up when gyro inputs appear. When you're lying down and holding it up to your face it messes with the gyro controls and guarantees you fail every QTE no matter how close you think you're following the input. They were intended for a controller held parallel to the floor. You don't need a custom control scheme, you don't need to connect any extra peripherals, you just need to hold your Deck so that you're looking down on it. Yes, it sounds like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but people on the Internet are still complaining about how the controls are broken and they're wrong. Don't listen to bedridden gamers.Otherwise it's OK, 6/10, the plot doesn't come together because they seemingly cut a bunch of stuff, but it has crazy action scenes, and the female character gets sexually assaulted multiple times - a classic David Cage game.

_childDocuments_.review: So I can recommend this game, but only with some BIG caveats. You see, this is less of a game and more of an interactive movie. It's basically one giant quicktime event. And sometimes the controls are infuriating: on rare rare occasion they don't detect what you're doing very well; also, you will occasionally select the option that is definitely NOT what you wanted to do because the choice isn't obvious. That all said, the story is pretty interesting and USUALLY you are able to do stuff competently enough that you can finish the game successfully. There's even a fair margin of forgiveness within challenges and you can even fail several and get a good ending anyways.If you do decide to try it, I have 2 bits of advice: 1) set it to easy because even that is somewhat unforgiving 2) the first hour-ish is SUPER boring, you just have to power through and it picks up from there

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the good points: I guess the graphics are pretty good for that time and I really love the way you can control the story as a player through decisions (which is one of the main reasons I bought this game)Now let's go on to the cons:Weird camera angles leading to problems controlling the character or the buttons that need to be pressed are partially or fully covered by objects sometimes made playing frustrating.Blake was written following such a stereotype of an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cop just seeking out glory without actual reasonable achievements, resulting in Blake becoming a flat, one-dimensional character that is just comical.At the same time Norman (in the beginning at least) is portrayed as the "good FBI agent" but he is actually incredibly incompetent. He doesn't really follow the clues he finds!!Madison could have been left out as a character completely: she just shows up at weird places without any explanation and her voice acting is horrible. No actual person talks like that and especially towards the end I kept cringing at what she was saying. And despite being a more or less aide, the story could have been executed without any hitch if she had been removed altogether.Now, to my main issue with this game: it doesn't really make sense who the killer is. There couldn't have been any time for a certain event in a certain workshop. Also, Ethan's blackouts are not explained AT ALL. There are so many plotholes that I'm really not convinced by the resolution and the 'twist'. I really don't know what happened here. I played Detroit: Become Human previous to this and as far as I remember correctly it was also written by David Cage. So why is Heavy Rain so weak on the plot and the characters? I really didn't expect to have such an opinion and I'm really disappointed in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rough game to recomend. Thing is Heavy Rain is a mistery murder story that allows you to make choices along the way to solve the mistery and also allow your mistakes to affect the history. With 3 main leads, the game allows itself some room so some to allow for different endings.Now, it's hard to recomend because this game plays very differently than other games. If you played fahrenheit  (AKA Indigo Prophecy) you're very familiar with it. The game prioritizes the use of the right analog as theaction button. That makes so you don't have the control of the camera, you can press L1 to change angles, but it's mostly fixed angles and because the game doesn't use tank controls, you'll have plenty of situations of turning around like an idiot because the camera changes your orientation. Everything else in the game are QTEs (quick time events), that force you to press a specific button before the time is up or will fail.The controls to their job, but it's rough, it was rough in the PS3 when this game launched, and talking about the PS3. This game is a port, meaning you will find random crashes, how many or when it depends entirely on luck, it seems. The game also has a warning that it might become instable if you use the max graphics and it shows, sometimes it froze on me for a few seconds while on max graphics.Now about the narrative that is the main point of the game. It has an interesting premise. Your son is kidnapped and you start receiving letters saying you can save him if you pass the trails to proove you're willing to die for your son. Problem is, the game flat out lies to you, literally changing scenes when flashbacking to it at the end and it's a specially hard problem to ignore, because in this game you have a button to listen to the thoughts of a character in any given scene. The game literally hides the thoughts of one character, hiding how much they really know about any specific situation to them revel to you at the end that they were behind it all along. A clear case of "we didn't thought this through".Despite all that, i still recomend just for it being a unique game. You can't really find a substitute for it and even with it's flaws, it's interesting enough to give you 2 or 3 play throughs. Get it when it's on discount.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that makes me wish we had more than a binary yes/no option.Pros: Story(most of it)SoundtrackCharacter development(most of it, see first spoiler if interested)EnvironmentsAtmosphereCharacter animationCons:Controls...Some of the worst controls I've ever had to deal with in a game. Combined with frequently forced changing of the camera angles it can be a real source of frustration. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved the storytelling - it was engaging, well thought out and executed perfectly! I have already been invested into the whole "serial killer" hype before - watching videos and reading reports on personalities such as Ted Bundy, John Wayne Gacy, Aileen Wournos, Jeffrey Dahmer just to name a few. I was curious to learn how their minds work, how they believe their actions to be just and how they operated. This game provided some insight in that regard too and I will say that it did it beautifully. The game forced me to think and to question my decisions before and after I make them, this means that Heavy Rain was successful in making me rethink my some of my moral beliefs and logical reasonings.The only downside to this game are the controls, or rather, it was painfully obvious that the game wasn't meant to be played on a mouse&keyboard medium. Actions requiring me to drag my mouse in specific directions would either not register or register incorrectly and moving in-game characters around was a nightmare.To end on a high note, because the game deserved it - these inconveniences above did taint my experience a little, but the storytelling and the way game forced my investment outweigh the bad by a very wide margin. I'd recommend this game to anyone who loves non-linear games and/or wants to be a part of a thriller involving a serial killer! (Wait, that rhymes?!)

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most frustrating games I've ever played. The game is unplayable with an XBox controller given the imprecise translation of the controller's stick inputs. So a mouse and keyboard are required. And boy does this game suck on M+K. It's not just the mis-tracked mouse movements during QTEs that's frustrating. It's the game not clearly and immediately visually conveying the type of input that's needed during QTEs (when to hold, when to button mash, etc.). The character movement in the game is awful, with tank-ish movement and imprecise turning radiuses reminiscent of PS Capcom games.That said, there are a lot of interesting ways they jam the same input schema into random activities - changing a diaper, preparing food, hooking up, escaping a torture bed. The story is a perfect blend of melodrama and bad dialogue and serviceable voice acting and legitimately interesting plot turns. And the game itself looks great - I assume they touched it up for PC, because some of these characters' pores just pop.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: So having revisited this game a couple weeks after initially playing it once through, I think I was overly critical of the experience because it was very much a let down by the end. It gives you a lot to think about while being under pressure to make decisions to plow forward, all with unforgiving controls and situations if you fail to master them. The story does have its fair share of problems, but its the combination of things on my first playthrough that really left a bad impression of Heavy Rain in my mind. If you play on the easiest difficultly and make sure its registering as such, I think this game goes a lot better with an attitude of "yea, it's ridiculous, but interesting and mildly fun," then you'll enjoy it a lot more than I did the first time through.(Rainfall: 4.386 Inches)"I'm here to see Heavy Rain.""Heavy Rain?"<Gets game out>..."Heavy Rain!"..."HEAVY RAIN?!"Memes aside...Heavy Rain stands out as a phenomenal game for when it came out, over ten years ago. The suspense, the choices, the graphics (updated for the PC release, but look just about as good as games later in the decade), are something quite amazing! Except... I truly think the whole thing falls apart approaching the climax of it, when things get very serious (and more punishing). Don't get me wrong, I liked this game going into it. But boy, if you don't reach a point where you get very angry with it, even after completing it some time later, then feel free to disregard my review in to ash bucket.Why would you possibly get angry at a game that is "quite amazing?" Well...1. The controls suck!!! Originally when I was looking at other reviews that pointed this out, I thought "this cannot be as bad as these people are saying, right?" When I got a fair amount of the way through, I still didn't even think they were that bad. Sure, not great considering the non-original port (PS3 era) of the game got criticised for being fiddly, but surely not that bad? Well, consider it with this next issue: (EDIT: play on the 'easiest' difficulty, make sure the game is configured for that before carrying on, and hopefully that will improve things a bit more!)2. Quick Time Events Ahoy. This game is pretty much all quick-time events when it matters. Sure, you can have moments of 'down-time,' but the game will eventually push you into more QTE's in order to 'move things' along. This would not be as bigger a problem if the controls were better ported perhaps. However, when the QTE's are stacked alongside timed events in which you only get 'x' amount of time to do certain thing - before you 'fail/the game chooses some option for you" - this feature outstays its welcome by the end. I should add that while I'm not faulting a game that came out a decade ago for implementing a feature that the developers thought would add more intensity to a game about saving someone, I was just disappointed with how heavily they leaned upon this by the end. Great for getting in the head of the characters, but absolute murder for people who don't like to have shaky QTE prompts for dialogue or actions performed in the game, which can be very punishing if you're not onto it perfectly. The lock picking door level, for example, really made me angrily wonder what I was doing with my time, when it wasn't even a proper QTE yet acted like one in order to progress (stupid controls). Speaking of which...3. The story is only weakly believable at best.Honestly, this bugged me the most at the end, because while there were annoyances and things that could be overlooked, THE ENTIRE PLOT'S TWIST IS ENOUGH FOR IT TO PLAY TWISTER ALL ON ITS OWN!Yes, it mostly makes sense not to give much of anything away until near the very end of the game (otherwise there's not much point to media like this). But I cannot understand why the mastermind behind this game's plot thought it wise to do what it did at it's climax, other than to 'be a bit clever' and present something that the vast majority of people will never see coming. Sure it kind of makes sense, but it felt like I was wasting a lot of time to get to the end, only to have things end up not being 'as they seem to be.' This only raises other issues with the plot however like "how come certain characters didn't have the crumb of plot armour that some of the other characters had?" I dunno, but it's not the job of the audience to put up with troublesome features to then have the assumption that this passes as a good example of storytelling.It's believable, yes, BUT BAFTA Best Story award levels worthy? All I'll say is there must have been some real crap choices that year or the judges were literally blown to pieces by the 'Interactive Drama' premise the game presented and forgot all of the game's story plot-holes. Either way, with the other information out there about cut storyline content for the game, the director should've thought a lot more carefully about the story if they wanted to leave the impression that this was a masterful way of telling a story in video game format.--- Final Comments ---All I can write for Heavy Rain is good idea, but bad execution by the end of the game. I was thinking even with the difficulty turned to the lowest point, and following a guide to get a decent ending, that things would be more enjoyable. However that can't even salvage my experience and opinion of the game when the controls ruin the 'Interactive Drama' thing and the story's direction clashes with the asinine controls and tiresome QTE's. The voice acting, which I haven't touched upon throughout, is also kind of hit and miss in some instances, but not enough to be irredeemable when a lot of the surrounding issues should have been a lot more polished for the praise it got. So, that gets a free pass.Heavy Rain's premise then, "how far would one man go to save his child?", seems 'ok' at best when the man should really ask himself why would he ever want to put up with quick time BS, plot inconsistencies up the wazoo, and controls that make one want to smash their devices up and take up paper mache design. Try it if you're quite intrigued with the premise and 'top of the line' kinds of games for the 2010's era, but I would not recommend anyone buy this for the full price, ever.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a chore to play, the game is just bad. I'm ashamed I've paid 20$ on this, and Steam doesn't wanna refund me because I played for more than 2 hours (this is a story game, you need to play a lot to get invested in it).In this game you play as 4 different characters. There's the main guy, Ethan Mars, who's rich and lived in this friggin hollywood suite with his wife and two kids. You play in this prologue for a while, moving around like an alien pretending to be human until one of your kids ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dies because Ethan didn't watch him alright and his kid got hit by a car. Fast forward to a couple of year and now Ethan lives with his remaining son in this sad, tiny apartment which I don't get btw since it's revealed later on he's an architect and he must be doing tons of money. The wife is nowhere to be seen and it doesn't tell you anything about her so you're supposed to assume they're divorced now. Ethan's last child gets kidnapped and that's the premise of the game.The second character is this obese private detective Shelby something something who's trying to solve the case because I don't know. He doesn't even know Ethan, he never interacts with his family. I don't know why he's doing this, he got no client or anything. He just one day decided "yeah imma check this case lol". It eventually leads him to this prostitute who's child was a victim of the kidnapper and they become best buds and partners in this investigation.The third character is this drug addicted FBI agent called Jayden. He's sent to work with the police to solve the case and got those weird VR glasses that doesn't fit at all in this game's universe and the game will force you to use them a lot, it's a pain in the ass and absolutely not fun. He's also got the worst voice acting and it's sometimes pretty funny.The fourth and last playable character is this chick who I never remembered her name. She lives in this sweet apartment but decides to go to a motel for some reasons. The first time you play as her she's fighting in her underwear against CSGO terrorists ninja guys then wakes up seeing it was a dream. She really doesn't do anything apart from tending Ethan's wounds later in the game and being this weird mary sue femme fatale. She was so boring I didn't even care to do the quick time events in one of her segments and that got her killed. There was literally no repercussions in the game, only a tiny cinematic in the graveyard at the ending.If I haven't convinced you already, here's a summary of the story: I played with a controller, the camera does what it wants. The right stick is used to interact with stuff and do some QTE. I wouldn't mind if this game was actually interesting, but it's just a pain to do anything. If you don't do the right stick movement, the animation is cancelled and you have to do whatever you were trying to do again.The pace of the game is extremely poor to me. This is the worst type of game to have 4 different playable characters. If it had only 2 maybe it would've worked, but this was just tedious and it broke immersion in the story anytime they switched characters.The music is generic cash-grab hollywood movie orchestra, no tracks were interesting, maybe apart from the game's main theme but it was overused and lost all meaning (they played it everytime one of Ethan's kids were on screen).That pretty sums up my review, I heard many good things about this game but I'm just extremely disappointed. I genuinely think this is the worst game I've ever played and I'm salty I can't refund it. I was interested in Beyond Two Souls and Detroit Become Human but I don't think I wanna play them anymore. The funny thing is, as a port, it is a very good port. Not bugs, lag or anything.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I spent the day binging it in one go. I think it's great, if you like murder mysteries. It's definitely more in the "action thriller" category, and not really in the "horror" category (although there are plenty of real world fears to think on). One thing to note is that the game is loaded with interactive cutscenes - the kind I remember from Resident Evil 4 when I was a kid, If that's not your thing, you might get a bit frustrated with the game. I don't think my immersion was ever completely broken, but there were a few points that borderlined on that. I think some of the fight scenes were a little too extended and had too many combinations, too. It kinda felt a little like the comical Peter Griffin vs. Chicken fights in Family Guy. I'm exaggerating a bit. I do think some of those were really well done, like    It was a bit tedious, but you could feel the desperation in the fight, with Madison trying to survive and get away. I can also see how some of the controls might be intentionally a bit difficult and awkward, since it's trying to simulate the difficulty of doing those actions in real life. Granted, I played the game with keyboard and mouse - it could be better playing on controller, so there's that. I also played on the hardest difficulty (I think?). It was a little unclear, with the "I play video games often" kind of prompt. I really enjoyed some of the really tense moments, like the   I think that's where the game really shines, when it makes you question how you would react to such situations in real life, and how far you would (or wouldn't) go. The other thing that I think the game did really well was the beginning. I loved how they set the original mood - here's a very successful architect in a pretty well-off house and environment, and everything's great. Then, things start to change.  There's definitely some twists, including one I wasn't expecting.  Furthermore - AND THIS IS A REALLY BIG SPOILER so don't read unless you've gone to an  ending -  There's definitely some things to think about, but can be handwaved because it's a fun journey.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had potential but was ultimately disappointing. You're trying to solve a murder, but are strangely uninvolved in the actual detective work. You don't have to look for clues; just press a button and all nearby clues are highlighted for you. You don't have to think; the characters put the clues together for you. With no actual puzzles to solve, the gameplay simply consists of the game displaying a button, for example "W", and then you press that button. Sometimes you have to press it quickly. That's it.The story is full of plot holes. It was certainly surprising who the murderer was, but for the wrong reason: It was surprising because it made absolutely no sense. Neither the person's actions nor their internal monologue matched the idea that they should be the murderer. We even witness some events that indicate the person is innocent, but they magically turn out not to have happened at all. How convenient.Also, the controls are terrible. I sometimes struggled just to walk across a room or open a cupboard. Your character starts walking in one direction, the camera angle shifts, and they walk right back. Again and again. It was aggravating. Eventually, I was just looking forward to finish the game and be done with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Heavy Rain is a unique and immersive game that blends interactive storytelling with moral dilemmas and weighty themes, which is a hallmark of Quantic Dream's style. The game's plot revolves around making difficult choices that can have far-reaching consequences and lead to different pathways and endings.One of the game's strengths is its impactful moments, which often prompt the player to make tough ethical and moral decisions. These moments add depth and emotional weight to the story and create a thought-provoking experience. However, the game's execution can be frustrating at times. The controls and mechanics can feel clunky and unintuitive, and the dialogues can be awkward. Additionally, some of the plot points and character motivations can be hard to follow, which detracts from the overall experience.Despite these flaws, Heavy Rain is still a unique and engaging game that is worth playing for its intriguing scenarios and impactful moments. However, the game's glaring plot holes suggests that the story was not well-thought-out from beginning to end.

Literally every action you do requires a prompt or your attention. It is borderline annoying and will definitely steer alot of potential players away from teh game. Push through it though. I played with a PS5 controller, but I had some issues with a few of teh prompts in that they would not register. Luckily you can easily swap on the fly with M&K and controller, so it didn't break the play through. You could also tell that they wanted to test the PS controllers move function at the time, cause there are some QTE's that require a full motion of the controller and it gets annoying and some are just there for the sake of the feature.To see the multiple endgins, you dont need to replay the whole game, just start from certain chapters. _childDocuments_.review: Heavy Rain is a dark noir murder-mystery in a modern (2011) U.S. city.The city itself is unnamed but it's based somewhere in Philadelphia. The year is 2011, in October. All of the game takes place in the city area, made up of different environments, typically at night time or in rainfall weather with few people around to create a sense of isolation and mystery.The world layout is just like their other titles. Each area is carefully crafted with a lot of detail in it's design. It's a linear experience so not an open world. Smaller locations with not a lot of freedom of movement. As the game focuses heavily on the storytelling, choices and characters, it is a straightforward experience as you go from level to level. In each chapter you'll interact with various items, clues and people. Be it talking to characters, finding evidence or quick time events.The gameplay of Heavy Rain is fairly limited. It's an interactive drama game. The game is separated into chapters, each one having you play one of the rotating cast of characters. They all play similarly, control using basic movement and input prompts. Each chapter typically tasks you with interacting with things in the environment, these can be people or objects. As you near an object an input prompt will appear indicating the correct movement to be performed. Typically mouse movement for most things but button presses for more intense scenes.The music in this game is phenomenal. Comprising many different instruments, my favourite being the piano instrumentals in the more emotional scenes. The soundtrack was composed by Norman Corbeil (who also done Quantic Dream's other titles such as Fahrenheit), winning Heavy Rain two awards for it's original music.Heavy Rain uses real actors for both the voices of characters and their motion capture acting. All interactions and movements are done by real actors. Interestingly, many of the cast for this title hadn't done any major acting work before this, typically smaller roles. This may sound like a red flag to some but they really pulled through with Heavy Rain. The acting is incredibly well done, both in it's motion and voicing. The main protagonist is played by Pascal Langdale.Watch this video if you're interested. Remember that this is just the casting and the acting in-game is much much better.Over the past few years someone called the Origami Killer has been abducting and killing young boys. The story takes place when the latest victim, Shaun Mars, has been kidnapped too. You play as a handful of different characters in this story. All of this tying together in this mystery as an FBI Agent, the cops and a journalist get closer to the truth, all while the father of the latest victim, Ethan Mars, undergoes challenging physical and mental trials, orchestrated by the Origami Killer, to save his son before time runs out.Heavy Rain is a narrative masterpiece showcasing the stories of many characters. Each chapter giving more clues. Each clue giving more answers. While the game says a lot, it leaves you with two questions:How far would your father go to save you? and how far would you go to save your son?

_childDocuments_.review: I was unsure if I should recommend this game or not, but after I've done some thinking, I simply cannot. The graphics are great for a rather old game and the plot seems very nice at first. I enjoyed the first half of it a lot and could ignore some of the standard movie cliches, but after a while I was getting bothered by one obvious method applied to the whole story again and again. What really makes this game bad for me is the reliance on several red herrings to keep the story going and in the end some things just don't make sense and seem forced. I'm aware that if you played it when you were younger, you probably would have enjoyed it much more, but from my perspective (especially after playing Detroit and loving it), I feel it is a game that isn't that good in terms of storytelling. If you have nothing better to do, it is a nice 9 hours, but I would rather recommend playing Detroit than this. Apart from this the voice-acting is often horrible (especially the kids and Ethan's "JASON" will haunt me forever).

The story of the game makes zero sense. The mystery of finding the origami killer isn't something you slowing find out. None of your choices in the game really matter as your choices are just to keep your character alive and otherwise don't affect the overall story at all (and in the case of one character they can't die no matter what due to plot armor. Characters act without reason with motivations that either don't make sense or (in the case of Blake) are such comical caricatures of stereotypes that it's impossible to believe they're an actual person that exist in this supposedly realistic world. The voice acting on almost all the characters lacks emotion and usually doesn't fit whatever is happening in the scene (insert funny clip of Ethan screaming SHAUUUNNNNN). Madison as a character could be removed from game and the story wouldn't change making her inclusion pointless. The music while good often times is more intense than whatever is actually happening in the game. And aside from the fact that this story game has a bad story even if you wanted to get some entertainment from streaming it or doing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ by intentionally failing qte's. Since this a ps3 game, this port runs like actual ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dogwater and it's an unoptimized to hell and back. Every time you finish sitting through a long loading scene you have to deal with the game stuttering and freezing most likely because they had to load every single one of those police officers so they can walk in circles and stand in place doing nothing. _childDocuments_.review: This so barely gets a positive review and this is why. I always wanted to play it. As a kid, this game was the biggest curiosity for me. Interactive movies weren't a thing really then and so this caught my eye. Finally it's on PC and... wow, what a mess of a game. The port is so bad that literally the emulator runs this ♥♥♥♥ better. Every time I loaded into a new area on an SSD, the game would have these insane freezes. I had to let the game only access 3 out of the 8 cores to reduce the stutters. I also had to turn the game to 30fps, which was a terrible 30fps as well with awful frametimes.I liked the characters and they were interesting in general. Likeable, at least. The story itself was too long and it's bad crime fiction. The answers are made up and the players can't take part in really speculating and analyzing the information presented to them since most of the time the game presents completely random people as suspects. It's watching people react after solving their crimes, not people actually solving a crime. Don't worry, no spoilers. But just saying, the conclusion is bad. The worst I've seen in any crime fiction. Why? Because it's literally impossible. Like it's literally impossible. Nothing fits and nothing makes sense. It's literally, as in physically, impossible. This is not a game about magic and stuff, so that doesn't explain it either. It's just flat out impossible. Overall I'm glad I was allowed the opportunity to finally play this and for that it gets the thumbs up. The price during sales is reasonable and at the end of the day I was one of the people begging for this game. But also if you're just stumbling on this game thinking it might be good, it won't. It's comically bad at best, but the comedy ends when instead of seeing like the most excessive amount of interactive urination you'll ever see turns into actual arrogance on the writer's behalf. So yeah... were you desperate to play it like me? Go and get your slap in the face for thinking it might just be so bad it's funny, rather than being a baffling case of incompetent writing that brags how clever it is.

(DEFINETELY the highlight of the game. The Plot twist and ending is truly epic. The only requirement to be any good at this game is purely fast reflexes.)☐ A fair challenge/ average for the genre☐ Difficult ☐ Book anger therapy in advanceReplayability☐ One and done☑ Justifies a replay for any missing content (The multiple endings may interest keen players but for me personally, ONE playthrough was enough. I am NOT going to play the game's chapters over and over and over again to see all of the  ultimately lazy, short cutscenes. Unique as they may be, it's simply far more efficient to just look up all the endings that you DIDN'T get on youtube!☐ Multiple playthroughs will not burn you out!Appropriate Pricing☐ N/A☐ Worth the full price!☑ Wait for a sale ☐ Don't waste your hard earned cash!Bugs☐ Very polished! Very minor bug experience overall.)☐ Bugs hinder immersion and overall enjoyment☐ Ultimately a broken experienceA stunning story that tests and surprises players, let down by braindead controls and generic side characters. _childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting to play this on PC for 10 years, so I was very excited when I read that it came to PC. Unfortunately, in hindsight, Heavy Rain at least viewed from today seems a so-so experience. But since steam tactically only offers thumbs up or thumbs down, in the end I consider the game a positive experience in spite of all the flaws it has.Most of all, because I believe you've simply got to give Quantic Dream credit for constantly trying to evolve interactive storytelling / interactive movies. Ten years after its realease, the multiple-perspective interactive thriller Heavy Rain may seem a bit dated in terms of graphics and controls, but still, it certainly did leave its mark on game design, offering heavily branching narrative iterations and facial animations which today may not be that impressive, but back in 2010 were paving the way for many other games.Pros:- rather interesting story about a serial killer - multiple branching narratives offering new experiences on multiple playthroughs- a range of facial emotions that at least in 2010,  were groundbreakingCons:- very clumsy controls that at times make you feel like you're playing against the interface- the visual representation of the (many) quick-time events often makes it impossible to watch what's happening in-game as you're staring at button symbols all the time- uneven level of difficulty - narratively important events may be very easy to play through, totally banal actions (i.e. rocking a baby to sleep) at times took me more than 10 times to get them right.- at times, rather cliché characters and plot elements- somewhat questionable representation of female characters: As soon as a female character appears with a virtual wireframe that was clearly built to emphasize her butt (which the camera framing underlines with multiple butt-shots of this camera), I though: "Ok, this is a David Cage game. She's clearly here to offer a sex scene for the male lead." And so it goes. The other female lead is portrayed as a sexually traumatized woman that sells her body for money - but, once the overweight, alcoholic, twice-her-age male lead character enters, is readily available to romance him. Of course, this being a branching narrative, these plotlines don't have to appear in all playthroughs, but they probably will in many.- main characters may die, and not all of these deaths seem narratively convincing. Some made me feel like plotlines had been arbitrarily clipped off.All in all, I think Heavy Rain is a rather mediocre game - if it weren't for it's (now historic) innovativeness. But for that you've certainly got to give it credit.

_childDocuments_.review: Listen, there's something to be said about the story that was meant to be told here. I did not play this game for nostalgic reasons, I played it at the recommendation of others. With that said, this game is obviously dated and looking at it as a novel idea, it fails to hold up. The entire story makes little to no sense when you take a step back for just a moment. Movement, controls, and needless little actions and task can be forgiven because that is what makes this a Quantic Dream production. Any level of critical thinking will pull you out of this story. I will not spoil the content of the game in this review but you should subvert your expectations and just ride along with the narrative being non-sense. Otherwise, you're going to have a terrible time. All in all, quick-time events included, I'm going to give this game a solid 4/10. If you're playing this game to see how Quantic Dream pushed the envelope in the early 2010s, then this is a great game for you. If you're more focused on 'Choices Matter, Narrative Driven Gameplay', this may not be the game you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to have two PS3 games, one was Heavy Rain and the other was GoW. I got it on eBay for $4.99 but didn't have the time to play. Glad to pick it up on Steam.I'm no stranger to Quantic Dream's games, big fan of Detroit and Two Souls, Heavy Rain was released earlier yet still in good shape, the tense kept me focused as there are a lot of QTE which lead to different consequences. If you want the best ending, try not to miss too many like you are playing Dark Pictures Anthology. Heavy Rain features a crime case, where a serial killer. The story is linear and straightforward, you take control of 4 people in turns, Ethan who's the victim's family, a journalist, a federal agent and a private detective. The story is rich and solid, you'll visit quite a lot of places with all kinds of crazy and dangerous people in high and low levels, each character has own way to work out the clues. Ethan's route is simple, he's given instruction from the killer and clearly the killer wants him to suffer, including. For others, the Federer agent has access to high-tech tools and databases to consult, the private detective starts with a former victim's family, and the journalist gets closer to Ethan. Apart from violence, there is agony, romance, love, according to your decision you'll see different endings, success or failure. What interests me is the protagonists visit the same person at the same place just hours later but the consequence could be very different. You also make decisions, my favorite goes to the mansion where the detective takes . I only finished one ending and it's satisfying, but I believe both the  are worth seeing. I enjoyed the mystery and the surprise of the killer's identity, it's interesting that . The whole story feels bitter, it is about how much one would sacrifice for a loved one.The game is 7 hours long for one gameplay, you can try other endings easily from manual saves. I recommend this game, it has a great crime story and thought provoking.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the thing in one sitting with lots of breaks in-between.This is a game I always wanted to play but never got around to. And now I can cross that off my list. To me this game really marked the beginning of an era of hyper-realism and a solid proof of concept that videogames could be cinematic and have gripping and deep stories just like a movie or show.I'm so glad I got to play it and in some ways get a strong reminder of where we were and where we are now in terms of how videogames have evolved over the past decades.The game deserves an absolute 10/10 for story and atmosphere.But of course there are some downsides, mainly platyer control and motion controls. I had a lot of issues and had to reset a lot of times due to some QTE's that required controller movement. But I got past it, got the best ending and had a blast!

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't think I can add anything to a Heavy Rain review that hasn't already been said.Its a good game with a good story and was a graphical powerhouse in the era it was release. The port is very stable and works well with control pad and mouse and keyboard.I am very happy to see Quantic Dream fully released from Sony as an exclusive brand. Beyond two souls and Detroit coming to PC is just good for gamers I think as I am not a fan of exclusivity.The story is bleak, depressing, gritty, has a great twist and is much more grounded and realistic than Fahrenheit indigo prophecy.Playing through on the PC yielded nothing new for me as I had already completed it on the console version. But it was nice to play through again and 100%.My advice to anyone who has yet to play it. Don't look up anything about it, stay away from forums and just play the story through naturally first, don't achievement hunt until after first play through. This way you will get to experience the story with no spoilers.There are multiple endings too.This was going to be made in to a film, the rights were acquired over a decade ago but nothing happened. The game has QTE actions like Shenmue I and II mixed with split second decisions from games like Bioware and fallout. The choices you make effect the ending and the way that the story unfolds. This leads to multiple play through's in order to see all endings possible. The only down side that i found frustrating in the PC port from the original PS3 was the fact that you could not play with a controller. The controls for PC were at times distasteful. in QTE events it was easier on the playstation because you knew what left, right, up down and R buttons were. The PC makes you do combinations with left shift, W, S, D, A, Q, E. The hard part was i did not have the exact keys memorized and it was a learning curve to pass the QTE's. Maybe even more so, the game will often give you a very short time to answer questions or say something. The problem is that the game has the options float around your head, so you often don’t even have the time to read them before one is picked automatically. Also, get ready for QTE: The Game. Honestly, I really wish I could enjoy the story, but the frustrating gameplay with all the terrible QTE’s really ruin the game. I don’t know what else they could have done, but this is not for me. I am hating the game more than I am liking it. The controls might even have been so bad that they made me fail some checks that could severely alter my ending (I think that because of my mouse sensitivity, all “move slowly”-checks were quite difficult. Maybe the game is better with a controller.)And what might be the worst offender is that you often don’t know what the prompts will do. I failed an essential part of the game, because I had just been able to walk around, went to wash my face, got up and then got a prompt to use some other hotkeys. I did not do it, as I tried to find out what it would do, but apparently, if you do not immediately do that prompt, you start using some drugs. Thanks game for telling me that. This game is so poorly made, when it comes to the actual gameplay and not the story. And another moment where the game didn’t indicate things properly had me accidentally fails to save somone. Also, what. A. Stupid. Kid. This game starts out with one of the best cases of Darwinian Abortion I have ever seen. Wow. In a way, seeing NPCs walking around in very emotional scenes like NPCs from 2005 really adds a humoristic and outlandish level to every level of seriousness and investment in the game you have. I can see why this became such a rewarded game in 2010. It has so many story elements going for it. The gameplay is just so terrible that it completely ruins any experience I could have with this And for a game that is all about decisions, it really chickens out towards the end. There is a scene, where I wanted to have the action to personally kill someone who really deserved it and who would be terrible for you not to kill. Yet, your character is about to walk away when said person gets… in trouble. You can then decide to help or to go. I wanted my character to personally kill the person way before this happened. This is the first point where I felt that the game took a decision away from me. Terrible. An issue with this game is that many characters have French accents even when they shouldn’t. Also, the majority of the characters look remarkably French (for something taking place in Pennesylvania) Also, the ending, if you get to realize who the killer is, disregards SO MUCH of the game. It completely removes any player action – and the thoughts/dialogue the player is given, for large parts of the game. It even doesn’t work with a few scenes as the killer is a different body type than the killer you see in the game (different scenes). I like the idea as it makes sense on paper, but it just screws so much with what the character tells the player that it becomes absurdly ridiculous. This whole game, the player gets to be inside the head of, and act as, several characters. There is not a single point where one character becomes dishonest with this concept. Until the ending. The ending is honestly terrible. I can see how some may write it off as brilliant, but those are people who don’t understand how the logic of the game should work. This is like someone saying “You can choose “A” or “B” for 10 hours. Then, at the very end, you realize that there was never an “A” or “B” scenario, but a “1” or “2” or “…”. Imagine if Jim Carrey in the Truman Show turned out to be the showrunner and director at the last 5 minutes of that film. It would also break with everything you had gotten, as an audience, up till that point. This is remarkably bad.And at the very end, I had a character killed because I wasn’t fast enough to react to one terrible QTE prompt – one that never worked well with PC in the first place.This game might have been good when it came out, but it is quite bad by modern standards.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has awkward voice acting, bad writing, an obnoxious soundtrack, a borderline incoherent plot, phoned in gameplay and janky controls. It also inexplicably crashed for me in the middle of an important sequence and has little lag dips every time a new scene is loaded.But I loved nearly every second of it. Heavy Rain is ridiculous, yet my enjoyment of it wasn't even a "it's so bad it's good" thing, I was wholeheartedly invested basically all the way through. This paved the way for games like The Walking Dead, Life is Strange and of course Detroit Become Human-- it was highly experimental for the time. A French studio trying to make an artsy, highly cinematic game on Playstation 3 hardware lmaoWhat Heavy Rain does better than those games is . Life Is Strange, for example, is all about thinking deeply about your actions and how they affect people, really trying to make the optimal choices. Those devs wanted you to dwell on everything. All about regret, rewinding to a different choice. Second guessing. In Heavy Rain you don't have time to dwell on anything and you have no idea what actions are even high-stakes. You can miss a 2 second quicktime window and it will completely alter the path you go down for the rest of the game. One of the downsides to this (at first glance) is that it doesn't really feel like a video game. This is very much the "movie game" meme that people parrot. At least it feels like it, because in reality it's not at all. So little emphasis is put on your choices but every little thing you're doing is weaving the options you get later down the road which ultimately determine your ending. The ending I got on initial playthrough, and the general path I went down didn't leave me super satisfied. I kept thinking "I wanna spend more time with the other characters, it feels like I've been locked out of the part of the game I was interested in" ...and that's cuz I was. Stupid decisions or lack thereof boxed me into playing as other characters. Stressfully realistic in that way. Do not expect masterful storytelling, or even good characters. Or anything good really, maybe it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks actually. But it's so fun and there was clearly a genuine passion from the creators of this game. Just play it, one of my favorite games ever now.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting much out of this game.  I wasn't impressed by the free sample Steam offers and the ending had already been spoiled for me.    But I love Detroit: Become Human, so I decided to give it a shot, anyway.I'm glad I did.  I love it.It's not a perfect game by any means.  The story is kind of nonsensical, the controls are awkward and the visual prompts that accompany them difficult to parse at points , and the voice acting... oh boy.  But the game still felt tense and disturbing to me at all the right moments; it hit its story beats well.  And I love thriller media, so this was right up my alley.  I was engaged the whole way through.  The graphics also hold up surprisingly well for a game that's a decade old, and I really enjoyed the soundtrack and how each character got his own distinct theme, much like in Detroit.  Scott Shelby's was especially prominent.  Overall:  9/10.  I don't love Heavy Rain as much as Detroit, but it has the same kind of charm and intrigue as its most recent successor, which is probably why I like it so much.  I want to play again to get different endings at some point when I have the time.

_childDocuments_.review: I love narrative games so my opinion in this might be a little biased and I obviously recommend this game. It doesn't come without flaws but we get so little of such games that i'm happy even if it's not perfect.Heavy Rain is an interactive-drama thriller. The Origami killer is kidnapping children and drowning them. One of the main character's son disappears and father who's name is Ethan gets a message from killer demanding him to take tasks in order to save his son. Killer is testing Ethan's courage and Ethan must decide how far he will go in order to save his son.Besides Ethan there are more main characters. An FBI agent Jayden who's suffering from drug addiction was sent to investigate the murders. A journalist Madison who's suffering from (PTSD?) starts investigating the murders too. Then there's Shelby, a private detective making his own investigation. Lauren, a mother who lost her child to origami killer plays a role too but she's not playable. Overall characters are interesting enough, I just wish the game would delve deeper into their psychology.The story or maybe the idea is really cool. The whole mystery, plot twist, atmosphere, basically the whole thriller aspect is very good. But it falls short when it comes to execution, acting and writing. While the story itself is amazing the writing is not so good. The whole game, especially the first half is so cheesy, cliché, cringy whatever you call it that it's not even funny. I've noticed same thing in Detroit too but not as severe as in Heavy Rain and Cage has improved a lot with later games. But when it comes to story itself it's a real pleasure to experience it. The game is pretty bleak and dark, tackling some serious issues.Maybe at some points the story makes no sense but before you play it you need to put yourself in a certain mindset. Look at this as it was a movie not a game, imagine yourself as an observer who can slightly change the flow of the movie rather than imagining you as certain character.You play as each character depending on the chapter. Gameplay is pretty straightforward. You explore the tiny surroundings a bit, pick up evidence, talk with people and do qte's, lots of qte's. All action scenes are a series of qte's. I know many people hate those but I honestly can't imagine a game like this without qte's. It's better than just sitting and watching.There are difficulty settings so you could make qte's easier or harder. Some of them can be really tricky.There are lots of beautiful locations. Most of them are dark and quite depressive. Each chapter takes place somewhere else so you won't be stuck at the same location for 2 hours looking at the same textures. One minute you're exploring a crime scene and shortly after you're dealing with suicide.It's an old PS3 game so don't expect revolutionary graphics. Although when it came on PS3 it was pretty revolutionary. Great animations in general but face animations are lacking. It feels like at times they're working fine and other times it doesn't work at all. It's as if they ran out of budget or something because some parts of the game feel less polished than others. Other than animations the game looks great considering its age.Performance is good. The game is locked to 60fps unfortunately, but hey at least it's not 30fps.No ultrawide support. And I will repeat the same thing when writing about a narrative games – such games should have native ultrawide support. There can't be any excuses. It's called “cinematic experience” for a reason.Controls are ok. This should be played with a controller obviously. Mostly it's fine but sometimes when camera changes and you're on the “edge” of where it changes you might get stuck in a loop of going forward and backwards. But I have this issue with all similar games. Nothing too bad, controls are well executed in general.When it comes to sound it's good and bad at the same time. Phenomenal soundtrack is contradicted with poor to ok voice acting. Soundtrack is really something, it increases that thrill factor and throughout the game plays an important role by keeping the tension on. But voice acting...well it's a tough one. Again like i mentioned before talking about graphics it's inconsistent. At the beginning it's pathetic. It's like some amateur kids decided to make a movie. Its bad, laughably bad. Later on it somehow gets better as if actors taken acting lessons or got paid more. Some characters are acted better, some worse.Overall a good game for the fans of narrative games. It even could make you to do an origami or two. A very good story riddled with cliches and cheesiest moments in gaming history. It's dark, full of thrilling moments, sadness and despair and a really enjoyable ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Heavy Rain

_childDocuments_.review: There's a serial killer on the loose. 7 victims, all young boys, kidnapped and eventually drowned in rain water. An origami figure is found at the scene of each crime.You are Ethan Mars, and your son has become the eighth victim of the person they call "the origami killer". In a matter of days your son will die if you cannot find him. The killer has left you trials that you must undertake, and by doing so you might save the boys life. But how far are you willing to go.....?Would you sacrifice your own well being?Would you take a life to save another?You are Scott Shelby, private investigator. Hired by the previous victims families to bring the origami killer to justice. A former cop yourself, you know how police investigations work and where to draw the line in your activities.Will you cross that line to save a life?You are Madison Paige, investigative reporter. Chance has brought you into Ethan Mars life, and either compassion or your journalistic instincts compel you to aid him.Can he be trusted?Can you make a difference, and help bring down a killer?Will you live to tell the tale.....You are Norman Jayden, FBI investigator. Very involved in your job, possibly a bit too involved, as your addiction to narcotics would suggest the pressures are beginning to wear you down. Will you find the killer?Will you be able to do so without giving in to your inner demon?And if not.....what will solving the case cost you?There's a lot of threads at play in 'Heavy rain', with each twist and turn of the plot being something you can manipulate through your choices and actions. Things you do, or don't do, can come back to haunt you later on. I think the identity of the killer is always the same, but there are several ways you can change the ending in regards to the four characters that are involved.It is an interactive narrative game, so you should know what you're getting into, but it is quite a lot more hands on than most. There are quick time events that put you into the more action packed, cinematic scenes, and on a controller at least, they're fairly trickily implemented. Requiring some dexterity as the button presses, multiple holds, and positions of the joysticks, can be like playing twister with your hands.How that works without a controller, I don't know. With that particular control scheme it works really well, and ensures that the "gameplay" (such as it is) is more exciting than most QTE's. It is like other narrative driven games, Man Of Medan for a recent example, and yet goes beyond the challenge of most in this department. I should repeat though, that I have no idea how that translates to mouse and keyboard, as I don't play that way.Story-wise it is entertaining, rewarding, and takes a decent length of time to complete (about 9 hours for me). The ending (which can vary of course) deals with the outcomes for each character, so you get a nice sense of closure for each part. Uh.....well.....unless you *fudged* it up for that person, as happened to me with a slightly sad stinger for one of them (ah, Norman....I hope your brain isn't totally fried, shoulda laid off the drugs man, but I, uh, pressed the wrong button at the wrong time, so.....)The writing is good, the graphics are good, the voice acting and direction is good. The only thing that lets it down production wise, is the slightly awkward movement of characters. Which can be a bit robotic and bumbling on the odd occasion. For what it is, this is excellent and I recommend it. But it is a type of genre in gaming that requires you to be invested in its story, as while the gameplay is more involving than other examples, it is still a simplistic mechanic that allows for participation in the more "exciting" moments. If you like Telltales games, or Man Of Medan / Life is strange etc, then I would say you should like this. If you really hate the format, then there is nothing here to change your mind.  If you liked this review, and want to see what I think of other games (maybe find a hidden gem), then check out my curator page

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game, and I really wanted to play it for a long time, so when it went on special I lunged at it like Muricans during Black Friday.Am I happy about playing the game? Well, yes, and no. There are things that intrigued me, and I wanted to see how it ended and who the killer was.What put me off, and nearly made me stop playing the game was the utterly horrible controls and clunky character movement. The time spent on trying to get your character to walk where you want them or to interact with something adds about 30 minutes to the gameplay, as you tend to frequently reposition your character, etc. The controls are also extremely awkward, I had to switch between by keyboard + mouse and my XBONE controller to accomplish certain QTEs. I started playing with the XBONE controller, then had to swap to keyboard and mouse because some QTEs just wouldn't complete. I completed 85% of the game with keyboard and mouse. For certain QTEs I had to switch back to the XBONE controller as I just couldn't look in a certain direction and then perform the QTE, as it would then look away.Sometimes when pressing my dialogue keys, I would have to press the option twice before the game would trigger it, the same with QTEs. It got my favourite character (Norman Jayden) killed, when I wasn't ready for him to die.The controls is but one of the issues though. The story, as it is told feels broken. The narrative does not make sense, and some things happen off screen. It's jarring. Also, the reveal of who the killer is just does not make sense at all, all things considered. It felt hollow, and I had a real wtf is this ♥♥♥♥ moment. Yet, it kept me playing, but I felt disconnected from almost all of the characters, except Jayden.There are some minor graphical glitches, the loading screen faces look great, but in-game faces look flat, and characters' eye look dead. I wished they all looked like they do in the loading screens.That being said, and those being the things that frustrated me the most.... for that 100 ZAR that I paid for the game, the overall experience of playing what is a classic wasn't too bad. I enjoyed the extras that you unlock.Will I play it again to get alternative endings to some chapters? Nope. I think the way that it ended was fine. If abrupt, and just a little weird.Would I recommend others to play it, given its flaws? Yep, why not, you might enjoy it, even the mess of the controls.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game with an interesting plot.I really enjoyed the true crime plot and thought the story coming form 4 different POVs was very interested and added a lot of suspense. I played through and got multiple endings and all were pretty solid.The controls were strange at first but easy to get used to. I stared with controller but actually found mouse and keyboard to be more enjoyable. I also really like the arrows that show up for the QTEs. They really helped me to pass them and didn't break the immersion. Beyond: Two Souls did not have the arrows and it was rather annoying.The voice acting was good for some parts but really bad for others. Specifically Ethan's voice acting was, at time, completely hollow. It was as if the VA recorded them out of order with no idea of the plot. At very stressful and climactic points, Ethan's VA spoke as if it was a Sunday afternoon on the beach. That kind of messed up the immersion but the other characters were strong enough to carry me through.Madison's character was rather hollow - more manic pixie dream girl than actual character, but still an interesting perspective on the overall story. Can't complain too much.The other two characters Jayden and Shelby were the best written IMO. They had the greatest depth and felt like actual people. I do with there was more backstory on Jayden though. There were some minor holes in his story I think would have benefited his character had they been filled.Overall, it was a great experience and I'd highly recommend.
