_childDocuments_.review: This game is an immersive and emotional story unrolling in front of you, and (in part) by your hand, as you take on the role of Jodie and live out pivotal moments of her life, from little girl to a young woman.The twist being that Jodie is connected with an "entity" - another soul - with which she interacts, and which interacts with Jodie's world.The game is a kind of cinematic story telling with you controlling Jodie and making her decisions at points which affects the story line. Some decisions are minor and only affect the the course of the current scene, while other decisions will affect the story line later on.This is in no way a difficult game - no difficult riddles to solve, no dying halfway and restarting. This is all about the story, experience and atmosphere - about human interaction and being human, even when you grow up as a subject of study due to your supernatural abilities.Personally I was a bit doubtful of the entire idea, but after trying the demo I was intrigued, and after buying the game and starting out for real I was spellbound. This has been the most immersive and emotional game I've yet to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond: Two Souls features a protagonist that is hardly likable, or overwhelmingly repulsive. She is exceptionally capricious, undeniably ungrateful, constantly disturbing, and most importantly, constituting the bane of all around her: she brings trouble, misery, and in a lot of cases, death to all those around her. She causes troubles constantly and has no sign of regret or repentance. She seems to have no respect for authority whatsoever and always treats herself as being superior to others, as evident in her actions in taking away countless innocent lives (a lot of them being the law enforcement) for her own survival. I cannot imagine seeing anyone who is so blatantly despicable and flagrantly evil. No one would conscientiously want to be around her. One might argue that her vindictive actions and gruesome personality is the result of her childhood pain and suffering. Nonsense. Why? Because she does “her justice” in a significantly unjustified manner. Folks used to say “an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth,” but in comparison, she would take away other people’s lives without a blink of an eye for a slight humiliation, which is both legally impermissible and morally inadmissible.Conclusively speaking, this game features a pathologically egocentric worldview that seems to justify and endorse the callous act of taking away lives of those who are completely innocent and get out of it with absolutely zero repercussions. It seems that it encourages female players of this game to live just as Jodie Holmes, ruining the lives of her own family and all around her and getting away from it freely. Academically put, (the following paragraph is composed by AI) this game reflects the existential nihilism pervasive in much of contemporary media. Her destructive actions are not framed as redemptive or purposeful but rather as a chaotic response to her circumstances. Jodie’s moral disengagement and lack of accountability reflect a broader societal shift: the celebration of victimhood as justification for unchecked actions, a phenomenon widely pervasive in much of contemporary media. While her story elicits sympathy for her traumatic past, it also raises critical questions about personal responsibility and the narrative consequences of empowering characters without ethical constraints.

_childDocuments_.review: What an unforgettable, emotional and often quite sad story, but if I was trying to be cynical, then I wouldn’t be able to decide whether to call this an amazing interactive experience or a sad excuse for a computer game. Perhaps the truth is somewhere in between as with most things.I played this with an Xbox controller and the sometimes counterintuitive actions were quite manageable. Sadly, I have to say: As much as the acting and production made this very immersive, the controls killed my immersion more than a dozen times for sure, and the lack of free movement you’d expect from a computer game didn’t help either.Immersion has a lot to do with the degree of comfort you experience while playing and the suspense created.Here’s some food for thought: This could mean that even the feeling of presence created by virtual reality means very little, if the content is boring, and you’re uncomfortable under your HMD. You might end up being less immersed, even compared to playing flat games.Despite the control issues this was a unique experience. It is one that I will never forget, and I will have to try some alternative routes through this unusual life. I’m familiar with inner conflicts, psychological, philosophical, emotional, it is part of who I am. So, this game certainly got under my skin; it was another pleasant opportunity to let my emotional-self  relax and release tension.I often wonder what it would be like, if you could live your life again, take different routes, explore different paths, make different decisions, what would be the outcome? All it can take is turning around a different corner and everything can change, and also the other people involved! Are there universes with all possible alternatives and outcomes?

_childDocuments_.review: When I see the tag 'choices matter' I expect my choices to actually matter. In Beyond they do . . . in a very limited capacity. The game is split into chapters that play in non-chronological order. For the narrative, it works, but this introduces an issue with making choices matter. How is what you do in the past supposed to change the future if you're playing through the future scenario first? Short answer: it doesn't.The choices you make will shape the way the chapter plays out, but will have limited, if any, impact on later chapters you play. This continues all the way to the end, where you are simply given a prompt to choose which ending you wish to see. It makes the entire game you just played through seem pointless when you can go against the choices you've made right at the end. Totally snub a character through the entire game? You can still choose the ending where you choose to be with them. Specifically, and with minor spoilers I suppose, I snubbed Ryan every single chance I could. He's a ♥♥♥♥ and the MC deserves better. Despite all of this, turning him down at every opportunity, he pulls her in for a passionate kiss right before the final encounter. Rapey much? It's not bad as narrative game if you consider the main story to be more 'the story missions have multiple solutions' rather than 'choices matter'.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game in the chronologically told story mode, just to keep that in mind for this review.This game isn't bad, but it could definitely be better. Unlike Heavy Rain or Detroit: Become Human, the choices in this game don't matter all that much. Some of them do matter, but not to the extent where if you do this this happens or that that happens. The fun part about this game, though, was its main mechanic, being controlling another entity aside from Jodie named Aiden. Being able to interact with my surroundings and mess with the living world or the spiritual world was quite fun. The only true problem with this system is that Aiden was simply too overpowered in the sense that the game developers had to force you to just not be able to use him a lot of the time in order to create the storyline. In one case it makes sense that you can't use Aiden, but then in other cases when Jodie is straight up about to die or gets knocked unconcious Aiden just can't help her. This could be justified by saying that Aiden also gets knocked out when Jodie is knocked out, but there are events in the game where Jodie is unconscious and Aiden is still able to interact with the world so that argument can't apply. Despite playing in chronological order, this game was kind of random with its chapters anyway. It felt fluid and made sense at the start, but then at the latter half they introduced a bunch of characters and random plot-lines that I didn't really care for. I liked the homeless plot-line with Stan and the others, but then they had a kind of Indigenous people evil spirit chapter that didn't apply to the rest of the game, was mostly forgettable, and stuck out like a sore thumb. Not to mention it was way too long of a chapter to really have any good point to stop at during any point of it. This would likely have made the story feel a lot more confusing had I played in the originally intended version of this game, that being the chapters not being in chronological order, but just straight up out of order.The final chapters of the game ruined a character for me as from what they were shown to be in the past was completely different from the character they actually turned out to be. They turned into a manipulative and uncaring ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who no longer cared about anyone except his dead family members. He used to see Jodie as a daughter to him, but as soon as they didn't see each other for a few years he just completely changed. Sure, people change over time, but if I don't see this change coming or foreshadowed in any way then it's not a change I'm going to welcome. And the solution to his problems in the end was literally killing himself so I don't quite know what to think about that message there, but I kind of had already lost hope for the game by then.Simply put, did I have fun with this game? Yes, but would I recommend this game to people looking for a similar experience to Heavy Rain and Detroit? Not at all. Go into this game cautious and with a friend to watch you to play and for you to talk to as that's honestly the only reason I was able to make it through this experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The Quantic Dream games have gotten better and better. Beyond: Two Souls is much, much better than Heavy Rain, which was barely playable as it was. BTS is outstanding, full of story and emotional choices, excellent graphics and mo-cap, and some really touching performances by Ellen Page, Willem Dafoe, and several other lesser known actors. With a huge diversity of locations interspersed throughout (similar to the globe-hopping missions in games like Splinter Cell) there's never a dull moment.There's way more going on than meets the eye at first glance, and I was swept along by the story, hanging on the edge of my seat to get to the next step. Still not as good as Detroit: Become Human, which as set the new current standard for the "interactive movie" type of games, beating BTS out by a decent margin due to BTS having some really odd control mechanics in the game. No matter what I tried, I still had issues right up until the end of the game. I got past them, but that doesn't mean I didn't spend a ridiculous amount of time trying to get past certain spots. Glad to see DBH upped the ante a bit and fixed most of that. Plus, DBH's story was just a good bit better, and I just liked the concepts presented in it just a lot better than BTS's.Still, BTS is a fine game, and well worth the effort to get past the wonky controls that kept coming back to haunt me too often.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆Beyond: Two Souls originally released on PlayStation 3 in 2013, is an interactive drama and action-adventure game developed by Quantic Dream. Lauded for its storytelling, its PC version release brought about enhanced visuals, improved controls, and a chance for a wider audience to experience its narrative.It boasts enhanced graphics compared to its original console release. With higher-resolution textures, better lighting effects, and more detailed character models, the visual experience feels more immersive. On a high-end PC, the game can be experienced in its full glory with smooth frame rates and detailed environments.The game's main attraction remains its narrative. Ellen Page and Willem Dafoe's stellar performances as Jodie Holmes and Nathan Dawkins, respectively, bring a cinematic quality to the game. The storyline, which spans different stages of Jodie's life and her connection with an invisible entity named Aiden, is both emotional and intense.However, the non-linear narrative structure might be disorienting for some players. While this storytelling method adds to the game's uniqueness, it may also create moments of confusion.The gameplay in is a mix of interactive cinematics, exploration, and decision-making. With the addition of the PC's mouse and keyboard setup, some interactions feel more intuitive, while others might be better suited for a game controller.Switching between Jodie and Aiden offers varied gameplay mechanics. However, the gameplay sometimes may feel too guided or linear for those who are accustomed to open-world games or those who seek more freedom in decision-making.The soundtrack, composed by Lorne Balfe, complements the game's emotional beats perfectly. Sound effects and ambient noises are well-produced, and the voice acting is top-notch, adding depth to each character.Beyond: Two Souls on brings a cinematic gaming experience that blurs the line between movies and video games. With its enhanced graphics and the freedom to choose between mouse-keyboard or controller, it caters to a broader audience. While it might not be for everyone, especially those looking for action-packed gameplay, it stands as a testament to what video games can achieve in terms of storytelling and emotional engagement.

_childDocuments_.review: My girlfriend and I haven't completed the game yet but it's been an exceptional experience thus far. She's not much of a gamer so she's playing on the lower difficulty which allows her to immerse herself in the story. The game actually lets each player decide which difficulty they want to play at.If you choose to play the game in "Duo" mode it lets you choose between Jodie and Aiden. Jodie is the face of the action with Aiden taking care of things behind the scenes with his spirit super powers. If you're playing as a couple I really recommend that you let the less experienced gamer take control of Jodie. It's a really unique experience where only one player plays at a time. The game has forced me to sit back and enjoy my girlfriends blunders and just appreciate the way the game plays out because of it. In fact, I've realized, by watching her play, that being new to games creates a lot more tension. The inability to hit buttons accurately all the time means that you really feel the pressure of those quick time events.

_childDocuments_.review: "That day, which you fear as being the end of all things, is the birthday of your eternity."-Seneca the YoungerEpistles CII:::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::SPOILER   ALERT:::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::So, this being my first review of a game on Steam ever,  I will try to be concise and clear as possible even though I am a few years late by this point, sadly.I came first in contact with the game reviewed around 11 years ago, just when it came out and saw the whole playthroughs of then popular streamers. After watching them till the end, I realized that the ending, irrelevant which one, has taken a heavy toll on my emotional side and made me pour out in emotions I have never thought of that a video game as a source of entertainment was able to pull off back then. Main character got me invested and got me to feel into her situation and life circumstances as a big, unified whole.I wanted to buy a game for myself back in the day, but me being exclusively a PC gamer and it being a console exclusive rendered the thought impossible. Happily, some time after we got a PC port and that is the reason why I am writing this review!Finally I got to experience the game first-hand, with unadorned and savage intensity got myself invested again and it made my stance on matter even stronger;---Worth every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ penny!---There is no game without negatives, so I will pass them up as follows;-It being a port from PS3, it inherited just awfully clunky controls and unflexible camera movement that could cost many nerves and healthy reasoning of one trying to..., take control?! It was also time consuming and frustrating for a lifetime PC user to get used to them!-The mission objectives are sometimes not clear or visible enough, which makes one just wandering aimlessly like a last vagabond.-Some of the characters tend not to be fully fleshed out when it comes to their ulterior motives and reasoning behind those just as much as the actions (ie Nathan Hawke).-There is, most of the time, no direct threat to the main protagonist (death/execution/serious injury), which makes the stress and fury of the moment much less serious and bland.-The romances in the game feel way too forced, just like the despised lunch meal given to a kid by his mother. Even though I tried avoiding it, it got me to the point which I avoided the whole time.There may be a thing or two that I maybe missed out, but that´s about it.Everything else not listed could be held as a positive, especially the depiction of the "Infraworld" universe free of any theological or cultural interpretation and hubris, which amazed me and made me to decide myself for Beyond, free of any responsibilities and pain.I tried to find a decent analysis of the game lore itself but I got displeased by the amount of bashing and sh❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️ this title took on every (!) corner. I tried to find justifiable reasoning behind (some of the) critique but came back with none, which made me disappointed in the said critics. My opinion is that they took it too hard on this game back in the day and that´s the primary reason why we wont be seeing any kind of sequel to it, alongside David Cage´s idiosyncratic reasoning and Ellen Page refusing to collaborate with the former, for her own good reasons for sure.I won´t be hailing this one as a perfect and flawless entry of Quantic Dream Studio. It surely is a *great* game, but not an *outstanding* one. It makes me sad to think that this one had limitless potential (character development, chosen path development, dialogue choices etc...) but instead it got either squandered, overlooked or budgeted down to fit certain (sub)standard mold. Maybe if I get my hands on a time machine someday, then maybe I would change some things...If you are looking for a griping story and fine cinematic experience which will leave you thinking for days and maybe even weeks about it, then I would wholeheartedly recommend it. For all the others it is still worth a try!For all the concerned, thank you for the taken time for reading my review and I wish you a nice day!

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to try this after playing Detroit Become Human and being really impressed with the graphics/story etc.Graphically it's very impressive for the time when it was released initially on the PS3.  Cloth dynamics, cinematics are all great.  I did notice some texture popping and graphical glitches even though I had plenty of resources available but apart from that there were no issues.*Spoilers*Story wise is where it's a bit of a let down, it has promise but it fails to deliver in a lot of ways.  Ellen Page is brilliant, I found DeFoe to be a bit wooden or maybe it was my preconceptions of him in that part (nice guy scientist who turns out to be mental, never seen that from him before lol).  The rest of the supporting cast are generally great.The story beats are as subtle as a hit to the face with a bat, there is a lot which seems contradictory or just makes no sense.  In Homeless, Jodie is near unconscious yet Aiden can on his own disturb items and alert Stan.  In Navajo she is knocked unconscious and Aiden protects her, yet in Black Sun she is drugged and this makes him weak? A separate 'spirit' entity is affected by drugs, wtf.  Then he is too weak too dislodge an IV but strong enough to go up a few floors, disturb numerous items.Plenty of other contradictions like this, Aiden is quick enough to protect her from bullets or to prevent her jumping to her death, but too slow to protect her from slow moving blunt object on four occasions. But my biggest problem, on no occasion do you get to attempt to murder Ryan, you know the one who lies, insults, berates, tries to sleep with a subordinate, drives you to contemplate suicide, yeah he's such a good character lol  ;)It's fun for a playthrough, just don't think too deeply about it or the glaring plot holes will make you shake your head :)

_childDocuments_.review: I know this game is already developing a cult-like following of fans, but you might wanna hear me out before you spend your money on this game. First of all, the video trailers and screenshots of the game are mildly misleading. The game seemed to me like an action-packed thriller (which is how the game is described under the description blurb), but the game is anything but thrilling. I don't want to give any spoilers about the story of the game, but all the action occurs during cut scenes. Think of this game as an interactive movie instead of an actual video game and you might actually enjoy it. If you liked the Life is Strange franchise, this is a game for you. Both Life is Strange and Beyond are story-based games where you occasionally can influence minor details of the story based on decisions you make. The problem with these types of games is that there's very little replay-ability. These game provide you with an illusion of being able to influence the plot of the story, but really you only affect very minor details that don't change the outcome of the overall plot.Another thing you should know: this game is unplayable without a controller. I'm serious, the keyboard controls are damn near impossible to use and you'll just end up angry and frustrated without a controller.It's also just kinda creepy having a real live actress playing the role of a character in a video game. Part of what makes a video game so immersive is the character models... and when I played this, all I saw was Ellen Page and not Jodie Holmes. The parts of the game that are actually interesting and immersive are short, and most of the "game play" is spent on very long and drawn out chapters that aren't vital to the overall plot of the game. This game is jam packed with filler chapters that feel more like a lazy afterthought after the developers realized their game was far too short for how much they charge for it. Is it a bad game? eh... depends on who you ask and what kind of gamer you are. I will say this though: the game has too much filler content, the store page severely misrepresents the actual game play, the player models are creepy (like Tom Hanks in the Polar Express), The game lacks immersive qualities to keep the player believing the story, and this game has no room for improvement.Just be mindful of Steam's return policy and be sure to set a timer so you don't go over the limit and get stuck with this game for good. Honestly you could get more enjoyment from just watching someone play this game on YouTube or Twitch.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond: Two Souls had all the potential to be an immersive, narrative-driven journey, but unfortunately, it falls short due to its clunky controls and overly demanding Quick Time Events (QTEs).From the outset, the game presents a captivating premise, promising a deeply emotional and cinematic experience. However, this promise is overshadowed by frustrating gameplay mechanics. The controls feel awkward and unintuitive, often leading to moments of unnecessary frustration as you struggle to execute simple actions.The biggest offender is undoubtedly the Quick Time Events. While QTEs can be an effective way to add tension and interactivity to cutscenes, in Beyond: Two Souls, they feel more like an exercise in frustration than a meaningful gameplay element. Not only are they abundant, but they also demand lightning-fast reflexes, leaving little room for error or immersion.Moreover, the pacing of the game feels disjointed at times, with abrupt shifts between intense action sequences and slower, more contemplative moments. This lack of coherence makes it difficult to fully engage with the narrative, as you're constantly being pulled out of the experience by clunky controls and overly fast-paced QTEs.Despite its flaws, Beyond: Two Souls does have some redeeming qualities. The story, while convoluted at times, is intriguing and kept me invested until the end. The performances of the cast, particularly Ellen Page and Willem Dafoe, are stellar and help to elevate the overall experience.In conclusion, Beyond: Two Souls ultimately feels like a missed opportunity. While it boasts a compelling narrative and strong performances, its frustrating gameplay mechanics detract significantly from the overall experience. Unless you're willing to overlook its flaws in favor of its story, I'd recommend approaching this game with caution.

_childDocuments_.review: I first played 'Beyond: Two Souls' back during its initial release on the PS3 and I was excited to revisit again on the PC.Just to get this out of the way, the keyboard/mouse controls are pretty bad. I ended up using game controllers instead (I alternated between a PS4 controller and a Steam controller for achievements; both worked fine) and the experience was much better. If this review had a numerical score I would dock a few points for the keyboard controls but it wouldn't change my recommendation.'Beyond' follows Jodie Holmes (Elliot Page) a young woman with a mysterious entity tethered to her. Willem Dafoe also co-stars as a scientist who is also her surrogate father. The game has received a lot of criticism for its story over the years but in my opinion its a solid one. The sci-fi elements don't always work but it's a compelling story overall; the story works best when it focuses on the human drama. Acting-wise I felt Page gave one of their best performances in the game and it's worth experiencing it for that alone. As far as gameplay goes, some sections are largely story-based whereas others are more action-oriented. Jodie will often rely on stealth while with Aiden you can possess people or just cause chaos. There's a fair amount of QTEs but overall I found the game to be fun to play. There's also a bonus level in the style of 'Portal' where Jodie and Aiden navigate through different obstacles and solve puzzles which is a highlight.Graphics-wise, the game is stunning. The character models and scenery are almost photorealistic at times.Control issues aside I highly recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond: Two Souls is an incredible interactive adventure that leaves an unforgettable impression. The game stands out with its deep and touching story, allowing players to experience every event alongside the main character. This makes the narrative more personal and emotional.All the characters in the game are charismatic and well-developed. Each of them has unique traits that make them memorable and lifelike. The main heroine evokes genuine empathy throughout the story, which is one of the game’s strongest points.The gameplay is simple and accessible, even for beginners. However, to fully immerse yourself in the story, I recommend starting the playthrough from the heroine’s childhood rather than the end. This approach helps you better understand her personality, motives, and life journey.This game is a truly outstanding interactive movie, perfect for those who value a quality story-line and strong emotions. Without a doubt, it’s a game worth purchasing and playing.=====================================================================================Graphics: 7/10Story: 9/10Gameplay: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: After three games, I guess Quantic Dream games are just not my type. The movie-like directing creates limitations that I just find annoying. So far it is the most balanced of their creations, but I have Detroit: Become Human to play still.As before, the actual gameplay is the weakest part. When interacting with people and items, you can't always be certain that what you meant to do or say, is what you will do in the game. The same ambiguity is also present in the combat. While the overall story and choices will probably go the way you intend to, the uncertainty is always there. It does not help that you interact with objects with the right thumb stick, which is also used for turning the camera. I'm also unsure what difference my choices made, if any. The direction and writing could also be improved. Was that really the best time to start talking about feelings, how about trying to survive first? Some events are just too unbelievable, mostly because the game has to wait for your reaction to events while trying to keep a fast pace. There are some interesting chapters and characters, and those are fun to play. These are usually the calmer ones with less emphasis on action.

If you enjoyed Heavy rain, this is right up your alley. The actors also gave so much emotion and depth to the characters and I felt my decisions were motivated by how I felt in the moment and what I learned in previous chapters. A+ game and I look forward to future titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent narrative game. Voice acting is incredible, and the story is great. It does an excellent job of bringing the characters to life and making the player care about them - plus, the ending is very satisfying (a rarity in this genre for some reason). _childDocuments_.review: The Games story looks like it would be interesting and I'm loath to give a not recommend review.Unfortunately as others have mentioned something is off with the QTE tracking and there does not appear to be a fix for it.To explain in more detail, certain QTE's that cause a slow-mo effect (combat or chase sequences) won't register the majority of your inputs.From testing on the "tutorial" of this QTE version I suspect what happens is the mouse controls tolerate no wiggle on the direction. Which is fine if you're using a controller, however if you're using a mouse your motion will naturally curve based on your hands reach. This hasn't yet blocked progress as failing them hasn't caused a game over but it's almost certainly putting the game down the "bad" end. More importantly it's making the game quite frustrating as valid inputs are not being counted.

_childDocuments_.review: The controls. Bad is not a strong enough word to describe them (playing with keyboard and mouse).This game is a movie which constantly pauses, and you have to press random buttons to keep it playing. That's the good part of the game.The bad parts are those where you actually think you can control the main character. If you went through the tutorial you may have the illusion that you know how the game works. You don't. The tutorial is just an example of how it *might* work.You learn that you sometimes need to click and drag the mouse towards you. Or away from you. Or sideways. Sometimes you need to click only one mouse button. Sometimes you need to click both. But you are never quite sure which combination is the right one at the current moment, unless those handy icons show up that tell you which way it is.This way you can fail missions without even knowing what you did wrong. You think you are doing good, and suddenly the camera starts to change position, shake, move, show the character from a different angle... "What is going on?" you ask. "Can I control something? Am I supposed to do something now?". And suddenly the mission fails.This stupidity made me rage quit the game and I even tried to get a refund. But it was too late for that. I've had the game in my collection for too long. So I guess I'll have to force myself through this pile of garbage only because I've paid for it.Not recommended at all. Not the tiniest bit. Don't buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: For years I wanted to try this game - I stayed away from it to keep it spoiler free if I ever did play it since the story is the majority of what makes these games fun. Boy, what a regret. I acknowledge i'm playing this years after it's release, but none of it's issues I believe are symptoms of the times.***SLIGHT SPOILERS***PROS:CINEMATOGRAPHY~The way the camera is utilised, and the cinematography is really well presented. Often the camera takes the perspective of Aiden and acts as if you're him watching Jodie play the game - other scenes, like chases, it weaves beautifully through the environment. This is also a problem as the least "gamey" thing a game could do is the best part of the game xD.The acting and cast is excellent, I also love how they recognise the lead as Elliot Page on steam! Nice.CONS:STORY~The story is horrid, the way the developer intended you to play it spoils any sort of surprise, or joy or anything really, and the alternative spoils things apparently. None of your decisions matter the first 8 hours and you know no matter what you do nothing will change, as the story bounces from past to present to future and the only visual representation of a choice is whether Jodie is dressed in punk clothing or traditional clothing in one (horribly written) scene genuinely titled "not like other girls". There are no divulging paths, no matter the choices you play the same chapters as everyone else, in the same order, with the same choices spanning from them. You are just watching Jodie make decisions and often don't get to choose otherwise (like taking over someone's mind to go to a bar - which in itself has a disturbing scene, only avoided if you intentionally get caught which you have 3 chances to not allow).The story becomes 'Merica and ruins any sort of potential the first 4 hours had. Really unfortunate they drop the supernatural potential for some militant cr@p that is so generic and trope filled you can call everything happening before it does. I kept playing thinking "This is so highly regarded, there must be a twist and it must get good!" but nope. I don't think this is a sign of the times. Even the "final reveal" so to speak is so predictable I thought they already told me this information earlier in the game.CONTROLS~This is a PC specific issue I imagine - the controls are HORRENDOUS. They are unresponsive, incorrectly work 20% of the time, and counter-intuitive. The QTE scenes especially. In a way it's good there are NO REPROCUSSIONS for missing any (makes you wonder why they even exist if they don't influence the story at all) and just are annoying more than exciting or nerve wracking. As I said - likely still a PC issue with KBM.In summary, if you want a story-driven narrative game, this is not worth the money and go play Life Is Strange, or The Wolf Among Us or anything else - as someone who has played a lot of games in the genre this is the worst I have ever played hands down.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: a well crafted interactive story, although a bit slow at some points, graphics/music/acting is fine, gameplay is OK (less than OK with mouse and keyboard), and choices don't really matter.The story is essentially a build-up on "A girl has an imaginary friend, but the friend is actually real." You can feel the writers brainstorming to flesh out the details.I call this an interactive story rather than a video game, because it's very linear, out of the cutscenes (sometimes you don't get a clear cue that you're actually out) you just move around, iteract with objects, and you press or mash or hold the buttons it tells you to. Some scenes are very mundane and could've been scrapped, e.g. at some point you have to clean your appartment, shower, cook and do the dishes... Many other moments consists in walking around trying to find things in the environment to interact with (in a fairly pointless way), waiting for some trigger for the story to progress. At the end of a chapter, it tells you what choices you made and how it reflects compared to all players. But many of the choices are either about the pointless interactions I mentioned prior (I, like 64% of other players, did NOT take a cookie from the cookie jar!), or whether you pushed the right buttons at the right time.The most frustrating part was probably due to the mouse and keyboard. There's one point where you have to open a bottle of wine, so you have to make a circle with the mouse to use the bottle opener. I almost quit because I couldn't make the circle it asked for, and couldn't move on with the story... But the main problem came from the choices of the game designer regarding the viewpoint. The camera position moves around according to the director's choice, like a movie director telling the cameraman where and what to shoot. The character has either some leeway for viewing direction, or a lot, but you never know. Also the character has to move depending on the camera, not the player's orientation. So sometimes you're moving straight, pressing the up key, and the camera turns to the right to show something in the background, and now, since your character is shown from the left side moving to the left on the screen, you have to press the left key to keep moving straight. This mechanic is particularly frustrating during the few combat portions, where you have to key in left or right according to how the character moves on screen, not according to what arm/leg the she is moving. There's a combat training scene, I must have repeated that one at least ten times before getting it right...Anyway, I'm glad I played it. I'm also glad to move on.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not really sure how to describe this, but I wouldn't necessarily go as far as calling it a game. Of all the interactive stories I've played (that are sold as "games"), this must be the least game like of all of them. For most of this it felt like a story being told and I was just dragged along for the ride. There is no sense of peril and I didn't die once (and I suspect that isn't even possible). Removing any fear further, the chapters of the main character's life are played out in a somewhat random order meaning you pretty much know whatever happens during her younger life, you are going to get through it. I don't really know why this was done as I don't feel it adds anything to the game and think I would have enjoyed it more had the story been laid out in chronological order.Other than the walking about, there are some QTE type parts which for the most, I felt were quite poor. Combat and avoiding things is just you moving the controller the way the character is moving, but most of the time you can't really see which way your character is moving so it is very hit and miss whether you pull off the correct move, which is fairly irrelevant anyway because fail or succeed, you still get through the chapter.As for the story itself, it was nothing like I was expecting (which given I had no idea what the story was about before playing isn't that much of a surprise), but it was a fairly decent story by videogame standards and nearing something of movie quality (which I suspect is what the designer was aiming for, or he really wanted to make films but never got the opportunity).Overall, this is a fairly enjoyable experience but not something I would class as a game. But if you are enjoying it, does it really matter what it is?
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: While the story is not bad, frankly I can name a few games like Bioshock that have more addictive storylines and characters. The acting, animations and mo-cap are top notch though. You WILL play and grow to CARE for the protagonist, you may get emotional; as someone with a traumatized childhood and deceased sibling, I certainly thought about the "what-ifs" in my past.After finally completing the entire story (tolerating mediocre controls), my biggest complain is the needless, bloated, pointless interactions in short "filler" chapters. For example the one on a "dinner date", why was I spending 20 mins walking around main character's apartment cleaning up garbage, cooking, taking a shower...? Do I as an audience really need to watch all these? Why did I even need to manually do them?!Bottom line, there is no real decision to make, nor consequences in those chapters, and there is also no way to skip them (even if you played through the story before), it made me feel like a few hours were wasted.All in all, it was not a bad game, not "stay away" bad; but it was not good enough to go on the "must play once in your lifetime" list.---------------------------------Control wise....this is where I think it should never be on the PC Steam store...Holy hell. After 3 chapters I just can't continue with mouse and keyboard.The camera is fixed and constantly sliding in directions pre-set by the game; you can't move it or rotate it or fishfry it or whatever. You also can't freely look around you at all, just simple things like looking around in a closed room, you can't do it.With WASD movements, it is so weird, for example if you want to go "right", you press D, then the camera starts moving and your character starts going diagonal then forward/backwards instead.It's absolutely ass when you want to change where you're facing to trigger an action. (direction specific)Then the mouse...its absolute nightmare if you have low sensitivity; and by low, I mean 800 dpi is already low.For example, there were actions that had to be done by "holding LMB then drag your mouse down", I dragged my mouse across the entire mouse pad and still had not finished it...I was interested in continuing the story but this feels such a chore to keep going.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond: Two Souls was one of my first ever Narrative, choices matter games. My first was Heavy Rain. Beyond: Two Souls is a game that I loved when I was younger playing on my PS3 back in 2013. I loved the concept of the game - being able to control 2 people. Jodie and Aiden. I thought it was revolutionary back then in storytelling but coming back to it now... I can feel how out of place the story was.Here I am playing it in 2024 to 100% completion. I do have a few personal... opinions about how Beyond: Two Souls has been handled which I will reflect upon below but first a quick disclaimer!   So Beyond: Two Souls tell's the story of Jodie, a young girl with a special "gift" looking for some sort of answers to her life and Aiden, a paranormal entity (which you find out more about) which is tethered to Jodie and protects her at all costs. However, the story is fragmented. What I mean by that is it tells you the middle of the story, start of the story, end of the story then back to start, then middle e.t.c e.t.c e.t.c. With this way of storytelling it completely undermines how good the story could be. One moment you can be training in a CIA facility honing your skills to all of a sudden be back playing as a 6 year old girl being "experimented on" by DPA/CIA or government officials. Then you can be in some sort of war torn part of the world sent to assassinate some politician to all of a sudden be in the Mojave desert fighting a big sand entity with the natives. Why is this an issue you might ask? To some, this might be hard to keep up with or in general - understand. Not only that there are some parts of the story that just made no damn sense whatsoever - The Mojave desert bit where you fight the big SAND entity. Why was this needed? It added NOTHING to the story and just felt like pointless filler. This part (and thing):   So for this part I want to mention 1 thing that got on my nerves - Your choices don't really matter if you think about it and the relationships felt out of place. What I mean by this is you can kiss Ryan and have a relationship with him or NOT kiss Ryan and still have a relationship with him.... what? You can let Ryan have his eye cut out, be mean to him, turn him down over and over again and still... end up with him. So in the end... your choices do not matter at all for this. Yes you can get multiple endings where you can and cannot be with him but that is the END of the game making any choice before hand... pointless.The way the story is told makes having feelings for any character pointless. At no point did I feel any remorse, sympathy or emotional attachment to anyone in this game. I also feel as if the relationships are forced onto the player which I did not like. Your choices throughout the story have the same outcome in the end until roughly the end of the game where people could die. The train segment is a prime example of this. On the train you get an achievement for not getting caught by the cops leading to a lengthy police chase on the train and trains roof, then a bike ride, then a scene in a town where Aiden protects Jodie and she escapes. Then you have the other option to get caught 3 times for an achievement called houdini. You get caught on the train, handcuffed. You escape the cuffs on the train to the roof and then the bike ride. Fail the QTE's and your caught again and hand cuffed. Escape again, fail the QTE's and cuffed again. Then you escape for good this time. Why not throw it in here where Jodie could die and it ends the story? No matter what you do, it leads to the same outcome and thus, made choices practically useless. The graphics still hold their own to this date and if you played the original console editions (PS3 mainly) you will notice a direct improvement to the graphics. Beyond: Two Souls on PC comes with a higher resolution, improved graphic textures and so much more. All of these improvements add add an extra layer of immersion onto the game, especially with the facial animations ad character models as you can actually see their subtle body emotions speak for themselves. The environments are packed with more detail and better textures compared to the original versions also and the dynamic lighting is an excellent addition as it adds a little more... cinematic feel? (for lack of better words). With these improvements  on PC, I reckon this will make Beyond: Two Souls last a lot longer before age kicks in again. I mean, just look at this scene here:   To this date we have still been waiting for a Beyond: Two Souls 2. The ending of the story heavily implied that there was more to come, here... have a look yourself and you tell me:   I have my theories as to WHY we will never get a sequel but I am going to keep that to myself.  I think that the developers changing the description of the game on Steam to state - "A unique psychological action thriller delivered by A-list Hollywood performances by Elliot Page and Willem Dafoe" - Is false because "Elliot Page" did not exist back then when this game was made and to top that off, the credits do not mention an Elliot Page at all. In fact, I will show you who the game mentions - Ellen Page:  I feel as if the world is being tilted to one side and all the good things are being ruined one by one by this new generation... this new phase... this new... whatever you want to call it. We need to tiptoe around EVERY single aspect nowadays and seeing ELLEN PAGE's name still in the credits means that ELLEN PAGE was the actor that done this game, not this ELLIOT PAGE.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the most unique in my huge library of Steam (and non-Steam) titles and is definitely a must-play.It used to be there in my PlayStation wishlist for a few years, then on my Steam wishlist, and then waited in my library at the top of the list of games I wanted to play. Now that I did play it, I'm glad I picked it.I played in the original sequence (not the chronological order), and boy it is a roller coaster ride! The levels (or episodes, if I may) occur at different points in the timeline of the story, and you're taken back and forth between every single chapter, so you have to merge it all in your mind to get a clear picture of what the character is going through during a particular chapter. The game features several genres in one, some of which include: point-and-click adventure, action, horror, stealth, slight puzzle-solving, driving, and many more.I played it on Linux on my relatively older hardware and yet was able to run it at 4K with reasonable framerates. Gladly I also used my Steam controller, and the game made me realize all the capabilities my controller had by making me perform those gestures that I do not remember I've ever used in a video game.During the start of the game when I realized that there are multiple choices, I decided to give it at least one more playthrough, but with the few episodes being very touchy, I doubt I would ever be able to pick it up and go through the emotional adventure again, especially given how many untouched titles I have in my library (at least at the time of this writing). Also, I'm not sure if I'd want to go through those few tearful moments again, as you might call me weak, but I consider myself over-emotional with this kind of content. If I were to play it again, I'd go in chronological order, and make sure I pick the choices I didn't go with during my first playthrough.This isn't a video game, in fact, an emotional interactive story that you can drive with the decisions your character makes. There are combat scenes that need time-based input, but failing them doesn't deter you from the story much as the game is smart enough to bring you back to the major story no matter how you play it.I love the attention to detail in the game. One example is how the face of Jodie changes on the menu screen depending on the episode you're playing. This was very noticeable for me as I barely ever have the time to play for more than an hour.I know this is probably my lengthiest review on Steam, but  .

_childDocuments_.review: I love Quantic Dream. Beyond is one of the weaker games that they made, but this game is still better than many story-based games you can buy. There is an excellent cast of actors that do a fantastic job. The story is good and there is a "surprise" at the end. I play the game the way it was designed and not in the chronological order. I have a few complaints about B:TS. The first is that, unlike heavy rain, it is unclear on what to do with the right stick on some prompts. There are dots on the screen that you direct your analogue stick to so you can "use" or interact with whatever item/person it is. The combat system is terrible. I found it hard to figure out if they wanted me to push left or down sometimes. I also did not enjoy controlling Aiden. He is floaty and doesn't always go where I want him to. Another complaint I have is that I felt no real danger or fear for Jodie until the very end. Several times, she should have died in my playthrough. I played this on PS4 the first time.A playthrough will take 9 or 10 hours. I played in offline mode for about 2 hours and it never updated my progress or achievements that I would have unlocked. I will most likely play this every 5 years or so. If you like this you should get Heavy Rain and Detroit: Become Human.

_childDocuments_.review: To me, it's the worst part of the Quantic Dream Collection that you can buy on Steam. I can understand the narrative the game aims for with memories being kind of broken, at the same time social problems and mental health issues are important and some of the events felt quite relatable, but the game just doesn't feel good to play through. It felt too tedious after 4 hours into the story, none of the things you do matter, because the whole game is a giant flashback essentially, it only shows you how Jodie remembers things, but it doesn't mean that they really happened like this. Of course, with small changes and small choices you can find out a little more about the characters, but in the end it comes down to a story that at times just doesn't feel like a connected plot, even in "Remixed" mode, because some things happen without your input and your actions in the previous chapters might be scrapped in the next one, which makes sense because of Jodie's broken memory, but doesn't make sense as a cohesive movie and works against being an interactive game. This is probably the lowest point in interactive dramas by Quantic Dream, as the controller basically gets in a way of the story without really contibuting in a meaningful way, and compared to Heavy Rain, it's used in interesting ways much less often, so the game just feels like a very long inchesive movie.

_childDocuments_.review: First let me say DO NOT play this on the Steam Deck, if you must, play on the steam deck plugged into a tv with an Xinput controller attached. As of 12/26/2023 I would consider this game to be unplayable on the deck controller. The gameplay largely consists of an arrow showing up on the screen pointing a direction, and you are supposed to point the right thumb stick in that same direction, I started on my deck and almost gave up because about 1/3rd of the time it just did not register the direction correctly and told me I messed up when I definitely pointed it in the right direction, I was starting to question myself but then I just used an xbox controller and got through the rest of the game without missing a single one so it is definitely a deck problem. It also utilizes the deck gyro in the worst way possible by making you shake the whole ass steam deck in some parts, AND it is in a forced 21:9 aspect ratio so you will have huge black bars on the 16:10 aspect ratio of the deck.Otherwise, WOW was this game awesome!! Obviously it is a game primarily focused on story so the gameplay really only consists of timed button presses and stick movement, as well as navigating around environments mostly with a fixed camera. The story was phenomenal it def took me a few chapters to really get into it but the last 2 days I played 4 hours each day to finish it and it was a very easy thing to binge because the story is so good. I was not a fan of the 21:9 aspect ratio because like just let me play the game full screen but it was fine on a large TV. I also was not a fan of how in many cases when trying to trigger a flashback it makes you push the sticks together and I could not really figure out the trick to make it work right and sometimes just had to sit there holding the sticks together for upwards of a minute before it finally triggered the flashback, I also was not a fan of the stealth gameplay in a few scenes but they were few and far between, and of course I was not a fan of the fixed camera in a lot of the scenes. The story was definitely good enough to overlook these minor inconveniences and just keep on playing with maximum engagement, the only time it really took me out of it was during the war scene when you need to assassinate the guy the stealth gameplay just took too long in that one and it took me out of it for awhile but the story at the end of that chapter was good enough for it to be worth it just so many twists and turns in the story of this game I love it. Story based games are my favorite but with Jodie and Aiden's powers it would be super cool to see a bigger game that let you use the powers in more creative ways but still for what it is this game is fantastic and very easy to recommend as long as you don't plan on playing directly on the steam deck

_childDocuments_.review: I gave up on Beyond: Two Souls before the end credits. It’s too frustrating for me. I have a pretty lenient view on game design in general. I don’t need Beyond to compete with any other game. It’s free to express itself in whichever way it wants. And it’s also free to embrace me as a player in whatever way it needs to. But something’s not working for me here. There’s something about how I’m just along for the ride, never in the driver’s seat. It’s frustrating. The game is obviously asking for my input -- pressing buttons, jiggling analog sticks. But these moments are so inconsistent. There are loads of moments in the game, where it sort of suggests that I get ready and remember my training from the previous chapters. Only to either disregard me completely -- doing its own thing without me -- or changing the expected prompts. That’s annoying, because this game is all about being reactive. Looking for the symbols on-screen and following suit. Walking around freely is a privilege. Still, it makes the process so unpredictable. I constantly have to second guess myself. Never knowing if the game is asking me to react according to relative directions or absolute ones. So I press something, and fumble. And never really know what went wrong. Or did it? The screen flashes red. Yet, I obviously dodged the blow. Was it the timing? It’s also impossible for me to know what’s at stake at any given time; whether my successes and failures matter. In one moment it’s shrugging them off like they don’t. But in the next, one jolt has apparently changed the course of history. It feels like one of those “you had one job”- moments. If everything that’s required of me is so simple in terms of input, why does it always feel so ambiguous? Sometimes it just feels like I’m doing the equivalent of scrubbing through a Youtube video. But one with random bits of meaningful interaction thrown in, just to make sure I’m not sleeping on the job.Thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Two Souls, or even better, the Quantic Dream Collection, are definitely worth checking out if you're the type of person that is entertained by a rich story.  The game play often leaves something to be desired, but these games will give you something different, a breath of fresh air, with every other new game being a generic, open world, live service, RPG wanna be, piece of crap.  Beyond Two Souls is completely linear.  There's very little exploration to be done, which helps to keep the story moving.  It's actually nice to play a game where I don't have to scrounge or grind for anything.  Beyond Two Souls is the type of game that is more like an interactive movie than a full on video game.  This is the first game in the series, so it's not as good as the other two, but still well worth playing.This game has its fair share of flaws.  I came across one glitch, but it was game breaking until I restarted the game.  There are levels where the main character, Jodie, who is played by Ellen Page, is a young girl or a teen.  These levels are kinda necessary for you to fully understand the story line, but they can get pretty boring at times.  Actually, I remember starting this game years ago when I got it free on PS+.  I got to the part where Jody is using her abilities to choose cards and it hit me, playing a game as a child couldn't possible be fun or entertaining, so I quit, and I was spot on.  Although, if I had just be patient I would have really enjoyed the game as a whole.  This game is the type of game that gives you multiple choices and each choice you make shapes the outcome to a certain extent.  The story line is headed in one direction, and you can't really change it too much.  But your choices do determine the details and who you will be interacting with in the game.  There is a level where Jodie is on a date, and unless you have an interest in hearing two peoples small talk you will literally find yourself waiting for it to end.  Although, this game does offer the opportunity to be much more entertaining.  You can be a complete monster in this game if you want to be.  You can run around attacking and killing some of the other characters.  I'm trying to write this review without any spoilers so I don't want to go into too much detail.  I chose to be a decent person, so I found myself just watching through a lot of the cut scenes.  I call them cut scenes, but most of the scenes where it's mostly dialogue, you can often times still interact with the environment through Jodie's entity, Aiden.  A lot of the game play has to do with finding a way to navigate through the levels using Aiden, who is basically like a ghost that you can control pretty much whenever you want.  Aiden can manipulate or move things to open doors, distract or attack people.Another thing I found irritating was all the little things that got overlooked or didn't make sense.  Just small details that were either overly embellished or ignored.  It happened quite a few times throughout the game, I'd find myself catching something that didn't make any sense and I'd start complaining about it out loud to my TV.  Just little stuff like people not seeing you even though you just killed someone right in front of their face.  The way this game is designed, it's not intended to be super hard and I can't recall any situations where I messed up so bad I was forced to start over without doing it myself because I was unhappy with an outcome.  The game is pretty forgiving.  There are just some little things that came across as lazy to me.OMG though, the worst part about this game is the controls. I played with an X1 controller and even that was clunky at times.  I have seen a good number of people complaining about mouse and keyboard controls.  I definitely would not recommend playing this game like that unless you're a masochist.  The game has a lot of quick time events where you have to be quick and press a button to achieve a positive outcome, but sometimes you're literally just guessing at what button they want you to press.  Although, I did find that even the quick time events are pretty forgiving.  You can mess up pretty bad and still get a positive outcome.  One of the things they rely on a lot is button mashing in quick time events, which I hate.  The worst part about the controls though is the camera.  It can be such a massive pain sometimes, and darn near impossible on occasion.  It's some of the most annoying camera control mechanics I can recall in a game in a long time.I am happy to say that they definitely put a polish on the graphics.  This in no way comes across as a PS3 game that was simply ported to the PC.  They definitely enhanced the textures, and there are a lot of spots where the game actually looks really good.  Performance optimization is pretty good, the game at 4K max settings utilized about 60% of my over clocked 2080 Ti.  There are very few graphics options to choose from, I just set them all to high.  There is one little issue that might bug some people and which is this game natively has black bars on the top and bottom like a movie.  It's like that to give you a wider POV, but I just found it annoying.  If you go into the Steam forums, or the Beyond  Two Souls discussions,  you can find a solution to this issue if you search for it.  The only trouble with it is that it narrows the POV and cuts off a lot of the captions.  I usually like to have captions on in case I miss any dialogue, but I just shut them off because I hate the black bars more.  Even though the POV was narrowed, I never once noticed it in the game play.  I published a bunch of screen shots of what you can expect with 4K max settings and no black bars, you can see them on my Steam profile, just search by game and select Beyond Two Souls.Audio quality is pretty good.  I did find at times though that the music was over powering the dialogue so I had to turn it down to 80% so I could hear what everyone was saying during the action scenes.Overall this game still holds up pretty well in 2020.  A lot of the in game characters are professional actors and their performance was excellent most of the time.  At no point in the game did anyone come across as cheesy to me.  Actually, I was thinking that this would be a great game for someone who's into movies but not good at video games.  The only hurdle to overcome would be learning the controls.  If you bought or are thinking about buying the Quantic Dream Collection, then it's my recommendation that you play the games in chronological order.  Because even though Beyond Two Souls is still a great game, it's the least good game in the collection.  Then Heavy Rain, and Detroit Become Human is a masterpiece.  Heavy Rain was actually really, really good too.  I would give this game a 7 out 10.  It's not perfect, but it's definitely worth checking out for the price.  Especially if you're an Ellen Page fan, her performance in this game was outstanding, although they have her crying A LOT.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best game of its genre I've ever played. Minor spoilers ahead.Now I have played my fair share of story-choice games. I've played The Quarry, Detroit Become Human, the first two season of TWD, Minecraft story mode, Little Hope, Until Dawn etc. Now all of the ones I mentioned with the exception of Little Hope are good in their own right and I really enjoyed The Quarry and Detriot; Become Human they're  in my top 3 for the genre. But wow this game is something else it was Stranger Things before Stranger Things and I know they said they weren't influenced, but the similarities are uncanny. Girl with magical powers and a shaved head with connection to a different world tries to get captured by government that she escapes from and the government tries to open a rift to that world etc etc you get the gist. But this isn't just your average tale of a girl with supernatural abilities it is a heartbreaking tale of someone who just wants a normal life just to be like others but can't. Everyone she encounters are truly awful for the most part with the exception of a few. Each chapter feels so well crafted and movie-esque you will never feel bored. You also wont feel that this game drags on too long, in fact I got teary eyed and had a lump in my chest when the ending rolled. The graphics for a game this old are better than a lot of games nowadays which says something. Truly a marvelous gem of a game that I should've played sooner 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really know where to start. Having played through it 3 times so far. They did great with this game. Watched the making of. They sunk substantial money into this. It is very cinematic (but not over the top), so if you don't like those types, back away.  I don't think a video game or movie has EVER taken me on a ride like that. The only bad thing I can say about it is the ending seemed a little forced and you might have to switch difficulty level alot for Aiden because controls were pretty hard to learn. it will give  you directionals with the low difficulty setting. The Mission level was the most fun I've had in a VG in a long time. Jody has pretty bad f**kin luck. This poor girl could never catch a break throughout the whole game, and the way she powers through it is pretty inspiring. Jody went through alot of pain (mind and body). The NPCs rely on her alot. But she never lets them down (if you decide not to). Aiden is fun and VERY powerful (like X-Men type ♥♥♥♥), i loved exploring the environments with him everywhere we went. Jody and Aiden will leave you feeling a bittersweet kinda hurt, and you want more than anything for ♥♥♥♥ to go right for her. Character's are well written. Most of them you can guess where they've been and where they'll end up. Graphics are outstanding. They put time into making this game look as real as a movie. _childDocuments_.review: So I got this for 10€ and after I finished it, I still feel like I paid too much for what this non-game had to offer. I like adventure games, but as it turned out, this is not an adventure game. In fact, it's not even a game. It's mostly a series of cut-scenes where you press a button to continue the cut-scene. And even that is optional. There doesn't seem to be any way to actually fail.The parts of it that actually do feel like a game are ruined by the horrible controls. You are constantly going to fight the camera and struggle to walk around. Just looking behind you requires you to swipe your mouse 7-10 times over your mouse pad. Walking straight is an ordeal. Your character turns left and right on her own and the camera constantly changes angle, requiring you to fight against it even more.It is clear that whoever made this game does not understand the most basic concepts of video games. I suspect this is what happens when people who don't play video games at all are tasked with making a video game.The story itself is engaging for 90% of it, which is the only reason I stuck with it. Until I got to the end, that is, where I rolled my eyes so hard, they flew out of my skull. I'm now struggling to find the thumb down button because of my empty eye sockets.

_childDocuments_.review: It's beyond me how anyone can take Quantic Dreams games seriously.They're trying to be these big narrative experiences, but end up with a writing worse than FMV games from the 90's.  i went into this one expecting some sort of improvment, because the premise sounded interesting. It's a story about Jodie, who grows up with a ghost entity called Aiden and we "play" through their life, from childhood to adulthood. Okay, i was intrigued, but after like 8 - 9 hours, i can tell you that it's just as, painful as other previous QD games. The classic problems are present. One particulary obnoxious one, is when characters are a-holes for no reason, just so we can feel for our bland protagonist, It's artificial melodrama at it's worst.That's not all. The game original played in non-linear fashion, but since i heard it being often critisized, i opted for remixed version, which plays in chronological order. Yet, even then it feels like it's all over the place. at one it goes from winter homeless adventures, to native american exorcism in the desert, to heartbreaking family moment. I'd be more forgiving of this game's random nature, if it had been well written, but no. Again, the characters are either bland or comically evil and, as i hinted at it before, the writing is atrocious. i guess it's slightly better than previous QD games, but that's not saying much. There are often moments, that feel very nonsensical. Like for example, there are situations where Jodie gets knocked out, but isn't warned or saved by Aiden, even though we saw him do that before. We're talking about overpowered poltergeist, who can heal, posses and use a barrier and hovers around the protagonist all the time, yet he just let it all happen. Was he taking a nap?   To be less negative - The acting is mostly fine and actors are trying their hardest, even though the dialogue sucks.And what about gameplay? or the lack there of? The best way to describe this mess, is that it's a movie pretending to be a game. The moments where you control Jodie are mostly just a giant waste of time. You can also control Aiden, and while they are the most interesting part, they are often very linear. Like you can only do, what the game wants you to do. You can also enjoy the game with your buddies, because it has multiplayer, for some bizzare reason. FEAR 3 had something simillar, but that was a shooter, where both players had something to do. Here it's very pointless, because you are mostly in control of one character, while the other one has nothing to do.i guess i can mention more things, like the fact, that while are there multiple endings, the major decisions comes right at the end, where you just pick out of the list of options. Honestly, this game was just boring. At least Heavy Rain had plenty of dumb things to laugh at, but here? The bad moments are just more eye-rolling, than funny. There are some improvements i appreciate and even sections i liked, but as a whole, i can't reccomend it. There are better interactive movie/adventure games out there, like the first season of The Walking Dead, that's well written, with characters that feel real and not like they were written by an alien.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I sometimes struggle with games that have complex plots, so I chose to play Beyond: Two Souls in chronological order. This approach helped me mostly understand the story, which was compelling.  It's also worth mentioning I played this on a controller, I don't know how good or bad the keyboard & mouse controls are. The graphics were impressive for its 2013 release; while still good today, they don't quite match modern standards. The gameplay is a unique blend of video game and movie, offering numerous choices. However, I was disappointed by how few of these choices have meaningful, long-term impacts on the story. The game is divided into many chapters, and your decisions seem to only affect the immediate chapter rather than having lasting consequences. The choices that truly matter and influence the ending are mostly concentrated in the final chapters. My disappointment likely stems from having played Detroit: Become Human first. In Detroit, choices have a more significant impact on the story, even in the long term. Despite this, I enjoyed my experience with Beyond: Two Souls. It felt like watching a good movie that you enjoy once but probably won't revisit anytime soon. Instead of replaying the whole game to see the different endings, I'll likely watch them online.

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased on sale for 160 baht.I don't what to say. It really is a journey through an extraordinary person's life. But oh so relatable and sometimes mundane yet beautiful. The reviews promised me something great, and I wasn't disappointed. My life feels enriched by this story and world that became a part of mine. Many of my core values felt affirmed. My favorite chapter is Homeless. I love having a say in how the story goes and how Jodie/Aiden reacts to people and events. I really feel empowered by the choices to express myself inside of the world. I'm looking forward to seeing how my adventure all wraps up in the final four chapters and maybe purchasing other Quantic game titles afterward. Even though it has been repeated many times, I really loved the performances in this. And the detailed environments just beg to be explored.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this one sucked, at least in its second half did. You see, the game start strong. Mixing clever game mechanics with a supernatural background - plus William Dafoe! - 8 hours in you feel you had your fill and the game should come to a conclusion somehow. Unlike their other titles here the QTEs feel inconsequential, but the setting is 'fantastic' enough to captivate you and there's a little gimmick which I won't spoil that makes interacting with the world around you very, very fun indeed. BUT:a) It's built around a single GIMMICK. When you step outside of it, especially as they attempted to mix their usual QTE and hamfisted control scheme into an action game and it simply doesn't work. In fact, the devs KNOW it doesn't work because your character can't die -I know, i tried. The game is programmed to always end the same way, unlike their previous and subsequent titles. Furthermore, the gimmick quickly loses its novelty value, which leads the script writer to err on the goofy side as they clearly  ran out of ideas. b) UNLIKE their next title: Detroit: Becoming Human, where you can do very ethical, or very unethical things without feeling judged or patronized, Beyond Two Souls, on the other hand, has a message for you. And that's "killing foreign Presidents" (the kind who lead roving bands of mobsters through the streets shooting civilians, you know, that kind of president) is BAD, but massacring waves of US SWAT units is totally warranted and fine. cries out the main character after completing her first assignment, almost killing 2 other people in her hissy fit (without any remorse). However, she spends exactly zero time wondering about the sons and daughters of , I don't know , the 200 to 300 police officer she kills in the most violent and brutal way possible throughout the game without any remorse whatsoever.It's hard not to laugh when she blows the head of a cop is a regular, almost daily thing, but when confronted when 'hacking' a cash machine, her strong 'ethics' make her hesitate. I'm terribly disapointed in this title, especially because a) i consider their next title: D:BH, as one of the finest video game ever crafted and b) the initial first 6 hours of B:2S were so strong and set the scene so well.Thumb down from me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still trying to recover from the rollercoaster of mediocrity it took me on. Forget Detroit, this one left me questioning my life choices. Everything's executed... decently. Simple gameplay, graphics that manage not to induce eye-rolling, and a story that's, I gotta say, exists.
