_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever played a game that gave me more shivers down my spine than Beyond: Two Souls.What an emotional rollercoaster! It is worth buying for the story alone. The graphics are fantastic. But, if you're playing on PC, the controls are really really frustrating. You can still play the game the whole way through, but it's just annoying. Overall, I would definitely recommend Beyond. It was a unique experience. Worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: If you like these types of movie-like games that Quantic Dream makes, like I do, you will definitely like this game. I did the remixed mode for my playthrough, since it made the most sense story wise. I recommend anyone playing for the first time to do the remixed mode.I found myself invested in the story and this game did a good job at making me care for the characters. Another reason I liked it was because it had a very Stranger Things type of vibe to it. If you like supernatural stories like that, this game is very similar.My main problem with this game is the movement / combat system. Rather than using button prompts for combat and movement like Detroit, this game has you use the analog sticks and move them in a certain direction to perform actions. While this seems fine, it was executed very poorly in my opinion. I often had a hard time figuring out which way the game wanted me to move the joystick which resulted in me failing a lot of the fight scenes in the game.Overall, I think this is a great story game and is worth playing if you can look past the janky combat system.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this game is plagued by bugs. The most common one I have repeatedly encountered was with getting through doors which are blocked by invisible walls. You have to perfectly line yourself up to the door to get through and its very annoying. I've had to reset saves to be able to get a chance to get past these issues multiple times. Other than that this game is incredible. I love the story and characters. I would absolutely recommend the game if these bugs are fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I'd definitely recommend you play this with a controller as a lot of people said playing with a keyboard is awful. Anyway, I'd never heard of this game and was surprised to learn that it came out 7-8 years ago! The graphics must have been insane for the time cause I assumed it was 1-2 years old until I read some reviews just before making this one. The story is good, although it kinda goes off the rails a little bit. The acting is very good also. It's not a difficult game at all, more of a story that you affect as you watch it. Definitely recommend, despite its flaws, as it was money and time well spent. I'll probably do a second playthrough at some point to see how different choices would affect the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This game just felt very mediocre for me. The story is fine I suppose, but it never felt like it was going anywhere that the user could control and pretty much every path was more or less depressing. Which is fine but when the same thing happens the whole game (getting used, and losing anyone you care about over and over again) It really felt like there was no point in any decisions you made in the end. Game-play wise the only issues I have are that: 1) Quick time events using the right stick are too annoying to do because they don't point where you need to go in order dodge/hit. So it was a bit of a guessing game sometimes.2) I'm pretty sure I didn't misclick, but towards the end of the game I swear I was picking the dialogue option I wanted just to have the game choose something else instead? Again I could be wrong but maybe there's a bug?Overall I think it's an okay game nothing particularly special about it in my opinion, but if you want a decent story game then sure it's an okay buy just wasn't for me personally. (5/10)*
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more of a middle ground for me. I found the game to be boring overall, but it seems a little niche. If you are looking for a dramatic story with a lot of attempts to pull heart strings, this is a game for you.Overall, I had no technical issues and the game was a mostly problem free experience.Beyond: Two Souls is more of a story experience with gaming aspects. I chose to use a guide, to see all of the endings. I believe this is where the game shines most. The choices do not always feel interesting, but the endings are a nice touch.In all, I recommend this game for those that want an interactive story with minimal controls and gaming in addition. The story is meant to be heartfelt, but if you do not relate, it might fall flat.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

You constantly do not understand where to move the mouse or joystick. But over time you get used to it. Since I played on the computer, I was very annoyed by the arrows drawn in a circle. _childDocuments_.review: Beyond: Two Souls is a story based game made by Quantic Dream. I've played Detroit: Become Human before, a more recent game from Quantic Dream, and both games exceded my expectations, especially this one. Beyond: Two Souls is by far the best game I've ever played in my life. Even better than Cyberpunk 2077. It was trully amazing. Before playing it for the first time, I didn't know what to expect, because I don't really enjoy playing games about "ghosts", but I tried the Demo and I found it amazing, so I decided to buy it. And I'll never regret it: worth every penny!It is a pretty long gameplay, it will take you around 8/9 hours if you speed run it, or some 12 if you want to enjoy every single piece of it.Comparing it to Detroit: Become Human, the game controls are similar, but Detroit is easier. Both have many different endings. Beyond has at least 24 different ones (from what I seen in gameplay playthroughs). Comparing it to Cyberpunk 2077, they have some similarities, especially in the story: in both, there's kind of a soul inside of you, in Beyond is Aiden, in Cyberpunk it's Jonny Silverhand. And the final is also simillar, in a way, but I won't spoil it.I really think this game should have been turned into a movie.Don't hesitate buying this game, you won't regret it!Be carefull! Only one mistake, and it will absolutely change the Final.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute emotional rollercoaster.I can’t believe I never played this game back when I was on playstation.Quantic Dream made one heck of an amazing game.It will definitely go down as one of the most memorable games I have ever played.Although the game is amazing I do have to mention that at times when you take control of Jodie (your character), it can be clunky at times and some of the choices are pretty hidden and I wish they were easier to find. _childDocuments_.review: Is it weird to recommend a game that was implemented so poorly?I find myself in the odd position of loving the story and aspects of the gameplay but pretty much hating everything else. Controls: horrible in almost every case. To make it playable at all you have to use a controller. And even then my characters run into walls and access the wrong panels.Choices: Now don't get me wrong I wasn't expecting Detroit: Become Human but I expected a little more control over the choices I make. Instead half of the choices are things I didn't even know I could do. Or they end up totally meaningless in the grand scheme of things. Gameplay: Every single rewarding gameplay experience is done as Aiden. Jodie basically just walks around or responds to quick time events. Aiden has the most fun every time. I almost feel like they should just make the game about Aiden. A lot of quick time events are based on moving a thumbstick in the "direction" that Jodie should go. A lot of times this is VERY ambiguous. Should I go towards the attack and hit them? Dodge away? It can feel really vague. Luckily most fight sequences don't matter too much.Overall I would say it was still a good game, just be ready to fight the controls a bit and exclaim when the game tells you about a choice you could have made but didn't know existed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game (along with Detroit: Become Human and the other Quantic Dream games) are some of the best games I’ve ever played, and would definitely recommend this to anyone. The story has a few cliché moments and can be a tad confusing to follow at times (especially when played in the original sequence, but’s that’s just me), but the story is very engaging and I found myself coming back and trying out all the other alternate paths and decisions I could’ve made in the missions. The game is also a little short (took me around 10 hours) but the multiple endings makes up for that and makes you want to go back and experience the parts you missed in your first playthrough. Some of the background scenery and textures appear low quality and comically bad in some sequences of the game but it isn’t enough to warrant not playing it. This game is without a doubt a masterpiece and I thoroughly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond: Two Souls is an extraordinary blend of storytelling and interactive gameplay that stands out as a masterpiece in narrative-driven gaming.What truly sets Beyond: Two Souls apart is its focus on human connections, morality, and the weight of our choices. It’s a deeply introspective experience that resonates on a personal level, making it more than just a game—it’s a work of art. For anyone who loves a compelling story and values emotional depth in gaming, Beyond: Two Souls is an unforgettable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Quantic Dream has once again woven a masterpiece, and I find myself utterly enchanted by their visionary craft.Beyond: Two Souls is not just a game; it is a profound journey of the soul, painted with a unique philosophy of game design that merges storytelling with emotion in ways seldom seen. From the very first moments, I was swept into a world where the boundaries of fate and free will blur, and the narrative arc twists and turns in ways that left me breathless.At its heart, the story embraces the concept of amor fati - the love of one's fate - delicately threading this theme through each chapter, deepening the emotional connection between the player and the protagonist. The allusions to fate, destiny, and acceptance stir something deeply personal within, turning the experience into one that resonates beyond the screen.The visuals are nothing short of stunning, a masterclass in artistic detail, while the soundtrack weaves a melancholic beauty, perfectly complementing the emotional weight of the tale. Though not as thematically charged with societal issues as Detroit: Become Human, this game is more introspective, a meditation on inner turmoil, the phenomenon of acceptance, and the raw, personal emotions that shape our existence.Admittedly, the controls can be cumbersome at times, an awkward dance that may frustrate some. But there is a grace in the game's simplicity, an accessibility that allows the emotional depth to take center stage. The inclusion of an easy mode broadens the game's reach, inviting players of all skill levels to experience its beauty - a generous touch that I deeply appreciate.The plot twist, nestled near the end, is a moment of pure brilliance - both haunting and sublime. I found myself utterly absorbed, swept into a cascade of emotions that left me in awe. The game's complexity unfolds gradually, its layers revealing characters and stories that you can't help but grow attached to, as if they were old friends.In the end, Beyond: Two Souls is a work of art, rich with meaning, depth, and beauty. I am grateful to have embarked on this journey, to have witnessed the brilliance of Quantic Dream once more.Thank you, Quantic Dream, for this unforgettable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever played Telltale games you will probably be familiar with the concept of "choices matter". The thing is, choices here actually matter even though there aren't too many of them.Story is really intriguing from the start. You play as Jodie, girl who has some strange entity tied to her, and it was always with her, everywhere she goes. She doesn't know what that entity is, but she calls him Aiden. You have 2 ways to play this game. You can either play it original way or chronological way. I've played the game original way, and I think that it's far better experience that way and it's easy to follow the story. Game is divided into many chapters, and each chapter is some period of Jodie's life. In one chapter you may play as kid Jodie, in next you may be older, than back to kid, or teen etc. I've found it really interesting this way, never knowing in what timeline game will take me next. As for Jodie, cause of constant presence of the entity, she has never had a normal life. Aiden doesn't want to harm her, he is always there protecting her, but he has a will on his own, and she can't get rid of him. That's why most of her life she has spent in special facility where her "powers" are being studied. A lot of people look at her as a freak, disrespect her and so on, so living normal life seems impossible for her. A lot of interesting things will happen through the course of this game, and without spoiling much cause story is everything in this game, I will just say that there are 11 endings, 2 main ones, and 9 that are just modifications to these 2. You can decide who lives and who dies few times through the game, you can romance people or stay single, and all these things together will affect the final outcome. Overall story is pretty good, but I feel like it would be better with a bit less fantasy, at the moments it felt like too much for me.Gameplay is pretty simple. Since I've played this game on keyboard and mouse I will talk about K+M controls. You can walk, and use mouse to interact with objects that have white dot next to them. However it's not just clicking with mouse, you need to hold mouse in right direction so it can be confusing occasionally. There are quick time events during fights in which you need to react quickly while also holding mouse in the right direction, but even if you miss most of the time nothing will happen, so it's not that important (well maybe for achievements), Aside from these basic controls you also have ability to use Aiden. When you press Tab in situations where you are allowed to, game will switch to Aiden's perspective. You can fly around with him, interact with objects (throw chairs, tables, books, open locked doors and so on), go through the walls, possess another human being and then kill your enemies or whatever game has planned for you, or just kill your enemies without controlling them. However you don't have any freedom to this, you can only do things that are scripted. You can't possess the enemy if the game doesn't want you to. For example there can be 5 soldiers and you will only be able to possess one of them, or throw specific objects. Basically everything that has white/blue dot next to it can be used. Aside from this limit, you are also not able to go too far away from Jodie, cause Aiden is tied to her. And that's about it as gameplay is concerned, you can't do much, but this game is all about story, so that's fine. Cast is pretty good. We got Elliot Page (previously Ellen Page) staring as Jodie, Willem Dafoe guy who played Green Goblin in of the Spiderman movies and so on. Even Hans Zimmer has his role in music production of this game. Port worked great for me, and for people using monitors with higher frequency the most game lets you is 60Hz, but there are ways to unlock the framerate. Controls are okay, not really good, but not bad either. Game is not very long, and you can replay chapters, but replaying chapters affects rest of the story.- Pretty good story with interesting concept of tied souls- Great acting cast- Playing with Aiden is fun- While the story is good, one chapter was a bit over the top for my taste, and I feel how story would be better if they just focused on Jodie and Aiden instead of most other paranormal stuff- Controls are not that goodThis was the first game from Quantic Dream that I've ever played and I really enjoyed it so I would recommend this game to anyone looking for good innovative story with choices that actually matter, and I will probably try their other games.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a fan of Ellen Page, and also a fan of story-rich games. I went into Beyond: Two Souls wanting to like this game, but unfortunately the obnoxious control has completely ruined the experience. Game controls should allow the player sufficient, well, control over the character so as to feel immersed in the game. The controls in this game are so arbitrary and unintuitive that they constantly force the player to guess at what command is needed and what the command would do, thus breaking immersion. With this sort of poorly designed control scheme, it makes more sense to just give players multiple choices like in Bandersnatch.

I just think the pacing could have been better. And playing through the remix might have been better than sticking to the original way they intended for you to play through the game. Jodie annoys me as a character; whiny, stubborn, and creates problems at random moments that don't make any sense to me survival wise. I play on PC with a controller, and the buttons are okay, but wonky at best. Your choices definitely impact the gameplay but there were a lot of moments where I got frustrated with what Jodie forced me to do anyway. And scenes like the forest where I was 'forced' to hit the dogs, and I didn't want to do it, she still went ahead and did it on her own.Definitely wouldn't have been upset if I had never been able to play this game. _childDocuments_.review: Initially, I played the demo before this released on PC. I was so excited, I finished the demo, loved the concept, what little of the story it gave away, and the unique mechanics I've yet to see in any other game.Said mechanics are in no other game for a reason. Once the full game FINALLY released on steam, I played through to just a little passed what I had in the demo, and there is where I essentially lost all interest and tapered off the game. The story got so disconnected, shuffled out of order, which sounds interesting at first, but honestly only made it harder to connect to the character emotionally. Missions got boring, and when they got boring the controls got annoying. This was no longer a new, novel idea, but now a self-imposed tedious hell that I just couldn't convince myself to go back to. I wish I had never bothered with the demo, because now all I have is a game that is only a husk of empty dreams that I'll probably never finish soley because there are better games out there. Oopse.

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a mixed review. Interesting game, concept and story with minor choices you can make throughout (like Life is Strange for example). Although you can make choices throughout, I am not sure of the significant impact they can make as throughout my experience, I didn't feel my choices had much of one if at all. The story is a bit cliché in some parts of the game but it's still ok throughout.-The game is very linear in the sense that if you fail a quick time event then you can still survive no matter what. In one part of the game I was seen by an enemy, to which they ended up just dying automatically at the hands of Aiden. There's a real lack of trial and error (except for the  so the game feels more like an interactive film in some ways. -There are traditional third person angles with the camera behind the shoulder but also areas where you're basically just forced to look one way - letterbox bars are also forced in some parts of the game which are a little bit annoying.-Some parts of the game have slightly buggy animations/scenes, there's only a small few of them but it does make me wonder how they're still like that after all this time.-Originally on a PS3/PS4 so the controls are a little weird. But you do get used to them.Overall, aside from those issues I think it's a great game and worth buying.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best story telling in games, the game play much improves from Heavy Rain and this game has way better performances from Willem Dafoe and Elliot Page. _childDocuments_.review: David Cage is such a horrible story teller. Dialogs are awful, the characters are behaving irrationally, you could drive a truck through all the plot holes.Yet, I can't say that this is a bad game. I don't play through bad games, I abandon them quickly when there is no fun to be had. The story is interesting enough and it manages not to go completely bonkers in contrast to some other Quantic Dream games. The talented actors manage to pull off quite a decent job, even with the horrible scenario they've been given. With just a bit of better writing, this game could have easily been a classic, it has that Quantic Dream originality and charm that from time to time shines through all the negatives. As it is, I could recommend the game to you only if you like cinematic games and only on a discount. Once again, I wish there was a neutral rating on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent game - engaging story, interesting premise, atmospheric, some eye-pleasing visuals. Just tell me one thing, please.How on earth did you break M+K controls SO BADLY? Perhaps my game was cursed by Aiden, but I have never encountered controls as broken, as wonky and as unstable as they are here. So let me share a small advice. What you SHOULD have coded is:- if you press W/S, you move forward / backwards- if you press A/D, you move or at least turn left / rightWhat this game HAS, though, goes something like this:- if you press W, you sometimes go forward, but sometimes go back, sometimes go left, sometimes go right, sometimes stop walking randomly and refuse to move, sometimes pirouette, sometimes don't react at all.- if you press A, you sometimes go right, but sometimes go forward, sometimes go back, sometimes go left, sometimes pirouette, sometimes (almost usually) don't react at all unless you are already walking, but then possibly switch directions in the process.And so it goes in this directionless world.It gets even worse when you are riding a horse. Then it's all freestyle which can switch to random directions WHILE you are pressing the same button. Freestyle rodeo indeed..It doesn't help that some (many) prompts require bizarre precision of facing them and being close by. I spent minutes trying and failing to orient my character towards them, seeing the prompt flash for a nanosecond and disappear to tease me. I can't imagine how many I missed because of that.It also doesn't help that sometimes Jodie gets stuck on invisible obstacles and refuses to move through an obvious empty path, just to change her mind after a few pirouettes and just walk the same path no problem on the 5th attempt. What?It also also doesn't help that you have plentiful of fast-paced sequences that require semi-proper movement and/or moving along quickly. It also also also doesn't help that you put plenty of button-press prompts that make the player guess which mouse-direction is required, for example to move your mouse down when you are ducking or up when you are jumping over something, etc. But sometimes these don't correspond to presented directions in the slightest! For example, sometimes your character obviously needs to dive underneath something, so you move the mouse down. Wrong! It turns out you were supposed to move it right or left or up or any other random direction, cause reasons. But a few seconds later you get another ducking action, but this time moving the mouse down works no problem. But then another ducking where, once again, moving down doesn't work, cause you needed to go right or left or something. What?Dear developers... are you, perhaps, directionally challenged? Did you get inspirations from Zoro from One Piece who can't make one step without getting hopelessly lost and on the exact other side of the recommended direction?Are directions the new rocket science?Pardon my rant, but either my game is truly broken, or you actually need to actively sabotage the controls to mess them up so very badly.Despite that, if you fancy yourself a saint of patience, do give this game a try. It's really decent. Besides, well, the gameplay. I wonder if it wouldn't work better as a fully animated movie.May the flames guide your way.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond: Two Souls was a gripping sci-fi thriller from start to finish. Told in an out-of-order yet narratively logical fashion, you will experience the key moments of the life of Jodie Holmes and her linked companion Aiden, ranging from the heart-warming to heart-breaking, awkward and intriguing, resulting in an overall memorable journey. Jodie tries their best to try and be perceived as normal and live a regular life distant from those who which to understand her powers better, and Aiden is a unique character in the sense that they can only communicate in the regular world by interacting with objects and people. Their personality is entirely constructed through non-verbal communication and presented more nuances that I’ve seen with certain regularly acted characters. Throughout the game, you make choices as both characters which mostly have a short-term, within-chapter impact which aids to personalize your experience through Jodie’s story. You can make Jodie work with and develop a positive relationship with Aiden, or you can set Aiden against Jodie.There’s brilliant acting from all of the cast members, and the facial animations are particularly impressive for their time. While some of the typical David Cage dialogue cringe remains, it wasn’t as particularly striking as it was in Heavy Rain. Some scenes didn’t hold up as well on subsequent playthroughs, but I feel most people will only play this game the one time. This is because choices make little impact on the narrative as a whole compared to other games in the genre, particularly because of how it is constructed. Whether this is a good or bad thing will be down to personal preference, but personally, the set points in the narrative that all players will experience were enough to keep me engaged. I should also note that the game is pretty serious in its presentation, with very little humour or any ‘so bad it’s good’ moments to speak of to laugh at, which again will certainly be a turn-off for some people. If both things don’t bother you and, of course, you enjoy this genre of game in the first place, this is certainly an experience I would recommend playing at least once. I will note that achievement completion journey was rather tiresome as you are unable to skip large portions of the game to meet certain criteria, and while I enjoyed the endings that are here. Apart from that though, I have few complaints, and I enjoyed this narrative and these characters way more than I was expecting to. 9/10.Heavy Rain Review - Detroit: Become Human Review -

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good. From start to finish I loved every bit of it. There are some issues porting console games to pc but overall they were very minimal. One thing that frustrated me and a lot of people are the quick time scenes, there is no real clear indication of where you're meant to move. It is easy to tell at times and at other times extremely difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Altogether this game is great. Yes, the controls are far from perfect and the camera is confusing at times, but it is manageable. I've also heard that it works better with a controller. I played with my keyboard and mouse and I got used to it. Had to reload one or two times because the controls failed me and I wasn't able to advance the story how I wanted to because of that. Anyway the great story behind this game and how it is told totally makes up for it. It even got through to me emotionally. I like how it made me smile when something nice or funny happened to Jodie. And of course the opposite. I also like that the fighting is kept to a minimum with a few points in time where you actually have to do all the ducking and crouching to avoid enemies. There are a few more encounters that require you to perform certain key presses and mouse guestures in the right time to avoid getting hit or something. They are also ok and most of the time you won't fail because you missed one single movement. Most of the time you can take your time exploring a bit though. When I say that, it really means a bit. You still follow the story line and you can't do what you want like in other games. But I like that as well. No need to look for clues under every rock. Some quite easy riddles. Altogether I enjoyed being Jodie and Aiden for some time very much. One of the few games I actually finished since Life is Strange 1. Since it seems I missed a few things that I might have done different but it didn't occur to me that it is possible until the end of the chapter, I will probably be Jodie again after some time has passed :)
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: The game is wonderful, and I highly recommend it.  Your choices affect the story, however, it tries very hard to hide this from you causing the story to feel railroaded even when it is not.  Just keep an open mind while playing and be proactive about your gameplay, as the game will not make every option or choice obvious to you.  Play the game blind and do what you want to do.  Don't try to min-max your decisions, and instead immerse yourself in the story and work with it.  This game does what it should and does not just gamify a movie, instead allowing the player to control the story, giving an experience unique to gaming.  If you are on the fence you should try the demo to get a good feel for what you can expect from the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not crying you're crying.Solid game. Encountered no bugs. Incredible graphics for a game from 2013. It's another interesting and emotional story from Quantic Dream and includes movie quality performances from Page and Dafoe. Recommend if you enjoy a compelling (yet very sad) story and want to have some agency in how that story plays out. If you prefer shooty shooty bang bang gameplay then move along.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It's an adventure/interactive movie type game with lots of QTEs and point and click stuff, made up of out-of-sequence episodes over the course of Jodie's life. The story builds up as you go which is a little odd as early in the game I was wondering about the motivation for certain actions, but it's slowly revealed; I think this order would work in film etc where you're watching someone else, but when you have to do things yourself it's a little weird. There's a "remix" option, which I've not tried but that might be better ordered??The movement controls (as Jodie) aren't great - even with a controller -  and the QTEs are easy to fumble until you get the hang of them. The view is quite restrictive and the direction movements annoyingly constrained, though when you play as Aiden there's a lot more freedom, so it's obviously a design decision, which maybe could have done with a bit more thought.Recommended as the story is really good (despite the sequencing and the controls!), but you'll want a controller and a lot of patience. And a swear jar.**Edit** So it took about 10 hours to complete (from cold, getting the hang etc.) but I think there's at least one replay in it to try different things (e.g. not screwing up a lot). I'm not expecting radical changes, but enough that it's worth giving it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: I am so surprised, Beyond Two Souls was a surprisingly good game. I played Detroit Become Human first on PS4, then when the pack came to PC I grabbed it. So far, I am not disappointed. Beyond Two Souls has given me a solid 15Hrs for my first play-through, and if what I read is correct - I have many more hours to go; with 23 more endings to uncover. If you enjoyed Detroit Become Human, or are looking for a more "interactive-movie" type-game, then this is for you. The story is a roller-coaster of events, and by the end I was quite attached to some of the characters. I can't wait to playthrough again and choose all different choices.

_childDocuments_.review: I hope you like janky game play and QTE's.I appreciate the scope of the game, but now that I have beaten it, I wont go back. If this story was a show, it would be unremarkable. I found myself counting down the hours until it was over. About halfway through, I lost interest. I paused the game knowing I wouldnt replay this game, to watch/read guides on how to get the best ending. After a while, everything felt like a chore, go here, possess this, talk to that, etc. It ended up really taking away from the experience, you know the reason you play games like this. It offers nothing new, nothing exciting. For most of the game I felt like a passenger, like I had no agency, watching the worlds longest QTE movie. The last few decisions, I just set the controller down and walked away. Again the saving grace could have been solid gameplay, but instead we get stupid action QTEs. So Im stuck, do I recommend it? Well, the story is ok, the gameplay is less than stellar. Though if you have time to go through your back catalog, try it and see if you like it. Will I play it again, I dont think so. There isnt enough here to pull me back.Now to the point, should I recommend it? I wish there was a maybe or depends option. I think that ultimately there is a reason no one talks about it today, which is why it seems like it is constantly on sale. I think maybe if you have nothing to do, and a day or so to just play it, pull the trigger. As long as you dont mind bad mechanics, and all the QTEs from every game ever, you might enjoy the story. Games like this are few, and maybe the next one is better? We'll see.Also while I was playing, I couldnt help but think that "Geist" on the GameCube did it MUCH better.

_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of the best artistic type of game that I've played. I wish there were a few more elements in the game, like dragging a body away, and better shooting mechanics. However, it has a great and interesting storyline, that is worth playing once in a while. Like let your life happen, and come back to the game to enjoy after you've forgotten most things in the game. It makes it better in my opinion to remember some things, but discover something different based on how you are doing in life, what life is like at that time for you. It translates into the game well. Every time I've played it's been 5 years, and it's been a beautiful new experience. I would love to see a sequel to the game, I hope that things would work out with Ellen Page or Elliot Page to do it. _childDocuments_.review: Quantic Dream does is again! If you were a fan of their other "choose your own adventure" games, then this is one of their best. But it tells an interesting story, albeit with very simple gameplay mechanics. Choice isn't a large part of the game, and when it does present you with options most of them don't have lasting consequences. But with the branching narrative, replay-ability is high. Fixed camera walking is my only real complaint about this game, which makes it difficult to see what you should be interacting with from time to time. But for the most part, I highly recommend this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond: Two Souls is a unique drama experience that blurs the lines between video games and cinematic storytelling. The game follows the story of Jodie Holmes, a young woman with a special gift – she can see and communicate with mysterious entity named Aiden. The game takes on a journey through Jodie life, from childhood to adulthood, as she navigates the complexities of her abilities and the consequences that come with them. Standout ability to switch between controlling Jodie and Aiden provides for diverse gameplay experiences. Aiden's special abilities offer a unique way to interact with the world, while Jodie's physical interactions with the environment create a distinct sense of action. The only con of this game is that controls can feel a bit clunky at times. Anyways, Beyond: Two Souls is definitely worth playing, just be prepared for a more cinematic experience than a conventional game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. I wouldn't classify this as a "video game" but more like an "interactive movie" like The Quarry, The Dark Pictures Anthology etc but without the horror.For this game, I bring the bad news first...The camera controls are terrible. That doesn't really work here. This takes a lot of effort to accomplish, but feels like a final boss fight in other games where you fail miserably. I would have preferred the traditional third-person movement and camera controls anytime.You'd better be prepared for anything without warning. Keep your hands on the mouse and keyboard. This game has so many QTEs that occur even in places where it can be unexpected. Fortunately, failure isn't fatal, but it could affect the plot.I found the character development imperfect but satisfying, but that's probably because the plot isn't presented in the usual chronological order, but in the order that's "right" for the performer, and the jumps are sometimes too big.Despite all of that, the storyline is fantastic, with amazing motion capture and voice acting. Actor Willem Dafoe was great. I've really liked him since the first Spiderman movie with Tobey Maguire. His character in this game was perfect and suited his role. The ending he deserves is great for "deciding" his fate.Aiden's abilities are very good, especially the ability to kill other people and take control of them. I wish I had a friend like that. The graphics settings for an "older" game are still impressive. There's an element of replayability thanks to its branching storylines. Throughout the game you have to make decisions that ultimately lead to different outcomes as the storyline progresses. You also have the option to play the storyline in chronological order.For these reasons, despite its shortcomings, I still recommend it to be experienced and for people who not only like multiple endings, but can also influence every decision in the gameplay, like in The Quarry.

_childDocuments_.review: Another fairly impressive interactive gaming experience from Quantic Dream. Beyond: Two Souls is a supernatural thriller written by David Cage that follows the story of a girl who was born with a ghostly attachment.  The game is set on a vast timeline which bounces between significant events of Jodie Holmes's life in a mixed order. This keeps the story fresh and forms the narrative in an interesting way. You never know what to expect next and filling in plot holes and asking questions is a big part of the experience. Mechanics are very similar to Heavy Rain but not quite as engaging. Some combat scenes are also quite cumbersome and frustrating but it's good enough overall. Choices you make are also compared to other users and some decisions can impact the story in more than an illusionary way. I really enjoyed the 9 or so hours it took to finish. The cast and their performances are brilliant as is the visuals and motion capture. It's a highly intriguing title that will keep you engaged to the very end and a flawless port too.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 7.5/10Genre: Quick time event, story telling The Good:+ Fantastic facial/body animations. Motion capturing the entire cast really pays off and brings many emotional moments to life. + The story itself is decent helped by the performance of some high-quality actors. Although I did figure the big twist very early on in the game, watching x-files at a young age really prepares you for the paranormal 😊. You can either play the game in chronological order or play how the developers intended, by jumping back & forth between different time periods in the main characters life. I think the developers felt this would make for a more suspenseful, mysterious story but it just comes across as disjointed. My personal opinion is playing in chronological order provides a more satisfying experience. + You can make choices within each chapter that causes different outcomes, some minor, some major, however you will always ultimately end up in the same place at the end of the chapter. It does provide some incentive to replay certain parts of the story.    Average:+/- The gameplay consists mostly of quick time events. There are some gameplay segments where you have to guess what button to press based on what is happening on screen, for the most part you will get it right but there are a few times when its hard to guess what the game wants. Luckily the game is very lenient on mistakes so it doesn’t affect anything but it does get frustrating. There is one chapter that is based solely on stealth and despite the animations, controlling the character feels odd. Controller is HIGHLY recommended.  The Bad:- Un-skippable dialogue and cutscenes. Conclusion: This is a fun game for what it is, the enjoyment you get out of this game is really dependant on how much you like the story and characters. The entire game will last just under 10 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Quantic Dreams second big game after their hit Heavy Rain.The story: It is again an interactive movie but this time a thriller with a pinch of sci-fi. The story is about Jodie and the ghost-like entity Aiden connected to her. You play Jodie over the course of about 20 years from a child to a young adult and see how people try to understand her connection to Aiden and want to exploit this connection. The story jumps between different points in time and the player has to order the stuff to make sense of it. Also there are no real branching storylines just minor changes depending on your choices. In addition to this the story is not really interesting since Jodie is merely a test-subject and not actively involved in exploring her connection to Aiden.The gameplay: With Jodie it is pretty much like in Heavy Rain: Draw stuff with your mouse and quicktime events. When you switch to Aiden you can freely move a certain distance around Jodie, even go through walls and manipulate certain objects. Aiden has even special powers like healing and possessing people. Unfortunately the developers decided what powers you can use at a certain time. Also Aiden’s powers are just cheaply used from a story-writing perspective. They are used whenever Jodie needs to do an impossible escape und forgotten literally 30 seconds later when they need to create drama. For example it is no problem to protect Jodie when she jumps from a burning building but Aiden is unable to help her when the arsonist attacks her immediately afterwards.The game has a two-player-mode but this should not be confused with coop-mode since one of the players is always forced to watch the other, sometimes for really long times but the mode nicely symbolise Aiden’s characterisation: An entity bound to Jodie but not controlled by her. This means that player two controls Aiden and player one can only helplessly watch once Jodie unleashes him until the Aiden-player gives the control back to Jodie.So the story is not impressive and the gameplay is bad, why do I still recommend the game? Because of the acting! You can see the work of some Hollywood-A-lists her and it is a pleasure to watch Page and Dafoe act no matter how bad the script is.The game also includes a DLC-chapter which feels like it comes right out of a Portal game. Jodie and Aiden need to navigate a number of test chambers which need an amount of switching between characters and riddle-solving not representative for the main game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond: Two Souls

_childDocuments_.review: I love Heavy Rain despite its many flaws but my god is this game not a slog to play through.The premise of the story is actually extremely interesting. Without spoiling anything you play as Jodie who was born with a ghostly entity attached to her. You play through crucial moments in Jodie's life and gradually piece together what this entity is. Sounds cool right? Except the execution is sloppy and really not complemented by the "gameplay" Cage has in store for players. So many times I was jazzed up by a scene or something we were about to do only to be reminded that ultimately all I had to do was push the joystick and trigger a cutscene or traverse through a corridor. Gone are the homomorphic QTEs that make you feel part of the action and simulate emotions that characters are experiencing on-screen. Now the game plays itself! It's actually more exhausting playing a game with such half-in-half-out involvements from the player because you're never quite sure when you can safely sit back and watch a scene play out yet whenever you need to do something it amounts to nothing more than moving the joystick or pressing a button. So even if the story promises something grand it's bogged down by this lethargy most people are sure to feel when playing through it.This is not me bashing the story itself because I actually don't mind the odd tonal shifts or the non-linear storytelling. QD games have always had cheesy stories. Yet the bottom-line has always been that they are fundamentally fun experiences. Beyond just isn't fun at all because of the way it virtually ignores the player. I also think taking away our ability to read the character's inner thoughts means mundane actions really do come off as mundane and Beyond is effectively this movie-game hybrid monstrosity where you don't get cinematic greatness because too many walking and interacting with things are shown, yet the interactivity also gives you very little dopamine because they're not gamey enough and offer no reward for the gamer other than advancing the scene. I've never felt so dissociated playing as a hovering ghost killing soldiers in a warzone than I did on Beyond. When you can make your high-octane action feel as uninteresting and perfunctory as chopping vegetables in a kitchen, you know something is seriously wrong with the game.Overall I think Beyond offers a very drab experience with a story that could've been told much much better given the acting talent involved. In a world with Heavy Rain I can't really recommend playing through this. It's very much one of those games that are more interesting to watch someone play than playing them yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Two Souls is a mixed game, with many elements of the story amounting to binary choices, some aspects of the narrative being poorly fleshed out and gameplay regularly amounting to choosing whether to be terrible or not. Overall 8 out 10.

_childDocuments_.review: (Note: Possible game spoilers, but not really? Read at your own risk)To me, this game was one of those..."Eh, I'll give it a shot" type. What I got was something that completely blew my mind on how fantastic this game was. I still have to try out the alternate ending from the one that I've chosen, along with all other choices given to me that I didn't pick. I've literally fallen in love with Ellen Page's character, Jodie as well as Kadeem Hardison's, Cole (Yup, you read that right, Kadeem Hardison from that 90's sitcom "It's a Different World" is in this game.). Willem of course is amazing, as his character's chemistry with Jodie will bring up so much mixed emotions as it did to me. All in all, this game just really woke me up from the "sleeper" I personally expected this game to be. I love everything about, well, mostly everything. The controls when it comes to the action sequences can be challenging to time, and can sometimes be clunky-ish, but it still doesn't ruin the game experience overall. I'll def be playing again just to see the other alternate ending for certain.

_childDocuments_.review: The controls kinda suck and I hated their implementation of auto-save, because whenever garbage controls got in the way of how I wanted to play the story I had to repeat an entire chapter, instead of just reloading the last scene.The story was decent, which is to say that I enjoyed it most of the time, while there were several moments that annoyed me.  Not that anyone is playing this game or reading my review for birthing advice, but never do what they did in the scene where they just cut the umbilical cord without clamping it down.  Other than that little bit, and some things they probably got wrong because they're French, it was like a Stranger Things--but not as good.  Oh, and if you pick the ending I did, apparently it's also Terminator and Jodie is Sarah Connor.  Not sure I have the patience to sit through another play through to see the stuff I missed, but I might consider it once I have my Steam Deck because this one is definitely one you need play the a gamepad.  I played Hard Rain with a mouse and keyboard, because despite those controls being awful, I felt like the gamepad controls were actually worse.  In this game it was the opposite.  They couldn't figure out how to map two-stick gestures to a mouse without it being awful, and anytime they prompted for quick time event, the keys were just so random that it wasn't intuitive.  With the gamepad, I feel like they could've done a better job at making the button prompts resemble the actual buttons a bit.  Only the A,B,X,Y and the sticks should've been circles, the others should've been rectangular at the least.Lots of nitpicking on my part, but it was close to being really good, it was just kinda good, and if you get it kinda cheap it's an interesting way to experience a story.

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of the best stories in a video game. You feel attached to the main character Jodie as you play through her life. The voice acting and graphics are amazing. You play this game for a story. In terms of game play, it is basically quick-time events, running/walking, and doing actions. This game play is similar to LA Noire in terms of moving the character and picking up objects. Your choices do matter and will effect future missions. There are some great action packed missions and other missions are short that help build the plot. The game took me 12 hours to complete and I want replay the game to take different paths that can lead to new endings. I beat this is game in 6 days and enjoyed a ton. Lastly, the controls for keyboard and mouse took me a few missions to get used to. So don't get to frustrated you will get used it and the game is worth putting up with in the beginning.

name: Grounded
detailed_description: Get Ready to Flex in 'Grounded' with the Upcoming 'Fully Yoked' 1.4 Update Hey, Grounded friends! We're absolutely buzzing to introduce the upcoming 'Fully Yoked' 1.4 update – the ultimate Grounded experience bulging with new content that's sure to get you pumped! Check out the announcement post for more details!
about_the_game: The world is a vast, beautiful, and dangerous place – especially when you have been shrunk to the size of an ant. Explore, build and survive together in this first-person, multiplayer, survival adventure. Can you thrive alongside the hordes of giant insects, fighting to survive the perils of the backyard? Uncover the mysteries while playing through the story! How did you wind up so small? Who did this to you? How do you go home? These are all answers you will uncover as you play through the story. Solo or with friends – anytime! You can face the backyard alone or together, online, with up to three friends. Not only that, but with the Shared Worlds feature, you can continue to play in your shared world even if the original host is not on, with all your progression saving! Nowhere is safe – not even your base! Creatures can be found roaming the yard in a multitude of environments, such as the depths of the pond, the caverns of the termite den, and even the sweltering heat found in the sandbox. You can even attract them to different places in the yard by activating the MIX.R devices. However, the more you interfere with the creatures in the yard, the higher the chance that they come knocking at your own door, so you better prepare. Play true to your playstyle! Use the in-game customization systems such as Mutations and Milk Molars to activate the bonuses and perks you want for your character. Not only that, but craft and upgrade your armor and weapons to give your character the stats and advantages you need in order to take on the perils of the backyard. It’s time to go big, or never go home!

_childDocuments_.review: Honey I Shrunk the Kids meets the survival/crafting genre of games!Starting out seems a little slow, some inhabitants are just "RUN" whenever you see them until you can unlock more recipes and understand strategies to dealing with them, but once you get over that progression is solid and paced only as much as you want to progress it. There are a lot of nifty 'tips and tricks' that the game doesn't tell you the first time around and sure you can whip through the story/campaign relatively quickly without too much investment into the exploration or gathering of materials etc.My partner and I love survival/crafting games and working together to problem solve and progress through them. If I were to critique one thing is the 'collectibles' mini games (Milk Molars/Mega Milk Molars, SCA.B schemes and Raw Science) need a little bit of tweaking when trying to locate them using the radar...and then being able to 'tick' them off the map for those of us who like to complete everything. All in all, a great little game that I thoroughly enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game.  I wanted to LOVE this game.  I was all primed for it - the premise is right up my alley, like a great 80s kid-caper sci-fi movie, and the graphics are indeed gorgeous and everything you'd want out of this game.  It's fun just to load it up and look around.  The problem is, it doesn't know what kind of game it wants to be, so it tries to be several types and fails at all of them.  Is it an FPS?  Is it an RPG?  Is it a crafter and builder?  Is it an MMORPG?  Who can say?  Only the game designers, who tried to blend all these game types and more together and ended up with a mess that's just plain frustrating to play and not fun at all.  It's not that it's a bad game, and it's not that it's a hard game, it's that it's an unfair game that frankly just expects too much out of the player, and in the end, for all the fun I wanted to have with it, I found myself just getting angry with it and not having any fun at all.  And yes, it was punishingly hard, making it even more frustrating.  So I stopped playing.  And that's the worst, buying a game and expecting to like it, wanting to like it, and finding out that you just plain don't.I plan to give it a try again some day.  Maybe I just didn't "get it", and wasn't ready to get it.  Now that I've played it a bunch and I know exactly what to expect, maybe I'd have a better time with a restart.  It has such great potential!  But my first experience with it wasn't great, and first impressions can be hard to break.  Extra Note:  this game is virtually impossible to play effectively without resorting to the online Wiki, which isn't necessarily a problem in and of itself, I like looking up the Wiki for lots of games.  But this game absolutely requires it, or there is stuff you simply will never figure out on your own.  Devs, that's always a bad sign in my book.  The game itself should tell me everything I need to know - not every winning strategy or best way to do something, but everything I need to KNOW.  In this game, several times I got stuck and could go no further without looking things up, because I couldn't for the life of me figure out some essential mechanic or didn't realize what I was really going up against.  That's just plain bad game design.There is so much potential here, but the game is so obtuse, difficult and inaccessible that it's difficult for me to believe it was actually play-tested by normal, average people.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has quickly become one of my favorite survival games. Most of it comes down to the style of the game, its very early 90's-honey i shrunk the kids-D&D adventure kind of atmosphere. I also love the scale of the game, it all takes place in one small to average sized backyard. One would think "wow only a small backyard? thats not a big map", but it is. When you are only 1/4" tall, a backyard is the size of a city, a pond becomes a massive lake, and an a sandbox a sprawling desert.As far as the mechanics, pretty standard survival features (hunger/thirst, base building, resource gathering, creature loot farming). A few differences are: Instead of normal leveling to boost stats, you collect upgrade points around the map and learn mutations (essentially perks) as you do certain things. There is also a heavy focus on exploration, with most of the game being locked behind various plot milestones. Most impressively (i think) is the building system, it mostly handles a lot like Conan Exiles, with the added feature of a "handy Gnat". it is essentially a small flying drone that can place and build blueprints from a ridiculous distance away from the player.As a final note, this game features "arachnophobia settings" which will reduce the "creepyness" of spiders on a sliding scale, with the highest setting making spiders nothing more than a floating ball with eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: Grounded: The Pinnacle of Gaming InnovationIn the vast landscape of video games, where genres collide and technologies evolve, few titles manage to stand out as truly groundbreaking experiences. Among them, "Grounded" emerges as a shining beacon of innovation, seamlessly blending elements of survival, exploration, and adventure into a captivating masterpiece. Developed by Obsidian Entertainment and released in 2020, Grounded not only redefines the boundaries of gaming but also establishes itself as one of the best games ever created.At its core, Grounded transports players into a world where they are reduced to the size of insects, navigating a backyard filled with towering grass blades and towering obstacles. This unique premise immediately sets the stage for an immersive experience that challenges players to adapt, survive, and thrive in a world where every blade of grass becomes a towering obstacle and every insect a formidable adversary.One of the most striking aspects of Grounded is its attention to detail and the sheer scale of its world. Despite the diminutive size of the player character, the game world feels vast and teeming with life, from the bustling activity of ants to the majestic flight of dragonflies. Every corner of the backyard is filled with secrets to uncover and challenges to overcome, ensuring that players are constantly engaged and enthralled by the world around them.Furthermore, Grounded excels in its implementation of survival mechanics, striking a delicate balance between challenge and accessibility. Players must scavenge for resources, craft tools and weapons, and build shelter to survive the harsh realities of the backyard. However, unlike other survival games that can feel punishingly difficult, Grounded provides ample opportunities for exploration and discovery, ensuring that players are always motivated to push forward and uncover the mysteries that lie ahead.The game's visuals also deserve special mention, as they are nothing short of breathtaking. Despite the technical constraints of rendering a world from the perspective of a tiny insect, Grounded manages to deliver stunningly beautiful environments that are rich in detail and brimming with life. From the shimmering dewdrops on blades of grass to the intricate patterns of a spider's web, every aspect of the game world feels meticulously crafted and lovingly rendered.However, what truly sets Grounded apart from other games is its emphasis on cooperative multiplayer gameplay. While the single-player experience is certainly enjoyable, it is in multiplayer where Grounded truly shines. Working together with friends to build a base, fend off enemies, and explore the backyard is an experience like no other, fostering a sense of camaraderie and teamwork that few games can match.In addition to its core gameplay mechanics, Grounded also boasts a compelling narrative that unfolds gradually as players progress through the game. While the story may not be the primary focus of the experience, it serves as a compelling backdrop that adds depth and context to the world around them. From uncovering the mysteries of the backyard to confronting the sinister forces that lurk within, the story of Grounded is both engaging and thought-provoking, ensuring that players are invested in the journey from beginning to end.In conclusion, Grounded stands as a testament to the power of innovation and creativity in gaming. With its unique premise, engaging gameplay, stunning visuals, and cooperative multiplayer experience, it sets a new standard for excellence in the industry. Whether you're a seasoned gamer or new to the medium, Grounded offers an experience that is truly unforgettable, cementing its status as one of the best games ever created.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played since early access, I have over 700 hours in the game. I'd say this is the best survival craft game I've played. There are some rare physics jank where a clover may launch you with enough force into a stem of grass above you that it kills you instantly or launches you so far into the air if you don't have a dandelion you're dead. But it was only a couple times that killed me and honestly is more funny then upsetting most of the time. Multiplayer could be better, one of us was getting disconnected every 10 minutes one day, we switched hosts and then it happened to the other person. Then there are times we've gone 2 hours with no DCs. It's very odd and unpredictable. Those are the 2 flaws that stand out for me, otherwise everything they've put into the game and improved over the years has just made the game more enjoyable. The story is well done, the music is great. I wish after 700 hours the main characters had more varied voice lines, but I'll chalk it up to my excessive hours.. But even adding new game plus I still feel like I have a lot to do, plus playing with friends feels like a new experience from my solo time from early access to new release. I'd love for a 2nd game in a new environment with new bugs since there's still much unexplored potential for insect species.  Thank you Grounded team for putting so much time and effort into this game and adding wonderful quality of life updates a long the way (The reverse zipper, dandelions working while not in the trinket spot, the building gnat, to name a few.)

_childDocuments_.review: Side Note before ReviewObsidian Entertainment is one of my favorite remaining studios. I say remaining as most companies in the last decade have all gone after quick cash grabs. While Obsidian was developing Out Worlds they allowed 13 of their team members work on a different "passion project". This is a game made by people that wanted to experience this game world and play this game not a group looking to make a quick profit. As a gamer I love to support projects like this!  Pro'sThe creatures/AI's - Even in early access each bug has its own personality. - Interesting world - Fun crafting system... I made a helmet out of dismembered ants.... - Crafting is really decent for a Early Access Game Con's (Addressing some other complaints I read from my perspective) Multiplayer- Have to use Xbox Live... - If you have a Microsoft Account really is not that big of a deal.$30.00 Price Tag (Frequent complaint)  - You spend all your birthday money?  - If you love coop the game is worth it  *Note* Issue I had was frequent crashes from multiplayer however, the game autosaves often. If this is a deal breaker wait a week and I am sure the developers will knock this issue out. - Going to possibly have a quick story line. Games great, I read that 20-25% of the story is out currently, I beat that in about two hours (focused on that goal not exploring). So imagining completed story would be around 6-8 hours? Time will tell. I always try and support passion projects and this game just came out. I want to give the developers Kudos and see where they go from here to improve this game. A passion project is always a risk, I hope Obsidian and Microsoft will stay this course over becoming like some of the other Triple A studios. With my rant over last thing to say is I am going to recommend this to my gaming crew, if they don't buy it then I will get it for them.

_childDocuments_.review: What I like:Art style, very pleasant for the eyeBuilding and crafting, the uniqueness of each weapon and armor.Lots of things to collect, like the creature cards, molars and items. _childDocuments_.review: It's very jarring to play a survival crafting game made with the polish and professionalism of an established studio like Obsidian. The graphical presentation is very nice, the mechanics are simple, but functional, and the map is really big and full of stuff to do. The content scope is really impressive considering the quality and polish that's on most of it. Dozens of hours in, there'll still be bosses to fight and better sets of gear to craft.I wouldn't say the game iterates on the genre much. So, if you like this kind of game, you'll like it. But, if you're looking for something super novel, this ain't it. That being said, this game does include the ability to do all crafting using the contents of nearby chests rather than just your inventory and the ability to deposit all of your random crap to your chests instantly with the press of a button. Grounded isn't the first or only game with these kinds of features, but they go a looong way here and not a lot of crafting games have that kind of quality of life. It's a good example of how the devs would make sure a system was actually convenient and fun to use before moving on and forgetting about it, which *cannot* be said about every early access game.The dialogue and constant pushing of the 80s gimmick can be cheesy, but it's overall voice acted quite well. It's just, maybe I don't need to hear Ally's water drinking quote on my 5000th swig.

_childDocuments_.review: So now that time has passed, and the game was finally released and I got around to fiddle with it a bit I think its time I revisit my old review. Right off the bat I have to say, the added content was very much needed and in the end it was what tipped me in the way of recommending the game. It is very important to note that the game is very far from perfect. This is by all means a sandbox game. The quests you get are sort of guidelines you can follow (the order of some content is questionable) but you cant get through the game just by following the quests. You need to explore, improve your gear and get to know your enemy - figuratively and literally to see resistances, and get better at perfect blocking. That being said the game is way more smooth than before and give you way more tools in the sense of base building. However as with many survival games I find it way more satisfying to play with a friend and not solo - trust me the scares from the game are way better if you can laugh at each other's reactions.

It may look like a small backyard at first glance, but every time you think you've seen it all, the Developers throw an entirely new environment or challenge at you to overcome.If I was to share one word of advice, it would be to check every corner or pathway you come across as it always offers you a wonderful or terrifying surprise at the end. With that said..Play this game. You won't regret it, I know I don't.

_childDocuments_.review: Grounded is a phenomenal survival game developed by Obsidian Entertainment and available on Steam that captures the essence of a world unseen by the human eye. In this expertly crafted open-world adventure, you'll find yourself shrunken down to the size of an ant, navigating a dangerous yet captivating backyard environment filled with various insects and creatures, each with their unique personalities and behaviors.The visual design of Grounded is nothing short of breathtaking, with every element of the environment rendered in stunning detail. From the towering blades of grass to the intricate networks of ant tunnels, players will be in awe of the level of immersion achieved. The game's soundtrack is the perfect accompaniment, seamlessly blending ambient sounds and emotive music that enhance the experience, making it one of the most memorable gaming soundscapes in recent years.Grounded offers a robust crafting system that encourages creativity and resourcefulness. As you explore the world, you'll collect materials to build shelters, tools, weapons, and even armor to better equip yourself for survival. The game masterfully balances the challenge of resource management with the satisfaction of progression, ensuring that players are constantly engaged and rewarded for their efforts.One of the standout features of Grounded is its diverse insect population. From the friendly ladybugs to the menacing spiders, the game's AI system ensures that each creature behaves true to its nature, offering a dynamic and ever-changing world to explore. This, coupled with the realistic day-night cycle and weather system, creates a sense of unpredictability and excitement in every play session.Grounded's multiplayer mode is a fantastic addition, allowing players to team up with friends to tackle the world together. This cooperative experience fosters a sense of camaraderie and teamwork, as players strategize to overcome the game's numerous challenges. Whether it's coordinating an assault on a spider nest or collaborating on the construction of an elaborate base, the multiplayer aspect of Grounded elevates the game to new heights.In conclusion, Grounded is a must-play title that offers a unique and enchanting experience for all. With its captivating world, intuitive gameplay, and engaging multiplayer mode, it is a true gem that has earned its place among the best survival games on Steam. Embark on this incredible journey, and prepare to be amazed by the wonders that await you in Grounded.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally, I highly recommended this game. Until I got to the upper yard. What the hell is this difficulty spike? It's worse than Rayman. You go from running around the back yard (AS A CHILD BY THE WAY) to exploring the Undershed full of spiders and a deep, pitch black hole full of these creepy spiky water fleas. The upper yard is RIDICULOUS. Even with upgraded T3 armor and weapons, it's hell. Poor Max, the teen I play as, has been eaten alive by water fleas, mangled by wasps, and eaten alive by black widow spiders more times than i care to count. No other game is like this. Skyrim? Kids are invincible. Grounded? Here's a tick that literally wants to drink you to death. I wouldn't have a problem with this game if we at least stood a chance, but the only way to kill a black widow (By the way, to finish the storyline you have to kill a black widow blocking the path) is by cheesing them or having absolute endgame equipment. Mithridaitism? Doesn't work on them! That awesome perk you spent hours hunting Wolf Spiders to level up has NO EFFECT on black widows! And just to screw you a little bit more than that, they filled the final boss area with bloodthirsty T3 mosquitos. I hate the developers. I've played hard games before, but this takes the cake. I got all the way to the end of the game only to discover all my perks, all my equipment, all my knowledge didn't make a damn bit of difference when I'm up against an enemy that spawns adds, heals itself insanely fast, gets faster as the fight progresses, and has super potent venom that my mutations don't help with. Thanks guys.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very grindy. I didn’t realize it was a crafting based game so if you don’t like that, this isn’t the game for you. It can be quite tedious but it also means there’s almost always something to do which is nice. The enemies take some practiced strategy to defeat, each one has its own strengths and weaknesses to help you kill them. At the beginning, the strategy is to get away, because you don’t have the weapons or armor to win. Pretty much every aspect of the game can be altered to your liking (how fast you become hungry and thirsty, how much damage you take, what you drop when you die, etc.) so if the default settings aren't to your liking, you can completely customize your playing experience. There are a few bugs. Enemies getting stuck in walls or even the ground. I was building walls and they were solid and built for me, but they looked like the blueprint of a build for my boyfriend, who I was playing with, though he couldn’t walk through them. I like that things such as missions and analyzed materials are synced across all players when playing co-op. I think you’ll appreciate it too if you’re playing with someone on a different skill set. I’ve found in other games I’ve played with my boyfriend, he’s miles ahead in player level and unlocked weapons and armor and I’m lagging behind and it’s just not as fun like that (yes, I know that’s a skill issue on my part, but the opinion still stands). It’s nice to play on equal ground with Grounded. One thing I really don’t like is the hot bar/inventory. You can’t scroll through your hot bar quickly, you have to open your menu wheel and enter your inventory that way. You do get used to it but there are still a few extra steps in there that shouldn’t be. If you can’t see your waypoints, etc. when you’re walking, it’s because you’ve accidentally toggled it off in your option wheel. It took me too long to figure that out and turn it back on. (By the way, I find it kind of ironic that to craft a gas mask, you need to kill a stinkbug, which hurts you with stink gas). Overall, I feel like the game could get a little repetitive and therefore boring just because of all the crafting, but so far it’s been pretty fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's visuals are good, and there's a lot of character in the art style and designs of the objects in the world compared to a completely realistic art direction. The amount of content in the game (creatures, equipment, building structures, resources) has also increased to a level that I would say there's a solid filling experience here, compared to the paltry experience I had in early access. While faster players could probably bust through these in about 25-30 hours, I played with a group that aimed to complete 100% of the collectibles, and it made for a leisurely time.The online infrastructure is still prone to the occasional disconnect/latency, but the system they set up is actually I think the greatest strength of Grounded. Grounded allows for the creator of the world to grant permissions to other players to open the world on their end and progress further without the host being present. In a simple example, this means that if my friend created and hosted the game, but then left on a trip for a month, I could still open up and host the world they initially created and keep playing/building/progressing with all the progress saved for when my friend gets back from their trip and we could continue playing. It created a very flexible experience that other survival/sandbox/building games should adapt if possible.Building can still be a bit janky on certain surfaces, but more structural options allow for players to have a better understanding of how to support their structures and bases, so I would consider this a marked improvement.There's a moment in survival games where players focus less on surviving and more on thriving, when a player uses their understanding of the games mechanics and systems is able to carve out a space in the world. Some games take a bit longer to achieve their level of "Home-ostasis" like Project Zomboid, and some can be done pretty much from the get go like Minecraft. This is a personal make-or-break kind of point for me in a lot of survival games, because if I perceive that a game is too difficult/complex to reach that thrive point or it isn't rewarding enough to reach that point, it demotivates me from continuing to play. Fortunately, Grounded is a little on the easier side to thrive in, it's very easy to set up a small base and resource collecting structure in the beginning areas of the backyard. With new resources for stronger tools and structures, interesting backyard set pieces that you can build new bases or rest stops at and a serviceable story structure (it mostly just moves you through exploring the backyard) Grounded does not punish you for taking your time and lets you explore and expand at your own pace.Overall, I'm glad I came back to see what changed and what new things Grounded has added (at the time of this writing, the November 13th update has yet to drop). I'm glad that Grounded did exactly what was needed to come out strong from early access and even . If you (and a few friends) have even a small interest in Grounded, it's a game I can fully recommend for people who are both new and experienced to games in the survival genre.The game looks great, and the mechanics in the game seem well-intended, if not a little lacking. But at the advertised price (unless you are on xbox gamepass) I'd say you're better off waiting. A little on the nose, but I found more bugs playing the game than actually in the biodiversity of the game. Constant disconnects, crashing, and weird building limitations (building is frustating and sometimes barely functional). I understand what early access means, and I see that with a bit of tweaking and polish this game has potential to be a great multiplayer co-op experience, just at this price for what's in the package, I can't say it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% Recommend, I think this game appeals to all walks of life and any personality. It is kid friendly, innocent and very, very enjoyable. The story line is immaculate, and it follows the story along the lines of the movie of "Honey I shrunk the kids." Worth every penny, and I wish I could play it over again from the beginning for the first time. You walk around a world surrounded by tall "Grass" what would be trees in any other generic survival game, this you chop down and use to build a home and tools, and other useful contraptions. This is the theme the game follows, gathering materials; and anytime it got repetitive or I got the least bit board, I look up into the sky and realize... i'm a tiny little human in this back yard and it feels like i'm on a safari in an endless world surrounded by giant insects that range from passive to aggressive. And i'm happy to say that isn't all. Enjoy a beautiful soundtrack that wont blare your ears out, but almost feel perfectly placed in every scenario almost like a movie, and the story line following a "Mad" scientist who has a play in why you are shrunk in the first place.
