_childDocuments_.review: One of the very freshest and most enjoyable survival games out there. It's right on the level of uniqueness that Subnautica brought to the table in terms of feeling as though you're against overwhelming odds. The learning curve is very abruptly steep, but once you climb that cliff, it becomes fluid and you will enjoy every second of the combat. Every single encounter feels impossible until you finally beat that damned (insert large bug here) and are rewarded for it. The environment is tailored to the experience, it is not random, and that makes me very happy. It's beautiful and there is an IMMENSE level of attention to detail, these devs thought of EVERYTHING. The satisfaction I get visually and emotionally while I play this game is the reason I am recommending it.There are, however, some cons I would like to bring to your attention.1. In VERY rare instances (literally I may be like one of 5 people to have ever had this problem), your save file can go out of whack. I attribute this to the forced multiplayer Xbox service login. It's such an archaic and absurd practice. Essentially what happened to my save file is that I played solo and not logged into live for a few days (about 30 in game days) and then joined a friend in a new save. The save I returned to for solo play was bizarre; all of my buildings and storage boxes had the correct loot in them, but my character's inventory was being loaded from a completely different save, the character himself was not the one I had been playing, and the mutations/molars (skills/upgrades respectively) I had worked very hard to unlock were no longer unlocked. Some of the molar upgrades were intact from a mechanical standpoint, but it was as if I had never finished the quest to upgrade them. I lost a ton of high tier items and armors, in addition to having a broken save that loaded the exact same thing regardless of which backup I loaded.2. The Xbox live service itself. Again, it is archaic and absurd that this is still a common practice. This is not a console game, and I'm playing it on Steam. I have an Xbox live account subscription for other games, not this one.3. This game is extremely unforgiving in the early stages. If you aren't paying attention, or you walk into the wrong creepy-crawly, you will be napping instantly.4. If you can't get creative with your combat strategies you may not be able to progress at all on higher difficulties. A lot of my victories against larger creatures happened either purely by accident (ie a spider missing me completely and pissing off a ladybug), or through some meticulous planning (ie dodging a spider so it misses me completely and pisses off a ladybug). All in all though, I would rate this a 10/10. I haven't had this much fun in a survival game since Subnautica was in early access.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a HUGE fan of survival games. Ever since my introduction to the genre with ARK, I have played as many as I can, as well as supported them with purchasing the early access. Games like The Forest, SCUM, 7DTD, all have been...ok games that all need some love from the developers to really shine. Grounded, however, is absolutely amazing. It is GORGEOUS, and the game play is very enjoyable. With some exploring, you can get a sense of where the story will be going for your characters. There are many hidden treats that will answer some questions and leave you asking more. Does the game have more to work on? Absolutely. However, the "lack" of content will still keep you busy for hours, exploring, gathering the goodies, etc. Does it have some bugs?  Yep. The little ones are annoying, but so far I've seen next to no "game breakers". And the big ones try to eat you. I am happy with the purchase, and would most certainly recommend this to anyone seeking a game with great potential!

_childDocuments_.review: I have such a love hate relationship with this game. I love a hardcore survival game, but I have found that the AI in this game is rigged against you. Once you begin to discover new enemy creatures, they just happen to start populating all over the map and you find them in places that you had never seen them before. The larva are extremely aggressive and their detection radius is out of control. The wolf spider you will eventually encounter has this uncanny ability to spawn anywhere with you on the map rather than it staying in it's habitat. As much as I want to love this game, I just cannot recommend this until they fix the AI. To each their own, I know there is a steady fanbase, but I will redirect my enjoyment back to my solid favorites such as The Forest, Scum, or perhaps jump back into V Rising.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Bought the game originally and absolutely hated it but played with friends, I have since continued to play the game occasionally and although some things have been fixed it is still massively irritating and disappointing. The atmosphere is amazing and the game itself is creative as hell, everything else constantly falls short in a way that ruins my enjoyment of the rest of the game.Parkour is the worst part, character movement is floaty unless you're in contact with a surface and moving, in which case it's momentum based forward and backward and instant to strafe. On it's own it's very bouncy and fun to run around, this is fine until you need precision. The game will also lag spike after sitting still before jumping, essentially any parkour jump is blind then instant. These 2 problems alone ruin any recommendation I have, it makes every part of the game-play loop constantly annoying.If you have time to fight the game constantly it's worth playing through for the environment, otherwise wait until they actually polish things.Original:$40 "Full release", this game is going to end up exactly like Subnautica, a buggy mess abandoned for a sequel. A majority of your deaths will be near instant, because of glitches, because of lag, or any combination of the 3. "Quality" changes render distance primarily but not exclusively, damn near every key is keybound and they're all terrible and overlapping. Take all being W by default speaks volumes to the actual polish they've put in, let alone a large content update before a "full release" in name only.The game as a concept is great, but their execution in actually making and releasing a game has been subpar in everything but creativity which is the literal opposite you'd expect from a 15 year old game company.TL:DR Not a full release, go buy game pass. _childDocuments_.review: I want to start this review by saying IT IS EARLY ACCESS. In all honesty, don't buy this game until there is more content. I would wait maybe 6 months, i'm sure (hoping) there will be more content by then. With that being said let's move on. The graphics for this game are absolutely stunning. I find myself frequently climbing to high places just to look around and enjoy the view. This game is gorgeous. The sound design is amazing and I am surprised to not see many people talking about it. You can tell, what enemy is nearby just based on the sounds alone. That mixed with really good ambient noises that really make the world seem alive. From dogs barking, to cars driving by. Heck, even the sound of someone mowing their lawn. The sound design of this game is amazing, and I cannot stress that enough. The story for this game is well... horribly unfinished. Which is to be expected of course. However, what we do have is a REALLY cool concept and something very interesting to be sure. Think of The Forest, which is probably the game closest to this one. The Forest has you surviving until you're prepared enough to uncover the secrets of the island. This game is practically the exact same thing. The creature design in this game is pretty good. I think in terms of enemies where this game REALLY shines is the large spiders. Spiders walk around and move the "giant" blades of grass that don't even jiggle if you walk on them. They give away their position with this detail but also blend in very well into the environment. This is the perfect mix of ominous, terrifying, and downright exciting. Seeing large enemies is always fun and gets my heart pumping. Overall this game has the most potential I've seen in a video game of this style in quite some time. I give this game a solid 7/10 and I am very sure Obsidian will not let me down once they have a more finished product. I look forward to exploring this game more and more with each update. As a final note, there is a ton of world for you to explore and enjoy the scenery. Just because the story of the game ends quickly without much content doesn't mean you can't run around and enjoy what there is to see and find. There's more to the game than the negative reviews would have you believe.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun, but I can't recommend it if you want to play Co-op.  I bought this game in early access and played if quite a lot. I expected issues, and there were issues.  Now at full release, the Co-op issues still persist.  If you plan on playing it as a single player game, you should be fine.However if you planned on playing as a full 4 player co-op survival game with friends & family then look else where. This game has constant HIGH PING issues even for players on the same LAN.  You will get constant discconects for all players that are not the host.  You will be able to rejoin the game a few times just to get disconnected  again.  This will happen a few times in fairly fast succession.  5-15 minutes.  But eventually you will just get an error when trying to rejoin. At this point the host will need to Close the game and and start over.  Once they have done that the whole process with just start over again.  There are no Dedicated server options, or any option for LAN only play.  It seems all the traffic is routed through MS XBox/LIVE so it gets backed-up and lags out.   There is an option for shared cloud saves, but the bugs out also. If you put your save in the cloud and share it with your friends/family to play, then you no-longer are allowed to have a local copy/backup.  The cloud save can then get corrupted (And it can happen often) and you loose your entire world.  It's really a shame as this game is designed for Co-op play and is quite fun for the 5-15 minutes when it works. TLDR:   Great game if you want to play Single Player.  BUT if you want to play Co-op. Look else where.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say?This game feel dated and it's not even out yet.It feels like one of thos many, MANY survival "Rust" style game we got 7 years ago, but without any new improvement, design or even just simple life quality improvement you could expect from a AAA version of that type of game. The game just feels like its trying to copy what someone who played Rust 5 years ago can remember fromt he top of its head about the game.The AI pathfinding is so utterly broken that basically all enemies either spend their time to glitch or are just a pain to fight against, it's especially obvious with the giant spiders that are supposed to be the star enemies.It feels like playing Falout 76 most of the time.The combat is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Throwing your spear will sometime act like a javelin but most of the time just bounce randomly 200 meters away because of the god awful game physic, heavy weapons are ♥♥♥♥ since they will drain all your energy in 3 shot, the enemies move WAY too much (especially the spiders) when attacking so you'll miss 2/3 of your mele attack, their attacks feels just random, sometime very telegraphied sometime just instant slap on the face, the pary system is just a disgrace, parying wont stop your attacks, in fact it seems it will instead continue your mele combo, and there's a weirdly long delay before you actually start to pary, so it's basically useless.The progression is (at the moment at leat) extrememly poorly balanced, you dont really know what to do and where to go and the UI is clearly designed for console without a single care put into it.The map feels really, REALLY small (no pun intended) and the playable kids are just the cringiest "that's what the marketing team think kids are" ♥♥♥♥ I've ever seen in my life, they look and sound like bad carricatures.And why would you try to make your game look so "kid friendly" when the actual game itself is a very punishing and obscure survival game?

_childDocuments_.review: I will update my review as things hopefully will change.I do recommend this game. I really like this game. But I want to love this game.I want to highlight all the wonderful aspects of this game that the developers have created over the last two years with feedback from the community. The game play and plot are truly special and bring a new perspective to survival games. I will touch on these things at a later time, but my frustration keeps me from singing this game's praises.I am thoroughly disappointed with the multiplayer aspect. When I am hosting, my friend lags and sometimes disconnects. When they host, the same thing happens for me. At times when I am playing on our shared world alone I will just get dropped for no reason. (No, it is not my internet). When this happens steam's cloud has sync issues and I have to wait for it to update and cross my fingers a save had been made. Occasionally I have lost some save data and have to do things over again. Lots of fatal error messages that cause panic after playing for hours... it is just sucking the fun out of the game for me. Single player mode, I have no issues but multiplayer is ridiculously flawed. I have never played another multiplayer survival with this many issues. I expect more from Xbox and don't know why they won't just create servers for this game or allow users to create their own servers. Additionally, I hate that Xbox won't just keep me logged in like every other game platform I use and I have to log in again every few days. It is so tiresome.In summary, this is a great single player game but the multiplayer mode is frustratingly glitchy. I really hope they solve these issues quickly since this is a full release. Please don't make me go back to Valheim. I want to continue my Honey I Shrunk the Kids fantasy.

_childDocuments_.review: After over 300 hours of playing almost exclusively solo both with an intermediate version and lately the full version (including ending), I can wholeheartedly say that I did enjoy this game. It's key selling point are atmosphere and level design - basically what I bought it for after watching a colleague play it. Ever since "Honey I shrunk the kids" I wanted to experience this concept in a game form and that's very much what you get here. It's absolutely great in that respect and unique in the way it represents it.What I didn't like, though, is (unfortunately) most of the gameplay. There's a whole load of base building, crafting, farming, grinding, being annoyed about overly tanky enemies (especially bosses) and a damage system that has conceptional connections to the bug world you're in but is so abstracted-out that I barely ever bothered using it. A lot of what you can do in the game is locked until you've found certain areas and have beaten certain bosses with areas of interest being simply unmanageable/inaccessible to due to lack of key items and/or resources. This will leave the more exploration minded player frustrated at first and then gradually bored since "the good stuff" requires grinding another hour to get key materials, build stuff and wait for crafting stations to have another layers of materials for more crafting. Combine this with an often more functional than exciting combat + item management system and you get a whole load of moments where you simply have to force yourself to continue. It gets better with major advances in your main quest  but I only found every, say, third point of key advancement to be interesting in terms of rewards (exploration, new interactions etc).Overall, it works quite ok since there are many elements to busy yourself with and certain moments only truly work if you've spend a decent amount of time working towards it. What absolutely didn't work for me under any circumstances were the bosses, consistently respawning enemies, overly long enemy health bars (without ways to shorten battles), lackluster base defense mechanisms (you're often better off just fighting normally) and the amount of grinding to required to advance any of your gear or even base building blocks. Maybe that's because I played solo and prefer exploring, but I can't imagine having fun grinding even more to upgrade four players than just one. Afaik there are game options to simply unlock most advances at game start but that of course kills the fun of progression. A poor but welcomed fix if I ever want to play it it again.As such, I can recommend it to players who don't mind tackling mandatory grinding with the outlook of experiencing a rather unique feel and level design. Personally I don't think I'll be touching it again for at least a couple years but will be looking forward to playing it again with adjusted settings where I don't need to bothered with its lackluster elements.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first played this game, I thought about switching Arachnaphobia mode on. Honestly, Spiders scare the hell out of me, and they certainly like to appear out of nowhere whenever you're least expecting it. Even now, over 100+ hours in, and I still get scared. I keep that slider off, because I want that feeling of dread even though i have the Coaltana. Ah, but thats when the Wolf Spiders aren't bad enough, oh no, they had to go and add another Spider that's probably worse than the Broodmother. I was still recovering a few days later after the one room in the undershed. The game just gets more enjoyable with each update. I dunno where it will go from here since we have the story, and the entire yard is accessible, but I'm here for it. This is a survival game that I can sink hours into and not be bored. _childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. I play this with my brother (we are both in our 60s) and this is one of the best co-op games around.Pros: Lots of depth to the game (and it's still in beta) with plenty to explore and do. A very immersive game with seamless areas of very different feel (jungle areas, underwater areas, grasslands, poison forests, etc etc). The equipment and upgrades are pretty well balanced and available at appropriate times.The feer aspect is nice with appropriate music and the occasional fierce critters (I’m looking at you wolf spider) you must avoid until well armed (much later ingame)Co-op: the level of cooperation to build and kill in this game is just amazing. I play alot of co-op games with friends and family and this is one of the best.Cons (most of these are pretty minor):The crafting is a little kludgy when building platforms or stairs and I expect that will change as it gets to release (Still very playable)The corps runs to get your belongings back when you die can be a bit of a pain, especially when you foolishly die deep in an underwater tunnel complex with no real way to recover your backpack and you have to constantly run past the marker reminding you you did something foolish…(maybe that’s just me).Conclusion: This game is going to be very popular when it is released.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently free to play for a limited period.Overall, I would maybe pick it up for a while if it cost around 10-15€.For what it is, I think the price is too high.The concept of the game is good and interesting and visually it looks good, but it has lots of bugs and technical issues.The progression is very confusing and the enemies can be hard to beat, even with multiple players.Often all you can do is run, and you can end up dying in a bad place and lose your items because you can't get to your backpack.After hours of playtime I have yet to find out how to make better equipment or improve the starting equipment, and for the recipes I know I need to kill more powerful enemies.I played this game with three friends. We just completed the hedge lab, but it took a long time and lots of backtracking and walkind around with no idea what to do or where to go. It was frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: Grounded is good. There are rough patches, but overall this is one of the best sandbox games I've ever played. The good: Scale is awesome. The yard feels enormous at first, but by the time you've gotten powerful enough to create a worldwide network of ziplines (not to mention tele-pottys in ng+), the world is manageable enough to not feel tedious. You can ignore most of the building and bosses if you don't feel like it, which is great for people who can't be bothered to fight the more difficult bosses that have terrible rewards (looking at you infected broodmother). The building is really in-depth, but simple enough to be easy! Some things cost a but much, but by the end-game superstructures are pretty easy to throw up quick. Bug fighting is challenging, yet rewarding to master, for the most part.The bad:Wasps. Absolutely the worst enemies in the game, as the drones in particular can be incredibly unlucky and spam regen their health and stay far from melee range- which is a problem in single player where ranged weapons suck in multi-enemy fights.Mixer events. Some of the mixer events are god-awful, and ALL of them are boring (in my opinion). They can be a pain to set up for, and can be a pain to complete. Most aren't too bad, but a few of the super mixers are brutal at the time you're supposed to complete them.Smoothies. Many people have neglected to mention the most annoying item in grounded, that being the gum nugget. The ONLY way to get smoothies (buff potions) to last longer is with gum nuggets- which are highly annoying to farm due to only having 1 or 2 per node and all nodes being mostly alone. This isn't usually a problem, until you want to make a boss smoothie or need a few long-lasting smoothies for a boss fight in WOAH mode.All in all, the downsides don't really outweigh the upsides in my opinion which leaves the game at a solid 8 or 9 out of 10 for me. Hopefully obsidian gets greenlit at some point to make a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: runs really well, the visuals and the audio are just beautiful. the map is fairly good sized, but im really hoping it grows into THE HOUSE and past the yard into THE WOODS. the only real criticism so far is the wildlife as it relates to base-building. no matter where i build, ants and brown stripey bugs invade by the tens and destroy wood walls in a couple of chomps for absolutely no reason. i even built on top of a rock they cant climb on and they somehow jiggle the rock releasing all my stored loot onto the ground for them to hijack. i did swim across the pond behind the tree and found some flagstones all lined up and seemingly bug free so for now ill live by the maps edge and keep my fingers crossed an army of ants dont swim my way. this game is truly a lot of fun so far and im looking forward to seeing it grow!

_childDocuments_.review: I have never once been disappointed in my decision to refund a game. I bought this back in it's 0.3 version and it was pretty bare. My friend and I started playing last night and burned up 6 hours without realizing it. These devs, for once in my life, I wholly trust. _childDocuments_.review: Inability to roll back patches without resorting to piracy. Gabe newell once said "Piracy is a service issue" and this is a good case for that. At 119 hours in I'm not digging the new update at all, and I have no recourse to roll it back. Honestly its another bad move by xbox game studios and honestly they are so close to being on my ban list (Like EA, Ubisoft, Blizzard) that this isn't that shocking.  Really disappointed and going to Hail Mary for a refund even after 120 hours. Its just not worth the time to deal with devs constantly changing the experience for no reason or to meet some sort of vision that I really don't care about. I was having fun, Keyword: WAS I appreciate that out of all survival games I was able to make Grounded a super painless experience which was good for a simple relaxing time or playing with friends who have very limited or poor FPS skills. If i wanted a tougher time at all id play literally anything else on the market. Even in the space of arcadey survival games it faces titans like Subnautica, and even they botched their sequel. The new content is good quality but over balance changing this late in the game is obtrusive. I had the same problem with Cyberpunk but at least in that case CDProjektRed had the foresight to add the 1.6 patch to the betas list for players to roll back. I hated the perk and combat reblance but I was easily able to go back to the experience I enjoyed.Honestly I play Grounded to shut my brain off and chill out. If i wanted restrictions on base building, 4 second delays on healing, among other changes then I would play something else. Which is what I'm going to have to do. Hope all who continue to play have fun but this is my stop and time to get off this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, what has started off as one of my favorite obsidian games, has now become a complete nightmare. Where do I startCombat-What WAS a simple but addicting combat flow has now become a chore and a inconvenience. The enemies have now become more strong since the weapons and armor became grinding excuses, which means that avoiding enimes is your best option. This is kinda hard when the hit detection is trash and there is no way to actually AVOID enemy attacks. This has been a problem since day one, and the devs have not even considered a way of dodging or weaving. This is 10x worse when you find out that 50 percent of light armors just have the status effect of just running faster. Speaking of armor, they added a armor upgrade system, and yes, its as bad as it sounds. Grinding for weapons and armor is pointless and the only reason its there is so obsidian can avoid making actual weapon balancing. All of the daggers in the game are garbage but hey, "When ya grind for ten hours for an extremely hard to catch enemy to upgrade ONCE, its pretty good!" progression- Can you believe these people made New Vegas in under 18 months. Because after taking a look at this progression, I honestly believe they are TRYING to stray away from their RPG masterpiece. Let me break down the progression: Step 1: make it to the mid portion of the game so you can actually progress ): Step 2: Look up a guide to finding all milk molars. Step 2: Get 5 perk slots and tons of health upgrade to become overpowered. Step 3: Grind for the perks that are better than the others ): Step 4: Come to find out that getting good doesn't change the flat, stale, and overly simplified gameplay so you decide to play Fallout New Vegas instead.Story- s-story? What story? You mean the 3 cutscenes that happen throughout the game? You mean that single NPC that you only talk to to progress? Or the voice characters that repeat the same lines over and over again (and half of those arent even voiced)? The ONE good thing about the story is that the tapes that you find in these outposts are pretty funny.Music- The core music isnt much special however the sound effects are spot on and are very satisfying. The sound that plays everytime you find a lab gives me a orgasm, and on top of that but the combats noises and visuals are flashy and quick. Prob the best thing in this game.Conclusion- This game is broken, boring, under developed, and in balancing hell. Their new update, "The Bugs Strike Back" doesn't hold my attention for a whole new game, and their factions and karma system (more akin to earlier games from them) is, like always, under developed. What this game NEEDS is a rerun; change the progression is it has more replay ability, change the combat so I actually want to take risks and fight, and balance the game out so I want to use weapons like daggers and swords. Cuz I feel as if this game is gonna get a wicked wiz video about it soon...

_childDocuments_.review: As of this review, Grounded is in early access. Having said that, it's already awesome. I'm having a blast with this game. Think "Honey I Shrunk The Kids" the game. Crafting, fighting bugs, searching for clues to explain why you're here and what's going on, navigating a jungle that's really just a backyard. It's great.The game feels huge, and if the boundaries of the world are any clue, it's meant to be much larger in future updates. It's not Skyrim huge, but it's big. There are even what I would call "biomes", different areas that have different resources and different enemies. You run into a bunch of different objects and landmarks that remind you of how small you are frequently, and it's like a childhood dream come true to be this small in a world this large. If Rick Moranis could somehow make a cameo, it would be perfect.The enemies can be terrifying, the first time I ran into an Orb Weaver spider, I almost had a panic attack. They're big, aggressive and powerful, and I'd recommend staying clear of them until you've crafted some of the better gear in the game. The same goes for the normally passive and admittedly cute lady bugs. Don't let their appearance fool you, they're one of the strongest bugs in the game. You fight a few different insect and arachnid types, and I'm hopeful many more will follow in the future. Even under the water isn't safe, there are a few insects down there to contend with, as well as a whale sized Koi fish! The insects can be aggressive or passive, depending on the type, but a battle with all will yield important crafting items, so go full insecticidal maniac on whatever you encounter, but be careful because some don't travel alone and don't take too kindly to you attacking their friends.There's a relatively large amount of gear to craft, and I'm confident much more will be added. Base building also has some diversity and the addition of defensive base structures will certainly come in handy for those who decide to build too close to enemies. There are tiered weapons and armors to craft and find in the game, but don't expect a Symphony of the Night sized arsenal. At the moment, there are a few Tier 3 weapons but mostly Tier 2 and below.Combat feels good, although there is a minor bug that occasionally occurs when swinging weapons and tools which consists of clicking without a swing of the weapon. It can be annoying but isn't permanent and a few attempts will get it working again. Otherwise, try to stick and move! Spiders can do major damage, particularly the terrifying Wolf Spiders, so use your bow and keep some distance. Try the different arrow types as well, they can offer different advantages depending on the situation.You must keep track of food and water intake, so cook up some meat from the insects you defeat or search for some vegan options if creepy crawlies give you the willies. Some food can expire, but acorns, mushrooms and hotdog chunks are forever, so try farming what you can store for long periods of time and leave it in your base and carry the perishables with you so you never go hungry. Water can be scarce at first but a dew collector and canteen really help with that. Hopefully a water purifier or some method to clean the stagnant puddles you find will be implemented soon.There is a story to this game as well, though it's quite limited in the current build. It seems fairly light-hearted and fun so far, so I'm personally excited to see more of it develop!My only real gripes with the game so far would be a lack of automatic inventory sorting, and a few minor bugs (no pun intended) like the no swing bug, a weird issue with being thrown into third person after escaping spider webs and the Koi fish being trapped behind some sea weed and not being able to actually prowl the pond. Also it feels like hunger and thirst drain too quickly, there's really no penalty for them depleting other than loss of stamina regeneration, but it's still annoying to have to eat and drink your body weight every 15 minutes. Really takes a lot of inventory space to have to carry that much food on you while exploring far from home. Most survival games are guilty of this though, so I really don't expect that to change here. I'd also add some more variety in the character dialogue, as they tend to repeat themselves a lot. "This is worse than Dad's brussell sprouts!" Another minor gripe is that the Orb Weavers tend to hang out in groups, and it's probably just nit picky but spiders are solitary hunters and cannibalistic, so they'd more likely kill each other than work together in a pack. They also almost never attack other insects, with the exception of the stink bugs. That's what they eat, so I don't know why you're the only thing on the menu for them. The ants attack aphids and whatnot, so it's not like the AI isn't there.All in all, I'd say it has a TON of potential to be a major name in the crafting/survival genre, and I can't wait for more updates! It's absolutely worth buying in it's current state, and the devs seem to be updating frequently, so don't be afraid to jump in and start exploring the back yard!

_childDocuments_.review: Almost all aspects of the game are good. The map is full of puzzles, hidden secrets, well designed with a very good and mastered player progression. You've got a lot of verticality, you can build your hideout/base almost anywhere and you could be scared around each corner of the map, trying to learn more and memorize a bit more of that map each time to avoid dangers or to profit on them. And there are always multiple ways to achieve your goals depending not only on your progress, but mostly on your creativity and thinking.In fact, for those who are lost among the plethora of games on Steam, you’ve got only a very few which are tuned with passion in the right way. Grounded is one of those few and I can also name Green Hell here (it’s another survival but in another genre).Grounded is made by passionate and dedicated developers which are very rare nowadays and has full rights to participate in the 2022 Game of the Year. And this point of view is shared by all my best friends.Very good work Obsidian Entertainment!

_childDocuments_.review: I like survival games, not I'm not that heavy into them. That being said, I launched this game last night and wow, I did not expect to be hooked 13 hours straight. It's still early development, so there are some odd bugs here and there, no pun intended, but it seems well put together. I only had to reset once and that was because I was breaching past caution tape into a development zone. The amount of freedom they give you early access is pretty neat in my opinion. The combat isn't incredible, but very similar to a lot of other games you would play, though I do like the perfect guard addition. The crafting system is very interesting, I like that there are layers, and I'm sure they'll expand even more when the game is fully released. I like the direction of the story, very eager to see what they do with this, usually games like this are very lack luster in this department, but I have high hopes. Aside from basic early development bugs, this game has been amazing, I highly recommend it, especially at it's current price.

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna write this review early into my playtime . I would put this up there with some of the best survival games ever released.Pros: Build like Valheim- The building in this game can be as simple as you'd like. It doesn't have a great need for 'defensive' purpose currently in the game as I feel your location can sometimes depict the troubles you will find yourself in. Build near a stink bug and your base might be stinky often (me) . Or build near some weevil's and enjoy the serenity of noises from creatures hunting them. Get lost in hours of discovery as you piece together your grassy castle. Souls Like Combat- A lot of reliance on dodge and block in this game. One of my frustrations with these souls like combat games is you can't just run in and mash your buttons and win. The enemies actually hurt, the enemies are actually designed to be blocked and dodged. If you do not , you will simply not have fun. Take this for what you will. Stunning graphics with just perfection working around field of view. Cyberpunk WHO?- Upon first arrival you start thinking, okay fortnite, as a 33 year old.. im not so much into the hype of cartoon graphics as much as I am the 7 days to die gore style graphics and realism. Just wait, give it time, the game will show you... this isn't  some cute and cuddly world. From fending off annoying mites to feeling awe struck by a passing wolf spider. The game will wow you with it's outstanding art work. The real gem comes in when you start to get some high ground and realize just what kind of world you are surrounded by. 7 days to die progression- I could be reaching a bit for comparisons but the whole idea is to say , this game is very good at its comparisons. There's some depth here , you have to fight for what you have and earn it over time. Theres plenty to discover and a lot of hidden gems if you choose to explore for them. Start out in a big world feeling a bit helpless with little direction, end up with a massive fortress ready to hunt any bug you once feared. Progression may not be fast, but the idea is , it becomes very rewarding when you get to the point of an accomplishment or a goal you pushed for. Cons : - Multiplayer gated behind an xbox live account.Im sure there are a million conversations around this but it has to be considered a con for most. I am not one to complain about this for it doesn't change a lot for me, but I am sure it's hindering a few people in a way that causes them problems.

_childDocuments_.review: So good I'm actually taking time to write a review for it! This game is definitely not easy even on the normal difficulty but that just makes it all the more rewarding when you finally get the hang of a new skill and start taking on the bigger baddies. -The crafting is unique and adds a really nice touch to the game - I didn't make a real base for my first few days playing but it really does make a huge difference. So good.-Leveling up my tools and weapons did seem pretty difficult all things considered since some of the materials needed to be collected from enemies my weaker stuff couldn't handle but it IS possible.-And for anyone out there worried about the concept of fighting giant bugs, don't worry. It does make aiming for them a tiny bit harder but as someone who is seriously terrified of all things arachnid, it's a lifesaver. _childDocuments_.review: Finally...a first access game worth playing (so far).  Not terribly buggy...except for the kinds you'd expect to find in a yard.  Of course there is room to improve the game which is the point of releasing a game before it is 'finished'.  I've tried a lot of early access games and this is one of two I didn't feel cheated by for the price.  If the developers actually hear what the feedback is saying and put more options into the game, it will be a best seller.  They just changed the menu and in some ways it is an improvement but in others it just doesn't cut it....yet.  They need to minimize the number of screen changes needed to repair items, add the ability to repair items inside chests without having to change screens, access and compare weapons and armor without having all those screen changes, have separate slots for food and water readiness, add to the mapping ability, add some type of compass and add a quick save/load ability...that kind of stuff.  If they listen and make the improvements, I would have been willing to pay sixty dollars for the game and would not hesitate to recommend it. All in all, if you don't mind putting up with the growing pains of a new game...this one is worth the time and money...and I don't give that endorsement lightly.  Having been a beta tester and gamer since PONG was the latest thing, I have played thousands of games and tested nearly 800 and recommended less than 20.  This one makes the list with Supraland, Slime Rancher, Dishonoreds, Thief franchise, Trine, Bioshock franchise and Darksiders franchise..excluding Genesis.  Hopefully disclosing those gives you an idea of what kind of games I have enjoyed.  If you liked the same sort of thing, even though Grounded is not a whole lot like any of these particular games...it has been both as relaxing as Slime Rancher and as interesting as Bioshock and Darksiders.  Hope this helps you decide.Latest update as of May 23, 2021....OK I have gone as far as possible in the game, been everywhere that is open and explored the entire map.  The Haze Lab is still locked -you can glitch in but I don't recommend it.  You have to leave your stuff outside, set a new respawn spot near the door in order to get out and it is not worth the hassle yet.  There are still tons of places to explore in the meantime and things to do...all good fun but as the game is in progress if you are a completionist and impatient it will frustrate you unless you love to build huge houses...now that is fun to do once you've explored the available areas and done the quests they have set up.  I can hardly wait until the 'under construction' areas are done and the game is finished.  until then, it is a nice game to explore and see develop...and I have enjoyed it.  Hopefully once the game is finished all the existing structures and collected material will remain because that is what I am working on doing now...accumulating materials and building stairs and bases.  Probably one of the most annoying things I have run across on the internet involving the game are all the old videos of how things used to be.  I've found stuff that is very old and it is hard to tell the date on some of it so I am not sure which update the material was recorded under.  Not a big deal for playing the game but it makes it hard to know if the feature was deleted or changed or upcoming.  Sort of like a package under the Christmas tree with no tag on it:).  Anyway, my opinion has not changed.  If they continue along this path, listen to players and respond to their concerns (which they have done quite well with me so far), this will be one great game with the potential for some killer sequels.  IMHO of course:).UPDATE TO REVIEW:  THE SHROOM AND DOOM update is very bad.  I have contacted Obsidian and let them know the issues I have found in just two days...first the graphics have been changed and it is impossible (nearly) to make the areas out at any time of the night.  Despite adjusting all parameters, without a torch you can no longer see anything clearly, even when the 'nightlights' come on.  Second they enlarged the gassy area surrounding the Haze Lab making any bases or walkways useless without a gas  areas previously accessible without the mask.  Because of the 'under construction' taped off areas it was unfair and illogical to increase or poison a larger area since players rightly assumed the map was stable except where marked 'under construction'.  Unless and until they address those issues, I recommend holding off purchasing the game.  It looks like what was a promising variety of a known genre is headed downhill unless they alter their direction and start listening to the players.  Had they read the suggestions and used some of them, this game had remarkable promise to be something very special.  Right now...I don't know.  I will continue playing and keep everyone updated as I hear from the company...but for now...it is a ten dollar game and that is a real shame.  It had a lot of potential but for the moment has taken a wrong turn.  Hopefully they will get it back on track, listen to those who've bought it and PAY ATTENTION to their advice.  We'll see.

_childDocuments_.review: Grounded is an absolutely fantastic survival game that I would highly recommend to anyone looking for a unique and immersive gaming experience. The game's concept of being shrunk down to the size of an insect and exploring a backyard is intriguing and offers a refreshing change of pace from traditional survival games.The game's graphics and sound design are top-notch, creating a realistic and immersive environment that truly transports players to a new world. The gameplay is challenging but fair, offering a wide range of activities and challenges to keep players engaged and entertained for hours on end.However, what really sets Grounded apart from other survival games is its multiplayer mode. Playing with friends is an absolute blast, allowing for strategic planning and collaboration that takes the game to a whole new level of fun. Whether you're building structures, crafting tools, or battling insects, the multiplayer mode offers an unforgettable and entertaining experience.Overall, Grounded is a fantastic game that offers adventure, strategy, and excitement in equal measure. Whether you're playing alone or with friends, you're sure to have a great time exploring the backyard and surviving against all odds. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: This game caught me by surprise. I saw the trailer and was fascinated. I bought it in early access and... well yes it was early access and lots of bugs... both of the moving kind and the computer kind. I've played it a fair but with a friend of mine who live about a 2 hour flight away from me and its a great way to have fun together. Admittedly we stopped playing for a while (life happens) but we have recently started playing again. Sadly our world from the early access broke but was fun starting over and we have made significantly more progress this play throughI must say the fact that multiplayer is done through Xbox is REALLY dumb and often buggy. We often get kicked out (even me as the host gets kicked out for losing connection to the server... buddy... I AM the server). With that you do need an Xbox account to play this online (It is free but just another thing to sign up for, bleg!)Game play: So much fun, there are still a few bugs (and then the LOTS of living bugs in the game) but I think its mostly still playable, there are a few issues with ping and lag making it difficult to time your perfect blocks but once again not game breaking. The scaling of the word is very impressive. It all takes place in a back yard but due to your new size its a full on adventure to get from one side of the yard to the other, and that's excluding our bug friends...On that: The bugs (insect and arachnid kind) are so frikken scary. My goodness. Some of them are just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (Looking at you mosquitoes, lawn mites and spiders) and some are friendly until you piss them off (#ladybug) and then you get some really cute harmless things like weevils, aphids and tadpoles. Apparently you can tame aphids, gnats and weevils but we haven't got that far yetThe story line is also pretty interesting, not going to give any spoilers but you slowly make your way around researching things (which is fairly typical of survival games) building a base (or bases) and figure out what happened and how you ended up getting shrunk down and (I assume) how to get yourself back to normal size.There are also some useful accessibility features, one I found particularly interesting is the arachnophobia safe mode which has 6 settings: 0: full on spider, 1: spider with 4 legs, 2: spider with no legs (just a floating body with fangs), 3: floating body, no fangs, 4: I don't even know how to describe it but the spiders shape effectively looks like some kind of teddy with only 2 eyes and a teddy nose, 5: only two floating textureless white blobs with two red eyesThere's colourblind mode for deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia and a bunch of other settingsAll in all highly recommend this game for hours of terrifying fun

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best 'Casual' survival experiences out there and well worth your time, as it certainly respects your time. At the time of writing I have about 17 hours and have played a little solo and a little with friends, I am about halfway through the game (or so it would have me believe). This game is a survival game, so you know, managing stats and inventories, building and upgrading to do the next tier of thing until you 'complete' the game. BUT the thing that's great about this game is it doesn't make things inconvenient for the sake of trying to add more 'gameplay'. It has some amazing systems that put the player first. You can move something you've built without having to grind out the materials again, crafting pulls from nearby containers, you can deposit similar items with a single button. You can switch up your 'build' at a whim, you aren't locked into playing any one way and even online is super straight forward. No having to set up servers, you can just share a world with friends and they can load it up and host it at any point and vice a versa. It respects your time and instead of bloating your play hours with grind, it actually focuses on the player experience.The map is really well crafted, no areas of copy paste or nothingness and there's a load to explore, each area has a really distinct feel and some great gimmicks/mechanics. Resources have their own flavour and are all fun to gather, the crafting is pretty well balanced and therefore going to gather materials is actually fun. You do have to consider what you are collecting and gear appropriately but it's not going to take hours to craft one weapon or add something to your base. The enemies are all their own thing too and the difficulty is just right, you never feel OP but you don't feel frustrated by having to run from certain things.But the best thing about this game and what I consider makes it a real gem is that anyone could play this. Be a first time survival player, someone new to gaming, a younger sibling or child, a seasoned survival player, there is really something for everyone here. It doesn't rely on lots of lore, lots of gore or lots of grind, it's a very straight forward concept that is frankly, just fun.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Game is good. 7/10. A few bugs here and there, but you're able to overlook most of them. Better as a solo-player in my opinion, and I like multiplayer games more. Overall Review (Spoilers Ahead):- Multiplayer is rough.At times it's hard to work together as a team with friends because of HOW the creatures attack you. Most fights with friends ended up with the creature never actually hitting any of us because we all just kept diverting its attention... or one person gets assigned "tank" and stands there with shield keeping its attention while everyone else gets a hit in. Not even mentioning the majority of creatures can be "cheated" by just standing on a leaf.It always seemed like they wanted this more as a single player game but at the last minute decided to change it to multiplayer. Not to mention it's kinda hard to play on a SHARED save WITHOUT your friends because you're basically forced to progress the story to get any good equipment. Sure you could avoid all the story stuff and save it for when your friends return and I tried that, but I always ended up picking up things by accident and forgetting to mention it to the others playing on the save.- There aren't too many in game bugs/errors, however when there are it's BAD.There are lots of little bits here and there that are extremely annoying (the secret lab in the log made me want to **** myself). Jumping puzzles should have never existed in this game. And for the ones who are going to say "but you can build" not in certain areas where you don't have 'land rights' (aka the hidden lab). In the map there are a few random spots me and my friends got stuck in just passing through. We lost 2 backpacks to those spots and didn't want to use the 'rescue backpack' feature since you can only do it once per save.- The pets... dear god the PETS.I hate those little f***ers. Their perks simply are NOT worth it. Every pet can get aggroed. Every f***ing pet. Ants were constantly climbing up into my base somehow mapping better than they EVER had before just to sit there and bite at my gnat or weevil. And I tried EVERYTHING. I put up 4 layers of walls, fences, traps, bombs, even had a turret handy just to shoo them away but they just KEEP COMING. I had my gnat's pet house super high up and those little bastards climbed up the entire base (breaking walls in their way mind you) just to chew at him.The only way you can "park" your pet is by having a 'pet house' in game which aren't too costly, but that doesn't stop the ants and other bugs from aggroing on them. And sometimes the houses didn't even work (another bug/error). There were plenty of times I'd put my gnat in there only to turn around and have him behind me, however it still said he was inside the house so i had to 'call' him to get anything from his inventory. Oh and the pets don't stay IN the house, they're just near it. Meaning you need a fence or to have the house on top of something to prevent them from wandering around too much (aka: ants get'em).And god FORBID you have pet damage on because these guys pretty much all die in one hit no matter if you have armor on them or not. The times we did have pet damage on we lots them like 5 seconds after getting them because an ant, spider or SOMETHING will inevitably come forward to kill it the moment you look away. They don't make a warning sound or anything either to alert you they're in trouble. They just stand there and BLAGH- dead. The only ones that seemed to survive a bit were the gnats since they were off the ground and overall had the best mapping compared to the weevil and aphid.But even then, the gnats are horrible. Even as pets they still bump into you like wild ones do. They're constantly in the way. My gnat killed me multiple times by either bumping me off, flying in the way of my attack/block, drawing aggro since everything wants to kill it- etc. Like I said, the little glide boost the gnat gives you isn't worth it. You'd get more bang for your buck by just having some sort of speed potion/juice instead.- Overall Game Function / PlayIt's good at the start, but late-game is where combat begin to fall apart.Many of the late-game weapons just sorta suck. Once you get the ox-bow that's pretty much it. Most creatures are just easier to fight at a distance even IF you do way more damage up close. Many creatures (spiders specifically) have combo moves that are so annoying to deal with I'd rather spend 10 minutes shooting at it with a bow & arrow from a leaf.I prefer melee attacks and the spider daggers are the best imo, but trying to time the blocks is HARD when half the time your shield breaks or you'll get knocked back no matter what. Not to mention spiders to poison damage too- which is actually venom for black widows (AND THEIR BABIES) & occasionally wolf spiders on chance which cannot be 'cured' AND goes through poison resistance because it's VENOM (why even have the poison resistance to begin with if it's basically only useful against orb weavers and semi-against wolfs). As as far as I know there's nothing in-game that allows you to decrease the venom damage like you can with poison.And I'll admit, the only reason I beat the infected spider queen was because she got glitched onto my gnat who wasn't even supposed to be there to begin with (he was 'in his pet home'). She was unable to move.- The story / CharactersWithout revealing too much about the lore; The story is what got me really wanting to play further.It's good, the characters are interesting, I love the way they explained how certain things work while still leaving an air of mystery, and there are multiple endings (2) to the game. The voice acting is good, but the lines get repetitive overtime.The characters you can interact with (Burgl and later on Dr. Wendell) only have so many lines to say so you can only go through their dialogues over and over. It's all the same text. Hearing Hoops say "Hoops VS. Ladybird Larva. Ding, Ding!" for the millionth time after 50+ hours in game got so tiring I ended up turning off the sounds in settings. However since you're able to switch between teens that can be fixed pretty easily by just picking a different character upon load-in since your stuff stays the same no matter which character you play. I'm glad they made all the teens 'equal' as in they don't have perks of their own that would make one a better pick over the other.Had it not been for the way everything was spread out around the map to get you to explore, I would've never perused it.The story at the start is very captivating, but this game suffers the same way Bioshock does.Audio and file logs are the main way to get the story. It's time consuming and tedious to find & read all of them. The audio logs do read out to you, but the file logs don't. You have to manually open them to read them- and sometimes I'd straight up forget to since most logs are found IN danger areas so you can't really stop to read since things are attacking you.I wish there was a way to track the data logs like you do with milk molars and other stuff in the game. I had to go online to find the rest because some are hidden WAY too well to ever be found my any casual player. I love exploring and looking for things I missed, but once you'd been in the same area 6 times only to find the data log (that looks like any other file/folder on the map) sitting right there in the corner is SO infuriating. There needs to be some sort of scanner or maybe a highlight (like a light or twinkle) that's more noticeable to see. Buried treasure twinkles & the scab wrist bands glow green, it's odd that the files (which are about the same size) don't have any indicator that's AS noticeable.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent addition to the survival-crafting genre! Ironically, GROUNDED doesn't break a lot of new ground...crafting works the way you expect it to; you collect crafting resources and assemble them. Resources are scattered across the map, but never so far away as to make the trip a chore. "Enemies" begin as almost impenetrable foes, but quickly become crafting resources themselves as you progress in ability. Some of the collection and building required is WORK, but it's never a slog that detracts from the game. Essentially, you've played games like this before.Where GROUNDED really shines is in the manner that new crafting skills and abilities are introduced.  Crafting abilities are doled out as you venture farther and farther into the corners of the map, acquiring and analyzing new crafting resources. It's just enough novelty to keep you interested--excited to see what the next upgrade will bring.Technically, the game is smooth and stable; things work the way you expect them to. Artistically, the game never fails to impress; the developers have created a beautiful and compelling landscape that is both familiar and alien to everyone who grew up in the suburbs. There is a lot to do and see in this game, and I'm excited to see future additions (what ARE those bees up to?).Oddly, I have not yet found much use for large basebuilding projects. Enemies don't seem too preoccupied with attacking me unless I wander into their field of vision. I have had the occasional orb-weaver wander into my grass-and-stem fort, but mostly the building has served as a locus for my storage chests and crafting areas. And this is mildly disappointing, given the range of base-building options you're given.As of this writing, I'm 26 hours into the world of GROUNDED and have been thoroughly entertained. Excellent!

_childDocuments_.review: The game started promising and fun, but the recent "into the woods' update.. just ruined everything.First lets talk about the need to log into microsoft account - it not logging in, and not saving, keeping you in 'offline' mode, which means you can't even give proper feedback.  That is just bad.Now let's get into game problems:the new combat system is horrible, your first attack is PUNISHED only doing 50% damage, and then you have to drain nearly all your stamina just to do a 3 hit combo to do "decent" damage.  Meanwhile, you need to block attacks - which ruins your combo.  It makes every fight tedious.Secondly. Since all weapons do less damage AND rely on combo now to do good damage, the durability drops rather fast, the only way around this is to upgrade them, but the upgrade cost is way too much, you basically run around gathering supplies for hours just to repair and upgrade your weapons, without any fun to it.  Tedious.  One of the achievements requires you to upgrade it fully, and the last few steps consume SO MUCH MATERIAL you feel like something went wrong in the calculation. (and the gains, aren't worth it)New areas are a let down honestly, mostly just 'more spiders' - sure there is some new bugs and it's fun the first time, but once you go through the termite mound, you get all the termite parts you will ever need. (because there are just so many of them attacking you) so you really have no reason to go back.   Splinters need more uses, walls, floors, whatever - but as they are you get all you need.Things that need done:base raids, with purpose (special resources, etc)change in upgrade so they are easier/less costly (using 500+ quartize is insane)change resource gathering to put the resource in backpack - unless your full (then it can explode into the world)change combat to do 100% , 100%, 200% damage so combos feel rewarding instead of punishment.Increase base health by material. (because they all break too fast with things attacking)cut the useless bugs, or at least give them 'same parts, different texture' to make unique variants of gear. Ladybirds drop ladybug parts... just make it drop ladybird parts, and the armor can be nearly the same as ladybug, but look different.Get rid of Ant Eggs all together.  They just seem to cause problems.  Instead of needing them for recipe, use Bug Rubber , which has very little other uses.  For the food - just use more ant parts.Also for food - change food.  the cooked food spoils too fast, doesn't stack, and so is a massive inventory problem on a timer.  Make buffs stronger and meals last longer, or, make meals stack with shorter buffs but never spoil. (like advanced jerky)  Getting the recipe, getting the parts, taking the time to prepare it, and then using inventory space to it - should be more rewarding than they currently are.and lastly.. do something about the spiders.  As it is, it seems wolf spiders respawn daily, and there are SO MANY of them now I always end up in combat with them, and they are no longer a threat as I have upgraded gear, so they are just annoying.  The yard should fluctuate with how players handle it, grass removed, spiders dying, other things moving in etc.  Instead I feel every game day is the same - I have to eat and drink immediately, then go out and gather stuff to repair, then gather a TON of resources to attempt any upgrades and all the while fight THE SAME bugs over and over, of which I no longer need parts of (and in some cases have chests FULL of their parts)

_childDocuments_.review: Grounded may be one of the most unique experiences I’ve had in a game for quite some time, this game truly is fascinating.Grounded is so much fun. The beginning is so intriguing but also scary because of how small and weak you feel as you see the massive spiders and Beatles roam the backyard as you try to fend for yourself. And then roaming the depths of the pond and avoiding the MASSIVE Koi fish is so much fun. Even with some of the best gear in the game you still feel challenged against the stronger enemies(and I haven’t even played at the highest difficulty yet!), this game is very much worth the buy in my opinion. It has it drawbacks like any game will, but they’re outweighed by the potential this game has. Unfortunately the development team is small(less than 20 people), however they’ve still managed to create what has so far been a fantastic experience. I’m really looking forward to seeing grounded grow and see more and more aspects be added, such as new insects, new environments, new labs, etc. The game I feel can be progressed through fairly quickly if you spend a lot of time playing all at once, however I have probably over 20 hours on it and can say there’s still a few things I’m working towards. I hope the developers keep up their great work, and honestly I hope their team gets bigger so they can be even more efficient with their updates and be able to release their bug fixes and patches more often, so they have more time to keep adding to the game. There’s so much they can add and I’m very pleased to now they’re currently working on adding many new insects. I probably sound like a broken record but again, I absolutely cannot wait to see this game continue to grow and expand, so much potential in an already beautifully designed game.

_childDocuments_.review: By far the most polished and fun co-op survival experience I had a pleasure to this. So many useful QoL features were baked in that in e.g. Valheim we had to use a mod for. The exploration is very rewarding - you have a feeling that you can find something interesting in every corner. The combat is challenging, but not overly punishing (we played on Medium). The base building feels really good, it's easy to build the kind of base you set out to. The gear/skill progression feels meaningful - but not to the point that new stuff invalidates all previous gear instantly. Also, it's not overly grindy (except maybe some of the late game weapons/enchantments).All in all, a masterpiece of game design we had a pleasure to experience. I'm not sure if I would still sing such praises if I played solo, because I don't really enjoy the survival genre when played solo, but in multiplayer Grounded shines like a well-polished diamond it is!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Grounded since it first came out in early access. I personally cannot recommend the game. I see everyone gives it high praise, which is fine, but my experiences have been very lackluster. Since it first came out Grounded has been a buggy mess. I had high hopes this would be resolved in their 1.0 update, but I still experience the same bugs and glitches as I always have. "Fake" water droplets are a big one, this is when the dew drops don't actually exist and I'm whacking at a piece of grass for nothing. Getting hard stuck and watching other insects get hard stuck can be detrimental, especially if I get hard stuck between roots when fighting a wolf spider. Speaking of wolf spider! Now this might not be an issue for most, and that's completely okay, but there are absolutely no safe zones on the map. No where to catch your breath. Within the first two nights my friends and I were being destroyed by three wolf spiders. We couldn't fight back, and we certainly couldn't get our items back. I like a challenge, don't get me wrong, but this was impossible. The wolf spiders poison you, so getting hit just once is typically a death sentence. Especially if you've just started and haven't been able to make bandages. Or a bow and arrows.  And I swear I read the wolf spider wasn't supposed to come out for the first few nights. Overall, the game isn't for me. If you're more of a casual gamer, and you prefer to have a safe place to return to when you just need a break from the challenge, this game is not for you. It's hell right out the gates, which would be fine if they gave you a fighting chance. Maybe I just suck, or maybe I've just been unlucky, but every time my friends and I start a save there's a wolf spider or two breathing down our necks within the first night or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Main thoughts: This game is great and i am having a great time playing it. it is just like hunny i shrunk the kids made into a video game. you're a child trying to survive in a person's yard while you are the size of an ant. you have to find sources of food and water as well as defend yourself from the many insects that lurk in the grass. you can build a base or multiple bases if you choose to do so and learn new crafting ideas as you gain new materials to craft with. everything that you find seems to have a use. while this game is still early access and is by no means a complete game, there is still a lot to do and explore in what they have made so far. Pros: -a nice crafting system that will surely grow as more gets released-various insects with different behaviors-a unique game idea that was implemented well-multiple difficulty levels to choose from to suit your play style-an "arachnophobia mode" that allows you to make spiders look less spider like if you are afraid of spiders-even though it is in early access it still feels like a full survival game (not including story)-not everything is trying to kill you. Cons:-because it is early access there are bound to be bugs (not the insect kind). if you want to store food be aware that it will attract ants and they will be bale to reach it seemingly regardless of where you put it. i had my food stored in a container 3 stories off the ground and in a secluded room. ants were still able to break into the container and steal food even while they were on the ground and the container was behind a wall. -SO MANY SPIDERS. spiders are one of the more difficult things to kill (at least they were for me) and they are way too common in my opinion. -while you can craft different armors from all of the creatures you kill, it didn't seem to me like one was better than another one, at least not by a significant amount. they do allow for different abilities though-at the moment there does not seem to be a way to increase your personal inventory (that i found) which fills up rather quickly and equipped items occupy inventory slots as well-though i am not sure the game really needs one, there is no fast travel system. i think it would be cool to add the ability to fast travel between the different science stations that you findFinal thoughts:This game is definitely fun and i look forward to what will be added and how the world might change. even though i finished the "story" of the early access game rather quickly, the game did not feel finished. if you like survival games where you can build and craft and you don't mind insects then i would suggest getting this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought I'd give a positive review for a game with so many bugs!Okay, now that the obligatory bugs joke is out of the way... this game surprised me in the best way. Despite my favorite genre of games being open world survival crafting games with base building, I had been reluctant to give  a try. I knew the game was "Honey I Shrunk the Kids" as an OWSC game. And that premise didn't seem like one that would draw me in. Likewise, a back yard seemed like an awfully confined setting for an open world. But Obsidian knocked it out of the park. The back yard may be small, but it is . There is not a single foot of wasted space. The crafting tree is enjoyable. The base building, while more limited in piece and furniture variety than I would prefer, is solid. I was able to create a player home for myself that I am quite proud of.I love the whimsy of this game. They had a lot of fun at Obsidian designing this. The backyard has a surprising number of biomes (including a desert setting thanks to the sandbox). There are several "dungeons", but the best is the one with the bees. I won't spoil it for you. And I get a real kick out of the attacks based on the elements of candy.The combat is fierce and feels great. There are a healthy variety of enemies, many of which have fun combat styles. I also appreciate that there is a respectable number of non-hostile critters spanning all tiers.There are multiple difficulties and a lot of very good custom game settings. I started playing on medium difficulty, which felt very challenging without being punishing. I don't care about achievements, so it took me about 60 hours to realize that I wasn't getting achievements because I wasn't logged into X-Box. At about the same time, I was hit by the first bug raid on the home I was meticulously crafting. Random home raids are an element of the game that I can appreciate the challenge of, but that I want to remove. So I switched my game to be a custom game where I could turn that off. I made other custom adjustments such as setting the game to pause while in a menu so I could read data entries at my leisure.I was happy to learn that there is an optional series of castle-defense style raids in the game that I can participate in to experience that element of gameplay even after having disabled the random home raids. As of this review, I have done all but the final quest chain. But I am avoiding that because I don't want the game to end. I'm having too much fun in the backyard.This qualifies as going outside and getting fresh air, right?

Everything I've seen so far has me interested in the game, but I would love to see more content related to the story as well as more areas to explore and new bugs to farm.I have high hopes for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game reminds me of "Mom I Shrunk the Kids".  Running around staying out of the way of spiders, and looking for pieces of the puzzle of why you find yourself the size of a bug.   Speaking of I came back to the game and found that the characters have a lot more to say, and are actually hilarious. Keep it up devs, you are doing great!
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot about this game that's great. The setting is really fun, much of the crafting is clever. I just played it for free, I'll probably get it when it goes on sale.There's some problems with it too. The building snapping is clunky. Progression is hard, you get in over your head very quickly and just stay there, which can be very frustrating and sap the fun out of it. Hopefully they fix this issues throughout the Beta.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful. The world is amazing to explore and you really feel tiny compared to the environment around you. The enemies are creepy and cool and they're all unique. There are still problems with the enemies pathfinding where you can exploit their size and lead them to get stuck between objects (or they just stop moving sometimes) and hit them without risk, but this is expected since the game is in pre-release. In my opinion the game is still worth buying and you can really feel the love the devs put in with the environment and the dialogues.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like how games USED TO FEEL! I'm absolutely hooked playing this game, and I play on PC while my husband plays on Xbox. We own a business and work 70 hours a week, but when we come home, we can't wait to play Grounded together. We've both been casual gamers most of our lives as millennials, and I thought finding something to play together would be a lot of fun, and man did I pick the right game. The custom game option to dial back the survival mode and just focus on exploring, team working staying out of trouble, and building has been a joy for both of us. I love the art style, the occasional glitches have been hilarious (thought you were safe in the soda can from a giant spider? How about he just magically appears inside it with you?!), and the AI for the insects has had me laughing out loud so many times. Curious ants stealing our food when we weren't looking, weevils dashing to the coveted early-food item of mushrooms before you can get there... It's so polished, and well thought out! I'm still getting used to the crafting and inventory menus, but I don't know if that's a design flaw or just because I'm getting older and it's harder to remember where everything is situated on a controller... this game has so much character, and so much replay value... I'm recalling lots of childhood memories playing outside while we work our way through the yard, and the visual marketing of the 90s aesthetic is honestly absolutely genius. The zoomers love the look, and the millennials are nostalgic! We're just getting started and I can tell this is going to be a staple in our free time for a very long time. Bravo Obsidian... BRAVO!
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: Week two and this game is already amazing. It has so much polish and honestly right now the only down sides are that there isnt enough story to do, and there could honestly be more wild life (Where are the bees/wasps from the title picture?) and the occasional crash. Expect more from this in the future. 4/5 stars from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game.I've been burned by early access when it was first introduced to Steam (StarForge anyone?), so I rarely buy early access titles anymore (Valheim was the last exception and rather disappointing :/ ).  So thanks for the free weekend Obsidian, was a fun taste but I think I'll wait for full release.Slightly difficult when starting and a chore to run to your backpack repeatedly.  A wolf spider right at the first resource analyzer was a little unexpected.  Thankfully he glitched out, getting stuck in the research tent, and we were able to poke at him for 10 minutes with sticks to take him down...The building is a little frustrating with the snaps and only 90° rotation it seems.  Needs a mousewheel smooth rotation implementation, specifically for wall building.Seems to be a lot of content but unless you're playing with friends, the chore of lugging resources will probably tire and bore you out.Don't currently recommend as early access title.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I was a little kid watching honey I shrunk the kids... Oh the joys of experiencing being so tiny in a world so large!I have thoroughly enjoyed this game and I love the updates! I can't wait to see what else they provide.The one downside, the map is static. I would love to see additional maps/backyards, or possibly seeing an addition to the game without the story and a procedurely generated map. That would be a lot of fun to explore and enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: "The story is too short." is what im hearing from a lot of people. Honestly, I dont think it needs a long story. I got the idea after the intro. I think it was well done. As far as the gameplay goes I havent loved a survival game more than this one. The realistic bugs, foliage, "big items" (like the cans and food containers), the concept of being shrunk, and really just the overall idea of it. I know this game just came out so there's bound to be a load of "bugs". I have posted quite a few myself. But I love this game enough to where im excited to see where its going. Sure the bugs can be a nuisance but hey.. welcome to Unreal Engine. Takes a bit to get fixed. I will suggest this game to everyone i talk to. I think the only thing i have an issue with that im sure will come later is being able to create your own character but I get that too because of the voice overs. Well done guys and gals. Id love to be apart of anything you can let me do.
