_childDocuments_.review: So I purchased this game a long time ago while it was still pre-release and I toyed around with it a little bit, but the story was limited to basically the first quest. I hadn't played it for a while and decided to try it on the Steam Deck. The store page says unsupported but I was curious and tried it anyway as many games that aren't supported actually work just fine. Turns out it runs PERFECTLY, but only in single player as it seems the xbox multiplayer isn't supported (please add steam multi-player @devs).This game has been an absolute blast, shockingly fun, and surprisingly engaging. It feels like a combination of games like Ark or Conan, but with Monster Hunter elements. I go out - kill some bugs - and come back to base to build armor and weapons to then kill harder and bigger bugs to do the same. The base building element is super cute and you get both utility and cosmetic items to put in your base. I have several bases in the different biomes and plan on building more.I think of all the survival/crafting games I have played, this is my favorite by far. In games like Ark or Conan I always felt things were a bit inaccessible unless I wanted to grind for 200 hours just to even begin the pve content. Grounded is very different in that I always felt (and continues to feel) challenging when fighting the enemies, but I feel everything is balanced remarkably well even for single player. A good example being even though I have higher-tier armor, certain earlier-game spiders can still wreck me if I am not engaged with the combat. Each enemy has unique combat and tells as to when they may attack, as well as attack patterns to learn - which I love. Also - I have read a lot of others do not think the story is very engaging, or is just average. I disagree. Having read all the notes and listened to many tapes scattered around, I actually feel very immersed in the story. Arguably it is actually one of my favorite aspects of the game as generally I rarely feel engaged in a game because of the plot. I have not yet completed the game, but I believe I am nearly to the end, having covered nearly the entire map already, and I have to say that the game has been amazing!If the devs were to add steam multi-player, the game would certainly be "Verified" for steam deck, and would be perfect. I would HIGHLY recommend this game really to anyone. It, to me, fits into a lot of genres of game that I like, and is fun for a multitude of reasons.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: So much fun.  Challenging but not frustrating.  Love the soundtrack.  Currently, just a few issues:Game crashes happen, but seem to taper off after a few hours of play.Some hit box issues during fights with the larger opponents.Please let us stack edible food!F*ck you Wolf Spider!Love being able to set up a base and spawn point where ever and when ever.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: Honey I Shrunk the Kids meets Ark Survival - though I've not played this at ALL on multiplayer, unlike Ark it is a ton of fun to run around on single player and experience the world for what it is. It's very well done, considering it's early access and there's a bunch of things you can do and enjoy. There's still some things that need work, obviously, such as the respawn issue I've ran into that if something runs away from you after you shoot it from up high or somewhere "safe", it tends to spawn another one, and the other one walks back. Meaning you could have... oh... 8 wolf spiders instead of 2. There's also some small building errors where things don't "snap" properly to existing structures, some floating wall lamps here and there, and the settings don't stick when you turn the game back on. (Curse you motion blur) the NPC occasionally gives you a daily quest of something not yet released in the game as well (Mosquitos, where art thou?) However, these are small complaints. I absolutely love the game, and I've been literally enjoying my time playing it. I love playing with the building mechanics and doing literally almost whatever I want, and really look forward to new stuff being added. It's everything I loved about Ark- the building, the exploration, and the sense of wonder as you find new and exciting sights and places. Crafting is a lot of fun, and does feel rewarding once you get it all together and working. I love that you have to physically carry things back to your base, and the ant armor of all things is what allows you to carry more. The existing lore and NPC  dialogue is very intriguing and I can't wait to learn more about it!
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun survival game. Not as silly managey as some other games, but has really fun gameplay and some great things to find and craft. Highly recommended with friends as this game thrives off multiplayer. The crafting system is easy to learn and fairly deep for what the game is right now. Looking forward to patches and update for more stories and content.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential. However there are a few things that aren't fantastic. If you're playing solo I think the combat mechanics could use tweaking as I found the only way to take on a significant foe was to use arrows and jump up and down from a position where they couldn't reach you. The game has a lot of potential though.Fun game, though not sure it's worth it at the current price of $40 in Aus
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing, I have played maybe a fraction of the hot and hazy update.So far since my last experience, the game has gotten so much better.Nearly double the content it had before.I'm taking my time and actually enjoying building bases with all the new things i discover.And every new discovery only brings more excitement.Obisidian is putting their heart and soul into this one here.It's great with friends and even fun to play in your spare time.The gameplay and immersive world experience is great(even for an early access title).
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy this game if you plan to keep your phone number! In order to play multiplayer, you will need a xbox account, not a big deal right? Well, if you don't give them all of your information, Microsoft will ban your account for "suspicious activity" and force you to give them your phone number. And they will wait till you're pass Steam's refund time, so don't even bother unless you want to play alone.As far as gameplay goes, it's fine, it's another survival game with decent combat but nothing that outstanding.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.The feeling of being tiny is quite convincing. As you find bits of information scattered around the backyard, the story unfolds, revealing how and why you were shrunk. It's a great premise for a survival game.Most of the resources you need come from bugs, so there's a lot of combat and the fights can get pretty hard. A single bug is usually no threat, but many of them are bigger than you and a swarm will easily kill you.Base building is fun but largely optional, so you don't have to build a lot if you don't want to. A couple of key structures and some storage crates will do. But you can also go nuts and build a gigantic house if you wish to.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing since the Haze, absolutely love the content additions and aesthetic of the Grounded world! Watching the yard grow over the years has been quite an adventure and I feel almost proud to say this game has made its way comfortably into my list of favorites. So many secrets and post-game content to dig into that I feel I may never truly walk away from this game. Oh yeah. And you guys complaining about having to log in through xbox? Not a sound argument when the online experience is free UNLESS you’re not playing on computer. Obsidian is not omnipotent, they can’t will cross platform multiplayer into existence willy nilly or stand to force everybody to create a new account just for this game. Im just glad its on as many platforms as it is with frequent updates. Despite cultural belief it feels good to have a dev team that listens and actively tries to fix problems!
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast, I highly recommend it. It’s a little limited on content right now, but it will be getting regular updates up until it’s release. Obsidian is a quality developer and I have no problem supporting this. Don’t pay attention to these whiners complaining about using the Xbox app, it’s already on Windows anyways. I think it’s pretty cool how they are integrating Xbox in with pc with their games. My daughter and I spent about 3 hours today crafting our base, myself on my PC and her on her Xbox with no problem. It’s a beautiful game that’s only gonna get better, so come join my daughter and I...these bugs are tuff!
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes the best aspects of many multiplayer survival games and they all mesh together perfectly to create a beautiful escape. There are a lot of little details and easter eggs everywhere and, much like the great work they've done in the past, you are rewarded for your adventuring with a landscape that is not monotonous. You do not feel like you are staring at recycled textures and the game invites you to build multiple outposts and explore every nook and cranny in the area. The storyline itself, I haven't beaten/finished yet, but it is both interesting and really funny.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely one of my favorite games. There is so much to do, so much to see, so much to build, and more. The collaboration (or ability to be solo, if that's your style) is amazing. Graphics, soundtrack, sound effects, story line, everything really makes this game great! I love survival games, and surviving in this one is so uniquely interesting. Highly, HIGHLY recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game and the challenges that come with it. The only thing that annoys me so much is the fact that paybacks (natural and from the waft emitter) have such a limited time. If it's OK (no need to rush) could you allow players to see how long they have on the payback, and increase the time the paybacks last for? This is not a requirement. I do recommend it to other players who are up for a great challenge.From: moonjangsamP.S. Please make it so that creatures placed in playground mode fight each other if they are angry, regardless if they are in the same animal family or not, please! It would make playground tournaments a lot easier to make and do.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is okay, nothing special. It's a mixture of "Honey I shrunk the kids" with a bit of "Toy Story".The concept is okay but there isn't much to do, the mechanics are clunky and hits don't register.I also don't appreciate that you need to also have an account with XBOX live in order to play coopFor anybody that has a fear of spiders:- F***ing grow a pair
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: For a work in progress, this game is fantastic. I like that it uses the Unreal engine. The gameplay experience is smooth now, compared to before, but with each update, major and minor fixes are introduced, as well as content. There is still a lot more content that will be released judging by the map size and the areas that are left "blank". It is pretty fun to play with your friends and the more the merrier.I do recommend you purchase this game and get a copy for a friend of yours to go at it together!Updated Review:The game is so much better and I still recommend it. They continue to improve the game with free updates and are fixing glitches. I was able to successfully continue an older save from 1 year ago. Right now my favorite part is the ability to share your world with a friend who can come online to do stuff while you are offline, such as base building and resource gathering (that's what I do) which makes it easier to explore the map when you don't have to keep worrying about the same resources.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: My girl and I love this game, it was a bit difficult at first to find out where we were supposed to go aka (blueberry tree) but after that the story basically tells you your next goal. Grounded is definitely worth playing now the progression is great, weapons feel rewarding, bosses are challenging to go against when you find them and your constantly running into new creatures so the game doesn't feel to grindy till the endgame once you get tier 3 items. moist lvl 100% when i play grounded ;}
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of my favorite survival games, up there with Subnautica. Takes a lot of ideas from Green Hell and Forest though. The game is quite immersive and does an awesome job with the setting and lots of small details. The story is well done even if it is all told through text/audio logs and Burgl. Milk Molar hunting is pretty satisfying (at least until you start running out of easy ones :) Really my only gripes are that when building and unlocking better materials, it is annoying to rebuild your base or re-locate (Sturdy grass > Weed is easy as your house is small still, but weed > brick is rough). Would be nice to replace/upgrade components in position without moving everything and recycling but I'm also a one big base type of player. Also solo, some of the enemies are pretty rough so it's either ranged cheese (stuck wolf spiders yay) or perfect parry javelin spam with some lifesteal in between. Would be really fun coop for more build diversity than solo.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game! Still in develepment and I love seeing all the new features, I feel like the game is really starting to take it's shape now and I hope this community grows and that the devs get more feedback. There are still times when we have to log off and log on 2 or 3 times to get multiplayer to run properly. The quests are difficult enough to keep them interesting , at least up through level 7 which is where I'm at currently.If you enjoy games that let you build, then you will love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: This games vibe and visuals are amazing. I love the soundtrack as well!As with any early access game, there are few quarks here and there. I've not personally experienced performance issues outside of playing multiplayer. I have crashed a few times while playing in a friends game but when I join back I haven't lost much or any progress.I have mostly experienced visual oddities from floating objects to odd animations (like the bow appearing weird when shooting it)I'm so excited to see where the narrative goes and how the game develops. _childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: Playing it as of 2023.  I didn't think I'd like it as it seemed kind of kid-like and I'm an old man.  After playing it, I'd say it's probably one of my favorite survival games ever!  Polished mechanics, challenging enemies, interesting tasks, and fun adventures to be had - especially with friends this game is really great.  A+++ If you love base building/crafting and stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Grounded

_childDocuments_.review: Grounded is a survival game developed by Obsidian Entertainment that puts players in the role of a shrunken down teenager fighting for survival in a backyard filled with dangerous creatures. Despite being my third favorite game, I have to admit that I am uncertain about how much more time I will spend playing it, as I have already exhausted all of the content currently available.One of the standout features of the game is its immersive world-building and survival mechanics. The game's graphics and sound design are top-notch, creating a visually stunning world that is both captivating and terrifying. The game's survival mechanics are also highly engaging, forcing players to be mindful of their resources and environment if they want to survive.However, I have to admit that I have already played through all of the game's content, leaving me unsure about how much more time I will spend playing it. While the game's story and setting are interesting and engaging, there is currently limited content and variety in terms of the tasks and objectives that players must complete. Additionally, while the game's world is rich and full of detail, it is currently limited to a single backyard, leaving me craving for more exploration opportunities.That being said, I am excited to see where Grounded goes from here. The game has a lot of potential, and with the addition of more content and features, it could become a true standout in the survival genre. I am particularly hopeful that the developers will add additional areas to explore, such as the inside of the house or other nearby backyards, which would greatly increase the game's replayability and exploration potential. For now, however, I will wait for more content to be added before diving back in, as I have already exhausted all that the game currently has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: I have personally had a great time in this game, but With the recent Into the woods update and the new guard update, the quality has taken a bit of a nosedive. There are too many time sinks in this game like the upgrade system for armor and tools of a weapon its around 250 quartzite just to upgrade to max and this is not counting the jeweled shells. Durability of items are way too low, every fight feels like a drawn out dark souls boss battle, every other enemy give you negative status effects that make it even worse, heavy armor which you need to just live in a fight for just 15 seconds and not get instantly deleted makes the fight even slower with the stamina penalty, mutations help but not enough to really help, some of the armors are just not worth it, and even just getting one tier three item is like pulling out all of your teeth except your only tools are a piece of fishing line, a broken pair of pliers, a door, and you have no pain killers.Grounded has a massive amount of potential but the devs are just squandering it, and apparently have a hard on for just making the game a grindfest with little reward. Honestly its one of the harder survival games I have ever played and in this case it isn't a good thing.But it has some of the best boss fights in a survival game. The brood mother and the assistant manager weren't super difficult but they made you think they didn't do so much damage to one shot you, and didn't have too much health. The only real problem with them is the fact that they both summon adds which the devs have to be careful with otherwise every boss will feel the same.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much going for it, and I have really enjoyed so many aspects of it, but I feel like the experience is ruined by one very important thing: bug AI. Most of the gameplay experience resolves around your interactions with the insects. Alas, the artificial intelligence governing their behavior is frustrating, unrealistic and borderline silly. How so? It's almost as if all the insects had a town hall and said “hey, these shrunken humans are a serious threat to our survival. So from now on we'll put aside our normal food chain preferences and join forces to only hunt down and murder humans”. Seriously, you can walk into an area where bombardiers, spiders and mosquitoes are hanging out peacefully together, with no interest in consuming one another, but the moment you show up they form a bloodthirsty mob bent on stamping out your miniature existence. Sure, some bugs do ignore you (e.g. ladybugs, aphids) and some insects do hunt other insects, but the AI was definitely written to prioritize the death of you, the player, at all costs. This can be frustrating early on and just feels completely unnatural. If a bug wants to murder you, it will stop at nothing to do so, even pursuing you clear to the other end of the map. But the moment I jump up to some slightly higher ground, they become idiots and either give up or make no effort to come get me. This feels especially silly since most insects are excellent climbers. Killing most predators can be done simply by standing somewhere high and shooting an unnecessarily large quantity of arrows into them (seriously, why does it take 60 arrows to down a single bug. Even my level 2 bow feels like a nerf gun).Everything else about the game is fantastic! The bugs are a huge part of the experience, and a welcomed one. But unless the ridiculous AI is reworked, I cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A very well put together game. It is also refreshing to have an all ages friendly survival style game out there. The only blood you see is grub goo, and ant innards. Very immersive with a cartoonish, yet detailed art style. Runs quite smooth for me, and as of yet there have been no game crashes. There have been some minor issues revolving around insects and some items ending up in the mesh.(under terrain etc.), but overall it is very well polished when compared to most other games, early access or not. And don't let the early access thing dissuade you from picking this up. There is a lot to do here and many of the core systems/story quests are in the game already w/ what seems like a good bit of future content being released. Building and crafting is very intuitive and fun, and the overall atmosphere and map is very well designed and laid out. Like other similar games, when you start, it seems excessively difficult, but once you figure out what sounds each bug makes and how they act, it gets a lot more manageable. Also you don't actually need xbox live if you only care about single player.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I start with this game. First off this games graphics are just phenomenal! Absolutely beautiful environments and it's all just one backyard! The longer I played the more I would section off each area as a different Biome and the more I got into the game. Exploration is heavily rewarded with the upgrades you can get or the REALLY hidden recipes and materials you can find. Some of the recipes you obtain throughout the game can also help you better explore certain areas as well. Now the combat system. At first I didn't like it, but the more I played the more intuitive it felt and the more I got into it. block at the right time and you nullify all damage (parry). If you have a shield you can block most damage until you run out of stamina or they knock you off balance (you get stunned in this case). You hit enemies in the head with a blunt weapon chances are you will stun them (same goes if you parry certain enemies). Then you got all sorts of healing items as well as weapons that can inflict different status effects. You can also use your weird hand scope power to see what enemies are weak against as well as strong against. Using this I ended up always having a different weapon type to handle each enemy. Now mutations, something I love the most in this game, this mechanic passively rewards you with a free skill the more you do something specific. Sprint more, you get more stamina and can sprint faster, use a two handed weapon, get the barbarian mutation where you can go crazy with two handed weapons, use daggers a lot, get a buff to where daggers will bleed enemies, etc, etc. You are very limited at first on which mutations you can have selected at first, but the further you get In the game, the more you can have! There is also plenty of enemy types and each enemy makes sense for its environment (will say wolf spiders are annoyingly abundant). Progression is actually pretty smooth and if your experienced can be pretty quick. Base building within the game is both fun and incredibly creative, also placement isn't annoyingly specific like in some games where you can build. Also with the cozy meter mechanic the game promotes players to be creative with their base building which I absolutely adore. The Game like most sandboxes also has a creative mode in case you just wanna build massive creations without having to gather the supplies. But it also has the Sandbox mode, where you can make the backyard however you want, making the base progression how you want it, or creative alternate stories or gamemodes. Another one of my favorite things of this game is the multiplayer and how they handled it. If you wanted to play the game with a few friends then you can set the game to be a cloud server. In doing so anyone who loads the save through the multiplayer menu, becomes the host until they leave. This allows your friends to join the server at anytime without needing to wait on someone to specifically host the game! I will say the major downside is when you first get the game you to play online you NEED to have or make a Microsoft account which for me to just retrieve my password was an absolute pain in the a**. However the trouble was worth it to play the game with my family :3.In all honesty if you are looking for a fun survival game whether it be to play alone or with a few friends I highly suggest this game.

I was constantly losing huge inventories of supplies, only to finally see a chest shaking  from inside my camp and realize it was being hit by something like 7 feet away. Whats even more fun is the incredible ease that the game will just have these never ending larva swarms break into your base and keep you in a death lock. They kill you, and no mater how damaged they are, the second you respawn, they get all their health back, and are still on your body. _childDocuments_.review: The game devs have really hit a sweet spot here, between challenging and entertaining.  Rather than a punishing grind requirement or ridiculous carry restrictions as a mechanism to (antagonistically) extend the playability time or cripple progression in a game that inherently lacks content; these devs have stepped up and created a world environment that is challenging - along with the gathering and progression feeling more natural and organic (cough), rather than punitive or ridiculously crippled to make up for a world design itself lacking in challenge as so many other games must resort to. Maybe it wasn't so - from the beginning of the game's life cycle.  At this point though I give a solid two thumbs up to these guys after playing for a good 3-4 days or so.  I've heard that the mid to late game progression feels like it stalls a bit, or ramps up too high too fast for gaining tiers and access to improved items.  If I hit something which seems to break or drastically reduce the games playability I'll post an edited rant and drop the thumbs down, which I'm just sure they are super terrified of coming from one other unknown nerd.

_childDocuments_.review: Launch impressions: This game is neat, but it's what I think of as a "polished early access." What's included is good: the core gameplay seems to be mostly there with a large number of craftables and materials, and the visuals and art are very nice, but there basically is no story at this time (half characters don't even seem to have any dialog recorded yet) and it has a fair number of bugs and balance issues and could use some work on interface.  The survival aspects of the game are fairly light on medium difficulty, with food and water being pretty much everywhere and the only death penalty being a dropped inventory which you can run back to and pick up. Basically right now you can explore the map and build a nice base, but have no particular gameplay reason or story motivation given to do so. I don't have any reason not to recommend it with the caveat that the $30  price tag is pretty high for what's on offer right now. That said, it seems about right for what I'd expect the game to become when it's nearer to completion, so be aware that if you're not going to wait for a sale or the game to be ready then you're basically paying extra to get an early look.

_childDocuments_.review: (The short version: this is The Forest if you played as Timmy.  It's good, go get it.)The full version:Do you hate children? Are you a soulless, old crank who will cringe at the sound of a tween groaning good-naturedly as they bravely chow down on aphid guts and battle gigantic spiders with makeshift weapons? If so, then this game isn't for you, because it's all about kids and that looming wonder called imagination - something most of us can relate to in some form. Remember as a kid, looking at your toys in the backyard dirt and wondering what it would be like if you were shrunk down to a fraction of your size, turned loose to roam a miniature jungle rife with deadly bugs and tantalizing adventure? Well, Grounded takes that dream and brings it as close as possible to reality, albeit in a video game format.How much content is there? If you are only playing this for the story objectives, it will take you perhaps around an hour to complete most of it.  Not bad, considering contemporary survival games ( i.e. The Forest) can often be completed in a similar amount of time.  If you want to dig into the base-building, survival aspect, I estimate you will receive at least a full week's worth of discovery before things start to become repetitive.  Base building is well-realized and allows great freedom; you can build in most places and with most environmental materials. If you are familiar with The Forest, the building system is only slightly less versatile, but still extremely enjoyable.How much variety of enemies is there?  There are at least 10 different types of "miniature monsters" you will face, and they are all gorgeously (hideously) realized and very realistic in their behavior.  Weapons are also quite varied in their kinds and will satisfy both melee and ranged combat lovers alike.The survival aspect is simple, easy to manage, but challenging enough. Basic food, water, wellness management gives you motivation to explore your surroundings and take care which foods you consume.Is the game buggy?  Yes, but most bugs I have encountered were minor ones, such as difficulty traversing certain types of terrain, some wonky physics, and the very occasional crash.  This game is very well polished in my opinion, considering that it is still in early access. If the devs did little more to this game, I would be a little disappointed but wouldn't regret the $30 spent on it.Conclusion - Grounded is a cute (but sometimes terrifying) gem of a game.  You can feel and see all the love and heart the team poured into the game, and it makes for a fun and satisfying experience.  There's not many things more fulfilling than squashing an annoying arachnid the size of a house!  If the game looks interesting to you, chances are extremely high you will love it. Give this game a chance, I don't think you'll be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10The suburbs of cities in the USA in the nineties, full of houses with beautiful well-kept gardens, with beautiful plants and almost no insects, but unfortunately our adventure does not take place in one of these, but in a garden that has not been for a long time receives attention, with the tall grass, the objects thrown in any way and rusting, and various insects from harmless aphids to dangerous spiders reside here, in this same garden where a suitcase rests, containing four teenagers inside, who in some mysterious way , is now the size of an ant. ^^This group of teenagers now needs to find not only a way to return to their normal size, but mainly to survive with the peculiarities of their new height. starting with the easier things like getting water and food, especially now having to compete with ants and other insects, and other issues a "little" more difficult, like not becoming part of the food chain, as carnivorous insects won't think twice, before trying to add a group of teenagers to they menu, surely the last thing our little protagonists want. ^^+ A survival game with a very different theme, taking place in an ordinary place like a garden, but with a very different perspective of being the size of a small insect.+ A wide variety of locations to explore and resources to find and figure out how to use, with some of these resources being quite rare.+ A large number of species of insects each with its own behavior, some harmless, others attack to defend themselves, and the vast majority attack at first sight, and all with their own spoils that they leave behind when being hunted.+ Beautiful graphics, which manage to both enchant during the day, and also cause chills at times like night or dark places.+ Good variety of types of weapons and armor, each with its advantage. including bonuses for wearing a full set of armor made from the same insect.+ Option to play solo or online with up to four friends.+ Having the option of a first or third person camera, I personally liked the third person camera a lot more.- The online mode only allows you to find games from people who are part of your friends list, making it very annoying for those who don't have friends who have the game to be able to play online, in addition to being mandatory to have an Xbox account to use the online mode .- The game is capable of giving some good scares, especially for those who have a phobia of insects and/or spiders, as they are very detailed and realistic.- The rarest achievement of doing 100% of the game is actually doing everything the game has, looking at all the bugs, analyzing all the resources, buying all the upgrades, and a bunch of other stuff.Thus begins the wild journey of survival for our player or group of up to four players, each of them controlling one of the four teenagers in this small big jungle, having first to take care of getting a constant source of food and water and build a small shelter. But once that's secured, begins to explore the large garden, discovering the world's various inhabitants among the grass, some peaceful and even serving as a source of food, while others won't think twice about trying to dine the players. ^^But while they have poison, webs and other abilities, the players have the power of science, as luckily this seems to have been a scientist's garden, which left a few small facilities where players can analyze new resources and learn how to transform them, in useful things, like weapons and armor to balance the level and be able to fight against insects, from which a considerable part of the resources comes from, in addition to which this same scientist seemed to be researching, among other things, a way to be able to make a person shrink return to normal size. ^^Produced by the studio Obsidian Entertainment I liked the graphics of the game, they are not super realistic graphics but I think they matched the game more like this, making this small world equally beautiful during the day and sinister at night, also a compliment to the team who modeled the various insects, I confess that some really scared me a few times, with those bright eyes. As for the soundtrack, I was also satisfied, good and relaxing music, and I liked that each type of insect had its own sound, making it possible for me to identify it by sound, even before seeing it. ^^Grounded was a fun experience, I enjoyed the experience of seeing something mundane like a garden from a new, much smaller point of view, which I must confess I was a little worried about at first because of the idea of huge insects, but after a few initial scares and help from the third person mode, I got used to it, and I could have fun exploring and hunting in this world of small giants. Apart from the complication of being able to play online, and if you're not afraid of insects and spiders, it's a fun game that I recommend to play alone or with a group of friends. ^^

name: Summer in Mara
detailed_description: ‘Summer in Mara’ is a summer adventure with farming, crafting, and exploring mechanics set in a tropical archipelago. ‘Summer in Mara’ is a single-player experience in a calm, relaxing environment, with a handmade look and an exciting narrative. You will be Koa, a little adventurer girl who wants to explore the world that surrounds her. In ‘Summer in Mara’ you’ll have to take care of your own island, harvest your crops, create new tools and buildings, and sail with your boat to discover new islands and secrets. KEY FEATURES - An open ocean with over 20 islands to explore. - Customize your own island with buildings, crops, and farm animals. - Over 25 characters to meet and befriend. - More than 300 quests to make Mara a better place. - Day and night cycle that has an effect on the world with climatic events. You’ll have your own island, but taking care of something like that is a lot of hard work. You’ll be able to plant trees to get wood and craft new tools and buildings with different materials. Or you can create crop fields to grow all kinds of vegetables. You’ll also have a farm with chickens and pigs to take care of. But be careful, because this isn’t as easy as it looks! You’ll also be able to fish in a pond or in the open sea, cut trees with your hatchet, build things with your hammer, and use a hoe to help you harvest your island. Koa will need your help. With a basic set of skills, she can acquire new abilities and learn from the world that surrounds her. We want you to feel like you’re growing up with Koa, bonding with her and with all the other people in the archipelago. You’ll be able to sail to new islands and find treasures and other secrets in the middle of the sea with your trusty boat, which you can upgrade with a little effort and time. With new islands come new people. You’ll talk and trade with over twenty characters, each one with their own story and life. They’ll give you quests, hints about the world, or just anecdotes about their experiences and travels. Getting to know them is a significant part of the game, so we put much effort into making them unique and exciting. But not everyone will be friendly. An evil corporation called Elit wants to conquer Mara and exploit the ocean. Napopo is one of their first victims, a strange creature that will seek Koa for help.

I believe there's a bug in the auto save feature that sometimes creates a new file that starts you from the beginning.As of December 18th 2021 the pc game still will lose progress (there was an update that rolled out in the summer that should have fixed this issue; however I have the newest version and the problem continues). My game has been lost twice, but after the first time I learned how to prevent the loss.  Here's a few steps below to continue playing the game you love below WITHOUT losing progress. Every few days the Save.JSON file will be replaced with a brand new save. Don't let that happen !Copy and paste your save files into a separate folder to backup files. DO NOT shortcut them.save files are found by looking up %Appdata% / LocalLow/ Chibig/ Summer in Mara/ SavesCopy and paste your saves folder EVERY TIME you stop playing! if the beginning sequence with Yaya and the ship begins and all progress is lost:Copy and paste your backed up saves back into the main save folder. Click REPLACE FILES. and there you go!!! Your saves will be restored to the last time you played!HAPPY PLAYING! Hopefully this bug can be fixed and my steps won't be necessary !

_childDocuments_.review: 19.4.2021.Summer in Mara is a game I really wanted to play. Ever since I saw that adorable looking cover and heard that it was a mix between Stardew Valley  and Wind Waker, I knew I had to play this… one day.The reason why I waited so long to play this game was because of all the reviews I watched about this game. It was criticized heavily for being shallow and having too many fetch-quests. I couldn’t see the problem. Believe it or not, I enjoy fetch-quests in games and I really enjoy the life simulator / farming simulator genera, so I was sure that I would be able to look past the game’s flaws. Well, I just finished this game and I even got all the achievements (I wanted to be sure that I’m really done with this game before I review it). You play the game as Koa, a young girl, about 12 who wants nothing more but to see the world and be kind and helpful to everyone. Koa was found by Yaya Haku, a half-fish half-human creature and was raised on a small island. Haku raised Koa as if she were her own grandmother. She taught Koa how to farm and how to take care of the island. However, she never let her leave the island. When Yaya Haku passed away, Koa was left on her own and after some things happened, she fixed Yaya Haku’s old ship and went on a journey to learn about the world she was in (Mara), about her grandmother’s past and to find her destiny. The world of Mara is filled with humans, fish-like-people, cat-like people and even humanoid aliens. They all live on the various islands of Mara and the world is kind of interesting. With that said, No matter where you go, no matter what you do, when people see Koa, they won’t even introduce themselves before they send the poor girl to fetch something. Nobody in this game has enough of heart to see a little girl and think: “Oh, maybe this girl is lost. Perhaps I should help her?”. Oh, no, when inhabitants of Mara see an underage girl, they think: “Great, free postal service”. Even when you think that you’ve finally met a decent character ( I thought the blacksmith was neat) after a while, they won’t feel bad for sending a 12-year-old across the world to fetch something random.That’s the thing: there really isn’t anything else except fetch-quests! Let me explain: In games like Stardew Valley and maybe My Time at Portia  you have your own plot of land. On that plot you can do things to progress, such as: growing crops and selling it, gathering items and crafting other items to make the game easier, socialize with NPCs, playing mini-games and so much more. You also try hard to do as much as you can every single in game day so you can make the next day easier for you. Summer in Mara has NONE OF THAT. In fact,  More examples: there’s no point in having days and nights because the only difference is that some shops don’t work during night, nothing else. The farming is extremely basic. So basic that you can finish everything from plowing the field, planting and watering the crops in less than one in-game hour (1 minute real time). Selling the crops and making money?  You really don’t need it for anything. There isn’t anything good to buy that can make the game easier or more enjoyable. The only time I needed money was when a fetch-quest demanded I have money. Upgrading tools? That’s also done though fetch quests. You just had to do them until you stumble upon one that will give you an upgrade and, apart from the hammer, no upgrades seem useful or necessary. Sailing “wind waker” style? You’ll do a lot of it actually. It’s pretty fun until you realize how much you’ll have to travel and for what stupid reasons too. Yup, you’ve guessed it, sailing is used so you can visit other islands to fetch things and bring them back.Again, it’s all about those fetch quests. You aren’t doing fetch quests so you can progress through the game: the game itself is a fetch quest.Sure, some quests are important. You will be tasked with delivering sensitive magical items and bringing them safely… a couple of times. The rest of the times you will do stupid crap like making tea and a croissant to butter up an NPC so she would listen to you. The game expects you to also craft the items before you fetch them and that ends up being a fetch-quest on its own. Pretty early in the game, an NPC will ask you to grow lettuces. Lettuces take 3-in-game days to grow (5 if you aren’t watering them) and you’ll literally have nothing to do but wait for those 3 days. Yes, I had to skip days to progress the story in the first 3 hours of a life-simulator game because, AGAIN, there isn’t anything to do in this game but fetch quests. Also, no, not the tea, nor the lettuces were important, they are simply filler until you get to the main plot which takes a long time of running back and forth. In fact, if you take away all the filler, this game would have been done in about 4-5 hours. Yes it is. Summer in Mara looks great for a kickstarter game. The game has a cartoony anime style and everything is presented in wonderful bright colors. The music is nice, when available and if it weren’t for all the running to retrieve items, the game would have been relaxing too. The game also runs really well despite being optimized for a controller and not having any graphical options. Well, a couple of things I, kind-of, liked the love letters. Kickstarter backers who pledged a bit more money, wrote love letters (or plain letters) that are hidden thru ought the game. When I found and read some of these, they made me feel all mushy inside. I also enjoyed how the game has a whole “save the nature” kind of vibe. My favorite thing about Summer in Mara is probably the main character herself: Koa. She is such a sweetheart of a character. She wants nothing more than to help people and doesn’t even realize how much everyone is misusing her good will. At one point, she was even asked to collect a debt for someone and she ended up paying it from her own pocket. She is pretty much a female version of Naruto, expect she isn’t a ninja, doesn’t fight but has a boat and can cook and plant produce. I really wanted to see Koa succeed in her mission despite being surrounded by such self-centered pricks of NPCs. There were also two fantastic, hand-drawn animated short movies (one at the beginning and one at the end of the film) but they do little to save this mess of a game.It’s such a shame. The game looks like it’s going to be a cute adventure but it ends up being an Amazon Prime courier simulator except you make most of your deliveries half the time. Don’t think that this game sucks because it has too many fetch quests.  If you want a good farming-sim, play Stardew Valley or My Time at Portia. Summer in Mara just isn’t much fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: You should definitely know what to expect when diving into this game, or else you might be disappointed. Summer in Mara isn’t really a deep farming sim, it’s a lot more about exploring and doing fetch quests. Yes, it does have the classic elements, like harvesting, cooking, scavenging and fishing, but on a very basic level, and most of the time you just need to craft certain new items to advance those quests. I guess probably it was designed with the idea in mind, that all the quests should give you a reason to cook or craft, but there are actually so many quests that you are busy full time with running around and doing errands. And most of the times you even already have the necessary item on you (either by finding it through exploration or random chances), so it often feels like the harvesting part just serves the story quests and is optional.That said, when you have accepted this prerequisite, the game can nevertheless be pretty cute and relaxing. You can definitely see that love went into the game, the drawings and characters are sweet, loads of dialogs (the story is told via some kind of visual novel style), the music is nice (though sound effects are a bit too few for my taste). All in all the game also is really family-friendly and might be aimed/appeal more to children, which is underlined by the strong environmental message the game generally spreads as well as the peaceful, teamwork-inspiring vibe.Anyway, even at my age I have to admit I had fun, a good casual game when you’re just braindead and need to chill out. There’s enough to do and explore (quite a large map of islands), no fights, no punishments, no real money problems. For a little criticism on the side, after doing all side quests and achievements, at the end I would have wished that the game was shorter and had maybe at least a quarter less quests. At some point I indeed felt kind of tired a bit with nothing to do any more (in the end I just used Fast Travel all the time and bought everything in the shops), and was glad when I finally finished it. Nevertheless, all things considered, even the small bugs here and there, the rugged tutorial or some translation weirdness all around, I do still recommend it, especially for people looking for another feel-good casual game to kill some time.

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is an addictive, family-friendly adventure with a handful of various elements to keep players entertained from start to finish. Personally, the absolute stand out feature is the sheer quantity of both side and main quests! This is not a short Indie game by any measure, with approximately 30hrs of content and plenty of means to casually farm, craft and sail around Mara, this title definitely has a lot to offer, however it is not without its shortcomings.+ Expansive world with many islands, characters and over 300+ quests.+ Gorgeous cinematics (only featured at the beginning and upon completion).+ Day/night cycle and random weather events.+ Maintain your own island! Plant and harvest crops, decorate the island with trees and feed your farm animals.+ Customisable character.+ Beautiful, vibrant colours with an equally uplifting soundtrack.+ Heart-warming story about growth, responsibility and friendship. - The quests are all fetch-related and some are more taxing than others, especially having to farm enormous amounts of coins in order to proceed.- Koa tires far too easily.- Various bugs including a glitch where the time freezes at 8:30am.- No fast travel, except to the main island and that costs coins.- Navigation is a tad confusing, it also does not display the pirate characters on the map, I always had to try and remember their locations.- Strange, unappealing NPC black speech bubbles. The protagonist, Koa is a young, determined and courageous girl who learned everything about life from her grandmother, Haku. Haku taught Koa how to live peacefully and sustainably, to respect the world of Mara, careful not to overuse resources and to always be grateful. With these teachings, Koa was prepared for life on her own and when the time came, she decided to explore other islands, meet other people and grow as a person. We meet a variety of different people along the adventure with troubled histories and unfavourable preconceptions. Every character in Mara is designed to reflect a life-lesson and our young protagonist soon discovers that everyone has their strengths and weaknesses, and not everyone from the same background is alike. This becomes especially apparent around halfway through the game when a wicked, greedy corporation called Elit try to take over and destroy the world of Mara, to over-farm the earth for its natural resources, indifferent to the chaos left in their wake.  Koa cherishes the land and ocean, believing that it is her destiny to halt this pollution and destruction and to restore harmony once more.Summer in Mara has an undeniable focus on farming, and it is perhaps one of the more fulfilling tasks throughout the game. Right from the beginning, players must prepare the land for crops, watering them once a day to accelerate their growth. Seeds are obtained either through exploration, quests or by purchasing from the various stalls and blueprints for better tools will become available to players as they progress. Each crop will display a number of days above it until its ready for harvesting, with random rain events also hastening the process. Once farm animals are acquired, players can not only pet them, but also feed them to gain eggs and milk, which is handy for selling or using in the many recipes that we can cook. Koa's home island is also a treasure-trove for supplies with the ability to both build and expand a mine for minerals, numerous trees to harvest fruit from, honey, wood and more. An interesting element is that all of the resources can be reused. For instance, if players chop down a tree, a seed may fall, allowing the tree to be replanted.Quests are the heart of the game and majority will involve crafting, farming or travelling to a location to fetch something and bring it back. With approximately 20+ characters to interact with, there are a bucket-load of side quests to choose from, but for some to be unlocked, progress with another character’s quest must be adhered to first. All quests are easily tracked through ctrl and supposedly able to find where to navigate to on the map, however more often than not, this was not the case and I had to try and remember where to go, as the location of the quest item itself was not marked, only the quest-giver was noted.With my 22 hours, I have completed the main story and copious side quests but am still yet to 100% it, this demonstrates just how enormous and time-constraining the quests are. Although I enjoyed majority of the gameplay, some main tasks involved a tremendous amount of grinding for 1000-3000 coins and the only way to get this was to just farm, travel and sell, repeatedly. This did make me lose my motivation a few times but luckily, there are only about 3-4 of these style tasks.All travel is accomplished using a boat, to traverse from one island to the next with a substantial amount of fuel. However, there is no fast travel and just involves sailing to either NESW on the navigational compass to pass through to the next area. Despite being able to dive, fish and collect some items along the way, a fast travel option would be much more beneficial.The beautiful art in the cutscenes at the beginning and end of the game is absolutely stunning, along with the interactions with characters. Yet, the extensive downgrade for the graphics of the main game took me by a bit of a surprise. The world is still vibrant, just not well-rounded and smooth as some of the other scenes appear. NPC's around the islands just display an odd, rather poor looking black speech bubble and all character models appear to be reused, all standing extremely still and many angles actually block the text from the speech bubble, making it impossible to read. The soundtrack is extremely uplifting with its strong instrumental cues and created a Peter Pan, fairy-tale atmosphere, making me feel like I was truly going on an adventure. Koa tires extremely easily and will often pass out when I am just trying to walk from A to B, resulting in her respawning closest to the nearest 'rest' area. Most rest areas on islands other than Koa's home island require coins and if she sleeps in the boat, the maximum energy gained is only half that. Sometimes when the protagonist would tire, the day would forever be stuck at 8:30am and the only method of rectifying this was to restart the game, which at least it does always auto-save and I never lost any progress.Travelling to other islands and trying to park my boat was equally frustrating and many times there is an invisible wall near the shore, forcing players to dock far away from the ground and having to swim over, tiring Koa further. Furthermore, players are unable to jump/climb when in water and I frequently found myself stuck, unable to clamber up a tiny wall and having to swim all the way around in order to find a slope to walk up.Summer in Mara is an enormous adventure title involving farming, crafting and exploring, all combined with its wholesome story. Although I do think it could benefit from perhaps being shorter or to add more depth to the quests, rather than relying on pure grind, it is undeniable that the developers have put in an extensive amount of effort to create a world with an abundance of different features that all casual players can enjoy for a considerable amount of time.This review copy was provided to the Devils in the Detail curator.

_childDocuments_.review: Allow me to preface this by saying that I did enjoy the game but is not without some precaution.The game starts off with Koa's adoptive grandmother showing her how to take care of the island by harvesting crops, planting trees, and paying respect to Mara. Koa is a very small child, probably between 4-5 years old judging from her appearance. Immediately afterwards there is a  animated cutscene hinting at things to come and showing off various characters she'll meet. The game proper follows a somewhat older Koa, possibly between 10-12 as she begins her  exploration of Mara and it's many little islands.The main story follows Koa's adventures and has her meeting (and helping) many different people. However, even before the story requires you to seek them out many can be encountered on their own and will have their own quest lines for you. The adventurous cat-child, Onzo, will support Koa an adventuring mentor. Bashful Brram works for his uncle along the beach bar in Qälis but the two don't always see eye to eye. There's also the fiery Akaji, a strong and beautiful blacksmith.Despite having many islands most of the game is nonetheless going to revolve around the  islands of Qälis and Koa's home island. This is because nearly every NPC lives on Qälis, and many quests (especially early ones) will require Koa to grow things on her farm. Brram's very first quest is to grow some corn because he was accidentally sent  instead. The pattern of going to Qälis and getting quests, heading back to Koa's island to harvest things, and then going  probably accounts for a solid third of the game. This is further caused by the simple fact that early on Koa's boat simply doesn't go very far, even after you finally get Saimi's map.This is Summer in Mara's biggest problem in a nutshell. To wit, most quests will involve being told to obtain X and/or Y then bring it back. The other common variation is to go from one end of Qälis to the other talking with different NPCs and coming back. Considering it's easily the largest island in the game you will at some point become a little tired of hiking from one end to the other and back again. I know I did. The best way to break that up is by just hoping in the boat and randomly going out to sea. Once you can explore other islands there will be little barrels and boxes drifting in the ocean you can ram into for random goodies. Everything from wood and coins to sleeping bags and ore. There's also plenty of mining spots, fruit laying around, and occasionally campsites to ransack for seeds or pots of food. The last one is especially important because Koa has an energy bar that drains with every action, including simply moving around. Different food restores different amounts of energy and hunger, represented by apples.To my knowledge there is  but Koa will pass out if her energy runs out; running out of stamina in the water puts Koa back on her boat. The premise of the game is supposed to be a relaxed adventure, so at worst you're simply inconvenienced from failing. You can fast travel to places for a small amount of coins depending on how far away you are, as well. A very welcome feature that was added after the game's release.On that note, it would appear that the developers have shifted their focus away from the game. Some of the Kickstarter stretch goals, such as photography and animal raising, have never been implemented.. although Koa can still obtain the camera from Mûn it serves no purpose. Perhaps more importantly, there are 91 Mail Crabs scattered throughout the ocean of Mara, but currently only 89 can be found. People know where the last two are, they're simply not there. Chibig has known about this for some 2 years now and never resolved it. Thankfully, there are no achievements related to it.Mara's other little issue is hanging threads. People will refer to or outright mention something, act as though it's important.. and then it never comes up again. Such as Ereta's father or the ship Dunna blew up. The game's climax moves very quickly after a previously glacial pace. There's a cool animated cutscene and then... nothing. Nobody comments on what happened, there's no changes to your island, no real impact from what happens. Perhaps the worst offender is that a plot relevant NPC can  be found on various islands saying the same thing despite plot related reasons they should no longer be here., there are four things that can only be done after beating the game. Rigatta & Saimi both offer a simple quest, and you can finish Edegan & Napopo's quest lines. Yet they are still unrelated to the game's overall story. In fact, quite a few people have speculated Napopo's quest line was supposed to have more.Long story short, I enjoyed Summer in Mara and if you can get it on sale and don't mind a very relaxed game then by all means go ahead and pick it up. It's got some rough spots and could use more polish, but for what is there it's certainly not a  little game. You may enjoy fiddling with Koa's island, as I did, or perhaps you'll want to catch all the kinds of fish. Just.. don't go in expecting a bigger, grander game than the store page might lead on.

_childDocuments_.review: They got a lot of stuff right.  No inventory management (hate having to decide whether to keep something or get rid of it for something new).  The graphics are great.  It's up there with My Time at Portia, maybe better.  There's no damage or fighting involved which I appreciate in the more casual game type.  If I want to kill something, I'll play 7 days to die.The two things that I really disliked were the fact you spend 65-70% of your time traveling.  Run here, run there, run back again.  Same with the boat.  One end of the map, back and back again.  All games have filler but this is beyond that.  The other issue is the dialogue.  You will spend another 10% of your time going through loooong conversations.  After a very short time,  I was just click, click, click...ad nauseum just to get past the dialogue.One final thing of note for those of you that like to build stuff.  The description on the sale page mention being able to "create new tools and buildings."  You cannot design any of the buildings.  When you get the blueprint, there is a designated space and when you have the right mat's you just click and it's done.  would have liked more variety in how my home area looked.   I would recommend this game as a way to pass the time but feel there were several very important missed opportunities.  And WAY TOO MUCH filler.This game would be good for a kid (little kid).  Especially one learning how to read ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I kickstarted this game because it looked like a great casual game in the vein of Stardew Valley and My Time at Portia, and on the surface, I wasn't disappointed.  It's got charm, an awesome soundtrack and, despite the simplified gameplay and a few localization issues, it was entertaining throughout.   Why the "no" vote?  Because the game feels unpolished.  Not unfinished - there's definitely an ending - but there are several loose ends, lost threads in the side-stories and outstanding bugs that the developers have not fixed, and are not likely to, as they have moved on to developing other games.*  Is the game playable?  Yes.  It's even enjoyable, but I would caution against paying full price for abandonware that still has major bugs. Actual playtime: under 20 hours.  Playtime to achieve all achievements: Impossible at this time due to achievement-breaking bugs.**C+  Would not purchase from Chibig again.*Although a patch was just released for this game on 11/19/2020, the patch did not actually fix any bugs, just deleted the broken achievements, so my assessment remains the same.** Correction, about 20 hours, because the two achievements that were broken have been deleted instead of being fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that I had been following this game for some time and was very excited to see this game in action. In the beginning it was very charming and aesthetically pleasing. The animated cutscenes are cute and draw you in to the world that is Mara. However, with that said, I am extremely disappointed with this game for a number of reasons which I will details below: 1. The game does not show you the basics. While I appreciate games that don't hold your hand during gameplay, I do not appreciate the basics being explained. It doesn't even show you how to open the menu. You discover that yourself by button mashing. On top of that, at the beginning my objective would not disappear off the screen until I completed it. This later sorted itself out. 2. The game is a massive fetch quest. You will spend so much time backtracking. Going back and fourth between the first island you unlock and your home island. This becomes so annoying and repetitive and doesn't let up almost 5 hours into gameplay. 3. Devs have been lazing with lighting, NPC design and general layout design. NPC's stand perfectly still, the assets are very clearly reused with maybe a colour change. For example there were two NPCs that were pink holding a camera, building are basically the same design just with different colour, towns have little to no texture and Speech bubbles are static (if you turn the camera so they are looking side on at an NPC while they speak the speech bubble does not move, it will almost disappear like its on a flat plain, instead of following the camera around. In relation to lighting, the character appears to have some sort of luminescent lighting around her. As well as lighting from light sources. There's a weird white light that attaches itself to the main character like YOU as the player are the light. In addition to when you go into the first town you will notice that NONE of the lampposts have shadows. However the seagulls that just loop around and sit on the same lamppost will have a clearly defined shadow, so much so that it looks like the seagull model was just reused for the shadow without any shape distortion. Another gripe with shadowing is the water. If the boat stands still on the water, there is no movement, it's like the boat is stuck in Jelly, and when you dock the boat the water looses all shadow and light and suddenly become a flat surface. 4. When i parked my boat and tried to jump on top of another boat i found myself floating on top of the asset, like quite a bit above it. And the sea "effects" were coming through the boat too. 5. How does a pumpkin take 10 days to mature, but a tree takes 2. 6. The wells do not fill up with water unless it rains. In 5 hours of gameplay my game rained once, in addition to the wells there are mushrooms that only seem to appear when it rains....again it rained once....Don't get me wrong, I'm a fan of simplistic design and stuff outside the box. But the game tried to be too many things, when all it actually is, is a glorified fetch quest. I struggled to really sink into the story of the game and found myself just thinking oh here we go again....another fetch quest. Overall i'm extremely disappointed with this game. I will be asking for a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Like someone said in another review. I don't think this is a bad game but if I have to recommend it, I won't. The game is quite enjoyable in the beginning, I love the visuals, the soundtrack is also good, and it starts as a nice relaxing farming game. Soon you will be able to start to explore the sea. You find new places and it seems quite exciting until you start to realise the more you play that exploring doesn't really reward you in a satisfying manner, most places you discover don't add anything new to the game, almost all the quests are fetch quests which there are so many and it will start to get boring and annoying to go from one part of the map to other just to talk to someone. You don't really get some sort of technological advance in your farming skill, you just get some new products and recipes but they are mostly useless or just for decoration. Some of the stuff you plant like some trees don't even have hitboxes, you have a limit of 100 trees that you can plant, the animals will get in your way most of the time and you end up wasting resources on them by mistake cause you want to click something else. I have completed this game 100%, like I said it's good at the start but it just starts to get annoying mid game to the end. Also some stuff isn't really explained and you are left sometimes clueless on what to do in some quests, those were rare occasions but I kinda got stuck on those parts.

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is a farming sim. The player controls Koa, who oversees her home island after her grandmother's passing and learns how to travel the sea with the help of Mara natives.Think of Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker, without combat and dungeons.==Pros==+ Beautiful graphics+ Many islands to explore+ Loads of items to craft+ 20+ characters to interact with and do quests for+ Very casual, no combat or overly difficult moments+ Tons of items to collect+ Fast travel+ Can continue to play after completing all of Koa's quests.==Cons==- The worst thing about this game is the huge amount of running back and forth on Qalis, it's a chore within itself.- Some grindy moments (coins, recipes, etc.)- Tutorial is pretty lackluster- Inability to change default keybinds- Occasional grinding (nothing too intense though)- Spelling/grammar mistakes- Qalis has a bunch of weird invisible walls when trying to jump over certain areas.- I haven't seen many, personally, but there are several known bugs, errors, and glitches.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to open up this review by saying my opinion on Summer in Mara are... mixed at best. Here are some things you should know going into the game. 1. Farming only... sort of matters. It is important insofar as it services the main thing you will be doing 90% of the time-2. FETCH QUESTS BAY-BEE!!!This game is mostly fetch-quest. You go a place, you talk to a person, you get the thing they need. Maybe you grow it, or do another fetch quest for it, or you find it, but that's what happens. Do not buy this game if you're looking for a farming sim to fill the void of your stardew valleys or your story of seasons. Why should you buy this game? It's cute, dude. Mechanically it's not much to write home about, but the mechanics wasn't what I was playing for. I WAS playing for the characters you meet. While they all remain rather simple, they all seem to have their own charm that definitely worked on me. The designs were beautiful and most of their dialog with Koa is charming on one end or the other. There are some stand-outs but there wasn't really any that I actively disliked or didn't want to have to deal with. It's got a very "rual town while a sci fi plot goes down just outside of the boarder" vibe to that and I found that charming. I would treat it more like a visual novel with some gameplay mechanics rather than a farming sim. My tips if you want to get through it without getting too frustrated, unlock as much of the map as you possibly can. The quicktravel feature is your friend. Also you can sell to all of the vendors if you click the mouse icon in the middle of the screen. They all have favorite items that they'll give you more money for, so it's easier to load up on money early game if you keep this in mind. Growing lots of fruit trees on your island also helps a lot. And don't be ashamed to use a guide, some things aren't explained. I wish they had ironed out some of the kinks, I feel this would have been a better game, but it's a nice way to kill some time if you want a relaxed game with a charming cast.

_childDocuments_.review: I overestimated this game and was disappointed. It's boring, sick and totally restrictive. After more than 1 hour of play, the quests ALWAYS ask for the same thing: Go to the place, pick up such items, craft or arrange it and repeat it endlessly. I expected a more Harvest Moon style game, Stradew Valley but nothing to do. I don't recommend it at all. If you expect a game to be able to plant, harvest, sell, build and expand your farm this game does not bring any of that. There are not even seasons. Honestly, what a pity.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited: Wrote this review saying the tutorial is lackluster, really, really lackluster to the point you have to guess which button to open quest journal and inventory but I still recommend this game. After reaching the first town, now I can truly say:Think twice before you buy this game. Watch gameplay videos on Youtube first before buying.This game is an example where presentation speaks louder than application. If you thought this game is like Harvest Moon or Stories of Season, you're not wrong. It has farming, raising animals, cooking, exploration etc. Just like your typical Harvest Moon-esque game.However, I'm gonna talk about their world building, specifilcally about how they handle their NPCs. It's like the devs thought they're not too important so they spend less time there. When I first arrive in the first town, I found most if not every NPCs don't move. It's like they're freaking statues. You can approach them to talk or trade but that's it, they don't move. I sleep it off for day, thinking maybe they're gonna move in the morning, considering it was evening when I arrived in the town but nope, no movement at all, everyone stays the same. Should have realize that during tutorial, the evidence's there.What makes me love Stardew Valley or Stories of Season is aside from taking care your farm, you can interact with the villagers. They also have their own schedules, walking around the village making the world's alive. The same thing can't be said for this game. I don't feel that excitement when I walk around the town.And exploration. I was thinking the whole world will be open, you can get in your boat and head to another island in real time, like AC: Blackflag minus the cannon and enemies who try to kill you. Turns out, the world is divided into a section or zone and to move to another zone, you just head towards the edge of the map, be it West, North, South or East and you'll be teleported next zone. So no.. no open world navigation.Such a shame though, I was enamored by the presentation and turns out, this is a huge disappointment for me. Will apply for refund. Lucky I didn't buy this on my Nintendo Switch.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to recommend this game but at its current state I simply cannot. I was really pumped for this game, and was expecting great things but my overall experience has not been great.- It's all back and forth for quests. You can only craft and do stuff in your house so get ready to travel back and forth between home island and the main city a bajillion times- In the tutorial they show you basic controls and the fact that there are quests. They don't teach you about the menus or nothing. In some aspects its nice that they don't take you by the hand but finding where my quest log was was in itself an adventure. - The diving minigames are just awful. The controls are weird, you can barely move. It's one of the worse minigames I have ever played in a game, I wish I was exaggerating- The amount of invisible walls, hitboxes where there shouldn't be none and getting stuck everytime you try to jump over something makes the movement very clumsy- The main city design is very poor, some parts are great and look amazing, but some others areas are just made to fill up space, with nothing good to look at. It feels like lazy design- Some doors have signs to say that the house is closed. Some others have the sign but they don't tell you why the sign is there- I get that the premise of the game is that you need to help others and they will help you in return. But I feel like here this concept has been streched too much. Let me explain: the protagonist is a young girl with a big character and not afraid to flip old ladies off. However, there's a quest where an NPC asks you to retreive some money from some other NPC that's owes it. When you go get the money, the NPC doesn't give you the money and tells you need to pay it. And the protagonist says yeah no probem imma do that thank you good sir. It just doesn't match with how the protagonist is being portrayed. They brag about the amount of quests in this game, but make absolutely no sense- The villagers you can interact with are great, everyone with its personality and quircks. However, the other NPCs are like statues, they barely move and have the same interaction over and over again. It doesn't feel like a thriving city. There's a guy on the beach that is having the longest party of its life and it's not looking like it's going to end any time soon- There's a way of getting back to the main island directly. I get that it's in case you get stranded, but the payement system should be worked on more I feel like- A well that only fills up with rain water is not a well, it's a bucket. And if decides to never rain, good luck finding mushroomsAnd I'm sure there's stuff I'm forgetting like the recycling bit of the game, but I feel like this is already some good reasons why you should not buy it at its current state. I really hope they make some changes.Cheers!
