_childDocuments_.review: A ship explosion occurs and a human baby is the only survivor. She is named Koa and raised by the old woman who found her. Sadly, Koa’s adopted grandmother dies before Koa is an adult. Despite Koa’s age, she learns to grow up fast, because she  – not just for her own survival, but Mara’s.      • Time progresses constantly unless a menu is open or dialogue is being read.     • Exploration consists of using a boat to travel around Mara, then docking adjacent to piers or land to explore islands. Koa’s map expands as more people tell her about locations.     • Gathering resources is simple. Hit trees/bushes to obtain fruit. Hit mining spots to obtain ore. Better tools grant access to better ore.     • : There are a total of 16 farming spaces that progressively get unlocked as Koa improves her tools. Each crop has a set amount of days it takes to grow. Fertilizer speeds crop growth and output. The crops  die if you fail to water them; they just take longer to grow.     • : There are only 3 animals that produce items. Chickens give eggs. Pigs give truffles. Sheep give milk. Each animal type has a designated area/structure on the home island that must be build by Koa before those animals can be housed there. Failing to feed the animals  make them sick or kill them. They just don’t produce their usual items.     • : Most recipes are unlocked from quests, but sometimes Koa will randomly get one. Cooking can be done on the home island or when borrowing NPC’s kitchens. The significant difference is that the player can cook a lot more at once at the home island, while only one item at a time can be produced at an NPC’s location. Cooking is instantaneous.     • : The same rules apply here that applied for cooking. Instead of kitchens, they’re worktables. Decorative items can only be placed on the home island.     • : There are fishing locations all over Mara. Some fishing spots are in the open sea, while others are off the shores of islands. To catch the fish, the player has to move a bar back and forth and attempt to keep it aligned with the fish icon. It’s fairly easy and straightforward. Each fish requires a particular bait. There are a total of 25 types of fish in the game.    • The diving mini-game is easy. Touch air bubbles to increased the time allowed under water. Touch treasure chests to obtain items. Touch the rescue inner tube to return to the surface. If Koa runs out of air, nothing bad happens. She just returns to the surface automatically, but you’ll miss any treasure that you didn’t reach.    • It was fun to play despite its flaws.     • Cute character portraits. Colorful, interesting environments. Lovely cutscenes.     • Simple, but cute story. (Seemed slightly inspired by Disney’s , tbh.)    • Encourages environmentalism.     • All the animals are cute. Yes, even those pesky chickens (See complaints). Furthermore, feeding wild animals lures them to the home island. By the end of the game, I had: a dog, a duck, some squirrels, some seals, and a few mice on my island. None of those animals produce anything, but they’re nice to have around.    • Koa’s appearance can be changed by outfit and backpack. There are several of both. The portrait also demonstrates the outfit change, not just the sprite.      • Free sh*t!!! As the player explores Mara, there are many free items floating around in the sea that can be collected by running the boat through them.     • Chickens get in the way of farming. I’d try to plant or harvest crops, but suddenly there’d be chickens in my way and I’d end up feeding/petting them instead.     • No way to sell animals. At first, I was rescuing every animal I came across, but soon my farm was overrun by chickens.     • No way to check full inventory.    • The game doesn’t inform the player of treasure maps already purchased.    • When selling/buying items, there isn’t a way to change the number of items. For example, if the player wants to sell 99 of one item, they have to hit the X (or A) button 99 times.     • Lacks character development.  (that I personally encountered)    • When fast traveling to the home island, if you’re carrying a rescued animal, the game glitches out and won’t allow the player to close the notification about the animal living on the island. The player must restart the game.    • Sometimes, seemingly at random, the quest page won’t allow the player to scroll, keeping them from seeing relevant quests.    • When crafting at a NPC’s worktable, sometimes items will appear as though they can be made even though the player lacks the necessary ingredients.     • Sometimes, money gained or lost isn’t displayed in the upper, right corner like it’s supposed to.    • Sometimes fast travel isn’t available, even if a story event isn’t going on. I’m not sure what the cause is, but if it was  unavailable at times, the player should be informed, at least.     • Sometimes, when approaching pirate ships, the options for talking and commerce won’t appear easily and it can take several tries to get it to work.     • Koa can get locked inside Akaji’s workshop gate when it closes.    • Koa’s sprite can walk through some objects, mostly trees.    • Fink can still be found on Islumber Woods Island after the Elits are defeated. I recommend this game to fans of the genre. It was really fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most "good-bad" game I've ever played. The stuff it does well is fantastic, the stuff it does poorly is absolutely awful. It feels like the untested alpha version of a great game, and it honestly should've been released in early access or pushed back a few months. But even though it's not a well-implemented game, I still think it's worth playing if you like this kind of game (farming sim adventure).First, the good- the artwork, music, and story. The game looks amazing despite some awkward animation and the music is catchy and fits the game perfectly. The environments are well-designed and the first time you leave your home and see the main island is actually a breathtaking moment. The characters are charming, even the ones who seem annoying at first, and the story is interesting with some mystery to it.Now, for the bad- the gameplay and lack of polish. This game is partially a farming sim where you need to grow crops for the hundreds of quests where people need cabbage or something. The crops take a few in-game days to grow, but that doesn't matter at all because you can just keep going to sleep immediately until the crops grow. Other farming games prevent this by having your crops die if you don't water them or having events that you would miss if you just keep sleeping. This game has neither, so the farming aspect has no point.Another huge aspect of this game is crafting. Unfortunately, you can only craft on your home island, so every time someone gives you a quest you have to travel back to your island, make the item, travel back to the person, and then they give you another quest that you have to craft for. It would be nice to have some places where you can craft on other islands. Even just making it so you can craft on your boat would improve it a lot.Finally, the game is just not polished. I've run into numerous bugs- just in the tutorial alone, I hit two bugs where you had to restart your game. I've had the game refuse to load, hud elements getting stuck on the screen forever, randomly teleporting back to my boat when I try to pick fruit, quests updating when they're not supposed to, quests not updating when they're supposed to, and more. Hopefully most of these bugs will be fixed now that the game is out.Anyway, despite all these gameplay problems, the game manages to be super addictive and I can't stop playing it. Even though the gameplay can be tedious, I'm always like "just one more quest!" and keep playing anyway. So in the end, I do recommend it and I hope they work on it more because this game has real potential! It's just not all the way there yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Other reviews say that this game is empty and has only fetch quests. And what can I say? They are right. Summer in Mara is no game for people who like to be busy. I play it to relax. And relaxing it is for sure. No way to die, crafting goes by the way and the rest of the game is enjoying the beautiful islands. When I need to heal my soul, I stroll through this game and feel like I'm on Summer vacation in Mara.

_childDocuments_.review: Little disclaimer: I am not going to change my review, because I had a good time with it, but as a backer I am greatly dissatisfied with the state the game was left in. Three stretch goals were never implemented and there is no further will for it. Also the game alone still require some additional polishing.  could have been even better game...Little Koa is growing up on a small island in the middle of Mara. She is alone now, tending to her island but dreaming about exploring the whole world and becoming a pirate one day! When she finds a strange little creature on the beach her days of loneliness are over. With her new friend, Napopo, she set sails to the vast Mara seas. Koa will then meet different kinds of people with their own dreams, problems or old pains and although she is only a kid, she will do everything in her power to help them. is a farming simulator game where you have your own island to take care of. As you progress in the story you will be able to build various structures on it - for example decorations or animal enclosures; cultivate many kinds of vegetables and fruits or plant new species of trees or shrubs. There is a lot you can do in Mara - you can harvest crops, create new items for sale or for manufacturing, go fishing or diving, pick up trash, cook various dishes or you can pat animals. :) I have very much enjoyed developing my island, it's nice to see it grow (not in terms of size).Exploration is another important part of the game, you can find a lot of new things on your travels (people really throw interesting stuff to the ocean). Also it's a great boost to your income as you can harvest wild crops and then sell it for profit without additional spend.Story is simple but really nice. It's about growing up, going after your own dreams and trying to be a good person, doing the right things and helping others around you too. Most of the characters are nicely written, although there could have been more varied interaction with them (especially after completing their quests). Quests are of “fetching type” when you do deliveries for them or they send you somewhere. I don’t really mind, as the idea of the game is about Koa helping others… and I usually pick quests and do something different and after I feel like it I deliver it, but I can understand why some of the players are bored by it. Not me though.I like the graphics, so colorful and cheerful (with a few exceptions) even though there are some shortcomings (rainy day without a rain or so). Soundtrack is very good, characters have their own themes and I visited some of them regularly just to listen to it (like Aquila, Edogan, Fink). I have also liked changing outfits of little Koa, would love to have some of the backpacks! :)I have truly enjoyed my time in Mara. Yeah, it has some rough edges and you can stump on some bugs (not working achievements were deleted some time ago). Ending was rather rushed and the main villain didn't get proper space, you know the anticipation for meeting up with him is building up and then it's over… truth is I was a little disappointed. City life doesn't change with day cycles (except for important characters), there are still the same people, they stand in the same spots, only animals are moving around… this could have been done in a better way. Also not all of the kickstarter stretch goals were added yet (taking photos, windsurfing, animal breeding…). After getting all you can for your island, completing your fetch quests, there is nothing to do… of course you can still tend to your island, it's very relaxing, but you were already doing it for some time… I think that there is a great potential to still develop the game, add new crops, new animals for your island, new buildings and so on. If not officially then through the mods. For now it seems like the developers are concentrating on different goals in their career, but well, who knows. I still very much recommend this game, it was a very pleasant experience.Oh, and as you will explore the Mara you can find little crabs with messages from the backers. They are filled with love, hope, happiness… that also add a nice feeling to the game.Edit: Added pictures and disclaimer.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say I completed this game in 23 hours including main and side missions and gained 46 of the 53 achievements. I have one side mission that I believe is bugged and I cannot complete it (I think I may have needed to complete this before the main quest line but have contacted the devs to inform and seems to be a common issue on forums). In a summary this is not purely a farm sim and it isn't purely adventure. It's a mix in between for those who want to chill out, shut off from the real world and sail around the seas pleasing as many people as you can in a bright and beautifully designed world.  I followed the progress of this game and awaited its release and after playing I would say it is different than what I expected. I wasn't disappointed but it perhaps came across more farming sim than it did quest adventure. This game is VERY heavily fetch quest based and farming only helps you fulfil these quests unlike Stardew which is more farming and you can fulfil a quest if you choose. The actual farming aspect is, what I would say compared to Stardew or even a Harvest moon, limited. To make a comparison to Stardew is unfair as this game is it's own style but I'm just trying give insight to those who are looking for a Stardew alternative, I don't think this is it; however still a lovely game.The story line reminded me of Jax and Daxter, saving your home and island from a dark powerful force. Even the Elits structures art style looked like precursor technology in J&D. I do feel like the first "cut scene" after the tutorial left me feeling lost and it wasn't until I explored the island I realised what had to happened; the cut scene felt a little cut off emotionally. Like most games it takes a couple of in game days to get going on the main adventure. There are some brilliant parts of this game but there are also some pain staking parts as well as a few bugs still lurking. If you like Wind waker it definitely has the similar style with exploration, sailing around, without weapons or enemies. One major thing I love is how customisable your island is. You can walk anywhere, jump down anywhere and place objects anywhere you want. You can fully make your island its own when you unlock all the items and explore finding unique crops. That makes it quite nice and personal. A unique aspect I don't believe I've seen any other game have. Character designs are really nice, some of the interactions are good. Although some characters are just rude and childish to the point where it is annoying. I can't even count on one hand the amount of time "adults" would tell me to go away and leave. I feel like the majority of the quests in this game, with British slang, you're getting absolutely mugged off. A lot of quests there is no reward, you can spend ages growing crops, exploring for loot and crafting an item for basically nothing. This happens A LOT. Your character is too nice and helps too many people and gains nothing 80% of the time. If you like doing a game for self satisfaction this is it. For example, the absolute worst mission is a quest in which you need to get some ink. To get this ink the banker wants you to collect his debt, to collect this debt you have to use YOUR OWN MONEY to pay off the three ladies' debt. The lady even says to you that you can make the money from buying and selling in her shop. WHAT. So you buy from her, to grow crops, sell those crops to her to then pay her debt. *Facepalm* I've seen a couple of minor criticisms that I wanted to address, someone mentioned that when you harvest your crops you don't get a seed to replace. You don't in Stardew either, you have to buy the seeds again. Nor Harvest moon games. I think it's unfair to knock the farming mechanics for this reason. Secondly customisation, some games you can't customise at all so I think that this games small amount of backpacks and clothing is sweet and simple. I don't think customising your character should be an aspect of this game when it is story based driven. This game has a fast travel option but it is costly and travelling around the map when you open up the full area becomes extremely time consuming. Especially with the guests that get you to travel from point A to point B which is four areas away. Then travel back to A to have to travel back B again etc.. Fast travel should either be free or cheaper as by 3/4 of the game you really start to get fed up travelling the same routes over and over. I think I enjoyed the calm essence and wholesomeness of this game. I pretty much binged this game so although it has some negatives, I completed it. It needs some polishing but as it's this developers first major exploration release it's a great start. Their future games can only go upwards and that is quite exciting. It may seem like I've pointed out quite big negatives but these are what make the game what it is and some people have different expectations. I don't think this game can be continued after completion as theirs no reason too do anything but while you are playing just take it slow and enjoy owning a farm and designing your island.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: It's not ready.I am so disappointed. This game has great bones as far as graphics design and mechanics but it's lacking in it's quest design and progression mechanics. There's nothing to do outside of fetch quests that feel meaningless after they are completed. Nothing you do early on has a real impact on the game world or even your own farm. Grow 2 items for a fetch quest. Sleep for 5 days to grow them. Harvest the two items once and deliver them. Pickup a new quest from the person you dropped them off to and repeat. It needs a lot more work and development. Likely a year. I'll keep checking back to see if things improve.It seems all the good stuff is in the first 30 minutes of demo play to sell you on the game. Then everything starts to fall apart as the game shows it's lack of depth the moment you start exploring the second island.

_childDocuments_.review: Summer of Mara is a fun, feel-good exploration and farm game!Overall Review:I purchased the game after playing the free prologue. As a fan of both Zelda: The Wind Waker and Harvest moon, Summer of Mara has a great in-between balance. This is a fun single player RPG game which gives you the exploration of Wind Waker and the fun of farming with more customize content, as the whole island is yours to design! I would recommend this game to people who love stress free farming  and exploration open world games. The game has a great story, music and overall game play.What I Like:* MUSIC:The music reminds me of final fantasy, as it has a adventurous themed music. The tone of the music changes based on interactions with people or objects. This is of personal preference opinion. The music was a great background to exploration.*GAME PLAY & CUSTOMIZATION:   - The farming is somewhat quest based, but there is a selection of crops of what you can grow in the game once you unlock the city. Some crops may be more expensive, but there is a wide variety to grow from the start.  - The Summer of Mara also gives more customization to the island itself; Placement of buildings and structures allow you to design the island the way you want.   - Non-plotted Bushes and trees are interchangeable on your island. The number of trees/bushes can be increased with upgrades, but you can plant and change the trees on the island with seeds. This is a great customization perk for your island. *FISHINGSummer of Marla gives fishing a more of a challenge than other games. First, you have to hook the fish. Second, you reel the fish with a slider-based technique: You have to slide the hook right or left (using keyboard) to keep slider hook on the moving fish. There are two "health" bars: One for the fish, which will decrease in time as the slider hook stays on the fish  and  a bar for  the string, which will decrease for the time the slider is not on the fish. The string will break if the bar is depleted,  but the game will keep going if you have another string in the inventory.As a person who plays a lot of RPG with a mini-fishing games, I like this mini fishing game as it has more of a challenge.Fishing is also based on type of bait. The bait must be found in exploration. I love this, as most game do not include bait as part of exploration.*STORY  - The story is a little sad, but I love the the positive views/comments in the game. Very encouraging.   - The game chat really captures a child's mind, with the constant random interruptions and the reactions of Koa, the main character.   - The general basis of the game is nothing is free. This is a important aspect/theme of the game, which is how most of the quest or story progress. Since the main character is a child, this is a very interesting concept.   - Overall, the story is very interesting and I love the story progression so far.   - The story and farming is not based on dates for events and season, but just time. This gives more freedom for farming and only limits you on when visiting people/stores. This makes this a great relaxing stress-free game.*Exploration:   - The tasks and interactions for exploration is endless. There is treasure hunting, mining, fishing, digging, and quest progression and supply hunting.    - Exploration for supplies can include: looking for seeds/plants, baits, seashells, quests and for things you can sell, and rescuing animals, and mining for minerals.  - Exploration is not limited to land, as there are boxes on the sea, and rescuing animals in the sea. This makes sailing not as boring!  - One unlock area opens a lot of exploration opportunities. What I disliked:* CONTROLS  - As many people said before, the controls are not cleared. I do not see this as a big Con, as the controls are accessible on the main menu. The only CON is the controls for the ship are not listed, and it took a while to understand the ship controls.  - There was no instructions on how to sell when quest was given. I could not figure out hoe to sell and had to look it up. I think the button to switch from buy and sell should be labeled. * ANIMALS:  - The game does not have a balance for rescued animal probability. As mention in other reviews, I find more chickens than anything else. I would be more encourage if the game had a more balance to finding pigs and sheep.  - Animal wrangling: So a lot of people talk about the fact that chickens are over running the crops and get in the way of farming. I am having this issue too. Although you have the option of fences and fence gates in the game, it would be great to have a way to call all the chickens together or move them.*QUEST  - There have been a few times I have no idea what to do for a quest and ended up googling. Some of the quest details do not give the player a clue what to do. A little frustrating when a required quest needs to be completed to unlock more quest. I have been stuck at least 2-3 times.* BUGS :- NPC Quest bug: Like other players, I ran into the bug with NPC. A simple restart of the game fixed it though. This review is after 20 hour game play; may update with more game progression

_childDocuments_.review: As nice looking and chill as it is, it's work as if it's barely finished. There is virtually no settings and you need to go into system files to do ANYTHING, even change it from full-screen. No key-rebinds, no graphic settings beside 1 'quality' who-know-what-it-means slider.DELETING SAVE FILE wasn't even included just a year back and you had to manually delete files (they added 'reset save files' but how the hell do you make a game that you cannot restart?!).There is no cloud sync and trying to add pevious save-files can just now work at all - and if you think that's as bad as it gets, game can just randomly overwrite your file and start you at the beginning! Enjoy messing with system files if you wanna prevent it.A pretty game not worth having to deal with absolutely abysmal technical support.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game on Indiegogo back in 2019. Was really looking forward to it, but decided to hold off for a while to wait for it to develop. Finally played it over a year after it officially released and I was pretty disappointed.It feels very similar to My Time at Portia and similar farming games, but it doesn't really do much well.My biggest problem is that there's WAY too many fetch quests. Running back and forth between characters endlessly. "Bring this item to a character on one side of the island. Okay now bring this item back to the original character." And it starts to get annoying when you have to sail back and forth between your home island and other item, just to grow a potato for a character. Even growing and selling resources is a tedious cycle of sailing between islands.I felt the sleeping/day cycle mechanics were not well designed. There were times where I would intentionally pass out because paying for the hotel was 40 Coins. At times, there isn't enough to do in the day, so I sometimes feel compelled to just wake up, water your crops, and then go back to sleep at 10AM to further their growth.Some of the things you do often -- crafting, gathering resources, chopping trees, are also kind of annoying. For example, chop a tree, then individually pick up each log, and wait for each animation to complete after you pick up a log.I ran into quite a few glitches where the character would clip on areas, get stuck in an area, or not be able to easily access my boat.I do appreciate the sea travel mechanic. I think that part sets it apart from similar games, but I actually found the sea travel to be rather tedious. There were too many times where I was just holding "W" and multi-tasking while sailing. One of the biggest issues is that it feels like there isn't enough purpose to building on your own island. You don't really feel a huge need or why you're progressing other than to unlock other things to sell.The game and story feels a little geared towards kids / younger players, which normally wouldn't be a huge deal when you have games like Animal Crossing / Harvest Moon that are a lot of fun for both kids and adults, but this game starts to feel like you're playing a kids game. Especially some of the mechanics (for example, the diving mechanic) feels like a simple kids game.The graphics are okay, but they definitely aren't adding anything to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start off by saying  and yes, I can understand why people feel it is somewhat boring, since you're literally just running errands for people. It's lacking in making you feel rewarded by completing quests as the next one will just be .  Most of the items you need, you can actually get just by exploring or buying them if you enjoy the grind for money. The fast traveling feature seems super expensive at first until you realize that if you don't have any money, it will be free. Getting money in this game is somewhat hard. Especially if you're like me and like buying stuff instead of farming for it but it makes the game fair and keeps you from just buying everything, even at the end. The story was okay, I felt it was lacking a bit. Especially towards the end.The character development by the NPCs was quite nice to see in regards to the Player, although I wish there were more casual dialogue options in general. There were very few bugs I encountered, it was three and two happened because of the mine. Overall it was bit of a mindless game, more so if you don't pay too much attention to the story. There is no challenge if you prepare for the achievements early on (catching fish, collecting oranges; I didn't and it still ended up only costing me less than an hour after turning my island into an orange farm and fast traveling through the squares to catch fish I had missed), everything else you will unlock by simply going through quests.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I struggled whether to recommend or not because I wanted to like the game, as a Stardew Valley fan. I like the story and the vibe, but the mechanics make it so painful.Time taken to complete (plus a short bit for all achievements): 33 hours.Story: cute, heartwarming, has an overall save nature theme.Music: not amazing, but not bad. A particular piece reminds me of the menu music for Life is Strange, generally nothing too exciting but upbeat and suitable for the game.Gameplay: the early game is a huge fetch quest. Fast travel is a thing, but costs money which you can't spare till mid-game. This means that if you don't want to be broke all the time, you have to spend forever sailing to and fro your tiny island and the main shopping island. Sail to big island, get asked for item, sail back, get item, sail to big island, get asked for another item, rinse and repeat. Short of checking a quest guide to prepare everything at once, you're going to spend half the time sailing back forth, and the sailing is the driest thing ever, contrary to its environment.Late game, when you build up your farm enough to be able to throw money wherever you like, the fetch quest becomes a frenzy of teleporting to and fro islands. I stuck with it only because I'm a completionist, after 2 months of letting this fetch quest nightmare rot on a shelf. Yes, the early game was so bad I dropped it for a while.Overall: lovely story, great vibes, terrible game progression. It is a fetch quest, you have been warned.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: First half hour of the game gives a feeling of wonder and excitement in what could possibly happen in this game. After leaving the home island and arriving to the first town to get treated with constant fetch quests while treating the player (and character) as a nuisance and finding ways to ruin the experience for them; constantly running back and forth from home island to town for a single crop or item that can only be crafted or harvested at the home. The exploration is pretty minimal once unlocked, alongside the diving mini-game that lets you get additional loot.Game has promise but at the current state, I cannot recommend this unless you enjoy spending your time running back and forth.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I remember seeing this game's trailer and being amazed by the animated trailer and cutscenes. The artwork for the game is so terrific! The animations, and the character profile illustrations! However, that's the only good thing I can say about the game. Gameplay is shallow, all you do is collect things and give them to people. I played for about 3 hours, trying to give it time, but it was a drag. I'm a little confused on the storyline itself as well, because at the point I stopped it didn't make any sense. Really though, I'm very disappointed on the graphics and actual game art though. The illustrations are SO GOOD, but that style choice doesn't carry through to the actual game. Everything is line-less, very bright, and very blocky. Game animations aren't polished, and the proportions are all over the place for game objects. There's a mansion on the first island, where the fences are taller than you, and the door to THE SAME MANSION is barely taller than you. The game simply doesn't feel finished to me. I feel like more attention to the game styling would be beneficial, as well as some actual gameplay that feels rewarding. I would not recommend because it doesn't live up to it's trailer.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Nice story and lovely visuals, but unfortunately this game is made up exclusively of the bane of all gamers: fetch quests. Every single quest involves going from one island back to another, back to another, back to another just to get that one thing the person asked for. If you want to fast travel between said islands, it'll cost you, and money isn't easy to make. Overall, it was nice visually and musically, but without obscene amounts of money allowing you to fast travel, it's painfully slow and tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah... I was super excited about this game. The idea of having a game looking like studio Ghibli animation, together with an interesting game design, that would combine Stardew Valley and Zelda Wind Waker was mind blowing. At least for me.However, when it comes to gameplay and game design Summer in Mara lacks a lot, and I must say as a game developer, I imagine how hard it was to come up with this super ambitious game, specially being an indie studio with, probably, a “not so good” budget. Yet, they did a terrific job creating a rich narrative, with friendly characters, and beautiful animation. But, in games likes this, you must have a just well polish game design to support your beautiful narrative, on the other hand players won’t be able to continue playing to find out the endeavours of your narrative. That is why I spent only 2 hours playing.That being said! Here is why I only spent 2 hours playing Summer in Mara:-	Fetch quests all over the place. I feel the game is about hold RT to run from point A to point B and press A to read your narrative. And not a “mix farming, crafting and exploring mechanic”.-	Exploration in this game it is like this: you go inside your boat; you drive your boat to the edge of the map, and you are teleported to a new island. So is not really an exploration per say! Right? Again, I’ve only played this game only for two hours, so I don’t know if it improves or not, but when I finally got the chance to explore, I didn’t explore at all.-	The last but not least, the UI/UX design drove me crazy. All the menus look the same, I lose track all the time, I am always pressing all buttons to understand what’s going on and what I should do, or what button I should press!  Some items I craft on pause menu, others I must do inside the home... So, lost of time wasted on trying to find my self in this mess. Now, the experience (UX) in this game is the worst, I thought I would be experiencing something magical, tropical, and alive. But all I see is a place with no live, no movement, no environment, no animals, no environment story telling. I only see robotic npcs, that just stand still (most of the time), a static environment in an empty Mediterranean world.In conclusion this game is beautiful, but it’s missing a lot of details which will improve the game experience and make the game more alive! I feel you guys reached beta in an incredibly good shape but needed more time to reach gold with thrive.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second game I've bought from these developers and I will never buy another. The games feel unfinished and unsatisfying. This was the better of the two games, but the world feels empty and kinda pointless. There are huge masses of land/water to slowly travel across but they're pretty void with no point to be there. Go play Windwaker, same experience but fun.

_childDocuments_.review: *** POSSIBLE SPOILERS***At almost 30 hours played of Summer In Mara by the time I completed it, it was unfortunately a case of being glad I was finally done with it and uninstalling it instantly.  I had hopes for this game, but what started out promising ended up an exercise in tedium.The character you play is, on the whole, not very likable.  She spends half her time mouthing off and giving people attitude.  The supporting cast of characters that you assist ranged from pretty forgettable to outright obnoxious and detestable. The bad guys (a race called the Elit) are given little more than stereotypical Eco-villain traits, and the main antagonist (the Baron) doesn't even make an appearance until the very end and is gone before you can even blink.The gameplay itself is insanely repetitive with more back-and-forthing than anyone should ever have to go through. Yes, they added  fast-travel ability in a patch, and that actually helped.  You still had to watch your fuel, but it made things a lot better.  But then, the game suddenly started charging you a fee to use it (which it did not when it was first implemented), and that did nothing but annoy.  And some of the distances between objectives was so great that NOT using fast travel would have added literal hours of mind-numbing travel to the overall game.  The gardening, animal tending and fishing are incredibly basic and do little to enhance the game.  If you are hoping for a Harvest Moon-type game, this is NOT it.   The quests range from typical fetch this, craft that tasks to... some of the more illogical and nonsensical jobs I've seen in games.  Some quests are given to you very early in the game... yet you are unable to obtain the items needed until much much later in the game, and you are left constantly wondering "Have I missed something?? Where is the thing for this quest??" when you can't even get to it yet.   It's a bit chaotic, feels disorganized and hap-hazard, and leaves a lot to be desired.  The story itself is uninspired and is full of overused save-the-environment cliches.In summation, Summer In Mara had the potential to be fun.  But in the end, there is nothing special about it, the repetitious gameplay dooms it to a game you just want to end, and the story and characters left me shrugging.  For me, there is no replay value here.  I finished it, I uninstalled it... I won't be back.  And that's a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I want to point out that Summer in Mara is not a bad game. However, as I have to choose whether to recommend it or not, I have to go with the latter. weak main line. Nothing special or at least catchy. Some sort of time gap between "Tutorial" (part of the game) and actual game that leaves holes. You catch on with that eventually but initial jump leaves you wondering. mostly get-and-deliver type. Often you get quests way too early and have no way of finishing them anytime soon. While each side quest line is progressing well, I can't call them great. you have your island where you can grow trees for wood or fruit, do general farming and later on get some animals to feed and get more resources. You can also build some structures on your island. The bad thing is that most of those structures are just for decorating purpose. Even things like oven and workshop don't let you interact with them to get access for cooking and crafting from different places on your island other than your house there.At some point of the game island management becomes nearly non-existent. Not due to upgrades but because you will probably ignore it unless you need to get some things from it. many colorful characters. However, there is little to none development to them. From the moment they are introduced almost nothing changes in their behavior or manners. there are 25 locations (5x5 grid if I remember correctly) that you can explore. Each locations may or may not contain an island with different resources available for you. It was fun to explore, then it got instantly boring as you got to every location. Most of them were ignored unless for a quest or specific resource required your presence. this is one of the positive aspects. The only bad thing about it is a static world - not so many things happen around. Some rare boats and NPCs that may be present on some islands. No NPCs that actually move around. mostly good. Fitting compositions for a relaxing gameplay. Some weird sound levels were noticed, however (some tunes got suddenly louder depending on the situation). controls were good except for the UI. I played with mouse and keyboard and UI was not really friendly to it. Some things were counter intuitive. I actually had to google how to sell things. Turned out you had to click on a specific icon (it does not look like a button, more like a hint).Small inconvenience within one quest: you can partially skip it but talking to the NPC would bring that quest later as if it was not complete.During another quest you had to boat race someone. Visually I was always in front, even when I crossed the finish line. But hard-scripted event said I lost.Major issue is fast-travelling. It costs money depending on how far you want to go. Fair enough. What's absolutely terrible is that it costs you 0 gold (and you actually can use it) when you have no money on you. This lead to the situation when having money on your character felt like a bad thing as you would lose it on fast travel. Instead, it felt rewarding to not trade with anyone unless exactly before you needed to buy something with extra money burning down during fast-travelling. Summer in Mara is a relaxing game that does not fit well neither in adventure type, nor in farming/management type of the game. It's colorful world and "help others / become friends with people around you" messages is probably good for kids, especially if you look at how casual the game is made. Overall okay-ish game that drastically gets boring after some time. Sadly, can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like fetch quests, chill games, and exploration, this is a summer you'll probably enjoy. It strikes me as similar to Yonder: The Cloud Catcher Chronicles with the exploration elements of Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker.  The devs seem to be responsive to player input based on the QOL updates since the game launched. If you're not into the "bring me # things" or "go talk to Y person" style of games, then this may not be one for you, but if you enjoy just helping people out, exploring the world, and just seeing what there is to see, then consider giving this one a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cute game, though I do want to say up front that as other reviews have mentioned, this is a very fetch quest heavy game. Pretty much the whole game is get quest, go from A to B, rinse and repeat. I felt in the beginning I was pretty resource starved, and the best way to solve that was to just keep moving forward. As soon as you can grow crops, buy cotton seeds and build boat models. There is a quest that will unlock that. It will help you out immensely in the beginning, until you start exploring more. Once I got to mid-game, I had so much money and resources that I honestly had no idea what to do with myself.The only thing I'm bummed about is that the ending felt very anti climatic. Other than that, I found this game very relaxing, and I absolutely loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Backed it up on Kickstarter after which it got delayed a couple of times, but I didn't mind, the more time they get, the better it should be. That, however, raised my expectations, which sadly weren't met completely. The game world is large, the game is lengthy, but that's both a pro and a con. There's a lot of quests, but very little variation, exploration is fun until you see everything there is, then traveling around the same areas gets boring and repetitive.Game world opens up to you in stages, and is all connected via quests, if you want to explore you need to progress the story, if you want to customize your island further, you need to progress the story... This wouldn't be an issue if majority of quests weren't copy pasted fetch quests.Island customization, as well as exploration, were my favorite parts, but these are again locked behind repetitive quests, if you want to get new recipes, items and plants to use, you'll have to follow the story. The game was advertised as a farming, crafting and exploration game, but I wouldn't even mention farming with such a system. It's really shallow, with preset field locations and not that interesting system. Animal keeping is also very basic, you build their habitat on a preset location and that's it, lost potential.I cannot make this review without comparing this to Deiland, and to be honest, Deiland is a much better game, on a smaller scale, but everything it has, is much more fitting and much less repetitive. Majority of mechanics in SiM are taken from there, and a lot of those just don't fit here, and are even downgraded.I enjoyed my time with the game, but I don't see myself playing it again, it has some issues, render distance for example seems to be cut down, probably to have a universal version over all systems, so PC squad got the short end of the stick again. There are some bugs present as well, hopefully they sort these out. So I will recommend it if you don't mind grinding and want a more casual game to pass your time with.

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxed farming game with oceanic exploration and a nice story. Game sounded perfect for me. Got into it and the controls felt stiff, even with the controller. Not something I'd moan about since this isn't uncommon in indie games, but mildly annoying nonetheless.My main issue with the game is how hollow it feels. Characters have a very stilted and awkward manner to them, the gameplay loop feels unrewarding and the story is just a long sequence of fetch quests with no real milestones or progression.

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara was a romp.Sure, the the UI isn't intuitive (I'm ashamed to say spent a good amount of time figuring out how to build/plant/etc), it's buggy (I crashed a few times, and my boat once dropped out of the map), and it's not completely polished. But I digress: there are many reviews that talk about how Summer in Mara isn't worth the $23 price tag. Mine isn't that.Let's get into it.Mara is a small but beautiful ocean planet. On an island in the centre, you're introduced as Koa, a spunky, stubborn girl who interrupts pretty much everyone but really just wants to learn about the world, keep her island safe, and help her community (she also wants to be a pirate). Koa's adoptive grandmother Yaya Haku is absolutely darling (perhaps I'm biased; she reminds me of my own Yaya) teaches you everything you need to know about how to harvest, plant, craft, and take care of the island. and although she leaves you quite early on in the game, her lessons of stewardship follow you throughout the game.Need to chop down an old tree? Plant a seed first. Need to fish? Don't take more than you need.I spent way too long sailing across the archipelago, digging up buried treasure, reading love notes and messages sent by carrier crab, and petting/feeding/rescuing all manner of Mara's creatures so they could come home with me. I made friends with pirates, arranged inter-species business partnerships, and stood up to researchers trying to terraform the land in the name of progress. Against my better judgement, I even .And, sometimes when COVID got me a bit too stir-crazy, I booted up the game to just sit for a moment on the roof, checking out my orchard, inspecting my vegetables, watching my chickens waddle, and seeing the seagulls swoop in the air.Truth be told, it was hard not to enjoy myself.Despite the very valid critique, there's a lot to respect about a game that knows its best asset is its vision. While it's not the next Mutazione or Stardew Valley, Summer in Mara does do a lot of things right:So, if you've been wondering how to introduce your five-year-old to sustainability, if you're into fetch quests tied together by a simple but enjoyable narrative with characters you'd love to borrow a cup of sugar from, and if you have the cash to support indie developers honing their skills, this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara feels like it's either a demo or made for children. I held off purchasing it despite my love of farming games until I saw it mentioned favorably on several videos of "the best farming games" compilations. I certainly wouldn't label Mara as one of the best but it's cute and can be fun at times... but it's simply too linear to be enjoyed by someone who's played Stardew Valley, Kyneseed, or Graveyard Keeper.The story is a bit bizarre, not for its fantasy setting but because it doesn't make a lot of sense. After your first day on the island you're treated to a rather beautiful animated cutscene and then you wake up and your adoptive grandmother is simply gone, all of the structures on your island are destroyed, and your boat is broken. Your character doesn't remark about this whatsoever and you just do the same things you did on the first day.As the days progress you slowly (very, very slowly) learn more crafting recipes that are always needed to edge the story along at a snails pace. The next character you meet is a lost... creature... whom you befriend. The character is barely animated and immediately made me think the developers of this game were fairly unskilled. There seems to have been a lot of emphasis placed on the visual style of the game at the detriment of every other component.It's a shame because the game does LOOK stunning in its cartoonish art style. Everything fits together well and the landscapes are like a painting. It's just not a fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: This game is charming, and I wish there was an "it's okay" or "meh" option, but there isn't so I'll just give it a thumbs down. A lot of people don't like the fetch quests, and I wouldn't mind them if running didn't use stamina. I hate farming games/exploration games that use stamina when you run. I know it's realistic, but it's annoying when you have to constantly run back and fourth and everything is spaced out. Maybe at some point in the game you get some kind of mount or something that would make the errand running better, but it's not. And even sailing and exploring isn't fun - and is ultimately what made me decide I didn't want to play the game anymore. Some of the mini games are annoying and you can't redo them. I haven't had fish on my main island since they ran out, and I wish you could just fish limitlessly, or at least the fish didn't go down if you failed to catch one. The same with diving. I think it's dumb if you have one diving helmet, you should be able to use it over and over. Especially since the diving mini game has awful controls.It is a charming game, but it just gets boring after a while. And I enjoy grind-y games. Graveyard keeper was my jam. But idk this one just doesn't give you a good turtorial and fetch quests just keep get rewarded with other fetch quests. Honestly, I'd refund it if I didn't play more than 2 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Yeahh... after playing it some more I've changed my mind.The amount of bugs makes this really hard to play.Especially regarding travel and movement. Like out of everything these two mechanics should've been solid, but they aren't.I'm constantly getting stuck and am unable to move, sometimes it makes sense because i fall in a hole, other times I just walk down the street and get caught on something that doesn't exist. The clipping and barriers in this game are impossible. It's mainly that the game won't let you walk off cliffs, but slopes count as cliffs and you can't climb slopes and automatically fall down them so you're infinitely stuck sliding off a slope that counts as a cliff so you can't walk off of it. Not to mention the boat. The sheer amount of times I either get softlocked while exploring or sailing makes this game actually unplayable. If you get stuck on an island, with no coin, no fuel, and the boat despawns. You are actually stuck and have to reset the game. This sucks because most people encounter this on the Volcano Island which is quite a bit into the game. I don't know what is is, other than some of the islands are bugged. Like really bad bugs. Not just, oh a slight inconvenience, I mean game breaking in all the worst ways regarding progress being reset. The most recent bug I just now ran into which has made me change my review from an up into a down, is the boat falling into the ocean when i loaded a new zone. Like, I fell into the ocean.  Boat and all stuck on a blue screen unable to move. I can't even pause and exit because you can't pause the game in a boat to exit to menu. You can only do that when you exit the boat which is a ret*rded mechanic.You should be able to access the menu in game to adjust sensitivity and volume levels, but you can't. Even things like trying to water, harvest, or plant crops are impossible if you have more than one chicken because they'll constantly push you around trying to get close to you and you'll end up petting them which wastes 4 seconds. Not to mention that they'll eat fruit and charcoal as well as any other item that drops to the ground. They'll eat cork, resin, and wood, if you let them. And again, petting them takes priority over picking up items on the ground so while you're stuck in that animation they'll eat whatever you just harvested. It's f*cking annoying. They need bug fixes instead of lowering the price. Play a different game. The grind is slow, and unrewarding, on top of the progression being all over the place. This is a very linear game pretending that it isn't. You can skip quests, but are eventually forced to go back and do the,.You can build up a lot of resources and not be slowed down by the later grind, but that's still a grind you have to do. You don't get more charcoal for burning trees than you do bushes, and if you have only one of an animal instead of at least 4, when you collect your reward it is restricted by how many animals you have. If you have one chicken, you get one egg, if you have at least 4 chickens you get 4 eggs. Which doesn't make sense because you're using the same amount of resources. It should change how fast you get eggs or other animal products, not how many. Not to mention the shop prices being all over the place, it fits in the story, but even still is just annoying given that's where you have to start. Which is why the grind is so tedious. You can either buy expensive seeds and wait longer periods of time, or buy cheaper ones and have to buy more and more everyday instead of a few every once in a while. You get better prices later in the game, but the venders are not in a single location and constantly move so their shops are incredibly unreliable.This is not that fun of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: All the charm of Harvest Moon with a Wind Waker-ish story and sailing adventure.The game starts off with a slow/basic tutorial, but once you get through the "prologue/first chapter" of the story you're basically free to do whatever you'd like. You can either focus on trying to expand your little farmland chunk or follow the story-line driven quests to progress the other unlocks\islands in the game.I haven't had patience for a lot of these kind of games, but something about this one and the way it teaches you and gives you "direction" if necessary is awesome. Also - you don't even have to worry about being forced to sleep! The stamina mechanic in this is WAY more forgiving than other games like this.If you're looking for a purely farming game, I would probably stay away from this though; this is definitely more story driven in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I got this because it was on sale and looked cute, and lots of people said it was a nice mix between Windwaker and Stardew Valley. I think the only similarity with Windwaker is that you are on the ocean with a boat. There's an open sea that you can sail around on, but the different quadrant are sparse, with only tiny islands and the occasional fishing spot - this is actually just like Windwaker, but I'd think if you wanted to take inspiration from another game, you wouldn't draw from the worst parts of said game :/With the Stardew Valley aspect, the game has a personal little island where you farm, grow trees, collect materials etc. The farming is tedious and 4+ hours in I can only plant around five things at once, and the watering/fertilizing system is implemented badly (you have certain amount of time to spread your water before it runs out, then you have to go back to your well to get any crops you missed, and when your well runs out of water you have to wait for the chance of rain to refill your well).The quests are straightforward but there is a LOT of running back and forth, sometimes between the same two people three or four times in a row. In order to do a lot of stuff, you need money to buy seeds or other items, but the game DOES NOT tell you how to sell stuff. It's not in the settings or controls, both of which you can only access from the main menu, not in-game. After looking it up, it turned out to be a random key that isn't used for anything else in the game.Gameplay-wise, it's alright. Again, the game doesn't tell you anything about your hunger or stamina bars. Like Stardew, you "faint" if your stamina runs out, but it seems like you don't lose anything - if there isn't a negative consequence, I don't know why it's even a feature. If anything, it respawns you a little closer to your boat if you're far away. The graphics are cute, but the character models and animations are a little stale - certain characters just rotate to look at you, and some of the player animations just seem like there wasn't a lot of work put into them - the running animation (that you stare at the whole game) is stiff, and when you're holding tools, they're just floating in your open hand. There are lots of giant invisible walls sticking out of terrain all over the world, which is especially annoying when the best way to travel all the long distances they give you is jumping up the sides of mountains - one of the selling points for a game like this would be the ability to explore, especially all the new islands on the open ocean, but they limit you quite a bit. I even saw a few places where the sides of mountains didn't actually touch the ground, and there was just empty air with a big floating rock. The only place to craft tools and items (so far) is by sailing all the way back to your island. I've found one place in the main city where I can use a kitchen, but at your house you can craft multiple things at once - this kitchen made me do them one at a time.I could go on to list a bunch of mild inconveniences I had, but bleh. The only reason I didn't refund the game is because I'm a fool and left the game open when I went to the bathroom. When I came back it had just reached two hours, so >:(I will say that the game has beautiful drawn art. The character art for dialogue and the animation they had near the opening were both fantastic, and have definitely been the highlight of the game so far. I'm gonna keep playing it because I have it now, so why not, but so far there hasn't really been much of a story line so I'm not expecting or looking forward to much. I got it on sale which softens the blow, and I'm sure plenty of people will enjoy it. This is just my annoyed two cents.

_childDocuments_.review: If you wish of a game that remind you of the good summer vibes at the farm close to the lake, summer is mara is made for you Not heavy into the farming sim nor crafting, it's a pretty relaxing game with good art and music that make you run errants for who accept to talk to the little child you are, pretty chill game, you'll find yourself playing it way more than it feels just because you want to discover the others islands and upgrade MaraI won't recommend it if you are searching a game that is more like stardew valley
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: The game is super cute and once the map unlocks the gameplay becomes fun. However, the tutorial needs work. On one hand, it's very hand-holdy but then on the other hand, super important things like shortcuts and hotkeys are skipped entirely. The biggest issue though is (and that is why the game currently gets a negative review from me) if you easily suffer from motion sickness, this game will make you hurl. The only graphic settings are Low, Medium and High. Low plays at a stuttery and janky 30 FPS. Medium at least turns off the absurdly high motion blur but it still retains a high enough amount of it that coupled with the non-adjustable FOV, I just can't recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game on kickstarter long ago, when it came out i was very excited and got about 1 hour into it before i lost interest and stopped playing. i decided to play again and restarted. Its definitely made of fetch quests. you don't get much freedom to do your own thing and everything seems to be unlocked through these micro, but big quests. It got annoying having to travel from home to one island. then have to go back home for one tiny thing and then go all the way back just to have to do the same for another quest. I was super excited for this game but quickly became annoyed, upset and bored with it. If i was home to grow crops i would sleep through all the days to get it over with faster.in the description it says harvest your own crops while helping others, but i feel like i just harvest the trees for myself and only farm for a quest that needs it. I thought id be able to make the island my own too, but there's not much to do on it except to grow plants. I didn't get to any part where animals come into play. but i doubt ill play long enough to see that.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played for long but I've found it a bit buggy and confusing.You have to figure out a lot of the mechanics by yourself (I had to google how to sell stuff because i couldn't figure it out). There's no shift in seasons or anything. Tends to skip cut scenes (I don't know if i keep accidentally pressing something or its just buggy). The first Noho quest is really confusing, it says 5 crabs in the quest log but I've looked up a walk-through for that specific quest and it says you only have to find the 3 on the beach and go speak to Noho but it doesn't seem to work.I feel like the game has potential but its just not quite there yet and needs a little time.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable game. I took my time and eventually did 100% achievements and it took me 38 hours.Worth the price of the game for me.There are however many things that could be improved. Ability to remap keys for keyboard players.Ability to change graphics settings.Pressing map (M) and inventory (I) should toggle and not require escape every time to close out menus.Numerous issues with getting stuck on terrain. Easy to fix but annoying.The targeting system is very finicky especial on the boats.and other minor things.The graphics are simple yet very nice and the overall world is well done.Simple to navigate and progress. The fast travel is very much appreciated.This was a fun and enjoyable game even with the minor annoyances and I would recommend.I hope there will be a sequel. :)SPOILERS

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the demo, and getting a bit into the full game, I can honestly say this is definitely worth the price. While yes, the controls are a bit odd (especially if using mouse and keyboard), it still is clear the developers put a LOT of work into this game. Summer in Mara focuses on minimal UI, so finding some things near the beginning can be a bit confusing. There are some things that could be polished, but I am sure over time things will be, and this game will expand into something even more amazing than it is now.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: The cut scenes in the beginning of the game really fill you with hope on these characters being full of life and adventure. Unfortunately, after the first 30 minutes, you are bound to the "I need this! Go back to your home island to get it for me", followed by the "Now, go back to your home island and craft this!" form of gameplay. Characters are static, and they don't have many if any animations. Koa herself seems awkward when running with her static head in every direction, and Mario backflip tier height to her jump. It's charming! The dialogue is cute. But it's very shallow waters in Mara.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is good, the story is well written, the characters are endearing and fit perfectly to the story, I like the drawings and the look of the different environments of the game, it's nice to explore, making the game feel like Wind Waker! I also like the fact that you do multiple things like helping the different characters and taking care of your island.But there's many improvements to make:- The time goes too fast so you can't really do much, one day (which means the moment you wake up to the moment you're forced to fall asleep) equals around 12 minutes, it's not enough. The seconds in game shouldn't go faster than seconds in real life, one day in game should at least an hour or half an hour in real life- The animals keep following you around, it's cute at first but it can quickly become annoying- The pause menu doesn't have options so you need to leave the game to change them- The characters look a bit weird in 3D and act like robots- You can walk through things like some trees- The hitbox of certain things is too big- Your character's stamina drops too fast so you constantly need to eat food, it even drops when you're not moving- The PNJs don't move so they look like statues, making them move would give a lot more life to the environments- The fact that sleeping in your boat doesn't give you back the same amount of energy than sleeping in your house, but sleeping in a sleeping bag in the middle of nowhere does is kinda weird (and yes, this one was hard to type)- The game needs more human characters, most of them are anthropomorphic fish/animals or aliens- When Koa gets forced to fall asleep, she appears on top of her house and you don't get all your stamina back, so she has enough strenght to climb on her roof but not to go in her house and lay down in her bed??Okay so I know I've said more complains but the game, besides those things I've said, is really nice to play, it's relaxing and it's easy to get attached to it, I just hope the game will improve more in the future
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and got all the achievements and...Mixed feelings.Honestly it's a beautiful game. I enjoyed the characters (even when they were being childish), the music is captivating and I love the art style. It's fun to sail around and not have to worry about HP, fall damage and the like. Just play the game and enjoy the story!The down side is that the story (while having some pretty decent emotional moments) was a little disjointed. I suppose if you play the main story straight through it would probably have more impact but I was doing all the side quests. Which, by the way, is about 100 fetch-quests back to back. Sometimes it wouldn't be so bad but there are a series of them that literally have you going back and forth to the same two people.14.5 hours of game play and about half of it is just running back and forth between NPCs on their fetch quest. It's my only real gripe.Otherwise I really enjoyed this little game! I honestly felt at peace (and a little sad) at the end when I got the last achievement, sat on top of my little island home and logged out for the last time. That, to me at least, is the sign of a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is  game that  fits for all ages and does not have pretty much close to nothing violent content in it.Characters are made mostly using a humor even if they should be a little "evil or shady"(Friendly pirates and so on)Farming, Fishing, diving, crafting and cooking while doing guests are the point in this chill and relaxing game.No actual leveling systems, only upgrading your tools and boat is possible and building your home island. Everything is bound to quests and in order to complete some of them you need to do another quest chains to unlock some missing ingredients or simply just make money and buy them. -  Game makes you run a lot of back and forth.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is a very peaceful game. It is chill and wholesome, something to play to unwind before the night is over. It is purely fetch quests, no combat whatsoever. A bit of a walking sim too, but I didn't mind it. The sailing and exploring of islands reminded me of Wind Waker, so that was fun. I don't recommend skipping cut scenes or spamming through dialogue since the conversations are where a lot of cute and interesting things happen. After beating the game, I do find myself looking for the next relaxing game to add to my library that was as feel-good as this one. As simple as it is, it is charming and left me wanting more.

_childDocuments_.review: (Update: Response to dev comment at the bottom.)Anything positive I could say about this title is overshadowed by what needs to be fixed before it approaches enjoyable.Cute games thrive on immersion and their tactile nature. Rigid character animations and quest loops that rely on tedium do not accomplish that goal. I can not recommend Summer in Mara at $25, or even the promotional launch price of $21. It  like a $12 game.-----Concerning the developer response: The issues addressed in the roadmap address many of the issues I had with the game, and I applaud the dev team for their work. _childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a game to lay back and relax this isnt it..Game is filled with small bugs and bad choices, at the start of the game getting used to navigating menus were very painfull also game doesnt do a good job of telling you what to do next so you have to constantly search for an answer online.  After many hours of getting used to the annoying stuff in the game farm animals became the biggest annoyance of them all. I made the mistake of rescuing many chickens which led to them over running the field area, they will constantly chase you and the feed button will keep popping up when you are trying to pick up fruits and such even after you feed them there is a pet button so they will keep blocking you no mather what.  Same goes for up the hill (some trees you can only plant there) with squirrels harassing you. There is also fruits on trees keep dropping and despawning in seconds (right in front of you) problem.. None of the (many) bugs broke my game completely and there were solutions online so lets ignore them, remove the pet button for the farm animals so that after feeding them they cant block you also make it so that dropped goods doesnt despawn so fast..  fix these 2 and i can ignore all the other issues and how lackluster the ending was..
