_childDocuments_.review: I had looked forward to Summer in Mara for a good while. It looked super cute and while I didn't hype it up at all, I did have a long history of games that fall under that farming-esque genre, like Story of Seasons (and under the old title of Harvest Moon), My Time at Portia, Rune Factory, Stardew Valley, etc. With that sort of a background this game was such a disappointment. I gave it a solid chance with over 30 hours played and the one constant throughout was hoping if I played just a bit more it would get good. I had hope. I was giving it that chance that maybe just the beginning was paced poorly and things would pick up. But that never happened. There are aspects of the story that might have become interesting, but they certainly weren't 30 hours in. And there were occasional characters that weren't completely bland and forgettable, but those were few and far between. Even the main character isn't really likable, at least not to me. I never had fun playing this game. I simply kept waiting for the possibility it would become fun. And it just didn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: The opening cinematic and the first 30 minutes are amazing. Playing the demo instantly sold me on this game.Unfortunately, as soon as you're past that point the game becomes a boring grind fest of fetch quests. Prepare to make hundreds of slow boat rides to and from your island as you help the charming characters of the main town.There is little to do in the way of farm customization. You get a handful of farm plots, and can rebuild some existing derelict buildings but you can't design your layout like with other farming sims. Also, the Devs have no idea how a well works, which isn't a good sign for a farming game. (Btw devs, a well draws water from the ground, it doesn't need to wait for rain to fill up).Other games such as Stardew Valley or My Time at Portia are much more worthy of your money than this boring garbage.<Edit> After sinking another 18 hours into the game to force myself to finish it, I can assure you it gets much much worse than I originally thought. The dev road-map suggests they are going to make some changes that will help with a lot of the tedium, so down the road it might be worth a buy.Here's the thing though.... This game desperately needs fast travel to break up the boredom. Bringing in fast travel though, will dramatically reduce the time to play through this game to the point where you could probably finish everything it has to offer in 5 or 6 hours. That's how much travelling you currently do in this game. This game looks great and runs as smooth as butter, but wow....it is boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is basically a more 3D version of Spiritfarer. It has it's ups and downs, but for the most part I'd give this game a 4/5. Firstly, the good stuff, the graphic's are fair, and the character sprites in the chat boxes are adorable! There's some real personality put into them and all their individual poses. Secondly, the music is nice, though it can get a bit jarring sometimes with it sometimes popping in out of nowhere. As far as the 'bad stuff' goes, there's no directional compass that tells you where you need to go for your quest. So you're stuck running around wasting stamina looking for stuff a lot. I also don't really like that it cost coins to fast travel, you should just be able to fast-travel but have it eat up time instead. Also there's no main menu in game for you to use, so there's no changing settings to suit your graphic's hardware needs, nor windowed version of the game. So if you want to look something up on the wiki, you're stuck pulling up your task manager to escape the game. There's also the issue of the 'controls' and I just wish people would allow hotkeys to be personally customized for our own individual needs. Because I know my hands are cramping up already because I'm too poor to afford a game controller.Also PLEASE make it so you can jump IN the water. I've fallen out of the boat many a time and had to swim great distances just to get back onto land. It is not fun swimming, it's slow. Also jumping is very jarring and sudden and I wish it wasn't.I'd say that the game is worth the money when it's on sale. But it's way too janky to be really considered a game worth the full price it is. If you have patience, and a LOT of it, there ya go.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Game completed and all achievements in about 34-35 hours for me. I tried to take my time and enjoy it too. I wouldn't say don't buy it, you should if it suits you but I wouldn't pay full price for it. That being said it is cute. A sort of adorable plot where a really bossy kid learns to be semi-responsible? If you like cute and relaxing this might be it. That's really what I liked about it. What I didn't like: I kind of felt like the farming wasn't as developed as it could have been? I took a lot of time to plant all the fruit trees on my island but I never really needed the fruit. I didn't really need most of my crops either. It really was mostly quests to find things and bring things to people. What I really hated.. what irritated me more than anything was the trees that would only grow on high ground. There is not enough room on your island to properly grow them. The peach trees are huge and they don't look right at the top of the little mountain by your shrine. Maybe the little pomegranates were fine up there... but I really hate that the peach trees had to go up there as well. Limited what I could plant and how much pretty severely.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: A game with a lot of potential and good moments, but ultimately lacking in polish. The sense of adventure, likened to some great inspirations, made me excited to play it. However the execution was not there, which was a great shame.I do appreciate what the small team of developers were trying to achieve, despite the gameplay letting it down. The heartwarming stories, defined and fascinating characters and an overall optimistic feeling with great messages about love, family, friendship and living in harmony with each other and nature, spurred me on to complete the game. But those elements should accompany and elevate the core gameplay. In this case, the missions aren't remarkable and suffer from bad pacing and missing variety. They comprise entirely of fetch quests with a back-and-forth disruptive flow to them. There is also minor bugginess and lack of general QoL in multiple areas, making it feel rushed and unfinished. The concept, music and art makes me want to rate the game higher, but since the gameplay overall falls short, it balances it out at being 'fine'.Considering that the 2D artwork, animations and music were by far the best stand-outs of the game, aside from the story and personalities, I'd say it's worth purchasing the art and OST, and reading up the story online instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. There are a few cons to the game, but the overall experience for me is enjoyable, and I’m so happy that I was gifted it. :)  If you’re someone that enjoy games like Stardew Valley, My Time at Portia, Harvest Moon ect, this has a familiar vibe to those games, but with simpler mechanics. (which isn’t a bad thing!) The game has a lot of fetch quests, a lot of the game you will find yourself running backwards and forwards to do simple tasks for the npc’s. There is a lot of great art in this game despite it being very simple, and there is also beautiful, relaxing music. I’ve enjoyed spending a few hours at a time to relax/wind down by playing this game. My only cons to the game:- Despite how pretty the game is, Koa’s hair is awful.- There is quite a few invisible walls, I find where I should be able to walk/jump or sail to I will get stuck by a wall. - When in open sea I noticed that the water would glitch at times and have harsh lines showing - I wish I could have gotten to know the characters more than running errands for them- Koa’s energy bar was really weird and I didn’t really understand it.- The map half way through my gameplay decided to not work properly when I would try to fast travel (it would freeze before I could get to where I needed, and I would have to force close the game and reopen it)Do I recommend the game? Yes! even though there was a few things I wish they had paid more attention to or would tweak, the overall game was still fun to me and it didn’t end up bothering me much.Keyboard and Mouse or Controller?: I preferred using a controller :) Is it something you would replay or continue to play?Personally I don’t see myself replaying the game. I have fully finished the main story/side stories, and I have unlocked all the steam achievements for the game. There is currently no more incentive to keep playing. However, if there will be more content released in an update in the future, I will definitely come back to the game to check it out. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara initially draws you in with appealing visuals and the chance to explore the open sea and visit islands which other similar games don't have.After you move past this, you're faced with a game that really isn't sure of its own identity. It's a bad farming/crafting game and also a bad adventure/RPG. The story, quests, characters and dialog are all very shallow and forgettable. There's only one main quest line that does a poor job of trying to make you care about the story. Other than that, the other quests are basic fetch quests. The farming, both animals and crops are honestly a chore with no real consequence of ignoring them. Fishing is really the only mechanic the involves more than just "Press E", but you're limited to about 3 fish at each spot then have to wait for a few days for the fish to regenerate.I've spent a lot of time and upgraded my boat to the point where I can explore all of the "islands" which again, are also forgettable. It's hard to recommend this game when games like My Time At Portia does basically everything better.

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant way to pass hours of time. Everything is adorable, and warm in a way that makes me smile. There's an underlying story, but very little pressure to complete it if you just want to goof around for awhile. I spent a fair amount of time just chasing a rabbit around for example. I didn't need to, but I sure wanted to.Additional (Added 5/22/23): I've been dealing with a mental funk that really breaks me down. The relentless optimism, cute graphics, and bright world of Summer in Mara has been a shining beacon of hope that things can get better. I've fallen so in love with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The first 30 minutes of story and game play are amazing but after that it is just a bunch of fetch questing. This game feels so unfinished. You only spend time on your island to grow and build things. You spend 90% of you time going between your island and the main town island. There is only 1 island besides these 2 that you ever even need to go to for anything. The game has the bones for making a great game but in it's current state it is really boring. I am very unimpressed. There is definitely more that can be done with this game. The story feels rushed and the quests are monotonous. Go farm this, now do nothing for 5 days while that grows. Now go make this. Run this thing to this person. I had higher hopes for this game. You are limited on farming plots and if you don't want to spend who knows how long sitting on your farm waiting for fruit trees to give fruit (aside from apples and oranges the trees give little to no fruit) then you have to buy materials for quests as is. I've played through and finished the story and gotten nearly every achievement because I didn't want to leave a review without having played the whole game. There were times I would easily get distracted and wander off to do something else for an hour or two just to break the monotony.

_childDocuments_.review: Being up front the game has a lot of issues. It won't teach you basic mechanics and it is very easy to get frustrated with quests due to a lack of information. There are some side quests that you are given that you cannot complete because you don't have access to certain items yet. However the game never mentions that you will later get access to those certain things if you progress the main quest which has led to me looking everywhere for certain things only to learn that I have to progress the main story to gain access to them. While this isn't outright a bad thing, I personally think it is poor game design to tell your players to get a certain item, while they don't have access to that item yet.The game has a lot of issues when it comes to story telling. A lot of the writing is poorly done and the character development feels empty, like there was no point in me interacting with them. They would be the same person from the start of the game to the end. The main NPCs, just like the filler NPCs, don't move, so there really is a lack of immersion in the world. Some of them do work on schedules, but they kinda just teleport around instead of actually moving. Some characters you will find in two different locations on the same island. I can only guess that I am just supposed to believe the character moves between those two spots, but it just feels off. Sometimes you'll find the main NPCs chilling on smaller islands which seems a little more realistic, but they don't add any real benefits besides maybe an extra few text lines and added immersion. To gain access to more islands you need to upgrade your boat which makes sense until a part in the main quest where you suddenly have more islands available because the game just decided it was time to give you more islands. No upgrading, it was just the plot holding my exploration back.15 of the main NPCs can all be found on the first island you are given access to besides your Home Island and you will spend a large portion of the game just going between your home island and this other island for what basically boils down to glorified fetch quests. You need to return back to your home island to farm and then you go back to the other island to complete quests. Also an NPC I met on the open sea, I had completed their entire quest-line just by talking to them once, so there were some obvious corners cut.  And here is the main issue with pacing for the game. A good 10-15 hours of the early game is spent just going back and forth between these two islands and I assume the later parts of the game once I'm finished exploring are going to be the same because most the NPCs are just bunched on the one island. Only until around 20-25 hours into the game (where I am as of making this review) do you gain access to the entire map and have more access for "customization" on your home island.Speaking of customization... You have predetermined spots where you are able to farm crops, maxing out at 16 available once you have upgraded all your tools and cleared out the plots. You can place fences, wells, and other various structures that you gain access to through quest completion. You are able to customize your character's clothes and backpack as you gain access to more cosmetics throughout the quests. You can also plant various trees around your island that provide resources and some decoration. In comparison to many other games like this where customizing a base is an option, this game falls short.And while you may be able to customize your island and character, you can't customize your settings. There is no option to while in the game, you need to quit to the main menu to change settings which is absurd. On top of the the amount of settings is embarrassingly low. A friend of mine who wanted the game said they weren't going to get it specifically because of how the bloom makes it hard for them to look at the scenery sometimes because it was too bright, and there is no option to change it in the game. The only settings you can change are the Volume, Graphics Quality, Language, and Inverted Camera. You aren't allowed to change controls either so anyone who doesn't have a standard keyboard, don't get this game until the option to change controls is available.Overall I think the game tried to reach too many people and shot itself in the foot. While I am all for inclusion and giving people more options, I have heard many issues from people who played the game on controller or Nintendo Switch that had issues so bad, the game was actually unplayable for them. There are also around 10 grammar issues that I have found in the English version, so I would assume it might be the same or worse for other languages. The game needed an actual Early Access for a larger community to play the game and give it feedback so they could update it. Instead they released a partially finished game on multiple platforms and while I would like the story and characters to have improvements, it's clear that the main focus is currently making the game playable on the other platforms (as it should be), but that makes me doubt that they will ever improve the actual game. If they had focused on making the PC version the best it could be, and then ported to consoles once the game was truly complete, most of these issues could have been avoided.  Game has a poor story and lacks fun gameplay. You will spend most of your time grinding resources and going between the same 2 islands. Looks good and has good music, but is sometimes unplayable on consoles. You can't change keybindings and you can only change settings in the main menu and the options are minimal. NPCs can break the immersion and character development seems nonexistent. I would assume the developers are prioritizing making the game work on other consoles before they consider improving the game, which isn't guaranteed either. After so long the game hasn't been updated to fix any of these problems so I have to recommend people to not get this game.Edit: (12/30/2021) Almost 2022 and this game hasn't received a major update addressing ANY issues whatsoever, in this review or not. Do NOT get this game. You will be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I participated in the Kickstarter for this game. It's a cute game with a nice story. I enjoy farming sim games and I had really high hopes for this game and while its not bad by any means I wouldn't recommend this game to just anybody. If you are new to farm sim style games I would say move on. There were times that this game felt a little to slow early on. I found myself sleeping as much as possible in order to pass the time and grow crops to turn in quests. It picked up as the game wore on but if you don't have the patience to push through the first bit of the game then it could be a bit rough for you. I'm going to click not recommend this game not because its awful but because it's not for everybody. 6/10

Some quests doesnt even give anything, you're just wasting your time reading dialogues and when it does its just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ reward. You just delivering an items from one npc to another when that npc is 3 meter away.In steam page it says over 20 islands to "explore". Most of those islands are empty, you can explore the whole island in 5min. After that you are done with that island, there nothing to do more. _childDocuments_.review: So I want to start out by saying this game is fun and I enjoyed it. the things that annoy me with the game is the massive amount of back and forth that you get from an MMORPG with quest lines and you can fast travel for money but litterally at the end of the game you have to shell out 12500gp which is a lot for a debt to egain and a spyglass from Aguila. It challenges me to see what I can achieve in a day because there is so much to do. Whether it be sailing and exploring to doing missions or taking care of my island. _childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game if you don't mind fetch quests, but after 8 hours of nothing but fetch quests, I find myself pretty disappointed. I was hoping there would be more to the game than that. I also thought the story was very disjointed from what I've seen so far. Maybe something is lost in translation? Koa says things that seem to be in response to something another character says even if the other character didn't say it, and some of the dialog didn't get localized super well. Also, I kept jumping off my boat and then not being able to get into it again, which is pretty frustrating. Not a huge fan, I think some other people would like it but it wasn't for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Koa is an orphan adopted by a retired navy officer, Yaya Haku. For years they lived on a large Island on Mara growing crops and raising animals until tragedy strikes leaving Koa alone to raise herself. One night there is a strange glow from the ocean, and Koa meets a strange girl named Napopo who needs help! Together they make their way off the Island and onto a huge adventure! I had a ton of fun playing, Mara is a huge open world that’s mostly ocean so you travel by ship. Rescue animals and bring them home to your Island to get livestock, feed them your crops to let them grow bigger, and you get other animals like dogs, geese, mice and squirrels as you play. There are a lot of npc’s and the music was really fun to listen to while you explore! You can grow trees on your island and dress up Koa with different outfits and backpacks, no quests are time-sensitive and there is a lot of Islands and activities like fishing, diving, mining, treasure hunting, etc…The only downside of the game I’ve noticed is that all the quests are fetch quests, but fast travel does exist in the game so it’s not a huge bother. A few bugs like during a pirate racing quest fast travel is disabled until you beat her, and when you grow coconut trees on your island you can just run through them like they don’t exist.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Really chill and captivating experience, the artwork is beautiful and the voice-less adventure has this older-games feeling that has its own charm. Koa is an adorable protagonist, and at several moments of the story is interesting how you, as an adult, can feel the same frustration she has as a child towards people who are supposed to be more responsible than her.I felt like the resolution to the buildup of the story was somewhat lacking but still worth playing. My biggest frustration was some mechanics being hidden and not hinted at, such as you being able to fill empty water bottles in a single location (and just likely discovering it by chance, as I did). If you're playing without a guide, at some point you'll run into the conundrum of not having certain materials to farm in the world, so you're stuck planting and skipping time by sleeping several days in a row until you can go out and grind again so you can progress on the quests.Frustrating griding aside, it's a really fun experience and I felt the 30 hours worth of gameplay were well invested.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first time writing a bad review. I really wanted to like this game. The music and the artwork are both amazing, and the mechanics are not bad per se, but:• The key arrangement makes no sense and it's not very intuitive.• I had to restart the game due to a flower that I sold not spawning anymore• I got tired of going to a point on the map, delivering an item just to be sent back to an other point again.• Charging you to fast travel? _childDocuments_.review: I was very excited when it was announced that Summer in Mara was out of Early Access, which essentially meant it was ready to play. I've had it in my wish list for a long time in hopes this is the Stardew Valley ♥♥♥ My Time at Portia game I've been waiting for. I've been playing this game for about 3-4 hours and it feels very much not finished at all. The island is bland and lacks key elements. The game seems to sneak in little things like "eh? We're smart!" but doesn't follow those ideas up. So the game itself feels unfinished. Alongside that, the features that are in the game feel very wonky. The map doesn't display your character, so you have no idea where you are. The health bar is blue, so it blends in with the sky background. Sometimes the mouse button works, sometimes it doesn't depending on what you're trying to do, etc. The beginning is polished for the demo, but after that you're more or less left on your own with no real direction. You just jump about and hope to find something to do. It feels like a child's game because of the dialogue and pace, but even a child will throw down the controller at some point and exclaim "I don't know what this game wants me to do!"I was also hoping that the plot would be at least decent. But it feels very simple, as if the was an afterthought. You do quest after quest so Koa can learn the simplest things that you the player already knows! Because they ALREADY TOLD YOU THE PLOT! So it's super frustrating. On the back of all that, they decided to make the game longer by simply making all the NPCs rude af. I'd be okay with that in a game that allowed you to play around, perhaps come back to those annoying MFers later, but you can only progress by agreeing to their terms. Those being the generic "bring me x bundles of LoTR DVDs so I can give you the slightest clue as to where to go next". You can't do anything else. Sure you can go back to your island and water your plants for 2 minutes and go worship the god of boat fuel, but it feels meaningless to be there other than grind items to complete quests for the NPCs. Everything to progress the game takes place on the island of city people. I'm going to keep playing for now and see if the game improves, as I know how hard it is to work in the game industry but currently I am very disappointed after the demo.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been following this game for a while now. Every time an ad popped up for it, I would click just to look at it again. While the animations are beautiful and make you feel like your are about to dive into a Studio Ghibli movie... don't let it fool you. It looks like most of their budget wen towards the animation and game graphics. Which is great... for the visual appeal. But I think we have all learned a think or two from the Elder Scrolls lines. Graphics doesn't always mean the game is amazing (or better then the last in the case of Elder Scrolls). The story was lacking and seemed to become less and less important as you played. NPC were nearly statues. Game play was basically fetching and back tracking. Constantly. Other flaws were the lack of instructions on how to open any form of menu or what button was for what. Just button mash, that's pretty much how you figure things out. There were also a few things that weren't explained like; you run out of energy when you run and how you are suppose to refule yourself so you can actually run again. I hope there are some major updates to the game so that I can come back and really enjoy it. As for now, I think it's sadly just going to collect dust.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh...it comes off as a rather nice beginner effort, with a few issues.Most glaring is that the controller support doesn't work.. apparently they left the prompts in from the console version, but the PC version doesn't actually pick up controller input.Next most glaring is a failure in tutorial...they missed a very important detail, namely how to sell to vendors instead of just buy from them. I ended up having to find a Guide post here on Steam to learn that.The rest of the issues are storytelling...the transition from the opening intro/tutorial to the main game is a bit abrupt, and only vaguely implies what happens to the intro character that tutored the main character. The ending is also quite abrupt, with the 'main villain' appearing for maybe a minute with a little scenery-chewing in-game dialogue, then disappearing again in the cutscene immediately after.There are also a couple of grindy missions, particularly in the post-game, but the biggest issue I had with them is certain key characters moving about the world map, requiring a good bit of searching to find them again to turn in missions and get the next.Other than that, it's a nicely made little game, and I'd be curious if the company ever came out with another, better one.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I say anything, I have 100% achievements in this game 👍.The positive first. You start at an amazing tropical island, the landscape is beautiful, warm, and welcoming. What is supper cool is that island is fully customizable. You can grow pretty trees and arrange them to make your island amazing. The pace of the game is very laid back and relaxed. There are treasures and treasure maps in the game, and who doesn't like digging chests full of goodies? Now the negative. NPC characters abuse the main character making her do their bidding for almost free in most cases. At times it feels like you are a corporate slave to please your master just to push the story forward. The narrative and story is towards little kids, and for a adult makes a supper boring story. The trade system is supper out of balance, and crafting makes no sense. You have to pay a lot for fast travel, so sometimes you waste good 10 minutes just to save your money.In the end the pleasant relaxed experienced that the game could offer is overpowered by a a childish fetch quests for no significant reward. I wouldn't buy it unless you are buying it for your little kids to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the previous Chibig's game, Deiland, despite its few flaws. It had a nice feel and some originality. So I backed their next project via Kickstarter, however when we got "Summer in Mara", it proved to be somewhat.. inadequate. Yes, this is a much bigger game than Deiland, with more things to do, a larger world, numerous characters and quests. However, after leaving the initial island, getting anything done becomes unproportionally difficult, you always lack money or resources and the knowledge what to do next. So, taking this into account, this is not a relaxing game. This is also no farm simulator, as farming seems to be quite optional. Therefore, thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game, I actually enjoyed it even though going in worried looking at reviews.I loved the artwork and even pretty much all the character designs in-game specially the "villains" of the game being my favourite.The game is pretty much do this for this person but the story pretty much tells you to help and give to others at the start. If you get bored of going from point A to point B and back then slow down and just enjoy other parts of the game. Go and plant on your island, replant the trees to your liking elsewhere, mass horde all the oranges or just travel across the ocean and steal from the islands. There is abit more to do than just be an errand girl.I enjoyed doing the quests for the characters, even those I hated but learnt to love later on in their quest line because you do learn about them. Often enjoyed doing a bunch of quests at once to save back-tracking and time.I enjoyed unlocking recipes and building more stuff for my island though I did not enjoy my chickens getting in the way of my button pressing. I used an Xbox controller so X does almost every action which is ok until you get animals and the chickens will follow you and instead of planting, you will feed them by mistake or pet them, an animation you cannot cancel. Little nitpick but would of been better if the chickens actually had a fenced area (and building one yourself they just go under it).The pirates were a little bugged, often getting too close will make the talk/shop command disappear, making me have to do a full circle multiple times just to re-talk to them.I not had my game crash or really any game breaking bugs so it ran fairly well for me in my 16 hours of playing.Last nitpick I guess is the other NPC's, they all stand in one area every single day and night not moving, would of been nice if the main town area had abit more life to it but the focus is mainly you and the other main characters.Is the game perfect? no, some islands seem bland and pointless part from a fruit but is it as bad as everyone says? no. It runs smooth and everything loads in fine with no issues and for the price asking, it is perfectly ok game to sit back with and just take it at your own pace.

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried to like this game but I'm struggling. It just seems like there are constant obstacles in your way. You have to repair a boat but to do this you need to make oars first (????) - why you need to do this I don't know as the boat apparently runs on fuel. You need board to make the oars but you've used up the board you had because you gave it to the creature from the light. Now you have no board to make the oars and the only way you can get the board from what I've seen is from the barrels that wash up. Guess what - no barrels. I will keep trying with it and if it improves I'll gladly change my view but for now I can't recommend it because of the constant dead-ends in the game. _childDocuments_.review: I was a bit skeptical to buy this at first because of the reviews, but I'm so glad that I did! So far it's everything I wanted and I feel like I've only just gotten past the beginning and into the main game. It's adorable, I LOVE the little short animations that go with the story, mechanics are all straight forward, and I'm so pumped to put probably 50 more hours into it. Thank you for this fantastic game, I needed something fresh and this was IT.Lots of people were complaining about invisible walls/ getting stuck and issues with controller connectivity. I see where the invisible walls are annoying, but we can't expect all games to allow us to travel like Skyrim does. The few times I've gotten stuck was because I jumped on something I should've just walked around and I've been able to wiggle myself out so far. As for the controller compatibility - I was able to fix this by going into settings (looking at Summer in Mara in your library), properties, then controller. From there I went to the link "Controller General Settings" and checked the boxes only for: guide button focuses steam, xbox config support, xbox extended feat support, and generic gamepad config support. I will say getting the controller to work was a HUGE game changer for me, so I understand why those who couldn't get it to work were upset. I hope my fix recommendation for the controller support helps, I was able to find the tip through a google search.

_childDocuments_.review: I fully recommend this game as long as you know what it is you are buying.Summer in Mara is a farming/exploration game with some light crafting elements.  It recalls other titles such as Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, or Rune Factory.  I would say that Summer in Mara is quite a bit more laid back than these other titles, though.  It’s quite a bit easier and not nearly as grindy.  This is not a game for you if you are looking for a full-on farm management game.  There’s only a handful of spots to grow crops or raise animals.  Animals don’t really need to be fed and crops grow just fine without water; they all grow a bit faster with care, though.  No tedious watering cans; just hold a bucket of water over your head and run around on top of your beets and potatoes.  Want to leave your island farm for 2 in game weeks while you go exploring?  No worries!There is a day/night cycle in this game, and an energy mechanic, but they are similarly forgiving.  From what I can tell so far, there are no timed tasks such as in a Harvest Moon game and no limits on the game overall.  There is no calendar, no such thing as a Sunday where all the stores are closed.  If you are out and about and you do not make it back home in time, the only penalty for sleeping outside is you have a bit less energy the next day.  Eat a few apples and you are A-OK again.So it’s just a super laid back game where you run around doing errands for folks, explore islands, and gradually learn to craft new things.  You’re not punished for making mistakes and you are not incentivized to min/max your economy.The soundtrack is super ultra catchy, especially the main theme, and the protagonist Koa is heart-meltingly charming.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is super charming and I really enjoyed it. The character design is wonderful, and the dialog is well-written, giving each character a distinctive voice, personality, history, and motivations. The music is excellent and really enhances the mood. I am especially fond of Dunna's theme, which is beautiful and does an amazing job of expressing her personality and the internal tension she feels.The gameplay is not bad per se, but it is quite shallow and unoriginal, and contradicts the moral of the story. The story tells you that you should respect nature and not overexploit it, but the gameplay treats nature like a bunch of machines for producing and converting resources, with no negative consequences for exploiting them as much as possible. Many other games are the same way, so it's not like Chibig are evil. I think they have good intentions, I only wish they had been able to create more nuanced and innovative gameplay that supports the story. Perhaps for such a small team, they attempted too many different features (crops, animals, trees, mining, fishing, diving, treasure hunting, crafting, building, boating, exploring, delivering, etc.), so they were not able to focus on making any feature very deep or original.Nevertheless, there is a lot to love about Summer in Mara, and I recommend it, especially if you are looking for a relaxing and peaceful game with interesting characters and good music.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl:dr The game is a buggy mess and it's entirely possible for you to get 15 minutes into the game only to have to restart or 15 hours into the game and have to restart. Wait to buy this one until more time has passed if you can't pass it up. So typically I don't post reviews on here, especially negative ones yet sadly I can't honestly recommend anyone play this game. My first experience with this game was actually downloading the Prologue which I tried to play through twice. Both times I got to a certain part of the quest where I was required to build a torch, I would build said torch, and the game would be complete unresponsive, couldn't open menus, couldn't move, had to Alt+F4. This is where I should have walked away, but I had been watching the game on Kickstarter for awhile and decided it was probably just a bug with the Demo, that the full release would be more stable. Sadly, I was wrong, about 30 minutes into playing the game I had a NPC give apparently give me a quest, not that I knew it because the game decided to not display any of the dialogue associated with the quest. As i went about opening a chest I was told to open, I found it empty, not items added to inventory, but my quest objective changed to meet the quest giving NPC by the "Guardian Door" I did this, only to be told I needed to open the chest....you see the issue? So I restart the game, for the 2nd time now, get back to that point, and when I open the chest, a slew i dialogue comes at me that i never got before, and I get the item in the chest. I thought, "Okay, minor issue but it was early enough on, no problem, lets keep going" Fast forward 4 hours into the game, and once again I am in a loop of an NPC telling me I need to do something I have already done, with no way to progress any. Again I should walk away but I decide to give the game one more chance. Reset my save data once again, only to have the original bug of the empty chest stop me after resetting my game progress for a third time. Overall the art is pretty. The concept seems fun. The game seems like a solid relaxing experience, but the it is just far too buggy to justify sinking any more time into it. Especially when the developer has acknowledged there are bugs they just "can't fix" because they don't know whats causing them. It's a huge bummer and I was really hoping this game would be something worthwhile, sadly, in it's current state it's just not.

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is an adventure game that has elements in the farming sim genre. All your usual's are here; farming, fishing, tending to animals, building things on your own island but It shines best as a exploration game.Pros:- A wide varied map broken down into squares. You unlock the map in three tiers as you upgrade your boat. The islands are mostly unique with Koa usually having something to say about each of them.- The characters and stories are decent. Don't expect stellar writing or mystifying twists but the heart of the story in my opinion is childlike adventure and freedom, Koa nailed it completely. Several story arcs were memorable.- A wide variety of crops to plant and things to build on your home island. There is a fair bit of customisationCons:I have to dedicate a paragraph to this because it stands out first and forth most from the moment you even start playing the game. This game has a lot of heart and soul put in to it but isn't a professionally made game. It is rough round the edges.You can tell when basic features like being able to view the key binds while playing the game isn't present. You have to exit to main menu to access the key binds. When you exit the game and come back, the day will have progressed. Your energy would be restored and the game plonks you at some spawn point. This even goes as far down as things like signposting. I can imagine a lot of players will get to Qälis and get thrown off; your map isn't like a minimap. It doesn't show you were individual characters are, you have to find them. Then they show up on the map. Mun was a particularly bad case of this, I didn't know she existed until I started achievement hunting, I had to crack out a wiki to know where she was. The game won't tell you to talk to her. (also, You can talk to the pirates, they aren't pirates in the traditional sense. Most people would associate pirate to avoid. This game wants you to run up to them and talk and get quests of them)The gameplay loop also eventually breaks down into. Grow X, Make Y, Go to Z. Repetitive. There are a few times that the game will make you run around Qälis. Just delivering stuff and talking to people. If you don't enjoy the setting or characters or theme the devs are going for here. It's going to spin you out of the game fast.  ConclusionSummer in Mara is a very indie game. I'd say it is feature complete but Do not get this game expecting a AAA or even AA experience. I'd rate it a single A if there is a bracket for that. It is very rough around the edges but for me. The setting, the theme and the story and I can see the heart of and soul poured into this game. That made it enjoyable for me.I'd rate it on the PiratePants scale a tentative 6 maybe a 7 out of 10. I think it's worth it's £15 but get it on sale if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, and it has a very summer-y positive aesthetic, but ultimately was hollow, repetitive and a buggy mess.Good art, amateur design. Bugged quest logic, breaking when you do things in an order the game doesn't expect you to, making at best the story gibberish, at worst completely bricking the game, forcing a complete restart. All sense of exploration is thus neutered, as you are constantly worrying that you'll break quests by progressing past where the game thinks you should be.Turns into a very rigid and mechanical "cook up this thing to that person".Very catchy traveling music though.

_childDocuments_.review: The heart of Summer in Mara is good. In the farming/resource management crafting games I've played, I know I've wanted for a while to see mechanics that reflect more responsibility to nature, and this game tries to deliver on that. It's a cute game with nice music and good intention, but it just seems to be lacking something to make it more fun. Something about it just made me feel rushed to finish with nowhere to really go and no one to talk to after the story was completed. My personal highlight is that it let me pet dogs and rats, and my personal gripe is that it wouldn't let me eat raw lemons like the child I'm supposed to be. It's a decent game to relax to, but I would recommend waiting for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics and music are really nice on the island. 2D animations and drawings are just amazing.But graphics in the city are not good at all, all walls seems flat, they could at least use texture to fake depth. That's tip of the iceberg, artists are very good but developers are not. They never played a PC game before to create such horrible keyboard bindings (and you can't rebind them). If you have not a qwerty keyboard it's over, they dont know what a keyboard layout is .... I had to play with controller which has standard bindings, very easy to use. On the matter of gameplay, game is very shallow. It's just a giant fetch quest game. You go to a NPC which ask you to craft something, you go back to your island, craft, go back to NPC, go back to island, go back to NPC etc .... Farming is pointless, just used to make components to craft ONE time per crop. After some time you have NPC who move and you dont know where to find them, you have to go to every island to see if they are here.....As another review said : "There's nothing to do outside of fetch quests that feel meaningless after they are completed. It's a bad farming/crafting game and also a bad adventure/RPG"If you want a good farming/RPG game, play portia or stardew valley. _childDocuments_.review: An adventure game about a girl named Koa living with her aunt on a lonely tropical island in the vast ocean, who wants to explore the world by farming and crafting. All that is required of us is to arrange a life on our own island, taking into account the time of day and climatic conditions: planting and harvesting fresh crops, caring for and feeding local animals, catching fish for our subsistence, making useful tools for mining resources, building structures out of various materials. We will do it in order to go on a trip to his boat in search of new islands and in the hope of finding a treasure or solve any mystery, as well as to meet new interesting characters and establish trade with them, who can give new jobs or advice on how best to act in certain situations. But do not forget that not all of them are friendly. At one point in time, a sinister corporation will try to take over the whole archipelago of Mara, and our protagonist will have to protect all the inhabitants and her own island.The game will be remembered for its pleasant visual style, interesting characters and meditative soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: and now onto the short review//Description//Summer in Mara mixes farming, crafting and exploring mechanic in a tropical archipelago with a colorful style and strong narrative.//Graphics, Sound & Artstyle//Simply put this is a moving piece of art, it's Harvest Moon meets The Legend of Zelda: the Wind Waker. Everything about the artstyle is perfect- the score of the game brings it altogether to a perfect mix of nostalgia for me. I can't stress enough how wonderful it looks & sounds. //Gameplay//Summer in Mara has you play as Koa, a little girl rescued at sea by Yaya (who you now refer to as your grandma). She teaches you the importance of the cycle of life and nature while on your home island. You farm, cut trees for wood, forage for fruits, mine for minerals, make dishes, craft  build on your island & sail to explore new islands. Koa is an energetic little girl with the hops that would even make Michael Jordan envious. She controls smoothly and while appearing to never slowing down while sprinting and hopping all over the place, the stamina bar is there to limit that, only replenished by either sleep or eating. The world of Mara is your playground and there is a miriad of people or erm creatures that need your help- you'll go around cooking dishes, crafting items and harvesting crops for the inhabitants of Mara while trying to figure out life's answers, your grandmothers connection to the world, & helping your little buddy Napopo who suddenly drops onto your island. While some draw comparisons to Stardew Valley, being a Harvest Moon veteran- I feel like its more of the pace to the latter but not as in depth as either of the two.//Price//24.99 USD//How many hours estimated//Personally I am 12 hours into the game and I still have ways to go, I'd say I'm about 1/4th of the game in for reasons you will estimate and figure out on your own in the tutorial.//Final Thoughts//Summer in Mara is a special game, it's a game I will be showing to my kids in the future and not only because it is EXTREMELY easy but because of the messages it has in it. I was immediately sucked into the world of Mara leaving offerings and paying my respect to my elders, I felt like Koa was a character the inner child in all of us could relate to. However often times that immersion is broken by some gameplay elements that dont seem to be polished. The lack of calender or any indication on knowing what day it is, makes being a farmer that much harder especially when more of the map opens up for exploration. The sailing is monotamous early on, only slightly improving later by finding lost crates but often times containing useless items. The fact that you can only hold 99 of a single item and then being reset to 98 back up to 99 if you get anymore of said item, I mean Koa's backback is already on that Mary Poppin's level, why couldnt she hold 999 of a single item? I mean she can carry a whole oven in her backpack (early game mission) Oh- and the missions; most often they are unimaginative fetch quests that will have you running back and forth and sometimes even planting seeds that will take up to 10 in game days to harvest. A day can be taken off vegetation if you water the crop and water can be attained in a well but after the water runs out (3 buckets for a regular well) you'll have to wait for rain to fill it up, my first rainy day took about 4 hours into my playthrough to come and considering on average it rains about 149 days out of the year in the carribean- I would really like more rainy days in Mara. But despite all it's flaws, I'm still having a lot of fun with the game. When I first was granted access to the game about a week ago, there was  many more things wrong with the game but during this week the dev has been patching the game, listening & to feedback. I was playing the game on a gamepad & whenever trying to make multiple items on any type it would just send me to the next screen, well thats ironed out. The stamina bar would deplete relatively fast, making the player either have to go to sleep or eat, well that's fixed. I had to redo parts of this review because the dev has been on top of the game breaking mechanics. I have faith that they can polish what I believe to be the surprise summer hit of 2020. It's quirky- the characters are cute, funny or sometimes just downright mean. In my humble opinion it's far better experience than Animal Crossing New Horizons, and for the asking price I don't think it's unreasonable.  Take into consideration that it's aimed to be a more lax game, more suitable for children. Still I say it's definately a  Buy Now from me.

_childDocuments_.review: 👎 I don't want to write a full review for this game, but I do want to give this game a thumbs down to help the games ratings because I think this game fails a bit on what it sets out to do, but if you're in a SPECIFIC TARGET AUDIENCE it's pretty good 👎I'm still in the middle of my playthrough at 26 hours in. But at this point it's blatantly clear that the cards have been out on the table for a long time now and I can write a review because it's candidly clear how the rest of the experience is going to play out.Summer in Mara is just Fetch Quests: The Game. If you are not on board with that. Do not buy this game, period.I wouldn't even pay attention to the tags because it's not even really a farming game either. It seems like it's going to be, but in reality it's just a trading game with endless fetch quests. This game has a remarkably tight economy, which I deeply appreciate in games because even if you get 'rich', you're always two or three shopping sprees from being incredibly broke again just like the start of the game, except with a little easier time of getting back into the market. Whereas in most other games when you get rich, money has very little meaning to you anymore. Anything you want, you have, and you'll never have to scrounge for cash again.In reality, the game is just about hoarding resources and carefully selecting which ones you're willing to sell off for money to get other resources for quests, or future quests. Pretty much every interaction in this game should be viewed with a transactional mindset.The writing in this game most of the time is pretty good, the reason you play this game boils down you wanting to play a game that requires very little motor skills to play, not a ton of thinking to what you're doing, and wanting to engage in a vibrant colorful world with good characters. As well as fairly slow-paced laid-back gameplay. And the game delivers on that front.It's not a grand adventure game, it's not a farming sim, it's not really even a crafting game either. At least not as I know it. Everything you do just is to meet the demands of quests, not for your gain and benefit of growing a trending machine that yields increasing rewards.The music is pretty alright, though serviceable at worst a fair bit of the time. The game is vibrant and pretty with a likeable cast of characters (though are pretty terrible people when you think about it demanding so much of a young child who's probably not even 12 or 11.)I think the game could have benefitted from giving you upgrades to speed or vehicles because as the game goes on, the running speed just gets incredibly wearisome as you blaze over the same trodden ground for the literal 200th time and counting.Summer in Mara, is a pretty decent game, going off the steam page of what it tries to be. I think it fails a bit, it seems and sounds like it's going to be more than it is, but it's just not. If you want a nice game of endless fetch quests with otherwise undemanding gameplay, I mean sure go for it. It's nice and the setting is good. Wish they did a bit more with the gameplay though, it just does not pan out I think as they were hoping. There's just not many times i'd ever catch myself relaxingly fishing or something because even getting bait costs quite a bit of money, therefore locking it out of my mind unless for a quest.

_childDocuments_.review: art direction and characters are beautiful but literally every other aspect of this game kinda sucks.i did not experience any game breaking bugs, but there is an obvious lack of polish on the game. spelling mistakes and unclear instructions sometimes. i've skipped ahead in quests by accident before. the 3d graphics look kinda terrible compared to the 2d sprites. sound design (including music) is genuinely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for lack of a better fitting term. the story is ok, the characters are a hit or miss but i generally liked them.i haven't even mentioned the gameplay. all the classic mechanics are there; farming, animal husbandry, mining, fishing and building. they're all extremely shallow and not particularly fun. not to mention how the game is one massive fetch quest.the sailing, which should be the draw of this game, is a pain and i'm very glad that caleb can just take me places instead.i played the whole damn thing and i got 100% achievements. i only played for 18 hours but each session felt like literal years. it's very eh, just get it on sale if you really want to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna preface this by saying I'm usually not a big fan of quests and going back and forth between locations so don't be disappointed if you find my review harsh on that particular genre. Summer in Mara is a quintessential "go there, do that, unlock recipes game", something we've seen already god knows how many times. And to be fair a game like this is enjoyable to a certain point. After that it becomes dull and you get lost in pending errands you're bound to leave for later, because you have to prioritize those that push the story forward. This particular nature of such games takes away from the spirit and the magic of a true adventure story many people were hoping for upon seeing those absolutely gorgeous animated clips in the trailer. Don't get me wrong, a game where the story takes away from the playtime is by no means a good game in my book, however you never see the level of interaction you've hoped for after watching the trailer. Most of the time you do small tasks alone and your only companion stays on the boat and is just THERE, serves no real purpose at all apart from being a checkpoint for story progression. I really wanted to like this game more than I do now, however Summer in Mara is a few points short of being a great kid's game. With all that said it's time for the good aspects of it:- Animation, Environment, Design, everything is on point. The movement of the character is so smooth, both on keyboard and a controller that it leaves you wanting to play for hours just to admire the fluidity with which your character turns, jumps etc. The game is just pretty in the truest sense of the word.- The story is interlaced with educational dialogues and advices for smaller kids and if you by any chance have kids that are between 5-8, Summer in Mara is undoubtedly one of the most appropriate games I can recommend.- Price was something I was reluctant talking about, still I think depending on your expectations the price could be too high for some. That said for me it's the perfect middleground for a product like this, mainly because it doesn't break your bank and the incentive for the developers is reasonably high. Besides I've seen a lot worse at a bigger price so at the time I was writing this my "money:quality" ratio expectations were greatly altered.Should you buy it?If you enjoy cheerful, feel - good types of games that benefit from exploration and running chores, this is the game for you. Even if you aren't a hardcore gamer this game is something you can just play and enjoy it for what it is and it doesn't leave you with the feeling - "Oh I need to invest a couple of more hours in this in order to proceed". Just play it and have fun at your own pace :)

_childDocuments_.review: I *hate* having to leave a poor review as the basic concept of the game is really cute, the animated cutscene I saw when I noticed the game on Kickstarter was really good, but I can't recommend this.  It's just too broken.  Issues I encountered:1. Unclear directions.  I didn't even finish the tutorial section because it was so frustrating.  You get a quest from an NPC or just from your character talking to herself, and it immediately vanishes from the screen and you have to open the quest log to look at it.  I have an incredibly bad short-term memory and this was really annoying.   In addition, you frequently don't know how many of an item to get because the quest doesn't tell you - only when you try and hand it in does it not complete, indicating that you need more of whatever it is.  At one point I didn't have any quests at all and it was only when I looked back at the quest log that I realised I'd had one added without any indication or dialog.  And this was in the tutorial section which is supposed to be easy.2. The UI seems very simplistic - I'm assuming this has been ported from a console game? The UI looks like a placeholder to be honest, waiting for another pass to give it some life.  There's never an 'OK' button to exit menus - have to right-button click on the mouse which is very unintuitive.3. I have to hit space a lot to progress through conversations, as frequently there are only a few words per speech bubble.4. No ability to rebind keys and controls - this is really annoying.  To switch tools you have to use the mouse wheel.  Well, my mouse wheel is pretty dodgy, which means changing tools takes forever of scrolling and hoping that it'll register this time.5. The sound issues have been mentioned by others.  The music and sound fx volumes - which are only adjustable from the main menu - don't seem to bear any relation to what's in-game, and the UI for them is really bad - I didn't understand what levels I was setting them to - what's wrong with a percentage of max indicator?.In summary - my recommendation is to hold off until some of the issues have been resolved, unless you can get it for a knock-down price.  It just looks half-finished right now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is *rough*--not in terms of difficulty (there is none) but in terms of polish.  Even a casual eye will notice places where quests abruptly cut off with little explanation.  Physics errors abound.  Many objects have no physics meshes at all, including several tree types, while others have nonsensical meshes.  Multiple bugs require quitting to title to correct (for example, never fast-travel home while you have an animal in the boat unless you hate being able to see).  The farming mechanics are mediocre at best, and around midgame you'll probably stop using it altogether in favor of just stuffing your pig army with carrots to get enough truffles to break the economy.  All in all, this game could have used a couple more months to bugfix and a couple more beyond that to clean up rough patches so that it feels less like a shipped prototype and more like a finished game.So why am I recommending such a buggy, unfinished mess?  Because it's an endearing unfinished mess!  Despite my frustrations, I found myself getting engaged with the various characters and wanting to know what their hopes and dreams were and what I could do to help them along.  The world is compelling enough that I'm left a bit frustrated, wanting more in-depth exploration of its details--but that's probably beyond the scope of a game targeted at young audiences.  The music ranges from catchy to *stellar*.  The character portraits are top-notch.  Gaining access to new islands scratches that Wind Waker explorer's itch, at least up until a few of the last islands that seemed hastily thrown together.There are few genuine surprises here for a seasoned gamer, but it's a fun time nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: From the handful of hours I've played so far, the game is pretty addicting. It's a fun and cute way to pass the time. I love the music. I also really like the art style. This is probably more of a personal issue, but I can't stand just being able to just place anything anywhere without some type of snap grid system. I'm not quite OCD, but it annoys me when things don't lineup how I want them to. Everything just looks so haphazardly placed everywhere. - One of my biggest problems is how tedious they make it to pick up items. Not only do you have to click each tree or bush for it to drop the items, but then you have to go around and click on each individual item to pick them up. Why couldn't it just be a simple single click gather from a tree? Gets annoying when you've got +40 trees to click, where each drop 1 to 2 items you then also have to click. But even this I can get past, not too big of a deal.- My only deal breaker so far is the fact that it constantly crashes. I can usually get an hour or two in of gameplay before it crashes. The first couple of hours it was fine, no issues. Then all of a sudden it was crashing left and right. I can't stand that. I'll give it a couple of weeks before picking it back up again and see if some of the issues have been solved, but until then, I can't recommend the game in it's current state.

_childDocuments_.review: The launch of Summer in Mara, by the Spanish studio Chibig, could not have come at a better time. The whole adventure takes place on a set of paradisiacal islands and given the current circumstances in which the world is immersed, nothing better than to dive into a relaxed environment, without violence, and with the proper safety distance. This project was supported through the Kickstarter campaign and almost raised an astonishing € 300,000.The player plays the role of Koa, a girl who was abandoned by her parents and adopted by her grandmother, a ladyfish of the liquid species, called Yaya Haku. It turns out that Yaya Haku is a very restrictive character, so she never let Koa travel outside of her island. On this island, there is a portal shrouded in mystery that is closed, and that holds a secret that only Yaya Haku knows.Unfortunately, one day Koa’s life receives bad news. Her grandmother embarks on a mysterious mission and has not returned to the island. Now the Mara Ocean is in danger since a mysterious corporation arrived on planet Qü, attracted by a strange energy emerging from the oceans. They want to dominate and exploit all of Mara’s resources.At the beginning Summer in Mara manages to print the adventurous spirit and graphics of titles such as Zelda. However, in this case, the feeling of progression is not so satisfactory, but it still works. This is a title that mixes humans, fish, cats, aliens, and other beings without anyone questioning or feeling less well about it.The gameplay is centered on a mix of adventure and an agricultural simulator. The vast ocean has space for several islands that can be visited, with different items and arrangements. Still, there is a feeling of emptiness, largely due to the half-naked environment.The island of Koa serves as the main point for farming, raising animals, fishing, creating new tools, and even cooking food that helps it to recover the “stamina” bar, which, by the way, is consumed quite quickly, and they satisfy the hunger. If the “stamina” bar is completely consumed, Koa passes out and starts immediately the next day, with only a portion of this bar available. Each food, or cooked dish, is equivalent to different recovery values ​​for these two premises.The whole idea of ​​Summer in Mara is trying to relax the player with calm gameplay. Although on paper it seems to be a very promising concept, in practice it leaves much to be desired. All the missions presented to the player give the idea that Koa is a girl of errands and the fact that one has to get on the boat, sail from island to island in an expressionless ocean every time an NPC asks for a fruit or vegetable that needs to be cultivated, is, in fact, a very frustrating point.Still touching this point, all the products planted, except for the fruits and the trees, have a number above the plantation indicating how many days it will take until it is possible to harvest them. It is still possible to use elements like fertilizers or water that will speed up this whole process. It is also possible to speed up the whole process if you sleep, this will advance the current day. There are no months or seasons, so there are no specific foods.That said, the problem is that there is no meaning whatsoever during the “days” lost in the loop between islands and long waits during the gestation of the planted products.Regardless of the time, you spend off the island, there is no sense of loss. The animals continued to live and the entire plantation will not be overdue, even if it is ready to be harvested. This title does not encourage the player to play optimally, among resources, share costs, and the benefits that these could bring him.Regarding history, it has no rhythm or emotion and is easily overlooked. While 2D drawings are quite vivid and expressive, all 3D models of the characters have no expression whatsoever. The world itself is perhaps the point in favor. Although it is often stripped of NPC’s, tropical environments are able to convey a sense of serenity.Unfortunately, Summer in Mara does not present anything new to the already huge catalog of games of this genre. Its mechanics of super repetitive missions, very simplistic gameplay, and a story with little weight can transport moments of some frustration.Check more recommendations from Exile

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! Its biggest strength is its world. The art style, music, characters and islands are beautiful and charming, which made exploring the map a relaxing experience. I thought it struck a nice balance between being simple yet still engaging. I was interested in the main story and I enjoyed meeting all of the new characters and seeing their side stories interwoven with the main quest.I was hesitant to buy it because of how many reviews talked about the monotony of fetch quests. I don't necessarily disagree -- gameplay definitely consists of traveling around fetching objects for your character or the characters she's helping -- but, I didn't feel it became tedious or boring or too drawn-out. If you check in with multiple main characters, you can easily organize your trip so you're gathering multiple objects in an efficient way and progressing multiple stories at the same time. I enjoyed the time/resource-management aspect of planning what I needed and what was the best route to go about getting it. If you're looking for something more high-energy, this isn't it, but if you're looking for something simple and relaxing, this game has that element of feeling satisfied by checking off lists -- meeting objectives, completing buildings, collecting animals and crops, etc.  The actual traveling around for quests by sailing "feels" good, for lack of a better way to describe it. It took me a minute to get used to navigating with the compass, but otherwise, there's no real gameplay or challenge to it -- it's just nice to sail around the ocean. The fishing minigame is fun and not hard to master.I also want to praise the game for its themes of taking care of the environment and your community. It's subtle, but the game tells you through story that it's important to give back to the world, and it rewards you through gameplay if you follow through.I definitely recommend this if you're looking for a peaceful, charming exploration game with a solid story. I enjoyed my time with it and will likely keep playing post-game now that I've beaten the story because it's relaxing and plays well while listening to or watching something else in the background.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is often frustrating in ways that it doesn't need to be, like the fishing mini-game.  I did eventually complete it everywhere I needed to, but I didn't enjoy it and I'm pretty sure there's a lot of luck involved in successfully fishing.  Sometimes it just swings so wildly that it's not possible to complete it.There's a *ton* of traveling back and forth.  Many of the quest descriptions seem a little vague, and the map pointer sometimes isn't useful.But my biggest problem with the game is that literally every single quest is a "fetch quest".  Someone tells you want they want, and you go bring it back.  You get every recipe from someone who wants something from you involving that recipe.  Tools upgrades are locked behind quests that often have nothing to do with the tool.  And I'm not even sure why you'd care about some of the upgrades.Building/planting on the island is often frustrating because it often wants you to pick flatter land, or you can only build a building in a certain location, but the game doesn't tell you where.  (Hint:  It's often along the coastline of your island.)I think the quest problems aren't solvable without a total rework, but the other problems can probably be fixed fairly easily.  If you *really* love these kinds of games, it's probably worth your money.  Otherwise, I doubt you'll feel terribly positive about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Mara is a game with a lot of heart that does so many annoying things that I have to wonder if the devs ever really played through it.It's got charming characters and locations, some interesting ideas in the writing, worldbuilding, and character conflicts, and it's cute and charming aplenty.Yet the actual gameplay is literally all fetch quests. All game, the entire game, go grow, craft, or buy some object and bring it back here. Most of these fetch quest require you to sail home, plant some seeds, wait some number of days, because that's all you've really got going on at home, and then sail back and drop it off, which unlocks the next fetch quest in the chain.A lot of the charm in other cutesy farming style games is how much you've got going on, and the steady march of time encouraging you to make the most of your days -- every day, you're given a new field to play with, ripe with opportunities and choices of how you want to spend your time.On paper, Mara seems like it might do that. It's got fishing, diving for treasure, chatting with locals, sailing, treasure hunts, and more. But it shoots itself in the foot by being too limiting, both in how you engage with these systems, as well as the demands the game asks of you. Each diving spot in the game, you go into once, get the unique item in there that someday, someone will ask you to fetch, and then there's very little reason to ever go back. Each fishing node costs bait, gives a max of 3 or so casts, and then takes what I assume is real-world hours to respawn, if it respawns at all. And until someone asks for that specific kind of fish, it's useless to you -- too hard to acquire to risk selling, but with nothing else to do but become inventory rot.To say nothing of the controls, which are non-rebindable, and I found annoying on both keyboard and controller. It just feels inept.I really wanted to like Summer in Mara, but instead of being a cute relaxing experience, it's an exercise in tedium. The market is becoming saturated with games like this, and unfortunately, Mara is just another one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: the game looks extremely cute, but actually playing the game feels almost miserable.a lot of the mechanics arent really explained that well, so youre left scrambling trying to figure things out on your own. as well, the map is a nuisance to use. there's no "you are here" feature, so you have to try to piece together where to are on your own. the diving mechanic is painfully done, and the fishing mechanic isnt all that great either.the game feels incredibly empty. everywhere you go, the world just feels...empty. theres a lot of open space, there are very few non-interactable townspeople and even fewer npcs that you can talk to and trade with. they all feel really bland and void of life. there really doesnt feel like theres any sense of direction in the game. sure, you have quests to do. but those quests are incredibly boring and often youre just waiting around while trying to complete the quests. a bunch of the quests also have hidden pre-requisites, things like getting recipes/items from other characters' quests, higher level tools, an upgraded boat/map expansion. basically, you have to do the vast majority of the quests in order to complete the other quests. you dont need to 100% the game in order to complete the main storyline, but there is a decent chunk of the main story that relies on other quests to make progress.the game overall just feels empty and unfinished, like theres a lot that could and should be added to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game. I backed it a little over a year ago, and I'd been looking forward to it, but  I wouldn't recommend it at present. I have 2 main gripes - first of all, it desperately needs some QOL changes. There is no fast travel, only one place you can craft, I can't open my menus when I'm in my boat, I can't get into my boat unless I jump into it which (since you can't jump when you're in the water) means sometimes you simply can't get in the boat. There is a map for the main town which doesn't show your location (so I don't know where things are relative to me), there's no compass (so when someone tells me I need to go West, I have precisely zero idea which way that is), the menu system is clumsy and unintuitive, sometimes character portraits cover the materials you need for a quest so you can't see exactly what you need.... the list goes on; these are really just the things I can think of off the top of my head.The game also seems to be quite buggy at present. I currently have 2 quests which I can't finish. Someone has asked for an item, but when I talk to them they just tell me to go away (I have the item in my inventory). For the other, I had to build a fire on my island. I have now built 2, but it hasn't registered at all. Personally, I'm not too bothered about repetitive fetch quests (although it does feel a little soulless) but the points above just mean that I'm not going to continue playing at present, although I'll try again at a later date.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this game, but within only 30 minutes I noticed serious quality issues.A quick read of the community forum and other reviews and I can clearly see that there are far, far too many bugs and issues.Some personally notable issues I had:* No sensitivity option.* UI/UX is very poor.
