_childDocuments_.review: A charming game with unique characters. The story took me by surprise since I went in to this blind thinking it was just a farm-esque game. If you don't like constantly running back and forth to advance the plot, you won't like this. Most quests are very quick to complete though (getting the materials requested), so I didn't mind doing the fetch quests, especially when i had the money to quick travel.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Because that is what the majority of the game teaches you what you need to do. There are several islands you can travel to, each beautiful in their own ways and exploring those is really satisfying. When you approach the islands, your first idea would be "hm, these islands are pretty small" untill you set foot on them. And the inhabitants, some contribute towards your involvement of the story directly, while others need something before they open up their mouths. Things like, which you can provide, but you need to go back to your island and get into farming those required items. Chop wood, collect stone, oranges, grapes, etc... Craft stuff too. In the beginning you start quite limited, but more recipes get unlocked when you get deeper in the story.You got a house in which you can sleep, cook and craft. Cooking is needed, because you get hungry from time to time. And sleeping is needed, because Koa has just a certain amount of energy to spend. Great kids game, no swearing, no double meaning behind things, but also great for adults. When it's raining, you can fetch mushrooms all over the place. Respecting nature, you chop a tree, say "thank you tree" and replant a seed. A little girl, on a small but fair sized island. On which she can expand. Because its not just a house and a few plots. Eventually she will bring pigs and sheep to the island, more buildings, more plots, more everything. Not unlimited, like you can only plant up to 33 trees in total. But that is more then enough to fill your grindy belly!We can overcome the grindyness to treat ourselves by exploring 20 more islands and more then 300 quests. So not ALL is lost...Accompanied with beautiful animation from which we are customed to Studio Ghibli and for so far, one the BEST anime related games out there on the market! Everything is well designed, up to a very acceptable range of detail. There are quite a lot of silent parts, I wish the music was a constant thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for a time waster/reality distraction. It got 40+ hours out of me, so I did enjoy it!I suppose I came into this, expecting a much broader experience than the game gave. There is no friendship/relationship system. No exp, levels, skills. The quests are all primarily fetch questions; Even main story quests. You can fish, farm, cook, build, but the only motivating factor to do any of it is to complete a quest or achievement. There's little to no re-playability once you complete it. Quests are the only driving point in the game, so once those are gone (or if you're stuck on one or two) there's nothing else to do of any significance.I recommend it as a one-and-done type of game. Questing is (mostly) rewarding, the visuals are really nice, and the music is relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend the game to an adult, I'd tell them it's a kid's game and let them make the choice. I would recommend it to kids. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! While I had some minor complaints I don't feel like they greatly impacted the overall game play or feel of the game. Issues I would love to see fixed are diving mechanics, some small bugs, and showing the wrong button for an action such as saying press a as if it were on a console controller instead of PC.I also wish that fences contained animals, that there was a way to put pigs back in the pen after opening it, and for there to be a way to sell off animals as I accumulated too many. I really enjoyed exploring and the characters. The freedom of the island designing was great. I loved decorating my island and planting a tree orchard. I was happy with how big the game was and I got lots of enjoyment out of it, but I would of course love even more to do. I'd be happy if they ever expanded the game, such as making a DLC with more quests, more build-able items to decorate your island, and possibly even more places to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I quite liked the idea of this as a very relaxing and chill and alternative to something like Stardew Valley, with no combat, lush art and lots of colourful characters to interact with.While I've largely enjoyed the moment to moment gameplay, the one thing that really spoils the game for me is that pretty much every character you meet is an absolute, selfish ♥♥♥♥. Nobody in this world ever gets anything done by themselves, and everyone is very keen to exploit the sweat and blood of a little girl at the blink of an eye.Even the 'nice' characters who are supposedly cheerful and friendly will ask you to do things like go and buy them some produce from the market and, when you do, the idea of actually compensating you for the items that you have either bought or grown yourself, never ever crosses their minds. Everyone is content to take things from you and give you nothing in return, often without even being thankful.It might seem like a small thing, but the entire world actually feels extremely, ruthlessly capitalist in a very unpleasant way. Everyone seems to be in it largely for their own gain and self-interest, whereas I would expect people to me more helpful and friendly, with more of a communal spirit, especially when dealing with an eight year-old girl who apparently lives all by herself and has no one to help her. It is deeply dispiriting and disheartening.This extends even to the farming mechanics - while 'wild' crops like apples and berries produce fruit and seeds that can be replanted to spread that crop, all of the vendors only ever sell Monstanto-level genetically modified terminator seeds, meaning that none of your crops ever produce seeds that can be replanted: whether carrots, potatoes, or cabbage or anything else, if you want to grow more of them, you have to buy more seeds from the merchants, you can't keep farming them self-sufficiently.It's certainly a believable world that Summer in Mara creates, but it is deeply bleak and unwelcoming, especially for a small child by their lonesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I was a Kickstarter backer for this game and only just now got around to play and beating them game after the initial reception. Boy howdy they weren't wrong. Summer in Mara had so much potential but ultimately is ruined by lack of polish and a more careful handling of the English Translation.  I found myself in cycles of bored, invested, bored again. I stuck it out because I wanted to see how the story ended only to be horribly let down. Is there a conclusion to the conflict? Barley. I got out in 22 hours, which is quite speedy for what I'm seeing from other players. It wasn't worth it.Ultimately it was just a lot of going back in forth in fetch quests in overly large empty maps. The 2d art was adorable, and I enjoyed the world building and character design, but they were all let down by lackluster game play and horrible balancing for item trees and when you got recipes. The Ending was incredibly unfulfilling after so much build up. If you want to just boat around in a lot of nothingness blue, pick up the game on deep discount. I think it is very telling that Koa's next game is a action platformer and not another 'farming' game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is stupendously relaxing and if you like cute games with farming and exploration mechanics, then you'll 100% want to play this one. The art is great, the gameplay is smooth, and the story is engaging. There is zero pressure to complete missions and you get rewarded for being curious, trying different things, and exploring. Mistakes are fairly easily corrected if they're made and learning to work within the games limits is also quickly done with not-so-harsh penalties if you do mess up. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically though,  is a kid-friendly farm adventure game, featuring simple quests to complete, a farm to develop and maintain, relaxing music and gameplay, and of course, a (seemingly) very young protagonist; an orphan girl by the name of Koa, who was adopted and raised by her Yaya Hoku. The game is all about Koa's adventures and discoveries, and her many interactions with various interesting characters as she sails away the only home she knew...  well, temporarily, since she always could come home.Extended gameplay so feel free to skip around :)+ Beautiful graphics and relaxing music. One of the tunes reminded me so much of Stranded Sails and Songbird Symnphony, both of which are among my favourite games!+ Thank goodness for being able to sprint. However, is it possible to make it toggle on and off instead? My ring finger on my left hand is cramping up a bit after a long Summer in Mara gaming session. Maybe put it as an optional setting?+ It's great that my crops will still mature, albeit much slowly, even though I don't water them - my farm experienced an extended drought unfortunately+ Can fish. The octopus one can be very hard though. I've only managed to catch one for a quest and that's about it.+ Love the variety of crops, fishes and materials. The crafting part is a bit limited though. Would be nice if players are able to craft some (more) decor as well.+ Has an energy system that can be supplemented with food... and yes, you can cook better food items too.+ I reckon there are 4 different locations for you to visit in this game. I've only unlocked Qalis so far.+ The story is alright here, but some parts of the story doesn't really makes much sense but the game delivers it in a matter-of-fact way. The pace can be a bit slow as well. I'd even say that the overarching story seems to be set on pause ever since I've reached Qalis and started doing all the quests there - because it's interjected with mini-stories from side quests.+ Kid-friendly gameplay. In fact, the game is so simple to play, anyone can play it.+ I can't tell how many hours I'll get out of this game as of yet, but since I reckon I'm only 1/4 through the game, seems like the game's worth its full price. Though, of course, a nice 15% launch discount doesn't hurt.- Can be a little bit grindy. It all depends on your tolerance level of when grinding/farming stuff. Personally, I don't mind - MMOs have trained me well - but I know of many people who would grumble.- Please add in an effect to show that the crops are fertilized, like sparkles and stuff. If there's an effect, please make it more prominent. I couldn't tell if the fertilizer did anything for my crops.- Feedback: The crab-mail quest is bugged - though in a way that's beneficial to the player I guess. I've managed to complete the quest simply by "re-reading" the letter for the same 2 crabs by the beach. I've, in total, found 3 crab-mails though. Not sure where the other 2 are.Summer in Mara is very similar to Stranded Sails in several ways, except that you're not building a community of islanders but rather you're playing as a self-sufficient young girl who's not only eager to explore the world, despite her early reservations; she also is taught by her beloved grandmother to always help people who needs her help and that's exactly what she's doing. It's a relaxing and fun game that's suited for both adults and kids alike. It's definitely getting a recommended from me! P/S: If you're still on the fence about the game, I'd highly recommend checking out the  first before buying to avoid getting disappointed. You'll basically get to play the first 20 minutes or so of the game and it's a good way for you to get a feel for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I went into it expecting something like Yonder but ended up with a game that makes every simple task a chore. Fishing needs bait, and each area needs THE RIGHT bait, and wells can actually run dry on water and require rainwater to be filled, which isn't something the game told me beforehand and has affected my food supply. There is no confirmation screen on crafting, meaning menu drag caused me to craft the wrong item once and required me to go out and chop down another tree to get the right amount of wood for the right item, and on top of that, I played for over an hour without getting off the starting island. This is while not taking my time.I got bored.This is all on top of forcing you to pass out at night, which is an extremely annoying thing devs throw in their games when they want to meter how far the player is able to travel in a day. There isn't another reason for doing it except to keep you from exploring too much. It breaks the flow of a game and is explicitly NOT FUN in games designed around fetch quests.If the goal was to make every simple task an annoying chore just to avoid the player getting through them too quickly, congrats, you've succeeded in making this player quit instead.Still better than Deiland though, but the bar was literally on the floor there since I dropped that game after 10 minutes. At least this one doesn't have mobile-style timers, I guess? Small victories.Really, just play Yonder if you're looking for something relaxed. You can chain quests and hoard inventory decently well so as far as fetch quest games go, it has a reasonable amount of QoL to make it possible to binge without getting frustrated.

_childDocuments_.review: Fully completed the achievements on this game. Would I recommend this game? Yes, but not to everyone. It's ok as an indie title and was clearly an early title for the dev. Wouldn't buy it unless it was on sale for more than 50% off.All in All score: 6.5/10Read on for longer review.Gameplay: 7/10It has some fun elements but the game loop is a little... boring. Travel to get quests, travel home, get items, travel to complete quest. The only reason you do anything is to complete the quests. Many of the islands in the game are for merely collecting resources a couple times and then never needed again. There's very little reason to go to them after the initial visit and you collect the single unique resource and then bring it back to grow on your island. They're also pretty bland for the most part. maybe there's an npc or an empty house, but not a lot going on. The only reason i wouldn't lower this score is because building things on your island and seeing your island grow was mildly fun, despite the appearance of freedom to design your island being fairly limited (because that's a big part of farming/life sims). pretty much placement of trees and a few objects was the only way to customize your island. There were a few bugs here and there but nothing terrible.Story and Characters: 4/10The story is only mildly interesting, Moana has to go and find the 4 hearts of Tafiti so the spirit thing can somehow (this part wasn't very clear) stop the colonizers from sucking the planet dry of resources. Don't worry we don't suck the planet dry... 'cause respawn and what not. The characters were mostly bland and mostly forgettable or a** holes. Here's looking at you Edegar the Edger and the b****y sisters. A big part of life sims is having interesting, and at least some likable, characters.art: 8/10Art was one of the aspects that drew me to this game. Art was nice and i liked the bright colors of Mara, it reminded me of Wind Waker, and the animation was my favorite part, which there was some so ill give them that.

_childDocuments_.review: This is att the same time one of the hardest, and easiest reviews I've ever written. I'll do a vid on this game when time and opportunity arrives.Where this opinion is coming from: My first video game system was the original Pong console in about 1975. Since then, Zelda. Final Fantasy, Might and Magic, EQ2, DnD, Diablo, Minecraft, 7 Days to Die, Ark Survival Evolved, Guild Wars 2, etc. I love adventure/survival games, complete with recipes, hundreds of quests when offered, and the genuine sense of exploration. Exploration being #1. What's over the next hill? What's around the next curve? What's on the next island, as it was in this game.To the devs: Amazing job and thank you so much. I have SO many games to offer me the fear of my demise around each corner as I venture forth on my journey. Still, I always wanted a game where my demise was never there, and the game contained absolutely NO combat, just that sense of wits to progress and find out what was around the next bend, yet, where I controlled the character in real time and sought ingredients, and materials, while growing said materials, (i.e. crops from farming, wood from trees). At... My.. Own... Pace... Most important. A chill game when needed, a constant adventure when ya slam the pedal to the metal. That's what I found with your game devs. That's what I found here.For anyone reading this, as I'm sure is done for an opinion, mine is this: If you enjoy the type of game I just described, and you find that you'd like to chill with no death threat in-game, while still enjoying that sense of adventure, this game is for you. Easiest way I can say it.Again, Great job devs on a "little game that could", that surpasses AAA games in many, many ways.The main thing I consider when playing ANY game, like many others I would guess, is... Do I want to keep playing? I do, I will, and I am excited to do so.\m/
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Koa is an adorable little girl, alone and abandoned, saddened by life, she has to survive alone and will discover the world with a personality that makes her mercilessly loveable.This game can be played by adults and children alike, so I suggest you do as I did and take the time to play it with your children.Koa evolves in a world that seems hostile but doesn't wish her any harm. Your children can play and learn, but some parts of the game can be very repetitive.There's a lot of back-and-forth to accomplish missions that sometimes seem pointless and children find it hard to understand the reason for doing them, and the boat trips are useful to the game but too frequent and repetitive.The characters who evolve in Mara's world are great and bring a lot to the story, some of whom are very popular with children.Very colorful and fun to play, the graphics are perfect for a children's game.The game is very smooth and bug-free.Koa is probably the most charming hero I've ever met in a video game. We'd love to have more of her.But...This game is a little long for children, the quests are too long and sometimes the children get stuck, it would have been nice to create simplified methods to allow some quests to be completed more quickly while keeping the interaction with the characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost; if you are looking into playing this game, you have either played Stardew Valley, or are familiar with it. Well, this is not Stardew Valley, so do not go into it thinking you will be playing a similar game.  While there are aspects of farming, crafting, fishing, mining, exploring, etc, I would say this game is more story/task based.  The artwork is absolutely fantastic.  I have a huge pet peeve of where I see the cover of a game and it looks amazing, but then when I go to play it I am playing as a 2d stick figure.  You will NOT be disappointed with that here.  The music is whimsical and fits the theme you of the game.  Sometimes you might be sailing and it sounds tropical, other times you might be feeling piratey.  The meat of the game is the story and doing tasks/quests for the npcs.  I personally did not have issues with this, but I guess some are not a fan of it.  You will be running around and being someone's errand boy, or chef, or treasure hunter.  I enjoyed the progression of the story with each individual character that I came into contact with, and how they played a role in the story overall.  One thing I really liked was how EVERY character fit into the story of the game.  Each one was like putting a piece of the puzzle of the larger picture.  I did not find the grind of getting items that off putting.  I guess my only issue is the "back and forth" that can happen when you have to travel between islands.  An npc needs x/y/z?  Ok, you go home to your workshop and then realize you don't have y to make it.  You then have to turn back around to the other island to get the right materials to make it, and then turn around again to craft it and so on.  This doesn't become as big of an issue if you use the workshop at one of the npc's houses.  There ARE ways to work around the issues I stated, but I guess I just wanted to put my only "issue" i had. I know another complaint I saw was people thought the story was too childish/simplistic.  I didn't have issue with it.  You honestly are a child in the game, so it only makes sense that the story and things will be geared towards a childlike mindset.  It wasn't overtly easily, but neither difficult.  It was at a perfect level where you didn't get frustrated with not being able to do something, but still kept your attention to wanting to complete what you are supposed to do.Oh! I just remembered my big "complaint."  The selling in the game is a bit...odd.  I honestly had to google how to sell items as for the life of me I wasn't able to figure it out.  (Spoiler alert, you left click your mouse button on the mouse button icon.)  Anyways, that is my wrap up review of this game.  It's a lovely game that I really enjoyed burning through, and liked checking off each achievement as well.  I would say it's worth the money, and even a better deal if/when you get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked to zone out to this game!  The characters were fun to get to know, and it made the small story more fun.  I learned things late in-game, like how to easily get coal, since I guess maybe I missed something or maybe there wasn't a tutorial?  I noticed this game could use some more quality of life, but overall I loved the game.  Can't wait to check out their new games next!

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited for this game for a while -- I'd backed it on Kickstarter a few years ago and was always very excited with the regular updates from Chibig about the progress of the game. However, not even an hour into the game, I couldn't help but feel unimpressed and a bit annoyed. Things that I noted were:I feel that more was put into the cinematics, which are gorgeous and endearing (nearly perfect, even!), than the actual game itself. If the developers had worked to carry the same kind of energy from the cinematics into the gameplay, it would have improved it tenfold.The controls are a bit weird. The game doesn't show you how to do anything in the beginning, beyond the barest of instructions (e.g. use this button). While I can appreciate that you should figure everything out yourself, when it comes to opening up your inventory, checking crafting, and quests, I feel that there should be some indicator of the keybinds.The gravity in the game is a bit heavy. The speed at which Koa jumps and falls is jarringly fast, and doesn't carry the fun and whimsical feel that the game is supposed to have.The lack of direction in the game leaves the player wandering. Fun at first, but redundant after a while. After the first major cinematic in the game, where the boat gets wrecked, there's no actual indicator of the events that had transpired and what you should be doing from there. It was like, "Huh! Everything's wrecked, but now what?"I really had higher hopes for this game, as I'd been very dedicated to keeping with with the Kickstarter updates. But right now, I think I'll hold off on recommending it to others. I'll be waiting for the next major update in the game before coming back to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is a cutesy Farming sim/Town management game where you play as a little girl that seemingly is being raised by a friendly blue cthulhu monster and is going to fix up their island and go adventuring into the big world.The first thing I noticed and what sold me initially was that the cutscenes are very pretty and adorable and even the 'ingame cutscenes' where you briefly have no control are very charming and almost gave off an oldschool point and click vibe where the main character is emphasized from the background.The game itself then is also very pretty and almost has a Windwaker-esque approach to the graphics but sadly there is only a very broad singular slider for the graphics and even for a game as simple as this on full settings (whatever that may be!?) this game chugs like a choo choo train using around 70% of an RTX 2060. As for the mechanics Mara sports the usual suite of managerial controls like farming, crafting, interacting, cutting down trees etc.The first thing I noticed after going into the settings is that not everything is translated to English yet like the button for exit game. Then after starting to play the other menus also felt a bit unintuitive where it's unclear what to do as sometimes it's press accept, sometimes it's exit the screen and sometimes it's press enter to place. Very often the menus also don't respond at all, pressing escape for the options to look at the controls which resulted in nothing responding to your mouse/keyboard and only having the option to press escape again (even needing to task manager kill the game to exit it). It is also very weird how little the mouse buttons do outside of menus as most interacting is delegated to pressing E and only E which felt a bit restrictive and unintuitive. On the subject of quests the tutorial was a very well guided quest structure until immediately after the tutorial where it gets a bit oh you know the drill and to my taste that was a bit too early to let you figure it out yourself (apparently metal comes from a stone and wood well for example and yes Koa mentioned it but that didn't make sense to me in that order when they said make a hammer and destroy the well but destroying the well was what was needed to make the hammer). The minigames like fishing are also generic and like so many other similar games but feel really clunky to play and he first hour of gameplay was running back and forth and back and forth but even when it let you go to do more things yourself it still felt uninteresting and bland. The island is also tiny and there is not much to it / to do and I expect that eventually you go other places but by that time to try and figure it out I had already lost all interest especially with the chonk of dealing with the menus and such.The soundtrack to Summer in Mara is a very generic upbeat feel good music vibe but it somehow constantly interrupted itself, when a song was finished it just went completely silent except for the ambient bird and sea noises until you did something to further the story and prompt a different song to start and in the end it quickly started to get boring to listen to and I swapped it out for my own. The singing however was a very charming detail as some songs have a moment where the instruments take the backseat and give the spotlight to some soft gentle vocals.So in conclusion I sincerely wish I could have more positive to say but my expectations have not been met. I'm not going to say I'm the farming sim guru but I do play a lot of these town management / crafty build games and Summer in Mara just felt lacking compared to other similar games besides the gorgeous cutscenes. For now (and again, I expect this to change!) the game feels very incomplete and unpolished and sadly not worth the price and I'm sad to say that I will be refunding it for now. It really is a charming and cute game and the start of something  good is there but in my opinion for now it's not worth the pricetag that's hanging on it and I genuinely hope to see Summer in Mara get better in the future. I'd also like to implore you to try it yourself, see if it got improved and hopefully enjoy the game for yourself, I wish you all the best devs of Summer in Mara and players of the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Was this game a mobile port? It feels like a mobile port. First time it loads, the menu assumes you have a controller connected, and says to press the "A" button. as soon as you click the mouse however it does turn into a mouse click symbol. Once in the game, the game does nothing to give you the impression there is a specific place to click to close dialog boxes, or windows, as the area you need to click has poor indication you need to click on it, maybe some mouse Hover_over feedback like highlighting might be beneficial, or make something a button shape that you can interract with, like almost every other piece of software, game, utility, or interface in the history of existence.     Beyond my frustration with the interface, as soon as you start running around the beginning area, I immediately see collision issues with running straight through some trees,     30 Minutes into gameplay, you're given unclear instructions on removing an old well, and are instructed to build a new one. The instructions are misleading, and you remove the old well believing you need to do so in order to replace it with a new one. This leaves you with insufficient resource to construct a new one, You at that point are stuck, and cannot advance in the game.     This title is broken, following unclear instructions, in under an hour. When you look for a workaround or fix for this issue, quick internet searches reveal the developer labels this as a "Bug" and has existed for years without being addressed, and the developer, with no real support as to how, simply instructs to reset and start over, but the only instructions to do so are for the mobile release.     tl;dr game breaking design error experienced within 30 minutes, no clear fix, and the problem has existed for years with no attempt at resolution by developer.      Not only will I ask for a refund, I will never buy from this developer in the future. I couldn't be more dissappointed and upset, because the aesthetic and feel of the title look adorable and I was really hoping for the best.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: This casual game is very appealing in the beginning with colorful and cartoony graphics, a cute main character, farming/crafting mechanics with resource collection, and a relaxing nature, but unlike this developer's some other games, it has a semi-open world, and unfortunately, this world is so empty and bland. The gameplay also consists of repetitive fetch quests, and there is no direction to find NPC's in this boring, semi-open world to take quests from these NPC's or complete them. In the first hour of my gameplay, I enjoyed this game, but when I started to travel with my boat to other islands, I also noticed controls were quite bad. Overall, this game's bad controls, directionless and uninspiring gameplay that depends on repetitive fetch quests, lack of an intriguing and substantial storyline, and lifeless world made it tedious for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the concept of this game, but it's just not it for me. This is just echoing so many of the other reviews: the controls (I'm playing on PC) are clunky and you're never actually *told* what the controls are for looking at a map, for example (or literally anything else though). _childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me so much of Wind Waker. It's a sweet little game with no pressure get anything done in a timely manner. The world feels vast and I love that you can explore everywhere. If you're looking for any kind of combat don't look here. This is not a draw back it's just not here and that's ok. It's very much pay attention to what the different vendors sell and gather/horde everything kind of game and I like that. Some things I do not like about this game. There is no cohesive story line. It has a feeling of 'Lost in translation' because a lot of the dialog between characters feels jarring. The fast travel is handy but only if the 'main' quest line needs you to go to particular location then you'll have it. If it's left kind of open, say you just have to wait till something happens, then you have no fast travel. I find having to communicate with the different npc's on boats out on the sea can be very difficult some times. The interaction box has a hard time popping up. These mostly feel like little kinks that need to be worked out. It's pretty good for the money spent on it. I'm about 41 hrs in and I've completed most of the 'story' lines within the game. It can be a bit repetitive but it also allows you to break up what you want to do. The animation is very pretty, the music is calming and sweet.  All in all I have enjoyed my experience with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Quick note to people with xbone controller issues: open Steam Big Picture Mode and go into the controller configuration for this game, turn both options to "on" then you should be able to use the controller like any gamepad. This took a restart or two to work for me but it makes the game a bit smoother to play. This is the only way I was able to solve it, though to be fair to the game keyboard controls are /fine/ so don't let this warning put you off.Giving this a positive rating unless something tragic happens I know what to expect from this game. Controls well, is very aesthetically pleasing and has a nice atmosphere. Just wanted to get that tip out there in case it helps anybody else enjoy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: the game art and music are very good. however , its a "story mode" game that hamstrings you intoa series of quests to progress the story. if you like those kind of games you might enjoy this. personallyit felt like a "my time in portia" but with much less farming , fishing , mining and general content.if i could i'd give it a "maybe" .

_childDocuments_.review: I truly can't believe I had played this game for only 5 hours when it feels like I've played it for 5 years in still haven't finishing it (just to preface how I feel). The graphics (as many may have been drawn to) & hope for another charming farming sim added to the library, has turned into a major disappointment. I really enjoyed the art style of the 2d character portraits, it's very whimsical and cool but the 3d models in comparison are kinda derpy or just lifeless at some points. I felt more disappointed with this aspect because the graphics itself reminded me of good ol' LoZ: The Windwaker quite a bit, that I thought it was going to be an easygoing rpg with farming on the side. Please forgive me if that was a stretch at all. The music was alright but quickly became less interesting and more annoying, I started to turn it down very low. The controls and very lack thereof a proper tutorial drove me insane for a bit as well. For some reason the developers only keep the control settings in the title screen instead of the pause menu once you're in the game. It was a weird take for me. I kept struggling (still do) to plant things because for controller to plant is the Y-button but you have to use the A-button to actually plant? Then the actual in-game menus were also very not user-friendly, d-pad and left-stick are apparently "on two different planets" according to this game so scrolling around to try access my inventory was annoying. However the thick of this review is gonna be the absolute never-ending fetch quests of the game itself. And to be honest I have played my many share of fetch questing games which were enjoyable, so usually this would not bother me. Playing Summer in Mara felt like a chore instead of actually enjoying the vast character cast (and not to mention some which their personalities were absolutely terrible), exploring the sea/islands, and just having fun. I did not play one sitting to get 5 hours either, I started this game a couple days ago and only played 2-3 times since then. I spent all of my time going back and forth from home to Qualis (which is the first island you come across after repairing the boat) way too often.  Not only for completing quests but also to take care of the mc, Koa, which is another feature I don't understand why they added when the game is already so time consuming with completing tasks but now having to make sure her energy doesn't deplete and belly is full.  It wouldn't have been so bad if they made the energy bar much slower, like I feel like I can't complete most actions in a day because her energy is always halfway done before midday in-game. Then also I feel like resources were kind of hard to come by at times. Like I mentioned previously, I do NOT mind fetch quests but there are way too much things to be done alongside them that drives the fun out of playing.I wish I could've had a better experience honestly because Summer in Mara seemed like such a charming exploration game. I unfortunately don't think I'll be playing it anymore & will be moving on. I wish I could refund this but I bought it through Humble Bundle last month. Lastly, I will say this game  be good for a younger audience (maybe) as it would keep them very distracted for a while & is a decent start for new gamers.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game with all of the quest lines done! I'm only missing a few achievements but that's fine with me. Spoiler-free feedback: I really, really enjoyed the game. I had early access which is why I've finished today, but I put 37 hours into it and enjoyed all of it. The lack of a minimap on the main island confused me at first but really you do only need the mini map when you're sailing, so I got used to it pretty quickly. I think it would be useful for some players to have a bit more of a tutorial when you're doing something for the first time, like buying or selling. Just a simple pop-up like, "click here to change to your inventory so you can sell". I loved watching all of the characters progress and learn more about them and their lives.  I really enjoyed sailing around, upgrading things, meeting new people, and exploring all of the islands!
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: The game looked promising in trailers and cinematics, but that's all I found interesting in this game in my 2 hours with it. The design of the game overall is very lacking. You'll find yourself waiting days in-game for crops to grow with literally nothing else to do in the meantime. Meaning, you'll go to bed as soon as you wake up just to advance time. Then, you'll travel to another island, get a quest from an individual that requires you to travel back to the island you just left. Don't get comfortable, because you'll only need to be there for the 30 seconds it takes to craft the item at your workshop. Now, jump back in your boat and travel back to the island you picked up the quest on. Who doesn't love load screen after load screen just to complete a fetch quest?
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara (SiM) is a farming sim. And a crafting one. And "go there, grab this, travel elsewhere thousand times" adventure.It's fun to run and navigate boat first few hours, but increasing amount of resources required for quests and cross-interactions between story NPCs gradually builds up irritation. And then there's 20 more hours to progress!The overall art is quite cute. But... it uses different styles. There are small adorable loading screens, there are few animated clips, there is main menu and 3d game itself. Not going to lie, when SiM showed the first cinematic pretty similar to Studio Ghibli technique, I thought there would be many more. Nope. Not the case. SiM is a perfect game for chilling. One finger gameplay - accepting/reading dialogues and then running in one direction, while eating or drinking IRL.6 by 6 areas, with a central island, will offer hundreds quests to complete, which vary from catching fish, growing fruits, to crafting new dishes, building complicated constructions and searching items, persons across the sea. Are you ready to explore?

_childDocuments_.review: I just played the first two hours, and while I acknowledge that's not very long, it's honestly the most boring first two hours of a computer game I've every played, and I've played several different farming/life sims. There are things missing from the tutorial that I had to look up, which shouldn't be the case, especially because this seems to be aimed at ~9 year olds. And unlike some other farming/life games that felt like they are aimed at young people but are still enjoyable to an adult (like Cursed Sails), this is painfully slow and really monolinear. I have some curiosity about the story and the broader world that is just beginning to be introduced, and I imagine it has to speed up a bit from here (...right?), but in two hours I've had basically zero choices in gameplay and only a few moments of story. The "quests" are like "cut down a tree", "make an axe out of two wood and one rock", "make juice out of oranges", "plant this seed", "turn the thing you planted into something with one click and deliver it far away"... So if you like farming games, even a bare-bones one like Harvest Life is much better from the beginning than this one, much less the nicer ones like World's Dawn.Refund requested.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, if you like this genre, this  is a solid game.  If you don't, it's not going to convince you to cross over.  That being said, this game oozes charm and there is tons to do.  Having the islands to explore is a good gimmick, and the main character is enjoyable to play.  The world is interesting and populated with NPC's who have distinct personalities.  These games need some sort of heart to keep you playing and this one has plenty.  A special shout out to the music.  One of the first things I do in video games is turn the music off, but I look forward to the music in this.  Some of it fades into the background, but there are certain tracks that make me smile no matter my mood.  Worth the price of admission just for that.

However, I can't seem to get into the game due to how floaty everything feels, how shallow most of the mechanics are, how slow both the character and the boat is. _childDocuments_.review: It was a nice experience to play this game. The story-building, the characters' personalities and the world-building were made beautifully. However, the gameplay itself can be tiring and buggy. There was plenty of time when I had to ask Google for a problem that turned out to be a bug that hasn't been fixed since it was released. While I don't find it as the type of bug that ruined the entire gaming experience, It's still a shame that a game with such potential is wasted on several annoying bugs. Furthermore, the gameplay tends to be too repetitive even for this type of games. Overall, I think this game is worth the time and I'd recommend to anyone to just..take it slow.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely game. It is a bit confusing at first but follow the quests as they come up and it helps. I started it 3 times before I realised I wasn't doing things in the right order. The characters and music are great, the build up is great to finishing the game. _childDocuments_.review: The music is really great. I like the settings. But the game feels unfinished. The way the NPCs just stand in the same spot, unmoving day after day with the weird style of dialogue box feel like placeholders that never got replaced in development. The dogs glitch around when moving and clip through buildings. I loved being able to explore and fish and farm but there is far too much fetch and collect quests without enough breathing room in between. Its not that the game is bad, it just feels unpolished and unfinished and like it needs more work to be good.

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara was much more fun than I expected.  I can't believe that I got more than 30 hours out of it.  It's a beautiful world and fun story.  I love all of the characters, and wish that the story was a little more clear sometimes.  I wish that all of the dream sequences were summarized in text.  My favorite character is Aquila!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of Chibigs games that I did really enjoy. It is a delight! This is probably the best Chibig game they have ever made.The story is a complete delight. _childDocuments_.review: I love chill, cosy games like this with no stress attached. Life is stressful enough as is, why would I want to add more stress during my downtime? You play as Koa, a headstrong and independent kid, who inherits an island. One day a mysterious creature arrives, and through your desire to help it, you end up travelling across the seas, where you meet and befriend a unique cast of characters.On your island, you can expand and build different facilities to host animals and crops, or plant lots of different types of trees to grow bushes. You learn to cook using the ingredients you gathered and learn to build a lot of different tools to help you on your journey. You can also fish on each island, or out in the open seas. Using all of these skills, you can help the various characters scattered throughout the islands, building friendship with each of them and learning more of their stories.There's also a fairly simple story that ties it all together, and sometimes you need to do more story quests to expand the number of islands that you can travel to. But all in all, you can take things at your own pace, doing what you please, as there's never any time pressure to anything.If these all sound like chill but enjoyable things to you, then you should buy this game and you won't regret it. I know I loved it!
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this game. It was simple but I loved the artwork, music, and unique characters. I recommend this game for anyone who is a fan of games like Stardew Valley and My Time At Portia. It's relaxing, you can't really do anything wrong on this game. My favorite thing was getting new farm animals and planting new fruit trees and seeing the trees and animals grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cute and the characters are somewhat interesting with plenty of things to do to keep you busy. Busy as in.. I hope you like fetch quests, because that’s what you’ll be doing. That alone I didn’t mind but there are bugs in this game that left me feeling disappointed. You won’t be able to 100% the game because one of the hidden achievements includes a bug that hasn’t been fixed in 3 years which tells me it has no plans to be. Additionally, I don’t know what happened when I beat the game because I heard only noises for a few minutes, and anything that was happening happens behind a black screen. In short, I can’t recommend this game because:- There’s only 1 cutscene in the whole game and I didn’t get to see it. - I spent so much time trying to 100% a game that has bug that prevents you from being able to do so.- The developers have been non-responsive regarding the games issues since 2020… I am writing this review in 2023.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself; the first 1 and 1/2 hours are addictive and fun great artwork like the mechanics to the game, controls are straight forward.The fetch quests are not that bad it does make it interesting however trying to figure out what in the world is next or going on or what do you have to do next in order to continue the story....Yeah what in the world I spent about 2 hours trying to figure out what was next and also running around talking to everyone and waiting for shops to open so you can talk to people to get more quests but eventually I found you run out unless there is someone hiding some where that I missed. I don't know I love farming games especially when there is a great story behind them but unfortunately this game its just not for me it seemed like it was going to be fun I played the demo and was really excited for it but now it feels like its nothing but fetch quests, go back to island to complete quest, wait, figure out what to do next because it is not obvious.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10Summer in Mara is basically just running from one point to another until it makes you feel like you have used 19 hours for nothing but walking. Okay but gotta be honest: The most dangerous games for me to play are ones that have really wholesome world with relatable characters and cute animals (e.g. stardew valley, animal crossing, the sims 3) since they will make me want to shut all my social life down and begin to live in a deserted island. Luckily this game isn't too long, so this time I didn't forget my name and personality while playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Although it may come as slightly grindy, specially for those used to other game genres, Summer in Mara excels in its purpose: To be a relaxing, cosy game, as it doesn't delve deep into sim or farming mechanics simply because it doesn't pretend to do so. It's all about exploration and doing errands for the multiple in-game characters (whose personalities prove to be quite fleshed out once you've done some work for them)There is a main plot that, while not groundbreaking, it's good enough. Its downside, though, is that some transitions between plot arcs are abrupt and will require for you to fill the gaps left behind, interpreting them with your own imagination and headcanons.If you came here looking the next Stardew Valley, Summer in Mara won't likely meet those expectations. If you're up for a upbeat fetch-quest game, though, you should really give it a try. The prologue is available as a separate free-to-play title and covers roughly 60% of the in-game mechanics, so it can help you decide if the game's worth your time and money.Personally I'm looking forward to try more games from this lovely small studio!

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, I'm going to say that yes, there are bugs/glitches, and some differ depending on what system you're using to play the game (PC vs Switch, for example).  I managed to work my way through these things, though the devs really need to look at the most common issues and fix them ASAP, or they might lose players.That said, THIS IS ADORABLE AND AMAZING.  It's a lot like 'Yonder: The Cloud Chronicles'.  There's a main storyline that the character has to deal with, heaps of characters with differing personalities, and a heap ton of quests to carry out.  Not all of the quests aid the main storyline; you can just do them for fun.  (And for the achievements.)At the time of reviewing, I've played it through once, doing all the quests that I could.  I haven't got all of the achievements, but I have most of them.  Yes, it really can take an awfully long time, although I was trying to do the side quests at the same time.  Not sure how long it takes just to do the main storyline quests.I nearly cried at the end, not gonna lie.  It got really emotional after defeating the bad guys.  (And the bad guys are obviously meant to represent capitalists, which is AWESOME.  About time we get to defeat them, even if it's only in a game.)There are spiritual aspects, a wonderful soundtrack, amusing interactions, emotional moments, LOTS of things to craft, and many animals to look after.  You play as the only human, and the animals are all familiar to us, but the rest of the humanoid (-ish) species are not human.  Most of the things you can craft, and the crafting materials themselves, exist in our world.I've noticed at least one person complain that the character tires easily.  Uh, yeah, SHE IS A CHILD.  Doing MINING and FARMING and SAILING THE OCEAN all by herself, with no help from her companions.  She WOULD wear out that quickly in real life.  What, are you not feeding her to maintain her energy levels?  You MONSTERS.But yeah, cute game, some dark stuff happens, nothing resembling jump scares, no combat necessary.  Yes, fishing can be necessary, since not everything can be bought from pirates or the marketplace.  And it can be necessary for the main story quests.  But since the game is all about maintaining the natural balance, planting trees to replace those you've cut down, then it's important to acknowledge that there is, in fact, a circle of life.  ("AND IT MOVES US AAAALL!")  Even if fishing isn't your cup of tea, it's a thing that happens, and you have to do it in this game.  If you want a game where fishing isn't compulsory, try 'Yonder' or 'Eastshade'.  Similarly relaxing quest games with central storylines, where if you need fish you can buy it, or fishing quests aren't important to the main story.Sorry for the long review, and kudos if you've made it to the end.  I hope this was helpful.Edit: If you're looking for a junior version of this game for a beginner or youngster, check out 'Alba'.  It was released 11/12/20.  It's shorter, real-life-based, no crafting or farming, but it's really cute and environment-positive.

_childDocuments_.review: As a pleasant and straight forward farm sim with a world of fun characters to meet, Summer in Mara has enough to satisfy both newcomers and sim enthusiasts alike.  For myself, it took a while to gather the concept of what was intended here.  Unfortunately, I had moments where I was backtracking for the trivial reasons.  For instance, taking my boat all the way home to plant and grow vegetables that I could've bought from a random town folk was an irritating waste of time.  Aside from a few controller support issues, primarily with sprinting, moving through the world of Mara is calm and satisfying.  Crafting, cooking, and resource collecting is straight forward and welcoming.  I can't say for certain if this has convinced me to convert to sims in general, but I have no issue with revisiting this adventure from time to time.

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is a beautiful gem hidden within the sea of the gaming world. From its rich story to its astounding soundtrack. This game will have you smiling, laughing, and even crying as you stick through it and enjoy the flow. With a positive and upliftingPros:Graphics: These graphics are artful and stunning. Not only do you have a very colorful world to explore and interact with, the points in which story is played, the art design is unique and beautiful in its own. I love being able to look across my island and seeing the setting sun, or being on the vast of Mara and seeing an island in the distance.Story: I know I have mentioned this before but the story in itself is beautiful and rich. Playing a young girl, you learn of the world you where shielded from for many years after the death of your grandmother. You uncover and learn to fight against fear to achieve what the adults presume as, impossible.Soundtrack: I will be honest, I started out playing this game expecting a mediocre setting and plot, let alone standard video game music. But instead, what I discovered was music that was tailored to the story, characters, and feel of the game. I started playing nodding along to the tunes, ended my 25 hours whistling along as I played. I will absolutely say, the music in this game has captured my heart and will be held as a personal favorite.Extra: Mail crabs! If you need a pick me up? Search for mail crabs, they are lovely and all written by fellow players! Absolutely a stunning addition to the game.Cons:Occasionally there are a couple bugs I had run into where the chat option disappeared upon trying to talk to one of the pirates, however, a simple changing of my ships position solved that.Conclusion: 10/10, This game is STUNNING! I have already recommended it to friends, and if you are reading this, I would recommend you enjoy it as much as I did. Take your time, and fall in love with Mara.

_childDocuments_.review: There is nothing critically or functionally wrong with this title. However, its marketing trades on an art style, concept, and mechanics that make you want to believe that it as a combat-free, cozy version of The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker. It is not. That 22-year-old title still has more exploration variety, better characterization, and a more intriguing story than this hopes to aspire to. It might be a bit unfair to compare an indie game to something created by the Nintendo Machine at the height of its creative powers, but Mara fails at being even a run-of-the-mill cozy game. The farming, fishing, and animal husbandry mechanics are tedious. The fractal structure of the fetch questing is equally tedious and only takes you between a handful of the game's 25 areas. Most of the game world is uninspired copy-pasting with little to nothing to do. The "mail crab" collection mechanic appears to be a way the team raised money to fund the project, but the supporter messages break immersion and feel like someone stopping a live play to read off the names of theater season ticket holders. Not that there is much immersion to break. The characters are all flat, stock, and radically change their attitudes and demands to conform to the whim of the threadbare plot.The bugs range from annoying (quests not updating with new objectives) to the hilariously obtuse (the fountain animation hovers over top of the town market, mid-air, instead of over ... the fountain in a different part of the town).Amazing music, though. The main theme is a banger, and the devs know it. It plays through a variety of arrangements, often all strung together. The music does not respond well to on-screen action though. The game will start a track for a particular mood and keep playing the track once the scene is over.Mara's incessent mediocrity ironically makes it a great fidget game, something to do while sitting through online meetings or training. It requires little thought, and it keeps your hands busy. However, that's hardly high praise.

_childDocuments_.review: My interest in the game was triggered by Koa and the Five Pirates of Mara. Usually, I don't play games where you have to craft, pay attention to your vegetable, fruits and animals, with quests, because I may shut down totally if I want a 100% on these or I have no patience to stay and make sure I don't loose everything. But what reassured me is the fact that nothing will be lost, at least for my fields, because I'm pretty sure that I'm loosing the fruits going down on the ground (like in Deiland, in the same universe).Koa is a young girl, being welcomed by Yaya Haku when she was a baby in Mara. Koa is human and Haku is a Quido but she was raised as she was family. Unfortunalely, Haku passes away, leaving Koa alone to take care of the island and perhaps to fullfill a greater destiny, by travelling on the ocean, meating new people, from cat-children like Mayo and Onzo, the Elite like Aquila and Rigatta, other Quidos like Taka, Saimi, Caleb and others or even an Ank like Aiwan (and apparently Taima) to humans like Akaji...Koa can farm vegetables, plant trees (fruits or not), she can mine rocks to get metal, silver, gold or rocks, she can dive into the ocean, once she gets a mask, she can fish, she can craft tools, regular items like boards or threads, cook (if making a juice can count as cooking). Everything of that is pretty chill. You can explore Mara and come back later and still find your vegetables to harvest. Koa can also find ressources on the sea or by buying them, though she can also sell items - you can have only 99 pieces of the same item, meaning that it's very useful to sell them to make some place. You gain money, which enables you to buy seeds, to harvest more and to keep making a bank for yourself.Because, yes, the more tedious in that game is probably having enough ressources to feed Koa or to restore energy or simply to finish the quests or to do the achievements. I must say that before upgrading the boat at the maximum, I spent quite some time harvesting fruits and vegetables, mining also what I could, fishing, etc... so that I had enough money (not only to call Caleb to ferry me where I wanted) in case of. After all, when you see the price at Milly, Pilly and Tilly's market, for a battery to be at 518 gold, when you need two because you didn't learn how to craft them (I think it's coming later after the quest)...Summer in Mara is very repetitive if you want to 100% all the quests. Even exploring Mara can be boring sometimes if you're doing every mile yourself (and refuelling at temples, for free). But it's worth to see all the islands, to meet the pirates and to recognize, for me, some locations from Koa and the Five Pirates of Mara. It helped me to understand better why Ereti was firing cannon balls at me... At the end though, the graphics and the soundtrack (was it the same as in the newest game? I don't really remember but the reuse of all the tracks in all the games is obvious, so...) were satisfying and changed everytime you're speaking to a character. I also loved the idea of finding the mail crabs, because with the messages are tied an item and sometimes, it helped me move forward (like the canvas for Napopo... when I see that I've unlocked the craft way later in game, I'm glad to have found it earlier). After the main storyline is done, you can still play, I mean, I did many of the quests before finishing the story itself, but if you didn't then, you can do it when you want. Summer in Mara is aimed to be chilling, even if repetitive by moments. You're free to do what you want on your island (apart for some buildings that have a fixed spot), so I'm pretty sure that everyone has a different island than me. I'm recommending the game but if there are discounts, it's better to buy it at that moment. But if I have to choose between Summer in Mara, Ankora: Lost Days and Deiland: Pocket Planet Edition (not counting Koa and the Five Pirates of Mara as it's a different category of games), I would choose Summer in Mara. It's the easiest to master and the less frustrating as there are no enemies to battle at all.

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as I got in-game, I really liked the atmosphere. The graphics and the soundtrack were nice and the adorable animals made me go "Awww!". I also really liked the way you picked up the oranges, that you plowed the land, and the way the watering system worked.Then, the hickups began. It took me a while to figure out which key to press to make Koa get up from the rooftop, and also to learn that you can't just left-click anywhere on the screen to close pop-up messages - you need to click where it says to click. I also couldn't find a minimap (because there isn't one) or open the quest log, which complicated things because I can't remember instructions for more than a minute or so. You can check the list of Controls from the Main Menu but, once you get in game, you no longer have access to the Controls (only Resume and Exit) so it took me a while to find out that the correct key to access the quest log was CTRL and not TAB, J, K or L like I had tried.That being said, once I did learn what the proper controls for the game were, things became a lot smoother and I was able to go back to just playing and enjoying the game, the interactions between Koa and , and the amazing cutscenes not only telling the story but also showcasing the unbelievable dinizens of the worls. But I did get stuck on a quest for lighting the fire... before getting a quest to light the fire... I was also getting a bit worried because I was chopping trees for wood and none of them would give me seeds to replant but once I noticed that you could Kick some trees and get seeds without having to chop them down, everything was back on track. The fishing minigame was also fun.My only critique is that quests do become a bit too repetitive, which can be a bit boring if you're playing the game for long periods of time. Also, you have an option to Start (aka continue your previous save) but not one to start a New Game.All and all, the game has cute graphics and a nice soundtrack but it's not relaxing due to how annoying the quests get. It might be a good addition to your collection if you're a fan of the genre but, if you want to invest in only a handful of tittles, this might be one of the ones that you'll skip.

_childDocuments_.review: The vibes are immaculate.  It gets a good rating just for capturing the "beach town of weirdos" feeling perfectly.  Lots of nice characters to interact with.The rest of it is kind of a really barebones farming sim.  Its still a lot of fun to play and everything flows together well enough.  But there's kind of a nagging feeling that everything could have been deeper.  Its a great setting, and it would have been amazing if it was fleshed out even more.Still, if you like summertime beachside vibes, farming, and weird talking fish and cats, its worth picking up on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I've never reviewed a game before, but this really delighted me so I wanted to add my support. As someone who mainly plays farming sims (Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley) and a few other games, this game was a slight shift, and one of the only games I have ever actually completed (it's hard to "complete" farming sims where you can keep going forever, lol).I like that there were so many quests, which got easier and faster to complete over time (maybe because I was hoarding materials...). If you aren't a fan of the "fetch quest" type of game, this may not be for you, because that's what a lot of them end up being, especially toward the end when you have to roam the map to find various pirates. I enjoyed the crafting and cooking mechanics, as well as the nearly limitless inventory (cap at 99 per item, but seemingly no limit to number of item types?).I really loved all of the cute messages you find throughout the game. 100% brightened my day every time. (There was at least 1 with a Harvest Moon reference!) The game itself also has a clear message about caring for one's planet, which I appreciated even if it was a bit unsubtle at times.Lastly, but definitely not least, the core story arc about saving Mara was both engaging and BEAUTIFUL at the resolution. I only wish I could watch the cut scenes again, because wow, the art - *chef's kiss*.The game is so full of color and wonder, and I highly recommend it to anyone who wants plenty of variety and accomplishments, but not necessarily a stressful or super-fast game. I think it would be a great game for kids of all ages. There's no rush in Mara!

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game. It's incredibly charming and you can tell the devs put a ton of work into the world and characters, but it's also a buggy mess. The game seems to decide if it will work with controllers at random each time you start it and I've had to edit my save file to fix softlocks twice before even getting off the tutorial island. Not that it's easy to tell when you've hit a bug since there's often very little helpful feedback on what you're doing. I gave up once it needed me to collect metal but had broken so that there was no way for me to get anyway. It didn't help that I hadn't really done anything interesting in that hour. It's got fishing, crafting, and some survival elements, but they're all so shallow that it feels like they were added to check content boxes rather than because they made it a more enjoyable game. I can't believe I'm saying this, but Summer in Mara really should've been a movie or anime. It has all the elements it needs to succeed in those media, but as a game it's not even close to ready for release. The devs have promised updates, so there is hope it will get to where it needs to be eventually. Right now, I honestly can't recommend this to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I recommend this. I had played the demo before the game released and since there was no way of skipping to the part where the demo finishes, I spent about 10 min replaying the demo. The game says open world but it offers little freedom. One of the first things I did was run around and harvest everything I could see, prep my fields and plant the carrots but because I had did this in advance, I got quest blocked. The game dictates what they want you  to do by giving you a single quest and each time you finish that quest you get another. However, if you are the type of person who likes to go at things your way and do things at your own pace, prepare to be quest blocked! Because I had planted my fields in advance, I had to sleep through 5 days for the carrots to grow in order for me to replant and finish the quest. There is little to no instruction and you are more of less left up to fend for yourself. I had no idea you could move the camera with the mouse until I accidentally bumped my mouse! Up till then I was playing with the arrow keys and having an awkward time with the camera view. The game is cute but is still lacking. I don't recommend getting this game till they update it or till it's on a proper sale. I don't believe it's worth $30.

_childDocuments_.review: *Mild spoilers*First maybe 40mins of the game was very exciting. The animations were really nice to watch and the world is very cute and charming. However, after those 40mins are over, you start to notice bits of details that makes you peeved. Farming is, what I'm assuming, important to the gameplay since this game is a fetch quest galore. Your crops need not to be watered, they will grow regardless after several days. Rainwater, the only water available, never came during my "1.5 weeks" of in-game time. Sleeping the days away has no negative consequences in the world since everything will thrive without you which is weird because the beginning of the game emphasizes that your presence is needed for the island to survive. I ended up sleeping my days away for the crops to grow to advance through my game. That soured my gameplay. Maybe it's because I gave up 1.5 hours into the game. The character animations can be clunky and feels very...lack luster. Stamina is a huge problem as it eats away from your energy. It can be replenished but it hinders the gameplay way too much. I was forced to walk to several places rather than run due to the lack of food available since the rainwater was so scarce.The bigger island you travel to is beautiful. It's very easy to get lost and gets frustrating when you're sent back and forth, back and forth between places. There is no fast travel so you have to sail through the waters each time to get to places. Again, I gave up pretty early so maybe this will change but I was too frustrated. There's lots of filler in this game that provides no enjoyable experience (like traveling between islands). I'll keep my eye on this game for further developments because I think the game is very cute and has a lot of potential. I hope to see future updates that tackle the problems everyone is having.

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is a somewhat cutsie “farming” game, maybe a bit too childish for my taste. I honestly found it to be very boring at times, and too easy (the racing quests - I mean come on). I love games where you have to explore things for yourself, and that I must give this game, there are a lot of islands for you to explore and a lot of stuff for you to farm. Surprisingly, there were a few items where I found myself thinking, what is the point of collecting these, you aren’t gonna use them in the game at all, not even for crafting or cooking. Also, can someone tell me what the point of upgrading your ax or shovel is? Maybe I just missed it, but I am a bit clueless as to why even bother?The storyline was okay, there are many quests for you to do, however, most of them are bring back this, or go fetch that → A LOT of running back and forth. Usually when I play games, I listen notoriously to what the NPC’s are telling me and I read EVERYTHING that can be read, but I honestly found myself skipping most of the conversations. Whilst playing I ran into a few bugs, most of them solvable by quitting and reentering the game (it autosaves pretty often), I also experienced some frustrations finding the RIGHT angle when trying to speak with someone on their boats. If you are an achievementhunter like me, be aware that there are some misdescriptions of some of the achievements, but the great interwebz has all the answers, so no worries.There were some aspects to this game that I enjoyed, but I am giving it a thumbs down because I am left with the feeling of “thank goodness I have completed this game - DELETE”. It feels like it was onto something and it just didn’t follow through.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved playing this game.  Very chill, no rush to accomplish anything, do everything at your own pace.  I loved every single character, I loved the graphics and the music.  I loved reading all of the notes on the mail crabs.  There is no punishment for not returning to your home island every day; your animals do not need to be fed and your crops will still grow without being watered, so you can spend days at the big island or exploring the ocean.  I even loved the movement of the boat while cruising around the ocean breaking crates. I have a couple of minor complaints, none of which are game breaking. Controls are not explained at all.  Many times I knew what I needed to do, but not HOW to do it.  I was able to eventually figure everything out through trial and error of just pressing keys until I found the one I needed, except selling items, which I had to google.  To sell, you need to left click on the actual picture of the mouse at the top of the shop screen, it will switch to a sell screen.  I would have never figured that out on my own.  A couple of times the image of the quest giver covers what is needed for the quest on the quest log screen, so if you missed it when they were talking to you, you can't see what they want. There's a glitch were 2 of the mail crabs are simply not in the game.  So if you are a completionist, you cannot get all 91 crabs, and you cannot get that last steam achievement.  Many of the buildings and items for your home island must be placed in specific places, but it doesn't tell you where those places are, so it can be frustrating figuring out where they are supposed to go.  Mine, I'm looking at you. Not a glitch so much as I simply missed it until almost the end of the game, but:  many times a character tells you they marked your map to find something they want you to find.  I never saw anything on the map when I pulled it up, so I just assumed it was a glitch, and spent far too much time just wandering the ocean looking for what they wanted me to find.  (I didn't actually really mind this, sailing the ocean is actually pretty peaceful and relaxing.)  It wasn't until the very end of the game did I notice you can hit E and it highlights which island you need to go to.   Hopefully that helps someone else.Overall, a very fun game, I definitely recommend it, and I will certainly play it again sometime.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a lovely cute casual game, clearly designed to be a stress free noting can go wrong kind of game so i definatly recommend it for that.But Unfortunatly there are quite a lot of bugs, and the overall UI design is rather simple, there a lot of quality of life things they could have added in which just arnt which are pretty commonplace now, even for instance when selling or crafting multiple items youhave to hold or keep pressing the button until it gets to slowly up to the amount you want instead of just being able to just sell all or go up in 10's ect.I have completed the game and i have absolutely no idea how it actually ended due a bug not displaying the cutscene properly, but there are other spots in the game the story does just seem to be entirly left out which is a shame because it seems a quite nice narrative about the personal growth of Koa.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been an hell of an year, and when summer was approaching, I knew already this game had to be in my shelf. I was considering the switch version as I was following this project already when it was in the making, but I absolutely don't regret getting it here. It's a casual game that can become challenging enough if one wants to get all the achievements and explore the entire world of Mara. Very nice Chill music from most of the play-through, most of them became my go to tunes, some are not that good. Graphics are extremely charming and is perfect for summer-time and screenshot-wise, but the camera really ruins the immersion, a lot. Controls are clunky and very old school, so they make the traverse of this great sea a bit troublesome, but overall very manageable. I absolutely suggest and recommend it if you're planning to have a relaxing summer time adventure as there are no threats apart from your in game wallet, or trying to farm and grind to get a full completion that will probably become a very memorable experience, if you can get past some woody controls and sometimes annoying music.
