_childDocuments_.review: Finally collected all of the achievements and ready to put a stamp on this game. The entire time I've been wondering whether to give it a positive or negative review - you can see where I've landed. It started out charming, got frustrating, won some charm back, turned excrutiating and flipped ever so often on a whim.The good: Summer in Mara's world has its own unique charm and does a decent job of establishing it's characters and setting. Nothing ever gets fully explained, but as you experience the game through the eyes of Koa, a young child, this incomplete understanding and the main characters willingness to go on endless fetch quests somewhat make sense.The game features some lovely 2D character art during conversations as well as multiple animated cutscenes I'll happily admit are very pretty. Along with a solid, if not particularly varied, soundtrack there are things to like about this game with an atmosphere that lives up to its title.The bad: Condensed into a rant list because writing it out would take too long.- endless fetch quests = run across the same island 8+ times within one quest chain , reading petty dialogue between two unlikable characters- worst offenders of fetch quest NPCs are the pirates who always disappear as soon as you do need them for a quest- some quests don't update their progress in your log, making it guesswork whether to return to the NPC or not- buttons prompts don't match up with the actual controls, I had to google how to swap to sell mode after enough frustration- farming is irrelevant, this is by no means even a partial farming simulator. Money is made faster and more consistently gathering resources from other islands. My farm went unused for 50% of the game. - days blend into each other. Other games in this genre mark the passage of time via changing seasons (obviously not applicable here), days of the week or even just the need to water your plants daily. Sleep skip as many days in a row to force grow/restock resources, you won't even notice. - the stamina bar is never relevant as you can simply sleep in your boat or eat the abundantly available fruit. If anything, it's an annoyance.- the diving mini game never has and never will be fun due to its sluggish controls- the 3D art style lacks any of the 2D art styles charm and is consistently blurry in the distance. I spent most of the time looking at the character rather than the environment to avoid feeling sick. - the story fell flat and the crisis could have been handled within 1 day if anyone had been willing. It also felt unnecessary in a story that otherwise seemed focused on childlike explorationConclusion: Stay away from this game unless you're particularly enarmoured with the nautical theme or intend to play it alongside a young child. It's not a horrible game. It runs fine enough, has moments of beauty and tugged at my heartstrings once or twice, but all of that is overshadowed simply thinking back to the amount of senseless running I've experienced over the past 20+ hours. After the game initially opened up the map with boat upgrades I enjoyed myself for a while and thought I might come around to the game, but that feeling didn't even last until the main story was tfinished.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly not enjoyable. Although the game has a lot of charm, and the intro animations and visual novel character art for it are absolutely stunning and evocative, the game and mechanics leave a lot to be desired. Simple quests have you running around gathering basic items, or crafting items. Basically a lot of busywork and chores. On top of this, the dialogue and characters are quite simple, and the actual activities you do in game are very shallow. On the starting island, I came to a point twice where the game's objective sheet said, "Something interesting will happen soon!" And it was frustrating. Like, why can't that interesting thing happen NOW? Why do I have to wait and fill my own time while I'm supposing to be enjoying myself with interesting adventures and explorations.Everything also just takes slightly too long as well. Chopping a tree? That's three clicks of a button, followed by clicking to pick up all the items. Planting veggies? Multiple clicks again. Building things? First, run across the island to your house with the workshop, then enter the menu, then enter a second menu, and then click the nondescript "accept" button. It's like the game mechanics themselves added to the busywork. Beyond that, the game just feels a bit unpolished. This is coming from someone who is usually pretty forgiving of indie games, and someone who accepts a lot of jank if the overall experience is fun. The world of Summer in Mara itself looks serviceable, but a lot of the details feel a bit barren. The player's model feels like a plastic action figure, with very simple walk animations. Most animations seem very plain as well, with no weight behind them. It looks like a game that was someone's college portfolio, or a demo made in Unity, rather than something that was properly polished for a full release. Maybe that reflects a slim budget, which is at least understandable. And given the scale of the game - with multiple islands to explore and lots of various mechanics, simplistic as they are - there is certainly a lot of game here for people who really vibe with it. But I did not. My favorite part of the game should not be the animated movie at the intro.I would recommend this game to children most particularly. For every complaint I just gave, none of that would matter at all to them. It would be perfect for someone who enjoys games like Minecraft, but may not be old enough for something like Stardew Valley. I'd also recommend this for people who might be new to survival/farming sims in general, as the cute story and visuals are at least entertaining for all of the busywork. But for anyone looking for a more in-depth experience, or who don't really want to waste their time on what amounts to a fairly simple game, then they would be advised to try something else.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just the worst case of fetch quest syndrome I've ever seen. All you do in this game is travel around, fetching some random item to continue the story. The developers probably thought that the method of acquiring the items would be sufficient for variation. It really isn't. Whether it's farming, mining, or fishing, it doesn't make a major difference. The biggest issue is how unnecessarily large the map is, with 99% of it being water. Needless to say, fast traveling becomes essential at a certain point to maintain your sanity. There are so many points in the game where you have to travel between the same two places several times in a row because you can't possibly predict what random item an NPC is going to demand from you next. What doesn't help is that the city, which acts as the hub area of the game, is also unnecessarily large and only has one fast travel point which isn't even at the center. Every time you're required to cook or craft something you have the option of running through the hub area for a minute to reach one of these places or you just fast travel back home to do it slightly quicker.Then there are minor things that all accumulate into one obvious observation I made, the developers are incredibly lazy. Characters in the game are barely animated and just stand around doing nothing. They couldn't even be bothered to give them a cheap walk cycle, they just teleport in and out of existence whenever the time is right. What was supposed to be the climax of the game was a laughingstock for this very reason. The 'menacing' villain who is about to destroy everything you love and care for just stand around allowing you to walk past him to finish this atrocious game. And speaking of that, the entire game has only two cutscenes, one at the beginning and one at the end. And while the effort that went into the art is commendable, it just highlights how lackluster the rest of the game is. You really want to know how incompetent and lazy these developers are? They literally mirrored character drawings that pop up during conversations. Now why is this a problem? Simple, if you are wearing a T-shirt with text on it, the text also becomes mirrored. I just can't grasp the utter obliviousness here, how did they not realize how awful this would make them look for putting their laziness on full display?Let's finish with some technical issues. While operating the boat, you can't open any menu to check where you have to go or even pause the game. I would like to say that you can't even access the options but that isn't even possible in the first place unless you're on the main menu. That's right, if you want to adjust your volume, change visual settings, or anything else you have to exit the game and go back to the main menu. They didn't even bother giving you the option to customize your controls. Everything that involves the boat is just incredibly tedious to put up with. You sometimes can't interact with other boats unless you're positioned pixel perfect, you can't exit the water via slightly elevated ground meaning you have to find a flat surface that leads into the water. The boat never becomes fast enough to make the unnecessarily large map bearable and just serves as an obstacle once you have enough money to fast travel around. The only redeeming factor that I can give this game is that the achievements are straightforward and in theory aren't grindy. While I can see glimpse of a great concept with the characters it simply falls flat due to the execution. The story isn't even worth mentioning.

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful slice of blue-skies gaming. It's refreshing to play a game that's completely conflict-free, where the only aim is to tend your garden and just, well, do nice things for people. And the ocean exploration is great, highly reminiscent of the wonderful Wind Waker. This is on a much smaller budget than Nintendo's game of course, so naturally it's smaller and a little more rough around the edges, but Summer in Mara is still a great way to while away the hours just pottering around the seas.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly cute. Its theme of be one with nature and equal exchange is wholesome and really lovely and kept throughout.While the overall polish on some elements is not exactly high this indie studio has managed to produce an incredibly awesome experience that seems to be quite the journey.NPC's will ask you to do tasks but you are not railroaded into completing them any faster than you feel comfortable with, and there are not markers telling you exactly where everything is all the time so you actually feel the sense for exploration when checking out everything. _childDocuments_.review: Before I begin, I would like to thank Chibg for the key to cover this game! Secondly, I want to address the false pretense to a review someone(SingingRobert) mentioned "lack of full controller support" That by every account is false. _childDocuments_.review: I played though the whole game in 40 hours. I would highly recommend it. It is a relaxing wholesome game with cute visuals and characters. It is definitely worth the price. [Theme]I liked the worldbuilding and characters. I liked the theme of multiple islands, traveling, pirates, and cozy home base. I wished there was more lore, and more mystery in the main questline. But I also liked the lightheartedness of it. All characters were memorable. [Music]I really liked music for each character and the main theme. [Accessibility]I liked how accessible this is as well. You have an autosave. There is no element of survival, horror, or violence in this game - you are expected to enjoy islands in a peaceful manner. The game is not, however, just simple 'click to proceed', you need to manage your quests, remember what you wanted to do, and figure out some easy puzzles. Even if you make a mistake, there is no punishment and you can try again. I think this would be an awesome game for both adults that want something simple and enjoyable and for younger audience. It was easy to navigate menus on PC. [Quests]Quests very very enjoyable and not that tedious if you gather materials as you go. I used fast travel a lot so I did not need to spend time on a boat.[Design]I liked how the game started small and taught you about the basics and then the world was expending gradually as you upgrade your boat. I liked the quest tracking system and ability to fast travel. I wish there was more impact when you finish the quest line for each character, but it was nice to receive new recipes\objects, too. [Similar Games]Other similar games I liked are: Eastshade, A Short Hike, Seabeard (IOS\Android), Guildlings, Alba: A Wildlife Adventure. [Time played]It took me a bit more than 7 evenings, so about 40 hours. Review might say that I have 8 hours, but that is because I played it on my partner's account. I decided to purchase it for myself as well to support developers. I must say this time is ideal for me, with larger AAA games I lose track of what I was doing and forget how to play if I don't play a week.  I finished all quest lines.[How I learned about it]I was looking for games that is not challenging, has a lot of characters, quests, and is not violent. I learned about this game  through a reddit thread on [Bugs]I have not noticed any game breaking bugs. I did however backup my save files in separate locations just to be sure, since I had similar issue with other games before. [Conclusion] I hope that developer will make more games! All parts of the game: art direction, game design, sound, animation, and interaction - they were all top notch. I recommended this to a few of my friends, and it is definitely worth the price!

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is a really great game where you can have fun for a bit of time. The game has good graphics and amazing songs. The short animations that appear from time to time are wonderful and, for me, the game lacks of them. However, this game can be annoying for fishing (because you need to always have thread on you to fish and have the bait which is needed to fish the fish you want). I would have preferred that we don't always have to make thread to fish. Another annoying thing is how the fast travel works : when we have money we have to pay to travel from an island to another island BUT when we don't have money it costs nothing. That's something i didn't find logical. Last thing is about the controls, i have an azerty keyboard but the game doesn't allow to change the keys so i had to set up a qwerty keyboard to play. It's not a big deal because i found a solution for that but it would be appreciated to have the possibility to change the keys because not everyone has a qwerty keyboard. Despite all this, I would totally recommend Summer in Mara for those who likes simulation and doing tasks (the tasks can be repetitive as you need to commute to different islands).

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of criticism was already in the last chapter, I don’t want to repeat it all now (see full review). Just a short summary. The game could be much better if it had more tutorials, a better translation, and a better UI design and the PC-typical options menus.There are generally too few tutorials and explanations. Of course exploring the world and game features is a part of the game, but especially for features like the map, the inventory, basic functions like fishing or diving and some other game features more detailed help and maybe a gentler introduction would be more pleasant at the beginning.Here the developers partly probably assume too much that you either know the predecessor games or they have problems to get into the heads of new players who really start the game for the first time. But if you have overcome these entry hurdles without being discouraged by them, you get more and more into the attraction of the beautifully designed and varied world and can dive into the story.Because the graphic style of Summer in Mara is very pleasant and pretty. The game has a very artistic approach and creates a world to sink into. It has a consistently positive and nice story, it radiates a lot of cheerfulness and you can feel and understand the childlike basic trust and the open-minded curious attitude of the main character again and again.The main story is very nice. It contains some twists and surprises. The quests are very often “Bring me this and that”-orders. But this is bearable, because you have to make these things by yourself and then you have to search and find the materials, recipes or other things first somewhere. All in all it is quite diversified.As a very positive highlight I would like to emphasize that Summer in Mara does not use any fights or violence at all. The game is suitable for children of all ages from front to back. It has received a USK rating of 6 (ESRB 7+), but I don’t know where to find things that shouldn’t be suitable for smaller children as long as they can either read or have parents around to help them with the texts.And Summer in Mara is suitable for children through and through, without being a game just for children. I’m a male, mid-40s, but I still had fun in Summer in Mara. And I can well introduce you to the fact that this game is suitable for single adults as well as for children, and even more so as a family-friendly joint activity.Then I also found the balance between farming, crafting and history very pleasant. There are always enough of these three game elements, and I never had the feeling that it swings too much in one direction or the other. Here the developers have really shown a deft hand and connected all parts of the game well.And on top of that, I remember the quest menu as a very successful highlight. Because there you can find all kinds of game characters at any time and there are hints if an NPC currently has a quest, maybe gets one later, and what you should do to get ahead. It is not intrusive so that one does not feel pushed by it. But you never feel helpless because you can’t find where to go from there. This game feature is well done, this way of implementing a quest menu is something that some quest-based games might like to play.This brings us to the overall standings. Summer, sun, sunshine, and a straight and positive story. Summer in Mara offers an interesting story in a pleasant and beautiful world. The farming and crafting parts of the game are well thought out and both are fun and it also fits well into the game. After more than 30 hours of gameplay, the end of the story is still a long way off, so the scope and overall gameplay are really neat.For this, I would like to assign a base score of 85%. For the somewhat fiddly controls, the not really good tutorials and the menus which have room for improvement I deduct 5% from this score and for partly wrong or missing translations in the menus and letters, I deduct another 3%.This brings me to a final score of 77% at the time of release. But I assume that many of the critical points that led to the point deduction can be improved by some patching work in the future, so there’s a good chance that Summer in Mara will slip over the 80% limit again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely adorable. If you've played my time at portia, it's very similar to that game except you own a whole island instead of a small plot. You play as a little girl who goes off on her own to explore and help others as well as keeping the island beautiful and slowly growing it into something else.If you're looking for a game to just relax in, this is it. It's not very expensive for some amazing cutscenes, really beautiful story (i'm far from finishing), beautiful graphics, and overall just a relaxing experience. If you want comparisons, it's very similar to my time at portia, stardew valley, and a little bit of animal crossing: new horizon, except there's no dating because you're playing as a child; however, you can befriend amazing creatures!Note: for those people reading reviews about how there's no guide or good tutorial, honestly all you have to do is press ESC > controls, and look at the controls yourself. This game doesn't hold your hand, but it doesn't take long to figure it out honestly. Just like stardew valley didn't hold your hand, but we all knew to go around and smash some rocks with the A button. You'll learn more and more later on, and it doesn't take long to learn the mechanisms of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:Due to the developers not fixing any of their bugs and certain issues simply getting worse over time, I have decided I cannot recommend this game anymore after losing my save file.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Summer In Mara is what I'd call a dream game on a budget. You have open world exploration, crafting, farming and questing. No this game is not close to something like Harvest Moon or Wind Waker. It's a jack of all trades master of none. However, what holds it together and helps it stand out is its great quest system and sense of progression. While sometimes feeling like fetch quests, I've never felt bored doing them because there is a genuine sense of progression for completing a quest because you get access to more and more items to craft and mess around with. The characters seem a bit flat but there is a sense of character development as you play. While traveling back and forth can be a bit tedious at times, it's always quick and simple. Where the game starts to falter is through its technical issues. The menus look so stock, like the game was just released in early access. The draw distance isn't great. The music mixing between areas is lacking (sometimes I feel like I'm listening to a playlist rather than music that is synced to your location or what you are doing. despite it sounding really good). Graphics options and resolution are non-existent in the main menu. NO CLOUD SAVES (yet)!!!! And the art is a "like it or don't" deal, and I really don't, at least for a decent amount of the illustrations, the in-game models are fine.However, Summer In mara is absolutely worth your time despite all these issues because they do not ruin the core gameplay, which is questing, exploring and harvesting. I'm about 4 hours in and I'm having fun still.For more recommendations, consider checking out our curator page:Thank you for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: "Summer in Mara" is a console ported third person platformer that's trying to rip off the general theme of Stardew Valley, but it's light on the quality gameplay loops that Stardew Valley has, and heavy on lame, pointless fetch quests.  This family friendly game does seem to be aimed at children, but as always parents should be careful when considering exposing their children to badly made video games and console garbage. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.The game assets are far from bleeding edge, with lowish polygon counts and somewhat low resolution textures, making this look like it's at least 10 years old.  It's unclear why the developers weren't able to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets for the game, and also irrelevant... what matters is that this looks poor in comparison to more professionally produced games as a result of their decisions.The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts.  Because this is designed for consoles, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game."Summer in Mara" has the laughable price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  This is also competing with over 9,000 free games available on Steam, many of them far better than this paid product.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm in love with this game! I got so invested in the characters and the world and couldn't put it down for four days until I had completed it 100%!Summer in Mara is a delightful mixture of a farming & cooking sim and Windwaker, with a colorful and very likable cast of characters. The game has in my opinion a great tutorial that teaches you all the basic mechanics and sets up the story nicely, after that it gets a bit to get going but once you're in the full gameplay loop it's so hard to not just keep playing! There's so many seeds to plant, items to collect, dishes to cook and places to discover, all the while a wonderful soundtrack of music plays and an overarching story unfolds.Like most indie 3D games Summer in Mara does have some jank, and while I don't mind that much it's good to be aware of it. You can jump out of any geometry you may get stuck in and all the loading issues or similar glitches I could fix by leaving and re-entering an area. Some dialogue hitboxes are a bit difficult to hit.Visually Mara is gorgeous! The character portrait art is incredible. The character models aren't super detailed but look nice, and I think the trees and the ocean especially look incredibly beautiful in this game. There's some great color usage for narrative purpose. A bit of pop-in and minor visual oddities with lighting or some effects, nothing too bad I think.The game doesn't have many settings. I got used to it, but I wish I'd been able to adjust the speed of the in-game camera's horizontal movement as it's very fast. I didn't double check but it also looks like you might not be able to remap controls, which is a huge problem if true.All this being said I thought the basic controls were okay and I rarely had problems with moving about or trying to do what I was trying to do. Overall most of the game is laid out in a very intuitive way and is great at guiding you both directly and indirectly! So much so that the few times when it drops the ball a bit are noticeable haha. But really, I felt like I understood some game mechanics via just vague dialogue moments and that felt super cool.You make progress in the game at a nice pace in my opinion, even if a couple of the tool upgrades feel a bit superfluous. A lot, and I do mean A LOT, of the gameplay loop revolves around fetch quests so if you hate those be warned! But I didn't mind at all. It all felt unusually well weaved into character dialogue somehow. I didn't feel like I was playing as a random kid pointlessly doing chores for adults, it all felt more natural somehow and made it enjoyable.My biggest problem with Summer in Mara is the English translation. I believe the game is originally written in Spanish, I hope the other language translations are better...  As a non-native English speaker I certainly don't expect perfection, but there were a handful of moments where I didn't entirely understand what a character was saying or a line was so awkward it took me out of the experience. It's a shame since I was so invested in the characters and the story, and like I mentioned before I felt like the game was pretty good at guiding you for the most part!My favorite thing about this game was the joy and wonder of discovering new things. I just feel like there were a lot of really cool and interesting things to see and discover. It was exciting to discover new plants to farm, to meet new characters, and find some really unique locations. The world of Mara feels very alive in an engaging way. The story leaves just enough unsaid so that you can fill in with the missing pieces with your imagination and it feels super satisfying.Looks like Chibig is building a "shared cinematic universe" with their games. That is quite fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Cooler story than you might be expecting, with fun character interrelationships to discover. I think that it has a place in your "I want a simple game that I can play with out thinking" list but not a play straight through. _childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a while to finish this game. Mainly because at the start, it is not very intuitive what is happening and what you need to do. I actually stopped for almost a year before I decided to continue it again. It took me a while to figure out how to sell stuff but thanks to the community, I managed to get some info. As time passes and you get a hang of the type of game this is, it gets more fun. The story and lore is nice and it leaves me wanting more.Lots of running about though, would have been nice if I didn't have to hold down the shift button to continuously run. Quests take you back and forth non stop so figure out the currency quick and you can travel fast. Very relaxing and chill game. Got all the achievements finally! But there are a few goals bugs that have been identified for years but it doesn't affect the gameplay/final achievements! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I'm in two minds over this game - it's cute, it's pretty and for the most part, it's fun.It did begin to drag after a while, as it is essentially a seemingly endless series of fetch quests. But sometimes that sort of gameplay can be pretty relaxing. I think that generally I'd recommend this, as long as you go into it not expecting a full on farming/life sim, and more of a farming sim lite with adventure elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara has a very slow start; at first you may think there isn't much happening or much to do, but it will eventually build up. You will meet people with many quests for you to complete. This is a farming, crafting, gathering, adventure type of game. It is definitely NOT for people that dislike quest fetching. I'm not sure why some people were disappointed when the game is exactly as described. In the first 2 hours of playtime, I thought this game was boring and disappointing. I remember really wanting to like this game. Fast forward almost 1 year later, I decided to give this game another try and I'm glad I did. I couldn't stop playing for 6hrs straight because there were so many things to do, they were like never-ending! This game is beautiful and relaxing. Having finished the game, I really enjoyed the journey. Although, there are some minor downsides I have to point out: 1. Some quests are unclear and difficult to figure out - where you need to go or how to get the thing you need. 2. Yes, the islands could be a bit bigger with more things on them or things to do, but I don't think it's a huge issue with the amount of things you need to do already.3. I'm quite upset how you are not able to craft everything. I remember hoping to learn the recipe for some things but it just never happened so I had to buy them.4. Towards the end when you finish the game, there are a few things left to do to get all the achievements. This was quite tiresome; I just wanted to get it over and done with at this point.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: The animated opening sequence after the tutorial is pretty, but I wish they used a bit of that budget for giving me a settings option in the pause menu. Or a help section to explain the janky controls. Or any info on how the game saves - apparently it's autosaving but when I booted the game up again I could only start a new game...
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy little quests and this game is full of them. Many of the quests revolve around gardening and collecting. They even have diving, which is also enjoyable. The map is quite expansive and the boating to one place after another is interesting and uses a compass to help you find the islands. Each new island is a  place to explore and really adds to the interest level of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I realy loved Deiland (the version BEFORE it got remastered) so I know I will like Summer in Mara. However: When playing make sure to follow the instructions first. Because if you use all the oranges to make juice befor making marmelade you will find yourself being stuck waiting for the trees to grow their oranges back, which eather doesnt happen or happens waaaaaay to slowly... I restart my game now and I'm looking forward to where I will find myself being stuck next <3
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: The game is charming, but not very technically polished (especially physics and movement could use some work) and the balancing requires you to sleep-wait multiple days at a time, some weird stuff (some buildings, for example) have limited times use after which you have to break them and build them again for no discernible reason, etc. The narrative is not all that interesting, not sure what the original language is, but the English translation is at best serviceable.If you like this kind of games and are out of stuff to play, then I guess it can be recommended at a discount as it is not outright bad, but there definitely are better games in this genre out there (Life at XY-rock series, etc.)
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: A Captivating Journey with Room for Growth!Dive into a captivating world where farming meets storytelling in this decently crafted game. Set apart from its counterparts like Stardew Valley, it embarks you on a thrilling journey as you explore breathtaking regions along the sea, seeking new and incredible adventures.While the game delivers on its promise of providing a unique combination of farming and storytelling, it does have its flaws. The repetitive nature of the missions, often requiring you to farm specific items for delivery, can leave a sense of monotony. However, amidst the familiar tasks, hidden gems shine through.One of the game's highlights is undoubtedly its mesmerizing soundtrack, which effortlessly sets the tone for your immersive experience. Additionally, the mini-games sprinkled throughout the gameplay bring an unexpected joy and entertainment factor, surpassing the main missions themselves.In conclusion, this game offers an enjoyable experience that fulfills its intended purpose. It successfully blends farming and storytelling elements to create a compelling world. However, it's important to manage expectations, as it falls short of achieving masterpiece status. Embrace the adventure, relish the soundtrack, and indulge in the delightful mini-games, and you'll find a satisfying gaming experience that keeps you engaged along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: This is nice, I did 100% achievements and quests in 26 hours so good value for money. Sandbox mode open afterwards. If you don't like quests this isn't the game for you - many items and areas are locked unless you do most of the quests and sometimes it is not clear if a quest on your list is possible to complete yet (for example the pineapple rice... can't complete that until much later in the game when you can get to the edge of the map). If in doubt and if you can't find the answer online, try talking to someone and it usually will trigger something to allow you to continue. The overall story is good and most of the characters are interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so lovely! The days feel way more relaxed than similar games, and I love the exploration mechanic. The controls aren't perfect - sometimes I get stuck on a ledge or in the water - but it's not enough to take away from the enjoyment. I am so glad I got this game, and I plan on getting more.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: It has some bugs (I still can't dig up that damn backpack!) and some game play mechanics that I don't find entirely logical, and they don't always explain everything. _childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a neutral option, this is a VERY VERY soft yes.  (to a soft no).  The game starts off BAF, and continues to be until you can start to leave the island.  The controls are clunky, the main character is a raging brat and stuff takes way too long to respawn.  However once you are able to start leaving the island and get quests, it becomes less boring.  I don't recommend this game to people who don't like this type of game to begin with, cause it would definitely turn you off of trying further games of this type.  However if you like this type of game, you just might find it tolerable.  I can't quite decide if it's tolerable (i'm leaning towards tolerable) or if i don't like it.  I'm stubborn so going to play it through but this could have been SO much better.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: If you really enjoyed Stardew Valley, My Time At Portia, Slime Rancher, etc and feel like nothing quite scratches that itch, give Summer in Mara a try. It's not exactly the same as any of the above but I feel like it has components from each.Some of the dialogue is a little bit awkward, but it doesn't really detract. My only "complaint" is that the order some things are earned in is a bit weird; for example, I had the ability to make the best hammer and axe before I had the ability to make the intermediate hoe.The sailing is a fun, different way to get around than most of these games have. Cute animals, fun characters, beautiful environments, and a heartfelt story. Summer in Mara felt very comforting and wholesome.• You can view quests/inventory/blueprints screens while on the boat if you open the map first and use the arrows at the top of the screen to switch between them.• • • •

_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Simple game filled with simple quests that require a lot of back and forth. The story is good and the art-style is very cute. Took me a bit over 30 hours to completely finish the game, including all achievements. If the game is on sale, it's definitely worth the price for someone who likes farming sim games. As the story progress, the player is granted access to more crops type, more things to build, recipes and more land to explore.  It's a casual and wholesome game, perfect when looking for a relaxing story to embark on. The only con is the constant back and forth necessary to complete the quests at the beginning (at some point, you have enough money to fast travel everywhere, but it's not cheap early).
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very addicting game! It's fun because you get to explore the island life, but what I want to highlight the most is about how it also teaches us to respect nature. There are many local wisdom that is being implemented to safeguard the balance of the island, like waiting until the fish get bigger before we can catch it, planting new trees after cutting it down, and other traditional and sustainable practices, even collecting the trash and recycling it! I'd recommend this to anyone who's looking for a fun and casual game to kill time, because time really flies when I was playing it
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is a simple game, with a lot of heart, systems that are repetitive, but relaxing and fun. The story is very straight forward and i think the biggest strength ist the exploration of the world which unfortunately isnt open from the beggining, i wish many of the islands were bigger, with more secrets and that recipees were found by exploring instead of completing tasks from other npc's, since that is what i enjoyed the most.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: It's 8.5/10 game for me. [-/+] Key binds are really easy to learn. However you can see that game is made mainly for console players. [+] I loved relaxing music and great atmosphere of this game. Getting to know all Mara's residents was beautiful journey. The story is really well made. I liked two particular creatures that I met. Their relationship was really harmwarming. [-] Only one downside of my playthough was almost constant fear that something will be bugged. For almost half of my game fishes haven't spawned on my Home Island, then one character went missing for some time. But hopefully issues fixed themselves. _childDocuments_.review: What if Zelda Wind Waker was a Life-Sim? Pretty much like this and it is really good.It is a prequel to Deiland, but there's no combat this time, they recycled a lot of assets and music from that one though. This game has farming, ranching, fishing, mining, crafting and trading. Most of the time you probably will be exploring the islands around Mara and swim around with your boat.Not really into the story and it has pretty much all the progressive talking points in it, the game was wholesome enough overall to not think about it that much. The story progression will unlock you everything you need for your island, but once you're done, there is not really anything left to do.Time to complete: 24,6 hours

_childDocuments_.review: This game oozes charm and loveliness, it feels like a summer back in childhood, the art is a solid 10, all the characters you meet are excellent, and the music is really good. The story is nothing groundbreaking but its good and engaging, though a bit underwhelming or weirdly paced in places. That being said enter this game knowing many, many, many fetch quests and a lot of going back and forth await you. Running around can get a bit grating at times, but i believe the good aspects of the game more than make up for it. The only aspect of this game i actively disliked were the diving missions, but luckily there are very few of them and theyre very short.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely farming game with a bunch of relaxing fetching quests.Pros:- beautiful visuals- different soundtracks for each character and the main soundtrack is very good- different islands to explore, each with their own creatures, plants and environment- love the mechanic of feeding the little (non-farm) animals on the islands and petting them (you can pet the dog in this game! All the dogs actually!), with the chance of them coming to your island- quest system is interesting in the sense that each character has its quest chain and as you complete the quests it will then tell you that in order to advance on getting more quests for X character, you need to progress with Y character.Cons:- some aspects of the world are unexplored: who are the little bug people in the volcano? Why does no one talk about them? What exactly happened to your yaya?- even after the main story ends, some characters retain the dialogue as if nothing happened - 2 of the 91 mail crabs are bugged, so you cannot find them- there's a bug where at a point the market building will disappear completely, but all the characters will still be in the marketplace- you have a racing minigame but the end result is already predetermined by the game, so you don't really need to do anything. E.g. I won all the races but one of them I was supposed to lose, so even if I finished WAY before my opponent, the dialogue was like "oh no, I lost"

_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I generally like Summer in Mara; it  is a beautifully rendered game that has a child-like charm to it. The game mixes farming and exploring mechanics together to tell a narrative of sharing the wealth of nature whilst not taking more then can give back. On top of the central narrative, there are many side stories that are split into different characters such as the rivalry of two chefs or building a colossal robot. However, the narrative of this game isn't the best developed with some of the pay off being lack luster or feeling like many of the contents of these quests just being busy work without a lot of build up to something spectacular; on top of that, dialog can be a bit dry or even a bit confusing in terms of how characters interact with each other or even react to events in the story. However, the actual art in the designs of the characters, Islands, and Animation is truly worth seeing. In terms of exploration, there are plenty of content around that you can pick up and bring back to your Island, and there are some really stellar locations to find; however, plenty of islands are relatively small with not a lot to do as far as content is concerned; maybe harvest a crop that you don't have on your island, or pick up a treasure map to find some neat bonuses, but they could have done more to make each island worth coming back to outside of specific quests or grinding specific materials. So whilst farming and exploring is core element of this game, they are generally bare bones and mechanically shallow which is fine, but that also means that exhausting the game of all its content only leaves behind a simple resource harvester just like Stardew Valley in that there isn't much to do other then grind for gold with nothing else to really do. The music on the other hand truly captures the general feel and vibes of the characters and the world. So, all in all, this game can be worth your while if you want to see the world for your self, get to know some of the characters, or want to take in the designs this game comes up with.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: 24~ hours later  I've finished this game. I kickstartered it and it took me a while to play through.This is mostly because the game is a long series of fetch quests, which bored me after some time. Still, the characters, artstyle and story are so charming, that I still finished it. It is a nice, relaxing game, and your island including all the little animals are adorable. It just doesn't have the most compelling gameplay. But if you want to relax and fish and look at the sea, this may be a game for you.The soundtrack is in my opinion absolutely amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Too much to do, too much to tell.In short : you play a young girl living alone on an small island in a world consisting of a big sea and lots of other small islands and you have to protect your world from outsiders who want to pillage the resources and thus destroy your world.I enjoyed it but often needed online help because some missions are really weird.Easy 100% achievements.Some frustrating bugs and things that looked like bugs but people said they were meant to look like bugs.Just play it and find out.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Did you hate fetch quests? Don't play this game. You are basicaly a courrier making errants. BUT, I enjoy the game, it have a really cute aesthetic, a really cool soundtrack. It's a game I can turn of my brain, and just enjoy the world. It's amazing? No it's not, but it's a good game that I'm really enjoing the grind and I want to know where the plot is going.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty enjoyable game. The crafting and sandbox elements are fun, and like how there's not too much survival and quest deadline pressure. Encourages selective farming and trading to maximize profit.I got on sale for maybe $9 and took about 33 hours to get most achievements. Not sure if I'd pay full price, but overall a fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed Summer in Mara. The game is wholesome, feelgood and relaxing. Really wonderful to come home to after a long day at work! The characters are charming and full of personality, and a lot of time and love has clearly been put into building a beautiful and unique world. Delighted to see that there's a sequel and more to dip into with this lovely world. I'd love to see another sequel featuring Koa as the protagonist in a new adventure on Mara.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: If you like relaxing but quest-driven games, this is for you.I really like the cartoon like graphics, music and style. You don't need to farm for hours but can grow veggies and plants according to the quests or your own play style. The places are nice (even if they are a bit small), you can take care of animals, mine and look for treasures (yes, there are pirates in the game). Despite the childish appearance, there are elements that are clearly meant for more grown people and remember you of the 'hard' life like financial aspects of society or how people try to make use of you. You will notice when you get to that point, trust me. That is an interesting mix if you like cartoon/cute art style but not only generic, superficial quests but with a little bit of background and twists. But all in all, it is very sweet, calming and fun to drive your small boat with your friend and to explore the world while helping people and uncovering the story.As many people stated, fishing takes quite some time to practice. But if you get the hang of it, you will be able to catch that squid you need so much! (I played with keyboard on PC. But I heard that switch players have more trouble with this mechanic.)I finished every quest there was to finish and enjoyed the game a lot during those 20 hours.This game deserves the recommendation for sure! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best game not made by Hayao Miazaki that seems inspired by studio Ghibli that I have ever played! If you have ever wondered what the Ghibli worlds were like from a little child's eyes and wanted to interact with it, this is definitely the game. I do not say this lightly for I am deeply respectful of Hayao Miazaki and all of his works and find them very close to my heart, and this game strikes all the perfect Studio Ghibli notes to be qualified as inspired by it. Thanks for this wonderful work of art devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Totally delightful game, taking what was great about Deiland and ditching what was not-so-great. I had so much fun sailing around to different islands, often finding something new each time I did even 20hrs in. It's really nice sometimes to play a game where the stakes are, generally, not that high - and even when they are, you know that you've made friends who can help you out.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: First thing first, this game is adorable! I'm in love with art style of this game. It's a laid back simple game. Decent story line of child trying to adult in an adult world. There's a LOT of fetch quest... a LOT of going to point A to point B to Point C then back to point A then back to point C. About 85% quest are like that, but in this game it didn't bother me. I'm super big sad that I'm almost done with game. Worth it though.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Cute graphics, fun easy going plot that lets you take the story at your own rate. Love the developing relationships between Koa and her newly acquired friends while they unlock new recipes and explore different islands. If you enjoy Harvest Moon or similar farming-story styled games, Summer in Mara is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cute and fun. The only thing that annoys me is the lack of game tips. As soon as I got into a flow , I would get stuck on a new mechanic. For example the instructions weren't clear when it came to making stuff in the kitchen, or how to control the boat, and how to sell things in the market. Tutorials are lacking when it comes to these features as well. My recommendation would be to label things a bit clearer and provide tips at the corner of the screen.Also , it would help to have a toggle able mission  list somewhere on the screen as well. This will help you keep track of what your goals are and what to do next. I would sometimes skip collecting things on islands only to find out once I am home that I needed those resources to complete a mission.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: If it was a AAA-game I'd definitely hate it for repetitive gameplay, slow plot progession and way too many fetch quests. But here, in Summer in Mara, atmosphere caught me and harvesting crops, feeding animals and sailing from island to island seemed like meaningful life. It was really relaxing experience, despite the manual labor of main character:)
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome no stress environmental adventure/base building game!Don't fret the beginning... it's a bit rushed, a bit emotional, and then it's kind of a very slow kinda confusing start, but the game picks up after a while!You don't really die in the game, so specially in the beginning, the biggest problem is getting too tired and needing sleep, but that's mostly it. And in the beginning you will need to do a lot of sleeping... xDBut in time you build up your island home, you get to know tons of different people and creatures, and the story progresses to understand your place in this island world.I haven't finished it yet... guessing I'm more or less over half way through the game, so it could be somewhere around 40 to 50 hours of gameplay if you are as thorough as I am. I tend to take a whole lot of time enjoying this type of game, so if you just rush through it could be a lot less.It's overall very wholesome. I called it environmental but it's not in your face... just educational. Characters have a lot of personality, and it's pretty interesting how the protagonist navigates through her entire situation. You kinda wanna be there in that world. xDVery much recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: A casual game where a little girl living on an island trying to explore Mara. The whole game takes around 20 hours to finish main storyline and decent amount of side storylines. The game rewards you with a casual, laid back island experience where you are able to have conversations and finish quest with around 15 talkable NPCs. Pro:Casual Decent graph for a game like thisLikeable character
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I have truly enjoyed my time in Mara. I adored this wonderful game. Endearing music, fun game play, fantastic artwork, and a charming story full of growth and finding your purpose. You play as Koa. A cute little precocious girl exploring the wonders of Mara. She can be loud, annoying and stubborn at times, but has her heart in the right place. She will mature as the game goes goes on. Although some of the other adult characters like the sisters, the banker, and some of the pirates are just rude and childish to a point where it gets super annoying. They do have some character development over time, but most are just a waste of space in my opinion. Also, Mayo is just the WORST. Some of the best characters in the game are Akaji, Onzo, Brram, Caleb, Awan, Napopo and Litio. They're so charming, fun, caring and insightful. I also loved the appearance of Mun in this game. It adds like a sense of a massive universe in this game, where on some other small planet far away is a little prince ~ Deiland. The sailing in the game is SUPER fun, but not so much when you have to chase down the pirates to talk to them in their ships. The ending is up to interpretation.. kinda... Please take note that there are A LOT of fetch quests in this game and NO COMBAT. It is a rinse and repeat type of game play. Please give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and relaxing family-friendly game - Summer in Mara is not really a farming sim, but more of an exploration game with lots of fetch quests to get further into the story (which can get pretty boring after a while if you're not into it). The story and characters are sweet and might be aiming more towards children due to the positive, "power of friendship" and teamwork vibes, but even at my age I have to admit I had fun. It's a good casual game when you just want to chill after a long day.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing farming sim. Great storyline and characters. The graphics are really nice. I really enjoyed the whole game. The pacing was good. Mostly open world, but some tiered unlocking. Not such a huge world you feel overwhelmed or get lost. Maybe one day I'll track down the last few mailcrabs. I really like that those aren't included in the achievements. Tip: run into as many barrels as you can while sailing, I picked up many good items, some which I couldn't craft yet which let me advance some bits early as I couldn't craft them until towards the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game. Took some time to get into it, but once you do.. a whole new world opens up. Its pretty relaxing and chill. The only thing I am a bit sad over is that I completed all the tasks for Brram, and then I could not finish Taka's questline, because Brram was done, so he just said the same thing everytime. If I can't do Taka's quest, I could not do Awan's quest either. But otherwise it was a really good game, and I plan to play it all over again, just to complete all the quests correctly!
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the quests were nerve racking. "Go get some paper, bring it back, now go get me some ink, bring it back, take this letter to my sisters. Take this gift back." Those ones were annoying. Overall, I really enjoyed playing the game until the end where I couldn't figure out how to do the "Glass eye quest".
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Basic RPG game heavily inspired by Anime with sounds / animations - In the beginning it's adorable, after 10 hours it's "meh" seeing the same drawings of different postures and sounds.Loads of hidden meanings in the game, some makes you think, others you might overlook if you don't notice them first time.This game is a relaxing game with pretty much no penalty ingame for doing what ever you want.It is very "strict story based" in the sense of progress, and if you get too far ahead, the game still wants you to "do things as described" in the right order. For quests, you can often have made / found items before you get the quest, and that might work, but in some cases, the game wont register untill you leave the area and reenter the area of the questgiver.The game itself feels like it's been inspired by Harvest Moon with a touch of Zelda (Windwaker), though you won't experience dungeons/difficult tasks in this game.Would I play this again if some extra content/updates came along? Yeah I just might. Alot of potential in this game despite its "final form".Get it on sale or not, you are guarenteed some sort of relaxing gaming regardless, I bought it on sale, but honestly, this game would easily be worth it full price. (And I don't say this often!)
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I tentatively recommend this game, because I feel like I did get my money's worth and I had fun playing it for the first couple of hours, but after a while the game becomes boring and I feel like I didn't get very far in the story.Pros:Super creative and cute charactersGame world is amazingI love sailing around to different island and exploringMusic and sound is greatCons:So my main problem with this game is the novelty of the fun creative characters and game world wears off when the game proceeds to continuously throw fetch quest at you. And by fetch quests I mean quests that have no meaningful impact on the characters, the world or have any relevance to Koa (the main character). The main character just kind of does things for other characters in the game 'just because, and she's nice' and I find that kind of boring as a player. She seems to have no personal ambition, or goals (at least in the first part of the game) It feels like she's just doing quests and exploring because it's a game and that's what you do in a game, you do random quests for characters and explore? The context is missing though.  Which is a shame because there is story/mystery going on, but it feels disconnected from the quests and the game-play in general. I wasn't motivated to keep playing to find out what happens because the side quests were painfully boring.However, despite all that I would recommend it because it's not a bad game. And it being boring after I got my money's worth is more of a subjective thing. It's cute, it's a cozy life sim game, and if you are looking for more cozy games (because there aren't many out there), definitely give this one a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. It's calming, it's fun, it can be challenging. The art styles are absolutely gorgeous and very anime-like. The music is soothing and the mechanics are so easy to configure. You farm, you harvest, you cook, build, boat places. It's not a massive farming sim, but it's still very fun. I decided to take a change on it and I'm glad I did. I've completely lost myself to this game, spending ages on it at a time and I'm not mad about it! I literally bought it a day ago and after coming home exhausted from work I've played over 2 hours! I love it! Hope fully it has some updates soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cute game. It combines several aspects of different generes, like crafting, farming, gathering, but also doing lots of quests and following a cute story-line. You have absolutely no time pressure and besides the quests you can do whatever you like in the speed you feel comfy with. Characters are also adorable and many things can be discovered.Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: The first hour was fun! Half an hour after that, it was okay. The last half hour started becoming annoying - too many fetch quests. It's a shame, I like the concept and I like these kinds of games; I have over 400 hours in animal crossing and about 380 in stardew valley. I was very drawn in by the exploration aspect; I expected a couple of big islands with cities, but you get your own farm island and one city island. All other islands are smaller and you visit them less.It comes down to: do you like fetch quests? If yes, this is MADE for you. Especially on sale. But for people who tolerate or dislike fetch quests, this is a big no-go.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is a fetch-quest game where you play as a young girl named Koa and follow her quest to live out her grandmother's message of being one with nature. The game is super cute, and I enjoyed exploring all Mara had to offer as I helped all the new friends I made along the way. This game has some of the best character designs I have ever seen, and I loved seeing each new person's quests. The game has plenty of flaws (some of the achievements are a bit buggy, Koa occasionally gets stuck, traveling is slow and some items are too difficult or tedious to get), but I had a lot of fun playing it and I'm happy to add it to my perfect shelf.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Such a sweet and lovely gameIt is very beautiful and there is no time pressure on any questYou are this little girl living alone on your island. All is peacefull untill these alien-like people invade your world. They wan't your island and does not care for the islands. You therefore set out to save your island as well as the others. This quest bings you on a great adventure where you must meet all the other people, explore the sea and other islands and complete lots of quests. This means that you always know what to do next, but as there is no time limit you can choose the order of your quests or focus on farming, exploring or anything else you want
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, Very much a grind.....Yes I am going to do it all over again. I think the end game itself could be better, but I had so much fun that I am willing to live with a little disappointment for a few days of fun. I do not see completing this game in a day unless you just don't eat, sleep, or use the restroom. It is very much go at your own pace. So hunker down and have a grindy fun filled time.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Writing a review for Summer in Mara is difficult, because I've had such a mixed experience with it. On the one hand, the setting and the characters were phenomenal. I fell in love with every NPC, their design, their clear likes and dislikes, and the subtle hinted relationships they had with everybody else in Qualis. I really enjoyed the island exploration as well, every boat upgrade was very exciting and incredible to be able to go out and see the whole ocean. Exploring every new island to look for new types of trees and fruits that you could bring back to sell or plant on your own island was exhilarating. The music was incredible, every character's theme worked perfectly with them and the overall mood of the game. The graphics were pretty good too, I didn't need incredible specs to run the game. I also really liked the lowstakes farming of the game. When I got lost wandering and exploring the islands, something that felt like an intended experience, I never had to worry about my crops withering and dying, which was a pleasant surprise. Where the game really struggles is its plot. I have a larger tolerance for fetch-quests than some other people seem to, I didn't mind running back corn and chocolate and rice for all the characters, I enjoyed the tidbits of character and connections you got from these sidequests, it really did make the world feel more alive. But the main story felt so strangely disconnected from everything else in the game, as if a sutured on addition. The beginning of Summer in Mara is a prologue chapter where Koa runs around with her guardian Yaya Haku, and Koa briefly daydreams about pirates and wonders about pirates. The title sequence starts after this tutorial and we see our large cast of characters, and the cinematic ends with a pirate ship drawing up to Koa's front door. When you start the game for real, Haku is dead and the island has fallen to pieces and Koa is keeping watch for pirates. I kept waiting for the game to explain this further, and yet nothing of the sort happens. Haku's death is addressed emotionally--by Koa dealing with the grief of two older women, and yet Koa's own grief is so rarely touched upon, until the ending cinematic, a moment that feels so strange without Koa ever really touching on her own fear and grief. And the villains of the story, the Elit, are given very little prominence in the story. The spirit orbs and balance and the final little build-up feels very startling and abrupt and I felt somewhat let-down by the ending moments. It feels perhaps that the developers had so much more about the characters thought-out, about Haku, Saimi, Dunna and the Navy that was just unable to become a part of the story, and it feels underwhelming for their lack. Although I loved the gameplay loop for Summer in Mara, I don't think I'll really replay it. The story didn't quite have enough going for me. But the characters were excellent, and if the develops ever returned to the setting of Mara with a new story, I'd eagerly welcome it.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara surprised me in the best way possible. The beginning feels a bit slow, but once you get the boat an travel to different islands you are hooked. It's a totally charming experience with memorable characters. The story is sad and uplifting at the same time with environmental and emotional topics. Decorating your island with whatever you want to craft or plant is such a relaxing distraction in these difficult times. If you're looking for a heartwarming tale with Studio Ghibli type graphics, this is an excellent way to distract yourself and escape from the real world. Summer in Mara makes me happy, makes me feel cozy, makes me feel sad and reminds me to be kind to all and with our world.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is sort of like a 3D Stardew valley set in a tropical island chain with a storyline and other islands to explore. The bright colors and the music really set a calm tropical vibe. There are a lot of fetch quests that also involve growing or cooking things. Its a fun game and its easy to put in more time than you intend to.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I totally dig this game!! Its a mix between Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing! I am here for it and for just recently scoring this game, I have put some major hours in. It is so easy to get sucked in by the story, graphics and charm of this game. I recommend this to those that have some time to relax and game

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a really fun pastime. _childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is a unique adventure without any rush. Planting the seeds and keeping the economy balanced is a refreshing session. The quests are fabulous; the dialogues are often funny and immersive. There are some visual bugs and something around the seeds when you have a questline with planting, but if you avoid buying seeds when you have an active task with your garden, nothing serious.

_childDocuments_.review: So first off, I've been excited about this game for a while. If you're on the fence or unsure, just snag it during a sale (I got mine on a Humble Bundle). While it definitely needs some work, this game was still a total delight. It gave me huge Windwaker vibes, maybe Windwaker minus the fighting, plus farming? I feel as though the devs have such beautiful groundwork laid out for what could, with a little bit of work, become a total Steam Library staple. I really appreciate that they have a roadmap planned out and they're going to continue to improve the game! Because even though I loved the game, it still had its flaws.The art style is incredible, the animated cut scenes were beautiful, I never got tired of the music (And I usually do by the end of a game), and it just overall, felt so fun and relaxing. Unlocking more islands bit by bit, exploring them, checking out their secrets. The characters you encounter are all so fun, with unique quests and stories. Something that bothered me a lot, is that there's all this cool stuff, fishing, farming, quests, characters, boating, adventuring, but it all kind of felt half done, especially on the adventuring side. Some places, you go to, and you're just like "Is this it? Do I come back later? Am I supposed to do or have something here?" and it's just, nothing. On one hand, you can appreciate the diverse islands and how they're designed, but on the other, I felt disappointed at knowing that there were all these beautiful islands and half of them had no true purpose, maybe even more than half.With the quests, I also felt a tinge of disappointment at how many were fetch quests. And on that note, also annoyed. Some quests were hidden, rightfully, behind "advance [X]'s quest to further this one". And that makes sense. But early on, you can get pretty far in some quests and hit a roadblock where you need an item that won't be obtainable for a LONG time. I wasted a lot of my time looking for these items, before finally googling things to see that I couldn't get it for another long time. It just made it hard to know what to do next. Some more tips or hints during quests would be very nice! I think I read somewhere that the devs were planning on doing that, which would make the experience better overall.With quests, I am a little sad, reading through the artbook (Which is a must have!), the lore, going through all the quests, and seeing all the cool things that could have been touched on more. Maybe a future DLC or second game? And how come, even though it is HEAVILY hinted at, we never get the reveal that it was (Spoils) I really wanted that touched on more! And some of the characters, like Aquila, seem to have such a rich backstory that I want to hear more about!Another kind of warning, is there is a lot of bugs. My game crashed continously, or bugged out to the point of needing Alt-F4'd, sometimes I started quests out of order (Litio's, I raced him before I "met" him). One of the achievements, to cook 50 things, was bugged out for me as well. Someone in the bug report said they found the achievement requirements, and in the code, it actually requires you cook 100 things! Also, I ran out of fuel once during a point in time where fast travel was blocked, and was just... stuck. Normally, you'd call Caleb, the ship dude, to come get you. But I couldn't, because I was at a point where they blocked any and all forms of fast travel. Luckily, you can very easily edit the game files to add items, so I added fuel when I was stuck, and milk (to spam make cheese) when I was trying to figure out if the achievement for cooking was broken. And for the crashes, the auto-save system managed to save me every time, I never lost anything, thankfully!On the note of fast travel, it's also kinda dumb that you can do it even without any money. At the end of the game, when money didn't matter, it was nice to be able to just fast travel around to get the last few achievements, but I also abused that during the game while just playing. So basically, my main problem boils down to "I'm a greedy hoe and I want more content" because I just love it so much. The devs have made such a beautiful, wonderful, happy world filled with amazing characters and adventure! Also, mad props for being one of the few non-LGBT+ focused games that features a married gay male couple! Mostly, in any kind of media, you only see lesbians, and hardly ever gay dudes, UNLESS, the media in question is LGBT+ focused. But for something like this, it was nice to just see a passive gay couple. It made my heart all happy inside <3 That being said, it was a super fun game, a wonderful experience, and I'll be eagerly awaiting new content!
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing this game and trying to get all the achievements I can say this: I wish I could love it. It has so much potential to be loved and I do love it but it's buggy in places, not so much they break the game but no one can finish the crab mail achievements because two of the crabs aren't in the world. That being said, it is an entirely fetch quest type of game, which if you're into you will love this game, but if you're not then it will tire you. It is a very beautiful game and very idyllic, but I would love to see more work done on this game, perhaps content updates and definitely bug fixes.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is a game about growth. It's a journey, both physically and mentally. I played it 3 times, unwillingly. To this day I don't know if it was a bug in the game or somewhere on my PC that made the game suddenly freeze. I frantically updated drivers, ran tests... which somehow managed to erase my save data twice. I eventually ended up replaying the game a third time, copying my save to google drive (just in case). I meticulously made offerings at the temples and to Nio and Nao... my game never froze. Each time I played, I appreciated the game more. Despite my tribulations, I have only fond memories of Summer in Mara. It was a peaceful and meaningful adventure- both Koa and I learned a lot about determination and perseverance. I made so many good memories... All in all, Summer in Mara was a beautiful experience and I hope others will be inspired to explore Mara <3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. I am a fan of "harvest moon" type games, although this game has a more direct approach to character- specific quests. there are some bugs, which i hope the dev's would work to fix right away. either way, overall, this game i a good escape from life. 8/10 until they fix bugs, then it's a 9.5/10
