_childDocuments_.review: after completing the story ( which is quite good in my opinion ), the left-over quests have a very strong "go fetch this" characteristic. i dislike that. during the main story, there are also quests that appear to be "just another fetch quest", but after actually doing it, it sometimes makes sense.generally speaking, i like this game, it looks nice and it runs very well ( even on my laptop with Quadro M1000M ).it was fun while the story lasted. anything else quickly becomes boring and i instantly loose interest. there are a few issues in the quest line like the game assuming the player has already ( or not yet ) met someone. which becomes very confusing.and do not even get me started on the chickens! i hate them. they are extremely annoying to me because they ruin any kind of building around Koa's house due to the fact that the chickens often keep running after Koa and stand in Koa's way so she can not place objects. also the option to feed them overrides other functions like harvesting the crops. i wish it was possible to deconstruct the chicken house to get rid of the chickens.overall, i am glad i got this game cheap.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Summer in Mara! My expectations were low since it's early access, but I was surprised at how much gameplay there actually is! I completed the game's main story after about 26 hours and then spent another hour finishing up the last few achievements, so for me it was well worth the money.Things I loved:- Koa: She is a wonderfully written character. Her relationships with everyone feel real and complex, and her dialogue genuinely made me laugh out loud at times. The quests some of the adults send her on seem utterly absurd, considering she's probably between 7 and 10 years old(?), but for me that just added to the humor. She's a young girl left with responsibilities that far exceed her age and I think her personality and how other characters react to her really reflect that.- Music: There are some absolutely beautiful songs in this game. Talking to certain characters trigger certain songs, so they become almost a motif for those characters. Dunna's song is my favorite. It is poignant and emotional while still being a joy to listen to while sailing around. There are a lot of songs in this game too so I rarely got tired of hearing them.- Worldbuilding / Lore: The lore of Mara feels very deep in that you never quite get answers to all the questions it evokes. [SPOILERS] How did all these different (alien?) races (Quido, Catchildren, Elits, Humans, Ank, etc.) come to be on this planet? What happened to Napopo and Blu's people? What happened to the Navy? Who were Koa's parents? What exactly is the creature/spirit behind the Guardian's door? But much like real people, the characters don't spend hours expounding upon their backstories to catch the player up. They just live in this world and it's up to you to discover its secrets. [/spoilers]Things that still need improving:- Fetch Quests: This is the main mechanic of the game, so if it's not your thing, this game may not be for you, but I think it works well within this framework of traveling around in your boat looking for new items / recipes. That said, several quests did frustrate me. For example, when Taima asks Koa to find her glass eye and I already knew it was in Ecco's shop because I had seen it there before, but I still had to go around asking the pirates before I could finish the quest. Another example, was when Ecco needed fabric, and then ink, and then paper/gold, making me travel back and forth three times for things I already had the supplies for but just hadn't crafted yet, when he easily could have asked for all of these items at once. It just felt unnecessary to be broken up that way.- Diving Minigame: I love this concept but Koa's movements are much too slow and the treasure chests too few to make it really satisfying. I would love the diving area to be expanded out and have the treasure chests more hidden by the environment so it's more of a "search", as well as have Koa lose the treasure she's collected if she runs out of air. The air bubbles really didn't do anything but extend your time underwater and I think a consequence for that would be more exciting.- Confusing / Buggy Dialogue: This didn't happen often, but a couple times Koa would begin a conversation with someone or say a piece of dialogue and I didn't understand what prompted it. For example, I was doing a diving minigame (by the abandoned station I think?) and when I resurfaced the boat was gone, Koa was in the water, and she said something about "that's what you get for messing with Napopo's family." It felt very out of place, like I'd triggered dialogue from another scene by mistake. Characters also said "it's alright" often and at times where it felt odd, which may just be a translation error or a particular English dialect I'm not familiar with, but I wouldn't really use that phrase the way they use it in the game.- Menus / Quest Tracking: I REALLY wish there was a way to mark the map. I had a hard time remembering where certain resources / pirates were and the quests only sometimes show you on the map where things you need are located. It would also be helpful to see what resources are needed to make quest items (for example, if I need to bring someone a dish, show in the quest screen what resources I need to MAKE that dish). I'd often sail to Qualis to get supplies and then go back to my island only to open up the Kitchen screen and realize I'd forgotten to get rice or some other ingredient I needed and have to go back and forth. You juggle a lot of quests at once and it can be hard to remember everything you need to get. The treasure maps were also confusing. There needs to be a way to mark which maps you've done already and mark their locations on the map.-[SPOILERS] The Baron / Ending: While I like the overall story of the game and the focus on Koa's arc rather than the climactic conclusion, the ending felt very rushed and unsatisfying. I didn't feel any connection to the Baron's character, as he shows up for the first time in the final scene and has a ridiculously cliched evil villain monologue. Maybe this is so we don't feel bad about killing him? Which also felt very out of character for a game about redemption, protecting nature, and friendships. I didn't really understand what the spirit / creature was behind the door, which had been built up the whole game. I'm assuming it's meant to be the spirit of Mara (based on something Koa says later) but also Yaya Haku is there? So it's very confusing and never really explained. I also expected Akaji's iron colossus to be involved in the final fight for Mara, but that never happened. Also CB and Fink are never dealt with or seen again, which I found odd. I would've liked Koa and CB's relationship to be developed more, as well, so his "betrayal" of the Baron felt more realistic. All that said, the ending didn't ruin the game for me. Summer in Mara is about the journey, not the destination.In summary, Summer in Mara is a wonderful game that combines the farming and mining mechanics of Stardew Valley with the sailing and exploration of Wind Waker. It's early access, so a few areas still definitely need polish, but the gameplay is solid and entertaining.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: It's OK for 10 euros, but I wouldn't spend more on it. In my opinion the characters (NPCs) and especially their dialogues are boring and I soon started skipping them. Plus, a lot of characters are just plain mean? And you get ripped off all the time (e.g. by having to pay off debts for someone). The story is average and boring. MOST of the time you play as a courier and it gets annoying very quickly. I mean, it's an average crafting game and despite the things I mentioned above, it's addictive in its own way. I liked the Wind Waker feeling and the overall cute, charming little islands. The crafting and farming mechanics were OK too.I still don't recommend it after playing it for 30 hours as I think you can play other stuff that is far more fun (e.g. Terraria) and I'm sorry to say that but I do feel like I've wasted my time on it but that's just my personal opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I am simply in love with this game, its world and its characters!It is very beautifully designed, has a bunch of really lovely npcs and a very enjoyable story line. I especially loved the calm and relaxing atmosphere of this game and the music - THE MUSIC! I've never had a video game soundtrack follow me for such a long time like this one.So I can totally recommend this game to anyone who wants to play something calm and is willing to get oneself into the heart warming world of Mara :)
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game. Plenty of hours of gameplay, lots of things to do! From sailing and exploring islands/collecting farm animals, upgrading island, or running errands. Similar to Harvest Moon on a smaller scale (no dating). If you liked Deiland, you'll love this!Game progression is a bit slow for the first 2 hours. Tool upgrades are only unlocked at specific intervals for storyline quests, as far as I can tell. A lot of the upgrades follow the questline, rather than being freeform or sandbox.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is quite a relaxing game with a charming world to explore but does become repetitive rather quickly.  This game is not a farming sim if you have this expectation before buying,  it is more so a quest fetch game with some farming in between.  I have no major complaints other than some of the quests bugging out during my playtime which I'm sure have been addressed in recent updates,  I also had some graphic glitches.   I gave it a positive rating due to enjoying my play through but I would offer a mixed opinion for those that haven't played it and may not like this type of game-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game a lot but can see why some people don't give it a very positive review. At some points there was a lot of traveling back and forth, you speak to person A and then go to person B to return to person A to return to person B... That is the only thing that annoyed me about this game. The rest was amazing, i like building the farm, sailing around, do quests and the storyline is nice. Also you can find some bottles with letters in it and the messages of those are positive or they are written in such a way where you can think about it..
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on sale and definitely glad that I did. It fits the relaxed gaming experience that I love, it has fun crafting recipes, a small world for exploration, and many fun and unique characters. However, I find the story lacking in the beginning. So far I am enjoying the game as a whole, and highly reccomend if you are looking for a relaxed gaming experiencec that has crafting, farming, and explorative aspects that I wholely enjoy. I would love to see it expand in the future, and maybe add some proper story.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing he demo and getting super hyped, I was afraid that Summer in Mara would eventually disappoint. But it does not! I simply cannot stop playing - the vibrant world, colorful graphics, cheerful music, funny characters, and the neat attention to details keeps me glued to the screen. I must pick the all the fruits, feed all the dogs, recycle (who leaves trash near the beach, really!), make all the juices, catch all the fish, learn to craft new things, and Oh its a lot to do when you have a tiny island in Mara! Summer in Mara is a very cute, super optimistic and pleasant game and I suspect it will keep my attention for quite a while. After 2 hours of trying to stop playing but being unable to, I was not asked to slay anything, nor go explore any dark dungeon, nor become some obscure and mighty hero. This game is a breath of fresh air in a time when we all could use some cheerful optimism on a sunny island with golden beaches. Now please y'all, wish me luck that I can get some sleep - it's 2am!
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: If you like resource gathering, crafting, building and progression style games then this light breezy game will probably scratch an itch for you. There's some themes about environmentalism, giving back what you take, being kind - all completely inoffensive but not subtle in any way.Finishing the game took just under 20 hours, with 100% achievements in 22 hours. Much of this game involves fetch quests so I wish you could traverse a little quicker to bring the total time down. Also wish the crafting was little more complex or gave you more options to experiment. But otherwise I definitely got my moneys worth playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: It's.. decent.  A nice little game if you want to unwind.  It is full of color with a slight bit of character added.Although I feel like it is missing something, I did enjoy the time I spent playing the game.Just keep in mind there is no time limits, no hooks, no seasons. _childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on sale. But it's fun and usually relaxing. It's basically traveling to different places doing quests for people. I like that the main character is not the usual type. As others have mentioned the boat travel can be quite slow, unless you want to pay for fast travel. _childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I adore the whimsy in this game. Some real love and dedication has went into crafting this little work of art. _childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: In the beginning, it starts off slow because you can do very little (collect seashells, oranges, etc.) and can even get a quite boring, but after you start progressing it becomes way more fun! I almost put it down because the beginning grind was dragging out way too long, but I'm glad I didn't, it's definitely worth it so far. You have the option to do several quests or free roam and collect/farm items. No quests expire, so there's no pressure to complete things.In terms of the graphics and gameplay, everything runs very smooth. I haven't run into any glitches. Koa is able to jump onto pretty much everything without getting stuck, which makes moving around the maps super easy. She also runs fast and the stamina takes an incredibly long time to decrease. I genuinely have no complaints about the gameplay.However, I play with a PS4 controller, and the controls are a bit wonky. The touchpad, Share button, and Options button all do something, but I get them confused constantly. I find myself pressing between all 3 just trying to pause the game. I don't know why, but I really cannot get the hang of it. I'm also not a fan at down on the d-pad being my inventory, I would much rather see that replaced with Options. I also have some issues with the fact that half the time you scroll you use left on the d-pad, while the other half you scroll using the left analog stick. That also gets very confusing. Lastly, I would like to see a way to still kick down fruit if you're holding an axe. Currently, if you're holding an axe, your only option is to cut down what you're looking at, so you must switch weapons to be able to kick again. It's a small change, but I would love to see the option for both.I think one of the biggest negatives is I can't access the settings from the pause menu, such as audio or video settings. I have to exit the game and go to the main menu screen to edit the options, which is very annoying, especially because when you quit the game and come back, it puts you at a sitting spot instead of where you left off.I definitely have my issues with it, but I actually do really enjoy this game and wish to continue playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game (did all the quests) and have most of the achievements and would therefore love to write a review. This game is very childfriendly in terms if events and language. Even so, for an adult like me, who loves games like The Legend of Zelda and Harvest Moon (and Stardew Valley), this game is very cute. It reminded me a bit of The Wind Waker, but also of Animal Crossing. If you like crafting, farming and easy going questing, aaaand having a boat in game, then this game is for you! You have your own little island to take care of, further more there are lot of other places to explore when sailing around. I spend quite some hours on the game and liked it a lot. There are, however, few bugs I ran into. Like the map froze on my screen once and one time my character got pushed of my screen by a chicken :') But hey, they don't make the game unplayable. I just hope these get fixed though, because if you run into one of these bugs, you have to end the game and you will loose process uptil the last time your character went to bed. Overall I did enjoy this game a lot. I would rate is a 7 out of 10! I payed full price, which I think is worth this game. One more thing! The OST is very well done 😃

_childDocuments_.review: I think that this is a really great game but I found it to be unpolished. Sometimes you will just get stuck on random parts of the environment and some objects just don't have collision as well as the sailing physics feeling a little clunky. The boat slightly clips into objects and it just felt a little off when I was sailing around    The main gameplay is fetch quests which is complimented by some really great adventure aspects if your looking for something with the more farming based gameplay of stardew valley this would a decent game to try out. if you want something good characters, adventure, and an amazing OST then I would say this is a good game that you should try out Take this recommendation with caution because the game is unpolished or at least it has seemed unpolished from what I have seen so far. It is such a great game but it feels like it was rushed out.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: short answer: i like this game, its not the most challenging or engaging game in the world but if youre up for some casual gaming i would definitely recommend this. it kind of makes me feel nostalgic for early 2000s gamecube games in a way. the visual style is like a hat in time, some of the environments are like zelda windwaker and the artwork is extremely cute. one of the issues i have had so far is that the translation is a little bit wonky at times, for example the game cant seem to make up its mind on whether or not to call crayons "paints" or "crayons" also to trade with NPCs you "commerce" with them. the game makers are based in spain and it clearly shows. also this game can be a bit buggy with how it handles collision but its really just a minor inconvenience if anything, nothing game breaking or anythingone of the things i like alot about this game is the character you play as, koa. her personality is very enthusiastic and kind as well as easily distracted. sure she can be a bit snippy sometimes but thats just how kids act in real life. its a small detail but ive always liked it when shows and games where child characters dialogue is written how real children act, it just adds a nice layer of immersion that really draws you into its universealthough one of the bigger issues ive noticed with this game is that there seems to be no penalty for just sleeping through the entire day and watering your crops until you get a fully grown crop, most farming games fix this by having a calendar system where certain events are only available during certain times of the year and you have to make the most of each day you get but here, you have all the time in the world. its not a terrible exploit because farming isnt the main core mechanic, youll actually be spending most of your time doing quests but still, it kinda sucks
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very cute game with some fun characters. I'm about 6 hours in and feel like I've only scratched the surface on all there is to do. There is a big (but not overwhelming) emphasis on conservation and giving back to the land which is really cool to see in a video game. This game would probably be fun for people of all ages.

_childDocuments_.review: Backed this game on IndieGoGo and i must say it is a very charming little game. I think one of the reasons i like playing this game is because unlike some other games that are similar to this one, the characters that you talk to actually have  a background and you get to better understand them, rather than just talking and that's it. _childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. I never had any difficulties with the quest lines, like quite a few others did for some reason. There were some minor flaws that bugged me, but those minor flaws never impacted my ability to play and beat the game.All I can say is, if you can't advance in one quest, that means you HAVE to advance other quests first. Just take your time and read the quest info, it tells you what you need to do, and once you advance Koa's beginning quests and get the map option, it'll open the map and show you where you need to go. The game isn't difficult by any means, and I'm no gaming expert either.It is a game based on fetch quests, so if you do NOT enjoy going back and forth a lot, then save yourself the hassle. I personally like this type of game. It's very similar to their Deiland game, like a mix of Deiland and Harvest Moon.Back to the rating.Sound: 9/10 for me. Wish I could adjust certain sounds vs. music.Graphics: 9/10, minor details with clipping and glitching, but very minor.Gameplay: 9/10- honestly, it's a great game with a couple of bugs that they've worked out.Cons: -As I said, there are some, or were minor bugs.-Koa does get tired, as she is just a kid, but stuff her full of pancakes and her energy and food level jump right back up. Haha!-I really wish we could add markers on the map.Pros:-Beautiful graphics and artwork. The characters even have such cute emotions.-Loads of quests to do.-Lots of interesting items to craft.-So. Many. Animals. XDThey've since updated and added more stuff since I played before the Steam and Switch general release. They've fixed bugs, and added fast travel options AND new cooking stations so you don't have to travel back and forth as much. I nearly beat the game before those new updates were added, and I didn't have a problem even then.Now, to work on finding those dang mail crabs. >.>
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Now I rate this as a "yes" because I did enjoy the game overall. HOWEVER! I do have a few complaints/warnings for new people. I will start with things I enjoyed and then get into the other stuff.Things I enjoyed:I love the art of the world, its very vibrant and colorful. The animated sequences are amazing and I wish there was more of them. The characters were amazing, the exploration was fun. Farming was nice and easy to understand, cooking was great etc. Things that could be better:literally the ENTIRE GAME is fetch quests, it seems like a cute farmy game with heavy story, but farming is only needed to get items for a quest. Otherwise, farming or taking care of animals is completely unneeded, which is a shame. Even to try and get a profit, there are better ways of making money, plus you only ever need money for quests. There is an obnoxious amount of running back and forth, it made me wish I had rollerskates or SOMETHING to make land travel a little faster on the main islands. The ending was kind of lack luster, to keep it as non spoiler as possible, the amount of preperation that goes towards the end, felt completely unneeded for what actually happens. It is over quick and left me with more questions and answers. (not even a heartwarming credit song, no credits at all?)  And if you play like me, where I was doing all the quests at once so I could 100% it as much as I could before the ending, there is no post game content, all thats left is to... idk run around? no reason to farm, dont need money, already explored everything etc. OH and fast travel costs money, on you own boat?? which doesn't make a lot of sense. (I know I said how money is kind of irrelivant but literally after a certain point, its only good for fast travel, which.. shouldn't cost you money in the first place)I know I have a lot of negative here but its mostly just, ending was hyped for something bigger than what it was. Some game mechanics are completely irrelivant if its not tied to a quest, and the game is.. slow, bit of a slog with it being nothing but fetch quests. I love the world, the people, the music, little bits of lore we learn along the way, but I wish there was more and some things done a little differently.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Last weekend I finished playing through Summer in Mara after about 30 hours. And I can't quite get over the mixed reviews here on Steam. Summer in Mara is certainly not perfect in any respect. It is quite casual, you can't do much wrong and the characters don't have much depth. Farming on your own island hasn't been implemented in a super complex way either and the options to customize the look and feel of your island are limited. However, I can't blame the game for any of this, because I hardly believe that Summer in Mara was planned as a challenging hardcore farming game for advanced players. Overall it's a very relaxing game. You're never really in a hurry, you're never in serious danger and the funny, (mostly) friendly characters and the sunny atmosphere feel a bit like a holiday in front of the screen.Nevertheless there are a few flaws: Rain (important for watering plants and picking up mushrooms) is poorly balanced. For the first 10 hours of playing i hardly had any rain at all. In the second half of the game on the other hand it was raining almost every other day. Maybe the devs patched something? Another thing: The quest design (usually "bring me item x!") is for the most part quite uninspired and very simple, which however is saved a little bit by well written dialogue and characters. UI could be better too, especially when playing with mouse and keyboard.Nevertheless I can recommend this game if you're looking for a colorful casual open world adventure with a mixture of farming, exploration and storytelling. Because of the harmless setting without violence and combat the game is also very suitable for children. Overall Summer in Mara was a slightly flawed, but overall fun little open world adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: There are a few things that need to be updated. Like ensuring that once you have gathered all the materials the quest updates to tell you the new location. Which is another thing, world map needs to be updated to say where people are located. Other wise. The story is amazing, all the little side quests and story lines are adorable. Love the graphics and design are cute. Overall, a good game
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: A very charming game, sort of like a fetch quest windwaker with some light farming elements. The music is top notch, and overall is a very chill game, and I found myself surprised at the exploration elements each time it opened up. The design of the places I've been have been really satisfying, and the art direction has taken me away with it. It does have some of the indie game pitfalls, for instance I'm not sure why it tells you left click is accept when it appears to be spacebar. Additionally the jump feels really awkward until you get used to it, the speed and hangtime feel very strange. Those two things are present RIGHT at the beginning when you start the game, and honestly give the game a much worse image than it deserves, they are actually the "worst" offenders I have found in around 5 hours of gameplay, and are simply learning that it means spacebar, and that jumping is not a big deal, the game was made around the jumping weirdness and feels correct in the environment once you are used to it. I have been very impressed by the "logic" paths of quests, it has done a great job of leading me from one thing to another, giving me opportunity to be rewarded for exploring on my own prior or leading me to something I had not yet explored. Many other adventuring and exploring indie games have issues with this, especially those developed in a different language than the player. The economy seems a little bit tight, crops seeming a bit too far into the unprofitable range. I have not yet beaten the game and don't know if this changes, and this is minor. Overall, every gripe is minor, and while the story seems a bit meandering the tone that it gives you along with the interactions of people have a very solid positive tone. It's an uplifting game for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I say this with love, this game isn't for everyone. There's a _lot_ of fetch quests. In many circumstances, you'll be talking to an NPC, then have to run all the way across the island to talk to another, only to have to run all the way back again. Now don't get me wrong, I love grindy gameplay, but this pushed even my limits.If you're interested in a _very_ slow paced game with fun visuals and a nice story, then I'd recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: this game is an awesome game. it has good graphics with a lot of cute/chibi stuff. but its so much more than that. it has a good story and lots of stuff to do to fill your day. its a great game if you like quests and farming. any reviews out there saying there isn't enough to do is wrong. there is plenty to do, game reviewers that nitpick at every little thing shouldn't be game reviewers because they make awesome games look bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game that just misses being a great game.  The developers are responsive and have already fixed several problems with the initial build and game play.  The story is engaging, the world is fun to explore, and the characters are entertaining.  I loved playing a relaxing game with a story that really drew me in.That being said, the game has several problems.  Mouse/keyboard controls are often clunky and counter-intuitive.  The menus are confusing and difficult to navigate - sometimes I would just give up on trying to figure out whether I had some of a particular item.  The game has a habit of freezing during the initial load, so that I often had to restart two or three times before I could get in.  The game play depends almost exclusively on fetch quests.  Because traveling through the game world is so charming, this isn't as bad as you'd expect, but there are times that it gets very tedious.  The farming, crafting and fishing/diving are rudimentary at best, possibly to allow the player to concentrate on the excellent story.  Unfortunately, this means that your island, which is supposed to be the heart of the game, becomes easier and easier to ignore as the game progresses.I thoroughly enjoyed playing this game, but by the time I finished all the story quests, I was ready to put it down.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 23 hours of gameplay to finish the story arc. I played on 3 separate days. Once you start playing the game is just addictive and you don't want to stop. The storytelling is amazing and even though most of the missions are courier type, it keeps it interesting by consistently providing new things to find and deliver to various characters, which all advanced the overall story of each character. All missions were within the scope of the story/plot, I never felt I had to "grind".It wan't ever 'hard' at any point, which allowed for a comfortable style of gameplay. Well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I watched the YouTube reviews and then bought this game.I've played just over 5 hours and I can say that I am in love.This game is a box of joy wrapped in a steam key.It reminds me of a time when games were games, and not just pay days.This game feels like it was built with passion and made with love.When I just listen to the music I feel myself becoming noticeably calmer.Mara takes me back to the days of the 8bit and 16bit game consoles.Where you bought a cartridge simply because the title and artwork looked cool.When you popped in a cartridge and started up a game with no tutorial, with no help.It was just an adventure.it was just to have fun.This game makes me feel 10 years old.Like I am kid Goku, from Dragonball, on a grand adventure.Except I'm a girl.... I think....Anyway, is the game perfect?Hell no.Controls are a bit clunkyShopping is a bit annoyingThe fetch quests are OK, because I care for my home base while doing them.The NPC's are OKThere is no mini map, but that's cool, because now I have to learn the map and landmarksWhat I love.The artThe musicShaping this island into what I envisionSitting on the benches and just watching what's going on
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fetch-quest game, but it doesn't take long to reach a level where it is less of a slog and more fun to see where the stories take you. The main character of Koa is a sprightly young girl with an enthusiastic personality that you can't help but be charmed by. Have fun exploring the islands of Mara.

_childDocuments_.review: This game tries to be too many things at once.We have a farming game where you don't have that much farming ground and can't realy expand that much.We have an economics game where you can't really make money working smart. (4 pieces of corn that sell for more than the 1 egg you can get by feeding the chickens 4 times with corn is... annoying)We have a story driven game where the story isn't really relevant, you have no choices and it's kind of basic.We have a 3D game with a kinda open world concept where the world feels really empty.Plus there are some annoying design flaws like getting locked in the blacksmiths shop when they close, the mini games are not really fun, and the whole game drags after a while.Though it has it's good ideas as well, the music is nice and soothing, the 2D art is amazing and the character design is great. And allthough this game is not as good as I hoped it would be, if they find an identity, one theme where they can succeed, the next game can be great.I'd rate it 4/10
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 7.5/10Summer in Mara is an adorable story about a little girl finding her way in the world and rising up to the challenge of doing what needs to be done. While the game still feels like it needs a little polish, like a map that shows where to go for objectives and perhaps an explanation that to descend while diving you need to hold the SHIFT key, what is there is very enjoyable and relaxing. Fans of games like Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley will be used to the tedium of farming simulators and fetch quests, but the story having a true purpose (and one I don't want to ruin, but is well worth your time) will be a welcome change.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Summer in Mara is an ambitious new game from a five man team which pulls heavily from games like Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, and Stardew Valley. Personally, I had a lot of issues getting my game to work and encountered many bugs throughout my gameplay, however, the development team was very responsive and quick to address the issues I had. I thoroughly enjoyed the game and highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys farming, building, and simulation games. This game allows the player to travel around between islands using their trusty boat, which they are able to upgrade as the game progresses, to complete missions. I will admit that these missions are primarily "fetch" in nature, but seeing as how the protagonist is a young girl, it made sense. Plus, quite a few of them can be completed simply by already having the item in your bag. I know other players found this mechanic annoying, but, as it helped develop character's stories, I didn't mind it too much. I would have enjoyed more variety in the quest types, and hopefully we will see that in some of the new updates the development team is working on. Already, the team has made more crafting points available and enabled fast travel between islands, which wasn't possible when I played through the game. Overall, I recommend this game and encourage people to check it out. It's quite relaxing and draws you in.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so far, Its so much fun. There is still some bugs with the audio compared to the Switch version but its nothing that is a deal breaker currently.If you enjoy games like Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons but want something with just a bit more story to it then Summer in Mara is probably a good fit for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: some players wanted FAST TRAVEL - today they got it.now the journey is no more.(until this update it was my absolute FAVORITE game of this summer...)since we only needed sailing DIAGONALLY between isles, this new 'ONE-CLICK teleport' destroyed key part of the game. why should you sail if it is only one click away on the map? (hereby I'm not referring to how easy it is to accidentally teleport via the map.)this is so sad. had really an awesome time before.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: So I've been playing for a few days now and I'm really enjoying myself. I think this game has a lot of potential. The developers are actively listening to fans and have already made some improvements to the game since launch (such as fast travel), so I would definitely recommend this game to anyone who is open to contributing to its development. What I love the most about this game is the dialogue between characters. This game has a lot of heart to it. I also love the graphics and the music. I like that the game caters to both adventurers and homebodies. I can go explore other islands and find treasure out on the open seas, but then come back to my home base for a while, grow crops and leisurely make improvements to my island. The game strikes a good balance here.8.5/10

I would also like proper interactions with objects and activities, cause now I don't "feel" as if she's doing that what's needed at the moment.I also noticed totally abrupt transition between her sitting on the roof and coming down the roof.I like the setting very much though - Legend of Zelda: Windwaker mood. _childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it's not great. Certainly not worth the $20 I spent on it, by a long shot!It's clearly a ported game, and the controls were meant to be played on a console. They never bothered even changing the tutorial text for it, so you have to do a lot of guessing to figure out some basic functions in the game. Diving, for example, only tells you to use an arrow. But if you use the arrow on your keyboard, you just float back up, wasting valuable resources. Turns out you have to hit shift, thanks internet!The quests come really out of order, and there's no hints telling you that. So you will get a quest telling you to do something...vague...and you will literally have no idea what that is until MUCH farther into the game.And hey, this game is ENTIRELY fetch quests, so you'd think the makers would have been a little more organized.Last, the game has a pretty cheap feel when it comes to the dialogue. They never bothered with animation, so you just get those image screens ala old school JRPGs...but with a canned set of two or three 'emotes' that basically just make all the characters look like they have wild mood disorders. And the voice acting is limited to a few weird grunts per character. If you want a great game, play My Time at Portia...don't bother with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I actually really enjoyed this game.  It does everything it sets out to do with an interesting approach to artistic design.  The characters eventually become very memorable and the main character really has a lot of kindness attached to her.  This being said, the story is fleshed out at a fairly slow pace and it feels like you're just doing chores for everyone constantly at some points in the game.I really do think this is a great game, ESPECIALLY for children to play.  It has a lot of amazing messages and the main character is lovable.  It's a game that tries to do a lot with the game's ecosystem and I really think that it succeeds in a lot of ways!
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Good game to play when you want to just chill out and forget the world around us. One or two minor bugs, one of the pirate ships you race against twice wasn't visible during the race and I couldn't tell if it was supposed to be a time trial or what. Didn't matter in the greater scheme of things ultimately though.Feel like there should be a late game item that allows you to home in on the messages in bottles more easily. Some of those messages didn't get translated to English.

_childDocuments_.review: I have discovered the game a few months ago and since then i have checked Steam weekly for a release date. Now that it's finally out and i have played it for more that 25 hours, i can say that i am not disappointed.It's a really relaxing game, the story is really sweet and i love how all the characters were developed.I am in love with the artwork and with how all the characters are drawn. Regarding the gameplay, it might take a while to discover all controls and mechanics of the game, for instance: i spent 2 hours trying to make some money for a quest at the beginning of the game,running around the island..until my boyfriend discovered how you can sell stuff to the merchants.I love that you can travel by boat from an island to another, finding loot on the sea, but a fast travel button would help from time to time. And i have seen the news from the Chibig crew that this will be implemented, which is great :)The animals are all adorable, the sounds are really making the atmosphere of the game more enjoyable - the chatter, the birds and the waves and so on.I really recommend this game to anyone who enjoys cute games with farming activities, pets and a lovely story. _childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Relax on a beach. Explore your tropical island. Explore the ocean and a dozen other tropical islands. Explore secret caves. Explore vast cities. Explore ancient mysteries. Meet interesting characters from all over the islands, and even from other planets. Pet dogs. Raise chickens. Pet the chickens too. Craft things. Go fishing. This is a great game.I enjoyed Deiland, and Summer in Mara is a strong improvement in every aspect. Every aspect. The world is so much bigger, and there's a lot more to do. Crafting is still a big part of the progression, but it doesn't feel tedious. The islands I've explored so far feel different from each other. The characters all feel unique. Players new to these games will enjoy everything without feeling like they're missing anything. Players familiar with Deiland will also appreciate the references and tie-ins. One minor thing that feels like a major thing to me is the fishing gameplay. I can catch fish! I feel like I'm actually doing something and have gotten better at it. Fishing in Deiland was mainly throwing your computer out a window in frustration unless you could literally see the future to know what random controller button would be the "catch" button this time, with only 0.001 seconds to press it. I could probably type more, but I want to go play the game more.

The back and forth gets so ridiculous I started skipping walls of text just to get through this game.The story is enjoyable but generic and not ground breaking. This game is missing many quality of life improvements you will feel along your journey, and the game doesn't utilize all the unique islands it has for missions.It just felt like there is so much more they could have done to really enhance the game.Now reading off the promises for the game based on Kickstarter:Koa backpack set :YES:Surfing minigame :NO: (Or not found yet, but I have discovered the whole map)Qu Navy old headquarters island :YES:New pirate character :YES:Opening 2D cinematic :YES:Customize Koa's outfit :YES: (But it is pick and choose a whole set)Animal breeding :NO:Photo mode :NO: (Or I don't understand how to get it)2D Cinematic Ending :YES:

It has cute music, cute characters, cute islands, and .If you're looking for a relaxing game that every now and then will make you go aww, you've found it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really cute, and kind of relaxing-yet-addicting at the same time. I'm the type of gamer who usually plays games on the easiest setting, and even with a lack of hand-holding in this game I've managed to make quite a ways into it. Playing with a controller on the PC I think the controls are pretty intuitive, and that an explicit tutorial isn't *needed*. If part of the charm of the game is exploration, then exploring how to use the tools given to you should be part of the charm as well.The game isn't fully voiced, which I found odd at first, but then grew to enjoy the little grunts and noises that characters make to convey their tone. If you can tell when someone's annoyed, sad, or happy, just by a little two-second noise, then I think it does its purpose. (and with how many languages the game is available in, I can see why going fully voiced could be a bit of a monumental feat.)The character designs are delightful, and full of their own charm. I'm particularly in love with how they're not afraid to make female-coded characters actually look like they're from some beastly alien race, an issue that we've seen a lot in character design. Mayo and Onzo are both read to me, as believably of the same race. Visually Taima looks like she's of the same race as Awan, and it's kind of refreshing to see good character design.Some people might say that going back and forth to your island is tedious, and it can be-- but an easy workaround to that i to buy every seed you see when you can, plant it, harvest it, and keep at least a few of those items in your inventory at all times so that you can easily spirit through some of the "go here, plant this, bring me this item" quests. Which, this game is essentially fetch quests with some farming, and if that's your jam, then it's perfect.It reminds me a bit of Don't Starve with the health/hunger meter, but you don't die and have to start completely over or go insane if it gets too low. You simply pass out and wake up elsewhere. I've also been reminded of Stardew Valley and My Time at Portia whilst playing it, at least in the farming and talking to people aspects-- but there's no actual time limit on completing tasks for various people, which makes it more of a casual game that's more story-driven than anything. Even the boat travel, once you've unlocked more than just the main trading island, reminded me of the Crash Bandicoot 3 levels where you had to use the jet ski... though much more workable than old ps1 water travel logic.Like the protagonist, you're trying to find out more about the world you've found yourself in, and what's happened to it around you while you've been blissfully unaware on an island for a few years. It's cute, it's fun, it's lighthearted and yet intriguing enough to continue playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: Even 2 hours in I'm am hooked...the animation quality is excellent and it's not trying to be anything it isn't...just a chill exploration/crafting game with colorful characters and a warm story so far, The food and energy together might be tedious but as easy has it's been to keep them full I'm not worried just yet. Can't wait to see what's next..this and My Time In Portia have both been very good surprises for a person who normally does not like this style of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: To start out this game won't be for everyone. It's a very relaxing, slow paced game. The music and art are just beautiful. The game doesn't hold your hand to much and lets you progress at your own pace. I'm excited to see where the story goes and what the rest of the world has in store. Gameplay involves a lot of grab/grow this and bring it to another person. It takes awhile to grow things so managing your time between crops and planning what to build next is key. UI has its flaws but it also has some great art and design. Controls take no time at all to get used to although menu switching is a little rough sometimes. Changing keybindings would be a nice addition in the future. For now I have setup quick keys on my mouse to handle opening inventory and closing out of dialogs. There are a few graphical bugs where you get stuck every now and then but nothing major yet. Fade animations in between night cycles or story points sometimes show the screen again after fade out but quickly cuts again. Character can get stuck near buildings or odd terrain but usually walking in a different direction or jumping will get you out of it. Your jump in this game is ridiculously high for your character but it can help getting over some terrain faster. All in all I'm excited to see how this game improves. I know a lot of work went into this especially for how small of a team that made it.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A simple, relaxing game that is flawed with a few glitches, and is fundamentally a fetch-quest game, but it's no-consequence and fun.I kickstarted this back when they first announced the game after loving Ankora (a free phone game that Chibig produced), and have only now finally completed the game. The music is lovely, the characters are flawed but grow on you, and the story warms the heart. I got frustrated some times, and the game is not perfect, but I would still recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Summer in Mara

_childDocuments_.review: I played the prologue and was intrigued by the degree of exploration Summer in Mara entails, hence why I decided to buy this game when it was released. I'm thankful that this game has a high fault tolerance- you completed an action before the game releases the quest, but the game still allows you to pass. Lemme explain more...First thing I did after the replay of the prologue was to prepare my fields and plant my carrot seeds instead of completing the first quest. Don't ask me why, I dunno why either. After, I used my axe to break down the well coz dumb me had the axe out when I interacted with the well ._. Then I got to the quest which told me to prepare the fields and plant my carrot seeds, which I already did but it wasn't counted. Well damn, I have no well = no water = crops not growing, did I fudge myself over in the first 10mins of the game? :(So I decided to explore the island and chop down trees in between sleeping through 5 days for the carrots to grow. Lo and behold! The carrots grew without needing water, harvesting them and planting 2 carrot seeds allowed me to pass the quest, whew. The next quest was to break down the old well and used the materials gained to craft a new hammer, which I completed quickly due to dumb me's axe-swinging skills :3There you have it, my first 30mins experience into the game. Despite the rocky start, I'm loving the gameplay, the music, the heaps of stuff there is to do in Summer in Mara because it comes without the feeling of grinding. Definitely glad I got this game <3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, despite there is some issues here and there, but remember its a team of five people, so they are doing the best that they can, and they listen to the fanbase. _childDocuments_.review:
'Summer in Mara' is a summer adventure with easy-RPG elements and farming, crafting, and exploring mechanics set in a tropical archipelago.

'Summer in Mara' is a single player experience in a calm, relaxing environment, with a handmade look and a interesting narrative. You will be Koa, a little adventurer who wants to explore the world that surrounds her.

In 'Summer in Mara' you'll have to take care of your own island, harvest your crops, create new tools and buildings, and sail with your boat to discover new islands and secrets.
KEY FEATURES
- 'Summer in Mara' is an adventure and farming game, with an archipelago full of islands and secrets to explore.

- Day and night cycle with climate events.

- More than 100 quests to make the world a better place.

- Over 20 characters to meet and trade with. Befriend them!

- Improve your boat, make it bigger, better and faster.

- More than 130 inventory items to make, use and trade.

- Unlock and acquire new abilities and skills for Koa, helping her to craft, trade and explore in an easy-RPG system.

You'll have your own island, but taking care of something like that is a lot of hard work. You'll be able to plant trees to get wood and craft new tools and buildings with it. Or create crop fields to grow all kinds of vegetables. You'll also have a farm with chickens and pigs to take care of. But be careful, because this isn't as easy as it looks! You'll also be able to fish in a pond on the island, cut trees with your hatchet, build things with your hammer and use a hoe to help you harvest your island.

Koa will need your help. With an easy-RPG system, she can acquire new abilities and grow stronger. We want you to feel like you're growing up with Koa, bonding with her and with all the other people in the archipelago.

You'll be able to sail to new islands and find treasures and other secrets in the middle of the sea with your trusty boat which you can upgrade with a little effort and time.
With new islands comes new people. You'll talk and trade with over twenty characters, each one with their own story and lifes. They'll give you quests, hints about the world or just anecdotes about their life and travels. Getting to know them is a very important part in the game, so we put much effort in making them unique and interesting.

But not all of the people you find will be friendly. An evil corporation called Elite wants to conquer Mara and exploit the ocean. Napopo is one of their first victims, a strange creature that will seek Koa for help.

name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness
detailed_description: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness is a Lovecraftian point’n’click graphic adventure. Drawing inspiration, places and characters from specific stories by H.P. Lovecraft such as The Shadow Over Innsmouth and The Mountains of Madness, this detective story sets you in the thrilling investigation of a horrifying mystery that will take you to iconic places like Innsmouth, Arkham and the South Pole. You play as the private investigator Lone Carter – but prepare to find yourself in the boots of the Mad Arab Abdul Alhazred, writer of the dreaded Necronomicon, and of H.P. Lovecraft himself… Private Investigator Lone Carter regains consciousness to find himself lying on a beach near Innsmouth. His body has been ripped apart. He tries to pull his last cigarette from the pack, but his arm fails to obey. As he fades away into death, terror growing in his eyes, he remembers in dreadful glimpses his fatal encounter with the Shoggoth… An endless period of darkness ensues. Then, some fire burning within awakens him, and he returns, completely recovered and unharmed – but he would never be the same. He is haunted by terrible visions, nightmares hinting at ineffable, horrifying truths. He needs to get back home, to understand what happened to him – but escaping from Innsmouth will only be the first step in his journey. In his hometown of Arkham, a mystery awaits for him. A disappearance. A ritual murder. A plot that intertwines different characters, different places, even different eras. An adventure that will test your wits and drag you to the very limits of your sanity… and perhaps beyond. Mountains of Madness is a new adventure game in the Chronicle of Innsmouth franchise. Set 10 years before the first chapter of this saga, these events will influence the events to come. Travel to ancient Yemen, playing in the role of the Mad Arab Abdul Alhazred, author of the Necronomicon, and step into the shoes of HP Lovecraft and guide him to unveil the mysteries of his bloodline. Features: - A mature, horrifying story, combining the thrilling mystery of a detective story with a cosmic horror setting - Inspired by The Mountains of Madness, but with many original elements to surprise you at every corner - Test your wits and deduction skills with clever puzzles, logical but challenging - Interact with many characters, both original and taken from Lovecraft’s works - Play as detective Lone Carter, but also as iconic Lovecraft characters as Abdul Alhazred – and even H.P. Lovecraft himself! - Retro art style rendered in 640 x 360 resolution, inspired by the early 90s Lucasarts classics - A brilliant unsettling original soundtrack

Play also as Abdul Alhazred and H.P. Lovecraft himself in this Lovecraftian point’n’click adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better attempts at brining the world of Lovecraft to P&C gaming.  Excellent graphics but can feel light on gameplay and relies heavily on exposition at times.   I think I'll start by asking a philosophical question to you my dear reader: can any idea be brought to all forms of media?  We know that  can.  Star Wars for instance has pretty much all of 'em: movies, tv, books, games, painting, sculpture, music, etc.  I'm sure you can think of more than a few other franchises yourself.  But my original question is can  ?  The reason I ask is that the Cthulhu mythos seems to do best in the world of literature but most attempts at bringing a true representation to any other contemporary media has faced difficulty.  At best, bits and pieces of its themes and ideas have certainly been used in various movies/tv shows/video games.  I have played pretty much all of the big Cthulhu mythos P&C games (including this developers original title Chronicle of Innsmouth which was great), spanning some 30+ years.  This is one of the better ones, however at the end of the day I think a true title that really hits the nail on the squid-faced monsters head still eludes us.---------------------------------------------------------------------------Impressive mastery of retro P&C style.  Excellent artwork and backgrounds.  Sprite design is mostly fantastic.-Also has some nicely drawn comic book style cutscenes.-Fully Voiced-Good background music with original score.  (Credit sequence has a rockin’ metal ending!)-Interactivity highlight function-Has some 90 odd save slots, greatly appreciated and nice to see for once in a 21st century P&C game!-Tutorial for those new to the genre.---------------------------------------------------------------------------Nice to see an option for a classic text style, however the scaling is too large and it takes up too much of the screen during long dialogues.-Voice audio could use some volume balancing.  Recording quality varies slightly at times. -Voice acting itself is also mostly good but can be hit or miss at times as well.-Double click scene exit sometimes works, sometimes doesn't.-Near ending elevator puzzle brought back memories of Star Trek: Final Unity.  If you've played that game and have fond memories of doing so but also remember the puzzle I am referring too here, then you know why this is in the Meh category.-Dialogue is stiff at times.  Couldn't tell if this was to emulate early 20th century speaking prose or was due to a once over by a rigid proofreader.  -After reaching the ending in about 4.5 hours I only got about 66% of the Steam achievements.  I'm not a big achievement guy so I most likely won't be going back for full completion.  For some this might be tedious issue. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------So my main con can be summed up with a question: is this a game or an audiobook?  This game feels like one exposition dump after another, starting with a rather long intro.  To me, this is a no-no in making a good P&C game.  Good P&C's should feel immersive and require constant interaction between the game and the player.  Every time a game pauses for an overly long cutscene or dialogue sequence, forcing the player to just sit back and listen, breaks that immersion.  You'll notice in my question I said game or .  If you have these long expositional transitions but there is still some action going on screen (i.e. actual animation) then it turns into something more like watching a movie or an interactive fiction game.  But if you literally are just reading text that is being displayed on screen with a black background, now your just an audiobook.  Like most modern P&C's from independent studios this is a Kickstarter game which means limited budget.  I still don't give it a pass on this faux pas, but I at least understand why they went that route (assuming it was due to budgetary constraints).  At the end of the day they did release a finished game which is more than a lot of Kickstarters can say.  -I've said it before and I'll say it again, I understand that I as a P&C afficionado owe a debt of gratitude to the Adventure Game System (AGS) game engine.  It basically is responsible for the modern P&C renaissance.  But WHY OH GOD WHY after 20+ years do we still have this AGS setup screen at the beginning of some games that use it?!?!  I don't know and don't care about the various scaling options, which MIDI source, or how large a sprite cache to pick.  Do I want to activate the setting to use a 60hz CRT monitor? NO!  How about language selection, do I want "English" or perhaps "English2" (this is an actual setting choice btw).  I barely know one English (just look at my writing) and I've been speaking it my whole damn life. Just. Start. The. Game.  It is 2021, there is no retro pixel P&C game in existence that will bog down even the lamest new computers out there.  This is an unnecessary thing to have and every time I see it, it irks me. -I'm now exhausted from that last heading so I will make this one brief but I could easily go into a pointless diatribe about it as well. Save features should always be available at any point during any game, full stop.  What if I gotta go see what the dogs barking at?  Or I want something to eat? Or my boss is looking over my shoulder?  Or I gotta take a S***?  Now I have to exit and then re-play something I already did.  Granted in this game that would only be at most a few minutes of replay in most cases, but life is short.  Just have save always available plz thanks.    Rereading the above I feel that I am being tough on this game.  I want to reiterate that it will def hit the spot for the P&C aficionado and Lovecraft enthusiast.  If you want to support a developer that was passionate about their project and you have the financial means to do so, buy it at full price.  This game as of writing is rarely on sale but I did manage to catch it for a 10% discount.  I'm not mad at the price I paid for this, but I'd have been happier if some of the issues I listed were delt with.      👑  👑⠀⠀⠀

_childDocuments_.review: Travel back to 1920’s Arkham and join Lone Carter in a mysterious investigation somewhat competently integrated into H.P. Lovecraft’s novella At the Mountains of Madness.Coming from Italian developers PsychoDev and made in Adventure Game Studio, it’s a point and click throwback to the glory days of adventure games from the 80s and 90s and a prequel to the Chronicle of Innsmouth from 2017. It’s set 10 years before the first game, but it’s not necessary to know the story of the original to enjoy this one.Just comparing the visuals to the first one, it’s obvious how much of a facelift’s been done here. Great pixel art, well animated characters and scenery, some really impressive areas and backgrounds and a very snazzy map of Arkham. I’m less impressed with the character voices. They’re not terrible and the main character’s voice is really well done, but a lot of them are kind of spotty and have this grating, mechanical feeling to them. Like they were recorded on a poor microphone or edited badly. The soundtrack fared much better, producing some nice pieces and even doing some, almost power metal vibes. Who would’ve thought that went well with Lovecraft?Story cutscenes are a mixed bunch. The best ones come in the form of animated comic-like panels and these are very nicely done. As is the norm for adventure games, a lot of exposition is done through in-game conversations where the player doesn’t have any control and these are not skippable, except the dialogue in some cases. The problem is, for a rather short game, there’s a bit too much player downtime. The worst offender visually are, no spoilers, some scene transitions that occur on a blank, beige screen with text and voice overs. That was kind of jarring every time.The story follows Lone Carter, a private investigator that looks, speaks and acts like he got pulled straight out of a comic noir into the Miskatonic County by forces unknown. The game also occasionally switches control to different characters, including Abdul Alhazred, author of the fabled Necronomicon and even H.P. Lovecraft himself. Without any spoilers, the story intertwines Lone’s search for answers to his condition after being touched by too many tentacles from the Beyond, investigations of grisly ritual murders and the original plot of the Mountains of Madness, but with less geological surveys and science talk. And it mostly succeeds.There are some abrupt character switches, a slightly underwhelming feeling of dread, some loss of focus, a few overly long cutscenes and a few tries at some light humour, which I think doesn’t sit well with Mountains of Madness. But, there are also some great, gory murder scenes, good characters and solid puzzles that don’t overstay their welcome or break the flow. Intuitive environmental clues, no needless inventory items or fiddling, no pixel hunting, very simple controls and interactive points highlighting will all help your brain not get consumed by madness within.The game is also filled with lots of references to Lovecraft’s other works and characters and just has a general feeling of smoothness, gently nudging you where you need to go next. I’ve never felt stuck in my 6 hour run time. I’ve also found at least one possible death scene, there may be more, but the game just put me right before my poorly thought out decision to run into a hail of bullets.I ran into some technical issues with the Steam overlay. I was running the game in 1920×1200, but the game uses 1920×1080 and puts black bars at the top and bottom. In full screen, when I brought up the overlay and then turned it off, it stayed visible on the black bars at the top and bottom. The highlight icons for interactive points also stayed displayed when I turned off the overlay. And I’ve managed to break the game by saving it with the highlights always visible after turning the overlay on and off and when I tried loading the game, it repeatedly crashed, always giving the same error, overlay not found. It seems that might be an issue with AGS and not necessarily the game. Switching to windowed mode solved the visible overlay issues, but it didn't solve the highlights staying visible and game freezing. Avoiding Steam overlay seems to be a good course of action, for now.For all the slight hiccups and issues I mentioned, Mountains of Madness still carries itself competently. It’s an interesting and enjoyable story, with simple game dynamics, tackling Lovecraft’s earlier work in a new light by adding a detective story into the mix. It certainly did push me to peek at the first chapter of the saga. I’m not really thrilled with the asking price of 17.99€, which is along with the issues it has and the short running time, the reason why I’d recommend getting this on sale.: 2 achievements aren't working, the devs are looking into it. Lots of missable achievements, like doing puzzles on the first try and clicking on certain things in the environment. It took me around 6 hours for a playthrough, so it's not a long running time. It's a new game, so there aren't any guides yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Masterpiece? Nah. It's a good adventure game, though. The artwork is really good, the voice acting is not so good. Everyone pronounces everything differently and it really started to get annoying by the end of the game. _childDocuments_.review: Short review: Buy this game if you are a fan of HP Lovecraft and adventure games, and if this game is on sale.Less Short Review:I truly wanted to give a good review to this game, because Psychodev are obviously a small team with love for the Cthulhu mythos, but the underlying adventure game is just too rough around the edges. Pros:  - You get to play as several interesting characters, including the classic down-on-his luck PI, HP Lovecraft himself, and Abdul Alhazred, original author of the necronomicon.- For fans of the mythos, many characters, stories and concepts are played upon quite well.Cons: - The underlying adventure game has a few good puzzles, but a lot are not satisfying to solve and a few are frustrating, tedious, and require a lot of back and forth. - Average voice acting- In my case, two game breaking bugs that made me lose all progress from the last manual save (and the autosave never actually saved my game...)So in summary: if you want your Cthulhu fix, go check out Reign of the Old Ones, and for good puzzles try out The Room.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: While it can be rough in places (voice acting being the most egregious), I thoroughly enjoyed the journey. The P&C gameplay was perfectly serviceable, and I personally really liked the comic style art and cutscenes. Its obviously made by a very small team but the fact that its also a labor of love is just as obvious. Its also a huge step forward from the previous game, which I also liked but Mountains of Madness is so much better in just about every way.It also takes a great deal more liberty with the events of various stories than its predecessor, making for a unique work of fiction set in the same Lovecraftian universe rather than a straightforward retelling of At the Mountains of Madness. Its a perfectly good game, and I'm sure anyone with a passing interest could enjoy it. However this is where I have to go off the rails a little and say that as someone very invested in cosmic horror and R'lyehean lore, almost every detail from names, to locations, to key items is 100% deliberate. You don't need to catch every reference to enjoy this game for what it is, but its something I found absolutely delightful. It stands alone as a narrative but is also an endless basket of Easter eggs.You can tell this was made by someone who really knows and understands the reference material, and I give it an enthusiastic 8 out of... ten...tacles.I'll see myself out now.

_childDocuments_.review: I was drawn to this game by its visuals and retro charm. I expected an intriguing detective story with supernatural elements.However, the game is pretty much a complete letdown. The story is dull, as are the characters and the dialogue. I didn't grow to care about any of the characters, and sometimes they would yammer on for what seemed like ages. The scenes, although beautifully drawn, are desolate with very little to do. Plenty of objects can be clicked on, giving only boring responses in the vein of 'I can't do that.'. Such wasted potential. This is, at best, an amateurish effort. I'm sure a certain amount of time and effort went into making it and I don't want to diminish that, but to be honest, I would only be somewhat impressed by the game if this were a free title. If you can manage to get it in a sale for a couple of euros, and you are drawn to Lovecraftian themes, then sure, try it. Yikes.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to say it, but I did not enjoy this.  I'm a fairly diehard Lovecraft fan, and even then I was pretty bored. About half way through the game it switches gears into really exposition heavy text scrawls that shatter the show-don't-tell rule and kind of abandons the whole purpose of playing a game.It's not a "bad game" per se, but I just didn't enjoy it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this is a masterpiece. No adventure gamer should miss this for any reason.The strength of this game is in its atmosphere: here, Mountains of Madness equals masterpieces such as Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis. And indeed you are going to have Indiana Jones vibes through all the game. Psychodev studio clearly has talent in creating immersive atmospheres. They achieve this in different ways: the stunning graphics is full of exotic and evocative locations; the amazing and evocative music is never repetitive and never intrusive, but manages to talk to your subconscious and increase the experience; the presence of a party of companions, who follow you through all your adventure; the many differeent flashbacks, which increase the variety of the settings; many small details such as the flickering lights or the animated clouds; the many comic-style cutscenes which highlight the key moments in the story; the english voiceover which is very expressive and competent.Gameplay-wise, the puzzles are good, varied, make sense in the context, are of medium/hard difficulty, are fair, and have just the right amount of clues. And, most importantly, they do not feel like arbitrary roadblocks.So just how good is this game? I honestly think it is one of the best adventure games i ever played--and I played hundreds of them. In my top 10 certainly, together with Indiana Jones 4, Monkey Island 1 and 2, Loom, and Thimbleweed Park.

_childDocuments_.review: For the unaware, Innsmouth is a pretty crumby place to live. Private detective, Lone Carter, certainly didn’t seem to enjoy his stay during 2017 point & click adventure, The Chronicles of Innsmouth, but I couldn’t tell you for sure. I missed that particular game. Mountains of Madness is either a prequel or a sequel (or maybe both; what importance is our perception of time in the face of cosmic horror?), but immediately offers you a recap of what you may have missed. Lone was hired to try and retrieve the wayward brother of a Miskatonic university lecturer, but found much more than he was searching for. The brother didn’t make it out alive and nor, seemingly, did Lone. His last few memories show him chased through an underground labyrinth by an impossible swarm of tendrils. He does not win the race. Missing limbs and broken beyond repair, the last we should see of Lone is how he drags himself out of the cave complex to quietly bleed out on an abandoned shore.That’s not what happens. Lone awakes in far from perfect shape, but the arm and leg that had been torn from him seemed to be in considerably better condition than they should be. They were no longer absent, for one. With significantly more questions than answers, Lone’s immediate attention focuses on escaping the isolated shore and, ultimately, getting the hell out of Innsmouth. If he hopes answers await in the town of Arkham, he’s going to be disappointed.Perhaps you’ve been clued in by the game’s name, but the main thrust of the plot is powered by H.P. Lovecraft’s story “The Mountains of Madness''. But the tale of an Antarctic expedition gone horribly wrong doesn’t immediately become Lone’s concern. Laudably, developers Pyschodev aren’t particularly interested in just unearthing Lovercraftian tales wholesale and transplanting them into an adventure game facsimile, but they take inspirations from across several tales and stitch them together to make a story of their own. Lone Carter certainly never came from H.P.’s pen, but existing fans will find plenty of names and places to recognise, borrowed from several different tales, existing either as sly Easter eggs, or used to help drive the macabre story forward.Mountains of Madness: The Game takes the scenic route before you get to the content directly supplied by “Mountains of Madness”; the novel. Lone’s failed investigation and the Arctic expedition are both linked by Miskatonic university, but there’s plenty of morbid discoveries to make before seeking out considerably more hostile climates. There seems to be some kind force, impatiently nudging the investigation along, trying to manoeuvre all the pieces into place. Lone’s guided towards the horrific murder of a student in the nearby slums, a quartered corpse left hanging from the rafters, a rough diagram sketched beneath in its own clogging blood. Witness leads run cold, some people having simply vanished, others confined to the madhouse. The local bookstore owner needs a list of collectable short stories stolen from his arch rival before he’ll provide much needed information. It can’t all be courting insanity and wading through gore, I suppose.
