_childDocuments_.review: Great art and atmosphere, engaging story and interesting characters. I'd say it's still a little weaker than its predecessor because the gameplay and puzzles are limited and simplified with the game literally turning into a movie for whole parts. Still, it was fun and I welcome trying to do things differently, but know I have given games  the thumb down for similar issues. The other qualities save this one from that fate. Speaking of being saved from one's fate ... will you be able to escape yours? Find out in this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the previous one, one of the better lovecraft games out there. But I can't recommend anyone to play this one. The voice acting is stale, they mix bad looking vector art in for the cutscenes, the dialogs overexplain everything to the point it becomes tiresome, the plot doesn't really go anywhere interesting and then it suddenly ends, the puzzles are few and terrible, and a lot of the second part is walking from npc a to npc b to unlock new places to examine in the most boring area where every npc looks the same. Not worth getting even on sale, I literally had to force myself to finish this because I was far in too deep already and it bugged me leaving it unfinished but I had to take breaks because of how boring it is. Oh, and worst part? They literally shove a narrator in who just reads text at you telling you what's going on instead of it actually happening... show don't tell has to be the most basic guideline for a game to follow but this game doesn't even manage that.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: "Mountains of Madness" is an atmospheric, compact and overall polished point and click adventure, who gives its own due homage to the source material and its gameplay-wise inspirations (Lucas Arts adventure games, especially "Fate of Atlantis"), while keeping its own strong autonomy and dignity. PLOT AND CHARACTERSThe setting is surprisingly immersive and mind-blowing, the plot is good with its own sparks, even if rarely shines: some narrative solutions felt forced and other underused, left wanting for more. But I experienced worse, FAR worse in my gaming career. The main character, Lone Carter, albeit the cliché-y hard-boiled detective, is a surprisingly strong and well written one from start to end, unfortunately the supporting cast doesn’t fly at the same height, but I've never felt them to be a burden.GAMEPLAYThe puzzles are the true gem of this piece of work: well designed, logical and craftly balanced, and even with some (inevitable) hiccups here and there, they are perfectly embedded with the storyline and almost never seem arbitrary or requires “moon logic” to be solved. We hit “top-notch” ground here!GRAPHICS AND SOUNDOn the tech side, MoM has good quality graphics (gotta love that pixel-art, motion comics interludes and hand drawn backgrounds), good animations, great original music (some themes will give you a chill or two, and the end credits theme is awesome) and a well-polished interface.FINAL THOUGHTSIf you are into Lovecraft “weird tales” and old school graphic adventures, you’ll hardly find something better, so don’t miss it. If not, consider to buy it on sale, worst case scenario you’ll lose just a few bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: This and the prequel were excellent games, I thought the point and click gameplay would be off-putting but as fans of the genre know, there's not much the protagonist can do except follow the story, and what a story it was. Tastefully combining several lovecraft classics into a way that made sense for this type of game was fun and definitely recommend to other fans of lovecraft.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: It was fun to play, I liked the artwork in the cutscenes (even though the main character's moustache seemed to change from scene to scene... sometimes it is a full on moustache, other times he has the thick chin strap), and it progressed quickly enough to remain interesting (with the exception of the archives lady... really?).I understood most of the puzzles with the exception of the pressure plates in the forest (I still don't get it, I had to look up the answer). There were a few "adventure game moments" where you knew what to do but couldn't until you triggered it. This led to a bit of the walk around and talk to everyone again, click on everything again, and combine everything again, but it wasn't overly time consuming.Overall, it is a great new adventure game that is worth the time if you like the subject matter and the previous instalment. I wouldn't say it is a scary or atmospheric game, but it is definitely an adventure/mystery hybrid. I kinda missed "THE DOG CAN DO A BETTER JOB!" guy, but maybe he will be in a future game. Lastly, thank goodness there were no quicktime events... Adventure games and quicktime don't mix!Thanks for the fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game that I've ever decided to refund here. Thankfully, the steam support approved my refund request really quick. I am a big Lovecraft fan and I am really into Point-and-Click games. However, this game is unplayable for me since right after finishing the tutorial  the screen just turns black. The sound is still on and I can hear characters talking, so the game is still running. But I can't do anything due to the black screen and I had to use the task manager to close it. I've tried twice and it was the same result. As it turns out, this issue has been encountered by many other players as shown in the Bugs & Tech issues thread in the steam discussion section. It looks like the Developer was aware of this issue but it never got fixed after all these years. I guess this game doesn't run well with AMD or something. In addition, I just wanted to point out the voice acting was kinda awful and robotic, which really took me out of it during the short time that I was able to play the game (i.e. the tutorial).

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell: Too slow. Too much wasted time. Too many conversations/cutscenes/mini-games that don't add a lot. It looks nice, very much like an old-fashioned point and click adventure, but it could have been so much better.Also, forcing me to sit though the credits for several minutes BEFORE starting the game for the first time is the best way for the developers/publishers to never get a penny from me again.

_childDocuments_.review: That's one of the worst point and click Lovecraft inspired games I ever played. I tried to be understanding and forgiving, but unfortunately I just can't. Nothing in this game makes sense. The music is godawful, it doesn't match the intended vibe. We get generic happy music when there's something tragic/scary happening on the screen, generic playful music when the characters are speaking about Great Old Ones and.... some kind of metal music on end credits?? The graphics are boring and bland (everything's plain, gray and lacks life), the map is unreadable and boring-looking as hell, the last sequence's map is also a tragedy - it shows that nobody wanted this game to truly look good. The used pixel art style for characters' design is strange, they look like they've been taken straight our of a parody. Voice acting is meh, puzzles are also meh, even the main character is bland and meh. I wanted to give this game a chance, I really wanted to do that - I am a big fan of Lovecraft and I love everything Lovecraft-related. This game though? Don't buy it. Or maybe buy it when there's a sale for like a 2 dollars and you finished all other point and click games ever created. I paid around 15 dollars for it and it wasn't worth it. The creators didn't want to make a good Lovecraft-inspired game, they wanted to make a game served in bland, plain, beige-like gravy. And it doesn't taste good. Avoid this title.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: This graphic adventure is a prequel to "Chronicle of Innsmouth", from the same software house, and focuses on one of its minor characters, bringing him under the spotlight.The changes since the previous games are mostly improvements.The game interface is very simplified and, rather than having the usual nine actions, only two mouse buttons are used: right-click to examine, left-click to talk/push/pull/open/close/get/use/whatever. The istant deaths are also greatly reduced and are actually so few that there is a special achievement for getting them all. Likewise, there are fewer skill games and the only real annoying one can be skipped.Is it a perfect game? Nope. The plot is too "railroaded" and most problems are solved just clicking everywhere one the screen and with "try to use everything with everything". Furthermore one has the impression that a few subplot had to be "cut" during the development and many secondary characters serve no purpose at all. Most annoying of all during replays is the inability to skip cutscenes (hitting "Esc" won't do), some of which are a few MINUTES long.Graphics, musics and voices are decent but nothing more.In the end, you should only choose this game if you are a hardcore H.P. fan and if it's in offer; otherwise it's just an overpriced and forgettable graphic adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to like this game and the previous Chronicle of Innsmouth I find the puzzles and the interface are too obtuse to get any enjoyment out of it. For example in the early part of the story there's an interactive cabinet from which you retrieve an object. At no point does the game train you that there may be more than one thing in a location and that things like cabinets can have multiple hotspots. After 30 minutes of trying everything I could think of I eventually looked up a solution which told me to search the top of the cabinet for the missing item. Add in the poor voice acting and I just can't recommend this game. I played the first game and had to also give up on that with some other obtuse and annoying things but had hoped they had cracked the code in the sequel. Sadly, they have not
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: Graphic adventure that throw me back to the past, fantastic pixel art in a perfect retro-game style.An horror story worthy of Lovecraft's tales, dark and gloomy setting at times gore.Original and pleasant soundtrack.Most likely I will also play the first chapter of the saga, hopefully waiting for the arrival of a third chapter ...
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I would say this story need to be rewritten from scratch to work. It fails as adaptation of the original work hard. No build up to the city, fascinating discoveries of the unknown having created all life and our place in the universe, no chase from the monster, no penguins. And only about 20% takes place in antarctic.As for on its own legs, it is also really fails on its own. The Lucasarts charm from the first one is blasted straight off this one, barely any fun in it, characters aren't great, so why care if they die? For plot reasons the main character is also invincible and will ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ murder anything that threatens him, which makes it so it is never scary. The puzzles are sub-par, there is a lot of nonsense with secret societies that totally undermines the lovecraft themes of these things being out of our control, main character is bland and there is very little to enjoy in this one. Stick to the first one, this is like a 4/10. I hope Psychodev makes a better project next time. This feels like the start to some kinda "Lovecraft Game Universe", apparently forgetting that Lovecraft already kinda made his stories like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent point and click adventure game, always fun to see more of Cthulhu Mythos adventure games. Some awkward voice acting and writing moments included yeah, such as two separate situations where a character suddenly snaps at another and is incredibly rude. Hard to tell if that is writing/translation problem or voice acting problem
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome sequel to the first game, with significantly improved graphics and much more detailed animations. The control scheme is simplified and it's so much better. The atmosphere rocks. But even after finishing the game twice I'm still confused about the story. I guess everything doesn't have to make sense in a lovecraftian story.But please, next time get a new game engine and let AGS finally die. That prehistoric engine can't even handle alt-tabbing, it crashed several times and often got stuck in fullscreen, forcing me to restart the whole machine.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: The developers have come a long way from their Chronicles of Innsmouth adventure game.  From what I've seen so far, the graphics have been greatly improved in both cut scenes and regular gameplay with a few truly incredible landscapes.  The voice acting seems better as well.  The puzzles, for the most part, seem logical though there are a couple that had me looking to the internet to figure out; WTF Graveyard church altar.The story has so far been good though the narrative technique doesn't seem cohesive.  This one is a little hard for me to explain fully but it seems like the developers weren't sold on a particular story telling technique or weren't sure how to transition from one narrative technique to another.  Maybe I'm missing something but there were a few moments that interrupted the flow in an abrasive way for me.Overall, I'm really happy with my purchase.  It's a good adventure in the old LucasArts "Day of the Tentacle", "Monkey Island" style of point-and-click games with a strong Cthulhu Mythos background.  They really improved their skills in development and it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: While somewhat pricey, I can tell a lot of care went into making this game. With eldritch horror, there are generally two sorts of approaches. The first involves trying to explain everything and the second explains little, leaving the player only able to guess at what is happening around them. This game falls more squarely in the former camp, providing a lot of details from the background lore and also presenting the narrative in a way that  lessens the horror and instead impacts drama and action.It's overall an enjoyable experience and one I would recommend, although some of the puzzles did need some additional signage in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Chronicle of Innsmouth: Mountains of Madness

_childDocuments_.review: The second chapter in the "Chronicle of Innsmouth" saga. A team of scientists are attempting to be the first to reach a previously unknown chain of mountains higher than the Himalayas. Within a huge cavern they discover the alien bodies of hithertofore unknown creatures frozen in the ice walls.

name: Prodeus
detailed_description: Prodeus is a first-person shooter of old, re-imagined using modern rendering techniques and technology. Experience the quality you’d expect from a modern AAA game, designed with retro aesthetics and gameplay that invoke the tech-imposed limits of older hardware. The game features a hand-crafted campaign from industry FPS veterans, co-op and competitive multiplayer play drawing on classic modes*, a fully integrated level editor, and a built-in community map browser for instantaneous action with nearly limitless levels to play. Get ready to paint the walls red. This is the Boomer Shooter you’ve been waiting for. FEATURES Retro look, modern era Shooters past and present collide with graphics that combine today’s high-quality 3D tech with retro visuals. Experience over-the-top explosions of lo-fi pixels and hi-tech particle effects as you clash against the Prodeans and forces of Chaos. Pure retro FPS chaos Steel yourself for fast and frantic nonstop action. Blast and blaze your way through hordes of chaos-spawned creatures using an arsenal of classically over-the-top weapons. Raining red Splatter the steel walls and alien halls with the blood of your enemies. Experience the gory thrills of the elder shooters, dialed up to 11 thanks to Prodeus’s delightfully demented dismemberment system. Community-crafted levels Unleash your inner map designer with Prodeus’s powerful but easy-to-use level editor, and keep the visceral combat fresh with a built-in browser filled with community-created maps. Multiplayer Mayhem Team up and go head-to-head in a variety of multiplayer modes. Take on the campaign in 4-player co-op, and dive into the fray in 16-player Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, CTF, and more—then take things to the next level by creating and sharing custom game modes. Frag to the Music Burst blood vessels listening to a supercharged metal soundtrack by retro FPS composer Andrew Hulshult that dynamically changes gears to accompany your actions.

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game, but the current "Nexus Point" system is pretty baffling. Essentially, whenever you "die", you respawn at one of these points but everything stays as it was when you died, level progress is retained and any enemies you killed stay dead. It removes any sense of challenge as you can just throw yourself repeatedly at any encounter until you win with practically no consequence. At this point all that changing the difficulty affects is how frequently you'll have to walk back to wherever you died which is obviously not the most fun or interesting thing. You might as well just have godmode on. And no, just clicking "Restart Level" everytime you die is not a solution. I know some people like this system and that's great, but having the option to use a more traditional checkpoint system would be much appreciated. Seeing as a Quick Save/Load option is being added, this should be a relatively easy addition. It stings even more because everything else about the game is really good, the level design is fantastic and all of the weapons feel great to use.Not a bad game by any means, but if you're looking for a genuinely challenging experience and don't want to deal with just restarting at the beginning of the level everytime you die, you might be disappointed,

_childDocuments_.review: Loved Doom and Quake since they came out, but haven't played many boomer shooters, nor been that interested in new FPS generally for the last few years. Picked this up because it looked cool, and like a modern Doom, and I really like it so far.It's made to look retro but it's also beautiful, with effects we could only dream of back in the day. Level design is spot-on and feels just like it could have been made by the original Doom and Quake teams. Movement feels just like Quake, including jumping and air control. Having to jump up ramps and find bits of geometry to climb up and hop between to find items and secrets makes me nostalgic for the first time I explored the levels in those old games.The weapons, while (so far at least) the standard categories, are actually where the game diverges a little from the old ones it's clearly influenced by. Combat is a little more tactical than in Doom or Quake, since you have to reload and weapons also have extra modes like burst-fire while zooming down in a little for sniping at a distance. It means a bit more ducking behind cover to reload and then pop out to pick off the next enemy than running around like a crazy person, although there is plenty of that as well (especially when the game occasionally forces it on you, which makes a cool change and hasn't been overdone so far). Then again, maybe I just can't remember how cautious I was the first time I played Doom or Quake, before I knew the layouts, enemy placements, ambushes and surprises? Either way, this isn't a downside and the combat is really good, just slightly different to what I expected.Blood and gore is completely over the top, with entire rooms ending up painted red after a fight. I am certain Doom would have done the same thing had the technology been available back in the day, so this seems completely fitting with the 90s shooter theme and I am into it, although the amount of blood flying around does occasionally make it hard to see what's going on, haha.Music feels like it came straight out of Doom 2016, which is no bad thing.Difficulty level seems fine, playing on Very Hard and losing health and dying once or twice in the first few levels but not excessively. I wouldn't recommend playing on the easier difficulties though, unless you're new to the genre or something.Despite the game being first person, and the way enemies are rendered, it has not made me feel motion/sim-sickness, which I tend to get quite easily with some engines and FOVs these days (one reason I don't play that many new FPS). That's really pleasing, and hopefully will be the same for you if that's something that effects you.Loading times are good, and the game doesn't waste your time with BS like endless cutscenes or bad game design like Doom Eternal's constant "surrender control and watch this glory-kill micro-cutscene for the 50000th time or you'll have no ammo" nonsense. You're always in control, and you spend your time blasting things and (if you're so inclined) trying to find and reach things, as it should be in a videogame.If you're looking for a modern throwback to the 90s single-player FPS genre, you can't really go wrong with this.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl; DrWhen Bethesda’s Doom is grown up, it wants to be just like Prodeus. Tl; Dr No.2This game is so good it deserves more than a single one-liner. Prodeus is an excessively good shooter which actually demands skill, positioning, reflexes and strafing. The game is ridiculously well balanced and yet the design will not hinder you from using your shotgun 90 percent of the time. This game is the exact opposite of everybody’s darling Doom Eternal which at the end of the day amounts to a game of rock paper scissors.++	Excellent sound design++	Excellent music++	Excellent weapon design++	Superb secondary fire modes++	You actually have to RELOAD. No more firing 300 shots with your shotgun like in a 80ies action movie. This little mechanic adds exactly that kind of tactical thinking that Doom Eternal tried so hard to implement with its rock paper scissor enemy-weapon dynamic.++	great balance! EVERY weapon has its meaning. Heck, I am still using the pistol since it is a good way to eliminate mid-range enemies. And yet you are not forced to use ell 9 different weapons in a single engagement like in Doom Eternal++	I cannot express how GOOD the weapons feel++	there are and will be more weapons than your usual 9++	hands down my favourite shotgun in a video game! ++	excellent checkpoints and dying doesn’t mean you have to do all the tedious shooting from the checkpoint again and again since the game memorizes the kills you made. It might make the game a bit too easy, especially since you spawn with full health. However, I prefer this to tedious busy-work.++	runs incredibly well and stable on my system++	fast-paced movement but you won’t get punished for going slowly++	superficially you could lament that the levels are very similar but damn is the level design deep and surprising and varied! You might need to have a brain to appreciate that though! ++	level editor and very easy to download new maps in-game. I have only tried 2 custom maps now but they were very good and suprisingly different from the vanilla maps. --	you can’t kick (and it wouldn’t make sense because the enemies have no throwback physics) but already numerous times I wished I could disengage with a proper melee attack--	maybe the Shotgun gets too much ammo and hence you are using it all the time. Then again: damn, does one feel naked IF the ammo runs out. --	as of yet there is no assault rifle in the game, only dual-wielded SMGs. We need a proper beefy AR! --	the asking price might seem a bit steep but I have definitively paid more for less. And considering that a lot is still to come (new weapons, new maps, new enemy types) and also considering the overall polish of the game, I think it is worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 2016 the demake.If you want a proper review watch Civvie or Yahtzee's videos on it.That being said, I will say that the level design is f*cking phenomenal. It has an extremely good 3d automap which you will never use because getting lost in this game is basically impossible. Which is especially impressive cause the levels are for the most part not especially colorful, so they mostly achieve this by making the various rooms look very distinctive and stand out from each other. Seriously, if you want an example of level design done right, this is a prime example.Another thing I want to say is that the feel of the weapons and especially the sound design for them is great. This game probably has the most satisfying sounding basic pistol of any fps I've ever played. So good. And it never becomes completely useless even when you get better weapons. It's fast, it's accurate, and it packs a punch. And the sound on that gatling gun? Mm mm. Nice. It's a real meat grinder of a weapon and it looks, sounds and feels the part. Well done devs. Oh and the homing minimissiles? Pure joy.I will say though, the railgun could do with a damage boost. Not being able to consistently one shot the not cacodemons is pretty sh*tty. Not being able to one shot the gatling gunners either also sucks.But yeah, all in all, I really like this game. It's been a blast to play, and it has a lot less of that f*cking obnoxious secret finding that plagued Doom 2016 so much. I don't want to explore levels, I just want to f*cking shoot things until they die. I feel like this game gets that.I will say that this game is pretty easy, so if you want an actual challenge then play on something higher than medium.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently in Early Access, so I'll keep this short...Current Pros:  Solid gun play, with some lovely sound effects and design going on.  Pace is brisk, and you never feel slow; like all classic shooters, you should be moving at all times.  Visually it's a treat; I personally really dig the aesthetic they have going on with this one.  Good music, but I think its Hulshult's weakest work right now.  Developers also seem to be taking comments seriously, and making great progress.  Also, works perfectly via Proton for me.Current Cons:  I won't comment on length at the moment, as it is still early access.  However I will comment on difficulty.  Personally I feel it leans toward the easy side, making the game feel a little dull (at times) as a result.  Enemy variety is pretty lacking, which contributes to a samey feeling.  Some weapons felt pretty much useless (alt fire on the plasma gun comes to mind) where as others were hilariously OP (you can snipe with the shotgun's alt fire for example).  Challenge maps felt pointless, as they weren't even a challenge.  Game needs quite a bit of balance tweaking as a result.  Biggest sin:  It borrows way too much from Doom 1/2/2016.  It has almost no identity as a result.  They frankly need to retool some of their designs into something more original.  There is a great game coming, but right now it feels like a literal Doom clone...If you're down with the Boomer Shooter trend like I am, this is a good buy; even in Early Access.  It has it's issues right now, but I am looking forward to where they take it.  If you're on the fence though; wait till release.

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is an interesting game, and I am somewhat divided on recommending it. Straightforward and entertaining for a shooter, a healthy variety of weapons, most lore being in the form of info dumps at the start and/or end of levels. Locational damage dismemberment are certainly a plus. That said, the campaign it shipped with ends on a cliffhanger and there is no real resolution or explanation for what is going on. _childDocuments_.review: Don't let the appearance fool you: This game isn't mindlessly chasing nostalgia points, nor is it aping modern-isms inanely. Prodeus is a surprisingly well-polished creation already, sporting not only gorgeously gothic-industrial levels but also gloriously fine-tuned combat. Locational damage is a welcome addition, and plays into the almost  feel of the guns; the hulking, blood-frenzied mutants can take an entire shotgun mag to kill...or one well-placed charge shot, if you aim for the head and hold that charge to its maximum.Ammunition balance is tight. The levels flow like water. Your movement is rapid and agile, though the minigun  slow you down while you fire it, so be careful about that. Enemies are both immediately readable in the thick of it--the silhouettes are really well-defined, and even with the resolution scaled down I can easily tell what I'm fighting, despite the limited palette. The fact that there's already a built-in level editor is promising.I want deathmatch.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: While Prodeus is certainly a great game overall, there's a huge, glaring flaw the devs will seemingly never acknowledge, let alone address; Nexus points. If you die, you respawn with full health at a "Nexus point", but with ZERO setback. Any enemies you've killed stay dead, any keys/items you found remain in your inventory, and any progress you made is kept. This essentially gives the player godmode, and makes the health and armor system pointless, because a player can die an endless number of times with no functional gameplay penalty. This means you can just mindlessly throw yourself at enemies over and over with no strategy and still succeed just because their attacks are meaningless when you'll just revive with no loss of progress whatsoever. (Sure you won't get the "highest score possible", but 99% of players don't care about minmaxing a meaningless number they see once at the end of a level and never care about again, they want death to matter more directly in the gameplay itself.)I'd much rather take a standard "checkpoint" system where it autosaves your progress at a nexus point, and just reloads that save with whatever health/ammo/items/progress you had at that point, or a "lives" system where you get 3 free nexus point respawns, but if you die after running out you have to restart the level, or even a basic "lose your weapons and ammo where you died and have to go pick them back up". At the moment I'd take literally anything over the godmode system we currently have.It takes all of the challenge and thus fun out of the game for me, having basically a cheat turned on that cannot be turned off. As a Kickstarter backer I'm disappointed and frustrated they seemingly ignore any and all complaints about the Nexus system, so I cannot in good faith recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Easy recommendation if you're looking to scratch that Doom Eternal itch.Good blend of the old and the new. Modern mechanics mixed with a pixelated art style that still pulls off quite an impressive amount of detail coupled with a great soundtrack. Combat is fast paced, brutal and bloody. When it comes down to just shooting enemies its as about as gratifying as it gets.The guns aren't anything we haven't seen before however they all feel fresh to the player. They're loud, feel heavy and hit hard. The sound design for the weapons is just amazing.In its current state you're probably going to get about 4-5 hours of playtime. However the road for new maps, weapons and other content is promising. It even comes with a fully integrated map maker that is already being put to work by the community and pumping out some great maps. Price tag is probs going to turn a lot of players away but if FPS games are your jam then Prodeus is right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Only got through three levels so far, but there's not much chance this game is ever getting boring or bad in any way. The gunplay is so solid, you really feel the punch of the guns and how destructive they are. Blood splatters everywhere, limbs dismembered, lots of enemies being nailed down by fast-shooting weapons...it has all the thrills any old-school shooter had in the golden days and more.The graphics are superb. A neat mix between the old and the modern. The level design is so good as well. From the maps i played i can say they really knew their thing when building it. Considering the accessible price tag and the fact it's still an EA game, with lots of room for improvement, i just can't recommend it enough. If you love old-school shooters, this is a must buy. _childDocuments_.review: is a pretty solid entry in the recent glut of FPS throwbacks, occupying that general space of retro high-speed gunplay, densely tangled levels filled with secrets and monster closets, and high quantities of enemies with fairly simplistic tracking behaviors that's intentionally evocative of  (1993), , and .  More than any of those games, though,  seems intentionally evocative of  (2016), itself a polished, high-budget throwback game to earlier installments in its own franchise.  The Prodeus-Guy (if he has a "canon" name, I never discovered it) spends most of the game bunnyhopping at mach speed through colorful, vaguely-hellish industrial passageways, shooting a large variety of guns (3 options for each of 5 ammo types, for a total of 15) at enemies who are, to be frank, direct copycats from those found in  both in terms of behavior and general aesthetic. big stylistic claim to fame is that it uses low-res spritework for its enemies in the fashion of the earlier  titles, but has a very smooth, polished, high-speed-low-drag gamefeel like the 2016 installment in that franchise, playing like a kind of greatest-hits album of  games prior to .  Aside from the enemy roster, which is uninspired, and the level design, which is stellar,  has some cool modularity to it in the form of a robust level editor, and a good soundtrack that -- like its gameplay -- hews a little too close to  (2016) at times not to feel like it's a cover act. doesn't reinvent the wheel.  In fact, it does the opposite: it slavishly worships the wheel, putting it on a pedestal and doing its best to replicate the wheel while reinventing as little as humanly possible.  But if you've ever played a  game, finished it, and thought, "damn, I could really go for more  right now," this I-Can't-Believe-It's-Not-Butter version will feed your hunger just as well as the real thing.Buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is overhyped big time and I fell into it, the game looked so good from the outside though. Look I looove Brutal Doom, I like Project Warlock but Prodeus is lacking something. Maybe it's the respawing issue? _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed a lot of this game, especially after finishing the game a couple times: the punchy and impactful weapons, the map designs, the style, the gratuitous violence, the lot are all great... BUT the length of the main campaign felt much shorter than it wanted to be. The weapons are your typical staples in any kind of boomer shooter but Prodeus give each weapon an alt fire to give them more diversity, some of which are unique to this game inparticular, like the first shotgun firing a concentrated incendiary shot or the shredders which are dual SMGs but work like they're one gun (it's weird to explain). All the guns feel very nice to use and ammo is pretty abundant to the point of almost being overwhelming even on highest difficulty. I think an improvement especially for the higher difficulties is to reduce the amount of ammo that is given to the player from weapon drops as they give the most ammo, for example: the minigun gives 100 bullets and by default you can carry 200 max. Difficulty affects ammo from ammo drops, why not ammo from weapon drops?The map designs is a fine mix of old 90's to 2000's FPS games like Unreal and Quake, there's a lot of structural detail but it's not too detailed to make it easy to lose your direction in a level (and if you do, automap is your friend), lotta secrets hidden in pretty sneaky places and not-so sneaky places but requiring a little creative thinking to get them. But the part that sells it to me is the special effects and literal moving parts of the levels, like a door opening/shutting and effects that emit while the moving parts are moving, I could watch them animations all day if I could.The art style of everything being pixelated with a slight dash of modern day visual features is such a perfect mix, pixel textures with normal maps and how the shadows cast in the textures works SO well. Particle effects too are also pixelated as well as the view models and enemies (which can be turned off). The art style is something you don't see everyday in a good way.There's a lot of blood that gushes out of the enemies, like an impossible amount of blood. So much blood that it can even pollute the screen making it difficult to see what's going on and if an enemy is killed or not. I never had this issue as I had enough ammo to just shoot things until they either exploded or played their death animation but I can see how some people would find this a problem.While I do enjoy the game for what it is, I have some complaints.One being the game ends way sooner than I thought. Don't get me wrong the game is still fun and the length shouldn't really tell the face value of a game especially if it encourages replayability but damn the last few parts of the game sorta felt rushed with how the last few areas in the world map were all just one way roads. No branching paths with less levels appearing in later dimensions not to mention the Runes, which is sorta how the story started, got thrown out pretty quickly at the same time wasting potential. What made the short length hurt worse is I only just picked the the Auto Shotgun, 2 levels before the last level, not to mention I hadn't even gotten close to getting enough ore for the Mammonth or the Swarmer.Second being I thought weapons in the shop would appear in levels on their own, so when I was playing and found ammo for a gun I didn't have I thought it would eventually give it to me but didn't so I sorta trapped myself into not using the shop as I thought it would be useless as I would find the weapons in a level later on, which is why I didn't get the auto shotgun until WAY too late in the game.Some guns felt under powered and/or inconsistent (At least on the hardest difficulty). The Mammonth while powerful felt like it needed to deal more damage to make it feel worth to use. The inconsistency issues effect all guns, some more than others. Again with the Mammonth would only kill a Prodeus Imp about 75% of the time, not a huge problem with say the automatic guns but still feels like there's some kind of RNG going on with the damage values.some other small ones include: over stocking of ammo and all "mini boss" enemies having homing attacks but they feel more like personal problems. I do hope that more official content will come in the future to fill in the cliff hanger the last level.

_childDocuments_.review: The true successor to DOOM, DOOM II.Exactly how I wanted the bound, flat DOOM to evolve to past the bottomless mag, infinite circle strafe without moving too close to being just another bunny-hopping QUAKE reflection.Play it slow first: enjoy the atmosphere, reminisce in the survival horror that you got when you first slapped in the two floppy disc version of shareware DOOM. _childDocuments_.review: Love the artstyle, love the gameplay (albeit I wish they did more to differentiate it from Doom), love the custom content, but boy does this one really get handicapped by the game design. Part of what made me fall in love with Doom Eternal was getting my ass kicked and actually having to get better at the combat to progress, you're not gonna get that in Prodeus. The single, biggest, most crippling flaw that this game has is that death carries absolutely no consequences even on the highest difficulty. And it's absurd this wasn't caught in early access, because it seems like the single most pervasive criticism that this game gets. When you die in Prodeus and respawn at a checkpoint, the enemies/level aren't reset to the point in time when you got that checkpoint, rather everyone you killed before dying remains dead. So it's essentially more efficient to just brute force every fight without giving much thought to tactics or getting better at the game's systems. Prodeus is insanely frustrating for me, because it's almost great. I remember in Early Access the level Hexarchy didn't give you a checkpoint until after this massive battle, so for the first time in the entire game death had actual consequence and I had to struggle to figure out how to get by. Despite this being an absurd difficulty-spike with consequence-free death the entire game before that point, I was finally beginning to respect Prodeus for actually challenging me and making me learn. A checkpoint has since been added to the beginning of Hexarchy, removing the challenge entirely. Death in Prodeus is a deflating experience, because it feels like you're being robbed of an opportunity to learn. Do I recommend Prodeus? Yeah, I guess. The artstyle, level design, and gunplay almost manage to carry the experience. It's a good casual game. And there are incredible user made maps, some of which actually introduce some level of difficulty to the game. But with the above caveats. This review, however, remains negative. Never before have I seen a developer so desperate to handicap their own gameplay experience.Also, also: they manage to handicap the multiplayer experience too. You cannot join a match in progress, so unless you have friends, you better hope you catch a lobby while they're still setting up. Such a baffling decision. A game like this was never going to have a high player population, but making multiplayer even less accessible is absurd.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. Perfect for jumping in for quick 30min sessions when bored. Im super keen on the full release with hopefully alot more maps etc.Its so good i bought it for a friend too.Edit: and this was after i could have been playing it for "free" on game pass. _childDocuments_.review: The game is excellent.The main factor why I bought it is the level editor. It's well done and offers several possibilities. Currently the community has made countless maps of very good quality. You can easily share and play maps in series (a bit like Portal 2). So it's the only retro FPS game I know that offers this.The second reason is the graphic style that takes advantage of shaders and the effects of current technologies in an old fashioned Doom style of play. The game is by the way gory, so it can't be for everyone.The soundtracks is impeccable.Even if I am satisfied and the game is fun to play, there is always a little place for improvement.Indeed, even if this early access game clearly doesn't intend to compete with big average games like Doom Eternal, I still agree that it would have everything to gain if it would improve the gameplay feeling after a long time to play. Therefore, to make the game a little more challenging, I advise devs to add tweaks that would change the gameplay dynamics:Like the skulls in Halo, it would be a good addition to find secret collectible malus in Campaign that would boost the score once activated and break the monotony a bit. You could for example remove cheackpoint, double enemy life, double enemy speed, double enemy domage and so on...But overall the game is almost perfect in my opinion. So buy it without hesitation if you are a fan of retro FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is a great FPS that captures the feel of the original Doom series but with upgraded graphics. _childDocuments_.review: The level of needless post-processing effects in this game is absolutely insane - you literally get a migraine in the main menu before you've even started playing it's that horrendous!Such a shame because it seems a good looking and mechanically solid boomer shooter but the amount of flashing and chromatic effects is ridiculous. I will never understand why developers need to plague their games with these elements because they serve no benefit in improving visual presentation or ambience.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is a good "boomer shooter" style FPS that really shines with its level design, but has a small enemy variety problem and a few weird weapon design choices.The level design is probably the game's strongest area, with every level being well crafted with a solid concept in mind, with the Prodeus dimension levels and the Sniper and Space Station levels being standouts. The "progression" of the levels as you play through the game is also well done, as it feels like you're travelling across the facility as if the game were something like Half-Life, while still keeping that isolated, one-level-at-a-time, feel that a world map gives.For most of the game you're fighting the same zombies, shotgunners, fire ball throwing imps, little spider things, and giant four legged demon dog things, and later on in the game, the blue variants for everything but the zombies and shotgunners. That's not to say these are the only enemies in the game, just that there should maybe be one or two more common land enemies. This isn't too big of a deal though, as their usage of the aerial and rarer land enemies makes up for the samey-ness of fighting these 5 enemies and their blue variants.The developers are very generous with a fair number of things, including: ammunition for your weapons, letting you backtrack through (most) levels when secret hunting, and a divisive checkpoint system that lets you respawn mid level after having killed everything. You can, however, completely ignore the checkpoint system by just hitting the restart level button when you die, and the game actively encourages this as it gives you a gold star if you beat the level deathless. As for the weird weapon design choices I mentioned earlier, it's mostly that there's only one electric ammo weapon, and three shotguns for some reason.Another small nitpick is it would be nice to travel around the level selection map a bit faster.Overall, it's a good game worth picking up if you like the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't think I was going to like this game. I passed on it for a while because I misunderstood what the game was like. _childDocuments_.review: So, Prodeus is STRAFE (remember that one?) only it's actually good and fun. Or one can say it's DOOM Eternal only with proper supply of ammo.Style is AMAZING, levels are clever, soundtrack is dope and the shooting is mighty satisfying. Every weapon feels useful and fun to use, difficulty is actually adequate.Can't say anything about user levels, not my jam.My main gripes so far:- Short campaign (but it's early access)- UI/UX still needs some work, especially for seasoned Quake players. Weapon switching should be faster, I think the game should give players more macro commands to toy with.So far it's the best 'new old shooter' around with terrific art and totally bonkers shooting. If you love Quake 1, Quake 3 or Bruta Doom, it's a must.

_childDocuments_.review: Game of the year.  5/5Impressive output from effectively 3* persons fulltime. The early access campaign was great value but now we have the full 1.0 campaign too, with the latter maps raising the bar each time in terms of intensity and scope. Highly replayable, most people will enjoy the campaign multiple times, and come back to the well again for co-op.Enhanced retro aesthetic.Where many boomer shooters use old engines, Prodeus sports a custom engine based on Unity that combines modern rendering techniques with a retro aesthetic to give the best of both worlds. The effects and atmosphere are top notch plus there's a satisfying gore system that splatters blood and goo everywhere.Addictive combat loop15+ satisfying armaments requiring a combination of weapon swapping and managing reloads means you're rarely out of guns to fire but also rewarded with the power fantasy of mastering your arsenal. A frenetic combat loop keeps the adrenaline flowing while never feeling stale. Versatile and interesting alt-fire modes on the weapons let you get creative and relive the excitement of Turok and UT's inventive ways to dismember your enemies.Accessible difficulties and high replay valueThere's a difficulty for everyone. Plus if you want to really push yourself you can compete for the public high score table against the community. Bonuses for faster times, no deaths, all secrets, all kills etc. Levels are short and sweet (10-15 mins) so you can pick it up and put it down. Lots of replay value.Fantastic level designAn homage to games like Doom, Quake, UT and Duke, Prodeus blends old and new, featuring very pretty "retro" maps in a style that feels simultaneously familiar and uniquely prodeus. The level design is excellent all around, always nudging you in the right direction and rewarding aggression. Unlike older 2.5D game engines (like Doom), Prodeus is fully 3D and if you slow down for a moment and soak in the art you'll truly appreciate the love that has gone into these levels and the engine. Music by Andrew Hulshult (Doom Eternal)A mix of midi and recorded music including bloodpumping tracks by Andrew Hulshult (Doom Eternal) that ramp up and down dynamically to suit the action.Built-in level editor and community mapsThe ENTIRE game was built in the light-weight in-game editor that ships with the game (PC only). The editor uses modern techniques and is surprisingly powerful given how accessible to learn and use it is. The community has only started tapping the long term potential but there are already some killer maps handily curated by the dev team under the category "Editor Picks".If you are unsure if this game is for you here is some guidance:Not every boomer shooter is going to lean into your niche preferences. What some people love about one boomer shooter they're going to miss in another one. HOWEVER: Prodeus is a solid game that does a great job across the board and will probably make most people's top 3. Where it sits among your favourites I can't predict, but I can safely say it's a fantastic value for money experience that will appeal to people looking for a fun romp you can just pick up and play. One that doesn't demand too much of a learning curve or time investment from you -- unless you want it to.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorta on the fence on this, but since there are so many glowing reviews, I figure I'll lean more negative here. TL;DR, Prodeus is pretty, loud, gory, has tons of attitude... but doesn't have much in the way of challenge or originality. A pretty firm "meh" for the price, worth it maybe at 10 bucks. If you aren't into the speedrun 100% secrets and kills lifestyle, there are better modern retro shooters.Too much ammo, too much life, enemies and spawns too predictable, weapons are too powerful. If you've never played a fast horror-ish FPS before, this would probably suit you. If you're impressed by flashy fire effects and punchy weapons, it has those things. But I would strongly, strongly recommend just grabbing Brutal Doom PB3.0+ or Dusk if that's the kinda thing you're after. If you've already got those and played them to death, you might be slightly disappointed in Prodeus... but then, the discord was full of people who swore it was better than both, or said "It's not trying to be those things". But if it isn't, it doesn't have much identity of its own. Kinda like an orange baby mode Doom with Duke jumping and pathfinding.Weapons are nice and punchy, a step up from the Alpha. Level design through the end of the early access campaign is solid, but VERY predictable if you've played old FPS before. See a goody? There's gonna be a spawn. Gonna open a door? Probably some dudes behind it. See a long bridge? Enemies gonna spawn... again. Clearly they're trying to make something good here, but it needs more though and more of the meanspirited ambushes, especially with the checkpoints every ten feet. And just like Dead Space, you basically have the best weapon equipped in the first two minutes. Quick assign pistol and shotgun and you're like 90 percent on the way to beating the campaign.  Meanwhile, I've fought exactly one enemy that isn't a Dollar Store version of a Doom enemy. And we're not talking Brutal Doom slick aggressive enemies; the budget Imp does throw fireballs that will track a la Doom 2016, but otherwise you've got zombie, shotgun zombie, chaingun zombie, fire poop cacodemon, chonky pain elemental, exploding lost soul, and Serious Sam Pinky hybrid. And a weird thing that's more like a Doom 2016 Summoner I guess. Levels are varied, sure, somehow making them feel different despite being variations on facility, rocks, lava, sewage in shades of orange. Levels are nice and linear, rarely leaving you lost ... lots of doors and elevators that pop you to the right path. But you know what's coming, and it's incredibly rare anything pulls the ol' pincer attack; instead you get big flashy spawns all to your front. A couple times you may have an arena, and in those cases you just run in circles with a shotgun blasting everything until you just need to mop up a couple zombies. Usually there's an escape in the room too, where you can get up high or cut a corner so everything is funneling through your meat grinder self.As hinted at before, biggest problem is your pistol is incredibly good. It's not Halo 1 sniper magnum garbage good, but it's VERY accurate. If you can put the cursor on an imp a canyon away, you can kill it in the same five to six shots you can when you're staring it in the face. Tons of ammo laying around for it. Need something heavy but no rocket launcher? Charge the shotgun alt fire and take out a cacodemon in two shots. Kill imps at a distance in one, fake pinkies in a single headshot. Minimal dodging required. Poke out, shoot, pop back. Pinkies, basic zombies, and nightmare imps are the only things that'll usually chase you with much gusto. Three headshots or four body shots kills a zombie, four and five a shotgun, and around ten for a chaingun dude. I spend most of my time on the pistol. It's easy. Alt mode is trash, seemingly dropping damage for a triple shot... just pull the trigger until things are dead. 200 rounds before you run out, chaingun and machine guns are inaccurate and terrible, so lots and lots of pistol shots are the key. So, is it good? Well, if you ONLY played the OG Doom/Doom2, yeah, it's good. It's got a lot more going on than Ion Maiden (or whatever it got renamed), has more claustrophobic environments, and Andrew Hulshult's music really makes that last point all the more intense. I like what they're trying to do, and I'ma keep playing through once the other 75 percent of the campaign gets opened up; but my critiques in the alpha discord were disregarded, except the shotgun doesn't sound like ass anymore. The same problems still exist, and being the state it's currently in, I can't imagine much will change. Nerf the pistol, nerf the shotgun alt, and maybe things will get more interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: A super polished boomer shooter. Satisfying weapons, fun levels, great art direction and music. The level editor and browser is a fun addition too.With that said, the checkpoint system desperately needs to be changed. It was hard for me to keep playing realizing that when you respawn, enemies stay dead which wipes away any challenge in the game. If you're in a tough spot you can just keep brute forcing into the fight chipping away at enemies without care if you get killed. If you don't care about this at all, the game is definitely worth picking up. I'm hoping the devs can at least update it with an option to have a normal checkpoint system where enemies you haven't killed after that point respawn. I'll change this review to positive if this change is made. This just really kills the game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game combines classic and modern style and gameplay. It has something from classic doom and quake, as well as from modern doom, and at the same time has its own charm.Pros:- Overall, the gameplay is fun and fast paced.- Gunplay is very satisfying.- Excellent level design, I enjoyed exploring maps.- The game has style and is pretty atmospheric.- No stupid plot. Just some brief texts like in good old days.- Soundtrack!Neutral:- For me, pixelating the image so much feels unnecessary. On the other hand, it fits the game style well.- In two locations the game lagged a lot, the frame rate was like 1 fps or something. This was the only bug I experienced despite the game is early access.Cons:- Checkpoint system. When you die, you respawn on last checkpoint, but  killed enemies do not respawn. While it helps to keep the pace fast, it drastically reduces tension, at least if your goal is just to complete campaign rather than achive highest score. It's not ruining the game, but it makes it worse.- A bit inconsistent difficulty. I completed about a half of the game on very hard and it wasn't hard. _childDocuments_.review: A cocktail of Doom Eternal and Doom 64 in both aesthetics and gameplay and excels at combining the two. It has a good mix of run and gun sections and arena combat and manages to surprise you with new monsters and setups fairly consistently. The sandbox of monsters and weaponry play off each other nicely and there is a lot of variety in both areas already, despite it only being an early access version of the campaign.The game is fairly ambitious in that it attempts to be simultaneously modern and capture the classic feel of Doom and Quake. Honestly it excels in both areas; the juxtaposition between intricate sprite work and 3D geometry and level design making the game feel like it knows its roots while not being bogged down by the rudimentary mechanics of some older 90s Doom clones.At around $40 AUD this game is a bit pricey for what you get at the moment (I spent about 4 hours with it to finish it on Ultra Hard - without finding all the secrets mind you), so waiting until full release might be best for more frugal folk.

_childDocuments_.review: It scrapes by as "barely okay" due to a number of decisions, some of which I'm slightly baffled by.Firstly, let's get the good out of the way: the soundtrack, absolutely slaps. It kicks ass. It's super good.Next, the graphics are... they are certainly a chosen style that has been decided upon for reasons I can only be questioned by. Like, Prodeus steps into the company of the rare games I've considered putting down again as soon as I've booted them up thanks to the main menu. The awful ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ screenflicker that's all over the place instantly summoned up the rare feeling of being carsick. Sort of the sharp edge of an approaching headache combined with a mild nausea threatening to become all-consuming. No option to turn it off or turn it down that I can see. There's absolutely a reason we're not longer using crusty CRT's, my dudes.Continuing in the graphics, in-game the HUD is just... titanic. Use the minimal HUD uption, hell, that should be default, and even then it feels a bit too big. Eats up way too much screen real estate considering that some of the weapon sprites are also absolutely chonking titanic and take up like a third of what you can see. Like the fists, what the hell?Enemies look... okay. But the weird sprite style does conjure up some oddities with corpses that sometimes feel like they're moving when you approach them and move away from them. The main problem with enemies is how they die, they're all so flashy and slow to die, and due to being sprites don't ragdoll, so it often takes a second or two to confirm that an enemy is actually dead and you can move on to the next one. Environments look alright but nothing special, if you really liked Episode 1 of Doom and wanted more of that but with better lighting, you're going to be super pleased. At no point did the environment ever really cry out "I have a style, I have an expression, I have something I'm going for" beyond "man, guys, remember Doom/Quake????"Behavior and challenge-wise the enemies are... once again, okay. There's sort of an odd disconnect where the game really wants to make you feel like you're playing Doom 2016, with the soundtrack and the fast movement and all, but rather than a frantic push-forward feeling, either I'm facing hordes of melee enemies and thus feel more encouraged to play it like Serious Sam(i.e. backpedalling while firing until they all stop following me due to being dead), and ranged enemies don't... they don't have any close range behaviors, like packing off, repositioning, etc. they just stand there like turrets and snipe at you, unless you're out of sight, in which case they advance until you're in sight, which tends to make the whole thing feel more like a cover shooter(the imps do have quite good target prediction, and yes, they're imps, I have no idea what Prodeus calls them but they are Doom Imps, that's final).Plus the narrow techbase corridors and stuff feel like they make poor use of the player's movement speed. Their horizontal movement speed, that is, the vertical movement is pretty anemic.Next up, the guns... there's probably a big and cool arsenal, but as of this review I've spent a while with just the fists(awful), pistol(surprisingly punchy for an FPS pistol, not bad), the shotgun(up close it... shoots... like a gun. not bad, but super wimpy at range, doesn't excite me), dual SMG's(low damage, awful accuracy, tiny magazines and glacial reload time. I would frankly rather use the pistol) and chaingun(actually a good weapon! uses the same ammo pool as dual SMG's and pistol, though, so lol to ever using them again) and except for the chaingun none of them make me feel hype. Add to this that only the chaingun doesn't need to reload.Once again, I would love to have reloading in my semi-realistic/fully-realistic cover shooter, but it just kind of feels out of place in my 80mph running speed doom homage. It slows down action that's already kind of slow.Lastly, we've got this game, right? That's got all these tall cliffs and pits and lava you can't escape from and... you're sticking me with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ checkpoints? Really, game? Checkpoints. CHECKPOINTS. That particular design decision can go right to hell and stay there.Long story short, Prodeus is, outside of the soundtrack and the imps' accuracy, mediocre and riven with design decisions I don't understand. Maybe once it's fully out and drops in price a bit I could recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get if you take the best bits of DOOM, Quake and Blood and smash them into one game? Prodeus.We're seeing a resurgence of retro FPS shooters lately, and quite frankly, I'm all about it. Prodeus has kept me engaged during the 30+ hours I've spent playing it. The main campaign is exciting and thrilling if you're just looking for a simple point-and-shoot FPS, but the level design is so intricate and detailed that there are secrets upon secrets just waiting to be found, I've completed the 'Go Get Some Fresh Air' achievement and I'm STILL finding stuff I missed on the first playthrough. Visually, the game is gorgeous, it does the aged voxel art style with the option of having both 2D and 3D voxels (2D voxels being akin to Doom, with 3D voxels being akin to Quake). The game is presented wonderfully and manages to cram a lot of detail into a game designed with the purpose of throwing back to the mid-90's. The levels span across DOOM-inspired space stations and facilities, to sprawling outdoor environments to castles and cathedrals reminiscent of Quake. Visually the levels are a feast for the eyes and are filled with puzzles, secrets, sequences and the occasional bit of platforming. The lighting and effects are striking and well presented and the in-game environment is beautiful. The cast of enemies remains engaging and challenging and the weapon roster is well balanced and dynamic, with most weapons being useful for almost the entire game, with the exception of a few stragglers (I'm looking at you Minigun and Auto Shotgun). Also the Super Shotgun has FOUR barrels and packs more punch than Mike Tyson on bath salts.To be critical about the game, I came into this game expecting a retro-FPS consisting of tropes from the DOOM and Quake playbooks, which at it's core, it is. There are a lot of similarities between the in-game enemies and the OG DOOM roster and in the later game, some of the 'late game' enemies are just blue color swaps of the standard enemies, just with fancy attacks and decorations. I felt that the Prodeus (Prodean?) enemies could have probably been fleshed out a little bit more and maybe have had some more variety given the stacked Chaos roster. The story has potential, but is almost optional, there is scant lore there should you care for it, but if you're just here to commit war crimes against an endless roster of demons, go nuts. For those of you who are completionists, there is lore and story to be enjoyed, but with no way of recalling said lore (Think the DOOM Eternal codex) it's almost moot. There appears to be room for more content in the future and given the campaign ending (No spoilers here - play the game for yourself) it almost seems to set the scene for more Prodeus/Prodean content in the future. The Shop is a strange addition, I can see what they were going for in regards to an in-game currency (Again, think DOOM Eternal) but the major frustration lies in the fact that your 'purchases' follow a pre-determined path; for example - to get the Double Jump power up, you've gotta purchase the Super Shotgun and Plasma Rifle (40 Ore worth of weapons IIRC) before you can spend another 20 ore on Double Jump (again IIRC), a bit of a pain at first seeing as some of the earlier levels require Double Jump to get 100% completion. Also, in-game 'paywalling' some of the weapons in said shop was a strange move, especially seeing as without the weapons you can obtain in the shop, the weapon roster you can get through the campaign is quite limited.All in all, despite the above grievances, this is a great game and probably the most fun I've had playing an FPS in quite some time. Looking forward to what this studio comes out with next.

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's an OK game, like 6/10 maybe 7/10 so I'm mainly thumbing it down for the sake of balance, because I feel like the current rating of the game is way inflated.Also I do think that a lot of effort and love has went into making this game so I feel somewhat bad for giving it a negative review, the issue for me is that they didn't really make it an engaging SHOOTER and this is my issue with a lot of these games (retro/boomer shooters) to be honest, cool graphics, cool extras if you will but the actual gameplay is just not that great. So first issue is that the game is easy, even on higher difficulties mainly because most of the mobs are melee   so they automatically pose little danger to you. You can also cheese them by just going up on platforms etc. Game feels slow, I've seen people say this is fast but for me the opposite has been the case, everything feels weighted, sluggish. Few reasons as to why, lots of reloads, slow animations, very basic movement mechanics and lack of projectiles from the enemies.. So what ends up happening is that you never feel like you're having to do a lot either mentally or physically. It's monotonous. For example another game that I played recently Metal Hellsinger, I was constantly engaged by having to keep tempo, dodge enemy attacks (with a dedicated dodge button), I'm given double jumps for example so I am constantly moving, platforming, doing something. Here it's just, "oh enemy, strafe/kite and shoot", this is the extent of the decision making process for pretty much every encounter, if there's a lot of enemies maybe switch to a grenade launcher.You are given a lot of weapons but it doesn't feel like you ever need to use them. I might as well just use the shotgun all the time. The weapons feel more or less equally effective at everything anyway. Other things, not a big fan of the sprite animation graphics, I think the artstyle is good as far as the blood fountains/gore etc but it's just, I don't know - doesn't have the impact. I guess for people who played the original it might be appealing but not for me.I also feel like the setting is very uninspired, I get that these games are meant to be "doom clones" but come on, you got to innovate or offer something unique otherwise you might as well just play the original Doom.

_childDocuments_.review: Strangely disappointed. Feels like a modern Quake 2. Now don't assume that's meant without nuance, (I have hundreds of hours into Quake 2. I love it.) that isn't meant only as an insult. Rather, very like Quake 2, the core gameplay is there. The weapons all feel especially lovely to use, the enemies explode into especially good gibs and new sprites with the top half blown off whenever you use the shotgun at point blank range. The dual machine guns are especially fun even if it feels strange to reload both after only having fired one. The enemies all look excellent, and the aesthetic of the environments looks fantastic, even if it's just a clear retread of every level in Doom Eternal. What the Quake 2 problem is, however, is theoretically functional level design with seemingly zero regard for the pacing of encounters, or how the player is likely to interact with the enemies present. Zombies are dotted randomly about each level in dull corridors that neither require nor give potential for tactical thinking, and are dispatched almost immediately. This is compounded by the fact that the enemies are all almost impressively puny on medium difficulty. (I do consider myself good at FPSs, and understood that medium was probably too low for my tastes, but "Hurt me plenty" on Doom Eternal was just barely doable for me so I don't like to assume too much) The majority of my time was spent running into groups of 3 to 4 zombielike enemies in tight quarters and killing them all in as many shots from the shotgun without getting a scratch. Things seem to ramp up very occasionally when you are pitted against a larger group with more variety within it, but even these battles are disappointingly short and easy. Compare to Serious Sam 4, released only recently, where nearly every battle was noticeably different and often harder than the last, and required an almost perfect management of positioning, ammunition, health, and gadgets to get through. Very like how Doom Eternal was virtually all design and no emergence, where the challenge seemed to be arduously performing the right steps to take down each individual enemy type under various amounts of pressure, this game is all emergence and no design, with seemingly no care taken to create a functional strategy to kill each enemy other than fire whatever weapon is the right range and avoid their attacks. Both these approaches feel lazy compared to the instinctive and naturalistic tactics that emerge from every enemy in Serious Sam 4. Looking at the kleer skeleton, it quickly becomes clear that waiting for it to get close and firing the double barrelled shotgun before it can hit you will be a powerful solution against a single one, but the large recovery time after doing this means that care must be taken against larger groups to thin them out at range before you get overwhelmed. This conditioning of the player makes the battle where you finally get a minigun instantly satisfying, as you know that it will be perfect for engaging the dozens of charging kleer on the other side of the bridge. Compare this to the vain attempt at creating a similar moment on getting the minigun in Prodeus, where dozens of enemies do appear, but since they are the same ones you've always been fighting and defeating with no challenge, it feels like you could do this battle almost as easily using the weapons you already have available. They lack offensive capability to the point where the ability to kill large numbers of them slightly faster only changes to number of ponderous fireballs you'll need to dodge from 3-4 to 1-2. I truly hope that this game gets better, as simply making more dangerous enemies and levels designed around their capabilities and how the player must interact with them would rapidly bring it up from a 4/10 to an 8 at least.Since writing this I have started the campaign again on Very Hard and had noticeably more fun, but all the issues are still there. As I suspected, the enemy design means that there is no actual increase in real difficulty, it's just less forgiving with letting you take damage. The imps now have accuracy on their fireballs which makes them frustratingly hard to dodge, but I feel I shouldn't moan about that when I'm the one complaining it's too easy. The checkpoint system is garbage for not respawning the dead enemies, and means there is no real punishment for dying unless you decide to restart the whole level. However, I don't particularly feel bad for abusing this for the same reason I cheat to give myself more health and ammo in overly hard Doom WADs, and that is because a real game should be an intelligently designed, difficult, but surmountable challenge set for you by the developers, where a bad game, particularly a bad shooter, is just a chance to get the mindless satisfaction of clicking on enemies to make a loud gunshot noise and see them explode into gibs. This delivers that, and that's why it can be fun to play, but there is absolutely no reason I would not abuse the checkpoint system when that is all I'm there for.
