_childDocuments_.review: As others have mentioned, it's basically the Doom 3 we all hoped for at the time. It definitely *strongly* references Doom, from the colored keys, level design, demons (which are almost exactly the same: marine-type, fireball throwing, charging bull-type, floating fireball, kamikaze ones, etc.) All of that said, as unoriginal as it might be, it's a TON of fun and well executed.  If you're a fan of the Boomer Shooter genre, this is an easy recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like games with a great storyline? Do you like games that spend the first 20 minutes trying to force you to care about the universe the game takes place? Do you like cutscenes that explain to you what's going on, why you're the good guy and why the guys you're going to be killing are the bad guys? Do you want a half hour tutorial that holds your hand as you begin the process of learning the game controls with instructions like "Okay, now LOOK TO YOUR LEFT"? Do you like complex game systems that force your left hand into impossible shapes with hard to remember key combinations so you can POWERSLIDE and ATOMIC CROUCH UPPERCUT enemies as you WALL RUN and SUPERDASH your way to victory? Do you like relaxing bluegrass banjo music? If you answered "yes" to any of those, this isn't the game for you.If you want an old school shooter feel that comes without all the frustrating backtracking of old school level design - if you want a game that is totally dedicated to being a GAME without aspirations of building a cinematic universe - if you want to blow the hell out of some cool looking enemies with simple, easy to use systems and weapons that feel and sound awesome - and if you want to do all of this with some awesome metal music playing behind the brutal, punchy sounds of your gunshots, then this game might be your thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game. At first it's pretty fun - the gameplay is like a mix of classic Doom and Doom 2016. In fact, most weapons, enemies and environments feel a bit too familiar if you've played Doom 2016. Unfortunately the game quickly becomes bland, the levels just blend together too much, there are some exceptions but overall it feels like playing the same level over and over. This is somewhat mitigated by finding new upgrades like a double jump or dash, but it takes way too long to get them - when I finished the game I didn't have all of them even though I wasn't exactly ignoring secrets/collectibles. Weapons are cool but the novelty quickly wears off, some of them become heavily obsolete midway through the game.The big deal breaker here is that you respawn every time you die. The only time you ever have to restart/load a map is if you die without activating any checkpoints (so basically just the first 2-3 minutes of a level). It didn't impact my enjoyment that much, but I definitely would have preferred an old school quicksave/quickload system. You also can't save your progress mid-level, so sometimes I felt like I was forcing myself to finish the map just so I wouldn't have to replay 75% of it if I quit out.Prodeus is quite short too, I finished it in about 7 hours on the 2nd hardest difficulty. I think I would be a lot more harsh towards the game if I bought it for the full asking price of ~$30. With how little challenge the game offers and with how quickly it gets stale, I don't feel like it's worth that much when you compare it to other recent boomer shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: This a Gem among Boomer Shooters, played through the playtest a few times before purchasing, jumped right in on Ultra hard, very competent shooter, just the right difficulty, weapons all handle & feel well, impactful. purposeful, soundtrack is amazing. the art style is very good on the eyes if you're into boomer shooters, pixelated mixed with 3D goes really well. map designs are a solid mix of open spaces and narrower (but not too narrow) corridors, platforming is very generous and not obnoxiously difficult, movement and controls are tight, quick. everything you'd expect from a well designed shooter. the only complaint I have.. & this is a preference because I'm very picky with shotguns in Shooters, just don't like the sound of it. that's really all I could find. Haven't experienced any bugs or glitches. This is a well made game, if you like OG shooters, or a well made challenging game that will punish you for you're mistakes but make those mistakes very obvious. Then yes, absolutely get this. you can tell it was made with a lot of love and thought.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: A fresh boomer shooter that's firing on all cylinders.Visually striking aesthetic, addictive fast-paced combat, satisfying weaponry that hits just right, and awesome music by James Paddock and that absolute lad, Andrew Hulshult.This game won me over instantly and I'm looking forward to the rest of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: You like FPS games / boomer-shooters - you must buy. Cool and stylish graphics, fantastic and fitting music, good enemy variety, fun gunplay and extremely cool weapon selection - with the four-barrelled super shotgun sitting on the top. Also: the design of some levels in the base game is simply jaw-dropping.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: PRODEUS is a Cover-Shooter masquerading as a DOOM Throw-BackThis game isn't anything like the advertising or videos on Steam claim it to be. I thought this would be a fast-paced DOOM-like retro-styled game. What it actually is is a cover-shooter put in a first-person format. The difficulties are complete fallacies. There's no change in how enemies react to you or how they proactively engage with the world. Each difficulty produces enemies that slowly saunter toward you, or stand completely still, while shooting at you. Which is fine on lower difficulties. However, on higher difficulties, it turns what was a fun, run-and-gun game into a very tedious, incredibly annoying, progress reset on death, stop-and-wait gameplay loop that is just not fun. Challenge comes from the world and the enemies existing in it, not from the flat damage the enemies dish out.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: I cant seem to like this game.The visuals are good, the gameplay is kinda like the original DOOM (you have to reload and that sucks) and the music is pretty good, BUT even for an Early Access title this game seems expensive for what you get, 90% of us wont use the map editor and the game's levels are repetitive.Is not a bad game, i'm sure that its pretty good because it "Overwhelmingly Positive" on steam, but for my taste? This is not a complete game, its expensive and Doom 2016 is better for an even cheaper price (For Argentina at least).Buy on sale maybe?
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhere in the liminal space of my mind, Prodeus has always been there.Saying the game is "old school" does it an injustice. Sure, it owes a debt to the golden oldies of QUAKE and Duke3D (to name just a couple) - but then doesn't every FPS ever made?Although it's inspiration is laid bare for all to see, this is neither the part or full story. Prodeus exists in it's own right; it's a daring, running jump into a creative space that demands respect.It's an atmospheric, blood-drenched thrill ride. The type of machine-tooled adrenaline shot sprung from the minds of geniuses, that looks simple. This is a grand deception indeed; because making it look this simple and easy is the most challenging thing of all.The weapons are like sledgehammers, responding to your fingertips like Mjolnir rumbles in mighty Thor's fist. The enemies are a varied, difficult cohort who will tear you limb from limb if you make a mistake. The soundtrack, by the eminent Andrew Hulshult, is a solid-onyx home-run of stinky riffs and hellish ambience. Can he do ANYTHING wrong? I think not.Whilst still in Early Access, this game has plenty of official content to offer, as well as access to the level editor and the wondrous creations the community has already put together. Witness Prodeus!
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: I love me a good boomer shooter. I've played and beat just about every one that comes to mind, and also have ran thru brutal doom 1 and 2 more times than I can count. I beat doom 2016, and doom eternal on nightmare. I love a hard ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fast, gory game. Now, let's talk about Prodeus... this ♥♥♥♥ right here. I've waited and waited since Gmanlives (watch him if you haven't, best reviewer of games hands down), and ♥♥♥♥ man it was so worth the wait! The gore, the break neck speed you can move at, the controls, the power of the weapons is all so spot on. What we have here isn't even finished and I'm not going to quite say it yes, as I'm not too far into the game. But this may just be the best boomer shooter I think I've ever played. It's for sure the best indie FPS I think I've played, only thing that can give this a run for it's money is DUSK. But from what i've played so far, i think this will have DUSK beat. If you love to shoot the limbs off of your enemies, if you like boomer shooters, or you're just into shooting games, you will most likely love and have a great time with this GEM we have here. It's a must buy for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is a nearly perfect amalgamation of old-school 90's shooter art styles & graphics brought bang up to date with all the modern game engine bells & whistles. Where to start? The game has a definite retro art style which is very reminiscent of Doom and the original Quake. A slew of favourite weapons such as the shotgun, super shotgun (and even an auto shotgun!), minigun and rocket launcher are accompanies by new and innovative energy weapons that make for a very satisfying loadout.Enemies are relatively varied and excellent map design ensures that each map offers its own tactical problem to be solved with the tools of destruction available to you. The main campaign is also non-linear (if you want it to be) ensuring replayability. As if all that wasn't enough there's also an in-game fully featured map editor which allows you to create your own maps & publish them to the in-game map library.Finally, for thos who think that Brutal Doom isn't brutal enough, this is the game for you. Every enemy you kill will erupt in huge oceans of blood & gore. Entire rooms are awash with innards after particularly large battles. Not for the faint hearted but the huge levels of blood & gore absolutely complement the art style of the game.After playing the beta and now the early access game, I would heavily recommend Prodeus to anyone looking for an authentic retro shooter feel. Fans of the Doom & Quake franchises will be right at home here. Unhesitatingly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: A boomer shooter of excellent quality. Movement feels great, fountains of blood paint the environment in delightfully excessive amounts and while the enemies are reminiscent of the titles this game takes inspiration from, they are tried and true and entice the player to cycle their impressive selection of weapons for maximum effectiveness. This game also includes a level editor right out of the gate which will most certainly extend the games life and replayability. Early access gave me 9 hours of entertainment thus far and will most certainly continue to do so while I eagerly await the full release. Excellent work developers, you really created something special here. Thanks guys!
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfying in all the right places. smooth controls, every gun is fun (even ur fists), music builds the dark atmosphere while pumping you up in a fight, secrets are well hidden but easy enough to find and figure out, the difficulty levels don't make the enemies take more bullets to kill, and the overall feel is that of a long lost Doom game. definitely worth it
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: SO MUCH BETTER than doom eternal, the gunplay, the gore, best of all this game doesn't force you to do gun switching/matching with 5 different active skills on top of all the different weapon mods to keep track of and having to deal with the downtime between switching them back and force. This is just back to the roots, which is shooting stuff feels good.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. Fast paced action, blood and gore, tones of awesome guns, fantastic campaign that gets better and better and hundreds of user made maps that extend the fun, mixed with a dope soundtrack. That all sounds great and it is, but there is a couple small downsides. Most boomer shooters already have key combat features part of the game the moment you start playing, or you unlock them just from progressing, but not Prodeus, you have to collect essentially currency to be able to purchase "double jump" and "dash", but first you have to purchase 2 guns to even be able to do that. I don't understand this decision, simple because of how much it improves the already fantastic combat. If you're not actively looking for secrets, you could go over half the game without having either of these features. The good thing is that there is a map and you can go back and forth through each levels and use the guns and features you unlocked. The enemy variety is also pretty much the same. You do get introduced to more when progressing through the starter levels and some new one here and there in different levels, though for the most part they eventually feel very similar. But that's not that big of a deal as ripping and tearing through them feels great so satisfying and it is an indie game, so you can't fault it to much in this department . I didn't like the either of the huds, never been a fan of ones that look like a helmet or one that obstruct the screen and then the minimal one looked better, I just wasn't a fan of having the guys face on the screen the entire time. So I turned off the hud entirely, this made the game feel so much better with all the action and blood and gore going everywhere. There was plenty of pick ups with health and ammo and you can see how much ammo you have in the weapons menu. I'd also recommend turning on always sprint in the options as this make the combat even more fast pace. Despite the very slight downsides. This game is very much worth checking out as it really is an absolute blast to play and so much fun ripping and tearing though the levels and enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game so far.  It's like Doom II on steroids.  The action is quick, the weapons are cool.  The graphics are an interesting mix.  The music is good.  Sometimes it gets a little heavy and stressful...sort of a Doom Eternal vibe.  Overall, this is a great game and the value is good.  I would recommend, especially if you like fast action shooters with no hiding.  Only downside is that some of the level seem a little bit like a chore to get through, but in the end, it's not too bad.  There are plenty of secrets to go back and find too.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Classic shooter with a great weapon loudout, highly satisfying, gorey combat and some pretty damn good level design and music. Great fun overall, easily recommended to anyone who likes FPS games. The game is divided up into levels so it's good for both longer sessions or in smaller chunks, one level at a time.Only little nitpick I can think of is that game performance doesn't match the retro/old-school aesthetic. The game is surprisingly heavy with everything cranked up. Modern effects like SSR and SSAO can take their toll.Also tried it out on Steam Deck, where it performs well at default settings (no SSR or SSAO) and maintains 60FPS. In this case it's worth mentioning that the game doesn't work well with simultaneous controller + mouse input, so if you want mouse input for a touchpad/gyro (highly recommended I'd say) you need a binding that only uses mouse & keyboard inputs.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is a game developed by Bounding Box Software Inc. and published by Humble Games and although it's still in Early Access, it's got a lot to offer!The game offers some nice graphics and environments, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the same and has a really great aestheticProdeus overall, however, is a fun game to play, and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is a fantastic FPS action game and to play in short bursts
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game enough. It has one of the best level designs Ive seen in a FPS in recent memory. the levels are long with intertwining paths, but somehow you just never get lost. The combat is so satisfying. Every weapon, even your standard pistol has such a nice impact to it and most of that attributed to the superb sound design.  Its not just the sounds of the weapons firing, but the sounds of the projectile hitting your enemies. You get a very convincing auditory feedback of your damage that you are causing.  Andrew Hulshult did something magical here and i don't think its been done like this before. Then there is the gore. Its excessive and unrealistic, yes, but it never gets in the way of the action. You can always see what youre doing through the red mistTLDR: buy it...heck, buy it twice....the devs deserve it.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: I backed Prodeus on Kickstarter and played it's alpha.Intense retro shooter with lots of interesting guns, enemies and levels. Action is great, arenas have good maneuveribility and guns have alternative fire so everything is in place for good combat.Good graphics, it looks uniquely. Sound is not bad. Music is insane (obviously... It's made by Andrew...) and level design is beyond expectations.It features leaderboards for all missions with scores, time and total completition. Also there is a built in level editor (the same editor they made the game with) and built in way for sharing the created levels so there is basically infinite content (player levels have leaderboards too).If you're into these kind of games then this must be your next buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: A game like this doesn't happen very often.I opened the game and I was immediately impressed, by the menu.BY. THE. MENU.So satisfying to click, move my mouse, open menus, everything. So satisfying.Told my partner "If this game is half as good as it's menu, I'm gonna be eating good."I was eating good. Every weapon feels usable and impactful. I'll open fights with any weapon then end with my double fists. Sometimes I only use the fists. I tend to run out of double machine gun ammo so either I use the shotgun into those, or vice versa. Sorry if I am waffling but honestly I am resisting the urge to gush.This game is LEAN.There doesn't seem to be anything there without purpose. The movement is smooth, and even without much air control, I feel in control. I am truly at a loss for words to explain it. The sound design is excellent; every shot, click, and reload is a pleasure to listen to. The music is intense, yet never feels out of place. The level selection screen is charming, and I wish more shooters incorporated similar features. You can replay maps from the beginning. Miss a few secrets? Simply replay the map and you will improve with each attempt. Have I mentioned how impactful every weapon is? Each weapon has its strengths and weaknesses, but I have not encountered a single dud. Not once has one weapon felt overshadowed by another. Each weapon has its own unique uses, and while they may have limitations, they do not render them useless in specific situations. They simply prevent you from relying too heavily on one weapon.This game is killer fun. If you like fast paced fps combat, this would be a worthy addition to your library.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is a shooter of old that truly uses modern technology to full effect. It maintains its roots with 90s graphics and lower framerates on guns while making use of modern technologies. It's found a true way to appeal to both parties, making this one of the easiest to recommend shooters of the past few years. It does have its flaws though, most of which I trust will be fixed during early access. If you're willing to look past those, I have no doubts Prodeus will be the adrenaline-filled thrill ride you've been looking for.If you want to see the rest of my impressions and more like it, check out . Thanks to Bounding Box Software and Humble Games for providing a review copy.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very early review but I wanted to get my initial thoughts down. If more play time changes my opinion, I will update this text accordingly. By way of establishing my preferences and biases, I enjoy retro-style shooters that bring a modern touch to 90s gameplay conventions.As you probably know, Prodeus is a retro-style shooter. In this case, "retro" means somewhere around Duke Nukem 3D but with actual 3D aiming like Quake and subsequent games - when level geometry was created with textured polygons but hardware wasn't quite up to creating moving character models. It is almost like the pre-Quake period lasted just long enough to produce another technological advance before the jump to full-3D models and areas. There were about six months between the release of Duke Nukem 3D and Quake. If that time period were stretched out to, say, a year, this game would have come out in that hypothetical year (call it  "1996 Part II").The graphics are a little hard to describe if you aren't familiar with the source inspiration. The levels are built from polygons with a "chunky" layout - no fine little details are 3D rendered - and pixelated textures that sell a 1996 look. The thing that a player with no grounding in that era might be hard-pressed to understand is the sprites used for enemy models. In games of that era, each enemy was represented by a sprite with alternate versions for a front-view, side-view, back-view, and two diagonals. This game recreates that but with more than just five versions (there are also above angle views). It is hard to explain, but it looks neat and retro as hell.With that out of the way, how does it actually play? If you are familiar with those high-speed run-and-gun shooters like Doom, Quake, Duke Nukem 3D etc., then you are in the right ballpark. You don't have regenerating health, so you have to dodge a lot and only sniper-style weapons have an aim-down-sights function, the rest you shoot from the hip. Unlike most of the games that inspire this playstyle, Prodeus actually includes reloading as a nice pacing mechanic.The gunplay is punchy and brutal. The gunfire is loud and really sells itself as powerful. Monsters are torn to bits and the area is splattered with copious volumes of blood. If you are familiar with Brutal Doom, it is something like that. In fact, this game makes me think of what a direct sequel to Doom 2 would have been like if Id had knocked one out before moving on to Quake.Once nice evolution from true classic shooters is that new weapons don't completely overshadow the old ones. The chaingun, for example, is generally better than the pistol, but the pistol remains the best long range gun up until you get a real sniper weapon. The weapons are big, mean, and over the top. They produce big loud bangs and flash the screen with their blasts.In general, one can rate a shooter by the quality of its gunplay and its movement. Prodeus has amazing gunplay and average movement. If you liked Brutal Doom, heavy metal, and teeth-clinching gorespatterfest battles with demon/alien monsters, then I can give this one a whole-hearted recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply intense, brutal and fun. The gameplay itself is not as deep as Doom Eternal obviously and is more a modern version of the old Doom games. Which is not bad at all, its really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome.A ton of weapons, easy weapon switches for fast gameplay, the HUD is quite centered so every important information is easy to watch and the level design is great so far.Btw I really love the graphic style, because while its pixel art, it still looks very modern. _childDocuments_.review: Very fun game for the most part, level design is excellent and the guns feel good. My only problems are as follows:*  Checkpoint system and no manuals saves/quicksaves is by and far the dumbest thing in a boomer shooter*  The other enemy faction is kind of boring, just harder reskins of other enemies, and there aren't that many unique enemy types to begin with*  While the whole modding scene is cool, the game has fundamental flaws that make them hard to enjoy*  I really really wish it were possible to turn down the gore since blood flying everywhere really obscures what's going on* I personally hate the Shop system where you buy weapons and upgrades, it's extremely immersion-breaking and it feels like it was a forced in mechanic, there's no reason for it to be there other than to be there. Playing without ever using it is just crippling yourself.I got the game on sale so I can't really be too mad about my purchase, but I don't really think you'd be missing out on anything. It's very cool to look at but it has a lot of flaws that kinda take me out of the game. GZDoom with any variety of thousands of mods can easily replicate any positive experience I had with this game.

_childDocuments_.user: The Man, the Miph, the Legend
_childDocuments_.review: I've been hyping this game up for quite some time, and now that it's finally arrived I have to say that it definitely has not disappointed me, even though I was apprehensive when I saw "Early Access". I've been hungry for a retro styled FPS such as this ever since the disappointment I felt from Doom Eternal (Low Ammo Simulator). Whilst Prodeus definitely does have a lot of similar aspects to Doom as a series overall, it has enough to stick out on its own and also has some things which just feel BETTER than they had in Doom. Weapons feel meaty and very strong, and overall the general gunplay is very enjoyable with a large variety of weaponry at your disposal with everything feeling like it serves a purpose.Even though I've hyped up this game, no game is without flaws and the ones in Prodeus that I've encountered up until now are somewhat irritating. This review is based upon my personal perceptions thus far according to what I've experienced until now whilst playing. As the game is currently Early Access, my review will be edited with further iterations of the game coming out. The Good:- Weapon variety & Gunplay. One of the key elements to any good FPS is just how good the weapons feel, and Prodeus' weapons feel incredibly impactful. It seems as though there's 15 or more different weapon, with almost all of the weapons feeling incredibly satisfying to use. Each weapon has a satisfying punch behind it, and it just makes the game feel great. - Map design. Map design hearkens back to that of the early years of FPS design, such as the Dooms, Hexen's, and various other similar games that were available back then, whilst also managing to feel retro and like it was pulled out of something like DOOM 2016.- Sound design. Every sound in this game feels as if it fits together in the overall framework of the game, coming together to add to the experience. From the heavy punch of a shotgun firing off at something across the map, or the scream of an enemy rushing across the map to attack, everything sounds fantastic.- The soundtrack. I'm not sure which I like better at this point, and the tie is between Doom 2016's or Prodeus' soundtrack. I've been thoroughly impressed by every single song that's been added into the game, and also impressed by just how much variety there is, considering this game is still in early access.- Secrets feel satisfying. One thing I have a hard time with is retro-styled FPS games and how they liberally sprinkle secrets all around the game, yet they seem to contain almost no sustenance typically. Prodeus rewards players with things which feel worthwhile to hunt, with weapon unlocks very early on, large amounts of health and various other things.- Difficulty. Difficulty within Prodeus feels great just from out of the gate. I began playing the game on the hardest difficulty, and the enemies don't feel as though they're bloated up or anything to the point that they're just ridiculous sponges.- Built-in level editor that allows users to publish their own maps. I've yet to dabble with the level editor myself, but a game having the capability to upload maps within itself so that users can download it is fantastic, as this just leads on to the game having much more longevity and replayability. User made campaigns can be uploaded as well, possibly telling unique stories that a creator would like to tell.The Ok:- Some weapons feel like they've been given TOO much power and thus diminish the usefulness of others. There's a few weapons in the game that just feel eclipsed by various other weapons, with the prime example of this being the starting shotgun, which seems like it's just been given TOO MUCH power and utility. When obtaining the starting shotgun it feels proper and well-placed, however upon obtaining more and more weapons as you continue further, the shotgun will continue to outplay some of them with the added functionality that it's essentially a Rifle as well, that can seemingly do as much direct damage to an enemy with the secondary fire as a single rocket.- Weapons sharing ammunition pools. I've not personally run into an issue yet with this, however almost every singular FPS that does this has the issue of the player being consistently out of ammunition across multiple encounters, or a single weapon from the shared ammo pool just outclassing the others tremendously which results in the others no longer being utilized.The Bad:- Enemies ALWAYS know where you are and ALWAYS attack at you regardless of whether you're in cover. Whilst I understand that if you were to pop behind a small rock an enemy would obviously be able to attack you, Prodeus seems to have the weird issue of enemies being omniscient. Regardless of where I've gone, or how far out of sight I've run at times, I'll immediately pop around a corner to get shot IMMEDIATELY by something. Imps will throw fire over walls at you even if there's multiple objects between you and then which they can't see through, and they'll throw directly where you are. As someone currently playing the game through on the hardest difficulty, this just feels cheap as most of my health is chipped away BEFORE I can even react to an enemy as they're omniscient.- The Checkpoint System. Checkpoints in Prodeus work like this: You press Continue and then there's no punishment for the player, no restarting of stuff you'd done before, nothing. Enemies rush at you from every corner of the area around you and can attack you before your screen begins to show you what's in front of you, causing you to lose chunks of health. It feels as though there should be a life system, keeping you from just bashing your head against the game until you win out of endurance, as you have infinite lives whilst the enemies have finite.- Some weapons feel as though they aim above where the reticle designates, and in an FPS this is problematic. This seems to only be an issue with a few weapons, and has only particularly felt evident whilst aiming directly at the heads of enemies to one-shot them, with the enemies head directly in the center or possibly even higher than the center sometimes resulting in the shot to careen over their hair resulting in giving them a shave.- Pause menu clutter. Every single button on the pause menu when you press esc is the exact same size with the "Restart" button being RIGHT BELOW continue, which I've no idea why this was considered a good idea. I've pressed Restart thrice purely on accident and had to trek along the entire map once more due to how close the button is to the option to continue.-Overall Rating: 8.5/10Worth $24.99? Honestly, I feel like it is. I typically keep from playing any early access game as I'd much rather experience the end product, but unfortunately I could not wait. I've not been disappointed since I purchased it.Closing thoughts: Whilst the game definitely exists in the same vein as the original doom games and various other retro-styled FPS games which are being released nowadays, I feel as though Prodeus will becomes its own beast as time goes on. I've enjoyed my time playing the game, and it's scratching that itch I've had, allowing me to run and gun like I'd wanted earlier this year.

There are a lot of dem fancy guns. And they are not just another double barrel ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or silly brrt brrt gun. They really pack a punch and it feels so satisfying to blast your load into the face of some monster trying to come for you (what are you thinking?). That's all I can say for now since I only played this game for ~30min and I really need to go now since I just remembered that I forgot to turn off the stove.But one thing to add: Prodeus is ealy access. _childDocuments_.review: It's like if iD had released a classicly-styled doom 3 in early 1996 instead of releasing quake later that year, but somehow found a way to cram in an extra 20 years of really good map design experience. The map design is really the star of the show, it's almost universally EXCELLENT map design. The level design tools and built-in custom map distribution have produced a lot of really good community maps as well.There are two flaws though. Everyone can see the other reviews discussing the bad checkpoint system that allows for just suicide rushing through a level and punching enemies to death when ammo runs out, so I won't go over that again. But the game ends so abruptly. You get tons of tech-base stuff, then a few onyx cavern levels in the prodean dimension which are also great, then a couple levels that are tech base again but with snow now and a new weapon that kind of sucks and a new enemy that seems to have a bull-fight gimmick but is really just "shoot it until it dies", and then one level in the chaos dimension that serves as the game's only bad level, followed a final one-room box of a boss arena. The last three tilesets (prodean, ice base, chaos) are woefully underutilized and the game's ending feels incredibly rushed and underwhelming as a result.But... I really want to emphasize, the level design in the tech-base and prodean areas is really, really good and absolutely worth playing. Interesting central concepts to every one of those levels that make them all feel unique. Even if the reported followup free additions by the devs never materialize, you'll still have a wealth of great community maps and campaigns to play too.

_childDocuments_.review: A Great Doom Clone from Modern Times. Prodeus is a Retro FPS game developed by Bounding Box Software and published by Humble Games. It's notable for being one of the earliest contenders of reviving the Retro FPS genre back in around 2018, finally coming out of early access around 5 years later. It is most notable for having some of the most bloodiest and chunky gore effects for the style of game it's going for as well as a plethora of uncommon features like a full blown level editor and a really in depth Automap. Though as the game itself is great I feel like it came a bit too late when it comes to the stand of Retro FPS games now. Gameplay of Prodeus oddly is recommencement of the infamous Doom mod: Brutal Doom. You have over the top gore, a plethora of weapons that extend the original Doom lineup of weapons (Shotgun, Chaingun, Rocket Launcher, Plasma, etc), and reloading for the sake of reloading. Starting with the Weapons, you got a decent lineup of big guns to use with nearly all of them being useful in someway or another, even late in the game. Like how the pistol is near accurate and has a alt-fire that is extremely useful instead of it being completely useless or how the Quad Shotgun, yes a Quad Shotgun, is able to be combined with other close range weapons to provide a swift end to the beefier enemies. With combos like that being able to be done fluidly with the game's quickselect menu. As Prodeus has a lot of weapons per slot and defaults to the first weapon on the number key when pressed, the quickselect menu makes it a absolute breeze thanks to it completely stopping time with it active. Futhermore the sound design for everysingle weapons is superb, absolutely fantastic stuff and it makes reloading a bit worth it to hear the sounds of the weaponry reloading.Now with the enemies, a lot of the enemy variety takes a lot of inspiration from Doom's Archetypes, like a bit too much from Doom's. Like you got your Shotgun Guys, your Imps, your big floating meatballs, and those annoying quick flying lost souls. Extremely familiar territory with a new coat of paint, so familiar that I kinda struggled to have a moment of fair challenge as these enemies were extremely easy to deal with even on Normal, or heck even the single level I did on Ultra Hard. However there are a few new enemy that shake things up a bit. Such as the railgun soldiers who are silentest the most annoying as they just cut straight through your health and armor or the entire Prodeus enemy subtype, who are blue versions of the normal, Chaos, enemies that will infight on sight. It's not much but it does just enough to not make it notable from other Doom-like enemy rosters. As for Style, Prodeus absolutely nails combining the 90s game engine aesthetic with modern effects without making it hard to read. Like the game runs on Unity, but the way the levels are designed look straight out of 90s shooter but with increased detail and moving parts. Though I think most of the level design does take more from Doom than it does Build with some expectations. As most of the campaign levels feels more like the abstract space facilities that Doom did than making a realish place that works well as a arena. But like Build there is a ton of detail put into the environments to make them not just feel like textured walls. Heck, there is even a somewhat proper vehicle level that you obviously blown up at the end.Overall, Prodeus was a great time, good visuals, outstanding sound design, and great combat! I do think the game could have done more however, like how there is only one weapon that uses plasma cells or the mostly familiar enemy roster. I think as a game released in 2022 there has been a ton of Shooters released prior that did more with the formula, and not even just with the whole movement shooter gameplay that ULTRAKILL or Turbo Overkill are going for. Hands of Nercomancy tried a stab at Hexen's format and made it less confusing, Vomitorium's visuals are udderly disgusting (in a good way) and a solid Metroidvania, and Hedon was able to stand out with it's world building, story, and very interesting character design. Again I'm not saying Prodeus as a whole is terrible far from it, but I think when it finally came out, other games had already did more with the genre than just being another Retro Throwback. Though thanks to the game having a extremely in-depth level editor will help keep Prodeus alive for a good while.(Also I recommend waiting for a sale as 25$ is a bit pricey even though the length makes up for it pretty well)

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is the best retro fps on the market, and a must buy for anyone looking for a old school shooter that has modern controls and game play. The hud of game is very customizable. Players can change the look and scale of ui and also how enemies are rendered.The sound track is great fit for this game, as more and more enemies spawn in and start attacking you the music will intensify. Once you've cleared a room it will get quieter, ramping up once more when more enemies are encountered.All the guns feel like mighty and have impact when firing them. Also they all have a secondary fire mode that expanse the viability of the guns and are useful in many situations. The down side right now is since it's early access, the story mode is short and not fully complete (it's also rather short). Although players can download and share community made maps to make up for it, with some excellent maps being made to keep players playing. Prodeus also isn't very hard, even on the hardest difficulty sittings you won't be finding your self struggling to complete a level. It's also lacking a multiplayer death match type mode and co-op offerings. If you're looking for that type of content you'll have to wait. The good news is that the devs have said they plan on adding those modes at a later point, and will also be expanding upon the stroy mode.With that said however. I can only see this game getting better with future updates and is currently worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly, highly, recommend.  I was waiting for a sale, it didn't come, it didn't need to.  This is an awesome throw back to the classic side-strafing fps of the 90s, except with a nice modern touch.  The gore and guts are awesome and brutal.  The weapon variety is tremendous, and I feel like this is where it really gets set apart from others in this genre such as Ion Fury, which have much more boring weapon varieties and fewer differences between them.  This game really nails it with impactful and fun weapons no matter what you're using.The levels seem the appropriate lengths and there is even a level editor I haven't gotten which I am guessing contains community-made maps!It's fast-paced, balls the wall.You do have to reload, and I wonder why they chose to add such a mechanic, however it's not a substantial deal, and is incredibly fast.The music is hardcore and heavy metal, as it should be.  You're always running.  The secrets are easy-ish to find, and I feel like it's the right amount of challenge.  I personally dont like playing a puzzle game when I want a ball-busting FPS.The maps are straight-forward in that you don't get lost or stuck finding where to go next.The environments are varied and different.The enemy types are very similar to many from the classic DOOM games, and that's fine, because those games are still to this day some of the best FPS ever made.One of my favourite things is seeing all ammo available for all weapons on the screen at once, so you aren't switching in combat wondering what you have stocked up, or running to pointless ammo pickups that you don't need.  A really nice touch!

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game, it is old-school Doom I / II, but improved in every aspect. So, if compared to Doom, it is:- More vertical- More action- More weapons- More monster types- Modern engine with all it's benefits- More dynamic / scripted maps in campaign- 3D map- optional 3D enemy models (2D models are made so good, that it is actually hard to recognize that they are just 2)- ...I kind of personally remember Doom II maps more, even they looked uglier, but they were unique in their time. In modern design, there are usually some techniques used to guide to player forward. I think it was missing in Doom, that made you usually thinking about the map ... where you should go next, and that way, plus some weird level design, plus being low on health and missing ammunition often, made the maps more memmorable - as they also brought in some (desperate, being lost, victorious to find way forward) emotions. In Prodeus, you just respawn, and can go mindlesly into the fight again, you can even mindlesly run through some levels. The secrets are kind of balancing that, and sometimes you need to revisit the level to collect previously unreachable secrets.I think, the levels will be more memorable if they will utilize more themes, more different textures. (I am around half-way in the campaign currently)Otherwise I must say, that there are a lot of great ideas in the maps. Playing a lot of games, makes it harder to remember, but I think some levels/level parts I will remember due to their unique mechanics and design.So, totally recommend to all who likes action FPS and are not scared of visible pixels :D

_childDocuments_.review: A game with unlimited potential. While the main campaign is still in early access, it's an amazing ride. A love letter to Doom and it's clones, Prodeus builds on the originals with a great soundtrack, wonderful level design, and tight controls. And the best part? The campaign will be a small portion of the overall experience. This features a full level editor, and user maps are already being created. These maps aren't so simple as more run in gun, rather fresh ideas that have no reference in the original content. You can, down to its core, make levels anyway you'd like. You can also build entire campaigns with your levels, to the point of creating you're own game.As I said, it's a game with unlimited potential, this is like the Mario Maker of FPS's, and content is constantly dropping from the community. This game isn't even $60, but it sure is worth that.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Brutal Doom x Halo 2; Great and worth playingProdeus is a great game. I fell in love with the art style and gameplay from the first mission. It does, however, have one major flaw (at least for me). I'm not a fan of the way this game handles difficulty. I played on hard mode, and generally speaking it is not a very difficult game; it's satisfying. However, the difficulty does spike a few times in a big way and when it does, it's almost always just you being locked in an area with hordes of enemies spawning around you until you finish the last wave. The checkpoint system keeps these sections reasonable, it's more-so just annoying getting swarmed by projectiles from all sides with the constant damage effects that seem unavoidable. Once or twice is fine, but in the mid-to-late game it seemed to happen in almost every other level. I personally prefer when they ramp up difficulty in more interesting ways, like the early-mid level  The game would benefit from more creative sections like this.Besides that, this game does have a ton going for it. The art-style, as I mentioned, is fantastic. The 2d/3d mix works really well and is always a spectacle. The gore is exactly how I imagined the original doom games were when I was a kid and probably how it would have been if they had the tech. The enemies are cool and wear their creative inspirations on their sleeve, a little more variety wouldn't have been a detriment but what's there is good. The two biggest strengths for me were the weapons and the level design. There's a good mix of large, labyrinthine maps and smaller, fast-paced and straightforward maps. This game also makes finding secrets very satisfying without being frustrating. Lastly and most impressively, are the guns. The game heavily rewards you for using every weapon type in the game, and I found myself constantly switching between every weapon in my arsenal. Even in the end game, I found myself using the starting pistol almost as much as every other game. Some weapons are obviously stronger than others but at the detriment of burning ammo, the selection is INCREDIBLY well-balanced. It might be the most balanced and enjoyable arsenal of any game I've played and I can't stress enough how impressive that is.Overall, it's an awesome game with one major gripe, and some people won't agree with the gripe and will have an even better time than I did. The ending is  but it's not nearly as bad as people say. I enjoyed this game a lot and I'll probably find myself replaying it at a higher difficulty, which is very rare for me and speaks a lot to the enjoy-ability of Prodeus.

_childDocuments_.review: To state that I adore boomer shooters would be a severe understatement, and having grown up around their ilk, such as Wolfenstein, Doom and Quake, they pretty much defined a generation of gaming for me. So, when I saw Prodeus come onto the radar, I just had to jump at the opportunity to experience what looked like a new-era vintage shooter.In a classic shooter sense, Prodeus doesn't sport much of a storyline.You assume control of a corrupted agent who seeks to destroy his creator, Prodeus.On your journey, you will face minions of Chaos, the arch-enemies of Prodeus and other minions of your creator's army, all of which are attempting to stop you before you kill their master and destroy the world as they know it.The plot isn't great, nor are the explanations you receive throughout it. But it provides enough incentive to turn your foes into red mist, and I guess is enough story for the genre.Prodeus is a fairly standard boomer shooter down to the very fundamentals.If it moves, it wants to kill you, and it's your job not to let them.You have a decent array of weapons, most of which unlock throughout the campaign, and the rest you will have to purchase from the in-game story, using in-game currency. that you earn from a thorough exploration of levels.The enemies aren't particularly abundant in variety, but there's enough to offer a decent challenge for the roughly 10 hours of gameplay it has to offer. You will likely get bored by the time you realise most of the enemies you are fighting are just reskins, but that's a pretty minor concern to have based on the format.Exploration is an essential aspect of Prodeus, as you will need to use the in-game currency to unlock items as you progress through the campaign, and the only way to attain it is to find them hidden across its many levels.But the currency isn't the only thing worth exploring, as there are secret guns, enemies, and hidden exits across the world for you to find that will significantly improve your chances of survival.With that said, the maps are well-designed from both an aesthetic and action perspective, and despite how linear they are they do give you a sense of being much larger than they are.The map is useful but perhaps a little too fidgety to accurately utilise in most situations, but it does provide a quick reference point if you're ever stuck.I genuinely believe this game is an iconic visual and audio experience.Capturing the old-school nostalgic shooter vibes with some modern-day visual effects that genuinely make you feel unstoppable as you run, gun and smear enemy forces across the facade of sprawling open maps.As for the audio, the animations and soundtrack are so well-designed that the heavy, visceral combat will make you feel like every step is real, and every shot fired hurts, all of this combined with a soundtrack that makes you want to cause mayhem for every second of the campaign.The Steam Deck had no issue running this game, and a fully-charged battery was able to sustain unfaltering gameplay for close to 5 hours without needing another charge.Is this the best boomer shooter on the market? No, not really.Is it a fun, and fast paced gun and gore-filled experience that will keep you on the edge of your seat? Hell yeah.Prodeus does a lot of things right and some of them wrong, with a little bit of "meh" in the middle, but is generally a pretty entertaining experience with some innovative ideas and a great aesthetic style that never gets old. It's probably not worth the $40 they are asking for, but I'd say it's worth it for anything close to 50% off, and if you can get it for cheaper then even better.

The only way to circumvent this, is to do a full restart which will restart you from the very beginning. The monsters are basically a straight rip of doom monsters. For instance, I use the shotguns a lot, but if you aim between two people that are stacked almost on top of each other, it will only hit the first enemy 95% of the time. _childDocuments_.review: Quite a fun retro-style shooter. Movement feels crisp and precise, combat is satisfying for the most part, and the campaign levels are well done. The weapons are satisfying to use, and each one has a place and purpose. Even the starting fists and pistol can be used in the later levels effectively. Additional replayability is added through the in-game custom maps browser where there seems to be quite a wealth of talent in community mapmakers. If you enjoyed games like DUSK and/or DOOM 2016 then you'll likely enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is awesome. Yes,  you'd think it's a boomer shooter, but actually it's a pretty modern shooter (except for the looks of course). It has a 3D automap, a decent overworld, Metroidvania elements, exploration and sure as hell - a lot of shooting. Its fast paced, action packed gunplay is addictive, the weapons are a lot of fun and looking for secrets, to be able to afford special guns, as well as double jump and so on, makes this game really worth your while. The story however is underwhelming, to say the least. Few text boxes, before starting a map and sometimes you stumble over another text box wihtin the map. On the other hand - who cares for the story? The game is short enough for you to enjoy every last second. And when you're done and want more - there's an awesome, easy to use map editor and a buttload of community maps. Stop reading this review - go BUY this gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Doom x slight Halo musicProdeus is an amazing retro fps that will make your day bloody with joy. It's gameplay is fast paced similar to Doom eternal as each weapon provides a different benefit as they get added to your arsenal from sustained fire, accurate shots, or just immediate huge damage. The music that accompanies this goreyfest has its share of metal as it dips to something like Halo with a choir piece that gives you an almost angelic feeling as you gun down everything in your vicinity till the map is red. The maps themselves ramp up from straightforward to complex ones that slowly teach the games mechanics from the enemies to the terrain but no matter how big they get you don't get the feeling of getting lost as there are map cues dotted where you need to go. If you do get lost the map is handy to look where u need to go or see odd spaces where a secret could possibly hide. Prodeus is an amazing game for something in early access, the campaign may not be finished but it has community made maps to keep you running on blood with its gunplay or maybe try your hand yourself to make one. It's honestly been therapeutic experience to play this game and see how much red is on the map.

Most of the ones that move, do so slowly. There's always more than enough cover and a LOT of ammo/armor/health.Peek, tap-tap-tap, peek, tap, peek, tap-tap-tap - the area is clear, hold W for half a minute till the next area. Rinse and repeat.You don't even have to have a good reaction to do that - most of the enemy attacks are telegraphed well in advance.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Co-op boom shoot built with arcade mechanics in mind. Everything is chunky, bloody, messy, and fast ('Always Run' for life). All weapons are amazing including the fists and pistol. My favorite however is the standard shotgun that has your usual buckshot and an alternate charged slug. In fact all weapons have alt modes. The pistol has burst fire, the rocket launcher has remote detonation, the Arc Gun has a railgun mod, etc. The only two negatives i have is that enemies spawn way too slowly, and the nexus point system. They're vita-chambers but completely unnecessary, especially in co-op where you can spawn next to your friend always without any penalty excluding points. They should include a timer so the others should hold on for dear life to revive you. Overall this is a fun and bloody mess. Thumbs up!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a doozy, a bloodbath, and above all else, a classic FPS contemporized.Looks stylish, the weapons are punchy, the music f-uckin-g slaps. I'm glad I backed this project up. And the level design is some of the most devious and yet amazing stuff (thanks Mike, Jason and Dragonfly).There is some amount of jank (limbless projectile toss) and the carnage sometimes obscures the enemy/projectile line up, but it's nothing a little extra spray for good measure won't solve.And I cannot for the love of god, figure out the scoring system.  .   Am big dummy. Time, secrets, kills, deaths and No news of multiplayer but there are rumors. There's a level editor making the game infinite.It's a good game. A damn good game. Get it.  Gripes:1) There is no option to change Brightness/Gamma.2) I wish I could delete my save slots.3) The options menu is very cluttered. _childDocuments_.review: This game needed to ditch the Nexus Point system when it was still an idea. For it to have been three years and a full release, with DLC on the way, and it's still the default and only option, is insanity. It removes all difficulty. It isn't just a check point system, it's just a spawn point system in real time. You die, you just spawn a few feet behind you, with full health. Often, the enemies will return to their spawn points too, allowing you a chance to get the drop on them. It's such a bizarre and weirdo choice for a game that so clearly wants to look and feel like an old school game. You know the expression "if it ain't broke, don't fix it?" Well, this game tried to fix quick saves and/or checkpoints, and failed miserably.It's the kind of thing that should be buried in an accessibility menu, made to appease unskilled children learning to play a video game for the first time, or the casual audience that doesn't want a challenge. To have this be the only option in a game that's meant to cater to old school shooter fans it's a truly wacky choice.If you can look past that, you'll also have to have the generosity to play a game with items in a shop that you can buy, with key bindings, but cannot use. And when I say items, I mean weapons. Even though the game is no longer in early access, these are still sitting there taunting you.When I first played this, years ago on Gamepass, I was willing to overlook this stuff because I kept seeing people say it was planned to be changed in the future. Now? Eh, it kind of annoys me.Despite all that, the game is fun. It feels like you've stepped into an alternate timeline where Doom 3 wasn't a spooky tech demo but was, instead, the goriest game ever made. Seriously the amount of blood in this game is absolutely wild. Ever play Brutal Doom? It's like that, except larger enemies erupt in a small explosion of blood.The weapon feedback is great, it sounds punchy and heavy. The weapons are great, with some great renditions of FPS classics like the super shotgun, rocket launcher, and plasma rifle. The overall look of the game is bleak and oppressive and metallic, which compliments the Hulshult soundtrack. Level design is great. You'll never get lost, even when the levels open up or have some complexity.I've played the game three times now, so it's clearly getting it right where it matters. It's a very straight forward shooter not looking to reinvent the wheel, and it more or less does what it sets out to do.

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of the glory days of Doom, Wolfenstien, Heretic, Hexen - that sort of game. Enjoying it very much so far! Edit: This game is so so so worth playing. It gets pretty frantic on some later levels - which is great fun and mowing through monsters with the different weapons hasn't gotten old. _childDocuments_.review: Its old school Doom on a modern engine but with checkpoints rather than saves.  It already has a rich and active mapping community producing high quality content.  I hope it will come to be the successor to Zdoom, but we will see.The art and design are very good, delivering an atmosphere of desperation and foreboding.  The game is good looking, but visually repetitive; it will be good when more resources become available. Story is minimal and thank god for that, I am here to shoot and when I want story, I read.  Weapon and monster design are spot on. The retro graphics are puzzling to me, I just do not see an advantage to the use of sprites over models (yes I know about the option for models, but lots of sprites remain). Grainy textures and especially filters to purposely degrade image quality are an odd choice.   I understand it is an aesthetic choice, but as someone that was playing old shooters before computers were powerful enough to support 3d models and full colour, it is one that makes little sense.  It strikes me as misplaced nostalgia for something that had little to no advantage over the technology that replaced it.  Doom was an ugly, ugly game, I am glad this game looks good.   I understand that the huge amount of labour needed for overly detailed artwork, textures, resources is a drain on small budget projects.  Games like this don't need ridiculous graphics, but I don't think they need to dumb the graphics down to the level they are either.The check point system is somewhat contentious.  Old fogeys like me like their save games.  I work, a lot, in a senior position with a lot of responsibility.  I have family.  I have other things to do.   It would be nice to just save a game and come back to finish a map another time, without having to start all over again.  It would be nice to go back and find secrets, replay sections with different tactics etc, without having to start a level over again.  Yes, I realise some people think this is cheating. I have talked to the arrogant little snots on the forum who think so.  ♥♥♥♥ them.  Give us a game mode that lets us use saves.  Make it separate from the leader boards if it makes people happy.  I don't want to tell anyone else how to play their game, but it sure would be nice to have the option of playing the game the way I like. I look forward to seeing what the finished product eventually delivers.

_childDocuments_.review: How odd for a game to start so strong yet fizzle out before even hitting the midway mark. I feel like I’ve been duped. But backing a Kickstarter is very much buying the pig in the bag, as they say. The preview build that was put out a couple of years ago covered the best parts of the game’s contents, which leads me to believe that perhaps – at the time – this was all they had accomplished from the time of the Kickstarter to entering Early Access on Steam. Why the game seems to go through a design and philosophy shift after these initial levels I don’t know – perhaps it was monetary reasons, perhaps the design team went through changes, or perhaps they just didn’t know what else to do. But somewhere along the line the game’s focus seems to have shifted from being a Quake-like into a Serious Sam-clone, and with that comes nothing of value. Hordes of enemies, tonnes of effects on screen, constantly having to duck and weave to dodge literally everything all at once, and pressing the backwards key considerably more than the forward key at times. It’s not what I had hoped for sadly. And in the end, the game is stupidly easy even on the hardest difficulty, including the later tougher levels where you’ll probably die numerous times – simply because of a respawn system not too dissimilar from the one found in Bioshock. You can simply whittle down the enemy hordes at your own leisure, one life at a time, because you’re not reloading a checkpoint, you’re just respawning. But I think the developers know this, because there’s not even an achievement for beating the game on the hardest difficulty, because, again: it’s not much of an accomplishment.I’d give Prodeus half-a-thumbs up if I could. It’s not bad. It’s just dull. 💩

_childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to love this one, but honestly I've just come away underwhelmed and I'm not really motivated to play it any further.The art style is unique and interesting, but the color palette leaves something to be desired. The enemies are all very basic and don't really have a lot of variance or visual/gameplay interest. They're less distinct from each other than the Doom games they were lifted from.The guns feel satisfying to kill with, but it doesn't really lift the gameplay from monotony when you're just killing the same slow, bland enemies in every fight. There's a lot of redundancy among the guns as well, so there's no really incentive to use all of them. The pistol, smgs, and machine gun all use the same ammo and have pretty similar use cases. The shotgun secondary fire charges up for an underwhelming long range shot that feels like a waste of time to wait for. In the same vein, the plasma gun (lifted straight from doom 3) has a secondary fire tracking dart that causes all the bullets to fly lazily towards the spot you designate. Why would you ever bother with that when you can just shoot them straight away? The ONE single application for this would be to mark ONE single enemy and hide behind cover to shoot them around the corner. Who the hell wants to do that in a fast paced doom style game? This same mechanic was done MUCH better in Overkill, and even in that game it feels kind of pointless.It just seems like the devs just added random stuff from the games they were copying, and had no idea how to make the gameplay actually engaging. There are no new ideas here besides the art style, and the visuals are not enough to keep me playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Disclosure: This gift was a gift from a friend. This review was written while still in Early Access, but the launch is so close to release I feel confident in standing by this review.TLDR: Prodeus is a great callback to older boomer shooters with a rocking metal OST, but barely misses the mark in surpassing its source of inspiration. Good, but I expected more. 7/10 The localized damage when enemies take damage and the stylized graphics are a great improvement on the old formula. Gibbing enemies with a fully-charged shotgun blast at close range will never get old, the shooter trance is here in full effect, and my reactionary panic swapping to the mini-gun when a room of enemies spawns in brings me to my younger days. I'll gladly play this over some classic games or their remakes like Serious Sam, but better games like Doom Eternal exist. I found myself constantly looking for newer innovations that simply weren't here. Things like melee executions, glory kills, and enemy specific weapon weaknesses cannot be found here. Weapon choice is purely a question of DPS needed, with no motivation outside of the ending score to play more aggressively. Far less forgivable are the hallmarks of the original games Prodeus pulls inspiration from that aren't there. The head in the game's HUD lacks animation and by extension... all character. The face is there, but there's no eyes looking for enemies to kill, no reaction when hit, and no homicidal smile when picking up a new gun. It might as well not even be there. Hopefully some additional "character" is added in the final release. The bar for "character" is pretty low in these old boomer shooters, but not even that is here. The metal OST is great and improves the experience. I will buy this OST.

_childDocuments_.review: this is a hard one for me.on the one hand, the gameplay is spot-on boomer shooter stuff.  the gfx have their own weird charm.  the weapons are fun to use.  the enemies explode in fountains of blood that drips off the ceiling if you kill them hard enough.  theres even a pretty cool enemy faction dynamic with the demons and angels fighting eachother.on the other hand, its short.  im mostly done with the campaign at 10 hours.  im an idiot who gets lost alot, so take that as you will.  theres also lots of user-created content, and props to the devs for including a decent level-maker.the big problem is the save/checkpoint system.  i literally cannot comprehend how a developer would choose something like this.  when you die, you respawn at your nearest checkpoint.  pretty standard stuff, right?  well, in prodeus all enemies you killed since last you passed that checkpoint do not respawn.  you are literally unkillable and can just brute force any level.  dont tell me i can just choose to restart.  that takes a certain amount of wherewithal and i dont have it.  quicksaves have been fps standards since doom for a reason.  or if not that, at least actual checkpoints.im probably going to play the rest of prodeus because i really like it, but im not going to be satisfied, because the game wont let me die

_childDocuments_.review: As an old-school shooter, the story certainly isn’t expected to be the strong suit of Prodeus. You’ll be put in the shoes of a soldier (?), sent to a science facility to investigate (?) what the hell is going on. Surprise, someone screwed with unknown, dangerous forces over there, and the whole thing went south when people started turning into monsters or bloodthirsty maniacs. Sounds familiar? Yeah, some guys called Id Software did something a -tad- similar some 30-years back, who would’ve known!The visuals here are nothing short of stunning. With a set of filters to emulate true retro aesthetics, Prodeus gives options to customize fidelity, resolution scaling and more aspects to have as much modern or retro as you want. Fights are a cornucopia of splattered guts, blood literally dripping from ceilings, limping enemies, mad quasi-humans turned into flesh mounds at a buckshot’s notice. Level layouts are varied in both locations and themes; most feel unique, even if there are some repetitions for story reasons.You’ll explore on foot, with sprint always on if you wish, as it’s simply an upgrade to just walking. Maps are often convoluted, expansive both in width and verticality, and some even have evolving layouts influenced by environmental effects - which is great. Of course, roaming around will trigger the appearance of numerous foes from thin air, being inter-dimensional horrors and all, but once you clear an area out, you’re free to explore for secrets, supplies and whatever else. A wise choice to do immediately, because you may get locked-out of a part of the level at a moment’s notice, which really sucks.Secrets range from our run-of-the-mill large armor hidden in some remote corner, to rather convoluted jumping puzzles housing rare weapons, ammo or the invaluable Ore Fragments, used as a currency to buy upgrades and new weapons. Each level has several of these, and finding as many as you can is important to unlock stronger weapons and utility upgrades as you progress through the linear, on-rails, top-down world map.Fights in Prodeus are fast-paced, and feature a low TTK for both yourself and enemies on higher difficulties. Numerous foes can blast you to shreds from full health in an instant, but so can you thanks to your veritable arsenal of guns, ranging from the classic Super Shotgun to more exotic implements such as the Mammonth energy revolver or the target-seeking plasma rifle. All of them feel unique, meaningful to use, and there’s no real “god gun” to beat them all: use what is best for the situation at hand. Utility modules like double jump and dash will help in a fight, but the good old strafing and getting to cover will be the go-to strats more than anything else.Enemies are lethal and fast, but also repetitive in archetypes: the various recolor or slight variants do not escape a mostly-limited array of base models, which gets stale in the 30+ levels of the campaign. You will definitely get tired of fighting the same crap over and over. Don’t worry about running out of ammo or saving up the good ones for when it really matters: levels are crammed with munitions, and some even have infinite ammo-restocking pads.Or, you’ll get tired - period - thanks to the mind-boggling design decision of enforcing “easy mode” for everyone, “those pesky gamers wanting a challenge be damned” probably being the thought crossing the devs’ minds after way too many pints. That’s right: in this old-school shooter you can never fail a level, as you can respawn unlimited times at no penalty; there are checkpoints, but they simply act as respawn beacons, not rolling back the level’s state upon death. This single choice invalidates any and all challenge, because one can simply not care anymore about staying alive, about being careful or about being mindful on resources, scavenging health and ammo to have a better chance in the next arena - there’s nothing of that in Prodeus, because you have de-facto god-mode always on.Is based on gathering Ore Fragments scattered throughout levels, mostly in secret areas, too then spend them at Shops that sell new weapons, utility augments such as double jump or dash, increased max ammo and more. There will be Ores in excess, so you don’t have to get all those in a level to get all upgrades. The progression feels alright, and it’s exciting to get enough ores to then stop by the trader and get that new shiny weapon you looked at for so long.PvP is available in the classic DM, TDM or CTF modes, for those so inclined. Aside from the co-op campaign, additional community maps are downloadable from the Workshop. The integrated map editor allows you to also create your own, and share them with others if you feel creative. Trials could be considered a sub-mode of the campaign: timed levels where you need to speedrun using a specific weapon, in order to get the Ore prize at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: BUY THIS GAME RIGHT. NOW.I bought Prodeus today. I'm a huge fan of boomer shooters. This game... Jesus christ. Buy it. If you're a fan of boomer shooters, buy it. If you're a fan of Doom, buy it. If you're a fan of ABSOLUTELY RIDICULOUS AMOUNTS OF BLOOD, GORE, VISCERA AND BODY HORROR, this game will make you incredibly happy. The game looks, sounds and feels incredible. Absolutely phenomenal. The music is God-tier. The sound effects are to die for. The guns are all SO DAMN CHUNKY. The shotgun is easily in my top 10 fps shotguns, up there with Blood and Wrath: Aeon of Ruin. The Pistol feels incredible. Like so chunky that I'd use it over practically better weapons just for the feel. The shredders are so satisfying, albeit situational. And the minigun. Oh. My. God. The minigun itches every scratch I've been needing from recent games I've been playing. The sound is incredible, it's so chunky, it looks amazing, and it's incredibly effective. The level where you unlock the minigun presents you with a massive murder montage at the end of the episode, where you get max ammo, pick up the minigun, and then the game feeds you more and more ammo along your path as you go through hordes of weak enemies, shredding them and painting yourself and your surroundings in blood, gore and viscera. I've felt like a god before in games. But I've never felt like I could FIGHT god in a video game. The rocket launcher is incredibly satisfying as well. Just like all of the other weapons, upon first firing I audibly gasped and exclaimed how good this game is. In my 2 hours playing it today I probably have recommended it 20 or so times and can't stop gushing about how good it is. I've audibly voiced my pleasure in mowing down hordes of enemies. And I keep catching myself talking to myself as well, just saying "This game is so good" "This game looks amazing" "Oh my god that felt awesome". Buy this game right now. It's an absolute gem. Genuinely worth the $25 just for the 2 hours I've played thus far, and I'm not even 10% through the campaign.BUY THIS GAME. NOW.  IT'S SO GOOD AND THE DEVELOPERS HAVE EARNED EVERY BIT OF MONEY I CAN POSSIBLY GIVE THEM FOR THIS OR ANY FUTURE PROJECTS.

_childDocuments_.review: Budget Doom.I love Doom Eternal, and this feels like the closest I've gotten to a competitor. It's not as good, but if you wanna scratch that itch, Ultra Hard in this game will probably get you there. It's honestly so close to Doom it feels almost unoriginal - but at least they pull it off.The art style is a cool throwback to classic FPSs, with its sprite enemies, and works surprisingly well. Equally the sound design is delightfully gory and bombastic.Two complaints though, which do sour the gameplay for me:- The AI isn't particularly exciting. It feels like every enemy will either just stand still or move towards you. No interesting flanking or shift in elevation. At best, enemies just become very easy to read. At worst, the game throws a horde of enemies at you in a tight space, with explosions and gore obscuring your vision.- The respawn system is absolutely baffling. The game doesn't have checkpoints, it has respawn points. Instead of resetting the game to a checkpoint, it just respawns you there. Meaning everything you killed until you died yourself stays dead. You straight up cannot die - meaning you cannot fail. The only downside to dying is a lowered score. It is INCREDIBLY annoying. Any big challenge in the game is rendered moot as soon as you die, because it feels like you failed. But you cannot restart at the respawn point. You'd have to restart the entire map. Every death just feels like cheesing the game without wanting to. I want to play this game on its hardest, but I don't wanna iron man every level, just because the game doesn't have checkpoints. It's a maddening choice game design wise, and I do not understand this decision.Supposedly they're working on a save system. Until then, I think I wanna wait...
