_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game but it's not for everyone. Truthfully I was mostly checked out by the halfway point. Level design is good but everything else is kinda meh.My complaints are that the game is too derivative, too repetitive, and the upgrade system sucks.This game borrows HEAVILY from Doom. Most of the enemies are ripped straight from Doom. Most of the guns are ripped from Doom or heavily inspired by Doom. The plot is extremely similar to Doom. There are some original things here and there, but for the most part it just feels like I'm playing an extremely overpriced Doom mod. To be fair, Doom is a good game so even a copy of it is fun, but it almost felt like I had played the game before despite it being brand new.My second problem is the repetition. There are only a handful of enemy types in the game, and there's only so many times you can kill them before it starts to get stale. Even the souped up enemies in "hell" are just palette swaps with more HP, they barely add to the variety at all. Eventually the enemies just become fodder and fighting them feels like a waste of time rather than something to be enjoyed. 98% of the time combat is very easy, I even turned up the difficulty to hard and still could count my deaths on one hand. The other 2% of the time the game just throws an unreasonable amount of ♥♥♥♥ at you. There's not a good middle ground where combat is challenging but fair, it's either too easy or overbearing. While the level design is good, it's not enough to carry the game on its own.As for the upgrade system, honestly that's the one thing I wish they copied from Doom and by that I mean left it out entirely. How it works is there's collectible currency scattered throughout each level, usually in hidden locations. You can then spend it at the shop to unlock new guns and abilities. Sounds fine but the implementation is awful. You can only buy from one "tier" of item at a time, and you need to buy everything from that tier to unlock the next tier. Problem is that the double jump and dash are in tier 2, not accessible right away. As far as I know, neither item is needed for progression so there's no reason to gate them off like that. Most of the time you'll be using them to access more currency so you can buy more stuff. I wish the upgrade system was totally gone and instead replaced with an organic system where you find new guns/abilities in the levels. Then there would be no frustration at not being able to buy what you want, no time wasted hunting secrets, and a more cohesive overall experience.And I have to mention the checkpoint system because it's just not right. Throughout each level are several checkpoints that you can activate to respawn there when you die. The problem is that they don't function how checkpoints should. Instead of respawning with the same amount of health and level progress as when you touched the checkpoint, you instead respawn with full health and all the enemies you killed before you died are still dead. Dying has no consequences at all. Not that I died a lot to begin with, but it's still a baffling design choice. And I'm not advocating for the removal of checkpoints. The levels in this game are not short and being forced to replay the whole thing upon death is not the answer. But the checkpoints should function how everyone expects them to function, not like the assist mode out of a Nintendo game.Again, game isn't bad, just didn't get a ton of enjoyment from it. It's fun for a bit but quickly grows old due to the very repetitive and easy combat. Honestly would have been better if it was half the price and half the length that it is.

_childDocuments_.review: So much done right!  This game is worth the money.  (99 hours played)  Movement done right:  There are none of the new mobility options like vaulting/climbing seen in newer titles like Doom 2016 or Eternals, but other than that the movement is super responsive.  If feels grounded and reliable, fast but not too fast.  The result is it feels like modern movement in and old school setting.  It's good.  Guns and Gun Play:  The weapons really shine.  Each weapon has a secondary fire and both the primary and secondary fire has something it does better then any other weapon or fire mode (with the exception of the pistols secondary fire).  Late into a level when I have much more powerful weapons I will still find myself switching to the pistol for specific situations.  The shotgun is a stand out and will be the weapon you use the most but they did a great job with it and its secondary so this isn't a problem.  Enemies:  A number of the enemies are direct analogues of ones from the original doom.  At first this may seem concerning but have no fear, once again they have taken inspiration and made improvements.  Both with the old and new enemies they have done well.  Each has something they do that will effect your movement and how you have to prioritize them.  This doesn't seem like much but when entering a room the addition of a enemy type or the specific mix will greatly effect what you have to do to stay alive.  This is something I rarely see done so well and serves to make each encounter into a moving/blasting puzzle, especially on the harder difficulties.  Level Design.  For me this is the weakest point of the game, but is still done very well.  The levels are designed well and I really do like them.  It's only in being critical for a review that I can find something negative to say.  There are times when the jaggedness and low poly count of an area will feel "too" jaggy.  When I think, "that rock outcropping is the designers trying to looks old school, tisk tisk, overkill".  In Summary:  This game is stellar.  A game that feels Old School but Modern in just the right mix.  The weapons, monsters, and levels are done in a way that fills familiar but fresh.  If you want an old school shooter this is it.  This game is good enough that it stands on its own and will still feel good for people who don't have nostalgia.  My guess is it could create some nostalgia of its own given time.  It's just that good! Oh and there's Community Maps and a Map editor which are outstanding, almost forgot LOL

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't hard to recommend, but there are a few big caveats for me. Look, don't get me wrong, I've never played a game that looks like this before. Amid Evil is probably the only thing that comes close and Prodeus is just that much more of a visual feast. I can't fault it in any way for its art design. It plays smooth, the weapon sounds are incredible, and I really appreciate the little touches such as the overworld map, giving secrets more worth by using them to dispense currency that you can use to buy upgrades, etc. If *only* they'd dedicated these achievements towards a more original and creative end. Prodeus looks unique. But it *feels* like a desperate clone of the Doom reboots.Prodeus is an example of the sallow middle ground between a literal copy-paste job and a throwback or tribute. It pulls so much inspiration from Doom and Quake, both old and new, that it ends up feeling like borderline identity theft. From top to bottom - enemies to art to music to an identical weapon roster - it doesn't just feel like the developers were inspired by those games, it feels like they had very few new ideas of their own. It doesn't help that it fails to balance its difficulty in the way that made both old and new Doom games so thrilling. The enemies are largely imitations of Doom's line-up - zombies, zombies with guns, imps that throw fireballs, stocky four-legged Pinky chargers, floating projectile lobbing caco-demon clones, but none of them exhibit the same threat. They appear in small numbers, go down quickly, and move so slowly that there's never a threat of being overrun before you can mow them down. It quickly became a source of humour for me that the heavy music stings would die down only seconds after starting up because you can kill the enemies in combat zones faster than the game can react to the fight breaking out. And this was on the 'hard' difficulty.It's a shame, because there's a lot of worth here from an artistic standpoint. But in drawing so much inspiration from a very specific and very recent series of games, Prodeus has surrendered any sense of individual identity it may have had, and it only invites unfavourable comparisons to gameplay elements that its mentors did better. In a vacuum it's a fun game. But unfortunately, beyond its fantastic visual style, it is in no way better than the now-cheaper games that it's sticking so close to.

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is basically the game 90s parents though DOOM was (in terms of violence).A solid retro FPS with a great arsenal, excellent levels, a level creator for potential infinite content.Weapon feedback is great, and all weapons in the arsenal remain useful throughout the game.Reloading is less common in arena style shooters for various reasons, but in Prodeus it's a mechanic to encourage switching weapons more often.For the most part, you will find weapons as you progress, but later weapons have to be purchased (with the 1.0 release).Exploration feels rewarding, with many secrets in each level rewarding currency for the upgrade store.Due to many enemies being melee based and the AI being fairly limited, combat is not that difficult until certain specialist enemies are intrdouced. But with an on-the fly difficulty slider, combat is only as easy/hard as you want it to be.What does blemish an otherwise great game is the strange checkpoint system.Dying has very small consequences in Prodeus. You can instantly revive at the last checkpoint, and the game does not reset any encounters - meaning no enemies

_childDocuments_.review: Best single player shooter since Doom 2016. Very much a Doom/Quake clone. Most enemies and weapons are nearly identical. If you play Doom on Ultraviolence I'd suggest the Very Hard difficulty. Pros:-Best level design out there, far surpassing any recent AAA games-Movement feels great and combat is more skillful and rewarding than most shooters. Easy to get in flow state. -Weapons and enemies feel great. Alternate fire modes are mostly great. -Beautiful environments-Excellent secrets. Platforming is limited to secrets and feels great-Enemies can accidentally kill each other-Love the weapon and enemy designs except for the giant dog (pinky demons) which look a bit dumbCons:-Music is pretty good but is overbearing. Often the battle music does not end properly when all enemies in an encounter are killed or just seems to continue throughout the entire level which is exhausting when the music is so intense and repetitive. Few standout tracks that I really love and want to listen to again. -Dismemberment is decent but not very impactful. It's mostly aesthetic and it's not nearly as good as in Brutal Doom where  there are a much wider variety of dismemberment behaviors such as enemies going down to their knees and bleeding out which you can then kick to explode. For example, in Prodeus an enemy with its arm blown off will still throw fireballs at you with the missing arm. -I use the shotgun alternate fire way too often. Don't much care for the damage over time mechanic and there seems to be very little downside to not just using alternate fire all of the time instead of primary fire-Melee is fun but I also never use it unless just messing around-Left a level by a secret exit which was a mistake because I then had to replay the entire level and leave by the normal exit to be able to progress in the game. Was confused and thought maybe I had reached the end of the early access section. The secret level that I went to was not a proper level but just some weapon armory that was disappointing. -Game is almost always very fair to the player. My worst experience was getting through a wave of 100 enemies only to be sniped by a newly introduced sniper enemy and having to redo the entire level/battle. Wait to introduce the snipers in the next level which is actually a sniper level.Wishlist:-Additional movement mechanics/gadgets such as grapple, jetpack, wallrun etc.-Better dismemberment/adding executing weakened enemies-Monster infighting-I like the pistol but never use it after having other weapons unless intentionally handicapping myself. If it had different ammo from the machine guns like an infinite energy recharge it could still be useful if you were out of ammo for other guns-Would have liked a quick melee kick-Would have liked thrown grenades as a weapon-Shotgun only damages a single enemy at a time so feels a bit weak. I'm guessing they are doing this to make the railgun feel more unique. Also guessing the super shotgun will have this ability. Still feels bad. -Could use more destroyable environment pieces

_childDocuments_.review: I am 32 years old.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: People say it's too easy, I don't agree, the game is not punishing, there's a difference; you'll die in the game, but you won't be as punished as in other titles. This isn't an accident, it happens deliberately to keep the flow of the game, basically you get points during the level that serve as respawn points, but your progress is always kept when you die, if you kill a bunch of enemies and got a bunch of keycards during your last live, this'll be saved after you respawn.There should definitely be ways to customize this system, mainly the ability to actually turn the respawn points into checkpoints that respawn the enemies and restart some of your progress -as it happens in other games-, but the devs chose to go the manual saving route, which I think is a really nice compromise. I personally love the way the system works, but I'm happy people who don't like it will get the choice to opt out of these respawn points.As for the actual game? The shooting feels amazing, everything just melts as you shoot it, every weapon is unique, having two types of fire modes which alter the weapons in some pretty significant ways; there's even some mobility upgrades that you can unlock which improve the pacing of the game even further, and make it so the game is a joy to replay. The game follows a similar system to that of the modern Doom games where the unlocks are universal, meaning, you can replay the game from the beginning whilst keeping all of your upgrades.The game is a bit short, but I don't mind with the replayability, what I do mind is that there aren't that many bosses, I think there's only one? With a couple of tough encounters here and there, I would have loved for the levels to have more visual variety as well, there are some levels that are themed around certain enemies, like "Marksman" which is a level where there's snipers that are hunting you as you play, and those levels really highlight how awesome it would've been for more variety in the levels and their concepts.Generall though, I really liked the game, it has a number of different difficulty options that are actually well balanced, very easy is really easy, normal is a very well balanced experience, and ultra hard is... well... ultra hard.I wholeheartedly recommend the game, specially considering the DLC is coming up in the next couple of months.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say that in a lot of ways Prodeus feels like the Doom 3 we never got, or the logical conclusion to Doom 2 if id hadn't completely shifted gears after going the Quake route. That basically means that if you love Doom 1 and 2 you'll love Prodeus, but if not I don't know why you'd be looking at the reviews for the game in the first place. That also means it's basically impossible to not compare it to Doom, or maybe something like Brutal Doom more specifically, but thankfully it stacks up very well.To get the best and the worst out the way right off the bat, the gunplay is really satisfying and the soundtrack is great. Really nice settings menu options too. The biggest and maybe only issue, at the time of writing, is that the game is short. What's currently in the campaign can be breezed through in about 5 hours, which is probably going to turn a lot of people off considering the base game cost. Prodeus makes up for this a bit by having a level creator to share user levels, so theoretically even if the devs just packed their bags and left, the userbase could continue to make content. There's definitely some excellent user made levels out there with their own scripted sequences and all, but the quality can obviously vary a lot and most of those content creators are probably only doing this as a hobby in their free time. For what is there in the campaign, I think on the whole level design is a lot nicer than Doom's occasionally confusing layouts, and there was virtually no point where I ever got lost in Prodeus because the levels flow very nicely. Hardly any monster closet bs either if you hate that sort of thing.Enemy visual design is really nice and the sprite work is gorgeous, but a lot of the enemies themselves are roughly all just Doom enemies in terms of behavior. Zombie shotgunners and minigunners, imps, lost souls, pinkies, cacos, and pain elementals are essentially all in Prodeus. One of the only really new things Prodeus does with them is introducing upgraded blue variants that belong to an opposing Prodean faction. I suppose if it isn't broke, don't fix it but I hope to see more new unique enemies down the line.For some closing remarks, the game probably banks on the easier side for the majority of difficulties, and I only ever started dying on the switch to Very Hard, so if you're used to shooters like this I'd probably say go for that first playthrough. I'd also recommend turning off the sprint in options so you can always run at max speed, does a lot to improve the pacing of the game and frees up the shift key for other keybinds.

I feel like there are too many weapons that the game doesn't know what to do with along with some downright stupid game design. For example there's pools of toxic waist that can harm you in a SHOP. The Shop is clearly designed to be a safe haven of sorts to test and buy weapons. (Another thing is buying upgrades rather than finding them in the game. I understand that the newer Doom games had a skill tree of sorts but I feel like it wasn't a necessary requirement. Like you could beat the game with as very few upgrades as possible. But in Prodeus it feels like you have to have all these upgrades to progress the game. _childDocuments_.review: Brutal and beautiful. This is what games like Doom looked and felt like in our heads when we played them as kids.So... what is Prodeus like? A big dose of classic Doom with a little bit of Quake 2, lots of gore, and lots and lots of heart. I'm not talking about the hearts ripped out, although there's plenty of that too.No filler level. Not a single one. That's a thing that not even series like the aforementioned Doom or Quake can tell about themselves. Every inch has been created by careful hands and you can feel that in every single pixel. So the level design is highly professional and polished to the extreme. It is a real pleasure to return to already played levels several times and find all the secrets.The visuals are carefully polished, with very clever, tricky solutions. The game is well optimized and the experience is highly customizable. Prodeus brings perhaps the best weapon arsenal of the last decade, at least as far as frantic, skill-based shooters are concerned.If I had to say something negative, I know that's not what these types of shooters are about, but I could have imagined a bit more story. A little narrative that's more than just a couple of hidden text entries. Even if only the beginning and the end of the game had some more substantial intro and outro to frame the game, that would have added a lot to the overall experience. But that's just nitpicking because it doesn't detract from the overall enjoyment of the game.Pro tip: Play on Hard difficulty or higher! That's where the game really shows itself. I've never felt so strong and so fragile at the same time which is blood pumping and rewarding.Overall, this game is clearly the product of years of blood and sweat and a love-child of a long-lasting affair. An almost perfect "boomer shooter" (perhaps the new dictionary example of it), and a real cult classic in the making. I can't wait for the next part, DLC, sequel, or whatever. Just bring it on!
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game but I had mixed feelings sometimes. Beginning is great, same as ending, but middle act seems off and makes game feel too long and boring. I also feel like getting rid of reloading in order to rely on weapon synergy more would be a better solution. Overall it's decent game, I had fun, I hope Unity won't drag it to a grave.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really great fps game that reminds me of doom, with a few things added from modern shooters. There is a reload, which I actually like. I always felt the idea that a gun not needed to reload wasn't a design choice, but back in the day games were so primitive they didn't make reload animations.But this is like Brutal Doom, and you can play with 3d models. The biggest stand out to me from old school shooters of the 90s and other "boomer shooter" games in early access, is that the level designs are so great. I usually get lost in these types of games. Everything on this game just flows so well that I am not spending an hour looking for where to go. Enemies seem to just spawn when you're in the right area and it seems pretty smooth to find where to go next, which imo helps the pacing of this game better than the 90s shooters it is emulating.Worth purchasing.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Man this is everything I want in an FPS. Hands down the best feeling shooter for years, and the best looking sprite based FPS ever. My only complaint is it's very hard to tell when you're being hit, or when you're low on health. I'll often just die seemingly out of the blue. But it's a small complaint. Buy this game now.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: You will not encounter a SINGLE bug playing prodeus. Gameplay is tight and very cool. Editor is awesome and the filters, the contests and all make it the best I have seen. The speed to load a custom map from the browser is 2 seconds. It's the best fps of this genre, made by pros who know what they want and deliver every single aspect of the game. The graphics are very good. Plus, the only thing I never liked in old games, and why I love quake, is I dislike sprites for the mobs. And they allow you to pick in the settings if you prefer sprites or 3d models for monsters. Nice. Oh BTW, the game isn't even released in gold. I don't even know how better it can become, but apparently it's what's gonna happen. What a wonderful time to be alive, my friends... Don't hesitate a second, and if you need to own only one retro fps, it's this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant game, absolutely love it and fully recommend it.I hate the term 'boomer shooter', mostly because I am old enough to have played the original FPS's and am most definitely not a boomer, only one of my parents is even a boomer! So I just prefer retro fps.But whatever you call it this is a perfect mix of old and new, this is the way your brain remembers DOOM, not the actual truth but better. The aesthetics, the gameplay and the audio are all perfect. This is in my opinion the best boomer shooter there is.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, listen.  It's Brutal Doom.  That's what Prodeus is.  It's Brutal Doom with a better engine and first-class support for community maps.  And it's friggin AWESOME.  Even in the Early Access state, it's smooth and balanced, and it's tons of fun.  The graphics take some getting used to, but they are gritty and cool.  The sounds are good, the music is incredible.  It's just a labor of love from a group of extremely talented up-and-comers.  If you like Doom at all, buy Prodeus.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is a thrill ride, but also a thoughtful one. The guns are satisfying and the blood is a rivers worth at least and yet with equally scary enemies that compliment the levels well it sounds out as a great FPS game. And with community supported levels within the game itself this one will keep you coming back for the thrills.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Comparisons have been drawn to the Brutal Doom mod, with which I must agree. Prodeus is essentially Doom with jumping, satisfying gore, and otherwise modernized presentation. There are a few points which drag the experience down a little, like checkpoints only saving position rather than progress (meaning enemies will not re-appear if you die), and the whole shop system being pretty forced. However, Prodeus is generally a great time and I often return to it for the simple joys of making demons go splat. The caching of models as billboarded sprites is very cool too and makes for a pretty unique style.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game from what I've played so far, and this is without any kind of nostalgic boner, I've never played the original DOOMs or Quake's.I really like the art style they went with this one, I find it very cool and satisfying. What you see in the videos here on the store page is actually what kind of experience you will be getting. To me at least, it's one of those games I could come back to again and again if I just want to kill time, relax a bit, whatever.The only tiny complaint I have so far is that you have to sign up to some other third party thingy if you want to create or download custom levels, It baffles me why they didn't use the steam workshop but whatever, it's really no big deal, that's the only complaint I can think of with this game so far. Everything else is absolutely perfect.I can understand if people on a tight budget may be concerned about the price, as I was too. You are getting a very good amount of content (with replayability) with the addition of custom maps. The game is in early access which means that more content is to come from the game as time goes on. If it helps, in the description of the Early Access section of this page, the developers say that they are working on multiplayer support, so you can invite your friends along and have a good time too further on down the road.Overall I'd say this game is most definitely worth a buy, and again if you're really concerned about purchasing this with a tight spending budget, maybe wait for a sale or find a better deal elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Forget about Doom(2016) and Doom Eternal. This is true doom successor and its even better than you think. Stunning effects, blood, gore, amazing weapons, sounds, badass soundtrack..its just awesome old-school game for boomer like me. I cant appreciate this enough.  BREATHTAKING GAME! Buy it. Its worth every cent! Great job! Please, just keep doing it like youre doing it now. Thats my only wish.

_childDocuments_.review: Good old fun "shoot everything that moves"! Very good music, suitable to the mood of each map, pumping up when the action heats up. It might even have a story, but I haven't bothered reading all the story pieces found in the maps (up to now).Runs on Linux just fine - just had to set it to use the latest Proton version, Triple-A fun for 1/3 of the cost!
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: This is what I wished Doom 2016/Eternal was. I'm only an hour in and so far I am blown away. As far I can tell - no gimmicky upgrade systems, not getting locked into rooms having to kill X until it opens, music is actual chugging guitars instead of pseudo-dubstep noise. Its over-the-top gore, break neck pace, hard difficulty feels balanced, FUN. I'm flush with ammo instead of only carrying 20 shells then be forced to do melee etc. You want to main a shotgun? Go ahead. It seems to not force you into a specific play-style or "tactic." I normally wouldn't write a review this early on but if you're on the fence and wish the old days were back instead of modern pretenders - here you go!
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!Buttery smooth and fluid movement with cathartic combat happens while a great sound track plays along.Campaign is a fair length and is fun both solo and in glorious co-op too.Creative and old school map design really speaks to me with this title.  Plus it has some replay value with the challenges and difficulty levels available.Workshop maps and campaigns are available if this wasn't enough for me.Great job Bounding Box, thanks!
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game; honestly this is what I was hoping for from Doom Eternal which was just all arenas, felt bad. This has big levels with the occasional arena but those are such a small part of the levels they're in. There's a good variety of weapons and they all feel really good to use in their own way. I wish there was more because it took me just 13 hours to 100% the game on Hard which was actually really easy; if you're experienced at games like Doom or Quake, bump it up to at least hard or go higher or you'll be bored. I died in only 1 level during my entire playthrough because I got overzealous and I really don't consider myself a super good FPS player.But yeah, game is great, hope to see more from them.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus was a fantastic experience. It plays exactly as advertised, and the progression keeps things fresh without getting too repetitive. Combat is fluid and fun. Great arsenal of weapons to use, while keeping some behind a progression system, which makes unlocking a new weapon very rewarding and satisfying to use. The game has a small group of enemies, but the way they are mixed up and how they are used in a level, make each encounter feel new and engaging. Fantastic level design. You can tell the levels were built with care and have been tested rigorously. Some levels gave me old Doom and Quake vibes, while others felt fresh and fun to traverse through. Finding secrets were super fun! I wish more of these types of Designers were available in the industry. It's sad that I have to rely on an indy game to experience great level design these days. Visually, Prodeus has some neat effects, and the blood and gore is top notch! Seeing a room or hallway painted red with the blood still dripping from the ceilings from a previous battle is a nice touch, and make you feel even more powerful as a player.Overall, I highly recommend Prodeus to anyone who enjoys retro FPS, or any FPS for that matter. It isn't much of a time sink, and can easily be finished over a weekend. My only real complaint with Prodeus was that the Campaign felt pretty short. It seems obvious the game was built with the intention to add in new Campaigns in the future, but until then, consuming user generated content seems to be the only option.

_childDocuments_.review: I received Prodeus as a gift from a fellow gamer.  Prodeus is a retro-style shooter using a modern game engine.  Visually enemies, items, and weapons are rendered as sprites, but this is done "on-the-fly" in the engine.  There is a toggle option to render enemies as models, which the sprites are drawn from, though this does not affect already present corpses, weapon models, or item models.The backstory is revealed through the game, what little story there is.  Focus is primarily on the gunplay, but I'm about halfway through and it's pretty standard fare for a Doom-style FPS - Humans were experimenting with something on an asteroid, something went wrong, and now everyone's dead or zombified except you, and you have to fight your way through to accomplish... something, but whatever that something is primarily involves fragging anything that moves.  You have fairly basic objectives - find key, open door, flip switch, exit the level.  Story info is provided by level descriptions before beginning a map and by radio logs found throughout the game - usually one per level though sometimes there is no log.Overall progression is displayed by a navigable world map.  You can replay levels to find missed items and secrets, restock on ammo and armor, or just for kicks.  Some levels are blocked by needing a certain number of runes to progress, and there are special "store" levels that lack enemies but give you access to additional weapons and abilities.  There are also special "trial" levels where the objective is to beat the level within a specific time in order to collect an ore reward at the end.  Once beaten you can also return to the level to restock on ammo specific to that map's weapon, as well as "turtle" the map for secrets that can't be collected effectively during the speedrun.  Map-based hazards include the standard fare - bubbling slime, lava, and falling into inescapable death pits.  Normal falling does not hurt you.Regarding items, you have the standard health, armor, and ammo picks for your weapons.  In addition there are runes, which tend to spawn a big fight when you pick them up as they are integrated into the story and are needed to progress past certain specific levels, and there is also ore, which is often but not always hidden behind a secret.  Ore is the game's "currency", which you use to purchase upgrades and new weapons in the game's Store levels.  Some weapons are found during gameplay, others must be purchased.  Once you reach the second store map you have the option to use ore to purchase ammunition, but I don't recommend this - ore is limited and can only be picked up once per level, and if you spend it on ammunition before acquiring new weapons you can lose the ability to buy those weapons later.  It's better to replay an easier level or a trial map to restock on ammo that way.  There is an automap to help you navigate through levels, and if you find an automap item on a level it will reveal the entire level, though not necessarily every secret area as some don't show on the map at all.Weapons vary from your bare fists to pistols, a minigun, a plasma rifle, a railgun-like weapon, rockets, grenades, and a quad-barreled super-shotgun that even the Doom Slayer would be jealous of.  Every weapon has some kind of secondary function that alters how the weapon works or just unleashes hell in a single shot.  There are movement upgrades you can acquire such as double-jump and a dash module.  Both are very helpful so you will want these as soon as possible.  So far every weapon has a niche and even the lowly pistol is useful later in the game to pick off distant enemies or down the stray zombie.Speaking of zombies, the enemies come in three varieties.  There's zombified humans, which either wander slowly and try to smack you, shotgunners that take a moment to shoot but will move more quickly toward you, a minigun-toting tank of a zombie, and snipers that use the Arc-rail weapon.  The first two are annoying, the last two are very dangerous.  There's also the odd hazard-suited zombie that blows up into an acid puddle when shot.  Protip- don't step in it.  There's the "Chaos" - basically the game's hell spawn, which range form imp-like "fiends" that throw fireballs, floating "Bloaters" that spit a lava projectile, crawling baddies that do the same, flying "skull-fish" that fly at you and explode on impact, a minotaur-like charging "demon" - see the parallels with Doom yet?  There's also a few more powerful monsters.  Then there's the Prodeans.  These are fairly rare, but have the ability to "possess" some of the Chaos monsters and control them, altering their appearance and attacks.  Prodeans by themselves are extremely dangerous as well.  Who the Chaos and Prodeans are is not revealed immediately in the game, so you'll get the backstory on where they came from as you play.  If you do happen to die there are Nexus Points scattered throughout the maps that act as checkpoints.  Whichever one you have touched last will be your respawn location.  You'll have the option to respawn at a Nexus Point or restart the level from scratch if you die.Pros:  Boomer shooter in a modern engine with a huge arsenal, great bestiary, excellent gameplay and level design.Cons:  The "model-to-sprite" visuals might be jarring to some newer gamers that haven't played many sprite-based shooters.  Some maps do block your return path after a point so you will have to replay levels to get missed secrets.If you like the original Doom combined with a bit of Doom '16 you will definitely want this game.  There's plenty of action, gore, secrets to find, and badass weaponry to blow stuff to kingdom come and back.  There's so much good and really not many negatives.

_childDocuments_.review: So, Prodeus. I really, really wanted to like it. It's a retro FPS, the weapons are sprites instead of models, and a famous DooM PWAD creator (Xaser Acheron) was a part of the team. By all accounts I should have loved it, but I didn't. Far from it.The level design was good to great. I was never lost and maps had intuitive interconnectivity that prevented backtracking. There were a few gimmick levels that were a lot of fun, and the sniper tower map is probably the highlight of the entire game. The weapons are a mixed bag, with shining examples on either extreme. The basic pistol and shotgun feel fantastic and I probably gimped myself for the first half of the game because I had a tough time switching to other guns. The plasma rifle is far and away the best looking, feeling, and most useful gun in your arsenal. The animated sprite gives it character, it evokes the Blood tesla cannon when you shoot it (this is a very good thing), and it's the only weapon half decent at stunlocking things. The super shotgun, on the other hand, is a freaking travesty. It's a QUADBARREL shotgun that feels both weaker and less satisfying than its single-barrel counterpart. The mind boggles. The single shot rocket launcher is fine; remote det feels good. There's also an ice melting weapon near the end of the game that I have nothing to say about other than it reminded me of the alien swarm gun from Half Life 1.I turned the OST off pretty quick. A mix of it being standard boomer shooter fare and me preferring to listen to death metal whenever I play an FPS at this point.My biggest gripe is that Prodeus more than overstays its welcome. Steam has me at just under 10 hours for a full playthrough. That's with minimal secret hunting and not replaying any levels outside of the 90 second weapon trial things (they're fun). There's a Super Mario overworld map and tbh if the game was just the first map I think it would have been enough. It's not though, and there's 2 more (admittedly shorter) maps after the first. I want to say there's around 20 levels. It wouldn't be too many if the first 5 or so were bite-sized experiences, but the game very quickly ramps up to 100+ enemies per map that regularly take (or took me) 20+ minutes to clear. FPS of this kin, in my mind, should have levels no longer than 10 minutes outside of set pieces or finales. 4-6 hours would have been much more appropriate. Prodeus is fine. It's got some high highs and equally low lows. I would happily recommend it as someone's first retro FPS, but if you have any familiarity with the subgenre's tendencies I would say skip it or wait for a good sale (33% off or more).

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I still love the game and have been waiting forever for 1.0 release. It brought a lot of good but also changed some things that I don't personally like.I've played through the campaign fully probably about half a dozen times in the past, before 1.0.I've just finished a play through on ultra hard, so I feel some of my opinions on some of the weapons and level balance are probably skewed based on that.The first things about the update that struck me were the Ore collectibles and the shop. I wasn't sure what to think about it, the double jump and dash being locked and labeled "Tier 2" made me think they would be available at a later shop. I abstained from buying the Plasma Rifle or Super Shotgun because I assumed they would still be available in the levels they were before.I couldn't remember exactly what levels you first got those guns in, but by the time I reached Meltdown I felt like I should have had the Plasma Rifle.Up until that point I had also been experiencing that quite a lot of the secrets I remembered were changed ever so slightly to require the double jump, which was still locked at "Tier 2", and that felt kind of bad to me.I reached the third shop and still the movement upgrades were locked so I knew something was up.I really don't like the shop. It never really felt exciting to have to comb through levels for Ore to have enough to buy the upgrades and new weapons rather than them being deliberately placed, in each next level or so, at good spots for you to try out your new toy.That was my biggest issue with the update, the rest below are more scattered thoughts and some disgruntles.For the new weapons:The Auto Shotgun is weird to me. The animations and sounds feel a little anemic, I swear the sound is literally just the normal shotgun firing sound. I feel like the recoil should be pushing back into your shoulder with each shot, not up which just looks kind of goofy as you flail it around on full-auto. The alternate fire is cool in concept, but I never found a spot where I would want to use it and even when I tried it out, it felt like it did so little damage for 4 shells a shot. Maybe I was using it wrong idk. Also I never found myself going for either of the other shotguns once I had it, it really just outclassed them I guess.The Swarmer is pretty fun, but I never felt like I needed the Rocket Launcher after I obtained the Swarmer, so that sucks. It occurred to me as I wrote this that I had never once used the alt fire for it, so I don't really have an opinion on it.The Mammonth is fun, but alike the Auto Shotgun it sounds a little anemic with some of the shots making nearly no noise. The alternate fire is basically unusable on anything further than barrel-stuffing territory with how much it covers your screen.The Caster is still a joke.Are the Plexus and Void Caster just not in the campaign at all or did I somehow miss them? If they really aren't, why????Most of the Prodeus enemies (the blue ones) still feel way over-tuned on health and projectile tracking, and are painful to try to even see through all their particle effects surrounding them that are the exact same colors as they are.The level progression difficulty of the last stretch of levels is all over the place, starting with Hexarchy which is still ridiculously difficult. And then the immediate level after, Trench, is so easy in comparison.The last room of Space Station is way too cramped to have a Slayer in there, I mean come on.On Aftermath, the big room with the immediate second Cryomancer just throws an absolutely unnecessary number of Prodeus enemies at you along with a Harbinger at the same time, it's really too much.The last level was very fun and felt well balanced to me, thank you for that.Slayers are still not fun to me, even with double jump and dash their enormous homing projectiles are ridiculous.I personally don't have much issue with the checkpoint system, yes it's kind of weird for this type of game but there's a "no death" accolade for each level that works well enough as encouragement to not die.Thanks for this amazing game guys, sincerely.

_childDocuments_.review: Bloodier even than the game "Blood" (1998), this is a FPS fan's dream come true that's bound to quench any bloodthirst. If there weren't already games called "Wet" (2009) and "Blood," I'd suggest a name change, because this is as close to a bloodbath I want to be in, with everything being coated, especially your guns---I love it.For gameplay, "Prodeus" combines all the best qualities from classics "DOOM" and "Quake" then adds the influence of a mod like "Brutal DOOM" and the "DOOM" (2016) remake that turn the experience up to 11. Gradually unlocking double-jump, dash, etc keeps the player coming back to find all the secrets or rank high on the leaderboards. I think the game is the best neo-boomer shooter I've played, better than "Dusk" (2018), "Ion Fury" (2019) and even "Nightmare Reaper" (2019). It's also the best-looking Unity game I've come across, with its colors and aesthetic being quite mesmerizing on an OLED panel. The game's design stumbles on some simple things like the UI and HUD which I think are a little goofy looking. The automap threw me for a loop as I didn't understand you're supposed to hit tab to open, then hold tab to look and move around with the mouse. These controls could be easily rectified, methinks, even if it has to copy how the automap works in "DOOM" 2016. Other things would be the flashing enemies make me want to glorykill them, or use a quick melee that doesn't seem to exist like say the chainsaw in the remake of DOOM. The fists are more akin to Lo Wang's in "Shadow Warrior" where they're a discrete weapon than a supplement.If you want arcade-like action at a low price with terrific gameplay and visuals, this is a solid value.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Competent Quake-style shooter. It doesn't do anything new, but it does it competently.  Sprite design is overall well-done, but I genuinely prefer the models for their readability (and I'm glad they include both options.). Levels are generally well-designed, but I think the aesthetic is a little too samey across the game, with only a few of the last levels really breaking through into their own. And I feel like quite a few of the weapons have very similar use cases or only exist until you get a better option.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Close your eyes and think. Come up with a number: how many bullets does this game have? Wrong. 6 trillion. How cool is the shotgun? Very? Wrong. It's one of the most satisfying boomer shooter shotguns out there but even this sentence is wrong because they made an even cooler Super Shotgun that is also in the game.  How much blood do you think is in the game? Wrong again. They put 35 Shining Elevator Scene's worth of blood in this game. How much heavy metal is in the game's soundtrack? Some? A lot? No. Exactly one Andrew Hulshult's worth.  I'm going to dock the game one point because the weapons need to be reloaded.  Reloading is for weak-willed people who can't commit to anything in life, let alone holding down left-click.  11/10

_childDocuments_.review: Although this game is pretty much like many games were during the 90's, Doom Clones, this game came out in 2020 when the whole "Doom Clone" thing went out of fashion and much like the reboot Doom, it's a formula that is still very enjoyable and worth playing and is a breather from the other FPS games that feature "Realism" when all we want to do is kill things and use big guns to do it with.I'd say this game has that down pretty well
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Quite good so far and has a lot of potential still. It's a little too much like Doom but it's certainly polished. Hopefully as it goes further into early access, it carves out more of its own identity gameplay wise and has improved balance because at this point I feel it's somewhat too easy. Still, the levels included are great, the creation tools are great and there's a lot of great levels online to keep you busy.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Great potential for a new golden standard in retro boomer shooters. The visual style is very distinctive and the gameplay is very reminiscent of Brutal Doom. The game is still in early access, so I can't outright recommend buying it or give it a full review, but the cover price is very fair and even at its current state the game has a lot of content and fun to be had for fans of retro FPS'es.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Even in it's current incomplete state of Early Access, Prodeus is one of the finest examples of the genre, standing tall amidst the retro FPS revival games a la Ion Maiden, Dusk, and mods like Brutal Doom. The movement is brisk and responsive, the weapons are tactile and purposeful, the levels are complex and varied without feeling like a labyrinth of back-tracking time waste. Top to bottom this game is a blast and worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: As a 90s kid who grew up on Doom, Duke, Heretic, Quake, etc., and is still a huge fan of those classic shooters, I've really been eating up all these new retro-style FPS games coming out lately. I've had a ton of fun with Dusk, Amid Evil, and Ion Fury already, and those are some of my favorite games of the past few years. And now there's this... Prodeus. Despite just recently coming out into early access and still having a while before full release, I was blown away and sucked into this game immediately. Doom is probably still my favorite game of all time, and though I played and enjoyed the newest Doom games from Id, Prodeus actually feels to me like the best "new Doom game" yet, despite not actually being Doom. I love everything about the look and feel, the gameplay, the presentation, the music, etc. so far. The 2D sprites with MANY more angles than any of the classic 90s FPS games had (including VERTICAL angles so the sprite looks different even when looking down on them from above!) was really cool and impressive to me. I'm happy to support this during development, and look forward to what else will be added.

There are pads that refill your ammo though, but I'd rather have a pad that refills armor and life.So... today I finally beat it, and I have to admit the endfight had me reduce the difficulty to the lowest difficulty, because a million hellspawn at once attack you and most of them got shields. _childDocuments_.review: Top notch first person shooter, a perfect marriage of original Doom and Doom 2016 mechanics and feel. There's not enough good things I can say about this game; gameplay is tight and responsive, enemies are plentiful and uniquely challenging, and you are given a pretty robust arsenal to take it all on. All the weapons feel great and are suitably punchy, even down to the starting pistol. The soundtrack kicks ass, tracks are dynamic and will swell during intense moments in gameplay for a truly pulse pounding experience. The game is also fairly long for a shooter, I just finished at around the 12 hour mark and I missed a lot of secrets. I will say if you are a veteran of the genre you may want to start off on Hard mode for a suitable challenge. While not a knock towards the game by any means, I was surprised to find the ease of normal mode given the kind of shooter Prodeus is. With that I will give this a high recommendation, it was an absolute blast to experience.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr If you like Doom, Timesplitters, and moving very fast then you'll love this. Early access campaign took me about 2-3 hours to get through but there's a lot of replayability here to master the levels and there are the community maps that are a decent challenge. I enjoy using the plasma rifle alt-fire and shooting a tanky enemy from round a corner which feels like a pro gamer move when you pull it off for the first time. Weapon switching is a bit unintuitive but time does stop completely when you have the weapon switch UI open. The minigun has too much spread to be useful. There's melee and a pistol that you're gonna use for the first five minutes only, of course.The assault rifles are dual-wield and each one seems to fire from the same magazine. OK. I think it's more accurate if you fire just one of them, but you can get higher DPS effectively at close range by firing both. I don't like the manual reloading, which feels like a bit of a chore in a game where you have so many weapons and I did find that by the end of the early access campaign I had so much plasma and chaos ammo left simply because early game had taught me how to use the rocket launcher, regular shotgun and rifles to take down 99% of the enemies effectively.When you die you respawn at a checkpoint instead of loading a save. Enemies are not respawned but you will increment your death counter on the post level results screen. This is fine and adds to the aforementioned replayability component.The sprite work here is phenomenal. You can play with 3D models instead of sprites if you wish but you'd be missing out on Prodeus accounting for your vertical position so you don't get that cardboard cutout effect that something like GZDoom has. It's a pretty unique way of doing sprites that I think works very well.The music sets the atmosphere very well but doesn't punctuate the action quite like that in something like Doom Eternal and there's a distinct lack of audio cues from the player character, which can make it easy to lose track of when you're getting wrecked.The Timesplitters comparison comes from that when you collect a rune, slightly tankier blue versions of the regular enemies spawn.There were a few times when I got stuck and had to use the automap which is a little clunky to navigate but thankfully the maps in the campaign flow together really well most of the time.Overall I am enjoying Prodeus and I look forward to the developers expanding the campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, though a lot of little things give me mixed feelings about it. The main one by far is performance. This is a retro-styled shooter with a lot of added visual flairs and details, on Unity. That combined means it'll definitely chug in some spots on systems that other "boomer shooters" run fine on, like mine.The levels themselves are well-designed and I basically never found myself getting lost in them. Many of them have little touches and setpieces that made them quite impressive, especially some of the levels in the latter half. Movement and basic flow of gameplay feels good for the most part, though there are a few intermittent hiccups that I'll bring up below. As for the weapons, they all do their job. Again a few things to grumble about, but just about all of them are perfectly usable.Enemies tend to be consistently gray, red, or blue. Thankfully they did crib some other notes from Doom on top of many of the core enemies filling the same niches, so they maintain distinct enough silhouettes that you can prioritize. There's a lanky gray blob in the distance, that's an imp. There's a thicc gray blob, that's a chaingunner. There's some gray and a bit of light blue, that's your worst nightmare. The only times this really breaks down are with basic zombies vs shotgunners, and with the cacodemons vs pain elementals. If it's nothing but basic zombies you're free to square up and put on your best Kenshiro impression, but shotgunners will require you to actually think a bit unless you're willing to tolerate getting plinked at. A caco-like is best answered with a rocket or grenade to the face, but the pain elementals are tanky enough to require more than one, and the fire rate for both is slow enough that you risk having a lost soul intercept your next shot.So for weapons, they all work, but some of them feel redundant or less consistent. The shotgun and auto shotgun are good examples. The charged altfire of the regular shotgun is not an example as it tightens the spread to slug levels, but the basic shot is underwhelming. The super shotgun seems to outdamage both even with single-barrel shots, in theory this is balanced by the others having tighter spread. In practice, it's only ever worth using the basic shotty's charged shot, and the auto shotgun is wasteful to use at all. 90% of the time it's better to just charge in and shove the super shotgun in your target's face. Almost every weapon is still usable, just most of them are outclassed by another weapon outside of situational uses. Except the blob gun, it seems to be nothing but a last-minute weapon for puzzles in a single level, the puddles it leaves don't deal anywhere near enough damage to be worth using.As for the hiccups I mentioned, this is a game that encourages you to stay on the move a lot and constantly unload into enemies, so everything that disrupts that momentum stands out. The only cases I'm reasonably sure were intentional was how the dash causes your momentum to reset briefly right afterward (annoying, but not hard to get used to), and the minigun doing that "you don't get any shots until it's finished winding up to full" thing that 90% of video game miniguns do that's always a pet peeve of mine. Early on you can rely on the standard cliche of the altfire pre-revving it up for you, and became one of my mainstay weapons despite that flaw, but later on the fact that having it active cripples your movement speed makes it far too much of a pain to rely on.The other hiccups are stuff I suspect are tied more to performance, I'm willing to bet people with actual graphics cards won't run afoul of, but they're something to watch out for if your PC is somewhere on the potato end of the spectrum. Melee took some getting used to initially, as the attack animation for the basic punch has some delays to it that make it feel slow and plodding in a way that messes with timing when you're trying to backpedal from a punch parade of zeds. Holding down fire and altfire steps up the fire rate to a degree that makes this a complete non-issue. The SMG and plasma rifle have a bit of input delay that requires the fire button to be held before that first shot will occur, so if your system chugs firing in short bursts is not an option. Lastly, reloading is prone to not triggering unless whatever firing animations are going on have had time to settle down and tuck themselves into bed. Doesn't affect switching weapons at least, good in a game that has a lot of then.Sound design is good and fairly distinct, and the music is by everyone's go-to retro shooter expert Andrew Hulshult. Does a good job overall. Levels have a basic ambient track, a low-intensity combat track, and a higher-intensity one. For the first couple levels the ambient track felt a bit repetitive, but soon all of the tracks settled into being tolerable at worst, usually far better. By the latter half of it even the basic ambient tracks were beyond merely "okay" and are damn good in their own right. The game seems to have a poor sense of timing as to just when to take things up or down a notch, though. You might have the full-intensity track ramp up for one or two enemies that will be erased from existence in under five seconds, the intense battle music playing for half a minute before it notices you've already murdered everything, etc.Levels are laid out on a SMB3-esque grid, with optional detours and shops to buy upgrades. The currency for these upgrades are pickups obtained throughout the regular levels. Even if you're bad about secret-hunting you'll find enough of them to grab every upgrade in the shop halfway through the campaign, unless you do something idiotic like blow it all on ammo refills. That does demonstrate a flaw however. If you don't intentionally screw yourself over you'll reach a point where you have nothing left worth buying, when levels keep coming with decent amounts of ore to collect. You could buy ammo refills sure. But the weapons you unlock? Their pickups give you ammo, and respawn every time you enter. Even if ammo wasn't easy to stay on top of, you can stock up on every ammo type except basic bullets, completely for free. Even more amusing, during one part of the campaign map, long after you should have everything important, they place a visit to the shop map in your path. You have to visit it, admire the pretty snow theme it now has, then turn around and hit the exit switch to be able to continue onward. All other shop maps are in offshoots like the challenge maps.As for the checkpoint system? In basically any other shooter, a checkpoint system is the bane of my existence. This game avoids the usual pitfall by having it be completely free respawns. There is zero penalty for dying, whatever you killed between checkpoints and any other level progress remains intact. The end-of-level stats do tally up your death total, but it's basically reddit karma. The only time the checkpoint system is really a nuisance is if you need to save and quit in the middle of a level. This is a problem in a game where levels can actually be pretty long affairs.Despite things that might annoy some players, and some hiccups that will definitely trip you up if your PC's performance isn't that great, it's still playable even if you suffer from a terminal case of integrated graphics like I do. Wait for it to go on sale if you're likely to be especially bugged by any of the problems I've brought up, otherwise it's in a fitting price range like other competently-made boomer shooters. It's not a super long campaign, but does come with custom level support, there are already countless finely-crafted CBT dungeons out there already. Given the game menu I would bet that more official levels may be added in the future, but no way to be sure of that.Moral of the story: I miss the days when you could find cheap prebuilts with actual graphics cards. :<

_childDocuments_.review: Run fast, shoot hard, bathe in the blood of your enemies. This is the dreamscape of modern oldschool shooters. There is not one element of this game that isn't standout and doesn't fit well. I am absolutely floored by the quality in this game. The in game leader boards and built in community content tools give this game the potential for as much infinite replayability as Doom has, calling absolutely true to half of the core DNA in this game, the rest of it being based heavily on Quake with it's atmosphere, and a lot of the enemy sprite and model design finding a beautiful fusion between Doom, Quake, Hexen with a little sprinkle of Sci-Fi design in there, mostly in the gunner grunts. Those mobs specifically remind me of killzone quite a bit. I only wish that if, when you've got models over sprites selected in the options that your characters gun and hands also changed to a model, but that is the only ultra nitpicky bit I can think of. I always opt for spirites though, grew up on Doom, hard to dodge that aesthetic. The models look great if you set up the old school Pixel/Scanline/CRT filters though! Great middle ground. The sprites look so good and have so many viewing angles covered they feel like models with a pixel filter on them anyway.So so pleased with the quality in this game. Between this, Ion Fury, Project Warlock and every oldschool shooter New Blood has published plus the multitude I haven't played yet, we have truly hit a massive renaissance for this style of game, and I'm so glad I'm alive to see it, this game is the peak of it so far. 20/10 I've replayed the second level 5 times just to crack top 3 on the timer leader board. Can't wait to see what I can do with the MIDI soundrtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is perfection!!I have been a huge fan of every Doom game that has released. This game deserves to be ranked within the doom games!  It is very fast paced; especially when you are in arenas. It has the feeling of Doom 1 & 2 but plays like Doom 2016 & Eternal. The variety of weapons this game has is insane and fun to play around with all of them. I have only play for ~2 hours so far and I am loving every minute of it.The gore in this game is fantastic and makes killing enemies even more satisfying! I cannot recommend this game enough! BUY IT!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is insanely good. Best of the boomer shooters by a wide margin, including anything by new blood. The level designs are perfect.. tight and compact instead of sparse and sprawling. Reminds me of sycthe.wad from Doom. This is the most fun I've had in an old school shooter since Brutal Doom. Looks like this game will provide a nice and updated backbone for future mods which is awesome. So much potential sitting right here and I'm excited for the future development of this game and hopefully franchise. If you think that Doom 2016 and Doom Eternal were a bit bloated and not really a true successor to Doom 1/2, you will love this one.

_childDocuments_.review: What if doom had better effects and modern hardware? What comes out is a really cool visual style, it invokes the old doom style and game play but adds a layer of sheen over it not capable of those old machines. The gameplay is fun and approachable, but doesn't overstay its welcome for too long. Solid shooting, if not particularly challenging at medium difficulty.  It has lots of secrets, gun unlocks, and more depth if you want it. I had my fill after blasting through the campaign at about 8-10 hours or so.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for people who play brutal doom on ultra violence and spam the resurrect command on death. The primary difficulty comes not from death, but from ammo, armor, health management and enemy prioritization. The player has the option to respawn at "nexus" points with the enemy count remaining unchanged. The score at the end and your position on the leaderboard will tally your score. The goal is to maintain your resources in order to beat the game with the least amount of deaths.The game works well on Steam Deck at 600p with fsr enabled. The campaign is short at around 10 hours but the primary method of play is actually the map workshop. The onscreen keyboard needs to be invoked when using some parts of the menu.The developers are the same ones that made the legendary Eviternity Megawad for doom and their primary goal was to create a mapmaking platform. I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Guys...this game is beautiful. The impact of the weapons is perfect. The sprite work is amazing. The soundtrack ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BANGS. But please, PLEASE fix the checkpoint system. As it is now, dying just sets you back a few steps and refills your health with all of your progress through the level intact, including enemies defeated. _childDocuments_.review: There is some incredible effort behind this. The level editor is probably the real star of the show here. The early access campaign levels and trials are a fine tuned demonstration of what their engine and editor are capable of. The levels are incredibly detailed and the scripted events are awesome and surprising. The art style and hulshult (music) are spot on. Some aspects are familiar (guns, enemies), but their patterns and attacks are retooled just enough to be recognizable and fresh.There are probably some balance issues, and I didn't play the game in try-hard mode. For my first run through I was mostly interested in the level design as a primer for what the editor was capable of, not to stress test the combat.I would like the option to turn the blood and gore up or down, just a qol thing.Not a huge fan of the weapon menu, and it seems like there will end up being more weapons that my current weapon binding strategy will allow for.

_childDocuments_.review: It's great if you love boomer shooters. Crank it up to Hard difficulty for your first play-through if you are familiar with the old-school stuff or current boomer shooters as anything lower seems to be a bit on the easy side but there is a wide variety of difficulty levels so it should suit everyone. The overworld map and sprites are cool, but did you know you can turn on 3D models for the enemies? Love the detail in these models. _childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Phew - what an oddly middling gameI  like to give a neutral option, but I can't.It feels harsh to give this the humb down, but advising someone to spend 25 bucks on this feels worse...The gameplay is actually okay and fun, as far as someone like me - who's uninitiated in the likes of o.g. Doom & Quake - can tell. The hit feedback is good, the animations are nice, sound is meaty - as is the sprite work. You can make an absolute mess of any room, given the amount of gore and viscera. It gets to the point where the blood spray can obscure a bit  much of the screen space, but it's not a huge issue.The weapons are all 'classics' but they're made well, handle well and have useful firemodes - even the pistol & basic shotgun can stay relevant in the lategame.Level design is actually really cool in  places, both visually as well as mechanically - especially some of the midgame & later levels are dynamic and drastically change during play - a lot of the levels are very unremarkable though.So I do feel the campaign is a bit short? Uneventful maybe?Better than too long I guess - Doom'16 & Eternal  outstayed their welcome, but this one just ends very suddenly and unseemly after a level that's just a single room survival fight. There's only one or two standout moments, but they don't last -  and they're are all more "level being pretty" and not "combat is amazing" moments.I'm not huge on the effortless respawn system either - the game doesn't employ checkpoints to reset you to, it just revives you - progress intact - and the latest respawn point.It's not a  dealbreaker for me - but it is incredibly odd that it's not an option, especially since the game has like 7 difficulty modes and it's been seemingly a sticking point for the community.The enemies / encounters are kinda lackluster - there's not that many types, with all the usual generic & basic chaff  - basic zombie, shotgun trooper, 'fat' gatling gunner, imp, sniper, lost soul, pinky demon, cacodemon, pain elemental, explody boi + one or two recurring 'minibosses'). The entire Prodeus faction are basically almost all palette- & vfx-swapped Chaos enemies.Combat - much like later D:Eternal fights - can kinda grow formulaic in the sense that they will spawn the same enemy arrangements every fight over and over.Early on the enemies behave noticeably static, though that changes in time with the midgame and later levels. The enemies also possess almost supernatural tracking abilities - once they have you on aggro, they'll pre-aim shots through & past walls, and have perfect aim correction. Circle strafing and moving around fast will NOT saveguard you from projectiles in this, which is an undue pain in many of the later & more cluttered fights.The visuals are mostly really cool, but I feel like the HUD craps all over the faux retro look of the actual game. The helmet bezel / vignette are dumb as ever & it all looks a bit too smooth, round and HD for the rest of the game.The state of the usermade content is kinda dire. The way it's handled in the ingame menu means it's shared between platforms, which is neat, but the steam workshop has like a hundred percent more browsing- & comfort functions.And while there's a bunch of cool individual levels, there's not very much in terms of cohesive content. There's only like 4 or 5 'completed' usermade campaigns TOTAL, which are either undercooked or just survival fight arrangements.So have fun digging through individual maps one at a time, playing it for 2 minutes and then go through the rigorous joy of navigating the weirdly cluttered menus all over again.It's a ~9 hour & kinda medium campaign, but the bones on this are solid. - so in a sale it might be worth it to some.For 25 bucks I would've felt a bit underwhelmed - but it sure as hell beats Dusk in my book, that I'm confident about.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm old enough to remember going to the mall and buying a shareware version of wolfenstein. It came on a floppy, and ran on my parent's i386 Packard Bell windows 3.1 desktop. I'm old enough to remember when you could set your modem up in receive mode and have your friends dial-in and play. That is, if you had friends.I remember when Quake was released and you could find games via Gamespy, joining said games and getting a massive 3 frames per second while some jackass just spawn camped you all day.I remember buying a big-ass book with *TWO* "cd-rom"'s called "The Doom Hacker's Guide", a book where I learned that there is a massive difference between bad and good level-design. I'm not a retro-game-loving person, but I am a fan of well designed games. And this game fits that model. If you don't love this game then you're a gimboid and should be banned from gaming.ONE LAST THING: FOR THE LOVE OF GOD, ADD A FREAKING EXIT BUTTON MENU ITEM! You have to cycle through 50 menus and load screens to simply exit.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played an hour so far and I can say for sure this game is excellent.  It's basically oldschool Doom and Quake put together.The level design is very similar to both games, where you're hopping around through interconnected areas with lots of switches and keys.  The enemies are *very* similar, with analogues to things like the shotgunners, imps, pinkies, etc.  The visual design is reminiscent of the old games too, with weapons and enemies presented as sprites with some really neat lighting/effects playing off them.  You can choose to have 3D models instead, as well as apply some postprocessing effects to make it like an older monitor, and for once I found myself actually using them. The gameplay is simple and straightforward, move forward gunning down everything that moves, get some keycards now and then, and get to the end of the level, no messing around with scripted events/cutscenes/etc.  It's perfect for jumping into and playing in bursts.  And for an early access game it is very well developed, honestly I wouldn't be able to tell if I'd just been handed the game without knowing.If you're a fan of older shooters this is great, and early access means more is coming, so yeah I'd say go ahead and grab this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: After four hours, I know enough about this game to know a few truths:Truth 1: I will keep playing it;Truth 2: This game was made with love and an attention to detail.It is remarkably smooth, satisfyingly fast, and screams of the shooters we all grew up playing. Don't sleep on this one--it is worth supporting the developers and enjoying all it has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Easiest way to explain this is that its a genuinely heartfelt love letter to doom fans both old and new. You want simple parkour and kill done! You want good weapons in less than 3 levels done! You want secrets done! You want gore done! You want similar enemies to doom done!Beyond that the graphics style used is reminiscent of doom 64 but with modern tweaks of course, also considering its early access I found no bugs either which was impressive. I look forward to seeing where the Dev's will go with this in the future. Also as far as difficulty goes there's something for everyone with many difficulty settings both easier and harder with medium being pleasantly entertaining. The campaign hasn't got any real story but its no frills fun if you don't want to bother with the online segment however it is a bit short so i hope they add to it in the future. Lastly the weapons feel like they might be hit scan as the shotguns got insane range for a scatter gun but otherwise no complaints. in short its a great game =)

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Doom 4 but without the influence of Brutal Doom. This will be the game.Instead of looking at the past, they would imagine if only Doom 4 is released on time.The influence is obvious. It's like the Doom 3 developers listened to the feedback and thus making the game world, while still pretty dark, it's very visible in proper brightness as well as glowing enemies.The enemies are also dominated with austere gray with a little orange and some have blue energy streaks.There is also the fact that a map editor is there and perfectly accessible.My only complain is that how the ammo clip and pool is too small, resulting in pace breaks where reload is often necessary, even if upgrade is unnecessary. Perhaps double the ammo clip and pool?That and some weapons (dual SMG and minigun) are nigh-worthless due to insane recoil, and the pistol burst, while satisfying, only have like 3 bursts before reload while 15, instead of 10, would be a better clip size, suiting the real life Beretta (which is mock-up into Robocop's iconic burst firing Auto 9)Palette swap for enemies might also be considered so it doesn't feel like you're fighting the same enemies over and over again.Map editor is fun but to incentivise playing and making map there should be rewards, like in Snapmap, such as weapon skin. Make it also community can contribute to custom models!Last but no least, with the advent of AI scaling, a separate DLC might be available that, using AI upscaler, upsize all textures instead of emulating low poly 90s to early 2000s shooters.
