_childDocuments_.review: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Very responsive developers who clearly care about their output. I buy just about every boomer shooter that hits Steam and Prodeus is set apart by its attempts to bring its own identity to the genre, as opposed to just imitating the basics of games like Quake without really expanding on the formula. The game features modernised mechanics like ADS and the ability to headshot enemies, whilst the art style attempts to bridge classic DOOM's sprite based visuals with modern rendering techniques, and higher poly environments with higher quality sprite based textures, and enemies/weapons that consist entirely of sprites rendered from models. Its clear the game took inspiration from DOOM 2016, and in its own unique way, Prodeus feels like a more faithful tribute to that games visceral brutality and grittier sci-fi/demonic themes than DOOM Eternal. The levels and the art have clearly had great thought and care put into their execution, although I do recommend enabling models in the settings to fix some sprite interpolation issues with corpses and barrels. The only thing that this game is missing right now is the same thing that every boomer shooter released in EA the past three years seems to be missing:  That, and full modding support. My understanding is the devs plan to facilitate these things, and the game has already released in EA with a very competent level editor reminiscent of TrenchBroom.If the devs can keep up the momentum and deliver on the above, this game will blow competitors like Wrath: Aeon of Ruin out of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ water. Definitely worth keeping an eye on at least.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: After attempting to play Doom Eternal, I found that it had far too much *stuff*. It was a toy box with so many toys my brain couldn't handle it. With like six different buttons all for doing damage to the thing in front of you, as well as a whole arsenal of kickass weapons, it always felt like I was being suboptimal.Prodeus brings us back to the basics. No special powers, just a wicked arsenal of guns that feel amazing. I'm tempted to call Prodeus simple, but *refined* is the correct word. Everything works together perfectly. The graphics are so compelling. Mixing 2D spritework with 3D environements and all the modern lighting technology is just so cool. I like it. It's good.

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's fair to say that while I would recommend this game, I would have to start that recommendation with "if you don't mind x y z, then..." because almost every positive I have is comes hand in hand with a "however,".I'm something like 70% through the campaign I think, and I do indeed feel the itch to keep coming back to play a level or two, but never more than that.the polish is great; movement is smooth; sound is great for the most part. combat is where I first start to get a bit of a mixed experience. I'd compare the combat to fast food; it is very good at quickly satisfying a craving, loaded with flavourings, but thats really where the depth ends. it's not even down to lackluster enemy design - there's a decent bit of variety but they all too often make themselves almost stationary targets; and there are way too many of those base level zombies that pose no threat but also don't serve any cannon-fodder purpose. it just starts to feel a little numbing after a while.the nexus point save system is a weird one. honestly I've been glad the system is there but not for a good reason, but because I'd rather just hurry up and get levels done than replay them or even replay them from a little while back, which isn't a good mindset. savegame systems are not something you can just develop overnight, but with the astonishing polish injected elsewhere in this game, I'm surprised they don't have something that feels less cheap.the level design is really really fun from a mechanical perspective, offering some very clever backtracking and switched-up reusing of older parts of levels, and some great sequences that evolve the playing field. very fun. it's super pretty in that respect too, but also a little tiring when it comes to theming. it's a lot of industrial tech fortressy kinda design that is done very well, but is almost all you see. I'm still having a good time with it, and definitely intend to finish it, but I can't truly gush over it.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Very fun weapons- Some secrets are very interactive- Secrets are actually rewarding (upgrades and weapons)- Secrets aren't required to progress but certainly help it a lot- Good sound design- Very fast weapon draw time to encourage weapon combos and self-swapping- Good movement speed- Enemies look like they actually take damage (missing limbs)The bad- Lack of enemy variety after The Forge (save for """bosses""")- Apparent power creep with the weapons (Plasma Rifle removes the need for Shredders, all bullet weapons eventually become useless when you get PR and Arc Rail, you will never use fists again once you have the Pistol, etc)- Chaos Caster is useful for only one thing and then never again- Auto Shotgun is also kind of useless and clunky to use since the recoil is horrendous and moves your cursor up for some reason- The blue versions of common enemies are pretty much just stat increased enemies and bullet sponges (and also just annoying)Conclusion- Game is pretty solid for the most part, a good game to turn your brain off to- I'd wait for a sale to buy it- DLC looks pretty cool ngl, we get a grappling hook, spear, and what looks like a stun ability

_childDocuments_.review: It's DOOM but in a 3D engine with more weapons and gore. If you like any of the classic DOOM games, you'll enjoy this! Many of the secrets have a currency you can use to buy new weapons or power ups. Prodeus also has a level editor and supports custom maps and campaigns (even in the console ports). While I enjoy its' unlock system, I look forward to seeing some classic-styled maps and doing pistol starts.My only nitpicks:Still I'm giving Prodeus a wholehearted recommendation. _childDocuments_.review: After completing the game post-release, I felt the need to update my review.While there's a solid "megawad" of levels to blast through in this game, I feel like they rushed the last "Chaos Realm" chapter of the game. The one level is pretty good, but the boss level and conclusion is unsatisfying.The game is missing a number of weapons from the main campaign (Chainsaw, Gauntlets, Plexus, Void Cannon) and I'm not a fan of the new "Shop". The weapon room in the early access version was more satisfying, as well as gaining new weapons in the levels instead of purchasing them.The secret level exits are gone, there are no secret levels to find. Only one secret exit still exists and doesnt take you anywhere. Additionally, I can think of at least one level that was shortened/changed from the EA version, but I have no idea why.Some very odd decisions indeed...Movement feels more like OG Doom (+Jumping/verticality), with naturally occurring arenas and organic combat flow (no forced mechanics like Doom Eternal). Additionally, the maps are very well crafted, and you dont get the sense of constantly starting and stopping to endure forced encounters.Weighty weapons with a variety of alt fires, complimented by another banging soundtrack by Andrew Hulshult. There are a number of objectives chucked into maps to add context to your journey, however there arent too many to give you the sense of being lead by the nose, and the game never feels overly linear.Devs, please add a feature to remove the vignette! XOXOXOXOXTop-tier boomer shooter made by devs with deep insight into the genre. If you wanted a game that sits between Doom 2016, and modern classics like Dusk and Amid Evil, you wont be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT MARATHON THIS GAMEOkay so this is rough for me. I played the game 80% of the way on the hardest difficulty and cleared levels pretty effortlessly without dying. At one point the game decides to Nightmare OG Doom on you with tiny rooms with explosive enemies and tanks. I lowered the difficulty down because I felt like I was being to harsh of a judge on the game because of this sudden spike of Romero unfairness. Lest ignore the difficulty factorCorpses of enemies still having hitboxes kind of sucks and here is an exampleFacing a reverse bowling pin sequence of enemies with a gunner or imp in the back line. ***** ****  **   & You pull out weapons that could mow down these enemies but the fact their corpses are body blocking shots makes it so a backfield shotgunner will hit you clean. These situations often happens in closed spaces that you have next to no mobility with. Now top this with yet another (some what weird issue). The game can be a little to blood happy sometimes. So your screen will just be covered with Gore so you can't see ♥♥♥♥, which is very awesome a lot of times, and just stupid frustrating at others. The locations don't start heating up and throwing interesting transitions at you until waaaay later in the game so you will be looking at space bases for a GOOD chunk of the game. The later levels variety helped but it was beginning to be to late. I still recommend this game. I think they could have given you better dashing, or maybe another upgrade to the dashing, reload your guns that are put away after X amount of time (♥♥♥♥ is soooo stupid and kills pacing). IDK there is a lot they could do to improve this game but....I would recommend this on a sale. They are currently working on DLC which should be adding more guns and more interesting locals but I'm sitting here wondering if that would still make me happy given the complete package. The AI for the enemies were mostly fun, you had to actually think about your movement because they could intelligently track you. I just don't think the game did you service with your mobility. eh....there is a lot to say here but again I will leave it withrecommend on a sale and again don't marathon it or you will hate it. I weaved in other games while playing it and took breaks when I usually just marathon things. Dusk for example, I couldn't put down.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually formulate lengthy reviews in way too much detail, praising or complaining about the most minute things. Not in this case.This game is an absolute banger.Buy it now! The price is worth it.Now, seriously, to give a little bit of insight here:Prodeus is another one of those boomer shooters that have been popping out a lot recently. And for good reason. Fast gameplay, lots of guns, scary monsters and good level design. 90s FPS reimagined in the current year, with improvements in areas where the 90s kinda sucked, let's be honest there. Most notably soundtrack, sound design, complex visual art, etc. Now, there are quite a lot of these neo-retro shooters that do mess up a lot of things, though. See STRAFE, most prominently (big sad).But, boy, does Prodeus not mess up much. And it improves in these given areas, in addition to being a visceral experience in the first place.Special shoutout to GmanLives for featuring this game on his channel btw. I honestly would have probably missed it for a while at least, otherwise.So, Prodeus was evidently inspired by the original Doom, first and foremost. More specifically, Brutal Doom. But then it took Brutal Doom and cranked it up to 100 with the gore and making the player feel like a god of war. Not to mention the soundtrack by Andrew Hulshult, though that is obviously more similar to Doom 2016 and Eternal. Two words: Industrial. Djent. That's all you need to know. However, Andrew's style is different from Mick Gordon's, and frankly, the more I get to experience his work, the more I appreciate it for its uniqueness and absolute, unmitigated brutality.There's also a bit of Quake mixed in here. The big brute that is the equivalent of a Pinkie for instance, for some reason reminds me of a Shambler, just slightly visually though. Overall, it's a good mix of what you can clearly recognize as demons and more eldritch horrors.Speaking of Quake, you can actually switch between sprites and 3D models for the enemies. With sprites, its more similar to Doom, with 3D models its more similar to Quake. Funny how that worked for me. I personally would only use the sprites though, as at least right now, your weapons and environmental models are always sprites too, making the 3D models stick out too much.Now, the game does have one (possibly big) negative, in my opinion. It's *too* brutal and gory. The amount of blood flying about when you're unloading on a group of enemies with your chaingun is visually very pleasing, but too much for gameplay's sake.You see, Prodeus is a pretty fast-paced game. And I think it is an issue when you cannot see how many enemies in a bigger mob you have dispatched, because there's tons of blood and particle effects (both of which look amazing btw) obscuring them. Never thought I'd see this day come, but yes, I think Prodeus has crossed the line just a little bit when it comes to weapons and impact feedback. So, hopefully, there will be an option later on that allows you to tone down the amount of gore just ever so slightly, or the way this system works is optimized a bit more for visual clarity. Other than that, I think Prodeus sets the bar pretty high for player feedback.Minor negatives or suggestions from my side would include a polish of the weapon selector you bring up with "Q". I think a weapon wheel would be much better here. Possibly also double usage of a hotkey, for instance the pistol and the Rippers on the same "2" key. The time to switch weapons is perfectly low, so I think a lot of people would appreciate this more oldschool categorizing of weapons on their hotkey numbers. But yeah, what you get here for your money, even right now in early access, is a game that is really tightly developed. And just really, really good in all the areas where it matters. Everything just fits and clicks. And when something doesn't, it's very minor. You get nicely paced levels that are well thought-out, featuring secret areas and sometimes secret exits to entirely new levels, with a nice learning curve when it comes to enemy progression and movement.You get one of the very best player feedback systems I have ever seen, for some weapons like the shotgun even surpassing Doom Eternal.You get a killer soundtrack that just pushes you to eviscerate everything you encounter.You simply get everything you love in boomer shooters, with everything you don't or didn't love at least improved heavily. Like I said, the one thing for me that'd be nice to see is further optimization of visual clarity when fighting big mobs of enemies, and perhaps, though this is very unnecessary, a bit more cohesion in the story. Or one at all, lol. But yes, I think the marketing claim here is pretty spot on. Prodeus might just be the boomer shooter you've been waiting for.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is a brilliant homage to classic first-person shooters like DOOM and Quake, but with a modern twist that elevates it into something truly special. It masterfully blends the old-school charm of pixelated graphics and fast-paced, brutal combat with modern visuals and fluid gameplay mechanics, creating a unique experience for both nostalgic gamers and new players alike.From the moment you start playing, Prodeus grips you with its high-energy action and tight controls. The game’s level design is impeccable, offering sprawling, intricately crafted maps filled with secrets, enemies, and non-stop mayhem. Each level feels like a playground for chaos, encouraging players to explore and find their own path through hordes of enemies, all while offering a steady stream of adrenaline-pumping combat.The weapon variety is a standout feature, with each gun feeling powerful, satisfying, and distinctive. Whether you’re mowing down waves of enemies with a shotgun or blasting through them with a plasma rifle, the gameplay never gets old. The gore system, which allows enemies to explode in a visceral shower of pixelated blood, adds an extra layer of visual satisfaction to every kill.One of the most impressive aspects of Prodeus is its balance between retro aesthetics and modern performance. The game allows you to switch between classic and modern graphical styles on the fly, which not only highlights the developers’ love for the genre but also provides a fresh experience for players. The music and sound design are another high point, with a thumping, metal-infused soundtrack that perfectly complements the intense gameplay.In addition to the campaign, Prodeus offers a robust level editor and community-driven content, meaning there’s always something new to play. The replay value is tremendous, whether you're gunning for faster times or exploring custom levels.Overall, Prodeus is a near-perfect blend of nostalgia and innovation. It’s a love letter to the golden age of shooters, wrapped in modern sensibilities. Whether you’re a veteran of the genre or someone new to fast-paced shooters, Prodeus is an absolute must-play.Pros:Perfect blend of retro and modern graphics.Tight, satisfying gunplay.Impeccable level design.High replayability with community-driven content.Cons:Some levels can feel a bit overwhelming at first.If you're a fan of classic shooters or just looking for a game that delivers unrelenting action and fun, Prodeus is the game for you!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first review I've ever posted of a game and it may be technically unfair but it deserves it.This game is one of those 50% games that is a mixture of elements that both work in its favour and against it.The game starts off with a promising aesthetic with that is pretty but the charm  soon wears off and will end up becoming the game's enemy. The overall feel of the look is colourful but is heavy and clunky and it overwhelms your vision in ways that make it hard to see what the enemy is doing which will end up getting you killed many times. Your vision of oncoming enemies gets heavily obscured by the effects so the player becomes disadvantaged in a way that will create many setbacks that rob game of its fun.To add to that, a lot of the enemies are able to predict your movement in a bot-like fashion that is so obvious at times that it feels like a slap in the face to the player. Other enemies have projectile attacks that lock on and follow you which is survivable when there are one or two of them but when there are heavy battle sequences you will get killed by those attacks that are impossible to see, let alone evade. You have to be near a decent sized object that you can hide behind and even then, some attacks seem to be able to go around or partially though solid objects.The enemy spawn-ins are very back-stabby during regular parts of the game but when you are in heavy battles this can often be something that kills you and which brings enjoyment to a grinding halt. Personally, this is one of the worst aspects of many games that seem to use this invisible surprise enemy as a synthetic difficulty. This is one of the biggest ruiners of games for me as it nearly impossible to sense and often decisively ends a battle. Moving backwards to evade an advancing enemy, who can often move more quickly than you, often results in your being attacked from behind while your movement suddenly stops for unknown reason and while you look around to figure out what's going on you will be killed from one of at least two directions.Some of the physics in the game are inconsistent or broken. Some objects stop your fire if you're right behind them but enemy fire is able to reach you perfectly fine.Put all these elements together and you get a game that sucks you in with enjoyable combat and then screws you over with lazy or incompetent design during important battles that corrodes the games enjoyment from the inside out.I gave it an overall thumbs down because the game has problems that have been present in other games I've played but those same mistakes are still being made. I can only guess that the developers don't have a full breadth of experience in previous FPS games so common mistakes have been re-created. It makes me wonder if this game is one of those by-the-numbers productions that happens to get some things right or if it wasn't given enough development time to mature some ideas which were good but couldn't be fully executed.I cannot give this game a simple yes or no recommendation. Just know that you are in for some good times and some bad times.

It's been a long time since a game won me over so hard, but here we are, RUTHLESSLY erect. Don't think, just buy it and call the ambulance while it installs.

_childDocuments_.review: There is potential for this game to be amazing, the enemy design is good, the core gameplay and weapons feel great and the graphics style is retro yet clean with some nice modern touches and additions to make it feel fresh. The built in level editor is fun to use and the community has and will likely continue to make some fantastic content.Unfortunately the included campaign is not great. This game obviously takes its inspiration from Doom but doesn't follow any of the level design ideas it mastered for its time. Every level plays the same - enter room, enemies spawn, hide and pick out snipers then clear out the rest by mostly circle strafing. Health and ammo balance needs fine tuning. Secrets are also not fun to find and are often just press this particular part of the wall or check off the beaten path for armor behind a wall. The checkpoint system isn't good, you can just endlessly respawn and there is no consequence to dying. You can choose to just restart a whole level but as some levels can be quite lengthy, this can lead to frustration.If you look back at Doom and to an extent Quake, every enemy placement, every room and even some secrets served a purpose in allowing you to approach each fight and level in multiple ways, allowing for extra replay value and requiring you to think on your feet. Far too many "old school" inspired shooters think making a pretty looking level, throwing in dozens of enemies and calling it a day is what old school shooters were like. It's for this reason I feel the modding and mapping community for the original Doom games are still so active to this day.If you have an old school shooter craving that needs satisfying, this will definitely do it but make sure to play some custom levels to really see this game at its best as some of the custom levels are amazing to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Great game, with a unique art style and feels like what Doom 3 should have been. I played through the early-access beta and have almost finished the main campaign. Will edit this when I'm done.Pros:- Runs at a smooth 60fps without hitching and at High settings (On RTX 2070, Ryzen 2600, 16gb RAM.)- Great level design throughout- Lighting and VFX work well with the artstyle- Weapons sound punchy and each is a tool that is useful in certain situations- Enemies and their placement are well thought-out- Movement feels buttery smooth and fast- Levels are easy to navigate and full of secrets- Support for community-made levels and campaigns- The shotgun!- Good range of graphical options (including field of view)- Awesome soundtrack Cons:- Zombie Shotgunners don't stand out from hordes of melee zombies. - Some enemies don't clearly telegraph attacks, making dodging awkward- Ammunition shared between multiple weapons can make cycling between them irritating- The alt-fire on some weapons feels redundant; the burst-fire alt on the pistol is a good example- Map controls are clunkyOverall, this is a game that is well worth the cost of entry. I would strongly recommend this for people who are fans of Doom 2016, Doom Eternal, Dusk and other Boomer-Shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus... Man, What a game!At first, it might be deceiving as in, it looks all kinda samey, like all gray and chrome and red and first maps are all tech bases, but soon enough it develops into a super fun and creative game that could be an incredible GzDoom mod.So this game is an amalgamation of old and new boomer shooters, as in, you get the retro look and style, similar to Doom or Quake, but then you get the gameplay options from more modern Boomer Shooters like Doom Eternal or Ultrakill, meaning you'll be double jumping, dashing, shifting weapons mid-combat to better suit the enemies in front of you.Levels, as said before start quite simple but grow more complex and interesting the further you progress on the campaign, you'll be seeing maps unfold, and change before your eyes and that makes it feel just so cool, also, the style will be changing as you progress from Tech Bases to Mars type open spaces, Spaceships, Foundries, Other Dimensions and stuff like that, none of it is quite "new", but it's done really well, and maps are so much fun to go through.Enemies have a limited roster that doubles, as there are "Heaven" and "Chaos" enemies that look kinda the same but change attack patterns and movement.Weapons all look cool and have their own utility to the combat, and they all sound punchy, super satisfying to use.There are some minor gripes about this game, at least for me, like the excess of particle effects sometimes makes it hard to see what you're pointing at, also the crosshair sometimes get lost in this same mix of colors, would be nice to be able to change its color. Another thing that is kinda tiresome is the Ore progression system... Just give me the damn upgrades and let me play with them instead of HAVING to unlock them by finding hidden Ore fragments in the maps. And for last, some people might complain about the checkpoint system... I mean, it DOES make things easier and would be nice to be able to turn it off for the ones who don't wanna play like that, it's easy to circumvent though, maybe die/restart level and that's it.Anyway, this is just a great, great boomer shooter, totally should be played by anyone who likes retro FPS games.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: 5 minutes into the game it already captured everything I wanted it from a boomer shooter. You can feel all the elements from 90's DOOM to DOOM Eternal.Shooting feels great. The guns are crisp down to the sound and feel of it and makes you want to encounter more demons than each level offers (which, by the way, already has tons of enemies).The graphics beautifully imitated the 90's CRT 16-bit era. A stroke of nostalgia during the PS2 days I'd say. Try setting the graphics to 360p with Scanline or CRT mode enabled and memories just rush back.Music made by Andrew Hulshult who composed amazing music from different Doom WAD mods. I would say this is almost or even on par with Doom Eternal's rage music that'll just keep you going until all evil from your body just oozes out.There are several features such as level editors as well. Personally haven't tried it yet, but looking at the reviews online I think it looks amazing.Kudos to the Bounding Box Software. Hope to see more boomer shooters like this.

_childDocuments_.review: The checkpoint system makes this game way too easy on the hardest difficulty.  However, the last boss fight has a rather big difficulty spike because it lacks the checkpoints that enable you to cruise through the rest of the game, so I turned the difficulty down one notch after around ten tries on the hardest difficulty and I was able to beat it on the first try without much sweat--that's botched game design as far as I'm concerned.  Another problem is the way double-jump, dash and several weapon upgrades are locked behind a currency (ore) you find largely from secret hunting.  This seems like a way of padding how much game there is because it incentivizes replaying levels to get most of the ore in each level so you can buy the things that are displayed in the shop before you run out of levels to play.   I'll still recommend it because it's pretty solid apart from these two issues, but they are really big issues that people need to know about before playing.

_childDocuments_.review: 6-7/10 Despite being one of the better 1990s throwback shooters I have played it is still a bit far from perfect. On the plus side there are loads of graphical and gameplay options to tune the game to your personal preferences. Generally, it has good use of pace change; though I think the game is at its best when the pace is fast and up-close. Some of the later levels "build" and "morph" in front of the player which is a unique and interesting design. However, the need to search heavily for secrets/hidden areas often is to the game’s detriment. It creates this counter incentive to comb every square inch of terrain which goes directly against what makes the game feel its best. Additionally, weapon utility balance is a bit off and all over the place. The base pistol is probably one of the best weapons in the game. Most enemies color palette is too similar the backgrounds and numerous palette swap enemies are present throughout. Overall I'm pleased enough to say its worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: 4 hours in and I feel like I've played enough to write an initial review.For anyone who grew up in the era of Doom, Quake, etc, this is close to being a must-buy, even at full price. It's fast paced, bloody, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ storyline you don't care about, and an awesome variety of weapons, enemies, and environments. The music is pretty good, though not as slamming as say Doom 2016 or Quake II. Some people have complained about the checkpoint system, but it hasn't bothered me at all.My complaints so far:- AI is ok, but by no means great. Enemies with projectiles lead in the direction you're headed which leads to them hitting walls right by their face or floor sometimes if you're falling. I can also easily cheese most enemies if they're a fair distance away from me - most have no problems standing still while getting blasted with a pistol. I've also seen a few get stuck on obstacles while trying to come after me.- A number of weapons are held behind "shops" which require "fragments" to purchase. A few of those fragments require purchasing the double-jump in order to reach them which isn't available until you get 20 fragments, hence requiring you to re-run a few levels to get them all. I would've preferred not having to purchase new weapons or abilities, and instead being able to purchase weapon or ability upgrades. And definitely do not want to re-run the same level more than once just to be able to get all fragments.- No rocket-jump. I discovered this while trying to reach said un-reachable fragments while I didn't have the double-jump.- The multiplayer is essentially dead, or at least public servers are. I've only spotted 2 servers so far, both were co-op and one was in the EU. The game came out of early access just under 6 months ago and I was surprised and disappointed I didn't see any deathmatch or CTF. There are also no bots either. Haven't dug around Discord looking for them.- Along the same lines, I wish they had a standalone executable for a public server. I would love to set up my extra PC to run one.All in all, it's a great single player, FPS that scratches that 90s itch. The fact it was done by 2 people is even more impressive. If you're ok with my complaints, then I'd say definitely go buy it. I'll update my review once I beat the game if anything changes.Edit: Just finished the campaign. I'm going to leave my original review and add on a few more points:I'd say it's no longer a must-buy. I think you'd better better of going back to Quake II, or if you want a modern take DOOM 2016.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed Prodeus on Kickstarter and I would say it  was well worth the investment.Someone referred to Prodeus as "Doom 2016 if it had been made in the 90s" and that is a not-inaccurate description. It is brought to us by two former Raven Software devs, specifically one of my favorite singleplayer FPSes of the previous decade, Singularity. It goes a long way to explaining the general chunkiness of Prodeus' combat: the game's weapon and enemy feedback convey a sense of power. The guns are guns, not "damage projectors" as my friend termed it.The setting of Prodeus is exceedingly vague at present, perhaps intentionally so, and draws what are doubtless deliberate visual and thematic parallels to Doom: It would appear to be the future, and you are a lone soldier in a military research base on a barren planetoid, beset by an invasion of seemingly demonic entities referred to as "Chaos", apparently led by an entity known as "Prodeus." Maybe that is enough of a backstory, maybe not. The reality of the situation however, is a clear and familiar one: The only way out of this hell is through, with all guns blazing.To that end, you have access to a relatively wide variety of weapons, more then can comfortably fit in the classic one-to-zero keyboard selections, in fact. They are familiar in form and function, and each has some form of alternate mode; a shotgun with a charge shot, a grenade launcher with sticky-grenade option, a lightning gun with optional sniper shot and so on. There are only five ammo types however, and each is shared between three of the guns: For example, the basic pistol with its Borderlands Dahl-style aimed burst fire, dual-wielded submachine guns and powered minigun all share bullet ammo. Maximum ammunition for each type is fairly limited, forcing you to juggle guns and weigh their effectiveness versus a given group of enemies. There is a slickness and level of visual polish to Prodeus that makes you believe it could have been a fifty-dollar game from the turn of the millenium. Smooth controls, high-resolution 3D weapon models rendered as sprites for style, and intricate directional lighting that still applies to said sprites as if they were 3D, and each sprite set has significantly more frames then games of yore would have had. Andrew Hulshult's soundtrack surprised me here: He captures that "neo-doom" feel much better then the noisome assault on the eardrums that passes for music in Doom 2016. I've had a few technical hiccups here and there, including a nasty crash-on-launch problem a few days prior to this writing, but said issue was fixed by the next hotfix, so I have little I could complain about beyond a small desire for more fine-tuning with the mouse sensitivity slider. I do think however, that the game would benefit from the addition of a weapon wheel. This early access build, complete with functional level editor, represents a strong framework for the game going forward.

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is greater than the sum of its parts, but the game doesn’t meet the expectations it sets for itself.The campaign is great, if a little on the short side. There are some excellent battles and set pieces, a wide variety of terrain and settings and some of the most ambitious terrain and geography I’ve seen in an FPS for a while later on in the campaign, which puts a lot of triple A titles to shame. The levels are to such a high standard that you’ll forgive the devs for not making more once you’ve experienced them. Since the dev team is two people plus a couple of extra mappers, I suspect there may have been some burnout across the team.The campaign did itself a disservice in terms of how it dishes out some (but not all) of its top tier weapons though, having them available for purchase at a shop after finding secret ore items within the missions. I much prefer finding weapons than having to earn the ore, which in some cases means repeating levels… its not a play pattern I enjoy. Finding a weapon mid mission after a well-placed secret or gruelling fight would be much better and more of its intended era.Not a single weapon felt bad to use but one felt worse than the others; that was the minigun, although it is in no way a bad weapon, it just lacks the oomph that some of the other weapons provide and with slowing the player down as it spins up… It feels less than rewarding to use once you’ve experienced some of the other guns in the game and consequently doesn’t see the use it deserves.Graphics wise I love Prodeus. It captures what it sets out to do perfectly. The real star of the graphics though is the shader which makes the 3D enemies appear as if they are 2D pixel images. It looks much better than the admittedly incredible work of the Doom Voxel mod and I feel like the tech Bounding Box have created will serve other games equally well. The game does tech bases and stony outcrops and the depths of evil machines and some other places incredibly well too.As for the terrific looking enemies… there are far too few of them and the limited bestiary takes too long to expand within the missions. There’s room for more zombies, with more weapon types especially when you consider the large arsenal of player weapons they could have access to. Several of the enemies look overwhelmingly similar too, just size variations on a similar creature which starts off as a small crawling type enemy, of which I hate. Low down enemies are fine but small creatures are just annoying and a heap of FPS developers constantly throw critter size enemies into games at the minute. If you want a low-down enemy look at Quake’s dogs or the sequel’s health sucking parasite. Also the game lacks a difficulty setting that parallels Doom’s Ultra Violence, the best FPS difficulty setting ever conceived. The higher difficulties don’t add enemies they essentially give them higher accuracy that feels unfair and substantially more damage too. I played every single level on hard but admit I struggled on the final level.It might sound like I am complaining about the game a lot… but I’m not. The game is incredibly fun to play, and understands what constitutes a great fps game. It’s a game made on roughly $100k from Kickstarter, early access donations and whatever the publisher coughed up, by mostly two people but you would think the team was a fair bit larger.Lastly I need to mention the inbuilt level editor. It’s amazing, studio quality stuff which I am gradually learning. I start making things which I think are okay and then I feel sick when I see the downright incredible creations people are making, my favourite of which is called THE SLIPGATE COMPLICATION by PULSAR. Yes from the name it’s exactly what you think it will be… but it isn’t. Please try it though, I think you’ll have a great time.It’s the best retro boomer shooter released by far, and makes a lot of other attempts look incredibly amateurish. Disclaimer: I kickstarted this btw.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Why I stopped Playing: The Gore GFX prevent you from seeing much of anything the moment you kill something halfway close to gibbable, which obscures other enemies, requiring you to waste ammo firing at enemies who might already be dead, in the hopes of killing enemies hidden in the ""pretty"" sprite-based graphics which, unfortunately, barely pop out much if at all, creating the problem that modern games have of low readability.Hitscanners.The campaign ends on a cliffhanger, the last level is the only vaguely difficult one to actually complete on any difficulty level because every other level gives you tons of space, and the last one doesn't. I was expecting to get roughly 4-9 Eldritch domain levels that would really begin pushing the player and testing their skills but ultimately it was mostly disappointing, given how there are also 4 weapons you don't ever pick up, making me think that the devs intentionally left empty weapon slots in a supposedly finished product, that the weapons aren't implemented in what is ostensibly their official introduction to the world of Prodeus, that they can't even provide the entire arsenal in the campaign while giving players absurd time and space to use their arsenal, which is objectively a core design element of any decent classic FPS title worth writing home about.The checkpoint system doesn't work as a backtracking mechanic like it rightfully should, as the game is ultimately too easy to need a checkpoint system to begin with. Most enemies have 1 strategy that'll render you immortal vs them, and most of it is circle strafing or peek-a-booing with only 1 enemy type (I don't count recolors as different enemies from weaker variants) providing any inherent challenge that requires some degree of moment to moment reaction, that being the Definitely Not An Imp From Doom enemy type.Prodeus enemy types are, save what I remember as the Harbinger, mostly just Chaos enemies with a cool texture placed over the existing texture, with an overlay filter applied and aside from the ability to Cloak, have literally no new tools to kill the player or serve as extra challenge, they are just tankier, with the Harbinger being the only enemy to vaguely challenge the player on the Prodeus side, it is still invalidated by circle strafing.No quick level selection within the Campaign making backtracking to previous levels an absolutely tedious chore.Trial levels do not communicate the time limit very well and at no point does the game communicate that previously-obtained Ore is permanently collected, meaning repeat playthroughs of other levels do not require the player to recollect it.Honestly I wish I could swap the Grenade Launcher and Rocket Launcher's positions, the GL is ultimately a worse weapon than the RL and having to double-press 5 to get the RL wastes my time, I would love a future QoL update to include the ability to change weapon positions within each button (swap pistol for the SMGs but not swap the shotgun and pistol's positions for example, not that anyone would ever do that).Personally for a classic genre "reimagined by modern technology and techniques" I died way less than I expected and while I enjoyed my time, it's got plenty of flaws that it leaves me more disappointed than happy to have played it. One could call me ungrateful, or say I'm taking Prodeus for granted, but it genuinely feels 60% shorter than it has any right to be, and given how the game has a built-in level editor that people have used to make some terrific custom maps with, I can't help but just feel the way that I do.I'm not a fan of requiring a 3rd party account to play singleplayer, that is ludicrous. Leaderboards add nothing to the game and rating campaign levels also functionally has no purpose.Each new line above is a gripe I have, save for the one that is immediately above this one.

_childDocuments_.review: i can't play doom 1993., its just too old and misses to many things that were invented later. prodeus feels like the bit of doom that i have played but as if it was released recently. looking at the mechanics i see doom 1993 everywhere. the health, secrets, ai, weapons, map geometry even the level end screen smudge. the best example of this is the graphics all of the things in the game are clearly 3d models displayed as 100 different sprites depending on the angle it looks so much better than the 8 sprites doom had while still capturing the same aesthetic. honestly if you wanted to play doom 1993 or other retro FPS but couldn't get yourself too then this is perfect

The multiplayer is incredible, more than what I expected. I'm currently playing through the campaign with one other person but I have a group of four lined up for other game modes. _childDocuments_.review: A good fusion of Doom 1/2 and Doom 4/5 style gameplay mechanics. Tons of gore, strong level design, a good sense of gameplay flow. Pretty solid from the little bit I played.A couple points of criticism: - Some of the monster attacks (the not-Imps specifically) seem a little hard to predict, which makes learning their "dance" kinda difficult.- Monster noises could be made a little more distinctive, the way old shooters use them to signal what you're up against in an area and help with spatial recognition.But mostly it's good. Looking forward to the full version.

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels like it was made by some people who felt that saw the latest DOOM instalments and said "Where is the option to play with sprite based graphics? This is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!" then disappeared into the woods, only to crawl out some time later carrying this game. The game itself plays well, is fun and visually really nice, the similarities to DOOM don't make it a carbon copy or a shameless ripoff, it has it's own style and it changes things around, adding old familiar concepts with new ones. _childDocuments_.review: Yes. Nothing more needs to be said. If you like the new Doom games, but also like boomer shooters, this is for you.More in depth (slightly). Go from level to level with "shops" in between, where you can spend your hard-earned ore, found in said levels, often hidden, for different weapons, double jump, etc. Not a big fan of that, to be honest, because it "incentivizes" you to revisit levels, especially once you get double jump.Music is great, shooting feels great, every weapon is useful, yes, even the basic pistol is a beast compared to other games. Graphics are neat, and you can change between sprite and 3d enemies. 7 to 8 hours and you're done. Doesn't overstay its welcome too much, although the lack of enemy variety towards the latter half of the game is noticeable, but the levels themselves can be completed within 10 to 20 minutes each. Latter half of the game gets quite chaotic. A bit overtuned for my taste, but since respawning doesn't have penalties attached, it's alright. On the other hand, that, of course, means that you can just repeatedly throw yourself against the enemies without any negative consequences... which makes it kinda pointless to play on higher difficulties for a challenge.Game ends "abruptly" if you've actually came here for the "story". Still, 8/10 imho if you're into these kinds of games. Might be a bit expensive for what it is if you just want to play through once, and not go backtracking and secret hunting. Prodeus enemies are uninspired though.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of this game is nothing new, but the execution definitely is. Prodeus seamlessly combines old school aesthetics with a modern day engine. The presentation looks both slick and smooth and pixelated at the same time. I have never seen a game use sprites whereby you can view it from all angles (including from above). You can turn off the sprites and use full 3D models and it’s then where you can see what kind of technology and “trick” they used to make the sprites viewable from all angles. The fact that they made the weapons you use pixelated and intentionally made the animations of the weapons a lower framerate just adds to the overall aesthetics. This is all backed up by really smooth and responsive controls. The guns feel very satisfying to shoot and I love the reload animation (I just love reloading guns in games for some reason). The enemies are basically Doom enemies and you can easily compare this game to brutal Doom. The difference between Prodeus and Brutal Doom is that Prodeus has higher production value. The game has very straightforward levels where you can look for secrets and almost never get lost. You’re just constantly pushing forward (when you die you just respawn at the last checkpoint with the monsters already dead). It has a momentum going on and that coupled with an awesome metal soundtrack just makes the game badass.The game has custom maps that you can easily download and play for fresh new content every time you boot it up
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a boomer shooter before. I just wanted a game with DOOM level violence. Well, here it is.Now I'm going to answer a few question that some people might be wondering:Is the soundtrack metal? Yes.Can you use 3D models? Yes.Is it story heavy? No.Are there waifus? Your shotgun.Are headphones recommended? Obviously.What about the gun SFX? BOOM BOOM BLAM BLAM CLICKY CLICK BANG BANG (It sounds like God slamming his car door).Is there reloading? Yes, but it somehow feels right.Are the controls tight? Very, and for a shooter, controls as tight as this are a must.Are the difficulty levels? Many. I play on Hard myself.I'm a girl, can I play this? Just buy it already.Hows the frame rate? I have it resting at 120fps, but it can go higher.Is the "infinite blood thing true? Yes.Is there multiplayer? At this time, no.This is an early access review. At time of writing, my gameplay time is around half an hour and I'm already loving it.I would recommend picking it up before the full release price hike.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: You like classic DOOM / QUAKE games ?If the answer is yes then you will love Prodeus.Perfect fast paced gameplay, absolutely amazing graphics with stunning looking sprites and 3D, great level design, sick soundtrack, list goes on...The game also comes packed with an awesome level editor for infinite replay value.What we have here is an absolute must have, a well crafted gem and probably the best throwback first person shooter of the last decade.Can't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent game.The good:Beautiful art style - it's almost like stop-motionThe guns actually feel powerful and are fun to shootThe amount of blood is just over the top and satisfyingFun, fast-paced gameplay as any good boomer shooter should beRewarding secrets throughout the mapsThe bad:This is where I think what could've been a 9/10 game goes down to like 6.5/10.The game is too easy, even on the hardest difficulty. And this doesn't even take into account the fact that there is no punishment to dying. As in, if you decide to respawn at a checkpoint, all the enemies that were killed stay dead. No life system, no having to re-do sections, just zero point to even having death in the game. Takes away all the challenge and really seems to just want you to speed run missions for a high score or something. That's not why I think most people bought this game.It's also a considerably short campaign. Overall, worth a buy on sale because it IS a fun game with satisfying combat, despite the lack of challenge. But not one I see myself playing through more than once.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up on games like Quake, Doom and Soldier of Fortune and love fast paced gore drenched games, this scratches an itch for sure. The art style is absolutely stunning, they've nailed the low poly map layout and paired in perfectly with more modern lighting and rendering techniques. Coupled with a fast paced heavy metal soundtrack you can't really ask for more.Weapons have a good punch to them and are satisfying to use, levels have a good flow to them and haven't so far left you scratching your head as to where to go. Well worth picking up if you've finished the new Doom installments and found yourself uninspired by the recent Quake 1 update. Also, props again to the map-makers, they deserve some praise!
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: So far, yet another excellent edition to the renaissance of old school FPS's.  In fact, I would put this game on par with Dusk in terms of just how good it is.  The level design is excellent, the weapons feel heavy and powerful (I particularly want to compliment the sound design; they really nailed that), the gore is over the top and twisted (in a very good way), and the combat is faced pace and has a nice overall feel to it.  The only minor nitpick I have is that a Half-Life esque weapon hot key selection system could benefit this game once all of the weapons are added in (as there are more guns than numerical keys per the in-game load out menu).  But apart from that small issue (which I admit is a personal preference), this is a superb shooter through and through.There is also a level editor that allows one to create maps.  I imagine this will increase the game's replay ability, but I have yet to try it out.In short, this is a MUST buy for fans of FPS games.  I can't wait to see how the game continues to evolve.

Only complaint about the campaigns is that you have to finish a level to save your progress (i.e. to be able to close out and return).update - after having finished the game, that is absolutely a feature, not a bug. If you played this game before it was finished, absolutely try it again now. Strong recommend to all fans of boomer shooters and FPS games alike. Each level is relatively short although it might take awhile to figure out. I also wish that they eventually fit all of the extra weapons in the main campaign. Unfortunately the online component is pretty dead in East US.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for November  2023, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before December 5th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Doom 2020. As I played Prodeus I couldn’t help myself, this is a game that screams Doom’s name as it emulates the king of all shooters so hard, and yet, that’s me praising Prodeus. The levels look great, the music got my blood pumping, and the enemies while taken from Doom look awesome. This feels like a version of the original Doom done in the modern era, with a similar-sized team. This just gave me flashbacks to 30 years ago when I was running around Phobos and Deimos for the first time, just having the most awesome time blasting enemies through a variety of levels. Prodeus is a boomer shooter that also seems to remind people why this genre is popular rather than trying to reinvent the wheel at every turn. I wish I could end there, but Prodeus does have some issues. There’s almost no difficulty in the early levels. I played on Medium and rarely went below 90 percent health and armor.  On Ultra Hard, the hardest difficulty level, I had almost no death the entire third level, and the respawn system will trivialize the difficulty I think. I’ve heard the game does get harder after what people call the first world, but experienced players won’t be too challenged. Pick this up if you were ever a fan of the original Doom, this lives up to the original incarnation, and that’s about as much praise as I can give. I’d have to play more but I could even see giving this a nod over Doom Eternal, as sacrilegious as that is to say. I like it that much. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of retro FPS since I was a child (even when I shouldn't had);  combines modern combat with the simplicity of shooting and running like . It really brings me back to those times.First of all, I completed the game but I still don't understand quite well who is the protagonist. It seems that he is a corrupted agent of the  and he is looking . He seems to be a relentless figure like the Doom Slayer but with other motives. As I mentioned before, there are 2 races: The Prodeus and the Chaos Demons. The basic units of each race look the same but with different color, later on the game, you will find unique and more challenging enemies of each species.From the menu design, the map selector, the HUD to the weapons, it feels very original. I think that the only 2 aspects that I dislike was that some enemy designs seems ordinary and that maybe, my point of view, the design of the last 2 levels were kinda simple or not impressive. The soundtrack comes in 2 ways: , made by Andrew Hulshult, which reminds me a lot to the Sonic Mayhem's OST from Quake II and the award winning Doom Ethernal OST. This one is very heavy, intense and also very electronic. I loved it. The other one is the , made by James Paddock, brings you back to the music of games like Hexen, Doom (1993) or Duke Nukem 3D. It's MIDI!, it feels somewhat modern if you hear each layer of sound with attention and you can tell that is very complex (this one is free to download by the way). I love both and they mesh very well with the gameplay for a deeper retro experience.Last part, the visuals. The game was made with Unity Engine. There is a "pixel/CRT/scanlines" effect that really looks like your monitor is like 20 years old; enemies are in 2D, not Voxel like some Doom mods (which I thing that would have been better but that's my own opinion), they look very cool, they made a lot of angles for each enemy or pick-up; the game offers modern effects like ambient occlusion, bloom, SSR or light scattering that blends very well with the retro effects. There is a lot of customization on it, so it's up to you.The game comes with a Multiplayer option. You can play the campaign in coop or just common PVP on deathmatch, Team DM and CT. Also, the game gives you a lot of tools to make your own levels for normal MP or to make campaigns. You can also share your designs with the community.This game has a lot to offer, , especially if you love retro FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: Does exactly what it says on the tin, and does it well!The combat is fast, the guns feel meaty and the particle/gore effects are wonderfully over-the-top. The visuals are also cool as all hell.The level editor, while slightly hard to learn, allows for some incredible freedom. You get to shape everything freely, rather than relying heavily on pre-built assets. There's already some great user generated content and I hope to see way more in the future.The campaign at the time of writing is about 3 hours long for a seasoned fps player. It's not long, but it's pretty sweet. I tolerate the short length of it on account of it being early access, and because players themselves will generate new content over time.Biggest complaint is the checkpoint system. The game doesn't reset the level to the last checkpoint, but just respawns the player, while enemies killed remain dead. I hate having a challenge stolen from me by being able to just respawn over and over. Single weakest aspect of the game right there.Final verdict for me is a very solid recommendation. Even at this stage it feels better than a lot of other fully finished games out there, which is pretty impressive.

_childDocuments_.review: I like Doom Eternal, but I completely dislike how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ technical and balance-y the developers got with their design (especially for a Doom game).Prodeus's gameplay is so golden that I'm probably gonna shift my 181 hours of singleplayer gameplay from Doom Eternal into this game. It has a level format that feels like New Super Mario Bros and smacks in the actual boomer shooter gameplay that I was hoping for (perfectly). This is the type of game that isn't a sweat-fest like Doom Eternal, and I could just casually play whenever.It would be nice if we could bind certain weapons to groups (and have that as a keybind) (because 12+ weapons seems a bit excessive to manage) but really, this game is a must-have (even when it's Early Access).Even if you don't like the game, go buy Andrew Hulshut's OST. It's actually a work of art, and it gives you perspective as to what will come for other titles composed by him.

_childDocuments_.review: When you decide to stick to an old formula and add nothing new, you ride or die based on whether you have good fundamentals and execution. Fortunately for Prodeus, "good fundamentals and execution" is exactly what describes it.As far as gameplay goes, it is a classic Quake-style shooter that decided it still wants to use Doom-like 2D sprites, albeit at a far greater scope. This sounds like an odd choice at first, but in practice it does indeed improve the style and atmosphere significantly. And not even at the cost of accuracy - the level of detail on the sprites is such that headshots are both easy to land, and meaningful. Gunplay in general is polished to a sheen and very satisfying to engage with. The level design starts out modest to let new players find their feet, but then quickly gets very bold and very good. This is amped up by the music experiencing a similar escalation in Andrew Hulshult-brand metal goodness as the game progresses. By the time you get to the really out-there levels, they start to feel like they were taken straight out of Doom 2016 and retro-demaked.And that's about your lot. Prodeus knows exactly what it wants to be, and doesn't waste time on any fluff that could bring it down. The only weakpoint I can think of is that the campaign ends abruptly on a cliffhanger, with the very clear intention for the game to be expanded via new episodes later.

_childDocuments_.review: I helped with kick starter and I got 2 copies of the game for helping. The Devs were always quick on answering questions and I feel they are really pouring their love in to this game. At this time I have played 3 hrs of this game and really enjoyed what I have played. The music is what really makes this game kick but the other aspects are very good.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still not entirely sure why a game like this need reloading, sprinting and checkpoints, but other than that it's a really great experience. Graphics are very nice, and there's lots of options. You can make it look pixelated and old, or very clean but still retro. Art direction is ok, i haven't seen much yet, and so far it's mostly grey rocks and industrial facilities, but some of the lighting effects are really nice. Overall a very clean look, easy to understand what's going on. Music is on point, Hulshult delivers great soundtrack once again.This game is clearly inspired by original doom games, and plays very similar to what slightly more modern doom would play if it came out around 2007. So it's doom, but with proper reloading instead of just pumping your shotgun, sprint and no quick save/load. Which is a bit weird imo, but doesn't make shooting demons any less fun, at least when it comes to shotgun. This one is probably going down in boomer shooter books as one of the best shotguns ever. It's a proper work horse, like any shotgun should be. Has good damage, fairly good range, and an alt fire that allows to charge up a very accurate and powerful shot. So far i actually like all of the weapons, except dual machine guns, because reloading them takes about just a long as emptying a magazine, and it doesn't deal nearly enough damage to justify that, especially after you already have a chain gun which just obliterates anything in it's path. Plenty of different enemies, but you already know all of them, because they are just doom enemies. Zombie soldiers, imps, cacodemons etc., they have unique traits compared to classic ones, but it's minor. And they all get gibbed very explosively, which is a pure joy for my eyes. Also level design is straight up fantastic. The levels so far stay on the edge of being maybe just a little too big and complicated, but the path to the end keeps finding itself. I haven't had to open up a map to find where i have to go, and got slightly lost only once. The amount of enemies is just perfect, and a lot of rooms you can clear without needing to reload your shotgun, if you hit your shots, which is a nice touch. And when there is too much enemies for that, you just pull out a rocket launcher or a chain gun and clean up what's left.Overall it's a fun old school shooter, and if you enjoy stuff like dusk or ion fury, i'm 99% certain that you will enjoy this one too.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Even though it's short it's a great taste of what's to come when the full game eventually comes out. As a fan of Quake and Doom this is the perfect combination of the two. It has the level design and speed of a Quake game with the weapons and enemies of a Doom game. The sound effects and gore is what keeps me looking forward to each combat encounter and thankfully there are a lot of them. The music is also amazing. The only issues that I have are that some weapons feel useless like the grenade launcher and dual assault rifles, and the game isn't that hard. Death is treated the same as Bioshock where you just respawn at the last checkpoint with full health. I wish that wasn't the case but then again this isn't the final product so anything can change. I still really enjoyed my time with this game and hope that it continually gets support.

_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Almost a great game but it is ruined by 'checkpoints'. The checkpoints are not really checkpoints, because if you resume from a checkpoint, you will find enemies you killed AFTER you activated the checkpoint have not respawned but are still dead. So you are forced to play with infinite health if you use the fake checkpoints. The only other option, if you want to play with a challenge, is to play the game  in such a way that you force yourself to avoid the faux checkpoint. But if you die, you have to restart the whole level, but at least the monsters will be back. There are no options to turn this off either. And you cannot save your game-in-progress manually! Complaints have been made but the developers have not addressed the matter and I suspect they never will. And because of how the game is designed, multiplayer with random people is not likely to happen but instead you have to organize a time to play with people if you want to get a game going, because you cannot join a game already in session. So if you want to play multiplayer, don't expect to just start up a game and play bots and wait for someone to join. Instead start a lobby and stare at the screen until somebody joins, and don't expect anyone to, as everyone got bored waiting for that so multiplayer never became a thing on this game.I would not recommend this game if you want a challenge or if you don't want to reward developers that charge people for a game and wont address their simple requests for challenge without tedious gameplay. Bounding Box Software has become a name I will remember and not for the right reasons...

_childDocuments_.review: Do you love Doom? More specifically classic old-school Doom? If so then you'll absolutely love Prodeus. It's clear while playing this the developers were most clearly inspired and big fans of id Software's original demon killing genre defining cult classic. Everything you love about the classic Doom games is here, just with more gore, blood, guns, violence and damn near everything. I've only been playing this game for a couple of levels in and it's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ f**king good. Dare I say I may like this even more so then the original 1993 Doom. There's apparently also a mode to customise and create your own levels which is an insanely cool feature. I would highly recommend checking this game out if your interested. I don't think you'll be disappointed. As of writing this, the game is still in early-access. I can't imagine how much better the final product will be when fully finished.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the early access campaign. It's good! Weapons are punchy, and they seem pretty well balanced. Levels are large and well designed, I rarely got lost. There can be a lot of secret hunting in this game, I never went out of my way very far so I only got about 1/3 of the secrets. Definitely an enjoyable FPS experience, so long as you like the art style.UPDATE: I have finished the game after it's final release. I'd give this a 7.5/10, entertaining, but not very far beyond that. Combat never truly gripped me, I almost never died on the "Hard" difficulty, and even the "Very Hard" difficulty wasn't satisfying, the monsters were still slow and easy to outplay, but hit you harder when you got lazy. Level design is still good, lots of creative ideas came together in the later levels.It's still fun, and if you're a fan of shooters you should check it out. Just don't expect anything legendary.

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus leaves nothing understated. Right off the bat, you'll be unceremoniously shoved up a menstruating elephant's snatch that violently bursts into squirting while being curb-stomped by a raging bucket-wheel excavator on top of the Sun. Truly, it's a mukbang of death. And the moment you pause to burp, it follows up with an explosive power-wash from myriads of Satan's pimples popped in concert, each jetting out at a pressure of a firehose, engulfing the world in a tsunami of clotty juices and sizzling hot innards. Groovy.Speaking of juices, the lighting is blooming! It's like the bases were built by boomers who just discovered gamer lights. Just joking, it's superb. Rich, applied in thick layers. The game's world is shiny, as if made of biteable rubbered plastic, and probably oily to the touch. In terms of visual design and themes, Prodeus is close to Quake 2 or rather 4, considering how bloody glistened its extraterrestrial bases get. Not my favourite style though, I prefer my industrial landscapes less rounded. But it's a remarkable take still. The experience is framed by awesome synth\metal music during fights, something to enjoy before it fades back to the repetitive droning loops of peace. The guns' reloading is pure ASMR and the shots are fine, but also slightly muffled and squeaky. Damn future and its fear of rough edges.I'm not the only one who thinks that the UI across the board is devolving, and Prodeus is a good example of that phenomenon. So far, it takes 3 logos, 3 loading screens, and up to 8 clicks to jump into a level after starting the game. This is excessive by any standards. Opening the main menu and allowing to press "continue" like in most other shooters would surely suffice. I know it's a nitpick, however, it's a recurring one. Initially, I was fond of the gorgeous 3D automap, albeit not for long. It pans too slowly and doesn't seem to have an option to speed it up, dissuading me from using it often. The menu fonts are generic, but hey, the sounds are appetising! It's not all doom and gloom, no worries. For one, the in-game HUD is ergonomic, looks pleasing and seems to be customisable, but I liked the default one well enough.Before we go on, I take issue with a couple of quirks. First, it's commendable that the game is so polished, otherwise, the lack of midlevel saves and reliance on a single campaign autosave would've caused all kinds of avoidable grief. Second, the asinine Nexus Point mechanic should be a togglable option. These things are akin to Bioshock's Vita Chambers or System Shock's Resurrection Bays, only unsuitable for a fast-paced shooter. Instead of dying, you teleport a few meters away after a sec, and that's all she wrote! Enemies stay dead after you respawn at full health, so you can outdie an encounter like Doctor Strange. Did it make me feel like a powerful wizard? Nah, more like a dirty cheater, even on Ultra Hard. I don't care how low the floor goes as long as the ceiling is high enough, and it would be high under a normal checkpoint system. With little to no incentive not to die besides the score a margin of people cares about, the Nexus Points system has lowered the stakes. This would've tanked a lesser game.Let's slip into something more comfortable. The levels appear outstanding, implementing a simplified design philosophy of Quake with its morphing compact spaces, surrealism, tight traps, verticality, and a reserved approach to map-making. Maps loop around neatly and, thanks to the lighting and an odd peculiarity in geometry here and there, the rooms are memorable, despite the repeated textures. I'd love to see more of the sparingly placed environmental hazards, which can be used against enemies - spectacular lasers, crushers, explosive barrels that REALLY bang. Yeah, Prodeus doesn't joke around when it comes to being bombastic, investing in fabulous dynamic lighting and voluminous particle effects. They've also nailed every facet of movement - from simple running speed to double-jumping, making the local platforming fluid, so climbing for secret nooks and participating in exciting weapon trials is pure joy.To create places so contained on the outside and so ripe for exploration on the inside is quite a feat! The game periodically allows you to see an odd level from a vantage point. As satisfying as looking at a Lego castle, a rather complex one, swarming with foes and locked doors hiding mouth-watering valuables. Every item here is chunky and instantly recognisable. From your standard pickups like keys, ammo, and health to meta-resources in the form of ore fragments and runes. Ore is used as a currency to buy weapons and upgrades while runes allow you to unlock more levels. New weapons and exploration upgrades like double jump are divided into several tiers, which you unlock one by one and eventually buy out in a semi-linear fashion. Was it worth creating a crude level hub to facilitate these gimmicks? Eh, while I'm not in awe of this fluff, it gets a pass for providing bonus incentives.Anyway, shooting is where it's at. Say, you have a starter pistol, which gets quickly replaced with dual-wielded SMGs, for them to soon get trashed in favour of a vastly superior Minigun. Weird. Where there could be 2-3 decent weapons with different ammunition, there's only one. And it happens to most guns! I adore the arsenal regardless, besides, with this gunplay and cool alt-fires, every piece whoops ass, making creatures erupt like gore-packed piñatas. Who the Hell refuses toys like a 4-barreled SSG or a chain-lightning sniper rail with an explosive kick? And boy, that Plasma is  Even better than in Doom 3. The low ammo cap enforces swapping them guns like crazy and I dig it, despite considering traditional ammo scarcity a better way. We get some resource management, but it's pretty mild. I realise that this technique is tricky to implement and not all people are as fond of it as I am, so I think they found a decent middle ground.And dotted the game's grounds with sizable enemy hordes, the bulk of which consists of Doom's zombies and imps, melee bat demons, acidic Caco-Overlords, power-armoured machine-gunners, toxic bucketheads, and the exploding Lost Souls who are even nastier than usual. Don't expect a lot more, the variety isn't great. But the sprites are delightfully beefy and, most importantly, Prodeus isn't another arena shooter. Akin to its revered ancestors, it doesn't feel segmented, for you explore without ceasing to fight. Foes are distributed across levels, creating that oldschool Doom flow where you always have something to kill, occasionally bunching or spawning in for big ambushes. During these massive shootouts, the roaring cacophony and the lack of distinct barks make it hard to read the room by the sound alone. It would be helpful, considering the constant stream of blinding gore hitting your eyes.Yet, the gore alone is worth getting lost in this game's bowels. As a whole, Prodeus stands up to the fierce competition. While not perfect, there are aspects of it I appreciate and even consider benchmarks... Oh crap! I completely forgot about the plot! All I can say about it is that no one forces the lore upon you or talks your ear off when you play. I planned to pay attention to it but got distracted by the spectacle the moment I started blasting. Once again, I have to emphasise how riveting said blasting is! So much so that I was able to let slip the whole Nexus Point fiasco when fully enjoying a massacre. Until another pathetic non-death spoiled the fun. Somewhat. The game is enjoyable enough to be vindicated of that unfortunate miss, but I hope the devs won't get complacent with their success and decide to give their players a choice instead.My curator
