_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Prodeus is the perfect blend of the retro 1990's FPS that we grew up loving, mixed w/ modern gaming innovations that we all have come to expect.  It's stunning visually, has a killer soundtrack, and is a love letter to the og Doom.  It's not perfect and could use a little more time in the oven, but has the potential to be one of the very best retro throwback shooters.*Notes:-I completed all of the early access content that is available as of September 2021.  It took me about 7 hrs to complete close to a dozen levels, find a couple of secret exits, and pick up one cool powerup for finding all of the secret exits.  What's Good:-I absolutely adore the way this game looks visually.  It really does look like the 1993 Doom made in 2021.  It's a gorgeous style of pixel art w/ full 3d models that looks so cool.  All of the weapons look badass and the blood splatter is over the top, just the way I like it.  I love the way it looks when you shotgun blast an enemy straight in the face and blood particles splatter everywhere.  -Andrew Hulshult has once again composed a perfect soundtrack for another stellar game.  At this point, you know what to expect when Andrew is the composer for a game.  It's going to be fast paced, badass, metal that rocks perfectly w/ the tempo of the game.  It fits perfectly w/ the tone and pacing of the game.-This is a really well polished early access title.  I experienced zero bugs, it always ran at 60 fps, and I never ran into a single glitch or fundamental problem.  All of the levels in early access feel complete.  There needs to be more content, but the content that is available right now, is really well polished and well designed.-The guns all feel great to use and look amazing.  They kind of look futuristic but feel realistic at the same time.  Every gun feels good to use and has a purpose.  The pistol can be zoomed in for a 3 shot semi auto.  The shotgun feels great even if the secondary shot isn't all that special.  Both the grenade launcher and rocket launcher look and feel great.  There is a plasma gun that locks on enemies and is probably my favorite gun so far.-There is a map select screen similar to Mario Bros that shows you which levels are available to play and which ones you haven't completed.  This is a small thing but it's a really nice choice by the devs.  There is also a map editor w/ tons of really unique and challenging maps.  They frequently have level making contests w/ prizes.  I think that this is a really smart decision by the devs as it adds tons of content to an already really great game.Could Use Some Changes:-My biggest gripe so far is the odd save system.  There are checkpoints scattered throughout the levels which is really common for a game in this genre.  However, what's not so common is that when you die, you respawn at the check point, and all of the enemies you killed before dying are still dead.  This really hurts the tension of the game.  There is no real loss upon dying.  The best games find a fine line between tension and frustration by placing checkpoints strategically throughout the levels and then punishing you for reckless play.  I'd like to see this fixed or at least another option available by the 1.0 launch.-The enemies look really cool, but they aren't very smart or tactical.  In fact, most of them just slowly walk towards you or stand in one place and shoot a projectile.  I'd love to see a bit more variety in enemy behavior as well as smarter AI.  Right now, even on the hardest difficulty, Prodeus is one of the easiest retro fps that I've played recently.-I'd love to see the dev takes a few more risks in the later levels w/ level design, enemy placement, and mix the environments up a bit.  This game is a blueprint on how to create a spiritual successor to the 1993 Doom, but it tend to play it pretty safe in most of the current levels.  I'd like to see a few bigger maps w/ more verticality involved.  That may not be the dev's vision, but I can certainly hope for it.Thoughts:-I really love what I've played so far.  This game has incredible potential, and I can't wait to see how it turns out.  Unfortunately, in it's current state, it's simply to too easy across the board.  I catch myself running forward and going guns blazing constantly b/c I'm never punished for reckless abandon.  However, this is a fairly straight forward fix, and I could see the final product being a perfect blend of challenge and excitement.Consensus:-Solid Game (Tier 3 and makes up 35% of my reviews).  For $25, you are getting an extremely well polished and well designed throwback shooter.  The dev just added coop and plans to add more content soon.  Now is as good a time as ever to pick it up Prodeus and enjoy every minute of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna talk about respawning, almost every single review already did. Enemies are pretty basic, but that's fine.  Enemies are not bullet sponges even on the highest difficulty, which is important for the flow of the game. Nothing kills the enjoyment of a shooter faster than needing too much time/bullets to kill basic enemies. The gore is perfect too, one of the best I've seen. You can shoot off parts of enemies, you can gib them and they explode their insides around the map. The graphics look very good for a retro-ish game, the low FPS reload animations are really clean looking. The games looks are recognizable and that is significant. Areas where you fight in are mostly industrial complexes from the future and few other dimension levels, pretty much like in DOOM. I enjoyed the rugged worn industrial buildings and bases, but the weird rock formations in the different dimension were boring. There are 2 levels where the developers are thanking patreons and supporters, which is very cool and I respect it, but they are intertwined with "normal" levels and it got me out of immersion crazy fast. Imagine getting credits scene midgame. Fists are completely useless and I think they are only in game to honor original boomer shooters that inspired this one.There is no "normal" assault rifle in the game. There is a plasma rifle that is really strong, but not fun to use in slightest, at least for me. There are 3 shotguns. Why? I don't know. One can fire an alternative charged shot that is very accurate, deals a lot of damage, can set enemies on fire and costs 1 ammo, so you pretty much have a sniper on you. There's the super shotgun which has 4 barrels and you can fire all 4 of them at the same time dealing huge amounts of damage close. Auto shotgun is almost exact copy of the Wolfenstein(new story line) shotgun, even having shrapnel shot and you can use it to clean up hordes of regular mobs. That said, you can just use shotguns for every type of enemy anywhere, no matter the difficulty. No need to use any other weapon unless you run out of bullets. There are even some levels where you can refill ammo. The Chaos Caster is a melting gun that is presented as more of a utility weapon than anything else. You get it almost at the end of the game and use it only on 1 level and that's that. They could have deleted the weapon and 3 obstacles you use it would have 0 impact on the game. Feels like an idea that wasn't work on at all. Double jump and dash being in shop is fine, but being locked behind tiers where you are forced to buy 2 weapons first, then double jump and dash feels bad. However, they are only used for secrets and help you preform better in fights. You can progress through the game without them. I know I gave a lot of criticism, however, I had fun playing this game and I would argue that for boomer shooters that is the most important thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus wants to be Doom 1, and absolutely succeeds. If you're into that, good. if you want anything else, then playing this game is like seeing your ex's instagram pictures. Marksman succeeds because it centers on an enemy, map features, and visual design that Doom 1 couldn't have. Prodeus' best moments come from where it is least like Doom, but it insists on being more Doom everywhere else.I'd still recommend it, nothing is "bad" about it, it's a huge accomplishment to do what they've done here, and anyone who likes sorts of things will love it. But be aware going in, you've already played this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus takes everything right about the entirety of 90s FPS games, including the community contributions, and wraps it in a neat little blood soaked package. The level editor is accessable and powerful. A newcomer can easily find their way. The gameplay is refined and smooth, it takes from the old and the new and despite an odd decision or two, like reloading (Which I personally like), it's practically seamless.The level design is top notch, DragonFly is on the team. The levels are creative and full of passion and play is extremely fun. The art style and direction is magnificent, I never knew retro graphics could look so stunning. The sprite work is an eyecatcher, being dynamically rendered by 3d models. And by God, The music by Andrew Hulshult is magnificent, undoubtedly his best work. A large part of the games charm is the interactivity between the devs and players. There's regular input between them and anyone who's interested in the game. The development is very much intertwined with community feedback. It feels like every day they're taking note of a suggestion or tweak.There's really not much bad I can say about the game, which feels odd. It's honestly kinda disturbing how hard it is to find something negative to say.But I'll definitely try:* Quicker implementation of options advertised early on (still waiting on changeable blood levels)* I would like to see more levels in diverse outdoor environments, even if it doesn't fit 100% with continuity. I wouldn't be surprised if they had that in store, specially since the level editor is seeing an influx of different textures. They're probably already on their way.* Not really a negative, but a level suggestion: Boats* Maybe make the music more dynamic, it can be a bit odd with transitions since a lot of early levels are relatively short.* The Big Red enemy type is uncharacteristically imposing for the amount of health he has, it can take one uncharged headshot from the shotgun to kill him. not a big deal, but I found it odd.* More frustrating traps, the extent of it is, "whoops this button actually traps you in the room and spawns a few enemies after a couple seconds." I know not everyone appreciates this aspect of 90s level design, but personally I love it. Annoy me, give me a cheap death.All in all a fantastic game. A definite recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Only played a couple levels, and I can see how fantastic of a boomer shooter this is except for one major flaw that, for me, ruins this game: you get unlimited respawns on death, and everything you killed remains dead. There's no death penalty, you just show up at the last accessed "Nexus" point and these are all over the place.  It's like playing an arcade game with infinite coins/credits - the ones like TMNT where a coin lets you continue from where you died. No challenge whatsoever.And then, from the opposite spectrum of bad game design, as there are no mid-mission saves of any kind, your progress is only saved in between levels, so don't bother launching the game unless you know you have enough time to finish the level, otherwise you'll lose all your progress (though I guess you could always just keep the game running until you have more time to play hours or whenever later).Graphics are great, gunplay is great, monsters gib pleasingly, but I just cannot recommend this game.  If they ever add the ability to quicksave, so that on death you can load your most recent quicksave and  instead of just respawning near where you left off, I'll gladly change my review to positive.Edit: I went ahead and beat the campaign. It ends on a nothing-note, with a text box pretty much telling you that nothing you did made any difference. OK. The good thing is that this final level had no checkpoints so it was actually a challenge, I had to dial the difficulty back down to Hard to beat it.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent retro-shooter that plays almost like a Doom 2016-themed DOOM 2 WAD. Classic FPS arsenal that feels great to shoot. Classic DOOM enemies. And some of the most amazing level design in a FPS, especially Prodeus dimension levels. Lots of influence from classic FPS games. Good campaign length and pacing.Looks great, feels great, what more do you want?What I enjoy the most about the old-school revival, especially Prodeus, is that the game does not force you into a resource-management mini-game where you have to do a little dance in every arena (Doom Eternal). Wanna shoot only shotgun? Go ahead. Upgrade the thing, get more ammo so you can shoot more. Have fun.Only minor gripes include slight performance issues even on a higher-end PC, and less challenging difficulty before harder modes (can be adjusted).Easy to recommend for a good old FPS experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Having fully completed the game now that it's out of early access, I can definitely say it's a great throwback shooter worth your time, but with some odd caveats that are worth mentioning beforehand.Pros:-Great weapon selection (most with meaningful alternate fire modes)-Good enemy variety.-Mostly good level design (with some levels being great).-Good/fitting music.-Good community level editing tools and level browser.Mixed:-Weapon balance is mostly good, but some weapons (pistol, regular shotgun) lack purpose later on, even when speedrunning. Also bullet based weapons are not well balanced (shredders are the only useful ones, and even then they are only useful to spread ammo usage if needed versus the shotguns/plasma rifle).-Game checkpoints don't respawn enemies; unless you are going for 100% game completion (all secret medals, kill medals, and deathless medals), then you can respawn freely with no penalty. Makes the game feel easy even if you are dying on the hardest difficulty due to a lack of penalty aside from the medal.Cons:-Game ends abruptly and like it was missing content. The world maps after the first are much shorter and missing similar content when compared to the rest of the game (for reasons noted below).-Weapon tutorials only exist for a portion of the weapons (only one of the shop weapons has a tutorial).-Weapon challenge levels also only exist for a portion of all weapons, (no weapon challenges for shop purchases, and some regular pickup weapons also don't have any).-Though there are two extra slots for melee and plasma weapons, there aren't any other melee weapons, and the plasma weapons (though they do exist and are fully implemented) don't actually appear in the campaign.-Though I don't care about the PvP, if you do, it is dead.Edit: Almost forgot, the screen shake is annoying and you can't turn it off.Overall a good game, but I wish the 3 world maps after the first had much more content developed for them, as it leaves the game a little short.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: This is what we've been looking for in terms of a modern take on the classic FPS (boomer shooter)!The game entered early access at the start of this month and already shows a TON of promise. The gameplay and polish for what's currently in-game rivals that of final releases of other comparable games.Pros: - this game looks good! Excellent mix of classic graphics/sprites with modern rendering and level geometry that sits somewhere in the middle.  - another Andrew Hulshult (Brutal Doom, Dusk, Quake Champions, Amid Evil, Doom Eternal: Ancient Gods) masterpiece! Excellent mix of heavy, metal, goodness and electronic beats.Level Editor - the in-game level editor is extremely capable and can be used by designers of all skill levels. The developers use the same editor to create the official levels, so you know it's powerful.Community - there is already a large community presence surrounding this game. Built-in community map browser. Tons of users in the official discord. Regular community map contests hosted by the developers. The devs have also been known to stream on Twitch when working on maps/bug fixes/community map reviews.Cons:None. There's a good amount of content included in the official early access release, and countless additional maps that are available via the community. If this is your kind of game, you will NOT run out of maps to play, especially if you are a completionist and want to find all the secrets and beat maps on the hardest difficulty options.Edit: After the official release, my positive review is even more solidified. We got more of the excellent gameplay and well-crafted levels. Achievements were not overly difficult but did range from quite easy to challenging. Some text in the game suggests there will be additional add-ons or episodes developed in the future, and I'm looking forward to it.

_childDocuments_.review: There's no shortage of "boomer shooters" on steam. And I've played more than a few of them. Like a lot of people, I got a kick out of Doom, Doom 2, Quake, Hexen and so on. I'm no stranger to the games that a lot of those are a love letter to.But this game, this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. It's like an exaggerated 90's commercial where some buff guy blows up the wall and then throws a floppy disc into a computer. Then bad 90's electricity effects start giving you a Jimmy Neutron brain blast."Buy me Prodeus or go to hell!"I was blown away by how much better this is then a lot of other games in the genre, I'm not very good explaining all the fancy technical details, I don't know if this game will raytrace your osculation coefficient on a polynomial or whatever, but the graphics are appealing and it runs like a dream. This is coming from someone with a glorified toaster.The guns are have (mostly) distinct roles, there might be a little bit of crossover, but they all serve a good function. And man, do they feel good to use. You have a clear idea of what enemies are all about. You might think that would be obvious, but I've played games where it seems like one enemy is using a hitscan attack, only to find out it was a completely different one. The levels have all been pretty distinctive, there were a few points where I felt a little confused, but I'm going to blame that on either alcohol, lack of sleep or just plain brain-rot on my end. Your results may vary.There's guts, gore, and glory, all kinds of fun alliterative stuff for you to sink your tubular teeth into.In short, if you like any of those classic shooters and you're on the fence, get off the fence, buy this. Full price, sale, doesn't matter. This is one game I am willing to endorse for a full price, and I'm a notorious cheapskate.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: Style: Retro style, the lighting and atmosphere is quite nice and sets a grim tone - with the added bonus of enemies' blood recoloring the walls and floors. Enemies can lose limbs and become visually damaged, it makes the combat feel like it has significant weight. A+Levels: Very classically inspired locations - lots of heavy industrial environments, dipping into some very Doom-esq levels at the end of the campaign. Solid stuff but other than a rather unique portion 2/3's in, you've probably seen this sort of thing before. B+Weapons: Wonderful, responsive, loud, an absolute blast to use; very lovely stuff - good lineup here. Most of the weapons have utility even until the very end of the game. A+++Enemies: Decent variety; they do different things and feel distinct to fight - although barring a couple of late-game surprises you run out of new enemy types halfway through the game. B+Music: Andrew Hulshult nailing the OST as always. The tracks alternate between rumbling, moody atmospheric tracks when there are no enemies to heavy riffs in the middle of combat. Only complaint is that the encounters set to the heavier stuff don't tend to last long enough to get into a good groove. A+Overall a very fun game, I highly recommend it to anyone interested in a retro shooter experience.

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as I saw early GIFs of the graphical style, I immediately Kickstarted this product. I have never regretted my decision. This is old school FPS, but with all the usability of a modern shooter. The graphical style has the look of sprite based enemies, however it is fully 3D. You can also choose to use that, or just standard 3D models. It looks great. and the framerate is sharp. The map style is very chunky, lots of solid metal structures, lots of heavy laval rock. There's really clever level design for secrets that reward exploration. Generally, it gives Doom vibes, but the enemies, lighting and VFX really shoot it up a notch. Weapons are nicely varied, from standard ballistics to energy weapons, something for every occasion and weapons have alt.fire modes to mix things up. The difficulty levels are great, but I personally recommend starting a little harder than you'd expect. I wound up finding Very Hard to be the sweetspot. Love the game, really happy with it!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty, with interesting set designs and things that happen in them. Respawn points are placed randomly throughout maps because the dev doesn't know how to properly supply the player with health and ammo at the right times/places while scaling enemy difficulty and placement, I think? Sure felt that way up to where I stopped, anyway. The whole game, once you stop collecting runes at the ends of levels, has no context or reason for why the character is where they are, or why they're even in the level if there's no rune there (but you still get a rune after finishing the level even though you never picked one up in that level, against previous levels where you did?) . Many of the objectives that come up after that point don't really explain themselves and you just have to guess at what the hell you need to do to go to the next unexplained area where you need to do something else you don't understand... Yeah, this game could really use some objective trackers a la borderlands, and a whole lot more context for quite a few levels... as well as a waypoint or even a mark on the impressive automap telling you where you need to go.As for the slander on the enemies and balancing.... If you play on Normal, you'll find that certain enemies have a lot more hp and do tons of damage, while others are tiny and do lots of damage, or have little hp and little damage. It's a little too simply done, oddly enough, and they seem to just be randomly placed and selected for the most part.... But, then the respawn points are there and it just... Confuses me. You get a Nexus Point when the dev feels like it- sometimes in arenas, sometimes not, sometimes before big fights, sometimes not. The same goes for health, armor, and ammo, it might be placed where the player might find themselves needing it, it might not.Then there's the death counter, ingame timer, and being able to rate the levels after you complete them, like there's some collectible or achivement or something, I don't really know... and this game has an overworld map and Trials, like a Crash Bandicoot or Donkey Kong game. There's a lot going on in this game, but not a lot of sense or direction to go with it. Hell, while I'm at it, there's three slots for "upgrades", but nothing ever gets brought up about that, and there's a counter for what looks like gold bars on the map screen, but, once again, no explanation of what that is or what it could do.

_childDocuments_.review: Update for full release, suffice to say Bounding Box has delivered.I didn't Kickstart this game, and this is the rare case where I regret it. Even in Early Access, Prodeus was a top-tier Boomer Shooter with some good old-fashioned gratifying gunplay. The chunky, earsplitting weapons are the star here, and can be used to blast a somewhat familiar enemy roster over every surface as you hop and careen around like a precise, frictionless angel of violence. The map design is an excellent blend of classic interconnected arenas with fun surprises scripted surprises and impressive sequences that feel more modern but never out of place. I would strongly recommend one of the harder two difficulties as the checkpoint system is fairly forgiving; these make every ammo and armor pickup feel like an actual reward instead of superfluous filling.The devs were definitely keeping some things close to the chest instead of overpromising; the new campaign is much chunkier and more varied than the original ~5 (updated to ~7) hour run; I'm not yet to the end of the new content but don't see myself slowing down on the ride there. The potent Hulshult soundtrack has been expanded and incorporated much more fluidly, blending in and out with combat instead of the more abrupt stops and starts earlier in development.The one actual weakspot is the enemies, which in addition to feeling lifted from a certain other demon-smashing series (aside from some late-game powerhouses) have pretty limited AI. They are still fun to annihilate en masse and can be truly overwhelming when the environments open up but these are not smart foes with huge libraries of varied attacks.Even before release the third-party mapping community was great, dropping awesome standalone levels with some cool scripted moments. With the expanded support of the full version I imagine they will give the game even more longevity, especially if new enemies and AI are added to the mix.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, Doom Eternal is nice and all... but have you played Prodeus?!If not, you should!The weapons feel great.The movement is fast and responsive.The level design has a great flow.Music and sound is just awesome and fits perfectly.And truckloads of blood.Haven't had a game in quiet a while that puts me in the zone as much as Prodeus.Currently the campaign is a little short, but it's fun to play them several times to find all secrets, get better, and maybe even get a good score for the leaderboard.Also there is a Mapeditor. Haven't looked into it for too long at the moment. But from a first glance it seems to be a way better version of the doom 2016 snap map editor. Played a hand full of player created maps already and they are great.The only, let's call it downside for the sake of the argument, is that there is no story at all. The campaign maps have a short description to give them at least a little bit of context, but that seems to be it.That's not bad in any way, since I'd rather start the game and jump into the action in literally a couple of seconds (the load times are godlike), than sitting through cutscenes and standing next to talking npcs... but I don't know... a little more context to the general lore of Prodeus would be a nice bonus. Maybe at a later stage of development, but if there will never be any more story I wouldn't shed a single tear.I see myself playing this game for a long time. There is currently no better old school shooter out there.Good work devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: So, in a sea of a bunch of shooters, which one stands out the most?I would say Ultrakill if you personally asked me. But does an old school type shooter really need to stand out from the rest of them to be good? I would say no to that.Prodeus is a unique game that uses elements from old school shooters and doesn't stray away from their roots with a twist. And this is a good thing.It's very similar to Ultimate Doom/Doom 2 and Quake, yet it feels a lot different from them too.If i could describe it easily, i would combine a few games that makes Prodeus a masterclass in the genre.It has movement and visual elements from Doom 2016, Map Design like Quake, Enemies like Original Doom, Weapons, Sound Effects and Gore like Brutal Doom.The game doesn't stop for a second in action, there is no chess game like in Doom Eternal, which is a brilliant game, obviously, you switch weapons, fire and repeat. So more action, less resource management.And don't let me start on the dynamic soundtrack the game uses. There is even a trailer just for the soundtrack alone how the Synths are used. I recommend watching. It's an eargasm.The OST is made by no other than the legendary Andrew Hulshult, and it's very different than the rest of his roaster. You know a soundtrack is good if your CPU nearly melted when making it. You can also download the free MIDI OST and use it In-Game or just listen to it via Steam.The combat is very visceral, you can shoot body parts like legs, arms, heads, torsos, etc. Enemies explode into blood mush.The art style is superb. It combines modern rendering with old school sprite elements and effects. You can set the game to Native, which is the default, and the Maps will look super clean, while the Weapons and Enemies will be rendered as sprites. Enemies can also be turned to be 3D. Weapons on the other hand are always sprites.Or you can use Rendering Emulation with either Pixel/Scanlines/CRT, both options look good.Weapons look noticeably better with Rendering Emulation turned On IMO.I personally prefer 360P, CRT with Slider set to 1.0 Emulation.Maps are big enough with multiple paths, secrets, etc. And you move your character through them via a Super Mario World or Super Mario Bros. 3 System. You gain runes, which you can spend to buy weapons, abilities, etc. Each map has a scoring system, and the difficulty can be ramped up to extreme.The game uses a checkpoint system that sadly does not reset enemies when you die.However if you find that annoying, you can just restart the level and play it again.I would argue that checkpoints are better than manual saves, because you have to act in a flight or fight scenario if something goes wrong. You can't save scum your way out of this other than using Nexus Stones, which act like checkpoints. If there was one fault to the game, the checkpoint system where enemies do not reset would be one of them.There is enough replayability just from the game alone. But that's not even the tip of the Iceberg.The game has a level editor and level downloader. Either singular levels or campaigns.Which means, it has almost endless replayability. There is also multiplayer packed in, and co-op for all maps.I HIGHLY recommend this game to any player on the verge of buying an old-school shooter with a new twist on the formula. Did i also mention the game has a bunch of weapons to use, each with alternate fire modes?No? Well, now i did. Because the game is packed full of interesting weapons to use. They do share similar tropes with other shooters, but they also stand out on their own.The game is easily worth the full price. An Indie game with such massive scale is not something you see every day, after all.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: While I'll point out my critiques quite extensively, I'd like to make one thing very clear from the get-go: If you are into these boomer-shooter types of games, just get this game. Get it now, and have a blast! This game features a very unique look, nicely blending old-school, pixelated graphics with modern effectswork and lighting. It fits this style of game perfectly in my opinion.Weapons do have a very satisfying “oomph” to them (sound-design-wise); everything you do from walking to jumping to shooting things just has some accustic weight to it, and it's awesome. Same can be said regarding the soundtrack. There's some sort of dynamic music here that switches from “idle/exploring/ambience” to “combat” whenever you encounter enemies in the levels. These tracks can get very intense, especially in the later levels, and it just fits the frantic combat of this game perfectly. That said, some tracks can get a bit repetitive though (especially in the earlier levels) and that makes them kinda annoying to listen to after a while.Movement in Prodeus feels tight and on-point, allowing for precise jumping, strafing, and moving around in the gameworld. There are advanced movement options later in the game (double-jumping, dashing), but these are optional upgrades that need to be purchased (which I don't think is a good idea since the game just plays better/faster with these advanced movement types available).Yes, there's a very basic “upgrade-system” in the game. There are shop-levels featured multiple times throughout the main campaign, offering upgrades (like the ones just mentioned) and new weapons in exchange for ore the player can find throughout the levels. These ores are mostly tied to secret-hunting, which makes exploring the maps rewarding and fun since it's not just health/armor/ammo pickups that you're able to find).However, I don't think this shopy-system is especially benefical to the game. Why not scatter your better weapons throughout the levels, maybe making them available earlier in hard-to-find secret areas? Additionally, I personally think this game feature too many weapons, especially considering the available guns in the shop, too. There are like 3 weapons on some of the weapon slots (e.g. slot 3: Shotgun → Super Shotgun →  Auto Shotgun), and once you've got the better variant there's basically no incentive to ever use the “base” weapon ever again since those other types are simply better. I didn't count, but it feels like there's somewhat like 20 weapons in the game, many of which feel redundant to others. Why not make fewer weapons, each with their very specific use-case? This would also save the “problem” of having not enough keys for switching between them quickly.While I'm at ranting about some minor stuff: I also don't like the world-map. There's a Super Mario World-esque world map where you have to move your player character from one level to the next. This... feels just odd? It basically just slows the game down through unnecessary menus and button clicking, especially keeping in mind there are basically no alternative routes to go (other than a few “challenge”-maps where you need to beat some time, running through the levels shooting targets with one specific gun the map is tailored around).One last critique maybe worth mentioning: Later levels somewhat feel uninspired, rushed maybe, both aesthatically as well as regarding the lack of difficulty-increase in comparison to some of the midpoint levels (which are arguably the high-point of Prodeus). Feels like the developers just weren't into it any more at some point.But enough with the nitpicking. As said in the beginning, this game feels in general very fun to play. There are lots of enemies to slaughter, a good amound of variety in enemy types (although very inspired by the original Doom from 93), and just very over-the-top gore effects that makes killing these enemies a joy, really. One very great thing that definitely is worth all the praise I can give the devs: Prodeus features an awesome community integration directly into the game, making user-created maps available from the main menu, vastly extending the content and scope of this game. And there are some incredible maps out there created by the community, so this is defintely worth checking out once you're done with the main game!Prodeus also comes with an easy-to-learn level editor, which plays right into this whole thing of community-created levels and campaigns. A very nice thing to see where modding and content generation for games is basically dead in the AAA-space. This is something more developers should integrate into their games!

_childDocuments_.review: We've gotten a bunch of good retro shooters in the last few years.  Prodeus is an interesting mixture of classic shooters.  It has sprite art in the style of Doom II but with modern shooter conventions.  Checkpoints, keep your arsenal when you die etc.  Its a nice sized, full featured game and feels good to play. There's only one serious flaw.  Dying simply respawns you right where you died with all the enemies you've killed still dead.  This is a massive problem as it basically completely neuters the difficulty and tension of the fights. It's no Ultrakill, Dusk or Amid Evil but it's easily one of the best retro shooters outside of those spectacular titles.  If the respawn and checkpoint system was fixed with a more coherent design it would be a can't miss.So, by all means, buy Prodeus, just know that this really baffling design choice means you simply can't get the same kind of challenge you'd get in other, better designed games.

_childDocuments_.review: A game the not so subtly draws from DOOM with just a hint of Quake 2 to it though in some ways it draws a little too much from DOOM that it loses some of it's own unique flair.Right off the bat, Prodeus hits the ground running with smooth and responsive controls and some really impressive level design. Much of the fun will be from fluidly ducking and weaving in and around enemy hordes dodging incoming projectiles in a kind of zen like trance that only the best kind of shooters can do. On the Map design side of things,  it's rare that you'll have that moment that some older shooters had where you simply get lost to poor sign posting or quite literal maze design ala Hexen: Beyond Heretic though you will occasionally have those "hunt the key card" moments where finding the yellow key for the yellow door can be a bit tedious.For enemies and weapons we have easy to understand guns, with easy to read enemies. You have your standard pistol/shotgun/machine gun/ rocket launcher/ fancy gun dichotomy here you'd expect with a few unique extras. The Quad Barreled shotgun is pure devastation in the palm of your hands, but sadly only appears late into the campaign to really appreciate. Others however feel completely redundant such as the twin machineguns that both require reloads and is fairly inaccurate. Which is a shame because said dual machine guns get completely outshined by the tried and true chain gun which has neither of those problems while also being more powerful. That's more a personal nitpick but otherwise guns shoot straight and hit hard, as a good fps gun should.Enemies however a little less inspired sadly, as many of them are almost 1 to 1 replicas of Dooms roster with only a handful of standouts. You've got your Imps, your possessed human soldiers, your Pinkies and Cacodemons. The interesting ones that Prodeus gives us are glowing blue monsters that infight with the basic monsters and also move faster and hit harder. Nothing really to mention about the enemy roster as they function as they should with no awkward hiccups in their aggression or behavior.The real selling point right now Prodeus as it is still an Early Access title is the custom made maps and levels by the community. This alone can potentially give even more value to the game as it's in production and the dev team finished up the main campaign and features. The map maker itself is really quite impressive and allows for all kinds of freedom in design so that has a lot of potential in the future as more people get familiar with it's capabilitiesAll in all, Prodeus is looking to be a promising game in the future and I can give it a solid recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Has played only a couple of hours of this, but already want to leave this here:The game is really great, but it took me a while to formulate what it feels like.  And then, one of the reviews called it "Brutal Doom", and I got it. It feels like a DOOM mod, in all the best ways. And not a "Cyberpunk RPG Horror total convesion" kind, but the "Demon Invasion 20: Now they're even stronger, somehow" kind.  It's a very simple experience, but the formula of it was improved for so long before this game, that it is foolproof. Not saying that it's easy to make such a game, not at all! Rather, it's just a practice of a venerable craft.Kind of in the same way as the eye is drawn to repeating curves and lines of celtic ornament, the brain revels in rushing from room to room to rip through zombies with red-hot stream from a bullet hose.TL;DR GO PLAY SHOOT HARD BLOOD RED CAVEMAN BRAIN CATHARSIS MODE ON

_childDocuments_.review: An homage to Quake II with elements of Doom sprinkled in, this game never quite reaches the heights of either, but is still able to grip you with enough boomer-shooter goodness to make a worthwhile experience. First of all, the game looks pretty damn great; it's a surprisingly accomplished mix of old-school sprites and modern rendering techniques that legitimately looks gorgeous. Lighting especially stands out and brings a missing depth to the old Quake-style graphics, projectiles lit the environments and even effects such as smoke, which is a particularly nice touch. That said, the art direction still doesn't manage to evoke the same kind of other-worldliness that Quake II did back in the day, for me at least.The weapon archetypes are not particularly innovative; you have your shotguns, automated machine guns, rocket launchers and plasma rifles, but thankfully they do feel absolutely great to use, the shotguns in particular. Enemy archetypes are not varied either, with three of them straight out of Doom and later enemies being just re-skinned versions, which is a bit disappointing. And while the art direction is not a show-stealer, the level design is pretty great. Levels are fun to explore, some have their own themes and gameplay loops they revolve around making them especially memorable and it's highly enjoyable to look for all the secrets.One other thing worth pointing out is that the game feels at odds with itself to an extent. On the one side, it's a boomer shooter of yore, on the other it has stuff like a sprint button (but thankfully you can enable auto-sprint), ADS and a shop you buy weapons and items from (with currency you pick up along the way, usually from finding secrets), all of which are modern shooter things mostly. You can choose to ignore them (except for the shop obviously) and play it like a boomer shooter through and through, which is recommended, but it still feels a bit jarring. Weapon alternate fire can be included here as well, though some of them are actually pretty cool. It's just that you don't really get combat set pieces tailored for them, since those set-pieces are something that you'd mostly find in more modern shooters, but some secrets do require them.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: EARLY ACCESS SUMMARY: Prodeus is a polished, unrependant Doomlike that captures the old flavor of early FPSes with modern touches.  Excellent sound, good stylized graphics, old school bizarre environments, a nice set of useful weapons deliver the fun.    Though the style sometimes leans too heavy on grays and brown, the game is extremely solid - and its not a mindless shooter, you have to think.  This is a bloody good way to scratch that Doom itchA note: Though a well polished Early Access game, all the content is not yet here.Prodeus is one of those games completely clear on what it's doing: It's a deliberate Doomlike straddling the line between the original inspiration and more modern ideas, and doing it surprisingly well.  An extremely solid creation that stands out for working hard to get the feel rightSo basically run around and shoot stuff.  Let's break it down.THE WEAPONS: There's a variety of weapons, many of which have multiple fire modes, and each has its own use - even the basic pistol is useful.  Weapons have excellent sound and a "solid" feel to them.  Weapon select is a bit clunky, because there a lot of them, but you can map hotkeys.THE ENVIRONMENTS: Environments range from labs to fortresses to monuments and more, and none are boring, while a few are spectacular and even beautiful.  There are plenty of hidden secrets, as well as some challenge levels.  As you play more complex environments are unlocked.THE ENEMIES: A mixed bag.  Enemies come in quite a variety, but many designs aren't that visually interesting.  However, they're not to be trifled with, and each takes its own strategy.THE GRAPHICS: Overall good graphics, and they manage to balance modern and retro aesthetics that give the game a unique look.  There are some irritating uses of darkness and an overeliance on browns and grays, even in enemy design.  It's strange to say a Doomlike needs to be brightened up but there you go.THE SOUND: Excellent.   You can feel the weapon noises, major battles invoke a grindy metal soundtrack, and everything just sounds good.  The sound actually enhances the game.THE GAMEPLAY: Good to excellent.  You really have to think about how you use weapons and ammo.  Environment is important to survival.  There is an over-reliance on "sudden onslaught of enemies" that is annoying, but doesn't spoil the game.EARLY ACCESS: The game doesn't feel early access - and having played Alpha, it was polished even then.  The game is already very good, and the devs are willing to patch fast and take feedback.  Two warnings: the game is not yet complete, and some earlier levels and enemy strategies are really not that interesting and need polish.So overall, Prodeus delivers exactly what it said it would and does it well.  So who's it for?* If you want a Doomlike, here you go.  It's extremely like Doom and does what it does well.* If you like FPSes and want something back to the not-quite-mindless shooting without plot or anything else getting in the way.* As a gift for a fan of FPSes and Doomlikes, i'ts great.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: This game came as a surprise to me; a less graphically-intensive version of Doom 2016 & Doom Eternal. It also proves that one does not need such accoutrements to make a thoroughly enjoyable experience. Prodeus was equally as fun, IMO. Give a boy a game and he'll go to the moon and back.The levels are well-designed and easy to understand, which I feel ought to be the case with a retro shooter like Prodeus. There was hardly any need to go back and forth, nor are there any complicated puzzles to solve. Simply mindless gibbings upon mindless gibbings, just the way I like it.The weapons selection was interesting, as are the types of enemies one comes across. I note with interest the presence of a level editor, which to my knowledge is the first time I've come across a retro shooter game with one. I didn't use it, as I prefer to leave it to the good graces of other players to do so.All in all, a good game. I look forward to any future titles or releases from Bounding Box Software Inc.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game, both graphics and gameplay-wise. _childDocuments_.review: Played for less than an hour. Amazing classic FPS in all the critical aspects except for one. I did not like that dying would respawn the player but not the enemies. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic mix of classic Doom and Doom 2016 that stays fun to the very end. The gameplay is tight and every weapon feels like it has a place even though you end up having multiple occupy the same slot. The levels are the perfect length to make them feel like constant action with no real downtime on them. They remind me of the Doom WADs that have come out more recently and taken advantage of level design evolving. You never feel like you are just key hunting as the levels have a natural way to lead you back to where the key will be used. The ending would be my only complaint, as it ends on a really weird note (not a turn of phrase here, it actually pops up a note for you to read), but I can get over it as there was quite a bit of game before that. Hopefully they make some levels so it feels a bit more natural of an ending.

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is definitely a love letter to the era of games that defined my xennial generation. If you're a fan of the classic run-and-gun of DooM '93 and its successors, you'll love Prodeus. It has it's own style that plays very well and offers difficulties for all levels of gamer. it's got some modern game play elements without being overly complex. Definitely worth the price of admission, even at the full ask, a sale just makes it that much sweeter. As a bonus, they even shipped it with a level editor and a full swath of multiplayer options.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: So far this game has been well worth the wait. Super tight controls, great enemy audio/visual ques, bumpin' dynamic soundtrack, STUNNING lighting/colorful environments, smooth smooth smooth flow/animation, interesting and well thought-out level design; an absolute blast.  Not the most challenging game on earth. I stared on Medium to be safe, then almost immediately bumped it up to hard, with still few deaths per level so far. There are more difficult settings still beyond this one, though.  This means that it's pretty accessable to people who are less familiar with Old-School FPS tropes, but engaging enough to keep the full attention of OS-FPS vets (especially once you start messing with stylistic/acrobatic movement during arena fights). My only real gripe so far is that navigating the level map is a bit clunky. The map itself is unbelievably detailed and stunning; almost excessively so, actually. With maps this meticulous, it's a shame that navigating it can be more of a chore than I would like. If that was a bit smoother, it would even stand to give some Metroidvania maps a run for their money. Overall, this game has been a blast so far. Combat is blistering and punchy, the level designs are compelling without being overly confusing, and to say that it's easy on the eyes would be criminally understating things. Would highly recommend this bad Larry to anyone with bones and/or eyeballs.

_childDocuments_.review: Having taken part of the alpha playtest, I immediately knew I had to buy this game when it came out. If you are a fan of old school shooters like DOOM, pick this game up. This game has a great blend of modern and classic visuals combined with the visceral gameplay you are used to. Lots of blood. There are also options to turn on 3D models vs sprites if you so choose, but I think the sprites fit better with this game. The guns are satisfying to shoot and plenty of secrets to discover within each level. The heavy metal music keeps you engaged throughout the entire playthrough. The level editor/workshop only boosts the replay value of this game. At $25 it might seem like a lot, but this quality is rare and worth the value.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wonderfully done. A recreation of sorts of the original Doom for DOS and Quake 2 combined into a fast slaughter/shooter. If Doom was remade today, it would be this, not Doom Eternal. It runs perfectly fine on max/4K on PC and macOS/M1 but even better if you have a dedicated GPU. I don't recommend it, I double dare ya. _childDocuments_.review: Don't buy this game until they fix the respawn mechanic. It is downright horrible and after getting 50% through the campaign and 100% secrets I can say that the core gameplay is fun but completely overshadowed by the respawn mechanics. When you die, the enemies do not get reset and you respawn at a checkpoint. Why is this bad and unfun?  - Enemies can spawn camp you - The game becomes unchallenging - Negative satisfaction from beating an arena - Unorthodox in a very uncomfortable wayOnce again, if you enjoy boomer shooters and arena shooters, the respawn mechanic will drive you up the wall. _childDocuments_.review: I'd imagine if you mixed doom 1/2 with 2020-21 gameplay mechanics, lighting and a whole bunch of new, challenging and interesting levels, this is what you'd get. enemy and gameplay-wise, it's phenomenal. Offers versatile scenarios, unique enemies, and on higher difficulties one hell of a challenge. The experience is on-par with driving your first car where you have no idea what you're doing. You start getting cocky after a while and ramp up the difficulty, thinking you've got the whole world of shooter games in your hand, just to get assblasted and wiped off the face of earth by shotgunners, imps, and running out of rifle ammo.The soundtrack is on-spot, perfectly balanced with the game, offering intense music for the most intense of historical fights, like when you try to pick off that one imp that has the high ground over you, and you just can't seem to reach. there's generally only one thing i wanted to address, being the face on the hud. I think adding the face wasn't a bad idea, although having the character unrevealed does add a pint of mystery to the game. Who's the psychopath running around, shooting through hordes and waves of demons, slaying the most colossal of demon barons, just to stupidly fall into a whimsy lava puddle and die?I generally really recommend the game, since it offers a fantastic experience for people that are into fast-ish paced retro-like shooters. Definitely give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant gun-play. great feedback on the kills which makes you keep playing for hours.  Amazing graphics and art-style.  Took just the right inspirations from the sprite based fps games.  Music is great too, looming and dark.  Not a negative per say but I would have loved this to be a fast paced arena shooter like doom. right now it s technically an arena shooter but there is no urge to keep moving for life preservation.   You can defeat hard enemies with patience. That should not be a feature in arena shooter in my honest opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun, awesome art-style, absolutely EXCELLENT sound effects. So very very chunky and splatty. Love it.I also very much appreciate the "very easy" difficulty setting as I hate hard games. I just want to power through being almost invincible, and this game is perfect for it. _childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is a boomer shooter if the tech was way more advanced at the time.  Yes, this is positive.The Story:You are a corrupted enforcer of the Prodeus dimension, a world of strict order to the point it alters physics to try and achieve that order.  You are the direct opponent of the world of chaos.  Somehow, you -the enforcer- got inexplicably corrupted on a deployment.  However, you still maintain your initially "programmed" purpose- to collect the Prodean (?) runes that mortals have stockpiled and attempted to study, protected deep inside impossible heavy-metal structures.  Everyone hates you.  Prodeus considers you chaos. Chaos considers you Prodean.  Both sides will instantly attack each other on sight, then drop what they're doing to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mutilate you when they realize you're there.  Your programming will not let you stop collecting, nor protecting, the unobtanium both of them want. Therefore:They could leave you alone.They could fight among themselves while you go about your business.They don't.Because they consistently target you, and get your attention, "Get out of my way. I'm doing the job I was given, if my boss approves it or not."Draw curtain, start act 1.Gameplay:You run around. You shoot things with weapons of varying types, effectiveness, and performance, such as a charging DOT shotgun or a gun which arcs electricity from the first enemy into numerous others like an explosion and has a secondary fire that's literally a railgun with headshot bonuses.  At time of writing, only half the guns are actually in the game, yet feels more differentiated and complete than a modern shooter.You swap guns for efficiency in overall ammo supply- IE- one shotgun blast and a railgun round to ensure 1 high-end enemies death, then swap to the minigun for a trash horde, then back to the shotgun to land the hit for another railgun finish. This can be done so fast you won't even realize  have done it until the only movement is giblets sloppily dripping from the ceiling, which yes, they have as an effect.You do this shooting and killing in some really varied environments. While most are industrial, each one actually serves some kind of inherent purpose and sticks to that ideal- there's a reactor you have to reactivate with toxins around, a crash sight that has significantly screwed up spaceship sections you have to fight through with mechanical hazards, even a church with gigantic rotating pylons to stir up the toxic and health-draining black sludge that is completely unexplained outside of theory and player assumption as to what it does.  Each place is it's own "thing," explained to the bare minimum before you're cut loose with your arsenal and "try not to die!"It's fast, it's brutal, it has locational dismemberment and damage to reward your headshots, and it doesn't forgive you if you screw up.  Secrets are suitably tricky but "why the hell didn't I notice that before?", and there's even a super secret that involves finding 3 secret exits in 3 different levels in just this current build. These secret exits lead to a different portion of a secret level with a secret power up, and each one must be access to "unlock" that power-up. They only give you hints as to where those exits are, by being in the secret area. Yeah, they went there.Setpieces are crazy. Like, you would only see them in cutscenes kind of crazy, but most of the time you're in active gameplay.  Some of them are even level-defining.  In the  you instigate a combination of Half-Life 1's opening, and the end of halo 3, because "I push this button? I guess?" and then proceed after you break the space-time continuum.  In another level called Marksmen, there is a force-fielded tower in the distance full of railgun snipers that you can't kill. You are constantly running around the outskirts, biting your lip at the charge-up sound, while you kill things in the shadows until you reach the tower and turn every single one of them into chunky salsa.  The level doesn't even end there, requiring an arena fight and a subway car crawl before you can even exit On a technical level, it pulls some stuff I'm legit not sure other newer games could actually manage, nor be willing to. As an example, sprites on old games used views from about 8 different angles to show where the enemy was facing, but they were never fully 3d. Just those 8 angles to show some facing and "fake it." Their corpse sprites were all the same, from 1 angle.  In this game, it's like it was a technical achievement 20 years ago, without 3d graphics. The game manages to do it from those original angles, but in addition, does all those angles from birds eye and worms eye view. This is in addition to locational dismemberment of every single individual limb (torso and head counts), including non-humanoid enemies with weird anatomy.  If you understand how much would go into this, for every single sprite including weapons,
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: I had a short go at this game and enjoyed the gameplay itself - but now I discover that the game can only be saved between levels.There is a 'respawn' checkpoint system which works but is not fun. (I greatly prefer manual saves, but even as a checkpoint system this one is not well thought out). But if you need to quit the game to do something else you have to start the entire level again. This is incredibly dumb and very frustrating for someone who is always on-call and has a kid.  Why should I sit down and play this when I could lose all my progress at any point?If the game saved your progress in a level when you quit, I'd recommend this from my limited game play so far. If you don't care that you're forced to keep playing until you're finished a level, then you'll probably enjoy.As it is I'm considering refunding because my life simply does not give me any guaranteed gaming time, and I don't want to have to start a level again every time 'real life' happens while I'm playing. It's an incredibly disappointing decision. If they fix it I'll change my review. In the mean time, I'm going back to a game that actually respects my time.

_childDocuments_.review: I spent nearly 200 hours in the beta playing around with the map editor and discovering community levels to my delight. The amount of community content that already exists for being a newly released early access game is really really good. Unlike most retro shooters, the editing tools are used within the game which makes it friendlier for new mappers to get into, no need to install third party map builders and figure out how to configure it to work for an engine in the 90s. This is a true successor to bring this up to speed in 2020. (wait for OBJ import/export!!!) I am thoroughly excited to see what the community comes up with, I've already seen some OG doom mappers create maps for Prodeus.

_childDocuments_.review: Prodeus is extremely disappointing. The game did have potential it seemed, back when it started early access, but it feels like very little progress has been made since the initial campaign update. The game is in nearly the same state as it was then including the various issues mentioned by many players which went ignored by the developers.I question why Prodeus was chosen for early access in the first place. Early access is meant to allow player feedback to guide development some and to better shape the game by catching early bugs and providing crucial feedback. It would seem that the developers really wanted no part of that process. Many criticisms made by players have gone completely unaddressed since early access started. Worse yet, the developers have issued bans to some criticizing the game's lacking AI, broken checkpoint system and even the simple accessibility option of being able to toggle the nauseating vignette. Rather than even issuing a statment of any kind, the developers chose to stick their heads in the sand and ban critics, both on the forums here and on twitter, that were just too vocal for their tastes.The current levels that are included in the campaign now are quite well designed. The AI being so underwhelming that challenge is negated, but the level design does as much as it can to mitigate this. The problem is that the campaign has been relatively unchanged for many months and rather than add new content themselves the developers continually spammed mapping contests to use the community to do their job for them while successfully drumming up undeserved hype.Overall this game is a perfect example of how not to do early access. The developers ignored as much as they could here, on various social media platforms, and even on their own discord. Censoring criticisms by players who at one time were very enthusiastic for the product is a great way to make an underwhelming game and trash your community's good will and your own reputation.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel compelled to write a negative review for the first time because this game could have been so great, but is ultimately such a let down.  I'm really just going to be echoing the sentiments that some have already voiced, but I might as well do it so that the message is clear.  The Nexus checkpoint system absolutely RUINS this game.  I feel like I'm playing it with cheats on by default, as the player effectively has infinite HP the moment they interact with a checkpoint.  I'm left scratching my head over the fact that difficulty options even exist, the challenge is the same no matter which one you pick.Pretty much everything about Prodeus is excellent, it's just that there are no stakes, there is no tension.  Unfortunately I don't think this issue will ever be fixed as the Devs have, to my knowledge, never publicly addressed this despite there being complaints from the community since early access began. The only proposed band-aid for this problem that I have seen is to reset the mission on death and create an all or nothing scenario. While I would enjoy getting flawless clears on every mission at some point, that sounds like a miserable experience for a first playthrough.  Ideally, it would be great to have a healthy bit of challenge while learning the ins and outs during my first run through the game.I'm just gonna start rambling if I keep writing so I guess the TL;DR is: the checkpoints suck and make you immortal as opposed resetting your progress back to when you found them and it robs the game of any challenge unless for whatever reason you intend to do a flawless first playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: So its a boomer shooter, that means it brings both the bang and the funk right? Its gotta be as good as Dusk, Ion Fury, Cultic and Turbo Overkill right? Like those other seminal titles its got to have a strong mission statement that it sticks to and really delivers on right?Nope. Its close! Its getting there! but its not quite there yet!So Prodeus aspires to be Doom 2.5 in weapons and roster, but at the same time, its level design is cribbed mostly from Doom 3 and Doom 4. IE: its mostly blue grey tech base levels, or red/orange pg7 "chaos" levels. Theres not a lot of color contrast from scene to scene, theres not a lot of spacial variation, your either corridor crawling or in arena areas slightly bigger than a basket ball court. The levels get much better over time, eventually they become legitimately interesting and they do open up a little, but your not getting something like a Mt. Erebus level and your not getting a lot of opportunities to allow for player intuition early game.Prodeus has an abundance of weapons, every one of which feels pretty okay. Early game weapons hold up into the late game, and this is a mark of good craftsmanship. The pistol in particular I felt was not to little, and not to much. Its really well balanced, especially when compared to other boomer shooters that are running into the territory of slowly turning their pistols into mini BFGs lol. Similarly Prodeus really compelled me to use and enjoy both shotgun and super shotguns respectively, which few other titles have done. The absence of a BFG is unfortunate. That certain weapons and perks have to be shop bought rather than acquired mid game play is unfortunate.The monster roster is thin, both in type and in map placement. 95 percent of the monsters are aped from Doom with Prodeus' equivalent of the Doom 3 imp especially begging for an infringement suit. The monster placement in a room is less relevant as after clearing a room, additional enemies will be "warped" in. A gimmick that is best used sparingly but often isn't. I appreciate that the game mixes in monster closets and warped in enemies, but id like it to lean far far heavier on monster closets than it presently does.Similarly the monster count per level is pretty low. You'll feel like you have a lot of weapons that are good at shredding enemies en masse, but its pretty hard to utilize a choke point when you are almost never engaging more than 8 enemies at a time. I feel like if there were even as few as ten set piece fights where Mr Rocket Launcher or Mr Chaingun got to reach out and touch people until their full ammunition pools ran dry, it would bump my impression of this game from a not recommend to a recommend.The final battle is odd and doesn't really feel very climactic. If they aped a wide open map like Tower of Babel, or less preferably Dis it would have connected better. The penultimate level by comparison immediately prior was fantastic.We're a little light on soundtrack, what is there is good, but theres not a lot of it.As far as graphics go, let alone graphics in relation to the games file size. Prodeus is truly a stunning, beautiful game. You would never guess by looking at it that its 1.3 gigs, and while id up the color contrast in a few places, the ice world levels and the out door rain levels look absolutely fantastic. The monsters for what little time they will appear on your screen before splattering, they also genuinely look great too. I feel like a lot of this can be made to come together and that there is a great game in progress here, I look forward to changing my review of it in the future as content and polish is added.

_childDocuments_.review: Very Doom 2016. Maybe a little too Doom-like at times, but it definitely has its own identity, particularly later in the game.It can be a bit too easy early on, because you mainly face the Chaos enemies, which are easy. The Prodeus enemies are much harder, but the game never gets too difficult. Earlier levels tend to be samey in appearance early on, but this also opens up later in the game.The game performs very well and has plenty of good options. You can select sprites or models for enemies, which is really cool. You can even change your player characters colors, which is reflected in the hands on gun sprites.Weapon selection also gets more unique later into the game. Otherwise, it's a standard Doom arsenal. You have your shotgun, SSG, rapid fire rifles, chaingun, plasma rifle, and rocket launcher, but with a few "upgraded" versions of some of these weapons, as well as a few more unique chaos-themed weapons.Lots of fun here and little to complain about.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels more like Doom than Doom Eternal does. Now don't get me wrong, Doom Eternal is a great game, but when you've played Doom since the 90s, this captures the spirit of Doom a lot better than Eternal did.Prodeus feels like it could have been Doom 3, as in, the place it could take in the franchise. The enemies move and feel a lot like improved versions of the Doom and Doom 2 enemies, the music feels like it goes from atmospheric like Quake to action like Doom and the gameplay has a nice blend of retro and modern.There's really not much to complain about Prodeus as a game except for a few things, the biggest complain I think most fans have had since the beginning is the checkpoint system that doesn't work like a checkpoint system. This game plays so much like a boomer-shooter that it feels like it should have a proper quick save and quick load system but instead has a checkpoint system that doesn't work like a checkpoint system, it's more like Bioshock's Vita Chamber, so all the enemies you killed remain killed and all the damage you made also remains. I didn't like that mechanic on Bioshock because it felt cheap, but I feel like Bioshock could get away with it as it worked well with the story and the world of Rapture, but in Prodeus, it just doesn't work at all, it really is one of the worst elements of the game and often I prefer to restart the whole level instead of continuing from the latest checkpoint.Another element of the game that could have some work is the enemy AI, like I said, for the most part the AI feels just smarter than Doom in the 90s, which can be fun for this type of game, but I found myself standing right behind enemies that didn't notice I was there at all and all the enemies just stand there on idle animations waiting for you to pop up in their visions to start attacking. I think it would have been better for the game if the enemies had more of an AI and were patrolling some areas for the zombie and soldier types and for the monsters just have them spawn but not just stand there. There's an area where it just looks goofy because you have the Skull Fish which is like the Lost Soul of the game and it's just floating in the air and you can see them through a window, just floating in place waiting for you to get in front of them to attack.Besides that, there's really not much to complain about that can't be attributed to personal preference. I liked the "Mario World" inspired map to access the levels, the guns are great and the upgrades for the player are great too. Prodeus is also one of the most satisfying games when it comes to carnage as killing enemies is like popping blood balloons and the soundtrack is fantastic, so if you like boomer-shooters, this one is up there among the best and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I watched a review about this game the other day titled "I'm Not Mad, I'm Just Disappointed" and that single sentence sums up my feelings about this game very well. It's one of those titles for which I'd really wish there was something in between recommending the game or not recommending it.Prodeus does a lot right, and somehow, that's just not enough.What does it do right? Well, the graphics are straight up brilliant. If the screenshots look like it's a style you'd like, there's going to be a lot for you here.The weapon roaster is also fun and varied. I especially enjoyed the fact that there are secondary fire modes on all the guns. And the gunplay and combat is fun and gorey. Again, all great so far. The music was a bit of a disappointment, it feels a bit like when mom says that we still have Doom 2016 OST at home...But it's also not bad, strictly speaking. Just more on the functional side.So why not recommend it then? Well, Prodeus sadly has a really hard time to stand out beyond the initial impression.If you've seen the trailer you've likely seen all the game has to offer. A slick, decent shooter.And then you've finished the first few levels, and it's still just that, decent. And then, after 6 hours you start to wonder when decent stops and the interesting levels begin. Or the hard ones. Or the ones with some fresh ideas.And then, another 5 hours later, you complete the last level. And it's just yet another level. No boss, no extra challenge, just another okay level and suddenly you've completed the game.I was honestly surprised and looked around whether I might have missed something. But no. A game like this doesn't need much of a story, but I found myself wanting one just to give at least some justification for what I was doing. Something to tie a finishing bow around my actions to kind of close the whole thing up.Or a climax, a final struggle to bookend the experience. But, alas, it's just kinda over.For some this would be the point where they'd jump into the user made maps. For me, after having played 10 or so hours of killing the same bunch of enemies in the same (admittedly often well designed) levels, I just wanted something else.And here's the crux of it. Price point aside, for some this might just be a good deal. A decent shooter, which doesn't reinvent the wheel, yet has about 10 hours worth of alright levels and good graphics to boot (+ possibly some good user maps, though I don't know).But I wanted them to do something with it. Something that stood out. Between hour 2 of the game and hour 10 you will be doing the exact same thing. Same enemies, same kinds of levels, same guns (though they're dolled out a bit more slowly).And then nothing more.If you're thirsting for a retro inspired shooter but can't bear the thought of playing OG Doom (or Brutal Doom) then this is for you.However, I've played too many games in the genre to find anything fresh here, aside from the really good graphics. And that alone won't make this worthwhile.

_childDocuments_.review: is good, not great.While I'm glad I helped kickstart it there are a certain number of issues with it that severely dampened the experience. The main one being the checkpoint system that you've probably seen mentioned a lot in relation to this game. It trivializes the entire difficulty as it simply respawns you from the nearest checkpoint instead of resetting the world state and letting you replay a fight that you lost. There's no penalty (or learning moment) as you can simply continue the fight with renewed health even! The fact that some arena fights seem to have been designed with this botched system in mind make it even more egregious and disappointing. I finished the game on Ultra Hard, something which should have been challenging but unfortunately wasn't in the slightest. Even more so as the player gains access to multiple movement upgrades that makes combat in general a lot easier as well.Another area where Prodeus felt lacking was in enemy variety. Later on in the game you're put up against a new faction which consists of the same enemy types you've fought before only this time they are a different colour and have slight modified behaviour. While the shooting is satisyfing it does get a bit samey going through the exact same set-ups of baddies over and over again. Speaking of shooting: be prepared to spend a whole lot of time reloading your weapons, something which can be extremely annoying during combat. This has been mentioned elsewhere but one solution would have been to let weapons auto-reload once they've been unused for a while. Either that or just take the reloading out altogether as it's more cumbersome than it incentivizes weapon variety. There's also a bunch of QoL issues such as not being able to simply level select from a campaign menu, not being able to teleport to previous Nexus points in a map or not having all your collectible stats available during gameplay. All of this adding up make the game feel more "meh" during the later parts. All that said I do still recommend . When everything clicks it feels like you're playing DOOM Eternal in 1995 (which is great!). The artstyle looks fantastic and easily combines old-school aesthetics with modern effects resulting in striking visuals. The level design is the real star of the show in my opinion. Some of the maps are really clever (and outright transform around you) and most have an excellent flow to them as well. I also really appreciate the fact that the game rewards player exploration by offering up plenty of collectibles that can be found in hidden areas throughout. Hunting down every secret location was probably the thing I enjoyed most about it. So if you're desperate for another boomer shooter then  is a solid get. I would, however, wait for a sale instead of grabbing it for its full price.It's a fun time but ultimately I feel games such as , , , , and plenty of others will be remembered much more fondly in comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: Typical example of these "oldschool FPS" that keep popping up as of late. It's not bad by any stretch, the music is good, gameplay is solid, level design is fine, but the game has no originality and doesn't really have anything that can make it stand out among the rest. If Brutal Doom doesn't scratch the itch anymore and none of the other "oldschool FPS" strike your fancy, then sure, give it a try, but you're not missing out on anything if you skip it.
_childDocuments_.name: Prodeus

_childDocuments_.review: I have a bunch of smallish issues with the game, but the worst thing for me is the graphics, particularly the astounding amount of visual clutter for a retro shooter. There doesn't seem to be any way to tone it down, the sprites and animations don't really do it for me. The highlighted red/green/yellow/blue pickups are particularly gaudy to me but I guess the visual style is such that the highlight is required for them to be visible.All that said, YMMV, the trailer is a pretty good indicator of how it looks. I thought I might feel better about it in-game but I was wrong. If the trailer looks good to you then go for it.
