_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I can recommend this game.  Or at least not without caveats.  The art is well done.  The comic book style works well.  But the writing is uneven.  It has typos and mistakes including things like mixing up which line goes with which character (the color tells you who said it, but they mess it up sometimes).  But more than that, the writing is just confusing sometimes.  Some of that may be translation difficulties, but sometimes it feels like the explanation or context needed to understand the character's words or actions is just missing.  All in all, the story is also kind of uneven, too, but it was pretty interesting and I enjoyed most of it.I didn't like how this game which is predominantly point and click and heavily story driven with puzzles suddenly switched to reflex-based arcade mini-games.  They were not the type of game play I was looking for.I'm not really sure how to summarize this game.  Maybe I'd just say that it's not bad, but with a bit more work maybe it could have lived up to the potential of its story's premise and been really good?  As it was, its various flaws mean I don't regret playing it, but I'm glad I'm done with it.Also: The game's mature content warning mentions the attempted rape, but the game was more violent than I was expecting.  So just be warned if that's not your thing.

_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like writing bad reviews of Indie games, but I believe it's necessary. I don't recommend the game, unless you want to help the studio.Everyone with two seeing eyes agree that the art is great. Period. Unfortunately for this game, the "good" ends here.I've been playing lots of these visual novels, story-driven games, so when I say there's not much to play it's because there's not. It's just too linear and things happen too fast. It also falls short on character development, where few are introduced just to make the plot move forward before they disappear (until they're needed again twice down the road). There's not much about them besides their role: the cop, the shop owner, the big bad villain, etc etc. The gameplay is what you expect in this kind of game, although too simple (4 or 5 events at most per act) with lots of needless backtracking. To illustrate, on one event we have to (i) talk to a guy; (ii) go to a building; (iii) when you arrive there you realise you need the guy; (iv) go back to the guy; (v) go back to the building. Nothing happens in between: it's just clicking one screen after another. Another thing that annoyed me is that early in the game you read an e-mail that hints about a secret key to open a room. I searched everywhere and couldn't find it (tbh maybe this one's on me, but I'm not sure). There were also some annoying bugs, but nothing TOO bad.The story, well.. It has a good setting, but feels rushed, and .There is potential here and I hope this game helps the studio to deliver a better project in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: The plot and writing, dark art style, and strong main character carry this adventure game well over the top.  Wish it was longer, but it told its story well.  Drawbacks are some slight glitches/interface hiccups remain, objectives are not always clearly suggested, and near the beginning the open map leaves you wandering lost through the world.  Did I mention the dark gothic art, which I think was buy the darkest dungeon artist?  Yowza!
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: A compelling, entertaining, and funny-at-times, story about the price of duty; accompanied by stunningly beautiful art with impeccable style. 8.5/10Some notes:1. Lovely detailing about environmental storytelling and characterization using the game's mechanics.2. Very minute jankiness in code and interface/clues, that hindered the gameplay only once that I recall.3. Great and colorful characters.4. Having played Hellslave, I enjoy the subtly hidden horniness in the art.4.b Having said that, I also noticed in Hellslave that the only Prince-of-Demons who was depicted as a woman was Asmodeus, as is the case here. I would've hoped for some subversion on that side, especially since the artist draws the male figure excessively well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is phenomenal. The music is great, and the characters are fun. I also enjoyed the story. I did run into a couple of bugs but nothing game breaking. I just wish there was more of this game or even a sequel. I wish I could play the game again and discover everything for the first time again.Hopefully, the developer keeps making more games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game its got a really interesting story that I don't think I've ever seen anywhere else, and the art and music combo just really immerses you into the world. The only real problem that I encountered whilst playing is there are a lot of grammatical errors that really shouldn't have made it into the final game. Things like words in the incorrect order or a missing word. I feel that the was a bit abrupt but still had a good hook at the end, and i would love to see more of this game or something similar to it. 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not typically a fan of point-and-click games, but this one's alright. It's got a good Gothic vibe, a nicely dramatic story, and some decent humor that serves as a pretty good foil for its overall depressing storyline. They even snuck in some OK character development and a optimistically downer opinion on humanity as a whole. I know this doesn't exactly sound like a ringing endorsement, but I'd remind you that I don't usually like these kind of games (I got it as part of a bundle), but even I was drawn in enough to enjoy it from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: if you like comic book art in the vein of frank miller or mike mignola this is one of the best looking games you'll ever play. it even has comic-style cut scenes.  actually makes me kinda sad you only spend roughly a minute, sometimes less, on each new map, knowing the work that went into it.  the story isn't particularly amazing but it's good enough.if you like both point and clicks and comic books you could do a whole lot worse.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good story that's presented by amazing art and incredible sound work. The soundscape and soundtrack is absolutely beautiful. This is an excellent visual novel experience, although it has some spelling and grammatical errors, especially in the last couple acts. If you can get past that, the game is worthwhile.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a great journey it was, and more importantly - very smart.There is a lot to say, so maybe I'll start with something bad to save the best for the end. A little disappointing is that the game feels rushed at some point. I feel like the story could be a little longer and the whole concept could be set up much better. The city (Gore/Rotbork) also feels a bit small, since after 2-3 hours we have seen almost everything and then we only waiting to go to some locations and "get the job done". This impression is also enhanced by the linear story.But now to the positives, there are many, but I'll start with very dark, brave and smart story. I am surprised that the values and overall message come from a French studio! In these times, France is on the complete opposite side when it comes to things like religion, morality, etc. It's good to see something refreshing, something with a good view of the world. At many moments I had a smile on my face, for example - when we had the mission to prepare a news article, or when the hippie in "Redpill" was ranting about Snickers and how it ruins our world, simply contradicting his proffesion. Just brilliant. The are many more of such examples, but you should understand what I mean from the one I mentioned above.Another thing and the most important - artstyle. Hellboy comics mixed with Sincity and some dark fantasy. The athmosphere created by these artworks is very disturbing, depressing and just sad. Sometimes you may assume, that you play a game which is purely horror based, because in many moments the pictures/backgrounds and overall art is very suggestive.The music is also on point. Starting with unusual, subtle and gentle guitar sounds mixed with single piano notes, to trance club music and then ending on variations of Chopin compositions (the beat with telephone sounds, office and drills is great!) Do not get me wrong - the music is not as great as in other games (Hollow Knight, Cuphead, Hotline Miami), but some tracks are worth remembering and the most important - they do their job! They are adding a little spice in many moments, and that's the most important thing.With that, I would like to end this short review. There's a lot more to say, but I do not want to spoil too much either, because you should check out the story in this game for yourself. Maybe try to get it on sale, because I think the price is too high for this content. Hence the cons, I recommend it, you won't be disappointed. Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: The writing, characters, and translation often suffer from a lack of consistency, but the few great character moments combined with the fantastic artstyle, engrossing environments, and surprisingly excellent soundtrack held my interest to the very last frame. Unfortunately I can only recommend this on sale due to what feels like an unfinished ending, but I would love to see more like this in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it for the art and it does deliver in that regards. There are no major issues with the game so you can pick it up just for that, but expect no good story and storytelling even less.The good parts are the visuals. It's a run down, kind of historic city with many features, which blends in a bit of dystopian cyberpunk elements. All beautiful if you like the art style.But this game is confusingly unique in the way that the art amount and quality heavily outwheight the story and the storytelling. Characters do not build up a distinctive personality long term. The story and characters lack complexity, mysteries and depth. All information is exposed in rather mediocre dialogues, there is hardly any lore to discover. Humor is a nonstarter all over. Regarding the amount of art it feels like there was a lot more content planned, but something went wrong. But there we are, with a lot of style and a lack of substance.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.user: I am the cream of the crop!
_childDocuments_.review: I love everything about this game, except the gameplay.The art style has this weird 80s style gothic thing going, combined with this great soundtrack. The story and dialogue are pure edge.If you like point and click adventures and edged cheese, this might be the game for you. I for one just can't get over the unintuitive point and click mechanics where I have to Observe, Take, Use everything and see if something happens.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: It was a fun short game. The puzzles were fairly simple, which I liked. The only puzzle I had an issue with was a "math" puzzle where I couldn't make sense of it and had to look it up because I was trying to do actual, proper math but the puzzle could only be answered by doing it incorrectly- it was rather frustrating. The art style is cute and unique, loved the sketchy comic book look. The story was interesting too, it had a bit of horror vibe that was a little spooky for me, I don't do well with scary games but this one had enough of a spookiness to it but it wasn't scary. There was plenty of things to click on that didn't have anything to do with moving the story along, but I liked that because I like clicking on everything and seeing how the mc responds to his environment. And I adored him, he was the typical "cold hearted" softy that I'm quite fond of. There were plenty of grammatical mistakes much of which were "the the" which could have easily been fixed by proof reading it, but it didn't affect my enjoyment at all, I'm used to reading a lot worse lol. I thought the ending was good, there seems to be some things not yet answered so I definitely see a sequel ahead which I will totally get if it ever comes out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on an impulse when it was on sale, only based on that I liked the art style. So one can say I went in with no expectations. Before writing this review, I had a quick look at what others wrote about it, and they thought the game was short and lacks a hint system. While it is true that the game does not have a hint system, I can add that it really does not need one as the puzzles will not be so hard that it hinders progress. As for the length of the game, I'd say it is as long as it needs to be to tell the story. A game does not need to be long to be a good game.The visual style of the game is what really makes it shine. Expecially the aestetics of Rotbork the town. I want to live there in spite of what takes place there. I hope there will be a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: ✔️ Really cool and unique visual style.✔️ Rich and varied environments.✔️ Nice soundtrack.💭 The story was good enough, but the writing felt a bit clumsy at times.❌ The gamefeel is generally pretty lacking.❌ Some puzzles feel a bit "glued" on the story without adding anything meaningful.Overall the game isn't incredible, but I would recommend to play it nonetheless if a rather rough gameplay and very Christian themes don't bother you too much, if only for its art style. Also, be warned, it has some pretty raw themes in it (sexual violence among others).
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: A game well worth for a slow day of gaming for the art and cinematography. The Blind Prophet is a game I stumbled across during a search for a more gritter point-n-click adventure and it mostly delivered on that. It reads a lot like a dark graphic novel and I really loved the aesthetics of it, even though the translation and the story were clunky or rushed in some places. The gameplay is definitively on the lighter side here as a means of story progression with puzzle elements and I recommend it more for people who are used to kinetic interactive fiction and want to read a decent story with great graphics.When I finished the game in under 5 hours I was sad that there wasn't more to it and while the ending made sense in this gritty world, I'd have loved some "afterstory" on how events or characters progressed or handled the outcome of the ending. It also confused me how we were introduced to the demons in the lore sections, My biggest issue was mainly the translation. At first I thought that it was just not-English natives translating it and found it impressive enough to overlook it, but it was then embarrassing to see a hired translator AND the proofreader mess up in so many places. And it wasn't just one error here and there, but some repeatedly happening ( was the most glaring one I noticed and remember), so I don't know, but it seemed like both were amateurs to some regard to let this pass into the final product.It would also have been great to unlock some minigames afterwards in the menu as well, instead of going back to that story section to replay it for example. The menu was very minimal as well, with no big options to accustom readability or make it windowed for example. So I wondered what game engine they used that either had no options or if they manually removed most of them, which sounds incredibly silly.But aside from that I enjoyed the short time with very minimal speech bubble bugs that can be overlooked, but I do recommend to grab the game preferably on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: Took a little bit to get used to it but the aethetic and lore are quite deep and the puzzles are nice and self contained so you don't spend the whole time wandering back and forth across the map pixel hunting, or rubbing everything on everything hoping something clicks.you're an ageless agent of god sent to hunt demons secretly corrupting a city. Good theme, good story, good experience overall.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: A great game overall. Brutal, atmospheric, with great sound and top notch art!Yes, the text needs a lot of work, but I understood everything the way it was meant to be.I also expected to see Satan, Lucifer and Leviathan since they were in the game lore... that was a bit let down for me... but I forgive them, because the game was very nice. Hope to see 2nd game if possible. :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: While there are clearly some things that are missing in the game (story wise some plot points never get resolved), I am inclined to give this game a positive review. The artstyle is magnificent, and while the gameplay is simple, it is effective in what it sets out to do and does not overpromise. For a game made by just three people it is a good and enjoyable result that doesn't waste your time. 6.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible visuals, solid sound design, and very pleasant music that fits the tone. The atmosphere is what made this game for me, and I'd love to know more about the world and the characters. The art is nothing short of spectacular in most panels. I loved that not everything you can interact with is useful - like statues and odd symbols in the eerie little square. It makes the world feel bigger and more convoluted than what we are allowed to see. There was an occasional typo in the eng version and some of the dialogues and the decisions of the characters were quite dubious, not going to lie, but overall the project is worth a try, and definitely worth the time spent on it, especially since HellSlave is now released, and you can find some familiar faces in there.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: i wish that the rating system on steam would be different, like a 10/10 rating. If there were i'd probs give this game a 7.5 out of 10. I have finished the game and honestly i really liked it despite its flaws. The story and characters, especially the lead are very engaging, the lore behind the demons and such is really cool. However the puzzles, from me at least are pretty tough to complete, some you could probably solve just be continuously clicking on ♥♥♥♥, some i had to bring up a walkthrough to get thru it. I also noticed alot of spelling mistakes in the texts that would appear, but considering that the developers aren't probably english speakers, i can totally overlook that. The artstyle to the game is an absolute highlight for me, it really reminds me of a gritty graphic novel and i absolutely loved that. Lastly i'd say the ending was pretty abrupt, but its definitely a fitting one for our protagonist. I wish that the relationship between him and Vic would have been a little more fleshed out but i understand he is supposed to be the lone antihero.I defs recommend anyone who likes point and click games that are deep in demon and angel lore, but i will warn you some of the puzzles you'll hate this game for. The game definitely has its flaws but again it was really good. I might even pick it up again in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit mixed on this game, the graphic style was really good overall I thought. Gave me some Heavy Metal vibes at certain points. It's pretty rough and dynamic, has some sexual and violent themes going throughout. It doesn't go all out with that  though to be clear, could be arguable whether that's good or not maybe. The music was pretty good also, maybe that's partly what brought Heavy Metal to mind while I was playing. The main problem I had is the dialogue, and writing in general, especially for the main character. Like the things he says I don't really think a two thousand (or whatever) aged religious warrior would say. There are many parts where he gets just silly, which I don't think should be part of his character. It probably would have been better to keep him serious and have the humor develop from that, or anything else. Initially I debated on just quitting after the intro case with how bad the dialogue was there, but decided to give it a second chance. It grew a bit on me over time as the main mystery did hook me in some, and I do like the graphic style of it. I might have leaned more towards a good or neutral review given some of the aspects I liked here, but there was quite a few bugs that affected my game play also unfortunately. There was a some scenes where I couldn't select anything and it happened quite a few times. Generally right after or during a story event. This forced me to reload the game, then when I continued the story, I found it saved right after the cutscene. So, I missed out on some of the story and didn't know what was going on. There's also sketchy mechanics for some puzzles that don't quite work naturally, feels more like bad game mechanics. I wouldn't really recommend this game myself, but it's not all bad to be clear. The art style is really great for the most part, there's a few badly drawn parts for the dialogue where the characters proportions are bad, but otherwise great. The music is good and fits the style well. Just the other major apects of a graphic novel are pretty subpar here is the problem. The writing being the main one, with some bugs and bad mechanics pushing it over the edge for me. I'd recommend waiting for it to be on sale if you really want to get it, don't think the original price fits what you'll get for it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful music, wonderful storytelling. This story will be lingering in my mind for quite a while, Im sure of it. Main character reminds me of Geralt of Rivia in a way. Would love to see more!I found the dialogues quite funny. But maybe its just my weird sense of humour. Puzzles are sometimes a bit confusing (corpse-puzzle) , but do-able and not difficult. Loved the comic-book-cutscenes, I could just lean back and enjoy the story unfolding. Without spoling the end: I would have loved to get more info about the world. The ending scene was really cool, but maybe a little abrubt.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed The Blind Prophet, but I do believe there was a lot of room for improvement. I believe that that Comic Book Aesthetic was a bit overused and the game likely would have been better if there were more mini-games used in place of them. Conversations were also a little bit long winded and likely could have been shorter in some areas. There were also quite a few mini-games that I felt could have been better done - especially the final boss fight mini-game.The key thing to note though is that this game really lacked polish. Spelling and grammar were pretty bad in this game - and this is outside of where it was 'suppose' to be intentionally bad. There were multiple mini-games where one couldn't leave and exit the game and the player would be forced to solve the puzzle - or give up and force quit the application. The game also felt a bit 'rough' in controls at times as well when interacting with stuff in the world or ones inventory.Worth noting, the game probably could have had Bart actively trying to figure out what Demon he might be up against as he went through the game. Besides Beelzebub, I don't think it was all that hard to determine who the Demon's Bart would be facing, and it felt like a missed opportunity on the part of the developers not to have some sort of mini-game where Bart gathers clues on the Demons and then determines what those clues relate too.As a side note, this game was a lot less 'game' and more so an 'interactive novel'. That isn't necessarily a bad thing but it is worth noting in case people are looking more something with more action in it - this is definitely more story based and that likely won't be for everyone. It is also a lot easier then the usual point & click adventure as there is something called the 'Stalker's Eye' in this game which is a game mechanic which helps to highlight what you can interact with.Do I recommend this game? Yes and No. I played through this game about a year and a half after its release and though I was able to fumble my way through from start to finish with no game breaking bugs, not needing to look up for hints or guides to get through any tight spots, and generally having no real problems understanding what was going on or what I needed to do; it still felt like there were a few bumps that could have been smoothed out. At the very least, I don't recommend this game as it is now at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: **REVIEW CONTAINS SPOILERS**Game has really nice arts and plot.I've found some issues with continuity:- Vic's shirt beeing torn and becoming whole the next scene- Windows in manor beeing shut with boards, but then not- Barthomolev's arm missng once on left once on right sideBug in which article triggers interwiev with Mammon once again tho we just finished it.And some issues with riddles - for example one near clinic where, according to laws of math, multiplication should be first to addition, but the riddle ignores it. Maybe on purpouse, maybe not, but it's confusing. Others were frustrating 'cause you couldn't pick up items before exact moment they were needed in, so remembering that I was just ignoring them and looking for something else, then finding out I can pick them up at last.Overall game is good, nice to play, curious to watch the plot unravel.Hope next time you'll get more testers to check it out beforehand, but keep up the good work ;)

It's a very stylish comics-like quest with atmospheric music. Story is dynamic, a little bit bitter sweet and totally awesome.Riddles are not difficult but very organic with the story which is nice. _childDocuments_.review: Really impressed with the Blind Prophet despite some misspelling (jz a few i noticed) and sometimes buggy. The narrative for me is quite interesting and the artwork is phenomenal (really love it in fact!). Simply put it, the game was immersive and I enjoyed it immensely. Just a little disappointed that its not that long.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game! I had to consciously take a two day break to not finish it all the moment I had bought it...still only took me two days. That's probably my only complaint, that it is now over.The puzzles were refreshing, different ones all throughout. The developers didn't create one type and then repeated it. Some of them it was faster for me to just try it randomly instead of putting any thought to it, but I guess that's more a problem that I have and not necessarily anyone else.The artstyle was what drew me to this game originally, it's sinister and very detailed. The story was the second part but I am the type to judge a book by their covers and this one did not disappoint.In the end I wish I would have had the option to choose between sides, but I guess it does make more sense like this. idk what else to say. Great game 10/10 would play again
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks stunning and stylish and sounds dark and atmospheric. Well-written story which impressed me a lot and gave me a ton of different emotions. You always has some ideas what to do and it's hard to got stuck. I really recommend The Blind Prophet to anyone who likes quest games, point-and-click and comics-like stories. I'm really glad i've found this game, i believe it deserves much more attention.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: The Blind Prophet is a really charming game.The art set in a comic book style is really beautiful and the sound is really immersive.It's a rather short game, about 8 hours, but very entertaining.The only negative aspect of the game is lack of choices, it's rather linear, and the puzzles are sometimes a bit too simple. Overall, it has a fun story and I'd recommend it to all the point and click adventure games fans.
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed this game a lot. I would say it's worth your money, even if te game isn't as long as I wish it would be. I hope we get some another game from this world, maybe from Vic's perspective , etc. In the end, it's amazing and well done point and click game with a good story that is worth your time.Pros:- Amazing well written story!- Awesome artwork.- Atmosphere and soundtrack are both amazing. Perfect for someone who loves exploring dark and mysterious places.- Sometimes it can be very humorous.- As a game that was done by so few people, it's 8/10 for me.- Geralt from heaven purging demons in small, Lovecraftian/mysterious city in 21st century.- Most of the puzzles are fairly easy to solve. Some of them can be a bit more challenging.- Quite a lot of blood and gore (pros/cons?)Cons:- Even with such interesting and gripping story, I wish it would be at least twice longer (Finished in 8h).- Straightforward story, no side quests.- No save points. Only the one where you currently ended the last time. But it's acceptable due to the story I guess.- Sometimes it can get a little buggy. Disapearing objects and icons, but alt+f4 helped and the game saved, so no such big deal. Happened to me only once, maybe twice with some minor, not important visual bug.- Few puzzles/objectives can be hard to someone who's English isn't that good (Had to use translator few times and all good in the end).- The ending was a bit rushed, could be better.- After finishing the game, I feel like there is a lot of questions without an answer and unfinished stuff.- Did I already mentioned it could be longer?
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game indeed! Visual style, the story, the hero, the sound... If you miss good-old Sierra Games quests, if you fond of noir atmosphere and like The Darkest Dungeon graphic style, if you can enjoy the modern biblical Good vs. Evil novel - The Blind Prophet is your game! Short but solid as a rock.Just need to put my hands on the OST now...
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the story. It is more serious than most point and click games, but there is a little humour in it.There is also a lot of story, more than usual. The puzzles were easier than normal, but I was grateful for this. It was nice not getting stuck every 5 minutes. However those looking for more of a challenge might not be satisfied. Overall, great job devs ^-^
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: As an apostle you fight to keep mankind alive. You will face off with demons, solve mysteries, save people. The Blind Prophet is a very interesting, immersive game. I love the way it plays, with tasks I need to solve along the way. Along the way you can check out the environment, talk with people, or at least observe them. Battles are handled through whether or not you have done the right thing, so you either win or die. Artwork in this game is amazing. It really sets the mood of this dark, rundown town of Rotbork where the story takes place. The soundtrack helps you with the mood setting. Lack of spoken dialogue is a great choice from the creators. There is the occational grunt, `no` and other noices, and that is more than enough. As a casual game it works well. I spend time just exploring and watching the environment. Soundtrack and imagery affects me when I suddenly have a time limit. Mini games along the way give me a break from the bigger tasks, and solving puzzles to go along keeps my mind going.I am hoping for a development in this game, maybe new chapters, new in-game mini games. The map you can use to check where you are and where you`re going is nice, but it would have been easier to use if there were names on the places. There are some typos in the game, but I know the developers are on it to fix these things. It`s a game I will revisit again and again. It is one of my new favourites!
_childDocuments_.name: The Blind Prophet

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been on my wishlist for a long time. There were multiple delays with the release date, and I was starting to become worried if the game would deliver. However, when the game came oh boy did deliver! I would say I got more out of the experience than what I was originally expecting. The game delivered one of the most beautiful hand drawn environments that I ever seen. Furthermore, the story is very dark and edgy. On top of that what took me be surprise how good the soundtrack was and how well some of the ost’s fitted with the environment and situations. Their were literally moments when the soundtrack made be on edge of my seat. That’s how good it is. The only bad thing that I didn’t like was the fact that the whole game basically has an adventure game system which really didn’t work that well with what the game was about. For example, there are a ton of problem puzzles that literally don’t add any value to experience, and I would say even hurt the games atmosphere. There’s also a lots of environmental filler in which you can interact with the environment, but its basically is just a waste of time that takes you out of experience. Overall, I think the problems are not game braking and mostly depend on your personal taste. I just personally don’t like when video games waste my time and adventure games are notorious for that sort of thing. Overall, I think its an incredible game for what it offers. If you have twenty dollars to spare its worth a shot just for experience alone. Its a must buy that was worth the wait!

name: Close to the Sun
detailed_description: WISHLIST MEOW! 😻 About the Game It’s 1897. Deep in international waters, the Helios stands still. Dark clouds loom overhead as unforgiving waves crash against the hull. Colossal effigies of gold, decorated with magnificent finery, stretch as far as the eye can see. Born of Nikola Tesla’s vision, the Helios serves as a haven for the greatest scientific minds. An unbound utopia for research, independent from state and isolated from the gaze of society. Free to push the boundaries of matter and time. Journalist Rose Archer steps aboard the Helios in search of her sister Ada. She quickly discovers not all is as it seems. Grand halls stand empty. The stench of rotting flesh lingers in the air. Silence. A single word is painted across the entrance… QUARANTINE! Experience a second era of scientific enlightenment, where the mind and inventions of the great Nikola Tesla have shaped the 19th century Step aboard the Helios - Explore the colossal and mysterious vessel of scientific discovery, a safe haven for scientific progress, away from the threat of corporate espionage Use your wits to guide Rose on her journey to find her sister Ada, overcome dangers unknown to understand the fate of the Helios and its inhabitants Solve challenging puzzles to progress through the game and unlock secret areas Search every corner to uncover hidden collectables and discover the history and secrets of Wardenclyffe and its workers Explore a visually stunning environment Built in Unreal Engine™ 4 PRESS QUOTES: KOTAKU: 'Close to the Sun is an Indie Bioshock Without the Combat.' GAMESRADAR: 'A little bit BioShock, a little bit SOMA.' GAMINGBOLT: 'Close to the Sun is looking like a unique, ambitious game, with an alternative history setting that puts the limelight on Nikola Tesla as one of its most major characters...'
about_the_game: It’s 1897. Deep in international waters, the Helios stands still. Dark clouds loom overhead as unforgiving waves crash against the hull. Colossal effigies of gold, decorated with magnificent finery, stretch as far as the eye can see. Born of Nikola Tesla’s vision, the Helios serves as a haven for the greatest scientific minds. An unbound utopia for research, independent from state and isolated from the gaze of society. Free to push the boundaries of matter and time. Journalist Rose Archer steps aboard the Helios in search of her sister Ada. She quickly discovers not all is as it seems. Grand halls stand empty. The stench of rotting flesh lingers in the air. Silence. A single word is painted across the entrance… QUARANTINE! Experience a second era of scientific enlightenment, where the mind and inventions of the great Nikola Tesla have shaped the 19th century Step aboard the Helios - Explore the colossal and mysterious vessel of scientific discovery, a safe haven for scientific progress, away from the threat of corporate espionage Use your wits to guide Rose on her journey to find her sister Ada, overcome dangers unknown to understand the fate of the Helios and its inhabitants Solve challenging puzzles to progress through the game and unlock secret areas Search every corner to uncover hidden collectables and discover the history and secrets of Wardenclyffe and its workers Explore a visually stunning environment Built in Unreal Engine™ 4 PRESS QUOTES: KOTAKU: 'Close to the Sun is an Indie Bioshock Without the Combat.' GAMESRADAR: 'A little bit BioShock, a little bit SOMA.' _childDocuments_.review: To be honest, this is one of the few games that I bought mainly because of the design. Sure, the story doesn't sound bad at first, but the logo reminded me of BioShock somehow. Especially as far as the design of BioShock is concerned, even after all these years it is still an absolutely grandiose and maybe even unrivaled game. It doesn't really matter to me whether the developers took BioShock as a template or really followed it, but at least it shows just how great BioShock is.However, if the thought behind it was to develop a game that was just as good, then it went haywire. And unfortunately in many ways.In the middle of the ocean, a visionary creates a place, in this case a huge ship called Helios, where scientists can work on all sorts of projects and even surpass themselves. As soon as you enter the environment driven by large machines, you cannot stop being amazed. There are large statues everywhere, flags on magnificently decorated walls and a dimmed light makes the rooms shine in a special glow.But soon you stumble over the first corpses, it creaks everywhere and suddenly a helping voice answers over the radio...As you can see, the comparisons to BioShock are no coincidence and you can already tell that the game is really based on it. The good thing is that while the scenario and narrative elements are the same, the story is different and distinct around Nikola Tesla, albeit a fictional one set in the late 19th century.I won't reveal exactly what happened or will happen, of course, but the game isn't just about collecting story pieces, it's also about having a pretty good scary trip.We play Rose Acher, who has received a letter from her sister asking her to come to the Helions immediately, as she has been researching a project that is turning all scientific knowledge upside down and, by the way, has also caused a catastrophe .What is supposed to happen when many scientists work in one place on various projects and play around with quantum physics, which then destroys the space-time continuum?When we arrived on the ship, of course, nothing is as we had hoped. Nobody is there, the ship is in quarantine and some experiment is out of control. The basic theme, the question of "how far can science go" and what happens to it when dreams meet reality quickly becomes apparent.Apart from that, the game unfortunately doesn't make more of it compared to, for example, BioShock or Soma because the science serves here in principle only as an explanation for everything.We quickly find out that Ada, Rose's sister, and other characters like Nikola Tesla or the strange technician Aubrey are still alive and contact us. You don't meet any of the characters at first, but the partly humorous and also amusing dialogues are really well written and welcomely loosen up the whole thing.The narrative collectibles that are distributed all over the ship provide significantly more depth. The memories of the crew, shown as figures of light, which just pop up from time to time, the letters lying around from a spy of Tesla's competitor Thomas Edison, or the machines actually designed by Tesla, give story fans a great time.In terms of play, the game relies on exploring and (really very) simple puzzles that are often limited to finding numbers or symbols and then entering them somewhere. You have to dodge Tesla flashes or flames from time to time, which integrates really well into the environment, it's never really that difficult or that you have to think about it.Unfortunately, the opponents in the game are only limited to scripted sequences that always play out in the same way. Someone or something appears and we run away until you reach a safe room. Since we cannot defend ourselves and these "run away passages" are really quite narrow, it is very often not clear where to run because everything is also quite dark and to make matters worse, some obstacles can only be jumped over with the right pressure, which is required , that you have aimed at it correctly and have to click several times.This not only costs nerves but also a lot of time because your pursuers have usually caught up with you with the smallest mistake and you die an agonizing screen death. So it can quickly happen that the whole thing quickly develops into annoying trial & error passages, which somehow damages the whole atmosphere and also loses its effect.Here I would have wished for the typical stealth and hiding mechanics from other games because I think that would have suited the game and Rose well.Don't get me wrong.Close to the Sun is a thoroughly entertaining game with an interesting story and thrives on its wonderful setting. The successful moments of shock complete the whole thing so that adventure also works as a scary trip.Unfortunately, there are no decisions in the game, not even multiple endings, which would have been a really good addition and if the game had mainly focused on its story and the "horror" and game mechanics had been better developed, then this would have been a really, really good game .It's more like that the game can show good approaches in all respects, but none of them can fulfill or convince nearly 100%.The collectibles also don't really bring much replay value if you missed them on the first run, especially since the levels can be replayed individually in order to collect everything necessary for the achievements.Depending on how diligently you search the area, you get a playing time of around 5-10 hours with Close to the Sun, so I can't recommend the game for the regular retail price.If you are interested in the game wait until the game is on sale.For me as a BioShock fan, Close to the Sun is like coming home.The game looks like I could imagine a Rapture with the Unreal Engine. You can't get enough of all the details, but unlike BioShock, the game simply lacks the necessary depth.Still, I enjoyed it and don't regret playing it. I would love to see an (even better) sequel.Review date: October 31, 2022✔ exciting idea✔ stunning art deco look✔ great details✔ spooky atmosphere✔ varied environment✔ great soundtrack✔ likeable characters✔ Big levels to explore✔ fair save points✔ surprising twists✔ optional puzzles✘ Annoying chase sequences✘ sometimes hard to see interaction points✘ a little too easy✘ few and too simple puzzles✘ bland / unsatisfactory ending

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wondered what would happen if Tesla managed to complete and put into action all his crazy, wild ideas, collect and steal all the world's greatest minds, build a gigantic ship in international waters and wage a constant spy war against Edison? Storm in a Teacup invites you for a spot of tea and a mostly successful, nightmarish, walking simulator frolick through Tesla's greatest minds utopia aboard Helios, a ship so large it requires it's own passports.You play as Rose, a journalist boarding the Helios after receiving a letter from your sister Ada, who's a scientist on the ship. Things immediately go sideways and from it's opening moments, comparisons to Bioshock are inevitable. Not only for Art Deco, but some of it's ideas as well. I was half expecting a banner with "No gods or kings. Only man." to greet me upon entering and a "Would you kindly..." sentence to pop in my ears. There is a large poster in the Tesla Museum with the words "Peaceful and neutral. Unbound. Unattached. Uncommited to the nations-states of the world, the Helios sails under it's own banner." and the story, although competently written for an indie game, with a bit of an ending letdown, wears some of Bioshock's influences on it's sleeve, but is nowhere near as nuanced. It certainly doesn't throw as much Objectivism in your face.Your search leads you through different parts of Helios and it quickly becomes apparent that visuals and ambience, along with sound design and some terrific voice acting, are this game's strongest features. Every part of the ship carries it's own distinct Art Deco design, and it's persistent and continually impresses, no matter where you go. From the harbour entry, living quarters and science labs to a giant theatre, all are impeccably made and feel lived and worked in, but always creepy and gloomy now that the ship has been abandoned. Storm in a Teacup went all out here and all the areas are full of human things, drawing you into the world even more and each chapter includes collectibles in the form of notes, letters, newspapers and other things that further flesh out the story and give some new angles on happenings, with Rose commenting on a lot of them. The main character's animations are also well made, increasing the immersion, with Rose having a few idle animations and reacting to the world around her, like waving away flies and putting a hand on the window if you get close enough.The game sets a good tension, playing with you, in the first part with some excellent jump scares that are not overused and the revelation of the first gruesome scene is very effective. As you play further, revealing more information and more bodies, the game loses that creepy luster a bit and turns into a few failable chase scenes with some wonky controls that have dead ends with Rose's death animations as rewards, but are not overly long or difficult and the checkpoint system is generous. Granted, they do break the immersion and flow if you fail them a few times, but the paths you need to take are well marked, with visuals leading the way, such as lights, strategically placed scenery or even opening doors. There are some minor puzzles, code and key searching along the way, but nothing major or stumping and when the plot twist hits, the story goes a bit downhill, like the developer's storm ran out of juice, since there's nothing to reveal anymore and it just keeps on plodding to the end that just happens, opening many questions and potentially setting up a sequel or a piece of DLC.I've noticed only one technical problem. The game stuttered and even froze a bit when loading some areas since the loading screens are only between chapters. Hardware specs, i7, RTX2070, 32GB of RAM and an SSD.It's evident how much work and love went into creating the world, ambience and characters over 2 years of development. It is a mostly railroaded experience and it does draw influences from things already seen, but it would be a bit unfair comparing it directly to them. It hugs the alternate history very tightly and does a good job presenting a what if scenario, with stunning ambience, great characters and some slight hiccups, including a somewhat abrupt and dangling ending, but it's still a wortwhile play in it's 5-6 hours run time in spite of all the rough patches. Especially if you're interested in the world building and setting. Yes, the 19.99€ price tag is a bit too much considering it's length, but you won't regret picking it up on any Steam sale. P.S. Fun tidbit, Rose has no head if you take screenshots with Nvidia Ansel.: Mostly straightforward achievements, a few hidden ones and lots of collectibles, nothing missable. Chapter select is available after finishing the game and there's a good guide on Steam for collectibles and missables.

_childDocuments_.review: "Close to the sun" is a narrative game with an interesting and well-researched setting, a decent story, eerie atmosphere, minimal puzzles, badly designed chase scenes that annoyed the heck out of me, and an okay-ish presentation.The game's strongest point (and the main reason why I'm giving it a thumbs-up despite several very obvious flaws) is its setting. It takes place in an alternate history where Tesla's famous Wardenclyffe Tower was completed and successful, enabling Tesla to bring many of his other ideas to fruition as well. In this universe, Tesla assembled many renowned scientists on a giant ship where they could do research free from politics or worries about funding. The game includes many references to Tesla's work and his contemporaries, and it's nice to see that it doesn't stop at the flashy Tesla coils that everyone already knows, but also addresses lesser-known ideas like automated radio-controlled boats or his experiments with X-rays. The story itself leans more on the One-Electron hypothesis though, which - in our world - was postulated in 1940 without any relation to Tesla, who at that point was already 83 and had largely been forgotten. But in an alternate universe, it might of course have been established earlier.While the setting provides lots of fascinating opportunities, the story unfortunately doesn't do much with it. The first few chapters include many interesting references, but somewhere around the middle the game drops those completely and mostly just sends the player through dark empty levels with occasional chase scenes. The main plot remains interesting, but leaves lots of open questions and several plotholes. It feels as if the first chapters were designed with a much bigger and more complex story in mind, which was abandoned mid-production and replaced with cheap chase scenes.The writing itself is rather hit-and-miss. Some of the sarcastic banter worked very well, but the scenes that were intended to be deeply emotional felt forced and superficial instead. There's a scene where two sisters reunite amidst danger, and one of them greets the other with the line "My big sister is here!". No one would talk this way in such a situation, it's clearly the author talking through the character to tell the player which sister is older. But in doing so, he makes the dialogue feel unnatural, breaks the player's immersion, and wastes the opportunity for a strong emotional moment.What else is in the game beyond the story? For one, there are a few puzzles, but all of those are extremely easy. Most of them are on the level of "pull a lever to open a door", "find a key to open a door", or "find a note with a number sequence to enter in a code lock". None of them require any thought - the most complex ones involve levers that need to be pulled more than once, or in a certain order. Exploration is possible and gets rewarded with collectibles that fit the setting, which is nice.The only other gameplay mechanic are, unfortunately, chase scenes - which are implemented in some of the worst ways possible. You usually have several paths, and need to take a specific one, but don't know which. You may not even see the correct path because it's way too dark. Your pursuer is right behind you, so taking the wrong path or stopping to take a closer look leads to an immediate death. Each time you die, the game shows the same unskippable lengthy animation of how you get killed. Once you know the correct path, the chase scenes are easy. But since you cannot know (or sometimes even see) it, it takes lots of mindless repetition to get there. Be prepared to get killed up to 20 times in repetitions of the same chase scene just because the one way out is shrouded in darkness. By the time you get through, any feeling of fear or challenge or engagement has evaporated into sheer annoyance.The game also includes several jumpscares. These are, to be honest, fairly pathetic - e.g. you look through a window, and suddenly a disfigured hand slaps against it from the other side, while an ultra-loud piano chord assassinates your eardrums. None of these scenes are actually dangerous for your character, in fact none of these scenes have any relevance at all. You never find out who the aforementioned hand belonged to. You never know who these poor guys are that suddenly show up from nowhere, only to be mutilated by monsters that also appeared from nowhere. All these "scares" are just cheap, amateurish, transparent, tacked-on attempts to create an atmosphere of threat and horror, which fails as soon as the player realizes that there is no threat outside of the chase scenes. That said - if you're averse to the occasional loud noise and (mild) gore flung into your face, you may want to play something else.Let's have a word about the production values next. The game tries very hard to make its graphics look better than they actually do. This is done via a common trick: The first few chapters are relatively well lit and show some amazing environments - a huge hall with beautiful architecture, a Tesla museum with lots of detail, etc. As you go on, the levels and textures become much less elaborate - but the game masks that by also making them darker. The idea is that the player, who's already in a "this looks great!" mindset from the previous levels, continues to perceive the environment as "highly detailed but too dark to really see", when in fact it's really just dark in order to hide a lack of detail. That said, the first few levels _do_ look very interesting. The way how steampunk elements, machinery, and luxurious architecture form a coherent whole shows a great sense of art direction.The sound and especially the music are also excellent. The soundtrack carries the feelings of melancholy, suspense, danger, and terror perfectly, while never pushing into the foreground. It's definitely one of the game's stronger points.Voice acting was rather uneven - Tesla and (in most scenes) the protagonist were done competently. However, why they chose an almost 80-year old German with a noticeable accent to voice a considerably younger main character without any German roots, is beyond me.On a more negative note, even basic usability functions are notably absent. There's no brightness slider, no key rebinding, no FOV slider, no y-axis inversion, only one save slot, and no manual saves. There's a pinned thread in the forum where a representative from Wired Productions acknowledges some of these issues and says the info "has been passed on to the developers". That was two months ago, and since then there has been total radio silence on the topic. Personally, while I agree that this is mostly the devs' responsibility, I think it's a bit shady from the publisher to just point to the devs - as if the publisher hadn't had every opportunity to insist on (or at least strongly encourage) the implementation of these features before _they_ released the title. Furthermore, I have played 5 out of the 5 first-person adventures that Wired Productions has released (The Town of Light, Deliver Us The Moon, Those Who Remain, Fractured Minds, and now Close To The Sun), and each and every one of them was held back by a lack of basic usability/accessibility features. (TWR is the only one that offered key rebinding, but had other problems.) At this point it's hard to not see a pattern. At the very least, any argument that Wired Productions actually cares about the usability of their products seems hard to maintain with an objective track record of 0:5 against it.FInal verdict: Despite its many flaws, I recommend Close To The Sun to fans of narrative games who feel a strong appeal from an alternate universe setting with a "Tesla succeeded" theme. However, it was a pretty close call and there are several caveats - read through the review, pick the parts that are relevant for you, and make your own decision. I definitely also recommend reading some other reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe this is the only  exclusive game that I purchased here. It should also be noted that it became free on  last year. I loved the story so much and I also wanted to enjoy additional benefits here on Steam that we don't have there (writing reviews, adding screenshots, unlocking achievements) that I decided to add  to my library.This game can be considered a long walking sim. You know, those FPS titles that miss the shooter aspect. Our protagonist, Rose, is a journalist. She's on board Helios, this massive ship full of scientists and her sole purpose is to find her sister, Ada. You immediately notice the message written on the wall upon your arrival: quarantine. It seems things have gone awry and once you find the first mutilated bodies you realise this will be a horror adventure. There is also a certain unpleasantness reading quarantine whilst having to go through a worldwide pandemic in real life.You make contact with Ada through a wireless device who claims she didn't invite you, at all, to the ship. In any case, you are here for the rescue but investigating what science experiment went wrong is also something you'll uncover in the 10 chapters lying ahead of you. No weapons just solving puzzles and surviving various scripted (mainly chase) events. The design elements reminded me of Bioshock - it should also be noted that the game is exceptionally beautiful. I noticed a couple of stutters here and there but nothing that made me stop playing. I also liked the late 19th century setting with its more advanced technology and the Nikola Tesla museum!And here comes the bad part, the reason why a lot of people feel mixed about the game. The chasing sequences are awful. I believe one in chapter 8 requires precision-perfect turning. You literally have a couple of seconds to press a button and go through the open door. Very annoying thing that requires a lot of trial-and-errors. The game also has some weird greenish spray painting symbols on almost every level as if the developers wanted to indicate something during the development stage. These are mostly hidden but because the game has a lot of collectibles you'll find them.  starts out great then it becomes even better only to remain a mediocre tale at the very end. The last chapter is especially a letdown but overall it is an interesting game with little replayability. I'm usually biased when it comes to this genre and the Bioshock-esque design also made this an immediatey purchase for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wondered what it'd be like if someone made a Bioshock-themed walking simulator "adventure" game using the design notes from Amnesia: a Machine for Pigs?Well, wonder no more because Close to the Sun is basically /that/.  Rather fittingly for a game with a story that heavily involves nonlinear time, this game appears to have fallen forward in time from about 2007.  In this walking simulator set in an implausibly massive, anachronistically-advanced, ocean liner created by an insane genius, the aesthetic is so blatantly copying 2007's Bioshock 1 that it's kind of impressive that 2K's lawyers having come after the devs at Storm in a Teacup.  But for the detail level in some of the set pieces, this game really looks like it's made from recycled Bioshock 1 art assets.As a game, it's unsatisfying and mechanically troubled.  The devs created environments that /look/ large and exploration-friendly, but you're really on an extremely narrow and linear course through a handful of obvious jump scares in an otherwise largely empty setting.  The player character, Rose, moves at a pace that most of the audience would consider surprisingly leisurely given how corpse-y the surroundings are and her running speed is more a purposeful walk.  She can't jump more than three vertical inches.  She can't crouch or crawl on her own.  Every action other than walking is a contextual left click that requires you to maneuver your invisible cursor onto an action icon and sit through an unskippable animation.  I get that they were trying to be atmospheric, but it's just tedious.  Rose maneuvers like she's got crippling arthritis and is coming off an overdose of general anesthetic.  As a result, the game is full of insurmountable ANKLE HIGH walls where Rose is incapable of stepping over... anything.  A folding chair or wet floor sign that's been knocked over is as good as a ten meter high electric fence to her.  Getting stuck on unseen obstacles is a near-constant issue.  On its own, this would merely be tedious... but the devs insisted on throwing multiple chase scenes where you have to "run" (just walking but they apply a blur filter over everything) away from something chasing you and since failure means instant death they're annoyingly unforgiving of the set design.As a horror-themed game... I'm sorry to say that the game does a terrible job of it.  It does some predictable jump scares with falling debris and so on, and you can guarantee that any time you're told to go somewhere the first path you try to take will be immediately blocked by an explosion that leaves some impassible obstacle in your way.  In combination with the above, this gets a bit silly at times.  Rose's path can end up being obstructed by a pool of fire roughly the size of a dinner plate or by objects that any able person (and many less-than-able ones) could easily climb over.  The efforts to give the game a horror-appropriate visual atmosphere are poorly executed as well.  In horror, less is more.  Finding the occasional dead body is scary if handled appropriately.  The Helios has so many dead bodies lying around that it swiftly loses all of its sting and just becomes obnoxious because they're more debris forming insurmountable ankle-high walls.  There are no textured wounds on most of them, so it looks less like they suffered fatal injuries and more like they passed out from shame after a tragic cranberry sauce accident.  The "ghosts" are stolen straight from the first Bioshock game too.  The animations are so weightless and boneless-looking that the violence when you're caught by the murderer or the monster after failing to negotiate an ankle-high wall looks and feels more like a toddler is slapping you.On every level, it's an interesting concept with just disappointing execution.

_childDocuments_.review: Close to the Sun is a pretty dark (literally...) and interesting Horror Adventure game.For my taste a little too dark, even if i set the gamma pretty high, it was hard to even navigate in some areas. For my taste it's also too gory, but i guess that's the point of horror games. The graphics are nicely done, sounds and music are good, the voiceacting is outstanding and really enjoyable. I liked the twisted story and also the characters.The gameplay mostly consists of solving little puzzles, exploring and collecting items.  At parts it's getting a little stressful because you have to run away from... something...  Negative things i remember were a single crash after about 1 hour of playtime, and that the game kept freezing randomly for a mere second here and there.

_childDocuments_.review: I had hesitated to play this game due to some of the negative reviews. I recently took the plunge and really enjoyed the entire experience. Close to the Sun is a first person adventure with exploration, a few chase scenes, and a well developed story. Although the story is not entirely unique (science gone wrong with terrible results), I think it is very well implemented and the pieces fall together in an ending that makes sense.You play Rose - a journalist who has come to the Helios in search of her sister. The Helios is a creation by Tesla to research/provide unlimited energy. Scientists have gathered to participate in his work. Upon arrival, Rose finds the ship in a state of disarray and littered with bodies. Obviously, all is not well in scientific paradise.I am an adventure gamer at heart and games with extensive combat, tricky stealth, or stressful chases are not my favorite. Close to the Sun had the right balance for me. The ship has been created in amazing detail and there is so much to look it along the way. It is visually stunning and incredibly interesting. There are collectibles in each chapter which I liked because it forced me to explore every nook and cranny. The chase scenes were easily survivable (although it took me several times to find each exit path). There is no combat.The dialog between Rose and other characters happens over a radio so you do not catch up with either, in person, until well into the game. The story takes place in the 1800's but the realization of Tesla's technology is very much science fiction. The Helios includes a 'Tesla museum' which was really interesting to peruse.The game does not appear to save mid-chapter, although your collectibles are retained. This meant that some of the trickier chapters need to be played to completion to avoid replay. I should note that the game is very forgiving when you are killed and little replay is required to 'catch back up.' Hard core action enthusiasts are likely to think this game is too easy. However, for adventurers like me, it is just about perfect!

_childDocuments_.review: Really quite good but completely forgotten about. Beautiful design, vast areas as good as anything AAA games can produce.  The moment you walk into the theatre, you realise they went all out here. Fun characters and a setting cribbing hard from Bioshock. You play the sister of one of the researchers on a boat responding to a call for help and once you arrive on this bastion of free thought and research you realise, predictably, it's all gone to hell in a hand basket. The controller could use a bit of work though, the contextual stuff was too precise making it hard to do things quickly. A little more leeway in where you were pointing could have helped especially in the chase scenes. ★★★★ 1/2

_childDocuments_.review: Bit of a mixed bag this one. I'd give it 6/10. The graphics and environments are amazing, and it's probably worth playing just to admire those. And the atmosphere is very good, with lots of built tension and jump scares. However, I'm not quite sure where this game fits; as a walking simulator, the paths are just too restricted, with large areas blocked off simply because you can't step around a chair or some other small obstacle; as a survival game, the attack/chase sequences would probably be too easy for lovers of that genre; and as an adventure/puzzle game the puzzles were too simplistic.But by far the biggest gripe is the automatic save system. In some places it was over an hour before a save triggered. I don't always have the time to spend hours at the keyboard, so was put off playing until I knew that I'd have enough time to reach a save point before I had to go do something else.But all that said, I did enjoy the game and would recommend it - but be warned it's very gruesome/gory with lots of dismembered corpses scattered around.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: After a certain point, ambition and hubris mix and form a deadly concoction. The myth of Icarus and his tragic demise can be summarized as someone who flew too close to the Sun and paid the ultimate price for not heeding to advice and common sense. I’ve had my fair share of walking sims, yet the one I’ll be covering today is definitely among the finest in a long time. It is the culmination of efforts undertaken by developer Storm in a Teacup (very fond of that phrase) whose journey over the past four years, saw them advance from the light-hearted themes in 2016’s Lantern to the literally dark tones in 2019’s Close to the Sun. After a brief stint as an Epic Games exclusive, we can finally play this mature adventure on Steam and I’ve been looking forward to writing about it on the one gaming platform fully supporting my little reviewing hobby.If you’re a fan of Nikola Tesla even remotely, I’m sure you heard of this game by now. Even if you aren’t already, it’ll be hard not to empathize with one of the greatest minds of the 19th Century. A visionary and inventor who was sadly obscured and undermined by corporate greed in its infancy at the time. “Edison might have the present, but the future is mine”. Not an exact quotation, yet Close to the Sun is also loosely based on Tesla’s inventions and grand plans that could never come to fruition. The game is a work of science fiction that still has its foundations in a few plausible “what ifs” however. As with most innovating theories, gathering the necessary funding to begin experimentation is the truly difficult phase.Not for our alternate timeline, in which Wardenclyffe (known for its non-operational Tesla Tower) became a highly successful company under Nikola’s careful guidance. Most of the inventor’s blueprints materialized into practical structures including an autonomous ship which could serve as company headquarters away from governmental oversight. Helios (“Sun” in ancient Greek) was not impervious to sabotage and espionage though. Our story begins aboard a smaller transport vessel taking the female protagonist towards the “mothership” and an uncertain destiny. I was fortunately mistaken in my initial assessment of Close to the Sun. You won’t be (re)playing “BioShock minus guns & plasmids”.Rose Archer boards the Helios at her sister’s behest. A rescue mission ensues, one which holds much higher stakes than anticipated. As far as the narrative is concerned, its originality cannot be contested. It is indeed a “walking simulation” that will have you frequently running for your life, followed by more relaxed sequences in which you can take in the sights, so to speak. Retrofuturism melding with the macabre elements of a still unfolding tragedy. Since this is a Tesla inspired Sci-Fi tale, it couldn’t dispense with wireless electricity or interdimensional travel after all. The dev team spent a lot of time creating auxiliary reading materials in-game, which manage to paint a vibrant picture of the late 19th Century in stark contrast with the violent reality of the early 20th that was slowly starting to catch up.  Ceasing all praise for a moment, as the technical difficulties of the inherently unstable Unreal Engine 4 were coupled with some questionable stylistic choices in regards to the overall illumination of the level design. In other words, it gets far too dark more often than not. The “abandoned facility” trope doesn’t need to go to such lengths, especially since we aren’t provided with a personal light source that could be carried by the heroine. In some ways, I’m glad this isn’t a hunt for flashlight batteries since that gameplay mechanic was done to death. Turning the brightness up a notch or two also won’t really cut it. There’s plenty of beauty in Close to the Sun and it gets partially hidden in plain sight. Regardless of that, I still managed to capture over a hundred screenshots, half of which will make the final cut on my Steam profile once any potential spoilers have been dealt with. Going for resolutions over 1080p will invite unavoidable frame rate drops unless you’re sporting a beefy GPU. UE4 standard fare, sadly. Both a capable soundtrack and the convincing voice acting, further breathe life into Close to the Sun. Accents are spot on and there are occasional attempts at (black) humor which manage to break the rather gloomy tone of those ongoing events aboard the Helios. Each chapter has its distinct theme which transcends the visual section as instrumental songs were carefully selected to fit the same pattern. This in my opinion usually marked a clear difference between indie gaming and AAA projects with far deeper pockets. A pleasant surprise to see the “AA type” aiming ever higher. Same as with the midrange segment of certain Tech sectors bluring the definition of high end nowadays. Sounds are definitely not as subdued as those pitch black corridors you’ll be traversing a lot.Eleven levels split into a prologue and ten chapters taking you on a trip across most areas of interest aboard Tesla’s floating laboratory. The sheer size and complexity of its sectors, reminds me of modern day ocean liners and in a strange twist of fate, quarantine has stricken both the real life counterparts and the ship simulated in our game. A descent into madness followed by attempts to salvage research from the Helios, you’ve got your work cut out for you as becoming prey to the…object of study can have terminal consequences. Thus, the gameplay is diversified enough to move past the subgenre misconceptions. You can stick around and admire art works or architectural elements reminiscent of Greek mythology, yet you also have a clear set of goals.The pacing suffers few impediments along the way, as chase sequences replace the few jump scares found in the first chapters. Of course there are a some horror elements at play here, yet they’ve been combined very well with the overarching Sci-Fi themes involving a few conspiracies as well. As I mentioned before, you will have plenty of stuff to read from newspaper headlines, internal memos or posters and blueprints. Attention to detail is obvious and there are references to period-appropriate events as expected. The lack of a manual saving option did annoy me enough to consider it a weak point since some of those levels are quite large and warrant a break. Autosaves at the start of each chapter (and a few before certain encounters), simply aren’t enough for this title.While I can’t go into details, the ending pretty much spells out the desire for a sequel and I can only hope the dev team can deliver upon that subtle promise. Still a cliffhanger conclusion which leaves far too many questions unanswered. Cthulhu knows for how long we’ll have wait until Close to the Sun 2 might surface on Steam in this day and age of “PC platform exclusivity”. One thing is crystal clear though: Tesla’s vision makes for one hell of a ride! It’ll probably be worth the wait and asking price. One leaf in, one thorn out.+ Beautiful visuals and sounds.+ Steam Achievements & Trading Cards.+ Original story backed by historical elements.- Level design is literally too dark.- No manual saving system.- Cliffhanger ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Rose has been invited by her sister, Ada, to come aboard the Helios, a gigantic ship run by Nikola Tesla and his Wardenclyffe company. Within it, scientists from around the world are conducting research into time, weaponry, and other fields. The ship is like a city. However, given the game’s canned nature, you’re never able to explore it, and you don't get a sense of it as an immersive place.Graphics aren’t everything, obviously, but when a game’s overall aesthetic pulls you in once you start it your expectations are raised.The greatest shortcoming is that there is no sense of a world to explore. The Helios divides into small, tight chapters, through which there is essentially one obvious path.At first glance  looks like a  clone. The art deco, the premise of the Helios and its scientific minds, the temporal experiments, and some specific story points in the game are straight out of  and . The game publicly available fact sheet even bears the disclaimer that this game is not .Like other horror games it has a number of puzzles for you to solve. More often than not, though, these puzzles are as elementary as finding a piece of paper with a code and then using that code on a door panel. As for the horror part,  manages to give you tense and shocking moments that are brief and fleeting. There are a few jumpscares, naturally, as well as audio cues and sound effects that might keep you on the edge.This protagonist is one of the few positive parts of . Her voice actor gives a solid performance as a protagonist who’s driven by curiosity.Sadly  fails to realize its potential by relying on cheap scares and gore without strong atmosphere and narrative to back it up.- Likeable protagonist- High production values- Solid graphics- Lack sense of dread- Week narrative- Chase scenes are a painDISASTER | BAD | MEDIOCRE |  | GOOD | GREAT | AMAZING | MASTERPIECE
