There's a couple of chase sequences that I felt were a bit out of place and kind of frustrating - mostly because when you get "caught" the sequence can't be skipped and goes from being a bit scary/frightening to boring/frustrating. Don't let that deter you though. It's really the only negative thing I have to say about this other than I would have loved it if it would have been longer. 6 hrs isn't too bad for this price, don't get me wrong, but longer would have been better. + Graphics. Good use of the Unreal 4 engine here. Very nice looking game. + Audio. Both the voice over and the music were very well done. Even the music in the credits made them worth watching.+ Story. I enjoyed it. I enjoyed the idea of exploring a huge steampunk type ship at sea. + All achievements work properly. +/- The increase when sprinting/running was very little it seemed too slow, but it also didn't bother me overall. +/- Very linear. It worked fine for this story, but it might have been nice to freely explore the ship. +/- All of the puzzles were pretty easy. I wouldn't say TOO easy, they did keep you from running a straight line from point A to B. +/- The collectibles were all really easy to find. They didn't require hours of combing dark corridors and looking under beds.- Death sequences were too long. After the first couple of times they got kinda boring and less scary.- Dead bodies on the floor can't be stepped over, nor can you jump. You must walk around them. Lame. Really enjoyable. I definitely recommend this one. The positives FAR outweigh the negatives. The negatives were in fact, very minor.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome atmosphere and music, style is similar to Layers of Fear with the prompt that you can run. If you like horror walking/running simulators with puzzles and someone NOT constantly chasing you this game is for you. You do reach some scenarios where you need to run/avoid but it's a small phase that will have you screaming but in a fun way.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: While I did some what enjoy this walking simulator it is expensive for what it is. While I did have a spook here or there I don't think I can recommend this game to anyone, while drawn in by the visuals bringing that nostalgia for Bioshock (First and Second). While having similarities visually, it is in no way the same for gameplay. The device shown MULTIPLE times in the trailer might as well be nothing as it's just a radio, it isn't used to hack, shoot, stun, detect anything and serves no purpose being in it other than to mislead.Enemies in this game while looking interesting are encountered 2-3 times and are only you running away in a scripted jump scare where the game is designed in a way to get you killed at least once.Story wise it is poorly written, you can pretty much guess what is happening as it's an incompletely Bioshock infinite (The third Bioshock)I would suggest you actually try Bioshock 1-2 if you thick this game looks good and haven't checked them out yourself! This just feels like a poor copy.If you still don't know how you feel about this game please check out my play through here!
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: If you love BioShock, this is not the game you're looking for. This game may have the look and feel of BioShock, but it's a far cry from it. But is that why I don't recommend it? No.This game is actually a walking simulator at best, with some horror elements to it. And I can tell you, the horror elements mostly don't work. You move slow, and ever your "sprinting" is just a slightly accelerated walk. And if you get caught by the bad guys, you'll have to suffer by watching yourself get killed over and over again, which can put you off.It's not a bad game per say. It looks beautiful with its art deco environment, but it just doesn't do it for me. If this is too close to the sun, then seek refuge with other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is terrible, it's not scary and the mechanis of using items is annoying. You need microscope precision to open doors or take a ladder, but also for jumping over crates. Be prepared to die many times when you're running for your life because the jump button doesn't activate getting past crates.The font of the note is too small to read from your TV, and you can't increase it.The graphics are nice and art deco, but you can also go to a museum for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Close to the Sun is absolutely packed with flavor items, not just in the few you can interact with, but in the letters and drawings scattered all around the floors and the walls.  It's really fun to explore the environment, and I appreciate the care that went into making sure even tossed aside documents on the floor had real words on them.If only that care had extended to the gameplay, this game might have been really fun for me.  But it didn't, so it wasn't.  This game is a point and click (everything can be done with the right mouse button) narrative story with jump-scare and chase-run "combat".  The point click was difficult sometimes, to get the target lined up just right...not too close, not too far away, or too far off center...which is...not the center of my monitor when I line it up with the icon.  Which isn't SUPER annoying accept when you're trying to do it while running away from things.  The jump-scare was pretty decent in the first, maybe 2 chapters.  Every aspect of this game drops off in the last 4 chapters, jump-scare was gone by then.  The chase and run...holy freaking crap I have NEVER HAD TO RUN SO SLOW IN A GAME BEFORE.  Like...you know when you have a dream and bad guys are chasing you but when you scream it comes out like super muffled or quiet and you're super sure no one can hear it but you?  Yeah, the running is like that.  Like you're running away...but as a novice level speedwalker.  It's SO BAD.  So like, the thing about this game is that it's really short.  10 Chapters and the last 2-3 are legit joke length.  And when your game is short and you want it to be longer, a SUPER effective strategy is to slow the player down using stupid MF mechanics that make the player want to gouge their flipping eyeballs out more than unskipable cutscenes.  This game does that with...slow running, slow sidewalking around tight spaces, SUCH slow long crawling tunnels, ladders that defy GD MF physics in their endlessly extending rungs, and slow jumping.  Did you know, if you press space bar your character jumps?  Not over anything...not even that really low barrier right over there.  You can't SEE your character jump, you just hear her.  Very rarely there are objects you can jump over as indicated by the icon that pops up.  You can use spacebar instead of right mouse button for that.  It works...idk maybe 50% of the time when you're moving "fast"?  Six of one, half a dozen of the other!  And oh, it's not just controls and mechanics that are annoying, it's also event triggers.  Dialog starts playing frequently while you are still outside whatever room it's in.  Stupid to spoiler the moderately engaging storyline when it's pretty much the only thing this game had left going for it.In the end, I wasn't a fan of this game.  I wanted to be, I really love this setting, the steam punk Tesla stuff, so fun.  BUT....if I'm honest with myself, if it were any other setting I would rate this game a zero and toss it away in chapter 2.  So...like...1 star?CRAP I'm super high.  LEFT MOUSE BUTTON....left...wait...I'm pretty sure.  I'm like 97% positive it's left.  It's really difficult for me to tell right now cause like...I am using my RIGHT hand to move the mouse and click.  So like....my mind says left but my mouth says right.  Pretty sure my mouth is full of ♥♥♥♥!
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where if I was just discussing the design, the basic quality of the dialogue / characterisation, or the graphics, I could be pretty positive and wax lyrical about it. But when it comes to the game itself..... urghhhhh...that's a harder aspect to muster much energy for, so why waste time doing a big old song and dance setting the scene about the rest of it.It's set at the beginning of the 20th century, and uses historical figures to build its fictional narrative. Nikolai Tesla, the chap who created electricity, has gathered a group of scientists upon a boat called the Helios.These great scientific minds have been set free to push the boundaries of invention, and inevitably have done gone ♥♥♥♥♥♥ things up royally with their experiments. Faecal matter gonna be hittin' the fan big time.You play as Rose Archer, whose sister Ada is a scientist aboard the Helios. Having received a letter begging her to come to the vessel, Rose sets off to investigate. What awaits her arrival? Well, that would be spoilers. But I can tell you what awaits you as the player.Getting bored out of your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mind by a tepid walking simulator. It takes bloody ages for anything to happen, and when it does it's a chase sequence that for whatever reason just doesn't nail being pant-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrifying. Then you play for another hour or more with ♥♥♥♥ all happening, before getting another chase sequence that failed to get my adrenaline pumping, or my heart pounding.In between these distinctly mediocre and simplistic bouts of "gameplay" there are a couple of effective jump scares, albeit nothing particularly subtle or clever. You walk along and something goes bang, or a nut job pops up and goes "oooga wooga" before running off. It startled me, but scared? nope, and that's not because I have nerves of steel either. It's just that the game is so familiar with it's choices for instilling fear, and is then a bit pish when it comes to doing anything more than ham-fistedly aping "horror tactics 101"Sometimes you'll have to jump over obstacles during these running sequences, and it doesn't feel as smooth as, say, Outlast. It kind of punctures the tension of "I'm in a race for my life, can't slow down!....Except to slightly sluggishly, and awkwardly, vault this table". It might even be an intentional attempt at racking up the fear by forcing you to slow down, but that lack of fluidity to your movement just makes it feel clunky. And the ease with which these events can be completed, both in terms of the number of attempts taken to complete (3 maximum at most, and even the later ones are not challenging) and the absence of any terror, shows a lack of skill in building up tension.They're tedious rather than exciting. Which just leaves the story, and that is passable at best. The tone is grim and serious, but the most memorable elements come from a character who is blackly humourous and seems somewhat out of place.Emotive beats just don't hit home, and the science fiction / drama etc are all unoriginal and underwhelming. It's all a bit bland, despite having a fair bit of oomph visually in it's design and technical prowess.  Having finished it I'd have to say that it really doesn't come together all that satisfactorily. It hasn't tried to be overly clever and deliver a twist ending, but I don't think it nailed some of the elements. There's not a feeling of much being at stake, and without going into spoilers quite a few things feel like  their explanations are either a bit rushed, or just glossed over as "timey wimey" stuff. Maybe if you're more clued up on time travel / relativity than I am, it might make more sense.In a nutshell this is a visually slick, seemingly fairly capable technical experience, with impressive design. And that's it. The gameplay is distinctly "meh" with something like 5 sequences of insipid running away, and the story, whilst reasonably written and voice acted, is pretty "meh" too. It's a 5 out of 10 game, so no recommended. Not so awful that I couldn't bring myself to finish it, but having done so I can't think of one single thing about it, beyond that oh-so-reflective surface level of it's art deco styled looks, to get even vaguely enthusiastic about.If you found this review to be helpful then why not check out my curator page here:

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game, due to how good the trailers looked. Well worth it. I was not disappointed. It looks good, it sounds good, it has tons of atmosphere, and I really liked the story. The story is also just the right length. This is the first user review I have actually written for a game. Normally I don't bother but this obscure gem deserves more attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the general aesthetics (although some minor things did not make much sense to me, at least compared to similarly styled Bioshock), but the rest... Gameplay wise it's your regular waslking simulator with a couple of chases. Characters are largely underdeveloped (collectables do not help much), The story is underdeveloped, too. The ending kind of begs for a sequel, so lore and cahracters can be, potentially, expanded, if it ever happens, but... Would you be willing to continue, when you do not feel much connection to Rose? Very difficult choice for me.Then there were also sudden dips in FPS for no apparent reason and you can't adjust brightness in game. My laptop has a decent monitor, but I had to put its brightness to 100% and still some places were too dark. I mean to an extent you could not see a thing even with high brightness. Perhaps shadows were too thick? I do not know.For aesthetics - 8, maybe even 9 at places with enough light. For the rest - probably a 6. Definitely grab it on discount if you like this kind of steampunk style. For the rest... Maybe if there is a sequel, grab it in a bundle, once it's available.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry to say, but this game is boring, bad, empty and not worth its full price.I bought it with a discount of 50% and still feel I paid too many.I had to think some time to even find one unconditionally good element.And this one are the easy to get Achievements, so with some open eyes it is easy to get 100%.But thats it and the rest of the review is just a listing of the bad things.The graphic looks impressive in some scenes, but in general it feels lifeless (no pun intended) and works bad (lags) on even a system over the recommended settings.The "monsters" you encounter feels not unique for what they should represent. I had a flashback to the vortigaunts from Half-Life. The gameplay feels wrong, as the movement and "exploring" is slow like for an adventure, but there are no adventure elements.This is just a walking simulator with some buttons to press or levers to push/pull. But maybe I'm wrong myself and this should be a monster avoding game like Amnesia.But this also doesn't work, as the "monsters" have no own path or so. Your encounter or better escape from them is put into a sequence, with so strict limits in time and movement, that you even die a lot if you know excactly where to go for an escape route.So from the short time of 3,5 hours to finish the game you can even take away 0,5 hours for dying unnecessary.Btw, the more hours in my account are just from waiting for all trading cards to drop ...The setting - that sold me the game in the first place - feels so wasted. Yes, Nicola Tesla and some of its visions and thought or build inventions are the base of this game. But thats it. They are just there. No puzzles or story elements that fit this man. He could easily be replaced by a fictional inventor. And then the "clever" ending. Nothing is explained at all to then "fit" the mystery of Tesla? Maybe I'm to dumb (or too uninterested) to see some hidden clues for a depper story or some explaining elemets. But how am I supposed to think so deep in a such a shallow game?
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I would say it's a good experience playing this game, and I enjoy the world view as well as the art design. However, as a game, it lacks multiple aspects. First of all, the STORY is, at least as I view it, unfinished. So many key plot left unexplained, such as how the letter came back, or why Tesla was alive, or what is the EXO leak. Second, the gameplay is quite simple and can get people bored after a while, since it's basically a walking simulator. I noticed some potentials, such as the Death Ray, First Aid kit on the wall, charging port (could be?), looks like this game is not complete and might be turned into something like Bioshock. Third, the storytelling is not great. The game seems give me a lot of information or background, yet the documents I collected and the texts within the game don't really explain anything actually. They are piles of fancy words making the game and setting seems high-end, yet can not cover its hollowness. After the game there are left no satisfaction or surprise, but more questions and a sense of "oh finally I get this done".Over all I would say get it for a discount price and spent perhaps three hours to finish all, if you are a fan of Bioshock series and enjoy the art style. Otherwise, wait and see if there will be an update on the game to make it complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: This was a mostly enjoyable experience in my opinion. The game is pretty short (about 4-7 hours depending on how many of the notes and collectables you try to find). The visuals are a treat throughout most of the game, and the voice acting is quite good most of the time. The gameplay is mostly walking simulator type gameplay with some chase sections sprinkled in as well. The chase sequences are more of an annoyance than anything in my opinion, as it can be hard to tell where you're supposed to go, and slowing down or making even once mistake during them causes you to die.I think you'd be best off waiting for a sale on this because of it's short length, but I do think it's worth the time it'll take to get through it if you do decide to buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Very 'cheap' horror. Nothing but jump scares and gore. Some cool themes to explore, but instead the devs opted for frustrating trial-and-error chase scenes and puzzles that may only challenge toddlers. The voice acting is also really bad. The game is set in the late 1800s, but the main character and her sister talk like social media influencers, and the guy doing the voice for Nikola Tesla makes him sound like some sort of Looney Tunes character. Kudos to the environmental design team though, the art style of the architecture and props is wonderful!
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Most FRUSTRATING game I've every played. I refuse to believe they play tested this.No brightness adjustment in a game where everything is very dark; neither can I switch the screen it's played on. I've missed half the details in a truly brilliant visual design. Rose is the most inept character ever to exist; I've gotten stuck in the middle of a level because of an office chair. You have to center the screen on an action prompt to preform certain actions and it's difficult while running away from a murderer with with knife. And she walks. so. insufferably. slow. it's. painful. Death scenes cannot be skipped, are traumatic as you constantly have a knife plunged into your face/neck, and the game reloads with about 2 seconds before the murderer catches up to you again; no prompt to continue. I keep dying because I can't see where I'm running. Cut scenes are PAINFULLY long, take control away from the player without telling them when they've regained control, and cannot be skipped.It's like an elegant wedding cake in which the baker dropped a microscopic turd in the batter. What would have an otherwise brilliant experience is completely ruined by basic AND FIXABLE design choices.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a big fan of Horror games, because the constant suspense is just exhausting for me after 1-2 hours, so I was a bit afraid that I wouldn't like close to the sun, but it was fine.It's more like an Adventure games with some creepy elements and fleeing sections, but no jumpscares or real horror/danger.The world is klind of interesting, but the story and background is unfortunately a little bit bland.Characters, voices and worldbuidling are fine and kind of reminds me on Rapture in Bioshock. Worth a playthough if you like Adventures and want some horror elements in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Would recommend it on sale & if you have a newer computer."Is it like Bioshock?"City surrounded by water - yepScience gone wrong - yepTalking with a radio - yepand similar art style.But it's a walking simulator. Where I'd rate Bioshock 9/10 this is more a 6/10.Pretty good story & length considering a walking sim, but eh ending and set up for a sequel. For it's time decent graphics, but not the newest. More ps4 than ps5 for console comparison, but it's not always smoothly running. For reference I have a 2070 super and it wasn't always stable, but not unplayable. Chase sequences get old quick, but thankfully the checkpoint system starts right before them. However there's no way to save mid chapter, and have to rely on it saving at the start of a chapter. Didn't know that and had to replay a bit. Timing on some puzzles and chase sequences could use a little more leeway and less instant death. Overall it's ok on sale price.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Is the strive for technological advancements no matter what the costs are and such a pursuit is a righteous thing? does it really matter what we do as long as we are advancing our race and reaching that next new thing? and truly, do the ends really justify the means?The Helios is the literal, physical embodiment of that question in the form of the biggest ship to ever sail, a colossal wondrous that not only in itself but in what it carries also, the most intelligent minds of that time in all specialties, all working towards one goal: the future.What interested me the most is the Helios state (when you arrive in it) and made me wonder, is such fate always inevitable whenever we possess great powers? can we humans not always end up in utter tyranny at the same time as we end up controlling limitless resources and infinite energy? is the: "If it was me in their place, none of that would have happened" a valid statement? or is it just part of us as humans to always stray away towards self-destruct -somehow- as we reach new heights? and most importantly, and I think what all of us should be asking ourselves after playing this game is: "Can science alone unlock the path to enlightenment?"Overall nice game and I think BioShock games were a great source of inspiration for this one, it shows in the atmosphere, in a very distinct part of the gameplay, and overall the feeling of it. I enjoyed it despite how the game was lacking in some areas such as animations, but however the good thing is that it doesn't dwell on those areas much so they are almost unnoticeable, for example, you rarely see humans moving up close, etc., even in cutscenes, they are blurred in a way to cover what they lack, same goes with faces and their details and animations.The Helios is vast and quite the sight and the game does look good, collectibles are 50/50, you either get something interesting to read or worthless stuff and so is voice acting actually, Rose's was good in my opinion, the rest were not as good and it shows, the gameplay is never bored me and it's not really a horror game more than just an adventure.And if you can come out of it questioning the nature of humans and their relationship with Power I think it was time well spent..recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: This review covers Close to the Sun.I Love games that are inventive and fun. I don't play games, Usually with a controller.This has controller enabled and I was having trouble figuring out the keys for actions.The controller became my friend. I was able to move around for the first few hours like a wild drunk.But then the controls made sense and I was able to move less like a drunk.I have real issues with controllers, but that did nothing to dampen my fun with Close to the Sun.This game is stunningly beautiful. It isn't restrictive and clumsy like a controller game. The game thats so beautiful you forget everything, at least I did.You'd have to play it to see what I'm talking about.Controls responsive and a bit much for me and the controller, but Really good controls.Game play is so entrancing I cant even give you a description of the game.I just know I learned what I needed and the game was kind to a death or two, and a novice, and let you eventually by any difficult places. Its player friendly but not so easy, you'll wonder what to do for long.I would give this is a gift, Id get it for my self, and then play it late like I do!It is that much fun! The plot centers around a Vessel you are traveling in and Tesla and Edison.There are a LOT of things that will electrocute you. The story is so twisted I still havent gotten my head around it; its that convoluted.10/ 10 for game play9/ 10 story and game10/ 10 for the beautiful scenery. Its lush.Buy this game. I did as a risk and it was a great gamble. I Dont usually pay full price but this I think was on sale, even if it wasn't I Still would get this game. Its worth every cent.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely little Indie game with gorgeous graphics. Certainly a love letter to Bioshock's aesthetic. Perhaps a poorly researched historical character, but a very fun game well worth the time. The puzzles are for the most part intuitive. I have seen reviews saying the chases are too hard, they are very simple and it is not hard to see where to go. The most frustrating thing about the game is AWFUL hitboxes, it can be incredibly hard to get something to activate. Overall really good for what it is and it accomplishes what it set out to do. If you want a fun, visually lovely indie experience, here it is. Great soundtrack too.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are great, that's definitely the strong point of the game.Story is cool, has an interesting setting with the Tesla vs Edison thing.The gameplay is very linear, and uses several known tropes that I won't mention here because spoilers. Then there's the chase sequences. These are plain annoying. You have to escape an enemy that's chasing you, having to quickly decide which way to go, often resulting in insta death. The game would be much better without these imo.Is it bad? No. Is it awesome? Not really. Do I recommend it? Yeah, it's good enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A deeply flawed game lacking a significant amount of polish. It draws heavily from Bioshock, but misses what makes Bioshock entertaining.Some things to note:You have a jump. It is literally pointless. It's like, a three inch vertical and actually slows you down when you land.There is no flashlight. The game is really dark at times, and the only solution is to bump gamma up to the maximum.This game falls into the trap where they put tech everywhere to fill void space, even when it's out of place. Why is there a four ton engine in a cafe?There is no crouch button. This game leans heavily on the Amnesia style "unable to fight back" trope and it squanders the enemy sections by making them simple chase sequences. The human models at a glance are passing decent, but the sheer ubiquity of corpses means you're going to see the same model over and over, sometimes in the same area.If you like an atmospheric walking sim that takes inspiration from Bioshock, this'll occupy about six hours of your time. But it's deeply flawed.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Oh no! It's not very good.It's a retrofuturistic alternate history walking simulator, and ♥♥♥♥ it, why not throw schizo science delusions in there for good measure. It's so poorly optimized that it overloads my 2080 to render everything, then hide it behind poor lighting.It rewrites Tesla's entire personality while still seemingly understanding random tidbits (e.g. love affair with a pigeon) of his life that make me wonder why exactly they chose Nikola Tesla for the story instead of literally making someone up.I am one of the three people who actually enjoys walking simulators, so I should have like this one, right? Nope. It's bad. There is no room for exploration or problem solving. There's a bit in chapter... 3, I think, where I found the problem I needed to solve (shutting off an emergency generator) but I wasn't allowed to do it because I hadn't tried to do something else first. So it wants your brain turned off. If I'm not thinking and I can't see anything, what exactly is the point to this game? This massive ship (that's a whole other thing... like I get that we're pretending Tesla did all sorts of things in this dumb game, but maybe they should have talked to marine engineers to understand what's remotely feasible today, let alone a hundred years ago) conveniently only has environments directly related to the story, meaning that there's exactly nothing you are allowed to do that doesn't progress the story. When I decided to just shut my brain off, it was still bad. The whirring of my GPU fans were the only comfort I had, knowing that in addition to wasting money on this game, I also got the pleasure of wasting money redlining my GPU just to 'play' a game I couldn't even see.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Not exciting, and I wasn't sure what to expect. Close to the Sun has several chapters starting at the elevator door opens at one floor, and ending with the door closes to the upper level. However, each floor has a similar setting, which makes it hard to keep my interest up.The entire place is a mystery, notes are scattered but contain little info. Besides, many times I walked a long way/climbed stairs just to pick a confusing note, anyone may lose patience in this frustrating way.However, it is not that desperately bad - The surreal/supernatural settings of ghosts walking at a station inside a house, and that the slaughter scene is alright. I gave up after an hour of gameplay, too painful to continue.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Close to the sun is a pretty walk simulator but just like Icarus it got his wings burn .I do belive this game could be alot more in terms of history and action for has much it looks good graphically ( and that includes the blurriness if you get too close to a window and such ) it is a 50/50 for me to advise someone to buy it at full price .Ps : do relase a dlc for that ending it was pretty bad in my opinion .
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: So I'll start with the good, I picked up this game because I had heard it was like Bioshock which is my all time favourite game, I even have a Bioshock tattoo, and as far as the look and feel of the game goes that part does not disapoint. It looks absolutely gorgeous all the art deco is beautifully realised and the sense of scale they have managed to create is just stunning! The voice acting is great, the music is wonderful and the soundscape is awesomly atmospheric. Same with the story and characters no complaints here, all really great.I even liked the puzzles even though they are pretty easy to figure out.Now on to the bad, it is so so dark, the well lit parts look so wonderful I just wanted a torch so I could light up the rest of it and look at everything. However this isn't a big problem its just cosmetic, except when you have to run and dodge, which you do...a lot...As for the 'running', for a game that asks you to run to avoid enemies, the running is only a snails pace faster than walking, its resident evil levels of slowness, like being mired in mud most of the time. Meaning unless you are exceptionally lucky or just very spacialy aware ( I am not) you are going to find yourself repeating the running segments again and again and again and again and again...some what frustrating and I came so very close to rage quitting on several occasions.There are also a few sections where I had no clue what to do, I just kept pressing levers and turning dials getting killed again and again by lightening until I finally pulled enough levers or turned enough dials to make something happen which meant I could blunder into an exit.On a few occasions, I kept going purely because, the gamed just looked so damn pretty.So to conclude looks amazing! Great story and characters but prepared to be frustrated by repetition. Would I recommend this game? Steam really does need a neutral rating.Having said that I would be interested to play any further games from this developer,
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Well, Close To The Sun... maybe. But far from delivering a satisfying experience. Starting with a bad pun, are we? Yes, because I wasn’t even trying, just like this game. Even if your idea for a game is decent, it fails if it resembles too much of... better titles. Close To The Sun is definitely in love with Bioshock, even if genres don’t match. Aesthetics, overall feeling, themes ... even some plot points. Well, Bioshock doesn’t have a monopoly on Victorian steampunk/diesel punk or whatsoever... Yes, indeed, but I had that game in mind, all the time. Thinking I should play Bioshock instead.Close To The Sun is a story driven adventure game, walking simulator. The story part never really “clicks”, unfortunately. Undeveloped ideas, lots of pseudoscientific mumbling, no “wow” factor, no plot twists. Brain dead puzzles don’t help. What is a point of an obstacle that 3yo can solve? We all know - adding few minutes of gameplay to 4h game. There’s like dozens of better games. Just skip this one. It brings nothing new to the “walking sim” genre. It’s a rehash. Dull, uninspired.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhat mediocre game.The best thing in the game is the art design, very BioShock like. Graphics are quite good too.But the performance is rather bad, especially in chase sequences, I often get only like 19 fps there. Btw. my graphics card is a GTX 1070 Ti and I don't have those performance issues usually.The story begins interesting and gets really interesting at a certain point, but then it gets really boring and bad. Like the twist is just ripped off BioShock and I knew the twist basically at the very start of the game.And then the ending: It is so cheap and so disappointing. Sadly because of the ending I can't say that this story is good. Characters are ok, at least the voice actors are good.Gameplay is what you would expect from a walking simulator with a few (quite easy) chase sequences here and there.I guess if you are a (big) fan of the genre you can play and kinda enjoy it, but for everyone else: skip it.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Close to the Sun is an ambitious game that ultimately gets in its own way and falls flat. As great as the environments are, you won't get a chance to enjoy them because the lighting does not cooperate to show off the work the developers put into the game. It took me 5 hours to get through, and too much of that time was spent getting lost because I couldn't see where I was going. This is especially frustrating during the chase sequences where failing to find the right path quickly transforms fear into aggravation. What's worse are parts where you need to interact with the environment, as missing the click to progress means an unskippable 10 second death animation followed by starting the event over again. It felt like surviving those threats were meant to be trial-and-error situations rather than obstacles I could have been able to complete on my first try. 	The plot is an exceptional letdown. There was enough story given to lay a solid foundation, but it was barely explored at all. Character motivations don't make any sense, and some actions taken are even more confusing. The player is required to suspend a substantial amount of disbelief while playing through this game, and by the time I had gotten through chapter 4 or 5 of 10, I was completely disinterested in what was being presented. I gave the game the benefit of the doubt and continued playing only to end up disappointed. 	I also had issues dropping frames. There were pregnant pauses throughout the game, and large lag spikes when entering an open area for the first time. If too many light echos spawn, the game would grind to a halt. I’m playing with a 5700 non-xt on 1080p, so this should play like butter. But even during the ending credits, I couldn’t get the names to scroll smoothly; every few seconds a few lines sputter out before going back to a regular crawl. 	This game has a lot of good going for it, but the issues are so overwhelming that they’re really not worth mentioning, and I can’t recommend playing it. If you’re curious about what this game is like, there’s a 3 hour longplay on YouTube without commentary. It’s a much better experience watching someone who knows what they’re doing walk through the game than it is trying to manage it yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Bioshock minus all the combat. And instead of Rapture, you’re on an absurdly large boat. That’s this game in a nutshell.What you’ll notice right away are the graphics and atmosphere, both of which are superb. That’s the main draw of the game. If you can’t run this at high settings, I would skip it because it doesn’t offer much in terms of gameplay. You walk around solving fairly easy puzzles. No combat, as you’re forced to run from enemy encounters. The characters and story feel a little unpolished, but it was a small development team.But again, the main attraction is walking around and soaking in the gorgeous environments. Some of the larger sets (like the Theater) will really blow your mind. Other reviewers complain about the save system and chase sequences. Those are legitimate critiques. But you shouldn’t be playing this game because of interesting mechanics. You should be playing it because you want to explore a beautiful fictional world.If that appeals to you, then go for it. Personally, I prefer games that are a bit more active.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Close to the Sun has a mildly intriguing story set within a detailed and exquisite setting.=====As I've only played over an hour (at the time of this review), I will keep this short, and to the point. In such a short playtime, I have come to a few conclusions regarding this game that most will notice right away:1) This game feels heavily, heavily inspired by Bioshock. Not solely because of the Art-Deco aesthetic, but also due to some of the choices in representation of story materials and word-choice. The phrase "The Circle Must be Broken" echoing "Will the Circle be Unbroken?" from Bioshock infinite. The introduction of Time Travel early-on (not a spoiler, its a plot-point from practically the get-go), and creepy, seemingly deranged people running around on-board the vessel also lead heavily into Bioshock territory as well. Not only this, but 'memories', as I'll call them, are also present - a particle-effect representation of a humanoid form, reliving and moving within the space to show representation of past events. Again, heavily Bioshock inspired. The pneumatic mail system? Basically the Pneumo from Bioshock. The earpiece communicator? Basically the radio from Bioshock, but more portable... see what I mean? This isn't necessarily a bad thing; however, it can't help but be more than just noticeable.2) The introduction of Nikola Tesla as the "Andrew Ryan" of the game. Am I the only one that seriously dislikes the trope of throwing Tesla into fiction for the sole purpose of beefing up a story line? I would've preferred it if they had gone the Bioshock route, and created their own fictional genius, akin to the Lutece twins from Infinite. I hate to repeat this comparison, but its far too abundant and obvious. Now I'm just waiting for a "Sinclair" to make an appearance.. 3) The Helios is gorgeous. From water fountains and indoor park areas, Tesla coil 'displays' showcasing the wiring/power system of the ship, and small attention to details present in scenery, its a pleasure to explore. The ambience is well-suited, the design is meticulous, and the thoughtfulness shown towards environmental story-telling in certain areas is a nice additional touch.4) The soundtrack, score, sound effects, and sound design are on-point from the moment the game starts. 5) The attention to detail overall. From the start of the game where the protagonist shuffles papers in her hands as she reads, then slides the chair back into place, realistically, while standing up to move, and the visual representation of her moving through the spaces is just so well-crafted and polished to a degree showing dedication and care to the end-result. My only gripe is that the controls (on keyboard) are a little stiff, when navigating, as she doesn't move that swiftly through large environments so it can feel like a trudge, the jumping mechanic is a joke (although somewhat realistic due to having a short recovery), and the only means of interacting within the environment itself is "Press to interact". That said, its simple, effective, and is a means to an end. For one who wishes to slow down and soak in the atmosphere, these issues aren't really issues at all.=====Do I recommend?I absolutely do... for a good price. Close to the Sun has got its appeal, aesthetically and otherwise, and is worth checking out for the atmosphere, visuals, and sound design alone. I'll continue to play this, after writing this review, and update as I go, if it requires it. But so far, I'm enjoying it enough to feel confident reviewing it so early on. If the story picks up a little bit more, it'll be a hit. If not, I won't be too Shocked.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Solid sci-fi story.  Enjoyed the design of the Helios, the alternate history tale told through good voice-acting and collectibles and even the chases didn't bother me.  Ends on a bit of a cliffhanger but I'd play the 2nd one.  There's nothing overly complicated here; switch puzzles, exploration, discovering world-building with some challenge added by the chases.  The one in chapter 8 is a jerk but it's do-able.  I don't go into plot detail much but the story on this one is you are a journalist (Rose) boarding Tesla's great watercraft the Helios, trying to find out what happened to her, the crew and the scientists on board.  At the end of this one I felt like the story and it's delivery was a high-point that kept me going even when the gameplay started getting a bit samey.Everything looks and sounds great, plays smoothly and I didn't find anything too particularly janky about this one than crawling through vents and the speed at which that happens is total murder.  If you're looking for an adventure/exploration/walking sim focused over a compact experience with some danger of death and challenge added this is a pretty good one to get.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: ***SPOILER FREE***It has been 13 years since Bioshock came out and thrilled the world with it's vivid setting of an Art Deco City underwater, rife with beauty and horror, and 7 years since Infinite left a poor final taste in our mouths of that franchise. But one year ago, Storm in a Teacup, decided they wanted to make their own Bioshock, but as a horror walking sim. The results are somewhat mixed as I dive into my 5 hours into the game start to finish, and put down to thought what I think. So first off the setting is a real hook if I ever heard one. It's an alternate 1897 where Nikola Tesla, instead of winding up as a sad homeless man sitting on a bench with pigeons until his death, he succeeded against Thomas Edison and has become a Scientist Superstar, netting both fame and glory, as well as quiet envy and concern from the world powers at the time. Tesla's tower worked and now powers half the globe with wireless electricity, while fighting over the other half with Edison and General Electric. Also somehow he built a freaking super ocean liner that contains basically a city called The Helios to bring on any Man and Woman with a giant brain to do science stuff in the middle of the Atlantic.One of those scientists was your Sister, Ana, and you, Rose, must take a small Steamboat to the derelict liner in a storm to find your sister, and uncover what exactly happened to Tesla's ship along the way.That is where I stop on the plot because the rest is too interesting and spoilery to go on about, so I can only hope if you're on the ball and reading this, that my review convinces you to give the game a shot. Speaking of which it's time to talk Pros and Cons.Pros:The story is, as I said, quite an enthralling one. It's the rare walking game where you do want to know more about the ship and what happened to it. Also, the Ship itself is just BEAUTIFUL. Storm in a Teacup really went all out to make most of the environments looks stunning in Unreal engine. My personal favorite is the Theatre chapter, which is just incredible to marvel at, graphics wise. Exploring every nook and cranny to find all the environmental story pieces isn't much of a hassle as there is a sprint button to get around some sections faster, and some of the puzzles, while not really engaging, aren't much of a chore to deal with. But sadly, I must now to the "other" side of the gameplay, which is where things are, well, not good.Cons:So there are two parts of gameplay. Medium-Long pieces of walking around, doing puzzles and exploring the levels as you go on, and, chase sequences. Yes there are things to run from, what they are I will not spoil, but there are enemies. There is no stealth, and since this is a walking horror game, no means of self defense. Also no hiding either, it's always a chase sequence and nothing more. You get to a part, and have to just run from whatever is chasing you for a short period, and this is where it falls apart because it's very trial and error. I have died most times from basically bull plop catching up to me while I was holding the sprint key going down a corridor with nothing in my way, just to arbitrarily die. There is no manual save either, just checkpoints, so you need to hot foot it the right way as soon as you spawn, or else die again in a , might I add, UNSKIPPABLE death scene. It's not a long one, just annoying.Also while the graphics look nice, the game, weirdly chugs. I'm on a good computer rig that runs games like Fallout 4 and Sea of Thieves on high with little to no chug. Yet in the Prolouge I have to play with the options because the textures were blurry, then I turned some stuff on ultra and had FPS drop. So I set it to high settings and resolution scale to 100%, and the game ran fine for the most part, but still had chugs in certain sections. You would think that a year after release, Storm in a Teacup would fix that somehow for the Steam release, but nah.Speaking which, while not a big deal to myself I have to mention, some people are giving this game the finger, because it released on Epic Games's platform one year ago. I think the whole "Epic bad, Steam good" thing is pointless enough and doesn't factor into making a game better or worse; it's just pointless politics.Conclusion:While not a perfect game, the setting, story, and overall art direction of the game are gripping to me, making me excited for a potential sequel if they are working on one, as I do want more. I found it worth my money and time, even if kinda short, for the experience I got overall. If you, dear reader, can overlook the crap chase sequences, and occasional chug, this is a great story experience to check out. Otherwise, I would wait for it to go on sale if you don't like the "gameplay loop" of Close to the Sun.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: It's a beautiful game, the music and sound direction is superb, and the voice acting is not bad. However, the story, I don't know what happened but it felt rushed. They started something that felt interesting then didn't follow up. Nothing was really expanded on or explained and there was no conclusion. Everything else, pretty good. I liked that there were no insufferable stealth mechanics instead there were "chase sequences" which I thought was pretty good idea. It kept the game moving along and were fairly easy but if you get caught then you have to watch a fairly long animation of yourself getting killed which is a little annoying to sit through if you get caught again. Also, if you like gore, there's tons of it, blood and bodies everywhere very gratuitous!
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Highly enjoyable and gorgeous horror rideThe comparisons to Bioshock are beyond clear, but take away the shooty bang bang and swap the horrors of capitalism for scientific hubris instead,  Rather than this being a minus for any reason they're very different games and there's more than enough room for both!Visually this is a real treat, the setting is vast and awe inspiring, some of the set pieces are hair-raising and I just had a lot of fun playing this.  I didn't expect this to be quite as suspenseful as I found it!  Some of the horror elements are wonderfully designed.On the downside, a few sequences are a chore. They're beautiful, they're intense, they're hard as hell.  Not that you have do much beyond run from A to B but the tolerance of how fast you do it is so thin that at times it just feels like a coin flip between life or death.  One wonderful sequence that I really really love, has one area where the clear way to go is the wrong way, and you're meant to double back on yourself, but there's no indication of this, you just can't quite make it the way you think you have to go, after half a dozen deaths I found the correct way, it wasn't obviousAdding to that, death sequences are a bit too long. They're great but with the ease of how frequently you can die, they're far too long for comfort to see over and over!The game will absolutely max out your GPU regardless of model, turning resolution or settings down actually decreased performance!  It was still quite playable on my 1060 by myself but it's desperation to hog it meant that I couldn't stream it properly.  Bizarrely disabling my webcam entirely and only having the game capturing at 30fps made it playable and streamable, but turning the camera back on had it slam down to 4-10fps on stream!Finally, the story feels like it's unfinished, like it's set up for a sequel but.. not?  Like you're meant to work out what the missing pieces are but I feel there's too much unexplained, though what is present is really good. Very strange!
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like the obviously-Bioshock-derivative, linear walking simulator -- it's very pretty, although the atmosphere is overbearing -- but the chase and otherwise running about sequences were keyboard-smashingly irritating. I'll probably finish it, but I suspect once I've done so, my reaction will be relief at not having to play it anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: It is freely based on Tesla's inventions walking simulator through nice steampunk world but the story is the weakest point. The scenario can be written on one A4 page. This world is predefined for many great logical puzzles but they were replaced with stupid quick time events. You can hardly admire the world when you have to run fast through long passages of the game. If you are fan of Tesla, play it, there are some Tesla coils and sparks but all together it is a $5 game. Maybe when the creators had studied Tesla's patents a bit more, they would create aso better game, not only better 3D models.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as I thought. Too many "dumb" jumpscares, unforgiving death scenes, in the "end chapters", the general intuitive system (as in where to go) is sometimes missing. And too much badly scripted action moments. Besides that, it has a beautiful atmosphere, and interesting story, but a very predictable one (especially if you have played bioshock). The gameplay feels a bit subpar standards if you do compare it to a game like bioshock. It had a lot of promise, it just didn't live up to what I've seen in trailers and gameplay. Finished the game in 3.7 hours. But it's a good effort game from probably not an AAA company. Who knows, their next game, might be better. (haven't tried Martha is dead yet) I would have regretted buying this game full price, it doesn't feel like it would have lived up. Nice attempt from the devs, but there are just too many things they should have handled differently for a "walking sim" game. Especially the unnecessary "jump scares". (they aren't even scary, only the "scripted" sound makes you jump) I'm disappointed how the story develops and ends. Also a bit annoying for the azerty keyboard users. (you can't edit keys) Recommended? No... it's better to replay Bioshock.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent horror-themed walking sim.  The world on display here is well crafted, the voice acting is great across the board, and the game is visually stunning.  Game play elements boil down to some very simple puzzles and a few short chase sequences.  In this walking sim, the exploration IS the game play, and it is excellent.Unfortunately, there's not a lot of substance to the story.  It works well enough to move the player through the game, but there are some major plot points that go unanswered and unexplained.Overall, this is easy to recommend for any fans of creepy environments and well crafted levels, or for anyone who enjoys exploring abandoned locations.  One of the best exploration focused games I have ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly short wallking simulator / light puzzle game with great atmosphere.First of all, this game is fairly short, so I can only recommend it if you can get it for a low price.The graphics are pretty good, clearly a lot of effort has gone into modelling the environment and the lighting, although the character models and animations aren't very good. The game leans on the same Art Deco style popularised by Bioshock and the whole feel of a "rich man's world" is fairly familiar.The game is fairly linear, and none of the puzzles are very hard.Where the game stands out is in the writing and the voice acting, especially the character of Aubrey:Rose: "Are you okay?"Aubrey: "I'm using my co-worker's dismembered arm as a backscratcher, no I am not okay".Having said that, the plot doesn't fully resolve itself and there are a few aspects that don't really justify their existence other than providing obstacles for the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Beautiful VisualsWell ActedWell writtenCons:The worst jumping mechanic I've seen in a modern gameSome optimization issuesI somehow managed to softlock the game by making a jump the developers did not intend and the game does not handle sequence breaking gracefully.You are constantly blocked by things that are knee height or lower, things you could easily push out of the way or sometimes just invisible walls.Most of these things may seem nitpicky, but together they detract enough from the experience that I wouldn't recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A walking simulator with interesting premise, great atmosphere and music design.A walking simulator where devs couldn't figure out how to implement proper saving mechanism. I kid you not: the game saves only between chapters  and despite a visible animation of cycling cog in the right bottom on your screen at the pivotal moments, your progress will be reset if you exit the game without finishing chapter first.You may think that this is all fine, and you can speedrun the level again with no issue, well, 'speed' does not exist in this games dictionary: main character barely runs, jumps like she weights more than a ton, and all of her climbing animations are so slow you'd want to kill yourself. Additionally, even if you know what to do from the start the game just won't let you, because you'll need to follow a scripted narrow path of the story that you already know and hear all the 'marvelous' dialogues that you've already heard.Not worth your time, as it just doesn't respect it.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying, I only recommend this game if you can get it on sale.I just finished the game and it was... okay. I bought it purely because the aesthetic seemed very similar to Bioshock. The gameplay however, was nothing like it. It's just another cinematic story that you have to press W to progress. What you actually do in the game boils down to running and solving "puzzles" (and I use that term very loosely). The biggest kicker is that the game will have significant frame drops RIGHT as tense scenes begin. There were quite a few animations that could've used a little more time in the oven and the voice acting ranges from Okay to Pretty Bad. The ending was very disappointing as well. It felt like they were setting up for a sequel or something because it raised a couple of questions and set up another potential objective. The horror aspects are pretty weak as well. It's really just a bunch of jump scares.Spoilers:Overall it really just seemed like they wanted to make a good LOOKING game rather than a good game. Certainly not worth $19.99, but if you can get it on sale and have an afternoon to kill, go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time playing this game. The story was interesting and fun to follow and be part of, the characters and setting were gripping and just enjoyed playing the game. The visuals are also stunning in this game. Well worth a play through. Just to say as well others say about performance issues and bad controls, I had none. FPS was stable and over 60 all the time and controls seemed fine to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Really surprised at how good this game is. For those who played Bioshock you feel right at home, a lot of similar themes and style, in a good way. The environment is very detailed and beautiful, I did feel like I had to increase brightness a lot since the game tends to be pretty dark by default. I really like the lone atmosphere, the puzzles and discoveries along the way, great voice acting, and the story overall is captivating. Don't miss this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: OK attempt at a walking sim game. It seems like it wants to be scary, but it seems to just end up relying on jumpscares, which I just find annoying more than anything. The environments and atmosphere are generally good. The story is interesting - alternate universe inventor-era steampunk.What really kills it for me is the controls and movement. It feels incredibly sluggish and slow, even when running (which requires a constant button press), and I frequently find myself stuck against objects lying on the floor. Jumping is basically useless against such obstacles which makes me wonder why they even bothered to include it. Interacting with objects is painful as even though there is a button prompt (so the game knows what I'm looking at) I still have to centre it exactly in the screen before I get a different prompt and can then interact with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to have a more mixed review option, but overall I enjoyed my time with Close to the Sun. I love the setting, and the overarching story is interesting if a little predictable. The art direction is lovely, I enjoy Tesla-Punk aesthetic, and the world that we get to explore is interesting.However, the ending is really quite a let down, and there's really only about 4 hours of content, most of which is inflated by you bumbling around searching for collectibles which offer almost no real story input, they simply exist. I'd recommend picking it up on a sale, as even though it's a rather cheap price, I'm not sure it's worth $20 (I bought the digital deluxe to also get the artbook and soundtrack, no complaints on either). It's a worthwhile experience if you have a long afternoon to kill and you enjoy the idea of a Tesla-era mystery.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it's an acceptable value for full price and a good value on sale. It's not long, but focuses more on aesthetic than quantity. The writing is weak in some areas and the story would be better if it concluded, as of now it feels like half a game, unless I'm missing some kind of new game+ feature.It's a walking simulator with some running sequences. As such, it suffers from the walking simulator pathing that happens to take you where you need to go, which is unfortunate as the visual splendor encourages exploration.  Another thing that would have encouraged exploration would have been more scraps of peoples lives on the station. There is so little personality that it is razor focused on the characters at hand the tragedy of the situation is largely lost. What characters are at hand resolve with merely a passing nod, which is unfortunate. Aubrey, in particular, I was dissatisfied with his arc. Voice acting is flat but fine from all but the main character and her sister who feel pulled from our time and culture and plopped awkwardly into this 1920's alternate reality.Puzzles can't really be called puzzles, there wasn't a moment that made me have to pause and think. Me of middling intelligence. Collectibles are strewn about in incredibly obvious places and there is only ever one type per level. I made it a point to explore, but hardly scrounged and 100% most levels.Despite the flaws, it was a pleasure to walk through and ended on a positive overall impression.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: - Unoptimized levels and SFX which causing horrible FPS drops. Could lead to problems especially in chasing scenes- No baked shadows for static object looks horrible- Useless actions. You can jump but you don't need to jump anywhere- Stupid items collection which used only to prolong your playing time.- Ending left you with feeling that it's only a half of way and a lot of questions without answers.- No cloudsync. If you uninstall your game then you will need to start from the beginning.+ Good environment design+ Interesting Story
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly short. Not even 4 hours if you don't hunt down collectibles, which can get tedious. I would not recommend full price due to that and the relatively uninteresting gameplay, but if you can get it even half off, it's well worth the money. The setting is amazing, being a combination of steampunk and teslapunk, but also with amazing Art Deco architecture. I also bought this game purely after discovering Porcelain Pill's "Close to the Sun" separately, BECAUSE it was good.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Stylish adventure that plays and looks great in vr using uevr injector by praydog (set it to head aiming for easy interaction) which is the reason I bought it.Some stunning locations to explore, great graphics, sound and atmosphere, light puzzles, okayish story and voice acting. Chase sequences can get a bit annoying and trial and error but have fair save points and it is good to have some threats to keep you on your toes. There is a lot of gore that seems a bit random. Jumpscares exist and are well placed and not overdone.A sub instead of a ship could have been even cooler with some views of the ocean.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished a replay of this, but had first played this game on Epic Games a few years ago when it was offered during free week.  At some point I ended up getting it here on Steam during a cheap sale.  It's worth full price though, for sure. I would liken this game to a combination of Syberia (in the idea of automotons), Bioshock (in location and atmosphere), and SOMA (for the horror aspect) but with no combat.  It's more than a walking simulator though, in my opinion, because there is still quite a bit of interaction.  There is a deep story element as well and that is usually what really draws me into a game.  I wouldn't say it's super graphically impressive because it just isn't that kind of game, but that doesn't mean there aren't some beautiful screens to be captured.  The ship the story takes place on holds a lot of impressive environments, quite diverse for being a floating piece of metal.All in all, I think the Devs truly captured the essence of what they were going for, and I highly recommend this game for both those who like the relaxing feel of a walking sim game, but with a horror aspect that really doesn't let you relax, haha!
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: is a first-person adventure game with horror elements set in the alternate 1890s. + Interesting premise+ Beautiful graphics- Technical issues- Bad controls- Lack of quality of life features- Anticlimactic ending In alternate 1890s, world's top scientists create a giant ship, where they all gather to perform the most daring experiments. Naturally, everything goes wrong. You take control of , who was invited to the ship by her sister . As you arrive, you notice the lack of security and any kind of welcoming committee. It's not long until you find out the fate of those people, but I don't want to spoil anything, so I'll end here. Throughout the game, you will be communicating with two characters: your sister  and a guy named . The dialogue is pretty fun, there's lots of jokes and characters have a good amount of charisma. The plot, on the other hand, is not so good. It starts intriguing and mysterious, but the mystery is unraveled way too quickly. The second half of the game is very predictable and boring, mostly because you have no motivation to move forward other than finishing the game. The ending doesn't feel like it at all; it doesn't reveal anything behind the mystery and it doesn't change perspective on past events. The gameplay consists of two parts: walking around and solving simple puzzles and frantically running away from dangerous individuals. The first part is very easy, there aren't that many puzzles and those that are there usually require you to find some note, containing the code and then inputting said code into a lock. The game usually provides some info on where to find the code, even though most locations are so small, there's basically no place to hide anything from the player. On top of that, all the notes will be highlighted with a big icon, when you get close to them, so you won't miss them even in complete darkness. The only problem with this part is the walking speed. You will constantly hold the run button throughout the game, because your character is too slow. Moreover, the game saves only at the beginning of each chapter. So, if you decide to call it quits near the end of the chapter, the next time you start it, you will have to walk the same exact path again.The other part of the game is a lot harder and not because of its complexity. At certain points of the game, someone or something will chase your character and you will have to run fast, jumping over the furniture and choosing the correct passageway to run into. The first thing that makes it frustrating is how little the margin of error is. Run in the wrong direction or stay in place for a second and you're done for. The second thing is the controls. Jumping over the barricades requires you to get into a very specific spot and press the action button. There's a separate button for jumping, but it makes such a small jump, that it's a big question why it's needed in the first place. So not only is it hard to find the correct spot to jump, but you can also make a mistake of pressing the wrong button. When you die, the game would play a 10 second dying animation, that is unskippable, then it would make your screen go black for around 10 seconds more. If you got frustrated and put down your controller during that time, then you will most probably die again, because the chase sequence will begin automatically. There's no "press a button to play" message, it just starts up as soon as it finishes those animations.It's not a photorealistic game with lots of effects, but the design of each location certainly has a lot of love poured into it. It's very stylish and there's a lot of detail to each location. However, there's one big problem with the visuals, for the most part of the game you will stumble around in the dark without a flashlight. The game doesn't even have brightness settings, so you will have to tinker around in your monitor settings everytime you start up the game. The voice acting for the main character, her sister, and that Aubrey guy is pretty good. I really felt for those characters, but there's another character, that becomes important towards the end. He sounds like a mad scientist from a cartoon and completely ruins the immersion.Specs: AMD Ryzen 9 5900HX, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Laptop GPU 8GB, 32GB RAM.On the highest settings at 1080p resolution, the game delivers an unsteady framerate ranging from 100 to 200 FPS. The game does not provide an option to limit FPS, so if you have a high Hz monitor, you would have to use your graphic card settings app to set it to a comfortable amount. The game also has some issues saving settings, even when you disable antialiasing it gets reset to maximum of 6x every time you start a new chapter. It would be ok if it was providing better image quality, but with 6x antialising, the game starts to look very blurry.   has an interesting premise, but the execution is far from perfect. It's been two years since the game's release, so there's no hope that the issues I've described will be fixed. So if you want something similar to play, but with less frustrating cons, I'd recommend you to look for other games like ,  or .

_childDocuments_.review: It’s common to connote without any argument a game as a «spiritual successor» to another one. Sometimes it's good to let the game express for itself. This is the case of this game, in which it’s doable to notice an influence of ; although it takes its own detachment and it proposals a haunting narrative. What really caught my consideration when boarding the Helios ship was its story and visual narrative. Since the endeavour has focused on it. The developers took advantage of what they have, to create a great story. So I took a ticket and this is what I spotted.When boarding the ship after a sea tour, the design and art catch the eye. It's easy to confess an influence of Bioshock, Art Deco in its posters, architecture and colours. Although I include, the majestic, lustrous and imposing art discloses that it has influences from Futurism, an Italian avant-garde of art. But everything is submerged in a gloomy atmosphere, where darkness and death conquest the scenes.That has been done well, giving the feeling of horror and seclusion, but at the same time I can contemplate a radiant beauty of machines, inventions and places frozen in time. Like when sighting the splendour of the buildings in some abandoned city. The artistic work that has been achieved can be appreciated in three ways. First of all, a good combination of opposites has been prepared: light and dark, organic and inorganic, crowded places and machine room, just to mention a few. Secondly, the visual art can be comprehended in the various locations that are often detailed. This also includes the scientific air with which posters and blueprints mainly are exhibited to develop a context before the catastrophe.Thirdly, it has a steampunk touch with sci-fi ambiance, giving a perfect environment to develop a plot. For this, an exotic energy is taken as emphasis, which is represented through a bright blue mist. Or, there’s the representation of electrical energy standing the pillar of the world. The bad, there’re misuses of corpses —generic-looking objects—, lack of optimization in some areas and an excess brightness on objects which looks a bit distorted. The good thing, it has an enthusiastic artistic design. Each place is unique and it’s worth standing up to contemplate every detail.The story begins when Rose receives a letter from her little sister Ada. The plot takes place in an  world, where Edison and Tesla rule their technology over the world. So I go to the Helios cruise ship, a place where the brilliant minds of the epoch would congregate, and they could continue to accomplish their inventions, research and discovery. I’ll soon realize that upon arriving there, it seems to be uninhabited and a quarantine sign has been posted as a warning. The entire site is closed. They keep in communication, so the adventure commences by looking for her in order to get out from the mysterious cruise ship.If there's one thing I enjoyed about this game, it's the way it tells the story. Maybe its gameplay is not good, especially when escaping from enemies. Neither did the soundtrack due to its brevity and monotony. The story is fascinating, without a demand to carve out character sculptures, I just listen to their conversation through a first-person narrative voice. The simple and sometimes odd dialogues retain the player rapt, although always preserving an ambiguity that’s difficult to explain. Since a mixture between science and fiction was created, where Tesla is the centre of its inspiration.The chapters are short, and it often invites me to explore. Thus the experience in the game was prolonged. Each one of them bears a title of some deity from Greek mythology. Each god represents something in the plot part. And this is how Icarus burned his wings when he got so close and so far from Helios. While the context is set in a war of currents between Edison and Tesla. The way of telling the story tried to weave time, quantum field theory, and the ether transmits electrical energy, all related to Tesla. Although there’s more fiction than science.Also something that preserved my absorption was the form of the narrative. The story of the sisters is related as an alternative version of the flow of time, an alternative story in the form of a loop or cycle. Although it’s temporary and inspired by alternating current. The bad thing, there was not a great development in the narrative of the other dimension. Exotic energy monsters are almost relegated. Although there’s a predominance of ambiguity as its essence of the plot, the conclusion is biased. Everything ends without further ado, it becomes something evanescent. Even so, the central plot is noteworthy, where I can enjoy dialogues of the omnipresent characters.Indeed, the game is inspired by Nikola Tesla. Despite its gameplay and soundtrack are limping, it nevertheless offers an excellent plot with fascinating art design. Above all, I liked the way the game epitomizes Tesla's many inventions and projects. The visual effects and its atmosphere are well performed. The plot is undeviating; and without exploring, it becomes short. I played it a couple of times to dig into its narrative. For this reason alone, it deserves the opportunity to enter the world of the Helios cruise ship.

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable ~3 hour walking simulator that wears its BioShock inspirations on its sleeve. Close to the Sun benefits from striking visuals, strong artistic direction, beautifully detailed environments, and particularly great voice acting from its lead actress. The script is mostly enjoyable, save the occasional groan-inducing attempt at humor (the game does at one point dip into the cliche of a scientist explaining some simple concept using techno-babble, and another character unironically responding with "none of that  stuff, alright?").The atmosphere is well-developed and surprisingly creepy, peppered with the occasional tasteful jump scare that nicely leverages the game's Rapture-esque setting. A tense ambient soundtrack and sense of mystery keep the introductory hour appropriately suspenseful.Unfortunately, the story and tone kind of fall apart after the halfway point; gameplay largely shifts to just "run everywhere," and the many interesting mysteries set up by the plot are never explored. The ending is abrupt and feels pretty undercooked, leaving all the wrong kinds of dangling questions after the credits roll.Close to the Sun is definitely a walking simulator; I've seen people reference "puzzles" in the gameplay, but that is a pretty generous interpretation of the word. Progress is rarely barred by anything beyond a door with a numeric password that can be found scribbled on a nearby note. There are chase sequences, but they are marred by a trial-and-error map design, with no clear conveyance as to which path leads to a dead end around the corner. The framerate struggles during these scenes as well, very effectively sabotaging any tension they may otherwise have held. Thankfully that tension is restored during the slower sections of the game, where you creep through each doorway of this massive, doomed tanker, fearful of what lies on the other side.Not flawless by any means, but I enjoyed my time with this game. This is an easy recommendation, and I'll look forward to Storm in a Teacup's future works.
