_childDocuments_.review: For me, this isn't a thumbs up or a thumbs down. If there was a neutral option, I'd have given it a neutral review. However, the thing that pushes it over the edge for me not recommending it is the ending. More on that later. A lot of people complain that this game is short or that it's a walking simulator. Truth be told, I don't mind either of those things. Yes, it's not a very long game, and it is a walking simulator. I was quite intrigued for most of the game, actually. It has a nice steampunk aesthetic and the atmosphere has a very Bioshock type of vibe. However, as I played, I started sensing that the story was a bit weak and shallow. Underneath the initial glitz and glam of the environment, you come to realize that the game relies heavily on a sense of intrigue and vagueness. So much so that it becomes a detriment. I enjoy a good mystery very much, and I don't mind being left in the dark about what's actually happening in the plot, however... Let's just say that the game pushes the narrative from start to finish about there being some big, vague mystery. You feel as though you've set out on a quest to unravel this mystery. Every time you unravel something, there's even more layers of intrigue and mystery underneath. There's this sense of "all shall be revealed" dangled in front of you the whole game. You're in a beautiful steampunk, Bioshock-esque world, and you're unraveling what seems like a giant mystery. You don't really get direct answers. Instead, more and more promises of "all shall be revealed" if you just keep going and keep striving towards your goal. Finally, you get to the very end, anticipating some climactic revelation. Then... cliffhanger. The story ends abruptly. It feels extremely incomplete. You set out to find clues, unravel mysteries, and kept being driven by the anticipation that something big was going to be revealed in the end. Well, the game sort of stopped abruptly and awkwardly. It comes off as though it was specifically designed to go hand in hand with a sequel. However, I don't think that a part two is coming, so it leaves a bitter taste in your mouth, reminiscent of a TV show being cancelled after one season, ending on a cliffhanger. For those reasons, I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: While the atmosphere of the game is decent and the buildup to the story is definitely a worthwhile and interesting premise, it quickly chugs down into what feels more like a walking simulator. The tension and potential anxiety and/or terror that is shown by the trailer and the little 'action' sections of the videos you find on the store page are not properly translated over into the actual game.Overall? The concept is neat, the story as far as I got into it was clearly developed with time and effort, but it all goes downhill from there. The problem is that the trailer gives you the idea that there's going to be a quick buildup and then a full-on launch into the horror/tension aspects from there on out, but I didn't see any of that in my time playing.If you think you can deal with a walking simulator with some high and low points mixed in? This is probably for you. If you prefer something that has consistent action and drive all the way throughout? You'll likely be better off with something like Bioshock.

_childDocuments_.review: Close to the SunMy first thought when i started playing this game was not the greatest. You are starting at the ship, in alternative reality, in 19th century. Onboarding Helios or Wardenclyff, which is a massive ship full of greatest scientists in the world, including Nikola Tesla. And as soon as you found yourself in the docks, you could tell that i will love this game. All the online reviews were saying something about many similarities with Bioshock series. Personally, I´ve found this game to be less traumatic version of Alien Isolation. You see, you are on the huge ship, looking for your sister, everywhere you look are dead bodies, ship is falling apart and then, you see past in front of you. How bad the experiments with time must have gone wrong for you - the present - to see the past? Yeah. Amazing game. I´m glad that i bought this one. Gameplay is simple - you walk around, or run around, switching the levers and sometimes you have to run like run run run run run run run. Or you´ll die. It´s really not that hard. Kinda feels like walking simulator, but at the same time it´s not walking simulator and as you´re progressing throught the game, it´s story is revealing and even when you don´t have all the answers, it still feels rewarding, sort of. Soundtrack is great, really fits the atmosphere of the game, which was as well amazing. Amount of details that are in this game are insane! From specifically looking lightbulbs to blue prints plans, posters around...just wow. As I said, it feels like less traumatic version of Alien Isolation. More specifically - It´s like Alien Isolation, but without annoying Alien lurking everywhere, without androids that want to kill you, without so much collectibles to find, without weapons to fight with.. Almost same, but in different time, with different settings, and much more easier than A:I 5 or 6 times in the game, you will have to run for your life, but many of these you can get on the first try, which is nice and if you did any mistake in those run, it´s your death for sure. I was able to find all the collectibles on my first playthrough which was great as well. And graphically the game is looking really good. So:+ Great story that wasn´t done before+ Atmospheric + Easy gameplay + Great soundtrack+ Great locations + Believable voice actors- Little bit too short- Way to easy (at least for me)- It´s not possible to explore everything, or going back to where you came from

_childDocuments_.review: Short:Pass on this game until they work out the graphical issues. A time frame for a fully functional game based on the responses in the Community Hub appear to be, never.Update: Cloud saving doesn't work either. Yesterday put a new HDD in my PC after not playing this game for days and did a clean install of Windows and Steam. Downloaded this game and no saves restored themselves. Checked Cloud settings and 0 bytes were being used. This means there is no save data on Steam Cloud for this game.Explanation:Trying to enjoy this game is difficult and I really wish I could. It seems like it could be interesting and fun but the graphics that look pretty when not moving become a jittery mess when you do. You're constantly reminded that it's a game you can't have fun with. At first I thought it was my graphics card which is still really good but it's a couple years old. I upgraded from a GTX 970 to an RTX 2060 (specifically for this game) and while I noticed a difference, the short comings of the game still stand out. Every few seconds I experience a brief pause or stutter before moving forward every time I move. If there's any animation it really restricts the visuals further. With the specs I have I shouldn't have to manually make adjustments in the game files to play the game the way it's portrayed in the videos on the store's page. Because I will have to do that, I'm going to say don't get this game. If they fix the game then I can update my review and say if the game play is worth it. _childDocuments_.review: Imagine rage quitting a walking simulator. I don't know this is mostly a middling creepy walkathon that is meant to invoke Bioshock vibes but through the lens of Tesla/Edison fanfic. Probably would be a recommend on sale because while the game looks rather stunning the gameplay is okay at best. But then there's Ludwig. Some dude that pops up every few chapters to chase you and add actual stakes to the game. His first introduction was rather easy with a few restarts to correct making wrong turns, but the level 6 chase has to be broken. Upon my 30th death I'm calling it. It's literally running down a hallway, but he catches me at the steps every time regardless of how perfectly I'm running. I had to max to gamma to even be able to see where I'm going I've watched multiple youtube walkthrus that have tried my best to mirror but either this game has a hundreth of a second margin of error or it's broken. Either way I've died 30 times during a walking sim and even watching others do it "correctly" doesn't help. This peaked as a 6/10 experience but then frustrated me into oblivion. Would rather fling myself into the sun that touch "close to the sun" again.

_childDocuments_.review: A rich mogul builds his utopia in a striking early 20th century art and architectural style only to have it fall apart and you explore it soon after that happens.This describes this game, also Bendy and the Ink Machine, but of course it most of all describes Bioshock.This game is VERY Bioshock, but without combat. Hell, it even has the same clashing voiceover character dynamics like Bioshocks Ryan vs Atlas.Does this mean I dislike the game? No it is pretty good. And it's environments are really well done. But it puzzles me why someone would take so many different aspects of another game and just re-create them as a new game. This game adds nothing new to the Bioshock formula, it only removes some aspects to make it into a sometimes walking simulator, sometimes Outlast style horror game.But hey, if you love Art Deco and Art Noveau style design, I'm sure you'll enjoy exploring this world.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure that, if this is what you're looking for, it's great. The setting has enough to it to catch your attention, the visuals live up to what the game is selling, and it controls fine. But this game feels like the main gameplay loop is just... Missing. Like they took the shooting backbone out of a System Shock game and forgot to replace it with anything, I spent nearly 3 hours trying to hang onto the setting's novel ideas, the architecture, the altered history, everything I could to keep the will to keep going, but it just wasn't enough.  For the most part, you are wandering a flashy city ship, "solving puzzles" in the barest sense of the word: walk from point a to point b. Flip a switch to open a door. And there's a smattering of in-universe recordings to listen to, as you move about, hints of noises and danger in the distance. If this game had some sort of structure to hang itself upon, it would be excellent! But the puzzles are basic and rare, the recordings simply not enough, and the danger, in my time playing, never really arrived. Which is why I cannot recommend Close to the Sun to other players.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: This game wants to be Myst and Amnesia at the same time. Instead it's just meh. Good graphics, great sound, yet they clearly did not agree on what they wanted as a finished product. Very bloated, ten chapters yet could have easily been five, or none. Considering the chapters idea just gave bloat, elevators were ALL end chapter areas where you faded to black and waited for the next load. it could be anywhere between half an hour to 15 minutes between areas, why were the elevators not the loading screens for a game of this price? Ten chapters. Story. Ambitious, but poorly executed as a game. Would have been better if . The trouble lies in the lack of cohesive play style. At one end you are peacefully looking around with a feeling of mystery, reading and picking up collectibles. At the other, you have attempts to make horror work, which occasionally reach the mark, not letting you ponder about the world around you and its mysteries. I think it's an issue of pacing, and a feeling of everything being very much put in the same places each time so you start to expect the same thing over and over again. Even the puzzles. Perhaps it's the lack of agency. There always needs to be a fine balance. When you cannot hurt your enemies, there needs to be a real feeling of threat. In Amnesia the collection and management of items to keep yourself alive and sane was part of that, which this game does not have. Or perhaps the lack of urgency, sure, something is happening on this ship that is dire, but what and why and how long you have is never really apparent, or seems to directly affect you in a meaningful way. Perhaps if there had been a mechanic that had made you feel that thrill, the urgency, it would be a better horror game. In short, this game is lacking in fun. Beautiful as it is, there is no real... soul. The love of people working together to create something cohesive that sings to you when you play, it's not there. Indeed, there are some beautiful parts, but they don't come together to create something that works, a jigsaw made from pieces that don't quite fit. However, I would keep an eye on this team, because I think with time and more experience, they will be able to create a masterpiece more worthy of their skills.

I just got it on sale for $8 (?) and it is worth that. 2) The game takes up an incredible amount of GPU and overall processing usage for a game that is literally a walking sim (I couldn't play it on default setting and stream it, yet a game like Fall Out New Vegas gives me zero problems (and yes my specs are capable)). _childDocuments_.review: Apart from the introduction, never felt that engaged. Ridiculous contrivances ('Come and save me, we have so little time! Oooh but first, solve the puzzle in my office and no I won't help you with it') and an absurdly obvious betrayal made it tough to care about the story too much and the main characters seemed strangely disengaged from the horror around them. It's all wrapped up with an unsatisfying cliffhanger. The gameplay itself can be frustrating. I'm easily scared but just found the monsters in this boring and predictable and the multiple chase sections are an absolute bore of trial and error. When mentioning trial and error, the normal environment also falls prey to this as well. You won't be able to get by a small waist-high chain in some areas but then in others the only way forward will be an absurdly small ledge which only becomes visible when you walk up to it and finally an interact button appears - led to some frustrating to and froing at multiple points! I'm usually a big fan of this style and genre of game but found it all sadly lacking. They do make a wonderful evocative atmosphere but it just never feels properly used both for the story and the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: A thoroughly mediocre walking sim that hits every single walking sim trope. It tries very hard to scare you at first, but the game becomes so predictable so quickly that I got bored an hour in and just made myself finish it.It gets to a point where you're walking down a corridor and you can call the incoming events perfectly, "Oh I bet a guy will pop up in that window" and they do. From a technical point of view, the game looks fine but stresses the GPU a lot and I had plenty of unexplained framerate dips  from 120+ down to 30 (I'm guessing those were loading zones). The art direction is also a bit mixed, it's an obvious Bioshock ripoff but I had to crank my gamma way up since some sections become very dark and you have no light source. The main character controls like a tank and the plentiful chase sequences are honestly a chore, you're basically sprinting forward in a straight line and clicking to cross the obstacles once in a while. I was expecting a good story but all I got was the same rehashed stereotypes. It doesn't help that the game completely misses to explain half the story, and with how the ending was presented this was presumably saved for a sequel. Do not buy this at full price (maybe don't buy it at all), I got it on sale and still feel I could've spent my money better.

_childDocuments_.review: Short but very sweet. Bioshock's narrative premise and *gorgeous* art deco opulence married to SOMA's light puzzling and IT'S-BEHIND-YOU-RUUUUUN sprinting terror. Characters are fun to meet but there's little in the way of surprises - most things unfold as you expect them to. Did I say the art was gorgeous? If not, it bears repeating. This is a very pretty game - full credit to the art team for a wonderful creation and some top-tier level creation.I do wish they'd done more with the narrative - it felt like it ended just as possibilities were opening up (setting up themes for a possible sequel?). I mean, why talk about alternate dimensions and time travel if you're not going to do anything interesting with either? And if there's one thing I'd change it's the way you have to angle your camera *just so* to interact with objects which never stops being slightly too fiddly and unintuitive, but it rarely asks you to do this under pressure, so....But moans aside this is a fun, quick, lovingly put-together little adventure that doesn't outstay its welcome. I enjoyed every minute.7.5/10: would ride the lightning again.

One day she sends you a letter, inviting you there.Stepping aboard, you quickly discover not all is as it seems. Character models though, don’t look particularly good.Atmosphere is really well done, it did feel quite scary at times.Gameplay is basically a walking simulator, where you walk around and read some notes and newspapers (interesting notes though), with a few chase sequences here and there.There are some puzzles, if you can even call it that. _childDocuments_.review: I lowered my expectations since the reviews weren't spectacular, and still left disappointed. It's a bland walking sim with a weak, forgettable story wrapped up in an alternate history scifi skin (the one good attribute). Partly my fault for thinking it would be a steampunk horror game (it barely qualifies as having a horror tag), but even without that, the poor writing, story, and overall execution make this a mediocre game.The visual design is incredible and really captures the atmosphere you'd expect for an alternate history Tesla science megacity ghost ship. It's by far the best aspect of the game and the only reason it's worth playing at all.The worst aspect is the woefully underutilized premise of Tesla's floating science haven. You'd expect unusual inventions, technology, and experiments, and there are some on the sidelines, but you never really interact with them in a meaningful way beyond collectible paper scraps or walking by. Much of the game consisted of opening doors and looking for generator codes. The sense of novelty was always in the background as you're given stereotypical tasks you get in other run-of-the-mill horror and adventure games. A stronger story might have salvaged this, but the deus ex machinae and unexplained loose ends (possibly leaving room for a sequel) ensured that didn't happen. Scifi stories with time travel are hard to pull off in a believable and consistent way, and this wasn't one of them.The main character's personality became increasingly annoying throughout the game. She was fine initially until becoming frequently helpless and indignant with hostility channeled mostly in the wrong areas. An ounce of grace or even one apology would have made more sense for the situation at hand. Aubrey was ok but needed to be fleshed out more than a stray note or two. Ada and Tesla also lacked personality and development beyond "quirky genius scientists with ambition". Overall, it was difficult to forge any sort of emotional connection to the characters, so the events of the story largely fell flat and were easily forgotten.The dialogue felt ill-suited for the characters much of the time. They certainly don't have to reflect 1900s norms and accents since it is a game (and an alternate history setting too), but the word usage and constant cursing by a few of the characters sounded very strange for the setting.There are a number of extremely dark areas in the game neighboring reasonably lit ones, and for some reason there's no brightness setting in-game. Stumbling in the dark until you see an icon to interact with something isn't fun.Door codes were always plastered easily within sight and nothing really qualified as a puzzle. Doesn't have to become a puzzle game, but I would have preferred to use my brain for more than admiring the scenery.Reading the positive reviews feels like I didn't even play the same game. If you're not bothered the way I was by the above issues you'll probably enjoy it the way many others have. Clearly this wasn't for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This Game is beautiful...Which is why it pains me to say that it falls short of capturing my interest for more than an Hour of Gameplay...This is one of those Games People will dub as a "Walking Simulator"...Games like "Agony" that have crazy good graphics and perhaps story too but destroy it all by taking the focus away from the main objective by forcing you to do stupid Puzzles.Hiding lore and key elements in letters and Photos that you have to manually read..Things like this are why I've never liked the original Resident Evil Games...Why spend my time looking for that Key to that Door when I could be having way more fun just opening the door to see whats on the other side so that 30 minutes of my time was given from the actual story itself instead of wasting it with puzzles that act as filler content...Games that do a good job of story telling whilst having you complete puzzles would be games like,Portal, Control, Mass Effect, Dishonored, Bio Shock even...Games like this keep the puzzles entertaining for you to complete by making them fun.This Game however, seems a bit misguided and repetitive with its puzzles.I just couldn't even bring myself to get past the 3rd Chapter without wanting to go play something else...The $15 price tag is fair based on Graphics alone, but sadly... Graphics aren't what make a game good...GRAPHICS9/10    (would be 10/10 For RTX Support, but almost doesn't need it as it looks as convincing as RTX)STORY( Cant accurately Judge it as I only played for an Hour, but who knows? Maybe the story could be a redeeming factor here but boring puzzles take away from the story so much that I was unwilling to continue. )SETTINGPerfect... 10/10This game does Steam Punk better than BioShock in my opinion.Highly detailed atmosphere no matter where you are in the Game.Only complaint would be the lack of detail on the Dead people.GAMEPLAY5/10Movement is sluggish kinda like in "Agony" every part of me while playing just wanted to sprint to where I wanted to go (Just as I would if I were in the main character's situation in real life.)Also, just like in "Agony", the Puzzles are just as boring and unoriginal. Having you find KeyCards to access Elevators and Rooms and unlock Safes with Codes to find them...This has been done already in many other games.I'm not saying that you cant do it though.I'm just saying that it isn't fun at this point and when your gameplay focuses on this more then the storytelling itself, that's when your game starts to get watered down.

_childDocuments_.review: Spooky Month may be over, but that doesn’t mean I’ll stop playing horror or spooky games. With that being said, I wanted to replay through  since it’s been a while since I have. It doesn’t hurt to revisit an underrated gem.The year is 1897. Nikola Tesla and Thomas Edison are fighting for technological predominance over the world. But, out on the dark blue ocean, the Helios stands still. Created by Tesla, it is home to the most innovative and remarkable minds of the 19th century. Journalist Rose Archer has received a letter from her sister, Ada, to come aboard the large vessel. However, when she arrives, nobody is around, and the ship appears dead. Everything isn’t as it seems. One single word has been painted at the entrance… QUARANTINE! What happened here, and where is her sister? What unspeakable horrors will she encounter? What's going wrong with time?I know not many people enjoy this game, but honestly, I think it’s a pretty good experience. It is a walking simulator, so there isn’t any combat. Still, there is some puzzle-solving, and exploration is rewarded slightly with collectibles. Overall, the game is pretty linear, so it shouldn’t be too difficult to find said collectibles. Along with this, there are some chase sequences that I found to be pretty intense at times. Everything felt well put together, especially the world, story, and alternate history lore. Graphically, the game is aesthetically pleasing and very mesmerizing. There are aspects of this game that make me think back to the BioShock series; being aboard the Helios reminded me so much of the city Rapture. All in all,  has several different aspects of storytelling I love: time travel, a mystery with elements of horror and jumpscares, and a period piece set in an alternate history.The game is clunky here and there, with moments when the overall experience froze up for a few seconds. Thankfully, I didn’t experience too many issues. But I can’t promise you wouldn’t. Even with this, I would still recommend this game. It’s fun, engaging, and an entirely enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game. Sadly, it just falls a little too short in too many ways.Let's start with some good points: The world it builds up is intriguing and fascinating, with a lot of potential, and the environmental design and graphics fully deliver on its promise. The Helios and its interior is a marvel of beauty and design, and I could (and did) spend hours just walking around, appreciating its many details and awe-inspiring setpieces.Unfortunately, gameplay and story do not have the same level of quality.The game is a walking simulator with horror elements, where dialogue and sightseeing are broken up by puzzles and escape sequences. The puzzles are a little too underwhelming, and the escape sequences are neither fun, nor exciting, nor terrifying, nor in any way satisfying to complete. Movement is sluggish, and anytime you need to vault an obstacle or climb a ladder you need to find the perfect angle or it won't work, and even if it does the animation is choppy and takes ages. Same with opening doors. At least you can jog.The story has an excellent setup, and the quality of the voice acting gave me high expectations. Unfortunately, the actual story never delivers on the potential of its setup and worldbuilding. Rather, everything that is set up over the course of its ten chapter (ca. 4h, probably less) runtime either falls apart towards the end or is left hanging, as apparently the goal of the writers has been to setup a grand finale twist that is only left implied, and not actually part of the game experience. Maybe I'll see if some fanfiction writer has solved this issue for me. Spoiler for details: I hope the developers learned from this experience, and I hope this won't discourage anyone to create more art and games in this kind of steampunk alternate-history space.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a walking simulator with a nicely written, though somewhat predictable, sci-fi story. If you're playing this game, you're probably playing it for the art. The game art has great moments once you turn the brightness up, and the flat design posters are a highlight. Sadly, the game doesn't spend enough time in its best 3D environments. Chapter 8 for example, was beautiful. But you spend most of the chapters in generic service tunnels or laboratory backrooms. The art book states they wanted more of the Chapter 8 aesthetic in the game. It's a shame that was cut back.The set dressing is also a bit over the top sometimes. Not everything would be an absolute mess. Why are there wood palettes everywhere? It doesn't make sense and it would be nice to have more contrast between the areas where chaos has occurred and those that show the ship before the event.What about the story? It's good, but it feels incomplete. You very much get the sense that more events - and possibly quite interesting events - will occur after the final chapter. It's not the most satisfying ending.The game itself is fine. It feels like your character moves too slowly. But I guess the game would be over too quickly if you could move faster. There are collectables to find, so you're rewarded for thorough exploration. The game does a good job of directing so you don't need to backtrack if you forget where you're supposed to be going.The voice acting and sound are very high quality. The music is very limited. The art book is lovely. 122 pages of pretty pictures. Sometimes I'd like more text in these art books explaining the process and the influences, but it was still great. If you like the art of the game, just get the book as well.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★☆☆ - 3 of 5 StarsI'll start with the good. It's an interesting story mixed with real historical figures like Tesla, and a creepy horror game rolled all into one. I'm an extremely thorough player, and it took me 13 hours of playing to finish this game and 100% the achievements. I like that there's a female protagonist and that it's about the relationship of two sisters. The environments were also incredible, and I seriously felt like I was back in Rapture, playing BioShock 1 all over again. It reminded me SO much of BioShock, I kept forgetting I was on a boat and not under the sea.The bad: OMG, the CHASE sequences. I hated them SO much, I dreaded having to do them. Instead of being scared, I was annoyed - the hit boxes made it impossible to jump over obstacles and I was killed repeatedly for the game's crappy mechanics. The most annoying one was in chapter 7, where you don't know where to go to avoid the thing that kills you, and when you die (which takes many seconds that feel like minutes), a lot of times it will start you right back up getting hit by the thing that kills you again, before you can even MOVE. If the hit boxes were better and I was given more guidance for where to hide/not killed the instant I revived, I might have been scared by the chase scenes. As it is, I definitely don't ever want to have to repeat those, so will never replay.I also was able to guess the big twist, but I'm not sure if that's because it was easy to guess or I've just watched too many horror movies. lolThe ending is a setup for a 2nd game, so expect that going in. There are a lot of questions left unanswered. If there is a second game, I would consider playing to find out more about Ada's research, but I would definitely get it on sale after the chase scenes in this. I still recommend it, though, for anyone who loves BioShock, a good mystery, science or exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: Close to the sun is a story about a woman who was sent a letter by her sister to come visit her, only to discover everyone aboard the ship has been killed. Only you and a few other are the only one left alive.The story is quite interesting, it’s about Tesla’s inventions to generate free electricity with his massive ships for the world. The ship is occupied by some of the worlds most famous scientist and engineers. The game play is rather simple, as it’s more of a walking simulator type game with a few chase scenes. You have no weapons and no stealth but there really isn’t any danger outside of the chases that happen.There’s some light puzzles that shouldn’t stump anyone for too long and some collectibles that also help tell the story.The graphics and voice acting were very good but I did have a few issue with the game as I played.1. Stutters and freezes were really bad, sometimes locking up the game for 10 seconds mid play before things went back to normal. These repeated frequently all through the game.2. The graphics setting’s refused to save and reset every single chapter and every time you restarted the game.3. Low voice volume despite being turned up to 10 in the game options. The voices would be fine interacting with other npc’s but when she talked to herself the volume was half of what it should be.These issues were on a steam deck and may not be an issue one a windows pc but they are there and I tried 3 proton versions including GE hoping to fix any of those 3 issues.Despite these issues I would still recommend playing this game as it was still really good just annoying having to deal with those issues. 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: People should stop comparing it to Bioshock becasue Close to the Sun is TOTALLY different. I would say that the world setting is more Dishonored-like.Close to the Sun is a jump-scare horror walking simulator with a A+ story behind it.Main (not going to spoil) and side story (Nikola Tesla and Thomas Edison making each other life terrible) are amazing. The little story lines you encounter are a nice bonus (basically reading/using keys from the hidden objects)✔ stunning world (ship) setting✔ great details✔ great soundtrack✔ exploring everything like it should✔ save points✔ jump-scares✔ the story✔ puzzles are not that hard (this is a walking sim)✔ around 7 hours playtime. Perfect.✔ 15sec intro and then you are dropped straight into the game✘ main character voice is horrible when she is talking to herself✘ main character finds it annoyingly normal to see dozens of chopped off bodies and acts too much with 'not a big deal' besides a 20sec interaction with her sister on how to distress✘ this game lacks a run-only button✘ you need to play it on x4 AA or the graphics are screwed because of the ship/furniture movement. Personally not a problem for me but I can imagine many of us can't run the game on a x4 AAProblems:1) No gamma correction2) No keyboard bindings3) FOV not adjustable (causing dizzines)Solutions:1) There is in the setting menu. I don't understand why recent reviews still talk about this. It's literally under 'Gamma'2) Change your keyboard settings to QWERTY/AZERTY if you play with 'the letter' or just use 'the arrows' ony your keyboard.  Another solution is to play with a controller.3) It's indeed not adjustable except written in the discussion forum to alter the in-game setting through a text file, or you can change it with a third party software (personally not recommended). For me I had no issues with the FOV. Perhaps people are talking about they are feeling dizzy because it's a ship, and the camera act as one? (slow lef to slow right; slow right to slow left).Good walking sims are hard to find and this is one of the best out there.If you like walking sims with a scary twist on it then buy it. Don't wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: The Summary:-Close To The Sun is NOT a Bioshock clone, but it kind of tries to be. It is a “walking simulator, plus” with mostly atmosphere and dialog, some simple puzzles, and a few intense action sequences.-If I could give it a thumbs sideways, I would.The Good:-The atmosphere is incredible. If you wish that you could walk around the halls of Rapture with truly modernized graphics, this is a great venue to explore.-There is a lot of great ancillary information and world-building done via posters, newspapers, photographs, and other items you find. There are a few minor details that show that some real thought was put into creating the environment. Ex: at one point early on there is a blinking light that seems like nothing but minor scenery, but actually indicates an environment you will encounter more than half the game later. There are several other clues and omens along the way.The Bad:-Your movement speed is too slow, and while you can “run,” it is little more than a slightly faster walk. You also can “jump,” except it isn’t a jump, just a hop, and serves no actual function in-game.-A LOT of scenery looks like it should be interactive, but isn’t.-Checkpoint style saves, with no ability to go back except to the beginning of each chapter. If you miss a collectible, you have to redo the chapter entirely.-Controls cannot be customized.-There is no gamma adjustment, despite some very dark areas.The Ugly:-The story, which has an absolute ton of promise and amazing world building, ends up falling flat on its face. Many of the concepts and characters that are built up via dialog and findable items, are left open ended. The core science fiction plot is never resolved, only a wistful ten second concluding dialog.My Final Two Cents:-Worth buying if you get it on sale. Worth playing if you want to enjoy a well built and slightly eerie atmosphere. Worth skipping if you expect a great and well concluded story, challenging puzzles, or above average gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty good horror game, though it leans more towards being a walking simulator with some hide-and-seek elements. While I found the game impressive, it is unfortunately quite short. Despite this, I'd love to see a sequel, but after four years, there's still no news. Nonetheless, I can definitely recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Bioshock + Half Life = Close to the Sun. That said, this is a "walking simulator" type game with no combat, but possibly my favourite example of this type of game. The story is brilliant and full of wibbly wobbly timey wimey stuff and the graphics are beautiful to look at. Really hoping for a sequel to continue the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said, it's a walking sim with horror elements, you will spend some time running in chase scenes but most of it is spent exploring the environment. And what an environment to explore! The Helios is *gorgeous*. It shares aesthetic dna with Rapture from Bioshock and Talos I from Prey 2017, and there are times where you just walk into an area and get that wow moment. I would love to have a free-roam camera mode to explore the environments.The story is interesting, it hints at a bigger plot which we unfortunately don't get to see all of, but the voice acting is well done and the sound design helps you enjoy the world.I'm looking forward to seeing what this developer does in the future.

_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A really great game! It's a Horror, Detective, Steampunk, puzzle solving game. I got Bioshock vibes from it. _childDocuments_.review: Wait for a saleThis game has one of most imaginative settings in a horror game I've ever seen, and I truly mean that. Except- it misses the mark on horror SOOO badly and it really hurts to think what this game could have been. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly feels like a walking simulator of Bioshock, great atmosphere, predictable yet interesting story, collectibles scattered about to help enjoy more of the areas and great atmosphere, and the game is not as horror themed as the pictures would lead you to believe (not really a pos or neg but worth mentioning) Overall a solid 7/10

_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable romp through a fantastical adventure based around Nicola Tesla.  Featuring a beautiful Art Nouveau set, great audio and excellent quality voice overs, unravel the story through the dialog of Rose, the character you play, and Ada her missing sister and the various characters and information you find along the way.  Solve some puzzles to progress, none of which are particularly challenging, and escape some situations which involves fleeing and may take several attempts, as the available paths are initially unfamiliar.  Great title track from Porcelain Pill too.  Recommended, it's a quality production and I enjoyed my time in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

I found myself just stopping and looking around at the environments more than anything.I probably should have taken more screenshots of some of the interior suite rooms. They were replete with detail.Voice acting is pretty spot on. Sound and music are good and set the atmosphere. _childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: As a ultra-fan of Bioshock, I was recommended this game by a friend that knew I was into the series. I noticed the art inspiration immediately, and the plot similarities came with time. Personally, this is a plus for me - it made me love the game even more. It didn't seem like the developers were 'copying' Bioshock, more just taking a bit of inspiration, and they still made this game their own. I enjoyed playing, and the voice acting was A+. Would definately recommend to fans of games like Dishonored, Bioshock, etc. I'd love to see a full-length game out of these guys.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A walking simulator with great aspect imitating bioshock art style, but boring. To be a good walking simulator you must have a good story, and this game apparently does. But guess what... that good story is not actually in this game, just a promise of giving the player that in the next game. All we have here is a teaser about a time looping story that we never get to see. It also has too ez puzzlez,  tedious and unnecessary action parts (escape type), and crawling through vents takes for ever for some stupid reason. So, buy it if you want, but only when is in 70% discount or more and don't say I didn't warned you.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: CLOSE TO THE SUNA absolutely beautiful looking game with a foreboding soundtrack, you play Rose Archer, a journalist looking for her sister Ada aboard the Helios science ship.The graphics are incredible though there are some major frame rate studder, the bodies and characters don't look good at all, its serviceable to the story but that's it.This game is terrifying at first, the couple of levels in the beginning have great jump scares but out of nowhere they stop and no story really explains why certain characters were hiding and slamming doors on you, I feel like this could have been amazing if consistent through the whole game.The story drifts down this odd rabbit hole and many questions don't get answered, I loved the pace of the story and some parts as things went on, things felt like they were missing - example - WTF is Ludwigs problem.. who is this guy thats chasing you..there are also to many cheap deaths.Overall this is a bit of a walking sim with cool effects and overly simple puzzles, a easy game to 100% if you find all the collectibles.I honestly believe if the protagonist had a revolver this would have been amazing, very bioshock feeling but without any gun play, without a way to defend yourself you will find many cut scene moments of running from the ememiesCheck it out for sure, I really enjoyed my experience.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Grade: C+This game is worth playing, especially if you pick it up on sale, but it has some serious flaws:1. Too Dark (in the literal sense). One of the most annoying things was the inability to adjust the brightness. There were sections of the game where I could not see where I was going. I kept walking into walls and missing stairwells/walkways I needed to travel to progress in the game. Even with my PC screen brightness on max, I often could not see anything at all.2. Unnecessary blood/gore. There were enough corpses on the ship to populate a small city (which is weird, because the game sets up the idea that Tesla was very selective/secretive about who gets to be on the ship). After a while, you get so used to the puddles of blood and dead bodies you get annoyed. "Get out of my way, dead body!" I get that it's a horror game, but the deaths have no horror if they're all identical corpses wearing identical clothing. Had we actually learned more about the dead people, it might have made more of an impact to see puddles of blood everywhere.3. Predictable plot twists. . 4. Tedious, linear exploration. There is only one path you can follow to advance the plot, with countless dead ends and fake-outs along the way. How convenient that dead bodies or debris would always, always block the most direct route to your objective? It got to the point where the blockages were so predictable I spotted them instantly and always chose the side route to my destination. I think this game would have benefitted from letting the player have more freedom of movement (I'm thinking of Alien: Isolation here--also a linear game, but it allowed you to move about and explore more). 5. Hotspot hunting. In each area, there are a series of "collectables" you can click on to get an achievement. Yet these things are unnecessary to the story or advancing the game (so I wound up ignoring them, because why meticulously search identical-looking corridors trying to find hotspots on a too-dark screen? I have better ways to waste time). Other than doors/levers and collectibles, there is nothing else to interact with in the environment. 6. Story is okay, but needs some work.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: - A Solid story with a great setting.- Very atmospheric with excellent audio for tension, spookiness and positional effects.- Wow, it is pretty to look at. The lighting is a little dark at times, so you may need to inch up the gamma.- Not much in the way of gameplay, it's certainly more in the walking-sim-style of narrative experience rather than survival-horror, but it's immersive none-the-less. Finding codes, turning valves, some chase sequences (which actually carry the tension well), that's about it.- Reminiscent of Bioshock in tone and theme.I got it on sale which was a bargain, although the quality is definitely there for the asking price.

We are talking about time travel ok, but nearly every situation in the entire game makes no sense, even using time traveling logic. _childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Although I enjoyed the incredible Art Nouvaeu/Deco environments, story, and voice acting, I was annoyed by the lack of a basic save-game feature and FPS adjustor. Since I have limited time to enjoy games, I had to power through these highly detailed and story-rich environments since I couldn't save and continue mid-chapter. Hopefully, the studio will take these issues into account as they develop their next title; I have very high expectations for this studio!
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: I actually enjoyed it!  It played well on my older machine and looked great.  All puzzles and escape scenes were doable for me without a guide, fortunately.  The storyline is interesting enough and I enjoyed the main protagonist's voice acting.Many people are complaining about a lack of manual save feature, but the chapters play in relatively short 20-30 minute episodes and can be paused.  It was really a non-issue for me.There are a LOT of unexplained plot mysteries....more than I'd like to see in a game.  I had to go online and verify there was only one ending (which seems to be the case).  Everything in the game points to a New Game plus mode at least.  . It let me a bit unsatisfied.  This isn't sold as a chapter based game or part of a series....now I'm just left disappointed.That being said, I'm sure the reasoning is for them to create a sequel....it just makes me feel like I'm being forced to purchase a sequel to conclude the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: A great game that took me about 9 hours which included some exploring( I'm very nosey ). The graphics are top notch and the story is well written if a bit confusing at times. No stuttering, no crashes, no problems.Others have moaned about lack of rebinding options which is also one of my pet hates but in this game it doesn't matter. The controls are so simple, just walk or run via wasd and left shift buttons. Any jumping or crawling or squeezing is done automatically via the left mouse button. It is as easy as any walking sim although you will have to run a lot and maybe die from time to time.I say just try it and if its not to your liking just refund.

_childDocuments_.review: How is this game not a bigger deal? I had a hard time believing this was an indie tittle to be honest. While i would have enjoyed some combat, mainly so i can stab a certain gentleman that will not be named, i can honestly say i had fun without it. I'm sad that this was such a small game in run time. It feels like the developers had more to show as story goes. That said it is worth your every cent.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Had a blast. It's mostly a walking simulator, but since it lets you die, the gameplay gets quite intense at times. I enjoyed the story, but man - the art design is simply astonishing. It kinda resembles that Bioshock's fallen utopia atmoshphere, being a mix of an art deco style, monumentalism and a bit of a steampunk vibe. The visuals alone are worth giving it a shot. The soundtrack is great, voce acting nothing short of either, but it lacks that polish of high budget titles. The steering gets clunky at times, and the framerate is all over the place - my regular 45, 50-ish FPS got down to even ~15 few times, but I did NOT expect that to happen during end titles scrolling on a black background (sic). NPC animations in interaction scenes also could be better - you get that hunch that because of this devs probably wanted to limit the amount of encounters in the game, which at times kinda spoils you the general plot direction. But overall the game was a very positive experience for me - positive enough to leave a review, which I rarely do.Oh, and it's pretty gory.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful aesthetics, and great creepy atmosphere. It has a few jump scares and chase events, though the gameplay is pretty average. There are a few collectibles to hunt for, but not really any puzzles to solve. The story is presented in bite sized episodes, and was good enough to hold my interest, but not very long at all. There are 10 chapters and the game took about 5 hours to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Completed Close to the Sun on PS4, as it didn't run very well on my laptop.This is quite long, sorry heh! Tl;Dr at the bottom.Story:Very interesting, and I like that Nikola Tesla is actually a character in the game! I won't say too much, to prevent spoilers if anyone wishes to play this game. I LOVE the concept, and the somewhat reality that surrounds it.Music:Fantastic! I love the song at the end, which is also in the main menu. The lyrics are quite poignant, and tug at your heart strings once you've gained an understanding of the story; particularly the last scene, as the credits start to roll.Gameplay:The gameplay is somewhat basic, but the game focuses more on being a mystery solving game. It was also very much a walking simulator, but not a *bad* one, as such. I do feel like there could have been less running scenes, though.I like that there's collectables, which if you don't acquire first time round, you can go back and get them by either replaying the whole game, or replaying the chapters from the main menu. These collectables, however, were somewhat lacking. It would have been awesome to be able to explore every area of the ship at will, and find trinkets, people, or useful items. This is a nice incentive to get players to play the game again!I was a little disappointed with the back-story aspect of this game, however. The notes and newspapers, despite mentioning some VERY famous scientific minds that had boarded the ship over time, could have had the focus shifted to them from time to time. Instead, this focus was always brought back to Tesla (to be fair, it was his ship!). It would have been nice to learn more about the Helios, its history, and its residents.Design:This game is absolutely STUNNING! I'm a bit of an addict when it comes to playing Steampunk games, but this one was GORGEOUS! It's veeeeeery similar to BioShock's underwater city of Rapture. This was definitely apparent throughout the whole game, but Close to the Sun was still very much its own game, and design. Hats off to the Storm In A Teacup team! Price:The price of this game really does reflect the price-tag. I didn't actually mind paying £25 for it, as most PlayStation games are more expensive than this as it is.Verdict:Gameplay wise, this game could have been richer, and more dynamic. Rose, the protagonist, is not supposed to be there, and I would have hoped that the gameplay would have included this in some way; perhaps stealth mechanics? "Play your own way"? Importance of choice, with differing endings depending on your actions?Overall, I'd rate this game a 8/10, or 4/5 stars. It was immersive, with a beautiful environment (which I wish I could have seen more of!), and an intriguing story. I hope to see a sequel of some kind, in the future!Tl;Dr?Great game, give it a go instead of reading reviews and enjoy the game for what it is. It's not BioShock, it's a steampunk game. All games will look similar. I feel nostalgic already!
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: Overall good game with an interesting story and nice visuals. Some spoilers in this review.All of the bad stuff:* Interact prompts have way too small of an activation area, which results in interactions consisting 90% of trying to position the camera in a way for the prompt to actually work.* The QTE-like chase scenes are almost always just a bit too tight to really be enjoyable. The unskippable, long death animations get tedious really fast, and the character stares blankly at their chasers for too long.* The time-ghosts regurlarly drop fps from 60 to 17 if you're standing closer than a meter to them. This does not seem intentional and breaks immersion.* Some parts of the story are way too railroady, only enabling certain prompts after a piece of ingame dialogue has been heard, which, combined with the very irregular autosaves can mean you need to repeat most of an entire chapter if youhad to quit for some reason before.* The main character's survival instincts, lack of a sense of self-preservation, and lack of tool-use greatly annoyed me throughout the game. Most, if not all major fights with Ludwig would've been avoidable if Rose had a pipe.* Aubrey's retreat animation in the tower he's locked himself in is just plain hilarious. He is stuck in the waving animation, and is just sliding backwards into darkness in order to escape the player's field of view.
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: OK, I hate not having the option to redefine keys but I like the game so...The setting is a ship that is so big it makes Putin's mansion look like a garden shed, it has it's own internal rail system for example. The Art Nouveau / Steampunk setting is amazing in it's size and detail, it sets a good atmosphere.Voice acting is good. There is the occasional jump-scare here and there.As a walking sim it is excellent, it has a strong storyline. The only action gameplay is in occasional sections that you have to run through to avoid being killed by the chaser, they're not difficult. There are no QTEs yet (half-way through). If you like walking sims, horror, attention to detail then you should love this game.ps they must be a lot of extremely ugly people on this ship, there isn't a mirror anywhere,
_childDocuments_.name: Close to the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: :For starters I have been looking forward to playing this game for quite some time, ever since I saw that trailer with the amazing soundtrack I was excited. Yesterday I saw it on sale and decided to buy it. Problem is that most games I buy I just play for an hour or so and then stop. But this game hooked me for some reason and wich might also have to do with the obvious inspiration the developers took from the bioshock series ( which I am also a big fan of ).:The gameplay itself is pretty standard. A lot of running around, searching for clues and notes. I am not a big fan of the "running away from the bad guys" sections. The movement is way too janky and slow for that, I even got killed one time in a case where I was just running straight because the character is just so darn slow. Also the game does not always do what you tell it to. I have died a couple of times in those chase scenes because the game just wouldnt let me jump over an obstacle. Which brings me to the animations, especially the ones where you die. They are just way too long, they don't even look good and are just annoying.:The game has some amazing enviroments like the theater or the great hall which are just beautiful to look at and immerse yourself in. The graphics in general are a huge plus point for the game in my opinion, everything from the plants to the lighting just looks gorgeous most of the time ( FOR INDIE STANDARDS mind you, don't expect Uncharted 4 ):Dissapointing at least. Nothing special at all and the few plot twists the game has you see coming a mile away. That being said I like the voice acting of most characters and their conversations. Especially the ones between Aubrey and the main chracter are pretty funny sometimes in my opinion.:It's an overall good game with nice visuals. Not something I'd pay 20 bucks for tho, also because it is a fairly short experience with me taking around 5 hours to beat it ( And that is if you are really trying to find notes and all that ). Wait until it's on sale and for half the price it is definetly worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had known this game was this good, I would have bought it months ago.  It's absolutely gorgeous and the Bioshock parallels are really strong even down to major story beats.  Even the setting of 'brilliant mind creates unrestricted utopia for geniuses to thrive in and oh wait it seems everyone is dead now' that is prevalent in Bioshock.   The comparisons are unavoidable but ultimately, irrelevant.  There's no combat here but this is so much more than the now-slanderous 'walking simulator' term I've seen connected to it.  Anyone that thinks this is a walking sim has clearly never played Dear Esther. The game gets some grief for the chase sections but I personally liked them.  But the problem with the chase sections in this game is the same problem with chase sections in any game: you always feel like an idiot once you figure out where you're supposed to go.  That is unavoidable but that generally leaves a bad taste in the mouth of a gamer.   With a half dozen or so such sequences in this game, it's nothing to get too worked up over but those didn't always stick the landing.  The voice acting work is really impressive though, Rose is one of the best I ever heard.  At half price this game is a steal but to the right person and/or screenshot aficionados, even full price could be worth it.  This feels like a game that was released just before the devs created something really really great.  Also can I please have this in VR?  I'd pay $50 for that dlc.

_childDocuments_.review: Close to the Sun is a well done Sci-fi story with horror elements sprinkled in to give some great flavor. The alternate history about Nikolai Tesla and progressing the future through science and innovation aboard the Helios was fantastic. I do not want to give away the plot, but it is decent. It can be predicted, but the way it is portrayed pulls you very well. You feel for the characters as their story is told and the voice acting was also well done. The level designs on the Helios were well done and the game was way better looking than I thought it would be (thank you Unreal 4). The added puzzles were a nice break up from all the traversing. They are not overly complicated, but make you think. Also finding all of the collectibles was fun too with how nice the levels look and feel. The horror aspect bodes well for the story, and adds that creepy ambiance. But this is not a horror game in the aspect of Resident Evils and others. It is secondary, but welcomed and done well. I also enjoyed the chase sequences for the most part. You can beat this within 4 hours, but do not. Take in the Helios and the story.With all of that said I have 2 negatives that did affect me. When chapter 3 started, I started to get low frames and shuttering. I am not sure why. So i lowered the settings and restarted. That made it WORSE. So i put them up to max and restarted again. It got better, but for some reason it never fully went away. It did not make the game unplayable, but really hurt me in the chase sequences. Speaking of chase sequences, i did enjoy them but one thing needs to be changed to make them better. Whenever you get caught (you will, trust me) the death sequence is drawn out and NOT SKIPPABLE. With the way the levels are designed during the chase sequences, it is very easy to make a wrong turn and get trapped. Not a big deal, but the death sequence is soooo long and unnecessary after you get caught once. During some of the chases when i would re-spawn, my frames would drop and I would get caught instantly... Like i said not a big deal, but frustrating. Those are my only 2 negatives. My computer could be at fault for the frames, but the drawn out deaths in the chases was annoying.With all that said, Close to the Sun is a fantastic walking simulator? with a fantastic story, level design, gorgeous and fun mechanics. Recommended to anyone who likes story driven, horror aspects, sci-fi, walking simulators, puzzle games and well rounded game play. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10Good game overall with an impressive visual presentation and style (there's still not enough art-deco Bioshockey visual style things in the world), well voiced and good sounds. However for me the story, atmosphere and intrigue begin to falter once you the main plot arc is revealed and the characters potential leanings become somewhat predictable.For it's presentation and setting, you'd be forgiven for expecting more from such a game with such aesthetics, especially with it's focus on narrative and lite puzzles and less mechanics to manage, but it really ends up being just a good, slightly more involved, walking simulator; one of the better ones though.The Good• The environment visuals, lighting and setting are nice with a strong Bioshockesque art-deco period setting.• Sounds and voices are well performed and executed.• A generous auto-saving system that largely prevents frustration which is important for a game with no manual saving.• An intriguing setting and curious character motivations from the outset.• It plays well overall and doesn't overstay it's welcome (especially if you aren't achievement hunting even taking the collectible hunt into account).The Bad• There are so performance drops on the pc despite running on an RTX 2080 in 1440p with 32GB ram and an octo-core AMD and playing on a SSD.• Story falls flat and becomes cliché once the main arc is revealed.• Most of the collectables don't add much to the story and hunting them can be frustrating potentially due to the lack of manual saving.• A disappointing, lack of impact and potentially unfinished feeling ending.The Ugly• Somewhat wasted setting considering the lack of gameplay mechanic depth.• Relies on the gone the wrong way, insta-death, try again loop on occasion which kills the fear factor especially when death & cut scenes cannot be skipped (PS there's an achievement for completing this game without dying).• Sometimes reloading a chapter in order to go back and retrieve a missed collectible for instance resulted in needing to close the entire game and reload due to the game hanging in a black screen (however pressing the stop game via steam client closed it without problem).

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game. The visuals are great, the story is intriguing, and the scares actually got me a few times. I honestly don't know what the negative reviews about the checkpoints/autosaves are talking about. I had NO issues with the checkpoints/autosaves as they literally brought me back right into the fray. My only issue with the game is that it needs more optimization as I can run DOOM Eternal just fine with more going on than this game. My overall conclusion? For $20 this game was well worth the purchase and was an enjoyable experience. Don't let yourself miss out because this game is a good one. -P.S. the level designers deserve a raise because the amount of detail in each chapter was phenomenal and in the big areas like the theater and dining hall I spent a good amount of time just looking around observing and appreciating the finer details of each setting.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give a thumb in the middle, I would, but I can't, so I shan't...Anyways do you like walking simulators? How about Bioshock? And maybe chase scenes that only have one correct path to follow, otherwise you will see an overlong death sequence you cannot skip?... Well.. 2 outta 3 ain*t bad, I guess.I like the artwork of this game a lot. It might be heavily inspired by Bioshock, but it brings a twist to it on occasion. I do enjoy the story, even though despite the subject matter very few will be actually surprised by the way things turn out. I think the worldbuilding is fantastic at times, from the collectibles you find to the posters on the wall and so on.However, those chase sequences, even if there are "only" about 5-6 in the game, can take a hike. I don't understand how they thought those would be fun. Even though there is only ever one correct path, at least they are short though. So that's something. TL:DR decent horror-y Bioshock-y walking simulator with some sequences that shouldn't be in there in this form, 6 or 7 outta 10. If you like the things mentioned above, get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Keeping it simple:Do I recommend it?: yesDesign: 9/10Sound Design: 7/10Creativity: 9.5/10Story: 8/10Performance: 4/10Playtime: +/- 5h (not on 100% completion)Replayable?: likely not, maybe onceMy rating: 8/10I really like this sorf of game and I'd say anybody that is interested in a mix between historic content and dystopian fantasy, wrapped around a story driven narrative would enjoy this game. I think that the sale price was very suited for the game but it is also worth it's full price for people that enjoy these kinds of games.Mild Spoiler Warning:I loved the historical context, the real-life parallels and the design idea of the game when I first saw it on steam. I got it on sale for 14.99 Euro and I think that it is well worth that money. I had actually never heard of it prior but I was pleasently surprised. The Graphics and the design of the Helios are absolutely stunning however the humans look kind of badly designed, which might be to them not appearing up close at all and rarely even being on screen at all. The Game hat several moments in each chapter where I walked through a door and I presume the new area was loading its graphics and my game just froze for a solid 10-15 seconds. That unfortunately also happened in chasing scenes where I was often caught by the enemy due to not being able to navigate the halls with 5-15 fps. Other than that the performance was okay and ran at a solid 50+ fps most of the time (running on a GTX 1060 6GB). I really like this sorf of game and I'd say anybody that is interested in a mix between historic content and dystopian fantasy, wrapped around a story driven narrative would enjoy this game. _childDocuments_.review: This game justifies its existence only as a demonstration of extraordinary graphics. Everything else's just all over the place. For instance:- Character movement is very basic. You cannot crouch, you can jump but it serves no purpose. You press M1 or space to interact with the World an that's it.- The inventory system is there but very scarcely utilized. At the beginning you can collect key cards to various rooms, but after that the inventory is pretty much forgotten.- The collectibles and various notes are interesting, but there's no journal or notebook to collect them or view them afterwards. The only purpose they serve is to unlock achievements.- The horror element is there, but not fully fledged. The tension is built up, and the atmosphere is pleasantly unnerving, but since there are no conventional horror mechanics such as hiding, the only thing you can do is to run through scripted corridors to "narrowly" escape danger to continue the story. When I figured out that is all there was, the game lost all of it's scariness and became just boring.- The story begun as very interesting and well built up, but it literally lead to nothing. The huge plot convenience this game uses is time travel of sorts, none of which is explained. What was the deal with the exotic energy? Who was that Ludvig guy and what was he on about? Who was the guy sending me the nameless messages? So many questions, so little answers, which made the game feel extremely rushed.- Finally, the characters started strong, only to be neglected later. Aubrey was the only complete and interesting character, while  So in conclusion, the game started strong, ran out of steam mid-way through and then just kinda ended. Although the visuals were amazing (was that actual ray tracing or just really well done lighting?) I cannot recommend it due to the obvious lack of content, replayability and comprehend story. There's just better options for the same amount of dosh.EDIT: some typos and better choices of words.

_childDocuments_.review: a quick review:-The game is quite short, took me around 4 hours to finish it (did some exploring but missed some collectables). -This game's locations are designed beautifully, most ppl should find good motives for screenshots.-The story was not bad and it had some twists in it, too (although one of them was quite predictable) but it doesn't excell story behemoths like the bioshok universe.-Bioshock definitively delivered some inspirations but only artwise.-The gameplay consists of mostly of walking, looking for some collectibles, sometimes collecting keyitems to proceed, some chase scenes, some small riddles and very few hiding scenes. Basically this game lives from its narration, the gameplay itself can feel a bit shallow if you're expecting something like Bioshock or a horror game.-The story is being told by lots of dialogues and the voice acting wasn't bad. Not AAA-material but it was good, nevertheless.Also you'll find some letters that give you a glimpse on what happened, too.-The animations were okay but overall they felt stiff. -"Jumping" is basically useless, because you can jump only a few cm/inches high and there's nothing to jump over. If you need to jump or climb over an obstacle you'll see an icont for it and you just have to either click it in the correct angle or proceed towards ledges to cross them.I think this game could've used more interactions with enemies. Just running doesn't really cut it for me. In certain areas there would've been alot potential to introduce some proper hiding like we had to do in "Amnesia" or even better: "Alien: Isolation".This would've also greatly improved the horror in this game. In its current state the horror is mostly deliver by abundandly placed corpes and severed limps + guts. The devs definitively have the skills for that. They've shown that by creating moody areas and placing nice lighting effects etc. Even the sounds in certain areas were really good and triggered my "HIDE" instincts.I did enjoy this game, despite its somewhat shallow gameplay. The atmosphere and the story kept me entertained and prevented me from going to bed early tonight.The short playtime may be something that some people might perceive as a dealbreaker, though.If you're okay with that, you should give this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review:
It’s 1897. Deep in international waters, the Helios stands still. Dark clouds loom overhead as unforgiving waves crash against the hull. Colossal effigies of gold, decorated with magnificent finery, stretch as far as the eye can see.

Born of Nikola Tesla’s vision, the Helios serves as a haven for the greatest scientific minds. An unbound utopia for research, independent from state and isolated from the gaze of society. Free to push the boundaries of matter and time.

Journalist Rose Archer steps aboard the Helios in search of her sister Ada. She quickly discovers not all is as it seems. Grand halls stand empty. The stench of rotting flesh lingers in the air. Silence. A single word is painted across the entrance… QUARANTINE!

name: Omno
detailed_description: Omno whisks you away on a journey of discovery through an ancient world of wonders. It’s a single-player adventure full of puzzles, secrets, and obstacles to overcome. The power of a lost civilisation will carry you on an epic quest through lush forests, sun-blasted deserts, and frozen tundras - even to the clouds. On your way, you’ll discover a vibrant world full of strange and wonderful lifeforms, from cute little critters to enigmatic giants, and everything in between. Jonas Manke, solo developer and father of 3, began work on Omno as a hobby project 5 years ago after working as an animator in both games and movies.

short_description: A single-player journey of discovery through an ancient world of wonders, created by solo developer Jonas Manke.

_childDocuments_.review: Omno is a single player, third person, exploration and puzzle adventure.As a staff bearer it is your duty to discover and retrace your ancestors’ footsteps. Travel through an ancient world filled with creatures who respond to your command and release a life force you can harness and power. Collect enough resources to carry on your journey, along the way learning more about the past and the lost civilization which lays broken before you. Omno is beautiful to behold. You can tell the solo developer has experience in animation. The creatures’ movements are very believable and full of charm. There are lots of weird and wonderful creations to meet. My favorites were the larger animals and the legendary beasts. I particularly enjoyed riding them at the end of chapters. It had an almost a Disneyesque like quality and feeling, watching those majestic beasts travel through the landscapes and hearing the captivating soundtrack. The environments are incredibly vibrant with a rich vein of color throughout. They’re not particularly detailed but somehow it looks great, and certainly fulfills all the requirements needed.The music is sublime and soars on waves of angelic splendor. The soundtrack throughout the game is extremely pleasant and relaxing.The combination of the two make it a thoroughly enjoyable experience, much akin to  in both structure and feel.The puzzle elements are a mixed bag.I think they have kept some relatively simple so that progress can be made by all ages. You are not required to complete all the puzzles to continue the journey, but you will be missing out if you don’t attempt them. Most of the time spent in game was trying to complete the harder puzzles. Some of them were quite imaginative and had me thinking they were impossible to complete. There is always a solution however and there were some eureka moments which felt satisfying.Puzzle solutions are nothing new and contain many features already seen in lots of other games of this type. They can feel a little repetitive sometimes. The powers you possess added spice to proceedings. I sort of wish they were all introduced earlier on rather than handed out in stages though!The story is typically ambiguous with room for interpretation, but I found it a little more interesting than some games of this genre. Obviously, the amount of lore you find in the game will determine how much of an overall picture you will receive, and some of those information cubes are difficult to locate so you could miss out. Please note there is only one save slot and for some absolutely bizarre reason you won’t be able to continue your game after completion. There are chapter selections but once you start a chapter it will write over your progress, completely negating all animals discovered, puzzles solved and lore collected. The only advantage being you can skip levels. If like me, on your first run through, you miss one animal, then you will have to play through the whole game again. Crazy!Omno has ten playable areas, within five chapters, which have their own distinctive feel. Expect to walk through forests, deserts, icy tundra, and the clouds, on your quest to find the truth about your lost civilization. To continue your journey, you need to collect at least three power globes which will activate the gateway to the next destination. Once activated, a trial ensues, and if completed, you will be led to the next area. The trial usually involves a memory game, jumping on platforms to light them in a certain sequence; Other times you may have to use your special skills to navigate an assault course of sorts.As a staff bearer you are a spiritual being and have a close connection to nature and the world around you. The creatures that roam the lands, respond to your presence and will drop essence for you. This power can be used to activate ancient machinery, used for puzzles, or collect a power globe.There are five power globes to collect in each level, four of which will need thought and precision.There are also information cubes scattered around the area which will reveal details of your ancestor’s thoughts and struggles when carrying out the same pilgrimage.Praying at a shrine will reveal the location of the power globes in a crude map, but will not reveal the location of the information cubes or the animals.There are forty-one animals to encounter from large dinosaur like looking creatures to ones that are small and nimble. After the end of each chapter, you will ride a legendary beast to the next area. As you progress through each chapter, you will acquire a new power. Eventually you will be able to ski, teleport, burst jump and float. As each power is introduced, the level will concentrate its puzzles on that power and any power received before. This makes later levels more difficult and more interesting as all powers need to be used in conjunction to solve puzzles.The puzzles vary in difficulty. It is usually quite straightforward to get the minimum of three globes needed to progress. One of these just requires you collecting enough energy to release the orb. Others might need creative platforming skills, finding hidden paths, or navigating a tricky route.New mechanics are introduced regularly including switches to move objects around; strategically pushing cubes to reach new areas; activating machinery to reveal new platforms or starting timed events; using wind drafts to soar into the air; hitting energy bursts that lift you and using trampolines.The environments are quite beautiful, with some lovely palettes of color. Levels aren’t very detailed but are charming. The main character shows some emotion, especially with his companion and pet, and moves around realistically, either on foot, on his skis or floating in the air.The creatures are very cute and the legendary creatures are awesome and very well drawn and animated. The sound is absolutely gorgeous with orchestral movements and haunting choral voices.This is particularly evident in the legendary beast scenes but the music is superb throughout the game.
