_childDocuments_.review: Take a journey across an ancient world filled with friendly creatures as you discover what is truly important to you.  is visually stunning with its gorgeous art style, has an inventive approach to introducing game mechanics seamlessly, and has a relaxing soundtrack that accompanies the game-play perfectly. Chapters (five in total) are tied to distinct biomes separated into multiple levels. Interacting with the creatures that roam the lands will drop energy orbs that are needed to activate ancient machinery used for puzzles or to collect a power globe. Each level requires you to complete simple puzzles/platforming sections and collect three power globes to access the next area. Additional towers to power up and log files to collect are scattered throughout the levels. Game can be completed between 3 to 7 hours depending on your play style.  If your looking for an easy, relaxing, and peaceful game with no combat than look no further. Everyone should experience  for its stunning vistas and creative creatures that you befriend on your journey. Impressive that only one person developed such an ambitious game. [10/10]

_childDocuments_.review: Omno is an amazing and heart-warming journey through fantastic landscapes populated by magical creatures. The original sound track sets a mood of wonder and discovery.You control a small lovable character who, with his flying furry friend, traverses 15 areas (split into 5 chapters) in search of answers. There is no dialog and the backstory is partially revealed through glyphs/books you find along the way. You gain abilities as you progress... dashing, floating, 'skiing' (riding your staff at high speed), and teleporting.  In each area there are new creatures, glyphs, and light spheres to find. Your progress in each area is tracked (0 to 100%). The areas become increasingly difficult as you combine your skills to reach seemingly impossible places to retrieve items. There are a handful of 'fun with animals' achievements that can be missed. All other achievements are earned by remaining  in each area until you have reached 100% for that area. The game alerts you as to your progress prior to exiting an area so you will not be caught by surprise. Once you leave an area, you can only return to it through a 'Chapter' menu which resets the areas within that Chapter. Thus, if you are going for all achievements, you are better served by staying in an area until you have unlocked all its secrets.The game is quite generous with auto-saves and the penalty for dying (from missing a jump and falling into the void) is a quick re-spawn to your most recent save point. Usually, this means almost no rework required. I did pay attention to the location of save points before abandoning a puzzle halfway through. Some of the harder sequences have save points along the way which was much appreciated.Puzzles are focused on figuring out how to reach an object of interest. These may be located high above you, across vast chasms, or on islands in the sky. Travel becomes an exercise in choreography... knowing when to jump, glide, float, or teleport in perfect timing as gates open and close. Clouds of insects, flocks of birds, and updrafts assist you along the way. In between chapters, there are fabulous cut scenes as you ride a magical creature to the next part of your adventure. For most of the game, I found that a controller gave me better results than the mouse/keyboard.I absolutely loved playing this game and highly recommend it to those who are willing to be patient and work through each area. Be prepared for some very tough sequences (towards the end) that may take some time to figure out and perfect. I was challenged rather than frustrated and the 'WOOHOO!' feeling when I finally completed a sequence made it worth the effort.The final ascent was complicated but I am so glad that I completed the trek. Omno's ending was perfect... I shed a few tears and have only one regret... that the game is now over and I will never be able to play it again 'for the first time!'

_childDocuments_.review: Omno is a game similar to Journey and Abzu, although it’s a little more interactive but relatively equally short.It has linear roads, though, with some open places for you to collect stuff and solve simple puzzles. During your journey you’ll gather powers that help you on your way and speed things up. Collecting 3 cubes will allow you to get to the next area and if you want to explore further there are animal species to log/register, towers to power up and log files to collect.It’s a relaxing game that will take you a few hours to complete and there’s no combat involved. There’s a story but I wouldn’t really call it a story since it’s very basic.Games like Abzu and Journey are still the better games, but that’s also because of the way they control. Controlling the main character feels a little stiff in Omno and it can sometimes make the platforming sections a little harder than they should.Graphically it’s a colorful game with impressive scenes and landscapes but it also goes for a minimalist look. It’s by no means an ugly game.Now, if you’re into these games don’t think about it twice. Yes, the price is a little higher than it should be (€12-13 would be ideal), but it’s a fine journey with a sweet ending. If you’re not into these games at all then this won’t change your mind. In that case I suggest you skip it until it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Omno is an atmospheric exploration based puzzle and platforming game with a sweet story about companionship. You wake up in a swamp, your only possessions are the clothes on your back and a staff, mysterious lands await you. This game does worldbuilding extremely well and creates a good sense of awe as you approach new areas. Music is beautiful, really sets the tone for the journey you are on. Visually it looked 'plasticy', some of the plant life especially reminded me of parts you can find in Lego sets but strangely it works. To complete a level you need to find hidden and just-out-of-reach orbs to unlock new pathways. This can be done by solving puzzles, collecting power with your staff and transferring it or simply climbing and jumping to their location. New abilities are gained as you progress which introduce new challenges for you to traverse the environment.There is no combat but the controls can feel a little awkward and inconsistent. The game is very forgiving with platforming, providing ledge grabs if you’re close and checkpoints are never too far away if you actually miss. It was only towards the end of the game where platforming was asking you to be more precise. Overall it’s a relatively easy and relaxing experience however there are still several occasions that require timing and speed.  There is an optional objective to collect ‘glyphs’ and discover creatures. The latter discouraged me because you can see creatures in the distance of some levels but you cannot actually reach them to discover their names and add to your entries.With about 4 hours of gameplay, Omno doesn’t outstay its welcome and honestly I was left wanting more. It’s very clearly inspired by games like ,  and  with their stunning open levels and grand sequences transitioning between them. Definitely an easy recommendation for anyone who enjoyed those.

_childDocuments_.review: Neutral recommendation.I don't hate the game.  But for the three hours it took to 100%, I don't believe it's worth the full $19.I'm not really going to go over the pros of the game, because I think it's unnecessary;  it's something of a Journey-like - linear exploration game with minor puzzle elements and a focus on environment - and most of the enjoyment can be inferred from just that.  I admit that this exclusion may make the review/critiques seem worse than I intend, and want to reiterate that I don't dislike the game, I did mostly enjoy my time.Playtime and price are irrelevant if the game delivers, but many small details collectively made the experience unsatisfying.The game is segmented into 5 locales, each with several sub-areas to scour for collectibles.  The sub areas themselves are perhaps too small, because they each feel too empty and too short.  The beauty of the game is found mostly in the environment as a whole, because there isn't much to look at in any single area, nothing particularly unique or noteworthy at least.  In addition, it feels like you spend far too little time in any one area.  Each area has a handful of puzzles and collectibles and then it's on to the next.  The rate at which you change areas makes it feel like quality was sacrificed for quantity.  I would have greatly preferred if the areas were more consolidated, but perhaps it was necessary for performance, since I noticed a bit of pop in.Another complaint is the transition between areas.  Neither variation are skippable, but the transitions where you ride a creature first give you a cutscene, after which you have about one second of gameplay to climb onto the creature, after which is effectively more cutscene.  These sequences could use streamlining, especially since the game warns you prior regarding your completion of an area, if a player has progressed to these transitions then there's no need for the option to turn back, just make it a cutscene start to finish (and give the option to skip it).Which leads into a major gripe, in that the game takes control away from the player every chance it gets.  Enter an area?  Collect a thing? Do a thing? Collect  things? Meet a creature?  So many events steal the camera, if not take away control completely.  I don't need to be shown exit just because I opened it.  There's a dedicated map button that shows its location, there's a dedicated section of hud to show if the prerequisites have been met, and each area has over twice of the mandatory collectibles needed to open it.  This, combined with the awkward tank controls for some abilities, just make the whole affair a little frustrating.  If platforming, exploration, and the enjoyment of the environment are the focus of your game, please don't interrupt these things every 30 seconds.Lastly, It is very impressive that this was made by a single developer, even more so as their first game.  I enjoyed my time with it, and do not regret playing it; however, I would not recommend buying this game at full price unless either you wish to support the dev, or have exhausted other similar games like the ones this surely took inspiration from.  For merit alone, wait until on sale.

Set in a mesmerising landscape teeming with life and wonder,  offers players an enchanting experience that seamlessly blends exploration, puzzle-solving, and a hint of nostalgia. Get ready to embark on a tranquil and heartwarming journey that will leave you feeling refreshed and fulfilled.:Visually,  is a pretty despite its minimalist graphical approach that uses low polygons to excellent effect. The handcrafted environments boast a striking combination of colours, unique flora, and magical creatures with enticing ancient civilisation ruins to uncover and explore. The art style exudes a sense of warmth and charm, creating a serene atmosphere that invites players to lose themselves in the beauty of the world. As players traverse the diverse landscapes, they'll uncover hidden secrets, ancient ruins, and delightful puzzles that demand a mix of wit and observation. The game introduces new abilities gradually, allowing for a sense of growth and progression throughout the journey. While the gameplay mechanics are simple and accessible, they mesh seamlessly with the overall atmosphere, making the experience a truly enjoyable and calming one.:The world of  is brought to life through its entrancing soundtrack and immersive sound design. The subtle sounds of nature, accompanied by the chirping of creatures and gentle whispers of the wind, elevate the overall experience and immerse players in the magical realm the game presents.: weaves a minimalist yet compelling narrative that unravels gradually as players explore the world. _childDocuments_.review: From the very first screenshot I saw, I fell in love with the artstyle - low-poly shapes, fantastic creatures, pastel colors and admittedly a bit much bloom lightning. The protagonist carries a staff, which is used for everything - surfing, flying, carrying light - and I really love the animations. The soundtrack is great as well, very calm..The premise of the game is rather simple: You enter an area, unlock the map, and find at least 3 light orbs to open the path to the next area. To 100% complete an area, you need to find all the orbs, interact with all the creatures and find some hidden glyphs as well.The game is divided into several biomes, and each biome unlocks another skill, for example surfing on your staff in the snowy areas. Later puzzles require combining the unlocked skills.The puzzles aren't hard, but they still took me forever, because I suck at platformers. Apparently I took twice the average completionist time. A few puzzles were on a timer; those were my least favorites. Save and respawn points are plenty, so you can just yeet yourself over the edge repeatedly trying to get that jump right.This is in no way a difficult game.Achievements are mostly straightforward, but missable: Complete each area 100%, and in some do a special task like interacting with the creatures in a special way.The story was... I don't know. I really didn't play this for the story. You're on a pilgrimage, following the footsteps of those who went before you, reading the notes they left.It took me 8 hours to finish, half of which I probably spent running in circles and falling off cliffs. There's no real replay value, but I had a fun time.In my experience, this game absolutely deserves to be deck verified; the reason for the badge merely being "playable" is listed as having to manually invoke the keyboard, but I never had to enter text.Despite all my love for it, there's also some negative points:It does feel kinda like an early console game - straightforward, no options, no save slots, nothing. But we're not in the era of early consoles anymore, and I am glad I didn't pay full price for it. The general consensus about time to finish seems to be 3-5 hours, which is one more reason I'd only suggest picking it up in a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Omno is an amazingly impressive feat for a solo developer, but as a game, it's okay. Omno presents a relaxed experience without any fighting; Instead the game play is about exploration and collection. Omno pulls off much of what it tries to accomplish, but the weaknesses are noticeable.The creature design is varied and the individual interactions give them personality and I had a lot of fun finding all the creatures. I also enjoyed the surfing movement which felt really smooth and is a fun way to get around. The pacing feels good, but is quick. I collected everything in maybe two thirds of the areas and I finished in under 4 hours. My biggest hesitation for recommending Omno is that the platforming is finicky. I had quite a few times where the grab animation would start, but my character would slide or fall off the edge anyway. The game is also unforgiving about jumping near edges. In what is otherwise a relaxing game, the platforming was my biggest source of frustration.There are other elements that were a bit of a miss for me, but not a huge deal. There was a story between the main character and his floating green cat/rabbit, but both characters aren't given much personality, so I found myself disinterested in the plot. Another miss is the cut scenes that show off grand landscapes with effusive music, but the feeling was undercut by the simplistic art style. Don't get me wrong, the art style works for most of the game, it just makes the "sweeping vista" shots fall flat for me.Overall, I had fun playing Omno, but I only weakly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, as an overall package I would recommend playing this game.Firstly, I disagree with the negative comments stressing the relatively short playthrough and cost. I will take a shorter well made game full of interactivity and content over a one which is forcefully prolonged into a boring/repetitive walking simulator every day of the year. It took me roughly 4 hours to get to the end.The adventurous atmosphere and overall feel is amazing and the feeling doesn’t go away even later in the playthrough. The story is interesting and fitting, the lore snippets are short enough to read without feeling like you’re reading a book instead of playing a game. You can ignore it and just solve the puzzles but you will miss out.Throughout the game you are gradually given new skills which are then used to get to some area, grab a collectable or solve a puzzle. The puzzles are quite simple but not trivial. You won’t get bored, nor frustrated.The achievements are well designed, evenly scattered and all easily gainable. No hidden ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that you have to search on the internet for.Lastly, from a technical standpoint, it's decent. It runs well, no lag, no issues with (still unusual) resolution 3440x1440 nor high framerates. The setting would benefit from a configurable camera sensitivity but other than that no complaints. It’s playable on both keyboard + mouse and a controller, with real-time switching.. I know it's still fairly new so I wouldn’t mention an occasional crash BUT 2 of these also corrupted my saves which were annoying. _childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. _childDocuments_.review: can be described as a chill and relaxing explore 'n collect game. You're the silent protagonist in a strange and magical world collecting.. . In each level you need to collect enough orbs to continue to the next. I have to mention the controls with gamepad were great. Some of the jumps need absolute precision, it worked great. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR review: The game is exactly what it looks like. A relaxing puzzle platformer to chill out with after playing anything with lots of action. 7/10Review: This game is like a meditation session for me.  Need something to calm your nerves but don’t want a walking sim?  This will do the trick.  Omno gives you pleasant vistas, effusive background music, and easy reloads for accidental deaths.  If you enjoy puzzle platforming, Omno falls in that category of the three little bears analogy.  Nothing too hard, nothing too easy, it’s like permanently set on “just right” for the difficulty.  That’s not to say the game is a bore.  Your basic core game is to explore a new area, meditate for a mini map, get some relaxing fun time with animals, grab their “light” to power up, unlock a magic monument, get a few orbs and on to the next level.  There are harder orbs which require more thought and skill in every level, yet those are optional.  The final difficulty entirely rests in the hands of the player. If you want more challenge, just get some of the harder to reach orbs.You gain some abilities as you progress and it changes up the puzzles and platforming.  My least favorite was the “float” ability, and platforming while floating literally defined the term “floaty platforming” and I died more often there than anywhere else in the game.  Felt like flying a falling paper airplane as I glided through Sonic rings to get to the next platform.Storywise, you gain some insight by finding hidden story bits written by previous explorers.  That bit was very much like a walking sim.  You’ll get a jist of a pilgrimage and lots of text expounding on that idea along with experiences and thoughts.  Well done, nothing major and the story is sort of just there rather than being mysterious.Overall, a quick enjoyable time.  Would I replay it? Nah, it’s a one and done kind of game. However, it was just the trick to relax after playing some other more hectic games. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: A very meditative exploration adventure made by a single dev. To be honest, gameplay-wise it’s nothing new, sure, and you mostly do the same in the around 15 areas (settled in 4 larger biomes), which is, looking for some glowing orbs to power an obelisk, while solving a few very easy puzzles or having to do some light platforming. But I have to admit, in this case, it’s not about what the game does, but HOW it does it. And the result is a kind of peaceful and extremely relaxing journey through a unique-feeling imaginative world. Graphics are fitting in their low-poly way (though this Unreal Engine style is overused a bit lately in my opinion), the melancholic music with its vocals is mesmerizing, the fantasy animals are highly original, and especially the ride sequences are probably its highlight. It’s hard to describe, but I definitely enjoyed it more than I would have initially thought, especially even over the length of the game. Reminded be a bit of titles like The Last Campfire, RiME, Spirit of the North, Lost Ember, Abzu and such, so if you like the slow speed, atmosphere-based gameplay and untertone of those games, you might want to take a look at this one as well. Anyway, nothing more to say from me, so a well-earned positive rating it is.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of good ideas, but not the best at using those ideas. there is a good game in here, but you won't find it until near the end. I don't want to hate this game, as it doesn't do anything awful, it is just very frustrating at points, and thinks it is more pretty and magical then it actually is. the camera control is constantly taken away from you to make you stare at basic polygonal objects, with a score backing it as though the developer is screaming at you "LOOK AT MY WORK!! ISN'T IT FANTASTIC?! LOOK AT MY COOL DRAGON!!!", but that fundamentally takes any magic that could have been found from looking at it on my own, and throws it away to TELL ME that it is magical. this is just 1 of many nitpicks and complaints I have, but I don't want to sit here and rag on this, because by the end it really does start to feel like a fun game. there are good ideas here, for what little they are around. the problem is, you have to get use to a lot of the developer's bad ideas in order to find those, and if this game had not been given to me as a gift, I would have never felt compelled to find said good things. I would have quit an hour in, and asked for my money back. instead, I played to the end of the game, and left it feeling as though I had seen some glimpses of what could be a fun time. I would not recommend this game, especially not for almost 20 dollars (like, seriously? it is a 4 hour game dude.) but I do hesitantly await the next game from this developer, because I really do feel like there's something here, just below the surface. like they have the potential to make something great, if they just learn how to buff out the blemishes on their design, and maybe go back over their earlier levels a few more times. for now though, I would say wait for a sale at least, before you consider picking this game up.

_childDocuments_.review: Waking up utterly alone in a marsh with no recollection on how you got there except a memory of a civilization making a sacred pilgrimage to the golden door that leads to paradise; start your own journey to find your people and see what exactly is behind this door that no one ever returns from. Make an unlikely friend, and find your own definition of utopia. 4+ hours to complete, 5 chapters, one really good ending. An atmospheric adventure game with simple puzzles, the gameplay is pretty smooth; I didn’t experience any errors or bugs. You learn a couple skills to make exploration more fun and gain access to bigger maps, Float, Surf, Teleport, and Navigate. In each area, you need a minimum of 3 “energy sources” to move to the next map, with achievements for getting all of them. A lot of the story is told through “Memory cubes” of a previous pilgrim making the same journey. I enjoyed Omno more than I was initially expecting, the skills were fun to use, especially surf, and the ending was honestly very surprising and I loved it! Omno is an easy game to play and an even easier game to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the good. This game is pretty, has some interesting creature design, and definitely gives off Journey vibes. If you really liked Journey -- who didn't -- and are itching for something similar, then maybe this is for you.Now the bad. And there's a lot of it. First, the prettiness of the game is undermined by its insistence on using a washed-out palette along with excessive lighting effects. The sun is constantly in your eyes. It illuminates the fog all around you in such a way that it feels smothering. I felt like I should've been wearing sunglasses half the time. If you're colour-blind, ♥♥♥♥ you.There are no audio options. Yep. You read that right. This is a game with ZERO audio options. You can't even adjust the volume. What the ♥♥♥♥?The platforming feels bad. It's like the designer never bothered to look at other platforming games to see what they do. For example, "coyote time" -- that brief moment after stepping off a ledge where you can still jump -- is absent. This might seem minor, but there's a reason platforming design has converged on things like this. It's just a good idea. Without it, and similar techniques, platforming feels stiff. And don't get me started on the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ air currents.The camera lags behind the character's movement in many cases. Is this meant to be cinematic? I need to see where I'm going.The puzzle design is... umm. These aren't puzzles. A puzzle needs two things: a goal, and some set of rules that govern what the player can and can't do to achieve that goal. The joy of solving a puzzle comes from understanding and applying its rules. But in Omno, the rules are so utterly trivial that most "puzzles" can be solved by moving things *in the only way they are allowed to move.* There is exactly one interesting puzzle in the game: the rotated "Simon says" one. All others are obvious.There is no reason to explore the environments. At least, I didn't come across anything. It feels sterile.This feels like a long demo. There's an idea for a game here. That's it.

_childDocuments_.review: The "puzzles" are completely trivial and obvious, yet I found applying the solutions to be incredibly frustrating. I persisted for quite a long time, before eventually giving up on the game completely, somewhere close to the end. This is backwards, good puzzle games should be intellectually stimulating and then the solution, once found, should be easy to apply. It shouldn't require dying a hundred times on the same puzzle, just because it requires the player to enter some ridiculously complex sequence of button presses with millisecond timing, or failing because some unnecessarily fast timer ran out; that is just lazy programming, and critically it is no fun at all.I certainly didn't have fun, it just made me frustrated, bored, and angry, and no amount of pretty graphics can make up for that.To be fair, if you have super-fast reactions, lots of patience, and are the sort of player who can 100% Crash Bandicoot with a controller, you will probably love this game.However, if you like relaxing puzzle games, you will regret your purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Omno tells a story about a journeyman seeking the light. In pursut of its kind and promised beauti he has to travel thru different lands and solve a number of puzzles. All while encountering numberous cute looking animals. Story is told thru journal entries found in the various maps. The game doesnt tell if you the Figure or another beeing wrote them. However the play along the same and the emotion reflected in the journey can be interpreted as emotions of the main character. The Story does its fair share of work in order to create an immersive game. But mainly the game is about scenery and discorvery. While wandering the levels you can log Animals in some sort of pokedex. Some animals are used in puzzles others are just there to give life to vabrant world. It cant be said enough but sound, art und design work really well together. I dont wanna spoil the plot but the ending is heartwarming yet leaves some question open. Beeing real even if it played out differently the game would rolled the credits at the exact same moment it did at the actual ending. In terms of problems any of the unwanted sort. They game is pretty polished. Sometimte grapping a ledge und pulling yourself up can cancel or be canceld easily and leave you falling down. Other than that there is no option to adjust the music and sound volume in the game. So prepare to have a louder game only to be handled by your OS Soundsettings. Another good thing worth mentioning is you can aquire all achievements in your first playthrough. If you missed something you can later select the levels you wanna replay. One Thing that may struck you away is the price. I bought in a 75% sale for 4,50 € which is fine considering my 4h playtime. But without sale 18€ is bit much. I know that this game is created by a single dev and he proubly had to pay a lot of stuff for assets and music. But the price is reasonbly a little to much for what you get. I enjoyed the game so it would have played out fine at the end. There are worse game out there for the same price or much more. Still i wouldnt be surprised if the price keeps people away. None the less i d recommend to buy and play this game. Be it in sale to keep an eye on your money or at full price to reward a dev for a great game from my point of view

_childDocuments_.review: You know what would be great? It would be great if satan sidled up to games like Omno, gathered up all the timed puzzles, and brought them to hell where they belong. That way, the proper audience for timed puzzles, such as Mao, Stalin, Hitler, Pol Pot, Lopez, Shipman, and their ilk could suffer them while enduring eternal blistering torment.And then--dream with me--with the timed puzzles gone, the rest of us could enjoy ostensibly 'chill' amusements such as Omno without reservation and frustration. Such fun we would then have. What recreational delights.But for now we're not having fun, because the timed puzzles are still there, so instead we are writing scathing negative reviews just before abandoning another daft game that injects novel misery late in the experience, after which we will buy someone else's game at full price because, while we are getting old and suffer from failing reflexes, we have reached the life stage where we have endless disposable income and can buy any game we want, when we want, but we won't be buying another game from you.

_childDocuments_.review: Starting off the New Year well with this absolutely phenomenal game. I'm very much an "all-genre" kind of gamer, so my review may be different than those made by gamers who stick to mainly one or two genres and don't understand just how wonderful of a game this is; and that's ok! If you are a fan of cute creatures, atmospheric exploration, simple but involved puzzles, and beautiful scenery, then this game very well may be for you!Graphics: This game is absolutely stunning, in a very simplistic way. While this game may not look like Baldur's Gate 3 or COD (in terms of realistic graphics) the game's beauty comes from its unique look. My PC is pretty beefy so running this was no issue, but I imagine even laptop gamers would have an easy time running and appreciating the beauty of this game.Soundtrack: I was a musician for years and very much appreciate a good soundtrack when I hear it. With some games, I find myself reaching to open Spotify in the background because the music is highly repetitive or just plain boring, but I was entrance by the music of this game the whole time. Each area had its own unique sound that was very fitting.Gameplay: This game is very easy, and I mean that in a good way. At no point did I find myself getting frustrated at the puzzles nor did I feel like it was tedious for me to complete them. I also found it very easy to find the different creatures and glyphs so that I didn't miss anything from the storyline. I also appreciated the size of each area. I find that too many exploration games nowadays have maps that are much too big and overwhelming for a lot of the exploration genre fans, and this game does a good job of maintaining the play area while allowing for ample exploration.Controls: I've seen a couple reviews complaining about a lag between pressing space and the character jumping. I have some bad news for those people: it may not be the game that's the issue. Doing the few parkour-esque puzzles in this game proved an easy feat and I found no lag between button and game input. Price: I got this game on sale (as I do most of my games because I'm a broke college student) and I thought it was absolutely worth it. Even without the sale, I think if you are a huge atmospheric exploration/puzzle game fan, then it's worth the money!All in all, this game is very impressive for a first time developer and I'm excited to add them to my list of developers to keep an eye on in the future!Happy Gaming!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely, mostly mellow third person exploration game with eye-pleasing graphics, a wonderful score, and the sort of (generally....) low stress puzzle platforming challenges that one feels a sense of pleasure and accomplishment from completing rather than tooth-grinding frustration.You play some sort of nameless wanderer/explorer who is attempting to gather up particles/spheres of light to open up a pathway to enlightenment followed by other pilgrims before you, exploring ruins to gather spheres of luminous wisdom and tomes of glyphs that act as knowledge repositories, all the while identifying new creatures along the way.Positives:*Graphics*  This could be referred to as low-poly, and you wouldn't be wrong, but some of the models, especially for a few of the larger creatures, do have a bit more detail than that.....call it mid-poly ;-)  Regardless of what niche you stick it in, the game is glorious to behold, full of bright, colourful environments and striking ruins to explore and solve puzzles within.*Gameplay*  As I intimated above, the gameplay loop of exploration and (largely) light puzzle platforming is a sheer pleasure to engage in, and 100%ing each level/biome is not terribly onerous as far as video-game challenges go.  Yeah, there's a few puzzles towards the end that require a bit more manual dexterity and good timing/reflexes, but even a relative clutz like me could succeed after only three or four (or five ;-)  attempts on these harder puzzles, and I NEVER felt frustrated.....I always knew that it was an achievable goal and I just needed a few more tries to get it right.   Also, the checkpointing is fairly generous, so that adds to the lack of frustration even if you plummet to your doom a few times trying to land on a distant block of stone or teleport into the midst of some glowing animals that will blow you upwards for an objective.  Additionally, there are a variety of special movement abilities that you gain as you progress through the game, and they are introduced gradually, and there refinement as puzzle-solving mechanisms is handled in a very even-handed, incremental way that never leaves you feeling overwhelmed by a need for ambidextrous key-board zen mastery.*Music*  On the one hand, it's nothing special (standard sweeping orchestral score) but it really, REALLY suits the game to a tee, and it's a pleasure to hear the sweeping musical accompaniment as you gaze out upon some beauteous vista.Meh:  Some of the puzzles took some trial and error to figure out exactly what I was supposed to accomplish, and how I was supposed to accomplish it.  Again, NEVER frustrating, just a little vague from time to time.Negatives:  None.  Seriously, there's nothing here that ticked a box titled "Annoyances".  It was that much of a joy to play.So, in summary, a visually pleasing, nice sounding, highly enjoyable third person exploration/puzzle platformer game.  Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is compared to Journey by many. Personally I would rather compare it to Fe. With its blend of exploration, puzzles and platforming the game creates a very satisfying gameplay loop. The absence of urgency perfectly fits this games cozy and relaxing soundtrack. Stylized graphics allow Omno's scenery to reach an epic scale while leaving it to your imagination to fill the gaps.The games progression follows a linear structure, introducing new abilities to you in each new area. As these abilities enhance your traversal options, level layouts become bigger and more complex. Movement options always feel accurate and satisfying to use. Interacting with the worlds lifeforms and ancient structures is pure joy. Constantly rewarding you while playing at your own pace. Omno feels like a deliberately handcrafted work of art from start to finish. I am impressed by the thought-provoking premise and refreshingly simple gameplay. My only gripe with Omno is the high price point. I will certainly remember my five hours spent with this game for a long time to come and can't recommend it enough when it is on sale.

The music is soothing, the game is calming and it brings joy, sadness at same time. It is an emotional journey set in a time when creatures walked, when there was peace and unity. Special thanks for making this game to all developers who was part of it. It belongs in my heart to just play through it.

_childDocuments_.review: Omno is a relaxing, cute and short game. It includes pretty views and creatures that you can interact with as well as simple puzzles. There isn't a whole lot to be said about it. There is nothing complicated about this game and it's rather straight forward. There is a level of satisfaction to the game though, especially with the surfing and flying. It also features a nice soundtrack that goes well with the relaxing theme of the game.Personally for this type of game I would give it a 6.5/10. _childDocuments_.review: Omno is stunning visually and has a very pleasing, uplifting soundtrack to go with it. You get to explore the world of Omno by meeting different magical creatures, solving puzzles, and wandering through different biomes. No characters ever speak, yet you get to follow along an interesting and sweet story line told between actions, and information left behind by another traveler. _childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: In Omno, you control a lil guy as you explore and solve puzzles in order to get to the next area in this 5-6 hour adventure. You'll get to see absolutely breathtaking visuals and areas that hark back to a long-lost civilization among a hidden world. The joy of Omno lies in the exploration of each new area in which Jonas Manke has managed to create to such a degree that entices exploration and wonder. It's aided by the really nice, low poly art style that a lot of indie games have. which basically tell you that you'll experience something pretty nice. Movement is really satisfying where you can walk/jog or use your staff as transportation depending on the biome and environment that you are currently in. All in all, Omno is a fascinating and chill game to play for a couple days to engage with your sense of awe.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Why do these kinds of games always insist on having "puzzles" that are just a matter of pushing blocks around in the only possible order until everything is solved?I guess I wouldn't mind as much if the default movement speed wasn't so absurdly slow. But if your character moved at a reasonable clip the game wouldn't last 2 hours. The thing I found really weird / annoying is that you can collect energy from random sources all over the place and when it fills up you get a temporary speed boost. But... you really don't have any control over when this occurs, it's just whenever your energy happens to become full, and there's no way to tell how far along it is, and so a lot of times you get a speed boost when you don't really need to go anywhere. Would've made more sense if you could trigger it yourself. Overall I found it to be beautiful and uninspired. The gameplay is just not on the same level as the atmosphere, and when it comes down to it, gameplay always matters more.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry, but although there were nice graphics and cool puzzles, after the first three areas the puzzles just started getting monotonous, and the constant mini cut-scenes or perspective changes for each small puzzle were giving me motion sickness. Other people may say this is a great game, and it is, but just not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a meh review... I can't really put my finger on what this game is missing here.You are a "light bearer" and you are traveling from area to area picking up bits of story along the way of those who came before you. Unlocking new mechanics for solving puzzles along the way. Each new area has new puzzles and and new environments and new creatures.Here's the good of it though...-The game is absolutely beautiful. It's so damn pretty. I took a ridiculous amount of screen shots of this game. Everything was so damn pretty. The colors, the lighting, the designs of the creatures in the world. It's just so damn pretty.-I mentioned you unlock new mechanics to solve puzzles. There's stuff like floating, surfing, teleporting, etc. Some of them are so damn fun. I had WAY too much fun surfing around. I really really enjoyed it. I spent a good amount of time surfing once I unlocked the ability. It was just so much fun and on the steam deck surfing was really flawless.-The puzzles are neither hard nor easy. I never felt like I couldn't figure something out and nothing ever felt so easy that it was boring.-I'll talk more about this in the negatives... but there is a story here... I just didn't get into it much. That being said... I DID get into the ending. The ending was really sweet and I really enjoyed it. It was really sweet and touching.-Very nice music. I really enjoyed the soundtrack.The Negative-The story.... is more frustrating than anything. There are little tablet looking things you find that give snippets of story... but for the most part every tablet truly felt like it was just using different words to say the same thing. Then each area shows what percentage of stuff you have found. You can go to the next area as long as you find 3 orbs. You don't have to get all of them or ANY of the tablets. But I was going for 100%. Finding those tablets each time.... was the most frustrating thing. There was always one tablet I was struggling to find. Then getting them didn't feel rewarding AT ALL because again... the story just felt each time like it was the saying the same thing using different words. Those tablets were hands down the most frustrating part of this game. Finding them was annoying... and not rewarding in the slightest.-You get new ways to solve a puzzle in the form of new mechanics... but the point of each puzzle is the same. Every puzzle is a slightly new variation of "Get to the orb". So it does get really repetative. It got to where I just wanted to hurry up and finish the puzzles and find the tablets so I could see a new area. Ride a new legendary creature. I wanted to experience the world, so the puzzles felt like a hinderance of that. Don't get me wrong. As I said the puzzles were neither easy nor hard. A lot of the puzzles were enjoyable. I didn't dislike the puzzles... but because it felt like I was mostly doing the same thing over and over (regardless of the changes caused from the surfing, floating, teleporting, etc) it started to get frustrating and boring. Because I JUST wanted to move on and enjoy more of the world.-Timing puzzles.... there's a certain point where you will get the ability to essentially teleport to certain areas. Then you get the ability to float. Once you have both of those there will be areas where you will be shooting through the air and have a certain window of time to look at JUST the right spot and get the indicator to teleport. If you miss that window... you have to start the puzzle over. This likely won't be a make or break for most people. It did become frustrating as hell for me though because I have sensory processing issues and reduced reaction time because of those issues. Which just makes those puzzles hella frustrating for me.Overall...This game was enjoyable. Again the environments were really gorgeous. The game just feels like it's missing something. I clearly have my complaints... but I can't tell you specifically what it was about those that made the feel like it was just... missing something crucial. I don't know if it's variety... if it's just the story. I don't know.But overall I'd say it's worth a play. Due to my issues with the game though AND the short play time. I definitely don't recommend it at full price. If you can get it on sale and you enjoy a decent puzzle game. I recommend it. The puzzles are generally decent. If you don't mind a very vague and redundant story. But enjoy really pretty environments and decent enough puzzles. You'll enjoy it.Overall despite my issues I could never say I didn't like the game. It just also isn't exactly a favorite amongst the other games I'm played this year. It is a middle of the road game for me.Additionally:-If you are looking for a game to play while sick this is a great game. I played it while I was recovering from a minor surgery. I was on bed rest and this was a good game to play under the groggy effect of pain killers. It was easy to pick up and put down. It was also simple enough that I could play it while maybe not firing on all brain cells. I will say that because I was getting bored at points... I did fall asleep a few times while playing the game.-I played entirely on the steam deck. It ran well. It controlled well. The battery life was good on it. Zero complaints. I'd actually be willing to wager I'd hate playing it on pc compared to playing it on my deck and that's a VERY rare occurance. Stuff like the surfing I can definitely say I doubt I would like as much on PC.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: OMNO is a beautiful experience in a world of peace, harmony and very good vibes.We take the role of a young "boy" who goes into a long journey through mountains and valleys, forests and swamps, deserts and ethereal planes, all to find the light and the other world long awaited.With extremely beautiful musical scores all along, OMNO reveals itself as an original game, allowing the player to advance in skills that will help him overcome all paths ahead until the end. I loved Rime, by Tequila Works, so I wanted to play this game that sounded a lot Rime-like. And I loved it. It's an amazing little piece of art that no one will regret playing.As a negative thing, I'd only point out the AWSD ER keys, since we have no option to redefine our own. I had a really hard time to get used to those keys that I never use and I never liked. Anyway, still a great game! Totally recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: All around a pretty chill and cool game with some satisfying puzzles. Very pretty to look at.As a kickstarter backer I was pretty excited for this game to come out. Once it came out it took me a few years to get around to beating though, as I didn't feel particularly compelled to progress. The most exciting parts of the game take some time to get to and are often fleeting. A lot of the promo material shows off wondrous moments of flying/snowboarding/windsurfing etc. but in practice its only like 20% of the game.Not a bad experience by any means, but I was expecting to be absolutely captivated. 7/10 or so. I'd like to see a sequel that focused more on integrating the awe-inspiring moments of gameplay as the main course. A lot of the gameplay was spent getting around areas much more slowly and frustratingly than I'd like to, whereas I got the impression from the promo material that the ways you could move was supposed to feel empowering. In my impatience I rushed through some of the earlier areas and ended up putting the game down for a while multiple times -- it was only until the back half of the game that I found myself replaying some of the platforming/warping/flying parts for fun (in part because as previously mentioned, it takes some time to get to the compelling parts of the gameplay.) I'd love to see a version of this game that focused more on the gameplay of the in-betweens and the final area.

_childDocuments_.review: beautiful and introspective game, fairly intuitive and just challenging enough for someone who doesn't play platformers very much. the story is intriguing, the music is great and atmospheric, the movement mechanics are really fun and fluid. i also love our lil companion and i need a plushie of them immediately. the creatures are a mix of adorable and horrendous abominations (in a good way), and i love how you can interact with them. i almost 100%'d it as i went, just a couple puzzles i couldn't figure out, but i will go back and try to complete them all. i got this on sale, but i think it's worth it at full price.def recommend, even if you're not a big platformer person!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really beautiful.It looks fantastic, the music is very soothing, the animations are smooth and the creatures looks amazing.The tasks in this game are relatively easy to understand and the plot line is clear and also easy to understand. This game does not add any unnecessary text, dialogue or information.I especially liked the abilities. They were creative and all felt very fun to use. The impact of certain actions, like smacking to the ground or dashing, felt very strong and I liked that.I sometimes had a bit of a fight with the float controls but other than that it felt very smooth and nice to use.A very soothing and relaxing experience. _childDocuments_.review: Cute little puzzle adventure/platformer created by one guy.'Omno' is a game in which the main character + his flying pet go on some kind of pilgrimage. On your journey you traverse through areas with their own environment like (swamp, desert, grass, snow etc.). Every level (I think around 10) has their own weird creatures and you will have to solve some puzzles to go over to the next area. Every few levels you gain a new skill like dashing or gliding which are necessary to continue. No one can really say Omno is a bad game, especially since it's pretty much made by one person. On the other hand, there is not a lot you haven't seen in other games or anything that really stands out. Omno is a quite easy game for most people. There is no combat and falling in a canyon just spawns you back somewhere near. The puzzles, for the most part, are childsplay. It will take most people a few hours to complete the game.Overall: If you want a cute and relaxing game to complete on a sunday afternoon, get this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game, the music is incredible and the visuals are so magical.It's a beautiful and immersive world, it was so fun to see and read about all the different creatures, especially the massive ones. It has a unique style to it that feels very cozy, and the puzzles were nice and simple. At no point did I get bored of the game, I played the whole thing in one sitting and would totally do it again. In fact, I would love to play so much more of this, I wasn't done hopping around this magical place.I loved the story, it told an awesome tale in just a few hours and I quickly fell in love with the characters. With just enough detail to keep you interested and understand it without becoming too much. A lot of games can sometimes give you too much information, but this was just perfect, and completely optional if you wanted to read extra about the animals you met. (Which I definitely did)The creatures and fauna in this game are so well made, they're cute and mystical and so awesome to meet. As someone who adores animals, I loved every second of it and mostly went around admiring the beautiful designs. Really amazing work in designing everything in this game.100% recommend this game, it's great if you just need a break from the world and need a cozy little expirence.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game, nothing overly complicated, mechanics pretty easy to understand and get used to, the scenes are beautiful and it has relaxing music.The puzzles are kinda easy to figure out, if not, there are plenty of walkthroughs for help.I'm really enjoying it, iI' doing the last chapter tomorrow.Another big plus is that is short, you finish it in 3-4 hours, for people with limited free time like me.I didnt find anything negative really, even that annoying part where you had to make some perfectly timed jumps/dashes/glides to get to the other side to grab a light globe was challenging and fun.So I recommend it, if you re fan of the platforming, puzzle solving, exploration, indie games.

The core gameplay is a movement oriented 3D platformer with a very satisfying power curve for upgrades. Overall it's a beautiful game and the ending is *chef's kiss*

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Omno felt like peacefully floating on a quiet lake in the middle of nature.It is a relaxing and enjoyable experience that gets underlined with a fitting Soundtrack.People who loved Games like "Journey" , "Sky: Children of Light" , "RIME" and "AER Memories of Old" will totally love this game !!!
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I played the demo a few years ago, I have been following Jonas and the development of Omno closely. I was so excited for this game to come out and I was not disappointed.The style, colour theory and musical score are gorgeous. The puzzles are fun and at times challenging. The story is very moving, which is especially impressive without there being any dialogue present.I highly recommend this game, Studio Inky fox's debut, to anyone who likes this genre.The only issue (which was minor) that I came across was that on keyboard controls the prompted actions weren't always responsive, but other than that I cannot fault it for anything.Well worth your money and time! Looking forward to future projects from this dev.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game for those who love imaginative game journey spiced with some platforming and puzzles. I waited for the game few years and I had wonderful time playing it. The only problem I had was in the last part of the game. Flying through air gates did not worked for me for several minutes. Glide boost always died out before I was able to reach the last gate and I was stuck with progress. But the problem went away after several tries.  Overall, the game is a relaxing experience filled with amazing vistas, cute creature designs, vivid colors, lovely soundtrack and simple yet captivating lore.  Thank you for meditative, heartwarming journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: This game was on sale so I decided to pick it up. I'm also patiently waiting on "Exo One". So glad I swooped on this game. At the time of writing this I'm 2 and half entertaining and relaxing hours in. I love these "Journey" style games where you are taking a....well......journey. While you may not encounter enemies during the game some of the puzzles in each world are the real enemy or more so overthinking and under thinking. Some puzzles are so easy they're hard and some so hard they'er easy. LOL! Omno is a screenshoters playground. The lighting and shadow effects are top notch. The worlds are so beautiful, elegant and have their own lovable elements and animals. The game is smooth as butter. I'm excited to continue. I have a couple of minor gripes. If you try to go back and 100% complete previous levels you overwrite your data. OUCH! Meaning you have to play from the point you went back aaaaaaalllll over again. Sucks if you are far in the game. I hope they release a patch or something so we can get achievements without having to do it all over again. The goal gets repetitive at times. New world, solve puzzle, grab orb, rinse and repeat. it's a minor gripe that you forget about when you are exploring and soaking in the scenery but that feeling is there. Other than that Omno is gorgeous, and rewarding.I give Omno a 9 out of 10 and HIGHLY recommend it. BRAVO!
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: I came across Omno while browsing for something to stream, and something told me "this it it, this is the game."And so, my journey with Omno began that same day.This game hit me on so many emotional levels, I honestly can't put it into words how incredible Omno truly is, this game will forever and always hold a very dear place in my heart.- The graphics are absolutely stunning, no matter what direction you look or area you are in, there is always something to admire.- The soundtrack is extremely relaxing, it makes the game play that much better.- The gameplay is fluid, fun, and ever-changing with each new area, there is always something new to do in each place.- The puzzles aren't over complicated, but just difficult enough to tickle your brain.- The creatures, and things you can interact with are plentiful, and give you a nice surprise when you discover what interactions some of the creatures have!- The story line is so... Incredible, this is something that MAKES the game, if you play Omno, please read each dialogue given to you, it makes it that much more worth it.Omno will always be a 10/10 to me, thank you for making such an incredible game.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: This game has soured the more I think about it, so keep in mind that my review is very naive. Go play The Pathless or Solar Ash instead, those will be more like what you're looking for.TL:DR - 8/10 Fun to play and a visual and acoustic treat! Would benefit from some more polish and length.This game was a game where I couldn't help but smile while playing it. The OST is magnificent for its noticeable limitations, the visuals are simple yet poignant, and the abilities flow well into one another, making for some exciting gameplay in the later stages. The game would definitely benefit from some more length, however. Chapters 1-3 flow very well, with the ice stages being SO GOOD HOLY FUNK THEY ARE SO GOSH DANG FUN! The finale is also a visual blast to play through, but the desert stage, part 4, feels rather crammed in and out-of-place, with the teleport ability deleting the euphoria gained from surfing over snow and sand alike. But the potential is obvious, and this game begs for a console/PC re-release with more stages, because this rides the line many games do between amazing and art.-Nate
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not only beautiful, but it has stunning music and amazing in game controls. Everything felt smooth to play. Where I've often felt myself get frustrated with puzzle platformers, this one was so relaxing it was never an issue. The puzzles are fun to figure out, the scenery is beautiful, interacting with the wildlife made me cry... twice. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for an ethereal, surreal and heart-warming gaming experience that few games manage to achieve, look no further than OMNO.I can't tell you how many times during my play-through of this game I had to remind myself this was all done by one person. Why? Because the game is as close to perfect as you could hope for.The game creates a world that pulls you in and holds you there for the entire duration, and there is literally nothing that gets in the way of your enjoyment. The controls are intuitive and fluid, the mechanics needed to easily move around the incredibly large levels are there and the music and transition scenes literally gave me goosebumps.  In short, the game is just an absolute joy to play and you'll be sad when it comes to an end.I can not recommend this game highly enough.  If you have any interest in this game at all, don't hesitate. It's more than worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: A very pleasant game! Despite a few minor glitches which can probably be just the lack of dexterity on my end. it's a very smooth ride and I'm enjoying it a lot. It really reminds me of my first sci-fi/ fantasy stories that I read from the 80's somehow, the music really compliments the game and brings so much depth to it. Just for the soundtrack alone and for the ability to glide in these beautiful areas this game gets a huge thumbs up for me. It's a beautiful experience. Definitely a game to rest with  <3
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: I have loved OMNO since I first heard about it a few years ago and tried out the early demos. It is my favourite kind of game with a mixture of exploration, platforming and puzzles so I backed it on Kickstarter. As a beta-tester I got to play it again during final development and I loved every minute of it. I also played through the full game since release.Everything about OMNO is just fantastic - the world is gorgeous and so enjoyable to travel through, meeting lots of cute creatures as you go; the main character and his travelling companion are beautifully animated and you really get the sense of their friendship developing as you both progress; the music is the perfect accompaniment to the emotional story; and the gameplay is so well balanced, and so much fun, making you feel more powerful as you gain abilities.I recommend everyone who plays OMNO to take your time to explore, play with the animals, listen to the wonderful music and enjoy the quiet moments, as that is essentially what the game is all about!
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely wonderful experience for 4.5-5 hours.  The ending is excellent though no spoilers, the puzzles offer challenge but not so much as to feel frustrating.  The world design is beautiful, score is perfectly suited and never repetitive or annoying.  This is one to chill out to and play.  My hat is off to the dev who made this what amazing pride they should take in this masterpiece, this is the reason I avoid AAA these days and look for indie titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond its atmosphere, its art, its animations and the incredible feel of its movement mechanics, the masterful thing about Omno is how it stays within itself: it understand what makes it special and focuses on that.No element overstay its welcome and each of them (the fauna!) feels unique and detailed;  making it one of the leanest, best paced game I've had in that genre; and a joy to play.There's only a handful of thing I wish would be eventually tweaked:1. capacity to deactivate scripted cameras when discovering areas: I feel the music swell and the area title would be accented enough; and the environment definitely stand on their own.2. make the transition from dash/glide into surfing more fluid/less strict, to make long traversal across different terrain even more satisfying.3. I think glide is interrupted when colliding; which made a couple of platform segments involving teleport and glide  not very satisfying.5. support turn on the spot better, for the most finicky platforming bits

Navigating the beautiful environment along with cute creatures is truly an experience people who love this genre should experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a simple yet very pleasant experience. I don't really think there is much story here besides the small tidbits that you read so I largely ignored them. And the gameplay is fairly straightforward. You have to collect beacons of light in order to progress in the level but you can choose to figure out all the puzzles in the area to achieve 100% completion. I found the game to be pretty easy and this is coming from someone who doesn't really like puzzle platform games; however, I didn't think this was a detriment to the game at all. A note though, I didn't 100% every area so there may be a few tough puzzles to crack that I never even attempted.What I really loved about this game was how calm and atmospheric it was. The low-poly art style is gorgeous and the charming wildlife does a lot to bring everything to life. The soundtrack did a lot to help accentuate the world's features as well. I think for the very casual experience that this is then the list price is a bit expensive; however, it is a well-polished, charming little game that is definitely worth your time especially if you get it on sale. Currently, as of this writing it's in the August 2022 Humble Choice, if you're interested in buying it. I received my copy as part of a bundle, and while I thoroughly enjoyed the game, I believe the price might be a tad high for its length.That being said, I completed the game in about 4 hours, and every minute was filled with charm and intrigue. So if you're in the mood for a captivating journey that won't overstay its welcome, Omno is definitely worth checking out when it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve known about OMNO after seeing it on a Steam friend’s feed, then decided to pick it up as I’m a fan of puzzle games. Turns out it was a very good idea.It’s several hours of mostly environmental puzzles in five or six worlds. Very reminiscent of , although maps are not as varied. Thankfully, every arena introduces some new creatures and mechanics, I also found the overall design (both style-wise and puzzle-wise) very captivating. Another good thing is that we are not required to complete all puzzles in a given level to progress to the next one. You can be as much of a completionist as you want to be, which is a very good choice for this type of title.Presented story is as shallow or as deep as you want it to be. For me more important was the emotional aspect, and that one hits the spot in OMNO with a big help from implemented music. It is coded in a way which makes it more intense as soon as you move further with your puzzle. This does the trick and works perfectly. Music tells a story here as much as text notes, if not more.The 20$ price tag may seem a bit steep, but I think it’s accurate if the whole experience is as good as in this one. It may also be treated as a form of support for that one person who created this entire game. Among other similar titles brought single-handedly (, ), this one shines as bright. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I was following along with the creator of the game on social media before it came out, so I was very excited when i could actually play it. I didn't and don't recommend buying it at full price because of how short the game is, but it's still DEFINITELY worth a play.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: Omno is a fun little puzzle platformer where you run around cataloguing animals and reading runes.The game is great fun, the animals are cute and the puzzles are mostly easy.The only complaint I have is about the controls. They are not weird, but they are not always responding.The game is very zen, I almost fell asleep and I mean that as a compliment.The game took me just shy of 5 hours to complete 100% but it didn't outstay its welcome.The art style is simplistic but also pleasant to look at.Overall a very nice game with only one minor problem 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very nice - amazing enviroment, great soundtrack, good graphics. Sometimes the controls and camera don't work as they should, but it is a very minor problem in comparison to the rest of the experience, and unless you're particularly prone to motion sickness it should be okay. The puzzles are good (although pretty easy) and have a great variety to them, thanks to the abilities you keep gaining.The story was very enjoyable. My first thought, one that lasted throughout my playthrough, was "the Light is a lie". But I am a known Moksha hater, so I wrote it off as personal bias, and in the end, the ending was very satisfying; watching the character interact with his surroundings adds to the story too, especially considering the end goal.The story (especially its final cutscene) can really be summed up as "". It is very similar to the Hindu idea of liberation (hence all the obnoxious reference), but overall manages to work with that concept in a way that comes off as an original take on it.Overall, I'd say it's not a full ten, thanks to the small issues and the overall short playtime, but comes very close. And I can recommend if you're into puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: Contemplative games are not usually my cup of tea but oh wow did I love playing Omno.Beautiful scenery, amazing soundtracks and sweet story with a pinch of (really easy) puzzles and exploration that made the whole experience very pleasant. Bonus points for the wildlife, it adds so much vibrancy and flavor to the already beautiful environment, definitely one of my favorite aspects of the game.Going for completion on each part of the map is really easy and rewarding, and it only makes this gem of a game longer, better and deeper.This is definitely a game I would eyes closed recommend to anyone, it's simply a hidden masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Omno is an indie gem that will take you on an unforgettable journey through a beautiful fantasy world. Inspired by the acclaimed game Journey, Omno offers a serene and evocative experience of exploration and discovery. With enchanting graphics, an immersive soundtrack, and intuitive gameplay mechanics, this game invites you to get lost in mystical landscapes and solve creative puzzles. Perfect for those seeking a moving and relaxing adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Very pleasant visuals and sound design in a minimalist style create a calming and beautiful environment for a bit of puzzle platforming. Each zone starts with some light exploration and then a short puzzle, and rewards you with a scenic transport on a large beast to the next zone. Very nice and simple game, but could even have done without the text on some of the lore pieces to complete the show-dont-tell experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game enough.Omno is a beautiful little platforming game following the journey of a staffbearer trying to find out what happened to their people. While searching different areas you will encounter curious wildlife to interact with and solve some minor puzzles but overall it feels more like a meditative exercise than real brain-teasers. There's not really much more I can say about it besides maybe comparing it to games like Journey or Abzu. Like those games, Omno is a fairly short experience but I will like it's one I will always treasure.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: Omno is the story of a man trying to find his people, and finding all sorts of unexpected treasures along the way. It is an indie puzzle game that will just take your breath away, as well as make you smile and laugh quite often as you experience all the funny creatures you encounter (41 total). StoryThe story is good, not riveting, but still interesting, and the ending is very good.VisualsThe visuals are beautiful and unique, as the creator invented all his own plants and animals, and the colors are diverse and well drawn. The views are amazing, especially when you look out over a great canyon with bits of floating city scattered all around.MusicThe music is amazing, I have not find many games with more fitting music in each level than in this game, which most reminded me of music from Ori and the Will of the Wisps.Difficulty of the puzzlesNot very hard, but hard enough to keep you from getting bored and keeps you from getting frustrated.LengthNot long enough, wish there was more. I finished it and all achievements in one afternoon, and thoroughly enjoyed every minute of it. However, it was short enough that I didn't have to stop and come back to it later, and it ended at a very good point, so I should't complain.PriceI got this in the August 2022 humble bundle, and I think it is worth $15.00 bucks for the length. But because it was all done by one guy, $20.00 is a good price.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun and relaxing game, with interesting creatures to discover on your journey. I enjoyed my playthrough of it quite a bit as I went for the 100% completion in every area, and all the while the music made the experience even better.Feels similar to games like Journey and Abzû in my opinion, which also means that a blind playthrough is the best way to experience this adventure. OMNO is on the shorter side like the previous mentioned games, and there's not really a lot of replay value if you did everything you could on your first playthrough... but if you take your time and just enjoy the journey (and if you know what to expect in regards to the length) it'll work out just fine. ^w^
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely have to recommend this game. It made me cry (in a good way) at the end! I really love the natural progression of the narrative, how it gives you hints and then broader clues as to the "core" of the story, and I definitely guessed where it was going but in one of those ways that makes you eager to see if what you want is going to play out. The graphics are good, the music is amazing, and the game definitely has a "Journey" feel, only with more-tangible puzzles. The puzzles were a bit frustrating at times, but never so bad that I had to look them up, and there were a lot of joyful, in-the-experience moments that I had a lot of fun with (I do love the 'surfing' mechanic").
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: The game is visually appealing, the controls are responsive for the most part, but overall a nice, short puzzle/adventure game with a visual narrative, unique character and creature design and  decent puzzles to solve.  The puzzles themselves aren't on the same level of the first Prince of Persia, which require a lot of planning ahead, but they're decent enough for anyone not get stuck on them for hours.  There is zero combat, but there are abilities gain while we journey through this game.  The music is very relaxing and I didn't feel bored playing the game which I've finished in a few hours.  The game can be finished under 2 hours or 5 in my case due to fact that I was just exploring everything this game had to offer and was screwing around a little.  I got the game for free from a friend who got it from the monthly Humble Bundle.  I don't really know if I would have bought the game personally for $19 despite how short this game is and there isn't anything else after I beaten the game and gotten all the achievements.Even if this game didn't have any achievements, again there really isn't anything else that pulling me to playing it again.  Like Prince of Persia and Chrono trigger for example, I could play those multiple times without ever getting tired of it, but this game however, I'm not feeling the drive to play it again for fun.  Maybe for some people out there that feel like this game is enough for and power to them; however, it's a one and done for me.  I did had an issue with the controls temporary where I couldn't move at all and was forced to restart, but after that, that problem ended after the restart.  I didn't care too much for the UI when pausing the game, but that didn't kill my experience with the game.  I would only recommend this if the game was very cheap, but keep in mind that this game is very short and while the puzzles were okay, but didn't wow me.  As for the developer who made this game, I hope he continues making more games, learn from each and every experience, take constructive criticisms over the blind ones that offer nothing remotely helpful and then most importantly have fun making art, which I assume he did with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: Thumbs up only because of how impressive this is for a solo developer to make. It's essentially a copy of journey from Annapurna Interactive. But personally I found the lore and story building better in Journey. Not much exciting gameplay, so only get this if you want to chill out to some nice visuals and music for an afternoon. Took me 4 hours to 100% it. I can't see myself playing this game again.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I finished the game (100% plus all achievements). Seriously, this game is a masterpiece. Stop reading my review and just buy/play it.I have only played this game for an hour so far, but I believe I have already experienced the core gameplay and I just need to get this review out before I forget. Honestly this game deserves every bit of hype and love it has received thus far and so much more.I kickstarted this game a while back and watching Omno grow has been so fulfilling. The developer's story and approach to this game has even inspired me in my game development journey. I'm just so absolutely thrilled that playing this game feels every bit what I expected it to be (and let me tell you, I had really high expectations). In a word, the game is just unbelievably thoughtful. The animations are so clean, the environment is so beautiful, the lore and creatures fascinating, the sound design is phenomenal, the player abilities feel so fluid, but most importantly, the world feels vibrant and alive.In an exploration game, you want to incentivize exploring and Omno does exactly that. There are very few games I have felt a compulsion to 100% but in my first four levels of playing, I have felt that compulsion. Why? Because interacting with stuff is so satisfying! I would say those who have enjoyed games like Journey or Abzu will find Omno in the same caliber.The puzzles aren't super difficult, but I have had a couple I've come across already where I had to take a step back and think about it, which was great. Oh and the music is amazingly relaxing, cinematic, and beautiful. I cannot say enough nice things about this game and really hope it gets the support it deserves!
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: Omno was great! I've heard of this game since before its release and was not disappointed. I really liked uncovering all the secrets and different wildlife! It was very fun, would play again! I definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a relaxing, fun, diverse game.
