_childDocuments_.review: Positives:- The music.- The radar (+ percentage indicator) is a good way to provide some guidance and a sort of checklist without using a full map or minimap.- Surfing is pretty fun and the section where it is introduced is very well done.Neutral:- This is an example of games that should be categorized as "audiovisual experiences with very light gameplay" because that's basically what it is. You look at nice landscapes and beautiful cutscenes for 3 hours while listening to good music - and collecting all the McGuffins is just so the game is not just one long walk that takes 90 minutes. Some of the plarforming and puzzles are nice additions and they provide a slight challenge, but overall it has to keep the mechanical aspects very light or else it looses the "relaxing" and "casual" vibe.- I have no idea why they only require 3 out of the 5-7 McGuffins to be collected in order to continue to the next level. They build this whole level and put everything in it (mind you, in an already very short game, ie. 100% in 3 hours) so why should I be allowed to skip like half of it?Negatives:- It lacks the most basic options like camera sensitivity, inverting the x-axis, key remapping, accessibility options, and lots and lots more. For me the game was completely unplayable with a controller and with mouse and keyboard it was ...- Platforming can be a bit frustrating. Not because it's difficult, but because the controls and the terrain are sometimes working against you.- "Meet fantastical creatures" it says in the description. Unfortunately they are reduced to checklist items that do an animation and give some glowy bits when pressing E next to them. The only real "fantastical creatures" are the ones between levels and they are in cutscenes.- Yeah it has a story and some people may acutally care, but as soon as I saw the obligatory emotional companion pet I lost all interest in it. And guess what, obviously it's the thing at the very end that's supposed to make you go "awwww" with a tear in your eye. It's soooooo cookie cutter and bland.

_childDocuments_.review: A really chill platformer for children or those who are new to gaming. More experienced gamers will definitely find this one a bit too easy. On the other hand, if you're collecting 100% achievement games this one won't tax you much.It feels like 'Omno' is trying real hard to have the same energy as 'Journey' and just isn't quite getting there. It's unfair to compare anything to 'Journey' because 'Journey' is a really good game. However 'Omno' practically begs for the comparison with some of its set piece moments, the way the (extremely bare bones) story is told, the way the character's energy is shown on his body, etc.So if you're looking for something that's sorta like 'Journey' but not quite as good... well you found it.That said, there are definitely some negatives. The controls need a few tweaks, such as allowing the Float ability to be activated by a button that's already being held when it becomes available rather than having to wait. Likewise the controls while flying are different than the controls while walking which makes it difficult to steer until you're used to switching off. Oh, and the game just not saving your journal progress after you finish the game and replay chapters. Fixing little problems like those would go a long way to make this a better game.At full price I don't feel like this is worth it but if you can get it for half-off or better you're going to have a relaxing day at an OK price. Just don't walk into this expecting a particularly memorable experience. But, as I said in the beginning, if there's someone in your life who's not used to holding a controller you could definitely do worse than 'Omno' to teach that person the basics..
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: I am legally required to mention the game Journey in any review of Omno.  So here it is: Journey.  The creative collapsed civilisation.  The novel flowing ways of getting around.  The faultless graphics.  The breathtaking bugless scenery, the bizarre life-forms.  Omno is not as good as Journey, of course, but nothing is.You figure out things about the collapsed civilisation.  You solve puzzles and complete sequences of jumps.  The puzzles aren't very difficult, and I never shouted "Well, how was I meant to guess that ?!" at the screen.  The jumps are mostly a case of figuring out what keys to press and when.  None of them require pixel-perfect positioning.  You can't die.  If you manage to get into an unsafe position you are just warped back to the most recent savepoint, with progress intact.Mostly, the game is fun.  Some of the levels are big.  There are methods of fast trave like snowboarding and flying.  They're wonderful experiences.  So much so that you might go back to do them again.  Some of the things you do require help from animals.  The animals are weird and kooky.  Interacting with them is fun.  So much so that you sometimes do it just because you can.  Very little about the game is pointlessly annoying.  The designer put a lot of thought into this and it shows.It's not a long game, but it's priced way below the point where you are desperate to get your money's worth.   Worth full price, and perhaps more.

_childDocuments_.review: A cute (so freaking cute) and easy going 3rd person 3D platformer. It took me about 3.5 hours to complete, and it was a very relaxing play through. You and your ADORABLE floating green cat friend travel from world to world, learning about its animals, plants, and environment, and maybe even... about YOURSELF. This game forces you to consider weather (as we are commonly told in our society) you must keep pushing for more, or can we simply stop, and appreciate and enjoy what you already have. I want to get better about saying why I gives games the reviews I do, so... negatives: As far as puzzle and platformer games are concerned, I think I just dislike the "find this" puzzle. I don't find just looking for a thing to be an enjoyable use of my time. There is a fair amount of "find it" puzzles in this game which are not my favorite. _childDocuments_.review: Short little puzzle game that was a bit of fun.You walk around and are solving puzzles that involve a little bit of platforming using various skills you obtain throughout the game. There is also a large focus on exploration. Each of the 10 areas has things you need to collect and see in order to get full completion. There are several abilities you unlock, the first is the dash which is self-explanatory and after its acquisition becomes a frequent use in the game. The next one is a skating-like ability that is used for faster traversal, unfortunately, this ability is a bit underused and doesn’t serve much of a purpose outside of faster movement when the areas open up a bit, the increase isn’t that much either. Another ability is teleport, this allows you to teleport to certain points in the areas and also sees frequent use in puzzles after its introduction, it combines with the dash ability to make a nice combination for solving the puzzles. Lastly is a glide ability, this one comes late in the game but does see frequent use and works extremely well with dash and teleport and for this, the last sections of the game are the strongest with the most diverse puzzles and interesting ideas. The game is definitely geared towards younger audiences as the puzzles are quite simple to solve and for the most part, don’t require too much thinking, this does make it a bit boring to play and definitely kills replay value especially with a lacking story. There isn’t much of a story but there are glyphs you can get to give some backstory and world-building, it is all textual though, and isn’t very engaging. The graphics are nice, have a simple art style that is nice to look at and the models are really good looking, each creature is unique and adds great diversity to the game. The soundtrack is alright, not much there but it doesn’t detract and is pretty good towards the conclusion of the game. Omno is an ok game, it is rather short and simple with some nice puzzles. However, at the current price point, I don’t really recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Omno is an experience, combining exploration and puzzle-solving as you learn about the world around you. Using an array of abilities that you obtain through the course of your journey, you will glide, dash, and surf through different biomes, unlocking knowledge about a long lost civilization. All that remains of this land are the abundant and various creatures that inhabit icy peaks, dunes, swamps, and plains. You feel at home, but, unwelcome at the same time. Your name-less Staffbearer doesn’t resemble any of the animals around you, however, the crumbling towers and statues bear an uncanny resemblance.I felt like I was alone in this world, even though I had my animal friends beside me. The only narration or dialogue was fed to the Staffbearer via remnants of past travelers. There was no direction, only an end goal. The Portal. This isn’t a spoiler as you learn it at the very beginning, but it is important to lay out the theme of Omno. You have this ever-growing sense that you are walking in purgatory, or the bridge between life and death. Even while surrounded by beauty, there is almost a sense of sadness and an expectation of “the end”. You are left questioning the events that took place that left this world in its current state. I think that this is where Omno succeeds, but also misses. There was so much opportunity here to add to the secrets that I’m sure lie hidden in the mountain sides, ancient ruins, and other landmarks. The secrets were out in the open, waiting to be stumbled upon. In a game that is zone based, I would have loved to see one “secret” per zone that unlocked a hint or piece of information pertinent to further understanding the journey that you are on. While the level design was enjoyably beautiful, it also felt empty and planned. That being said, I found myself enjoying the different types of available puzzles and zones as they felt different enough to keep the game feeling fresh.What makes Omno feel the most like an experience is the atmosphere set by the visual storytelling and the emotional music. The long panning shots when moving from zone-to-zone was one of my favorite moments. It set my excitement levels to high right before I started exploring the new area. All the while, the slow, epic, and deep music playing in the background, setting me in the correct mood, whether it was a hot desert or a wintery plain. It gives me the same chills that Ori and the Blind Forest does. I’m a sucker for music like this so you can be sure that I’ve added it to my Spotify favorites and will be listening to it when I am relaxing.I 100%’d the game in just under 3 hours and while I don’t see myself playing it again any time soon, I enjoyed the time that I spent playing the game. It is a story that left my mouth open at the end. I was glad that I got to experience it. If you are on the edge about whether or not you want to play it, there is a demo available on Steam for you to try first! Go give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this is a nice little puzzle-ish platofrm-ish game. It's not particularly difficult -- the only source of mild frustation that I had was finding all the stuff in some areas; all sections that required some quick and reasonably accurate movement had a checkpoints right in front of them.There's a bit of a story, but it's nothing to write home about, at all -- and the ending could be better.It's rather short -- I 100%-ed it in one day, which is rare. I'm usually a slow player.As I said, it's not difficult either -- the puzzles are straightforward, nothing weird or complicated. I actually 100%-ed each level, without a guide, on the first playthrough. Which is actually pretty good -- a puzzle game that you can just play, without having to look up things, is kind of rare. Levels are all structured identically as well, so you know what to do.There's NO combat of any kind; the world is peaceful and nice (there's just ONE puzzle where some kind of laser can kill you; for everything else, the only danger is falling off the floating islands (especially later in the game, when you get more airborne movement and the game has you traverse the open skies without solid ground below you).

_childDocuments_.review: I hesitate to leave a negative review for such a beautifully crafted game, but there are just too many annoyances for me to make a recommendation right now.I'm using a XBox 360 controller, and the controls for gliding and surfing are just not robust, leading to many failed attempts at puzzle solving. This led me on several occasions to think that I was not understanding the puzzle, but it was simply that the controls didn't do what I was asking. Also, the teleports only seem to activate half the time during the faster puzzles. I think you have to be looking at them in a special way, but I can't do it intuitively.As a result of these issues I never feel like I'm in control, which breaks the immersion for me.Lastly, I cannot play this game with the sound on, because of the DREADFUL music score and the lack of an option to switch it off. I did find that Butterfly 3000 makes a much better soundtrack. Yes, it's just an opinion, but it's pretty arrogant if you ask me, to assume that everyone will love the horrible pastoral strings and muted trumpets. Makes me feel ill!I'm not going to give the dev a pass simply because they're a one person show. Frankly, they should have enlisted some help to polish the game, which would bring it up into the company of all those games it's compared to - Journey et al.It is at heart a pleasant wee puzzle game, using simplistic graphics to tell a codswallop story about something or other, but for the current asking price of £15, given the problems outlined above, it's a wee bit hard to justify.There are many, many better games out there for those many pounds.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to give props to the devs for making a game like this. I can tell they took a lot of inspiration from games like Ori and Journey. I can tell they wanted to give this sense of wonder about the world they present you. However, neither the story, environment, nor the art style really backs up what I perceive to be their aesthetic goals.Each level is basically an arena filled with puzzles. There are linear transitions with no collectables between most of these arenas. The graphics are simple and low-poly. There isn't anything wrong with this art style, but I don't think it supports a game where the intended main draw is the environment and the world. The story is a simple number about Onion-san and his cat going to the Temple of Doom or something. The game doesn't do a good job of "show, don't tell," and I didn't find the narrative very compelling, personally.I simply can't recommend this as a consumer, as much as I want to support the devs in their future endeavors.

_childDocuments_.review: For what it’s worth mentioning, I’m a kickstarter backer for this game and have been following development for a while.Omno is a platforming puzzle solver. All of the basics are there with running, jumping, and some neat abilities. These abilities are pretty standard for a platformer; you have a dash, a surfing ability, a hover, and a teleport. They're used with the puzzles fairly well, with only the occasionally wonkily placed platform that you accidently dash past. The abilities all feel fun but they also almost feel half finished. You use them for their dedicated puzzles and that’s about it. I’d love if you could do MORE with them. The surfing ability is by far the most fun and all it’s really used for is some downhill segments.Puzzles are very standard and, well, easy. Only a few require precise timing and there is absolutely no danger or risk of failing at all. When you fall off the map you’ll respawn at the nearest checkpoint with no repercussions. Alone I wouldn't really have this as a negative, as I think the indie trend that “difficulty = a good game” is a bad one but it does feel a little too easy at times. Maybe a slight cranking up of difficulty would be nice, especially towards the end.There are some collectibles on each map in the form of discovering the local animal species and some journal entries. There’s only 3 journal entries on each map and 3-4 new species. Very easy to discover everything in one playthrough and if you look at the achievements ahead of time it’s trivial to 100% in one go. Which is good because in my opinion there’s not a lot of replayability. Sound is great. The game has a very instrumental moody track that I feel fits the overall tone. Not a lot more to be said.The story is all but non-existent. You’re going on a journey for some reason and that’s about all there is. There are journal entries around the world you can collect that hint of a deeper lore but you feel as if they’re just scratching the surface. It’s a shame because what little lore there is seems intriguing. Combine that with the interesting architecture you encounter and I would love to know more about the world of Omno. Graphics are good, if simple. The art style is nice.I think the Omno world has a lot of potential and I would love to see a sequel, but I think it just needs more. I 100% the game in about 3ish hours and don't feel like there’s any reason for me to play through the game again. There’s also parts of the game I feel are only half utilized. Abilities don't feel like they’re used to their full potential and I’d love to see way to combine abilities to enhance each other. It would be amazing to use the dash during surfing to give yourself a boost or dash during a hover move to float farther.There’s also a mechanic when you interact with animals and some parts of the map that drop pieces of “light” that you collect. When the meter on your arm is filled up ig gives you a little speed boost and you can spend it at a pillar to get one of the objectives on each map. But that’s its only use! It would be cool to incorporate that into a boost in your abilities or have some other purpose so you dont just grab the pillar at the beginning of a map and then you’re done with it.I think this game is a really good first game for the dev, bravo! I’d love to see you use what you learned and enhance the game to another level. I think an Omno 2 could truely be an amazing game. As it is I can really only recommend this game when on sale, I think the $20 price tag is just a little too high for only 3ish hours of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure what to think of this one. The presentation is done well! However while this game gives off a similar vibe to other great games like journey and abzu, the gameplay itself felt way too formulaic and repetitive compared to those other games.The gameplay consists of being put into a relatively small open area, then solving puzzles to get at least 3 orbs with multiple of them in the area so some of them can be skipped, then unlocking the next area by solving a final puzzle of the area and be rewarded by either a legendary animal ride or a new power or just a warp to the next area. The process repeats like this until the game ends.There's a whole bunch of optional stuff that can be done too, like discovering animals and messages throughout areas, and of course the extra orbs.Overall I like this game, but it didn't impress me as much as I thought it would. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a thing of beauty. Pure beauty. A "need to remap  from the keyboard onto one of my controller buttons" beauty.Gameplay-wise? Oh, it's a 3D puzzle platformer, without enemies. It's accommodating to all levels of skill. In each consecutive world there's six-or-so orbs, of which you must collect any three, so that you may solve an end-level puzzle and progress to the next world. Three are always easy to get, whereas getting the remainder (for 100%ing the world) will require a bit of exploration and coordination.The fact that it's a puzzle platformer merely gives you something to do, but the thing with this game is how beautiful the worlds are. It's incredible that the whole game was made by one fellow (plus one music composer, who wrote tracks that fit the mood perfectly). Each world is different, and a joy to immerse into. The "puzzle platformer" bit is just giving direction for the immersive exploration, and soaking in the scenery, which is what enjoy most about this game. Getting such a low-poly world to be so gorgeous, that is a true art. It is a mastery of colours, and of light. Of imagination.To give you some bearings compared to other games that you might have experienced. I find the worlds of Omno to be even more beautiful than those in Journey. Plus, in Journey you're not expected to do  except to pass through the worlds. The comparison made me realise that Omno  have been made in similar fashion (only asking of you to stride through those worlds it created), but its experience is so much richer for giving you the puzzle-platformer tasks; those drive you to engage with the world that you're immersed into.The other game that comes to mind is The Witness. That one is a hard-core puzzler (not platformer), set in an absolutely gorgeous low-poly world. The Witness' visuals are perhaps an even more stunning display of colour-picking-and-combining genius. But its gameplay experience is fundamentally different - a down-n-up roller coaster made up of a draining frustration with the next crazy puzzle that the game throws at you, followed by the exhilaration rush of having worked it out.Omno is no such roller-coaster; on the contrary, it is a pure battery-filling experience, where you immerse yourself in a series of gorgeous worlds with cute creatures, to the background of a relaxing soundtrack. An experience I'd recommend you to treat yourself to.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite indie game style and basic graphics quality, the gameplay and narrative is amazing in a way that draws you in on each chapter.There are some semi-repetitive points in the story, but you won't quite feel it, The music and sound effects are on point, there's climax and boom effect perfectly applied to each type of progress/achievement or behaviour/action. Narrative combined with the music, on each section or chapter seems to follow a nice and steady begin to end cyclic structure that despite simplicity brings a sense of accomplishment throughout the entire game.My favorite is the relationship of the pilgrim with his pet! Love it. May be if there was an element of melee it would be nice, but it's debatable as it also could hurt the peaceful story of the game.I think it's best to not compare this game with non-indie games. If you'd like so many adventure and lots of melee, this game doesn't offer that, yet it's fun and keeps you going when you need to have some peaceful and calm moments playing a simple game.

There were also the occasional artifacting in certain areas that tricked me into thinking there were functions to address when there were not...but overall, I would recommend for a beautiful and engaging experience. Great job, and I look forward to the next game!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;Dr: This is a game in which every asset, every level, every design choice screams "made with love". Support indie Devs who put this much effort into their works. But it to instantly heal your soul.Combat-free casual puzzle plattformer with minimal "explicit" story telling (i.e. documents). During the first level, I have to admit it felt a bit empty, a bit too "new blender showcase for low poly models and volumetric lighting" - of course I was wrong, of course the beginning being /very/ accessible is an absolutely conscious design choice. This isn't a try hard game - this is a game in the tradition of Journey, Abzu, Gris, et al., which means it is an experience to be lived through.I /could/ recommend this game on the incredibly cute and well-rounded creature design alone. They're a delight in every respect, visual design, movement loops, interactions, even the in game description.The game has however, despite its ultra-casual nature, pretty neat abilities bestowed upon certain level completions and puzzles that were original despite using well established mechanics - did I mention every asset is like a handcrafted lil trinket?My only gripes with the game were overall level layouts (e.g. the desert inviting surfing but making it impossible at the slightest upward movement) and sound scape out of pure personal preference (the soundtrack is perfectly fine generally speaking).

_childDocuments_.review: Super loved this game! The atmosphere and soundtrack are stunning. Absolutely beautiful. The puzzles were a lot of fun. Amazing how a narrative with zero dialogue can still get you in the feels and make you think all the same. Super well done to accomplish that. Really the only caveat I would say is be aware that the game is rather short. I 100%ed it in about 4 hours. Which is fine narratively. I think the story lasts as long as it should and making it longer would be unnecessarily drawing it out. So I think the length here makes sense. But I would just wait to get the game when it's on sale, cause I do think the price is high for only 4 hours of content. And that's only if you're 100%ing it. Really it's shorter than that. Otherwise though, stellar game and highly recommend!!

_childDocuments_.review: Omno is a short, exploration-based 3D platformer.It has quite relaxing gameplay, to be honest. There are five main chapters. Each chapter adds new mechanics, like dash movement, skateboarding, flying, teleporting, etc. These were fun to play with. There is enough variety of animals, which helps in various ways to progress through the game. There are also some puzzle elements, but they are on the easier side. There is a map that shows the location of missing collectibles as well as the completion percentages of the relative sections. So, I didn't get lost at any point. I also got 100% completion on a single playthrough.The art style is nice and colorful. The sound tracks are top-notch. Great work on that front. I've added the album to my favourites list on Spotify.The game is made using Unreal engine. So, it has that typical rock formation, vegetation, and sound design.The story is simplistic, easy to follow, and told through text.I've played using an Xbox gamepad without any issues. The movement felt smooth. The platforming felt clunky at times, but you will get used to it as the game progresses.Overall, it was a nice experience. Grab it during a sale if you are interested.My verdict: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game about journeys, following in the footsteps of the last of your people to come before you. Seeking out the light of a new world. A few even respond to you moving around nearby and make the world feel so much more alive. The little leafy friend soon following you closely only made this better, providing small moments of cute play while solving puzzles.Each area is distinctive in layout and flora, the chapters introducing new skills to get around that match these quite well. Racing down sand dunes, flying among towering rock spires, and finding creatures in lush vegetation make the game all the more fun to explore.While a very short experience - able to be completed to 100% in one playthrough if you're thorough, and mine taking around 4 hours to slowly explore the world and find everything - I cannot recommend it enough and will likely be replaying it very soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple platforming + collecting game with some puzzle elements. No combat and mostly undemanding/slow paced for the first 3 hours, but later levels do have some tricky timing bits that require switching from dashing, floating, and teleporting, all in very quick succession. This is a fairly short game, but well done and fairly varied in both level design, puzzles, and aesthetics. I'm hugely impressed that a single person (albeit working for about 5 years) made this, given the level of polish. If it were the work of 10 people I'd be less impressed, but I'd have still enjoyed the gameplay equally. My biggest complaint is that this game doesn't really progress very much in terms of taking a mechanic and slowly elaborating it to ramp up the challenge. Instead, entirely new mechanics are introduced with every new level, which keeps the game fresh but diminishes the sense of mastery that makes reflex based games like this satisfying to master. Also, I'm not really into the only bit of challenge he did introduce later on, which was the narrow time window in which to engage the teleportation mechanic (while falling, floating, etc.). I could have used more puzzles and tricky jumping challenges that used the in-air dash move, which was super satisfying to use and watch. In terms of controls, you need two joysticks for movement and camera control, plus buttons for jumping, dashing, floating, and teleporting, and occasionally buttons for interacting with objects and for showing the in-game map.  None of which are remappable.  That's a lot to juggle and makes what at first glance seems like a great game for disabled gamers not so well-suited after all.

_childDocuments_.review: One of those moments where it's a shame there's nothing similar to a neutral recommendation vote, but overall it's more of a "no" than a "yes" for me. It can still be a nice experience, but due to the level of quality and the price, I would only recommend it on a good sale.- Relaxing atmosphere- Cute creatures- Occasional nice scenery- No sound settings- Movement often feels heavy/clunky- During the traveling "cutscenes" the camera keeps snapping back into the position it wants, not allowing you to look around and see the scenery- Jumping between chapters removes all discovery notes- Some levels feel a bit more bland where nothing stands out in particular- You can't pet your follower whenever you want

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of platforming but the basic movement mechanics are simple and clunky meaning they don't flow well together. Even jumping into a glide requires you to stop pressing jump and wait before you can start holding glide (dear Mr. Gamedev: you're looking for the 'button is held' state, not the rising edge). It feels like the player controls have been adapted from a Unreal Engine template.Lots of things are mapped to X/square in a way that is intrusive. Why are there two face buttons dedicated to rare actions if it means I risk teleporting to the other side of the map when I try to interact with a creature?Some of the later jump puzzles seem not to have been playtested thoroughly - you can 'solve' the puzzle by having the right intention but fail because of buggy execution. Speaking of bugs, my little green dude gets yeeted into the backrooms every time I interact with him. There's not much content but by the end I was too bored of what the game had to offer to want more.Seeing the in-game Kickstarter memorial made me understand why this is so well-reviewed. Outsiders will never appreciate a game in the way trauma-bonded backers do. The moment-to-moment experience of this game is one of boredom. It's just not fun to move around in the way it is for a 3D Mario or Spyro game. Omno would be a lot more enjoyable if this fundamental had been improved. For £15 it's just not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're on the fence about this game, watch the trailers. If you like the trailers and think it looks fun and relaxing and pretty, then you'll like the game.This is a very kid-friendly, zero-combat, peaceful game with simple but fun puzzles. The graphics are very stylized and cartoony but also very pretty. The music is very pretty and atmospheric, if not exactly riveting.It's not very long... but it's also not very expensive.The message is wholesome and one the world needs more of, with a nice emotional twist.My only real complaint is slightly finnicky controls, most in terms of rotating in the air being slow for some abilities (gliding) but instant for others (air-dashing), which can feel slightly frustrating at times; and the targeting for teleportation can be a little aggravating and unintuitive.I thought the game could have used a bit more density in terms of things to do. There's a lot of just journeying without any objective but to get to the next puzzle area, which admittedly does fit the mood of the game, but at the same time, I started off exploring everywhere like I would for a typical open-world game with collectibles. After the first couple of levels, I figured out that there just aren't really many secrets hidden anywhere.Each level requires three puzzles to be solved to pass, but has five to seven puzzles and a few side-quests total, so a younger kid could skip the hardest (and, for me, most rewarding puzzles) and still have a good time, while an older kid or adult can easily complete everything in about 5 hours total.Of course I simply adore that the main character is barefoot! Even in the snow, which is really cool! Great footstep sound effects, too, especially on stone.Overall, I'd say this game is worth about $5 to $10, which is conveniently about where it's priced in a sale. I wouldn't be upset if I'd paid full price, but I wouldn't jump at it either.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: For the majority of the game I had my mind set on making a mixed review that teeters towards the positive. Unfortunately, steam operates on a binary recommendation system and a few nitpicks near the end really soured my experience. I'll attempt to be as positive as I can, especially considering the game was created by a solo dev but as much as it hurts me to give it a thumbs down I still want to be realistic considering just how oversaturated the market is.The Pros:* The simple aesthetics of the game are delightful, the atmosphere it sets is relaxing and the sound design complements it well, however the visuals are not strong enough to carry the experience on their own.* The creature designs are incredibly imaginative and charming but it's a shame most of them aren't involved in the actual gameplay aside from playing a single animation when you do something next to them.* The game is very accessible, if you have a kid they can probably pick this up and have some fun with it.* Solo dev, bravo and I hope we see more from Jonas!The Cons:* The Puzzles: If you market your game as one "full of puzzles and obstacles to overcome" you have to make sure you have solid puzzles. The puzzles in Omno are entirely too simplistic usually only having 1 or 2 movable parts and only having 1 or 2 ways to interact with said parts meaning you'll never really need to stop and think about what you need to do. A good puzzle is a puzzle that constantly puts the goal at arms length of the player but throws curve balls when the obvious approach forcing them to stop and think about a solution then making players feel good about themselves when the solution is found. Due to a lack of more complex game mechanics and the tiny scale of the puzzles there's realistically never a reason to stop and think and you'd still solve all of them on your, at worst 3rd try by brute force.* The Clunkiness: You have to let go and re-click surf/glide if you want to dash meaning that you can lose all your momentum/height without a perfectly timed re-click. The wall grab animation sometimes plays and still doesn't climb you up a wall. I got stuck in level geometry 3 times. The glide itself just feels very awkward to use at times and it doesn't help that the uplift indicators are hard to see.* The Camera: The camera should never be something you fight with. If you want to show something either strip control out of the players hands and show it or point to the place and let the player choose if they want to see it or not. By taking most but not all of the camera's control from the player you just make people fall off cliffs. This is especially annoying during the mythical beast riding sequences, why give me the option to look around if you're gonna force me to look forwards anyway?* The Ending/Narrative: SPOILER: I know that overall the point of the story is that the journey is more important than the destination but if you set up a mystery and then never deliver on a resolution you definitely disappoint some people. Stripping away the decision at the end and having a character abandon his life goal because a green-bean-squirrel would be sad doesn't mesh well with me. * The lack of Completionist options and the save/load system: The game is extremely linear with no way to go back after you've gotten a new power so why is there only 5 different load points? Why can't each location be loaded in to directly? And why does loading a specific location erase your entire history of animals and notes rather then just allow you to find the ones you missed? I missed 1 note and 1 animal because I was in a hurry and to get those, instead of just playing two stages again and searching for them you're forcing me to play the whole game again for the achievements? Seriously? I know some might see this as a nitpick but it's honestly just too frustrating and could have been thought out better.So yeah, overall not a bad experience but unfortunately you don't miss out on much if you skip it.
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some nice moments, but overall I would not recommend it.The best parts of the game are when you unlock new ways to move around and interact with the world (surfing, teleporting, etc.) Mainly because there is not much else to do other than explore.Story: The biggest issue with this game for me was that the story felt very lacking. The world is nice and pretty, and so are all the animals and stuff, and the music sounds grand -- but behind it there is very little world-building other than the cryptic journals which don't say much at all other than "follow the light". I just wasn't that interested in the story. There was no real plot, just explore each area and collect the little orb things so you can go to the next area--which felt more and more like a chore. There also doesn't seem to be any clear reward for getting 100% in an area, other than for the sake of getting 100%.Controls: Overall the movement is nice, but it feels a little slow. There are long animations that I felt myself wanting to skip through most of the time. I never finished the game, but I wish sprinting (like when you're at full energy) was built-in as an ability somehow. Controller support is not the best; would like to have more options for controls. Moving with the analog stick feels clunky. D-Pad would be better but there is no way to change the controls. I switch to keyboard and mouse for this reason. However there are some issues with that as well -- for one the mouse sensitivity can't be adjusted in game.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely excellent game. _childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: We all love cute little adventures that give us great fun and after which we usually regret that the game is beautiful but too short. Omno is a typical example of such games, an adorable adventure game, but very short.A journey about which we know nothing except what we read on the nearby monuments and obelisks, where we learn details based on what our ancestors wrote down.It is a very strange world, we will come across strange devices that do something, strange animals and plants that are part of the world, but we will find out that light is something that everyone has and that light is a resource that is necessary.Part platform, part puzzle game all wrapped up in one cute adventure.The game is very peaceful, there are no enemies, the strange creatures we meet will give us some lights to activate strange devices and machines.The puzzle part is very easy, it usually boils down to moving platforms, opening portals, etc. The only puzzle that gave me more trouble is somewhere in the middle of the game, you'll see when you get to it, it will take you some time to solve it.The world is really beautiful and at the same time very simple. As you go through, the world will change, from the swamp to the sea, the desert, and all the way to the high and beautiful mountains, Omno maintains the same quality and beauty of the landscape at every moment. After each completed area, a legendary animal will be waiting for you, which will lead you to the next part.The levels don't look the same, but there are routines you do on every level. You collect light, you meditate in order to aquire a map and see where you need to go, when you collect enough the main puzzle will activate and it's the same on every level, you could say it's repetitive, but it's not boring because the landscapes are different. Our little hero will get small upgrades through the levels, he will be able to float, dash, skate and teleport, which will enrich the game by making it much more interesting and challenging.The music is very relaxing and fits the game perfectly, giving it a sense of calmness and bliss, and even peace at the end.Omno is a fantastic adventure, although it doesn't last long, it offers a nice story and a nice feeling while playing, a feeling of satisfaction and tranquility
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: This is an adventure game with some platforming elements to it. There are no audio options on this one, so you're forced to listen to the soundtrack at full volume. It wasn't too much of an annoyance as the music was pleasant, but please devs, give us the option here, it's not difficult to have a volume level mixer in a game - this is a solved problem.You're placed straight into the "action", of collecting energy balls, there's no tutorial so you're on your own to fathom how things work. Eventually, you'll get the rush power, and this allows you to jump-dash to get you across longer gaps in platforms. There are also some moving platform puzzles which you then use your dash on.You'll also meet various plants and animals that have a journal entry to tell you about them, these make up the story along with the diaries of another adventurer who went on this trek before you.It's a pleasant game with a nice art style, but eventually, I got stuck on a puzzle and so my progress through the game was halted - I turned it off.This one gets 7 maroolas out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: A recommendation, though a very slight one. _childDocuments_.review: Omno is a surprisingly good game, especially considering that it was developed by a single person. The focus of Omno is on providing a beautiful cinematic experience and to create a relaxing athmosphere. The little puzzles are rather simple, and are mainly there to give you something to do on your journey. The platforming in Omno is also very minimal, only a couple of times the platforming becomes mildly challenging.The developer has created lots of fantasy flora and fauna in the game. Most of the fauna is just there to collect energy from, only a handful of creatures you can interact with in a meaningful way to actually do some platforming and solve a puzzle.Even though Omno is not a long game, you can expect to get about 5 hours of gameplay out of it if you choose to 100% each chapter before moving on to the next. It is nice that the game indicates how many percent of all collectibles you have found thus far, so you always know when the hidden treasure hunt if over and it is time to move on to the next chapter. The game does not force you to 100% complete each chapter before moving on.The biggest issue I had with the game is that it tended to give me motion sickness if I moved the camera around to fast.  Movement in general tended to feel quite unnatural and floaty. Unfortunately, camera speed is not something you can customize, you just have to take things a little slower to avoid motionsickness.

_childDocuments_.review: Omno is an adventure platformer with some light puzzle elements. The best games I can liken it to are Abzu or Journey where the gameplay is rather simple and there's a lot more flash and oomph on the visuals. _childDocuments_.review: And through the light we journey onwards.Nice little exploration game, with minor puzzles and platforming sections, but nothing too challanging. The whole point of the game is to relax, sit back, and enjoy the environments, the little details, and the absolutely amazing music. There's no voice acting, just occasional notes of a bygone traveller, leaving behind his thoughts, so don't expect a deep story, but it's just enough to give you an idea of the world you're in.If you are not into the thought of just exploring without a driving force of a story or a challenge, the game will get very boring half way through, but if you're fine with that idea, the game gives you new abilities just so often enough to keep you engaged till the end. Personally, I didn't like the ending. Yes, it hits home the point of the game, but I was just hoping for a little more here in terms of story and worldbuilding. Just keep in mind that this is a project by a single developer, it is not gonna blow your mind and it's not trying to either. But for what it is it absolutely succeeds at a bringing you that feeling of discovery and a journey full of wonder and beauty. 100% recommended soulfood right here!
_childDocuments_.name: Omno

_childDocuments_.review: I got the game from August 2022's Humble Choice. With that in mind, I think it's a fair price to pay - or to wait for a discount.A simple "It's the journey and friends made along the way, not the destination that counts" type of game. Very basic exploration based platformer with some fairly basic puzzle solving. It's very short, which is the main reason I'd suggest waiting for a sale - for $15, there are better and longer games, and that's just taking the indie scene into consideration.Visuals are pretty uninspired, being the 20th indie game with a low poly, basically no textures art style. It doesn't stand out from any other games with such art style whastoever - it doesn't look bad by any means, but it won't take your breath away or make you remember anything. Even the designs of creatures in the game aren't anything to write home about, you probably have seen very similar ones in not only gaming, but animated movies as well.Sound design is pretty solid, about what you'd expect. Everything sounds like you'd imagine it would. Music is fantastic, though I wouldn't say it's very original either - again, piano, strings, very emotional, kind of basic tracks at times. Well composed, just nothing you'd recognize outside of the game.Gameplay is just... Okay. Platforming isn't very challenging, there's no penalty for falling to your death either - checkpoints are plenty and you respawn almost instantly to try again.Exploration can be fun, especially after getting the Surf ability - a godsend too, as later levels get pretty big, considering the fact that there is no combat: you JUST run around to platform and solve puzzles. In theory you could say that these in-between sections of running allow you to take in the world and music (when you surf, the music kicks in, which is a nice touch), but because the graphics and designs aren't really anything special as I already mentioned, it just becomes boring to run around - even despite the game being 3, maybe 4 hours long.Puzzles, once again, aren't very hard. They mostly consist of having to press E to activate something, push some blocks around for a platforming section, press buttons in a specific order, set a specific combination of symbols... Stuff like that.Going for 100% isn't difficult either, achievements just require you to find everything in a level and maybe 3 or 4 have a hidden task to complete, like "interact with a thing 5 times in a row". They're also in the achievements descriptions, so you can look them up beforehand. The game also has a level selection menu, so you can go back after finishing the game, if you'd prefer to do it that way.Overall, I'd say this is a perfect game for a bundle, or just snatching for a few bucks tops on a sale. It probably won't stick with you, because the themes, story, visuals, music, anything really isn't remarkable. There's nothing  with the game, it's just one that will most likely sink in the sea of other, very similar titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmospheric game! The visuals are stunning, the soundtrack complements the graphics beautifully, most of the puzzles are just on the right level (not too easy, but also not too hard). Some are a little difficult if you struggle with adjusting perspectives (especially the time-sensitive ones) which can be frustrating at times, but they are still doable.  Towards the end the puzzles become a bit repetitive, but this doesn't take away from the overall gaming experience. There is an overarching story, but it does not take center stage and poses more questions than it answers. For me personally, the story could be a little bit better elaborated, but it also adds to the mystery of the world you explore. The character you play is relatable nevertheless, not least because over the course of the game it develops a tender friendship with a little funny animal and treats all other creatures it encounters with awe and respect - a nice reminder of how all life is valuable and how connected we are with the environment around us. I particularly liked the allusions and references to some children's books, which triggered great memories. If you want to get lost in another world and just have some fun and relax, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous game with fun and straight-forward puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: To start this review off -If you are looking to buy this game : If you enjoyed Journey, you will enjoy this game very much. If you enjoy a relaxing game with a linear path, and some problem solving, all while being able to explore and discover the new world around you, you will enjoy this game very much. I thoroughly enjoyed it from start to finish. Feedback/Highlights : I have a couple of small pain points : - not being able to control the audio volume in game- some of the control felt janky (particularly movement, particularly the jump and long jump control - sometimes holding down space still registered as just tapping space, resulting in a shorter jump than planned)- it began to feel a little repetitive for me by the end BUT for (what I understand to be) your first game made, pain points/learning curves are to be expected and this game is honestly incredible despite those very tiny nuisances I had (which didn't take away from the experience of the game at all). ONTO THE GOOD STUFF! This game is beautiful with an elegant yet simple message that will really hit home, regardless of who you are. The soundtrack is beautifully done, absolutely perfect in setting the atmosphere. I love the graphics and the world you have created. So beautiful, so full of colour, with each level/area showcasing a new type of scenery and new animals and new fauna to explore and discover. I am a huge fan of the surfing and that you are able to do that pretty much wherever you have a slope from that point forward, made exploring a little quicker and more fun!The puzzles admittedly did catch me out on a couple of occasions where I spent a little longer than I would have liked on them, but that was something I also enjoyed as it broke up some of the repetitive aspect I was noticing and gave me something new to figure out. The ending - no spoilers but my goodness, that ending was just perfect. You should be proud of yourself, this is a fantastic game that I thoroughly enjoyed. I look forward to seeing more of your work in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ridiculously pretty. It's hard to take screenshots because there's so much to choose from, every angle looks good... Great job, especially considering the simple, untextured aesthetic of each individual part!I went in (distractedly) expecting a walking sim, but this isn't one, not exactly. There are puzzles and platforming challenges, although the difficulty level is reasonably low and you won't get frustrated - reminded me a lot of Rime (which I liked!) Since each level only requires you to collect 3 of the 5 orbs available in it, you can get away with barely any friction if you just want to make progress, or choose to tackle the slightly harder challenges if you want to 100% it (which I did).  Everything outside the menu works very well and is polished to a shine. The music was good, too. I didn't encounter any gameplay related bugs.My controller disconnected many times while I played due to hardware damage (the typical xbox controller's failing USB port). Nothing to do with the game, but it caused some bizarre behavior in the game from time to time, including an inability to reach some menu options or a complete freeze, requiring a game restart (that happened twice). An edge case, since most people won't be unplugging their controller while they play, but it might be worth looking into.I was disappointed I couldn't fine tune the display settings individually. Much like everyone else, I hate motion blur, but it wasn't possible to turn that off, which made any screenshots I attempted to take during cutscenes or  those "meditation" (map unlocking) scenes slightly blurry. Maybe there could be a "screenshot" mode accessible from the pause menu that hides the menu and lets you pan the camera around the protagonist!

_childDocuments_.review: Entering the world of Omno you are greeted with this magical storybook world created from low-poly landscapes and simple flat textures, yet somehow this world is more alive than many photo-realistic game worlds.  Spanning five chapters, you’ll explore all the typical climates; jungles, winter mountains, desert canyons, and lush forests, all modestly detailed with trees and grass, ancient architecture, and a vast catalog of creatures – seriously, you get to catalog all 41 creature types that populate the world.  There is also this green flying squirrel-like creature that will join you for the adventure; remember to interact with him often as he become the heart and soul of the game.The core game is all about collecting energy from the world.  There are energy orbs scattered about each environment and you need three to power each level’s shrine and unlock the path to the next level, but you’ll need twice that many if you want a perfect 100%.  Energy can be gathered from just about any organic thing like plants and animals.  You can use your staff to release energy shards from rocks, trees, bushes, or interact with any of the creatures you encounter for them to release their energy in unique and delightful animations.  Energy gathered shows up as a strip of light on your arm and when fully charged grants you increased movement for a time.  It also fuels your staff and special abilities as well as unlocking a certain shrine in each level to earn one of those energy orbs.  Also scattered about the levels are books or Glyphs that combine to create a journal telling the story of why you are here and what you are doing.  These also factor into your 100% rating for each chapter.Simply put, Omno is a Zen-inspired adventure like no other.  Nine out of ten Buddhist monks achieved total consciousness playing this game; the tenth just vanished into the astral plane during the closing credits.  Seriously, this is a must-play game for anyone and everyone.  I’m not even going to qualify it beyond that.  Read full review at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Pretty, fun and relaxing game with beautiful music. but don't expect any form of difficult platforming/puzzles/trying to reach difficult places for neat little rewards.I really liked the game, it has a very distinct Journey-esque feeling to it. The simple yet colerfull artstyle, the relaxing atmosphere, the slow beautiful music, and the somewhat vague story. You can see that Jouney was an inspiration for this game, in a good way.It isn't a very long game, only around 4 hours (I left mine opens for two). The platforming felt very solid most of the time, and all the extra skills you gather feel like fun additions.I do want to talk about some stuff I would have liked to see more of, it would be the difficulty, or lack thereoff. The platforming, puzzles and collectibles never got very challenging. The platforming stayed pretty much the same throughout the entire game, even with the additional powerups it didn't get more difficult. I feel the difficulty could have ramped up a bit towards the end, and I'm not even a hardcore platform game lover. Same for the puzzles. The developer did a good job with making sure the puzzles weren't all exactly the same, but they never got even slightly difficult. (Except for just one which i could not figure out for the live of me. After I found out what the actual gimmick was all the difficulty fell apart)Lastly, the collectibles. These are what give you the story of the game, which is probably why they're so easy to find. Which i found to be a bit of a shame. You could collect all of them just by running normally through each level. I constantly wanted to use the skills to get to hard to get to places to see if it game gave some secret little reward, but sadly it didn't. This was probably my biggest gripe of the game, I really wanted to explore the beautiful levels, but there wasn't really any incenstive to. I.e. in Mario Odyssey I got to a really hard to get to place and thought 'take that devs, didn't think that was possible did ya?!', only to see a neat little stack of coins at the top to commemorate my small little achievement.Seeing how I wrote more about the 'bad' parts than the good parts, I want to state again that I really enjoyed the game and very much recommend it to people! I probably got in with slightly skewed expectations for it to be a tad more of a challange. But after I realized that this game was made by a solo Dev, those expectations might have been a bit too high. You did a fantastic job already! You have a new fan.Ps, I would LOVE an extra level or something similar just for sliding around on the stick, that would be so much fun

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous little game. I enjoyed the artstyle of the game, the colour palette, locations and worlds are beautiful. _childDocuments_.review: Charming, breathtaking and beautiful are the words I'd use for Omno. The world that Jonas has made is alive with colour and stunning landscapes to explore and enjoy. The game itself is simple in it's execution - the puzzles aren't overly difficult to work out, and the depth of technical mastery you need for the game is relatively easy. Far from being a negative, these points are a real positive - because Omno is designed to be an experience. Meeting the various fauna around the various landscapes is a real treat, ranging from cute and sprightly to grand and elegant. From a technical aspect, it's very clean - cleaner than many independent games for sure. Now for what I wouldn't necessarily call ' a negative', perhaps more 'something that I wouldn't personally have done'. The story-line is overly simplistic, and the various 'journal' parts you collect, don't contribute much, other than to explore the mind of an abstract person who is no more relevant to the outcome of the game at the end as they are at the beginning. It may have been better to have a story being told of past events - and used this as a premise for the journey for answers. As it is - don't expect to learn much from collecting the narration cubes beyond achievement of clearing the game.Having said this - the music is outstandingly lovely, and matches really well with the game world. It took me just under 5 hours to complete the whole game 100% with all achievements. So it's a very playable game, and I can see myself coming back to it in future, for the relaxing experience, stunning landscapes, the beautiful soundtrack, the charming characters, and the fun that comes with well executed game-play.At a time when there is acclaim for games like Ori and the Blind Forest & Will of the Wisps, and Journey - Omno is a real triumph, made all the more impressive in that it's mostly a labour of love by one developer. Can't recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Omno, the Atmospheric Adventure, is something special. To think that only one person completely designed the game is almost unfathomable considering the finished product.So, what does it have that really shines?- Uniqueness- Beautiful scenery- Imaginative animal creations- Wonderful, peaceful soundtrack- Small puzzles- Amazing animation (for actions performed)- Well broken up sections/biomes- Runs smoothly- Easy learning curve- Repetitive styleAll of that said, I do have a few things that I didn't care for.- The sun (it was way too bright in some worlds - I adjusted the brightness, but still the sun was just overpowering at some points- The story was fairly weak, and the ending (in my opinion) wasn't the best- Non-adjustable sound- Could use a warning for epileptics, particularly with the one animal creation that spins you around and around- Repetitive style- In my opinion, too steep an asking price at $18 - you'll get 4-6 hours out of a playthrough to 100% it.All in all I certainly recommend the game, but I'd wait for it to drop a bit in price. NOTE: I was a kickstarter backer for this and received the game as a result of that.

_childDocuments_.review: I first heard about OMNO nearly 3 years ago when it was at Kickstarter stage. Back then it promised to take you on a journey of discovery through an ancient world of wonders. With the support of its backers the developer, Jonas Manke, was able to take the time to exceed his promise and fulfil his vision with magnificent graphics, beautiful soundtrack and a journey you won't want to end.You play in an open world environment as a character I shall refer to as OMNO, though the title may not in fact be in reference to this. As the player you will take OMNO on a journey through a series of landscapes; from swampland, to forest, through icy tundra, across blistering desert and finally to floating islands.He carries a staff which he uses to gather energy from the natural world which is required to activate pillars. Each area you move through has collectables in the form of orbs, glyphs, books and magical creatures. Orbs are required to activate puzzles within a region. These need to be completed before moving to the next area. The books and the glyphs help to tell the story of the journey to the tower and final gateway which OMNO seeks to find. There are 41 creatures spread throughout all 5 regions. These can also provide OMNO with energy when interacted with accordingly. A favourite feature of the staff though has to be its ability to allow OMNO to surf across the landscape, dash, glide and even teleport across vast distances. If there was ever a way to travel, this surely has to be it!As you travel you meet a companion and that friendship becomes something you cherish by the end of the game. The final scenes are heart wrenching but I won't spoil them by revealing it. This game is a journey everyone should take. Perhaps you will take something away from the game - for me it was that the journey can matter as much as the final destination and to place value in the here and now.
